## Purpose
Fix a random bug from tests/v1/sample/test_sampler.py::test_sampler_bad_words when batch size is 32 and bad words lengths is (2, 2). 
There are two corner cases that would trigger this unit test to fail but the input is random generated so this error is diffcult to replicate during CI test in vLLM.

#### Corner Case 1:
When two randomly generated token ID sequences share the same first token ID — for example, [[522, 2], [522, 3]] — only [522, 2] will be considered in the bad words filtering process. [522, 3] will be ignored, leading to incomplete coverage.

#### Corner Case 2:
When the first token IDs of two randomly generated token ID sequences differ by only 1 — for example, [[524, 2], [523, 3]] — and the has_bad_words check happens to return False for both, the last token in the output may incorrectly be replaced with 524 (a bad word), causing an error.

## Test Plan
100 runs of the following command and make sure all passes
```
python3 -m pytest -s -v  -p no:faulthandler /vllm/tests/v1/sample/test_sampler.py -k test_sampler_bad_words

title: [BugFix][AMD][Quantization] Fix torch.compile issue where wvSplitKQ not being called when it should when using quantized FP8 model
author: rasmith
body:
This PR fixes an issue where `wvSplitKQ` is not being called when it should be when using a quantized FP8 model. This is because during compilation, this code path is not being used so does not get called during model execution even though it should be (e.g. batch size = 1).

I tested using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV.

Before this, this kernel was not being called at all when eager mode was not enforced.  

Without the fix, and running with eager mode enforced:

```

title: vllm fix check on max vocab size
author: xw285cornell
body:
Summary:
the tokenizer.vocab_size and model.vocab_size can be different. For QWen model, the tokenizer max token id is 151643 and the model config is `"vocab_size": 151936`. If we send an id between 151643 and 151936, it'll fail. Though in reality the tokenizer will just put ''. 

It's probably still valid to send the ids in between, because the model can legitimately produce such token id.

author: faaany
body:
# Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.

## Purpose
This PR fixes the following OOM issue when starting a vllm server using data parallel with ray backend:
```bash
(APIServer pid=1370745)   File "/home/sdp/fanli/vllm/vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1143, in __init__
(APIServer pid=1370745)     super().__init__(vllm_config, local_client, "", executor_class,
(APIServer pid=1370745)   File "/home/sdp/fanli/vllm/vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 936, in __init__
(APIServer pid=1370745)     super().__init__(vllm_config, local_client, handshake_address,
(APIServer pid=1370745)   File "/home/sdp/fanli/vllm/vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 474, in __init__
(APIServer pid=1370745)     super().__init__(vllm_config, executor_class, log_stats,
(APIServer pid=1370745)   File "/home/sdp/fanli/vllm/vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 86, in __init__
(APIServer pid=1370745)     self._initialize_kv_caches(vllm_config)
(APIServer pid=1370745)   File "/home/sdp/fanli/vllm/vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 172, in _initialize_kv_caches
(APIServer pid=1370745)     kv_cache_configs = [
(APIServer pid=1370745)   File "/home/sdp/fanli/vllm/vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 173, in <listcomp>
(APIServer pid=1370745)     get_kv_cache_config(vllm_config, kv_cache_spec_one_worker,
(APIServer pid=1370745)   File "/home/sdp/fanli/vllm/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py", line 1075, in get_kv_cache_config
(APIServer pid=1370745)     check_enough_kv_cache_memory(vllm_config, kv_cache_spec, available_memory)
(APIServer pid=1370745)   File "/home/sdp/fanli/vllm/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py", line 679, in check_enough_kv_cache_memory
(APIServer pid=1370745)     raise ValueError(
(APIServer pid=1370745) ValueError: To serve at least one request with the models's max seq len (131072), (3.50 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (1.26 GiB). Based on the available memory, the estimated maximum model length is 47104. Try increasing `gpu_memory_utilization` or decreasing `max_model_len` when initializing the engine.
``` 
The reason for this failure is that both Ray actors use the same device to allocate the kv cache tensors, indicating that the env var set in the init method of [DPEngineCoreActor](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L1169) doesn't take effect.

The reason why it doesn't take effect is that Ray has already initialized the XPU context before loading Ray actors.  As a result, any environment variable changes made in the actor's __init__ method are too late to influence device selection.

To fix this problem, we need to set the XPU environment variable before Ray actors are initialized. Since runtime_env is set while starting Ray worker processes, this PR configures the required XPU environment variable ZE_AFFINITY_MASK via runtime_env for each actor. 

## Test Plan
```bash
RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B --data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-backend=ray
```

## Test Result
ray server can be started.

title: Fix(benchmarks): allow multiple mm contents in OpenAI Chat Completion Benchmarks
author: h-brenoskuk
body:
## Purpose

Accept both dict and list[dict] for multi_modal_content in RequestFuncInput to support multiple multimodal parts (e.g., multi-image) in a single message, matching openai chat completion requested format.


-Preserve backward compatibility for a single-item dict.
-Relax and assert input validation in the initial single-run checks to allow None | dict | list[dict] with element-type checks.
-For audio streaming, explicitly validate multi_modal_content is a dict containing the audio key before calling `to_bytes`, preventing type/indexing errors.

## Test Plan

This issue was identified while implementing a synthetic multimodal (image) data generator by extending the already existing `RandomDataset`:

(will open another PR soon)

```python

#####
# WIP
#####
class RandomDataset(BenchmarkDataset):
    # Default values copied from benchmark_serving.py for the random dataset.
    DEFAULT_PREFIX_LEN = 0
    DEFAULT_RANGE_RATIO = 0.0
    DEFAULT_INPUT_LEN = 1024
    DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LEN = 128

    def __init__(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        random.seed(self.random_seed)
        np.random.seed(self.random_seed)

    def sample(
        self,
        tokenizer: PreTrainedTokenizerBase,
        num_requests: int,
        prefix_len: int = DEFAULT_PREFIX_LEN,
        range_ratio: float = DEFAULT_RANGE_RATIO,
        input_len: int = DEFAULT_INPUT_LEN,
        output_len: int = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LEN,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> list[SampleRequest]:
        input_lens, output_lens, offsets = self.get_sampling_params(
            num_requests, range_ratio, input_len, output_len, tokenizer
        )

        # Generate prefix once
        prefix_token_ids = self.get_prefix(tokenizer, prefix_len)
        vocab_size = tokenizer.vocab_size

        requests = []
        for i in range(num_requests):
            prompt, total_input_len = self.generate_token_sequence(
                tokenizer=tokenizer,
                prefix_token_ids=prefix_token_ids,
                prefix_len=prefix_len,
                vocab_size=vocab_size,
                input_len=int(input_lens[i]),
                offset=int(offsets[i]),
                index=i,
            )
            print(f"total_input_len: {total_input_len}")
            requests.append(
                SampleRequest(
                    prompt=prompt,
                    prompt_len=total_input_len,
                    expected_output_len=int(output_lens[i]),
                )
            )
        return requests

    def get_prefix(self, tokenizer: PreTrainedTokenizerBase, prefix_len: int) -> list[int]:
        """
        Get the prefix for the dataset.
        """
        return np.random.randint(0, tokenizer.vocab_size, size=prefix_len).tolist() if prefix_len > 0 else []

    def get_sampling_params(
        self,
        num_requests: int,
        range_ratio: float,
        input_len: int,
        output_len: int,
        tokenizer: PreTrainedTokenizerBase,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Get the sampling parameters for the dataset.
        """
        # Enforce range_ratio < 1
        assert range_ratio < 1.0, "random_range_ratio must be < 1.0 to ensure a valid sampling range"
        num_special_tokens = tokenizer.num_special_tokens_to_add()
        real_input_len = input_len - num_special_tokens
        # New sampling logic: [X * (1 - b), X * (1 + b)]
        input_low = int(real_input_len * (1 - range_ratio))
        input_high = int(real_input_len * (1 + range_ratio))
        output_low = int(output_len * (1 - range_ratio))
        output_high = int(output_len * (1 + range_ratio))

        # Add logging for debugging
        logger.info(
            "Sampling input_len from [%s, %s] and output_len from [%s, %s]",
            input_low,
            input_high,
            output_low,
            output_high,
        )

        input_lens = np.random.randint(input_low, input_high + 1, size=num_requests)
        output_lens = np.random.randint(output_low, output_high + 1, size=num_requests)
        offsets = np.random.randint(0, tokenizer.vocab_size, size=num_requests)
        return input_lens, output_lens, offsets

    def generate_token_sequence(
        self,
        *,
        tokenizer: PreTrainedTokenizerBase,
        prefix_token_ids: list[int],
        prefix_len: int,
        vocab_size: int,
        input_len: int,
        offset: int,
        index: int,
    ) -> tuple[str, int]:
        """
        Replicates the per-request logic from previous version of `sample` without changing behavior.
        Returns (prompt, total_input_len, expected_output_len).
        """
        # Build the deterministic inner sequence by sampling sequentially from the vocab
        inner_seq = ((offset + index + np.arange(input_len)) % vocab_size).tolist()
        token_sequence = prefix_token_ids + inner_seq

        # Decode, then re-encode and truncate to preserve token count invariants
        prompt = tokenizer.decode(token_sequence)
        total_input_len = prefix_len + int(input_len)
        # total_input_len = len(token_sequence)  # equals len(prefix_token_ids) + input_len

        re_encoded_sequence = tokenizer.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)[:total_input_len]
        prompt = tokenizer.decode(re_encoded_sequence)
        total_input_len = len(re_encoded_sequence)

        return prompt, total_input_len


class RandomMultiModalDataset(RandomDataset):
    """
    Random multimodal dataset that generates synthetic images with random text.

    Provides two sampling methods:
    - sample(): OpenAI API format for serve.py compatibility.
        - images are in base64 format, multimodal_data is a list of dicts
    - sample_raw(): Return sample with images in PIL format for benching the AsyncLLM engine (omitted here).
        - images are in PIL format, multimodal_data is a MultiModalDataDict
    """

    IS_MULTIMODAL = True
    DEFAULT_HEIGHT = 224
    DEFAULT_WIDTH = 224
    DEFAULT_NUM_IMAGES = 1
    DEFAULT_ENABLE_MULTIMODAL_CHAT = False

    def _generate_synthetic_image(self, width: int, height: int) -> Image.Image:
        """Generate synthetic PIL image with random RGB values."""
        random_pixels = np.random.randint(0, 256, (height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
        return Image.fromarray(random_pixels)

    def sample(
        self,
        tokenizer: PreTrainedTokenizerBase,
        num_requests: int,
        prefix_len: int = RandomDataset.DEFAULT_PREFIX_LEN,
        range_ratio: float = RandomDataset.DEFAULT_RANGE_RATIO,
        input_len: int = RandomDataset.DEFAULT_INPUT_LEN,
        output_len: int = RandomDataset.DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LEN,
        width: int = DEFAULT_WIDTH,
        height: int = DEFAULT_HEIGHT,
        num_images: int = DEFAULT_NUM_IMAGES,
        enable_multimodal_chat: bool = DEFAULT_ENABLE_MULTIMODAL_CHAT,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> list[SampleRequest]:
        """
        Standard sample method compatible with serve.py and other datasets.
        Returns OpenAI API format for compatibility with serve.py.

        Args:
            tokenizer: The tokenizer to use for processing
            num_requests: Number of requests to generate
            width: Image width in pixels
            height: Image height in pixels
            num_images: Number of images per request
            enable_multimodal_chat: Whether to apply multimodal chat
                transformation
            **kwargs: Additional arguments passed to parent sample method

        Returns:
            List of SampleRequest objects with properly formatted openai multimodal data.
        """
        input_lens, output_lens, offsets = self.get_sampling_params(
            num_requests, range_ratio, input_len, output_len, tokenizer
        )

        # Generate prefix once
        prefix_token_ids = self.get_prefix(tokenizer, prefix_len)
        vocab_size = tokenizer.vocab_size
        # Add synthetic images to each request
        mm_requests = []
        for i in range(num_requests):
            prompt, total_input_len = self.generate_token_sequence(
                tokenizer=tokenizer,
                prefix_token_ids=prefix_token_ids,
                prefix_len=prefix_len,
                vocab_size=vocab_size,
                input_len=int(input_lens[i]),
                offset=int(offsets[i]),
                index=i,
            )
            # Create synthetic images
            # The process_image returns {"type": "image_input", "image_url": f"{base64_image}"}
            # This follows the OpenAI API chat completions https://github.com/openai/openai-python
            mm_content = [process_image(self._generate_synthetic_image(width, height)) for _ in range(num_images)]
            mm_requests.append(
                SampleRequest(
                    prompt=prompt,
                    prompt_len=total_input_len,
                    expected_output_len=int(output_lens[i]),
                    multi_modal_data=mm_content,
                )
            )

        return mm_requests
```

## Test Result

Calling the `RandomMultiModalDataset` above with more than one image would directly fail the assertion at `serve.py` and also send an invalid request due to the append.  With these changes it handles the code above while maintaining retrocompatibility.

author: hmellor
body:
It would be nice to enable `--strict` mode in the docs build so that it can catch any broken links before we merge docs PRs.

This is currently not possible because the docs build contains too many warnings.

This PR begins the process of fixing them.

title: [BugFix] Fix logits repetition penalty cuda check
author: PicoCreator
body:
# Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist

One line bug fix for sampling on CPU, on systems with GPU's as per reported here: 
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22591

It really is a simple fix

```python
def apply_repetition_penalties(logits: torch.Tensor, prompt_mask: torch.Tensor,
                               output_mask: torch.Tensor,
                               repetition_penalties: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """Apply repetition penalties to logits in-place.
    Args:
        logits: The logits tensor of shape [num_seqs, vocab_size].
        prompt_mask: A boolean tensor indicating which tokens appear in the prompt.
        output_mask: A boolean tensor indicating which tokens appear in the output.
        repetition_penalties: The repetition penalties of shape (num_seqs, ).
    """
    # if current_platform.is_cuda() and logits.is_contiguous(): # <-- this was the original code
    if logits.is_cuda and logits.is_contiguous(): # <-- this is the fix
        apply_repetition_penalties_cuda(logits, prompt_mask, output_mask,
                                        repetition_penalties)
    else:
        apply_repetition_penalties_torch(logits, prompt_mask, output_mask,
                                         repetition_penalties)
```

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22591

author: frankwang28

## Purpose
There is a newer version of DeepGEMM which fixes some bugs, notably around smxx layout assertions. The current version of DeepGEMM in the Dockerfile does not have these fixes and we should bump the git reference accordingly. For reference, I am encountering the issue when serving DeepSeek-R1-0528 on 8xB200 with DeepGEMM, expert parallelism (DP=8, TP=1) and pplx All2All backend.

## Test Plan
Launch vLLM before and after the updated DeepGEMM version.

title: [BugFix][Nixl][PD] Fix heterogenous TP
author: NickLucche
body:
In the attempt to deprecate V0 here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21785, we introduced a subtle bug that would prevent a KVConnector from forwarding its KV cache layout preference.
This would result in the following log:
```
(EngineCore_0 pid=1204777) INFO 08-11 16:32:10 [utils.py:113] Connectors do not specify a kv cache layout, defaulting to NHD.
```
which, in the case of NixlConnector for D TP != P TP means breaking one of the single core assumption about the layout. This results in a garbled output.

This PR brings things back to
```
(EngineCore_0 pid=1306559) INFO 08-11 17:17:38 [nixl_connector.py:151] NixlConnector setting KV cache layout to HND for better xfer performance.
```


Also added @njhill fix for KVConnectorOutput or it would break even earlier than observing the correctness regression.

title: Fix Transformers backend tensor parallel for multimodal models
author: hmellor
body:
This PR fixes 2 things:

- Top level multimodal configs don't have `base_model_tp_plan`. So we make sure we get it from each sub config in `TransformersBase`
- If a model with a TP plan is a sub model, the to plan patterns won't match because there is a missing prefix. We now add this prefix before matching.

title: Fix cuda illegal mem access with Llama4 TP8 + rms_norm custom op
author: nvpohanh
body:
The rms_norm custom op cuda kernel supports non-contiguous striding on the "num_tokens" dim, but it assumes that all the num_tokens dims (if there are more than one num_tokens dim) are contiguous.

This causes a CUDA illegal mem access when running Llama4 with TP8 with +rms_norm custom op.

To work around this issue, reshape the Q/K to 2D tensors before calling the qk_norm. This makes the num_tokens dims collapse into one dim and it will be obviously contiguous.

When rms_norm custom op is disabled, this reshape will be fused with the RMSNorm's forward_native() anyway so there is no perf impact.

I will add additional checks in the custom rms_norm kernel in another PR.

title: fp8 kv cache support fix for torch.compile
author: maleksan85
body:
Torch compile was erroring in attention layer on assert for q_scale to be equals 1.0. The error came originally from HIP saying that operation is not allowed during cuda graph capture. Thus implementing a copy of q_scale - q_scale_float (similar to k_scale_float and v_scale float).

PS q_scale needs to be one because upscalling doesn't happen on AMD from predeceasing GEMMs and scales are only applied to k and v if those are in fp8.

title: [FIXBUG] Add return_success parameter to moe_wna16_weight_loader function
author: JartX
body:
This PR fixes a TypeError that occurs when attempting to load models like Qwen3-30B-A3B.

The bug was introduced in commit [d979dd6bebb1857052e6beae682e5186f8447fde](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/d979dd6bebb1857052e6beae682e5186f8447fde). In that commit, the return_success=True argument was added to the function call for moe_wna16_weight_loader, but the function's definition was not updated to accept this new argument.

As a result, the weight loading process failed with a TypeError when attempting to load models such as Qwen3 30B A3B.

This fix updates the function signature of moe_wna16_weight_loader to include the return_success parameter, allowing model loading to complete successfully.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix compilation error in topk softmax fused kernel
author: kliuae
body:

- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.


## Purpose
With ROCm deprecating the use of `warpSize`, wavefront size cannot be used as a constexpr in host code. In the topk softmax fused kernel (#22211), this breaks the compile-time assertion on `WARP_SIZE`, producing the following error:
```
error: static assertion expression is not an integral constant expression
note: expanded from macro 'WARP_SIZE'
```

This PR addresses the issue by compiling kernels for both wavefront size 32 and wavefront size 64, and selecting the appropriate version at runtime based on the runtime device characteristics queries.

title: [BugFix] Fix initial DP request load imbalance
author: njhill
body:
The internal DP load-balancing logic currently only sends requests to the first rank until it receives the first stats update from the coordinator. This means that an initial burst of requests after startup can result in a temporary imbalance.

It was causing the load-balancing test to sometimes fail.

title: [Structured Outputs] [Bug] Fix misalignment in apply_grammar_bitmask causing unintended masking and NaN logits
author: rishitdholakia13
body:
## Purpose
Fix a bug in apply_grammar_bitmask where the number of bitmasks was derived from the pre-initialized sorted_bitmask tensor instead of the actual indices requiring masking. This misalignment caused non-structured output requests to be masked, leading to illegal memory access issues due to their logits being converted to NaN.

## Changes Made
Derive bitmask count from the actual required indices rather than `sorted_bitmask `length.
Ensure masking is applied only to relevant requests to prevent unintended NaN logits.

author: maxdebayser
body:
This fixes two places where the value set by the user was overwritten erroneously:

- In `_set_default_args_v1` the user specified value was overwritten by `max_model_len`

- In `VllmConfig.__post_init__` the values was set to the max of DEFAULT_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS, which is only 2048, and  `max_model_len`.

As shown in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22941, tuning this value is essential to get the the maximum performance out of encoder models.

title: [Bugfix] Fix gemma3 with transformers backend
author: zucchini-nlp
body:
Gemma3 had issues with transformers backend and was explicitly left out from supported models. There are two reason for that:

1. The model's embedding layer is a custom embedding module which applies scaling. vLLM replaces input embedding layer with internal class which doesn't handle scaling, so we were seeing garbage generation with the model
2. The model requires extra kwargs in the input, apart from text ids and images. To support bidirectional mask we need `token_type_ids`. I decided to exploit an existing `SupportsMultiModalWithRawInput` for that but keep input merging on vLLM side. If we were to delete merging and let transformers handle it, we will need a bigger PR. So lmk if the current appoach works or if you want me to delete input merging code


cc @hmellor @Isotr0py

title: [Bugfix] Fix mamba2 prefill chunking
author: tomeras91
body:
## Purpose
Fix a few bugs with prefill chunking for the mamba2 kernels.

Prefill chunking with valren batching support for the Mamba2 block was added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10909, but it contained a few bugs relating to handling of initial states across mamba chunk boundaries. Some of these bugs were fixed recently in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21783 - specifically regarding the decay factor of the initial states. Yet, in cases where chunk boundaries and sequence boundaries don't align (a sequence changes in the middle of a chunk), the state passing kernel with initial states was still buggy. Namely, the computation of `dA_cumsum` was computed from the start of the mamba chunk instead of from the start of the current sequence. This PR fixes this.

Other changes:
- Added unittest for `mamba_chunk_scan_combined` with prefill chunking and varlen batching, comparing chunked results to those of the full sequence.
- Added documentation to `_query_start_loc_to_chunk_indices_offsets`, which is a somewhat cryptic function
- Added documentation to the bugfix in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21783 

## Test Plan
Make sure all cases in `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py::test_mamba_chunk_scan_cont_batch_prefill_chunking` pass. These cases fail on `main`.

## Test Result
Tests pass

title: [BugFix] Fix Python 3.9 Support
author: jaredoconnell

## Purpose
The purpose of this PR is to fix a change introduced in #22534 
That PR used the pipe operator `|`, which only supports being used in place of union in Python 3.10 and newer. So this switches the file to use the python 3.9 supported method.

There was no indication that Python 3.9 was officially dropped, and the documentation still lists 3.9 as the minimum version, so this PR makes the code reflect that.

title: [BugFix] Fix the issue where image embeddings were incorrectly split.…
author: bppps
body:
… They should be merged by the spatial_merge_size parameter on image_grid_thw in the Qwen2_VL and Qwen2_5_Omni DataParsers.

## Purpose
   Fix the issue https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/23371 where image embeddings were incorrectly split by `image_grid_thw`'s product. They should be divided by the `spatial_merge_size` parameter on `image_grid_thw`'s product in the Qwen2_VL and Qwen2_5_Omni MultiModalDataParsers. It's already present in Qwen2_VL's model's input embedding processing procedure, which may not be  considered carefully in the scenario when user provide `image_embed` and `image_grid_thw`, then `image_embed` are split across `image_grid_thw`'s product, which will cause a slice error(out of range without merging). There is similar problem on video processing.

FIX #23371
  
Image embedding spatial merge  code reference:

title: [BugFix] Fix batch updates for pooling models
author: njhill
body:
Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/23381.

Changes in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/19912 mis-assumed that pooling requests only last a single step. But with sequence chunking this might not be the case.

We should have CI tests to cover this, to be added in a follow-on.

Unfortunately this bug is in the v0.10.1 and v0.10.1.1 releases.

Summary of changes:
- Use `BatchUpdateBuilder` in `InputBatch` to track removed requests consistent with non-pooling case, used to fill in empty slots when requests are added in the same step
- Add `batch_changed` flag to `BatchUpdateBuilder` to track whether requests have been added (since the added list is only used for non-pooling reqs with sampling params)
- Reorder operations in input batch `condense()` and `swap_states()` so that only the applicable ones are done in the pooling case
- Other minor code cleanup changes

title: fix(tests): Ensure reliable CUDA cache clearing in MoE test
author: AzizCode92
body:
In `test_mixtral_moe`, `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` is called immediately after an `F.pad` operation.

Due to the asynchronous nature of CUDA kernels, there's no guarantee that the padding operation has completed on the GPU before the cache is cleared. This can make the `empty_cache()` call ineffective.

This commit adds `torch.cuda.synchronize()` before `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` to ensure all pending GPU work is finished, making memory management in the test more reliable and deterministic.


## Purpose
This PR improves the reliability of memory management in the test_mixtral_moe test by addressing a potential race condition between the CPU and GPU.

Currently, torch.cuda.empty_cache() is called immediately after an asynchronous CUDA operation (F.pad). There is no guarantee that the GPU has finished the operation before the cache-clearing command is issued, which can render empty_cache() ineffective.

This change introduces a torch.cuda.synchronize() call before empty_cache() to ensure all pending GPU kernels are complete, making the test's memory handling more robust and deterministic.

## Test Plan

pytest tests/kernels/test_moe.py -k test_mixtral_moe

## Purpose
In the test_bigger_truncation_size test, the 'err' variable from the pytest.raises context manager was being incorrectly reassigned by the API call.

Because the `await client.post(...)` line raises an exception as expected, the `assert` statement on the following line was unreachable and never executed. This means the test was only verifying the exception type, not the content of the error message.

This commit fixes the test to correctly handle the exception. The API call is now made without assignment, and the assertion is moved outside the `with` block, checking `err.value` to inspect the actual exception instance. title: [quantization] use channel scales for w4a8 + misc fixes
author: czhu-cohere
body:
## Purpose
Load per-channel scales for w4a8. This can recover the quality drop from naively casting bf16 scales to fp8 on certain benchmarks (mmlu pro). Computationally, this is 'free' since the [previous implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/23198) used `torch.ones` as a placeholder.

The `fp8` group scales and `fp32` per-channel scales can be generated as a post-processing step after we have a w4a16 checkpoint with `bf16` scales. For testing we used an adhoc workflow to generate the checkpoint but will look at integrating that into `llm-compressor` as a next step:
1. Take bf16 scales from the w4a16 checkpoint
2. do `fp8_scales, fp32_chan_scales = quantfp8(bf16_scales)`
3. divide `fp8_scales` by 8 to avoid saturation when multiplied by int4
4. multiply `fp32_chan_scales` by 8 to compensate

Then pass the adjusted `fp8_scales/fp32_chan_scales` to the `w4a8` kernel.

## Test Plan
lm-eval (gsm8k, mmlu pro) compare to w4a16 and previous w4a8 (Cohere Command A)

also add an example model `czhu-cohere/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-W4A8-e2e` and add corresponding test in `tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py`
```

title: Fix writing benchmark results with tuple keys
author: huydhn
body:
## Purpose

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/23119 introduced a new dataset parameter `--random-mm-bucket-config` which is default to a dictionary with a tuple key, i.e. `{(256, 256, 1): 0.7, (720, 1280, 1): 0.3}`.  The problem here is that `json.dump` doesn't like this type.  So, a bunch of benchmark runs are failing with `TypeError: keys must be str, int, float, bool or None, not tuple` error, for example https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch-integration-testing/actions/runs/17208394287/job/48814081180#step:16:1634.  The benchmark jobs keep track of the all benchmark arguments in its JSON results.

This PR fixes this error by converting the tuple to string before passing the benchmark results dictionary to `json.dump`.

## Test Plan

Run a benchmark with the change in this PR

cc @h-brenoskuk @ywang96

title: [bugfix] [spec-decoding] fix data race in sample_recovered_tokens_kernel (vLLM v1)
author: He-Jingkai
body:
[bugfix, spec-decoding] fix data race in sample_recovered_tokens_kernel (vLLM V1)


## Purpose

This PR resolves a data race bug in the `sample_recovered_tokens_kernel` Triton kernel.

The original implementation temporarily modifies `target_probs_ptr` to zero out a token's probability before restoring it. This is unsafe in a multithreaded environment where multiple GPU threads could concurrently access and modify the same memory address, leading to non-deterministic behavior and correctness issues.

During the development of speculative sampling in vLLM V1, we found that this data race causes different Tensor Parallelism (TP) GPUs to produce inconsistent speculative decoding verification results. Once inconsistent verification results occur, the GPU will hang (ref https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/17929).

This change replaces the unsafe read-modify-write pattern with a safer, atomic-friendly approach using a mask. Instead of modifying the memory, the kernel now uses a mask during the tl.load operation to directly set the probability of the draft token to 0. This change maintains the original logical intent while eliminating the data race and potentially improving performance.

This bug was identified and fixed during the development of the HistoSpec RL project (https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2508.18588v1), where we extended vLLM v1's speculative decoding to accelerate reinforcement learning training for LLMs.

## Test Plan

1. A full integration test with speculative decoding enabled is required to verify its correctness.
2. Deploy LLMs (we test Qwen2.5-7B/14B/32B, Qwen3-8B/14B) with TP>=2 and enable spec decoding to test its correctness when TP>=2.

## Test Result

This modification is internally used for thousands of GPU hours.


1. The change has been locally verified, and the speculative decoding pipeline functions correctly with this modification, without any observed issues or performance degradation.
2. After applying the fix, speculative decoding functions correctly with TP>=2. The issue of GPU hangs caused by inconsistent verification results across different TPs has been resolved.

## Purpose

title: [Bugfix] Fix --config arg expansion called from api_server.py
author: dubejf
body:
## Purpose

Per `--help`, the argument parser for the `vllm` CLI and the `api_server` entry point both accept the `--config` command-line argument, but only the CLI handles it correctly. This PR ensures consistent config file handling for all entry points.

**Examples:**
- `vllm serve --config config.yaml`  
  ✅ Works as expected

- `docker run <docker_arguments> vllm/vllm-openai --config config.yaml`
  ❌ `api_server.py: error: argument --config: expected one argument`

- `python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --config config.yaml`
  ❌ `api_server.py: error: argument --config: expected one argument`

**Cause:**  
`_pull_args_from_config` expects the first argument to always be a `vllm` CLI subcommand (`serve`, `chat`, `complete`, etc.), which is not the case for `api_server`.

This leads to incorrect expansion:
```
--config config.yaml <other_cli_args>
```
is mistakenly expanded to:
```
--config --arg1 value-from-config --arg2 value-from-config ... <other_cli_args>
```
instead of:
```
--arg1 value-from-config --arg2 value-from-config ... <other_cli_args>
```

## Test Plan

- Added unit tests for `--config` argument parsing in [`tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py`](tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py).

## Test Result

- The new unit tests pass.
- Existing tests for CLI config override (in [`tests/utils_/test_utils.py`](tests/utils_/test_utils.py)) already cover configuration file expansion in the `vllm serve` context; no changes required.

The error is:
```
[2025-08-29T20:36:33Z] (EngineCore_0 pid=14176)   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/compilation/activation_quant_fusion.py", line 174, in __init__

author: Csrayz
body:
## Purpose

Fix several issues with p2p xPyD in GET type:

1. When using GET mode, such a situation can occur. The GPU buffer size configuration is just at the critical value of the KV Cache size. Some requests larger than the buffer size will clear all tensors, causing `next(iter(self.send_store))` to raise StopIteration.
2. When calling recv_tensor, the remote_address of the p node is missing from the parameters, which causes kv_cache to always be None.

title: [Doc]: Fix CPU install docs: force torch-backend=cpu to avoid GPU torchvision errors
author: yankay
body:
## Purpose

After the #22089

This PR updates the CPU installation guide in by changing the `uv pip install` commands to use `--torch-backend cpu` instead of `auto`.
If `auto` is used on a GPU server, torchvision may be installed as a GPU version (e.g., torchvision 0.21.0+cu126), which causes runtime errors such as:

```
  File "/root/oss/vllm-cpu/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/_library/fake_impl.py", line 31, in register
    if torch._C._dispatch_has_kernel_for_dispatch_key(self.qualname, "Meta"):
```

Explicitly setting `--torch-backend cpu` ensures all packages are installed as CPU versions, preventing such issues.

## Test Plan

Before change
```
#uv pip install -r requirements/cpu-build.txt --torch-backend auto
#uv pip install -r requirements/cpu.txt --torch-backend auto
#uv pip list |grep torch
intel-extension-for-pytorch       2.6.0
torch                             2.6.0+cpu
torchaudio                        2.6.0+cu126
torchvision                       0.21.0+cu126
#VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python setup.py develop
#vllm serve facebook/opt-125m
...error...
  File "/root/oss/vllm-cpu/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/_library/fake_impl.py", line 31, in register
    if torch._C._dispatch_has_kernel_for_dispatch_key(self.qualname, "Meta"):
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
RuntimeError: operator torchvision::nms does not exist
...error...
```

After Change

We identified a regression in throughput caused by #21146 in some tests (most noticeably when using small input & output lengths). Specifically, on 8xMI300X:
```
VLLM_USE_V1=1 VLLM_V1_USE_PREFILL_DECODE_ATTENTION=1 python3 vllm/benchmarks/benchmark_throughput.py --model /models/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV -tp 8 --num-prompts 1024 --kv-cache-dtype "fp8" --input-len 128 --output-len 128 --dtype float16  --max-num-seqs 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"}'
...
Capturing CUDA graphs (mixed prefill-decode, FULL): 100%|██████████| 67/67 [00:06<00:00, 10.02it/s]
...

Result (avg over 5 runs): 15694.636 total tok/s
```
Whereas if we disable gc freeze during graph capture by setting `VLLM_ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH_GC=1`:

```
VLLM_ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH_GC=1 VLLM_USE_V1=1 VLLM_V1_USE_PREFILL_DECODE_ATTENTION=1 python3 vllm/benchmarks/benchmark_throughput.py --model /models/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV -tp 8 --num-prompts 1024 --kv-cache-dtype "fp8" --input-len 128 --output-len 128 --dtype float16  --max-num-seqs 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"}'
...
Capturing CUDA graphs (mixed prefill-decode, FULL): 100%|██████████| 67/67 [00:39<00:00,  1.68it/s]
...

Result (avg over 5 runs): 16416.11 total tok/s
```
The throughput is ~5% higher with `VLLM_ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH_GC=1`.
It seems that we can recover the throughput if we force a gc.collect() right after the CUDA graph capture is complete. With this PR:
```
VLLM_USE_V1=1 VLLM_V1_USE_PREFILL_DECODE_ATTENTION=1 python3 vllm/benchmarks/benchmark_throughput.py --model /models/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV -tp 8 --num-prompts 1024 --kv-cache-dtype "fp8" --input-len 128 --output-len 128 --dtype float16  --max-num-seqs 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"}'
...
Capturing CUDA graphs (mixed prefill-decode, FULL): 100%|██████████| 67/67 [00:06<00:00,  9.99it/s]
...

Result (avg over 5 runs): 16334.29283 total tok/s
```
That is, with this PR, it seems that we can recover the baseline throughput while getting the speedup from freezing gc during CUDA graph capture.

## Purpose

When Ultravox wraps a multi-modal model (e.g. Gemma) vLLM fails to load because the `UltravoxModel.text_config` is the multi-modal model's config. title: [Bugfix][Wide EP] Fix redundant work when using DeepEP, TP Attn, and EP MoE
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
## Purpose

Currently, when running attention with TP and using `--enable-expert-parallel`, the MoE layers will do duplicate work when using DeepEP. In this case, the output of attention will be replicated across TP ranks and each token copy will be dispatched to the EP ranks it gets routed to, multiplying the amount of work by `tp_size`.

This PR avoids this duplicate work by ensuring the input to the MoE layer is sequence parallel instead of replicated.


### Notes:
* The performance bug applies to any MoE model but this PR only fixes it for DeepSeekV3
* We can do better by replacing the `all_reduce` at the end of attention with a `reduce_scatter`. This reduces the amount of computation but is a little more invasive to the model definition since we need to handle the sharding of the residuals. This has an extra effect of de-duplicating the work done during layer norms (minor improvement). 

## Test Plan

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528,base_url=http://infra-wide-ep-inference-gateway-istio.llm-d-wide-ep.svc.cluster.local/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1000,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False

title: [Kernel][Bugfix] Fix grouped topk cu
author: mayuyuace
body:
When I tried to run the grouped_topk UT with the parameters (test_grouped_topk.py::test_grouped_topk[dtype0-1.0-softmax-4-8-True-2-16-2048-256]), a hang occurred.
I discovered that the kernel used cuda::std::numeric_limits<T>::min() to represent the minimum value of dtype T.
However, cuda::std::numeric_limits<T>::min() represents the smallest positive number, such as 1.175494e-38 for float, which does not represent the minimum value.
This causes an infinite loop in lines 538-547.
Replacing **cuda::std::numeric_limits<T>::min()** with **constexpr float kNegInfinity = INFINITY * -1** fixed the problem.

author: yeqcharlotte

## Purpose
1. introduce tool output tokens count. see details in RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/24284
2. fix reasoning token count (which used to hardcode recipients, and it'll miss mcp tools).
3. simplify reasoning token count to avoid creating empty list on the fly, this will cause more pressure to GC.

Added unit tests to simulate append_output `pytest -vv tests/entrypoints/test_context.py`. Honestly this codepath needs more test coverage. :(

title: [Doc] Fix UTF-8 encoding issues in documentation generation on Windows
author: alhridoy
body:
## Summary

Fixes #24360: Cannot build documentation locally without adding encoding to generate examples

This PR resolves Windows-specific encoding issues when building documentation locally by explicitly specifying UTF-8 encoding for file operations in documentation generation scripts.

## Problem

On Windows, Python's default file encoding is often `cp1252` (Windows-1252), which cannot handle Unicode characters like `\uff5c` (fullwidth vertical bar `｜`). This caused:

- **UnicodeEncodeError** when processing files with Unicode content
- **Documentation build failures** on Windows systems
- **Inability for Windows contributors** to build docs locally

### Error Examples
```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\uff5c' in position 61: character maps to <undefined>
```

## Solution

### **Core Changes**
- **`docs/mkdocs/hooks/generate_examples.py`**: Added `encoding='utf-8'` to file operations
- **`docs/mkdocs/hooks/generate_argparse.py`**: Added `encoding='utf-8'` to file operations
- **Comprehensive testing**: Added Unicode handling tests
- **Documentation**: Added Windows development guide

### **Files Modified**
```python
# Before (problematic)
with open(self.main_file) as f:
    first_line = f.readline().strip()

with open(doc_path, "w+") as f:
    f.write(example.generate())

# After (fixed)
with open(self.main_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    first_line = f.readline().strip()

with open(doc_path, "w+", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(example.generate())
```

title: [Bugfix] Fix platform-specific routing in CustomOp implementations
author: kzawora-intel
body: Some layers inheriting from `CustomOp` are overwriting the `forward` method, effectively disabling the platform routing logic defined in `CustomOp.dispatch_forward()`, resulting in `self._forward_method` not being called. This is problematic for any out-of-tree backends, as providing backend-specific `forward_oot` doesn't result in calling the proper forward pass method, even though it's properly selected in `self._forward_method`. This PR moves `forward` overrides in layers inheriting from `CustomOp` to `forward_native`, and adds `forward_cuda` also calling `forward_native` - preserving the current behavior for all existing in-tree backends, but preserving routing logic for out-of-tree backends.

title: Enable conversion of multimodal models to pooling tasks
author: maxdebayser
body:
Currently, when the automatic conversion of multi-modal generative models to pooling model is attempted, there a many failures which basically boil down to the fact that the conversion code is based on pure language models.

This PR takes advantage of the fact that most MM models use `init_vllm_registered_model` to load a language model internally, which triggers the code that attempts the conversion. So in this PR when `get_model_architecture` for the MM model is called, the function just returns a subclass which forwards to pooler to the language model.

```python
from vllm import LLM

def update_config(config):
    # Update language model configurations. This is currently only
    # possible with a hf_overrides function.
    config.text_config.update({
      "architectures": ["Gemma3ForSequenceClassification"],
      "classifier_from_token": ["Yes", "No"],           # last token
      "method": "no_post_processing",            # no postproc
    })
    return config

llm = LLM(
     model="google/gemma-3-4b-it",
     runner="pooling",
     task="classify",
     convert="classify",
     trust_remote_code=True,
     load_format="auto",
     hf_overrides=update_config,
     override_pooler_config={"pooling_type": "LAST"},
     gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
     max_model_len=1024,
     enforce_eager=True,
     tensor_parallel_size=1,
     disable_log_stats=True,
)
result = llm.classify("Is this review positive? 'The food was cold and the service slow.'")
print(result[0].outputs.probs)
```

@noooop, if you have the bandwidth, I would like to request your feedback on this before working on tests.

title: [Bugfix] Fix  hidden_size for multimodal classification model
author: jeejeelee
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose
Since some models (e.g., [Idefics3](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceM4/Idefics3-8B-Llama3/blob/main/config.json#L41)) have `hidden_size` in text_config, whereas others (e.g., [qwen2vl](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct/blob/main/config.json#L14)) have it directly in config, therefore we add a function to check this
## Test Plan
```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project

from argparse import Namespace

from vllm import LLM, EngineArgs
from vllm.utils import FlexibleArgumentParser


def parse_args():
    parser = FlexibleArgumentParser()
    parser = EngineArgs.add_cli_args(parser)
    # Set example specific arguments
    parser.set_defaults(
        model="HuggingFaceM4/Idefics3-8B-Llama3",
        task="classify",
        load_format="dummy",
        enforce_eager=True,
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


def main(args: Namespace):
    # Sample prompts.
    prompts = [
        "Hello, my name is",
        "The president of the United States is",
        "The capital of France is",
        "The future of AI is",
    ]

    # Create an LLM.
    # You should pass runner="pooling" for classification models
    llm = LLM(**vars(args))

    # Generate logits. The output is a list of ClassificationRequestOutputs.
    outputs = llm.classify(prompts)

    # Print the outputs.
    print("\nGenerated Outputs:\n" + "-" * 60)
    for prompt, output in zip(prompts, outputs):
        probs = output.outputs.probs
        probs_trimmed = (str(probs[:16])[:-1] + ", ...]") if len(probs) > 16 else probs
        print(
            f"Prompt: {prompt!r} \n"
            f"Class Probabilities: {probs_trimmed} (size={len(probs)})"
        )
        print("-" * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()
    main(args)

```
## Test Result

The above script should pass correctly, rather than raise the following error:

```text
AttributeError: 'Idefics3Config' object has no attribute 'hidden_size'
```

title: [Bug] [Spec Dec]: Fix kv_cache dtype mismatch for Eagle3 drafter on FP8 target
author: vllmellm
body: Resolves [#21308](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/21308#issuecomment-3192203896) ### **Purpose** This PR resolves a RuntimeError that occurs on the ROCm platform when using speculative decoding (eagle3 method) with FP8 quantization. The root cause was a data type mismatch in the attention backend. The drafter model was not inheriting the kv_cache_dtype from the target model, causing its KV cache to default to uint8 while the target model used fp8, leading to a crash in the Triton kernel. This fix ensures the drafter model inherits the global CacheConfig from the vLLM engine, guaranteeing type consistency. The core fix is the logic to retrieve and pass down the configurations. The other changes are mainly to support this parameter passing through the class constructors. Part B-2 Performance Test (benchserver.sh) Used an automated script to conduct stress tests. Across both math benchmarks, enabling speculative decoding shows no regression—stable on gsm8k and mildly improved on hrm8k_math_en. **B2. Benchmark Serving (Latency and Concurrency Performance Test)** We conducted a comprehensive comparison of the following scenarios: 1: AMD + without speculative decoding + FP8 vs. AMD + with speculative decoding + FP8 2: AMD + without speculative decoding + FP16 vs. AMD + with speculative decoding + FP16 3: NVIDIA GPU + without speculative decoding + FP16 + default flash-attention vs. NVIDIA GPU + with speculative decoding + FP16 + default flash-attention 4: NVIDIA GPU + without speculative decoding + FP16 + Triton vs. NVIDIA GPU + with speculative decoding + FP16 + Triton (This example is not available because it generates an error in this environment and is not supported internally by vLLM). We can see that under AMD + FP8, Spec-dec significantly improves throughput (+44%) and reduces TPOT (-30.7%), demonstrating that speculative decoding is very effective for low-precision inference. There is almost no speedup compared to the baseline (Output/Total +≈1.3–1.4%, ≈1.01×). TTFT degrades by +≈4.8% and ITL by +≈50.5%, while TPOT improves slightly by −≈1.7%. This is presumably because the FP16 baseline is already faster, and the overhead of ROCm/kernel scheduling offsets the gains, resulting in limited overall gains. However, Under NVIDIA GPU + FP16 + FlashAttention, Spec-dec significantly improved throughput (+41%) and TPOT (-8.3%), but TTFT increased (+7.2%) and ITL slightly deteriorated (+6.2%), indicating that it is more suitable for long text scenarios and has limited benefits in short prompts. ### **Other potential points** **1：In the case of auto, we check as follows: if the target model is fp8, process it. If it is float16, keep it as it is.** Modification Location: "The core code for this fix is ​​located in the vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle3.py file, specifically in the init method of the LlamaModel class." Implementation: "By importing and calling the get_current_vllm_config() function, the global, parsed configuration of the current vllm engine, is obtained." Logic Explanation: "Then, the cache_config objects obtained from the main model configuration are directly passed to the LlamaDecoderLayer in the draft model for initialization." If the main model's kv_cache_dtype is fp8, then the cache_config.cache_dtype obtained by the draft model will naturally be fp8, resolving the issue. If the main model's kv_cache_dtype is auto or float16, then the configuration obtained by the draft model will also be auto or float16. float16, completely unchanged, without any side effects. This avoids hard-coding code like "if 'fp8' in ...," making the fix more general and robust. **2：We have reproduced and fixed the issue with rocm. We need to mention the issue with cuda.** In the GPU environment, the combination of the V1 engine, mandatory Triton backend, and egale3 instructions in the def is_kv_cache_dtype_supported function in vllm/vllm/platforms/cuda.py does not meet the scenario requirements and returns false. As a result, the def _is_v1_supported_oracle function in vllm/vllm/engine/arg_utils.py enters the if self.kv_cache_dtype != "auto": logic, ultimately throwing an assertion error unless you use a graphics card model supported by the code. As shown below: This diagram is because in the combined scenario described above, the NotImplementedError in _raise_or_fallback is triggered because of the returned false **3：Why isn't the kvcache for speculative decoding VLLM separated? Will adding the kvcache dtype config for speculative decoding to the top-level configuration take effect?** The architecture was originally designed for a single master model, with global configurations such as CacheConfig and QuantizationConfig. Modular Implementation: Speculative decoding was added later and is implemented by loading a separate "scratch model." vLLM creates a separate model configuration (ModelConfig) for this scratch model. Bug Root: This is the problem. We originally added code to vllm/vllm/engine/arg_utils.py to retrieve the target model's configuration from the draft model. Then, in the next layer, vllm/vllm/config/__init__.py, in the `def __post_init__(self):` method, `if self.model is not None:`, `self.draft_model_config = ModelConfig(...)`, we added the `kv_cache_dtype` parameter to `ModelConfig`, but this did not take effect. This is because this ModelConfig lacks a default `kv_cache_dtype` attribute, causing the loading process to fall back to a default, simpler configuration path. In this path, `kv_cache_dtype` in auto mode ultimately resolves to `uint8` (a basic quantization type), rather than querying the main model's configuration. Conclusion: The root cause of the bug is the lack of a reliable configuration inheritance and synchronization mechanism between the two independent configuration domains of the main model and the draft model. Our final fix (directly retrieving the global configuration in `llama_eagle3.py`) aims to establish this direct and reliable connection.

title: [Bugfix] Fix unable to run encoder model when disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager is true
author: lianyiibo
body:
In GPU devices, when running the encoder model, the `kv_cache_spec` is processed at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/feaf202e93a18228cd34ae2e6698aece83a15e87/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L3497-L3500 and its return value is an empty dictionary. This causes the `kv_cache_spec_one_worker` variable at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/feaf202e93a18228cd34ae2e6698aece83a15e87/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L192-L197 to be empty. The `get_kv_cache_config` function uses the `unify_hybrid_kv_cache_specs` method to check the type consistency of the `kv_cache_spec` list. However, in the function at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/feaf202e93a18228cd34ae2e6698aece83a15e87/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L747-L765
there is no empty check for the value of kv_cache_spec, which leads to the IndexError reported in #24407. This PR fixes the error by adding a empty check.

> Additionally, I discovered that when running encoder models, the `GPUModelRunner.initialize_kv_cache` method reassigns the spec of `kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups` to `EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec` https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/feaf202e93a18228cd34ae2e6698aece83a15e87/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L3416-L3441
An alternative fix might be to add the encoder model's `kv_cache_spec` as `EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec` in the `GPUModelRunner.get_kv_cache_spec` method, thereby avoiding returning an empty dict.

## Purpose
resolve #24407

## Test Plan
```python
from argparse import Namespace

from vllm import LLM, EngineArgs
from vllm.utils import FlexibleArgumentParser


def parse_args():
    parser = FlexibleArgumentParser()
    parser = EngineArgs.add_cli_args(parser)
    # Set example specific arguments
    parser.set_defaults(
        model="BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", task="score", enforce_eager=True, disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=True
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


def main(args: Namespace):
    # Sample prompts.
    text_1 = "What is your favourite fruit?"
    texts_2 = [
        "Banana.",
        "Apple.",
    ]

    # Create an LLM.
    # You should pass task="score" for cross-encoder models
    llm = LLM(**vars(args))

    # Generate scores. The output is a list of ScoringRequestOutputs.
    outputs = llm.score(text_1, texts_2)

    # Print the outputs.
    print("\nGenerated Outputs:\n" + "-" * 60)
    for text_2, output in zip(texts_2, outputs):
        score = output.outputs.score
        print(f"Pair: {[text_1, text_2]!r} \nScore: {score}")
        print("-" * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()
    main(args)
```
Observe: No crash, valid scores returned.

## Test Result
Before: Server crashes with IndexError in is_kv_cache_type_uniform.
After: No crash, rerank results returned successfully.

title: [Bug] [Spec Decode] Fix model_initialization test and mismatch in aux_hidden_layers
author: wwl2755
body:
1. Fix the bug of model_initialization. The model should be initializated by a target model which is different from the `speculative_model`.

2. After changing to the correct target model, I faced another error which is because of the dfferent shape in `hidden_states + residual`

Root cause is the `num_layers` is initialized to 1 in the test (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.10.2rc1/tests/models/utils.py#L387). However, the aux_hidden_layer is determine as `(2, num_layers // 2, num_layers - 3)`. (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.10.2rc1/tests/models/utils.py#L387)

```
# In the test: 
DEBUG: self.aux_hidden_state_layers: (2, 0, -2)

# It is supposed to be:
DEBUG: self.aux_hidden_state_layers: (2, 20, 37)
```
So, before this PR, it will treat the layer-0 as the aux-layer and entering the code path of `hidden_states + residual` (where hidden_states is a tensor and residual is None). 

Solution: we set some of the eagle3 models to have the original number of layers. 

cc: @DarkLight1337 @WoosukKwon @LiuXiaoxuanPKU @22quinn @benchislett

title: Fix implementation divergence for BLOOM models between vLLM and HuggingFace when using prompt embeds
author: qthequartermasterman
body:
## Purpose

The HF implementation of Bloom models assumes that `inputs_embeds` do not have the word embedding layer norm pre-applied. So doing `PretrainedModel.get_input_embeddings()(token_ids)` and vLLM's `BloomModel.get_input_embeddings(token_ids)` will give different embeddings. This divergence causes downstream differences in the model forward when passing in prompt embeds.

This is the relevant portion in the HF source code: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/cf084f5b40e19b5a5f946cee75bead6d4247b071/src/transformers/models/bloom/modeling_bloom.py#L545-L562

This was not caught by the prompt embeds tests because the prompt embeds `common_models.py::test_models` test for `bigscience/bloom-560m` only ran in the v1 engine, and prompt embeds inputs were tested only if the v0 engine was active.

## Test Plan

1.  Update `common_models.py::test_models` to test with `use_prompt_embeds` as both True and False (parametrize the tests). Because since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/17615, when needing prompt embeds support, the test will automatically fall back to the v0 engine for prompt embeds tests, until https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24278 lands.

## Test Result

Newly updated tests failed before patching the Bloom model definition, and pass now that the Bloom definition is updated.

title: [Perf] Fix DeepGEMM Contiguous Layout Issue, 5.5% Throughput Improvement
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

We call `get_col_major_tma_aligned_tensor` to get an aligned col-major tensor, but unexpectedly call `contiguous()` and convert it to row major, which causes a lot of perf overhead during runtime.

This PR fixes the issue

`VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 --load-format dummy --input-len 1000 --output-len 100 --trust_remote_code --enable-expert-parallel`

title: [Bugfix] Fix accuracy issue for silu_mul + nvfp4 quant fusion kernel
author: elvischenv
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose
- Fix accuracy issue for silu_mul + nvfp4 quant fusion kernel
  - In previous #23671, the original author used an approximate way to compute silu. The sigmoid was computed by `tanh(x/2) * 0.5 + 0.5`, while the standard definition should be `1 / (1 + e^(-x))`.
  - **We didn't observe the accuracy issues previously by offline lm_eval evaluation. see #23671. However, when doing online lm_eval, the accuracy is dropped slightly.**
  - We fixed the issue by using a standard implementation to compute silu_mul.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/567939953b7a9cb0ded6bf0bb21a76917b8fed97/csrc/quantization/fp4/activation_nvfp4_quant_fusion_kernels.cu#L34-L54

- Do some cleanups for `activation_nvfp4_quant_fusion_kernels.cu`. We don't need an extra `silu_and_cvt_warp_fp16_to_fp4` but just `compute_silu_mul` + `cvt_warp_fp16_to_fp4`(reuse from the nvfp4_utils).
- There were only 3 tests covered the silu_mul + quant fusion in `test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py`. Improved the test coverage.
- Clean up the kernel test `test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`. Removed lots of unnecessary components.

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] - Fix Conv State Kernel FP32 Support
author: Josephasafg
body:
## Purpose
There was a bug in the FP32 support recently added to mamba conv state where if you pass this arg `--mamba-cache-dtype "float32"` you'd get this error:

```bash
E       triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 102:8:
E           w_base = w_ptr + (idx_feats * stride_w_dim)  # [BLOCK_N,]
E
E           # Does 2 things:
E           # 1. READ prior-block init-state data - [done by every Triton programs]
E           # 2. update conv_state with new data [only by the Triton program handles chunk_offset=0]
E           if chunk_offset == 0:
E               # read from conv_states
E               load_init_state = False
E               if HAS_INITIAL_STATES:  # the new HAS_INITIAL_STATES
E                   load_init_state = tl.load(has_initial_states_ptr + idx_seq).to(
E                       tl.int1)
E               if load_init_state:
E               ^
E       AssertionError("Mismatched type for col0 between then block (<['256'], fp32>) and else block (<['256'], bf16>)")

The kernel needed to cast the input type to be the same as conv state.

Use threadIdx.x to select the correct mask at runtime.

This change follows a [patch to SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9620) for the same kernel.

title: Fix: Add explicit #include <omp.h> for OpenMP compatibility on certain toolchains
author: ihb2032
body:
## Purpose

This PR fixes a compilation failure on native RISC-V platforms when using certain newer, yet incompletely configured, GCC toolchains.

The build would fail with errors like `error: ‘omp_get_max_threads’ was not declared in this scope` in C++ source files that use the OpenMP API.

The root cause was traced to a specific build environment:

  * **Platform:** sg2044
  * **OS:** EulixOS 3.0
  * **Toolchain:** A custom GCC 15.1 compiler was required to get RVV support. However, this toolchain had an incomplete OpenMP configuration, which prevented CMake's `FindOpenMP` module from working correctly.
  * **Symptom:** Although the `-fopenmp` flag was correctly passed to the compiler, the necessary `<omp.h>` header was not automatically included, leading to undeclared function errors.

This PR resolves the issue by explicitly adding `#include <omp.h>` to the C++ source files that directly call OpenMP functions (`csrc/cpu/attention.cpp`, `csrc/cpu/utils.cpp`, `csrc/cpu/mla_decode.cpp`). This makes the build process more robust and less reliant on a perfectly configured compiler environment, enhancing portability for emerging and non-standard platforms like RISC-V.

## Test Plan

The test plan consists of successfully compiling the vLLM project from source in the specific environment where it previously failed.

**Test Environment:**

  * **Platform:** sg2044
  * **Python Environment:** Python 3.11 in a virtual environment.
  * **Compiler:** Custom GCC 15.1 located at `/opt/gcc-15.1/`.
  * **Core Dependency:** PyTorch was successfully compiled from source using the *exact same* GCC 15.1 toolchain to ensure ABI compatibility.

**Test Command:**
The following complete environment setup and build command was used:

```bash
source /AI/hebo/.venv/bin/activate
export CC=/opt/gcc-15.1/bin/gcc
export CXX=/opt/gcc-15.1/bin/g++
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/gcc-15.1/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export CFLAGS="--sysroot=/"
export CXXFLAGS="--sysroot=/"
export LDFLAGS="--sysroot=/"
pip install --no-build-isolation -v -e .
```

## Test Result

**Before this PR:**

title: Enable symmetric memory all reduce by default only enabling for TP
author: ilmarkov
body:
## Purpose
Enable torch symm mem by default and fix DataParallel crash. Enable torch symm mem only for TP communicator.

<details>
<summary>Conflict with DataParallel</summary>

In DataParallel we have multiple workers that are assigned to the same set of devices in their environment (with different CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES). 

In case of DP communicator, we have wrong local_rank:rank mapping, e.g.
`unique_name: dp:0, device: cuda:0, rank: 1, world_size: 2`.

In case of EP communicator in DP setup we have two workers with the same device a different ranks within group:

```
unique_name: ep:0, device: cuda:0, rank: 0, world_size: 4                                                                                                                                                 
unique_name: ep:0, device: cuda:0, rank: 2, world_size: 4
```

So in following line, we basically use the same `self.device` in the same group. That makes torch [here](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/f8d379d29ed093b5f19875de0e33ec007bc3ae9d/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/CUDASymmetricMemory.cu#L460) think that we overlap devices, although the allocated tensors are in different environment. Torch symm mem fails to do rendevouz in this setup so we basically can not use symm mem
with DataParallel. This PR only avoids the crash. 

```
         self.buffer = torch_symm_mem.empty(
            self.max_size // self.dtype.itemsize,
            device=self.device,
            dtype=self.dtype,
        )
```
</details>

Fixes #24694.


## Test Plan
Added test to `test_symm_mem_allreduce.py`
## Test Result
Passed test

title: [Bug] Fix torch Compilation Cache Hit Error
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/24915

The root cause of this issue is from `(runtime_shape, graph_index, backend_name)` is not a strong enough cache key for compiled cuda graph. And in complicated situation like DeepEP HT, we split the piecewise graph `moe_forward` and `moe_forward_shared` and make the wrong cache hit.

I am not sure if it is a good idea to refactor the cache key system throughly just for the support of piecewise graph for HT (Perhaps not worth enough), so simply cancel the support for HT graph now. If we encounter other scenarios where the cache key proves insufficient, we should revisit and redesign the cache system.

Note: The rough idea to refactor the cache system: Adding a fourth key introducing the signature of sub_graph like. Works good locally

```bash
def compute_subgraph_signature(graph: fx.GraphModule) -> str:
    parts: list[str] = []
    for node in graph.graph.nodes:
        parts.append(f"{node.op}:{str(node.target)}")
    sig = "|".join(parts)
    return hashlib.md5(sig.encode(), usedforsecurity=False).hexdigest()[:16]
```

title: [BugFix] Fix async scheduling CPU tensor race take 2
author: njhill
body:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24527 intended to address an async scheduling race condition but the scope of the synchronized section wasn't large enough. Reused CPU tensors are also modified and copied async to GPU from within `_update_states()` (in particular sampling tensors).

The synchronization is needed to guarantee that these copies have completed before we begin to modify the same tensors in the subsequent step.

I also made this into a context manager to make the changes in `execute_model` a bit cleaner.

I will benchmark as it's possible this has a minor negative effect on performance. But it's needed for correctness regardless. I'm working on a follow-on change to optimize this.

title: [Bugfix] Fix `vllm bench ...` on CPU-only head nodes
author: Aydin-ab
body:
Ensures the benchmark CLI works when using ray clusters with a CPU-only head node

## Purpose

Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/23967 :  `vllm bench serve` fails on CPU-only head nodes with “Failed to infer device type.”

### Cause

* Running `vllm bench *` initializes all subcommands, including the `serve` CLI parser.
* During the `serve` CLI parser init, the platform is lazily set and on CPU-only head nodes, it resolves to [`UnspecifiedPlatform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a3ae45a38cb0ee920427e3f2db2a237afd557fd8/vllm/platforms/__init__.py#L219).
* A later device check reads an empty `device_type` and raises the ['Failed to infer device type` error](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/48ecb4438b2845f757edf228c5455ca6095938af/vllm/config/__init__.py#L127).

### Solution

* For `vllm bench *` commands, switch `UnspecifiedPlatform` to `CpuPlatform`. That command is just a client simulation that sends requests; it doesn’t launch models, so the platform shouldn't matter anyway.
* This yields `device_type="cpu"` and avoids the inference error.

Now you can run the benchmarking with a CPU-only head node with:
```
vllm bench serve \
  --model ...
  ...
```

Note: our previous workaround was using the benchmarking script at [benchmark_serving.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/48ecb4438b2845f757edf228c5455ca6095938af/benchmarks/benchmark_serving.py) but this seems to be quickly deprecated.

title: [Bug] Fix Long Context OOM Issue
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

Context from @smarterclayton 

>Trying to test a very long context response - 128k input, 1 output token.  I used DeepSeek-V3.1 and changed --max-model-len (although deepseek v3.1 is 128k automatically).
>When I try to run a single request I'm getting an OOM:

```bash
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=948) ERROR 09-16 14:10:49 [v1/engine/core.py:720] torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 4.12 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 178.35 GiB of which 3.91 GiB is free. Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 174.41 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 154.86 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 3.79 GiB allocated in private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 1.95 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation.  See documentation for Memory Management  (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda.html#environment-variables)
```
>I had 53GB for KVcache per GPU on this DP=16 2 node B200 config.

The main reason is we allocated too much mem for MLA chunk padding, this PR fixes the issue.

Note: As the comments said, 

```bash
# For long-context models try not to over-allocate limiting
            # kv-cache space, limiting it to 64k tokens,
            # which would result in the workspace being:
            #   2*(576)*(64*1024) = 144mb
            # (assuming 576 MLA head dim, and fp16)
            # which would result in up-projected context being
            #   2*(192*128)*(64*1024) = 3gb
            # (assuming 192 QK head dim, 128 heads, and fp16)
```

We should assign `64 * 1024` instead of `128 * 1024` here as well, so this PR also fixes the consistency between comments and code.

**The OOM issue is reasonable if we have even more context length using limited GPU memory, considering add `tp` or reduce --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 to a smaller number when OOM. **

title: [BugFix] Fix OOM in vLLM replicas by ensuring consistent NCCL memory accounting
author: kouroshHakha
body:
## Description

This PR fixes an Out of Memory (OOM) issue that occurs inconsistently when deploying multiple vLLM replicas with ray distributed backend (not sure if the ray backend is part of the cause). The problem manifests as some replicas failing with insufficient KV cache memory while others work fine, despite identical configurations.

### Root Cause

This is a viable hypothesis. The issue seem to stem from a race condition in the `init_device()` method of the GPU worker:

1. **Threading Issue**: When using Ray Compiled DAG, model execution happens on background threads, but memory snapshots were taken on the main thread
2. **NCCL Initialization Timing**: NCCL buffers (~4.5 GiB for tensor parallelism) were allocated after the memory snapshot in some cases, leading to inconsistent memory measurements. The NCCL buffer allocation shows up as non-torch memory increase during forward pass. 
3. **Inconsistent Behavior**: Replicas would sometimes see 78.59 GiB free memory (before NCCL init) and sometimes 74.07 GiB (after NCCL init), causing the KV cache calculation to fail

### Solution

The fix reorders the initialization sequence to ensure NCCL is fully initialized before taking memory snapshots:

1. **Move NCCL Initialization First**: `init_worker_distributed_environment()` now runs before memory measurement
2. **Force NCCL Initialization**: Added a dummy `all_reduce` operation for tensor parallelism to ensure NCCL buffers are allocated on the correct thread (Note this is already done as part of [pynccl communicator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl.py#L104-L107) init)
3. **Consistent Memory Accounting**: Memory snapshots now always include NCCL overhead, providing accurate KV cache calculations

### Code Changes

```python
# Before: Memory snapshot taken before NCCL init
self.init_snapshot = MemorySnapshot()
init_worker_distributed_environment(...)

# After: NCCL init first, then memory snapshot
init_worker_distributed_environment(...)
self.init_snapshot = MemorySnapshot()
```

### Testing

I have added unittests that makes sure the distributed group is called before the memory snapshot. However, besides this, here is what the snapshots look before and after this PR for Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, TP=2 on 4xL4 machines. The diff is small but still visible.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeekV31ToolParser to correctly parse multiple tools in non-streaming output
author: taohui
body:
…ming output

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

### Problem
In non-streaming output mode, `DeepSeekV31ToolParser` fails to correctly parse multiple tool calls. 
For example, given the input:

<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>get_current_time<｜tool▁sep｜>{}<｜tool▁call▁end｜>
<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>big_number_add<｜tool▁sep｜>{"a": 923, "b": 24922}<｜tool▁call▁end｜>

The parser incorrectly extracts:

- function_name: "get_current_time<｜tool▁sep｜>{}<｜tool▁call▁end｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>big_number_add"
- function_arguments: '{"a": 923, "b": 24922}'

This merges two separate tool calls into one, breaking downstream processing.

### Solution
- Update the regex and parsing logic to correctly identify each `<｜tool▁call▁begin｜> ... <｜tool▁call▁end｜>` block independently.
- Ensure that each tool call is parsed into its own `function_name` and `function_arguments`, even when multiple tools appear consecutively.

### Result
Now, the same input correctly parses into:

1. function_name: "get_current_time", arguments: {}
2. function_name: "big_number_add", arguments: {"a": 923, "b": 24922}

## Test Plan
I have added test cases in `test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py` specifically covering the issue described above. 
The tests verify that multiple tool calls in non-streaming output are parsed correctly, 
ensuring each tool's function name and arguments are extracted independently.

body: ## Purpose On current main branch, when using MTP with Qwen3-Next, I found that there were some puzzlingly long sections of the forward pass: If you zoom into the first CUDA call after the pause you can see its cuModuleLoadData followed by the kernel in this PR: To me this signaled that triton was JIT compiling a new kernel for a special case of the parameters that it hadn't encountered before (i.e. specialization). This PR resolves this problem by removing some of the parameters from compile-time, and therefore reducing the amount of specialization triton introduces. After this PR I no longer see any bubbles like the one shown in the picture above. Additionally, the num_warps for this kernel was hard coded to 1, which I confirmed with the FLA developers on their discord is not necessary for the kernel. Limiting the number of threads to 32 was likely limiting the throughput this kernel could achieve. I kept the `num_stages=3` because I don't have understanding of what that impacts. Though since this kernel doesn't use shared memory, it can likely be removed? ## Benchmark results These benchmarks are done on a 4xB200 node. server: ``` rm -rf ~/.cache/vllm rm -rf ~/.triton/cache vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct -tp 4 --tokenizer-mode auto --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_next_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' --no-enable-chunked-prefill ``` Bench command: ``` vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random --random-input 2048 --random-output 1024 --max-concurrency 256 title: [BugFix] Potential Fix for FA3 full-cudagraph IMA
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
@WoosukKwon reported an IMA with FA3 full-CG that was fixed by doing https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/compare/woosuk/fa3-ima?expand=1

the theory here is that `get_scheduler_metadata` was being called with a different `max_num_splits` than what was being passed to `FlashAttentionMetadata`

this is an alternative solution that doesn't lose the logic to use `max_num_splits=0` (i.e. use the heuristic) for batches larger then `max_cudagraph_size`

we do not currently have a repo so cannot confirm this resolves @WoosukKwon 's IMA but this should be resolved regardless; we should alway make sure the arguments to `get_scheduler_metadata` and `FlashAttentionMetadata` are inline
