title: [Bugfix] Fix grouped_topk pytorch impl when num_experts can't be grouped properly
author: divakar-amd
body:
This pull request adds a safeguard to the `grouped_topk` function in `fused_moe.py` to ensure correct behavior when the number of experts does not meet the requirements for grouped top-k computation. If the conditions are not met, the function now logs a warning and falls back to the standard top-k computation.

    - "n_group": 8,

title: [NIXL][Bugfix] Fix NIXL/RDMA registration failure over CuMemAllocator
author: Somoku
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose

During the implementation of my NIXL-based weight transfer engine for RL, I found that the NIXL memory registration progress will fail if I turn on `enable_sleep_mode` option. Specifically, it reports `ibv_reg_mr() failed: Bad address` inside UCX. As mentioned in [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#351](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/351#issuecomment-2888725354), the root cause is that the CuMemAllocator for model weights and KVCache provides virtual addresses for RDMA, but RDMA requires physical addresses.

This PR fix this issue by allocating cuMem memory with RDMA flag to support GPUDirect RDMA.

BTW, I'm new to vLLM community, please let me know if any further requirement for this PR.

Related reference:
[kvcache-ai/Mooncake#351](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/351)
[pytorch/pytorch#153688](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/153688)
[pytorch/pytorch#153261](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/153261)

## Test Plan

Tested by running the model with external NIXL agents for `enable_sleep_mode` on and off scenarios, where the NIXL agents will register the weight tensors through `register_memory` API.
## Test Result

The memory registration progress will pass without "Bad Address" or NIXL_ERR_BACKEND errors.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix CPU KV cache fallback memory allocation
author: gausah01
body:
##Description

Fixes #29233

## Purpose

This PR fixes the CPU backend’s KV-cache default memory allocation logic.

Previously, when `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE` was not set, the CPU backend defaulted to a hard-coded 4 GiB KV-cache size. This behavior was problematic for large-context models (e.g., Qwen3-0.6B with `max_model_len=40960`), leading to initialization failures even on machines with large amounts of available RAM. 

This PR aligns CPU behavior with GPU's fallback logic:  
- If `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE` **is set**, we honor it as a manual override.  
- If it **is not set**, we automatically derive the KV-cache size from
  available system RAM (e.g., 50% of `psutil.virtual_memory().available`),
  removing the previous 4 GiB limitation.


## Test Plan

**1. Verify fallback behavior**

unset VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE
vllm bench throughput --input_len 32

**2. Verify setting manually VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE
export VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=64
vllm bench throughput --input_len 32

## Test Result

- Original behavior: failure due to 4.38 GiB > 4.00 GiB KV-cache requirement
- Fixed behavior: KV-cache automatically sized to ~92 GiB (50% of ~185 GiB free RAM)

title: [Bugfix] Fix prefix_repetition routing in bench throughput
author: jr-shen
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Fix a bug in `vllm bench throughput` where `--dataset-name prefix_repetition` is incorrectly routed to `RandomDataset` when `--dataset-path` is not provided, due to:

```python
if args.dataset_path is None or args.dataset_name == "random":
    ...
    dataset_cls = RandomDataset
```

This causes prefix-repetition benchmarks to ignore `--prefix-repetition-*` arguments and fall back to random dataset defaults (e.g. input-len=1024, output-len=128). 

The fix makes prefix_repetition explicitly use `PrefixRepetitionRandomDataset` with its own CLI args, and only uses `RandomDataset` for true random/default cases.

## Test Plan

1. prefix_repetition dataset

```bash
vllm bench throughput \
  --model facebook/opt-125m \
  --backend vllm \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 60 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 40 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 1 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 1 \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --num-prompts 1 \
  --dtype float16 \

```

## Problem

When no match found, the loop incremented `start_idx` but `_find_matches()` used `prev_end_idx` (unchanged), re-scanning the entire prompt each iteration.

Exit loop when no matches remain instead of incrementing uselessly.

## Impact
- InternVL: 2.6s → <10ms for 5k tokens
- Models using token-based matching (Qwen3-VL) unaffected

title: [Bugfix] Suppress non-TTY color output on the process name part of the log
author: a4lg
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose

Regular logs are not decorated with colors when non-TTY stdout/stderr is selected as logging output (c.f. `_use_color` function in `vllm/logger.py`).  However, process-based decoration part in `vllm/utils/system_utils.py` did not implement color output suppression as the regular logger.

It resulted in excess escape sequences in a redirected output (e.g. `log.txt` after running `vllm serve ... >log.txt 2>&1`) when all conditions are met:

1.  Neither `NO_COLOR` nor `VLLM_LOGGING_COLOR` prohibit decoration with colors,
2.  The output is non-TTY stdout/stderr and
3.  The environment variable `VLLM_LOGGING_COLOR` is not `1` (if this is unsatisfied, decorating with colors is mandatory and we cannot call some ineffective escape sequences *excess*; particularly useful with `less -R`).

This commit fixes this issue by implementing the same logic as the regular logger.

Related: #29017

## Test Plan

Sorry, no new `pytest` test case because:

1.  The change is too simple and
2.  Testing the log seems trickier than I first initially thought.

On many Linux environment, you can manually test this behavior by running:

```sh
# 1.  TTY stdout/stderr (color decorations are acceptable)
vllm serve [OPTIONS]
# 2.  non-TTY stdout/stderr (shall not be decorated with colors)
vllm serve [OPTIONS] |& tee /dev/null
```

By using the `tee` command and a pipe (on the second invocation), both stdout/stderr (now redirected as `tee`'s stdout) are now non-TTY and decoration with colors shall be suppressed.

## Test Result

With this commit, process decorating logs like `(APIServer pid=xxxx)` are no longer decorated with colors on non-TTY stdout/stderr.

title: [XPU] Fix AWQ skipped layer detection in IPEX quantization
author: faaany
body:
## Purpose
When running Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-AWQ on XPU with Tensor Parallelism (TP=4), the engine failed to start with the following error:
```bash
ValueError: The input size is not aligned with the quantized weight shape. This can be caused by too large tensor parallel size.
```
This occurred because the visual encoder layers (e.g., visual.blocks.0.attn.proj) were not being identified as skipped layers. The IPEXConfig, which performs an exact string match, still uses the old logic, resulting in a validation error.

Analog to PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/27416 , we need to add skip_with_substr=True to IPEXConfig.

title: [BugFix] Fix index error in ngram_proposer
author: usberkeley
body:
## Purpose
There is an index variable usage error in the `batch_propose_numba` function. The code incorrectly uses the loop index `i` to write to the `valid_ngram_num_drafts` and `valid_ngram_draft` arrays, when it should use the actual request index `idx`.

- **Incorrect behavior**: When `valid_ngram_requests` contains non-contiguous indices (e.g., only requests 0 and 2 need ngram proposals), results will be written to incorrect positions
- **Data corruption**: May cause draft tokens from some requests to be incorrectly written to other requests' positions, or completely lost
- **Severity**: This is a serious bug that affects correctness in batch processing scenarios with non-contiguous request indices

## Test Plan
Add test case `test_ngram_proposer` for non-contiguous index scenarios:
- When requests 0 and 2 need proposals, and request 1 is in prefill
- The internal arrays `valid_ngram_num_drafts` and `valid_ngram_draft` are correctly written to the corresponding request index positions

title: [CI] fix url-encoding behavior in nightly metadata generation
author: Harry-Chen
body:
## Purpose

After #29690 is merged, nightly index and metadata can be generated as expected, but the `metadata.json` generated will cause HTTP 404 errors when `setup.py` tries to download pre-compiled wheel from S3 with URLs like `https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/vllm/../../36db0a35e45f32f7c37f6f1967dc8d6ff301d882/vllm-0.11.2.dev428+g36db0a35e-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_31_x86_64.whl`.

This is due to AWS S3 encoding filenames [at its discretion](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/21067141/amazon-s3-url-encoding), where the `+` in the filename will become `%2B`. This encoding must be handled on index generation (but not `setup.py`), because `metadata.json` should contain the final path for any client (e.g. `setup.py`) to consume.

title: Fix some more Transformers nightly tests
author: hmellor
body:
- `MiDashengLMModel`, `GteModel` - explicitly sets `rope_scaling=None` in their checkpoints (which gets forwarded to `rope_parameters` in Transformers v5) so `hasattr(config, "rope_parameters")` was not sufficient
- `Mamba2ForCausalLM`, `MistralForCausalLM`, `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`, `PixtralForConditionalGeneration` - `MistralCommonTokenizer` was renamed `MistralCommonBackend` so this PR updates `vllm/tokenizer/mistral.py` to get it from the new location, falling back to the old location for Transformers v4

---

Tarsier2 gets its own section because it's very weird:

The `config.json` is written in an unexpected way, causing the class structure of the initialised config to be:

- `config - LlavaConfig`
  - `text_config` - `Qwen2VLConfig`
    - `text_config` - `Qwen2VLTextConfig`
    - `vision_config` - `Qwen2VLVisionConfig`
  - `vision_config` - `Qwen2VLConfig`
    - `text_config` - `Qwen2VLTextConfig`
    - `vision_config` - `Qwen2VLVisionConfig`

In Transformers v4 this is a problem because accessing attributes directly from `Qwen2VLConfig` will fetch them from the `Qwen2VLTextConfig` instead. So if we access `config.vision_config.num_heads` the returned value will actually come from `config.vision_config.text_config.num_heads`. 

In Transformers v5 this `__getattr__` behaviour is no longer present, so this cannot happen.

---

Also adds some error messages to bare `assert`s so they're actually informative.

title: [bugfix] fix MiniMaxM2ReasoningParser streaming output not separating reasoning_content.
author: JaviS-Rei
body:
## Summary

Fix `minimax_m2` reasoning parser not separating `content` and `reasoning_content` in streaming mode.

## Problem

MiniMax-M2 models don't generate `<think>` start token, only `</think>` end token. The base class `BaseThinkingReasoningParser.extract_reasoning_streaming` assumes the model generates both tokens, so when `<think>` is missing, all output is incorrectly placed in `content` field instead of `reasoning_content`.

Non-streaming mode worked correctly because `extract_reasoning` already handled this case.

## Solution

Override `extract_reasoning_streaming` in `MiniMaxM2ReasoningParser` to assume all content is reasoning until `</think>` is encountered, matching the non-streaming behavior.

## Purpose
Fix [issue#28852](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28852).

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix v1/logits_processors failure on ROCm
author: micah-wil
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
Without this PR, we are seeing failures on ROCm in `pytest -v -s v1/logits_processors` (part of the "V1 Test others" test group) with the following error:

```
pytest -v -s v1/logits_processors

(EngineCore_DP0 pid=632406)   File "/projects/vllm/vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/__init__.py", line 141, in _load_logitsprocs_by_fqcns
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=632406)     raise RuntimeError(
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=632406) RuntimeError: Failed to load 0th LogitsProcessor plugin DummyModule:DummyLogitsProcessor

...

========================================================================================================================= short test summary info =========================================================================================================================
ERROR v1/logits_processors/test_custom_online.py::test_custom_logitsprocs[server1-facebook/opt-125m] - RuntimeError: Server exited unexpectedly.
ERROR v1/logits_processors/test_custom_online.py::test_invalid_custom_logitsproc_arg[server1-facebook/opt-125m] - RuntimeError: Server exited unexpectedly.
========================================================================================================== 23 passed, 6 warnings, 2 errors in 209.37s (0:03:29) ==========================================================================================================
```
The problem is ultimately caused by using this sys modules patch `sys.modules[DUMMY_LOGITPROC_MODULE] = dummy_module` in a spawned subprocess as opposed to forked. With spawn, child processes apparently don't inherit `sys.modules` patches. ROCm forces spawned multiprocessing because without it you get errors like `RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess`. That issue doesn't occur on CUDA which is why the above error is not observed on NVIDIA machines (the test uses forked multiprocessing on NVIDIA machines). I've observed that most vllm imports trigger CUDA initialization on ROCm systems, but not on NVIDIA. which is ultimately why that error mentions re-initializing CUDA in a forked subprocess. 

My solution is to use an importable module so that we don't have to rely on sys.modules patching at all. I hope this upholds the integrity of the test and correctly tests the "fully-qualified class name (FQCN)" functionality.

title: [CI] fix docker image build by specifying merge-base commit id when downloading pre-compiled wheels
author: Harry-Chen
body:
## Purpose

Currently the docker image building stage in CI will try to download prebuilt wheels from the latest HEAD commit on the main branch:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/506ed87e876e9dca3c64ac83e21051c02e9cb2e3/setup.py#L512-L514

However, this might lead to 404 error when the main branch is too new (e.g. it taks ~30min to build a wheel), especially when PR author rebases it to the latest main.

Before PR #29838 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/4b612664fdfb4e87af6684403872d83ac04fa496) was merged, the wheel downloading mechanism in `setup.py` will fallback to `/nightly/` if 404 occurrs:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7c1ed45848890a06693d36d372d8e8e50cdc9593/setup.py#L674-L680

This was not safe, because `/nightly/` might be newer than the merge-base of the current PR, and have native code changes, causing their `.so` files to change.

This PR passes the merge base commit to the Docker build process (and Python-only build test) in CI, so it could download the correct wheels. The `VLLM_MERGE_BASE_COMMIT` is provided by buildkite bootstrap script in vllm/ci-infra repo.

title: [Bugfix] Fix parse_output_message crash on commentary with no recipient
author: strinczer
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #24170 

Resolves `ValueError: Unknown recipient: None` crash in `harmony_utils.py` when gpt-oss models generate commentary channel preambles (explanatory text before tool calls) without a specific recipient.

**Root Cause**: 
Per [Harmony format docs](https://cookbook.openai.com/articles/openai-harmony), the commentary channel can contain "preambles to calling multiple functions." When instructions prompt the model to generate explanation text alongside tool calls, gpt-oss-120b generates these preambles in the commentary channel with `recipient=None` (since they're not addressing a specific function). The parser crashed because it only handled commentary with specific recipients like `functions.X`, `python`, `browser`, or `container`.

**Impact**: 
Stream terminates prematurely after successfully sending reasoning chunks, never sending `response.completed`. Clients see "Premature end of chunk coded message body: closing chunk expected."

## Solution

Modified `parse_output_message()` in `vllm/entrypoints/harmony_utils.py` to handle `recipient=None` in commentary channel by treating it as reasoning text (semantically correct since preambles are explanatory content).

**Code Change**:
```python
elif message.channel == "commentary":
    if recipient is not None and recipient.startswith("functions."):
        # ... create function call ...
    elif recipient is None or (  # ← Added recipient is None
        recipient.startswith("python")
        or recipient.startswith("browser")
        or recipient.startswith("container")
    ):
        # ... create reasoning item ...
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown recipient: {recipient}")
```

## Test Plan

**Reproduction (FAILS before fix)**:
```bash
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/v1/responses" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    "input": "update my name to bob",
    "instructions": "Today is Thu, 27 Nov 2025.\n\n### Current Application Variables ###\n-------------------------\nThe current state of the application you are operating in is represented by the following variables. A\nvalue of <no_value> indicates that the variable has no current value:\n- name: name, value: carl, type: string\n\n\n### Tool calling protocol - follow exactly ###\n\nSTEP 1: Write explanation text (what you need to accomplish + which tools + why)\nSTEP 2: Make tool calls in the same response\n\nCRITICAL: Text content must be present and contain your explanation when tool calls are present.\nFORBIDDEN: Tool calls without explanatory content.",
    "temperature": 0.0,
    "stream": true,
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "name": "Update_application_variable",
      "description": "Update the value of an application variable.\nYou may update the following variables. Do not attempt to update any other variables.\n - name: name, type: string\n\n",
      "parameters": {
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["variableName", "newValue"],
        "properties": {
          "newValue": {"description": "The new value to set for the variable. Expected format: String", "type": "string"},
          "variableName": {"description": "The name of the variable to update in the application. Expected format: String", "type": "string"}
        }
      }
    }],
    "max_output_tokens": 1024
  }'
```

**Control (WORKS without fix)**:
Same curl but with simplified instructions (no tool calling protocol):
```json
"instructions": "Today is Thu, 27 Nov 2025.\n\n### Current Application Variables ###\n-------------------------\nThe current state of the application you are operating in is represented by the following variables. A\nvalue of <no_value> indicates that the variable has no current value:\n- name: name, value: carl, type: string"
```

**Unit Tests**: Added tests in `test_harmony_utils.py` covering commentary with `recipient=None` and other edge cases.

## Test Result

### Before Fix:
```
event: response.output_item.done
data: {...}

curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining
```

**vLLM Log**:
```
ERROR: recipient=None, type=<class 'NoneType'>, channel=commentary
ValueError: Unknown recipient: None
  at vllm/entrypoints/harmony_utils.py:438
```

### After Fix:
```
event: response.completed
data: {
  "response": {
    "status": "completed",
    "output": [
      {"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"text": "Need to explain then call function..."}]},
      {"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"text": "I will use Update_application_variable..."}]},
      {"type": "function_call", "name": "Update_application_variable", "arguments": "{...}"}
    ],
    "usage": {"reasoning_tokens": 83, "output_tokens": 107}
  }
}
```

✅ Stream completes successfully  
✅ Preambles correctly converted to reasoning items  
✅ Tool call executed properly  
✅ All unit tests pass

---

## Checklist

- [x] Fix issue #24170 - ValueError: Unknown recipient: None
- [x] Test plan: Reproduction curl provided
- [x] Test results: Before/after comparison showing stream now completes
- [x] Unit tests added for commentary channel edge cases

title: [Bugfix]: Fix `TokenizerLike` interface
author: Rohan138
body:
## Purpose

Corrected+rebased version of #22121 to fix #22013. Note that this function is only called from `RandomDataset.sample`, which calls `tokenizer.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/benchmarks/datasets.py#L407). Hence, the tokenizer only adds the bos token; not eos,\<INST\>,\</INST\>.

title: [Bugfix] Fix the issue with interleaved thinking when using streaming
author: chaunceyjiang
body:
## Purpose
Fix the issue with interleaved thinking when using streaming.

```
｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>

## Tools
You have access to a set of tools you can use to answer the user's question.

<think>...thinking about results</think>

The current date is: 2024-09-30<｜User｜> What is the weather like in 
Beijing today? And tomorrow? <｜Assistant｜><think>


```

When the user's prompt contains something like `<think>...</think> ... <think>`, `is_reasoning_end` incorrectly determines that reasoning has already ended. In reality, because the last token is `<think>`, the reasoning has just begun. This causes reasoning to fail to work properly.


Especially in interleaved thinking mode, where the chat_template renders a `<think>...</think> ... <think>` prompt with 100% consistency.

title: [CI] fix silent error in nightly wheel index generation script, add generation time to HTML index
author: Harry-Chen
body:
## Purpose

#30008 introduced a silent error when generating nightly wheel indices. `$PYTHON pip install regex && .buildkite/scripts/generate-nightly-index.py --version "$SUBPATH" --current-objects "$obj_json" --output-dir "$INDICES_OUTPUT_DIR" $alias_arg` is wrong because: (1) it should be `$PYTHON -m pip` (2) the second half is not run with the same python (3) former half failure in `&&` shortcut will not be caught by bash.

So currently the `generate-nightly-index.py` is not run at all, thus no indices are generated. Wheels are uploaded nonetheless. The logs look like:

```text
[2025-12-04T11:26:21Z] + docker run --rm -v /var/lib/buildkite-agent/builds/bk-arm64-cpu-queue-postmerge-i-04192f6325ee0943d-1/vllm/release:/app -w /app python:3-slim python3 pip install regex
[2025-12-04T11:26:21Z] python3: can't open file '/app/pip': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
[2025-12-04T11:26:22Z] + echo 'Uploading indices to s3://vllm-wheels/1b7c7f5159484063af28cb47809d79e83d3301ec/'
[2025-12-04T11:26:22Z] Uploading indices to s3://vllm-wheels/1b7c7f5159484063af28cb47809d79e83d3301ec/
[2025-12-04T11:26:22Z] + aws s3 cp --recursive indices/ s3://vllm-wheels/1b7c7f5159484063af28cb47809d79e83d3301ec/
```

This PR fixes this issue by monkey-patching `regex` back to `re` in that script to both (1) make pre-commit linter happy and (2) get rid of any external dependencies. We are using very simple regexes and do not need the performance brought by `regex` here.

I also added comments in the generated HTML index to clearly specify the generation time and commit.

## Test Plan

title: Fix AWQ MoE marlin check issue in marlin_utils.py for AMD backend
author: yuttian1
body:
### Summary
This PR disables Marlin support for AWQ dense and MoE layers when running on ROCm, preventing the runtime from calling the unavailable `awq_marlin_repack` operator.

### Problem
On ROCm builds, the `vllm._C` extension does not include the `awq_marlin_repack` operator.  
However, both `check_marlin_supports_layer` and `check_moe_marlin_supports_layer` may return `True` for AWQ layers on AMD GPUs.  
This incorrectly enables the Marlin execution path, which leads to:

This error prevents AWQ models — especially AWQ MoE models — from running on AMD GPUs

### Fix
- Detect ROCm by checking `torch.version.hip`.
- If running on ROCm, both `check_marlin_supports_layer` and `check_moe_marlin_supports_layer` now return `False` immediately.
- This forces AWQ dense and MoE layers on ROCm to fall back to the supported non-Marlin kernels.
- CUDA behavior remains unchanged; Marlin continues to be used when supported.

### Impact
- Resolves the `awq_marlin_repack` AttributeError on ROCm.
- Restores AWQ and AWQ-MoE model functionality on AMD hardware.
- No changes to CUDA behavior; no regression in performance or correctness on existing CUDA paths.
- No runtime overhead on ROCm since Marlin kernels were not available there.

### Test Plan
Validated AWQ and AWQ-MoE models on AMD MI300X; error no longer occurs.

### Additional Notes
- This is a minimal compatibility fix for ROCm.  
- Future Marlin support on ROCm can remove this condition as new kernels become available.

Summary:
Fixes circular import error introduced by upstream vLLM PR #29966 which added a module-level import that creates a circular dependency chain which causes the following errors:

This circular import happens because:
```

    → imports from vllm.config.utils
    → requires vllm/config/__init__.py to execute first (Python package rule)
    → which imports from vllm.config.model
    → which imports from vllm.transformers_utils.config
    → DEADLOCK: transformers_utils/config can't finish initializing!
```

title: [Bugfix] fix streaming final output for non harmony
author: penfree
body:
# Summary

  Fixed a bug where the output field in response.completed event was empty when using streaming mode with non-Harmony
  models (e.g., Qwen), even though the streaming delta events contained correct content.

# Problem

  When using the Responses API with stream=True, the streaming events (response.output_text.delta) correctly returned
  text deltas, but the final response.completed event had an empty output array:
```json
  {
    "type": "response.completed",
    "response": {
      "output": [],  // Should contain the message with full text
      "status": "completed"
    }
  }
```

# Root Cause

  In _process_simple_streaming_events, each iteration overwrites context.last_output with only the latest incremental
  output (delta). When responses_full_generator builds the final response, it reads context.last_output.outputs[0].text
  which only contains the last token's text instead of the accumulated full text.

# Fix

  At the end of _process_simple_streaming_events, save the accumulated previous_text and previous_token_ids back to
  context.last_output:
```python
  # Update context.last_output with accumulated text and token_ids
  # so that responses_full_generator can build the correct final response
  if (
      isinstance(context, SimpleContext)
      and context.last_output is not None
      and context.last_output.outputs
  ):
      context.last_output.outputs[0].text = previous_text
      context.last_output.outputs[0].token_ids = tuple(previous_token_ids)
```

# Test Plan

- Added test_streaming_output_consistency unit test that verifies:
  - Concatenated text from all response.output_text.delta events
  - Matches output_text in the final response.completed event
- Manual testing with Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct model confirmed the fix

# Files Changed

- vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py - Bug fix
- tests/entrypoints/openai/test_response_api_simple.py - Added unit test

title: [bugfix][quantization] Fix fp8 per_tensor scale shape
author: haoyangli0109
body:
For fp8 quantization, the [scale.dim()=2 ](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/_custom_ops.py#L1729)returned by pertensor's input quantization causes errors during inference.
The occurrence of this issue is also related to the judgment conditions of pertoken. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/w8a8_utils.py#L477 



Script to Reproduce the Error
```
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

import argparse
prompts = [
    "Hello, my name is",
    "The president of the United States is",
    "The capital of France is",
    "The future of AI is",
]
sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", type=str, default="auto", choices=["auto", "float16", "bfloat16", "float32"], help="Data type for model weights and computation.")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    llm = LLM(model="/mnt/Qwen/Qwen1.5-0.5B",  dtype=args.dtype, tensor_parallel_size=1, enforce_eager=True, quantization="fp8")

    outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params)
    for output in outputs:
        prompt = output.prompt
        generated_text = output.outputs[0].text
        print(f"Prompt: {prompt!r}, Generated text: {generated_text!r}")
```

title: [ROCm][CI][Bugfix] Multi-Modal Model Support Fixes and Attention Backend Improvements
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
This PR addresses several ROCm-specific issues with multi-modal/vision-language models and improves attention backend dispatching for encoder-only self-attention models. It renders green the following test groups on ROCm:
- `Multi-Modal Models Test (Standard)`
- `Multi-Modal Models Test (Extended) 1`
- `Multi-Modal Models Test (Extended) 2`
- `Multi-Modal Models Test (Extended) 3`

#### Key Changes

**Attention Backend Selection (`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`):**
- Added dtype validation (fp16/bf16 only) for Flash Attention backend selection
- Added automatic FlexAttention fallback for `ENCODER_ONLY` attention types
- Implemented `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND` environment variable override mechanism for model-specific backend selection
- Improved logging messages with "V1 engine" suffix for clarity

**Qwen3-VL Support (`vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py`):**
- Added ROCm-specific attention backend override to use `ROCM_AITER_FA` on gfx9 architectures
- Sets `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND` env var to propagate backend choice to platform layer

**Transformers Multimodal Mixin (`vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py`):**
- Force `MATH` SDP backend for vision encoder on ROCm to avoid accuracy issues with `flash_sdp` and `mem_efficient_sdp`
- Patches issue [#30167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/30167)

**SigLIP2 NaViT (`vllm/model_executor/models/siglip2navit.py`):**
- Disabled `vllm_flash_attn` rotary embedding on ROCm

**Test Updates:**
- Moved `conftest.py` up one level to share ROCm SDP workarounds across multimodal tests
- Use `float16` dtype instead of `float` for CLIP/SigLIP pooling tests on ROCm
- Added ROCm-specific processor kwargs for Qwen2.5-VL tests
- Skip MiniMax-VL-01 on ROCm due to GPU OOM and pickle issues with spawn + tp>1
- Modified CI timeouts for multi-modal test suites for precision

**CI Configuration (`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`):**
- Extended timeouts for Multi-Modal Models Test suites (Standard: 100min, Extended 2: 120min, Accuracy Eval: 240min)

title: [Bugfix] Fix compressed-tensors models failing to load with transformers backend
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

The transformers backend's `WeightsMapper` uses a broad prefix mapping (`"" -> "model."`) to transform weight paths. This mapper is also applied to quantization config targets via `apply_vllm_mapper`. However, compressed-tensors targets can be module class names (e.g., `"Linear"`) or regex patterns (e.g., `"re:.*proj"`), not just layer paths.

When `"Linear"` is transformed to `"model.Linear"`, the target matching fails because the module class name check looks for `"Linear"` in `"model.Linear"` (substring match), which fails.

The fix filters which targets get transformed: only layer paths (containing `.` and not starting with `re:`) are mapped. Class names and regex patterns are preserved.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Previously failing, now passing - compressed-tensors with transformers backend
vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8-BLOCK --model-impl transformers

# Verify native backend still works
vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8-BLOCK

# Verify fp8 (non-compressed-tensors) still works with transformers
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 --model-impl transformers
```

title: [CI/Build][AMD] Fix ref_dynamic_per_token_quant reference implementation on ROCm.
author: rasmith
body:
This PR fixes the reference implementation in `ref_dynamic_per_token_quant`.  When on a platform that uses `torch.float8_e4m8fnuz` as its fp8 dtype,  it is necessary to use `-224/224`  for the fp8 min/max values instead of `240.0/240.0` which torch's `finfo` returns.  Using the slightly larger min/max values results in accuracy issues. This was causing a mismatch between the reference and actual implementation which was causing test failures which were false negatives.

All the tests in kernels/quantization/test_int8_quant.py pass with this change.

title: [CI/Build][Kernel][BugFix][AMD] Fix per_token_group_quant_fp8 to use correct fp8 min/max values and update atol/rtol in test_quantfp8_group_functionality
author: rasmith
body: This PR updates per_token_group_quant_fp8 to use `-224.0/224.0` values for fp8 min/max values when the platform uses the `torch.float8_e4m3fnuz` fp8 dtype.  Without this, torch returns `-240.0/240.0` which results in accuracy issues and can result in mismatches between implementations since the `-224.0/224.0` values are returned.  I also modified the `atol/rtol `values in `test_quantfp8_group_functionality `since the failures were just barely out of the range of the original ones.

title: [CI] Fix Flaky test_eagle_max_len Test
author: micah-wil
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
After https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29916 was merged, which fixed the original failure in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py`, we are now noticing that the test is flaky on ROCm. Roughly 15% of the time, I am seeing this when running `pytest -v -s v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py::test_eagle_max_len[ROCM_AITER_FA-3]`:

```
AssertionError: This test is only meaningful if the output is longer than the eagle max length
...
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py::test_eagle_max_len[ROCM_AITER_FA-3] - ...
======================== 1 failed, 6 warnings in 27.39s ========================
```

This occurs when `len(o.prompt_token_ids) + len(o.outputs[0].token_ids) = 200` (the failure mode that I observed multiple times was `len(o.prompt_token_ids) = 50` and `len(o.outputs[0].token_ids) = 150`, which seems to be a valid case that was mistakenly not accounted for). After changing the condition to `len(o.prompt_token_ids) + len(o.outputs[0].token_ids) <= 200`, the test passed 50 times in a row locally. Further, I captured an example of the previously failing case where `len(o.prompt_token_ids) = 50` and `len(o.outputs[0].token_ids) = 150`, and the test passed the final correctness assertion `o.outputs[0].text == "a b c d e " * 15`, showing that it is a valid case and the root cause of the flakiness has been addressed.

Now, I am consistently seeing the following when running the whole test_max_len suite `pytest -v -s v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py`:
```
======================================================= 9 passed, 6 warnings in 170.14s (0:02:50) ====================================================================
```

title: [Model][Quantization] Fix / Add GGUF support for Qwen2 MoE models
author: a4lg
body:
## Purpose

This is a follow-up after #30116 (which unblocks loading Qwen2/3 MoE + GGUF models).

This commit fixes two issues preventing to load Qwen2 MoE + GGUF models:

1.  Initialization of `Qwen2MoeModel.embed_tokens` is fixed to use correct prefix and respect quantization settings.
2.  Added GGUF-specific compatibility layer for `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock.shared_expert_gate` (GGUF: 1D tensor `(n)`, HF/vLLM: 2D tensor `(1, n)`).

The latter was implemented in HF Transformers [as a part of `Qwen2MoeTensorProcessor`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v4.57.3/src/transformers/modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils.py#L110-L113) but since vLLM's weight loader directly uses [`gguf` library](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/gguf-v0.17.1/gguf-py) without such compatibility layer, we need to implement the equivalent.

## Test Plan

You may download a quantized Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat model such as [tensorblock/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/tensorblock/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-GGUF) and run like:

```sh
vllm serve \
	Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-Q4_K_S.gguf \
	--tokenizer Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat \
	--max-model-len 4096 \
	--gpu-memory-utilization 0.5
```

**WARNING:** Qwen2-57B-A14B-Instruct with the same architecture won't work (alone) because a bug in HF Transformers prevents loading non-default parameters.
See #30116 for details (fixed in upcoming V5 by huggingface/transformers#42650 but not sure whether V4 (which vLLM currently depends on) will be fixed the same).

## Test Result

Before this PR, either one of the errors will occur (each corresponds to a fix above):

1.  `KeyError: 'embed_tokens.qweight_type'` (you should normally see this) or
2.  `AssertionError: Attempted to load weight (torch.Size([2048])) into parameter (torch.Size([1, 2048]))`
    (2048 is the value on `Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B{,-Chat}`).

After this PR is applied, these errors will go away and you should be able to use Qwen2 MoE + GGUF models.

title: [Bugfix] Fix HunyuanOCR cross-image contamination in batch processing
author: anker-c2
body:
This fixes a bug where differently sized images in a batch would have their features / chunks mixed.

The fix processes each image independently one by one through the transformer layers by splitting, processing, and concatenating per layer.

Fixes #30342

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose
- Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/30342
- Changes the VisionTransformer such that each image in a bad gets processed independent per Layer
- Done like this instead of implementing a mask like discussed in https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanOCR/issues/60 for simplicity. This way no change to attention needed. 
- Split / merge kept inside loop for consistency, could be moved outside. 

## Test Plan
- Ran the changes on a batch of ~900 independent images. 
- Same isolated environment reproduced the same issue in the same resulting chunks three times. 
- Additional test on a minimal example would be appreciated, since i was not yet able to reproduce the behavior on public files. 

## Test Result
- I was not able to reproduce the issue after the fix. All inspected chunks were extracted as expected / found no loss in precision
- Speed seems to be slightly improved as a bonus in some cases (depending on the batch configuration) since less attention calculations should be required at times

title: [CI/Test] Fix FP8 per-tensor quant test reference scale shape
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Summary

Fixes `test_dynamic_per_tensor_fp8_quant` that was broken by [#30257](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30257). (CI failure: https://buildkite.com/organizations/vllm/pipelines/ci/builds/42664/jobs/019b03c9-8e5a-4fb8-baec-7ba031141cbf/log)

## Issue

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30257 changed `ops.scaled_fp8_quant` to return scale with shape `[1]` instead of `[1, 1]`. However, the test's reference function `ref_dynamic_per_tensor_fp8_quant` was not updated to match, causing all `test_dynamic_per_tensor_fp8_quant` tests to fail with:

```
AssertionError: The values for attribute 'shape' do not match: torch.Size([1, 1]) != torch.Size([1]).
```

## Fix

Updated `ref_dynamic_per_tensor_fp8_quant` in [`tests/kernels/quant_utils.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/tests/kernels/quant_utils.py) to return scale with shape `[1]` instead of `[1, 1]`, matching the new behavior of the ops implementation.

## Testing

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py -v
# 109 passed
```

title: [NIXL][BUG FIX] Fix both failing issue and accuracy issue with nixl + host_buffer on CUDA
author: xuechendi
body:
## Purpose

This PR is fixed upon https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30420
Should get that one merged firstly

Two issue detected and resolved in this PR

1. Fix a bug after #29665 for running PD with cpu host buffer
2. Fix accuracy issue for running PD with cpu host buffer, described in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/30358

## Test Plan

```
PREFILL_BLOCK_SIZE=16 DECODE_BLOCK_SIZE=16 bash tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh --kv_buffer_device cpu
```

Qwen3-0.6B
Before: accuracy is ~0.3
Now: Accuracy is = 0.4109

## Root Cause and proposed change

Previous:

when scheduler call `schedule`, only brand new request will gets `self.connector.update_state_after_alloc`

=> However, if one prefill request is chunked into small request, the `self.connector.update_state_after_alloc` only registered partial of block_ids(first request of the prefill) into nixl_metadata

--

Solution:

Add another call to `self.connector.update_state_after_alloc` at running queue process, so if the following chunked gets scheduled, it will continue to update block_ids to nixl metadata.

title: [ROCm] Fix broken import in platform attention backend dispatching
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Summary
Removes broken dependency on `get_env_variable_attn_backend` from `vllm.attention.selector` in ROCm platform configuration.

## Problem
The import `from vllm.attention.selector import get_env_variable_attn_backend` was causing failures on ROCm. This was used to check for `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` backend selection when setting KV cache block size.

## Fix
Deprecate the `get_env_variable_attn_backend` check and rely on environment variables (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTENTION`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`) directly for block size configuration.

Tracking upstream PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30396 for the proper way to handle attention backend selection going forward.

## Testing
Verified ROCm platform initializes correctly without import errors.

title: [Bug][KVConnector][Metrics] Remove a vacuous assertion breaking external-launcher
author: qierli
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose
Remove a vacuous assertion that breaks external-launcher mode, which is essential to RL on DP use cases.

### Why is this assertion vacuous?
It checks the field _KV_CONNECTOR_AGENT that spans [only in Worker](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1e6b115300b8b3629d10e69db0933246fe3253af/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_transfer_state.py#L67-L71).
But this check is at Scheduler, so serves no purpose at all.

### Why it breaks?
Under external-launcher mode, Engine is created per GPU rank, with one Scheduler and one Worker **within the same process**.

## Test Plan
Existed tests.
The change is a no-op for non external-launcher cases.

## Test Result
No new breakages.

title: [Bugfix][benchmarks] Fix input token calculation for rerank benchmark metrics
author: Flink-ddd
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #30465

This PR fixes a bug where the bench serve tool incorrectly reports 0 for "Total input tokens" and "Total token throughput" when benchmarking Rerank/Embedding models.

**Changes:**
- Updated `calculate_metrics_for_embeddings` to calculate input tokens using the source `input_requests` (ground truth) instead of relying on outputs[i].prompt_len.
- In the rerank backend, outputs often do not populate the prompt length correctly, causing the metrics to default to 0.
- This change aligns the logic with the `calculate_metrics` function (used for Generation tasks), which already uses `input_requests` for accurate token counting.

## Test Plan
I verified the fix by running the benchmark on an NVIDIA RTX A4000 using the `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` model.


Reproduction Command

```
python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
    --model BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 1000 \
    --endpoint /v1/rerank \
    --backend vllm-rerank \
    --dataset-name random-rerank \
    --random-input-len 1024 \
```

author: princepride
body:
## Purpose
Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/29641
1.  **Fix `content: null` on truncation**: The `OpenAIToolParser` (used by default for logic-enabled models) was discarding partial content when the generation stopped mid-way (e.g., hit `max_tokens`). This PR updates `extract_tool_calls` to correctly extract `current_content` from the parser state when the channel is `final` but the message object hasn't been finalized yet.
2.  **Fix Prompt Inconsistency**: `serving_chat.py` was unconditionally appending an empty Developer message to the prompt, whereas `serving_responses.py` only added it if tools were requested https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/64251f48df0ed16fb67f12ece26ab6c7ea730e74/vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py#L1013-L1017. author: drslark
body:
…nferring

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

To solve a bug in Qwen3-Next-MTP which produces a lot of redundant tokens when batched inferring. It is descibed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/30631.

We found this bug in `vllm-ascend`, which is described in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/4930.

We solve it for `vllm-ascend` in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/4932.

FIX https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/30631
## Test Plan

We use the same environment described in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/30631.

Run codes below.

```python
    prompts = [
        "Hello, my name is", 
        "The president of the United States is",
        "The capital of France is", 
        "The future of AI is"
    ]

    sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=40, max_tokens=20)
    llm = LLM(model="/home/model/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct",
              tensor_parallel_size=4,
              enforce_eager=True,
              distributed_executor_backend="mp",
              gpu_memory_utilization=0.7,
              speculative_config={
                  "method": "qwen3_next_mtp",
                  "num_speculative_tokens": 1,
              },
              max_model_len=4096, 
              enable_prefix_caching=False)

    outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params)
    for output in outputs:
        prompt = output.prompt
        generated_text = output.outputs[0].text
        print(f"Prompt: {prompt!r}, Generated text: {generated_text!r}")
```

## Test Result

Before we modified, the outputs are:

```text
Prompt: 'Hello, my name is', Generated text: ' [Your Name], and I am a 20-year-old student from [Your Country]. I'
Prompt: 'The president of the United States is', Generated text: ' 2024 is the president of the United States of America. The president of the United'
Prompt: 'The capital of France is', Generated text: ' the of capital isThe the of capital isThe the of capital isThe the of capital of capital'
Prompt: 'The future of AI is', Generated text: ' the future of the world is in the hands of the people of the world. The future of the'
```

The third conversation has a lot of redundant tokens.

After we modified, the outputs are:

```text
Prompt: 'Hello, my name is', Generated text: ' [Your Name], and I am a 20-year-old student from [Your Country]. I'
Prompt: 'The president of the United States is', Generated text: ' the head of state and head of government of the United States, directing the executive branch of the federal'
Prompt: 'The capital of France is', Generated text: ' Paris. The capital of Germany is Berlin. The capital of Italy is Rome. The capital of Spain'
Prompt: 'The future of AI is', Generated text: ' not just about technology—it’s about people. As AI becomes more integrated into our daily lives, the'
```

We can see the third conversation has no more redundant tokens.

title: [Bugfix] Fix missing first token in tool calls during reasoning-to-tool transition
author: mondaylord
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

This PR refactors the streaming logic in the generation handler to fix an issue where the first token of a tool call could be dropped or set to `None` during the transition from `Reasoning` to `Tool Calling`.

### The Problem
Previously, the logic used a mutually exclusive `if-else` structure:

```
if not reasoning_end_arr[i]:
    # Handle reasoning...
    if is_end: reasoning_end_arr[i] = True
else:
    # Handle tool calls...
```
In streaming scenarios, if the "Reasoning End" token (e.g., `</think>`) appeared in the current iteration, the `reasoning_end_arr` flag was set to `True`, but the else block was skipped for that iteration. This resulted in the immediate next token being generated by the engine but dropped from the streaming response.

### Evidence (Log Analysis)
The following SSE logs demonstrate the issue before the fix. Observe the second chunk: the model generated the token **"Ap"** (visible in `logprobs`), but the `delta.content` was set to null. The next chunk continues with **"ologies"**. Result: The user receives **"ologies"** instead of **"Apologies"**.

```
// 1. Initial chunk
data: {"id": "...", "choices": [{"delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": null}}]}

// 2. THE BUG: Transition happens here.
// 'token' is "Ap" (logprob exists), but 'delta.content' is null.
data: {"id": "...", "choices": [{"delta": {"content": null, "reasoning_content": null}, "logprobs": {"content": [{"token": "Ap", "logprob": -8.55, ...}]}}]}

// 3. Next chunk continues, missing the start.
data: {"id": "...", "choices": [{"delta": {"content": "ologies", "reasoning_content": null}, "logprobs": {"content": [{"token": "ologies", "logprob": -0.0008, ...}]}}]}
```

### The Fix
The logic is now changed to sequential `if` statements:

- Sequential Processing: After checking/processing reasoning, the code immediately checks `if reasoning_end_arr[i]:`. This ensures that if reasoning finishes in the current step, the `tool_parser` is immediately invoked to process the remaining tokens in the same iteration.

- Optimization: The check for `prompt_token_ids` (disabling reasoning via prompt) is moved before the expensive `extract_reasoning_streaming call`, avoiding unnecessary processing when thinking is disabled.

## Test Plan

Just directly test tool-call + reasoning case, such as
```
'{
  "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2",
  "stream": true,
  "stream_options": {
    "include_usage": true
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "What is the weather like in Boston in fahrenheit?"
    }
  ],
  "max_tokens": 65536,
  "temperature": 1,
  "top_p": 1,
  "frequency_penalty": 0,
  "presence_penalty": 0,
  "seed": null,
  "min_p": 0,
  "repetition_penalty": 1,
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_current_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather in a given location",
        "strict": true,
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "location": {
              "type": "string",
              "description": "The city and state, e.g. San Francisco, CA"
            },
            "unit": {
              "type": "string",
              "enum": [
                "celsius",
                "fahrenheit"
              ]
            }
          },
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": [
            "location",
            "unit"
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}'
```

## Test Result

The first token is generated normally, without setting to `None` or just dropped.

title: fix: add warmup for audio preprocessing
author: TheCodeWrangler
body:
# Audio Preprocessing Warmup for Whisper Models

## Purpose

Fixes first-request latency issue for Whisper transcription models where the first request can take significantly longer (10-20x) than subsequent requests.

**Problem**: The first Whisper transcription request experiences substantial latency overhead due to lazy initialization, causing poor user experience and potential timeout issues in production.

**Root Cause**: Investigation revealed two lazy initialization bottlenecks:
1. **Librosa/audio preprocessing**: First call to `librosa.load()` and mel-spectrogram functions triggers FFTW plan initialization, numba JIT compilation, and audio codec loading
2. **Input processor**: First call to `input_processor.process_inputs()` with multimodal audio triggers WhisperProcessor initialization and tensor operation JIT compilation

**Solution**: Add warmup methods that run during server initialization to eliminate first-request overhead:
- `_warmup_audio_preprocessing()`: Warms up librosa functions with dummy audio
- `_warmup_input_processor()`: Warms up multimodal processing pipeline with dummy request

## Test Plan

### Setup
```bash
# Start vLLM server with Whisper model
vllm serve openai/whisper-large-v3 --dtype bfloat16

# Run test client that makes 10 consecutive transcription requests
python testing/timed_requests_whisper.py
```

### Test Script
Sends 10 requests with the same 60-second audio file and measures client-side latency for each.

## Test Results

### Example Results

**Test Configuration:**
- Model: `openai/whisper-large-v3`
- Hardware: H100 GPU
- Audio: 60-second MP3 file
- Test: 10 consecutive transcription requests

#### Before Fix
```
Request 0: 15.56s  ← First request (18x slower!)
Request 1-9: ~0.85s each
```

**Server-side breakdown (first request)**:
- Audio preprocessing (librosa): **7.67s** (lazy initialization)
- Input processor (multimodal): **2.53s** (lazy initialization)
- Model execution: ~0.02s (already warmed up)
- Text generation: ~5.3s

#### After Fix
```
Request 0: 1.08s  ← First request (now similar to subsequent!)
Request 1-9: ~0.85s each
```

**Server-side breakdown (first request)**:
- Audio preprocessing: **0.08s** (warmed up during startup)
- Input processor: **0.007s** (warmed up during startup)
- Model execution: ~0.02s
- Text generation: ~0.5s

#### Impact Summary

| Component | Before | After | Improvement |
|-----------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Audio preprocessing | ~7-8s | ~0.04-0.08s | ~100-200x faster |
| Input processor | ~2-3s | ~0.002-0.007s | ~400-1500x faster |
| **First request** | ~15-20s | ~1-1.5s | **~10-20x faster** |
| Subsequent requests | ~0.8-1s | ~0.8-1s | No change |
| **Server startup** | Baseline | +10-12s | One-time cost |

**Note**: Exact timings vary based on model size, hardware, audio duration, and system configuration. The key improvement is eliminating the large first-request overhead caused by lazy initialization.

### Trade-off Analysis
- **Added startup time**: ~10-12s (warmup runs once during initialization)
- **Saved per first-request**: ~10-15s
- **Break-even**: After just 1 first request
- **User experience**: Consistent latency across all requests

## Implementation Details

### Changes Made

**File**: `vllm/entrypoints/openai/speech_to_text.py` (+95 lines)

1. **`_warmup_audio_preprocessing()`**
   - Creates 1-second dummy audio (silence at target sample rate)
   - Calls `librosa.get_duration()` to initialize librosa
   - Calls `librosa.feature.melspectrogram()` with Whisper-specific parameters
   - Initializes FFTW plans, numba JIT, audio codecs
   - Non-fatal: logs warning if warmup fails

2. **`_warmup_input_processor()`**
   - Creates dummy audio and generates proper prompt using `model_cls.get_generation_prompt()`
   - Creates minimal `SamplingParams`
   - Calls `input_processor.process_inputs()` to process dummy request
   - Triggers WhisperProcessor initialization, multimodal hashing, tensor operations
   - Non-fatal: logs warning if warmup fails

3. **Called in `__init__()`**
   - Both warmups run after audio config setup
   - Executed before server starts accepting requests
   - Logs clearly indicate warmup progress

### Why This Approach

- **Targeted**: Only warms up components that showed first-call overhead
- **Safe**: Error handling ensures server starts even if warmup fails
- **Observable**: Clear logging shows warmup completion and timing
- **Efficient**: Uses minimal resources (1-second dummy audio)
- **Complete**: Warms up entire pipeline end-to-end

### Alternate Approaches Considered

1. **Lazy warmup on first request**: Rejected - still causes bad UX for first user
2. **Background warmup**: Rejected - adds complexity, potential race conditions
3. **Only librosa warmup**: Insufficient - still left 2.5s input processor delay
4. **Disable JIT**: Rejected - would hurt performance on all requests

## Documentation Update

None required - this is an internal optimization with no API changes.

## Release Notes

**Performance Improvement**: Whisper transcription models now warm up audio preprocessing and multimodal input processing during server initialization, eliminating 10+ seconds of first-request latency. First requests are now 14x faster (15.5s → 1.08s), providing consistent latency for all users.

## Related Issues

This addresses first-request latency for audio/speech-to-text models, particularly Whisper. The issue manifests as:
- First transcription request timing out or taking 15+ seconds
- Poor user experience for cold-start scenarios
- Inconsistent latency patterns

## Testing Checklist

- [x] Tested with `openai/whisper-large-v3` model
- [x] Verified warmup completes successfully during server startup
- [x] Confirmed first request latency reduced from 15.5s to 1.08s
- [x] Verified subsequent requests unchanged at ~0.85s
- [x] Tested with 60-second audio files
- [x] Verified warmup logs appear during initialization
- [x] Confirmed non-fatal error handling (server starts even if warmup fails)
- [x] No functional changes to transcription accuracy or behavior
- [x] No changes to API surface or response format

## Additional Notes

- First request may still be slightly slower than subsequent requests (~10-30% overhead) due to first HTTP connection, first batch through scheduler, and first encoder hash computation - this is acceptable and unavoidable without significantly more complex warmup
- Warmup is automatic and requires no configuration changes
- Applies to all speech-to-text models using the OpenAI-compatible transcription API (Whisper, Voxtral, etc.)
- Server startup time increase is a one-time cost that provides immediate value on first user request
- Warmup uses minimal resources (1 second of silence) and completes in the background during initialization

title: [ROCm][GPTQ][Bugfix] Fix GPTQ GEMM kernel output zeroing race condition
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Summary

Fixes a race condition in the GPTQ GEMM kernels that caused incorrect results when `input_size > BLOCK_KN_SIZE (128)`.

## Problem

The GPTQ GEMM kernels use multiple thread blocks along the k-dimension (`gridDim.z > 1`) that accumulate partial results via `atomicAdd`. The output tensor was being zeroed inside the kernel by `blockIdx.z == 0`:
```cpp
if (blockIdx.z == 0) {
  for (int m = 0; m < m_count; m++)
    *((uint64_t*)c_.item_ptr(offset_m + m, n)) = 0;
}
__syncthreads();  // Only syncs within block, not across blocks!
```

Since `__syncthreads()` only synchronizes threads within the same block, not across different blocks, this creates a race condition where:
- Blocks with `z > 0` may `atomicAdd` their results before block `z=0` finishes zeroing
- Block `z=0` may overwrite results that other blocks have already added

This caused numerical errors up to 45x the expected values, particularly when:
- `input_size > 128` (triggers multiple k-blocks)
- Errors concentrated in specific rows at m-block boundaries

## Solution

1. Pre-zero the output tensor using `torch::zeros()` instead of `torch::empty()`
2. Remove the in-kernel zeroing logic from all GPTQ GEMM kernel variants

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] fix(structured_output): Skip guidance backend for schemas with patternProperties
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a structured output generation failure when using `backend="auto"` with JSON schemas containing `patternProperties`. The fix adds detection for `patternProperties` in the auto-mode fallback logic and routes such schemas to the `outlines` backend instead of `guidance`.

## Problem

When using `structured_outputs` with `backend="auto"` and a JSON schema containing `patternProperties`, the `llguidance` library produces malformed output consisting of `{` followed by endless whitespace characters. This affects **both NVIDIA and AMD/ROCm platforms equally**.

Example failing schema:
```python
{
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "score": {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 5},
        "tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "minLength": 10, "maxLength": 20}},
    },
    "required": ["score", "tags"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "patternProperties": {"^score$": {"type": "integer"}},
}
```

Output with guidance backend:
```
'{  \r\n\r\n\r\n  \r\n\r\n\r\n  \r\n\r\n\r\n  ...'
```

## Root Cause Analysis

Through extensive debugging, we identified the following:

1. **Not an xgrammar issue**: The `xgrammar` backend correctly identifies unsupported JSON schema features (like `multipleOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `patternProperties`) via `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features()` and raises `ValueError` to trigger fallback. This works correctly.

2. **Upstream llguidance bug**: When xgrammar falls back, auto-mode selects the `guidance` backend. The `llguidance` library:
   - **Silently accepts** `patternProperties` during grammar validation (no error returned)
   - **Produces broken grammar at runtime** that only allows `{` followed by whitespace
   
   Verified with:
```python
   import llguidance
   
   schema = {
       "type": "object",
       "properties": {
           "score": {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 5},
           "tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "minLength": 10, "maxLength": 20}},
       },
       "required": ["score", "tags"],
       "additionalProperties": False,
       "patternProperties": {"^score$": {"type": "integer"}},
   }
   
   grammar = llguidance.LLMatcher.grammar_from_json_schema(schema)
   err = llguidance.LLMatcher.validate_grammar(grammar, None)
   print(err)  # None - no error, but runtime output is broken!
```

## Solution

Add detection for JSON schema features unsupported by `llguidance` and skip the guidance backend in auto-mode when detected:

1. **New function** `has_guidance_unsupported_json_features()` in `backend_guidance.py`:
   - Recursively checks for `patternProperties` in the schema
   - Returns `True` if unsupported features are found

2. **Modified auto-mode fallback** in `input_processor.py`:
   - Before falling back to guidance, check if schema has unsupported features
   - If yes, fall back to `outlines` instead (which correctly handles `patternProperties`)

## Related Issues

- Upstream issue filed: https://github.com/guidance-ai/llguidance/issues/265

title: [Bugfix] Whisper fix number of allocated CrossAttn blocks per-request
author: NickLucche
body:
This PR fixes a bug introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29421, which in order to allow for multiple encoder requests to be processed at the same time, upped the `scheduler_config.max_num_encoder_input_tokens` which was previously capped at 1 item (1500 for whisper).
This change results in allocating `max_num_batched_tokens` blocks per-request, as the crossattn blocks are currently using the same `scheduler_config.max_num_encoder_input_tokens` value to determine allocation.

This PR makes sure we're only allocating one item-size per-request, by adding a separate independent variable to determine this value.

```
# vllm serve openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo (defaults to max-num-batched-tokens 8192)
...
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=401191) BEFORE 8192 (self.scheduler_config.max_num_encoder_input_tokens)
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=401191) AFTER 1500 (1 item, self._num_encoder_input_tokens)
```

cc @DarkLight1337

title: [Fix]Load kv-cache dtype from hf_quant_config.json automatically (fix for reverted PR)
author: danielafrimi
body:
HF checkpoint hf_quant_config.json (modelopt) file specifies "kv_cache_quant_algo": "FP8", but vLLM loads the unquantized version of kv-cache.

setting the vLLM server argument explicitly as below:
"--kv-cache-dtype fp8" makes it worked.

this PR fetched the kv_cache_quant_algo from the config itself without specifying it as args (while there is hf_quant_config.json).


The key fix was doing this conversion early when creating `CacheConfig` in `arg_utils.py`, so the resolved value is seen everywhere in the codebase. this way it works exactly like you explicitly passed `--kv-cache-dtype`


The reverted [PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29980) that should supposed to supported this feat had a bug, [CI](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/43393/steps/canvas?jid=019b176c-8881-47f4-aaf9-5dac38740906) failed on some tests (managed to pass them locally on B200)

title: [Bugfix] Fix tool_choice="none" being ignored by GPT-OSS/harmony models
author: HaloWorld
body:
GPT-OSS models using the harmony format were ignoring the `tool_choice="none"` parameter and could still trigger tool calls when tools were provided in the request. This issue arose because the `_make_request_with_harmony` method only checked for the existence of `request.tools`, without accounting for the `tool_choice` setting or the `exclude_tools_when_tool_choice_none` flag. This fix ensures that harmony models respect the `exclude_tools_when_tool_choice_none` flag, aligning their behavior with other model types and OpenAI API standards. When tool_choice="none" and the flag is enabled, tool definitions are no longer included in the system message. ## Purpose Modified _make_request_with_harmony to incorporate checks for tool_choice and exclude_tools_when_tool_choice_none. ## Test Plan - Start vllm server with `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none` ```shell vllm serve /aifs4su/yujiepu/models/openai/gpt-oss-20b/ \ --served-model-name gpt-oss-20b \ --exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --tool-call-parser openai \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --trust-remote-code \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 4 ``` - Test tool-calling ```shell curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-oss-20b", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Dallas, TX?" } ], "tools": [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "get_current_weather", "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": { "type": "string" }, "state": { "type": "string" }, "unit": { "type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"] } }, "required": ["city", "state", "unit"] } } } ], "tool_choice": "none" }' ``` ## Test Result - Before - After ---

title: [Bugfix] fix the alias bug of AttentionBackendEnum when register CUSTOM attention backend to vllm
author: zejunchen-zejun
body:
The bug is the TORCH_SDPA is the alias of the CUSTOM backend in AttentionBackendEnum because both of them don't have the value. When you register your attention backend as below, it will be unexpectedly registered to TORCH_SDPA:
```
import torch
from vllm.attention.backends.registry import register_backend, AttentionBackendEnum
from vllm.attention.backends.abstract import AttentionType
from vllm.attention.selector import get_attn_backend
from vllm.attention.backends.abstract import AttentionBackend, AttentionImpl

head_size = 128
dtype = torch.bfloat16
kv_cache_dtype = "auto"
block_size = 16
attn_type = AttentionType.DECODER

class CustomAttentionImpl(AttentionImpl):
    pass

class CustomAttentionBackend(AttentionBackend):
    @staticmethod
    def get_name():
        return "CUSTOM"

    @staticmethod
    def get_impl_cls():
        return CustomAttentionImpl

register_backend(backend=AttentionBackendEnum.CUSTOM,
                 is_mamba=False,
                 class_path="reproducer.CustomAttentionBackend")

attn_backend = get_attn_backend(
                head_size,
                dtype,
                kv_cache_dtype,
                block_size,
                use_mla=False,
                has_sink=False,
                attn_type=attn_type,
            )
```
When you run above code by _VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=CUSTOM python -u ./reproducer.py_, the CustomAttentionBackend will be unexpectedly registered to TORCH_SDPA. Here is the associated log:
`vllm register_backend backend:  AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA . class_path:  reproducer.CustomAttentionBackend`

So this PR is trying to fix it by assigning None to CUSTOM, so that the CUSTOM is different with TORCH_SDPA, they are not alias. The registry can work successfully.

title: [BugFix] Handle errors when preprocessing added requests
author: njhill
body:
`preprocess_add_request()` runs in the engine core input socket processing thread. It's not expected to raise exceptions but if it does, they aren't caught or logged - the input processing thread exits and the engine hangs silently :(

This PR catches and logs request-scoped preprocessing errors, and returns an output to fail the request in question.

I'll open another PR to deal with any other unexpected exceptions occurring in the input socket processing thread (which should be considered fatal, but we should log and shutdown rather than hanging silently!).

Example occurrence: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/43897#019b2b2f-7961-46c0-8511-5ee297eddac6

title: fix fp8 online quantization streaming with tp > 1
author: vkuzo
body:
Summary:

Fix for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/30830

When we added online fp8 quant with streaming weight post-processing in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29196, a bug was introduced where TP>1 case was not always handled correctly. Specifically:

* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29196 assumed that `weight_loader` copies `loaded_weight` to `param` directly
* this is not always true, as `weight_loader` can call arbitrary logic on both `param` and `loaded_weight` before eventually calling `copy_`. An example is here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e3a0f21e6ce78268865cafcdc3dc58c7a80dbc57/vllm/model_executor/parameter.py#L195

A fix is to track exactly how many number of elements were updated with `copy_`.  The PR implements this fix with `TorchDispatchMode`.

Test Plan:

```bash
// tp 1 still works
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6,7 with-proxy python3 examples/offline_inference/basic/generate.py --model Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B --enforce-eager --quantization fp8 -tp=1
// tp > 2 was broken before, now works
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6,7 with-proxy python3 examples/offline_inference/basic/generate.py --model Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B --enforce-eager --quantization fp8 -tp=2
```

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix `fa_version` argument error in `flash_attn_maxseqlen_wrapper` for ROCm without aiter
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
### Problem
On ROCm platforms with `AITER` either uninstalled or disabled, `flash_attn_varlen_func` fails with:
```
TypeError: flash_attn_varlen_func() got an unexpected keyword argument 'fa_version'
```

This occurs because `is_rocm_aiter` is `False` when `aiter` is disabled, causing the code to fall through to the else branch which unconditionally passes `fa_version` to `flash_attn_varlen_func`. However, the ROCm version of Flash Attention (via `vllm.attention.utils.fa_utils`) does not support the `fa_version` argument.

### Root Cause

The existing logic only checks for `is_rocm_aiter` to determine whether to pass `fa_version`, but this doesn't account for ROCm users who don't have `aiter` enabled. The `fa_version` parameter is CUDA-specific and should never be passed on ROCm platforms.

### Solution

Add an explicit `current_platform.is_rocm()` check before adding `fa_version` to kwargs. This ensures that:
- CUDA users continue to get `fa_version` passed through as expected
- ROCm users with `aiter` use the aiter path (unchanged)
- ROCm users without `aiter` now correctly skip the `fa_version` argument

title: [Fix][FlexAttention] return max logical block index to handle reused blocks
author: ivanium
body:
## Purpose For FlexAttention, we need to build `physical_to_logical_mapping` to reversely map physical block ids to logical block ids. This process previously assumes logical block ids are always unique, which is not true for some attention types such as sliding window attention, where some blocks may be released and reused later, causing the same physical block id to appear multiple times in a row of `block_table` at different logical block indices. As a result, before this PR, the physical to logical mapping will be non-deterministic (most times return the first matched logical block index) and lead to errornous results as shown in the following example.
test_gemma3_reuse.py

```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams # Initialize LLM with LMCache configuration # Adjust gpu_memory_utilization based on your GPU memory # Parameters below are for 80GB GPUs llm = LLM( model="google/gemma-3-4b-it", max_model_len=75000, gpu_memory_utilization=0.28, # 80GB*0.28 = 22.4GB max_num_seqs=16, enforce_eager=True, ) sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=10) outputs = llm.generate("hi" * 70000 + "\nhow are you?", sampling_params) generated_text = outputs[0].outputs[0].text print(f"Generated text: {generated_text!r}") # Wrong results: 'hihihihihihihihihihi' # Correct results: '\nI am fine, thank you for asking!' ```

This PR fixes this issue by always returning the latest (maximum) logical block index during this building process, given the fact that the latest/newly allocated block must be the one in use while previous ones are stale. ## Test Plan The standard flex attention tests should pass. Additionally, this PR adds a new test case with reused blocks. ```shell pytest -q tests/kernels/test_flex_attention.py ``` The above example `test_gemma3_reuse.py` should also pass. ## Test Result Passed. ---

title: [BugFix] Fix spec decode + structured outputs + preemption edge case
author: njhill
body:
Fix an edge case that can be triggered when using spec decode with structured outputs.

There is a sequence of preemption and drafting being skipped that can result in the scheduler's `request.spec_token_ids` being stale which can then fail bitmask generation because they will be out of sync with the grammar.

When triggered, vLLM crashes with an error like this:
```
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)   File "/home/nickhill/workspace/vllm2/vllm/vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 920, in _process_engine_step
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)     outputs, model_executed = self.step_fn()
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)   File "/home/nickhill/workspace/vllm2/vllm/vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 344, in step
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)     grammar_output = self.scheduler.get_grammar_bitmask(scheduler_output)
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)   File "/home/nickhill/workspace/vllm2/vllm/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 1022, in get_grammar_bitmask
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)     bitmask = self.structured_output_manager.grammar_bitmask(
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)   File "/home/nickhill/workspace/vllm2/vllm/vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py", line 277, in grammar_bitmask
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)     assert accepted, (token, req_id, scheduled_spec_decode_tokens)
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249)            ^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore_DP0 pid=1549249) AssertionError: (220, '80', {'80': [330, 220]})
```

This PR fixes that case by ensuring that `request.spec_token_ids` is cleared when drafting is skipped for a given step, rather than potentially leaving set to a prior step's draft tokens.

It will covered by tests once we extend [test_async_scheduling.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/tests/v1/e2e/test_async_scheduling.py) test matrix in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29821.

Note that this bug/fix doesn't actually apply to the async scheduling case.
