title: Fix DFlash prefix cache corruption due to missing lookahead block
author: shreyas269
body:
## Summary

Fixes a KV cache corruption bug in DFlash that causes persistent MGL degradation under prefix caching with concurrency.

## How we found this

While trying out DFlash, under high concurrency with prefix caching enabled, we observed MGL degradation on requests that were otherwise running correctly. Their KV cache was being corrupted by other newly-arriving prefix-hit requests. We saw a steady decrease in MGL. Specifically, those new request's first DFlash drafter pass was writing KV into shared prefix blocks because their slot mapping was never set up (no lookahead blocks were allocated for them). We didn't see this degradation in sglang under the same workload, which confirmed this was a vllm-specific bug. Once we traced the corruption back to the missing block allocation on first prefill, the fix was straightforward.

## Root cause

The target prefill and the first drafter pass run in the same scheduler step for both Eagle and DFlash. The DFlash drafter issues `num_spec_tokens + 1` query tokens (1 bonus token + N mask tokens) at positions beyond the prefill.

These positions require allocated KV blocks because DFlash draft attention is bidirectional and the drafter writes KV at future positions via block table lookup. If the block table doesn't cover those positions, the drafter writes into the wrong block.

The scheduler had this logic when allocating blocks for a new request:

```python
effective_lookahead_tokens = (
    0 if request.num_computed_tokens == 0 else self.num_lookahead_tokens
)
```

From the comment it looks like this was added as a P/D disaggregation edge case guard to avoid allocating extra blocks for brand-new requests. However, `request.num_computed_tokens` is still 0 at the point where `allocate_slots` is called for a new request's first scheduling pass (it's only updated after allocation succeeds, at a later line). This means zero lookahead blocks are allocated at prefill time, yet the DFlash drafter immediately needs to write KV beyond the allocated range.

When the correct blocks don't exist, the drafter ends up writing KV into the last prefill block instead...which with prefix caching is shared across requests. It silently overwrites valid prefill KV data in that block.

**Without prefix caching:** The corrupted last block belongs only to the current request. In the next scheduling step, `request.num_computed_tokens > 0`, so lookahead blocks are allocated correctly. The drafter has one bad step...and then recovers. This is likely why MGL impact was negligible without prefix caching and we still saw good speedups with DFlash.

**With prefix caching under concurrency:** Multiple requests share the same prefix blocks. When a new request's drafter writes KV into the wrong block, it corrupts a shared prefix block. All other requests using that prefix...including ones that were running fine...now read corrupted KV. This is what we observed: MGL degradation on healthy requests, caused by new arrivals corrupting their shared prefix cache. Kind of only impacts MGL in a special case where the unalloted KV blocks are overwritten very fast due to high prefix-hit and conurrency.

## Changes

~~### 1. Scheduler (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`)~~

title: [Bugfix][MoE] FlashInfer one-sided: workspace union across heterogeneous layers

## Purpose
`FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager.initialize()` was first-call-wins: it sized the shared MNNVL workspace from the first MoE layer and short-circuited the rest. title: [ROCm][MLA][Bugfix] Reserve FP8 prefill workspace before lock for Kimi-K2.5
author: xaguilar-amd
body:
## Summary

Fixes a ROCm AITER dense MLA FP8 prefill crash after #42509 where the per-call scratch workspace introduced for `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` could be first requested after the global workspace manager had already been locked.

The fix reserves the maximum FP8 prefill scratch shapes while initializing the FP8 persistent-scheduling metadata buffers, before `lock_workspace()` runs. The reservation is sized from the AITER metadata capacity so it covers multiple-request batches and KV-split partial tiles.

## Problem

Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4 on ROCm AITER dense MLA could fail on the first served prompt with:

```text
AssertionError: Workspace is locked but allocation from 'rocm_aiter_mla.py:767:_mla_fp8_prefill_attn' requires 61.08 MB, current size is 0.00 MB. Workspace growth is not allowed after locking.
```

Runtime debugging showed that the workspace locked at `0.00 MB` before the dense FP8 MLA prefill path ran. When `_mla_fp8_prefill_attn()` later requested `logits`, `attn_lse`, and `final_lse` through `current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous(...)`, the request required growth after lock and tripped the assertion.

## Fix

- Reserve the FP8 MLA prefill scratch workspace during `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder._init_fp8_prefill_ps_buffers()`, which runs before workspace locking.
- Bound the reservation by the AITER persistent-scheduling metadata capacity:

```text
max_num_partial_tiles = numel(reduce_partial_map_size)
```

- Reserve the same three scratch tensors used at runtime:

```text
(max_num_partial_tiles * _FP8_PREFILL_TILE_Q, num_heads, v_head_dim) float32
(max_num_partial_tiles * _FP8_PREFILL_TILE_Q, num_heads) float32
(max_prefill_qlen, num_heads) float32
```


## Validation

Runtime validation performed on the local branch with temporary instrumentation, then instrumentation was removed:

- Reproduced the original Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4 failure:
  - Workspace locked at `0.00 MB`.
  - Runtime dense FP8 MLA prefill requested scratch after lock.
  - Assertion came from `rocm_aiter_mla.py:_mla_fp8_prefill_attn`.
- Verified the fix:
  - FP8 MLA scratch reservation happened before workspace lock.
  - Workspace no longer locked at `0.00 MB`.
  - Kimi still entered `rocm_aiter_mla.py:_mla_fp8_prefill_attn`.
  - No post-lock workspace growth assertion occurred.
- Reviewed a narrower scheduler-token reservation:
  - It was smaller, but it could under-reserve for batches with many requests or KV splitting because `fp8_prefill_num_partial_tiles` is a PS/reduce metadata count, not simply `ceil(total_q / tile_q)`.
  - Final reservation uses the AITER metadata capacity to avoid post-lock workspace growth for all metadata-representable batches.

This change was developed with AI assistance.

title: [MISC] Fix symm_mem cap-equal gate; log AR backend selection
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Summary

Two small changes in `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/`:

- **Fix misprint in `SymmMemCommunicator.should_use_symm_mem`** — the size gate
  used a strict less-than (`inp_size < self.max_size`), which silently rejected
  tensors whose byte size exactly equals the per-capability symm_mem cap and

- **Add startup logging for all-reduce backend selection** in

title: [Docs] Fix MooncakeStoreConnector role in disaggregated example
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Summary

In `docs/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage.md`, the Disaggregated Prefill-Decode (XpYd) example sets the inner `MooncakeStoreConnector` to `kv_producer` on the prefiller. The surrounding text advertises "cross-instance prefix cache sharing via the distributed store" — but with `kv_producer` the prefiller only saves to the store and never loads from it, so prior-prefix hits across instances do not actually take effect.

This is verified against the connector source: in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py`, only `kv_consumer` skips saves (`force_skip_save = self.kv_role == "kv_consumer"`), and `worker.py` save paths gate on `kv_role in ["kv_producer", "kv_both"]`, so `kv_both` enables both directions.

title: [Bugfix] Clear P0 mm sender cache on sleep/pause to fix mm_hash desync
author: wasnertobias
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #42995.

`/sleep?level>=1` and `/pause?clear_cache=true` go through `EngineCore` on the engine side, which only clears the **P1** multimodal receiver cache via `pause_scheduler -> _reset_caches -> reset_mm_cache`. The **P0** sender cache (`MultiModalProcessorSenderCache`) lives in the API server process and was never cleared on these paths. On the next request that reuses a previously-seen `mm_hash`, the sender hits, strips the payload, and forwards `mm_item=None` over IPC. P1 has no entry → `assert mm_item is not None` in `MultiModalReceiverCache.get_and_update_item` (`vllm/multimodal/cache.py:660`) trips, and after enough retries the EngineCore async loop wedges (only a process restart recovers).

> The gap was introduced by PR #34528, which centralized cache resetting in `pause_scheduler`. The `# we don't attempt to re-sync the internal caches (P0 sender, P1 receiver)` comment in `EngineCore.reset_mm_cache` was accurate when the method was only reachable via the debug `/reset_mm_cache` endpoint (which goes through `AsyncLLM.reset_mm_cache` and already dual-clears). It became wrong once `/sleep` and `/pause?clear_cache=true` reached the same code path implicitly.

## Fix

Mirror the existing `*.reset_mm_cache` dual-clear pattern at the engine-wrapper layer (same abstraction level as the existing fix in `AsyncLLM.reset_mm_cache` / `LLMEngine.reset_mm_cache`). Three small additions:

- `AsyncLLM.sleep`: when `level >= 1` (i.e. `EngineCore.sleep` will internally clear P1), `await self.renderer.clear_mm_cache_async()` first.
- `AsyncLLM.pause_generation`: when `clear_cache=True` (i.e. `pause_scheduler` will internally clear P1), `await self.renderer.clear_mm_cache_async()` first.
- `LLMEngine.sleep`: same shape, sync - fixes offline `LLM(enable_sleep_mode=True).sleep(level=1)` (e.g. RLHF training loops).

Six lines added across two files, no deletions. `EngineCore.reset_mm_cache` is untouched - its P1-only behaviour is correct; callers are responsible for the P0 side, which the three wrapper methods above now handle. The standalone `/reset_mm_cache` endpoint and the `assert` in `MultiModalReceiverCache` are unchanged. PR #34749 (softening that assert into an exception) is orthogonal and can land independently; once the desync no longer happens on sleep/pause the wedge it would otherwise cause here can't happen either.

## Out of scope

- The `MultiModalCacheMissError` softening proposed in #34749 (orthogonal; addresses the engine-thread wedge symptom under concurrent eviction divergence, not the sleep/pause-induced desync).
- The EngineCore async-loop wedge symptom - without the desync there's nothing to wedge on.

## Test plan

```bash
# Cache contract test + engine-wrapper tests (CPU-only, fast):
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py -v \
  -k "sleep_dual_clear_invariant_at_cache_layer or \
      async_llm_sleep_clears_p0_renderer_when_level_ge_1 or \
      async_llm_pause_generation_clears_p0_renderer_when_clearing_cache or \
      llm_engine_sleep_clears_p0_renderer_when_level_ge_1"

# Run the whole mm cache test module to be sure nothing regressed:
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py -v
```

## Test result

Locally, against this branch:

- `test_sleep_dual_clear_invariant_at_cache_layer` - passes. Demonstrates the desync mechanism at the cache layer (asserts the existing `assert mm_item is not None` invariant) and that the symmetric clear restores the fresh-request behaviour.
- `test_async_llm_sleep_clears_p0_renderer_when_level_ge_1` - passes; also verifies that level 0 (pause-only) does NOT clear P0.
- `test_async_llm_pause_generation_clears_p0_renderer_when_clearing_cache` - passes; also verifies `clear_cache=False` leaves P0 intact.
- `test_llm_engine_sleep_clears_p0_renderer_when_level_ge_1` - passes; level 0 leaves P0 intact.

I verified the same tests against an unpatched vLLM (0.18.1, where the bug is present): the cache contract test passes, and all three engine-wrapper tests fail - i.e. they correctly catch the regression.

**I did not run the live HTTP repro** from #42995 myself on a CUDA box; the cache-layer unit test is a deterministic reproduction of the same desync, and the engine-wrapper tests directly assert the fix is in the call path.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR, including this description, was prepared with Claude Code (per AGENTS.md §1). I personally reviewed every changed line, ran the regression tests, and will defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix] Make CuMemAllocator free callback stream-aware
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Problem

`CuMemAllocator` (sleep-mode allocator, `vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py`) uses a CUDA *pluggable* allocator. When a pool-backed tensor's refcount hits zero, `_python_free_callback` returns the allocation handle, and the C extension (`csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp:unmap_and_release`) immediately calls `cuMemUnmap` + `cuMemRelease` *synchronously from the host*. Which can trigger IMA in the case where the memory is released before all kernels on the cuda stream have completed. 

This has showed up when running deepseek v4 with sleep mode turned on. 

## Test plan
- Before the fix, running this code triggers IMA:
```
from vllm.device_allocator.cumem import CuMemAllocator

with CuMemAllocator.get_instance().use_memory_pool(tag="weights"):
    for _ in range(200):
        torch.randn(2048, 7168, device="cuda")

torch.cuda.synchronize()
print("OK")

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/zixi/repos/vllm/repro_cumem_race.py", line 15, in <module>
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
  File "/home/zixi/repos/vllm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 1162, in synchronize
    return torch._C._cuda_synchronize()
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
Search for `cudaErrorIllegalAddress' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information.
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
Compile with `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA` to enable device-side assertions.
```
- After the fix, no IMA

---

🤖 This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The diagnosis, repro, fix, and PR text were AI-drafted; I reviewed every changed line, ran the repro on a B300 cluster against this patch, and own the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix] Auto-raise max_num_batched_tokens for prefix-LM multimodal models
author: ashwing
body:
## Summary

Fixes #42687.

Multimodal prefix-LM models (e.g., Gemma 4) that require `disable_chunked_mm_input` need the entire multimodal item to fit in a single batch. Gemma 4's video budget is 2496 tokens (`32 frames × (70 + 2 + 6)`), but the auto-calculated `max_num_batched_tokens` defaults to 2048 on GPUs with <70GB memory (A100-40GB, L4, A10G). This causes a `ValueError` during initialization, blocking Gemma 4 deployment on cost-effective hardware without manual `--max-num-batched-tokens` override.

## Changes

- Add `EngineArgs._get_min_mm_batched_tokens()` — queries the multimodal registry for the maximum per-item token count across all supported modalities.
- In `_set_default_max_num_seqs_and_batched_tokens_args()`, after the initial auto-calc, check if the model is a prefix-LM multimodal model and raise `max_num_batched_tokens` to the multimodal floor if needed.
- Only triggers when:
  - `max_num_batched_tokens` is **not** explicitly set by the user
  - Model is both multimodal **and** prefix-LM (`is_mm_prefix_lm=True`)
  - Registry query succeeds (graceful fallback to `None` on error)

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

@abinggo expressed interest in the issue on May 15 but has not submitted a PR after 4 days. Their analysis identified two approaches (auto-raise vs hard error) but was blocked on the belief that the multimodal processor isn't available at the auto-calc point. This PR demonstrates that `MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.get_processing_info(model_config)` works at this stage — it only requires `model_config`, not a tokenizer or full processor.

This approach is:
- **Auto-recovery** (not just a better error) — the model starts without user intervention
- **Minimal surface** — 25 lines of production code, scoped to prefix-LM models only
- **Safe** — falls back to `None` if registry query fails; does not touch user-provided overrides

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py::test_mm_prefix_lm_raises_batched_tokens_floor` — asserts Gemma 4 config gets `max_num_batched_tokens >= 2496` regardless of GPU memory
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass
- [ ] Existing tests pass (requires GPU CI)

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py -v -k "test_mm_prefix_lm"
```

title: [Bugfix] Add early validation to reject incompatible runner types for embedding models

title: [XPU] Fix CUDA API shims breaking Torch Dynamo during AOT compile
author: lslusarczyk
body:
## Summary

On XPU, `XPUModelRunner` applies `_torch_cuda_wrapper()`, which patches `torch.cuda.*` to delegate to `torch.xpu.*`. Previously, callables were assigned by direct alias (e.g. `torch.cuda.current_stream = torch.xpu.current_stream`), so CUDA and XPU shared the **same function object**.

During EngineCore startup, `profile_run()` triggers AOT compile. Torch Dynamo builds its in-graph handler table (`TorchInGraphFunctionVariable._get_handlers()`) and registers `torch.cuda.current_stream` and `torch.xpu.current_stream` separately. Duplicate identity causes:

```text
AssertionError: Handler already registered for <function current_stream at 0x...>
```
This surfaces as EngineCore failed to start during KV cache initialization.

This PR wraps each patched callable in its own `functools.partial(...)`, preserving XPU behavior while giving Dynamo distinct registration keys.

## Symptom (original EngineCore failure)

EngineCore failed during KV cache init while profiling memory. The worker dies on the first AOT compile inside `profile_run`; the root exception in the EngineCore log is Dynamo failing to build in-graph handlers (not a generic init error):

```text
(EngineCore pid=235924) ERROR ... EngineCore failed to start.
...
  File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 250, in _initialize_kv_caches
    available_gpu_memory = self.model_executor.determine_available_memory()
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 392, in determine_available_memory
```

title: [BugFix] Fix Humming MoE deploy error
author: adotdad
body:
## Purpose
We attempted to deploy the model `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-2Bit-GSQ`, which uses Humming packed quantization.

With the latest version of vLLM, the model weights load successfully, but execution immediately fails with an assertion error at line 871 in:

`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/humming.py`

Specifically:

```
assert self.moe_quant_config is not None
```

The issue is that `self.moe_quant_config` is never initialized because `self.get_fused_moe_quant_config(layer)` is not called anywhere before the assertion. As a fix, we add a call to initialize `self.moe_quant_config` immediately before the assertion.

After resolving this, we encountered a second issue where:

```
layer.input_schemas
```

was empty.

Looking at lines 816–817 in the same file, `layer.input_schemas` and `layer.weight_schemas` are only populated when the checkpoint is *not* already in Humming format. As a result, these schemas remain uninitialized for Humming-formatted checkpoints.

The fix is simply to move the schema allocation logic outside the conditional block (i.e., remove one indentation level), ensuring the schemas are initialized in both cases.
## Test Plan
After applying these two fixes, vLLM runs the model `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-2Bit-GSQ` successfully. The test command:

```
vllm serve GSQ-dev/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-2Bit-GSQ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --served-model-name qwen3.6-35b-a3b-2bit-gsq --tensor-parallel-size 2   
```

## Test Result

We tested the above model and verified that it produces correct outputs.

title: fix(processor): route MiMo-V2-Omni media fetch through MediaConnector
author: ibondarenko1
body:
### What this PR does

Fixes SSRF + arbitrary local file read in `MiMoV2OmniMultiModalProcessor` by routing caller-supplied media strings through `MediaConnector` instead of raw `requests.get` / `Image.open` calls.

`vllm/transformers_utils/processors/mimo_v2_omni.py` had two sinks:
- `_fetch_image()` at line 231 - issued `requests.get(src, timeout=30)` directly on any `http://` or `https://` string, did `Image.open(src[7:])` on `file://` strings, and fell through to `Image.open(src)` on any other string (local-file primitive).
- The audio loader around line 471 - same `requests.get(audio, timeout=30)` pattern on URL strings, raw local path passthrough otherwise.

Both surfaces bypassed the `allowed_media_domains` allowlist and the `allowed_local_media_path` policy that already harden the OpenAI chat path via `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py:838+`. This PR routes the string branches in both sinks through `MediaConnector` so the processor inherits the same hardening that was applied in `GHSA-qh4c-xf7m-gxfc`, `GHSA-v359-jj2v-j536`, and `GHSA-pf3h-qjgv-vcpr` to the chat path.

### Change

`vllm/transformers_utils/processors/mimo_v2_omni.py` only. Two function bodies updated:

1. `_fetch_image`: keeps the `Image.Image` and `bytes` short-circuits unchanged. For `str` inputs, delegates to `MediaConnector().fetch_image(src)`. The function-local import is intentional - keeps the new dependency confined to the call site and avoids a top-of-module import cycle if a future refactor moves things around.

2. Audio loader: keeps the `bytes` and `data:` decode-via-`BytesIO` flows unchanged. For URL and local-path `str` inputs, delegates to `MediaConnector().fetch_audio(audio)`, which returns `(np.ndarray, sample_rate)`. The numpy array is converted back to a `torch.Tensor` so the existing downstream resampling code keeps working without further adaptation.

### Impact

- `LLM.generate(multi_modal_data={"image": "http://attacker/..."})` and the audio equivalent are now constrained by `MediaConnector`'s URL allowlist and local-path policy. Deployers who set `--allowed-media-domains` (and `--allowed-local-media-path`) get the corresponding protection; deployers who do not get the same default behavior the chat path has had since the earlier advisories landed.
- Bytes and `data:` paths behave exactly as before.
- Existing API surface is unchanged.

### Related

GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7 (this advisory). Maintainer (`jperezdealgaba`) acked the report and requested a fix-commit link before opening the CVE flow.

### Tests

- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('vllm/transformers_utils/processors/mimo_v2_omni.py').read())"`: clean.
- `grep -E "requests\.get\((src|audio|image)" vllm/transformers_utils/processors/mimo_v2_omni.py`: 0 matches (sink-leak check).
- Full vLLM test suite not run locally (heavy GPU-dependent suite). The change is type-preserving where it can be (image case returns `Image.Image`; audio case returns a `torch.Tensor` with the existing sample-rate handling). Happy to add a unit fixture if the team wants regression coverage for the SSRF / LFI primitives.

### Why no broader refactor

Keeping the diff minimal so it can be reviewed quickly and the corresponding CVE can be requested through the GHSA flow. If the team prefers a larger refactor (e.g. forbidding `str` inputs from reaching the processor at all, and pushing all media resolution upstream into the renderer layer), happy to do that as a follow-up.

title: [BugFix] wire make_empty_intermediate_tensors on AyaVision and Voxtral
author: JasonKeyiL
body:
## Summary

`AyaVisionForConditionalGeneration` and `VoxtralForConditionalGeneration` (and, by inheritance, `VoxtralRealtimeGeneration`) declare the `SupportsPP` mixin but never wire `self.make_empty_intermediate_tensors` from `self.language_model`. The attribute then resolves to the stub method inherited from the `SupportsPP` Protocol — its body is `...`, so it returns `None`.

This is subtle: `@runtime_checkable` only verifies the attribute exists, so `isinstance(model, SupportsPP)` passes through the inherited stub. `supports_pp()` returns `True` and the engine enables PP. On non-first PP ranks, [`gpu/model_runner.py:322`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L322) does

```python
self.intermediate_tensors = self.model.make_empty_intermediate_tensors(...)
```

gets `None`, and crashes downstream. Same exact failure mode that #42819 fixed for Cohere2 Vision.

The fix is the one-line forward that the rest of the VL wrappers already use (see `eagle2_5_vl.py`, `internvl.py`, `lfm2_vl.py`, `skyworkr1v.py`, …):

```python
self.make_empty_intermediate_tensors = (
    self.language_model.make_empty_intermediate_tensors
)
```

Both inner `language_model`s expose the real method (`CohereForCausalLM` for Aya, the Mistral/Llama family for Voxtral), so the forward is safe.

### Quick repro of the Protocol-stub behavior

```python
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

@runtime_checkable
class P(Protocol):
    def m(self): ...

class C(P): pass
c = C()
isinstance(c, P)  # True
c.m()             # None    <-- the stub
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `vllm serve <Aya-Vision-model> --pipeline-parallel-size 2` starts up
- [ ] `vllm serve <Voxtral-model> --pipeline-parallel-size 2` starts up
- [x] `pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/aya_vision.py vllm/model_executor/models/voxtral.py` (ruff, mypy, etc.) passes locally

## Notes

- Duplicate-PR check: no open PR mentions Aya/Voxtral + PP or `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`. Closest prior art is the merged #42819 (Cohere2 Vision), which this PR mirrors.
- AI assistance was used to locate and verify the missing wire-up across the multimodal wrappers; every changed line was reviewed and the failure mode was reproduced via the Protocol-stub snippet above.

title: [AMD][CI][BugFix] Fix  Distributed Compile Unit Tests (2xH100-2xMI300) group
author: rasmith
body:
## Purpose
Multiple problems were encountered with the `Distributed Compile Unit Tests (2xH100-2xMI300)` tests.

For `test_tp2_ar_rms.py:`
* `disable_custom_all_reduce=False`  needed to be set for the fusion passes to initalize on ROCm. Leaving this disabled causes the tests to fail since the custom all-reduce setup will be skipped during initalization.
* On ROCm, `RocmAiterAllReduceFusionPass`  is used, so this test also needs to check patterns for `aiter_ar_rms_fusion` instead of `ar_rms_fusion`
    - added patterns to `FUSION_LOG_PATTERNS` in ` tests/compile/fusions_e2e/common.py`
    - update counts in `tests/compile/fusions_e2e/models.py` 
        + `llama3_8b`: `n_layers * 2` (dense MLP, all-reduce after both attn and MLP)
        + `qwen3_a3b`: `n_layers * 2`
        + `gpt_oss_20b`:` n_layers + 1` (MoE MLP has no all-reduce, only attn `o_proj`)
* Swap out the `ar_rms_fusion` pattern for `aiter_ar_rms_fusion` on ROCm in `test_tp2_ar_rms.py::test_tp2_ar_rms_fusion`
* Skip `openai/gpt-oss-20b` with `ROCM_ATTN` backend due to the following error:
` ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_ATTN is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['attention sinks not supported]`

For `test_async_tp.py`:
* ` async_tp_pass_on_test_model ` tries to use port 12345, but on some systems `alloy `will be running which will use the same port
     - find an open port and use that instead
 * `AsyncTPPass `does not check if CUTLASS is available before registering the `CutlassScaledMMReduceScatterPattern` and `AllGatherCutlassScaledMMPattern `patterns
     - check if `cutlass_scaled_mm `is available in `torch.ops._C` before registering
  * `test_async_tp_pass_replace` tests the `TestCutlassScaledMMRSModel` and `TestAGCutlassScaledMMModel` models but also does not check if `cutlass_scaled_mm `is available
      - wrap these parameters using `param `and `skipif` `cutlass_scaled_mm` is not available.

## Test Plan
1) `pytest -sv compile/fusions_e2e/test_tp2_ar_rms.py::test_tp2_ar_rms_fusions`
2) `VLLM_TEST_CLEAN_GPU_MEMORY=1 pytest -sv compile/passes/distributed/test_async_tp.py`

title: [BugFix] Use correct logprobs for `logprob_token_ids`
author: njhill
body:
When gathering the logprobs for the `logprob_token_ids` option (used in generative scoring), we should honor the logprobs mode. This also avoids unnecessarily recomputing the logprobs from logits, and keeps the rank computation consistent with the top_k logprobs case.

title: [BUG] Fix FP64 Gumbel precision coverage
author: tianyu-z
body:
The existing --use-fp64-gumbel flag only covered the explicit Triton Gumbel sampler. V1 sampling and spec decode also use the equivalent exponential-race form q.exponential_(); probs / q; argmax, so those paths still used fp32 exponential noise even when the precision flag was enabled.

Thread use_fp64_gumbel through the Python V1 sampler, TopKTopPSampler, rejection sampler recovery sampling, and LLM draft proposer sampling. When enabled, these paths now draw Exp(1) noise in float64 and compute the race scores in float64, while preserving the existing fp32 fast path by default.

Add regression coverage for the fp64 paths and a CUDA proof script. On H100 with PyTorch 2.9.1+cu126, 200M fp32 exponential samples had min exactly 2^-24 and zero samples below 2^-24, while float64 produced samples below that cutoff. In the many-tail race with trials=100000, tail_tokens=262144, gap=20.5, expected tail hits were 32.76; fp32 produced 0 hits and float64 produced 32 hits.



## Purpose
### Summary

This PR extends `use_fp64_gumbel` coverage to the V1 sampling paths that use the exponential-race form of Gumbel-max sampling.

Concretely, it makes `use_fp64_gumbel=True` apply to:

- V1 top-k/top-p sampling via `q.exponential_(); probs / q; argmax`
- spec decode recovered-token sampling from residual probabilities
- LLM draft proposer sampling
- the V1 sampler wiring from `ModelConfig` into `Sampler` / `RejectionSampler`

The default path is unchanged: `use_fp64_gumbel=False` still uses the existing fp32 fast paths.

### Why

`q.exponential_(); probs.div(q).argmax()` is mathematically equivalent to Gumbel-max sampling:

q ~ Exp(1) = -log(U)
argmax(probs / q)
= argmax(log(probs) - log(q))
= argmax(log(probs) + Gumbel)

So the same fp32 tail-truncation issue that affects explicit Gumbel sampling also affects these exponential-race sampling paths.

On CUDA, fp32 random draws cannot represent the very small lower-tail events that fp64 can. For ordinary single-token AR sampling this is usually tiny, but for wide distributions / many parallel categorical races, the missing tail can become observable and can systematically remove rare-token wins.

## Test Plan
```bash
python tools/gumbel_precision/prove_exponential_race_precision.py
```

## Test Result
On an H100, the script showed:
torch.float32: samples=200000000 count(q < 2^-24)=0 min=5.960464477539062500e-08
torch.float64: samples=200000000 count(q < 2^-24)=8 min=1.963535558298479652e-09

many-tail race: trials=100000 num_tail_tokens=262144 gap=20.5 expected_tail_hits=32.7613
torch.float32: tail_hits=0
torch.float64: tail_hits=32

This demonstrates both pieces:

fp32 exponential noise has a lower-tail cutoff around 2^-24.
In an exponential-race sampler, those missing lower-tail events can change actual categorical outcomes.

### Impacted Paths
This PR updates the following paths to honor use_fp64_gumbel=True:

#### vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py

- random_sample
- native top-k/top-p sampling
- CPU/native fallback sampling
- CUDA/FlashInfer fallback behavior when fp64 is requested
- ROCm/aiter fallback behavior when fp64 is requested

#### vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py

- spec decode recovered-token sampling from residual distributions
- Triton kernel accumulator dtype for fp64 exponential-race scores

#### vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py

- draft-token sampling path

#### vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py

- threads use_fp64_gumbel into TopKTopPSampler

#### vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py

- threads ModelConfig.use_fp64_gumbel into the V1 sampler

#### vllm/config/model.py

- updates the config docstring to mention both explicit Gumbel-max and equivalent exponential-race sampling

### Tests
Added targeted tests for:

wiring Sampler(use_fp64_gumbel=True) into TopKTopPSampler
fp64 exponential-race sampling in random_sample
fp64 recovered-token sampling in rejection sampling
fp64 draft-token sampling in compute_probs_and_sample_next_token

### Validation run on H100:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py::test_sampler_threads_fp64_gumbel_to_topk_topp_sampler \
  tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py::test_random_sample_uses_fp64_exponential_race_when_requested \
  tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py::test_sample_recovered_tokens_uses_fp64_exponential_race_when_requested \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_compute_probs_and_sample_next_token_uses_fp64_exponential_race
```

title: Fix _riscv_supports_rvv_vlen128() to detect RVV on hardware without zvl flags
author: lyd1992
body: ## Purpose Fix `_riscv_supports_rvv_vlen128()` so that RISC-V hardware without `zvlb` flags in `/proc/cpuinfo` can still correctly detect RVV support. On some RISC-V hardware (e.g. SG2044), `/proc/cpuinfo` advertises the V extension (`rv64imafdcv`) and `zve*` / `zvfh` flags but does **not** report any `zvlb` VLEN hint. The existing Python-only check required `zvl128b` to be present: ```python if "zvl128b" not in cpuinfo: return False ``` This caused `_get_attn_isa()` to fall back to `"vec"` even though the RVV kernel was correctly compiled with `-DVLLM_RVV_VLEN=128` at build time. The CMake build requires explicit `-DVLLM_RVV_VLEN=128` when no `zvl` flag is auto-detected, so the RVV kernel **is** compiled — but the Python runtime check was out of sync with the C++ compile-time guard. ### Changes 1. **`csrc/cpu/cpu_attn.cpp`** — Add `cpu_attn_has_isa()` helper that checks the same preprocessor guard (`__riscv_v_min_vlen == 128`) that gates the RVV kernel at compile time. 2. **`csrc/cpu/torch_bindings.cpp`** — Declare and register the new function as `torch.ops._C.cpu_attn_has_isa`. 3. **`vllm/v1/attention/backends/cpu_attn.py`** — Update `_riscv_supports_rvv_vlen128()`: - zvl256b+ → return `False` (larger VLEN, RVV-128 kernel not compiled) - zvl128b → return `True` (explicit VLEN=128 hint) - No zvl flags → delegate to `torch.ops._C.cpu_attn_has_isa("rvv")` ## Test Plan ```bash # On RISC-V hardware without zvl flags (e.g. SG2044) python -c " import torch from vllm.v1.attention.backends.cpu_attn import _get_attn_isa print('bfloat16:', _get_attn_isa(torch.bfloat16, 128, 128)) print('float16:', _get_attn_isa(torch.float16, 128, 128)) print('float32:', _get_attn_isa(torch.float32, 128, 128)) " # Expected: all should return 'rvv' (instead of 'vec') when built with VLLM_RVV_VLEN=128 ``` ## Test Result Before: ```json { "attn_isa": { "float16": "vec", "bfloat16": "vec", "float32": "vec" } } ``` After the fix, `_get_attn_isa()` correctly returns `"rvv"` when the C++ RVV-128 kernel is compiled in, even when `/proc/cpuinfo` has no `zvlb` flags.

title: [CI] Lower granite-4.0-h-tiny gsm8k threshold for Hybrid SSM NixlConnector PD accuracy tests (4 GPUs)
author: haosdent
body:
Failing build: [Hybrid SSM NixlConnector PD accuracy tests (4 GPUs)](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/66835/canvas?sid=019e3ed4-250f-4035-99b7-e6c0ba9162c1&tab=output)

## Purpose

`ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` gsm8k under NIXL PD disagg shifted from ~0.80 to a wider, lower-mean distribution after #42430 rerouted the D-side 1-token recompute from `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` to `selective_state_update`.

Investigated the kernel divergence with a fp64 reference at bf16 inputs (the granite dtype). Both kernels hit the bf16 ULP floor (~3.7e-3 vs fp64), but they land at different points within that ball — chunk_scan goes through bf16 matmul with intermediate bf16 casts, while SSU keeps the SSM step in fp32 throughout. Neither is "more correct"; they just produce different bf16 outputs of similar magnitude error. The model's published gsm8k baseline was measured under chunk_scan's specific error pattern, so the SSU-routed recompute lands in a slightly different numeric regime and flips a few greedy-decode tokens.

Per maintainer feedback, set `expected=0.77` and widen `RTOL=0.03 → 0.05` to absorb the observed run-to-run jitter, with a TODO pointing back here for the kernel-level follow-up.

Observed measurements across recent CI runs of this test:
- #66759: 0.7498
- #66782: 0.7415
- #66835: 0.7559
- recent rerun: 0.78

Spread ~0.04 over 4 runs. `expected=0.77` with `RTOL=0.05` gives a passing window of (0.72, 0.82), covering all four measurements with ~2 pp margin.

The underlying kernel divergence (`tl.dot` bf16 cast in chunk_scan vs fp32 reduce in SSU) is left for a separate change.

title: [Model] Fix MiniCPM-V 4.6 vit_merger qkv weight loading
author: tc-mb
body:
In MiniCPMV4_6 (vllm/model_executor/models/minicpmv4_6.py), the vit_merger.self_attn module uses vLLM's fused QKVParallelLinear (a single qkv_proj), while the HuggingFace checkpoint stores the projections as three separate tensors: q_proj, k_proj, and v_proj.

Although the top-level model already declares:

packed_modules_mapping = {
    "qkv_proj": ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"],
    ...
}
AutoWeightsLoader does not correctly stack the three shards into qkv_proj for the vit_merger sub-tree. As a result, vit_merger.self_attn.qkv_proj is never populated with the pretrained weights — loading either raises missing/unexpected-key errors for vit_merger.self_attn.{q,k,v}_proj.*, or silently leaves qkv_proj at its random init, producing corrupted vision features.

Fix: add a dedicated load_weights method on MiniCPMV4_6ViTWindowAttentionSelfAttn that follows vLLM's standard stacked_params_mapping pattern — feeding q_proj / k_proj / v_proj into qkv_proj.weight_loader with shard_id="q"/"k"/"v" respectively, and falling back to default_weight_loader for the remaining parameters (e.g. out_proj).

title: Fix FlashInfer TRTLLM NvFP4 monolithic MoE routing
author: zhangxin81
body:
## Summary

This MR fixes the FlashInfer TRTLLM NvFP4 monolithic MoE path for Qwen3.5 MoE NVFP4 models.

The monolithic TRTLLM NvFP4 kernel was receiving vLLM routing metadata with subtly different semantics from FlashInfer TRTLLM. For Qwen3.5 MoE NVFP4 checkpoints, this caused the fused monolithic path to select the wrong routing behavior and quickly diverge into low-quality or repetitive generations. The fix keeps the monolithic implementation enabled and corrects the inputs passed to the FlashInfer TRTLLM fused MoE kernel instead of bypassing the issue via the modular path.

## Motivation

`TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsMonolithic` uses FlashInfer's `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` kernel to fuse routing and expert execution. vLLM's `RoutingMethodType.Renormalize` corresponds to the common `fused_topk_softmax(..., renormalize=True)` behavior:

1. softmax over router logits
2. top-k selection
3. renormalization over selected experts

FlashInfer TRTLLM, however, names this behavior `RenormalizeNaive`. Its `Renormalize` mode means a different route:

1. top-k selection
2. softmax over selected experts

Passing vLLM `Renormalize` directly to the FlashInfer TRTLLM monolithic kernel therefore selected a different router path. On the tested Qwen3.5 MoE NVFP4 checkpoint, this made the monolithic path produce incorrect and repetitive output.

## Changes



1. Map vLLM `RoutingMethodType.Renormalize` to FlashInfer TRTLLM `RoutingMethodType.RenormalizeNaive` .
   - Source: `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py:162`

## Validation

### Backend and code path validation

using FlashInfer TRTLLM NvFP4 monolithic MoE path.

### GSM8K evaluation

I evaluated the Qwen3.5 MoE NVFP4 checkpoint(fine-tuned) with the `flashinfer_trtllm` NvFP4 MoE backend before and after this fix.

Because only the GSM8K test split was available locally during this run, this comparison uses zero-shot GSM8K (`num_shots=0`) on the full 1,319-question test set. Both runs used the same model, backend, decoding parameters, and `max_model_len=4096`.

#### Commands

Before fix:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
GSM8K_MONOLITHIC_VARIANT=before PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
python /path_to_root/compare_moe_backend_out/gsm8k/run_gsm8k_eval.py \
  --variant before \
  --model /path_to_model \
  --out /path_to_root/compare_moe_backend_out/gsm8k/before_fix.json \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 0 \
  --max-tokens 256 \
  --max-model-len 4096
```

After fix:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
python /path_to_root/compare_moe_backend_out/gsm8k/run_gsm8k_eval.py \
  --variant after \
  --model /path_to_model \
  --out /path_to_root/compare_moe_backend_out/gsm8k/after_fix.json \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 0 \
  --max-tokens 256 \
  --max-model-len 4096
```

#### Results

| Variant | Accuracy | Correct / Total | Invalid Rate | Latency | Output Tokens |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Before fix | 0.016679 | 22 / 1319 | 0.131160 | 44.80s | 333,580 |
| After fix | 0.687642 | 907 / 1319 | 0.007582 | 52.49s | 225,048 |

The fix improves GSM8K accuracy by `+0.670963` absolute, from `1.67%` to `68.76%`, and reduces invalid responses from `13.12%` to `0.76%`. The after-fix run also produces substantially fewer output tokens, which is consistent with eliminating the previous repetitive/garbage generations.

title: [Bugfix] Qwen3-VL(-MoE): pass architectures to with_hf_config for pipeline parallelism
author: xonder
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #43271.

Qwen3-VL-MoE (and dense Qwen3-VL) crash at engine init with `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`:

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for VllmConfig
  Value error, No model architectures are specified
```

The inner language model is constructed from `config.text_config`, whose `architectures` is `None` (architectures only exist on the top-level config). `with_hf_config()` does not infer them, so the language model's `ModelConfig` ends up with an empty architectures list and `registry.inspect_model_cls` raises.

This passes the text-model architecture explicitly, matching the convention already used by the sibling models that construct the same language-model classes:

- `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py` → `architectures=["Qwen3MoeForCausalLM"]`
- `qwen3_asr.py` → `architectures=["Qwen3ForCausalLM"]`

## Not a duplicate

Checked for existing work before opening this (`gh pr list --search "qwen3_vl_moe"`, plus an issue/PR search for "Qwen3-VL pipeline parallel architectures") — no open issue or PR addresses this. Filed as #43271 with this PR as the fix.

## Test Plan

Serve a Qwen3-VL-MoE checkpoint across 2 nodes with pipeline parallelism:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking-AWQ \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 (and node-rank 1 --headless on the second node)
```

## Test Result

- **Before:** crashes at init with the traceback above.
- **After:** the engine initializes, loads weights, allocates the KV cache, and serves correct completions. Verified end-to-end on 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), `pipeline_parallel_size=2, tensor_parallel_size=1`, generating coherent output.

Scope note: validated end-to-end on the **MoE** path (`qwen3_vl_moe.py`). The dense `qwen3_vl.py` has the identical construction and the same latent bug; the fix uses the same idiom and the matching architecture value (`Qwen3ForCausalLM`) per `qwen3_asr.py`.

title: [CI] Fix "test_awq_load[gemma4-moe-*]" failure
author: haosdent
body:
## Purpose

Fix nightly [`Quantized Models Test #67339`](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/67339/canvas?sid=019e491f-f86c-4408-8a5a-8a3a5a9ce757&tab=output) failures of `test_awq_load[gemma4-moe-*]` introduced by #43169.

That PR sized the batched vision-encoder chunk by `0.05 * total_memory` with a cost model that counted only the encoder residual stream. On a 22 GiB L4 with a 26B AWQ model loaded (~3 GiB free), the heuristic admitted `chunk ≈ 53` and OOMed inside `Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder._position_embeddings` allocating a 2.88 GiB `F.one_hot(num_classes=position_embedding_size)` int64 buffer, which is the actual dominant transient and ~4x larger than the old cost term.

This PR sizes the chunk by currently-free GPU memory (`min(free // 2, total // 10)`) with `F.one_hot` as the dominant per-patch cost, hoists `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` out of the per-bucket loop, and extracts the math into a pure static `_encoder_chunk` for GPU-free unit testing. Batching speedup is preserved on roomy GPUs (chunk = 92 on 80 GiB A100 with 60 GiB free vs. 17 on the failing L4).

## Test Plan

Added `tests/models/multimodal/test_gemma4_mm.py` with 4 unit tests against `_encoder_chunk` (no GPU required): tight-budget allocation fits in free memory, roomy GPU keeps batching, zero-patches safe, zero-free falls back to 1.

## Test Result

Unit tests (no GPU):

```
$ pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/test_gemma4_mm.py
4 passed in 0.88s
```

Integration tests (the original failing parametrizations):

| Platform | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A30 (24 GiB) | `test_awq_load[gemma4-moe-standard-awq-dot-suffix]` | passed in 237s |
| A30 (24 GiB) | `test_awq_load[gemma4-moe-compressed-tensors-underscore-suffix]` | passed in 85s |
| A100 (80 GiB, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`) | both `gemma4-moe-*` parametrizations | 2 passed in 416s |

`profile_run` reaches the `Encoder cache will be initialized with a budget of 8192 tokens, and profiled with 3 video items of the maximum feature size.` log line, the exact point that OOMed in CI, and proceeds without `OutOfMemoryError` on both SKUs.

title: [Bugfix] Fix broken profile_modular_kernel.py
author: x41lakazam
body:
## Purpose
Make `tests/kernels/moe/modular_kernel_tools/profile_modular_kernel.py` usable again.

## Explanation
The profile_modular_kernel utility has been unrunnable on main since the modular-kernel cleanup commit 8ad7285e ([Kernels] Clean up FusedMoeMethodBase and modular kernel setup, #22035). Every invocation fails with `TypeError: FusedMoEKernel.apply() got an unexpected keyword argument 'w1_scale'`, regardless of `--pf-type` / `--experts-type`.

The fix mirrors the working call sequence in `run_modular_kernel` (common.py) / `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`:

- Build `FusedMoEQuantConfig` from the per-rank weights and pass it to `make_modular_kernel` (the third parameter is `quant_config`, not `weights`).
- Update `mk_kwargs` to the current `FusedMoEKernel.apply` signature: add `activation`, drop `w1_scale`/`w2_scale`/`a1_scale`, cast `topk_ids` with `prepare_finalize.topk_indices_dtype()` (falling back to the input dtype when the backend has no preference — `topk_indices_dtype()` can return `None`).
- Clone `hidden_states` before the timed loop; some backends mutate the input tensor in place, which would otherwise corrupt warmup iterations 2-N.
- Wrap the profiled call in `set_forward_context` (required by DP-aware prepare/finalize backends, e.g. DeepEP HT/LL).
- Build `num_tokens_across_dp` on CPU. `DPMetadata` indexes it on the host; a CUDA tensor would trigger a device-to-host sync inside the timed region and skew profiler measurements.
- Call `init_workspace_manager(...)` once per rank (normally done by `GPUModelRunner`); without it the kernels hit `WorkspaceManager not initialized` inside `_allocate_buffers`.
- Pass `device` positionally to `torch.accelerator.synchronize` to match call sites elsewhere in vLLM.

The measurement loop (5 warmups + 1 profiled apply + chrome trace export) is unchanged.

## Duplicate-PR check
No other open PR addresses `profile_modular_kernel.py`:
```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "profile_modular_kernel"
# returns only this PR.
```

## Test plan

### CI smoke test (added in this PR)
`tests/kernels/moe/test_profile_modular_kernel.py` invokes `profile_modular_kernel.run(config)` with the simplest universally-supported combination (`world_size=1`, `MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular` + `TritonExperts`, bf16, tiny shapes), then asserts a chrome trace was emitted. Runs in ~25 s, requires only a single CUDA device. Verified to fail on the unfixed harness (with the `'w1_scale'` `TypeError`) and pass on this branch.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_profile_modular_kernel.py -v
tests/kernels/moe/test_profile_modular_kernel.py::test_profile_modular_kernel_smoke PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 22 warnings in 23.45s ========================
```

### Manual before/after smoke (single-rank, GB200)
Same invocation, run once with the unchanged file from `origin/main` and once with the patched file. Single GPU, single rank, no EP.

```bash
python -m tests.kernels.moe.modular_kernel_tools.profile_modular_kernel \
  --world-size 1 \
  --pf-type MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular \
  --experts-type TritonExperts \
  --torch-trace-dir-path /tmp/traces
```

**Before (origin/main):**
```
Running m=64, topk=4 ...
TypeError: FusedMoEKernel.apply() got an unexpected keyword argument 'w1_scale'
Running m=64, topk=1 ...
TypeError: FusedMoEKernel.apply() got an unexpected keyword argument 'w1_scale'
EXIT CODE: 1
TRACES PRODUCED: 0
```

**After (this PR):**
```
Running m=64, topk=4 ...
Running m=64, topk=1 ...
EXIT CODE: 0
TRACES PRODUCED: 1   # m64_0_trace.json, 285 KB
```

(Both `m=64` configs share an output filename — pre-existing `TODO (varun): Add a descriptive trace file name`. Not addressed in this PR.)

### Wider combination matrix
The same fix has been exercised across multi-rank combinations:
- NoEP / DeepEP-HT / DeepEP-LL prepare/finalize backends
- Triton / DeepGEMM / CUTLASS / Batched-Triton / Batched-DeepGEMM / Naive-Batched / Triton-or-DeepGEMM expert kernels
- bf16 / fp8 per-tensor / fp8 block-quant quantization

```bash
python -m tests.kernels.moe.modular_kernel_tools.profile_modular_kernel \
  --pf-type <PF> --experts-type <EXPERTS> --quant-dtype <DTYPE> \
  --torch-trace-dir-path /tmp/traces
```

title: [CI] Fix test_lora_with_spec_decode on V2 model runner
author: haosdent
body:
## Purpose

Fix [Spec Decode Draft Model](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/67339/canvas?sid=019e491f-f878-435f-8c62-f9d811d79906&tab=output) and [Spec Decode Draft Model Nightly B200](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/67339/canvas?sid=019e491f-f87a-4c08-9901-62184eae3614&tab=output): `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_lora_with_spec_decode.py::test_batch_inference_correctness` failed 76/100 since #43139 landed (was 100/100 before).

Root cause: the `LoRAMapping(0,0)` workaround in V2's `_run_model_forward` dummy_run resolves to all-`-1` indices, which sets `no_lora_flag_cpu = True`. The Python wrapper around `lora_shrink/expand` then short-circuits, so the LoRA Triton kernels are never launched at capture time and the cudagraph contains no LoRA work. Replay at real inference silently skips the LoRA delta.

Fix: new `PunicaWrapperBase.prepare_for_cudagraph_capture()` sets `no_lora_flag_cpu = False` and `num_active_loras_cpu = 1`, leaving `active_lora_ids` all `-1`. The kernel launch is captured into the cudagraph, but each CTA hits the existing per-CTA `if lora_id == -1: return` early-exit inside the kernel (`lora_shrink_op.py:74`, `lora_expand_op.py:67`) and does no work. At real inference, `set_active_loras` overwrites the slot index and the captured kernels run. Applied to every wrapper in `punica_wrapper_mapping` so MM tower/connector paths are covered.

## Test Plan

```
pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_lora_with_spec_decode.py::test_batch_inference_correctness
```

## Test Result

Test in H20:
- baseline (commit `050611a3d`): FAIL `match ratio: 76/100`
- with this fix: PASS `match ratio: 100/100` (verified twice)

title: [CI] Fix AMD docker build tests
author: haosdent
body:
## Purpose

Fix an intermittent ROCm wheel-build [race in CI (AMD: :docker: build image)](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/67384/canvas?sid=019e4a21-b199-4ba9-94ec-2f29928d4bd2&tab=output) introduced by #42663. Four parallel `hipify${NAME}` cmake targets share `${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/csrc`; when their `shutil.copytree` + `matched_files_iter` calls overlap, one process reads a `.cu` mid-copy, reports `[skipped, no changes]`, and the matching `.hip` byproduct (e.g. `paged_attention_v1.hip`) is never produced, failing the wheel build.

Replace the four targets with a single `hipify_all` that runs `cmake/hipify.py` once on the union of sources. A `FATAL_ERROR` guard catches new HIP extensions added after the finalizer call.

Test AMD build image via CI

title: [Bugfix] FusedMoE: coerce shape-(1,) per-tensor scales to 0-D scalar …
author: V-3604
body:
Fixes #43297 ## Purpose I checked open and merged PR's for `_load_per_tensor_weight_scale` and issue #43297, no existing PR addressed this issue. `FusedMoE._load_per_tensor_weight_scale` assumed per-tensor weight scales arrive as 0-D scalars. llm-compressor NVFP4 presets emit them as shape-(1,) tensors by default (`torch.tensor([x])` rather than `torch.tensor(x)`). PyTorch's `copy_()` path rejects the `(1,) -> ()` broadcast: RuntimeError: output with shape [] doesn't match the broadcast shape [1] This crashes server init for any compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE artifact produced by llm-compressor before any inference runs. Fix: call `.view([])` on `loaded_weight` in both the w1/w3 and w2 assignment, paths. `.view([])` coerces a singleton tensor to a 0-D scalar in-place (no copy), and raises error if the tensor has more than one element. ## Test Plan Standalone reproducer (torch only, no GPU or model weights needed): ```python import torch, torch.nn as nn param = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(4, 2, dtype=torch.float32), requires_grad=False) slot = param.data[0][0] slot.copy_(torch.tensor([0.5])) # RuntimeError before fix slot.copy_(torch.tensor([0.5]).view([])) # passes after fix ``` ## Test Result ## AI Assistance disclosure Local test file and PR descrioption written with AI assistance. title: [Bugfix] Map reasoning_effort to enable_thinking in chat template kwargs
author: ashwing
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the Responses API not surfacing reasoning output when `--reasoning-parser gemma4` is active and `reasoning: {"effort": "high"}` is passed
- Maps `reasoning_effort` to `enable_thinking` in `chat_template_kwargs` for both Chat Completions and Responses API
- Models like Gemma4 whose chat template defaults `enable_thinking` to `false` now correctly activate thinking when reasoning is requested

Fixes #43395

## Root Cause

Gemma4's chat template requires explicit `enable_thinking=True` to inject the `<|think|>` token and activate reasoning mode (line 181 of the template: `if enable_thinking is defined and enable_thinking`). The Responses API passed `reasoning_effort` as a raw kwarg but never translated it to `enable_thinking`, so the model never entered thinking mode.

DeepSeek R1/V3 worked because their parser auto-sets `enable_thinking=True` in `__init__`. Qwen3 worked because its template defaults thinking to `True`.

## Changes

- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py`: Inject `enable_thinking=True` in `build_chat_params()` when `reasoning.effort` is non-None (and `False` when `"none"`)
- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py`: Same mapping for Chat Completions consistency
- User's explicit `enable_thinking` in `chat_template_kwargs` is respected (not overridden)
- For templates that don't declare `enable_thinking`, `resolve_chat_template_kwargs` filters it out automatically — no impact on other models

## Test plan

- [x] 14 unit tests covering all edge cases (effort levels, "none", no reasoning, explicit user override)
- [x] Integration test on Docker (vllm/vllm-openai:latest, Gemma4 26B, TP=4, A100):
  - Responses API with `reasoning.effort=high` → `reasoning_tokens: 442`, `ResponseReasoningItem` present
  - Responses API without reasoning → no thinking injected (no regression)
  - Chat Completions with `reasoning_effort=high` → reasoning correctly surfaced
- [x] Verified `resolve_chat_template_kwargs` filters `enable_thinking` for non-thinking models

## Related

- PR #38100 (open) — maps `reasoning_effort="none"` → `enable_thinking=False` for Qwen3. Our fix is complementary (handles the inverse direction: activating thinking when reasoning is requested).
- Issue #42962 — docs about `chat_template_kwargs` in Responses API

title: [Reasoning] [Bugfix] Reject invalid thinking_token_budget values
author: linzm1007
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose

Fix incorrect handling of invalid `thinking_token_budget` values in the OpenAI-compatible API and `SamplingParams`.

Previously, negative values (e.g. `-2`) were accepted and passed into `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder`, which immediately forced an empty reasoning block. Completion API docs also implied `-1` meant "unlimited", but that value still activated budget tracking. This PR rejects invalid inputs with `VLLMValidationError` (HTTP 400), matching how other request parameters (e.g. `logprobs`, `prompt_logprobs`) are validated. `-1` is normalized to `None` to preserve the documented unlimited semantics.

**Changes:**
- Add `validate_thinking_token_budget()` in `vllm/sampling_params.py` to reject negative, non-integer, and boolean values.
- Add `ThinkingTokenBudget` (`Annotated` + `BeforeValidator`) for request field parsing so invalid values are rejected before type coercion.
- Apply validation in `SamplingParams.__post_init__`, `ChatCompletionRequest`, and `CompletionRequest`.
- Add unit tests for validation, request parsing, and rejection of invalid `SamplingParams`.

**Why this is not a duplicate:** Searched open PRs for `thinking_token_budget` / `thinking budget validate`; no existing PR addresses invalid-value rejection. Related PRs (#20859, #34668) implement the feature itself, not input validation.

**Behavior change:**
| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-1` | Budget tracking enabled despite "unlimited" docs | Accepted; normalized to `None` (no budget limit) |
| `-2` | Budget tracking enabled; could force empty reasoning | Request rejected with `VLLMValidationError` (HTTP 400) |
| `0.6`, `10.5`, `3.14` | Passed through or failed with generic type error | Request rejected with `VLLMValidationError` (HTTP 400) |
| `True` | Could be accepted as `1` (bool is subclass of int) | Request rejected with `VLLMValidationError` (HTTP 400) |
| `0`, positive int | Applied as budget | Unchanged |
| omitted / `null` | Unset | Unchanged |

title: [Bugfix] Detect wrong libcute_dsl_runtime.so variant in FlashInfer GDN
author: arpera
body:
## Purpose

Detect a packaging conflict in `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]` that silently breaks FlashInfer's Blackwell GDN prefill kernel — and, by extension, any other cuTe-DSL-based kernel.

`nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-base` and `nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13` both ship into the shared `nvidia_cutlass_dsl/` namespace and write many of the same on-disk paths (the runtime `.so`, MLIR Python bindings, cuTe-DSL Python sources) with different content. Whichever wheel extracts last wins; with a parallel installer (`uv pip install`) the order is racy, and the resulting venv can end up with a mix of files from both variants. The `-libs-base` variant fails MLIR legalization for `tcgen05.make_tmem_copy` and crashes the server when the FlashInfer Blackwell GDN kernel (#40717) JIT-compiles. The same install command on the same host can produce a working or broken venv depending on extraction order. Affects every `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.5.x release we have looked at. Tracked upstream at [NVIDIA/cutlass#3259](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/issues/3259).

This PR adds a runtime check in `_should_use_flashinfer_gdn_prefill` that walks every file declared in `nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13`'s wheel `RECORD`, re-hashes it on disk, and compares against the SHA-256 the wheel itself declares. The check is version-agnostic — it asks `importlib.metadata` for whatever `-libs-cu13` is installed and reads that wheel's own `RECORD`. On any mismatch we log a `warning_once` with the repair command and fall back to Triton/FLA instead of crashing. Result is cached per-process; returns False on any error (uninstalled, missing RECORD, missing file) so older / non-Blackwell setups are unaffected.

## Test Result

TODO

```
# Server
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size <TP>
```

| `nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13` install state | Before this PR | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| intact (every on-disk file matches RECORD) | server starts, FI GDN used | server starts, FI GDN used |
| contaminated (one or more files come from `-libs-base`) | server crashes with MLIR ICE in `tcgen05.make_tmem_copy` legalization | warning logged, falls back to Triton/FLA, server starts |

The contaminated state is reproduced by running `pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-base` after a normal install (or by losing the `uv` install race). The intact state is restored by `pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13`.

title: [rust] fix: aggregate `is_sleeping` and `reset_prefix_cache` across DP engines
author: willamhou
body:
## Summary
- `is_sleeping()` now verifies all DP engines agree and returns the new `Error::InconsistentUtilityResults` if they don't, instead of silently using only engine 0's value.
- `reset_prefix_cache()` AND-aggregates per-engine results, so it reports success only when every engine confirms the reset.
- Adds `Error::InconsistentUtilityResults { method, values }`.

All changes are scoped to `rust/src/engine-core-client/`.

## Background

title: [Bugfix] hadacore_transform: respect inplace parameter to fix garbage outputs with QuIP transforms
author: Yatimai
body:
## Purpose

Fix garbage outputs from QuIP transforms on Blackwell GPUs under `torch.compile` + CUDA graph capture. Initially observed on RTX 5090 (SM120); since reproduced on B200 (SM100) with the v0.21.0 prebuilt wheel + torch 2.11.0. Addresses the runtime side of vllm-project/llm-compressor#2006.

## Background

The `hadacore_transform` op is declared with a mutable schema:

```cpp
ops.def("hadacore_transform(Tensor! x, bool inplace) -> Tensor");
```

Two interacting issues:

**1. Kernel ignores the `inplace` parameter (latent bug).** In `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/hadamard/hadacore/hadamard_transform_cuda.cu`, the kernel always writes to `x.data_ptr()` regardless of `inplace`:

```cpp
torch::stable::Tensor out = inplace ? x : torch::stable::empty_like(x);
hadacore::run_fht<SCALAR_TYPE>(x.data_ptr(), x.data_ptr(), x.numel(), ...);
// `inplace=False` callers receive `out`, but `out` was never written to
return torch::stable::reshape(out, res_shape);
```

The conditional copy-back cannot fire because `out` is only aliased to `x` when `inplace=True`. The path is currently unused in vLLM but is publicly exposed.

**2. Mutable schema causes inductor to elide protective clones.** In `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod.apply()`, the `.clone()` introduced in #26849 for compile robustness:

```python
x[:, start:start+length] = self.output_transform(
    x[:, start:start+length].clone(), part_id=part_id
)
```

Inductor analyzes the `Tensor!` schema, decides the clone is redundant (the op will mutate anyway), and elides it from the FX graph (verified via `TORCH_LOGS="output_code"`). The kernel ends up receiving a slice view aliasing `x`, producing garbage outputs under `torch.compile` + cudagraph. Initially observed on SM120; later also reproduced on B200 (SM100) with the v0.21.0 prebuilt wheel + torch 2.11.0 (QuIP variants: WikiText-2 PPL ~1.4e6; coherent with `enforce_eager=True`). @mgoin's `gsm8k_eval` in #28748 (0.697) used a combination that does not trigger the inductor elision: whether the bug manifests depends on the (torch version x compile/cudagraph) configuration, not the hardware.

| Test | Hardware | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| W4A16 + QuIP, compile | RTX 5090 | ❌ Garbage | ✅ Coherent |
| NVFP4A16 + QuIP, compile | RTX 5090 | ❌ Garbage | ✅ Coherent |
| NVFP4A16 only, compile | RTX 5090 | ✅ Coherent | ✅ Byte-identical |
| NVFP4A16 + QuIP, cudagraph, v0.21.0 wheel + torch 2.11 | B200 | ❌ Garbage (PPL ~1.4e6) | N/A |
| Same, `enforce_eager=True` | B200 | ✅ Coherent (6.84) | N/A |
| Kernel sanity (`inplace=True` vs `False`) | B200 | N/A | ✅ max diff 0.0 |
| `gsm8k_eval` @mgoin SpinQuant model | B200 | 0.697 (#28748) | 0.697 |

## Changes

Kernel writes to `out.data_ptr()` instead of `x.data_ptr()` (respects `inplace`); call sites in `module.py` pass `inplace=False` to opt into the non-aliasing path. The existing `.clone()` from #26849 is retained as a defensive layer.

## Reproduction

The bug manifests on any compressed-tensors checkpoint using online Hadamard transforms (QuIP) under vLLM's default `torch.compile` + cudagraph execution. The root cause is in the kernel, independent of the calibration path. It also blocks the MXFP4 W4A4 + MR-GPTQ path (where rotations contribute ~+3 pts PPL recovery vs GPTQ alone on Llama-3.1-8B) and any future recipe relying on online Hadamard rotations.

### Step 1: produce a QuIP-transformed checkpoint

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor
cd llm-compressor
pip install -e .

# QuIP + GPTQ + NVFP4A16 example from vllm-project/llm-compressor#2751 (~10 min):
gh pr checkout 2751
python examples/transform/nvfp4_quip_gptq_example.py
# produces Llama-3.1-8B-quip-gptq-nvfp4a16
```

The attached logs were produced with an equivalent minimal datafree variant (`examples/transform/quip_example.py` adapted to the NVFP4A16 scheme, on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, producing `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quip-nvfp4a16`). Both recipes trigger the same bug.

### Step 2: reproduce the failure on `main`

```bash
# vLLM main branch build (per-commit nightly wheel; the version string embeds the main commit)
pip install vllm==0.22.1rc1.dev255+g4dcd10eb0 --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly

VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 python validate_nvfp4_quip.py <checkpoint_dir>
```

(`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` works around an unrelated FlashInfer sampler init failure on SM120 with this build; it does not affect the transform path.)

`validate_nvfp4_quip.py` is a minimal 5-prompt sanity script (greedy, `max_tokens=80`, vLLM defaults, no `enforce_eager`):

<details>
<summary>validate_nvfp4_quip.py</summary>

```python
import sys

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

CHECKPOINT_DIR = (
    sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quip-nvfp4a16"
)

PROMPTS = [
    "The capital of France is",
    "Quantum mechanics is the branch of physics that",
    "Once upon a time, in a distant kingdom,",
    "def fibonacci(n):\n    ",
    "Translate to French: 'Hello, how are you today?'\nFrench:",
]

SAMPLING = SamplingParams(max_tokens=80, temperature=0.0)


def main() -> None:
    print(f"Loading checkpoint: {CHECKPOINT_DIR}")
    model = LLM(model=CHECKPOINT_DIR, dtype="auto")

    print(f"\nRunning {len(PROMPTS)} sanity generations...\n")
    outputs = model.generate(PROMPTS, SAMPLING)

    for i, output in enumerate(outputs):
        print(f"=== Prompt {i + 1}/{len(PROMPTS)} ===")
        print(f"PROMPT: {output.prompt!r}")
        print(f"OUTPUT: {output.outputs[0].text!r}")
        print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

**Failure on `main` @ `4dcd10eb0` (RTX PRO 6000 / SM120, torch 2.11.0, engine `v0.22.1rc1.dev255+g4dcd10eb0`):**

<details>
<summary>Garbage output (NVFP4A16 + QuIP) on main</summary>

```text
=== Prompt 1/5 ===
PROMPT: 'The capital of France is'
OUTPUT: 'inousMainFrameublangينهift sweepsăngalseroGaplugpletσί้าวorneềnatomliteatoreCtrls...'
```

All 5 prompts garbage. Full log (engine version visible in the log): `validate_quip_nvfp4a16_MAIN_GARBAGE.log` (attached).

</details>

Notably, on this main build, dynamo itself now flags the aliasing this PR fixes:

```text
UserWarning: _C::hadacore_transform (with implementation in ???): The output of this custom
operator (1) must not also be an input to this custom operator and (2) may not alias any inputs
to this custom operator or other returns. [...] This is deprecated and will become an error in
PyTorch 2.12.
```

Same failure also reproduced on the `v0.22.1` release (`g0decac0d9`), and previously on `v0.21.0`: RTX 5090 (`validate_quip_nvfp4a16_GARBAGE.log`, `validate_quip_w4a16_GARBAGE.log`, attached) and B200 SM100 with the prebuilt wheel + torch 2.11.0 (WikiText-2 PPL ~1.4e6; coherent 6.84 with `enforce_eager=True`). The trigger is the (torch version x compile/cudagraph) combination, not the hardware alone.

## Test Plan

Same command, with this PR's commit cherry-picked onto the **same main commit** (the fix touches `csrc/`, so a full build is required):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm && cd vllm
git checkout 4dcd10eb0  # same main commit as the failing run above
git fetch https://github.com/Yatimai/vllm.git fix/hadacore-respect-inplace
git cherry-pick 9867bb81d658787e31c7fce0290cce173e40c742
TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation

VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 python validate_nvfp4_quip.py <checkpoint_dir>
```

Only delta between the two runs is this PR's 3-line change (same GPU, same checkpoint, same command, same base commit).

## Test Result

**On `main` @ `4dcd10eb0` + this fix (engine `v0.22.1rc1.dev256+g1ea902a7c`, same GPU / checkpoint / command):**

<details>
<summary>Coherent output (NVFP4A16 + QuIP) on main + fix</summary>

```text
=== Prompt 1/5 ===

OUTPUT: ' Paris, and it is also the most visited city in the world. Paris is known for its beautiful architecture, art museums, and fashion...'
```

All 5 prompts coherent (incl. correct fibonacci code and French translation). Full log: `validate_quip_nvfp4a16_BRANCH_OK.log` (attached).

</details>

Earlier validation on v0.21-era builds (RTX 5090): `validate_cppFIX_nvfp4a16_OK.log`, and the W4A16 variant `validate_cppFIX_w4a16_OK.log` (attached).

**No-regression checks:**

title: Fix RunAI streamer tensor buffer reuse during weight loading
author: bbartels
body:
## Purpose
Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43163.
`runai_safetensors_weights_iterator` currently yields tensors directly from RunAI Model Streamer. The streamer may reuse internal tensor buffers, so downstream code that retains a yielded tensor beyond the current iterator step can observe overwritten contents.
This PR makes the RunAI loader yield cloned tensors, so the iterator provides tensors that are safe to retain after advancing the iterator. This matches the expected behavior for model loading paths that temporarily buffer or reorder weights.
The change is intentionally scoped to the RunAI safetensors iterator.

title: [feature][kv_offload] Self-describing KV events for OffloadingConnector
author: Change72
body:
## What

This PR makes native `OffloadingConnector` CPU-offload KV-cache events self-describing behind an
explicit opt-in:

```python
kv_connector_extra_config={
    "self_describing_kv_events": True,
}
```

The flag is inert unless vLLM KV cache events are also enabled. With the flag off, the connector
keeps the legacy placeholder *payload* (`token_ids=[]`, `block_size=0`, `parent_block_hash=None`);
note that stored events are now emitted one-per-offload-key rather than one-per-batch.

The implementation isolates the event payload logic in `events.py`, derives
`OffloadingKVEventsConfig` once from the vLLM KV-event config plus connector extra config, and
carries per-group KV-cache metadata through `OffloadingEventGroupSpec`. The opt-in is documented in
`docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`.

For CPU offload stores, the connector now records the request metadata while it still has access
to the request and KV-cache-group context, then emits `BlockStored` events with:

- `block_hashes`
- `parent_block_hash`
- `token_ids`
- per-block `block_size`
- LoRA metadata
- `group_idx` and cache-spec metadata

For chunked offloading (`kv_connector_extra_config["block_size"] > --block-size`), one offloaded
CPU chunk is emitted as one `BlockStored` carrying all constituent per-block hashes plus the whole
chunk token span. `block_size` remains the GPU/hash block size, not the whole chunk size. Removal
events fan out the same constituent hashes.

## Why

The legacy connector events were useful for observability but not sufficient for external routers
or lower-tier indexers. They often carried placeholder payloads (`token_ids=[]`, `block_size=0`,
`parent_block_hash=None`), so consumers such as Dynamo could not reconstruct their own block keys
or parent chain and had to drop the CPU-tier events.

Making the producer self-describing keeps the event contract local to the connector: a consumer
does not need to join CPU events with a separate GPU event stream or depend on event ordering.

## Chunk overlap semantics

The producer intentionally uses plain fan-out. In chunk mode, if a shared prefix is not aligned to
the offloaded chunk size, two sibling chunks can legitimately list the same constituent per-block
hash. In that case duplicate store/remove announcements are expected on the wire.

Consumers that index at per-block granularity must ref-count or deduplicate those duplicate
announcements. Dynamo's standard worker publisher path already does this with `EventDedupFilter`.
Filter-less consumers may conservatively under-credit CPU-tier cache after overlapping chunk
evictions, but this does not create data corruption.

## Scope

- Native `OffloadingConnector`.
- `CPUOffloadingSpec` / single-tier CPU offload.
- Full-attention groups.
- By-block mode and chunk mode.
- Sliding-window / SSM groups keep the legacy placeholder payload.
- `TieringOffloadingSpec` rejects `self_describing_kv_events` for now; multi-tier support needs a
  follow-up design that preserves event metadata across tier transitions.
- `extra_keys`-heavy workloads such as multimodal/cache-salt/prompt-embedding paths should be
  validated separately before relying on the new payload for routing.

## Tests

Unit coverage is split between a focused event-tracker test file and scheduler-level integration
coverage.

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py` covers:

- by-block self-describing `BlockStored`
- chunked store/remove with multiple constituent hashes
- cross-batch parent chaining
- order-independent store emission
- opt-out placeholder behavior
- sliding-window fallback behavior
- multi-group removal grouping
- store -> remove -> re-store after eviction
- reset behavior
- `TieringOffloadingSpec` scope guard

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py` keeps the scheduler-level
integration coverage.

Validated on the workstation:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py -q
# 9 passed

python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
# 70 passed
```

The latest GitHub `pre-commit` check also passes on the PR head.

## End-to-end validation

Validated with [Dynamo PR #10368](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/10368) on a real single-GPU L4 stack:

- model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`
- vLLM block size: 16
- offloaded chunk size: 48 (`factor=3`)
- CPU pool: 128 MiB, intentionally small to force real CPU LRU evictions
- explicit ZMQ KV events enabled
- `self_describing_kv_events=true`
- Dynamo worker publisher `EventDedupFilter` in the path

Result:

- CPU `BlockStored`: 354 events, zero placeholders, every CPU chunk store has `n_hashes=3`
- CPU `BlockRemoved`: 24 events from real CPU evictions
- GPU `BlockStored`: 331 events
- router metric `kv_cache_events_applied`: stored ok = 685, removed ok = 24
- zero lower-tier warnings / `BlockNotFound`

## Duplication check

Not a duplicate. `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "self_describing_kv_events"`
returns only this PR (#43468). Nearby open `OffloadingConnector` / KV-offload PRs address different
concerns, for example #43946 (eviction-triggered store), #44295 (request convoy on shared loading
blocks), #42992 (DSV4 crash fix), #45693 (hugepage tiering), and #44865 (reshape per-group transfer
data model). #44865 is the closest in surface area (it touches per-group offload specs/alignment)
but is orthogonal to self-describing KV events.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance. The human submitter has reviewed every changed line,
runs the tests, and owns the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix] Apply fc_norm in Eagle3DeepseekV2 combine_hidden_states
author: yubofredwang
body:
## Purpose

Fix missing `fc_norm` application in `Eagle3DeepseekV2ForCausalLM.combine_hidden_states()`.

PR #42764 added `fc_norm` support for EAGLE-3 post-norm speculators. The `fc_norm` `ModuleList` is correctly created in `__init__` and weights are loaded, but `combine_hidden_states()` in `deepseek_eagle3.py` never applies it — the hidden states go straight to `self.model.fc()` without normalization.

The `llama_eagle3.py` variant correctly applies `fc_norm` in its `combine_hidden_states()`, but `deepseek_eagle3.py` was missed.

## Test Plan

- Verified that `fc_norm` weights are loaded but produce no effect without this fix
- Tested with EAGLE-3 speculator with `fc_norm: true` in config against a DeepSeek-architecture target model
