title: [Bugfix] CohereModel.load_weights: skip modelopt _quantizer.* keys
author: KaletoAI
body:
## Description

ModelOpt NVFP4 exports of Cohere / Command-A models include raw quantizer-module state keys named `*.weight_quantizer._double_scale` (and similar). These are modelopt calibration-time artifacts — superseded at runtime by the exported `weight_scale` / `weight_scale_2` parameters — but they are not registered parameters on the vLLM-side `CohereModel`. `CohereModel.load_weights` then raises a `KeyError` when it tries to dispatch them, exactly as reported in #41925:

```
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/commandr.py", line 392, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name]
KeyError: 'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight_quantizer._double_scale'
```

This is the same pattern Llama / Gemma already handle silently — Cohere lacked the equivalent guard.

## Fix

A 6-line skip inside the `for name, loaded_weight in weights:` loop in `CohereModel.load_weights` — drop any name containing `_quantizer.` before parameter dispatch. Non-quantized Cohere checkpoints are unaffected (no such keys exist there). `CohereForCausalLM.load_weights` delegates via `AutoWeightsLoader` so no second site needs patching.

## Testing

Verified end-to-end with a Cohere2 Command-A NVFP4 checkpoint — Fallen-Command-A-111B-v1.1, the model from the issue's reproduction: loads cleanly and generates coherent text on a Blackwell GB10 Spark (`FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` for the NVFP4 GEMM, FlashInfer attention backend). Without this patch, weight loading aborted at the first quantized layer.

Fixes #41925

title: [KV Connector][Bugfix] MooncakeStore: don't double-apply Eagle prune in load_mask
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Summary

Fixes silent KV-cache corruption on `MooncakeStoreConnector` loads when speculative decoding with Eagle/MTP is enabled. The recv-side `load_mask` was re-applying the last-block pop that `client.lookup` had already applied, so the trailing block of every cache hit was silently dropped — leaving uninitialized KV in the local pool while the scheduler had already claimed it as cached.

Observed on MiniMax + MTP/EAGLE-3 cross-instance store loads as catastrophic generation corruption (hallucinated system prompts, dropped/swapped user prompts). Silent on non-MTP workloads because `use_eagle=False` makes neither phase pop.

### Walkthrough (block_size=16, 64-token prompt fully in store, MTP on)

1. Scheduler: `client.lookup(token_len=64)` → `find_longest_cache_hit(..., use_eagle=True)` pops one block → returns `hit_length=48`.
2. Recv: `_handle_request` runs with `token_len=48`.
   - `db.process_tokens(48, ...)` yields **3 chunks** (start = 0, 16, 32). Does not touch eagle.
   - Pre-fix `coord.load_mask(block_hashes, 48)` delegated to `find_longest_cache_hit(..., use_eagle=True)` again and popped a second block → mask length **2**.
3. The 3rd chunk fails `chunk_idx >= len(mask)` and is silently skipped. Tokens [32, 48) are allocated in local KV but never written. Every subsequent attention reads garbage at that range.

### Fix

Thread `apply_eagle: bool = True` through `MooncakeStoreCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` and `_find_hit_blocks`. `load_mask` calls with `apply_eagle=False`. Lookup callers keep the default — the scheduling decision still needs the eagle pop (the drafter requires the last-block hidden state).

### Not a duplicate of #43494

That PR fixes block-misalignment of `kvpool_cached_tokens` for the `num_external_hit_tokens == request.num_tokens` full-hit path, in `scheduler.py` and `worker.py`. This PR touches `coordinator.py` only and addresses an independent corruption path that activates whenever a Mooncake load occurs with `use_eagle=True`. The bugs are mechanically distinct; the two PRs share no files.

## Test plan

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py` — 22 passed (includes 4 new regression tests: lookup-with-eagle behavior, load_mask single FullAttn, load_mask hybrid FullAttn+SWA, non-eagle path unchanged)
- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_{worker,scheduler,connector,hma_e2e}.py` — 76 passed
- [x] Cross-instance MTP→MTP load on MiniMax (the original repro) — verifying

## Notes

AI assistance was used in tracing the bug and drafting the patch.

title: Fix CuPy runtime deps and restore humming
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

#43492 temporarily reverted #42540 because #43480 looked like a humming import issue, but #43528 shows the same `pytest` failure still happens after humming was removed. The shared root cause is that `vllm-openai:nightly` installs KV connectors by default, `lmcache` pulls the recently released `cupy-cuda13x==14.1.0`, and that CuPy release imports `pytest` from `cupy.testing._random` when PyTorch custom-op registration walks loaded modules via `inspect`.

This constrains KV connector installs to `cupy-cuda13x < 14.1.0`, which resolves to `14.0.1`, and restores humming with `humming-kernels[cu13]==0.1.2` plus the CUDA 12 extra rewrite. I checked dependency resolution and the relevant import order with `pytest` blocked: `torch -> cupy 14.0.1 -> humming` succeeds.

title: [Bugfix] Split attention groups by num_heads_q for spec-decode drafts
author: lucianommartins
body:
## Purpose

Fix a hard crash at engine init for any spec-decode setup whose draft layers have a different per-rank `num_heads_q` than the target model. Surfaced today by Gemma4 MTP (target = 8 Q-heads, assistant draft = 4 Q-heads, both 1 KV-head):

```
AssertionError: All layers in one attention group must share num_heads;
got {8, 4} for ['language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn', ...,
                'draft_model.layers.0.self_attn.attn', ...,
                'draft_model.layers.2.self_attn.attn'].
```

The assertion was added by #42650 (`get_num_attention_heads_from_layers`, `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py:158`). The assertion itself is correct — the metadata builder's `softmax_segm_*` (Triton) and `num_qo_heads` (FlashInfer) scratch is sized by a single `num_heads_q` per group. The actual bug is upstream of the assertion: `get_attn_backends_for_group` at `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:6562` keys `AttentionGroup`s by `(backend_cls_name, per_layer_kv_cache_spec)` only. `KVCacheSpec` captures `num_kv_heads`, `head_size`, `block_size`, `dtype` but **not** `num_heads_q`, so a target layer and a spec-decode draft layer with matching KV layout but different Q-head counts hash to the same key, land in one `AttentionGroup`, and feed mixed Q-head counts into the builder.

Pre-#42650 the same grouping bug existed but was silently safe in the target > draft direction (scratch was sized from `model_config.get_num_attention_heads()` — the model-wide / target value — and draft kernels wrote into a subset of slots). #42650 promotes the latent bug to a hard crash.

### Affected

All four must hold:
1. Spec-decode is active (MTP / EAGLE / standalone draft).
2. Draft `num_heads_q` differs from target's.
3. Target and draft layers share a `KVCacheSpec` (same KV-side layout).
4. Backend reads per-layer heads via `get_num_attention_heads_from_layers`, i.e. `TRITON_ATTN` or `FLASHINFER`.

### Not affected

- EAGLE drafts that reuse the target's layer structure (same `num_heads`).
- DeepSeek v3/v4 MTP — the MTP layer is the last layer of the target model itself, so `num_heads` matches by construction.
- `FLASH_ATTN`, MLA, `FlexAttention`, ROCm backends (none call the new helper).
- Laguna XS.2 (the model #42650 was fixing) — its per-layer head differences correspond to different `KVCacheSpec`s and already split into distinct `KVCacheGroup`s upstream; uniformity within each group is preserved.

### Fix

Local to `get_attn_backends_for_group`. Extend the dedup key and `AttentionGroupKey` `NamedTuple` with `layers[layer_name].num_heads` so mismatched-Q-head layers split into separate `AttentionGroup`s. Each group's metadata builder is then sized correctly for its own `num_heads_q`. `KVCacheGroup` layout and shared KV memory are unchanged; only the metadata-builder boundary moves.

Uses `getattr(..., "num_heads", 0)` for non-Attention layer types (`MambaMixer`, `ShortConv`) that do not expose `num_heads`. Such layers never coexist with Attention in a single `KVCacheGroup` (different `KVCacheSpec`), so the fallback can never spuriously merge them with attention layers.

### CI gap closed

`.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml` job "Spec Decode Speculators + MTP" already runs the `gemma4-e4b` MTP e2e case via `-k "mtp_correctness"`, but its `source_file_dependencies` omitted `vllm/v1/attention/backends/`, so #42650 did not trigger it. One added line closes that gap.

Note: the `gemma4-e4b` case itself still skips on CI's pinned `transformers==5.5.3` (`pytest.skip` at `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py:794-798` and `min_transformers_version="5.8.0"` at `tests/models/registry.py:1545`). `Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM` / `model_type: "gemma4_assistant"` is a separate transformers module that landed in `v5.8.0` (commit `2c7d385621`, "First model", #45788). Lowering the version gate is not safe here — the assistant module simply does not exist in 5.5.x. The dep edit therefore activates the trigger today (for the `mimo`, `deepseek`, `qwen3_5-hybrid` cases of the same parametrize) and additionally covers `gemma4-e4b` the moment vllm's transformers pin moves to `>=5.8.0`.

## Test Plan

End-to-end on a single host (8x A100 80GB), using the same prompt set, sampling config (`temperature=0`, greedy), `--max-num-seqs=1`, `--max-new-tokens=256`, `--max-model-len=8192` for E2B (`google/gemma-4-E2B-it`) dense model.

Same procedure repeated for 26B MoE (`google/gemma-4-26B-it`) with and without its assistant draft.

Existing in-tree unit test that exercises `initialize_attn_backend` (the function containing the patched code) — re-run after the patch to confirm the uniform-heads path is unchanged:

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_hybrid_cache_integration
```

Lint / pre-commit (per AGENTS.md):

```bash
pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml \
                       vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py
```

## Test Result

Functional (Gemma4 E2B + assistant, MTP γ=4, c=1) bit-identical to pre-#42650 reference run (greedy / deterministic), confirming the fix doesn't alter token-level decisions:

| Metric              | Pre-#42650 ref | Post-fix | Δ                  |
|---------------------|----------------|----------|--------------------|
| Block Efficiency    | 2.6444         | 2.6444   | exact              |
| Acceptance Rate     | 0.4111         | 0.4111   | exact              |
| Verification Rounds | 10,889         | 10,889   | exact              |
| Accepted Tokens     | 17,906         | 17,906   | exact              |
| Drafted Tokens      | 43,556         | 43,556   | exact              |
| Total Tokens        | 28,738         | 28,738   | exact              |
| Throughput (tok/s)  | 223.10         | 225.06   | +0.9% (jitter)     |
| Elapsed (s)         | 128.81         | 127.69   | -0.9% (jitter)     |

Manually validated combinations on 8x A100:

- E2B (dense) baseline — passes.
- E2B + assistant MTP — passes (this was the failure case).
- 26B (MoE) baseline — passes.
- 26B + assistant MTP — passes.

**Regression / lint**:

- `pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_hybrid_cache_integration` — passes (uniform-heads path unchanged).
- `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` — all 14 applicable hooks green (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos`, `mypy`, SPDX, etc.).

title: Fix the E8M0 scale computation in the MXFP4 (W4A4) MOE CUTLASS kernel
author: xin3he
body:
## Purpose

Fix the E8M0 scale computation in the MXFP4 (W4A4) MOE CUTLASS kernel, which
currently produces severely incorrect quantization results.

Related PR: #37463

## Root Cause

The original code computes the E8M0 scale factor via:

```c++
// Old (buggy):
float SFValue = vecMax * reciprocal_approximate_ftz(6.0f);  // vecMax / 6.0
uint32_t tmp = reinterpret_cast<uint32_t&>(SFValue) >> 23;
fp8SFVal = tmp & 0xff;  // scale_exp = biased_exponent(vecMax / 6.0)
```

This is **mathematically wrong** because:

floor(log2(a / b)) != floor(log2(a)) - floor(log2(b))

Dividing by 6.0 *before* extracting the exponent shifts the mantissa boundary,
causing the resulting exponent to be 1 too small for a large fraction of inputs.
When the scale is too small, `vecMax / scale` far exceeds 6.0 (the E2M1 max),
and the block-max value saturates -- destroying information.

| vecMax | Old: `biased_exp(vecMax/6)` | Correct: `biased_exp(vecMax)-2` | Ratio (old) | Ratio (fixed) |
|--------|-------|-------|------|------|
| 2.7 | 125 (scale=0.25) | 126 (scale=0.5) | 10.8  | 5.4 |
| 5.5 | 126 (scale=0.5) | 127 (scale=1.0) | 11.0  | 5.5 |
| 1.2 | 124 (scale=0.125) | 125 (scale=0.25) | 9.6  | 4.8  |

## Fix: Exponent-First with 0.75-Threshold Rounding

The new implementation extracts the exponent directly from `vecMax`, applies a
rounding bias, then subtracts 2:

```c++
uint32_t max_bits = __float_as_uint(vecMax);
// Round up exponent when mantissa >= 0.75
uint32_t rounded_bits = (max_bits + (1u << 21)) & 0xFF800000u;
uint32_t biased_exp = (rounded_bits >> 23) & 0xFFu;
uint32_t scale_exp = (biased_exp > 2u) ? (biased_exp - 2u) : 0u;
```

### Origin: Matching the Quantization Toolchain

This rounding scheme (`VAL_TO_ADD = 1 << (mantissa_bits - 2)`) is used by upstream quantization libraries:


- **compressed-tensors** ([`quantization/utils/mxfp_utils.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/compressed-tensors/blob/c170de622fbbed42f6792c1ca4397cc76a960225/src/compressed_tensors/quantization/utils/mxfp_utils.py#L113-L118)):
  ```python
  VAL_TO_ADD = 1 << (mantissa - FP4_E2M1_DATA.mantissa - 1)  # 1<<21 for fp32
  block_max_uint = torch.bitwise_and(x + VAL_TO_ADD, SIGN_EXPONENT_MASK)
  scale_exp = 127 + torch.floor(torch.log2(block_max)) - 2
  ```

The CUDA kernel **must** match these implementations to ensure consistency
between offline weight quantization and online activation quantization.

### Why This Helps Precision (Not Strict OCP MX)

This is **not** the strict OCP MX spec. The differences:

| Approach | Formula | Clipping zone | Behavior |
|----------|---------|---------------|----------|
| **Strict OCP MX** | `biased_exp(vecMax) - 2` | mantissa in  [0.5, 1.0) -> ratio in [6, 8) | 50% of max values clip |
| **This fix (threshold 0.75)** | `biased_exp(round_0.75(vecMax)) - 2` | mantissa in [0.5, 0.75) -> ratio in [6, 7) | 25% of max values clip |
| **Threshold 0.5 (1<<22)** | `biased_exp(round_0.5(vecMax)) - 2` | never clips | scale often too large |

The 0.75 threshold is a **precision-optimized tradeoff**:

1. **Avoids premature scale increase**: For mantissa in [0.5, 0.75), the code
   keeps the smaller scale rather than doubling it. If the scale doubles, ALL
   values in the 16-element block lose half their effective resolution.

2. **Tolerates mild clipping of block-max**: The ratio falls in [6.0, 7.0),
   so vecMax clips to 6.0 -- at most ~14% error on a single value. This is a
   better tradeoff than halving the precision of all 16 values.

3. **Prevents extreme clipping**: For mantissa >= 0.75 (ratio would be >= 7.0),
   the exponent rounds up, preventing excessive saturation.

In summary: the dynamic range is effectively extended to [0, 7*scale) with
graceful saturation at 6.0, **avoiding the scale growing too early** which
would compress the representable range for the entire block.

## Other Fixes

- **Input contiguity**: Added `.contiguous()` for FlashInfer quantization path
  to prevent incorrect results from non-contiguous tensors.

## Test Plan

- UT:
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mxfp4_moe.py -v
```

- Real model:
Verified on Kimi MXFP4 model
https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4-AutoRound


## Test Result

Command (B200): 
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 lm_eval --model vllm     --model_args pretrained=/workspace/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6,tensor_parallel_size=4,data_parallel_size=1,max_model_len=8192,trust_remote_code=True --tasks gsm8k,mmlu,piqa,hellaswag  --batch_size auto
```

lm_eval on B200 (Kimi-K2.6, TP=4):

| Config | gsm8k | mmlu | piqa | hellaswag | avg |
|--------|-------|------|------|-----------|-----|
| FP16 weights (W4A16) | 0.948 | 0.889 | 0.852 | 0.773 | 0.866 |
| MXFP4 W4A4 (old, broken) | 0.809 | 0.808 | 0.809 | 0.653 | 0.770 |
| MXFP4 W4A4 (**this fix**) | 0.921 | 0.874 | 0.842 | 0.744 | 0.845 |

Recovers ~78% of the quantization accuracy loss.

cc @dsikka @mgoin @yiliu30 @wenhuach21 @thuang6 @hshen14

`tests/models/quantization/test_gpt_oss.py` (which does
`from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx950`).

Fix: wrap the fallback in try/except, return `""` on failure.
Empty arch → all `_ON_GFX*` flags False, which is correct on non-AMD boxes.
NVIDIA already returned `""` here; ROCm path unchanged.

### Test
Before: `ERROR ... AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled`
After:  `8 skipped` (via existing skipif guards)

title: fix: prevent MM cache hang from stale LRU order keys
author: jeffye-dev
body:
FIX #43941

LRUCache.touch() inserted keys into the internal LRU order even when the key was not present in the cache data. The multimodal processor and receiver caches touch every hash in a request before updating the cache so that items used by the current request are not evicted midway through the batch. For cache misses, the old touch() behavior created order-only ghost keys.

When the cache was full, eviction selected the oldest key from the order and called pop(). If the selected key was a ghost key, pop() returned without deleting a real value, currsize did not decrease, and cachetools could keep retrying eviction without making progress. In vLLM this can leave the EngineCore input processing path spinning inside MM cache updates, so requests are accepted but never reach scheduling or model execution.

Make touch() a pure recency update by ignoring missing keys, and harden popitem() to remove stale order-only keys left by older behavior before returning a real cache item. Add regression tests for both missing-key touch behavior and stale order cleanup during popitem().

## Summary
This PR fixes a possible infinite eviction loop in `vllm.utils.cache.LRUCache`
that can be triggered by the multimodal processor cache.

The issue is caused by `LRUCache.touch()` creating an entry in the internal LRU
order for keys that are not actually present in the cache data. Such
order-only entries can later be selected by `popitem()` during eviction. Since
there is no real cache value for that key, `pop()` does not reduce `currsize`,
so cachetools can repeatedly try to evict without making progress.

In the multimodal path, this can leave the EngineCore input processing thread
spinning inside MM cache updates. The API server may accept the request, but
the request never reaches scheduling or model execution.

## Root Cause

The multimodal processor and receiver caches intentionally call `touch()` for
all multimodal hashes in a request before updating cache values:

- P0 processor cache: `_merge_mm_kwargs()` calls
  `cache.touch_sender_cache_item(item_hash)` for every item hash before
  inserting or reusing cached processor outputs.
- P1 receiver cache: `get_and_update_features()` calls
  `touch_receiver_cache_item(cache_key, feature.data)` for every feature before
  inserting or reusing cached multimodal kwargs.

That pre-touch step is meant to keep the cache eviction order stable within a
single request. If a request contains several multimodal items and inserting a
new item triggers eviction, items used later in the same request should not be
evicted halfway through the batch.

However, the old `LRUCache.touch()` implementation did this:

```python
def touch(self, key):
    try:
        self._LRUCache__order.move_to_end(key)
    except KeyError:
        self._LRUCache__order[key] = None
```

For cache misses, this added the key only to the internal LRU order, without
adding a value to the underlying cache data. This creates a "ghost key":

```text
key exists in __order
key does not exist in __data
```

When the cache is full, eviction selects the oldest key from the order and then
calls `pop()`:

```python
lru_key = next(key for key in self.order if key not in self.pinned_items)
value = self.pop(lru_key)
```

If `lru_key` is a ghost key, `pop()` sees that the key is not in the real cache
and returns without deleting any value. As a result:

- `currsize` does not decrease.
- The stale order key may remain in the order.
- cachetools eviction can keep retrying without making progress.

This is especially visible in multimodal workloads because cache misses are
normal for new images, videos, or audio inputs, and the MM cache may be close to
its configured capacity.

## User-visible Impact

When this happens, a vLLM instance can appear to accept requests but stop making
forward progress on them:

- The request is added by the API server.
- The EngineCore input processing path can spin inside MM cache update logic.
- The request does not reach scheduling or model execution.
- GPU utilization can remain at zero.
- The client or upstream proxy may eventually cancel or abort the request.

The py-spy call stack is like as below:
```plain
top -H -p 1209
PID USER PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S  %CPU  %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
5713 root 20   0  196.8g 105.3g   2.4g R  99.9   3.5     14,01 VLLM::EngineCor 

py-spy dump -p 1209 --locals 
Thread 5713 (active+gil): "Thread-1 (process_input_sockets)"
    popitem (vllm/utils/cache.py:197)
        Arguments:
            self: <cell at 0x7f802d99baf0>
            remove_pinned: False
    __setitem__ (cachetools/__init__.py:85)
        Arguments:
            self: <LRUCache at 0x7f86a46ac4a0>
            key: "79ba13f0055eab5fe445ab4047cf29e4993a4c872d4bc095e766cdffb3217fa0"
            value: <MultiModalKwargsItem at 0x7f802b85d820>
        Locals:
            maxsize: 4294967296
            size: 19418136
    __setitem__ (cachetools/__init__.py:297)
        Arguments:
            self: <LRUCache at 0x7f86a46ac4a0>
            key: "79ba13f0055eab5fe445ab4047cf29e4993a4c872d4bc095e766cdffb3217fa0"
            value: <MultiModalKwargsItem at 0x7f802b85d820>
            cache_setitem: <function at 0x7f876d276700>
    get_and_update_item (vllm/multimodal/cache.py:646)
        Arguments:
            self: <MultiModalReceiverCache at 0x7f86b82e7b00>
            mm_item: <MultiModalKwargsItem at 0x7f802b85d820>
            mm_hash: "79ba13f0055eab5fe445ab4047cf29e4993a4c872d4bc095e766cdffb3217fa0"
        Locals:
            cached_item: None
    get_and_update_features (vllm/multimodal/cache.py:591)
        Arguments:
            self: <MultiModalReceiverCache at 0x7f86b82e7b00>
            mm_features: [<MultiModalFeatureSpec at 0x7f802d1dac90>, <MultiModalFeatureSpec at 0x7f801ad2f1a0>, ...]
        Locals:
            feature: <MultiModalFeatureSpec at 0x7f801ad2f1d0>
            cache_key: "79ba13f0055eab5fe445ab4047cf29e4993a4c872d4bc095e766cdffb3217fa0"
    preprocess_add_request (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:787)
        Arguments:
            self: <EngineCoreProc at 0x7f873fc731d0>
            request: <EngineCoreRequest at 0x7f802d6b20b0>
    process_input_sockets (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1466)
        Arguments:
            self: <EngineCoreProc at 0x7f873fc731d0>
            input_addresses: ["ipc:///tmp/99992e83-a376-465d-9b75-2460c26a9fb0"]
            coord_input_address: None
            identity: <bytes at 0x7f873fc98ea0>
        Locals:
            add_request_decoder: <MsgpackDecoder at 0x7f8d1f7b33b0>
```

## Fix

This PR makes two defensive changes to `LRUCache`.

First, `touch()` is changed to be a pure recency update:

```python
def touch(self, key):
    if key in self:
        self._LRUCache__order.move_to_end(key)
```

Missing keys are ignored. This prevents new ghost keys from being created.

Second, `popitem()` is hardened to handle any stale order-only keys that may
already exist, either from older code or from an existing in-memory cache state:

```python
while True:
    ...
    if lru_key in self:
        value = self.pop(lru_key)
        return (lru_key, value)

    self._LRUCache__order.pop(lru_key, None)
```

This ensures eviction only returns a real cache item and can make progress even
if stale order entries are encountered.

## Tests

This PR adds regression coverage for both sides of the fix:

- `test_lru_cache_touch_missing_key_does_not_add_order_entry`
  verifies that touching a missing key does not add it to the cache order.
- `test_lru_cache_popitem_cleans_stale_order_key`
  manually creates a stale order-only key and verifies that `popitem()` removes
  it while still evicting a real cache entry.

Local validation:

```bash
python3 -m py_compile vllm/utils/cache.py tests/utils_/test_cache.py
```

`uv run pytest tests/utils_/test_cache.py` was attempted locally, but dependency
setup failed while fetching the `triton-cpu` git dependency due to a network/RPC
disconnect. The failure happened before the test file was executed.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE chunking
author: amitz-nv
body:
## Purpose

To mitigate crashes in TRTLLM fused MoE NVFP4 kernel that occurs with a very large number of tokens (>=305k), that can be reached with EP & high DP and/or with high `max_num_batched_tokens`. There are actually two distinct crashes:
1. TRTLLM fused MoE kernel may exceed the CUDA grid.Y 64k limit. See [getMaxNumCtasInBatchDim flashinfer function](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/719ee23fd82cb220d51ad118ca60198718f6c9d1/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fused_moe/runner.h#L97) that calculates the CUDA grid.Y dim.
2. IMA in the TRTLLM fused MoE kernel. On Nemotron 3 Super (`num_experts=512`, `top_k=22`) it occurs when `num_tokens>=305k`, while the CUDA grid.Y 64k limit should be reached at around ~370k tokens. Example use case: EP with DP=8 with `max_num_batched_tokens=50k`

So this PR adds MoE chunking only for TRTLLM fused MoE NVFP4 to tackle those issues. The chunk size is:
`min(300k, _calc_max_supported_tokens(top_k, num_experts))`

Where:
* `_calc_max_supported_tokens(top_k, num_experts)` calculates the max chunk size so the CUDA grid.Y 64k limit won't be exceeded.
* 300k limit because there's IMA crash on Nemotron 3 Super with `num_tokens = DP * max_num_batched_tokens >= 305k`.

### Notes
* This PR intends to solve the CUDA grid.Y limit issue by chunking, and sets the extra 300k limit as a workaround for the IMA issue.
* The IMA issue should be debugged further and fixed in a separate PR.
* This PR also removes the unused `supports_chunking` method from all `trtllm_<quant>_moe.py` files.

## Test Plan
Compare Nemotron 3 Super GSM8K score on:
* This PR on high number of tokens config, on 8 B200 GPUs
* Without this PR on a high number of tokens config, on 8 B200 GPUs
* This PR on a simple low number of tokens config, on 1 B200 GPU

Configs:
* High number of tokens config: EP, DP=8, `max_num_batched_tokens=50k`, which results in `num_tokens = DP * max_num_batched_tokens = 8 * 50k = 400k`, where before this PR it would crash.
* Simple low number of tokens config: No EP/DP/TP, default `--max-num-batched-tokens` (that's 8k).

## Test Result

```
  --max-num-batched-tokens 50000 --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-flashinfer-autotune --async-scheduling \

```

title: [Bugfix] Disable allreduce_rms_fusion when pipeline_parallel_size > 1
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Summary

Re-gate the FlashInfer allreduce+RMSNorm fusion to `pipeline_parallel_size == 1`. Verified hang on GB200 with `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct`, PP=2 TP=2, FlashInfer 0.6.11.post2 — disabling the fusion makes startup complete and inference correct.

## Why this isn't a duplicate

The same gate originally landed in #35424, was removed in #41458 (which claimed FlashInfer 0.6.7's [#2662](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2662) fixed PP/DP), and the auto-generated revert #41503 was closed without merging. Open PR #35960 only adds a regression test — it does not restore the gate. Empirically, PP > 1 + TP > 1 + fusion still deadlocks the FlashInfer fused-AR peer-signal kernel during cudagraph capture / kernel warmup on FlashInfer 0.6.11.post2 because divergent per-rank launch configs are still possible.

## Root cause (short)

The fused op synchronizes TP peers via a GPU-side peer-signal spin-wait (`trtllm_allreduce_fusion.cuh:902-916`) that assumes byte-identical `gridDim.x` across peers. With PP > 1, the two TP subgroups warm up concurrently (no PP send/recv in `_dummy_run`), and the resulting cross-PP contention is enough to flip near-tied per-rank launch-config decisions inside a single TP subgroup — leading to mismatched CTA counts and an infinite spin on barrier flags.

## Test commands run

- Env: GB200, FlashInfer 0.6.11.post2.
- Repro: `PP=2 TP=2 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct ...` with fusion on (current main): hangs at `Capturing CUDA graphs (decode, FULL) 0/51` with one GPU at 100% util and the rest at 0%.
- With this gate: startup completes; `curl /v1/completions` produces coherent output (`"Once upon a time" → ", in a small village nestled in the rolling hills of Tuscany,..."`).
- PP=1 TP=4 regression: still works correctly (fusion still on for the supported path).
- Verified GSM8K
```
local-completions ({'model': 'meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct', 'base_url': 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions', 'num_concurrent': 32, 'max_retries': 3, 'tokenized_requests': False}), gen_kwargs: ({}), limit: None, num_fewshot: 5, batch_size: 1
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9272|±  |0.0072|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8688|±  |0.0093|

```

## Note

AI assistance was used to investigate the spin-wait mechanism and draft this PR; the change itself is a one-line gate restoration matching the previously-merged #35424.

title: Fix Qwen3-VL and Qwen3-omni-thinker accuracy degradation from deepstack inputs under torch.compile
author: andakai
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes an accuracy regression for Qwen3-VL models when running with vLLM's default `torch.compile` / CUDA graph path.

Qwen3-VL uses `deepstack_input_embeds` to inject visual features into the decoder. Before this change, `_get_deepstack_input_embeds()` returned `None` when `deepstack_input_embeds_num_tokens == 0`. **During compile warmup / profiling, this can make the decoder graph specialize to the no-deepstack path**. Later real multimodal requests may reuse that compiled graph even though they carry real `deepstack_input_embeds`, causing the visual deepstack additions to be skipped or handled incorrectly.

This PR keeps the decoder input structure stable by **always returning `IntermediateTensors` when the deepstack buffers exist**. For no-vision/dummy paths, the tensors are zero-backed, which is semantically equivalent to no deepstack contribution but avoids changing the compiled graph structure. The resize logic is also factored into a helper to keep `_get_deepstack_input_embeds()` and `_set_deepstack_input_embeds()` consistent.

## Motivation

We observed a large Geo3K eval accuracy drop for Qwen3-VL under the default compiled serving path, while eager/no-compile execution was much closer to expected results. The issue does not reproduce on text-only Qwen3 models, which points to the multimodal deepstack path. see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43602

The root cause is the unstable decoder input contract:

```text
compile/profiling path: deepstack_input_embeds = None
real VL request path:  deepstack_input_embeds = IntermediateTensors(...)
```

After this change:

```text
compile/profiling path: deepstack_input_embeds = IntermediateTensors(zero tensors)
real VL request path:  deepstack_input_embeds = IntermediateTensors(real tensors)
```

This makes the compiled decoder graph see a consistent input structure.

## Eval Results

All runs used:

- Dataset: Geo3K full eval, 601 samples
- Sampling: `temperature=0.0`, `top_p=1.0`, `top_k=-1`, `seed=42`, `max_tokens=4096`
- GPUs: 8x H20
- vLLM base commit: `d4004455d [Kernel] Remove NormGateLinear (#43554)`

### Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct

| Config | Score | Time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| pre-patch default compile + cudagraph | 0.20465890183028287 | 116.751s |
| pre-patch no compile + no cudagraph | 0.2911813643926789 | 310.972s |
| pre-patch no compile + decode cudagraph | 0.2778702163061564 | 106.961s |
| post-patch default compile + cudagraph | 0.28286189683860236 | 102.586s |

We can clearly see that it is the `torch.compile` that causes this issue.

### Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct

| Config | Score | Time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| pre-patch default compile + cudagraph | 0.5224625623960066 | 143.152s |
| pre-patch no compile + no cudagraph | 0.5490848585690515 | 259.145s |
| post-patch default compile + cudagraph | 0.5657237936772047 | 124.998s |

For reference, SGLang on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with comparable sampling and 8 GPUs reached:

| Backend | Score | Time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| SGLang | 0.5590682196339434 | 123.258s |

## Notes

The zero-backed deepstack tensors are intended as a semantic no-op for dummy/no-vision paths while preserving the tensor-based input contract needed by compiled execution.

This change only keeps the `deepstack_input_embeds` payload shape/type stable for compiled execution. It does not change the visual encoder output, sampling configuration, chat template, or request preprocessing.

Fix two ROCm multimodal regressions seen in Buildkite build [68098](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/68098/list):

title: [Bugfix] flashinfer: fail fast when --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 used on unsupported arch
author: Kartavyasonar
body:
## Problem

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` is silently accepted on architectures without
a trtllm-gen FP4 FMHA kernel. The engine starts cleanly, captures
graphs, then dies on the first request with either:

- `AttributeError: module 'torch' has no attribute 'nvfp4'` (flashinfer
  dtype resolution), or
- `RuntimeError: Unsupported architecture` deep in trtllm-gen FMHA

The server appears healthy until the first token, making this harder to
diagnose than a startup crash.

Reported in #43562 (sm_120 / RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell).

Root cause: trtllm-gen FP4 FMHA kernels only exist for sm_100/sm_103
(GB200/GB202). vLLM forces `backend = "trtllm-gen"` when
`is_kvcache_nvfp4` is True (flashinfer.py:773) but never checks whether
the current device can actually run those kernels.

## Fix

Add a capability check immediately after `is_kvcache_nvfp4` is set to
`True`. If the detected compute capability is not sm_100 or sm_103,
raise a `ValueError` at engine init with a clear, actionable message
pointing the user to `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

`current_platform.get_device_capability()` is already imported and used
in this file.

## Before
NFO: Using max model len 8192
... engine starts, graphs captured ...
first request ->
AttributeError: module 'torch' has no attribute 'nvfp4'
or: RuntimeError: Unsupported architecture

## After
ValueError: --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 requires sm_100 or sm_103
(GB200/GB202); detected sm_120. Use --kv-cache-dtype fp8 instead.

Fixes #43562

title: Fix uniform_random routing simulation to sample without replacement
author: elvircrn
body: torch.randint can pick the same expert twice for a single token, violating DeepEP v2's dispatch kernel precondition that topk selections within a warp are deduplicated. Use torch.topk on random scores instead, which inherently produces distinct indices.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] `ApplyRotaryEmb`: fall back to native when flash_attn rotary grid would exceed the HIP per-dim limit
author: amd-fuweiy
body:
## Summary

On AMD ROCm/HIP the per-dimension launch grid is capped at **65,535**.
`vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/common.py::ApplyRotaryEmb.forward_hip`
delegates to the `flash_attn` Triton rotary kernel, whose grid is
`(cdiv(nheads, BLOCK_H), cdiv(seq_len, BLOCK_M), batch)`. With
`BLOCK_M = 8` (the default when `rotary_dim <= 128`) any `seq_len`
above `65535 * 8 = 524,280` overflows `gridY` and
`hipModuleLaunchKernel` aborts the worker:

```
RuntimeError: Triton Error [HIP]:  Code: 1, Messsage: invalid argument
  File ".../flash_attn/ops/triton/rotary.py", line 159, in apply_rotary
    torch.library.wrap_triton(rotary_kernel)[grid](
  ...
  File ".../triton/backends/amd/driver.py", line 675, in __call__
    self.launch(self.launch_cooperative_grid, gridX, gridY, gridZ, ...)
```

This is reliably hit during vLLM's `profile_run` for any Qwen2.5/Qwen3-VL-style
VL model when the engine packs `max_num_seqs` dummy images into a single
varlen sequence. For Qwen3.5-VL on MI300/MI308X (gfx942) with the default
`max_num_seqs=256` and `max_pixels=589824`, the call becomes:

```
total_tokens = 256 * 2304 = 589824
gridY        = cdiv(589824, 8) = 73,728   (> 65,535)  -> hipErrorInvalidValue
```

and the engine never reaches "Application startup complete".

## Fix

Detect the case in `forward_hip` and fall back to `forward_static`
(the existing PyTorch-native implementation) when the launch grid
would exceed the HIP limit. The flash_attn fast path is preserved for
every in-range shape — i.e. every real-inference single-image and
multi-image-per-prompt case below the limit.

```python
_HIP_MAX_GRID_DIM = 65535

def forward_hip(self, x, cos, sin):
    if self.apply_rotary_emb_flash_attn is not None:
        x, cos, sin, origin_shape, origin_dtype = self._pre_process(x, cos, sin)

        seq_len, nheads = x.shape[-3], x.shape[-2]
        rotary_dim = cos.shape[-1] * 2
        block_m = 8 if rotary_dim <= 128 else 4   # mirrors flash_attn
        block_h = 2
        grid_y = (seq_len + block_m - 1) // block_m
        grid_x = (nheads  + block_h - 1) // block_h
        if grid_y > self._HIP_MAX_GRID_DIM or grid_x > self._HIP_MAX_GRID_DIM:
            output = self.forward_static(
                x, cos, sin, self.is_neox_style, self.enable_fp32_compute
            )
            return self._post_process(output, origin_shape, origin_dtype)
        ...  # existing flash_attn path unchanged
```

The CUDA (`forward_cuda`, via `vllm_flash_attn`) path is untouched —
it has its own rotary kernel that doesn't have this AMD-specific
limit.

## Root cause analysis

flash_attn's `apply_rotary` does not split the seqlen dimension across
multiple kernel launches, so for AMD targets it implicitly relies on
the caller never producing a grid larger than the per-dim HIP limit
(an assumption that holds on NVIDIA where the limit is 2^31-1 on
`gridX/Y/Z`). On ROCm the per-dim limit is 65,535 for `gridY` and
`gridZ` (CUDA-equivalent, even though `hipDeviceProp_t::maxGridSize`
returns a much larger number for `gridX`). Verified by binary search:

```
gridY = 65,535    OK
gridY = 65,536    OK
gridY = 73,728    FAIL  (Triton Error [HIP] Code 1)
gridY = 131,070   FAIL
```

The fix is therefore correct (`>65535` is the right threshold) and
the simplest possible workaround that:

- preserves correctness (`forward_static` is the documented
  numerically-equivalent reference path),
- preserves performance (we only fall back for the pathological
  out-of-range shape; the rest of inference keeps the Triton kernel),
- doesn't require touching `flash_attn` upstream.

A more aggressive upstream fix in `flash_attn/ops/triton/rotary.py`
could split the launch into seqlen-tiled chunks and would reclaim the
~3.6× perf gap, but that is out of scope for vLLM.

## Verification

### Reproduction (before fix)

```bash
# Inside a ROCm container with rocm7.0.2, triton==3.5.1+rocm7.0.2,
# vllm @ 1ff9d3353, flash_attn (Tri Dao) installed; 8x MI308X.
export RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1
vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
  --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 163840 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-chunked-prefill \
  --mm-processor-kwargs '{"min_pixels":3136,"max_pixels":589824,"fps":2.0}' \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}'
# -> fails during profile_run with "Triton Error [HIP] Code: 1"
```

### After fix

```
init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 37.19 s
Multi-modal warmup completed in 11.201s
Application startup complete.   # HTTP 200 on /health
```

Verified with both pure-text and multimodal `/v1/chat/completions`
requests (image correctly described).

### Microbenchmark (per-call, MI308X, bf16)

| seq_len | gridY | flash_attn Triton | `forward_static` (fallback) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,304 | 288 | 0.016 ms | 0.049 ms | 3.15× |
| 23,040 | 2,880 | 0.041 ms | 0.157 ms | 3.86× |
| 524,280 | **65,535** | **0.776 ms** | **2.805 ms** | **3.61×** |
| 524,288 | 65,536 | 0.777 ms | 2.806 ms | 3.61× |
| 589,824 | 73,728 | **launch FAIL** | 3.147 ms | — |

Triton path keeps its full performance for any `gridY ≤ 65,535`; the
fallback only fires beyond it.

### End-to-end serving impact (per-request)

`Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, TP=8, 768×768 image (2,304 patches),
`max_tokens=32`, measured client-side over 5 requests:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| TTFT (prefill) | 165 ms |
| E2E total | 391 ms |
| `ApplyRotaryEmb` GPU time (TP wall-clock, max worker) | 4.85 ms |
| `ApplyRotaryEmb` GPU time (median worker) | 0.60 ms |
| Fraction of TTFT | 2.9 % |
| Fraction of E2E | 1.2 % |

For longer outputs (`max_tokens=256`) the E2E fraction drops to
**0.24 %**. So even if the fallback fires on every prefill (it does
not — only for shapes above the limit), the worst-case serving-side
slowdown is `(1.2% × 2.6×) ≈ 3%` of E2E.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Release GPU pin on failed store in MooncakeStoreConnector
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Summary

`KVCacheStoreSendingThread._handle_request` in `MooncakeStoreConnector` decremented `stored_requests[req_id]` only on the happy path. If `batch_is_exist` re-raised (it always does on a Mooncake error — see `worker.py:573`), or any other exception fired between `add_stored_request` and the trailing `dec_stored_request`, the counter stayed `> 0` forever:

- `_get_and_clear_finished_sending` would never mark the request as `done_sending` (it only fires when `stored_requests[req_id] == 0`).
- The scheduler kept `delay_free_blocks=True` for that request (`MooncakeStoreScheduler.request_finished` waits on `tracker.num_saved_tokens` / on save completion).
- The GPU blocks pinned for that save were never returned to the KV cache pool.

Under any transient Mooncake-side error this leaks GPU KV blocks until the worker exits.

## Fix

Wrap the post-`stored_requests` body of `_handle_request` in `try`/`finally` so `dec_stored_request(req_id)` and `request_queue.task_done()` always run, even on raise. Behavior on success is unchanged. The `batch_is_exist` raise still propagates up to `KVTransferThread.run()` for logging.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open PRs for: `MooncakeStoreConnector pin release`, `MooncakeStore stored_requests`, `mooncake delay_free`, `mooncake KVCacheStoreSendingThread`, `mooncake save fail`, `mooncake gpu memory pin`, `mooncake leak`, `mooncake batch_is_exist`. Closest matches:

- #36014 — HBM leak in **`MooncakeConnector`** (P2P transfer engine), not `MooncakeStoreConnector` (shared KV pool). Different connector, different code path.
- #43509 — KV leak in **NIXL** connector. Different connector.
- #42694 / #43701 — `MooncakeStoreConnector` features (`reset_cache`, `DummyClient`), unrelated to store error handling.

No existing PR covers the `KVCacheStoreSendingThread._handle_request` exception-cleanup path.

## Test Plan

New unit tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py`:

- `test_store_sending_thread_releases_pin_on_batch_is_exist_failure` — `batch_is_exist` raises (re-raise path). Asserts `stored_requests["req-a"] == 0`.
- `test_store_sending_thread_releases_pin_on_batch_put_failure` — `batch_put_from_multi_buffers` raises (caught-and-logged path). Asserts `stored_requests["req-a"] == 0`.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -v \
    -k "store_sending or releases_pin"
```

## Test Result

```
============= 10 passed, 45 deselected, 3 warnings, 10 errors in 1.10s =============
```

All 10 `store_sending` tests pass (existing + 2 new). The 10 "errors" are macOS-only teardown failures (`torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` against the MPS allocator from `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory`) unrelated to this change.

Pre-commit checks on changed files:

```
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
    vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py
```

All hooks pass: ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy-3.10, SPDX headers, root lazy imports, forbidden imports, torch.cuda call check, config-doc check, attention backend docs, boolean-ops-in-with-statements.

## AI assistance

This change was drafted with Claude (Anthropic). Every changed line was reviewed and tests were run locally before opening this PR.

## Essential Elements Checklist

- [x] The purpose of the PR
- [x] The test plan
- [x] The test results
- [ ] (Optional) Documentation update — N/A

title: [Bugfix][Reasoning] Fix thinking_token_budget not enforced on re-entry after forced end
author: ashwing
body:
## Summary

Fixes #43708

After `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` forces the complete multi-token end string (END_COMPLETE), the state machine fails to detect and enforce budget on subsequent thinking blocks. With `ignore_eos=True` and `max_completion_tokens >> thinking_token_budget`, the model re-enters `<think>` mode unchecked — the parser then returns `content=null` because it sees `<think>` without a corresponding `</think>`.

**Root cause:** After END_COMPLETE, `start_thinking`, `end_thinking`, and `continue_thinking` remain cached at their first-found values, preventing re-detection. The `_find_last_sequence_index` call re-matches the already-processed forced end sequence instead of scanning only new tokens.

**Fix (3 changes to `_update_think_state`):**
1. Add `scan_offset` field — after END_COMPLETE, set to current output length so subsequent scans only examine new tokens
2. Reset `start_thinking=-1`, `end_thinking=-1`, `think_count=0`, `continue_thinking=False` in END_COMPLETE block
3. REENTRY_KILL: when `scan_offset > 0` (post-enforcement) and a new `<think>` is detected, immediately transition to `in_end=True` with zero additional budget

## Reproduction

### Environment setup

```bash
# Serve a Qwen3 model with reasoning parser
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --reasoning-config 'ReasoningConfig(reasoning_start_str="<think>", reasoning_end_str="BUDGET_STOP</think>")' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 4096
```

> **Note on `reasoning_end_str`:** Using a custom end string that the model will never produce naturally (`BUDGET_STOP</think>`) isolates the re-entry bug — the ONLY way thinking ends is via budget enforcement forcing the end token sequence. This makes the failure deterministic rather than probabilistic.

### Minimal single-request reproduction

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -s -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}],
  "max_completion_tokens": 800,
  "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 50},
  "ignore_eos": true
}' | python3 -c "
import json, sys
r = json.load(sys.stdin)
c = r['choices'][0]
content = c['message'].get('content') or ''
reasoning = c['message'].get('reasoning') or ''
tokens = r['usage']['completion_tokens']
print(f'content length: {len(content)} chars')
print(f'reasoning length: {len(reasoning)} chars')
print(f'completion_tokens: {tokens}')
print(f'finish_reason: {c[\"finish_reason\"]}')
print(f'BUG: content is empty!' if not content.strip() else f'OK: content present')
"
```

### Multi-turn reproduction (mirrors original issue scenario)

The reporter observed 40% failure rate on turns 1 and 2 of multi-turn conversations where `max_completion_tokens` increases across turns while `thinking_token_budget` stays constant:

```bash
# Turn 0: max_completion_tokens=900, thinking_token_budget=800 → small gap (100 tokens)
# Turn 1: max_completion_tokens=1800, thinking_token_budget=800 → large gap (1000 tokens)
# Turn 2: max_completion_tokens=2800, thinking_token_budget=800 → huge gap (2000 tokens)

# The larger the gap between max_completion_tokens and thinking_token_budget,
# the more room the model has to re-enter <think> after budget enforcement forces </think>.
# With ignore_eos=true, re-entry is nearly guaranteed at large gaps.
```

```python
import requests, json

BASE = "http://localhost:8000"
MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B"

def send(messages, max_tokens, budget):
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/v1/chat/completions", json={
        "model": MODEL,
        "messages": messages,
        "max_completion_tokens": max_tokens,
        "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": budget},
        "ignore_eos": True,
    }, timeout=120)
    return r.json()

# Simulate multi-turn with increasing token budget gaps
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum entanglement briefly."}]

for turn, max_tok in enumerate([900, 1800, 2800]):
    result = send(messages, max_tok, 800)
    choice = result["choices"][0]
    content = choice["message"].get("content") or ""
    reasoning = choice["message"].get("reasoning") or ""
    tokens = result["usage"]["completion_tokens"]

    print(f"\n--- Turn {turn} (max_tokens={max_tok}, budget=800, gap={max_tok-800}) ---")
    print(f"  content: {len(content)} chars | reasoning: {len(reasoning)} chars")
    print(f"  completion_tokens: {tokens} | finish_reason: {choice['finish_reason']}")
    print(f"  {'❌ BUG: content=null' if not content.strip() else '✓ OK'}")

    # Add assistant reply for multi-turn context
    if content.strip():
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Can you elaborate further?"})
```

### Docker validation results — WITHOUT fix (vllm/vllm-openai:latest baseline)

```
============================================================
Reproducing issue #43708: thinking_token_budget re-entry
============================================================
Model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B
Budget: 50 tokens, ignore_eos: true

------------------------------------------------------------
TEST 1: budget=50, max_completion_tokens=120 (small gap=70)
------------------------------------------------------------
  Budget violations: 0/10
    reasoning=198 chars, content=45 chars, tokens=120, finish=length

------------------------------------------------------------
TEST 2: budget=50, max_completion_tokens=800 (large gap=750)
------------------------------------------------------------
  Budget violations: 7/10
  Null content: 7/10
    reasoning=3847 chars, content=0 chars, tokens=800, violated=True, finish=length
    reasoning=3612 chars, content=0 chars, tokens=800, violated=True, finish=length
    reasoning=3491 chars, content=0 chars, tokens=800, violated=True, finish=length

------------------------------------------------------------
TEST 3: budget=50, max_completion_tokens=1500 (gap=1450)
------------------------------------------------------------
  Budget violations: 9/10
  Null content: 9/10
    reasoning=7234 chars, content=0 chars, tokens=1500, violated=True, finish=length
    reasoning=6891 chars, content=0 chars, tokens=1500, violated=True, finish=length

============================================================
SUMMARY: 16/30 requests had budget violations
  Small gap (70):  0/10 violated  ← budget works when headroom is small
  Large gap (750): 7/10 violated  ← model re-enters thinking, budget not re-enforced
  Huge gap (1450): 9/10 violated  ← nearly always fails with large headroom
============================================================
```

### Docker validation results — WITH fix applied

```
============================================================
Reproducing issue #43708: thinking_token_budget re-entry
============================================================
Model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B
Budget: 50 tokens, ignore_eos: true

------------------------------------------------------------
TEST 1: budget=50, max_completion_tokens=120 (small gap=70)
------------------------------------------------------------
  Budget violations: 0/10
    reasoning=198 chars, content=45 chars, tokens=120, finish=length

------------------------------------------------------------
TEST 2: budget=50, max_completion_tokens=800 (large gap=750)
------------------------------------------------------------
  Budget violations: 0/10
  Null content: 0/10
    reasoning=201 chars, content=2814 chars, tokens=800, violated=False, finish=length
    reasoning=187 chars, content=2943 chars, tokens=800, violated=False, finish=length

------------------------------------------------------------
TEST 3: budget=50, max_completion_tokens=1500 (gap=1450)
------------------------------------------------------------
  Budget violations: 0/10
  Null content: 0/10
    reasoning=195 chars, content=6012 chars, tokens=1500, violated=False, finish=length
    reasoning=203 chars, content=5891 chars, tokens=1500, violated=False, finish=length

============================================================
SUMMARY: 0/30 budget violations
  Small gap (70):  0/10 ✓
  Large gap (750): 0/10 ✓  ← re-entry detected and killed immediately
  Huge gap (1450): 0/10 ✓  ← all tokens now go to content after budget enforcement
============================================================
```

### What changed in behavior

| Scenario | Without fix | With fix |
|----------|------------|----------|
| Budget=50, max_tokens=120 (gap=70) | ✓ Works (model hits max before re-entry) | ✓ Works |
| Budget=50, max_tokens=800 (gap=750) | ❌ 70% fail: content=null, all tokens as reasoning | ✓ 0% fail: re-entry killed |
| Budget=50, max_tokens=1500 (gap=1450) | ❌ 90% fail: content=null | ✓ 0% fail |
| Normal case (no ignore_eos) | ✓ Works | ✓ No regression (0/20 failures) |

**Key insight:** The bug only manifests when `max_completion_tokens - thinking_token_budget` gives the model enough headroom to re-enter `<think>`. With a small gap (turn 0 in the original issue), the model hits `max_completion_tokens` before it can produce a full `<think>` re-entry. With a large gap (turns 1-2), re-entry is nearly guaranteed with `ignore_eos=True`.

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests added (`tests/v1/sample/test_thinking_budget_reentry.py`):
  - Single-token end re-entry detection
  - Multi-token end re-entry detection
  - Single-block regression (common case still works)
  - Logits forcing verification on second block
- [x] Docker validation on 8xA100 with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`:
  - 0/60 failures WITH fix across all gap sizes
  - 16/30 failures WITHOUT fix (increasing with gap size)
  - 0/20 regressions for normal case (no `ignore_eos`)
- [x] Concurrent load testing: 10 simultaneous requests per test
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass
- [x] No existing PRs address this specific re-entry bug (checked #43210, #43692 — orthogonal)

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) was used in developing and testing this fix. All changes were reviewed and validated by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Pass `routed_scaling_factor` to FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Purpose

`routed_scaling_factor` was not passed to FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE, leading to serious correctness issues. This affects all BF16 MoE models with `routed_scaling_factor` and `apply_routed_scale_to_output=False` on Blackwell.

(looks like no one runs BF16 MoE Blackwell so far 🙃)

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix Accuracy Drop in Sparse Indexer on gfx950
author: kliuae
body:
## Purpose
ROCm's sparse indexer path now supports DeepSeek-V4. However, currently its configuration degrades the accuracy for older models like DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 on the gfx950 path.

This PR fixes the accuracy drop. Specifically two issues are addressed.
- The indexer cache layout is hard-coded to `SHUFFLE` and can cause erroneous cache reads when indexer cache `block_size=1`. This PR dispatches the shuffle layout based on the block_size setting.
- On ROCm, the sparse indexer has a fast path for rotary embedding that omits tensor split/cat/copy, and that relies on the RoPE implementation mutating the input arguments in-place. However, that is not the case for the pytorch-native rotary embedding which is the default when TorchInductor is on. This PR limits the fast path to the inplace-mutating implementations, i.e. those invoked when `rotary_embedding`'s custom_ops implementations are used.

title: [BugFix] Fix blocked reasoning parsing with MRV2
author: njhill
body:
Model Runner V2 does not yet support the thinking_token_budget request parameter and so fails at startup if it's enabled.

However, since #38214, the `reasoning_config` which enables/controls thinking token budget functionality, is auto-created when a reasoning parser is specified, meaning MRV2 fails to start in this case.

This PR changes to validate at request time, since we no longer have an explicit "enable thinking budget" signal at startup time.

This change however means that there will be breakage for folks using thinking_token_budget budgets when upgrading to the next version of vLLM (at least until we support this feature in V2), since we will be enabling it by default for more models and this won't be covered by the auto-fallback-to-V1 on startup.

I think this is OK since the feature and change to have it be auto-enabled itself is very new. We will want to mention it in the release notes however so affected users can set `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` manually.

title: [Bugfix][MiniCPM-o] Fix cuda/cpu device mismatch in Resampler2_5 pos_embed
author: parthash0804
body:
## Summary

Resampler2_5.forward adds the cached positional embedding to the input without moving it to the input's device:
```
pos_embed = self.pos_embed[:tgt_h, :tgt_w, :].reshape((tgt_h * tgt_w, -1)).to(dtype)
...
x + pos_embed   # <-- x is on cuda, pos_embed is on cpu
```
When self.pos_embed (a non-persistent buffer) stays on CPU while the hidden states x are on the GPU, this raises:
```
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but found at least two devices, cuda:0 and cpu!
```

## Root cause
pos_embed is registered as a non-persistent buffer, so it is not moved by the normal weight-loading device placement and stays on CPU unless something explicitly relocates it. Factors that decide whether the bug actually surfaces:

**Patch grid size vs. the cached pos_embed size (max_size, default 70×70).**
`_adjust_pos_cache` only rebuilds pos_embed (on the input device) when the target grid exceeds the cached size. For images whose grid stays within 70×70, the original CPU buffer is used as-is — exposing the mismatch. Very large images can incidentally rebuild the buffer on the GPU and hide the bug.


## Fix
One line: pass device=device so pos_embed matches x.

## Steps to Reproduce
Use vLLM's built-in synthetic multimodal benchmark. The random-mm bucket key is (height, width, num_frames); (800, 1024, 1) produces a single 800×1024 image per request, keeping the resampler grid under 70×70 so the buggy CPU pos_embed is used directly.

```
vllm bench throughput \
  --model openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6 --trust-remote-code --dtype float16 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 1 --enforce-eager \
  --num-prompts 1 --input-len 512 --output-len 32 \
  --dataset-name random-mm \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config '{(800, 1024, 1): 1.0}' \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0
```

## Test Result
Before the fix — crash during engine init (exit code 1)
```
File "/.../vllm/model_executor/models/minicpmv.py", line 1586, in get_vision_hidden_states
    return self.resampler(vision_embedding, tgt_sizes)
File "/.../vllm/model_executor/models/minicpmv.py", line 233, in forward
    x + pos_embed,  # L * B * D +  L * B * D
    ~~^~~~~~~~~~~
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device,
but found at least two devices, cuda:0 and cpu!
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

After the fix — benchmark completes (exit code 0)
```
Processed prompts: 100%|██████████| 1/1 [00:09<00:00,  9.12s/it,
    est. speed input: 112.30 toks/s, output: 14.04 toks/s]
Throughput: 0.11 requests/s, 122.49 total tokens/s, 13.61 output tokens/s
```

## Scope
1. Single-line change in Resampler2_5.forward; mirrors the already-correct
Resampler4_5.forward.
2. No API or behavior change

title: [Bugfix] Exclude Ray DP from #42585's deferred port allocation
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Summary

PR #42585 introduced kernel-assigned-at-bind ports for the API-server input/output sockets (`tcp://host:0` placeholders + `gather_actual_addresses` report-back). The new mechanism was never intended to cover the Ray DP backend — Ray pickles `addresses` into each engine actor at `.remote()` time and `EngineCoreActorMixin._perform_handshakes` is a no-op, so the driver's post-bind rebind cannot reach the actors. The implementation, however, didn't gate on the backend, so Ray DP got silently routed through the new path and now hangs deterministically (multi-node, `num_api_servers > 1`): each actor keeps the `tcp://host:0` snapshot and DEALER-connects to port 0 forever (ZMQ connect is async and does not raise).

## Fix

In `run_multi_api_server`, gate the deferred path on `data_parallel_backend != "ray"` and skip `gather_actual_addresses` for Ray. Ray DP falls back to driver-side `get_open_port()` — the pre-#42585 behavior. This re-introduces the original TOCTOU race only on the Ray DP path; mp DP keeps the full bind-time fix.

## Test

Adds `tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py::test_ray_dp_addresses_resolved_before_actor_creation`. It exercises the orchestration end-to-end with Ray `local_mode` and CPU-only placement groups (no GPUs needed), snapshots `self.addresses` from each Ray engine actor, and asserts every URI is a real bound port. Fails on current main, passes with this fix.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py -v
# => 2 passed 
```

title: Correct model layer aliasing for Bert style models
author: ap9272
body:
Correct model layer aliasing for Bert and ModernBert style models.

## Purpose

When loading Hugging Face checkpoints for BERT-style models (specifically `ModernBertModel` and `BertModel`), weight loading failed due to mismatched parameter names (aliasing) or unexpected task-specific weights in the checkpoint (e.g., Masked Language Modeling heads) that are not defined in the vLLM backbone model.

This PR resolves these issues:
1. **ModernBertModel (`vllm/model_executor/models/modernbert.py`)**:
   - Updated `hf_to_vllm_mapper` to properly map `model.layers.` and `layers.` to `encoder_layer.layers.`, and strip `model.` prefix.
   - Added a safeguard in `load_weights` to skip any weights not found in `params_dict` (e.g., extra MLM heads like `cls.predictions.*` or sequence classification heads in checkpoint files). This prevents a `KeyError` crash during model initialization.
3. **Warmup issues (`vllm/model_executor/warmup/deep_gemm_warmup.py`)**:

title: fix: keep DeepSeek V4 RoPE cache on inv_freq device
author: galletas1712
body:
#### Summary

`DeepseekV4ScalingRotaryEmbedding._compute_cos_sin_cache()` currently creates
`inv_freq` on the active/default torch device, but creates the position arange
with `device=current_platform.device_type`.

That can mix meta tensors with CPU/CUDA tensors during meta-device model
construction:

- `inv_freq`: follows `torch.device("meta")`
- `t`: forced to `current_platform.device_type`

The constructor then fails in `torch.einsum` before loaders that materialize
meta models can replace buffers with real tensors.

This PR creates `t` on `inv_freq.device` so the cache construction stays
device-consistent.

#### Error fixed

Reproduced with the installed vLLM runtime in a throwaway container using
`/tmp/.venv/bin/python`.

Minimal repro. The throwaway container was CPU-only, so the script patched the
RoPE module's `current_platform` to `CpuPlatform()` to mirror a concrete vLLM
platform and reach the DeepSeek V4 cache construction path:

```python
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
from vllm.config import DeviceConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.rotary_embedding import (
    DeepseekV4ScalingRotaryEmbedding,
)
from vllm.platforms.cpu import CpuPlatform

vllm_config = VllmConfig(device_config=DeviceConfig(device="cpu"))
with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
    with patch(
        "vllm.model_executor.layers.rotary_embedding."
        "deepseek_scaling_rope.current_platform",
        CpuPlatform(),
    ):
        with torch.device("meta"):
            DeepseekV4ScalingRotaryEmbedding(
                head_size=128,
                rotary_dim=64,
                max_position_embeddings=128,
                base=10000,
                is_neox_style=False,
                scaling_factor=16,
                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
            )
```

Logged failure before this change:

```text
python_executable=/tmp/.venv/bin/python
torch_version=2.11.0a0+git70d99e9
vllm_version=0.20.1
BEGIN_REPRO
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 29, in <module>
  File "/tmp/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/deepseek_scaling_rope.py", line 224, in __init__
    cache_fp32 = self._compute_cos_sin_cache()
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/tmp/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/deepseek_scaling_rope.py", line 234, in _compute_cos_sin_cache
    freqs = torch.einsum("i,j -> ij", t, inv_freq)
            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  ...
  File "/tmp/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/_prims_common/__init__.py", line 917, in check_same_device
    raise RuntimeError(msg)
RuntimeError: Tensor on device meta is not on the expected device cpu!
```

After applying the one-line change inside the same throwaway repro container,
the same constructor succeeds and preserves the intended cache properties:

```text
VERIFY_SUCCESS
cos_sin_cache_device=meta
cos_sin_cache_is_meta=True
cos_sin_cache_shape=(2048, 64)
cos_sin_cache_dtype=torch.float32
```

#### Why

This matches the existing generic DeepSeek RoPE implementation, which leaves
both tensors on the active/default device, while preserving the DeepSeek V4
fp32 cache dtype.

#### Duplicate-work check

Checked open PRs with:

```bash
gh issue view 43926 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "43926 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "DeepSeek V4 RoPE meta device"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "deepseek rope inv_freq device"
```

No existing open PR appears to address this fix. The exact-area search only
returned this PR; the broad keyword search also returned unrelated draft PR
#38354.

#### Tests / validation

- Repro before fix: reproduced the `torch.einsum` device mismatch traceback
  above.
- Verification after applying this one-line change inside a throwaway repro
  container: constructor succeeded and produced a meta fp32 `cos_sin_cache`
  with shape `(2048, 64)`.

#### AI assistance

AI assistance was used to help prepare this PR description and validation notes.

author: V-3604
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #43894.

`InputBatch.condense()` copies `allowed_token_ids_mask_cpu_tensor` from a moved request's row into the freed index but never clears the source row. `add_request` only writes that row when the new request sets `allowed_token_ids`, so unrestricted request that later reuses the index keeps the previous request's whitelist and is sampled against a stale mask. title: [ROCm][CI] Fix AITER unified attention for encoder-decoder cross-attention
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
Fixes ROCm AITER unified attention for encoder-decoder cross-attention when it shares KV cache storage with ROCM_ATTN decoder self-attention. It addresses the regression was introduced by [vllm-project/vllm#43660](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43660). That PR changed `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend.get_kv_cache_shape` from K/V-first:

```python
(2, num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)
```

to blocks-first:

```python
(num_blocks, 2, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)
```

That is correct for the standalone AITER unified layout, but Nemotron Parse on ROCm selects a mixed backend setup:
- decoder self-attention: `ROCM_ATTN`
- encoder-decoder cross-attention: `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`

`ROCM_ATTN` still uses K/V-first KV cache storage. For encoder-decoder models, those attention groups can share the same raw KV allocation, so viewing the same storage with different physical block dimensions makes identical block IDs address different byte ranges.

Auto git bisect:
- Known good commit tested: `e1814f822d51225e0c6240386d65b2182758c2a4`
- Parent tested good: `53a20886752bdf8f26c4c5121458c514096da107`
- Culprit commit: `5b115bb8a33d72820075450ecefcd292607bfe57`
- Culprit PR: [vllm-project/vllm#43660](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43660)

title: [Bugfix] Corrupted MLA + linear attention
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Problem

I noticed that for Kimi Linear, once the KV cache is filled up, the model starts outputting garbage. After a lot of debugging with Codex, we found out that it's related to #35219, which fixed the problem for Qwen. Kimi Linear uses MLA, which is somehow not covered by that PR. I'm not too familiar with KV cache management code, but the fix in this PR (done by Codex) seems to fix the issue.

This problem was not surfaced before probably because Kimi Linear is the only MLA + Linear attention model.

Note: this problem only affects FlashMLA and FlashInfer MLA backends, which does not mask out tail KV cache page (relies on `* 0` to get zeros, which is only true for non-nan and non-inf inputs). Triton MLA masks the inputs, hence it's not affected.

cc @ZJY0516 

## Validation

The easiest way to observe the original problem is to run gsm8k for multiple epochs to fill up the KV cache. Once the KV cache is full, the model starts outputting garbage, and the eval scores dropped.

Epoch | Main | This PR
---|---|---
Epoch 0 | 0.9075 | 0.8946
Epoch 1 | 0.7096 | 0.8931

title: [BugFix] [GDN] Read linear_key_head_dim from hf_text_config for multimodal models
author: IdoAtadTD
body:
## Summary

For multimodal Qwen3.5 models (e.g. [Qwen3.5-397B-A17B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B/blob/main/config.json)), `linear_key_head_dim` (128) lives on `hf_text_config`, not `hf_config`. GDN prefill backend selection only read `hf_config`, so `head_k_dim` was `None` and CuteDSL/FlashInfer on Blackwell (SM100) was never enabled:

`INFO 05-29 16:47:49 [qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:228] Using Triton/FLA GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, head_k_dim=None).`

This mirrors the pattern used elsewhere in vLLM for multimodal configs (e.g. MLA backends reading from `hf_text_config`).

Related: #43273 — CuteDSL GDN prefill on SM100 gates on `head_k_dim == 128`; without this fix, multimodal Qwen3.5 models never satisfy that check.

## Changes

- Fall back to `vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config` when resolving `linear_key_head_dim` in `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend` and `_log_gdn_backend_decision`.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix GPT-OSS Quark MXFP4 MoE loading - emulation buffer not block-aligned
author: xuebwang
body:
### Purpose

Quark-quantized MXFP4/FP8 GPT-OSS loading was first introduced in #29008, and has since been
refactored and extended by several follow-ups. Those changes correctly added OCP-block-aligned
TP slicing in `gpt_oss.py`, but the **emulation** path in `quark_moe.py` was left out of the
size-rounding logic, so today the emulation backend is broken under TP (traceback below).

### Environment

- ROCm, MI300/325
- Model: `amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8`, `amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8`, etc
- MXFP4 **emulation** MoE backend `--moe-backend emulation`

### Traceback

One example:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 283, in init_device
    self.model_runner.load_model()
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 421, in load_model
    self.model.load_weights(self.model_config.model, ...)
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py", line 1154, in load_weights
    return self._load_weights_quark(...)
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py", line 774, in _load_weights_quark
    expert_data.data[:dim1, :dim2].copy_(sliced_weight)
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1440) must match the size of tensor b (1472) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

Note: Native MXFP4 backends are unaffected: they already round the per-partition sizes. Only the emulation path skipped this rounding.

## Fix

Round the per-partition `hidden_size` / `intermediate_size_per_partition` up to `OCP_MX_BLOCK_SIZE` for the emulation backend too.

## Test Plan

**Integration smoke test** — on ROCm with the affected model and the emulation backend:

```bash

    --model amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --quantization quark \
    --moe-backend emulation \
    --trust-remote-code
```

## Test Result

No `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (X) must match the size of tensor b (Y)` during
weight loading; server reaches `Application startup complete`.


Root cause: #41892 registered a `packed_modules_mapping = {qkv_proj: [q_proj,k_proj,v_proj], gate_up_proj: [gate_proj,up_proj]}` on `Step3p5ForCausalLM` so that Quark INT8 exports (whose `modules_to_not_convert` lists unfused per-shard names) are handled correctly，https://huggingface.co/nameistoken/Step-3.5-Flash-Quark-W8A8-INT8/blob/main/config.json.
 However, the block-FP8 Step-3.5-Flash-FP8 checkpoint lists **fused** names directly in `modules_to_not_convert` (e.g. `model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj`, `model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj`). With the new mapping in place, `is_layer_skipped` unconditionally expands `qkv_proj` to its unfused shards and looks those up in `ignored_layers`. The unfused names are not present, so attention/MLP layers that should stay in BF16 are routed through `Fp8LinearMethod` and produce corrupted logits.
https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash-FP8/blob/main/config.json

Fix: in `is_layer_skipped`, when the projection name is in `fused_mapping` AND the fused prefix itself already matches an entry in `ignored_layers`, return skipped directly. Only fall back to the per-shard expansion when the fused name does not match. This keeps the Quark INT8 behavior from #41892 intact while restoring correct behavior for FP8/other exports that list fused names. One file changed, +9/-1.

## Test Plan

Verification on ROCm MI308X (TP=4) with Step-3.5-Flash-FP8:
  * Without this commit: `test_raw_completion.py` produces wrong output -- every prompt degenerates to repeated `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` tokens.
  * With this commit: `test_raw_completion.py` output is normal (coherent completions on 4/4 sanity prompts), and gsm8k eval also runs normally.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma4 MTP block_table batch_size mismatch under concurrent load
author: Dymasik
body:
## Purpose

Fix `RuntimeError: batch_size must be equal to batch_size_k` that occurs with **Gemma4 + MTP + FlashAttention** under concurrent load when the batch is partially occupied.

`Gemma4Proposer.set_per_group_block_table()` captures block tables with shape `(num_reqs_padded, max_blocks)` during `_prepare_inputs`. Later, `spec_decode_common_attn_metadata` is unpadded to `num_reqs` via `.unpadded()`, but the per-group block tables stored on the proposer instance are never sliced. When `build_per_group_and_layer_attn_metadata` swaps in the stored block table for secondary KV cache groups, FlashAttention sees `page_table.size(0) == num_reqs_padded` while `cu_seqlens_q` implies `batch_size == num_reqs`, triggering the assertion.

Fix: slice `_per_group_block_tables[gid]` to `[:batch_size]` in `build_per_group_and_layer_attn_metadata`.

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mtp.py", line 550, in forward
```
