title: [Bugfix] compressed-tensors: allow int8 grouped WNA16 MoE on Marlin
author: joerowell
body:
The num_bits==8 branch of CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod asserted group_size == -1, rejecting int8 experts quantized with a group size (e.g. group_size=128) even though Marlin supports them: uint8b128 is a supported quant type and MARLIN_SUPPORTED_GROUP_SIZES includes 128, and check_moe_marlin_supports_layer already admits group_size in {-1,32,64,128} (so the method is selected and then asserts against itself).

The assert isn't needed, and crucially, it unblocks mixed-precision INT models (such as `poolside/Laguna-XS.2-INT4`, which has INT4 & INT8 layers).

title: [Bugfix] Return HTTP 422 for unprocessable image URLs instead of 500
author: akinsella
body:
## Associated issue

FIX #47163

## Description

This PR fixes the issue where vLLM returns HTTP 500 (Internal Server Error) when image URLs in requests point to non-existent or inaccessible resources. The fix ensures these client-side errors properly return HTTP 422 (Unprocessable Entity), making it clear that the issue is with the request content, not the server.

Applies to: Both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses APIs`

## Motivation

When users submit requests with invalid image URLs (404, 403, DNS failures, connection errors), vLLM currently returns HTTP 500, which:

- Misleads users into thinking there's a server-side problem
- Makes debugging harder (client vs server error distinction)
- Doesn't follow HTTP semantics for error classification

Example issue:

```shell
curl http://<GPU_INSTANCE_IP>:8000/v1/responses \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://invalid-url.com/image.jpg"}}
  ]}]}'
```

Before: HTTP 500 - `{"error": {"type": "InternalServerError", "code": 500}}`

After: HTTP 422 - `{"error": {"type": "UnprocessableEntityError", "code": 422, "param": "image_url"}}`

## Changes

### Core Implementation

1. **vllm/exceptions.py** - Added `VLLMUnprocessableEntityError` exception class
2. **vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py** - Added `_wrap_media_fetch_error()` helper that:
- Converts client errors (4xx, DNS, connection) to `VLLMUnprocessableEntityError`
- Preserves server errors (5xx) as-is
3. **vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/error_response.py** - Handle new exception with HTTP 422
4. **vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py** - Register exception handler

### Test Coverage

5. tests/multimodal/media/test_unprocessable_entity_error.py - 30+ test cases covering:
- Exception creation and properties
- Error wrapping for various client errors (404, 403, DNS, connection)
- Preservation of server errors (5xx)
- MediaConnector error handling (sync/async)
- Error response creation
- Full integration flow

## Testing

### Unit Tests

```shell
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_unprocessable_entity_error.py -v
```

Test coverage includes:
- ✅ **TestVLLMUnprocessableEntityError** - Exception creation
- ✅ **TestWrapMediaFetchError** - Error classification (12 test cases)
- ✅ **TestMediaConnectorErrorHandling** - Sync/async error handling (5 test cases)
- ✅ **TestErrorResponse** - HTTP response creation (2 test cases)
- ✅ **TestIntegration** - Full error flow (3 test cases)

### Manual Testing

Tested with various error scenarios:
- DNS resolution failure → HTTP 422 ✓
- 429 Too Many Requests -> HTTP 422 ✓

### Existing Tests
Verified no regressions:
- test_fetch_image_error_conversion() - Unaffected (uses data URLs)
- All other connector tests pass

## Breaking Changes
None - This is a bug fix that corrects error classification:
- Client errors now correctly return 422 instead of 500
- Server errors continue to return 500 (unchanged)
- No API contract changes
- Backward compatible

## Related Issues
Fixes issue where unprocessable image URLs return misleading HTTP 500 errors.

title: [AMD][Bugfix][EPLB] Fix elastic EP scaling accuracy on ROCm
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Purpose Two fixes for distributed/test_elastic_ep.py, which collapsed GSM8K accuracy at the initial and scaled checkpoints on ROCm: Bug 1 Scale-up produces garbage output on ROCm (accuracy=0) Root cause. New elastic-EP ranks are created with load_dummy_weights=True. On ROCm, initialize_single_dummy_weight() .zero_()s every non-floating-point tensor in model.state_dict(). The FusedMoE expert-topology buffers _expert_map, expert_mask, and expert_{global_to_physical,physical_to_global,local_to_global} were registered as persistent integer buffers, so they were zeroed right after being built correctly for the new EP topology. That corrupted all2all dispatch garbage output. CUDA never zeroes integer tensors, so the bug was ROCm-only. This corrects an earlier hypothesis: the map is not built unsharded at ep_size==1; it is built correctly at the target ep_size and then corrupted. (Thanks @itayalroy for identifying the dummy-init zeroing path.) Fix. Register those five buffers with persistent=False. They are per-rank, deterministically-derived EP topology metadata not checkpoint state so they should never be in state_dict() (matches moondream3.py's _expert_map registration). This keeps them out of state_dict(), so: - ROCm dummy-weight init can no longer zero them, and - batch_transfer_weights() (which iterates state_dict()) can no longer clobber them from a sender rank. As a result, no post-reshuffle metadata rebuild is needed and no name-based transfer filter for these tensors is needed. Bug 2 Sync-EPLB accuracy loss from redundant rearranges rearrange_expert_weights_inplace() was firing every step_interval even when the proposed map barely improved balance (imbalance 1.0), causing ~16s lateral all-to-all churn that starved the engine and dropped accuracy. We now compute per-rank load imbalance for the current vs proposed map and skip the rearrange when improvement is <5%, decided collectively via all-reduce and guarded to non-scale-up rearranges. ## Test Plan run failed CI tests ## Test Result ``` distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling[sync_eplb] PASSED distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling[async_eplb] PASSED distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling_uneven[sync_eplb] PASSED distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling_uneven[async_eplb] PASSED ================= 4 passed, 18 warnings in 1194.63s (0:19:54) ================== ``` Per-checkpoint accuracies (all >= 0.58 threshold; previously 0.19 / 0.016): ---

title: [CI][Bugfix] Rerun test_engine_log_metrics_ray on Ray GCS startup timeout
author: peizhang56
body:
## Purpose

`tests/v1/metrics/test_ray_metrics.py::test_engine_log_metrics_ray` intermittently fails on ROCm CI (e.g. buildkite build 75329, the "AMD: V1 Core + KV + Metrics" step) with:

```
RuntimeError: Timed out waiting for file .../gcs_server_port_...
```

The test starts a Ray cluster implicitly: the first `EngineTestActor.remote()` call triggers Ray's `auto_init_ray()` ~F~R bare `ray.init()`. On a contended CI host, Ray's GCS server subprocess occasionally fails to write its port file within Ray's fixed 30s bootstrap ww
indow, so `ray.init()` raises before the test body runs. This is a Ray cluster-bootstrap flake, not a defect in vLLM. Ray's 30s timeout is compiled into the binary and is not configurable (no env var or `ray.init()` kwarg reaches it), so the only resilient option is to retry the bootstrap ~@~T a fresh `ray.init()` gets a fresh GCS subprocess and a fresh 30s window.

This marks the test flaky with reruns scoped to that specific error via `only_rerun`, matching the existing `@pytest.mark.flaky` convention already used across the suite (`pytest-rerunfailures` is pinned in `requirements/test/{rocm,cuda,xpu}.txt`). Scoping to the message ensures only the GCS bootstrap timeout is retried; any genuine failure in the metrics-logging code fails immediately and is not masked.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to diagnose the failure and prepare this change. Not a duplicate: no open PR references `test_ray_metrics`, `test_engine_log_metrics_ray`, or the GCS-port flake.

## Test Plan

ROCm (gfx942), the CI command from `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`:

```
pytest -v -s -m 'not cpu_test' v1/metrics
```

Plus targeted validation of the rerun behavior by injecting a real GCS-startup failure (redirecting Ray's `gcs_server` binary to a wrapper that hangs past the 30s timeout) and a non-matching failure, to confirm the `only_rerun` scoping.

## Test Result

- Transient GCS timeout (first attempt fails, then recovers): `RERUN` ~F~R `PASSED` (`1 passed, 1 rerun`), confirming the scoped marker retries the bootstrap and the rerun's fresh `ray.init()` succeeds.
- Persistent GCS timeout (every attempt fails): `RERUN` ~W 3 ~F~R `FAILED` (`1 failed, 3 rerun`) with the genuine `RuntimeError: Timed out waiting for file .../gcs_server_port_...` ~@~T a sustained problem is still surfaced, not hidden.
- Non-matching failure (unrelated `AssertionError`): `FAILED` immediately with no rerun (`1 failed`, no rerun delay), confirming `only_rerun` does not mask real regressions.
- Baseline with no fault: `PASSED` with no spurious reruns.

title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Keep image bidirectional attention within the sliding window
author: lucianommartins
body:
## Purpose

Gemma4 vision models that use blockwise bidirectional image attention
(`use_bidirectional_attention="vision"` → 12B, 26B-A4B, 31B) silently fell back
to **causal-only** attention over image tokens whenever a single image's
soft-token span exceeded the text sliding window (e.g. ~1100 soft tokens at
`max_soft_tokens=1120` vs `sliding_window=1024`). This degraded vision/OCR
quality — catastrophic on the encoder-free **12B** (no vision tower to
compensate, output collapsed into fragmented `...` text) and latent on the
tower-based 26B/31B.

The defect is backend-agnostic (the runner builds the ranges), so it affected
both TRITON_ATTN (A100/SM80) and FA4 (SM90/Hopper); the fix touches both kernels.

- **Root cause:** `GPUModelRunner` dropped the *entire* bidirectional
  `mm_prefix` range for an image when `(range_len > sliding_window)`, leaving
  those image tokens fully causal in the LM.
- **Intended behavior** (HF reference, https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46850): on local/sliding
  layers the bidirectional block is **clamped to** the sliding window —
  `(causal OR blockwise) AND sliding_window` — not dropped. Global/full-attention
  layers are causal-only (already handled in vLLM via
  `_clear_mm_prefix_for_full_attn_layers`).

### Fix (three parts, gated to Gemma4)

- **Runner:** gate the oversized-range skip on a new model capability flag
  `mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window`. Models that bound `mm_prefix` in-kernel keep
  the full range; all other models keep the existing drop (default-unset).
- **Triton kernel (A100/SM80):** add an `MM_PREFIX_CLAMP_SW` `constexpr` to
  `compute_kv_seq_mask`; when set, AND each `mm_prefix` range with the
  sliding-window past-bound `(q - kv) < SLIDING_WINDOW` (equivalent to HF's
  `sliding_window_overlay`; future `kv` passes trivially). Plumbed
  `Attention → TritonAttentionImpl → unified_attention → kernel`. Default
  `False` is dead-code-eliminated, so other models/backends are byte-identical.
- **FA4 / FlashAttention kernel (SM90/Hopper):** Gemma4 is forced onto the
  FLASH_ATTN backend whenever FA4 is available and `max_head_dim ≤ 512`
  (`Gemma4Config.verify_and_update_config`), so the Triton clamp does not run
  there. FA4 builds its mask via a CuTe-DSL `mask_mod` that is the *sole*
  element mask (causal/window masking is off when a `mask_mod` is present), so
  the bidirectional block was not window-bounded. `_make_mm_prefix_mask_mod`
  now takes an optional `sliding_window`; when set it ANDs each range with
  `(q_idx - kv_idx) < sliding_window` — the exact analogue of the Triton clamp.
  `FlashAttentionImpl` passes it only for the same per-layer flag; window =
  `sliding_window_size[0] + 1`.

### Scope / safety

- Gemma4-only, defense-in-depth: the model flag is set only on
  `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` (+ its `Gemma4Unified...` subclass); the
  per-layer kernel flag is set only by `Gemma4Attention` on sliding layers
  (`self.is_sliding`).
- The FA4 path is gated by the same per-layer flag: `_make_mm_prefix_mask_mod`
  defaults `sliding_window=0` (clamp dead-code-eliminated at jit-trace time), and
  only Gemma4 sliding layers pass a positive window. Other FA4 mm-prefix models
  (gemma3, etc.) are unchanged.
- **Unaffected:** E2B/E4B (`is_mm_prefix_lm=False`), gemma3 (separate class),
  all non-Gemma models, and any Gemma4 case where the image fits within the
  window or the request is text-only (bit-identical).
- Not a duplicate: no existing open PR addresses the vLLM-side oversized-range
  drop; transformers#46850 is the HF-side counterpart and the reference spec.

## Test Plan

Reference parity against HuggingFace `transformers` (which implements [#46850](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46850)),
using a dense OCR image at `max_soft_tokens=1120` (1100 soft tokens > 1024
window), greedy decoding:

- E2E: `gemma-4-12B-it`, `--max-soft-tokens 1120`, temperature 0, original chat
  template; compare generated transcription against the HF reference output.
- Numerical localization (custom harness): dump and diff, at identical inputs,
  (a) vision embeddings, (b) post-merge `inputs_embeds`, (c) first-step logits,
  HF vs vLLM. Ablation: re-run HF with `use_bidirectional_attention` disabled to
  confirm the broken vLLM state == HF-causal.
- SM90/FA4: same E2E + parity check on an H100 box (the harness hooks the model
  forward, not the kernel, so it is backend-agnostic). Verify the log reports the
  FLASH_ATTN/FA4 backend (not FA3/Triton) so the clamped path is exercised.

## Test Result

### A100 / TRITON_ATTN

8×A100-80GB, `TRITON_ATTN` backend (FA4 unavailable on SM80; forced for Gemma4
due to heterogeneous head dims 256/512), CUDA graphs enabled.

- **First-step logits (12B @ 1120), vLLM vs HF reference:**
  - Before: argmax **818**, `MATCH=False` (HF argmax 236825) — i.e. vLLM ==
    HF-with-bidirectional-disabled (confirmed by ablation).
  - After: argmax **236825**, **identical top-5**
    `[236825, 2717, 818, 1018, 236777]`, cosine **0.998**.
- **Vision embeddings** and **post-merge `inputs_embeds`** were already
  bit-identical to HF (`max_abs_diff = 0.0`), isolating the defect to the LM
  attention mask.
- **E2E OCR (12B @ 1120):** before → fragmented `...`-delimited output; after →
  fluent transcription matching the HF reference.
- **Regressions:** 12B @ 280 and text-only are bit-identical before/after.

### H100 / FA4

H100, FlashAttention v4 — log confirms the path is exercised:
`Using FA4 for all layers`, `Using FLASH_ATTN attention backend`,
`Using FlashAttention version 4`.

- **E2E OCR (12B @ 1120), temperature 0:** before → fragmented `...` output;
  after → fluent transcription verbatim-matching the HF reference (same text as
  the A100/Triton run). Confirms the gated CuTe `mm_prefix` sliding-window clamp
  on the FA4 path.

title: [Bugifx][INC] Fix INC quantization method selection for non-quantized layers
author: lvliang-intel
body:
## Purpose

Fix NotImplementedError: The class UnquantizedLinearMethod must implement the 'embedding' method when running AutoRound int4 DiffusionGemma model ([Intel/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-int4-AutoRound](https://huggingface.co/Intel/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-int4-AutoRound)).

```
(Worker_PP1 pid=58) ERROR 06-30 07:29:23 [multiproc_executor.py:898] File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py", line 973, in init

(Worker_PP1 pid=58) ERROR 06-30 07:29:23 [multiproc_executor.py:898] self.embed_tokens = VocabParallelEmbedding(

(Worker_PP1 pid=58) ERROR 06-30 07:29:23 [multiproc_executor.py:898] ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

(Worker_PP1 pid=58) ERROR 06-30 07:29:23 [multiproc_executor.py:898] File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/vocab_parallel_embedding.py", line 290, in init

(Worker_PP1 pid=58) ERROR 06-30 07:29:23 [multiproc_executor.py:898] raise NotImplementedError(

(Worker_PP1 pid=58) ERROR 06-30 07:29:23 [multiproc_executor.py:898] NotImplementedError: The class UnquantizedLinearMethod must implement the 'embedding' method, see UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod.

(Worker_PP0 pid=57) ERROR 06-30 07:29:23 [multiproc_executor.py:898] WorkerProc failed to start.
```

**Root cause:**
INCConfig.get_quant_method unconditionally returned UnquantizedLinearMethod() for all unquantized layers (bits >= 16), including non-linear layers like VocabParallelEmbedding which expect an UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod. The fix ensures only LinearBase/ParallelLMHead layers get UnquantizedLinearMethod(), while other layer types (e.g., embedding layers) return None so they fall back to default handling.

## Test Plan

Run the DiffusionGemma model that previously failed.

## Test Result

The model loads successfully without the NotImplementedError after the fix.

title: [BugFix][Spec Decode] Compact shared topk indices buffer after first MTP draft step
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# Context
Deepseek-style topk index selection for MTP has a bug during proposal stage when the topk indices are shared among all MTP draft step forward passes. After the first draft step, `set_skip_topk` is called on the MTP model to force the remaining draft steps to reuse the same topk indices values (held within `topk_indices_buffer` of the attention module). The issue is that the first draft forward pass will fill the `topk_indices_buffer` tensor with the per-request, multi-token, bonus + accepted tokens. So they are laid out like:
```
a0, a1, a2, a3, b0, b1, b2, b3, c0, c1, c2, c3, ...
```
with a total of `num_tokens = num_reqs * (1 + num_spec_tokens))` rows.

But the remaining `num_spec_tokens - 1` draft steps are expecting a layout of:
```
a3, b3, c3, ...
``` 
with a total of `num_tokens = num_reqs`. Consequently, they use the wrong topk indices, potentially from other requests. The draft tokens becomes lower quality, and acceptance rates drop.

# This PR
Fixes the above issue by compacting the topk indices for the last query token of each request, so that they are contiguous at the front of the buffer.

# Validation
**Server**
```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4 \
  -tp 4 \
  -O3 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=False \
  --speculative_config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "full_decode_only", "mode": 0}'
```

**Bench**
```
vllm-bench \
    --model $MODEL \
    --backend openai-chat \
    --dataset-name speed-bench \
    --speed-bench-config throughput_16k \
    --speed-bench-max-input-len 10240 \
    --speed-bench-category low_entropy \
    --request-rate inf \
    --max-concurrency 32 \
    --num-prompts 256 \
    --output-len 2048 \
    --ignore-eos \
    --temperature 1.0 \
    --percentile-metrics "ttft,tpot,itl,e2el" \
    --result-dir ~/dev \
    --save-result
```

**Results**
Metric | index sharing = True, main | index sharing = True, #47238
-- | -- | --
Request throughput (req/s) | 0.74 | 0.79
Output token throughput (tok/s) | 1517.50 | 1625.59
Total token throughput (tok/s) | 9105.00 | 9753.52
Median TTFT (ms) | 676.75 | 605.60
P90 TTFT (ms) | 4772.12 | 4512.80
Median TPOT (ms) | 19.61 | 18.46
P90 TPOT (ms) | 22.95 | 21.72
Acceptance rate (%) | 57.73 | 61.48
Acceptance length | 2.73 | 2.84
Drafts | 191,923 | 184,332
Draft tokens | 575,769 | 552,996
Accepted tokens | 332,388 | 339,992
Pos 0 (%) | 88.18 | 87.27
Pos 1 (%) | 56.03 | 60.86
Pos 2 (%) | 28.97 | 36.31

The position > 0 acceptance rates are fixed.

title: fix(security): add resource bounds validation to derender endpoints
author: jperezdealgaba
body:
The /v1/completions/derender and /v1/chat/completions/derender endpoints accepted caller-supplied GenerateResponse objects with unbounded token_ids, choices, generate_responses, and logprob structures, processing them via tokenizer.decode() without enforcing the resource limits that the normal generation path applies (CWE-400 / CWE-770). Add _validate_derender_bounds() to ServingDerender that rejects oversized payloads before any detokenization or parser invocation:
- choices count capped at VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES
- token_ids length capped at max_model_len
- generate_responses batch count capped at VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES
- logprobs.content and prompt_logprobs capped at max_model_len
- top_logprobs per entry capped at 20 (OpenAI spec)
- negative token_ids rejected via Pydantic field_validator

title: Fixes non-coalesced HBM access in marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_kernel_awq
author: flutist
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes non-coalesced HBM access in `marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_kernel_awq` (AWQ int4-fp8 weight preprocessing kernel, model-load cold path).

### Problem
Original thread mapping used `threadIdx.x` for the row dimension:
```cpp
qweight[(blockIdx.x * 32 + threadIdx.x) * size_n / 8 + blockIdx.y]
```
Adjacent threads (tidx 0..31) read elements strided by `size_n/8` int32 words — non-coalesced, ~12.5% sector utilization on large matrices.

### Fix
Remap `threadIdx.x` to the column dimension (stride 1, fully coalesced):
```cpp
int col = blockIdx.y * 32 + threadIdx.x;
if (col >= size_n / 8) return;
int32_t val = qweight[blockIdx.x * (size_n / 8) + col];
```
- Grid: `dim3 blocks(size_k, (size_n / 8 + 31) / 32)`, `blockIdx.x` indexes rows directly
- Alignment relaxed from implicit `size_n % 256` to explicit `size_n % 8` + tail boundary check

### Coverage equivalence
Old: `(row=bx*32+tidx, col=by)`; New: `(row=bx, col=by*32+tidx)` — same `[0,size_k) × [0,size_n/8)` element space, each processed exactly once, logically equivalent.

## Why is this not duplicating an existing PR?
Searched open PRs/issues for "marlin preprocess" and coalesced-access fixes on this kernel; found only general marlin performance discussions, no PR addressing the non-coalesced thread mapping in `marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_kernel_awq`.

## Test commands and results

### Correctness
```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py::test_marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_awq \
       tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py::test_marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess_without_zp -v
```
Both pass.

### Performance
```bash
python -c "
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
k,n,g = 16384,16384,128
qw = torch.randint(0,2**31,(k,n//8),dtype=torch.int32,device='cuda')
qz = torch.randint(0,16,(k//g,n//8),dtype=torch.int32,device='cuda')
for _ in range(5): ops.marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess(qw,qz)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
s,e = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
s.record()
for _ in range(50): ops.marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess(qw,qz)
e.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f'{s.elapsed_time(e)/50*1e3:.1f} us/iter')
"
```
- Before: 1291.1 us/iter
- After: 581.9 us/iter
- Speedup: **2.22x**

Control: the unchanged `without_zp` kernel path shows no regression (557.7 → 557.4 us/iter, within noise), confirming measurement stability.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Reserve the KV null block when validating max_model_len
author: 92hyungjun
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #35541 (still not fully resolved).

That issue was previously addressed by #41069, which made the startup capacity check account for `num_gpu_blocks_override`. However, #41069 validates against the **total** block count, so the exact-boundary case — where the KV cache holds exactly as many blocks as a `max_model_len` request needs — still passes at startup and then hangs at runtime. It also only covers the override path, not `kv_cache_memory_bytes` or profiled memory. This PR completes the fix.

`BlockPool` permanently reserves one block as the null block, so only `num_gpu_blocks - 1` blocks are usable for requests (`BlockPool.get_usage()` already subtracts it). But the startup check (`_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` in `get_kv_cache_configs`) compares `max_model_len` against the **total** block count. A config with exactly `ceil(max_model_len / block_size)` blocks passes the check (it logs `Maximum concurrency for <max_model_len> tokens per request: 1.00x`) but is one usable block short at runtime, so a request can never be scheduled and the engine hangs (0 tok/s).

### When it happens

All sources of the block count flow into the same check, so any can hit the boundary:

- `num_gpu_blocks_override = N` with `max_model_len == N * block_size`
- `kv_cache_memory_bytes` sized to exactly `N` blocks
- `gpu_memory_utilization` (including the default) when the profiled block count equals `ceil(max_model_len / block_size)` — uncommon (auto-profiling usually leaves head-room), but the same bug.

### Why it hangs

With `block_size=16`, 50 total blocks -> 49 usable (784 tokens), and `max_model_len=800` (needs 50 blocks):

1. Startup: needed = 50, total = 50 -> the check passes.
2. A prompt fits in the 49 usable blocks and starts decoding.
3. When the length crosses 784 tokens it needs a 50th block; only 49 are usable, so `allocate_slots()` returns `None`.
4. The request is preempted, `num_computed_tokens` reset to 0, and requeued.
5. It is re-admitted, needs the same 50 blocks, and fails again. Nothing is running to preempt and there is no infeasibility guard, so it retries identically every step.
6. `running == 0`, `waiting >= 1`, `scheduled_tokens == 0` every step -> 0 tok/s.

### Reproduction (current `main`)

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

# 50 total KV blocks -> BlockPool reserves 1 null block -> 49 usable = 784 tokens.
# max_model_len=800 needs ceil(800/16)=50 blocks: the check counts the 50 total
# blocks and passes, but only 49 are usable.
llm = LLM(
    model="facebook/opt-125m",
    load_format="dummy",
    block_size=16,
    num_gpu_blocks_override=50,
    max_model_len=800,
)
sp = SamplingParams(max_tokens=40, ignore_eos=True)
llm.generate({"prompt_token_ids": list(range(1, 771))}, sp)
# current main: hangs forever. With this PR: raises ValueError at startup.
```

## The fix

In `get_kv_cache_configs`, reserve one block (the null block) in the capacity used by the admission check and auto-fit, while allocation keeps using the full memory. Since all sources of the block count funnel into `available_memory`, this covers `num_gpu_blocks_override`, `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, and profiled memory with one change, and keeps auto-fit consistent with the check.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k reserves_null_block
```

Plus the reproduction above.

## Test Result

- Reproduction — before: hangs at 0 tok/s; after: raises at startup with `ValueError: ... max seq len (800) ... estimated maximum model length is 784` (= 49 usable blocks × 16).
- New unit tests cover the boundary for both the override and the memory-derived paths; related `test_kv_cache_utils.py` tests pass with no regressions.

## Not a duplicate

#41069 (merged) is override-only and validates against the total block count, leaving the null-block boundary unfixed. #35542 (an earlier, unmerged attempt) added a separate override-only check. This PR fixes the shared capacity accounting for all sources of the block count.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and draft this change; all changed lines were reviewed and the tests were run locally as described above.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix memory access fault in AITER MLA backend for DPA+FP8 KV
author: simondanielsson
body:
## Purpose

Fix memory access fault in DSv3 when running DPA with FP8 KV. Fix is to cast Q to FP8 whenever KV is FP8 as Q is already quantized to FP8 in this case and the MLA decode kernel expects Q to be FP8 as well.

**The issue is only observed with DP, not with TP**. This is because MLA metadata tiles are sized based on dtypes OR when there are TP8 head shapes. The following snippet from [AITER](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/90ee2737d56da01ab51a1755552cfd3332c3a79c/aiter/ops/attention.py#L1174) summarizes why sizing is correct on TP8 independent of dtypes, but fail on DPA if Q dtype is not correctly FP8:
```python
# get_mla_metadata_info_v1
    if (
        num_head_qo == 16 # always hits on TP8
        or ( ... )
        or (
            get_gfx() == "gfx942"
            and num_head_qo == 128 # hits on DPA
            and kv_dtype == dtypes.fp8 
            and q_dtype == dtypes.fp8 # needs to hit!
        ) 
        or (
            get_gfx() == "gfx950"
            and kv_dtype == dtypes.fp8
            and q_dtype == dtypes.fp8  # this needs to hit!
            and (
                (num_head_qo == 32 and effective_seqlen_qo == 4)
                or (num_head_qo == 64)
                or (num_head_qo == 128) # hits on DPA
            )
        )
    ):
        max_qo_tiles_per_batch = int(math.ceil(packed_qo_len / 128))
```

Co-authored with @nikonyrh-siloai.

### Technical details

- The Q is actually FP8 whenever KV is FP8:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f5a8d73377d0f0a4e00cba172f9fbd0d50471b07/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L794-L799
with `fp8_attention = is_quantized_kv_cache(self.kv_cache_dtype)`

- AITER's `get_mla_metadata_info_v1` explicitly checks Q/KV dtypes to determine tile sizes (e.g. by checking if both Q/KV is FP8 or both are BF16): https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/90ee2737d56da01ab51a1755552cfd3332c3a79c/aiter/ops/attention.py#L1189-L1211
- When Q is not cast to FP8, it selects the "wrong" tile size for the kernels inside `get_mla_metadata_info_v1` as none of the conditions are hit.
- The issue is _not_ observed with TP8 due to the explicit branching on `num_head_qo == 16` (true for DSv3 with TP8) here: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/90ee2737d56da01ab51a1755552cfd3332c3a79c/aiter/ops/attention.py#L1174. When using DP this branch is not hit, so the issue is exposed

title: [XPU][Bugfix] Fix GroupCoordinator device_index
author: mganczarenko
body:
## Purpose

  Fix regression introduced in #45026 (`ebfbcfe46`) where `GroupCoordinator.__init__` makes all subgroups inherit `device_index` from `_WORLD`.

  For CUDA this is safe — `device_index` passes through `logical_device_id_to_visible_device_id()` before reaching `torch.device()`. For XPU and out-of-tree platforms, `self.device` is set directly as
  `torch.device(f"{platform}:{self.device_index}")` with no further remapping.

  The `EngineCore` process is not a TP worker — its `_WORLD.device_index` is always 0. When it creates a broadcaster `GroupCoordinator`, the ZMQ shm_broadcast sockets bind to paths keyed to device 0. TP
  workers bind to their own correct device paths. The mismatch means the broadcaster never collects all reader acks, causing an infinite hang at `"Waiting for core engine proc(s) to start"`.

  Fix: always use `local_rank` as `device_index`, restoring pre-`ebfbcfe46` behavior. The `assigned_physical_gpu_ids` mapping introduced by #45026 is applied via `logical_device_id_to_visible_device_id()`
  for CUDA and is unaffected by this change.

  ## Test Plan

  Intel XPU (B60 TP=8, B70 TP=4) with a 48B MoE model:

  python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server
    --model moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dtype bfloat16
    --max-model-len 8192 --trust-remote-code

  ## Test Result

  | | Without fix | With fix |
  |---|---|---|
  | Past `init_process_group` | ✓ | ✓ |
  | Distributed init completes | ✗ infinite hang | ✓ |
  | `Application startup complete` | ✗ | ✓ |
  
  Logs:

[kimi-fixed.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29551243/kimi-fixed.log)

title: [Bugfix] Guard CUDA-only rms_norm_per_block_quant in FUSED_OPS for non-CUDA builds
author: tsvikas
body:
## Purpose

`FUSED_OPS` in `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rms_quant_fusion.py` dereferences `torch.ops._C.rms_norm_per_block_quant.default` at **import time**, but that is a CUDA-only custom op. On builds where it is not registered (e.g. `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=tpu`), merely importing this module raises `AttributeError`. Because the module is imported by `pass_manager` and several sibling fusion passes, this breaks importing models that pull this path (surfaced building MiniMax-M3 on TPU).

## Fix

Guard the four `rms_norm_per_block_quant` entries behind `hasattr(torch.ops._C, "rms_norm_per_block_quant")`, mirroring the existing `per_token_group_fp8_quant` / `scaled_fp4_quant` guards a few lines above for `QUANT_OPS`. On CUDA the op is present, so all four entries are populated exactly as before — no behavior change.

## Test Plan / Result

On a `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=tpu` build, `import vllm.compilation.passes.fusion.rms_quant_fusion` (and importing a model that pulls it) no longer raises `AttributeError`. On CUDA, `FUSED_OPS` is unchanged.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and validated the behavior end-to-end; the change is a minimal import guard mirroring the existing `per_token_group_fp8_quant` pattern in the same file. Attribution is included as a `Co-authored-by:` commit trailer.

title: [Bugfix] Don't read KV cache past `seq_len` in triton paged attn kernels
author: njhill
body:
The Triton unified_attention and ROCm paged-decode kernels load KV cache slots beyond seq_len (the unwritten tail of the last partial block) and rely on the score mask to drop them. That is unsafe when the tail is non-finite: masked positions get softmax weight 0, but 0 * NaN = NaN still poisons the output. In `compute_tile_loop_bounds` the causal-derived `max_seq_prefix_len` can additionally overshoot seq_len for non-causal (cross-)attention, widening the over-read.

- `triton_attention_helpers.compute_tile_loop_bounds`: clamp the non-causal / mixed / prefix branch to exactly `seq_len`.
- `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.kernel_paged_attention_2d`: bound the K/V loads to `seq_len` (other=0.0), matching the score mask.

Surfaced as Whisper cross-attention emitting garbage on ROCm once MRV2 made it the default model runner. The over-read only affects output when the unwritten tail is non-finite (NaN under MRV2 on ROCm; harmless zero under MRV1 and on CUDA via 0 * 0). Freed KV blocks are never re-zeroed, so correctness relies on never reading past seq_len. MRV2 (unlike MRV1) runs a dummy warmup forward; for encoder-decoder it has no encoder input, so cross-attn attends to zero keys - an empty softmax that yields NaN on the ROCm kernel - and that NaN lands in the block tails the first real request reuses. The fix is correct regardless, since reading beyond seq_len is never valid.

I will open a separate PR to improve the MRV2 warmup in encoder-decoder case.

Claude was used to help find this!

title: [BugFix][MLA] Support kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers for MLA attention
author: ruikangliu
body:
## Purpose

Fix two gaps in `MLAAttention` that prevent `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` from
working with MLA models (DeepSeek-V2/V3/V4, GLM and others).

### Problem 1: `MLAAttention.__init__` ignores `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers`

The `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` flag (introduced in #33695) allows skipping
FP8 KV cache quantization for specified layers. However, it was only wired up in
`Attention.__init__` — `MLAAttention.__init__` **never checked it**. MLA layers
listed in the skip set were still quantized to FP8, defeating the purpose of the
flag.

**Fix**: Added the `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` check in `MLAAttention.__init__`,
mirroring the same logic from `Attention.__init__`. When a layer index is in the
skip set, `kv_cache_dtype` is reset to `"auto"` before backend selection and
quantization initialization.

### Problem 2: `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` passes wrong `cache_dtype_str`

`get_kv_cache_spec` used the **global** `cache_config.cache_dtype` instead of
the per-layer `self.kv_cache_dtype` when constructing `MLAAttentionSpec`.
`MLAAttentionSpec.real_page_size_bytes` uses `cache_dtype_str` to decide between
the custom FP8 layout (656 bytes/token for `"fp8_ds_mla"`) and standard
dtype-based sizing. Even when a layer is correctly skipped (after Problem 1
fix), the spec would still get the global FP8 string, causing **incorrect KV
cache page size calculation**.

**Fix**: Changed `cache_dtype_str=vllm_config.cache_config.cache_dtype` →
`cache_dtype_str=self.kv_cache_dtype`, consistent with how
`Attention.get_kv_cache_spec` uses `self.kv_cache_dtype` to determine
quantization mode.

### Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate-work check)

- **#33695** ("enable skipping of SW attention layers") — introduced the feature
  but only wired `Attention.__init__`; this PR completes coverage for MLA.
- **#27185** (closed) — touched `cache_dtype_str` in `get_kv_cache_spec` but
  was abandoned.
- **#47043** (open) — fixes `real_page_size_bytes` for plain FP8 formats on the
  spec side; complementary to Problem 2.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py` | Added `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` check in `MLAAttention.__init__`; fixed `get_kv_cache_spec` to use per-layer `self.kv_cache_dtype` |

## Test Result

Verified on GLM-5.2-FP8 (an MLA model) with FP8 KV cache and skip layers:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 70 75 77
```

The server starts and serves requests successfully. Before the fix, skipped MLA
layers were still quantized to FP8; after the fix, the specified layers (70, 75,
77) correctly use the native dtype in their KV cache.

---

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Anthropic Claude, Opus 4.8) under
human direction; the submitting human has reviewed every changed line and run
the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] poolside_v1: accept tool calls without newline after function name
author: joerowell
body:
### Problem
`poolside_v1`'s non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` uses a `func_detail_regex` that **requires a literal newline** between the function name and the `<arg_key>` block:

```python
r"<tool_call>([^\n]*)\n(.*)</tool_call>"
```

That matches GLM-4's format, but some models emit the tool call with **no newline** after the name — e.g. `<tool_call>get_weather<arg_key>city</arg_key><arg_value>Paris</arg_value></tool_call>`. For that output `func_detail_regex.search()` returns `None`, the call is silently dropped (`tools_called=False`), and the raw `<tool_call>` markup leaks into `content`.

### Fix
Relax the regex so the name→args separator is optional, parsing **both** the GLM-4 newline form and the newline-less form; name/arg extraction is otherwise unchanged:

```python
r"<tool_call>\s*([^\n<]+?)\s*\n?\s*(<arg_key>.*?)?</tool_call>"
```

The **streaming** path already tolerated the missing newline (its cut logic falls back to `<arg_key>`), so it is unchanged.

### Tests
Adds regression tests: no-newline and newline forms on the non-streaming path, and the no-newline form on the streaming path. Full `tests/tool_parsers/test_poolside_v1_tool_parser.py` passes (10 existing + 3 new).

In the next week, we'll replace this with the template.

title: [Bugfix] handle grammar compilation failures to avoid engine crash
author: izhuhaoran
body:
This PR resolves the long-standing `TODO` in `StructuredOutputManager._create_grammar`:

> `# TODO: we still need to handle xgrammar compilation failures, though it should be unlikely as we test that up front as well.`

A structured-output request whose grammar fails to **compile** currently crashes the whole `EngineCore` instead of failing just that request. `_create_grammar` re-raises, and because it runs in a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, the exception is stored in the grammar `Future` and re-raised later when the scheduler reads `StructuredOutputRequest.grammar` inside `schedule()` — which has no per-request guard — so it escapes the busy loop and takes down every in-flight request.

The `TODO`'s assumption that up-front validation already covers this is wrong, because the two calls do different work:

- **Admission** (`validate_xgrammar_grammar`) runs `xgr.Grammar.from_json_schema(schema)` — only the **schema → grammar (BNF)** conversion.
- **Engine** (`compile_grammar` → `GrammarCompiler.compile_json_schema(...)`) does that conversion **and** compiles the grammar into the token-level FSM + adaptive token-mask cache.

`from_json_schema` is a strict subset of `compile_json_schema`, so passing admission does **not** guarantee the engine-side compile succeeds: a schema can convert cleanly yet still fail at the FSM/token-mask stage (which specific schemas fail is xgrammar-version dependent). The up-front check structurally cannot catch compile-stage failures, so the compile step needs its own per-request guard.

This PR makes `_create_grammar` catch compilation failures and finish only the offending request with a per-request error, leaving `EngineCore` and all other in-flight requests running.

title: [BugFix] Fix ModelOpt mixed-precision quantization for sparse `quantized_layers` configs.
author: danielafrimi
body:
Fix ModelOpt mixed-precision dispatch so missing sibling layers do not inherit
quantization from unrelated siblings.

The previous fallback could see one quantized layer under a parent, e.g. `o_proj`,
and incorrectly apply the same quantization to a missing sibling like `qkv_proj`.
This is unsafe for sparse mixed FP8/NVFP4 configs.

Now we only infer quantization for known packed projections:
`qkv_proj <- q_proj/k_proj/v_proj` and `gate_up_proj <- gate_proj/up_proj`.


For Nemotron Super NVFP4, the config is sparse and mixed precision.

title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Fix FA4 mm_prefix mask: add sliding window and absolute q_idx
author: lucianommartins
body:
### Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47300

Gemma4 vision models emit total gibberish on the FlashAttention-4 (CuTeDSL, SM90) backend when the context is long (>=~1k tokens past the sliding window) and contains at least one image. The Triton backend produces correct output on the same input.

Root cause — two bugs in `_make_mm_prefix_mask_mod` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`):

- Missing sliding window constraint. The mask implemented `causal OR mm_prefix` instead of `(causal AND sliding_window) OR mm_prefix`. When `mask_mod` is present, `_resolve_causal_local_window` sets `causal=False, local=False`, which disables the kernel's built-in window enforcement — the `mask_mod` becomes the sole element-level mask. Since it lacked the sliding window term, non-image tokens attended to the full causal context instead of the configured window (1024 tokens for Gemma4), destroying attention distributions on any sequence longer than the window.
- Local `q_idx` instead of absolute position. The FA4 kernel passes `q_idx` as 0-based within the current prefill chunk, while `kv_idx` is absolute (0-based over the full KV cache). The causal term `kv_idx <= q_idx` and the mm_prefix range comparisons used raw `q_idx`, producing wrong masks whenever `seqlen_q != seqlen_k` (chunked prefill with prior context, multi-turn conversations).

#### Changes

- `_make_mm_prefix_mask_mod` now accepts `sliding_window_left: int | None` and enforces `(q_abs - kv_idx) < sw` on the causal term when non-None. Two separate `@cute.jit` branches (with/without window) avoid runtime branching in the CuTe DSL.
- Both branches compute `q_abs = q_idx + (seqlen_k - seqlen_q)` via `seqlen_info` and use it for all position comparisons (causal, window, mm_prefix ranges), matching the Triton reference path (`compute_kv_seq_mask`).
- Call site passes `1 + window_size[0]` (Triton convention) with a `>= 0` guard so global-attention layers (`-1, -1`) correctly get `sw_left=None` (causal-only, no window).

#### Scope

- Only affects models with `is_mm_prefix_lm=True` running on FA4 (SM90+).
- Global-attention layers (no sliding window) take the `else` branch — causal-only mask, no window. Behaviour matches the pre-fix code for these layers (plus the `q_abs` correction).
- Models without sliding window (bagel, molmo2, paligemma) get `sw_left=None` — causal-only branch. No change in behaviour beyond the `q_abs` fix.
- Text-only, decode, non-FA4, and non-mm_prefix paths are completely untouched.

### Test Plan

Manual end-to-end NIAH (needle-in-a-haystack) reproduction on H100 (SM90), `google/gemma-4-31B-it`, TP=2, prefix caching off, `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`:

Server:

```bash
MODEL=google/gemma-4-31B-it TP=2 PC=off VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 \
  bash /tmp/issue-38257-serve.sh
```

Client — 32k tokens, 1 image, single-chunk prefill (MNBT=45000):

```bash
python3 /tmp/issue-38257.py --model google/gemma-4-31B-it \
  --num-images 1 --target-tokens 32000
```

Client — 144k tokens, 3 images, chunked prefill (MNBT=16384):

```bash
python3 /tmp/issue-38257.py --model google/gemma-4-31B-it \
  --num-images 3 --target-tokens 147000
```

### Test Result

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 32k tokens, 1 image, single-chunk (MNBT=45000) | GIBBERISH (`764368764368...`) | Correct NIAH UUID |
| 144k tokens, 3 images, chunked (MNBT=16384) | GIBBERISH (`la la la de de...`) | Correct NIAH UUID |
| Image-only turns (3 turns) | Coherent (unchanged) | Coherent (unchanged) |

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` all pass.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Allow Run:ai memory_limit sentinel values
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #45291. @svasilinets pointed out that Run:ai documents `RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT=-1` as the unlimited/default CPU memory mode, and the same section documents `0` as the minimal CPU buffer. The validation added in #45291 currently rejects both values because it requires `memory_limit > 0`.

This PR keeps `concurrency` as a positive integer, but lets `memory_limit` follow Run:ai's range semantics: `-1`, `0`, or any positive integer. Values below `-1`, bools, and non-integers still raise before any `os.environ` mutation.

Run:ai docs: https://github.com/run-ai/runai-model-streamer/blob/master/docs/src/usage.md#cpu-memory-capping

## Test Plan

Run a loader-construction before/after check over `memory_limit=-1`, `0`, `1024`, `-2`, and `concurrency=-1`. Then run the focused `extra_config` tests and ruff on the changed files.

## Test Result

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Loader constructor before/after | Before rejects `memory_limit=-1` and `0`; after accepts both and still rejects `memory_limit=-2` and `concurrency=-1` |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader/test_runai_model_streamer_loader.py -k extra_config -q` | `7 passed, 6 deselected in 1.92s` |
| `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on changed files | Passed |

<details><summary>loader constructor before/after</summary>

```python
import os

from vllm.config.load import LoadConfig
from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.runai_streamer_loader import RunaiModelStreamerLoader


def try_loader(extra):
    os.environ.pop("RUNAI_STREAMER_CONCURRENCY", None)
    os.environ.pop("RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT", None)
    try:
        RunaiModelStreamerLoader(
            LoadConfig(load_format="runai_streamer", model_loader_extra_config=extra)
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"{extra}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
    else:
        print(
            f"{extra}: accepted; "
            f"memory_limit={os.environ.get('RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT')!r}; "
            f"concurrency={os.environ.get('RUNAI_STREAMER_CONCURRENCY')!r}"
        )


for extra_config in (
    {"memory_limit": -1},
    {"memory_limit": 0},
    {"memory_limit": 1024},
    {"memory_limit": -2},
    {"concurrency": -1},
):
    try_loader(extra_config)
```

Before:

```text
{'memory_limit': -1}: ValueError: memory_limit must be a positive integer, got -1
{'memory_limit': 0}: ValueError: memory_limit must be a positive integer, got 0
{'memory_limit': 1024}: accepted; memory_limit='1024'; concurrency=None
{'memory_limit': -2}: ValueError: memory_limit must be a positive integer, got -2
{'concurrency': -1}: ValueError: concurrency must be a positive integer, got -1
```

After:

```text
{'memory_limit': -1}: accepted; memory_limit='-1'; concurrency=None
{'memory_limit': 0}: accepted; memory_limit='0'; concurrency=None
{'memory_limit': 1024}: accepted; memory_limit='1024'; concurrency=None
{'memory_limit': -2}: ValueError: memory_limit must be an integer >= -1, got -2
{'concurrency': -1}: ValueError: concurrency must be a positive integer, got -1
```

</details>

title: [Bugfix] Exclude kv_cache_memory_bytes from CacheConfig.compute_hash
author: matteso1
body:
## Purpose

Setting `kv_cache_memory_bytes` — the documented alternative to `gpu_memory_utilization` for sizing the KV cache, and the way to skip the memory-profiling measurement on boot — changes `CacheConfig.compute_hash` and therefore the torch.compile cache key. The result: using the fast-boot knob silently invalidates the compile cache and forces a full recompile.

The field only sizes the KV-cache allocation; it does not affect the compiled computation graph. `gpu_memory_utilization`, which controls the same allocation in different units, is already in the ignored set — this adds `kv_cache_memory_bytes` next to it.

Measured on H100 PCIe (vLLM 0.24.0, torch 2.11, warm caches):

| model | warm boot | warm boot + `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 43.8 s (compile-artifact load 5.2 s) | 64.5 s (full recompile 27.5 s) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | 69.8 s (10.3 s) | 96.6 s (39.2 s) |

i.e. the knob saves ~2 s of profiling and costs +21–27 s of recompile. Confirmed via distinct `torch_compile_cache/<hash>` directories per run.

## Test Plan

New regression test `tests/config/test_cache_config.py`: hash equality when only `kv_cache_memory_bytes` (and, for the existing precedent, `gpu_memory_utilization`) differs, plus a sanity check that graph-affecting fields (`block_size`) still change the hash.

## Test Result

`2 passed`. Also re-verified end-to-end boot behavior on the H100 measurements above.

title: [CI/Build][AMD] Fix ROCm OOM in eagle_correctness_heavy by reserving CUDA graph memory
author: peizhang56
body:
## Purpose

test_eagle_correctness_heavy builds a reference engine and a speculative engine back to back in one process, and its parametrized cases run sequentially. On the AMD "V1 e2e (4 GPUs)" step the TRITON_ATTN Llama-4-Scout cases (llama4_eagle, llama4_eagle_mm) aborted at engine init with HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES ("Available Free mem : 0 MB") right after CUDA graph capture, while the same model passed on ROCM_AITER_FA.

There are two independent problems, both fixed here:

1. Lazy VRAM reclaim between engines. ROCm frees VRAM lazily, so after cleanup_dist_env_and_memory() the next engine can start memory profiling while the previous engine's VRAM is still resident, read inflated free memory, and size the KV pool too large. Fixed by a wait_for_rocm_memory_to_settle() barrier after each engine teardown so the next engine profiles against a clean device (reuses the existing helper; no-op off ROCm).

2. CUDA graph capture memory not reserved on ROCm (root cause of the remaining OOM). The memory profiler skipped CUDA graph profiling on ROCm (#36720), so the KV cache was sized as if capture were free; capture then had to fit in the (1 - gpu_memory_utilization) slack, and when the fixed capture cost exceeded that slack, startup OOMed. #36720 skipped ROCm because torch.cuda.mem_get_info() and graph_pool_handle() produced incorrect/negative estimates. Both causes are gone: #44825 moved the profiler to torch.accelerator.get_memory_info (reliable on ROCm, already used by the AMD-CI mem tests), and graph_pool_handle resolves to the same torch.cuda handle the live capture path already uses on ROCm. So this re-enables CUDA graph memory profiling on ROCm; XPU stays excluded (#39977).

This supersedes the earlier per-model gpu_memory_utilization=0.85 override (addressing @AndreasKaratzas's review): the profiler now reserves capture memory automatically, which is portable across GPU sizes (a fixed byte cost, not a utilization ratio that maps to different absolute headroom on MI300 vs MI325). The override is removed in this PR.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to diagnose and implement this change. Not a duplicate: no open PR re-enables ROCm CUDA graph memory profiling (#46932 fixes negative estimates on NVIDIA unified-memory GPUs, a different platform and failure mode).

## Test Plan

```
pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py -k "eagle_correctness_heavy"
```

Hardware: AMD MI300 (gfx942), 4 GPUs, TP=4. Run with `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`. Reproduced with the `TRITON_ATTN` cases run back to back (the CI ordering that failed).

## Test Result

Before: the two `TRITON_ATTN` heavy cases fail during engine init:

```
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES: ... Available Free mem : 0 MB
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError'
FAILED v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py::test_eagle_correctness_heavy[TRITON_ATTN-llama4_eagle]
FAILED v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_spec_decode.py::test_eagle_correctness_heavy[TRITON_ATTN-llama4_eagle_mm]
```

After: both cases pass back to back, and the barrier drains VRAM to ~0.28 GiB on all 4 GPUs before each subsequent engine starts:

```
Done waiting for stable free GPU memory on devices devices=[0, 1, 2, 3] ... dur_s=5.10
================= 2 passed, 16 warnings in 2110.20s (0:35:10) =================
```

No `HSA_STATUS_ERROR` occurred in the passing run.

title: [Bugfix][Model Runner V2] Order uniform decodes first so spec decodes aren't misclassified as prefills
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #47239 (GLM-5.2 on Model Runner V2 + MTP: large TPOT fluctuations and low aa_lcr scores).

`split_decodes_and_prefills` assumes the batch is ordered `decode -> short_extend -> prefill` (this contract is in its docstring; the V1 runner enforces it via `reorder_batch_to_split_decodes_and_prefills`). Model Runner V2 sorted requests purely by scheduled-token count. With spec decode (`decode_query_len > 1`), any request scheduling fewer tokens — a 1-token chunked-prefill tail, a prefix-cache-hit remainder, or a P/D-transferred request with no drafts scheduled yet (the issue's NixlConnector setup) — sorts **in front of** the uniform decodes. `require_uniform` backends key uniformity off `query_lens[0]`, so every real decode in that batch gets classified as a **prefill**.

For DSA models (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V3.2) the consequences are severe: the sparse indexer's prefill path gathers each request's **entire KV history** (100k+ tokens on aa_lcr, per full-indexer layer) for every misclassified decode, and the non-uniform batch also drops from FULL cudagraph to eager — multi-second decode steps that recur whenever such a request coexists with decodes. This explains the TPOT fluctuation, and (via eval-client timeouts/truncation) the low long-context scores. The fix cannot live in `split_decodes_and_prefills` itself: it returns a positional prefix split of an already-laid-out batch, so only the runner's layout can restore the invariant.

The fix orders requests with `query_len == decode_query_len` first, then the rest ascending by count. With spec decode disabled (`decode_query_len == 1`) this is exactly the previous ordering.

Also hardens `DeepseekV2MLAAttention` so MTP layers never construct with `skip_topk=True`: the V1 proposer toggles this at runtime via `set_skip_topk` (`index_share_for_mtp_iteration`), but Model Runner V2 never calls it, so a checkpoint whose skip pattern lands on the MTP layer id would leave the draft permanently reading a never-written (`torch.empty`) topk indices buffer. GLM-5.2 (`num_hidden_layers=78`, offset 3, freq 4) happens to evaluate to `False`, so this is preventive, not the cause of #47239.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Checked `gh issue view 47239 --comments` (no linked fix; one contributor offered to investigate but no PR) and `gh pr list --search "47239 in:body"` / searches for "model runner v2 GLM", "V2 model runner mtp accuracy" — no open PR addresses the batch ordering or this issue.

## Test Plan

- New unit test: `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py` — covers the sort key with and without spec decode, and the end-to-end interplay with `split_decodes_and_prefills(require_uniform=True, decode_threshold=2)` reproducing the misclassification scenario from the issue (a 1-token tail + eight 2-token MTP decodes).
- `pre-commit run --files ...` (ruff, mypy 3.10/3.12 manual stage, etc.) on all changed files.

## Test Result

```
$ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py -q
3 passed
```

title: [Bugfix][Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Fix int32 offset overflow in block verification kernels
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

`_compute_cumulative_log_p_kernel` and `_compute_local_residual_mass_kernel` (used when `rejection_sample_method="block"`) multiply int32 logit/request-state indices by vocab-scale strides before int64 promotion. With a GLM-scale vocab (~155k tokens) the byte offset wraps once `logit_idx * vocab >= 2**31` (`logit_idx >= ~13.8k`, reachable with large `max_num_seqs` × `1 + num_speculative_tokens`), or once `req_state_idx * num_speculative_steps * vocab >= 2**31` for the draft-logits buffer. Block verification then reads out-of-bounds logits for requests late in the batch, corrupting acceptance decisions (or crashing with an illegal memory access).

The sibling kernels (`_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel`, `_rejection_kernel`, `_resample_kernel`) already promote these indices to int64 (#46560 fixed the same class of bug in the sampler kernels); this brings the two remaining block-verification kernels in line.

Found while auditing the V2 spec-decode sampling path for #47239 (not the cause of that issue — this path requires the non-default `rejection_sample_method="block"`).

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

`gh pr list --search "rejection sampler overflow"` / `"block verification int32"` — no open PR touches these kernels or this overflow.

## Test Plan

New GPU regression test `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py`: runs one request through `rejection_sample(use_block_verification=True)` alone at index 0, then again placed past the int32 overflow threshold (target-side `logit_idx=15000` with V=155264, and draft-side `req_state_idx=8000` with k=2), asserting identical outputs. Each case allocates ~5 GiB.

## Test Result

```
$ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py -q   # GB200
2 passed

# with the kernel fix reverted (git stash), same test:
2 failed, 2 errors   # CUDA illegal access / output mismatch from wrapped offsets
```

Pre-commit (ruff, mypy) passes on changed files.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fix batch chat endpoint corrupting logprobs when return_token_ids is set
author: fenghourun
body:
### Summary

The `/v1/chat/completions/batch` endpoint wired logprobs rendering to `request.return_token_ids` instead of `return_tokens_as_token_ids`. As a result, setting `return_token_ids` (which should only add a separate `token_ids` list) also silently rendered every logprob `token` as a `"token_id:{id}"` placeholder.

`BatchChatCompletionRequest` was missing the `return_tokens_as_token_ids` field entirely (present on the non-batch `ChatCompletionRequest`), so this PR adds it — default `None` to preserve the server-level `--return-tokens-as-token-ids` fallback — and repoints the logprobs call. The correct use of `return_token_ids` (the token-ID list) is unchanged.

### Not a duplicate
Searched open/closed PRs and issues (`return_token_ids batch logprobs`, `return_tokens_as_token_ids batch`); no existing PR or issue covers this.

### Testing
- Added a GPU-free unit test (field present, defaults to `None`) — passes locally.
- Added integration regression tests (`RemoteOpenAIServer`): logprob tokens are not placeholders with only `return_token_ids` set, and *are* placeholders when `return_tokens_as_token_ids` is set. These require a GPU and rely on CI (no local GPU available).

title: [ModelRunner V2] Fix Mamba2 crash on non-spec-decode
author: njhill
body:
`MambaHybridModelState.build_metadata` populated num_accepted_tokens on every forward pass, so the Mamba2 attention builder passed a wrongly shaped tensor `(num_reqs, not num_decodes)` straight into `selective_state_update`, tripping `assert num_accepted_tokens.shape == (N,)`. This crashed hybrid Mamba2 + MoE models (e.g. `GraniteMoeHybrid`) now routed to V2.

Gate the population on speculative decoding being enabled, matching the V1 runner which only passes `num_accepted_tokens`/`num_decode_draft_tokens` to the Mamba2/GDN builder under use_spec_decode. num_speculative_tokens is the same signal the builders use for use_spec_decode; the conv/ssm kernels treat None as the neutral (offset 0) value, so this is a no-op versus V1 for non-spec-decode steps and also avoids a redundant per-step gather that GDN discards.

This also avoids doing some redundant work in non-spec-decode cases.

Verified on GPU: GraniteMoeHybrid runs to completion on V2 and produces output numerically identical to V1; Falcon-H1 (Mamba2, non-MoE) passes test_hybrid on both V1 and V2.

Bug found with help from Claude

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Add missing draft_id_to_target_id to DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM
author: Laurent-Zhang
body:
## What this PR does

Fixes #47418

`DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` is a full-vocab draft model (draft ids are target ids, no d2t remapping). However, `DSparkSpeculator.load_draft_model` accesses `model.draft_id_to_target_id` unconditionally, causing an `AttributeError` when running DeepSeek-V4-Flash with DSpark.

### Root Cause

In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py:86`:
```python
if self.draft_logits is not None and model.draft_id_to_target_id is not None:
```

This line assumes the draft model has a `draft_id_to_target_id` attribute, but `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` doesn't define it.

### Fix

Add `draft_id_to_target_id = None` as a class attribute to `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, consistent with:
- The full-vocab identity mapping already implemented in `map_draft_to_target()` (returns draft_ids directly)
- The pattern used in `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` (which sets it to `None` when draft_vocab == target_vocab)

### Testing

The fix is minimal and follows the existing pattern. The check `model.draft_id_to_target_id is not None` will now correctly evaluate to `False`, skipping the d2t scatter logic that isn't needed for full-vocab drafts.

title: [Bugfix] Fix pooled Whisper encoder sliding-window kernel size
author: njhill
body:
The causal Whisper encoder pools `block_pool_size` encoder tokens per KV block, so its `SlidingWindowSpec.sliding_window` is expressed in pooled units for the KV cache manager. The attention kernel, however, reads its window from the same spec field but runs on the `block_pool_size`x-expanded (unpooled) sequence, so it interpreted the pooled window as an unpooled one and attended to `block_pool_size`x too few tokens.

This was latent until #47071 scaled `sliding_window` down into pooled units (to stop over-reserving KV blocks): that scaling also shrank the kernel window `block_pool_size`x, truncating the encoder's effective context and changing Voxtral Realtime transcriptions (test_realtime_validation failure).

Fix by decoupling the two consumers: keep the pooled window (plus a one-block eviction margin) for the manager's retention/reservation, and pass the model's real unpooled window through to the block-pooling builder so the kernel attends over the correct range.

Fixes the CI failure on main: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/75877#019f2067-ce90-4ce8-ba8c-e54c54dae0c4

cc @andylolu2

title: [BugFix] Fix ModelOpt quantization inference for fused siblings
author: jasonlizhengjian
body:
## Summary

Fix ModelOpt mixed-precision dispatch so unlisted fused projections remain unquantized.

This removes the generic parent-sibling fallback from `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig._resolve_quant_algo` and adds explicit `packed_modules_mapping` declarations to the NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 causal and conditional model classes. Explicit packed mappings preserve MiniMax `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj` dispatch without inferring quantization for unrelated or intentionally unquantized siblings.

Fixes #47241.
Follow-up to #46756.

## Root cause

Qwen3.6 stores GDN `in_proj_a` and `in_proj_b` as BF16 tensors without quantization scales, while vLLM fuses them into `in_proj_ba`.

The parent-prefix fallback added by #46756 observed that the other direct `linear_attn` children were FP8 and incorrectly classified the unlisted `in_proj_ba` as FP8. The loader then copied BF16 checkpoint tensors into FP8 parameters while the expected scale placeholders had no checkpoint values. Shapes still matched, so loading completed, but recurrent attention state and logits were corrupted.

## Why this is not duplicate work

#47354 guards the fallback with `packed_modules_mapping`. That fixes unregistered siblings such as Nemotron Mamba `conv1d` and `norm`, but Qwen's unquantized `in_proj_ba` is itself a registered packed module, so the guarded fallback still classifies it as FP8.

This PR removes the unsafe inference entirely and makes the original MiniMax requirement explicit in the NVIDIA model classes. Resolution therefore succeeds only when declared packed shards are present and agree on their quantization algorithm.

## Validation

- B300 SXM6 AC, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, deterministic prompts with `temperature=0` and `enable_thinking=false`:
  - Before: both prompts emitted token `248050` (`<|box_end|>`) repeatedly.
  - After: France prompt returned `Paris`; `2+2` returned `4`.
- B300 focused ModelOpt mixed-precision tests: `6 passed`.
- After rebasing onto current `main`, CPU-safe resolver regression tests: `4 passed`.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py`: all applicable hooks passed.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with root-cause analysis, implementation, and test execution. The human submitter reviewed the complete diff and validation results.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Ship examples/ in the CPU release image
author: leoojiang
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #47401. The `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu` image is missing `examples/` (e.g. `examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja`), so `--chat-template examples/*.jinja` and the documented example paths don't work out of the box on CPU.

The `vllm-openai` release stage in `docker/Dockerfile.cpu` is `FROM base`, and never copies `examples/`. The `ADD ./examples/ ./examples/` that already exists in the file is in the `vllm-test` stage, which is only used to run the test suite — it doesn't reach the released image. So this isn't a stale-tag issue; a nightly/next build wouldn't include `examples/` either. The CUDA image, by contrast, ships `examples/`.

This copies `examples/` into the CPU `vllm-openai` stage (inherited by `vllm-openai-zen`), restoring parity with the CUDA image.

title: [Bugfix] Recycle post-final-norm hidden in GLM MTP (single norm)
author: zhou9402
body:
The compile-free DeepseekV32 MTP draft layer returned the pre-final-norm hidden as both the draft-logits hidden and the recycled previous_hidden_states. Recycling the pre-final-norm hidden mismatches the draft model's hnorm and drops MTP acceptance; the reference deepseek_mtp.py (PR #45895) recycles the post-final-norm hidden.

Fix by computing the post-final-norm hidden once -- fusing the residual-add into the final RMSNorm (fused_add_rms_norm) -- and returning it for both tuple positions. compute_logits then applies the LM head only (no second RMSNorm), so the norm count is unchanged (one per draft step per layer) while the recycled hidden is now correctly post-norm.

The tuple return is understood by both the V2 speculator (isinstance-tuple check in autoregressive/speculator.py) and the legacy proposer (model_returns_tuple() is True for the DeepSeekMTPModel architecture used by GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2). SharedHead and the proposer contracts are unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Outputs] Reject empty `structural_tag` at request validation
author: linnea-lin-00638949
body:
## What does this PR do?

Rejects degenerate `structured_outputs.structural_tag=""` input at request validation (HTTP 400), extending the existing guards added in #45346.

`structured_outputs.structural_tag=""` passes the `is not None` exclusivity check in `get_structured_output_key` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/request.py`) and reaches `json.loads("")` inside `compile_grammar` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py`), raising `JSONDecodeError`. Since #47312, such grammar compilation failures no longer tear down the engine — the scheduler finishes the request as a per-request error — but the request still surfaces as an engine-side error (500) instead of a clean 400 at validation.

This PR adds an empty-string guard for `structural_tag` next to the existing `json`/`grammar` checks in `_validate_structured_outputs` (`vllm/sampling_params.py`), so the degenerate request is rejected at request validation (HTTP 400) for consistency. Also extends the parametrized `test_degenerate_structured_outputs_rejected` with the new case.

Note on `regex`: an empty or whitespace-only `regex` is a valid pattern (e.g. `regex="\n"` or `regex=" "` compile to a valid grammar), so it is intentionally **not** checked — see the code comment and review discussion.

## Why is this not duplicating an existing PR?

- #45346 fixed `json=""` and `json_object=False` but did **not** cover `structural_tag=""`.
- #47312 made engine-side grammar compilation failures non-fatal, but does not reject this degenerate input at the validation layer (it surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400).

Searched open issues/PRs for "structural_tag empty" / "structured_outputs crash" — none address these.

## Test commands run and results

Unit test (extends `test_degenerate_structured_outputs_rejected`):

```
pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_validation.py -v
```

All 21 cases pass on the latest `main`, including the 3 parametrized degenerate cases (`json_object=False`, `json=""`, `structural_tag=""` all raise `VLLMValidationError` with the expected messages).

End-to-end behavior (verified on Ascend NPU, qwen3.5-122b-a10b-w8a8-mtp, TP=8, MTP, xgrammar backend via `auto`):

| request | before this PR | after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `structured_outputs.structural_tag=""` | engine-side per-request error (non-fatal since #47312) | HTTP 400 |
| `structured_outputs.json=""` | HTTP 400 (existing guard) | HTTP 400 |
| `structured_outputs.json_object=true` (normal) | HTTP 200 | HTTP 200 (no false positive) |

Note: at the original base of this PR (pre-#47312), `structural_tag=""` crashed EngineCore with `EngineDeadError` and took down all workers; that failure mode was fixed upstream in #47312. This PR now purely adds the validation-layer rejection (clean 400 + consistency).

`GET /v1/models` stayed 200 after normal requests; the backend did not change behavior for valid requests.

title: [macOS][CPU][Installation] Fix the broken installation of vllm 0.24.0 in macos + cpu
author: WindChimeRan
body:
## Problem

vllm-metal installation is broken, because it cannot compile the vllm dependency on mac before this PR. 

`tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2` in `requirements/cuda.txt` has no platform marker, but the package itself only publishes `manylinux` wheels (no sdist). Since `setup.py`'s `get_requirements()` copies this file's lines verbatim into vLLM's published `install_requires`, the unconditional requirement ships in every release regardless of installer platform. Result: `pip install vllm==0.24.0` fails to resolve on macOS entirely, before any build-time device detection even runs.

<details>
<summary>Repro logs (macOS/arm64/M5 Pro)</summary>

```
$ uv pip install vllm==0.24.0
Using Python 3.12.13 environment at: repro-before
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2 has no wheels with a matching
      platform tag (e.g., `macosx_26_0_arm64`) and vllm==0.24.0 depends on
      tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2, we can conclude that vllm==0.24.0 cannot be used.
      And because you require vllm==0.24.0, we can conclude that your
      requirements are unsatisfiable.

hint: Wheels are available for `tokenspeed-mla` (v0.1.2) on the following
platforms: `manylinux_2_28_aarch64`, `manylinux_2_28_x86_64`

$ uv pip install tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2   # isolated, no vllm involved
Using Python 3.12.13 environment at: repro-before
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2 has no wheels with a matching platform tag
      (e.g., `macosx_26_0_arm64`) and you require tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2, we
      can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.

hint: Wheels are available for `tokenspeed-mla` (v0.1.2) on the following
platforms: `manylinux_2_28_aarch64`, `manylinux_2_28_x86_64`
```

</details>

## Fix

`tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2` → `tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2; platform_system == "Linux"`

## Why a Linux marker is correct here, even proposed from macOS

Platform markers are evaluated by the installer against the machine running `pip install`, not against whatever machine built the wheel — that's the whole mechanism that makes this fix work at all. `tokenspeed-mla` only ships Linux wheels, so gating on `platform_system == "Linux"` is exactly true where the package can install and exactly false everywhere the current unconditional requirement breaks today.

<details>
<summary>Verification logs</summary>

```
$ python3 -c "from packaging.requirements import Requirement; \
    req = Requirement('tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2; platform_system == \"Linux\"'); \
    print('marker:', req.marker); \
    print('evaluates on THIS machine (Darwin):', req.marker.evaluate()); \
    print('evaluates if platform_system=Linux :', req.marker.evaluate({'platform_system': 'Linux'}))"
marker: platform_system == "Linux"
evaluates on THIS machine (Darwin): False
evaluates if platform_system=Linux : True

$ uv pip install 'tokenspeed-mla==0.1.2; platform_system == "Linux"'   # same package, marker added
Using Python 3.12.13 environment at: repro-after
Checked 1 package in 0.37ms
```

</details>

Also confirmed `setup.py`'s own `_read_requirements()` parsing preserves the marker unmodified when reading `requirements/cuda.txt`.

Added repro log, before and after.
