title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Detokenizer: avoid leaking prompt on zero-generated-token completions
author: xiaguan
body:
## Summary

`DecodeStream::flush()` called before any `push_token()` (i.e. a request that finishes with zero generated tokens — the engine suppressed the only emitted EOS) leaks the entire prompt text into `cumulative_output`, because `seed_prefix` never ran and `prefix` stays empty.

This mirrors the Python V1 path, where `BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.update()` early-returns on empty `new_token_ids`, leaving `output_text` untouched.

## Root cause

`DecodeStream` stores prompt token ids in `self.ids` as left context and relies on `seed_prefix()` to move the decoded prompt into `self.prefix`, so subsequent decodes only emit the delta after the prefix. `seed_prefix()` was only called from `push_token()`; `flush()` bypassed it and decoded the whole `self.ids` (== prompt) with `prefix_len = 0`.

## Fix

Call `seed_prefix()` at the top of `flush()` when it has not been seeded yet. After seeding, `ids` holds only prompt context and `prefix` matches it, so the delta slice is empty — matching the Python contract.

## Repro

Engine emits EOS as the first generated token on a degenerate prompt; the engine suppresses it (counted, not emitted) and finishes with `stop` after zero emitted tokens. The non-stream collector then returns the entire 7001-token prompt as `choices[0].text` with `completion_tokens: 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `flush_without_push_token_does_not_leak_prompt` — new regression test (red before fix, green after)
- [x] `cargo test --features test-utils --lib -p vllm-tokenizer` — 56 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `cargo test --lib -p vllm-text` — 63 passed, 0 failed

title: [Bugfix]Fix DeepSeek-V4 fp8_ds_mla KV cache reshape
author: ACEEE-1222
body:
Fixes #47648.

DeepSeek-V4 FlashMLA uses a custom `fp8_ds_mla` KV layout with 584 bytes per token. The main MLA and SWA cache specs already carry `cache_dtype_str`, but they did not consistently expose `kv_quant_mode`, and the GPU model runner used the global cache dtype when computing backend KV cache shapes.

As a result, DSpark serving on H200 could allocate/reshape SWA KV cache as the semantic 512-byte head size, then fail in FlashMLA sparse decode with:

```text
RuntimeError: kv must have shape (num_blocks, page_block_size, h_kv, bytes_per_token)
```

This PR propagates `kv_quant_mode` for DeepSeek-V4 MLA/SWA specs and prefers the layer-local `cache_dtype_str` when computing KV cache shapes.

Co-discovered and validated with @yy-fighting.

## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark startup on H200/SM90 with FlashMLA when using `--spec-method dspark` and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

Before this change, the DeepSeek-V4 SWA KV cache could be reshaped as:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 512)
```

but FlashMLA expects the DeepSeek-V4 `fp8_ds_mla` layout:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)
```

## Test Plan

Tested on 4x H200 with `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`.

Serve command:

```bash
vllm serve /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --spec-method dspark \
  --spec-model /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --spec-tokens 5 \
  --port 30004
```

Small serving benchmark:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30004 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 128 \
  --random-output-len 32 \
  --num-prompts 16 \
  --request-rate 4 \
  --max-concurrency 4 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

## Test Result

Before the fix, startup failed during DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA warmup:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 512)
RuntimeError: kv must have shape (num_blocks, page_block_size, h_kv, bytes_per_token)
```

After the fix, the cache shape is correct:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)
kv_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)   # compress_ratio=4
kv_shape=(83520, 2, 1, 584)    # compress_ratio=128
```

Full startup completed:

```text
DeepGEMM warmup: 100%|...| 1281/1281
Graph capturing finished
/health -> 200
```

Benchmark result:

```text
Successful requests: 16
Failed requests: 0
Total input tokens: 2048
Total generated tokens: 512
Request throughput: 1.34 req/s
Output token throughput: 42.99 tok/s
Acceptance rate: 2.56%
```

title: [BugFix][LoRA] Refresh punica metadata when LoRA slots are reassigned under an unchanged mapping
author: AmeenP
body:
FIX #47724

## Purpose

`LoRAModelManager.set_adapter_mapping` memoizes on `self._last_mapping` (the
per-token LoRA ID mapping of the running batch) and skips the punica metadata
refresh when it is unchanged. The memo is never invalidated when a GPU slot is
reassigned: an out-of-band `add_lora()` on a live engine eagerly activates the
new adapter (`LRUCacheWorkerLoRAManager.add_adapter` -> `activate_adapter`),
which can LRU-evict a slot held by an adapter that is currently decoding and
rotate `lora_index_to_id`. Because the in-flight request set is unchanged, the
`LoRAMapping` is identical, the memo hits, and `punica_wrapper.update_metadata`
is skipped — `token_lora_indices` still encodes the old slot layout, and
in-flight requests silently decode with another adapter's weights. See
#47724 for the full analysis and a self-contained reproduction.

This PR keys the memo on the slot layout as well as the mapping: the refresh
now also runs whenever `tuple(self.lora_index_to_id)` has changed since the
last call. Per-step no-op calls (the common case) still hit the memo, so the
optimization is preserved.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs and issues for `set_adapter_mapping`,
punica staleness, and `add_lora` eviction — no existing report or fix
(closest are unrelated: #36187 LoRA shrink kernel contiguity, #39935
sleep/wake with LoRA).

## Test Plan

1. New regression test
   `tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_set_adapter_mapping_refreshes_after_slot_reassignment`:
   drives the exact production sequence at the manager level — two adapters
   decoding in both slots, an out-of-band activation LRU-evicts and the
   re-activation lands the batch's adapters in swapped slots, then
   `set_adapter_mapping` is called with an identical mapping. Asserts
   `punica_wrapper.token_lora_indices` follows the new slot layout. Fails on
   `main` without the fix (metadata stays `[0, 1]`), passes with it.
2. End-to-end reproduction script from #47724 (1x H100): reference
   phase, repeated reference phase (determinism control), then a test phase
   with `add_lora()` churn against two greedy in-flight decodes.

```
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_set_adapter_mapping_refreshes_after_slot_reassignment -v
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn python3 lora_memo_bug_min_repro.py
```

## Test Result

All validation on 1x H100, vLLM `main` @ `ba2215209` via the per-commit
precompiled wheel, plus released 0.22.1 / 0.24.0.

Unit test (main @ `ba2215209`):

- without the fix: FAILED at the final assertion (`assert [0, 1] == [1, 0]` —
  `token_lora_indices` still encodes the pre-eviction slot layout)
- with the fix: PASSED
- (both runs show one teardown error specific to the validation pod's
  environment; unmodified neighboring tests, e.g.
  `test_lora_lru_cache_model_manager`, show the identical teardown error there)

End-to-end repro script from the issue (three phases: reference, repeated
reference as per-stream determinism control, then `add_lora()` churn; greedy,
prefix caching disabled):

| build | slot-map changes | punica refresh skipped | A1 stream (control bitwise-clean) |
|---|---|---|---|
| stock 0.22.1 | 62 | 59 | diverges under churn @ token 509 |
| stock 0.24.0 | 64 | 58 | diverges under churn @ token 510 |
| stock main @ ba2215209 | 63 | 58 | diverges under churn @ token 515 |
| fixed 0.24.0 | 64 | 0 | bitwise identical under churn |
| fixed 0.24.0 (repeat) | 63 | 0 | bitwise identical under churn |
| fixed main @ ba2215209 | 53 | 0 | bitwise identical under churn |

The fixed rows double as the determinism control for the divergence claim:
the identical churn workload with only the fix applied produces zero skipped
refreshes and byte-identical outputs, so the stock-build divergence is caused
by the stale routing, not by add/decode timing.

Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.

---

reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][V1] Free out-of-window blocks on the processed-token basis under async scheduling
author: Saddss
body:
> **Attribution.** Core fix is the main contribution of @ivanium (Yifan Qiao), from `ivanium/vllm#50` (original commit authorship preserved). The problem/fix write-up below is transcribed from that PR. @Saddss added the empirical verification, the regression analysis, and additional test cases (second commit).

## Problem

With async scheduling (now default) or PP, the scheduler runs ahead of the GPU: `request.num_computed_tokens` is advanced at schedule time. `remove_skipped_blocks` (SWA / chunked-local / mamba) used this optimistic count as the free boundary, causing two bugs:

1. **vllm-project#47282 (load-WAR):** blocks still covered by an in-flight step's attention window are returned to the pool; a KV-consumer connector reallocates them as load destinations and overwrites them on an unordered stream mid-read.
2. **Spec-rejection misfree (silent):** rejected spec tokens roll the boundary back below already-nulled blocks, so attention reads null KV. Upstream only patched this locally for Mamba (`num_speculative_tokens` subtraction); SWA / chunked-local were exposed.

## Fix

One mechanism fixes both: track `Request.num_in_flight_tokens` (scheduled minus processed, structurally symmetric across preemption / spec rejection / failed-KV-load) and free on the **settled basis** `num_computed_tokens - num_in_flight_tokens`.

Invariant: a block is returned to the pool only when it is outside the attention window of every unprocessed step and no rollback can make it needed again. Sync scheduling has zero in-flight tokens — behavior unchanged, no gating flag.

Consequential (not an independent fix): the SWA / chunked-local per-request admission bound grows to `W - 1 + max_concurrent_batches * max_num_batched_tokens`, applied in the single source of truth used by both startup pool sizing and the runtime gate. MambaManager's local subtraction is removed (subsumed exactly, now also covering prefill chunks and PP depth).

Alternatives considered: vllm-project#47653 (BlockPool fence) and a scheduler-callback defer both fence the free downstream; this PR corrects the lying input instead — no new queues, no BlockPool state, no callbacks. Request-level finish/preempt frees remain behind the vllm-project#45357 fence (write-after-free, unreachable by a lagged basis).

## Tests

- New: `tests/v1/core/test_swa_inflight_window_free.py` — counter symmetry, out-of-window blocks held until the reader step is processed, sync unchanged, admission cap.
- Regression (all pass): `test_deferred_block_free`, `test_single_type_kv_cache_manager`, `test_kv_cache_utils`, `test_async_scheduler`, `test_prefix_caching`, offloading-connector scheduler suite (82), `test_scheduler.py` failure set byte-identical to clean main (35 pre-existing env failures).

AI assistance was used for this change; every line reviewed by the submitter.

---

## Added by @Saddss

### Additional test coverage

Extends `tests/v1/core/test_swa_inflight_window_free.py` (7 tests total, all pass on latest nightly):

- `test_chunked_local_free_waits_for_in_flight_step` / `test_chunked_local_admission_cap_accounts_for_overlapping_batches` — chunked-local analogues of the SWA in-flight-free and admission tests (it prunes whole chunks and is exposed to the same WAR).
- `test_connector_finish_frees_on_settled_basis` — covers the second prune site, `Scheduler._connector_finished`: the out-of-window prune done *before the block table is handed to a KV connector* (the simple CPU offload / NIXL store, i.e. the exact #47282 load-WAR site) must also use the settled basis. **Control-verified**: reverting `_connector_finished` to raw `num_computed_tokens` makes this test fail.

### GPU e2e garble repro (the item left "not yet run" above)

Gemma-3-27B-class model, single GPU, simple CPU offload (100 GB), async scheduling:

| | stock nightly | with fix |
|---|---|---|
| Garbled responses | **4.5%** (27/600) | **0.0%** (0/600) |

### Performance (no offload, KV-bound)

- **Normal length (~3.7k tok/req)**: throughput/latency **identical to stock** — the reduced *reported* KV size / max-concurrency from the wider admission bound is cosmetic for this shape.
- **Near-max length (~15.5k tok/req)**: ~34% lower total throughput, +51% duration, +125% mean TTFT — the cost of the (intentional) more conservative admission cap for SWA / chunked-local when overlapping batches are possible. Known trade-off, to be revisited via admission-logic optimization for KV-constrained cases.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen2.5-VL] Honor video fps for temporal M-RoPE
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

Qwen2.5-VL currently loses video metadata before calling the HuggingFace processor. Since the HF video processor refactor, `second_per_grid_ts` is computed from `video_metadata.sampled_fps`; when vLLM drops that metadata, pre-decoded videos fall back to a default sampled fps instead of the request/video fps. That value drives the temporal M-RoPE scale used by the model, so videos tagged at 1fps and 30fps get the same temporal spacing in vLLM.

This fixes the Qwen2.5-VL path by keeping video metadata in the data parser, splitting `(video, metadata)` tuples before the HF processor call, and forwarding `video_metadata` so HF can compute `sampled_fps` from the real frame metadata. The dummy video builder also attaches synthetic metadata, matching the Qwen3-VL pattern and keeping memory profiling inputs valid once metadata is required.

Scope: the Qwen2.5-VL processor path. Qwen2-VL does not capture `second_per_grid_ts` in the same way, so that would be a separate change. vLLM's video loader already attaches metadata for URL/file inputs; the changed behavior is that bare pre-decoded video arrays without metadata now fail clearly instead of silently using a fallback fps.

Duplicate-work check: I did not find an open PR covering Qwen2.5-VL video metadata forwarding. PR #23058 is Qwen2.5-Omni only, PR #43198 only lets video frame sampling use a request `fps` override, PR #45555 only adds loader-side metadata that this path still dropped, and PR #47407 only bounds M-RoPE positions.

## Test Plan

Run a real `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` `LLM.generate` path on an RTX 4090, instrument the live model's `iter_mm_grid_thw`, and compare the temporal `t_factor` for the same video tagged as fps=1.0 and fps=30.0 before, after, and after reverting the fix. Add one CPU regression case to the existing Qwen2-VL processor test file to assert `second_per_grid_ts` tracks fps, run affected Qwen2.5-VL video tests, and run ruff on all changed files.

title: Fix KV offloading GSM8K eval: prefix caching, CPU reload verification, device fit
author: Etelis
body:
Fixes for #46893 — addresses @orozery's review and the failing `lm-eval-kv-offload-*` steps.

- Enable prefix caching and reset the GPU prefix cache between passes (`POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false`) so pass 2 must reload KV from CPU. Without it, hybrid models crash at startup and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` silently disables itself.
- Wait for `BlockStored(medium="CPU")` KV events before the reset so pass 2 never races the async offload (`OffloadingConnector`).
- Assert `vllm:external_prefix_cache_{queries,hits}` deltas to verify loading actually occurred (both connectors).
- Fix device fit: Qwen3.5-35B → 2xH100 (TP=2), DeepSeek-V4-Flash → 4xH100 (TP=4); both OOMed on the current devices.
- Widen `source_file_dependencies` to cover `vllm/v1/kv_offload/` and the simple connector.

Qwen's 0.75 threshold needs a baseline from the first green run.

title: [ROCm][KVConnector][MoRI-IO] Fix WRITE-mode remote-TP rank collapse (#46332 follow-up)
author: avininjamay8
body:
## Purpose

 In WRITE mode, each prefill TP rank must target the correct decode TP rank for KV transfer. #46332 introduced heterogeneous TP support, requiring the prefill to query the decode's TP size (remote_tp_size) from the proxy to compute the correct target rank. The rank mapping reads peer TP size from kv_transfer_params, but the proxy sets remote_tp_size not tp_size. The old code read tp_size which was never set, defaulting to 1. This caused all 8 prefill TP ranks to fan into decode rank 0, leaving 7/8 of the decode KV cache unwritten and accuracy collapsing to near zero in WRITE mode. READ mode was unaffected.

**Changes**

- moriio_common.py - read remote_tp_size (falling back to tp_size, then 0) when building transfer params.
- moriio_connector.py - treat remote_tp_size <= 0 as homogeneous TP (use local world_size) instead of collapsing to rank 0.

## Test Plan

MoRIIO connector over RoCE RDMA fabric, 1P1D WRITE mode (`read_mode: false`), nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`.

### Homogeneous TP8 — MI350X

Serve DeepSeek-V3 1P1D, prefill TP8 / decode TP8.

        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"proxy_ip":"$PREFILL_IP","proxy_ping_port":"36367",                                                       "http_port":"8200","handshake_port":"6301","notify_port":"61005","read_mode":false}}'

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Key sparse-MLA persistent metadata on per-request context lengths
author: Rohan138
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the sparse-MLA persistent-metadata cache collision behind #47042
(GLM-4.6 / DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA models on ROCm produce correct output up to
~20K tokens, then collapse into repetition/garbage at longer context).

The ROCm sparse-MLA backend caches the persistent work-stealing metadata and
recomputes it only when `metadata_key` changes. The key was keyed on
`min(seq_lens, topk)`, but the metadata actually depends on the per-token KV
length distribution: a first prefill chunk ramps `1 → topk`, while a
continuation chunk whose context already exceeds `topk` is uniform at `topk`.
Both clamp to the same value, so a prefill spanning ≥3 chunks reuses the first
chunk's work partition for later chunks and corrupts the output, which compounds
across layers and breaks long-context decode.

The persistent kernel itself is correct given correct metadata (see
ROCm/aiter#4076); this is purely a vLLM-side cache-key bug.

## Fix

Add the clamped per-request **context length** and per-request **query lengths**
to `metadata_key` so ramp-vs-uniform chunks no longer collide. Decode
(context ≫ topk) still yields a stable key, so it keeps hitting the cache — no
regression to the persistent perf path.

This supersedes the disable-persistent-for-prefill mitigation in #47567 by
fixing the actual cause and retaining the persistent path for chunked prefill.

## Test

NIAH via raw `/v1/completions` (greedy, cudagraph + compile on), GLM-5.1-FP8,
MI355X / gfx950, TP8:

| context | chunks | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2K  | 1 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| 30K | 3 | 0/10 (garbage) | 10/10 |
| 40K | 4 | garbage | 9–10/10 |

Reproduces and is fixed on both pinned `aiter 0.1.16.post2` and aiter ToT.
`gsm8k` (lm_eval) unchanged — the decode path is untouched.

title: [ROCm][BugFix] Triton W4A16 handling for GPTQ/AutoGPTQ qzeros layout
author: giuseppegrossi
body:
## Purpose

Fix ROCm Triton W4A16 handling for GPTQ/AutoGPTQ `qzeros` layout specifically issue #47159.
This addresses two related issues:
- Symmetric/biased GPTQ models may still have `qzeros` tensors registered by the loader, but the Triton kernel should not use them. For biased types such as `uint4b8`, `apply_weights()` now passes `qzeros=None`, so the kernel uses scalar `zp_bias` and runs with `HAS_ZP=False`.
- `TritonW4A16LinearKernel.process_weights_after_loading()` previously always transposed `qzeros`, assuming compressed-tensors layout `[N // 8, K // group_size]`. GPTQ/AutoGPTQ models can already load `qzeros` in the kernel-expected layout `[K // group_size, N // 8]`, causing a shape assertion failure during vLLM startup.

## Test Plan

On MI300 machine using nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`

`python3 -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_triton_w4a16.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_w4a16_kernel_selection.py`

- Add regression coverage that verifies symmetric uint4b8 calls triton_w4a16_gemm() with `qzeros=None` and scalar `zp_bias`.
- Add a regression test covering GPTQ/AutoGPTQ-style `qzeros` layout.
- Run end to end on a GPTQ model using lm-eval and GSM8K dataset
 
## Test Result

- Both the new tests passed
- All 20 tests passed
- `gsm8k flexible-extract exact_match: 0.8423 ± 0.0100`

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Align CrossEncoder token type ids after truncation
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

CrossEncoder scoring compresses `token_type_ids` into a query/document split point before post-tokenization truncation runs. When a request uses `truncate_prompt_tokens` with `truncation_side="left"`, the kept prompt tokens can all come from the document segment, but the stale split still marks them as query tokens. `LLM.score()`, `/score`, and `/rerank` can then return HTTP 200 with silently wrong scores for BERT-style cross-encoder models such as `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2`.

This change applies the same post-tokenization truncation to `token_type_ids` before compressing the split, while preserving existing pooling extras such as `cache_salt`. Requests without token type ids keep the old path, and requests that do not change the prompt length keep the same compressed boundary.

I did not find an existing issue or PR for this token type boundary bug. The nearest merged PR is #47082, which preserves cross-encoder `extra_kwargs` but does not update the compressed boundary after truncation.

## Test Plan

Run a real `LLM.score()` E2E with `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2`, comparing vLLM raw scores against HF references using the correct left-truncated segment ids and the stale all-query segment ids. Run the same script with the fix, after reverting the fix, and after restoring the fix. Run the full cross-encoder offline scoring test file plus scoped ruff, format, and diff checks.

## Test Result

The E2E flips in the expected direction. On main/reverted, vLLM is closer to the stale all-query HF score. With the fix, vLLM is closer to the correct left-truncated HF score.

| checkout | `vllm_raw` | abs vs correct HF | abs vs stale HF |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fix reverted | -2.5138039588928223 | 1.7291163206100464 | 0.08860945701599121 |
| fixed | -0.8064682483673096 | 0.02178061008453369 | 1.6187262535095215 |

<details><summary>repro and checks</summary>

Environment:

```text
source commit: 990c2a0187228b6596e355a7045f7acf3f2f0ca1
model: cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2
model snapshot: c5ee24cb16019beea0893ab7796b1df96625c6b8
runner: pooling
dtype: float32
max_model_len: 128
GPU: RTX 4090 24GB
request: LLM.score(..., truncate_prompt_tokens=16, truncation_side="left", use_activation=False)
```

Repro script:

```python
import os

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer

from vllm import LLM, PoolingParams
from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.scoring.utils import compress_token_type_ids


MODEL = os.environ.get("MODEL", "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2")
QUERY = os.environ.get("QUERY", "query " * 30)
DOCUMENT = os.environ.get("DOCUMENT", "document " * 30)
TRUNCATE_TO = int(os.environ.get("TRUNCATE_TO", "16"))


def score_hf(
    model: AutoModelForSequenceClassification,
    input_ids: list[int],
    token_type_ids: list[int],
) -> float:
    with torch.inference_mode():
        outputs = model(
            input_ids=torch.tensor([input_ids], device=model.device),
            token_type_ids=torch.tensor([token_type_ids], device=model.device),
            attention_mask=torch.ones((1, len(input_ids)), device=model.device),
        )
    return float(outputs.logits[0, 0].detach().cpu())


def main() -> None:
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
    encoded = tokenizer(
        text=QUERY,
        text_pair=DOCUMENT,
        truncation=False,
        add_special_tokens=True,
    )
    input_ids = list(encoded["input_ids"])
    token_type_ids = list(encoded["token_type_ids"])

    kept_input_ids = input_ids[-TRUNCATE_TO:]
    correct_token_type_ids = token_type_ids[-TRUNCATE_TO:]

    stale_boundary = compress_token_type_ids(token_type_ids)
    wrong_token_type_ids = [
        int(i >= stale_boundary) for i in range(len(kept_input_ids))
    ]

    hf_model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(MODEL).cuda().eval()
    hf_correct = score_hf(hf_model, kept_input_ids, correct_token_type_ids)
    hf_wrong = score_hf(hf_model, kept_input_ids, wrong_token_type_ids)

    llm = LLM(
        model=MODEL,
        runner="pooling",
        dtype="float32",
        enforce_eager=True,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.25,
        max_model_len=128,
    )
    outputs = llm.score(
        QUERY,
        DOCUMENT,
        pooling_params=PoolingParams(use_activation=False),
        tokenization_kwargs={
            "truncate_prompt_tokens": TRUNCATE_TO,
            "truncation_side": "left",
        },
        use_tqdm=False,
    )
    vllm_score = float(outputs[0].outputs.score)

    print(
        {
            "full_len": len(input_ids),
            "kept_len": len(kept_input_ids),
            "stale_boundary": stale_boundary,
            "correct_boundary_after_left": compress_token_type_ids(
                correct_token_type_ids
            ),
            "hf_correct_raw": hf_correct,
            "hf_wrong_raw": hf_wrong,
            "vllm_raw": vllm_score,
            "abs_vllm_minus_correct": abs(vllm_score - hf_correct),
            "abs_vllm_minus_wrong": abs(vllm_score - hf_wrong),
            "vllm_prompt_len": len(outputs[0].prompt_token_ids),
        }
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

title: [Bugfix] Fix handling 5D KV cache in kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive
author: dsocek
body:
## PR Purpose

Fixes `IndexError` in `kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive()` for 5D blocks-first KV caches.

`kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive()` (added in #30275) permutes a received KV cache from HND to NHD layout. It assumes the cache is 4D. But since #42095 is recently merged, non-MLA backends allocate a 5D cache `(num_blocks, 2, block_size, H, D)`. This causes the following error:

```bash
IndexError: index_copy_(): Source dimensionality (4), destination dimensionality (5)
```
(This was also flagged as future work in #37943)

### Fix
Use a 5D-aware `inv_order` when the cache is 5D (while 4D path remains unchanged)

## Test Plan
Quick test with:
```bash
DECODER_KV_LAYOUT=NHD DECODER_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN \
bash tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh
```

Before: `IndexError`
After: **pass**

title: [Bugfix] Allocate HY V3 expert_bias in float32 to prevent silent downcasting
author: aoright
body:
## Purpose

This PR fixes a bug in Hunyuan-V3 (`hy_v3` / `hy_v3_mtp`) MoE model execution where the router selection bias `expert_bias` was allocated in the serving dtype instead of `torch.float32` (closes #47777).

`HYV3MoEFused` allocated `expert_bias` as:
```python
self.expert_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(config.num_experts))
```
Under default torch dtypes like `torch.bfloat16`/`torch.float16`, this parameter was allocated in 16-bit precision. During checkpoint weight loading, the true float32 bias tensor from the checkpoint was silently downcast to 16-bit by `param.data.copy_()`. Because this bias is critical for top-k routing decisions, downcasting flips routing choices on boundary tokens.

This PR explicitly pins `expert_bias` to `torch.float32` (matching `deepseek_v2.py` and Hugging Face's `_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict` settings):
```python
self.expert_bias = nn.Parameter(
    torch.empty(config.num_experts, dtype=torch.float32)
)
```

No duplication: We verified that there are no open PRs addressing this expert bias issue for `hy_v3`.

AI-assisted contribution: This contribution was prepared with the assistance of Claude and Gemini.

## Test Plan

- Run the new unit test confirming correct allocation and `copy_` behaviors:
  ```bash
  pytest --noconftest tests/models/test_hy_v3_expert_bias.py
  ```

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Cast LSE to fp32 in a2a combine to fix bf16 bitcast crash
author: shawntsai
body:
# [Bugfix][DCP] Cast LSE to fp32 in a2a combine to fix bf16 bitcast crash

## Purpose

Fixes #47800.

The DCP all-to-all combine backend (`--dcp-comm-backend a2a`) crashes at
startup on MLA models whose decode backend returns a non-fp32 softmax LSE:

```
ValueError: Cannot bitcast data-type of size 16 to data-type of size 32
```

`dcp_a2a_lse_reduce` (in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/dcp_alltoall.py`) and its
pack/unpack Triton kernels treat the LSE as **fp32** — the packed layout
bit-casts a 32-bit LSE through the output dtype's 16-bit lanes, and the combine
kernel reconstructs it to fp32. The function docstring already documents this:
`cp_attn_lse: [B, H] log-sum-exp values (fp32)`.

But some MLA decode backends create the LSE in the model's activation dtype
(e.g. `triton_mla.py`: `lse = torch.zeros(..., dtype=q.dtype)`), so a bf16 LSE
reaches the pack kernel and `lse_val.to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True)` fails on a
16-bit input.

**Fix:** upcast `cp_attn_lse` to fp32 at the top of `dcp_a2a_lse_reduce` before
packing. No-op when the LSE is already fp32; the LSE is small (`[B, H]`).

## Test Plan

```bash
# Before this PR: crashes at startup with the bitcast ValueError.
# With this PR:   serves normally and produces coherent output.
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --dcp-comm-backend a2a --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code
```

(`--enforce-eager` avoids an unrelated CUDA-graph interaction on some setups;
the fix itself applies to both eager and captured execution.)

## Test Result

- **Before:** `vllm serve ... --dcp-comm-backend a2a` on DeepSeek-V2-Lite
  (bf16, `-tp 8 -dcp 8`) aborts during engine init with
  `ValueError: Cannot bitcast data-type of size 16 to data-type of size 32`.
- **After:** the server reaches `Application startup complete`, `/health`
  returns 200, and completions are coherent (verified at ~65K-token prompts).

## Notes

- The default `ag_rs` backend is unaffected (it doesn't use the packed bitcast
  layout), so this is scoped to the `a2a` path.
- An arguably cleaner long-term fix is to have the MLA decode backends allocate
  the LSE as fp32 directly; this PR fixes it at the consumer to keep the change
  minimal and localized to the code that relies on the fp32 layout. Happy to
  take the alternative approach if maintainers prefer.

title: [Bugfix][OpenAI] Fix streamed completion logprob offsets with echo
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

`/v1/completions` can silently return wrong `logprobs.text_offset` values when `stream=True`, `echo=True`, and `logprobs` are used together.

The first streamed completion chunk may include both the echoed prompt and generated text, but the stream state only advanced by the generated `output.text` length. Later chunks then started their `text_offset` from the generated-only length, so every later offset was shifted left by the prompt length.

This PR advances the offset state by `delta_text`, which is the text actually emitted in the chunk. Non-echo streaming is unchanged because `delta_text == output.text` there.

Why this is not duplicating an existing PR: #44106 covers V2 prompt logprobs, #44938 covers Rust prompt-only completions, #19379/#19380 cover `return_tokens_as_token_ids`, and #19368 is the linked issue for that path. None covers this Python streaming echo offset state.

title: [CI] Fix Transformers modeling backend LoRA test
author: hmellor
body:
As identified in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47804, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47187 added a new attribute to `QKVParallelLinear` for the `split` operation that is added as part of Transformers backend fusion. This new attribute was not copied over by LoRA wrapping classes which caused a test failure.

This PR removes the need for this new attribute as all the necessary information is already contained in `QKVParallelLinear.output_sizes` and `QKVParallelLinear.tp_size`. It does add a minor performance hit in eager mode, but since the values are constants they are compiled away when compile is enabled.

Supersedes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47804 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47824

title: fix: use configured max_logprobs instead of hardcoded 20 in derender validation
author: jperezdealgaba
body:
## Summary

- Replace the hardcoded `top_logprobs` limit of `20` in `_validate_derender_bounds()` with `self.model_config.max_logprobs`, so the derender endpoints respect the server's `--max-logprobs` setting.
- The default value (`20`) comes from the [OpenAI Chat Completions API spec](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/create) which defines `top_logprobs` as "an integer between 0 and 20".
- When `max_logprobs` is `-1` (no cap, via `--max-logprobs -1`), the check is skipped entirely.
- Add a comment documenting the origin of the default value and the OpenAI spec reference.

Follow-up to #47260 per [review comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47260#discussion_r3534286952).

## Test plan

- [x] Updated test docstring and assertion in `test_derender_chat_oversized_top_logprobs_rejected` to validate the error message references `max_logprobs`.
- [x] All pre-commit hooks pass.
- [x] Existing derender bounds tests remain unchanged and compatible (the test model uses the default `max_logprobs=20`).

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve logprobs when top_logprobs is null
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

`/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` both accept `top_logprobs: null`. When a client explicitly requests output logprobs and serializes this optional field as JSON null, current main returns 200 but silently omits generated-token logprobs.

The request conversion uses `top_logprobs` directly as `SamplingParams.logprobs`, so `null` becomes `None` and disables logprob computation. Chat serving also checks `top_logprobs is not None` before rendering logprobs into the response.

This treats `top_logprobs: null` like an omitted `top_logprobs` only when output logprobs are requested: sampled-token logprobs are computed with zero extra top candidates. Requests that do not ask for output logprobs still keep logprobs disabled.

## Test Plan

I reproduced this with a real OpenAI-compatible server using Qwen3-0.6B against both Chat Completions and Responses. The same script fails on current main, passes after this change, fails again after reverting this patch, and passes again after restoring it.

I also added focused protocol tests for Chat, Batch Chat, and Responses request conversion.

## Test Result

Current main returns `chat_logprobs_present=false` and `responses_logprobs_present=false`. After this change, both endpoints include sampled-token logprobs with `top_logprobs=[]`. Reverting the patch brings the missing-logprobs behavior back. Restoring the patch returns both endpoints to `*_logprobs_present=true`.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end reproduction</summary>

Hardware and software:

- 1x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24564 MiB
- vLLM base commit: `373eb314af66559f9ef9d6b50bc2cb835012ef34`
- Engine: V1
- Model used in my run: local cache of `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`

Server command:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:${PYTHONPATH:-}"
export HF_HOME="${HF_HOME:-/root/autodl-tmp/cache/huggingface}"
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-/root/autodl-tmp/cache/xdg}"

PORT=18163
MODEL="${MODEL:-Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B}"

python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name qwen3 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --max-model-len 512 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-log-requests
```

Client script:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request


def post_json(base_url: str, path: str, payload: dict) -> dict:
    data = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{base_url}{path}",
        data=data,
        headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Authorization": "Bearer token",
        },
        method="POST",
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
            body = response.read().decode("utf-8")
            return json.loads(body)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        body = exc.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
        raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {exc.code} from {path}: {body}") from exc


def wait_ready(base_url: str, timeout_s: int = 300) -> None:
    deadline = time.time() + timeout_s
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base_url}/health", timeout=5) as response:
                if response.status == 200:
                    return
        except Exception:
            time.sleep(2)
    raise TimeoutError(f"server did not become ready within {timeout_s}s")


def chat_logprobs_present(response: dict) -> tuple[bool, object]:
    choice = response["choices"][0]
    logprobs = choice.get("logprobs")
    if not logprobs:
        return False, logprobs
    content = logprobs.get("content")
    if not content:
        return False, logprobs
    return all("logprob" in item for item in content), content


def responses_logprobs_present(response: dict) -> tuple[bool, object]:
    for item in response.get("output", []):
        for content in item.get("content", []):
            if content.get("type") == "output_text":
                logprobs = content.get("logprobs")
                if not logprobs:
                    return False, content
                return all("logprob" in item for item in logprobs), logprobs
    return False, response.get("output")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:18163")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="qwen3")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--expect",
        choices=("present", "missing"),
        required=True,
        help="Expected output logprobs state for both Chat and Responses.",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    wait_ready(args.base_url)

    chat_payload = {
        "model": args.model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say one word."}],
        "max_tokens": 2,
        "temperature": 0,
        "logprobs": True,
        "top_logprobs": None,
    }
    responses_payload = {
        "model": args.model,
        "input": "Say one word.",
        "max_output_tokens": 2,
        "temperature": 0,
        "include": ["message.output_text.logprobs"],
        "top_logprobs": None,
    }

    chat = post_json(args.base_url, "/v1/chat/completions", chat_payload)
    responses = post_json(args.base_url, "/v1/responses", responses_payload)

    chat_ok, chat_detail = chat_logprobs_present(chat)
    responses_ok, responses_detail = responses_logprobs_present(responses)

    result = {
        "chat_logprobs_present": chat_ok,
        "responses_logprobs_present": responses_ok,
        "chat_detail": chat_detail,
        "responses_detail": responses_detail,
        "chat_text": chat["choices"][0]["message"].get("content"),
        "responses_text": responses.get("output_text"),
    }
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))

    expected = args.expect == "present"
    if chat_ok != expected or responses_ok != expected:
        print(
            f"EXPECTATION_FAILED expected={args.expect} "
            f"chat={chat_ok} responses={responses_ok}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    print(f"EXPECTATION_OK {args.expect}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

title: fix(security): bound completion prompt list to prevent unbounded engine fan-out
author: jperezdealgaba
body:
The /v1/completions endpoint accepted prompt as a list of arbitrary
length without any outer prompt-count limit. Each list element becomes
a separate engine request, allowing an authenticated client to turn one
HTTP request into an attacker-chosen number of backend subrequests,
starving other tenants of CPU, memory, and scheduling resources.
Add VLLM_MAX_COMPLETION_PROMPTS (default 1024) and reject oversized
prompt lists at Pydantic validation time, before any renderer
preprocessing, engine generator allocation, or response buffering.

title: [CPU][Bugfix] Fix flaky ShortConv prefill test on ARM (uninitialized weights)
author: rahulssv-ibm
body:
## Summary

`tests/kernels/mamba/test_cpu_short_conv.py::test_short_conv_forward_native_prefill`
failed on ARM CI while passing on x86.

## Root cause

The test never initializes the `ShortConv` layer weights — it only calls
`dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm`, which packs the *existing* weights. vLLM Linear
layers allocate weights with `torch.empty` (uninitialized).

- On x86, the heap returns dirty (nonzero) pages, so `in_proj` produces nonzero
  output and the prefill path writes a nonzero `conv_state` → assertion passes.
- On ARM/Linux, fresh allocations come from zero-filled mmap pages, so `in_proj`
  weights+bias are zero → `B`/`x` are zero → prefill writes zeros into
  `conv_state` (initial state is also zero with `has_initial_states=False`) →
  `assert not torch.allclose(conv_state, zeros)` fails.

The decode test passes on ARM because `causal_conv1d_update_torch` shifts the
pre-seeded `randn` state regardless of weight values.

Production code is correct; the defect is a test relying on uninitialized memory.

## Fix

Seed and initialize the layer parameters (`torch.nn.init.normal_`) before the
GEMM dispatch in both tests, making output deterministically nonzero on all
platforms.

Fixes: #35059

title: [Quantization] Bound peak memory when repacking FP4 MoE weights for Marlin
author: joerowell
body:
## Purpose
The FP4 MoE Marlin prep functions repack each expert's weight into a Python list and torch.cat the list into the final [E, ...] tensor. At the cat, the per-expert list and the concatenated result are both live, transiently holding ~2x the repacked weight footprint. For large MoE checkpoints on unified-memory devices (e.g. GB10 where "GPU" memory is shared host DRAM) this spike can exhaust the box during model load.

Fill a preallocated [E, ...] output expert-by-expert instead. Output is byte-identical to the cat; only the intermediate allocation changes. Applied to the weight repack in prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin, prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin, and prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin (the memory-dominant path; scales/bias are much smaller and left unchanged).

title: [Rust Frontend] Fix flaky `tls_handshake_timeout_drops_silent_client` test
author: tahsintunan
body:
### Summary

- Problem: the test manually advanced the paused clock and raced the handshake close against the socket read, making it flaky.
- Reproduce: `for i in $(seq 20); do cargo nextest run -p vllm-server tls_handshake_timeout_drops_silent_client; done`
- Fix: drop the manual `advance`/`yield_now`, let tokio's paused clock auto-advance a bare `read().await`, and assert the close lands at the handshake deadline (20/20 after).

title: [ROCm][CI][MoE] Fix double-transpose of fused w3 expert weights
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a crash when loading fused MoE expert weights whose checkpoint stores the
`gate_up_proj` tensor in a transposed layout (e.g.
`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`).

In `RoutedExperts.load_weights`, a single fused checkpoint tensor
(`gate_up_proj`) is matched **twice** by the expert mapping — once for `w1` and
once for `w3`. The transpose reassigned the outer-loop `loaded_weight`, so the
`w3` iteration saw the tensor **already transposed** by the `w1` iteration and
transposed it a second time. For block-scale tensors (`gate_up_proj_scale_inv`)
this made `chunk(2, dim=1)` split the hidden-block dimension instead of the
intermediate-block dimension, producing shards of the wrong size and crashing
weight loading:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (6) must match the size of tensor b (8)
at non-singleton dimension 0
```

The plain weight survived by luck (after the first transpose its last dim equals
`hidden`, so the second transpose is skipped), but the block scale did not.

Fix: use a per-iteration local variable so the transpose never mutates the shared
`loaded_weight`. Both `w1` and `w3` now start from the original tensor, making
them symmetric.

The `w2` (down_proj) branch matches only once and the non-fused path is
untouched, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_length.py -k "qwen3-30b-moe-vl-eagle3"
```

## Test Result

On ROCm (MI300, gfx942) the target FP8 MoE model now loads and the `tp1`
case passes end-to-end (including the acceptance-length assertions):

```
test_eagle3_acceptance_length[auto-tp1-3-qwen3-30b-moe-vl-eagle3] PASSED
```
---

- [x] Root cause identified (shared `loaded_weight` mutated across w1/w3).
- [x] `w2` and non-fused paths verified unchanged (no regression).
- [ ] (CI) Validate on the ROCm CI lane.

title: [Bugfix] Allow non-contiguous query in FlashInfer FP8 query quantization
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
Fix #47905 

## Purpose

Fix an `AssertionError` in the FlashInfer attention backend when running models that slice their query from a fused QKV projection (e.g. Nemotron) with FP8 KV cache.

#43232 moved the query→FP8 quantization inline into `FlashInferImpl.maybe_quant_query`, guarded by `assert query.is_contiguous()`. Models such as Nemotron produce their query via `q, k, v = qkv.split(...)`, which returns a **view** into the fused QKV tensor. That view has a token-dim stride equal to the full QKV width, so the query is non-contiguous and trips the assert on the native FlashInfer FP8 prefill/decode path:

```
File ".../flashinfer.py", line 1587, in maybe_quant_query
    assert query.is_contiguous()
AssertionError
```

The assert is over-strict. Both `query.view(num_tokens, num_heads * head_size)` and the `scaled_fp8_quant` kernel only require that the per-token `(num_heads, head_size)` block is contiguous — the token-dim stride is free (the kernel reads it from `stride(-2)` and only requires `stride(-1) == 1`). This PR replaces the contiguity assert with that precise precondition (`query.stride(2) == 1 and query.stride(1) == head_size`), keeping the existing zero-copy `view` path.

This is not a duplicate: no open PR addresses the FlashInfer FP8 query-quantization contiguity assertion. It is a follow-up bugfix to #43232.

## Test Plan

Repro: serve a Nemotron model with `--attention-backend FLASHINFER --kv-cache-dtype fp8` (previously raised `AssertionError` in `maybe_quant_query`; also reported on Nemotron + FlashInfer FP8 outside PD-disagg).

- [x] Nemotron + FlashInfer + FP8 KV cache serves without the assertion.
- [x] Existing FlashInfer FP8 paths (contiguous query) unchanged.

## Test Result

Confirmed working

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to diagnose and draft this change.

title: [Bugfix] Patch Hopper MXFP4 OOB scales reads leading to NaN
author: yzong-rh
body:
## Purpose

Patch https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47303 by padding the swizzled scales so that OOB reads won't happen. Mirrors upstream fix in https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/10800. Can be cleaned up when we upgrade our triton kernels to v.3.8.0+.

title: fix: hash speculative draft model config
author: alexeldeib
body:
## Purpose

AOT compilation cache keys include VllmConfig.compute_hash(), which delegates to SpeculativeConfig.compute_hash(). For DFlash and related aux-hidden-state methods, the speculative hash only distinguished whether aux states were used and which aux layer IDs were returned.

That is insufficient when two deployments share an AOT cache root but use different draft model configs with the same aux layer IDs. The second deployment can load an AOT artifact compiled for the first draft model, even though the compiled graph shape contract belongs to a different draft backbone.

Include draft_model_config.compute_hash() whenever aux-hidden-state speculative decoding uses a draft model. Keep the existing layer-id factor so configs that share the same draft model but request different aux states still hash separately.

## Test Plan

~Add a focused regression test covering two DFlash-like configs with identical aux layer IDs but different draft model hashes.~ removed per feedback

## Test Result

Avoids collision between two incompatible models on the cache key. This solves a real-world serving issue where the drafters have slightly different architectures but attempt to reuse the cache leading to assertion errors on code paths like this qwen3_dflash.py -> flash_attn.py -> vllm_flash_attn/cute/interface.py
```
assert k.shape == (num_pages, page_size, num_head_kv, head_dim)
```

Running either model independently with a clean cache works, making the fingerprint fully unique solves the collision.

title: [ROCm] Fix pooling startup workspace lock
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
Motivation: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/76664/list?sid=019f3900-a887-45a4-bd39-f1e71a7beaee&tab=output

`Language Models Test (Extended Pooling)` failed in `test_openai_privacy_filter` while starting `openai/privacy-filter`. This model exposes the startup bug because it combines token-classification pooling, a GptOss/FusedMoE backbone, ROCm modular MoE workspace allocation, and a post-capture warmup shape larger than the graph-capture shape. The root cause is that graph capture locked the workspace after only the small capture-size MoE allocation, then the later sampler/pooler warmup needed the larger max-request MoE workspace. On ROCm V1 workers, this PR now runs the max-request model warmup before CUDA graph capture, so the workspace is sized before captured graphs take workspace pointers and before `lock_workspace()` freezes growth. The post-capture sampler/pooler warmup remains locked, preserving the no-growth invariant for serving. The PR also threads attention sinks through encoder-only Triton/ROCm prefill attention and aligns ROCm encoder-only sliding-window handling with the other backends for the privacy-filter HF comparison.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve abort finish_reason for scale-out token streams
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Purpose

In token mode, `/inference/v1/generate` streams skip engine outputs that have no new token IDs. An abort always ends with such an output (`token_ids=[]`, `finish_reason="abort"`), so an aborted stream ends with `[DONE]` and no `finish_reason`. The only exception is when the abort happens to be merged into a pending token delta. Text mode (#58588) and the Rust frontend already emit every terminal output.

- Every output that has a `finish_reason` is now emitted, in both output modes.
- The per-choice token counter is now sized by `sampling_params.n`. It was sized from the first output, which with `n > 1` may hold only choice 0. The next choice then raised `IndexError`, and the stream ended in a 500 error chunk.

## Test Plan

Live server on H200 with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`. The same requests went to `main` (bc21cba967) and to this PR:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 2048 --no-enable-prefix-caching --tokens-only
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 2048 --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-scale-out --max-num-seqs 1
```

Each request was a streamed `/inference/v1/generate` call with `max_tokens: 900`, `ignore_eos: true` and `include_usage`. It was aborted through `/abort_requests` (or `/inference/v1/abort_requests`) once the first token chunk arrived. With `--max-num-seqs 1`, a second request could also be aborted while still queued.

## Test Result

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| tokens mode, abort mid-stream (also with `logprobs` / `flat_logprobs`) | no `finish_reason` unless the abort merged into a token chunk | final chunk `token_ids: [], finish_reason: "abort"` (`logprobs: {"content": []}`) |
| abort while queued (0 tokens) | no choice chunk | one `abort` chunk |
| `n=2`, abort mid-stream | `list index out of range` 500 chunk in 4/7 runs | both choices get `abort`, 12/12 runs |
| text-mode abort, non-stream abort, `length` / EOS `stop` | — | unchanged |

Usage `completion_tokens` matched the streamed token count in every case.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Restrict embedding-width share guard to EAGLE drafts
author: evantakahashi
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #47794 — Gemma4 MTP fails engine initialization on nightly with a linear shape mismatch (`[s47, 3840] x [5632, 1024]`).

Root cause: #43957 added an embedding-width guard to `_maybe_share_embeddings` that disables target↔draft embedding sharing when the widths differ. That is correct for EAGLE drafts, which consume `input_embeds` in their decoder layers at their own hidden size (the `Eagle3MiniMaxM2` XPU case #43957 fixed). It is wrong for MTP drafts: Gemma4 MTP's `pre_projection` is built as `Linear(2 * backbone_hidden_size, hidden_size)` and its draft-width `embed_tokens` exists only to populate the tied draft-dim `lm_head` — `gemma4_mtp.py` explicitly documents that sharing replaces it with the backbone-width table. With sharing disabled, the concat width becomes `1024 + 2816 = 3840` instead of `2816 + 2816 = 5632`, crashing at init.

Fix: apply the width guard only to EAGLE drafts, keyed on the `has_own_embed_tokens` attribute — the existing EAGLE/MTP discriminator in this method. MTP drafts return to unconditional sharing (pre-#43957 behavior); the #43957 EAGLE behavior is preserved.

## Relationship to existing PRs

I claimed #47794 in the issue at 04:13 UTC with this diagnosis and fix plan ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47794#issuecomment-4900048127)); #47833 was opened at 07:17 UTC without engaging that claim. Beyond the overlap, this PR adds runtime verification driving the real `Gemma4MTP` module (see below), which #47833 notes it could not do, plus an additional MTP dims-match regression case. Happy to consolidate whichever way maintainers prefer.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_share_embeddings.py -v
```

Runtime A/B verification (CPU, no GPU needed): instantiated the real `Gemma4MTP` module (0 decoder layers, draft width 8, backbone width 32) plus a target with a backbone-width embedding table, ran the real `SpecDecodeBaseProposer._maybe_share_embeddings`, then the real `Gemma4MTP.forward` — the exact seam that crashed in the issue.

## Test Result

- On `main` (unfixed): new test `test_mtp_shares_embeddings_when_dims_differ` FAILS; runtime harness reports `embeddings shared: False` and forward crashes with `mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (4x40 and 64x8)` — the scaled analogue of the issue's `3840 x 5632` mismatch.
- With this PR: all 4 tests PASS; harness reports `embeddings shared: True`, `forward OK: draft_hidden=(4, 8) backbone_hidden=(4, 32)`, and the tied draft-dim `lm_head` is left intact.
- EAGLE regression coverage: dims-differ stays unshared (#43957 behavior), dims-match shares.
- `pre-commit` (ruff check/format, mypy hook, typos) passes on changed files.
- Not run: end-to-end GPU serve with the 26B checkpoint (no hardware) — @realmorita, could you confirm on your setup?

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the analysis, fix, tests, and verification; submitted after human review.

title: [Bugfix] Re-sync parameter tp_rank after process_weights_after_loading (fix replicated / disable_tp weight reload)
author: alexxu-roblox
body:
## Purpose

Weight reload can crash for replicated (`disable_tp=True`) parameters such as the DeepSeek-V2/V3 / GLM MLA fused `a`-projection (`q_a_proj` + `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` when `q_lora_rank > 0`).

`BasevLLMParameter.__init__` stamps `self.tp_rank` with the global rank. It is reconciled to the layer's `tp_rank` (0 for `disable_tp`) by `update_param_tp_status()`, but that only runs at construction. When a parameter is re-created after construction (e.g. an FP8 `process_weights_after_loading` that builds a fresh `ModelWeightParameter`) and then reloaded via `load_weights` (RL weight refit), the new parameter carries the global rank again. A replicated weight is then narrowed at `global_rank * shard_size` and every rank > 0 overflows:

```
IndexError: start out of range (expected to be in range of [-576, 576], but got 1152)
RuntimeError: start (576) + length (576) exceeds dimension size (576).
```

## Fix

Make `update_param_tp_status()` the single source of truth for a parameter's TP state, and re-run it whenever parameters are re-created:

- Re-run `layer.update_param_tp_status()` right after `quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(...)` in the default loader (`model_loader/utils.py`) and the layerwise reload path (`model_loader/reload/layerwise.py`).
- Drop the redundant `tp_rank=self.tp_rank` kwarg from the `MergedColumnParallelLinear` / `QKVParallelLinear` (and Minimax indexer) `weight_loader_v2` call sites. The parameter loaders narrow with `self.tp_rank`, which is now always correct.

This supersedes the earlier version of this PR, which instead taught the parameter loaders to honor the `tp_rank` kwarg. Thanks @Isotr0py for the suggestion to unify on `update_param_tp_status`.

## Backward compatibility

- Regular TP layers: `update_param_tp_status()` sets `param.tp_rank == layer.tp_rank`, so offsets are identical.
- Replicated (`disable_tp`) layers: `layer.tp_rank == 0`, so the full replicated weight loads at offset 0 on every rank, matching the initial load.
- This also fixes `load_column_parallel_weight`, which the previous kwarg-based approach left untouched.

## Test Plan

- Existing TP loading is unaffected (offsets identical for `tp_size > 1`).
- Repro: load a DeepSeek-V3 FP8 checkpoint (MLA, `q_lora_rank > 0`) with `tp > 1`, then trigger a weight reload (re-run `load_weights` after `process_weights_after_loading`, as RL weight-refit flows do). Before this change ranks > 0 raise the `narrow` overflow above; after it the replicated `a`-proj reloads correctly.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Let pooling chunked prefill use full context
author: TommyTranX
body:
## Summary

- Fix a V1 scheduler liveness bug for pooling requests with chunked prefill.
- Pooling runners emit an output from the final prefill hidden state and do not append a sampled token, but the scheduler reserved one context slot for every non-diffusion request.
- When a pooling prompt length equaled `max_model_len`, the first chunk could run, the next running-step schedule would stop one token early, and the request could no longer make progress.
- Reserve zero sampled-token slots for pooling runners so the final prefill chunk can reach `max_model_len` and emit the pooling output.

Fixes #47971, Fixes #24704, Fixes #55427

## Duplicate-work check

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search 'repo:vllm-project/vllm 47971 in:body'` returned no open PRs.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search 'repo:vllm-project/vllm 24704 in:body'` returned no open PRs.
- A root-cause search for pooling + chunked prefill + max_model_len did not find an overlapping open scheduler fix.

## Tests

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_pooling_chunked_prefill_can_finish_at_max_model_len -q`
- [x] `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py`
- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_is_chunked_prefill_supported -q` was attempted locally, but this macOS environment failed unrelated teardown with `Allocator for mps is not a DeviceAllocator`, and one model-inspection case also lacked `compressed_tensors`.

## Model evals

Not run. This is a scheduler liveness fix for pooling request progress and does not change model outputs when the request already finishes.

## Assistance

OpenAI Codex assistance was used to investigate the scheduler liveness issue, implement the fix, and add the regression test. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines and test results.

title: [Bugfix] Fix FlashMLA dense fp8 metadata crash (num_sm_parts clamp)
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Summary

Fixes #47935

## Root cause

FlashMLA's `get_mla_decoding_metadata_dense_fp8` computes

```
int num_sm_parts = sm_count / num_heads_k / cutlass::ceil_div(num_heads_per_head_k, block_size_m);
```

This can be 0 when `ceil_div(num_q_tokens_per_head_k, block_size_m) > sm_count` (with `num_heads_k == 1`). The bf16/fp16 version clamps the minimum to 1: https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/blob/a6ec2ba7bd0a7dff98b3f4d3e6b52b159c48d78b/csrc/api/dense_decode.h#L79

In vLLM, `num_q_tokens_per_head_k = max_query_len * num_q_heads` (`FlashMLAMetadataBuilder._build_decode`), and short prompts (query length ≤ `reorder_batch_threshold == 128`) are routed to the decode pathway. So **DeepSeek-R1 (128 heads) crashes on any 67–128 token prompt** on a 132-SM GPU (H100/H200).

## Fix

**vllm-project/FlashMLA#14** clamps `num_sm_parts` to `>= 1` like the bf16/fp16 version

## Testing

On an H200 (132 SMs), with the patched FlashMLA build:

- Direct `get_mla_decoding_metadata_dense_fp8` call at `num_q_tokens_per_head_k` = 8449 and 16384 (both previously `num_sm_parts → 0`, assert): returns valid metadata, no crash.
- End-to-end vLLM `generate` on a dummy DeepSeek-V3 (128 heads, 1 dense layer, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, FlashMLA): 100- and 128-token prompts complete normally (previously crashed with the assertion above).
- Control (66-token prompt, `num_sm_parts = 1`): unaffected.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, build the repro, and prepare this change.

title: [Bugfix] Use int8 workspace for FlashInfer MLA decode
author: njhill
body:
FlashInfer's CuteDSL MLA-decode tactic requires an int8 workspace_buffer, but vLLM allocated it as uint8. The trtllm-gen path (used for normal inference) views the buffer as uint8, so the mismatch is invisible until the FlashInfer autotuner enumerates the CuteDSL tactic. Model Runner V2's warmup autotunes trtllm_batch_decode_mla, so once V2 became the default runner for MoE models it hit `workspace_buffer must be torch.int8`, crashing every DeepSeek MLA test on Blackwell (#46646). Model Runner V1 never tunes that op, which is why it was unaffected.

int8 is accepted by every tactic (trtllm-gen still views it as uint8), so allocate both the dense and sparse FlashInfer MLA workspaces as int8. Add a regression test that drives the decode under the FlashInfer autotuner with vLLM's workspace buffer.

With help from Claude.

title: [BugFix][Mooncake] Use global data_parallel_index for the DP engine index
author: ivanium
body:
## Purpose

`get_mooncake_dp_engine_index` asserted `data_parallel_rank_local is not None` under external/hybrid DP LB. This crashes on headless wide-TP follower nodes: they go through `run_headless` → `MultiprocExecutor` directly, which never populates `data_parallel_rank_local`.

Preferring `data_parallel_rank_local` was also inconsistent: for a replica launched with `--data-parallel-rank N` (N > 0), head-node processes computed `rank_local = 0` while follower-node workers would compute the global index N, so TP ranks of the same replica disagreed on their DP index.

Fix: use `parallel_config.data_parallel_index` unconditionally. It is populated in every launch path (`ParallelConfig.__post_init__`, `run_engine_core`, Ray actor), is identical on head and follower nodes, and unlike `data_parallel_rank` is not reset to 0 for dense-model DP engines. That reduces the helper to a one-line accessor, so it is inlined at its two call sites (`MooncakeStoreWorker.__init__`, `get_zmq_rpc_path_lookup`) and removed; the lookup IPC path stays unique per node since co-located engines have distinct global indices.

## Duplicate check

No open PR touches this helper (searched `mooncake dp index`, `get_mooncake_dp_engine_index`, `mooncake wide TP`, `data_parallel_rank_local mooncake`; open Mooncake PRs #47317 / #41093 are unrelated).

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) via commit hooks.
- Wide-TP (multi-node TP, headless followers) × DP deployment with MooncakeStoreConnector, which crashed on the assert before this change.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py` (monkeypatch replaced by `data_parallel_index=0` on the fake parallel_config).

## Test Result

Wide-TP DP serving comes up and serves traffic; previously every follower node died at engine init with `AssertionError` in `get_mooncake_dp_engine_index`. No model-output/accuracy impact (side-channel identity only).

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change; the diff was reviewed and the deployment validated by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix eagle3 first-layer qkv_proj prefix for quantized drafts
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Purpose

The EAGLE3 first decoder layer overrides `self.self_attn.qkv_proj` but builds it with `prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "qkv_proj")`, yielding `…layers.0.qkv_proj` instead of the canonical `…layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj`. For a quantized draft, the quant config matches its `exclude_modules` against this prefix — the missing `.self_attn` segment lets the excluded attention get quantized, and the `2 * hidden_size` first-layer qkv weight then fails to load (shape assert in `load_qkv_weight`). This blocks serving any quantized (e.g. NVFP4) EAGLE3 draft. No-op for non-quantized drafts.

```python
-            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "qkv_proj"),
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "self_attn.qkv_proj"),
```

## Test Plan

Tested with MiniMax-M3 + [`Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3); GSM8K accuracy and speculative acceptance rates both unaffected by this change.

For quantized draft model like https://huggingface.co/Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA-NVFP4 verified that it is now loaded correctly according to the quantization config:
```

"quantization_config": {
...
},
"ignore": [
  "embed_tokens",
  "fc",
  "self_attn",
  "lm_head"
],
...
}


```

title: [Bugfix] Fix parallel_tool_calls=null crash in Responses API from_request()
author: mahadrehmann
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #48097.

Sending `"parallel_tool_calls": null` to the Responses API (`/v1/responses`) caused `from_request()` to pass `None` to `ResponsesResponse.parallel_tool_calls` (typed as `bool`, non-optional), raising a Pydantic `ValidationError` during response construction. vLLM's error handling catches this and returns a **400** with a raw Pydantic error message, instead of resolving to the documented default like the request-side field does.

Fix: resolve `None` to the documented default (`True`) in `from_request()`, mirroring the fix applied to the ChatCompletion path in PR #44955.

> **Note:** this is distinct from #44955 — the Responses API never calls `maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls` from `tool_calls_utils.py` (zero hits across `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/`). The crash is in `from_request()` in `responses/protocol.py`, a separate code path.

## Test Plan
```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/tool_use/test_responses_request_validations.py -v
```

Also verified end-to-end against a live server (`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --dtype=half`, T4 GPU via Colab), both before and after the fix, since a reviewer initially couldn't reproduce this via the OpenAI Python SDK (which excludes `None`-valued fields during serialization by default, so the bug only surfaces when `"parallel_tool_calls": null` is explicitly present in the raw request body — e.g. via curl or a client that doesn't drop nulls).

## Test Result
```
21 passed, 21 errors in 4.99s
```
The 21 errors are pre-existing teardown failures from the `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory` fixture trying to clear GPU memory on a CPU-only environment. They are present in all tests in this file before our changes and are unrelated to this PR.

**Before fix (live server, `main`):**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/responses \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "input": "test", "parallel_tool_calls": null}'
```
```
HTTP_STATUS:400
{"error":{"message":"1 validation error for ResponsesResponse\nparallel_tool_calls\n  Input should be a valid boolean [type=bool_type, input_value=None, input_type=NoneType]","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}
```

**After fix (same server, same request):**
```
HTTP_STATUS:200
```
`"parallel_tool_calls":true` present in the response body, request completes normally.

## Related
- #44948 — same class of bug reported for ChatCompletion (closed)
- PR #44955 — fixed ChatCompletion path only, Responses API not covered

title: [Bugfix][KV Offloading] Fix stale transfer_jobs after reset_cache + harden job completion
author: Alex-ai-future
body:
## Purpose

Fix a bug in `reset_cache()` where `transfer_jobs` for active (unfinished) requests was not cleared.

### Bug

`reset_cache()` discards in-flight jobs (`_jobs.clear()`) and sets `_stale_job_threshold` to filter stale worker completions. However, it did not clear `transfer_jobs` for surviving requests. Since stale job_ids are filtered by `_stale_job_threshold` and never reach the completion handler, they can never be removed from `transfer_jobs` through the normal completion path.

This causes permanent request deferral:

1. `transfer_jobs` retains stale job_ids
2. `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` checks `if req_status.transfer_jobs:` → returns `None`
3. Scheduler moves request to `step_skipped_waiting` every step
4. Request is permanently stuck — never scheduled, never completes

### Fix

Add `status.transfer_jobs.clear()` in `reset_cache()` for surviving (active) requests.

## Test Result

- pre-commit hooks pass
- All 87 existing tests in `test_scheduler.py` pass

Part of KV Offloading roadmap (#33689)

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Fix Mamba state pointer overflow
author: Oxygen56
body:
Fixes #48059

## Purpose

XPU USM device pointers can exceed the positive signed int64 range. The Mamba
align-mode fused copy path stores state tensor and block-table `data_ptr()`
values in `torch.int64` metadata buffers before passing them to Triton kernels,
so assigning a high-bit XPU pointer directly can raise:

```text
ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long
```

This preserves the 64-bit pointer pattern by reinterpreting unsigned pointer
values as signed int64 before storing them in the existing metadata buffers. The
Triton kernel ABI stays unchanged.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR currently references #48059 or matches the
`state_base_addrs` / overflow keywords.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix DFlash draft/target layer-count mismatch
author: njhill
body:
The DFlashDraftModel test paired z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16 with Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, but that drafter's dflash_config.target_layer_ids ([1, 9, 17, 25, 33], resolved with +1 to aux layers (2, 10, 18, 26, 34)) require a target with at least 35 layers. Qwen3.5-4B has only 32, so the aux hidden state for layer 34 is never produced: the drafter's `fc` is sized for 5 concatenated aux features but receives 4, giving a cryptic `mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (Nx10240 and 12800x2560)`. Qwen3-4B (36 layers) is the drafter's actual target and works.

This is an incompatible model pairing rather than a runner bug, but it surfaces differently under Model Runner V2: V2 exercises the drafter's `propose()` during memory profiling (profile_run -> _dummy_run), so the mismatch fails fast at engine init. V1 does not profile the drafter, so the init test passed on V1 and the same error would only appear at the first decode step.

- Point the DFlashDraftModel test at its real target (Qwen/Qwen3-4B).
- Raise a clear error in combine_hidden_states when the collected aux feature count does not match the drafter fc, instead of the cryptic matmul failure (helps both V1 and V2).

Written with Claude.

title: [PD][Bugfix] Fix validation of cache shape for attn backends enforcing different `kernel_block_size`
author: NickLucche
body:
I have started looking into heterogeneous attn backend selection here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48012 (an extension of hybrid ssm setup if you want).
This exposed a latent bug in the **validation of cache shapes** that we have in the registration phase.

Say we have 2 attn backends enforcing different block sizes:
- user block_size=128
- FA kernel_block_size=128
- SWA kernel_block_size=64

with the setup above, we compute a `r=_physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block=2` (how many physical blocks per logical ones), register all caches as `[NB*r, PS/r]` and do all the computation into "kernel space" from there on
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1cd75b3dd4b3bf90e4ef81831b6f0dd91fde2fe1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py#L1087-L1107

The issue is that when validating the `num_blocks=NB` that we expect caches to have, if the SWA(64) is registered first, this check 
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1cd75b3dd4b3bf90e4ef81831b6f0dd91fde2fe1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py#L1142-L1144
passes just fine, as cache.shape is already `[NB*r, ..]`. All FA layers are then skipped as the corresponding address of the shared KV tensor is already mapped out.

If instead, for any reason, an FA(128) layer comes first in the registration loop, `cache.shape=[NB, ..]` as the kbs matches the bs the user requested, and`cache.shape[0]==num_blocks==NB*r`  validation fails, despite logic of transfer still working out.

Therefore I am proposing to just skip the validation for such cases, and rely on HMA which by design enforces that **logical/view cache shapes** are either NB*r or NB.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Reset num_accepted_tokens on add_request in all modes
author: njhill
body:
Under P/D disaggregation a decode-role request's prefill runs on the remote producer, so its first local step is a decode. The GDN/Mamba attention metadata reads num_accepted_tokens_gpu[req_index] before postprocess_state updates it, so without a reset the request inherits a stale value from the previous occupant of that batch slot, advancing the SSM state by the wrong number of tokens and corrupting its output.

The reset was previously gated on align (prefix-caching) mode; move it out of that branch so it applies whenever a request is added.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Limit chat top_logprobs in responses

body:
## Purpose

Fixes a Rust frontend chat response parity issue where `top_logprobs` entries were not truncated according to the requested count.

title: [Bugfix] Fix FlashInfer non-causal draft attention (DFlash/DSpark) on Blackwell
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

DFlash/DSpark drafts on Blackwell had near-zero acceptance or crashed with an illegal memory access when the drafter used FlashInfer; Hopper was fine.

Root cause: non-causal attention skips trtllm-gen and runs FlashInfer's prefill wrapper, which is only CUDA-graph-replayable when constructed with `use_cuda_graph=True` and persistent buffers — vLLM does not use that mode for draft attention, so replaying a captured `run()` after `plan()` returns wrong output, then an IMA as sequences grow. On SM100 the FlashInfer builder claimed `UNIFORM_BATCH` graph support based on trtllm-gen, so drafts were FULL-graph captured on this path; SM90's support level already kept them eager. Kernel numerics are fine (FI eager == FA eager, identical accepted tokens).

Fixes:
- Prefer FLASH_ATTN for SM100 non-causal attention (CUDA-graph-safe default).
- FlashInfer `get_cudagraph_support` only claims `UNIFORM_BATCH` for causal attention.
- Draft speculators build attention metadata under the draft's attention config and honor its cudagraph support; DFlash/DSpark fall back to eager draft attention with a warning (the model runner initializes the speculator's cudagraph manager after `set_attn`).

Follow-up: adopt the prefill wrapper's cuda-graph mode for draft attention to restore full graphs for FlashInfer drafts.

## Test Plan

B300 (SM103): `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --spec-method <m> --spec-model <d> --spec-tokens 7 --speculative-config '{"attention_backend": <b>}'`, greedy completions.

Larger draft, GSM8K acceptance (NVFP4 target needs bf16 KV + autotune off): `vllm serve txn545/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-NVFP4 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}' --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'`, then `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 200`.

## Test Result

| Draft | Backend | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.dflash | FLASHINFER | AL 1.11 (IMA on other ckpts) | AL 2.13, eager draft |
| deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7 | FLASHINFER | near-zero AL / IMA | AL 2.62, eager draft |
| RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.dflash | FLASH_ATTN | AL 2.17 | AL 2.17, full graphs |
| deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7 | FLASH_ATTN | AL 2.62 | AL 2.62, full graphs |
