title: [Bugfix][Elastic EP] Reject scale below the minimum data parallel size
author: Etelis
body:
Fixes #30660.

Scaling keeps the per-engine physical expert count fixed, so any target below
`ceil(num_experts * cur_dp / num_physical_experts)` makes `num_redundant_experts`
negative. That request was accepted, then failed on the bare
`assert num_redundant >= 0` in `eplb/policy/default.py`, killing the engine core.

## Test Plan

Qwen3-30B-A3B on 4xH200, launched at DP2:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --data-parallel-backend ray --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-eplb \
  --enable-elastic-ep --api-server-count 1

curl -X POST localhost:8000/scale_elastic_ep -d '{"new_data_parallel_size": 1}'  # below minimum
curl -X POST localhost:8000/scale_elastic_ep -d '{"new_data_parallel_size": 4}'  # legal
```

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/serve/elastic_ep/api_router.py
```

## Test Result

Before: `DP2 -> DP1` was accepted, standby groups were created, the reconfiguration
was committed, and then `AssertionError` in `replicate_experts` took down the
engine core; the server was left unusable.

After: `DP2 -> DP1` is rejected with `Cannot scale to data_parallel_size 1, minimum
is 2`, the server stays alive and keeps serving (`/v1/completions` returns 200),
and `DP2 -> DP4` still returns `{"message":"Scaled to 4 data parallel engines"}`.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Fix OCP MX MoE emulation silently skipping mxfp6 activation QDQ
author: xuebwang
body:
## Purpose

`OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts` overrides the `quant_dtype` property with a scheme→dtype map built in `__init__`. For the four mxfp6-activation schemes that map produced `"mxfp6"` — not a key `moe_kernel_quantize_input` dispatches on, which knows `"mxfp6_e3m2"` and `"mxfp6_e2m3"`. Those schemes therefore fall through to the dispatcher's closing `else: return A, A_scale` and run with **unquantized activations**. Nothing raises; the emulation just quietly stops emulating, and accuracy numbers for these schemes come out optimistic.

Affected schemes:
- `w_mxfp4_a_mxfp6_e3m2`
- `w_mxfp4_a_mxfp6_e2m3`
- `w_mxfp6_e3m2_a_mxfp6_e3m2`
- `w_mxfp6_e2m3_a_mxfp6_e2m3`

### Solution

Map each scheme to the concrete dtype, and extract the mapping into `activation_quant_dtype` so it can be tested without standing up a full `FusedMoEConfig`. The chain also had no arm for `w_mxfp6_e2m3_a_fp8`, which left `_quant_dtype` unset and would raise `AttributeError` from the `quant_dtype` property; it now takes the fp8 path with its siblings, and an unhandled scheme raises `NotImplementedError` instead of falling through.

### End-to-end failure

Two MoE forwards through `FusedMoEModularKernel` with `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts`:
- one for `w_mxfp4_a_mxfp6_e3m2`
- one for the weight-only `w_mxfp4`
same quantized weights, same activations, same routing, only the scheme differs. The first is supposed to fake-quantize
activations and the second is not, so their outputs must differ. 
However, on `main` they are bit-identical:

```
E   AssertionError: w_mxfp4_a_mxfp6_e3m2 MoE output is bit-identical to the weight-only
E   w_mxfp4 scheme (max|diff| = 0.0): the emulation never fake-quantized the activations
E   assert 0.0 > 0.0
FAILED test_a_mxfp6_e3m2_moe_fake_quantizes_activations_end_to_end
1 failed in 7.63s
```

With this PR the QDQ reaches the layer output (E=8, topk=2, hidden=256, intermediate=256, 64 tokens, bf16, MI325X):

```
max|a_mxfp6_e3m2 - w_mxfp4| = 1.875   mean|diff| = 0.2942
|w_mxfp4| max = 26.2500  mean = 3.1170   ->  9.44% mean shift
1 passed in 8.24s
```

That ~9% mean shift in the MoE output is precisely the emulation error these schemes are meant to model, and were not.

## Test Plan

Add a test case `test_emulation_activation_quant_dtype_is_dispatchable` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py`


## Test Result

Passed.

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Prevent negative external block allocation
author: haic0
body:
## Summary

- Clamp external computed-block allocation at zero when a request already holds more blocks than its final computed-token count requires.
- Prevent a negative `get_new_blocks()` request from inflating `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue.num_free_blocks` without removing list entries.
- Add a regression test covering speculative over-allocation followed by a smaller external computed-token count.

## Root cause

`allocate_external_computed_blocks()` passed this value directly to the block pool:

```text
ceil(total_computed_tokens / block_size) - len(request_blocks)
```

After speculative allocation and rejection, `len(request_blocks)` can be larger, making the value negative. `BlockPool.get_new_blocks()` only rejects values larger than the free count, while `popleft_n()` subtracts the negative count and iterates `range(negative)`. The queue counter therefore increases even though no blocks are removed, and a later valid pop can walk beyond the linked-list tail.


## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` — 12 passed
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [ ] Repeat the long-running Kimi-K3 external-KV workload on the source branch
- [ ] Human submitter review of every changed line before marking ready

title: [Bugfix] Support MistralCommonBackend tokenizers in structured output
author: thanhpt1110
body:
## Purpose

Structured output fails for Mistral models whose tokenizer transformers loads as a `MistralCommonBackend`.

Transformers picks that class when `mistral-common` is installed and `TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES` maps the model's `model_type` to it — `mistral`, `ministral`, `ministral3`, `mistral3`, `mixtral`, `pixtral`, `voxtral`, `voxtral_realtime`. vLLM reaches it whenever `resolve_tokenizer_args` does not select `tokenizer_mode="mistral"`.

That class subclasses `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` rather than `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, and the two grammar backends fail on it differently:

**xgrammar — HTTP 500.** `is_mistral_tokenizer()` is `False`, so the working Mistral path is skipped and `xgr.TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface()` raises `ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type`. The backend is built lazily on the first structured-output request, so the server starts fine and plain completions keep working.

**outlines — silently wrong.** No crash: `get_cached_tokenizer` returns a `CachedTokenizer` subclass whose `convert_tokens_to_string` falls back to `"".join(tokens)`. The vocabulary it builds is wrong instead. On `mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407` via `get_tokenizer(tokenizer_mode="hf")`, 409 of 129044 reduced-vocabulary entries map to the wrong token ids, collapsing onto 3 shared ids, so the grammar is compiled over a corrupted vocabulary.

## Fix

`MistralCommonBackend` already carries what the Mistral path needs, and vLLM already has a wrapper that consumes it (`MistralTokenizer.__init__(tokenizer: MistralCommonBackend)`). The wrap happens once in `StructuredOutputManager`, where the tokenizer is acquired, so it covers every backend and keeps a single `MistralTokenizer` instance — the vocabulary caches keyed on the tokenizer object (outlines' `_outlines_vocabulary`, lm-format-enforcer's `lru_cache`) are not discarded.

`backend_xgrammar.py` and `backend_outlines.py` are untouched.

## Test

`tests/v1/structured_output/test_mistral_common_tokenizer.py`, built through `get_tokenizer`:

- the reduced vocabulary is correct after wrapping and mismapped before it
- both backends accept a valid document token by token, and reject an invalid token
- the xgrammar bitmask width matches the vocabulary
- xgrammar still raises `ValueError` without the wrapper
- a non-Mistral tokenizer passes through untouched

9 tests, ~15s.

## Notes

`guidance` already handled `MistralCommonBackend` and is unaffected. It rejects SentencePiece-backed instances with `TypeError: Guidance only supports Tekken tokenizers`, raised by mistral_common's own `from_mistral_tokenizer`; that is unchanged by this PR and reproduces identically without it.

title: [XPU][CI] fix hf runner
author: mayuyuace
body:
**CI failure**: https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/9188/canvas?jid=01a01374-c384-470a-b40c-b58c27dc7ceb&tab=output
**Root cause**: During `hf_runner.__exit__`, the default threshold is 0.100; GPU0 usage was 17.74 GiB (76%), far exceeding the threshold, resulting in a timeout error after 240 seconds.
**Fix**: In `HfRunner.__enter__` within `tests/conftest.py`, the XPU platform has been included in the same memory baseline recording logic used for ROCm; this ensures that `wait_for_memory_to_settle` in `__exit__` employs a dynamic threshold—based on the actual memory level at the time of `__enter__` plus a 5% buffer—rather than a fixed 10% threshold.

title: fix(build): correct preprocessor guard for GDN decode to fix Ampere c…
author: prakharPant
body:
fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp was mistakenly placed inside the VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE block in ops.h. Since KDA is restricted to SM90+, this caused compilation to fail on pre-Hopper architectures (like Ampere SM 8.6) which support GDN but not KDA. This commit moves the declaration to the correct VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE guard.

## Purpose
Building vLLM from source fails on Ampere (SM 8.6) and other pre-Hopper architectures with the following error:
`error: ‘fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp’ was not declared in this scope`

This occurs because `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/ops.h` was mistakenly placed inside the `#ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` preprocessor block. Because KDA requires SM90+ (Hopper) or newer, the `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` flag is not defined on Ampere systems. However, GDN is supported on Ampere (`VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE=1`), so `torch_bindings.cpp` attempts to bind the GDN function, resulting in a compilation failure since the declaration is missing.

## Solution
Separated the declarations. Moved `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` out of the KDA block and placed it under its correct `#ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE` preprocessor guard.

## Test
- Verified that `pip install -e .` successfully compiles and installs on an Ampere (SM 8.6) system without build errors.

---

title: Fix Transformers modelling backend `RMSNormFuser.fuse` performance
author: hmellor
body:
#50128 identified that `RMSNormFuser` was taking an excessively long time at startup tracing every norm module in `fuse` bypassing the caching efficiency in `match`.

This PR determines and caches the attribute to read the `eps` from at in `match` so we no longer need to trace in `fuse`.

Measured on the Transformers-backend fuser path: `Fusers(model, vllm_config)` (per-class matching, cold cache) plus `fuse()` on every matched instance, which is the work `recursive_replace` does.

| Model | Norms | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | 113 | 998 ms | 50 ms | 20.1x |

| `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` | 33 | 261 ms | 45 ms | 5.8x |
| `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | 65 | 548 ms | 83 ms | 6.6x |
| `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` | 65 | 679 ms | 84 ms | 8.1x |

Split by phase, since the two changes pull in opposite directions:

| Model | match (per class) | | RMSNorm `fuse` (per instance) | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| | before | after | before | after |

title: [Bugfix] OffloadingConnector: stop zeroing offload hits under MTP/EAGLE spec decode
author: kamb-code
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52735. In the affected hybrid configuration, enabling MTP/EAGLE trailing-block handling caused `OffloadingConnector` to store KV in the CPU tier but return zero reusable tokens. Root-cause chain and unit-level reproduction: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52735#issuecomment-5328641909

Three defects combined:

1. **All-groups drafter fallback** (`SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec`): with trailing-block dropping enabled and no `is_eagle_group` annotation — the normal state for shared-group MTP models (Qwen3.5/3.8-style: the drafter is a regular `full_attention` decoder layer merged into the target group, see `qwen3_5_mtp.py`) — every group was treated as a drafter group. The fallback is removed: leave the drafter-group set empty and log once. If a genuinely separate drafter group remains unannotated, this can change draft proposals and acceptance; accepted tokens remain target-verified. The B70 report observed no output change and the H200 report produced a byte-identical greedy completion, but no controlled acceptance-rate A/B was run for this hunk. The `use_eagle_block_drop()` capability introduced by #53388 remains honored.
2. **Volatile-tail pop without widening on non-SW groups** (`_lookup_complete_chunks`): the old comment said widening is only needed for sliding-window groups. That's true for the group's own hit, but not for its **siblings**: the un-widened pop shrinks `max_hit_size_tokens` below what was queried, which pushes the confirmed boundary under a coarser group's chunk granularity (e.g. a mamba-align group) and returns 0 for the whole request. Widening now applies to every drafter group; the pop lands on the extra queried chunk and the boundary holds. This matters independently of (1) for genuinely annotated drafter groups.
3. **Permanent trailing-chunk store hole** (`storable_chunks`): the decode-time exclusion could permanently leave the last otherwise-storable complete drafter chunk unpublished. This PR lifts that exclusion once the request is finished. The legacy lookup-side pop remains unchanged. The changed finish tests cover normal EOS completion under synchronous and asynchronous scheduling; abort-specific tail publication is not separately asserted.

## Not a duplicate

#47890 reports, and #47891/#48459 address, a genuinely annotated ephemeral DSpark group vetoing multi-group lookup. #52047 adds spec-driven annotation for the Kimi-K3 DSpark hybrid path; it is not generic coverage for every separate drafter. #41640 proposes broader drafter annotation but does not fix the legacy full-attention pop or finish-store path. #50897 replaces the legacy drop with successor-aware hashes only where that protocol is enabled; legacy `OffloadingConnector` paths still retain the behavior fixed here, and the branches require interaction testing. #53388 makes dropping configurable but preserves the fallback by default. #54637 changes the local/core Mamba fallback, not `OffloadingConnector`. No one of these implements this PR's three-part legacy-offloader fix.

## Related safety dependencies

- #52807 fixes an independent partial-hit boundary assertion that restored loads make easier to reach. Its production hunk applies cleanly on this rebased branch; after resolving one test-import conflict, the combined offloading-connector suite passed (**319 passed, 2 skipped**). It should land first or alongside this PR.
- [#54288](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54288) prevents finish-time offload from treating the terminal sampled token as written KV. It changes the same finish watermark and three expectations this PR extends. Its two commits apply cleanly here; after updating those expectations to the safer contract, the combined suite passed (**318 passed, 2 skipped**). It should land first or be composed and rerun with this PR before merge.

## Test plan

Rebased onto `2a4e3cc3db` and verified on 2026-09-02. At publication, GitHub reports the branch mergeable against `main`; intervening commits do not touch this PR's files.

```bash
../vllm-docs/.venv/bin/python -c 'from vllm.platforms import current_platform; current_platform.support_hybrid_kv_cache = lambda: True; import pytest; raise SystemExit(pytest.main(["tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector", "-q"]))'
```

**318 passed, 2 skipped**. On this CPU-only host, `current_platform.support_hybrid_kv_cache()` was stubbed to `True` because these fixtures explicitly enable HMA and current vLLM rejects that configuration on a non-GPU platform; no GPU kernel path was exercised.
- Eight affected sync/async cases pass. In a detached copy at the same base, reversing only the three production changes makes the same eight cases fail on their intended assertions.
- The `pre-commit` `ruff-check` and `ruff-format` hooks passed on all three changed files, and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- The Mamba round-trip fixture now follows #51358's exact `boundary_state_offloads` handoff; that upstream storage change does not alter the failing lookup behavior.

## Model/serving validation

Independent hardware reports in this thread predate the current rebase and were not run by the submitter: B70 measured 18.9 s → 2.62 s (7.2×) after eviction, GB200 measured 5.43 s → 0.95 s, and H200 measured 15.1 s → 0.6 s after resetting local APC. B70 reported no output change but did not run a controlled acceptance A/B; H200 reported a byte-identical greedy completion; the GB200 report was performance-focused. No GPU kernel path was rerun after rebasing onto `2a4e3cc3db`. Since the rebase, two further independent reports (also not run by the submitter): H100 NVL reproduced the defect on the stock `v0.27.1` image with an MTP-off control (#52735); and a 4× DGX Spark deployment with an NVMe offload tier independently implemented the same correction on a 0.23 base and measured 339→389 of 390 blocks stored per 100K prompt and 335 s→3–8 s reloads across evictions and restarts (#52735).

*AI-assistance disclosure: developed with Claude and rebase-audited with OpenAI Codex. I reviewed and understand every changed line; the local commands above were run in my workspace, and the hardware results are independent reports linked in this thread.*

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Support PCP producers
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Purpose

Support NIXL P/D disaggregation when the producer uses prefill context parallelism (PCP) and decode context parallelism (DCP) is disabled on both sides.

PCP expands the worker world without increasing the KV-cache shard count, so every PCP rank holds an equivalent KV replica. NIXL should publish and wait for one replica instead of treating all PCP workers as distinct KV shards.

This change:

- records each NIXL worker's PCP rank;
- publishes handshake metadata only from PCP rank zero on a producer;
- forwards producer send completions only from PCP rank zero;
- aggregates PCP producer completions over `TP * PP`; and
- rejects PCP consumers, `kv_both`, and combined PCP+DCP configurations.

It does not change the NIXL handshake protocol, worker addressing, transfer topology, KV layout, or token mapping.

## Scope and related work

This PR is intentionally limited to `DCP=1` on both producer and consumer. It does not enable consumer-side PCP or combined PCP+DCP layouts.

PR #50611 owns NIXL DCP support and its shard-routing/configuration changes. This PR is complementary: it only selects a canonical replica along the PCP axis when no DCP sharding exists.

The duplicate-work searches for `NIXL PCP`, `prefill context parallel NIXL`, and `PCP producer KV connector` found #38433, #45340, #49109, #49342, and #50611. None implements this PCP-only NIXL replica selection on current main:

- #50611 handles DCP sharding and currently requires PCP to be disabled.
- #45340 handles CP-scaled scheduler block accounting.
- #49109 is Mooncake-specific.
- #49342 is the older mixed PCP+DCP version of this work and is superseded by this smaller PR.

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \

  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  -k "not abort_timeout_on_prefiller and not register_kv_caches and not reqs_to_send_deadline_rebased_to_worker_clock" \
  -q
# 144 passed, 7 deselected
```

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files <changed files>
# passed
```

Four-GPU P/D validation on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`:

- Producer: `TP=1, PCP=2, DCP=1, EP=2`
- Consumer: `TP=2, PCP=1, DCP=1, EP=2`
- NIXL transport: local UCX TCP/CUDA IPC
- Final-commit smoke: four prompts passed, including a long multi-block transfer
- GSM8K: 1,319 questions, 5-shot, accuracy `0.636846`, invalid rate `0.000758` (159,800 output tokens)

```bash
chg run -g 4 --timeout 45m -- env \
  MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
  GSM8K_QUESTIONS=1319 GSM8K_CONCURRENCY=64 \
  bash ./pd_test.sh pcp2-nodcp-gsm8k \
  '--tensor-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-batched-tokens 2048' \
  '--tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel'
```

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Support simulated routing in monolithic MoE backends
author: roigarnettNvidia
body:
With `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`, monolithic TRT-LLM MoE backends can receive the vLLM-only `Simulated` routing enum (102), which FlashInfer does not implement.

Separate router identity from the routing method used by kernels. Backend selection now uses the model’s routing method, and the shared MoE runner asks the simulation router to generate random logits before monolithic execution. The router also supplies zero correction bias so learned biases do not skew simulated routing.

- Remove `Simulated` from the TRT-LLM FP8, MXINT4, and NVFP4 monolithic allowlists.
- Let each simulation strategy declare whether it supports generating monolithic logits; require a decomposed backend otherwise.
- Preserve ordinary router behavior when simulation is disabled.

Monolithic simulation retains the model’s routing algorithm, including expert grouping and weight calculation. Modular simulation continues to sample expert IDs directly with unit weights, so the two paths do not produce equivalent routing weights or expert combinations.

Added tests cover router contracts, factory selection, bias handling, shared-runner integration, and simulated routing capture with BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 monolithic kernels.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Normalize FlashInfer prefill LSE before merging
author: yimdev
body:
## Purpose

Prefix-cache hits could produce different logits from a cold prefill and
eventually lead to repetitive output. This was initially observed with GLM-5.2
in a disaggregated prefill/decode deployment.

KV cache digests matched before and after transfer, and the issue also
reproduced with BF16 KV cache. A local prefix-cache cold/warm comparison then
reproduced the logits divergence without KV transfer, narrowing the issue to
the cached-context attention path.

A cold prefill computes attention in one operation. On a prefix-cache hit,
vLLM computes attention over the cached context and new suffix separately, then
combines the two partial states with `merge_attn_states`.

FlashInfer prefill kernels, including the TRT-LLM ragged kernel, return base-2
log-sum-exp values. vLLM's CUDA and Triton `merge_attn_states` implementations
use natural `exp` and `log`. Passing base-2 LSE values directly therefore
produces incorrect context/suffix weights.

This PR:

- adds a shared `log2_lse_to_ln` conversion helper;
- converts LSE returned by the FlashInfer MLA prefill backend;
- converts LSE returned by the TRT-LLM ragged MLA prefill backend;
- converts generic FlashInfer DCP prefill LSE after the base-2 cross-rank
  reduction and before the natural-log attention-state merge.

The conversion is performed at the external kernel boundary so the rest of
vLLM continues to use the natural-log LSE contract.

### Duplicate-work check

No open PR currently fixes the MLA prefill paths changed here.

PR #36503 previously experimented with scaling generic FlashInfer prefill LSE
in an older commit (`f10579e`), but that change is not present in its current
diff. Its current scope is persistent buffer management for FlashInfer DCP
decode. This PR fixes the missing conversions on current main and additionally
covers both FlashInfer MLA prefill and TRT-LLM ragged MLA prefill.

PR #47779 concerns SM120 sparse MLA decode DCP and does not modify these
prefill merge paths.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \
  -k 'test_chunked_context_backend_correctness and \
```

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Stop XGrammar token batches at termination
author: sfeng33
body:
## Purpose
Prevent XGrammar from receiving additional tokens after accepting a terminating stop token within the same batch.
Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52767.

This covers two related problems:
1. `accept_tokens()` could return early after rejection without synchronizing LLM's cached `_is_terminated` state.
2. Batched speculative acceptance and validation could continue past a terminating token, producing XGrammar warnings and possible FSM state inconsistencies.

## Test Plan
Unit test:
```
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py
```

Live model test:
```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B     
--tensor-parallel-size 2     
--enable-auto-tool-choice     
--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder     
--reasoning-parser qwen3     
--mm-encoder-tp-mode data     
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}
```
| Scenario | How the bug was triggered | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tokens after termination | Aligned EOS with MTP draft slot 1 or 2, leaving additional draft tokens after EOS | Matcher processed tokens after termination and emitted warnings | 20/20 requests returned HTTP 200 without matcher errors |
| Second advance after termination | Used strict JSON with `ignore_eos=true` to force another grammar advance after EOS | HTTP 500 | 5/5 requests returned HTTP 200 |
| Normal tool calling | Sent strict-tool requests using `tool_choice=auto` and `required` | Baseline behavior | 10/10 requests returned correct tool calls |

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not let a recurrent group's unhashed block truncate the load boundary
author: yifjiang
body:
[`update_state_after_alloc`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L993) scans [the allocated block list](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L1027-L1032) for the first block that is `not is_null and block_hash is None` and treats that index as the start of the freshly allocated region.

This PR also renames that value from `num_locally_computed_gpu_blocks` to **`load_start_gpu_block_idx`**. It is not a count of computed blocks — it is the index in `group_blocks` where the load region begins, used only as a slice bound. The old name is actively misleading: in `test_partial_lookup_returns_exact_boundary_and_group_load_keys` it is `1` while `num_locally_computed_tokens` is `0`. The `_gpu_block_idx` suffix follows the sibling store path (`_build_store_jobs`), which already calls its equivalent `start_gpu_block_idx` and feeds the same `block_indices` field; the `load_` prefix keeps the two unambiguous now that both are visible in one file. The store path is left untouched.

**The assertion that fires is [`scheduler.py#L1034-L1037`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L1034-L1037)**, reached from [`Scheduler.schedule`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1069).

The scan started at **index 0** — inside the region already reported as locally computed, where every block is computed by definition. For a **recurrent (Mamba / GDN) group** that is not merely redundant but wrong. Such a group has no per-token KV at all: it carries a fixed-size state, which is why `get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks()` returns 1 for `MambaSpec` (["Mamba depends on a single state"](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L122)). Most positions in its block table point at the shared null sentinel, and the one real block holding the state is legitimately **not full-and-cached** — non-null, unhashed, sitting below the computed mark.

```
legend   [H] hashed   [·] null placeholder   [U] non-null, UNHASHED   [F] fresh

recurrent group (GDN/Mamba, window = 1 chunk), 21 chunks computed + 1 loaded:

  idx      0    1    2    3    4   ...   20   21
         [H]  [H]  [·]  [U]  [·]  ...   [·]  [F]
                         ^
BEFORE   scan starts at 0, stops here          boundary = 3
         |<-------- claimed computed: 21 ------------>|
         assert 21 <= 3   ✗  AssertionError
         load region would be blocks 3..21  ->  19 wrong destinations, wrong keys

AFTER    scan starts at first_fresh = 21 ------------>^
         boundary = 21,  assert 21 <= 21  ✓
         load region = block 21 only  ->  matches the 1-chunk hit
```

For a full-attention group this is a **no-op**: every token has KV, every block below the boundary is full-and-cached, so the old scan skipped them anyway. The existing assert now holds by construction (`nlcgb >= cdiv(nlct, tpb)` ⟹ `nlct <= nlcgb * tpb`); it is kept as a guard against other causes rather than deleted.

## Reproduction

4-node GB200, Qwen3.5-family hybrid GDN+GQA (4 KV cache groups, 3 recurrent), MTP, TP=4 x DP=4, 200 GiB host tier, `--num-gpu-blocks-override 259`. Under sustained load the leader crashed after **47,142 requests**:

```
  File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 963, in schedule
    self.connector.update_state_after_alloc(
  File ".../kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py", line 832, in update_state_after_alloc
    num_locally_computed_tokens
AssertionError

leader exit=1 | other three exit=137 (gang teardown)
```

The captured 3h22m window on the crashing rank makes the trigger unambiguous. It saw **22 lookups that hit offloaded tokens, but only 4 that were true partial hits** (`num_locally_computed_tokens > 0`) — and all four arrived in the last 36 seconds:

| time | external tokens | locally computed | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00:57 – 04:18 | 18 lookups | **0** | fine — assert reads `0 <= X` |
| 04:18:45 | 4256 | 8512 | ok |
| 04:18:52 | 2128 | 4256 | ok |
| 04:19:07 | 2128 | 10640 | ok |
| 04:19:21 | 4256 | 10640 | **AssertionError, same second** |

**Why this is easy to miss.** It needs `num_external_tokens > 0` **and** `num_locally_computed_tokens > 0`. Tests that flood to full eviction before re-sending produce `num_computed_tokens == 0` — 18 of the 22 lookups above — where the assert reads `0 <= X` and cannot fire. The rank sat clean for 3h21m under exactly that pattern before the first partial hits appeared.

### Reproduced on a build that carries the #49146 clamp

The assert is **not** masked by [#49146](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49146)'s `num_allocated_chunks` clamp (`94ed0bf4e0`, in `main`). A build composed as `#49146 clamp + #52771, without this fix` was put under sustained production traffic and asserted **three times across two independent clusters**, with a fault-free lifetime of roughly **20 minutes / ~850 requests**:

```
vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:963                     schedule
vllm/.../kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py:840    update_state_after_alloc
AssertionError
```

Both tracebacks are this same assertion. The line numbers above come from the deployed vLLM-0.26.0-based image, not from `main` (where it is [L1034-L1037](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L1034-L1037)): within that tree it sits at 832 without the #49146 clamp and at 840 with it, the clamp inserting exactly 8 lines above.

Across four builds under the same workload and config, the correlation is with **this fix**, not the clamp and not #52771:

| build | #49146 clamp | #52771 | this fix | fault-free lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | ✓ | — | — | 22–70 min, 3 asserts |
| B | — | ✓ | — | 10 / 30 / 40 / 88 min, ≥4 asserts |
| C | ✓ | ✓ | — | ~20 min, 3 asserts |
| D | ✓ | — | ✓ | **336 min, zero asserts** |

Every build lacking this fix asserts — including **two** that carry the clamp (A and C); the only build carrying this fix is the only one that holds. Memory was never implicated (no `OOMKilled`; peak well under limit).

A separate note on reproducing it: a synthetic driver that holds the hit *shape* constant does not surface this. On a smaller same-family deployment I drove **12,000 consecutive requests at a 100% true-partial-hit rate** with no assert — but every request had an identical `num_locally_computed_tokens`, so it probed one boundary alignment repeatedly. The production crashes arise under organically varied prefix lengths, which is what walks the boundary across block offsets.

### Why the boundary is exact, and why the null-skip stays

The caller block-aligns the local hit before handing it to the connector ([`scheduler.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L830-L840)), so `num_locally_computed_tokens % tokens_per_block == 0` and `first_fresh_gpu_block` is exact. The existing assert then reduces to `boundary >= first_fresh_gpu_block` — this fix makes it hold by construction rather than detecting the violation after the fact.

The null-skipping loop is **retained and is not redundant.** With `num_locally_computed_tokens == 0` a group's block table can begin with the shared null sentinel, and the load must start at the first real block. [`test_partial_lookup_returns_exact_boundary_and_group_load_keys`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6/tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py) (from #50507) pins this on a Mamba hybrid: replacing the loop with a plain `= first_fresh_gpu_block` makes it emit `[31, 32, 0, 41]` — writing loaded KV into null block `0`, which is shared across every request. Verified by running it both ways.

## Relationship to #52735 / #52771

**This is independent of the drafter-annotation defect, and of the abort fix.** Three arms, all at current `main` (which already carries the [#49146](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49146) `num_allocated_chunks` clamp, commit `94ed0bf4e0`), running the regression test below:

| arm | #49146 clamp | #52771 | this fix | `offloading_connector/` suite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | ✓ (in `main`) | — | — | regression test **fails** |
| B | ✓ | ✓ | — | **1 failed**, 254 passed |
| C | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **255 passed, 0 failed** |

Arms B and C were run back-to-back in a single GPU allocation, toggling only this hunk, so the environment is identical; the one failure in B is this PR's regression test and nothing else. Every test that passes without the fix still passes with it.

Arm B is the decisive one: with #52771 (`44a3045ec1`) cherry-picked on top of `main`, the all-groups drafter fallback removed and no group marked as a drafter — so the volatile-tail pop never runs — the boundary assert still fires. The assert is not gated on `is_eagle_group` anywhere.

#52771 is also **complementary**: by restoring real loads it raises how often `num_external_tokens > 0`, and therefore how often this path is reached. It is the right fix for the annotation defect and should land; this is the crash underneath it.

*(This PR previously also carried a competing fix for #52735 — removing the eagle query-widen, `required_window += 1` and the volatile-tail pop. I have dropped all of it in favour of #52771, which was filed first, targets the root cause rather than the symptom, and additionally fixes a store-side hole mine did not. What remains here is only the boundary fix.)*

## Tests

`test_recurrent_group_unhashed_block_does_not_truncate_load_boundary` plants exactly that block — non-null, unhashed, below the boundary — and asserts the **destination blocks** are correct (`41 not in loaded`, `42 in loaded`), not merely that nothing raised. Verified to **fail against unpatched `main`** and pass with this change.

Full `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` suite green on an aarch64 GB200 node.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Scope DSpark backend inheritance to DeepSeek V4
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

#52288 made an unspecified DSpark draft backend inherit the target's backend.
That fallback is required for DeepSeek V4 because its target and draft layers
share a KV-cache layout, but it is not valid for every DSpark architecture.

For example, a Kimi MLA target can use a Qwen3/SWA DSpark draft. Inheriting
`FLASHINFER_MLA` makes draft initialization fail because that backend does not
support sliding-window attention.

Keep the explicit draft override behavior, but inherit the target backend only
when the normalized DSpark draft has `model_type == "deepseek_v4"`. Other
DSpark drafts leave the backend unset so their own attention kind participates
in normal backend auto-selection.

## Why this is not a duplicate

This is a narrowly scoped follow-up to the regression introduced by #52288.
No open PR matched the backend-inheritance regression. Nearby #48381 addresses
the draft KV-cache dtype and #51042 addresses DSV4 SWA index width; neither
changes draft backend selection.

## Tests

```text
HF_HOME=/data/mgoin PYTHONPATH=/home/mgoin/code/vllm-dspark-backend-scope \
  /home/mgoin/code/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_utils.py -v
# 3 passed

/home/mgoin/code/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_utils.py
# passed

/home/mgoin/code/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual \
  --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_utils.py
# passed
```

The regression test covers DSV4 inheritance, non-DSV4 auto-selection, and an
explicit draft override.

## Model validation

On 4x B300, main reproduced the non-DSV4 failure with a Kimi-K3 MLA target and
the Qwen3/SWA `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark`: the inherited
`FLASHINFER_MLA` backend was rejected because sliding-window attention is not
supported. With the independent-selection behavior restored, the target chose
`FLASHINFER_MLA`, the draft chose `FLASHINFER`, the engine initialized, and a
32-token chat request completed.

No output-accuracy evaluation was run because this changes startup-time backend
routing only. The DSV4 path retains the behavior validated in #52288.

## AI assistance

This PR was produced with AI assistance. It is intentionally a draft; the human
submitter must review every changed line before marking it ready.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Run the serve arg checks for `vllm launch` too
author: vineethsaivs
body:
## Purpose

`vllm launch render` silently skips every one of the pre-load serve argument checks, so an invalid flag combination is accepted at the CLI and only fails (or misbehaves) later.

`vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py` registers subcommands with `dest="subparser"` and then calls `cmds[args.subparser].validate(args)`. `LaunchSubcommand.validate` calls `validate_parsed_serve_args(args)`, and `LaunchSubcommandBase.add_cli_args` builds the component parser with `make_arg_parser`, so `vllm launch render` genuinely accepts the full serve flag set. But the first line of the validator is:

```python
if hasattr(args, "subparser") and args.subparser != "serve":
    return
```

For `vllm launch render` `args.subparser` is `"launch"`, so the function returns before doing anything. Everything it guards is skipped:

- `validate_chat_template(args.chat_template)`
- `--enable-auto-tool-choice` requires `--tool-call-parser`
- `--enable-log-outputs` requires `--enable-log-requests`
- `--enable-per-request-metrics` conflicts with `--disable-log-stats`
- `validate_multi_port_external_lb_args` for `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`

The `hasattr` half of the guard is still needed: `vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py`'s `__main__` block parses with `make_arg_parser` and no subparser at all, and must be validated. Only the `!= "serve"` half is wrong now that `launch` exists.

This changes the CLI contract in the direction the code already intended, catching bad arguments at parse time instead of letting them through. `vllm serve` behaviour is unchanged, and a subcommand that does not build its parser from `make_arg_parser` is still skipped.

## Not a duplicate

No open or merged PR touches `validate_parsed_serve_args`'s subparser guard, and no open issue reports `vllm launch` skipping serve validation. The `launch` subcommand and its `render` component are recent, and the guard predates them, which is how the gap opened.

## Test Plan

Two tests added to `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py`, next to the existing serve-validation tests:

- `test_launch_render_validates_serve_args` builds the parser the way `vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py` and `LaunchSubcommandBase.add_cli_args` do (`dest="subparser"`, nested `launch render` component built from `make_arg_parser`), asserts `args.subparser == "launch"`, and asserts `--enable-auto-tool-choice` with no `--tool-call-parser` raises `TypeError`.
- `test_subcommand_without_serve_args_skips_validation` pins the remaining purpose of the guard: a subcommand that does not carry serve args is still skipped and must not raise.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py -k "launch_render or without_serve_args"
```

## Test Result

I do not have a GPU or a vLLM build in my environment, so the pytest run above is left to CI. What I did run locally:

1. A standalone `argparse` harness that reproduces the exact wiring (root parser with `dest="subparser"`, a `serve` subparser and a nested `launch render` subparser, both built by the same `make_arg_parser` stub) plus the validator's guard and its first check:

```
serve --enable-auto-tool-choice           subparser=serve   before='TypeError: --enable-auto-tool-choice requires --tool-call-parser'  after='TypeError: ...'
launch render --enable-auto-tool-choice   subparser=launch  before='SKIPPED'                                                          after='TypeError: ...'
```

So `launch render` is skipped before the change and validated after, while `serve` is unaffected.

2. `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` on both changed files. `ruff format` reports both already formatted, and `ruff check` reports exactly the same four pre-existing findings before and after the change (`PLR0402`, `RUF010`, `PIE807` in `cli_args.py`, `I001` in `test_cli_args.py`), none on a line this PR touches.

This is a CLI argument-validation change only. It does not touch sampling, kernels, model execution or output, so there are no accuracy or serving benchmark numbers to report.

## Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some bug".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after.
- [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update.

---

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Preserve reasoning adapters for shared parser engines
author: sfeng33
body:
## Purpose
Fix structured-output reasoning configuration being silently disabled when the reasoning and tool parsers use the same parser engine.

`ParserManager.get_parser()` returned the raw shared `ParserEngine`, whose `reasoning_parser` attribute is `None`. The Chat Completions and Responses serving paths interpreted this as reasoning being disabled and skipped forwarding
request-specific parser kwargs such as `enable_thinking=False`.

The structured-output backend could then use the parser's default thinking mode and wait for a reasoning boundary that the model was instructed not to emit, leaving schema generation unconstrained or running until `max_tokens`.

## Test Plan
| Case | STRICT | main (before) | PR (after) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| required, non-stream | 1 | no tool_calls | ✅ get_weather {"city": "San Francisco"} |
| required, stream | 1 | no tool_calls | ✅ get_weather {"city": "San Francisco"} |
| named, non-stream | 1 | no tool_calls | ✅ get_weather {"city": "San Francisco"} |
| named, stream | 1 | no tool_calls | ✅ get_weather {"city": "San Francisco"} |
| required, non-stream | 0 | no tool_calls | ✅ get_weather {"city": "San Francisco"} |
| named, non-stream | 0 | no tool_calls | ✅ get_weather {"city": "San Francisco"} |
| named, stream | 0 | no tool_calls | ✅ get_weather { "city": "San Francisco" } |
| auto, non-stream | 0,1 | content: "" (24 tokens dropped) | ✅ content: "<tool_call>\n{\"name\": \"get_weather\", ...}\n</tool_call>" |
| auto, non-stream, no-think | 0,1 | content: "" | ✅ same content restored |
| auto, non-stream, include_reasoning:false | 0 | content: "" | ✅ same content restored |

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Offload producer partial tails on request finish
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Summary

Offload a producer's final partial Mamba `align` tail when the request finishes before another allocation can trigger copy-on-write.

The core now finalizes the unchanged table source only when the request ends exactly at the registered boundary with no tokens in flight. The handoff is routed through `KVConnectorBase_V1` and `MultiConnector`; Mooncake immediately pins the exact boundary-state block, queues metadata with its store-job ID, and releases the pin after every worker reports completion. The finished request itself does not remain retained.

## Root cause

Partial-tail offloads were emitted only when a later allocation triggered CoW and moved the registered boundary state into a durable private block. A prefill-only producer that finished at that boundary never allocated again, so its final partial Mamba state was dropped and could not be persisted for later prefix hits.

## Impact

Later requests can reuse a producer's final partial hybrid prefix from Mooncake Store even when the producer ends immediately after prefill. Safety checks consume the marker without emitting a handoff if tokens remain in flight or computation advanced past the registered boundary.

## Duplicate-work check

This is not duplicate work:

- #51358 handles exact Mamba boundary states emitted during the CoW path; it does not finalize a producer that finishes before CoW.
- #50409 changes local replay-boundary scheduling and does not implement connector finish-time handoff.
- #52371 adds tests for separate EAGLE/Mamba prefix-cache defects and has no production fix.

No open PR was found for the head branch or for searches covering producer partial-tail finish-time offload.

## Validation

Focused prefix-cache, Mooncake Store scheduler, and MultiConnector suites:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  -q -k "not multi_example_connector_consistency"
```

Result: **103 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected**. On macOS, only the repository global cleanup hook was disabled because the installed PyTorch build raises an unrelated MPS allocator assertion during teardown; all selected test bodies passed.

The four finish-time handoff tests also passed independently. Pre-commit passed on every changed file, including ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, and repository policy hooks.

The deselected MultiConnector test requires a runnable accelerator and model engine, which were unavailable in this environment.

## Model evaluation

Not run. This conflict resolution was validated at the focused unit-test level; serving/model evaluation still requires a Mooncake deployment.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to resolve conflicts, adapt the change to the current per-store-job pinning design, run validation, and prepare this PR. The human submitter must review every changed line and be able to understand and defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][AMD] A GPU-CPU KV transfer fault in OffloadingConnector takes the engine down instead of degrading the cache.
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Purpose

A GPU<->CPU KV transfer fault in `OffloadingConnector` takes the engine down, although the connector
declares itself a best-effort cache (`requires_kv_delivery` is False, `offloading_connector.py:74`:
*"a dropped save is just a future cache miss"*).

On main (f47792af7f):
- `swap_blocks_batch` raises through `STD_TORCH_CHECK` when the batch copy fails
  (`csrc/cache_kernels.cu:229` on ROCm, `:187` on CUDA). A device error latched by earlier work on
  the transfer stream surfaces at `end_event.query()`.
- No caller catches it. The V1 mixin starts async loads and submits deferred stores inside a bare
  `try/finally` (`kv_connector_model_runner_mixin.py:86-90`); the V2 `pre_forward` / `post_forward`
  (`v1/worker/gpu/kv_connector.py:70`, `:131`) and `gpu_model_runner.handle_preemptions` have no
  handler at all.
- The failure channel is dead code: `offloading/worker.py:286-288` asserts `transfer_result.success`,
  and its only producer hardcodes `success=True` (`cpu/gpu_worker.py:715`).

## What this changes

Faults are reported, not raised.

- **Submit fault** (`transfer_async`). The `RuntimeError` is caught, and the error the failed copy
  left pending on the thread is cleared. On ROCm the batch call does not read it, so without the
  clear the next kernel launch raised `hipErrorInvalidValue` and killed the engine anyway (measured
  on MI355X). `end_event` is still recorded on the failing stream and the job is queued as a failed
  transfer, so `wait()` and the next job's stream ordering still fence it. It is reported as failed
  only once that event completes, because copies enqueued before the failing one may still be
  running. Its stream, events and descriptor buffers are not returned to the pools.
- **Poll / wait faults.** `get_finished` reports a `RuntimeError` from `end_event.query()` as
  `TransferResult(success=False)`; `wait()` no longer raises and leaves reporting to the next poll.
  Only `RuntimeError` is downgraded (device faults raise it); anything else still propagates.
- **Failed store.** The worker marks the job failed in `OffloadingWorkerMetadata.failed_jobs` (kept
  across ranks by `aggregate`), and the scheduler calls `complete_store(success=False)`, so the
  chunks are never published as cache, and drops the KV event metadata recorded for them. Serving
  is unaffected: the chunk is simply not cached.
- **Failed load.** Its destination blocks hold undefined KV, so the request is reported through
  `KVConnectorTransferResults.failed_recving`, which the scheduler handles for any number of KV
  cache groups (block-level reports are rejected for more than one group since #56855). The outcome
  follows `kv_load_failure_policy`:
  - `fail` (the default): the request finishes with an error; other requests keep being served.
  - `recompute`: the request is rerun from scratch. It is marked `load_failed`, so its later lookups
    skip the offloaded cache and a persistent fault cannot reload the same chunks forever. Other
    requests still read those chunks, since the CPU copy itself is intact.

Scope: this covers the batch-copy path (ROCm 7.1+, CUDA 12.8+ drivers). The per-copy fallback in
`csrc/cache_kernels.cu:237-247` ignores `cudaMemcpyAsync` return codes and behaves as on main.

## Not a duplicate

- #50984 (merged) and #56855 did this for Mooncake; this PR follows the same `failed_recving` design
  for `OffloadingConnector`.
- #56032 (open) handles disk I/O failures in `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`; no file overlap.
- #42461 (open, dormant) would remove the per-block API; this PR no longer uses it.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ tests/v1/kv_offload/
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py   # real weights
```

Plus an engine-level fault injection (a real `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` failure from a zero-size
descriptor) with `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, for store and load faults, both policies, with
and without a concurrent request.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-fe4df3df` (torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, HIP 7.15), sources
overlaid:

| suite | main f47792af7f | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/` + `tests/v1/kv_offload/` | 2713 passed, 12 failed | 2737 passed, 12 failed |
| `test_offloading_connector.py` (real weights) | 4 passed | 4 passed |

The 12 failures are identical on both sides and environmental (no `ray`, offline HF hub, Mooncake
bootstrap DNS); the +24 are this PR's tests. Each of the 7 fixes was reverted individually and turns
its test red.

Engine-level fault injection (real weights, `kv_load_failure_policy` as noted):

| fault | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| store | engine dies | chunk dropped; later output identical to the no-fault run |
| load, `fail` | engine dies | that request ends with `finish_reason=error`; a concurrent request and later requests are unaffected |
| load, `recompute` | engine dies | request recomputed; output identical, no reload |

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and test this change; I reviewed every changed line.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Complete DeepSeek-V4 FSE test fixture contract
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Complete the test-fixture fix for the DeepSeek-V4 fused-shared-expert regression on `main`.

This builds directly on #52829 by @tdoublep. Their exact commit `038d308c4` is preserved as the first commit in this PR, retaining its original authorship. Buildkite #84493 showed that the original `runner_type` / `is_moe` additions clear the first `SimpleNamespace` contract error, but the test then fails one layer later because its speculative-config mock lacks `method`.

## Change

- Preserve #52829's `runner_type="generate"` and `is_moe=True` model-config fields.
- Add `method="mtp"` to the later speculative-config mock used to construct `DeepSeekV4MTP`.

`"mtp"` mirrors the resolved production `SpeculativeConfig` for this path and satisfies the direct method checks in `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` without weakening the fixture semantics.

## Duplicate-work check

This intentionally supersedes #52829 rather than competing with unrelated work. Kevin requested a replacement after #52829's Buildkite validation reproduced the regression with the next missing fixture field. The original author's commit and credit are preserved here, and the failure/follow-up were documented on #52829 before opening this PR.

Passed locally:

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Reject n > 1 in the `/inference/v1/generate` route
author: qgallouedec
body:
## Purpose

Closes #52843

With `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `/inference/v1/generate` silently ignores `n > 1`: `vllm_text::SamplingParams` has no `n` field, so the key is dropped at deserialization and a single choice is returned. The Rust OpenAI routes already reject `n > 1` explicitly; this makes the raw generate route do the same. Route-local change only (a wrapper capturing `n` + validation mirroring the completions validator); the shared `vllm_text` crate is untouched.

Rust-frontend counterpart of #52399, which fixed the same silent drop in the Python frontend and skips its regression test under the Rust frontend.

## Demo

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/inference/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"token_ids": [1, 2, 3], "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 5, "n": 4}, "stream": false}'
```

Before — HTTP 200, three completions silently missing:

```json
{"request_id":"42a4300a","choices":[{"index":0,"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"length","token_ids":[1805,3263,1085,138472,55057]}], ...}
```

After — HTTP 400:

```json
{"error":{"message":"Only n=1 is supported.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":"n","code":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

## Test Plan / Result

New tests: validator (`rejects_parallel_sampling`, `accepts_explicit_n_one`) and HTTP route level (`raw_generate_rejects_parallel_sampling`). `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib`, fmt and clippy: all pass.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Mistral3: fix image placeholder grid for processor size overrides
author: anmolgupt
body:
## Purpose

`Mistral3MultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_updates` currently computes the image placeholder grid via `PixtralHFEncoderInfo.get_patch_grid_size`, which uses `vision_config.image_size` as the max edge. It ignores `mm_processor_kwargs={"size": {"longest_edge": N}}` and any `preprocessor_config.json` whose `size.longest_edge` differs from `vision_config.image_size`, so the placeholder count no longer matches the `pixel_values` geometry emitted by the HF `PixtralProcessor` and inference fails with:
```
RuntimeError: Expected there to be N prompt placeholders corresponding to
N image items, but instead found M prompt placeholders! ...
```
This PR derives `ncols`/`nrows` directly from `out_mm_kwargs["image"][item_idx]["pixel_values"].data.shape[-2:]` divided by `patch_size * spatial_merge_size` — the effective post-`Mistral3PatchMerger` grid stride. HF's `PixtralImageProcessor.get_resize_output_image_size` rounds resized dims to a multiple of that stride, so the floor divides are exact.
No checkpoint, output-shape, or user-facing API changes.

## Test Plan

```
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/mistral3.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py
pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py
```

## Test Result
- Pre-commit hooks, Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and repository checks: passed.
- `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py`: all cells passed across `mm_processor_kwargs ∈ {{}, {"size":{"longest_edge":1008}}, {"size":{"longest_edge":1288}}}`, image sizes `{(1540,1540), (1536,1187), (2200,1700)}`, `num_imgs ∈ {1, 2}`, and both `kwargs_on_init` modes.
- Standalone reproduction on `mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503`: before the patch, requests with a `longest_edge` override raise the "N prompt placeholders … found M" runtime error; after the patch, every case succeeds and the placeholder count matches the raw HF processor's `pixel_values` geometry.

title: [Bugfix][KVOffload] P2P tier declares REQUEST_LEVEL on the producer leg
author: liranschour
body:
A PD producer whose prefix cache is already warm computes no new blocks, so under BLOCK_LEVEL the tiering manager cascades nothing to the P2P secondary tier. The remote decoder's fetch demand then parks until the 30s load timeout and it recomputes the prompt.

Declare OffloadPolicy.REQUEST_LEVEL for requests carrying a remote_decoder kv_request_id. That makes TieringOffloadingManager cascade blocks already resident in the primary tier (read from primary, so no GPU access) and keeps prefix-hit chunks in the store path when a primary-tier load supplied them. Other requests, including the consumer leg, keep BLOCK_LEVEL.

Creating the store job also lets the peer's first FetchMsg bind the session, so on_request_finished can fast-fail unmatched demand instead of waiting out the timeout.

Fixes #52808

## Purpose

## Test Plan
Five tests were added across two levels. In
`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py`, a new `TestOnNewRequestPolicy`
class pins the policy returned by `on_new_request` for all four request shapes the
P2P tier can see: a `remote_decoder` request with a `kv_request_id` gets
`REQUEST_LEVEL`, while a plain request, the `remote_prefiller` consumer leg, and a
malformed `remote_decoder` without a `kv_request_id` all stay on `BLOCK_LEVEL` —
the latter three are what keep the change scoped to the producer leg. In
`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py`,
`test_fully_warm_request_still_cascades_to_request_level_tiers` covers the bug's
actual shape at the `TieringOffloadingManager` level: a request whose blocks are
*all* already resident in the primary tier asserts `keys_to_store == []` (so no
GPU→primary transfer runs) yet still hands the complete block set to the
request-level tier, and leaves the block-level tier untouched. This fills a real
gap, since the pre-existing cascade test mixed new blocks with existing ones and
so never exercised the nothing-is-new case.

Command: `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py
tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py -q` → 121 passed (5 new).

title: [Bugfix][DP] Synchronize the device on pause completion
author: aoshen02
body:
Addresses the third problem in #51476: `pause_generation()` resolves before the device is idle — and in DP, the pause path is itself what makes the device busy. Companion PR #52957 (independent, no shared commits) removes the DP dummy-batch burst; this PR makes the pause completion contract correct regardless of how much work is in flight. ## Purpose **1. Pause completion is a CPU-side predicate.** The pause future resolves off `has_work()` and the DP consensus is a gloo CPU all-reduce; nothing on the pause path touches a CUDA stream. `sleep()` is safe only because `GPUWorker.sleep` synchronizes before unmapping — bare pause is sleep minus the synchronizing half. RL callers pause, run their own weight-sync kernels/NCCL, then sleep; that work races whatever the engine launched last. Reported from production, surviving today only on the incidental ~0.5s between pause and sleep. **2. The pause path launches unwaited GPU work.** `DPEngineCoreProc._pause_complete` kick-starts `engines_running = True` so every rank reaches the consensus all-reduce in `_has_global_unfinished_reqs` — and the fixed every-32-step cadence then forces **32 dummy forwards per rank per pause call** on an idle engine. The final dummy batch is launched in the consensus iteration itself, is not in `batch_queue`, and is invisible to `has_work()`; one iteration later the future resolves while it can still be executing. `wait_for_requests_to_drain()` cannot compensate: the coordinator only tracks request-driven waves, so during the burst it publishes "not running" and drain returns instantly. Measured (DP=2 + EP, PowerMoE-3b, dummy batch inflated to ~110ms to model a large-MoE step): `pause_generation()` on an **idle** engine takes **3.40s** and returns with the device still busy. ## Change A device barrier at pause completion. `WorkerBase.synchronize_device()` synchronizes through the device-generic `torch.accelerator` API whenever an accelerator is registered — the same barrier `sleep()` relies on — so CUDA, XPU and any other `torch.accelerator` backend get it without an override, and it stays a no-op only where there is genuinely no accelerator (CPU); backends outside `torch.accelerator` must override with their own wait. `EngineCore._finish_pause()`: `collective_rpc("synchronize_device")`, *then* cache reset — synchronizing first also stops `clear_cache=True` from resetting state the last launched batch may still be using. Called from all three completion paths (in-proc, fast path, deferred idle callback). `collective_rpc` waits for **all** workers, which also closes `execute_dummy_batch` waiting only for the output rank. The barrier does not shrink the burst itself: an idle-engine DP pause still runs 32 dummy forwards, it just waits for them honestly. #52957 cuts the burst to a single step with a one-condition cadence change; the two PRs compose but neither depends on the other. The same contract is applied to the mirror transition: `GPUWorker.wake_up` now ends with `torch.accelerator.synchronize()`. `sleep` synchronizes on both sides of the memory transition, `wake_up` on neither — its tail work (buffer restores after level-2 sleep, `post_kv_cache_wake_up`'s re-init kernels) was unwaited, so a caller could start same-device work (e.g. RLHF weight sync right after wake) racing it. Covered by the existing sleep/wake e2e cases in the regression suite below. ## Reproduction (scripts included) Requires 2 GPUs and `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`. Save the three files below into a directory `$W`, then: ```bash # baseline: the bug docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \ -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface -v $W:/patch \ --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /patch/gpurepro.sh instr # with this PR: check out the branch, then git diff main...HEAD -- vllm/ > $W/fix.patch docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \ -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface -v $W:/patch \ --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /patch/gpurepro.sh fixed ``` (If NCCL fails at init on a CUDA-13.1 driver, add `-e NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`.)
gpupatch.py — instrumentation only: inflates the dummy batch to ~110ms to model a large-MoE step, and adds a device_idle() probe RPC ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Usage: gpupatch.py — instruments a vLLM install.""" import sys site = sys.argv[1] def sub(path, old, new): with open(path) as f: src = f.read() if new in src: return assert old in src and src.count(old) == 1, f"pattern not found/unique in {path}" with open(path, "w") as f: f.write(src.replace(old, new)) OLD = """\ def execute_dummy_batch(self) -> None: num_tokens = getattr(self.model_runner, "uniform_decode_query_len", 1) self.model_runner._dummy_run(num_tokens, uniform_decode=True) """ NEW = """\ def execute_dummy_batch(self) -> None: num_tokens = getattr(self.model_runner, "uniform_decode_query_len", 1) self.model_runner._dummy_run(num_tokens, uniform_decode=True) import os as _os _cycles = int(_os.environ.get("REPRO_SLEEP_CYCLES", "0")) if _cycles: # Simulate a large-MoE forward: keep the stream busy after launch. torch.cuda._sleep(_cycles) def device_idle(self) -> bool: return bool(torch.cuda.current_stream().query()) """ sub(f"{site}/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", OLD, NEW) print("instrumented") ```
repro_gpu.py — the scenario: pause / drain / probe ```python import asyncio import time from vllm import SamplingParams from vllm.engine.arg_utils import AsyncEngineArgs from vllm.v1.engine.async_llm import AsyncLLM async def main(): engine = AsyncLLM.from_engine_args( AsyncEngineArgs( model="ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b", data_parallel_size=2, enable_expert_parallel=True, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, max_model_len=512, enforce_eager=True, ) ) async def gen(rid): async for _ in engine.generate( "The capital of France is", SamplingParams(max_tokens=8), rid ): pass async def probe(tag): idle = await engine.collective_rpc("device_idle") print(f"PROBE {tag}: device_idle={idle}", flush=True) return all(idle) await gen("warmup") await asyncio.sleep(6) await probe("settled") # sanity: True when quiet # scenario 1: pause on a quiet engine t0 = time.perf_counter() await engine.pause_generation(mode="abort") t1 = time.perf_counter() await probe("after_pause1_returned") print(f"S1 pause took {t1 - t0:.2f}s on an idle engine", flush=True) await engine.wait_for_requests_to_drain(60) await probe("after_drain1_returned") # scenario 2: second pause+drain right before sleep (the production recipe) t0 = time.perf_counter() await engine.pause_generation(mode="abort") t1 = time.perf_counter() await probe("after_pause2_returned") await engine.wait_for_requests_to_drain(60) await probe("after_drain2_returned") print(f"S2 second pause took {t1 - t0:.2f}s", flush=True) # scenario 3: drain called while the pause burst is mid-flight await engine.resume_generation() await gen("rearm") await asyncio.sleep(6) task = asyncio.create_task(engine.pause_generation(mode="abort")) await asyncio.sleep(0.8) await engine.wait_for_requests_to_drain(60) idle = await probe("drain_during_pause_burst") print(f"S3 drain returned while pause_done={task.done()}, idle={idle}", flush=True) await task engine.shutdown() asyncio.run(main()) ```
gpurepro.sh — container entrypoint ```bash #!/bin/bash # usage: gpurepro.sh instr|fixed set -x SITE=/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages if [ "$1" = "fixed" ]; then (cd "$SITE" && patch -p1 --forward) < /patch/fix.patch || exit 89 fi python3 /patch/gpupatch.py "$SITE" || exit 90 export REPRO_SLEEP_CYCLES=200000000 # ~110ms on H200 export VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=WARNING python3 /patch/repro_gpu.py ```
Output on `0.26.1rc1.dev942` (H200): | probe | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | device idle when engine settled | True | True | | device idle when `pause_generation()` returns | **False** | **True** | | `pause_generation()` wall time on an *idle* engine | 3.40s | 3.40s (burst kept; #52957 cuts it to 0.17s) | | device idle when drain returns | **False** | **True** | | second pause+drain before sleep | 3.40s, busy | 3.40s, idle | | drain mid-pause | "Engines are idle" while `pause_done=False`, device busy | pause already complete, device idle | ## Test Plan Three unit tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py` (no GPU): the pause-ordering contracts — fast path and deferred path run synchronize → cache reset → future resolution, and overlapping pause calls each complete behind their own barrier. Two adversarial DP tests for edges the pause path crosses that had no coverage: `mode="wait"` draining through the DP consensus path, and pausing a *sleeping* engine — whose ranks skip dummy batches yet must still reach consensus, with the barrier running against unmapped memory. Regression: `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py -k "dp_pause or dp_sleep or prefill_schedule"` — includes the anti-#38009 staggered-race and barrier-deadlock guards and the #51481 late-request pair. ```bash python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -k "pause_" -v python -m pytest tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py -k "dp_pause or dp_sleep or prefill_schedule" -v ``` ## Test Result `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`0.26.1rc1.dev942`), A/B on H200s, `before` = unpatched image: | suite | before | after | |---|---|---| | test_engine_core.py unit tests (new) | **3 failed** | **3 passed** | | test_async_llm_dp.py (14 cases incl. the 2 new adversarial) | 14 passed | 14 passed | | GPU probe repro | table above | table above | | offline `LLM` sleep/wake smoke, MPClient and in-proc | — | both pass | ## Essential Elements - Not a duplicate: no open PR gives pause a device barrier (#31741 adds a different, step-bounded pause endpoint and does not synchronize the device). Filed under #51476; #52957 is the independent cadence companion. - Control-plane only; no effect on model output, so no eval run is included. - AI assistance was used (the design was adversarially reviewed with a second model, which also surfaced the non-`torch.accelerator` backend hole fixed in the base implementation). The submitter has reviewed each changed line and the runs above.

title: [Bugfix] Align CPU offload pool size across PP/spec-decode workers
author: charxwu
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix CPU offload block-count mismatches between the scheduler and workers under uneven pipeline parallelism or speculative decoding, preventing out-of-bounds offload copies.

## Claims

- Workers synchronize the block count with MIN before allocating offload storage.
- The engine queries the aligned count only for enabled `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` configurations, including `MultiConnector`, and requires a valid worker result.
- The scheduler uses that count directly. Removed the unused config-based fallback and per-worker config plumbing.

## Validation

After merging main (`f143f65d7c74`) and cherry-picking the Nixl CI fix, Python 3.12 / CPU:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/config/test_config_utils.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py -q
```

- **144 passed, 18 skipped**. The CPU-offload worker module and 17 GPU-dependent embed-sharing cases require CUDA/ROCm and were skipped; this includes the three worker synchronization tests. The failing AMD GPU cases must be validated in CI.
- Six focused regression cases cover RPC gating, MultiConnector and a missing worker result. The missing-result case failed before the assertion was added and now passes.
- `bash -n tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh` and pre-commit checks on all PR files passed, including shellcheck, Ruff and mypy. Inapplicable actionlint was excluded because its Go download failed certificate validation; no workflow files changed.

Previously reported ROCm smoke validation, before these review fixes:

| Configuration | Baseline worker / scheduler blocks | Aligned blocks | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kimi-K3 TP4×PP2 | Workers 50 / 46; scheduler 50 | 46 everywhere | Two-pass generation matched |
| Kimi-K3 TP8×PP2, two-node MI355X | Workers 809 / 746; scheduler 809 | 746 everywhere | Health and completion smoke passed |

These runs used dummy weights and `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5a4c8d99242e9e069b604d0e9b969e77f7dd501d`. GPU/PP smoke tests were not rerun for the current review fixes on this CPU-only host.

## Details

CI dependencies: merged main to include the AMD fixture fix in [#62869](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62869). Also cherry-picked only [`4ca9ef5ded05`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/4ca9ef5ded05b393c6a6978574dba4598a2dd543) from the still-open [#62879](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62879), preserving its author and provenance. Its 11-line test-script change waits for prefillers to be ready before starting decoders that share their GPUs, preventing overlapping memory profiling and weight loading. This addresses a Nixl CI failure also observed on main; GPU validation is pending CI. The dependency is already proposed upstream rather than being a separate new fix PR here.

Heavier PP ranks can store fewer blocks in the same byte budget, while the scheduler previously sized its pool using a lighter rank. The resulting block IDs could exceed a worker's allocation and crash a copy operation.

Workers derive capacity from live KV storage; the startup RPC transfers the aligned result to the scheduler. With offloading enabled, a missing result is an initialization error rather than a reason to estimate capacity again. The explicit `num_cpu_blocks` override remains supported.

This provides automatic alignment rather than requiring per-topology tuning such as InferenceX's `KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_CPU_BLOCKS` workaround. Open PRs were searched for matching SimpleCPUOffload/PP alignment work at initial submission; none matched this automatic fix.

title: [Bugfix] Wait for offload keys before storing chunks
body:
## Summary

- cap storable offload chunks by the number of available offload keys, in addition to computed tokens and allocated KV blocks
- defer a chunk when its request block hash has not arrived yet instead of asserting in `_build_store_jobs`
- add a CPU-only regression that verifies the deferred chunk is stored after the missing hash becomes available

Fixes #52170.

## Why this happens

`_build_store_jobs` can observe allocated KV blocks before `Request.block_hashes` has produced the matching offload key. `storable_chunks` previously used only the token-derived and block-allocation bounds, so the key and block slices could have different lengths. Treating available keys as the third bound preserves `next_stored_chunk_idx`, allowing the chunk to be reconsidered on a later scheduler step.

title: [Bugfix] Reuse CUDA streams in packed weight transfer to cap reserved-memory waste
author: qgallouedec
body:
Fixes #52950

The packed weight transfer creates new `torch.cuda.Stream` objects every time it runs, and allocates its two 1 GiB pack buffers on them. The problem is that the caching allocator keys cached blocks by the stream they were allocated on. So when the buffers are freed, they go to a cache that only the same stream can reuse, and the next call uses different streams. Each sync leaves 2 GiB of reserved memory behind, until the 32-stream pool wraps around and the memory saturates at about 32 GiB per process. In principle the allocator can release this cache under pressure, and it does in isolated tests, but in practice our 4B training runs on 80 GB GPUs (weights synced every step) OOMed reproducibly while carrying this stranded memory, and stopped OOMing with this fix. See #52950 for the full analysis and a small repro of the stranding.

The fix is to just create the streams once and reuse them across calls. The stranded cache then caps at 2 GiB. This is safe because each call already synchronizes a buffer slot before reusing it.

I validated it two ways: the repro from the issue (reserved goes from a 2 -> 16 GB climb to flat at 2 GB), and a real RL run (TRL AsyncGRPOTrainer, sync every step, Qwen3-4B on 2 H100 + a tp2 server), where reserved memory went from +2.09 GB per step to flat, with everything else identical.
