title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] Fix MoRI-IO KV block-offset for speculative decoding (MTP)
author: MohitAMD
body:
## Summary
Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation, the prefill
(producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead blocks that the
decode (consumer) side never allocates. The producer's local block list therefore ends up
**longer** than the consumer's remote list, and the first prefill→decode KV write crashed
with `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` (e.g. 8003 vs 8000 at n=3),
making MTP unusable on MoRI-IO.

## Fix
The surplus is trailing lookahead scratch, not prompt KV, so it must be dropped **before**
the producer saves — not masked at transfer time.

- **Clamp on the WRITE producer save path** (`MoRIIOConnectorScheduler`): a new
  `_clamp_to_prompt_blocks` trims each **full-attention** KV group to its prompt length
  (`ceil(num_prompt_tokens / block_size)`), block-size-agnostic and per-group so it works
  under the hybrid multi-KV-group manager. Sliding-window groups are left untouched.
- **Chunked-prefill final-chunk detection by token progress** (`_is_final_prefill_chunk`):
  the save fires when `num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled >= num_prompt_tokens`, which is
  immune to speculative-lookahead block inflation (a block-count check is not). This also
  correctly handles a final chunk that allocates **no new blocks** (`new_block_ids is None`),
  which previously dropped the save and hung the decode leg.
- **Keep the loud invariant**: `compute_block_transfer_offsets` still raises on a genuinely
  longer-local list — a real bug in READ mode — rather than silently clamping. The relaxation
  lives only in the WRITE save path where the surplus is legitimate.
- **Fail closed on unsupported combos**: MoRI-IO WRITE mode + sliding-window attention (with
  or without spec decode) raises `NotImplementedError`, because the positional prompt-prefix
  save would ship out-of-window null blocks. READ + SWA (+ spec) is unaffected: block ids are
  pre-clipped to computed tokens before the connector sees them.

## Tests
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_connector.py`: WRITE-mode clamp (single- and
  multi-group), chunked-prefill accumulation, the lookahead final-chunk regression (final
  chunk with `new_block_ids=None`), and the WRITE spec+SWA guard (reachable only under a
  uniform SWA model with `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py`: retains the loud longer-local
  `ValueError` guard and the shorter-local READ-mode partial-transfer behavior.

## Validation
GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP **1P1D / 1P2D PD-disagg** (vLLM v0.27.1 + AITER v0.1.19), MTP n=3:
- KV transfer succeeds (clamp fires, e.g. `8003 -> 8000` / `8 -> 5`); no more ValueError.
- Coherent output, **0 token-0 (`!`) corruption**, FULL cudagraph engaged.
- 8k/8k decode-heavy shows the expected MTP TPOT win (1.36–1.45×) at low concurrency.

## Not a duplicate
This is the only open PR addressing MoRI-IO KV block-offset handling under speculative
decoding. It builds on (does not duplicate) the upstream hybrid/multi-KV-group MoRI-IO
refactor: it keeps that connector's structure and guards, and only adds the spec-decode
clamp + lookahead-safe final-chunk detection on top.

## AI assistance
Prepared with AI assistance (Cursor). All changed lines and tests were reviewed, and the
behavior was validated end-to-end by the submitter on GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP PD-disaggregated
serving (1P1D/1P2D).

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py` (ROCm + mori) — 62 passed
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean
- [x] MoRI-IO PD-disagg smoke with `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` on both roles
- [x] Non-spec PD-disagg regression (equal local/remote path unchanged)

title: [BugFix][Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Fix decode instance's multi-layer MTP kv caches during P/D
author: TheEpicDolphin
body: ## Context During multi-module MTP with P/D, the prefill instance runs prefill on the full prompt and the last N MTP layers each generate a draft token. This is problematic on the last prefill chunk, because MTP layer i will embed its draft token into MTP layer i + 1. Those draft tokens are unverified, and remain in the KV cache for those last N-1 MTP layers. See the visualization below: During standalone serving, the next decode step would receive the number of rejections, and would re-prefill those stale cache slots accordingly. During P/D, the decode instance doesn't receive this information, and thus the unverified draft tokens remain in the KV cache, hurting acceptance rates. ## This PR Generalizes the 1-token backoff used by Mamba to skip prefilling the last token on the prefill instance, and recompute that token on the decode instance, for multi-module MTP. Now, the prefill instance no longer pollutes the last N-1 MTP modules with unverified draft tokens, and the decode instance completes prefill for the last N-1 prompt tokens. I created a helper method in `VllmConfig` called `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens` that is used to get the number of MTP modules, and use them for this prefill backoff. It is now called by several other callsites to reduce code duplication. ## Benchmarks Inkling-Small-NVFP4, 1P1D on one 4×GB200 node (prefill GPUs 0,1 / decode GPUs 2,3, TP=2 each), `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":8}`, SPEED-Bench `throughput_16k`/`low_entropy`, 2048 in / 2048 out, concurrency 64, 512 prompts. Acceptance read from the decode instance's `/metrics`. | Metric | Before (`ae71862c51`) | After (`5ee6a77da2`) | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | **acceptance_length** | **1.0891** | **3.5207** | **+2.4316** | | **acceptance_rate** | **1.11%** | **31.51%** | **+30.40** | | Total token throughput | 3,520 tok/s | 12,156 tok/s | +245% | | Mean TPOT | 35.67 ms | 9.99 ms | −72% | | Mean E2EL | 73.6 s | 20.5 s | −72% | | Benchmark wall time | 634.8 s | 204.4 s | −68% | | Position | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Before | .0259 | .0179 | .0132 | .0095 | .0074 | .0060 | .0050 | .0042 | | After | .6745 | .4802 | .3575 | .2806 | .2282 | .1917 | .1644 | .1436 | Both arms completed 512/512 requests with 0 failures on identical input (1,048,576 tokens). Output token counts differ by 2.3%. An acceptance length of 1.089 means ~99% of drafts were rejected. Speculative decoding was effectively inert under P/D before the fix.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Allow TRTLLM FP8 block-scale MoE with SwiGLU clamp
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

`TrtLlmFp8ExpertsBase.is_supported_config` rejects any model that requests a SwiGLU clamp (`swiglu_limit` / `swiglu_alpha` / `swiglu_beta`) unless the weights are MXFP8. That was correct when the guard was added in #54160: FlashInfer's FP8 block-scale MoE raised

```
ValueError: gemm1_alpha, gemm1_beta, and gemm1_clamp_limit are only supported
for Fp8QuantizationType.MxFp8 in FP8 block scale MoE.
```

FlashInfer 0.6.18 — the version pinned in `requirements/cuda.txt` — accepts the DeepSeek-FP8 block-scale kernel as well (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4405, merged 2026-08-11). Its validator now reads:

```python
if Fp8QuantizationType(fp8_quantization_type) not in (
    Fp8QuantizationType.MxFp8,
    Fp8QuantizationType.DeepSeekFp8,
):
    raise ValueError(...)
if int(activation_type) != int(ActivationType.Swiglu):
    raise ValueError(...)
```

So an fp8 block-scaled model with a SwiGLU clamp (DeepSeek-V4 sets `swiglu_limit`) no longer needs to be excluded from `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM`. This PR relaxes the guard to match FlashInfer's current contract exactly:

- allow the clamp for block-scaled weights: MXFP8 **and** DeepSeek-FP8 (`kFp8Static128BlockSym` / `kFp8Dynamic128Sym`);
- keep rejecting the per-tensor kernel, which has no clamp at all;
- **also require a SwiGLU activation**, which FlashInfer requires for both block-scaled kernels. The previous code let MXFP8 + `RELU2_NO_MUL` + clamp through, which 0.6.18 rejects at runtime.

## Test Plan / Test Result

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py::test_trtllm_fp8_swiglu_clamp_support` (new, extended here to cover the activation condition) — 5 cases: MXFP8+SiLU, DeepSeek-FP8+SiLU, DeepSeek-FP8+SwiGLU-OAI accepted; per-tensor+SiLU and DeepSeek-FP8+Relu2 rejected with the corresponding reason. All pass.
- The same five cases were also run against an installed vLLM on a GB200 node with the patched file overlaid, to check the predicate outside the test harness — all five match.
- The premise was verified directly rather than assumed: FlashInfer 0.6.16 raises the error quoted above when `trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe` is called with `gemm1_clamp_limit` and `Fp8QuantizationType.DeepSeekFp8` (reproduced on a GB200), and the v0.6.18 source of `_validate_fp8_block_scale_gemm1_activation_params` accepts it.

This is a backend-eligibility predicate, so it changes which kernel a model may select, not the arithmetic of any kernel. Models that were already eligible are unaffected; models that were excluded now reach the FlashInfer path, whose numerics are FlashInfer's.

Note on version skew: like the guard it replaces, this check assumes the pinned FlashInfer. With an installation older than 0.6.18, an fp8 block-scaled model with a clamp will now reach FlashInfer and get the explicit `ValueError` above instead of falling back. If reviewers prefer, I am happy to add a capability probe in `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py` and gate on it.

## Performance A/B (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base)

A same-node serving A/B confirms that this eligibility change switches the FP8 MoE backend and improves steady-state performance for the affected model:

| Median of 3 measured runs | Baseline | This PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Auto-selected FP8 MoE backend | DeepGEMM | FlashInfer TRT-LLM | expected switch |
| Request throughput | 13.421 req/s | 16.036 req/s | **+19.49%** |
| Output throughput | 1717.861 tok/s | 2052.617 tok/s | **+19.49%** |
| Mean TTFT | 340.679 ms | 334.251 ms | **-1.89%** |
| Mean TPOT | 16.058 ms | 13.073 ms | **-18.59%** |
| P99 TPOT | 17.461 ms | 14.459 ms | **-17.19%** |

Setup:

- one node with 4x GB200, TP=4 and EP=4;
- `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base` with FP8 block-scale experts and `swiglu_limit=10`;
- the same immutable nightly image for both arms: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:a551e05307cd2e0092139d84db32af9c97e67d2eeeff072d21e429131d8c23f0` (source commit `8a728663c1`, created 2026-09-04 05:34 UTC);
- `--moe-backend auto`, `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, `--enable-expert-parallel`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, max model length 8192, max batched tokens 8192, max sequences 64;
- random ISL=512 / OSL=128, concurrency=32, unlimited request rate, temperature=0, ignore EOS;
- an identical 256-request preconditioning pass per arm, followed by 3 measured repetitions of 512 requests with 64 warmups each.

Command shape:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name random \
  --num-prompts 512 --num-warmups 64 \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 32 \
  --temperature 0 --ignore-eos --seed 0
```

All 1,536 measured requests per arm completed successfully with zero failures. Output-throughput spread was at most 0.30% in either arm. JIT monitor warnings occurred only during preconditioning and not during any of the six measured runs. Slurm job 14379 completed with exit code 0.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Skip cleaned-up async lookup batches
author: Alex-ai-future
body:
## Purpose

Skip a secondary-tier async lookup when its last requester finishes before
the scheduler flushes that step's lookup batch.

### User case

1. Request A adds KV key `K` to the current step's async lookup batch.
2. A is cancelled or finishes before `on_schedule_end()` calls `flush()`.
3. Cleanup removes A's lookup state, but previously `flush()` still submitted
   `K` to the background worker.

The fix revalidates each entry against the scheduler-owned lookup state before
queueing it. It drops only missing or superseded generations; a key shared by
another active request remains eligible. It deliberately does not attempt to
cancel batches that are already queued or backend calls already in flight.

No open PR was found for this flush-before-submit cancellation case. This is
complementary to #54872, which protects the result side after a batch has
already been submitted.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
```

title: [Bugfix][Examples] Launch prefill and decode concurrently in NixlPushConnector demo
author: junuxyz
body:
## Purpose

The previous implementation in NixlPushConnector demo fully consumed the prefill response before starting the decode request:

```python
async for _ in self.forward_request(prefill_url, prefill_request, headers):
    continue

generator = self.forward_request(decode_url, decode_request, headers)
return StreamingResponse(generator, media_type="application/json")
```

Since the `async for` loop must finish before execution reaches the decode request, the two upstream requests run sequentially.

This change drains prefill in a background asyncio task and starts the decode stream immediately, allowing both requests to run concurrently.

## Test Plan

Tested with one prefill and one decode vLLM instances on 2 × A100 SXM4 GPUs.
Compared the request timing before and after the patch using the reproduction script below.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

VLLM_SRC="${VLLM_SRC:-/workspace/vllm}"
EXP_DIR="${EXP_DIR:-/workspace/nixl-exp}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B}"
VLLM_BIN="${VLLM_BIN:-$VLLM_SRC/.venv/bin/vllm}"
PYTHON_BIN="${PYTHON_BIN:-$VLLM_SRC/.venv/bin/python}"
PROXY_REL="examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/disagg_proxy_pushconnector_demo.py"

mkdir -p "$EXP_DIR"
git -C "$VLLM_SRC" show "HEAD^:$PROXY_REL" > "$EXP_DIR/proxy.before.py"
git -C "$VLLM_SRC" show "HEAD:$PROXY_REL" > "$EXP_DIR/proxy.after.py"

tee "$EXP_DIR/trace_proxy.py" >/dev/null <<'PY'
import importlib.util
import sys
import time

proxy_file = sys.argv.pop(1)
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("push_proxy", proxy_file)
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(module)

forward_request = module.PushProxy.forward_request
origins = {}


async def traced_forward_request(self, url, data, headers, use_chunked=True):
    role = "prefill" if ":8100" in url else "decode"
    request_id = headers["X-Request-Id"]
    now = time.perf_counter_ns()
    origin = origins.setdefault(request_id, now)

    def trace(event):
        elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter_ns() - origin) / 1_000_000
        print(f"TIMELINE {request_id} {event} +{elapsed_ms:.3f} ms", flush=True)

    trace(f"{role}_start")
    try:
        async for chunk in forward_request(self, url, data, headers, use_chunked):
            yield chunk
    finally:
        if role == "prefill":
            trace("prefill_end")


module.PushProxy.forward_request = traced_forward_request
args = module.parse_args()
module.PushProxyServer(args=args).run_server()
PY

prefill_pid=""
decode_pid=""
proxy_pid=""

cleanup() {
  for pid in "$proxy_pid" "$decode_pid" "$prefill_pid"; do
    if [[ -n "$pid" ]] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      kill "$pid"
      wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  done
  prefill_pid=""
  decode_pid=""
  proxy_pid=""
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

wait_ready() {
  local url="$1"
  for _ in $(seq 1 180); do
    curl -fsS "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    sleep 1
  done
  return 1
}

run_case() {
  local name="$1"
  local proxy_file="$2"
  local case_dir="$EXP_DIR/$name"

  mkdir -p "$case_dir"

  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  UCX_NET_DEVICES=all \

      '{"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","engine_id":"prefill-engine-001"}' \
      > "$case_dir/prefill.log" 2>&1 &
  prefill_pid=$!

  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \
  UCX_NET_DEVICES=all \
  VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG \

    "$VLLM_BIN" serve "$MODEL" \
      --port 8200 \

      '{"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","engine_id":"decode-engine-001"}' \
      > "$case_dir/decode.log" 2>&1 &
  decode_pid=$!

  wait_ready http://127.0.0.1:8100/health
  wait_ready http://127.0.0.1:8200/health

  "$PYTHON_BIN" "$EXP_DIR/trace_proxy.py" "$proxy_file" \
    --model "$MODEL" \
```

title: [Bugfix] Fall back to full decode graphs for noncompiled models
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Apply the fallback only to platform-selected model paths without an active torch-compile boundary.
- Preserve ROCm's compiled MRV1 defaults and the generic compiled implementations used by DeepSeek V3.2 and GLM DSA models.
- Default unset graph modes to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` at O2/O3 and `NONE` at O0/O1 when breakable graphs are unavailable.
- Default DeepSeek V4 MRV2 to `NONE` on gfx950 because full-decode capture has an unresolved accuracy risk in [#52644](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52644).
- Preserve safe explicit graph choices, reject compile/adaptive combinations that can require unavailable piecewise capture, and clear stale capture sizes.
- Causal changes were [#52861](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52861), [#53155](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53155), and [#53183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53183); [#54852](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54852) exposed the combination.
- Draft [#54127](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54127) changes global breakable-graph policy but not this ROCm fallback, while [#52968](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52968), [#53166](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53166), and [#54038](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54038) are workload-specific overrides.

These model paths lack an active torch-compile boundary and normally rely on breakable CUDA graphs for piecewise capture. ROCm disables breakable graphs by default for performance, so O2 otherwise selects an unavailable `PIECEWISE` path. On gfx942 the fallback keeps uniform decode captured through `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, while gfx950 DeepSeek V4 stays eager until its graph-pool correctness issue is resolved. Safe explicit modes remain available, while impossible piecewise and adaptive-verification combinations now fail early or normalize to an executable mode. All 69 focused cases and applicable pre-commit hooks passed, and the broader configuration run passed 289 tests with six skips after deselecting two gated-repository cases. Stacked validation served the full DeepSeek V4 Vision checkpoint on four MI300X GPUs, passed seven semantic probes, and scored `0.942381` across 1,319 GSM8K questions. AI assistance supported investigation, implementation, validation, and PR preparation; the human submitter must review every changed line and confirm the evidence before marking this draft ready.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Bugfix] Multi-stream perf improvements; rocprofiler fixes
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose
This PR does the following:

1. Relocates the ROCR+CLR build to its separate stage, instead of being a prerequisite of the `base` stage. This allows ROCR+CLR updates to not invalidate + force rebuilds of all build stages. Downstream libraries currently only ever link against them dynamically, so this relocation is safe.

2. Brings a backport of changes in https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/11212 to ROCm 7.2.4's ROCR+CLR, which resolves slow cross-stream dependencies in various workloads (primarily observed in multi-stream use cases, e.g. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52033, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51794, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51117) and completes the fix series started in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53712 which only worked on certain stream events.

3. Brings in the aforementioned multi-stream improvements into the ROCm 10.0 image as well.

4. Update ROCR to contain a 7.2.4-specific backport of https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/6942. This resolves the issues previously reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51174 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51173 (also occasionally seen during test teardown in some AMD CI jobs e.g. [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12530/list?jid=01a05ec7-04f4-4c0d-99e5-b5b9a496101c&tab=output#L515)), so those PRs are reverted as part of this change. Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51644.

5. Sets the env var `ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=0` to avoid the hangs mentioned in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54171. While most of them were resolved by said PR, a few remain in some profiling workloads.

## Test Plan
Full AMD CI will run on the image built from this PR.

There are no new regressions.

title: [gRPC] Fix ping tolerance so long non-streaming RPCs are not dropped
author: gongwei-130
body:
## Purpose

Long non-streaming `Generate` RPCs against `vllm serve --grpc` are dropped with `UNAVAILABLE: Too many pings` once the client sends a few keepalive PINGs while the engine is decoding. Two server-side channel args are at fault:

1. **`grpc.http2.min_recv_ping_interval_without_data_ms` is not a gRPC Core key.** The macro `GRPC_ARG_HTTP2_MIN_RECV_PING_INTERVAL_WITHOUT_DATA_MS` expands to `grpc.http2.min_ping_interval_without_data_ms` ([channel_arg_names.h](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/include/grpc/impl/channel_arg_names.h)). gRPC Core ignores unknown keys silently, so the intended 10 s floor was never applied and the 300 s default stayed in force. A client pinging every 30 s (the SMG gateway default) strikes on every PING.
2. **`grpc.http2.max_ping_strikes` was left at the default of 2.** Strikes reset only when the server writes a frame, which never happens while a non-streaming `Generate` is decoding, so every PING in that window that lands under the floor is a strike and a finite budget is spent within a few keepalives or BDP probes. This PR sets `max_ping_strikes` to `0`, which disables the check and is what the SGLang, TokenSpeed and MLX servicers in `smg-grpc-servicer` already do ([smg#1766](https://github.com/smg-project/smg/pull/1766)). The same key typo was fixed in those servicers in [smg#2312](https://github.com/smg-project/smg/pull/2312); vLLM builds its own server, so it needs the same fix here.

With strikes disabled the interval option is inert and only documents intent; the key is still corrected so the value means what it says. `keepalive_permit_without_calls` is kept because without it gRPC Core widens the floor to a fixed two hours on an idle connection (`transport_idle` in `frame_ping.cc`), which would strike a 30 s keepalive between requests.

**Trade-off:** `max_ping_strikes = 0` together with `keepalive_permit_without_calls = True` removes the server's ping-flood backpressure, so a misbehaving client can PING indefinitely and get ACKs without a GOAWAY. The cost of a PING ACK is negligible and the alternative is dropping legitimate long requests, but it is a change in default for every `vllm serve --grpc` deployment and reviewers should weigh it as such.

The change is confined to the existing option list in `grpc_server.py` — 12 lines, most of them comments.

## Test Plan

Behavioural repro in a vLLM image (grpcio 1.83.0): a unary handler that sleeps 8 s, client keepalive every 1 s, upstream option list vs this PR's:

```
upstream (wrong key, 2 strikes): DROPPED -> UNAVAILABLE: Too many pings
                     this PR: OK  -> b'done'
```

An earlier revision added `vllm/entrypoints/grpc_options.py` plus a unit test pinning the key strings. Per review feedback that has been dropped: `vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server` needs the optional `grpc` extra at import time, so a test over the inline list skips in any image without `smg-grpc-servicer` (as `tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_grpc_health.py` does), and where it does run it only asserts literal key strings against themselves.

`pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/grpc_server.py` passes (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` clean).

## Test Result

See above. No model evaluation: this changes HTTP/2 transport settings only, not sampling, scheduling or any output path.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs and issues for `min_ping_interval_without_data_ms`, `max_ping_strikes`, `too many pings`, `grpc keepalive`, `GOAWAY`; none address this.

---

AI assistance (Claude) was used to implement and test this change; the change was reviewed line by line by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Account for PCP in multi-node world size validation
author: DebugSy
body:
## Purpose

`EngineArgs.create_engine_config` recomputes the world size for the `--nnodes` divisibility check, but omits `prefill_context_parallel_size`:

```python
world_size = (
    self.data_parallel_size
    * self.pipeline_parallel_size
    * self.tensor_parallel_size
)
```

`ParallelConfig.world_size` already multiplies in PCP, so this local recomputation disagrees with the authoritative value.

With `TP=1 / PP=1 / PCP=2` across 2 nodes, the check computes `world_size = 1`, and `1 % 2 != 0` aborts the launch before the engine starts:

```
ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: `--nnodes 2` must evenly
divide the total world size (1). Adjust `--nnodes`, `--data-parallel-size`,
`--pipeline-parallel-size`, or `--tensor-parallel-size`.
```

There is no way to work around this from the CLI: raising TP or PP to satisfy the check would change the parallelism layout that was actually requested.

This PR multiplies PCP into both `world_size` and `world_size_within_dp`, and adds `--prefill-context-parallel-size` to the error message since it now contributes to the total.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed PRs for overlapping work:

- #51490 — *Fix DCP max-size check to account for PCP-induced KV duplication*: also a PCP validation fix, but targets the DCP max-size check in the KV cache path, not the `--nnodes` world size computation.
- #33207 — *[WIP] PCP simplification*: draft, no activity on this code path.
- #53743 — *Fix ZeroDivisionError with external LB when DP size exceeds node count*: touches the same `nnodes` block but fixes a DP/external-LB division issue; orthogonal to the missing PCP factor.

No open PR or issue covers the PCP factor missing from the multi-node world size check.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -k multi_node_world_size -v
pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py
```

The new test constructs the failing configuration (`TP=1`, `PCP=2`, `nnodes=2`) and asserts the resulting `parallel_config.world_size == 2`. It monkeypatches `HAS_TRITON` because PCP requires the V2 model runner, which is gated on Triton availability.

To confirm the test actually guards the bug, revert the `arg_utils.py` hunk and re-run — it fails with the exact `world size (1)` error above.

## Test Result

```
$ pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -k multi_node_world_size -v
platform darwin -- Python 3.10.11, pytest-9.1.1, pluggy-1.6.0
configfile: pyproject.toml
tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py::test_multi_node_world_size_includes_pcp PASSED [100%]
================ 1 passed, 97 deselected, 14 warnings in 3.19s =================

$ pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py
======================= 98 passed, 14 warnings in 20.45s =======================
```

Reverting the `arg_utils.py` hunk and re-running the new test reproduces the
reported failure, confirming the test guards the fix:

```
E  ValueError: Invalid data-parallel launch options: `--nnodes 2` must evenly
   divide the total world size (1). Adjust `--nnodes`, `--data-parallel-size`,
   `--pipeline-parallel-size`, or `--tensor-parallel-size`.
```

Lint (`ruff==0.14.0`, matching `.pre-commit-config.yaml`):

```
$ ruff check vllm/engine/arg_utils.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py
All checks passed!
$ ruff format --diff vllm/engine/arg_utils.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py
2 files already formatted
```

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This change only affects launch-time argument validation in `EngineArgs.create_engine_config`. It does not touch model execution, sampling, or KV cache behaviour, and cannot alter model output for any configuration that already starts successfully. Configurations that previously started are unaffected: with `PCP=1` (the default) both expressions are numerically unchanged.

## Real-world validation

The equivalent change was verified on a multi-node prefill/decode-disaggregated deployment whose prefill role runs with `TP=1` and `PCP=2` across 2 nodes. The role fails to start without the fix and comes up cleanly with it.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests listed above locally, and can defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Copy every overlaid KV view in copy_kv_cache_blocks_inplace
author: zhewenl
body:
## Purpose

`copy_kv_cache_blocks_inplace` (the CoW copy for partial prefix-cache hits) skips a KV cache view when another view with the same `data_ptr` has already been copied. That is right for cross-layer KV sharing (identical aliased views) but wrong for hybrid models: the KV cache config puts one layer of each KV cache group on the same tensor, so a Mamba state view and an attention view share a base address while spanning different bytes per block, and whichever view comes first in layer order decides how many bytes of a block get copied.

For Kimi-K3 (3 KDA groups + 1 MLA group, block_size 5760, kernel page 64) the KDA view `(num_blocks, 1, 1, 814080)` int8 comes first, so the MLA view `(num_blocks*90, 1, 64, 576)` bf16 of the same tensor is skipped and an MLA block copy moves only 814080 of its 6635520 bytes, i.e. the first 706 of 5760 token slots. The whole-storage fast path would hide this, but it is not taken when several tensors live in one allocation.

Observed effect (het-TP PD, TP8 prefill -> TP1 decode, `--prefix-match-unit 128`, GSM8K 5-shot): every prompt's prefill stops at its last 128-token boundary `B` (Mamba align mode caches the state there); on the small-KV prefill engine the request is then preempted and resumes with a local partial prefix-cache hit on its own boundary entry, which redirects every group's block through this CoW copy (any new request with a partial hit takes the same path). The block the request continues in and ships to decode reads `slots [0,707) valid | [707,B) zero | [B,N-1) valid`. Accuracy dropped to 0.72 with a 128-token sawtooth (about 0.2 right after a boundary, 0.95 late in a chunk), only for `B >= 768`, deterministic per prompt and independent of the KDA kernel. Decode-local prefill on TP1 was unaffected because its per-block Mamba state is 8x larger (5653 slots), which is why the problem only showed up with a high-TP prefill engine.

## Fix

Key the dedup on `(device, data_ptr, shape, stride, element_size)`, so only identical aliased views are skipped and every overlaid geometry is copied. Overlaid views copy the same source block, so the extra narrow copy is redundant but harmless.

### Why the deduplication key includes view geometry

The key answers: "Has this view's block copy already been performed?" The same starting address does not imply the same copy coverage.

Consider the layout used by the regression test: four scheduler blocks per tensor region, 64 bytes per block, and two 256-byte tensor regions in one 512-byte storage. Within each region, a narrow Mamba view and a wider attention view start at the same address:

```text
One scheduler block:
byte offset     0              24                         64
                |--------------|--------------------------|
Mamba view      |  state data  |
Attention view  |              full KV data               |
```

The two views have these properties:

| Property | Mamba view | Attention view |
|---|---|---|
| Device | CPU | CPU |
| Starting address | A | A |
| Shape | (4, 1, 1, 24) | (8, 1, 8, 2) |
| Stride, in elements | (64, 1, 1, 1) | (16, 16, 2, 1) |
| Element size | 1 byte (int8) | 2 bytes (int16) |
| Bytes covered per scheduler block | 24 | 64 |

The attention view splits each scheduler block into two kernel pages: each page contains `1 * 8 * 2 = 16` int16 elements, so the two pages cover `2 * 16 * 2 = 64` bytes.

When copying block 0 to block 2, with the Mamba view visited first:

1. **Before the fix:** both views have the key `(device, A)`. The Mamba view copies the first 24 bytes and records the key. The attention view is then skipped, leaving the remaining 40 destination bytes unchanged.
2. **After the fix:** the views have different geometry keys. The Mamba view copies the first 24 bytes, and the attention view subsequently copies all 64 bytes. The overlapping 24 bytes are copied from the same source block to the same destination block, so the extra copy is redundant but harmless.

This example deliberately uses two tensor regions in one storage. The whole-storage fast path requires `storage.nbytes() == num_blocks * scheduler_block_stride`; here that is `512 == 4 * 64`, which is false. The fallback copies the current view's logical elements, so the narrow view cannot cover the full attention block. With a single 256-byte region, the whole-storage fast path would copy the full block and hide the bug.

The new key describes both the starting location and the layout:

```python
key = (
    cache.device,
    cache.data_ptr(),
    tuple(cache.shape),
    tuple(cache.stride()),
    cache.element_size(),
)
```

- `device` and `data_ptr()` identify where the view starts.
- `shape` describes its logical extent.
- `stride()` describes where its elements lie. For example, two views starting at `a` with shape `(3,)` can select `[a, b, c]` with stride 1 or `[a, c, e]` with stride 2.
- `element_size()` converts element-based strides to byte distances: stride 2 means 2 bytes for int8 but 4 bytes for int16.

Matching these fields lets identical aliased views retain the existing deduplication optimization without skipping overlaid views that cover different bytes.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_copy_kv_cache_blocks_overlaid_views_copy_whole_block`: two tensors in one storage, each with a narrow Mamba view listed before a wide attention view at the same address. Fails before the fix (only the first 24 of 64 bytes of the block are copied), passes after.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`: 16 passed.
- E2E: Kimi-K3 het-TP PD (TP8 prefill, TP1/DP16 decode, NIXL + Mooncake Store), GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 prompts:

  | | before fix | with fix |
  |---|---|---|
  | exact_match (strict) | 0.7218 / 0.7286 (two runs) | **0.9682** |
  | decode-side MLA page scans with interior all-zero pages | 344 of 347 requests with B >= 768 | 0 of 31656 scans |

  (Second pass of the same run pending; decode-only baseline for this model is ~0.964.)

## Notes

- No open PR touches `copy_kv_cache_blocks_inplace` (searched `copy_kv_cache_blocks_inplace`, `kv_cache_block_copies`, `CoW block copy hybrid`).
- AI-assisted (Claude Code); the analysis, fix and test were reviewed line by line and the tests above were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][PD] Pad resumed speculative decode requests
author: ZeldaHuang
body:
## Purpose

Keep resumed speculative-decode requests on the uniform verifier shape when a data-parallel rank has no already-running requests.

In P/D serving, a synchronous KV connector can resolve a waiting consumer to all but the final prompt token. During that scheduling pass, the matched prefix exists in the local `num_computed_tokens` variable, while `request.num_computed_tokens` is updated only after admission. The current padding condition also requires local `scheduled_running_reqs`, so this rank schedules one token even when peer ranks run the `1 + num_spec_tokens` verifier shape. A single `qlen=1` rank then prevents the DP group from using the full decode CUDA graph.

This change treats a request with resolved computed tokens as resumed and applies the existing reject-only `-1` padding, provided no prefill was scheduled. Ordinary prefills and diffusion speculative decoding retain their current behavior.

The regression test uses a synchronous mock KV connector with 32 matched tokens and does not manually mutate request state.

## Why this is not duplicate work

I searched open PRs for speculative-decode padding, resumed KV-connector requests, P/D CUDA graphs, and the relevant scheduler condition. No open PR changes admission for a synchronously resumed request on a rank without running work.

- #54102 addresses Mamba alignment, rejection sentinels, adaptive verification, and verifier graph topology; it retains the `scheduled_running_reqs` requirement.
- #53812 prevents resumed padding from exceeding `max_model_len`.
- #54028 prevents padding from conflicting with the long-prefill threshold.
- #50518 separates reject-only padding from acceptance metrics.

## Tests

Full scheduler test file, using an offline model redirect and a local pytest shim selecting `CpuPlatform` on the CPU-only test host:

```bash
uv run --python .venv/bin/python --no-project python -m pytest -q \
  -p cpu_platform_plugin tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
```

```text
158 passed, 175 warnings in 43.74s
```

Changed-file repository hooks:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
```

All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff check/format, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, and configuration validation. `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` also passed.

## Serving validation

The equivalent scheduler-only change was validated on four 4xGB300 nodes (DEP16/EP16). Set the model paths and host names for the target cluster before running the commands below.

Run the same server command on all four nodes, with a shared `MASTER_ADDR`. Each process owns four local DP ranks:

```bash
export MODEL=<path-to-Kimi-K3-model>
export DRAFT_MODEL=<path-to-K3-EAGLE3-draft-model>
export MASTER_ADDR=<first-node-hostname>
export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER_MLA
```

title: [Spec Decode] Fix Qwen3 DSpark d2t requirement for padded-vocab drafts
author: orestis-z
body:
## Purpose

`Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` flags *any* draft whose vocab size differs from the target as reduced-vocabulary, requiring an `lm_head` + `d2t` mapping:

```python
uses_reduced_vocab = self.config.draft_vocab_size != self.target_vocab_size
```

But a draft can be **larger** than the target's *logical* `vocab_size` when padded to its *physical* embedding size — e.g. `Inkling-Small-NVFP4`: `get_vocab_size()` = 200058, but `embed`/`unembed` are `[201024, 4096]` and the draft's `draft_vocab_size` = 201024. Such a draft covers the full vocab and maps **identically**, yet loading fails with `Reduced-vocabulary Qwen3 DSpark checkpoints must include a d2t mapping`.

Only a genuinely *pruned* draft (`draft < target`) needs `d2t` to scatter ids up. This gates the reduced-vocab path on `<` instead of `!=`:
- **Pruned** (`draft < target`): unchanged — requires `lm_head` + `d2t`.
- **Equal/padded** (`draft >= target`): `draft_id_to_target_id = None`, identity map, no `d2t`. Ids stay within the target's physical embedding (no OOB).

## Test Plan

- `ruff` + `py_compile` pass.
- Validated end-to-end serving an Inkling DSpark drafter (draft 201024 / target 200058): loads without the false error and decodes coherently. The identity path is equivalent to the previously-required all-zeros `d2t` (`draft_ids + 0`).
- Pruned drafts (`draft < target`) keep the `d2t` requirement, unaffected.

cc @Zhou248 (added the check in #52560)

title: [Bugfix][V1] Honor enable_jit_warmup for V2 kernel warmup
author: jiakangkangfuzhe
body:
## Purpose

Honor `kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup` for the V2 scheduler-level kernel warmup.

Currently, `Worker.compile_or_warm_up_model()` calls `warmup_kernels()` unconditionally when the V2 model runner is enabled. As a result, setting `enable_jit_warmup=False` does not actually skip this JIT warmup path.

This PR gates the V2 `warmup_kernels()` call on the existing `enable_jit_warmup` configuration flag while preserving the current behavior when the flag is enabled.

This addresses the `enable_jit_warmup=False` behavior reported in #54866.

On an A100 40GB reproduction with a locally cached tiny Llama model, disabling JIT warmup reduced cold engine startup from:

* Before: 125.865 s
* After: 36.089 s
* Reduction: 71.3%

As expected for lazy JIT, the first request became slower because compilation moved to first use:

* First request: 68.1 ms -> 605.0 ms
* Second request: 49.7 ms -> 47.7 ms

Greedy output token IDs were identical before and after the change.

## Test Plan

Added a focused regression test for the V2 worker initialization path:

* `enable_jit_warmup=False` -> `warmup_kernels()` is not called
* `enable_jit_warmup=True` -> `warmup_kernels()` is called exactly once

Also ran the complete nearest worker test file and an A100 runtime smoke test with V2 enabled.

Commands:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -q
git diff --check
```

## Test Result

```text
10 passed
```

Pre-commit checks for the modified files passed.

Runtime smoke test on NVIDIA A100 40GB:

* V2 engine initialized successfully with `enable_jit_warmup=False`
* Two consecutive greedy generations completed successfully
* Output token IDs were identical
* First request: 76.875 ms
* Second request: 45.129 ms

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fall back for high-rank MoE LoRA
author: xiaoyu-xyz
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55158.

`LoRAConfig` accepts `max_lora_rank` values above 128, but the non-fully-sharded
MoE LoRA dispatch unconditionally selected the one-shot Triton kernel, whose
rank dimension is limited to 128. This caused engine initialization to fail
during CUDA graph warm-up even when the loaded adapter's actual rank was only
4, because the MoE LoRA buffers are padded to the configured maximum rank.

This change:

- keeps ranks up to 128 on the existing one-shot fast path;
- routes larger ranks to the existing two-kernel shrink/expand path;
- lets that fallback preserve the existing `add_inputs=False` contract used by
  dual-stream and other MoE LoRA callers; and
- retains the one-shot assertion as a defensive kernel-local guard.

Rank tiling could extend the one-shot kernel in the future, but the existing
fallback is a smaller correctness-first fix and avoids changing the kernel's
register-pressure/performance characteristics.

## Duplicate check

No exact open issue or fix PR was found after searching for the assertion text,
function name, `max_lora_rank=256`, and MoE LoRA rank fallback. PR #42290's
review did identify both the missing rank fallback and the dual-stream risk,
but those comments were not addressed before merge and current main still has
the mismatch. Related issues and PRs are listed in #55158.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx --from ruff==0.15.12 ruff format --check \
  vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py

uvx --from ruff==0.15.12 ruff check \
  vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py

uv run --no-sync pytest -q \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py \
  -k large_rank_fallback
```

The targeted numerical test compares the Triton result with a PyTorch
reference across:

- rank 128 (one-shot boundary) and 256 (fallback);
- `add_inputs=True` and `False`; and
- one and two LoRA slices, covering both TMA descriptor layouts on supported
  GPUs.

An end-to-end check starts the public Nemotron MoE model from #55158 with
`--max-lora-rank 256` and verifies that CUDA graph warm-up completes and a LoRA
request returns HTTP 200.

## Test Result

- Ruff format: passed.
- Ruff lint: passed.
- Python syntax and custom-op real/fake signature checks: passed.
- Targeted numerical test on an NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB: passed
  (`8 passed, 417 deselected`). This covers rank 128/256,
  `add_inputs=True/False`, and one/two LoRA slices.
- End-to-end test on 2x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB with TP=2: passed. At commit
  `29a6af589`, the public Nemotron MoE model and rank-4 dummy adapter started
  with `--max-lora-rank 256`; both PIECEWISE and FULL CUDA graph capture
  completed, `/health` returned HTTP 200, and a request to the `dummy` LoRA
  model returned HTTP 200.

GPU test environment: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA runtime 13.0, compute
capability 8.0.

OpenAI Codex assisted with code-path analysis, drafting the patch and tests,
and duplicate-work research. The human submitter reviewed every changed line,
validated the design, and verified the reported GPU test results.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve Mamba state for padded prompt tails
author: natsala13
body:
## Purpose

Fix recurrent-state corruption in hybrid Mamba models when speculative decoding pads the last prompt token to a uniform `K + 1` query length.

This is most visible in prefill/decode-disaggregated serving:

1. The prefill node transfers the Mamba recurrent state after prompt token `N - 1`.
2. The decode node must process the final prompt token `N` to produce `h(N)`.
3. If another speculative request is already running, the scheduler pads this one-token prompt tail with `K` placeholder positions so every row has query length `K + 1` and can use the same FULL CUDA graph.
4. The Mamba backend currently classifies that row as a prefill. Prefill persists only the state after the final query position, so it saves `h(N + K placeholders)` instead of `h(N)`.
5. The scheduler discards the placeholders from token accounting, but the prefill state path cannot roll the recurrent state back. The next real target token therefore reads a corrupted convolution/SSM state.

The requests do not need to share a prefix. They only need to enter the same scheduler step. Both may have MTP enabled: one request is already in steady-state speculative decode, while the newly resumed request still has one real prompt token left.

The trigger is:

- a hybrid Mamba model;
- speculative decoding with `K > 0`;
- a request with prior recurrent state and exactly one prompt token remaining; and
- another running speculative request, which activates uniform `K + 1` padding.

Disaggregated serving makes this common because the NIXL Mamba handoff deliberately transfers `h(N - 1)` and leaves token `N` for the decode node. The same state can also arise after a local prefix-cache hit, preemption/replay, or another short prompt extension, so the fix is not NIXL-specific.

## Fix

Pass the scheduler's draft-count tag into Mamba metadata construction. When a row is:

- tagged as speculative padding,
- shaped as one real token plus `K` placeholders, and
- extending an existing recurrent state,

route it through Mamba's existing speculative-decode state layout even though the real token is still part of the prompt.

That layout is already transactional: it keeps `h(N)` in the running state slot and writes later speculative states to scratch slots. Normal acceptance/rollback therefore discards the placeholder states and retains exactly `h(N)`. Genuine multi-token prefills and first prompt chunks remain on the prefill path.

This preserves the original performance optimization: the scheduler still emits a uniform `K + 1` row, so the FULL CUDA-graph batch shape is unchanged. The change only selects the state-management path that can safely roll back speculative positions.

## Reproduction

Deploy a hybrid Mamba model with prefill/decode disaggregation and NIXL KV/state transfer. Use separate prefill and decode workers, and enable MTP with five speculative tokens on **both** roles so their cache layouts remain compatible. Our reproducing deployment used two TP4 prefill workers and two TP4 decode workers, but the essential condition is that a decode worker handles more than one request concurrently.

Run SWE-bench Verified against the P/D router with enough concurrency for a newly transferred request to join a scheduler step that already contains a speculative decode request. The transferred request arrives with recurrent state through prompt token `N - 1`; the decode worker must process token `N`. Stock vLLM pads that one-token prompt tail with five placeholders to match the existing six-position speculative row.

On an affected vLLM 0.28 deployment, the padded row is sent through the Mamba prefill state path. The next decoding iteration then reads state after the placeholders instead of state after token `N`. In the full 500-instance, three-repeat SWE run, this appears as invalid byte-piece output, Unicode replacement characters, leaked literal tool-call XML, missing structured tool calls, and a large resolved-accuracy drop with MTP5. A matched MTP-off run using the same checkpoint, serving topology, sampling settings, and benchmark provides the control.

Apply this PR and repeat the same MTP5 workload without changing the checkpoint or serving parameters. The padded batch shape remains unchanged, but the prompt-tail row uses transactional speculative state handling; the corrupted-output phenotype disappears and SWE accuracy returns to the matched MTP-off level.

## Why this is not duplicate work

No open PR found in the required duplicate-work search routes scheduler-tagged, padded prompt-tail rows through Mamba's transactional speculative state path.

- #55126 changes the scheduler so a resumed speculative request can retain the uniform verifier shape even when its data-parallel rank has no already-running request. It does not change Mamba state handling. The changes are complementary: #55126 can broaden where prompt-tail padding occurs, while this PR makes that padding state-safe for hybrid Mamba models.
- #51483 distinguishes stateless first-token KDA chunks from stateful one-token updates. This PR instead handles a row that already owns recurrent state and contains one real prompt token plus `K` scheduler placeholders, in the shared Mamba metadata path.
- #53945 addresses EAGLE/MTP prefix-cache checkpoint placement in Mamba `align` mode. It does not address placeholder positions being persisted through the prefill state path.

## Validation commands and results

The rebased source-only branch passes the following checks:

```bash
UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-pr-uv-cache uv run --no-project python -m py_compile \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mamba_attn.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mamba2_attn.py
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
```

A focused metadata regression in the deployment image passed all three cases: a stateful padded prompt tail becomes a speculative-decode row; an ordinary six-token prefill remains a prefill; and a stateless first prompt chunk remains a prefill.

An exact-image CUDA state probe compared three lanes from identical initial recurrent state. The padded speculative-decode lane retained the same accepted state and next-token result as the single-token decode lane. The unpatched padded-prefill lane persisted the placeholder-advanced convolution and SSM states and diverged on the next real token.

The bounded P/D MTP5 reproducer changed from 7/8 corrupted responses before the fix to 0/8 after it while retaining the uniform `K + 1` batch shape. The full SWE-bench Verified qualification is reported below.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with root-cause analysis, implementation, validation harnesses, experiment analysis, and PR preparation. I reviewed and understand every changed line and am responsible for the contribution and the results reported here.

## Test Result

`mean/resolved` over all 1,500 SWE trajectories:

| Cohort | vLLM state handling | MTP | Resolved | Accuracy |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Original regression | Before fix | off | 580 / 1,500 | 38.67% |
| Original regression | Before fix | 5 | 57 / 1,500 | 3.80% |
| Post-fix qualification | Fixed image | off | 573 / 1,500 | 38.20% |
| Post-fix qualification | Fixed image | 5 | 576 / 1,500 | 38.40% |

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Reject prompt-wide truncation for Jina ranking
author: bvolpato
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reject prompt-wide truncation for Jina ranking and remove nested reserved markers from user text before formatting the query and documents.

## Claims

- Reject `truncate_prompt_tokens` through Jina's offline and HTTP entry points before inference, including limits that would leave the prompt unchanged.
- Preserve `max_tokens_per_query` and `max_tokens_per_doc` for scoring.
- Prevent nested reserved markers in queries, documents, or instructions from changing ranking cardinality.

## Validation

The focused pooling suites and scoped pre-commit hooks pass. The committed offline and HTTP model-test helpers fail against the previous head `df2cf312cf` and pass with this change. Existing score and embedding reference comparisons still pass.

Run the related suites in a configured development environment:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/language/pooling
```

Before the change, the offline truncation regression reports `Failed: DID NOT RAISE VLLMValidationError`, and nested marker text fails the clean-input comparison. The fixed checks cover `LLM.encode`, `LLM.score`, `/pooling`, `/score`, and `/rerank`, including HTTP 400 with `param="truncate_prompt_tokens"`. Separate query/document limits match client-truncated inputs.

The GPU smoke used jina-reranker-v3 with BF16, MRV2, eager execution, context 1024, and an RTX 5070 Ti. It reused precompiled native extensions and a Humming overlay, with FlashInfer autotuning disabled. Local Torch is 2.13 rather than the branch's 2.14 pin. The model regressions are selected by optional nightly Extended Pooling. Full model evaluation and upstream GPU CI remain unrun.

## Details

Jina formats the query and documents into one prompt. Truncating that combined prompt cannot express separate query and document limits and can remove ranking markers. Reject the option in the shared Jina processor; scoring callers can use the per-query/document limits, and token-embedding callers can truncate each input on the client. The restriction is local to Jina.

Sanitization runs until no reserved marker remains because removing an inner marker can expose another marker around it. The model documentation now describes the truncation restriction and supported alternatives.

No competing Jina truncation fix was found. #61363 and #61524 concern generic renderer behavior; #55359 concerns Sentence Transformers configuration.

AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix per-video cache option reuse
author: bvolpato
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve each Qwen3-VL video's effective sampling options across repeated items and partial multimodal-cache hits. Reject option lists that are too short before indexing them.

## Claims

- Each video's selected `fps` and `num_frames` contribute to its cache identity.
- Partial cache hits filter option lists together with the remaining videos.
- Configured defaults, request options, flat/nested scopes, UUID reuse, and encoder profiling preserve their existing behavior.
- Short option lists raise a clear `ValueError` with and without a processor cache. Unused trailing entries remain supported.

## Validation

Validated on 2026-10-11 at head `a0067713d3`, rebased onto upstream `01abe975b5`.

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' uv run --no-project -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' uv run --no-project -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py tests/multimodal/test_processing.py -q
uv run --no-project -- .venv/bin/pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py
```

The Qwen3 processor, generic processing, and cache suites pass, as do the applicable scoped hooks. The CUDA sleep/wake integration was skipped in the CPU suite. The short-list reproducer failed with `IndexError: list index out of range` before the guard and raises the expected `ValueError` afterward. Regressions exercise empty/short lists, warm caches, longer lists through partial hits, and profiling with fewer videos than configured options.

The cache regression checks prompts, placeholders, tensors, hashes, scalar-reference grids, duplicate videos, partial hits, reordering, model/request options, flat/nested scopes, and UUID-only reuse. Input options remain unmodified.

| Loaded-model comparison | Configuration/result |
| --- | --- |
| Model/runtime | Real `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` weights, snapshot `89644892e4d85e24eaac8bacfd4f463576704203`; RTX 5070 Ti, BF16, MRV2, FlashAttention 2, eager execution |
| Workload | Synthetic video pairs with `num_frames=[8,16]`, duplicate/partial/reordered cache use against uncached references; greedy 8-token generation |
| Result | Prompt IDs, placeholders, tensors, hashes, output token IDs, and complete top-5 logprob maps match; maximum logprob difference **0.0** |

Validation used the shared development environment, pinned Humming 0.1.16, and existing precompiled CUDA extensions. Optional FlashInfer autotuning and JIT warmup were disabled. This is a focused 2B family comparison, not a 4B answer-quality benchmark.

## Details

Request-wide option-list hashes let repeated videos reuse the first video's result despite different sampling settings. Partial hits removed videos without removing the corresponding option entries.

The existing base hooks let Qwen3-VL refine item hashes and select cache-miss options while preserving other processors. The final text/image HF call suppresses configured video lists so merging cannot reintroduce them. The review fix stays in the Qwen3 processor and its existing regression suite.

Merged #56372 handles option scoping and the cache API; this fix uses that behavior. The current overlap search found no competing per-item cache identity/partial-hit fix. #54527 addresses scoped option reads in other models; #60879 bounds MiniMax video decoding.

Affected hashes retain the full option list as well as selected item options, so equivalent reordered requests can incur extra misses. Scalar paths retain their existing hashes.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Initialize DCP metadata after batch partitioning
author: Sy0307
body:
## TL;DR

Initializes MRV2 DCP-local sequence metadata once from the final runtime `InputBatch`, after PCP partitioning, padding, and dummy-batch construction. This removes duplicated setup paths and prevents missing or stale `dcp_local_seq_lens` in eager, CUDA Graph, and DFlash execution.

## Purpose

Initialize MRV2 DCP-local sequence lengths from the final runtime `InputBatch`, after PCP partitioning and request padding.

Previously, several paths prepared `dcp_local_seq_lens` independently and at different points. Dummy/cudagraph batches could leave it unset, while PCP could replace the batch after DCP metadata had already been derived. Consumers then observed stale metadata or failed with `TypeError: NoneType object is not subscriptable`.

This PR centralizes the conditional initialization in `maybe_prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens` and uses it for:

- normal runtime attention preparation;
- generic cudagraph capture inputs;
- DFlash cudagraph capture inputs;
- PCP-partitioned batches.

Authorship is retained from Raphael Rialland, including DCO sign-offs.

title: [ROCm] [BugFix] Fix AITER MXFP4 ASM-GEMM crash on unfused shared experts
author: ColinZ22
body:
## Summary
Serving AMD Quark MXFP4 quantized Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoint on gfx950 (MI350x) crashes during weight loading: the shared expert's `down_proj` (in_features=640) violates the AITER ASM FP4 GEMM's scale-swizzle shape assumption. This PR aims to address this issue by adding a per-layer ASM shape guard that flips the layers with crashing shape to the fallback Triton FP4 GEMM. For the case of shared expert fusion enabled, this PR also moves the shared-expert fusion resolution before the TP shared expert replicate gate to ensure correct behavior. 

## Modifications
`kernels/linear/mxfp4/aiter.py`: add per-layer ASM shape guard; originally `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` gated the ASM path on a global flag, then unconditionally reshaped `weight_scale` into the ASM tile layout. That reshape needs scale rows `% 32 == 0` and scale columns `% 8 == 0`. The shared-expert `down_proj` scale `(2560, 20)` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next fails it and raises `RuntimeError: shape '[80,2,16,1,2,4,1]' is invalid for input of size 25600`. Added `_asm_fp4_scale_swizzle_supported()` and `process_weights_after_loading` checks it per layer. When unsupported, it falls back to the Triton FP4 GEMM for that layer only.

`models/qwen3_next.py`: resolve shared-expert fusion before the replicate gate;  `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` (inherited by `Qwen4ExpSparseMoeBlock`) evaluated `_should_replicate_misaligned_shared_expert` before deciding fusion, so at TP sizes where `shared_expert_intermediate_size` (640) isn't divisible by the OCP-MX FP4 group size of 32, it would raise or force replication (if using EP) and thereby block fusion. Reordered so fusion is resolved first; when fused, the standalone shared-expert projections no longer exist, so `replicate_shared_expert` is `False` and is the intended behavior. Fusion-off behavior is unchanged.

`tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py`: add coverage for the ASM shape guard; `test_asm_fp4_scale_swizzle_supported_shape_rules` parametrizes `_asm_fp4_scale_swizzle_supported` over aligned vs. misaligned scale shapes. Shapes that don't satisfy ASM kernel assumptions must fall back to Triton GEMM path, and the rest stay on ASM kernel path; 

## Tests and Validation
Run MI350x GPUs (gfx950), TP=2:

**Launch (FSE off):**
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```
**Launch (FSE on):**
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

**gsm8k (5-shot):**
```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:<port>/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,timeout=1200,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=2048" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template
```

| Config | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| FSE off (Triton fallback enabled) | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | 0.9606 ± 0.0054 |
| FSE on (fused MoE) | 0.9682 ± 0.0048 | 0.9674 ± 0.0049 |

title: [Bugfix][Docs] Package glm5next nvidia subtree and fix its docstrings
author: hmellor
body:
## Purpose

The docs build emits these warnings on `main`:

```
WARNING - api-autonav: Skipping implicit namespace package (without an __init__.py file) at .../vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia
WARNING - griffe: vllm/models/glm5next/amd/ops/kpool_compress.py:634: No type or annotation for parameter 'key / slot_score'
WARNING - griffe: vllm/models/glm5next/amd/ops/kpool_compress.py:634: Parameter 'key / slot_score' does not appear in the function signature
WARNING - griffe: vllm/models/glm5next/amd/ops/kpool_compress.py:636: No type or annotation for parameter 'slot_mapping / positions'
WARNING - griffe: vllm/models/glm5next/amd/ops/kpool_compress.py:636: Parameter 'slot_mapping / positions' does not appear in the function signature
```

The first one is more than a docs nit. `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/` and `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/` have no `__init__.py`, and `pyproject.toml` uses `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` (regular packages, not namespace packages), so **the entire nvidia subtree is silently dropped from built wheels**:

```python
>>> from setuptools import find_packages
>>> sorted(p for p in find_packages(include=["vllm*"]) if "glm5next" in p)
['vllm.models.glm5next',
 'vllm.models.glm5next.amd',
 'vllm.models.glm5next.amd.ops',
 'vllm.models.glm5next.amd.ops.third_party',
 'vllm.models.glm5next.amd.ops.third_party.kda']
```

Note the missing `vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia*` entries, including `nvidia/ops/third_party/kda` (which does have its own `__init__.py`, but is unreachable because its parents do not). Editable installs work by path so this is invisible locally.

## Changes

- Add `__init__.py` (SPDX header only, matching the sibling `amd` packages) to `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/` and `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/`.
- Split the combined `key / slot_score:` and `slot_mapping / positions:` Google-style docstring entries into one entry per parameter in both `amd/ops/kpool_compress.py` and `nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py`. griffe treats the combined text as a single parameter name that does not exist in the signature. (The nvidia copy had the same defect but was never reported, because the missing `__init__.py` meant griffe never loaded it.)

No behaviour change.

## Test Result

Packaging fix verified:

```python
>>> sorted(p for p in find_packages(include=["vllm*"]) if "glm5next" in p)
[... 'vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia',
     'vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops',
     'vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops.third_party',
     'vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops.third_party.kda']
```

Docstring fix verified by loading the package with griffe and forcing every docstring to parse; no warnings are emitted, and `nvidia` is now discovered as a package with submodules `attention, kda, model, mtp, multimodal, ops`.

Linters:

```
pre-commit run                                     # all hooks Passed
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual   # Passed
```

The GPU tests that touch these modules (`tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py`) were not run locally: no GPU available. The change is docstring text plus two SPDX-only `__init__.py` files, so it cannot affect model output, accuracy, or serving, and no evals are applicable.

## Duplicate check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "glm5next"` and `--search "docs warnings griffe"` return no PR touching these files or warnings.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change. I have reviewed every changed line and verified the packaging and docs results quoted above.

title: [Bugfix] GLM-5.3-Flash: fp8 plan dtype on SM90 sparse MLA, and right-size the indexer prefill workspace
author: drakosha
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

## Not a duplicate

- #51252 divides the *builder's* chunk budget by `compress_ratio` for DeepSeek; this is
  the model-side `max_total_seq_len` for GLM-5.3. Per @nood-co1 the two compose.
- #54743 scopes offload group configs to prefix-cacheable groups; different file,
  different failure.
- Searched open PRs for `get_max_prefill_buffer_size`, `max_total_seq_len` and the SM90
  sparse backend; nothing else touches these call sites.

## Testing

No unit test covers either path (both need a GLM-5.3 checkpoint and FlashInfer on
Hopper), so this was validated by serving. 2x H200 NVL, TP2, LibertAI NVFP4 weights,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, MTP k=3, CUDA graphs on, CPU offload
with a 256 GiB region. Both fixes have been running in production here since 2026-08-29
and 2026-09-01 respectively.

- fp8 fix: without it the server does not start; with it `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` is
  selected and the KV pool holds 4,503,445 tokens against 2,532,577 in bf16.
- workspace fix: available KV memory 29.44 -> 32.06 GiB, GPU KV cache size
  4,503,445 -> 4,904,494 tokens (+8.9%). Note that run also raised `--max-num-seqs`
  16 -> 32, so part of the freed memory went back into per-sequence buffers.
- Regression battery after the workspace change: needle retrieval on 1M-token prompts
  4/4 at depths 0.05/0.35/0.65/0.95; 32 concurrent 118k-token prompts, 32/32 with 0
  failures and 0 preemptions; an eviction cycle of eleven 500k-token prompts against a
  4.9M-token KV pool, where the return visit is served from CPU offload (61.0s cold,
  3.5s on return, `external_prefix_cache_hits_total` +492,800).

## Model evaluation

fp8 KV against bf16 on the same checkpoint: GSM8K 0.888 vs 0.880, MATH exact 0.9050 vs
0.9071 (symbolic 0.9671 vs 0.9664), MBPP 0.910 vs 0.920, IFEval prompt strict 0.880 /
instruction strict 0.925. All within noise. The workspace change moves no math: same
kernels, same inputs, only a smaller scratch allocation, and the needle battery above is
identical before and after.

AI assistance was used for this work.

title: [Bugfix][DP] Prevent mismatched collectives on duplicate resume
author: bvolpato
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A duplicate `resume_generation()` can hang a data-parallel MoE engine when a request starts a new wave. An idle rank can enter the resume all-reduce while the rank that received the request skips it.

## Claims

- Unpaused ranks skip the resume collective even when they hear about a wave at different times.
- Paused ranks and newly joined Elastic EP ranks still synchronize before stepping. The engine still rejects a resume that arrives while its pause is pending.

## Validation

The regression sends a resume to an idle rank, submits a request to rank 0, then sends rank 0 its resume. For the baseline comparison, restore only `vllm/v1/engine/core.py` from the merge base. Run the test on both trees at `TP_SIZE=1` and `TP_SIZE=2`.

```sh
RAY_ADDRESS=local DP_SIZE=2 TP_SIZE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py::test_dp_duplicate_resume_while_one_rank_starts_a_wave
```

On B200 GPUs with `ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b`, reverting the production change left only rank 1 logging `setting pause state to UNPAUSED` before pytest reported `+++ Timeout +++`. With the fix, the request finished at both TP sizes. The thread timeout also allows for a cold MoE JIT cache.

For the documentation update, `mkdocs build --strict` built the full site locally and the pre-commit hooks passed on the changed files. Upstream pre-commit and the docs preview both stopped at the contributor check.

<details>
<summary>Additional GPU coverage</summary>

The comparison used the branch merged with `410ab341a8` and a precompiled build of `b8c04dd3b4`. The regression also passed on a merge with `b2a9480dc7` using `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`. Earlier runs covered the full `test_async_llm_dp.py` file and a stress run that hung within 25 rounds on the baseline and completed 200 rounds with the fix.

Elastic EP eager and CUDA graph variants passed with the host-wide Ray shutdown fixture omitted. The NIXL variant failed at startup on both trees. A separate `test_engine_core_tp` run also failed on both trees. ROCm and model accuracy were not evaluated.

</details>

## Details

`engines_running` changes when an individual rank learns about work. `ignore_start_dp_wave` is set when the ranks agree to pause and when a new Elastic EP rank joins. Using that flag to guard the all-reduce gives every rank the same decision. [Review discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55229#discussion_r4170893423)

The related change in #59559 moved responsibility for starting waves to the engines. I found no other open PR for the duplicate-resume guard.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Restore DSpark cache-group capability under optimized Python
author: GirasoleY
body:
## Summary

- restore `non_causal_multi_token_decode` as an MLA cache-group capability, promoted when any group member needs the non-causal draft path;
- keep the inherited KV-cache merge incompatibility check active under `python -O` while preserving the `AssertionError` contract used by grouping callers;
- extend existing tests to cover a causal target and non-causal draft sharing one capability-enabled builder, plus the optimized-Python fallback.

## Why

#54277 changed `non_causal_multi_token_decode` from `any()` aggregation into an equality constraint. That made allocation compatibility depend on runtime causality even though the target and draft use the same physical MLA cache layout. Execution already selects the causal target path or non-causal draft path from each invocation's `CommonAttentionMetadata.causal`, so the group only needs to advertise the union of supported behavior.

Optimized Python removes the default `KVCacheSpec.merge` assertion. `MambaSpec` inherits that implementation, so unequal Kimi-K3 cache specs could then be reported as uniform and collapsed. Raising the same `AssertionError` explicitly keeps the existing `is_kv_cache_spec_uniform()` fallback behavior under `-O`.

## Non-duplication

This is materially different from #55187, which broadly converts merge assertions to `ValueError`. Existing cache-group compatibility probes catch `AssertionError`, so changing only the exception type makes normal incompatibility abort grouping. This PR instead preserves the caller contract and removes the target/draft marker mismatch by restoring capability semantics. #51065 addresses a Triton-specific causal multi-token execution path; this issue reproduces with FlashInfer MLA and originates in KV-cache grouping.

The distinction and validation were documented on #54649 before opening this PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54649#issuecomment-5531763473.

## Testing

- `uvx --offline ruff check vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` — passed.
- `uvx --offline ruff format --check vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` — passed.
- Reserved `pod4-gb300-4-tray10-f3`, applied the production patch to the pinned nightly image, and ran the updated `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py` through a uv-created `.venv` — 6 passed.
- Ran the new uniformity probe with `.venv/bin/python -O`; unequal inherited specs correctly took the non-uniform fallback.
- Full model evaluation on two reserved GB300 nodes with `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1`, Kimi-K3 target revision `37743f8aa061dea001dc89e11d13520d8973090c`, Kimi-K3-DSpark draft revision `6f659232a007121d5203e9619d3e97b81756887c`, TP8/DCP8, FlashInfer MLA for both models, and full/piecewise CUDA graphs: completion returned HTTP 200 with the expected answer (`56`), DSpark accepted 81/220 drafted tokens, and neither node logged CUDA, engine-core, or Mamba-state errors.
- Validation processes and temporary runtime directories were removed, and all machine reservations were released.

## AI assistance
