title: [Bugfix] Exclude DP token padding from draft attention metadata
author: khluu
body:
DeepSeek-V3.2 DP8 + EP + MTP crashes when DP ranks have unequal request counts. A rank with 12 requests receives model inputs padded to 13 tokens; the sparse indexer then fails with `shape '[12, -1, 64, 128]' is invalid for input of size 106496`. This is confirmed in [main build 87584](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87584#01a07dad-00e7-4a29-9abe-6cdc65c9100f). The subsequent GSM8K result of 0.0000 reflects the engine failure.

Autoregressive draft decode produces one query per request. Use the descriptor's request count, falling back to the actual local request count, for the attention token count in both ordinary and fused multi-step decode. Preserve padded model inputs/collective sizes and FULL graph request padding.

Validation:
- The exact [H200 large-model job in build 87389](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87389#01a0712c-2e18-480d-bda7-dfac8725ed44) passed all **6 evaluations** on implementation commit `39ba6cbae8e1`. DeepSeek-V3.2-DP scored **0.9568**, above its **0.8700** lower bound.
- After merging main and removing the added regression test, unused imports caused pre-commit to fail. Those imports are now removed. `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle_draft_attn_metadata.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh targeted H200 validation for current head `c34119ecbe4d` is [build 87771](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87771). Its result is pending; the older passing run above is not represented as current-head validation.

Duplicate checks found no competing PR for the one-query-per-request draft-decode metadata mismatch. Related #53660, #54102, and #53577 address draft prefill, verifier residual padding, and DSpark PP respectively. This PR updates the existing fix rather than introducing a second implementation.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and validation.

title: [Bugfix] Fall back to T1 when ARC cannot reclaim enough entries from T2
author: zupengwang
body:
## Purpose

CPU KV offload stores can fail even when ARC has enough evictable entries. When T1 is below its adaptive target, eviction prefers T2 but currently returns `None` once T2 has no eligible candidates. This also occurs partway through a batch, or when T2 entries are pinned or protected.

Fall back to eligible T1 entries after exhausting T2. Preserve the existing preference order, monotonic queue scans, pin/protection rules, and atomic failure when the total candidate count is insufficient. Add six parameterized cases to the existing manager suite using normal stores and ghost hits to reproduce the adaptive state.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-09-05 found no open PR implementing this CPU ARC fallback. #50422 adds session-aware policy context without fixing this selection path; #40270 targets GPU BlockPool ARC; #51787 concerns LRU transfer ordering. This change preserves the single-pass optimization merged in #50992.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change.

## Test Plan

Tested against upstream `7fbd44cbe0a90b9c8fd3a94a0f0401ac4b1bc719` on Linux with Python 3.12.13 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. The isolated checkout imports its own upstream Python source and reuses dependencies and binary extensions from an existing vLLM 0.28.0 installation.

```bash
# Baseline: original ARC implementation with the new regression test.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py -k test_store_falls_back_to_t1_when_t2_cannot_satisfy_eviction --timeout=60

# Fixed implementation.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py --timeout=60
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py --timeout=60
```

## Test Result

- Baseline regression: 5 failed, 1 passed. All five requests with sufficient eligible capacity failed; the insufficient-capacity control passed.
- Fixed manager suite: 34 passed.
- Policy factory and tiering suites: 62 passed.
- Ruff check/format, typos, mypy for Python 3.10–3.13, and the applicable repository validation hooks passed individually on the two changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- The bulk pre-commit invocation was blocked during unrelated Actionlint environment installation by TLS/download timeouts. Applicable Python checks were subsequently run individually using the unmodified repository configuration.

These are CPU unit tests. No model evaluation, GPU test, or end-to-end offload throughput benchmark was run; no performance or model-quality claim is made.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Recover locally invalidated pull peer metadata
author: xijiaat
body:
## Summary

Recover a pull peer whose **local NIXL metadata is missing while Prefill is still alive with the same engine ID**. Without recovery, vLLM's cached `_remote_agents` entry and prepared dlists can keep subsequent requests on the stale path.

A receive failure schedules a descriptor-free `check_remote_metadata(agent)` check. This queries **local metadata existence, not peer health**. Only confirmed absence makes the peer eligible for recovery; a transfer error or probe exception alone does not.

## Implementation

- Track failed and locally invalid peers in `NixlBaseConnectorWorker`. One `_cleanup_remote_engines()` pass handles both replacement and invalidation, reusing `_cleanup_remote_engine()` to release resources.
- Defer probes and cleanup while background handshakes are pending. For invalid peers, reject new reads and wait for all existing receive handles to settle before cleanup. Replacement cleanup retains its existing queued-request guard.
- Clear recovery state in the shared per-engine cleanup, including TTL eviction and shutdown. A peer that is both replaced and invalidated is cleaned once; the replacement's address mapping is preserved.
- Route new and handshake-ready requests through the pull worker's existing read entry point. After cleanup, a fresh request re-handshakes the unchanged engine ID and uses newly prepared descriptors. Failed requests are **not replayed with old remote block IDs**.

The production changes are in `nixl/base_worker.py` and `nixl/pull_worker.py`. Recovery remains **pull-only**, with an explicit push-mode TODO. There is no new router API, configuration, or metadata probe on successful transfers.

Following Yannik's review, tests reuse `TestPeerReplacement` and `FakeNixlWrapper` instead of a separate hand-built recovery fixture. The existing receive/HMA fixtures and push test stub initialize the new fields. Nick Hill's read/handshake simplification is retained with authorship preserved.

## Related Work and Scope

Related to #49238. This is a follow-up to merged #50047, not another replacement detector:

| Change | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| #50047 | A new engine ID is confirmed at the same address. |
| This PR | The engine ID is unchanged, but NIXL has lost the decoder's local peer metadata. |

Both now use one base-worker cleanup pass, rather than separate replacement and recovery passes. The scope split was discussed in [#50047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50047#issuecomment-5629552908).

#52232 addresses HMA failure propagation and is **not included here**. Recovering future requests does not by itself guarantee that the failed HMA request returns an error instead of invalid output. TTL policy and the native UCX race discussed in NIXL #1987 are also outside this patch's scope.

Stuck reads or handshakes defer recovery; this patch does not forcibly release active resources. Native cleanup exceptions propagate rather than being swallowed. Recovery is not a claim that every UCX failure is recoverable.

## Validation

### Refactor and CI

| Check | Result and revision scope |
| --- | --- |
| Local source-AST/mock regressions after the refactor and September 29 main merge | 32 passed: 20 previous recovery cases plus 12 existing receive-lifecycle cases. These external harnesses are not full-import vLLM tests. |
| Old-fixture negative control | The same 12 receive-lifecycle cases fail with the original missing-field fixtures. |
| Recorded-main behavioral negative control | 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passing controls. |
| Local pre-commit, including Ruff and mypy; `git diff --check` | Passed on the September 29 merged revision. |
| [Buildkite #91865](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91865), September 29 merged revision | NVIDIA KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**; AMD KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**. The overall build reports "passed and blocked"; not every defined pipeline job was executed. |
| [Subsequent automatic main merge](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8aba1056b6b811b4770fd6bba860b54835c84ca6), September 30 | Pre-commit and DCO passed. No full Buildkite result is attached to this new head at the time of this update; #91865 tested the preceding revision. |

The failures in earlier CI #91736 were missing recovery fields in fixtures that bypass the worker constructor. Those fixtures are now initialized, and the subsequent KV Connector shards pass.

Regression coverage includes confirmed-missing versus healthy/probe-error cases, same-ID re-handshake with fresh descriptors, pending-handshake gating, sibling-handle drain ordering, new-read rejection, healthy-peer isolation, replacement/invalidation overlap, notify-only requests, expiry accounting, cleanup exceptions, TTL eviction, and shutdown.

Local full-import pytest collection was blocked by missing `tblib` and the incomplete vLLM runtime environment; the 32 local cases are not a substitute for CI. There is **no new native NIXL/GPU or model-serving evaluation of the refactored revision**. Historical experiments below remain evidence only for their stated revisions and configurations.

### Reproduction Commands

From a vLLM checkout with the repository's test dependencies installed:

```bash
# Focused replacement and local-invalidation coverage.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -k TestPeerReplacement -v --tb=short

# Broader connector CPU regression suite.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -v --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

These commands select the current tests; they are not presented as the exact Buildkite shard commands. The old `-k peer_recovery` selector no longer describes the consolidated tests.

<details>
<summary>Historical native and serving evidence, before the current refactor</summary>

### September 23 H20 validation

Full vLLM Python imports in isolated H20 containers: **357 selected CPU tests passed**, including 18 recovery cases; the corresponding main-only selection passed 339. Eight selected baseline cases produced 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passes.

Real NIXL/UCX probes passed with 1 MiB CPU and GPU buffers. With the peer still alive, the probe deliberately removed local metadata, observed the stale-read failure, invoked patched cleanup, and explicitly reloaded the same agent's metadata for a byte-checked read. Healthy-peer reads continued working. Automatic re-handshake was covered separately by pytest.

Runtime: NIXL 1.4.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3. The rebased Python source used native extensions from the existing vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9` image, not a fresh CUDA build of main. No weights were loaded for this validation. This is not a model-serving, natural-disconnect, or NVLink/RDMA validation of the current revision.

[Exact commands, full selected logs, and native probe](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/34c74ce35e1f68958e5881a1907bf84d).

### Original TP1 P/D serving experiment

The original implementation was tested with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, NIXL 1.3.2, fp8 HMA KV, eager mode, `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy`, and the existing TP1 packed-layout fix. With no active reads, a controlled hook removed only Decode's local remote metadata, retaining the Python cache. A real stale read failed with `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`; fresh requests automatically re-handshook the unchanged Prefill engine ID and returned the expected short answers.

The **recovery-only failed request still emitted 32 invalid tokens**. Adding #52232 and an API terminal-error follow-up produced a passing 10-request scenario: two normal controls, four controlled failures across Chat/Completion and streaming/non-streaming, and four fresh Chat recoveries. The failed requests emitted no generated content. This combined result must not be attributed to the recovery-only diff. Attribution for the HMA change belongs to Tyler Michael Smith.

The original recovery-only CPU selections passed 353 distinct cases across two runs. The combined recovery/HMA/API experiment passed 425 selected tests, not 425 tests of this standalone patch. Full original logs retain earlier failures and an independently wrong pre-injection arithmetic control.

This is controlled failure-path evidence, not general accuracy, natural transport-failure reproduction, multi-rank native-race coverage, or a guarantee of production readiness.

[Selected raw logs, response bodies/SSE, commands and patches](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/a975858a507d6c45fd394b3675cc0ab9). Internal addresses and paths are anonymized. The HMA/API evidence is also reported in [#52232](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52232#issuecomment-5552174526).

### Maintainer simplification

Nick Hill's [simplification](https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/7dc2a0eb49dbc62fdfc329885e663a672160cdec) was incorporated with authorship and sign-off preserved. It reuses main's in-flight-transfer guard rather than a second request-to-engine map: receive metadata remains available until the handles settle. The subsequent refactor retains that approach and moves cleanup into the base worker as suggested by Yannik Hinteregger.

</details>

## AI Assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, and this report. The human submitter reviewed and approved the original contribution; subsequent compatibility adaptations remain subject to human review. Historical results and limited failure-path tests are not claims of comprehensive model evaluation or production readiness.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Preserve target parallel config (DCP) for DSpark
author: starkwj
body:
## Purpose

Fix Kimi-K3 startup with DSpark when decode context parallelism (DCP) is enabled.

#50514 changed `load_dspark_model` to use `speculative_config.draft_parallel_config` instead of target's `parallel_config` when constructing the draft `VllmConfig`.
However, `speculative_config.draft_parallel_config` only copies a subset of the target parallel settings and leaves DCP fields at their defaults (dcp=1) (in function `create_draft_parallel_config`).
Thus, when launching models (e.g, Kimi-K3) with DCP and DSpark, the DSpark failed to inherit the DCP settings, and results in assertion failure.

```shell
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py", line 299, in create_metada
ta_builders
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]     builder_cls(
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla.py", l
ine 141, in __init__
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]     super().__init__(
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.p
y", line 2376, in __init__
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]     assert isinstance(self.dcp_manager, MLADCPManager)
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055]            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(Worker_TP3_DCP3 pid=19149) ERROR 09-05 13:03:34 [multiproc_executor.py:1055] AssertionError
```

#50514 only changes this behavior for DSpark (not DFlash/Eagle).
Thus, this PR is a quick "revert" fix for DSpark, and retaining the setting `PP=1` in #50514.
This PR does not fix by modifying `create_draft_parallel_config`, as it may affect other drafters' behavior.
And according to RFC #53673, more refactor for decoupling target and draft parallel config may be required.


## Test Plan

Launch Kimi-K3 with DCP 8 and DSpark (Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark).

## Test Result

Succeed to start Kimi-K3 with DCP and DSpark.

title: [MyPy][4/N] Fix mypy errors in medium-hard tests/ dirs
author: theSatvik
body:
## Purpose

PR 4 of #49569, covering the "medium-hard" test directories. Fixes every mypy error in them at the stricter `follow_imports=silent` setting and routes them into `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so the fixes are enforced. Claimed [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49569#issuecomment-5552556980).

**511 errors → 0** on current `main` (`10f6ab01a`):

| Directory | Errors on `main` | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tests/v1/kv_offload` | 232 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/worker` | 94 | 0 |
| `tests/parser` | 64 | 0 |
| `tests/model_executor` (incl. `model_loader`, `kernels`) | 49 | 0 |
| `tests/renderers` | 28 | 0 |
| `tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text` | 20 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/metrics` | 13 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/streaming_input` | 11 | 0 |
| `tests/models/test_initialization.py` | 0 | 0 |

With #51043 merged, `tests/model_executor` is a single silent-group entry, and this PR no longer touches `tests/model_executor/layers`.

## Approach (reworked per review)

- **No `cast()` anywhere.** Fixes use, in order:
  1. Runtime-true narrowing (`assert x is not None`, `assert isinstance(...)`, small typed narrowing helpers, e.g. for `EMABackpressureDetector` in `test_backpressure.py`).
  2. Stubs fixed once per file (`MockVllmConfig`, stand-in builders with honest return types).
  3. `MagicMock(spec=...)`, only where it can't make a test vacuous.
  4. A scoped `# type: ignore[code]` with a reason.

  `cast(X, None)`, `cast(Any, ...)` and `_NO_BACKEND` are gone. `supports_eagle3` uses `assert isinstance(target, SupportsEagle3)`.
- **Ignores.** Monkeypatched methods use `monkeypatch.setattr`, as PR 3 did. That includes the 4 older `method-assign` ignores that were already in these dirs on `main`, so there are 0 left. The 36 remaining scoped ignores (12 `type-abstract`, 7 `list-item`, 6 `misc`, 3 `call-arg`, 3 `attr-defined`, 2 `override`, 2 `dict-item`, 1 `call-overload`) each carry a reason. Starting fresh from `main` with `--warn-unused-ignores`, the migrated directories had 8 unused ignores; they now have 0. The two `apply_post_tokenization` ignores were already unused on `main` before the overloads below went in, so the overloads didn't remove them. The overloads are kept because they give callers the precise return type.
- **`vllm/` fixes folded in:**
  - `RayPrometheusMetric.labels() -> Self` (the 7 casts in `test_ray_metrics.py` disappear and that file is unchanged from `main`).
  - `@overload`s on `TokenizeParams.apply_post_tokenization`.
  - `"azacinto_foscolo"` in `AudioAssetName`.
  - `StreamingInput.prompt: PromptType | EngineInput`, because its consumers, `process_inputs` and `extract_prompt_components`, already take `PromptType | EngineInput`.
- **HiSparse.** No cast and no issue: production always passes a `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup`, and the base class only appears because the test registers without a HiSparse config.

## Defects the type checker surfaced

1. **`RoutingMethodType.FUSED_TOPK` doesn't exist** (`tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`). Any read of `DummyRouter.routing_method_type` raised `AttributeError`, and `FusedMoE` does read that property. Fixed to `TopK`.
2. **Dead setup writes in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`.** `worker.refines_row_mirrors` and `worker._layer_mirror_callbacks` exist nowhere in `vllm/`, left behind by an upstream refactor. `test_hisparse_appends_reference_slots_within_a_mirror_phase` reads as if it toggles a row-mirror mode, but that setup did nothing. Removed.
3. **Dead observer attributes in `test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py`.** `slot_mapping_observer` and `host_mirror_forward_observer` likewise exist nowhere in `vllm/`. Removed.
4. **`CPUExpertsFp8` → `CPUExpertsInt4`.** The old test built its "monolithic" expert from a non-monolithic class, so it never reached the replay-support check. #59455 has since fixed this independently on `main`, so it's no longer in this diff.
5. **Wrong helper annotation in `test_obj_tier.py`.** `lookup_and_wait` was annotated `-> list[bool]` but returns `list[LookupResult]` (matches `test_fs_tier.py` now).
6. **Missing isinstance check in `test_factory.py`.** It lacked the `assert isinstance(spec, CPUOffloadingSpec)` its siblings have.
7. **`DUMMY_TOOLS` raw dicts (found, not changed here).** In `tests/parser/engine/replay_harness.py`, raw dicts are assigned to `request.tools`, and pydantic never validates them (no `validate_assignment`). The tool-schema helpers skip non-`ChatCompletionToolsParam` entries, so the parsers see no tool schema. Since fixing it changes what runs, it's left out of this PR; happy to send it separately.

## Behaviour changes

**None.** The three changes you flagged (`DUMMY_TOOLS`, `mock_request`, `block_ids`) are reverted. Every change is now a type annotation, a runtime-true assert, an equivalent rewiring, the `FUSED_TOPK` fix, or removal of writes to attributes nothing reads.

## Annotation issues in `vllm/` worked around (follow-up candidates)

- **`GDNAttentionBackend`** doesn't implement the abstract `get_impl_cls`, so mypy treats it as abstract, which causes the `type-abstract` ignores in the worker tests. Model classes that subclass protocol interfaces with optional members are treated as abstract for the same reason.
- **`EMABackpressureDetector.default_config`** is annotated `-> dict | None` but always returns a dict.
- **`VllmJitKernel.dispatch(self, **kwargs: Any)`** makes subclasses with named keyword-only parameters fail the override check.
- **`supports_eagle3` / `supports_eagle` overloads** list `type[object]` first. With `nn.Module` resolving to `Any`, a model *instance* matches the class overload, and `TypeIs` narrows it to `type[SupportsEagle3]`. That's why `test_plamo3.py` and `test_qwen3_omni.py` use `assert isinstance(target, SupportsEagle3)` (the helper's exact body) instead of calling the helper.

## Test Plan

```bash
# strict-group mypy on every target file + changed vllm/ files, all CI Python versions
mypy --python-version {3.10,3.11,3.12,3.13} <target dirs> vllm/{assets/audio,engine/protocol,renderers/params,v1/metrics/ray_wrappers}.py
mypy --python-version 3.10 --warn-unused-ignores <target dirs>
ruff check / ruff format --check (v0.14.0) and typos on all changed files
python -c "from tools.pre_commit.mypy import group_files; ..."   # routing
# CPU (macOS, torch 2.13, VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty):
pytest tests/parser tests/renderers
pytest <every changed test file outside parser/renderers>
```

## Test Result

title: [Bugfix] Bound GDN speculative decode query widths
author: DimensionSTP
body:
## Overview

Keep oversized profiling rows out of GDN's bounded speculative state layout. This follows merged #56531, whose shared routing implementation is already in main.

I utilized AI tools to assist in refining the implementation, executing tests, and analyzing logs.

## Claims

- Require a decode row's query width to fit within `num_speculative_tokens + 1`, addressing the profiling failure reported by @okorzh-amd.
- Keep valid zero-draft and boundary-length rows on the speculative path.
- Add one small regression in the existing worker test file, as requested in review.

## Validation

On upstream main `4187ade7b87e` without the bound, the retained regression fails: query widths `[12, 8, 1]` with seven speculative tokens produce `[0, 0, 0]` instead of `[-1, 0, 0]`. It passes with the bound.

The official worker/GDN CPU suites pass: 74 passed, 3 platform skips. All applicable project checks pass, including Ruff, spelling, mypy for Python 3.10-3.13, and test-to-Buildkite wiring.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_zero_draft_spec_rows.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py

pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py
```

This update only reduces tests. Production code is unchanged from published `a1f1e1b7`. Earlier CUDA validation remains recorded in the PR history; this revision does not claim a new GPU or full-model E2E run.

The original reporter [confirmed that the change works in E2E tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55504#discussion_r4212822637). That is external confirmation, not an AMD run performed locally for this PR.

## Details

With seven speculative tokens, the state-index table has eight columns. Unflagged 12-token profiling rows were classified as speculative even though they exceed that layout. The inclusive width bound fixes this without requiring query length to equal the supplied draft count plus one, which would break adaptive verification.

The only production change is this bound in `MambaHybridModelState.prepare_attn()`. Existing upstream comments and inline routing are retained. The regression reuses the existing worker helpers. The added kernel coverage has been removed, leaving a two-file diff with one new test and no new helper, kernel, backend default, or public configuration.

#59824 carries this dependency as a separate backport. Landing the width bound through #55504 would let that PR use it from main.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Make streaming TTFT/E2E latency accounting consistent across endpoints
author: surajm20061998
body:
## Purpose

`vllm/benchmarks/serve.py` derives TPOT from the end of the request:

```python
latency_minus_ttft = outputs[i].latency - outputs[i].ttft
tpot = latency_minus_ttft / (output_len - 1)
```

For that to mean "average inter-token latency", `latency - ttft` has to equal
`sum(itl)`. Today it does not, and it fails differently per endpoint, so E2EL
and TPOT are not comparable between an `openai` run and an `openai-chat` run.

Two independent causes:

**1. TTFT is read off a second clock call (`/v1/completions`).**

```python
timestamp = time.perf_counter()          # chunk arrival; seeds the ITL chain
if not first_chunk_received:
    first_chunk_received = True
    ttft = time.perf_counter() - st      # a different, later reading
    output.ttft = ttft
...
most_recent_timestamp = timestamp        # the earlier reading
```

TTFT is measured from one reading while the ITL chain continues from another,
so `latency - ttft` comes up short by the gap between the two calls.
`async_request_openai_chat_completions` and `async_request_openai_audio` already
do the right thing (`output.ttft = timestamp - st`), so this aligns completions
with its siblings rather than introducing a new convention.

**2. The trailing `usage` chunk extends E2E latency (chat and audio).**

`vllm bench serve` always sends `stream_options.include_usage`, so every stream
ends with a choice-less `usage` chunk after the last token. In chat and audio,
`most_recent_timestamp = timestamp` sits *outside* the `if choices:` branch, so
that trailer advances the end of the request; `output.latency` therefore runs
past the final token. `async_request_openai_completions` updates it *inside*
the branch and stops at the last token. `serve.py` assigns
`e2els.append(outputs[i].latency)` directly, so this lands in reported E2EL and
TPOT.

I fixed it in the direction that stops at the last token, because the
alternative — having completions also count the usage chunk — would break the
identity on *both* endpoints instead of fixing it: the usage gap appears in
`latency` but never in any `itl`. The loop already refuses to let the `[DONE]`
sentinel move the clock; the usage chunk is the same category of non-token
trailer.

`benchmarks/backend_request_func.py` carries the same two defects and is still
imported by `benchmark_prefix_caching.py` and
`benchmark_serving_structured_output.py`, so it gets the identical hunks (plus
the same one-line TTFT fix in `async_request_tgi`). Happy to split that file
into its own PR if you'd rather keep this one to `vllm/benchmarks/`.

### Magnitude — deliberately not overstated

This is a correctness and cross-endpoint-comparability fix, **not** a
performance claim. `chat_completion/serving.py` yields the usage chunk
immediately after the final content chunk in the same generator with no engine
await between, so in normal operation the error is tens of microseconds — I
measured ~24 µs on a 200 ms request, about 0.01%. The gap is not bounded by
anything, though: it is whatever separates two SSE writes, which on a saturated
client event loop is not guaranteed to stay small.

The lasting value is the test: `endpoint_request_func.py` currently has no test
coverage of its timing accounting at all, so nothing was stopping this from
drifting further.

## Not a duplicate

Per `AGENTS.md` I checked:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "endpoint_request_func"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "backend_request_func"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "usage chunk latency"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "benchmark ttft latency"
```

The only open PRs in this area are **#42661** and **#46652**, which both address
a *different* bug: servers batching multiple tokens into one SSE chunk, making
ITL per-chunk rather than per-token. Neither touches which clock reading TTFT
uses, nor where the request is considered to end. They are complementary — with
either merged, `sum(itl)` still spans the same decode window, so the identity
asserted here continues to hold.

#46652 also adds `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func.py`; this PR adds
`test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, so there is no filename collision, and
the two suites could be folded together later if that is preferred.

## Test Plan

New: `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, parametrized over
all three streaming request functions (completions, chat, audio). CPU-only — no
GPU, model, or socket; the request functions are driven against a fake session.

The exactness tests substitute a **scripted clock** that advances by a fixed
tick on every read. What a code path observes then depends only on how many
times it reads the clock, so a stray or misattributed read shows up as a whole
tick of drift instead of sub-microsecond jitter. That makes the assertions
exact and free of timing flakiness.

1. `test_decode_span_identity_is_exact` — `(latency - ttft) - sum(itl) == 0`.
2. `test_trailing_usage_chunk_does_not_extend_latency` — E2E latency stops at
   the final token.
3. `test_decode_span_identity_holds_with_real_clock` — same identity against the
   real clock with real inter-chunk gaps.
4. `test_usage_only_stream_is_not_reported_as_success` — a stream with no token
   chunk fails rather than reporting a zero-duration success. The residual differences out the same
   recorded timestamps, so jitter cancels and only float rounding remains; the
   1 µs bound is ample rather than tight.

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_audio_dataset.py -v   # sibling suite, same module
pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py \
    benchmarks/backend_request_func.py \
    tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py
```

## Test Result

On unpatched `main` (f4eccda), the new tests fail with the defects visible as
whole ticks of the scripted clock — negative for the extra TTFT read, positive
for the counted usage chunk:

```
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[completions]
  AssertionError: completions: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = -1.0
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[chat]
  AssertionError: chat: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = 1.0
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[audio]
  AssertionError: audio: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = 1.0
8 failed, 1 passed
```

With the fix applied:

```
tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py 12 passed
tests/benchmarks/test_audio_dataset.py                 8 passed   (no regression)
(20 passed total)
```

Reverting only the two source files and re-running reproduces the 8 failures,
confirming the tests actually exercise the fix.

Independently, driving the unpatched request functions against a local SSE
server over a real socket, residual `(latency - ttft) - sum(itl)`:

| scenario | completions | chat |
|---|---|---|
| usage chunk emitted immediately (realistic) | −0.35 µs | +24.09 µs |
| usage chunk delayed 30 ms (mechanism probe) | −0.32 µs | **+31 473 µs** |

The probe isolates the mechanism: a 30 ms delay before the usage chunk moves
chat's residual by ~30 ms and leaves completions flat. After the fix, all four
cells are 0.00 µs.

`pre-commit` / `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean on all three files.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This changes only how the **benchmark client** measures latency
on the wire. No engine, scheduler, sampling, or serving path is touched, so
model outputs and accuracy are unaffected.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance. I have reviewed every changed
line, run the tests above myself, and can defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache][MLA] Align packed block strides for V3.2 sparse MLA
author: 200lz
body:
## Purpose

V3.2 sparse MLA did not publish the physical block-stride alignment its selected kernel requires. This PR sets the existing `block_stride_alignment` contract at the producer, lifts the field to `KVCacheSpec`, and lets the allocator consume it without an MLA type check. HiSparse hot-page and stride constraints are combined in one LCM so sequential rounding cannot invalidate the first constraint.

The requirement is selected by backend and cache format. Flattened-row paths, including FlashInfer sparse, share their predicate with warmup. SM100 FlashMLA paged FP8/NVFP4 additionally require independent native TMA alignment (`fp8_ds_mla`: 656 bytes; `nvfp4_ds_mla`: 352 bytes), without flattened-row warmup. Existing BLHNC/BLNHC support is retained.

This adopts LucasWilkinson’s minimized suggestion in 200lz/vllm#1: six files, +187/-27, including compact alignment/merge tests and the existing producer/allocator/binder contract test. Layout gating/threading, admission/auto-fit rewrites, and HiSparse PP capacity work are outside this PR.

## Scope and validation

This complements #56254’s existing alignment propagation and pool rounding by supplying the missing V3.2 producer requirement; upstream #53781 already fixed the fused-writer issue. Those changes are not duplicated here.

CPU validation on exact suggestion `1d45dcafade7903237c627d941fda7df26341d76`: **258 passed, 41 skipped**. A clean temporary merge with main `79468c20ef23227d4e051f807e10fd54fb24e24f` passed **265 tests, 45 skipped**. The PR branch itself was not merged with main.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Enable NIXL telemetry for the OBJ tier
author: zupengwang
body:
## Purpose

The OBJ secondary tier reads NIXL transfer telemetry for every successful store or load, but creates its agent with telemetry capture disabled by default. Without `NIXL_TELEMETRY_ENABLE`, a completed transfer raises `nixlNoTelemetryError` before releasing its handles or reporting the job result.

Enable telemetry capture when constructing the OBJ agent. Make the existing mock respect the disabled default, and extend the store/load roundtrip test to check transfer timing and completion bookkeeping.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-09-06 found no open PR implementing this fix. Searches covered OBJ telemetry, objectstore, `capture_telemetry`, and `nixlNoTelemetryError`. The open backpressure PR #50045 touches OBJ constructor plumbing but does not enable telemetry. The telemetry read was introduced by #48798.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change.

Tested against upstream `808f8cd3ac6751278d8b7be97f6fde5295ca4653` on Linux with Python 3.12.13 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. The isolated checkout imports its own upstream Python source and reuses dependencies and binary extensions from an existing vLLM 0.28.0 installation.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Fix batched CUTLASS workspace overallocation
author: itayalroy
body:
Batched CUTLASS receives one token buffer per local expert. Its `M` dimension is already the total token capacity from all dispatch ranks:

`M = max_tokens_per_rank * num_dispatchers`

The kernels reserve M token slots per expert, but workspace sizing multiplied `M` by `num_dispatchers` again. This counted the dispatch ranks twice and allocated memory that the kernels never use.

Instead, size both workspaces directly from `M`. For DeepSeek-V3 at DP 32 with 16 local experts, this reduces the shared workspace from 112 GiB to 3.5 GiB per GPU.

cc @tlrmchlsmth @mgoin

title: [Bugfix] Seed hybrid mamba state index with mamba_block_size on prefix-cache hits
author: pondzikk
body:
## Purpose

Fix an out-of-bounds read on prefix-cache hits for hybrid mamba models whose KV config contains a prefix-cacheable attention group with a block size smaller than `mamba_block_size` (e.g. a DFlash2/EAGLE sliding-window drafter group with block 64).

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot with `(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`. By then `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has reassigned `cache_config.block_size = min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`, so on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA + sparse MLA, mamba block 7168, drafter block 64/1024) the seed is in the wrong units. `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` takes it as `src_col` and `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`): cached prefixes of ≥ 8 mamba blocks fault (`Xid 31`, `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the next sync), shorter hits silently restore the wrong recurrent state.

The fix divides by `cache_config.mamba_block_size`, the unit used for mamba blocks everywhere else (`MambaSpec.block_size`, the preprocess kernel, the block-table width; `mamba_attn.py` already derives the same quantity from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`).

Fixes #55600.

## Test Plan

No unit test is included; the failure needs a hybrid model whose KV groups include a smaller-block prefix-cacheable group. Manual verification on GLM-5.3-Flash (EXL3, TP=1, DFlash2 `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `max_num_seqs=1`) on a DGX Spark, before/after on identical inputs.

## Test Result

- Prompt A = 57 344 tokens (8 full mamba blocks), then A + a different question: before → HTTP 500 in 0.2 s, `NVRM: Xid 31 ... FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`; after → completes in 11.7 s with 50 176 cached tokens.
- After: 13-, 34- and 63-block prefix hits complete; multi-needle recall on warm (cached) requests equals cold at 100k / 250k / 450k tokens (5/5 each); warm TTFT 8.7 s vs 139 s cold at 100k.
- 3-hour soak (57 multi-turn conversation turns with a prefix hit on every turn, contexts up to 184k tokens, fresh 41k–354k-token prompts): 133/133 requests OK, zero faults.

title: [Bugfix] Avoid nested rerank cancellation handlers
author: migarci2
body:
## Summary

The `/v1/rerank` and `/v2/rerank` aliases passed the same request to the already decorated `/rerank` handler. That created two concurrent consumers of `raw_request.receive()` and could leave the real rerank handler running after disconnect.

This removes the redundant outer cancellation decorators. Each alias now relies on the canonical `/rerank` handler, so every request has one disconnect listener.

I checked issue #55502 and searched open PRs for the issue number and rerank cancellation before updating this. I found no duplicate.

## Testing

- Pre-commit hooks for the affected files: all passed
- The regression fails for both aliases with the old nested decorators and passes after this change

No model evaluation was run because this only removes duplicate request-disconnect listeners and does not affect model output.

AI assistance was used to help investigate, implement, test, and review this change.

Fixes #55502

title: [Bugfix] Validate extension integers before engine serialization
author: khluu
body:
The OpenAI schema test failed with a 500 and an empty error message in [build 87389](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87389#01a0712c-2d63-40f8-918e-bed30aa34054). Its generated `ec_transfer_params` contained a nested integer outside MessagePack's supported range. The API accepts arbitrary JSON integers, but encoding the engine request raises `OverflowError` after request processing has begun.

Validate nested integers in `SamplingParams.extra_args` during construction and raise `VLLMValidationError` before engine submission. This covers `ec_transfer_params`, `kv_transfer_params`, and `vllm_xargs`, which flow into the same extension dictionary. Accept the full MessagePack range, `-2**63` through `2**64 - 1`, including unsigned 64-bit values. Preserve custom extension objects, shared containers, and other value types.

Reproduction: `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":2,"ec_transfer_params":{"x":18446744073709551616}}` returns 500 before the fix. Both positive and negative overflow reproduce; adjacent valid boundaries return 200. This was confirmed on H200 with the public CI image for commit `784cac7c424db2f2fdc879b672abad7e231f5698`, including the exact original CI payload.

Duplicate checks: searched open PRs and issues for `msgpack integer`, `extra_args overflow`, `ec_transfer_params 500`, and integer/validation combinations. #50353 prevents mutation of request extension dictionaries; #55290 handles remote encoder-transfer failures. Neither validates integer bounds before serialization.

Validation:
- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu /tmp/vllm-ci-api-validation/.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/test_sampling_params.py`: **19 passed** on macOS CPU. This suite uses no shared fixtures; `--noconftest` avoids loading unrelated GPU integration fixtures.
- Direct request-path checks with `ChatCompletionRequest.to_sampling_params` and `create_error_response`: the exact CI payload and both overflow boundaries produce **400 / BadRequestError**, with `param=extra_args`.
- `MsgpackEncoder.encode` still succeeds for all four signed/unsigned boundary values.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/sampling_params.py tests/test_sampling_params.py`: all applicable hooks, including mypy, passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The patched full GPU/API suite remains pending CI. The H200 HTTP reproduction above is the pre-fix baseline; the post-fix checks are local request-path/unit tests, not a claim of full GPU execution. Valid model inputs and generation behavior are unchanged, so no model evaluation result is claimed or required for this validation-only change.

CI: [build 87457](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87457) runs head `778b9bb391`. The original failing [Entrypoints Integration (API Server OpenAI - Part 1) lane](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87457#01a0781e-0ab7-4ede-bd99-d152e0df756b) is enabled and waiting for dependencies.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and validate this change. Published as a draft for human review; human review is not claimed as completed.

title: [Bugfix] reject string file on translation like transcription
author: Oskii
body:
## What

The audio transcription request already 422s when `file` is a string (`Expected 'file' to be a file-like object, not 'str'.`). The translation request has the same `file: UploadFile` field and the same stream-option validator, but it never ran that string check.

On `main` at `6865e67`:

```python
# transcription/protocol.py
if isinstance(data.get("file"), str):
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=HTTPStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
        detail="Expected 'file' to be a file-like object, not 'str'.",
    )

# translation/protocol.py
# stream options and vllm_xargs only
```

A translation form that sends `file` as text therefore misses the 422 and fails later with a worse error.

## Why

I was comparing the two speech-to-text request validators. Transcription already treated a string `file` as untrusted input. Translation copied the stream-option half of that validator and left the file check out. I added a unit test that calls both `model_validate({"file": "not-a-file.wav"})` and expects the same 422.

## How

Use the same `HTTPException` / `HTTPStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` check at the start of `TranslationRequest.validate_stream_options`.

## Testing

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/test_audio_request_file_type.py -q
```

The parametrized case covers both `TranscriptionRequest` and `TranslationRequest`. The translation case fails on `6865e67` and passes with this patch.

title: [Bugfix][Audio] Restore soundfile-first automatic decoding
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
Speech jobs passed in [AMD build 12635](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12635/list) before [PR #51826](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51826) made TorchCodec the preferred automatic audio decoder. A local GPU `git bisect` identified its merge commit, `6a039f465e37`, as the cause of the `test_long_audio_request` failures in build 12653 on [MI300](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12653/list?jid=01a070cd-0522-4363-a01e-2cf8338d4e38&tab=output) and [MI355](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12653/list?jid=01a070cd-0547-40c5-8a3f-42ffac5cacfb&tab=output). title: [Bugfix] Fix NVFP4 fused SiLU+mul scale allocation and global scale direction
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

Fix two independent bugs in the manual SiLU+NVFP4 fusion producer (`_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_dynamic`, introduced in #51415) that break the `(B200) Kernels Shard 2` lane on main (builds [87376](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87376), [87450](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87450), [87460](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87460)): `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in `vllm::silu_mul_cvt_fp16_to_fp4<__nv_bfloat16, false>` for both `test_nvfp4[flashinfer_cutlass-*]` variants.

**Bug 1 — scale buffer under-allocation (the IMA).** The producer allocated the swizzled block-scale tensor as `(M, ceil(N/64)*4)` fp8 = `M*N/16` bytes, but the kernel writes the tensor-core swizzled SF layout `[numMTiles, numKTiles, 32, 4, 4]`, which requires `round_up(M,128) * round_up(N/16,4)` bytes. For M=1, N=14336 (Llama-3.1-8B intermediate size): 896 bytes allocated vs 114688 written. The OOB writes usually land inside a mapped caching-allocator segment and silently corrupt neighboring tensors (wrong text output in eager mode); when they escape the segment they produce the CI IMA. Fix: allocate the padded swizzled shape, mirroring `create_fp4_scale_tensor`.

**Bug 2 — global scale direction (wrong output once the crash is fixed).** The producer passed `input_global_scale`, but the consumer GEMM's `alpha = input_global_scale * weight_global_scale` only cancels when the activation was quantized with the inverse scale, as the unfused `scaled_fp4_quant` path does (`layer.input_global_scale_inv`). With the wrong direction the GEMM input is off by `input_global_scale^2`. Fix: pass `input_global_scale_inv`.

Existing tests could not catch either bug: the kernel test takes its buffer from `scaled_fp4_quant` (correctly padded) and only uses shapes with `M % 128 == 0` (where both size formulas coincide); the manual-fusion test used `num_tokens=128` and `input_global_scale=1.0` (its own inverse).

## Relation to existing PRs (duplicate-work check)

Searched open PRs for `nvfp4 silu`, `silu_and_mul_nvfp4`, `nvfp4 illegal memory`, `fused_act_quant`:

- #55456 fixes bug 1 with the same approach (reusing the canonical padded allocator) but is a **draft with no Blackwell hardware validation** ("B200 access was unavailable"), and explicitly does not touch bug 2.
- #55505 fixes bug 2 as a side effect of a **larger `InputQuantScales` contract refactor** (8 files), also without SM100+ validation.

This PR is the materially different **minimal combined fix**: both one-paragraph fixes plus regression tests, validated end-to-end on GB200 hardware. It is intended as a fast CI-stopgap; either of the above PRs can land instead and this one can be closed. @khluu and @jjjxia are credited as co-authors since their PRs identified/fixed the same bugs independently.

## Test Plan / Results (GB200, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130)

Kernel + fusion unit tests (on this PR's base, `f43ef1531d`):

```
python -m pytest tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py
=> 54 passed
```

`compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`, direct `torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` call, M=1, N=1048576:
- old allocation: `Invalid __global__ write of size 1` in `silu_mul_cvt_fp16_to_fp4<__nv_bfloat16, false>`, 4132865 bytes past a 65536-byte allocation (same kernel as the CI core dumps);
- fixed allocation: `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`, and dequantized output matches the unfused `scaled_fp4_quant` reference at M in {1, 8, 127}, N=14336.

Model evaluation (the exact CI-failing cases, on GB200):

```
python -m pytest tests/models/quantization/test_nvfp4.py \
  -k 'test_nvfp4 and flashinfer_cutlass'
=> 2 passed   # both variants, previously IMA during warmup
```

pre-commit (ruff check/format, mypy 3.10, sign-off): all pass.

## AI assistance

Kimi Code (Moonshot AI) performed the investigation, implementation, and validation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

Co-authored-by: khluu <khluu000@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: jiahao <jxia77@terpmail.umd.edu>

## CI wiring (so the regression actually runs)

The regression tests only help if CI runs them; verification of the job wiring on main:

- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py` — already run by `(B200) Kernels Shard %N` (shard 0). ✅
- `tests/models/quantization/test_nvfp4.py` — already run by `(B200) Kernels Shard %N` (shard 1; the lane that fails on main). ✅
- `tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py` — **was not collected by any job** (the `(B200) Fusion and Compile` job runs only `test_fusion_attn.py`, `test_mla_attn_quant_fusion.py`, `test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py`, and `distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py`). This PR wires it into that job (B200 hardware, required by its NVFP4 cases) and adds `vllm/model_executor/layers/fusion/`, `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/fp4/`, and the two NVFP4 test files to the relevant jobs' `source_file_dependencies` so future changes to the producer/kernel trigger these lanes.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Take video placeholder timestamps from the pixel path's frame sampler
author: NNNtrance
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55644.

GLM-5.3-Flash video prompts are expanded by one frame sampler and encoded by another.

- **Pixels**: `Glm5NextVideoProcessor.sample_frames` samples with the checkpoint's policy — `fps_interval = 2.0`, `extract_t = int(duration * target_fps)` — and `_preprocess` pads the frame axis to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size` and divides by it to get `grid_t`.
- **Placeholders**: `Glm4vProcessingInfo._construct_video_placeholder` emits one frame of placeholders per *timestamp*, and the timestamps come from `_get_video_second_idx_glm46v`, a second sampler on GLM-4.6V's constants — `DYNAMIC_FPS_THRES = {30: 3, 300: 1, 2400: 0.5}`, `extract_t = int(duration * target_fps * temporal_patch_size)`, then `[::2]`.

`Glm5NextProcessingInfo` moved the pixel half over to the checkpoint's own processor (`get_hf_processor`, `_get_vision_info`, `_get_image_max_pixels`, `_get_video_max_pixels`) but left the timestamp half on GLM-4.6V's. The two samplers agree only for source durations between 30 s and 300 s, where `target_fps = 1` makes `duration * 1 * 2` coincide with `duration * 2`. Outside that window the prompt gets a different number of placeholders than the vision tower produces rows, the counts first meet on the GPU in `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, and the resulting error inside a worker takes the engine core down with it — one malformed request kills the server:

```
models/utils.py:709  RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [1656, 4096]
                     cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [1728, 4096]
models/utils.py:718  ValueError: Attempted to assign 1656 = 1656 multimodal tokens
                     to 1728 placeholders
...                  EngineDeadError
```

A 4 s clip at 8 fps: the pixel path picks 8 frames → `video_grid_thw` `[4, 36, 46]` → 1,656 encoder rows, while the timestamp path yields 12 timestamps → 4,968 placeholders (ratio 3). Past 300 s the error flips sign (ratio 0.5 and lower). The issue has the full sweep.

This PR overrides the timestamp computation in `Glm5NextProcessingInfo` so it samples with the video processor's own policy. The count then becomes structural rather than coincidental: one timestamp per temporal patch is exactly `grid_t` timestamps for any clip, because `_preprocess` pads the frame axis to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size` and divides by it. Only the timestamp *values* come from the sampler, and they keep the existing convention — the first frame of each temporal patch, `int(frame_index / fps)` seconds. The `do_sample_frames=False` branch (loader pre-sampled the frames) takes the count from the delivered frames and the values from `frames_indices`, so it stays exact as well.

Also folded in: a clip too short for the sampler to pick a single frame (`duration * fps_interval < 1`) currently reaches the pixel path with an empty index array and dies on an opaque `IndexError`; it is now a `ValueError` naming the clip, i.e. a rejected request.

Scope is deliberately narrow — one `ProcessingInfo` override plus a test. The issue lists two further findings (`max_pixels` never reaching the video processor, and the `{"video": 1}` supported-limit clamp) and argues that a placeholder/embedding mismatch should be a 400 rather than an engine death; those are separate changes and are not in this PR.

## Test Plan

New file `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py`. It needs no GPU and no checkpoint — both samplers and the canvas geometry are arithmetic, so the video processor is stubbed from its class defaults with `Mock(spec=...)`, as `test_glm4_1v.py` already does for `Glm4vProcessingInfo`.

For each clip it recomputes the pixel path's `video_grid_thw` (`glm_sample_frame_indices` + `smart_resize` + the `_preprocess` padding rule), then asserts `len(timestamps) == grid_t` and `len(timestamps) * tokens_per_frame == grid_t * grid_h * grid_w // merge_size ** 2`, plus that the timestamps are non-decreasing seconds within the clip. Cases:

| clip | pixel frames | `video_grid_thw` | encoder rows | timestamps before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 s @ 8 fps, 640x480 | 8 | `[4, 36, 46]` | 1,656 | 12 (4,968 placeholders) | 4 (1,656) |
| 20 s @ 30 fps, 1080p | 40 | `[20, 78, 138]` | 53,820 | 60 (161,460) | 20 (53,820) |
| 60 s @ 30 fps, 1080p | 120 | `[60, 78, 138]` | 161,460 | 60 (161,460) | 60 (161,460) |
| 301 s @ 30 fps, 720p | 602 | `[301, 42, 74]` | 233,877 | 151 (117,327) | 301 (233,877) |

The 60 s row is the regression guard: it is inside the window where the two samplers already agreed, and the count must not move. Two more tests cover the pre-sampled (`do_sample_frames=False`) branch and the too-short clip.

```bash
pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py
```

## Test Result

```
6 passed
```

Without the fix, 4 of the 6 fail (the three disagreeing clips and the too-short clip); the 60 s case passes either way, as intended.

End to end on a 3-node TP=3 deployment of `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, video prompts that previously killed the engine core on every rank now serve correctly, with `prompt_tokens` matching the arithmetic above (1,656 for the 4 s fixture); single- and multi-video prompts, mixed image+video prompts, temporal ordering in the answers, and speculative-decoding acceptance were all checked and unchanged, with no measurable throughput cost.

Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean at the pinned `v0.14.0`, plus `typos`, `check-spdx-header` and `check-root-lazy-imports`. The remaining pre-commit hooks (notably `mypy`) were not run locally — no GPU-capable build environment here.

- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

title: [Bugfix] Make KV cache and MFU log lines backend-neutral
author: Ianniu123
body:
## Purpose

Three log lines hardcode `"GPU"` regardless of the active backend, which is misleading on
the CPU backend (and on XPU/NPU). This addresses items 1–3 of #55614.

The label is now derived from `device_config.device_type`, which is already resolved at
config construction and available at every call site — no new imports.

**CUDA and ROCm output is unchanged**: `device_type == "cuda"` yields the same `"GPU"`
literal as before, and ROCm reports `device_type == "cuda"` as well.

| site | before | after (CPU backend) |
|---|---|---|
| `v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` | `GPU KV cache size: …` | `CPU KV cache size: …` |
| `v1/metrics/loggers.py` (x2) | `GPU KV cache usage: …` | `CPU KV cache usage: …` |
| `v1/metrics/perf.py` | `MFU: … TF/s/GPU … GB/s/GPU` | `MFU: … TF/s/device … GB/s/device` |

The MFU line is a unit rather than a device label — the underlying calculation divides by
`tp_size`/`pp_size`, i.e. it is a per-rank rate — so `/device` is used instead of a
platform-derived name.

## Scope

Item 4 of the issue (renaming the exported Prometheus metrics
`vllm:estimated_flops_per_gpu_total`, `…_read_bytes_per_gpu_total`,
`…_write_bytes_per_gpu_total`) is **deliberately not included**. Those are public metric
names and renaming them breaks existing scrapers and needs a maintainer decision on a
deprecation/alias path. Happy to follow up separately if wanted.

## Test Plan

Built the CPU backend from source on x86 (AVX2) and captured the three log lines with the
change reverted and applied, on the same machine and same commit:

```bash
FILES="vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py"

git checkout HEAD~1 -- $FILES
vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --enable-mfu-metrics 2>&1 | tee /tmp/cpu-before.log

git checkout HEAD -- $FILES
vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --enable-mfu-metrics 2>&1 | tee /tmp/cpu-after.log
```

## Test Result

**Before** (CPU backend, `device_config=cpu`):

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Anchor Jamba streamed tool arguments to what was sent
author: shoutoutuoadi325
body:
## Purpose

Streaming tool calls with the `jamba` parser lose the start of the arguments when the delta that delivers the function name also carries a complete argument pair.

The name-sending delta updates `prev_tool_call_arr` with everything `partial_json_parser` could complete at that point — including argument keys that were never streamed. The next delta takes the `cur_arguments and prev_arguments` branch and diffs with `extract_intermediate_diff(cur, prev)`, which yields only the new tail (say `', "state": "TX'`). The `{"city": "Dallas` prefix never goes out, so the arguments the client accumulates are not valid JSON, and the end-of-stream rescue in `get_remaining_unstreamed_args()` cannot recover it because the streamed text is no longer a prefix of the expected JSON. Non-streaming requests return the full arguments.

Multi-token deltas of this shape are routine since incremental detokenization buffers output — it is how the single-delta regression fixed in #48852 came about. That fix covers arguments arriving complete in one delta *after* the name; arguments that begin inside the name delta itself were still broken.

Both argument-diff paths now anchor to `streamed_args_for_tool`, the approach `llama_tool_parser.py` already uses:

- the same-tool branch sends `cur_args_json` from the streamed length, with a full flush once the JSON completes, instead of diffing against the previous completion
- the flush when moving to the next tool slices the unsent arguments by streamed length instead of `str.replace`

## Not a duplicate

- #50461 stops tail truncation by reconciling the last diff once the JSON is complete. It does not cover this case: with the prefix lost, `cur_args_json.startswith(streamed + argument_diff)` fails and nothing is sent. I applied its patch on top of main and the new test fails the same way.
- #48709 adds `count=1` to the `str.replace()` scan on the tool-transition flush. This PR replaces that path with length-based slicing (keeping a guarded replace as fallback), which resolves the same corruption; its regression scenario passes with this change.
- #48295 / #48852 handle calls that arrive whole in a single delta, a different failure mode; that limitation (#48294) is unchanged here.

No open issue describes the name-delta prefix loss; happy to file one if it helps tracking.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_jamba_tool_parser.py -q
```

The new test feeds the triggering sequence (name and the first complete pair in one delta, completion in a later delta) and asserts the accumulated arguments parse back to the original dict. Before the fix it fails with `JSONDecodeError` on `', "state": "TX'`.

I also compared the patched and unpatched parser across ~2800 random splittings of single- and parallel-tool outputs (strings, numbers, booleans, null, nested objects, unicode): the patched version produces complete arguments everywhere the unpatched one did, plus ~1700 splittings the unpatched one mangles. The remaining failures are the pre-existing single-blob limitation tracked by #48294.

## Test Result

Run against the v0.28.0 wheel with this parser file applied (main and v0.28 differ in this file only by an import-path move):

```
before:  1 failed, 9 passed   # new test fails, JSONDecodeError
after:  10 passed
```

This change was written with AI assistance; I reviewed every line and ran the tests above myself.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Preserve speculative metrics when coalescing outputs
author: git-jxj
body:
## Overview

Preserve terminal per-request speculative-decoding metrics when a slow DELTA consumer coalesces request outputs.

## Claims

- Keep `CompletionOutput.spec_decode_metrics` from the terminal chunk when merging it with earlier chunks, without changing generated tokens or text.

## Validation

The regression fails on baseline `f0c44cc7d5` with `spec_decode_metrics=None`. The regression, collector/sampling-mask tests, and upstream pooling-error regressions pass: **12 passed, 40 deselected**.

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_outputs.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -k 'request_output or collector or sampling_mask or specialized_pooling_outputs'
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --hook-stage manual --files vllm/outputs.py tests/test_outputs.py
```

All applicable changed-file manual hooks pass, including mypy for Python 3.10–3.13. The human submitter confirmed review of every changed line and personally passing the relevant tests. The unchanged tree at `19660d2a6e` was independently revalidated on the node before this update.

Real GPU validation used Qwen3-0.6B on an RTX 5060 Ti, n-gram speculation with three draft tokens, DELTA output, and a consumer sleeping three seconds between chunks:

| Configuration | Baseline `f0c44cc7d5` | Updated `19660d2a6e` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Terminal speculative metrics | Lost (`None`) | All **93 draft / 77 accepted tokens** retained |
| Generated output | 128 tokens | Identical 128 token IDs and text |

This exercised the real AsyncLLM serving engine with checkout Python source and existing precompiled native extensions (`0.28.1rc1.dev396+g9cd956c7e`), using MRV1 and the PyTorch sampler. HTTP API behavior and rebuilt native extensions were not tested. Current-head `pre-run-check` stops before upstream pre-commit at the contributor authorization gate; upstream CI has not run.

<details>
<summary>GPU reproducer configuration</summary>

Use a local Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, and `.venv/bin/python` with the following AsyncLLM reproducer. The baseline returns `None`; the fix returns the engine's terminal metrics.

```python
import asyncio
from vllm import AsyncEngineArgs, SamplingParams
from vllm.sampling_params import RequestOutputKind
from vllm.v1.engine.async_llm import AsyncLLM

async def main():
    engine = AsyncLLM.from_engine_args(AsyncEngineArgs(
        model="/path/to/Qwen3-0.6B", dtype="bfloat16",
        max_model_len=512, max_num_seqs=1, max_num_batched_tokens=512,
        kv_cache_memory_bytes=256 * 1024 * 1024,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.25, enforce_eager=True,
        enable_prefix_caching=False, disable_log_stats=True,
        speculative_config={"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
                            "prompt_lookup_min": 1, "prompt_lookup_max": 3},
        per_request_spec_decode_metrics="summary",
    ))
    prompt = ("<|im_start|>user\n/no_think\n"
              "Repeat the phrase red blue green fifty times, separated by spaces. "
              "Output only the repeated words.\n<|im_end|>\n"
              "<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n")
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128, ignore_eos=True,
                            output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA)
    try:
        async for output in engine.generate(prompt, params, request_id="slow-delta"):
            if output.finished:
                print(output.outputs[0].spec_decode_metrics)
            else:
                await asyncio.sleep(3)
    finally:
        engine.shutdown(timeout=10)

asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

## Details

`RequestOutput.add(aggregate=True)` appends token data and copies finish state, but misses `spec_decode_metrics`, which is populated only on the terminal completion. Copy its non-null value in that existing aggregation path.

Rebased onto `f0c44cc7d5`, preserving upstream #58975 pooling-error regressions and the sampling-mask behavior from #55935. This PR addresses the remaining terminal-metrics loss. Checked against subsequent main `8442117446`: relevant output/engine/test code is unchanged, and an offline merge is clean with the identical two-file patch. Earlier open-PR searches found no other matching aggregation-metrics fix; #55935 covers the separate sampling-mask behavior.

title: [Bugfix] Honor explicit empty and zero CLI arguments

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Validate SWA coverage at unaligned cache-hit boundaries
author: xijiaat
body:
## Purpose

Prevent an offload cache hit from passing lookup when it lacks an SWA chunk
that GPU block allocation will require. With mixed cache-group granularities,
the common hit boundary can fall inside an SWA CPU chunk. The fixed suffix
window then misses a required chunk on the left, causing
`CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_load()` to assert.

For example, with a 3904-token hit, a 128-token window, 64-token GPU blocks and
256-token CPU chunks, lookup checks chunk 15 but allocation needs chunks 14
and 15. This reproduces without concurrent eviction or transport failure.

Compute the first lookup window from the actual hit boundary, and use the same
coverage when checking in-flight loads. Missing coverage is rejected before
allocation; pending coverage defers. Earlier chunk-aligned candidates retain
their existing window size. Store behavior, transfer code, and the CPU cache
assertion are unchanged. No new configuration or public API.

Related #54914: the assertion matches, but this does not establish the cause of
that historical incident. Duplicate checks found no matching open fix.
#52287 preserves store-side EAGLE replay windows; #55118 concerns verified
full-attention EAGLE tail handling. This patch validates load coverage even
when entries are already absent, including without EAGLE.
#55168 changes a different connector (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`) under DCP;
this fix is for `OffloadingConnector` and reproduces with world size 1.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return all logprobs when completions requests logprobs=-1
author: superdiaodiao
body:
## Purpose

`logprobs=-1` on `/v1/completions` means "return every logprob". The request validator accepts it explicitly (`completion/protocol.py:538-547` special-cases `-1` as valid) and `SamplingParams` expands it to the vocabulary size (`sampling_params.py:818-820`), so the engine computes full-vocabulary logprobs. But the serialization filter is purely `>=`-based:

```python
for i, top_lp in enumerate(step_top_logprobs.items())
if logprob_token_ids or num_output_top_logprobs >= i
```

With `num_output_top_logprobs == -1`, `-1 >= 0` is False, so the comprehension drops every candidate at every position. The client gets HTTP 200 with `logprobs.tokens` and `logprobs.token_logprobs` populated but `top_logprobs == [{}, {}, ...]` — silent data loss, after paying the full-vocabulary compute cost.

The chat handler already handles this correctly (`chat_completion/serving.py:1236-1238`):

```python
if return_all
or top_logprobs == -1
or (top_logprobs is not None and i < top_logprobs)
```

This applies the same rule to completions. One-line condition change plus regression coverage.

**Not a duplicate.** Per the duplicate-work checks in `AGENTS.md`:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "completion logprobs"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "top_logprobs"
gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "completions logprobs -1"
```

The nearest open PRs address different defects: #53722 guards a `KeyError` when the sampled token is missing from top logprobs; #47838 preserves logprobs when `top_logprobs` is *null*; #49320 handles an empty `logprob_token_ids` list. None touches the `-1` path. No open issue reports this.

**Existing coverage gap.** `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py::test_logprobs_minus_one_allowed` asserts only that the *request validator* accepts `-1` (`assert request.logprobs == -1`) — it never inspects the response. The chat side does assert the full-vocabulary result (`test_chat_echo.py:110-131`, `len(top_logprobs) == vocab_size`). That asymmetry is why this survived.

## Test Plan

The defect is in result serialization, so it is reachable without an engine, a model, or a GPU. `_create_completion_logprobs` reads only `self.return_tokens_as_token_ids`, so the test constructs the serving object via `__new__` — the same pattern `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py:625-640` already uses.

Added `test_completion_logprobs_honors_requested_count`, parametrized over `-1`, `1`, `2` against a three-candidate step, next to the existing `-1` validator test.

```bash
cd vllm
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py
```

## Test Result

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py
34 passed in 17.84s

$ .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files <the two files above>
ruff check .......... Passed
ruff format ......... Passed
typos ............... Passed
(exit 0)
```

Negative control — reverting only `serving.py` and keeping the tests:

```text
>       assert len(logprobs.top_logprobs[0]) == expected
E       assert 0 == 3
1 failed, 2 passed
```

Only the `-1` case flips. The `1 → 2` and `2 → 3` cases pass both before and after, so the change is scoped to the broken path and does not alter the normal one.

**Model evals:** not applicable. This changes only how already-computed logprobs are serialized into the HTTP response; it does not touch sampling, the model, or generated token ids. No accuracy or serving-quality metric is affected.

**Environment note:** vLLM publishes no precompiled wheel for macOS arm64, so `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .` is unavailable on this machine. The tests above ran against the source tree in a `uv` venv with CPU torch and the transitive imports installed; they exercise pure-Python serialization and need no compiled kernels. Full-CI confirmation is welcome.

## Open question for maintainers

`logprobs=0` is handled inconsistently between the two endpoints, and I have deliberately **not** changed it here since it would alter existing behaviour:

| value | completions (`num_output_top_logprobs >= i`) | chat (`i < top_logprobs`) |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | keeps 1 candidate | keeps 0 candidates |
| `1` | keeps 2 | keeps 1 |
| `-1` | keeps 0 *(this PR: all)* | keeps all |

OpenAI's completions API documents `logprobs=n` as "the n most likely tokens", so completions returning `n + 1` looks off-by-one — but it is long-standing behaviour that clients may depend on, and `test_completion.py` has cases built around it. Happy to follow up in a separate PR if you would like it aligned.

---

*AI assistance was used for this change.* An agent located the defect by auditing the entrypoints package, drafted the fix and the tests, and ran the commands above. I reviewed every changed line, ran the test suite and the negative control myself, and can defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Preserve large integer tool arguments
author: Woolgathererer
body:
## Purpose

Preserve large integer tool arguments when their JSON Schema type is `number`.

`coerce_to_schema_type` currently sends every `number` value through `float`
before converting integral results back to `int`. Integer-form values above the
IEEE-754 exact range are silently changed. For example:

```text
input:  9223372036854775807
before: 9223372036854775808
after:  9223372036854775807
```

JSON Schema permits integers wherever `number` is accepted, and Python's JSON
encoder can preserve these values exactly. The change therefore tries `int`
first and falls back to the existing floating-point path for decimal and
exponent forms. Existing behavior remains unchanged for values such as `5.0`,
`1e3`, `3.14`, and non-finite inputs.

The shared conversion function is used by the parser engine and directly by the
K2 Horizon tool parser. Regression coverage exercises the K2 Horizon JSON and
XML formats in both streaming and non-streaming modes.

Related to #47179, which discusses Python/Rust tool argument coercion parity.
The Rust number converter already parses valid JSON integer literals without an
intermediate `f64` conversion.

### Duplicate-work check

I checked #47179 and searched open PRs for references to that issue, large
integer tool parsing, number precision, and `coerce_to_schema_type`. No open PR
addresses this precision-loss case. #47203 changes Rust union-type precedence,
and #53729 resolves property schemas inside combinators; neither changes this
integer conversion path.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/tool_parsers tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/tool_parsers tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py -q
```
