title: [Bugfix] Disable sequence parallelism / async TP under batch invariance and add a TP regression test
author: LioEinaudi
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56370.

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` did not prevent `pass_config.enable_sp` / `fuse_gemm_comms` from being enabled. The `SequenceParallelismPass` rewrites `all_reduce + rms_norm` into `reduce_scatter + rms_norm + all_gather` for compile ranges above `sp_min_token_num`; the reduce-scatter goes through the plain PyNccl path whose reduction order depends on which rank owns a token's chunk, i.e. on the batch composition. Measured on 4x RTX PRO 6000 with Qwen3-1.7B: with SP on, 1522/1536 sampled-token logprobs differ between `bs=1` and `bs=64` and greedy outputs change; with SP off all 1536 match.

This PR:
- forces `enable_sp = fuse_gemm_comms = False` with a `warning_once` when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, next to the existing batch-invariance guards in `vllm/config/vllm.py`;
- adds a multi-GPU regression test (`TP=4`, prompts on both sides of `sp_min_token_num`) under `tests/v1/determinism/` that fails on main without the guard and passes with it;
- documents the limitation in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`.

Making the SP reduce-scatter itself batch-invariant (owner-independent reduction order, as `reduce_scatterv` already does for the MoE combine) is left as a follow-up so that SP can be re-enabled under batch invariance later.

## Test Plan

- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k sp -x -q` on 4 GPUs (new test), before and after the change
- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k bs1_vs_bsN` (existing test, unchanged)
- Manual: the repro script from #56370 with `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"sp_min_token_num":64}}'` now logs the warning, keeps SP off, and reports 0 mismatches

## Test Result

Note: with `enable_sp` set, `VllmConfig` currently falls back to the V1 model runner (MRV2 does not support SP yet), so every SP-on measurement above ran on V1; SP-off arms on V2. A forced-V1 SP-off control is bitwise stable (see #56370), so the effect is specific to the SP path. The gate is config-level and runner-agnostic; the SP/batch-invariance interaction should be re-measured once SP lands in MRV2.

Hardware: 4x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, PCIe), vLLM main @ 7470082f5 + this patch, torch 2.13.0+cu130, `TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B`, attention backend `TRITON_ATTN`.

New regression test (batch invariance with SP requested; the guard forces SP off, bs=1 vs bs=64 logprobs bitwise equal):

```
$ pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k with_sequence_parallelism
WARNING [vllm.py:1562] Disabling sequence parallelism and async TP (pass_config.enable_sp / fuse_gemm_comms) when VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT is enabled: the reduce-scatter path is not batch-invariant (see vllm-project/vllm#56370).
PASSED
========== 1 passed, 19 deselected, 14 warnings in 144.62s (0:02:24) ===========
```

Same configuration on main without the guard (from #56370, `enable_sp=True, sp_min_token_num=64`, TP=4): 1522/1536 sampled-token logprobs differ and 17/64 greedy outputs change. With the guard, the standalone repro script from #56370 reports `enable_sp=False`, `logprob_mismatch_tokens=0`, `max_abs_logprob_diff=0.0`.

Existing TP regression (unchanged test):

```
$ VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "bs1_vs_bsN and TRITON_ATTN and 16-16"
PASSED
=========== 1 passed, 19 deselected, 14 warnings in 95.76s (0:01:35) ===========
```

Lint: `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the two Python files.

title: [Bugfix] Carry over queued work when materializing the dedicated stream
author: zhaoguochun1995
body:
# Carry over queued work when materializing the dedicated stream

## Purpose

`vllm.utils.torch_utils.current_stream()` is a getter that *mutates* the current
stream: the first call per thread runs
`torch.cuda.set_stream(torch.cuda.Stream())`. Nothing ties the new stream to the
one it replaces. Pool streams are created with `cudaStreamNonBlocking`
([`c10/cuda/CUDAStream.cpp`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/c10/cuda/CUDAStream.cpp):
`constexpr unsigned int kDefaultFlags = cudaStreamNonBlocking;`), so there is no
implicit ordering with the default stream either. Work already enqueued before
the switch and work issued after it are therefore unordered: a consumer on the
new stream can read a tensor whose producer is still pending on the old one.

Whether the first call happens before any device work is enqueued is decided by
runtime config, not by construction. On the common CUDA path it is early —
pynccl's `_init_communicator` calls `current_stream()` before its warmup
`all_reduce`, and cudagraph capture calls it too — but those are the only things
pinning it. With a distributed backend that does not go through pynccl and
`--enforce-eager`, the first call landed in
`fused_moe/runner/shared_experts.py`'s `self._stream.wait_stream(current_stream())`,
inside the first MoE layer of a warmup forward: the sequence-parallel
`input_ids` produced immediately before stayed on the old stream while MoE
routing consumed them on the new one, reading unwritten bytes and routing on
garbage token ids.

The fix makes the new stream `wait_stream()` the one it replaces. The switch
still happens (the dedicated stream is required for cudagraph capture); this
adds a single cross-stream dependency, once per thread, at a point where the
process is switching streams anyway. No steady-state cost: `current_stream()`
takes the fast path after the first call, and deliberate overlap via
`with torch.cuda.stream(...)` is untouched.

## Not a duplicate

`gh` was unavailable in my environment, so the duplicate check was done through
the same queries via the GitHub search API:

- `is:pr is:open wait_stream` → 6 results: #53997, #51349, #47355, #51117,
  #29288, #45452. All add or move *deliberate* side streams, or fix an unrelated
  CPU-side race; none touch the lazy first switch inside `current_stream()`.
- `is:pr is:open "current_stream" stream ordering` → #53782, #41834, unrelated.
- `is:pr torch_utils current_stream dedicated`, `is:pr "first call" set_stream`,
  `is:issue is:open current_stream race` → 0 results.
- `git log -- vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` shows no prior attempt at this ordering.

## Test plan and results

Hardware disclosure: I have no NVIDIA GPU available. Verification was done on a
vendor accelerator whose platform reports `PlatformEnum.CUDA` and which goes
through this exact branch, so the code path under test is the one being changed,
but **the CUDA-hardware runs still need to come from CI or a reviewer.**

1. Targeted repro of the hazard (single device, `--enforce-eager` equivalent):
   dirty a 256 B block and free it → back up the stream in use with 200 chained
   2048² bf16 matmuls → reproduce the `reorder_token` `index_select` that
   allocates that block → call `current_stream()` (the switch) → read the tensor
   on the new stream with no explicit sync, then run the routing kernel.

   ```
   before: stream 0x0 -> 0x565543daba10  switched=1 stale=1 routed_ok=0
           truth=[0, 1, 2, 3, 60, 61, 62, 63]
           peek =[2816, 2817, 2818, 2819, 2820, 2821, 2822, 2823]
   after:  stream 0x0 -> 0x562057893010  switched=1 stale=0 routed_ok=1
           peek == truth, routing correct, two consecutive runs identical
   ```

   `switched=1` in both arms: the change makes the switch safe rather than
   avoiding it.

2. Real model, TP8, `--enforce-eager`, MoE model with the shared-experts runner:
   with the switch left wherever it lands by default, 13 of 20 warmups faulted
   with out-of-window device reads or silently mis-routed. Forcing the first
   `current_stream()` call into worker init — a vendor-side change that moves the
   switch out of the forward, *not* this patch — made warmup clean and
   completions correct. That run establishes the mechanism and where the first
   call lands; the effect of *this* patch is established by (1).

3. Lint: `ruff check vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` → `All checks passed!`;
   `ruff format --diff` → `1 file already formatted` (ruff 0.14.10).

Not run by me, and worth asking CI for: any CUDA test that exercises cudagraph
capture plus multi-stream overlap, e.g. `tests/compile/` and the
`tests/distributed/` pynccl tests, to confirm the extra dependency changes
nothing on the paths where the switch already happens at init.

## Model evaluation

The change is an ordering fix only; it adds no numerics. On the affected
configuration it turns a silent mis-routing / fault into correct output. No
accuracy delta is expected on configurations where the switch already happens
before any queued work (i.e. everything using pynccl or cudagraph capture),
which is why I did not run a separate eval sweep — say the word if you want one
on a specific config.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Opus, via a CLI agent):
the root-cause analysis, the patch, and the repro script were produced in that
session and reviewed line by line by me before submission. I understand the
change and can defend it in review.

title: [Bugfix][MM] Fix swapped H/W in dummy video profiling inputs
author: hungnnvidia
body:
## Purpose

`BaseDummyInputsBuilder._get_dummy_videos` builds the dummy profiling video with **width and height swapped**:

```python
# vllm/multimodal/processing/dummy_inputs.py (before)
video = np.full((num_frames, width, height, 3), 255, dtype=np.uint8)
```

Every other video code path in `vllm/multimodal/` uses the `(T, H, W, C)` layout, e.g. `rescale_video_size`:

```python
# vllm/multimodal/video.py
_, height, width, _ = frames.shape
```

So for any **non-square** dummy size, the profiling video has H and W transposed, feeding memory profiling / max-token estimation the wrong aspect ratio. Square sizes hide the bug. The sibling `_get_dummy_images` already uses the correct order (`Image.new("RGB", (width, height))`).

Fix is one line:

```python
video = np.full((num_frames, height, width, 3), 255, dtype=np.uint8)
```

## Reproduction (from the real code)

**Before:**
```
requested width=1920 height=1080 num_frames=4
dummy video shape   = (4, 1920, 1080, 3)   (expected (4, 1080, 1920, 3))
downstream height   = 1920 (should be 1080),  width = 1080 (should be 1920)
rescaled 0.5x shape = (4, 960, 540, 3)     (expected (4, 540, 960, 3))
```

**After:**
```

downstream height   = 1080 (want 1080),  width = 1920 (want 1920)
```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][MoE] Avoid uninitialized EPLB state in DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark drafter
author: luoyuctl
body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark startup when EPLB is enabled for the target model.

The target and DSpark draft use different routed-expert topologies (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash target: 384 routed experts; DSpark drafter: 128). When target-model EPLB is enabled, the draft routers inherit `enable_eplb=True`, but the drafter is not registered with a compatible EPLB model state. Its router-level `EplbLayerState` therefore never receives `expert_load_view` / logical-to-physical mappings and profiling fails with:

```text
ValueError: EPLB requires expert_load_view != None
```

## Fix

- Keep EPLB enabled for the target model.
- Apply the override in the shared `load_dspark_model()` path while constructing the draft `ParallelConfig`.
- Use shallow config `replace()` calls only; do not deep-copy the full `VllmConfig` after target-model construction.
- Disable draft EPLB, redundant experts, and elastic EP atomically in the same `ParallelConfig` replacement.
- Preserve the target config and shared runtime/compilation state.
- Add a focused regression test for atomic target/draft parallel-config isolation.

This intentionally disables EPLB for DSpark draft models while leaving target EPLB unchanged. Full heterogeneous target/draft EPLB support belongs in the EPLB multi-model machinery and should be handled separately.

## Validation

Focused regression test:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py
# 1 passed
```

Revalidated on the original 8x NVIDIA H20 environment:

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- TP8 / EP8
- NVIDIA driver: 595.58.03
- CUDA: 13.2
- Target EPLB enabled
- DSpark speculative decoding enabled with 5 draft tokens

Observed after the patch:

```text
Using ['PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends for group 'eplb:0'
EPLB is disabled for the DSpark draft model. EPLB remains enabled for the target model.
EPLB is enabled for MoE part of model /models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
Initialized EPLB communicator: NixlEplbCommunicator.
DSpark draft model loaded: 97 params
Rearranged experts (profile) in 1.09 s.
OpenAI server is ready to accept requests
```

A real completion request succeeded with speculative decoding active:

```text
vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total 5
vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total 25
vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total 16
```

No `deepcopy`/pickling, EPLB-state, CUDA, or EngineCore errors occurred.

For transparency, the H20 runtime validation used the production DeepSeek image with this loader change backported rather than a full binary rebuild of the PR head. The focused regression test was run against the PR implementation.

Model-evaluation impact: not applicable to model numerics or output semantics; this only changes the draft parallel configuration used during DSpark model construction.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open vLLM PRs for `DSpark EPLB DeepSeek V4.1`, `expert_load_view DSpark`, and `expert_load_view EPLB speculative`; no other open PR addresses this startup failure. Issue #50576 concerns SM8x/Ampere DSpark support and is unrelated. Related precedent: #25311 added multi-model EPLB support for MoE speculative models with compatible expert topology.

## Trade-off

The DSpark draft MoE does not receive EPLB balancing with this workaround. The target model remains EPLB-enabled, preserving the primary EPLB benefit while avoiding the startup correctness failure.

## AI Assistance

OpenAI ChatGPT assisted with root-cause analysis, patch drafting, regression-test drafting, and PR text refinement. The submitter supplied the production H20 reproduction environment and failure logs, reviewed every changed line, ran the focused test, and performed the H20 validation described above. AI assistance is also recorded in the commit trailers.

title: [Nano-Nemotron] Fix Nano-Nemotron precomputed multimodal embeddings
author: taneem-ibrahim
body:
## Purpose

Ran into this issue while addressing the mypy fixes for the NO models (#54142). Nano-Nemotron could not correctly consume precomputed multimodal embeddings:

- Tensor-valued `image_embeds` triggered ambiguous tensor truth-value evaluation.
- `video_embeds` was parsed by the model but never routed through the video path.
- Parsed video embeddings would be passed to the vision encoder instead of used directly.

This change uses an explicit `None` check for image embeddings, routes `video_embeds`, and bypasses the vision encoder for precomputed video embeddings.


## Reproducer

```python
import torch

from vllm.model_executor.models.nano_nemotron_vl import NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2

model = object.__new__(NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2)
embeds = torch.arange(64).reshape(2, 4, 8)

for key in ("image_embeds", "video_embeds"):
    outputs = model.embed_multimodal(**{key: embeds})
    print(key, len(outputs), [torch.equal(x, y) for x, y in zip(outputs, embeds)])
```

On Main:

```text
image_embeds: RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor with more than one value is ambiguous
video_embeds: 0 []
```
On this branch:

```text
image_embeds 2 [True, True]
video_embeds 2 [True, True]
```

## Model regression test

Using nvidia/Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Nano-VL-8B-V1 on an H100 with MRV2 explicitly enabled, main and this branch generated identical output:

```text
token_ids: [32, 4382, 3776, 1495, 389, 264, 4251, 4092, 430, 2795, 330, 9906, 11, 15592, 1917, 94093]
text: A simple black text on a white background that says "Hello, AI world!".
```

## Additional Test and Results

```text

2 passed in 1.63s

tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron_vl.py:
96 passed in 77.69s

```

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) assisted with drafting this change

title: [Frontend] Constrain non-strict GLM-4.7 tool calls with a shallow structural tag
author: Dovis01
body:
## Purpose

Fix GLM-4.7-family tool calling when strict tool calling is disabled.

When `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0` and no tool is marked `strict: true`, the glm47 parser currently falls back to unconstrained generation. This means `auto`, `required`, and named tool choices can emit malformed GLM tool-call XML or arguments that do not follow the provided tool schema.

This PR adds a non-strict structural tag for the non-strict GLM tool-calling path. The constraint is built and registered in `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py` (like `kimi_k3` and `hy_v4`, which use the same XML pattern), instead of hand-written grammar rules in the parser file.

The tag constrains the post-reasoning assistant output rather than only the tool arguments. It covers:

- normal assistant text (with GLM structural tokens excluded);
- one or more GLM `<tool_call>` blocks;
- tool names from the request;
- shallow argument typing derived from each tool's JSON schema.

For example, instead of allowing the model to freely generate the native GLM tool syntax, the parser installs a structural tag that constrains the output shape while still allowing normal reasoning and text before tool calls. The thinking prefix stays owned by the engine-side reasoning gate, matching the contract of the existing strict structural-tag path.

### Request handling

`Glm47MoeModelToolParser.adjust_request()` now attaches this tag when:

- tools are provided;
- `tool_choice != "none"`;
- `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING` is disabled;
- no tool is explicitly `strict: true`;
- no structured output / response-format constraint is already present.

Existing strict-tool behavior is unchanged and continues to use the xgrammar `glm_4_7` builtin.

Named tool choice is narrowed to the selected tool (via `normalize_tool_choice`), while `auto` and `required` use the available request tools. Both Chat Completions and Responses API tools are supported, including Responses API namespace tools.

### Structural tag registry builder

`get_glm_4_7_structural_tag` is registered under `"glm_4_7"` in `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py`:

- schema-exact mode (`non_strict=False`, the existing strict-tool path) delegates to the xgrammar `glm_4_7` builtin. The delegation rebuilds the builtin's input protocol from the normalized tools (normalize is idempotent and has already filtered `"forced"` down to the named tool) and is verified byte-identical to the previous dispatch across {auto, required, named} x {strict, non-strict} tool sets (6/6 cases).
- non-strict mode (`non_strict=True`) builds shallow tags from the same composable formats the other vLLM builders use (`TagFormat` / `TriggeredTagsFormat` / `TagsWithSeparatorFormat` / `StarFormat` / `OrFormat` / `AnyTextFormat`): tool names are constrained, argument keys may be omitted / repeated / emitted in any order, values are typed shallowly (strings are raw text excluding GLM structural tokens, other types are bare JSON scalars, enums enumerate), and free text cannot contain GLM structural tokens.

Because the constraint is a regular structural tag, the existing plumbing is reused end-to-end (xgrammar compile path, reasoning gate, spec-decode rollback, bitmask application). No Responses API protocol or serving changes are needed; the diff stays inside the parser and the registry.

## Scope

The change only affects the glm47 parser family when strict tool calling is disabled, plus a mechanical signature extension (`non_strict: bool = False`) for the builders registered in the structural tag registry and the harmony builder.

The existing paths remain unchanged for:
- `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=1`;
- tools with `strict: true`;
- requests with an explicit structured output;
- requests with an explicit JSON response format;
- requests without tools;
- `tool_choice="none"`.

There are no model, scheduler, kernel, sampling, or tokenizer changes.

## Performance

A/B on a GLM-4.7-format model (TP=8 H100, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0`), 12 sequential requests per case; "valid" = structured `tool_calls` returned with no markup leakage:

| Case | main (unconstrained) | This PR (non-strict tag) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required`, valid tool calls | **0 / 12** (raw JSON leaks into `content`) | **12 / 12** |
| `required`, latency median | 0.51 s (garbage output) | 0.41 s |
| `auto`, valid tool calls | 12 / 12 | 12 / 12 |
| `auto`, latency median | 0.36 s | 0.37 s |
| `auto`, decode throughput | 186 tok/s | 185 tok/s |
| `required` streaming TTFT / total (median) | 0.08 s / 0.50 s | 0.08 s / 0.27 s |

Constraint overhead measured offline with the `zai-org/GLM-4.7` tokenizer: tag build ~0.8-10 ms; cold xgrammar compile 12-20 ms (compiled asynchronously in the engine); cached re-compile ~0.1 ms; compiled spec 2.6-15 KiB for 2-12 tools. No measurable latency or throughput regression on the auto path; the required path additionally goes from unusable to fully functional.

## Test Plan

Unit tests (run locally):

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py -q      # 19 passed
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -q    # passed (part of the 315 below)
```

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/ -q   # passed
```

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py \
        tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py \
        tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
        tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py -q                     # 315 passed

pytest tests/parser -q \
  --ignore=tests/parser/mistral \
  --ignore=tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py \
  --ignore=tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py                   # 786 passed

pytest tests/v1/structured_output -q \
  --ignore=tests/v1/structured_output/test_mistral_common_tokenizer.py   # 72 passed
```

Structural-tag validation with the tokenizer via `GrammarCompiler.compile_structural_tag` + `GrammarMatcher`: valid turns (text + tool calls) are accepted; `<tool_call>` markup inside text, wrongly typed argument values (e.g. a string for an `integer` param), invalid enum values, and unknown tool names are rejected; omitted / reordered / repeated arguments are accepted (non-strict semantics); named choice narrows to the selected tool and rejects others; EOS and turn-taking stop tokens stay selectable.

End-to-end (GLM-4.7-format model served with `--tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45`, TP=8 H100, MTP speculative decoding `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0`), 8/8 scenarios pass:

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tool_choice="auto"` non-strict tools | well-formed `tool_calls`, `finish_reason="tool_calls"`, no markup leakage |
| `tool_choice="required"` | well-formed `tool_calls`; e.g. `{"city": "Beijing", "days": 3}` with correct integer typing |
| named tool choice (Chat Completions) | only the selected tool is called, `finish_reason="stop"` per OpenAI semantics |
| named zero-argument tool | zero-arg call parsed as `"{}"` |
| no tools | plain text answer, no markup |
| `enable_thinking=false` | grammar-structural validity: single text block, no `<think>`/`<tool_call>` leakage |
| streaming (SSE) | deltas assemble the same tool call, clean finish |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back and answered normally |

No "Failed to advance FSM" errors appeared in the server logs across all runs.

Note: this change is output-format constrained decoding only (grammar-guided); model weights and sampling defaults are untouched, so no accuracy evaluation delta is expected beyond the format guarantees above.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Preserve selected-token logprob mode
author: alec-flowers
body:
## Summary

Clients can request log probabilities for specific token IDs at each generated position. The Rust gRPC converter always paired those IDs with `logprobs=1`, so requests selecting more than one token failed validation.

For example, requesting scores for two valid token IDs `[100, 101]` produced:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Selected IDs | `[100, 101]` | `[100, 101]` |
| Numeric `logprobs` count | `1` | Unset (`None`) |
| Result | Rejected: count 1 does not match two IDs | Accepted: the engine derives the count from the IDs |

The new behavior matches Python HTTP's selected-token mode. An unset numeric count does not disable scoring when selected IDs are present. It also avoids applying the ordinary top-N limit to selected IDs: for example, 21 selected IDs are valid with `max_logprobs=20`, subject to the separate selected-ID limit and vocabulary checks.

Empty and absent selectors now use `top_n(0)`, returning only the sampled token’s logprob. Numeric top-N requests keep their existing behavior. This aligns request conversion with Python; existing response-rank and batch-padding issues are separate.

## Validation

From `rust/`:

- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-server --lib grpc::convert::tests` — 14 passed; regression fails without the fix.
- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-text --lib logprob` — 7 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Live Qwen3-0.6B checks with paired vLLM 0.29 Python HTTP and a matching Rust backport: all eight gRPC cases pass; 21 selected IDs work with `max_logprobs=20`, and all 42 compared scores match Python within 0.000001 absolute difference.

This fixes Rust gRPC request conversion; related #49320 addresses Python HTTP empty-list validation. AI assistance was used for implementation and independent review.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Restore token limits for offline Jina scoring
author: shaohuaxi
body:
## Purpose

`LLM.score()` with `jinaai/jina-reranker-v3` silently ignores `max_tokens_per_query` and `max_tokens_per_doc` passed through `PoolingParams.extra_kwargs`. Long inputs remain untruncated and can fail the model's input-length check even when these limits are set.

Jina previously inherited this truncation from the bi-encoder's offline preprocessing. It was omitted when [#47699](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47699) moved that path to request factories. Restore it by reusing the existing token-limit validation and truncation helpers before formatting the query and documents, matching Jina's online path. Unset or zero limits retain the current behavior, and custom instructions are preserved.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing Jina unit tests to cover query-only, document-only, and combined limits, unset and zero limits, 1:N and N:N inputs, and invalid limits. Check the resulting prompts, including document order, ranking markers, and the instruction.

Run the focused CPU suite with the repository's parent conftest excluded:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py \
  -q -p no:cacheprovider

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 \
  --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py
```

## Test Result

- Before the fix: **8 failed, 3 passed** with the same test suite.
- After the fix: **11 passed** on macOS with CPU dependencies.
- All applicable pre-commit checks and the separate mypy 3.12 check passed.

Also ran before/after offline end-to-end tests on a single A10 with `jinaai/jina-reranker-v3`, using the real `LLM.score()` path and model weights:

- Covered 12 combinations: 1:1, 1:N, and N:N inputs, each with no limits, query-only, document-only, and both limits. Before the fix, setting limits had no effect. After the fix, prompt token IDs and scores matched a control that manually truncated the input text with the model's tokenizer; the observed score difference was zero. Unrestricted inputs produced identical tokens and scores before and after the fix.
- For the long 1:1 input, setting both limits to 10 reduced the full prompt from 567 to 177 tokens. With `max_model_len=256`, the baseline raised an input-length error; the fixed version completed scoring.
- Custom-instruction checks also passed.

Checked related open, closed, and merged PRs on September 11, 2026; no equivalent fix was found. [#55200](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55200) checks for ranking markers lost during whole-prompt truncation; this change restores query/document truncation before prompt formatting. The changes can be merged independently.

AI assistance: Codex helped with the investigation, implementation, and tests.

title: Revert "[Rocm][Kimi-k3] Fix pipeline_parallel support for the kimik3 DCP mode  (#53664)"
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Purpose

This PR reverts #53664 ("[Rocm][Kimi-k3] Fix pipeline_parallel support for the kimik3 DCP mode"). That PR added a fallback in `MLAAttentionLayer.build()` that derives `dcp_local_seq_lens` from `seq_lens` whenever `CommonAttentionMetadata` does not carry it, together with an assert and two test-registry entries. The fallback is dead code: in vLLM's in-tree paths, `dcp_local_seq_lens` is always populated before the MLA decode path runs whenever DCP is enabled.

Evidence:

- The monolithic V1 model runner populates `CommonAttentionMetadata.dcp_local_seq_lens` unconditionally when `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2456-2466`), and this has been in place since before #53664 was authored.
- The modular model runner (MRV2) does the same via `maybe_prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens()` right before attention metadata is built, after PCP batch partitioning (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1728`, helper in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py`). The helper returns `None` only when `dcp_size == 1`, in which case the MLA layer's `dcp_world_size` is also 1 and the branch is never taken, so the fallback is unreachable.
- Both runners always set `seq_lens` on `CommonAttentionMetadata`, so the assert added by #53664 is likewise unreachable.

Keeping the fallback would also mask future regressions in runner-side population: if a path ever stopped populating `dcp_local_seq_lens`, the layer would silently derive it instead of failing loudly. Removing it restores a single source of truth for DCP-local sequence lengths (the model runner). The two test-registry entries added by #53664 are removed along with the revert.

title: [bug-fix] Fix KV block leak with fault tolerance enabled in P/D disaggregation
author: tiankaijin
body:
## Purpose

Extend the fault tolerance (FT) framework (#44428) to prefill/decode (P/D) disaggregated deployments. When KV transfer is enabled, a worker failure currently causes two problems:

1. **KV transfer progress loss.** When `_model_forward` raises, the exception path discards the `kv_connector_output`, so `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` / `invalid_block_ids` for in-flight transfers are lost. After `retry` recovery, the scheduler's KV transfer bookkeeping no longer matches the actual connector state, and requests can hang or leak KV blocks.

2. **Response queue residue.** In the executor's `get_response`, the first `FAILURE` response raises immediately, without dequeuing the remaining workers' responses. The stale responses left in the MQs are then consumed by the *next* RPC call, corrupting subsequent steps.

Key design:

- **Preserve KV state on failure**: a failed worker's `kv_connector_output` is extracted before the exception is shipped, carried via a new `ExceptionWithKVConnectorOutput` / `ResponseStatus.FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT` status, and deferred into the executor's `KVOutputAggregator`
- **Drain-then-raise**: `get_response` always dequeues **all** workers' responses before raising (this covers all collective RPCs, not just `execute_model`), so no residue is left in the response queues
- **Defer-and-replay**: `KVOutputAggregator.ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs` stashes salvaged outputs; they are replayed through the normal `aggregate()` loop at the next successful step, so pending transfers are correctly reported without any special-case merging logic. Salvaged `kv_cache_events` are dropped (see Details)
- **Consume, don't drop**: on recovery, `EngineCoreSentinel` drains the batch queue and consumes each future's `kv_connector_output` (worker-side connectors use get-and-clear semantics) instead of clearing the queue wholesale
- **No new control flow**: everything rides the existing response MQ, batch queue, and `KVOutputAggregator` mechanisms

### Details

1. **Async output extraction.** `get_kv_connector_output()` is added to `AsyncModelRunnerOutput` and its implementations (v1 GPU runner, v2 `AsyncOutput` / `AsyncPoolingOutput`). In `WorkerProc.enqueue_output`, when `get_output()` raises, the pending `kv_connector_output` is extracted and shipped to the executor as `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT`.

2. **Drain-then-raise in the executor.** In `get_response`, a `FAILURE` / `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT` no longer raises immediately. All workers' responses are dequeued; KV connector outputs (explicit or embedded in successful responses) are stashed via `KVOutputAggregator.ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs`, and only then is the error raised. Stale exception responses from other ranks are dropped. When FT is disabled or the executor has already failed, the original raise-immediately behavior is preserved.

3. **Defer-and-replay in the aggregator.** Salvaged outputs are stashed by `ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs` and replayed through the normal aggregation loop at the next successful `aggregate()` call, so `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` / `failed_recving` / `invalid_block_ids` and worker metadata are preserved exactly as if they had arrived late. Salvaged `kv_cache_events` are dropped at stash time: a dropped event only costs a cache miss until its blocks are stored again, while replaying them could perturb the surviving workers' event quorum (e.g. overshooting LMCache's `count == num_workers` exact-match threshold). `aggregate()` itself is unchanged.

4. **Batch queue drain on recovery.** `EngineCoreSentinel` now drains the batch queue instead of `clear()`ing it: each pending future's `kv_connector_output` is consumed and applied via `scheduler.update_from_output(SchedulerOutput.make_empty(), ModelRunnerOutput.with_kv_conn_output_only(...))` (KV transfer state only -- the rest of the model output is not applied to avoid corrupting scheduler state mid-recovery).

## Test Plan

Unit tests added in this PR:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
    tests/v1/executor/test_executor.py \
    tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_engine_core_sentinel.py -v
```

- `test_output_aggregator.py`: replay of salvaged transfer fields, completion of recv votes, and salvaged event votes never entering the quorum (LMCache exact-match and Mooncake `>=` semantics, including late-live-vote cases)
- `test_executor.py`: drain-then-raise behavior of `get_response` under `FAILURE` / `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT`
- `test_engine_core_sentinel.py`: batch queue drain surfaces `kv_connector_output` and drops failed futures

CI wiring: `.buildkite/test_areas/fault_tolerance.yaml` now runs the sentinel test in the FT pipeline, and `source_file_dependencies` covers `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/` and `vllm/v1/executor/` so aggregator/executor-only changes trigger it.

Manual verification:

**Model**: Qwen3-30B-A3B
**Configuration**: 1 prefill (kv_producer) + 1 decode (kv_consumer), MooncakeConnector, fault tolerance enabled

### Launching the cluster

Each instance runs as a separate `vllm serve` process.

**Prefill instance (producer)** -- GPU 0, port 8010:

```bash
VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
vllm serve <MODEL> \
    --port 8010 \
    --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer"}' \
    --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30 \
    --enable-fault-tolerance \
    --fault-tolerance-config '{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 500}'
```

**Decode instance (consumer)** -- GPU 1, port 8020:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \
vllm serve <MODEL> \
    --port 8020 \
    --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}' \
    --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30 \
    --enable-fault-tolerance \
    --fault-tolerance-config '{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 500}'
```

**Proxy** (routes requests between P and D instances):

```bash
python3 examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
    --prefill http://0.0.0.0:8010 8998 \
    --decode http://0.0.0.0:8020 \
    --port 8000
```

### Simulating faults

To simulate a device-side failure on the decode instance, inject a `RuntimeError` in the forward path, raising at a chosen step on the target rank:

```python
# Fault injection: raise at specific steps
if step_count in [250, 5000]:
    raise RuntimeError("FAULT INJECTION: exception in forward path")
```

### Sending inference requests

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model": "<MODEL>", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 128}'
```

### Querying FT status and issuing recovery

```bash
# Query engine status (one per instance port):
curl -s http://localhost:8010/fault_tolerance/status
curl -s http://localhost:8020/fault_tolerance/status

# Issue retry to both instances after both become unhealthy:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8010/fault_tolerance/apply \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"instruction": "retry", "params": {"timeout": 120}}'
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8020/fault_tolerance/apply \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"instruction": "retry", "params": {"timeout": 120}}'
```

title: [Bugfix][EPD] Preserve explicit multimodal UUIDs with caches disabled
author: gty111
body:
## Summary

Preserve explicit multimodal UUIDs when both prefix caching and processor caching are disabled. Only missing UUIDs receive request-local IDs; other hashing behavior is unchanged.

Currently, disabling both caches replaces even proxy-provided UUIDs with frontend-local IDs, so E and consumer can use different identifiers for the same image. An ECExample cache miss or NIXL announcement lookup miss can then fall through to local encoding. Since the rewritten request contains only metadata, not image tensors, this triggers `Expected multimodal embeddings ... got <class 'NoneType'>` and crashes the consumer engine. Mooncake instead waits for the mismatched identifier and times out.

Unlike #55583, #55616 and #36692, this fixes UUID replacement with both caches disabled, not media-cache lookup or cache-key configuration.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/renderers/test_process_multi_modal_uuids.py tests/renderers/test_multimodal_hashes.py -q`: 14 passed; preservation cases failed before the fix.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/renderers/base.py tests/renderers/test_process_multi_modal_uuids.py`: passed.
- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B EPD image smoke tests (baseline `e4091f34` + fix): ECExample, Mooncake RDMA and NIXL passed producer-only, consumer-only and both-sides cache disabling, mismatched request counters, and two-image requests. Both images were correctly identified; follow-up text requests succeeded. No full benchmark evaluation.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix AITER preshuffled FP8 block-scale kernel
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose

This PR fixes breakages in MLA models on ROCm.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51692 added AiterPreshuffledFp8BlockScaledMMKernel first in the ROCm block-scaled priority list, so DeepSeek-V4/V3/Kimi-K2/many MLA models select it. Four things there lead to incorrect results:
- It reads the activation scale as column-major, while pre-quantizing callers emit row-major scales. Both unfortunately have the same shape `(M, N // 32)`
- The kernel B-preshuffles the weight after loading, and models like DS V4 on ROCm shuffle `fused_wqa_wkv`, `wo_b` and `gate_up_proj` again.
- `wo_a` is a BMM layer whose weight is read by the model directly rather than through the linear kernel, so preshuffling it corrupts the output projection.
- `kv_b_proj` is read by MLA via `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` to build `W_UK` and `W_UV`, so preshuffling it leads to incorrect construction.

In particular, DS V3/R1 is fine at TP1/TP2 but gives incorrect results at TP4/TP8, and Kimi K2 is fine at TP1 but gives incorrect results at TP>2. The general rule here is whether AITER FP8 block-scaled GEMM has tuning entries for the problematic matrices and preshuffle them. The PR tested DS V3 at TP1/DP8, so did not run into the regime where output was corrupt.

DS V4 cannot start on ROCm at all because its `_wq_b_proj` hits `apply_block_scaled_mm` and raises `NotImplementedError`, on top of the other correctness issues mentioned above.

## Test Plan
Test DeepSeek V4 TP8, DeepSeek V3 TP8 gsm8k after the fixes above. The former is also tested as part of the LM Eval (Large Models) test group in AMD CI.

## Test Result
DeepSeek V4 and V3 TP8 gsm8k recover from 0 to 0.9568 and 0.9458 respectively.

---

title: [Bugfix] Align vLLM YaRN with Transformers and stop re-scaling max_model_len
author: hmellor
body:
## Purpose

`_get_and_verify_max_len` reset the derived length to `original_max_position_embeddings` only for the exact string `"yarn"`. YaRN variants registered under another name therefore multiplied an already-scaled `max_position_embeddings` by `factor` a second time, letting requests index past the end of the cos/sin cache:

| model | `rope_type` | before | after |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `Tele-AI/TeleChat3-36B-Thinking` | `telechat3-yarn` | 131,072 | **32,768** |
| `sarvamai/sarvam-105b` | `deepseek_yarn` | 5,242,880 | **131,072** |

## Why the cleanup is bundled

The exact-string check was a symptom of drift from `transformers.modeling_rope_utils._compute_yarn_parameters`, which is why each vendor alias needed its own special case. Realigning with upstream makes both bugs fall out of the general rule:

- Upstream never multiplies `max_position_embeddings` by `factor` for YaRN — adopting that fixes both models and deletes the `"yarn"` reset.
- Upstream has one YaRN implementation, not a class per vendor. `telechat3-yarn` is a copy of upstream's function with `0.1` changed to `0.07`; normalising it to plain YaRN at config load deletes vLLM's duplicate class and puts TeleChat3 inside every `"yarn"` guard.
- Upstream's RoPE keys are the shared vocabulary. vLLM now honours `mscale`/`mscale_all_dim`/`attention_factor`, and drops `attn_factor`/`extrapolation_factor` (dead — nothing set them) and `apply_yarn_scaling` (re-spelled as `attention_factor`, removing an `ignore_keys_at_rope_validation` workaround). Every key in a YaRN `rope_parameters` dict is now a Transformers key with Transformers' meaning.

TeleChat3 uses a precomputed `attention_factor` rather than `mscale: 0.7`, which looks natural but does not round-trip: upstream only consults `mscale` when `mscale_all_dim` is also truthy, so it would compute `1.1386` where vLLM computed `1.0970`. The same re-spelling fixes `mistralai/Mistral-Large-3`, where upstream computed `1.3583` against vLLM's `1.0`; both now say `1.0`, with vLLM's value unchanged.

## Duplicate-work check

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "telechat3-yarn"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "deepseek_yarn max_model_len"
```

This supersedes **#55116** (adds `telechat3-yarn` to the exclusion tuple) and **#56279** (adds `deepseek_yarn`). Both diagnosed the bug correctly for their model; generalising to the whole family with upstream's rule covers both and the next alias, and lets TeleChat3 shed its duplicate RoPE class. Credit to @leex404 and @pushkar-sarvam.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py \
    tests/kernels/core/test_mrope.py tests/kernels/core/test_pos_encoding.py -q
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Two regression tests added, both direct calls with no network: `test_get_and_verify_max_len_yarn_is_already_scaled` (parametrised over `yarn`, `deepseek_yarn`, `deepseek_llama_scaling`, plus a `linear` control) and `test_patch_legacy_rope_type_normalizes_telechat3_yarn`.

## Test Results

- No new failures against `upstream/main`; `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, SPDX) passed.
- New max-len test fails without the fix: `assert 1310720 == 32768`.
- TeleChat3 `cos_sin_cache` is `torch.equal` to the deleted class's; `mscale` exactly `0.07*log(4)+1 = 1.097040605278392`.
- `inv_freq` bit-identical to `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS["yarn"]` (max abs diff `0.000e+00`), and attention scaling equals upstream's `attention_factor`.
- The cleanup commits leave `mscale` unchanged on every path that accepted the removed kwargs (plain yarn, `apply_scale: false`, `attention_factor`, `deepseek_yarn`, mrope+yarn).
- `max_model_len` unchanged for DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2, gpt-oss-120b, A.X-K1, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B; only the two models above move.

## Model evaluation

**Not yet run — needs a GPU run before merge.** The equivalence above is analytic and unit-level. This touches attention scaling and derived context length, so TeleChat3 and an MLA model on the `deepseek_yarn` path should be evaluated before this lands; treat it as unvalidated end-to-end until those results are posted here.

---

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Cap DFlash/DSpark profiling query batch
author: wangyicong52
body:
Fixes #56443.

## Root Cause
The memory-profiling dummy run can hand-build max_num_seqs requests without applying the scheduler's speculative query-token budget. For DSpark/DFlash, each request can require num_query_per_req draft query rows.
For example, with max_num_seqs=512, max_num_batched_tokens=2048, and DSpark K=5, the profiling path asks the speculator for 512 * 5 = 2560 query rows while its input buffers are sized for 2048 rows, so DSpark can read _anchor_idx past input_ids and later surface CUDA IndexKernel/device-side assert errors.

## Changes
Cap the initial dummy/profile draft-generation pass to the largest complete set of query blocks that fits the speculator input buffer, preserve the full target-context and sampler projection for memory profiling, and fail early with a clear ValueError if a real query batch exceeds the input buffer.

Other profiling dummy runs, including FlashInfer autotune, build target attention metadata and cannot use the initial skip-attention shortcut. Add a default no-op speculator hook that lets DFlash-family speculators cap the dummy request count before GPUModelRunner builds those synthetic batches. This does not affect real serving requests or other speculator implementations.

## Existing PRs

#53970 addresses the same `max_num_seqs * parallel-draft query width > max_num_batched_tokens` failure condition with a broader capacity-based fix: it raises `max_num_batched_tokens` to cover the worst-case parallel-draft batch and enlarges the DFlash input buffers. This PR instead leaves the configured target token budget unchanged and caps only synthetic profiling batches to the existing speculator capacity. It covers both the initial skip-attention memory profile and full-attention profiling dummy runs such as FlashInfer autotune, and adds a fail-fast check if a real serving batch violates the scheduler invariant already established by #51256. The approaches are alternatives for the startup crash, but differ in scope and memory/scheduling impact.

#53080 separates target and draft scheduler budgets, but it does not constrain model-runner-generated profiling batches that bypass normal scheduler admission. #53577 covers broader DSpark/PP and padded graph safety work, but it has no matching profile query-buffer cap. #55133 and #56387 address different DSpark failure modes.

## Test Plan

### Common Configuration

- Hardware: 4x NVIDIA H20
- Tensor parallel size: 4
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909`
- CUDA graph mode: `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

```bash
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --moe-backend auto \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","draft_sample_method":"greedy","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2

FlashInfer autotune was left enabled by default.

```bash
vllm serve /data00/models/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8001 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"/data00/models/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Qwen3-8B + DFlash

FlashInfer autotune was left enabled by default.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8001 \
  --served-model-name qwen3-8b \

  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":16}' \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

## Test Result

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Without this PR, startup fails during memory profiling before the API server becomes ready:

```text
/__w/pytorch/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernel.cu:111: operator(): block: [0,0,0], thread: [...] Assertion `-sizes[i] <= index && index < sizes[i] && "index out of bounds"` failed.
RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED when calling `cublasGemmEx(...)`
EngineCore failed to start.
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

With this PR, the service completed profiling, KV cache creation, CUDA graph capture, and API startup. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the logs contained none of the failure signatures above.

### Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2

Without this PR, startup fails during the initial memory profile. DFlash2 tries to process 128 requests with query width 8, requiring 1024 query rows while its input buffer contains only 512 rows. The logs show:

```text
IndexKernel.cu:111: Assertion `... index out of bounds` failed.
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
EngineCore failed to start.
```

With this PR, both the initial memory profile and the default FlashInfer autotune completed, followed by KV cache creation, target/DFlash2 CUDA graph capture, and API startup. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. A 128-concurrency run completed 128/128 requests and generated 2812 completion tokens. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the startup/request logs contained no CUDA, EngineCore, traceback, `ValueError`, or HTTP 500 failure signatures.

### Qwen3-8B + DFlash

Without this PR, the initial memory-profile phase completes, but the default FlashInfer autotune dummy run uses 64 requests with query width 17, requiring 1088 query rows while the input buffer contains only 512 rows. The workers fail with:

```text
CUDA error (.../flash_fwd_launch_template.h:199): an illegal memory access was encountered
EngineCore failed to start.
```

With this PR, the initial profile, default FlashInfer autotune, KV cache creation, target/DFlash CUDA graph capture, and API startup all completed. `/health`, `/v1/models`, and two `/v1/completions` requests succeeded. A 64-concurrency run completed 64/64 requests and generated 2048 completion tokens. The pod remained running with restart count 0, and the startup/request logs contained no CUDA, EngineCore, traceback, `ValueError`, or HTTP 500 failure signatures.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepGEMM FP8 warmup coverage
author: ayush1399
body:
# [Bugfix] Fix DeepGEMM FP8 warmup coverage

DeepGEMM warmup missed compressed-tensors and ModelOpt block-FP8 layers, including block-FP8 ParallelLMHead layers. It also excluded supported weight shapes whose output dimension N is divisible by 64 but not 128. The missed compressed-tensors layers caused kernels to JIT compile during requests in the Gemma run below, producing 10–20 second stalls.

The DeepGEMM linear kernel now registers a warmup provider during weight loading. Warmup uses that provider to find eligible layers and weights. This also covers the FlashInfer dynamic fallback, skips BMM layers, and shares scale lookup through `FP8BlockParams.block_scale`.

## Related work

The duplicate check recorded on 2026-09-11 found:

- #50617 adds ModelOpt-specific lookup. This PR overlaps that fix but replaces attribute probing with kernel registration, also covering compressed-tensors, `ParallelLMHead`, and supported non-128-aligned shapes.
- #49930 addresses BMM/einsum warmup, which this change excludes.
- #41851 skips warmup when DeepGEMM is unavailable.

## Validation

Commands and results from the recorded runs:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k fp8_block -v
```

- Warmup tests: 6 passed on CPU and 6 on H100. Covers both scale names, supported shapes, skipped layers, and provider registration.
- Compressed-tensors: `[auto]` passed; `[marlin]` failed with `cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion` in `marlin_utils_fp8.py`. The recorded cause was a toolchain mismatch: driver 580 supports CUDA 13.0; extensions used 13.3.
- Ruff check and format: clean on all four changed files.

### Serving and model output

Tested `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block` on one H100 80GB with CUDA 13.3, vendored DeepGEMM, and a fresh `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` per run.

| Configuration | Layers warmed | JIT cache entries after load |
| --- | --- | --- |
| This PR, `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=relax` | 240 / 240 | 72 |
| This PR, `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip` | 0 | 51 |
| Main (`3735c2d5f`), `relax` | 0 | 51 |

Warmup took 84 seconds. With warmup skipped, a sweep of 463 prompt sizes found three request-time compilation stalls:

| Prompt tokens | First request | Repeat request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 517 | 12.5 s | 0.05 s |
| 641 | 9.7 s | 0.05 s |
| 785 | 20.0 s | 0.07 s |

All 11 kernels compiled by these requests were present in this PR's warmup cache and absent from main's.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Match fast-prefill padding to active LoRA batches
author: waizuichougou
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Fixes a Model Runner V2 fast-prefill regression for batches containing LoRA
requests.

The main model dispatch and the fast-prefill dispatch must use the same
`num_active_loras` value for a batch. This keeps the LoRA specialization
consistent between the two paths; their token counts may differ because
fast-prefill dispatches a reduced logits batch.

The main model dispatch computes the number of active LoRA adapters, but the
second dispatch in `FastPrefillHelper.prepare()` always used
`num_active_loras=0`. A batch with an adapter could therefore select a
no-LoRA CUDA graph descriptor for fast-prefill, even when the main model path
selected an eager or LoRA-specialized descriptor. The resulting padded logits
metadata could have a different token shape from the actual model input.

Pass the active-LoRA count from the main dispatch into fast-prefill so the
reduced logits dispatch uses the same LoRA specialization and computes padding
for its own token count. The production fix is limited to three worker files
(`+14/-3` lines); the remaining changes are regression coverage (`+61` test
lines).

## Test Plan

- Add a regression test that simulates a captured no-LoRA graph and an eager
  active-LoRA batch, verifying that fast-prefill forwards the active-LoRA
  count and does not add unrelated padding.
- Exercise 42 combinations of logits token counts (1 through 128) and active
  LoRA counts (1, 2, and 4).
- Run `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py` and
  `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py`.
- Run an end-to-end Gemma 4 E2B mixed batch with one base-model request and one
  rank-8 LoRA request while fast-prefill and CUDA graphs are enabled.

## Test Result

Before the fix, the regression setup selected an 8-token no-LoRA descriptor
for an active-LoRA batch whenever the no-LoRA graph was available. Across 14
token counts and 3 active-LoRA counts (42 combinations), the old choice
differed from the active-LoRA choice in 39 cases. With the fix, all 42 cases
forward the active-LoRA count and match the main dispatch's LoRA
specialization.

Tests pass:

```
70 passed, 14 warnings
```

Ruff and whitespace checks pass.

The Gemma 4 E2B mixed-batch run completed CUDA graph capture and generated
outputs for both requests (one without an adapter and one with the dummy
rank-8 adapter). This exercises model initialization, LoRA registration,
request batching, fast-prefill preparation, and graph dispatch together.

The regression is a dispatch/metadata shape error, so the worker test checks
the `BatchExecutionDescriptor` contract directly while the mixed-batch run
verifies execution through the real model path.
