title: [Bugfix] Avoid repeated dummy initialization and random CPU Engram fills
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

Avoid repeatedly initializing descendant weights under `--load-format dummy`. The loader already walks `model.modules()`, so each iteration now initializes only local parameters and persistent buffers. This matches default PyTorch state selection without recursively revisiting descendants and preserves parameter attributes used for dummy initialization.

CPU-offloaded DeepSeek V4.1 Engram tables request constant dummy weights of 1.0 and UE8M0 scale byte 127 (scale 1.0). Their lookup access pattern does not require randomly generated table contents. Checkpoint loading is unchanged; online quantization retains its existing materialize/initialize/process path.

Duplicate checks found #54958, which addresses full-size FP8 temporary allocations and OOM. This PR addresses recursive duplicate initialization and CPU Engram constant initialization; it contains no generic FP8 allocation or chunking changes. No open PR addressing the same changes was found in the dummy initialization/loading searches.

## Test Plan

Run the existing checkpoint-sharding, nonpersistent alias-buffer, and online-processing tests:

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py -k 'online_processing_waits_for_late_registered_bias or head_shards_reconstruct_checkpoint or layerwise_reload_skips_non_persistent_parameter_alias_buffers' -q
```

Pre-commit was run on all three changed source files.

## Test Result

10 existing tests passed (101 deselected) in 5.26 seconds on the isolated PR branch. Applicable pre-commit hooks and git diff --check passed.

A standalone differential audit found exact old/new initialized values for nested and tied weights and persistent buffers. Tied parameter identities and nonpersistent alias buffers were retained; nonpersistent scratch buffers were unchanged and None tensors skipped. Tied parameters can still be visited under multiple owners: the change removes ancestor-level repetition, not all storage aliasing.

Development measurement on four GB200 GPUs with dummy weights and FlashInfer autotuning disabled: model loading completed in 19.66–19.80 seconds per worker; health returned HTTP 200 after 514.145 seconds and a 16-token smoke request succeeded. The previous run remained in dummy initialization at its 600-second cutoff. The development run also included separate mHC JIT and generic FP8 temporary changes, so its end-to-end time is not an isolated benchmark of this PR. No real-checkpoint accuracy evaluation was run.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation, and validation.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Initialize Ray NIXL agents for sharded RDT
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Add a shared ROCm initializer that creates Ray's process-local NIXL agent through vLLM's existing `nixl_rocm` loader and populates Ray's cached agent.
- Call the initializer in both the producer actor and inference worker before NIXL memory registration, keeping transport compatibility in the sharded RDT implementation.
- Reuse an existing agent, leave non-ROCm initialization unchanged, and report a clear error when the ROCm NIXL package is unavailable.

[PR #50922](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50922) extends AMD CI coverage and exposed a failure in the final sharded RDT example in [Buildkite build 88592](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/88592/list?jid=01a098e8-e816-48fd-b7dd-c7a96e7ad377&tab=output), on both the initial attempt and its retry. Ray 2.56.1 creates its NIXL agent by importing `nixl._api`, while the ROCm installation provides `nixl_rocm._api`. The evidence points to a transport integration gap exposed by the added coverage, rather than a regression in the tiny DeepSeek model.

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this PR description.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Normalize single-channel audio to 1D
author: Woolgathererer
body:
## Purpose

Mono audio with an explicit channel dimension can fail in Whisper preprocessing.
For example, passing a `(1, 16000)` waveform at 16 kHz through the offline audio
tuple path raises `ValueError: Failed to apply WhisperProcessor`, while the same
samples in a `(16000,)` array work.

`normalize_audio` returns early when the input channel count already matches
the target, leaving a 2D array for mono input. This also makes
`AudioProcessorItems.get_audio_length()` report 1 instead of 16000.

Return the only channel as a 1D waveform when the target is mono. Extend the
existing NumPy, Torch and parser tests to cover both channel layouts and the
single-sample case.

This reproduces without resampling. #47693 changes the order of normalization
and resampling, #56023 addresses unsupported multi-channel reduction, and
#51022 optimizes downmixing. Their current patches leave this early return
unchanged.

## Test Plan

Run the audio and parser tests on CPU:

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
export PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONPATH=.

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_audio.py \
  -k 'mono_passthrough_for_numpy or mono_passthrough_for_torch or parser_mono_passthrough' -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/multimodal/test_audio.py tests/multimodal/test_parse.py \
  -k 'not torchaudio and not resampling_with_channel_normalization_e2e' -q

SKIP=actionlint .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/multimodal/audio.py tests/multimodal/test_audio.py
```

Also compare the same one-second WAV in `(16000,)`, `(1, 16000)` and `(16000, 1)`
layouts through vLLM's Whisper multimodal processor, using the official
`openai/whisper-tiny` configuration, tokenizer and feature extractor.

## Test Result

- Focused regression cases: **8 failed, 3 passed before; 11 passed after**.
- Audio and parser selection on main `fa1b3b1922` plus this patch:
  **71 passed, 1 skipped, 8 deselected**.
- Whisper preprocessing: both 2D layouts failed before. After the fix, all
  three layouts produce exactly equal features, prompt tokens and placeholder
  ranges. Feature shape is `(1, 80, 3000)` and parsed audio length is 16000.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Actionlint was skipped; no workflows changed.

The local environment has no matching torchaudio build. An earlier full audio
test run had 55 passes and 7 failures due to that missing dependency; the
filtered run excludes those cases and the default-backend assertion. The
skipped parser test requires CUDA. Whisper validation covers CPU preprocessing;
model generation and accuracy evaluation have not been run.

AI assistance was used, and I reviewed all the changes and tests.

title: [Bugfix] Fix stale HPC QK-norm weights after weight refit
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

`HpcRopeNorm` kept float32 mirror Parameters (`qnorm_weight` / `knorm_weight`) of the
`q_norm` / `k_norm` weights. They were filled by `process_weights_after_loading()`, and that
hook was dispatched **only** by the generic `HpcModule` loop in
`model_executor/model_loader/utils.py`, which runs at cold start.

No reload path reaches that loop:

| path | dispatcher | reaches the HPC loop? |
|---|---|---|
| `base_loader.load_model` | `utils.process_weights_after_loading` | yes (cold start only) |
| `weight_cache/ipc_loader` | same | yes (cold start only) |
| `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` | `initialize/finalize_layerwise_reload` | **no** |
| NCCL / IPC / sharded-RDT weight transfer | same | **no** |
| `wake_up` after sleep | CuMemAllocator restore | **no** |

`layerwise.py` only dispatches `process_weights_after_loading` for layers carrying a
`QuantizeMethodBase` and for deferred attention layers. `HpcRopeNorm` is neither, so after an
RL weight refit the fused kernel consumed **pre-refit** QK-norm weights — silently, with no
error and no warning.

### Fix

Build `q_norm` / `k_norm` in float32 when the HPC path is active, and have the kernel read
them directly. No derived copy means nothing to refresh, on any load path. The checkpoint is
untouched (still bf16) — `default_weight_loader` casts on `param.data.copy_()`.

### Cleanup bundled in (not a fix)

`HpcIHCPre` / `HpcIHCHead` bound owner weight *aliases* in the same hook. Those aliases do
survive refits (verified empirically, see Test Result), so their forwards now read the owner
attributes directly purely to remove the last reason for the hook to exist. With no
`HpcModule` needing it, the three overrides, the base no-op and the loader loop are deleted
(4 `process_weights_after_loading` mounting points → 3).

The two failure modes are different and it matters:

| | what was cached | after a refit |
|---|---|---|
| `HpcIHCPre` / `HpcIHCHead` | an **alias** to the owner's Parameter | pointer unchanged, alias still valid |
| `HpcRopeNorm` | an independent `copy_().float()` **duplicate** | nobody refreshes it → stale values |

An alias follows its owner because layerwise reload's `_copy_and_restore_kernel_tensors`
copies in place and `_place_kernel_tensors` re-registers the original Parameter objects.
A duplicate does not.

## Test Plan

```bash
# lint (all hooks, changed files)
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD)

# unit
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -v -m "not slow_test"
```

New test `test_hpc_rope_norm_kernel_sees_refit_norm_weights` drives the production
`_forward_impl` with a recording `hpc` stub and asserts the kernel receives the refit Q **and**
K weights, float32, same storage.

End-to-end on GB200 (sm100) with Tencent **hpc-ops** built from source, HY4
(`HYV4ForCausalLM`, `enable_ihc: true`, `hc_mult: 4`, `hidden_size: 6144`), three arms —
`base`, `base2` (same code as `base`, to establish the run-to-run noise floor), `pr` — plus a
deliberately perturbed arm as a positive control.

## Test Result

**Unit** — `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -m "not slow_test"`, run inside
`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (aarch64, GB200):

| | result |
|---|---|
| without this PR | 27 passed, 2 failed |
| with this PR | **28 passed, 1 failed** |

`test_hpc_rope_norm_kernel_sees_refit_norm_weights` **FAILS without the change and PASSES with
it** — it is the new test, and it does catch the bug.

The one remaining failure, `test_kv_scale_reload`, fails identically with and without the
change; it is pre-existing in that image and unrelated.

Applying only this PR's `utils.py` deletion (the `HpcModule` loop + its import) on top of an
otherwise untouched tree gives byte-identical results to not applying it, confirming the
removed mounting point is inert for every non-HPC path.

**Lint** — `pre-commit run --files <changed>`: all hooks pass. (mypy initially flagged
`rope_norm.py:398-399 Item "None" of "Any | None" has no attribute "weight"` — the same latent
crash the removed `fallback_qnorm is not None` guard used to prevent. Fixed by validating the
invariant in `__init__` with an explicit `ValueError` and narrowing at the use site.)

**End-to-end, HY4 on GB200 / sm100** — the HPC gate fires: `HpcIHCPre: 8`, `HpcIHCPost: 8`,
`HpcIHCHead: 1`, `gated_mla_layers: 4`, identical across arms, so the changed code really is
executed.

`process_weights_after_loading` mounting points, read off the live model:

```
base: ['HpcIHCHead', 'HpcIHCPre', 'MLAAttention', 'UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod']
pr:   [                           'MLAAttention', 'UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod']
```

Exactly the two HPC hooks are removed; the other mounting points are untouched.

Output equivalence — greedy, fixed prompts, token ids compared one by one:

| | vs base |
|---|---|
| pr (cudagraph) | **8/8 identical** |
| pr (eager) | **8/8 identical** |
| base2 (same code, control) | 8/8 identical |
| **positive control** (`hc_fn.weight * 1.01` on the changed line) | **6/8 diverge**, first at token 56 |

The positive control is what makes the 8/8 meaningful: the same test does detect a
perturbation on the very line this PR touches.

Throughput, batch 256 × 512 output tokens, 7 reps, median:

| mode | pr vs base | same-code noise floor (base2) |
|---|---|---|
| cudagraph | +0.16% | +0.15% |
| eager (run 1) | +1.21% | +0.05% |
| eager (run 2) | +2.91% | **+2.47%** |

In eager run 2 the *same code* (`base2`) moved +2.47%, so the apparent gain tracks arm
ordering (warm-up), not the change. No measurable difference in either mode, which matches the
mechanism — a handful of extra attribute lookups per forward.

Refit-alias validity, `reload_weights` on the `base` arm (the claim that the iHC cleanup is
not a fix):

```
modules holding a cached alias: 9  (8x HpcIHCPre + 1x HpcIHCHead)
alias still points at the live weight after reload: 9 / 9
sample pointer before -> after: 26843826176 -> 26843826176   (unchanged)
generation identical after reload: 6 / 6
```

Confirms the alias half is genuinely cleanup.

**GSM8K on the full 78-layer model** — the 4-layer slice I first used has no
discriminating power (every arm, including a deliberately sabotaged one, scores 0.000 with
`invalid_rate=0.985`), so I pulled the full `tencent/Hy4-preview` (131 shards, 1.5 TB bf16) and
re-ran on 4 nodes / 16 GPUs, TP=4 x PP=4 with expert parallelism, via
`distributed_executor_backend="external_launcher"`:

| | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `fused_modules` | `HpcIHCPre: 156, HpcIHCPost: 156, HpcIHCHead: 1` | identical |
| `gated_mla_layers` | 78 | identical |
| greedy output, 8 prompts | — | **8/8 token-identical** |
| **GSM8K accuracy (500 q, 5-shot)** | **0.5660** | **0.5660** |
| GSM8K invalid_rate | 0.0120 | 0.0120 |

156 = 78 layers x 2 iHC boundaries per layer, so the changed path is exercised on every layer.
`invalid_rate` drops from 0.985 on the slice to 0.012 here, i.e. the model is actually
answering and the score is meaningful. Accuracy is identical between the arms.

(0.566 is the raw-completion score without a chat template; it is used only for the A/B
comparison, not as a claim about the model's ceiling.)

### Not verified

**sm90 + HY3 + `HPC_ATTN` refit.** `HpcAttentionBackend.supports_compute_capability` is
`capability == DeviceCapability(9, 0)`, so the actual fix (`HpcRopeNorm`, `hy_v3.py`) cannot be
exercised on sm100 at all — my cluster is GB200 only. What I verified end-to-end is the iHC
cleanup half plus the mounting-point removal. I'd appreciate the Tencent hpc-ops authors (or
anyone with H100/H800) running an sm90 refit-consistency check; the script must **fail on
`main`**, otherwise it isn't exercising the bug.

### Reproducing the hpc-ops build

hpc-ops ships no wheel (no GitHub release, nothing on PyPI), and building it inside
`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` needs three environment fixes unrelated to this PR:

1. PyPI is throttled on some clusters — prefetch build deps and install with `--no-index`.
2. The image has no `git`, and `hpc-ops/setup.py:get_version()` shells out to it for a short hash.
3. CUDA headers come from the `nvidia-*-cu13` wheels, so `cusparse.h` is not under
   `/usr/local/cuda/include`; torch's `ATen/cuda/CUDAContextLight.h` fails to include it.
   `export CPATH=<site-packages>/nvidia/cu13/include`.

## Known limitation

Sharded-state artifacts saved by an older build contain the retired
`hpc_rope_norm.qnorm_weight` / `knorm_weight` keys; `ShardedStateLoader` indexes `state_dict`
by checkpoint key and raises `KeyError`. Regenerate the artifact.

Worth noting this swaps the direction of an existing incompatibility rather than introducing
one: on `main`, loading a sharded artifact saved *without* HPC into an HPC-enabled build
already fails, because those two keys stay in `state_dict` and hit
`raise ValueError(f"Missing keys {tuple(state_dict)} in loaded state!")`. I chose not to touch
the shared loader from an HPC PR — happy to add a narrow tolerance here or as a prerequisite PR
if maintainers prefer.

## Follow-ups deliberately left out of this PR

- `HpcRopeNorm.__init__` could also reject a non-float32 `fallback_qnorm.weight`. The fp32
  contract now lives with the caller (`hy_v3.py`), and `hy_v3` is the only in-tree caller, but
  nothing checks it for the next model that wires up `HPC_ATTN`.
- After this PR nothing does `isinstance(x, HpcModule)` anymore, and the base class is reduced
  to `support()` returning `True` plus a `pass` `forward()` — both overridden by every
  subclass. It is arguably dead and could be dropped.

---

Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses HPC QK-norm staleness across weight reload
(searched `vllm-project/vllm` for `HpcRopeNorm`, `hpc qk norm refit`,
`process_weights_after_loading refit`; the only nearby open PR, #47443, changes HPC attention
decode split-K selection). RFC #54477 is the umbrella for selective weight reload in RL.

AI assistance was used for this change. Every changed line was reviewed by me, and I ran the
lint, unit and end-to-end runs reported above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Restore MTP-retained sliding-window history
author: jacklin78911-collab
body:
## Purpose

Fix native KV offload restoring MTP-retained sliding-window blocks that lookup never checked and the producer may never have stored. Implements the conservative coverage option discussed in #56701.

For example, with a 64-token external hit, SWA block size 16, window 32, and three extra retained tokens, lookup checks chunks 2–3 while allocation also restores chunk 1. If chunk 1 is absent or still being written, `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_load()` asserts after the hit has already been admitted. Hybrid store pruning can itself omit chunk 1.

Include `extra_retained_tokens` in aligned/partial lookup coverage, the existing in-flight-load check, and producer store reachability. Preserve the base coverage lower bound so retaining one extra token does not unnecessarily request another chunk. The store mask uses a temporary coverage spec; actual attention windows, allocation, cache keys, and transfer ownership are unchanged. Restoring the required older blocks can increase CPU cache usage and transfer volume.

Duplicate checks on 2026-09-13 found no open PR for `56701 in:body` or `extra_retained_tokens offload`. #55818 handles allocation scaling and #53499 page-size normalization; neither fixes this lookup/store mismatch.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing scheduler tests to cover retained history at aligned and unaligned hybrid boundaries, EAGLE tail handling, missing/pending/loading chunks, and a producer followed by a cold GPU-cache consumer. The consumer only hits keys actually stored by the producer.

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result

- Related suites: **474 passed** locally. Native H20: **378 passed**, then the remaining **96 passed** with `--lf` after seeding the missing public `facebook/opt-125m` config/tokenizer cache and enabling offline mode; no code changes.
- Focused regressions: **102 passed**. With only the production file reverted to base `de500290ffffeb7bd834872c0dea5331590dd40d`: **14 failed, 88 passed**.
- Pre-commit, including mypy 3.10, and the explicit mypy 3.12 hook: passed.
- Tiny Step3.5 smoke with two MTP modules, four speculative tokens, SWA window 32 / extra retention 3: both RTX 4060 V1 and native H20 V2 restored **64 cached tokens / 7 chunks**, with **16/16 identical cold/warm output tokens**.
- H20 V2 instantiated `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`; the unmodified proposals exercised **30 decode calls with four rejected drafts**, entering the three-token re-prefill path. A separate controlled draft-rejection check also passed the restore/output assertions.

V1 used Python 3.12.13 / PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130; H20 V2 used Python 3.12.14 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 with UVA available. Compiled extensions were reused, and both changed source files on H20 were SHA-256 verified against `1e89fa93a662a321e29860f3f30a25a362070fc8` (the reused environment's package version metadata identifies the older build).

These GPU checks use tiny dummy weights, BF16, eager mode, and disabled optional JIT warmup. They validate the serving/re-prefill paths for this configuration. **Trained-model quality, acceptance rate, and performance have not been evaluated; no throughput improvement is claimed.**

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the H20 V2 functional smoke</summary>

Save the script below as `../tiny_mtp_v2.py` relative to the checkout and run:

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 \
  .venv/bin/python ../tiny_mtp_v2.py
FORCE_DRAFT_REJECTIONS=1 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 \
  .venv/bin/python ../tiny_mtp_v2.py
```

The temporary model directory below is generalized from the executed script.

```python
"""Tiny Step3.5 two-module MTP, real GPU kernels and CPU offload transfers."""
import os
os.environ['VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING']='0'
os.environ['VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER']='1'
import json
from pathlib import Path
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.step3p5 import Step3p5Config
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import SlidingWindowSpec

model_dir=Path('/tmp/vllm-offload-mtp-smoke')
Step3p5Config(hidden_size=128, intermediate_size=256, num_attention_heads=2,
    num_attention_groups=1, head_dim=64, num_hidden_layers=2, vocab_size=256,
    max_position_embeddings=256, max_seq_len=256, sliding_window=32,
    num_nextn_predict_layers=2, moe_layers_enum='1', moe_num_experts=2,
    moe_top_k=1, moe_intermediate_size=128, share_expert_dim=128,
    architectures=['Step3p5ForCausalLM']).save_pretrained(model_dir)
llm=LLM(model=str(model_dir),skip_tokenizer_init=True,load_format='dummy',
    enforce_eager=True,dtype='bfloat16',seed=42,max_model_len=256,
    max_num_seqs=2,max_num_batched_tokens=256,gpu_memory_utilization=0.25,
    kv_cache_memory_bytes=16<<20, block_size=16,enable_prefix_caching=True,
    disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=False,compilation_config={'mode':0},
    kernel_config={'enable_jit_warmup':False},
    speculative_config={'method':'mtp','num_speculative_tokens':4},
    kv_transfer_config={'kv_connector':'OffloadingConnector','kv_role':'kv_both',
        'kv_connector_extra_config':{'cpu_bytes_to_use':16<<20}})
try:
    core=llm.llm_engine.engine_core.engine_core
    cfg=core.vllm_config
    assert cfg.speculative_config.use_multi_module_mtp()
    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.multi_module_mtp.speculator import MultiModuleMTPSpeculator
    runner=core.model_executor.driver_worker.worker.model_runner
    speculator=runner.speculator
    assert isinstance(speculator,MultiModuleMTPSpeculator),type(speculator)
    proposal_trace=[]
    force_rejections=os.environ.get('FORCE_DRAFT_REJECTIONS')=='1'
    original_propose=speculator.propose
    def track_propose(*args,**kwargs):
        batch=kwargs.get('input_batch',args[0] if args else None)
        rejected=kwargs.get('num_rejected',args[6] if len(args)>6 else None)
        proposal_trace.append({'has_prefill':bool(batch.has_prefill),
            'num_rejected':rejected[:batch.num_reqs].tolist()})
        drafts=original_propose(*args,**kwargs)
        if force_rejections:
            drafts.fill_(75)
        return drafts
    speculator.propose=track_propose
    connector=core.scheduler.connector.connector_scheduler
    specs=[g.kv_cache_spec for g in connector.config.kv_group_configs]
    assert any(isinstance(s,SlidingWindowSpec) and s.extra_retained_tokens==3 for s in specs)
    load_keys=[]
    original_load=connector.manager.prepare_load
    def track_load(keys,ctx):
        keys=list(keys)
        load_keys.append(len(keys))
        return original_load(keys,ctx)
    connector.manager.prepare_load=track_load
    prompt={'prompt_token_ids':list(range(10,75))}
    params=SamplingParams(temperature=0,max_tokens=16,ignore_eos=True)
    cold=llm.generate([prompt],params,use_tqdm=False)[0]
    for _ in range(1000):
        if not core.scheduler.has_requests(): break
        core.step()
    assert not core.scheduler.has_requests()
    assert llm.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=False)
    warm=llm.generate([prompt],params,use_tqdm=False)[0]
    assert cold.outputs[0].token_ids==warm.outputs[0].token_ids
    assert warm.num_cached_tokens>0 and load_keys
    assert any(not call['has_prefill'] for call in proposal_trace)
    if force_rejections:
        assert any(max(call['num_rejected'])>1 for call in proposal_trace)
    result={'proposal_trace':proposal_trace,'force_draft_rejections':force_rejections,
        'speculator_class':type(speculator).__name__,'cold':cold.outputs[0].token_ids,'warm':warm.outputs[0].token_ids,
        'cached_tokens':warm.num_cached_tokens,'load_chunk_counts':load_keys,
        'kv_specs':[str(s) for s in specs],'weights':'dummy',
        'mtp_modules':2,'speculative_tokens':4,'model_runner':'V2'}
    Path('../tiny_mtp_v2_rejection_result.json' if force_rejections else '../tiny_mtp_v2_result.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps(result))
finally:
    llm.llm_engine.engine_core.shutdown()
```

</details>

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, testing, and this description; the commit includes attribution.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Complete FSE fixture R-SWA contract
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fix the H200 Model Executor regression introduced by #56305.

That PR made `get_attn_backend()` read `model_config.rswa_window`, but the focused FSE model-construction fixture still builds a minimal `SimpleNamespace` without that field. Main build [#88651](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/88651#01a09b47-c668-4e25-a3cd-342c156b6511) therefore failed all 12 applicable `test_models_fse_init` cases with `AttributeError` after 709 other tests passed.

Add the non-R-SWA default to the fixture contract. This does not change production behavior.

The culprit PR's exact build #88637 and immediate post-main build #88647 both left H200 Model Executor blocked, so neither exercised this fixture before the next main commit selected it.

This change was prepared with AI assistance and manually reviewed against the exact failing log and introducing diff.

## Test Plan

- Run applicable pre-commit hooks on the changed file.
- Collect the complete focused test file locally.
- Run the exact H200 Model Executor lane in CI; the host-only MXFP4 kernels make the 12 failing model-construction cases unavailable on this CPU machine.

## Test Result

title: [Bugfix][Gemma 4] Don't read fft_length when profiling unified audio
author: averma12
body:
## Purpose

`Gemma4DummyInputsBuilder.get_dummy_mm_data` reads `processor.feature_extractor.fft_length` unconditionally to size the dummy audio item:

```python
if num_audios > 0:
    audio_len = processor.feature_extractor.fft_length
```

`Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor.__init__` sets `self.fft_length`. `Gemma4UnifiedAudioFeatureExtractor` defines no such attribute, so the unified (encoder-free) Gemma 4 variant fails during memory profiling, before the engine finishes starting:

```
AttributeError: 'Gemma4UnifiedAudioFeatureExtractor' object has no attribute 'fft_length'
```

## Why it is latent rather than always-on

The line is only reached when audio is the modality with the largest per-item token count, because `compute_mm_encoder_budget` takes a `max()` over `get_mm_max_tokens_per_item` and profiles that one modality alone. With the shipped defaults audio loses:

| modality | per-item tokens |
|---|---|
| image | 280 |
| audio | 750 (`audio_seq_length`) |
| video | 2496 (32 frames x 78) |

Video wins, the dummy video branch runs, and the audio line never executes. So a default deployment boots fine.

It stops booting as soon as `audio_seq_length` is raised above the video budget — which is exactly what you do to serve audio longer than 30 s on this variant, since `_compute_audio_num_tokens` ends in `return min(t, audio_seq_length)` and the mel framing yields 25 tokens/s, so 750 tokens is 30.0 s. Raising the ceiling makes audio win the `max()`, the profiler switches to the audio branch, and the engine no longer starts.

## The change

```python
feature_extractor = processor.feature_extractor
if isinstance(feature_extractor, Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor):
    return feature_extractor.fft_length

sampling_rate = feature_extractor.sampling_rate
max_duration_s = processor.audio_seq_length * processor.audio_ms_per_token / 1000.0
return int(max_duration_s * sampling_rate)
```

`audio_seq_length` and `audio_ms_per_token` are the same pair this file already uses to warn about over-long audio in `_call_hf_processor`, so the dummy item is sized to the worst case the model will actually accept. Behaviour is unchanged for `Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor`.

## Test Plan

Two unit tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py`:

- an extractor that is not a `Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor` sizes the dummy audio from the declared budget (3000 tokens x 40 ms at 16 kHz = 1,920,000 samples);
- a `Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor` subclass still returns its `fft_length`.

## Test Result

Please treat this section as a statement of what I could and could not run.

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both changed files.
- The two new tests have **not** been executed. The environment I have does not ship `transformers.models.gemma4`, so that test module cannot even be collected here, and CI on this PR has not run — `pre-run-check` gates it on a label or four merged PRs, and I have neither.
- What I did verify directly is the branch logic, by evaluating `_dummy_audio_num_samples` in isolation against both shapes: the fallback returns `1,920,000` for a 3000-token budget at 16 kHz, and the `fft_length` path returns its value unchanged.

An earlier revision of this description said the tests pass. That was wrong and I have corrected it rather than leave it standing.

## Note for reviewers

Using `fft_length` as a *sample count* for the dummy audio looks questionable on the tower path too — it is an FFT window size (`2 ** ceil(log2(frame_length))`, so typically a few hundred samples), which makes the dummy item far shorter than the audio the model accepts and profiling reserves correspondingly little. I have deliberately not changed that here, to keep this PR to the crash. Happy to follow up separately if maintainers agree it is worth addressing.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Ignore descales for unquantized AITER caches
author: dongluw
body:
## Problem
`ROCM_AITER_FA` passes the attention layer's K/V scale tensors to AITER decode kernels even when the KV cache is unquantized. If those otherwise-unused tensors contain non-neutral values—for example, stale values left by dummy-weight initialization after loading real weights—AITER treats them as descales and corrupts attention output. In our MI300X reproduction, this reduced the post-reload InfoVQA score from the expected `0.952` to `0.000`.

## Solution
- pass null K/V descales to ROCm AITER decode kernels for unquantized KV caches
- preserve expanded descales for FP8 KV caches
- construct expanded descales only in unified-attention branches, avoiding unused eager tensor views in ordinary paged-attention decode
- add a ROCm backend correctness test with non-neutral scale tensors on an unquantized sliding-window cache

## Why this is not duplicate work
I searched open vLLM PRs for `AITER unquantized descale`, `ROCM_AITER_FA KV scale reload`, and `dummy weights attention scale` and found no PR addressing this behavior. [#53823](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53823) concerns prequantized FP8 attention and does not change descale handling for unquantized caches.

## Test plan
- [x] manual pre-commit hooks on the changed backend and test — passed, including Ruff and mypy for Python 3.10-3.13
- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py::test_rocm_aiter_fa_unquantized_cache_ignores_kv_scales -v` on MI300X — 1 passed in 14.62s after the hot-path refactor
- [x] MI300X model evaluation with the equivalent backend change: InfoVQA reload score improved from `0.000` to `0.952` (4/4), with both CUDA graph recaptures succeeding

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and validate this change. I reviewed the resulting changes and test results and can explain the implementation end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Stop dummy draft decode steps from writing KV through stale block-table rows
author: ivanium
body:
## Purpose

Fix a KV-cache corruption in Model Runner V2 speculative decoding under data parallelism: an idle DP rank's dummy batch runs the drafter's multi-step decode, which computes real slot mappings through the *persistent* per-slot block tables using `idx_mapping = arange(num_reqs)` (real request-state slots whose rows are stale), and writes drafter-layer K/V into offsets `1..k-1` of the first block of whatever request last occupied those slots. Those blocks are typically already registered in the prefix cache, so every later request that hits them reads corrupted drafter K/V while the target model's K/V stays intact.

Observed on GLM-5.2 (glm_moe_dsa, MTP k=5, DP=4 EP, prefix caching) as a per-request, exactly-zero MTP acceptance (`p0 = 0.0000`, `acc_len = 1.0`, `drafts == max_tokens`) that latches onto a conversation and disappears after `POST /reset_prefix_cache`; the poisoned rows were NaN (fp8 `0x7F`) in `model.layers.78.self_attn.attn`, with the target layers and indexer cache of the same block clean. On current main the same stale write still happens on every idle step (the written values happen to be finite there, so acceptance is unaffected), i.e. the write path is latent.

#49757 protected the read side (`get_dummy_block_tables` zeroes `input_block_tables`) and the target's dummy slot mappings are PAD (`prepare_dummy_attn`), but `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` reads `block_table_ptrs` (the persistent tables), which neither protection covers.

## Fix

- `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`: a row with `idx_mapping < 0` (dummy or CUDA-graph padding request) emits `PAD_SLOT_ID` and never dereferences a negative block-table row.
- `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.propose(dummy_run=True)`: mark every dummy row with `idx_mapping = -1` (already the speculator's convention for padded rows, ignored by `gumbel_sample`).

The guard lives in the kernel rather than in Python because the fused multi-step path re-runs `compute_slot_mappings` inside the captured CUDA graph between draft steps; only the kernel can neutralize a replayed dummy run.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py::test_dummy_request_slot_mapping_is_pad` (new): `idx_mapping == -1` yields all-PAD slot mappings; a real row still resolves through its block table.
- End-to-end on 4x GB200 with GLM-5.2 NVFP4, DP=4 + EP, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'`, prefix caching on, fp8 KV, block 64, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs (the production decode geometry), driven by a growing-prefix multi-turn probe plus a unique-prompt load/probe "transition hunt":
  - f94666b60d unpatched: hunt trial 1 flips DEAD; 4/4 dead requests hit the same poisoned first block, all healthy requests on that rank do not; dumped drafter K/V rows 1-4 of that block are NaN.
  - f94666b60d + this fix: semantic gate passed, 3x20 chain requests 0 dead, 6/6 hunt trials 0 dead (mean p0 0.61-0.76); 66,164 dummy draft decode steps logged, every slot mapping PAD.
  - main dc07f1638f + this fix: semantic gate passed, 3x20 chain requests 0 dead, 6 hunt trials 0 dead; the dummy draft steps log `slots=[-1]`.

## Test Result

```
$ pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py      # GB200, main + fix
10 passed
$ pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/multi_module_mtp/speculator.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py
all hooks passed
```

End-to-end reproducer (4x GB200, GLM-5.2 NVFP4, DP=4 EP, MTP k=5, prefix caching, fp8 KV, block 64, FULL_DECODE_ONLY):

| tree | chain probe (3x20) | transition hunt | dummy draft slots |
|---|---|---|---|
| f94666b60d (production) | 0 dead | trial 1 DEAD (1/6, then 1/6 and 2/6 on confirm) | real slots; poisoned block rows 1-4 NaN |
| f94666b60d + fix | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | 66,164 steps, all PAD |
| main dc07f1638f | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | real slots (finite values) |
| main dc07f1638f + fix | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | all PAD |

The acceptance metrics above (mean p0 0.61-0.79 in every healthy run) double as the model-quality check: the change only affects dummy batches, and the semantic gate (answer planted at the prompt tail) passed in every run.

## Notes

- Duplicate check: `gh issue list`/`gh pr list` searches for the dummy-run / stale block table / draft KV path found no existing report; the closest related changes are #49757 (read-side zeroing) and #55458 (excludes DP padding rows from draft attention metadata; likely why the written values are finite on main).
- A follow-up could make read and write sides share one source by computing slot mappings from the per-batch gathered `input_block_tables`; this PR is the minimal, backportable fix.
- AI assistance: this change was investigated and drafted with Claude Code and reviewed with Codex; the submitter has reviewed every line and run the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Measure complete pooling responses
author: taneem-ibrahim
body:
## Purpose

Pooling benchmarks recorded E2E latency as soon as response headers arrived. JSON responses were subsequently consumed during parsing, but binary `bytes` responses were never consumed, so their reported latency excluded response transfer and the connection could be closed while the server was still writing. The newer `bytes_only` format was also treated as JSON and every request failed.

This change consumes the complete response before recording latency. Binary bodies are drained incrementally without retaining the embedding payload in memory. The existing metadata header remains the source of token usage for `bytes`; because `bytes_only` intentionally has no metadata, it falls back to the benchmark's client-side prompt length.

## Reproducer

Start an MRV2 pooling server:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  vllm serve intfloat/e5-small-v2 \
  --runner pooling \
  --dtype float16 \
  --max-model-len 512 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --port 8911
```

Run the benchmark once per encoding format:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-embeddings \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8911 \
  --model intfloat/e5-small-v2 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 128 \
  --random-output-len 1 \
  --num-prompts 32 \
  --max-concurrency 8 \
  --extra-body '{"encoding_format":"bytes_only"}'
```

Replace `bytes_only` with `bytes` or `float` to exercise the other response paths.

## Output on main

A direct main-versus-branch invocation of the request helper against the same live MRV2 server produced:

```text
main float success= True latency_ms= 15.603 prompt_len= 4 error=
main bytes success= True latency_ms= 8.372 prompt_len= 4 error=
main bytes_only success= False latency_ms= 8.671 prompt_len= 0 error= 200, message='Attempt to decode JSON with unexpected mimetype: application/octet-stream', url='http:
```

A deterministic server that sends headers immediately and delays its body by 250 ms also showed that main reported only header latency and abandoned the binary body:

```text
float success= True reported_latency= 0.0017 wall= 0.2526 prompt_len= 7 error=
bytes success= True reported_latency= 0.0005 wall= 0.0006 prompt_len= 7 error=
bytes_only success= False reported_latency= 0.0008 wall= 0.2534 prompt_len= 0 error= 200, message='Attempt to decode JSON with unexpected mimetype: application/octet...
```

## Output on this branch

```text
branch float success= True latency_ms= 12.401 prompt_len= 4 error=
branch bytes success= True latency_ms= 12.815 prompt_len= 4 error=
branch bytes_only success= True latency_ms= 12.648 prompt_len= 2 error=
```

The same deterministic delayed-body check now includes the full transfer time for all formats:

```text
float success= True reported_latency= 0.2525 wall= 0.2526 prompt_len= 7 error=
bytes success= True reported_latency= 0.2512 wall= 0.2513 prompt_len= 7 error=
bytes_only success= True reported_latency= 0.2513 wall= 0.2513 prompt_len= 11 error=
```

`bytes_only` prompt-token accounting is intentionally client-estimated because that wire format omits server metadata; this does not affect request success or latency.

## Test Plan

```bash
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -q
# 18 passed in 0.81s
```

MRV2 E2E sweep:

| Endpoint | Format | Requests | Result |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `/v1/embeddings` | `float` | 32 | 32 passed, 0 failed |
| `/v1/embeddings` | `bytes` | 32 | 32 passed, 0 failed |
| `/v1/embeddings` | `bytes_only` | 32 | 32 passed, 0 failed |
| `/pooling` | `float` | 16 | 16 passed, 0 failed |
| `/pooling` | `bytes` | 16 | 16 passed, 0 failed |
| `/pooling` | `bytes_only` | 16 | 16 passed, 0 failed |

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix DeepSeek-R1 (FP8 MLA + MoE) correctness on CPU backend
author: bigPYJ1151
body:
## Purpose

Fixes two independent bugs blocking `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1` (and any other DeepSeekV3-routed / FP8 MLA model) on vLLM's CPU backend.

1. `CPUExpertsFp8._supports_routing_method` didn't allowlist `RoutingMethodType.DeepSeekV3`, so the model fails to load with `ValueError: Unsupported FP8 MoE backend: NONE`.
2. `CPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.process_weights_after_loading` didn't honor `layer._cpu_skip_gemm_dispatch` (set by MLA's "absorb" optimization on `kv_b_proj`), so it unconditionally VNNI-prepacked the FP8 weight bytes for AMX BRGEMM. `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` then dequantized those prepacked bytes as if still row-major, scrambling `W_UK`/`W_UV` against mismatched per-block scales — producing incoherent garbage output. `UnquantizedLinearMethod` already honors this flag for bf16 checkpoints; this brings the FP8 kernel in line.

## Test Plan / Results

- Root-cause isolation: built a real-weight-truncated 4-layer DeepSeek-R1 and compared vLLM CPU layer-by-layer hidden states against HF transformers on the same weights. A bf16-dequantized control run matched HF at cos_sim=1.0000; with FP8, divergence was isolated to attention output specifically (cos_sim ~0.25-0.48 pre-fix, its norm ~15x too small), confirming the bug was FP8-specific and inside MLA's kv_b_proj handling.
- `examples/basic/offline_inference/generate.py --dtype=bfloat16 --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 --enforce-eager` (TP=4): garbage output pre-fix; coherent, factually correct output post-fix (e.g. "The capital of France is" -> "Paris").
- Full GSM8K accuracy eval (`lm_eval`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1`, TP=4, torch.compile enabled, full 1319-example test set, `apply_chat_template=True`, `fewshot_as_multiturn=True`, greedy decoding): `exact_match,strict-match=0.8795` (stderr 0.0090), `exact_match,flexible-extract=0.9568` (stderr 0.0056).

title: [Bugfix][EPD] Preserve media processing options in encoder requests
author: jiangkuaixue123
body:
## Purpose

The EPD proxy drops per-request media processing options when constructing encoder primer requests. An encoder can therefore use the default image size while PD applies the requested override, producing incompatible embeddings and placeholders. With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, the pre-fix proxy reproduced an HTTP 500 and `Attempted to assign 54 = 54 multimodal tokens to 475 placeholders`.

Forward `mm_processor_kwargs`, `media_io_kwargs`, `priority`, and `session_id` to each encoder request when present. Preserve the encoder-reported hash as the key for connector handles so NIXL consumers can find handles after processing options derive a new hash. Extend the existing HTTP round-trip test to cover requests with and without these options, derived encoder hashes, streaming, optional prefill, and decode retries.

Related to #52409 (not closing the umbrella tracker).

Duplicate-work checks: reviewed #52409 and its comments, searched open PRs referencing it and EPD/media-processing keywords, and inspected related changes. #50164 and #55842 address the Rust frontend; #56242 addresses shared encoder output reuse; #54176 adds dynamic proxy registration/routing. None implements this encoder-primer field forwarding fix. #56657, which introduced the existing HTTP round-trip coverage, is already merged.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Keep transient checkpoints out of prefix-cache eviction
author: Sy0307
body:
## Summary

Keep transient KDA/Mamba prefill checkpoints out of the ordinary prefix-cache eviction set when sparse retention is explicitly active.

This change targets Kimi-K3's hybrid attention path.

## Problem

FlashKDA creates internal checkpoints so the current prefill can continue from a recurrent-state boundary without an additional scheduling step. A checkpoint in the middle of a prompt is useful to the current request, but it is not necessarily a reusable shared-prefix boundary.

Before this change, such a checkpoint could be re-keyed and registered as a normal prefix-cache block. It then participated in the same GPU LRU eviction pool as reusable hot prefixes:

```text
middle checkpoint -> hash -> prefix-cache LRU -> evicts hot prefix
                                             -> later local hit becomes a miss
                                             -> extra load or prefill work
```

Before/after cache lifecycle:

```text
Before:

  KDA prefill
      |
      +--> temporary checkpoint
      |        |
      |        +--> hash + ordinary LRU
      |                     |
      |                     +--> competes with hot prefix
      |                                  |
      |                                  +--> local prefix miss

After:

  KDA prefill
      |
      +--> temporary checkpoint ------------------> current request can use it
      |                                              |
      |                                              +--> no ordinary LRU entry
      |
      +--> shared-prefix-boundary checkpoint ------> reusable prefix cache
                                                     |
                                                     +--> may be retained/shared
```

This is particularly problematic when `prefix_cache_retention_interval == 0`: intermediate checkpoints are not intended to be retained as dense semantic checkpoints, but their temporary hash could still make them eviction candidates.

## Fix

Pass the active retention interval into checkpoint publication. When sparse retention is active and the checkpoint is neither at the end of the prompt nor at the shared-prefix boundary, treat it as request-local state:

```text
middle checkpoint -> current request may use it
                  -> temporary hash is removed
                  -> no ordinary prefix-cache LRU entry
                  -> reusable hot prefixes remain protected
```

Prompt-end and shared-prefix-boundary checkpoints retain the existing publication behavior. This change does not disable KDA checkpoint computation or change the state written by FlashKDA.

## Performance

On a representative B200 Kimi-K3 hybrid workload using TP8/PP2/direct DCP8, the isolated production-style comparison was:

| Configuration | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: |
| Checkpoint disabled (diagnostic baseline) | 1013.00 tokens/s |
| Checkpoint enabled with transient-checkpoint retention fix | 1091.80 tokens/s |

The fixed configuration improved throughput by 7.78% over the checkpoint-disabled diagnostic baseline while retaining the internal checkpoint feature. A separate run with the GEMM-AR option disabled measured 1108.89 tokens/s; that result is included only as context and is not an isolated measurement of this patch.

These measurements are workload-specific and are not used as a claim that this small cache-lifecycle change explains every difference between software stacks. The primary regression signal is the cache-manager reproduction: temporary checkpoint publication changes which blocks compete in the local prefix-cache eviction pool.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- PR #55760 changes the default sparse/dense retention policy for Mamba + EAGLE; this change keeps the explicit sparse-retention behavior but fixes transient checkpoint publication.
- PR #56615 fixes MooncakeStore boundary pairing between Mamba/KDA and attention KV; this change is limited to local prefix-cache block retention.
- PR #56525 guards cache hits until the writing scheduler step is committed; this change addresses eviction eligibility, not write visibility.
- PR #52527 adds observability for sparse-retention misses; this change modifies the cache lifecycle.

## Validation

Focused prefix-cache tests should be run with:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
```

The change is intentionally small and preserves the current-request checkpoint path. Model-scale performance validation is still required on a representative hybrid KDA workload.

This change was prepared with AI assistance; the author should review the complete diff and test results before merging.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Skip non-prefix-cacheable groups in SimpleCPUOffload (GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail and QSA)
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash carries a kpool-tail scratch group (`KpoolTailSpec`, `prefix_cacheable=False`, `block_size=index_kpool=4`) next to prefix-cacheable groups that hash at 1152 tokens on this box (MLA 1152, 4× Mamba 1152 in `align` mode). Core (`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, `KVCacheManager`) and the `MooncakeStore connector` already skip such groups. `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` did not, and treated every KV cache group as offloadable:

- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` views the request hashes at each group's block size to build `BlockStored` metadata. For the tail group that is `resolve_block_hashes(hashes, hash_block_size=1152, block_size=4)`, which trips the divisibility assert as soon as `--kv-events-config` enables KV cache events. The engine dies on the first prefill store.
- `update_state_after_alloc` maps external (CPU-hit) tokens onto the scratch group and asserts alignment against its block size, although the coordinator never returns hit blocks for it.

This PR records which groups take part in offloading (`prefix_cacheable`) and skips the rest in eager store selection and in load pairing. Scratch blocks never carry a hash, so nothing is stored or loaded for them either way; the scratch slot in the per-group hit tuple stays empty, exactly as the coordinator leaves it.


## Duplication check

Two open PRs touch the same code path: #55033 (draft since 2026-09-02, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA ring, also adjusts `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) and #56404 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gates `resolve_block_hashes` in the store path only, currently conflicting). This PR is scoped to the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool-tail layout and adds what neither of them covers: a regression test for the actual crash trigger (`enable_kv_cache_events=true`, `BlockStored` emitted for cacheable groups only) and an end-to-end store/load + accuracy check on GLM-5.3-Flash. Happy to fold the test into #55033 instead if the maintainers prefer to land that one. #54743 applies the same scoping to the *OffloadingConnector* (`build_offloading_config`) and does not touch `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload`; the two are complementary.

## Test Plan

Unit:

```
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
    tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py -q
```

E2E: GLM-5.3-Flash, 4× GB300, TP4 + EP, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 32768`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` with 16 GB pinned host memory per rank, `--kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events":true,"publisher":"zmq"}'`, dev endpoint `/reset_prefix_cache` used to evict the GPU prefix cache between runs (`?reset_external=true` also clears the CPU pool).

## Test Result

E2E store/load (10,277-token prompt, greedy, 32 new tokens):

| step | GPU prefix hit | connector hit |
|---|---|---|
| fresh | 0 / 10277 | 0 / 10277 |
| same prompt again | 9216 / 10277 | 0 / 1061 |
| after `/reset_prefix_cache` | 0 / 10277 | 9216 / 10277 |
| after `/reset_prefix_cache` again | 0 / 10277 | 9216 / 10277 |

Hits are 1152-aligned (the Mamba/MLA block); the kpool tail block is a fresh per-request scratch block at every resume, as with a GPU hit.

Accuracy (4 natural-text prompts built from `docs/`, 3.4k–24k tokens, `max_tokens=16`, greedy, `logprobs=20` at the first generated position; every case compared against the first fresh run of the same prompt):

| case | top-1 \|Δlogprob\| mean / max | mean \|Δlogprob\| over shared top-20 | max \|Δlogprob\| | identical 16-token greedy output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh again (no cache at all) | 0.10 / 0.25 | 0.42 | 2.06 | 3 / 4 |
| GPU prefix hit | 0.13 / 0.31 | 0.27 | 1.03 | 2 / 4 |
| CPU (connector) hit | 0.11 / 0.16 | 0.28 | 0.91 | 3 / 4 |
| CPU hit, second time | 0.11 / 0.12 | 0.32 | 1.88 | 3 / 4 |

The CPU-hit deltas sit inside the band that two *fresh* recomputations of the same prompt already show on this model/backend (the fresh-vs-fresh spread is not caused by this PR; it is present with the connector disabled as well, see the `fresh again` row), so the offload round trip adds no measurable error over a plain GPU prefix hit.

AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude Code (analysis, patch, tests and the reproduction scripts); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above.

title: [Bugfix][SparseMLA] Fix piecewise cudagraph capture crash in index group
author: JaredforReal
body:
## What

Fix an engine-startup crash when a sparse-MLA model captures decode batches with **piecewise** cudagraphs (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash, a hybrid KDA + sparse-MLA model):

```log
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 133, in _convert_once
    self.side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

Full startup traceback (4x GB300, TP4, `load_format=dummy`; identical with real weights, the capture path does not read weights):

```log
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 988, in profile_cudagraph_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 920, in profile_cudagraph_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 456, in capture
File "vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 206, in add_eager
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 1483, in unified_mla_attention_with_output
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py", line 736, in _convert_logical_to_physical_topk
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 95, in convert_logical_to_physical_topk
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 133, in _convert_once
    self.side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

## Root cause

`SparseMLAIndexGroup` overlaps the logical→physical topk conversion with the compute stream via the `logical_topk_ready` event: the indexer records it on the compute stream after computing topk, and `_convert_once` waits on it on the side stream.

In piecewise cudagraph mode the indexer runs **inside a captured graph segment**, while the consumer runs in the following **eager break** (`unified_mla_attention_with_output` is an `@eager_break_during_capture` point, executed by `add_eager()` after the segment's `capture_end()`). An event recorded during stream capture is graph-local; waiting on it eagerly is `cudaErrorInvalidValue`.

Minimal reproduction of the exact pattern (no vLLM involved):

```python
g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(g):
    ev.record(torch.cuda.current_stream())   # inside capture
side.wait_event(ev)                          # eager, after capture -> invalid argument
```

Why only some models: FULL cudagraph capture (non-hybrid sparse MLA, e.g. DeepSeek-V3.2 decode) records and waits in-graph, which is legal; prefill-sized batches take the workspace-overflow branch of `_convert_once`, which never touches the event. Hybrid models like GLM-5.3-Flash capture decode batches piecewise and hit the crash during `profile_cudagraph_memory`.

## Fix

In piecewise mode, skip the event entirely: `set_logical_topk_ready` does not record (a record inside a capture segment would be graph-local and unusable anyway), and `_convert_once` orders the side stream with `wait_stream(compute_stream)` — identical to the existing `has_indexer=False` path, and correct because the convert is always invoked after the indexer on the same compute stream. FULL/eager modes keep the fine-grained event. The same guard is applied to the HiSparse copy stream. Adds `in_piecewise_cudagraph()` to `forward_context.py`.

## Tests

- New regression test (record inside captured segment + convert in eager break under `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`); fails pre-fix at `index_group.py:133` with the production error, passes post-fix:

  `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k piecewise_capture`

- Sparse MLA subset (convert / index_group / piecewise / hisparse): 47 passed

  `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "convert or index_group or piecewise or hisparse"`

- E2E on 4x GB300, GLM-5.3-Flash real weights, TP4: engine starts with cudagraphs enabled (crashed at startup before), generation works.

## Model evaluation

GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on 4x GB300 (this branch, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, no speculative decoding): **91.8%** accuracy (invalid rate 0.0%).

## Notes

- Bisect: the crash starts with #53781, which introduced the side-stream + `logical_topk_ready` event for the topk conversion (before it, the convert ran on the compute stream with no event). Verified empirically: its parent commit starts cleanly, it crashes at engine startup. Purely informational for locating the change — the piecewise interaction was easy to miss.
- Duplicate check: no open PR covers this crash; #54851 is a different piecewise-mode issue (KV-cache writes baked into captured graphs for DSA models on multi-node TP).
- AI assistance: developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code); all changes reviewed and tested by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Bound unanswered P2P lookup waits
author: jacklin78911-collab
body:
## Purpose

Addresses the unanswered-lookup portion of #56823. After a P2P handshake succeeds, a peer that keeps its transport alive but stops answering `LookupMsg` leaves the consumer returning `RETRY` indefinitely. The server's pending-lookup timeout cannot help when its serving loop stops progressing.

Start a 30-second progress deadline when the first unanswered lookup batch is sent for a request. A response that resolves a previously unanswered probe rearms that request's deadline while other probes remain pending. Repeated scheduler polls, additional keys, duplicate responses and unknown keys do not extend it. Completing all probes, fetching the matched prefix, or finishing the request clears the deadline. Unsent probes wait for `ConnectAckMsg` before their response deadline starts.

Each poll drains buffered messages and completed transfers before checking lookup expiry. Deferred store results are drained after transfer finalization, including jobs whose supplied blocks were not fetched. This preserves timely replies read by a delayed scheduler and returns completed load/store results before teardown. The warning identifies the peer, the expired request and elapsed time without progress. This is a progress timeout observed by the scheduler, not a per-key age limit or a transport-arrival timestamp guarantee.

### Session failure policy

An expired lookup sends a best-effort `DisconnectMsg` before marking the **whole peer session** dead, allowing the peer to retire its old session before reconnecting. Existing manager teardown converts unresolved requests to `MISS` for local prefill, retains their failure markers until request completion, and releases session resources. Other outstanding work on that same peer also fails through the existing disconnect path; completed results from the current poll are preserved. Maintainer agreement on retaining this session-wide policy is still requested. A request-local timeout would leave the same stalled peer available for subsequent requests to wait on again.

### Issue scope

This PR does **not** bound the pre-handshake `ConnectAck` wait. #51504 covers that path and is still open as of this revision. #56823 must remain open until both failure paths are addressed; this PR has no automatic issue-closing keyword.

The wire format and model computations are unchanged.

## Duplicate-work checks

The original submission checked #56823 and its comments and searched open PRs for `56823 in:body`, `P2P lookup`, `P2P lookup timeout`, and `P2P connect timeout`.

- #51504 covers handshake deadlines, peer caps and idle eviction; this PR bounds unanswered lookup responses after the handshake. The later PR to land will need to reconcile overlapping edits.
- #55962 advances control traffic while model work is running; it does not bound a missing response.
- #53087 bounds primary-tier `HIT_PENDING` waits, a separate state from remote P2P lookup `RETRY`.
- #53330 guards producer supply versus consumer demand; it does not add lookup response deadlines.

## Validation

### CI follow-up: `b98ec16094c2bfbd81a62bf1a2cef866f356b19e`

The main merge at `fb8ed9c` brought in a Ruff failure in `tools/recipes/sweep/sweep_html_report.py`. This follow-up applies the two-line `datetime.UTC` change requested by CI. The UTC timestamp behavior is unchanged; the current minimum Python version is 3.11.

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files --hook-stage manual
.venv/bin/python tools/recipes/sweep/sweep_html_report.py --help
git diff --check
```

All passed, including the changed-file mypy hook. The complete two-line diff and the report-generation call path were reviewed again. AI assistance was used for this follow-up.

### Current revision: `9d1f68dff8f43aee265c69a789b6393df9828825`

Based on the merged PR head `5d23150e49e28fa79b46bab7ae502dc311025ef7`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p -q --tb=short
```

**229 passed**. The partial-fetch case supplies two store jobs but fetches only one; both completion results reach the caller in the poll that expires an unrelated lookup, and teardown reports neither as failed. The existing failed-transfer case now checks that its deferred failure also arrives in the same poll and is not repeated.

The reconnect regression uses two managers and real loopback TCP/ZMQ control connections with fake data transports. It checks local MISS fallback, retirement of the peer's old session, a fresh bidirectional handshake, and preservation of the expired request's failure marker. It waits for TCP disconnect events before reconnecting. Three additional consecutive runs passed.

Negative control: restoring only `server.py` and `session.py` to `5d23150` makes both new regressions fail (the unused store result is absent, and the peer retains its old session); the existing full-fetch case still passes. The revised production files were restored afterward.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Make ExampleHiddenStatesConnector abort-safe
author: ys2025-AI
body:
Fixes `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` abort-path crash.

## Purpose

`ExampleHiddenStatesConnector.request_finished()` crashes `EngineCore` when a
request is aborted while still **waiting** (i.e. before it was ever scheduled) —
the common case when an API client times out and cancels queued requests.

`_request_filenames` is only populated in `build_connector_meta()` for
`SchedulerOutput.scheduled_new_reqs`. A request aborted before its first
schedule never reaches that code, but `Scheduler.finish_requests()` still calls
`request_finished()` for waiting requests, where the unconditional
`self._request_filenames.pop(req_id)` raises:

```
example_hidden_states_connector.py request_finished
    filename = self._request_filenames.pop(req_id)
KeyError: 'cmpl-b98ee80d8ff99a38-0-8e7006c7'
```

The `KeyError` becomes `EngineCore encountered a fatal error`; every API server
process then dies and clients see a storm of `APIConnectionError`.

This is the connector-side counterpart of the scheduler-side stale-completion
crash tracked upstream:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46240
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46304
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53079

### Changes

1. `request_finished` uses `pop(req_id, None)`; when no filename was recorded
   (aborted before scheduling) it drops residual `_pending_saves`/`_lock_fds`
   state and returns `(False, None)` — no hidden states to save, no blocks to
   delay.
2. `request_finished_all_groups` no-ops when the per-group block table is
   missing instead of indexing out of bounds.
3. `get_finished` only reports `finished_sending` for requests it actually
   tracked (a submitted DtoH copy); abort/never-scheduled requests no longer
   trip `assert req_id in self.requests` in `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished()`.
4. `get_finished_count()` returns `1`: only TP rank 0 writes hidden states, so
   exactly one completion notification is expected per request; without this,
   `KVOutputAggregator` waits for `world_size` notifications.

(3) and (4) are coupled: (3) alone would never complete a request; (4) alone
would let non-writer ranks report before rank 0's copy finishes, freeing KV
blocks too early.

## Test Plan

New CPU-only unit test
`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector_abort.py`:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector_abort.py -q --noconftest
```

Covers:

- `request_finished` on a never-scheduled request returns `(False, None)` (no `KeyError`)
- `request_finished_all_groups` handles a missing group table
- `get_finished` does not report an untracked/aborted request
- `get_finished` reports a tracked request once its copy completes
- `get_finished_count() == 1`

## Test Result

```
$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector_abort.py -q --noconftest
5 passed, 15 warnings in 18.92s
```

End-to-end: on vLLM 0.26.0 + vllm-ascend (Ascend NPU) during online DSpark
hidden-state training, aborting queued requests (client timeouts) previously
fataled `EngineCore` with the `KeyError` above; with this change the engine
survives abort storms and training runs to completion. Reproducer: send a batch
of long-prompt requests, let some time out and get aborted while queued.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Report request-level KV load failures under HMA
author: NickLucche
body:
Implements my suggestion back in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50388#pullrequestreview-4827494872, reverting PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50388 in doing so.

## Background

#50388 fixed a hard crash (`ValueError: too many values to unpack`) that hit the scheduler whenever a KV load failure was reported on a hybrid (HMA) KV cache layout. The crash happened in `_report_failed_recv` when unpacking multi-group block ID tuples, and the fix taught the scheduler how to unpack them.

The unpacking was never really the problem, though. Under HMA the scheduler tracks a single merged KV cache group while block IDs are only unique *within* a group, so a block-level failure report is ambiguous by construction — there is no correct way for the scheduler to interpret "block N failed" when the same block ID exists in multiple groups. Patching the unpack just moved the ambiguity around.

Nixl ran into the same situation earlier and solved the simple way in #35264: when HMA is required, `_report_failed_recv` skips block-level reporting entirely and the request is reported as a whole via `KVConnectorTransferResults.failed_recving`. The scheduler already handles `failed_recving` for `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests under both the recompute and fail policies, so no scheduler-side changes are needed.

## What this PR does

Reverts #50388 and mirrors the Nixl approach in the two connectors that could still hit the crash:

- **MooncakeConnector (P2P)**: the worker determines `_is_hma_required` the same way its scheduler does, and under HMA routes failed receives to a request-level queue surfaced through a new `get_transfer_results()` on the worker, which the connector delegates to. Requests that failed before any blocks were assigned locally are still aborted as before.
- **MooncakeStoreConnector**: all mooncake store loads are asynchronous, so load failures land on requests in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. The worker passes the HMA flag into `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread`, and the three failure sites (oversized key, partial batch, exception) report the request via `failed_recving` instead of invalid block IDs. The worker aggregates these across receive threads.

Non-HMA layouts keep the existing block-level failure reporting unchanged.

## Testing

Added unit tests for both connectors covering the HMA case (failure reported as `failed_recving`, no invalid blocks touched) and the non-HMA case (block-level behavior preserved), alongside the existing mooncake and load-failure-recovery suites.

To be explicit: this reverts #50388 on purpose rather than building on it, because the block-level reporting path it fixes cannot be made correct under HMA — the group information is simply not there at the point of failure. If reviewers feel strongly about keeping the scheduler-side unpack robustness anyway, that could be reintroduced separately, but I'd rather not keep dead ambiguity-handling code around.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Release stale FlashMLA workspace views after growth
author: vMaroon
body:
## Purpose

Release obsolete FlashMLA scratch storage when another layer grows the shared workspace.

`FlashMLASparseImpl` keeps constructor-time tensor views in `q_concat_buffer`, `prefill_bf16_workspace`, and, with PCP+DCP, `gathered_kv_workspace`. When `WorkspaceManager` grows its allocation, those views keep the old storage alive. Both buffers remain allocated, reducing the memory available for KV cache.

This change stores shapes and dtypes, reserves capacity during initialization, and reacquires simultaneous views from the current workspace when used. Workspace sizing, tensor layout, and the manager's locking policy remain unchanged.

### Observed impact

We reproduced this on GLM-5.3 with DP/EP64, TP1, MTP1, automatic KV/context sizing, and a 0.95 GPU memory target, using a vLLM 0.29.0-based deployment. Allocator snapshots showed a 5,904 MiB FlashMLA workspace retained alongside a new 6,144 MiB MoE workspace on 18 of 64 ranks. The new allocation was traced to `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl._allocate_buffers` during profiling.

The corresponding fix on that deployed version produced these startup measurements:

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ranks retaining both allocations | 18 | 0 |
| Minimum KV capacity per rank | 490,816 tokens | 603,904 tokens |
| Total KV capacity across 64 ranks | 36,934,975 tokens | 38,971,455 tokens |

Total allocated memory recovered was **103.78125 GiB**. These are startup allocation measurements, not throughput or model-accuracy results. This PR ports the fix to current upstream and also covers its PCP+DCP gather buffer.

### Duplicate check

Searched open PRs for `flashmla workspace` and `workspace memory leak`, and checked issue #51743 and its linked open PRs. The closest workspace PR, #42856, changes workspace bounds for SM120; it does not release retained views after growth. Issue #51743 concerns runtime padded-Q allocation rather than this retained-storage case. No matching lifetime fix was found.

## Test plan and results

- Added a parametrized regression to the existing sparse FlashMLA test suite for BF16, FP8, and FP8 with PCP+DCP. It checks obsolete-storage release, buffer shapes and non-overlap, locked pointer stability, and active workspace lane selection.
- Ran those three cases through a local CPU isolation harness loading the constructor/accessors from this checkout and the unchanged `WorkspaceManager` implementation, with real PyTorch storage. **All three fail before the patch and pass after it.** CUDA-dependent imports are stubbed in that harness; this is not a full-module or attention-kernel test.
- Ran the repository's pre-commit checks on both changed files, including Ruff and mypy.
- The deployed-version fix also passed four focused CPU regressions and the 64-rank GPU startup allocation check above.

Full-environment regression command:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py \
  -k workspace_growth_releases_storage -v
```

That direct test invocation, model evaluation, long-context inference, and CUDA-graph replay validation are still pending. The local macOS environment lacks the required current vLLM dependencies and GPU runtime. The measured DEP64 configuration had CUDA graphs disabled.

title: [Bugfix] Make GPU sync checks safe under torch.compile
author: khluu
body:
## Summary

`gpu_sync_debug`'s patched tensor-copy wrappers currently read a `ContextVar`
before checking whether Dynamo is tracing. A full-graph compile therefore fails
with an unsupported `ContextVar.get()` instead of bypassing sync checks as
intended.

This change:

- checks `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` before accessing either `ContextVar`;
- routes the original C++ `Tensor.to` descriptor through a weak-referenceable
  Python callable registered with `torch.compiler.allow_in_graph`, so Dynamo
  treats the call as opaque while AOT/Inductor can still lower it;
- adds a full-graph `torch.compile` regression with device and dtype derived
  dynamically from another tensor;
- runs the two new Voxtral CUDA-graph parameter cases in explicitly spawned
  processes so neither prior pytest CUDA state nor the other graph mode can
  contaminate them.

## CI incident and test-selection evidence

Daily main build #88920 first exposed this in
`test_voxtral_realtime_cudagraph[FULL_DECODE_ONLY]` in the H200 Multimodal
Models (Extended Generation 1) job. PR #51167 added the compiled Voxtral path,
but that exact job was blocked in both its PR build #88857 and post-merge main
build #88899, so the failure was not exercised before the daily run.

I searched open vLLM issues and PRs for the exact `ContextVar.get` / Voxtral
full-graph failure and did not find an existing fix.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files vllm/utils/gpu_sync_debug.py tests/utils_/test_gpu_sync_debug.py tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py` — passed all applicable hooks
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Local pytest was not run because this regression requires CUDA and this development host has no GPU.
- Exact H200 build #88941 passed Async/Inputs/Utils/Worker but exposed the
  saved C++ `Tensor.to` descriptor as Dynamo-unsupported in the Voxtral
  full-graph test.
- Replacement #88962 proved that registering the method descriptor directly
  is invalid at import time because `allow_in_graph` stores a weak reference.
- Replacement #88969 passed Async/Inputs/Utils/Worker and the original Voxtral
  `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` compile/CUDA-graph surface at literal head `c2fbacb1`.
  The following `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` parameter then hit the normal startup
  guard with only 25.73/32.5 GiB free after the prior in-process compiled
  runner retained about 6.5 GiB; later failures were cascades from that state.
- Replacement #89000 passed Async/Inputs/Utils/Worker, but the default CUDA
  isolation helper chose `fork` after the parent pytest process had initialized
  CUDA. Both Voxtral cases therefore failed before engine compilation with
  `Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess`.
- #89010 used an invalid copied full SHA and failed in bootstrap; it contains
  no test evidence.
- #89011 also passed Async/Inputs/Utils/Worker, then reproduced the same two
  pre-compilation CUDA-fork failures. Its literal head still contained the
  helper's default mode because the intended one-line `spawn` edit had not
  been staged into the prior commit.
- Current exact replacement #89026 runs only the same two H200 lanes at
  literal signed head `f7f21d97caecf810db069402ed02c4624311af32`, which
  explicitly passes `method="spawn"` to the isolation helper.

No model evaluation is required because the production change only alters
debug-wrapper control flow while Dynamo is tracing. The exact affected
generation test is included in targeted CI.
