this draft is marked ready or merged.

title: [XPU][Bugfix] Fix Qwen2-Audio ValueError on audio clips longer than 30s
author: jbyczkow
body:
# [Bugfix] Fix Qwen2-Audio ValueError on audio clips longer than 30s

## Purpose

`InputProcessingContext.call_hf_processor()` sets
`merged_kwargs.setdefault("truncation", False)` so the dummy placeholder
text passed to the HF processor isn't cut short — vLLM needs the full
untruncated placeholder sequence to keep multi-modal token positions
aligned with the audio embeddings.

`Qwen2AudioProcessor` forwards that same `truncation` kwarg unmodified to
its Whisper-style feature extractor, whose own default is
`truncation=True`: it truncates/pads every audio clip to the model's
fixed 30s window (3000 mel frames). With `truncation=False` leaking in
from the text-side default, clips longer than 30s are no longer
truncated, so their extracted `input_features` keep their native (larger)
frame count. This later fails `Qwen2AudioFeatureInputs`' fixed-shape
validation:

```
ValueError: input_features dim[2] expected 3000, got 3495
```

which crashes the engine core and takes the whole server down
(`EngineDeadError`).

First introduced by 0b19ebcacd0e9578460206035c4b3575361c19c4
("[MM] Simplify `_apply_hf_processor_main` (#53275)"), which added the
`truncation=False` default in `call_hf_processor()`. Not
`--enforce-eager`-specific — reproduces on both eager and
`torch.compile` paths, since the bug is in multi-modal preprocessing,
before model execution.

## Fix

`Qwen2AudioMultiModalProcessor._preprocess_hf_mm_data()` now explicitly
sets `truncation=True` in the kwargs it returns, so it wins over
`call_hf_processor()`'s `setdefault()`. The dummy-text truncation this
default was originally protecting against is unaffected here — the
dummy text is tiny (`<audio_bos><audio_token><audio_eos>`) and never
actually gets truncated either way.

## Test Plan

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  -cc '{"inductor_compile_config":{"benchmark_combo_kernel":false}}' \
  --port 8001 --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":1}'
```

Client (any audio clip longer than 30s triggers it; the snippet below
synthesizes one so it's fully reproducible without external data):

```python
import base64, io, requests, numpy as np, soundfile as sf

sr = 16000
duration_s = 35  # > 30s Whisper window
audio = (0.1 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 440 * np.arange(sr * duration_s) / sr)).astype(np.float32)

buf = io.BytesIO()
sf.write(buf, audio, sr, format="WAV")
b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii")

resp = requests.post(
    "http://localhost:8001/v1/chat/completions",
    json={
        "model": "Qwen/Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct",
        "messages": [{
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Transcribe the audio."},
                {"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": b64, "format": "wav"}},
            ],
        }],
        "max_tokens": 64,
    },
)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text[:500])
```

## Test Result

Before fix: server crashes on the first request with a >30s audio clip:
```
ValueError: input_features dim[2] expected 3000, got 3500
EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```
All subsequent requests get `500 Internal Server Error`, server has to
be restarted.

After fix: server processes the same request successfully, returns a
transcription with `200 OK`. Confirmed on Intel BMG B70 (XPU) and NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (CUDA).

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix EAGLE and dense draft startup with EP
author: kyleliang-nv
body:
## Purpose

After #55914, pairing an EP-enabled MoE target with a dense EAGLE, EAGLE3, or independent draft model fails during configuration validation:

```text
Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled.
```

Pass the final draft `ModelConfig`, after draft architecture overrides, to `create_draft_parallel_config`. Disable inherited EP only when that config reports a dense draft through `ModelConfig.is_moe`, the same classification used by the existing validator. MoE drafts, including DeepSeek V4 MTP and DSpark, continue to inherit target EP. Target EP and target/draft TP settings remain unchanged.

The new `draft_model_config` argument is optional. Existing two-argument calls, or calls that explicitly pass `None`, retain the previous EP inheritance. The normal configuration-construction path always supplies the final draft config. This preserves helper-call compatibility; it does not infer draft density or fix existing validation failures for callers that omit model information.

## Test Plan

The regression constructs real `ModelConfig` and `SpeculativeConfig` objects from small local configuration files, exercising architecture conversion and production validation without mocks or model weights. Its 24 cases cover dense independent/EAGLE/EAGLE3 drafts and MoE independent/MTP/DSpark drafts, target EP on/off, and matching target/draft TP sizes of 1 and 2.

Four additional compatibility cases cover omitted and explicit-`None` draft model configs, each with target EP on/off.

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py tests/test_config.py
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k 'draft_inherits_ep_only_for_moe or draft_parallel_config_preserves_ep_without_model' -v
```

## Test Result

Rebased without conflicts onto public `main` at `fc8132a5e523294ea69decb5e7cbf50e9d3e135e` on 2026-09-16. The three existing patches are unchanged by the rebase.

- Pre-commit: passed.
- On the rebased head `a2e2e9035de0e81252cda7164198c4d2f5230a9d`: 28 passed.
- Before replacing the required boolean argument with the optional model config, all four new compatibility cases failed with `TypeError`.
- Negative control: keeping the optional helper and EP guard but omitting the draft config at the production call site caused 6 expert-count validation failures and 22 passes. The failures were dense independent/EAGLE/EAGLE3 drafts with target EP enabled. This confirms the configuration-level tests catch a missing call-site update even when the compatibility tests pass.
- On the earlier head `e679fb51c48b62b83920a24ea733bd4b3efb6cbe`, repeated the negative control using an in-process wrapper that deliberately omits the draft model config when calling the real helper: the same 6 dense-draft/target-EP cases failed with expert-count validation errors, and 22 passed. The on-disk source was unchanged.
- Full inference and model accuracy evaluations were not run; these tests cover configuration construction and validation only.

## Related work

This PR overlaps #56933, which addresses the same regression. Following review, this PR adopts the same backward-compatible optional-model-config interface, with an explicit legacy fallback and real configuration-construction regression coverage. These are alternative fixes, not dependencies; maintainers can select or consolidate the overlapping changes. #35143 addresses a separate dense-draft DP synchronization optimization.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the regression, implement the change, and prepare tests. Test commands, results, and validation limits are documented above.

title: [Bugfix] Use DP index for dense DP weight updates and EC CPU region
author: lxy-alexander
body:
## Purpose

Fix #56949

This change is about the wrong rank-local payload selection in vLLM dense DP weight transfer. Because an independently reconfigured dense DP engine resets data_parallel_rank to 0 but keeps its original DP identity in data_parallel_index, using data_parallel_rank makes all DP engines select the payload of the first DP replica. Therefore, data_parallel_index should be used instead.

```python
data_parallel_index * world_size + worker_rank
```
This ensures each worker selects the payload belonging to its original global DP replica.

## Test Plan

Update the existing test as test_rank_local_update_uses_data_parallel_index_after_reconfigure, configure four DP replicas with the current engine at DP index 2, reconfigure it as an independent DP rank, and verify that data_parallel_rank resets to 0, data_parallel_index remains 2, and worker rank 0 selects the DP-index-2 payload.

## Test Result

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py -v

12 passed in 7.55s
```

This is my current understanding of the issue and the expected behavior. Please let me know if I misunderstood any part of the DP rank/index semantics or if additional test coverage is preferred.

## Same bug class: EC CPU connector shared region

`create_ec_shared_region` keyed the `/dev/shm/vllm_ec_{instance_id}_dp{N}.mmap` region by `data_parallel_rank`. Under the multiprocessing launcher, dense DP engines all reset that to 0 and inherit the same pickled `instance_id` (only the Ray launcher appends a per-DP suffix), so every DP engine on a node opened the same region and their independent schedulers overwrote each other's encoder cache blocks. It now uses `data_parallel_index`, same as this PR's weight-update fix.

Added `test_dense_dp_engines_get_distinct_regions`: it fails before the change (the second engine logs `Opened existing EC mmap file ..._dp0.mmap`) and passes after.

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py -q
124 passed
```

This follow-up commit was written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and reviewed by @aoshen02. It was found by auditing other `data_parallel_rank` readers that need per-replica identity. MoRIIO (`fold_local_rank(data_parallel_rank, data_parallel_size_local)`) looks affected too, but the fix also involves the `remote_dp_size_local` handshake and can't be verified without ROCm, so it is left out of this PR.

title: [CI] Fix NIXL push worker test stub after failure deferral
author: khluu
body:
## Summary

PR #56104 moved NIXL push registration failures from direct background-thread
handling to the existing `_failed_recv_reqs` queue. A test stub added on main by
PR #56317 still omitted that queue and asserted the old direct-handler behavior.
The combined main tree therefore failed before exercising the intended contract.

This change initializes the real base-worker queue on the stub and updates the
regression to verify that an unhandshaked registration is queued exactly once.
The duplicate queue initialization in the specialized pollable stub is removed.

## CI evidence

Main builds #89015, #89016, #89017, and #89022 failed the H200 V1 KV Connectors
lane in
`TestPushWriterRegSend::test_fails_request_when_engine_not_handshaked` with
`AttributeError: '_StubWriterWorker' object has no attribute '_failed_recv_reqs'`.
Build #89016 otherwise completed 1,218 tests in that command before the single
failure.

PR #56104's exact build #89004 was run on a stale head without PR #56317's newer
test, so its passing V1 KV Connectors result could not catch this cross-merge
contract mismatch.

I searched open vLLM issues and PRs for `_failed_recv_reqs`,
`TestPushWriterRegSend`, and this NIXL push test failure. No existing fix was
found.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py -q` — 52 passed
- `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py` — all applicable hooks passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

No model evaluation is required because this changes only test-fixture state and
assertions; production code and model behavior are unchanged.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was prepared with AI assistance. Human review is required before
this draft is marked ready or merged.

body:
## Purpose

Fix a start-up crash of GLM-5.3-Flash in data-parallel deployments (TP=1 per rank): `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` was launched with `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)`, and with 64 KDA value heads on one GPU the first CUDA-graph capture batch of 1024 sequences needs `1024 * 64 = 65536` programs — one over the CUDA `gridDim.z` limit of 65535 — so the launch fails with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument` and `--data-parallel-size 4` (with or without EP) cannot start. TP4 (16 heads per rank) is unaffected.

The kernel now carries `N * HV` in `gridDim.x` (limit 2^31-1) with the `program_id` mapping swapped accordingly. Scope (narrowed in review): only the NVIDIA GLM-5.3-Flash copy under `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/third_party/kda/` (`kernels.py`, `fused_recurrent.py`) and its test are changed. The same `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)` pattern exists in the AMD GLM copy and in `third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/{fused_recurrent,fused_sigmoid_gating,kda}.py`; those are intentionally left unchanged here (no AMD reproduction available; the shared kernels serve other models and need their own validation) and are candidates for separate follow-up. The packed-decode kernel in the same GLM file already guarded this case (`split_batch_head_grid = B * HV > 65535`). The narrowed change serves every GLM-5.3-Flash TP configuration; the failure itself needs TP=1 per rank (DP) at the default capture sizes.

Fixes #56973

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched vllm-project/vllm open and closed PRs and issues (GitHub search, 2026-09-13 and 2026-09-15) for `fused_recurrent_kda`, `gridDim.z`, `65535`, `invalid argument` + GLM-5.3-Flash / KDA / DP: no report of this crash and no PR touching the launch grid of `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`; the only related guard is the existing `split_batch_head_grid` check in the packed-decode kernel of the same file.

## Test Plan

- Regression case added to the existing `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (`test_fused_recurrent_kda_more_than_65535_programs`, parametrized 1024×64 and 2048×48 (sequence, head) programs with head dim 16): the full batch must be bitwise identical to the same batch run in two halves. It fails on the unpatched kernel with the Triton launch error and passes with this change.
- Existing test that exercises the changed kernel: `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (NVIDIA glm5next `fused_recurrent_kda`). The flash-linear-attention and AMD copies are no longer touched by this PR.

## Test commands run and results

On 4× GB200 (SM100), 2026-09-11 nightly image, the changed kernel files mounted over the installed package (`/tmp/t` holds a copy of `tests/` so `import vllm` resolves to the installed package):

```
pip install tblib
python3 -m pytest -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py
python3 -m pytest -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py \
    tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py tests/kernels/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py \
    tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py
```

- `test_kda_recurrent.py` with the new case: stock kernel — 2 failed (the two new parametrizations, `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`), 6 passed; patched kernel — 8 passed.
- The six files (before the new case was added): 197 passed / 7 skipped on stock, 197 passed / 7 skipped with the fix.
- Bitwise equivalence stock vs patched on identical inputs (plain-decode calls at 16, 1024, 4096 and 64000 programs; spec-decode-style calls with 2-D state indices and `num_accepted_tokens` at T=4 and T=6): outputs and state updates `torch.equal`; both deterministic run to run. On the crashing shape (1024 × 64) the patched output equals a reference assembled from two stock half-batches, bitwise.
- End to end: `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel` starts, captures its graphs and serves an 8k-in/1k-out sweep at concurrency 1–128; TP4 with the patch reproduces stock TP4 throughput (169.6 vs 169.1 tok/s at c=1, 1898.6 vs 1897.4 at c=32); gsm8k 5-shot greedy on the patched DP4+EP server 0.927 vs 0.934 for stock TP4 (paired exact McNemar p = 0.29 on the 57 discordant questions).
- 2026-09-21, after narrowing — kernel regression test only (the TP4 / DP4+EP serving runs and the gsm8k evaluation above were done before the narrowing and were not repeated, since the NVIDIA GLM kernel files are unchanged by it): same image and procedure, with only the two NVIDIA GLM kernel files copied over the installed package; the three shared flash-linear-attention wrappers were left as installed (their `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)` lines checked present by grep). Stock: 2 failed / 6 passed in `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (the two > 65535-program cases, `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`); with the two files: 8 passed.

## Model evaluation

gsm8k, lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13, 5-shot, greedy, one prompt per request, all 1319 questions: patched DP4 + EP server 0.927 (1223 correct) vs stock TP4 0.934 (1232 correct); paired exact McNemar on the 57 discordant questions p = 0.29 (no detectable difference; the kernel outputs themselves are bitwise identical to stock where stock can run).

## AI assistance

This change was developed with an AI assistant (Claude); the author reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements above.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Add per-tensor FP8 W8A16 kernel to fix Ministral crash on CPU
author: bigPYJ1151
body:
## Summary

- Add `CPUFp8PerTensorScaledMMLinearKernel`, a per-tensor FP8 W8A16 CPU kernel
  built on the existing AMX block-scaled kernel. `PerTensorTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`
  was the only per-tensor FP8 CPU kernel available and wasn't wired up for
  AMX-capable CPUs, crashing on load of fp8-quantized `PixtralForConditionalGeneration`
  models (e.g. Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512).
- CI: match the wrapped `RuntimeError("Cannot find any model weights with ...")`
  that `default_loader.py` raises for a partial HF cache snapshot, so the CPU
  CI offline→online retry fallback actually triggers for that cache-miss shape.
- CI: mount `~/.cache/vllm` (in addition to the already-mounted `~/.cache/huggingface`)
  so multimodal test fixtures (`VideoAsset`, `ImageAsset`, `AudioAsset`, which
  download into `VLLM_ASSETS_CACHE`) persist across CPU CI container lifetimes
  instead of being re-fetched, and falling back online, on every run.

The two CI fixes were found while chasing recurring CPU CI flakiness during
verification of the kernel fix above (Buildkite builds #89028 and #89045).

## Test plan

- `python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_cpu_fp8_scaled_mm.py -v`
  → 80 passed (covers both the new per-tensor kernel and the underlying
  block-scaled kernel it reuses, including the N-not-a-multiple-of-32 rejection path).
- CI script changes verified with `bash -n` and against the actual failing
  Buildkite logs they target: #89028 (CPU multi-modal tests re-fetching video
  assets every run) and #89045 (CPU spec-decode failing outright on a partial
  weight-file cache instead of retrying online).

title: [Bugfix][Responses] Clean up MCP tool sessions once before closing them
author: shaohuaxi
body:
## Purpose

With multiple MCP tool sessions, both Responses contexts register the same cleanup callback once per session. Each callback visits all called tools. This can send duplicate cleanup requests to an open session and attempt another call on a session that has already closed.

Register the callback once, after the sessions have been opened, so cleanup runs before any of them closes. The tests cover both `ParsableContext` and `HarmonyContext`, including unused tools, repeated initialization, and partial initialization failure.

Related to #25697. This addresses the cleanup ordering discussed there; it does not fix the separate cross-task cancel-scope error. I found no open PR covering this change: #25790 skips initialization for requests without tools, while #52521 changes MCP header handling.

AI assistance was used to develop and validate this change.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_parsable_context_unit.py \
  -q -o addopts='' -p no:cacheprovider

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/context.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/context.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py
```

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the new lifecycle tests had 6 failures and 8 passes. All failures involved two sessions with at least one called tool.
- After the fix, the two unit test files pass: **59 passed, 1 existing xfailed**.
- Pre-commit and Python 3.12 type checks pass.
- A separate local check using real MCP SDK clients and servers over in-memory streams passes all 8 cases. Each called tool receives one cleanup request before its session closes, with no calls attempted after close.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Force reasoning mode for GLM-5.3 chat templates in the GLM MoE parser
author: Dovis01
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54744.

GLM-5.3 keeps the GLM-4.x prompt and tool-call format but replaces the `enable_thinking` toggle with an always-on `"Reasoning Effort:"` header. The template's generation prompt unconditionally appends `<|assistant|><think>`, so the model output carries no opening `<think>` tag and thinking cannot be turned off. When a client passes `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` (or `"thinking": false`, honored by GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7 templates), the `Glm47MoeParser` disabled reasoning extraction while the model still thought, leaking the whole scratchpad into `message.content` and reporting an empty reasoning field. It also made `is_reasoning_end()` return `True` immediately, so structured-output constraints applied from token 0 while the model was still reasoning.

The fix detects the GLM-5.3 template signature on the tokenizer (`[gMASK]<sop>` + `Reasoning Effort:` + no `enable_thinking` + GLM tool-call tags, the same predicate SGLang uses) in `Glm47MoeParser.__init__` and discards the thinking-disable kwargs with a one-time warning. The parser then builds the thinking-armed engine config (`initial_state=REASONING`), so streaming, non-streaming, and `is_reasoning_end` paths all behave exactly as they do today for requests without the kwarg. GLM-4.5–4.7 templates declare `enable_thinking` and are untouched (pinned by a negative-control test).

## Why this is not a duplicate

Two open PRs touch the same symptom with materially different approaches:

- #54276 nulls only the `enable_thinking` kwarg when the template lacks it. A client sending `thinking: false` still leaks, and the loose `"enable_thinking" not in template` check is replaced here by the positive GLM-5.3 family signature ported from SGLang.
- #54825 splits leaked think blocks post-hoc in non-streaming extraction and explicitly leaves streaming broken. Fixing the config at construction time (this PR) covers streaming, non-streaming, tool calling, and the structured-output `is_reasoning_end` gate in one place.

## Test commands and results

- `pytest tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py -q` — 20 passed (16 existing + 4 new: both kwarg names forced, streaming split, GLM-4.7 negative control). The three force-tests fail on current main as expected.
- `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py -q` — 13 passed.
- `pytest tests/reasoning/ -q` — 436 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on both touched files; pre-commit hooks passed on the commit.

## Model evaluation (GLM-5.3-Flash, 8xH100, TP8+EP, MTP k=5)

A/B against unpatched main, same launch flags (`--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47`):

| Request | main (unpatched) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`, non-stream | reasoning empty; content = scratchpad + `"4"` (leak) | reasoning parsed, content = `"4"` |
| `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": false}`, non-stream | same leak | reasoning parsed, content = `"4"` |
| no kwargs (control) | correct | identical behavior |
| `enable_thinking: false` + stream | leak | reasoning deltas then content delta, 15 deltas |
| `enable_thinking: false` + tool call | — | `finish_reason=tool_calls`, `get_weather({"city": "Paris"})`, reasoning parsed |

title: [Perf][Attention] Source Triton metadata builder geometry from kv_cache_spec
author: ZhengGong-amd
body:
## Overview

`TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder` is built per KV-cache group but sizes its 3D-kernel threshold and split-K scratch from the model-wide KV head count and head dim, so on heterogeneous models such as Gemma 4 decode stays on the slower 2D kernel; this PR reads both from the group's `kv_cache_spec`, as `FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder` already does (#42650 did the same for `num_heads_q`).

`unified_attention` takes the 2D grid's `num_kv_heads` from `k.shape[2]`, the group's own count. On `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` the full-attention group has 2 KV heads against a model-wide 8, so `seq_threshold_3D` is `128 // 8 = 16` instead of `128 // 2 = 64`: at batch 24 the grid is 48 blocks, below `MIN_LAUNCH_GRID_SIZE_2D = 128`, yet the builder stays on 2D. The sliding groups size `softmax_segm_output` for head dim 512 instead of 256.

The buffer uses `head_size`, the stride `unified_attention` applies (`next_power_of_2(q.shape[2])`); `head_size_v` belongs to the DiffKV path, which re-sizes its own buffer. Switching kernel changes the bf16 reduction order, so generated text can differ. Where the spec matches the model-global values, nothing changes.

#54191 changes `num_heads_kv` only. #57409 changes `headdim` only, inside a DFlash change. This PR does both, and the new tests fail on either half alone. #47520 rescales the grid-size target and keeps the divisor, so it composes with this.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 full-attention decode at batches 24–64 moves from the 2D to the 3D kernel: **+66%** at batch 24 (506 µs → 172 µs) and **+36%** at batch 64 on MI325X. Batches that keep their kernel are flat.
- On vLLM v0.29.0 (MI355X), `vllm bench serve` of gemma-4 at 32K input and concurrency 24 gives **+6.7%** total tok/s and **−11.5%** median TPOT, with TTFT flat. Not re-taken on this `main`.
- GSM8K strict-match on that build goes from **0.4155 to 0.4511**; a repeated base run is bit-identical.
- Affected locally: gemma-4-26B-A4B and gemma-4-31B, which `Gemma4Config` forces onto `TRITON_ATTN` on ROCm. Homogeneous models are unchanged.

## Validation

Base is `main@7128f568ac`; the patched arm adds only this diff.

| tree | Triton cases in `test_group_head_counts.py` |
|---|---|
| `main` | 3 failed |
| `num_heads_kv` only (#54191) | 2 failed: geometry, scratch stride |
| `headdim = head_size_v` | 1 failed: scratch stride |
| threshold capped before the capture snap | 1 failed: snaps to 48, not 64 |
| this PR | 4 passed, 12 skipped |

`test_triton_attn_metadata_builder.py` and `test_triton_attn_segments.py` pass 44/44 on both arms. One new case uses an off-grid `max_num_seqs=50`, where the threshold snaps to a capture size (64) before `max_num_seqs` caps the scratch rows.

Kernel, MI325X, `unified_attention` at the full-attention group shape (16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 512, block 16, ctx 4096, decode), median of five `do_bench` repeats, both run orders within 0.5 points:

| batch | main | this PR | gain |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---:|
| 8 / 16 | 3D | 3D | −0.1% / −0.3% |
| 24 | 2D | **3D** | **+66%** |
| 32 | 2D | **3D** | **+63%** |
| 48 / 50 | 2D | **3D** | **+49% / +48%** |
| 64 | 2D | **3D** | **+36%** |
| 96 | 2D | 2D | ~0 |

Outputs match exactly where the kernel is unchanged, and to 2.8e-3 relative L2 where it switches.

Serve on v0.29.0 (`98dff2a81d`), MI355X, six interleaved pairs, 32K input / 256 output, concurrency 24:

| metric | base | patched | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 25835 | 27574 | **+6.7%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 65.18 | 57.68 | **−11.5%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 13823 | 13793 | −0.2% |

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, `seed=1234`:

| comparison | identical text | strict-match |
|---|---:|---|
| base vs base | 100% | 0.4155 → 0.4155 |
| base vs base at `max_num_seqs=128` | 4.6% | 0.4155 → 0.4314 |
| base vs this PR | 12.7% | 0.4155 → 0.4511 |
| Qwen3-8B (never builds this) | 99.9% | 0.8726 → 0.8726 |

`main` alone at a different `max_num_seqs` already changes 95% of generations: the 2D/3D boundary is batch-dependent, and this PR moves it.

## Details

Of 17 local checkpoints, only Gemma 4 reaches this builder without an explicit backend selection; the others, forced onto it, match `main` in every builder field. Under full graph capture with an off-grid `max_num_seqs=50`, batches 49–50 pad to 56 tokens and stay on 2D on both arms; that sizing comes from `main`.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [Bugfix][Test] Synchronise ranks before the profiled call in profile_…
author: x41lakazam
body:
Adding a barrier before the profiled function, otherwise the jitter introduced by CUPTI startup from `torch.profiler.profile` impacts the dispatch duration.

Measured on 4 ranks in one node, profiling the same AllGather:

    rank 0   30.418 ms      rank 1    4.137 ms
    rank 2    0.036 ms      rank 3    3.842 ms

An 850x spread on one collective, where only the rank that happened to arrive last (rank 2) reports a meaningful number. With a barrier placed inside the profiler context, immediately before the profiled call:

    rank 0    0.034 ms      rank 1    0.105 ms
    rank 2    0.204 ms      rank 3    0.236 ms

Per-rank compute time is unchanged either way (0.064-0.070 ms), which is the check that this moves waiting out of the collectives without perturbing the work being measured.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Validate mixed prompt embedding mask lengths
author: shaohuaxi
body:
## Purpose

Reject a `prompt_is_token_ids` mask whose length differs from the number of prompt embedding rows before submitting the request to the engine.

For example, a Python mixed-embedding prompt with three embedding rows, three token IDs, and a two-element mask currently passes input processing and reaches a NumPy broadcast error in `InputBatch.add_request()`. A one-element mask can instead broadcast silently. The mask describes each prompt position, so both inputs should be rejected at admission.

This adds the check to `InputProcessor` and reports `VLLMValidationError` with `parameter="prompt_is_token_ids"`. Requests without a mask and correctly aligned mixed prompts retain their existing behavior.

I checked related work and did not find an existing fix for this admission check. #54509 fixes mask alignment during truncation; #56656 adds the mask to prefix-cache keys. #51891 touches input validation, but its mask-length condition controls embedding replacement positions and does not reject a mismatched mask.

## Test Plan

The regression tests exercise `InputProcessor.process_inputs()` with empty, short, broadcastable, and long masks. They also cover pure embeddings, token IDs plus embeddings without a mask, and an aligned mixed prompt.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_request_input_bounds.py \
  tests/renderers/test_chat_utils_prompt_embeds.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_input_processor_trace_replay.py -q -p no:cacheprovider

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
```

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the new cases produced **4 failed, 3 passed**: all four malformed masks were accepted.
- With the fix, the three suites above produced **123 passed**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks and the manual mypy 3.12 check passed.
- A10 / Qwen3.5-0.8B (BF16, eager, prefix caching disabled): the baseline legacy runner reproduced the broadcast error; the next normal request returned `EngineDeadError` as well.
- With the fix, the legacy and V2 runners each passed **11 checks**: three valid generation controls, four rejected mask lengths (0, 1, 2, 4), and successful normal generation after each rejection. The valid controls produced the same token IDs before/after the fix and across runners.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to prepare the fix, tests, and this description.

title: [Bugfix] Fail loudly instead of no-op NCCL weight transfer
author: tzielinski-habana
body:
## Purpose

An NCCL weight-transfer round can report success while moving zero bytes. `PyNcclCommunicator` disables itself (`disabled=True`) when the NCCL library won't load (e.g. on XPU) or when `VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL=1`, and every collective then returns early. The workers keep their old weights, and an RL run trains against a frozen policy with nothing in any log.

This PR rejects a disabled communicator at rendezvous, in `stateless_init_process_group` and `uid_init_process_group` (trainer and worker, dense and sparse), on every platform. A weight-transfer group always has `world_size >= 2`, so on CUDA it only fires with `VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL=1` or a missing libnccl, which is the same bug.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py -k disabled_communicator
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/weight_transfer/nccl_common.py tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py
```

## Test Result

- New test passes; it fails with the check removed.
- 2x Intel Arc Pro B70, RL trainer driving `/init_weight_transfer_engine` -> `/start_weight_update` -> `/update_weights`: before, every route returns 200 and nothing moves (`importance_sampling_ratio` 0, loss and `grad_norm` 0). After, the rendezvous raises on both ranks.

The code was co-developed with Claude Code.

title: [Bugfix] Avoid nested score cancellation handlers for /v1/score alias
author: taneem-ibrahim
body:
## Purpose

Fix nested cancellation and server-load accounting on the deprecated `/v1/score` alias. `create_score_v1()` applied `@with_cancellation` and `@load_aware_call`, then delegated to `create_score()`, which already applies both wrappers. A single request therefore created two disconnect listeners and incremented server load twice; one listener could consume the disconnect while the real score handler continued running, leaving the load counter nonzero. Removing the two outer alias decorators makes `/v1/score` rely on the canonical `/score` handler's wrappers.

## Relationship to PR #55602

[PR #55602](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55602) removed redundant cancellation wrappers from the `/v1/rerank` and `/v2/rerank` aliases. This PR applies the same narrow delegation principle to `/v1/score` and additionally removes its redundant load-accounting wrapper. It does not change shared helpers or canonical score/rerank handlers.

## Reproducer

Run the following on upstream `main` and on this branch:

```bash
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import asyncio
from types import SimpleNamespace

from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.scoring.api_router import create_score_v1


async def main():
    disconnects = asyncio.Queue()
    handler_started = asyncio.Event()
    handler_cancelled = asyncio.Event()
    receive_calls = 0

    async def receive():
        nonlocal receive_calls
        receive_calls += 1
        return await disconnects.get()

    async def handler(request, raw_request):
        handler_started.set()
        try:
            await asyncio.Future()
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            handler_cancelled.set()
            raise

    state = SimpleNamespace(
        enable_server_load_tracking=True,
        server_load_metrics=0,
        serving_scores=handler,
    )
    raw_request = SimpleNamespace(
        app=SimpleNamespace(state=state),
        receive=receive,
    )

    route_task = asyncio.create_task(create_score_v1(None, raw_request))
    await asyncio.wait_for(handler_started.wait(), 1)
    for _ in range(100):
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

    print(
        "before_disconnect",
        f"receive_calls={receive_calls}",
        f"load={state.server_load_metrics}",
    )
    await disconnects.put({"type": "http.disconnect"})
    print("route_result", await asyncio.wait_for(route_task, 1))
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    print(
        "after_disconnect",
        f"handler_cancelled={handler_cancelled.is_set()}",
        f"load={state.server_load_metrics}",
    )

    current = asyncio.current_task()
    pending = [task for task in asyncio.all_tasks() if task is not current]
    for task in pending:
        task.cancel()
    await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)


asyncio.run(main())
PY
```

## Output on main

```text
before_disconnect receive_calls=2 load=2
route_result None
after_disconnect handler_cancelled=False load=1
```

## Output on branch

```text
before_disconnect receive_calls=1 load=1
route_result None
after_disconnect handler_cancelled=True load=0
```

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_late_interaction_serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_utils.py -q
# 17 passed, 34 warnings in 2.21s

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_bi_encoder_online.py -q
# 16 passed, 14 warnings in 33.42s

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/api_router.py
# All applicable hooks passed
```

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) drafted the code.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Preserve per-layer offsets in KV cache bindings
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
FIX https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57019

## Purpose

Fix cross-layer KV overwrites when HiSparse packs multiple layers into one allocation. Both resident and hot bindings used the tensor's base offset for every layer, allowing later layers to overwrite earlier layers' cached rows. Compute `tensor.offset + layer_index * tensor.layer_stride` once per layer and use it in both bindings.

Addresses #57019; the faulty bindings were introduced by #53781.

Add a nightly HiSparse GSM8K job using the existing accuracy harness and real `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` weights. It runs on four B200s with TP4, BF16 KV, eager execution, and a 32 GiB host pool. All 1,319 questions are evaluated with 5 shots and an explicit 90% minimum accuracy. The job is optional in regular CI, following the existing nightly-job convention. No new unit test or standalone evaluation harness is added.

Duplicate-work check: read #57019 and its comments, searched open PRs for `57019 in:body`, `HiSparse`, and `HiSparse offset`. No open PR addressing these missing layer offsets was found. The host-mirror replay work in #56158 addresses a separate failure path.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, validation, and this description. The human submitter is responsible for line-by-line review and independent test validation.

## Test Plan

Run the new nightly test:

```bash
chg run -g 4 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -v \
  tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py \
  --config-list-file=configs/models-hisparse.txt
```

Existing GPU suites run against the binding fix:

```bash
chg run -g 1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse -q

chg run -g 1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -q
```

## Test Result

- New nightly configuration, run locally on four B300s: **94.39% (1,245/1,319)**, **zero invalid answers**, evaluation time **594.9 seconds**. The 90% accuracy assertion passed. B200 execution remains for CI.
- Local pytest teardown failed in the existing `RemoteOpenAIServer._get_gpu_memory_used` check: it reads physical NVML indices `0..3` instead of mapping `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2,5,6`, so growth in another user's GPU allocations exceeded its baseline. All our server/worker processes exited and GPUs 0, 2, 5, and 6 returned to 0 MiB; the full pytest command is therefore **not** reported as passing.
- Set `request_timeout_seconds: 1800` because the evaluator's total timeout includes waiting for a connection. An initial run with the default 600 seconds timed out approximately 60 queued requests; the final configuration completed all requests without API errors or timeouts.
- Negative control for the nightly server configuration: restored only the original `bind_hisparse_kv_caches` from `0136df94b0` in all four workers, keeping TP4, BF16 KV, concurrency 32, and automatic GPU cache sizing. The first **64 GSM8K questions scored 0/64 (0%)**, with no request errors or timeouts (72.9 seconds). This was a sampled negative control, not a full 1,319-question unpatched run. Its GPU pool was 138.1 GiB and reported about 8.4% usage, demonstrating that low cache capacity is unnecessary to expose the missing layer offsets. This does not establish memory-pressure spill coverage. The local validation helper scoped NVML cleanup checks to the reserved GPUs; production code and the GSM8K scorer were unchanged.
- HiSparse attention tests on B300: **30 passed**.
- Spill/prefix-restore tests on B300: **2 passed**, covering standalone/offload variants and FULL CUDA graph replay.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Buildkite step-key validation.

Earlier sampled evaluation, separate from the new nightly configuration: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` revision `53e0691e21895a3863a606dfd12910c69eba94ab`, TP2 on B300, automatically selected FP8 KV, eager mode. Used the existing GSM8K scorer with the first 64 questions, 5 shots, 256 output tokens, temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 16; server limits were model length 8192, 32 sequences, and 4096 batched tokens. The fixed arm enabled default HiSparse settings with a 32 GiB host pool.

| Sampled GSM8K arm | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HiSparse disabled | 61/64 | 95.3125% | 0 |
| Fixed HiSparse | 59/64 | 92.1875% | 0 |

**Accuracy parity remains unverified.** The sampled fixed-arm continuations were readable but differed from the control. This uses a different checkpoint and KV dtype from the issue's RedHatAI/BF16 reproduction.

## Curl reproduction: unpatched versus fixed HiSparse

Both responses below were captured with HiSparse enabled, the same NVIDIA checkpoint/revision, TP2 on B300, FP8 KV selected by the checkpoint, eager mode, and the same request. The before run restored only `bind_hisparse_kv_caches` from `0136df94b0` in the workers; the after run used the fix. These are not the HiSparse-disabled control responses.

Equivalent server command for either version:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --revision 53e0691e21895a3863a606dfd12910c69eba94ab \
  --served-model-name glm52 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --enforce-eager --seed 0 \

  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32}}'
```

Request (the after response was captured earlier using the equivalent HTTP JSON request):

```bash
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"glm52","prompt":"What is the capital of France?","max_tokens":32,"temperature":0,"seed":0}' \
  | jq '{text: .choices[0].text, finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason, completion_tokens: .usage.completion_tokens}'
```

Before, unpatched HiSparse:

```json
{
  "text": " ( is is'] .istsististig, \"..\" of of of23-2-; of----!.",
  "finish_reason": "length",
  "completion_tokens": 32
}
```

After, fixed HiSparse:

```json

  "text": " (Oh, I know this one!)\nWhile searching our database we found 1 possible solution for the: What is the capital of France? (Oh, I",
  "finish_reason": "length",

```

title: [Bugfix] Treat max_tokens as output upper bound, not input-space reservation
author: YuvrajSinghBhadoria2
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

Fixes #42474.

`TokenizeParams.max_input_tokens` was defined as `max_total_tokens - max_output_tokens`, treating the client's requested `max_tokens` as a **hard reservation** off the model's context window. Per the OpenAI API spec — and how Zed/Factory/opencode-style clients actually use it — `max_tokens` is an *upper bound* on generation, not a reservation. The real generation budget is already clamped downstream by `get_max_tokens()` in `vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py` based on actual post-tokenization prompt length, so the output side stays bounded regardless.

Example: model context 128000, prompt 62466 tokens, `max_tokens: 65535`
- before: rejected (`62466 > 128000-65535 = 62465`)
- after: prompt accepted, sampling `max_tokens` clamped to `65534`

## Why this is a fix at the source, not whack-a-mole

The property feeds seven consumers. Patching only one (e.g. `_token_len_check` alone) left `get_encode_kwargs` capping the tokenizer at `max_input_tokens + 1`, silently truncating prompts for left-truncation chat models and breaking prefix-cache locality. Fixing the property at the source corrects all seven consistently.

## What stays correct

- `__post_init__` still rejects `max_output_tokens > max_total_tokens` (a genuine bug)
- `_token_len_check` / `_text_len_check` still reject genuine context overflow; their messages are updated to reflect that the rejection means *input alone* exceeds the context, not input+output
- `with_kwargs` now preserves the original `max_output_tokens` when no explicit `max_length` is passed, instead of recomputing it to 0 (this was flagged on the existing POC PR)
- `get_max_tokens()` continues to clamp `sampling_params.max_tokens` to `max_model_len - input_length`

## Tests

`tests/renderers/test_completions.py::TestMaxTokensNotReservation` (7 tests):
- large `max_tokens` no longer eats the prompt budget (the reported symptom)
- genuine prompt overflow is still rejected
- `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1` / `pad_prompt_tokens=-1` map to `max_total_tokens`, not `max_total - max_output`
- `with_kwargs` preserves/re-derives the output budget correctly

All pre-existing renderer tests run with `max_output_tokens=0`, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Related PR

#42482 is an open proof-of-concept for the same fix. This PR additionally addresses the functional regression (output budget reset in `with_kwargs`) and the now-inconsistent validation messages that its bot review called out.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Import full blocks without tail prefill on D
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse currently rejects host imports whose computed-token count is not block aligned. This draft explores an alternative to #56946: receive the full final block and restore its contents into one writable GPU page, so a successful NIXL full-prompt import resumes with a single-token forward instead of prefilling the unaligned tail on D.

The idea is that we want to avoid having to run prefill on D, however short they might be (<block_size here), with north star being deploying D with decode-only CG (aligned with rest of cases).

### NIXL analogy: transfer capacity is not sequence length

NIXL already transfers physical blocks containing partially filled prompt tails. Moving the unused bytes does not make them computed tokens. HiSparse can use the same distinction:

| For a 32,019-token prompt, block size 128 | This approach |
| --- | --- |
| Real imported tokens | 32,019 |
| Host blocks received | 251 |
| Physical capacity | 32,128 token slots |
| Unused tail capacity ("holes") | 109 token slots |
| Prompt work on D after a full import | The usual last-token replay for logits |

The holes are unused rows within the request's final host block. They do not change token positions or sequence length, and generation fills them at their normal offsets. P does not compute dummy padding tokens. No sub-block allocator or NIXL wire-protocol change is required.

### Implementation and tradeoff

- Reserve one writable resident page for the final imported block, including aligned prompts whose last token is replayed.
- After a successful external receive, enqueue a full-page host-to-device restore on every TP rank. Copies run on the compute stream before the forward/CUDA-graph replay.
- Retain both endpoints until every participating worker completes its copy. Avoid publishing an uninitialized resident copy to prefix-cache users, and keep an incomplete host page unsealed.
- Register a completed, valid restored GPU page for later prefix hits only after all workers finish. Pending restores remain hidden, and incomplete pages and aborted requests are excluded. This incorporates [NickLucche/vllm#12](https://github.com/NickLucche/vllm/pull/12).
- Continue using the existing row-mirror and page-sealing paths for newly generated KV.

Compared with #56946, this transfers the final block and pays for one page of H2D copying per layer/rank rather than recomputing up to `block_size - 1` prompt tokens. It also reserves a resident tail page for aligned imports. The unused host rows are ordinary tail capacity, not extra logical tokens or permanent gaps between prompt and output. No performance improvement has been measured.

The intended benefit is to keep successful full-prompt P/D handoffs on single-token execution, compatible with decode-only graph capture. This is not a guarantee that D can never prefill: cache misses, failed transfers, preemption, or partial external hits can still require recomputation.

### Related work

Checked #56699 and its comments, open PRs mentioning it, and open PRs matching HiSparse import, landing, tail, partial, full block, and tail restore.

- #56946 addresses the same admission failure by rounding the imported prefix down and prefilling the remainder locally. This draft is the explicitly requested alternative that retains all real prompt KV and changes tail residency instead.
- The notify-only read and empty-region shape fixes are reused verbatim from #56946 (originally #55398). They prevent empty local destinations from entering region expansion when P and D have different cache-group layouts. They are independent of tail policy; empty receives notify P, and report `finished_recving` only when `awaiting_kvs=True`.
- #55398 chooses direct GPU landing for imported history when capacity permits. This draft preserves host landing and restores only the final page.
- #56109 concerns broader pool/residency management. This draft uses the current pool model.

Related to the deployment discussion in #56699; this does not claim to fix that issue's CUDA launch failure or establish end-to-end P/D correctness.

## Test Plan

Exercise aligned, unaligned, and sub-block imports; last-token resumption; partial-page publication; multi-worker completion and abort lifetime; and tail-copy contents on both host-writer and non-writer ranks.

Before marking ready, run real NIXL P/D on NVIDIA GPUs with decode-only graphs, check generated-token/logprob parity against the prefiller reference, and exercise page-boundary crossing, eviction/preemption, and concurrent traffic. Heterogeneous TP/DCP coverage remains pending.

## Test Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py \
  -k 'hisparse or connector_completes_partial_prefix' -q
```

**99 passed, 2 skipped, 117 deselected** on macOS. The two skipped cases require CUDA. Commit-time pre-commit hooks passed, including the configured mypy hook.

Rerun after integrating #12 and rebasing onto `upstream/main` at `fc8132a5e5`: **99 passed, 2 skipped, 117 deselected**. The existing import test now checks that one worker completion does not publish the GPU copy and that full completion publishes aligned tails. Pre-commit hooks passed across all PR files. GPU/model validation of the combined change remains pending.

Additional existing empty-receive checks after restoring those two NIXL hunks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k empty_recv_is_reported_only_when_awaited -q
```

**4 passed, 130 deselected** on macOS. The separate completion-time positional group-pairing workaround reported by the GPU investigation is not included in this draft.

After rebasing onto `upstream/main` (`c6fa1f05d1`, including #57027), fixed the H200 CI failure in `test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore[offload]`: the sync checker reports the tail copy as potentially synchronous because PyTorch does not recognize the host pool's external `cudaHostRegister` registration. A narrow `gpu_sync_allowed()` scope covers that copy; the transfer and stream ordering are unchanged. The existing CUDA tail-restore test now allocates the host pool through the production registration path and enables strict sync checking.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k empty_recv_is_reported_only_when_awaited -q
```

Post-rebase results on macOS: **88 passed, 2 CUDA cases skipped** and **4 passed**, respectively. Pre-commit hooks passed across all PR files. The CUDA regression and failing GPU e2e test still require the new CI run.

**Model evaluation / GPU serving: not run.** This is a draft for design review, published at the submitter's explicit request without waiting for GPU testing. No accuracy, graph-replay, throughput, or latency claim is made.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, tests, and this description. Human line-by-line review and human-run GPU validation remain pending before this draft is ready for merge.

title: [Bugfix] Fix incorrect Mamba block allocation estimate that prevents request admission
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose
It is found for Kimi K3, a long request can be rejected admission when loading prefix cache from external KV storage (e.g., Mooncake) and get stuck in the waiting queue forever, causing entire system to stall. Investigation shows the bug is in Mamba's block allocation estimation call `get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, which incorrectly calculates the physical blocks needed for such requests, potentially a regression caused by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53614

Stall reproduction on 8 x B300:
```
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
export WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0
export MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH=mooncake_config.json
export VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=50052
export MC_ENABLE_DEST_DEVICE_AFFINITY=1

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
    --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --prefix-match-unit 128 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --max-cudagraph-capture-size 2048 \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":0}' \
    --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA \
    --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \
    --language-model-only \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"load_async":true,"lookup_async":true,"enable_cross_layers_blocks":false}}'
```

Sending a 1M-length request, clear the GPU local kv cache, and send the same request again causes the entire system to stall as the request fails the admission gate.

## Test Plan
Added unit test that checks equality of estimated blocks vs actual allocated blocks for mamba in `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, existing main fail the tests while the branch passes.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Honor dynamic K in autoregressive speculators, 1.2~1.3x kernel perf improvement
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

MRV2 did not propagate `SchedulerOutput.num_spec_tokens_to_schedule` to autoregressive speculators, causing unnecessary draft forwards and stale draft tokens.

This PR fixes the issue

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
from functools import partial
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch
import triton

from vllm.v1.spec_decode.dynamic.utils import build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.autoregressive.speculator import (
    AutoRegressiveSpeculator,
)

MAX_K = 5
MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 48
HIDDEN_SIZE = 4096
NUM_REQS = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 48)
DYNAMIC_K_SCHEDULE = [(1, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, 3)]


class SyntheticSpeculator(AutoRegressiveSpeculator):
    """MRV2 proposer whose model forward is replaced by a matmul."""

    def load_draft_model(self, target_model, target_attn_layer_names):
        raise NotImplementedError("This benchmark does not load a model")

    def __init__(self, device: torch.device) -> None:
        # Deliberately skip the real constructor: it allocates model-related state.
        self.num_speculative_steps = MAX_K
        self.max_num_reqs = MAX_BATCH_SIZE
        self.max_model_len = 8192
        self.dp_size = 1
        self.dp_rank = 0
        self.pcp_manager = None
        self.eplb_state = None
        self.use_fused_multi_step_decode = True
        self.prefill_cudagraph_manager = None
        self.decode_cudagraph_manager = None
        self.speculative_config = SimpleNamespace(
            uses_dynamic_speculative_decoding=lambda: True,
        )

        self.input_buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device)
        self.hidden_states = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.last_token_indices = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )
        self.current_draft_step = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
        self.sample_src_positions = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )
        self.idx_mapping = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
        self.temperature = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device=device)
        self.seeds = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
        self.draft_tokens = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_K, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )

        self.weight = torch.randn(
            HIDDEN_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.src = torch.randn(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.dst = torch.empty_like(self.src)
        self.count_steps = False
        self.steps = 0

    def _synthetic_forward(self, num_tokens: int) -> None:
        torch.mm(self.src[:num_tokens], self.weight, out=self.dst[:num_tokens])
        self.src, self.dst = self.dst, self.src
        if self.count_steps:
            self.steps += 1

    def _prefill(self, num_reqs: int, num_tokens: int, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        self._synthetic_forward(num_tokens)
        self.draft_tokens[:num_reqs, 0].zero_()

    def _generate_draft(
        self, num_reqs: int, num_tokens_padded: int, *args, **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        self._synthetic_forward(num_tokens_padded)


def count_forwards(speculator: SyntheticSpeculator, run) -> int:
    speculator.steps = 0
    speculator.count_steps = True
    run()
    speculator.count_steps = False
    return speculator.steps


def main() -> None:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("CUDA is required")

    device = torch.device("cuda")
    speculator = SyntheticSpeculator(device)
    target_buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device)
    target_hidden_states = torch.randn_like(speculator.hidden_states)
    temperature = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device=device)
    seeds = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    last_sampled = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    dense_schedule = build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup(
        DYNAMIC_K_SCHEDULE,
        vllm_max_batch_size=MAX_BATCH_SIZE,
        vllm_num_speculative_tokens=MAX_K,
    )

    print("batch  sched_k  buggy_ms  fixed_ms  speedup  forwards(buggy->fixed)")
    for num_reqs in NUM_REQS:
        batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_reqs, target_buffers)
        common_args = dict(
            input_batch=batch,
            attn_metadata={},
            slot_mappings={},
            last_hidden_states=target_hidden_states[:num_reqs],
            aux_hidden_states=None,
            num_sampled=torch.ones(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
            num_rejected=torch.zeros(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
            last_sampled=last_sampled,
            next_prefill_tokens=target_buffers.input_ids,
            temperature=temperature,
            seeds=seeds,
            dummy_run=True,
            skip_attn_for_dummy_run=True,
            is_profile=True,
        )
        dynamic_k = dense_schedule[num_reqs]

        # Buggy: model_runner omitted runtime K, so propose() used max K=5.
        buggy = partial(speculator.propose, **common_args)
        # Fixed: model_runner passes the scheduler-selected runtime K=3.
        fixed = partial(
            speculator.propose,
            **common_args,
            num_speculative_tokens=dynamic_k,
        )

        buggy_steps = count_forwards(speculator, buggy)
        fixed_steps = count_forwards(speculator, fixed)
        assert dynamic_k == 3
        assert buggy_steps == MAX_K
        assert fixed_steps == dynamic_k

        buggy_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(buggy)
        fixed_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(fixed)
        print(
            f"{num_reqs:>5}  {dynamic_k:>7}  {buggy_ms:>8.3f}  "
            f"{fixed_ms:>8.3f}  {buggy_ms / fixed_ms:>7.3f}x  "
            f"{buggy_steps}->{fixed_steps}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

And we can get

```bash
batch  sched_k  buggy_ms  fixed_ms  speedup  forwards(buggy->fixed)
    1        3     0.151     0.115    1.306x  5->3
    2        3     0.148     0.115    1.286x  5->3
    4        3     0.149     0.115    1.298x  5->3
    8        3     0.148     0.115    1.282x  5->3
   16        3     0.151     0.115    1.315x  5->3
   32        3     0.150     0.114    1.306x  5->3
   48        3     0.149     0.115    1.287x  5->3
```

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject stop strings on --tokens-only servers instead of silently ignoring them
author: shimib
body:
## Purpose

Partially addresses #57052 (the `--tokens-only` half; the derender-side stop-string truncation is a separate design discussion tracked there).

A `--tokens-only` server sets `sampling_params.detokenize = False` **after** the request has already passed validation, bypassing the `SamplingParams` guard that forbids `stop` strings without detokenization. Downstream, the tokenizer-less `IncrementalDetokenizer` never calls `check_stop_strings`, so client `stop` strings were **silently ignored** — generation ran to EOS or `max_tokens` with no error, warning, or log line. The failure is easy to miss because `stop_token_ids` still work (they need no detokenization).

This PR rejects the combination with a 400 in `serve_tokens`, mirroring the error a client already gets when it sets `detokenize=False` itself (see the first leg of the existing `test_stop_string_workflow`). The error message points at the documented contract from that same test: check stop strings on the coordinator, or use `stop_token_ids`.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Checked open PRs before submitting (`gh pr list --search` on "stop", "tokens-only", "include_stop_str_in_output", "derender", plus `57052 in:body`). The closest is #46310, which rejects `stop` when `--skip-tokenizer-init` is set — but that guards `SamplingParams` construction from CLI-level config and does not catch this path, where the request validates cleanly (client-side `detokenize` defaults to `True`) and `force_no_detokenize` flips it afterwards. No open PR touches the scale-out `serve_tokens` validation.

## Test Plan

title: [Bugfix] Fix np.float64 leaking into the KV transfer metrics log
author: NickLucche
body:
The KV transfer metrics log line currently shows raw numpy scalar reprs when the stats come from a connector inside a MultiConnector:

```
(APIServer pid=3547631) INFO 09-15 19:44:52 [metrics.py:107] KV Transfer metrics: NixlPullConnector={'Num successful transfers': 8, 'Avg xfer time (ms)': np.float64(2.338), 'P90 xfer time (ms)': 2.772, 'Avg post time (ms)': np.float64(1.111), 'P90 post time (ms)': 1.88, 'Avg MB per transfer': np.float64(25.441), 'Throughput (MB/s)': np.float64(10883.285), 'Avg number of descriptors': np.float64(133.5)}
```

The single-connector path was fine because the log line formats each value with an f-string (`str()`), which renders `np.float64` as a plain number. With a MultiConnector, `reduce()` returns a nested dict and the whole dict gets rendered with `str()`, which formats every value with `repr()` — and numpy 2 renders `repr(np.float64(2.338))` as `np.float64(2.338)`.

The fix is to have the nixl/mooncake/hf3fs `reduce()` implementations return plain Python scalars via `.item()`, which is what their `dict[str, int | float]` annotation already promised. After the fix the same line reads:

```
KV Transfer metrics: NixlPullConnector={'Num successful transfers': 8, 'Avg xfer time (ms)': 2.338, 'P90 xfer time (ms)': 2.772, 'Avg post time (ms)': 1.111, 'P90 post time (ms)': 1.88, 'Avg MB per transfer': 25.441, 'Throughput (MB/s)': 10883.285, 'Avg number of descriptors': 133.5}
```

title: [Bugfix][Metrics][MFU] Size activation traffic from the model dtype
author: thillai-c
body:
## Purpose

`BaseConfigParser` sizes weight traffic from the model's dtype but pins activation traffic to 2 bytes:

```python
args.weight_byte_size = get_dtype_size(torch_dtype)

# FIXME: handle this better by parsing whether activations use
# bf16, fp32, etc...
args.activation_byte_size = 2
```

`torch_dtype` is already resolved on the line above, so the two values come from the same config and disagree. For a model served with `--dtype float32`, every activation term in the MBU accounting is counted at half its real size while that same model's weight terms are correct. Activations are produced in the model's compute dtype, so this keys them on it.

`activation_byte_size` is set once here and never overridden. Quantization parsers override `weight_byte_size` (fp8, mxfp4 and friends) but leave activations alone, which is why the model dtype remains the right source after this change.

## Impact

- bfloat16 and float16: unchanged, 2 bytes, which covers the overwhelming majority of deployments.
- float32: 2 to 4 bytes. Activation read and write traffic doubles and reported MBU drops accordingly.

The float32 change is user visible. Anyone tracking MBU for a float32 deployment will see the number move; that movement is the correction, since the previous value understated memory traffic.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py
pre-commit run ruff-check ruff-format --files \
  vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py
```

New tests in the existing file:

- `test_base_config_parser_activation_byte_size_follows_dtype`, parametrized over float16, bfloat16 and float32, asserting activation and weight byte sizes agree with the dtype.
- `test_attention_read_bytes_scale_with_activation_dtype`, which goes through `AttentionMetrics.get_read_bytes_breakdown` and asserts `qkv_input`, a pure activation term, is exactly twice as large for float32 as for bfloat16.

The existing `test_base_config_parser` assertion of `activation_byte_size == 2` for float16 still holds and is unchanged; only its comment was updated, since 2 is now the dtype's size rather than a default.

## Test Result

```text
72 passed, 1 warning in 19.45s
```

That is the 68 pre-existing tests plus the 4 added here.

Linting:

```text
ruff check...............................................................Passed
ruff format..............................................................Passed
```

No model evaluation: this changes analytic MFU/MBU accounting only. No kernel, no model computation, and no output logits are affected.
