title: [Bugfix][ROCm] AMD-Quark mixed-precision DeepSeek-V4.1 support
author: xiao-llm
body:
## Purpose

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` does not load today. It is a **mixed-precision** AMD-Quark export — MXFP4 experts, but 226 per-layer attention specs in MXFP8:

| | scheme |
|---|---|
| `global_quant_config` | `fp4` / `per_group` / `group_size=32` / `e8m0` |
| `layer_quant_config` (226 entries) | `fp8_e4m3` / `per_block` / `block_size=[32,32]` / `float8_e8m0fnu` |

Four independent bugs block it. Each one assumes DeepSeek **V4**'s `128x128` block geometry, or the DeepSeek-native scale naming.

| # | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | All 226 per-layer specs silently discarded | Decline mixed-precision Quark exports, let `QuarkConfig` take them |
| 2 | `NotImplementedError: No quark compatible scheme was found.` | New `QuarkW8A8Mxfp8` scheme |
| 3 | Attention shards silently fall back to global MXFP4 | Expose the VL wrapper's mappings as class attributes |
| 4 | Engram scale tensor never routed | Add a `weight_scale$` mapper rule |

### 1. The V4.1 config claims the checkpoint, then throws the specs away

`DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method` accepts any Quark export whose *global* scheme is MXFP4 — this one qualifies. But `from_config` then rewrites the config into a single global FP8 scheme with `weight_block_size = [128, 128]`, discarding all 226 per-layer specs. `get_quant_method` then gates its MXFP8 path on `weight_block_size == [32, 32]`,
which that rewrite has just made unreachable.

**Fix:** a Quark export carrying `layer_quant_config` is mixed precision by definition, so decline it and let `QuarkConfig` handle it.

### 2. QuarkConfig has no scheme for 32×32 per-block FP8

`_is_fp8_w8a8` only accepts per-block FP8 at `[128, 128]` (V4 geometry), and the OCP-MX matchers only accept 1-D `per_group` weights. A 32×32 per-block e8m0 weight matches neither, so dispatch raises.

**Fix:** extend `QuarkOCP_MX` to handle MXFP8 as a first-class OCP-MX dtype. `mxfp8_e4m3` is added to `_WEIGHT_QUANT_KEY_MAP` / `_ACTIVATION_QUANT_KEY_MAP`, a normalizer (`ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows()`) accepts both config dialects, and `QuarkOCP_MX` gains an unpacked MXFP8 branch with 3-way `packed_factor` (`1` for mxfp8, `2` for mxfp4, `8/6` for mxfp6).

The only difference from canonical 1-D MXFP8 is scale layout. MXFP8 carries one e8m0 value per weight *row* per 32-element group; Quark's `block_size=[R, 32]` carries one per *R* rows. The loader expands each scale row:

```python
loaded_weight.view(torch.uint8).repeat_interleave(rows, dim=0)
```

At `R == 1` the two layouts coincide and expansion is a no-op. The kernel is the shared `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel()` — the same one compressed-tensors and INC MXFP8 schemes use. Existing 128×128 per-block FP8 keeps
`QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`, asserted in the new tests.

This also fixes a latent dispatch inconsistency: `get_quant_method()` and `get_quant_method_target()` now agree on MXFP8 layers, since both walk the same `QuarkOCP_MX` matcher chain.

Both MXFP8 config dialects are accepted:

| | Shape A (canonical MX) | Shape B (DeepSeek-V4.1) |
|---|---|---|
| `dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| shape | `qscheme=per_group`, `group_size=32` | `qscheme=per_block`, `block_size=[32,32]` |
| scale | `scale_format="e8m0"` | `scale_type="float8_e8m0fnu"` |
| `scale_block_rows` (R) | 1 | 32 |

### 3. The VL wrapper hides its module mappings from the quant config

`configure_quant_config` reads `hf_to_vllm_mapper` and `packed_modules_mapping` off the **class**, before `__init__` runs.
`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` (vision variant) defined neither at class level, only as instance attributes. So per-layer keys naming `layers.N.attn.wq_a` never matched the runtime `language_model.model.layers.N.attn.wq_a`, and every
attention shard silently fell back to the global MXFP4 spec.

**Fix:** expose both as class attributes, with the prefix rules shared via one module-level constant so they cannot drift.

### 4. The engram scale name

Quark spells it `engram.embed.weight_scale`. The mapper's rules match `\.scale$` — a literal `.scale` suffix — so the rule never fires.

**Fix:** add an explicit `weight_scale$` rule alongside the existing one.

## Scope

ROCm/AMD path only (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`). The `nvidia/` twins have the same shape for items 3 and 4, but this PR deliberately leaves them alone — only the AMD path has been validated on hardware.

## Test Plan

**Quark dispatch tests (`test_quark.py`):**

- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_2d_block` — a 32×32 per-block e8m0 linear dispatches to `QuarkOCP_MX` with `scale_block_rows == 32`; experts still fall through to the global MXFP4 spec; 128×128 per-block FP8 still gets
  `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_canonical` — canonical 1-D per-group MXFP8 (Shape A) dispatches to `QuarkOCP_MX` with `scale_block_rows == 1`; `get_quant_method` / `get_quant_method_target` agree.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_moe_raises` — MXFP8 experts raise `NotImplementedError`.
- `test_quark_override_delegates_to_quark_config` — all `quant_method=="quark"` configs (MXFP4, MXFP8, mixed, etc.) return `None` from  `DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method`, confirming delegation to `QuarkConfig`. Parametrized over V4 and V4.1 model types (10 cases).

**FP8 / DeepSeek-V4.1 tests (`test_fp8.py`):**

- `test_deepseek_v41_declines_mixed_precision_quark_config`
- `test_deepseek_v41_vl_exposes_quant_mappings_on_class`
- `test_deepseek_v41_engram_scale_accepts_quark_name`

## Test Result

**0 new code failures.** 

### End-to-end

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` (48 shards, 475 GB) on 4x MI355X at TP=4: all shards load in 74.5 s, MXFP8 attention resolves to `QuarkOCP_MX` via the `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`, and the model is coherent.

GSM8K accuracy (1319 problems, greedy, seed=42, 8-shot)
| Config | flexible-extract | strict-match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MXFP4 | 92.34% ± 0.73 | 92.42% ± 0.73 |
| Base FP8 | 92.87% ± 0.71 | 92.95% ± 0.71 |

Hardware: 4x MI355X (gfx950/CDNA4), TP=4.

title: [ROCm][CI] Enable AITER FP8/unquantized cases in modular-kernel sweep + fix MoRI per-tensor FP8 dispatch
author: divakar-amd
body:
This is step 1 ("FP8/unquantized case identification") of the plan in #54966; the MXFP4 config/weight-conversion work needs gfx950 hardware and will follow separately.

### What

`AiterExperts` in the modular-kernel combinations sweep (`tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`) was only reachable indirectly through the general quant-config cross-product, with no assertion that the exercised `(weight_key, activation_key)` pair is one it actually declares supported. The harness also hardcoded `torch.float8_e4m3fn` everywhere, which on FNUZ FP8 platforms (gfx94x / MI300):

- unconditionally skipped this whole test file (`current_platform.is_fp8_fnuz()` module-level guard), so none of these cases had ever run on MI300/MI200-class hardware
- registered `AiterExperts` under `fp8_types` only, silently excluding the fully-unquantized `(None, None)` scheme it also supports

### Changes

- `mk_objects.py` / `common.py`: use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` / `is_fp8()` instead of the hardcoded `torch.float8_e4m3fn` literal (no-op on CUDA/gfx950, where `fp8_dtype()` returns the same literal); register `AiterExperts` under `common_float_types` (was `fp8_types`) so `(None, None)` is actually generated.
- `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: drop the module-level FNUZ skip; add `assert_aiter_quant_scheme_case()` to make the exercised `(weight_key, activation_key)` pair explicit and assert `AiterExperts._supports_quant_scheme()` agrees — gated on `fused_experts_type.__name__ == "AiterExperts"`, so no other backend is affected.

### Additional Fix: MoRI Missing Per-Tensor FP8 Dispatch

Broadening quant-config coverage also exposed a real bug (distinct from #57029): `MoriPrepareAndFinalize.prepare()` only quantized activations for block-quantized/per-token FP8, so per-tensor FP8 configs fell through to unquantized dispatch while weights stayed FP8, which surfaced downstream as a misleading `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4b8` Triton assertion.
Fixed in: (a.) `all2all_utils.py`: extend `use_fp8_dispatch`/`scale_dim` to `is_per_tensor` (b,) `mori.py`: add the per-tensor quant branch, broadcasting the scalar scale to `[num_tokens, 1]` since MoRI's dispatch reads scales via a raw pointer
Fixes: 
`test_modular_kernel_combinations_multigpu[... quant_config15-MoriPrepareAndFinalize-TritonExperts-2]`

### Pre-existing bug surfaced

Running on MI300 (gfx942) for the first time (previously skipped at module-level) reproduced a deterministic HIP `illegal memory access` for every `AiterExperts` × `{DeepEPHTPrepareAndFinalize, MoriPrepareAndFinalize}` combination at `world_size=2`, including the plain unquantized case. Filed as #57029 with a full repro; this PR adds a scoped skip referencing it so CI doesn't regress on this newly-exercised combination. Not fixed here.

### Test plan

On MI300 (gfx942, FNUZ FP8), 
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -sv tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py
```
All 6 target `(weight_key, activation_key)` pairs from #54966 (5 FP8 + `(None, None)`) verified individually, each triggering the new assertion. Confirmed the FNUZ-skip removal doesn't affect CUDA/gfx950, and that the DeepEP-HT/Mori skip actually suppresses the crash (ran that node id before/after).

### AI assistance disclosure

Portions of this change (diagnosis, harness edits, and the new AITER test infra) were developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). All changes were reviewed and the tests above were run and verified by me on MI300 hardware.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Bound the prompt after multimodal expansion
author: dilberx
body:
FIX https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57038

## Purpose

`truncate_prompt_tokens` is applied before multimodal placeholder expansion, so the rendered prompt can exceed the requested limit. With Qwen3-ASR, asking for 96 tokens returns 147: truncation keeps 96 unexpanded tokens, then one audio placeholder expands into 52, giving `96 - 1 + 52`.

The two steps run in this order, and nothing re-checks the bound between them:

```python
# vllm/renderers/base.py::BaseRenderer.render_cmpl
dict_prompts = self.render_prompts(prompts)
tok_prompts = self.tokenize_prompts(dict_prompts, tok_params)   # truncates here
...
return [
    self.process_for_engine(prompt, arrival_time, ...)          # expands here
    for prompt in tok_prompts
]
```

`tokenize_prompts` ends in `TokenizeParams.apply_post_tokenization`, which truncates the still-unexpanded token ids:

```python
# vllm/renderers/params.py::TokenizeParams._validate_tokens
for validator in (
    self._token_truncation,
    self._token_padding,
    self._token_len_check,
):
    tokens = validator(tokenizer, tokens)
```

`process_for_engine` then reaches `_process_multimodal`, which expands the placeholders. It never received `tok_params`, so the requested limit was not available at that point.

This adds `BaseRenderer._truncate_expanded_prompt`, which re-applies the bound once placeholders are expanded, and threads `tok_params` through `process_for_engine` / `_process_singleton` as an optional keyword argument. The one external caller, `entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py`, is unaffected, and encoder-decoder prompts keep their current behaviour.

Multimodal spans are never cut. A request whose spans would not all survive the truncation is rejected with `VLLMValidationError`, matching the existing post-expansion rejection in `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py::_validate_model_input`. Cutting mid-span would leave the audio features and placeholder metadata disagreeing with the token ids, and silently dropping an item would change the meaning of the request. Happy to switch to dropping or to rejecting outright if you prefer.

No open PR addresses this issue; it had no linked PRs and no comments when I started.

## Test Plan

New unit coverage in `tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py`: the reported case, an under-limit no-op, a split span, a span dropped entirely past the cut, left-side truncation shifting placeholder offsets, and no limit requested. These call `_truncate_expanded_prompt` directly, so they need no model weights and no GPU.

```bash
pytest tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py -v
pytest tests/renderers/ -q
ruff check vllm/renderers/base.py tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py
ruff format --check vllm/renderers/base.py tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py
python repro_57038.py   # reproducer from the issue
```

## Test Result

```text
pytest tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py -v
6 passed

pytest tests/renderers/ -q
4 failed, 498 passed, 2 skipped

ruff check / ruff format --check
All checks passed! / 2 files already formatted
```

The 4 failures are pre-existing and unrelated: they fail identically with this change reverted (`test_cohere.py::test_async_cohere_renderer_does_not_block_event_loop`, two `test_hf.py::test_resolve_content_format_hf_defined` parametrisations, and `test_multimodal_hashes.py::test_mm_hash_includes_uuid_and_processing_kwargs`). One surfaces a `PixtralRotaryEmbedding` import error from the installed transformers version.

The reproducer from the issue, before and after:

```text
before: Requested token limit: 96 | Returned tokens: 147 | Matches full prompt[:96]: False
after:  Requested token limit: 96 | Returned tokens:  96 | Matches full prompt[:96]: True
```

Verified on `main` at dffbb714e, torch 2.13.0+cu129.

No model evaluation: this path validates and truncates request prompts before they reach the engine, and does not change model execution, kernels, or sampling. Prompts that already fit the requested limit are byte-identical to before.

AI assistance was used to reproduce the issue and analyse the call path. I have read and tested every line of this change.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][PD] Align region-mapped pulls across logical block sizes
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

Fix a NIXL pull that can silently load the wrong prompt pages when P and D allocate KV differently. The motivating setup has **plain NIXL on P and NIXL + HiSparse on D**, with **`--block-size 128` on both servers**.

The same command-line block size does not guarantee the same allocation. A logical block is the unit the scheduler allocates; a physical page is the unit used by the attention kernel and transfer. With a kernel that requires 64-token pages, plain P can keep 128-token logical blocks and split each into two physical pages. HiSparse's setup on D resolves its MLA scheduler blocks to the native 64-token size directly. That produces this geometry in the affected path:

| | Command-line block size | Scheduler's logical block | Physical/kernel page |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P: plain NIXL, HiSparse disabled | 128 | 128 | 64 |
| D: NIXL + HiSparse | 128 | 64 | 64 |

For a **160-token prompt**, P must allocate two logical blocks: capacity for 256 tokens, or **four physical pages**. D needs only **three physical pages**. Let `A` and `B` each hold 64 tokens, and `C` hold the remaining 32:

```text
P advertises:       [ A | B | C | unused ]
D has space for:    [   |   |   ]

Current selection:  [ B | C | unused ]  <- last three producer pages
Correct selection:  [ A | B | C ]
```

Logical-to-physical expansion already happens. The mistake comes afterward: the region-based suffix matcher assumes that any extra pages on P represent a prefix D has already cached. Here the extra page is unused capacity at the end, so that assumption shifts the whole transfer. If D has actually cached `A`, the remaining transfer should select `B, C`; the old logic selects `C, unused`.

**The fix selects pages by token position.** Pass the producer's existing `remote_num_tokens` through to the worker, combine it with each destination group's cached-prefix offset, and select the corresponding physical pages. Whole-page transfers remain: `C` is transferred with its unused rows, but the entirely unused fourth page does not shift the selection. This adds no prefill on D.

**HiSparse also exposes a separate assumption at transfer completion.** P can keep main KV and indexer KV in one merged cache group. D separates host KV and GPU indexer KV into different groups, so NIXL uses *regions* to match the corresponding memory buffers. The old `get_transfer_results()` still pairs groups by position. Looking up P's group 1 for D's group 1 can fail because P has only group 0, or pair the wrong blocks when the index exists.

Completion now uses the region read plan. The worker records `region_blocks_to_zero`: whole destination pages that were allocated but excluded from the read. For example, in the reverse allocation geometry, D may reserve four pages while P supplies three:

```text
D after the read:   [ A | B | C | untouched ]
D after completion:[ A | B | C | zeroed    ]
```

For two example regions with destination IDs `[10, 11, 12, 13]` and `[20, 21, 22, 23]`, receiving three pages into each produces a cleanup plan of `[[13], [23]]`. Completion clears page 13 only in its region and page 23 only in its region, then skips the old positional group processing.

This plan is local to one request on the receiving worker. `None` means use the existing completion path; empty per-region lists mean a region-mapped read with nothing to zero. In the original P-four-pages/D-three-pages example, D receives all its pages, so there is **no zeroing**. The plan does not include cached prefix pages or unused rows within the transferred partial page. It is discarded with the request's receive metadata; failed reads skip this cleanup.

Scope: pure MLA region pulls with equal physical page sizes, DCP=1, and one cache-group owner per region. Heterogeneous logical geometry without the required metadata or with shared-group regions is rejected. Existing homogeneous fallback behavior remains.

**Dependency:** the empty-receive fixes belong to #57049 (also present in #56946, originally from #55398). They are excluded from this PR, which will be rebased after that prerequisite lands. #57049's HiSparse tail-import policy remains separate from this transfer-alignment fix.

Duplicate checks included related issue #57019, its comments, and open PR searches for that issue, NIXL logical/physical geometry, and region padding. #57027 fixes layer binding offsets. #55374 introduces broader piecewise token-window loading in the ordinary group-based pull/push paths; its current diff does not wire that through the region-based path introduced by #53780. This PR addresses that region path without adding the piecewise-loading API.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, and validation. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the changed lines and validating the patched GPU deployment. GPU accuracy validation remains pending.


## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -m cpu_test -q

uv run --no-project pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/metadata.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py
```

title: [Bugfix] Make online FP8 MoE experts batch-invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
author: ybwbqg9379
body:
Fixes #57016

## Purpose

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a MoE model served with `--quantization fp8` (online per-tensor FP8, Triton experts) still produces output that depends on which other requests share its batch: greedy tokens flip within the first ~10 positions and prefix-cached K/V differs depending on who wrote it. Dense layers are invariant; only the experts are not.

Two things were wrong:

1. `Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod` (and `Fp8MoEMethod` for FP8-serialized per-tensor checkpoints with dynamic activations) quantize the expert inputs with one dynamic scale over the whole activation tensor (`kFp8DynamicTensorSym`), i.e. the max over every token of every co-batched request. Under batch-invariant mode this PR selects `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` and passes `per_act_token_quant=True`, mirroring what `Fp8LinearMethod` already does for dense layers.
2. Switching to per-token activations exposed a latent launcher bug: `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` passed `stride_bse=0` for 1-D `[E]` weight scales (and `stride_bsn=1` for the singleton dim of `[E, 1, 1]`), so the kernel's `per_channel_quant` branch read expert 0's scale for every expert or indexed past the buffer. The combination tests already skipped "per-tensor weights + per-token activations" for the Triton experts as NYI, although `TritonExperts._supports_quant_scheme` advertises the pair. This PR passes the expert stride unconditionally and broadcasts singleton scale dims, and narrows the NYI gate to the still-unsupported "per-channel weights + per-tensor activations" case so the combination suite covers the fixed pair.

The bf16 Triton expert path is already invariant on `main` (`get_default_config`/`get_moe_configs` pin the tile config under the flag); the reporter's bf16 mismatch was on 0.27.1.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_online_fp8_moe_logprobs_bitwise_bs1_vs_bsN` (granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct, `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`, greedy, BS=1 vs BS=8 bitwise tokens+logprobs). Fails on `main`, passes with this PR.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: the per-tensor-weight + per-token-activation FP8 config is no longer skipped for `TritonExperts` / `BatchedTritonExperts` / `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts`.
- Reporter's reproducer (co-batch and writer-suffix modes) against a running server.
- Kernel check: `fused_experts` vs `tests.kernels.utils.torch_experts`, E=32, N=1024, K=2048, M=128, topk=4, per-tensor `[E,1,1]` weight scales: max abs err 0.010 with per-tensor activations, 0.003 with per-token activations (before the launcher fix the per-token case returned values in the thousands).
- Existing suites: `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py::test_fused_moe`, pre-commit, `mypy-3.12`.

Hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), WSL2, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The modular kernel combination suite itself does not run on this WSL2 machine (spawned worker fails with `CUDA error: invalid resource handle` on unmodified `main` too), so that part relies on CI and on the independent H20 run linked below.

## Test Result

- Reporter's probe, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 --quantization fp8`, before: A-alone vs A-with-B first token flip at 11 (logprob gap 0.166), warm-vs-cold flip at 11 (gap 0.347). After: every comparison identical, both rounds.
- gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` (tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py): default (no flag) 34.1%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on `main` 34.3%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with this PR 32.7%. Per-token activation quantization is strictly finer than per-tensor, and the kernel-level error is lower, so the small delta is sampling noise from a 1B model.
- New e2e test: PASS with the PR, FAIL on `main` ("logprobs are not bitwise equal between BS=1 and BS=8; max abs diff 2.2e-01").
- Independent cross-architecture validation by @CarrotSwordsman on H20 (sm_90, real Linux GPU, driver 535), [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57092#issuecomment-5730213177): the same e2e test FAILS on a clean 0.28.0+cu129 wheel (max abs diff 2.8e-01) and PASSES with this PR's files applied, reproducing and eliminating the #57016 symptom on Hopper. Their `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` run on the patched wheel was 8 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped, the two failures being `deep_gemm`'s `NVCC >= 12.3` assert in a container pinned to 12.1. As they note, that suite does not discriminate against a release wheel (the pre-PR NYI skip is not present there to be removed), so the e2e pair is the evidence in that setup.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` (non-DeepGEMM): 164 passed, 20 skipped. `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k test_fused_moe`: 241 passed. pre-commit and `mypy-3.12` clean on all changed files.

> Note: since #53585, online per-tensor FP8 is selected with `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`; commands above that use `--quantization fp8` predate that change.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #57016 (checked with `gh pr list --search "57016 in:body"` and by searching open PRs for "batch invariant moe"); #55881 is the XPU MoE variant and does not touch the CUDA Triton path or FP8 activation quantization.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and drafting; every line was reviewed and every test run by the submitter.

title: [Kimi K3 Bug] Fix kimi k3 reasoning parser
author: yewentao256
body:
## Purpose

This bug from a real user case, minimal reproduce command:

```bash

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark","method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"standard"}'   --use-replayssm   --max-num-seqs 48
```

## Test

Use this script

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce Kimi-K3 truncated-reasoning classification through vLLM."""

import json
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen


URL = "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions"
MODEL = "moonshotai/Kimi-K3"

payload = {
    "model": MODEL,
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": (
                "Solve this carefully: find the exact number of distinct ways to "
                "color the vertices of a dodecahedron with four colors, modulo all "
                "rotational symmetries. Return only the required JSON after reasoning."
            ),
        }
    ],
    "temperature": 0,
    # Deliberately stop K3 before it can finish its reasoning.
    "max_tokens": 16,
    "stream": False,
    "response_format": {
        "type": "json_schema",
        "json_schema": {
            "name": "answer",
            "strict": True,
            "schema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["answer"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
    "chat_template_kwargs": {
        "thinking": True,
        "enable_thinking": True,
    },
}

request = Request(
    URL,
    data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
    headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer EMPTY",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    method="POST",
)

try:
    with urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
        result = json.load(response)
except HTTPError as error:
    print(f"HTTP {error.code}: {error.read().decode('utf-8', errors='replace')}")
    raise SystemExit(1) from error
except URLError as error:
    print(f"Cannot connect to {URL}: {error.reason}")
    raise SystemExit(1) from error

choice = result["choices"][0]
message = choice["message"]
content = message.get("content")
reasoning = message.get("reasoning") or message.get("reasoning_content")

print(f"finish_reason: {choice.get('finish_reason')}")
print(f"content: {content!r}")
print(f"reasoning: {reasoning!r}")

if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length" and content and not reasoning:
    print("\nBUG reproduced: truncated reasoning was incorrectly returned as content.")
elif choice.get("finish_reason") == "length" and reasoning and not content:
    print("\nFIX verified: truncated text is reasoning; content is empty.")
else:
    print("\nThe model did not take the expected truncation path; rerun the request.")

```
Before:

```bash
python repro_kimi_k3_truncated_reasoning.py 
finish_reason: length
content: 'We need solve. Need return only JSON after reasoning. Need compute exact number of'
reasoning: None

BUG reproduced: truncated reasoning was incorrectly returned as content.
```

Now

```bash
python repro_kimi_k3_truncated_reasoning.py
finish_reason: length
content: None
reasoning: 'We need solve. Need return only JSON after reasoning. Need compute exact number of'

FIX verified: truncated text is reasoning; content is empty.
```

title: [BugFix][KV Connector] Fix Deadlock with KVConnector + MTP under KV Pressure
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
## Purpose

Scheduler can deadlock under KV memory pressure with MTP + KV connector --- encountered in production deployment of GLM5.2

### Example

- 2 requests A (needs 4 blocks + 1 for mtp), B (needs 3 blocks + 1 for mtp)
- Total blocks 7

#### Step 1 — A and B arrive and get added to `skipped_waiting` queue

A is admitted (4 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`
B is admitted (3 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`

- result: 
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

#### Step 2 — A's transfer lands. 

Schedule the `skipped_waiting` queue first. Peek `skipped_waiting` → A.

`_is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS)` is True → `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request(A)` succeeds → `A.status=WAITING` 

Then, schedule A. Need to allocate for the MTP blocks [these are only allocated after async load]. We need 1 block, but there is 0 left. `allocate_slots` returns None and we `break` (end attempting to schedule.

- result:
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

As we can see, the queues are in the same state as before this step, and will continue to be in this state (trying to schedule A, asking to allocate blocks) forever.

#### Step 3 onward — Same cycle

Peek `skipped_waiting` → still A, now status WAITING. _is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING) is False, so no promotion branch; straight to allocation; fails; break. Spin forever.

## Root Cause

Async KV load is allocated without lookahead slots (see `limit_lookahead_tokens`), and `_request_remaining_blocks()` -- which backs the `_inflight_prefill_reserved_blocks()` admission gate -- does not count them either. 

Then, after the `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV` is done, we ask `allocate_slots()` for the lookahead margin on top ---> if this block is not available, we `break` --- with this request at the front of the `skipped_waiting` queue. If no requests are running, then no new blocks come free and we deadlock in this loop

**So there is a mismatch in the blocks reserved and what is actually needed to start running**

## Test Plan

- unit test
- reproducer (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57104#issuecomment-5701283900)

## Test Result

title: [Bugfix][ModelLoader] Make enable_weights_track check quantized layers
author: siliangchen-amd
body:
## Purpose

`enable_weights_track` is meant to catch weights a checkpoint did not provide, but it exempts every parameter of any layer whose quant method defines `process_weights_after_loading`. `QuantizeMethodBase` defines it, so that is every linear, MoE and embedding layer, quantized or not. On a quantized model the opt-in check therefore never fires: a block-FP8 checkpoint missing a `weight_scale_inv` loads and serves garbage.

- For quantized models, where the flag is opt-in, only KV-cache quantization parameters, empty placeholders, fbgemm_fp8's config-built `input_scale_ub` and online-quantization parameters stay exempt. The check now also reaches the model's unquantized layers, such as a vision tower. Unquantized models, where the check is on by default, are unchanged.
- `MoERunner.load_weights` now prefixes `routed_experts.`, so the names it returns match the registered parameters; otherwise every expert weight is reported as missing once the check is on.

## Related PRs

- #41086 added `enable_weights_track` together with the module-wide exemption narrowed here.
- #35074 tracked quantized models by default and was reverted the same day (#35309); the false positives reported against it (#35299, #35305) were GPTQ/AWQ MoE `g_idx` parameters, which vLLM no longer registers. Here quantized models stay opt-in; the KV-cache exemption follows #35074 and the empty-placeholder one #35299.
- #34930 (open) tracks quantized models by default with a warning and keeps the current exemption. It changes when the check runs, this PR what it checks; both edit `track_weights_loading`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py`: three new cases, each failing if its part of the change is reverted. They run in CI's Model Executor job.
- Load one checkpoint or more per quantization format with `--model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_weights_track": true}'`, intact and with one tensor removed.

## Test Result

All with the flag on.

End to end on MI325X, DeepSeek on 8x MI300X; measured on earlier revisions of this PR, which exempted fewer parameters, the intact checkpoints on vLLM 0.27.1 with the change applied.

| checkpoint | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 repack, `attn.wo_a` block scale missing in all 43 layers | boots, serves, gsm8k 0.00 | refuses to load, names the 43 `wo_a.weight_scale_inv` |
| same repack with `wo_a` in `ignored_layers` (its correct config) | boots | boots, gsm8k 1.00 (50 samples) |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 with one `weight_scale_inv` removed | boots, outputs garbage | refuses to load, names that parameter |
| intact: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8, Qwen3-14B-FP8, gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4), Qwen3-30B-A3B (bf16) | boots | boots |

Load check on main with this PR on MI300X, running vLLM's loader up to and including the check, with no inference. Every checkpoint below loads intact. With the listed tensor removed from a `down_proj` or `o_proj`, unless named otherwise, the load is refused and names exactly that parameter; main accepts all of them. Main checks 11–28% of these checkpoints' parameters and this PR 63–100%; the rest are KV-cache quantization parameters, empty placeholders and fbgemm's `input_scale_ub`.

| format | checkpoints | tensor removed |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 (block), Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct-FP8 (static), Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-KV | `weight_scale_inv`, `input_scale` |
| compressed-tensors | Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct FP8-dynamic and W8A8, Qwen3-0.6B W4A16, Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8-dynamic and AWQ-4bit (MoE) | `weight_scale`, `weight_packed` |
| AWQ, GPTQ | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct AWQ and GPTQ-Int4, Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 (MoE) | `qweight` |
| ModelOpt, Quark | Qwen3-8B-FP8 (ModelOpt), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct PTPC (Quark) | `input_scale`, `weight_scale` |
| fbgemm_fp8 | Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct FBGEMM | `weight_scale` |
| vision-language | Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-FP8, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct FP8-dynamic | a weight scale; vision-tower `attn.proj.bias` |
| MTP draft | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 | `o_proj.weight_scale_inv`; `fc.weight`; `lm_head.weight` |

Online fp8 on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct loads and stays exempt. A missing shard of a fused parameter (one of q/k/v or gate/up, or one expert) is still not detected, as on main, because the fused parameter is reported loaded.

`test_registry.py`: 9 passed. `models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_mla` and `lora/test_sequence_classification.py`, which failed in this PR's first CI run, pass locally.

AI-assisted (Claude); I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom) while optimizing DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix MLA RoPE fused-kernel tests for TheRock image
author: mawong-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
The `Core Operations Kernels` test group fails on TheRock image (see [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12914/list?sid=01a09eed-c3fc-4155-8ae7-ad55792cdc2c&open=false)). This has been root-caused to the Triton 3.8 upgrade.
Specifically, in the computation of RoPE, we compute terms similar to  `x * cos - y * sin`. In Triton 3.7, the LLVM backend lowers to `FMA_F16(x, cos, MUL_F16(-y, sin))`, which is the same as the HIP reference fused kernel. However, in Triton 3.8, the LLVM backend instead lowers to `FMA_F16(-y, sin, MUL_F16(x, cos))`.
In short, the LLVM backend makes a different choice for which product to pre-round to F16 in the fused multiply-add. This pre-rounding can lead to a 1 ULP difference (wrt the product) compared to a hypothetical reference which does all the arithmetic in FP32 before rounding to F16 once at the end.
Thus, the 2 choices of which product to pre-round can lead to differ by up to 2 ULP wrt `max(abs(x * cos), abs(-y * sin))`. The current tolerances do not adequately capture the subtleties in this regime, which is partly why the tolerances for this test have been adjusted at least 3 separate times (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51083, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46409, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32408).

## Purpose
This PR reworks and unifies the tolerances for this test for half-precision dtypes on ROCm.
Specifically, for the non-RoPE portions of the tensors, we compare to the references using default `atol` and `rtol`. For the RoPE portions of the tensors, we now have a 2 part test:

1. Compare to the references using default `atol` and `rtol`. The number of failing elements must not exceed 0.01 (for bf16) or 0.0001 (for fp16) of all elements.
2. For all failing elements, check that they differ from the reference elements by up to 2 ULP wrt the relevant products (e.g. `max(abs(x * cos), abs(-y * sin), abs(-x * sin), abs(y * cos))` for non-Neox-style RoPE).

## Test Plan
For ROCm 10:
Run the Core Operations Kernels test group on AMD CI [with this fix](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002/list) applied vs [without this fix](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13000/list).

For ROCm 7.2:
Run the Core Operations Kernels test group as part of CI on this PR.

## Test Result
The Core Operations Kernels test group is fixed on ROCm 10, and there are no test regressions on both ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix macOS multimodal SHM cache initialization
author: shaohuaxi
body:
## Purpose

On macOS, enabling `--mm-processor-cache-type shm` without setting `VLLM_OBJECT_STORAGE_SHM_BUFFER_NAME` fails during cache initialization:

```text
OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long
```

The generated name is 63 characters long. This change uses a shorter prefix and URL-safe Base64 encoding of the full UUID to produce a 30-character name, while preserving name reuse within a process tree and explicit environment overrides.

The longer default was introduced in #32429, and the macOS failure was previously noted in #47966. No open PR addressing this naming issue was found during the duplicate check.

## Test Plan

Tested on macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.13, using the modified Python sources in an existing CPU environment.

The new regression test checks that the generated name fits macOS's 30-character limit. The existing SHM cache eviction test exercises the cache with the generated default name.

```bash
env -u VLLM_OBJECT_STORAGE_SHM_BUFFER_NAME \
  VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/test_envs.py tests/multimodal/test_cache.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
```

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the generated default name is 63 characters long and the SHM cache eviction test fails on macOS with `File name too long`.
- After the fix: **70 passed, 1 skipped**. The skipped test requires CUDA.
- The existing SHM cache eviction test passes with the generated default name.
- Pre-commit checks and mypy 3.12 pass.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with implementation and testing.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix Qwen3-ASR audio preprocessing parity
author: MatthewCYM
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #56981.

Qwen3-ASR currently inherits Omni's waveform padding and forces a Whisper feature extractor, which can change audio features and placeholder counts relative to the checkpoint's upstream processor.

Following the review feedback, this revision:

- Uses the upstream Transformers `Qwen3ASRProcessor` and removes the bundled processor and its registration.
- Requires Transformers >=5.13.0 and updates the corresponding test metadata.
- Uses `BaseMultiModalProcessor` without Omni's waveform padding.
- Processes clips independently and packs valid features, preserving parity across differently sized clips and partial cache hits.
- Preserves text-only and precomputed-feature inputs.

Both checkpoint formats remain supported: the original checkpoint declares `WhisperFeatureExtractor`, while the native `-hf` checkpoint declares `Qwen3ASRFeatureExtractor`.

No shared Omni/VL implementation, model weights, encoder kernels, or speculative-decoding behavior is changed.


## Test Plan

Validated against upstream main `528fa835fd37d0805a824d516e22f88df61a771a`
  with Transformers 5.13.0 and 5.17.0.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_asr.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py \
  tests/multimodal/test_audio.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_asr_mrope.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_qwen3_asr_sanitize_prompt.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing.py \
  -k 'not transformers and (Qwen3-ASR or test_qwen3_asr or test_qwen3_omni or test_audio.py or ForcedAligner or test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing)' \
  -q
```

- 152 repository tests passed per Transformers version, including all 50 new regression cases.
- Supplementary local validation passed another 63 pytest cases and four realtime-processor comparisons per version. These supplementary checks are not all included in this PR.
- Applicable repository pre-commit hooks, the scoped manual Python 3.12 mypy hook, and whitespace checks passed.

### Model validation

Tested both `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` and `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf` with both Transformers versions.

Each run compared raw audio against independently computed upstream features in the same vLLM engine, using 32 LibriSpeech test-clean utterances plus 32 near-hop-boundary variants. Settings: single H100, BF16, greedy decoding, eager execution, `max_num_seqs=1`, and processor/prefix caches disabled.

All four model/version combinations matched prompt IDs and generated token IDs on 64/64 clips. Raw/reference WER was 2.8846% in every run. This is a bounded correctness evaluation, not a full-split accuracy or speed benchmark.

Environment: Python 3.13.15, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, and NumPy 2.4.6. Tests used this checkout's Python source with existing vLLM 0.29 CUDA extensions, not a fresh CUDA build. Full upstream CI remains necessary. Realtime and forced-aligner checks cover preprocessing, not complete streaming or timestamp-accuracy evaluation.

## Related work and disclosure

This uses the processor hook introduced by #53610; that refactor does not implement this ASR preprocessing fix. #57076 addresses the separate post-expansion truncation issue.

AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation, and test preparation.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Restore causal image SWA for DeepSeek V4.1
author: Juntian777
body:
## Summary

Restore causal sliding-window attention for image tokens in DeepSeek V4.1 VL.

V4.1 inherited the image visibility rules used by DeepSeek V4 Vision-Exp: tokens inside an image could attend to earlier image tokens outside the sliding window and to future image tokens. This differs from the [official V4.1 reference implementation](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277/inference/model.py#L410), where `_window_kv` uses `get_window_topk_idxs` and both image and text tokens attend to the same causal window. With a window of 128, query position `p` should see only `[max(0, p - 127), p]` through SWA.

The incorrect widening affects full-image prefill as well as continuation chunks. For example, at the beginning of image span `[1900, 3948)`, the inherited rule exposes future image tokens through position 3947; the V4.1 reference permits only positions 1773 through 1900.

The key line in the [official `get_window_topk_idxs`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/blob/dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277/inference/model.py#L421) is:

```python
idxs = torch.where(idxs > end, -1, idxs)
```

The reference masks every index greater than the query position with `-1`; this is a causal 128-token window, including the current token. Executing the published `get_window_topk_idxs` at query position 1900 produces exactly 128 indices, from 1773 through 1900, with no future positions.

## Changes

- Disable multimodal prefix-LM/bidirectional-range configuration for V4.1.
- Make the shared SWA metadata builder respect an explicit `is_mm_prefix_lm=False`, keeping V4.1 metadata and paged indices causal.
- Set the V4.1 attention-side image window extension to zero. Image preprocessing, the vision encoder, and `vision_max_n_token` remain unchanged.
- Keep the existing causal gather lengths and workspace sizes. The final diff does not change NVIDIA or AMD workspace allocation.
- Add six regression cases: full prefill and continuation prefill, each with compression ratios `0/1/2`. Verify causal key positions in both gathered and paged indices, gather/CPU-plan consistency, and absence of image visibility extensions.

V4 Vision-Exp retains its existing image visibility behavior.

## Validation

Run on GB200:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py \
  -k 'not test_builder_' -q --tb=short
```

**Result: 30 passed, 3 deselected.** The three existing builder tests require an inaccessible gated Hugging Face configuration. The new regression uses a local configuration and requires no model download.

Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. A local FlashMLA numerical sanity check also matched the causal reference, retaining a gather length of 227 and a first-query SWA length of 128 for `seq_len=4000`, `query_len=100`, and image span `[1900, 3948)`.

Full-model VL accuracy, generation-length evaluation, and AMD runtime validation were not run. The evidence here establishes attention-window correctness at the metadata/kernel level.

## Related work

Open-PR searches for SWA/gather, V4.1/prefill, and V4.1/causal/image found no other matching fix. [#56986](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56986) concerns cross-layer compressed-KV gather reuse; it does not correct the image attention-window semantics addressed here.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for analysis, implementation, and validation.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][KV Offload] Use private pinned tensors for CPU KV offload
author: yuzhouo7
body:
## Purpose

Native CPU KV offload stalled during startup on an 8x MI308X node with TP8 and a 500 GiB offload pool. Six ranks reported `cudaHostRegister failed (code=1)`, and the engine never became ready.

`_uses_shared_region()` includes ROCm through `is_cuda_alike()`, so each worker registers the entire shared mmap region. Exclude ROCm to use the existing private per-rank pinned tensor allocator instead. The CUDA path is unchanged; ROCm no longer uses shared-region replicated KV deduplication.

Unlike #51081 (chunked registration) and #52296 (coordinated registration), this change bypasses shared mmap allocation on ROCm.

## Test Plan

Tested with vLLM 0.29.0 and ROCm 7.2.3 on two 8x MI308X hosts, running GLM-5.3 with TP8, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, and:

    --kv-offloading-size 500 --kv-offloading-backend native

Check startup and generation, then evict a cached 32K prompt from GPU KV cache using distinct filler prompts and replay it.

## Test Result

- Both hosts completed startup and served generation requests.
- Transfer counters confirmed CPU-to-GPU KV reload after eviction.
- The tested 32K gold-answer prompt returned the expected answer on both the cold request and the post-eviction replay.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Stop sleep(level=2) from zeroing compressed-tensors KV scales
author: AlanFokCo
body:
## Purpose

`sleep(level=2)` zeroes the calibrated KV-cache scales of compressed-tensors
KV-FP8 checkpoints, so the first request after a weights-only reload — the shape an
RL weight-sync uses — returns **NaN logprobs and a wrong first token**.

Level 2 discards the weights allocation without keeping a copy, and the only
generic safety net is the `named_buffers()` snapshot in `Worker.sleep()` /
`Worker.wake_up()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:253`, `:291`) — that file has no
`named_parameters` walk. `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading()`
rebinds `_q_scale`/`_k_scale`/`_v_scale` onto the `nn.Parameter` placeholders,
moving those names out of `_buffers`, so the snapshot never sees them and they come
back as blank pages reading `0.0`. `_prob_scale`, never rebound, survives — that
asymmetry pinpoints the cause, and every other KV-cache quant method is unaffected
because it `.copy_()`s into the existing buffer (`kv_cache.py:152/156/157/195`).

**Fix (+10/−3, one file):** `register_buffer()` the three scales — the form
`set_default_quant_scales(register_buffer=True)` created them in
(`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:129-135`). `register_buffer()`
rather than `.copy_()` because ATTN_HEAD loads `num_kv_heads` scales into a buffer
created 0-dim; `persistent=True` because `sharded_state_loader.py:162` needs the
keys. Shape, dtype, device, virtual address and the `state_dict` key set are
unchanged (measured: same keys, shapes and dtypes, 0 pointer moves). The single exit
covers TENSOR and ATTN_HEAD by measurement, MLA and the draft model statically (same
`_init_kv_cache_quant`, same buffers snapshotted) — we have not run MLA or
spec-decode.

We fixed the quant method rather than the snapshot because compressed-tensors is the
only one that breaks that buffer invariant; a worker-level `named_parameters()` net
would also cover the W8A8 case below, but it carries a host-memory cost and a policy
question, so it belongs in its own change.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs/issues for compressed-tensors KV scales, `sleep(level=2)`,
`_q/_k/_v_scale`, the `named_buffers` snapshot and `register_buffer`: nothing open
addresses this. Nearest hits #38975 (`_prob_scale_float` sync, no sleep involved)
and #55206 (release pinned host memory after `wake_up`). Related RFCs #48310, #48312.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py -k compressed_tensors_kv_scale
cd tests && VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s basic_correctness/test_mem.py
```

New case `test_deep_sleep_fp8_kvcache_compressed_tensors_kv_scale`, above the two
`…_mrv1` cases (the second builds its engine in the pytest parent and leaves its 0.9
KV pool mapped there, which a fork inherits). It asserts registration form, non-zero
values, exact equality with the pre-sleep copies, and greedy output/logprob parity
against a never-slept control, plus a `sleep(level=1)` negative control and an
anti-vacuity probe that the weights really were discarded and reloaded. Red arm =
revert only the fix. Exact equality is deliberate: an injected 4.657e-09
perturbation of these scales flipped a greedy decision at token 10.

Checkpoint `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor` (static
`kv_cache_scheme`, so the scales are genuinely calibrated; already used by
`tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py`). Measured floor 2.46 + 0.69 GiB, so
`gpu_memory_utilization=0.6` fits the `h200_18gb` slice this file runs on — no
`large_gpu_mark`, **not skipped in CI**.

## Test result (H20)

| arm | rc | result |
|---|---|---|
| pristine tree | **1** | `1 failed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 16.37s` — assertion names all 66 lost scales |
| with this fix | **0** | `1 passed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 23.18s` |
| with this fix, 10.8 GiB budget (≡ 18 GiB slice @ util 0.6) | **0** | `1 passed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 22.16s` |
| whole file as CI invokes it | **0** | `14 passed, 41 warnings in 221.09s` |

With the fix, output is **bit-exact against the never-slept control** (36/36 rounds,
324-tensor census 0 zeroed / 0 pointer moves), the noise floor is 0, and
`sleep(level=1)` is a clean negative control. Lint on the two changed files:
`ruff check` / `ruff format --diff` / `py_compile` clean and
`pre-commit run --files <both>` 13 Passed / 0 Failed — including
`check-forbidden-imports`, which is why the test resolves the hub id with the shared
`hf_api()` helper.

<details>
<summary>Full characterization on the 8B checkpoint (96/96 scales, NaN logprobs, FLASHINFER, CUDA graphs, TP=2, ATTN_HEAD)</summary>

8B `nm-testing/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-KV-FP8-tensor-static_minmax`, greedy with
logprobs: unfixed, **96/96** parameter-form scales read back `0.0` while **0/32**
buffer-form did and all 34,560 logprobs are NaN; with the fix, **36/36 rounds
bit-exact** vs the reload-only control, 324-tensor census 0 zeroed / 0 pointer
moves. Noise floor 0 (no-sleep reload 36/36 bit-exact; 22 pre-sleep references
across 22 processes identical); `sleep(level=1)` clean (0/128 changed). FLASHINFER
reproduces it identically, so it is not backend-specific; with CUDA graphs on, wake
re-captures nothing; at TP=2 exactly those 96 names flip form; ATTN_HEAD (`[8,1,1]`)
covered; old-format `quant_method="fp8"` unaffected at these scales.

</details>

## Model evaluation

GSM8K, full 1319-question test set, vLLM's own harness
(`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` — `_build_gsm8k_prompts` / `get_answer_value` /
`_score_gsm8k`; 5-shot, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, seed 0) on
`nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor` with
`kv_cache_dtype=fp8`:

| arm | accuracy | invalid | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — never slept | 2.65% (35/1319) | 0.6% | — |
| B — level=2 → wake(weights) → weights-only reload → wake(kv_cache), **with fix** | 2.65% (35/1319) | 0.6% | **1319/1319 byte-identical output** |
| C — same sequence, **without fix** | **0.00% (0/1319)** | **100%** | 0/1319 |

Absolute accuracy is low because TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat is weak at 5-shot GSM8K; the
signal is that B reproduces A byte-for-byte while C collapses (all 66
`_q/_k/_v_scale` read back `0.0`, every response runs to `max_tokens`, most decoding
to an empty string). Both sleeping arms assert the weights pool really was discarded
and the reload really restored 135 parameters bit-exactly, so the delta can only
come from the scales. A 500-question subset gave the same picture (500/500).

## Scope

The documented level-2 recovery -- `collective_rpc("reload_weights")` -- self-heals, and
this PR does not claim otherwise: the layerwise path re-creates the `k_scale`/`v_scale`
placeholders before replaying the checkpoint, so `process_weights_after_loading()` runs
again (measured: green with and without the fix). What does not self-heal is anything
that skips it: `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` with no reload at all,
`reload_weights(is_checkpoint_format=False)` (the kernel-format branch, `param.copy_()`
only, next to the `# TODO: buffers?`), and a third-party `model.load_weights()`. There
the `named_buffers()` snapshot is the only net, which is the level-2 contract in
`docs/features/sleep_mode.md` ("the model's buffers are kept in CPU") and the invariant
`test_static_model_tensors_survive_level2_restore` asserts at the same point. Measured
matrix and the exact reason a plain reload cannot restore them: follow-up comment.

## Platforms

Verified on CUDA/H20 only. The AMD mirror of `basic_correctness` collects this test
(`requires_fp8` is true on CDNA, sleep mode is available on MI3xx) and two assertions are
platform-sensitive: `discarded["all_zero"]`, which relies on the driver handing back zeroed
pages, and the bit-exact logprob comparison. If the mirror goes red we will relax those two
(tolerance / platform guard) and keep the buffer-form assertion, which is the point of the test.

## Not covered (disclosed)

- W8A8 `weight_scale` / `input_scale` are `nn.Parameter` too and are lost by the
  same mechanism: on `neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV`, **449 of 580**
  censused tensors read back `0.0` after level=2 + a weights-only reload (256
  weight/input scales, 129 weights, 64 norms), while its 128 KV/attention scales are
  buffers and survive. Needs the worker-level net above — separate change.
- The test pins `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, like the two adjacent `…_mrv1` cases.
  Both runners share `Worker.sleep()` and `_sleep_saved_buffers`, but we have not
  measured the V2 runner and do not claim it here.
- TP=2 shows a pre-existing per-engine output bimodality (2 of 24 snapshots; same
  signature with `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, also in the unfixed control arm) —
  unrelated to sleep or to this patch.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Reject non-contiguous routing tensors
author: NikitaLogvinenko
body:
## Purpose

MoE routing kernels consume `topk_ids` and `topk_weights` as dense linear
buffers. A sliced routing result such as `wide[:, :top_k]` can have shape
`(num_tokens, top_k)` but stride `(wide_top_k, 1)`. The previous
`topk_weights.stride(1) == 1` checks accepted this layout, while the kernels
ignored the row stride and could silently read incorrect routing data.

This change fails fast without introducing hidden copies:

- validate `topk_ids` in the `moe_align_block_size` C++ wrapper before the
  CUDA kernel launch;
- require fully contiguous `topk_weights` at the shared MoE dispatch boundary;
- apply the same validation in the direct Triton launcher used by the modular
  Triton backend;
- reject non-contiguous `topk_weights`/`topk_ids` once in
  `FusedMoERouter.select_experts`, so every modular backend is covered, not
  only Triton. FlashInfer CUTLASS, for example, also reads these as dense
  buffers. ZAYA1 (#65302) hit this with a custom routing function that
  returned column slices of one packed `[num_tokens, 2 * top_k]` tensor: token
  1 silently got token 0's expert id as its weight. All in-tree routers already
  return contiguous tensors.

## Test Plan

- Add a regression test passing sliced, non-contiguous `topk_ids` to
  `moe_align_block_size`.
- Add a regression test passing sliced, non-contiguous `topk_weights` to the
  Triton MoE launcher.
- Add a regression test where a custom routing function returns column slices
  of a packed tensor through `create_fused_moe_router(...).select_experts`.
- Run the relevant formatting and static-analysis hooks.

## Test Result

Passed:

- `ruff-check`
- `ruff-format`
- `clang-format`
- `typos`
- `check-spdx-header`
- `git diff --check`
- Python bytecode compilation for the changed Python files

The CUDA regression test was not run locally because the source-tree C++
extension was not rebuilt. The repository virtual environment also cannot run
pytest currently because it lacks `tblib` and contains an incompatible PyTorch
installation; CI is expected to run both regression tests against a matching
build.

### Update (@mgoin): merged main, added the router-boundary check

Merged latest `main`; there were no conflicts once git followed the
`csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/` to `csrc/moe/` rename. Rebuilt
`_moe_C_stable_libtorch` on B300 and ran:

```
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_align_block_size.py
```

2162 passed, 6 skipped, 1 failed. Both regression tests above pass, including
the C++ `topk_ids` check. The failure,
`test_unquantized_bf16_flashinfer_trtllm_backend`, also fails without this PR
(`AttributeError: 'Module' object has no attribute 'moe_config'` in the test's
layer fixture).

Not a duplicate: this is still the only open PR on non-contiguous MoE routing
tensors; #65302 only works around the issue inside the ZAYA1 model.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex was used for investigation, implementation, and test
orchestration. The submitter reviewed all changed lines before submission.



The update was written with Claude Code (AI-assisted) and approved by @mgoin;
the tests above ran on a B300.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][GLM-5.3-Flash] Apply deferred tilelang.jit already on attribute access
author: simondanielsson
body:
## Purpose

Required to run GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350, otherwise errors during warmup with:

```bash
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup.py", line 969, in compile_many
  self.compile(compile_key)
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 141, in launch
  return compile_tilelang(jit_impl, *args, **call_kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 104, in compile_tilelang
  compiled = jit_impl.compile(*args, **kwargs)
AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

### Why

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51159 added lazy import of tilelang and made the `tilelang_jit` decorator return a **regular function on ROCm** instead of a `tilelang.jit.JITImpl`. On ROCm, this function would create and return the JITImpl when **called**. That's fine as long as you just _call_ the kernel the first time you need it, which is how warmup was previously done.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50178 refactored the warmup logic of tilelang mHC kernels. Previously the warmup was done by literally calling/running the mHC layers. After that PR, warmup now runs `.compile(...)` on the kernel to compile it, and later caches the compiled kernel manually. That's ok on CUDA where the kernel is a JITImpl, but not on ROCm where it's a regular function.

Hence the assumption that the tilelang kernel will be _called_ the first time it's used is no longer true. It's no longer launched during warmup, just `.compiled()`. This PR ensures that the first time we touch the (lazily created) kernel we convert it into a JITImpl to be compiled.

## Test Plan

title: [Bugfix][PP][Spec Decode] MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 aux-state relay at PP > 1 and per-stage FlashInfer autotune
author: venkywonka
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enables EAGLE3 for MiniMax-M3 (NVIDIA model file) at PP > 1 on Model Runner V2, and scopes FlashInfer autotune to each PP stage's TP group, fixing a startup deadlock. Builds on #50514 (PP aux-state relay), changes the autotune sync from #50892, supersedes #57198.

Motivation: MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 PP2/TP4 + EAGLE3 serving on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (also needs #59081, which supersedes #47665). No performance claim; the speedup there comes from split-K admission (#45450 / #52879 / #56148).

## Claims

1. **MiniMax-M3 + EAGLE3 runs at PP > 1.** Base rejects it at load (`ValueError: ... does not support eagle3 with pipeline parallelism`). The drafter then gets all aux states every step; acceptance length and GSM8K match TP8.
2. **FlashInfer autotune no longer deadlocks at PP > 1** when stages tune different shapes. Each stage tunes within its TP group and writes `<cache>_tp_<ranks>.json`. PP = 1 is unchanged.

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` + `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3`, offline `LLM`, greedy, cold autotune. Both arms: vLLM 213c379 + FP8 Triton-indexer enablement (as in #47665; needed on SM120) + #56148's Triton-attention guard hunks (not its split-K path). Arms differ only in this PR's files as of 4683f1e3 (since then: `kernel_warmup.py` comments only; extractor hunk dropped).

| Config | Aux relay (steps) | Mean AL | GSM8K-200 spec / no-spec | Stage cache entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | – | 3.471 | 94.5 / 94.5 | unchanged |
| PP2/TP4 | 4600/4600 | 3.460, 3.449, 3.452 | 95.5 / 95.5 | 140 / 80 |
| PP3/TP2 | 7200/7200 | 3.469 | 94.0 / – | 140 / 80 / 80 |
| PP4/TP1 | 9200/9200 | 3.498 | 94.0 / – | 140 / 80 / 80 / 80 |

AL: 32 GSM8K prompts × 256 tokens. GSM8K-200: first 200 test questions, chat, thinking on, 0-shot, max 2048 tokens; all within ~1 SE. Autotune ≤10 s/stage.

Main engine args (PP2/TP4):
```text
-tp 4 -pp 2 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend marlin --max-model-len 65536 --language-model-only
--max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 12 --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95
--disable-custom-all-reduce --enable-prefix-caching --seed 0
--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3","num_speculative_tokens":3,
  "draft_tensor_parallel_size":4,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
```

**Base** (same image, base files):
- With these args: the `ValueError` on all 8 ranks.
- Without `--speculative-config`: hangs in autotune; `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'` avoids it. PR `model.py` with base `kernel_warmup.py` + EAGLE3 hangs too (both changes needed).
- Non-spec PP2/TP4 (autotune off, 16 prompts, two setups): identical greedy outputs 2–3/16 PR vs base, 2–5/16 PR vs PR (mean hidden cosine .95–.97): no detectable PR effect.

**Non-MiniMax, H200:** Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 bf16 PP2/TP2, PR vs base: both start; PR writes per-stage caches; GSM8K-200 96.0 vs 95.5 (default MoE, 0 tuned entries), 95.5 vs 94.0 (`flashinfer_cutlass`, 44 entries/stage): equivalent.

**Pre-existing, not fixed here:** a warm restart with a `flashinfer_cutlass` cache at PP2/TP2 hangs in base and PR (TP rank 0 hits the cache, rank 1 re-tunes); matches #57423 (fixes: #57579, #57635; untested).

@SloptimistPrime reported the autotune fix on 6x GB10 (SM121), TP2/PP3 (#57198); their test commit 1291f3fe is not included.

**CPU tests and lint:**
```bash
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py
# 17 passed (11 added). Production files reverted: 8 of the 11 fail
# (incl. PP = 1 layer-0 tap); the 3 passing are PP = 1 / no-aux guards.
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files $(git diff --name-only 5c3b61e9)
# all pass, incl. mypy 3.10-3.13 and test tethering
```

## Details

**Root cause, autotune.** Since #50892 all ranks sync over the world group (cache broadcast, barrier, per-tactic all-reduce). PP stages can tune different shapes (140 vs 80 `mxfp8_gemm` entries), so PP0 waits on a collective PP1 never joins. Fix: at PP > 1, leader, broadcast, barrier, timing average and cache file use the stage's TP group.

**Root cause, MiniMax-M3.** No #50514 opt-in; taps used stage-local layer indices. Fix: set `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp` and use the `EagleModelMixin` helpers (global indices, pack local / collect upstream taps), like Llama, Qwen2, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3. Tap 0 aliases `residual`, which fused add-RMSNorm updates in place, so it is cloned when layer 0 is a tap (any PP size; CPU-tested; GPU runs above use taps 2/30/57).

**Dropped:** #57290's `extract_hidden_states` draft PP = 1 hunk (extractor-only; EAGLE3 unaffected): at PP2 it turned a config-time `NotImplementedError` into a startup `AssertionError` (`ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` needs a change; separate PR). Supersedes earlier status comments.

**Size and tradeoffs.** 2 production files, +40/−13. Tests +342/−2 (CPU fakes). At PP > 1, old unsuffixed caches are not read (one re-tune) and stages may pick different tactics for the same shape (unmeasured). Each PP hop carries one extra `[tokens, hidden]` tensor per upstream tap (not benchmarked).

**Limits.** Aux relay is V2-only (V1: #45985); the autotune change also affects V1 (not run). Untested: MiniMax-M3 dflash/dspark and multimodal inputs at PP > 1 (both now accepted), ROCm (AMD model file unchanged), DP > 1 with PP > 1, MiniMax-M3 FlashInfer MoE (runs used Marlin). CI gap: `test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py` does not run on `vllm/models/`-only changes. #57579, #57635, #55671, #52292 also edit `flashinfer_autotune` (on conflict, keep the per-stage group); #53901 reworks the PP aux helpers. No duplicate found.

**AI assistance.** OpenAI Codex, Claude Code and Cursor agents wrote code and tests, ran and analyzed GPU validation, and drafted this text (`/pr-checklist` from unmerged #57084). The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing and defending every changed line.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Initialize _transfer_layer_group_ids in region_pull_worker fixture
author: vllm-agent
body:
## Problem

Main is red on `:computer: (CPU) V1 Others` (builds [#89375](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89375), [#89376](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89376)): all 7 parametrizations of `test_region_pull_ignores_allocation_padding` fail with

```
AttributeError: 'NixlPullConnectorWorker' object has no attribute '_transfer_layer_group_ids'
```

Root cause is a stale-base merge conflict between two PRs:

- **#50494** (merged Sep 15) added the `_transfer_layer_group_ids` attribute to the NIXL base worker and reads it in `base_worker.py:198` (`use_layer_name_routing = bool(self._transfer_layer_group_ids)`).
- **#57077** (merged Sep 16) added the `region_pull_worker` fixture, which constructs the worker via `object.__new__(NixlConnectorWorker)` and sets attributes manually — without `_transfer_layer_group_ids`. Its CI ran against a base that did not yet contain #50494, so the conflict only surfaced after both landed on main.

## Fix

Set `worker._transfer_layer_group_ids = ()` in the fixture — the same empty-tuple default the base-class `__init__` uses, and the same value the sibling `_make_mock_worker_for_desc_ids` fixture already sets.

Note: not runnable locally on my box (no torch), so validation is via CI — pre-commit hooks (ruff, mypy, DCO) pass.

Signed-off-by: kimi-no-na-wa <kimi-no-na-wa@users.noreply.github.com>

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Reduce CUDA graph divergences
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose
This PR cuts down on some ROCm-specific divergences that have now outlived their use. This serves as a cleaner base for the ModelRunner V2 default enablement on ROCm (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56360).

1. Reverts https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48526, which performed graph capture profiling on the current stream rather than a new side stream on other platforms after a performance regression was observed. The reason given then was that a side-stream "shifts the KV/activation buffers' physical placement and slows every bandwidth-bound decode kernel ~20%"; this is not correct.
The true reason is due to a latent runtime defect involving long cross-stream waits which was subsequently fixed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53712 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55099. In particular, the revert is now measured to be performance neutral rather than incurring a 20% slowdown.

2. Reverts #55095's DS V4 fallback on ROCm to `CudaGraphMode.NONE` if MRV2 is enabled. The justification given was #52644, but it no longer applied on `main`, so DS V4 was suffering an unnecessary performance degradation on ROCm with MRV2 enabled.

3. Gate `compile_or_warm_up_model`'s `torch.compile` specialization warmups not only on whether the compilation mode is `VLLM_COMPILE` but also on whether there's even a torch.compile'd submodule.

## Test Plan
Full `gsm8k` was run on DS V4 before/after these changes (2 in particular), on both ModelRunner V1 and V2, and accuracies between 0.954-0.972 were observed.
Performance was measured on TP8, concurrencies 1, 8, 32, 128, 256, 8K/1K, on DS V4 and Qwen-3.5-35B after these changes, and found to be the same (within noise).

Main and AMD CI will also be run on this PR. 

## Test Result
There are no new regressions in CI.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Tolerate malformed EXIF in Molmo 2 image preprocessing
author: Hotragn
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #56576 (issue #56527), which made `MultiModalHasher` tolerate a
malformed EXIF header. Molmo 2 keeps its own copy of the EXIF normalization and
that copy is **not** tolerant, so for that model the merged fix moved the
failure one step later instead of removing it.

`vllm/multimodal/image.py` suppresses the read:

```python
def normalize_image(image: Image.Image) -> Image.Image:
    """Normalize EXIF orientation so the pixel data matches visual display."""
    with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
        image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image)
    return image
```

`vllm/model_executor/models/molmo2.py` does not:

```python
def exif_transpose(images: ImageInput | None) -> ImageInput | None:
    ...
    elif images is not None and isinstance(images, Image):
        images = ImageOps.exif_transpose(images)   # bare
    return images
```

The fix reuses `normalize_image` rather than adding a second
`contextlib.suppress`, so there is only one place that decides how a bad EXIF
block is handled. `vllm/multimodal/parse.py` already imports it the same way.

## Why the second read is the one that raises

This is the non-obvious part, and it is why the bug survived #56576. Measured on
Pillow 12.3.0 with the payload from #56576's test:

| sequence | result |
| --- | --- |
| `Image.open(...)` then `ImageOps.exif_transpose(im)` | no raise |
| `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes(...)` then `ImageOps.exif_transpose(im)` | `SyntaxError: not a TIFF file (header b'XXXX\x00\x00\x00\x08' not valid)` |
| the same, second call on the same object | no raise |

`ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` (`vllm/multimodal/media/image.py:90-92`) runs
`normalize_image(image)` -> `image.load()` -> `_convert_image_mode(image)`. The
suppressed transpose plus `load()` is what primes Pillow's lazy EXIF state, and
`.convert()` carries that state forward — so the *next* read raises, and only
the next one (Pillow caches the failure afterwards). That last row is why the
regression test loads a fresh image for every case; reusing one would make the
test pass on `main` by coincidence.

## Reachability

`POST /v1/chat/completions` against a Molmo 2 model with an `image_url` whose
JPEG carries a malformed APP1/Exif segment:

1. `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` primes the EXIF state (above).
2. Hashing runs next and is now tolerant, thanks to #56576.
3. `Molmo2MultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_updates` ->
   `get_image_replacement_molmo2` (`molmo2.py:2218`) -> the bare
   `exif_transpose` -> `SyntaxError`.

`SyntaxError` is neither `VLLMClientError` nor `GracefulHTTPError`, so
`AsyncLLM.generate`'s generic handler wraps it as
