title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Support scalar priority and wire priority into LLM.chat()
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Purpose

`OfflineInferenceMixin._add_chat_requests` accepts a priority and applies it:

```python
seq_priority = self._priority_to_seq(priority, len(seq_convs))
```

Its only caller, `_run_chat`, has no `priority` parameter and never passes one, and
neither does `LLM.chat()`. `LLM.generate()`, `LLM.enqueue()` and `LLM.enqueue_chat()`
all expose it, so the value is plumbed the whole way down and is reachable from every
offline entrypoint except this one:

```
>>> llm.chat(messages, priority=1)
TypeError: LLM.chat() got an unexpected keyword argument 'priority'
```

A second defect sits in the same class. `_priority_to_seq` calls `len(priority)`
whenever priority is not `None`, so a single value fails even for a single prompt:

```
>>> llm.generate("Hello", priority=1)
TypeError: object of type 'int' has no len()
```

Its two siblings, `_params_to_seq` and `_lora_request_to_seq`, both test
`isinstance(x, Sequence)` first and broadcast a scalar with `[x] * num_requests`.
`_priority_to_seq` is the only one of the three without that branch.

Normalising `None` to `0` first leaves the rest of its body identical to those two.
Existing callers are unaffected: a list is still length-checked and paired one by one
with the prompts, and `None` still yields `[0] * num_requests`.

The scalar half is the looser of the two, since the annotation did say `list[int]`.
Happy to drop it and keep this to the `LLM.chat()` gap.

### Duplicate-work check

No open PR or issue covers this. Searched open PRs for `priority_to_seq`,
`offline_utils priority` and `offline_utils in:path`, all empty. #50884 also edits
`llm.py` and `offline_utils.py`, for per-prompt seeds, and does not touch priority
handling; I will rebase if it lands first.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_offline_utils.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/llm/test_chat.py -k priority -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/llm/test_generate.py -k priority -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/offline_utils.py vllm/entrypoints/llm.py \
    tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_offline_utils.py \
    tests/entrypoints/llm/test_generate.py tests/entrypoints/llm/test_chat.py
```

`test_scalar_priority_broadcast` extends the existing unit tests and needs no GPU and
no model weights. `test_chat_priority` extends `test_chat.py` and mirrors
`test_multiple_priority` in `test_generate.py`; it needs weights, so it is left to CI.

## Test Result

```
5 passed
```

Reverting `offline_utils.py` fails `test_scalar_priority_broadcast` with
`TypeError: object of type 'int' has no len()` at `offline_utils.py:288`.

pre-commit is clean, including `mypy-3.12` at the manual stage CI uses.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix Nixl+Offloading PD edge cases on TheRock image
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose
This PR fixes two issues observed on the (MI300) MultiConnector (Nixl+Offloading) PD edge cases test group on TheRock image (observed [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13000/list?sid=01a0a804-5e41-45dc-81bc-82b154c38890&tab=output) and [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002/list?sid=01a0a870-9608-4b69-970f-f7eb2ea5138f&tab=output)).

1. There is plenty of spam of the form `ucp_worker.c:3328 UCX  DATA  arm iface 0x39efd290 returned Success`. Resolved by bumping the AINIC version up to match what's currently in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`, per the previous updates in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54112 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56459.

2. `test_prefill_cpu_offload_after_gpu_eviction` fails the direct output match test. This was root-caused to slight (reasonable) numerical differences in the prefix cache hot vs cold path. See for instance the following issues:
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33123
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/5543#issuecomment-4625222702
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54490
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42699

This is compounded by the particular eviction prompt here being an open-ended exposition with many plausible continuations. In particular, the next-token logprobs were measured:
- ROCm 10:  ' However' -2.2956 / ' In' -3.3581   → margin 0.0625
- ROCm 7.2:  exact tie above on a cold cache     → margin 0.0000

i.e. almost or exactly tied between the top 2 candidates. The two observed diverging CI continuations (' The development...' vs ' The field...') are exactly the tied top-2 candidates.
Prefix-caching hit in this case legitimately shifts logits by ~0.005–0.06. This is measured to be backend-independent (triton 0.06, AITER 0.074). A 0.0625 margin sits inside that noise floor, so a hot-vs-cold shift can flip the argmax and cause direct text-matching to fail.
Fix: For direct text-matching to be reliable here (insensitive to small reasonable numerical divergences), the continuation has to be reliable i.e. not invite open-ended drift. Appending a sentence to count to 5000 ensures this while still preserving the spirit of the test. In particular, the exact eviction prompt is irrelevant, and slight numerical differences between the prefix cache hot-vs-cold paths are not what is under test here.
 
## Test Plan
All NixlConnector tests were run [before](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002) and [after](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13014) this PR on ROCm 10 and it was found to fix the failing test group and remove the UCX clutter while not causing any test regressions.

Main and AMD CI will also run on this PR on ROCm 7.2 to verify it causes no new regressions both on the AMD and Nvidia code paths.

## Test Result
All NixlConnector tests pass on ROCm 10 without clutter, and there are no new regressions on ROCm 7.2 and on CUDA.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Add record_logical_topk_ready to ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl (GLM-5.3-Flash boot crash)
author: mustafayildirim
body:
## Why this is not duplicating #56604

#56604 (open since 2026-09-12) fixes the same crash class by adding a **default no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` on the `MLAAttentionImpl` base class** in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py`, so every backend silently inherits it.

This PR instead adds the method **on `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` itself**, mirroring the existing `SparseMLACommonImpl` contract (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py:717`): impls that participate in sparse-MLA index groups implement the hook with real semantics; impls that don't declare an explicit no-op at their own site.

Trade-off: the base-class default in #56604 is broader (also covers any other backend that skips `SparseMLACommonImpl`) but weakens the interface — a new sparse backend that *should* implement index-group notification would silently no-op instead of failing loudly. This PR keeps that failure loud and fixes the one backend that currently crashes (ROCm AITER sparse MLA, GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350X). Either fix resolves the boot regression in #57248; happy to withdraw this in favor of #56604 if maintainers prefer the base-class default.

## Description

`MLAAttention.forward` calls `impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` on every sparse layer (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:235`). `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` inherits `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` directly (not `SparseMLACommonImpl`) and never gained the method, so serving GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (gfx950, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`) crashes at the first forward with `AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'`.

This impl shares the top-k indices buffer via `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` but does not participate in `SparseMLAIndexGroup` host-side prefetching, so the correct implementation is a no-op.

Fixes the first boot regression in #57248.

## Test commands run and results

- Reproduced on the cluster before the fix: nightly `af1c01499` on 8×MI350X TP8, engine dies at first forward with the AttributeError above.
- With the equivalent no-op method patched in-pod (same 5-line change), the model boots and serves; combined with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` it passes the full chunked-prefill repro suite with zero faults (details in #57227).
- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` — syntax OK; AST check confirms the method is now on the class.
- No GPU/ROCm environment is available in CI for the full path, so no new automated test is added here; #56604 already adds an interface-level test (`tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_topk_ready_hook.py`) that covers this method's presence on backends.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Hermes Agent). The change was reviewed and validated end-to-end on the affected hardware by the submitter: the same no-op patch was applied in-pod on the MI350X cluster and confirmed to resolve the crash.

title: [Bugfix] Honor skip_reading_prefix_cache for KV connector hits
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

`skip_reading_prefix_cache` (#28194) means "compute every prompt token in this request". `SamplingParams` sets it for `prompt_logprobs` and `PoolingParams` for the token-level tasks (`token_embed`, `token_classify`, `plugin`), because a prefix served from cache has no logits or hidden states for those rows; callers may also set it explicitly. Today it only gates the local prefix cache (`KVCacheManager`). The scheduler adopts a KV connector's `get_num_new_matched_tokens` result unconditionally, so honoring the flag has been left to each connector: `OffloadingConnector` (#44592) and `SimpleCPUOffload` (#54998) got individual fixes, while NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake and MoRIIO do not check it (`grep skip_reading_prefix_cache` over `kv_connector/v1/` finds only the two offload connectors).

Consequences with the remaining connectors:

- A `prompt_logprobs` request whose prefix is served remotely (LMCache, Mooncake) skips those rows silently. `LogprobsProcessor._update_prompt_logprobs` appends per received chunk with no placeholder, so the returned list is shorter and its indices no longer line up with prompt positions.
- In P/D disaggregation the decode engine gets the whole prompt from the connector, ships an unfilled `LogprobsTensors` and crashes with `OverflowError` (#50792; #50795 patches that symptom in the runner by not shipping the tensor).

This PR fixes it where the decision is made: the scheduler discards the connector hit when the request sets the flag (4 lines), so the flag holds for every connector, present and future, exactly as it does for the local cache. The request still computes and stores its KV as usual; only its read is skipped, which is what the two in-tree offload connectors already do.

Relation to #50795: that PR keeps the remote hit and returns no prompt logprobs for the request; this one recomputes the prompt on the decode side and returns correct prompt logprobs, at the cost of that request's prefill. NIXL's decode side already handles `num_external_tokens == 0` as a full local hit and notifies the prefill side to free its blocks (`pull_scheduler.py`, "If remote_blocks and num_external_tokens = 0 ..."), so nothing leaks. Happy to reduce this to the runner-side guard if maintainers prefer that trade-off; the two are complementary rather than conflicting.

Found while auditing #54335 (fixed-token prefill scoring), which also sets the flag and needs every prompt row; that PR will depend on this one.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_kv_connector_honors_skip_reading_prefix_cache`: with the mock connector reporting a 32-token hit, a plain request schedules 32 of its 64 tokens while a `prompt_logprobs` request schedules all 64.
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "skip_reading_prefix_cache or kv_connector_basic"`: 3 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passes.

## Test Result

The new test fails on `main` (the `prompt_logprobs` request schedules 32 tokens) and passes with this change. No GPU path is touched.

## AI assistance

Implemented with Claude Code; every line reviewed by the submitter. Not a duplicate: #50795 addresses the same symptom in the runner rather than the flag; no open PR changes the scheduler's connector-hit handling (`gh pr list --search "skip_reading_prefix_cache"`).

title: [Bugfix][Model Runner V2] Route dummy tokens to MoE experts during profiling
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
## Purpose

With Model Runner V2, the memory profile run never sends a token to the MoE experts, so MoE memory (workspace, all2all receive tensors, expert activations) is not counted when the KV cache is sized. **For WideEP Deployments, e.g. EP32, this can easily cause OOMs during runtime or during DeepGEMM warmup** as the size of the MoE buffers and intermediate activations grows with EP size (num_dp_groups * max_tokens)

`InputBatch.make_dummy` marks every dummy token as padding. With `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1` (the default, from #46428), the router then sets every top-k id to `-1`. That is intended for idle DP ranks, but `profile_run` and the other `is_profile=True` warmups use the same dummy batch.

**Fix:** `make_dummy` takes an `is_padding` argument (default `True`), and the V2 runner passes `is_padding=not is_profile`. Idle-DP dummy runs still skip padding.

## Example

```bash
VLLM_DEBUG_WORKSPACE=1 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput \
  --max-model-len 9000 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  2>&1 | grep -E "WORKSPACE DEBUG|Available KV cache"
```

Rank 0 startup output, with the log prefixes trimmed:

**main:** the MoE workspace is only allocated *after* the KV cache is sized.
```
Available KV cache memory: 110.84 GiB
[WORKSPACE DEBUG] Resized workspace: 0.00 MB -> 48.00 MB
[WORKSPACE DEBUG] Resized workspace: 48.00 MB -> 144.00 MB
[WORKSPACE DEBUG] Resized workspace: 144.00 MB -> 176.00 MB
[WORKSPACE DEBUG] Resized workspace: 176.00 MB -> 192.00 MB
```

**this PR:** the profile run allocates the workspace, and the KV cache accounts for it.
```
[WORKSPACE DEBUG] Resized workspace: 0.00 MB -> 256.00 MB
[WORKSPACE DEBUG] Resized workspace: 256.00 MB -> 512.00 MB
[WORKSPACE DEBUG] Resized workspace: 512.00 MB -> 768.00 MB
[WORKSPACE DEBUG] Resized workspace: 768.00 MB -> 896.00 MB
Available KV cache memory: 109.96 GiB
```

**What main skipped:** about 0.9 GiB per rank in this setup.
- **Workspace:** the 896 MB above.
- **Temporaries:** about 35 MB of extra peak inside each MoE layer, measured with a temporary allocator probe.

On main, that memory is allocated later, once the KV cache has already taken it. DeepEP HT never locks the workspace, so it keeps growing while serving; a skewed batch grew it to 384 MB here. The amount skipped grows with hidden size, top-k and DP size.

** NOTE : this is a relatively small amount of RAM in this simple case, but this becomes 5-6GB for an EP32 deployment, which is common for large models like KimiK3 and GLM5.3 **

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py -q
```

Plus the example above, run on H200 against `main` and this PR.

## Test Result

- **Unit tests:** 12 passed. The new `test_make_dummy_padding_controls_moe_routing` runs the real top-k kernel: dummy tokens marked as padding get `-1`, the others are routed.
- **End-to-end:** the output above; completions are unchanged.
- **pre-commit:** passes.
- **Evals:** no accuracy eval was run. Only dummy (profile and warmup) batches change.

**Duplicate-work check:** no open PR changes MRv2 profile-run padding. #55231 and #57036 handle the `-1` sentinel in specific kernels, which is a different problem.

**AI assistance:** this PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter has reviewed the changes and is responsible for them.

title: [Bugfix] Isolate supplemental FlashInfer BF16 autotuning
author: jiahanc
body:
## Purpose

The supplemental 32-token FlashInfer BF16 warmup currently applies its bounded `tuning_buckets` to every operation in the dummy run. An MXFP8 drafter GEMM with M=40 can consequently inherit the BF16 bucket cap and reuse a low-M tactic that does not support its input.

Run this supplemental pass after the full-model autotune context exits. Only `flashinfer_bf16_mm` enables tuning and installs the BF16 buckets; other operations execute using their normal cache lookup or fallback. Preserve the existing token-count helper's default behavior while excluding the supplemental BF16 pass from the full-op loop. Deferred-MoE tuning retains its own pass even when its token limit is also 32. Skip-op controls, HiSparse skip-attention, distributed tuning and cache persistence remain in effect.

This isolates the BF16 supplemental pass; it does not change the bucket policy of full-model/deferred-MoE passes or provide a general cached-tactic validity fix. Related: #50572, #55377 and https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5269.

Duplicate-work checks found no equivalent isolation fix. #54524 changes default BF16 backend selection, while #55671 migrates autotune cache persistence; neither isolates the supplemental BF16 tuning context.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/utils/flashinfer.py \
  vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
```

```bash
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \

```

- The two modified files passed Ruff, formatting and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13 in a clean tracked-files snapshot. `git diff --check` passed. Repository-wide pre-commit also reports pre-existing EC connector docstring/formatting issues; those unrelated files are intentionally unchanged by this PR.

These are local validation scripts, not committed tests in this PR. The results below are from those probes, not from the repository pytest command above.

| BF16 supplemental tuning | Exactly `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`; M=32 numerical comparison passed. The existing vLLM BF16 eligibility predicate accepts M=32 and rejects M=33/8192 for this CuTeDSL path. |
| MXFP8 full warmup | Completed all 21 buckets through M=8192. At `(M,N,K)=(8192,1792,5120)`, the selected tactic produced finite output with cosine similarity **0.99930** against the PyTorch reference. |

title: [AMD][Bugfix] Make the nested-RoPE patch reach automatic validation
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Summary

Two spec-decode checkpoints fail to load at the same line, for two unrelated reasons:

```
AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'get'    # poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'      # deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7
  transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py:850, in validate_rope
```

`validate_rope` treats a `rope_parameters` mapping as nested whenever the config declares `layer_types` and any top-level key appears in it, then iterates **all** of the mapping's values, guarding only against `None`. Any non-dict entry next to the per-layer dicts therefore raises, and the reported type is just whichever stray the iterator reaches first.

**Two producers, and only one is a malformed config.**

- `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7` ships the strays itself: its `config.json` stores `"rope_type": "default"` and `"rope_theta": null` beside the `full_attention` / `sliding_attention` dicts. `Gemma4TextConfig` overrides `convert_rope_params_to_dict` with a bare `return kwargs` — one of six config classes in transformers 5.17 that do (`DiffusionGemmaTextConfig`, `Gemma4TextConfig`, `Gemma4UnifiedTextConfig`, `LagunaConfig`, `MellumConfig`, `MiMoV2FlashConfig`) — so neither it nor `standardize_rope_params` ever runs to normalize them.
- `poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4`'s checkpoint is clean: its `rope_parameters` holds only the two per-layer dicts. The stray is injected at load time. The repo ships remote code (`auto_map` → `configuration_laguna.LagunaConfig`, under `trust_remote_code=True`) which inherits the base `convert_rope_params_to_dict`, and that does a flat `rope_parameters.setdefault("rope_theta", ...)` without checking for the nested shape; `standardize_rope_params` Case 2 then only walks `set(layer_types)`, so it never removes it again.

**The existing workaround does not run on the path that needs it.** `huggingface_hub`'s `@strict` decorator snapshots every `validate_*` method into `__class_validators__` at class creation, and automatic post-`__init__` validation dispatches off that snapshot rather than off the class attribute. Assigning `PretrainedConfig.validate_rope` therefore only affects explicit `config.validate_rope()` calls — which is why `laguna` fails today *even though its `model_type` is already in the allowlist*. That list is not unique to `PreTrainedConfig` either: transformers decorates individual config classes with `@strict` and each owns a separate snapshot.

## Changes

- Add `_install_hf_config_validator`, which sets the class attribute and then walks the loaded `PretrainedConfig` subclass tree, rewriting each `__class_validators__` snapshot that still holds the superseded function. Matching is by **identity**, so a genuine per-model override such as `DeepseekV4Config.validate_rope` is left in place. Classes imported later snapshot the patched function themselves.
- Route **both** rope patches through it. Routing the `sarvam_mla` shim is load-bearing rather than tidiness: if it keeps the plain assignment, a later nested-rope patch supersedes a function that is in no snapshot and the rewrite silently has no effect.
- Add `gemma4_text` to `_PATCH_HF_NESTED_ROPE_VALIDATION`. Per review, the patch stays gated on `model_type` rather than installing for every model, so malformed checkpoint configs are not silently accommodated. The subclass walk is what makes the gate sufficient: it repairs an already-frozen snapshot, so it no longer matters whether the patch installs during the target's parse or the draft's.

Four hunks in one file. The warning, the removal predicate, the wrapper signature and the existing docstrings are unchanged.

**No tests are added.** The two reproducers are GPU e2e suites; I did not add unit coverage for `_install_hf_config_validator` (the snapshot rewrite and the identity-match carve-out). Happy to add it in `tests/test_config.py` next to the regression #57189 introduced, if reviewers want it.

## Testing

Run on MI355X in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-af1c01499b289be555c475669ba50a88e96d846e`, with this branch's Python source overlaid on the image's compiled extensions. Caveat: that image is 125 commits behind this branch's base and predates the transformers 5.17.0 bump (#56108), so the kernels are older than the Python. The image ships `transformers==5.17.0` / `huggingface_hub==1.31.0`, the transformers minor that introduced the crash. Each test ran in its own pytest session, matching how CI shards them.

```bash
python3 -m pytest -v -s -rA tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py -k gemma4-deepspec --no-header
python3 -m pytest -v -s -rA tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py -k laguna-nvfp4-mrv2 --no-header
python3 -m pytest tests/test_config.py -q --no-header
```

| | `main` (fef55fd26d) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_dspark_...[gemma4-deepspec]` | **FAILED** — `'str' object has no attribute 'get'` | **PASSED** — accuracy 0.930, acceptance rate 0.567, acceptance length 4.971 (floors 0.874 / 0.551 / 4.750) |
| `test_dflash_correctness[laguna-nvfp4-mrv2]` | **FAILED** — `'float' object has no attribute 'get'` | GSM8K eval runs end to end; **fails the acceptance assertion**, `3.051 < 3.195`, accuracy 0.895 |
| `tests/test_config.py` | 2 failed, 371 passed, 6 skipped | 2 failed, 371 passed, 6 skipped |

The `test_config.py` failures are identical on both sides and pre-existing — `test_rope_customization` and `test_eagle_draft_model_config` need gated HF repos and the container has no token. Also checked: a non-allowlisted model with a flat `rope_parameters` is left untouched, and the `sarvam_mla` legacy `validate_rope(ignore_keys=...)` path still works.

**The bug is not ROCm-specific.** Reproduced on an **NVIDIA GB300** (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-0bfc7a15d0...`, same transformers 5.17.0, native NVFP4 via `FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4LinearKernel` + `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` MoE): the same `Dropping ['rope_theta'] from rope_parameters` fires and both Laguna configs resolve, so unpatched CUDA fails the same way AMD does.

**On the laguna result, stated plainly: this change does not turn that test green.** It turns a config-parse crash into an assertion failure — the GSM8K eval now runs end to end, which it never did before, and the test then fails the acceptance-length threshold. That shortfall is not caused by this change, and it is not AMD-specific:

| hardware | NVFP4 path | acceptance_len | accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| MI355X | emulation | 3.051 | 0.895 |
| GB300 | native | **3.0495** | 0.890 |
| enforced floor | | **3.195** (`3.55 × 0.9`) | 0.700 |

Two vendors, native versus emulated quantization, agreeing to three significant figures, ~14% under the reference. In-run metrics oscillate 2.97 / 3.09 / 3.04, so ~3.05 is steady state rather than a tail artifact. The `3.55` figure is annotated in the sibling references as coming from Table 1 of the DFlash paper rather than a measured run, and this parametrization has never completed in CI — it has crashed at config parse since it was added in #50330 — so nothing has ever checked it. I have not found a prior run of it on any hardware to compare against. Worth fixing platform-agnostically in a separate PR rather than with a per-platform carve-out; if anyone has an H200 nightly result for it, that would settle it.

Note these two suites are `optional: true` nightlies (`:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) Spec Decode AL DFlash/DSpark Nightly`, with `:amd: (MI300)` mirrors) whose `source_file_dependencies` do not include `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` — so this PR does not trigger either job, and no CI number is coming without a manual run.

`ruff check` and `ruff format` pass at the pinned v0.14.0. The diff touches configuration parsing only, but the patch deletes keys from `rope_parameters` before validation for the two gated model types, so it is not output-neutral by construction. Evals run: the two acceptance-rate tests above. Not run: the other four parametrizations in these shards.

## Notes

Related to #57188, which the merged #57189 already fixed and closed — that layer-type gate is on `main` and this change leaves it byte-identical. The gate is in fact what makes the patch safe for flat mappings; it does not address either failure here. #57193 was a duplicate of #57189 and was closed unmerged.

title: [Bugfix] Fix wrong vLLM version reported by pip install (proto-v* tag collision)
author: RyanMa29
body:
## Purpose
setup.py calls setuptools_scm's get_version() directly, bypassing pyproject.toml config, with no tag filter. On main, unrelated tags like "proto-v0.3.0" (used for the Rust vllm-proto crate, introduced by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57233) can be closer to HEAD than the last real "vX.Y.Z" vLLM release tag, so `pip install -e .` reports a bogus version such as 0.3.1.dev3+g0bfc7a15d.xpu instead of something close to the real release.

Fix: restrict both git-describe's --match pattern and get_version()'s tag_regex to "v[0-9]\*" tags in setup.py and tools/build_rust.py, so "proto-v\*" tags are ignored.

## Test Plan
```
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm
cd vllm && VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=xpu pip install --no-build-isolation -v -e .
```

## Test Result
Before this PR:
```
Successfully installed vllm-0.3.1.dev3+g0bfc7a15d.xpu
```

After this PR:
```
Successfully installed vllm-0.29.1rc1.dev263+gb0b2f27da.d20260917.xpu
```

`pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache][GLM-5.3-Flash] Disable slot mapping kernel for the kpool tail buffer
author: simondanielsson
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57227.

GLM-5.3-Flash crashes with MAF when sending 500k ISL prompts.  This is caused by out of bounds indexing in the default `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` applied to the Kpool tail buffer. The kpool tail buffer has a fixed size for each request and anyway uses its own slot mapping kernel `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping`, and hence should not use the default kernel.

**Alternatively: make KpoolTailSpec inherit from CircularBufferSpec instead of the SW spec.**

## Why

The KpoolTailSpec is a ring buffer with one block per requests, and is addressed by `pos % kpool` (bounded). The generic slot mapping kernel `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` addresses by `pos // kernel_block_size` (unbounded), and it's used to be enabled for all kv specs except for `CircularBufferSpec`. 

#53781 refactored what kv specs should use this generic slot mapping kernel to instead those specs declaring `uses_slot_mapping: true`. However, KpoolTailSpec inherits from SW and not the circular buffer spec, meaning it still deemed to use the generic slot mapping kernel even though it's a ring buffer. Since that kernels addressing grows unbounded with sequence length (`pos // kernel_block_size`) while the actual KpoolTail buffer is fixed in size, this eventually triggered a MAF at long enough requests.

This PR fixes is it by excluding not using this generic slot mapping kernel for KpoolTailSpec. Instead it just relies on its tailored `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` inside the metadata builder.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Register int8 scaled_mm as a custom op
author: limkcreply
body:
### What is wrong

`TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` calls `triton_scaled_mm` directly at line 134. That function is plain Python. It picks a tile shape from `triton.next_power_of_2(M)`, does some reshapes and asserts, then launches a Triton kernel.

There is no custom op wrapper around it, so dynamo and inductor trace straight into all of that. The fp8 block scaled path a few lines below in the same file does have one, registered as `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm_func`. So fp8 is opaque to the compiler and int8 is not.

### What it costs

Measured on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, Strix Halo), vLLM 0.28.0 built for ROCm 7.2. One linear layer at the fused gate_up shape N=34816 K=5120, one token of decode so M=1:

```
eager, called directly              1.321 ms    134.9 GB/s
torch.compile, called directly     38.072 ms      4.7 GB/s
torch.compile, through a custom op  1.314 ms    135.6 GB/s
```

End to end on a Qwen3.5 27B model quantized to int8 w8a8 with AMD Quark. Same server flags both runs, default cudagraph mode, the patch is the only difference:

```
                  single stream    4 concurrent
before             2.17 tok/s        8.40 tok/s
after              5.15 tok/s       19.37 tok/s
```

Three runs each way. Before: 59.10, 59.09, 59.11 seconds. After: 24.88, 24.86, 24.88 seconds.

The same model in bf16 is not affected either way, 4.10 tok/s compiled against 4.04 eager, so this is specific to the int8 path.

No setting recovers it. `--enforce-eager` is the only mitigation and it still lands at 5.02 tok/s, below the patched number, and it turns off compilation for the rest of the model.

### The fix

Register `int8_scaled_mm_func` with a fake impl and call that from `apply_weights`. This mirrors what `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm_func` already does a few lines below.

Output is unchanged. `torch.allclose` against the unpatched kernel passes at rtol 1e-2 atol 1e-2, and generation on the 27B model reads the same as before.

### Testing notes

I only have gfx1151, so that is the only hardware this was measured on. On CUDA the cutlass int8 kernel is normally picked ahead of the Triton one, so fewer users reach this path there and I could not measure it. The change is platform neutral. It adds a wrapper and does not touch the kernel or the tile selection.

This is int8 w8a8 only. AWQ, GPTQ and compressed-tensors W4A16 go through Marlin, `awq_triton` or `wNa16` and are untouched.

### Repro without a large model

```python
import torch
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.triton_scaled_mm import triton_scaled_mm

N, K = 34816, 5120
w = torch.randint(-127, 127, (K, N), dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
ws = torch.rand(N, 1, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
x = torch.randint(-127, 127, (1, K), dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
xs = torch.rand(1, 1, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")

c = torch.compile(triton_scaled_mm, dynamic=True, fullgraph=True)
c(x, w, xs, ws, torch.bfloat16, None)
```

Time the compiled call against the plain one. On gfx1151 the compiled one is about 29 times slower.

title: [Bugfix] Max-load throughput cliff when `max_num_seqs` is not a multiple of 8
author: andylolu2
body:
## Why

By default, cudagraphs are captured in (mostly) multiples of 8. When `max_num_seqs` is not set to a multiple of 8, it has the unfortunate side effect that the last bucket of batch sizes doesn't fall into a FULL cuda graph. For example, with `max_num_seqs=100` (and no spec decode), we get:

| Num decodes | Cudagraph mode |
|---|---:|
| 95 | FULL |
| 96 | FULL |
| 97 | PIECEWISE |
| 98 | PIECEWISE |
| 99 | PIECEWISE |
| 100 | PIECEWISE |

This is quite bad practically, because servers can get stuck in the slow PIECEWISE mode when it's overloaded (num_running_reqs = max_num_seqs).

In a TP4/B200 reproduction this was not a small boundary effect: batch 97 started behind batch 96 and progressively slowed over a 2,000-token decode, eventually falling below 1,000 tok/s/server. Adding the legal FULL-100 shape removed the cliff.

## Fix

This is actually already correctly handled when spec decode is turned on by #50488, but not when spec dec is off. The fix is to simply piggy-back off the PR's changes: when the inferred default is used without speculative decoding, add `max_num_seqs` as the widest uniform-decode shape if it fits under the existing capture ceiling:

```python
elif max_num_seqs <= max_cudagraph_capture_size:
    uniform_decode_sizes = [max_num_seqs]
```

For the example above, the ladder becomes:

```text
..., 88, 96, 100, 104, 112, ...
```

The unchanged graph manager then produces FULL descriptors through 100, while later sizes remain PIECEWISE-only.

## Benchmark evidence

The reproducer used [Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603) with TP4 on B200, `max_num_seqs=100`, logprobs enabled, 2,000 generated tokens, and a production-shaped prompt distribution with roughly equal mass around 8k, 16k, 32k, 64k, and 127k input tokens.

| Batch | Before | With FULL 100 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 96 | 3,753 tok/s | 3,760.78 tok/s |
| 97 | 1,523 tok/s | **3,876.85 tok/s** |

Batch 97 improved 2.55× (+154.6%) and became comparable to batch 96. Before the fix its server-throughput windows decayed from 2,922 tok/s near output token 302 to 829 tok/s in the final window. After the fix they stayed flat at 3,923, 3,890, 3,862, and 3,824 tok/s. Total time fell from 129.72 s to 52.41 s.

An Nsight trace showed that the PIECEWISE path accumulated tensor-parallel rank drift: attention remained around 0.58 ms, while graph-launch gaps grew from about 0.69 ms to 5.5 ms and MNNVL all-reduce wait medians grew from about 10 µs to 3.6–4.7 ms. This PR avoids that path for a legal decode batch; it does not attempt to independently repair PIECEWISE rank drift.

## Test results

```text
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/test_config.py \
  -k default_cudagraph_capture_size_respects_platform_ceiling
11 passed, 61 deselected

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  -k 'uniform_decode_pads_up_to_full_graph or uniform_decode_exact_match_is_not_over_padded or uniform_decode_beyond_capture_ladder_falls_back or divisor_query_len_dispatch_is_unchanged'
6 passed, 5 deselected

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/vllm.py tests/compile/test_config.py
all hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and repository checks
```

Revert check: with the production hunk reverted while retaining the new test, both cases fail (`2 failed`): neither 100 nor 101 is present in the inferred capture sizes.

No model evaluation was run because this changes only which execution graph serves an already-valid shape; model operations and outputs are unchanged.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `max_num_seqs`, `cudagraph`, `capture sizes`, `off-stride`, and `uniform decode`. The nearby work addresses different contracts:

- #50488 introduced `uniform_decode_sizes` for speculative decoding and deliberately kept non-speculative defaults unchanged. This PR closes that remaining non-speculative boundary hole using its abstraction.
- #37865 appends `max_cudagraph_capture_size`; here that value is 200, so it still does not add the required 100-request boundary.
- #55004 covers uniform decode under an explicitly configured scalar maximum, primarily with speculative decoding. This PR changes only the inferred default and leaves explicit configuration untouched.
- #53407 lets a uniform decode pad to a wider compatible FULL graph, but it requires such a graph to exist. In this case 104 requests exceeds the scheduler limit, so there is no compatible FULL graph until 100 is captured.
- #56136 concerns candidate ladders for multiple dynamic-speculation query lengths, not the non-speculative capture set.
- #54352 is a draft auto-revert for the memory regression caused when #50488 raised capture ceilings. This patch never raises the ceiling and adds only a shape already below it.

No open PR covers an off-stride, non-speculative `max_num_seqs` boundary.

## Reviewer guide

- `vllm/config/vllm.py`: the two-line behavior change reuses the uniform-decode capture-size path; the nearby comment is updated to match its broadened scope.
- `tests/compile/test_config.py`: one new parameter exercises the existing capture-boundary contract at `max_num_seqs=100`.

There are no moves, generated files, or mechanical propagation changes.

## AI assistance disclosure

title: [bugfix] Mark draft tokens to rebuilt their embeddings.
author: HieDean
body:
## Purpose
Fix an inconsistency between input_ids and is_token_ids when enable_prompt_embeds is used together with speculative decoding.

Speculative draft token IDs are scattered directly into input_ids.gpu, but the corresponding positions in is_token_ids were not marked as token IDs. As a result, the prompt-embedding path treated these positions as external embeddings and reused stale embeddings during target verification, causing incorrect target predictions and very low acceptance lengths.

This change marks spec_flattened_indices as token-ID positions before synchronizing is_token_ids to the GPU.
## Test Plan
```
import torch

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
from datasets import load_dataset
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

TARGET_MODEL = "Qwen3-8B"
DRAFT_MODEL = "Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16"
DATASET = "gsm8k"

# Create a sampling params object.
sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=128)

def main():
    hf_target_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(TARGET_MODEL)

    # Create an LLM.
    llm = LLM(
        model=TARGET_MODEL,
        enable_prompt_embeds=True,
        speculative_config={"model": DRAFT_MODEL, "num_speculative_tokens": 16},
        disable_log_stats=False,
    )
    tokenizer = llm.get_tokenizer()

    dataset = load_dataset(DATASET, "main")
    dataset = list(dataset["test"])[:10]
    for data in dataset:
        messages = [
            [{"role": "user", "content": f"{data["question"]}"}]
        ]
        input_ids = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages,
            tokenize=True,
            add_generation_prompt=False,
            return_tensors="pt"
        )

        embeddings = hf_target_model.get_input_embeddings()(input_ids["input_ids"])
        prompt_len = embeddings.shape[1]

        inputs = {
            "prompt_embeds": embeddings,
            "prompt_token_ids": [tokenizer.vocab_size] * prompt_len,
            "prompt_is_token_ids": [False] * prompt_len,
        }
        outputs = llm.generate(inputs, sampling_params, use_tqdm=False)

        # Print the outputs.
        print("\nGenerated Outputs:\n" + "-" * 60)
        for output in outputs:
            prompt = output.prompt
            generated_text = output.outputs[0].text
            print(f"Prompt:    {prompt!r}")
            print(f"Output:    {generated_text!r}")
            print("-" * 60)

        num_drafts = 0
        num_accepted_tokens = 0
        for metric in llm.get_metrics():
            if metric.name == "vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts":
                num_drafts += metric.value
                print(f"{metric.name}: {metric.value:.2f}")
            elif metric.name == "vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens":
                num_accepted_tokens += metric.value
                print(f"{metric.name}: {metric.value:.2f}")

        acceptance_length = (
            1 + num_accepted_tokens / num_drafts if num_drafts > 0 else 1.0
        )

        print(f"Mean acceptance length: {acceptance_length:.2f}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
## Test Result

Before this PR:
`Mean acceptance length: 2.79`

After this PR:
`Mean acceptance length: 2.95`

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Release consumed MRV2 CPU inputs
author: Sy0307
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Release consumed request-local CPU multimodal payloads from MRV2 workers while requests are still decoding. This extends #52041's prefix-hit stripping to inputs that actually reached a worker, while retaining EngineCore replay data and GPU embeddings.

## Claims

- Release each occurrence only after its placeholder range is confirmed consumed; exclude in-flight prefill, unconfirmed output placeholders and inputs being encoded in the same step.
- Restore payloads when KV-load rollback schedules encoding again, including inputs initially stripped by a prefix hit. Preemption and streaming request installation rebuild tracking.
- Keep SHM processor-cache descriptors on their existing ACK protocol. MRV1 and encoder embedding eviction are unchanged.

## Validation

Code baseline: `2f1041e8dd05415d9984d0a83ad957d54a049eb4`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused scheduler regressions | 8 passed |
| Entire `test_encoder_runner.py` | 25 passed |
| Qwen3-VL live-generation regression, unchanged main | Fails: worker still holds the image payload after three steps while the request is alive |
| Same real-model regression, this patch | Passes: payload released, request completes 16 output tokens |
| Changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX and CI tethering | Passed |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

CPU commands:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k cpu_encoder_input -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py -q
```

`--confcutdir` is only for the local macOS environment. Expanded scheduler/output testing had the same two unrelated failures on both arms: missing root `caplog_vllm` fixture and the local no-Triton fallback rejecting async MRV1+PP. The original main had 255 passes; the initial patch had 260 passes, and the three subsequent parameter cases passed separately.

Real-model reproducer on one H200:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_memory_leak.py -k consumed_cpu_inputs -v -s
```

Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, greedy, eager. Both arms used Torch 2.14.0, Transformers 5.20.2 and FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1. The native wheel is `921ed7fa1`; its only difference from the tested main is `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml`, so runtime and native sources match. `VLLM_MODEL_REDIRECT_PATH` pointed the existing model name at the local weight snapshot.

The GPU regression uses the real LLM entry point and the worker's actual EncoderCache, and is selected by the existing Multimodal Models Standard 4 job. Scheduler regressions exercise real constructors, scheduled outputs, forced preemption and invalid-block rollback. Worker tests verify storage reclamation, independent ownership and restored inputs reaching `EncoderRunner.prepare_mm_inputs`.

TP=2 integration checks also used Qwen3-VL on physical H200 GPUs 2/3, with the tensor arena enabled, processor caching disabled, prefix caching enabled, and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:

| Live request at step 4 | Main | This patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1024px image, below the arena threshold | Both workers retain approximately 6 MiB of inputs | Both workers drop their inputs |
| 1536px image, confirmed arena allocation | Both workers retain approximately 13.5 MiB; slot readers remain unacknowledged | Both workers drop their inputs; a fully acknowledged, reusable slot is observed before request completion |

Each arm completed a first request and a repeated-prefix request with 32 output tokens each. Token IDs matched exactly across main/patch in both image-size cases; cancellation cleared request-local cache entries. These are small deterministic comparisons, not a full quality evaluation. Slot snapshots are asynchronous; the memory figures describe each worker's payload references, not additive physical-memory savings. Cancellation may still leave short-lived references outside EncoderCache.

The node could not initialize NVLS multicast, including on main; both TP2 arms ran with `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`. Existing fallback all-reduce paths were used without changing vLLM code. No GPU synchronization error was raised. Physical GPUs 4/5 were excluded throughout.

Current-revision host-memory A/B (Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, MRV2, TP=2, physical H200 GPUs 0/2): 16 distinct 1536px image requests arriving in two waves of 8, each generating 128 tokens. Each configuration/arm had two independent engine starts with reversed arm order on the second start, one warmup and three formal rounds per start. PSS sums the driver/EngineCore and its worker process tree, avoiding shared-page double counting. Means below use snapshots with all 16 requests alive and each having generated at least 8, 32 and 64 tokens.

| Configuration | Main decode PSS | Patch decode PSS | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default 4 GiB LRU processor cache, arena off | 6.950 GiB | 6.567 GiB | 393.0 MiB / 5.52% |
| Processor cache off, arena off | 6.733 GiB | 6.303 GiB | 440.7 MiB / 6.39% |
| Processor cache off, arena on | 8.493 GiB | 8.131 GiB | 370.1 MiB / 4.26% |

Worker request-cache input references fell from approximately 216 MiB per rank to zero in all cases. With the arena enabled, slot-exhaustion fallbacks fell from 8 to 0 per round; all 8 slots became reusable while requests were still alive. The arena's 2 GiB pinned mapping remains allocated, so this is slot reuse, not unmapping the arena. In this small workload, the arena's fixed mapping also makes its absolute PSS larger than the arena-off configuration.

Corresponding output token IDs matched for all 576 formal requests across the three configurations, with 128 tokens per request. The two independent-start PSS reductions with default LRU caching were 402.0 and 383.9 MiB. These are workload-specific decode-residency measurements, not universal percentages or exact prefill peaks. The driver and EngineCore share a process in this harness; workers use the real multiprocess TP executor. Configuration: eager, max model length 4096, batched tokens 2048, sequences 16, GPU memory utilization 0.20, seed 0, prefix caching enabled with distinct inputs, NVLS disabled equally on both arms, and GPU sync checking enabled. No allocator trimming or production-code instrumentation was used. EngineCore replay inputs and its LRU cache are still retained.

No throughput speedup or full accuracy result is claimed for this revision. KV-load failure restoration is covered by CPU scheduler/worker tests, not a distributed KV-transfer model run.

## Details

A single `SchedulerOutput.encoder_input_updates` map carries payload replacement by request ID and input index: `None` releases an input; a payload restores it. An index has one update per step, avoiding separate restore/free ordering. The scheduler tracks only remaining releasable inputs and stops scanning once none remain.

Workers apply updates after request installation and RoPE position initialization. Replacing entries in a worker-owned list preserves EngineCore's original feature objects, including with the uniprocess executor. The same placeholder metadata remains available for embedding gathering and PrefixLM ranges.

Related work and scope:

- #52041/#53456 handle stripping before initial position computation. This patch releases after that initialization and does not change their metadata rules.
- #54994 preserves SHM address references; those descriptors remain excluded here.
- #51207 shares transport storage. It does not release request-local references, and its slots cannot be reused until their storage references are dropped. This PR adds no COW or other transport.
- #62834 checks remote encoder embedding readiness during EPD replay; it does not restore a local worker's raw inputs for re-encoding.
- Open #50871 clears EngineCore inputs for resumable sessions. This patch requires retained EngineCore payloads for rollback; combining the two requires an explicit replay policy.
- #56813 caches position ranges, which this patch does not change; #56826/#62850 optimize other cache cleanup. None implements this running-request payload lifecycle.

No user-facing configuration or behavior contract is added, so no separate design document is introduced. AI assistance was used for implementation, upstream comparison, review and validation.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix AMD CI pipeline upload rejected by an invalid block-step key
author: mawong-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose
After https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57080, every non-nightly AMD CI build currently dies before running a single test:

>   Pipeline upload rejected: One of the steps you provided was invalid: may only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, dashes and colons

The reason is that `test-template-amd.j2` emits a gating block step keyed `block-{{ step_slug }}`, and the slug is derived from the label, stripping only spaces, parentheses, `%`, `,` and `+`. A `/` in the label therefore lands in the key, which BuildKite rejects.
The problematic step is `optional: true`, and optional steps stay gated whenever `nightly != "1"`, so the bad key is generated for every ordinary PR build while nightly runs are unaffected. This is also why #57080 did not run into this issue (its CI ran with `NIGHTLY=1` and `RUN_ALL=1`.)

Fix: Rename the label to drop the slash. This is the only one of the 199 steps in test-amd.yaml that produces an invalid key.

The durable fix belongs in ci-infra: `amd_step_slug` should sanitize the key rather than enumerate a handful of characters to strip.

## Test Plan
AMD CI will run on this PR.

## Test Result
AMD CI now makes it past the pipeline upload in the `bootstrap` stage.

title: [Bugfix][Platform] Fall back to torch when device-level NVML memory is unsupported (GB10)
author: hclsys
body:
## Problem

`nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo` is not implemented on integrated parts. On GB10 (DGX Spark) it raises
`NVMLError_NotSupported`, and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total` returns `[N/A]`. The platform
still resolves to `NvmlCudaPlatform` (`is_integrated_gpu()` is `True`), so
`get_device_total_memory()` propagates that error.

The visible damage is in `EngineArgs.get_batch_defaults()`, which wraps the call in
`try/except Exception` and falls back to `device_memory = 0`. A 121.7 GiB card therefore misses the
`>= 70 GiB` branch and lands on the smallest defaults, with nothing logged.

On this machine, before:

```
card reports (torch)                    121.7 GiB
current_platform.get_device_total_memory()  -> NVMLError_NotSupported
resolved max_num_batched_tokens  API=2048   LLM=8192
resolved max_num_seqs            API=256
```

after:

```
current_platform.get_device_total_memory()  -> 130669424640 (121.7 GiB)
resolved max_num_batched_tokens  API=8192   LLM=16384
resolved max_num_seqs            API=1024
```

So every DGX Spark is currently serving with batch defaults 4x lower than the ladder intends.

There is a second caller, `startup_plan.py:66`, which is *not* wrapped — with
`VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` the same `NVMLError_NotSupported` aborts worker startup outright. That
path is opt-in (default `0`), which is why this shows up as quiet misconfiguration rather than a
crash for most users.

## Fix

Catch `NVMLError` and fall back to `torch.cuda.get_device_properties().total_memory` — the same
source `NonNvmlCudaPlatform.get_device_total_memory` already uses, and the same NVML-tolerance
shape as `is_fully_connected()` a few lines below. The discrete-GPU path is unchanged; the fallback
only runs when NVML refuses.

## Test

Verified on the affected hardware (NVIDIA GB10, compute capability 12.1, driver 580.95.05,
aarch64 / CUDA 13); the fallback value matches `torch`'s `total_memory` exactly.

I have not run this on a discrete NVIDIA GPU — I do not have one to hand — but that path is
untouched. No unit test here since it would be all pynvml mocking for a six-line guard; happy to add
one if you'd prefer it.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix Entrypoints Integration (Pooling) tests on TheRock image
author: mawong-amd
body:
## Purpose
`tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_cross_encoder_online_vision.py` has a number of [failures on TheRock image](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13085/list?sid=01a0ae47-79de-4154-ad16-daf19cd84150&tab=output).

This was root-caused to a slight difference in codegen on Triton 3.8 vs Triton 3.7: namely, `chunked_prefill_paged_decode`'s `_fwd_kernel` has a slightly different FP32 accumulation order which leads to a 1-ULP BF16 divergence out of 32768 elements in layer 3 given identical inputs; this 1-ULP divergence is enough to snowball over the succeeding 20+ layers.
It is important to note that both codegens are equally correct: the problematic value sits 0.034 ULP from a BF16 rounding boundary, and both codegens' values have the same max error vs a FP64 reference.

Fundamentally, the issue is that this test's golden values were designed for CUDA in #33060. ROCm's attention backends cannot reasonably be expected to have exactly the same numerics as CUDA, and indeed there have been 3 rounds of tolerance relaxation (#41341, #46891, #53646) in an attempt to reconcile the slightly different (yet still correct) numerics of ROCm's attention backends vs CUDA's golden values.
In particular, FlexAttention differs from the other backends in that it accumulates `P = softmax(QK^T)` in `Q.dtype` (which can be BF16/FP16 rather than FP32 used on all other backends on ROCm/CUDA), so it naturally has more numerical divergence.
Rather than adding yet more attention-backend-specific tolerances, the proper fix is to establish a ROCm-specific set of golden values tuned for its attention backends, which also allows the use of a unified set of `atol` and `rtol` rather than the current fragmented regime.

## Test Plan
AMD CI (in particular the `Entrypoints Integration (Pooling)` test group) was run on both [ROCm 10](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13103) and [ROCm 7.2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13108/list), on both MI300X and MI355X.

## Test Result
The test group now passes (on ROCm 10) and there are no new regressions (on ROCm 7.2).

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix DCP pulls across MLA cache regions
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
When prefill and decode use different cache-group layouts, as with a HiSparse decoder, NIXL matches their KV blocks by memory region. That receive path currently assumes a single source rank and fails when a DCP prefiller supplies multiple ranks.

Create a read for each source rank using the existing region mapping. For each region, reuse `_apply_dcp_prefix_caching` to select the pages owned by that rank and skip the decoder's cached prefix. Bound the reads by the sequence length and zero any remaining allocation padding. The ordinary DCP path stays unchanged. Requires unshared MLA regions with matching logical/kernel page sizes.

Independent of #55398's GPU-landing feature; #57077 covers DCP1 only.


title: [Bugfix] DiffusionGemma: hand out stashed logprobs only on the committing step
author: mmastrac
body:
## Purpose

Two concurrent DiffusionGemma requests with `logprobs` on can stomp on each other's logprobs, one then fails with an HTTP 500.

The diffusion sampler stashes a request's top-k logprobs on the step it converges and attaches them to the SamplerOutput on the commit step. The attach loop pops the stash for every decoding request in the batch though, not just the ones committing on this step. 

So... if request B converges in the same step that request A commits, B's logprobs get emitted under A. When B's own commit comes around there is nothing left to pop, the API sees fewer logprobs than tokens, and chat completions dies with `IndexError: list index out of range in _create_chat_logprobs`.

Any two requests whose schedules line up one step apart will hit this, so it shows up as soon as you run a concurrency sweep with logprobs. The fix is to only pop for the slots that are actually committing this step.

This is split out of #57250 since it's a standalone bug.

## Test plan

Run the serve command with --max-logprobs 32 and a 2-way to 32-way sweep of identical requests with logprobs on.

Hardware: 1 DGX Spark.

Before: identical requests sent together line up one step apart, so a 2-way sweep already fails with 500 `list index out of range` on the request that converged while 
the other committed.

After: 32-way sweep is clean, every response carries one logprob entry per token, and the 1-way path is unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Alias SparseAttnIndexerKpool.forward_cuda to forward_native (GLM-5.3-Flash boot crash)
author: mustafayildirim
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57424. `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` on the AMD/ROCm path (`vllm/models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`) defines only `forward_native`. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward` routes *enabled* ops to `forward_hip` on ROCm, and `forward_hip` falls back to `forward_cuda` — which doesn't exist → `NotImplementedError` at the first forward of the indexer op.

On the `v0.29.1rc0.dev265+g0bfc7a15d` ROCm nightly, serving GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at `profile_run` with:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 149, in forward_hip
    return self.forward_cuda(*args, **kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 145, in forward_cuda
    raise NotImplementedError
```

because the resolved `compilation_config.custom_ops` contains `'all'` there, enabling every registered op — including `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool`.

## Why

The NVIDIA `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` defines both `forward_native` and `forward_cuda`; the AMD one is native-only but was never given the alias the ROCm dispatch requires. This blocks GLM-5.3-Flash boot on current ROCm nightlies entirely.

## Test results

- New unit test `tests/models/test_rocm_sparse_indexer_forward_cuda.py`: fails on the unpatched file, passes with the fix (run with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`).
- End-to-end on 8×MI350X (TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash fp8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0bfc7a15d` + this patch in-place): engine boots Ready with 57 FULL + 106 PIECEWISE cudagraphs captured; chunked-prefill repro (20K prompt, 16K chunks) plus a long-context ladder 32K→524,212 tokens all pass with zero memory access faults, engine healthy after.

AI assistance was used in preparing this PR; the change was reviewed and hardware-validated end-to-end by the submitter.

## Related

- #57227 — original gfx950 16K-chunk memory access fault; root-caused by #57317
- #57317 — kpool tail slot-mapping OOB fix (the root cause of #57227)
- #57248 — nightly GLM-5.3-Flash ROCm boot regressions (`record_logical_topk_ready` + jit-warmup)
- #57252 — our fix for the `record_logical_topk_ready` AttributeError
- #56604 — base-class `record_logical_topk_ready` alternative
- #57192 — jit-warmup tilelang fix

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Fix FlashInfer DSpark non-causal attention
author: WoosukKwon
body:
DSpark's non-causal draft window has 133 valid keys at draft length 5, padded to 256 indices. The DSV4.1 FlashInfer integration passed the padded width as the active sparse length, so padding entered softmax normalization. A constant-value reference expecting 1 returned 0.51953125 (133/256). Short contexts also inherited causal visibility from the launcher's per-request query positions.

Use the valid SWA length, retaining FlashInfer's required 128-column minimum, and present each draft query with the full non-causal sequence length. Prepare the per-token active lengths and sequence lengths once in the metadata builder, using persistent buffers refreshed before FULL CUDA graph replay and shared across layers. Singleton query/output views remove the need to construct query offsets in each layer. This changes vLLM metadata only; no FlashInfer source changes or new Triton kernel are needed. The two int32 buffers use 8 bytes per configured maximum batched token per builder (64 KiB at capacity 8192).

Validation on 4× GB200 with FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`), DSpark length 5 and full decode graphs. DEP4 uses MegaMoE/adaptive verification; TP4 uses auto MoE/fixed verification.

Full GSM8K: 1,319 identical 5-shot chat prompts per pair, greedy, seed 123, thinking off, 1,024-token output cap. Accuracy below uses flexible extraction.

| Configuration | Acceptance before → fixed (including bonus) | GSM8K before → fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DEP4 | 3.1823 → **3.8248** (+20.2%) | 1268 → 1271 / 1319 (96.13% → 96.36%) |
| TP4 | 3.2075 → **3.8879** (+21.2%) | 1266 → 1263 / 1319 (95.98% → 95.75%) |

All 1,319 requests completed in each fixed run, with no errors or empty responses. DEP had no capped outputs; TP had one (versus zero before). Strict extraction: DEP 1042 → 1042; TP 1060 → 1049. These evaluations establish acceptance recovery, not exact greedy-output equivalence or an accuracy improvement. MegaAttention measured 3.8437 acceptance on the DEP cohort. These are short-context results, not 100K-context throughput measurements.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py \
  -k test_dsv41_flashinfer_dspark_window_matches_reference -q -rs
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py
```

The original 12 regression cases failed before the correctness fix. All 12 expanded cases pass with persistent metadata: BF16/FP8, 16/64 heads, short/long windows, mixed query lengths, padding, and CUDA graph replay after Q/KV and visible-length updates, with unchanged buffer addresses. Attention outputs are bitwise identical to the initial correctness fix across eight FP8 shapes (16/64 heads, batch 1/8/32/128). Nine full draft-forward runs have zero observed eager/graph, changed-input, restored-input and post-replay error. Pre-commit checks pass. Validation ran on the optimization worktree; all three changed files are identical in this isolated PR branch. The GSM8K results above evaluate the correctness fix; the metadata refactor was validated by parity and replay checks, without repeating the full accuracy runs.

Metadata-refactor performance on GB200 ×4, relative to the initial correctness fix: synthetic weights and 102,400 KV tokens/request, draft length 5, TP auto MoE / DEP MegaMoE. Medians of five distributed-MAX samples, 20 graph replays/sample after 3 seconds of warmup; each comparison uses the same runner and repeats one endpoint to expose order effects.

| Workload | Initial fix (µs) | Prepared metadata (µs) | Draft-forward result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| TP4 B1 | 403 / 425 | 366 | 9–14% lower latency |
| DEP4 B8 | 703 / 691 | 669 | 3–5% lower latency |
| DEP4 B128 | 1370 | 1431 / 1327 | Inconclusive |

The forward boundary excludes metadata preparation, LM head, scheduler and sampling; these are not serving-throughput gains. Preparation costs 3.9–8.5 µs per build in a separate CUPTI/CUDA-graph/cold-L2 microbenchmark and is shared across layers. Exact commands and raw results are archived locally under `/home/woosuk/.cache/v41-dspark-opt/metadata-opt/metadata-paired-002-*`; the microbenchmark results are in `prepared-results.json`.

Duplicate check: searched open DSpark/FlashInfer, acceptance, noncausal sparse, and padding PRs. #52499 and #57292 address SM120 routing/page geometry; #54834 addresses dense FlashInfer cache-layout resolution; #55692 addresses block-table bounds. None fixes the SM100 DSV4.1 non-causal active lengths and visibility corrected here.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Preserve logprobs across streaming continuations
author: i-m-aditya
body:
## Problem

When a resumable streaming request finishes one chunk while its continuation
is already queued, the continuation can replace `request.sampling_params`
before the scheduler packages the completed chunk's logprobs.

If chunk A requests logprobs and chunk B does not, chunk A's final output loses
its logprob payload. The result incorrectly depends on whether the continuation
arrived before or after chunk A's final model output.

## Solution

Snapshot the finishing chunk's sampling parameters before handling the stop and
possible streaming continuation. Use that snapshot when extracting logprobs for
the completed output.

Added a scheduler regression test that covers both continuation arrival orders
and verifies the exact logprob payload remains attached to the finishing chunk.

## Tests

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -v`
- `.venv/bin/ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`
- `.venv/bin/ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`
- `git diff --check`
- `pre-commit` hooks

## Duplicate work

Searched open pull requests for scheduler, streaming, logprobs, and `new_logprobs`; no matching open PR was found.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Retain offload event metadata through batch translation
author: karya0
body:
## Purpose

`OffloadingEventsTracker` caches a `BlockStored` payload per offload key and drops it when the key's last residency goes away. The drop happened inline in `_take_removed_event`, so within a single `take_events` batch a removal could delete the payload that a *later* event in that same batch still needed — a primary removal preceding a queued secondary (KVCR) store. That store then fell back to the placeholder payload, publishing an event with no block hashes and no token ids.

Fix: collect the removed keys during the batch and drop their payloads once, after every event in the batch has had a chance to register its residencies.

Scope: this does not address a store that only completes in a later batch; that needs the in-flight store set and is left for a follow-up.

Not a duplicate of #52103, which touches the same files to add request provenance to stored events.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py
```

`test_primary_removal_preserves_metadata_for_same_batch_kvcr_store` is added to the existing suite, parametrized over the secondary removal landing in the same batch or the next one. It asserts the store keeps its full payload, and that the payload is still dropped once no residency remains.

## Test Result

```
25 passed, 14 warnings in 18.96s
```

Both parametrizations fail with the fix reverted and pass with it applied. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, ruff format, mypy).

No model evaluation: this changes only the KV-event payload published to external consumers, not the offload data path or any generated output.

AI assistance was used for this change; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Preserve NaN-scored candidate block indices
author: WoosukKwon
body:
DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MegaAttention can fail startup with a DeepGEMM sparse-slot assertion during dummy prefill/autotuning. The candidate-source logits contain NaNs. Although `torch.topk` selects their block IDs, `value > -inf` discards them, leaving only the pinned newest block. Expanding that underfilled row repeats its last block inside the prefix DeepGEMM expects to be unique (389 copies of block 388 in the captured failing rows).

Exclude only the `-inf` padding sentinel when storing selected candidates. This retains NaN-scored block IDs, keeps the active prefix unique for the observed configuration, and works with the existing DeepGEMM dependency. Finite-score selection is unchanged; this adds no kernel, buffer, fallback, or host synchronization. It does not sanitize logits or fix the upstream numerical source of dummy-run NaNs.

Extend the existing candidate suite with empty/partial rows and aligned/unaligned starts under zero/NaN scores, and update its reference to retain selected NaN entries.

Validation on GB200:

- Both new NaN regression cases fail against the original selector; both finite control cases pass.
- All 13 candidate tests pass on PR commit `707b81b021`; scoped pre-commit hooks (including mypy) pass.
- Four captured TP-rank inputs replay through unmodified DeepGEMM after the fix, recovering 389 unique blocks in each previously failing row.
- Selector checks at 8K, 50K and 100K cover random, zero, NaN and mixed-NaN scores; finite outputs match the original exactly.
- The identical selector change on the previously validated model worktree passes real-weight TP4 MegaAttention startup with sparse logits, DSpark5, autotuning and FULL target/draft graphs. Short (18-token) and long (16,526-token) chat prompts both return the expected answer `4`. This is a serving smoke, not a full accuracy evaluation or a full-model build of current main. No full accuracy evaluation was repeated.

Duplicate-work check: #56558 optimizes the candidate-source selector but explicitly preserves NaN exclusion. #50201 and #49897 address the downstream token top-k kernel. None fixes this candidate-store predicate. vllm-project/DeepGEMM#16 instead adds repeated-index support to the native metadata API; this PR prevents vLLM from constructing the invalid active prefix for the observed NaN case and needs no dependency update. No linked issue.

AI assistance: implementation, investigation and validation used OpenAI Codex. The human submitter confirmed reviewing every changed line of commit `707b81b021` and running the relevant GPU tests.

title: [Bugfix] Use the correct repository revision for secondary artifact loaders
author: KernelClint
body:
Bugfix for two regressions introduced in #51446. That PR added revision pins to two secondary-artifact loads, but each used the wrong repository's revision. When a model and its tokenizer are pinned to different revisions, both loads fail.

- **Chat template (`renderers/hf.py`):** loading a chat template from the tokenizer's processor used the model's revision instead of the tokenizer's. Now uses the tokenizer's revision, which falls back to the model revision when unset, so the common case is unchanged.
- **FunAudioChat speech tokenizer (`funaudiochat.py`):** the speech tokenizer is loaded from the model's repository but was pinned to the tokenizer's revision. Now uses the model revision, matching the feature extractor that loads from the same place.

AI assistance was used for this change (GPT-5.6-sol).

title: [Bugfix] DiffusionGemma: cast the self-conditioning soft embed to the buffer dtype
author: mmastrac
body:
## Purpose

The self-conditioning soft embed is computed in the embedding weight's dtype and written 
into the fp32 `self_conditioning_embeds` buffer. 

Once dynamo falls back to eager (past the recompile limit, which happens when requests
