title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Address kpool tail blocks by the padded indexer stride in the NVIDIA prefill seed kernel
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

Fix silent indexer-cache corruption for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA: the kpool prefill tail-seed kernel addresses tail blocks with a dense stride while the tail cache is stored with the indexer's padded block stride.

**How the tail cache is laid out.** `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` pads the `KpoolTailSpec` page to the indexer page (`page_size_padded = idx_page`; 38016 B for the default `block_size=1152`: 288 pool rows x 132 B), and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places every indexer layer's tail tensor at the *same offset* as that layer's indexer tensor with `block_stride = idx_page`. Tail block `b` is therefore the first 2048 B (`[2, kpool=4, 128]` bf16) of indexer block `b`; the two never collide because both groups draw distinct block ids from one pool. `create_kv_cache_views` builds the view with `as_strided`, so `tail_kv_cache.stride(0) == 19008` elements instead of the dense 1024.

**The bug.** `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py` computed

```python
base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM   # dense 2048 B block stride
```

so for every prefill it (a) left the request's own tail block unseeded and (b) wrote 2048 B of raw bf16 K / gate rows at byte `blk * 2048` of the layer's indexer region, i.e. into indexer block `blk * 2048 // 38016` at offset `blk * 2048 % 38016` — fp8 key rows or the fp32 scale region of whatever request owns that block. The decode kernel (`TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS` / `KPOOL_HEAD`) and the AMD seed kernel already address the tail through `stride(0)` / `stride(1)`; only the NVIDIA seed kernel did not, and the existing regression test for exactly this layout was `skipif(not is_rocm)`.

**Why it shows up as "the cached system prompt is broken".** Only indexer blocks with id below `num_blocks * 2048 / 38016` (~5% of the pool) can be hit, and those are the ids handed out first after startup, i.e. the blocks of the first prefix-cached prompt, typically a long-lived system prompt. Every later request whose tail block id falls in `[19, ~19 * k]` overwrites part of that prompt's indexer blocks `1..k`; prefix-cached blocks are never recomputed, so the damage persists and accumulates, on every TP rank identically. The MLA KV itself is untouched (all writes stay inside the layer's indexer region), so the effect is a corrupted sparse top-k selection for any context longer than `index_topk` (2048). The predicted signature is therefore: with prefix caching on, requests that hit a long-lived cached prompt degrade over time while the same prompt sent with a `cache_salt` (fresh, high block ids) stays correct even on repeated cache hits, and all TP ranks are affected identically. The reproduction below confirms exactly this.

**Fix.** Pass `TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS = tail.stride(0)` and `KPOOL_HEAD = tail.stride(1)` to the NVIDIA seed kernel (same as the AMD kernel), assert the expected view layout in `kpool_seed_tail_cache`, and run `test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride` on every platform.

**Origin.** The tail cache has aliased the indexer tensor with a padded, strided view since the tail spec was introduced on the GLM-5.3-Flash development branch (07-28); the prefill seed was a torch fancy-index scatter (`tail[block_ids, 0, offsets] = k`, stride-correct) until it was replaced by this Triton kernel with dense addressing (08-17, "perf: indexer eager path tail seed and scatter"). The kernel reached main unchanged with #53906 and is unchanged in the current main, so every NVIDIA build since #53906 is affected.

**Not a duplicate.** #56059 adds a `NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS` out-of-range guard to the same kernel for a ROCm fault (#56037); it does not change the addressing, and the two changes compose. No other open PR touches the NVIDIA seed kernel's addressing.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py -q
```

Kernel-level repro (SM103): build the runtime tail view with `create_kv_cache_views(KpoolTailSpec(block_size=4, num_kv_heads=2, head_size=128, dtype=bf16, page_size_padded=38016), ...)` over a sentinel-filled 256 x 38016 B buffer, seed one 6-token request whose tail block is 200 (and 18), then inspect which bytes changed.

End-to-end byte-level probe (GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on 4 x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `enforce_eager`, prefix caching on, `num_gpu_blocks_override=800` so the block pool wraps every ~130 requests): an offline `LLM` serves a 14.5k-token system prompt of 420 "vault -> access code" records, then `collective_rpc` snapshots the indexer K cache pages and the tail cache of the prompt's blocks on rank 0. Eight rounds of 50 unrelated filler prompts (200-2000 tokens each) follow; after every round one lookup question re-hits the cached prompt (keeping it hot in the LRU) and the cached pages are diffed against the snapshot taken right after the first request. Finally seven lookup questions are asked against the hot cached prompt. Same script, same seed, on main and on this branch.

Request-level reproduction against a running server (OpenAI API only, no GPU introspection): same 14.5k-token registry prompt, 7 lookup questions, then batches of 100 unrelated filler prompts (150-1500 tokens, unique prefixes, concurrency 16) each followed by the 7 lookups (cache hit), then the same prompt with `cache_salt` twice. Server: main, TP4, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `enforce_eager`, `--num-gpu-blocks-override 800` so the block pool cycles quickly (with the default pool the same script needs several thousand fillers).

## Test Result

Kernel-level repro, tail view `stride = (19008, 512, 128, 1)` elements:

| kernel | tail block | own tail block seeded | bytes written (layer indexer region) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 200 | no (still sentinel) | `[409600, 411648)` = indexer block 10, fp8 rows 230..245 |
| main | 18 | no | `[36864, 38912)` = indexer block 0 scale region + block 1 rows 0..6 |
| this PR | 200 | yes | `[7603200, 7605248)` = block 200, bytes 0..2048 |
| this PR | 18 | yes | `[684288, 686336)` = block 18, bytes 0..2048 |

`pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py`: on main the un-skipped `test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride` fails (`tail[3, 0, 2]` is still the sentinel); with this PR 29 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only preshuffle test).

End-to-end probe. Runtime views match the analysis: indexer `k_cache` `[7200, 32, 132]` uint8 stride `(4224, 132, 1)` (800 blocks x 9 DeepGEMM pages) and `tail_cache` `[800, 2, 4, 128]` bf16 stride `(19008, 512, 128, 1)` share one `data_ptr`. The system prompt occupies indexer blocks 1..13; the 38 fully cached pages of blocks 1..5 were watched.

| filler requests since the prompt was cached | main: cached pages modified | main: bytes modified | main: re-hit lookup | this PR: pages modified | this PR: re-hit lookup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 16 / 38 | 18.4 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 100 | 21 / 38 | 28.6 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 150 | 21 / 38 | 36.7 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 200 | 24 / 38 | 41.6 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 250 | 25 / 38 | 45.7 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 300 | 25 / 38 | 47.8 KB | no code | 0 | correct |
| 350 | 27 / 38 | 58.0 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 400 | 30 / 38 | 64.1 KB | no code | 0 | correct |

Final seven lookups against the hot cached prompt: main 1/7 correct, with garbled answers such as `vault harbor-harbor-7` and `raven-saffron-203? No, wait`; this PR 7/7 correct. The modified regions on main are contiguous 2048 B runs (e.g. page 9 offsets 0..2816), i.e. one misplaced tail seed per filler request, and on main the very first request already writes 2048 B into indexer block 0 (the null block); neither happens with this PR. In a shorter server-based run on main (default pool of 9259 blocks, only 120 fillers, no wrap-around) the cached prompt was still answered correctly, which is consistent with the sparse per-request damage: each filler misplaces one 2048 B chunk, so a hot prompt degrades as the free list keeps cycling through the low block ids, while a `cache_salt` copy of the prompt (fresh, high block ids) is never hit.

Request-level reproduction on main (correct lookups out of 7; `/metrics` confirmed 96768/101978 prompt tokens served from the prefix cache in every re-hit pass):

| pass | correct |
|---|---|
| fresh prefill | 7 |
| cache hit, before fillers | 7 |
| cache hit after 100 / 200 / 300 / 400 / 500 / 600 fillers | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| same prompt with `cache_salt` (fresh blocks) | 7 |
| salted prompt again (cache hit) | 7 |

After the fillers the model no longer even reads the question correctly (`vault velvet-tundra-143` for `velvet-tundra-67`, `they haven't specified which vault`, `the human turn is empty`): the cached prompt is unusable while the salted copy of the very same prompt is fine.

---

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix Aria expert weight names and layout
author: jiangLLM
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57473.

Aria cannot load its expert weights. The name conversion leaves an extra `.weight` suffix, so the loader cannot find the right parameter. After that suffix is removed, the tensor shapes still do not match because HF and vLLM use different layouts.

This PR fixes both issues in Aria. It corrects the weight names and enables the existing transpose option. The new tests check the exact values of both expert weights and a shared-expert weight. The mapper also keeps the existing module and scale names for quantization configs.

I also tested #57484 at `0402820` on CPU. The name error is fixed, but both Aria weights still fail with shape errors. In a separate check, its shared-loader change left Granite's expert weights unloaded. That is why this fix stays in Aria and leaves the shared loader unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
/opt/venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_aria.py tests/models/test_utils.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/aria.py tests/models/multimodal/test_aria.py tests/models/test_utils.py
```

The tests use weights from an HF Aria `state_dict` and the vLLM loader.

## Test Result

Before the fix, both expert cases fail and the shared-expert case passes. All six tests in `tests/models/multimodal/test_aria.py` now pass. The config-name test also fails on the earlier version of this PR and passes with the updated mapper. Together with the general loader tests, the result is **13 passed and one CUDA-only skip**. title: [Pooling] Fix normalization of chunked long-text embeddings
author: taneem-ibrahim
body:
## Purpose

Averaging normalized chunks can produce a non-unit long-text embedding. Re-normalize multi-chunk aggregates when `use_activation=True`, preserving single-chunk and raw outputs.

## Reproducer

The temporary CPU reproducer passes two equal-weight, orthogonal normalized
chunk embeddings through `_post_process_chunked`. It also checks a one-chunk
BF16 prompt and the `use_activation=False` path.

```bash
env PYTHONPATH=<main-worktree> .venv/bin/python /tmp/chunked_norm_cpu_reproducer.py
env PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python /tmp/chunked_norm_cpu_reproducer.py
```

## Output on main / on branch

Main:

```text
multi=[0.5, 0.5] norm=0.707107
single_exact=True value=[0.6015625, 0.80078125]
raw=[0.5, 0.5]
```

Branch:

```text
multi=[0.7071067690849304, 0.7071067690849304] norm=1.000000
single_exact=True value=[0.6015625, 0.80078125]
raw=[0.5, 0.5]
```

## H100 multi-model evaluation

The  end-to-end sweep used BF16, `max_model_len=128`, and long inputs of 1,192-1,682 tokens. It covered encoder mean pooling, encoder CLS pooling, and decoder last-token pooling.

| Model | Architecture / pooling | Old multi-chunk norms | New multi-chunk norms | Short max abs delta across independent servers | Minimum cosine with old output | Retrieval ranking |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `intfloat/e5-small-v2` | encoder / MEAN | 0.997116-0.997419 | 1.000000 | 7.45e-9 | 1.000000 | cosine and IP unchanged |
| `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` | encoder / CLS | 0.986880-0.993246 | 1.000000 | 1.49e-8 | 1.000000 | cosine and IP unchanged |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` | decoder / LAST | 0.784638-0.821176 | 1.000000 | 7.45e-9 | 0.999994 | cosine unchanged; IP changed |

For E5 and BGE, the new long output matched an explicitly normalized old weighted mean within `2.98e-8`. Qwen's maximum BF16 difference was `4.73e-4` with the same cosine ranking. Its IP ranking changed from `[0, 1, 2, 4, 3]`
to `[0, 1, 4, 2, 3]`, demonstrating why this should be documented as an intentional correctness-related output change rather than a refactor.

Short prompts do not execute the new normalization operation. The direct BF16 aggregation check is bitwise exact; independent H100 server launches differed by at most `1.49e-8`, consistent with normal numerical variation.

### Compatibility note

Only normalized outputs formed from multiple chunks change. Their direction is preserved while their magnitude becomes approximately 1. Cosine retrieval is therefore expected to remain stable, but inner-product scores and rankings can change. Deployments using inner-product indexes should not mix old and new long-document embeddings; re-embed affected long documents when upgrading.

## Test plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_io_processor.py -q
# 46 passed

env UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-uv-cache .venv/bin/pre-commit run \
  --files vllm/entrypoints/pooling/embed/io_processor.py
# Passed

env UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-uv-cache .venv/bin/pre-commit run \

# Passed, including dependency locks and mypy for Python 3.10-3.13
```

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Retain offload mappings after unsafe KVCR startup failure
author: karya0
body:
## Purpose

If KVCR startup fails while its native thread is still running, the teardown path still unmaps the offload region — `CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager.shutdown()` calls `SharedOffloadRegion.cleanup()`, and `TieringOffloadingSpec.get_manager()` only logs a failed `tier.shutdown()` before continuing. NIXL has that memory registered, so the NIC can complete writes into pages the process has already unmapped and reused: corruption, not a leak.

KVCR now signals this case with `KVCRStartupError` (ai-dynamo/kvcr#43). This translates it into `OffloadingStartupError`, hands the affected buffers to `retain_until_exit()`, and skips the unsafe cleanup. A leaked mapping in a process that is failing to start beats corrupting one that isn't. Ordinary failures keep their existing cleanup, and interrupts still propagate as themselves.

Requires the paired KVCR change; the worker-side mapping is untouched, since NIXL registers the separate scheduler-side view.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py
```

Both tests extend existing files and are parametrized over the three paths that must differ: an ordinary `RuntimeError` (cleanup runs), the startup error (buffers retained, cleanup skipped), and `KeyboardInterrupt` (retained, re-raised unchanged). One covers `TieringOffloadingSpec`, the other the KVCR tier; the latter asserts on a real `mmap` and `memoryview` rather than mocks.

## Test Result

All passing. Note `test_kvcr_tier.py` is gated by `pytest.importorskip("kvcr")`, so it needs an environment with the kvcr package to exercise.

No model evaluation: startup failure handling only, with no effect on the offload data path or generated output.

---

AI assistance was used for this change. Every changed line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][DBO] Fix DeepEP low-latency profiling crash with DP+EP+DBO
author: micah-wil
body:
## Summary
`tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py::test_dbo_dp_ep_gsm8k[deepep_low_latency]` started crashing at engine init (memory profiling) on ROCm (MI300X) with DP+EP+DBO.

Root cause: after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/5607, in the V1 `GPUModelRunner._dummy_run`, the MoE padding mask (`is_padding`) was computed **after** `num_tokens_padded` had been shrunk to a single microbatch for DBO forward-context bookkeeping. The mask only spanned one microbatch, so the DBO ubatch wrapper sliced an out-of-range (empty) mask for the trailing microbatch. That desynchronized the DeepEP low-latency combine across the two microbatches and crashed with:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'recv_hook'
ValueError: torch.cat(): expected a non-empty list of Tensors
```

## Fix
- Compute `is_padding` against the **full** padded token count, before the single-ubatch adjustment, so every microbatch gets a correctly sized mask.
- Route the dummy tokens through the experts during a **profile** run (instead of masking them all as padding), mirroring the ModelRunner V2 behavior so MoE memory is measured and the MoE kernels are exercised.

## Test
Verified on MI300X (2x, DP=2, EP, DBO, DeepEP built from ROCm/DeepEP):
- `test_dbo_dp_ep_gsm8k[deepep_low_latency]` -> PASSED
- `test_dbo_dp_ep_gsm8k[deepep_high_throughput]` -> PASSED

This PR was generated with AI assistance. All code and reasoning has been reviewed by myself.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix MiMo-V2.5 fused fp8 qkv_proj sharding (pre-shard count is num_key_value_heads; MTP path too)
author: vllmellm
body:
## Purpose

`XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` cannot load on current main at any TP size. 

Currently with TP4, on mi355x/mi300x we will hit this error.

```
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py", line 527, in _shard_fp8_qkv_proj
    w_g_dequant = w_g * s_g_expanded
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1856) must match the size of tensor b (1792) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

This is not platform specific, so every platform that runs this checkpoint is affected.

The root cause is, the checkpoint's fused `qkv_proj` is pre-sharded at `ckpt_tp = config.num_key_value_heads` (4 here), each chunk holding `[Q_c | K_c | V_c]` with its own fp8 block scales, while `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` (#45200) assumes one chunk per KV head. The assumption holds for Pro (8 KV heads / 8 chunks) and for V2.5's GA layers (4/4) — those load fine today — but not for the SWA layers: 8 KV heads over 4 chunks, so each chunk carries two KV heads.

Concretely, for `model.layers.1.self_attn.qkv_proj`:
- weight `(14848, 4096)` = 4 chunks of 3072 Q + 384 K + 256 V = **3712** rows = **29** blocks exactly
- `weight_scale_inv` `(116, 32)` = **4 × 29**; the one-per-KV-head reading expects 8 × 15 = 120 and per-group-floor 112, so the loader's `116 // 8 = 14` expands to 1792 rows vs the 1856-row slice

For GA layers (`(13568, 108)`, chunks of 3392 = 3072+192+128) and Pro (`(27136, 216)`, 8 chunks of 3392) the pre-shard count happens to equal the KV-head count, which is why SWA breaks. 

## Change

1. `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` takes `ckpt_tp` (= `config.num_key_value_heads`, i.e. the number of ranks the checkpoint was pre-sharded into — 4 for MiMo-V2.5, 8 for Pro) and derives the chunk geometry from the layer's own heads/dims.
   - `tp_size == ckpt_tp` → plain chunk of weight and scales (the chunk already is `[Q_r|K_r|V_r]`; scale rows line up with `ceil(rows/128)`);
   - otherwise gather each rank's Q/K/V head rows from the chunks that hold them, dequantize with the per-chunk scale mapping `(row // rows_per_chunk) * ceil(rows_per_chunk/128) + (row % rows_per_chunk) // 128`, reorder and requantize (zero-padding the 26.5-block tail, since `scaled_quantize` needs full blocks);
   - a scale tensor matching neither the per-chunk nor a continuous grid now raises instead of being dequantized with the wrong scale.
2. TP > `num_kv_heads` (GA layers at TP=8) via KV replication, the same convention `QKVParallelLinear` uses for split checkpoints: rank *r* owns KV head `r // (tp_size // num_kv_heads)`, so each Q head stays with the KV head it attends to.
3. `mimo_v2_mtp.py`: the MTP draft loader sharded the fused qkv with a plain `chunk(tp_size)` for weight *and* scales. At TP=4 that is correct by coincidence, at TP=8 the scale chunks come out `[15]*7 + [11]` against a 15-row parameter (rank 7 asserts in `default_weight_loader`) and mid-block ranks take a neighbouring block's scale. It now buffers weight + `weight_scale_inv` per layer and shards them through `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` with `ckpt_tp = config.num_key_value_heads`; non-fp8 fused checkpoints keep the old path.
4. added `tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py`: new CPU-only unit test. It builds GA, SWA and Pro checkpoints in the export's chunk layout with known fp32 weights and asserts, for TP = 1, 2, 4, 8, that every rank's dequantized rows match an independent reference; that tp_size == ckpt_tp returns the checkpoint chunk unchanged; and that reading the SWA scales as one slice per KV head is detectably wrong (relL2 > 5x tolerance). 

For reference, #53242 fixes only the SWA symptom (global row map — exact for SWA, but it mis-scales 62.7% of GA rows and would mis-scale 81.4% of Pro's), and #46755 adds the TP > `num_kv_heads` case with per-KV-head scale arithmetic, which for V2.5's MTP tensors would compute `116 // 8 = 14` and break TP=4 spec decode that works today. 

## Test Plan

Non-spec, the reported configuration (TP=4) and TP=8 + EP:

```bash
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len auto --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo

vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len auto --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo
```

Spec decode (MTP), both TP sizes:

```bash
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len auto --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mimo_v2_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo
```

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template
```

## Test Result

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm serve ... --tensor-parallel-size 4` | crash at load | **Server started, with sensible output** |
| TP=8 (w/wo EP) | `AssertionError: TP size must evenly split the number of KV heads` | **Server started, with sensible output** |
| TP=4 + MTP spec (`num_speculative_tokens=1`) | crash at load | loads, draft acceptance **~95%** |
| TP=8 + (w/wo) EP + MTP spec | crash at load | **loads, draft acceptance 20703/21660 = 95.6%** |
| GSM8K (TP=2/4/8) | n/a (never loaded) | ** around 0.9704 flex / 0.9712 strict ± 0.005** |
| real tensors at TP=4 (GA, SWA, MTP), relL2 vs independent reference | crash | **0.0000** (pure chunk); TP=1/2 ≤ 0.011; TP=8 GA 0.0000, SWA 0.008-0.011 |
| TP=2 end-to-end | crash | *Server started, with sensible output** |
| synthetic GA/SWA/Pro checkpoints, TP 1/2/4/8 | crash / assert | 0.026-0.028 (fp8 round-trip floor) |
| old reading (`ckpt_tp = num_kv_heads`) on SWA | — | detectably wrong: relL2 1.05 |

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Remove stale W4A8 weight after repacking
author: gc-fu
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57503.

`XPUW4A8IntLinearKernel.process_weights_after_loading()` repacks the checkpoint-format W4A8 weight into the runtime `weight_packed` parameter.

Previously, after repacking, it released the original unpacked weight with:

```python
layer.register_parameter("weight", None)
```

This leaves the `weight` attribute present with a value of `None`.

LoRA device detection checks `weight` before `weight_packed`, so the stale attribute causes LoRA wrapper creation to fail on:

```text
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'device'
```

This change removes the obsolete `weight` attribute after repacking:

```python
delattr(layer, "weight")
```

The XPU W4A8 runtime path uses `weight_packed`, `weight_scale`, and `weight_zero_point`, so the unpacked `weight` is no longer needed after conversion.

This also allows the existing LoRA `weight_packed` fallback to work without changing generic LoRA device-detection behavior.

Removing the original weight after packing follows an existing compressed-tensors pattern, for example `compressed_tensors_wNa8o8.py`.

This PR supersedes #57480, which addressed the same failure by changing generic LoRA device probing. This PR instead fixes the stale state in the XPU W4A8 repacking path where it is introduced.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and validation. The resulting changes were reviewed by the submitter.

## Test Plan

* Exercise XPU W4A8 post-load repacking directly.
* Verify the obsolete `weight` attribute is removed.
* Verify the existing LoRA device detection selects `weight_packed`.
* Run the broader LoRA layer tests.
* Serve a compressed-tensors W4A8 `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` export with LoRA enabled using TP=2 on Intel XPU.
* Send an OpenAI-compatible completion request.

title: [Bugfix] Reclaim cached GPU memory during weight loading
author: debanshd
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57440.

During `BaseModelLoader.load_model()`, temporary tensors created in `load_weights()` and `process_weights_after_loading()` (such as FP8/MXFP4 weight repacking buffers) remain reserved in PyTorch's caching allocator pool (`reserved - allocated`). On discrete GPUs, `release_device_memory_under_pressure()` is a no-op because it only runs on integrated GPUs, leaving raw CUDA driver allocations (such as DeepEP v2 `cuMemCreate` / DMA-BUF buffers, `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`, or secondary model fit checks via `mem_get_info()`) starved of free driver HBM.

This PR adds `gc.collect()` and `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` (when `current_platform.is_cuda_alike()`) at the two weight-loading lifecycle boundaries in `BaseModelLoader.load_model()`:
1. Immediately after `self.load_weights(model, model_config)` before `process_weights_after_loading()`
2. Immediately after `process_weights_after_loading(model, model_config, target_device)`

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_base_loader_memory.py -q
```

## Test Result

`2 passed` verifying the exact ordering of `load_weights` -> `gc.collect` / `empty_cache` -> `process_weights_after_loading` -> `gc.collect` / `empty_cache` on CUDA-alike platforms and skipping `empty_cache` on non-CUDA platforms.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Fail streams that end in a server error event
author: tevinshi2015
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`vllm bench serve` counts a request as successful when any token arrived, even if the stream then ends in a server error event. This fails those requests in the completions, chat and audio backends, in both `vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py` and the standalone `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py`.

Benchmark client only: no model, kernel or serving path is touched.

## Claims

- A stream that delivers tokens and then an `error` event is reported as failed, with the server's error object in `output.error`. Partial `generated_text` is kept for `--save-detailed`.
- The server's error takes precedence over "Never received a valid chunk to calculate TTFT", which names a symptom rather than the cause.
- Under a mid-run EngineCore kill at concurrency 64, the unpatched report overstates completed requests by 22% and output throughput by 14%, and understates mean E2EL by 8%.

## Validation

Unit (no GPU), at the rebased head `4a4eb4257`, on base `76c6f3f2a`. `test_error_event_stream_is_not_reported_as_success` and its legacy counterpart stream two tokens, then the error envelope, then `[DONE]`, over all three streaming endpoints.

```bash
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -k error_event
```

| Sources | Result |
|---|---|
| Base `76c6f3f2a` (new tests only) | 6 failed, each `AssertionError: assert not True` on `output.success` |
| This PR | 6 passed |
| This PR, full `test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py` + `test_responses_request_func.py` | 74 passed |

Those pytest runs used `--noconftest` in a CPU-only environment. `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files <changed>` passes, including mypy.

End-to-end on one RTX 3060 (clocks locked), Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, `vllm bench serve --save-detailed`, random 512-token prompts, 128 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`; `kill -9` on EngineCore 20 s into the run. Measured at the original commit, before the rebase. Classifying one unpatched run's own requests by token count, at concurrency 64:

| Reported by the benchmark | Reported | Complete requests only | Error |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| completed | 274 | 225 | **+22%** |
| mean E2EL | 2,566 ms | 2,790 ms | 8% too fast |
| output tokens | 32,684 | 28,800 | +3,884 partial tokens |
| output throughput | 2,745 tok/s | 2,418 tok/s | **+14%** |

49 of the 274 "successful" requests (18%) never produced their 128 tokens; their counts run 1-127, median 121, so they do not stand out by eye. With the fix, the same fault reports 221 completed, all complete, and each failed request carries the server's error object.

Only a request that has already streamed a token and then receives the error event is miscounted, so the effect scales with in-flight streams at the fault: 49 at concurrency 64, 1-4 at concurrency 16.

Independent validation at the earlier commit `1e74a69c7`: [regression corpus](https://github.com/k21993/benchmark-stream-audit) from a comment on this PR.

No `RemoteOpenAIServer` regression test is added: a real server cannot deterministically emit this event mid-stream without fault injection, so the tests drive the real request functions over the existing fake session, and the end-to-end run above covers the real failure.

**Model evaluation:** not applicable; this only changes how the benchmark client classifies a response.

## Details

**Root cause.** A generation that fails after the response has started cannot change the HTTP 200 already sent, so the stream generators report the failure in-band:

```text
data: {"error": {"message": "EngineCore encountered an issue. ...", "type": "InternalServerError", "param": null, "code": 500}}
data: [DONE]
```

The clients read only `choices` and `usage`, so the truncated request joins `completed`, its partial tokens join `total_output` and `output_throughput`, and its short end-to-end time joins the E2EL statistics. The report is biased in the optimistic direction exactly when the server is failing.

**Design.** The same envelope is emitted for a dead engine, a failed tool parser and a generation error, so the fix keys on the `error` object rather than on one cause. It uses the same `stream_error` shape as the Responses backend.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched the PRs touching these files:
- #54708 (merged) fails streams with no token chunk; a stream that produces tokens and then fails still counted as a success.
- #55508 (merged) fixed TTFT/E2E latency accounting; it does not look at error events.
- #54628 (merged) handles error events for the Responses backend only.
- #62341 (merged) filters content-free chat chunks; this PR is rebased on it and keeps `_choice_has_streamed_output`.
- #64143 (open) changes SSE data-field parsing, not failure classification; it touches the same file, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

**Follow-up.** The Rust bench client (`rust/src/bench/src/backends/openai_completions.rs`, `openai_chat.rs`) has the same gap and is left out to keep this change in one language. #59736 covers token-less streams there, not this case. I can send it separately or fold it in here.

**How this was found.** While `SIGKILL`ing EngineCore under load to compare what each observer reports, requests in flight at the fault ended with HTTP 200 after 1-116 of their 128 tokens.

---

title: [Build] Fix DeepGEMM CUDA 12.9 release builds
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Restore the six CUDA 12.9 release targets that fail in [release-v2 #6858](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/6858): x86_64 and aarch64 wheels, plus both architectures' default and Ubuntu 24.04 images.

All six fail while compiling DeepGEMM's host extension because `layout/mega_mhc.cuh` uses `__nv_fp8_e4m3` without including `<cuda_fp8.h>`. CUDA 13's transitive includes mask the missing declaration; CUDA 12.9 does not. The subsequent `y_fp8` errors are consequences of that missing type.

Update both synchronized DeepGEMM pins from `a6bbb800` to the merged upstream commit [e1f418c2](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/commit/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f) from [DeepGEMM#12](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/12). The dependency delta is exactly five include lines in two headers; it preserves all current SM90/SM120 and Mega MoE changes.

## Duplicate-work check

The header fix is merged in DeepGEMM#12; this PR consumes that work in vLLM and does not propose another upstream implementation. The merged commit has vLLM's current pin as its sole parent. The original duplicate-work checks found no competing open vLLM integration PR or matching open issue for `mega_mhc.cuh`.

## Validation

The merged pin `e1f418c2` and previously tested cherry-pick `70874eca` have the identical Git tree `cd1947d66f49ef498fdeb6f227bb9e52b5ba0787` (including submodule gitlinks). `git diff --exit-code 70874eca e1f418c2` passes with no changes. title: [fix] Mistral-Large-3 accuracy regression on `main`
author: jdebache
body:
## Purpose

It appears some changes to the config parsing for Mistral Large 3 degraded accuracy. These changes try to remediate.

### Root cause

Mistral-Large-3 ships a Mistral-format `params.json` with

```json
"yarn": {"factor": 36, "beta": 32, "alpha": 1, "original_max_position_embeddings": 8192, "apply_scale": false},
"llama_4_scaling": {"beta": 0.1, "original_max_position_embeddings": 8192}
```

i.e. YaRN frequency interpolation **without** YaRN's magnitude correction (mscale), plus
llama4-style position-dependent attention scaling. vLLM serves it as
`MistralLarge3ForCausalLM`, a subclass of `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, so the DeepSeek
attention code runs on a config synthesized by the Mistral adapter
(`vllm/transformers_utils/configs/mistral.py`).

Commit `c191787a68`, "[Bugfix] Align vLLM YaRN with Transformers and stop re-scaling
max_model_len" (#56446, merged 2026-09-11).

Mistral-Large-3 is the only model that both goes through the Mistral remap and asks for
YaRN without magnitude scaling, which is why nothing else moved. Verified by loading the
checkpoint's config through `get_config(..., config_format="mistral")`: on `main` the
resulting `rope_parameters` has `attention_factor: 1.0` and no `apply_yarn_scaling`.

## Test Plan

Start server with `vllm serve` and evaluate on GSM8K.

Identical for both arms (TP1 / DP4 / EP4, default MoE backend, which resolves to
FlashInfer TRTLLM for this checkpoint):

```bash
vllm serve \
    /models/Mistral-Large-3-675B-Instruct-2512-NVFP4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --moe-backend auto --tokenizer-mode mistral --language-model-only \
    --max-model-len 5120 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --seed 42 --port 8000
```

Testing is done using the gsm8k eval, launched with the helper script: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` from the vLLM checkout against the running server, five
times back to back per arm (only `--save-results` changes between passes, we ran multiple times to reduce variance):

```bash
python /workspace/vllm/tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
    --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
    --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 \
    --temperature 0 --seed 42 --max-concurrency 128 \
    --save-results gsm8k-rep<N>.json
```

## Test Result

(accuracy, %)

| arm | pass 1 | pass 2 | pass 3 | pass 4 | pass 5 | mean | sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main-no-fix` (`4c6c1a40b3`) | 87.41 | 87.72 | 87.49 | 87.87 | 89.76 | 88.05 | 0.97 |
| `fix` (`265b1c54e3`) | 92.49 | 92.72 | 92.95 | 92.80 | 92.19 | 92.63 | 0.30 |

Difference: **+4.58 points** for the fix (about 60 more correct answers per pass of 1,319).
Welch t = 10.1 on 5 vs 5 passes; the per-pass binomial noise floor at this accuracy is
0.81 points. Invalid-answer rate was 0.00% in every pass except one fix pass at 0.08%
(one question). The fixed arm matches the 92.2 / 92.8% measured on 2026-09-10, before
#56446 was merged.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement get_top_tokens() on the ROCm DeepSeek V4 MTP drafter
author: BaoYunkai
body:
## Purpose

Enabling `speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` with a `deepseek_v4` draft model **fails
engine startup** rather than falling back to the full-vocab path:

```
ValueError: use_local_argmax_reduction is enabled but draft model DeepSeekV4MTP
does not implement get_top_tokens().
```

Both opt-in sites probe the draft model with `hasattr(model, "get_top_tokens")` and raise when it
is missing (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:1606`,
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py:387`), and `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictor` implements
only `compute_logits`. So the flag is a trap for every `deepseek_v4` checkpoint: it does not run
slower, it does not start.

`model_type: deepseek_v4` is rewritten to `DeepSeekV4MTPModel` by its own branch in
`SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`, which the registry resolves to the per-platform
`DeepSeekV4MTP`, so the generic MTP drafter fix in #56995 does not reach it.

**Fix.** Forward to `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` from both the predictor and the wrapper in
the ROCm implementation (`amd/mtp.py`), mirroring the `compute_logits` pair already in the file.
The `nvidia` and `xpu` drafters are not changed: this was verified on MI355X only, so they are
left to a follow-up that can be tested on that hardware.

V4 reaches its LM head through `hc_head` over the `(T, hc_mult, D)` residual and then the shared
head's RMSNorm, unlike V3 (`shared_head` alone) and V3.2 (an already-normed hidden state). Running
a different transform returns a *different draft token* instead of failing, so that transform is
factored into `_pre_head()` and shared by `compute_logits` and `get_top_tokens` rather than written
twice.

`use_local_argmax_reduction` defaults to `False` and gates every call site, so the default path is
unchanged.

## Test Plan

Hardware: MI355X (`gfx950`), HIP 7.2.53211, torch 2.11.0. Measurements ran against a substrate
built from upstream `releases/v0.27.1` (the sha the host's build names) plus that build's compiled
extensions; in the region this PR touches, v0.27.1 and `main` differ only in how the shared-head
RMSNorm kernel is re-exported, so the arms transfer. The two arms are one tree differing in exactly
one file (`diff -r`).

1. **Unit tests** (added, ROCm only; the module skips before importing the ROCm drafter elsewhere):
   `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dsv4_mtp_local_argmax.py`, asserting that the token
   `get_top_tokens` selects carries the row maximum of the full-vocab logits. Re-run on a v0.30.0
   substrate after rebasing onto current `main`.
2. **Falsifiability**: the same tests run against the merge base, and against two deliberately
   wrong implementations — the shared-head RMSNorm dropped, and `hc_head` dropped.
3. **Micro, TP=2**: both arms as methods on the same predictor over a real TP process group with
   the real `hc_head` op, RMSNorm kernel, `ParallelLMHead` and `LogitsProcessor`, swept over draft
   batch. Four pairs per point, pair 0 discarded, arm order alternated.
4. **e2e, TP=2**: `vllm bench serve` on `DSV4-base-tpl`, fp8 KV cache, 1024 in / 512 out, 300
   prompts, `--max-concurrency 68`. Four interleaved pairs, pair 0 discarded.
5. **GSM8K A/B**: `lm_eval --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, greedy, all 1319 items,
   `enable_prefix_caching=False`, per-sample logging, **with a base-repeat control** (`base2`, a
   second run of the same build) so the noise floor is measured rather than assumed.

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** 3 passed. All 3 fail on the merge base. Dropping the shared-head RMSNorm fails 2 of
3; dropping `hc_head` fails 2 of 3. The norm gain is `normal_(1.0, 0.5)` and the `hc_head`
scale/base are non-trivial on purpose: an argmax is invariant to RMSNorm's per-row rescale, so a
default all-ones weight could not detect a skipped norm at all.

**Micro (TP=2).** This is a trade-off with a crossover, not a uniform win, so the crossover and the
absolute per-step cost matter more than any median over the sweep:

| shape | crossover (draft batch) | worst cost below | best saving above |
|---|---|---|---|
| hidden 4096, vocab 129280 | 36 → 44 | bs=6: +80.8 µs/step (−42.7 %) | bs=1028: −2496.6 µs/step (+80.1 %) |
| hidden 7168, vocab 129280 | 12 → 20 | bs=6: +29.6 µs/step (−12.4 %) | bs=1028: −2511.1 µs/step (+71.9 %) |

**Token agreement is 1.0000 at all 32 swept points**, on both the selected index and the selected
logit value. The crossover had to be recomputed for V4 rather than carried over from #56995's V3
numbers, and it differs between the two V4 shapes.

**e2e (TP=2, concurrency 68, above the crossover).** No change in either direction:

| metric | base | patched | pairwise median | pairwise range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s | 1935.13 | 1929.16 | −0.17 % | −0.92 … +1.26 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 31.25 | 31.22 | +0.55 % | −0.73 … +0.62 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 30.37 | 30.48 | −0.07 % | −1.72 … +0.89 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 584.73 | 588.33 | −1.11 % | −1.59 … −0.33 % |
| Acceptance length | 1.31 | 1.31 | −0.11 % | −1.08 … +0.67 % |

That is the expected result, and it is worth stating why rather than leaving it to be read as a
disappointment: the micro saving at the batch this run reached is 84.7 µs, while the measured
engine step is 40.83 ms (mean TPOT 31.25 ms × acceptance length 1.31), so the predicted e2e effect
is **+0.21 %** — an order of magnitude below the pair-to-pair spread. The e2e arm can show that
nothing regressed; it cannot resolve the win. Pair 0, had it been kept, would have read +8.41 %,
because the base arm alone rose from 1775.6 to 1935.1 tok/s between pair 0 and pair 1 on AITER JIT
warmup. Unchanged acceptance length is the e2e-level statement that the draft tokens did not
change.

**GSM8K (1319 items, 5-shot, greedy).**

| arm | strict | flexible |
|---|---|---|
| base | 0.9515 ± 0.0059 | 0.9507 ± 0.0060 |
| base2 (same build, control) | 0.9522 ± 0.0059 | 0.9530 ± 0.0058 |
| patched | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | 0.9492 ± 0.0060 |

Effect (base → patched) is −0.0015 strict against a noise floor (base → base2) of +0.0008; both are
well inside the ±0.0059 stderr. Per-sample agreement is the sharper test and needs the same
control: base vs base2 produce identical text on **36.5 %** of items, base vs patched on **36.0 %**
— indistinguishable. Same-verdict rates are 98.1 % and 98.2 %. Two runs of one build already
disagree on most generations because vLLM's batching makes bf16 reductions batch-shape dependent,
so without the control column the 64 % of differing prompts would read as a regression. Claim: no
measurable accuracy change on GSM8K within the base-repeat noise floor — not bit-exactness.

**Not covered.** GSM8K exercises one shape of one path and says nothing about long context,
sampling or multi-turn.

---

AI assistance: the patch, its tests and the measurements above were produced with Claude via
Cursor, and reviewed by the submitter. Found by
[Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom).

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Avoid receive reports for notification-only requests
author: NickLucche
body:
A notif-only decode request (abort/full prefix cache hit) can still need to notify the prefiller to release KV. 
If that notification's handshake fails, NIXL reports a failed receive for a request the scheduler has already removed, crashing EngineCore. 
See "CI issue example" for how this relates to [Buildkite 89597](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89597/list?jid=01a0aefa-3c19-4a8d-b721-4199af7bf4d8&tab=output).

Keep notification-only entries out of receive tracking. This also covers full local prefix hits, where the KV is already local and the scheduler never waits for a receive. Producer notification is still attempted, but its failure no longer reports a receive failure or completion. 

Actual receives retain both signals: completion is needed to release blocks under `fail` or resume scheduling under `recompute`.

## Cancellation example

1. Prefiller P has computed KV for request A.
2. Decoder D cancels A before scheduling it. D removes A from the scheduler, but queues a notification telling P to release its KV. This has `awaiting_kvs=False` and no local receive blocks.
3. The worker attempts the handshake needed to notify P. The handshake fails—for example, because of a block-size mismatch.
4. Before the fix: A was registered as a receive, so the worker reports both `failed_recving={A}` and `finished_recving={A}`. The scheduler processes the completion, cannot find A, and crashes.
5. After the fix: A isn’t registered as a receive. The notification is still attempted and its failure logged, but no receive failure or completion reaches the scheduler.

## CI issue example

In [Buildkite 89597](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89597/list?jid=01a0aefa-3c19-4a8d-b721-4199af7bf4d8&tab=output), a four-block KV receive fails because of the 1920/1024 block-size mismatch (_expected_ for SSMs has block size is tp dependent). 

While returning the generation error, D's serving wrapper submits a separate cleanup request with `abort_immediately=True` and the same producer KV reference. 

That request never runs inference: it only tells P to release its KV. Its handshake hits the same mismatch, and NIXL reports a failed receive for a request already removed from the scheduler, crashing EngineCore.

1. P computes KV for request A. D's attempt to receive it fails; A finishes with an error.
2. D's serving error-cleanup wrapper submits a separate request B with `abort_immediately=True`, carrying A's producer KV reference.
3. The engine immediately aborts B. The connector queues an empty receive solely to notify P to release its blocks: `awaiting_kvs=False`, no local receive blocks. B is removed from the scheduler.
4. B's notification handshake hits the same block-size mismatch. Before the fix, the worker reports `failed_recving={B}` and `finished_recving={B}`; the scheduler cannot find B and crashes.
5. After the fix, B is not tracked as a receive. Notification is still attempted and its failure logged, but no receive failure or completion reaches the scheduler.

cc @njhill @jyizheng since you guys introduced `awaiting_kvs` 

### On Buildkite

The Buildkite adjustment is orthogonal, included in this PR to unblock the release: set both Kimi DP/EP block sizes to 2048 to avoid the 1920/1024 handshake mismatch

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Reserve sparse prefill buffers before KV cache sizing
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
FIX #57449 

Addresses #57449 by reserving sparse-prefill query/output buffers before KV-cache sizing and reusing them through FlashMLA's `out=` argument. Preserves compact output layout and supports the HY V4 override. Native FP32 statistics still allocate.

title: [Bugfix] DiffusionGemma: fix multimodal support
author: mmastrac
body:
## Purpose

DiffusionGemma reuses `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration._process_image_input` for its image path. That method reads `self._enable_mm_lora`, which Gemma4's constructor sets. DiffusionGemma's doesn't, so any request with an image raises `AttributeError` in the encoder runner and takes the engine down.

Set the flag in DiffusionGemma's constructor the same way Gemma4 does.

Required for #57250 to support multimodal inputs.

## Test plan

Hardware: 1 DGX Spark.

Send an image.

```
vllm serve nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4 --max-model-len 4096 --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 64}'
```

```
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4", "max_tokens": 32,
```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix multimodal embedding merge in Llama 4 and Mistral Large 3 EAGLE drafters
author: nishantrevur
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57630.

Regression from #50417 (first released in v0.28.0): that change marked these drafters as `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` so the speculator started routing multimodal batches through their `embed_input_ids`, which had been an unreachable alias of `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids` until then. cc @TQCB

`EagleLlama4ForCausalLM` and `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM` implement `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` by borrowing the method object `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids`. That method calls `self._embed_text_input_ids(...)` and reads `self._has_oov_mm_tokens`, both of which live on `SupportsMultiModal`, which the drafters do not inherit. Any multimodal target paired with one of these drafters fails during the first draft prefill (already in the profile run at startup):

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 427, in _run_model
File "vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py", line 507, in embed_input_ids
AttributeError: 'EagleLlama4ForCausalLM' object has no attribute '_embed_text_input_ids'. Did you mean: 'embed_input_ids'?
```

Reproduced on main (bf13ecc) and present in v0.28.0 and v0.29.0 with `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, TP=4, `--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle","model":...,"num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, default cudagraph mode. The same aliasing exists in `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM`; Model Runner V1 takes the same `embed_input_ids` path.

## Change

Replace the borrowed method with an explicit `embed_input_ids` in both drafters that embeds the draft input ids via `self.model.embed_input_ids` and merges external multimodal embeddings with `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, the same shape `EagleMistralForCausalLM` already uses. No behavior change for text-only batches.

## Test plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py -v   # 21 passed (2 new)
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/llama4_eagle.py vllm/model_executor/models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py
```

New test `test_mm_capable_drafter_merges_multimodal_embeddings` (parametrized over both classes) checks text-only embedding and the merge of multimodal rows; it raises `AttributeError` on main.

E2E (4x NVIDIA L4, TP=4, TRITON_ATTN, `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, `max_patches=4`, 18 text + 12 image prompts, greedy, 48 new tokens):

| build | cudagraph_mode | text AL | image AL | image per-pos acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main @ bf13ecc | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | startup crash (`AttributeError: ... '_embed_text_input_ids'`) | | |
| main + this PR | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 2.637 (328 drafts) | 2.424 (238 drafts) | 0.710 / 0.445 / 0.269 |
| main + this PR | NONE | 2.674 (322 drafts) | 2.413 (240 drafts) | 0.708 / 0.446 / 0.258 |

Image prompts now draft with acceptance close to text prompts, i.e. the drafter is receiving the image embeddings.

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and draft this change; every line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Persist FlashInfer autotune cache per rank to fix the rank-0-only cache-hit deadlock
author: MadhavJivrajani
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57423.

`flashinfer_autotune` persists the FlashInfer autotune cache from rank 0 only and, on the next
engine start, broadcasts that file to every rank. FlashInfer keys persisted MoE entries by
`tp_rank` / `ep_rank` (`MoERunner.get_cache_key_extras`), so only rank 0's lookups can hit. A hit
skips the per-tactic reduce of the synchronized tuning pass (`autotuner.py`: "a cache hit skips
that profile's reduce"), so ranks 1..N-1 block in the reduce while rank 0 spins at the trailing
barrier until the 30-minute timeout. Any second engine start that sees the file trips it: a
container restart with the cache directory on a pod-lifetime volume, or a persistent
`VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`.

Fix: each rank saves and loads its own file (`autotune_configs_dp{dp}_rank{r}.json`), and ranks
load only when every rank has a file, decided by one `all_gather_object` over the CPU group. That
gather replaces the previous broadcast and barrier at the same spot, so no collective is added.
Old single-file caches are ignored by name and re-primed on the next start.

## Field report

Observed on one 8xH100 node (SM90), TP8 + EP8 FP8 MoE model, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8a728663`
(v0.28.1rc1.dev388), FlashInfer 0.6.18, `$HOME` on a pod-lifetime emptyDir.

- The engine died of an unrelated GPU fault. The kubelet restarted the container in place 18 times
  over 8.5 h. Every restart: weights and KV cache fine, then all 8 ranks log
  `Loaded 42 configs from .../flashinfer_autotune_cache/0.6.18/90a/<hash>/autotune_configs.json`,
  rank 0 logs `Config cache hit for trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1 (runner=MoERunner, source=config file)`
  (and `gemm2`), ranks 1-7 sit in `Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1: k/21 [30:00<...]`, EngineCore
  logs `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds` every minute, then
  `torch.distributed.barrier` in `flashinfer_autotune` times out and the API server exits with
  `Engine core initialization failed`. Same signature as the log in #57423.
- During the hang: GPU 0 at 100 % utilization, GPUs 1-7 at 0 %; rank 0's worker at 100 % CPU in
  state R, the other seven sleeping. No other process held GPU 0.
- Mitigation/confirmation: renamed only the `flashinfer_autotune_cache/` directory aside and
  restarted the same container on the same GPUs. Autotune ran for 1 s on all ranks
  (`Saved 42 configs`), engine init took 20 s, READY. 19 identical failures, then one success with
  one variable changed.
- The stale and the fresh cache files hold the same 42 keys and identical `_metadata`; the stale
  one is rank 0's, so its keys only match `ep_rank=0`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py
```

New test: `_all_ranks_have_file` with world size 1, world size 2 all present, and world size 2
with one rank missing (must not load). CPU-only, no GPU needed.

## Test Result

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.0) clean on both files.
- The three `_all_ranks_have_file` cases pass when run against the affected 8xH100 pod's Python
  (torch available there).
- The full pytest file was not run locally (no torch on the dev machine); relying on CI for it.
- Live validation of the patched build on the affected deployment: not yet. The failure mode
  itself was confirmed by the cache-removal experiment above.

## Note

This is an alternative to #57579 which ensures all ranks load identical files as the leader.
However, the deadlock leading to vLLM being stuck (and subsequently in a crash-loop) on K8s is
caused by non-leader ranks expecting to see their entries in the cache file, so even if all
ranks load files that are identical, you would still run into this issue.

## AI assistance

The the patch, and the test were drafted with Claude Code and reviewed line by line by the author.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Fix MoE reprocess test mock after #57405's kernel refactor
author: vllm-agent
body:
## Problem

title: [CI][Bugfix] Correct the Laguna DFlash acceptance-length reference
author: okorzh-amd
body:
`test_dflash_correctness[laguna-nvfp4-mrv2]` enforces `expected_acceptance_len=3.55 * 0.9` = 3.195, which nothing reaches:

    AssertionError: acceptance_len 3.051 is below 3.195; accuracy=0.895

The reference is wrong rather than the platform slow. Measured with the same test, 200 GSM8K questions, transformers 5.17.0:

    MI355X (ROCm, emulated NVFP4)  acceptance_len 3.051   accuracy 0.895
    GB300  (CUDA, native NVFP4)    acceptance_len 3.0495  accuracy 0.890

Native and emulated NVFP4 on two vendors agree to three significant figures, and the in-run metrics oscillate 2.97/3.09/3.04, so ~3.05 is the steady state rather than a tail artifact. The sibling references in this file are annotated as coming from Table 1 of the DFlash paper; 3.55 looks like the same, and it was never exercised because this parametrization crashed in HF config parsing from the day it was added in #50330 until #57289 fixed that. Its first complete run is what surfaced the bad number.

Set the reference to the measured 3.05 and keep the file's 0.9 tolerance, giving a 2.745 floor and an 11% margin. Adjusting the reference rather than the tolerance leaves the other parametrizations untouched. Deliberately not a `current_platform` branch: the two vendors measure the same thing, so a per-platform floor would encode a difference that does not exist.

Verified on MI355X against main at a1bf8ac12d:

    tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py
        ::test_dflash_correctness[laguna-nvfp4-mrv2] PASSED
    1 passed, 5 deselected in 117.80s

title: [Bugfix][DP] add_dp_placement_groups does not require ray[default]
author: beenpow
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #23822.

That PR removed the `ray.util.state.list_nodes()` call from `CoreEngineActorManager.create_dp_placement_groups()` because `list_nodes()` is a developer API backed by the Ray dashboard HTTP server (`127.0.0.1:8265/api/v0/nodes`), which only exists when Ray is installed as `ray[default]` and started with the dashboard. vLLM does not depend on `ray[default]`.

The sibling `add_dp_placement_groups()` (used by `scale_up_elastic_ep()` for elastic EP scale-up) still called `list_nodes()`, so `/scale_elastic_ep` fails with `Failed to connect to API server` on any Ray cluster started without the dashboard, e.g. `ray` core only or `ray start --include-dashboard=False`. Downstream projects have had to monkeypatch `ray.util.state.list_nodes` around the call to work around this (NVIDIA Dynamo, `components/src/dynamo/vllm/handlers.py`, `TODO(upstream-vllm)` block in `scale_elastic_ep`).

This PR applies the same fix as #23822 to `add_dp_placement_groups()`:

- Drop the `ray.util.state.list_nodes` import.
- Use `available_resources_per_node()` (already imported there, keyed by node id, live nodes only) to enumerate nodes, and locate the DP master node via its `node:<dp_master_ip>` resource key, exactly as `create_dp_placement_groups()` does today.
- Read each node's IP with the existing `_node_ip_from_resources()` helper.

Placement group bundles, names (`dp_rank_{rank}`), strategy (`STRICT_PACK`), and the local DP rank computation are unchanged. The old "there can only be one head node" check is kept.

## Test Plan

New unit tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py`:

- Mock a Ray cluster with two GPU nodes and one CPU-only node, with the DP master deliberately not first.
- Replace `ray.util.state.list_nodes` with a function that raises, so any regression back to the dashboard API fails the tests.
- Cover: multi-node growth, TP>1 growth, no-growth early return, missing master node.

```shell
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py -q
```

End-to-end on one node with 4x RTX PRO 5000 (vLLM 0.29.0 wheel + this patch, ray 2.58.0), same model and flags as `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py`. Ray is started **without** the dashboard, i.e. the no-`ray[default]` case:

```shell
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0   # sm120: FlashInfer sampler rejects the arch
ray start --head --include-dashboard=False --num-gpus 4 --disable-usage-stats
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-backend ray \
  --enable-expert-parallel --enable-eplb --eplb-config.use_async=false --enable-elastic-ep \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --port 8006
curl -X POST localhost:8006/scale_elastic_ep -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"new_data_parallel_size": 4}'
```

## Test Result

With this change:

```
7 passed in 40.39s
```

Without the `utils.py` change (tests only), 3 of the 4 new tests fail with
`AssertionError: ray.util.state.list_nodes() must not be called ...`; the remaining one is the no-growth early return.

`pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/utils.py tests/v1/engine/test_core_engine_actor_manager.py`: ruff check / ruff format / typos / mypy all pass.

End-to-end, scale 2 -> 4 on the dashboard-less Ray cluster:

Before (0.29.0 as released):
```
ERROR [api_router.py:79] Scale failed: Failed to make request to http://127.0.0.1:8265/api/v0/nodes. Failed to connect to API server. Please check the API server log for details. Make sure dependencies are installed with `pip install ray[default]`.
POST /scale_elastic_ep -> 500 {"error":{"message":"Scale failed", ...}}
```

After (this patch):
```
POST /scale_elastic_ep -> 200 {"message":"Scaled to 4 data parallel engines"}   # 43 s
(Worker_DP2_EP2) [EP Rank 2/4] Expert parallelism is enabled ... Local/global number of experts: 32/128
(Worker_DP3_EP3) [EP Rank 3/4] Expert parallelism is enabled ... Local/global number of experts: 32/128
```
All four GPUs hold an engine afterwards (~40 GB each), completions still return `" Paris."`, and a subsequent scale 4 -> 2 also returns 200.
AI assistance was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests myself.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix DeepSeek V4.1 import without Triton
author: jiangLLM
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57653.

DeepSeek V4.1 fails to import when Triton is unavailable. `sparse_mqa_logits.py` calls `tl.constexpr` at import time, but vLLM's fallback sets it to `None`. This blocks model inspection and causes the MI250 processor tests to fail on main.

Make the placeholder's `constexpr` return its input. This allows modules to define constants without Triton. The real Triton implementation stays unchanged. The existing placeholder tests now cover integer and float values, so no model-specific test or guard is needed.

The error was [reported in #56254](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56254#issuecomment-5644796189). I found no other open PR for this fix.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_triton_utils.py \
  -k 'placeholder or no_triton_fallback' -v --tb=short

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/deepseek-stub-after \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py \
  -k DeepseekV41 -v --tb=short

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/deepseek-stub-processor \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py \
  -k 'DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash' -v --tb=short

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_triton_utils.py \
  -v --tb=short

pre-commit run --files tests/test_triton_utils.py \
  vllm/triton_utils/importing.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py
```

## Test Result

| Tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Placeholder and no-Triton fallback tests | 7 passed |

The two updated placeholder tests fail before the patch and pass after it. The existing DeepSeek tests also pass with the model-specific guard removed. All pre-commit checks passed.

The full Triton utility suite has 9 passes and 2 failures on this CPU wheel. Both failures also occur before this patch: `test_single_gpu_backend_keeps_triton` and `test_cpu_backend_alone_disables_triton`. They concern backend detection; the wheel's CPU version changes that path.

Tested on Linux arm64 with Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu and Transformers 5.16.1. The container uses vLLM v0.29.0 CPU native libraries and this branch's Python source. GPU kernel tests were not run locally.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Dedup transfer regions by (base_addr, block_len)
author: G-haoyu
body:
Fixes #57661

- **Root cause**: NIXL region registration deduped transfer regions by `base_addr` alone, and the collapsed branch only refreshed block geometry for MLA regions. In hybrid-attention models, a layer with a different block length aliasing another layer's base address (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash compressor `state_cache` / indexer `k_cache` overlaid on `swa_cache`) was silently folded and inherited the first region's block length. PD transfers of its state were truncated and misaligned, producing garbled output with no errors.
- **Fix**: dedup key is now `(base_addr, block_len)`. Identical-geometry aliases still fold (`test_overlaid_transfer_groups_share_region_geometry` continues to pass, confirming the lossless path is unchanged).
- **Behavior change (maintainer sanity-check welcome)**: `test_ring_scratch_without_mamba_registers_and_addresses_its_own_regions` now expects `_scratch_region_indices == [2]` instead of `[1]`. That fixture (introduced in #56214) overlays rings on a paged region whose block_len differs from the rings' page size — the old expectation had recorded the benign form of this very bug (the ring inheriting the paged region's geometry). If overlay folding was intentional design, this one assertion is trivially revertible.
- **Tests**: added `test_shared_base_regions_with_distinct_block_lens_stay_separate` (two geometries at one base address — 256B MLA swa page vs 128B compressor ring page — must register as two regions with their own block lens and descriptor geometry). Verified in a container: target test fails on HEAD / passes with the fix; `test_nixl_connector_hma/push_connector/tp_mapping` failure sets are identical before/after. `ruff check` + `ruff format` pass.

**Why this is not a duplicate**: searched open issues/PRs (nixl region dedup, deepseek pd disagg, base_addr, garbled output); #52627 is Mooncake-specific and #54926 is un-transferred draft KV — different root causes.

**Model evals**: 2×8 H200 cluster, NIXL P/D disagg — before: fully garbled output; after: clean English/Chinese generations, 0% garble rate, 6 concurrent streams clean (details in #57661).

**AI assistance disclosure**: root-cause analysis and this fix were produced with ZCode (local agent); cluster diagnosis, the initial mitigation patch, and remote test runs were done with Chaterm (remote agent). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and performed the end-to-end cluster verification above.
