title: [Bugfix][DSA] Avoid runtime JIT for offset candidate end buffers
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

Mixed prefill batches can pass an offset view of the candidate expansion's `end` buffer after warmup used an aligned pointer. Triton specializes on that alignment and JIT-compiles another kernel during serving.

Disable alignment specialization for `end_ptr`: each program stores one scalar, so alignment does not enable vectorized stores. Extend the existing reference tests to cover both aligned and offset output buffers, including strided outputs and untouched padding. Candidate selection, ordering and bounds are unchanged.

Extracted from #57643 at the author's request; the fix and tests are removed from that PR. This targets `main` independently of the all-reduce/mHC changes. Open-PR searches for `end_ptr`, sparse candidate alignment and sparse-indexer warmup found no other PR addressing this specialization; #57206 changes prefill selector dispatch instead.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -k candidate -q -rs
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/sparse_mqa_logits.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

Standalone GB200 GPU test results: **16 passed, 17 deselected** on commit `325d7bf6ad`. Applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

Earlier real-weight validation used this exact patch together with the separate mHC and FlashInfer warmup fixes: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4, no speculative decoding, FlashInfer FP8 attention and MXFP4 sparse indexer. All 23 requests (3–8192 prompt tokens, mixed batches up to eight requests, 736 generated tokens) completed with `--jit-monitor-mode error` and zero runtime JIT events. This is combined warmup coverage, not an isolated end-to-end performance claim. No additional GSM8K evaluation: kernel arithmetic is unchanged and reference tests check exact candidate outputs.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation and this description.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Refresh max tokens for streaming continuations
author: i-m-aditya
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose

Streaming-input sessions reuse the same scheduler `Request` across input
chunks. Although each continuation carries its own `max_tokens` value in
`StreamingUpdate`, `_update_request_as_session` only replaced the sampling
parameters and left `Request.max_tokens` unchanged. The scheduler could
therefore stop a continuation using the preceding chunk's output-token limit.

This change refreshes `Request.max_tokens` when applying a continuation. The
existing scheduler test now changes the limit from 2 to 10 and then from 10 to
4, so it verifies replacement in both directions instead of using the same
value for every chunk.

This is not a duplicate of an open PR. Searches for `streaming max_tokens` and
`StreamingUpdate max_tokens` found no scheduler continuation fix. Related open
work on cumulative session length and truncated frontend output addresses
different behavior.

No documentation update is required because this corrects the existing
per-chunk `SamplingParams` behavior without changing the public API.

Related issue #37842 and PR #37843 identified and proposed the same fix, but both were closed for inactivity without merging. This PR revives the fix against current main with regression coverage for increasing and decreasing per-chunk limits.

AI assistance was used to investigate the bug, update the implementation and
regression test, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line,
ran the tests listed below, and can explain and maintain the change.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_stop_via_update_from_output \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_check_stop_min_tokens \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_check_stop_length_cap_below_min_tokens \
  -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-format --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py

git diff --check
```

Model evaluation is not applicable. The change only corrects scheduler stop
accounting for streaming continuations and does not modify token generation,
sampling, or model execution.

## Test Result

Before the fix, the updated regression test failed after changing a session's
limit from 2 to 10:

```text
assert session.max_tokens == 10
E assert 2 == 10
```

After the fix:

```text
Streaming scheduler tests: 8 passed
Focused scheduler stop tests: 3 passed
Pre-commit hooks: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Accept Anthropic tool_addition and tool_removal content blocks
author: Anurag-M1
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57324.

With tool search on, Claude Code sends `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` blocks in `role: "system"` messages. `/v1/messages` rejected them with a 400, so the client silently retried without them. Accepting and ignoring the blocks is not enough either: tools added this way are declared with `defer_loading: true`, so deferral-aware chat templates (e.g. GLM-5.1) keep hiding them.

This PR resolves the blocks into the tool list the chat template sees, following the [upstream semantics](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages): an added tool is no longer deferred, a removed tool is dropped (until added again), a `tool_definition` is declared, and a reference to an undeclared tool is a 400. The blocks are only accepted in `role: "system"` messages. MCP references are rejected, since there is no MCP connector.

## Test Plan

Live A/B on 1x H200, `main` vs this PR, same args (GLM-4.7-Flash served with GLM-5.1's chat template, which hides `defer_loading` tools; same tool format):

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --max-model-len 32768 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --chat-template glm-5.1-chat_template.jinja
```

Example request (tool added mid-conversation):

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash", "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0,
  "thinking": {"type": "disabled"},
  "tools": [
    {"name": "Bash", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}}},
    {"name": "get_weather", "defer_loading": true,
     "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}}}
  ],
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Paris right now? Use a tool if one is available."},
    {"role": "system", "content": [
      {"type": "text", "text": "The following tools just became available."},
      {"type": "tool_addition", "tool": {"type": "tool_reference", "name": "get_weather"}}
    ]}
  ]}'
```

Plus a real Claude Code 2.1.287 session (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true`, a local MCP weather server) through a logging proxy.

## Test Result

| Request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| deferred tool added by reference (stream and non-stream) | 400 `literal_error ... 'tool_addition'` | 200, `tool_use get_weather {"city": "Paris"}` |
| tool removed via `tool_removal` | 400 | 200, `end_turn`: "I don't have access to a weather tool" |
| tool added by value (`tool_definition`) | 400 | 200, `tool_use db_query` |
| `count_tokens`, addition / removal | 400 | 241 / 184 (186 / 239 without the block) |
| undeclared reference, MCP reference, block in a `user` message | 400 | 400 with a specific message |
| no tool changes (incl. deferred tool never added) | 200 | identical |

title: [Bugfix][V1] Reject encoder-cache hits with mismatched embedding counts
author: jackLei0901
body:
## Purpose

Addresses the engine-containment part of
[#55546](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55546) and is related to
[#55547](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55547). It does not close
#55546 because frontend multimodal processor-cache (P0) fingerprint/content
validation remains follow-up work.

Keep the encoder embedding count with each V1 multimodal encoder-cache entry and
reject a cache hit when the incoming request expects a different count. Complete
only the mismatched request through the scheduler's existing request-error path,
leaving EngineCore available to later requests.

Client-provided multimodal UUIDs must uniquely identify their data, but accidental
reuse can pair a cached encoder output with a request that expects a different
number of embeddings. The existing
[Multimodal Media UUID Security](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/usage/security.md#multimodal-media-uuid-security)
documentation already assigns UUID uniqueness to the client and documents the
integrity and confidentiality consequences of reuse. This PR leaves that
contract and those risks unchanged while closing the availability gap caused by
different embedding counts.

Related work: [#57833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57833) makes
`MultiModalReceiverCache` prefer a full payload resent by P0, preventing one
stale processor-payload substitution path. The harmful mismatch in both PRs
requires a client-provided multimodal UUID to be reused for different content;
without a UUID, the cache identity is derived from the media content. #57833
does not validate an encoder-cache entry already retained under that identifier:
if an earlier request completed and left such an entry, scheduling can still
skip encoding the preserved payload and reuse the old encoder output. This PR
checks the embedding count at that admission point; same-count,
different-content reuse remains outside its scope.

If the cached tensor is shorter, the mismatch currently reaches embedding merge,
EngineCore exits, and every subsequent request on that engine fails. If the cached
tensor is longer, slicing can succeed and silently serve embeddings from different
content. Checking counts at cache admission prevents both availability and silent
correctness failures; catching only the merge exception would not cover the latter.
This intentionally changes the longer-cache case from apparent success with
embeddings from different content to an explicit request error.

The old release path also re-derived cache size from the request being released.
With one identifier and different request sizes, that could corrupt freeable
capacity accounting and lead to later allocation assertions.

This PR keeps the existing UUID contract and cache keys. It rejects the request
rather than evicting or re-encoding under a contested identifier. Once admission
is validated, the stale entry cannot make EngineCore unavailable; evicting it on
a client-triggered mismatch would also let that client flush a shared entry that
other requests may still be using.

The request finishes through `FINISHED_ERROR`, which currently represents a
retryable request-level internal error and maps to HTTP 500, even though this
input will fail again until its UUID is corrected. The scheduler has no separate
client-error finish reason, and client-provided grammar compilation failures
already use the same `grammar_compile_error_reqs` drain. This PR reuses that
existing request-scoped containment path; it does not introduce the 500 mapping.

No flag is added because the change converts an engine-fatal condition into a
request-scoped error while preserving behavior for identifiers whose embedding
counts satisfy the existing contract.

For EC connectors, an external load calls `allocate()`, which records the
requesting request's expected count locally. That value is not derived from the
tensor returned by the remote cache, and the arriving tensor's row count is not
compared with it. A first remote hit is therefore outside this validation;
later reuse of the locally recorded entry is checked.

A mismatch schedules zero tokens, but it does not spin: both engine loops still
reach `update_from_output`, which drains and removes the request within one
scheduler step.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "encoder_cache and embed_count" -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "mamba_align_encoder_cache_cap_makes_progress or \
eagle3_mm_encoder_cache_with_shift or \
free_encoder_inputs_defers_for_eagle_lookahead or \
encoder_cache_retained_across_preemption_and_resume or \
encoder_cache_recomputed_when_evicted_during_preemption" -v
pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
pre-commit run ruff-format --files \
  vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
git diff --check
```

The GPU comparison runs three sequential SmolVLM requests with
`max_num_seqs=1`: seed a short entry, reuse its identifier for a longer input,
then submit a healthy request under another identifier.

## Test Result

- Five new tests: one encoder-cache-manager lifecycle test and four scheduler
  tests. Three existing manager tests also gain eviction/reset/subclass
  assertions.
- Full encoder-cache-manager file: 21 passed.
- Scheduler tests selected by `encoder_cache and embed_count`: 4 passed.
- Five named adjacent scheduler tests: 5 passed.
- Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check`: passed.

The baseline and fixed GPU arms used the same source baseline, SmolVLM model,
Python environment, and compiled artifacts. The HF processor produced 320 image
tokens for the cached input and 1088 for the later input under the same
identifier.

- Baseline: the mismatch reached V2 worker embedding merge; the mismatched request
  and a later healthy request both reported `EngineDeadError`.
- Final fixed revision: the mismatched request completed with
  `finish_reason="error"`, the healthy request completed, and the process status
  was 0.

The fixed `WARNING` identified `collision-id`, reported that its entry held 320
embeddings while the request expected 1088, and explained that a client-provided
multimodal UUID may have been reused for different content. It contained no
`Attempted to assign`, `EngineDeadError`, or `EngineCore failed` line.

The frontend multimodal processor cache (P0, configured by
`mm_processor_cache_gb`) was disabled to construct cache-lifetime drift
deterministically. A P0 hit reuses the old processed item, while production can
retain an encoder entry after the corresponding P0 entry has been evicted.

Model evals are not applicable. The check only runs while admitting an
identifier-based encoder-cache hit and cannot alter outputs for requests whose
identifier and embedding count satisfy the existing contract.

## Changes

- Store `identifier -> num_encoder_embeds` metadata in `EncoderCacheManager`.
- Preserve it while an unreferenced cache entry remains reusable; remove it on
  eviction and reset.
- Use the stored entry count when updating freeable capacity.
- Compare cached and requested counts before cache-hit admission mutates reference
  state.
- Compare counts when one request repeats an identifier in the same scheduling
  call without double-counting the encoder budget.
- Complete mismatched requests as `FINISHED_ERROR` through the scheduler's existing
  request-error drain.
- Warn with the identifier, cached and requested counts, and likely UUID-reuse
  cause.
- Add coverage for lifecycle accounting, compatible layouts, dangling-reference
  prevention, same-request duplicate identifiers, and scheduler liveness afterward.

The check is entirely in the scheduler and `EncoderCacheManager`, so it applies to
both model runners. The GPU reproduction used the V2 Model Runner.

## Duplicate-work check (2026-09-19)

- `gh issue view 55547 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`: #55547 is open.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "55547 in:body"`:
  no open PRs.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "encoder cache multimodal mismatch"`:
  no direct competing implementation was found.

#55549 and #55952 are closed, unmerged prior art. #55583 and #55616 remain open,
but modify processor/rendering and UUID-derivation paths rather than scheduler
encoder-cache admission. #55616 makes reuse more likely by allowing UUIDs to be
derived from URLs, which further motivates validating the cached embedding count.

<details>
<summary>GPU reproduction script</summary>

The short image must run first so its 320-row encoder output is reusable when the
long image requests 1088 rows. The frontend multimodal processor cache is disabled
so each request keeps its own placeholder layout.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate request-level handling of mismatched encoder-cache lengths."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import traceback
from typing import Any

from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoProcessor
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


PROMPT = "<image>\nDescribe the image briefly."


def make_image(width: int, height: int, color: tuple[int, int, int]) -> Image.Image:
    return Image.new("RGB", (width, height), color=color)


def make_request(image: Image.Image, identifier: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    prefix = f"Image dimensions {image.width} by {image.height}. " * 4
    return {
        "prompt": prefix + PROMPT,
        "multi_modal_data": {"image": image},
        "multi_modal_uuids": {"image": [identifier]},
    }


def count_image_tokens(processor: Any, image: Image.Image) -> int:
    processed = processor(text=make_request(image, "unused")["prompt"], images=[image])
    token_ids = processed["input_ids"]
    if hasattr(token_ids, "tolist"):
        token_ids = token_ids.tolist()
    if token_ids and isinstance(token_ids[0], list):
        token_ids = token_ids[0]
    return token_ids.count(processor.image_token_id)


def generate_once(llm: LLM, image: Image.Image, identifier: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        outputs = llm.generate(
            make_request(image, identifier),
            sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0),
        )
        output = outputs[0].outputs[0]
        return {
            "returned": True,
            "finished": outputs[0].finished,
            "finish_reason": output.finish_reason,
        }
    except BaseException as exc:
        traceback.print_exc()
        return {
            "returned": False,
            "exception_type": type(exc).__name__,
            "exception": str(exc)[:500],
        }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    short_image = make_image(1024, 128, (20, 20, 200))
    long_image = make_image(224, 224, (200, 20, 20))
    healthy_image = make_image(672, 224, (20, 200, 20))

    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True)
    short_tokens = count_image_tokens(processor, short_image)
    long_tokens = count_image_tokens(processor, long_image)

    result: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": args.model,
        "processor_cache_disabled": True,
        "prefix_cache_enabled": True,
        "token_counts": {"short": short_tokens, "long": long_tokens},
        "token_count_guard": short_tokens < long_tokens,
    }

    if short_tokens >= long_tokens:
        result["guard_error"] = "short image must produce fewer image tokens"
        with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            json.dump(result, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            handle.write("\n")
        print("SUMMARY_JSON=" + json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
        return 2

    llm = LLM(
        model=args.model,
        enforce_eager=True,
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        mm_processor_cache_gb=0,
        max_model_len=2048,
        max_num_seqs=1,
        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
    )

    result["short_seed"] = generate_once(llm, short_image, "collision-id")
    result["long_reuse"] = generate_once(llm, long_image, "collision-id")
    result["healthy_after"] = generate_once(llm, healthy_image, "healthy-id")

    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
        json.dump(result, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
        handle.write("\n")
    print("SUMMARY_JSON=" + json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))

    return 0 if all(
        step.get("returned", False)
        for step in (
            result["short_seed"],
            result["long_reuse"],
            result["healthy_after"],
        )
    ) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

```bash
python repro_55546_smolvlm.py \
  --model /path/to/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct \
  --output result.json
```

</details>

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Fix MoRI-IO WRITE-mode requests stranded in WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
author: akshayv
body:
## Purpose

In MoRI-IO WRITE (push) mode, decode requests can get stuck in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever when decode is overloaded. The engine stays healthy and keeps serving new requests, so this shows up as a benchmark that never finishes rather than as an error. At 1024 in / 1024 out, 128 requests at concurrency 64, with decode limited to 20 running requests, runs on `main` stall before all requests finish.

This PR fixes two causes. A third cause, decode preemption, is fixed by #53250. This PR used to include the same change, but it has been removed in favour of that PR.

### 1. Prefill gives up on a deferred write without telling decode

In push mode the proxy sends each request to prefill and decode at the same time. Prefill computes the KV cache and then waits for decode to allocate blocks and send their IDs. If decode is busy, the request can wait in decode's queue for longer than `defer_timeout` (60 s). On `main`, prefill then frees its blocks and drops the write, but never tells decode. When decode later admits the request, it waits for KV that will never arrive.

Now, when a deferred write times out:

- Prefill marks the transfer as finished under the lock, so a late block allocation from decode is ignored and no write can start. If the allocation arrived just before the timeout, the write goes ahead as normal.
- Prefill sends `write_failed` to every decode DP rank. Prefill never received the allocation, so it cannot know which rank owns the request. Ranks that do not own it ignore the message, and decode keeps only a bounded number of unmatched failures.
- Prefill then releases its blocks, even if sending a notification failed. This is safe because no write was ever issued.
- Decode reports the request as a failed KV load. It is then failed or recomputed according to `kv_load_failure_policy`. Because no write was issued, decode can free its blocks straight away.

The prefill scheduler no longer has its own WRITE-mode timeout that freed blocks on its own. Only the worker releases them, after the transfer is marked finished.

### 2. A full local prefix-cache hit sent an empty block list

When decode already had the whole prompt in its prefix cache, it sent prefill an empty block list. Prefill rejects that with `MoRIIOError("block_notify_list cannot be empty")` and keeps its blocks. Decode now sends a release message instead, so prefill frees them.

### Related PRs

- #53250 stops a preempted decode request from waiting for a second push. Under the overload above, decode preemption also strands requests, so this PR relies on #53250 to fully fix the hang. With `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`, #53250 is also what lets a failed request recompute locally.
- #58962 adds a receive timeout on decode for when prefill dies mid-transfer. In that case decode cannot know whether a write is still in flight, so it keeps the blocks. The two PRs cover different failures: this one handles a live prefill that never started the write, and #58962 handles a prefill that cannot send anything.

## Test Plan

Unit tests, which need neither ROCm nor the `mori` package:

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_write_done_routing.py
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio*.py
```

End-to-end reproduction in WRITE mode with the `xgmi` backend. Start the proxy first so both engines can register:

```bash
python examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8402
```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --port 8400 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_producer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "xgmi",
      "read_mode": false,
      "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
      "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
      "http_port": "8400",
      "handshake_port": "8600",
      "notify_port": "8500"
    }
  }'
```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --port 8401 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 20 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "xgmi",
      "read_mode": false,
      "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
      "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
      "http_port": "8401",
      "handshake_port": "8601",
      "notify_port": "8501"
    }
  }'
```

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://localhost:8402 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 8088 --ignore-eos
```

`--max-num-seqs 20` makes decode the bottleneck so that some requests wait longer than `defer_timeout`. Add `"kv_load_failure_policy": "recompute"` to the decode config to have timed-out requests recomputed instead of failed.

## Test Result

All 207 MoRI-IO unit tests pass on ROCm with `mori` installed (204 on `main`, plus 3 new). The new tests, in the CPU-only `test_moriio_write_done_routing.py`, cover:

- an expired deferred write: the transfer is marked finished, prefill blocks are released, `write_failed` reaches every decode DP rank across pods, and a late allocation is ignored
- the prefill scheduler waiting for the worker's ACK instead of freeing WRITE blocks on its own timeout
- decode reporting `write_failed` as a failed KV load on the rank that owns the request

End-to-end, using the commands above with #53250 applied (2× Radeon AI Pro R9700S, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), the benchmark finishes and KV cache usage returns to zero on both prefill and decode:

| decode `kv_load_failure_policy` | Successful | Failed | Deferred writes timed out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fail` (default) | 109 | 19 | 19 |
| `recompute` | 128 | 0 | 34 |

title: [Bugfix] Fix generative scoring body cancellation
author: taneem-ibrahim
body:
## Purpose

Competing request-body consumers can hang `/generative_scoring`.  With this PR, `FastAPI` now parses the body before cancellation and load tracking begin to eliminate the hang condition, as it does for other typed-body endpoints. The serving and scoring paths are unchanged.

## Reproducer

A full-ASGI reproducer sends valid JSON in two `http.request` frames, yields control after the first frame, and records every `receive()` caller. This deterministically allows the endpoint body reader and disconnect listener to compete for the stream.

Save the following file as `/tmp/repro_generative_scoring_body_race.py`.

```python
import asyncio
import json

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from vllm.entrypoints.generate.generative_scoring.api_router import router
from vllm.entrypoints.generate.generative_scoring.serving import (
    GenerativeScoringRequest,
    GenerativeScoringResponse,
)
from vllm.entrypoints.serve.engine.protocol import UsageInfo
from vllm.entrypoints.serve.utils.api_utils import (
    load_aware_call,
    with_cancellation,
)


class Handler:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls = 0

    async def create_generative_scoring(self, request, raw_request):
        self.calls += 1
        return GenerativeScoringResponse(
            model="model",
            data=[],
            usage=UsageInfo(prompt_tokens=0, total_tokens=0),
        )


app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(router)
app.state.serving_generative_scoring = Handler()
app.state.enable_server_load_tracking = False


@app.post("/fixed")
@with_cancellation
@load_aware_call
async def fixed(
    request: GenerativeScoringRequest,
    raw_request: Request,
):
    return JSONResponse({"query": request.query})


async def invoke(path: str) -> None:
    queue: asyncio.Queue[dict] = asyncio.Queue()
    sent: list[dict] = []
    receivers: list[str] = []

    async def receive() -> dict:
        task = asyncio.current_task()
        assert task is not None
        receivers.append(task.get_coro().__qualname__)
        return await queue.get()

    async def send(message: dict) -> None:
        sent.append(message)

    scope = {
        "type": "http",
        "asgi": {"version": "3.0"},
        "http_version": "1.1",
        "method": "POST",
        "scheme": "http",
        "path": path,
        "raw_path": path.encode(),
        "query_string": b"",
        "headers": [(b"content-type", b"application/json")],
        "client": ("127.0.0.1", 12345),
        "server": ("127.0.0.1", 8000),
        "app": app,
    }

    payload = json.dumps(
        {
            "query": "q",
            "items": ["i"],
            "label_token_ids": [1],
        }
    ).encode()
    midpoint = len(payload) // 2

    app_task = asyncio.create_task(app(scope, receive, send))

    # Let the endpoint and disconnect-listener tasks start before delivering
    # the fragmented request body.
    for _ in range(3):
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

    await queue.put(
        {
            "type": "http.request",
            "body": payload[:midpoint],
            "more_body": True,
        }
    )
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    await queue.put(
        {
            "type": "http.request",
            "body": payload[midpoint:],
            "more_body": False,
        }
    )

    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(app_task), timeout=0.05)
        outcome = "completed"
    except TimeoutError:
        outcome = "hung_after_complete_body"

    statuses = [
        message["status"]
        for message in sent
        if message["type"] == "http.response.start"
    ]

    print(
        f"{path}: outcome={outcome} statuses={statuses} "
        f"handler_calls={app.state.serving_generative_scoring.calls}"
    )
    print(f"{path}: receive_consumers={receivers}")

    app_task.cancel()
    await asyncio.gather(app_task, return_exceptions=True)


async def main() -> None:
    await invoke("/generative_scoring")
    await invoke("/fixed")


asyncio.run(main())

```

Run it as:

```bash
.venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_generative_scoring_body_race.py
```

### Output on main

```text
/generative_scoring: outcome=hung_after_complete_body statuses=[] handler_calls=0
/generative_scoring: receive_consumers=['create_generative_scoring', 'listen_for_disconnect', 'create_generative_scoring', 'listen_for_disconnect']
```

### Output on this branch

```text
/generative_scoring: outcome=completed statuses=[200] handler_calls=1
/generative_scoring: receive_consumers=['FastAPI.__call__', 'FastAPI.__call__', 'listen_for_disconnect']
```

## Test Plan

```text
.venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_generative_scoring_body_race_full.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/test_generative_scoring.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/test_generative_scoring_e2e.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/api_router.py
```

Results:

- deterministic ASGI reproducer: main hangs; branch returns 200 and calls the handler
- unit suite: 10 passed
- H100 endpoint E2E: 6 passed

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) assisted with root-cause analysis, the patch, and test execution.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Guard record_transfer against None telemetry
author: ntheanh201
body:
> Supersedes #57403, which was closed because its head picked up merge commits from an updated `main` (354 files, diff unreadable). This PR carries the same single-commit fix (patch-id `c182a17c19c1538a7e4fe2fb84217732e7ae2371`), rebased onto current `main`. cc @NickLucche

### Problem
Some NIXL backends do not capture transfer telemetry by default (UCX without `NIXL_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=1`, and OBJ in some configs). For these, `get_xfer_telemetry()` returns `None` instead of a `nixlXferTelemetry` struct.

`NixlBaseConnectorWorker._pop_done_transfers()` in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py` passes that result straight to `self.xfer_stats.record_transfer(res)`. When `res is None`, the call raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'xferDuration'`. The surrounding `try/except Exception` catches it and treats it as a transfer failure (`transfer_exception`): the blocks are invalidated and downstream workers report the request as failed. With Dynamo P/D disaggregation, the frontend then returns HTTP 500 to the client.

The bug does not depend on any one backend. It triggers whenever a backend reports `xfer_state == "DONE"` but cannot fill in telemetry.

### Reproduction
Deploy DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with P/D disaggregation on NVIDIA H200 using the NIXL UCX backend. `NixlBaseConnectorWorker` calls `get_xfer_telemetry()` for each DONE handle, and the UCX plugin returns `None` because it allocates no telemetry buffer by default. `record_transfer(None)` then raises `AttributeError`, the request is marked failed, and Dynamo returns HTTP 500. Stack trace excerpt from a production deploy (2026-09-17):

```
ERROR vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.base_worker:_pop_done_transfers:3031
Marking blocks as invalid
transfer_exception
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'xferDuration'
```

This error is logged on every KV transfer completion, so the log noise alone makes it a production problem.

### Fix
Make `NixlKVConnectorStats.record_transfer()` (`nixl/stats.py`) accept `None` and skip recording when the backend returned no telemetry:

```python
def record_transfer(self, res: "nixlXferTelemetry | None"):
    # Keep metrics units consistent with rest of the code: time us->s
    if res is None:
        return
    ...
```

The guard sits inside `record_transfer()` rather than at the call site, so every caller is covered, including future ones. Nothing changes for backends that do return telemetry. For backends that don't, that transfer simply isn't recorded in the metrics. That's better than marking a successful transfer as failed.

### Related
- #55576 (open) handles a sibling case: the OBJ tier explicitly enabling telemetry. This fix complements it. Even with telemetry fully enabled, the `None` guard stops future backends from hitting the same crash.
- #35876 (open) reworks throughput computation, which is a different metric path.

### Test plan
- [ ] Run the existing unit tests under `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/`.
- [ ] Add a regression test that mocks `get_xfer_telemetry` to return `None` and checks that the transfer is released cleanly without raising.

### Diff

```diff
-    def record_transfer(self, res: "nixlXferTelemetry"):
+    def record_transfer(self, res: "nixlXferTelemetry | None"):
         # Keep metrics units consistent with rest of the code: time us->s
+        if res is None:
+            return
         self.data["transfer_duration"].append(res.xferDuration / 1e6)
         self.data["post_duration"].append(res.postDuration / 1e6)
         self.data["bytes_transferred"].append(res.totalBytes)
```

title: [Bugfix] Accept EOS after grammar finish in outlines backend; reject json_object at validation
author: SIDDARTHAREDDY8
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57723 — with the `outlines` structured-output backend, every `choice` / `regex` / `json` request that completes returns HTTP 500.

Root cause: once the `outlines_core` guide reaches an accept state, `Guide.accepts_tokens()` rejects *every* token — including the EOS that the guide's own bitmask still allows through. The sampler therefore emits EOS right after the match completes, and `OutlinesGrammar.accept_tokens([eos])` returns `False`. The scheduler interprets that as a grammar rejection and fails the request with a 500 (`"Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens ... Terminating request."`).

The fix: in `OutlinesGrammar.accept_tokens()`, when the guide is already finished, accept the tokens without advancing — mirroring the `xgrammar` backend (`if self._is_terminated: return True`) and the `guidance` backend (`if self.ll_matcher.is_stopped(): return True`), which both accept tokens after termination.

Also fixes the related issue from the same report: `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}` with `backend="outlines"` passed request validation and then threw a 500 from `compile_grammar()` (`ValueError: Invalid request type for Outlines backend`). It is now rejected at validation time with a `VLLMValidationError`, so the request fails fast with a 400.

## Test Plan

CPU-only regression harness driving `OutlinesGrammar` directly against the pinned `outlines_core==0.2.14` with a tiny synthetic vocabulary (`0->"yes"`, `1->"no"`, EOS id `2`) and regex `(yes|no)`:

1. Accept `[yes]` → `True`, guide finished; bitmask allows only EOS (bit 2 set).
2. `accept_tokens([eos])` after finish → `True` (was `False` before the fix), `num_processed_tokens` unchanged (no advance), still finished.
3. Pre-finish rejection preserved: fresh grammar rejects `[eos]` (not in `(yes|no)`), then still accepts `[no]` normally.
4. `reset()` after finish restores the grammar.
5. `validate_structured_output_request_outlines` raises `VLLMValidationError` for `json_object=True`; `regex`/`choice`/`json` still pass.

## Test Result

```
PASS: eos accepted after finish, no advance
PASS: pre-finish rejection preserved
PASS: reset works after finish
PASS: json_object -> VLLMValidationError (Outlines structured outputs backend does not support json_object specifications)
PASS: regex/choice/json still pass outlines validation
ALL GREEN
```

Also verified the negative: on the unpatched code the same harness prints `accept_tokens([eos]) on ORIGINAL code: False`, reproducing the reported bug.

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched file: no new findings (2 pre-existing import-sort notices also present on the unpatched file with this ruff version).

title: [Bugfix] Fix Whisper engine crash on audio clips longer than 30s
author: twu3202
body:
## Purpose

Offline `LLM.generate` with Whisper and an audio clip longer than 30 s kills the engine on main and on v0.29.0:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1750) must match the size of tensor b (1500) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

Every later request then fails with `EngineDeadError`. v0.26.0 accepts the same input and truncates the clip to 30 s, which is what the HF feature extractor does by default.

The cause is the same as in #56912 (Qwen2-Audio). Since #53275 the multimodal processor passes `truncation=False` to the HF processor so that the placeholder text is not cut. `WhisperProcessor` forwards the same kwarg to `WhisperFeatureExtractor`, which then stops truncating audio to its 30 s window. A 35 s clip becomes 3500 frames, which is 1750 positions after the conv, and the encoder has 1500.

The fix is the same line as in #56912: `WhisperMultiModalProcessor._get_hf_mm_inputs` passes `truncation=True`. Clips of up to 30 s are processed exactly as before.

`/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations` are not affected, because the server splits audio into chunks of at most 30 s before it reaches the processor, and Whisper does not serve the other endpoints. Only offline use with a longer clip hits this.

I did not find an existing issue or PR for this (searched for whisper truncation, whisper 30s, and the error message). Of the other audio models I could load, GLM-ASR and Qwen3-ASR handle long clips correctly and Qwen2-Audio is already fixed. I have not checked the rest.

Repro:

```python
import numpy as np
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

sr = 16000
t = np.arange(sr * 35) / sr  # 35 s, longer than Whisper's 30 s window
audio = (0.1 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 440 * t)).astype(np.float32)

llm = LLM("openai/whisper-small", max_model_len=448, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 1})
out = llm.generate(
    {
        "prompt": "<|startoftranscript|><|en|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>",
        "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio, sr)},
    },
    SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=50),
)
print(out[0].outputs[0].text)
```

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_whisper.py
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k whisper
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py -k whisper
```

The new test runs the processor on 5 s, 30 s and 35 s clips and checks that `input_features` always has the feature extractor's 3000 frames. It needs no GPU.

End to end on one RTX 6000 Ada: the repro above, and a second script that sends 25 s, 35 s, 65 s and 25 s clips of real speech (FLEURS `cmn_hans_cn`, concatenated) to one `LLM` in that order, with `temperature=0`.

I did not run `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py`. It asks for `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9` and my GPU is shared.

## Test Result

New test at e378275a8:

| | 5 s | 30 s | 35 s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | pass | pass | fail, `assert 3500 == 3000` |
| this PR | pass | pass | pass |

`test_common.py -k whisper`: 6 passed. `test_tensor_schema.py -k whisper`: 2 passed.

Repro: v0.29.0 and main (e378275a8) die with the error above, this PR prints a transcript.

Real speech, `openai/whisper-small`:

| | 25 s | 35 s | 65 s | 25 s again |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v0.26.0 | ok | ok | ok | ok |
| v0.29.0 | ok | `EngineDeadError` | `EngineDeadError` | `EngineDeadError` |
| main (e378275a8) | ok | `EngineDeadError` | `EngineDeadError` | `EngineDeadError` |
| this PR | ok | ok | ok | ok |

With this PR every transcript is identical to the v0.26.0 one, and the 35 s and 65 s transcripts are identical to each other, as expected when both are cut to the first 30 s. `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` with this PR also returns all four.

title: [XPU]Fix the accuracy issue when meet topk_ids=-1 on DP+EP scenarios
author: yisustc
body:
When running MoE models with DP + EP, dummy/padded tokens are marked with topk_ids = -1 (e.g. from dummy batches executed by an idle DP rank). Under EP, the dispatch all-gathers these -1 entries to every rank's fused MoE kernel.
The XPU MoE kernel uses topk_ids directly as indices, so -1 causes an out-of-bounds read (undefined behavior). This corrupts not only the dummy rows but also real tokens' outputs, producing nondeterministic results and occasional NaN, which then spreads to all ranks through the EP combine.
The error found in the UT v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py::test_external_lb_completion_streaming[api-1-ep-enabled-ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b] can be seen below:
        # Check that the combined text matches the non-streamed version.
>       assert "".join(chunks) == single_output, (
            "Streamed output should match non-streamed output."
        )
E       AssertionError: Streamed output should match non-streamed output.
E       assert ' (-RelatedRelated BR' == ' Share ( JavaScript CloseAn'
E
E         -  Share ( JavaScript CloseAn
E         +  (-RelatedRelated BR

The same judgement also occurs on other platforms like DeepEP HT
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_ht.py#L225
to avoid lead topk_ids=-1 to do the calculation.

title: [Bugfix][RL] Load attention sinks through weight_loader for layerwise reload
author: Ronald1995
body:
## Overview

Attention sink writes bypassed parameter `weight_loader` callbacks, leaving stale sink values after layerwise reload during RL weight updates. Register checkpoint-backed sinks with a common TP loader and factory, and route model loading through the registered callbacks.

This consolidates and supersedes #57798, #57801, #57803, #57804, #57805, and #57806.

## Claims

- DeepSeek V4/V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2 (including MTP and Omni MTP), GPT-OSS, Laguna, and Qwen3-DFlash load sinks through their current parameter loader; GPT-OSS preserves MXFP4, Quark and other quantization dispatch.
- The loader partitions global checkpoint heads once, writes the local shard in place, and restores padded heads to `-inf`. The factory initializes sinks to `-inf` and registers the loader.
- Regression coverage checks changed sink values across two layerwise reloads, TP sharding, padding, storage preservation, quantization dispatch and pipeline-stage skips.

## Validation

### Current review revision: `7964a96f87`

Merged upstream `main` at `61d9c777bf` before committing the review fixes. Local Windows / Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu:

- Isolated CPU regression run: **35 passed, 1 skipped** (CUDA case). Runs the exact repository sink test functions with real PyTorch, unchanged production reload modules, and production model loading methods/helpers extracted from source. It bypasses unrelated vLLM startup imports and model constructors, with stand-ins for unrelated configuration/attention/quantization infrastructure. This is isolated verification, not a standard-suite or full-model run.
- The six new DeepSeek V4/V4.1 and HY-V4 dispatch cases (TP ranks 0/1) detect an in-memory mutation that loads correct sink values while bypassing the parameter's current loader. Mutation harnesses remain outside the PR.
- Ruff checks/format, `git diff --check`, SPDX, forbidden-import and test-tethering checks passed.
- Standard `pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k sink -q` remains blocked during startup by missing `uvloop` on Windows. Full pre-commit could not initialize its environments because the configured local proxy is unreachable; commit hooks were bypassed for this revision after the checks above.
- No remote H20, GPU or full-model validation was performed for this review revision.

<details>
<summary>Historical H20 validation before this review revision</summary>

### Previous revision

Environment: H20 Slurm cluster, node `vllm-h20-02`, 2 x NVIDIA H20-3e, driver 580.105.08; Python 3.12.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130. Compiled extensions come from the per-commit precompiled cu130 wheel built for this PR's base commit (`vllm-0.31.1rc1.dev295+gd4e92ccc3`) with the branch's Python files overlaid, so Python and extensions are from the same commit without a rebuild.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k sink -q` | **41 passed** (GPU node) |
| full `test_weight_utils.py` + `test_reload.py`, this branch | 18 failed, **110 passed**, 14 skipped, 2 xfailed, 7 errors |
| full same two files at upstream `main` (control) | 18 failed, 70 passed, 13 skipped, 2 xfailed, 7 errors |
| failure-name diff, main -> branch | **identical set** (25 names); every additional pass is a sink test |
| `run-precommit.sh` (every hook the diff touches) | exit 0, no file rewritten |
| DCO over the branch range | all commits signed off, `DCO pass` |

The failures are model-download / multi-GPU cases that fail identically before and after the change, so they carry no signal about this PR.

Additional out-of-tree verification (harness deliberately kept outside the PR, results in the review comments): each sink model's real attention module was built from tiny dimensions with dummy weights on H20, for TP=1 and TP=2, and driven through the real layerwise reload lifecycle, asserting the per-rank slice, the `-inf` padding and the preserved kernel storage; the pre-PR loading shape was reproduced as a control and never received the reloaded sinks.

These results were recorded before the current review changes and are not a rerun of the current head.

</details>

## Details

A dedicated sink loader derives shard length from the checkpoint rather than the runtime parameter: DeepSeek pads its runtime sink, so `sharded_weight_loader(0)` would use the wrong shard length. Unpadded sinks use the same loader without reconstructing storage. Checkpoint heads must divide evenly across TP ranks.

The loader keeps the divisibility check and relies on tensor slicing and the default loader for incompatible shapes. Empty checkpoints are no longer explicitly rejected. Lifecycle rationale stays here rather than in long helper docstrings.

Tests in the existing CI-selected `test_reload.py` and `test_weight_utils.py` suites cover actual model dispatch for MiMo MTP/Omni MTP, Laguna, DFlash, GPT-OSS, DeepSeek V4/V4.1 and HY-V4. The DeepSeek/HY-V4 tests replace the current loader and verify the unsliced global checkpoint reaches it exactly once for each load. AST factory-name scanning and redundant empty/padding tests were removed.

No full-model accuracy evaluation, real-checkpoint end-to-end reload, TP>2 or multi-node run was performed. Pipeline parallelism is covered by the skip-path test. Backend-converted sink copies and GPT-OSS expert reload follow-ups are outside this PR; their behavior is unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Reset SimpleCPU eager-store placement state on MRV2 resume
author: kamb-code
body:
## Purpose

SimpleCPU eager offload retains each request's accumulated GPU block table and
per-group store cursors. Under MRV2, preemption is reported through
`SchedulerOutput.preempted_req_ids`, while the resumed request is represented
as complete `NewRequestData`. Its `yield_req_data` entry is not marked
preempted, so the eager-store state appends the replacement table to the freed
placement and keeps its old cursors. In the regression, the resumed
three-block request therefore schedules no newly confirmed tail block for
offload instead of scheduling the third block.

When preemption is observed, immediately clear the retained block table and
reset every group cursor before processing any placement data from that
scheduler output. MRV1 resumed-cached requests and MRV2 `NewRequestData` then
consume their complete replacement tables through the same reset site.

The change is confined to eager SimpleCPU store bookkeeping. It does not alter
lazy mode, cache lookup, or eviction policy.

#47234 documents current below-cursor CPU-cache eviction behavior, while
#47235 proposes cursor re-scans for that case. This change is narrower: it
restores the existing preemption reset for MRV2's `NewRequestData`
representation and does not change eviction tracking. #57325 touches the
same files but contains no equivalent reset. #55033 also touches the
manager and scheduler tests for non-prefix-cacheable QSA/lazy sizing, but does
not reset retained placement after MRV2 preemption. #57505 guards
hashless sources at store completion; it is downstream of placement tracking
and contains no preemption reset.

implementation, testing, and drafting. I reviewed the final diff and the test

The reviewer-requested simplification removes the deferred reset marker and

title: [Bugfix] Fix stalled local-only Elastic EP scale-up
author: taneem-ibrahim
body:
## Purpose

When an Elastic EP deployment already has remote engines and scale-up adds only local engines, the new remote-engine count is zero. Slicing remote_engine_actors[-0:] selects every existing remote actor, so scale-up calls wait_for_init() on actors already executing their long-running run() method. Those calls can remain queued and block scale-up.

Example topology: start with one local engine and one remote engine, then scale from DP=2 to DP=3 by adding one local engine using spare capacity on the head node.

Scale-up now collects actors as they are created, so initialization and startup touch only engines added by this scale-up.

An open-PR search for Elastic EP scale-up actor fixes found no other PR addressing this bug.

## Reproducer

CPU-only reproducer using real Ray actors and the production scale-up method. Simulates adding one local engine to an existing local + remote pair on one node; model initialization is stubbed. Main blocks until the existing remote actor’s run loop is released; the branch completes while it remains running.

<summary>Save as /tmp/repro_elastic_scaleup_ray.py</summary>

```python
import argparse
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch


def wait_for_file(path: Path, timeout: float = 60) -> None:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while not path.exists():
        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            raise TimeoutError(f"Actor did not reach {path.name}")
        time.sleep(0.05)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, default=Path.cwd())
    parser.add_argument("--expect", choices=("hang", "complete"), required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    repo = args.repo.resolve()
    sys.path.insert(0, str(repo))

    import ray
    from ray.util.placement_group import placement_group, remove_placement_group

    import vllm.v1.engine.core as core
    from vllm.v1.engine.utils import CoreEngineActorManager

    class CPUActor(core.EngineCoreActorMixin):
        def __init__(self, addresses, dp_rank=0, **kwargs):
            self.directory = Path(addresses)
            self.rank = dp_rank
            (self.directory / f"initialized-{self.rank}").touch()

        def run_busy_loop(self):
            (self.directory / f"running-{self.rank}").touch()
            while not (self.directory / f"release-{self.rank}").exists():
                time.sleep(0.05)

        def shutdown(self):
            pass

    revision = subprocess.check_output(
        ["git", "-C", str(repo), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True
    ).strip()
    source = Path(CoreEngineActorManager.scale_up_elastic_ep.__code__.co_filename)
    assert source.resolve() == repo / "vllm/v1/engine/utils.py", source
    print(f"revision={revision}", flush=True)
    print(f"ray_version={ray.__version__}", flush=True)
    print("topology=1 local + 1 remote; add 1 local", flush=True)

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ep-ray-") as temporary:
        directory = Path(temporary)
        actors = []
        pg = None
        finished = threading.Event()
        errors = []
        manager = None
        thread = None
        ray.init(
            address="local",
            num_cpus=4,
            num_gpus=0,
            object_store_memory=100 * 1024 * 1024,
            include_dashboard=False,
            log_to_driver=False,
            _node_ip_address="127.0.0.1",
            _temp_dir=str(directory / "ray"),
            runtime_env={"env_vars": {"PYTHONPATH": str(repo)}},
        )
        try:
            actor_type = ray.remote(CPUActor)
            actors = [
                actor_type.remote(addresses=temporary, dp_rank=rank) for rank in (0, 1)
            ]
            ray.get([actor.wait_for_init.remote() for actor in actors], timeout=60)
            initial_runs = [actor.run.remote() for actor in actors]
            for rank in (0, 1):
                wait_for_file(directory / f"running-{rank}")

            master_ip = ray.util.get_node_ip_address()
            pg = placement_group(
                [{f"node:{master_ip}": 0.001}, {"CPU": 1}],
                strategy="STRICT_PACK",
            )
            ray.get(pg.ready(), timeout=60)

            manager = CoreEngineActorManager.__new__(CoreEngineActorManager)
            manager.local_engine_actors = [actors[0]]
            manager.remote_engine_actors = [actors[1]]
            manager.created_placement_groups = []
            manager.placement_group_is_local = [True, False]
            manager.env_vars_dict = {"PYTHONPATH": str(repo)}
            manager.addresses = temporary
            manager.executor_class = object
            manager.log_stats = False
            manager.run_refs = list(initial_runs)
            manager.actor_run_ref_dict = dict(zip(actors, initial_runs))
            manager.add_dp_placement_groups = lambda *_: ([pg], [1])
            config = SimpleNamespace(
                instance_id="elastic-ep-repro",
                kv_transfer_config=None,
                model_config=SimpleNamespace(is_moe=True),
                parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(
                    data_parallel_size=2,
                    data_parallel_size_local=1,
                    data_parallel_master_ip=master_ip,
                    world_size=1,
                    eplb_config=SimpleNamespace(num_redundant_experts=0),
                ),
            )

            def scale_up():
                try:
                    manager.scale_up_elastic_ep(config, 3, 0)
                except BaseException as error:
                    errors.append(error)
                finally:
                    finished.set()

            with patch.object(core, "DPMoEEngineCoreActor", CPUActor):
                thread = threading.Thread(target=scale_up, daemon=True)
                thread.start()
                wait_for_file(directory / "initialized-2")
                # Exclude actor creation time from the hang observation window.
                completed = finished.wait(timeout=10)
                if errors:
                    raise errors[0]
                print("new_local_actor_initialized=True", flush=True)
                print(f"scale_up_completed_while_remote_busy={completed}", flush=True)
                assert completed == (args.expect == "complete")
                if not completed:
                    # Releasing only the old remote run unblocks its queued init.
                    (directory / "release-1").touch()
                    assert finished.wait(timeout=30), "Still blocked after release"
                    if errors:
                        raise errors[0]
                    print("scale_up_completed_after_remote_release=True", flush=True)

            added_refs = len(manager.run_refs) - len(initial_runs)
            replaced = manager.actor_run_ref_dict[actors[1]] != initial_runs[1]
            print(f"new_run_refs={added_refs}", flush=True)
            print(f"existing_remote_run_ref_replaced={replaced}", flush=True)
            assert added_refs == (2 if args.expect == "hang" else 1)
            assert replaced == (args.expect == "hang")
            wait_for_file(directory / "running-2")
            print("RESULT=PASS", flush=True)
        finally:
            for rank in (0, 1, 2):
                (directory / f"release-{rank}").touch()
            if thread is not None:
                thread.join(timeout=10)
            if manager is not None:
                actors = manager.local_engine_actors + manager.remote_engine_actors
            for actor in actors:
                ray.kill(actor, no_restart=True)
            if pg is not None:
                remove_placement_group(pg)
            ray.shutdown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL", "ERROR")
    main()
```

</details>

Run with the same installed development environment against the two checkouts
(replace the checkout paths):

```bash

.venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_elastic_scaleup_ray.py --repo /path/to/pr-57820 --expect complete
```


title: [Bugfix][MoE] Respect padded row strides in top-k routing
author: Id545
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #56900.

Inductor can produce router logits with padded physical rows, for example shape
`[M, 60]` and stride `(64, 1)`. The native MoE top-k path used
`blockIdx.x * num_experts` to locate each input row, so it read the wrong logits
whenever the physical row stride differed from `num_experts`. This silently
changed expert routing under compilation.

This change:

- propagates `gating_output.stride(0)` to the native top-k launcher;
- uses the existing unfused softmax/sigmoid plus top-k path for padded rows;
- allocates the required workspace for padded power-of-two expert counts;
- keeps packed rows on the existing specialized path; and
- adds regression coverage for softmax and sigmoid with 60/64 and 64/72
  logical/physical row widths.

The input-row offset is `int64_t` because PyTorch tensor strides are 64-bit;
this also avoids 32-bit wraparound in the input address calculation. Open PR
[#53131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53131) independently widens
packed-row pointer arithmetic more broadly, but it does not propagate
`stride(0)` or handle padded rows. The two changes overlap only on the
input-offset width; this PR addresses the separate functional stride bug.

No open PR referencing #56900 or implementing padded-row support for this
kernel was found before submission.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx pre-commit run --files \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py \
  -k padded_row_stride

EXPECTED_VLLM="$(.venv/bin/python -c 'import vllm; print(vllm.__version__)')"
.venv/bin/python \
  /workspace/fp-atomics-census/probes/diagnostics/moe_compile/moe_compile_reproducer.py \
  --output-dir /workspace/results-56900/patched-e2e \
  --runners v2 \
  --compiles on off \
  --graphs off \
  --expected-vllm "$EXPECTED_VLLM"
```

The same focused cases were also run with a standalone kernel reproducer before
and after rebuilding vLLM from source. The end-to-end command uses the
[issue reproducer](https://github.com/catmcgee/fp-atomics-census/blob/2137e7b6347c0027fc48e5cd66b1f7d86e5ad2e4/probes/diagnostics/moe_compile/moe_compile_reproducer.py).
Each end-to-end arm ran in a fresh process with separate vLLM, Inductor, and

## Test Result

| Focused padded-stride pytest | not applicable | 4 passed |

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Handle leading missing packed groups
author: gc-fu
body:
## Purpose

Fix packed LoRA expansion when a multi-slice packed projection has a missing
leading member.

Qwen3.5 maps the two adapter-visible modules `in_proj_qkv` and `in_proj_z`
onto the four output slices Q, K, V, and Z. A valid PEFT adapter that targets
only `in_proj_z` is loaded as `[None, z_lora]`. The current implementation
assumes that a missing member covers every remaining output slice, so the
leading `None` consumes Q/K/V/Z and the subsequent Z tensor cannot be placed.

This is the converse of the trailing-`None` case fixed by #47640.

## Fix

A missing member's row count is unknown, so its coverage is inferred from the
present groups around it: groups before the first `None` are aligned from the
front, groups after the last `None` are aligned from the back, and the `None`
groups in between take the remaining slices (left at base weights).

Existing trailing-`None` and all-`None` behavior is preserved. Present B tensors
whose row counts don't match the output sizes, or present groups sandwiched
between missing ones, fail explicitly instead of silently misaligning weights.

## Reproduction

A real on-disk PEFT adapter was created for `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` with only the
first GDN layer's `in_proj_z` targeted. Its files were a standard
`adapter_config.json` and `adapter_model.safetensors`, with rank 8 tensors:

```text
in_proj_z.lora_A.weight: [8, 1024]
in_proj_z.lora_B.weight: [2048, 8]
```

On the unmodified base commit, the first LoRA request terminates EngineCore:

```text
ValueError: Cannot determine how to split lora_b with 2048 rows into 4
slices with output sizes [2048, 2048, 2048, 2048] starting from index 4.
```

With this change, the same model, adapter, and request load successfully and
complete generation on Intel XPU.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py \
  -k 'column_parallel_packed or expand_packed_lora_with_missing_group' -q
python -m pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py -q
pre-commit run
```

The regression test covers `[valid, valid]`, `[valid, None]`,
`[None, valid]`, and `[None, None]`, and verifies the actual contents of every stacked A/B buffer.

## Test Result

- Focused packed-layer tests: 40 passed, 36 skipped.
- LoRA layer and manager suites: 248 passed, 182 skipped.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks: passed.
- Real Qwen3.5 disk PEFT adapter: failed before the fix with the error above;
  loaded and generated successfully after the fix.
- A full `pre-commit run --all-files` additionally exposed an unrelated
  container-specific failure in `test-nonroot-entrypoint` case 3; all other
  hooks passed and its generated requirements change was not retained.

## Duplicate-work check

Checked current open PRs/issues around expand_packed_lora and partial
Qwen3.5 GDN LoRA. #47640 only handles the trailing-missing case and does
not address an adapter targeting only in_proj_z.


AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change. I
reviewed the resulting diff and validation evidence.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Reject unsupported EP for monolithic AITER MXFP4 MoE
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Reject `use_ep=True` for the monolithic AITER MXFP4 W4A16 and static-FP8 W4A8 backends.
- Check expert sharding directly: `use_all2all_kernels=False` does not imply that all experts are local.
- Preserve supported tensor parallel configurations and the existing data parallel and EPLB restrictions.
- Add four capability-selection cases covering both backends with and without expert parallelism.

This issue surfaced while reproducing the [CI 90039 speculative-decoding group](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90039/list?sid=01a0bd6c-73d2-48d6-82a3-1e021270e178&tab=output) locally on MI300. [#50622](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50622) split the CK and Triton W4A16 backends and made the unsafe selection reachable on gfx942; a source-predicate bisect identified that change, rather than a GPU numerical bisect. With TP4 and expert parallelism enabled, the runtime observer measured 256 global routing experts but only 64 local weight experts, and the W4A16 kernel faulted after indexing those local weights with global expert IDs. Both current monolithic implementations ignore the expert map, so they must reject expert parallelism until that contract is implemented.

Related work: [#53261](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53261) fixes token-row metadata in native modular AITER, while [#45711](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45711) introduces a new MXFP8 backend. Neither implements this EP exclusion for the two existing monolithic backends.

Investigation, implementation, validation, and this description were AI-assisted.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Reject hash routing for unsupported monolithic backends
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Add a per-layer `has_hash_routing` field to `FusedMoEConfig`, defaulting to false.
- Populate it from the hash table supplied to `FusedMoEFactory`.
- Reject hash-routed layers in the common capability check for all current monolithic backends, whose interface does not carry token IDs or hash tables.
- Preserve modular hash routing and ordinary non-hash monolithic selection.
- Add six factory-to-oracle cases covering monolithic AITER, native modular AITER, and modular Triton with and without hash routing.

This issue was uncovered during local MI300 reproduction of the [CI 90039 speculative-decoding group](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90039/list?sid=01a0bd6c-73d2-48d6-82a3-1e021270e178&tab=output). The A16 DeepSeek V4 capability added in [#46516](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46516) already lacked a hash-input path, and [#50622](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50622) later made that backend available on gfx942. Modular execution selects experts using token IDs and the hash table, but current monolithic execution bypasses that router and drops the required inputs. Recording the layer requirement before backend selection prevents an otherwise eligible monolithic backend from silently using a different routing algorithm. 

Related work: [#45711](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45711) extends the monolithic interface and implements hash routing for a new AITER MXFP8 backend. This standalone change contains none of that implementation and intentionally rejects every monolithic backend under the current interface. If that extension lands, this blanket check must be revisited to admit explicitly implemented hash capability while continuing to reject unsupported backends. [#50844](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50844) bounds token IDs in a hash-routing kernel; it addresses input validation rather than backend eligibility.

Investigation, implementation, validation, and this description were AI-assisted.

title: [Bugfix][DSV4.1] Restrict mHC overlap to full CUDA graphs
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Problem and fix

DSV4.1's small-batch eager warmup selected overlap, while breakable PIECEWISE capture selected Mega mHC. That could leave Mega mHC's stream-local barriers uninitialized until capture, causing startup to fail.

Use overlap only during FULL CUDA graph capture, still bounded by the existing 16-token cutoff and hardware requirements. Eager execution/warmup and PIECEWISE execution retain native mHC dispatch (Mega mHC where supported). Eager warmup therefore initializes Mega mHC on the capture stream. FULL replay retains the captured overlap kernels without executing the Python check per token.

The selection checks actual stream capture and excludes PIECEWISE. This works with V2's existing FULL-capture context, which advertises NONE while the runner explicitly wraps the model in `torch.cuda.graph`. CUDA graph runner/context code, AMD model code, and shared model-state code are unchanged. There is no separate warmup helper or cache. Mega mHC eligibility remains centralized in its implementation module.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k decoder_mixes_match_torch -q -rs

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mhc.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mega_mhc.py \
  tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py
```

- **20 passed**, 285 deselected on GB200. Decoder/reference parity covers broadcast, pipeline, residual, and Engram entry paths under disabled overlap, eager execution, FULL capture/replay, PIECEWISE, and larger batches. The FULL cases verify overlap is called during capture, never eager warmup.
- Pre-commit passed.
- Fresh-process real-weight GB200 TP4 FULL_AND_PIECEWISE startup/capture passed on all four ranks with capture sizes [1,2,4,8]. Both measured exact8192-input/1024-output C1 requests completed, with no monitored inference-time JIT warnings. Mean TPOT 4.553 ms, median ITL 4.385 ms, P99 ITL 10.368 ms. These two requests are a serving smoke check, not a matched performance comparison or a tail-latency improvement claim.
- Earlier revision's GSM8K 128-example smoke: 126/128 (98.44%) flexible extraction, strict 106/128. Checkpoint revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4, FlashInfer FP8 KV, MXFP4 sparse indexer, greedy, five-shot, thinking disabled. This predates the FULL-only-overlap revision and is not a new accuracy evaluation of it. Eager small-batch execution now uses the existing native path, so cross-path bitwise equivalence is not claimed.

## Related work and AI assistance

Open-PR checks found no equivalent fix for the overlap/Mega mHC warmup mismatch exposed by #57603. #57843 warms standalone DeepGEMM prenorm projection specializations; it does not initialize Mega mHC's stream-local barriers. This PR changes DSV4.1 dispatch policy instead.

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation. The human submitter reviewed/tested an earlier revision and requested this FULL-only overlap policy; the revised validation above was performed by the agent.

title: [Bugfix] Profile maximum DeepSeek V4.1 vision features
author: xijiaat
body:
# [Bugfix] Profile the largest legal DeepSeek V4.1 image patch grid

## Purpose

The profiling dummy assumes a square maximizes vision features. The image-token
budget includes one newline token per LLM row, however:
`tokens = rows * (columns + 1) + 2`. A wider legal image can spend less of the
budget on newlines and produce more ViT patches than the square dummy.

With the Flash defaults (patch 14, downsample 3, budget 1024):

| Image | Size (width x height) | ViT patches | Image-span tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Previous dummy | 1302 x 1302 | 8649 | 994 |
| Legal wide image | 2814 x 630 | 9045 | 1022 |
| New dummy | 42882 x 42 | 9189 | 1024 |

Enumerate LLM row counts, maximize the patch grid under the token budget and
optional aspect-ratio clamp, and avoid the minimum-pixel upscaler changing the
chosen aspect ratio. Runtime image preprocessing is unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Size transfers by measured encoder output widths
author: gty111
body:
## Summary

EC producers size each transfer before the item is encoded: Mooncake reserves the destination, and CPU/NIXL allocates blocks at schedule time. The size depends on the encoder output width, which varies by model and modality. For example, Qwen3-Omni's visual DeepStack output is 8192 wide and its audio output is 2048. The HF-config sniff on main misses Qwen3-Omni (it has no top-level `vision_config`), Granite4-Vision and MOSS-Audio.

- **Measure the width instead of inferring it.** After the model loads and before the KV cache is allocated, an EC producer encodes one dummy item per modality on every worker. It records the widths in `ec_transfer_config.mm_encoder_output_widths`, which is internal (`init=False`). Mooncake push specs and CPU save blocks are sized from these widths, and the config sniff is removed.
- **Fail closed.** A producer refuses to start if it measures no width or its ranks disagree.
- **Consumers take the shape from the transfer.** CPU/NIXL announcements carry `shape`, and loads restore it. Mooncake already sends the shape in the reservation.

Outside `ec_transfer/`, the change is one config field and one call in `EngineCore.__init__`. The NIXL protocol version is now 2, so producers and consumers must be upgraded together.

## Validation

Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct at 5003085f09, run as 1 encoder + 1 PD with TP=1, BF16, Model Runner V2 and proxy `--no-rewrite`:

| Path | Measured widths | Requests | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| NIXL | image/video 8192, audio 2048 | image, audio, image+audio: 3/3 OK | 0 size/shape mismatches, 0 local fallbacks |
| Mooncake | same | 3/3 OK | 0 `EC source shape mismatch` |
| CPU offload (`ec_both`) | same | 7/7 OK, then 2/2 after GPU eviction | 0 block overflows; the CPU reload matched round 1 exactly |

The measured widths match the checkpoint: 2048 × (1 + 3 DeepStack layers) = 8192. NIXL and Mooncake returned identical text.

Not run: video requests, Mooncake store, Granite4-Vision and MOSS-Audio (no checkpoints available), and accuracy evals.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR sizes EC transfers from the encoder output. #58853 (NIXL ack block-count check) and #58123 (Mooncake reservation races) touch different files. This PR is independent of #57887's audio metadata-only support.

AI assistance was used: OpenAI Codex for the initial transfer-shape fix and Claude Code for the startup-measurement rework. Pending the submitter's line-by-line review.
