title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Disable SWA bounded replay on ROCm
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## Purpose

Disable SWA bounded replay on ROCm, where it currently faults the GPU.

SWA bounded replay (#56227, on by default) keeps the sliding-window KV out of prefix caching and rebuilds it after a prefix hit by padding the replayed tokens' slots in the prefix-cacheable groups. Correctness depends on the consuming prefill kernel clamping the window; that clamp landed in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA paths.

The ROCm sparse SWA metadata builders (`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder` in both `deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py` and `deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`) only gained the `replay_start` kwarg and forward it to the base builder. Nothing on the ROCm prefill path clamps the window, so the first prefix hit that carries a replay start walks off the padded slots and raises `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, which takes down the worker and then the engine core:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x5621a810) on address 0x7ba8c13ff000. Reason: Unknown.
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered'
RuntimeError: Engine core process EngineCore died unexpectedly.
```

This adds a ROCm guard alongside the existing model-runner-V2 and prefill-context-parallel guards in `DeepseekV4Attention`. Prefix caching itself is unaffected — the sliding-window cache simply takes part in it again, which is the pre-#56227 behavior. The guard should be removed once the ROCm prefill kernels clamp the window too.

## Test Plan

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0, torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0, TP=4, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, DSpark speculative decoding, `--moe-backend aiter`.

Single prompt per request at `max_tokens=1`, sweeping input length across the prefill-chunk boundary:

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,...}'
```

## Test Result

Baseline (`swa_bounded_replay` on, the current default):

| Input tokens | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 4,096 | OK |
| 32,768 | `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, engine core dies |

A prompt that fits in one prefill chunk passes; the fault appears once the prompt spans more than one chunk. Every fault immediately follows the first launch of `_pad_replayed_slots_kernel`. Setting `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` makes the same 32,768-token request pass, which is consistent with reading past the padded slots rather than with a bad constant. `TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0` only moves the threshold (32,768 passes, 131,072 still faults), so this is not a Triton async-copy issue.

With this change, on the same build and the same four GPUs:

| Input tokens | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 32,768 | OK (1.4s) |
| 131,072 | OK (5.5s) |
| 262,144 | OK (10.4s) |
| 314,510 | OK (4.3s) |

Zero memory faults, and `_pad_replayed_slots_kernel` is never launched.

End to end, a 16-configuration MI355X AgentX sweep (TP=2 and TP=4, concurrency 1-128) failed every point before this change and runs clean after it, with the accuracy arm reporting gsm8k `em_strict` 0.9750 / `em_flexible` 0.9742 over 1319 effective samples.

No new test is added: the two sibling guards in this function (model runner V2, prefill context parallelism) are likewise untested, and exercising this one requires a ROCm device with the model loaded.

title: [XPU] [Test] Extend spawn-safe sitecustomize monkeypatch to XPU
author: chaojun-zhang
body:
## Root cause
XPU forces the `spawn` multiprocessing start method , so `monkeypatch.setattr` in the parent test process doesn't propagate to spawned subprocesses. The `rocm_sitecustomize_factory` fixture in `tests/v1/shutdown/conftest.py` was gated to `is_rocm()` only, so it silently no-ops on XPU and the patch never reaches the subprocess.

## Fix
Extend the gate to cover XPU as well, so the fixture applies the sitecustomize patch on both ROCm and XPU.

title: [Bugfix][Engram] Fall back when /dev/shm is absent before sharing tables
author: Juntian777
body:
Follow-up to #57651. `can_share_engram_tables` called `shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm")` unguarded, so a host without `/dev/shm` raised `FileNotFoundError` at model construction instead of falling back to per-rank tables. This checks `os.path.isdir(SHM_PATH)` first and reuses `SHM_PATH` from `shm_broadcast` for the remaining `/dev/shm` references. No duplicate PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

Also flattens `DPSharedEngramStorage._allocate` while touching it: the nested try/except, the `stage` tracker and the manual `finalizer()`/`mapping.close()` rollback become one try/except around the mmap+register step. On a peer failure the locals are dropped (`del tensor, owner, mapping`), so the owner's finalizer unregisters the pages and the mapping unmaps in the same order as before. Error messages carry the exception text instead of a stage prefix. No behavior change.

Test: `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py tests/test_config.py -k "shm or shared_memory or engram"` -> passed
Test: `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -k shared_across_dp_replicas` (4x GB200, covers the create/open/mmap/register/pinned failure injections and the mapping lifetime checks) -> 2 passed on the flattened `_allocate`

### Model evaluation

Evaluated with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` at revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277` on one 4x GB200 node using DEP4 (`TP1 x DP4`, expert parallel) and DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and adaptive verification. MQA GSM8K 5-shot ran through the Completions API with `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, concurrency 32, and all 1,319 examples. It achieved `0.9325` flexible exact match and `0.9325` strict exact match with 0 request errors in 107.46 seconds. `dp_shared_memory=True` initialized successfully, and both Engram tables were shared across all four DP replicas (`94.42 GiB` per table/layer).

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Explicitly reject FSE=1 with DPA+ETP deployment for DeepSeek-V4
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Purpose

Running DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm with data-parallel attention (`--data-parallel-size 8`) and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` fails during weight loading with an obscure error.

```bash
File "/.../vllm/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py", line 1243, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name_mapped]
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_weight_scale_inv'
```

Fused shared experts are not supported under data parallelism: the fused path has no way to load the FP8 shared expert into the MXFP4 routed slot, so users end up debugging weight loading instead of the configuration.

This PR fails fast at model construction time: when fused shared experts are requested (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`), expert parallelism is off, and `data_parallel_size > 1`, the model now raises:

```bash
ValueError: DeepSeek-V4 fused shared experts (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1) are not supported with data parallelism (data_parallel_size > 1). Set VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 to run the shared expert as an unfused FP8 MLP.
```

The check lives in `_fuse_shared_experts_enabled()` in the ROCm-only model file (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`), so non-ROCm paths are untouched. Configurations where FSE is already silently disabled (e.g. expert parallelism enabled) do not raise.

## Test Plan

Launch the DPA+ETP server with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`.

## Test Result

Directly raise `ValueError` so that users know they need to set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` for this scenario, instead of debugging the weight loading code.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix startup OOM in AITER MLA FP8 prefill workspace sizing
author: simondanielsson
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a startup OOM on Kimi K2.5 (or similar) when using the AITER ASM MLA prefill kernel, caused by overly pessimistic bounds on the size of the required persistent metadata buffers. These sizes were subsequently passed to the workspace manager which triggered the OOM.

**Triggered by**: The AITER bump to v0.1.22post1 picked up ROCm/aiter#3606 which slightly changed the logic for workspace sizing. 

**Long term fix in AITER**: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5759

### Why

For causal FP8 MLA the AITER backend uses a persistent kernel. It needs buffers to hold the work items to be completed by each work group. The metadata scheduler is responsible for sizing these buffers so that they are sufficiently large to handle any requests that might come in.  

The MLA metadata scheduler now emits a very loose bound. The bound is based on the assumption that every request can use max_qlen query tokens. (The actual upper bound is that the sum of query tokens equals max_num_batched_tokens). If one uses these to size the logits/attn_lse partial buffers we get huge KV reservations:

| max_num_batched_tokens | before aiter#3606 | after aiter#3606 (OOM) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8192  | 1.88 GiB | 64.03 GiB  | 2.56 GiB |
| 16384 | 3.75 GiB | 128.03 GiB | 2.62 GiB |

**Short term fix**: Size with assumption that the total query tokens is bounded by the token budget.

**Long term fix**: AITER should give us this budget-aware max buffer size. Ticket: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5729

title: [Bugfix][Core][MRV2] Profile the sampler with the params the warm-up actually uses
author: longluubao
body:
## The gap

`profile_run` builds its dummy batch with `InputBatch.make_dummy`, which registers no sampling parameters. Every dummy request therefore leaves `Sampler.needs_logits_processing` False, so `apply_sampling_params` takes its early exit:

```python
if not np.any(self.needs_logits_processing[idx_mapping_np]):
```

and the fp32 logits upcast — plus the logit-bias, penalty and bad-words work behind it — never enters the profiled peak. The KV cache is then sized against a sampler that costs less than the real one.

`warmup_kernels` runs **after** the KV cache has been allocated and uses `SamplingParams.for_sampler_warmup()`, which does engage those parameters. So the first time the expensive path is exercised is the one moment when nothing can be given back, and it can OOM there.

The existing `NOTE(woosuk)` in `_dummy_sampler_run` documents this exact gap. This closes it by profiling with the same helper the warm-up uses, so the two stay in step if that path grows more work later.

## Measurements

One L4 24GB, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, `max_num_seqs=256`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `max_model_len=2048`. Only this patch differs between the two columns.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | KV cache before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.98 | 1,733,440 tokens | 1,710,928 tokens | -1.30% |
| 0.97 | 1,714,176 tokens | 1,691,680 tokens | -1.31% |

The profiler now reserves what the sampler actually costs, so the cache it hands out is smaller by that amount. These four numbers reproduced digit-for-digit on a re-run against current `main`.

### On the OOM, stated precisely

An earlier run - on a different L4, against vLLM 0.29.0 rather than current `main` - had the unpatched build fail outright at 0.98:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py", line 348, in warmup_kernels
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py", line 222, in apply_sampling_params
    logits = torch.empty_like(logits, dtype=torch.float32).copy_(logits)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 150.00 MiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 22.04 GiB of which 127.12 MiB is free.
```

Re-running that A/B against current `main`, **I could not reproduce the hard failure**: both builds start, the unpatched one simply lands closer to the edge (with `enforce_eager=True` it emits a non-fatal `CUDACachingAllocator` OOM and recovers). An earlier revision of this description presented "OOM before, starts after" as the headline result; that overstated it. Read this instead as the profiler under-reporting a real cost, which makes startup fragile near the top of the utilization range. The case rests on the tests below, not on that traceback.

## Cost

KV cache capacity drops about 1.3% at a given `gpu_memory_utilization`, because the profiler now reserves memory it was previously handing to the cache. That is the intended trade: the budget the profiler hands out becomes one the warm-up can actually live within.

## Scope

MRv2 only (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`). The MRv1 runner reaches the same wall from a different direction — its sampler warm-up sits after `capture_model` in `gpu_worker.py` — and is not touched here.

This is narrower than #51590, which corrects the CUDA-graph memory estimate. The two are complementary: that PR fixes how much the graph pool is predicted to take, this fixes what the sampler is predicted to take. Neither subsumes the other.

Also reproduced independently on 8x RTX PRO 4500 (32GB, SM120) with gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 at TP=8, where the same class of failure appears at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95` and clears at 0.90.

---

## AI assistance, duplicate check and testing (per AGENTS.md)

**AI assistance was used.** This change was investigated, written and measured with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter is reviewing it and is responsible for defending it.

### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched before and after opening:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "sampler warmup memory profiling"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "_dummy_sampler_run"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "for_sampler_warmup"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "profile_run sampler"
```

The nearest open PRs, and how this differs:

| PR | Relationship |
|---|---|
| **#43013** `Use realistic top_k in _dummy_sampler_run to avoid SM120 startup hang` | Closest by title, but different runner and opposite intent. It touches `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` (MRv1, labelled `mrv1-only`); this touches `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` (MRv2). It fixes a **kernel hang** caused by `top_k = vocab_size - 1` and states explicitly that it keeps "an identical memory-profiling footprint". This PR is specifically about **changing** that footprint, because in MRv2 `InputBatch.make_dummy` registers no sampling parameters at all, so `apply_sampling_params` early-exits and the fp32 logits upcast is never profiled. The two are compatible and neither subsumes the other. |
| **#51590** `Measure complete CUDA graph capture footprint for KV budgeting` | Same family — a profiled budget that does not survive to post-KV-allocation — but a different term. That PR corrects how much the **CUDA graph pool** is predicted to take; this corrects how much the **sampler** is predicted to take. |
| **#46270** `Fix sampler peak memory profiling for speculative decoding` | Speculative-decoding scope, MRv1, `mrv1-only`. Does not cover the non-specdec MRv2 path. |
| **#46883** `Profile persistent FlashInfer workspace before KV sizing` | Same idea applied to a different allocation (FlashInfer workspace). Complementary. |
| **#52054** `Chunk prompt-logprobs logits to bound the activation peak` | Reduces the peak rather than profiling it. Orthogonal. |

### Test commands run, and results

Environment: 1x NVIDIA L4 24GB (GCP `g2-standard-4`), CUDA toolkit 13.2, torch 2.13.0+cu132, Python 3.12, upstream `main` at `54020c3c3` plus this change, installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto` per AGENTS.md.

```
tests/v1/worker/                                813 passed,  1 skipped
tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py                 41 passed, 19 skipped
tests/v1/sample/test_sampler.py
tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py
tests/v1/sample/test_thinking_budget_state.py   170 passed,  2 skipped
```

No failures and no errors. `pre-commit run --files <the three changed files>` - all hooks passed.

### The new tests fail without the change

This is the part worth checking. With the production hunk reverted to its parent and the test files left in place:

```
this branch          3 passed
change reverted      3 failed
```

- `test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_dummy_sampler_run_registers_warmup_params_before_sampling` - CPU only. Asserts every dummy request is registered with `SamplingParams.for_sampler_warmup()` and that `apply_staged_writes()` runs after all of them and before the sampler. The ordering is the point: flush late and the profiled run does not see the params.
- `test_gpu_model_runner_v2_sampler_profiling.py::test_dummy_sampler_run_profiles_the_path_the_warmup_takes` - wires the real `Sampler`, real `InputBuffers` and a probe `LogitsProcessor`. Unpatched the pipeline never runs (`applied_dtypes == []`); patched it runs on the fp32 copy, and the peak grows by at least the size of that copy.
- `test_gpu_model_runner_v2_sampler_profiling.py::test_profiling_residue_does_not_put_serving_on_the_expensive_path` - pins down why no cleanup is needed: a slot is rewritten from the arriving request's own params before anything reads it.

### On not restoring the sampler state

An earlier revision wrapped the profiling in `try/finally` and restored `needs_logits_processing`. That is gone, deliberately. It ran *after* the sampler call, so it never affected the profiled peak; it restored one of the six structures `Sampler.add_request` writes, and not the ones (`top_k`, `top_p`, `temperature`) that are read outside the `needs_logits_processing` gate; and `warmup_kernels` recreates identical residue moments later through the real `add_requests` path, which mainline has always accepted.

No model-evaluation results are included because this change does not alter sampling behaviour or model output - it changes what the memory profiler accounts for, and therefore how large the KV cache is.

If maintainers want other suites run, name them and the results will be posted here.

title: [Build] Fix CUDA 12 KV connector dependency selection
author: jeejeelee
body:
Use LMCache 0.4.4 and CuPy CUDA 12 for CUDA 12 images, and constrain the installed Torch/CUDA stack during KV connector installation in Docker and CI. Dependency conflicts now fail the build instead of silently replacing Torch.

Related to #56829. Unlike #56967, this also selects CUDA 12-compatible connector dependencies; Torch constraints alone conflict with LMCache 0.5.5 requiring CUDA 13. The CUDA 13 requirements remain unchanged.

Validation: `uv pip compile` passed for cu129/x86_64 and cu130/aarch64 with Torch 2.13.0 pinned; 10 mocked installer scenarios and `bash -n .buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh` passed. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Refresh online NVFP4 scales before reload post-processing
author: S1ro1
body:
## Problem and change

Online NVFP4 reuses its MoE kernel and quantization config across weight reloads. Conversion installs new weight-scale tensors on the layer, but the reused config still references the previous alpha storage. Expert post-processing can therefore rebuild derived scales (for example TRTLLM's `g1_scale_c`) using the previous weights' scales. Restoring graph-visible parameter storage afterward is too late to correct those derived values.

Copy the converted `w13_scale_2` and `w2_scale_2` values into the persistent config alphas before expert post-processing. Preserve the kernel, config, and alpha storage identities. This follows up the kernel reuse introduced by #50074; it does not rebuild the kernel or change quantization policy.

Extend the existing lifecycle test with changed scales over three processing calls. Check the values visible during expert post-processing and stable config/alpha storage.

## Related work

Checked open reload/scale work, including #49789, #50521, #50538 and #53741. Those address broader reload arenas, CUTLASS/B12x runtime storage, or ModelOpt reload. None modifies `online/nvfp4.py` to refresh an already-reused config before expert post-processing. This is the narrow online-NVFP4 refresh; broader storage work may eventually subsume it.

## Validation

- On upstream base `606d124b377e6462fe0f9076df4d50c88e4dcf48`, the extended existing test fails before the fix: expert post-processing observes the preceding alpha values on the first changed-weight reload. It passes with this fix.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, and repository checks. The port adds explicit non-null alpha assertions for current-main typing.
- Focused test command on this CPU-only login node (using the existing dependency environment):

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" uv run --no-project --python /home/matej/prime-rl-pd-validation/.venv/bin/python python -c 'import vllm.platforms; from vllm.platforms.cpu import CpuPlatform; vllm.platforms._current_platform=CpuPlatform(); import pytest; raise SystemExit(pytest.main(["--confcutdir=tests/quantization", "tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_nvfp4_reuses_kernel_when_weights_are_reprocessed", "-q"]))'
```

- Earlier B300 component validation of the same seven-line fix used the GLM-5.3 RL deployment's older vLLM base (`2e6816c274496e0a6436773bfa3c1c640b64567b`) and the FlashInfer TRTLLM NVFP4 expert backend. Reloaded versus freshly loaded identical weights had approximately 9.58% and 22.49% relative output RMS error for deliberate 1.1x and 0.9x weight changes before the fix. Afterward both were bit-identical, including replay of a graph captured before reload. Same-weight reload was already exact. These deliberately large changes expose the bug; they are not estimates of normal optimizer-step error.
- No new full-model evaluation or GPU validation on current main was run for this draft. Earlier full-model GLM-5.3 RL measurements retained approximately 0.04–0.05 KL and included a separate trainer experiment, so they do not establish model-level improvement from this fix alone.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex investigated, ported the fix, extended the regression test, and prepared this draft. Submitted as a draft for collaborator assessment; human review and current-main GPU/model validation remain pending.

title: [Core][Logging] Fix JSON logging process decoration
author: markmc
body:
`decorate_logs()` wraps `stdout` and `stderr` to prefix output with the logical process name and PID. This corrupts JSON emitted by custom Python logging configurations, including the documented `python-json-logger` example, because each JSON object gains non-JSON leading text.

Store the vLLM logical process name in a `LogRecord` attribute instead. The default text formatter renders it alongside the standard process PID provided by logging, preserving normal console output without altering standard streams. JSON formatters then retain the name as structured metadata and emit valid JSON.

Fixes #57955

---

title: [Bugfix] Don't drop the rest of the allocator config when toggling expandable segments
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Purpose

`CuMemAllocator.use_memory_pool` turns expandable segments off for the duration of the sleep-mode pool, because the two are incompatible (pytorch/pytorch#147851). Two bugs in how it does that:

1. **It drops the rest of the allocator config.** It writes the bare string `"expandable_segments:False"` and restores with `"expandable_segments:True"`. Torch parses the allocator config as a whole — `parseArgs` resets every option absent from the string it is handed — so the write also clears `max_split_size_mb`, `garbage_collection_threshold` and `roundup_power2_divisions`, and the restore does not bring them back. Whatever the user tuned is gone for the rest of the process, silently, from the first sleep-pool entry.

2. **It reads the wrong environment variable.** It only looks at `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`. A user on torch's current `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`, or ROCm's `PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF`, gets no toggle at all and runs the sleep-mode pool in exactly the configuration the toggle exists to avoid.

Adds `vllm/device_allocator/alloc_conf.py`, which reads the config that is actually live (falling back to the environment), flips a single field while preserving every other one, and writes the whole string back. `use_memory_pool` now goes through it.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/test_alloc_conf.py` (CPU-only), registered on the `(CPU) Params, Env, Tokenizers, Parser` step.
- Manual before/after on one GPU: enter `use_memory_pool`, read `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()["allocator_settings"]` before, inside and after, under each environment variable.

## Test Result

30 new tests pass. Measured on torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, with
`expandable_segments:True,max_split_size_mb:512,garbage_collection_threshold:0.9`:

| | before pool | inside pool | after pool |
|---|---|---|---|
| before, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` | es=True max_split=536870912 gc=0.9 | es=False **max_split=-1 gc=0.0** | es=True **max_split=-1 gc=0.0** |
| before, `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF` | es=True max_split=536870912 gc=0.9 | **es=True** (toggle never fires) | es=True max_split=536870912 gc=0.9 |
| after, either variable | es=True max_split=536870912 gc=0.9 | es=False max_split=536870912 gc=0.9 | es=True max_split=536870912 gc=0.9 |

## Notes

`expandable_segments_enabled()` returns `None`, not `False`, when the live state cannot be read: the environment can never reflect a runtime write, so a caller verifying a write it just issued must not read "cannot tell" as "the write did not take".

The new test is wired onto the shared `&cpu-async-engine-deps` anchor, which three other CPU steps reuse, so it slightly widens their triggers too. Happy to inline the two dependency lines on the one step instead if preferred.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Skip the fused silu-mul block-quant fast path when a swiglu clamp is set
author: garrett361
body:
## Purpose

The fused `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` fast path in `TritonExperts.apply` has no clamp
parameter, so a configured SwiGLU clamp limit (`gemm1_clamp_limit`, or `swiglu_limit` from
the model config) is silently dropped for fp8 w8a8 block-[128, 128] experts. Gate that fast
path on `clamp_limit is None` so clamped models fall back to the existing
`swiglu_limit_func` path, while unclamped models keep the fusion.

- Introduced by #42497. In-tree, EXAONE MoE reaches this path: it passes
  `activation="silu"` with a per-layer `swiglu_limit`.
- `TritonExperts` is selected whenever `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts` rejects DeepGEMM, so
  exposure depends on shape and environment: small `M`, small `N`, non-contiguous weights,
  or DeepGEMM not installed, in which case every shape is affected.
  `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1` also masks the bug via the existing
  `not is_deep_gemm_e8m0_used()` term in the same condition.
- `CutlassExperts` already gates its own fused SiLU+quant fast path on
  `activation_config.clamp_limit is None`, so this follows existing precedent.
- `DeepGemmExperts`, the sibling backend for larger shapes, threads `gemm1_clamp_limit`
  through its activation paths and was never affected.

**Relation to #53875.** That PR contains the same guard alongside a new fused CUDA kernel;
this PR is just the correctness guard, which was asked for separately in that thread so it
can land and be backported on its own. Close this one if #53875 lands first.

## Test Plan

`pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` on an H200, which now includes a dispatch
regression asserting the fused kernel is skipped when a clamp limit is set.

## Test Result

The new test fails before the fix and passes after. The rest of the suite is unchanged:
163 passed, and its 3 `test_w8a8_block_fp8_fused_moe` failures at N=4608/K=7168 reproduce
identically on unmodified `main`.

No model eval was run: the change routes clamped SiLU back onto the pre-#42497 unfused
path that the existing block-fp8 suites already cover. Separately, in our own deployment
(out-of-tree, `swiglu_limit = 10.0`, fp8 block quantization) this bug produced deterministic
junk-token argmaxes during decode, which the fix removes.

title: [Bugfix] Release prompt_embeds tensor when its InputBatch slot is freed
author: khushali9
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #57974
InputBatch.remove_request() clears every other per-slot state but never
drops req_prompt_embeds[req_index], so a finished prompt-embeds request
leaves its (num_prompt_tokens, hidden_size) tensor owned by the
persistent batch. The tensor stays alive until the same slot is reused
by another prompt-embeds request or the dict is cleared; reusing the
slot with a token-id request does not release it. A worker can thus
retain the peak prompt-embeds footprint of a past burst after switching
entirely to token-id traffic, up to max_num_seqs * sizeof(embeds) of
host memory.

Pop the entry in remove_request(), before the pooling-model early
return, so a vacated slot owns nothing from its previous occupant.
condense() already relocates surviving requests' embeds, so no
additional cleanup is needed in the reuse or empty-batch paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8

## Test Plan
Added three CPU-only unit tests to
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch.py

## Test Result

12 passed

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Scope DSpark non-causal capability to builder layers
author: xaguilar-amd
body:

title: [Bugfix] Reject a prefix_match_unit that a single KV cache group cannot honor
author: QHarshil
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58020.

With a single KV cache group, `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` uses the block size as the hash unit and drops `--prefix-match-unit` without a warning. The Mamba prefill checkpoint builder (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/checkpoint.py`, used by the Kimi-K3 KDA path with FlashKDA) still reads the flag. It writes the checkpoint for a different position than the one the scheduler registers for that block, and a later prefix-cache hit resumes from the wrong recurrent state. Nothing errors.

This rejects a `prefix_match_unit` other than the block size when there is exactly one group and block hashing is active (prefix caching or a KV connector), the same condition the multi-group path checks before it reads the flag. The flag's docstring already requires every group's block size to be divisible by it, and one group can't honor anything else.

#58020 proposed propagating the resolved unit to the workers. The case above is the only divergence I could reach. With the flag unset, align mode sets the Mamba block size to the attention block size (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`), so the builder's fallback equals the resolver's GCD. #56960 moves the same builder into the shared GDN metadata path, and this check covers it there too.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/kv_connector/unit
```

The suites were also run on clean `main` in a separate worktree with the same packages. On an H100 NVL: the repro below on `main` and this branch, plus `lm_eval` gsm8k and `vllm bench serve` with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`.

## Test Result

- The resolver called directly: it raises for one group with prefix caching or a connector on and a different flag, and returns the block size with the flag unset or equal, with prefix caching and connectors off, and with no KV cache groups.
- `tests/v1/core` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` on CPU: every failure also fails on `main` (`e440b75`) from the environment (no CUDA, no ray, gated models), apart from Hugging Face 429s. Those were rerun three times on both trees and passed each time.
- `test_mooncake_store_worker.py` builds `cache_config` as a `SimpleNamespace`, so the stub gains `prefix_match_unit=None`.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files: passed.

The GPU runs below were on `3300c8c`, before the check was gated on block hashing. The repro enables prefix caching, so it takes the same path.

Repro, a tiny all-KDA `KimiLinearForCausalLM` with seeded random weights and a 2040-token prompt:

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 python repro_kda_checkpoint.py \
    --layout kda-only --prefix-match-unit 32 --block-size 16 --splice 2016:2032
```

On `main` the worker writes the checkpoint at 2016 into the slot the scheduler registers as 2032. The cached request matches a cold run of the prompt with tokens 2016-2031 removed exactly (max first-step top-20 logprob diff 0.0) and differs from the plain cold run by 0.0464. On this branch the command stops at startup:

```text
ValueError: Invalid prefix_match_unit=32; with a single KV cache group, prefix-cache hits land on the block size (16). Unset it or set it to 16.
```

Without the flag, and with one MLA layer added (two groups, flag honored), both arms produce byte-identical output.

`lm_eval` gsm8k 5-shot through `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --language-model-only`: flexible-extract 0.3601 on `main`, 0.3571 here (stderr 0.0132).

`vllm bench serve`, random dataset with a 512-token shared prefix plus 512 input tokens, 128 output, 400 prompts, concurrency 64, seeds 0-2, three rounds per arm with the last two interleaved: output throughput 6598 tok/s on `main` and 6422 here, sd about 400 on both, and the per-round gap changes sign. The shared prefix is shorter than the 544-token block, so there were no prefix-cache hits, and the model has four KV cache groups, so the new check is not on this path. Treat it as a regression check.

Full logs, sha256sums and scripts are attached in the review thread.

## Not a duplicate

```bash
gh issue view 58020 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "58020 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "prefix_match_unit"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes"
```

No open PR validates `prefix_match_unit` for single-group models. #56960 touches the checkpoint builder but not the resolver.

AI assistance was used for parts of this change. I have reviewed every changed line and can defend the design end to end.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Clamp FP8 scales before UE8M0 rounding
author: rao-ashish
body:
## Purpose

Without this PR, [this reproducer][reproducer] crashes during DeepGEMM warmup for `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base` with the DeepGEMM FP8 linear backend.

`QuantFP8._quantize_group_native` previously rounded activation scales to UE8M0-compatible powers of two before applying `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR`. For zero or sufficiently small activation groups, the subsequent clamp replaced the rounded value with `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR`, which is not a power of two. DeepGEMM requires FP32 scale factors used for UE8M0 packing to have zero sign and mantissa bits, so these clamped scales triggered a device assertion while DeepGEMM packed them.

This PR applies the minimum-scale clamp before UE8M0 rounding. The resulting scale therefore remains at least `_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR` while satisfying the exponent-only representation expected by DeepGEMM. The non-UE8M0 path retains its existing behavior.

The existing group-quantization edge-case test is extended to cover an all-zero input with UE8M0 enabled. It verifies both the minimum-scale bound and the zero-sign-and-mantissa invariant enforced by DeepGEMM.

[reproducer]: https://gist.github.com/rao-ashish/8a648b7aadbf4380bc3a6e643b1cb471

## Test Plan

Run the targeted `QuantFP8` group-quantization edge-case test:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant_group.py::test_quantfp8_group_edge_cases
```

Run the [reproducer][reproducer] on an NVIDIA GB300 with the DeepGEMM FP8 linear backend and verify that model initialization and DeepGEMM warmup complete without the scale-layout device assertion.

## Test Result

- The targeted pytest test passes.
- Before this change, the reproducer triggers the assertion in `smxx_layout.cuh` that FP32 scale factors must have zero sign and mantissa bits, followed by `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED`.
- After this change, the reproducer completes model initialization and DeepGEMM warmup without that assertion or CUDA launch failure.
- No documentation update is needed because this only corrects existing quantization behavior.

title: [Mypy] Fix mypy typing for Qwen and Qianfan models
author: ashraf-bhuiyan
body:
## Purpose

Address part of [#26533](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26533) by fixing typing in the Qwen/Qianfan model family and removing `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[qQ]"` from the mypy exclusions. All 24 selected model files are now checked.

The changes cover optional configuration and multimodal fields, tensor/container and cache types, generic processing-info types (including ASR inheritance), MoE mixin attributes, and the realtime async-generator protocol.

Five documented, line-specific typing exceptions preserve existing runtime contracts: four incompatible speculative-drafter/MTP overrides and one instance-local override of a class-level LoRA mapping. No file-wide ignores or replacement exclusions were added.

The branch incorporates upstream `main` at `276db94fb2`. The conflict resolution preserves upstream's multimodal processor interfaces, typed dummy options, ASR position fix, tensor video timestamps, and vision caches. The remaining diff against that revision touches 23 files.

## Reproducer

On upstream main, first remove the Q-model exclusion from `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, then run:

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Drop -1 sentinels when building the ragged sparse-MLA indices
author: cagrikymk
body:
## Purpose
The sparse MLA kernel (pa_sparse_prefill_opus) currently seg. faults when -1 sentinels happen within accessed region as there is no check for it.

 `combine_topk_swa_indices` reserves top-k columns from a position-derived count and writes `-1` wherever a candidate fails its validity test, and `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` copies the row prefix verbatim, sentinels included.
 
 ## The fix

Make the ragged index stream sentinel-free at the point it is built, so no consumer can dereference one. `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` now keeps only valid entries per row, and `indptr` counts those. Semantically identical, skipping an index and masking it out give the same attention result.

This is layout-agnostic: it does not matter whether the sentinels are leading, interior or trailing. Getting rid of 
"-1" indices should not cause any side-effects as they are supposed to be masked out anyway.

## Tests

GSM8K 5-shot shares a few-shot prefix, so with prefix caching on (the default)
it generates partial hits:

| build | aiter | GSM8K (full 1319, 5-shot) |
|---|---|---|
| without the fix | ToT | **engine crashes mid-eval**, 4x `Memory access fault`, lm_eval aborts |
| with the fix | ToT (`tot_main`, 93 commits past v0.1.22) | **0.9750** strict / **0.9742** flexible, 1319/1319 |
| with the fix | **v0.1.22.post1**, vLLM's pin (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`) | **0.9727** strict / **0.9719** flexible, 1319/1319 |

## Performance

This function is already almost invisible e2e as it is called few times:

For dsv41 flash:

| phase | calls | vs the model's 40 sparse-attention layers |
|---|---|---|
| **prefill** | **40 per chunk** | one per layer, not shared |
| **decode** | **~3 per step** | already shared across layers |

I still did a unit-benchmark to show the fixes do not make this kernel expensive, and kernel count goes from 4 to 3 as no need for clamping (in kernel logic now) and torch zeros is folded into the newly created kernel.

| topk | sliding_window | width | C | upstream | this fix | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 1 | 7.2 us (4 kernels) | 6.3 us (3 kernels) | -0.9 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 64 | 7.4 us (4) | 9.4 us (3) | +2.0 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 128 | 7.6 us (4) | 9.6 us (3) | +2.0 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 1024 | 9.0 us (4) | 10.9 us (3) | +1.9 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 8192 | 32.6 us (5) | 28.4 us (4) | -4.2 us |
| 512 | 128 | 640 | 16384 | 52.7 us (5) | 43.3 us (4) | -9.4 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 1 | 7.2 us (4) | 7.3 us (3) | +0.1 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 64 | 7.6 us (4) | 11.0 us (3) | +3.4 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 128 | 7.5 us (4) | 11.0 us (3) | +3.5 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 1024 | 10.8 us (4) | 13.1 us (3) | +2.3 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 8192 | 48.2 us (5) | 41.3 us (4) | -6.9 us |
| 1024 | 128 | 1152 | 16384 | 78.2 us (5) | 67.4 us (4) | -10.8 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 1 | 7.4 us (4) | 8.6 us (3) | +1.2 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 64 | 7.5 us (4) | 12.8 us (3) | +5.3 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 128 | 8.1 us (4) | 12.6 us (3) | +4.5 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 1024 | 13.9 us (4) | 15.8 us (3) | +1.9 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 8192 | 71.6 us (5) | 55.5 us (4) | -16.1 us |
| 2048 | 128 | 2176 | 16384 | 164.1 us (5) | 91.2 us (4) | **-72.9 us** |

E2E runs with dsv41 flash:

ISL=1024, OSL=1024, C=1 with NP=10 and C=32 with NP=320.
Speculative decoding and prefix caching both off, to keep the comparison simple.

(The bug doesnt trigger without prefix caching, no perf delta as expected since this module has very little part in e2e in terms of perf)

| | | upstream | with this fix | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C=1** | output tok/s | 95.15 | 95.59 | +0.5 % |
| | TTFT mean | 142.14 ms | 142.06 ms | -0.1 % |
| | TPOT mean | 10.38 ms | 10.33 ms | -0.5 % |
| | duration | 107.62 s | 107.12 s | -0.5 % |
| **C=32** | output tok/s | 1885.15 | 1881.40 | -0.2 % |
| | TTFT mean | 894.94 ms | 891.07 ms | -0.4 % |
| | TPOT mean | 16.11 ms | 16.15 ms | +0.2 % |
| | duration | 173.82 s | 174.17 s | +0.2 % |


## Duplicate check

I searched vLLM PRs and issues for `pa_sparse_prefill_opus`, `build_ragged_indices_from_dense`, and "Memory access fault" with DeepSeek V4 sparse attention. No other PR fixes this crash. Related work that is not a duplicate:

- #52628 and #58352 (draft) add `build_ragged_indices_from_dense_out`, which writes ragged decode metadata straight into caller-owned CUDA graph buffers. They don't touch the prefill crash, but they build on `_pack_dense_prefix_to_ragged_kernel`, which this PR replaces. Whichever lands second needs to keep the sentinel-free behaviour, or decode rows will carry `-1` again.
- #55695 hardens the same DSv4 prefill path against chunks with zero query tokens. That's a different failure.
- #48266 is a memory fault on gfx942 (MI325X). It predates the OPUS routing added in #54855, and gfx942 never takes the OPUS path, so it isn't this crash.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). I used it to trace the root cause through #54855 and #56228, to help write the kernel changes and the unit test, and to address review comments. I reviewed every changed line and understand the change end to end.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Run the dense MLP layers on the sequence-parallel shard
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash served with DP > 1, TP > 1 and `--enable-expert-parallel` (the configuration that turns on `use_sequence_parallel_moe`) sporadically emits a wrong first token, stray `</think>` tokens followed by a repeated reasoning block, and occasionally byte garbage such as `ԥԥԥԥ� Canadian French, ԥԥ�1ԥ…`. DP with TP=1 and TP-only serving are clean.

`Glm5NextModel` follows the DeepSeek-V4 sequence-parallel layout: the token dimension is sharded across the TP group once at the model entry (`sp_shard`) and every layer runs its mHC and MLP on that shard, gathering only for attention. Every non-MoE module on the shard therefore has to be sequence-parallel aware. The dense MLP of the first `first_k_dense_replace` (3) layers was still constructed as a standard TP MLP, so its `down_proj` all-reduce summed the partial outputs of *different* tokens held by the two TP ranks:

- multi-token batches (prefill, concurrent decode): rows of the first three layers are mixed pairwise, hence the wrong first token / garbage under load;
- single-token decode: the peer rank holds a zero padding row, so the real token only loses half of the intermediate dimension, which is why the model still looked mostly coherent and the bug went unnoticed.

The shared experts already pass `is_sequence_parallel` (replicated weights, `disable_tp`, no collective). This PR passes the same flag to the dense `Glm5NextMLP` and adds a unit test for the layout. TP-only and DP-with-TP1 deployments do not enter this branch and are unchanged.

Related but different: #50154 describes a sequence-parallel bug in the `deepseek_v2` path (GLM-5.2), where the SP boundary sits inside the MoE block; glm5next shards the whole model, so the fix lives in the dense layer construction instead.

## Test Plan

Unit test (single process, fakes a TP=2 world in the parallel linear layers and forbids the all-reduce):

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_sequence_parallel.py -v
```

The layer-level case fails on `main` (the dense `gate_up_proj` weight is sharded to half the intermediate size) and passes with this PR.

End to end on 4x GB300, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8), FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE attention, FLASHINFER_TRTLLM FP8 MoE, `allgather_reducescatter` all2all, default CUDA graphs, prefix caching disabled, `--max-num-seqs 64`:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Each chat completion is scored as anomalous if the parsed reasoning/content contains U+FFFD, non-printable characters, a run of 8+ identical non-whitespace characters, a 4-gram repetition ratio above 0.5, or more than one `</think>`. `lm_eval` gsm8k 5-shot on 200 problems via `local-completions`.

## Test Result

| config | 16 prompts sequential (temp 0) | 64 prompts, concurrency 64, 1024 tok | 8 x ~15k-token prompts + 8 short, concurrent | gsm8k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP4 TP1 EP | 0 / 16 | 0 / 64 | 0 / 16 | 0.935 |
| DP4 TP1 EP + MTP(3) + kv fp8 | 0 / 16 | 0 / 64 | 0 / 16 | 0.94 |
| TP4 EP | 0 / 48 (3 runs) | - | - | - |
| DP2 TP2 EP, **before** | 4 / 16 | **31 / 64** | 3 / 16 | 0.95 |
| DP2 TP2 EP, **after** | 0 / 48 (3 runs) | 0 / 64 | 0 / 16 | 0.935 |

Before the fix the three temperature-0 runs of the same prompt typically diverged at the first or second character (the prefill result itself was wrong). After the fix they diverge only late (character 84 to 724), the same as the TP4 EP baseline (47 to 1228), which is the usual batch-dependent nondeterminism. gsm8k is insensitive to this bug because the answers are short.

Ruled out on the way: the MNNVL Lamport custom all-gather / reduce-scatter kernels used by `sp_all_gather` / `sp_reduce_scatter` on this platform pass a 2-GPU stress test against NCCL (3000 iterations, 1 to 1024 rows x 4096 bf16, all-gather and reduce-scatter back to back, 0 mismatches).

`pre-commit` hooks `ruff-check` / `ruff-format` pass on the changed files.

This change was made with AI assistance (Claude Code); the analysis and results above were reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Transformers backend] Fix CUDA graph capture for dynamic-rope models
author: YongfengX
body:
## Overview

Transformers' `@dynamic_rope_update` syncs on `torch.max(position_ids)` in every rotary forward, so dynamic-rope models crash during CUDA graph capture on the Transformers backend. Since #53615, this stops Hunyuan V1 dense models (e.g. Hunyuan-7B-Instruct) from starting on `main` with default settings. Completes #23738.

Closes #57890

## Claims

- When `max_model_len <= max_position_embeddings` the update can never fire, so the decoder's dynamic rotary modules are relabelled as `"default"` after init. `inv_freq` is untouched, so outputs are bit-identical.
- These models are now compiled and run with CUDA graphs: 1.7x throughput on Hunyuan-7B-Instruct.
- Unchanged beyond `max_position_embeddings`, or with a `longrope` layer type, where the sync is real.

## Validation

`tencent/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct`, 1x B200, default `max_model_len` (32768):

| | Startup | GPQA-Diamond | gsm8k | Throughput (req/s) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model card | | 60.1 | | | |
| `main` | ❌ capture crash | | | | |
| `main`, `cudagraph_mode: NONE` | ✅ | | 0.321 | 34.78 | 4451 |
| PR | ✅ | 61.1 | 0.316 | **59.44** | **7608** |

GPQA-Diamond: 198 questions x 2, thinking mode, 1σ ≈ 2.5 pt. gsm8k: 1σ ≈ 1.3 pt, and it is low for this model regardless of implementation (native v0.28.0 also scores 0.314).

```bash
vllm serve tencent/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct --model-impl transformers --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
vllm bench throughput --model tencent/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct --model-impl transformers \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --dataset-name random --input-len 1024 --output-len 256 \
    --num-prompts 1000
# GPQA-Diamond: serve with --reasoning-parser hunyuan_a13b, gpt-oss simple-evals
# GPQAEval(n_repeats=2) with ChatCompletionsSampler(temperature=0.7, max_tokens=28000)

pytest tests/models/transformers/test_dynamic_rope.py  # 5 passed
```

## Details

- The rope type is relabelled on the modules rather than in the config, because model-specific dynamic inits (e.g. Hunyuan's `alpha`) only run when `rope_type == "dynamic"`.
- `can_enable_torch_compile` runs before the modules exist, so it shares the config-level check with the relabelling.

title: [Bugfix] Make disable_any_whitespace actually disable whitespace on xgrammar
author: stu-cao
body:
## Purpose

`disable_any_whitespace` does not disable whitespace on the xgrammar backend — it **makes whitespace mandatory**, and as a side effect masks out the token the model wants at every JSON value position.

xgrammar's `any_whitespace=False` selects a *fixed* JSON format rather than a whitespace-free one. Its docstring is explicit that the format follows `json.dumps()` conventions, and with `separators` left unset the default is `(", ", ": ")` — *with* spaces. `backend_xgrammar.py` never passes `separators`, so today the flag requires a space after every comma and colon.

The second-order effect is the damaging one. Because the space is mandatory, the bare `"` that opens a string value becomes illegal at the value position. Measured on the mask with a real GLM-5.3 tokenizer, immediately after `{"location":`:

| grammar config | allowed tokens | whitespace-leading | bare `"` | digit-leading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `any_whitespace=True` | 1450 | 719 | yes | 395 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, default separators — **today** | 268 | **268, all of them** | **banned** | 0 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, `separators=(",", ":")` — **this PR** | 703 | **0** | yes | 395 |

The middle row is what vLLM produces now: every legal continuation begins with a space. A model prompted for minified JSON wants the bare `"`; with it masked out, probability mass shifts to the whitespace-prefixed set, where `␣0`, `␣1`, `␣-` compete with `␣"`.

On a production GLM-5.3 deployment this corrupted **26.5%** of `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` responses, returning a number where the first string value belonged:

```
{"location": 2,      "conditions": "cloudy", ...}
{"location": 0.2373, "temperature": 12, ...}
{"location": 0,      "temperature": 0, ... "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

Nothing errors — `finish_reason` and `usage` are normal, so the caller simply receives wrong types.

It is worth noting `json_schema` requests with typed properties were unaffected: a strict schema leaves only `"` legal at that position, so even a forced space yields `␣"` and no digit is reachable. Only permissive grammars (`json_object`, or schemas with loose value types) expose it.

## Fix

Pass compact separators when the flag is set, so it means what its name says:

```python
separators = (",", ":") if self.disable_any_whitespace else None
```

This is strictly better than both current behaviours — genuinely whitespace-free output (0 whitespace-leading tokens) *and* the model's preferred token stays legal.

## Test Plan

Adds `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar_whitespace.py`, which inspects the bitmask at the value position after `{"a":`:

- a bare digit and a bare `"` must be legal when whitespace is disabled
- `' 1'` must **not** be legal when whitespace is disabled
- both forms stay legal when whitespace is enabled (guards the default path)

## Test Result

Run against vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b` with xgrammar 0.2.6:

**Before this change — 3 failed, 1 passed.** Each failure is the real defect:

```
FAILED test_compact_value_tokens_survive_disable_any_whitespace[1]   <- bare digit masked
FAILED test_compact_value_tokens_survive_disable_any_whitespace["]   <- bare quote masked
FAILED test_disable_any_whitespace_forbids_the_space                 <- ' 1' legal, i.e. the space was required
1 passed                                                             <- whitespace-enabled control
```

**After this change — 4 passed.**

End-to-end on the affected deployment, n=200 per arm, interleaved, Wilson 95% intervals: `json_object` defect rate **24.0% [16.7, 33.2] → 0.0% [0.0, 1.9]**, whitespace **17.8 → 0.1 chars/response**. The fix is also *cheaper*, since the model minifies on its own once the grammar stops forcing spaces.

## Notes

- `separators` has been part of `compile_json_schema` since well before the pinned xgrammar 0.2.7 (verified present in 0.2.6), and it is ignored when `any_whitespace=True`, so the default path is unchanged.
- The `guidance` backend is unaffected — it maps the same flag to `whitespace_flexible` and was measured clean (0/200) on the same deployment.
- Branch is based on `869f7873` rather than current `main`; the touched region of `backend_xgrammar.py` is byte-identical between the two, and I am happy to rebase.

title: [Bugfix][Model][CPU] Fix Mamba2 quantized in_proj weight and scale loading for TP >1
author: Akashcodes732
body:
## Purpose
Fix `RuntimeError: start (...) + length (...) exceeds dimension size (...)` when serving quantized Mamba-2 models (e.g. `granite-4.0-h-tiny-quantized.w8a8`) with TP > 1.

- **Cause**: In `MambaMixer2`, `self.in_proj` groups B and C are replicated when `ngroups < tp_size`. While `weight` used `mamba_loader`, quantized parameters (`weight_scale`, `input_scale`) used default linear slicing, causing out-of-bounds indexing on Rank 1+.
- **Fix**: Apply `mamba_loader` to all parameters of `self.in_proj` and align sliced scale dimensions with `target_slice`.



## Test Plan
```bash
# Serve model with TP=2
vllm serve fedora-copr/granite-4.0-h-tiny-quantized.w8a8 --tensor-parallel-size 2

# Test completion
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "fedora-copr/granite-4.0-h-tiny-quantized.w8a8", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}]}'


## Test Result
- **Before**: Crashed on Rank 1 at startup: `RuntimeError: start (3352) + length (3352) exceeds dimension size (6448)`
- **After**: Server starts cleanly on TP=2 and successfully responds with `"2 + 2 = 4"`.
```

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Restore KVCR construction through the secondary-tier factory
author: ai-yang
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58087.

A standard `type="kvcr"` secondary tier fails to initialize because `SecondaryTierFactory` passes `backpressure_detector=None` even when backpressure is not configured, while `KVCRSecondaryTierManager` does not accept that argument. Consequently, the server exits before it can serve a request.

Accept the optional detector in the KVCR constructor and forward it to `SecondaryTierManager`. Keep the parameter at the end of the existing signature to preserve existing positional arguments. Route the existing KVCR test helper through the production factory and exercise request/load behavior with both default and explicitly configured backpressure.

This restores the constructor contract introduced by [#50045](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50045) after the KVCR adapter landed in [#53624](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53624). Default configurations retain a `None` detector; explicitly configured detectors are preserved rather than silently discarded.

Duplicate checks on 2026-09-22 found no existing issue or PR addressing this constructor mismatch. [#57500](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57500) concerns buffer lifetime after a native startup failure and leaves this signature unchanged.

## Test Plan

Run the focused suites with the optional KVCR package installed:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_backpressure.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py -q
```

The adapted KVCR tests use the real factory with the existing recording backend. They cover construction, configured detector retention, request hints, key/descriptor translation, load completion, and request cleanup.

Changed-file checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/kvcr/manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/kvcr/manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py
```

For serving validation, repeat the accompanying issue's Qwen3-0.6B startup command on the same RTX 3090 and send three deterministic `/v1/completions` requests. Compare their generated token IDs with the primary-only reference. Run the repository's required checks on the changed files.

## Test Result

The published fix is commit `ab62868f6f16b4b21ced4655150833100a07cb83`. Its patch is byte-for-byte identical to the validated two-file patch.

Before the production fix, on vLLM source `c723a831a81cb4ff89ea6d61b2d15109306ed1bc`:

- The KVCR suite with its helper routed through the production factory failed all 21 cases with the constructor keyword error.
- The generation-only GPU reproduction with real Qwen3-0.6B weights exited during startup with the same `TypeError`.
- The primary-only control started successfully and returned HTTP 200 for all three completion requests, each generating `[7407, 304, 279, 3283, 315, 12095, 13, 362]`.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Keep zero MiniMax MXFP8 activation blocks finite
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Compute the finite reciprocal block scale in the fused MiniMax-M3 SwiGLU/MXFP8 kernel.
- Multiply by that reciprocal to avoid `0/0` when the byte-zero E8M0 divisor flushes to zero on CDNA, while preserving the encoded scale bytes.
- Reuse the existing mixed-magnitude/zero-block regression and the full AMD MiniMax kernel suite.

The MI355 parity run exposed NaNs in an all-zero activation block. Merged #53674 corrected the fused kernel’s scale formula but retained division by the decoded scale. The generic quantizer already uses reciprocal multiplication from merged #53110, and this change applies the same arithmetic to the fused path. Fresh searches and the related PR review found no open change covering this remaining fused-kernel defect.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with diagnosis, implementation and validation.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Register MRV2 sampler JIT warmups
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Register the existing top-k/top-p warmup providers in MRV2’s active registry on the last pipeline rank for generation models.
- Add a cold-cache ROCm regression that checks worker JIT monitoring is active in error mode and reuses the existing prefill, decode and sampling shape battery.
- Mirror the upstream No Runtime JITs E2E job through `mirror.amd`, overriding the ROCm command and runtime settings while inheriting parent file triggers; keep the matching optional MI355 legacy job and explicit engine cleanup.

MRV2 bypasses the V1 sampler constructor that normally registers these providers. The MI355 parity run consequently hit a sampling-kernel compilation during generation after warmup. Registering the existing providers fixes the dense native-path regression without changing sampling arithmetic. 

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation.

title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Support reload_weights with runai_streamer load format
author: viktorkou
body:
### Purpose

`GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` reloads weights from the checkpoint source through the configured model loader's `get_all_weights()`. Only `DefaultModelLoader` implements it. With `--load-format runai_streamer`, the documented sleep level 2 flow in `docs/features/sleep_mode.md`

```python
llm.sleep(level=2)                    # discard weights and KV cache, no host backup
llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"])
llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights")  # fails
llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])
```

fails at the reload step with `NotImplementedError: Model reloading with runai_streamer format`.

`reload_weights` originally called the loader's `load_weights()` (#20096), which every loader has. #32133 switched it to `get_all_weights()` so the runner can wrap `model.load_weights()` in the layerwise reload, gated on `hasattr(model_loader, "get_all_weights")`, and left `# TODO(@kylesayrs): generalize to all runners and loaders`. This PR is the loader half of that TODO for `runai_streamer`.

### Consequences

Sleep level 2 is unusable for engines started with the streamer. Level 1 works but keeps a full host-RAM copy of the weights, which is what level 2 exists to avoid. There is no supported way to load with the streamer and reload with the default loader. Checkpoints served from object storage (`s3://`, `gs://`, Azure Blob) cannot be reloaded at all: `VllmConfig.__post_init__` resolves `load_format=auto` to `runai_streamer` for these URIs and rejects other formats, so every object-storage user is affected, not only those who chose the streamer.

### Solution

**Loader.** Add `get_all_weights()` to `RunaiModelStreamerLoader`. It resolves the same source as `load_weights()` (`model_weights` when set, otherwise `model`, with `revision` passed through), and `load_weights()` now consumes it so the two paths cannot diverge. `reload_weights` then streams the checkpoint from local FS, NFS or object storage exactly as the initial load did.

**Runner.** Making the streamer reachable from `reload_weights` exposed a second gap, specific to object storage plus `weights_path`. `ModelConfig` keeps an object-storage model in two fields: `model_weights` holds the URI and `model` points at the temp directory of pulled config files. `reload_weights(weights_path=...)` rewrote `model` and reset `revision` but never touched `model_weights`, so the loader kept preferring the stale URI and silently re-streamed the original bucket. One line in `gpu_model_runner.py` clears `model_weights` in the same block that resets `revision`, for the same reason: both belong to the model being reloaded away from. `DefaultModelLoader` never reads the field, and a bare `reload_weights()` leaves both fields alone and still reloads the original bucket.

### Testing

All runs on an NVIDIA H200 NVL with `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0`, the loader and runner changes applied in place, each test run on the stock code first and then on the patched code.

| Test | Job | Stock | Patched |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_runai_get_all_weights_resolves_source[object_storage\|hf_repo]` (CPU, mocked iterator) | Model Executor | `AttributeError: no attribute 'get_all_weights'` | 2 passed |
| `test_runai_deep_sleep_reload_weights` (GPU) | Model Executor | `NotImplementedError` at the first reload | passed, whole directory 18 passed, 1 skipped |
| `test_runai_reload_weights_path_from_mocked_s3` (GPU, `StreamerPatcher`, no real S3) | Model Executor | fails at the `weights_path` step, parameter unchanged (relative diff 0.50) | 2 passed |
| `test_reload_weights_path_replaces_object_storage_source` (CPU, `Mock`) | v1/worker | `'s3://bucket/original' != ''` | passed |

- `test_runai_get_all_weights_resolves_source`: `get_all_weights` prefers `model_weights` when set, falls back to `model` when empty, and forwards `revision`.
- `test_runai_deep_sleep_reload_weights`: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B with sleep mode on, three cycles of `sleep(level=2)` → `wake_up(["weights"])` → `reload_weights(weights_path=...)` → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`: the multiply and add debug checkpoints must flip the perplexity ordering, and reloading the base checkpoint must reproduce the pre-sleep output byte for byte. GPU usage is bounded after each sleep and each reload step, mirroring `test_deep_sleep`. Not fork-isolated on purpose: in the Model Executor session CUDA is already initialised in the pytest process, and a forked child that touches CUDA fails with "Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess" (reproduced).
- `test_runai_reload_weights_path_from_mocked_s3`: engine started from `s3://my-mock-bucket/gpt2/` served from `tmp_path`, like the existing mocked-S3 test. A bare `reload_weights()` must re-stream the original bucket (tensor zeroed first), `reload_weights(weights_path="s3://my-mock-bucket/gpt2-mod/")` must load the second checkpoint (`ln_f.weight` scaled by 2), and a bare reload afterwards must reload the second checkpoint.
- `test_reload_weights_path_replaces_object_storage_source`: the runner hands the loader `(model=weights_path, model_weights="", revision=None)`. Kept alongside the integration test because the Model Executor job is not triggered by changes under `vllm/v1/worker`; this one runs in the v1/worker job.

End to end on the same H200 with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct` (BF16, 8 shards, 27.5 GiB): `sleep(level=2)`, `wake_up(["weights"])`, `collective_rpc("reload_weights")`, `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`, outputs byte-identical to pre-sleep over 20 cycles, `CuMemAllocator` confirming `0.00 GiB is backed up in CPU`. Against MinIO on the node, across two buckets: an engine started from `s3://vllm-models/qwen3-0.6b/` kept serving the original weights after `reload_weights(weights_path="s3://vllm-models-b/…")` on the stock runner, and matched an HF-started reference with the runner change; a bare `reload_weights()` reloaded the original bucket before the override and the new bucket after it, and the target prefixes held only `model.safetensors`.

### Performance Results

**Local XFS (virtio disk), cold reload after `sleep(level=2)`:**
- runai_streamer (this PR): 23.9 s, 22.4 s
- default loader, default heuristic (no prefetch on local FS): 112.7 s, 112.4 s
- default loader, `--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch`: 26.9 s, 26.7 s

**NFSv4.1, cold reload:**
- runai_streamer, default settings: 113.9 s, 98.8 s
- runai_streamer, `RUNAI_STREAMER_CONCURRENCY=8`, 8 MiB chunks: 89.3 s, 82.2 s
- default loader: 89.0 s, 63.3 s

**Object storage (MinIO on the node):** stock v0.29.0 fails at reload with `NotImplementedError` for both `--load-format runai_streamer` and `auto`; this PR reloads in 31.7 s and 30.6 s with identical outputs.

### Documentation

`docs/features/sleep_mode.md` already describes the level 2 + `reload_weights` flow; no change needed.

### AI Disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). All lines were reviewed by the submitter; the end-to-end runs above were executed and checked manually.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Dispatch the QuantFP8 CUDA fallback on the class
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

Three tests in `tests/kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py` fail in the
`(MI355) Core Operation Kernels` job:

```
FAILED test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-False] - IndexError: tuple index out of range
```

title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo: keep fused fp8 qkv_proj pairing state across weight-loading calls
author: vllmellm
body:
## Purpose
`XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` (and V2.5) produce degenerate output when using `--load-format fastsafetensors` or `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` when testing on Mi355x.  This issue should be platform-agnostic. 

## Root cause

MiMo's fused fp8 `qkv_proj` arrives as two checkpoint tensors (`weight` and `weight_scale_inv`) that must be sharded together, so `MiMoV2Model.load_weights` paired them in a dict and flushed only when both members arrived in the *same* call.

`AutoWeightsLoader._groupby_prefix` (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:260-274`) groups the stream with `itertools.groupby` on the first name component and calls a child's `load_weights` **once per contiguous run of `model.*`**. Any pair that straddles a group boundary therefore never flushes and both parameters are left uninitialised — zeros/NaN for the fp8 weight and `-inf` for its scale:

Instrumented load (`mimo_v2.py`), TP=2:

| loader | `layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight` | `…weight_scale_inv` |
|---|---|---|
| default | correct | correct |
| `--load-format fastsafetensors` | `sum=0` | `sum=-inf` |
| `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` | `sum=0`/`NaN` | `sum=-inf` |

`eager` fragments heavily because `safetensors.torch.load` returns a Rust `HashMap` (not file order). Nothing errored because weights tracking is disabled for quantized models (`default_loader.py:435-438`), hence gibberish tokens instead of a load failure.

## Fix

MiMo's fused fp8 `qkv_proj` arrives as two separate tensors — the weight and its scale — which have to be sharded together, so the loader holds the first one until the second shows up. That holding area was a local variable, and a local variable only lives for one call of `load_weights`; when the loader runs more than once (fastsafetensors, eager), a pair can be split across two calls, both tensors are dropped, and the attention projections are left empty.

Keep the holding area on the model instead (`mimo_v2.py`, and the same spot in `mimo_v2_mtp.py`), so a pair still completes no matter which call each half arrives in. Nothing in the loader itself is changed, so no other model is affected.

## Test Plan
Start serving with this, change model id to `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` and add `--load-format fastsafetensors` or `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` when testing the different case. 
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
  --tool-call-parser mimo \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser mimo
```

Test with lmeval, change model id to `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` for the mimo v2.5 test. 
```
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \  
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template
```

## Test Result

| case | result |
|---|---|
| MiMo V2.6, default loader |  gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97)  |
| MiMo V2.6, `--load-format fastsafetensors` | gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97) |
