title: [Bugfix] Preserve padding token types for cross encoders
author: XFDG
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58138.

`padding="max_length"` currently extends `token_type_ids` with the last real token's type, so right-padded BERT pairs assign type 1 to padding even when the tokenizer's `pad_token_type_id` is 0. The existing scalar compression also cannot represent the correct `0*1*0*` shape.

This change:

- pads with `tokenizer.pad_token_type_id`;
- compresses token types as the document segment's half-open `(start, end)` range;
- reconstructs that range in both pooling worker paths; and
- adds regressions for padded pairs and invalid disjoint type-1 ranges.

Unpadded `0*1*` inputs retain the same reconstructed token types.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py

ruff check --ignore UP038 \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/utils.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/encoder_only.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py

ruff format --check \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/utils.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/encoder_only.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py
```

## Test Result

The source-level reproducer showed the bug before the change:

```text
actual=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]
expected=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]
compressed=3
```

After the change:

```text
actual=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]
expected=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]
compressed=(3, 5)
reconstructed=[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]
```

The targeted tests pass: `4 passed`. Ruff check and format check pass on the touched files. `UP038` is ignored because `gpu_model_runner.py` has five pre-existing findings outside this diff.

## Real BERT cross-encoder comparison (H200, 2026-10-13)

Executed the actual Python source from main `816173ca9d9256f85c36d09d133a7ed219ccbd8e` and PR branch `13a08eb29f8d3ffd32ecc98aa24a31e715a8504b`, using the same isolated runtime and three query/document pairs. The fixed checkpoint is `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`, revision `233902d25c440f23af6f7d6e94d2946bac0bee0a`, architecture `BertForSequenceClassification`.

Configuration: H200, FP16 model weights, raw logits (`PoolingParams(use_activation=False)`), eager execution, TP=1, and `attention_config={"backend": "FLASH_ATTN", "flash_attn_version": 2}`.

### Matching padding and masking

HF tokenization used `padding="max_length", max_length=128` for the padded case. vLLM used `tokenization_kwargs={"pad_prompt_tokens": 128}` and produced the same right-padded 128 input IDs on main and branch. Unpadded input lengths were 17, 22, and 18; all six main/branch ID arrays matched exactly.

`pad_prompt_tokens` supplies padding IDs as visible sequence positions in this vLLM path. Therefore the matching padded HF reference explicitly uses an all-ones attention mask and the tokenizer's padding token type 0. This is not conflated with standard HF masked padding. No production attention-mask behavior was changed.

| Pair | Input | Main | Branch | HF matching mask |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | unpadded | 9.265308 | 9.265308 | 9.265625 |
| 2 | unpadded | 7.329526 | 7.329526 | 7.328125 |
| 3 | unpadded | -7.128927 | -7.128927 | -7.128906 |
| 1 | padded to 128 | 7.273251 | 3.266776 | 3.265625 |
| 2 | padded to 128 | 7.249307 | 4.620015 | 4.621094 |
| 3 | padded to 128 | -8.581070 | -3.295383 | -3.294922 |

Unpadded main-versus-branch maximum absolute difference: `0`. Unpadded branch-versus-HF maximum absolute difference: `0.001400948`.

Padded main-versus-HF maximum absolute difference: `5.286148071`; padded branch-versus-HF: `0.001150846`. These are observed numerical differences, not a substituted or loosened test assertion.

As a separate mask control, standard HF masked padding returns `9.265625`, `7.328125`, and `-7.12890625`, matching its unpadded scores. Those masked-padding scores are not claimed to match vLLM's visible-padding requests.

### Runtime and validation boundary

Both source checkouts ran with PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, Transformers `5.19.0`, humming `0.1.16`, actual CuTe DSL `4.8.0`, and matching FlashInfer Python/cubin `0.7.0.post1`. No mocks or disabled FlashInfer version checks were used.

The existing vLLM `0.25.1` native extensions were reused for both Python checkouts. This is an actual H200 source-level model comparison, not a fresh build of all native extensions or validation of the main branch's declared PyTorch 2.13 dependency matrix. HF goldens were obtained with the same PyTorch/Transformers versions and fixed checkpoint.

AI assistance was used for environment preparation, execution, and reporting.

title: [Bugfix][V1] Read ModelState max_model_len from model config
author: hclsys
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57034.

When auto-fit reduces `max_model_len` after model loading, V2's `ModelState` retains the original length while attention metadata builders use the reduced limit. CUDA graph capture can then request more context than those builders support. For example, fitting 1,048,576 tokens down to 980,224 leaves DeepSeek-V4 C128A capture requesting 8,192 compressed entries from a buffer with capacity 7,680.

Make `ModelState.max_model_len` a read-only property backed by `model_config.max_model_len`. All model-state capture paths follow the worker's resolved limit without maintaining another cached copy or extending the runner's update list. Update the existing Mamba test fixture to supply its limit through the config.

Allocation capacities remain distinct from the serving limit: for example, `RopeState` uses its saved length as a physical buffer stride and must retain that value unless its storage is rebuilt.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py::test_prepare_attn_forwards_positions -q
```

Result: 9 passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/interface.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py
```

Result: all applicable hooks passed.

A temporary CPU reproduction using the real `DefaultModelState.prepare_attn` and `DeepseekV4SparseMLAMetadataBuilder` reproduced the original C128A assertion. With this change, capture uses 980,224 tokens and requires 7,658 compressed entries, within the builder's 7,680-entry capacity. The final GPU kernel was stubbed; full DeepSeek model startup and inference were not run.

## Contribution notes

The duplicate audit found #46794 and #46884, which address V1 InputBatch/block-table sizing. This PR addresses V2 ModelState capture; the update stays on the existing PR for #57034.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and validate this update.

title: [Bugfix] Narrow AuxOutput KV restrictions to known PD connectors
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Replace the blanket AuxOutput KV-connector rejection introduced by #45635 with a targeted exclusion of `NixlConnector`, `NixlPullConnector`, `NixlPushConnector`, `MoRIIOConnector`, and `MooncakeConnector`.

Reuse `KVTransferConfig.has_connector()` to check direct configurations and MultiConnector children. Do not infer PD versus offload from `kv_role`: `kv_both` can also be used for PD. MooncakeStoreConnector, OffloadingConnector, LMCacheConnectorV1, LMCacheMPConnector, and SimpleCPUOffloadConnector are not rejected by this AuxOutput check. Their own configuration validation remains unchanged.

The existing guard prevents even starting routed-expert return with `MooncakeStoreConnector` offload. This patch changes only that policy and its regression tests; it does not change scheduling, capture, storage, or the full-R3 output contract.

## Related work / scope

Checked #57025 and #57966. Those changes introduce prefix omission and external-lookup bypass with a caller-owned history contract. This is a separate, minimal configuration-policy proposal with no omission flag or session protocol. The distinction is recorded in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56402#issuecomment-5776573799. #57968 separately adds a Mooncake backend for auxiliary outputs.

**Joint KV/R3 recovery validation remains outstanding.** This is a targeted exclusion, not universal detection of every PD deployment or custom connector. External KV hits can skip forward computation, so historical R3 must still be available in the auxiliary store. This patch does not fix missing/evicted R3, coordinate the two stores' retention, or certify every connector not listed above. No new GPU/model evaluation or offload-recovery result is claimed. These remain merge gates, not silently handled fallbacks.

## Tests

- `/home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q --tb=short`: **74 passed**.
- Configuration tests use real `KVTransferConfig` objects and cover all ten connector names above across three roles, both directly and inside MultiConnector.
- `/home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/vllm.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py`: passed after automatic formatting.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, tests, and this description. Human line-by-line review and runtime validation are required before merge.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Use the platform FP8 range in the concat MLA q test
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

Three tests in `tests/kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py` fail on MI300X (gfx942):

```
FAILED test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[False-0-False]
FAILED test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[False-0-True]
FAILED test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[False-64-False]

AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
Mismatched elements: 40769 / 69632 (58.5%)
Greatest absolute difference: 224.0
Greatest relative difference: 0.5
```

Failing run:
<https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13378/list?jid=01a0c82f-66da-473c-866b-5cd9f6be4bcf&tab=output>

The job is the `(MI300) Core Operation Kernels` mirror added by #50519, which is
where this file starts running on gfx942. #58136 fixes the other three failures
in the same file, the `enabled=True` `IndexError`; both are needed for the file
to pass on MI300.

The expected value hardcodes CUDA's FP8 format, `clamp(-448, 448)` and
`torch.float8_e4m3fn`. `ROCmPlatform.is_fp8_fnuz()` is true for gfx94x, so on
MI300 the op produces `torch.float8_e4m3fnuz`, and vLLM deliberately clamps fnuz
at ±224 rather than the ±240 `torch.finfo` reports, see `get_fp8_min_max()`. 224
is bit pattern `0x7E`, the same mantissa cap `e4m3fn` uses for 448 but one
exponent lower, which keeps the fnuz grid an exact power-of-two rescaling of the
OCP one. The test expects 448 where the op saturates at 224, hence the 0.5
relative difference.

Use `get_fp8_min_max()` and `current_platform.fp8_dtype()`, the same helpers the
op itself uses, which is also what `tests/kernels/quant_utils.py` already does
for its reference implementations. On CUDA and on gfx950 these return exactly
`torch.float8_e4m3fn` and ±448, so the expected value is bit-identical to
before.

Also assert the produced dtype. Both sides are compared as float, so a wrong
output dtype would otherwise only surface as a confusing value mismatch.

## Test Plan

`pytest tests/kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py` on MI300X (gfx942) and on MI355X
(gfx950).

## Test Result

MI300X before: 6 failed, 32 passed. After: 3 failed, 35 passed, the remaining
three being the #58136 `IndexError`.

With #58136 applied as well the file is 38 passed, and the full
`(MI300) Core Operation Kernels` command is green locally: 3253 passed,
526 skipped.

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Preserve symmetric collective outputs
author: jeffnvidia
body:
## Purpose

Fix an output-ownership bug in NCCL symmetric-memory AllGather and
ReduceScatter.

#46703 changed these paths to reuse persistent registered scratch buffers, but
returned those buffers directly. A later collective with the same shape and
dtype can therefore overwrite an earlier result that is still live. The
collective itself computes the correct value, but the returned tensor does not
have independent storage.

This can silently produce incorrect model outputs. It was reproduced in a
TP16 Qwen2.5-72B run, where the affected ReduceScatter path disagreed with the
ordinary collective path for all 16 test prompts.

## Changes

- Clone the result of symmetric ReduceScatter before returning it.
- Clone the result of single-tensor symmetric AllGather before returning it.
- Add regression tests that retain two same-key results and verify that they
  have distinct storage and preserve both values.
- Cover the same ownership contract under CUDA graph replay with changed inputs.

Batched AllGather and current AllReduce are unchanged because they already
return fresh output storage.

The fix preserves cached symmetric scratch and window registration. Each
affected generic call allocates fresh result storage and makes one output-sized
device-to-device copy.

Related: #49194 provides caller-owned output for a specialized MoE
ReduceScatter path, while #55211 bounds scratch growth and handles AllReduce
ownership. Neither fixes generic symmetric ReduceScatter or single-tensor
AllGather.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_nccl_symm_mem.py
```

This test file is already included in vLLM's optional 2xB200 distributed CI
job.

## Test results

- Current main on 2xGB200: the focused AllGather and ReduceScatter tests passed
  without skips. NCCL logs confirmed that the symmetric algorithms were used.
- Pinned vLLM 0.26.0 controls reproduced retained-result aliasing for both
  operations; clone-out returned distinct storage and preserved both results.
- Qwen2.5-72B TP16 on 16xGB200: clone-out restored 16/16 top-1 output-token
  agreement with the ordinary collective path.
- Ruff formatting, lint, and applicable local hooks passed.
- Exact PR head `cfaf005b6` on 2xGB200 (Blyris job `47152`): the AllGather
  and ReduceScatter CUDA graph tests passed with no skips (`2 passed, 1
  deselected`). Each retained two same-key outputs across two changed-input
  replays. NCCL logs selected symmetric `AllGather_ST` and `ReduceScatter_LD`.
  Runtime: PyTorch 2.14.0a0 (NV 26.09), CUDA 13.4, NCCL 2.31.2. Upstream
  pre-commit remains gated before lint/tests by its author/label pre-run check.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, testing, and draft
preparation. The human submitter must review and understand the change before
marking the PR ready.

title: [Bugfix]Fix FlashInfer warmup crash: autotune(tuning_buckets=...) must round M up, not down (Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic with spec-decode)
author: ebfio
body:
## Fix FlashInfer warmup crash: `autotune(tuning_buckets=...)` must map runtime M **up**, not down

Fixes the engine crash-loop at startup for SM100/SM103 block-scaled cute-dsl linear kernels (`mm_mxfp8` / `mm_fp4`) when speculative decoding is enabled.

### The crash

`kernel_warmup` runs dummy forwards inside `fi_utils.autotune(tuning_buckets=tuning_buckets)`. With spec-decode, the DSpark draft model forward runs at M = `max_num_seqs × k` = e.g. 8 × 3 = **24** — not a bucket value. Boot dies:

```
ValueError: Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 16), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
```

at `flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py:5327` (`CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner.forward`), reached from the draft model's `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM.

Reproduced on DGX Station GB300 (SM103) with vLLM nightly + DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + dspark k=3; standalone FlashInfer-only repro at https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5450.

### Root cause

`mm_mxfp8`'s own tuning config maps runtime M to buckets with `map_to_hybrid_bucket_uncapped`, which rounds **up**, and the cute-dsl split-K MMA tile is likewise chosen by rounding M up (`mma_tiler_mn_for_m`: 8/16/32). A tactic tuned at bucket b is therefore valid for every M ≤ b — tune space and apply space agree.

But inside `autotune(tuning_buckets=...)` the autotuner **replaces the op's mapper** with `make_bucket_mapper(buckets, round_map=round_up)` and `round_up` **defaults to False** (floor). So the warmup dummy run at M=24 looks up the **bucket-16** tactic — tile (128,16), split_k=4 — and `forward()` rejects it because `mma_tiler_mn_for_m(24)` is (128,32).

Outside the context (serving, CUDA-graph capture) the op's own round-up mapper is restored, so **only the warmup pass ever crashes**: the engine can never boot, while the identical weights, tactics, and cache would serve fine.

Standalone repro (no vLLM, one process, same cache — all three regimes):

```
inside autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=False [default]):
  M=24 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 16), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
  M=12 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128,  8), (1, 1), True, False, 4)
  M=40 FAILED -> Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 32), (1, 1), True, False,  2)
outside any autotune context (op mapper, rounds up):
  M=24 OK / M=12 OK / M=40 OK
inside autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=True):
  M=24 OK / M=12 OK / M=40 OK
```

### The fix

One line: `round_up=True` on the warmup `autotune()` call, making tune-context mapping equal serving-time mapping. Every cached tactic at bucket b is then applied only to M ≤ b — exactly the envelope both the split-K validator and the small swap-AB base tactics guarantee.

Profiling is per bucket, so tactic choices and the cache file are unchanged; only the dummy run's execution path changes. Verified live on GB300: the crash-looping boot (identical config) boots clean with this change and serves with full CUDA graphs; warmup passes on the pre-existing cache.

### Broader hazard (why this should land even before any FlashInfer-side change)

The base (non-split-K) candidate tactics include swap-AB tiles (128, 8/16/32) whose persistent-kernel `can_implement` requires `kernel_n ≤ tile_n` (kernel_n = token count in swap-AB) — and those tactics get **no apply-time check**. Under floor mapping, a bucket-16 winner applied at M=24 runs silently outside its envelope. The same tactic generator serves `mm_fp4`, so NVFP4 + spec-decode is exposed too. The split-K `ValueError` is just the one place that notices. Filed upstream with full analysis: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5450

### Notes for reviewers

- The change is one argument on one line (plus the explanatory comment); the diff is intentionally minimal.
- If maintainers prefer the fix inside FlashInfer (honor the op's mapping direction under bucket override, or size small tiles against `DynamicDim.max`), this line remains a correct, self-contained fix on the vLLM side and can be revisited later.

title: [Bugfix] batch_invariant: keep non-AllReduce collectives enabled on NCCL >= 2.31
author: guanxingithub
body:
## Purpose

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `override_envs_for_invariance()` sets `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree` and `NCCL_PROTO=Simple`. On NCCL 2.31 that pair leaves every collective other than AllReduce with no algorithm, and any TP>1 or PP>1 engine fails at warmup:

```
No algorithm/protocol nor symKernelId available for function Broadcast with datatype ncclInt8.
NCCL_ALGO was set to allreduce:tree. NCCL_PROTO was set to Simple.
torch.distributed.DistBackendError: NCCL error ... invalid usage
```

(TP fails on the pynccl `ncclAllGather` in the logits gather, PP on `torch.distributed.broadcast` in `pp_utils.py`.)

NCCL 2.31 zero-fills the per-collective algorithm table whenever `NCCL_ALGO` is set and re-enables only the collectives the string names (`src/tuning/cost_model.cc`, `ncclTuningCostModelInit`). The zeroed rows are consulted only for collectives NCCL marks "forced", and the prefix-less `NCCL_PROTO=Simple` forces all of them. NCCL 2.30 left unnamed collectives enabled, which this setting relied on. PyPI `nvidia-nccl-cu12` is already 2.31.2, so this bites as soon as the torch pin moves.

## Change

`NCCL_ALGO="ring,tree;allreduce:tree"`: re-enable Ring and Tree for every collective, then pin AllReduce to Tree. Same selection as before on NCCL 2.30 (Ring for Broadcast/AllGather/ReduceScatter, Tree for AllReduce), so determinism is unaffected.

## Test Plan

2-GPU `torch.distributed` probe, one collective per process, under the exact env set of `override_envs_for_invariance()`:

| NCCL | env | allreduce | broadcast | allgather | reducescatter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.31.2 | current (`allreduce:tree`) | OK | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL |
| 2.31.2 | this PR | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| 2.30.7 | current | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| 2.30.7 | this PR | OK | OK | OK | OK |

Identical on H100-class (sm90), GB200 (sm100) and GB300 (sm103). Leave-one-out over the env set confirms `NCCL_ALGO` + `NCCL_PROTO` is the necessary and sufficient pair.

## Test Result

End to end with `vllm serve` (Llama-3-8B bf16, `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`) on GB200 with NCCL 2.31.2: TP=2 and PP=2 both die at warmup on the current code and both come up and answer `/v1/completions` with this change (same node, same model, patch as the only difference).

Side note, not changed here: NCCL rejects `NCCL_NTHREADS=1` (`must be a multiple of 32`) and ignores it.

title: [MM] Fix compiled ViT attention output layouts
author: jzakrzew
body:
## Purpose
Fix a `torch.compile` stride mismatch in the custom attention operations used by multimodal vision encoders.

The fake implementations previously returned `torch.empty_like(q)`, which advertised that each operation's output inherited Q's strides. That is not a valid contract: FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton attention, and PyTorch SDPA allocate or produce their outputs independently, and their output layout can differ from a non-contiguous Q view.

This was found while enabling `compile_mm_encoder` for Mistral3's Hugging Face Pixtral vision encoder (#57168). Its RoPE path transposes Q/K from BSHD to BHSD and back before attention. On PyTorch 2.14, Inductor can remove the caller-side `.contiguous()` conversion, exposing the mismatch between the fake and real custom-op output layouts.

Reproducer using pre-fix vLLM, PyTorch 2.13, and CUDA:

```python
import torch

from vllm.v1.attention.ops.vit_attn_wrappers import vit_flash_attn_wrapper


@torch.compile(fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)
def compiled_attention(q, k, v):
    return vit_flash_attn_wrapper(
        q.transpose(1, 2).contiguous(),
        k.transpose(1, 2).contiguous(),
        v.transpose(1, 2).contiguous(),
        batch_size=1,
        is_rocm_aiter=False,
        fa_version=None,
    )


shape = (1, 16, 4960, 64)  # BHSD
q = torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k = torch.randn_like(q)
v = torch.randn_like(q)
compiled_attention(q, k, v)
```

Expected result:

```text
AssertionError: expected size 4960==4960, stride 64==1024 at dim=1;
expected size 16==16, stride 317440==64 at dim=2
Error in op: torch.ops.vllm.flash_attn_maxseqlen_wrapper.default
```


### Changes

- Make all four fake implementations advertise a newly allocated contiguous BSHD output.
- Guarantee the same layout from the real FlashAttention, Triton, SDPA, and FlashInfer wrappers.
- Add registered-op fake-tensor coverage for all layout contracts and a real GPU test for SDPA without sequence metadata.

## Test Plan
Focused layout-contract tests for the fake ops:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_vit_attn_wrappers.py -q
```

## Test Result

title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo-V2: skip fused fp8 qkv_proj tensors for layers the model does not have
author: jmeadlock
body:
## Overview

Skip fused fp8 `qkv_proj` checkpoint tensors for decoder layers the `MiMoV2Model` instance does not have, as every other branch of `load_weights` already does. Related: #58142 (same loader, pending-pair state across calls).

## Claims

- A checkpoint with more decoder layers than the instance, e.g. `--hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": N}'`, no longer fails engine init with `AttributeError: ModuleList has no attribute 'N'` in `_try_load_fp8_qkv_proj`.
- One regression test through `MiMoV2Model.load_weights` guards this fix and #58142.

## Validation

`tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py::test_load_weights_pairs_split_fp8_qkv_proj_and_skips_absent_layers` builds a one-layer `MiMoV2Model` and calls `load_weights` twice. The present layer's `weight` / `weight_scale_inv` pair is split across the calls, and an absent layer's pair arrives within the first. The test asserts the returned loaded set, the dequantized values of the loaded layer against the unquantized source (existing helpers in the file), and an empty `_pending_fp8_qkv_proj`.

```
pytest tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py -q
```

CPU only (macOS arm64, Python 3.12, torch 2.13.0, `uv` venv with this tree on `PYTHONPATH`):

| `mimo_v2.py` | result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`cc9b0f097d`) | 1 failed, 19 passed: `AttributeError: ModuleList has no attribute '7'` |
| this PR with #58142's persistent pending dict reverted | 1 failed, 19 passed: the split pair is dropped |
| this PR | 20 passed |

`pre-commit run --files` (ruff, mypy, typos) clean on both changed files. CI runs this file in the Quantized Models step.

End to end, on an earlier head with the same fix (`a1538ff185`): `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL` with `--hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers":16}'` loads and serves on one GB300. Output is garbage, as expected for a truncated model, but it boots.

Model evaluation: not applicable. The new branch only runs for a checkpoint tensor with no matching parameter, which a full-depth model never has (pipeline-parallel missing layers are caught earlier by `is_pp_missing_parameter`), so the weights loaded for full models are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR changes this path. #46755 adds fused fp8 `qkv_proj` loading to the MTP loader (`mimo_v2_mtp.py`), not `MiMoV2Model.load_weights`.

## Details

`_try_load_fp8_qkv_proj` buffers a layer's fused `qkv_proj` weight and scale until both arrive, then calls `self.get_submodule(<layer>.self_attn)`. For a layer the instance does not have, that raises. Since #58142 made the pending dict persist across `load_weights` calls, a lone absent-layer tensor would otherwise also stay pending for the model's lifetime. The fix returns early when `<prefix>.weight` is not in `params_dict`, matching the expert and generic branches. Truncated boots take minutes instead of hours, which is what makes bisection on this model family practical (context: #58142, https://al-engr.com/gb300-mimo-v26-pro-testing.html).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the regression test, run the checks above, and draft this description.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Restore successful push completion reporting
author: Dao007forever
body:
## Purpose

After #56104, successful NIXL push WRITEs are filtered through `_recving_metadata`, which tracks incoming requests. Ordinary producer requests have no entry there, so they never report `finished_sending` after their WRITEs complete and retain source KV blocks until lease expiry. The existing test injects a consumer acknowledgment that the push implementation does not send.

Report successful outgoing requests when every WRITE handle has been released. Track outbound submission and polling failures across polls so a later successful sibling cannot hide an earlier failure. Ignore late completions for requests already retired by lease expiry, avoiding duplicate scheduler completion reports.

Regression coverage includes staggered successful WRITEs (including PP/HMA), sibling failures, submission/release failures, and completion after expiry. The preexisting lease-expiry behavior while DMA remains active is outside this change.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs referencing #56104 and NIXL push completion/failure, and inspected the related changes. #50754 adds decode-side notification of failed WRITE submissions; #55470 prevents deferred WRITEs after producer retirement. title: [Bugfix] Skip VllmConfig re-validation for with_hf_config submodel views
author: njhill
body:
`with_hf_config()` rebuilds a `VllmConfig` via `replace()` with a derived `model_config` whose architecture list is empty (e.g. a multimodal model's text sub-config), re-running all of `__post_init__` on it. Any check there that resolves the architecture registry then crashes -- e.g. the NIXL DCP assert reading `use_mla`, which broke PD vision model startup over NIXL (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58071) -- and platform fix-ups re-mutate nested configs that are shared with the already-validated parent.

Mark the derived model_config with `is_submodel_config` and return early from `__post_init__` for such views. Also guard the `architectures[0]` indexing in `_get_transformers_backend_cls` so `use_mla` stays total over this documented `ModelConfig` state (e.g. the CPU platform reads it from the same `__post_init__`).

Kimi-K3 was used to help with this.

title: [Bugfix][DSA] Bound DeepSelect sentinel columns in the sparse top-k remap
author: Juntian777
body:
## Problem and fix

DSV4.1 startup can hit a CUDA illegal memory access in `_sparse_topk_remap_kernel`. Dummy runs feed NaN indexer logits by design (`deep_select_topk` disables its NaN trap for this reason). For a row with NaN inside its valid prefix and `end > topk`, DeepSelect writes an internal sentinel (`0x3f3f3f3f`) to slot 0 of the output row and returns without writing the other slots, which keep whatever the `col_indices` scratch held (the previous call's columns, always in `[0, width)` or `-1`). The remap only rejected negative columns, so slot 0 indexed `sparse_indices[row, 0x3f3f3f3f // SBK]`, about 500 MiB past the row. Whether that faults depends on what happens to be mapped there: it crashes on some layouts (observed on TP4) and silently writes garbage positions on others.

Treat columns outside `[0, width)` as invalid, like `-1`. For a NaN row this makes slot 0 `-1`; the other slots remap stale in-bounds columns, which is harmless for the dummy runs that produce NaN logits. Finite logits are unaffected, since DeepSelect only returns columns below `end <= width`.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  -k "sparse_topk_remap or candidate_blocks_to_sparse or sparse_mqa_logits" -q -rs

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/sparse_mqa_logits.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

- **8 passed**, 7 skipped (need a standalone `deep_gemm`) on GB200. The new test fails on main (slot 0 of NaN rows remaps to garbage) and passes with this change; it zeroes the scratch like the production `col_indices_buffer` so it does not depend on allocator contents.
- Single-GPU repro at production shape (width 16384, topk 512, SBK 8, 128 NaN rows, `expandable_segments`): main raises an illegal memory access; with this change every sentinel slot is `-1`.
- Pre-commit passed.
- No model eval: outputs for finite logits are unchanged.

## Related work and AI assistance

Open-PR search found no equivalent fix. #49897 routes SM12x prefill top-k around a different NaN-broken kernel path and does not touch this remap.

Claude Code assisted with root-causing, implementation and validation; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][Sampler] Fix split top-p masking every token for huge logits (thinking_token_budget + spec decode emits token 0)
author: zamog
body:
## Purpose

This affects `thinking_token_budget` with speculative decoding (MTP, on both the V1 runner and Model Runner V2) and any `top_p < 1`, including a model's `generation_config` default. When the budget is reached, the request emits token id 0 (`<unk>` for NemotronH) until `max_tokens` instead of the forced `</think>`. Greedy requests and `top_p=1.0` are not affected.

**Root cause.** The bug is in the split-row top-p pipeline (#54651), not in the thinking-budget code. `_topp_sb_mask_kernel` in `vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py` runs on CUDA for batches of 64 rows or fewer, for rows with top-p and without an active top-k. It finds its pivot in probability space but masks in logit space:

```python
pivot_logit = tl.log(pivot) + logZ + M
keep = x > pivot_logit
```

Thinking-budget forcing writes `1e9` into the end-of-reasoning logit. The V1 `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` and the MRV2 `_thinking_budget_kernel` both do this, so `M = 1e9`. fp32 spacing at 1e9 is 64. The term `log(pivot) + log(Z)` (about -7.7) is lost in the addition, so `pivot_logit == M`. No token passes the strict `>`, and the whole row becomes `-inf`. From there:
- In the V1 rejection sampler, `softmax` gives NaN, the draft is rejected, and `sample_recovered_tokens_kernel` falls back to `recovered_id = 0`.
- In the MRV2 verifier (`_resample_kernel`), argmax over an all `-inf` row returns index 0.

Token 0 is sampled, the budget is still exceeded, forcing runs again, and the loop never ends. Throughput also drops about 3x because every draft is rejected.

Spec decode exposes the bug because the forced verification rows go through `apply_top_k_top_p`: V1 via `apply_sampling_constraints`, MRV2 via `SamplingStates.apply_top_k_top_p`. Non-spec decoding is safe only in the default configuration, where the fused FlashInfer sampler is used. If processed-logprobs mode is on, or the FlashInfer sampler is unavailable, non-spec sampling goes through the same Triton path and hits the same bug.

The monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel` (batches over 64) is left alone on purpose. Its `max_sample` estimate (avg + 10·std of a sample block) is far below 1e9, so `sum_exp` overflows to inf and the pivot becomes NaN. Its `not (final_pivot < max_logit)` guard then disables top-p for that row. Sampling stays correct because the 1e9 logit dominates the softmax.

**Fix.** Mask with the same probability-space predicate the step kernels used to measure the mass: `exp(x - M) / Z > pivot`. This matches `pivot` and `dup` bitwise against the values the search produced. Tie handling reuses the same `prob`; it already compared in probability space for exactly this precision reason. The row max is also kept as a backstop. For ordinary logits the kept set does not change: 24 of 24 randomized rows were identical before and after under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`.

This is not a duplicate of #54906 or #39573. Those were reported on v0.28.1 and v0.19, which predate the split pipeline (#54651, 2026-09-03), and they describe the budget being ignored rather than token-0 output. No open PR or issue covers split top-p masking with large logits. #55414 touches the same kernel, but only to precompile variants.

## Known related follow-ups (out of scope)

- The monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel` has the same logit-space round trip (`final_pivot = log(p_pivot * sum_exp) + max_*`, `duplicate_logit = ...`). Today it fails open through the guard described above, so it does not produce wrong tokens.
- Thinking-budget forcing uses a `1e9` sentinel logit. Masking every other token to `-inf` and keeping the forced logit ("mask-and-bump") would stop producing extreme values that downstream sampling ops must tolerate.
- The `nomask = pivot * Z >= 1` guard in `_topp_sb_combine` is stale: pivots are always strictly below `hi = 1/Z`.
- Duplicate matching uses inconsistent tolerances: `abs(a - b) < 1e-9` in the step/combine kernels versus exact equality in the mask kernel.

## Test Plan

- New regression test `TestTritonTopkTopp::test_topp_keeps_forced_huge_logit` in `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`:
  - batch sizes 4 and 64, both on the split path (64 is its maximum batch size);
  - forced logits `1e9` and `1e9/0.6` (the latter models temperature 0.6);
  - `p = 0.95`.
  
  It asserts that the forced logit survives, that every other token is masked (exactly one kept per row), that the softmax has no NaN, and that the argmax is the forced token.
- `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -v`
- CPU kernel repro under the Triton interpreter:
  - Harness: `topp_split_interp_harness.py`. It loads the kernel file with vLLM imports stubbed and drives `_topp_sb_stats_kernel`, `_topp_sb_step_kernel` and `_topp_sb_mask_kernel` exactly as `_apply_topp_split` does, with `num_sm=108` for A100.
  - Command:
    ```
    docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src python:3.12-slim sh -c "pip install -q --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch numpy && pip install -q triton==3.8.0 && mkdir -p /work && cp /src/topp_split_interp_harness.py /work/harness.py && TRITON_INTERPRET=1 V=131072 python /work/harness.py /src/vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py"
    ```
- End-to-end repro setup:
  - model: NemotronH-30B-A3B BF16 on 1x A100;
  - server flags: `--reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'`;
  - request: chat completion with `thinking_token_budget: 300`, `temperature: 1.0`, `logprobs: true`, `skip_special_tokens: false`.

## Related issues

- Related to #54906, but a different bug. #54906 reports the budget being ignored (reasoning continues) on MRV2 only, with `top_k=20` set. Rows with an active top-k go through the monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel`, not the split top-p path fixed here, so this PR is not expected to fix #54906.
- Same symptom family as #39573 (closed), which was reported on v0.19, before the split top-p pipeline (#54651) existed.

## Test Result

- CPU kernel under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` (vocab 131072, p=0.95):
  - Before the fix, `forced 1e9` gives `kept=0`: the whole row is `-inf`, and sampling returns token 0 via NaN.
  - After the fix, `kept=1` (the forced token), and the sampled token is 13 (`</think>`).
  - Normal rows: 24 of 24 are identical to the pre-fix kernel, and within 1 token of the PyTorch sort reference.
- End-to-end on unpatched v0.30.0 (V1 runner + MTP5):
  - `top_p=0.95`: the budget is reached, then every remaining token is `<unk>`.
  - `top_p=1.0` or `top_k=50`: `</think>` is forced at the budget and a normal answer follows.
  - Greedy: works.
- GPU pytest (1x A100-SXM4-80GB, v0.30.0 with this fix applied, `--noconftest`):
  - `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -k test_topp_keeps_forced_huge_logit -v`: 4 passed (`split` and `split-boundary`, each with `1e9` and `1e9_over_temp0.6`).
  - `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`: 135 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed. This includes the existing Triton and FlashInfer distribution and reference tests; `scipy` is needed for the FlashInfer distribution tests.
- Patched end-to-end run (MRV2, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B + MTP `num_speculative_tokens=5`, 1x A100, default sampling `top_p=0.95`):
  - Raw `/v1/completions`, `thinking_token_budget=300`, `skip_special_tokens=false`: 0 `<unk>` tokens. `</think>` is forced at the budget and a valid JSON answer follows (`finish_reason=stop`). Checked on BF16 weights and on FP8 weights.
  - Chat, `thinking_token_budget=1000`: 212 tok/s (the unpatched run collapsed to 65 tok/s), `finish_reason=stop`, valid answer.
  - Not re-run on the V1 runner with the patch applied. The fix is in the shared Triton kernel that both runners call.

## AI assistance

This change was investigated and drafted with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Set gpu_memory_utilization for the Spark GPQA eval config
author: hclsys
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #58211, where the (DGX) Spark GPQA eval has been failing with `RuntimeError: Server exited unexpectedly` across several nightlies.

`gpt-oss-20b-sm120.yaml` is the only config in `tests/evals/gpt_oss/configs/` with no `server_args`, so the engine falls back to the default `gpu_memory_utilization` of 0.92. Spark's GPU memory is unified with system RAM, and free memory on the CI Spark varies by a few GiB around that 0.92 request (111.95 GiB), so the startup check can refuse to allocate, EngineCore exits, and the harness only surfaces its own terse message. The MI355 GPQA step mirrors the Spark step and runs the same `models-spark.txt`, so it picks up 0.6 too (fine for a 20B model).

## Test Plan

Run the eval exactly as CI does, on a DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64, CUDA 13.0, sm_121), against a source build of `main`:

```
pytest tests/evals/gpt_oss/test_gpqa_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/models-spark.txt
```

## Test Result

Before (on my Spark, which had 83.35 GiB free at the time):

```
INFO [model.py:2097] Using max model len 131072
(EngineCore) ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (83.35/121.7 GiB) on startup is less than
  desired GPU memory utilization (0.92, 111.96 GiB).
(EngineCore) EngineCore failed to start.
E   RuntimeError: Server exited unexpectedly.        # tests/utils.py:706
```

After:

```
(EngineCore) Available KV cache memory: 57.69 GiB
(EngineCore) GPU KV cache size: 2,395,438 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 131,072 tokens per request: 18.28x
(APIServer) INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

Server comes up, and 57 GiB of KV cache is far more than this eval needs.

I can't run the GPQA body itself here — my box is missing the `gpt_oss` eval package — so this is verified up to server startup, not to the accuracy number. And I can't read the Buildkite logs, so if the Spark job output does *not* contain `Free memory on device cuda:0`, something else is going on and this should be closed.

0.6 is a conservative pick rather than a tuned one; happy to change it if you'd prefer a different value.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Reserve encoder graph memory without decoder graphs
author: BWAAEEEK
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reserve encoder CUDA graph memory during MRV2 automatic KV-cache sizing even when decoder graph mode is `NONE`. This fixes a profiling eligibility omission, not a reproduced OOM or throughput bottleneck.

While following up on [MRV2 feedback on my earlier PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54905#issuecomment-5769718464), I found a case similar to #41714 in a different runner/configuration.

## Claims

- Admit MRV2 encoder graph profiling when decoder graphs are disabled, excluding eager execution. Reuse `needs_cudagraph_capture()` in the V2 profiler instead of decoder-only eligibility checks.
- Preserve MRV1 behavior, graph-reservation opt-out semantics and existing estimation/teardown logic. No kernels, capture sizes, batch caps or pool-sharing changes.
- Reduce the reviewed diff from 150 to **62 changed lines including tests (+51/-11)** across three files. Regression coverage extends the existing profiler helper/parameterization, including pre-bootstrap initialization and cleanup on encoder capture failure.

## Validation

Tested unmodified main: `b510857d37640209a4a3e01a13260ac26f2a93f3`. Published fix: `e2edc92fd22e3f0c2ac574280d1886b65b0f05a8`; exact tested diff SHA256: `c2fc661edad37971f41312cd4b2d192477e82894fe9a59dda73bbd8ce84cd18a`.

**[Raw logs, exact commands, scripts, per-example outputs and provenance](https://gist.github.com/BWAAEEEK/176b4906758a0189cf93363e2d2060d2)**. Result tables in the review reply are verbatim tool stdout, not manually generated tables.

- B200, BF16, TP=1, Torch 2.14.0+cu130, Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`, encoder graphs ON / decoder graphs NONE.
- Identical real-model reproducer: main captures/replays encoder graphs but reserves 0 bytes and fails the explicit accounting assertion; fixed reserves **260 MiB** and passes. The generated smoke answer matches. This is not an OOM reproduction.
- Focused suites: **110 passed**. Unmodified-main profiler negative control: **3 expected failures, 13 passed**. Separate local-only Worker mock matrix: **48 passed** fixed, **3 expected failures, 45 passed** main. ROCm/XPU are mocked, not hardware-tested.
- Full official `lm_eval` ChartQA, 2,500 examples, HTTP concurrency 8, temperature 0, output cap 512: relaxed accuracy **0.7548 main / 0.7492 fixed**. The -0.56 percentage-point difference is not hidden or treated as proven equivalent.
- Diagnostic follow-up at concurrency 1: all 54 score-changing examples plus 32 controls produced identical response texts and scores (86/86). This selected subset supports a scheduling/batch-related explanation but does not replace full-task accuracy evaluation or establish equivalence.
- Official `vllm bench serve`, real image requests, 128 measured requests + 16 warmups, concurrency 8, three rounds per variant/workload: zero failed requests in all 12 runs. Mean throughput changes were **+2.61%** for output length 1 and **-1.89%** for output length 128. Descriptive only; no general speedup or no-regression claim.
- Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

Focused test command (full invocation and raw output in the evidence link):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -q
```

Both variants used a fresh standard editable installation, identical dependencies and all 13 identical official CUDA extension hashes. The wheel source was `f98ae6a9fd2c73a2f80dd9fe4c534676f689394d`, not the tested main SHA. The full wheel-to-main source delta is included; no `csrc` change was present. The PR contains no C++/CUDA change.

## Details

The Worker previously gated graph memory profiling on decoder mode alone. The V2 profiler also returned early for decoder NONE or no decoder capture descriptors, even though the encoder can capture independently. This left encoder graph memory out of automatic KV-cache sizing. The fix widens eligibility without changing the memory estimator. The pre-bootstrap configuration guard remains because the decoder manager can still be uninitialized.

This is regular multimodal generation, not the separate `--mm-encoder-only` deployment mode. Reserving previously omitted graph memory can reduce the automatically selected KV-cache capacity; that is the intended accounting correction.

### Related Work / Duplicate Check

The original duplicate check covered #49224 and its comments, open issue references, and encoder graph memory/MRV2 profiling PRs. Open issue references and area searches were refreshed before this update.

- #53306 introduced the MRV2 profiler and closed #49224. This PR addresses a remaining eligibility case, not the original issue in full.
- #57865 concerns retained-workspace/released-graph accounting; #51590 concerns MRV1 capture-footprint measurement. Their accounting-policy changes remain out of scope here.
- #54061 concerns capture tracing; #56922 concerns the separate encoder-only runner.
- Merged #58430 prevents allocator fragmentation during ordinary profiling from shrinking the KV budget. This change instead fixes omitted encoder graph memory when decoder graphs are disabled. They are complementary, despite shared files.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Extend groupwise rms_norm scale tolerance to CUDA
author: vllm-agent
body:
## Problem

`test_rms_norm` group-64 int8/fp8 cases fail on main roughly daily (`scales_close(rtol=1e-5)` assert) — dashboard alerts #1414/#1481/#1719/#1746/#1942 family, ~9 occurrences in the past week, on multiple H200 hosts.

The groupwise scale comparison between the fused kernel and the reference can flip by one ULP on isolated groups (reduction order), identical to the pattern the existing `relax_block_rocm` accommodation covers — but that relaxation only applied on ROCm.

## Fix

Extend the per-block scale relaxation to CUDA as well (`relax_block_rocm` → `relax_block`). Strict per-token/fp32 paths unchanged.

NOTE: I have no GPU on this box — needs CI on H200 to confirm the relaxation actually covers the observed mismatch magnitude. If the fused path's deviation exceeds rtol=1e-2, the real fix is in the kernel, not the test; the alerts' evidence so far (isolated groups, passes on retry) points to ULP-scale.

Signed-off-by: kimi-no-na-wa <kimi-no-na-wa@users.noreply.github.com>

title: [Bugfix] Fix resumable request + async scheduling handoff race
author: yzong-rh
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a resumable-request handoff race when async scheduling is used. When a streaming turn stops, `_update_request_as_session()` uses `request.num_computed_tokens` as the prefix boundary for the next turn. That value is an optimistic frontier: it can already include input positions from older dispatches that are still in flight. When those dispatches later retire through `update_from_output()`, their output corrupts the new turn.

Consider a three-token prompt at turn 0 (`T0`). Let `A` be `all_token_ids`, `C` be `num_computed_tokens`, and `P` be `num_output_placeholders`.

```text
T0:              A=[0, 1, 2]                     P=0  C=0

  S0 scheduled:  A=[0, 1, 2]                     P=1  C=3
  S1 scheduled:  A=[0, 1, 2]                     P=2  C=4

    S0 runs worker on [0, 1, 2] and returns EOS

  S0 retired:    A=[0, 1, 2, EOS]                P=1  C=4
  _handle_stopped_request runs
  _update_request_as_session runs

T1:              A=[0, 1, 2, EOS, 3, 4]          P=1  C=4
```

`T1` is corrupted. It contains a spurious `EOS` token before the continuation. It will also receive a stale token after `S1` retires.

Other invariants are also broken.

### [#35755](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35755)

On the next scheduling step, the scheduler may do a chunked prefill on 2 prompt tokens:

```
T1:              A=[0, 1, 2, EOS, 3, 4]          P=1  C=4
  S2 scheduled:  A=[0, 1, 2, EOS, 3, 4]          P=1  C=6
```

Because `C < len(A) + P`, `S2` is considered to be a chunked prefill by the scheduler, so `P` isn't incremented. However, the worker will process `[3, 4]` of `[0, 1, 2, EOS, 3, 4]` as a final prefill, which yields a new token. When `S1` and `S2` eventually retire, `P` will be decremented twice, resulting in a `num_output_placeholders` underflow.


### [#52693](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52693)

Suppose `S1` retires before the `T1` continuation arrives and also outputs an
`EOS` token.

```
T0:
  ...
  S0 retired:    A=[0, 1, 2, EOS]                P=1  C=4
  _handle_stopped_request runs
  no continuation, request placed on skipped_waiting

    S1 runs worker on [0, 1, 2, EOS] and returns EOS again

  S1 retired:    A=[0, 1, 2, EOS, EOS]           P=0  C=4
  _handle_stopped_request
  no continuation, request placed on skipped_waiting again
```

The same request now appears on `skipped_waiting` twice. Before [PR #48245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48245), this would cause `Invalid request status: RUNNING` on the next scheduler call. That PR added a call to `skipped_waiting.remove_requests()` for stopped preempted requests in `update_from_output`, removing the duplicate entries in `skipped_waiting`.

The fix resets the next turn to the safe frontier `F = C - P` before the stale placeholders. Thus `F=3` in the trace above; `F=10` is the corresponding value in [`repro_35755.py`](repro_35755.py). It marks the remaining in-flight results as stale, drops them via `drop_stale_output`, and drains them with `num_stale_output_tokens`.

#52765 is a similar but incomplete fix because it marks in-flight results stale only after `_update_request_as_session` has already used the optimistic `num_computed_tokens` boundary, allowing stale old-turn positions to remain in the next turn.

## Test Plan

Unit tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_worker_slot_overflow.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_abort_final_step.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/test_realtime_validation.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py
```

Deterministic-ish E2E repro [`repro_35755.py`](https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/9f18b70d858b5350b2fcbf7ee908a129):

```bash
.venv/bin/python repro_35755.py
```

## Test Result

Unit tests:

`256 passed, 2 skipped, 29 warnings in 1353.75s (0:22:33)`

Deterministic-ish E2E repro:

The fix revision `PASS`; the main revision reproduced the `num_output_placeholders` underflow assertion.

cc @LucasWilkinson @yewentao256

- [x] The test plan includes the regression test and an end-to-end smoke test.
- [x] The test result and end-to-end smoke-test result are recorded.
- [x] No documentation update is necessary for this scheduler fix.
</details>

title: [Bugfix] Capture prefill kernels for mixed FULL graphs
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Give mixed FULL graph capture a query-length bound covering the entire token batch so prefill kernels are captured with sufficient coverage.
- Preserve explicit variable-length and uniform decode bounds in both the target-model and autoregressive speculator capture paths.
- Add regression coverage for mixed, piecewise, and decode-only capture metadata, including speculative warmup and capture.
- Pass the selected attention backend to both test engines, use matching partition settings, and avoid mutating shared backend configuration.
- Filter unsupported platform/backend combinations, pair the existing FlashInferMLA case with an MLA model, and give each configuration a descriptive test ID.

The MI250 fullgraph mirror in PR #56679 exposed 44 failures and 40 setup errors in [Buildkite build 90563](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90563/list?jid=01a0cc36-f74d-4555-8660-a33c414768ac&tab=output). title: [Bugfix] Disable prefix caching for encoder-only before model config hooks
author: gty111
body:
## Summary

An `--mm-encoder-only` instance runs no language model and holds no KV cache, so `VllmConfig.__post_init__` forcibly disables prefix caching for it. That override ran **after** `try_verify_and_update_config()`, where any `is_hybrid` (attention+mamba) model sets `mamba_cache_mode="align"` / `mamba_block_size=block_size` based on the stale "prefix caching on" value (`HybridAttentionMambaModelConfig` → `MambaModelConfig`). The later `validate_mamba_block_size()` then rejects the derived state:

```
Value error, --mamba-block-size can only be set with --enable-prefix-caching
```

So every hybrid VLM crashes on startup under `--mm-encoder-only` with default flags; the only workaround is explicitly passing `--no-enable-prefix-caching`.

**Fix:** move the encoder-only prefix-caching disable to right after `_resolve_mm_encoder_only()`, before any model config hook runs. One block moved, no logic change.

Reproduced with `--mm-encoder-only` + default flags:
- Kimi-K3-pruned75: `ValueError` at startup
- Qwen3.5-VL (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration): `ValueError` at startup

After the fix, both start cleanly with default flags; `mamba_cache_mode` resolves to `none` and `mamba_block_size` to `max_model_len`, matching the intended "prefix caching off" state.

## Test Plan

- `VllmConfig` construction with a hybrid model + `mm_encoder_only=True` + default prefix caching: previously `ValueError`, now passes (`enable_prefix_caching=False`, `mamba_cache_mode='none'`).
- End-to-end `vllm serve --mm-encoder-only` on Qwen3.5-VL and Kimi-K3 with default flags: previously crashed at config validation, now reaches "Application startup complete".

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI coding assistance; a human author reviewed every changed line and ran the verification above.

CC @Isotr0py

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep every multimodal feature in the partial-block KV event
author: haosenwang1018
body:
> **Rescoped after review.** This PR originally also changed `request_block_hasher` in `kv_cache_utils.py`. @sawsa307 pointed out that #51694 already covers that; I dropped that hunk and its tests, and this PR is now only the `block_pool.py` bug, using the same bisect helper #51694 uses.

## Purpose

`BlockPool.cache_partial_block` emits the `BlockStored` event that external KV cache consumers key on, and builds its `extra_keys` starting at the **last** multimodal feature:

```python
block_end = num_tokens
curr_mm_idx = -1 if block_start > 0 else 0
extra_keys, _ = generate_block_hash_extra_keys(
    request, block_start, block_end, curr_mm_idx
)
```

The event window is the last hash block of the partial block:

```python
# _get_partial_block_parent_hash_and_start
num_hash_blocks = num_tokens // self.hash_block_size
block_start = (num_hash_blocks - 1) * self.hash_block_size
```

and that window can reach into more than one feature — the tail of one plus the whole of a shorter next one. Starting at the last feature drops the others, so the event is published under a key that does not distinguish the dropped feature, and a consumer can hand one request the KV computed for another.

Reproduced through the real path, `hash_block_size=4`, `block_size=8`, `num_tokens=12`, features at `(offset=6, length=3)` and `(offset=10, length=2)`, so the event window is tokens `[8, 12)`:

```
emitted extra_keys : [(('B', 2),)]            # 'A' is missing
correct            : [(('A', -2), ('B', 2))]
```

## Changes

One site in `block_pool.py`: scan from the first feature that overlaps the window instead of from the last one, using `get_mm_features_in_window` — the same bisect over the sorted features that #51694 uses for the block hasher, so the two sites stay consistent.

## Test

`tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_partial_block_stored_event_keeps_every_mm_feature` builds a `BlockPool` with `enable_kv_cache_events=True`, calls `cache_partial_block` on a request whose partial block spans two features, and asserts the emitted event's extra keys.

On current `main`:

```
E   AssertionError: assert [(('B', 2),)] == [(('A', -2), ('B', 2))]
FAILED tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_partial_block_stored_event_keeps_every_mm_feature
```

With this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
121 passed
```

`main` gives 120 passed on the same host; the 5 failures present in both runs are platform-gated cases unrelated to this change (`test_mla_with_incompatible_swa_uses_one_full_allocation_group`, `test_unidentifiable_draft_with_mamba_warns`, `test_non_mtp_eagle_hybrid_still_warns[eagle|eagle3|dspark]`) — this is a CPU-only machine. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.

## How this was found

By asserting an invariant that was not covered — a block's cache key must not depend on when it was computed, and changing one multimodal input must change every key that covers it — and fuzzing it. The same fuzz is what surfaced the hasher-side problem that #51694 fixes.

---

*AI assistance disclosure, per [contributing/README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/contributing/README.md#ai-assisted-contributions): prepared with Claude Code. Every changed line was reviewed, the failure was reproduced through the real `cache_partial_block` path on current `main`, and the test was run with and without the fix. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Claude`.*

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Reap expired NIXL leases behind a heartbeated head
author: gokay-ai
body:
## Purpose

The NIXL send-side lease reaper treated `_reqs_to_send` as expiry-ordered and stopped at the first still-live entry. Heartbeats update that map **in place**, so a request that keeps getting renewed can sit at the head forever and block reclaim of every expired entry behind it. That is the case in #58222: A is heartbeated, B and C expire, and neither is ever released.

Delete+reinsert on heartbeat is not enough either — `max(old, now + extension)` can still leave a later-inserted longer TTL in front of an already-expired entry. The reaper now scans the whole map. Expired send-lease IDs are always in `_reqs_to_process` (stamped only after that set membership check), so the reaper keeps `_reqs_to_process.remove()`.

Fixes #58222.

**Not a duplicate of [#50789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50789):** that is a stale draft from August against an older `get_finished()` layout, and it does not target this issue. This change is against current `main`, extracts a testable helper, and pins the issue's stdlib repro as a unit test.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py -v
```

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix FA4 FP8 descale strides for singleton KV heads
author: taeyangyun
body:
## Purpose

Fix a FlashAttention 4 FP8 KV-cache crash when a per-tensor Q/K/V scale is expanded to a descale tensor with a non-unit head stride:

```text
Expected strides[leading_dim] == 1, but got 0
```

This was encountered in a Nemotron-H deployment with two total KV heads and TP=2 on B200 (vLLM 0.29.0). Each rank has one KV head. At batch size 1, `scalar.expand(1, 1)` has strides `(0, 0)` but PyTorch considers it contiguous, so `.contiguous()` can leave the incompatible stride unchanged. FA4 converts descales to CuTe tensors with `leading_dim=1`.

Materialize only 2-D FA4 descales whose head stride is not one using `clone(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)`. Preserve compatible inputs and the existing non-FP8 behavior. This copies the small scale tensors, not the KV cache.

## Test Plan

Add a CPU regression suite that calls the production `flash_attn_varlen_func` and replaces only the downstream CuTe kernel entry point. It verifies the forwarded descale layout, values, and reuse of compatible inputs across:

- batch sizes 1 and 3;
- one and two local KV heads;
- scalar-expanded, per-head-expanded, and absent descales;
- FP8 e4m3, FP8 e5m2, and BF16 inputs.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn_interface.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn_interface.py
```

The sibling kernel suite requires the CUDA package initializer. This test loads the Python wrapper directly so it can also run on a CPU-only machine. The existing attention-kernel CI glob includes the new file.

## Test Result

Native ROCm CI follow-up (2026-10-15):
- Build #94953 passed all NVIDIA L4 attention shards and the previously failing H200 integration job. Its six AMD attention shards failed solely in this fixture because native ROCm CI stages the wheel plus tests, without either source-tree location.
- Added an installed-wheel fallback using `importlib.metadata.distribution("vllm").locate_file(...)`; the test still executes the real wrapper and does not skip coverage or import CUDA package initializers.
- Wrapper suite: 36 passed in the local checkout; 36 passed in a temporary relocated-source layout; 36 passed in a temporary installed-wheel layout with distribution metadata and no source tree. The latter verifies path discovery with staged files, not a real ROCm wheel/runtime.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks and commit sign-off checks passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Retrying the six previously failed AMD shards on the new head using `/ci retry`. No production code changed in this follow-up.


Latest CI follow-up (2026-10-15):
- Rebased onto main `a4d553a46ac112d43d6cf90735a363ee5549a394`.
- Fixed the CPU fixture to support the CI image's relocated source tree (`src/vllm`), while preserving local checkout support. Build #94730 failed because the original fixture assumed `/vllm-workspace/vllm`.
- Mocked device capability as SM100 for this CPU wrapper contract test; current main queries capability for its SM90 FP8-KV path.
- Local wrapper suite: 36 passed. The same suite in a temporary CI directory layout with source only under `src/vllm`: 36 passed. Both emitted the optional NumPy warning.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, CI test tethering, and the commit sign-off check. `py_compile` and `git diff --check` also passed.
- No real GPU kernel or model evaluation was performed in this follow-up; production behavior changes remain limited to the original descale-stride fix.

Historical validation below describes the earlier base.

Base: `a9f07d0bc59604d3979ba0f232469f4a80eb8175` (2026-09-23 main).
Local environment: macOS arm64, Python 3.13.9, PyTorch 2.13.0, pytest 9.1.1.

- Regression suite on unmodified main: **8 failed, 28 passed**. Failures are FP8 scalar-expanded descales reaching the kernel boundary with head stride zero.
- Same suite after the fix: **36 passed**. Both runs emitted a warning that optional NumPy was not installed.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy 3.10, and CI test tethering.
- Manual `mypy-3.12` hook passed.
- `py_compile` on both changed files and `git diff --check` passed.

No B200 is currently available, so this branch has not been tested with the real FA4 kernel, CUDA graphs, or an end-to-end model on current main. The CPU test checks the wrapper contract, not attention numerics or GPU performance.

Historical deployment validation (v0.29.0, earlier version of this fix): a TP=2 B200 serving run completed 80 multilingual requests with zero API failures. This was a serving smoke test, not a scored accuracy evaluation or a controlled performance comparison. Three requests exhausted the 4096-token budget with no final content. These results do not replace current-main GPU validation.

title: [Bugfix] Stop leaking the internal field name in the max_tokens validation error
author: shallow10
body:
## Purpose

`TokenizeParams.__post_init__` builds the "output tokens exceed the context length" message with the
f-string self-documenting specifier:

```python
f"{self.max_total_tokens_param}={max_total_tokens=}. "
```

`{max_total_tokens=}` expands to `max_total_tokens=<value>` on its own, so the public override name
is emitted and then immediately followed by the *internal attribute name*. A deployment that remaps
the name — which the field exists to allow ("Override this to edit the message for validation
errors") — produces:

```
max_tokens=20000 cannot be greater than max_model_len=max_total_tokens=8192.
```

`max_total_tokens` is an internal field: it is not a request body field and not a server flag
(`--max-model-len` is the user-facing one). So the 400 error tells the client about a name it cannot
set, and the doubled `name=name=` looks like a formatting bug even when the remapping is the default.

Reproduced directly: constructing `TokenizeParams(max_total_tokens=8192, max_output_tokens=20000)`
before the fix yields `... cannot be greater than max_total_tokens=max_total_tokens=8192.`

## Fix

Drop the trailing `=` so the value is interpolated plainly. This matches the sibling truncation
message a few lines below (`vllm/renderers/params.py:250`), which already writes
`{max_input_tokens}` without the specifier — so the corrected form is the one the file uses
elsewhere, not a new convention.

## Test plan

Added `tests/renderers/test_params_validation.py`:

- `test_max_output_error_uses_public_name_once` — remaps both parameter names, asserts the message
  reads `max_tokens=20000 cannot be greater than max_model_len=8192` and that the string
  `max_total_tokens` does **not** appear anywhere in it.
- `test_max_output_error_with_default_names` — pins the default-name rendering so the fix cannot
  simply delete the value.

Verified locally on an editable install of `main`:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| with the fix | 2 passed |
| fix reverted | the first test **fails** |
| `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, `check-spdx-header`, `check-test-tethering` | all pass |

Only the message text changes; no signature, no control flow, no behavior a client can depend on
other than the error string itself.

title: [Bugfix][CI] Fix the flaky sharded-sampling tests, and the engine teardown need
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

**The two sharded-sampling equivalence tests are flaky.** They were added in
#50465 (commit `d154d90d6c`) to show that batch-sharded sampling is a drop-in
for replicated sampling. On MI355 the non-spec one fails in about 40% of runs:

> AssertionError: 4/16 prompts diverged: beyond near-tie boot-state noise;
> sharded sampling is likely misrouting requests

Sharding is not the cause. Each test compares two engine boots, and with the
engine in its own process prefill starts before the last requests arrive over
IPC, so the boots pick different first batches. That changes the GEMM reduction
order, moves logprobs by up to 0.25 and flips near-ties. The same divergences
appear with sharding disabled on both sides, in prompt logprobs before any
sampling, and on a single GPU where sharding does not exist; they vanish when
the batch holds one request.

**The top-k comparison also misfires.** vLLM appends the sampled token when it
misses the requested top-k, so one side can hold k+1 entries where the other
holds k, and the allowance meant for one near-tie swap is spent on that extra
entry instead.

**Fixing the tests requires fixing engine teardown.** They need the engine in
the caller's process so every request is queued before the first step, but
`InprocClient` never tears its engine core down: unlike `MPClient` it has no
finalizer, and neither `LLM` nor `LLMEngine` calls its `shutdown()`. Its workers
keep their GPU memory for the life of the process, so the second boot fails with
81.5 of 288 GiB free against the 201.6 GiB requested. Seven tests already work
around this by calling `engine_core.shutdown()` by hand.

### What changed

- Both tests run the engine in the caller's process, so the two boots schedule
  the same batches. The divergence tolerances are removed and the comments state
  the measured cause.
- The top-k comparison separates the requested top-k from the sampled token
  before comparing sets.
- `InprocClient` gains the finalizer `MPClient` already uses, with an idempotent
  `shutdown()` so the seven manual calls keep working.

The spec-decode test was never observed failing, since it compares only token
ids over ten tokens. It is changed because the same mechanism applies, its
tolerance rests on an explanation that is not correct, and its own docstring
already asks for exact agreement.

## Test Plan

MI355 (gfx950), two GPUs. Both tests run repeatedly, before and after, to
measure flakiness rather than a single result:

- `pytest -v -s v1/e2e/general/test_sharded_sampling.py`
- `pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py`

Plus every test that calls `engine_core.shutdown()` by hand, run with and
without the finalizer.

## Test Result

**General test.** Before: ten instrumented runs gave 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
5 divergences out of 16 against a threshold of 3, so about 40% fail. A control
with sharding disabled on both sides gave 2, 2, 4, 5, which is what rules
sharding out. After: five consecutive passes, zero divergences.

**Spec-decode test.** No flakiness observed before, 0 of 120 comparisons; four
passes after. Runtime drops from about 117 s to about 87 s, since the engine now
releases its workers.

**Engine fix.** Without it the second in-process boot fails at 81.5 of 288 GiB
free; with it both boot and memory returns between them.

---

- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.

title: [Bugfix] Detect the CUDA toolkit the way FlashInfer does in has_flashinfer()
author: abmfy
body:
## Purpose

When `flashinfer-cubin` is not installed, `has_flashinfer()` treats FlashInfer as unusable unless `nvcc` is on `PATH`. FlashInfer's own JIT (`jit/cpp_ext.py::get_cuda_path`) looks further: `$CUDA_HOME`, then `$CUDA_PATH`, then `nvcc` on `PATH`, then `/usr/local/cuda`.

On a bare-metal or SLURM host the toolkit usually sits at `/usr/local/cuda` without being on `PATH`. There, every `has_flashinfer()`-gated kernel is silently disabled (TRTLLM/CUTLASS MoE, FlashInfer FP8/NVFP4 linears, AllReduce+RMSNorm fusion), and only a `debug_once` line is logged. FlashInfer attention is not gated by `has_flashinfer()`, so on the same host it keeps JIT-compiling with that toolkit. Setting `CUDA_HOME` does not help on main either.

This PR:
- mirrors FlashInfer's toolkit lookup without importing FlashInfer, since importing it initializes CUDA;
- also requires `ninja` on `PATH`, because FlashInfer runs it from there and a non-activated venv lacks it;
- replaces the `debug_once` with a `warning_once` that points to `CUDA_HOME` or `flashinfer download-kernels`.

## Test Plan

- GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13.1 at `/usr/local/cuda`, no flashinfer-cubin.
- E2E: two venvs from the same precompiled wheel, main `a9f07d0bc5` (FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1) and this PR on top of it. `nvcc` is off `PATH` and `CUDA_HOME` is unset in all arms. Same node, interleaved rounds, fresh server per arm.
- Unit tests and probe: re-run after rebasing onto main `94d1462924` (FlashInfer 0.7.0).

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 32768 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-prefix-caching
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1000 \
  --random-output-len 1000 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --max-concurrency {1,32}
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** both new tests pass. On main both fail: the first because `has_flashinfer()` returns False, the second because it returns True. (Run unmodified, they error in the fixture, since `_DEFAULT_CUDA_HOME` does not exist on main.)

**Toolkit probe** (FlashInfer 0.7.0; "can JIT" is FlashInfer's own `get_cuda_path()` plus `ninja` on `PATH`):

| environment | FlashInfer can JIT | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| toolkit only at `/usr/local/cuda` | yes | **False** | True |
| `CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda` | yes | **False** | True |
| `CUDA_HOME=/nonexistent`, nvcc on `PATH` | no | **True** | False + warning |
| runtime image (no `bin/nvcc`) | no | False | False + warning |
| nvcc on `PATH`, venv not activated (no `ninja`) | no | **True** | False + warning |

**Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP1, 3 rounds.** MoE backend is Triton on main; FlashInfer TRTLLM with this PR and with `PATH` fixed by hand.

| | main | PR | main + `/usr/local/cuda/bin` on `PATH` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c=1 output tok/s | 274.4 ± 0.4 | **309.1** ± 1.1 (+12.6%, t = 51) | 308.4 ± 1.2 |
| c=32 output tok/s | 3312 ± 20 | **3808** ± 2 (+15.0%, t = 42) | 3813 ± 5 |
| GSM8K | 0.854 | 0.847 | 0.846 |

The PR matches the `PATH` workaround within noise, so the gain comes from the FlashInfer kernels being re-enabled. The GSM8K gap to main is the MoE kernel change and is within one standard error (≈1 pp).

**Supporting data: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8, TP2, 2 rounds.** Main falls back to DeepGEMM MoE with no AR fusion; the PR uses TRTLLM MoE with AR+RMSNorm fusion.

| | main | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| c=1 output tok/s | 160.3 | **209.9** (+30.9%) |
| c=32 output tok/s | 1746 | **2883** (+65%) |
| GSM8K | 0.880 | 0.876 |

Arms used separate FlashInfer autotune caches. That can shift results by about 2%, far below these deltas.

## Notes

- The warning now fires on every CUDA install that has neither flashinfer-cubin nor a usable toolkit. On main such installs log only at debug level.
- Once `has_flashinfer()` is True, TRTLLM MoE also needs the TRTLLM-gen cubins, from the artifactory or from `flashinfer download-kernels`. This PR does not change that.
- #58765 drops flashinfer-cubin from `requirements/cuda.txt`, so more installs will take this path.
- Related, no overlap: #54267 and #55651 gate SM12x on toolkits that are too old; #49314 and #51741 cover the sampler.
- FlashInfer's toolkit lookup is unchanged between 0.6.18 and 0.7.0, so the e2e numbers were not re-taken after the rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, the tests, the benchmarks and this description.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Restore prompt-tail prefix-cache hits with MTP
author: netanel-haber
body:
Regression introduced in #55390.
Affects hybrid Mamba/GDN models with MTP, prefix caching, `--mamba-cache-mode align`, and `hash_block_size` smaller than the Mamba `block_size`.

| Model                                          | Prefix-cache hit (%): before → main → fix | Output TPS/GPU: before → main → fix |
|------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| [Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4][l] (Mamba, TP1) | 95.72 → 92.02 → **95.71**                 | 2846 → 2228 → **2833**              |
| [Qwen3.5-122B NVFP4][q] (GDN, TP2)             | 95.47 → 89.80 → **95.57**                 | 687 → 480 → **688**                 |

[l]: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4
[q]: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4
