- GSM8K is on par across the three builds (1319 questions, temperature 1.0): Lightning 91.7±0.6%, Qwen3.5 80.4±0.2%.

<details>
<summary>Full results, images, and commands</summary>

#### Full results

| Model        | vLLM          | Prefix-cache hit | Uncached prompt tokens | Output TPS/GPU | Gen TPS/user | GSM8K  |
|--------------|---------------|------------------|------------------------|----------------|--------------|--------|
| Lightning    | Before #55390 | 95.72%           | 2.25M                  | 2846           | 108.7        | 91.05% |
|              | Main          | 92.02%           | 4.19M                  | 2228           | 88.9         | 91.81% |
|              | Main + fix    | 95.71%           | 2.26M                  | 2833           | 109.4        | 92.27% |
| Qwen3.5-122B | Before #55390 | 95.47%           | 2.35M                  | 687            | 48.9         | 80.29% |
|              | Main          | 89.80%           | 5.27M                  | 480            | 34.1         | 80.67% |
|              | Main + fix    | 95.57%           | 2.29M                  | 688            | 49.4         | 80.21% |

Gen TPS/user is the mean of `1 / inter-token latency` per request.

#### Images

- Before #55390: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3df4ae153eb385e27b52f26c81f8edb9e20b9984`
- Main: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19`
- Main + fix: the main image with this PR's `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` mounted over the installed one.

#### AIPerf

Server environment: `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`.

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 114688 --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 64 --prefix-match-unit 64 --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
  --speculative_config.method mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --speculative_config.rejection_sample_method synthetic --speculative_config.synthetic_acceptance_length 3.0
```

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --language-model-only \
  --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 114688 --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 64 --prefix-match-unit 64 --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --speculative_config.method mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --speculative_config.rejection_sample_method synthetic --speculative_config.synthetic_acceptance_length 3.0
```

```bash
aiperf profile --model $MODEL --tokenizer $MODEL --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --url http://0.0.0.0:30000 \
  --endpoint-type chat --streaming --use-server-token-count --random-seed 42 \
  --concurrency 32 --num-conversations 32 --request-count 640 --warmup-request-count 16 \
  --shared-system-prompt-length 51200 --isl 2048 --isl-stddev 0 --osl 1024 --osl-stddev 0 \
  --conversation-turn-mean 20 --conversation-turn-stddev 0 --conversation-turn-delay-mean 0 \
  --extra-inputs temperature:0 --extra-inputs ignore_eos:true
```

#### GSM8K

Same `vllm serve` commands as above, without the two `synthetic` flags and without `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY`. [NeMo-Skills](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills) at `467b057372`:

```bash
python -m nemo_skills.inference.generate \
  ++server.server_type=vllm ++server.base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 ++server.model=$MODEL \
  ++input_file=$GSM8K_TEST_JSONL ++eval_type=math ++eval_config.split=test ++prompt_config=generic/math \
  ++inference.endpoint_type=chat ++inference.tokens_to_generate=4096 ++inference.temperature=1.0 \
  ++inference.top_p=0.95 ++inference.random_seed=0 ++chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=True \
  ++inference.extra_body.skip_special_tokens=False ++max_concurrent_requests=512 ++output_file=output.jsonl
```

</details>

## Explanation of regression

Example: `hash_block_size = 64`. Prompt A has 1600 tokens. Prompt B starts with A. With MTP, the prefix-cache lookup drops the last 64 matched tokens, so B can reuse at most 1536. [The scheduler](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L479-L486) ends a prefill chunk of A at 1536 to compute the Mamba state there. But [`_cache_partial_tail_block`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L2078-L2086) saves the state at 1536 only if the Mamba group has `use_eagle`. Otherwise, it saves at 1600.

The Mamba group got `use_eagle` only from **the all-groups fallback** in [the coordinator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L108-L110):

```python
if use_eagle and not self.eagle_group_ids:
    self.eagle_group_ids = set(range(len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups)))
```

#55390 marks the MTP group, so the all-groups fallback no longer runs. The Mamba state is saved at 1600, and B reuses 0 tokens instead of 1536.

## Fix
`_cache_partial_tail_block` checks `drop_eagle_checkpoint_block` instead of `use_eagle`. [The coordinator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed8158/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L153-L156) sets it on every Mamba manager exactly when the scheduler shifts the chunk end:

```diff
-if self.use_eagle:
+if self.drop_eagle_checkpoint_block:
     latest_prompt_hash_boundary = max(
         latest_prompt_hash_boundary - hash_block_size, 0
     )
```

#### Tests

`pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_mamba_eagle_resume_checkpoint.py`: the new `annotated-draft` cases fail on main and pass with this change.

AI assistance was used.

title: [CI][ROCM] Add the Fusion E2E TP2 Quick group on MI355, and the AITER MLA fix it needs
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

**Add one AMD CI group.** It mirrors `(H100) Fusion E2E TP2 Quick`, keeping only the payloads the two AITER backends support, and is split out of #50519 so it can be reviewed and validated on its own.

**The test could not run on AMD.** `test_tp2_ar_rms_fp8_fusions` was CUDA only and offered three NVIDIA backends, so the models and backends are now parametrized per platform and `ROCM_AITER_MLA` is added as a backend case.

**The group's third command crashed the worker.** DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite at TP2 gives 8 heads per rank, which selects AITER's Gluon MLA decode on gfx950. Past 2 GiB of KV cache per layer that kernel swaps its masked `buffer_load` for an
unmasked `global_load` and reads outside the allocation:

> Memory access fault by GPU node-4 on address ... Reason: Unknown.

The fault surfaces in whichever kernel runs next, so the traceback points at the Triton MoE rather than at the attention kernel that caused it. Reported upstream as ROCm/aiter#4490, which is open with no reproducer.

### What changed

- Models and attention backends in `test_tp2_ar_rms_fp8_fusions` are chosen per platform. On ROCm the AITER all-reduce 
  pass owns the post-AR RMS sites, so the group checks `aiter_ar_rms_fusion` instead of the native fusions. DeepSeek-Coder
  on AITER MLA runs its MoE on Triton, since AITER's MoE GEMM rejects the reduced dummy shape; Llama-3 gets 
  explicit memory limits to fit alongside the second rank.
- The group is added as a `mirror: amd:` block and as the matching legacy `test-amd.yaml` entry. Three commands, 
   60 minute  budget.
- AITER MLA refuses the Gluon decode once the per-layer cache passes 2 GiB and takes the padded persistent-scheduling 
  ASM decode instead. The bound mirrors the kernel's own `within_2gb` computation, so the fallback engages exactly where the
  unmasked path takes over.
- The builder now derives the per-layer cache size, so the hand-built builder stand-ins in `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` 
   gain the two fields it reads, and a new routing test covers the bound.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), two GPUs. The whole group, all three commands in sequence as Buildkite runs it, plus the AITER MLA routing tests the new bound affects.

## Test Result

**Group.** Passes end to end

**Gluon guard.** Above the bound the kernel faults at every KV length tried (1, 64, 128, 129, 256); below it the same shapes are clean. End to end the ASM decode lands within about 2% of Gluon.

**Routing tests.** 552 passed; the new bound test fails when the guard is removed.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix TileLang mHC fused RMSNorm on 64-wide wavefronts
author: djramic
body:
## Purpose

27 tests in `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` fail in the `(MI355) Miscellaneous Kernels` job added by #50519, all with the fused RMSNorm enabled:

```text
FAILED test_mhc_pre_tilelang[True-*] (8 cases)
FAILED test_deepseek_v41_mhc_pre_delayed[True-False-*] (15 cases)
FAILED test_deepseek_v41_decoder_mixes_match_torch[disabled-*] (4 cases)

Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13378/list?sid=01a0c82f-6637-4452-80c8-a00e9f20a69b&tab=output>

The fused-norm mHC pre kernels split 96 threads: the mix phase runs on threads 0-31, and the collapse + RMSNorm on threads 32-95. TileLang's HIP AllReduce shuffle phase ignores the thread offset of the reduction group, so on a 64-wide wavefront the RMSNorm reduction sums only half of the values. As a result, layer_input is sqrt(2) times too large. CUDA is not affected because its 32-wide warps keep the group aligned.

On ROCm, the mix phase now runs on the last 32 threads, so the RMSNorm reduction uses threads 0-63, one full wavefront. On CUDA the generated kernel is unchanged.

title: [Bugfix] Stop allocator fragmentation from shrinking the KV cache during memory profiling
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
## Purpose

Wrap the memory-profiling forward pass in `Worker._scoped_allocator_max_split(max_split_size_mb=20)`, the same scoped allocator setting #41268 applies around weight loading.

During `profile_run`, workspaces such as the MoE workspace grow in steps, and each step frees the previous, smaller buffer. With PyTorch's default (unlimited) `max_split_size_mb`, a later small allocation can be carved out of one of those freed multi-GiB blocks. That live block keeps the whole segment reserved through the `empty_cache()` in `memory_profiling`. The profiler measures consumption from free device memory, so the stranded segment is counted as consumed and taken out of the KV cache.

How much gets stranded depends on allocation order, so it varies per rank. With context parallelism the worst rank in each group sets the group's KV size, so the loss compounds. With a split limit, blocks above the limit are never split, so they stay whole and `empty_cache()` releases them. The limit is restored when the profiling pass exits, before `memory_profiling` measures, so serving and KV cache allocation run with the original allocator settings.

`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` also avoids the stranding. But vLLM rejects it alongside a KV connector such as NIXL unless `--enable-cumem-allocator` is also set, and in the deployment below that combination raised baseline consumption by ~2.9 GiB on every GPU. The scoped split limit keeps the default `cudaMalloc` allocator throughout.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py::test_scoped_max_split_keeps_freed_large_blocks_releasable` (needs CUDA). It frees a 512 MiB buffer and then allocates a 2 MiB tensor. Without the scope, the tensor pins the 512 MiB segment through `empty_cache()`. Inside `_scoped_allocator_max_split(20)`, the segment is released.

  ```
  pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -k scoped_max_split
  ```

- End to end: GLM-5.2-FP8, DP4 × PCP8 (DCP8), TP1, EP32 on 4 × 8 H100 (RoCE), DeepEP high-throughput, DeepGEMM MoE, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, `--enforce-eager`, `NixlConnector` producer. The same change was applied as a startup patch, and each worker logged a per-worker breakdown of `total_consumed` after `profile_run` (torch allocated / reserved / inactive-split, non-torch memory, MoE workspace size).

## Test Result

The dummy-batch routing was identical across runs, so each GPU's MoE workspace peak was the same (4.0–7.1 GiB); only the allocator setting changed.

Per GPU, before the change: `consumed = 46.83 GiB + MoE workspace peak + stranded`, where stranded (reserved but unallocated, held by partially used segments whose size matched earlier workspace buffers) ranged from 0.04 to 5.36 GiB. Non-torch memory was 3.14 GiB on every GPU.

After the change: stranded is 0.01–0.04 GiB on all 32 GPUs, and `consumed − workspace` is 46.87–46.89 GiB everywhere.

| DP rank | KV before | KV after |
|---|---|---|
| DP0 | 13.87 GiB / 2,168,877 tokens | 16.14 GiB / 2,521,938 tokens |
| DP1 | 12.31 GiB / 1,925,510 tokens | 16.43 GiB / 2,561,734 tokens |
| DP2 | 13.60 GiB / 2,127,551 tokens | 16.00 GiB / 2,501,530 tokens |
| DP3 | 9.93 GiB / 1,552,551 tokens | 15.06 GiB / 2,351,020 tokens |
| Total | 7.78M tokens | 9.94M tokens (+28%) |

The spread between ranks fell from 3.94 GiB to 1.37 GiB; what remains comes from the per-rank MoE workspace peak. All four ranks completed warmup and reached `Application startup complete`.

The new unit test has not yet been run on a GPU; the author's machine has no CUDA device.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Treat padded prompt tails as spec-decode rows for hybrid models
author: njhill
body:
The scheduler pads a one-token prompt tail over prior state (e.g. a P/D decode-node arrival) with K placeholder drafts to keep the K+1 spec-decode shape (#45237). For recurrent-state layers these rows must run the spec-decode kernels, which keep the running state and roll the rejected placeholders back; the prefill kernels store only the state after all K+1 tokens (#55178).

#52988 changed the hybrid model state to classify spec-decode rows by request state (not prefilling) instead of num_scheduled_tokens, which adaptive verification rewrites. That sent every padded tail's draft count to -1, so Mamba's padded-tail handling no longer fires and GDN/KDA build the row as a prefill, folding the placeholder tokens into the request's recurrent state.

Also count prefilling rows with exactly one remaining prompt token and prior state as decodes, still using request state only.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Give LM heads standard linear metadata
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Checkpoints that explicitly quantize `lm_head` can fail during Humming weight preparation because `ParallelLMHead` lacks the linear dimensions and bias metadata expected by quantization backends.

Retain the linear weight dimensions, partition sizes, and prefix in `VocabParallelEmbedding` before quantization dispatch, and initialize `ParallelLMHead.has_bias` before weight creation. The weight factory consumes the same dimensions exposed on the layer. Vocabulary padding, tensor-parallel sharding, and checkpoint-controlled quantization selection are preserved.

Remove the now-redundant LM-head metadata fallbacks from ModelOpt and compressed-tensors, and compute the added-vocabulary count once in the embedding constructor.

This is an alternative implementation to #48856, addressing https://github.com/vllm-project/humming/issues/70. That PR adds LM-head fallbacks inside Humming's preparation helper; this change fixes the shared layer interface so the metadata is available to all quantization backends. No Humming code changes are needed. Open-PR searches for the issue, `humming lm_head`, and `ParallelLMHead linear` found no other implementation of this shared metadata fix.

Extend the existing LM-head suite with one parametrized test comparing real quantized heads against `ColumnParallelLinear`, including bias and vocabulary padding, for compressed-tensors FP8, NVFP4A16, INT4 W4A16, and ModelOpt NVFP4 W4A16. title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] kpool corruption with speculative decoding
author: mmastrac
body:
## Purpose

_Partial_ fix for #56868 and #56605. See also #58704 for one more fix. These both help, but there will likely be one or two more PRs with followups.

This patch is the result of hunting down random corruption in long GLM-5.3-Flash traces.

Rejected pool-completing drafts can end up subtly corrupting the pool selection logic: When a pool-completing draft is rejected, the drafts stashed behind it have already overwritten that pool's committed keys. A pool of 4 generated tokens gets an incorrect summary key, so the indexer may skip those tokens or pick a less useful pool.

This affects any speculative method with `num_speculative_tokens >= 2`. 

Only pools built during decode (the model's own output) are affected, and only once the context exceeds `index_topk` (2048), where pools compete for selection.

The most likely place it hurts is long reasoning traces, where later thinking refers back to earlier thinking, as slightly worse long-range self-reference. This _may_ be causing specific failures in re-transcription from memory.

The ring now holds `kpool * cdiv(kpool + num_spec, kpool)` slots, and the seed and decode kernels address it by `pos % RING`. The tail slot mapping already uses the spec's block_size, so it follows. 

Encountered this locally, fix based on work in #55219 by @ivanium. This is only a surgical fix + test for this particular issue.

## Test Plan

Tests included.

Also, a standalone repro that isolates the specific bug and corruption:

| kernel | ring | pool vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 4 (current sizing) | wrong: 106 of 128 fp8 key bytes differ |
| `main` | 8 | `AssertionError` (ring must equal `kpool`) |
| this PR | 8 (`4 * cdiv(4 + 3, 4)`) | identical 

<summary>
(repro file hidden here)
</summary>
<details>

```
"""Repro: rejected speculative drafts corrupt the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer.

kpool = 4 (GLM-5.3-Flash). A spec-verify step stashes 1 + num_spec rows into
the per-request tail ring before acceptance is known. Pool W covers positions
4..7; positions 4 and 5 were accepted earlier. Step t verifies 6, 7, 8, 9
(num_spec = 3): 6 is accepted, the pool-completing draft 7 and drafts 8, 9 are
rejected. With a ring of exactly kpool slots, drafts 8 and 9 overwrite ring
slots 0 and 1, which still hold the committed keys of positions 4 and 5. Step
t+1 re-verifies from 7 and recompresses pool W from those slots.

Reference: the accepted tokens fed one per step (no speculation).
Run with RING=4 (before the fix) and RING=8 (kpool * cdiv(kpool + num_spec, kpool)).
"""
import os
import torch
from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops.kpool_compress import (
    kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache_batched as update,
)

D, P, PAGE, BLOCK, POOL_LOC = 128, 4, 64, 3, 5
RING = int(os.environ.get("RING", P))
dev = "cuda"
torch.manual_seed(0)
rnd = lambda: torch.randn(D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)  # noqa: E731
keys, gates = {p: rnd() for p in range(4, 12)}, {p: rnd() for p in range(4, 12)}
dkeys, dgates = {p: rnd() for p in range(6, 12)}, {p: rnd() for p in range(6, 12)}
ape = torch.randn(P, D, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)


def fresh():
    return (torch.zeros(4, PAGE, D + 4, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev),
            torch.zeros(8, 2, RING, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev))


def step(kv, tail, positions, K, G):
    n = len(positions)
    t = lambda xs: torch.tensor([xs], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)  # noqa: E731
    update(kv, tail, t([BLOCK * RING + p % RING for p in positions]),
           torch.stack(K).view(1, n, D), torch.stack(G).view(1, n, D), ape,
           t([POOL_LOC if p == 7 else (99 if p % P == P - 1 else -1) for p in positions]),
           t(positions), pool_size=P, head_dim=D)


def pool(kv):
    return kv.view(-1, D + 4)[POOL_LOC].clone()


kv, tail = fresh()
for p in (4, 5, 6, 7):
    step(kv, tail, [p], [keys[p]], [gates[p]])
ref = pool(kv)

kv, tail = fresh()
for p in (4, 5):
    step(kv, tail, [p], [keys[p]], [gates[p]])
step(kv, tail, [6, 7, 8, 9], [keys[6], dkeys[7], dkeys[8], dkeys[9]],
     [gates[6], dgates[7], dgates[8], dgates[9]])
step(kv, tail, [7, 8, 9, 10], [keys[7], dkeys[8], dkeys[9], dkeys[10]],
     [gates[7], dgates[8], dgates[9], dgates[10]])
spec = pool(kv)
bad = (ref[:D] != spec[:D]).sum().item()
print(f"RING={RING}: pool W matches the no-speculation reference: {torch.equal(ref, spec)}"
      f" ({bad}/{D} fp8 key bytes differ)")
```

</details>


## Test Result

All tests pass.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Limit MRV2 sampler JIT warmup registration to ROCm
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

#58092 ("[ROCm][Bugfix] Register MRV2 sampler JIT warmups") calls `register_top_k_top_p_warmups()` in the MRV2 `GPUModelRunner` on **all** platforms, not just ROCm. On CUDA these Triton sampler warmups recompile on most engine starts (about 110s each, against `finished in 0.00s` before), so NVIDIA CI jobs slowed down a lot and many now time out.

This PR keeps the registration for ROCm, which #58092 targeted, and puts CUDA back where it was before #58092.

## Impact of #58092 on `main` CI

Median passing runtime per step, ~26 `main` builds before vs ~26 after `96e203b08e`:

| Hardware | Steps | ≥15% and ≥3 min slower | faster |
|---|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA | 185 | **46** (+4 that now only time out) | 1 |
| AMD | 175 | 3 (noise) | 0 |

- About **+430 job-minutes per `main` build** on the affected NVIDIA steps.
- **45 timeouts** on 7 steps that never timed out before, e.g. Language Models (Hybrid) Shard 2 ×15 and Basic Correctness ×11.
- Examples: Basic Correctness 42 → 68+ min, PyTorch Compilation 25 → 49, PyTorch Fullgraph 55 → 83, Samplers 23 → 39, H100 Fusion E2E Quick 7 → 15.
- Clean break on `main`: build 90618 (`26879f3260`) ran Basic Correctness in 42 min; the next build, 90619 (`96e203b08e`), took 63 min, and every build since has taken 66–68 min or timed out.
- Per-test view (Basic Correctness, same runner type): every test became about 140s slower, e.g. 43s → 191s, with the time spent in `JIT kernel warmup (120 compile keys)`.

The CUDA `No Runtime JITs E2E` step passed before #58092 without this registration, so leaving it out on CUDA shouldn't bring back runtime JITs there. If CUDA does need these warmups for its FlashInfer fallback, that can come back once the per-start recompile is fixed.

This PR is also why the open timeout bumps (#58376, #58386, #58320) shouldn't be needed.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `58092`, "Revert 58092", "topk topp warmup", "JIT warmup timeout" and "sampler warmup CUDA". None addresses this; #58410 adds another MRV2 sampler warmup and doesn't touch the platform scope.

## Test Plan

- `ruff check`, `ruff format` and the full pre-commit hook set pass.
- CI: `:amd: (MI355) MRV2 Sampler JIT Warmup` should still pass on ROCm, and NVIDIA steps such as Basic Correctness, PyTorch Compilation and `No Runtime JITs E2E` should go back to their pre-#58092 runtimes.
- No model eval: this changes which kernels are warmed up at startup, not model outputs.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Shard a GQA draft's KV by head under an MLA target
author: stu-cao
body:
## Update (2026-10-13)

Adopted @NickLucche's simplification from #60368 (thanks!): the source files now match that branch exactly, carried as a commit authored by him (his three commits squashed, his sign-off kept), followed by one commit of mine adapting the tests. Relative to the earlier revision:
- draft-region identity is computed once at `register_kv_caches` into `_head_sharded_draft_regions` (via `_layer_specs`), replacing the per-region head-count list and the three per-call helpers;
- the push-mode guard lives in `NixlPushConnectorWorker` and rejects only heterogeneous TP, so equal-TP push works; the base class keeps the `tp_ratio < 0` / DCP rejection;
- `tp_mapping.compute_head_offset` carries the rank-offset arithmetic for both the target and the draft mapping.
Tests were adapted to the new structure (see Test Plan); the end-to-end results below predate this revision and were obtained with the earlier implementation of the same behaviour.

## Purpose

Fixes #58470.

NIXL P/D mis-handles a draft model's KV when **all three** hold:

1. **The target is MLA** (e.g. GLM-5.3), so NIXL maps every KV region as replicated: `total_num_kv_heads=1`, `rank_offset_factor=0`.
2. **The draft is not MLA** (e.g. DFlash2, 8 KV heads), so its KV is actually split by head across TP.
3. **Prefill TP ≠ decode TP** (e.g. a DEP8 prefill with attention TP1 feeding a TP8 decoder), so each decode rank needs a different head slice.

Drop any one and it works: an MLA draft (MTP), or equal P/D TP. `_is_region_replicated` already marks the draft regions SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer:

| where | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| handshake size check (`model_replicated = self.use_mla or …`) | rejects the correct geometry, accepts an unscaled draft block | checks draft regions as SPLIT |
| read offset (`_build_fa_remote`) | every decode rank reads draft head 0 | rank *r* reads head *r* |
| hetero-TP layout guard | skipped when `use_mla` | requires the same block-contiguous layout on P and D |

**Fix.** When the target is MLA and the draft isn't, build a second `TPMapping` from the draft's KV head count (`compute_tp_mapping(..., head_sharded_kv_heads=...)`). The draft's SPLIT regions use it for reads, size checks and the layout guard; MLA regions are unchanged. Prefill TP > decode TP and DCP are rejected with `NotImplementedError` for such drafts. Mamba, CSA-linear and MLA drafts behave as before.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches this. Related:
- #49230 (merged): checks that P and D speculative configs match; they do here.
- #54926: Gemma 4 MTP draft groups are not transferred at all.
- #57309: moves helpers out of `tp_mapping.py`; a refactor only.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py
```

New tests:
- `test_resolve_head_sharded_draft_kv_heads`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_under_mla_target_gets_gqa_offset`
- `test_handshake_mla_target_reads_draft_head_slice` (also `_block_outermost`, for BLHNC)
- `test_handshake_mla_target_rejects_unsharded_draft_block`
- `test_handshake_mla_target_rejects_draft_with_prefill_tp_above_decode`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_regions_check_layer_identity`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_push_rejects_heterogeneous_tp` (push worker)

End-to-end A/B on 2 × 8×H200 over NIXL/IB:
- **Model:** GLM-5.3 FP8 + DFlash2 (k=4).
- **Topology:** P DP8/EP8 (attention TP1) → D TP8, `LBHNC`.
- **Builds:** the same wheel (`0.30.1rc1.dev29+g711fc55c1`) with and without this change.
- **Workload:** 80 MT-Bench prompts, 256 tokens, temperature 0, following `nixl_integration/test_spec_decode_acceptance.py`.
- **Comparison:** each prompt goes once through the P/D proxy and once straight to decode (local prefill), both on the same decode server.

## Test Result

**Unit:**
- This PR: 29 / 152 / 84 / 210 pass.
- The 2 failures are `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller`, which needs 24 GiB of RAM; it fails on `main` too.
- The new tests fail on `main`.

**End-to-end:**

| | P/D over NIXL | local prefill |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | **0 / 80**: handshake `AssertionError: KV cache sizes must match … (region 99: local=32768, remote=262144)`, HTTP 500 | 80 / 80, acceptance length 3.253 |
| this PR | **80 / 80**, acceptance length **3.221**, 0 failed transfers | 80 / 80, acceptance length 3.253 |

- **Acceptance:** P/D is within 1.0% of local prefill. The upstream test's tolerance is 5%.
- **Local path:** the local-prefill counters are identical on both builds.

**Follow-up B300 validation (GLM-5.3 NVFP4 + DFlash2):**
- Ran on `research-b300-pf` with one DEP8 prefill node and four TP4 decode engines across two B300 nodes (NIXL pull, `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV).
- GPU unit suite on the PR source: **357 passed** across the four NIXL test files in the test plan.
- 2026-10-13, after adopting #60368 and rebasing onto `main` `791f92135a`: 528 passed, 2 deselected (`test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller`, the known RAM-bound test), 0 failed across the four files on B300 (2026-10-14).
- Functional gate: **42/42** requests passed; long-context retrieval passed **3/3 at ~10.8K** and **3/3 at ~66.5K** tokens. Two 12-way concurrent repeat rounds passed **12/12** each and matched sequential outputs.
- Sustained AgentX load at concurrency 8 for 900 seconds: **310/310** successful requests, **0 errors** (including 0 HTTP 429), TTFT p50 **714 ms**, ITL p50 **4.06 ms**. The aggregate export completed with exit code 0. Worker logs showed **0 NIXL transfer failures** or handshake failures.

**Scope:** GQA draft KV under an MLA target is supported in NIXL pull mode, and in push mode at equal P/D TP; heterogeneous-TP push raises `NotImplementedError` at handshake (`NixlPushConnectorWorker`).

**Not covered end to end:**
- NIXL push mode for a GQA draft under an MLA target (equal TP allowed, heterogeneous TP rejected; covered by a unit test, not run end to end);
- fp8 draft KV;
- CUDA graphs;
- other TP pairs (unit-tested: 1→8, 2→8, 1→16);
- `MultiConnector`;
- NVLink transport.

title: [KV Connector] Fix DecodeBench fp8 fill values and add a startup fill mode
author: liuzijing2014
body:
## Purpose

Two changes to `DecodeBenchConnector`, one commit each:

- **Fix fp8 fill values.** fp8 KV caches are stored as `uint8`, and the fill used `torch.full(fill_mean, dtype=uint8)`, which truncates to 0. So the dummy prompt KV was all zeros, and random fill (`fill_std > 0`) raised.
  - Plain fp8 `uint8` caches now get the fill encoded in their fp8 dtype (platform e4m3, or e5m2 for `fp8_e5m2`).
  - Random values are sampled in float32 and clamped to the finite range.
  - Packed `uint8` layouts with scales or metadata (e.g. `fp8_ds_mla`, NVFP4) keep the zero fill, now with a one-time warning.
- **Add an opt-in `startup_fill` option** (`kv_connector_extra_config`).
  - Today's per-request fill runs inside the decode steps that admit new requests. For every layer it copies block IDs to the device, filters them with a boolean mask (a device sync) and builds a temporary tensor.
  - With `startup_fill`, the worker fills the KV cache once in `register_kv_caches` and skips the per-request fill.
  - Circular-buffer groups, and attention groups whose new blocks the engine zeroes (hybrid Mamba, mixed precision), keep the per-request fill, so the dummy KV is never left as zeros.
  - The fill isn't redone after sleep mode. The default behavior is unchanged.
- No open PR covers either change. #57751, which fixes Mamba state filling in the default mode, is complementary.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py`. New tests:
  - read-back as fp8 for `fp8` / `fp8_e5m2` `uint8` caches and a `float8_e4m3fn` cache, with constant and random fill;
  - a packed layout stays zero;
  - startup fill of strided, padded and fp8 caches;
  - no per-step fill;
  - circular-buffer and engine-zeroed groups keep the per-request fill.
- KV read-back on the workers, in the default mode and with `startup_fill`:
  - `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`;
  - `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` TP4 with fp8 main KV and fp8 indexer KV.
- Decode-only A/B with `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"[,"kv_connector_extra_config":{"startup_fill":true}]}'` and `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`: a warmup, then 3 runs per mode.
  - Qwen3-0.6B on 1× GB200, 3584 in / 256 out, concurrency 4.
  - M3 TP4 GB200 (`--language-model-only --block-size 128 --max-num-seqs 88 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`), 32000 in / 256 out, concurrency 32.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 29 passed (14 new). On `main`, the fp8 cases fail with zeros or `NotImplementedError`.
- KV read-back holds 0.015625 with no non-finite values:
  - default mode: 5.3% (Qwen) and 4.4% (M3) of cache elements, i.e. the blocks the requests used. On `main` these `uint8` caches hold 0.
  - `startup_fill`: 99.5% (Qwen) and 99.99% (M3 main and indexer caches), before and after requests.
- Decode-only A/B, mean of 3 runs (min–max):

| Model | Mode | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | P99 ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B | default | 1636 (1550–1682) | 70.8 (68.8–72.5) | 2.18 (2.11–2.31) | 2.15 (2.05–2.28) | 3.03 (2.86–3.19) |
| Qwen3-0.6B | `startup_fill` | 1839 (1782–1926) | 50.0 (47.0–51.6) | 1.99 (1.90–2.05) | 1.96 (1.87–2.02) | 2.59 (2.54–2.64) |
| M3 TP4 | default | 1273 (1265–1279) | 1477 (1382–1535) | 19.39 (19.13–19.65) | 11.55 (11.53–11.57) | 218.3 (216.3–219.5) |
| M3 TP4 | `startup_fill` | 1282 (1261–1303) | 1185 (1144–1242) | 20.34 (20.09–20.82) | 11.97 (11.77–12.25) | 193.3 (191.9–194.6) |

- M3: TTFT −20% and P99 ITL −11% at the same throughput. TPOT +4.9% because more requests are in the decode phase (24.6 → 26.0).
- Smoke runs with `startup_fill` passed:
  - `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` (circular buffer, TP4): 200/200 requests.
  - `Falcon-H1-0.5B` (Mamba): 100/100 requests.

title: [Elastic EP] Fix EPLB load statistics during scaling
author: itayalroy
body:
EPLB records load per physical location. After a reshuffle, a different expert may occupy that location, but the old measurements remain. Elastic EP can force another reshuffle before a full window of new measurements replaces the old measurements, causing EPLB to attribute the old load to the wrong expert.

On Elastic EP-triggered reshuffles, use the last saved load for each expert instead of the current load history, which may be wrong or incomplete.

Note that regular EPLB can hit the same stale-history problem when step_interval is smaller than window_size. That should be fixed separately.

cc @tlrmchlsmth @ilmarkov

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Keep pinned PLE prefetch ids out of the CUDA graph pool
author: Juntian777
body:
## Problem and fix

Fixes #58441. With `engram_config.cpu_offload=True`, `Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding.start_prefetch` launches the PLE lookup on a side stream and returns; `_finalize_prefetch` joins it one decoder layer later. Qwen4Exp defaults to breakable CUDA graphs, so for PIECEWISE batches (prefill/mixed batches up to the capture size, or every batch with `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`) `start_prefetch` is an eager break and its arguments are replaced by `weak_ref_tensor`s. Two things then combine:

- `gathered_ids.record_stream(prefetch_stream)` is a no-op: with `etp_data_parallel_size == 1`, `gathered_ids` is the weak ref itself, and the caching allocator skips `recordStream` for storage it does not own.
- The only strong reference to the ids is the local `ngram_ids` in `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding.start_prefetch`, which drops as soon as it returns, while the next segment is already being captured. The graph-pool block goes straight back to the free list and the rest of the preceding decoder layer can be captured on top of it.

At replay the side stream reads the ids while the main stream may be overwriting them, so greedy outputs silently stop being reproducible.

The fix computes the prefetch ids into a persistent per-layer buffer through the existing `output=` argument of `compute_ngram_ids`. This mirrors the persistent `_prefetch_buffer` already used for the lookup output, adds no kernel or copy, and costs `max_num_batched_tokens * ngram_heads * 8` bytes per PLE layer. FULL graphs and eager runs were already safe (the argument stays a real tensor there), and ETP spanning DP is unaffected (the ids are re-gathered into a fresh tensor inside the eager break).

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py
```

- **51 passed** on GB200. The new `test_ngram_prefetch_ids_outlive_start_prefetch` reproduces the lifetime bug without a full graph capture: the prefetch stub keeps a weak ref to the ids, as the eager break does, and a fresh `MemPool` makes the next same-size allocation reuse freed storage, as a later graph segment would. On main the weak ref reads the overwritten `-1`s (3/3 runs); with this change it reads the reference ids.
- Pre-commit passed.
- No model eval: the ids are produced by the same kernel into a different buffer, so outputs only change where the race corrupted them. The reporter's cold/warm greedy table in #58441 (8/8 identical once the ids are in a persistent buffer) covers the end-to-end effect.

## Related work and AI assistance

Open-PR search found no equivalent fix. #57785 joins side-stream work during breakable capture and does not affect replay (row 2 of the table in #58441); #57497 and #58439 move or add PLE backends without changing this lifetime.

Claude Code assisted with root-causing, implementation and validation; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

title: [BUG] Fix KV offload shared-memory slot selection using worker rank
author: hlin99
body:
# KV offload selects the wrong shared-memory slot when device index differs from worker rank

## Description

CPU and Tiering KV offload select a worker's shared-memory slot using the
physical device index modulo the worker world size. The device index is not
necessarily the worker's rank, so this can select the wrong slot in a
non-replicated layout.

For example, with `world_size=4`, `rank=1`, and `device_index=6`, the current
calculation selects slot `6 % 4 = 2` instead of slot `1`. Workers can therefore
read or write a different slot from the one assigned to their rank.

## Expected behavior

Non-replicated layouts should select the shared-memory slot using the worker
rank. Replicated layouts should continue to use slot `0`.
~

title: [Bugfix] Don't sync-police or retry FlashInfer all-reduce workspace creation in eager mode
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fix a nightly regression from #58197 ("[Core] Disable JIT warmup in eager mode").

With `--enforce-eager` the V2 `warmup_kernels` dummy forward is now skipped. The standalone FlashInfer all-reduce (`FlashInferAllReduce`, enabled by default through `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1`) creates its workspace lazily. The profile run uses large tensors that are above the FlashInfer size cap (e.g. 0.5 MB at TP8 or 2 MB at TP4 on H200), so it never touches the workspace. As a result, the workspace is first created inside the first real `execute_model`, which runs after `enable_gpu_sync_check()`. In CI (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`), `flashinfer_comm.create_allreduce_fusion_workspace(...)` then raises `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` part-way through a collective. The failure is caught and returns `None`, and `get_fi_ar_workspace` does not remember it. The mnnvl attempt fails, the trtllm fallback fails, and the collective creation keeps getting retried. Each retry leaks partially created buffers, which leads to CUDA OOM, then a deadlock, then `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` and `EngineDeadError`.

Evidence (nightly build 90589):
- H200 LM Eval DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 (`--enforce-eager`): https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90589#01a0ccda-d861-443c-bcb5-9c8b22260601. At 11:45:56 it logs `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected`, followed by repeated `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. OOM follows by 11:46:18 and the RPC timeout at 11:50:53.
- B200 HiSparse (GLM-5.2-NVFP4 TP4), job `01a0cd35-9fed-4cff-a2be-b8c4ea5fb773` in the same build, fails the same way.
- Passing build 90513 (before #58197) logs `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during warmup.
- This is likely also behind the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E failure (`rank 0 did not report UNHEALTHY within 45s`) that #58318 is bisecting. That link is not verified.

## Fix

In `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py`:
1. Wrap the one-time `create_allreduce_fusion_workspace` call in `gpu_sync_allowed()`. This covers both the regular and the quant workspace paths, since both go through `_create_workspace`. Setup syncs are expected here and are not a per-step cost.
2. Remember a failed creation (`_fi_ar_workspace_failed` / `_fi_ar_quant_workspace_failed`) so a collective creation is never retried on every all-reduce call. `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()` resets both flags.

I also considered creating the workspace eagerly before `enable_gpu_sync_check()` when warmup is skipped. That approach would have to guess the hidden size and dtype in the worker. It would also leave the retry-storm failure mode in place for any other lazy-creation failure. The change above is smaller and local to the module that owns the workspace.

## Not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --state open --search "flashinfer all reduce workspace"`, `"58197"`, `"gpu_sync_allowed"`, `"flashinfer allreduce eager"` and `"enforce-eager warmup"` returned no PR that fixes this.
- #58318 is a DNM CI-bisect probe that reverts #58197. It is not a fix.

## Test Plan / Results

GPU checks ran on an idle 8×H200 host (GPUs 0-3), using the nightly image `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:de6674b0023b...` (the same image as build 90589). For "after", the patched file was mounted over the installed one. At that commit the file is identical to current `main`.

Repro: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", tensor_parallel_size=4, enforce_eager=True)`, 3× `generate` of 4 prompts. TP4 puts the FlashInfer cap at 2 MB, so the profile run skips it, which matches the CI case.
- **Before:** `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected` (mnnvl, then trtllm), then `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. Generation still finished because this small model falls back to other all-reduce backends, so the full OOM/deadlock cascade seen with DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 did not reproduce here.
- **After:** `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during the first step. No sync errors, and output is correct (`' Paris. ...'`).

Unit tests, run in the same image with the patched files mounted:
```
pytest distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer or checkpoints"
14 passed, 17 deselected
```
The new `test_flashinfer_workspace_failure_is_not_retried` checks that a failing creation runs once (mnnvl plus the trtllm fallback) across repeated calls and runs again after `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()`.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

Not verified: the full DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 and GLM-5.2 HiSparse CI jobs themselves, and the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E job.

title: [Bugfix][DSV4.1] Avoid host sync in ViT CUDA graph replay metadata
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 35GB) Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)` has failed on every main build since 2026-09-20 (first failure: build 90097). The failing test is `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_vit_cudagraph_image[deepseek_v41]`. Example: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90589#01a0ccda-d883-4363-b95b-3c0434c9726e

```
encoder_cudagraph.py _run_budget_graph -> model.prepare_encoder_cudagraph_replay_buffers
deepseek_v41/common/vl_cudagraph.py -> build_packed_vit_metadata
deepseek_v4/common/vision.py:282   cos = torch.cat(cos_list).to(device)
gpu_sync_debug.py:81 RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
```

CI runs with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. The encoder CUDA graph path added in #56625 syncs the host in two places. The `deepseek_v41` test entry has no `core_model` mark, so it only runs in the Extended lane, not on the PR.

1. `build_packed_vit_metadata` / `build_packed_merge_metadata` copy host tensors to the GPU with pageable `.to(device)` / `torch.tensor(..., device=...)`. The eager `DeepseekV4ViT.forward` RoPE tables do the same.
2. After (1) is fixed, `postprocess_encoder_output` fails next. It copies `types` with a pageable `.to()`, then builds the span with boolean-mask assignment (`index_put_` calls `nonzero`, which syncs).

## Changes

- `vision.py`: use `async_tensor_h2d` (pinned staging, `non_blocking`) for cos/sin, `cu_seqlens`, `merge_idx`, `merge_mask`, and the eager RoPE tables. `max_seqlen` stays on CPU.
- `vl_cudagraph.py::postprocess_encoder_output`: build the gather index on the host from `types`, which is a CPU tensor, and copy it with `async_tensor_h2d`. The span is then assembled with a single index into `[aligner rows, image_start, image_newline, image_end]`. The result is still a freshly allocated tensor, so later replays cannot overwrite it. I checked on CPU that this matches the old masked-fill output bit for bit, across several grids.

I left the eager `_build_image_span` unchanged. I also did not add `core_model` to the test entry: several other entries (step3_vl, ernie45_vl) are also Extended-only, and adding it would put a DSV4.1 model build into the per-PR Standard 4 lane. Reviewers can decide whether to promote it.

## Not a duplicate

On 2026-09-23 I searched open PRs for `deepseek v4 vision`, `vit cudagraph deepseek`, `56625`, `vl_cudagraph` and `deepseek gpu sync`. None of the results touch these code paths. The closest one, #57898, changes DSV4.1 profiling in `mm_preprocess.py` only.

## Test Plan / Results

I ran this on an H200 using the CI image `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:e9f167129c09` (main), with the patched files bind-mounted over the installed package:

```
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -v -s models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k deepseek_v41
```

- Before (unpatched image): `1 failed, 1 skipped`. It fails with the same `GPU<->CPU sync detected` in `build_packed_vit_metadata`, matching CI.
- With only the `vision.py` change: still fails, now at `postprocess_encoder_output` (`types.to(...)`).
- With both changes: `1 passed, 1 skipped` (video is skipped for this model). The log shows the encoder CUDA graph was captured and used, with no sync errors.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, mypy).

I have not run model evals. The span-assembly change is an exact rewrite, confirmed by the bit-for-bit CPU check. The H2D changes affect only how the copies are made, not the values.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fix Gemma AR+RMS prefill fallback
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose

1. Teach the AITER compilation pass to preserve raw Gemma weights and pass `gemma_norm` through the fused all-reduce op.
2. When custom all-reduce rejects a large prefill tensor, run the regular all-reduce followed by AITER's fused-add RMSNorm (the registered `vllm_aiter.fused_add_rms_norm` op, which gains a `gemma_norm` flag) instead of decomposing the norm into fp32 pointwise and reduction kernels. Keep Gemma inputs out of the QuickReduce fused RMSNorm path, which has no weight-bias mode.

On main alone, large prefill does not reach this fallback, so the speedup only shows up together with #57547, which sends prefill above the custom all-reduce pool through it.

---

## Test Plan

- Hardware: 8× MI355X (gfx950)
- Model: `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`
- Base: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-21d93d0d8c0e9627900020382bfce4730e61cab7`, each arm adds only the PRs listed; empty compile caches per run
- Serving A/B: ISL=60000, OSL=600, concurrency `{4, 32, 128}`, range-ratio=1.0
- Accuracy: GPQA diamond, 198 problems, thinking on, temperature=1.0, top-p=0.95, top-k=20, max-tokens=100000, num-threads=32. Same servers as the serving A/B.
- Unit tests:
  - `tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py` — Gemma prefill that misses 1-stage fused AR+RMS goes through regular all-reduce then `fused_add_rms_norm(..., gemma_norm=True)`, and never enters fused QR+RMSNorm
  - `tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py` — Gemma variants of the AR+RMS fusion tests; fused graph matches the unfused Gemma residual path

---

## Test Result

### Unit tests

Hardware: 2× MI355X, this PR's diff applied to the nightly above.

```bash
python -m pytest -v --tb=short \
  tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py \

Median TTFT and output throughput.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Respect max_output_tokens in the Harmony tool-call loop
author: errmakov
body:
## Purpose

When a gpt-oss (Harmony) request calls a built-in tool (browser, python, MCP), `_generate_with_builtin_tools` renders the next turn and resets `sampling_params.max_tokens` to `max_model_len - prompt_len`. That ignores the request's `max_output_tokens`, the server's default `max_tokens` from `generation_config`, and the `--max-tokens` override. So a request with `max_output_tokens=100` is capped on its first turn and then unbounded on every turn after it.

The first turn and the `ParsableContext` branch of the same loop already use `get_max_tokens()`. This PR makes the Harmony branch do the same. `HarmonyContext` now keeps the request, the way `ParsableContext` already does.

This is a rebased port of #38226 by @dubin555. That PR was closed by the stale bot after 120 days without a maintainer review, not for anything wrong with the change. The code has moved since then (`StreamingHarmonyContext` is gone, and the next-turn prompt now comes from `render_responses_harmony_messages`), so the original no longer applies. The original author is credited with `Co-authored-by`.

## Duplicate check

- `gh pr list --state all` keyword searches for "max_output_tokens harmony", "max_output_tokens tool", "harmony max_tokens" and "max_output_tokens responses". Among open PRs, only #38143, #39413, #58500, #58018, #42482 and #45386 are in this area. I checked their diffs, and none of them changes the `max_tokens` assignment in the tool-call loop. (#38143 and #39413 handle prompt truncation.)
- #38226 is the only earlier attempt at this fix. It was closed as stale.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_context.py -q
```

The new test, `test_harmony_tool_followup_respects_max_output_tokens`, runs one tool-call turn with `max_output_tokens=10` and `max_model_len=100` and records the `max_tokens` sent to the engine on each turn.

## Test Result

- Without the fix, the new test fails: `assert [10, 97] == [10, 10]`. The second turn got 97 tokens instead of 10.
- With the fix: `75 passed, 1 xfailed`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` (v0.14.0) are clean. Running mypy on the two changed source files gives the same error count before and after the change, and none of the errors are on the changed lines.

No GPU was available, so I did not run an end-to-end check against a gpt-oss model. The change only affects the `max_tokens` value passed to the engine on tool-call follow-up turns.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the compressor ring out of the null block
author: bluemelov1
body:
## Purpose

`_ring_slot_mapping_kernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/compressor.py`) maps each token to `block_table[req, 0] * capacity + pos % capacity`. Warmup and CUDA-graph capture run dummy batches whose block tables are zeroed, so their compressor state rows are written into **block 0**. That is the null block, and every KV-cache group shares it. The fp32 state bytes therefore land in other layers' pages. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, layer 2's ring overlaps the sliding-window KV of layers 0–13, and layer 8's overlaps layers 0–27.

Why it matters: sparse MLA decode kernels gather the null block for masked candidates and weight it by zero. When the bytes decode to a non-finite value, 0 × NaN is still NaN. On sm_120 (FlashInfer's DSv4 sparse decode) with DSpark speculative decoding and FULL CUDA graphs, this produced wrong outputs on the first request (0 accepted drafts), then `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` / Xid 31 MMU faults on the next prefill.

The bug is latent without DSpark too: block 0 still ends dirty (we measured 29 NaN bytes). It used to be masked because `warmup_kernels` ran after `capture_model`, and that warmup zeroed block 0 again. `gpu_worker.py` now runs `warmup_kernels` before `capture_model`, so the bytes survive into serving.

The fix maps tokens whose ring block is 0 to PAD (`-1`), which the ring consumers already skip. Real requests never own block 0, so their mapping is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- New `test_v41_compressor_ring_never_writes_the_null_block`, next to the existing `test_v41_compressor_metadata_maps_tokens_to_their_ring`: a dummy request on block 0 must map to PAD, and a real request next to it must keep its ring slots.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched files.

## Test Result

- Both tests pass with the fix. As a control, the new test fails without it: `assert [0, 1, 25, 26] == [-1, -1, 25, 26]`, i.e. the dummy tokens are written to slots 0 and 1 of the null block. This ran on an RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120) in the `nightly-e9757321` image with the patched `compressor.py`, using the two test functions verbatim (the full test file imports modules newer than that nightly).
- End-to-end on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8, DSpark (`num_speculative_tokens=5`), FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs, prefix caching, v0.30.0 plus our sm_120 page-geometry patch (needed to serve this model on sm_120 at all, and unrelated to this change):
  - without the fix: block 0 of every sliding-window layer is non-finite after capture, the first request decodes garbage, and the next ~1.6k-token prefill raises Xid 31;
  - with the fix: all 13 block-0 views stay clean through capture and 11,000 decode steps (including c16 load); needle retrieval 9/9, greedy determinism and shared-prefix divergence checks pass; 0 Xid; c1 131 tok/s, c16 672 tok/s, DSpark acceptance 0.38.
- Not verified: an end-to-end run on current `main`, and GPUs other than sm_120.

A related robustness point, arguably for FlashInfer: its SM120 DSv4 sparse decode is only correct while slot 0 is finite, because masked candidates still contribute 0 × V.

AI assistance was used to find this bug and write the patch and test. The tests above were run as described.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep logprobs of parser-suppressed streaming chunks
author: errmakov
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #37737. Supersedes #37738, #37795 and #37747. All three were auto-closed as stale with no maintainer review.

In streaming chat completions, if the parser returns `None` for a delta (for example, a tool parser swallowing the `<tool_call>` control token), `chat_completion_stream_generator` skips the whole chunk. That token's logprobs are lost with it. The bug is intermittent because it depends on how tokens are grouped into stream chunks: if `<tool_call>` arrives in the same chunk as visible text, its logprob survives.

`return_token_ids` already forces an empty-delta chunk for this reason ("to ensure all tokens are included in the response"). This PR does the same when logprobs are requested, so the concatenated streamed logprobs cover every generated token, as the non-streaming response already does.

Concerns raised by automated review on #37738, and how this PR handles them:
- **Leaking hidden reasoning** (`include_reasoning=false`): not possible. `hide_stream_metadata` (#44301) already sets `logprobs = None` before this check. The new test covers this case.
- **Reasoning/control markers such as `<think>` now appear in streamed logprobs**: this is intended. Non-streaming `logprobs.content` already includes them, and `return_token_ids` already emits them.
- **`tool_choice="required"`**: every mode now goes through `parser.parse_delta` and this one check, so it is covered too.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k suppresses_delta -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py
```

The new test `test_streaming_logprobs_kept_when_parser_suppresses_delta` streams two outputs through a parser that returns `None` for the first one (`<tool_call>`). It then checks which logprob tokens are streamed:
- `include_reasoning=True`: `["<tool_call>", "answer"]`
- `include_reasoning=False`: `[]` (metadata stays hidden)

## Test Result

- New test before the fix: `AssertionError: assert ['answer'] == ['<tool_call>', 'answer']`. After the fix: 2 passed.
- `test_serving_chat.py`: 40 passed. The 10 `RemoteOpenAIServer` GPT-OSS tests error at setup with `Failed to infer device type` because this machine has no GPU. They do not depend on this change.
- `pre-commit`: ruff check, ruff format, mypy, typos all pass.

I have not run a model eval. The change only affects which SSE chunks are sent when `logprobs=true`; generated text is unchanged.

## Notes

- Duplicate check: keyword searches (open and closed PRs) for streaming logprobs / tool_call / suppressed delta / `delta_message None logprobs` found only the three stale PRs listed above. No open PR touches this branch.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. I have reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Disagg] Allow MoRIIO HMA per-layer block_len
author: avininjamay8
body:
## Purpose

MoRIIO KV cache registration under HMA requires a uniform `block_len` across attention layers. Hybrid models (GLM-5.2 DSA, MiniMax, Gemma4) register layers with different per-layer `block_len` / `block_size` (e.g. `9216` vs page default `2112`). Registration then raises:

```
ValueError: MoRIIO KV cache block length mismatch for layer ...: 9216 != 2112
```

and PD bring-up fails at health-gate. Layer transfers already size RDMA from per-layer geometry; the uniform check is stricter than the transfer path.

## Changes

`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py` (KV registration):

- Allow divergent per-layer `block_len` (bytes) always; log at debug per layer; advertise `max(block_lens)` to the peer with a single summary `logger.info`.

title: [Bugfix] Keep JIT warmup under enforce-eager when fault tolerance is on
author: njhill
body:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58197 disabled JIT warmup in eager mode. Fault-tolerant deployments run peer-fault detection against deadlines, and in-inference Triton compilation latency spikes can delay detection past the deadline: the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E job became flaky right after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58197 landed (rank 0 misses the test's 45s detection deadline when the injected
fault trips while kernels are still compiling mid-serving).

Keep `enable_jit_warmup` on when parallel_config.enable_fault_tolerance is set, so kernels compile during startup warmup instead of during serving.

title: [Bugfix][FT] Pass stateless process-group timeouts explicitly
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
In `get_cpu_distributed_timeout_or_none`, we get the gloo timeout from `vllm_config.parallel_config.cpu_distributed_timeout_seconds`, which awkwardly is not set when we call `stateless_init_torch_distributed_process_group` in `vllm/config/parallel.py` (ultimately `stateless_init_torch_distributed_process_group` calls `get_cpu_distributed_timeout_or_none`). For fault tolerance, the gloo timeout needs to be shorter than the faulted rank's recovery waiting time: `engine_recovery_timeout_sec`, which defaults to 120 seconds. Fix issues like [Buildkite #90967](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90967/list?jid=01a0d41b-5f76-429a-a17e-5f7107a6333e&tab=output) AI generated details below
Details

## Summary Fix the recovery hang in [Buildkite #90967](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90967/list?jid=01a0d41b-5f76-429a-a17e-5f7107a6333e&tab=output). EngineCore's Gloo group received the 30-minute default instead of the configured 30 seconds because initialization read an unset global config. The survivor stayed blocked in `all_reduce` while its faulted peer waited for retry. Pass timeouts explicitly from the caller's config during group creation and recovery. The helper no longer reads global config; `None` uses PyTorch's backend default. **For fault tolerance, the collective timeout must be shorter than the faulted rank's remaining recovery wait: `engine_recovery_timeout_sec` (120 seconds here).** Allow margin for coordination and retry, while accommodating healthy execution skew. The test uses a 30-second collective timeout and a 45-second detection deadline. Duplicate searches found no matching fix. #58593 covers JIT warmup; #51404 covers recovery-port allocation. This change is independent of #58473. ## Validation Two H200s, original failing CI image (`5323584b7b`) with changed source files overlaid: ```bash UCX_NET_DEVICES=ibp0:1 /work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \ tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_fault_tolerance_e2e.py /work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/test_config.py \ -k dp_group_uses_configured_timeout_without_current_config ``` - E2E: **1 failed, 1 passed → 2 passed**, including recovery and serving. - CPU regression: **fails before, passes after** (0.62 s). Checks the timeout passed to Gloo creation without global config; no processes or collectives. - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files `: **passed**. - Model computation is unchanged; no separate accuracy evaluation was run. ## AI assistance Codex assisted with implementation, testing, and this description. Draft pending human review.

title: [Bugfix][Outlines] Fix EOS termination and unconstrained masks after rejected drafts
author: njhill
body:
`outlines_core` never advances on EOS: in a final state its mask allows only EOS, but `advance(EOS)` raises and `accepts_tokens([EOS])` is `False`. `OutlinesGrammar` papered over this with a side-effecting `is_terminated()` that delayed the finished flag by one call. That caused:

- Every completed outlines request was terminated with `FINISHED_ERROR`, since the scheduler's `accept_tokens([EOS])` returned `False` (#57723).
- With spec decode, `is_terminated()` is polled several times per step, so the delay was consumed mid-step and grammar-valid drafts were rejected during bitmask fill. The manager then wrote fully unconstrained masks for every later row and the bonus row, letting grammar-illegal tokens be sampled and committed (e.g. the IPv4 regex producing `'9.1.2.3\n\n'` in `test_structured_output[...outlines-auto-speculative_config6]`).
- `rollback()` did not restore the delay state.

Track termination explicitly in `OutlinesGrammar`, mirroring `XgrammarGrammar`: EOS is accepted only in a final guide state (without advancing the guide), tokens after it are ignored, `is_terminated()` is a pure read, `rollback()` undoes an accepted EOS, and `validate_tokens()` agrees with `accept_tokens()` on EOS.

Harden `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask()`: after a draft is rejected during fill, copy the row filled from the last valid grammar state into the remaining rows and the bonus row instead of leaving them unconstrained. The row is copied rather than refilled because some backends (`llguidance`) enter a sticky error state after consuming a rejected token.

Fixes the main issue from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57723 and current CI failures like https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90994/list?jid=01a0d45a-e568-4ac2-83b7-3538da8007ac&tab=output.

PR by claude opus 5.5.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Anchor the partial-tail lookup on the full-attention prefix
author: nvyutwu
body:
## Purpose

Split out of #57216 per @orozery's review (part 1 of 2): the lookup half. The DCP store half is #58619.

`_lookup` anchors the partial-tail search on `_lookup_complete_chunks`, which requires *every* KV cache group to have a complete chunk at the anchor boundary, including the recurrent groups. A recurrent `align` group holds state only where a scheduler step ended on one of its block boundaries: in practice at the producer prompt's last full recurrent block and at its tail.

With **uniform block sizes** (dcp=1, the only shape `supports_partial_tail` admits today) the last-full-block boundary is also a full-attention chunk multiple, so that aligned row lands on the chunk grid, `complete_hit` reaches it, and the existing one-window probe finds the tail. The anchor only fails when that row is missing, e.g. evicted separately from the tail. So on `main` today this is a robustness fix.

With **mixed block sizes** -- under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp x` the attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8) -- the aligned row sits at a recurrent multiple that is essentially never a full-attention multiple. `complete_hit` is then 0 for any prompt past the first chunk, the search is capped at one window from zero, and a correctly stored tail further out is never probed although it is resident. That is the state #58619 (the DCP store side) would land in without this PR: tails get stored, but only those within one window of the complete-chunk hit are ever found -- the "#58619 only" column of the hardware table below. **This PR is the prerequisite for #58619's lookups to work.**

Instrumented `_lookup` on a replay (chunk 12288, hash 128), before the change:

```
n=12620  complete_hit=12288  complete_boundary=12288  max_boundary=12544
           boundary=12544 ALL GROUPS HIT                  <- restores
n=15136  complete_hit=0      complete_boundary=0      max_boundary=12160
           boundary=12160 group=0 MISS ... 11776 MISS     <- tail stored at 15104,
                                                            never probed
```

Fix: anchor the partial-tail search on the boundary the full-attention groups proved, which `_lookup_complete_chunks` already returns (since #63566), and check recurrent groups only at the candidate boundary. Per review, the search runs from one window past the anchor down to the complete-chunk hit and skips block-aligned boundaries (complete chunks, which the complete-chunk lookup already missed), so a longer full-attention prefix stored by another request cannot hide this request's own tail. If a full-attention chunk between the complete hit and the anchor is still being loaded, the search falls back to the complete hit. No second lookup and no new parameters.

The reported hit is never shorter than the complete-chunk hit, so the change can only widen what a lookup reports. Pending full-attention chunks are handled exactly as in the complete-chunk lookup on `main`.

## Test Plan

Unit tests on the existing dcp=1 hybrid fixture (`_make_partial_tail_scheduler`: 16-token full-attention and Mamba blocks, hash 4):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

- tail found with no recurrent state at the chunk boundary (30-token prompt, tail at 28)
- the same across **two** complete chunks (46-token prompt, tail at 44): the production shape, where the complete-chunk anchor is 0
- a longer full-attention prefix stored by another request does not hide this request's own tail, including when that prefix covers the whole prompt (per review)
- the load path requests only the verified chunk keys plus the tail keys
- `max_num_new_tokens` caps which tail the search may report
- a tail is found after a GPU prefix hit
- 0 when no tail was stored; 0 when the full-attention chunk is not resident
- the tail is preferred over an aligned recurrent state at the chunk boundary
- the search falls back while the anchor chunk is being loaded

## Test Result

**Unit tests** (`pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/`, GB300, same image), base `main` @ e318ac0979:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | 690 passed, 3 failed |
| this PR | 707 passed, 3 failed |
| this PR + #58619 | 721 passed, 3 failed |

The 3 failures are the same on `main` at this commit: `test_partial_tail_store_uses_attention_and_recurrent_cow_sources` and `test_eagle_partial_tail_round_trip_serves_mamba_checkpoint[True/False]` expect a recurrent group's CPU `BlockStored.block_size` of 0, which is 4 since #62613. `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes.

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-2b009fc6`; "fix" overlays the branch's `vllm/`, "main" is the stock nightly). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP2, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. "fix" is this PR + #58619.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| prompt tokens | DCP1: `main` | DCP1: fix | DCP2: `main` | DCP2: fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1541 | 1536 | 1536 | **0** | **1536** |
| 12549 | 12544 | 12544 | 12288 | **12544** |
| 24069 | 24064 | 24064 | **0** | **24064** |
| 39685 | 39680 | 39680 | 38912 | **39680** |

- **DCP1:** identical to `main` on every prompt (no regression).
- **DCP2:** every prompt restores to its last hash boundary.
- **All trials:** replayed greedy output (32 tokens) is identical to both the cold run and a GPU-prefix-cache replay, with 0 allocation failures. The same numbers reproduced on a second GB300 cluster on the previous rebase.

<details><summary>Earlier revision, per PR (TP4, DCP1/DCP4), measured before the review changes</summary>

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-29468dde8b` with only `offloading/scheduler.py` replaced). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP4, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. Recurrent block 512, full-attention offload block 2048 at DCP4 (512 at DCP1), hash 128: the K3 shape (1536 / 12288 / 128) scaled down.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| prompt tokens | best boundary | DCP1: `main` | DCP1: this PR | DCP4: #58619 only | DCP4: #58619 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 645 | 640 | 640 | 640 | 640 | 640 |
| 2309 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 |
| 2565 | 2560 | 2560 | 2560 | **0** | **2560** |
| 2949 | 2944 | 2944 | 2944 | **0** | **2944** |
| 3717 | 3712 | 3712 | 3712 | **0** | **3712** |
| 4101 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 |
| 4485 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 |
| 17029 | 17024 | 17024 | 17024 | **0** | **17024** |
| 2949, replay diverges at 2700 | 2560 | 2560 | 2560 | **0** | **2560** |

- **DCP1:** this PR is identical to `main` on every trial, including store and load bytes. That is the expected no-regression result: the aligned row is on the chunk grid there, so the anchor equals `complete_hit`.
- **DCP4:** without this PR, only tails within one window of the complete-chunk hit are found. With it, every prompt restores to its last hash boundary.
- **All trials:** replayed greedy output is byte-identical to the cold recompute (32 tokens), with 0 allocation failures and no errors in the server logs.

</details>

An earlier run of the combined change on a 2-node GB300 K3 deployment (TP8/DCP8) is in #57216.

## Notes

- Related: the DCP store-side half is in #58619. Both are standalone and merge cleanly together (verified; the merged tree passes the suite).
- Not duplicating an existing PR: #52832 fixed the analogous producer-side gap for the Mooncake connector; #52397 covers the `max_offload_tokens` cap in the store path, which this PR does not touch. #63566 also uses the full-attention boundary, to pin a shared-prefix junction for the next request; this PR uses it to find a tail that is already stored, so they are complementary.
- AI assistance (Claude, Codex, Devin) was used to draft code and tests; every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Count reasoning tokens for Harmony, DeepSeek-V3 and Step3 parsers
author: sammaji
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

  ## Purpose

`/v1/chat/completions` always reports `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens: 0` for gpt-oss, even though `message.reasoning` is populated. `/v1/responses` reports the count correctly for the same prompt.

Chat Completions gets the count from `parser.count_reasoning_tokens(token_ids)` (added in #45802). `HarmonyParser` doesn't override it, so the call falls through `DelegatingParser` to `GptOssReasoningParser`. That parser only detects reasoning boundaries, so it inherits the base `ReasoningParser.count_reasoning_tokens`, which returns `0`. `HarmonyParser.process_chunk()` already counts reasoning tokens for the Responses API, but Chat Completions never used that count.

The same always-zero result affects two other parsers with no open fix:

  - **`deepseek_v3` / `holo2`**: `DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser` passes every method to its wrapped R1/identity parser except `count_reasoning_tokens`, so it always returns 0.
  - **`step3`**: `Step3ReasoningParser` never implemented counting.

  ### Changes

  - `HarmonyParser.count_reasoning_tokens`: counts with a fresh `StreamableParser`, so the instance's streaming state is untouched. This matters because Chat Completions calls it after `parse()` (non-streaming) and after each chunk with the
  cumulative token IDs (streaming).
  - The channel rule (`analysis`, or `commentary` with a recipient) moves into `_is_reasoning_token`, shared by `process_chunk()` and `count_reasoning_tokens()`, so Chat Completions and Responses report the same number.
  - Harmony control tokens (`<|message|>`, `<|end|>`, …) are no longer counted as reasoning. This matches #45802, where engine parsers exclude `<think>`/`</think>` boundary terminals. **Behavior change:** Responses API `reasoning_tokens`
  for gpt-oss drops by about 1 per reasoning message or tool call (previously `<|message|>` was counted).
  - `DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser.count_reasoning_tokens` passes the call to the wrapped parser. With the R1 template the `<think>` start token is in the prompt, so a non-zero count for that case also depends on #49743.
  - `Step3ReasoningParser.count_reasoning_tokens` counts the tokens before the first `</think>` (all tokens if it's absent), matching its existing `extract_reasoning`.

  ### Why this is not a duplicate

  - #56914 (per-request reasoning/content token metrics, +1186/-37, open, awaiting review) also adds `HarmonyParser.count_reasoning_tokens`, as part of a larger opt-in metrics feature. This PR is the small, standalone bug fix for the
  user-visible usage field, so it can land independently. If #56914 merges first, I'll rebase onto it or close this in its favor.
  - Other open PRs cover different parsers: #58372 (Kimi K3), #54091 / #54238 / #54585 (Muse Glimmer), #50240 (Poolside), #49743 (base thinking parser without a start token). None touch Harmony, `deepseek_v3` or `step3`.
  - Out of scope: `granite`, `hunyuan_a13b` and `olmo3` detect markers in decoded text rather than by token ID, so counting needs a text-to-token mapping. `minimax_m2_append_think` intentionally returns reasoning inside `content`.

  ## Test Plan

  Unit tests (CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty`, tokenizers only):

  ```bash
  pytest tests/parser/test_harmony.py \
         tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv3_reasoning_parser.py \
         tests/reasoning/test_step3_reasoning_parser.py \
         tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_context.py \
         tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py -q

  New tests:
  - TestCountReasoningTokens in tests/parser/test_harmony.py:
    - the count matches process_chunk().reasoning_token_count for analysis plus a tool call
    - a final-only output gives 0
    - control tokens are excluded (the count equals the analysis text's token count)
    - counting doesn't disturb the streaming parser's state
  - test_count_reasoning_tokens_delegates in tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv3_reasoning_parser.py: thinking on/off.
  - New tests/reasoning/test_step3_reasoning_parser.py. Step3 had no test file; test_step3p5_reasoning_parser.py covers a different parser.

  End-to-end check with openai/gpt-oss-20b:

  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b
  curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-oss-20b",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    "reasoning_effort": "high"
  }' | jq .usage

  Test Result

  Unit tests: 150 passed, 1 xfailed. Without the source changes, the 4 new tests that expect a non-zero count fail (Harmony test_matches_process_chunk, DeepSeek-V3 thinking=True, both Step3 tests).

  ruff check / ruff format --check: pass.

  End-to-end, gpt-oss-20b, same prompt:

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Fix startup with config-only model
author: louie-tsai
body:
## Purpose

Fix Rust frontend startup when the model is provided through `--config`.

When running:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve --config config.yml
```

the resolved model is stored in `args.model`, while `args.model_tag` remains unset. The Rust frontend bootstrap requires `model_tag` in `--args-json`, causing startup to fail with:

```text
invalid JSON arguments: missing field `model_tag`
```

This was reproduced with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` through the vLLM Recipes flow.

## Changes

- Fall back to `args.model` when `args.model_tag` is not set.
- Explicitly pass the resolved model as `model_tag` to the Rust frontend.
- Add a regression test for config-only model selection.

This keeps positional model behavior unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
python3 -m pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py \
  -k "rust_frontend"
```

Manual validation:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
vllm serve --config config.yml
```

Verify the Rust frontend `--args-json` includes:

```json
"model_tag": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B"
```

and the server starts without the `missing field model_tag` error.
