title: [Bugfix][Core] Uncount stop-trimmed spec tokens from num_computed_tokens
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

When a speculative decode step stops on an accepted draft (EOS, a stop token, or `max_tokens` reached before the bonus token), `_update_request_with_output` trims the step's later tokens, but `num_computed_tokens` keeps counting them. Rejections are rolled back in `update_from_output`; trimmed tokens are not.

Ordinary requests are freed right after the stop, so the count is never read again. A resumable (streaming-input) request continues: `_update_request_as_session` uses `num_computed_tokens` as the fold boundary, so the next chunk starts "already computed" over positions whose KV belongs to the trimmed drafts.

Prompt `[1, 2, 3]`, `max_tokens=2`, k=2. The prefill samples `10`; a step with drafts `[11, 12]` returns `[11, 12, 13]` (both accepted) and stops at `11`. Folding in the next chunk `[7, 8]`:

| | `all_token_ids` | `num_computed_tokens` | next step computes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | `[1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 7, 8]` | 6 | `8` only; `7` reuses draft `12`'s KV |
| this PR | `[1, 2, 3, 10, 7, 8]` | 4 | `7, 8` |

The fix uncounts the trimmed tokens, so `num_computed_tokens` again covers all new tokens but the last kept one. The fold then drops that token exactly as it drops the final sampled token of a non-speculative turn, which is what makes a session's output identical with and without speculative decoding (see the GPU check below).

Under async scheduling the trimmed tokens' placeholders were never released either (`num_output_placeholders` was decremented by the post-trim count), so they are released too. `num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders` is unchanged, so neither the async `cache_blocks` frontier nor the `C - P` frontier from #58259 moves.

This count is also what stale block-hash truncation keys on (#52806, and the `del session.block_hashes[num_computed_tokens // hash_block_size:]` suggested on #58259): with the overshoot, the cut point lands too late and leaves stale hashes behind.

Diffusion schedulers inherit the change; resumable diffusion requests were not exercised.

## Not a duplicate

- #44526 clamps `num_computed_tokens` to `num_prompt_tokens` after the fold. That catches only an overshoot past the whole new chunk (`num_new_tokens <= 0`); in the example above it is a no-op and `7` is still skipped. This PR fixes the count where it goes wrong.
- #58259 (merged) fixed the async handoff race. Its `C - P` frontier also covers this case under async scheduling, but not under sync scheduling, where `num_output_placeholders` is always 0. This PR keeps `C - P` unchanged, so the two compose.
- #54979 caps its terminal `cache_blocks` call at `request.num_tokens` to work around the same overshoot; the cap stays correct.
- Searched open and closed PRs and issues for streaming input + speculative decoding, `num_computed_tokens` trimming, and `_update_request_as_session`; no other PR fixes this.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding -v
```

New test: `test_next_chunk_fully_computed_after_stop_on_accepted_draft` (scheduler, sync and async scheduling): after the trimmed stop, the fold drops the last kept token and the next chunk is scheduled in full.

GPU check, run manually and not kept in CI: a 6-chunk streaming session (opt-125m, fp32 + FLEX_ATTENTION, greedy, `max_tokens=2` per chunk) must produce the same tokens and logprobs with and without ngram speculative decoding (k=4), with drafts accepted. The greedy tokens of this repetitive prompt do not change with the context, so logprobs are what catch the difference.

## Test Result

- Scheduler test: the sync case fails on main and passes with the fix. The async case passes on main since #58259 and is kept to check that this PR's `C`/`P` accounting still composes with it.
- `test_scheduler_streaming.py` + `test_scheduler.py` + `test_async_scheduler.py`: 221 passed.
- `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input` (CPU): 797 passed. The 1 failure and 6 errors (`test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e`, `test_scheduler_e2e`) need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU on GB200:
  - Streaming session check, main: diverges from the second chunk on, e.g. logprobs `[-0.3593, -0.5455]` with ngram vs `[-0.3427, -0.7063]` without.
  - Streaming session check, this PR: tokens match and logprobs agree to ~1e-5; `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py` passes.
  - Async spec-decode regression check (the placeholder accounting change applies to every async spec request, not only streaming): `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding` passes, all 6 configs (sync/async, preemption, chunked prefill, mp/uni executor) match the non-speculative baseline in outputs and logprobs.
  - `ngram` is not yet supported by Model Runner V2, so the streaming session check uses the V1 model runner. The fix is in the scheduler and runner-independent. Async scheduling is covered by the scheduler test only.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][CI] Report subprocess test skips as skips, not passes
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

**Split out of #50519.** Code only; the affected tests are already collected by
existing jobs.

**A skipped test is currently reported as passed.**
`spawn_new_process_for_each_test` runs the test body in a fresh interpreter and
decides the outcome from the child's exit code alone. The child catches
`Skipped` and exits 0 so a skip is not mistaken for a crash, but nothing carries
the skip back, so the parent records a pass. A test that never ran counts as
green.

**The reach is wider than the decorator's direct users**, since it is also
applied through `create_new_process_for_each_test` and `multi_gpu_test`. What
matters is where the skip happens: a collection-time marker is evaluated in the
parent and is fine, while a `pytest.skip` inside the test body runs in the child
and is lost. `tests/compile/fusions_e2e/test_tp2_ar_rms.py` does that in four
places, so those combinations report as passing today without ever executing.

**The fix reuses the file already carrying tracebacks.** The child serializes
the skip reason into `tb_file` before exiting 0, and the parent reads `tb_file`
unconditionally rather than only on failure. A recorded reason plus a clean exit
means the child skipped, so the parent re-raises it. JSON is used because the
reason is arbitrary text that has to round-trip exactly. The failure path is
untouched: a non-zero exit still raises `RuntimeError` with the child traceback,
and a native crash still leaves `tb_file` empty.

## Test Plan

`tests/utils_/test_spawn_decorator.py`, with a new case that runs the existing
intentionally-skipped test through a nested pytest and requires the outer report
to show one skip carrying the original reason.

## Test Result

4 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed. `test_spawn_decorator_skip` is now reported as
`SKIPPED` instead of as a pass, attributed to the parent:

```
SKIPPED [1] tests/utils.py:2002: intentional skip
```

Line 2002 is the new `pytest.skip` in the parent, so the reason recorded by the
child reached the report through the intended path.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Preserve literal values in Guidance disable_additional_properties
author: abhayjoshi201
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58695.

When `StructuredOutputsConfig.disable_additional_properties=True` is enabled for the Guidance structured-output backend, `process_for_additional_properties()` previously walked all nested dictionary and list values indiscriminately via `_walk_json_for_additional_properties()`. As a result:
1. Object literals inside `const`, `enum`, `default`, or `examples` that happened to contain a `"properties"` or `"patternProperties"` key (e.g., GeoJSON Features) had `"additionalProperties": false` injected into the literal value, causing the compiled `llguidance` matcher to reject the valid literal value and accept the mutated one instead.
2. Property maps containing a property named `"properties"` or `"patternProperties"` also had `"additionalProperties": false` injected directly into the `properties` map.

This PR updates `_walk_json_for_additional_properties()` in `vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py` to recurse only into schema-bearing keywords (`_SCHEMA_MAP_KEYWORDS` and `_SUBSCHEMA_KEYWORDS`), preserving literal instance values (`const`, `enum`, `default`, `examples`) and property maps unchanged.

### Duplicate Check
Checked open PRs searching for `58695`, `process_for_additional_properties`, `_walk_json_for_additional_properties`, and `disable_additional_properties`. No existing open PR addresses this bug (#57592 only touches `backend_xgrammar.py`).

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Stop the host pool feeding device KV cache residency metrics
author: eopXD
body:
> **NOTE:** This PR was reduced to a one-line change: the HiSparse host pool no longer gets the device pool's metrics collector (`metrics_collector=None` in `HiSparseSourceManager.bind_host_pool`), so host blocks stop feeding the device `vllm:kv_block_*_seconds` histograms. That removes the block-ID collision described below at its source, instead of keying samples by pool. Host-tier residency metrics are proposed separately in #59485 (on top of #58949). The description below is the original.

## Purpose

With HiSparse and `--kv-cache-metrics`, the host and GPU pools share a metrics
collector, but each pool numbers its blocks independently. The collector keys
samples by `block_id` alone.

This results in incorrect metrics recording in KV cache block activities
when using HiSparse.

A false lifetime, idle-time, and reuse-gap histogram will affect users
relying on it to investigate cache turnover and reuse.

For example, allocate GPU block 1 at t=1 s and host block 1 at t=2 s. The host
allocation currently emits a false one-second GPU eviction sample, even though
the GPU block remains allocated. With this fix, **both histories remain active
and no eviction sample is emitted**.

This MR key samples by `(block.pool, block.block_id)` in allocation, access
and eviction callbacks. Allowing the KV cache block activities to be correctly
accounted.


The callbacks only update telemetry; allocation and eviction decisions are
unaffected. Ordinary hybrid/SWA groups sharing one pool retain their existing
behavior.


## Test Coverage

`test_hisparse_host_pool_preserves_device_lifecycle`
(`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py:59`) verifies the
production-wiring example. The test fails with metrics enabled without the fix.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Gather nvfp4_ds_mla chunked-context KV with the NVFP4 kernel
author: stu-cao
body:
## Status (2026-10-15)

Reworked after @zyongye's review (thanks — every point was right) and @LucasWilkinson's stu-cao/vllm#2, which proposed the same `seq_starts` change; rebased onto `main` `19b0efce30`. Lucas's kernel-level test (random cache bytes, non-block-aligned starts, bit-exact against the same slots gathered without starts) is included as his commit in `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py`. Where this differs from #2: the BF16 workspace hunk is dropped (zyongye's point 1, it was unreachable) and DCP is rejected at startup instead of being left to fail in the generic gather (point 4).

- **`seq_starts` on the NVFP4 gather kernel** instead of a block-table shim. `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache` gains an optional `seq_starts` like its fp8 twin (`token_offset = out_token - workspace_starts[req] + seq_starts[req]`), and the dense dispatch passes `chunk.starts` exactly as the `fp8_ds_mla` branch does. `shift_block_table_to_starts`, its alignment precondition, the clamp, the per-chunk gather and its CPU test are gone. Other callers are unchanged (the argument defaults to `None`).
- **Dropped the `MLACommonMetadataBuilder` workspace hunk and the `fp8_query` test arm.** `nvfp4_ds_mla` is only accepted by `FlashMLASparseBackend`, whose builder (`SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder`) allocates its own BF16 workspace and hard-codes a BF16 prefill query, so neither was reachable.
- **DCP is rejected at startup** (`VllmConfig.validate_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_mla`) instead of in the per-layer forward on the first request with context; covered by `tests/test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism`.
- The raw `kv_c_and_k_pe_cache` pass is intentional: the `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache is allocated as `torch.uint8`. The three other gather dispatch sites that still send `nvfp4_ds_mla` to the generic gather (`mla_attention.py` DCP path, `kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py`, `sparse_mla_attention.py`) are unreachable today and left for a follow-up.

Verification on the rebased head (`dc6aa4ae53`, B300 SM103, from-source build): **17 passed, 0 failed** — `test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py` (1, the `seq_starts` path on real NVFP4 rows), `test_mla_context_chunks.py` (14), `test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism` (2); registered schema `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache(..., int batch_size, Tensor? seq_starts=None)`; torch 2.14.0+cu130, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3a`. `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k nvfp4`: 27 passed including `test_cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_seq_starts`.

## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` crashes in the MLA chunked-context prefill:

```
mla_attention.py  _compute_prefill_context
_custom_ops.py    gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache
RuntimeError: get_fp8_kv_cache_data_type, csrc/attention/dtype_fp8.cuh:34,
              Unsupported fp8 kv cache data type: nvfp4_ds_mla
```

`MLACommonBaseImpl._compute_prefill_context` gathers each chunk's cached context KV into a BF16 workspace. It has a branch for `fp8_ds_mla`; every other dtype goes to `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache`, which only knows the fp8 variants. The NVFP4 upconvert kernel added with the `nvfp4_ds_mla` format, `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache`, is never called here.

Sparse MLA reaches this path through its dense-MHA prefill: a prefill whose total length is `<= index_topk` and that has cached context. In practice:

- **speculative-decoding warm-up**: the dummy batch takes this path, so an engine with `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV and a DFlash draft never finishes starting;
- **chunked prefill splitting a short prompt**: the continuation step has context;
- **prefix-cache hits** on short prompts.

Longer prefills use the sparse FlashMLA kernels, which already handle `nvfp4_ds_mla`.

**Fix:**

- Route `nvfp4_ds_mla` to `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache`.
- Give that kernel an optional `seq_starts` (csrc + bindings + `_custom_ops`), mirroring `cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache`: a continuation chunk reads from its context start instead of the request's first token. Without it, every chunk after the first would silently re-read the request's first tokens.
- Reject `nvfp4_ds_mla` with decode context parallelism at config validation; that combination is not validated.

Other dtypes are unaffected. I found no existing issue or PR for this.

## Test Plan

New tests:

- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py` (SM100). Writes random KV into an `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache with `concat_and_cache_mla`, then runs `_compute_prefill_context` on it. The reference is the same method on a BF16 cache holding the dequantized values, through the generic gather. Every chunk must see bit-identical Q/K/V; the batch includes a chunk that continues one request and starts another.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py::test_cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_seq_starts` (SM100): the kernel's `seq_starts` with non-block-aligned starts, bit-exact against a full gather.
- `tests/test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism` (CPU).

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py tests/test_config.py -k "nvfp4 or context_chunks"
```

End-to-end on 1 × GB200 node (4 GPUs), run with the first revision of this change (block-table shift; same gather semantics):

- **Model:** GLM-5.3 (NVFP4 weights) + DFlash2 draft (fp8 KV, k=4).

title: [Bugfix][Logging] Preserve application log record factories
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #57957. If an application imports vLLM, installs a log-record factory adding `request_id`, then initializes vLLM, logging configuration replaces that factory with the import-time snapshot. A formatter using `%(request_id)s` now fails with `ValueError: Formatting field not found in record: 'request_id'`, dropping application logs.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Detect Anthropic inline-system merge against the resolved chat template
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58727.

`/v1/messages` checks whether the chat template accepts inline `role: "system"` messages, and merges them into the leading system block if it doesn't. The check was run on the `--chat-template` CLI value, which is usually `None`, and `None` means "merge". So every deployment merged, including GLM-5.3, whose template accepts inline system messages. Claude Code adds a `<total_tokens>` system message every turn, so the leading block changed on every request and the rest of the prompt missed the prefix cache.

Changes:
- Run detection on the template the renderer actually uses (`resolve_chat_template`), checking both the tool and non-tool variants. Applies to the Anthropic and render servers.
- Log a startup warning when merging is required, since it defeats prefix caching.

Not a duplicate: no open PR targets #58727. #56520, #53501, #52978 and #47681 change other parts of inline-system handling and are complementary.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -q
vllm launch render zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --reasoning-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47
python glm_cache_hit.py render   # script below
```

## Test Result

`pytest`: 110 passed. `pre-commit`: clean.

Prefix cache hits for a 6-turn Claude Code-style GLM-5.3-Flash session (script below). Hits are the tokens each turn shares with the previous turn's prompt, rounded down to 16-token cache blocks.

| turn | main: cached / prompt | main: recomputed | PR: cached / prompt | PR: recomputed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2208 / 2342 (94.3%) | 134 | 2272 / 2347 (96.8%) | 75 |
| 3 | 2224 / 2430 (91.5%) | 206 | 2336 / 2437 (95.9%) | 101 |
| 4 | 2224 / 2506 (88.7%) | 282 | 2432 / 2515 (96.7%) | 83 |
| 5 | 2240 / 2566 (87.3%) | 326 | 2512 / 2577 (97.5%) | 65 |
| 6 | 2256 / 2624 (86.0%) | 368 | 2576 / 2637 (97.7%) | 61 |
| **total** | **89.4%** | | **96.9%** | |

On `main`, the cache hit stops after the system prompt and tools, so recomputation grows with the length of the conversation. With the PR, only each turn's new tokens are recomputed. Run the script with `live` against `vllm serve ... --enable-prompt-tokens-details` to measure real `cache_read_input_tokens`.

Model evaluation: not yet run. GLM now sees inline system messages where the client placed them rather than in the leading system prompt.

<details><summary>glm_cache_hit.py (sample prompts)</summary>

```python
"""Prefix-cache hit rate for a Claude Code-shaped session on /v1/messages.

Each turn resends the whole conversation plus one tool call, its result and
the inline ``<total_tokens>`` system reminder Claude Code appends every turn.

  render: vllm launch render MODEL ... ; python glm_cache_hit.py render
          best-case hit = block-aligned prefix shared with the previous turn
  live:   vllm serve MODEL --enable-prompt-tokens-details ... ;
          python glm_cache_hit.py live
          measured hit = usage.cache_read_input_tokens
"""

import argparse
import json
import urllib.request

MODEL = "zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash"
SYSTEM = [
    {"type": "text", "text": "x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=2.1.281; cch=abc"},
    {"type": "text", "text": (
        "You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. You help users "
        "with software engineering tasks: fixing bugs, adding features, "
        "refactoring and explaining code. Prefer dedicated tools over shell "
        "commands, keep answers short, and verify changes by running tests. "
    ) * 40},
]
TOOLS = [{"name": "Bash", "description": "Run a shell command.",
          "input_schema": {"type": "object",
                           "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}},
                           "required": ["command"]}}]
STEPS = [
    ("git status --short", "M vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py"),
    ("ls vllm/entrypoints/anthropic", "__init__.py\napi_router.py\nprotocol.py\nserving.py"),
    ("grep -n merge_inline_system vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py",
     "148:        self._merge_inline_system = ...\n325:        if merge_inline_system:"),
    ("wc -l vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py", "1712 vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py"),
    ("pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic -q", "110 passed in 40.51s"),
    ("git diff --stat", " 2 files changed, 30 insertions(+), 12 deletions(-)"),
]


def session_turn(n: int) -> dict:
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "Find where inline system messages are "
             "merged in the Anthropic endpoint and check the tests pass."},
            {"role": "system", "content": "# Environment\n - Platform: linux"}]
    left = 15_000_000
    for i, (cmd, out) in enumerate(STEPS[:n]):
        msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"type": "thinking", "thinking": f"Next I run `{cmd}`.", "signature": ""},
            {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{i}", "name": "Bash",
             "input": {"command": cmd}}]})
        msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": f"toolu_{i}", "content": out}]})
        left -= 1_000 * (i + 1)
        msgs.append({"role": "system",
                     "content": f"<total_tokens>{left} tokens left</total_tokens>"})
    return {"model": MODEL, "max_tokens": 1, "system": SYSTEM,
            "tools": TOOLS, "messages": msgs}


def post(url: str, body: dict) -> dict:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"content-type": "application/json"})
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("mode", choices=["render", "live", "dump"])
    ap.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8020")
    ap.add_argument("--block-size", type=int, default=16)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    turns = [session_turn(n) for n in range(1, len(STEPS) + 1)]
    if args.mode == "dump":
        print(json.dumps(turns, indent=2))
        return

    hit = total = 0
    prev: list[int] = []
    for i, body in enumerate(turns, 1):
        if args.mode == "render":
            ids = post(f"{args.url}/v1/messages/render", body)["token_ids"]
            k = 0
            while k < min(len(prev), len(ids)) and prev[k] == ids[k]:
                k += 1
            n, cached = len(ids), k // args.block_size * args.block_size
            prev = ids
        else:
            usage = post(f"{args.url}/v1/messages", body)["usage"]
            cached = usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens") or 0
            n = (usage["input_tokens"] + cached
                 + (usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens") or 0))
        if i > 1:  # turn 1 is a cold start
            hit, total = hit + cached, total + n
        print(f"turn {i}: prompt={n:5d} cached={cached:5d} ({cached / n:6.1%})")
    print(f"turns 2-{len(turns)}: {hit}/{total} prompt tokens cached "
          f"({hit / total:.1%})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
</details>

title: [Bugfix] Register IR providers before hashing configuration
author: matteso1
body:
## Purpose

A model-info cache hit can leave IR providers unregistered when `IrOpPriorityConfig.compute_hash()` reads their implementation UUIDs. The lookup raises `KeyError`, and the API fingerprint falls back to `nohash`.

Call `current_platform.import_ir_kernels()` before that lookup, as the priority-setting path already does. This keeps implementation UUIDs in the hash without depending on an incidental model-inspection import. No matching open fix was found in the provider/hash searches.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep resumable sessions that stop while preempted
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58776.

With async scheduling, a resumable (streaming-input) request can be preempted while a step is still in flight. That step's output is delivered as stale output, and if it hits a stop condition the request stops in `PREEMPTED` state. Two things then go wrong:

1. **The session drops out of every queue.** `_handle_stopped_request` re-enqueues the resumable request, but the stopped-while-preempted cleanup in `update_from_output` removes it from `waiting`, `kv_holding_waiting` and `deferred_waiting`, including that new entry. The session is then in no queue and is never scheduled again. (Still the case after the queue rework in #58947 and the handoff fix in #58259.)
2. **The fold deletes the prompt.** `_update_request_as_session` keeps `all_token_ids[num_prompt_tokens:num_computed_tokens]` and deletes the rest. After preemption `num_computed_tokens == 0`, so it deletes the whole list, while `prompt_token_ids` (a separate list) is only extended; `num_prompt_tokens` then no longer matches `all_token_ids`, and the previous turn's output is lost.

Changes:

- After the stopped-while-preempted cleanup, re-enqueue requests that did not finish, so each ends up in exactly one queue.
- In the fold, keep up to `max(num_computed_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`. On a normal stop `num_computed_tokens == num_tokens - 1`, so nothing changes; after preemption the session keeps all but the final sampled token, and `num_computed_tokens` stays 0 so everything is recomputed.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for this path (`stopped_preempted_reqs`, streaming/resumable + preempt, `_update_request_as_session`, session hang symptoms); none found. #58668 fixes a different case where `num_computed_tokens` is wrong at the fold (a speculative step stopping on an accepted draft). Both PRs append a test to `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, so whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -k stop_while_preempted
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py -v
```

New tests in `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, using a real `AsyncScheduler`:

- `test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted` (next chunk queued before / after the stop) reproduces #58776. It asserts that the session is scheduled again, that `all_token_ids` and `prompt_token_ids` both hold the old prompt, the kept output and the new chunk, and that everything is recomputed.
- `test_non_resumable_request_stays_dequeued_after_stop_while_preempted` guards the re-enqueue: a request that finishes while preempted must stay out of the queues. It passes on main and fails if the `is_finished()` check is dropped.

## Test Result

`test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted`, with each half of the fix:

| scheduler | result |
| --- | --- |
| main | both cases fail: tokens are `[20, 21]` (prompt and output lost) |
| re-enqueue fix only | both fail: same token loss |
| fold fix only | both fail: `KeyError`, the session is never scheduled |
| this PR | both pass |

- CPU, `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input`: 806 passed with this PR vs 804 on main. The only difference is the two cases above; the remaining 1 failure and 6 errors need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py`: 14 passed.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/streaming_input` + the GPU-only core tests above: 19 passed, 2 errors. The errors are `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py`, which fails identically on main: engine profiling hits `assert prefill_query.shape[0] == num_prefill_tokens` in the FlashInfer backend with `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` on this machine.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line.

</details>

## Impact (update)

Besides the client-visible hang, the parked variant leaks scheduler capacity. When the session stops while preempted with no continuation queued, it is parked as `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` and `num_waiting_for_streaming_input` is incremented — and the queue cleanup then drops the session from every queue. If no continuation ever arrives, the counter is never decremented: each occurrence permanently consumes one `max_num_active_reqs` admission slot (the `num_running = len(self.running) + self.num_waiting_for_streaming_input` accounting in `schedule()`), so repeated occurrences silently shrink admission capacity. Verified locally on main: after the preempted stop, the parked case leaves `num_waiting_for_streaming_input == 1` with the session in no queue; if a continuation later arrives the counter rebalances in `_update_request_as_session`, but the session itself is already lost.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stream DeepSeek V4/V3.2 string tool arguments incrementally
author: jayzuccarelli
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52846.

DeepSeek V4, V4.1 and V3.2 streamed a long string tool argument as one fragment when `</｜DSML｜parameter>` arrived. The configs set `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, so the engine skipped every plain body delta.

The fix now uses the per-parser `arg_value_extender` hook, the same way GLM (#61253) and Gemma4 (#61494) do. The earlier engine-level gate change is dropped.

- `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py`: `_dsml_arg_value_extender` returns an extender while the last parameter is an open `string="true"` value. Each delta streams as escaped JSON text without rerunning the converter. It stops on a parameter tag, keeping a tail so a tag split across deltas is caught.
- Wired into `deepseek_v4_config`, `deepseek_v32_config`, and `deepseek_v41_config` (spaced DSML tags via `functools.partial`).
- `_param_patterns`: the trailing-partial regex holds back an unfinished next `<｜DSML｜parameter` tag, so a streamed value never includes it (implicit close case).

- `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py`: `test_streaming_long_string_argument_is_incremental` (4096-char body in 32-char chunks, needs >1 non-empty body delta and exact round-trip), `test_streaming_non_string_argument_is_withheld_until_close`, `test_streaming_string_argument_with_markup_is_incremental`.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Reject draft slots that were never proposed
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Purpose

On a P/D decode instance, Model Runner V2 verifies draft slots its drafter never proposed. After the remote KV load the request resumes with one token left, and the scheduler pads that step with `k` placeholder drafts of `-1` (#45237, #55126). MRV2 fills those slots from `req_states.draft_tokens`, which are still zeros, so the rejection sampler verifies `k` real token-0 drafts against a stale draft distribution. With probabilistic drafting at T > 0 and block verification all `k` are accepted: on main, 71/80 MT-Bench responses through 1P1D start with at least 8 NUL tokens (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` + `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark`, `k=8`). MRV1 is not affected (#47029).

Fix: `RejectionSampler` gathers the verified tokens and positions with a Triton kernel that sets the draft rows of any step starting within the prefill (first position < `prefill_len`) back to `-1`, which the rejection kernels already reject. Drafts are only proposed after sampling past the prefill, so these rows are always placeholders. No new request state, and `input_ids` is unchanged.

#54102 (open) also restores these placeholders, via scheduler-side counts; this PR is a standalone runner-side fix with no scheduler changes. #58434 assumes these placeholders are rejected.

## Test Plan

- New `test_verify_rejects_unproposed_drafts`. Also ran the rejection-sampler, spec-decode and MRV2 worker suites, and `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k spec_decode_padding`.
- E2E on GB300, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=8`, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`, `rejection_sample_method=block`. Topologies: 1P1D (TP4 + TP4, `NixlConnector`) and co-located TP4. Workloads: 80 MT-Bench prompts at T=1 (count responses starting with NUL), the same prompts greedy (byte-compared with main), and GSM8K 5-shot.

## Test Result

| | NUL-prefixed (T=1) | Greedy vs main | GSM8K strict |
|---|---|---|---|
| P/D, main | 71/80 | – | – |
| P/D, this PR | 0/80 | 80/80 identical | 0.9545 |
| co-located, main | 0/80 | – | – |
| co-located, this PR | 0/80 | 80/80 identical | 0.9575 |

Unit tests pass.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Document 404 response for `/generative_scoring`
author: njhill
body:
_check_model returns 404 (NotFoundError) when the request names a model that is not served, but the /generative_scoring route only documented 200/400/500 in its responses. Since #57729 made GenerativeScoringRequest a FastAPI body parameter, the request body (including the optional "model" field) is now part of the served OpenAPI schema, so the schemathesis-based test_openapi_stateless fuzz test started generating random model names and hitting the undocumented 404, e.g.:

  SUBFAILED entrypoints/openai/test_openai_schema.py::test_openapi_stateless[POST /generative_scoring]
  schemathesis.openapi.checks.UndefinedStatusCode: Undocumented HTTP status code
  Received: 404
  Documented: 200, 400, 500, 422

Add HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND to the route's responses, matching every other serving router (completion, chat_completion, tokenize, scale_out, ...).

This fixes flaky CI test, example: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91237#01a0d982-85c8-4a3d-a152-b406bc7685ce.

author: baljinderhothi-cohere
body:
## Purpose

Fix the Inkling function name leaking into streamed `delta.content` when a tool call follows a thinking block (`--reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling`).

`<|end_message|>` (`THINK_END`) emitted `REASONING_END` immediately, so the two-pass `DelegatingParser` handed off to the tool pass before the next block opener, and the function-name header after `<|message_model|>` was emitted as content. This defers `REASONING_END` for `THINK_END` inside a reasoning block; the next typed opener already emits it from `MESSAGE_HEADER`. `END_SAMPLING` still ends reasoning immediately.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Refresh DSpark context KV cache pointers after the KV cache is re-bound
author: okorzh-amd
body: ##Purpose Fixes a GPU memory fault and silent memory corruption in the Kimi-K3 DSpark draft, introduced by #57632. ``` 21:05:36 JIT kernel warmup finished (all 8 ranks) Warning: Queue error - HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT Memory access fault by GPU node-14 ... on address 0x7ec3c95b0000. Reason: Unknown. 21:15:38 [Rank 0..7] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: _ALLGATHER_BASE ... 600000 ms RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed ``` K3DSparkModel caches the per-layer KV cache base pointers, and the block-layout flag, on first use and never rebuilds them. Since #57632 captures the context K/V precompute in the draft CUDA graph, that first use now happens during the CUDA graph memory-profiling capture. That capture runs against a temporary KV cache that is freed afterwards. The real KV cache is then allocated at different addresses, but the draft keeps the stale pointers, so every later context K/V insert writes into freed memory. This change keys both cached values on the live kv_cache.data_ptr() tuple and rebuilds them when it changes. The pointer array is updated in place, so captured graphs keep reading live pointers. The rebuild only runs on eager calls; an assert guards against it running during capture. kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py is the only K3 DSpark implementation and is used on every platform, so this also applies to CUDA. It was only tested on ROCm. ##Test Plan - 8x MI355X, Kimi-K3 TP8 + DSpark (ROCM_AITER_MLA, fp8 KV cache), nightly 29468dde (which contains #57632). - Recipe config for the conc-4 cell: --max-num-seqs 8, K=5, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, 8k/1k random prompts. ##Test Result

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor endpoint plugin route overrides
author: shaohuaxi
body:
## Purpose

Endpoint plugins are documented to support overriding core routes, but core routes are registered first and win during request dispatch. For example, a plugin can register `GET /version` successfully while requests still reach the built-in handler. OpenAPI can meanwhile describe the plugin's handler, so the schema and actual response disagree.

This change replaces earlier HTTP operations when a plugin registers the same path template and method. Other methods remain available, and the last registered plugin operation takes precedence. Plugin hooks still run after core router registration. The OpenAPI cache is also cleared so the schema reflects the routes that handle requests.

The endpoint plugin documentation is updated to describe these rules.

Duplicate-work check on September 26, 2026: searched open and closed endpoint-plugin issues and PRs and found no existing fix for this behavior.

## Test Plan

Run the existing plugin and HTTP status metrics suites against this checkout. `TEST_PYTHON` points to the Python executable in the CPU test environment.

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
"$TEST_PYTHON" -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/plugins_tests/test_endpoint_plugins.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/test_http_status_metrics.py
```

The added cases exercise HTTP dispatch and OpenAPI through FastAPI's ASGI interface, covering core route overrides, hook access to core routes, preservation of other methods, and conflicts between plugins.

## Test Result

- **30 passed**: 18 plugin tests and 12 HTTP status metrics tests.
- All six added regression cases fail on the unpatched baseline, `bbc4ddeca`.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve caller parameters in offline pooling
author: shaohuaxi
body:
## Purpose

`LLM.encode()` writes its internal pooling task into the caller's `PoolingParams`. Reusing `PoolingParams(use_activation=False)` first with an `embed` LLM and later with a separate `token_embed` LLM fails before inference:

```text
You cannot overwrite param.task='embed' with pooling_task='token_embed'!
```

Each instance keeps its own configured task. The problem is the first call leaving that task in the shared parameter object.

Clone each request's parameters before assigning the task in the base offline IO processor, and before calling the plugin's `merge_pooling_params()`. BGE-M3 and ColBERT change the parameters during that merge, before reaching the base processor. The existing check for an explicitly conflicting task stays unchanged.

I checked existing issues and PRs for parameter reuse and task mutation and found no matching fix. #50884 handles `SamplingParams` seeds and does not change this path.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py \
  tests/test_pooling_params.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_late_interaction_serving.py \
  -q -p no:cacheprovider

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/io_processor.py \

```

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix receive post-process for different P/D block sizes
author: lucamotz
body:
## Purpose

NixlConnector pull with a smaller `--block-size` on P than on D writes wrong KV on D, or crashes D when a rank holds fewer KV heads than `block_size_ratio`. The receive post-process indexes attention views as `[B, N, H, D]`; since #44455 they are `[B, H, N, 2*D]` on every layout.

- `kv_postprocess_blksize_on_receive`: drop the two "physical order" permutes. On `LBHNC` they scramble every received block; with fewer heads than `block_size_ratio` the reshape fails.
- `post_process_device_kv_on_receive`: zero the untransferred tail along the token dim, not the head dim.
- `kv_postprocess_blksize_and_layout_on_receive` (`enable_permute_local_kv`): read the received bytes in memory order before viewing them as the remote's head-major blocks. It now also serves ratio 1 and replaces `kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive`, which had the same bug and a 5-D branch from #47791 that is dead since #51718.
- `enable_permute_local_kv` is enabled only for a local `LBNHC` cache; any other local layout (e.g. head-major `BLHNC`) now fails the handshake instead of receiving wrong KV.
- HMA groups alias the same KV tensors, but each group's block ids went through every attention view, regrouping a block once per aliasing group. Each group now uses its own views.
- `LBNHC`/`BLNHC` receive the remote sub-blocks in token order; only `is_block_contiguous` layouts are regrouped.

Block lists that start or end at different tokens on P and D are paired in #59746. No other open PR changes the receive post-process.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -k test_post_process_zeroes_untransferred_tail
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k test_handshake_fails_on_kv_cache_layout_mismatch
```

The test now holds distinct values in a `[B, H, N, C]` cache with fewer KV heads than the ratio, aliased by two attention groups, on `LBHNC`, `LBNHC` and `LBNHC` + `enable_permute_local_kv`.

GB10: P and D on one GPU, pull, greedy, `--enforce-eager`. Each run is compared with P and D both at D's block size, without `enable_permute_local_kv`; D loads the whole prompt over NIXL, except the last token on GDN or with #59330.

## Test Result

CPU, main `0cbac6cd13`: the 3 cases pass, and reverting any one fix fails at least one of them. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

GB10, main `0cbac6cd13`:
- Qwen3-0.6B, FLASH_ATTN, `LBHNC`, P 16 / D 64: 0/6 outputs match.
- `LBHNC` P to `LBNHC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`, 64/64: 0/6.
- Gemma-4-E2B-it, TRITON_ATTN, 1 KV head, 16/64: D's EngineCore fails with `shape '[-1, 4, 128, 0, 512]' is invalid`.

GB10, this PR at `ef0cc618a0` on main `0cbac6cd13`, logprobs bitwise equal:
- Qwen3-0.6B 16/64 on `LBHNC`, `BLHNC`, `LBNHC`, and `LBHNC` P to `LBNHC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`, the last also at 64/64: 6/6 each.
- Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN), FLASH_ATTN, 544/1088: 6/6, also with two attention groups forced by a local grouping hook.
- Gemma-4-E2B-it 16/64 no longer crashes; 4/7 outputs still differ in text. With #59746 and #59330: 7/7.

GB10, main `dd30786fef` + this PR's files at `0ccf122132`, MiniCPM5-2B (2 KV heads), `LBHNC` P to `BLHNC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`: main crashes D at 16/64; without the handshake check, 0/4 outputs match at 16/64 and 64/64 with no error. With it, the handshake fails and D keeps serving; an `LBNHC` D stays bitwise equal (4/4) at both.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, patch and tests. I reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Use prefiller cache hits for P/D usage
author: thuongvu
body:
## Purpose
Fix `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` in Rust P/D responses.

The decoder currently counts KV received from the prefiller as cached tokens. That can make a cold request look fully cached, even though the prefiller computed the entire prompt.

The Python frontend already handles this through `remote_prefill_cached_tokens` (#54222). This change reads the same metadata in Rust and uses it for response usage:

- Use the prefiller's count when `do_remote_prefill` is `true`, including an explicit zero. The parameters are read through a small typed view, so a non-boolean flag or a count that is not a non-negative integer leaves the decoder's count in place.
- Keep the existing decoder count when no usable override is available.
- Include `cached_tokens: 0` when prompt-token details are enabled. This also applies to ordinary local requests.
- Keep decoder metrics based on the raw engine statistics.

No new wire fields or prompt-length upper clamp are added.

Related-work searches found no matching open Rust fix. #58730 proposes bounds handling in Python; #56318 concerns cache-source metrics.

## Test Plan
From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p vllm-llm -p vllm-server --lib --tests
cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-llm -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
```
The added tests cover metadata parsing, positive and zero overrides, missing-count fallback, streamed and collected usage, unchanged decoder metrics, and explicit-zero JSON serialization.

## Test Result
Validated against `a9eafde59cbd`:

- The mock-engine regression fails without the fix and passes with it.
- 454 tests passed: 15 LLM unit, 11 LLM integration, and 428 server tests.
- Clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed.

Also tested with real NIXL transfers on two H100 GPUs using Qwen3-0.6B. Across chat and completions, streaming and non-streaming, eight baseline cases reproduced the bug and eight patched cases reported the correct prefiller count. Detailed setup and results are in the follow-up comment.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix race on AITER MLA FP8 prefill scheduling metadata under async scheduling
author: amd-mghanimi
body:
Fixes #58886

## Purpose

Fixing `Memory access fault`

**Type:** bugfix. **Backend:** `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, FP8 KV cache, gfx950 (FP8 ASM prefill). **Affected:** MLA models served with async scheduling on this path (Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V3, TP8, MI355X). 

On this configuration the CPU and the GPU get out of sync. `aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1` writes its plan into persistent device buffers with a copy that is not ordered on the current stream, so the next step can replace metadata the current prefill is still reading.

This PR gives `aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1` two pinned host output buffers and copies the active buffer on the current stream. A CUDA event on each buffer waits until that copy has finished before the buffer is reused.

Reproduction and analysis: [vllm-project/vllm#58886](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58886). No AITER change. Follow-up: [ROCm/aiter#5879](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5879).

## Test plan

1. Kimi-K3
   - performance
   - accuracy
2. DeepSeek-V3
   - performance
   - accuracy
3. Existing unit tests

## Test results

MI355X, TP8, ROCm 10 nightly (`29468dde`), FP8 KV cache, async scheduling. Commands are in [vllm-project/vllm#58886](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58886).

**1. Kimi-K3**

Performance, `sglang.bench_serving` random 8k/1k, on streams that do not crash before the fix:

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (before / after) | Median ITL (before / after) |

| 32 | 1083.0 / 1082.6 | 18.14 / 18.14 ms |

| 64k, 32 | 0.922 | 0.928 |
| 128k, 32 | 0.888 | 0.888 |

**2. DeepSeek-V3**

Performance: no throughput was measured. Before the fix, the 8k/1k stream (concurrency 32, 1024 prompts, seed 4) crashes at request 111. After the fix, it completes 1024/1024.

Accuracy, `lm_eval` gsm8k 5-shot, flexible-extract, `num_concurrent=64`:

| before, async scheduling | GPU memory fault (x2) |
| after, async scheduling | 0.657, 0.673, 0.666 |
| before, `--no-async-scheduling` | 0.739, 0.691 |
| before, bf16 KV (FP8 prefill path off) | 0.671 |

The unpatched runs without async scheduling vary by about 3 points from run to run. The fixed runs fall within that spread and match the bf16 KV run, where this code path is off.

`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py` passes 9/9, and the other 634 AITER MLA cases also pass. Before and after are identical.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix M-RoPE offset double-count in Qwen3-Omni
author: C1ves
body:
get_mrope_input_positions treated PlaceholderRange.offset as the index of the modality-start token (<|vision_start|>/<|audio_start|>), but the prompt replacement machinery only replaces the pad token, so offset points at the first pad token and the start token is already covered by the preceding text segment. The extra bos slot emitted per media item made the assembled positions one slot longer than the token span: prompts ending with a media item always hit the "Position ids length mismatch" RuntimeError (fatal to EngineCore), and prompts with trailing text got silently misaligned M-RoPE positions from the first pad token onward.

Drop the redundant bos slot and fix the st advancement in each media branch (image/audio/video/audio-in-video) so the emitted position count always equals seq_len. Add unit tests covering media-at-prompt-end for each modality and exact positions for media followed by text.



## Purpose

`Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration.get_mrope_input_positions` misinterprets `PlaceholderRange.offset`: the prompt replacement machinery only replaces the pad token, so `offset` points at the first pad token and the modality-start token (`<|vision_start|>` / `<|audio_start|>`) is already covered by the preceding text segment. The function instead treats `offset` as the modality-start index and emits an extra bos slot per media item, making the assembled positions one slot longer than the token span:

- Prompts ending with a media item (e.g. custom/transcription-style chat templates) always hit `RuntimeError: Position ids length mismatch with input ids length`, which is fatal to EngineCore.
- Prompts with trailing text (stock chat template) don't crash, but every M-RoPE position from the first pad token onward is silently misaligned by one slot — a correctness bug on all multimodal requests.

This drops the redundant bos slot and fixes the `st` advancement in each media branch (image/audio/video/audio-in-video) so the emitted position count always equals `seq_len`. The audio-in-video value structure (shared bos/eos positions) is preserved, consistent with the Qwen2.5-Omni behavior in HF.

Follow-up to GHSA-328w-h674-qp56 (per maintainer feedback, the crash path requires an operator-chosen chat template; this PR fixes the offset handling itself).

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py -v
```

New unit tests use synthetic input_ids + `MultiModalFeatureSpec` (no GPU/weights needed):
- `test_mrope_positions_{image,audio,video,audio_in_video}_at_prompt_end`: prompt ending exactly at the modality-end token must yield `positions.shape == (3, seq_len)`.
- `test_mrope_positions_image_then_text`: media followed by text must produce the exact expected per-position values.

## Test Result

Before the fix: all 5 tests fail — the 4 media-at-prompt-end cases raise `RuntimeError: Position ids length mismatch` (the engine-death path), and the image-then-text case fails on misaligned position values.

After the fix: all 5 tests pass.

```
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_image_at_prompt_end PASSED
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_audio_at_prompt_end PASSED
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_video_at_prompt_end PASSED
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_audio_in_video_at_prompt_end PASSED
tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py::test_mrope_positions_image_then_text PASSED
```

title: [Bugfix] Fix the two multimodal root tests that fail on main (OpenPangu-VL embed merge, MiMo sink test fixture)
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Six test files at the root of `tests/models/multimodal/` run in no CI job: `test_aria.py`, `test_cohere_asr.py`, `test_conformer_encoder.py`, `test_mimo_v2_omni.py`, `test_nano_nemotron_vl.py`, `test_openpangu_vl.py`. None has a `core_model` marker. The only jobs that sweep `models/multimodal` select `-m core_model` or `-m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)'`, so all six are deselected. The plan is to add a `find models/multimodal -maxdepth 1` root sweep to Extended Generation 1 (proposed on #56901). Before that can land, the files have to pass, and two of them fail on `main`:

- **`test_openpangu_vl.py`, both cases.** #55941 fixed `OpenPanguVLForConditionalGeneration.get_input_embeddings` and added this test. #54142 was branched before #55941 and merged after it, and it brought back the old body with a `# type: ignore[call-overload]`. That body passes `(input_ids, inputs_embeds, embeddings, token_ids)` to `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids`, which raises `TypeError`. This PR puts #55941's `is_multimodal` mask back. mypy passes without the ignore. The model runner calls `embed_input_ids` rather than this method, so serving is unaffected, but anyone calling this public method directly gets the `TypeError`.
- **`test_mimo_v2_omni.py::test_window_attention_applies_sinks[2]`.** `vision_attn_env` was module-scoped. The autouse `cleanup_fixture` in `tests/conftest.py` tears down the TP group after every test, so the second parametrization always fails with `tensor model parallel group is not initialized`. The fixture now builds on the function-scoped `dist_init`. `dist_init` also cleans up afterwards, so later files in the same pytest process can set up their own groups. The old fixture never tore down its NCCL group, which broke `test_aria.py` / `test_conformer_encoder.py` whenever they ran after it.

## Not a duplicate

- No open PR touches `OpenPanguVLForConditionalGeneration.get_input_embeddings`. #58571 and #56390 edit OpenPangu's video path. #58235 edits `mimo_v2_omni.py` model code, not this test.
- #53959 wires the `tests/` root files, not `tests/models/multimodal/`.
- The CI wiring itself is a review suggestion on #56901, which rebuilds Extended Generation 1, so it doesn't conflict with that stack.

## Test Plan

Ran in the CI image for `main` (`vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:c8d7a7dd13e2`) on one H200, with the two changed files mounted in. The command is the root sweep proposed for #56901:

title: [ROCm][Model][Bugfix] Fix GLM-5.2 shared-expert fusion and MTP on the ROCm DSA path
author: jin-amd
body:
#51915 aliased `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` onto `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/`. That enabled GLM-5.2-MXFP4 there, but it also moved GLM-5.2-FP8 onto a path missing two things the model needs, so the AMD command from the [GLM-5.2 recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/zai-org/GLM-5.2) now fails twice on ROCm:

1. **`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` can't load the checkpoint** — `KeyError: 'layers.10.mlp.shared_experts.down_proj.weight'`. With fusion on, the checkpoint gives one widened `mlp.shared_experts` tensor per layer. `deepseek_v2.py` splits it into the expert slots appended after the routed experts, but `DeepseekV32Model` subclasses `torch.nn.Module` rather than `DeepseekV2Model`, reimplements `load_weights`, and has no equivalent handling.

2. **MTP kills the engine on the first request** — `AttributeError: 'DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor' object has no attribute 'compact_topk_indices'`. `llm_base_proposer` calls that method once `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is set, which GLM-5.2's config sets. `nvidia/mtp.py` implements it; `amd/mtp.py` never did.

Before #51915, GLM-5.2 fell through to the generic `deepseek_v2` implementation on ROCm, which handles both. This adds the missing pieces rather than changing the routing, so MXFP4 keeps the AMD path.

## Changes

- `amd/model.py`: set `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled`, size the expert params mapping to `n_routed_experts + n_shared_experts`, and split the widened shared-expert tensor into `mlp.experts.{n_routed_experts + j}` — dim 0 for the ColumnParallel gate/up, dim 1 for the RowParallel down. Ported from `deepseek_v2.py` to keep both paths consistent.
- `amd/mtp.py`: add `compact_topk_indices`, matching `nvidia/mtp.py`. The ROCm attention already maintains `skip_topk` and `topk_indices_buffer`, so it ports over unchanged.

## Test Plan

8x MI325X (gfx942), `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, recipe AMD command unmodified (fusion on, 5-token MTP on). Baseline `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` at `0.30.1rc1.dev143+g29468dde8`; patched run is the same image with these two files replaced.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter
```

## Test Result

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Weight loading | `KeyError` at `layers.10` | completes |
| KV cache @ 524288 | n/a | 1,668,416 tokens, 3.18x concurrency |
| First request | `AttributeError`, engine dies | returns normally |
| MTP | unusable | active, mean acceptance length 3.41 |

Correctness checked too, since a bad tensor split would give fluent-but-wrong output rather than an error: `17 * 23` → `391`, capital of Peru → `Lima`, `Is 91 prime?` → 822 chars of reasoning then the correct 7 x 13, and a correct three-sentence Rayleigh-scattering answer with `enable_thinking: false`. The `glm47` parsers behave as before.

I only have gfx942, so MI300X and MI355X are untested — the changed code is shared ROCm model code with no gfx-specific branching, but an MI355X run from someone would be welcome. MXFP4 on the AMD path is untouched here but likewise unverified.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Emit buffered post-reasoning text when no tool parser is configured
author: dhairyashilRG
body: ## Purpose With an engine-based reasoning parser and no tool parser, streaming can drop the text right after the end of reasoning. For example, with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3 --stream-interval 2` and the greedy prompt "Reply with only this exact HTML and nothing else: `hello`", the answer is `"\n\nhello"` without streaming but `"hello"` when streamed. It happens when one delta carries several tokens around ``. When reasoning ends inside a delta, `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` gets the text the engine held back from `finish_streaming()` and adds it only to `current_text`, which is the tool parser's input. With no tool parser, nothing emits it. #47606 added this flush for the reasoning-to-tool case. This PR emits the text as content when there is no tool parser. The fix is in `abstract_parser.py` because every engine-based reasoning parser is affected (14 of 15, see below). Not a duplicate: I searched open and merged PRs for stream interval, multi-token deltas, `finish_streaming` and `abstract_parser.py`. #51669 edits the same block, but for non-engine parsers and a different bug. #55210, #53924 and #39044 change the non-engine `BaseThinkingReasoningParser`. None of them fixes this case. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/parser/test_streaming.py -k no_tool_batched_holdback pytest tests/parser tests/reasoning tests/tool_parsers tests/v1/structured_output ``` - Every engine-based reasoning parser, no tool parser: stream `plan it\n\nbold a < b done` (with the parser's own markers) in 60 random chunkings of 1-4 tokens and compare the content with `parse()`. - End to end on GPU: compare streamed and non-streamed content of greedy chat and Responses requests. ## Test Result - New test (3 cases): fails on main, passes with this PR. - Suites: 6877 passed (main: 6874; the difference is the new tests). Both have the same 15 setup errors, from a gated Llama tokenizer. - Chunkings whose streamed content differs from `parse()`: | parser | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | deepseek_v4, deepseek_v41, glm45, glm47, kimi_k2, ling3, mimo, minimax_m2, mistral, nemotron_v3, qwen3, seed_oss | 17/60 | 0/60 | | gemma4 | 33/60 | 0/60 | | granite_thinking_parser | 8/60 | 0/60 | | inkling | 0/60 | 0/60 | ling3, nemotron_v3 and inkling used the Qwen3 tokenizer; the others used their own model's tokenizer. - End to end, 1x L4, 8 greedy prompts, requests whose streamed content differs (chat / Responses): | model, `--stream-interval` | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | Qwen3-0.6B, 1 | 0/8 / 0/8 | 0/8 / 0/8 | | Qwen3-0.6B, 2 | 3/8 / 3/8 | 0/8 / 0/8 | | Qwen3-0.6B, 4 | 3/8 / 3/8 | 0/8 / 0/8 | | Qwen3-1.7B, 2 | 3/8 / 3/8 | 0/8 / 0/8 | Each non-streamed request was sent twice; all pairs matched, so the differences are not nondeterminism. AI assistance: I used an AI assistant (Claude) for parts of the analysis, the patch and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.

title: [Bugfix][Compile] Replace Transformers AOT caching with graph caching
author: Taimys
body:
## Purpose

Fix compilation caching for the Transformers backend by running Dynamo tracing on each startup while reusing PyTorch graph caches.

Decorated HF `forward` methods can fail model-AOT serialization. Disabling model AOT alone is insufficient: direct artifact lookup can reuse stale compiled code when decorator state changes between processes.

Following the review suggestion, HF opts out through `support_torch_compile(..., use_aot_compile=False)`. The option is passed explicitly through `init_backend` to the backend, compiler manager, and adaptors:

- Skip model AOT, mega artifacts, and direct artifact loading/saving, including existing cache-index lookup.
- Retain PyTorch graph caching and initialize persistent Inductor/Triton cache directories.
- Preserve native AOT caching, including native EAGLE3 drafts under an HF target.

This replaces the earlier `CompileCachePolicy`, owner ContextVar, and loader changes. The opt-out applies in `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`; cache-disable settings remain respected. HF does not attempt forced model-AOT loading when opted out.

Related to #50128, specifically compilation caching. Follows the graph-caching recommendation in #53295 and preserves the cache-relocation behavior from #52142. This addresses HF cache routing rather than the cache-key API migration in #39517 or empty-artifact validation in #56879.

## Test Plan

- Fresh-process regression for changed decorator closure state, warm graph-cache hits, and repeated forward calls, covering both Inductor adaptors.
- Native AOT save/load after an opt-out module runs under the same configuration.
- Functorch configuration restoration on normal/exceptional exit and hash calculation; bypass of existing direct-cache metadata and handles.
- Three HF models and a native control under two cache-persistence protocols; real TP=2 and full HF-target/native-EAGLE3 generation.
- Full Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K evaluation under the batch-invariant compilation configuration described below.

## Test Results

### Warm startup: 8.9%–10.5% less time with persistent caches

Before is main at `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`; After is the smaller implementation described above.

Single L20, TP=1, BF16. Each model/backend/version/protocol has **1 cold + 5 fresh-process warm runs**, alternating A/B order. Values are `LLM(...)` initialization **median [min, max] in seconds**, excluding imports.

For the primary protocol, both versions receive persistent Inductor/Triton cache-directory settings. Caches are isolated by model/backend/version, and each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. Worker paths are verified because vLLM may redirect Inductor to its own persistent subdirectory.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 20.344 [20.105, 20.953] | **18.204 [17.595, 18.343]** | **10.52%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 15.570 [15.160, 16.111] | **14.121 [13.734, 14.297]** | **9.31%** |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 27.830 [27.769, 28.155] | **25.355 [25.183, 25.572]** | **8.89%** |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.857 [11.723, 11.978] | 11.719 [11.659, 12.030] | Ranges overlap |

The HF results are consistent in magnitude with the earlier 8–10% observation. No native speedup, throughput improvement, or TTFT improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Supplement: only VLLM_CACHE_ROOT persists</summary>

Inductor/Triton directory overrides are unset; each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. This measures the case where only the vLLM cache root persists, rather than ordinary same-user restarts.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 30.274 [30.041, 31.056] | **18.180 [17.794, 18.358]** | **39.95%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 25.188 [24.725, 25.983] | **14.109 [13.875, 14.304]** | **43.98%** |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 37.718 [37.262, 38.034] | **24.810 [24.631, 25.560]** | **34.22%** |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.909 [11.545, 12.693] | 11.958 [11.618, 12.532] | Ranges overlap |

The **34.2%–44.0%** reduction is specific to this protocol. Compared with explicit lower-level caches, HF Before is 9.62–9.93 s slower; After differs by 0.011–0.545 s. Worker paths and cache counters support a cache-persistence explanation, without establishing per-kernel attribution. Independently compiled caches and shared-host load also limit cross-protocol attribution.

Native median changes are −1.17% with explicit caches and +0.41% with root-only persistence. Ranges overlap in both protocols; no consistent native regression or speedup is established.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cold timings and reproducibility</summary>

| Model / backend | Explicit Before / After, s | Root-only Before / After, s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 46.855 / 44.519 | 47.267 / 45.283 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 37.518 / 35.636 | 37.459 / 36.782 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 56.375 / 54.423 | 56.104 / 52.939 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 51.503 / 51.999 | 52.575 / 51.835 |

- **96/96 starts completed; all 96 cache checks passed.** No samples were discarded. These are new measurements of the smaller implementation, not reused smoke timings.
- Baseline: `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`.
- Measured patch SHA256: `5edec6ae4c933e25df921c1c1d045b2ff277c0d8c56ed473ac12f99a2b2bf4eb`.
- Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Transformers 5.15.1, Triton 3.7.1. A/B use identical hashes for the five rebuilt dense-runtime extensions.
- BF16, FlashAttention, seed=0, max model length=512, max batched tokens=512, max sequences=8, memory utilization=0.8, CUDA graph sizes `[1,2,4,8]`, four CPU/compilation threads.
- Raw AOT/mega/standalone flags are enabled; cache-disable and force-load are disabled. No batch invariance or additional deterministic controls are enabled. All workers use `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`.
- Fixed physical L20 GPU 4, checked idle before every start. Runs were serial within the task; the host was not CPU-exclusive. A/B never share compiled artifacts; remote graph caches are disabled.
- Cold means an empty compilation cache. OS page caches were not cleared; model-file verification may warm them. Single cold observations and five warm samples do not establish statistical significance.
- Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. TinyLlama and Qwen3-14B snapshots are identified by per-file SHA256.

</details>

### Correctness and cache behavior

- **HF:** all After warm performance runs hit FX/AOTAutograd caches; model-AOT/direct-artifact save/load counts remain zero.
- **Native:** all cold runs save AOT; all five warm runs per version/protocol load it with zero model-AOT recompilations. Separate forced-load checks also pass.
- **TP=2:** Qwen3-0.6B HF completes cold/warm initialization and generation on both versions. Both After ranks record three FX and three AOTAutograd hits on warm start, with separate rank cache directories.
- **EAGLE3:** full generation with Qwen3-0.6B HF and `Nicolassuez/Qwen3-0.6B-eagle3` completes across cold/warm processes. The HF target uses graph caching; the native draft saves AOT on cold start and loads it on warm start.
- **Cache disable:** separate HF cold/warm checks retain compilation while recording zero FX/AOTAutograd cache hits and zero model-AOT/direct-artifact saves or loads.

Performance runs generate the same 32 prompts after initialization, using batch sizes 1/4/8, greedy decoding, and up to 64 tokens. **All 128 comparisons pass the existing repository helper without relaxed tolerances; 124/128 contain token-sequence differences.** Each comparison covers 32 prompts; this count is not a prompt failure rate or an accuracy measurement.

| Model / backend | Explicit: comparisons with token differences | Root-only: comparisons with token differences | Helper failures |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 16/16 | 16/16 | 0 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 14/16 | 16/16 | 0 |

Each group includes ten within-version cold/warm comparisons and six corresponding A/B comparisons. The helper checks first-divergence tokens against the other output's top-5; it does not establish full-sequence or accuracy equivalence.

### Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K

All **1,319 questions**, 5-shot, greedy decoding, 256-token generation limit. Before cold, After cold, and After warm each score **519/1319 (39.35%)**, with **identical per-question answers and complete token sequences**. Each run has 3 invalid answers and generates 132,670 tokens. After warm records **29 FX graph hits and 29 AOTAutograd hits**.

This uses batch invariance with compilation enabled, max model length=4096, max batched tokens=2048, and max sequences=8. Batch invariance disables model AOT upstream; mega/standalone remain enabled. This evaluation does not establish quality equivalence under the default AOT-enabled configuration or for Qwen3-14B. Evaluation timings are excluded from the performance results.

<details>
<summary>Numerical diagnostics and coverage limits</summary>

Default runs contain token differences across versions and between cold/warm starts within a version, despite passing the repository helper. Separate smaller-implementation smoke comparisons also pass the helper, with these token-sequence differences among 32 prompts:

| Path | Before cold → Before warm | Before cold → After cold | After cold → After warm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| HF | 4/32 | 6/32 | 3/32 |
| Native | 4/32 | 1/32 | 4/32 |
| HF TP=2 | 7/32 | 5/32 | 6/32 |
| EAGLE3 | 2/32 | 2/32 | 3/32 |

These smoke comparisons are separate from the 128 performance-run comparisons above. Cache-disabled HF runs also differ on 5/32 prompts, showing that cache hits are not necessary for output variation; this does not rule out all effects of the patch.

The largest common-prefix logprob difference in the performance matrix is **4.312496** for Qwen3-14B: an unselected token has logprobs −13.250004 and −17.5625, while both runs select the same token at that position. This is not evidence of an incorrect selected token, but the differences should not all be described as negligible rounding. Operator-level attribution has not been established.

The batch-invariant GSM8K result is separate evidence with its own configuration limits. Full Qwen3-14B quality evaluation has not been repeated for this implementation. Earlier implementation-specific numerical controls and quality results are not counted as current validation.

Testing covers the recorded dependency environment and L20 GPUs. Required dense-runtime components were rebuilt from pinned source, but this is not a full wheel/Rust build, every optional extension, or full upstream CI. ROCm execution and a separate real `model_impl=auto` → HF resolution check remain unverified. The independent TinyLlama breakable-CUDA-graph issue is outside this patch.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Regression commands and results</summary>

Relevant suites ran with fresh vLLM cache roots and the verified task environment:

```bash
.venv-verified/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/compile/test_config.py

.venv-verified/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/test_decorator.py \
  tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py \
  tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py
```

- **127 passed, 1 skipped:** configuration tests 89 passed; decorator/AOT/compiler-interface tests 38 passed, 1 skipped.
- Six targeted mutations were detected: index read, direct load, configuration restoration, second forward, disabled native AOT, and hash-configuration restoration.
- A subsequent test-only isolation fix mocks adaptor cache initialization in the old-index test. A focused rerun including an environment-state probe reports **5 passed**; both index-read/direct-load mutations remain detected. Product code was unchanged. These counts are not additive, and the full suite was not rerun after this test-only change.
- Twelve applicable Python hooks passed on the smaller implementation; ruff, formatting, mypy, and diff checks were rerun after the isolation fix. Full pre-commit was blocked by offline actionlint dependency installation; full CI is not claimed.
- Existing binary/unpacked artifact-relocation tests are retained. The ROCm adaptor call site was updated, but ROCm tests were not executed locally.

Performance harness: `performance_controller.py`, `run_models.py`, `model_probe.py`, `export_results.py`, and `final_audit.py`. Per-run commands, environments, source hashes, worker paths/counters, full outputs, and exit codes were retained alongside the 96-sample CSV.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Retry Mooncake bootstrap registration on timeout (reopens #55763)
author: LCAIZJ
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55729.

This PR reopens #55763 and credit goes to @Sarimsaljook, the original PR author. Compared with #55763, the attempt limit is now an internal constant set to 3 instead of a user-facing environment variable. The original tests and documentation are adapted accordingly; the remaining fix is preserved.

During slow rank-0 initialization, bootstrap registration can time out. Previously, only connection errors were retried, and a failed sender listener could leave startup waiting indefinitely.

This change:

- Adds an explicit registration timeout through `VLLM_MOONCAKE_CONNECTOR_TIMEOUT` (default: 30 seconds).
- Retries connection errors and timeouts for up to 3 total attempts, with exponential backoff.
- Makes repeated registration of the same worker address idempotent, while still rejecting conflicting addresses.
- Bounds the sender-listener readiness wait and propagates startup failures.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Per-module LM heads for multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

Fix two issues with multi-layer MTP on Model Runner V2 (MRV2):

1. **Multi-module MTP samples every draft step with module 0's LM head.**
   `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` runs step `i` through MTP module `i` (`spec_step_idx=step`), but `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` calls `self.model.compute_logits(hidden_states)` without `spec_step_idx`. MTP drafters whose `compute_logits` selects the module's own `shared_head` by `spec_step_idx` (Step3.5/3.7, DeepSeek MTP, GLM MTP, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, ...) therefore use module 0's head/norm for all steps. The same applies to the `use_local_argmax_reduction` path (`get_top_tokens`).
   Fix: `sample_draft` goes through two `DraftModelSpeculator` hooks, `compute_draft_logits` and `get_draft_top_tokens`, which ignore the step by default. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` overrides them to pass `spec_step_idx`, so other drafters (EAGLE, DFlash, ...) are untouched.

2. **Step-3.x MTP cannot run on MRV2** (needed to reproduce 1 end-to-end):
   - The drafter read `vllm_config.model_config.hf_config`, which for the Step-3.7 VLM target is the top-level `Step3p7Config` (`AttributeError: ... 'vocab_size'`), and used the target's quant config (`output_partition_size = 24 is not divisible by block_n = 128`). It is now built from its own text config and draft quant config, as the V1 `Step3p5MTPProposer` does.
   - `load_eagle_model` replaced every MTP layer's `shared_head.head` with the target `lm_head` because `Step3p5MTP` has no top-level `lm_head`. Step-3.7's three MTP heads differ from the target `lm_head` (checked in the checkpoint), so this collapsed position-0 acceptance from 0.93 to 0.06. `Step3p5MTP` now declares `has_own_lm_head = True`, and `_should_share` keeps a declared-own copy that has no top-level module.

## Relation to existing PRs

Item 2's config part overlaps #49490 by @chanh, credited as co-author on that commit. This PR additionally fixes the per-step LM head selection (item 1) and the per-layer LM head overwrite, without which the drafter loads but barely accepts anything.

## Test Plan

E2E on 4×GB200, `stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash-FP8`, TP4, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, GSM8K 500 questions 5-shot, temperature 0. Acceptance from the `/metrics` counters.

## Test Result

| MRV2 | GSM8K | pos 0 | pos 1 | pos 2 | mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Item 2 only (per-step head bug present) | 0.910 | 0.934 | 0.743 | 0.526 | 3.20 |
| This PR | 0.902 | 0.931 | **0.786** | **0.592** | **3.31** |

Position 0 (always module 0's head) is unchanged, while positions 1 and 2, the steps affected by the bug, improve by 4.3 and 6.6 points (~16k drafts per run). GSM8K differences are within noise. Before item 2, main fails to start with this model on MRV2.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; all changes were reviewed and tested by the submitter.
