title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fall back to default GEMM for CPU tensors on ROCm builds
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched for existing fixes before starting: `gh pr list --search "rocm_unquantized_gemm"`, `--search "test_gemma.py"`, `--search "gemma4_dspark"`, and the ~20 open/merged DSpark/confidence-head PRs in this area — none touch `dispatch_unquantized_gemm`/`rocm_unquantized_gemm` or this device-dispatch bug. Filed as vllm-project/vllm#58922 for tracking.

## What broke

`tests/models/language/generation/test_gemma.py::test_gemma4_dspark_loads_confidence_head` (added in #57263, merged 2026-09-26) fails on ROCm CI:

```
NotImplementedError: Could not run 'vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm' with arguments
from the 'CPU' backend. ... 'vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm' is only available for
these backends: [CUDA, ...]
```

`dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` picks `rocm_unquantized_gemm` for any ROCm build purely from `current_platform.is_rocm()`, ignoring the tensor's actual device. The custom op is only registered for the CUDA/HIP dispatch key, so a CPU tensor (as this test uses, exercising `DSparkConfidenceHead.proj`, a `ReplicatedLinear`, without moving it to a GPU) hard-crashes. The CUDA and CPU branches of the same dispatcher already fall back to plain `torch.nn.functional.linear` for this kind of case; the ROCm branch didn't.

This surfaced while running full ROCm CI on an unrelated PR (#58867, AITER version bump) — `amd-mi355-dpx-language-models-extended-generation` is `optional: true` and never ran on #57263 itself, so it was never caught.

## Fix

Add the same device fallback the CUDA/CPU branches already have:

```python
def rocm_unquantized_gemm(layer, x, weight, bias=None):
    if not x.is_cuda:
        return default_unquantized_gemm(layer, x, weight, bias)
    return torch.ops.vllm.rocm_unquantized_gemm(x, weight, bias)
```

No change to real GPU-tensor behavior/perf; only changes the previously-crashing CPU-tensor case.

## Test commands run and results

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Count Responses reasoning tokens per tool round
author: sfeng33
body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_PARSER_CONTEXT=1`, a Responses request that makes tool calls underreports `usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`: it counts only the first round's reasoning.

`ParsableContext` never counted reasoning tokens, so `responses_full_generator` counted the output ids of all rounds concatenated, in one parser pass. For templates that put `<think>\n` in the generation prompt (Qwen3, Qwen3.5), later rounds have no generated opener, so their reasoning follows round 1's `</think>` and is counted as content.

This PR counts each round on its own ids in `ParsableContext.append_output`, and limits the serving fallback to `SimpleContext`.

## Test Plan

Same GPU, same request, baseline `main` (924707f1bf) vs this PR, temperature 0.

```bash
VLLM_USE_EXPERIMENTAL_PARSER_CONTEXT=1 \
PYTHON_EXECUTION_BACKEND=dangerously_use_uv \
VLLM_ENABLE_RESPONSES_API_STORE=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
    --tool-server demo \
    --max-model-len 16384
```

Request: "What is 123 * 456? Use python to calculate the result." with `tools=[{"type": "code_interpreter", "container": {"type": "auto"}}]`. This path does not render `code_interpreter` into the prompt (the same reason `test_mcp_tool_call` is xfailed), so its schema is described in `instructions`. The model calls it once, the demo python tool returns `56088`, and the model answers in a second round.

Expected `reasoning_tokens` = tokenized length of each `reasoning` output item, summed: **34 + 35 = 69**.

**Before (`main`)**: only round 1 is counted

```text
reasoning   "The user wants me to calculate 123 * 456 using Python ..."        34 tokens
mcp_call    code_interpreter  "result = 123 * 456; print(result)"  ->  56088
reasoning   "The Python code successfully calculated 123 * 456 = 56088 ..."   35 tokens
message     "The result of 123 * 456 is **56088**."

usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens = 34   ✗
```

**After (this PR)**: both rounds are counted

```text
reasoning   "The user wants me to calculate 123 * 456 using Python ..."        34 tokens
mcp_call    code_interpreter  "result = 123 * 456; print(result)"  ->  56088
reasoning   "The Python code successfully calculated 123 * 456 = 56088 ..."   35 tokens
message     "The result of 123 * 456 is **56088**."

usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens = 69   ✓
```

Controls, a single round with no tools, are unchanged:

| | `main` | this PR | expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ParsableContext` (flag set) | 316 | 316 | 316 |
| `SimpleContext` (flag unset) | 316 | 316 | 316 |

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Sample batched chat completions from the adjusted requests
author: sfeng33
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #42103. Supersedes #42105.

`/v1/chat/completions/batch` created every per-conversation `ChatCompletionRequest` twice. The renderer ran the parser's `adjust_request` on the first copy, then the endpoint sampled from the second, unadjusted copy. Parser adjustments therefore never reached `SamplingParams` in batch mode. These include `skip_special_tokens=False`, the Mistral grammar and structural tags. With a reasoning parser such as Gemma 4, the engine strips the `<channel|>` end marker. Reasoning then never ends: the answer is absorbed into `reasoning` and `content` comes back `null`.

`render_batch_chat_request` now returns the requests it rendered, and `create_batch_chat_completion` samples from those. This matches the non-batch path. The batch-level parser is now built after rendering, so it reads `chat_template_kwargs` from the adjusted request. Non-batch chat is unchanged.

This PR supersedes #42105 (@Kimahriman). That PR takes the same approach but has had merge conflicts since May, targets APIs that no longer exist, and also changes `reasoning_ended` handling. This PR keeps only the request fix, rebased on current `main`.

## Test Plan

**Setup:** A/B on one H200, same GPU and port, one server at a time. Model `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, `temperature=0`, `seed=1234`, `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": true}`. The "before" server ran from a `main` checkout, the "after" server from this branch. Server command (identical for both):

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve google/gemma-4-E4B-it --port 8011 \
  --reasoning-parser gemma4 --enable-log-requests --max-model-len 8192
```

Batch request with two conversations: `"What is 17 * 23? Give just the number."` and `"Which is larger, 9.11 or 9.9? Answer in one word."`.

**Before (`main`):** batch choice 1 has the answer stuck inside `reasoning`, and `content` is `null`.

```json
{
  "index": 1,
  "reasoning": "...I will provide the number as the single-word answer.9.9",
  "content": null
}
```

```text
Received request chatcmpl-882284ede918a9ef_0: params: SamplingParams(... skip_special_tokens=True ...)
Received request chatcmpl-882284ede918a9ef_1: params: SamplingParams(... skip_special_tokens=True ...)
```

**After (this PR):** reasoning ends cleanly and the answer is in `content`.

```json
{
  "index": 1,
  "reasoning": "...I will provide the number as the single-word answer.",
  "content": "9.9"
}
```

```text
Received request chatcmpl-ad0dc647e98ebeca_0: params: SamplingParams(... skip_special_tokens=False ...)
Received request chatcmpl-ad0dc647e98ebeca_1: params: SamplingParams(... skip_special_tokens=False ...)
```

**Full comparison:**

| Check | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Batch, thinking on, choice 1 | `content: null`, answer inside `reasoning` | `content: "9.9"`, clean `reasoning` |
| Batch sub-request `skip_special_tokens` | `True` (non-batch sends `False`) | `False`, matches non-batch |
| Non-batch `/v1/chat/completions`, thinking on (control) | `"391"` | identical |
| Batch, thinking off | `"391"` / `"9.9"` | identical |
| Batch, `response_format` json_schema | `{"answer": "yes"}` / `{"answer": "no"}` | identical |

Choice 0 (`"391"`) has no reasoning on either side because the model skips thinking for that prompt, including non-batch.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix macOS build on Apple Clang < 17: structured binding…
author: blueberry808
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58928.

Building the CPU backend from source on Apple Silicon fails with Apple Clang 16.0.0, even though the docs list `Apple Clang >= 15.0.0` as supported:

```
csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/fla.cpp:2312:9: error: capturing a structured binding is not yet supported in OpenMP
  2312 |         query_,
       |         ^
csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/fla.cpp:2300:9: note: 'query_' declared here
  2300 |   auto [query_, key_] = use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel ? l2norm_fwd(query, key, eps) : ...
```

(6 errors total, one each for `query_`, `key_`, `w`, `u`, `decay_mask`, `chunk_offsets`.)

**Why it happens**

In `chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu`, the `launch_inter` generic lambda captures six structured bindings via `[&]`. The CPU build always compiles with `-fopenmp`, and Clang's OpenMP mode rejected lambda captures of structured bindings until LLVM 19. This happens even when the lambda is not inside any `#pragma omp` region. Apple Clang 16 is based on an older LLVM, so it hits this.

**The fix**

Switch `launch_inter` from `[&]` to explicit init-captures (`local_query = query_`, etc.). Init-captures create new variables inside the lambda rather than capturing the structured bindings, which older Clang accepts under `-fopenmp`. The copies are `at::Tensor` handles (refcount bump, no data copy), and every parameter of `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_inter` is `const at::Tensor&`, so behavior is unchanged. I added a comment explaining the workaround so it isn't reverted in a future sglang kernel sync.

This touches only `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/fla.cpp`, in one function.

**Duplicate check:** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `structured binding OpenMP`, `fla.cpp macOS`, and `Apple clang build`.
## Test Plan

Environment: Apple M2, macOS 26.5 (arm64), Apple Clang 16.0.0 (clang-1600.0.26.6), PyTorch 2.13.0, Python 3.12.13, CMake 4.3.2. Base commit `b28c3e156`.

1. Build from source on unmodified `main`: `uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`
2. Build again with this patch.
3. Run the GDN CPU kernel tests, which exercise the changed function:
   `python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py -v`

## Test Result

- **Build before:** fails. `fla.cpp` produces 6 errors and `cmake --build` exits with status 1.
- **Build after:** succeeds.
- **Tests after:** `90 passed, 41 skipped`
  - All `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu` and `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu_two_call_split` cases pass, covering fp32/bf16/fp16 inputs and all three `initial_state` dtypes (`state_dtype0/1/2`). This exercises each `launch_inter(float{} / at::BFloat16{} / at::Half{})` branch.
  - The skipped tests require AMX or AVX-512BF16 (x86-only) and are unrelated to this change.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to help investigate the root cause and draft this description. I reproduced the failure, wrote and reviewed the change, and ran the build and tests myself.

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Forward softcap and alibi_slopes in xpu_ops.flash_attn_varlen_func
author: ChaseZhang-ai
body:
## Purpose

`xpu_ops.flash_attn_varlen_func()` accepted `softcap` and `alibi_slopes` in its signature but dropped both at the call into `vllm_xpu_kernels.flash_attn_interface`, so models that require attention logit soft-capping (Gemma-2 and friends) ran uncapped on Intel GPUs, with no error and no warning. `get_flash_attn_version()` also short-circuits to FA2 on XPU, so the usual softcap/ALiBi backend fallback never engages.

The kernel wrapper (`vllm_xpu_kernels/flash_attn_interface.py`) already accepts and forwards both parameters down to the kernel, so this PR only forwards them from the vLLM-side wrapper.

The new tests stub the kernel module with a recording wrapper and assert that `softcap` and `alibi_slopes` actually reach `vllm_xpu_kernels.flash_attn_interface.flash_attn_varlen_func`, including the neutral defaults on a plain call.

title: [Bugfix][MiMo] Declare embedding_fields so an EPD pair can serve images
author: peperunas
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58934.

This is my first contribution, so please let me know if there is anything I have to adjust!

### What

`MiMoV2OmniProcessingInfo.get_data_parser` now returns `MiMoV2OmniMultiModalDataParser` — a `Qwen2VLMultiModalDataParser` subclass declaring image fields only, built with MiMo's own `spatial_merge_size`, its 24 kHz audio target, `expected_hidden_size` and `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` — instead of the base `MultiModalDataParser`, which declares no `embedding_fields` at all.

The vision tower is Qwen2.5-VL-derived and the model already consumes `Qwen2_5_VLImageInputs` / `Qwen2_5_VLImageEmbeddingInputs`, splitting them with `grid_thw.prod(-1) // merge_size // merge_size`, so Qwen2-VL's field declaration (`image_embeds` = values, `image_grid_thw` = metadata) is the one it needs. Without it `collect_ec_item_metadata` publishes `metadata: {}`, the EPD proxy finds nothing to rewrite and forwards raw media to a `--language-model-only` decode server, where every modality limit is 0 and the request dies with `At most 0 image(s) may be provided in one prompt`.

### Why this is not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "58934 in:body"` → empty
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "MiMo embedding_fields"` → empty
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "MiMo EPD"` → empty
- `gh search issues --repo vllm-project/vllm "embedding_fields"` and `gh search prs ... "embedding_fields"` → no hit on a model declaring (or missing) these fields

The nearby EPD work (#52409 tracker, #50160, #50390, #51222) is about the connector and proxy plumbing itself; none of it covers MiMo's missing declaration.

## Test Plan

`prek`/`pre-commit` cannot install its hook toolchain in this environment (its bundled `uv` binary does not run on NixOS), so the two hooks that apply to this file were run directly with `ruff`:

```
ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2_omni.py     # All checks passed
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2_omni.py  # 1 file already formatted
```

No `.venv` could be built here, so `pytest tests/multimodal/test_parse.py` ran inside the vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev449+geb8798058` serving container:

```
with this change:    8 failed, 18 passed
with the change reverted (same container, same tests):  8 failed, 18 passed
```

`tests/multimodal/test_embedding_shape_validation_unit.py`: 18 passed, 0 failed.

## Test Result

Only the image path got end-to-end testing on my side; audio and video didn't.

Identical either way: the 8 failures in `test_parse.py` are all `test_audio_metadata_*`, which fail inside `assert_never` on `audio_num_tokens` — a field today's `main` tests use and this build does not implement — and that file never references MiMo.

No benchmark eval was run: the pre-change baseline rejects every image request with HTTP 400, so there is no comparable score. Serving was verified end to end on a real EPD deployment (encoder-only producer on one GPU, `--language-model-only` consumer on two, `ECExampleConnector` over shared storage): before the change the encoder answered 200, the proxy logged no rewrite and decode answered 400; after it, the proxy logs `Rewrote 1 media item(s) as metadata references` and decode answers 200.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Use a fresh parser per choice in non-streaming chat completions
author: sfeng33
body:
## Purpose

**Bug:** non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` with `n > 1` parses every choice with the *same* parser instance, so parser state from one choice leaks into the next. Streaming already uses one parser per choice.

**Visible symptom:** Kimi K2-style tool-call IDs (`functions.<name>:<idx>`) keep counting across choices. With `n=2` and one tool call per choice, non-streaming returns `get_weather:0` and `get_weather:1`, while streaming returns `get_weather:0` for both. With H prior tool calls in the history, non-streaming gives `:H`, `:H+1`; streaming gives `:H` for each.

**Fix:** `chat_completion_full_generator` keeps the existing parser for choice 0 and builds a fresh one for each later choice (`n=1` creates no extra parser). The constructor call moves into a small `_make_parser` helper shared with the streaming path, which is otherwise unchanged. No protocol change: non-streaming now matches streaming.

## Test Plan

Live server A/B on one H200: the same requests against the parent commit `e7900156e1` (before) and this branch (after).

```bash
VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes \
  --hf-overrides '{"model_type": "kimi_k2"}'
```

`--hf-overrides` makes a small model use Kimi K2 tool-call IDs, and `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0` routes `required`/named `tool_choice` through the parser path that assigns them.

Example request (other cases vary `messages`, `tool_choice`, `n`, `stream`):

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "n": 2, "temperature": 0.8, "seed": 7, "max_tokens": 128,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Tokyo?"}],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}],
  "tool_choice": "required",
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}
}' | jq '[.choices[].message.tool_calls[0].id]'
```

## Test Result

Tool-call IDs per choice (`functions.get_weather:<idx>`):

| Request | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| non-streaming, `n=2`, `tool_choice=required` | `:0`, `:1` ❌ | `:0`, `:0` |
| non-streaming, `n=2`, `required`, 2 prior tool calls in history | `:2`, `:3` ❌ | `:2`, `:2` |
| non-streaming, `n=2`, named `tool_choice` | `:0`, `:1` ❌ | `:0`, `:0` |
| non-streaming, `n=1`, `required` | `:0` | `:0` |
| streaming, `n=2`, `required` (reference) | `:0`, `:0` | `:0`, `:0` |
| streaming, `n=2`, `required`, with history (reference) | `:2`, `:2` | `:2`, `:2` |

Also sent `n=2` with `tool_choice=auto` (Hermes random IDs), plain `n=2` chat, and `n=3` with thinking enabled. With IDs removed, the before/after responses for all nine requests are identical: the only change is the three non-streaming ID fixes above.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve streaming chunk boundaries in RequestOutputCollector
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

**Bug:** `RequestOutputCollector` (`vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py`) keeps a single `self.output` slot and merges DELTA outputs into it when the producer runs ahead of the consumer. `RequestOutput.add()` overwrites `finish_reason`, so for streaming-input (resumable) sessions the per-chunk boundary marker (a `finish_reason` on a non-finished output) is erased when a merge spans a chunk boundary — the consumer sees two chunks' replies glued together.

**Fix:** `RequestOutputCollector` keeps its original single-slot merging. A new `StreamingInputOutputCollector` subclass, constructed only by `_add_streaming_input_request` (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py`), adds a `_backlog` deque: while the slot or the backlog tail carries a chunk boundary, incoming outputs are queued into / merged within the backlog instead of being merged into the boundary output, and `get`/`get_nowait` promote backlog entries into the slot in FIFO order. Exceptions remain terminal (they clear the backlog and take over the slot). Non-streaming requests use the base collector and are unaffected.

## Why this is not duplicate work

This PR is bug 1 of 4 split out of #53861 so the collector fix can be reviewed and merged independently; the original author of #53861 (Benedikt Falk) is credited via `Co-authored-by`. Bugs 2+3 of #53861 are split into #58942; bug 4 remains in #53861.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -q -k collector
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py
```

## Test Result

- Collector tests: `3 passed, 50 deselected` — including `test_streaming_input_collector_preserves_chunk_boundary`, which exercises the new subclass. Bug-guard verified: replaying the same output sequence through the base `RequestOutputCollector` erases the boundary (`finish_reason` becomes `None`, token_ids from two chunks glued together).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `mypy` (pre-commit hook): pass.
- A full-file pytest run on this Mac is blocked by two pre-existing environment issues unrelated to this change: a segfault in `tests/conftest.py` `cleanup_fixture` → `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache` (reproduces on unmodified `main`; bypassed locally via the repo's `skip_global_cleanup` marker) and 401 gated-repo errors fetching `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` from HuggingFace (tokenizer-dependent tests). The 19 non-tokenizer tests pass.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi Code CLI); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Terminate streaming sessions on ABORT/ERROR and prevent zombie sessions
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

Split out from #53861 (bugs 2 and 3 of the 4 streaming-input session lifecycle fixes there), with the original author included as co-author — this is a carve-out for independent review/merge, not duplicate work. Bugs 1 (collector merging across chunk boundaries) and 4 (zero-chunk streams / DP sticky routing) are being split separately.

**Bug 2 — engine-side ABORT/ERROR treated as a normal chunk boundary.** `OutputProcessor.process_outputs` treated any `finish_reason` on a streaming-input request as "chunk done, wait for next chunk". ABORT and ERROR end the whole session, so treating them as a chunk boundary left `generate()` waiting forever and desynced the frontend/scheduler chunk queues. Fix: only non-terminal finish reasons are chunk boundaries (`streaming_chunk_boundary`); ABORT/ERROR finish the request state and also send an abort back to the engine (see below).

**Bug 3 — a chunk sent after the session finished resurrects it as a zombie.** If a chunk ADD reaches the engine after the session was aborted/finished, the scheduler sees an unknown resumable id and admits it as a new session. That session then sits in `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` forever, holding KV blocks, with no frontend state left to abort it. Fix (reworked per review, no new request fields):
- `handle_inputs` checks `output_processor.has_request()` before each non-first chunk and before the final empty request, and stops if the session is gone. There is no `await` between this check and the ADD send, and `AsyncLLM.abort()` removes frontend state before sending ABORT on the same socket, so any chunk that passes the check is ordered before the abort. This holds for every abort path, including direct `abort()` calls (e.g. realtime `cleanup()`).
- For the engine-finished race (engine finishes the session with ABORT/ERROR while a chunk sent before the frontend saw that finish is in flight), the output processor always re-sends an abort for a terminally-finished streaming session. That abort is ordered after any such chunk, so a re-created session is cleaned up.
- `DPLBAsyncMPClient.abort_requests_async` broadcasts aborts for ids with no routing entry to all engines, since the routing entry is dropped when the engine reports the request finished.

## Test Plan

```
ruff check / ruff format --check (ruff 0.14.0) on changed files
pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_async_llm_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -k "streaming or abort or chunk"
```

New coverage: `test_streaming_input_stop_is_chunk_boundary`, `test_streaming_input_abort_error_is_terminal[abort|error]` (bug 2); `test_handle_inputs_stops_after_session_finished[True|False]`, `test_dplb_abort_of_finished_request_goes_to_all_engines[1|2]` (bug 3).

## Test Result

- ruff check / format: pass.
- On macOS CPU: all streaming-input and output-processor tests above pass. `test_abort_requests[*]` errors only because the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` tokenizer cannot be downloaded here (same on main).
- `test_engine_core_client.py` is skipped on non-CUDA platforms, so `test_dplb_abort_of_finished_request_goes_to_all_engines` was run standalone: it passes with this change and fails against the previous `abort_requests_async`.
- Not yet validated end-to-end against a realtime model on GPU.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (split and adaptation onto latest main). The bug-3 approach was reworked following @njhill's review suggestion. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Fix moe_wna16 w13 zero-point shard split for 8-bit asym GPTQ MoE
author: spandantiwari
body:
## Summary

`MoeWNA16Method`'s weight loader splits the fused `w13_qzeros` (gate/up) zero-points at `shard_size // 2`, which is only correct for 4-bit. `w13_qzeros` is packed along the intermediate dim by `bit8_pack_factor` (`8 // weight_bits`), so the w1/w3 boundary is in **packed** units — `shard_size // bit8_pack_factor`. For **8-bit asymmetric GPTQ MoE** (`bit8_pack_factor == 1`, `has_zp=True`) the param's intermediate dim is `2 * intermediate` (unpacked), but each shard's loaded tensor is `intermediate` wide, so writing into a half-width `[: shard_size // 2]` slice raises a shape mismatch at load. The common 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ path is unaffected (`bit8_pack_factor == 2`, so `shard_size // 2 == shard_size // bit8_pack_factor`).

## Fix
My fix is as follows:
`moe_wna16.py` — split `w13_qzeros` at `shard_size // layer.quant_config.bit8_pack_factor` instead of the hardcoded `shard_size // 2`. Only `w13_qzeros` is affected: qweight/scales aren't packed on that axis, and `w2_qzeros` isn't shard-split.

## Impact for various backends

Platform-independent: the defect is in load-time weight-loader code with no CUDA/ROCm gate, and WNA16 INT4/INT8 GPTQ/AWQ MoE runs on ROCm (Triton fused-MoE). So this **affects AMD** as well as CUDA. Failure mode is a **loud load-time error** (shape mismatch), not silent wrong output, in the narrow 8-bit-asymmetric config. (Marlin doesn't support asymmetric GPTQ, so `sym=False` MoE routes to `moe_wna16` by construction — this path can't be diverted to Marlin.)

## Test plan

Added `test_moe_wna16_w13_qzeros_shard_split_int8_asym_gptq` in `tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py` — CPU-only. Builds a real 8-bit GPTQ `MoeWNA16Method`, runs `create_weights`, drives the actual weight loader for the w1/w3 shards, and asserts both load without error and land in the correct halves.

```
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py -q
# 16 passed, 9 skipped (CUDA/humming-gated)
# new test PASSES on the fix; FAILS when reverted to `shard_size // 2` (guards the exact regression)

ruff check <both files>          # All checks passed
ruff format --check <both files> # already formatted
```

## Model evaluation

No full-model eval — this fixes a checkpoint-**load** failure (weight placement / shape), not inference math, and the 4-bit path is provably unchanged (`shard_size // 2 == shard_size // bit8_pack_factor` when `bit8_pack_factor == 2`), so no accuracy regression is possible.

I did attempt to do an end-to-end run by quantizing a small MoE (OLMoE-1B-7B) to 8-bit asymmetric GPTQ, but it is blocked in this vLLM environment: **transformers 5.x fuses MoE experts into a single module**, while the GPTQ tooling (`gptqmodel`) quantizes per-expert submodules that no longer exist — so no MoE can be freshly GPTQ-quantized here without downgrading transformers. No public 8-bit *asymmetric* GPTQ MoE checkpoint exists to load directly either.

Evidence in lieu of an eval: the added unit test drives the **real** `create_weights` + `moe_wna16_weight_loader` on the actual code path (fails before the fix with the exact shape mismatch, passes after), and verifies the loaded zero-points land in the correct gate/up halves. A reviewer with an 8-bit-asym GPTQ MoE checkpoint (or a transformers-4.x quantization env) can confirm end-to-end load.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open/merged PRs touching this area:
- #51645 (open) — fixes `create_weights` **allocation** along the group dimension for non-divisible group sizes; different axis, doesn't touch the loader split.
- #51125 (merged) — sized `w13` allocation by `w13_num_shards`; established that pattern but left this loader split hardcoded.

Neither of these two PRs addresses the packed-unit shard boundary fixed here.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Account for new requests in DP routing
author: reidliu41
body:
## Purpose

The routing score `max(inflight, running + waiting)` can remain unchanged
across successive admissions when the scheduler snapshot exceeds local
inflight counts. After cancellations reduce local inflight, a burst can
therefore concentrate on one engine before updated stats arrive.

For example, with fixed scheduler loads of 10 and 12 and zero local
inflight requests, 14 consecutive admissions produce a 13/1 split.

Track admissions since the latest scheduler snapshot and include them in
the load estimate. Reset this delta whenever a new snapshot arrives,
retaining local inflight as a lower bound. Each admission then immediately
increases the selected engine's score, producing an 8/6 split in the example.

Both automatic and explicitly targeted requests update the estimate.
Existing tie-breaking and explicit rank selection remain unchanged.

## Test Plan

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply Harmony adjust_request in batched chat completions
author: sfeng33
body:
## Purpose

For gpt-oss (Harmony), `/v1/chat/completions/batch` skipped the Harmony parser's `adjust_request`, which `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` both run. With a `json_schema` `response_format`, the raw schema then constrained the whole output rather than only the `final` channel. Batched responses came back with no reasoning and a trailing `<|call|>` token, so the content wasn't valid JSON.

This PR moves the adjustment into `OnlineRenderer.adjust_harmony_request` and calls it from all three Harmony render paths (chat, Responses, batch). 

## Test Plan

A/B on 1x H200 with `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b` (default args), temperature=0, same requests against `main` (027b6f3a22) and this PR:

1. Control: `/v1/chat/completions` with a strict `json_schema` `response_format`.
2. `/v1/chat/completions/batch` with 2 conversations and the same `response_format`.
3. `/v1/chat/completions/batch` without `response_format` (regression).

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions/batch -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "openai/gpt-oss-20b", "temperature": 0,
  "messages": [
    [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France? Reply with its city, country and approximate population in millions."}],
    [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of Japan? Reply with its city, country and approximate population in millions."}]
  ],
  "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "city_info", "strict": true, "schema": {
    "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["city", "country", "population_millions"],
    "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}, "country": {"type": "string"}, "population_millions": {"type": "number"}}}}}
}'
```

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Release the profiling KV cache held by QSA key views
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58960.

`QSAKeyStateCache.bind_kv_cache` stored the views `key_cache` and `rope_position_cache` next to `kv_cache`. `clear_layer_kv_caches` only resets `kv_cache`, so after CUDA graph memory profiling these views kept the profiling KV cache alive (9.76 GiB for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 at TP2) past `_teardown_profiling_state()`'s `empty_cache()`. It was freed only in the real `initialize_kv_cache`, stayed cached, and a later long-lived allocation pinned the block. FULL CUDA graph capture then ran out of memory at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` with 9.38 GiB free but unreleasable in the default pool. The issue has the memory-snapshot evidence.

The change derives both views from `kv_cache` on access, so `kv_cache` is the only reference to the bound storage, the same contract Mamba layers follow. Read sites (`indexer_qsa.py` on NVIDIA and AMD) are unchanged; they get the same tensor views as before.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR or issue covers QSA cache lifetime or profiling teardown for Qwen4Exp. #58439 and #58815 change Qwen4Exp PLE storage, not the QSA cache; #46515 fixes a different leak during CUDA graph memory profiling.

## Test Plan

```sh
# Regression test (new) and the rest of the QSA suite
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -q

# End to end (2x RTX PRO 6000, TP2)
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

## Test Result

- `test_clearing_qsa_key_cache_releases_its_storage` fails on `main` (the cleared layer still holds the bound storage) and passes with this change.
- `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py`: 73 passed.
- `pre-commit` hooks (ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy-3.10, check-test-tethering) pass on the changed files.
- End to end, same command, memory snapshots from the worker:

| default pool | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| free after KV cache init | 9.79 GiB (9,996 MiB profiling segment still held) | 0.02 GiB (segment released) |
| free before capture | 9.25 GiB, 9.23 GiB pinned in one segment | 3.95 GiB, largest segment 0.82 GiB and fully free |
| FULL CUDA graph capture | OOM in `qsa_select_paged_decode` | completes (`0.74 GiB (actual), 1.37 GiB (estimated)`), server ready |

Model evaluation: the change only affects when the profiling cache is freed; the views used at inference are the same tensors, so outputs are unchanged. For reference, the same model and stack at TP2 score 0.8931 on chat-template GSM8K (flexible-extract).

AI assistance was used (Claude) to investigate, write, and test this change.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep Mooncake bootstrap ports bound during startup
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Bind the bootstrap socket before starting Uvicorn and keep that listener open.
- Report bind errors immediately and stop waiting when startup fails.
- Let the ROCm test own a running bootstrap server and pass its endpoint to the workers and proxy.
- Cover port ownership, cleanup, startup failures, and external registration.

[PR #58095](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58095) added the ROCm test and selected its bootstrap port before model startup without keeping the socket reserved. In [AMD CI 13668](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13668#01a0e3aa-1025-420f-9503-7c8a7ca86e87), that port was occupied when Mooncake tried to bind, and the test waited 20 minutes before failing. The startup loop that hid the bind failure dates to [#31034](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31034). This addresses the reservation gap in [#51275](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51275); duplicate checks found no open listener-ownership fix, while [#55137](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55137) handles registration timeouts.

AI assistance was used for the investigation, implementation, and tests.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Handle multimodal cache misses without crashing
author: Lcy0801
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #33865.

When EngineCore reports a multi-modal processor cache miss, it returns a
terminal `FinishReason.ERROR` output with `mm_cache_miss_hashes`. Pooling
requests do not have a detokenizer, but OutputProcessor previously followed
the generation path when the error output did not contain a pooling tensor.
The resulting `req_state.detokenizer is not None` assertion killed the shared
output-handler task and shut down the server.

This PR:

- represents terminal pooling failures with a structured `RequestError`;
- keeps the output handler healthy and allows unrelated requests in the same
  EngineCore output batch to complete;
- propagates the error through embedding, classification, and scoring output
  conversions;
- short-circuits bi-encoder, late-interaction, and Jina scoring post-processing
  before the placeholder tensor can be used in score calculations;
- maps retryable online pooling failures to HTTP 503
  `ServiceUnavailableError` so clients can retry the request;
- invalidates multi-modal cache-miss hashes in synchronous `LLMEngine.step()`,
  matching the existing `AsyncLLM` behavior;
- releases cached late-interaction query embeddings after query/document
  failures or cancellation, including document cache misses before worker
  registration; and
- assigns request-scoped late-interaction document IDs so cleanup cannot abort
  documents from concurrent requests that share an `X-Request-Id`.

## Why this is not duplicate work

The required issue and open-PR searches were rerun immediately before opening
this PR. No open PR implements this pooling OutputProcessor fix.

- #44543 only appears because it mentions #33865 as related work. It fixes
  audio/video cache coupling inside the multi-modal processor cache, not the
  terminal pooling error path.
- #40986 handles zero-token error ordering in Chat/Completion SSE streams. It
  does not change pooling outputs or the pooling OutputProcessor path.

## Test plan and results

Environment: macOS arm64, Python 3.12.11.

```console
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rA \
    tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py \
    tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_pooling_cache_miss_is_a_request_error_and_batch_continues \
    tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_async_pooling_cache_miss_does_not_fail_output_processor \
    tests/test_outputs.py::test_specialized_pooling_outputs_preserve_request_error \
    tests/v1/engine/test_llm_engine.py::test_step_invalidates_mm_processor_cache_misses \
    tests/v1/worker/test_late_interaction_runner.py::test_release_queries_is_targeted_and_idempotent
14 passed
```

```console
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
    --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring \
    tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_late_interaction_serving.py
3 passed
```

```console
$ changed_files=($(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD))
$ .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files "${changed_files[@]}"
All hooks passed

$ git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# no output
```

The full CUDA test requirements cannot be installed on macOS arm64 because
`runai-model-streamer` provides Linux-only wheels. A full OutputProcessor test
run also includes tests that require access to the gated
`meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` repository. A real Qwen3-VL-Embedding GPU end-to-end
run was therefore not performed.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This change does not alter successful model outputs or model
accuracy; it only changes handling of terminal request errors and cleanup of
failed late-interaction requests.

## AI assistance

reviewed the complete diff and the test results before submission.

## Overview

Add the H20 block-FP8 Triton MoE configuration for GLM-5.3-Flash at TP4 (288 experts, per-rank MoE intermediate width 512, 128×128 weight blocks), and read its nested text configuration in `benchmark_moe.py`.

Updated in `40cab637f7d0c2ef03c6e696c98fa87451a62407`. The diff is **36 added lines across two files**: 27 configuration lines and 9 benchmark parsing lines. Per the November 9 review, the dedicated GLM tests and their NVIDIA/AMD CI source dependencies have been removed. Existing test and CI files match the PR base. The tuning guide remains in this description.

Open-PR searches on November 10 for GLM5Next and H20 MoE found no duplicate of this configuration and nested-config handling; the other H20 tuning PRs target different expert/intermediate sizes.

## Claims

- The benchmark reads the routed-expert count and MoE intermediate width from either GLM5Next architecture's text configuration, while preserving the outer quantization metadata.
- The bundled configuration tunes the existing Triton MoE path for the stated H20 shape. It does not change backend selection. The measured throughput and accuracy tradeoffs are reported below.

## Validation

**The full H20 runs below used `eb34e115`, before the October 29 merge of main `fa3b9d13`; they have not been rerun on the current head.** The baseline uses the same PR source with only the target H20 JSON removed. It is not a separate main-branch baseline. This November 10 update removes tests and CI dependencies only; the benchmark parsing and tuned configuration are unchanged from `7fff7220`.

### Full H20 accuracy and serving comparison

The tuned run has six fewer correct GSM8K answers: strict-match **1225/1319 → 1219/1319**, flexible-extract **1226/1319 → 1220/1319** (both −0.454890 percentage points). AIME25 changes from **19/30 → 21/30**. These are one temperature-0 run per arm; quality equivalence is not established.

Each GSM8K filter has 50 discordant questions: 28 correct only in baseline and 22 correct only in tuned. Their union across filters contains 51 questions. [Per-question official labels, reference answers and original responses](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/0709a4ef48511ea616d92cd97053177e4ceaa705/reports/pair2-gsm8k-discordance.json) are retained without rescoring.

All 28 workloads completed with command exit 0. Each of the 24 serving runs has 128 successful measured requests and 16 successful warmups. Actual benchmark inputs match across arms, and all four complete logged test-document sets match the pinned official test-split digests. Both model servers and the launcher exited cleanly; the pool reported no foreign GPU process contamination.

Three-run median **total token throughput (input + output tokens/s)**, baseline → tuned; ranges show the three observed run values, not confidence intervals:
- 8192/1: **6791.86 → 6755.25 tokens/s (-0.54%)**; baseline range 6784.61–6820.02, tuned 6704.06–6766.72.

- 512/128: **3992.04 → 4683.60 tokens/s (+17.32%)**; baseline range 3931.88–3999.38, tuned 4590.94–4800.80.

These upstream CI results do not constitute a rerun of the full H20 accuracy and serving comparison above.

CUDA remained uninitialized. Those cases have now been removed at the reviewer's request; these are historical results, not tests present in the current diff. The CPU run used the existing common native extension import links; it did not rebuild or validate GPU libraries.

The original regression sequence checked the MoE width (2048, rather than the dense width 12288) and outer FP8 block metadata. Removing the 9-line GLM branch produced 2 failures and 1 pass; restoring it produced 3 passes. This unchanged validation evidence is reused. The CPU runs and this follow-up's local checks were agent-executed.

## Details

The parser previously fell through to the generic model configuration path, which reads the dense MLP width and expects `num_local_experts`. GLM5Next instead exposes `n_routed_experts` and `moe_intermediate_size` on its text configuration. The added branch follows the existing nested-config pattern and leaves the original outer config available for quantization metadata.

The configuration contains 24 token-count entries. Its compact formatting preserves all values, types and key order, including nearest-key tie behavior; [the earlier equivalence receipt](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/0709a4ef48511ea616d92cd97053177e4ceaa705/review-followup-20261028/config-format-equivalence.json) records that comparison. The generator continues to emit its existing expanded format.

<details>
<summary>Native build provenance and exact evaluation protocol</summary>

The historical comparison uses two checkouts of `eb34e115` and the same native libraries built for that revision. The baseline removes only the target H20 MoE JSON; the tuned checkout retains it. Both ran sequentially on the same four H20 GPUs, with the same model files, client, dataset revisions, seeds, resource limits and server arguments.

The original startup failure came from the `eb34e115` Python wrappers calling older native libraries: FlashMLA passed 14 arguments to a 13-argument extension; MLA cache writes passed 7 to a 6-argument extension. The required ten native targets were rebuilt from that pinned source and its dependencies, including FlashMLA, the core/cache and MoE libraries, FlashKDA, DeepGEMM and FA3. Fresh-process loader checks confirmed the assembled module paths and matching schemas. The evaluation runner verifies the frozen files and selected backend. Separate read-only snapshots record the target native libraries mapped by the actual server and worker processes. Build commands, source revisions, CMake cache, compile commands, stdout/stderr, generated-file receipts and loader output are included with the raw evidence.

This is a build of the required execution paths on the fixed CUDA 13 / Torch 2.13 environment. It is not a clean build of every main-branch target. The main CMake Torch 2.14 expectation and FA recipe Torch 2.4 warning remain in the logs. Source identity comes from the actual Git commit and native receipts; installed distribution metadata from the common environment is recorded separately.

### Evaluation protocol

The executable scripts and full command/environment/exit receipts are linked with the results. Every accuracy request retains its response, input and reference. The two arms must pass source/native provenance checks, model readiness plus a real request, complete sample/request counts, and equality of actual accuracy inputs and benchmark prompts before a paired summary is produced.

- GSM8K: all 1,319 test samples, 5-shot, `local-completions`, 256 generated-token limit; report the official strict-match and flexible-extract scores and standard errors.
- AIME25: all 30 test samples, 0-shot, `local-chat-completions` with the model chat template, 32,768 generated-token limit. This is one temperature-0 attempt per question, not a multi-attempt estimate.
- Accuracy uses lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13, temperature 0, concurrency 8, seed 20261028 and no request retries. GSM8K and AIME25 dataset revisions are fixed in the linked offline-cache preparation receipt and reused by both arms.
- `vllm bench serve`: input/output lengths 8192/1, 2048/512, 512/1024 and 512/128; three runs per shape and arm, each with 16 warm-up and 128 measured requests. Temperature 0, ignored EOS, unlimited request rate, maximum client concurrency 128, per-run seed and cache salt fixed across arms. Every warm-up and measured request must succeed. Actual prompt digests are matched across arms.
- Both servers use TP4, Triton MoE, maximum model length 40000, 32 sequences, 4096 batched tokens, GPU memory utilization 0.92 and MTP with 3 speculative tokens. All model weights are reused read-only; all caches, temporary files and raw output are on the independent data disk.

Both arms keep `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`; the fixed seeds and temperature-0 settings do not establish bitwise batch invariance. The 62-shard local checkpoint is identified by the existing structural/header receipt and read-only start/end file-stat checks; tensor bodies were not rehashed. Server startup and the 16 warm-up requests are outside the official timed region; work occurring during measurement remains included. Three-run medians describe this workload and fixed environment. They are not confidence intervals or an across-workload speedup. Per-run values and official CLI output remain available; latency percentiles from separate runs are not pooled.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Triton MoE configuration usage and retuning</summary>

When GLM-5.3-Flash uses the Triton fused MoE backend on NVIDIA H20 at TP4,
vLLM automatically loads the bundled configuration for 288 experts, a per-rank
intermediate size of 512, and FP8 weights with 128×128 quantization blocks.
No additional flag is needed for this configuration. It tunes the existing
Triton backend; it does not change which MoE backend vLLM selects.
Batch-invariant execution (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`) uses its fixed configuration
instead of tuned configurations.

To search the benchmark's parameter space for this model from a source checkout:

```bash
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py \
  --model /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash --tp-size 4 --dtype fp8_w8a8 \
  --tune --save-dir ./moe-tuned
```

The benchmark reads the model configuration and uses synthetic inputs; it does
not load the model weights. Its batch size is the number of tokens passed to
MoE, rather than the number of serving requests. Use `--batch-size` to select
the token counts to tune. Set `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` to the generated
configuration directory to evaluate the results in vLLM. Validate numerical
correctness and model behavior before adopting new settings, and measure
performance with the intended hardware, software versions, and serving workload.

For example, start a new server process with the generated configuration and
explicitly select Triton:

```bash
VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER=/absolute/path/to/moe-tuned \
  vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --moe-backend triton
```

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Preserve host prefix publication after request completion
author: eopXD
body:
With HiSparse, a request can reach EOS or its output limit in the same step that reports completed host writes. The scheduler handles the final token and cleans up the request before processing the transfer acknowledgements from that same output. Any prefix publication still waiting for those acknowledgements is discarded, leaving valid host KV unavailable for reuse.

This PR preserves the publication information and host-page references until acknowledgement, then publishes the valid pages for reuse.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Relax packed_qk_rope_ correctness test to one ULP
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

`tests/kernels/core/test_apply_rotary_emb.py::test_packed_qk_rope_correctness` asserts that `packed_qk_rope_` is bitwise identical to `ApplyRotaryEmb(enable_fp32_compute=True)`. That fails on ROCm: 157 of 216 shape/dtype/seed combinations disagree, always by exactly one ULP.

**Why** 
Every mismatch sits at an odd `head_dim` index, i.e. only in `o1`.`o0` reads the same four values and is exact everywhere, so both sides seebitwise identical inputs and both compute in fp32. The only difference is which product the backend keeps exact inside the `o1` fused multiply-add:`flash_attn`'s rotary kernel contracts `x1*cos`, this kernel contracts`x0*sin`. That choice follows the register layout of `cos`/`sin`, so it is decided by codegen, not by the source.

The source cannot steer it. `x0*sin + x1*cos` is bit-identical to`x1*cos + x0*sin`, because the compiler canonicalizes the commutative add, andan explicit `tl.math.fma` is worse (bf16 39 -> 28 but fp16 226 -> 312). Restructuring the kernel *does* recover bit-exactness, but only by trading itfor performance: reading re/im as two strided loads instead of one contiguous
load plus `tl.split` costs up to 13% on MI300X and up to 9% on GB300, growing with sequence length, and it then breaks bit-exactness on NVIDIA instead.

So the assertion pins codegen rather than correctness, and it is not stable across Triton versions or backends. On ROCm even `ApplyRotaryEmb.forward_hip` and `forward_native` are not bitwise identical to each other.

**Change** 
Relax the Q/K comparison to one ULP on all platforms. `V` is never read or written by the kernel, so it stays exact. The kernel itself is unchanged; only its docstring, which made the same bit-exactness claim, is corrected.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/core/test_apply_rotary_emb.py
```

The tolerance is one ULP at the largest magnitude in the tensor, rather than relative, because `o1` can cancel: the error scales with the inputs to the sum rather than with the result. Checked that it is still tight enough by measuring the real rounding gap and by mutating the kernel (flipping the sign in `o0`).

## Test Result

MI300X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.13, triton 3.8.0.

`4 failed` -> `7 passed, 3 skipped`.

| case | tolerance | observed | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| bfloat16, 2304 tokens | 3.93e-02 | 1.56e-02 | passes, 2.5x margin |
| float16, 2304 tokens | 4.91e-03 | 1.95e-03 | passes, 2.5x margin |
| sign flip in `o0` (bf16) | 3.93e-02 | 8.66e+00 | caught, 220x over |
| sign flip in `o0` (fp16) | 4.91e-03 | 8.66e+00 | caught, 1764x over |



---

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Avoid generation for empty streaming input
author: nvbfalk
body:
## Purpose

Fix the case where a streaming-input generator ends without yielding any chunks.

vLLM creates a placeholder request while setting up the stream. Previously, if the stream ended before sending its first chunk, that placeholder was submitted to the engine as a real generation request.

This change tracks whether any input chunk was submitted:

- If at least one chunk was submitted, the existing final-request behavior is unchanged.
- If the stream ends normally without any chunks, `STREAM_FINISHED` is placed directly on the output queue.
- If the input stream raises an error, the existing `InputStreamError` is preserved.

This was split out of #53861 following review feedback. It does not overlap with #58941 or #58942, which cover the collector-boundary and abort/session-race fixes.

## Test Plan

Added a regression test that verifies an empty input stream:

- Returns `STREAM_FINISHED`.
- Does not submit the placeholder request to the engine.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep in-flight requests on the same DP engine
author: nvbfalk
body:
## Purpose
Fix data-parallel routing for requests that are already in flight.

When another chunk arrives for an existing streaming request, the request must continue on the same engine that received its earlier chunks. Previously, the load balancer could select a different engine when processing the next chunk.

This change checks `reqs_in_flight` before performing load balancing. If the request is already assigned to an engine, that engine is returned directly.

This was split out of #53861 following review feedback.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Support raise_exception in chat templates
author: YashasviAsthana
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59009.

The Rust frontend renders HF chat templates with minijinja, which does not define `raise_exception`, the helper [transformers injects](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py) into chat templates. Templates that use it to reject unsupported input, such as Qwen3.8 rejecting `reasoning_effort: "high"`, failed with `unknown function: raise_exception is unknown` and returned HTTP 500, which clients retry. The reporter's agent client retried in a loop.

Register `raise_exception` so it fails the render with the template's own message, and surface that as a new `ChatTemplateRejected` request-validation error. The existing `chat_submit_error` then returns 400 `invalid_request_error` with the template's message, matching the Python frontend's `TemplateError` → 400 mapping in `vllm/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/error_response.py`.

Other template failures (e.g. an unknown function from a template typo) still return 500. Python returns 400 for every `TemplateError`; happy to widen this if you prefer full parity.

## Test Plan

```sh
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
pre-commit run --all-files
```

New tests cover the template's message passing through, an untaken raise_exception branch still rendering, unknown functions staying 500, and the 400 mapping in server/src/error.rs.

Test Result

- Full Rust workspace: 1894 passed, 13 skipped; clippy and pre-commit clean.
- The new tests fail with the raise_exception registration removed.
- No model evaluation needed: rendering output is unchanged for templates that don't raise. The reporter offered to verify on their 2x4090 Qwen3.8 setup.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Read Ling quantization_config from top-level config for Bailing V3 VL
author: mganczarenko
body:
## Purpose

`inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL-fp4` fails at weight loading on every platform:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (3) must match the size of tensor b (12) at non-singleton dimension 1
  (routed_experts.py, _load_w2)
```

The routed experts are MXFP4 (`routed_experts_quant_method: mxfp4`). `_configure_ling_fp8_quant_config` reads that from `config.quantization_config`, but the VL model builds its language model from `text_config`, which has no `quantization_config` (it lives on the top-level VL config). The helper returns early, `store_dtype` stays unset, and the experts get `Fp8MoEMethod` instead of `Mxfp4MoEMethod`. The same bug makes the model OOM at TP=1, because FP8 expert buffers are ~2x the MXFP4 size.

This PR makes the helper fall back to the current vLLM config's top-level `hf_config` when the config it receives has no `quantization_config`. Text-only Ling and the MTP draft (whose config already carries `quantization_config`) are unchanged.


## Test Plan

title: [Bugfix][Core] Schedule encoder-only prompts larger than one step
author: peperunas
body:
## Purpose

An encoder-only instance (`mm_encoder_only`, e.g. image-only serving) holds no KV cache, so `EngineCore.__init__` turns chunked prefill off *after* config validation has already passed (`"Disabling chunked prefill for model without KVCache"`, `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`). `SchedulerConfig.verify_max_model_len` only rejects `max_num_batched_tokens < max_model_len` while chunked prefill is off at validation time, so such an instance starts normally with a per-step budget smaller than its largest prompt.

At scheduling time `Scheduler.schedule` then reaches:

```python
if (
    not self.scheduler_config.enable_chunked_prefill
    and num_new_tokens > request_token_budget
):
    break
```

The request is only peeked from the waiting queue and never popped, and neither its prompt length nor the budget ever changes, so the same `break` fires on every step: the request waits forever and no error is raised anywhere.

This PR exempts encoder-only instances from that break with one clause, `and not self.is_mm_encoder_only`, so the existing `num_new_tokens = min(num_new_tokens, request_token_budget)` splits the prompt across steps. That is safe here specifically because an encoder-only instance keeps no KV cache for a resumed prefill to lose.

### Changes

- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — skip the "chunked prefill is disabled" break for encoder-only instances, letting the token budget split their prompt.
- `tests/v1/core/utils.py` — `create_scheduler(..., mm_encoder_only=True)` sets `model_config.multimodal_config.mm_encoder_only` after the model config is built.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` — `test_encoder_only_prompt_longer_than_budget_is_chunked`: a 2500-token prompt with `max_num_batched_tokens=1024` and `enable_chunked_prefill=False` schedules 1024 / 1024 / 452 over three steps.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and PRs for "encoder-only prompt", "max_num_batched_tokens validation", "mm_encoder_only stall" and related terms. No open PR makes the scheduler split an encoder-only prompt that exceeds one step; the nearest open work (#56826, #57368) concerns encoder input lifetimes across steps, which this does not touch.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py
ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=... .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q
```

## Test Result

- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` clean on the three changed files.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: 194 passed, the new test included.
- Negative control: reverting only the 4-line scheduler change makes `test_encoder_only_prompt_longer_than_budget_is_chunked` fail, so the test guards this change.
- No model eval: the change only schedules oversized encoder-only prompts that previously never ran; no logits-affecting code path changes.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used (pi coding agent): analysis, draft, and test runs were produced by the agent; the human author reviewed every changed line, ran the checks above, and defends the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Requeue encoder-stalled waiting requests
author: peperunas
body:
## Purpose

A waiting request can end a scheduling pass with `num_new_tokens == 0`: its encoder inputs do not fit the cache or the compute budget, or the prefill-lookahead reserve consumes the tokens. The waiting loop `break`ed there, so the request kept its head-of-queue position and every request behind it went unscheduled for that step — repeating on every step while the resource condition holds.

It is now requeued with `skip_request()`, which preserves the drain-first priority of requests holding KV blocks (async KV-load resumes) and the `deferred_waiting` accounting.

The self-pinned encoder-cache release from the earlier revision is dropped here; #60553 proposes that.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and PRs for waiting-queue requeue / head-of-line blocking and encoder cache stalls. No open PR touches this path; the nearest matches are #56826 and #57368 (encoder input lifetimes across steps — different concern), #40707/#40709 (mamba split deadlock — different path), and umbrella EPD tracker #52409.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py
ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

## Test Result

- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` clean.
- 248 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_encoder_cache_embed_count_mismatch_restores_prior_hit_state`: the mismatch path also returns zero tokens, so the `encoder_cache_manager.free(request)` added in d12809f1 drops the prior-hit references that test guards. It fails at 5219f995 as well, so it is not introduced by this drop.
- 3 tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` cover the requeue: queue head-of-line starvation, `deferred_waiting` accounting, drain-first queue membership.
- No model eval: the change only alters failure-path control flow, no logits-affecting code.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used (pi coding agent): analysis, draft and test runs. The human author reviewed every changed line, ran the checks above, and defends the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix] Load stacked expert weights for non-gated MoE
author: roikoren755
body:
## Purpose Fixes #49106. Supersedes #49110. NemotronH is non-gated and passes an empty up-projection name, so the fused-checkpoint name lookup in `build_expert_params_mapping` logged `Unexpected gate/up projection names` for every MoE layer. The warning hid a real bug: on lookup failure the whole fused mapping was dropped, so a NemotronH checkpoint in transformers' native stacked layout (`experts.up_proj` as `[E, I, H]`, written by `save_pretrained(..., save_original_format=False)`) loaded without error and produced garbage. - Mapping and loader branch on `moe_config.is_act_and_mul`. Non-gated layers get a single-shard `up_proj` fused entry plus `down_proj`, and the loader no longer halves w13 for them. The warning is only reachable for gated layers. - The up-projection checkpoint name is `str | None`, checked against the activation in the `RoutedExperts` constructor. NemotronH passes `None`, and the LoRA `..` workaround for the old empty-name entry is removed. Not a duplicate of #49110: that PR only silences the log line and leaves the stacked checkpoint unloadable. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py tests/lora/test_lora_weights.py -v ``` Three new tests cover the non-gated mapping, the unsplit stacked load, and the warning still firing for gated layers. Black-box smoke test: greedy decoding on 4 prompts, 32 tokens, comparing the merge base against this branch for gated and non-gated models, stacked and per-expert checkpoints, with and without LoRA. Scripts are in the details section below. ## Test Result Unit tests: 88 passed. Smoke test, all exact string matches unless noted: | Model | Checkpoint | LoRA | Merge base vs branch | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (gated) | per-expert | – | MATCH, under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | | Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct (gated) | stacked `gate_up_proj` | – | MATCH | | Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 | per-expert | – | MATCH | | Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 | per-expert | zero-init expert adapter | MATCH | | Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 | per-expert | random expert adapter | MATCH | Branch-only checks on the fix itself: | Check | Result | |---|---| | Stacked Nano checkpoint == hub checkpoint | MATCH (on the merge base it loads silently and generates garbage) | | Stacked Nano + zero adapter == per-expert Nano + zero adapter | MATCH | | Zero adapter == LoRA engine with no adapter | 1 token differs on 1/4 prompts after 137 identical chars | | No `Unexpected gate/up projection names` in any branch log | confirmed; every merge-base Nano log has it | Noise baseline: running the unchanged branch twice diverges late (after 43–131 chars) on 3/4 prompts for Qwen3-VL and 2/4 for Nano, so the exact matches above are stronger than the harness guarantees, and the one-token LoRA difference is inside run-to-run noise. NemotronH does not support batch-invariant kernels, and enabling them for Qwen3-VL-MoE produces garbage on both sides, so only the Qwen3 text model ran with deterministic kernels. Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); all changes reviewed and tests run by the submitter.
How the merge-base side was run The "merge base" arms run the same checkout with the five production files this PR changed swapped for their merge-base versions, via a `sitecustomize.py` import hook on `PYTHONPATH`. This isolates exactly the PR's effect with no drift from unrelated commits. Each merge-base log is checked to confirm `routed_experts` was imported from the shadow directory.
smoke_compare.sh — driver ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # A/B smoke test for PR 59031: runs dump_outputs.py on the current tree ("branch") # and on the same tree with the PR's changed modules swapped for their merge-base # versions ("main"), without checking anything out. set -euo pipefail cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" OUT=${OUT:-smoke_outputs} SHADOW=$OUT/main_shadow BASE=${BASE:-$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)} TP=${TP:-1} NANO=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 STACKED=${STACKED:-./nemotron3-nano-stacked} ZEROS_LORA=dasereb/Nemotron_3_Nano_BF16_r16_zeros DUMMY_LORA=ace-nguyen/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16-dummy-moe-lora PY=.venv/bin/python rm -rf "$SHADOW" mkdir -p "$SHADOW" echo "shadowing merge-base $BASE versions of:" for f in $(git diff --name-only "$BASE" HEAD -- 'vllm/*.py'); do git cat-file -e "$BASE:$f" 2>/dev/null || continue mkdir -p "$SHADOW/$(dirname "$f")" git show "$BASE:$f" > "$SHADOW/$f" echo " $f" done cat > "$SHADOW/sitecustomize.py" <<'EOF' import importlib.util import os import sys SHADOW = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) MODULES = {} for root, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join(SHADOW, "vllm")): for name in files: if name.endswith(".py"): path = os.path.join(root, name) rel = os.path.relpath(path, SHADOW)[: -len(".py")] MODULES[rel.replace(os.sep, ".")] = path class ShadowFinder: @staticmethod def find_spec(fullname, path=None, target=None): if fullname not in MODULES: return None return importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(fullname, MODULES[fullname]) sys.meta_path.insert(0, ShadowFinder()) print(f"[shadow] {len(MODULES)} modules overridden from {SHADOW}", file=sys.stderr) EOF # launch : runs one arm, skipping it if its JSON exists. launch() { local name=$1 json=$OUT/$1.json log=$OUT/$1.log shift echo "=== $name" if [ -f "$json" ]; then echo " exists, skipping: $json" return fi echo " log: $log" $PY dump_outputs.py "$@" --tp "$TP" --out "$json" > "$log" 2>&1 \ || { echo "FAILED, last lines of $log:"; tail -20 "$log"; exit 1; } tail -3 "$log" } run_branch() { local tag=$1 shift launch "${tag}_branch" "$@" } run() { local tag=$1 shift run_branch "$tag" "$@" PYTHONPATH=$SHADOW launch "${tag}_main" "$@" if [ -f "$OUT/${tag}_main.log" ]; then grep -q "routed_experts from: $(cd "$SHADOW" && pwd)" "$OUT/${tag}_main.log" \ || { echo "shadow did not take effect for $tag"; exit 1; } fi } # Gated, per-expert: A/B against merge-base with deterministic kernels, so the # comparison is exact. Only this model has a batch-invariant MoE path. VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 run qwen_text_per_expert --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 # Gated, stacked: A/B without deterministic kernels (batch-invariant mode breaks # this model), plus a branch repeat to measure run-to-run noise. run qwen_vl_stacked --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct run_branch qwen_vl_stacked_repeat --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct # Non-gated, per-expert checkpoint: A/B, with and without LoRA, plus a branch # repeat for the noise baseline (NemotronH does not support batch invariance). run nano_base --model "$NANO" run_branch nano_base_repeat --model "$NANO" run nano_zeros --model "$NANO" --lora "$ZEROS_LORA" run nano_dummy --model "$NANO" --lora "$DUMMY_LORA" # LoRA kernel path with no adapter: the reference for the zero-adapter no-op checks. run_branch nano_lora_noadapter --model "$NANO" --lora-enabled-no-adapter # Non-gated, stacked checkpoint: branch only (merge-base loads it as garbage). if [ -d "$STACKED" ]; then run_branch nano_stacked --model "$STACKED" --tokenizer "$NANO" run_branch nano_stacked_zeros --model "$STACKED" --tokenizer "$NANO" --lora "$ZEROS_LORA" else echo "skipping stacked Nano rows: $STACKED not found (set STACKED=...)" fi echo echo "=== results" $PY summarize_results.py --dir "$OUT" ```
dump_outputs.py — one arm ```python """Dump greedy outputs for a model, optionally with a LoRA adapter, to a JSON file.""" import argparse import json import sys from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.routed_experts as routed_experts from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest print("routed_experts from:", routed_experts.__file__, file=sys.stderr) PROMPTS = [ "The capital of France is", "def fibonacci(n):", "Water boils at a temperature of", "Write one sentence about the moon.", ] parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--model", required=True) parser.add_argument("--tokenizer", help="defaults to --model") parser.add_argument("--lora", help="HF repo id of a LoRA adapter") parser.add_argument( "--lora-enabled-no-adapter", action="store_true", help="enable LoRA in the engine but attach no adapter (kernel-path control)", ) parser.add_argument("--out", required=True) parser.add_argument("--tp", type=int, default=1) args = parser.parse_args() llm_kwargs = dict( model=args.model, tokenizer=args.tokenizer or args.model, tensor_parallel_size=args.tp, max_model_len=2048, ) if args.lora or args.lora_enabled_no_adapter: llm_kwargs.update(enable_lora=True, max_loras=1, max_lora_rank=16) llm = LLM(**llm_kwargs) params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=32, temperature=0) lora_request = None if args.lora: lora_request = LoRARequest("adapter", 1, snapshot_download(args.lora)) outputs = llm.generate(PROMPTS, params, lora_request=lora_request) result = {p: o.outputs[0].text for p, o in zip(PROMPTS, outputs)} with open(args.out, "w") as f: json.dump(result, f, indent=2) print(json.dumps(result, indent=2)) del llm ```
summarize_results.py — report ```python """Summarize smoke_compare.sh outputs into a markdown report.""" import argparse import json import os import re from pathlib import Path PAIRS = [ ( "qwen_text_per_expert_main", "qwen_text_per_expert_branch", "gated, per-expert, batch-invariant: main vs branch", ), ("qwen_vl_stacked_main", "qwen_vl_stacked_branch", "gated, stacked: main vs branch"), ( "qwen_vl_stacked_branch", "qwen_vl_stacked_repeat_branch", "gated, stacked: noise baseline (branch vs branch repeat)", ), ("nano_base_main", "nano_base_branch", "non-gated, per-expert: main vs branch"), ( "nano_base_branch", "nano_base_repeat_branch", "non-gated: noise baseline (branch vs branch repeat)", ), ("nano_zeros_main", "nano_zeros_branch", "non-gated + zero LoRA: main vs branch"), ("nano_dummy_main", "nano_dummy_branch", "non-gated + random LoRA: main vs branch"), ( "nano_zeros_branch", "nano_lora_noadapter_branch", "zero LoRA == LoRA engine without adapter (branch)", ), ("nano_stacked_branch", "nano_base_branch", "stacked == per-expert (branch)"), ( "nano_stacked_zeros_branch", "nano_lora_noadapter_branch", "stacked + zero LoRA == LoRA engine without adapter (branch)", ), ] WARNING = "Unexpected gate/up projection names" SHADOW_LINE = re.compile(r"routed_experts from: (.*)") def load(path: Path) -> dict[str, str] | None: return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else None def common_prefix(a: str, b: str) -> int: n = 0 for x, y in zip(a, b): if x != y: break n += 1 return n def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--dir", default="smoke_outputs") parser.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="defaults to /RESULTS.md") args = parser.parse_args() out_dir = Path(args.dir) report = Path(args.out) if args.out else out_dir / "RESULTS.md" lines = ["# Smoke comparison results", ""] lines += ["| Check | A | B | Result |", "|---|---|---|---|"] details = [] for a, b, label in PAIRS: ra, rb = load(out_dir / f"{a}.json"), load(out_dir / f"{b}.json") if ra is None or rb is None: missing = [n for n, r in ((a, ra), (b, rb)) if r is None] lines.append(f"| {label} | {a} | {b} | MISSING {', '.join(missing)} |") continue if ra == rb: lines.append(f"| {label} | {a} | {b} | MATCH |") continue differing = [p for p in ra if ra[p] != rb.get(p)] lines.append(f"| {label} | {a} | {b} | DIFF ({len(differing)}/{len(ra)} prompts) |") details += ["", f"## DIFF: {label}", ""] for prompt in differing: x, y = ra[prompt], rb.get(prompt, "") details += [ f"**Prompt:** {prompt!r} ", f"common prefix: {common_prefix(x, y)} chars", "", f"- `{a}`: {x!r}", f"- `{b}`: {y!r}", "", ] lines += ["", "## Logs", "", "| Run | gate/up warning | routed_experts source |", "|---|---|---|"] for log in sorted(out_dir.glob("*.log")): text = log.read_text(errors="replace") warned = "YES" if WARNING in text else "no" m = SHADOW_LINE.search(text) source = os.path.relpath(m.group(1), out_dir) if m else "?" lines.append(f"| {log.stem} | {warned} | `{source}` |") report.write_text("\n".join(lines + details) + "\n") print(report.read_text()) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
Creating the stacked Nano checkpoint Loading without `trust_remote_code` uses transformers' built-in `NemotronHExperts`, whose `up_proj`/`down_proj` are single `[E, ...]` parameters; `save_original_format=False` keeps that layout on disk instead of reverting to per-expert tensors. ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM MODEL = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16" model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cpu") model.save_pretrained("./nemotron3-nano-stacked", save_original_format=False) ```
