title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Never allocate GPU pages without host backing
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Description

When the HiSparse host pool fills, `HiSparseSourceManager.allocate_new_blocks` gives new pages a null host entry. Those pages are never written back, so they never become clean and their GPU blocks can never be reclaimed: they stay pinned for the life of the request. Freeing host capacity does not fix it, because later allocations extend the host table and the freed blocks go to new tail pages, never to the old null ones. Host prefix publication for the request also stalls at the first null page.

The result is GPU KV pressure and preemptions that HiSparse is meant to prevent, plus lost host prefix-cache coverage, persisting after host capacity has recovered.

Fix: never allocate a page without host backing (alternative to #58963, which backfills null pages after the fact):

- `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` requires host blocks for every page being allocated, not just external-load destinations, and reuses the existing admission sentinel when they don't fit. The scheduler then waits or preempts exactly as it does for GPU exhaustion.
- The best-effort `allocate_new_blocks` override (null padding) is deleted.
- `has_pending_reclamation` also reports host blocks that an in-flight write-back will return (freed request, spill not yet acked), so the scheduler waits a step instead of over-preempting.
- Startup rejects a host pool that cannot hold one `max_model_len` request (plus the null block and a copy-on-write tail), which would otherwise livelock.

## Effect on KV-cache memory over time

**Before.** While the host pool is full, every page a running request seals gets a null host entry and keeps its GPU block for the rest of the request. The pinned set only grows: host blocks freed later go to new tail pages, never to the old null ones. A request that decodes through a host-full window therefore holds GPU KV proportional to the tokens produced during that window, as if HiSparse were off for those pages, and releases it only when it finishes or is preempted. Across the batch, GPU free blocks drift down while the host stays full, and the scheduler preempts (and later recomputes) requests that HiSparse should have kept running. Prefix publication for those requests also stops at the first null page, so the host prefix cache never covers the rest of their context.

**After.** Every GPU-resident page has a host page, so its GPU footprint is transient: a sealed page is dirty until its write-back completes (about one step), stays pinned while within the two-page active tail, and is unpinned once the request can read from host (it has a hot region). Unpinned pages stay readable but count as free, so the GPU pool reclaims them under pressure. Per-request GPU usage is bounded by the hot region, the active tail and in-flight write-backs, independent of context length, for as long as the request runs.

The host pool becomes the hard capacity limit instead: running requests together hold one host block per computed page, and when it is full, new allocations wait or preempt even if GPU blocks are free. Since HiSparse only pays off when the host pool is much larger than the GPU pool, this replaces the gradual, hard-to-see GPU buildup above with a rare, explicit admission limit.

## Related

- #58963 fixes the same bug by backfilling host blocks for null pages after capacity frees up (one page per step). This PR prevents the null pages instead, which removes rather than adds state; only one of the two should land.
- #57457 also edits `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` (counts GPU copies pinned by a host-prefix hit). The changes compose: its copy-pin count replaces this PR's final `return 0`.
- #58949's steady-state concurrency estimate assumes resident pages spill to host; this PR makes that hold under host pressure, and its host-pool gauges become the direct signal for the new admission limit.

## Test Plan

Repro on main (unit-level): with a 3-block host pool, the request's pages 1-3 get null host entries; after the donor frees its block, the capacity goes to new tail page 4, and pages 1-3 stay pinned (`ref_cnt=1`) indefinitely while page 5 is null again.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -q
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py -v
```

## Test Result

- CPU: 341 passed; other HiSparse-tagged suites (scheduler, NIXL HMA, stats, config): 22 passed.
- e2e (B300, reduced DeepSeek-V3.2, dummy weights): 3 passed. The new `test_hisparse_host_exhaustion_defers_requests` fails on main (a scheduled request has a null host page).

Accuracy with trained weights and serving throughput under host pressure were not measured.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation, tests, and this description.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Apply expert_map remapping for CUTLASS FP4 MOE expert parallel
author: ilmarkov
body:
## Purpose
Fixes silent MoE corruption when running CUTLASS NVFP4 or MXFP4 MoE with expert parallelism.

CutlassExpertsFp4 and CutlassExpertsMxfp4 accepted expert_map in apply() but never used it. With EP enabled, `topk_ids` stayed in global expert space while weights are local, so tokens were to the wrong experts. 
This showed up as degenerate outputs (e.g. ~0% GSM8K on RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4 with DP=8 / EP=8 see issue #58729 ).

PR remaps global `topk_ids` local ids via `expert_map` before CUTLASS FP4/MXFP4 grouped GEMM.

## Test Plan

gsm8k validation

server:
```
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4 \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --served-model-name RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-cumem-allocator \
  --enable-ep-weight-filter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --numa-bind \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.87 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 64 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","mode":0}'
```

client:

```
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=5,tokenized_requests=False,timeout=600" \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --gen_kwargs reasoning_effort=low \
  --batch_size 1
```


result:
```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9507|±  |0.0060|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9484|±  |0.0061|
```

(Result before was 0% score)

pytests:

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py::test_remap_topk_ids_to_local -v`
- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py::test_cutlass_fp4_moe_EP -v`
- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_make_mxfp4_moe_kernel_validates_cutlass_expert_parallel -v`
- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_make_mxfp4_moe_kernel_rejects_cutlass_unsupported_expert_parallel -v`

New remapping kernel overhead is ~1.6 us, i.e. ~1% of Gemm kernel.

Changes:
- Move the existing Triton `remap_topk_to_local` kernel from `gpt_oss_triton_kernels_moe.py` into `fused_moe/utils.py` and reuse it from both GPT-OSS Triton and CUTLASS paths.
- Add `out_dtype` support (int32 for CUTLASS, int64 default for GPT-OSS) in the `remap_topk_to_local` kernel.
- Fix misleading CutlassExpertsFp8 comment: FP8 EP already applies expert_map in moe_permute, not in the CUTLASS kernel itself.
- Relax `_supports_parallel_config` for `CutlassExpertsFp4` / `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`: allow EP with allgather_reducescatter; still block FlashInfer NVLink / DeepEP HT backends (same as FP8).
- `make_mxfp4_moe_kernel` validation so compressed-tensors CUTLASS bypass fails fast on unsupported parallel configs (adapted from #59033 ).

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Seed derender detokenization from the prompt
author: hickeyma
body:
## Purpose

On SentencePiece tokenizers (Llama-2, Phi-3), `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` drop the first output token's leading space but the main endpoints keep it. The engine seeds its detokenizer with the prompt while derender decoded the output tokens with no prompt context.

Derender now seeds its decode window from the prompt tail too. That covers batch chat and completions, streaming with and without a parser, and streaming completions. Each derender request takes an optional `prompt_token_ids` (the `token_ids` from `/render`). If it's missing, derender uses the generate response's `prompt_token_ids`. If that's missing too, it decodes as before and logs a warning once. Nothing breaks for existing callers.

Other changes:
- The batch paths now go through the same incremental `_detokenize_delta` as streaming, so `clean_up_tokenization_spaces` no longer applies there. That matches what the engine does.
- `_detokenize_delta` trims its window after every token, so long batch decodes stay linear.
- `prompt_token_ids` is capped at `max_model_len`, like the other caller- upplied token lists.
- Derender now works out `skip_special_tokens` and `spaces_between_special_tokens` the same way the engine does. Before, the parser paths hardcoded `skip_special_tokens=False` and never passed `spaces_between_special_tokens`, so a request with `spaces_between_special_tokens: false` could decode differently. The fast/slow detokenizer check is now a shared helper (`uses_fast_detokenizer()`) used by both the engine and derender, so the slow path matches too.

Fixes #59043. Reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42729#issuecomment-5857086699.

Also fixes #59089. When the output stopped mid-character (e.g. `max_tokens` cutting an emoji), batch derender decoded the whole id list in one go and tacked a `�` on the end. The engine holds those partial bytes back and so does streaming derender. As the batch paths now go through `_detokenize_delta` (same as streaming), they get the same hold-back, so the trailing `�` is gone. Added a unit test that cuts 🌈 one byte short and checks batch, streaming and the engine's `DecodeStream` all give the same text.

## Test Plan

`pytest -s -v tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py`
`pytest -s -v tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py`

The new unit tests use the tiny Llama (Metaspace) tokenizer and compare each decode path against a `DecodeStream` primed with the prompt. The HTTP tests check that seeded output gains exactly the leading space and that the new length and bounds checks return 400.

## Test Result

All tests pass.

title: [CI] Allowlist-shrink batch 2: wire 9 tests/models/ files into Buildkite, fix 2 stale bugs found
author: wjabbour
body:
## Summary
- Follow-up to #54867 / #58055 (test-tethering check): shrinks the allowlist by 9 more entries, all of `tests/models/`.
  - Wires 5 CPU-safe files into `models_basic.yaml`'s `basic-models-test-other-cpu` job (`Basic Models Other`): `test_language_model_cache_is_weak.py`, `deepseek_v32/test_sequence_parallel.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py`, `test_dspark_mla.py`, `transformers/test_layer_registry.py`. None need a GPU (each is `cpu_test`-marked, says so in its own docstring, or has no device/compiled-op use). The job's timeout goes 20 -> 30 minutes for the added files.
  - Wires 3 ROCm-specific files (`test_deepseek_v4_dspark_rocm.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_rocm_wo_a.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_rocm_compressor_gemm_fusion.py`) into the `Basic Models (Other)` AMD MI355 mirror only; they are ROCm-named and not run in the NVIDIA job.
  - Splits `transformers/test_layer_registry.py`: its four unit tests (pure `layers._resolve` logic) stay in that file and run in the CPU job; the one test that serves a model through `vllm_runner` moves to a new `transformers/test_layer_registry_e2e.py`, wired into the `Basic Models (Other)` job (H200, + its AMD MI355 mirror). The two files' docstrings point at each other.
  - Wires `test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py` into the same `Basic Models (Other)` job and its AMD MI355 mirror. It hardcodes `device="cuda"`, which is the HIP device on ROCm builds (`torch.cuda.is_available()` is true there), and uses only mocks and small tensors, so it runs on both vendors. It passes on a ROCm gfx1201 box. The mirror also now runs upstream's two sibling `deepseek_v41` replay tests (`test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`), which were NVIDIA-job-only but pass on ROCm too.
- Since these files hadn't run in CI, running them surfaced pre-existing bugs (not introduced by this PR), now fixed:
  - `test_dspark_mla.py::test_dspark_markov_head_is_replicated` constructed a `ParallelLMHead` directly and called `.bias()` without calling `process_weights_after_loading()` (the step real model loading always performs before a layer's `quant_method.apply()` is usable). On any real platform this crashes: `NotImplementedError` on ROCm (no GPU tensor), `AttributeError` on a CPU build (`layer.cpu_linear` never set). Traced through `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()`'s `is_rocm()`/`is_cpu()` branches and reproduced both failures; the fix calls `process_weights_after_loading()` after constructing the head, matching real model loading.
  - `transformers/test_layer_registry.py`'s two caplog tests relied on plain `caplog`, which only sees vLLM's records before any `LLM()` has been constructed in the session: `vllm/logger.py` sets `propagate=False` on the `"vllm"` logger on the first `LLM()`, after which records never reach the root logger. In the target job `test_backend.py` constructs several `LLM()`s first, so this failed for real. title: [Bugfix][Core] Remove redundant AuxOutput reset guards after pause
author: aoshen02

AuxOutput reset checks unnecessarily constrain the pause mode. For example, an abort-mode pause can finish draining outputs without setting `PAUSED_ALL`.

title: [Bugfix][Engram] Keep THP tables private when resolving shared memory
author: yuzhouo7
body:
## Purpose

`use_thp` is silently ignored under DP. It is only validated against `dp_shared_memory` at construction, where the field is still unset. The DP default from #57651 then resolves sharing on for any CPU-offloaded, non-elastic run with DP > 1, and the table allocator takes the shared branch before the THP branch added in #56926:

```python
config = EngramConfig(use_thp=True)  # dp_shared_memory=None
config.resolve_dp_shared_memory(ParallelConfig(data_parallel_size=2))
config.dp_shared_memory  # True on main; the tables are never THP-backed
```

This PR leaves automatic sharing off when THP is requested (one added predicate, `and not self.use_thp`). That is what both fields already document: sharing defaults on "whenever the other settings allow it", and `use_thp` "requires cpu_offload without dp_shared_memory".

Effect on a DP > 1 run with `use_thp=True`: instead of one `/dev/shm` table shared by the node-local replicas, the tables are private, THP-backed and head-sharded across the node-local Engram DP group, which is the existing non-shared path. Host memory stays at one table per node (without co-located replicas, sharing was not possible anyway); lookups use the per-step Engram DP collectives that sharing avoids. THP versus shared-table performance under DP has not been measured here. Users who prefer sharing can leave `use_thp` unset.

Unchanged: every configuration without `use_thp`, explicit `dp_shared_memory=False`, and the construction-time rejection of explicit `use_thp=True, dp_shared_memory=True`.

Not a duplicate: open PR searches for `use_thp`, `dp_shared_memory`, `resolve_dp_shared_memory` and Engram THP found no fix for this interaction. #58439 adds a `checkpoint_mapped` predicate to the same expression for a different option; whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase.

## Test Plan

The existing resolver test matrix now also covers implicit THP, explicit private tables and elastic EP. A new test checks that explicit shared memory plus THP is still rejected. Both are pure config tests and use the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker, so their teardown does not need an accelerator.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \
  -k 'engram_dp_shared_memory_defaults or engram_thp_rejects_explicit_shared_memory'
```

## Test Result

Against main `6b24bd8e75a3e465083e8a131968915bc00efaf4`, running the new tests on the original and on the fixed `vllm/config/engram.py`:

```text
Original: 1 failed, 6 passed   (only the implicit THP case fails)
Fixed:    7 passed
Both:     0 errors, 0 skips
```

The tests ran in a CPU-only container (Python 3.12.13, pytest 9.1.1), with no config mocks or custom pytest plugin. Ruff 0.14.0 check and format passed.

No model evaluation: the change only selects which existing storage path holds the tables and does not change lookup results. The THP storage path and its exact-row lookups are covered by #56926's tests.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not let mark_miss() flip a pending or in-flight async lookup probe
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Purpose

When a slow KV offload tier (the filesystem or object-store tier) fails to load a block, it records "this block is not really there" so the scheduler stops retrying it. That note is written against whatever lookup currently exists for the block. If the request that started the load was cancelled in the meantime, and another request has since asked about the same block, the note lands on the newer, unfinished lookup, and the engine crashes on an internal consistency check. The trigger is ordinary traffic: a client disconnects while its cached prefix is being loaded, and another request shares that prefix. The result is that the whole engine goes down, not just one request. This PR makes the note apply only to lookups that have already finished.

Concretely, `AsyncLookupManager.mark_miss()` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/async_lookup.py:216-224`) forces a cached lookup entry to `RESOLVED`/`False` without checking its phase. If the entry belongs to a newer probe that is still `PENDING` or `IN_FLIGHT`, that probe's own result later trips the phase asserts on the scheduler thread (`drain_results()` at `:204`, or `flush()` at `:181`), and the engine core dies.

How it happens with the FS tier (the OBJ tier calls `mark_miss` the same way, `obj/manager.py:400`):

1. Request A looks up key K and gets a hit. The tier starts a promotion (load job) for K.
2. A is aborted or finishes while the load is still in flight. `on_request_finished` calls `cleanup("A")`, which deletes the `RESOLVED` entry for K.
3. Request B looks up K. This creates a new `PENDING` entry, and `flush()` at the end of the step moves it to `IN_FLIGHT`.
4. A's load fails (file evicted, truncated or unreadable). `get_finished_jobs()` calls `mark_miss([K])` (`fs/manager.py:306`), which flips B's `IN_FLIGHT` entry to `RESOLVED`/`False`.
5. B's next `lookup()` drains the probe result and hits `assert state.phase is LookupPhase.IN_FLIGHT`. If step 4 lands while the entry is still `PENDING`, `flush()` asserts instead.

Needed: a client disconnect during a promotion, a failed load, and another request that shares the prefix.

**Fix:** `mark_miss()` now overrides only `RESOLVED` entries. A `PENDING` or `IN_FLIGHT` entry belongs to a newer probe, and that probe returns its own verdict. The #49176 livelock guard is unchanged: if the block is still bad, the next failed load marks the resolved entry `False` exactly as before, and the request stops re-issuing the promotion. One side effect: a newer probe that read the file before the failure can still return `True` once, which costs one more failed load. It does not loop.

**Not a duplicate:** I checked the open PRs that touch `async_lookup.py`: #57474 (draft, per-request-group result publishing), #58168 (draft, manager `lock()`/`unlock()`) and #52103 (draft, provenance). None of them changes `mark_miss` or the phase handling. `mark_miss` itself came in with #49328; #55823, #54872 and #55075 are the neighbouring merged fixes.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py -q -k "mark_miss or failed_load"
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

New tests:

- `test_async_lookup.py::test_mark_miss_skips_newer_unresolved_probe[in_flight|pending]`: the unit sequence above, for both phases.
- `test_fs_tier.py::test_failed_load_after_abort_does_not_break_newer_probe`: the same sequence end to end on `FileSystemTierManager`, with a load that really fails.

## Test Result

With the fix (macOS arm64, CPU, rebased on `32cc3f1ea`):

```
tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py + test_fs_tier.py -k "mark_miss_skips_newer or failed_load_after_abort" ... 3 passed
tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ ... 436 passed, 1 skipped
```

On `main` (fix reverted, new tests kept): all 3 new tests fail on the engine asserts:

```
vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/async_lookup.py:204: AssertionError   (in_flight)
vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/async_lookup.py:181: AssertionError   (pending)
vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/async_lookup.py:204: AssertionError   (FS tier end to end)
3 failed
```

pre-commit (`--from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`) and `mypy-3.12` (manual stage): clean.

This is a scheduler-side control-path change; model outputs are unaffected, so no evals are needed.

**Related:** one of a few independent fixes from an audit of the KV transfer paths (CPU offload, NIXL, P2P): #59099, #59102, #59325, #59329. None depends on another; they can be reviewed and merged in any order.

## AI assistance

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to audit this code path, write the fix and write the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer, as `AGENTS.md` asks.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Make reset_cache re-entrant
author: sohom-cs
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A second `reset_cache()` on the offloading connector before the engine steps again fails on `assert not self._current_batch_jobs_to_flush`. The engine keeps running, but the call that made the second reset gets the error. It happens when two `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` calls arrive with no step in between while store jobs are in flight: the first reset moves those jobs into the flush set, which stays set until the next step sends it. In the multiprocess engine, pause and sleep clear caches only once the engine is idle, so they don't hit this; in the in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`), pause clears at once, so a pause or sleep can be one of the two resets. This lets the second reset add to the pending flush set instead of asserting.

The first version of this PR also kept an idle engine stepping until the flush set reached the workers. #62929 now does that (the engine keeps stepping until the flushed jobs are reported), so that part is gone after merging main.

## Claims

- Two `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` calls with no step in between no longer raise. The first reset's flush set still goes out on the next step, and the engine goes idle once the workers report those jobs.
- A single reset is unchanged, and the other three "not in the middle of a step" asserts stay.

## Validation

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q -k reset_twice_before_a_step
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

`test_cache_reset_twice_before_a_step_still_flushes` uses the real-scheduler helpers from #62929: it finishes a request with its store jobs in flight, resets twice, then checks that the next `schedule()` carries exactly those jobs in `jobs_to_flush` and that the engine goes idle once they are reported.

On main (8321d1119bc2, Linux CPU) the second reset fails:

```
>       assert not self._current_batch_jobs_to_flush
E       AssertionError
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py:2463: AssertionError
```

With the fix it passes, and so does the rest of the file (446 passed, Linux CPU); pre-commit is clean on both files. These tests build the CPU offload region in `/dev/shm`, so they don't run on macOS. No CI step runs this file today: the GPU "V1 KV Connectors" step is disabled, and the CPU step selects only `cpu_test`-marked tests. No GPU run: the reproducer is scheduler-level. Model outputs are unaffected, so no evals.

## Details

`_reset_cache()` moves every in-flight job id into `_current_batch_jobs_to_flush` and leaves it set on purpose: the workers must wait on those jobs before a later store reuses their CPU chunks, and the set goes out in the next step's metadata. A second reset before that step finds it non-empty. Merging into it is safe: the first reset already moved and cleared every in-flight job, so the second adds no ids, leaves #62929's fence as it is, and does not call `on_reset_flushed()` while the fence is held.

The reset is reached from `pause_generation(clear_cache=True)` and sleep (`EngineCore._reset_caches`, the RL weight-update path), from the dev-mode `POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` and from `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`.

Not a duplicate: #62929 leaves this assert in place, and none of the open offload PRs that touch this file removes it.

AI-assisted; reviewed and tested by me.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Drop stale block hashes when a session truncates tokens
author: sawsa307
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #49377.

When a streaming-input session continues, `_update_request_as_session` truncates `_all_token_ids` at `num_computed_tokens`, discarding the last sampled (never-computed) output token. `update_block_hashes` only appends and the hasher resumes at `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size`, so if the discarded token completed a hash block, that hash kept identifying the replaced sequence and could later be committed under the stale identity — letting a request whose prefix matches the old tokens hit KV computed from the new ones. The fix drops the block hashes covering discarded tokens right where the token truncation happens; blocks fully inside the kept prefix stay valid.

## This PR carries #52806

This carries #52806 by @brianosaurus (original author unresponsive to review requests) with all review comments from @sawsa307 addressed:

- Removed the comment in `scheduler.py` that only described code behavior.
- Test no longer hardcodes the block size (`hash_block_size = scheduler.hash_block_size`).
- Test docstring shortened per AGENTS.md; details kept here instead.

The original author and contributors are credited via `Co-authored-by` trailers: Brian Woods (original #52806 author), Claude Opus 5 (original commit's co-author trailer), and Change72 (initial fix idea in #49377, requested by the reviewer). This is not a duplicate PR: #52806 has been stalled since the review round; this PR applies the identical fix with the requested changes so it can move forward, with full credit preserved.

Note on forward interaction with #58778: if #58778 (keep_end fold) lands first, this drop's lower bound should switch from `num_computed_tokens` to `keep_end`; conversely if this lands first, #58778 should keep the drop at `keep_end`.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=/tmp /Users/davidcheung/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -q -p skip_cleanup_plugin
```

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Reserve the bonus KV slot for fill-in DSpark
author: notimesea
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59104. DSpark with `sample_from_anchor=false` writes a bonus query plus N draft queries, but reserves only N lookahead slots. At a KV-block boundary, the extra write can use a stale block-table entry and corrupt another request's target KV.

Reserve N+1 slots for this layout. Anchor-sampling DSpark and DFlash behavior remain unchanged.

Related PR #48909 addresses the same mismatch with a broader four-file change, including a shared query-width property and the older runner's max-length guard. This PR is a smaller two-file alternative limited to lookahead reservation and its regression test.

## Tests

The commits are ordered test-first, fix-second:

1. `58eff92e7`: adds a plain regression test with loops and asserts; no pytest import or decorators.
2. `a26af2d9d`: fixes lookahead reservation.

```sh
python -m pytest --noconftest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py -k dspark_lookahead_covers_query_window -q
```

**Before: 1 failed. After: 1 passed.** The test covers 12 combinations of true/false/missing anchor flag, N=1/7 and block sizes 16/32, with prompt lengths spanning two blocks. Validation used the exact test file in an isolated pinned-nightly environment with the source fix applied; the full repository suite was not run. Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.

Standalone [synthetic CUDA reproducer](https://gist.github.com/notimesea/7de52434b9ef659e1ae6a6aab4d201b7) exercises the actual draft slot-preparation kernel without model weights or user prompts. It fails before the fix and passes after it; instructions and expected output are included in the gist.

## GPU validation

Gemma4-31B-it + RedHatAI DSpark on one H200, BF16, FA4, V2 runner, eager, synchronous scheduling, prefix caching off, no LoRA; vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev284+gbeef814e1`.

- Before: deterministic malformed output on batch 9; instrumentation confirmed two draft writes into target-owned blocks.
- After: three cold starts × 20 batches × 16 requests (**960 responses**), no observed corruption; identical output tokens across the three runs. On the originally failing batch, no invalid draft writes or target-KV mutations were observed.

This is bounded regression validation, not a full quality benchmark or a claim of bitwise equivalence to non-speculative decoding.

title: [Bugfix][Determinism] Preserve output dtype in batch-invariant mean
author: Prudhvivuda
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59078. In batch-invariant mode, `mean_batch_invariant` returns FP32 for FP16/BF16 inputs when no output dtype is requested. This promotes DeepEncoder's `LayerNorm2d` output to FP32, causing the next BF16 convolution to fail during startup.

Restore the input dtype at the final return while retaining FP32 accumulation and the existing reduction order. Explicit FP32 requests remain FP32. Extend the existing determinism suite with default/explicit output dtype coverage across FP16/BF16/FP32 and single/multiple reduction dimensions.

Duplicate-work check (2026-09-28): reviewed #59078 and its comments and searched open PRs for `59078 in:body` and `mean_batch_invariant`. No competing fix or ownership claim was found. Related #55249 fixes softmax and #55466 fixes matmul precision; neither addresses this mean output dtype.

title: [Bugfix][CPU][DiffusionGemma] Support narrower canvas w/ sync scheduling
author: ojeda-e
body:
## Purpose

Fixes DiffusionGemma structured reads on the CPU backend.

Structured reads were added to DiffusionGemma in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57250 and tested on GPU. On CPU they fail with the faster narrower canvases. When async scheduling is disabled, reads that ask for a canvas narrower than the served one are rejected. CPU always runs synchronous scheduling (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31525), and the error asks for `--async-scheduling`, but CPU ignores that flag.

The same happens on any platform started with `--no-async-scheduling`.

This PR adds a synchronous diffusion scheduler that trims each request's canvas to its own width. The async diffusion scheduler already does this. Other models are not affected.

### Changes in this PR

- Add a `DiffusionScheduler` for sync scheduling. It cuts each request's canvas down to the width the request asked for, in `update_draft_token_ids()`. `DiffusionAsyncScheduler` now inherits from it.
- `VllmConfig` selects the matching diffusion scheduler for both sync and async scheduling.
- Remove the check that rejected narrow canvases unless `--async-scheduling` was set.
- Update the structured diffusion README and the tests in `tests/test_sampling_params.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` to match.

No open issue or PR covers this. I searched for `diffusion_canvas_length`, DiffusionGemma on CPU and CPU async scheduling for diffusion. The closest is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58964, which fixed a separate DiffusionGemma crash on CPU. Structured reads still fail on CPU after that fix. 

I used Codex to help with this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C, Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at 32cc3f1ea8, with the real `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` checkpoint in BF16.

**Unit tests:**

```bash
pytest -v tests/test_sampling_params.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
```

**End to end:**

1. Before and after. Send a read with a 32-token canvas to a server with a 64-token canvas, on `main` and with this PR.
2. Correctness. Compare that read with a full-width read on a server with a 32-token canvas. Both give the model the same 32 tokens. The logprobs of 8 label ids at the answer position should match.
3. Serving. Run `vllm serve` with `structured_server.py` in front of it, as in the example README. Send the README's `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/systemone` requests with an outage ticket and a typo ticket. Then send a plain chat completion straight to vLLM.

```bash
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=8 vllm serve google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it --served-model-name dgemma \
    --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 64}' --max-logprobs 32 --enable-prefix-caching \
    --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 8
python examples/features/structured_diffusion/structured_server.py --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
    --tokenizer google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it --canvas 64 --port 8011
```

## Test Result

Before (`main`), the read fails. The issue has the full traceback and the `collect_env.py` output.

```text
vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: A diffusion_canvas_length smaller than the served canvas requires --async-scheduling. (parameter=extra_args)
```

After:

- Unit tests: 276 passed.
- The narrow read now works. `DiffusionScheduler` serves it, and its logprobs at the answer position match the full-width read exactly (max difference 0 across 8 label ids). Both answer "yes" with p = 0.89.
- Through `structured_server.py`, `/v1/systemone` gives 0.91 urgency for the outage ticket (4 reads, 2.0 s) and 0.00006 for the typo ticket (1 read, 0.7 s). Every request returns HTTP 200, and the server logs show no errors.
- A plain chat completion straight to `vllm serve` returns `"thought\nThe capital of France is Paris."` and stops normally.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix GLM-5.3-Flash vision tower crashes on image input
author: gaby
body:
## Purpose

Fix two independent ways an image request takes down the engine in the GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) vision tower.

**1. Every image trips the GPU sync check.** `rot_pos_emb` builds `pos_ids` on the host and copied it with `.to(device, non_blocking=True)` from pageable memory, and the eager `forward` did the same with `cu_seqlens`. A non-blocking copy from pageable memory can block the host, so with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` the first image raises `Implicit GPU<->CPU sync detected - use a pinned, densely laid out CPU tensor, or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()` and the engine dies.

Fix: stage both copies through pinned memory with `async_tensor_h2d`, as `Glm4vVisionTransformer` does for its position tables. The eager and CUDA-graph forward paths are otherwise unchanged. The `max_seqlen` read-back in the ViT attention wrappers already runs under `gpu_sync_allowed()`, so nothing else in the eager path trips the check.

**2. Slim images overflow the vision rope table.** Since vllm-project/vllm#57387, images go through the transformers `Glm5NextImageProcessor`, whose `smart_resize` bounds them by token budget only, with no aspect-ratio cap. A slim image therefore gets a grid side beyond the hardcoded `max_position=8192`. For example, with the checkpoint's `processor_config.json`, a 200000×20 px image is accepted at 7143 tokens with `image_grid_thw = [1, 2, 14286]`, and `cos[pos_ids]` reads past the table: an `IndexError` on CPU, a device-side assert on GPU.

Fix (suggested in review): size the table from `text_config.max_position_embeddings`. For GLM-5.3-Flash that is 1,048,576 rows, about 64 MiB in bf16 per GPU.

For every grid that fit the old table, the vision tower's output is bit-identical to before.

Neither bug depends on quantization or KV-cache dtype: the tower is built with `quant_config=None` and uses no KV cache, and the `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` vision weights are BF16, as in `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`.

**Not a duplicate:** On 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-02 I searched open vllm-project/vllm PRs for `glm5next`, `rot_pos_emb`, `GLM-5.3-Flash image`, `glm5next sync` and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK vision`, and issues for GLM-5.3-Flash image crashes. Nothing addresses either bug. The two closest PRs have since merged, and both bugs are still on `main`:
- vllm-project/vllm#57387 replaced the vendored processor with the transformers one. Slim images still reach the tower; the example above was re-run through it.
- vllm-project/vllm#55389 added input normalization ahead of the patch embedding.

**AI assistance:** The investigation, code change, tests and this description were produced with Claude Code. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer.

## Test Plan

- `tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_rotary.py` (rewritten). The existing `pytest -v -s models/glm5next` Buildkite step already runs this directory.
  - `test_rot_pos_emb_covers_grid_longer_than_8192`: builds the real vision tower (no transformer blocks) and checks `rot_pos_emb` on a `[1, 2, 8194]` grid against a float64 reference.
  - `test_image_forward_has_no_implicit_gpu_sync` (CUDA only): runs the eager forward of an image under the GPU sync check in `error` mode, set up the same way as `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py`.
  ```bash
  python -m pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_rotary.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py -v
  ```
- Old vs. new: ran `main`'s `multimodal.py` and this one side by side on CPU with the same weights and inputs.
- Lint:
  ```bash
  pre-commit run --files vllm/models/glm5next/common/multimodal.py tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_rotary.py
  pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/models/glm5next/common/multimodal.py tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_rotary.py
  ```

## Test Result

- **Overflow test on `main`:** `IndexError: index 8192 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 8192`. **With this PR:** passes; 30 of 30 consecutive runs on the previous revision, whose `rot_pos_emb` is byte-identical to this one.
- **Suites (CPU):** 10 passed, 1 skipped (the CUDA-only test).
- **Old vs. new:** forward output and rotary tables bit-identical for `[1, 78, 138]` (a 1920×1080 image), a mixed batch including a two-frame item, and the boundary `[1, 2, 8192]`. The tower was built without transformer blocks, which need Triton; the GPU image request below covers them.
- **Lint:** all pre-commit hooks and the CI mypy 3.12 hook pass.
- **GPU:** not run yet; no GPU was available where this was developed. Still to run: `test_image_forward_has_no_implicit_gpu_sync`, and an image request to GLM-5.3-Flash served with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

**Model evaluation:** Not run. Output for every input that worked before is bit-identical; only inputs that previously crashed the engine take a new path.

title: [Docs] Fix stale W4A16 NVFP4 default kernel in ModelOpt docs
author: WarrierRajeev
body:
## Purpose

The ModelOpt docs say that for `W4A16_NVFP4` checkpoints, `auto` "currently selects Marlin". That isn't what the code does. #53014 added this sentence together with the logic that makes `auto` pick the FlashInfer CuTe-DSL kernel on SM100/SM103, which the `v0.30.0` release notes list under "New defaults".

ModelOpt W4A16 layers go through `select_linear_kernel` → `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel(use_a16=True)`:

```python
elif linear_backend == "auto" and use_a16:
    ...
    # Weight-only: prefer FlashInfer CuTe-DSL W4A16 on SM100/103,

    cutedsl_ok, _ = FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4W4A16LinearKernel.is_supported(
```

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Fix inaccurate proportional store dropping
author: thuongvu
body:
## Purpose

`ThrottledDropPolicy` calculates what fraction of store attempts should be dropped based on pressure. This PR fixes how it applies that fraction.

For a calculated drop rate of 75%, the expected result over 20 store attempts is 15 drops and 5 allowed stores.

- Before: 10 dropped, 10 allowed. Only 50% are dropped.
- After: 15 dropped, 5 allowed. The calculated 75% rate is honored.

The old implementation rounds the rate into a "drop every N attempts" interval, which cannot represent rates such as 75%. The replacement carries fractional drops between decisions, keeping the cumulative drop count within one store of the calculated target.

This corrects application of the existing rate; it does not change how pressure determines that rate. Pressure detection and cooldown behavior are unchanged. These decisions control optional writes to secondary cache tiers, not inference-request admission.

Related to #50045. Duplicate-work checks found no open PR implementing this arithmetic correction. #51576 adds admission-policy infrastructure without changing this calculation; #51240 tracks the broader admission/backpressure work.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement and test this change.

## Test Plan

Tests cover steady and changing drop rates, preservation of fractional state, reset behavior, and manager submissions, drop metrics, and pin release.

Run from the repository root with the test environment at `.venv`:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=. \

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/backpressure.py \

```

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Keep the prompt-end prefill checkpoint under sparse retention
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

Mamba prefix caching in align mode with internal prefill checkpoints and sparse retention (`retention_interval == 0`) drops the **prompt-end** checkpoint for most prompts. As a result, the next request that extends the prompt misses the entire prefix.

`MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` (added in #56794) treats a checkpoint as request-local and evicts it when `num_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens`. That is right for mid-prompt chunks. But the hybrid coordinator caches the final chunk only up to its last full block (`_align_cacheable`), so whenever the prompt length is not a multiple of the Mamba block size, the condition also holds on the final chunk. The prompt's own reusable checkpoint is then evicted.

Only a later request that happens to stop a chunk at the shared-prefix junction re-materializes the state. So the first follow-up after every new prompt misses, and in a multi-turn session, where each turn extends a prompt that was prefilled exactly once, **every turn misses**.

The existing test (`test_internal_checkpoint_publication_respects_retention`) does not catch this: it uses `hash_block_size < mamba_block_size`, where the final chunk is cached at full prompt length.

### Fix

Keep the checkpoint when its position is the prompt's own final checkpoint position (`get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(num_prompt_tokens, ...)`). Mid-prompt checkpoints are still evicted as before.

## Test Plan

- New test `test_prompt_end_checkpoint_survives_sparse_retention_with_coarse_hash`:
  - `hash_block_size == mamba_block_size`, a non-aligned 240-token prompt, two chunks;
  - checks that the prompt-end checkpoint is published and that a request extending the prompt hits 224 tokens;
  - fails on main, passes with this change.
- `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache`, `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`.
- End to end on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA with prefill checkpoints, B300), sending a prefix-only prompt, then 3 requests extending it:

| | TP2: hit on the 1st / 2nd follow-up | TP1 ranks (DEP4): hit on the 1st / 2nd follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0 / 193,280 | 0 / 192,000 |
| this PR | 193,280 / 193,280 | 192,000 / 192,000 |

## Test Result

- Unit tests on this branch: 317 passed across the files above, including the new test.
- `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` could not run in this environment: engine init fails in the Qwen3.5 GDN path with an unrelated `chunk_gated_delta_rule(... backend=...)` TypeError from the local library versions.
- Multi-session P/D serving (GLM-5.3-Flash, DEP4 prefill + DEP4 decode), prefill-side prefix hit rate:
  - main: 87.9%, i.e. one full miss per session;
  - this PR: 96.97%, the block-granularity ceiling.
  - TTFT p90 dropped from 16.7 s to 0.76 s.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; every line was reviewed and the tests above were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Honor `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` for the KDA recurrent state
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Purpose

`Glm5NextLinearAttention.get_state_dtype()` and `Glm5NextForCausalLM.get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config()` call `MambaStateDtypeCalculator.kda_state_dtype()` without the SSM cache dtype. As a result, the KDA recurrent state is always float32, and `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16` is **silently ignored** for GLM-5.3-Flash. Kimi-K3's KDA already passes it through.

This PR passes `cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` in both places. `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` delegates to the causal-LM class, so it is fixed too.

Why it matters: with bfloat16 the recurrent state page halves. Mamba align-mode prefix caching sizes the attention block from that page, so at TP2 the block shrinks from 2304 to 1280 tokens. With speculative decoding, each running request holds `2 + num_speculative_tokens` state blocks per group, so on decode instances this state is what bounds concurrency.

## Test Plan

- New test `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_state_dtype.py`:
  - `auto` / `float32` / `bfloat16` must reach both the model-level and the layer-level recurrent-state dtype;
  - the bf16 case fails on main.
- Existing tests: `tests/models/glm5next`.
- End to end: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP2, B300, with `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16`:
  - the KV-cache spec now reports the bf16 state page;
  - teacher-forced NLL on long-context prompts is unchanged within run-to-run noise vs the float32 state.

## Test Result

- `tests/models/glm5next`: 14 passed.
- With bf16 state, a spec-decoding decode instance (K=4, P/D serving) fits ~1.25× more concurrent requests before running out of state blocks (≈64 → 80+).

AI assistance (Claude) was used; every line was reviewed and the tests above were run by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Make DeepSeek V4 FP8 sparse decode graph-capturable
author: yongqiw-i
body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4-Flash failing to start on XPU with graph capture enabled:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'level_zero backend failed with error: 44 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE)'
```

**Root cause:** `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8` used `.item()` host syncs, data-dependent tensor shapes, and a per-token Python loop. Level Zero graph capture doesn't support any of these.

**Changes:** Rewrite `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8` to use static shapes and vectorized index construction without host syncs, making it graph-capture safe to fix this bug.


## Test Plan

Start a DeepSeek-V4-Flash server on XPU with graph capture. The test cmds are as follows:

```
# EP4xDP2
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 --enable-expert-parallel  --data-parallel-size 2     -tp=4  
# TP4xPP2
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 -pp 2     -tp=4
# TP8
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
```

title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Exclude synchronous READ destinations from KV zeroing
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Synchronous MoRIIO RDMA READs can race GPU zeroing of recycled attention pages in hybrid models. Exclude this step's aligned READ destinations in `build_connector_meta()` and explicitly document the limited zeroing-list exception to that hook's read-only contract.

This fix was extracted from #58968. It complements #59504's asynchronous-load handling; neither contains this synchronous MoRIIO protection.

## Claims

- Only fully overwritten hybrid READ attention destinations skip zeroing. Local compute tails, recurrent-state/scratch pages, other requests' pages and later reuse retain zeroing.
- Check READ mode, hybrid state and a nonempty zeroing list once, outside the request loop. No new synchronization or metadata format.
- The base hook permits removal only from `new_block_ids_to_zero`, with completion-before-use and fail-on-load-error obligations. Every other output field remains read-only; scheduler/cache-manager/model-runner/MultiConnector runtime code is unchanged.
- Reuse `test_update_state_drops_decode_recompute_tail_block` and its helpers. Remove the duplicate test from `test_moriio_tp_ack.py` and the obsolete ROCm/MoRI skip around the CPU scheduler suite.

## Validation

**Review revision `a1aef7fe3`:** 16 parameterized boundary cases pass, including no external attention hit, attention-only loads, empty zeroing lists, local tails, other output fields and next-step reuse. The same cases pass against the previous PR method; substituting the unmodified main method produces the expected **2 failed / 14 passed**. Connector regressions: **216 passed / 4 deselected**. Core regression selection: **47 passed / 369 deselected**. Selections overlap. Changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy pass. Four local checks using the real MultiConnector allocation/metadata methods also pass, covering MoRIIO in either position and selected/unselected ownership.

**Completed model evaluation:** [run 37203257111](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/37203257111), integration `34735d677`, achieved **1268/1319 (96.1334%)** for both flexible extract and strict match. This evaluated the previous connector-local implementation (`08469e5c9`) before this minor refactor and documentation update, plus the K3 MLA grouping, atomic TCP-port allocation and discovery-heartbeat prerequisites. It is not a new model run of `a1aef7fe3`.

Configuration: Kimi-K3 + natural DSpark3, P8/D8, TP8/DCP8, eager, MoRI RDMA READ, no LMCache; full GSM8K, five-shot, C64, 4096 generated tokens, no limit. P/D each completed 1319 HTTP 200 requests without evaluator retries; external KV use was confirmed. Natural draft acceptance was **96858/126675 (76.4618%)**, with all three positions positive.

Both workload ranks returned 0, phase tokens matched, both cleanup queries returned 0 and container lists were empty. Slurm nevertheless records **FAILED/1:0**, while the workload records **COMPLETED/0**. Results were timestamped 13:46:18 UTC; prefill shutdown began at 13:46:22 and its output-handler `EngineDeadError` occurred at 13:46:34 during teardown. This discrepancy is retained, not counted as clean scheduler shutdown.

Historical evidence from before the allocation rebase and connector-local revision:

| Version | GSM8K Accuracy — Flexible Extract | GSM8K Accuracy — Strict Match |
|---|---:|---:|
| Main without #59164 | 265/1319 — **20.0910%** | 285/1319 — **21.6073%** |
| with #59164 | 1268/1319 — **96.1334%** | 1268/1319 — **96.1334%** |


<details>
<summary>CPU reproduction commands</summary>

From the candidate checkout with a prepared test virtualenv:

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  -k 'not multi_example_connector_consistency and not fewer_blocks_with_hma and not actual_lmcache and not multi_connector_handle_preemptions_integration and not multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'kv_connector or sync_kv_load or invalid_blocks or prefix_replay or zeroing or external'
```

Model validation ran outside upstream CI on the two-node ROCm runner. The run's matrix artifact records the pinned source and full serving configuration. The boundary test is now collected on CPU without pretending ROCm or MoRI is available.

</details>

## Details

```text
scheduler drains allocation zeroing IDs into a fresh output
  -> connector builds metadata and subtracts full READ destinations
  -> worker zeroes remaining pages and issues READs
  -> existing load barriers wait before the corresponding KV/state is used
```

Hybrid READ metadata already puts the aligned attention group first and excludes local compute tails. The output is built before the metadata hook and dispatched after it; no other connector currently consumes `new_block_ids_to_zero`. MultiConnector passes the same output to its children and gives external tokens only to the selected child. An unselected MoRIIO child has no attention READ destinations to exclude. The exclusion set is local to this call, so later allocations are unaffected.

The interface documentation change is deliberate: the prior unconditional read-only sentence conflicted with this implementation. The exception allows removal of fully overwritten attention blocks only, with load completion before use and step failure on error. Existing hybrid load barriers/failure handling satisfy those obligations. It does not permit changing scheduling counts, block assignments or other fields, or adding pages to the zeroing list.

This change is reversible and its runtime scope remains MoRIIO hybrid READ metadata. READ source ownership and FULL pre-forward context remain separate work.

``` python

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Concurrent traffic driver to force adaptive draft-budget trimming."""
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

PORT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "8002"
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 16
MAXTOK = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 8

URL = f"http://localhost:{PORT}/v1/completions"
PROMPTS = [
    "Explain the theory of relativity in simple terms.",
    "Write a poem about a rainy day in the city.",
    "Summarize the history of the Roman Empire.",
    "Describe how a neural network learns.",
    "List five facts about the human brain.",
    "Tell a short story about a lost dog.",
    "Explain photosynthesis to a child.",
    "What are the causes of climate change?",
    "Describe the water cycle step by step.",
    "Write about the importance of sleep.",
    "Explain how the internet works.",
    "Give a recipe for chocolate chip cookies.",
    "Describe the life cycle of a butterfly.",
    "Explain the stock market in simple words.",
    "Write about the benefits of exercise.",
    "Describe the process of making coffee.",
]


def one(i):
    body = json.dumps({
        "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
        "prompt": PROMPTS[i % len(PROMPTS)],
        "max_tokens": MAXTOK,
        "temperature": 0.7,
        "seed": i,
    }).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
            d = json.load(r)
        return i, d.get("usage", {}).get("completion_tokens"), time.time() - t0
    except Exception as e:
        return i, f"ERR {type(e).__name__}: {e}", time.time() - t0


with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N) as ex:
    for i, ntok, dt in ex.map(one, range(N)):
        print(f"req {i}: tokens={ntok} in {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
print("DONE")
```

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Ignore reused prompt token ids for media in /v1/responses
author: shijie-lyu
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #55771, suggested by @hickeyma in its review. On non-Harmony `/v1/responses`, `kv_transfer_params["prompt_token_ids"]` is used even when the input has an image, so the image is silently dropped. #55771 fixed this for `/v1/chat/completions` in a request validator; Responses reaches the same reuse path through `OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat` without that check. The bug predates #55771. I found no open PR for it.

Changes:

- `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py`: the non-text part scan from the chat validator becomes `has_non_text_content(messages)`, next to `TEXT_PART_TYPES`.
- `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py`: `_reused_prompt_token_ids` also takes the messages and ignores the ids when they have non-text content, the same way it already does for `echo`. `preprocess_chat` passes its messages, so this covers every `render_responses` caller (`/v1/responses` and `/v1/responses/render`), including images in `previous_response_id` history and inside `function_call_output`.
- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py`: the chat validator calls the shared helper; its behaviour is unchanged. Chat keeps the check at validation time because validated chat content can be a one-shot iterator.

Behaviour on non-Harmony `/v1/responses` with forwarded ids:

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| text only | ids used as sent | unchanged |
| an image (in a message, a `function_call_output`, or history) | ids used, image dropped | ids ignored and input rendered: same result as without the ids |
| an image plus malformed ids such as `[1.5]` | 400 | ids ignored and input rendered, as on chat since #55771 |
| an image on a text-only model | ids used, image dropped | the same render-time 400 as without the ids, raised inside `_with_kv_transfer_rejection_cleanup`, so the connector is notified |

`/v1/responses/render` now also returns the image features for such requests.

Not changed: the Harmony `/v1/responses` path does not read the alias (a known limit from #55771), and the docs still describe reuse for `/v1/chat/completions` only. Whether Responses reuse should be documented as supported is a maintainer call; I'm happy to add a docs line in a follow-up.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd tests
pytest -v entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py -k kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids
pytest -v entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids
pytest -v entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py -k kv_transfer
pytest -q entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py entrypoints/cohere/ \
  entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_echo.py
```

The new tests run the real `render_responses` and `preprocess_chat` with only the inner `render_chat_async` mocked.

## Test Result

1x NVIDIA L4, torch 2.13.0+cu132, this diff on main c6843d397c.

- New tests: 6 passed. On main, the 5 image cases fail and the text-only case passes. They also fail with only the `preprocess_chat` call site reverted.
- Existing reuse tests: chat 20 passed, batch 1 passed.
- Responses, Anthropic, Cohere, render and echo suites: 391 passed, 1 xfailed.
- `pre-commit` ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, check-spdx-header and `mypy-3.10`: passed.

Live server, main vs this PR, `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, temperature 0. The image is a red square with the word "CAT". The forwarded ids are the tokenized text-only prompt, which shows on main whether the image reaches the engine.

| `/v1/responses` request | main | PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| image, no ids | 92 input tokens, "Red image, word CAT." | same |
| image + ids | 26 input tokens, "Blue sky, green grass." | 92 input tokens, "Red image, word CAT." |
| text + ids | 26 input tokens (ids reused) | same |

title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix mamba prefill checkpoint block reservation and prompt-end eviction in align mode
author: kliuae
body:
## Purpose
Enabling Mamba prefill checkpoint in the `align` mamba cache mode allows for the elimination of a second forward pass in prefill when the chunked context lengths are not multiples of the block size. In enabling prefill checkpointing for Kimi-K3 on ROCm (#58344), two issues were found where the scheduler and kv cache manager disagree on the block boundaries, causing wasted allocation and dropped cache that hurt prefix cache hits. This PR extracts the fixes to the core parts that are hardware independent out from the ROCm checkpoint enablement and addresses the following:

### 1. Surplus block reservation
The scheduler determines checkpoint positions from the prefill_end token
```
vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py's _mamba_block_aligned_split
prefill_end = max(request.num_prompt_tokens, request.num_tokens - 1)
...
checkpoint_position = get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(
    prefill_end, self.hash_block_size, drop_eagle_block=self.use_eagle_block_drop,
)
...
use_internal_checkpoint = (...
    and is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid(..., checkpoint_position=checkpoint_position, ...)
)
```
whereas the `MambaManager` uses a prefill chunk's end token `num_tokens`.
```
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's MambaManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate()
checkpoint_position = get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(
    num_tokens, self.block_pool.hash_block_size, self.drop_eagle_checkpoint_block,
)
...
# member methods that call
is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid(..., checkpoint_position=checkpoint_position, ...)
...
```
As the `num_tokens`-derived `checkpoint_position` is always below the end of the prefill chunk, the `query_start < checkpoint_position < query_end` condition in `is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid` is always True for MambaManager, and it allocates an additional block even for chunks that are in the middle of the requests. This makes MambaManager allocate blocks for mid-request chunks that the scheduler never plans as the scheduler only plans for blocks at the prompt-end chunks. These mid-request blocks are immediately discarded as transients, but they still consume and evict physical blocks that have held real prefix. Measured with AgentX workload at concurrency 64, these surplus block reservation can drop cache hit rate from 89% -> 49%.

This PR addresses this by using the same `prefill_end` as the scheduler to evaluate `checkpoint_position` in `MambaManager`, so that `query_start < checkpoint_position < query_end` is True only for the prompt-end chunk and checkpoint blocks are only allocated there where they're only required. This is only changed under `retention_interval == 0` where the surplus checkpoint blocks are truly redundant.

### 2. Dropped prompt-end checkpoint states (Superseded, fixed by #59146)
MambaManager's `_cache_partial_tail_block` decides whether a checkpoint block is mid-request by
```
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block
if (
    retention_interval == 0
    and **num_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens**
    and checkpoint_position != request.shared_prefix_boundary
):
    self.block_pool._maybe_evict_cached_block(checkpoint_block)
    return None
```
where `num_tokens` is rounded down to block size by the HybridKVCacheCoordinator
```
def _align_cacheable(self, num_tokens: int) -> int:
    if self.enable_partial_hash_hits:
        return num_tokens
    return round_down(num_tokens, self.scheduler_block_size)

def cache_blocks(self, request, num_computed_tokens):
    cached_num_computed_tokens = self._align_cacheable(num_computed_tokens)
    ...
```

This makes last chunk of a non-multiple-of-block-size prompt rounded down to below the prompt length, and, under retention_interval=0, its hash is then removed on the same step the kernel writes it. The next conversation turn then cannot find the checkpoint states at the prompt-end boundary, and the reusable prefix becomes the last boundary or to zero, causing prefix to be recomputed.

This PR addresses this issue by adding `_is_reachable_checkpoint` where it decides if a checkpoint belongs to a prompt-end chunk using checkpoint position instead of the rounded-down count.

## Test Plan

New unit tests are added for core partial prefix cache hits:

- `test_intermediate_chunk_checkpoint_reserved_only_under_dense_retention`: prefills a prompt in two chunks and checks that the mid-prompt chunk reserves a checkpoint block only under dense retention while the prompt-end chunk reserves one either way. Fails on main under retention_interval=0.
- `test_prompt_end_checkpoint_survives_block_aligned_cache_count`: prefills a prompt whose length is not a multiple of the block size at the default match unit and checks that the prompt-end checkpoint stays in the prefix cache and that a replay of the same prompt resumes from it. Fails on main for the unaligned lengths.

## Test Result

The added unit tests pass where they fail on main branch.

The performance impact of the two issues were measured together with the ROCm Kimi-K3 mamba checkpoint enablement #58344 on MI355X. In the following benchmarks and evaluations, #58344 only adds the enablement of prefix checkpoint for Kimi-K3 on ROCm, and the pre- and post-fixes for KV cache manager and scheduler are the distinction between the main branch and this PR.

AgentX benchmark runs were performed to reflect agentic workloads with prefix caching, and different conditions were set so that the two issues could surface individually.

The issue 1 "Surplus block reservation"'s cost surfaces under memory pressure when physical blocks holding real prefix caches get evicted to make space for mid-request transient blocks that get discarded immediately. For this, the concurrency=64 AgentX benchmark setting was used.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply output_config and thinking in Anthropic count_tokens
author: ejrtks1020
body:
## Purpose

`/v1/messages/count_tokens` ignores `output_config.effort` and `thinking`, so the returned `input_tokens` can differ from the prompt that `/v1/messages` actually renders for the same request. Templates that change with `reasoning_effort` (e.g. the thinking prefix toggled by `enable_thinking`, or Harmony's effort line) make the count wrong for clients like Claude Code that budget context with `count_tokens`.

Root cause:

- `AnthropicCountTokensRequest` does not declare `output_config` or `thinking`, so pydantic silently drops them. Both fields are part of Anthropic's `messages.count_tokens` spec.
- `_handle_output_config` and `_handle_thinking` return early for `AnthropicCountTokensRequest`.

Changes:

- Add `output_config` and `thinking` to `AnthropicCountTokensRequest`.
- Remove the early returns so both endpoints share one conversion path.
- Resolve `disabled_thinking_effort` in `count_tokens()` the same way `create_messages()` does, so `thinking.type=disabled` maps to the same effort on both endpoints.

`output_config.format` is now also applied to the converted request. It does not change the rendered prompt; it only keeps the two conversions identical.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched issues/PRs for `count_tokens`, `output_config`, `_handle_output_config` and `anthropic effort`. None fix this:

- #42396 added `_handle_output_config` and excluded count_tokens from the start.
- #58613 (thinking config) explicitly left count_tokens out of scope.
- #58647 (RFC, `/v1/messages` enhancements) does not mention count_tokens.
- #58753 touches the count_tokens path for inline-system detection, unrelated to effort/thinking.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to draft this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

Added `TestThinkingConfig::test_count_tokens_matches_messages` in `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`. For effort, thinking disabled and thinking enabled, it checks that a count_tokens request converts to the same `reasoning_effort` and `thinking_token_budget` as the equivalent messages request.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \
       tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_protocol_exports.py -v
```

E2E: serve `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, send the same request with `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` to both endpoints, and compare `input_tokens` from count_tokens with `usage.input_tokens` from `/v1/messages`.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8000
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages/count_tokens -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}' | jq .input_tokens
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","max_tokens":1,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}' | jq .usage.input_tokens
```

## Test Result

- New test: 3 failed before the fix, 3 passed after.
- `test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` + `test_protocol_exports.py`: 89 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: pass.

E2E (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`):

| | count_tokens `input_tokens` | `/v1/messages` `usage.input_tokens` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 9 | 13 |
| this PR | 13 | 13 |

On main, count_tokens drops `thinking`, so it renders the prompt without the empty `<think></think>` block that `enable_thinking=False` adds and undercounts by 4 tokens. With this PR both endpoints agree.

Model evaluation: not applicable. Only the token count reported by count_tokens changes; generation requests are unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Skip SWA bounded replay for KV loads that carry the window
author: ivanium
body:
Also credit to @wangyicong52 who originally reported the issue and helped test the PR.

## Purpose

SWA bounded replay (#56227) replays the last window of every prefix hit, including KV loaded by P/D connectors, which transfer the request's own sliding-window KV. P/D decode on DeepSeek-V4.1 therefore recomputed the last 128 prompt tokens of every request. The whole-block rounding that replay applies to external hits also shrinks decode's allocation below what prefill exports, so NIXL's end-aligned pairing puts prefill block k + 1 into decode block k for the MLA groups whenever N % 128 != 0 (found with a CPU probe of the real scheduler and NIXL code).

## Changes

- The scheduler takes a load that restores every replayed group (`get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, added by #59504) as is: no replay, no whole-block rounding, and no dropping of hits no longer than the window. Async loads record the decision at admission and apply it when the KV arrives; failed loads and store / offloading loads still replay.
- Without the replay, decode relies on the transferred window as laid out, so NIXL and Mooncake now back off the last prompt token for models with bounded replay, as they already do for Mamba: prefill stops at N - 1, decode loads N - 1 tokens and computes the last one. Loading all N tokens and rewinding one after laying the window out for N dropped the block holding position N - W when N % block_size == block_size - 1, and the recomputed token attended to the null block, which DeepSeek-V4.1 does not keep zero.

- The prompt cut keeps two prompt-indexed features working (they were already broken for Mamba P/D): a request with prompt logprobs (e.g. completions with echo and logprobs) is not cut, since it skips reading the prefix cache and the decoder never loads its KV; before, the prefiller returned prompt logprobs for one token fewer than the prompt and the frontend failed. The routed-experts (R3) start is clamped to the prompt length; a start equal to the original length lay past the cut prompt and made the scheduler assert.

This PR stands alone. #59330 is the general fix: it applies the backoff to every model (a sliding window has the same rewind problem everywhere, it is only masked by a zero null block) and handles the prompt shapes that only Mamba used to reach (mixed token-id / embeddings prompts, a cut inside a multimodal item, push and Mooncake zero-token loads). DeepSeek-V4.1 is text-only and needs none of those.

## Not a duplicate

#59142 (draft, opt-in, Mooncake only) moves replay to prefill and certifies checkpoints; this PR drops the replay of KV that P/D already transfers, for any connector that declares it, with no new config. #58504 keeps partial external hits exact by retaining the boundary block; loads carrying the window skip the rounding here.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_nixl_connector_hma,test_nixl_connector,test_nixl_push_connector,test_mooncake_connector,test_mooncake_connector_hma,test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba,test_multi_connector,test_remote_prefill_lifecycle,test_invalid_blocks_correctness,test_kv_load_failure_recovery}.py`: `test_kv_load_carrying_window_does_not_replay` (sync/async, window-long and unaligned hits), the NIXL backoff tests extended to bounded replay and prompt-logprob requests, and the aux output connector test extended to a start past the cut prompt.
- `pre-commit`
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (NIXL, 1P1D TP4 + TP4), two-pass GSM8K 5-shot, concurrency 512; pass 2 re-sends the prompts so decode gets local prefix hits.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 754 passed.
- GSM8K flexible-extract. "N%32==31" counts pass-2 errors on prompts with N % 32 == 31 (the rewind case); "t < 16" pass-2 errors elsewhere with (N - 1) % 128 < 16, where the kept window lies almost entirely below a decode-side prefix hit (the zeroing race #59504 fixed). Main and the earlier rows were run on main 4e0a414c44, this PR on main 84bcbc6264:

| Build | Pass 1 | Pass 2 | N%32==31 | t < 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9174 / 0.9249 | 0.9219 / 0.9189 | 5 / 6 | 18 / 15 |
| replay skip only, without the backoff or #59504 | 0.9181 | 0.9052 | 13 | 23 |
| this PR | 0.9212 | 0.9227 | 5 | 13 |

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Skip engine-derived metrics under `--disable-log-stats`
author: BugenZhao
body:
## Purpose

With `--disable-log-stats`, the engine runs with `log_stats=False`: `Scheduler.make_stats()` returns `None` and request lifecycle events (`QUEUED` / `SCHEDULED` / `PREEMPTED`) are not recorded. The Python frontend exports no `vllm:*` engine or request metrics in this mode. The Rust frontend kept exporting metrics derived from that missing data, with misleading values:

- Scheduler gauges (`vllm:num_requests_running`, `vllm:num_requests_waiting`, `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc`, prefix cache, spec decode, ...) are created eagerly per engine and stay at `0` forever. Consumers such as autoscalers or an inference-gateway endpoint picker would see every replica as idle.
- `vllm:request_queue_time_seconds`, `vllm:request_prefill_time_seconds`, and `vllm:request_inference_time_seconds` observe `0` for every request, and the preemption counters stay at `0`.
- `vllm:lora_requests_info` never sees `SCHEDULED` events, so every in-flight adapter is reported as waiting.

This PR adds `EngineCoreClientConfig::engine_stats_enabled` (set from `!disable_log_stats` by the server) and skips those metrics when engines do not record stats:

- The scheduler-stats recorder and the LoRA info exporter are only created when engine stats are enabled. Routing still consumes scheduler stats whenever they arrive.
- The event-derived request metrics are grouped into `EventMetricHandles`, resolved only when engine stats are enabled.
- Metrics the frontend observes itself (TTFT, ITL, E2E latency, decode time, TPOT, token counters including cached prompt tokens, `request_success`) are still exported, since `prefill_stats` and output timestamps do not depend on `log_stats`.

The `--disable-log-stats` help text now also mentions the skipped metrics.

Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses `--disable-log-stats` metric behavior in the Rust frontend (searched open PRs for `disable-log-stats rust` and `log stats metrics Rust Frontend`).

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py --no-fail-fast
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

`generate_without_engine_stats_exports_only_frontend_observed_metrics` (`llm/tests/generate.rs`) drives a LoRA request through a mock engine that behaves like one started with `--disable-log-stats` (no events, no scheduler stats). It asserts that the adapter never appears in `/metrics` while the request is in flight, that frontend-observed metrics are exported, and that scheduler gauges and event-derived request metrics are absent. The existing metrics test additionally asserts `vllm:request_queue_time_seconds` on the stats-enabled path.

## Test Result

- Workspace nextest: 1891 passed, 13 skipped. `vllm-tool-parser-py` was excluded because its test binary cannot load `libpython3.14.so` in the local environment.
- clippy and fmt: clean.
- Reverting each gate separately (scheduler recorder, LoRA info, event-derived request metrics) makes the new test fail.
- Not yet validated end to end against a real engine with `--disable-log-stats`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
