title: [Bugfix] Preserve FP8 indexer WK pairs across load_weights calls
author: pllopis
body:
## Purpose

**In short**: Bugfix for GLM-5.3 sometimes starting with degraded performance (thinking loops) due to dropped weights when using runai_streamer loader due to a "race" (non-deterministic I/O completion order).

**Details**:
GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V3.2 (`deepseek_v32`) checkpoints store the indexer `wk` projection in FP8 as two tensors: values and a scale factor. The loader parks the first half in a dict and dequantizes once the second half arrives, but that dict was created fresh on every `load_weights()` call, so the two halves had to arrive within the same call.
 
With runai_streamer as loader, tensors arrive in IO-completion order (this is partly the cause for the non-deterministic "race"), and `AutoWeightsLoader` splits the weight stream into multiple `load_weights()` calls at every `model` <-> `lm_head` prefix transition. When the split between calls happens to fall between the two halves of a pair, both are silently dropped: the WK half of the fused `wk_weights_proj` parameter keeps its initialization, one layer's sparse-attention indexer runs on garbage, and every load-completeness check still passes. In production this shows up as a per-launch coin flip where short answers look fine but long reasoning degenerates into thinking loops, rendering the performance almost useless.

Fix: keep the pending dict on the model instance instead of a local variable (similar fix as #46168 for the generic `deepseek_v2` path, applied to the remaining copies: `deepseek_v32` nvidia/amd model+mtp, and `deepseek_mtp`).

Note that this is NOT a duplicate of #56584, which fixes the `glm5next` (GLM-5.3-Flash) copy of the same bug. The two PRs touch disjoint files and both are needed.

## Test Plan

```bash
     .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_deepseek_v32_weight_loading.py -v
```

That test is CPU-only, no GPU and no checkpoint needed.

## Test Result

* Unpatched main: 13 failed (the WK half of the fused parameter stays all-zero, which is the bug addressed in this PR)
* With this PR: 13 passed.

Also verified end-to-end on a real GLM-5.3 deployment (TP=8, B200, --load-format runai_streamer). In addition to checking by hand with complex prompts that force the model to do multi-thinking steps and therefore validating that the thinking loops were gone, the following checks were done (with help of AI):
* Dumped the live in-VRAM wk_weights_proj tensors from all 8 TP workers and compared them bitwise against values dequantized from the on-disk checkpoint: 168/168 identical.
* 10 greedy prompts (math / code / instructions): content and reasoning byte-identical to a known-good instance of the same weights, so a healthy load is provably unchanged and accuracy benchmarks are unaffected.

No documentation update is needed.
AI assistance was used to help investigate, implement, and test this change.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Resolve MTP verification rows with a union residency kernel
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Resolve all of a request's MTP verification rows with one union residency kernel, on every sparse MLA backend, and drop the fragile routing that worked around the old kernel.

The old `hisparse_resolve_residency_kernel` ran one block per row, but `device_global_indices` and the LRU are per request, so two rows of one request in one launch could claim the same free slot and read each other's KV. Callers avoided that by resolving verification one step per launch (FlashMLA, FlashInfer TRTLLM) or by treating it as prefill (backends without `hisparse_supports_multi_token_decode`). On FlashAttn sparse MLA a FULL CUDA graph froze that prefill path's residency check at capture, so replays with spilled pages still hit the race. Found via #59036's CI failure (`test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore`).

## Changes

- **Union kernel.** Each request's first-row block resolves all its rows: one hash-table union of host misses, one LRU walk, eviction slots in deterministic (row, top-k) order, one LRU rewrite. Each host row is copied once per request; a reused slot counts as a hit. The table is sized from `max_decode_query_len * index_topk` (~90 KB for GLM-5.3 + MTP3, MTP ≤ 9 at `index_topk=2048`), checked at startup; a union past that bound traps.
- **One routing path.** Verification resolves in one `swap_in` per layer, and `hisparse_supports_multi_token_decode` is removed, so every backend keeps verification as decode. Request ids (with CUDA-graph padding rows masked) live in a group-owned buffer, since the resolver reads them on the copy stream.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_speculative_rows_resolve_host_misses_consistently` (disjoint, overlapping, and multi-pass rows) plus unit tests for hit counting, union-bound sizing, the startup check, spec-as-decode, and padding/request-id handling.
- HiSparse kernel, sparse MLA backend, and e2e tests; #59036 applied on top.
- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 + MTP3 on B200 (FlashInfer TRTLLM, HiSparse under spill pressure), and a layer-level benchmark on H100.

## Test Result

- Race test fails 30/30 on main's kernel and passes with this PR; HiSparse tests pass (H100, H200, B200); `test_hisparse.py` passes, also with #59036.
- GLM-5.3 B200: MTP acceptance in line with main (1.06–1.32 vs 1.19 per window on random prompts); a shrunk GLM-5.3 config matches main's tokens and drafts exactly under FULL graphs.

Decode residency per layer, µs (H100, MTP3, `index_topk=2048`, main → this PR). **Bold** = faster by >5%.

| Mode | Regime | 1 req | 8 reqs | 32 reqs | 64 reqs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph | steady | 155 → **64** | 185 → **87** | 264 → **167** | 373 → **268** |
| | cold | 189 → **129** | 582 → **539** | 2119 → 2174 | 4213 → 4139 |

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the root cause was reproduced and validated on H200, H100, and B200.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return 400 for malformed RL dev route bodies
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Malformed request bodies on the RL dev routes surface as 500s, and one of them breaks an in-progress weight update.

- A JSON body that is not an object (`[]`, `1`, `"x"`, `null`) makes `/abort_requests`, `/init_weight_transfer_engine`, `/update_weights` and `/collective_rpc` fail in `body.get(...)` with `AttributeError`, which the generic handler turns into **500**.
- A mistyped field (`{"init_info": []}`, `{"update_info": 1}`) reaches the engine and also returns **500**. For `/update_weights` the failure **aborts the in-progress weight update session**: every later `/update_weights` fails with `start_weight_update must be called before update_weights`, so the trainer has to restart the update from `/start_weight_update`.

The Rust frontend already rejects all of these with 400 before calling the engine.

## Changes

- `/init_weight_transfer_engine` and `/update_weights` take `init_info` / `update_info` as typed embedded body fields (`Body(embed=True)`). The types are the existing `WeightTransferInitRequest` / `WeightTransferUpdatePayload` ones, and this is the same style as `/finish_weight_update`. FastAPI rejects a non-object body, a missing field, or a wrong type, and vLLM's validation handler returns 400 before the engine is called. The hand-written JSON parsing and `is None` checks go away.
- `/abort_requests` and `/collective_rpc` keep their free-form bodies, so `{}` still aborts everything and RPC args are passed through unchanged. They now return 400 when the body is not a JSON object.

## Not a duplicate

#42961 adds the same non-object guard to the shared `validate_json_request` dependency. That covers routes that use it (OpenAI endpoints, `/scale_elastic_ep`, token-in-token-out `/abort_requests`), but not the RL dev routes and `/collective_rpc` here, which don't use that dependency. It also doesn't cover the mistyped-field case that aborts a weight update session.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_dev_route_request_bodies.py
```

The test runs an in-process app with vLLM's real exception handlers:

- Non-object bodies on all four routes return 400 and never reach the engine.
- Missing or mistyped `init_info` / `update_info` return 400 and never reach the engine.
- Valid bodies (including `update_info` as a list of per-worker objects) reach the engine.

Manual check with a real `vllm serve` (IPC weight transfer): `init` → `start` → `/update_weights {"update_info": 1}` → `finish`.

## Test Result

- New tests: 28 passed. Against unpatched `main`: 21 failed, which are exactly the non-object and mistyped cases.
- Real server, patched: the bad update returns 400 and `finish` returns 200, so the session is intact. On `main` the same bad update returns 500 and later updates fail with `start_weight_update must be called before update_weights`.
- pre-commit (ruff, mypy, test tethering) clean.
- No model output path changes, so no accuracy eval.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Stop vllm-bench chat latency at the last token
author: ZhenchengLin
body:
## Purpose

Port #55508 to the Rust `vllm-bench` `openai-chat` backend.

#55508 fixed Python `vllm bench serve` so that the trailing choice-less `usage` chunk no longer advances the end of a request. The Rust port still updates `most_recent_timestamp` for every non-`[DONE]` message, and its comment still describes the old Python behavior. As a result, `latency` (E2EL) runs past the final token, `latency - ttft != sum(itl)`, and TPOT is inflated relative to ITL. This also means the Rust and Python clients disagree on the same server.

This PR moves `most_recent_timestamp = timestamp` inside the token branch, matching Python and the Rust `openai` (completions) backend, which already stops at the last token.

Found while investigating #59154. This PR does **not** explain the 3-4x gap reported there; that gap comes from temperature defaults, as analyzed in the issue thread.

## Not a duplicate

#55508 changed only the Python clients (`vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py`, `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py`); the Rust `vllm-bench` was not touched. I checked for open PRs covering the Rust side:


None of them touch `rust/src/bench/src/backends/openai_chat.rs`. The temperature-warning PR from #59154 (#59247) only touches `rust/src/bench/src/config.rs`, so there is no overlap.


title: [Bugfix] Gate Kimi-K3 KDA warmup on sys.modules to skip Kimi import for non-Kimi models
author: YueshenZ
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59250. Non-Kimi models should not import Kimi model code during kernel warmup. That import can initialize a numba cache and fail when a non-root process has no writable cache directory.

Look up the already-loaded KDA module in `sys.modules`, following the existing Kimi warmup gates. Kimi model construction imports this module before warmup, so the existing layer scan and kernel dispatch are preserved. This does not change numba caching for actual Kimi deployments.

## Validation

The CPU-only regression suite exercises the public `kimi_k3_triton_warmup()` entry point with the CUDA predicate and GPU warmup callbacks patched:

- A non-Kimi worker never attempts to import Kimi model code or warm Kimi kernels.
- A loaded module with an invalid context or no KDA layer remains a no-op.
- A matching KDA layer still dispatches both warmup callbacks with the expected arguments.

The tests use the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker because they allocate no accelerator resources. Without it, this macOS environment crashes in the repository's unrelated global accelerator teardown.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_kimi_k3_warmup_import_gate.py
SKIP=actionlint pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/warmup/kimi_k3_triton_warmup.py tests/v1/worker/test_kimi_k3_warmup_import_gate.py
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual mypy-3.12 --files vllm/model_executor/warmup/kimi_k3_triton_warmup.py tests/v1/worker/test_kimi_k3_warmup_import_gate.py
```

Local results: 4 tests passed with a normal process exit on macOS arm64, Python 3.13.15 and torch 2.14.0. Running the same non-Kimi regression with the original helper fails on the forbidden Kimi import. Linux read-only-container startup and Kimi GPU/model evaluation have not been run locally; the callback assertions cover dispatch, not GPU kernel correctness or model accuracy.

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, spelling, test tethering, SPDX/import checks and mypy (Python 3.10 and 3.12 targets). `actionlint` was skipped because its Go dependency download timed out; it has no matching files in this Python-only change.

## Duplicate-work check

Checked #59250's timeline, open PR titles, issue-reference searches and related warmup diffs. #50760 changes AttnRes warmup profile coverage, which is a different bug. Draft #54784 is related: its broader Kimi de-JITification migration removes this warmup file and its caller, so it would supersede this failure path if merged. This PR is a small fix for the unconditional import still present on current `main`, without depending on that migration. No other open PR implementing this narrow import gate was found in these checks.

The original patch used Claude Code. This follow-up review and test revision used OpenAI Codex. The validation results and limitations above describe the checks actually performed.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Forward the reasoning wiring to the engine for batch chat completions
author: apex-mochen
body:
## Purpose

`/v1/chat/completions/batch` never tells the engine how to treat reasoning:
`create_batch_chat_completion` hard-codes `reasoning_ended=None` and leaves
`reasoning_parser_kwargs` unset, while `/v1/chat/completions` computes both.

Both fields travel on the request into `EngineCoreRequest` and are consumed by
`StructuredOutputManager._get_reasoner()`, which rebuilds the request-local
reasoning parser from the forwarded `chat_template_kwargs` -- its own comment
says it does so precisely "so the structured-output gate observes the same
template kwargs used by the frontend".

Without them a template-kwarg-driven parser silently falls back to its default.
With `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3` (or `deepseek_v3`) and
`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` the single-conversation
endpoint builds an engine-side parser with thinking disabled, so
`is_reasoning_end()` answers True on the prompt and the grammar is applied from
the first token. The batch endpoint built the same parser with thinking
*enabled*, `is_reasoning_end()` answered False, and the structured-output gate
never opened: a batch request that asked for `response_format` received
unconstrained output, with no error to show for it.

This is the batch half of the wiring proposed in #42105; the batch endpoint is
still unwired on main.

## Test Plan

New regression test:
`tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py::test_batched_reasoning_wiring_matches_single_chat`

It is a differential test: both frontends are built over one and the same
model/renderer, fed the same conversation and the same `chat_template_kwargs`,
and the test asserts the two `engine_client.generate()` calls agree on
`reasoning_ended` and `reasoning_parser_kwargs`. Two guards assert the
single-conversation side is not itself `None`, so the comparison cannot pass
vacuously. A final assertion rebuilds the engine-side reasoner exactly the way
`StructuredOutputManager._get_reasoner()` does and asserts
`is_reasoning_end()` is True -- i.e. the gate actually opens.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py -k reasoning_wiring
```

Negative control: with `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/batch_serving.py`
physically restored to `main` (md5 asserted before running, not `git stash`) and
the test left in place, the test fails on
`assert batch_call.kwargs["reasoning_ended"] == single_call.kwargs["reasoning_ended"]`
(`assert None == True`), and the two non-degeneracy guards still pass.

## Test Result

Patched:

```
1 passed, 9 deselected
```

Whole file (the 5 ERRORs are the pre-existing `FileNotFoundError: 'vllm'` from
`RemoteOpenAIServer` needing the CLI on PATH; they are identical with the source
reverted, so they are not caused by this change):

```
5 passed, 5 errors
```

Negative control (source at `main`, test present):

```
E       assert None == True
1 failed, 9 deselected
```

Semantic differential in-process, comparing what `_get_reasoner()` builds:

| | engine-side parser | `is_reasoning_end(prompt)` |
|---|---|---|
| single | `KimiK3ReasoningParser`, `thinking_enabled=False` | `True` |
| batch before | `KimiK3ReasoningParser`, `thinking_enabled=True` | `False` |
| batch after | `KimiK3ReasoningParser`, `thinking_enabled=False` | `True` |

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Adopt GPU prefix copies after the hit's allocation
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fix an engine crash (`Cannot get N free blocks from the pool`) on a HiSparse host-prefix hit under GPU memory pressure. This is an alternative to #57457.

Closes #59440.

"Adopting" a GPU copy means a host-prefix hit points its page at a still-valid GPU copy of that host page (a GPU-side prefix-cache hit) instead of reading the page back from host.

A host-prefix hit re-pins free GPU copies of its pages so the prefix comes back GPU-resident. Admission counts those copies as free blocks, but adoption pinned them before the hit's own allocation (hot region and new pages), which could then run the pool dry.

#57457 fixes this by charging the pins at admission. That mixes host and GPU accounting in `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, and under pressure it defers a request that could run by reading its prefix from host, just to keep an optimization.

## Changes

HiSparse-only (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`):

- **Adopt after allocation.** `commit_computed_blocks` records the pages to adopt, and `update_residency` (in `cache_blocks`, after `allocate_new_blocks`) adopts the copies that survived. The allocation always gets what admission counted, so no admission accounting is needed. A copy the allocation reuses is dropped by its reuse watcher and never adopted.
- **Tail first.** HiSparse releases a prefix's pages tail first, matching `free_blocks`' convention, so pressure trims a prefix from its end.

Replaying #57457's scenario (a resumed 3-page host prefix hit, `free_blocks` left in the pool):

| `free_blocks` | main | #57457 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5–6 | rejected | rejected | rejected |
| 7–8 | crash | rejected | admitted, 0/3 copies |
| 9 | crash | rejected | admitted, 1/3 |
| 10 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| 11+ | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |

Near the boundary this keeps fewer copies than #57457, because blocks freed after the copies are queued behind them. #59283, stacked on this PR, is an optional core change that restores 3/3 at 10.

## Test Plan

- `test_hisparse_prefix_hit_under_pressure_adopts_surviving_copies[7, 10]`: exact adopted pages, and no block shared between adopted copies and fresh allocations. `7` fails without the adoption timing, and `10` without tail-first release.
- `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, with `CpuPlatform` selected:

```bash
python cpu_pytest.py --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

## Test Result

- Both new cases fail on main and pass with this PR.
- CPU (`CpuPlatform`): 295 passed. 8 errors are `fixture 'caplog_vllm' not found`, from running outside the top-level conftest, and are identical on main.
- H100, HiSparse unit tests across `tests/v1` (`-k hisparse`): 156 passed.
- H100, `test_prefix_caching.py` + `test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 301 passed. The 2 failures (`test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_*`) need 4 visible GPUs and fail identically on main with 1.
- H100, `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: fails with this PR alone (see the dependency note); with #59235 merged in, 2 passed in each of 2 runs.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject LoRA adapters named after a served model
author: njhill
body:
A LoRA adapter loaded (dynamically or via `--lora-modules`) under a served base model's name was registered in lora_requests, which _maybe_get_adapters consults before the base models, so the adapter silently captured every request for that model and `/v1/models` listed a duplicate id. Reject such names with a 400 in
`_check_load_lora_adapter_request`, including `load_inplace`, mirroring the Rust frontend's `LoadLoraError::BaseModelName` check. Static LoRA modules go through the same path, so `init_static_loras` now fails at startup.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Qualify Transformers backend attention layer names with the model prefix
author: Legend-2727
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59292.

`method="draft_model"` speculative decoding fails at engine start-up when both the target and the drafter run on the Transformers modeling backend. One example is OLMo-2, which has been served through `TransformersForCausalLM` since v0.26.0:

```text
ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn
```

`Base._create_attention_instances` named every attention layer `f"{i}.attn"` and ignored the `prefix` passed to `Base.__init__`. The drafter is built in the same engine with `prefix="draft_model"`, in both the V1 proposer and the model runner V2 speculator. Target and drafter therefore registered the same layer names.

This PR passes the model prefix through and names each layer `maybe_prefix(prefix, f"{attn_prefix}.{VLLM_ATTN_ATTR}")`, where `attn_prefix` is the attention module's qualified name inside the model:

- The drafter's layers now sit under `draft_model.`, so they no longer collide with the target's.
- Layer names follow the module path, which is how native models already name their attention layers. This also changes the names of a model built with an empty prefix, from `0.attn` to the module path.
- The new argument is optional, so direct callers of `Base._create_attention_instances` are unaffected.

**Update after review.** My original commit named the layers `maybe_prefix(model_prefix, f"{i}.attn")`. The review commit 9bef685 by **hmellor** switched to the qualified module name, renamed the loop variable to `attn_prefix` so the parameter can be called `prefix`, and removed a unit test that only restated the naming formula with mocks. The description above reflects the final code.

## Test Plan

- End-to-end (1 GPU): `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_draft_model.py::test_draft_model_transformers_backend`. OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct drafts for itself with greedy sampling, so acceptance should be close to 1.
- The issue's minimal reproduction, on model runner V2 (default) and V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`), before and after the change.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`
- Full CI on the final commit.

## Test Result

**Final commit (`de4e6c4`).** [Buildkite CI #92113](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92113) passed, including the `spec-decode-draft-model` jobs on NVIDIA and AMD.

**Local runs.** These were done on my original commit (`d544cff`), before the review changes. I have not repeated them on the final commit.

Before (`main` at `cb4f016c5`), the minimal reproduction from the issue fails on both model runners:

```text
ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn
```

The new end-to-end test fails the same way (`1 failed … RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`, root cause `Duplicate layer name: 0.attn`).

After:

- Reproduction: the engine starts and generates on model runner V2 (default) and on V1. Greedy output is identical on both: `' Paris, and the largest city in France is Lyon. Lyon is known for its'`.
- A realistic pairing, `OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct` as target with `OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct` as drafter: fails with `Duplicate layer name: 0.attn` before the change; after it, the engine starts and generates.
- End-to-end: `test_draft_model_transformers_backend` gives `1 passed in 200.68s`, with `acceptance_rate=0.99, acceptance_len=3.98` (K=3, so at most 4.0), as expected when a model drafts for itself.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed, including ruff, typos, mypy and the Buildkite test-wiring check.

Environment: NVIDIA RTX 5090, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python-only build (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`). This machine has no CUDA toolkit, so FlashInfer's JIT sampler cannot build here. I ran the V1 reproduction and the end-to-end test with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`; that setting is unrelated to this change.

title: [Misc] Remove tool name from warn logs
author: sfbemerk
body:
## Purpose

Tool names are user input and must be kept private. 

Previously, WARN logs for malformed tool calls did include tool names, e.g.:
```
Tool call 'my_tool' has arguments that are not valid JSON (420 chars); coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.
```

After this change, the WARN log does no longer print sensitive information:
```
Tool call has arguments that are not valid JSON (420 chars); coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.
```

Upside: vllm can be used in privacy-relevant applications without custom patches
Downside: debugging is more complex in case of malformed tool calls. We could add DEBUG logs that include the tool name, if strongly desired.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor parallel_tool_calls=false in the Responses API
author: sfeng33
body:
## Purpose

`/v1/responses` ignores `parallel_tool_calls: false` whenever the grammar doesn't already limit the model to one call. That happens with parsers that have no structural tag, with `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0`, and with `tool_choice: auto`. Chat completions already filters these calls after parsing (`maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`, #44955); Responses never did.

This PR reuses that helper in the non-harmony Responses path, streaming and non-streaming. Only a literal `False` filters, and `None`/`True` behave as before. When streaming, dropped calls emit no events, so `output_index` values stay contiguous.

## Test Plan

Live A/B on one H200: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, base `a96ee5935d` vs. this PR.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes
```

- **Server runs:** one with `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0` (no grammar) and one with default settings.
- **Requests per run (20):**
  - Responses: non-stream and stream, `tool_choice` `auto` and `required`, `parallel_tool_calls` set to `false`, unset or `null`.
  - Chat completions controls: non-stream and stream, `tool_choice` `auto` and `required`, flag `false` or unset.
- **Prompt:** "Get the weather in Paris, Berlin, and Tokyo. Call the tool once per city." with one `get_weather(city)` tool and thinking off.

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
  "input": "Get the weather in Paris, Berlin, and Tokyo. Call the tool once per city.",

  "tool_choice": "auto", "parallel_tool_calls": false,
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}, "temperature": 0
}' | jq '[.output[] | select(.type=="function_call") | .arguments]'
```

## Test Result

**No grammar** (`VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0`):

| Request | `parallel_tool_calls` | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Responses auto / required, non-stream | `false` | 3 calls | **1 call (Paris)** |
| Responses auto / required, stream | `false` | 3 items, `output_index` 0,1,2; `completed` has 3 | **1 item, `output_index` 0; `completed` has 1** |
| Responses auto / required, stream + non-stream | unset / `null` | 3 calls | 3 calls |
| Chat auto / required, stream + non-stream | `false` | 1 call | 1 call |
| Chat auto / required, stream + non-stream | unset | 3 calls | 3 calls |

title: [Bugfix][Responses API] Build streamed final response from streamed items
author: sfeng33
body:
## Purpose

In non-harmony streaming, `/v1/responses` builds `response.completed` by re-parsing the full output instead of reusing what it streamed, and the two disagree. Items get new ids and a function call's `call_id` changes, so a client that continues with `previous_response_id` references a `call_id` the stored response doesn't have. Streamed items can also go missing (e.g. a whitespace-only message before a tool call), and logprobs move from the message to every generated token.

This PR builds `response.completed` from the streamed items. Streamed items get `rs_` / `msg_` / `fc_` ids and the parser's `call_id`, as in non-streaming, and the done message carries its text logprobs. `function_call_arguments.done` is now always emitted, including for calls with no argument deltas, as the Harmony path does.

Related: #47916 fixes only function-call ids, #54064 bundles a similar change with unrelated work, and #54236 overlaps on `function_call_arguments.done`.

## Test Plan

Live A/B on one H200: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, base `1d331f8341` vs. this PR, both servers started with:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --max-logprobs 5
```

Four streaming `/v1/responses` requests at temperature 0: a single tool call, two parallel tool calls, a zero-argument tool, and plain text with output logprobs. For each, every `response.output_item.done` item is compared with `response.completed.response.output` (id, `call_id`, arguments, text, logprob count), each function call is checked for a `function_call_arguments.done`, and the same request is sent non-streaming to compare usage.

```bash
curl -sN localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "input": "What'"'"'s the weather in Paris?", "stream": true, "temperature": 0,
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get current weather for a city",
             "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}]
}' | grep -E '"type":"response.(output_item.done|completed)"'
```

## Test Result

| Request | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Single tool call | streamed `reasoning`, `message "\n\n"`, `function_call` (`call_id` `call_86cf…`); completed `reasoning`, `function_call` (`call_id` `chatcmpl-tool-937d…`); all ids differ | streamed == completed: `rs_b195…`, `msg_b916…`, `fc_a37a…` with `call_id` `chatcmpl-tool-8f95…` |
| Two parallel tool calls | completed drops the message; both calls get new ids and `call_id`s | streamed == completed |
| Zero-argument tool | completed drops the message; ids and `call_id` differ | streamed == completed |
| Text with logprobs | streamed message 0 logprobs, completed 103 (all tokens) | 3 and 3 (`"\n\n"`, `Hello`, `!`) |
| Usage, stream vs non-stream | output 104 / 125 / 110 / 103, reasoning 81 / 81 / 91 / 97 | identical |

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix MTP acceptance collapse under FULL graphs with a saturated GPU pool
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Purpose

Fixes MTP acceptance collapsing with HiSparse + speculative decoding under FULL CUDA graphs once the HiSparse GPU pool saturates. Two independent causes; both are needed on current main.

**1. Draft rows mirrored before the drafter writes them.** The MTP layers are HiSparse layers too, and HiSparse marks a page clean and releases it for all of its layers, target and draft, at once. Each step does:

```
start_step → target forward → finish_forward → propose (drafter writes its rows)
```

`finish_forward` mirrored *all* layers to host, including draft layers whose rows `propose` had not written yet, and then reported the step's pages clean. The drafter's own per-layer mirror is skipped under FULL graphs, so the fresh draft rows never reached host. When the page's GPU block was reused, the drafter read stale host rows.

**2. The residency resolver can read stale request ids** (regression from #59235). The resolver runs on the HiSparse copy stream, which outside PIECEWISE graphs waits only on `logical_topk_ready`, recorded right after the indexer. #59235 writes the masked request ids later, on the compute stream, so the resolver can read the previous call's ids. The MTP layer alternates four rows per request (draft prefill) with one (draft decode), so stale ids resolve draft rows against other requests' KV.

## Changes

- The speculator tags its draft attention layers (`AttentionLayerBase.is_draft_layer`); HiSparse binding marks their cache handles as draft layers.
- `finish_forward` mirrors only target layers.
- The next step's `start_step` first mirrors the previous step's draft-layer rows (the drafter has run by then), then submits that step's page transfers behind them on the same DMA stream, so a page is only reported clean after its draft rows are queued. They are queued before the step swaps host write events, so the new step's forward and host copies wait for them: by then the scheduler may have handed a finished request's GPU and host blocks to another request. No connector API changes (`wait_for_save` stays a no-op).
- Build the resolver's masked request ids on the copy stream after its wait, into buffers owned by the HiSparse index group (moved from the generic `SparseMLAIndexGroup`); `swap_in` now requires the valid-row count.

**Why not just move `finish_forward` after `propose`?** Outside FULL graphs the drafter re-prepares the draft handles with its own (decode-shaped) metadata, so a combined end-of-step mirror hits HiSparse's metadata consistency checks (`RuntimeError`) for every target/drafter graph-mode mix except FULL/FULL. Target and draft layers need to be mirrored at different points, which requires knowing which layers are draft layers.

**Known limitation (follow-up).** A host block freed after step N (finished or preempted request) can be reallocated to a P/D import before step N's deferred copies land; NIXL writes are not ordered against the copy stream, so an imported request could, rarely, receive stale draft-layer rows (or, with the non-default lazy mirror mode, stale rows for all layers of a preempted request's spilled page). GPU writes and host copy-on-write are ordered: the next step waits for the deferred copies before its forward and host copies. The follow-up holds freed host blocks until the step's deferred writes are reported done.

## Test Plan / Results

**Unit:**
- `test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter[FULL|NONE]` drives the real worker and checks that host draft rows equal the drafter's writes, with exactly one draft-layer copy and the page reported only after it. On main the FULL case fails.
- `test_hisparse_resolver_reads_current_request_ids` (GPU) stalls the compute stream between `logical_topk_ready` and attention, then resolves four rows per request followed by one row per request plus a padding row. It fails on main and passes here.
- H100: `test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or index_group"` 40 passed; HiSparse connector/worker tests pass.
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: the FULL-graph host-mirror check now verifies MTP rows when the next step's start mirrors them (it compared them right after `finish_forward`, before the drafter writes them) and requires the MTP layer to be detected as a draft layer. 4 passed (H100); fails if the speculator stops tagging its layers.

**E2E, cause 1 (on the pre-#59235 base):** H200 2×8, GLM-5.3 TP8/EP8 HiSparse decoder, MTP3, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, NIXL P/D from a PCP8/DCP8 prefiller; Agent X workload at concurrency 48 (HiSparse GPU pool ≥95%).

| | MTP acceptance | per position | output tok/s | ITL p50 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 0.248 | 0.46/0.19/0.09 | 438* | 66.0 ms |
| cause 1 fixed | **0.503** | 0.68/0.48/0.35 | **727.7** | 50.1 ms |
| before, PIECEWISE only (per-layer mirror active) | 0.471 | 0.66/0.45/0.30 | 664.6 | 51.8 ms |

\* includes debug-counter overhead; the pre-fix sweep peaked at ~500 tok/s.

- Host-vs-GPU audit of sealed MTP-layer pages: 98.7% mismatch before, 60.3% after, in line with the target layers' 58.6% (the audit also samples pages that are still being written).
- gsm8k (5-shot, 500) through P/D: 0.928 (0.920–0.936 before).

**E2E, current main:** B300 ×4, GLM-5.3 FP8 TP4, MTP3, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, GPU KV capped at 8 GiB (pool saturated), 40 code prompts × ~16k in / 512 out.

| | acceptance length | output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 1.37 | 113–138 |
| cause 1 fix only | 1.31–1.48 | 123–138 |
| cause 2 fix only | 1.37 | 133 |
| **both (this PR)** | **2.68** | **295** |

PIECEWISE on main under the same pressure: 2.29. The cause-2-only row used an earlier variant of the same fix (re-recording the event after the write).

Mirroring draft rows at the next `start_step` instead of in `wait_for_save` (B300, same setup, `--async-scheduling`, 2 runs each): acceptance length 2.80/2.72 vs 2.78/2.70, median ITL 33.6/34.0 ms vs 33.3/33.8 ms; throughput differences are within run-to-run noise.

Cost of the copy-stream build, per resolving layer in a CUDA graph (H100, 32 reqs × 4 rows, top-k 2048, all hot hits): 132.5 µs → 134.1 µs (+1.2%); with host misses the difference is within noise.

No other open PR addresses this. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; changes reviewed and tested by the submitters.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Drop a timed-out store job's blocks from the round's parked supply
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Purpose

In the symmetric P2P KV offload tier, a decode instance asks a peer whether it holds a prompt's KV, and the peer pins the matching blocks in its own cache until the fetch arrives. If the fetch is late, the pin times out and the peer's engine frees those cache slots for reuse, but the round still advertises the blocks as available. A fetch that arrives after the timeout then RDMA-reads slots that may already hold another request's KV, and reports success. The decode instance would continue generating from someone else's cache. This PR withdraws the advertised blocks when their pin times out, so the late fetch fails fast and the request prefills locally.

Concretely, in `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/session/server.py`:

- Answering a lookup, the server pins the blocks through a store job and parks them in the fetch round: `add_stored_blocks` (`:94`) records them in `available` and the job in `pending_job_ids`.
- `_timeout_pending_store_jobs` (`:1121`) fails a job older than `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` (`:40`, 30 s) with `StoreResult(success=False)`. The tiering manager maps that to a failed `JobResult` (`p2p/manager.py:859`), and the engine unpins the slots.
- The round's `available` entries and `pending_job_ids` are left as they were. A late `FetchMsg` matches them in `on_fetch` and submits the transfer.

**Fix:** when store jobs time out, remove their entries from every round's `available` map and `pending_job_ids`. The late fetch then has unmatched demand and takes the existing fail-fast path for symmetric rounds (`server.py:372`): `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)`, and the consumer prefills locally. The PD case where the prefiller finishes first has the same problem when its store stays parked longer than `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` before the fetch arrives, and this fix covers it too: `finish()` has already set `finishing`, so `on_fetch` fails the round (thanks @liranschour for pointing this out and for reproducing the bug).

**Not a duplicate:** #53453 added a one-round-trip rejection of a late fetch for stores the *manager* reaps while still unbound (`_reaped_stores`). This PR covers the other case: a store job already bound to a session that `_timeout_pending_store_jobs` fails. #58168 (draft) edits `server.py` elsewhere and does not reference these identifiers. No open PR touches `_timeout_pending_store_jobs`.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py -q -k symmetric_supply_timed_out
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

New test, `TestServerFlows::test_fetch_after_symmetric_supply_timed_out_reads_nothing`: a lookup pins block `hA` (slot 7); the store job is aged past `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` and reported failed; then a `FetchMsg` for `hA` arrives. It checks that no transfer is submitted and the round ends with `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)`.

## Test Result

With the fix (CPU, macOS arm64, on main `4e0a414c4`):

```
-k symmetric_supply_timed_out ... 1 passed
tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ ... 434 passed, 1 skipped
```

On `main` (fix reverted, test kept):

```
E   AssertionError: assert {0: ('peer:8000', [7], [20])} == {}
    (the late fetch RDMA-reads the unpinned slot 7)
1 failed
```

pre-commit (`--from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`) and `mypy-3.12` (manual stage): clean.

This only changes a failure path (a fetch after its pin timed out now fails instead of reading a possibly reused slot); no evals are needed.

**Related:** one of a few independent fixes from an audit of the KV transfer paths (CPU offload, NIXL, P2P): #59096, #59099, #59102, #59325. None depends on another; they can be reviewed and merged in any order.

## AI assistance

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to audit this code path, write the fix and write the test. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer, as `AGENTS.md` asks.

title: [Bugfix] Make `suppress_stdout` redirect fd 1 instead of `sys.stdout.fileno()`
author: usmanmateen
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59268
Fixes #59269

`suppress_stdout()` wraps gloo process group creation to hide what C code prints to stdout. It redirects `sys.stdout.fileno()` to /dev/null, but C code writes to fd 1, and the two are only the same when `sys.stdout` is the plain process stdout. When they differ:

- `sys.stdout` has no fd, e.g. inside `contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())`: `fileno()` raises `io.UnsupportedOperation` (#59268).
- `sys.stdout` is bound to stderr: stderr is sent to /dev/null instead of stdout, so C error output is lost and stdout isn't suppressed (#59269).
- Jupyter on Linux/macOS: ipykernel redirects fd 1 into a pipe that feeds the notebook, and its `OutStream.fileno()` returns a copy of the original terminal fd. The terminal copy gets silenced and the C output still shows up in the notebook.

This redirects fd 1 directly. The rest of the context manager is unchanged. It doesn't affect model output, so there are no evals.

Not a duplicate: neither issue has comments or assignees, and no open PR mentions either issue number or `suppress_stdout`.

## Test Plan

Two tests added to `tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py`, one per issue:

- `test_suppress_stdout_when_sys_stdout_has_no_fd`
- `test_suppress_stdout_keeps_stderr_when_sys_stdout_is_stderr`

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py -v
```

I also checked the #59269 scenario in a plain process, and ran `os.write(1, ...)` inside `suppress_stdout()` in a real Jupyter kernel (ipykernel via `jupyter_client`).

## Test Result

`tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py`:
- main: 2 failed, 2 passed (`io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno`, and fd 1 output not suppressed)
- this PR: 4 passed

#59269 scenario (`sys.stdout = sys.stderr`, then `os.write(1, ...)` and `os.write(2, ...)` inside `suppress_stdout()`):
- main: the stdout line is printed and the stderr line is lost
- this PR: the stdout line is suppressed and the stderr line is printed

Jupyter kernel:
- main: `sys.stdout.fileno()` is 41, and the fd 1 output shows up in the notebook
- this PR: the fd 1 output is suppressed

`pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including mypy for 3.10 and 3.12.

Tested on WSL2 Ubuntu, Python 3.12, CPU-only torch.

AI assistance: I used Claude Code to help investigate and write this fix. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Align MRV2 lm_head LoRA with logits rows
author: Shr3yash
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59161.

Model Runner V2 built the lm_head LoRA mapping with one id per request. Under speculative decoding each request owns one bonus row plus one row per draft token (`cu_num_logits`), so an lm_head adapter missed its own request or landed on a neighbor. `make_lora_inputs` now repeats each request id by `np.diff(cu_num_logits_np)`.

author: khluu
body:
## Summary

Fix the main-branch pre-commit failure introduced by #59286 ([failed job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/36655375579/job/109699177322)). `OpenAIServingModels.engine_client` is typed as `EngineClient`, so mypy sees `add_lora` as an async method and rejects `assert_not_called()`, even though the test creates it with `MagicMock(spec=EngineClient)`.

Assert that `add_lora` is an `AsyncMock` before checking its call count. This narrows the type while preserving the regression test's guarantee that rejected adapter names never reach the engine. No production code changes.

Searched open PRs for `59286 in:body`, `LoRA mypy`, and `"assert_not_called"`; no existing PR addresses this failure.

### Why #59286 passed before merging

Its passing pre-commit run tested merge commit `4865d3e` against base `7aa8372` and finished at 2026-09-29 19:39 UTC. At that point, `tests/entrypoints/serve` used `--follow-imports skip`.

At 20:27 UTC, #51043 (`5dd693122c`) merged and moved this directory to `SILENT_GROUPS`, enabling `follow_imports="silent"`. #59286 merged at 2026-09-30 01:29 UTC, after that stricter check landed. The earlier green run therefore did not validate their combined state.

Confirmed on the same unfixed test with mypy 1.20.2: `--follow-imports skip` passes; `--follow-imports silent` reproduces the exact line-115 `attr-defined` error. Skipping imports hides the imported EngineClient method type; following imports exposes it.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Suppress completion for empty pulls
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Purpose

Mooncake can issue a pull with no local destination blocks only to notify the Prefill side that its producer blocks may be released. The Decode request does not wait for remote KV in this case.

`MooncakeConnectorWorker.process_pulling_result` currently reports every successful pull as `finished_recving` after its worker tasks drain. For an empty pull, this sends a completion for a request that is not in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and can trip the scheduler's request ownership/status assertion.

Empty pulls are reachable both during early-abort cleanup and when a remote prefix hit is reduced to no transferable local blocks.

## Change

Report a successful receive completion only when the pull contains at least one local destination block:

```python
if pull_meta.pull_tasks_count == 0 and any(pull_meta.local_block_ids):
    self.finished_recving_reqs.add(pull_meta.d_req_id)
```

The producer notification and pull-task accounting are unchanged. This also matches the existing failed-receive path, which already skips scheduler notification when the pull has no local blocks.

## Relationship to other work

#50565 addresses the early-abort cleanup variant by adding an explicit `notify_scheduler` flag. Its current version intentionally still reports completion for an ordinary empty-block full-prefix pull. That does not cover the case where Decode does not enter `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` after the connector returns no transferable blocks.

This PR applies the check at the worker completion sink, covering both cleanup-only and full-prefix empty pulls while preserving completion for every pull with real local destinations.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/v1 \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py::test_pull_completion_requires_local_blocks \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py::test_kv_consumuer

ruff check \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py

ruff format --check \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
```

The regression test covers:

- `local_block_ids=[]`: no scheduler completion;
- `local_block_ids=[[]]`: no scheduler completion;
- a non-empty pull: normal scheduler completion.

## Test Result

- Targeted pytest: 4 passed.
- Ruff check and format: passed.
- Python compilation and `git diff --check`: passed.

## GPU Validation

### Environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-36768d1bfd39094681cdbc8cb37d4b31c0729c89` (`v0.30.1rc1.dev312+g36768d1bf`).
- Hardware: two nodes with 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs each.
- Runtime: Mooncake RDMA, 64-token blocks, prefix caching, and SWA bounded replay.

### Prefill

```bash
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --enable-cumem-allocator \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma","device_name":"mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3,mlx5_4","enforce_handshake_compat":false}}' \
  --block-size 64 \
  --swa-bounded-replay \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --api-server-count 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \

  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

### Decode

```bash

  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8002 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --trust-remote-code \

  --block-size 64 \

  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --api-server-count 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
```

### Results

- Original image: the first 13-token request reproduced the issue. Decode hit `assert RequestStatus.is_finished(req.status)`, returned HTTP 500 through the P/D proxy, and shut down its API server with `EngineDeadError`.

title: [BugFix][Multimodal] Pick worst-case DeepSeek-V4 VL dummy image size (#59271)
author: YidaWeng
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59271.

`DeepseekV4VLProcessingInfo.get_image_size_with_most_features` assumed a square maximizes ViT patches within the token budget. Because each aligner row costs an extra `IMAGE_NEW_LINE`, a wide grid (`1932x336`) produces more placeholder tokens and patches than the previous `756x756` dummy, so memory profiling under-estimated peak multimodal usage.

Search budget-feasible LLM grids (respecting `vision_max_wh_ratio`) and pick the one with the most ViT patches, breaking ties by sentinel-block length. For the default config this returns `1932x336`.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v4_vl.py -q
```

Also re-ran the issue reproducer against the local CPU editable install.

## Test Result

```
2 passed
```

Issue reproducer after fix:

```
dummy ImageSize(width=1932, height=336) (378, 3312)
1932x336 (378, 3312)
```

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Return lazily offloaded GPU blocks to the eviction end
author: obendidi
body:
## Purpose

In lazy mode, SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler offloads the cached blocks at the eviction end of the GPU free queue, then releases them with free_blocks, which appends cached blocks as most recently used. The blocks the CPU now holds outlive fresher blocks it doesn't hold, so the allocator evicts those instead. The scan keeps offloading new blocks, and the CPU cache turns over faster than it can serve hits.

* Adds evict_first to BlockPool.free_blocks (off by default) to free cached blocks to the front of the queue.
* Lazy store completion uses it, eager mode and abandoned stores are unchanged.
* Adds test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end, which fails without the fix.

## Test Plan

Regression test fails on `main`

```bash
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -k test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end
```

The bug only affects throughput when the lazy CPU tier is smaller than the GPU KV cache, and the GPU free queue is
much longer than one lazy scan (for example `2 × max_num_batched_tokens` tokens). 

With a small GPU cache, each scan covers the whole free queue, so block order doesn't matter: in a run with a 1,024-block GPU cache on one L4, `main` and this branch served the same CPU hits.

## Test Result

## AI assistance

Claude helped with debugging this problem and wrote the fix, the code changes were reviewed by a human

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix FlashInfer MLA DCP decode on ragged spec-decode batches
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Purpose

Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59065

With DCP > 1 and speculative decoding, FlashInfer MLA decode crashes when the decode batch is ragged, i.e. requests carry different numbers of query tokens. That happens whenever a request has fewer drafts than the others, and also during warmup. For example, Kimi-K3 with `-tp 2 -dcp 2` and DSpark fails at engine startup:

```
ValueError: causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)
```

Here a 1+7 request and a 1-token request make 9 decode tokens.

DCP cannot take the compact ragged path (`cum_seq_lens_q`), because it needs LSE. So ragged batches fall to the "uneven length" branch. That branch has two problems:

- **Shape mismatch.** It splits `q` into one row per token, but it keeps `block_table`, `seq_lens` and `causal_seqlens_kv_global` per request. FlashInfer then rejects the call.
- **Silent wrong reshape.** The branch is only taken when `num_decode_tokens % num_decodes != 0`. A ragged batch whose token count happens to divide evenly (e.g. 8 + 2 tokens) is instead `view`ed as a uniform 5 + 5 batch, and each request's rows attend to the wrong KV.

## Fix

A batch is now treated as ragged when `num_decode_tokens != num_decodes * max_query_len`. Ragged causal batches are split into single-token rows:

- `block_table` and `seq_lens` are expanded per row with the existing `_flattened_decode_metadata`.
- Each row's DCP bound is `T - (tokens of its request after it)`. FlashInfer defines `causal_seqlens_kv_global` as the global exclusive causal bound of each row's newest query token, and `dcp_tot_seq_lens` (`T`) already includes all of the request's query tokens.

The non-DCP causal path is unchanged; it already goes through `cum_seq_lens_q`.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR touches this branch. #56784 edits the same file, but only for backend selection.

## Test Plan

- Kernel check on GB200, run directly against `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` with the cute-dsl backend, `cp_world=2`, both ranks, and `(T, q_len)` in `{(301, 8), (97, 8), (130, 4), (64, 1)}`:
  - One request with `q_len` rows and bound `T` gives bit-identical output and LSE (max error `0.0`) to `q_len` single-token rows bounded at `T - (q_len - 1 - j)`.
  - Negative control: bounding every split row at `T` gives a max output error of `0.26`.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py`: `test_flashinfer_mla_forward_uses_native_dcp_api` is extended with a ragged `(3, 1)` batch. The new `ragged-causal` case fails without this change and passes with it.

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py
```

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py` + `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py`: 23 passed, 1 skipped (GB200).
- Without the source change, only `ragged-causal` fails.
- An end-to-end run with Kimi-K3 was not done here. The `dcp2-*-dspark` cases in #59229 are strict xfails for this bug and will flip once this lands.

No output changes for batches that worked before, so no model eval was run.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [CPU][Bugfix] Skip KV cache memory reservation for pooling models
author: Akashcodes732
body:
## Purpose

Encoder-only and pooling models (embeddings, rerankers, classifiers) do not perform autoregressive generation and do not need a KV cache. 
Previously, `CPUWorker.__init__` eagerly required `requested_cpu_memory <= available_memory` at startup, causing models to fail in memory-constrained environments (e.g., container `--memory=5g`) unless users manually passed `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=0`

This PR:
1. Skips the startup memory reservation check in `CPUWorker.__init__` when `runner_type == "pooling"`.
2. Automatically sets `kv_cache_size = 0` in `determine_available_memory()` for pooling models, matching GPU worker behavior out-of-the-box.

## Test Plan

Run an encoder-only reranker model without any KV-cache environment variables or flags:
```bash
vllm serve BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 --dtype bfloat16
```
## Test Result
Server starts cleanly out-of-the-box without requiring VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=0

title: [ROCm][Perf][Bugfix] Probe the preshuffled FP4 GEMM config by logical K
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`, `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` sends decode-sized MXFP4 linears (M ≤ 64) to AITER's Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle` when `rocm_aiter_ops.is_triton_gemm_afp4wfp4_presh_ws_tuned(N, k_bytes)` reports a tuned config, and to the ASM `gemm_a4w4` otherwise.

The gate checks the wrong file. `k_bytes` is `weight.shape[1]`, i.e. K/2, and the gate probes `GEMM-AFP4WFP4_PRESHUFFLED-N={N}-K={4 * k_bytes}.json`, which is 2K. `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle` itself resolves `N={N}-K={2 * k_bytes}`, the logical K. So the gate asks about a different shape than the one the kernel then runs:

- If the layer's own shape is tuned but 2K is not, the gate says no and the layer falls back to ASM.
- If 2K is tuned but the layer's own shape is not, the gate says yes and the layer runs the Triton kernel on AITER's generic default config.

Of the 25 `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffled` configs AITER ships for gfx950 (ROCm/aiter@89a47b8), 19 are never selected on main. Another 19 shapes are accepted only because a file exists at twice their K:

| | (N, K) |
| --- | --- |
| Tuned, rejected on main | (1280, 8192), (2112, 7168), (2560, 8192), (3072, 1536), (4096, 512), (4096, 14336), (5120, 8192), (7168, 8192), (8192, 8192), (8192, 28672), (10240, 8192), (14336, 8192), (16384, 16384), (16384, 53248), (18432, 16384), (28672, 8192), (36864, 7168), (57344, 8192), (106496, 16384) |
| Untuned, accepted on main | (1280, 4096), (2112, 3584), (2560, 4096), (3072, 768), (4096, 256), (4096, 7168), (5120, 4096), (7168, 4096), (8192, 512), (8192, 1792), (10240, 4096), (14336, 4096), (16384, 8192), (16384, 26624), (18432, 8192), (28672, 4096), (36864, 3584), (57344, 4096), (106496, 8192) |

This PR probes `2 * k_bytes`, the same file the kernel loads.

The existing tuned-shape case in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py`, `(M, N, K) = (32, 8192, 16384)`, only passed because `N=16384-K=16384` exists. It is replaced by `(64, 4096, 8192)` and `(32, 16384, 16384)`, and the test now also asserts that the kernel resolves a tuned config for the shape. `test_aiter_fp4_preshuffled_tuned_gate_uses_logical_k` pins the gate itself: `(N=16384, K=16384)` is tuned and `(N=16384, K=8192)` is not.

---

## Test Plan

- Hardware: 8× MI355X (gfx950)
- Unit tests: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py -k preshuffled`
- Model: `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`. The GDN `in_proj_qkvz` (N=4608, K=8192) and `out_proj` (N=8192, K=2048) linears are quantized online to MXFP4 and served with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`.
- Serving A/B (same image except this change and one AITER config file, see below): random dataset, ISL=8192, OSL=1024, range-ratio=0.8, concurrency `{4, 8, 16, 32, 64}` with 32/64/96/128/256 prompts and one warmup request per concurrency slot
- Accuracy: GSM8K, 1319 problems, 5-shot, thinking off, temperature=0.0, max-tokens=2048. Same servers as the A/B.

The PR arm also carries a gfx950 `GEMM-AFP4WFP4_PRESHUFFLED-N=4608-K=8192.json` from https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5998 tuned for `in_proj_qkvz`. Without this change the file is never read, because the gate probes `N=4608-K=16384`, so `in_proj_qkvz` runs the ASM `gemm_a4w4` in the control either way (confirmed in the control trace below). `out_proj` uses AITER's existing `N=8192-K=2048` file and runs the preshuffled kernel in both arms, only because `N=8192-K=4096` also exists.

---

## Test Result

### Unit tests

On one MI355X (gfx950), with AITER 0.1.22.post1. None of the selected tests use the config from ROCm/aiter#5998.

```bash
python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py -k preshuffled
```

This PR:

```text
tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py::test_aiter_fp4_gemm_preshuffled_tuned_shapes[shape0] PASSED [ 33%]
tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py::test_aiter_fp4_gemm_preshuffled_tuned_shapes[shape1] PASSED [ 66%]
tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py::test_aiter_fp4_preshuffled_tuned_gate_uses_logical_k PASSED [100%]
================ 3 passed, 55 deselected, 14 warnings in 4.73s =================
```

The same tests against main's gate (`4 * k_bytes`) fail wherever a shape's own config exists but its doubled K does not: both failures are `N=16384-K=16384`, where main probes the missing `N=16384-K=32768`. `shape0` (`N=8192-K=4096`) passes on main too, because `N=8192-K=8192` also exists:

```text
tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py::test_aiter_fp4_gemm_preshuffled_tuned_shapes[shape0] PASSED [ 33%]
tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py::test_aiter_fp4_gemm_preshuffled_tuned_shapes[shape1] FAILED [ 66%]
tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py::test_aiter_fp4_preshuffled_tuned_gate_uses_logical_k FAILED [100%]
E       AssertionError: assert False
E        +  where False = <functools._lru_cache_wrapper object at 0x7f205e0138a0>(16384, (16384 // 2))
E        +    where <functools._lru_cache_wrapper object at 0x7f205e0138a0> = <class 'vllm._aiter_ops.rocm_aiter_ops'>.is_triton_gemm_afp4wfp4_presh_ws_tuned
=========== 2 failed, 1 passed, 55 deselected, 14 warnings in 4.73s ============
```

### Performance

8k/1k, output throughput, mean TPOT and mean TTFT:


| Cell | Control out tok/s | This PR + the AITER config out tok/s | Δ | Control TPOT (ms) | This PR + the AITER config TPOT (ms) | Δ | Control TTFT (ms) | This PR + the AITER config TTFT (ms) | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c=4 ¹ | 266.24 | 337.15 | +26.6% | 14.37 | 11.30 | −21.4% | 319.8 | 324.9 | +1.6% |
| c=8 | 474.03 | 498.87 | +5.2% | 16.11 | 15.28 | −5.2% | 406.7 | 417.5 | +2.7% |
| c=16 | 673.06 | 705.34 | +4.8% | 22.60 | 21.55 | −4.6% | 619.1 | 614.2 | −0.8% |

| c=64 | 1382.14 | 1408.95 | +1.9% | 42.57 | 41.81 | −1.8% | 2350.5 | 2272.1 | −3.3% |

¹ c=4 seems like an outlier. Geomean output throughput, c=8 to c=64: **+3.8%**. 

This PR changes only affects decode-sized GEMMs (M ≤ 64), so TTFT is expected to be flat; added here as a sanity check.

Kernel-level, from c=4 profiled decode steps (rank 0, 69 GDN layers):

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Select page-aligned kernel blocks for pooled indexers so the block table addresses storage pages (GLM-5.3-Flash)
author: vllmellm
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58858

GLM-5.3-Flash serving on ROCm silently corrupts its DSA index cache. Root cause: `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` returned `[1, MultipleOf(16)]` on ROCm for every deployment, so `select_common_block_size` keeps the hybrid KV manager block (640/1152/2176/4352 for TP8..TP1) as the kernel block size, while `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` drops the spec's `storage_block_size` which every other consumer (cache views, metadata builders, hisparse) already uses as the kernel block. `Glm5NextIndexerCache` with `index_kpool = 4`, however, stores index-cache entries in pool pages of `page * index_kpool` = 128/256 tokens, and both the writer (`get_compressed_slot_mapping`) and the gather address the block table as `column = pos // storage_block_size`. A manager-granular table therefore skips the builder's conversion branch (`storage % kernel != 0`), indexes far outside the request's row (TP2 @32K: raw table 16 columns wide, 256 needed -> page 0 aliased everywhere), and at TP4 writes past the row buffer entirely.

This is also the root cause behind these issues, #55280, #54359 and #56380.

## Changes

* `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py` - `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` is the point where the cache group's spec (`kv_cache_group.kv_cache_spec`) and the group's backends are both in hand, but `storage_block_size` was dropped before dispatch. It now takes `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size` as the kernel block size if the group's backends support it, otherwise falls back to `select_common_block_size` unchanged. On CUDA the indexer declares an exact `[64]`, so the storage block fails validation there and the conversion path keeps working the same way as today. The support check is the existing `block_size_is_supported` logic moved out of `select_common_block_size` to module level, so both call sites use the same check (exact `==` for `int`, multiple-of for `MultipleOf`).

## Test Plan

Sample command gsm8k + bench:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size {2,4} --max-model-len 262144 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser glm47

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template

vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --host localhost --port 8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 100 --max-concurrency 32
```

> If NIAH config is required, I can add in. 

New tests:

* `tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_indexer_block_sizes.py`: `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` returns the storage block (128/256), not the manager block (640/1152/2176/4352), for the kpool group at every TP floor with the real group backends (indexer + tail + aiter sparse MLA) - fails on main as `[640] == [128]`; plus the fallback, backend rejects the storage block (CUDA-style exact `[64]`) or spec without `storage_block_size` -> `select_common_block_size` as before.


## Test Result

| suite |  main (`713ec07`) | this fix |
|---|---|---|
| NIAH 4096-32000, TP2 | 12/28 | **28/28** |
| NIAH 4096-32000, TP4 | 12/28 | **28/28** |
| NIAH 131072/261632, 3 seeds, TP2 | 3/42 | **32/42** | 
| lm-eval gsm8k 20-shot (1319) | 0.8552 ± 0.0097 | **0.9742 ± 0.0044** |

> Likely something else in play for the not 100% NIAH result on long context 131072/261632 case. Fixing that would be out-of-scope of this PR. 

Benchmark (`random` 1024/1024/100, c32, 4 runs incl. `--no-enable-prefix-caching`):

| branch | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `713ec07` | 1017.8 / 1066.7 | 2035.5 / 2133.4 | 24.58 / 24.71 ms | 
| this PR | 1051.4 / 1033.3 | 2102.8 / 2066.5 | 24.90 / 24.97 ms |

In general no difference between main and this PR. 

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_indexer_block_sizes.py  -> 5 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
       tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py          -> 120 passed
test_gpu_model_runner block-size cohort            -> 12 passed
```

P.S. TP8 is not tested, because on the tested main `713ec07` TP8 will produce gibberish outputs.
