title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Strip `x-anthropic-billing-header` billing header from `/v1/chatcompletions`
author: vMaroon
body:
## Purpose

Some versions of Claude Code open their system prompt with `x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=...; cc_entrypoint=...; cch=<hex>;`, and in the versions that send a real `cch` it changes on every request (see below for which versions). #36829 drops this block on `/v1/messages`.

LiteLLM and other gateways that translate Anthropic requests into `/v1/chat/completions` pass the block through, so every turn misses the prefix cache from the header on. We need to strip this header in both the `/v1/messages` case and in the `/v1/chat/completions` case.

### Which Claude Code versions send it

The block is built client-side as a plain string and sent as the first text block of `system` in the request body, not as an HTTP header, so it reaches any server behind an Anthropic-to-OpenAI gateway. Whether it carries `cch` depends on the client version and provider. The "client code" column comes from the published `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` builds. The "on the wire" column comes from capturing request bodies from 61 versions with an API key (or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`) and a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`; reproduction steps are below.

| Versions | Released | `cch` per client code | On the wire (custom base URL) |
|---|---|---|---|
| <= 2.1.34 | to 2026-02-06 | never (the block exists, without `cch`) | 2.1.18: no `cch`; <= 2.0.70: no block |
| 2.1.36 - ~2.1.75 | 2026-02-07 to 03-13 | always, for every provider | 2.1.47, 2.1.75: constant `cch=00000` |
| ~2.1.100 - 2.1.179 | 2026-04 to 06-16 | every provider except Bedrock (`bedrock` / `anthropicAws` / `mantle`) | 2.1.108 - 2.1.112: constant `cch=00000`; **2.1.113 - 2.1.179: changes on every request** |
| 2.1.181 - 2.1.286 | 2026-06-17 onward | only for Vertex, or first-party under a further client-side check | no `cch` |

Boundaries marked `~` were not bisected to a single release, and 2.1.180 could not be fetched. Versions from 2.1.140 ship as compiled binaries, so for those the condition was read from the constants next to `cch=00000;` rather than from source, and the extra first-party check was confirmed in 2.1.286 only.

With a custom base URL, the per-request `cch` that breaks prefix caching was observed from 2.1.113 through 2.1.179. Earlier versions sent the `cch=00000` placeholder unchanged, which is the same on every request. Those clients stay in use well after newer releases. Other auth paths (OAuth/subscription, Vertex) were not captured and may send `cch` in other versions too. With 2.1.286 through LiteLLM we saw `x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=2.1.286.99b; cc_entrypoint=cli;` with no `cch`, and the `cc_version` suffix was stable across turns of the main conversation.

On the first-party path, 2.1.286 also adds per-turn fields to the same block (`cc_prev_req`, `cc_prompt_id`, `cc_turn_origin`, `cc_prompt_index`, `cc_turn_index`). That is why this PR drops the whole block rather than only `cch`.

In every captured version the block is system block 0, on its own, with no `cache_control`. LiteLLM 1.77.7 through 1.103.1 forward it as its own text part of the chat-completions system message; it is never joined to the prompt text. The entrypoint (`cli`, `sdk-cli`, `claude-desktop`) changes only the `cc_entrypoint` value.

Clients can omit the block by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER` to a false value (tested with `0` on 2.1.139 and 2.1.286, and with `false` on 2.1.286), but a server cannot rely on users doing that.

This does not duplicate existing work: #36829 covers `/v1/messages` only, and no open PR touches the chat path (searched "billing header", "x-anthropic-billing-header", "cch"). #58754 is a separate `/v1/messages` fix for inline system messages.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_billing_header.py
pre-commit run (all hooks, Linux, python 3.12)
```

Serving check on GLM-5.3 (P/D disaggregated, prefix caching on), Claude Code traffic through LiteLLM:
- render: `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` for 5 turns of one conversation with a fresh `cch` per request, comparing each turn's prompt with the previous one
- cache: prefill `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source_total` on a 1P/1D canary (8 turns) and on the production fleet (6P/6D) before and after

Captured traffic: the system messages LiteLLM forwarded for Claude Code 2.1.18, 2.1.47, 2.1.108, 2.1.139, 2.1.199 and 2.1.286 were run through `_parse_chat_message_content` in both `openai` and `string` content formats.

End-to-end: real Claude Code sessions through LiteLLM into a vLLM server, for the base commit and for this branch. Each session runs 4 turns in one `claude -p --input-format stream-json` process (one conversation). The prefix cache is reset before each session, and each later turn's prefix-cache hit rate is read from vLLM's `/metrics`.

<details>
<summary>Reproducing the header captures</summary>

1. Save this capture server as `capture.py`. It logs each request body and returns a non-retryable 400:

```python
import json, os, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

port, out = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0)))
        n = len(os.listdir(out)) + 1
        with open(f"{out}/{n:04d}.json", "w") as f:
            json.dump({"path": self.path, "body": json.loads(body or b"{}")}, f, indent=1)
        msg = b'{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"captured"}}'
        self.send_response(400)
        self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("content-length", str(len(msg)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(msg)
    def log_message(self, *a): pass

ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), H).serve_forever()
```

2. Capture a given Claude Code version directly. Use a clean environment, because inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_*` variables change the header:

```bash
V=2.1.139
npm install --prefix cc-$V @anthropic-ai/claude-code@$V
python capture.py 8701 caps/$V &
mkdir -p home-$V
env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=$PWD/home-$V TERM=xterm \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-dummy ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8701 \
  DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 cc-$V/node_modules/.bin/claude -p hi </dev/null
kill %1
python -c "import json,glob; [print(b['text']) for f in sorted(glob.glob('caps/$V/*.json')) \
  for b in (json.load(open(f))['body'].get('system') or []) if b.get('text','').startswith('x-anthropic')]"
```

Run it twice: on 2.1.113 - 2.1.179 the `cch` value differs between the two runs.

3. Capture through LiteLLM. Run the capture server as the upstream and point Claude Code at the proxy:

```yaml
# litellm.yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: "*"
    litellm_params:
      model: hosted_vllm/test
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:8702/v1
      api_key: dummy
```

```bash
python capture.py 8702 caps/litellm &
litellm --config litellm.yaml --port 8700 &
env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=$PWD/home-$V TERM=xterm \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-dummy ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8700 \
  DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 cc-$V/node_modules/.bin/claude -p hi </dev/null
```

The `/v1/chat/completions` body in `caps/litellm/` has a single system message whose first text part is the header.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproducing the end-to-end check (Claude Code → LiteLLM → vLLM)</summary>

1. Serve a small model with tool calling. `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` enables `/reset_prefix_cache`. Run it once on `main` and once on this branch:

```bash
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 40960 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --port 8000
```

2. Put LiteLLM in front of it:

```yaml
# litellm.yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: "*"
    litellm_params:
      model: hosted_vllm/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
      api_key: dummy
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

```bash
litellm --config litellm.yaml --port 8001
```

3. Save this as `multi_turn.py`:

```python
"""A multi-turn Claude Code session through LiteLLM into vLLM.

Reports how much of each later turn's prompt hit vLLM's prefix cache.

Usage: python multi_turn.py CLAUDE_BIN VLLM_URL LITELLM_URL [TURNS]
"""

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import urllib.request

claude, vllm_url, litellm_url = sys.argv[1:4]
turns = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 2


def prefix_cache():
    text = urllib.request.urlopen(f"{vllm_url}/metrics").read().decode()
    totals = {"queries": 0.0, "hits": 0.0}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        for k in totals:
            if line.startswith(f"vllm:prefix_cache_{k}_total{{"):
                totals[k] += float(line.rsplit(" ", 1)[1])
    return totals


def turn(proc, text):
    msg = {"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": text}}
    proc.stdin.write(json.dumps(msg) + "\n")
    proc.stdin.flush()
    for line in proc.stdout:
        if json.loads(line).get("type") == "result":
            return
    raise RuntimeError("claude exited before finishing the turn")


urllib.request.urlopen(
    urllib.request.Request(f"{vllm_url}/reset_prefix_cache", method="POST")
)
home, work = tempfile.mkdtemp(), tempfile.mkdtemp()
env = {
    "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin",
    "HOME": home,
    "TERM": "xterm",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-dummy",
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": litellm_url,
    "CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS": "256",
    "DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER": "1",
}
proc = subprocess.Popen(
    [claude, "-p", "--verbose", "--input-format", "stream-json",
     "--output-format", "stream-json"],
    cwd=work, env=env, text=True,
    stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
)
turn(proc, "Say hi.")
for i in range(2, turns + 1):
    before = prefix_cache()
    turn(proc, f"Say the number {i}.")
    after = prefix_cache()
    queries = after["queries"] - before["queries"]
    hits = after["hits"] - before["hits"]
    print(f"turn {i}: {queries:7.0f} prompt tokens, {hits:7.0f} cached "
          f"({100 * hits / max(queries, 1):5.1f}%)", flush=True)
proc.stdin.close()
proc.wait(timeout=60)
```

4. Run a session for each Claude Code version:

```bash
for V in 2.0.70 2.1.18 2.1.75 2.1.112 2.1.113 2.1.139 2.1.179 2.1.181 2.1.286; do
  npm install --silent --prefix cc-$V @anthropic-ai/claude-code@$V
  echo "== $V"
  python multi_turn.py cc-$V/node_modules/.bin/claude http://127.0.0.1:8000 http://127.0.0.1:8001 4
done
```

Two separate `claude -p` launches are not comparable: the order of the agent and skill lists in the prompt changes between launches. That is why the turns run in one session.

</details>

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 7 passed with the fix; 4 of the 7 fail on main.
- Captured traffic: for every captured version the header is removed and the rest of the system prompt is unchanged, in both content formats.
- End-to-end, prefix-cache hit rate of turns 2 / 3 / 4 of one session (Qwen3-0.6B, LiteLLM 1.103.1):

  | Claude Code | Header | Base | This PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2.0.70 | none | 99.7 / 99.7 / 99.7% | 99.8 / 99.9 / 99.9% |
  | 2.1.18 | no `cch` | 99.8 / 99.9 / 99.9% | 99.7 / 99.9 / 99.9% |
  | 2.1.75 | `cch=00000` | 12.2 / 99.8 / 99.7% | 12.1 / 99.9 / 99.9% |
  | 2.1.112 | `cch=00000` | 65.2 / 99.8 / 99.9% | 99.2 / 99.9 / 99.9% |
  | **2.1.113** | per-request `cch` | **0.2 / 0.1 / 0.1%** | **99.0 / 99.8 / 99.8%** |
  | **2.1.139** | per-request `cch` | **0.2 / 0.1 / 0.1%** | **99.1 / 99.8 / 99.9%** |
  | **2.1.179** | per-request `cch` | **0.2 / 0.1 / 0.1%** | **98.6 / 99.9 / 99.9%** |
  | 2.1.181 | no `cch` | 98.5 / 99.9 / 99.9% | 98.4 / 99.9 / 99.9% |
  | 2.1.286 | no `cch` | 99.8 / 99.9 / 99.9% | 99.7 / 99.9 / 99.9% |

  On base, the versions with a per-request `cch` reuse only the 32 tokens before the header on every turn. With this PR they reuse the whole previous turn, the same as versions whose header doesn't change. The 2.1.75 turn-2 miss happens on both builds and is client-side: that version inserts an "# Output efficiency" section into the system prompt after the first turn, and from turn 3 on the cache hits again. The 65.2% for 2.1.112 on base occurred once in turn 2; that version's header is the constant `cch=00000`; the same turn with this PR, and turns 3–4 on base, are at 99%+.
- Render: with the fix each turn starts with the previous turn's whole prompt; without it only the 237 tokens before the header match (1.5% of the previous prompt).
- Canary, 8 turns with the fix: 29.8K of 158.8K prompt tokens computed, reuse after turn 1 87.9%. Without it each turn shares only those 237 tokens with the cache, so nearly the whole 158.8K is computed.
- Production, prefill engines: prefix-cache reuse 79.8% -> 95.6%, computed tokens per prompt token 0.20 -> 0.044 (30 min before vs 16 min after, same fleet and config otherwise).

On this path the model no longer sees the billing line, which matches `/v1/messages` since #36829.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
author: amd-sriram
body:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

On ROCm native decode is used for `next_n` 1 and 2 today, so MTP with one speculative token goes through this path. #59421 raises that cap, which needs this fix.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mqa_context_lens.py` (new): the helper returns the per-sequence lengths for a `(B, next_n)` table and passes `[B]` / `(B, 1)` through unchanged.
- Direct call of `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` on one MI355X against a torch reference: `B=4`, `next_n=3`, contexts 8192/1500/3000/700, block size 64.

## Test Result

| Gluon | Rows correct | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| This PR | 12/12 | max rel diff 2.4e-7 |
| Before | 9/12 | the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row |

With this fix, GLM-5.3 MTP at `next_n=3` and `next_n=5` completes the full throughput sweep, GPQA (0.889 / 0.904) and RULER niah_single_2 (1.0 / 1.0).


| next_n (spec tokens) | GPQA | NIAH | Geomean tok/s/GPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| no MTP | 0.879 | 1.00 | 2435.5 |
| 3 (2) | 0.889 | 1.00 | 3309.1 |
| 5 (4) | 0.904 | 1.00 | 3607.8 |

Throughput per GPU:

| Conc | 8k/1k no MTP | 8k/1k n=3 | 8k/1k n=5 | 60k/600 no MTP | 60k/600 n=3 | 60k/600 n=5 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 544.4 | 1105.3 | 1337.0 | 2925.1 | 4067.3 | 4422.3 |
| 8 | 897.5 | 1650.6 | 2015.3 | 3889.2 | 4658.8 | 4408.6 |
| 16 | 1415.4 | 2177.6 | 2648.5 | 4550.6 | 4948.6 | 5050.4 |
| 32 | 2058.7 | 3061.8 | 3638.4 | 4938.2 | 5175.0 | 5303.4 |
| 64 | 2853.3 | 4013.9 | 4447.8 | | | |
| 128 | 3741.3 | 4715.5 | 4291.3 | | | |
| 256 | 4603.2 | 4663.6 | 5208.6 | | | |

The no-MTP run is the same setup without speculative decoding (decode paged MQA logits on the FlyDSL kernel instead of Gluon).

title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Keep discovery heartbeats running while workers hold the GIL
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Keep MoRIIO discovery registration alive during worker GIL holds and temporary
router outages. Report unexpected heartbeat subprocess exit through worker
completion polling. This independent fix was extracted from #58968, which no
longer contains the implementation; it has no dependency on the K3 data path.

## Claims

```text
rank-0 worker -> heartbeat subprocess -> unchanged MessagePack registration
  temporary send timeout -> retry until the worker exits
  unexpected child exit -> worker get_finished() raises with its exit code
  worker shutdown / parent pipe EOF -> stop and reap the child
```

## Validation

- **Before:** main's actual threaded sender fails the 300 ms GIL-hold test.
  At pre-review HEAD `512a877511`, the new router-outage test fails to resume
  registration; killing the child or ending its input pipe leaves worker
  completion polling silent (**3 failed**).
- **After:** **46 passed, 0 skipped** across the existing proxy-routing and
  MoRIIO TP-ACK suites. Tests use real subprocesses and loopback ZeroMQ for
  GIL independence, initial registration, router disappearance until the send
  queue times out, registration after the router returns, parent death,
  repeated shutdown, and propagation of both signal and zero-code child exits.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy 3.10, and manual mypy 3.12 passed.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_heartbeat.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_heartbeat.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_proxy_routing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py
```

Validation covers process and worker lifecycle on CPU. No model-output,
accuracy, throughput, or end-to-end model-serving result is claimed for this
isolated control-plane change.

## Details

The finite retry limit previously treated ZeroMQ send timeouts during temporary
disconnection as terminal. Those timeouts now retry for the worker lifetime;
other repeated ZMQ errors still terminate the child. The parent previously
never inspected child status. It now checks on each worker completion poll,
including unexpected exit code zero. An idle worker observes a fatal child
exit when it next polls; this does not introduce a background restart manager.

**Door:** Two-way. Reverting restores the threaded sender without changing the
discovery wire format. **Blast radius:** MoRIIO workers with a discovery proxy.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, extraction and PR preparation.

---

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Scoped changes; pre-commit and mypy passed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes cause, before/after evidence, reproduction commands and limitations.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Load PLE tables unquantized under Quark checkpoints
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose

`amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` no longer loads on `main`. Fail at model construction:

```text
NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config QuarkConfig
```

`Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config` handles `None`, FP8 and the ModelOpt configs, and raises for everything else. It came in with #57497 (PLE n-gram table CPU offload). Before that, the Quark checkpoint served normally, for example on `nightly-cd10ed6f9`.

Quark quantizes only Linear and MoE layers, and this checkpoint's PLE shards (`ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding.shard_*.weight`) are BF16 with no scales. So under a `QuarkConfig` the table is unquantized, and this PR returns `Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`.

`test_ple_embedding_is_unquantized_under_quark` covers the new branch. The existing rejection test, for NVFP4 and online FP8, is unchanged.

---

## Test Plan

- Hardware: MI355X (gfx950)

- Serving: `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`, TP2, the model-card recipe, and GSM8K 5-shot (chat template, thinking off), on the latest ROCm nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-18f8f96025` with only this PR applied

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Size the KV cache from the groups HiSparse allocates
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

With HiSparse, a GPU pool too small for one `max_model_len` request passes the startup check, and requests then wait forever with no error ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55398#issuecomment-5903470382): `--num-gpu-blocks-override 160`, two 6k prompts never run).

The startup check sized HiSparse from the model's grouped specs rather than the groups HiSparse actually allocates. So it counted only indexer pages, missing the resident and hot groups, and used the wrong block size for the override.

## Changes

- HiSparse's grouping hook now returns the groups it allocates, and workers report its derived resident/hot caches. The standard startup check, override conversion and cross-rank sync then work for HiSparse unchanged.
- KV cache layout resolution skips specs without per-layer views, such as these caches, which lay out their own raw backing.
- Resident groups are sized by their admission window (`max_admission_blocks_per_request`), which #59494 now enforces at runtime.
- Auto-fit uses the startup check's criterion, so it can't pick a length that check rejects.
- Removed the HiSparse-specific memory estimate and the cross-worker `min(available_memory)` workaround.
- Projection returns a group unchanged when all its layers are on the worker, so HiSparse's group flags survive.

A pool that can't hold one request now fails the standard "max seq len" check at startup, before KV cache allocation.

## Test Plan

- Unit test: a 160-block pool is rejected at `max_model_len=8192`, and the boundary is exact at 32768 with 2048 tokens in flight (656 blocks rejected, 657 accepted). Auto-fit with 657 blocks starts. Layout resolution is unaffected by the derived caches.
- B200 (shrunk GLM-5.3, dummy weights), on this branch merged with #59494: TP=1 and TP=2 including ranks with unequal memory, 131k context, auto-fit, the reported setup, and `test_hisparse.py`.

## Test Result

- Unit tests pass.
- B200, this branch (includes #59494):
  - Too-small pools fail at startup: 160 blocks at 8192, 2400 blocks at 131072.
  - Pools that fit serve: 1000 blocks at 8192, auto-fit, and 3200 or 4000 blocks at 131072 with a 120k-token prompt. Without #59494, the 4000-block case livelocks.
  - TP=2 serves, including with unequal ranks.
  - The reported setup at 700 blocks: both 6k prompts complete.
  - `test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Use a zero default for masked scales in the MXFP8 GEMM
author: cagrikymk
body:
## Purpose

This fix changes masked scale data from 127 (value 1.0 for e8m0) to 0 (value 2^(-127). This change is benign in terms of accuracy as the main value side already loads corresponding lanes for mfma as 0. So, scales get multiplied by 0 and has no accuracy effect.

When other=127, triton 3.8.0+gitc0a142ff leads to reading stale LDS data for the lanes corresponding to the masked scales due to a compiler bug. This bug is fixed on upstream triton but this fix resolves stale data reading issue for both compiler versions.

With other=127 and triton 3.8.0+gitc0a142ff, if LDS addresses corresponding to the masked lanes have "NaN", this leads to the result and produce inaccurate results. This is a rare case but it can still happen in practice. Reproduction relies on what LDS contains from previous runs.

This is a cleaner solution as hardware can already handle writing 0s to the masked lanes almost for free compared to writing any other value.

title: [Bugfix] Bind routed-experts capture to the MoE layer, not the kernel
author: erictang000
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59449. With `enable_return_routed_experts`, the FLASHINFER_TRTLLM (monolithic) MoE path returns stale `routed_experts` after a layerwise weight reload, which every full-weight RL sync performs.

**Root cause.**
- The capture callback carries a `layer_id`, so it has the lifetime of the layer.
- It was bound to the kernel's `fused_experts` instance, whose lifetime is a single weight version: FP8 `process_weights_after_loading` builds a new kernel on every reload.
- The new kernel has no callback, so the capturer keeps the rows from before the reload.
- The router-side path does not have this bug, because it binds to the router, which lives as long as the layer.

**Fix: give the state to its owner, then pass it explicitly.**
- `RoutedExpertsSink` holds the preallocated int16 replay buffer and the callback. `bind_routed_experts_capturer` creates it once and stores it on the layer as `RoutedExperts.routing_sink`.
- Every quant method's `apply_monolithic` passes `routing_sink=layer.routing_sink`, the same route `e_score_correction_bias` and `expert_map` already take.
- `FusedMoEKernel.apply_monolithic` takes `routing_sink` as a required keyword. A method that forgets it fails mypy (or raises `TypeError` out of tree) instead of silently dropping capture.
- `FusedMoEKernelMonolithicImpl.apply` hands the batch's rows of the sink buffer to the experts as a plain `routing_replay_out` output tensor, then passes the same rows to the sink's callback. FlashInfer already rejects a replay buffer shorter than the batch.
- The experts hold no capture state: `set_capture_fn` and the replay-buffer helpers are removed, so a rebuilt kernel has nothing to lose.
- The buffer address is fixed for the layer's lifetime, so CUDA graphs captured before a reload keep writing to a valid buffer.
- Capability is checked on every call. A reload that switches to a kernel without replay support raises instead of returning stale routing.

**API note.** Out-of-tree code that calls `FusedMoEKernel.apply_monolithic` directly must now pass `routing_sink` (use `None` when not capturing).

## Test Plan

- Unit tests:
  - For the trtllm bf16, fp8 block and nvfp4 kernels, under both Renormalize and DeepSeekV3 routing: the router logits plant an unambiguous top-k, and `routing_replay_out` must report exactly those experts and nothing past the batch.
  - Capture follows each rebuilt kernel through the real `FusedMoEKernelMonolithicImpl`, and a rebuild to an unsupported kernel raises.
  - Binding gives the layer the sink; the sink holds a full DP/EP-gathered batch.
  - Mutation checks: dropping the capture in the impl fails the rebuild test, and dropping `routing_sink=` from any quant method fails mypy (`Missing named argument "routing_sink"`).
- End-to-end state-transition oracle (aoshen02/vllm-state-transition-verifier):
  - Setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 on FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, weights updated over the NCCL weight-transfer engine.
  - Each request is a 1024-token single-forward probe. The run alternates a scored prompt Q with a prime P, so stale capture would return P's routing.
  - Transitions: no update, lifecycle only, identity reload, reload to an expert-relabelled copy σA, and back to A.
  - Every step on A must match the first probe bit for bit.
  - Afterwards, 16 concurrent decodes replay FULL CUDA graphs captured before the reloads.

## Test Result

GB300, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (gac68c3087, digest `b5406fca`), with this PR's files synced in and sha-checked:
- **Unit tests:** 259 passed, 36 skipped across `tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py`, `test_fp8_tp_loading.py`, `test_flashinfer.py` and `test_ocp_mx_moe.py`.
- **mypy:** clean over the whole repository.
- **State-transition oracle** (49,152 routing rows per probe), run on 6995f55, which has the same runtime path (the only later change to it is the required-keyword signature):

| step | nightly | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| no update | identical | identical |
| pause/resume only | identical | identical |
| identity reload | 48,946 rows differ, **all equal to the previous request's routing (stale buffer)** | identical |
| A → σA → A reload | same stale rows | identical |
| decode under FULL CUDA graphs after the reloads | valid | valid |

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Report the real cause when the worker outgrows its memory reservation
author: mosafariuk
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59471.

When the CPU worker's own footprint (model weights plus runtime) exceeds the memory reserved by `--gpu-memory-utilization`, `CPUWorker.determine_available_memory` computes a negative KV cache budget. That case shared the "available < requested" error, which printed the negative size and told users to reduce memory used by other processes, the opposite of the fix:

```
ValueError: Available memory on node 0 (1.34/8.0 GiB) on kv cache allocation is less than requested memory for kv (-0.6/0.16 GiB). Reduce CPU memory used by other processes.
```

This PR splits the two conditions:

- **Worker outgrew its reservation** (`requested_memory_for_kv <= 0`): a new error states the footprint and the reservation, and points to what actually works. That is a larger `--gpu-memory-utilization`, with the smallest fraction that could fit, or an explicit `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` / `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`. The wording follows #42479's CPU messages.
- **Node short of free memory** (`requested_memory_for_kv > available_memory`): the existing error is unchanged.

Only the error path changes. When the budget fits, sizing and startup behave exactly as before, and nothing runs after startup.

**Not a duplicate.** No open issue or PR covers this branch. #42479 reworded the neighbouring CPU memory errors (the startup check in this file, and two in `kv_cache_utils.py`) but not this one. Among open PRs touching `cpu_worker.py`, #51876 changes only `__init__`, with no overlap.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py`, CPU-only, no model. It covers three cases:
  - the worker outgrew its reservation: the new error with the right remedy, no negative size and no "other processes" advice;
  - the node is short of memory: the existing message still fires;
  - the budget fits: the KV size equals the reservation minus the footprint.
- Real engine on the CPU backend: `LLM(model="HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M", dtype="float32", gpu_memory_utilization=0.02)` on `main` and on this branch.

## Test Result

Unit tests, this branch:
```
PASSED tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py::test_footprint_above_reservation_asks_for_a_larger_reservation
PASSED tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py::test_short_node_memory_still_asks_to_free_memory
PASSED tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py::test_budget_that_fits_sizes_the_kv_cache
3 passed
```
The same file against unmodified `main`: only the first test fails, so the other two paths are untouched.
```
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py::test_footprint_above_reservation_asks_for_a_larger_reservation
1 failed, 2 passed
```

Real engine (macOS 27.0, Apple M1, 8 GiB, CPU backend built from `main` `fc2c801ad9`), `gpu_memory_utilization=0.02`:

- `main`:
  ```
  ValueError: Available memory on node 0 (1.34/8.0 GiB) on kv cache allocation is less than requested memory for kv (-0.6/0.16 GiB). Reduce CPU memory used by other processes.
  ```
- this branch:
  ```
  ValueError: The worker already uses 0.64 GiB (model weights and runtime), more than the 0.16 GiB of CPU memory reserved for it on node 0, leaving none for the KV cache. On the CPU backend, the `--gpu-memory-utilization` flag controls the fraction of CPU memory reserved (despite its name). To resolve: increase `--gpu-memory-utilization` to more than 0.09, or set the KV cache size explicitly with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` or VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE.
  ```

Separately observed, and identical with and without this change: on this machine the engine process sometimes does not exit after this worker startup error (2/2 runs on each side hung past a 240 s timeout; an earlier run on `main` exited promptly). This PR does not touch shutdown.

`pre-commit` on both files: ruff check and format, typos, mypy, SPDX and the remaining hooks passed. `check-test-tethering` and `check-root-lazy-imports` also pass when run with Python 3.12. The new test sits in `tests/v1/worker/`, which the `v1-executor-worker` job runs as a directory.

No model evaluation: the change only affects an error raised before the engine starts, so no model output changes.

title: [Bugfix][Tokenizer] Fix off-by-one max_token_id from vocab_size
author: shijie-lyu
body:
## Purpose

Fixes an off-by-one in `get_cached_tokenizer`'s `max_token_id`. Reported as GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4; the VMT rated it moderate and asked for a public PR.

`max_token_id` is the largest valid token id, inclusive:

- `InputProcessor._validate_model_input` rejects prompt ids above `max(tokenizer.max_token_id, model_vocab_size - 1)`.
- `SamplingParams` rejects `token_id > tokenizer.max_token_id` and reports the vocab size as `max_token_id + 1`.
- `MistralTokenizer` sets `_max_token_id = vocab_size - 1`, and `KimiAudioTokenizer` returns `n_vocab - 1`.

`vllm/tokenizers/hf.py` instead takes `max(max(get_vocab().values()), tokenizer.vocab_size)`. `vocab_size` is a count, so for tokenizers whose largest id is `vocab_size - 1` (Llama-2 family, GPT-2, ...) it returns `vocab_size`, one past the last id.

For a model whose embedding has exactly `vocab_size` rows (32000 is a multiple of the 64-row padding, so Llama-2-family models get no padding rows), a prompt containing id `vocab_size` passes the engine's check. At TP=1 the embedding does not mask the index, and the lookup fails with a CUDA device-side assert.

The fix uses `vocab_size - 1`. `max(get_vocab().values())` stays the primary source, so tokenizers whose added tokens sit above `vocab_size` (e.g. Qwen2.5) are unchanged.

| Tokenizer | `max_token_id` before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 (vocab 32000) | 32000 | 31999 |
| openai-community/gpt2 (vocab 50257) | 50257 | 50256 |
| Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | 151664 | 151664 |

I found no open PR for this.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/tokenizers_/
pytest -v tests/test_sampling_params.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py tests/benchmarks/test_sampling_params.py
pytest -v tests/entrypoints/llm/test_prompt_validation.py

pytest -v tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_logit_bias_validation.py
pytest -v tests/v1/sample/test_sampling_params_e2e.py
```

## Test Result

1x NVIDIA A10G, torch 2.13, this diff on main cff08b461e.

- `tests/tokenizers_/` with and without the fix: 0 failures with the fix. The only failure without it is the new test. Both runs also have errors in the Mistral and Pixtral tests (gated repos and HF 429s on this machine); which of those error varies from run to run, and none outside that group.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix a chunked-prefill preemption livelock
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fix a HiSparse prefill livelock: a long chunked prefill can be preempted and recomputed from token 0 forever, with no progress and no error.

Two things combine:

1. **The prefill outgrows the pool it was admitted into.** Admission caps each request's resident pages at the in-flight window (`HiSparseResidentSpec.max_admission_blocks_per_request`), assuming older pages move to host. At runtime, a request keeps its resident pages pinned until free GPU blocks fall below a fixed watermark (a tenth of the pool). A chunk that needs more than that is never switched to host reads, so the request is preempted.
2. **The preempted request resumes from nothing.** Host pages were only published once the **whole** computed prefix was durable. Host writes trail a chunked prefill by about a chunk, so nothing was published until the prefill ended. The request found no prefix hit, recomputed from 0, and was preempted at the same point again.

## Changes

`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`:
- Publish the durable prefix of a pending publication as it becomes durable (`min(computed tokens, ready pages)`), instead of all-or-nothing. A preempted prefill resumes from it. When the whole prefix is durable this publishes exactly what it did before.
- `update_residency` also switches a request to host reads (asks for a hot region, then releases its written-back pages) once its resident pages fill the window admission reserved for it. Runtime then enforces the assumption admission makes, so these preemptions no longer happen.

`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`: `max_admission_blocks_per_request` becomes public so the coordinator can read it; `HiSparseResidentManager` declares it as `int` (always set for resident specs). No behavior change.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_preempted_prefill_resumes_from_durable_prefix`: chunk 1's writes are acked after chunk 2 is allocated, then the request is preempted; the resumed request must hit chunk 1's pages.
- New `test_hisparse_prefill_reads_host_once_it_fills_admission_window[4-True, 3-False]`: a prefill that fills its admission window requests a hot region while free blocks are still above the watermark; one below it does not.
- `test_hisparse_terminal_prefix_waits_for_all_workers_and_preserves_identity` now expects the page every worker finished writing to be published (it previously pinned all-or-nothing publication).
- Engine repro on H100: shrunk DeepSeek-V3.2 (8 layers: indexer + 8 resident groups share the GPU pool), 8192-token chunks, eager.
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`; HiSparse unit tests across `tests/v1` (`-k hisparse`).

## Test Result

| Repro | main | publication fix only | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1×120k prompt, 4000 blocks | livelock (250 preemptions, stuck at 24576 tokens) | 35 steps, 1 preemption | 32 steps, 0 preemptions |
| 1×120k prompt, 12000 blocks | livelock (125 preemptions, stuck at 81920) | 26 steps, 1 preemption | 23 steps, 0 preemptions |
| 2×60k prompts, 4000 blocks | livelock (333 preemptions) | 40 steps, 2 preemptions | 34 steps, 0 preemptions |
| 3×40k prompts, 6000 blocks | 35 steps, 2 preemptions | 29 steps, 2 preemptions | 24 steps, 0 preemptions |
| 1×120k, 1024-token chunks | 126 steps | 126 steps | 126 steps |

- Each new test fails without its fix. `test_prefix_caching.py` passes on CPU.
- H100: `test_hisparse.py` 4 passed; HiSparse unit tests 169 passed.

title: [Bugfix] Keep batch-invariance NCCL pins out of the weight-transfer group
author: guanxingithub
body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` pins `NCCL_ALGO`, `NCCL_PROTO`, the channel count and a few related variables in the worker's environment. NCCL never reconciles these across ranks. An external trainer that does not carry them therefore deadlocks with the workers in the warm-up `all_reduce` of the weight-transfer group, or a worker fails with `ncclInternalError`.

The pins only matter for vLLM's own collectives, so this PR keeps them out of the communicators shared with the trainer:

- `vllm.utils.nccl.pin_nccl_env(pins)` sets the pins and records the values they replace. It also lists the pins in `NCCL_NO_CACHE`, so NCCL re-reads them for each communicator instead of caching the first value. `override_envs_for_invariance` now pins its NCCL settings through it.
- `vllm.utils.nccl.unpinned_nccl_env()` restores the launch values while `stateless_init_process_group` / `uid_init_process_group` create the trainer-facing communicator, then puts the pins back. Every NCCL weight-transfer engine creates its group through these two functions.
- `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE` stays a plain process-wide setting, because NCCL keeps it in a global.
- On ROCm, or when the NCCL library vLLM loads is older than 2.29.7 or cannot be loaded, there is no `NCCL_NO_CACHE`, so nothing is lifted. In that case vLLM logs a warning, once, when a shared communicator is built.

The trainer needs no change. The transfer group uses the environment both sides were launched with, as for any NCCL group. Copying vLLM's pins into the trainer is no longer needed and would now cause a mismatch. If `NCCL_ALGO`, `NCCL_PROTO` or the channel limits are set only in an `nccl.conf` file rather than exported, the worker cannot see them when it restores the launch values, so export them instead.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py`. `test_nccl_weight_transfer_between_processes` gains a `batch-invariant-worker` case: the worker applies the pins and builds a pinned NCCL communicator first, as vLLM's own groups do; the trainer stays unpinned.
- End-to-end on 4x GB300, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (NCCL 2.29.7), Qwen3-0.6B:
  - The server runs `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with TP2, and separately with PP2.
  - An unmodified external trainer, with no batch-invariance env, runs 3 rounds of `pause → NCCL weight update → resume`. Each round sends 1.5 GB.
  - Before and after every round, one prompt is sent alone and inside a batch of 16, and the tokens and logprobs are compared.

## Test Result

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `batch-invariant-worker` test | times out (deadlock) | passes |
| same test with the `NCCL_NO_CACHE` line removed from this PR | — | fails, so the test depends on the mechanism |
| `test_weight_transfer.py` on 2 GPUs | — | all passed |
| e2e TP2 / PP2 | all ranks hang in the warm-up `ncclAllReduce` | 3/3 rounds each; batch invariance holds and outputs are identical before and after |

NCCL INFO logs on the worker show vLLM's TP communicators at 1 channel before and after the transfer group is built. The transfer group uses NCCL defaults on all ranks.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Exempt exactly the blocks an async KV load writes from zeroing
author: ivanium
body:
## Overview

Prevent allocator zeroing from racing async KV loads, including sliding-window blocks below a local prefix hit and circular-buffer blocks at index 0. Keep zeroing enabled for groups the selected connector does not load.

## Claims

- Exempt newly allocated external blocks in exactly the groups declared by the connector; synchronous loads still zero before loading.
- Introduce `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids(request)`, moved from #59197: prefix-cacheable groups by default, all transfer groups for NIXL/Mooncake P/D, and request-selected delegation for MultiConnector. #59197 consumes the same API for replay decisions.

## Validation

- Final unit run: 649 passed, 4 GPU/integration cases excluded by the command below. The two GPU setup cases were also exercised separately.
- Two GPU setup cases initially hit concurrent memory profiling failures; both passed when rerun sequentially on a separate GPU. The async failure fixture now declares its loaded group.
- Pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy passed. Tests cover store/P/D group selection, async/sync zeroing, KpoolTail allocation, MultiConnector routing, replay and failure recovery.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \

pre-commit run --files <changed-files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed-python-files>
```

</details>

Earlier end-to-end results, collected before this API move: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D with NIXL, 1P1D TP4 + TP4, two-pass GSM8K 5-shot, concurrency 512. Pass 2 includes decode-side prefix hits. “Other wrong” excludes prompts with N % 32 == 31 (#59330); “t < 16” counts those with (N - 1) % 128 < 16. These model evaluations were not rerun for the API refactor.

| Build | Pass 1 | Pass 2 | Other wrong | t < 16 |

| main | 0.9174 / 0.9249 | 0.9219 / 0.9189 | 98 / 101 | 18 / 15 |
| #59330 + #59197 | 0.9234 | 0.9113 | 113 | 20 |

## Details

Store/offloading connectors retain zeroing for their excluded scratch/window groups.

Failed-load recovery is unchanged: multi-group loads free and retry; single-group partial failures re-record the unwritten suffix. Tests cover async/sync loads with and without the window, circular-buffer zeroing, and MultiConnector selection.

Not a duplicate: #59197 uses this shared contract to skip replay; #59164 concerns synchronous MoRIIO READ destinations; #55085 handles unwritten Mooncake Store tail pages; #52187 concerns worker-side per-group zeroing.

title: [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
author: ivanium
body:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block `> 0`.
- Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes `_make_block_table` in the AMD pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. For the kpool tail, the existing CPU padding test now ends with a padding request on the null block, and the existing Triton-vs-CPU test adds a mixed batch and an all-null dummy batch. Both check that the null-block request maps to PAD.

## Not a duplicate

- #58560 covers only the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.
- #57158 zeroes block 0 after capture. That does not cover DP idle-rank dummy batches during serving.
- #57169 and #59297 move the kpool tail onto `CircularBufferSpec` / the packed layout but keep its slot kernel unchanged.
- #54296 masks out-of-range block indices in the generic slot mapping kernel, which neither ring uses.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- Rebased on main `d6fe5dca68`. 102 passed, 16 skipped on GB200. The 16 skips are `test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py`, which requires ROCm.
- Control: with the QSA change reverted, the dummy-batch check fails: dummy tokens map to real slots in block 0.
- Control: with the kpool tail change reverted, the CPU padding test and the two null-block Triton cases fail.
- `pre-commit` passes.
- No model eval. Only tokens of requests on the null block change, and those are dummy or padding rows whose outputs are discarded. Real requests never own block 0 (`BlockPool` pops it as the null block at init), so their mappings and outputs are unchanged.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. The submitter reviewed the changes and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Bench] Clean up synthetic video files and writers
author: Prudhvivuda
body:
## Overview

Fix unbounded temporary-file accumulation when `random-mm` benchmarks generate synthetic videos. Clean up the MP4 after reading its bytes and release the OpenCV writer when initialization or frame encoding fails.

## Claims

- Successful video generation leaves no temporary files behind.
- Failed writer initialization and frame writes release the writer and remove temporary storage while preserving the error.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_random_multimodal_dataset_video.py -v`: **13 passed** on macOS ARM64, Python 3.12.11, OpenCV 5.0.0. The three cleanup regression cases failed on the original implementation and pass with this fix.
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py tests/benchmarks/test_random_multimodal_dataset_video.py`: **passed**.
- CPU before/after reproduction with seed 42: three 320×240, 16-frame videos left **2,111,976 bytes in three files** before the fix, and zero afterward. A subsequent 1280×720, 16-frame video added **7,501,136 bytes** before the fix and left zero afterward. All four returned MP4 payloads were byte-identical between implementations and decoded to the expected dimensions and frame counts in this environment.
- Existing `benchmarks-cli-test` CI already runs this suite. Model evaluation is not applicable to this benchmark-client resource-lifecycle change; no model or serving validation is claimed. Local tests used CPU dependencies after the precompiled editable installation failed to fetch wheel metadata for baseline commit `31ec1c3` (HTTP 404).

## Details

`NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` persisted every generated MP4, and frame-writing exceptions skipped `VideoWriter.release()`. A `TemporaryDirectory` owns the encoding path, while `try/finally` releases the writer before reading or removing the file. RNG use, pixels, codec, FPS, and return format are unchanged. This adds no dependency or public API change.

This is a newly reproduced bug with no associated issue. Duplicate-work checks on 2026-09-30 found no competing open PR for `generate_synthetic_video`, `video tempfile`, `random-mm leak`, or `video temporary files`. All-state searches found the original video support (#25963) and optional OpenCV import change (#27780), neither of which addresses cleanup.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Keep GDN prefill checkpoint metadata local to each cache group
author: ai-jz
body:
## Overview

In the GLM-5.3-Flash configuration we tested with Model Runner V2 (MRV2) and prefix caching, later requests could return garbled output despite succeeding. A **checkpoint**—attention state saved for prefix reuse—could be written to the wrong cache page. Found while testing [providers-verifier](https://github.com/smg-project/providers-verifier).

## Claims

- The [two-line fix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L129-L139) makes checkpoint configurations use the runner's [existing per-group metadata construction](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py#L523-L548).
- Configurations without checkpoint blocks still reuse metadata.
- Prefix caching and GLM's internal prefill checkpoint optimization from #56960 remain enabled: a full prefill can save an intermediate checkpoint without an extra model forward when the token budget permits.

## Validation

### Minimal reproducible example

Each **KV cache group** has its own cache-page mapping. When switching groups, [`update_block_table()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L613-L661) updates the active-state page but retains the previous group's checkpoint page:

| Page for the next cache group | Expected | Actual |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Active state | `202` | `202` |
| Checkpoint | `222` | **`111`** |

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproducible example — CPU Python script</summary>

Requires a configured vLLM Python environment with Torch. No GPU or model weights are needed.

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.checkpoint import MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import (
    GDNAttentionMetadata,
    GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder,
)

builder = object.__new__(GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder)
builder.vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(
    cache_config=SimpleNamespace(mamba_cache_mode="align")
)
builder.use_full_cuda_graph = False
builder.mamba_aligned_state_indices = torch.tensor([[202]], dtype=torch.int32)
source = GDNAttentionMetadata(
    num_prefills=1, num_prefill_tokens=100,
    num_decodes=0, num_decode_tokens=0,
    num_spec_decodes=0, num_spec_decode_tokens=0, num_actual_tokens=100,
    checkpoint=MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata(
        torch.tensor([96], dtype=torch.int32),
        torch.tensor([111], dtype=torch.int32),
    ),
)
updated = builder.update_block_table(
    source, torch.tensor([[222, 202]], dtype=torch.int32), None
)
print(updated.non_spec_state_indices_tensor.tolist())  # [202]: correct
print(updated.checkpoint.state_indices.tolist())       # [111]: expected [222]
```

</details>

The script directly calls the unsafe method. The fix prevents the runner from using it for checkpoint configurations; the regression test verifies that check.

### Testing before and after the fix

We ran the same 46-request test plan against a running GLM-5.3-Flash server before and after the fix, using the same image and settings. Prefix caching stayed enabled.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| CPU regression: with/without checkpoint blocks | 1 passed, 1 failed | **2 passed** |
| Complete GDN metadata test file | Full baseline not rerun | **54 passed, 0 skipped** |
| GLM serving requests | **36/46** | **46/46** |

Nine original responses contained garbled output; none did after the fix. The remaining failure hit the output-token limit and is not attributed to this cache bug. These are selected checks; full qualification and performance were not evaluated. The current PR has CPU validation; serving tests used the earlier revision below. Pre-commit passed.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and detailed results</summary>

After the repository's [development setup](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/AGENTS.md#development-workflow), run from its root in Linux:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_cross_group_reuse_requires_no_prefill_checkpoint -q

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py -q
```

`FakeTensorMode` tests the CUDA reuse check without allocating CUDA buffers. The recorded container run used Python source `4ed438b79ceaff5fe5d6d4a98b09bfb8718cceaa`, Torch 2.13, and precompiled extensions from `ac68c3087215e0a4f3cdfa218508c6aada57235d`, via system Python and a pytest launcher combining that source with the image's extensions. No inference kernels ran. Relevant source/test files are unchanged in the refreshed PR base; commands above assume a standard developer installation.

| Serving requests | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 32K context probes | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| Short tool requests | 10/20 | 20/20 |
| Long tool requests | 20/20 | 20/20 |

The 46 requests repeat three selected cases across six phases using the verifier's sampling settings. Serving tests used `ac68c3087215e0a4f3cdfa218508c6aada57235d`; its update method matches the inspected PR base.

</details>

## Details

**Cost:** checkpoint configurations build extra metadata per group, including decode-only batches, and use the existing per-group gather instead of the aligned-index precompute. The end-to-end performance cost has not been measured.

**Scope:** [Kimi-K3's builder](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/42f1b0494f688005c4d6b5e1d601b3f502dfd97e/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py#L302-L316) is a subclass and [already excluded](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/42f1b0494f688005c4d6b5e1d601b3f502dfd97e/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L132-L133) from this reuse path. GLM's checkpoints from #56960 use the base GDN builder, so that exclusion did not protect them. The added checkpoint-block check protects any model using that same builder and feature, rather than checking for GLM by name.

**Related work:** the failure involves metadata reuse from #58762 and checkpoints from #56960. Draft #58851 proposes broader sharing; its coverage of this GLM failure is unverified. This fix is independent.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep heterogeneous-vocab draft models on Model Runner V1
author: nishantrevur
body:
## Purpose

Since #43091 (merged 2026-09-28) moved `draft_model` to Model Runner V2, a draft model with `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` (TLI, #38174) runs on V2 by default. The V2 draft-model speculator (`PlainDraftModelSpeculator`) has no `VocabMapping`, so the target's token ids are fed to the draft model and the draft's token ids are fed back to the target untranslated. Whenever the two vocabularies differ, that indexes past the smaller model's embedding table and the engine dies with a device-side assert. TLI on V2 is still listed as TBD in #47172.

This change reports heterogeneous-vocab drafting as unsupported on V2, so:

- by default the config falls back to Model Runner V1, where TLI is implemented, with the usual warning: `Model Runner V2 does not yet support heterogeneous-vocabulary draft models; using the V1 model runner instead.`
- with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, config validation fails with `Model Runner V2 does not yet support: heterogeneous-vocabulary draft models` instead of crashing later.

## Reproduction (main @ 9e6550bd0, 1x NVIDIA L4 per run, greedy, k=3)

```python
LLM(model=TARGET, speculative_config={
    "method": "draft_model", "model": DRAFT,
    "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "use_heterogeneous_vocab": True})
```

| Target (vocab) | Draft (vocab) | main, default (V2) | main, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | this PR, default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (151,936) | HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct (49,152) | crash: `index out of bounds: 0 <= tmp1 < 49152` in the draft's embedding | runs, mean AL 1.88 | falls back to V1, mean AL 1.88 |
| HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct (49,152) | Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (151,936) | crash: `index out of bounds: 0 <= tmp1 < 49152` in the target's embedding | runs, mean AL 2.37, outputs identical to no-spec on 8/8 prompts | falls back to V1, mean AL 2.37 |
| Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, no TLI | V2, mean AL 3.19 | | unchanged, V2, mean AL 3.19 |

The crash surfaces as `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered` in EngineCore; with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the assert is the embedding bounds check shown above.

## Not duplicating existing work

Searched open issues and PRs for `use_heterogeneous_vocab`, `heterogeneous vocab`, `TLI`, and `universal draft`. Related open PRs are orthogonal and touch only the V1 path: #51564 (rejects TLI with `use_local_argmax_reduction`), #54780 (tokenizer revisions in the TLI mapping, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/draft_model.py`), and #45018 (SLEM, a different heterogeneous-vocab algorithm, also V1-only). None changes runner selection. #43091 does not reference the flag.

## Test plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -q
# 406 passed, 5 skipped, 3 failed (pre-existing: gated meta-llama models, fail identically on main)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -q -k heterogeneous_vocab
# 2 passed (the True case fails without this change)
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/vllm.py tests/test_config.py
```

New test: `test_v2_model_runner_heterogeneous_vocab_draft_falls_back_to_v1`.

## Follow-up

Porting TLI to the V2 draft-model speculator (the "TLI (universal draft): TBD" item in #47172). Happy to take that on if nobody else is.

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and draft this change; every line was reviewed and the tests and reproductions were run by the submitter.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix ROCM_ATTN sliding-window boundary
author: tangzzycc
body:
## Purpose

`ROCM_ATTN` stores the decoder window as `(W - 1, 0)`, where `W - 1` is the left span. The underlying [decode](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py#L234) and [prefix-prefill](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/prefix_prefill.py#L435) kernels use `query_position - key_position < SLIDING_WINDOW`, so their argument must be the total window length `W`, including the current token. Passing `W - 1` excludes the oldest valid token; for `W=1`, passing zero disables the window entirely.

This PR passes `1 + self.sliding_window[0]` to `chunked_prefill_paged_decode`. This matches the existing [KV-cache docstring example](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L1160): with `sliding_window=4` and seven computed tokens, the next token at position 7 must attend to tokens **4–7**. The old argument is 3 and attends to **5–7**; the corrected argument is 4 and attends to **4–7**.

`TRITON_ATTN` [stores the same `(W - 1, 0)` tuple](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py#L511) and already passes [`SLIDING_WINDOW=(1 + window_size[0])`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py#L1133). Applying the same conversion makes the causal window boundaries consistent between the two backends. The no-window sentinel maps to zero, which the helper treats as disabled; encoder attention uses a separate path.

Open-PR searches on 2026-10-01 found no duplicate. Related #49588, #53628, and #59132 do not modify this backend argument conversion.

## Test Plan

Run the focused backend regression and the existing cached-KV boundary test:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py \
  -k 'rocm_backend_sliding_window or cached_kv_block_table_boundary' -q
```

## Test Result

Before the fix, all four windowed regression cases fail and both no-window controls pass. After the fix: **7 passed**, including the existing boundary test. All applicable pre-commit checks passed.

Gemma3 1B IT (BF16, window 512) completed inference on Radeon 890M (`gfx1150`) with inputs within and beyond the window, including chunked prefill and HIP graph decode. Compared before/after ROCM_ATTN with TRITON_ATTN and Transformers FP32. Before/after prompt logprobs were identical for input lengths up to 512; longer inputs showed changes, with errors against the reference implementations increasing or decreasing depending on input length.

AI assistance was used during implementation, testing, and preparation of this PR. vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill was used to review the change.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Check reused prompt token ids against the vocab before streaming
author: shijie-lyu
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #55771, from @NickLucche's review: check that the reused `kv_transfer_params["prompt_token_ids"]` are inside the vocabulary when the prompt is rendered.

Today only `InputProcessor._validate_model_input` checks the vocab bound. With `stream=true` it runs after the stream is returned, so an out-of-vocabulary reused id comes back as an error event inside a 200 response, and `_with_kv_transfer_rejection_cleanup` does not notify the KV connector. The prefill KV then stays held until its lease expires.

Changes:

- `vllm/renderers/base.py`: the engine's vocab check moves into `BaseRenderer.validate_token_ids(token_ids, *, parameter=None)`. The bound (`max(tokenizer.max_token_id, model_vocab_size - 1)`), the negative-id check, the error messages and the "skipped without a tokenizer" rule are unchanged.
- `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py`: `_validate_model_input` calls `self.renderer.validate_token_ids(prompt_ids)`. Behaviour is unchanged for generate, embedding and pooling requests.
- `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py`: `_reused_prompt_token_ids` calls the same helper after its malformed-id check, with `parameter="kv_transfer_params.prompt_token_ids"`. The 400 is raised at render time inside `_with_kv_transfer_rejection_cleanup`, so no stream is opened and the connector is notified, the same path #55771 exercised on a NIXL 1P1D setup for malformed ids. This covers chat (HF and Harmony) and non-Harmony `/v1/responses`.

One helper means the engine and the renderer check cannot drift apart. It is independent of #59491, which fixes `max_token_id` itself; the test uses id 999999.

Not changed: other checks that only run in the engine (for example `bad_words` ids, or out-of-vocab ids in a `/v1/completions` token prompt) still fail after the stream opens under `stream=true`, without notifying the connector. A general fix would notify on pre-admission rejection in `AsyncLLM.generate`; I'm happy to do that separately.

I found no open PR for this.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids
pytest -v tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py -k kv_transfer
pytest -v tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
pytest -v tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py
pytest -v tests/entrypoints/llm/test_prompt_validation.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_prompt_validation.py tests/v1/sample/test_sampling_params_e2e.py
pytest -v tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py -k "negative or vocab or invalid"
```

`test_chat_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_rejection_notifies_kv_connector` gains an out-of-vocab case with `stream=true`, which fails without this change.

## Test Result

1x NVIDIA A10G, torch 2.13, this diff on main 51048b13ce.

- Chat reuse tests: 21 passed. Responses and batch reuse tests: 7 passed. `tests/test_request_input_bounds.py`: 39 passed.
- Full `test_serving_chat.py` and `test_serving_responses.py`, engine path (`LLM` and completion prompt validation, sampling-params e2e) and embeddings negative id: 249, 62 and 1 passed on the first revision of this change. The source is unchanged since; review only folded two new tests into the existing one.
- With the render-time call removed, the new out-of-vocab case fails.
- `pre-commit` ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, check-spdx-header and `mypy-3.10`: passed.

title: [DP] Engines own wave wake-ups; drop the front-end FIRST_REQ
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Fix a DP hang and simplify DP wave control. After this change, the engines alone start DP waves, and the front-end no longer sends `FIRST_REQ`.

**The bug.** Before this change, a front-end sent `FIRST_REQ` whenever it believed the engines were idle. The coordinator then broadcast `START_DP_WAVE`, and the rank that received the request assumed its peers had been woken. That assumption fails when a peer is still paused, because a paused rank drops `START_DP_WAVE`. With two API servers A and B and two ranks X and Y, all paused:

1. B sends an ADD to X and a `FIRST_REQ` to the coordinator.
2. The coordinator sends `START_DP_WAVE` to Y. Y is still paused and drops it.
3. A resumes both ranks. Neither rank has work, so both stay idle.
4. B's ADD reaches X. Its wave is current, so X does not announce, steps alone, and blocks in the DP collective forever.

Nothing orders these three sockets (B→X, coordinator→Y, A→X/Y). The same false assumption ("a sent wake took effect") was removed from the coordinator in #51481.

**The fix, from first principles.** Only the rank that is about to step knows it is about to step. So an idle, unpaused rank that receives a request now always announces `start_wave`. The coordinator already deduplicates these announcements and broadcasts to the other ranks. With that in place, the front-end wake carries no correctness role and only adds an optimistic running flag that can go stale. This PR removes it.

## Change

- **Engine** (`DPEngineCoreProc.add_request`): an idle, unpaused rank always announces the wave. Previously it announced only for a stale wave.
- **Python front-end** (`DPAsyncMPClient`): no longer sends `FIRST_REQ` and no longer sets `engines_running` optimistically. The PAIR socket now carries only elastic EP scale notices, so it is renamed `scale_*`.
- **Python coordinator**: the front-end wake handler is removed.
- **Rust front-end**: removes `CoordinatorCommand::FirstRequest`, `notify_first_request`, the command channel, and the external wakeup message. The in-process coordinator now relays only engine `StartWave` and `WaveComplete`.
- **Unchanged**:
  - `ignore_start_dp_wave`, so a paused rank still drops `START_DP_WAVE`. A new unit test pins this.
  - Rank 0's `start_wave` after the collective, which covers waves started by resume with queued work or by an elastic EP switch.
  - The request `current_wave` stamp and the coordinator's deduplication.
- **Messages per idle→busy transition**:
  - Before: `FIRST_REQ`, one broadcast, and rank 0's mirror.
  - After: one announcement, one broadcast, and rank 0's mirror.
- **Compatibility**: a new front-end needs engines that include this change. The front-end and engine ship together, so a normal deployment always meets this. An old Rust front-end still works with new engines; the coordinator logs and ignores its wake message.

Net diff: 12 files, +226/−531.

## Why not a duplicate

No open PR changes this. #54762 (wave-0 bootstrap) and #55229 (idempotent resume) touch DP wave state but not the wake path. This came out of review of #51488. #51488 now builds on this PR instead of adding a request field.

## Test Plan

All GPU tests ran in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image with this change mounted, on H200, unless noted.

- **Unit tests**: `test_engine_core.py -k dp_rank` covers the announcement (current, stale, and newer wave; running; paused) and that a paused rank ignores `START_DP_WAVE`. Rust: `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-server`. `cargo fmt` and `clippy` are clean.
- **DP**: `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py`, with the mp and Ray backends. It includes a new e2e reproduction: hold the ADD on the client across pause and resume, then release it.
- **LB modes with multiple API servers**: `test_internal_lb_dp.py`, `test_external_lb_dp.py`, `test_hybrid_lb_dp.py`.
- **Launchers**: `test_multi_api_servers.py`, `test_dp_supervisor.py`.
- **Other DP configurations**: `test_pp_dp_v2.py` and `test_dense_dp_world_size.py`.
- **Elastic EP**: `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py` on 4 GPUs, using DeepSeek-V2-Lite with the accuracy threshold lowered because only the base checkpoint was cached locally.
- **HTTP e2e, DP=2 MoE with EP, PowerMoE-3b**. Three front-ends:
  - `vllm serve --api-server-count 2`
  - standalone `vllm-rs serve` (Rust in-process coordinator)
  - `vllm serve` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND` (Python coordinator)

  Each front-end ran 10 cold starts, 3 bursts of 16 requests from idle, and four pause/resume cycles (abort, wait, keep, abort) with requests in flight, sent while paused, and sent right after resume. The Python front-end also ran sleep/wake. Every request had to complete.
- **Idle TTFT at scale, against main.**
  - Model and image: Qwen3-30B-A3B with EP, same nightly image (77154ca61), default `vllm serve` settings.
  - Request: streaming `/v1/completions` with `max_tokens=1`.
  - Sizes: DP=2, DP=8 on one node, and DP=16 across two nodes. For DP=16, one node runs the API servers, the coordinator, and ranks 0–7; the other runs ranks 8–15 headless.
  - Load patterns:
    - single request after 1 s idle, pinned to a rank with `X-data-parallel-rank`
    - burst of DP requests from idle
    - open-loop Poisson at 1 and 4 req/s
  - Ordering: DP=16 ran ABBA, then BAAB, to cancel drift.
  - Locating the cost: one round per side added timestamps to the engine, the coordinator, and the DP all-reduce.

## Test Result

A/B e2e on main vs this PR (DP=2 MoE, real engines). Each case is a stale "wake was sent" assumption on main:

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| ADD held across pause/resume, so the wake reaches a still-paused peer and is dropped (`test_dp_request_reaching_rank_after_resume_wakes_peers`) | hangs | passes |
| Python front-end: request sent while paused, cancelled before resume, next request right after resume | hangs in round 1 (front-end believed running) | 20/20 rounds pass |
| Standalone `vllm-rs serve`: request sent while paused, client disconnects, resume, wait 10 s, then cold requests | first request hangs (45 s timeout) until another request reaches the peer rank | 3/3 pass |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Unit (Python) | 7 passed |
| Rust `vllm-engine-core-client` / `vllm-server` | 121 / 437 passed |
| `test_async_llm_dp.py`, mp + Ray | all pass (the new repro hangs on main) |
| LB DP (internal / external / hybrid) | 25 passed |
| Multi API server + DP supervisor | 22 passed |
| PP+DP / dense DP | 6 / 1 passed |
| Elastic EP (5 cases) | 5 passed |
| HTTP e2e (3 front-ends) | 3 passed |

**Idle TTFT.** p50 in ms, measured on a single request after the engines were idle. DP=8 and DP=16 cells have ~120 samples each.

| | target rank | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP=2 | rank0 / rank1 | 18.94 / 19.41 | 17.88 / 18.17 | −1.1 / −1.2 |
| DP=8 | rank0 / rank7 | 25.81 / 25.56 | 26.04 / 26.16 | +0.2 / +0.6 |
| DP=16 | rank0, rank7 (coordinator's node) | 52.98 / 53.08 | 53.04 / 52.95 | +0.1 / −0.1 |
| DP=16 | rank8, rank15 (remote node) | 51.93 / 52.75 | 52.53 / 52.32 | +0.6 / −0.4 |

All of these differences are smaller than the 1–2 ms spread between rounds.

**Under Poisson load at 4 req/s** (`max_tokens=16`, wakes are frequent):
- DP=16: this PR is consistently 1.5–2 ms slower at p50. It measured 76.2 vs 74.6 ms over the BAAB rounds and 77.7 vs 75.5 ms over the ABBA rounds, and pinning the target rank gave the same result.
- DP=8: no difference (25.95 vs 25.92 ms).

**Where the cost comes from.** The table shows target-rank time from ADD to the end of the first DP sync, p50 in ms over ~70 wakes per cell. Each duration is measured on one host's clock.

| request lands on | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| coordinator's node | 8.28 | 8.26 |
| remote node | 8.35 | 9.68 |

- On the coordinator's node, the PR adds one in-node hop (rank → coordinator) before the peers wake. The cross-node sync hides it.
- On the remote node, the cost is real. On main, the front-end's `FIRST_REQ` wakes peers in parallel with the ADD. With this PR, the target first notifies the coordinator across the network, and the coordinator then wakes the remote peers back across it. That adds about two cross-node one-way trips.

The cost is paid once per idle→running transition. Only the first request after idle pays it, and only when it lands on a remote-node rank. It does not grow with DP size, and it is zero while the engines are running.

Two pre-existing observations from the same traces:
- The first cross-node DP all-reduce after idle takes 6–7 ms even after every rank has reached it. That is most of the idle wake time, in both versions.
- Main broadcasts `START_DP_WAVE` twice per wake (360 broadcasts for 180 wakes), because the front-end's running flag lags and a second `FIRST_REQ` goes out. With this PR, each wake broadcasts once.

Failures seen in the same runs also occur on main with identical results, so they are unrelated to this change:
- `test_async_llm.py::test_multi_abort[DELTA]` fails on main too, 3 of 3 runs on each side.
- Tests that need a model not cached offline, or that fork CUDA, fail on both sides.

AI assistance (Claude, Codex, Kimi) was used for the analysis, the change, the tests, and two rounds of adversarial review. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
