title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fix Responses namespace aliases in named tool calling
author: YueshenZ
body:
## Overview

Fix forced-function schema lookup for Responses namespace tools on the schema-derived JSON constraint path. Prevent unrelated plain function names from shadowing namespace-local aliases, and preserve local names containing `__`.

## Claims

- Given plain `other__add` before namespace `math/add`, a valid choice of `add` selects the namespace function's parameters, not `other__add`'s parameters.
- A namespace function named `vector__add` remains selectable by that complete local name. Full names and explicit plain-function names keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py -q`: **184 passed** on Linux with normal GPU fixtures and teardown. The same file also passed on macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. All applicable code hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy 3.10–3.13, and Buildkite test tethering; the added documentation passed its applicable hooks.

Live A/B: **80 real HTTP requests** (20 cases × JSON/SSE × baseline/fixed) using one RTX 5090 D, driver 595.71.05, Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, and Qwen3-0.6B revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. Both servers used Hermes, xgrammar, disabled thinking, temperature 0, seed 17, and **`VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false`** set before startup.

| Case | Baseline `eec3c36` | Fixed source `b8f27a9` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plain `other__add` precedes namespace `add`; choose `add` | 200 with the unrelated `y` schema | 200 with the selected `x` schema |
| Namespace-local `vector__add`; choose its local name | 400: tool not passed in `tools` | 200 with the selected `x` schema |
| Full names, reversed ordering, explicit plain names | Expected schema | Unchanged |
| Unknown plain-function short name | 400 during request validation | Unchanged |

All 40 fixed cases matched the expected HTTP status, argument keys/types, and tool identity. The baseline reproduced both faults in JSON and SSE, while its controls passed. The only subsequent change is documentation. Existing Buildkite coverage runs the whole `tool_use` directory in `entrypoints-integration-api-server-generate`, including its AMD mirror.

<details>
<summary>Minimal live reproduction</summary>

Run either source version with the same model and settings:

```bash
VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --revision c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca \
  --served-model-name namespace-check --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18082 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 --enforce-eager \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes \
  --structured-outputs-config.backend xgrammar --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \
  --generation-config vllm --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18082/v1/responses \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
    "model": "namespace-check", "input": "Call the selected function. Use x=7 or y=seven.",
    "temperature": 0, "seed": 17, "max_output_tokens": 128, "store": false,
    "tools": [
      {"type": "function", "name": "other__add", "strict": true,
       "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"y": {"type": "string"}},
                      "required": ["y"], "additionalProperties": false}},
      {"type": "namespace", "name": "math", "description": "Math tools",
       "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "add", "strict": true,
                  "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"x": {"type": "integer"}},
                                 "required": ["x"], "additionalProperties": false}}]}
    ],
    "tool_choice": {"type": "function", "name": "add"}
  }'
```

The baseline returns a function call whose arguments contain `y`; the fix returns `x`. Rename the namespace child and the selected name to `vector__add` to reproduce the erroneous 400. Add `"stream": true` to exercise SSE.

</details>

Both phases reused the same installed official CUDA 13 wheel from parent `5b6b657`; its only source difference from the baseline is the AMD-only `rocm_aiter_fa.py`. Model files were hashed, and actual imported source paths and changed-file hashes were verified for both phases. No NVIDIA compiled code or dependencies were changed by this patch.

## Details

The old lookup created a short alias for any resolved name containing `__`, then used `rsplit` to derive it. Register aliases only for `NamespaceTool` and remove its exact namespace prefix. This preserves separators inside the local function name without introducing aliases for plain functions.

Scope: this fixes schema-derived named function calling. The default Hermes structural-tag path has a separate namespace limitation tracked in #56368; it is not fixed here. Turning off structural tags uses the documented JSON constraint path and still enforces named-call parameter schemas.

Duplicate check: refreshed all 5,916 open PR titles and inspected related closed/merged results and #56368, #57147, #49581, #46784, and #56285. None fixes these forced-function alias behaviors. #59718 concerns Anthropic tool removal and is independent.

AI assistance: Claude Code prepared the initial patch; Codex assisted with review, follow-up fixes, tests, documentation, CPU/GPU validation, and this description.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Declare max_tp_shards on the DSpark MLA KV cache spec
author: hyukjlee
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes a Kimi-K3 + DSpark perf regression from #57652: the K3 DSpark draft's `MLAAttentionSpec` does not declare `max_tp_shards`, so its MLA layers stop merging with the target's and the KV cache splits from **4 to 20 groups**. One-line fix: declare `max_tp_shards=1` on the draft spec, matching `MLAAttention`.

## Claims

- Restores Kimi-K3 + DSpark to 4 KV cache groups (20 on current `main`).
- Recovers the regression: **+3.7% total throughput/GPU, −3.3% median TPOT** vs. current nightly on MI355X TP8, matching both the pre-#57652 nightly and a full revert of #57652.
- Restores the pre-#57652 GPU KV pool size (3,192,149 → 3,274,215 tokens).
- Keeps #57652's offloading change; no behavior change for K3's offloading `kv_tp_replicas` (KDA layers already pin the gcd to 1).

## Validation

**Unit test** (`tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py::test_k3_dspark_mla_kv_cache_spec_groups_with_target_mla`): builds the target spec via `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` and the draft spec via the K3 `MultiHeadLatentAttention.get_kv_cache_spec`, then groups 24 target + 5 draft layers with `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size`.
- Without the fix: `AssertionError: assert 6 == 1`
- With the fix: passes (1 group, 29 layers)

Run inside `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-ac9126e5…` with `python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py -k k3_dspark_mla_kv_cache_spec`. `pre-commit` passes on both files.

**End-to-end**: Kimi-K3 (MXFP4) + Kimi-K3-DSpark, MI355X ×8, TP8, exact InferenceX CI serve command (DSpark k=7 synthetic AL 3.84, fp8 KV, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, FULL cudagraph, `--max-num-seqs 16`). Client: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 80`, 3 seeds per arm after a 16-prompt warmup, same host, arms run back to back.

| image | KV cache groups | total tput/GPU (tok/s) | output tput (tok/s) | median TPOT (ms) | median ITL (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| nightly `36768d1` (before #57652) | 4 | 729 | 648 | 11.13 | 33.4 |
| nightly `ac9126e` (includes #57652) | 20 | 701 | 623 | 11.47 | 34.4 |
| `ac9126e` + revert #57652 | 4 | 726 | 646 | 11.15 | 33.2 |
| **`ac9126e` + this PR** | **4** | **727** | **647** | **11.09** | **33.1** |

Per-seed median TPOT for this PR: 11.10 / 10.99 / 11.18 ms (vs 11.43 / 11.44 / 11.54 without it). The regression was first seen in InferenceX CI on the K3 agentic c8 cell (`kimik3 fp4 mi355x vllm TP8 mtp dram KV offload vllm-simple c8`): −6.1% total throughput/GPU and −16.6% p90 interactivity between the two nightlies.

**Accuracy (gsm8k)**: same server config but with real DSpark verification (`"rejection_sample_method": "block"`, no synthetic acceptance length), evaluated with the InferenceX CI lm-eval setup: `lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template --tasks gsm8k` (5-shot, CI task YAML), full 1319-question test set, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=16384`, `num_concurrent=16`.

| image | KV cache groups | gsm8k exact_match (strict / flexible) |
|---|---:|---:|
| `ac9126e` + this PR | 4 | 0.9636 ± 0.0052 / 0.9636 ± 0.0052 |

Mean DSpark acceptance length during the eval was ~3.0, confirming real verification.

## Details

**Root cause.** #57652 added `AttentionSpec.max_tp_shards` and set it to `1` in `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec`. `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py` (used for the K3 target on NVIDIA and for the DSpark draft on both vendors) builds its own `MLAAttentionSpec` and leaves it `None`. On ROCm the K3 target uses `MLAAttention` (`1`) while the draft uses this class (`None`), so `MLAAttentionSpec.merge`'s per-field `AttentionSpec` equality check rejects them. `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` then sees buckets of 69 KDA / 24 target MLA / 5 draft MLA layers instead of 69 / 29, the group size drops from 29 to 5, and the group count goes from 4 (3 KDA + 1 MLA) to 20 (14 + 5 + 1). The server log shows `kv cache group sizes` growing from 4 to 20 entries and `Add 1 padding layers` twice instead of `Add 18 padding layers`.

**Why 20 groups is slower.** `_build_attention_metadata` builds per KV cache group each step, and neither the ROCm K3 KDA builder nor the AITER MLA builder supports `update_block_table` reuse, so every extra group is a full `builder.build()` plus its own block-table/slot-mapping work.

**Why `1` is correct.** The draft's MLA latent KV has a single head and is replicated across TP ranks, same as `MLAAttention`. On NVIDIA the target and draft both go from `None` to `1`, so they still merge and grouping does not change. `kv_tp_replicas` remains 1 for K3 because its KDA (Mamba) layers contribute 1 to the gcd, so offloading behavior is unchanged.

**Not duplicate.** No open PR sets `max_tp_shards` on the K3 draft spec. #57942 (draft) adds a separate AMD DSpark MLA module, and #58207 changes the group-size heuristic. Both are broader and neither fixes this mismatch on `main`. This PR is the minimal fix for the regression.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Fail token-less streams in vllm-bench openai-chat
author: ZhenchengLin
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59722.

The `openai-chat` backend in the Rust `vllm-bench` marked a request as successful whenever the stream ended cleanly, even if no token ever showed up. The completions backend and Python `vllm bench serve` only count it as a success once the first token arrives, so chat was the odd one out.

So a 200 response with no tokens got counted as a success, with `ttft`, `latency` and `output_tokens` all left at their defaults. Thanks to @aron-intframe for pointing out in the issue that this goes beyond Mean TTFT:

- Mean TTFT and Mean E2EL get pulled down, since both are `0` for those requests.
- The `1 + output.itl.len()` fallback in `metrics/calculator.rs` counts each one as a phantom output token, which inflates total output tokens and output throughput.
- They pass every goodput SLO, because TTFT/TPOT/E2EL are all `0`.

The fix gates `success` on the `first_token_received` flag that's already there, and fails the request with the same error as the completions backend and Python. That message now lives in a shared `NO_VALID_CHUNK_ERROR` const so the two backends can't drift apart.

This also lines up with #64626 (thanks @dilberx). That PR stopped counting vLLM's opening role chunk as a token, so the stream vLLM actually sends when it generates nothing (a role chunk, then usage) now reaches this check and fails as it should.

**Heads up for multi-turn:** `multi_turn.rs` branches on `output.success`. Right now a token-less turn gets appended to the history as an empty assistant message and the run keeps going. After this change that turn is reported as failed, like any other failed turn, which is what the completions backend and Python already do.

## Not a duplicate

Claimed in #59722. Other PRs that touch `openai_chat.rs`:

- #55809 adds server queue time / TTFT to the detailed results, which is a different change.
- #59694 (mine, merged) changed the usage-chunk block a few lines up. This branch is rebased on top of it.
- #64626 (merged) decides which chunks count as tokens, and this PR decides what happens when none do, so the two fit together.
- #57519 handles server error events, but only on the Python side.

## Test Plan

Two new tests in `openai_chat::tests`:

- `test_tokenless_stream_is_failed`: the local SSE test server sends zero token chunks, then usage and `[DONE]`.
- `test_role_only_stream_is_failed`: the role chunk plus usage that vLLM sends when nothing is generated. It uses the `run_chat` helper from #64626, and thanks @esmeetu for suggesting it.

Both check that `success == false` and `error == NO_VALID_CHUNK_ERROR`.

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib
cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

For the end-to-end check, I used a mock OpenAI-compatible server that returns 200 with only the usage chunk and `[DONE]` for every 8th request, run with `--dataset-name random --random-input-len 100 --random-output-len 8 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8`.

## Test Result

- `cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib`: 225 passed on current `main`. Clippy and fmt are clean.
- If I revert the fix, both new tests fail.

End-to-end against the mock server. I re-ran the Rust rows after the rebase and got the same counts (28 ok, 4 failed, 224 tokens). The mock doesn't send a role chunk, so that case is covered by the unit test instead.

| client | Successful | Failed | Total generated tokens | Mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Python `vllm bench serve` (`openai-chat`) | 28 | 4 | 224 | 212.28 ms |
| Rust `vllm-bench` (`openai`), reference | 28 | 4 | 224 | 203.13 ms |
| Rust `vllm-bench` (`openai-chat`), before | 32 | 0 | 228 | 178.32 ms |
| Rust `vllm-bench` (`openai-chat`), after | 28 | 4 | 224 | 202.93 ms |

In the "before" row you can see the four phantom output tokens (228 vs 224) and the TTFT skew. With the fix, chat matches the completions backend and Python.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Pair P/D blocks by the last token with different block sizes
author: lucamotz
body:
## Overview

With different P/D block sizes, NIXL pull pairs D's and P's block lists by position, so KV lands in the wrong blocks, or D crashes, when the two lists start or end at different tokens. This pairs them by the request's last token and rejects DCP across different P/D logical block sizes.

## Claims

- With different P/D block sizes, D receives every page into the right block, also after a partial prefix hit on D or sliding-window clipping.
- Equal kernel blocks under different logical block sizes (e.g. FLASHINFER) land in the right blocks too, and D's EngineCore no longer dies on `assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)`.
- DCP across different P/D logical block sizes is rejected at the handshake.
- Pulls between equal P/D block sizes are unchanged.
- Without `remote_num_tokens`, pulls between different P/D block sizes fail instead of pairing by position, with an error logged once per remote engine.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k "hetero_ppl or dcp"
```

`_run_hetero_case` now passes `remote_num_tokens`, the hetero-ppl sweep and `test_hetero_ppl_with_block_size_ratio` gain a pure-MLA row (the latter with a 2-block hit on D), and `test_dcp_rejects_different_logical_block_sizes` covers the DCP guard. `test_hetero_ppl_pull_without_remote_num_tokens_fails` covers the failed pull, and `test_dcp_pull_with_block_size_ratio_writes_stay_within_request_blocks` DCP reads between different kernel block sizes.

CPU, this PR at `4524ec3cdc` on main `8530a778f7`: 44 cases fail without this PR and pass with it. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>CPU output</summary>

```
# main 8530a778f7 + this PR's tests
44 failed, 182 passed, 106 deselected
  34 TOKEN MISALIGNMENT, 8 assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group), 1 DID NOT RAISE NotImplementedError, 1 READ posted without remote_num_tokens
# this PR 4524ec3cdc
226 passed, 106 deselected
```

</details>

GB10 (setup as in #58860): with this PR, every case below gives logprobs bitwise equal to matched-block P/D, and gpt-oss-20b with FLASHINFER, P 64 / D 128, no longer kills D's EngineCore.

<details>
<summary>GB10 runs</summary>

main `8530a778f7`, without and with this PR at `0afbebd9e0`. Identical texts vs the matched-block P/D run on the same image (D's block size on both sides; for TRITON_ATTN, whose prefill tile follows the block size, P's):

| case | without | with, logprobs bitwise equal |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B, FLASH_ATTN, 16/64, 512-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |
| Gemma-4-E2B-it, TRITON_ATTN, 16/64 | 4/7 | 7/7 |
| Gemma-4-E2B-it, 16/64, 512-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN), 544/1088, 1088-token D hit | 2/4 | 4/4 |

gpt-oss-20b, FLASHINFER, P 64 / D 128 kills D's EngineCore on main (`assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)`) and runs with this PR.

</details>

## Details

With different P/D block sizes:

1. P's scheduler returns its block ids and `remote_num_tokens` in `kv_transfer_params`, with the sliding-window blocks that left the window dropped.
2. D's scheduler hands NIXL its block ids past a local prefix hit, window-clipped the same way. The hit and the clipping start the two lists at different tokens, and each side pads to its own logical block past the last token.
3. D's pull pairs each group's block lists by position: `_map_block_ids_for_block_size_ratio` front-clips D's sub-blocks to P's count, then `_apply_prefix_caching` end-trims P to D's count. That holds only if both lists start and end at the same token, which step 2 breaks. Pages then land one or more blocks off.
4. D's receive post-process zeroes the sub-blocks the read did not cover.

Equal kernel blocks under different logical block sizes (e.g. FLASHINFER) shift pages the same way; when D's padded list is longer than P's, D's read fails `assert num_decode_blocks <= len(prefill_group)` and its EngineCore dies.

This drops each side's padding past the last of the `remote_num_tokens` that P already sends and pairs the lists backwards from there, once per request in `_read_blocks_for_req`. `ReqMeta.covered_sub_blocks` lets the receive post-process zero exactly what P doesn't send: D's padding, and D's leading sub-blocks when D's sliding window starts before P's.

Without `remote_num_tokens`, which a router may not forward, D can't find the last token, so the pull fails. P's block size is only known after the handshake, so the scheduler can't decline the request earlier.

DCP reads keep positional pairing, which needs equal logical block sizes because each side shards tokens at its own. They are mapped to remote-sized sub-blocks in `_read_blocks_for_req` too, so `_read_blocks` no longer maps block ids.

#51527 (draft) lets Mamba hybrids with different logical but equal kernel block sizes use prefix caching, pairing their full-attention groups from new scheduler metadata; it leaves the attention-only end-trim and the `block_size_ratio > 1` pairing fixed here unchanged. #60483 (draft) rejects different P/D DCP sizes when `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` differs from the block size; this PR rejects DCP across different P/D logical block sizes. #60484 rejects DCP peers with different interleave sizes; since NIXL sets the interleave to the block size by default, that overlaps this PR's DCP guard when both sides use DCP.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Reject push handshakes between different P/D block sizes
author: lucamotz
body:
## Overview

NixlPushConnector now rejects P/D peers with different block sizes at the handshake, so their requests fail at once instead of stalling or crashing D.

## Claims

- A P/D pair that differs in kernel block size or kernel blocks per logical block is rejected at the handshake, and D keeps serving.
- Pull and equal-block-size push are unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py
```

`test_push_handshake_rejects_different_block_sizes` covers the new check. Of the two tests of the removed PP-only check, `test_layer_handshake_rejects_unsupported_geometry` keeps only its TP case, and `test_packed_mla_rejects_unequal_block_sizes_before_peer_registration` is removed: the new check does not depend on packed MLA or PP and runs before any registration.

CPU, this PR at `32bad14c7d` on main `8530a778f7`: the new test's 3 cases fail without this PR and pass with it. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

GB10, main `8530a778f7` without and with this PR at `1675f70e48`: both P/D pairs that stall or crash D on main are rejected at D's handshake and D keeps serving; 64/64 push is bitwise equal to main's push.

<details>
<summary>GB10 runs</summary>

Qwen3-0.6B, NixlPushConnector, P and D on one GPU, greedy, `--enforce-eager`, code prompts (2 per rejected pair, 6 for 64/64).

| P / D | backend | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 / 64 | FLASH_ATTN | P's handshake fails with `Local block size 16 is not divisible by remote block size 64 or vice versa.`; both requests still pending at the 150 s client timeout | D's handshake raises `NixlPushConnector requires identical P/D block sizes. Kernel block size and kernel blocks per logical block: local (64, 1), remote engine … (16, 1).`; both requests fail at once |
| 128 / 64, both with 64-token kernel blocks | FLASHINFER | D's EngineCore dies with `IndexError: tuple index out of range` in `get_transfer_results` | rejected the same way (local (64, 1), remote (64, 2)) |
| 64 / 64 | FLASH_ATTN | 6/6 served | 6/6 outputs, logprobs bitwise equal to main's push |

In both rejected cases D's `/health` stays 200 and a direct completion sent to D succeeds.

</details>

## Details

NixlPushConnector cannot convert or re-pair blocks when P and D differ in kernel block size or kernel blocks per logical block, and D registers P for notifications without checking either. On main, for such a pair:

1. D handshakes with P and sends `PUSH_REG` with its block ids.
2. P handshakes with D and WRITEs into those blocks. Depending on the sizes, P's handshake fails or P writes misaligned blocks.
3. D waits for a WRITE that never comes, or its receive fails on the block-size-ratio assert or on empty push block ids.

This PR rejects such peers in `NixlPushConnectorWorker._validate_remote_parallel_config`, which `_nixl_handshake` runs for P's and both of D's handshakes (registration and heartbeat) before registering the peer, so the request fails like any failed handshake. It replaces the PP-only block-size check in `add_remote_agent` and removes push's `block_size_ratio > 1` branch in `_xfer_blocks`, which can no longer run.

No open PR rejects push peers with different block sizes.

title: [Bugfix] Validate tool-parser/tokenizer compatibility at startup
author: www6v
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59087.

Some tool parsers need special tokens from the tokenizer. For example, the `mistral` parser needs `[TOOL_CALLS]`. The parser checks for the token in its constructor and raises an error if it is missing. The server only builds the parser when it handles a chat request. So `vllm serve` starts, `/health` returns 200, and every chat request returns HTTP 500, including requests without tools.

This PR builds the parser once in `ParserManager.get_parser()` at startup. If the parser does not work with the tokenizer, the server stops with a `TypeError` that names the flag and the model:

```
TypeError: --tool-call-parser mistral cannot be used with the tokenizer of 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct': Mistral parser could not locate the tool call token in the tokenizer!
```

The check covers the composed parser, so it also applies to reasoning parsers and to composite parsers such as Harmony. If the tokenizer is `None` (`skip_tokenizer_init`), the check is skipped.

## Test Plan

Live `vllm serve` runs on H200:

- `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral`: must stop at startup with the error above.
- `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`: must start and answer chat requests.
- `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 --tokenizer-mode mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral`: must start and return a parsed tool call.
- `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 --tool-call-parser hermes`: must start and return reasoning and tool output.

Existing suites: `tests/parser`, `tests/tool_parsers/test_hermes_tool_parser.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_render_parity.py`.

## Test Result

- The mismatched server exits with code 1 and the `TypeError` above. No `Starting vLLM server` line is logged.
- The three matched servers start, and plain chat, chat with tools, and `/v1/completions` all return 200. The Mistral and Qwen3 servers return parsed tool calls.
- Existing suites pass: 482 passed in the parser suites, 261 passed in the serving suites.

Fixes #59681: keep SM100 FlashInfer sparse MLA prefill out of FULL CUDA graphs while preserving DSpark variable-length decode graphs.

title: [Bugfix][Quark] Pass grouped-routing arguments to OCP MX monolithic kernels
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

`QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.apply_monolithic` does not forward `num_expert_group`, `topk_group`, `e_score_correction_bias` or `routed_scaling_factor` to the monolithic kernel, so the kernel falls back to their defaults.

Quark OCP MX picks its experts through `select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, the same path `Mxfp4MoEMethod` uses. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` has forwarded these four arguments since #50000; the Quark copy, added earlier in #38774, was never updated.

**Who is affected.** The bug needs three things at once:

1. A Quark **weight-only MXFP4 (`w_mxfp4`, W4A16)** checkpoint.
2. DeepSeek-V3/V4-style routing (grouped top-k and/or a correction bias with a scaling factor).
3. A **monolithic** MXFP4 kernel. On SM100, the BF16-activation priority list selects `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16` (`TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic`, which supports `DeepSeekV3` routing) by default. On ROCm, `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` (`DeepSeekV3`/`DeepseekV4`) is used when requested explicitly.

In that setup the kernel routes with `n_group=0`, `topk_group=0` and no bias, and the scaling factor is `None` (TRT-LLM) or 1.0 (aiter).

The published Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints are W4A4: `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4`, `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4`, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4` and others. W4A4 resolves to the modular `AiterExperts` on ROCm and to emulation on CUDA, so routing happens in vLLM's router with every argument. As far as I can tell, no public checkpoint hits this today. This PR fixes a latent inconsistency before a W4A16 export does.

This PR forwards the four arguments exactly as `Mxfp4MoEMethod` does. Models without grouped routing pass `None` or the default values and are unaffected.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy).
- Code-path analysis above (`oracle/mxfp4.py` activation filtering and priority lists). There is no public W4A16 Quark checkpoint to run end to end.

## Test Result

`pre-commit` passes. Related: #59757 moves the monolithic kernel call into `FusedMoEMethodBase`, which also removes this inconsistency.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire stale Mamba spec blocks in prefill checkpoint steps
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step. The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path. ## Claims - Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`. - No behavior change without speculative decoding, for `mamba_cache_mode` other than `align`, or for steps without an internal checkpoint. ## Validation Setup: RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on 2 H200 GPUs, served with default settings plus MTP: ``` vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' ``` Reproducer (script below): send a long prompt while another long prompt is still being processed, then send the exact same prompt again. The second request reuses the cached start of the prompt. - Before the fix, the second answer was garbage in 3 of 3 trials, for example `File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4 # File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4 ...`, while the first answer was a normal list of function names. - With the fix, both answers were normal in 3 of 3 trials. Other checks: - A single long prompt sent twice, with nothing else running, also came back broken in 4 of 7 runs at about 25k tokens before the fix, and in 0 of 12 runs after. - In an 8-agent coding-agent run (10 turns, full history resent each turn), 2 agents switched to word salad right after reusing their cached history and stayed broken. With the fix, and with MTP off, no agent broke. - New test `test_mamba_checkpoint_hash_maps_only_to_checkpoint_block` fails on main and passes with the fix. - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache` passes; the GPU part, `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` (`base` and `mtp`), was run on one H200.
repro.py ```python """Reproducer: with MTP on, sending the same long prompt twice can return garbage the second time. Server (any recent main): vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' Run: python repro.py http://localhost:8000/v1 Each trial sends a long prompt while another long prompt is running, then sends the same prompt again. The second answer reuses the cached start of the prompt. Before the fix it is often garbage; after the fix both answers are normal. """ import random import sys import threading from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="none") MODEL = client.models.list().data[0].id WORDS = "alpha beta gamma delta kernel buffer index cache shard block token commit".split() def long_prompt(seed, size): """Made-up Python code of about size characters, different for every seed.""" rng = random.Random(seed) lines = [] while sum(map(len, lines)) < size: lines.append(f"def {rng.choice(WORDS)}_{rng.choice(WORDS)}(x): return {rng.randrange(10**6)} " f"# {' '.join(rng.choices(WORDS, k=8))}\n") return "Here is a file:\n" + "".join(lines) + "\nList the first five function names, then summarize the file." def ask(prompt, max_tokens): out = client.chat.completions.create( model=MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], max_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0, extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "low"}}) # GLM-5.3: short thinking msg = out.choices[0].message thinking = getattr(msg, "reasoning", None) or getattr(msg, "reasoning_content", None) or "" return (thinking + (msg.content or "")).replace("\n", " ") def run_together(prompts, max_tokens): threads = [threading.Thread(target=ask, args=(p, max_tokens)) for p in prompts] for t in threads: t.start() for t in threads: t.join() # Whether a prompt is affected depends on its exact length; these lengths trigger it. for trial, size in enumerate([60000, 60000, 60000]): # Keep the server busy for a moment, as it would be in production. run_together([long_prompt(1000 + 10 * trial + k, 90000) for k in range(6)], 64) # A long request is running while the target prompt is processed for the first time. background = threading.Thread(target=ask, args=(long_prompt(10 * trial + 1, size), 300)) background.start() threading.Event().wait(0.3) target = long_prompt(10 * trial + 2, size) first = ask(target, 60) background.join() # The exact same request again. second = ask(target, 60) print(f"trial {trial}") print(f" first: {first[:100]}") print(f" second: {second[:100]}") ``` Example output on main (before the fix): ``` trial 0 first: **First five function names:** 1. `alpha_beta` 2. `index_token` 3. `buffer_cache` 4. `gamma_shard` 5 second: List the first five function names, then summarize the file. ## Details In align mode a request keeps its running state in the block after the last computed one, followed by `num_speculative_blocks` scratch blocks. A normal `allocate_new_blocks` call moves the old scratch blocks that fall below the new running state to the end of the table and nulls their slots. In a checkpoint step this was skipped (`if blocks_allocated and not checkpoint_block`). With MTP, the checkpoint position P is shifted one block down. When one of the previous step's scratch blocks sits at index `P // block_size - 1` (with k=1: the chunk starts one block below P), it occupies the natural slot of P. The checkpoint itself is written into a new block at `cdiv(end, block_size) - 2`, one index above it. In the same step, `cache_full_blocks` registers the unwritten scratch block under hash(P), and `_cache_partial_tail_block` then adds the real checkpoint block under the same hash. `get_one_block` returns the first block registered, so later hits at P resume from the scratch page. The entry stays until eviction, so every request that shares this prefix is affected. It happens when a prompt's final prefill chunk starts one block below the shifted checkpoint, so it depends on prompt length and on how much of each step's token budget other requests use. Overlapping long prompts make it much more likely. For example, with a second request of 22350 tokens, a first request of up to 23424 tokens triggers it (3/3) and one of 23440 tokens does not (0/3). The fix relocates scratch blocks below the checkpoint index (`block_idx < num_skipped_blocks - checkpoint_block`). A scratch block exactly at the checkpoint index stays and becomes the checkpoint block, since the worker exports the checkpoint into that column. Because relocated blocks are reused, checkpoint steps for already-allocated requests no longer need `num_speculative_blocks` extra new blocks. The allocation cap in `allocate_new_blocks` and the admission estimate in `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` both drop that term, so they stay equal. The existing `test_mamba_checkpoint_admission_matches_allocation` and the new test both check this. On unfixed builds, disabling MTP or prefix caching avoids the bug. Possible CI follow-up: no current job would catch this. The only nightly on this path, the B200 Kimi-K3 spec-decode GSM8K job, uses ~640-token prompts, and GSM8K accuracy does not move noticeably. A small extra phase in that job could catch this class of bug. After the GSM8K pass, it would send about 15 long prompts with lengths spread over one chunk-budget period, then send each again and check that the cached answer starts the same as a fresh computation. On GLM-5.3-Flash such a phase failed on unfixed main in 3 of 3 runs and passed with this fix in 3 of 3. I can send it as a separate PR if that is useful. title: [CI] Fix ModelExpress handling in weight transfer tests
author: djramic
body:
## Purpose

10 tests in `tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` fail in the `(MI355) Distributed Features` job since #58399 added the optional ModelExpress weight transfer backend:

```text
FAILED TestDeferredProcessingContract::test_every_engine_declares_whether_it_defers
FAILED TestDeferredProcessingContract::test_every_engine_can_be_drained
ImportError: The 'modelexpress' weight transfer backend requires ModelExpress.
 ...
FAILED test_modelexpress_missing_backend_explains_source_install[*] (6 cases)
FAILED test_modelexpress_preserves_transitive_import_errors[*] (2 cases)
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/vllm-workspace/vllm/distributed/weight_transfer/modelexpress_engine.py'
```

Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92561#01a0fb65-44f8-4273-bec4-5c1f7d71d243>

The two groups fail for different reasons:

- `TestDeferredProcessingContract` loads every registered backend. `modelexpress` is always registered, but ModelExpress is a separately installed package that CI does not install, so loading it raises `ImportError`.
- The shim tests locate `modelexpress_engine.py` relative to the test file. The CI image moves the source tree to `src/`, so that path does not exist.

This PR fixes both in the tests:

- `TestDeferredProcessingContract` skips `modelexpress` when the package is not installed. The other five backends are still checked, and `modelexpress` is checked when it is installed.
- The shim tests resolve the installed module with `importlib.util.find_spec` instead of a path relative to the test file.

## Test Plan

On MI355X:

```bash
VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py
```

## Test Result

Before:
```text
10 failed, 88 passed, 24 skipped
```
After:
```text
98 passed, 24 skipped
```

AI assistance was used during the development of this PR; submitter manually reviewed all changes and ran the tests listed above.

title: [Bugfix][Watermarking] Keep draft prompt lengths valid under CUDA graphs
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

Fix stale prompt lengths in the draft watermark deduplication mask under CUDA graphs. The bug came in with #56807. I found it while reviewing #59554, which would expose DFlash to it too.

## Claims

- With `dual_key_gumbel` and the default `deduplicate_contexts="single_turn"`, draft sampling under FULL CUDA graphs (default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) read prompt lengths from a stale UVA buffer after new requests arrived. This affects EAGLE3, MTP and DSpark (reproduced; EAGLE shares the autoregressive path). Some drafts were sampled without key A where they should carry it, and some repeated contexts were not deduplicated. Graph and eager mode now agree.
- No host sync, and no end-to-end change I can separate from run-to-run noise (see Performance). The fix adds one async copy of `max_num_reqs` int32 values per propose. The captured dedup kernel then reads device memory instead of pinned host memory, which is faster in a microbenchmark.

## Validation

Engine harness: Qwen3-4B targets (Qwen3.5-0.8B for MTP) with dedup `single_turn`. It compares the dedup mask each draft row actually used against a CPU reference built from the true prompt lengths. Compared with the engine-level script under Reproduction, it also covers Poisson arrivals, MTP and DSpark. λ is arrivals per engine step.

| Workload | Before (FULL graph) | After (FULL graph) | Eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 K=3, crafted (one request at a time, prompt-copying) | 576/1905 mask rows wrong; 536 accepted drafts lacked key A | 0/1896 | 0/1896 |
| EAGLE3 K=3, online Poisson (λ=0.2, mean concurrency 12) | 43/23178 mask rows wrong (41 falsely skipped, 2 missed dedup) | 0/23178 | 0/23325 |
| MTP K=3, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 32.6% / 2.06% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |
| DSpark K=7, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 39.5% / 2.05% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |

The MTP and DSpark "after" numbers come from the harness's patched `prepare()`, not from a commit tree. The EAGLE3 online "after" rows used the first revision of this fix, which differed only in copying into a `[:num_reqs]` slice. The EAGLE3 crafted "after" and eager runs use this commit.

Host sync: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, EAGLE3 under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, 12 staggered admissions and 98 `prepare()` calls: clean. A deliberate `.item()` in `prepare()` trips the check, so the check does cover this path.

Unit test:

```bash
pytest tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py -k reads_current_prompt_lens   # fails on main, passes with the fix
pytest tests/watermarking/                                                    # 148 passed (B300)
```

The test is CUDA-only. CI runs `tests/watermarking` only in the CPU "V1 Others" step, where it is skipped. I ran it locally on a B300: it fails on main and passes with the fix, and the suite passes (148).

About 1-2% of accepted drafts are affected at low traffic (EAGLE3 0.98%, MTP 2.06%, DSpark 2.05%) and 0.54% when busy (EAGLE3). Per-category detection rates in paired runs are identical for EAGLE3 and within noise for MTP and DSpark: at most 2 of 19-20 requests differ. The bug still breaks the watermark's own contract, and graph and eager runs diverge.

### Performance

Setup: B300, Qwen3-4B with EAGLE3 (`AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3`, K=3, probabilistic), `dual_key_gumbel`, temperature 1.0, random 1024 in / 256 out with `--ignore-eos` (64 prompts at c=1 and c=8, 256 at c=64), default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Main and fix servers ran in parallel on two GPUs, swapped each round, for 10 rounds of 2 passes. Δ is the mean of the per-round paired change, ± the 95% CI. A/A is the same comparison of main against main (4 rounds).

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (main → fix) | Δ tok/s | Δ mean TPOT | Δ mean TTFT | Acceptance length | A/A Δ tok/s | A/A Δ TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 464.7 → 462.3 | −0.5% ± 0.6 | +0.5% ± 0.6 | +1.8% ± 2.0 | 1.632 → 1.632 | −0.4% ± 0.6 | +0.6% ± 3.4 |
| 8 | 3032 → 3012 | −0.6% ± 0.8 | +0.4% ± 0.9 | +2.3% ± 1.7 | 1.658 → 1.662 | −0.3% ± 3.3 | −1.2% ± 5.6 |
| 64 | 10543 → 10495 | −0.4% ± 0.8 | +0.3% ± 0.9 | +0.8% ± 1.5 | 1.533 → 1.533 | +0.3% ± 1.2 | −0.7% ± 4.1 |

Throughput and TPOT change by less than 1%, with CIs that include zero. The A/A differences are of similar size.

Mean TTFT is 0.35-0.65 ms (0.8-2.3%) higher. Only the c=8 CI excludes zero (+0.7% to +4.0%). Between two identical main servers, per-round TTFT differences range from −6% to +3%, and one A/A CI (c=64 acceptance length) also excludes zero. I read the TTFT difference as noise, but these runs cannot rule out a TTFT cost of a few percent at c=8.

`prepare()` alone, with a UVA-backed prompt-length source and the speculator's two gathers: host time goes from 48.4-48.9 µs to 51.4-52.1 µs (+3 µs for one more copy launch). The copy itself takes 4.2 µs on the GPU at `max_num_reqs=1024` and 0.9 µs at 256. The dedup kernel runs once per draft step, so three times per propose at K=3. Replayed in a CUDA graph, those three steps get faster because the kernel reads device memory instead of pinned host memory: 12.3 → 8.7 µs with 1 request and 30.2 → 17.0 µs with 1024 requests (`max_num_reqs=1024`).

### Reproduction

A standalone script shows the bug without a model. It captures the draft dedup mask in a CUDA graph, admits a request (which moves `prompt_len.gpu` to the next pool buffer), and compares the replayed graph with eager mode. Run it on a CUDA GPU with `python repro_stale_prompt_len.py`.

<details>
<summary>repro_stale_prompt_len.py</summary>

```python
# Draft watermark dedup mask under a CUDA graph reads a stale prompt length.
import torch

import vllm
from vllm.v1.watermarking.gumbel import GumbelWatermarker
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils import UvaBackedTensor

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
dev = torch.device("cuda")
wm = DraftWatermarker(GumbelWatermarker(key=42, context_width=2), max_num_reqs=1,
                      device=dev, num_speculative_steps=1,
                      deduplicate_contexts="single_turn",
                      deduplicate_contexts_max_history=None)
prompt_len = UvaBackedTensor(1, dtype=torch.int32)  # like req_states.prompt_len
# Request in slot 0: prompt [5, 6, 9], generated [5, 6], next draft context
# [5, 6]. The context repeats only inside the prompt, so with single_turn the
# draft must use key A. Read with prompt length 0, it looks like repeated
# generated text and the draft skips key A.
tokens = torch.tensor([[5, 6, 9, 5, 6]], device=dev)
total_len = torch.tensor([5], device=dev)
ctx = torch.tensor([[5, 6]], device=dev)
enabled = torch.tensor([True], device=dev)
logits = torch.zeros(1, 8, device=dev)
idx = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
temp, draft_step = torch.ones(1, device=dev), torch.tensor(0, device=dev)

def prepare():  # the speculator calls this on every propose()
    wm.prepare(ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_len.gpu, total_len)

def uses_key_a():  # per-row mask that draft sampling uses for key A
    return wm._sampling_state(logits, idx, temp, draft_step, ctx)[1]

prepare()  # capture time: slot 0 has prompt length 0
uses_key_a()  # warm up outside capture
graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
    graph_out = uses_key_a()
# A step that admits a request runs copy_to_uva(), which moves
# prompt_len.gpu to the next buffer of its round-robin pool.
prompt_len.np[0] = 3
prompt_len.copy_to_uva()
prepare()
eager = uses_key_a().item()
graph.replay()
replayed = graph_out.item()
print(f"eager: key A={eager}  graph: key A={replayed}  ->",
      "OK" if eager == replayed else "STALE prompt length in graph")
```

</details>

Main:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=False  -> STALE prompt length in graph
```

With the fix:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=True  -> OK
```

An engine-level script runs EAGLE3 with `dual_key_gumbel` through `LLM`, admits 24 requests one at a time, and counts draft rows whose dedup mask differs from the mask built from the current prompt lengths. Run `python engine_repro.py` for the default CUDA graph mode and `python engine_repro.py eager` for eager mode (30-45 s each on a B300).

<details>
<summary>engine_repro.py</summary>

```python
# EAGLE3 + dual_key_gumbel: compare the dedup mask each draft row used with the
# mask recomputed, in the same CUDA graph, from the current prompt lengths.
import os
import sys

import torch

os.environ.update(VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER="1", VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING="0")
import vllm  # noqa: E402
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker as DW  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.watermark import draft_watermarking_mask  # noqa: E402

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
orig_init, orig_prepare, orig_state = DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state
instances = []

def __init__(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args):
    orig_init(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args)
    self.true_pl = torch.zeros(max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    self.stats = torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)  # rows, wrong, skip
    instances.append(self)

def prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens):
    orig_prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens)
    self.true_pl.copy_(prompt_lens)  # current prompt lengths

def _sampling_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx):
    steps, mask = orig_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx)
    ref = draft_watermarking_mask(
        self.all_token_ids, idx, self.true_pl, self.total_lens, self.prior_contexts,
        ctx, steps, self.enabled[: len(ctx)] & (temps != 0),
        self.deduplicate_contexts_max_history, False)
    self.stats += torch.stack(
        [torch.ones_like(ref).sum(), (mask != ref).sum(), (ref & ~mask).sum()])
    return steps, mask

DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state = __init__, prepare, _sampling_state
wm = {"algorithm": "dual_key_gumbel", "key": 42, "context_width": 4}
spec = {"method": "eagle3", "model": "AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}
llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-4B", speculative_config=spec, watermark_config=wm, seed=0,
          max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
          enforce_eager=sys.argv[1:] == ["eager"])
(dw,) = instances
dw.stats.zero_()  # drop warmup and capture rows
text = ("The committee met on Tuesday to review the annual budget. The members agreed "
        "to fund the public libraries, repair the old bridge near the river, and hire "
        "two more nurses for the clinic. The mayor promised a full report next month.")
for i in range(24):  # one request at a time; each admission rotates the UVA pool
    ask = f"Repeat exactly, word for word:\n{text}" if i % 3 == 1 else "Say hi."
    llm.chat([{"role": "user", "content": f"[{i}] {ask}"}],
             SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, seed=i, max_tokens=96), use_tqdm=False,
             chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False})
rows, wrong, skipped = dw.stats.tolist()
print(f"draft rows={rows}  mask rows wrong={wrong}  wrongly skipped key A={skipped}")
```

</details>

| Run | Output |
|---|---|
| Main, CUDA graphs (2 runs, identical) | `draft rows=714  mask rows wrong=129  wrongly skipped key A=129` |
| Fix, CUDA graphs | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Main, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Fix, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |


## Details

**Root cause:** `req_states.prompt_len` is a `UvaBackedTensor`. `copy_to_uva()` runs from `apply_staged_writes` on steps that add requests, and it moves `.gpu` round-robin across the buffer pool. `DraftWatermarker.prepare()` stored that reference, so a captured `draft_watermarking_mask` kept reading the capture-time buffer. Newly admitted requests then see the previous occupant's prompt length until the pool comes back around:
- If the stale length is shorter than the real one, prompt n-grams count as generated history and the draft skips key A.
- If it is longer, real repeats are missed.

**Fix:** `DraftWatermarker` owns an int32 `[max_num_reqs]` buffer, and `prepare()` copies into it. This follows the existing `contexts` and `enabled` copies in the same method. It is also the principle MRV2 states for fused draft decoding: replayed tensor state must live in persistent storage.

I found no other inputs to captured draft sampling that go stale:
- `all_token_ids` and `total_len` are `StagedWriteTensor`s whose `.gpu` never moves.
- `contexts` and `enabled` are already copied into owned buffers.
- Other UVA-backed inputs to the draft path (temperature, seeds) are already copied into speculator-owned buffers. The remaining readers run eagerly.

**Unchanged behavior:** eager mode and the watermark-off path are unaffected. By code inspection, dedup modes `none` and `all` do not depend on prompt lengths: `none` returns before the mask is built, and `all` searches from position 0. The copy still runs in those modes; its cost is negligible.

**Alternatives:**
- Making `RequestState.prompt_len` a stable `StagedWriteTensor` would fix this for every future graph reader. It touches the penalties, bad_words, trace_replay and model_runner readers, and the `LogitsProcessor` interface types `prompt_len` as `UvaBackedTensor`, so it is better done as a separate refactor.
- A persistent device mirror inside `UvaBackedTensor` would cost a copy for every user.

---

title: [Bugfix] Give each data-parallel engine its own global RNG streams
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Every data-parallel engine re-seeds the global RNGs with the same engine `seed` at the end of warm-up (`Worker.compile_or_warm_up_model`). Requests without an explicit `seed` sample from those global streams:

- Model Runner V2 draws each unseeded request's per-request seed from the global NumPy RNG (`SamplingStates.add_request`).
- The fused FlashInfer top-k/top-p path (V2), and V1's sampler and rejection sampler, use the global CUDA generator.

So the n-th unseeded request on every DP engine samples the same tokens. GRPO-style rollouts are hit hardest: they send the n siblings of a prompt across DP engines, and many groups come back with identical siblings.

This PR mixes the DP index into that final re-seed. `set_random_seed(seed, data_parallel_index)` seeds with `SeedSequence((seed, data_parallel_index))` when the index is non-zero.

- **Index 0 keeps the plain seed.** DP=1, and DP rank 0, are bitwise unchanged.
- The seed and the index are combined as a pair, not as `seed + index`. RL frameworks that give replicas `seed + replica_rank` therefore do not collide.
- **Placement.** The re-seed happens after weights are loaded and after profiling and CUDA graph capture. Anything seeded at init stays identical across engines, including `load_format=dummy` weights; the seed in `init_device` is untouched.
- **Why the index is passed at the worker re-seed rather than seeding once at engine start.** The workers already re-seed the global RNGs with the plain engine seed at the end of `compile_or_warm_up_model`, in the worker processes, after `init_device` seeded them and after profiling and warm-up consumed RNG. A seed set once when the engine core starts would be overwritten by that re-seed. So the change is one extra argument at the two existing post-warm-up call sites (`gpu_worker.py`, `cpu_worker.py`) plus the helper; the earlier per-sampler / model-runner wiring is gone.
- **`data_parallel_index`, not `data_parallel_rank`.** Dense models reset the rank to 0 on each independent DP engine.
- **Workers.** The GPU worker's final re-seed covers the XPU worker, which inherits `compile_or_warm_up_model`; the CPU worker overrides it and gets the same change.
- **Unchanged paths.** Requests with an explicit `seed` use their own generators (V1) or per-request seeds (V2), so they are not affected.

Global RNG consumers on the serving path, none of which needs identical streams across DP engines:

- V2 `SamplingStates` default seeds.
- `flashinfer_sample` / `random_sample` / V1 `rejection_sampler` noise for unseeded rows.
- The MoE routing simulator (`torch.rand`, debug only).
- Python `random`, used for KV-cache metric sampling and the tmp-file suffixes of tiering fs I/O.

Within one engine, every TP/PP worker gets the same `(seed, index)`, so the ranks stay consistent with each other.

## Duplicate check

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` with each of:
  - `data parallel seed`
  - `default seed data parallel`
  - `sampler generator data parallel`
  - `identical samples data parallel`
  - `data_parallel_rank seed`
  - `seed dp rank sampler`
  - `model runner v2 seed`
  - `duplicate outputs data parallel`
  - `same seed data parallel engines`
  - `set_random_seed data parallel`
  - `global RNG data parallel`
  - `data_parallel_index seed`
- No other open PR matches. This PR was force-updated on 2026-10-05 from its earlier version (per-rank generators inside the V2 sampler, ~40 lines, V2 only, keyed on `data_parallel_rank`, so it did not fix dense models) to the current minimal re-seed. Review comments from before 2026-10-05 refer to that earlier version.
- #57018 (bounding request seeds to int64) touches request seeds, not the default streams.
- Issue searches found no existing report.

## Test Plan

- Unit test `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py::test_set_random_seed_differs_per_data_parallel_index`. It checks that index 0 equals the plain seed, that each index is reproducible, that 4 indices give 4 distinct streams, and that the engine seed still matters.
- E2E on GB200 ×4 with Nemotron-H Lightning 30B-A3B NVFP4: DP4 + EP, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `--seed 42`, V2 runner unless noted. The workload is GRPO-like: 32 prompts × 8 samples, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, max_tokens 512, 6 consecutive rounds on one server. It is submitted either as one `n=8` request per prompt or as 8 × `n=1`.
- Determinism checks with every request pinned to a rank via `X-data-parallel-rank`:
  - explicit-seed outputs before vs after;
  - a seeded request alone vs inside a 64-request mixed batch under batch invariance;
  - run-to-run reproducibility of unseeded requests over two server launches.
- Train/inference parity: the verl GRPO recipe's quick alignment gate (rollout vs actor `probs_diff`), with rollout dumps to count distinct samples per group.

The head `e7fbd79895` adds a merge of main and the 3-line CPU worker change; `torch_utils.py`, `gpu_worker.py` and the test are identical to what was measured. The CPU worker change and the merged head have not been run.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Keep store pins and AbortAck until NIXL transfers stop
author: apex-mochen
body:
## Overview

The P2P producer released store pins, and sent `AbortAck` to the consumer, while its NIXL WRITEs could still be running. Neither cancelling the handle nor removing the remote peer stops a running WRITE with the UCX backend. This PR keeps the pins, and holds back `AbortAck`, until NIXL reports each transfer terminal. Addresses #59569 and the review on this PR. The consumer-side counterpart is tracked in #61532.

## Claims

- `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` releases only transfers that are no longer `PROC`/`PEND`. Previously it reported running WRITEs as cancelled, because `release_xfer_handle` never fails for an in-progress UCX request.
- A round whose store timed out, or which the consumer aborted, fails its jobs but keeps the pins of jobs that inflight transfers still read, until those transfers are terminal. Late completions settle each job exactly once, and new supply cannot restart such a round.
- The abort drain no longer falls back to `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `AbortAck` after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. Past the timeout it logs once and keeps retrying. `AbortAck` is sent only when no transfer of the round can still write to the consumer.
- Wait-mode cancel retries are paced to one attempt per round per 100 ms, shared by the store-timeout sweep and the abort drain.
- When one transfer of a round fails, the round's other transfers are no longer cancelled with `mode="immediate"`. The round is marked cancelled instead: their pins and the round's `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)` wait until they are terminal.
- `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` from `check_xfer_state`, which NIXL raises when the peer process is gone, is treated as a terminal failure, so a dead peer no longer pins its transfers until the session closes.

## Validation

Real NIXL 1.4.1, UCX over TCP, CPU DRAM. This is not RDMA hardware.

| scenario | result |
|---|---|
| 512 MiB WRITE, old `cancel(mode="wait")` | returned `[]` while `PROC` in 5/5 runs; all bytes landed afterwards |
| 512 MiB WRITE, new `cancel(mode="wait")` | returned the tid as still inflight in 5/5 runs; `poll()` reported DONE only after all 512 MiB landed |
| 512 MiB WRITE, `remove_remote_peer` | returned with 14–392 MB landed in 5/5 runs; the rest still landed, and the handle then raises `nixlNotFoundError` |
| 1 GiB WRITE stalled by SIGSTOPping the target, then `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `remove_remote_peer`, then resume | 64/64 blocks still landed |
| stalled WRITE, target left stopped | stays `PROC` for 60 s, no timeout of its own |
| stalled WRITE, target SIGKILLed | `check_xfer_state` raises `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` |

Unit tests use the fake transport in `test_sessions.py` and a mocked NIXL agent in `test_data_transport.py`. The new behavior tests fail on the respective previous logic and pass now.

```sh
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q
# head 387b0ba092 (agent-run):  486 passed, 1 skipped
# head 84ec0d792f (I ran it myself, and the agent independently): 484 passed, 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 78.57s
```

ruff 0.14.0 and mypy 1.20.2 (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12`) are clean.

Not done: RDMA/InfiniBand hardware, GPU memory, serving load or model evaluation.

## Details

**Root cause.** `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` relied on `release_xfer_handle` raising for a transfer that is still running. With UCX it never raises: `nixlUcxBackendReqH::release` calls `ucp_request_cancel`, which does nothing for an RMA PUT, then frees the request and returns success. The producer therefore treated running WRITEs as cancelled, released their store pins, and acked aborts while bytes were still landing. `remove_remote_peer` → `invalidateRemoteMD` only drops the connection entry, and the endpoint is later closed in flush mode, so outstanding writes complete rather than stop. That rules out the suggested "tear down the peer, then ack" fallback.

**Abort flow after this change.**
1. The consumer sends `AbortFetchMsg`.
2. The producer marks the round cancelled, fails the jobs no transfer reads, and keeps the rest pinned. A failed transfer takes its round down the same path.
3. It retries `cancel(mode="wait")` at the paced rate. A transfer leaves only when NIXL reports it terminal, or the peer is gone.
4. When no transfer of the round remains, the producer releases the remaining pins and sends `AbortAckMsg`. An aborted round sends no `TransferDoneMsg`.

**Tradeoff.** There is no hard deadline on the producer side. If a peer stays alive but the WRITE never progresses, the pins stay held, with one warning after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. A bound would need a transport primitive that guarantees a running WRITE has stopped. An awaited forced endpoint close (`UCP_EP_CLOSE_FLAG_FORCE`) might be one, but NIXL does not expose it. The consumer still gives up after `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S` and frees its slots; that is the open issue #61532.

The `store_timed_out` flag on a round is renamed `cancelled`, because it now covers aborts and failed transfers as well. All three paths share it: jobs no transfer reads fail at once, and the others keep their pins until their transfers are terminal.

The remote-disconnect check matches the binding's class name or the `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` status code, so the NIXL bindings are not imported in this module. An error it does not recognize keeps the transfer inflight, which is the conservative side.

The shutdown drain in `manager.py` still falls back to `mode="immediate"` after `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`, because the engine is exiting. Only its docstring is updated.

This is distinct from #59329, which withdraws timed-out parked supply before Fetch. Its withdrawal set must be derived from the results actually emitted (`{r.job_id for r in results}`), so that unconfirmed inflight jobs are not removed from the round's pending jobs. Whichever PR merges second needs that adjustment.

AI assistance was used for the investigation, implementation, tests and this description.

Fix the Nemotron Parse 2.0 multimodal test failure:

`DuplicatePatternError`

- The tokenizer loaded successfully with `tokenizers==0.23.2`.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Apply PEFT rank_pattern / alpha_pattern scaling per module
author: surajsharan
body:
## Overview

PEFT adapters can set a per-module rank and alpha with `rank_pattern` / `alpha_pattern`. vLLM ignored both and applied the global `lora_alpha / r` everywhere, so those modules were served with the wrong scaling and no warning. This applies PEFT's per-module rank and scaling when loading the adapter.

Part of #59799 (the scaling and `max_lora_rank` parts; the bare `AssertionError` for 3D MoE adapters on non-3D models is left for a follow-up).

## Claims

- Adapters with `rank_pattern` / `alpha_pattern` now match PEFT's outputs (dense and MoE, including PEFT's MoE docs recipe of `rank_pattern = r // num_experts` on the experts).
- MoE packing (`pack_moe`, `pack_moe_stacked`) keeps each projection's scaling instead of copying w1's to w2 and w3.
- `validate_legal` checks the largest rank in `rank_pattern` against `max_lora_rank`. Before, `r=8, rank_pattern={"q_proj": 32}` passed with `max_lora_rank=16` and then killed the engine with a tensor size mismatch.
- No change for adapters without patterns (same code path), or for PEFT `save_as_lora` dynamic-rank adapters (`r=1, lora_alpha=1`, equal per-module `rank_pattern` / `alpha_pattern`), which were already served correctly.

## Validation

vLLM vs PEFT 0.21.2 on an RTX 3090, mean absolute difference of per-token prompt logprobs (the adapter itself moves them by about 0.35; bf16 noise is 0.002 to 0.007):

| adapter | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| tiny Qwen3 dense, `r=16, rank_pattern={"q_proj": 4}` (repro in the issue) | 0.0176 | 0.0019 |
| tiny Qwen3 dense, `r=4, rank_pattern={"q_proj": 16}` | 0.0619 (max 0.46) | 0.0022 |
| tiny Qwen3 dense, dynamic-rank conversion layout | 0.0025 | 0.0025 |
| tiny GPT-OSS, PEFT MoE recipe (3D MoE path) | 0.292 | 0.0078 |
| tiny Qwen3-MoE, PEFT MoE recipe (`enable_mixed_moe_lora_format`) | 0.220 | 0.0127 |

Model evaluation, OLMoE-1B-7B with a LoRA trained using PEFT's MoE recipe (`r=16`, 64 experts, so expert rank 1) for 200 steps on wikitext-2, perplexity on the wikitext-2 test split:

| | perplexity |
|---|---|
| base model, PEFT / vLLM | 13.09 / 13.08 |
| adapter in PEFT | 10.06 |
| adapter in vLLM, main | 11.28 |
| adapter in vLLM, this PR | 10.06 |

Tests:

```text
pytest tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py tests/lora/test_lora_weights.py
26 passed (the 14 new tests fail on main)

pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_lora_huggingface.py tests/lora/test_lora_checkpoints.py tests/lora/test_moe_lora_ep_load.py tests/lora/test_lora_utils.py
40 passed
```

The new tests are CPU-only and run in the existing `tests/lora` CI job. The per-expert (2D) MoE packing change is covered by unit tests only; the end-to-end MoE runs above use PEFT's fused 3D layout. The dense reproducer is in the issue; I can share the MoE and OLMoE scripts on request.

## Details

Root cause: `PEFTHelper` only read `r` and `lora_alpha`, and `LoRALayerWeights.from_config` gave every module `peft_helper.r` and `peft_helper.vllm_lora_scaling_factor`.

- `PEFTHelper` reads `rank_pattern` / `alpha_pattern` and `get_rank_and_scaling(module_name)` resolves them with PEFT's `get_pattern_key` rule (a key matches a suffix of the module name at a `.` boundary; first match in the config's order). For non-overlapping keys this is also what PEFT's planned order-independent matching (huggingface/peft#3818) gives; overlapping keys would need to follow PEFT once that lands.
- Patterns are matched against the checkpoint module name, before the weights mapper renames it (`from_lora_tensors` parses the tensor name once more without the mapper).
- PEFT stores fused MoE expert LoRAs from `target_parameters` as `experts.base_layer` (gate_up_proj) and `experts` (down_proj) and matches patterns against the parameter names, so those two names are mapped back. PEFT nests gate_up_proj as `base_layer` regardless of the order in `target_parameters` (checked), which is also what `_stack_moe_lora_weights` assumes.
- Modules keep their real rank, which also makes the `num_experts = lora_a.shape[0] // rank` fallback in `_stack_moe_lora_weights` correct for adapters with expert rank patterns. `LoRAModel.rank` stays the global `r`; it is only used by `clone()`.

title: [BugFix][DiffusionGemma][CPU] Copy async output snapshots instead of aliasing reused buffers
author: ojeda-e
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59828

## Claims

With async scheduling, the V2 model runner snapshots each step's sampled tokens and counts with `async_copy_to_np()`. It reads them after the next step starts. On GPU, `.to("cpu")` copies into new memory. On CPU it returns the same tensor, and the snapshot aliases the sampler's buffers. DiffusionGemma reuses those buffers on every step, and the next step overwrites the snapshot before it is read.

This is latent on `main`. CPU forces sync scheduling, which reads each output before the next step runs. I found it while testing DiffusionGemma structured reads on CPU with async scheduling enabled, after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59107. Every read returned a phantom first token, overwritten tokens and one logprob row too few.

### Changes in this PR

- `async_copy_to_np()` passes `copy=True`. A CPU snapshot now owns its memory. GPU behavior does not change. The device-to-host copy already allocates.
- Add a regression test to `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`, next to the other V2 model runner tests, instead of a new file. It snapshots a CPU tensor, overwrites the tensor and checks that the snapshot keeps its values.

I checked the other snapshots in `AsyncOutput`. Logprobs, sampling masks and prompt logprobs also alias on CPU. They are safe because their producers allocate new tensors on every step. I left them as is.

No open issue or PR covers this. I searched for `async_copy_to_np`, CPU async aliasing and overwritten sampled tokens. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58082 edits the code next to `async_copy_to_np()` but does not change it.

I used Claude Code to help with this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Validation

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C, Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at e006d761a5, with the real `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` checkpoint in BF16. Unit tests also on macOS (Apple Silicon).

**Unit tests:**

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
```

**End to end:**

1. Sync path, the default on CPU. Run greedy generation with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and a DiffusionGemma structured read (32-token canvas on a 64-token server). Run on `main`, with this PR, and on `main` again for the noise floor. Compare tokens, logprobs and throughput.
2. Async path. Enable async scheduling on CPU with a local change to `CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config()`. Send the same DiffusionGemma read 10 times with a batch of 1 and 10 times with a batch of 4. Compare each read with sync.

## Test Result

Before (`main`, async on CPU), the read's tokens are overwritten. The issue has the details and the `collect_env.py` output.

```text
sync   tokens[:8] [45518, 45518, 107, 148436, 148436, 236787, 11262, 1]   logprob rows 32
async  tokens[:8] [45518, 1, 1, 1, 1, 148436, 236787, 11262]              logprob rows 31
```

After:

- Unit tests: 90 passed. The new test fails on `main` with `assert [1, 1, 1, 1] == [0, 0, 0, 0]`.
- Async: 50/50 reads match sync, up from 0/50. No snapshot changes before it is read, even with the reader delayed by 50 ms.
- Sync: [layer 3 results: tokens and logprobs before and after for both models, throughput against the noise floor]

## Details

On CPU, .to("cpu") returns the same tensor, and with async scheduling the next step overwrites the sampled-token snapshot before it is read. That corrupted every DiffusionGemma read I tested (linked in the issue).

This PR copies in `async_copy_to_np()`, the one place sampler outputs cross the async boundary. GPU behavior does not change. CPU pays one small copy per step. main is unaffected today because CPU forces sync scheduling. Logprob snapshots still alias but stay safe because their producers allocate new tensors.

title: [Bugfix][DeepEP] Upgrade to 2.1 and retain per-context GIN completion ordering
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Upgrade vendored DeepEP to 2.1 (`a56d6156febcd9976e55adc85b5155bfac9f28f8`), which includes the upstream NVLink visibility fix, and retain a smaller patch for per-context GIN completion signaling.

## Claims

- Use upstream flush, NVLink fence, and grid synchronization placement; remove the custom deferred-flush implementation. Completion signals cover every allocated context, while arrival-only barriers use context 0.
- Retain the nine-context allocation for vLLM's direct-mode MoE buffers, matching automatic active-QP selection. Hybrid allocation stays automatic.
- Preserve skipped/already-applied/failed patch diagnostics requested in review, including aborting on failed application. Add the NCCL library search path required by DeepEP 2.1's SONAME linking and document runtime-version requirements.

## Validation

**Current revision: build and offline checks pass. Distributed correctness, model execution, and overhead remain unvalidated on this revision.** GPU attempts were blocked by unavailable capacity and RDMA device admission failures (`no healthy devices present ... rdma/ib`); these are infrastructure failures, not correctness results. Earlier performance numbers do not apply to this upgrade, so this description makes no overhead claim.

| Current-revision check | Result |
|---|---|
| Fresh native wheels, CUDA 13 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130 / SM90 | Built against NCCL 2.30.7 and 2.31.2 |
| Patched world/rail barrier templates, completion and arrival variants | Compiled with nvcc against both NCCL versions |
| Linux patch application, byte-exact header, complete reverse dry-run | Passed; patched header SHA256 `1bc42abd841cc6e9ba6c59b68962d7e260e163a750873bd50633f91e89d0979f` |
| Native import and loaded-NCCL provenance | Passed on two H200 workers with NCCL 2.30.7; distributed operation did not start |
| Installer behavior | Seven paths passed: fresh, already applied, partial, wrong ref, broken patch, missing patch, other project |
| NCCL linker-path selection | Passed for explicit EP root, legacy root, pip metadata, missing installation |
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks | Passed |

Build checks used `uv build --wheel --no-build-isolation` with `EP_NUM_TOPK_IDX_BITS=64`, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0`, and explicit matching NCCL roots. Patch checks used `patch --batch -p1` and `patch --batch --force --reverse --dry-run -p1`. Local validation artifacts retain the source, wheel, NCCL, and resulting-header hashes.

```bash
pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile docker/versions.json \
  docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md \
  tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh \
  tools/ep_kernels/patches/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch
```

Before merge, rerun matched EP8 direct-mode stock/patched correctness at 9/17 contexts, representative direct/hybrid operator timings, and the original vLLM model reproducer on this revision. Ordinary CI does not cover the three-node H200/GDAKI reproducer.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence on the previous DeepEP pin — not validation of this upgrade</summary>

The previous `d4f41e4e` implementation at PR commit `c781de2f82` passed the original DeepSeek-V4-Flash reproducer: DP8/TP1/EP, three H200 nodes (4+2+2), NCCL 2.30.7, direct `deepep_v2`, eager execution. Six rounds of 64 requests completed (384/384); all eight audit ranks saved checkpoints and all three servers exited 0, with no count/slot mismatches, barrier timeouts, or illegal memory accesses. The audit run was not a serving-performance comparison.

The old pristine pin and per-context-only variant had previously faulted. Subsequent isolated controls also reproduced old-pin correctness failures before graph capture/profiling. These results concern the old pin with direct mode explicitly forced; they do not establish that default hybrid deployments are affected or that stock DeepEP 2.1 fails.

</details>

## Details

GIN ordering is per context ([NVIDIA/nccl#2302](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/2302)); a completion signal on context 0 alone does not supply ordering for puts on other contexts. The selected upstream revision already contains the NVLink visibility fence from [DeepEP#715](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/715). The remaining vendor patch signals and waits on each context at data completion, retaining upstream flush/fence placement and adding context information to timeout diagnostics.

The pin also includes runtime-sized NCCL DevComm compatibility and strict-ordering window registration. Builds against NCCL <2.31 require the same runtime NCCL version. Both tested NCCL configurations used rebuilt native extensions. The constructor/combine signatures are unchanged, and dispatch's new optional argument is compatible with vLLM's keyword calls. DeepEP 2.5 removes the ElasticBuffer and legacy APIs used by vLLM, so that broader migration is outside this fix.

This updates the existing PR rather than creating a duplicate. AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation, validation, and this description. The human submitter must review all changed lines and the validation evidence.
