title: [Bugfix][Responses API] Reuse streamed item ids in final harmony response
author: he-yufeng
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the harmony (gpt-oss) part of #59834; #59307 fixed the non-harmony path. When `/v1/responses` streams, `response.completed` rebuilds its output from the harmony messages with `harmony_to_response_output`. That rebuild mints a new item `id` and function `call_id`, which no longer match the ones sent in `response.output_item.added`/`done`, so strict clients abort.

- `_process_harmony_streaming_events` records, for each completed harmony message, the items sent in its `output_item.done` events (`HarmonyContext.streamed_items_by_message`).
- `responses_full_generator` matches each message to its own record by object identity. `reuse_streamed_item_ids` then copies `id`/`call_id` onto that message's rebuilt items by type. Content and `incomplete` status still come from the rebuild. Items that were never streamed (zero-delta) keep a new id.
- Streamed harmony reasoning items now use the `rs_` prefix instead of `msg_`, matching the non-streaming path and the non-harmony path.

Matching per message matters. A built-in `python` call streams as `code_interpreter_call` but is rebuilt as `reasoning`. If ids were matched across messages, that call would take the streamed id of the next reasoning item.

## Testing

`vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b --no-enable-prefix-caching` (1x H200), then the request from the issue:

```bash
curl -sN localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "openai/gpt-oss-20b", "stream": true,
  "input": "Call the get_weather tool for Paris. You must call the tool now.",
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object",
    "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}]
}' | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | jq -c '
  if .type == "response.output_item.done" then ["done", .item.type, .item.id, .item.call_id]
  elif .type == "response.completed" then .response.output[] | ["completed", .type, .id, .call_id]
  else empty end'
```

main (5f30fc7): `completed` changes every id.
```
["done","reasoning","msg_832f7cd8a3888df4",null]
["done","function_call","fc_8019379c1a695c28","call_b07a9991be290d4c"]
["completed","reasoning","rs_b5c9be54d08ca702",null]
["completed","function_call","fc_bc041d3276faf22e","call_bc041d3276faf22e"]
```
This PR: `completed` keeps the streamed ids.
```
["done","reasoning","rs_a972e97aaf1f0eb1",null]
["done","function_call","fc_be95d8cf99657077","call_84160cffacc40ff2"]
["completed","reasoning","rs_a972e97aaf1f0eb1",null]
["completed","function_call","fc_be95d8cf99657077","call_84160cffacc40ff2"]
```

I ran the same check, 3 times each, on a forced tool call, a reasoning + text answer, and a `max_output_tokens=40` cut-off (`incomplete`). Results: main had id mismatches in 9/9 runs, and this PR in 0/9.

Other tests:
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py`: 64 passed. The 2 new tests fail on main.
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony.py` (gpt-oss-20b e2e): 37 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xpassed on both main and this PR.

No change to generated content: only item ids change, so no eval is needed.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Pass through raw characters in byte-level decode
author: BugenZhao
body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend's byte-level decode fast path turns raw whitespace in added tokens into NUL bytes. Pass those characters through, as HuggingFace `tokenizers` does.

## Claims

- Non-special added tokens whose content has a raw space, newline, or other character the GPT-2 byte table never emits now decode verbatim instead of as `\0`.
- Fixes code indentation for GPT-NeoX-tokenizer models (Pythia, OLMoE, Mamba), whose whitespace-run added tokens decode to runs of `\0` on `main`.
- Fixes tool-call parsing when the parser's markup is such a token: a checkpoint with `<parameter name="` / `\n</parameter>`-style added tokens returned every tool call with `"arguments": "{}"` from the Rust frontend, while Python parsed them correctly from the same token IDs.

## Validation

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-tokenizer
cargo clippy -p vllm-tokenizer --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

- `vllm-tokenizer`: 96 passed. The new `added_tokens_with_raw_whitespace_decode_verbatim` fails on `main` with `left: "<parameter\0name=\"city\">\nParis\0</parameter>…"` and passes here; it checks the fastokens fast path and the HF backend against the same text, including an added token `\ncafé` that a per-character pass-through decodes as `\ncaf�`.
- Real tokenizer, out of tree: a scratch crate with a path dependency on `vllm-tokenizer` decodes `def f(x):\n        if x:\n                return x\n` with `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct`'s `tokenizer.json` (IDs 50270 and 50262 are 8- and 16-space added tokens):
  - `main`: `"def f(x):\n\0\0\0\0\0\0\0\0if x:\n\0\0\0…\0return x\n"`
  - this PR: identical to the HF backend and the original text.
- End to end, on the checkpoint with tool-call markup tokens (GB200, TP4): prompt and generated token IDs were identical between the Python and Rust frontends, and the Rust raw completion text showed the `\0` in place of the space and newline. That run predates this patch; the unit test reproduces the same decoded string.

## Details

`CHAR_TO_BYTE` is a flat reverse table over U+0000..U+0143, filled only at the 256 codepoints the GPT-2 byte-to-unicode map emits. Every other slot was `0`, so a codepoint like U+0020 or U+000A mapped to byte 0 instead of falling through to the pass-through branch that already handles non-GPT-2 codepoints such as DeepSeek's `｜` and `▁`. Byte-level vocab entries never contain those codepoints, but added tokens store raw text, and `id_to_token` returns that text unchanged. HuggingFace's `ByteLevel` decoder passes a token through verbatim when any of its characters is unmapped, so the Python frontend was unaffected.

The table now stores `Option<u8>`, and a token with any `None` or out-of-table codepoint passes through whole, as in HF. Characters the table does emit in the same token, such as `Ġ` or `é`, therefore stay verbatim; previously, out-of-table codepoints such as DeepSeek's passed through one character at a time. The common path still does one table lookup per character.

The fast path was written to match `fastokens::decoders::ByteLevelDecoder`, and fastokens 0.2.1 has the same table; that will be fixed there separately. vLLM only reaches fastokens' decoder for decoders that are not a single `ByteLevel` stage, so the common byte-level tokenizers are covered by this change.

Duplicate check: no open PR touches `byte_level_decode.rs` or byte-level decoding of added tokens.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Release pending CPU lookup pins on cache reset
author: zupengwang
body:
## Overview

Release SimpleCPUOffload lookup-only CPU block references during cache reset. A request waiting for GPU allocation can otherwise prevent `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` from succeeding even after GPU blocks and in-flight transfers have drained.

## Claims

- Reset releases temporary CPU lookup pins and invalidates their saved lookup state.
- Existing in-flight DMA references remain protected until completion.
- A deterministic regression covers eager/lazy modes and one/two cache groups.

## Validation

Validated against upstream `5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c`, using its matching precompiled native extensions.

| Check | Unpatched + regression | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| New reset regression | 4 assertion failures (`reset()` returns False) | 4 pass within the full scheduler suite |
| Scheduler, KV events, connector and metrics suites | — | 92 passed |
| CUDA worker suite, RTX 4090 | — | 21 passed |
| Real Scheduler allocation-pressure diagnostic | Reset fails after GPU blocks are released | Reset succeeds; retry has no stale CPU hit |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct GPU diagnostic | 16 lookup references prevent reset | References released; reset and subsequent generation pass |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -k test_reset_releases_pending_cpu_hits
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
```

All applicable changed-file hooks, mypy 3.10/3.12 and `git diff --check` passed. The existing Buildkite KV Offload suite collects the new test; test tethering passed. Upstream CI has not run for this candidate.

The GPU diagnostic used MRV2, FP16, TP=1, eager execution and 128 MiB each of GPU/CPU KV cache. After a real CPU store/load round trip with 256 cached tokens, it explicitly paused a queued request after the production CPU lookup. Baseline reset returned False; the patch released all 16 lookup pins, reset successfully and generated the same token `[19]` with zero cached tokens. Actual allocation pressure is covered separately by the real Scheduler diagnostic, whose worker token output is synthetic. This is a focused correctness check, not a performance or broad model-quality claim. Multi-node, disk/GDS and other GPU backends were not validated.

## Details

`get_num_new_matched_tokens()` pins matching CPU blocks until `update_state_after_alloc()` consumes the lookup. Failed GPU allocation leaves that lookup in `_pending_cpu_hits`. Reset already abandons transfers safely but omitted these pre-allocation references.

Reuse `_free_pending_cpu_hit()` before clearing the pending lookup map. These references have no associated worker DMA; submitted transfers retain their separate pins and existing completion-based cleanup. A waiting request performs a fresh lookup when scheduling resumes. No API, storage format or normal scheduling policy changes are introduced.

Duplicate screening on 2026-10-03 covered open/closed/merged PRs, related issues, recent commits and the contributor's existing PRs. [#42289](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42289) introduced temporary lookup pins; [#39726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39726) introduced reset support. Both are merged. The active [#57816](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57816) addresses eager-store placement after MRV2 preemption, a different state transition. No active implementation of this lookup-pin reset fix was found. This draft does not claim to close an existing issue.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Count heartbeats as remote engine activity
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

`_send_heartbeats` does not stamp `_engine_last_active`, so a decode instance that holds requests waiting on a prefill engine evicts that engine once `engine_ttl` passes, and the same heartbeat starts a new handshake that reloads every remote agent. This stamps the engine when a heartbeat is sent to it.

Fixes #59871

## Claims

- An engine that this instance is heartbeating is no longer evicted by `_evict_stale_engines`, so heartbeats stop causing an evict-and-handshake cycle every `engine_ttl`.
- Engines with no reads and no heartbeats are still evicted after `engine_ttl`, unchanged.

## Validation

New test `test_heartbeated_engine_is_not_evicted` sends a heartbeat every 5 s for twice the TTL with no reads, and checks that the engine stays registered, no remote agent is removed and no handshake is submitted.

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_heartbeated_engine_is_not_evicted
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `1 failed`: `AssertionError: assert 'remote-engine-1' in defaultdict(<class 'dict'>, {})` |
| this PR | `1 passed` |

NIXL unit files (`test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_nixl_heartbeat.py`, `test_nixl_push_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_handshake_pp_aggregation.py`, `test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `3 failed, 609 passed` |
| this PR | `3 failed, 610 passed` |

The 3 failures are the same on both and come from the CPU-only test machine: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]` and `[None]` (no `torch.ops._C.init_cpu_memory_env`, no Ray on CPU) and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` (gated model, run with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`). Runs were on macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and the manual-stage `mypy-3.12` hook pass.

End-to-end on GPUs. Rig: upstream `main` CI image for `5f30fc7031` (`0.30.1rc1.dev619+g5f30fc703`), NIXL 1.4.1 installed as CI does, bundled UCX 1.22.0, `UCX_TLS=rc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc` over 8 ConnectX RoCE HCAs per node, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B TP1, prefill engines on one H100 node and the decode on another. The change is applied as an overlay of the installed package. Decode with `engine_ttl: 60` and `--max-num-seqs 1`; a 14,000-token request from prefill 2 holds the decode while a request from prefill 1 waits behind it for about 150 s:

| | Handshakes on the decode while the request waits | Decode EngineCore `VmPin` | Requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 2 -> 3 -> 4 (prefill 1 evicted and re-handshaked every ~62 s) | +2,560 KiB per re-handshake | both complete |
| this PR | 2 -> 2 | flat | both complete |

Accuracy, `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_accuracy.py` (gsm8k, P/D through `toy_proxy_server.py`, expected 0.41): `main` 0.4147, this change together with the other two NIXL fixes from the same investigation 0.4139. Both pass.

## Details

Root cause: `_engine_last_active` is stamped at handshake completion (`base_worker.py:1336` on `main`) and when a read is issued (`pull_worker.py:156`). A request queued on the decode side is heartbeated from `on_new_request` until `finished_recving` or abort, and it issues no read until it is scheduled. When `engine_ttl` passes, the heartbeat's `_ensure_handshake` call runs `_evict_stale_engines` first, evicts the engine it is about to heartbeat, finds it missing and submits a handshake.

Why it matters: each reload runs `remove_remote_agent` and `loadRemoteMD` for every remote rank. On a deployment with TP2 decode and PCP8 prefill (8 remote agents per engine per worker), each full re-handshake left 476-481 64 KiB UCX buffers (about 960 VMAs) per worker, which is a separate NIXL/UCX issue. A decode rank that could not admit work kept requests waiting for tens of minutes at a time. It ran about 6 handshakes per hour against about 1 per hour on healthy ranks, and it hit `vm.max_map_count` after about 31 hours. This change removes the heartbeat-driven part of that churn. An engine that is idle with nothing waiting on it is still evicted, and it is handshaked again when new work arrives, which is the intended TTL behavior.

The stamp sits after the pending-handshake `continue`, so it runs only when `_ensure_handshake` returned `None`, which means the engine is in `_remote_agents`. That keeps the invariant #52245 relies on: no `_engine_last_active` entry without a `_remote_agents` entry, since `_cleanup_remote_engine` asserts it.

Tradeoff: a dead prefill engine stays registered while requests still wait on it. Those requests fail their reads, which stops the heartbeat, and #50047 releases a replaced peer without waiting for the TTL.

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR or issue matched `nixl heartbeat`, `engine_ttl`, `engine ttl evict`, `nixl heartbeat engine_ttl`, `engine_ttl heartbeat`, `stale remote engine` or `nixl re-handshake` for this mechanism. Closest precedents are #52245 (same stamp for the push-mode D side) and #54689 (eviction skips engines with in-flight reads).

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Release shared memory on NIXL setup failure
author: DGlan
body:
## Overview

Prevent leaked shared memory when ECCPU scheduler initialization fails with NIXL enabled. The constructor currently raises without releasing the region it has already allocated.

## Claims

- Failed NIXL setup releases the scheduler-owned mmap file, file descriptors, and mapping while preserving the original exception.

## Validation

Review validation with NIXL 1.4.1: the previous constructor test file reproduced the test-order failure (6 passed, 1 failed); importing `data.nixl` before monkeypatching fixes its cached bindings, and all 7 constructor tests pass together. The suites below were rerun after merging upstream main.

The missing-NIXL regression fails against the unchanged scheduler because the mmap file remains, and passes with this fix. A second CPU regression raises during control-transport creation after data transport setup, and checks deregistration, shared-region release, and preservation of the original exception.

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/scheduler \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/test_ec_shared_region.py -q
# 76 passed (NIXL 1.4.1 installed)

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -m cpu_test tests/v1/ec_connector/unit -q
# 62 passed, 350 deselected

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/scheduler/__init__.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.
```


Nearby transport/session/scheduler tests also passed (95 tests):

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_data.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_session.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_control.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_consumer.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_producer.py -q
```

A separate CPU check exercised `ECConnectorFactory` through `ECCPUConnector` using real `VllmConfig`/`ModelConfig` objects and a local tiny Llava configuration, without replacing the shared-memory factory. The unchanged scheduler left the file, two file descriptors, and a mapping after the missing-NIXL error; the fixed scheduler left none, with the same error. Descriptors and mappings were checked through `/proc/self/fd` and `/proc/self/maps`.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cpu, editable source with official v0.30.0 CPU precompiled binaries. Exact-commit CPU binaries were unavailable. NIXL 1.4.1 was installed for this review revision, and the constructor wiring test exercised real NIXL registration and ZMQ session startup. Full GPU serving and cross-process NIXL data transfer were not run; local validation covers scheduler construction and startup-failure cleanup. The new test is selected by the existing CPU EC connector job in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

The region is allocated before `_setup_nixl`; if setup raises, the caller never receives a scheduler to shut down. The constructor owns failure unwinding through `shutdown()`, releasing NIXL resources before the shared region. `_setup_nixl()` propagates errors without a second cleanup handler.

Related: #56507, #56508. The related test/doc PR covers import isolation and documentation, rather than constructor cleanup. Searches for EC scheduler cleanup, NIXL initialization, and shared-memory leaks found no equivalent open PR.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the patch and this review revision, and ran the validation above. The submitting human reviewed the original patch, personally reran its 74-pass/1-skip suite, and authorized this revision to address the review. No inference-output or performance change is claimed.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Build tool-call grammars from the tools the prompt renders
author: JRJRJPRO
body:
## Purpose

Non-Harmony chat templates only render function tools. Responses namespace functions are flattened to `<namespace>__<name>`, and builtin tools (`mcp`, `web_search`, ...) are dropped (`construct_tool_dicts`). The tool-call structural tag was built from every request tool instead, so the grammar and the prompt disagreed:

- **Builtin-only tools:** they produce no grammar rule, so the tag is empty and xgrammar rejects it. Since #56403 this returns `400` for every GLM-4.7 Responses request whose tools are all builtin. PLaMo3, MiMo and HY-V4 fail the same way, and so does any model with `tool_choice="required"` (an opaque `400`, or a bare `AssertionError` inside xgrammar).
- **Namespace functions:** the model is shown them but has no grammar rule for them. Under a constrained grammar it is blocked from calling them, or forced into a different tool. The legacy JSON-schema path, used when strict tool calling is off, silently returned an empty `completed` response for `required` with only builtin tools.

The first commit fixed the GLM-4.7 builder only. This change fixes it at the shared entry point:

- `get_function_tools()` (`vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py`) is the single source of the tools the model is shown. The prompt helpers, `get_structural_tag_tools()` in the structural tag registry, and the legacy JSON-schema `required` path are all built from it, so the prompt and the grammar cannot drift apart.
- Harmony can call builtin tools, so it opts out with `register_vllm_structural_tag("harmony", builtin_tools=True)`.
- When no callable tool remains, `auto` gets no grammar, as before #56403, and `required` or named tool choice returns a `400` with `param: "tool_choice"`.
- The rendered prompt is byte-identical to before.
- The GLM-4.7-only fallback from the first commit is removed: the shared filtering makes it unreachable.

## Test Plan

Live before/after on one H200 with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`. The same 10 requests were sent to main `55b80221ed` with and without this diff, under three server configs:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
# 2) same, with --tool-call-parser glm47 (no reasoning parser): the GLM-4.7 tag path;
#    it fails while preparing the request, before generation, so GLM weights are not needed
# 3) same as 1) with VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0: the legacy JSON-schema path
```

Builtin-only tools:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "input": "What is the capital of France? Answer in one word.",
  "tools": [{"type": "web_search"}], "max_output_tokens": 64}'
```

Function tool plus a namespace tool (also sent with `"parallel_tool_calls": false`, with `"stream": true`, and with only the namespace tool):

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "input": "Look up customer 42 in the CRM.", "tool_choice": "required",
  "tools": [
    {"type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather for a city",
     "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}},
    {"type": "namespace", "name": "crm", "description": "Customer relationship management tools",
     "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "lookup_customer", "description": "Look up a customer record by id",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["id"]}}]}]}'
```

Regression requests: `get_weather` alone with `required` on `/v1/responses`, and a streamed `/v1/chat/completions` call with `get_weather`.

## Test Result

| Config | Request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| glm47 | builtin only, `auto` (with and without `parallel_tool_calls: false`) | `400 Invalid grammar specification: 'triggers'` | `200`, text answer |
| glm47 | namespace tool only, `parallel_tool_calls: false` | `400 Invalid grammar specification: 'triggers'` | `200`, calls `crm.lookup_customer` |
| hermes, glm47 | `get_weather` + `crm` namespace, `required` (also streamed) | calls `get_weather` | calls `crm.lookup_customer` |
| hermes, glm47 | same, `auto` + `parallel_tool_calls: false` (glm47 also plain `auto`) | calls `get_weather` | calls `crm.lookup_customer` |
| hermes, glm47 | builtin only, `required` | `400 Invalid grammar specification: 'triggers'`, `param: null` | `400 tool_choice requires a function call, but tools contains no function tool the model can call.`, `param: "tool_choice"` |
| legacy JSON path | builtin only, `required` | `200` `completed` with empty `output` (schema `anyOf: []`) | the same `400` as above |

On hermes, the namespace requests went from `get_weather({"city": "New York"})` to `lookup_customer({"id": "42"})`, with `namespace: "crm"` in the Responses output.

Hermes with plain `auto` applies no grammar, on main and with this PR. Its namespace requests under plain `auto` and the regression requests produce the same output on both sides; only generated call IDs differ. The glm47 regression output is also identical: `{}` arguments on both sides, because the Qwen model is forced into GLM's call format.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and test this change; the changes were reviewed by a human maintainer.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix speculative block reservations across KV cache groups
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix speculative decode block reservations for asynchronous KV loads with
multiple KV cache groups. Under KV memory pressure, under-reserving these
blocks can leave a request admitted for an asynchronous KV load but unable
to start decoding once the load completes.

## Claims

- Account for every KV cache group using its actual allocation block size.
- Extend the existing promotion-margin regression test to cover single-group,
  multi-group, and mixed-block-size configurations.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

**32 passed.** Pre-commit checks and manual Python 3.12 mypy passed.

Regression controls replace only the reservation method in the test process:

| Implementation | Single group | Multiple groups | Different block sizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original | Pass | Fail | Fail |
| Original × group count | Pass | Pass | Fail |
| This fix | Pass | Pass | Pass |

The broader scheduler/decode/recovery run showed no additional failures:
both the patched implementation and the original reservation method produced
171 passes and the same 46 failing test IDs. Observed environment limitations
included unavailable offline model configurations and insufficient visible
GPUs for parallel tests.

Validation exercises the scheduler and KV allocation paths with simulated
remote completion. Live NIXL P/D and model-level evaluations were not run.

## Details

The existing calculation converts the speculative token margin to blocks
using the scheduler block size once. However, each KV cache group allocates
independently from the shared block pool, and groups may use different
allocation block sizes.

Sum the reservation across cache managers using each manager's block size.
Simply multiplying the old result by the group count is insufficient for
mixed-block-size configurations. The existing conservative reservation
approach is preserved.

The regression test checks admission and subsequent scheduling rather than
asserting the helper's arithmetic directly.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmarks] Name the real cause when the /tokenize alignment probe fails
author: TyroneNel
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`vllm bench serve` aligns `random` / `prefix_repetition` prompts to the server tokenizer through a `/tokenize` probe. Every failure of that probe prints `WARNING: /tokenize unavailable, skipping alignment.`, even when the route exists. This PR names the actual cause instead.

Replaces #58024 (closed when my fork was re-created). Related: #59889 is the server side of the same 404.

## Claims

- A failed probe names its cause: 404 (no route, or `--model` is not a served name), another HTTP status, an unreachable host, or the exception.
- Alignment behavior is unchanged: a failure still skips alignment and never stops the run, and a tokenizer mismatch still re-aligns the prompts.

## Validation

The patched `_align_prompts_to_server_tokenizer` against a local `aiohttp` server for each case (no GPU or model needed):

| Server | Output |
|---|---|
| 404 | ``/tokenize unavailable (404 Not Found: either this server has no /tokenize route, or it does not serve a model named `my-model` (its served names are listed by GET /v1/models))`` |
| 500 | `/tokenize unavailable (HTTP 500)` |
| nothing listening | `http://127.0.0.1:18902 unreachable (ClientConnectorError(... ConnectionRefusedError ...))` |
| tokenizer mismatch (server 6 tokens, local 3) | `tokenizer mismatch (server=6, expected=3), re-aligning prompts.`, then prompt `'a b c'`, `prompt_len=3` |

The 404 on a live server (`--model /models/x --served-model-name my-model`):

```
POST /tokenize {"model":"my-model"}   -> 200
POST /tokenize {"model":"/models/x"}  -> 404 The model `/models/x` does not exist.
```

**Live run on upstream main** (RTX 3090, at the main merge-base `84bcbc626`). The server is `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --api-key test-key`. The client is the same checkout, with the `serve.py` from main or from this PR. All runs use `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 16 --num-prompts 20 --ignore-eos --seed 0` against the same server:

| client | `--model` / `--tokenizer` | probe output | ok / failed | Total input tokens | server `prompt_tokens_total` Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `gpt2` | `tokenizer mismatch (server=696, expected=512), re-aligning prompts.` | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| this PR | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `gpt2` | `tokenizer mismatch (server=696, expected=512), re-aligning prompts.` | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| this PR | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | (no probe line) | 20 / 0 | 10240 | 10240 |
| main | `not-a-served-model` / `gpt2` | `/tokenize unavailable, skipping alignment.` | 0 / 20 | 0 | 0 |
| this PR | `not-a-served-model` / `gpt2` | ``/tokenize unavailable (404 Not Found: either this server has no /tokenize route, or it does not serve a model named `not-a-served-model` (its served names are listed by GET /v1/models)), skipping alignment.`` | 0 / 20 | 0 | 0 |

- Tokenizer mismatch: the server reads the 512 gpt2-token prompt as 696 tokens. After re-alignment, the server counts 10,240 prompt tokens for the 20 requests (512 on average), with and without this PR. I checked the totals, not each request.
- Auth: on this server, `POST /tokenize` without a key returned 200, and `GET /v1/models` without a key returned 401.

`pre-commit` passes. No unit test is added; the harness above can go into `tests/benchmarks/` if you want it in CI.

## Details

**Root cause.** The probe sends `args.model` as the request `model` and catches every exception into one message. With `--served-model-name`, the model check answers 404, which reads as "no `/tokenize` route".

**Review changes.** An earlier revision also sent `OPENAI_API_KEY` with the probe. It is removed: `--api-key` does not guard `/tokenize` on vLLM, and it overrode a lowercase `authorization` passed with `--header`.

title: [Bugfix] Drop enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce from FlashInfer CuteDSL MegaMoE config
author: wangshangsam
body:
## Overview Fixes #59887. `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` (added in #54049) passes `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` to FlashInfer's CuTeDSL MegaMoE config. The pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 calls that field `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, so the backend raises `TypeError` while the layer is built. This PR drops the kwarg and adds a regression test that doesn't need SM100. `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` is unaffected. ## Claims - With the pinned `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` no longer raises `TypeError` when the layer is built. Behavior is as intended: `False` is the field's default in every FlashInfer release from v0.7.0 through v0.7.1. - The fix doesn't depend on the FlashInfer version: 0.7.1 (released 2026-10-09; #60948 bumps the pin) renames the field but keeps its `False` default, and the new test passes against 0.7.1's config types (constructor check only; the backend itself was not run on 0.7.1). With 0.7.1, `main`'s current kwarg becomes valid too; this PR keeps 0.7.0.x working and adds the drift test. - On 4× GB200 at current `main`, with `nvshmem4py` installed and #61041's decoder-replay fix copied in, the backend serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with default CUDA graphs (FULL and PIECEWISE captured). GSM8K is 0.891 (one run), vs 0.901 for `deep_gemm_mega_moe` and 0.910 for the default MoE backend on the same image. - New test `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer`: it builds the adapter against the installed FlashInfer's real config types, without SM100 or multiple GPUs (it also passes with no GPU visible). It lives in `tests/kernels/moe`, which the L4 `kernels-moe-test` job runs; no Buildkite job has run on this PR yet. - **What it catches:** a renamed or removed kwarg in FlashInfer's MoE-EP config types, or removal of the deprecated `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`/`DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig` aliases. Before, these only failed at model load on SM100. - **What it doesn't cover:** `MoEEpTensors` and the megakernel layer's own methods. Only the SM100 e2e test covers those. ## Validation ### Retest at current `main` (3c062d391d) `main` was merged into this branch (no conflicts); the PR still changes only `flashinfer_moe_ep.py` (the kwarg) and its test. All runs were on 4× GB200 (docker, with the Slurm job's IMEX channel) in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:f853a683…`, built from 7d0b4e57aa. That image's `flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and `vllm/config/kernel.py` are identical to `main`'s. - **base:** the image as is. - **fix:** the image with this PR's `flashinfer_moe_ep.py` copied over the installed one. - Tests ran from this branch's `tests/` tree. The CuTeDSL path also needs `nvshmem4py` (#59903, installed by #59912), so `nvshmem4py-cu13` (0.4.0) was installed in the container. | Check | base | fix | |---|---|---| | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer` | `[cutedsl]` ❌ `TypeError: Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce'`; `[deep_gemm]` ✅ | ✅ 2/2; also 2/2 with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=` | | Same, with `flashinfer-python==0.7.1` installed (constructor check only; run with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`, and with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1` because the image's `flashinfer-cubin` is 0.7.0.post1) | ✅ 2/2 | ✅ 2/2 | | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k "test_init_warmup and cutedsl"` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | ❌ same `TypeError` (ran the 2-GPU dsv4-flash case) | ✅ 8/8, run twice | | DEP=4 serve, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, default CUDA graphs | all 4 DP ranks raise the same `TypeError` right after the checkpoint loads; the server exits about 2 minutes in | serves (FULL and PIECEWISE graphs captured); answers correct; GSM8K **0.891** | - **Serve command:** `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` (revision `2cba9e42`, pre-downloaded; containers run with `--ipc=host` so the DP replicas share the Engram tables through `/dev/shm`). Startup takes about 10 minutes, which can exceed the default 600 s engine-ready timeout. - **GSM8K:** `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 128`, one run. For reference, on the same image the default MoE backend scored 0.910 and `deep_gemm_mega_moe` 0.901 (#61041's validation). One run's standard error is about 0.008 (about 0.012 for a two-run difference), so the gap to the default is about 1.6 SE; other runs of this backend scored 0.888–0.899 (#59912's retest, #61041). The fix run also had #61041's one-file decoder-replay fix copied in: without it, every FlashInfer MegaMoE backend crashes under GSM8K load on current `main` (#61040), independent of this PR. - **Also covered:** #59912's retest, on images built from `main` c41b2639e2 + #59912 + this PR, passed the kwargs test (2/2) and the CuTeDSL e2e tests (8/8) on GB200, GB300 and B200, and, with the same decoder-replay fix, served DEP=4/8/16 with GSM8K 0.888–0.897. - **pre-commit:** `pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/flashinfer_moe_ep.py` passes. - **pytest:** run from `tests/` with `-v -rs --timeout=900`.
Earlier validation (at 7712663, on main 84bcbc6264; locally built images) All runs were on 4× GB200. Images were built from `docker/Dockerfile` with the arm64 CI build args, with these deviations: `torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0`, no sccache, `RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false`, local `max_jobs`/`nvcc_threads`, and an added `vllm-openai` target. **fix** from this branch at 7712663 (35b3ca5 only edits a comment and docstrings), **base** from `main` @ 84bcbc6264. | Test | base (main) | fix | |---|---|---| | `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[cutedsl]` | ❌ `TypeError: Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce'` | ✅ | | `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[deep_gemm]` | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs[*-cutedsl-*]` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | ❌ same `TypeError` in every worker | ✅ 8/8 (one case hung once and passed on retry) | Serving DEP=4: base, with the default cudagraph mode, crashed on every DP rank with the `TypeError` before graph capture. Fix, with `--compilation-config.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (full-graph capture failed in that environment), served, answered correctly, and scored GSM8K 0.898 (`flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`) vs 0.901 for the default backend with the same flag. `nvshmem4py-cu13==0.4.0` was installed in a test-only layer, and containers got the Slurm job's IMEX channel (without it NVSHMEM's fabric `cuMemCreate` fails with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`).
## Details **Root cause.** FlashInfer renamed `in_kernel_fc2_reduce` to `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4604, first shipped in v0.7.1rc1 and now in v0.7.1. The adapter was written against the new name while vLLM still pins 0.7.0.post1 (`requirements/cuda.txt`). Every other kwarg and method the adapter uses on FlashInfer's MoE-EP types is present in both 0.7.0.post1 and 0.7.1, so this was the only mismatch. **Why CI missed it.** The only test that constructs the adapter, `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs`, needs SM100 and 2+ GPUs. `kernels-moe-test` runs on L4, so it always skips there, and no B200 job runs this file. The new test fakes four things: - `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpMegaLayer`, which allocates symmetric memory; - the EP group; - the device index; - `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer`, which imports DeepGEMM. Everything FlashInfer receives is its own config dataclasses plus a real `MoEWeightPack`. **Relation to #60948 (FlashInfer 0.7.1).** #60948 bumps the pin to 0.7.1 and doesn't touch `flashinfer_moe_ep.py`; the two PRs don't conflict and pass in either order. After #60948, `main`'s explicit `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce=False` would be valid; dropping it still gives the same `False` default (0.7.1 documents the flag as an opt-in to nondeterministic accumulation), keeps the backend working on 0.7.0.x, and the new test guards both versions. **Alternatives considered.** *Version-gate the kwarg name:* unnecessary, since the value equals the default. **Related, found while validating.** - **`nvshmem4py` packaging:** vLLM's images don't ship `nvshmem4py`, so without it `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` fails at FlashInfer's runtime bootstrap. Tracked in #59903, fixed by #59912. - **Decoder replay under load:** on current `main`, DeepSeek-V4.1 with either FlashInfer MegaMoE backend crashes under GSM8K load in the decoder-replay CUDA graph. Tracked in #61040, fixed by #61041. - **Earlier limitations that no longer reproduce at current `main`:** full CUDA-graph capture with this backend (FULL graphs captured above), and the DeepGEMM "type Runtime is already registered" import error (#59904; the vendored DeepGEMM moved to `TORCH_LIBRARY` in #48962). The one-off 2-GPU e2e hang did not recur in 16 cases. - The adapter still imports FlashInfer's deprecated `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`/`DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig` aliases, which FlashInfer has scheduled for removal. Switching to the `Sm100_*` names is a follow-up; the new test would flag the removal. **Duplicate check.** Apart from #59887, which I filed for this bug, no open or closed issue or PR mentions `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` or `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig` as a fix for it. #60948 (FlashInfer 0.7.1 bump) makes `main`'s kwarg valid but leaves 0.7.0.x broken and adds no test. ---

title: [Bugfix] Scope deprecated CLI argument warnings to the parser that defines them
author: TylerMa-debugg
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #48094 (also reported earlier as #42852). On Python 3.10–3.12, `vllm chat` and `vllm complete` print a spurious `argument 'url' is deprecated` warning on every run, because `run-batch`'s deprecated `--url` leaks into sibling subcommands.

cc @hmellor

## Claims

- `vllm chat` / `vllm complete` no longer warn that their own (valid) `--url` is deprecated.
- Deprecated arguments still warn for the subcommand that defines them (`vllm run-batch --url ...` still warns once).
- Each parser now only checks its own deprecated arguments, so the same leak can't happen for future deprecated arguments, and the top-level parser no longer re-checks a subcommand's arguments.

## Validation

Python 3.12.3 (WSL2 Ubuntu), editable install with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

New regression test `test_deprecated_arg_scoped_to_subcommand`:

```
pytest tests/utils_/test_argparse_utils.py -k deprecated   # on main: 1 failed
pytest tests/utils_/test_argparse_utils.py                 # with this PR: 24 passed
```

End-to-end, counting `argument 'url' is deprecated` lines (no server or GPU needed):

| Command | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm chat --url http://127.0.0.1:9/v1` | 1 | 0 |
| `vllm complete --url http://127.0.0.1:9/v1` | 1 | 0 |
| `vllm run-batch -i x.jsonl -o y.jsonl --model facebook/opt-125m --url 1.2.3.4` | 1 | 1 |

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>` (ruff, mypy 3.10–3.13, etc.) pass.

## Details

**Root cause.** Below Python 3.13, `FlexibleArgumentParser` emulates `add_argument(..., deprecated=True)` by recording the action in `_deprecated`, a set defined on the class and therefore shared by every parser and subparser. `parse_known_args` then walks that whole set. `run-batch` marks its `--url` (default `0.0.0.0`) as deprecated via `frontend_kwargs["url"]["deprecated"] = True`, and since `vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py` builds every subcommand's parser on each invocation, that action is always in the set. When `chat`/`complete` parse their own `--url` (default `http://localhost:8000/v1`), the value never equals run-batch's default, so the warning fires. (This is also why a grep for `deprecated=True` doesn't find it.)

**Fix.** Make `_deprecated` an instance variable. It is created at the top of `__init__`, because `ArgumentParser.__init__` already adds argument groups and `-h`, and `_FlexibleArgumentGroup` shares its parser's set, because argparse groups don't keep a reference to their container. `_SubParsersAction` calls each subparser's own `parse_known_args`, so a subcommand's deprecated arguments are only checked when that subcommand is parsed. The warning condition (value differs from the default) is unchanged. Python 3.13+ is unaffected since it uses argparse's native support.

**Prior work.** #42854 proposed the same per-instance fix but was auto-closed as stale without a review. No other open PR addresses this issue.

AI-assisted; I reviewed and tested all changes.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Validate incompatible MoE adapter formats
author: Btwestyo
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reject fused 3D MoE LoRA weights on a 2D wrapper when the required format settings are missing, with an error naming both settings.

Addresses the actionable-error follow-up in item 4 of #59799; complements #59801.

## Claims

- Detect this incompatible layout before adapter registration and activation.
- Explain how to enable `enable_mixed_moe_lora_format` and set `is_3d_lora_weight`.
- Check during worker loading before replacing or evicting a cached adapter.

## Validation

Validated on one NVIDIA A10G (AWS g5.2xlarge), FP16, using a tiny random Qwen3-MoE model and a PEFT 0.21.2 adapter, based on commit `6f75cc7d5d1b5adfb399cbf79a8231ae66844fcf`.

These results cover the patch committed as `2f8c900063f3`, before the subsequent merge of `main` into this branch. They are not CI results for the updated PR head.

- `python -m pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py -v`: **28 passed**, including eight new cases.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/model_manager.py vllm/lora/worker_manager.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py docs/features/lora.md`: all applicable hooks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

| Full-engine case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original reproducer, missing both settings | Bare assertion replaced by a descriptive worker `ValueError`; generation still ends with `EngineDeadError`. |
| Original reproducer, both settings enabled | Generates `[190, 737, 34, 78]`, matching the baseline control. |
| Dynamic `add_lora`, each of the three missing-flag combinations | Returns the actionable error; generation continues afterward. |
| Dynamic rejection with a valid adapter already filling the cache | Valid adapter ID remains registered; deterministic generation is unchanged. |

The original generation reproducer is in #59799; these runs use FP16 on the
A10G. The dynamic-loading harness below is self-contained:

```sh
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn python validate_59799.py
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn python validate_59799.py --mixed
```

Both commands complete successfully. New unit cases run in the existing LoRA CI
job. Multi-GPU behavior and HTTP serving were not tested.

This is a loading/activation smoke test, not a model-quality evaluation. The change does not alter LoRA scaling, conversion or kernels.

<details>
<summary>Dynamic-loading validation harness (save as validate_59799.py)</summary>

```python
"""Validate dynamic loading errors and continued generation on a CUDA engine."""
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import torch
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, Qwen3MoeConfig
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest


def make_checkpoint(directory):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    config = Qwen3MoeConfig(
        vocab_size=1024, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512,
        moe_intermediate_size=128, num_hidden_layers=2,
        num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=64,
        num_experts=8, num_experts_per_tok=2, tie_word_embeddings=False,
    )
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(config, dtype=torch.float16)
    model.save_pretrained(directory / "base")
    lora = LoraConfig(
        r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=[],
        target_parameters=["mlp.experts.gate_up_proj", "mlp.experts.down_proj"],
    )
    get_peft_model(model, lora).save_pretrained(directory / "lora")

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--mixed", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        directory = Path(tmp)
        make_checkpoint(directory)
        llm = LLM(str(directory / "base"), skip_tokenizer_init=True,
                  dtype="float16", enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16,
                  max_cpu_loras=1, max_loras=1, max_model_len=256,
                  gpu_memory_utilization=0.3, enforce_eager=True,
                  enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=args.mixed)
        prompt = TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=list(range(10, 40)))
        params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, temperature=0, detokenize=False)
        engine = llm.llm_engine
        good = LoRARequest("good", 1, str(directory / "lora"), is_3d_lora_weight=True)
        if args.mixed:
            assert engine.add_lora(good)
            before = llm.generate(prompt, params, lora_request=good)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            expected_ids = {1}
        else:
            before = llm.generate(prompt, params)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            expected_ids = set()
        declarations = [False] if args.mixed else [False, True]
        for declared in declarations:
            bad = LoRARequest("bad", 2, str(directory / "lora"), is_3d_lora_weight=declared)
            try:
                engine.add_lora(bad)
            except Exception as exc:
                message = str(exc)
                assert "enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=True" in message, message
                assert "is_3d_lora_weight=True" in message, message
                print("EXPECTED REJECTION:", type(exc).__name__, message, flush=True)
            else:
                raise AssertionError("Incompatible adapter was accepted")
            actual_ids = engine.list_loras()
            print("REGISTERED ADAPTERS:", repr(actual_ids), flush=True)
            assert set(actual_ids) == expected_ids, actual_ids
            after = llm.generate(prompt, params, lora_request=good if args.mixed else None)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            assert after == before, (before, after)
            print("PASS: engine remains usable; adapters", expected_ids, "tokens", after, flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Details

Without both format settings, fused expert tensors reach `FusedMoEWithLoRA.set_lora`, which expects packed lists and raises a bare assertion. The validator checks actual loaded weights and wrapper type, preserving native 3D wrappers and the supported mixed-format conversion path. Per-expert and attention-only adapters are not rejected.

The check runs on adapter loading, not each token. It is deliberately limited to this layout mismatch; it does not provide general adapter validation or change exception handling during generation. Lazy loading through `LLM.generate()` can still terminate the engine, now with actionable configuration guidance in the worker error.

No duplication: #59801 handles per-module scaling and rank validation and explicitly leaves this error-handling follow-up open. #52198 handles tensor orientation, and #59915 handles Inkling-specific conversion.

AI assistance: Codex was used for implementation, regression tests, and GPU validation.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Recover genuine tool calls after unclosed Qwen3 <function= opener in prose
author: abhayjoshi201
body:
## Overview

Fixes #58227. Recovers subsequent genuine tool calls in `Qwen3Parser` (`qwen3_config`) when the model writes an unclosed `<tool_call>` + `<function=...` header in prose, while preserving literal `<tool_call>` strings inside `<parameter=...>` values.

## Claims

- Recovers genuine `<tool_call>\n<function=...>` calls that follow an unclosed `<tool_call>\n<function=function_name` (without `>`) or `<tool_call>\n<function=function_name>` (with `>`) written in prose or reasoning, in both non-streaming (`extract_tool_calls`) and streaming (`parse_delta`) modes.
- Preserves literal `<tool_call>` text inside parameter values (e.g. `<tool_call><function=write_file><parameter=content>Document <tool_call> usage</parameter></function></tool_call>`) without truncating the argument span.
- Keeps the fix localized to `qwen3_config` in `vllm/parser/qwen3.py` with zero changes to core engine files.

## Validation

Reproduced the failure from #58227 and verified the fix + positive-control cases in both non-streaming and streaming modes:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py -v
# 72 passed in 0.14s (including 6 new non-streaming and streaming test cases)

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/ -q
# 5733 passed in 6.53s

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/parser/qwen3.py tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py
# ruff check, ruff format, typos, check-test-tethering, mypy, SPDX headers: Passed
```

| Case | Baseline (`main`) | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Unclosed `<tool_call>\n<function=function_name` (no `>`) before real `<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>...` | Real `get_weather` call swallowed into `function_name` | `get_weather` emitted with `{"city": "Tokyo"}` |
| Unclosed `<tool_call>\n<function=function_name>` (with `>`) before real `<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>...` | Real `get_weather` call swallowed into `function_name` | `get_weather` emitted with `{"city": "Tokyo"}` |
| Positive control: `<parameter=content>Document <tool_call> usage</parameter>` | `{"content": "Document <tool_call> usage"}` | `{"content": "Document <tool_call> usage"}` (unchanged) |

*Note on model evaluation:* This change is strictly in the deterministic `qwen3_config` parser state machine (`vllm/parser/qwen3.py`) and does not modify model weights, kernels, or logits; correctness is validated across the non-streaming and streaming parser test suites.

## Details

### Root Cause
In `qwen3_config`, once `<tool_call>` (`TOOL_START`) transitions to `ParserState.TOOL_PREAMBLE` and `<function=` (`FUNC_PREFIX`) transitions to `ParserState.TOOL_NAME`:
1. If the prose example never writes `>` (`FUNC_NAME_END`), `TOOL_NAME` only had a transition on `FUNC_NAME_END` (`>`). Any later `</think>`, `<tool_call>`, or `<function=get_weather>` was accumulated into `TOOL_NAME` until the first `>` of the genuine tool call, naming the call after the prose fragment and swallowing the genuine function name.
2. If the prose example writes `<function=function_name>` (`ParserState.TOOL_ARGS`) without `</function>` or `</tool_call>`, `TOOL_ARGS` only exited on `FUNC_END` (`</function>`) or `TOOL_END` (`</tool_call>`). A subsequent genuine `<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>` was swallowed as part of the unclosed span's argument body.

### Design & Trade-offs
- **Why transition `(ParserState.TOOL_ARGS, "FUNC_PREFIX")` instead of `(ParserState.TOOL_ARGS, "TOOL_START")`:** As noted in [#58227 (comment)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58227#issuecomment-5851527797), transitioning out of `TOOL_ARGS` on `TOOL_START` (`<tool_call>`) truncates valid tool calls whose parameter value contains literal `<tool_call>` (such as `<parameter=content>Document <tool_call> usage</parameter>`). Because a genuine Qwen3 tool call always begins its header with `<function=` (`FUNC_PREFIX`), transitioning `(TOOL_ARGS, "FUNC_PREFIX") -> TOOL_NAME` with `(EventType.TOOL_CALL_END, EventType.TOOL_CALL_START)` recovers the subsequent real tool call while leaving `<tool_call>` inside `<parameter=...>` untouched as content.
- **Why `ParserState.TOOL_NAME` transitions on `TOOL_END`, `TOOL_START`, and `FUNC_PREFIX`:** A valid function identifier cannot contain `<tool_call>`, `</tool_call>`, or `<function=`, so encountering any of those terminals before `>` unambiguously indicates the `<function=...` header was unclosed.
- **Why this does not duplicate existing PRs:**
  - #57553 handles markdown code fences (```` ``` ````), not unfenced prose.
  - #56661 checks for a `<function=` header before committing a span, which is already present in `<function=function_name`.
  - #50986 (`validate_tool_names`) filters unknown tool names (`function_name`), which works together with this PR: once this PR splits the unclosed prose span from the subsequent genuine `get_weather` span, `get_weather` is preserved even when `function_name` is filtered out.
  - #59821 defers `<tool_call>` inside `<think>...</think>` blocks; this PR also recovers unclosed `<tool_call>\n<function=...` spans in non-thinking mode or post-`</think>` assistant prose without buffering the entire reasoning stream.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve fp16 in legacy fused MoE LoRA
author: sudhanshu112233shukla
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59920. Preserve the input dtype in the legacy fused MoE LoRA GEMM instead of unconditionally converting operands to bfloat16.

## Claims
 Prevents silent fp16-to-bfloat16 conversion in the legacy shrink/expand kernel.
Keeps both Triton descriptor and pointer-load paths aligned with the hidden-state input dtype.
Extends large-rank fallback correctness coverage to fp16 and bf16.

## Validation

 `uv run --no-sync ruff check vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`
 `uv run --no-sync ruff format --check ...`
 `uv run --no-sync python -m compileall -q vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`
 The focused Triton test collection/execution could not run in this Windows CPU-only environment: vLLM native extension and `uvloop` are unavailable. CI or an Intel/NVIDIA/AMD GPU runner must execute `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`.
 No kernel benchmark was claimed; this is a correctness fix.

## Details

The legacy two-kernel path previously cast both dot operands to `tl.bfloat16` to work around ROCm type inference across TMA and pointer-load branches. That changes fp16 LoRA arithmetic and can produce incorrect outputs. The kernel now derives the dot dtype from the input pointer element type and casts both operands to that type. The large-rank fallback test is parameterized over the existing fp16 and bf16 dtype matrix.

title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Quantize audio towers independently
author: sudhanshu112233shukla
body:
## Overview

Fixes [#59905](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59905) by selecting quantization for Gemma 4 vision and audio towers independently.

## Claims

Quantizable Gemma 4 audio towers now receive the checkpoint quantization config even when the vision tower dimensions are not supported by that kernel.
Non-quantizable towers retain the existing unquantized path.
Methods that support arbitrary tower dimensions keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

Ruff check passed for the changed Python files.
 Ruff format check passed.
Python compileall passed.
 git diff --check passed.
 Added a focused regression test for independent tower dimension checks.
 The focused pytest could not complete in the available Windows environment: the local uv environment lacks pytest, and the prepared pytest environment hung while importing the full Gemma 4 multimodal module. No GPU checkpoint load was available locally.

## Details
The constructor previously computed one tower_quant decision from vision_config and reused it for audio_tower. AutoRound-GPTQ Gemma 4 checkpoints can have a non-quantizable vision tower and quantized audio tower. In that combination, vLLM created an unquantized audio weight, while the checkpoint provided GPTQ tensors such as qweight, scales, qzeros, and g_idx.

The new helper applies the existing dimension and method checks to each tower configuration separately. The change is limited to Gemma 4 multimodal model construction and does not alter quantization behavior for the language model.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Export corrupted request metric
author: reidliu41
body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend already decoded `EngineCoreOutput.num_nans_in_logits`, but the value was discarded before request metrics were recorded. Consequently, `/metrics` did not expose `vllm:corrupted_requests_total`, even when engine-core detected NaNs in request logits.

Track corruption across the complete request lifecycle and export the request-level counter already provided by the Python frontend. This restores visibility into numerical corruption that may indicate model, kernel, or hardware problems.



## Claims



## Validation

```bash
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

cargo nextest run -p vllm-llm --test generate \
  generate_records_request_metrics_in_prometheus_output

cargo nextest run -p vllm-metrics -p vllm-llm \
  --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```



## Details

title: [Bugfix] Resolve eager_break_during_capture at call time, not import time
author: C-C-Hao
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59940. `@eager_break_during_capture` decided whether to wrap a function when the decorated module was
imported. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the breakable-graph flag is turned on later, inside `VllmConfig` (#57586).
Any import of `attention.py` before that point leaves `unified_attention_with_output` unwrapped, and FA2 then produces
wrong tokens for short prefills. This PR makes the decorator always return its wrapper, so the setting is read at call
time. It's a 2-line removal plus CPU tests.

## Claims

- Breakable-graph eager breaks no longer depend on import order. In-process and default-fork engines with a cold
  model-info cache now get the wrapped attention op.
- With the flag off, behavior is unchanged: the wrapper calls the function directly when no breakable capture is
  active.
- Every current and future user of the decorator is covered (33 sites, plus those added by #46372 and #57881), with no
  new imports.

## Validation

Environment: `uv venv --python 3.12`, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .`, plus `requirements/lint.txt`, `pytest`
and `tblib`; Python 3.12.14, main 5f30fc703 plus this commit. Tests ran on CPU only.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py -v
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py
```

| Test | Before (main 5f30fc703) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_decorator_breaks_when_enabled_after_decoration` | FAIL | pass |
| `test_attention_op_breaks_when_imported_before_enable` (subprocess, real op) | FAIL | pass |
| `test_decorator_passthrough_returns_fn_result[False/True]` | pass | pass |
| `test_decorated_op_traces_without_graph_break[False/True]` (`fullgraph=True`) | pass | pass |
| whole `test_breakable_cudagraph.py` | 2 failed, 11 passed, 13 skipped | 13 passed, 13 skipped (the skips need CUDA) |

`tests/test_config.py` and `tests/test_ray_env_utils.py`: 13 failed, 424 passed, 5 skipped, with and without this patch
(identical failing test IDs: they need gated HF models such as Llama-3.2 and Mixtral, plus the engram DP shared-memory
config tests, on my host). pre-commit: all hooks pass.

End to end on GPU (RTX PRO 6000, SM120, FA2, default V2 model runner, Qwen3-1.7B, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, fresh `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` per cold
run, main 5f30fc703), using the repro from the issue:

| Run | Output |
|---|---|
| unpatched, in-process, cold | `first_token=16448 first_logprob=-2.7350 hash=5f5950387de45eaa` (wrong) |
| unpatched, in-process, warm (same cache root) | `first_token=271 first_logprob=-3.8602 hash=19ba86ff8b6b181d` |
| patched, in-process, cold | `first_token=271 first_logprob=-3.8602 hash=19ba86ff8b6b181d` |
| patched, default multiprocess, cold | `first_token=271 first_logprob=-3.8602 hash=19ba86ff8b6b181d` |

BI=0 (`VLLM_COMPILE`) is not run-to-run deterministic on this shared host, so bitwise comparison isn't a valid check. On
main 5f30fc703, 14 prompt lengths (2 to 513), 2 runs per tree: both trees compile one graph with 0 graph breaks and 0
recompiles. Two unpatched runs agree on 10/14 hashes (all 14 token sequences equal, max |Δlogprob| 0.097). One patched
run is bitwise identical to one unpatched run (14/14); the other patched run differs from every other run (3 token
sequences, max |Δlogprob| 0.11). On 766b4ae54 a single pair was 14/14 identical. With the flag unset no breakable capture
exists, so the wrapper only calls the function.

`vllm bench latency --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10` (input 32, output 128, batch 8), avg latency per run, shared host
with other jobs on the GPUs:

| | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| BI=0 | 0.507 ± 0.061 s (n=3): .466 .477 .577 | 0.560 ± 0.151 s (n=3): .472 .474 .735 |
| BI=1 | fast runs: .488 .498; slow runs: .707 .642 .632 .608 .747 .663 | .495 .495 .503 .492 .536 .564 |

No run showed the patched tree slower than the unpatched one: patched BI=1 took 0.49-0.56 s in all 6 runs, unpatched
0.49-0.75 s. Both trees have identical worker state (flag set before attention is imported, `CompilationMode.NONE`).

Pass-through overhead, from a microbenchmark of 1e6 calls × 5 with no capture active: about 0.5 µs per call on a shared,
loaded x86_64 host with Python 3.12. That's an upper bound of about 14 µs per step for 28 attention layers. Before this
change, the cost only arose when the flag was on.

## Details

- **Root cause:** `vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py` had `if not is_breakable_cudagraph_enabled(): return fn`.
  On a cold model-info cache, `ModelConfig` construction imports `attention.py` via `registry._save_modelinfo_to_cache`
  → `weight_utils.atomic_writer` before `VllmConfig._maybe_enable_breakable_cudagraph` sets the env. Forked engine
  cores inherit the bare op. First reported by @Taimys in #58918 and in the #57311 thread.
- **Scope beyond batch invariance:** as @LioEinaudi pointed out in #59940, the other branch of
  `_maybe_enable_breakable_cudagraph` (`_uses_breakable_cudagraph_by_default`, #52861) sets the same env var after the
  same early import, for the `DEFAULT_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH_ARCHITECTURES` models on CUDA, with no
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` involved. The ordering hazard is the same and this change covers it. I only validated the
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` path above, and I did not run those models, so I can't say whether their outputs are
  affected.
- **Why this isn't a duplicate of #57311:** #57311 (open) removes that particular import chain, and @Taimys confirmed it
  fixes that trigger on L20. The decorator stays import-order dependent, though: with #57311 applied on main and a warm
  cache, a user script that imports `vllm.model_executor.model_loader` before building `LLM` still ends up with the
  unwrapped op (verified by inspecting the op, not by comparing outputs). #53293 fixed the same root cause for Ray only. This PR removes the
  dependence at its source and works alongside #57311.
- **Dynamo:** the wrapper's thread-local lookup traces without a graph break (`fullgraph=True` test), so no
  `is_compiling()` fast path is needed.
- **Not included:** a GPU end-to-end regression test. Maintainers: would you like one (for example a cold-cache
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` FA2 run in the BI test suite)?

title: [Bugfix][Core] Retain encoder cache references for repeated multimodal inputs
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Prevent premature encoder-cache eviction when repeated multimodal inputs are deduplicated within the same scheduling step. 

## Claims

- Preserve cache references for partially consumed duplicate inputs, including locally encoded and externally loaded inputs.
- Avoid unnecessary re-encoding and scheduling stalls caused by premature eviction.
- Register duplicate occurrences within the final scheduled window, including the existing prefill lookahead, without registering later occurrences outside that window.

## Validation

On upstream base `d61081dc3d`, using the existing development environment:

```bash
uv run --no-project --python /workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -q
```

Result: **241 passed, 2 failed**.

Both failures require multiple GPUs and also fail on the unchanged upstream base in the same single-GPU environment:

- `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`
- `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait`

The new parameterized regression test covers newly admitted and running requests, with local encoding and external cache loads. All four cases pass. It verifies that:

- a competing request cannot evict an input that still has a partially consumed duplicate;
- no additional local encoding is scheduled; and
- later unscheduled occurrences are not registered as references.

Pre-commit checks pass.

Model end-to-end validation and latency measurements have not been performed, so no measured performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

Same-step deduplication allocates cache space only for the first occurrence of an input. Later occurrences within the same scheduling window reuse that entry but are not registered as references.

Once the first occurrence is consumed, the cache manager can therefore consider the entry reclaimable even though another occurrence is still partially consumed. A competing request can then evict the entry prematurely.

After scheduling is finalized, register cached occurrences overlapping the final scheduled window before advancing request progress. This reuses the existing reference-tracking mechanism without allocating additional cache space or scheduling duplicate encoder work.

The additional work is a window lookup and reference updates for overlapping inputs on scheduled requests that already hold encoder-cache references. Encoder-decoder models retain their existing behavior.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Derive the QSA head_dim from the unsharded head count
author: lesj0610
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen4Exp QSA computes its fallback `head_dim` from `num_heads`, which is already divided by the tensor-parallel size, so on TP > 1 the fallback is `tp_size` times too large. The fallback is latent: `Qwen4ExpTextConfig` defaults `head_dim` to 256 and rejects `None`, so only an explicit `head_dim: 0` reaches it. This fixes the arithmetic so it matches the `hidden_size // total_num_heads` idiom used elsewhere.

## Claims

- The fallback divides by the unsharded head count, so it is correct on any TP size.
- No change for any config with a nonzero `head_dim`, which covers every real checkpoint.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/
```

Unchanged against `main` on compute capability 8.0: this is reached only when `config.head_dim` is 0, which no Qwen3.8-Flash-Next config sets, so no existing test exercises the fallback.

The defect is by inspection of the surrounding lines:

```python
self.total_num_heads = int(config.num_attention_heads)
...
self.num_heads = self.total_num_heads // tp_size
...
self.head_dim = int(config.head_dim or self.hidden_size // self.num_heads)
```

`hidden_size` is sized against the unsharded head count, so dividing by the sharded one overstates `head_dim` by exactly `tp_size`. `q_size` and `kv_size` are then built from it, so the QKV projection is created at the wrong width and the checkpoint fails to load with a shape mismatch rather than producing wrong output.

No test added: the fallback has no checkpoint behind it in the suite, and a test would have to fabricate a config with `head_dim: 0` purely to assert one arithmetic expression. The failure mode is a loud shape mismatch, not a silent wrong result.

Not validated end to end: no real checkpoint reaches the fallback.

## Details

The same expression appears on the CUDA and ROCm QSA owners and both are changed. `total_num_heads` is assigned a few lines above the fallback in each, so no reordering is needed.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Do not modify caller params in LLM.score()
author: apex-mochen
body:
## Overview

`LLM.score()` wrote the model's pooling task into the `PoolingParams` object the caller passed in, so reusing a `PoolingParams()` with another pooling model failed before any inference ran. #58842 fixed the same footgun for the other offline pooling entry points; this applies the same one-line pattern to the scoring path, which it left untouched.

## Claims

- `LLM.score()` no longer modifies the caller's `PoolingParams`: the task is filled in on a clone, matching `LLM.encode()` / `embed()` / `classify()`.
- An explicitly conflicting `task` still raises the same `ValueError`; nothing else changes.

## Validation

The original regression failed on unpatched main (1 failed, 1 passed), then passed with the parameter clone. Following review, the caller-ownership regression and its helper now live in `tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py`; the separate file and redundant conflicting-task case were removed

Current focused run on commit `ec22afe9b829e95159d2a66d9e24addcb6fa50c6`:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu /home/dcl/projects/vllm-v2-gpu-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_utils.py -q --tb=short
```

14 passed, 16 warnings in 3.72s. Applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX and Buildkite test tethering. This revision only moves tests and imports; production code is unchanged

## Details

Root cause: unlike the other offline pooling entry points, `score()` filled in the task inline on the object it was handed:

```python
assert isinstance(pooling_params, PoolingParams)
pooling_task = io_processor.pooling_task
if pooling_params.task is None:
    pooling_params.task = pooling_task   # <- writes into the caller's object
```

`encode()` / `embed()` / `classify()` only forward the parameters and clone them downstream (#58842: `base/io_processor.py`, `pooling/io_processor.py`). Every `pooling_params.task` write in `offline.py` was checked: the scoring path was the only remaining one, so the same one-line clone is applied there instead of restructuring anything.

The conflicting-task check keeps its behavior: the clone carries an explicit `task` through, so `You cannot overwrite ...` is still raised.

Before opening this, I checked for existing work: no open or merged PR/issue claims this path (searched for `PoolingParams` clone, `cannot overwrite`, `LLM.score`); the only related change is #58842, which does not touch `score()`.

title: [Bugfix][DSv3.2] Carry the shared indexer top-k across pipeline stages
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Overview

Fix a GSM8K accuracy loss on GLM-5.x / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models under pipeline parallelism. These models reuse the previous layer's indexer top-k, and when a PP stage starts on a reusing layer, that stage read a stale top-k. This PR sends the top-k along with the intermediate tensors, using shared helpers that also fix HY-V4 and reject the unsupported MiniMax-M3 AMD case.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 PP2 × TP2 on main: GSM8K 0.879 → 0.908. Before the fix, stage 1's first three layers attend with the previous step's top-k.
- With gather-based DCP (#59916), where it was more visible: 0.820 → 0.908.
- When any later stage starts on a top-k-reusing layer, every stage boundary also sends `(num_tokens, index_topk)` int32 per step. Other models and partitions are unchanged.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 q) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `-pp 2 -tp 2` | 0.879 | 0.908 |
| `-pp 2 -tp 2 -dcp 2` with gather DCP (#59916) | 0.820 | 0.908 |
| same, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=38,40` (boundary aligned to a top-k group), no fix | 0.882 | - |

GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 q, greedy) on 8x MI350X (ROCm 7.2), GLM-5.3-BF16, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, default cudagraph mode (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`):

| config | code | strict-match |
|---|---|---:|
| `-tp 8` (reference) | this PR | 0.932 |
| `-pp 2 -tp 4` | first commit (NVIDIA-only fix) | 0.886 |
| `-pp 2 -tp 4` | this PR (8 runs, two revisions) | 0.916–0.931 |

Both PP configs on ROCm also include the AMD part of #60477, so the top-k fix is the only difference between them. Repeated runs of the same code vary by about 1.3 points on this setup; interleaved runs of the two revisions overlap.

## Details

**Root cause.** GLM-5.3 sets `index_topk_freq=4` with offset 3, so groups of layers reuse the top-k computed by the group's first layer.
- The default PP2 split puts the stage boundary at layer 39, which is inside a group.
- Stage 1's first layers (39-41) therefore skip the indexer and read `topk_indices_buffer`. On that stage the buffer holds the top-k of the previous step's last indexer layer, for the previous batch.
- Aligning the partition (38/40) restored accuracy, which confirms the cause.

**Fix.** Shared helpers in `model_executor/models/utils.py`:
- `compute_skip_topk_layers` moves there from HY-V4 and replaces the copy in the DSA attention init.
- `pp_splits_layer_sharing` checks whether a later stage's first top-k layer reuses the top-k. `pp_topk_buffers` returns the buffer to send in that case.
- `make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory` takes those buffers, and `copy_pp_buffers` copies them into place on the receiving stage.

Models:
- DSA (NVIDIA, AMD, dots3) and HY-V4 (NVIDIA, AMD) send the top-k, which is TP-replicated and token-major. `Dots3NoteModel` inherits `forward` but has its own `__init__`, so it calls the helpers too.
- MiniMax-M3 AMD with `use_index_cache` raises instead, since its top-k is sharded over TP index heads. Setting `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION` avoids the split.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 needs nothing: its index-sharing groups sit inside kv-sharing groups, which already reject PP splits.

`tests/models/deepseek_v32/test_pp_topk.py` covers the stage-boundary check, the empty tensors, and a middle stage receiving and forwarding the top-k.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR fixes top-k across PP stages (searched "pp topk_indices", "pipeline topk").
