title: [Bugfix][RecoverSSM] Correct aligned state indices at exact block boundaries
author: apex-mochen
body:
## Overview

**Upstream full-model evaluation pending.**

Fix RecoverSSM align-mode final-state indexing at exact Mamba block boundaries in both the KDA commit planner and V2 postprocessing. Fixes #59933.

## Claims

- At an exact boundary, commit and record the state for the block containing the last accepted token, rather than advancing to the next block.
- Retain the zero-length clamp and block-table upper bound; leave non-align behavior unchanged.
- Extend existing numeric-reference and mixed-batch CUDA tests to cover boundary neighbors, request remapping, and first/second exact boundaries.

## Validation

Base: `bd42276e1e25f540f019381c65994120158aa2a1`. NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (SM89), PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA runtime 13.0. Tests use candidate source with the installed GPU wheel's compiled extensions and missing vendor interfaces linked into ignored paths.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py -k recoverssm -q --tb=short
```

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New tests, original production code | 4 failed, 15 passed; 11.98s |
| New tests, fixed production code | 19 passed; 6.51s |
| Human personal test run | 19 passed, 101 deselected, 14 warnings; 7.62s; user screenshot |
| Changed-file pre-commit | All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

Both pytest runs deselected 101 unrelated tests and reported 14 existing Torch deprecation warnings. Two baseline failures were KDA committed-state comparisons against `naive_recurrent_kda`; two were incorrect V2 state columns at totals 8 and 16. The KDA test compares all state slots, including slots that should remain unchanged, as well as convolution state.

An additional metadata run was interrupted while waiting in a network socket (20 tests had passed); this is not a completed passing run. No upstream Kimi-K3 full-model accuracy/generation evaluation has been performed. The repository's Kimi-K3 GSM8K configuration requires TP4 hardware beyond this single laptop GPU. No throughput or latency claim is made.

## Details

Aligned state columns correspond to the block containing the last committed token. `total // block_size` advances prematurely when `total` is an exact multiple. Use `max(total - 1, 0) // block_size`, capped to the existing width limit, in both writer planning and recorded next-step state selection.

Credit: @seanphan reported #59933 with the downstream diagnosis/proposed arithmetic fix credited to @YulHeon. This patch independently reproduces the issue in upstream GPU tests and adds regression coverage. The reporter's downstream GLM A/B results are not claimed as our validation or as upstream Kimi-K3 evaluation.

Duplicate checks: issue body/comments, all-state PR search `59933 in:body` (no results), related RecoverSSM searches, and inspection of #56082. #56082 changes recovery performance/warmup and does not change these final-column expressions.

AI-assisted with Codex. **Human submitter confirmed line review and personally ran the relevant tests (19 passed, 7.62s). Opened for review at the human submitter's explicit request. Human line review and personal GPU/reference tests are complete; upstream full-model validation remains outstanding. Please help coordinate that evaluation before merging.**

title: [Bugfix] Fix Mamba page size AssertionError with spec decoding on GraniteMoeHybrid, FalconH1 and Zamba2
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

This fixes the `AssertionError` in `MambaSpec.page_size_bytes` that stops the engine at startup. It happens when `GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM` (for example `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny`) runs with speculative decoding and `num_speculative_tokens=2`. The config-time Mamba state shape now counts the speculative tokens, the same way the layer does. `FalconH1ForCausalLM` and `Zamba2ForCausalLM` had the same one-line gap and get the same fix.

Fixes #57721

## Claims

- `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` with ngram speculative decoding and `num_speculative_tokens=2` now starts. Before this fix, it failed during KV cache setup with `AssertionError` at `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:1075`.
- `GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM`, `FalconH1ForCausalLM` and `Zamba2ForCausalLM` now pass `num_spec=vllm_config.num_speculative_tokens` in `get_mamba_state_shape_from_config`. `Mamba2ForCausalLM` and `NemotronHForCausalLM` already do this.
- A new unit test checks the config-time shape of these three models when speculative tokens are set.

## Validation

Setup: 1 × NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3. vLLM at commit `18f8f96025b556071eb627076f94df560fbd3a22` (`0.30.1rc1.dev630+g18f8f9602`), editable install. This PR is one commit on top of that commit.

Reproducer (`repro.py`), from the issue:

```python
from vllm import LLM
print('=== Starting LLM with num_speculative_tokens=2 ===')
llm = LLM(
    model='ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny',
    max_model_len=4096,
    speculative_config={
        'method': 'ngram',
        'num_speculative_tokens': 2,
        'prompt_lookup_max': 4,
        'prompt_lookup_min': 2,
    },
)
print('=== LLM started successfully ===')
```

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 python repro.py
```

| Tree | Runs | `AssertionError` | Engine started | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `18f8f96` (before) | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| this PR (after) | 2 | 0 | 2 |

The same crash also happens with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit.

Before:

```
(EngineCore pid=217923) INFO 10-04 21:20:48 [interface.py:970] Setting attention block size to 400 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.
(EngineCore pid=217923) INFO 10-04 21:20:48 [interface.py:994] Padding mamba page size by 1.59% to ensure that mamba page size and attention page size are exactly equal.
...
  File ".../vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py", line 1075, in page_size_bytes
    assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size
AssertionError
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

After (exit code 0):

```
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:36:57 [interface.py:970] Setting attention block size to 416 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:36:57 [interface.py:994] Padding mamba page size by 3.94% to ensure that mamba page size and attention page size are exactly equal.
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:37:28 [core.py:373] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 31.43 s (compilation: 0.61 s)
=== LLM started successfully ===
```

Unit test: `test_mamba2_config_state_shape_includes_speculative_tokens` in `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends_selection.py`.

- With the fix: 3 passed.
- With the three model lines reverted: 3 failed, each with `assert ((3, 288), (8, 32, 16)) == ((5, 288), (8, 32, 16))`.

The test was run with `--noconftest`, because the local env had no `tblib` and could not load `tests/conftest.py`. The test uses no fixtures. `pre-commit run --files` passes on the four changed files, including `mypy` and the check that new tests are wired into Buildkite CI.

## Details

Root cause: vLLM plans the Mamba page size at config time and checks it against the real page at runtime. For these models, the planned page and the real page used different conv state shapes.

- `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`) sizes the padded Mamba page from `get_mamba_state_shape_from_config`. That function did not pass `num_spec`, so the planned conv state for granite-4.0-h-tiny was `(3, 3328)`.
- At runtime, each `MambaMixer2` layer builds its spec from `get_state_shape()`, and that function does pass `num_spec`. So the real conv state is `(5, 3328)`.
- The real page is 13312 bytes bigger than the planned page (3328 × 2 tokens × 2 bytes). Rounding up the attention block size only leaves 12800 bytes of slack. So the real page (819712 bytes) is bigger than the padded page (819200 bytes), and `assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size` fails. With 1 speculative token the gap is only 6656 bytes and fits in the slack. This is why the crash starts at 2 tokens.

Temporary debug prints of the planned shape and the real shape confirmed this. They also showed that the padding arithmetic was correct for the shape it was given: 400 × 2048 = 819200 ≥ 806400. The prints are not in this PR.

#33726 added `num_spec` to `MambaMixer2.get_state_shape` and to the config-time shapes of `Mamba2ForCausalLM` and `NemotronHForCausalLM`. It did not add it to the other three models that use `MambaMixer2`. Only these five models use `MambaMixer2`, so with this PR all five plan the same shape that the layer builds. The assert, the padding logic and the layer are not changed. Now the planner sees the real page size, so it picks an attention block size of 416 tokens (3.94% Mamba padding) instead of 400 tokens (1.59%).

Limitations:

- FalconH1 and Zamba2 get the same one-line fix, but only the unit test checks them. They were not run end to end.
- The reproducer only starts the engine. No generation was run.
- The config-time shape in `vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2.py` does not pass `num_spec`, but `ShortConv.get_state_shape` does. This may be the same kind of mismatch. It is outside this PR and was not tested.

title: [Bugfix] Keep force-killing the process tree when a child exits mid-walk
author: liulanze
body:
## Overview

Fix a regression from #52314: `kill_process_tree` stops early, leaving the rest of the tree and the target alive, when a child exits between `parent.children()` and `child.name()`.

## Claims

- `kill_process_tree` now SIGKILLs every remaining descendant and the target pid even if a child is reaped while it walks the tree.
- Before this change, `psutil.NoSuchProcess` escaped the function. Callers such as `vllm/v1/utils.py::shutdown()` then abandoned their loop over the remaining processes, so EngineCores, API servers or workers that were meant to be force-killed survived.

## Validation

The new test `tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py::test_kill_process_tree_skips_child_that_exits_mid_walk`:
- starts four real processes and makes `children()` report three of them as the target's children;
- ends one of the three with SIGTERM and reaps it before `kill_process_tree` runs, so psutil's own `name()` raises `NoSuchProcess` for it;
- asserts that this child exited from that SIGTERM, and that the other two children and the target exit with SIGKILL.

Results on Linux (base `04462732a4`, Python 3.12):

| psutil | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 6.1.0 (pinned in vLLM's CUDA/CPU test requirements) | fails: `NoSuchProcess: process no longer exists`, from `child.name()` | passes |
| 7.2.2 (latest; pinned in vLLM's ROCm/XPU test requirements) | fails: same | passes |

- `pytest tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py`: 5 passed with each psutil version. The new test also passed 30 runs in a row with each.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual` (the stage CI runs) passes on the changed files, including ruff, typos and mypy.

## Details

**Root cause.** #52314 added `logger.warning(..., child.name(), child.pid)` inside the existing `contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError)`. On Linux, `psutil.Process.name()` re-reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` on every call; only Windows caches it. Once the child has been reaped it raises `NoSuchProcess`, which is not a `ProcessLookupError`. Before #52314 the loop only read `child.pid`, which only returns the stored pid, so this path could not raise.

**Why the window is real.** The force-kill path runs when a process did not exit within its grace period. Typically that process is still tearing down and reaping its own children, for example EngineCore joining its workers after SIGTERM, so a child listed by `children()` can be gone by the time `name()` runs.

**Fix.** Also suppress `NoSuchProcess` for that child. The child is already gone, so it needs no SIGKILL, and skipping it avoids signalling a pid that may have been recycled. This matches the existing `psutil.NoSuchProcess` guard at the top of the same function and `vllm/entrypoints/launchers/dp_supervisor.py`.

**Affected callers.**
- `vllm/v1/utils.py::shutdown()`, used by `CoreEngineProcManager`, `APIServerProcessManager` and the DP coordinator.
- `vllm/v1/utils.py::_shutdown_subprocesses()`, used by `RustFrontendProcessManager`.
- `dp_supervisor.py` already suppresses the exception, but before this fix it silently skipped killing the rest of the tree.

**Not a duplicate.** I found no issue or PR that reports or fixes this. I searched `kill_process_tree`, `NoSuchProcess` and "force killing sub process" for anything after #52314 was merged on 2026-09-30.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find this, write the patch and the test, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: [Bugfix] Keep GateLinear batch invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
author: yifanFengg
body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, MoE models whose gate uses `GateLinear`'s specialized router GEMM tiers are not batch invariant. I found this while validating models for #27433 on NVIDIA GB300: `zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2` and `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` all fail the batch-invariance suite. This PR makes `GateLinear` use the batch-invariant linear path in that mode.

## Claims

- GLM-4.5-Air, MiniMax-M2 and ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B pass the full batch-invariance suite on GB300 (22/22 each). Without the fix they fail 12, 16 and 6 of the 22 tests.
- New regression test `tests/v1/determinism/test_gate_linear_batch_invariant.py` fails without the fix on both Blackwell and Ampere and passes with it.
- No change when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is off.

## Validation

NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), driver 580.167.08, CUDA toolkit 13.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM `f590eb2448` (`gate_linear.py` is unchanged between that commit and this PR's base).

**Model level.** Each test id of `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` run in its own process:

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=<model> VLLM_TP_SIZE=<tp> VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=<tp> \
  pytest -p no:rerunfailures "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::<test id>"
```

| Model | GPUs (TP) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air` | 2 | 12 failed, 10 passed | 22 passed |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2` | 2 | 16 failed, 6 passed | 22 passed |
| `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` | 1 | 6 failed, 16 passed | 22 passed |

What fails without the fix:

- All three: the 6 needle tests (`Nondeterministic outputs detected`, 2 to 5 of 5 trials).
- GLM-4.5-Air and MiniMax-M2: the 6 `bs1_vs_bsN` bitwise tests (`Batch invariance violated` in 30 to 32 of 32 prompts).
- MiniMax-M2 only: the 3 ragged chunked-prefill tests and the decode/prefill logprob test (49 mismatches).

GLM-4.5-Air also fails the needle test at TP=1 (4 of 5 trials), so this is not a tensor-parallel effect. MiniMax-M2 used `VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9`. For MiniMax-M2 and ERNIE the before and after runs were on two identical GB300 nodes at the same commit, one unmodified and one with this change.

Models whose results do not change: `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B` passes the suite without the fix (its gate does not use the specialized tiers). `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` pass the needle and bitwise tests with and without it.

**Unit level.** `pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_gate_linear_batch_invariant.py`:

| GPU | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3) | 10 failed, 2 passed | 12 passed |
| NVIDIA A10 (SM 8.6) | 6 failed, 6 passed | 12 passed |

**No regression with the mode off.** `tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py` and `tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py` give 19 passed, 136 skipped both before and after (A10). `pre-commit` passes.

## Details

**Root cause.** `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` is where `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is honored for linear layers (it calls `linear_batch_invariant`). `GateLinear.forward` returns from tiers 1 to 4 before reaching it. Those tiers also dispatch on the number of tokens:

- tier 1 (`ll_bf16_gemm`) is used for `M <= 16`, otherwise the cuBLAS `out_dtype` tier;
- tier 2 (fp32 kernel) is used for `M <= 32`, otherwise BF16x3 or `F.linear`;
- tier 3 (BF16x3) picks its tile size and split-K from the token count in `_pick_tile_config`.

So the router logits of one row can come from a different kernel, or a different K-reduction order, depending on how many tokens share the batch. A small difference in the logits can change the selected experts, which then changes logprobs and tokens. GLM-4.5-Air and ERNIE-4.5 have fp32 gates that take the BF16x3 tier on Blackwell; MiniMax-M2's gate shape (3072 x 256) also has the fp32 kernel, so it switches kernels at `M = 32`.

To localize it I compared the same prompt alone and inside a mixed batch on GLM-4.5-Air. Disabling fused grouped top-k did not restore bitwise-equal logprobs; disabling the `GateLinear` tiers did.

These tiers were added between June and September (#46385, #42562, #47973, #55899), and #58234 moved all MoE models to `GateLinear`, after most of the batch-invariance model validation was done.

**Fix.** The tier eligibility flags are now false when `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set, so `forward` falls through to tier 5 (`ReplicatedLinear`), which uses the batch-invariant matmul. The flags are also what `set_out_dtype` and the kernel warmup read, so warmup for the unused kernels is skipped too.

**Cost.** In batch-invariant mode the gate no longer uses the specialized kernels. Median time of one `GateLinear.forward` call on GB300 (bf16 input, 200 iterations after warmup):

| Gate (hidden x experts) | M | Specialized tiers | Batch-invariant path |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fp32, 3072 x 256 | 1 | 54 us | 139 us |
| fp32, 3072 x 256 | 1024 | 134 us | 145 us |
| fp32, 4096 x 128 | 1 | 105 us | 146 us |
| fp32, 4096 x 128 | 1024 | 98 us | 155 us |
| bf16 with fp32 output, 7168 x 256 | 1 | 73 us | 131 us |
| bf16 with fp32 output, 7168 x 256 | 1024 | 72 us | 133 us |

That is 1.1x to 2.7x per call, between 10 and 90 microseconds, and only when the mode is on. I disabled all four tiers because that is the configuration I validated. If a tier can be shown to be batch invariant on its own, it could be re-enabled separately.

**CI.** The new test is added to the H100 and B200 Batch Invariance jobs, where the specialized tiers exist.

**Related.** #57016 and #57092 are about batch invariance of the MoE experts, a different component.

**AI assistance.** Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line and the test logs.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep DSV4.1 sparse prefill out of FULL cudagraphs
author: he-yufeng
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59970. Fixes #62417. The five DSV4.1-specific sparse metadata builders declare `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, so with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` prefill and mixed batches get FULL-graph captured even though their prefill metadata is not graph-safe, and the engine dies with an illegal memory access once adaptive verification runs mixed batches at concurrency. Downgrade them to `UNIFORM_BATCH` and report the speculation width as the varlen decode bound, mirroring the reviewed pattern from #59751.

## Claims

- Prefill and mixed batches leave FULL capture for all five builders named in #59970: `DeepseekV4FlashMLAMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekV4FlashInferSparseMLAMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekSparseSWAFlashInferMetadataBuilder`, `DeepseekSparseSWAFlashMLAMetadataBuilder`, `CompressorMetadataBuilder`. `FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend` inherits the same builder, so it is covered too.
- FULL varlen decode graphs are kept for uniform batches sized up to 1 + num_speculative_tokens, so DSpark adaptive verification keeps its decode graphs.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -q
```

82 passed on CPU. The 10 new parametrized cases pin, per backend and num_speculative_tokens in {0, 7}, that support resolves to `UNIFORM_BATCH`, that decode widths up to the speculation width stay graph-eligible, and that one token wider is rejected with the reported bound. Changed-file pre-commit (ruff-check, ruff-format) passed.

Not run: the B300 (SM103) end-to-end reproducer from the issue, no compatible hardware available here, and CI does not exercise these builders. The change only narrows what FULL graphs capture: prefill moves to the piecewise path that the issue's adaptive-verification-off and FULL_DECODE_ONLY arms already exercise for 30+ minutes under load, so no batch that was not captured before becomes captured.

## Details

Root cause, from the issue's arm table: adaptive verification on + FULL_AND_PIECEWISE hits the IMA 4/4 within a minute; verification off in the same mode is stable; verification on with FULL_DECODE_ONLY is stable. The failing ingredient is prefill inside FULL graphs. Each affected builder now also overrides `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` to return `max_decode_query_len(vllm_config)` (1 + num_speculative_tokens on MRV2), the same width the V2 runner uses when it builds varlen decode replays.

Not a duplicate of #59751: that PR changes only the generic `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` for #59681, while the DSV4.1 model wires its own five builders, which the #59970 reporter calls out explicitly. Checked the issue thread and open PRs referencing #59970 before starting; nothing else covers them.

AI assistance: Kimi Code (Kimi K3) prepared the patch and tests; I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Qwen3-VL reranker crash on missing tie_word_embeddings in text config
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59784. Serving `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B` as `Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification` crashed during weight loading with `AttributeError: 'Qwen3VLTextConfig' object has no attribute 'tie_word_embeddings'`. The seq-cls weight loaders in `adapters.py` now read `tie_word_embeddings` from the language model's config, which is where vLLM puts it for VLMs.

## Claims

- `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B` with `--runner pooling` and the `Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification` override now loads, starts and answers `/rerank`. Before this change, the engine crashed while loading weights.
- Both `load_weights_using_from_2_way_softmax` and `load_weights_no_post_processing` had the same line. Both are fixed.
- Text-only models read the same value as before, because there `language_model is model`.
- A new regression test fails with the base `adapters.py` and with a `getattr(..., False)` fallback. It passes with this change.

## Validation

All runs used 1× NVIDIA B200 and `transformers==5.18.0`. vLLM was `18f8f96025b556071eb627076f94df560fbd3a22` (`0.30.1rc1.dev630+g18f8f9602`), with or without this change.

Reproducer, run from the root of the vLLM repo:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B \
  --runner pooling \
  --served-model-name qwen3-vl-reranker-8b \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --hf-overrides '{"architectures":["Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification"],"classifier_from_token":["no","yes"],"is_original_qwen3_reranker":true}' \
  --chat-template examples/pooling/score/template/qwen3_vl_reranker.jinja \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8002
```

**Before** (base commit, 1 run; the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit gave the same error): the engine failed during weight loading, and the process exited with code 1.

```
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/adapters.py", line 542, in load_weights_using_from_2_way_softmax
    if text_config.tie_word_embeddings:
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'Qwen3VLTextConfig' object has no attribute 'tie_word_embeddings'
```

**After** (with this change, 2 runs, both green): the weights load (`Model loading took 15.81 GiB memory`) and the server reaches `Application startup complete.`. There is no `AttributeError` or `Traceback` in either log. In both runs, one rerank request ranked the relevant document first, with the same scores:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8002/rerank -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"qwen3-vl-reranker-8b","query":"What is the capital of France?","documents":["Paris is the capital and largest city of France.","The mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell.","Berlin is the capital of Germany."]}'
# "results":[{"index":0,...,"relevance_score":0.3587302267551422},{"index":2,...,"relevance_score":0.0023183708544820547},{"index":1,...,"relevance_score":0.0002262023917865008}]
```

New test, 1 run for each version of `adapters.py`:

```bash
python -m pytest -v -s "tests/models/language/pooling/test_mm_classifier_conversion.py::test_qwen3_vl_reranker_tie_word_embeddings_only_on_top_level"
```

| `adapters.py` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| this PR | `1 passed` |
| base commit | fails at load with the `AttributeError` above |
| this PR, but with `getattr(text_config, "tie_word_embeddings", False)` | loads, then `assert 0.5 > 0.5` (`1 failed`) |

`pre-commit run` passes on both changed files. The new test runs in the existing "Language Models (Extended Pooling)" Buildkite step, so `.buildkite/` needs no change.

The issue was reported on a CPU-only build. The failing line only reads a config attribute and has no device-specific path.

## Details

**Root cause.** With Transformers v5, `tie_word_embeddings` is a field of `Qwen3VLConfig` but not of `Qwen3VLTextConfig`. The 8B checkpoint sets `"tie_word_embeddings": false` only at the top level. For multimodal models, `VllmConfig.with_hf_config` copies the top-level flag into the text config. But when `architectures` is passed, it first deep-copies that text config. `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` passes `architectures=["Qwen3ForCausalLM"]`. So the inner language model gets a copy that has the flag, while `model.config.text_config` still has no flag. The seq-cls loaders read the flag from `model.config.get_text_config()`, which is the original config. The read raises `AttributeError` before any weight is loaded.

**Fix.** Read the flag from `language_model.config.get_text_config()`. The language model was built with this config and uses it to tie its own `lm_head`, so now the loader and the model agree. For text-only models, `language_model is model`. When `with_hf_config` makes no copy, this is the same object as before.

**Why not `getattr(text_config, "tie_word_embeddings", False)`** (the fallback suggested in the issue): it stops the crash, but it reads `False` for a tied checkpoint whose text config has no flag, even when the top-level config says the embeddings are tied. The loader then does not tie `lm_head` to `embed_tokens`. A tied checkpoint has no `lm_head` tensor, so the score weights built from it are wrong. With that fallback, every score in the new test is 0.5.

**Test.** `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B` has tied embeddings. But its real config has the flag at both levels, so by itself it does not reach the failing state. This includes the existing `tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_cross_encoder_online_vision.py`. The new test removes the flag from the 2B text config, so the config looks like the 8B one. Then it checks that the relevant document scores higher than the unrelated one.

**Other VLMs.** `language_model.config` is read without a guard. The language model classes used by other VLMs (for example `LlamaModel` and `MolmoModel`) set `self.config`, so this change adds no new failure for them. This PR does not check whether seq-cls conversion gives correct scores for those models.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Qwen4Exp PLE embedding rejecting INC (AutoRound) checkpoints
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59798. `Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound` is an AutoRound checkpoint, which vLLM loads as `INCConfig`. It failed at model construction with `NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config INCConfig`. `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config` now asks `INCConfig` whether the PLE layer is quantized. #59431 does the same for compressed-tensors.

## Claims

- The command from the issue (TP=2, expert parallel) no longer raises. Both workers build the PLE n-gram table with `Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` (bf16), and model construction finishes.
- The checkpoint's own INC metadata makes the choice: its `extra_config` has `".*ple.*": {"bits": 16, "data_type": "float"}`. If INC says the PLE layer is quantized, the old `NotImplementedError` is still raised, because there is no INC-quantized PLE format.
- The branch is in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/ngram_embedding.py`, so both the NVIDIA and the AMD Qwen4Exp paths get it.
- A new unit test covers both cases.

## Validation

Hardware: 2 × NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB. Before: commit `18f8f96025b556071eb627076f94df560fbd3a22`. After: this PR on top of that commit.

Reproducer, from the issue. No request is needed, because the crash happens at startup:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel
```

| | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 1 | Both workers raise `NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config INCConfig` during model construction, before weight loading. The engine exits with code 1. The `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit gives the same error. | | After | 2 | No `NotImplementedError` in either run. Both workers build the PLE table, and model construction finishes (about 56 s). |

After the fix, both workers log:

```
Initialized PLE embedding language_model.model.layers.1.ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding: quantization_method=Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod, weight_dtype=torch.bfloat16, weight_device=cpu, pinned=True
```

Limitation: neither "after" run reached a ready server. Both runs next stopped at the weight download, with a `PermissionError` from `huggingface_hub`. The HF cache on the test machine had only the config and tokenizer files for this model, and we could not write to it. This happens after the bug site, in code the patch does not touch. The "before" run never got that far. No run here loaded the real weights, and no accuracy eval was run. Before merge, someone with the weights should run the reproducer to a ready server and run an accuracy check.

Extra checks (not the reproducer):

- The same command with `--load-format dummy`: weights loaded (35.44 GiB per GPU), CUDA graphs were captured, and the server became ready. One `/v1/completions` request returned 16 tokens. The text is noise, because the weights are random.
- The checkpoint's safetensors headers on the Hub: the PLE n-gram table is 128 plain BF16 shards (`[2500012, 160]` each), with no `qweight`, `scales` or `qzeros`. This matches the unquantized method.
- Unit tests: `pytest --noconftest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -k "inc_layer_config or rejects_unsupported or modelopt_exclusion or shard_exclusions or mixed_precision"` gives `6 passed, 69 deselected`. `--noconftest` was used because `tests/conftest.py` needs `tblib`, which the test env did not have. With the INC branch turned off in a separate process (tree unchanged), the new test's config gets the old `NotImplementedError` again. So the test catches the bug.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed files: every hook passed or was skipped, including ruff and mypy.

## Details

Root cause: `from_quant_config` gets the model-level quantization config. That config describes the model body, which is not always the same as the PLE table. The method could only ask four config families whether the PLE layer is excluded: ModelOpt mixed precision, ModelOpt, compressed-tensors and FP8. Any other config fell through to the `NotImplementedError`. This checkpoint quantizes `model.language_model.layers` to 4 bits, but its `extra_config` marks `.*ple.*` as 16-bit float. `INCConfig` keeps this metadata and resolves it with `config_parser.resolve(layer, prefix)`, but the PLE code never asked it.

How it was found: on the unpatched tree, a debug print just before the raise showed three things. The config was a plain `INCConfig`, with no handled class in its MRO. The prefix was `language_model.model.layers.1.ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding`. And `resolve(None, prefix)` returned `bits=16, quantized=False`. So the INC metadata is already mapped to vLLM names and matches the prefix. Only the dispatch ignored it.

Fix: one `if` in `from_quant_config`. For an `INCConfig`, when `quant_config.config_parser.resolve(None, prefix).quantized` is false, it returns `Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`. `INCConfig.get_quant_method` uses the same `resolve(...).quantized` check for its own layers. Passing `None` as the layer is safe: `_resolve_raw` only uses the layer in `isinstance(layer, ParallelLMHead)` and `layer.__class__.__name__`, and both work with `None`. The compressed-tensors branch also passes `None`. Size: +6 lines in `ngram_embedding.py`, and +19 lines of test in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py`. That test file already runs in Buildkite (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`).

Design choice for review: INC's own `get_quant_method` treats every layer that is not linear or MoE as unquantized, whatever `resolve` says. This patch is stricter. An INC checkpoint that puts the PLE table inside a quantized block, with no 16-bit exclusion, still gets `NotImplementedError`. The new test checks this case on purpose. Please say if you prefer INC's looser behavior.

---

title: [Bugfix][DiffusionGemma] Read the causal mask as int32 and compile the sample step
author: ojeda-e
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59991. 

This PR has two fixes for DiffusionGemma. The first unblocks the CPU backend. The second applies to every platform.

1. DiffusionGemma fails on every CPU run. #51994 made the per-request causal mask `int32` and updated FlashAttention and Triton. CPU attention still reads it as `bool`. This PR makes the CPU kernel read `int32`.

2. #58226 left `_compiled_sample_step` uncompiled on every platform. This PR moves its `torch.compile` decorators back from the `_denoise_temperature` helper.

No open issue or PR covers either fix. For the causal mask I searched for the error message, `dynamic_causal` on CPU and DiffusionGemma on CPU. For the sample step I searched open PRs for `_compiled_sample_step`, `_denoise_temperature` and `58226`. The only hits, #45954, #47278 and #56210, do not touch the decorators.

## Claims

CPU causal mask (7b1cee8156):

- Fixes `RuntimeError: expected scalar type Bool but found Int` on the CPU backend. It is raised at engine startup. No DiffusionGemma request can run on CPU on `main`.
- CPU attention follows the `int32` contract from #51994. The mask is passed through without a cast, like FlashAttention, Triton and the XPU support in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57747.
- `test_cpu_attn.py` builds the mask as `int32`, like the model does. The existing per-request causal test reproduces the bug on `main`.

Sample step compile (c4a07b1796):

- `_compiled_sample_step` is compiled again, as it was before #58226. `_denoise_temperature` stays compiled and drops the raised recompile limit, which it does not need.
- On CPU, given the same random tokens, the compiled step matches the eager step. It is about 2x faster without self-conditioning and 1.0x to 1.5x faster with it. End-to-end CPU throughput is unchanged within noise.
- `test_sample_step_is_compiled` fails if `torch.compile` moves off the step again.

## Validation

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C (AMX), Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at 7867d6c52d.


### CPU causal mask

| check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_varlen_with_paged_kv_dynamic_causal` | 36 failed, `expected scalar type Bool but found Int` | 36 passed |
| `tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py` | | 1621 passed, 1153 skipped |
| DiffusionGemma structured read, `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` in BF16 | fails at startup with the same error | 3 runs of 50 reads, identical outputs |

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py -k dynamic_causal
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py
```

Any DiffusionGemma request on a CPU build reproduces it. I used `LLM.generate` with a structured read (32-token canvas, read-only, one step).

### Sample step compile

- `test_sample_step_is_compiled` fails before the change and passes after. Its module skips without CUDA and I have no GPU, so I called the test function directly on CPU.
- Compiled against eager over 16 combinations of canvas width, self-conditioning on or off, fp32 or bf16 embeddings, and peaked or flat logits, 6 steps each, with inductor's `fallback_random` on. Sampled tokens and state match. No graph breaks.

Sample step alone, vocab 262144, hidden 2816, bf16 embeddings, median of 10 calls. Eager is the same build under `torch.compiler.set_stance("force_eager")`.

| requests x canvas | self-conditioning | eager | compiled | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 x 256 | off | 0.4 ms | 0.2 ms | 2.3x |
| 8 x 64 | off | 0.5 ms | 0.2 ms | 2.1x |
| 1 x 256 | on | 56.9 ms | 56.7 ms | 1.0x |
| 8 x 64 | on | 189.7 ms | 123.6 ms | 1.5x |

End to end with `LLM.generate`: `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` in BF16, `enforce_eager=True` (it does not turn off the step's own `torch.compile`), canvas 64, 8 chat prompts per call, `max_tokens=128`. 3 timed calls after a warmup, arms run in the order shown.

| arm | sample step | tokens (last call) | tok/s (median call) | per-call time (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (7b1cee8156) | eager | 769 | 16.45 | 49.8, 46.7, 40.2 |
| after (c4a07b1796) | compiled | 762 | 16.75 | 45.5, 48.2, 43.6 |
| before (7b1cee8156) | eager | 769 | 15.97 | 49.3, 48.2, 42.3 |

The difference is within run-to-run noise. On CPU the sample step is a small share of each call. The compiled arm words answers differently because the renoise tokens now come from inductor's RNG.

I couldn't test in GPU (running short today).

## Details


### CPU causal mask

#51994 fixed a FULL CUDA graph bug. FlashAttention cast the `bool` mask to `int32` on every `build()`, and the captured graph kept reading the tensor from capture time. The fix allocates the mask as `int32` in DiffusionGemma, and FlashAttention now rejects other dtypes. CPU attention passes the same tensor to its C++ ops, which read it with `data_ptr<bool>()`. The CPU tests built their own `bool` mask. CI stayed green.

The kernel reads `int32` instead of `CPUAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` casting the mask. A cast there would bring back the per-step allocation #51994 removed. It is harmless on CPU today, since CPU has no graph capture, but it would break the contract every other backend follows.

No measurable tradeoffs. The kernel reads the flag once per request and once per work group. The mask grows from 1 to 4 bytes per request.

Limitations:

- The CPU ops now reject `bool` masks. The only caller passes the model's `int32` mask.
- `test_varlen_with_paged_kv_dynamic_causal` runs only on CPUs with AMX. Other ISAs share the changed lines, but no test covers their per-request causal path, before or after this PR.

### Sample step compile

#58226 added `_denoise_temperature` directly below the `@torch._dynamo.config.patch(recompile_limit=64)` and `@torch.compile` decorators of `_compiled_sample_step`, and Python applied them to the helper. Since then the step has run eager on every platform. The step body has not changed since #58226. The fix restores the earlier layout.

Tradeoffs, each the same as before #58226:

- The renoise `torch.randint` uses inductor's RNG. At a given global seed, outputs differ from the eager step. Diffusion models reject per-request seeds.
- On CPU, warmup does not reach the sample step. Each new shape specialization compiles on first use while serving.

Limitations:

- No GPU numbers and no accuracy eval.
- `test_sample_step_is_compiled` checks `_torchdynamo_orig_callable`, which `test_batched_count_greater_than.py` also reads. Compiled and eager differ only in random draws, so no output assertion can tell them apart.


---

title: [Bugfix] Offload model runner construction buffers on sleep
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59158. Part of RFC #59055.

#59158 builds the KV-cache initialization state inside the `runtime` cuMem pool, so sleep backs it up to CPU and restores it on wake. Buffers that the model runner allocates in its constructor are still allocated outside every pool, so they stay on the GPU while asleep. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash with MTP, the drafter's `hidden_states` buffer (`spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py`) is 512 MiB/GPU.

The earlier revision of #59158 built the model runner inside the `runtime` pool too; that part was dropped before merge. This PR brings it back:

- `Worker` builds the model runner inside the `runtime` pool.
- The check that the allocator is unused when the `weights` pool is entered is removed. The runner now enters the `runtime` pool first, so the check would fire whenever its constructor allocates (MTP, DSpark). It guarded two engines sharing one `CuMemAllocator` in a process, which V1 rules out by default because the engine core runs in its own process.

## Test Plan

- `test_runtime_state_survives_sleep` in `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` (from #59158) now allocates its state while `Worker._init_workspace_and_model_runner` builds the runner, instead of under the `runtime` pool directly. It passed on main before; now it fails there (`{'kv_cache'} == {'kv_cache', 'runtime'}`) and passes with this change. Its other checks (nested `kv_cache` tag, offload, restore by the first selective wake) are unchanged.
- `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py`, with and without this change.
- GB300, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP4 with MTP, level-1 sleep: memory while asleep, with and without `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, and outputs after wake compared with the awake run.

## Test Result

At c2e07c4deb (main c9e4cb2b79), GB200:
- `test_runtime_state_survives_sleep` fails on main and passes here; `test_cumem.py` 22 passed; `test_gpu_worker.py` + `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` + `test_kv_cache_allocation_scope.py` 64 passed.
- `test_sleep_mode.py` 16 passed, 1 skipped, on Model Runner V2 (default) and on V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`).
- With a speculator, so the runner allocates while it is built: `test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_lm_head_quantization_survives_sleep_and_reload` (Qwen3.5 MTP, V2) passed.

Earlier results, before the check was dropped:

- `test_cumem.py`: 16 passed with this change vs 14 on main; the 7 failures are the same on both sides (models not in the offline cache). `test_gpu_worker.py` + `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`: 29 passed on both.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, memory per GPU while asleep:

| | main (+ graph pool released) | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| sleep mode | 8633 MiB | 8121 MiB (−512) |
| + `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` | 6451 MiB | 5939 MiB (−512) |

- The `runtime` tag grows from 4704 to 5218 MiB. Outputs after two wakes are identical to the awake run, and wake time is unchanged.
- Not yet covered: GSM8K.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Transfer the whole PLE short-conv page in disaggregated P/D
author: aijanai
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59642 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 0% MTP acceptance in disaggregated P/D serving with `NixlConnector`).

The NIXL worker folds every KV cache layer that reports the same base address into one region (`register_kv_caches`, `if base_addr in seen_base_addresses`). In the block-outer HMA layout every cache group places its first page at byte 0 of the shared allocation, so on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next the PLE short-conv state (`Qwen4ExpPLELayer`, a tp-replicated `MambaSpec`, page = `channels × (conv_state_len + num_spec_tokens)` = 245760 B) lands in the same region as layer-0 GDN, the layer-3 QSA ring and the layer-3 MLA indexer cache, and that region keeps the MLA page length (204800 B). The PLE descriptors built from `block_len_per_layer[_ple_region_index]` therefore transfer only 204800/245760 bytes of each PLE slot: 8534 of 10240 channels arrive on the decode worker, the rest is whatever the block held before (never zeroed: the block is exempt from zeroing because an async load is expected to overwrite it). With `num_speculative_tokens >= 2` the spec-decode short conv reads those stale columns, the layer-1 hidden state becomes NaN, the target logits are NaN and the rejection sampler rejects every draft (the generated tokens are garbage too, not just slow).

This PR records the PLE page length at registration (`_ple_block_len`) and uses it for the PLE descriptors on both sides of the transfer (`_build_mamba_local` / `_build_mamba_remote`), exchanging it through `NixlAgentMetadata.ple_block_len` (optional, backward compatible) so the existing P/D geometry check still compares PLE pages. Region discovery is unchanged: the PLE keeps sharing its region with the pages it aliases, as `test_csa_linear_registration_discovers_shared_regions` expects; only the transfer length of its pages changes.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_ple_region.py`: a CSA-linear-like config (MLA + GDN + ring + PLE sharing byte 0 of one block-outer tensor, PLE page larger than the MLA page); asserts the PLE descriptors cover the whole PLE page and that the page length is advertised in the handshake metadata. Before the fix the PLE descriptors carry the MLA page length.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` + `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` run inside the serving image (vLLM `109b5363fc`) with the patch hot-patched: 307 passed before and after (one HF-download test deselected).
- End-to-end on GB200 (vLLM `109b5363fc` + this patch hot-patched into the image, Dynamo + `NixlConnector`, 1P/1D, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, MTP k=3, 200 requests of 64/64 tokens): mean acceptance length goes from 1.00 on 20/21 windows (zero accepted drafts) to 2.7–3.5 on every window, no NaN; the same configuration in aggregate mode gives ~2.1–2.4.

## Test Result

See above; details and the full investigation (per-request probes of the PLE conv state on prefill and decode, per-column comparison of the transferred slot) are in #59642.

title: [Bugfix] FlashInfer: declare only KV layouts it can address
author: hyunnnchoi
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59998. On non-SM100 GPUs, declare the five KV cache layouts FlashInfer can address, so layout resolution can no longer pick LHBNC.

### User case

1. FlashInfer on SM80/SM90/SM120 with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`.
2. `FlashInferBackend.supported_kv_cache_layouts()` returns `None` there, so `resolve_kv_cache_layout` accepts LHBNC.
3. FlashInfer only takes NHD/HND pages; `get_flashinfer_layout_string` has no LHBNC entry.
4. The engine dies at startup on `AssertionError: KV cache layout LHBNC has no FlashInfer equivalent` (A100, Llama-3-8B) instead of rejecting the layout at resolution.

The fix returns the default preference order without LHBNC (LBNHC, LBHNC, BLNHC, BLHNC, BHLNC) instead of `None`.

Unchanged: the default layout (still LBNHC), the SM100 set, connector preferences (LBHNC and BLHNC stay valid), and every layout FlashInfer could already run.

Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR covers this. #46329 and #56550 add an SM120 branch to the same function but keep the `None` fallback. Related: #55431, #55312.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \
  -k test_flashinfer_declares_only_layouts_it_can_address
ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
ruff format --check vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
git diff --check
```

The new test patches the device capability to SM80/90/100/120 and checks that every declared layout maps through `get_flashinfer_layout_string` and that LHBNC is not declared.

## Test Result

```text
4 passed; on main 3 fail (SM80/90/120: supported_kv_cache_layouts() is None)
ruff check, ruff format --check (v0.14.0), git diff --check: passed
```

| A100, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, FlashInfer | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` | `AssertionError` during startup | `ValueError` at resolution listing the 5 valid layouts |
| default | LBNHC, serves | LBNHC, serves |

<details>
<summary>Test environment</summary>

- A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03, torch 2.13.0+cu129, flashinfer-python 0.6.18.post1.
- Unit test: main (1388100) with this patch, compiled extensions from the v0.30.0 wheel, run with `--noconftest` because the env lacks `tblib`; the test only uses `monkeypatch`.
- Engine check: v0.30.0 (ced6857) with the same patch. `supported_kv_cache_layouts` and `get_flashinfer_layout_string` are identical on v0.30.0 and main.
- The other five layouts also run in FlashInfer's attention benchmark on A100; LHBNC is the only one that asserts.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, code and tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests on my own hardware.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Clean up sweep workers after the server exits
author: zupengwang
body:
## Overview

Fix benchmark sweep cleanup when a server exits before its workers: terminate the surviving process group and reap the directly owned server process. This update also avoids signalling an already-reaped process group during test cleanup and documents the cleanup scope.

## Claims

- `ServerProcess.stop()` terminates workers remaining in the server's process group after its leader exits.
- Cleanup reaps the direct child and is safe to repeat after successful cleanup.
- The regression's fallback cleanup only signals the group while its direct child has not been reaped.

## Validation

Current candidate is based on main `fce61a05a76ccf34e1af6511ff7071affc306424`. Linux RTX 3090 host, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; CUDA devices were hidden throughout these CPU/process tests.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unmodified main plus the same regression tests | 2 failed: direct child unreaped / surviving worker |
| Candidate, standard `tests/benchmarks/sweep` suite with normal conftest fixtures | 28 passed |
| All 17 applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, mypy, markdownlint and test tethering | Passed |
| Diff whitespace check | Passed |

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py --timeout=60
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/benchmarks/sweep --timeout=60
pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/sweep/server.py tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py docs/benchmarking/sweeps.md
```

The tests use real subprocesses, a forked worker, and a socket handshake. The standard suite uses normal global fixtures, with no `--noconftest`. Hooks with no matching files were excluded using their actual file/type filters after an unrelated actionlint environment download failed.

The environment reuses an older official native wheel. No fresh native build, real model-serving or GPU-resource-recovery test, upstream CI, or performance benchmark is claimed. The earlier macOS global-teardown failure remains uninvestigated; this Linux result does not establish that it was fixed.

## Details

`start_new_session=True` makes the server PID the process-group ID. Previously, the `poll() is None` guard prevented cleanup after the leader was reaped, and looking up its PGID required it to remain alive. Signal the known group ID and wait for the direct child; a per-start completion flag prevents repeated successful cleanup from signalling the old group again.

The test's finalizer now checks `returncode` before its emergency signal, addressing the review suggestion about PID/PGID reuse. Closing the worker's socket releases the deliberately orphaned child on failure paths. Production cleanup still covers only workers in the original group, not detached sessions, and does not promise complete GPU-memory recovery. Numeric PGID reuse before the first cleanup remains a limitation.

The rendered benchmark guide at `docs/benchmarking/sweeps.md` describes these semantics. Existing Buildkite benchmark CLI coverage selects the tests. Duplicate-work checks were recorded when the original PR was opened; this updates that same PR.

title: [Bugfix][weight loader] Stop warning when a parameter only widens the weight
author: lesj0610
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to [#51792](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51792), which added this warning. `AutoWeightsLoader` emits it whenever a checkpoint weight's dtype differs from the parameter it lands in. A parameter declared wider than the checkpoint is a deliberate choice and the copy is exact, so that line reports nothing and buries the narrowing cases it was added for. Log the float widenings that cannot change a value at DEBUG instead of WARNING; every other mismatch still warns exactly as before.

## Claims

- A 48-layer Qwen3.x emits this warning 36 times at every start, once per linear-attention layer, for fp32 decay accumulators reading a bf16 `A_log` — counted from 180 occurrences over 5 starts in a serving log. All 36 are exact widenings, so the change is expected to log them at DEBUG instead; the post-change count was not measured on a model run.
- No other warning changes: the condition only subtracts from the cases that already fired.
- The conversions moved to DEBUG are exact for every finite input, not approximately: all 63,488 finite fp16 and 65,280 finite bf16 bit patterns round-trip through fp32 and fp64 unchanged, and fp32 round-trips through fp64.
- Nothing about loading changes — same values, same returned names. Only the level of the line changes; it is still logged, at DEBUG.
- Every other dtype mismatch still warns, including the fp8 pairs whose range looks wider but whose subnormals are shorter.

## Validation

On the branch point (`92044241a0`) and this PR, on CPU: load one parameter through `AutoWeightsLoader` for each stored → declared pair and record the level of the `Attempted to load weight` line.

| stored → declared | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bfloat16 → float32`, `float16 → float32`, `float32 → float64` | WARNING | DEBUG |
| `float32 → bfloat16`, `float16 → bfloat16` | WARNING | WARNING |
| `float8_e4m3fnuz → float8_e4m3fn` | WARNING | WARNING |

`pytest tests/models/test_utils.py`: 9 passed, the same tests as the branch point.

Exhaustive check of the pairs moved to DEBUG, run outside the suite: every finite fp16 and bf16 bit pattern cast to fp32 and to fp64 and back compares bit-identical, and none of them loses a value at `tiny/4`, `±max`, `1e-30` or `0.1`. Across the 8 float dtypes checked, 56 ordered pairs, the 5 widenings moved to DEBUG lose nothing at the probed values.

No model run, no multi-GPU, no performance measurement.

## Details

**Why a whitelist and not a predicate.** Comparing what the two formats hold reads as the general answer and is not. `eps`, `max` and `min` describe the normal range, so they miss the subnormal reach: `float8_e4m3fnuz` has the same 3 mantissa bits and a smaller `max` than `float8_e4m3fn`, which makes it look strictly narrower, but its exponent bias is one higher, 8 against 7, so its smallest subnormal is 2⁻¹⁰ against 2⁻⁹ and `0.0009765625` loads as `0.0`. A predicate built on those three fields calls that cast lossless and demotes a warning that matters. `torch.finfo` exposes no subnormal bound to repair it with, and the existing `is_lossless_cast()` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` compares `resolution`, `min` and `max`, and returns `True` for this very pair, so reusing it would carry the same gap. Listing the widenings that are exact by construction — fp16, bf16 or fp32 into fp32 or fp64 — is smaller and easier to verify at this scope.

**Relation to existing work.** [#51836](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51836) proposes config-driven changes to Qwen parameter dtypes, which is separate work on the parameters themselves; it is not landed, and it would need a config field present in each affected checkpoint. This PR changes the log level only: known-lossless widenings log at DEBUG instead of WARNING, every other dtype mismatch still warns, and no parameter or loaded value moves.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Honor --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers in QSA attention
author: stecasta
body:
## Purpose

`Qwen4ExpQSAAttention` takes its KV cache dtype straight from `cache_config.cache_dtype`, so
`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` is silently ignored on every Qwen4Exp full-attention layer, the MTP
draft layer included. This resolves the dtype per layer, the same way `Attention` and `MLAAttention`
already do (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/{attention,mla_attention}.py`).

Why it matters: with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, FP8 KV in the MTP layer's own attention lowers draft
acceptance at depth on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. Skipping just that layer (`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48`)
keeps the target KV in FP8 and restores acceptance.

## Evidence

DGX Spark (GB10), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 @ada4da32, MTP with 6 drafts, greedy, 41 prompts,
c=1, one node, with this change applied (measured on a nightly 0cbac6cd1-based image; the change is the same two lines on current main):

| target KV | MTP-layer KV | AL | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| fp8 | fp8 | 3.215 | 43.3 |
| bf16 | fp8 | 3.178 | 43.7 |
| fp8 | bf16 (`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48`) | 3.473 | 48.7 |
| bf16 | bf16 | 3.504 | 50.0 |

With FP8 KV in the MTP layer, conditional acceptance at depth 2 to 6 is 0.66 to 0.72. With BF16 it
is 0.74 to 0.80. Depth 1 is unchanged.

At 32k context (8 prompts of 32,928 tokens, 6 GiB KV), the skip costs 7% of the KV pool
(211,502 to 196,608 tokens at 3 drafts). Converting the whole cache to BF16 costs 29%.

## Duplicate check

- PRs and issues searched: "kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers", "kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers",
  "Qwen4Exp kv cache dtype", "QSA fp8 KV", "MTP fp8 kv cache acceptance", and open PRs touching
  qsa.py. None changes how QSA picks its per-layer KV dtype.
- Related, but not overlapping:
  - #54846: fp8/nvfp4 KV read path for QSA.
  - #56116: ModelOpt layer-wise mixed KV.
  - #47618: v1/v2 runner dtype sync.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -k skip_layers`
  - New regression test: the MTP layer prefix resolves to `auto` when listed, and stays `fp8` otherwise.
- End to end on GB10 as in the table above (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48`).

## Test Result

- `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py` on this branch (rebased on main 042ab0305c): 18 passed, 56 skipped (GPU-only cases).
- pre-commit clean.

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitter reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Cap JSON schema nesting to prevent 500s and API-server stalls
author: Mazukiri
body:
## Overview

A structured-output JSON schema or structural tag can be nested arbitrarily deep, and vLLM validates and converts it on the API server. That causes two problems:

- **Crash:** past ~980 levels, the recursive schema walks (`has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` and similar) raise `RecursionError`. The request returns HTTP 500 with an empty message.
- **Freeze:** below that, the schema is accepted, but `xgr.Grammar.from_json_schema` / `from_structural_tag` costs roughly *size × depth²* and runs synchronously on the event loop. One small request blocks every other request and `/health` for seconds; a depth-512 structural tag stalled the server for 34 s and still returned 200.

This PR rejects schemas nested more than 64 levels of objects and arrays with a 400, before any backend walks or converts them. OpenAI's spec allows 10 levels of schema nesting (`max_nesting_depth: 10` in `x-openai-structured-output-limits`), so 64 leaves plenty of headroom.

The first commit caught `RecursionError` instead. That fixed the crash but not the freeze, so the second commit replaces it with the depth cap.

## Test plan and results

End to end: NVIDIA H200, `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --no-enable-prefix-caching`. The same 42 requests were sent to `main` (`55b80221ed`) and to this change, measuring the worst concurrent `/health` latency during each request. Schema depth is the PR's original shape (2 JSON levels per step):

| Request | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response_format` depth 30 (63 levels) | 200 | 200, same output |
| `response_format` depth 31 (65 levels) | 200 | 400 |
| `response_format` depth 200 | 200, `/health` stalled 1.7 s | 400, no stall |
| depth 512 on chat, `structured_outputs`, Responses, completions, Anthropic `/v1/messages` | 500, `"message": ""` | 400 |
| structural tag depth 512 | 200 after 98.6 s, `/health` stalled 33.8 s | 400, no stall |
| strict tool + `tool_choice=auto` + `response_format` depth 512 | 500, "maximum recursion depth exceeded" | 400 |
| strict tool parameters at 65 levels | 200 | 200, same output |
| strict tool parameters at 123 levels | 200 | 400 |

The other 23 requests produced identical output on both: shallow schemas, a realistic nested schema, `json_object`, and shallow and strict tool calls.

The 400 message is: `The JSON schema is nested too deeply: objects and arrays may nest at most 64 levels`.

title: [Bugfix] Register the aten::mm out_dtype overloads for batch invariance
author: Mazukiri
body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and an fp32 lm_head (`--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'`, which
`ModelConfig` documents as "required for RL training-inference consistency"), the head runs
`torch.mm(x, w, out_dtype=torch.float32)`. That call dispatches to `aten::mm.dtype`, a separate overload
from `aten::mm`, so on CUDA SM8x, where batch-invariant mode installs the Triton matmul overrides, it
stays on cuBLAS. Whether the result then depends on the batch size depends on the shape: on an A40,
Mistral-7B-v0.1 (vocab 32000) shows it and Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (vocab 151936) do not. This PR registers
`aten::mm.dtype` and `aten::mm.dtype_out` next to `aten::mm`.

## Claims

- **Bug:** on `main`, Mistral-7B-v0.1 with an fp32 head gives different logprobs at batch size 1 and 32
  for 32 of 32 prompts on an A40. In an earlier run on an A40 (`main` 34051ad714, driver 595.91.07,
  2026-10-05), Qwen3-0.6B (bs 32) and Qwen3-1.7B (bs 64) with an fp32 head showed no difference; there,
  `torch.mm(out_dtype=fp32)` gave the same row 0 for every M tested at N = 151936, but not at N = 4096,
  8192 or 32000.
- **Root cause:** `aten::mm.dtype` and `aten::mm.dtype_out` are separate overloads of `aten::mm`, and
  `enable_batch_invariant_mode()` does not register them.
- **Fix:** one function, `mm_dtype_batch_invariant`, is registered for both overloads.
  `matmul_persistent()` takes an `out_dtype` and allocates its output in that type; the kernel already
  accumulates in fp32 and casts on store. The function keeps ATen's dtype checks for these overloads
  (for each case the same `RuntimeError` and message as `_mm_dtype_out_cuda`); shape errors still come
  from `matmul_persistent`, as with the existing `aten::mm` override.
- **Scope:** only the CUDA SM8x branch, and every `torch.mm(..., out_dtype=)` there, not just the
  lm_head. In-tree, that is also `GateLinear` tier 5 (the cuBLAS bf16→fp32 router GEMM), the non-SM90
  branch of the Inkling MoE router and the DeepSeek-V4 compressor/indexer scores. On the A40, `GateLinear`
  tier 5 was batch dependent on `main` at all four router shapes tested and is invariant with this PR.
  The lm_head runs eagerly (`compute_logits` is outside the compiled graph) and reaches `aten::mm.dtype`;
  `aten::mm.dtype_out` is what Inductor emits for the compiled callers. Hopper and Blackwell do not install
  the Triton overrides. XPU is unchanged: the fp32-head path is CUDA/ROCm only, and XPU's `aten::mm`
  override uses `matmul_descriptor_persistent`, which this PR does not touch. ROCm has no Triton matmul
  overrides on `main`; #52231 adds them and registers `aten::mm.out`, not `aten::mm.dtype`, so the same
  gap would reach ROCm when it lands.
- **Cost:** with the flag on, the fp32 head GEMM runs on the Triton persistent matmul instead of
  cuBLASLt. On the A40 that is 0.2–0.3 ms slower per call up to M=32 (Mistral-7B head shape), about the
  same at M=128 and 9% slower at M=512. It did not show in `vllm bench serve`.

## Validation

Commands, output excerpts and the full logs: [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60047#issuecomment-6012055668) and
[the dtype-check follow-up](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60047#issuecomment-6044314681). NVIDIA A40 (SM86), vLLM nightly wheel for
`main` `30ab428235` (`0.30.1rc1.dev708+g30ab42823`), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

- `pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py::test_mm_out_dtype_batch_invariance`
  fails on `main` (8166 of 8192 values of row 0 differ between M=1 and M=32) and passes with this PR.
- `test_mm_out_dtype_keeps_aten_dtype_checks`: with the flag on, invalid `out_dtype` / `out` dtypes raise
  the same errors as ATen (passes on `main` and with this PR; failed on the PR's earlier head).
- End to end, `repro_60047.py`: 32 of 32 prompts differ between batch size 1 and 32 on `main`
  (max |Δ logprob| 5.531e-05), 0 of 32 with this PR. Greedy tokens did not change in either run.
- `vllm bench serve` with the fp32 head, two runs per side (main, this PR, this PR, main): 3.87 and
  3.86 req/s on `main`, 3.86 and 3.88 req/s with this PR.

The new tests run in CI's A100 Batch Invariance job (`-k mm_out_dtype`, one line added here); the B200
job, which runs the whole file, skips them because Blackwell installs no Triton overrides.

## Details

- **Related:** #52231 (open) adds batch invariance on ROCm, including the `.out` overloads of
  mm/addmm/bmm. #59985 (open) turns `GateLinear` tier 5 off under the flag; on SM8x it overlaps with this
  PR there, without conflicting. #59952 (draft) rewrites `matmul_persistent`, and #55249, #54503, #55466
  and #60034 also edit these files, so one of them will need a small rebase.
- **Not a duplicate:** on 2026-10-06 I searched all vLLM PRs for `"mm.dtype"`, `"mm.dtype_out"`,
  `out_dtype batch invariant`, `head_dtype batch invariant`, `fp32 lm_head batch invariant` and
  `logits fp32 batch invariance`; the only match is this PR.
- **Not changed:** `aten::bmm.dtype` and `aten::bmm.dtype_out` have the same gap, but no in-tree caller
  uses them.
- **Limitations:** the fix was verified end to end on one model (Mistral-7B-v0.1) on one GPU (A40). It
  was not run on A100 or XPU.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and to run the measurements. I reviewed every changed line and the logs.

title: fix: exclude flashinfer-jit-cache from wheel install_requires
author: tarukumar
body:
## Problem

`setup.py` excludes `flashinfer-cubin` from `install_requires` because it is only published on the FlashInfer custom wheel index (`https://flashinfer.ai/whl`), not on PyPI. However, `flashinfer-jit-cache` — which is hosted on the same custom index — is not excluded.

The Dockerfile already installs `flashinfer-jit-cache` separately from the custom index:

```dockerfile
uv pip install --system flashinfer-jit-cache==${FLASHINFER_VERSION} \
    --index-url https://flashinfer.ai/whl/cu...
```

If `flashinfer-jit-cache` is added to `requirements/cuda.txt` (e.g. for pre-compiled JIT cache support), it would leak into the wheel metadata and make the published wheel uninstallable without the custom index configured:

```
error: No solution found when resolving dependencies
  cause: Because there is no version of flashinfer-jit-cache==X.Y.Z
         and vllm depends on flashinfer-jit-cache==X.Y.Z, ...
```

## Fix

Extend the existing `flashinfer-cubin` exclusion in `setup.py` to also cover `flashinfer-jit-cache`, keeping wheel metadata free of custom-index-only dependencies.
