title: [BugFix][Frontend] Pass reasoning_ended through render → generate (#60059)
author: YidaWeng
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60059.

With `--reasoning-parser`, `/v1/chat/completions` tells the engine when to start enforcing structured outputs through `reasoning_ended` and `reasoning_parser_kwargs`. The scale-out `/render` → `/inference/v1/generate` path dropped both, so the same rendered request was constrained differently depending on which path served it:

- `include_reasoning=false`: chat constrains from the first token, while generate let the model reason unconstrained first.
- Mistral parser grammars (`_grammar_from_parser`): the grammar expects to start at token 0, but on generate it only started after `[/THINK]`.
- Reasoners that read `chat_template_kwargs` (e.g. `deepseek_v3` with `enable_thinking`): the engine-side reasoner never saw the kwargs and disagreed with the frontend about whether thinking is on.

## Test Plan

Live model tests on an H200 with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, comparing this branch against main (`d0d6e5f3a2`) with the same requests.

1. Issue repro: serve with the `qwen3` reasoning parser, send the same JSON-schema chat request to `/v1/chat/completions` and through `/v1/chat/completions/render` → `/inference/v1/generate` (`output_mode="text"`), with `include_reasoning=false`, with `enable_thinking=false`, and with defaults.

   ```bash
   vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
       --enable-scale-out --no-enable-prefix-caching
   ```

2. Template kwargs: same comparison with `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v3`, which reads `enable_thinking` and uses Qwen3's `<think>` tokens, with `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": true}`, with and without `include_reasoning=false`.

3. Render routes: checked that `/v1/responses/render` and `/v1/messages/render` return the new fields.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Honor speculative cacheability in SimpleCPU
author: SherifWaly
body:
## Overview

Fix lost CPU prefix-cache reuse during speculative decoding with eager `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. Share the GPU coordinator's per-group cacheability rule with CPU store selection, and pass the configured prefill lookahead to the CPU coordinator.

Related: #54736, which is already merged and provides the underlying per-group offload geometry.

## Claims

- Prevent the CPU store cursor from permanently skipping blocks whose trailing KV is still re-prefillable during multi-module MTP.
- Preserve the extra cached draft block required by hybrid speculative prefix lookup.
- Preserve existing GPU cache-publication behavior by extracting its eligibility calculation into a shared helper.

## Validation

[Complete public reproducer, exact model config, patches, commands, and structured before/after records](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217).

Both GPU A/B cases use native `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` with a reduced config and **dummy weights**, three MTP modules, BF16, TP2/DCP2, model runner V2, a 64-token prefill budget, and real GPU/CPU transfers. The before/after columns compare separate unpatched and patched engines. Full reuse means matching that prompt's GPU-reusable prefix; block alignment and speculative cache-safety rules leave a suffix to recompute.

### Serial: the missing block persists across two CPU replays

Run one prompt at a time (`max_num_seqs=1`). For each prompt, clear both caches initially, then run **cold → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay 1 → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay 2 → GPU-hot control**. CPU caching survives both intermediate resets.

| Prompt tokens | CPU replay | GPU-hot reuse, both arms | CPU before | CPU after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,257 | 1 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,257 | 2 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,321 | 1 | 8,192 | **8,064** | **8,192** |
| 8,321 | 2 | 8,192 | **8,064** | **8,192** |

Both CPU replays have **zero local GPU-cache hits** in both arms. The unpatched 8,321-token case stays one effective 128-token block short on the second CPU replay; the later 8,192-token GPU-hot hit is a separate local-cache control. Output token IDs match across all four phases and both arms (16 request outputs).

Raw records and checked summary: [`serial-before.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-before-jsonl), [`serial-after.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-after-jsonl), and [`serial-comparison.json`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-comparison-json).

### Concurrent: uneven prefill chunks can eliminate CPU reuse

Submit both prompts together (`max_num_seqs=2`). They share the 64-token prefill budget with `long_prefill_token_threshold=63`, allowing uneven 63/1-token chunks. Each arm runs **cold → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay → GPU-hot control**. Each row below identifies a different prompt in the same concurrent batch.

| Prompt tokens | GPU-hot reuse, both arms | CPU replay before | CPU replay after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,257 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,321 | 8,192 | **0** | **8,192** |

The 8,257-token prompt is an unaffected control: its 8,064-token CPU hit already matches its full GPU-reusable prefix. The 8,321-token prompt reproduces the bug: CPU reuse is zero before the fix and reaches its full 8,192-token reusable prefix afterward.

CPU replay has **zero local GPU-cache hits** in both arms. Output token IDs match across all three phases and both arms (12 request outputs). The later GPU-hot control cannot warm the earlier CPU replay.

Raw records and checked summary: [`concurrent-before.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-before-jsonl), [`concurrent-after.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-after-jsonl), and [`concurrent-comparison.json`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-comparison-json).

### Environment and additional checks

- **GPU environment:** 2× B200, driver 580.126.20; public image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:584c6bc58f76411936e0f22a37039e436019e155ae144c017b7eebbe2edc1d4e`; vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`. Only the two production files in this PR are patched in the fixed arm. They are identical at the image's source revision and the PR base `30d4032363d4a1f6412d9a235049673b41309f98`.
- **New CPU regression on the PR base:** baseline **12 failed / 6 passed**; patched **18 passed**, included in the **78/78** passing offload scheduler tests. The matrix covers replicated SWA, replicated full-attention, and sharded full-attention drafts; dense/latest-only retention; small/large chunks and multi-token prefill lookahead. It checks GPU/CPU hit equivalence and the loaded block hashes using real cache managers with simulated transfer completion.
- **Existing prefix-cache coverage:** **31 passed**, selecting EAGLE, cache publication, retention, and per-group DCP tests.
- **Code checks:** all applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy 3.10, and CI test tethering; the additional mypy 3.12 check and `git diff --check` passed.
- The added cases extend the existing offload scheduler suite already run by `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

The tables report one serial A/B and one concurrent A/B. They establish cache/transfer consistency, not trained-model accuracy or production throughput. Elapsed times include warmup effects and are not used to claim a speedup. Both cases exercise sharded MTP; replicated SWA is covered by the CPU matrix. A trained-model accuracy evaluation is not included.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Download the linked gist into a fresh directory for each case. This command selects the concurrent case:

```bash
mkdir -p models/tiny_mtp
cp config.json models/tiny_mtp/config.json
docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --ipc=host \
  -e REPRO_CASE=concurrent \
  -v "$PWD:/repro" --entrypoint bash \
  vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:584c6bc58f76411936e0f22a37039e436019e155ae144c017b7eebbe2edc1d4e \
  -lc 'REPRO_ROOT=/repro bash /repro/run_in_container.sh'
```

For the serial case, run the same command in another fresh gist directory with `-e REPRO_CASE=serial`. It runs both CPU replays with a GPU-only reset before each. Each invocation uses a fresh container so the baseline starts from the stock package.

The measured run used this image through Enroot; the equivalent Docker launcher above has not itself been run. The scripts and comparison logic are the measured versions. No checkpoint download is required. The wrapper enables serialization for its own offline layout-inspection RPC and starts no HTTP server.

CPU commands run on the PR checkout (`GIST_DIR` points to the downloaded gist containing the upstream logging fixtures; dependencies and the public OPT-125M config used by the existing test fixture are already installed):

```bash
# Run with only regression.patch applied to reproduce the baseline failures.
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q \
  -k test_dcp_draft_offload_preserves_prefix --tb=short
# Baseline: 12 failed, 6 passed.

# Run with the full fix applied.
PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$GIST_DIR" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  -p upstream_log_fixtures tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q --tb=short
# 78 passed, including all 18 new cases.

PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q \
  -k 'eagle or cache_blocks or retention or per_group_dcp' --tb=short
# 31 passed, 140 deselected.
```

Code checks (with the three changed files staged):

```bash
uv --no-config tool run --from 'pre-commit>=4.5.1' pre-commit run
uv --no-config tool run --from 'pre-commit>=4.5.1' pre-commit run \
  mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py
git diff --check
```

</details>

## Details

Eager CPU selection currently rounds confirmed tokens to a common alignment. This can disagree with GPU cacheability in two ways:

1. Multi-module MTP keeps `num_prefill_lookahead - 1` trailing tokens re-prefillable. A block can fall inside the CPU scan before the GPU has hashed it. Selection skips it as not hashed but advances the persistent store cursor, so it is never revisited after finalization. A missing early block can collapse the reusable CPU prefix to zero.
2. Hybrid speculative lookup matches an extra draft block and then drops it. GPU publication already allows this block past the aligned boundary, but CPU selection truncates it away, losing otherwise reusable prefix length.

`get_num_cacheable_tokens()` extracts the existing GPU eligibility calculation. GPU publication and eager CPU selection now use it, including the per-group draft-block rule. The CPU coordinator also receives `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens`, so both sides agree on finalization. This adds no GPU synchronization and does not change model computation.

**Duplicate-work check:** #54736 fixes geometry/fine-grained offload support, not this speculative eligibility mismatch. #58413 changes align-mode Mamba chunks in the separate `OffloadingConnector`; #54979 concerns terminal GPU cache registration; #50897 proposes a broader successor-aware hash/publication protocol. None implements this `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` store-boundary fix. Searches for open SimpleCPU/speculative offload fixes found no equivalent PR.

**AI assistance was used** for implementation, tests, reproduction, and this description.

title: [Bugfix] Use FusedMoEWithLoRA for shared MoE LoRAs on 3D models
author: Aravind-11
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60093. `--enable-moe-shared-loras` on a 3D-weight MoE model crashed during LoRA warmup because the experts module was still wrapped in `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA`, which never builds `lora_a_stacked`.

## Claims

- Shared-outer MoE adapters (`experts.w1` / `experts.w2` / `experts.w3`) now use `FusedMoEWithLoRA` on 3D-weight models such as GPT-OSS.
- Engine startup with `--enable-lora --enable-moe-shared-loras` completes warmup instead of raising `AttributeError: 'MoERunner' object has no attribute 'lora_a_stacked'`.
- 3D PEFT adapters without this flag still use `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA`.

## Validation

Reproduced the crash and the fix on a Colab Tesla T4 (16 GB, compute capability 7.5, driver 580.82.07), vLLM 0.31.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The checkpoint was `openai/gpt-oss-20b` cut to 1 layer and 8 experts, unquantized, `load_format=dummy`, float16, so the run fits the T4. `LLM()` takes the same profile run as `vllm serve`.

Before the change, model load succeeded (2.62 GiB) and warmup failed in `create_dummy_lora`:

```text
AttributeError: 'MoERunner' object has no attribute 'lora_a_stacked'
```

After the wrapper change, the same `LLM()` call returns. vLLM 0.31.0 with this patch applied to `vllm/lora/model_manager.py` finished warmup (`PY_EXIT:0`) on that T4. The previous run, identical except for the patch, died in `create_dummy_lora`.

A second load of that engine printed:

```text
model GptOssForCausalLM
WRAPPER FusedMoEWithLoRA shared True lora_a_stacked True n 24
```

The full 24-layer mxfp4 `vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b` command was not run. The failure and the fix are both in wrapper selection during warmup, before any token is generated. CI does not currently run an `enable_moe_shared_loras` test; there was no existing coverage to extend without a GPU MoE checkpoint.

## Details

`enable_moe_shared_loras` rewrites the experts packed mapping to `["experts.w1", "experts.w2", "experts.w3"]`. `create_dummy_lora` then treats the module as packed and indexes `lora_a_stacked`. That list is built only by `FusedMoEWithLoRA.create_lora_weights`, which also reads the flag and collapses the shared factors to expert-dim 1. `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA` overrides `create_lora_weights`, ignores the flag, and keeps the fused gate/up pair (`set_lora` requires two tensors).

The manager already forces `FusedMoEWithLoRA` for `--enable-mixed-moe-lora-format`. Shared-outer adapters are the same 2D layout, so a 3D base model has to use that wrapper too. `_is_3d_moe_model` stays true only when neither flag is set, which preserves the fused PEFT path.

Limitation: a 3D PEFT checkpoint (fused gate/up on disk) is not a shared-outer adapter. Serving that file still requires leaving `enable_moe_shared_loras` off, or converting it under `--enable-mixed-moe-lora-format`.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Size per-region replicate flags by each region's block count
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Background

With P_TP > D_TP (e.g. PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 decode), each decoder rank reads a block from several prefill ranks. Each local descriptor gets a replicate flag: full-attention regions are **SPLIT** (each rank fills its head slice), MLA regions are **REPLICATE** (whole block read once).

`_fa_desc_replicated` assumed every region holds the same number of blocks. HiSparse breaks this: host-resident MLA regions hold `hisparse_host_num_blocks`, GPU regions hold `num_blocks`. Every P_TP > D_TP handshake into a HiSparse decoder failed with `AssertionError: FA desc flags N != num_fa_descs M`.

## Fix

Build the flags the same way `_build_fa_local` builds the descriptors: same region order, `region_num_blocks[i] * block_size_ratio` per region. Companion fix for the same topology: #60108. No other open PR touches this function.

## Validation

**main vs. this PR**, checked against the descriptors `_build_fa_local` emits:

| Region layout | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Equal block counts | OK | OK |
| HiSparse, unequal block counts | assert | OK |
| Unequal counts that divide evenly | flags silently wrong | OK |
| Layer-name routing, region listed twice | flags silently wrong | OK |

**Unit:** `test_tp_mapping.py` + `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`: 121 passed.

**E2E** (GLM-5.3, 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 HiSparse decode, with #60108): main asserts on the first request. With both fixes, 8 one-hour agentic benchmark points ran with 0 errors and a 100% decoder prefix-cache hit rate. That run used an earlier revision of this fix that produces identical flags for this topology.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Return NumPy descriptors from mixed-memory local registration
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Overview

With mixed DRAM/VRAM registration (HiSparse host-resident regions), `register_local_xfer_handler` returned the local descriptors as a list of tuples instead of its annotated `np.ndarray`. The P_TP > D_TP split path (`_build_local_splits_from_plan`) calls `.tolist()` on them, so a PCP8/DCP8 prefiller feeding a HiSparse decoder failed the NIXL handshake with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist'`. Companion fix for the same topology: #60107.

**Fix:** keep the Nx3 `uint64` array in the mixed-memory path. DRAM rows get device 0 via `blocks_data[desc_is_dram, 2] = 0`, and the DRAM/VRAM subsets are array slices.

## Validation

**Unit:** `test_mixed_memory_local_descriptors_split_by_memory_type` now asserts the returned descriptors are an `np.ndarray` (fails before the fix). `test_tp_mapping.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`: 498 passed (3 GPU e2e tests left to CI).

**End to end**, GLM-5.3 on 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8/EP8 prefill → DP8/EP8 HiSparse decode, MTP3:

| vLLM | Result |
|---|---|
| main + #60107 | decoder fails in `_build_local_splits_from_plan` on the first request; no KV transferred |

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Alias `qwen3_xml` to `qwen3_coder` and add `qwen3_json` for the Qwen JSON format
author: lianakoleva
body:
## Overview

In Python, `qwen3_xml` has always parsed the Qwen3-Coder XML format (`<tool_call><function=...><parameter=...>`): it was added as a second implementation of `qwen3_coder` in #25028 and became the same class in #45003. In Rust, `qwen3_xml` instead parsed the Qwen2.5/QwQ/Qwen3 JSON format (`<tool_call>\n{"name": ..., "arguments": ...}\n</tool_call>`), so recipes such as [Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B](https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) that use `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` with `--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml` produced no tool calls.

This PR fixes the name without regressing Qwen models that rely on Rust parser auto-detection.

## Claims

- `qwen3_xml` is an alias of `qwen3_coder` in both frontends.
- The existing Rust parser for the Qwen JSON format is kept unchanged and renamed to `qwen3_json`. Rust auto-detection routes Qwen2.5, QwQ and Qwen3 models to it.
- Python registers `qwen3_json` as an alias of `hermes` for now, so both frontends accept the same `--tool-call-parser` values. A TODO tracks a dedicated Python parser.
- Explicit `--tool-call-parser hermes` keeps the generic Hermes behavior shared with Python.

## Validation

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser --features test-util`: 553 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat`: 392 passed, including the roundtrip tests and the XGrammar grammar replay.
- New test `factory_parses_qwen3_coder_format_with_qwen3_xml`: `qwen3_xml` parses the Qwen3-Coder XML format.
- Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, checked locally with temporary roundtrip cases (not committed):
  - Under `hermes`, `content` gets a trailing `\n\n`.
  - Under `qwen3_json`, all three tool-choice modes (auto, required, named) roundtrip, and their grammars pass a token-zero XGrammar replay.
- QwQ-32B renders tool calls character-for-character the same as Qwen2.5.
- Python: `ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("qwen3_json")` resolves to `Hermes2ProToolParser`.

## Details

- `qwen3_xml` registers `Qwen3CoderToolParser` directly, like `llama3_json`/`llama4_json`, instead of a separate wrapper type.
- Why Qwen models are not routed to `hermes` in Rust. The Qwen chat templates render `\n` before and between tool calls, and `hermes` does not handle it:
  - The `hermes` parser leaks this `\n` into `content`.
  - The Hermes structural tag joins calls with an empty separator, so `tool_choice=required` rejects the `\n` between parallel calls. With `hermes`, the Qwen3-0.6B grammar replay fails on exactly this token.
- `qwen3_json` keeps the newline framing and the `Model::Qwen3` structural tag, so the Qwen3 `tool_call_mix` roundtrip and its grammar replay fixture are unchanged.
- The bench is renamed from `qwen3_xml` to `qwen3_json`.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Qwen4Exp FP8 PLE pinned lookup kernel failing to compile below SM89
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #59868. On GPUs below SM89 (the report uses 4 × RTX 3090), Qwen4Exp with an FP8 E4M3FN PLE table and `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}'` crashes in `profile_run`. The crash is a Triton `CompilationError` from `_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel`. This PR makes that kernel copy rows as raw bytes, so the FP8 type never enters its signature.

## Claims

- `_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel` now compiles and runs on sm_86 with an FP8 E4M3FN table, and it copies FP8 rows bit-exactly.
- On an A40, three existing FP8 pinned-lookup tests in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py` failed before this change. They now pass.
- BF16 lookups are unchanged: same bits, same speed.
- The module still imports when Triton is not installed.

## Validation

Hardware: a machine with 4 × NVIDIA A40 (sm_86). The reproducer uses one GPU. Software: vLLM commit `92044241a` (`0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`), with and without this PR, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12.12.

**Reproducer.** The reported path needs a checkpoint with FP8 PLE weights and a global scale. The public `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` checkpoint has BF16 PLE weights and no scale. So the reproducer launches the kernel directly with a small FP8 tensor. Below is the core of the script that ran. The full script only adds prints and a `try`/`except`.

```python
import torch
from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.ngram_embedding import (
    _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel,
)

N, D, BLOCK_D = 4, 16, 16
device = torch.device("cuda", 0)
weight = torch.zeros(N, D, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device=device)
ids = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
output = torch.zeros(1, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)

_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel[(ids.numel(),)](
    weight, ids, output, D, 0, N, BLOCK_D=BLOCK_D,
)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

Run it from outside the source tree: `python -P repro_59868.py`.

| | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 3 of 3 failed | `CompilationError`, exit code 1 | | After | 2 of 2 passed | launch completes, exit code 0 |

Two of the "before" runs used the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` image, and one used a source install. The "after" runs used the final patch. Three more runs on earlier versions of the patch also passed. Before the fix, every run showed the same error as the report:

```
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 1:0:
def _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel(
^
ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')")
```

The reproducer writes from an FP8 weight into a BF16 output. vLLM never does this, because `_lookup` requires `output.dtype == weight.dtype`. After the fix, that call copies the raw FP8 bytes. So the reproducer only shows that the launch compiles. The tests below check the values on the real path.

**Existing tests.**

```
python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q --noconftest -k "pinned or uva"
```

`--noconftest` was used only because `tblib` was not installed locally.

- Before: `3 failed, 13 passed, 59 deselected`. All three fail with the error above: `test_ple_pinned_embedding_loads_on_cpu_and_looks_up_through_uva[True]`, `test_amd_pinned_embedding_output_written_under_compile[fp8]` and `test_amd_pinned_embedding_output_written_under_cudagraph_capture[fp8]`. They go through `_lookup` and check exact values.
- After: `16 passed, 59 deselected`. The full `test_ple.py` together with `tests/test_triton_utils.py` gives `88 passed`.

**Other checks.** These used one-off scripts that are not part of this PR.

- NVIDIA serving flow with FP8 on the A40 (`start_prefetch` → `forward` → `dequantize`): bit-exact against `weight[ids]` for row widths 3 and 160. With an ETP size of 2, rows owned by the other rank come out as zero bytes, in FP8 and in BF16.
- Large BF16 lookup with 160-element rows, compared row by row with `weight[ids]`: 7,000,000 and 8,388,608 rows gave 0 wrong rows, with byte offsets up to 2,684,354,240. Without the int64 row index (see Details), 7,000,000 rows hit `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`.
- BF16 speed against the old kernel, reading a pinned host table through UVA: time ratio ×0.993 to ×1.03 for row widths 64 to 1024 and for 160 (the real model's width). Outputs were bit-identical.
- Import with Triton hidden (`sys.modules["triton"] = None`) passes. Without the placeholder change it fails with `AttributeError: module 'triton.language' has no attribute 'pointer_type'`.
- `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passes.

**CI gap.** On NVIDIA, CI does not run the GPU tests in `test_ple.py`, and no CI runner is below SM89. So CI cannot catch this bug if it comes back. The runs above are the validation. The AMD MI355 job does run `test_ple.py`, so it covers the new byte copy on AMD.

## Details

**Root cause.** The kernel's pointer parameters had no annotations, so Triton took their types from the tensors. An FP8 E4M3FN table became a `*fp8e4nv` parameter. Triton 3.7.1 accepts `fp8e4nv` only on compute capability 8.9 and higher. It rejects the type while it lowers the signature, before it compiles the body. That is why the error points at `1:0`, the `def` line. On the A40, a kernel with an empty body and one `float8_e4m3fn` pointer fails the same way. With `float8_e5m2` it compiles.

**Fix.** The kernel does no math on the values. Its only caller, `Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding._lookup`, requires the output dtype to match the weight dtype. FP8 scaling happens later, in PyTorch (`dequantize`). So the kernel is a pure row gather. Both pointers are now annotated `tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8)`. The caller passes `row_bytes = embedding_dim * weight.element_size()` and sets `BLOCK_D = next_power_of_2(row_bytes)`. This works for FP8 and for BF16. `_reduce_etp_embeddings` in the same file already moves FP8 rows as raw bytes. The fix has to be in the signature, because the signature is where the error happens. A `uint8` pointer cast inside the body would come too late. A `.view(torch.uint8)` at the call site would fix `_lookup`, but not a direct launch with an FP8 tensor like the reproducer.

The fix also needs two more changes:

- `row_id` is now int64. Offsets are now in bytes, so for BF16 `row_id * row_bytes` is twice the old element offset. An int32 product would overflow at half as many rows as before. With `embedding_across_dp`, it would overflow at DP × `max_num_batched_tokens` ≥ 419,431 instead of 838,861 (for example, DP8 × 65,536). `tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)` is the usual vLLM idiom.
- `TritonLanguagePlaceholder` gets `uint8` and `pointer_type`. Python evaluates parameter annotations at import time, so without these names the module fails to import when Triton is missing. This is the first `tl.pointer_type` annotation in `vllm/`. mypy rejects it, so both lines carry `# type: ignore[valid-type]`.

**Limitations.**

- No end-to-end `vllm serve` run with an FP8 PLE checkpoint (see Reproducer). Only sm_86 was tested, not sm_80.
- `_engram_lookup_kernel` in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` also takes an FP8 E4M3FN table with no annotation, so it may fail the same way below SM89. It was not run. It does math on the values, so this byte-copy fix does not carry over, and it is not part of this PR.
- No model evaluation was run. The lookups are bit-exact in the tests above.

## E2E results (patch)

`vllm serve` with `-tp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 32768 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}'`. The patch is applied on top of `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691`. GSM8K is 5-shot, chat mode, thinking disabled (stderr ≈ ±0.7).

| Model | GPU | PLE dtype | Result | GSM8K flexible / strict | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | A100 (SM80) | FP8 E4M3, pinned host | starts and serves | 92.95 / 91.96 | 
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | B200 (SM100) | FP8 E4M3, pinned host | bit-identical to unpatched | 92.49 / 91.51 |
| `Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | B200 (SM100) | BF16, pinned host | bit-identical to unpatched | 93.40 / 92.34 |

"Bit-identical" means greedy decoding at batch size 1: 10/10 prompts and 640/640 tokens match the unpatched build, with exactly equal logprobs.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Preserve small FP8 softmax weights in Triton attention
author: andylolu2
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Why

The Triton unified-attention kernel casts softmax probabilities to `V.dtype` before `P @ V`. With an FP8 KV cache, small probabilities can underflow to zero and lose meaningful contributions to the attention output.

## Summary

- Scale `P` before its FP8 cast and undo the scale after the FP32 dot. The scale is 256 for NVIDIA E4M3 and 128 for other FP8 formats.
- Add a focused regression test for an `exp(-8)` probability that previously became zero. Existing tests and tolerances are unchanged.

This is the same [low-precision scaling technique](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/2e3a6694ba2f0d8e106f28d2a5d3f6050ebf1572/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm100.py#L85-L90) used by FlashAttention's Blackwell kernel. Its 8-bit path sets [`max_offset = 8`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/2e3a6694ba2f0d8e106f28d2a5d3f6050ebf1572/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm100.py#L2189-L2209), equivalent to scaling `P` by 256 before the low-precision dot.

## Reviewer guide

- `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py` contains the scaling fix.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py` only adds the focused underflow regression.

## Test plan

The exact two-file patch was validated on an NVIDIA B200 in a compatible vLLM checkout; the available GPU image does not include the PyTorch 2.13 environment declared by current `main`.

- `test_fp8_softmax_preserves_small_probabilities`: passes. Before the fix it returns `0.0` instead of `0.0102923084`; after the fix its maximum absolute error is `2.2633e-5` with `atol=5e-5` and `rtol=0.01`.
- Pre-commit passes on both changed files.
- WikiText-2 with [`nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor`](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor), `TRITON_ATTN`, FP8 KV cache, eager execution, and `max_length=2048`: PPL improves from `8.025217` to `8.003337` (`-0.273%`). Of 167 chunks, 123 improve and 44 regress.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Fix TP handshake test after per-region FA desc flags
author: gty111
body:
## Purpose

#60107 changed `_fa_desc_replicated` to size flags from `region_num_blocks[i]`. `test_prefill_tp_size_greater_than_decode_tp_size` registers a single local block (`num_descs=1`) but its fake handshake sizes `region_num_blocks` from `kv_cache_config.num_blocks` (default 100), so the new cross-check fails:

```
AssertionError: FA desc flags 100 != num_fa_descs 1
```

Fix: pass `num_blocks=1` to both the connector and the fake worker so the registration stays consistent. Test-only change.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -q
```

## Test Result

175 passed (was: 2 failed on main).

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Fix Humming FP8 linear for per-tensor/per-channel FP8 weights
author: Manfredss
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60162. With the Humming FP8 linear kernel, `fp8` checkpoints with per-tensor weight scales and online `fp8_per_tensor` / `fp8_per_channel` quantization crash while loading weights. On Ampere with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, Humming is the only FP8 linear kernel left (Marlin opts out of batch-invariant mode), so these models cannot start in that mode. Humming FP8 is W8A16, so `fp8_per_channel` (PTPC, which asks for per-token FP8 activations) now gets the same clear error as on Marlin instead of running.

## Claims

- `Fp8LinearMethod` (non-block) and `Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod` load and run on Humming. GSM8K accuracy is within about one standard error of Marlin.
- On Ampere with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, these models start and are batch-invariant under the default torch.compile + CUDA graphs.
- `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` rejects Humming with the same error it already raises for Marlin.

## Validation

Latest run, after merging main (Oct 26): one A40 (SM86) on Runpod, official image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b`, with this PR's diff applied to the installed package. Raw logs: [PTPC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60163#discussion_r4383165873), [everything else](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60163#issuecomment-6428742135).

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_model_load_and_run` | `humming` case fails (stride error) | 3 passed, 3 skipped |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (stride error)* | starts; batch-invariant 3/3; GSM8K 0.7544 |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (stride error)* | starts; batch-invariant 3/3; GSM8K 0.8673 |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_channel`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (stride error) | `ValueError`: Humming is W8A16 (same check as Marlin) |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_channel`, `--linear-backend humming` | — | same `ValueError` |

\* From the earlier runs below; main's code path for these is unchanged.

GSM8K is lm_eval `gsm8k` (5-shot, all 1319 questions), flexible-extract. For reference, on the Oct 20 RTX 3090 run, Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 in default mode (Marlin on both sides) scored 0.7642 on main and with this PR.

<details>
<summary>Earlier runs (Oct 6, Oct 15, Oct 20)</summary>

Rows that show `fp8_per_channel` starting on Humming predate the PTPC check.

**Oct 20**, RTX 3090, nightly `e68efc68`: repro, lm_eval and bench with raw logs in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60163#issuecomment-6286567601).

**Re-validated after merging main (Oct 15).** Head `671702b6e` (main `984c242ede` + this PR). Since main's latest wheel was not published yet, I used the precompiled extensions from `388a610dfb` (the only build change in between is the DeepGEMM tag) with torch 2.14.0, humming-kernels 0.1.17 and flashinfer 0.7.1, on an A40 inside the official nightly image's CUDA environment. Toggling between main and this PR was checked by SHA-256 of the touched files.

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (stride error) | starts; batch-invariant 3/3; GSM8K 0.780 |
| Qwen3-8B `fp8_per_tensor` / `fp8_per_channel`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | — | start; batch-invariant 3/3 each |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8, `--linear-backend humming` | — | GSM8K 0.784 (Marlin baseline on main: 0.772) |
| `test_model_load_and_run` with this PR's test | `humming` fails (stride error) | 3 passed |
| `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py` | 3 `test_fp8_reloading` failures | same 3 failures, 26 passed |

GSM8K uses 500 questions, 5-shot.

The original validation below was done before the merge, on nightly `92044241`.

Run on the official image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` on an A40 (SM86), with the container's environment. The installed source files were checked against commit `92044241` by SHA-256 before testing. "This PR" means this diff applied to the installed package; the touched files are unchanged between `92044241` and this PR's base. Batch invariance uses the reproducer from #59086: request A alone, alone again, then batched with a longer request B; 48 greedy tokens; 3 rounds.

| Model / quantization | Flags | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8` (`fp8`, per-tensor) | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash: `self.stride(-1) must be 1 to view Float8_e4m3fn as Int ... but got 4096` | starts; A batched vs alone identical 3/3; GSM8K 0.790 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B --quantization fp8_per_tensor` | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (same error) | starts; identical 3/3 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B --quantization fp8_per_channel` | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (same error) | starts; identical 3/3 |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 | `--linear-backend humming` | crash | starts; GSM8K 0.784 |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_tensor` | `--linear-backend humming` | crash | — |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 (control) | default (Marlin) | GSM8K 0.786 | — |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8` (block, control) | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | works, identical 3/3 | — |

GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 500` (5-shot).

`test_model_load_and_run` now also runs with `linear_backend="humming"` (`pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_model_load_and_run -v`, same image):

| | auto | marlin | humming |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | passed | passed | **failed** (stride error above) |
| this PR | passed | passed | passed |

The rest of `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py` gives the same result with and without this PR on this GPU. Three `test_fp8_reloading` cases fail on the A40 either way with identical errors, and are unrelated to this change. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

</details>

## Details

**Missing layout tag.** `process_fp8_weight_tensor_strategy` returns the weight as a `(K, N)` transposed view, and `Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod` transposes it itself. Humming's `convert_linear_layer_to_humming_standard` reads `layer.processed_weight_dims` (falling back to the parameter's checkpoint `input_dim`/`output_dim`) to detect the layout. Without it, Humming assumes `(N, K)` and calls `.view(torch.int32)` on the transposed view, which fails. Since #62326, CompressedTensors, fbgemm, ModelOpt and Quark FP8 set `processed_weight_dims = (0, 1)` after transposing. This PR does the same in the two methods that lacked it. Humming is the only FP8 scaled-mm kernel that reads it, so other kernels are unaffected.

**PTPC.** `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` already refuses Marlin because PTPC requires per-token FP8 activations and Marlin FP8 is W8A16. `HummingFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` builds its layer without an input schema, so it is W8A16 too. With the layout fixed, PTPC would silently run as weight-only FP8 on Humming, so this PR adds Humming to that check. `Fp8LinearMethod` and `fp8_per_tensor` already accept Marlin's W8A16 fallback, and Humming matches it.

**Batch-invariant `apply`.** In batch-invariant mode these methods call the kernel only when `fp8_scaled_mm_is_batch_invariant()` (from #52231) says so; otherwise they dequantize `layer.weight` and run `F.linear`. After Humming's `process_weights_after_loading`, `layer.weight` is in Humming's packed layout, so that fallback fails (`a and b must have same reduction dim, but got [s, 4096] X [256, 24576]`). Humming has its own batch-invariant mode (`use_batch_invariant` in its compute config), and the block-FP8 path and compressed-tensors already call it in this mode. This PR makes `fp8_scaled_mm_is_batch_invariant()` return True for Humming. Humming FP8 is weight-only here, so the dynamic per-tensor activation amax that the helper guards against doesn't apply.

**Notes.**
- Without batch-invariant mode, two identical requests on Humming were not bitwise identical (first difference at token 4). With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` they were. vLLM only promises this in batch-invariant mode, and it does not come from this change.
- CI: the new `humming` case is in `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py`, whose Quantization step is temporarily disabled by #63608. The layout bug does not depend on the GPU architecture. I validated on SM86 only.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open issues and PRs for Humming FP8 linear, the stride error message, the layout tags, and FP8 batch invariance on Ampere. #59460 also edits `scaled_mm/humming.py` (activation-quantization fallbacks) but not the weight layout or batch-invariant dispatch, and this PR does not touch `humming.py`.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Preserve Rust SSE payloads across chunks and comments
author: Jaeyeong-CHOI
body:
## Overview

Preserve SSE text and usage in the Rust benchmark clients across HTTP chunk boundaries, LF/CRLF/CR event framing, and leading comment lines. This combines the related response-data-loss fixes in one small production change and one shared HTTP test fixture.

## Claims

- Preserve transport-fragment whitespace instead of stripping generated text and SSE delimiters.
- Normalize CRLF/CR framing while retaining byte buffering and early complete-JSON dispatch.
- Keep valid data fields in events beginning with comments in both OpenAI-compatible backends.

## Validation

On repository-pinned Rust 1.95, the combined backend suite passed all 20 tests; the full package passed 172 unit + 3 CLI integration tests, with 12 existing resource-dependent tests ignored. Whole-workspace fmt, all-targets/all-features clippy with warnings denied, applicable pre-commit hooks and the diff check passed. Tested Spark source SHA-256 matches local source. Independent reviews found no blocking source issues; exact-union checks confirmed no extra integration logic.

Executed on an isolated ARM64 CPU, one build/test thread, without model downloads or GPU use:

```bash
cd rust
cargo test --locked -p vllm-bench backends:: -- --test-threads=1
cargo test --locked -p vllm-bench -- --test-threads=1
cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-bench --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

Nextest was unavailable in the isolated toolchain. Supporting standalone baseline evidence: the newline tests produced 16 passes / 3 failures, including `leadingtrailing!` instead of `leading  trailing!`; the comment tests produced 16 passes / 1 failure, returning `!` instead of `hi!` in the first completions/content case. That loop stops at its first failure, so other baseline comment cases are not claimed as executed. These are two separate pre-fix runs, distinct from the combined results above. Four added regressions exercise the handler and both real HTTP backends without new sleeps or timing-duration thresholds.

This modifies benchmark response clients, not model inference or the serving engine. The HTTP regressions use loopback fixtures, not model servers. No live model evaluation, performance improvement, or production deployment reproduction is claimed.

## Details

Three stages could lose valid response data: each backend trimmed raw byte fragments, the handler recognized only `\n\n` framing, and each backend discarded a whole event beginning with `:` before selecting its data field. The fix passes bytes intact, normalizes framing with a persisted CR state, and lets the existing multi-field selection skip comments rather than their payloads. The existing socket fixture is shared once by both HTTP regressions.

The union does not introduce a general SSE parser or change existing early-JSON, EOF, `[DONE]`, success-classification, or usage-accounting semantics. One-line comment-only messages now take the existing harmless failed-JSON path. Multiline-data and other EventSource conformance questions remain outside scope.

Live duplicate checks on 2026-10-06 found no open Rust fix covering these data-loss paths. [#51172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51172) changes Python transport; merged [#50868](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50868) introduced the UTF-8 buffering retained here; [#59736](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59736) changes tokenless-chat success; [#59694](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59694) changes prompt-token accounting. Textual backend conflicts remain possible, but their behavioral changes are not duplicated.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, tests, integration, and review. The human submitter reviewed the changes and authorized submission. The validation results above were obtained with AI assistance.

title: [Bugfix][Weight Cache] Key non-MoE DP daemons as DP=1 like the engine
author: nien-hui
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60178 . A dense (non-MoE) engine with `--data-parallel-size N` sends `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` to the `vllm preload` daemon, which keys each rank as `dp_size=N, dp_rank=r`, so `--load-format ipc_cache` never maps the cached weights. The daemon now keys dense DP ranks as `(1, 0)` like the engine; MoE daemons are unchanged (follow-up to #57386).

## Claims

- A dense model with `--data-parallel-size N` and `--load-format ipc_cache` now maps its weights from the daemon on every rank.
- MoE daemons, daemons started without DP, and the per-GPU workaround from the issue are unchanged.
- No open PR touches the daemon's key. #59648 (`protocol.py`) and #59813 (`ipc_loader.py`) each add tests to `test_weight_cache.py`, a trivial rebase either way. #60006 rewrites `docs/features/preload.md` and keeps listing data parallelism as supported, which this fix makes true for dense models too.

## Validation

Unit test, no GPU needed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k "daemon or key or copy_mode" -q
```

`5 passed`. The new `test_daemon_keys_dense_dp_ranks_like_the_engine` checks that the daemon's key for a dense DP rank equals `ParallelConfig` after `reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()`, and that a MoE rank keeps `(dp_size, dp_rank)`.

End-to-end on 2x RTX A6000 with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `main` at 5f30fc7031 vs this branch. Each scenario runs `vllm preload`, then `vllm serve --load-format ipc_cache`, then one greedy completion. "Map" means the worker logs `Mapped 339 tensors from the weight cache daemon`.

| | daemon | engine | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `-dp 2` | `-dp 2`, `fallback=false` | fails to start, `WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size']` | 2/2 ranks map |
| B | `-dp 2` | `-dp 2`, default | 0/2 map, both ranks fall back to disk | 2/2 map |
| C | no DP | no DP | 1/1 map | 1/1 map |
| D | one no-DP daemon per GPU | `-dp 2` | 2/2 map | 2/2 map |

Every run that starts returns the same text before and after. `pre-commit` passes.

The unit test runs in the existing Model Executor CI step (`pytest model_executor`). The DP scenarios need two GPUs and a server, so they are not added to CI.

Not validated: TP > 1 with DP, multi-node DP, MoE with DP end to end, the Ray DP path, and draft daemons with DP.

## Details

Root cause:

1. For a non-MoE model, `run_engine_core` calls `reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` on every DP rank, which sets `data_parallel_size = 1` and `data_parallel_rank = 0` ([`core.py` L1388-L1397](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L1388-L1397)).
2. `IpcModelLoader` builds the key from `get_dp_group()`, so a dense engine sends `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` on every GPU ([`ipc_loader.py` L345-L357](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L345-L357)).
3. `WeightCacheDaemon` used the launcher's `data_parallel_size` and its own `dp_rank` regardless of the model.

Fix: a new `get_engine_dp_placement(vllm_config, dp_rank)` in `daemon.py` returns `(1, 0)` when the target model is not MoE and `(dp_size, dp_rank)` otherwise. The daemon passes that to `WeightCacheKey.from_model_config`. It keys on the target model's `is_moe`, like `core.py`, so a draft daemon follows its target. It has one call site but stays a function so the test can compare it with `ParallelConfig.reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` without constructing a daemon. Only the key changes; daemon placement and the world group are untouched.

All dense DP ranks now share one key. That is correct because they hold identical weights, and the per-GPU socket plus `_check_gpu_uuid` already bind each engine worker to the daemon on its own GPU.

Same class of bug as #56949 (RL weight transfer), where dense DP ranks also reset `data_parallel_rank` to 0.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix host-buffer h2d sync overwriting received KV
author: lucamotz
body:
## Overview

With `kv_buffer_device="cpu"`, `sync_recved_kv_to_device` overwrites D's received KV with host pages NIXL never filled, for models with several KV cache groups or KV-sharing layers. Each group now copies only its own layers' host buffers; the multi-group case regressed in #53780.

## Claims

- With host buffers, D keeps the received KV for models with several KV cache groups or KV-sharing layers.
- Each layer of a transfer group is still copied once per request, as after #54483; KV-sharing layers are no longer copied.

## Validation

CPU, this PR (`a42440c748`) on main `a70e48deba`:
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -k test_sync_recved_kv_copies_each_group_own_layers`: #54483's parametrized test now checks which layers and block ids each h2d copy gets, with a KV-sharing layer added. All 3 rows fail on main; with this PR they pass. The rest of `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py` and `test_nixl_push_connector.py` has the same pass/fail set as main.
- A local byte-level check runs real `allocate_kv_cache` tensors, `save_kv_to_host`, NIXL replayed between host buffers and `sync_recved_kv_to_device` on toy models at TP 1/1 and 2/2. On main, D's KV differs from P's in all 16 multi-group cases, which mix sliding-window and full-attention layers, and matches in all 4 full-attention-only cases. With this PR it matches in all 20.

GB10, Gemma-4-E2B-it, which has sliding-window and full-attention groups and 20 KV-sharing layers, P TP1 → D TP1, main `8530a778f7` without and with this PR (`a42440c748`, merged): with `kv_buffer_device="cpu"` on both sides, main's outputs differ from the same run with device buffers in all 4 prompts; with this PR all 4 are identical, logprobs bitwise equal.

<details>
<summary>GB10 runs</summary>

| | identical to device buffers | max \|Δlogprob\| per prompt |
|---|---|---|
| main `8530a778f7` | 0/4 | 3.27, 0.81, 3.74, 2.02 |
| this PR `a42440c748` merged with main `8530a778f7` | 4/4 | 0, 0, 0, 0 |

Both runs, P and D: `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --num-gpu-blocks-override 2048`, greedy, 4 code prompts of 1100–1300 tokens; D read 4880 tokens over NIXL. Host-buffer runs add `"kv_buffer_device": "cpu"` on both sides; both logged `use_host_buffer: True`.
</details>

## Details

On D, with `kv_buffer_device="cpu"`:

1. NIXL READ writes into D's per-layer host buffers. Each host buffer is its own region, and since #53780 each group's descriptors cover only its own regions, so a layer's host buffer is filled only at its own group's blocks. Layers that reuse another layer's KV cache have host buffers but no transfer group, so NIXL never fills them.
2. `sync_recved_kv_to_device` copies the host buffers into the device tensors, which layers of different KV cache groups share, as does a KV-sharing layer with its target.
   - Main copies every layer's host buffer at all groups' blocks, so unfilled host pages overwrite the other groups' received blocks. A KV-sharing layer, copied after its target, overwrites the target's received KV, even with one group.
   - This PR copies each group's layers at that group's blocks only.

The byte-level check matches in all 10 multi-group cases that build at #53780's parent and differs in all 10 at #53780.

`save_kv_to_host` still copies every layer for all groups' blocks; NIXL never reads the extra host pages.

#59037, a 60-file draft for hidden-state extraction with packed layouts, contains the same per-group copy; this PR is the standalone fix.

title: [Bugfix][Model] K-EXAONE: restore loading of pre-2.0 configs and apply RoPE to the MTP layer
author: Godmook
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes two K-EXAONE-236B-A23B (K-EXAONE 1.0) problems introduced with #50524 (K-EXAONE 2.0 support, 2026-08-03):

1. Checkpoints whose `config.json` predates that change fail to load.
2. With the current official config, the MTP drafter runs its attention without RoPE, which lowers MTP acceptance by 3–5 pp.

## Claims

- **Legacy configs load again.**
  - `"architectures": ["ExaoneMoEForCausalLM"]` resolves through a registry alias, in the same way as `LLaMAForCausalLM`.
  - When `sliding_windows`, `mtp_layer_types` and `mtp_sliding_windows` are missing, `ExaoneMoeAttention` falls back to the scalar `sliding_window`. The MTP layer then takes the settings of the main layer with the same index, which is what vLLM did before #50524.
- **The MTP layer always applies RoPE.** Main-model full-attention layers stay NoPE.
  - With the current official 1.0 config, MTP acceptance goes from 85.0% to 88.3% on GSM8K and from 67.9% to 73.1% on MT-Bench.
  - K-EXAONE 2.0 and legacy 1.0 configs already ran their MTP layer with RoPE (sliding window), so they are unchanged.
- Main-model layers are unchanged for every config. Output quality is unaffected, since spec decoding is lossless.

## Validation

**Setup.** 16× A100-SXM4-40GB. Model: K-EXAONE-236B-A23B FP8 (compressed-tensors), TP=8. Flags: `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`, temperature 0, no prefix caching. Two config variants of the same weights: the current official HF config, and a legacy copy predating 2026-08-03.

**Metric.** MTP acceptance comes from the `vllm:spec_decode_num_{draft,accepted}_tokens` counters. Prompts: 200 GSM8K test questions and the 80 MT-Bench prompts. Reruns of the same configuration varied by ≤0.2 pp.

**Loading, `main` @ b2863c0de9**

| checkpoint config | result |
|---|---|
| legacy | `ValidationError: Model architectures ['ExaoneMoEForCausalLM'] are not supported for now` |
| legacy + `--hf-overrides '{"architectures":["ExaoneMoeForCausalLM"]}'` | `AttributeError: 'ExaoneMoeConfig' object has no attribute 'sliding_windows'` |

**MTP acceptance and output throughput** (concurrency 16)

| checkpoint config | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| official, GSM8K | 85.01% (1062 tok/s) | **88.28%** (1081 tok/s) |
| official, MT-Bench | 67.86% (940 tok/s) | **73.07%** (970 tok/s) |
| legacy, GSM8K | fails to load | 88.84% |
| legacy, MT-Bench | fails to load | 74.69% |

GSM8K answer accuracy stays within noise for every run.

**Static check.** I evaluated the old and new logic on every main layer and on the MTP layer, for three configs: legacy 1.0, current 1.0, and K-EXAONE-2.0-750B-A37B.
- Window and RoPE choices for all main layers are identical in every config.
- The only change for configs that load today is the current 1.0 MTP layer, which goes from full + NoPE to full + RoPE.
- K-EXAONE 2.0 is unchanged.

**Tests** (`main` + this PR, A100, TP 8)

```text
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/test_initialization.py -k "ExaoneMoE or ExaoneMoe or coverage"
PASSED test_registry_imports[ExaoneMoEForCausalLM]                # new
PASSED test_can_initialize_large_subset[ExaoneMoEForCausalLM]     # new
PASSED test_registry_imports[ExaoneMoeForCausalLM]
PASSED test_registry_imports[ExaoneMoeMTP]
PASSED test_hf_registry_coverage
PASSED test_can_initialize_large_subset[ExaoneMoeForCausalLM]
PASSED test_can_initialize_large_subset[ExaoneMoeMTP]
```

- **Alias coverage.** Removing the alias makes `test_can_initialize_large_subset[ExaoneMoEForCausalLM]` fail with `Model architectures ['ExaoneMoEForCausalLM'] are not supported`.
- **Not covered in CI.** The legacy-field fallback is validated by the end-to-end runs above only. The public repo now serves the new config, so CI cannot load a legacy one.
- **EXAONE 4.5.** `Exaone4_5_ForConditionalGeneration` and `Exaone4_5_MTP` initialization tests also pass. Their MTP layer uses `Exaone4DecoderLayer`, so this PR does not affect them.
- **Lint.** `pre-commit` passes, including mypy-3.12 at the manual stage.

## Details

**Root cause: loading.** #50524 renamed the registry key `ExaoneMoEForCausalLM` to `ExaoneMoeForCausalLM` without keeping an alias. It also replaced `Exaone4Attention`, which reads the scalar `sliding_window`, with code that reads `sliding_windows`, `mtp_layer_types` and `mtp_sliding_windows` directly.

`transformers`' `ExaoneMoeConfig` does not define these fields. The official HF repo added them on the same day ([61e6d57](https://huggingface.co/LGAI-EXAONE/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B/commit/61e6d578eb102b578e5704e2916ac841df9eca0a)), but existing copies kept the old config. Public examples still on it include:
- `furiosa-ai/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B-NVFP4A16`
- `Hyun9junn/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B-W4A16-G128`
- `haanjack/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B-MXFP4`
- `tazza26/K-EXAONE-236B-SFT-full`

**Root cause: MTP RoPE.** `ExaoneMoeAttention` applied RoPE only to sliding layers. That matches the main model, whose global layers are NoPE in both HF and vLLM. vLLM applied the same rule to the MTP layer, which `transformers` does not implement at all.

- Before #50524, the 1.0 MTP layer inherited layer 0's settings (sliding 128), so it ran with RoPE.
- After #50524 it reads `mtp_layer_types: ["full_attention"]` from the new config, and so loses RoPE.

Measured on v0.30.0, with only the MTP layer's attention changed:

| MTP layer attention | GSM8K | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|
| full, NoPE (current) | 85.05% | 68.32% |
| full, RoPE (this PR) | 88.24% | 73.61% |
| sliding 128, RoPE (pre-#50524) | 88.96% | 74.63% |

RoPE accounts for most of the gap, so the MTP layer was trained with RoPE. This PR keeps the configured attention type and only fixes the positional encoding.

**Duplicate check.** No open issue or PR covers this.
- #50865 (closed) only renamed the test registry key after the HF change.
- #51558 (K-EXAONE-2.0 DSpark) edits `exaone_moe.py` class bases and Eagle hooks, not the attention init.

title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Fence decode indexer shared-memory stage reuse
author: vovani
body:
## Overview

Add the missing generic-to-async proxy fences before the decode indexer
releases its Q and K shared-memory stages for TMA reuse.

## Claims

- Prevents wrong indexer scores under concurrent GPU writes.
- Extends the existing indexer correctness test; no new test harness or file.

## Validation

B200, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13, CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1:

- The six decode-indexer pytest cases pass.
- In five fresh processes, the concurrent-write test failed without the fences
  and passed with them. Each fixed run checks 20 stressed launches.
- Quiet baseline and fixed outputs are bitwise identical for the stress input.
- Three alternating timing runs, 1,000 launches each: baseline means
  14.698 / 14.567 / 14.550 us; fixed 14.593 / 14.551 / 14.516 us.
  No measurable slowdown at this shape. These are kernel timings, not an
  end-to-end serving measurement.

Test selector in a matching vLLM development environment:

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py \
        -k decode_index_score_cutedsl_correctness -v

## Details

The consumer reads through ldmatrix (generic proxy), while the producer
refills through TMA (async proxy). Releasing the empty-stage barrier does not
by itself establish the needed cross-proxy ordering. Fence before both
releases, including the Q tile that aliases K stage zero.

title: [Bugfix] Index Mamba align state copies by request slot in MRV2
author: ZJY0516
body:
## Overview

Fix Mamba "align" state copies reading another request's block ids under MRV2 + PP + MTP, which poisons recurrent state (all-NaN logits, constant-token output, acceptance collapse). Consolidates #55506 and #57807 into a smaller change; both authors are co-authors. Refs #54173.

## Claims

- The precopy/postprocess state-copy kernels index the persistent per-request-slot block tables by `req_idx`, so a postprocess that runs steps after its batch (non-last PP rank) no longer reads tables re-gathered for a later batch.
- `compute_aligned_state_indices` is unchanged: it still reads the gathered batch-order tables, so padded rows and CUDA graph capture behave as on main.
- The align context is built once in `initialize_kv_cache` instead of lazily from whichever caller runs first, which removes the capture-time / profiling binding issues raised on #55506 and #57807.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_precopy_mamba_align.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py`: 146 passed (GB200).
- With the kernels reverted to batch-row indexing, the new/updated kernel tests fail (26 failures), so they cover the bug.
- E2E on GB200, Qwen3.6-27B, MRV2, MTP 4, `--async-scheduling --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align` (reproduction from @tomasruizt on #55506). main = upstream 31e2443.

| | GSM8K 5-shot (mqa, chat, no think) | Mean acceptance length (completions GSM8K / bench) | Output tok/s (random 2k/1k, c=8) | Mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main, PP=2 | did not finish: 8 requests stuck at AL 1.00 (no draft accepted) for 15 min at 772/1319, cancelled | 2.95 / 3.56 | 1177 | 5.50 ms |
| this PR, PP=2 | 0.9727 strict / 0.9719 flexible | 4.13 / 4.42 | 1506 | 4.76 ms |
| this PR, PP=1 (reference) | 0.9727 strict / 0.9719 flexible | 4.13 / 4.35 | 1589 | 4.46 ms |

  The stuck requests on main are the constant-token loop from poisoned recurrent state; with a 4096 max-token cap, main PP=2 averaged 235 output tokens per GSM8K question vs 82 for this PR at PP=2 and PP=1. The fix does not change kernel work; the throughput gain comes from the recovered acceptance length.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B --language-model-only \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --async-scheduling --enable-prefix-caching \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 4}'
# PP=1 reference: drop --pipeline-parallel-size 2

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.75 \
  --random-prefix-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 42 \
  --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 \
  --max-concurrency 64   # acceptance length column; accuracy from mqa gsm8k (5-shot, chat, no thinking)
```

Acceptance length is `1 + spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens / spec_decode_num_drafts` from `/metrics`.
</details>

## Details

Root cause: `MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext` captures block-table pointers once. MRV2 bound it to `input_block_tables`, a single buffer re-gathered in batch order every step, and the copy kernels indexed it by batch row. On a non-last PP rank the postprocess for step N runs after step N+k has re-gathered that buffer, so batch rows point at other requests' blocks. With the unified hybrid cache layout those copies land in live state.

Why not just #55506 or #57807: both keep lazy binding and add machinery around it (temporary bindings / `bind` flag, or two lazily bound contexts plus profiling teardown), and #55506 remaps the aligned-index kernel through `idx_mapping`, which changes padded-row behavior. Binding both table sets eagerly avoids all of that. The source tables are safe to read late because a request is not rescheduled (so its row is not rewritten or its slot reused) until its in-flight step's output is processed.

MRV1 is unaffected: it launches both kernels without `idx_mapping`, where `req_idx == batch_idx`, and passes a single table set, which stays the default for the aligned-index tables.

Credit: root cause first identified by @zebgop-ops; fix direction and kernel tests from @Karl0007 (#55506); separate metadata/copy tables and the profiling lifetime issue from @yongqinwang-cmd (#57807).

title: [Bugfix] Fall back to auto for unquantized MoE layers when --moe-backend is marlin
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #56832. With `--moe-backend marlin`, an unquantized MoE layer (here, the BF16 MTP draft of an NVFP4 model) now uses the auto-selected unquantized backend instead of raising `ValueError`. `humming` already works this way. Related: #56964 discusses the same fix.

## Claims

- `vllm serve RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 --moe-backend marlin --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` now starts and serves requests with MTP speculative decoding. Before this change, loading the draft model failed with `ValueError: moe_backend='marlin' is not supported for unquantized MoE`.
- Quantized MoE layers still use Marlin. Only unquantized MoE layers change: they now use the auto-selected backend instead of raising.
- A new unit test checks that `marlin` and `humming` give the same unquantized backend as `auto`.

## Validation

Hardware: 2× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), driver 595.58.03, CUDA 13.2. Base commit `92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` (`0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`).

Reproducer (the command from the issue):

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder
```

To check that the draft model really runs, send one request after startup and read the spec-decode counters:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17 * 23? Answer briefly."}],"max_tokens":400,"temperature":0}'
curl -s http://localhost:8000/metrics | grep -E "^vllm:spec_decode_num_(drafts|draft_tokens|accepted_tokens)_total"
```

| Tree | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| base | 2 (one in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a…` image, one in an editable install) | 2 of 2 failed. Both TP workers raised `ValueError` while building the MTP draft's MoE layer, about 2.5 minutes after start. No requests served. | | base + this PR | 2 (editable install) | 2 of 2 started and served the request. The answers were correct (391, and 408 in the second run, which asked for 12 × 34). Draft acceptance was 73.3% (33/45 tokens) and 76.9% (30/39 tokens). No `Traceback` in either log. |

Before:

```
ValueError: moe_backend='marlin' is not supported for unquantized MoE. Expected one of ['triton', 'batched_triton', 'flashinfer_trtllm', 'flashinfer_cutlass', 'aiter'].
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

After (log excerpt):

```
[nvfp4.py:268] Using 'MARLIN' NvFp4 MoE backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL', 'FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'VLLM_CUTLASS', 'MARLIN', 'HUMMING', 'EMULATION'].
[unquantized.py:365] Using FlashInfer CUTLASS Unquantized MoE backend out of potential backends: ['FlashInfer TRTLLM', 'FlashInfer CUTLASS', 'TRITON', 'BATCHED_TRITON'].
INFO:     Application startup complete.
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 3.20, ... Accepted: 33 tokens, Drafted: 45 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.800, 0.800, 0.600, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 73.3%
```

Unit test (run with `--noconftest` because `tblib`, which the top-level conftest imports, was not installed in the test environment):

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py -q -p no:cacheprovider --noconftest
27 passed, 3 skipped
```

With the old condition put back, the new `marlin` case fails with the error from the issue and the `humming` case passes. The file already runs in CI through `pytest -v -s kernels/moe` (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`). The end-to-end check above was run by hand, outside CI. `pre-commit` passes on both changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** `--moe-backend` is one global value (`KernelConfig.moe_backend`). It reaches every MoE layer, quantized or not. The MTP draft inherits it unless `speculative_config.moe_backend` is set. This checkpoint has NVFP4 main experts, but it excludes `mtp.*` from quantization and stores those experts in BF16. So `mtp.layers.48.mlp.experts` correctly gets `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, with `moe_backend='marlin'`. A debug run showed that the draft keeps `ModelOptNvFp4Config` and gets no quant method only because its prefix matches `mtp.*`, so the draft is not losing its quant config by mistake. Marlin has no BF16 MoE kernel: `MarlinExperts._supports_quant_scheme` lists only quantized schemes. `select_unquantized_moe_backend` already lets `humming`, another quantization-only backend, fall through to `auto` (#41652), but `marlin` was not in that list. So it reached `map_unquantized_backend`, which has no entry for it and raises.

**Fix.** Add `"marlin"` to the fall-through list in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/unquantized.py`, and update the comment. Quantized layers go through other oracles, so they keep Marlin. The NVFP4 experts above still log `Using 'MARLIN'`.

**Why the draft override is not enough.** Users can work around the draft case with `"moe_backend": "auto"` in `--speculative-config`, but that override only reaches the draft. In a quantized checkpoint, MoE layers of the main model that are left unquantized (`modules_to_not_convert` / `ignore` / `exclude_modules`) go through the same function with the same global value. No flag reaches them. This change covers them too, but that case was not run end to end here.

**Behavior change.** `--moe-backend marlin` on a model whose MoE layers are all unquantized used to fail at load with a clear error. Now it loads on the auto-selected backend. Only the `Using ... Unquantized MoE backend` info line shows that Marlin was not used. This matches `humming`. No existing test asserts the old error: the tests that set `marlin` all use quantized models, which go through a different oracle.

**Limitations.** Other quantization-only backends still raise the same error for unquantized layers, for example `flashinfer_cutedsl`, `flashinfer_b12x`, `b12x`, `cutlass` and `deep_gemm`. This PR leaves them alone to keep the fix small. A general rule ("no unquantized kernel → auto") could replace the list if maintainers prefer. For the same reason, the comment in `vllm/config/speculative.py` about the draft inheriting the target's `--moe-backend` is still true for those backends, so it is unchanged.

---

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix fused Gumbel-max wrapping-window bias
author: R3hankhan123

Fixes biased V1 CPU sampling from the fused Gumbel table in #53913. `fused_gumbel_argmax` now draws independent 53-bit Gumbel noise per `(seed, token)` via SplitMix64, which is the #59786 wrapping-window bug.

```
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_output_in_range[65-128256] PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_output_in_range[128-32000] PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_output_in_range[128-49152] PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_output_in_range[128-128256] PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_output_in_range[256-32000] PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_output_in_range[256-49152] PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_output_in_range[256-128256] PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_samples_only_from_finite_logits PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_single_unmasked_token PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_tokens_beyond_gumbel_max_cannot_win PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_serial_batch1_matches_batched PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_noncontiguous_matches_contiguous PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_empty_batch PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_masked_support_matches_softmax PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestFusedGumbelArgmax::test_zipf_tail_matches_softmax PASSED
../../tmp/test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::TestMemory::test_fused_no_intermediate_allocs PASSED

```

## Details
Root cause. g_gumbel_table[(seed + i) & (2^20 - 1)] makes every row one sliding window of a single 1M-entry table. Enumerating windows on Zipf(1.1), V=151936 (from #59786): TV≈0.07 vs softmax, 79078 / 151936 tokens never win, P(top-1) 0.141 vs 0.132. The old chi-squared test used small_vocab=100, so it missed this. GPU / MRV2 Triton Gumbel was already unbiased; V1 CPU is the default on non-x86 (no triton-cpu wheel).

Fix. Drop the table. Each row keys SplitMix64(seed); token i gets 53-bit u and score logit - log(-log u). Consecutive seeds no longer share a shifted window.

Perf tradeoff. Top-k/top-p leave most logits -inf. x + 37.5 <= best_score skips those, so serving batches got faster than the old full-vocab SIMD add. Unfiltered random must visit the live vocab with RNG/exp/log, so fused latency rose (e.g. batch=1 random 0.44 ms → 6.17 ms). That path is uncommon next to top-k/top-p.

Other. OpenMP over rows, no fork at batch=1. greedy_argmax unchanged. RISCV still use forward_native.
