title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Reject PEFT adapter features vLLM does not implement
author: surajsharan
body:
## Overview

`PEFTHelper` drops `adapter_config.json` keys it doesn't know, so adapters using PEFT features vLLM doesn't implement loaded without an error and were served with wrong outputs. This rejects them with a clear error, the same way DoRA is rejected, and fixes a regression from #53555 that let `lora_A` / `lora_B` `.bias` tensors replace the LoRA weights.

Fixes #60223

## Claims

- Adapters with `lora_bias`, an `init_lora_weights` that modifies the base model when PEFT loads the adapter (`pissa`, `pissa_niter_*`, `olora`, `corda`, `loftq`) or any other value not on the allowlist, `alora_invocation_tokens`, `layer_replication`, `use_bdlora` or `use_qalora` are rejected in `validate_legal` with a message naming the feature. Before, they loaded and gave outputs that differ from PEFT.
- `parse_fine_tuned_lora_name` accepts `.bias` only for the `score` / `classifier` heads again, not for `lora_A` / `lora_B`. This restores the behavior before #53555 (v0.30.0 rejects these adapters; v0.31.0 loads them and silently drops the bias or swaps it with the weight).
- No change for other adapters: `init_lora_weights` = `true` / `false` / `"gaussian"` / `"eva"` / `"orthogonal"` / `"mica"` / `"lora_ga"` and PEFT's converted PiSSA / OLoRA / CorDA adapters (`init_lora_weights: true`) load as before.
- Not changed: `target_parameters`, `trainable_token_indices` and DoRA, which open PRs #52198, #55796 and #47395 are adding support for. If BD-LoRA support (#28136) lands first, its rejection here can be dropped.

## Validation

Every feature saved with PEFT 0.21.2 on a tiny random Llama (bf16, RTX 3080), loaded with `llm.llm_engine.add_lora` in one engine, then the accepted ones served. Mean absolute difference of per-token prompt logprobs between vLLM and PEFT:

| adapter | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| plain | 0.0018 | 0.0018 |
| `use_rslora` | 0.0021 | 0.0022 |
| `init_lora_weights` = `gaussian` / `orthogonal` / `mica` | 0.0021 | 0.0021 |
| `lora_bias=True` | loads (0.33 in the issue repro) | rejected |
| `init_lora_weights="pissa"` | loads (0.10) | rejected |
| `init_lora_weights="olora"` | loads | rejected |
| `alora_invocation_tokens` | loads | rejected |
| `layer_replication` | loads (0.17) | rejected |
| `use_bdlora` | loads (0.44) | rejected |

The rejected adapters fail `add_lora` with the message from `validate_legal` and the engine keeps serving the other adapters afterwards. The same holds for `POST /v1/load_lora_adapter` (new case in `tests/entrypoints/serve/lora/test_lora_adapters.py`). As with DoRA today, an unsupported adapter passed directly in a `LLM.generate` request still ends in `EngineDeadError`.

Real adapters: of the 628 most-downloaded Hugging Face PEFT repos with an `adapter_config.json`, this rejects 2 more than main (both PiSSA). A targeted search found about 100 more PiSSA / OLoRA / aLoRA adapters. For one of them, `AkameV6p5/qwen2.5-3b-agent-pissa-sft` on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B`, vLLM main differs from PEFT by 3.44 (mean, PEFT run to run: 1.55 because of its randomized SVD) and matches PEFT with `init_lora_weights` forced to `true` (0.06), i.e. it is served as a plain LoRA on the unmodified base.

Tests (on main e11962fc1c):

```text
pytest tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py tests/lora/test_utils.py
34 passed (the 12 new cases fail on main)

pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/lora/test_lora_adapters.py
13 passed

pytest tests/lora/{test_lora_utils,test_lora_weights,test_lora_manager,test_lora_checkpoints,
       test_lora_huggingface,test_sequence_classification,test_moe_lora_ep_load,test_resolver,
       test_worker,test_add_lora,test_lora_functions,test_transformers_model,test_qwen3_with_multi_loras,
       test_qwen3_unembed}.py
all passed; test_default_mm_loras.py (needs vllm[audio]) and test_llama_tp.py (gated model) fail the same way on main in this environment
```

The new tests are CPU-only and extend the existing suites. `test_sequence_classification.py` covers the `score.bias` path that #53555 added.

## Details

- The fields are added to `PEFTHelper` with PEFT's defaults only so that `from_dict` keeps them for validation.
- `init_lora_weights` is checked against an allowlist of the values that load in PEFT as a plain LoRA, so a future PEFT init is rejected rather than silently accepted. I checked this by loading one saved adapter in PEFT 0.21.2 with each value: `gaussian`, `eva`, `orthogonal`, `mica` and `lora_ga` give the same logits as `true` (`lora_ga` changes the base weights only during training, when its gradients are attached); `pissa` and `olora` change them (max logit diff 0.15 and 0.23); `corda` fails to load in PEFT without `preprocess_corda`; `loftq` replaces the base weight with the quantized one (`loftq_init` in `peft/tuners/lora/layer.py`). The error points to PEFT's `path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` and to setting `init_lora_weights` to `true` when the served base already holds the modified weights.
- A shape check in `set_lora` would also catch BD-LoRA / QALoRA style layouts, but it runs at activation time, so it is left for a follow-up next to the load-time validation in #59924.

title: [Bugfix] Allow pipeline parallelism for Qwen4Exp PLE models and their MTP drafter
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #54709. Qwen4Exp models with n-gram PLE layers (here `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`) refused every `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`, and their MTP drafter failed on the last PP rank. Since #61016, Model Runner V2 passes `input_ids` to every PP stage for models with `requires_raw_input_tokens` (Qwen4Exp sets it), so the PP refusal is obsolete. This PR removes it and fixes the two remaining failures on that path: KV cache allocation on PP ranks and the MTP drafter.

## Claims

- PP>1 works for Qwen4Exp PLE models, with PLE layers on any PP rank.
- KV cache allocation no longer fails on a PP rank that owns none of the layers of a uniform-type cache group.
- The MTP drafter works with PP>1. This is the second bug in the issue. With PP>1 it also needs #62129 (see Details).

## Validation

Hardware and software: 4× NVIDIA H200, branch head `8d2dd01d18` on top of `b515648641`, Model Runner V2, CUDA graphs on. Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` (48 layers, `ple_layer_ids = [2]`, so decoder layer 1 has PLE).

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 8192
```

Before (`main`): exits at config validation, before weights load:

```
NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp N-gram PLE embedding requires pipeline_parallel_size=1 because non-first pipeline ranks do not receive the raw input_ids it needs. Please run with PP=1.
```

After:

| Config (PP=4) | Result |
|---|---|
| Default partition (PLE layer on rank 0) | `Application startup complete.`, coherent greedy output. Reference for the rows below. |
| `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=1,15,16,16` (PLE layer on rank 1) | Serves. Greedy output matches the reference until the first near-tie: 28/32, 4/32 and 32/32 identical tokens on 3 prompts. Max \|Δ logprob\| before divergence 0.11. Needs a local core workaround, see Details. |
| Default partition + `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'` | Serves, also with 4 concurrent requests. `Avg Draft acceptance rate: 89.6%`, mean acceptance length 1.90. Greedy output matches the reference: 28/32, 32/32, 32/32. Run with #62129 applied locally. |

The divergences are near-ties. Where the outputs split, the chosen tokens are ` Lisbon` (−0.77) vs `\n\n` (−0.80), and ` <=` (−1.02) vs ` ==` (−1.09).

Unit tests, on H200:

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

All pass. `test_kv_cache_config_skips_uniform_group_owned_by_other_pp_stage` fails without the `kv_cache_planning.py` change. `pre-commit` passes on all changed files.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation on 4× A100 (before the rebase onto #61016)</summary>

An earlier revision kept a gate that required all PLE layers on rank 0. On 4× A100 80GB PCIe with the default partition and `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` (that host's NCCL P2P hangs even for a plain `torch.distributed` send/recv), it served coherent output, and MTP reached `Avg Draft acceptance rate: 88.9%`. Without the `mtp.py` change, the MTP run failed on the last PP rank with `AssertionError` at `assert intermediate_tensors is not None`.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** PLE needs the raw `input_ids`. Until #61016, the V2 model runner set them to `None` on every PP rank except the first, so `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGenerationConfig.verify_and_update_config` and `Qwen4ExpModelState.__init__` (nvidia and amd) refused any PP>1 when PLE was present. #61016 keeps `input_ids` on later stages for `requires_raw_input_tokens` models but left those refusals in place.

Changes:

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py` and `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/{nvidia,amd}/model_state.py`: remove the PP refusals. The state they guarded (`ngram_context`, query start locations) is built from `req_states`, which every PP rank keeps, and the model forward passes `input_ids` to PLE layers on any rank. If PLE inputs are ever missing, the decoder layer still raises `PLE inputs were not prepared`.
2. `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py` (core): on PP ranks without PLE, `allocate_kv_cache` raised `StopIteration`. `_project_kv_cache_groups_to_worker` keeps the global `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` for a group whose layers are all on another rank, with empty `layer_names`, so that the worker still has a block size for that group. But `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` took the layer list from the spec, so those ranks got a cache tensor for `layers.1.ple`, which only one rank has. It now loops over `group.layer_names` with `_get_per_layer_spec`, as `_get_kv_cache_bytes_per_block` and `validate_kv_cache_layout` already do. For every non-empty group, `layer_names` and the spec's dict hold the same layers in the same order, so the layout does not change. Only the empty-group case changes.
3. `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/{nvidia,amd}/mtp.py`: `Qwen4ExpMultiTokenPredictor.forward` branched on `get_pp_group().is_first_rank`. The V2 speculator builds the whole drafter on the last PP rank and calls it with `hidden_states` and no `intermediate_tensors`, so with PP>1 it took the wrong branch. It now branches on `intermediate_tensors is None`, as `qwen3_5_mtp.py` already does.

Tests: `test_kv_cache_config_skips_uniform_group_owned_by_other_pp_stage` is new. The old `test_qwen4_exp_rejects_pipeline_parallel_only_with_ple` asserted the refusal and is removed. The mocked MTP test from an earlier revision is removed per review. The PP path itself is not covered in CI: it needs ≥2 GPUs and this checkpoint.

**Needs attention:**

- MTP with PP>1 hangs in kernel warmup on current `main`, independent of this PR. `warmup_kernels` runs a second greedy pass only when `rejection_sampler is not None`, which is true only on the last PP rank, so that rank waits forever for activations. #62129 fixes it, and the MTP row above was run with that change applied.
- PLE on a later rank for this checkpoint means `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=1,...`, which leaves rank 0 with only a linear-attention layer. Startup then fails in `resolve_kv_cache_layout` with `Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts` (rank 0 supports all layouts, the other ranks `BLNHC`/`BLHNC`). That check is unrelated to PLE and is not changed here. For the PLE-on-rank-1 row, it was relaxed locally to the intersection of the reported layouts.
- `kv_cache_planning.py` is core code. The change only affects the case described in item 2.

---

title: [Bugfix] Warn only on per-request do_normalize/do_rescale overrides
author: lesj0610
body:
## Overview

With `mm_device_do_normalize` on, the default for the Qwen2/2.5/3-VL family, every process that builds the HF processor warns that it is ignoring per-request `do_normalize` and `do_rescale`, with no request involved. This warns only when a request actually asks for normalization.

## Claims

- No warning at startup: building dummy image inputs makes 0 `warning_once` calls instead of 10.
- A request that sets `do_normalize` or `do_rescale` still gets the warning; before, the startup calls had already spent the `warning_once`, so it never appeared.
- The merged kwargs are unchanged, so outputs are not affected.

## Validation

On main (`6ad2e06c4a`) with and without this commit, on CPU with the Qwen3-VL processor: count `warning_once` calls while building dummy image inputs, then merge request kwargs.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| warnings while building dummy image inputs | 10 | 0 |
| request `do_normalize=False` | 1 | 0 |
| request `do_normalize=True, do_rescale=True` | 2 | 2 |
| merged kwargs | `do_normalize=False, do_rescale=False` | same |

```text
pytest -q tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py
83 passed
```

## Details

`InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor` merges the kwargs through `MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs`, which forces both keys to `False`, and `cached_processor_from_config` then merges the result again. The second merge sees the forced `False` values as request kwargs and warns. The warning came with #56798. Warning only on a truthy request value fixes that without touching either merge: a request that passes `False` is not overridden, so there is nothing to report.

No open PR addresses this. The open PRs that mention `mm_device_do_normalize` (#58972, #57924) extend it to other models and do not touch this warning.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Restore DP wave delivery after XPUB reconnects
author: reidliu41
body:
## Overview

Fix the Rust in-process coordinator so an EngineCore that reconnects its
XPUB/XSUB control connection can receive DP wave notifications again.

Previously, a reconnected engine could permanently miss `START_DP_WAVE`.
Other ranks could then wait for it in distributed communication, causing
the DP group to hang.



## Claims

- Continuously processes XPUB subscription notifications after the startup handshake.
- Restores the XPUB subscription table when an EngineCore reconnects.
- Replays the current DP wave when a subscribe-all notification arrives during an active wave.
- Avoids replaying a stale wave when the coordinator is paused.
- Adds regression coverage for a subscriber joining during an active wave.




## Validation

```
cargo nextest run -p vllm-engine-core-client
cargo clippy -p vllm-engine-core-client \
  --all-targets \
  --all-features \
  --locked \
  -- -D warnings
```

Manual validation on a two-GPU DP=2 MoE setup confirmed that requests
continued to complete after an engine connection was interrupted and
restored. Repeated reconnects returned HTTP 200 without stalling the DP
group or replaying completed work.



## Details

The `zeromq` XPUB implementation applies subscription changes while
`recv()` processes subscription messages. The in-process coordinator
previously called `recv()` only during the startup gate. A reconnecting
XSUB resent its subscribe-all command, but that command remained
unprocessed and the XPUB subscription table stayed empty for the new
connection.

The coordinator event loop now receives XPUB subscription notifications.
When it receives the EngineCore subscribe-all message during an active
wave, it broadcasts the current `START_DP_WAVE` again. Engines already
running that wave ignore the duplicate notification, while the
reconnected engine receives the wave it missed.

When the coordinator is paused, receiving the subscription only restores
the subscription table. The next normal wave broadcast then reaches the
reconnected engine without replaying completed work.

Peer-specific network and codec errors are logged without terminating the
coordinator. Other XPUB errors retain the existing fail-closed behavior.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep SW draft block a divisor of the primary block
author: Anchen798
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Related to #60174. **The correctness fix for #60174 is #55601**, not this PR. That bug is the mamba state column being seeded with the lowered `cache_config.block_size`. I briefly added the same one-line fix here (a24c836) without noticing #55601, and have reverted it (thanks @twu3202).

What this PR does: since #53007, a sliding-window layer whose largest fitting kernel block does not divide the primary block gets a padded page instead of an integer-scaled one. With a GDN hybrid target (1648-token block) and a SW DFlash2 drafter on a backend limited to `[16, 32, 64]` (FlashInfer on sm_120), the SW group runs on 64-token blocks. This:

- raises the scheduler block (LCM of all group blocks) from 1648 to 6592, the kind of LCM inflation #53007 set out to avoid;
- lowers `cache_config.block_size` to 64, which is what exposes the seeding bug in #55601;
- disables fine-grained prefix-cache hits (`Disabling fine-grained prefix-cache hits ... SlidingWindowManager`).

This PR keeps the SW block a divisor of the primary block, so `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` scales it as on v0.29.0. Configs where the chosen block already divides the primary block (the #53007 target case) are unchanged.

> **History.** Earlier versions of this PR described the padded SW page as the cause of #60174, then added the seeding fix. Both are superseded: the cause is the seeding bug, and its fix lives in #55601. Thanks to @sinmkd, @nej1gotnochill and @twu3202 for the reviews that got there.

## Validation

Single RTX PRO 5000 (sm_120), TP=1, vLLM 0.31.0 wheel with patches applied; Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 + `Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (k=7), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, prefix caching on; fresh engine per run. 5-request replay with growing prefix (33K → 69K tokens):

| build | SW block / LCM | requests 3–5 | prefix-cache hit rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.31.0 | 64 / 6592 | degenerate (all-NaN logits) | – |
| + seeding fix (#55601 equivalent) | 64 / 6592 | coherent | 43.8% |
| + seeding fix + this PR | 1648 / 1648 | coherent | 71.2% |

Independent measurements:
- @stecasta, same-node A/B on DGX Spark (GB10), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 + DFlash2 (k=8), only this change: KV groups go from 1648x14 + 64 (scheduler block 6592, fine-grained hits disabled) to all 1648; a 168-turn agentic replay goes from 26.1 to 20.0 min, prefix-cache hits 56.3% → 77.4%, decode tok/s unchanged.
- @twu3202 on sm_89 (SW-only arm: `kv lcm block sizes 1616`, 3 prefix hits vs 1 without it).

On its own, this PR also stops the #60174 corruption in my setup, but only because `min(group block sizes)` becomes the mamba block again. That masks the seeding bug and does not fix it.

Tests:
- `test_largest_kernel_block_within_divisor_of`: the new `divisor_of` option, including the fallback when no supported block divides the primary block.
- `test_sliding_window_spec_unifies_without_padding`: runs `Attention.get_kv_cache_spec` for a SW layer on a `[16, 32, 64]` backend, then `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size`. It asserts the SW page is scaled, not padded. With the fix disabled, the 1648 case fails and the 1536 case (unchanged path) passes.

These were run as plain assertions on the patched 0.31.0 install (no pytest there). CI covers `tests/v1/attention`. Lint: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `typos` on the changed files.

## Details

`_largest_kernel_block_within` gets a `divisor_of` option. With it, the helper returns the largest fitting block that divides `divisor_of`, and falls back to the previous choice if none does. The SW branch passes the primary block when there is no `shared_page`. Without `divisor_of` the helper behaves exactly as before, so the existing `test_largest_kernel_block_within` cases are unchanged.

**Not a duplicate:** #55601 changes `mamba_hybrid.py`; this PR changes the SW kernel-block selection in `Attention.get_kv_cache_spec`. None of #55818, #59683, #58207, #54163 or #56552 touches that selection. I'm fine with this being reviewed after #55601, or closed if reviewers consider the padded layout acceptable.

title: [Bugfix] Check batch-invariance support for every attention backend
author: yifanFengg
body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the attention selector refuses backends that do not declare `supports_batch_invariance()` ("VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for ..."). Models that select their own attention backend never go through the selector, so they start anyway and silently return batch-dependent output. This PR applies the same check to every attention layer when the attention groups are built.

## Claims

- `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` starts in batch-invariant mode on `main` and the determinism tests report violations (for example 32 of 32 prompts). With this PR the engine refuses to start with the existing error message.
- Models on the standard backends are unaffected: the determinism tests still pass for `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8` (GB300), `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (A10). Every model on the tested list in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` uses a standard backend.
- New unit test for the check.

## Validation

GB300 runs: 4x NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), `main` at `182247257f` versus that commit plus this PR's source change. A10 runs: 2x NVIDIA A10 (SM 8.6), `main` at `d09ff77637` plus this PR's source change. One pytest process per test. The blocks are copied from the logs without editing.

**1. `main`: MiniMax-M3 runs in batch-invariant mode and is not batch invariant** (tensor-parallel 4)

```text
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN]"
E               Failed: Nondeterministic outputs detected: 5 failed out of 5 trials (max_batch_size=128).
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 532.70s (0:08:52) ==================

VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN[16-16-FLASH_ATTN]"
E           Failed: Batch invariance violated in 32/32 prompts. See output above for details.
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 116.67s (0:01:56) ==================
```

**2. This PR: the engine refuses to start for MiniMax-M3 in batch-invariant mode**

```text
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 VLLM_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9 python -m pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[FLASH_ATTN]"
(Worker_TP2 pid=2792149) ERROR 10-06 05:23:45 [multiproc_executor.py:1058] RuntimeError: VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE_INDEXER.
================== 1 failed, 32 warnings in 73.05s (0:01:13) ===================
```

**3. This PR: models on the standard backends still pass**

```text
# GB300, tensor-parallel 2: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8 VLLM_TP_SIZE=2 VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=2 VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[FLASH_ATTN] PASSED
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 131.31s (0:02:11) ==================
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN] PASSED
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 197.04s (0:03:17) ==================
# A10: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN] PASSED
================== 1 passed, 17 warnings in 113.06s (0:01:53) ==================
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[TRITON_ATTN] PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 53.84s ========================
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[FLEX_ATTENTION] PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 27.90s ========================
# A10, tensor-parallel 2: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_TEST_MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat
tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_simple_generation[TRITON_MLA] PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 17 warnings in 29.12s ========================
```

**4. New unit test** (without and with the source change)

```text
python -m pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_init_attn_backend_checks_custom_backend_batch_invariance
# main + only the new test
E       Failed: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_init_attn_backend_checks_custom_backend_batch_invariance[False]
=================== 1 failed, 1 passed, 14 warnings in 1.08s ===================
# this PR
======================== 2 passed, 14 warnings in 1.08s ========================
```

`lm_eval` and `vllm bench serve` comparisons are not included because the change is a start-up check only: no kernel or request path is touched, and for the affected model the "after" state is that the engine does not start.

## Details

**Root cause.** `supports_batch_invariance()` is enforced in `vllm/v1/attention/selector.py`. Attention layers that set their backend themselves (the model packages under `vllm/models/`, for example MiniMax-M3's sparse attention and indexer) are not created through the selector, and none of those backends declares support, so batch-invariant mode was accepted for them without any guarantee. I found this by running the determinism suite on MiniMax-M3: it fails on `main`, and still fails with #59985 applied, so it is not the router issue fixed there.

**Change.** `init_attn_backend` already visits the backend of every attention layer; it now raises the selector's error for a backend that does not declare support when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set. Backends that do support it only need to override `supports_batch_invariance()`.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- Models with self-selected backends (MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3 and similar) now fail fast in batch-invariant mode instead of starting. None of them is on the tested list, and for the one I could test the mode did not hold.
- Only the Model Runner V2 path is changed; the equivalent loop in the V1 runner is left as is, given its deprecation.
- This does not make MiniMax-M3 batch invariant; it makes the lack of support explicit.

title: [Bugfix] Reland #53020: tie lm_head.weight for Nemotron Parse when checkpoint omits it
author: aniskumar-nv
body:
## Purpose

Re-lands #53020 (commit `83cadd65d9`), reverted in #59805. The diff is byte-identical to the reverted commit (`git patch-id` matches). Original bug report: #53019. Supersedes #60266, which carries the same diff; thanks @DiegoCao for preparing it.

`NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration` builds a standalone `ParallelLMHead` and only populates it from `lm_head.*` weights. A checkpoint that sets `tie_word_embeddings` and ships no `lm_head.weight`, such as `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0`, therefore keeps a randomly initialized output head. Nothing reports it: the server starts, reports healthy, and returns garbage.

## Why this can land now

#59805 did not revert because the fix was wrong. It reverted because the `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` case added to `test_nemotron_parse.py` failed in the nightly full CI run while loading that checkpoint's tokenizer, before any model code ran:

```
transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py:120 in convert_to_native_format
    local_kwargs["tokenizer_object"] = TokenizerFast.from_file(fast_tokenizer_file)
E   Exception: DuplicatePatternError: [225, 131, 156] at line 449472 column 1
```

The cause was the CI pin `tokenizers==0.23.1`. The 2.0 `tokenizer.json` uses an NFKC normalizer, and 14 pairs of its added tokens become identical after normalization (for example `ნ` U+10DC and `ჼ` U+10FC both normalize to `e1 83 9c`, the `[225, 131, 156]` in the error). 0.23.1 rejects the duplicates when it builds its matcher; 0.23.2 (daachorse 1.0.1 → 3.0.0, huggingface/tokenizers#2050) accepts them. #59796 bumped the pin.

| | PR | merged (UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| fix | #53020 | 2026-10-01 16:26 |
| revert | #59805 | 2026-10-02 17:19 |
| tokenizer bump that unblocks it | #59796 | 2026-10-02 18:33 |

`Tokenizer.from_file` on the 2.0 `tokenizer.json`, by `tokenizers` version:

| 0.22.2 | **0.23.1** | 0.23.2 | 1.0.0rc2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| loads | **`DuplicatePatternError`** | loads | loads |

Under the current CI pins (`tokenizers==0.23.2`, `transformers==5.18.0`), `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0")` loads (`TokenizersBackend`, vocab 72,249).

## Test Plan

- `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_nemotron_parse.py::test_models`: the `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` parametrization is restored. It is the only coverage of the tied-head path and is the case that must be green before merge.
- That test runs in `Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)`, which is `optional: true`, so it did not run on #53020's PR CI and only surfaced in the nightly run. Could a maintainer include that step when triggering CI here?
- `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-v1.2` stays in the same parametrization and is unaffected (see below).

## Test Result

Out-of-CI validation on one RTX 6000 Ada, serving the 2.0 checkpoint with `vllm serve … --dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}'`, one greedy request (50 max tokens) with the model's documented control-token prompt on the deterministic test image from the model repo's `test_golden.py`:

| build | output |
|---|---|
| vLLM v0.30.0 without this patch | `<s><s><s>…` (50 × `<s>`) |
| **v0.30.0 with this patch** | `<x_0.3906><y_0.5969>\begin{tabular}{ccccc}\n\end{tabular}<x_0.6084><y_0.6367><class_Table>` |

The patched output is byte-identical to what the model's own shipped workaround (`vllm_tied_patch/sitecustomize.py` in the HF repo) produces on the same input.

Why v1.2 cannot be affected: the two checkpoints differ exactly where the new branch reads.

| checkpoint | `tie_word_embeddings` (config / `config.decoder`) | `lm_head.weight` in checkpoint | tensors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-v1.2` | `false` / `false` | present | 667 |
| `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` | `true` / `true` | absent | 666 |

The tie goes through `ParallelLMHead.tie_weights()`, so it routes via `quant_method.tie_weights` rather than assigning `.weight` directly.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both files.

## Notes

- Commit trailers preserve the original authorship (`Signed-off-by: Anish Kumar`, `Co-authored-by: Cyrus Leung`).
- Root-cause write-up on the original PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53020#issuecomment-5957763325.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Always attempt NIXL agent removal during peer teardown
author: nej1gotnochill
body:
## Overview

Fixes the stale NIXL peer-registration state in the P2P tiering transport that can permanently wedge the data plane after a peer-down/reconnect cycle such as SIGSTOP/SIGCONT, while the control plane keeps reporting HIT. Fixes #60205.

## Problem

`NixlTransport.remove_remote_peer()` runs two independent teardown operations in sequence: releasing the remote descriptor-list handle, then removing the remote agent. If `release_dlist_handle()` raises, the exception aborts the method before `remove_remote_agent()` is attempted, so the NIXL remote agent stays registered after the peer is gone — leaving a stale registration behind.

`_publish_peer()` has the same problem on its superseded-registration path: both teardown calls share a single `try` block, so a release failure skips the agent removal for a registration that is being discarded.

**Reporter's reproduction (#60205), condensed:** disaggregated prefill/decode, `TieringOffloadingSpec` over UCX/NIXL. After SIGSTOP of one EngineCore and SIGCONT, the control plane recovers (sessions reconnect, heartbeats and lookups keep returning HIT), but transfers to/from that rank fail permanently — `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, then `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` on every poll. Fetches time out after 30 s and recompute; healthy ranks keep working; only a group restart fixes the wedged rank.

## Fix

Move both teardown calls into one small `_release_remote_handles()` helper that runs each operation under its own `try`/`except`, and call it from both `remove_remote_peer()` and `_publish_peer()`. Failures from either teardown operation are logged rather than aborting teardown midway, so `remove_remote_agent()` is always attempted. The `_peer_lock`/`_peer_gen` handling in `remove_remote_peer()` on `main` is unchanged.

## Evidence from the reviewer

The reviewer reproduced the stale-registration wedge on real NIXL/UCX: two pods on different nodes, nixl 1.5.0, `rc_mlx5` over InfiniBand, DRAM-only transfers, using the same call sequence as `NixlTransport`, with every WRITE checksum-verified at the target:

- Teardown plus a same-name re-add after a 249-second SIGSTOP/SIGCONT cycle recovers cleanly; the re-add does not reuse a stale endpoint.
- With the peer frozen, the WRITE raises `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`. If `remove_remote_agent` was also skipped (the pre-patch path when `release_dlist_handle` raises), the SIGCONT plus re-add reports OK, but every WRITE after that still fails with `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` (3 attempts over ~2 min). This matches #60205.
- Calling `remove_remote_agent` unconditionally, then re-adding, recovers it.

## Important qualification

The regression tests simulate `release_dlist_handle()` raising. Why it raised in the original incident is not confirmed.

## Scope boundary

This PR does not claim to stop in-flight writes, change transfer polling semantics, or fix the server notification ordering — `remove_remote_peer()` does not stop an in-flight WRITE. Server notification ordering and transfer-terminal handling are covered by #59790; `poll()`/`NOT_FOUND` handling stays out of scope and will be decided jointly with #59790/#49632.

## Root cause and design

**Root cause.** `remove_remote_peer()` released the dlist before removing the remote agent with no error handling — if `release_dlist_handle()` raised, `remove_remote_agent()` never ran, orphaning the NIXL registration with no Python reference left. `_publish_peer()` shared one `try` block across both calls with the same skip-on-raise behavior.

**Why teardown failures are logged, not raised:** `remove_remote_peer()` runs inside `manager._reap_dead_sessions()`, which has no exception guard up to `get_finished_jobs()`; raising would abort the reap loop and propagate into the scheduler. The EC connector's NIXL transport follows the same log-and-continue pattern.

## Testing

Commands (run from the repo root):

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ -q --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p        # 277 passed
python -m ruff check <changed files>                                                                      # passed
python -m ruff format --check <changed files>                                                             # passed
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD                                                                       # clean
```

New regression tests, both verified to fail against unpatched upstream `nixl.py` (negative control: 2 failed, exit 1) and pass with the fix:

- `test_remove_peer_removes_agent_even_if_release_fails` — a release failure during peer removal must not skip `remove_remote_agent()`.
- `test_superseded_registration_removes_agent_even_if_release_fails` — a release failure while discarding a superseded registration in `_publish_peer()` must not skip `remove_remote_agent()`.

Runs are CPU-only with a mocked NIXL agent, in WSL2 Ubuntu, Python 3.12, torch 2.14.1+cpu.

**Outstanding limitation:** no GPU/RDMA/UCX hardware validation was performed by the contributor. The hardware reproduction above was performed by the reviewer, not locally.

## Disclosure

This contribution was prepared with AI assistance (Codebuff).

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix mypy safe-super error in EmbeddingGemma2Model
author: ywang96
body:
## Overview

Fix the mypy pre-commit failure on `main` introduced by #60254 (`EmbeddingGemma2Model`): `super().__init__()` in a class inheriting `VllmModelForPooling` (a Protocol) trips `[safe-super]` + `[call-arg]`.

## Claims

- Fixes the 2 mypy errors at `vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py:1023` that break the `mypy-3.10`–`mypy-3.13` pre-commit hooks on main.
- No runtime behavior change: the MRO already resolved `super().__init__()` to `nn.Module.__init__`; this makes the call explicit.
- Not a duplicate: checked open PRs for `embedding_gemma2` / `safe-super` / #60254 follow-ups — none address this.

## Validation

```bash
# Fails on main, passes with this change (2 errors -> 0)
mypy --python-version 3.10 vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py
# Also verified: --python-version 3.11, 3.12, 3.13

# The hook as CI runs it, on every file #60254 touched
python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.10 \
  vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/config.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py \
  vllm/multimodal/video.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py \
  tests/models/registry.py

ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py
```

All pass. The change is typing-visible only (`super().__init__()` already resolved to `nn.Module.__init__` at runtime), so no model eval was run; happy to run one if reviewers want it.

## Details

Root cause: `VllmModel`/`VllmModelForPooling` are Protocols whose `__init__` requires `vllm_config`. When a class explicitly inherits such a Protocol, mypy treats the protocol's trivial-body `__init__` as the abstract method reachable via `super().__init__()` and rejects the argument-free call. Fix follows the established codebase pattern (`nn.Module.__init__(self)` in `llama_eagle3.py`, `cohere_eagle.py`, `opencua.py`, `qwen3_dflash.py`, `openpangu_mtp.py`).

AI assistance (Kimi Code) was used to prepare this PR; the submitter has reviewed the change.

title: [Bugfix] Limit GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM fp8 KV cache default to SM100
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Narrow the fp8 KV cache default that #60140 added for `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` to NVIDIA SM100, and stop it from leaking into separate draft models.

## Claims

- The default is applied only when `--kv-cache-dtype` is `auto`, the platform is `is_cuda()`, and `is_device_capability_family(100)` holds.
- All other platforms (SM90, SM120, ROCm, XPU, CPU) keep `auto`, as before #60140. The XPU branch and the `auto` -> `bfloat16` rewrite are removed.
- A separate draft model (anything other than `mtp`) keeps `auto` unless the user sets `kv_cache_dtype` in the speculative config. MTP still follows the target.
- The default is logged once at startup.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` hooks pass on the changed file.
- **Not run end-to-end.** No GLM server was started with this change, on any hardware. In particular the fp8 target + bf16 draft combination that this makes the SM100 default for non-MTP drafts has not been exercised; it goes through the existing explicit `speculative_config.kv_cache_dtype` override path.
- No test added. A config-level test would only mirror the hook's own conditions with mocked platform checks.
- SM100 + MTP behaviour is unchanged from #60140, so its benchmark and gsm8k results still apply to that configuration.

## Details

Problems with the #60140 hook that this addresses:

- `is_cuda_alike()` includes ROCm, where the capability major comes from the GCN arch string, so `capability.major >= 10` selected fp8 on gfx11xx/gfx12xx and explicit `bfloat16` on MI3xx by accident.
- `>= 10` also covered SM110/SM120, which the PR did not report measurements for.
- Rewriting `auto` to explicit `bfloat16` (including on XPU) has no benefit, since `auto` already resolves to the model dtype, and it drops the "user did not choose" signal. The `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` hook just above maps `bfloat16` back to `auto`.
- `cache_config` is shared with the draft, which only gets its own dtype when `speculative_config.kv_cache_dtype` is set. A model-level default therefore changed the draft's KV cache dtype too, e.g. for DSpark drafts.

Limitations: unquantized GLM checkpoints on SM100 still get the fp8 default; #53138 restricts it to `fp8`/`modelopt_fp4` checkpoints.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs for `60140 in:body`, `GLM fp8 kv cache default`, and `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM kv cache`. #53138 (open, predates #60140) proposes adding an fp8 default for quantized GLM on NVIDIA; it does not address the hook now on `main`. No open PR narrows or reverts #60140.

AI assistance was used to write this change.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Always include token_ids in completion stream choices
author: devshah-cohere
body:
## Overview

Ensure the Rust `/v1/completions` stream includes `token_ids` on every choice when `return_token_ids=true`.

## Claims

- Prompt chunks serialize `token_ids: []` alongside `prompt_token_ids`.
- Generated-token chunks preserve their actual token IDs.
- Terminal chunks serialize `token_ids: []`.
- Requests with `return_token_ids=false` are unchanged.

## Validation

- Manually verified the affected streaming behavior with `return_token_ids=true`.
- Added `completion_stream_serializes_requested_token_ids_on_every_choice`, which serializes the prompt, generated-token, and terminal chunks and asserts their exact `token_ids` values.
- The regression test is covered by the existing Rust Frontend Cargo CI for changes under `rust/`.
- Focused pre-commit checks passed:

  ```bash
  pre-commit run --files rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/completions.rs
  ```

- Rust formatting passed locally in a Rust 1.95 container:

  ```bash
  cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
  ```

- The targeted regression test passed locally in a Rust 1.95 container:

  ```bash
  cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-server \
    completion_stream_serializes_requested_token_ids_on_every_choice
  ```

## Details

`CompletionStreamChoice` skips fields whose value is `None`. Generated deltas already populated `token_ids`, but prompt and terminal choices left the field as `None`, so it disappeared from serialized responses even when requested.

The Python frontend already enforces this contract in [`OpenAIServingCompletion.completion_stream_generator`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bb87d227d4b964abb2a966cdf9194f3d376d9bbe/vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py#L399-L417): every emitted `CompletionResponseStreamChoice` sets `token_ids` to `as_list(output.token_ids)` whenever `return_token_ids` is enabled. This explicitly supplies a list, including an empty list, instead of leaving the optional field unset. The Rust frontend only set the field on generated-token chunks, so prompt and terminal choices omitted it.

The existing stream-yield path now fills only missing `token_ids` values with an empty list when `return_token_ids` is enabled. Centralizing this at emission covers every completion choice while preserving real IDs already attached to generated-token chunks. The only payload change is an empty list on opt-in prompt and terminal chunks; no dependencies or public request fields change.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Accept num_speculative_tokens in NgramGPUSpeculator.propose

title: [Bugfix][Core] Count unscheduled running requests toward max_loras
author: sricursion
body:
## Overview

Count the LoRA adapters of all running requests, not only those scheduled in the current step, when deciding whether a waiting request fits within `max_loras`. Without this, a skipped running request lets a request with another adapter in, and the next batch holds more than `max_loras` adapters and trips an assertion in `Scheduler.schedule()`.

Fixes #60301

## Claims

- With `--max-loras N`, a waiting request whose adapter would exceed `N` once a currently skipped running request resumes is no longer admitted early. This happens with pipeline parallelism and also on a single GPU, e.g. when a multimodal request is skipped because the step's encoder budget is used up.
- Fixes `AssertionError` in `schedule()` (`assert len(scheduled_loras) <= self.lora_config.max_loras`), which escapes the engine core busy loop and kills the engine.
- No behavior change when every running request is scheduled in the step.
- One-line source change (the iterable the set is built from) plus its comment; `create_scheduler` in the scheduler test helpers gains a `lora_config` argument.

## Validation

Repro on `main` (`bf049ddb8f`), CPU, `Scheduler` with `max_loras=1`, stepping `schedule()` and `update_from_output()` the way a pipeline-parallel engine does (a step's output returns only after the next `schedule()`):

1. `r1` (LoRA 1, 8-token prompt) is scheduled; its output is still in flight.
2. `r2` (LoRA 2) arrives. `r1` has nothing to run in step 2, so `scheduled_loras` is empty and `r2` is admitted.
3. `r1`'s output returns. Step 3 schedules `r1` (decode) and `r2` (next prefill chunk) together.

Before:

```
max_loras: 1
step1: {'r1': 8}
step2: {'r2': 16} running: ['r1', 'r2']
  File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 877, in schedule
    assert len(scheduled_loras) <= self.lora_config.max_loras
AssertionError
```

After:

```
max_loras: 1
step1: {'r1': 8}
step2: {} running: ['r1']
step3: {'r1': 1}
distinct LoRAs in batch: {1} max_loras: 1
```

Randomized check (12 requests with LoRA ids drawn from {none, 1, 2, 3, 4}, random prompt lengths and arrival steps, `max_loras=2`, PP=2, `max_num_batched_tokens=16`, 200 seeds, requests complete after 4 tokens):

| | seeds finished | `AssertionError` in `schedule()` | max adapters in one batch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 176 | 24 | 2 |
| this PR | 200 | 0 | 2 |

Regression test `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output`:

```
# main
E       AssertionError: assert {'b': 8} == {}
E         Left contains 1 more item:
E         {'b': 8}
tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py:358: AssertionError
1 failed, 1 passed, 199 deselected

# this PR
tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output PASSED
```

Existing tests (CPU, `pytest -p no:cacheprovider`):

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
  45 failed, 175 passed
pytest tests/v1/core
  59 failed, 877 passed, 4 errors
```

All of these failures and errors are pre-existing: the same 59 test ids fail and the same 4 tests error on `main` (rerun there by node id). They are multimodal and e2e tests (`Llava`/`Qwen2.5-VL`/`Qwen3.5` architecture inspection fails, engine and server fixtures cannot start) in an environment without GPU or compiled kernels. None involve LoRA.

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output` fails with `scheduler.py` reverted to `main` (`AssertionError: assert {'b': 8} == {}`) and passes with the fix.
- The scheduler-level repro in #60301 hits the assertion on `main` and runs to completion with this PR; the randomized check gives the same numbers as in the table (24 of 200 seeds fail on `main`, 0 with this PR).
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 343 passed, 46 failed. The same 46 tests fail on `main` (45 `LlavaForConditionalGeneration` inspection errors because `torchvision` is not installed here, 1 subprocess timeout in `test_kv_cache_utils.py`); none involve LoRA.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: `Scheduler.schedule()` seeds `scheduled_loras` from `scheduled_running_reqs` (`scheduler.py:869-877` on `main`) and the waiting loop admits a request only if its adapter fits in that set (`:918-929`). A running request is skipped in a step when it has nothing to schedule yet: with PP>1 once its prompt is fully scheduled but the output is pending (the `num_new_tokens == 0` case documented in the running loop), and through the other `continue` paths of the running loop (`next_decode_eligible_step` cadence for V2 + PP + async, DP prefill deferral, EC connector and encoder budget waits). Its adapter is then missing from the set, a request with another adapter is admitted, and once the skipped request is scheduled again both end up in one batch. The running loop does not consult `max_loras`, so the existing `assert` is the first thing to notice.

Fix: seed the set from `self.running`. Every request enters `self.running` through the waiting-loop admission check, so the number of distinct adapters among running requests stays at most `max_loras` and the assert holds. This is how the V0 scheduler counted (`curr_loras` was built from all running sequence groups), and what `LoRAConfig.max_loras` ("Max number of LoRAs in a single batch") requires. The variable keeps its name since it is still the set the waiting loop extends as it admits requests.

Scope and limits: the check is more conservative only when a running request that holds an adapter is skipped in the step; that request's adapter slot is kept until it finishes. Two tests cover it: the pipeline-parallel case and, without PP, a running request skipped because earlier requests used up the step's encoder compute budget (suggested in review). Both fail on `main` and pass with this change. Open priority-preemption PRs (#40087, #45558, #45561, #54530) read and update `scheduled_loras` but do not change how it is seeded.

Not a duplicate: I searched issues and PRs on `vllm-project/vllm` for `max_loras`, `scheduled_loras`, `LoRA scheduler`, `LoRA pipeline`, `LoRA async`, `max_loras assertion` and `no free lora slots`, and open PRs for `scheduler.py lora` and `LoRA schedule running requests`. Nothing reports or fixes this. Closest hits: #15422 (merged, introduced the current seeding), #14495 (closed feature request about "No free lora slots" for over-full batches, predates #15422), #17003 (usage question), #10840 (closed, a V0 LoRA scheduling policy), and the open priority-preemption PRs above.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.

End-to-end validation in review: on 2×H20 (Qwen3-0.6B, 3 LoRAs, PP=2, `max_loras=1`) `main` dies with `EngineDeadError` from this assert in all four MRV2/V1 × sync/async combinations and this PR completes with outputs matching per-request runs; the single-GPU encoder-budget case (Qwen3.5-4B, `max_loras=2`) reproduces and is fixed as well.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor default penalties in batch chat completions
author: sricursion
body:
## Overview

`/v1/chat/completions/batch` ignores server-default `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` (from `generation_config.json` or `--override-generation-config`) because `BatchChatCompletionRequest` still defaults both fields to `0.0`. This applies to the batch request the same `None` defaults that #50769 gave `ChatCompletionRequest` and `CompletionRequest`, in the same way #47597 did for `temperature`, `top_p`, `min_p` and `repetition_penalty`.

Fixes #60302

## Claims

- An omitted `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` on `/v1/chat/completions/batch` now resolves to the server default, exactly as on `/v1/chat/completions`.
- Explicit client values still win, including an explicit `0.0`.
- With no server default the penalties stay `0.0`, so behavior without a generation config does not change.
- Two-line change in `protocol.py`, plus a regression test.

## Validation

Repro on `main` (`bf049ddb8f`), server defaults `presence_penalty=0.5`, `frequency_penalty=0.25`, client omits both:

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import (
    BatchChatCompletionRequest, ChatCompletionRequest)

conv = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]
server_defaults = {"presence_penalty": 0.5, "frequency_penalty": 0.25}

sp = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=conv).to_sampling_params(16, server_defaults)
print("single  :", sp.presence_penalty, sp.frequency_penalty)

batch = BatchChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[conv])
print("batch field defaults:", batch.presence_penalty, batch.frequency_penalty)
sp = batch.to_chat_completion_request(conv).to_sampling_params(16, server_defaults)
print("batch   :", sp.presence_penalty, sp.frequency_penalty)
```

```text
# main                                  # this PR
single  : 0.5 0.25                      single  : 0.5 0.25
batch field defaults: 0.0 0.0           batch field defaults: None None
batch   : 0.0 0.0                       batch   : 0.5 0.25
```

With no server default (`to_sampling_params(16, {})`) the converted batch request gets `0.0 0.0` on both `main` and this PR, and an explicit `presence_penalty=0.0, frequency_penalty=0.0` on the batch request gives `0.0 0.0` even with the server defaults above.

The same through `OpenAIServingChatBatch.create_batch_chat_completion` with a mocked engine whose model config reports `{"presence_penalty": 0.5, "frequency_penalty": 0.25}`, printing the `SamplingParams` handed to `engine.generate`:

```text
# main                                          # this PR
/v1/chat/completions       : 0.5 0.25           /v1/chat/completions       : 0.5 0.25
/v1/chat/completions/batch : 0.0 0.0            /v1/chat/completions/batch : 0.5 0.25
batch, explicit 1.0 / 0.0  : 1.0 0.0            batch, explicit 1.0 / 0.0  : 1.0 0.0
```

Regression test: `TestBatchChatCompletionPenaltyDefaults` in `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_penalty_default_resolution.py` (existing file, already collected by the `entrypoints/openai` Buildkite step).

- On `main`, `test_defaults_applied_when_client_omits` fails with `assert 0.0 == 1.5` (`presence_penalty`) and the other six tests in the file pass.
- With the fix, all seven tests in the file pass.

Test runs on CPU, with the fix applied (the last selector is the five mock-engine tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py`, the ones marked `skip_global_cleanup`):

```text
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_penalty_default_resolution.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_watermarking.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat.py::test_null_top_logprobs_is_same_as_omitted \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py::<five mock-engine tests>
-> 77 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_error.py
-> 31 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k "not gpt_oss"
-> 180 passed, 11 deselected
```

No failures. Not run: the 11 `gpt_oss` tests in `test_serving_chat.py` (they start a real `gpt-oss-20b` server) and the server-backed tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py`, which need a GPU.

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- `TestBatchChatCompletionPenaltyDefaults::test_defaults_applied_when_client_omits` fails with `protocol.py` reverted to `main` (`assert 0.0 == 1.5`) and passes with the fix.
- The request-level repro above still prints `0.0 0.0` for the batch request on `main`.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_penalty_default_resolution.py` plus the five mock-engine tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py`: 12 passed.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/entrypoints/openai/test_penalty_default_resolution.py vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

`BatchChatCompletionRequest.to_chat_completion_request()` builds each per-conversation request from `self.model_dump(exclude={"messages"}, exclude_none=True)`, so every non-`None` field default is forwarded as if the client had set it. `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` defaulted to `0.0` (`protocol.py`, `BatchChatCompletionRequest`), so `ChatCompletionRequest.to_sampling_params()` always saw `0.0` and never consulted `default_sampling_params`. #50769 added both names to `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()` and made the fields `None` on `ChatCompletionRequest` and `CompletionRequest`, but the batch request kept the old default. The batch request's own comment says it mirrors `ChatCompletionRequest`; this restores that.

The fix sets both fields to `None`. `exclude_none=True` then drops them from the converted request, and the existing resolution order applies: client value, then server default, then the OpenAI default of `0.0`. Nothing else reads these two fields from the batch request.

Scope: only the two field defaults. The request schema default for these two fields changes from `0.0` to `None` (a client that omits them still gets `0.0` unless the operator configured a default).

Not a duplicate. Searched `vllm-project/vllm` issues and PRs (open, merged and closed) for: `batch penalty`, `chat completions batch`, `BatchChatCompletionRequest`, `presence_penalty batch`, `frequency_penalty batch chat`, `presence_penalty override-generation-config`, `frequency_penalty generation_config`, `penalty defaults chat batch endpoint`, `to_chat_completion_request penalty`, `batch endpoint default sampling params`, plus `gh pr list --state open --search` for `BatchChatCompletionRequest`, `chat_completion/protocol.py presence_penalty` and `presence_penalty`. Closest hits:

- #47597 (merged): same bug class on the batch request for `temperature`, `top_p`, `min_p`, `repetition_penalty`; it did not touch the penalties, which were still `0.0` on `ChatCompletionRequest` at the time.
- #50769 (merged, fixes issue #50767): fixed the single-conversation and completions paths. A comment on that PR expected the batch defaults to be inert because `check_batch_mode` dumps with `exclude_unset=True`. They are not: that dump only feeds validation, the model still gets the `0.0` field default, and `to_chat_completion_request()` dumps with `exclude_none=True`, which keeps it (see the repro above).
- #50042 (open PR): adds `stream` / `tools` validation to `BatchChatCompletionRequest`; different fields, no overlap.
- #54469 (open PR): server-default `thinking_token_budget`; different fields.
- #57935, #50026 (open issues): other batch endpoint bugs, unrelated to sampling defaults.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return 400 for images rejected by Pillow's bomb check
author: sricursion
body:
## Overview

`ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` lets Pillow's `DecompressionBombError` escape, so an image above Pillow's pixel limit gets an HTTP 500 from the API server. This converts it to a `ValueError` like the other undecodable-image errors, so the client gets a 400.

Fixes #60303

## Claims

- A 23 KB PNG of 14000x14000 pixels (196M pixels, above the 178,956,970 default of both Pillow's 2x limit and `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`) changes from `500 InternalServerError` to `400 BadRequestError`.
- `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` now raises `ValueError` for these images instead of `PIL.Image.DecompressionBombError`, so `MediaConnector.fetch_image`, `fetch_image_async` and the `video/jpeg` frame path of `VideoMediaIO.load_base64` report them as client errors too.
- No change to which images are accepted or rejected, and no change to the `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` check.

## Validation

Repro on `main` (`bf049ddb8f`), CPU only, Pillow 12.3.0. It builds the PNG, calls the same `MediaConnector.fetch_image_async` that `chat_utils` uses for an `image_url` part, and puts that behind vLLM's registered exception handlers:

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
from io import BytesIO
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pybase64
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from PIL import Image

from vllm.entrypoints.serve.exception_handling.register import init_exception_handler
from vllm.multimodal.media import ImageMediaIO, MediaConnector

buf = BytesIO()
Image.new("1", (14000, 14000)).save(buf, format="PNG")
data = buf.getvalue()
print("png bytes", len(data), "pixels", 14000 * 14000)

try:
    ImageMediaIO().load_bytes(data)
except BaseException as e:
    print("load_bytes ->", type(e).__module__ + "." + type(e).__name__,
          "| is ValueError:", isinstance(e, ValueError), "|", str(e)[:160])

url = "data:image/png;base64," + pybase64.b64encode(data).decode()

app = FastAPI()
app.state.args = SimpleNamespace(log_error_stack=False)
init_exception_handler(app)


@app.post("/v1/chat/completions")
async def chat():
    await MediaConnector().fetch_image_async(url)


r = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False).post("/v1/chat/completions")
print("HTTP", r.status_code, r.json())
```

</details>

Before (`main`):

```text
png bytes 23859 pixels 196000000
load_bytes -> PIL.Image.DecompressionBombError | is ValueError: False | Image size (196000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.
HTTP 500 {'error': {'message': 'Image size (196000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.', 'type': 'InternalServerError', 'param': None, 'code': 500}}
```

After (this PR):

```text
png bytes 23859 pixels 196000000
load_bytes -> builtins.ValueError | is ValueError: True | Failed to load image: Image size (196000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.
HTTP 400 {'error': {'message': 'Failed to load image: Image size (196000000 pixels) exceeds limit of 178956970 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.', 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': None, 'code': 400}}
```

Regression test `test_image_decompression_bomb_rejected` in `tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py`. It lowers `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` so a 20x20 PNG trips Pillow's limit, and checks that `load_bytes` raises `ValueError` caused by `Image.DecompressionBombError`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py -v
```

- On `main` with only the test added: `1 failed, 13 passed`. The failure is `PIL.Image.DecompressionBombError: Image size (400 pixels) exceeds limit of 100 pixels, could be decompression bomb DOS attack.` raised from `open_image` in `load_bytes`.
- With the fix: `14 passed`.

Wider run, `tests/multimodal/media` (CPU only):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media -q
```

- `main`: `3 failed, 162 passed, 4 skipped`.
- This PR: `3 failed, 163 passed, 4 skipped` (the added test).
- The 3 failures are the same on both and unrelated: `test_audio.py::test_audio_media_io_from_video`, `test_load_audio_backend_matches_default[pyav]` and `test_audio_media_io_audio_backend_kwarg` fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'av'` because my environment lacks `vllm[audio]`. The 4 skips are `torchcodec` not being installed.

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- `test_image_decompression_bomb_rejected` fails with `image.py` reverted to `main` (`PIL.Image.DecompressionBombError: Image size (400 pixels) exceeds limit of 100 pixels`) and passes with the fix.
- The repro above still returns `HTTP 500` on `main`.
- `pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py`: 14 passed.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py vllm/multimodal/media/image.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: `Image.open` calls Pillow's `_decompression_bomb_check`, which raises `Image.DecompressionBombError` for an image above `2 * Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (178,956,970 pixels by default). That class derives from `Exception`, not `OSError`, so the `except (OSError, Image.UnidentifiedImageError)` in `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` does not catch it. The raw exception propagates through `MediaConnector.fetch_image_async` and `AsyncMultiModalItemTracker.resolve_items`, and `create_error_response` has no mapping for it, so it falls through to `InternalServerError` (500). A `ValueError` takes the `BadRequestError` (400) branch.

The default `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (178,956,970) equals Pillow's 2x threshold, and Pillow's check runs inside `Image.open`, before the `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` check. So with default settings an oversized image is always stopped by Pillow first, and the 400 that `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` is meant to provide (see `docs/usage/security.md`) is only reachable once the variable is lowered. The variable does not change Pillow's limit, so raising it or setting it to `0` leaves the same 500.

The fix adds `Image.DecompressionBombError` to the exception tuple, so the message is reported as `Failed to load image: ...` with the original exception chained. It is the same treatment #38253 gave truncated and corrupt images.

Scope and limits:

- Pillow's own limit stays in force. Images between `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` and twice that still only produce Pillow's `DecompressionBombWarning` and load as before.
- Only the exception type seen by callers changes. Nothing is decoded that was not decoded before.

Not a duplicate. I searched `vllm-project/vllm` issues and PRs, open and closed, for `DecompressionBombError`, `decompression bomb`, `DecompressionBombWarning`, `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`, `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`, `ImageMediaIO` and `oversized image 500`, and listed open PRs matching `multimodal/media/image.py`, `decompression bomb image` and `Pillow image error`. Nothing covers this bug. Closest hits:

- #47010 (merged) added `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` and the pixel check in `load_bytes`. It does not handle the exception Pillow raises from `Image.open`.
- #38253 (merged) returned 400 for corrupt or truncated images. It covers `OSError` and `UnidentifiedImageError` only.
- #56527 (closed issue) is a 500 from malformed EXIF in `MultiModalHasher.serialize_item`, a different code path.
- #57752 (open, marked "Don't merge", `needs-rebase`) is an experiment that moves media decoding into the multimodal processor. It keeps the same `except (OSError, Image.UnidentifiedImageError)` tuple, so it does not address this and would need the same one-line addition if it lands.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return 4xx for client errors in /cohere/v2/chat
author: sricursion
body:
## Overview

`POST /cohere/v2/chat` and `POST /cohere/v2/chat/render` answer every exception raised while handling a request with HTTP 500, including errors caused by the request itself. `/v1/chat/completions` returns 400 for the same input. This routes the exception through `create_error_response`, the way #52246 did for `/v1/messages`.

Fixes #60304

## Claims

- Client-caused errors raised by the Cohere chat and render handlers (`VLLMValidationError`, `pydantic.ValidationError`, and the other cases `create_error_response` maps to 4xx) now return 4xx instead of 500, e.g. `temperature: -1` or a `seed` outside int64.
- The response body keeps the Cohere `{message, id}` envelope.
- Unexpected errors still return 500 with the same body as before.
- The Cohere SDK retries every status >= 500 (`_should_retry` in `cohere/core/http_client.py`, cohere 7.2.0), so a malformed request is no longer replayed by SDK clients.

## Validation

Reproduced on current `main` (bf049ddb8f) with FastAPI's `TestClient` and vLLM's global exception handlers installed. `/v1/chat/completions` gets the same input for comparison.

| input | route | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seed = 2**63` | `/cohere/v2/chat` | 500 | 400 |
| `seed = 2**63` | `/cohere/v2/chat/render` | 500 | 400 |
| `seed = 2**63` | `/v1/chat/completions` | 400 | 400 |
| `temperature = -1` | `/cohere/v2/chat` | 500 | 400 |
| `temperature = -1` | `/v1/chat/completions` | 400 | 400 |
| `temperature = 5` | `/cohere/v2/chat` | 500 | 400 |
| `temperature = 5` | `/v1/chat/completions` | 400 | 400 |

- `seed = 2**63` fails `ChatCompletionRequest` validation while the v2 body is converted, using the real `CohereServingChatV2` conversion with no engine.
- The `temperature` rows go through the real `create_chat_v2` -> `create_chat_completion` -> `to_sampling_params` path, with the renderer and engine client stubbed out. Both routes return the same message, e.g. `temperature must be non-negative, got -1.0. (parameter=temperature, value=-1.0)`. The Cohere body is `{"message": ..., "id": "chatcmpl-..."}`.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script for the seed case</summary>

```python
import os

os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API"] = "1"

from argparse import Namespace

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from vllm.entrypoints.cohere.api_router import attach_router
from vllm.entrypoints.cohere.serving import CohereServingChatV2
from vllm.entrypoints.serve.exception_handling.register import init_exception_handler

app = FastAPI()
app.state.args = Namespace(
    log_error_stack=False, enable_scale_out=True, tokens_only=False
)
init_exception_handler(app)
attach_router(app)
app.state.cohere_serving_chat_v2 = CohereServingChatV2.__new__(CohereServingChatV2)

body = {"model": "m", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "seed": 2**63}
with TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as client:
    r = client.post("/cohere/v2/chat", json=body)
    print(r.status_code, r.text)
```

</details>

Regression tests, added to `tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py`:

- `TestEndpoint::test_handler_client_error_returns_400_envelope` (parametrized: `VLLMValidationError`, `ValueError`)
- `TestRenderEndpoint::test_conversion_client_error_returns_400_envelope` (the existing `test_conversion_exception_returns_500_envelope`, which asserted 500 for a conversion `ValueError`, now asserts 400)

With only the tests applied on top of `main`'s `api_router.py`, all three fail because the route returns 500 where the test expects 400:

```text
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py -k client_error
FAILED ...::TestEndpoint::test_handler_client_error_returns_400_envelope[vllm_validation_error]
FAILED ...::TestEndpoint::test_handler_client_error_returns_400_envelope[value_error]
FAILED ...::TestRenderEndpoint::test_conversion_client_error_returns_400_envelope
3 failed, 28 deselected
```

With the fix they pass, and so do the existing `RuntimeError` -> 500 tests (`test_handler_exception_returns_500_envelope`, `test_render_exception_returns_500_envelope`).

`pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere --ignore=tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_chat_v2.py`: 217 passed with the change. `test_chat_v2.py` boots a server with model weights and was not run.

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- The three `client_error` tests fail with `api_router.py` reverted to `main` (`assert 500 == <HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST: 400>`) and pass with the fix.
- The `seed` and `temperature` repros still return 500 on `/cohere/v2/chat` and 400 on `/v1/chat/completions` on `main`.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere --ignore=tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_chat_v2.py`: 217 passed.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py vllm/entrypoints/cohere/api_router.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: both handlers in `vllm/entrypoints/cohere/api_router.py` (the `except Exception` blocks at lines 141 and 197 on `main`) built a fixed `HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` response, with the comment "report as 500 for parity". `/v1/messages` had the same hard-coded 500 until #52246 switched it to `create_error_response`. The OpenAI routes never catch the exception and let the global handlers map it, so the same bad input produced 400 there and 500 here. The conversion in `create_chat_v2` and `to_sampling_params` in the chat path both run outside any handler that would turn their exceptions into an `ErrorResponse`, so they reach this `except`.

The fix replaces the hard-coded response with `_error_response(create_error_response(e), raw_request)`. `create_error_response` is the mapper the global exception handlers and `/v1/messages` use: client-error `VLLMError` subclasses and the legacy `ValueError`/`TypeError`/`OverflowError` fallbacks map to 4xx, `NotImplementedError` to 501, server-side `VLLMError`s keep their 5xx status, and anything else is 500 with the same message as before. `_error_response` already builds the `CohereError` body, so the wire shape is unchanged. The stale `noqa` comment is dropped along with the wrong "parity" claim.

Scope and limits:

- Only the two `except` blocks change. The `ErrorResponse` branch and `CohereErrorEnvelopeMiddleware` are untouched.
- Like the shared handlers, a stray `ValueError` raised by an internal bug is now reported as 400 rather than 500.
- The existing `logger.exception` calls are kept, so client errors are still logged with a traceback, as in `/v1/messages`.

Not a duplicate: I searched `vllm-project/vllm` issues and PRs, open and closed, for combinations of `cohere`, `/cohere/v2/chat`, `api_router`, 500, 4xx, client error, `create_error_response`, `seed` and `temperature`, and listed all `cohere in:title,body` PRs. No issue or PR covers the Cohere status mapping. Closest hits:

- #52246 (merged): the same fix for `/v1/messages`; this follows its approach.
- #52622 (merged): the same for `/detokenize`.
- #57018 (open): bounds `seed` in `CohereChatV2Request` and `SamplingParams`. It closes one trigger at the schema level; this change covers the other errors reaching the same `except` (e.g. `temperature`), and the two do not overlap in code.
- #55489 (open): changes one line inside the render route's `try` block (passes `raw_request` to `render_chat_request`); no change to the error handling.
- #52467, #53750, #56146 (merged) and #52437 (open): validate fields of the Cohere request model, before the handler runs.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Log the full request body when max_log_len is unset
author: sricursion
body:
## Overview

With `--enable-log-requests` at DEBUG level, the request JSON body log added in #58163 drops the last character of every body when `--max-log-len` is unset, which is the default. The closing `}` is missing, so the logged line is not valid JSON. This slices the body with `max_log_len` as is, so `None` keeps the whole body.

Fixes #60305

## Claims

- With the default `--max-log-len`, the DEBUG `Request <id> JSON body: ...` line contains the complete body and parses as JSON.
- With `--max-log-len N`, the body is still cut to its first `N` characters.

## Validation

There was no GPU available, so this was not checked against a live `vllm serve`. Instead I called `BaseServing._check_model`, which is where the serving paths call `log_request_body`, with `RequestLogger(max_log_len=None)`, the logger at DEBUG and a `ChatCompletionRequest` with one user message:

```
# main (bf049ddb8f)
Request ae92dec5c10116ec JSON body: {"messages":[{"content":"Say hello.","role":"user"}],"model":"test-model"
logged body is NOT valid JSON: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 74 (char 73)

# this PR
Request b632ee1a8e84b1f6 JSON body: {"messages":[{"content":"Say hello.","role":"user"}],"model":"test-model"}
logged body is valid JSON
```

Calling `RequestLogger.log_request_body` directly on `CompletionRequest(model="test-model", prompt="Hello, world!")`:

```
# main
max_log_len=None  : ... JSON body: {"model":"test-model","prompt":"Hello, world!","max_tokens":16
max_log_len=10    : ... JSON body: {"model":"

# this PR
max_log_len=None  : ... JSON body: {"model":"test-model","prompt":"Hello, world!","max_tokens":16}
max_log_len=10    : ... JSON body: {"model":"
```

`max_log_len=0` (empty body) and `max_log_len=10000` (full body) give the same output on both.

The example logs in #58163's description show the same missing closing brace (e.g. `..."stream":false,"temperature":0.0`).

Regression test `test_request_logger_log_request_body_truncation` in `tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_request_logger.py`, parametrized over `max_log_len` in `[None, 10]`. With the new test and the old `request_logger.py`:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_request_logger.py
.........F.
FAILED ...::test_request_logger_log_request_body_truncation[None]
E         - _tokens":16}
E         ?            -
E         + _tokens":16
1 failed, 10 passed
```

With this PR, `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/utils` gives `41 passed` (the 39 existing tests and the two new cases).

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- `test_request_logger_log_request_body_truncation[None]` fails with `request_logger.py` reverted to `main` (the logged body ends in `_tokens":16` instead of `_tokens":16}`) and passes with the fix.
- The repro above still logs the body without its closing brace on `main`.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/utils`: 41 passed.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_request_logger.py vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/request_logger.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: `log_request_body` (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/request_logger.py`) turned an unset `max_log_len` into `-1` and used it as the slice end, so `[:-1]` removed the last character instead of meaning "no limit". `--max-log-len` documents `None` as unlimited, and `log_inputs` and `log_outputs` in the same class leave their text alone when it is `None`. Slicing with `None` already keeps the whole string, so the `-1` mapping is simply dropped. Nothing else changes: the DEBUG gate and log format are the same, and `max_log_len=0` still logs an empty body.

Not a duplicate. I searched issues and PRs in `vllm-project/vllm` for `log_request_body`, `request_logger.py`, `max_log_len`, `request JSON body` and `enable-log-requests`, and found nothing that reports or fixes this. Closest:

- #58163 (merged) introduced the body log.
- #45634 (open) adds request arrival and completion logs to `RequestLogger`; it does not touch `log_request_body`.
- #58573 (closed, unmerged) correlates request logs with external request IDs; it does not touch `log_request_body`.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.
