title: [Bugfix] Don't Eliminate Clones for graph I/O Aliases
author: alex-jw-brooks
body:
## Overview

Currently, the compile clone elimination doesn't check for aliases to graph inputs and outputs, which can unexpectedly clobber values if we take a snapshot of an input that doesn't have any writes & leverage in place kernels (e.g., all reduce for TP>1) and return it outside of the compile boundary for later processing. 

I don't think that there are many models in vLLM that do this with the current compile boundaries, but an example of this case came up yesterday in vLLM Omni, since the thinker snapshots the embeddings, which get `.clone`d and forwarded to the talker (more details in: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8532), where the audio gets mangled with TP=2 and compile, because the fused allreduce & rms norm runs in place and the clone on the embeddings is right inside the compile boundary.

This PR skips elimination when the clone is returned from the graph and its source aliases a graph input or another output (assuming the clone has no writes). It also adds a regression test for piecewise and full-graph compilation.

title: [Bugfix][ToolParser] Stream every tool call when one delta completes several
author: Kylinny
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #60351. With `tool_choice="required"`, streaming lost or mixed up tool calls when one stream chunk (a delta) held text from more than one call. This PR makes streaming send every call with the correct index, name, and arguments.

## Claims

- Streaming sends every call in the `required` JSON array once, with its id and name first. This is true for any split of the text into deltas.
- Argument text goes to the correct call index. The streamed arguments of a call are exactly its `"parameters"` value, so they parse as JSON and match the non-streaming result.
- `/v1/responses` streaming no longer stops in the middle of the response with a `ResponseFunctionToolCallItem` validation error (`name=None`).

## Validation

Live A/B test on one H200 GPU. Before is main at 3ca00a8261. After is this PR on the same base. Server command:

```bash
VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --stream-interval 5 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384
```

`VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0` makes `tool_choice="required"` use the JSON array path. A `--stream-interval` above 1 puts several tokens in one delta, and that causes the bug.

A script sends each request two times, with and without streaming, at temperature 0. A case passes only if all of these are true:

- Each tool call index gets exactly one id and name, before its arguments.
- The ids are unique and the indexes have no gaps.
- The streamed arguments are valid JSON and equal the non-streaming result.
- The finish reason (or stop reason) is correct.

The 19 cases cover chat completions, Responses, and Anthropic `/v1/messages`, with thinking on and off. They include four calls in one response, three calls with `}`, `]`, `"` and `}, {"name": ...` inside argument strings, one call, and `n=2`.

| Server | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, `--stream-interval 5`, 2 runs | 11 of 19 fail in both runs | 19 of 19 pass in both runs |
| Qwen3-0.6B, `--stream-interval 8` | 7 of 19 fail | 19 of 19 pass |
| Qwen3-0.6B, `--stream-interval 1` | 19 of 19 pass | 19 of 19 pass |

On main, the failures were:

- Chat: argument text went to the wrong index (index 0 got `{"city": "`, index 1 got `Dallas"}{"city": "Berlin"}`), and later calls got no id or name.
- Responses: the server raised the validation error above and closed the stream.
- Anthropic: the streamed tool inputs did not match the non-streaming ones.

The server logs for this PR have no tracebacks. At `--stream-interval 1`, one `n=2` case (temperature 0.8) returned different sampled arguments one time. It passed on two more runs.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

Start the server above, then:

```bash
curl -N localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B", "stream": true, "temperature": 0,
  "tool_choice": "required", "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Get the current weather for Dallas, Berlin and Tokyo, and also a 3-day forecast for Dallas. Make one tool call for each of these four things."}],
  "tools": [
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_current_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_forecast", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}, "days": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["city", "days"]}}}
  ]
}'
```

On main, the `tool_calls` chunks have no id or name for some indexes, and the argument text is split across the wrong indexes. With this PR, each index gets one chunk with its id and name, then only its own argument text.

</details>

## Details

Root cause: `extract_required_tool_call_streaming` looked only at the last element of the partly parsed array (`obj[-1]`). It used `len(obj) - 1` as the index and kept one shared `function_name_returned` flag. Also, `filter_delta_text` stopped at the first top-level comma. When one delta ended a call and started the next, or ended several calls, the earlier calls lost their id and name chunk. Argument text also went to the wrong index.

Fix: the new `_scan_required_tool_calls` reads the partial array once, one character at a time, and keeps track of strings and nesting. For each array element, it records the name (after the string closes and decodes as JSON) and the start and end offsets of the `"parameters"` value. These offsets do not change when the text grows. Thus one scan of `current_text` also shows what `previous_text` already contained, and the helper keeps no state between calls.

Each delta then holds one `DeltaToolCall` for each call that has unsent text. The first chunk of a call holds its id, its name, and the arguments so far. Later chunks hold only new argument text. `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` now counts every new id in a delta for `history_tool_call_cnt`, so the `kimi_k2` ids stay consecutive.

The second commit replaces the approach of the first commit (per-index progress in `StreamState`) with this stateless scan. The PR diff now changes only `vllm/tool_parsers/streaming.py`, `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`, one stale comment in `vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py`, and the tests.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- The helper no longer takes `delta_text` or `function_name_returned`. The return value does not change. The only in-tree caller is updated. This PR removes `filter_delta_text`, `_bracket_level_state`, and the use of `partial_json_parser` in this file.
- Streamed arguments no longer include the whitespace between array elements. Main sent `{...}\n  ` and this PR sends `{...}`. You can see this change at `--stream-interval 1` too.
- Streaming sends a call only after its `"parameters"` value starts. The guided decoding schema for `required` makes `parameters` mandatory, so this always occurs in practice. For text without `parameters` (for example `[{"name": "f"}]`), streaming sends no call, but the non-streaming path returns `f` with `null` arguments. On main, this input raised `IndexError` (#58309).

This PR is not a duplicate. It is the PR linked from #60351. #58309 only guards the `IndexError` in the code that this PR removes.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Reject unsupported regex inside groups
author: shreyanshj10
body:
## Overview

`validate_regex_is_buildable` only walked `BRANCH` and `MAX_REPEAT` nodes, so any
construct `outlines_core` cannot build was accepted as soon as it sat inside a group.
Fixes #60344.

## Claims

- `\b`, backreferences and look-arounds are now rejected wherever they appear, not
  only at the top level of the pattern.
- Lazy, possessive and atomic groups were leaking the same way and are covered too.
- Patterns that merely look like a word boundary (`[\b]`, `a\\b`) are still accepted.

## Validation

`_check_unsupported` recursed into two node types, so these three all passed
validation and then blew up in `StructuredOutputManager._create_grammar` with
`Failed to build DFA`:

```python
validate_regex_is_buildable(r"(a\b)")
validate_regex_is_buildable(r"((a)\2)")
validate_regex_is_buildable(r"(a(?=b))")
```

Two parametrized tests in `tests/v1/structured_output/test_validation.py` cover the
newly rejected patterns and the lookalikes that must stay accepted. Both are
pure-stdlib and run under the existing `cpu_test` marker:

```
pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_validation.py -k regex -v
```

Before this change the ten rejection cases fail (nine of them are accepted when they
should not be; `a\b` alone was already caught) and the seven acceptance cases pass.
After it, all seventeen pass. `ruff format` and `ruff check` are clean on both files.

## Details

Rather than adding `SUBPATTERN` to the list of node types to recurse into, I made the
recursion structural: whatever the node, any `SubPattern` reachable in its value gets
walked. The enumeration is what went wrong in the first place, and `MIN_REPEAT`,
`POSSESSIVE_REPEAT` and `ATOMIC_GROUP` were missing for the same reason — `(?:a\b)*?`
and `(?>a\b)` were accepted as well. Listing those explicitly would also mean guarding
the constants, since they only exist on 3.11+. `BRANCH` keeps its own arm because its
sub-patterns live in a list rather than directly in the tuple.

The check stays on the parse tree, which is what keeps `[\b]` (a backspace literal in a
character class) and `a\\b` (an escaped backslash) out of the rejection: a text-level
scan for `\b` would reject both, and that would be worse than the bug.

I left `_prefix_needs_context` alone. It has the same narrow node handling, but an
unrecognised node there just means the walk keeps looking for an anchor, so it errs
toward rejecting rather than admitting a pattern that cannot be built.

Not a duplicate: no open PR mentions #60344 or this function.

AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Parse multi-line JSON arguments in the DeepSeek V3 and V3.1 parsers
author: niansia
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60342. The `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_v31` tool parsers lose tool calls whose JSON arguments the model pretty-prints over several lines: their regexes match the arguments with `.`, which stops at a newline.

## Claims

- Tool calls with multi-line JSON arguments are now parsed by `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_v31`, in both streaming and non-streaming mode.
- Single-line arguments and parallel tool calls are unchanged.

## Validation

Reproducer from the issue, run through the test helpers with the real tokenizers (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1`), with `{"city": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"}` dumped with `indent=2`:

| Parser | Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v3` | non-streaming | no tool calls (`tools_called=True`, `tool_calls=[]`) | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v3` | streaming | `get_weather` with arguments `{` | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v31` | non-streaming | no tool calls | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v31` | streaming | `get_weather` with arguments `{` | `get_weather` with the full arguments |

Added `test_multiline_json_arguments` (DeepSeek-V3, two parallel calls with pretty-printed arguments) and `test_extract_tool_calls_with_multiline_arguments` (DeepSeek-V3.1), each run in streaming and non-streaming mode. All four cases fail on main and pass with this change.

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py
22 passed, 1 xfailed
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py` pass on the changed files.

These ran on CPU (WSL, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty`, with the post-test GPU cleanup skipped since there is no accelerator). I did not run a server end to end with a DeepSeek-V3 checkpoint, which needs a multi-GPU node; the change is limited to the parsers' regexes.

## Details

- Root cause: `DeepSeekV3ToolParser` matches `function_arguments` with `.*` (`` .*[^\n`] `` when streaming), and `DeepSeekV31ToolParser` with `.*?` / `.*`. Without `re.DOTALL`, `.` doesn't match `\n`, so the non-streaming regex finds nothing and the streaming regex captures only the first line of the arguments.
- Fix: only the arguments group uses `[\s\S]`. It stays non-greedy in the regexes used with `findall`, so parallel calls still split at the first closing tag. The type and function-name groups keep `.`, so a name can't span lines and the whole pattern doesn't need `re.DOTALL`.
- The Rust frontend's parsers (`rust/src/parser/src/tool/deepseek_json`) don't use a regex here; `take_json_object` scans the object by brace depth, so from reading the code they already handle pretty-printed arguments. Only the Python parsers change.
- Related PRs: #60361 (opened a few minutes before this one, still a draft) makes the same change to the V3 regexes and leaves V3.1 for later; this PR covers both parsers. #47503 edits the same DeepSeek-V3 regexes to accept an optional newline before the JSON fence, which is a different case, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase. #55473 wraps these regexes with timeouts and is independent.

AI assistance was used for this change (tracking down the cause, writing the tests and this description). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Don't int-sort attention-type names in --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers for packed KV dtypes
author: lobo235
body:
## Overview

`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` accepts layer indices or attention type names like `sliding_window`, but with a `turboquant_*` or `ultraquant_4bit` cache dtype, `create_engine_config` sorts the merged skip list with `key=int` and crashes on any name.

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers sliding_window` (and the same with `ultraquant_4bit`) no longer fails with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'sliding_window'`.
- Index-only skip lists hold the same layers as before. They are now ordered as strings (`"10"` before `"5"`), so a list with two-digit indices gets a different `CacheConfig` hash once, i.e. one compile-cache miss after upgrading.

## Validation

Reproduced at config level, platform forced to CPU (no kernels involved; I don't have a CUDA box):

```python
EngineArgs(model="facebook/opt-125m", kv_cache_dtype="turboquant_4bit_nc",
           kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers=["sliding_window", "5"]).create_engine_config()
# main:        ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'sliding_window'
# this branch: skip list ['0', '1', '10', '11', '5', 'sliding_window']
```

Same result with `ultraquant_4bit`. No test added: per review, the field is typed `list[str]`, so the int sort key shouldn't come back. `pre-commit` passes on the changed file.

End to end, I hit this on ROCm (gfx1201) with a hybrid GDN target and a DFlash2 drafter: TurboQuant gets picked for the target's full-attention layers, and the drafter's sliding-window layers have no TurboQuant backend, so skipping `sliding_window` is the documented way out. With the same fix applied to our ROCm build, the engine gets past config.

## Details

The user's list can hold names, but the merge with TurboQuant's boundary layers (always indices) sorted everything as ints. Now the merged list is sorted as strings. The sort stays because the list is a `CacheConfig.compute_hash()` factor and is built from a set, so without it the order (and the hash) would vary with `PYTHONHASHSEED`. Order doesn't change behaviour, since `Attention` matches entries as strings.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this sort. #54599 mentions the `sliding_window` case not working with TurboQuant "for a different reason" but doesn't change it, and #59178 / #60252 / #60023 touch the same flag in other places.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change. I reviewed the diff and ran the reproduction above.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Map sleep-mode cuMem memory for the host
author: mawong-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm ≥ 7.2, any `Tensor.item()` on sleep-mode (cuMem pool) memory segfaults. As a result, every FP8 checkpoint with `enable_sleep_mode=True` crashes during `process_weights_after_loading`. This PR maps the pool for the host as well, as PyTorch already does for its own VMM memory, and re-enables the FP8 sleep test on ROCm. That test was skipped as "Segfaults on ROCm." in #57163.

## Claims

- FP8 models start and sleep/wake with `enable_sleep_mode` on ROCm. Before this change they segfaulted at startup with AITER on or off, e.g. Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 on MI300X.
- `test_deep_sleep_compressed_tensors_kv_scales` runs on ROCm again and passes.
- The CUDA path is unchanged, and the fix adds no measurable cost to allocation or wake.

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-bb87d227` (ROCm 7.2, torch 2.13), with only `cumem_allocator.cpp` rebuilt. The file is identical between that commit and this branch's base.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_deep_sleep_compressed_tensors_kv_scales` (skip removed) | fails: worker segfault in `_local_scalar_dense_cuda` | passes |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8, `enable_sleep_mode`, TP1 | segfault at `kv_cache.py:169` (`layer.q_scale > 0.0`) | starts; greedy output bit-exact over 2 cycles × (level-1 full, level-1 selective, level-2 + `reload_weights`) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-FP8, `enable_sleep_mode`, TP2 | segfault at startup | starts; bit-exact over level-1 full, level-1 selective, level-2 + `reload_weights` |
| `.item()` on a cuMem tensor (offset 0 / 300 / 700 MiB into a 1 GiB segment) | segfault | correct value |
| `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` | — | 19 passed, 2 skipped (graph-pool tests are CUDA-only on main) |
| 100 GiB `kv_cache` allocation: first map / first wake | 0.085–0.089 s / 0.096–0.121 s | 0.098–0.102 s / 0.097 s |

MI355X (gfx950), same image, amdgpu 6.16.6, AITER on:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_deep_sleep_compressed_tensors_kv_scales` (skip removed) | fails: worker segfault | passes |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8, `enable_sleep_mode`, TP1 | segfault at startup | starts; sane output with no NaN logprobs over 2 cycles × (level-1 full, level-1 selective, level-2 + `reload_weights`). Exact match isn't meaningful here, because with AITER the output varies run to run even while awake. |

Repeated wakes of the same 100 GiB slow to about 1 s in both builds, which points to the driver still wiping the previously released memory, not to this change.

`pre-commit` passes. The re-enabled test runs in the existing ":amd: (MI300) Basic Correctness Sleep Mode" step (`basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode`).

## Details

**Root cause.** On ROCm ≥ 7.2, `_local_scalar_dense_cuda` (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/CUDAScalar.cu`) has a large-BAR fast path. It syncs the stream and dereferences the device pointer from the host. The path is taken when `isLargeBar` is set and the tensor's deleter is the caching allocator's `raw_deleter`. That's true for vLLM's pluggable cuMem pool too, because it is wrapped by the caching allocator.

The fast path relies on the device memory also being mapped for the CPU. That holds for `hipMalloc` memory on a large-BAR part. It doesn't hold for a `hipMemCreate` + `hipMemMap` mapping whose access was granted only to the device, which is what `create_and_map` did, so the host read segfaults. PyTorch's own VMM path (`ExpandableSegment::setAccess`) adds a `hipMemLocationTypeHost` access descriptor under the same `ROCM_VERSION >= 70200` gate, which is why `expandable_segments` never crashes. This change mirrors that.

I confirmed the mechanism with a standalone HIP program. With device-only access, a host dereference segfaults for every size, chunking and alignment I tried (2 MiB to 1 GiB, 256 MiB chunks). Adding the host descriptor makes the dereference succeed.

**Why FP8.** `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading` calls `layer.q_scale > 0.0`, which is an `.item()` on a parameter allocated in the sleep-mode `weights` pool. It is simply the first `.item()` that runs on sleep-mode memory at startup. Any other `.item()` on that memory would crash the same way.

**Scope.** Only ROCm builds with `HIP_VERSION >= 7.2` change. On CUDA and older ROCm, a single device descriptor is passed exactly as before. The host mapping applies at first allocation and on every wake, since both go through `create_and_map`. It uses no extra memory.

**Limitations.** Validated on gfx942 and gfx950. Like PyTorch, the host descriptor is added unconditionally rather than only on large-BAR devices; I haven't checked small-BAR parts.

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Support strided LSE in direct A2A reduction
author: john-evan08
body:
## Overview Fix the `partial LSE must have packed heads` error when using `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=1` with transposed FlashAttention MLA LSE tensors, as encountered with **DeepSeek-V2-Lite**. The direct P2P kernel now reads both tensor strides, without a contiguous copy. Unlike the NCCL fallback proposed in [#54472](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54472), this enables the direct path for these LSE layouts. ## Claims - Enable direct P2P for strided LSE without changing reduction arithmetic or backend defaults. - Improve DeepSeek-V2-Lite throughput at concurrency 32/128 on the measured long-context workload; c512 is inconclusive. ## Validation ### Serving performance DeepSeek-V2-Lite, **8 x H100 80 GB**, TP=DCP=8, expert parallelism enabled, Q/KV gather through NCCL. Both arms use the same image and Mooncake agentic workload; only `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A` changes between 0 and 1. Metric: **generated output tokens/second/GPU**; higher is better. Three nodes, two order-balanced repetitions per node: six paired measurements per concurrency. | Concurrency | A2A NCCL | A2A direct P2P | Paired throughput gain | 95% CI | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 32 | 343.97 | 359.51 | +4.52% | +2.93% to +6.13% | | 128 | 617.97 | 638.68 | +3.35% | +2.29% to +4.41% | | 512 | 860.21 | 868.15 | +0.92% | -1.47% to +3.36% | At c512, the interval includes small slowdowns and improvements: zero regression is not established. These points vary concurrency, not context length. Performance was measured before rebasing, with the same kernel fix; the newer build was revalidated for correctness, not rebenchmarked.
Benchmark methodology and versions Maximum context 163,840; 60 GiB KV cache/GPU; FlashInfer autotune off; AIperf 0.12.0; fresh server/cold prefix cache; no timed profiling. Request counts: 128/256/1,024; all 16,896 requests succeeded. Trace: `64k_400_90kv_agent_new_noschedule_short_15perc.jsonl`, filtered to input plus output lengths <=163,840. Model revision: `604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0`. Throughput: arithmetic means. Gains: paired log ratios averaged per node, with a t(2) interval over three node means. Output-token totals differ by <=0.147% within pairs. Benchmark upstream base: `f3b77eff640b5ed5cc9221a4f5f402ab65adc021`; patched source: `132c7f5fc41094d91aecb72cd03389326ff80431`.
### Correctness - **Four GPU tests passed, zero skips:** packed/padded/transposed LSE, singleton tokens, empty shards, and graph replay; packed/strided kernel outputs are bitwise-identical for identical inputs. - Latest DeepSeek rerun passed eager TP=2 and graph TP=2/8 numerical/path checks. Traces confirm direct kernels. Packed-copy/strided-P2P model controls produced identical saved outputs. - Additional models are being tested; current model-level evidence covers DeepSeek-V2-Lite only.
Test command and numerical limitations On at least four peer-access-capable H100 GPUs, with the patched build: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py \ --noconftest -k direct_a2a_matches_reference -v -s ``` `--noconftest` avoids unrelated dependencies. CI is configured for the two-rank cases on two H100s; four-rank cases passed locally. Upstream CI has not run for this branch. Lint, syntax, and `git diff --check` passed. Six prompts, 32 tokens each; comparable logprob bounds: 0.5 maximum / 0.1 per-prompt mean. First divergences require mutual top-five membership and greedy gap <=0.25; later, different contexts are not compared. This is not broad accuracy evaluation or bitwise NCCL/P2P equivalence. One default-scheduling comparison exceeded these bounds; unchanged reruns and fixed-scheduling controls passed. NCCL itself varied across runs, and its rejected output also exceeds the gap bound against packed-copy P2P. The precise cause remains unisolated; tolerances were not relaxed.
## Details FlashAttention MLA's `[heads, tokens]` LSE becomes a strided `[tokens, heads]` view after transpose. Reading both strides fixes addressing without adding copies, allocations, or synchronization. The receive buffer and combine kernel are unchanged. Output-layout/capacity restrictions and oversized-prefill fallback remain. This does **not** fix the separate GLM attention-output layout issue [#54305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54305). If [#54472](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54472) lands first, relax only its LSE guard for this newly supported layout. Related test-fixture/CI work: [#55492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55492); consolidate overlapping support changes if it lands first. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, validation. ---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Report NIXL submission failures and escalate persistent faults to session teardown
author: liranschour
body:
## Overview

This PR fixes two P2P data-plane failures and adds a reconnect backoff. Each part is its own commit (the backoff plus a follow-up that counts faults in its log, then a commit addressing review), so they can be reviewed, or split, independently:

1. **Submission failures are reported to the fetching peer** (fixes #60204). A NIXL error raised while submitting a fetch's WRITE escaped to the session dispatcher, so the peer waited its full 30 s load timeout before recomputing.
2. **Persistent NIXL faults end the session** (fixes #60205 together with #60279). A peer with a stale NIXL registration but a healthy control plane failed every WRITE for the rest of the process. This also answers @snadampal's review question on this PR about recovering the peer instead of fast-failing forever.
3. **Reconnect backoff.** A peer that faults again right after each re-handshake backs off before the next reconnect, as the NixlConnector does for invalid peers.

#61500 independently traces the same root cause in NIXL 1.5.0 for the NixlConnector's pull path: after one `REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, the UCX endpoint stays `FAILED` until the remote agent is re-added. Its production numbers show the before/after effect.

Replaces #55553 (closed in favour of this, by @Etelis). Together with #60279 it covers #55181.

## Claims

**Commit 1 (transfer scope)**
- An error from `make_prepped_xfer` / `transfer` takes the existing fail-fast path. The round fails, the peer gets `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)`, the store job fails at once, and the created handle is released.
- `transfer()` returning `"ERR"` (how the bindings report a failed post) is a failed submission. Previously it was ignored and the handle parked inflight.
- `on_fetch` no longer finalizes a round a second time after a failed submission. That raised `KeyError` in the store-first and finish-before-fetch orderings.

**Commit 2 (escalation)**
- `NixlTransport` classifies each NIXL failure in one place:
  - `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` / `nixlNotFoundError` fault the peer at once.
  - A `check_xfer_state` that raises faults the peer at once (commit 5). NIXL's binding raises for every error status (only `SUCCESS` / `IN_PROG` are returned), so a raise is how a failed WRITE is reported, e.g. `nixlBackendError` for a UCX error.
  - Any other failure (a failed submission, or a transfer in state `"ERR"`) is a strike, and 3 consecutive strikes with no success between them fault the peer. Strikes from one `poll()` batch are applied after the batch is classified, so a `DONE` for the peer anywhere in it counts as the success between (commit 5).
  - Only `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` ends a transfer whose state check raised. Any other raise keeps it inflight, because its WRITE may still be landing (#59790 measured bytes landing while the handle raised `nixlNotFoundError`); the peer fault and the drain cap below bound it.
  - The fault is reported through a new `PollResult.peer_fault`.
- After a fault, no new WRITE goes to that peer. Once its inflight WRITEs drain (capped at 10 s), the session sends `DisconnectMsg`. The existing reap then tears down both sides, and the next request re-registers them.
- Every session death records a reason, and the manager's `peer X down (<reason>)` log reports it. Examples: `data plane: NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, `protocol error: …`, `handshake timed out`, `lookup response timed out`, `control connection lost`.

**Commits 3–4 (reconnect backoff)**
- After reaping a session that ended on a data-plane fault, the faulting side records a per-peer backoff. The first fault reconnects at once. A repeat fault within 60 s of the previous wait expiring doubles the wait, from 1 s up to 60 s, as in the NixlConnector (#55471, #61500). Expiry is by time alone: no successful transfer is required, so a peer that is only idle for 60 s starts over at an immediate reconnect. Control-plane deaths don't back off.
- During the wait, outbound connects to the peer are skipped, so lookups fall back to local prefill. An inbound connect from the peer gets `DisconnectMsg` and is closed, so the peer falls back at once instead of waiting for its handshake deadline. There is no protocol change.
- The peer-down log carries a per-peer lifetime count of data-plane faults, e.g. `peer X down (data plane: …); data-plane fault #7; reconnect backoff 8s`. Unlike the backoff it never expires, so a peer that keeps faulting under traffic too sparse to escalate shows up as a rising count rather than as a series of unrelated faults.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ -q    # 308 passed (commit 1 alone: 281)
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ -q        # 554 passed, 12 skipped
pre-commit run --files <changed files>        # passed, incl. mypy
```

| Scenario | Before | After | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `transfer` / `make_prepped_xfer` raises, including when the release also fails | escapes to the dispatcher; no `TransferDoneMsg`; round stays alive | `None`, handle released, no inflight leak | `test_write_blocks_submission_exception_returns_failure` |
| `transfer()` returns `"ERR"` | handle parked inflight | `None`, handle released | `test_write_blocks_transfer_err_status_returns_failure` |
| Failed submit, store-first or finish-before-fetch | `KeyError` from double finalize | one finalize, one `TransferDoneMsg(False)` | `test_write_blocks_failure_finalizes_with_failure[*]`; fails without the `on_fetch` change |
| 3 failed WRITEs to a peer whose control plane is healthy (#60205) | every later WRITE fails, session never ends | peer faulted → drain → `DisconnectMsg` → reap | `TestNixlPeerFaults`, `TestPeerFaultEscalation` |
| `check_xfer_state` raises (`nixlBackendError`) while other WRITEs to the peer succeed | one strike, reset by the successes; transfer stays inflight for good: ~40 s consumer stall, pins and session held | peer faulted at once; transfer kept until it drains or the 10 s drain cap, then reaped | `test_raising_state_check_faults_the_peer_and_keeps_the_transfer`, `test_raise_faults_despite_a_success_in_the_batch` |
| `check_xfer_state` raises `nixlNotFoundError` | peer faulted; transfer kept, warning on every poll | peer faulted; transfer kept (not terminal, per #59790); warns once | `test_not_found_state_check_keeps_the_transfer`, `test_not_found_in_cancel_keeps_the_transfer`, `test_raising_state_check_warns_once` |
| strikes=2, one poll batch with `ERR` iterated before 3 `DONE`s | peer faulted, session torn down | strikes reset, no fault | `test_success_in_the_same_batch_prevents_the_fault`; fails on the previous code |
| Fault while WRITEs are inflight | — | new rounds fail fast; disconnect only after the drain or the 10 s cap | `test_fault_waits_for_inflight_then_disconnects`, `test_fault_disconnects_after_drain_deadline` |
| Peer faults again right after each re-handshake | reconnect, register and fail on every request | waits 0, 1, 2, 4 … 60 s; outbound skipped, inbound told to disconnect; resets 60 s after the last wait expires; the logged fault count keeps growing across the reset | `TestReconnectBackoff` |

**End to end on real NIXL** (two H200 pods, PDConnector + P2P tier, Llama-3.2-1B, NIXL 1.5.0, commit dc2d0b94fc). Happy path in both proxy modes: correct output and a 95–96 % external prefix-cache hit rate (240 of 254 prompt tokens pulled per request). A persistent fault was then forced with a test-only hook (not in this PR) that makes the prefiller's `transfer()` return `"ERR"` while a flag file exists:
- Every fetch failed fast: 20 consecutive requests finished in 1.6–2.3 s with correct output (recomputed locally), with no 30 s load timeout.
- Each 3 strikes ended the session: prefiller `peer D down (data plane: 3 consecutive transfer failures …); data-plane fault #1 … #6`, decoder `peer P down (peer disconnected)`; both sides re-registered on the next request.
- The backoff grew 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s; during the 8 s and 16 s waits the prefiller logged `rejecting inbound peer … (2.5s / 10.6s left)` and the decoder fell back at once.
- After the flag was cleared, hits returned (240/254) on the fresh session, with no crash, `KeyError` or segfault on either side.

**State-check faults, end to end** (same setup, commit a1cc819cb6). A second test-only hook makes the prefiller's `check_xfer_state` raise an exception named after the real binding class while a flag file exists. That is how NIXL 1.5.0 reports a failed WRITE: the binding raises for every error status.

| Injected fault | Faulted request | Prefiller log | After clearing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| every check raises `nixlBackendError` | 11.7–11.9 s, correct output (recomputed) | peer faulted on the first raise; `disconnecting once inflight transfers drain`; `peer D down (data plane: check_xfer_state raised nixlBackendError …)` exactly 10 s later; backoff 0, 1, 2 s over three faults | 240/254 hits |
| every check raises `nixlNotFoundError` | 11.6–11.8 s, correct output | peer faulted (`NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`); the transfer stays inflight (not terminal, per #59790) until the 10 s drain cap, then teardown | 256/256 hits |
| one transfer keeps raising while all others succeed | 12.2 s for that request; the next two 1.8 s with 240/254 hits | one fault, teardown at the 10 s cap, reconnect 6 s later | 256/256 hits |

- The last row is the case the previous revision left unbounded: its single strike was reset by the other successes, so the transfer stayed inflight for good, holding its pins and session. It is now torn down within the 10 s drain cap. Each faulted request costs the cap plus normal latency, versus an expected ~40 s (load timeout plus abort-ack timeout) before; that before-number was not measured.
- One `check_xfer_state failed` warning per transfer, not one per poll.
- One EngineCore per pod throughout; no crash, `KeyError` or segfault. Happy path afterwards in PD mode with the hook removed: 95.9 % hit rate.

These exercise faults that leave both processes alive. A genuinely restarted peer still can't be tested here: restarting either P2P peer segfaults the survivor in NIXL `loadRemoteMD`, a pre-existing problem (see #60205).

## Details

**Root cause (commit 1).** `_submit_transfer` fails fast only when `write_blocks` *returns* `None`. `NixlTransport.write_blocks` caught nothing, so a NIXL error reached `P2PSession._on_message`, which only logs. The dispatcher's disconnect-after-5-errors guard doesn't fire either, because successful messages in between reset its counter.

**Root cause (commit 2).** Only control-plane signals can mark a peer dead: heartbeat, protocol error, handshake, registration, and lookup timeout (#56836). Data-plane failures were never an input. In #60205 the heartbeats and lookups stay healthy while NIXL's endpoints for the peer are stale.

**Flow after a persistent fault (prefiller P writes into decoder D):**
1. D sends `FetchMsg`. P's `write_blocks` fails, or `check_xfer_state` raises in `poll`. The round fails with `TransferDone(False)` and D recomputes.
2. After 3 strikes, or one decisive error, P's `poll(D)` returns `peer_fault`. P's server role stops submitting, so later fetches from D fail fast.
3. Once P's inflight WRITEs to D drain, P sends `DisconnectMsg` and marks the connection dead with reason `data plane: …`.
4. P's manager reaps the session: it fails its jobs and calls `remove_remote_peer(D)`. D receives `DisconnectMsg` and runs the same reap for P.
5. D's next request opens a new connection, `ConnectMsg` goes both ways, and both sides register fresh. The registration generation keeps a late async registration from reviving the old peer.

**Design choice: one death path.** A data-plane fault ends a peer the same way a control-plane fault does. The transport never re-registers a peer in place. The alternative was `remove_remote_peer` after N failures, inside the transport. That tears down only one side: the session still believes the peer is registered, and the peer keeps *our* stale registration. It also cannot work for a restarted peer. Reusing the reap means no new teardown code.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- A `check_xfer_state` that raises with anything but `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` stays inflight, as #59790 established: it isn't provably terminal, and its WRITE may still be landing. It faults the peer at once, so the session's 10 s drain cap bounds how long it can last. The cost is that one failed state check tears down a peer that is otherwise working (a re-handshake, plus the backoff if it repeats). Treating `nixlBackendError` / `nixlCancelledError` as terminal (the UCX request finished with an error) would avoid the drain wait, but needs evidence that NIXL's UCX backend reports a handle's error only once all of its requests are done; left for a follow-up.
- The disconnect waits for inflight WRITEs because D frees their destination blocks on `DisconnectMsg`. The 10 s cap trades that guarantee for not hanging on a stuck transfer, the same exposure a heartbeat death has today.
- The thresholds (3 strikes, 10 s drain, 1→60 s backoff) are conservative constants, not measured values. The backoff uses the NixlConnector's numbers.
- The backoff forgets a peer by time, not by a successful transfer, matching the NixlConnector. Under sparse traffic a persistently broken peer therefore cycles at a 0 s backoff (3 fast-failing requests that recompute locally, plus one re-registration per cycle); the fault count in the log makes that visible. Requiring a success before forgetting would close the gap but needs a transport→manager success signal, and is better done for both connectors together.
- Only the faulting side knows about the backoff. During the wait, the other peer still tries to connect on each new request and is turned away within one round trip; concurrent requests share the pending attempt. A retry-after hint in `DisconnectMsg` would remove that, at the cost of a protocol change.

**Relation to other PRs.**
- #59790 (merged) provides the sibling drain before `TransferDone(False)`; this PR builds on it.
- #60279 (narrowed to `remove_remote_peer` teardown robustness) is complementary. Expect a one-line conflict in `remove_remote_peer` for whichever lands second.
- #61500 (NixlConnector, pull mode) releases a peer after a failed read, with the same backoff. It touches no shared code. That connector's teardown is one-sided because only the decoder holds the remote registration; P2P registers both ways, so here both sides tear down.
- #49632 marks any `check_xfer_state` raise as failed and releases the handle, which can free a handle whose WRITE is still landing. Here such a transfer stays inflight and is bounded by the escalation instead.

**Changes since the previous revision.**
- Rebased onto main, which now includes #59790, #56836 and #58168.
- Dropped the `try/except` around `write_blocks` in `_submit_transfer`, and its test. The contract, now documented in `data/base.py`, is that transports don't raise for NIXL errors.
- Added commits 2–5. Commit 4 adds the per-peer fault count to the peer-down log and corrects the description of when the backoff resets (time since the last wait expired, not time healthy); behaviour is unchanged. Commit 5 addresses review of `poll()`: strikes per batch, and any raising state check faults the peer (`NOT_FOUND` is deliberately not terminal; see the review thread).
- About 330 source lines are added, comments and docstrings included: roughly 30 in commit 1, 190 in commit 2, 60 in commit 3, 20 in commit 4 and 30 in commit 5. Each commit stands alone, so the PR can be split along those lines if reviewers prefer.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] RDNA3 W4A16 MoE: handle the N-first CT weight layout
author: JartX
body:
## Purpose

#52798 ("Use canonical N-first weight format for CT WNA16 MoE", merged
September 28) changed the layout compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE weights reach
the backends in, but the RDNA3 (gfx1100) path was not updated. Since then any
compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE checkpoint fails on RDNA3 at the first forward,
with an assertion on `w1_zp` in the experts.

Two things broke:

- `_process_weights_rdna3` still read the weights as K-first
  (`[E, K // 8, N]`, scales `[E, groups, N]`), which is what
  `moe_gptq_gemm_rdna3` needs, but they now arrive N-first
  (`[E, N, K // 8]`, scales `[E, N, groups]`).
- `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod` registered the synthesized zero points
  only for the CPU backend. The RDNA3 kernel needs them too, even for
  symmetric checkpoints (the oracle synthesizes them), so `w13/w2_qzeros`
  never reached the layer.

## What changes

- `oracle/int_wna16.py`: `_process_weights_rdna3` transposes weights and
  scales to the kernel's K-first layout before the exllama shuffle.
- `compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py`: register the synthesized zero points
  for `WNA16MoEBackend.RDNA3` as well as CPU.

Nothing changes for other backends.

## Not a duplicate

`upstream/main` (df417f780a) still has the K-first read. I searched open PRs
for `rdna3 moe`, `rdna3 w4a16`, `gfx1100 moe`, `moe_gptq_gemm_rdna3`,
`rdna3 compressed-tensors` and `52798`. The only open PR touching
`int_wna16.py` for RDNA3 is #59783, which adds a group-size check in backend
selection and does not touch weight processing.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py -v
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

- [x] A regression test, `test_process_weights_from_compressed_tensors_layout`:
  it builds weights the way compressed-tensors hands them to the oracle
  (N-first, packed `[E, N, K // 8]`, scales `[E, N, groups]`), runs them
  through `_process_weights_rdna3` and a full MoE forward (w1, SiLU, w2,
  top-k reduce), and compares with a dequantized PyTorch reference. The
  existing tests build the kernel's K-first layout directly and call the op,
  so they never exercised weight processing, which is why this regression
  went unnoticed.
- [x] End to end on 4x RX 7900 XTX with a symmetric compressed-tensors
  checkpoint (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B GPTQ W4A16, g32, `pack-quantized`): fails on
  `main` without this change, starts and passes GSM8K with it (below).

## Test results

On gfx1100, in an image built from `main` (df417f780a):

- Without this change, the new test fails for fp16 and bf16: the kernel
  rejects the weights (`group size (K/groups = 1) must be a multiple of 32`),
  because it reads N-first data as K-first.
- With this change (its `int_wna16.py` applied on the same `main` and mounted
  into that image; the C++ kernel is unchanged): the new test passes, and `test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py` passes
  in full (99 passed).
- pre-commit passes, except `update-dockerfile-graph`, which needs
  `/bin/bash` and could not run on my machine.

End to end, on an image built from `main` (df417f780a) for gfx1100, 4x RX
7900 XTX, TP4, `--dtype float16`, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B GPTQ W4A16 g32 (symmetric,
compressed-tensors):

- Without this change the engine fails at the first forward:
  `assert self.w1_zp is not None and self.w2_zp is not None`.
- With this change it selects `Rdna3WNA16Experts`, starts, and scores 97.5% on
  GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --num-questions 200
  --temperature 0.6 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 2048`, 5-shot, 0% invalid).

The two files of this change were mounted over that image; the C++ kernel is
unchanged. The stock RCCL in the image could not set up P2P between these
GPUs, so it was rebuilt; this is unrelated to this PR.

## AI assistance

I used AI assistance to find the cause and write this change. I have
reviewed every changed line and will run the tests above before marking it
ready.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep MLA derived weights in place on weight reload
author: mawong-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With CUDA graphs on, `sleep(level=2)` + `reload_weights` (or any in-place weight update) corrupts MLA output in two configurations: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, where output turns to garbage, and DCP query replication (`dcp_q_replicate`), where output degrades silently. The cause is the same in both. `MLAAttention.process_weights_after_loading` rebinds derived weights to new tensors: the AITER BMM weights `W_K`/`W_K_scale`/`W_V`/`W_V_scale`, and the DCP gather `W_UK_T_dcp_qrep`. Captured graphs then keep reading the old storage. This PR copies them in place with `replace_parameter(..., prefer_copy=True)`, as the default branch already does for `W_UV`/`W_UK_T`.

## Claims

- Fixes both AITER BMM branches, FP8 (gfx942) and MXFP4 (gfx950), and DCP query replication. The DCP fix applies to every DCP-capable MLA backend.
- `test_reload_weights` now fails if any module's device tensor moves across a reload, and runs with AITER on ROCm. This catches this bug class generically, not just these four tensors.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, CUDA graphs, 2 cycles of level-1 full, level-1 selective, and level-2 + `reload_weights`:

| GPU (branch) | TP | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| MI300X (FP8) | 1, 2 | garbage after level 2 (`" Paris.\ntopNavRename to topNavRename…"`); `W_K` address changes | sane on every wake; `W_K` address unchanged |
| MI355X (MXFP4) | 1, 2 | garbage after level 2, then `" Paris."` only | sane on every wake; `W_K` address unchanged |
| MI300X, TRITON_MLA, DCP 2 + `dcp_q_replicate` | 2 | all 8 outputs change after level 2 and stay changed (`"Paris, the capital city of France, Paris is the capital city of the the – well, you know."`); `W_UK_T_dcp_qrep` moves in all 27 layers on both ranks | matches pre-sleep output; nothing moves |

`enforce_eager` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0` were already unaffected.

`pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "test_reload_weights and DeepSeek"`: without the fix, the AITER variants fail on both GPUs with `[['…mla_attn.W_K', '…W_K_scale', '…W_V', '…W_V_scale']] == [[]]`. With the fix, every case passes. The existing perplexity check alone passed even without the fix, because the debug checkpoints evidently don't change the attention weights, so stale storage still held usable values.

## Details

`reload_weights` restores a layer's registered parameters and reruns `process_weights_after_loading`. `prefer_copy` then writes into the restored storage. Plain attributes aren't tracked, so they were reallocated on every reload. As with `W_UV`/`W_UK_T`, these tensors are now registered parameters: they appear in `named_parameters()` and in the reload "not loaded from checkpoint" warning. The new check in `test_reload_weights` would flag the DCP case too, but the DCP configuration isn't part of that test (it needs TP ≥ 2), so it was validated manually as above.

title: [Bugfix][Quant] Read safetensors headers of checkpoints with other file names
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Summary

A GPTQ checkpoint whose weights are not named `model.safetensors` fails to load whenever they are not already in the local cache, because the lookup that decides which layers are quantized cannot see the file and every linear layer is then built unquantized.

Failure in CI: [build 93298](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93298/list?jid=01a11652-3695-4590-86b6-eda1b6ced9ea&tab=output)

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.qweight'
in LlamaModel. The available parameters belonging to layers.0.mlp.down_proj
(RowParallelLinear) are: {'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight'}
```

## Cause

`modules_in_block_to_quantize` is optional, and older GPTQ checkpoints do not carry it, so `AutoGPTQConfig.maybe_update_config` derives the list from the safetensors headers. That goes through `HfApi.get_safetensors_metadata`, which asks for two fixed names only, `model.safetensors` and its index.

`LnL-AI/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-GPTQ-4bit` stores its weights in `gptq_model-4bit-128g.safetensors`, so the call always raises `NotASafetensorsRepoError`. That error is fatal, so it is raised without a log line and swallowed, which is why nothing shows up in the logs. The only remaining fallback reads the local cache, where files are matched by `*.safetensors` and the odd name is found, so a warm cache is the only reason this ever worked.

AWQ handles the same checkpoint shape correctly because it derives the complement, so an empty answer excludes nothing instead of excluding everything.

Nothing changed in `safetensors` or `huggingface_hub`. The local cache fallback added in #43197 has been masking it since, and this checkpoint only entered the test in #54809, so CI has only ever met it through a warm shared cache.

## Fix

When the fixed-name lookup fails, list the files the repo actually has and read the headers of every `*.safetensors` among them, the way the weight loader already locates weights. Only headers are fetched.

An empty module list now also means "unknown" rather than "nothing is quantized", so a machine with no network at all still loads the checkpoint. This is reachable only for GPTQ checkpoints without the field, and only when no metadata can be read by any route.

## Validation

Cold cache, the test that fails in CI: `1 failed in 21.16s` before, `1 passed in 52.56s` after. With the metadata forced empty, standing in for a machine with no network: `1 failed in 16.30s` before, `1 passed in 48.32s` after. Cold cache, both `test_quantization` parameters plus `quantization/test_auto_gptq.py`: `10 passed in 105.78s`.

title: [Bugfix] Don't warn about missing watermark config for default requests
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

Since #56801, every engine started without `--watermark-config` logs "Watermarking is enabled for this request, but the engine has no watermark configuration..." on its first request, although nothing asked for watermarking ([reported here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56801#issuecomment-6032728937)). This PR keeps that warning only for requests that set `watermarking=True`.

## Claims

- On an engine without a watermark config, default requests (`watermarking` unset) no longer log the warning.
- `watermarking=True` on such an engine still warns once and runs without a watermark.
- The greedy, beam search, and trace replay fallback warnings on engines with a watermark config are unchanged.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/watermarking/` (1x H200): 184 passed, 3 skipped (the skipped tests need 2 GPUs). `tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py`, `tests/test_sampling_params.py` and `tests/v1/engine/test_input_processor_trace_replay.py`: 82 passed.
- CI: `tests/watermarking` already runs in the "(CPU) V1 Others" Buildkite step, which triggers on `vllm/config/`.
- With the old condition restored, the updated `test_requests_without_engine_config_are_unwatermarked` fails for all 3 of its cases.
- Offline `LLM.generate` with Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and no watermark config. Before (main c83935b300): one warning on the first default request. After: no warning for default sampling, default greedy, or `watermarking=False`. One warning for `watermarking=True`.
- `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` plus `/v1/completions`. Before (merged #56801 code, same condition as main): one warning after a default request. After: none for a default request, one for `"watermarking": true`.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

Root cause: the branch of `VllmConfig._check_supports_watermarking` for engines without a watermark config tested `config.watermarking is not False`, so the default `None` also warned. It now tests `is True`. The docs already say watermarking is disabled when `--watermark-config` is omitted, so no docs change is needed.

The test changes update the two assertions that expected a warning for default requests on an engine without a config. They also add a plain `SamplingParams()` case to the existing test for such requests.

The Rust frontend sets `watermarking=true` before the engine and does not go through this check, so it is unaffected.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Drop the unaccounted, write-only prefill mirror staging buffer
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

`initialize_hisparse_runtime_buffers` allocates a per-layer prefill mirror staging buffer (`num_layers × max_num_batched_tokens × row_bytes`) after the KV cache is sized, so memory profiling never counts it. That's about 0.69 GiB per GPU for GLM-5.3 (78 layers).

Nothing reads it: `HiSparseConnectorWorker.start_step` sets `mirror_from_resident = True` every step, so the host mirror always copies from the resident cache, and only dummy batches ever wrote the buffer. This PR removes it, along with `mirror_write_target` and `mirror_from_resident`.

Related: #60420.

## Test Plan / Result

1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 8 layers with dummy weights, MNBT 16384, HiSparse with `host_pool_gib=24`. Measured persistent torch memory after init, excluding weights and KV:

| | allocated beyond weights + KV | KV budget |
|---|---|---|
| no HiSparse | 0.7031 GiB | 112.99 GiB |
| HiSparse, main | 0.7756 GiB | 112.96 GiB |
| HiSparse, this PR | 0.7052 GiB | 112.96 GiB |

- Greedy outputs are identical on main and this PR (4 prompts, 300–7000 tokens).
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k "hisparse or profiling"`: 10 passed. The CUDA-only kv-update test now asserts only the resident write.

title: [Bugfix] Fall back from DeepGEMM when nvcc is older than 12.9
author: ilyas-mallah
body:
## Overview

DeepGEMM compiles its kernels at runtime and aborts the engine when nvcc is missing or older than 12.9. vLLM only checks the GPU architecture and that DeepGEMM is installed, so on Hopper with an older toolkit, block-FP8 models crash on load. This PR adds the nvcc check, so vLLM warns and falls back to its other FP8 kernels. To find nvcc, it reuses FlashInfer's existing lookup, moved unchanged to `find_nvcc()` in `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py`.

## Claims

- Block-FP8 models load on Hopper with nvcc 12.8 or no nvcc, instead of aborting with `NVCC version must be at least 12.9`.
- The fallback logs one warning naming the nvcc version it found and where it looked.
- No change when nvcc is 12.9 or newer, or with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`.
- No change to FlashInfer: `has_flashinfer` finds the same nvcc as before, and its existing tests pass unchanged apart from the patched module.

## Validation

H100 NVL, CUDA 12.8.1 toolkit (`nvcc` 12.8), driver for CUDA 13, vLLM `528772a4b` (precompiled; `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` is identical on current main), `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8`, offline `LLM.generate` with two prompts:

| | kernel selected | result |
|---|---|---|
| main | `FlashInferFp8DeepGEMMDynamicBlockScaledKernel` | `RuntimeError: ... NVCC version must be at least 12.9`, then `Engine core initialization failed` |
| this PR | `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` | warning below, then `'The capital of France is' -> ' Paris. ...'` |

```
WARNING DeepGEMM kernels are disabled: its JIT needs nvcc 12.9 or newer (DG_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER, CUDA_HOME,
CUDA_PATH, PATH or /usr/local/cuda), found 12.8. Set CUDA_HOME to a newer CUDA toolkit.
```

`pytest tests/utils_/test_deep_gemm_utils.py tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py`: 7/7 (nvcc 12.8, 12.9 and 13.0; missing nvcc; the `DG_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER` override; FlashInfer's existing lookup tests against the shared helper).

## Details

The check finds nvcc the way DeepGEMM's JIT does (`DG_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER` or `DJ_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER`, then `CUDA_HOME`, `CUDA_PATH`, `nvcc` on `PATH`, then `/usr/local/cuda`). After the override, that is the lookup FlashInfer already had, which is why the two now share `find_nvcc()`. The check runs once, since `is_deep_gemm_supported` is cached. A fallback instead of an error matches how vLLM already handles an unsupported GPU or a missing DeepGEMM package. The cost is speed, which the warning states. On Hopper the fallback is the CUTLASS block-FP8 path.

#49051 proposed a similar check and was closed in favor of the JIT warmup RFC #47456, which does not cover the toolchain. Unlike #49051, a missing nvcc also disables DeepGEMM here, because DeepJIT has no NVRTC path: it asserts that nvcc is executable and at least 12.9 (`include/deep_jit/backend/cuda/backend.hpp` at the pinned DeepGEMM).

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Remove invalid NC from Kimi-K3 KDA autotune keys
author: warrendeng
body:
## Overview

Both AMD and NVIDIA Kimi-K3 KDA kernels list `NC` in their autotune keys even though they have no `NC` argument. Older Triton ignored this unused entry but Triton 3.9 rejects it at import so this PR removes `NC` from both copies (fixes [test-infra #9028](https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/9028)).

## Claims

- AMD and NVIDIA KDA modules import with Triton 3.9, without changing kernel computation or the effective autotune key used by older Triton.

## Validation

  - With `torch==2.15.0+cu130` and `triton==3.9.0`, unchanged `main` (`a8260cbc5c`) fails during KDA test collection with `ValueError: key contains names that are not kernel arguments: NC`. Importing the NVIDIA copy separately fails the same way.
  - With the fix, both modules import, and `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only -q tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py` collects 102 tests. Local `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
  - On an AMD MI350 (`gfx950`), compared Triton-ROCm `3.8.0+git10f6be36` and `3.9.0+gitaad2a60d` with the same Torch build, GPU, inputs, and vLLM sources. The unpatched AMD and NVIDIA modules both fail to import on 3.9; both import with this fix. Both versions import on 3.8.
  - Ran the actual vendored AMD `chunk_kda_fwd_intra(safe_gate=True)` kernels on MI350. For a synthetic BF16 input (`B=1, T=1024, H=HV=12, K=128`, chunk size 64), the defined outputs on patched 3.9 were bit-identical to unpatched 3.8. A ragged input with sequence lengths `[63, 73]` also matched within `rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-6`

## Details

[Triton #11602](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11602) added validation of autotune key names. `NC = ceil(BT / BC)` is computed for the launch grid, not passed to the decorated kernel. The KDA test imports the AMD vendored copy first, masking the same bug in the NVIDIA copy.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Size the permute scratch from its inputs
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Stop predicting the MoE permute scratch capacity from `FusedMoEConfig`; size it from the inputs it actually receives, growing until the workspace manager is locked. This is intended as the root fix behind #55105 (DeepEP v2 + sequence parallelism) and #60423 (PCP), which each patch a different term of the same capacity formula for the `assert n_token <= self.max_num_tokens` failure in the Humming grouped path.

## Claims

- The Humming grouped experts no longer derive a row bound from `max_num_tokens * dp_size * experts_per_token`, so DP, sequence parallelism, PCP, and DeepEP v2's power-of-two receive buckets cannot make the scratch too small.
- The scratch no longer has a hidden-state buffer or dtype, which removes the `hidden_states.dtype == self.hidden_dtype` mismatch on the prequantized (block-FP8 activation) path.
- `CutlassExpertsFp8` and the CUTLASS W4A8 experts get the same behavior. They sized the scratch with `max_num_tokens` and no `dp_size` factor.
- One scratch is shared per `(num_experts, num_local_experts, device)` instead of one per `(capacity, topk, hidden size, dtype)`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "permute or humming or cutlass or block_fp8"` (1x B300) | 906 passed (with `tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py` and `-k "permute or humming or cutlass"`) |
| GSM8K, `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, `--moe-backend humming`, `VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped_contiguous`, 1x B300, eager (existing `configs/humming/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-humming.yaml`) | 0.8817 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| GSM8K, same model, DP=2 + EP, `allgather_reducescatter`, CUDA graphs, `--max-num-batched-tokens 3000` | 0.8969 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "test_reload_weights and FP8_DYNAMIC"` (1x B300, `VLLM_CUTLASS` FP8 backend, in-place weight reload) | 1 passed, 1 skipped; failed in CI before the shared-scratch fix |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PCP on 8x H20 (SM90), run by @wangyicong52 (results in #59857) | reported working; #60423 closed in favor of this PR |
| pre-commit on changed files, `mypy-3.12` | passed |

Not validated:

- The DeepEP v2 topology from #55105 is not reproduced here: DeepEP v2 is unavailable on the test machine (NCCL 2.29.7 < 2.30.4). @elvircrn, could you try this branch on your setup?
- The prequantized Humming grouped path (block-FP8 activations before dispatch) was not run with real kernels; in-tree coverage of `HummingGroupedExperts.apply` is mock-based. It is guarded by dtype and shape assertions.

## Details

**Root cause.** `workspace13`/`workspace2` are sized from the actual `M` and grow until `lock_workspace()`. `MoEPermuteScratch` was instead sized up front from config, which requires knowing how many rows every prepare/finalize backend can return in every topology. That bound is a property of the dispatcher, not of the experts, and it has been wrong for PCP, for DeepEP v2 with non-power-of-two capacities, and for CUTLASS with DP.

**Change.**

- `MoEPermuteScratch` holds only index metadata and gains `reserve(expanded_rows)`. It reallocates while the workspace manager is unlocked and raises `Scratch growth is not allowed after locking` afterwards, matching the shared workspace's contract.
- Permuted hidden states come from the caller's workspace. CUTLASS already passed a `workspace2` slice. Humming's prequantized path now writes into `quanted_gate_up_input`, which is allocated with the right shape and dtype and is otherwise unused when w13 quantization is skipped, so this costs no extra memory.
- The index buffers stay a persistent resource rather than moving into `get_simultaneous`: a second `get_simultaneous` call inside `apply()` would alias the live `workspace13`/`workspace2`, and `token_expert_indices` is an `arange` that would otherwise be refilled every call. They are small (seven int32 arrays over the expanded rows plus the sort workspace).

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- A runtime shape larger than anything seen during warmup still fails, with the same contract and at the same point as `workspace13`.
- `moe_permute(scratch=...)` without `permuted_hidden_states` now allocates that tensor per call. Both in-tree callers pass a buffer; `benchmark_moe_permute_unpermute.py`'s scratch numbers are not comparable to earlier ones.
- `get_persistent_resource`'s docstring is loosened from "must not resize" to "must not resize once the manager is locked".
- The CUTLASS experts use the same shared scratch as Humming. A scratch owned by the experts instance broke weight reload: the experts are rebuilt after the workspace is locked, so the new scratch was empty and could not grow (caught by `test_reload_weights` in CI build 93385).
- Anything that first reaches a scratch-using path after the lock, without that path having run during warmup, now fails where the old fixed-size scratch would have allocated lazily.

**Relation to open PRs.** Not a duplicate: #55105 and #60423 extend the capacity formula for one topology each and conflict with each other; this removes the formula. The DeepEP v2 handle-capacity change in #55105 (`next_power_of_2(ceil(max_num_tokens / sp_size))`) is independent and still useful. Searches for `MoEPermuteScratch` and `permute scratch workspace` found no other open PR.

AI assistance was used to analyze the capacity mismatch, implement the change, and run the validation above.

title: [WideEP] Explain how to fix a too-old NCCL for DeepEP v2
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Make a too-old NCCL for DeepEP v2 self-explanatory on pip/uv installs. PyTorch pins an NCCL older than the 2.30.4 that `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` needs (PyTorch 2.13 pins `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`). The Docker images override it since #45321, but installs outside the images fail with a message that states the requirement and not the fix. This does not change any dependency.

## Claims

- The startup log line and the `DeepEPV2All2AllManager` assertion now name the cause and the upgrade command for the installed CUDA major.
- `tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh` warns, before and after the build output, when the installed NCCL is too old for DeepEP v2. It does not fail, so DeepEP v1 builds are unaffected.
- `tools/ep_kernels/README.md` reflects the current PyTorch pin, explains that later `uv pip install` runs restore it without `UV_OVERRIDE`, and that DeepEP must be rebuilt after upgrading NCCL.

## Validation

On an environment with torch 2.13.0, `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`, and DeepEP 2.0.0:

```console
$ python -c "from vllm.utils.import_utils import deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason as r; print(r())"
DeepEP v2 requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 but found 2.29.7. PyTorch pins an older NCCL; upgrade it with `pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps` and rebuild DeepEP against it. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md.
```

The NCCL check from the install script, run in isolation against the same environment:

```console
WARNING: nvidia-nccl-cu13 2.29.7 is installed, but the deepep_v2 backend
requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 when DeepEP is built and when it runs. To use deepep_v2, run
    uv pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps
and then run this script again. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md.
```

pre-commit (including shellcheck and markdownlint) and `mypy-3.12` pass on the changed files.

Not validated: the full install script was not re-run end to end, the Docker build was not run (it sets `UV_OVERRIDE`, so the warning should not trigger there), and the available path (NCCL >= 2.30.4) was not exercised on a real environment. No tests were added; the change is message text plus a shell warning.

## Details

`has_deep_ep_v2()` now delegates to a new `deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason()`, so the log line and the assertion share one message. One behavior difference: an environment with a pre-v2 DeepEP installed now also gets the one-time INFO line saying `deepep_v2` is unavailable.

The alternative of forcing a newer NCCL through `[tool.uv] override-dependencies` in `pyproject.toml` was left out on purpose to avoid changing dependencies.

Not a duplicate: searches for `deepep_v2 NCCL` and `nccl install_python_libraries` found no open PR addressing this.

title: [Bugfix] Close MessageQueue zmq resources via finalizer to avoid exit
author: aarushjain29
body:
## Purpose

Fixes an intermittent hang where a spawned EngineCore never exits after a startup failure, timing out `tests/v1/shutdown/test_startup_error.py::test_async_llm_startup_error[forward-2-...]` (seen on AMD CI in `Distributed Torchrun + Shutdown`, which runs with `spawn`). Related: #60121, #60141.

### Root cause

Each `MessageQueue` owns a private zmq `Context` and sockets that are never closed explicitly. After a failed `collective_rpc`, the executor's response `MessageQueue` is only reachable through a reference cycle (`FutureWrapper` → exception → traceback → `collective_rpc` / `get_response` frames → `response_mqs`), so it is freed by the cyclic GC.

When the context and its sockets are collected in the same GC pass, CPython clears the context's weak socket references first. pyzmq's `Context.__del__` → `destroy()` then closes nothing, and `term()` blocks forever on the still-open sockets. pyzmq only skips this after its own atexit hook runs, so the hang occurs when GC triggers inside an earlier atexit hook (e.g. `ray.shutdown`, which lazily imports `ray.dag`).

Evidence:
- Captured stacks of real hangs: `term` ← `destroy` ← `Context.__del__` during GC inside `ray.shutdown`.
- Tracing every engine-process zmq context over 46 runs: the response queue's context (`create_from_handle`) was freed by cyclic GC in exactly the 2 runs that hung, and was not freed or was freed by refcount in the 44 that passed.
- A minimal pure-pyzmq repro (context and socket in a cycle, `gc.collect()`) hangs every time, even with `LINGER=0`, and does not hang without the cycle.

## Fix

Register a `weakref.finalize` per `MessageQueue` that holds the context and sockets, closes the sockets with `linger=0`, then terminates the context.
- The context can no longer be collected as garbage, so the deadlocking `Context.__del__` path is unreachable.
- The finalizer only runs once the queue is unreachable, so no other thread can be using its sockets.
- `atexit = False` keeps exit-time behavior unchanged for queues still alive at shutdown.

## Test Plan

- New `test_reader_in_reference_cycle_is_collected_without_blocking` in `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`.
- `pytest tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`
- Loop the startup-error test with `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` on MI300X.

## Test Result

- New test fails on main (GC blocks) and passes with this change; full `test_shm_broadcast.py`: 31 passed.
- Startup-error test with spawn on MI300X (TP=2, CPU limited to match CI): **10 hangs in 544 runs before → 0 hangs in 298 runs after** (expected about 5.5 at the baseline rate).
- pre-commit passes.

title: [Bugfix] DSA: all-reduce partial hidden_states before PP send
author: SumanthRH
body:
## Overview

Fixes wrong activations at every pipeline-parallel stage boundary for DSA models (`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/{nvidia,amd}/model.py`, which serves DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x) when TP > 1. The last layer's un-reduced MLP/MoE output is now all-reduced into the residual before the PP send.

Separate from, and complementary to, #59961 (stage-local shared indexer top-k).

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 BF16 with TP8PP2 now matches TP16 on GSM8K accuracy and on output length. Without this fix, it loses 7–9 points and generates about 7.6× more tokens.
- No extra all-reduce: it moves from the receiving stage to the sending stage, and `residual` is no longer sent. There is no change when PP = 1.

## Validation

All runs use GLM-5.3 BF16 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16`) on 2 nodes × 8 B200 with the default 39/39 layer split. Every TP8PP2 row also includes the #59961 top-k fix, so this PR's effect is isolated. The TP8PP2 runs used vLLM 0.30.0 with an earlier, numerically equivalent variant of this fix (`residual += all_reduce(hidden_states)`, then send zeros as `hidden_states`). The changed model files are unchanged between 0.30.0 and current `main`, apart from this diff.

**GSM8K.** `lm_eval` 0.4.13 against `vllm serve`, first 100 test examples, zero-shot, greedy, `max_gen_toks=16384`. The prompt and filters are from `gsm8k_cot_llama`, with no stop strings so the reasoning isn't cut off. Generated-token counts come from the server's `/metrics`.

| Layout | strict-match | flexible-extract | Mean generated tokens | Hit 16k cap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP16 (reference) | 0.94 ± 0.024 | 0.94 ± 0.024 | 224 | 0 |
| TP8PP2 + #59961 | 0.87 ± 0.034 | 0.85 ± 0.036 | 1,707 | 7 |
| TP8PP2 + #59961 + **this PR** | **0.95 ± 0.022** | **0.95 ± 0.022** | **225** | **0** |

With the fix, total generated tokens are 22,461, against 22,446 for TP16.

**Long-form sampling.** `LLM.generate` on 128 reasoning prompts, temperature 1.0, fixed seeds, `max_tokens=8192`.

| Layout | Capped at 8192 | Mean output tokens | >10% repeated 16-grams | Multiple `</think>` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP16 (reference) | 37% | 4,638 | 3 | 0 |
| TP8PP2 + #59961 | 78% | 7,055 | 17 | 6 |
| TP8PP2 + #59961 + **this PR** | 41% | 4,687 | 3 | 0 |

<details>
<summary>GSM8K reproduction</summary>

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray --reasoning-parser glm47 --served-model-name glm

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=glm,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=100,tokenized_requests=False \
  --apply_chat_template --include_path <dir with gsm8k_glm.yaml> --tasks gsm8k_glm --limit 100
```

`gsm8k_glm.yaml` is `gsm8k_cot_llama` with `until: []`, `do_sample: false`, and `max_gen_toks: 16384`.
</details>

`test_pp_stage_sends_tp_reduced_residual_stream` checks that a middle PP stage sends only the TP-reduced residual stream. A tiny-model PP-vs-TP comparison (`tiny-random/glm-5.2` in `tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py`) can't catch this bug, since with dummy weights it passes with or without the fix.

The AMD path gets the same change but this was not tested on ROCm.

## Details

**Root cause.** DSA decoder layers run MLP/MoE with `reduce_results=False`, and the TP all-reduce happens inside the next layer's `fused_allreduce_rms_norm`. The last layer on a non-final PP stage therefore returns `hidden_states` that are a per-TP-rank partial sum. `gpu_worker` sends `IntermediateTensors` with `all_gather_group=get_tp_group()`, which assumes the tensors are identical on every TP rank. TP rank `r` sends only `tensor.reshape(tp, -1)[r]`, and the receiver all-gathers (`isend_tensor_dict` / `irecv_tensor_dict`). With partial sums, the receiver ends up with token chunk `r` holding rank `r`'s partial sum. It then all-reduces again, so chunk `r` becomes `tp × partial_r` instead of `Σ_r partial_r`.

**Fix.** The sending stage sends only `residual + all_reduce(hidden_states)`, which is replicated across TP, so the sliced send stays valid. The receiving stage starts with `residual = None`, so its first layer applies a plain RMSNorm, as it does on the embedding. This matches the old receiver math `fused_allreduce_rms_norm(all_reduce(hidden_states), residual)`.

**Tradeoffs.** The all-reduce moves from the receiving stage to the sending stage, and `residual` is no longer sent, so PP traffic per boundary halves.

**Symptom.** The output stays fluent, so the bug is easy to miss. It shows up as much longer reasoning, repetition loops, and repeated `</think>`.

title: [Bugfix] Keep GPTQ linear layers batch invariant
author: yifanFengg
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` still runs the Marlin GEMM. Marlin picks its tiling and K-split from the number of tokens, so the reduction order changes with the batch size and the logprobs depend on the batch.

This PR makes the GPTQ path use `matmul_batch_invariant` directly: in batch-invariant mode it skips the Marlin kernel selection and repacking, keeps the checkpoint layout in memory, and unpacks the weight in `apply()`.

(The matching AWQ change was part of this PR until 2026-10-19 and was dropped: on current `main` the AWQ fallback is already batch invariant through #52231, which overrides `aten::mm.out`/`aten::addmm.out`; #60013, which this PR deferred to, was closed for the same reason.)

## Claims

- On `main`, `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` fails for `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4` (14 of 22 ids). With this PR all 22 ids pass.
- Accuracy is unchanged: `lm_eval` gsm8k on the batch-invariant path matches the Marlin path within noise, and the top-1 tokens of the two GPTQ paths agree on a fixed prompt set.
- Without `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` nothing changes: the same Marlin kernel is selected.
- Throughput in batch-invariant mode is lower than on `main` (numbers below): the GPTQ weight is dequantized on every forward and the model uses the batch-invariant Triton matmul instead of Marlin.
- New unit test checks the GPTQ unpack against vLLM's reference packer bit for bit.


## Details

**Root cause.** `vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py` overrides `aten::mm`/`aten::matmul` through `torch.library` and exposes `matmul_batch_invariant` for callers; linear methods that run their own kernels have to opt in. `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` never did: it always builds a Marlin `MPLinearKernel`. The same pattern is why `UnquantizedLinearMethod` calls `linear_batch_invariant` explicitly.

**Change.**
- `auto_gptq.py`: with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` skips `verify_marlin_supported` / `choose_mp_linear_kernel`, leaves `qweight`/`scales`/`qzeros` in the checkpoint layout, and `apply()` unpacks the weight (`(q - bias) * scale` in the scales dtype, the same arithmetic as the Marlin dequantization) and calls `matmul_batch_invariant`. Without the flag the code path is unchanged.
- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_gptq.py`: `_dequantize_gptq_weight` is compared bit for bit against `gptq_quantize_weights` + `gptq_pack` for 4/8 bit, group sizes -1/32/128, fp16/bf16.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- The GPTQ weight is unpacked on every forward in batch-invariant mode, and the model runs the batch-invariant Triton matmul instead of Marlin. On the A10 this costs throughput in batch-invariant mode (blocks in section 6): the decode-heavy benchmark takes about 2.5x longer than `main`'s non-invariant Marlin path, the prefill-heavy one about 1.4x. Keeping a dequantized copy would be faster but would need the memory of the unquantized model, which is usually why a GPTQ checkpoint is used. A fused batch-invariant W4A16 Triton kernel would remove the cost; I kept that out of this PR.
- Only symmetric GPTQ without act-order is covered, which is what `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` supports today (`desc_act=True` is rejected at config time).
- `AutoGPTQMoEMethod` (GPTQ MoE experts) still uses Marlin MoE and is not batch invariant; #46639 covers that kernel. (The compressed-tensors wNa16 dense scheme was fixed separately in #60524.) This PR covers the dense GPTQ path that was tested.
