title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Declare 64-token kernel blocks for SM120 sparse backends
author: xzwgit
body:
### Summary
On SM120, the DSV41 sparse-MLA backends declare only `[128]`-token kernel blocks (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` returns `[64 if family(90) else 128]` / `[128]`), so serving with `--block-size 64` dies in block-size negotiation:

```
ValueError: No common block size for 64 (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41: [128]; DEEPSEEK_V41_INDEXER: [128])
```

This declares `[64]` on SM12x for the two sites (indexer backend, sparse MLA backend, FlashInfer sparse backend), mirroring the existing SM90 branch. The SWA/backend selection is untouched.

The approach is @aagallo's (described in #59203); this PR adds the validated matrix below.

### Matrix validation (8x RTX PRO 6000, SM120, TP8)
Stack: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev158+gab905a885` + FlashInfer `0.7.1rc5`, `--block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`, DeepGEMM switched between PR14 head (`40592bd`) and the current pin (`1e1842a`):

| vLLM tree | DeepGEMM | result |
|---|---|---|
| stock | `1e1842a` | fails negotiation (error above) |
| this PR (uniform `[64]`) | `40592bd` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| this PR (uniform `[64]`) | `1e1842a` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| per-layer variant (`[64,128]` + `64*max(1,cr)` specs) | `40592bd` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| per-layer variant | `1e1842a` | serves, 17x19=323 |

All four patched cells boot in ~90-160 s and answer correctly; zero failures. An earlier `attention.hpp:484` observed with uniform-64 on an older stack (0.30.1rc1.dev738 + FlashInfer main @c11f8ba + DeepGEMM 6901431) does not reproduce on current main with either DeepGEMM build — details in #59203.

Pairs naturally with #57292 (fail-fast when FlashInfer lacks runtime page sizes).

Addresses the SM120 serving failure in #59203.

### Test Plan
- [x] 5-cell matrix above (serve + correctness per cell)
- [x] pre-commit / CI

---

## Requirements & validation (added after review)

**FlashInfer requirement: `flashinfer-python >= 0.7.1rc5` (runtime page sizes).** Measured end to end on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120):
- pinned `0.7.0.post1` + this PR: does **not** serve — fails in ~110 s with `page_block_size=32 is unsupported; decode kernels are instantiated only for page_block_size=64` (64-token kernel blocks give ratio-2 layers 32-token compressed pages; the pin has no runtime page sizes). Stock fails on the pin as well.
- `0.7.1rc5` + this PR: serves at default and `--block-size 64`; `--block-size 128` does not serve on this stack in either declaration form (see matrix below), so the PR buys default-64 — the only geometry that serves on the default BLHNC layout.

Landing order per review discussion: after the FlashInfer bump (#60948), or together with the #57292 guard.

**Matrix (stock / A=[64] / C=[64,128] x default / 64 / 128, GSM8K n=100):** stock fails both ways (assertions upthread); A and C serve at default and 64 (GSM8K 89-91%, no variant-dependent degradation); 128 fails under both declarations (A: BLHNC layout guard; C: FlashInfer `block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64`). Decode throughput of the four servable configs is within <1% at c1/c4.

**No unit test, by review:** an earlier revision added `tests/v1/attention/test_dsv41_indexer_block_sizes.py`, but it pinned kernel-support values that will drift (and the block size is asserted in C++ at kernel launch, so a black-box version would need a real kernel anyway). Per review it was removed and each SM12x `[64]` now carries a short inline comment naming the failure it avoids (#59203).

**Revalidation on the final form** — 8x RTX PRO 6000 96 GB (SM120), vLLM 0.33.0 with these two declarations, fp8 KV, no explicit `--block-size`: negotiation reports `Setting kv cache block size to 64 for FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41/DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA/DEEPSEEK_V41_INDEXER/CompressorBackend`; READY in ~7.5 min (cold JIT); KV cache 2,397,337 tokens at 32,768 max-model-len; 4/4 short-answer probes correct and greedy output byte-identical across 3 runs.

Coordinated with #56509 (same failure, overlapping declarations).

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2/EAGLE3 aux hidden-state capture with the upstream config
author: ischencheng
body:
## Overview

`Glm5NextModel._aux_hidden_state` (added in #56983) reads `self.config.mhc_num_residual_streams`, but since #57387 the config is the upstream `Glm5NextTextConfig`, which calls it `hc_mult`. So capturing aux hidden states for a DFlash2 / EAGLE3 drafter on GLM-5.3-Flash raises `AttributeError` during startup. #56983 was developed on a base from before #57387, so it never hit the rename.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-Flash with the recipe's DFlash2 config no longer dies with `AttributeError: 'Glm5NextTextConfig' object has no attribute 'mhc_num_residual_streams'`.
- Adds a CPU test that runs `_aux_hidden_state` against the upstream config.

## Validation

New test, red/green:

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_aux_hidden_state.py
```

main: fails with the `AttributeError` above. This PR: passes.

E2E on 1xH100: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` with dummy weights, all 45 layers kept (the drafter reads layers 5/14/24/33/42), `hf_overrides={"text_config": {"n_routed_experts": 8}}` to fit one GPU, `language_model_only`, `enforce_eager`, and the recipe's `--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}'`:

| code | DFlash2 startup |
|---|---|
| main | `AttributeError: 'Glm5NextTextConfig' object has no attribute 'mhc_num_residual_streams'` |
| main + this PR | gets past aux capture, then `NotImplementedError: Layer ...indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded` (KV grouping, #59656) |
| main + #59656 | same `AttributeError` |
| main + #59656 + this PR | starts and generates |
| main, no speculative decoding | starts and generates |

## Details

`hc_contract` only averages over the stream dim and ignores its `n` argument, so the change does not affect numerics; it just stops the attribute lookup from failing.

DFlash2 on GLM-5.3-Flash also needs the KV-cache grouping change that was split out of #56983 into #59656: with only this fix, startup moves on to `NotImplementedError: Layer ...indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded`. The two changes are independent; the table above shows both are needed.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this line; #57171 (PP for GLM-5.3-Flash) predates #56983 and adds new code that still uses the old name.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find this, write the change and run the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Platform] Don't resolve current_platform during import vllm
author: haotiaa
body:
## Overview

Since #45424, `import vllm` resolves `current_platform` and loads platform plugins while vLLM is still half-imported, because `PIN_MEMORY` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` is computed at import time. This PR computes `PIN_MEMORY` on first access, so `import vllm` no longer resolves the platform, as `vllm/platforms/__init__.py` requires. Same root cause as #48397; #48444 fixed only that issue's WSL symptom.

## Claims

- `import vllm` no longer resolves the platform. The resolver runs 0 times during `import vllm`, down from 1.
- An out-of-tree platform plugin whose `register()` imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils`, directly or through another vLLM module, is detected again. Before this change it failed with `cannot import name ... from partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`, and vLLM silently fell back to another platform.
- `PIN_MEMORY` keeps its value. All `from vllm.utils.torch_utils import PIN_MEMORY` sites and monkeypatches (e.g. `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py`) keep working.

## Validation

The existing dummy platform plugin's `register()` now imports a vLLM module, as real plugins do. A new subprocess test checks that `import vllm` leaves the platform unresolved and that the plugin platform still wins.

```bash
pip install -e tests/plugins/vllm_add_dummy_platform
pytest -v tests/plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py
pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py
```

| Check | main + new tests | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py`, CPU, rebased on current main | 1 failed, 2 passed | 3 passed |
| same, CUDA (L4)\* | 2 failed, 1 passed (`Expected DummyDevice, got cuda`) | 3 passed |
| resolver calls during `import vllm` (L4)\* | 1 | 0 |
| `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` (CPU) | 34 passed, 1 failed | 34 passed, 1 failed (same unrelated test) |
| `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` (L4)\* | — | 38 passed |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` greedy smoke run (L4)\* | — | OK, `PIN_MEMORY=True` on CUDA |

\* The L4 rows were run on an earlier base, 9dba339; I couldn't get GPU capacity to re-run them on current main. They also used an earlier version of the test, in which the dummy plugin imported `vllm.config`. On current main that import also runs into the separate `compilation.py` resolution described below, so the PR imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils` instead. The `torch_utils.py` change is identical, and no commits since 9dba339 touch `torch_utils.py`, `env_override.py`, `platform_utils.py` or `platforms/__init__.py`.

<details>
<summary>Fake out-of-tree plugin matrix (L4): 4 plugin styles × 4 first-import styles</summary>

**Plugin styles.** `register()` does one of:
- imports nothing;
- `import vllm.config`;
- `from vllm.config import VllmConfig`;
- nothing, but the platform module imports `vllm.config` at top level.

**First imports:** `import vllm`, `from vllm import LLM`, `EngineArgs`, `import vllm.config`.

| | cells not OK |
|---|---|
| main | 12/16 (plugin replaced by `NvmlCudaPlatform`, or `ImportError ... partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`) |
| this PR | 4/16 |
| before #45424 | 4/16 (same cells) |

The remaining 4 cells come from `vllm/config/compilation.py:22`, which resolves the platform during `import vllm.config`. That predates #45424 and is out of scope here.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main):
1. `vllm/__init__.py:14` imports `vllm.env_override`.
2. `vllm/env_override.py:153` imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils`.
3. `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py:76` runs `PIN_MEMORY = is_pin_memory_available()`.
4. `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py:45` imports `current_platform`, which resolves the platform and loads plugins.

This happens while `torch_utils` has only run up to line 76. A plugin that imports vLLM in `register()` gets an `ImportError`. Detection swallows it (`vllm/platforms/__init__.py`, `resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname`), so vLLM falls back to another platform and caches that platform's pin-memory setting.

**Fix.** A module `__getattr__` (PEP 562) computes `PIN_MEMORY` on first access and stores it as a module global, so later reads are plain global lookups. The three uses inside `torch_utils.py` go through `_pin_memory()`, which also honours an assigned or monkeypatched `PIN_MEMORY`.

**Why the existing plugin test missed this.** The dummy plugin's `register()` imported nothing from vLLM, and the test only checks the final `device_name`. Also, the Plugin Tests CI step only triggers on changes under `vllm/plugins/` and `tests/plugins/`, so it did not run for #45424. It does run for this PR. Adding `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` / `vllm/env_override.py` to that step's `source_file_dependencies` would catch future regressions; I left it out to keep CI load unchanged, but can add it if maintainers prefer.

**Alternative considered.** Move `is_torch_equal*` out of `torch_utils`, so `env_override` no longer imports it (3 files, +68/-51). That also fixes `import vllm`, but it leaves the import-time platform resolution in `torch_utils` for the next early importer.

**Duplicate check.** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `PIN_MEMORY`, `is_pin_memory_available`, `current_platform` + `import vllm`, `platform plugin circular import` and `partially initialized module torch_utils`. Only related, none open: #48397 / #48444 (WSL symptom of the same root cause) and #52285 (logging of detection failures).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write and test this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][V1] Null sliding-window block-table entries below the window
author: stu-cao
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60560.

The sliding-window KV manager frees blocks once they fall wholly outside a request's window, but the worker's persistent block table keeps the freed block ids. Attention kernels load KV in tiles (FA4 uses 128-key tiles on SM100). With 64-token pages, the tile that holds the window start can include one page lying wholly below the window. That page is masked, but masked NaN still propagates (0 × NaN). After the freed block is reused, its bytes can decode as NaN in the layer that reads it, and that request's attention output turns NaN.

#60560 has the full analysis. In short, on B300 with a DFlash2 drafter (all 6 layers sliding window, 2048) under the hybrid KV cache manager and `--block-size 64`:
- draft acceptance falls from about 40% to 27–29% at 32 concurrent sessions;
- the first divergence is NaN in the last draft layer's attention;
- about 21% of that layer's in-tile stale pages contain fp8 NaN bytes.

This PR makes the worker never hand those entries to attention. When `gather_block_tables` builds the forward-pass tables, every sliding-window entry wholly below `first_scheduled_position - (sliding_window - 1 + extra_retained_tokens)` is replaced by the null block:
- **No query of the step can attend those positions.**
- **The cutoff is never below the manager's free boundary.** The manager frees on the processed-token count, which is at most the first scheduled position, so every block it may have freed is covered.
- **Only the forward-pass copy changes.** Slot mappings and the persistent tables are untouched.
- **GPU only.** The first scheduled position is the request's `num_computed_tokens`, already on the device, so there is no host sync.
- **Every sliding-window spec is covered.** `SlidingWindowSpec.num_retained_tokens` gives the reach. (`KpoolTailSpec`, which an earlier revision opted out, was removed on `main` in #57169; its successor `CircularBufferSpec` is not a `SlidingWindowSpec` and is unaffected.)
- **Context parallelism is excluded.** Masking is disabled when `cp_size > 1`, where a block-table column is not a contiguous token range.

Speculator steps that reuse the gathered tables (e.g. DFlash) are covered too, since their queries sit at or after the target's first scheduled position.

### Scope

The change is not specific to any model or drafter. It applies to every KV cache group whose spec is a `SlidingWindowSpec` (including `SlidingWindowMLASpec`), target or draft, with any attention backend. Why it is safe:
- **No KV write is redirected.** Every KV write slot is computed from the persistent tables (`compute_slot_mappings`), or, for DFlash, from this step's positions, which are above the cutoff.
- **Entries are whole KV blocks.** Since #57169 `BlockTables` holds one entry per KV block, so the cutoff is `max(first_pos - reach, 0) // block_size` entries.

Not covered:
- **The V1 model runner.** The default V2 runner is covered; V1 is still selected for some speculators, DBO and some ROCm architectures.
- **Context parallelism (DCP/PCP).** Excluded on purpose, since a block-table column is not a contiguous token range there.
- **Chunked-local attention.** Not changed. Its chunk boundaries are multiples of the KV tile, so no wholly-outside page shares a tile.

**Assumption:** the null block holds no NaN. The KV cache is zero-allocated, and the null entries the tables already contain (sliding-window prefix hits, P/D tail clipping) rely on the same thing.

**Validation:** end-to-end validation so far covers a DFlash2 drafter under the hybrid KV cache manager. A check on a target model with sliding-window layers (e.g. gpt-oss, Gemma 3) at high concurrency is still to do.

### Relation to existing PRs

- **#42276** (for #42273, "SWA eviction leaves stale block table entries") targets the same stale entries from the scheduler side: it resends the full rewritten block table to the worker after an eviction. It has had merge conflicts since May and no review. This PR is a worker-only alternative: no scheduler or `SchedulerOutput` change, and no table resend. If maintainers prefer #42276's direction, I'm happy to close this one in its favour, and the regression test here should carry over.

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Store conv_kernel - 1 inputs in Mamba2 prefill checkpoints
author: sungsooha
body:
## Overview

With speculative decoding, the Mamba2 prefill checkpoint (added in #57329) stored conv inputs that were `num_spec` tokens too old. After a prefix-cache restore from that checkpoint, the model read stale conv inputs for its first new tokens and could give a wrong answer. This PR stores only the `conv_kernel_size - 1` inputs that the conv readers use.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong outputs after a prefix-cache hit that restores from a Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoint when MTP or another speculative method is on.
- No change without speculative decoding: then `conv_state.size(-1)` already equals `conv_kernel_size - 1`.
- No change to cache layout, KV capacity or speed.

## Validation

**Unit test.** `test_store_selects_the_checkpoint_from_all_chunk_states` now runs with `spec_slots` 0 and 3. It checks that the first `state_len` slots hold the newest inputs and that the spec slots stay untouched. All 8 tests in the file pass on GPU with the fix. With the old `store_prefill_checkpoint`, both `spec_slots=3` cases fail and both `spec_slots=0` cases pass.

**End to end.** A Mamba2 hybrid model with one MTP layer, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16 --enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint`, FP8 KV cache, temperature 0, thinking off. These three files are identical at the tested commit and at current `main`.

- **Resend test:** a ~71k-token prompt (a record table; the task copies records 100-160) sent 3 times. Sends 2 and 3 restore 16-31 tokens before the end, on the question.
- **Block-boundary test:** a ~11.6k-token prompt whose key digits sit right before a 4,544-token (4,416 with 5 draft tokens) block boundary, so the restore lands at that boundary.
- **Wrong** = a copied record differs from the source table.

| Setup | Test | Wrong before | Wrong after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 draft tokens | resend, 24 resends | 8 / 24 | 0 / 24 |
| 7 draft tokens, default `--prefix-match-unit` | block boundary, 12 resends | 10 / 12 | 0 / 12 |
| 5 draft tokens, probabilistic drafting | resend, 24 resends | 6 / 24 | 0 / 24 |
| 5 draft tokens, default `--prefix-match-unit` | block boundary, 12 resends | 12 / 12 | 0 / 12 |
| P/D disaggregated (NIXL), 7 draft tokens | resend, 24 resends | 13 / 24 | 0 / 24 |

- First sends (no cache hit) were wrong 0 times before and after, and gave the same text before and after.
- All 270 sends restored at the predicted token count, so the tests went through the restore path.
- Controls before the fix: prefix caching off gave 0 / 24 wrong; speculative decoding off gave 0 / 24 wrong.
- KV cache size and resend latency did not change.

## Details

**Root cause.** With speculative decoding the paged conv state has `conv_kernel_size - 1 + num_spec` slots (`mamba_utils.py`). `store_prefill_checkpoint` set `state_len = conv_state.size(-1)` and wrote inputs `[ckpt - state_len, ckpt)` into slots `0..state_len-1`, oldest first. Every reader takes slots `0..conv_kernel_size-2` as the newest inputs:

- `causal_conv1d_fn` uses `state_len = KERNEL_WIDTH - 1`.
- `causal_conv1d_update` reads from slot `num_accepted_tokens - 1`, which is 0 for a restored request.

So slots `0..2` (conv kernel 4) held inputs that were `num_spec` tokens too old. `--prefix-match-unit 16` makes such restores frequent: the restore point lands 16-31 tokens before the prompt end. The default unit restores at block boundaries, which the same export also writes.

**Fix.** `store_prefill_checkpoint` takes a required keyword `state_len`, and its only caller passes `self.conv_kernel_size - 1`. `FlashKDAPrefillCheckpointExporter` already takes an explicit `state_len` for the same reason. The kernel keeps the physical strides, so both conv layouts (dim-first and the transposed view) work. The spec slots of the checkpoint block are not written. Nothing reads them before the next update rewrites all slots, and before this change they held no useful data either.

**Other paths checked.** The align-mode copies, the shared-prefix checkpoint, NIXL transfer and CPU offload copy whole conv rows or already use `conv_kernel_size - 1`. They need no change.

**Limitation.** This covers Mamba2 only. When `state_len` is unset, `FlashKDAPrefillCheckpointExporter` still falls back to the full conv width.

title: [Bugfix] Size the HiSparse hot buffer from the rounded sparse top-k width
author: qimcis
body:
## Overview

HiSparse sized its scheduler hot-cache allocation from `index_topk`, while GLM-5.3-Flash allocates a wider, padded top-k buffer. This updates the existing fix in #60805 following review; related GLM support is tracked in #61243 and #60072.

## Claims

- Keep GLM's width calculation in its model definition, shared with MTP. Pass the actual allocated width through `MLAAttentionSpec` so HiSparse does not need to import GPU model code in the scheduler.
- Allow custom `device_buffer_size` values whose physical allocation includes block padding, by removing the startup equality assertion.

## Validation

All applicable pre-commit hooks pass, including Ruff, mypy, test tethering, and forbidden-import checks. No new tests are included; existing MLA test fixtures only gain the metadata field required by the code change.

The normal focused pytest run cannot collect on this macOS ARM checkout due to missing vLLM dependencies. The documented precompiled editable install also fails because no macOS ARM wheel is available. CUDA startup, model evaluation, and full pytest remain to be run in a supported environment.

## Details

For `index_topk=2048` and `index_kpool=4`, the model reserves the incomplete pool tail and rounds the buffer width to 2176. With seven speculative tokens, HiSparse therefore needs `9 * 2176 = 19584` default hot rows per request, rather than `9 * 2048 = 18432`. The scheduler now receives this width from the model's cache specification, preserving the model's own sizing rules.

A user-selected capacity can differ from the physical allocation: 129 logical rows occupy three 64-row blocks. Registration must accept that padding.

AI assistance was used to implement and review these changes. The existing PR is updated rather than opening a duplicate; no broader GLM enablement is included.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO READ: await every read before the forward
author: MIR-AMD
body:
## Overview

MoRIIO READ loads KV synchronously (`load_kv_async=False`), so the decode worker posts every READ in `start_load_kv` and must not run the forward until they land. Main awaits all of them only when the forward context says FULL; otherwise it awaits only mamba/KDA reads and leaves attention to the per-layer `wait_for_layer_load` hook. Two cases fall through:

- **MRv2 FULL replay.** `pre_forward` runs before `run_fullgraph` with no forward context (`gpu/model_runner.py`), so `start_load_kv` sees mode NONE and awaits only KDA reads, and the per-layer hook never runs inside the graph. All attention-side reads (MLA, indexer K, kpool tail) can still be in flight when the graph consumes them. #60636 addresses this case by passing the FULL context.
- **PIECEWISE / eager.** Indexer caches (`DeepseekV32IndexerCache` and subclasses) never call `wait_for_layer_load`, so their reads are never awaited.

This PR awaits every READ posted in the step inside `start_load_kv`, in every cudagraph mode, and makes `wait_for_layer_load` a no-op (kept because the base method is abstract). Attention-only failures no longer stop the wait early, so one request's failure can't let the forward run on another request's in-flight reads; hybrid still fails fast and raises.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, 1P/1D MoRIIO READ, EP8, MTP 1, KV block 8, MI300X, default decode cudagraph mode (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE). Base: main `19b0efce30` + #60867 (needed to boot this model); "with" adds this PR.

**Race (instrumented, logging-only).** After each admission step's forward, a device sync, then a check of every READ the barrier did not await. Context length determines race likelihood: below ~32K reads usually land in time; above ~96K every admission races in the default recipe.

| context (tokens) | admissions racing without this PR | MLA / tail reads still pending after the forward | MLA bytes still pending, worst step | latest landing after the forward | with this PR: admissions / races | barrier wait with this PR (median) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ≤8K | 0 / 1306 | 0 / 0 | – | – | 2414 / 0 | 2–16 ms |
| 32K | 5 / 60 | 29 / 34 | 0.32 GB | 30 ms | 28 / 0 | 13–17 ms |
| ~100K | 4 / 4 | 8 / 0 | – | 17 ms | 8 / 0 | 33–64 ms |
| 256K | **36 / 36** | **359 / 420** | **3.0 GB** | **216 ms** | 63 / 0 | 73–155 ms |
| 512K | **3 / 3** | **33 / 36** | **5.0 GB** | 168 ms | 9 / 0 | 157–271 ms |
| ~713K | **3 / 3** | **35 / 36** | **8.0 GB** | 195 ms | 9 / 0 | 364–396 ms |

Without = main `19b0efce30` + #60867, default recipe (every admission replayed FULL), 4 runs on 2 node pairs; with = + this PR, default recipe plus forced PIECEWISE (21/3/3 of the 256K/512K/~713K admissions). Indexer K reads: 0 pending in every row. In 450/464 MLA cases the bytes the graph read differ from what the READ delivered afterwards (stale blocks from earlier requests). Forced PIECEWISE on main + #60636: 233 kpool tail reads consumed while still in flight (the indexer runs before the MLA hook); with this PR 0.

**Accuracy (same runs, without vs with).** Single-needle long-context probe (243K/486K/713K tokens × 3 depths) 9/9 vs 9/9, identical answers. GSM8K full 5-shot strict 92.04% ± 0.75 vs 92.42% ± 0.73. NIAH 96K words (3 seeds) 3, 1, 2 vs 1, 10, 10 (bimodal, not significant). We have not reproduced a wrong output caused by the race; the evidence is the pending-after-forward reads and the snapshots.

**Perf (c=1, same image with/without this change, same node pair).** Forced PIECEWISE 8K–512K: TTFT −1.8..+1.8%, ITL −3.4..+1.0% (same-build repeat spread: TTFT up to ~9% at 8K, ITL ≤1.8%). Default FULL_AND_PIECEWISE 32K–512K: TTFT +0.5..+1.4% (pair-to-pair spread 2–3%). Against #60636 on the same base: −0.3..+1.4% (noise 2–6%).

**Final head E2E.** Default recipe: 1242 admissions (all FULL replay), every READ awaited before the forward (104 per request), 0 MLA / indexer / tail reads pending after the forward; long-context probe 9/9; GSM8K 91.89% ± 0.75; no MoRIIO errors. Forced PIECEWISE: 32 admissions, 0 pending reads, probe 9/9. Barrier wait on admission steps (median): 150 ms at 256K, 271 ms at 512K, 364 ms beyond; ~3 ms for short prompts.

**Unit.** `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py` 36 passed; all `test_moriio_*.py` 256 passed (main 248), 260 stacked with #60867, 0 failed (ROCm nightly, MI300X). New tests fail on main / the previous head on their assertions. `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, typos) passes.

> `pre-run-check` is the author merge-count gate, not lint; full CI runs once a maintainer adds `ready`.

## Details

**Tradeoff.** Steps that admit a transferred request outside FULL lose per-layer overlap; the added wait is bounded by the transfer tail that overlapped the forward. It is a host wait on RDMA completion statuses, no device sync, and only runs when the step has sync loads and posted reads. Steady-state decode is unchanged.

**Failure semantics.** Attention-only: the barrier waits for every request's reads (bounded by `transfer_timeout`) and failed requests are reported via `get_block_ids_with_load_errors`. Hybrid: fail fast and raise, since HMA load-error recovery is unsupported. A read still in flight when the barrier gives up (e.g. at `transfer_timeout`) fails the step closed in both modes.

**Relation to #60636.** Complementary. #60636 fixes the MRv2 FULL context; it does not cover indexer reads outside FULL. With both, FULL steps already await everything and this PR adds the non-FULL coverage.

- [x] Code quality: ruff, mypy, typos pass.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Reset a resumed streaming session's block table in OffloadingConnector and SimpleCPUOffloadConnector
author: albertoperdomo2
body:
## Overview

`OffloadingConnector` and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` corrupts the CPU KV cache for streaming-input sessions. A session resumed for its next input chunk arrives as `NewRequestData` with its full block table, but `yield_req_data` flagged it as a delta, so the connector appended it to the table it already held.

## Claims

- A resumed streaming session's new chunks are offloaded from their own GPU blocks, so requests reusing that prefix from the CPU tier get correct KV.
- `yield_req_data` reports `is_full_table` (`True` for new requests) instead of `preempted`; the connector resets on it. NIXL and SimpleCPUOffload ignore the flag, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_streaming_session_stores_new_chunks` (sync and async): the session's second chunk stores blocks `(0, 1, 2)` on main (earlier chunks' blocks) and `(2, 3, 4)` with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/`: all pass.
- E2E ran, and after a three-chunk streaming session, a greedy request on its 192-token prefix is served from the CPU tier and compared with a full recompute.
  - main: the outputs differ (the CPU-tier output loops on `5, 276, 183, 9`).
  - this PR: all 32 tokens match.

## Details

`_build_store_jobs` pairs chunk *j*'s key with `block_ids[j]`, so the duplicated table (`[1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]` vs `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]`) stored earlier chunks' KV under later chunks' keys. For every other request the table is already empty when the reset runs, so it is a no-op for them.

`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` duplicates the table the same way. It doesn't corrupt KV (it keys by block hash), but it skips offloading the session's new blocks. That will be a follow-up.

AI assistance (codex) was used; I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes `_requires_qwen38_tep8_emulation`, which forces OCP MX emulation for Qwen3.8 Flash Next's (`amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`) routed experts at TEP8 on gfx950 when the fused shared expert is off. The guard was added because AITER padded the MoE width from 640 to 768 for that shape and the native W4A4 kernel lost accuracy. Since #55104 aligns the W4A4 intermediate to 128, Flash Next's width stays at 640 with no pad, and the native kernel is as accurate as emulation and about twice as fast.

Existing work:
* #55104 removed the pad that the guard worked around, and on its own fixes Flash Next's accuracy at EP4 and TEP8 (measured below) and at TP1 (0.9651, #55104 on `nightly-43b4aaea`).
* The first revision of this PR also changed the pad rounding at MoE `tp_size == 1`. With #55104 merged, that is a no-op for Flash Next, so it is dropped here.

## Claims

- At TEP8 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0`, the only configuration where the guard fires, the native AITER W4A4 kernel matches emulation's accuracy (GSM8K 0.9651 vs 0.9629) at 2.3x the output throughput at 8k/1k concurrency 4 (362 vs 158 tok/s) and 1.9x at concurrency 32 (1399 vs 741).
- No change for the checkpoint card's recipe: with the fused shared expert each rank holds 65 local experts, the guard requires exactly 64, so it never fired there.
- No change for any other shape: the guard matched only `E=512, H=2560, N=640` at EP8 on gfx950.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (MI355X, gfx950, `nightly-5555a2d8` with this PR): 5 passed.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py
```

`test_qwen38_tep8_selects_native_aiter` replaces the guard's two tests: the TEP8 shape now selects `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` under both `auto` and `aiter`.

**Accuracy**, GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319 questions, MI355X, the checkpoint card's recipe, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8` vs the same image with this PR, one run per cell. Exact match, higher is better:

| config | stock | this PR |
| ------ | ----- | ------- |
| TEP8, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` | 0.9629 (emulation, guard hit) | 0.9651 (native) |
| TEP8, the card's recipe | 0.9644 (native, guard not hit) | unchanged |
| EP4 (TP4 + `--enable-expert-parallel`) | 0.9636 (native) | unchanged |

Flexible-extract; strict-match for the first row is 0.9636 → 0.9659. Standard error is about 0.005.

**Throughput**, TEP8 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0`, emulation (stock) vs native (this PR), random dataset, one run per cell. Output tok/s is higher-is-better, mean TPOT lower-is-better:

| ISL / OSL | Conc | Output tok/s, emulation → native | Mean TPOT (ms), emulation → native |
| --------- | ---- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 158 → 362 | 24.2 → 9.5 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 32 | 741 → 1399 | 38.7 → 20.0 |
| 128 / 8 | 1 | 40 → 90 | 21.2 → 7.2 |

**Reproduce:**

```bash
# plus the checkpoint card's ROCm environment, identical in both arms
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,max_gen_toks=2048,num_concurrent=32
```

## Details

* **Why the guard is stale.** Its docstring says AITER pads `N` to 768 for this shape. Since #55104 the W4A4 intermediate is aligned to 128, so 640 is stored as is, with no pad. The native kernel at 640 is accurate (first accuracy row), so CK-Tile's `inter_dim % 256` scale issue does not show up for this shape.
* **When the guard fired.** It matches `num_local_experts == 64`. The fused shared expert adds one local expert per rank (`ExpertMapManager`), so with the card's recipe the count is 65 and the native kernel already ran; only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` hit the guard.
* Only the ROCm MXFP4 oracle changes; nothing changes on CUDA.

**Limitations and CI gaps.**

* gfx950 only. The W4A4 MXFP4 MoE path does not run on gfx942.
* The end-to-end image applied the previous revision of this PR, which also changed the pad rounding at MoE `tp_size == 1`. With #55104, Flash Next's pad there is 0, so that part did nothing in these runs; the guard removal is the same code.
* The unit tests run in the AMD kernels CI job. The accuracy and throughput runs happened outside CI.

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Don't create hash directories on cache-miss lookups in ECExampleConnector
author: zhouyou9505
body:
## Purpose

`ECExampleConnector.has_cache_item()` resolves the safetensors path via
`_generate_filename_debug()`, which auto-creates the `<mm_hash>/` directory.
Since `has_cache_item()` is called from the scheduler's encoder-input
admission check and from `update_state_after_alloc()` on every multimodal
allocation, **every probed-but-missed hash leaves an empty directory in
shared storage**. On a long-lived deployment the EC storage root accumulates
one empty directory per unique missed hash, making the cache impossible to
inspect and polluting any listing-based tooling/backup jobs.

Fixes #60820

## Approach

Keep auto-creation on the **save** path (where the directory is actually
needed) and disable it on the **lookup** path:

- `_found_match_for_mm_data()` now passes `create_folder=False` to
  `_generate_filename_debug()`.
- `_generate_filename_debug()` gains a `create_folder: bool = True`
  parameter, forwarded to `_generate_foldername_debug()`. Defaults are
  unchanged, so `save_caches()` / `start_load_caches()` behavior is
  identical.

No behavioral change beyond the filesystem side effect.

## Testing

- Added `test_has_cache_item_miss_creates_no_folder` to the existing
  `tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_ec_example_connector.py`: a cache-miss
  lookup leaves no empty folder in shared storage.
- Also verified on a live A100 EPD testbed against a producer-role
  connector: `VERIFY-OK`.

## Notes

- Observed on a live deployment; the same code paths exist on current main.
- `start_load_caches` is untouched: it only loads hashes that
  `has_cache_item()` has already confirmed to exist.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Decode current NIXL connector stats
author: ilmarkov
body:
## Overview

Rust's strict `NixlStats` decoder rejected two fields emitted by current Python NIXL stats. In `MultiConnector` payloads, that caused the NIXL child to be treated as opaque data, so the Rust metrics recorder dropped its transfer histograms. The recorder also omitted handshake/notification failures from the combined failure counter and did not export late notifications.

## Claims

- Decode current Python NIXL `MultiConnector` stats while retaining compatibility with payloads that omit newer fields.
- Record NIXL transfer histograms and align the Rust failed-transfer counter with Python by including transfer, handshake, and notification failures.
- Export `vllm:nixl_num_notifications_after_expiry` from the Rust frontend.
- This does not duplicate [#58563](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58563): that PR adds descriptor-driven metrics for other connectors and explicitly leaves NIXL on its existing typed path. This change fixes that typed path and completes the Rust metric coverage.

## Validation

- `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-engine-core-client kv_connector_stats_are_recorded_into_mooncake_and_nixl_metrics` — passed (1 test); verifies the combined failure count and late-notification counter.
- `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-engine-core-client python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics` — passed (1 test); decodes the Python-generated fixture and checks rendered failure, expiry, and histogram metrics.
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --check`, `git diff --check`, and commit pre-commit hooks — passed.

## Details

EngineCore sends `MultiConnector` stats as a map from connector class name to its stats payload. Current Python NIXL stats include `num_failed_handshakes` and `num_notifications_after_expiry`; the Rust `NixlStats` used `deny_unknown_fields` but did not declare these fields. Serde therefore rejected the typed NIXL child, the flattened `other` map retained it as opaque data, and the recorder ignored it.

The relevant flow is: (1) the P/D connector accumulates transfer and notification outcomes, (2) EngineCore serializes connector stats into the `MultiConnector` MessagePack payload, and (3) the Rust frontend decodes NIXL stats and records the matching Prometheus metrics. Adding the missing fields with defaults keeps older payloads compatible. The recorder now groups transfer, handshake, and notification failures under the existing failed-transfer counter, keeps the dedicated notification-failure counter for compatibility, and records notifications received after expiry separately.

The regression extends the Python-generated MessagePack fixture and asserts the decoded fields and rendered counters, including a failed handshake, a failed notification, and two notifications after expiry.

title: [Bugfix] Fix depyf incompatibility with Inductor's set_sys_modules
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Overview

Any `torch.compile` run with `debug_dump_path` set fails once compilation reaches an autotune code block, because depyf's `load_by_key_path` hook does not accept Inductor's `set_sys_modules` argument. A compatibility shim gives the hook `**kwargs` and forwards them.

Seen on the `PyTorch Fullgraph` step in [Buildkite #93716](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93716/list?jid=01a11edf-b64d-4af0-91f8-60f8f72d7308&tab=output).

## Claims

- Fixes `InductorError: RuntimeError: Failed to run autotuning code block: patched_load_by_key_path() got an unexpected keyword argument 'set_sys_modules'`.
- Not platform-specific. The failing step is a ROCm mirror, but nothing in the cause or the fix is vendor-dependent; it needs only a cold compile cache.
- The shim is conditional on depyf's hook signature, so it disables itself if depyf ever ships a fix.
- The existing depyf test could not catch this. It was one parametrization of `test_custom_compile_config`, which reuses vLLM's on-disk compile cache, so on a persistent agent it usually verified nothing. It is now a separate test that disables the cache.
- Adds a CPU-only unit test that reproduces the incompatibility in 2.3 s, instead of only through a GPU end-to-end run.
- Costs 27 s on `PyTorch Fullgraph` and 11 s on `PyTorch Compilation`, both against budgets of 90 and 30 minutes. The other six parametrizations keep using the cache.
- Not fixed: depyf's other two hooks are unchanged. Both were audited and are already compatible.

## Validation

1× AMD MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2, PyTorch `2.13.0+git733fca1`, depyf 0.20.0, vLLM `19c0bed584`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New unit tests, CPU only | 6 passed, 2.3 s |
| End-to-end depyf test, cold cache, after the fix | passed, 50.6 s |
| Same, before the fix | failed, 25.8 s |
| Same, before the fix, warm cache | passed, 23.3 s |
| Unit tests with the shim forcibly disabled | 4 of 6 failed |

The last two rows are the ones that matter. The warm pass is why this reached `main`: with a populated cache nothing is compiled, depyf's hook is never called, and the test is green. The forced-disable run confirms the new tests measure the fix rather than the environment.

## Details

`depyf.prepare_debug` replaces `PyCodeCache.load_by_key_path` with a hook that dumps each generated kernel before loading it. The hook's signature is frozen at `(key, path, linemap, attrs)`, and `generate_and_run_autotune_block` now also passes `set_sys_modules`. The resulting `TypeError` is raised inside the `exec` of the tuning block, so it surfaces as an `InductorError` about the autotune block rather than as anything mentioning depyf.

Bumping the pin is not available: 0.20.0 is the last release upstream published, its repository has had no commits since that release, and four pull requests have been open without review. The hook is therefore patched in vLLM, in the way depyf already handles this for `lazy_format_graph_code`: accept `**kwargs` and forward them.

The shim forwards the keyword rather than dropping it. Dropping it would also make the call succeed, while quietly reintroducing the `sys.modules` exhaustion that pytorch#184285 fixed; one of the unit tests pins exactly that. Both vLLM entry points into depyf go through the shim, so neither can miss the patch.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject beam search with echo and logprobs in /v1/completions
author: surawut-jirasaktavee
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60875.

`POST /v1/completions` with `use_beam_search`, `echo` and `logprobs` all set returns HTTP 500 with an empty message. This PR rejects that combination in request validation, so the client gets a 400 that names the conflicting parameters.

## Claims

- `use_beam_search=true` + `echo=true` + `logprobs` set now returns HTTP 400 instead of 500, both for `max_tokens > 0` and for `max_tokens=0`.
- Valid combinations are unchanged: beam search with `echo` only, beam search with `logprobs` only, and `echo` + `logprobs` without beam search still return 200.

## Validation

Reproduced and verified with `vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --max-model-len 512 --dtype float16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.15` on the macOS CPU backend (Apple M3), sending `{"model": "facebook/opt-125m", "prompt": "Hello", "n": 2, ...}`:

| Extra request fields | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `use_beam_search, echo, logprobs: 1, max_tokens: 5` | 500, `""` | 400 |
| `use_beam_search, echo, logprobs: 1, max_tokens: 0` | 500, `"Did not output logprobs"` | 400 |
| `use_beam_search, echo, max_tokens: 5` | 200 | 200 |
| `use_beam_search, logprobs: 1, max_tokens: 5` | 200 | 200 |
| `echo, logprobs: 1, max_tokens: 5` (no beam search) | 200 | 200 |

Tests:

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py   # 43 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_watermarking.py                  # 24 passed
pre-commit run                                                         # passed
```

The new test fails on main (`DID NOT RAISE VLLMValidationError`) and passes with this change. It runs in the existing `entrypoints/openai/completion` Buildkite step.

## Details

Root cause: beam search never computes prompt logprobs, but the echo + logprobs response path asserts they exist. The full trace is in #60875.

The fix adds one check in `CompletionRequest.check_logprobs`, next to the existing beam search check for `logprob_token_ids`. I chose rejection over computing prompt logprobs inside beam search, because that would change the beam search implementation for a rarely used combination. The Rust frontend already rejects `use_beam_search`, so it is not affected. Chat completions does not echo prompt logprobs, so it has no equivalent path.

Duplicate check: no other open issue or PR covers this (searched "beam search echo logprobs", "use_beam_search echo", "beam search prompt_logprobs").

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find the bug, write the fix and test, and run the validation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

title: [Bugfix] Reject mismatched float16/bfloat16 KV cache dtype
author: cipheraxat
body:
## Overview

Reject an explicit `float16`/`bfloat16` `kv_cache_dtype` that differs from the model dtype in `VllmConfig.__post_init__`, before backend selection and CUDA-graph capture. Fixes [#60859](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60859).

No other open PR addresses this issue (`gh pr list --search "60859 in:body"`).

## Claims

- `dtype=bfloat16` with `kv_cache_dtype=float16` raises `ValueError` while the engine config is built, so `mha_varlen_fwd` never sees a bfloat16 query and a float16 key.
- The error is `kv_cache_dtype="float16" is incompatible with dtype="bfloat16". Please set --kv-cache-dtype to auto or bfloat16.`
- The swapped pair is rejected the same way. A `float32` model with an explicit `float16` KV cache is rejected with a hint to use `auto` only, because `float32` is not a legal `--kv-cache-dtype`.
- `"auto"`, a matching float16/bfloat16 pair, and FP8 stay valid.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k mismatched_float_kv_cache -q
```

6 passed: both mismatched float pairs and `float32` with a `float16` KV cache raise `ValueError`; matching `float16`, `"auto"`, and `"fp8"` are accepted. A direct `VllmConfig.__post_init__` call with a bfloat16 model and `kv_cache_dtype="float16"` raises the same error. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0) pass.

End-to-end `LLM.generate` on A6000 was not run (no CUDA GPU here).

## Details

**Root cause.** FlashAttention `mha_varlen_fwd` requires the query and the key to share a dtype. The engine accepted `dtype=bfloat16` and `kv_cache_dtype=float16`, then crashed during CUDA-graph capture.

**Why config-level.** The review asked to reject this mix once in `VllmConfig.__post_init__` rather than deselect backends. The check runs after `try_verify_and_update_config()`, so a model hook can still rewrite the cache dtype first (DeepSeek V3.2 rewrites an explicit `bfloat16` cache to `auto`). Triton can cast an unquantized KV tile up to the query dtype; this change refuses the mismatched pair instead of falling through to that path. The A100 data on #60859 supports rejecting rather than steering selection: FlashInfer asserts at init, and FlexAttention runs but produces silently wrong output (mean NLL 13.98 vs 3.96 with `auto`).

**AI assistance:** Used during diagnosis, implementation, and PR drafting. The human submitter reviewed the change and ran the checks above.

title: [Bugfix][Build] Build fused GDN MTP decode for SM80-SM90 with CUDA < 13
author: kimseunghyun-kr
body:
## Overview

`FUSED_GDN_DECODE_ARCHS` is set only inside the `CUDA >= 13.0` block of `CMakeLists.txt`. So every CUDA 12.x build, including the published cu129 images, ships without `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` on all architectures, and GDN models fall back to the Triton spec-decode path. This PR builds the kernel for `8.0;8.6;8.9;9.0a` when CUDA < 13.0. The family targets (`10.0f;11.0f;12.0f`) still need CUDA 13.

Builds on #51674 (kernel, "only needs cp.async and BF16 math"), #52743 (Ampere declaration guard) and #53835 (SM110 target).

## Claims

- CUDA 12.9 builds include the fused GDN MTP decode kernel for SM80–SM90.
- No change for CUDA ≥ 13.0 builds.

## Validation

On A100-SXM4-40GB, with nvcc 12.9 and torch 2.13.0+cu129 from the `cu129-nightly` image (vLLM 81198e97 + this patch, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.0`):

| | `tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py` + `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py` |
|---|---|
| Without patch | 71 passed, 29 skipped ("fused GDN decode MTP op is not built"), 2 failed (`test_fused_model_path_matches_reference[pure-mtp]`: the fused path is not called) |
| With patch | 102 passed |

- Configure prints `Building fused GDN decode for archs: 8.0`.
- End to end: serving Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (TP8) logs `GDN spec decode kernel: cuda` instead of `Falling back to the Triton GDN spec decode path: ... is not built`.
- Kernel time at CUDA-graph replay, per-rank shape H=2, HV=6, K=V=128, 4 MTP tokens per request: 0.48–0.76× of the Triton path at 1–32 requests.

## Details

- Not tested here: SM86/SM89/SM90 on CUDA 12.x (same source and gate; only SM80 was built).
- Related open PRs #53807 and #54034 change only the `ops.h` guard, which #52743 already fixed.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix][MLA] Fix FP8 MLA prefill unpad for interleave-padded heads
author: lucas-santos-amd
body:
## Overview
The gfx950 FP8 asm MLA prefill pads heads to a multiple of 16. When the target is a multiple of the real head count (8 → 16, e.g. Kimi-K2.x at TP8), `get_mla_padded_q` uses `repeat_interleave`, but the output was sliced back as `[:, :num_heads]`, which is only correct for tile padding. The model then attends with the wrong heads and produces garbage. Introduced by #51040.

## Claims
- Restores accuracy for interleave-padded head counts: Kimi-K2.6 MXFP4 TP8 GSM8K 0.027 → 0.933.
- No performance change: same kernels; the unpad copy is still one kernel at the same cost.
- Adds the 8-head (interleaved) case to `test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`.

## Validation
Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X, fp8 KV cache. GSM8K 5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions ... --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, num_concurrent=64:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| Before (upstream main) | 0.0273 ± 0.0045 | 0.0235 ± 0.0042 |
| After (this PR) | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 |

Torch profiler, random 1024/1024, 64 prompts, concurrency 64: 40 kernels per prefill MoE layer before and after.

Unit test on MI355X: `pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`

| Code under test | Result |
|---|---|
| This PR | 12 passed |
| Upstream unpad, with the new test cases | 2 failed, 10 passed: only `test_fp8_prefill_matches_reference[128-8]` and `[512-8]` fail |

<details>
<summary>Failure details on the upstream unpad</summary>

- `[128-8]`: mismatched elements 81,670 / 131,072 (62.3%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- `[512-8]`: mismatched elements 230,240 / 524,288 (43.9%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- All tile-padded (12, 24) and unpadded (16) cases pass on both versions.
</details>

## Details
Real heads sit at stride `nhead // num_heads` after `repeat_interleave` and at `[0:num_heads]` after tiling; the fix selects accordingly. Existing test head counts (12, 16, 24) only exercised tile padding.
No duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this; #59966 changes `get_mla_padded_q` but keeps `repeat_interleave` for the divisor case.

title: [Fix] MiniMax: fix CUDA IPC handle exchange on cuda-bindings >= 13.4
author: laithsakka
body:
Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58599, https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/8931

### What's wrong

The MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm kernel needs each GPU to read the other GPUs' memory directly. To set that up, every GPU allocates a buffer, gets a small 64-byte "IPC handle" for it, and sends that handle to the other GPUs. They then use it to open the buffer.

vLLM converted the handle to bytes and back through its .reserved field. In cuda-bindings 13.4 (part of cuda-python), NVIDIA removed that field from cudaIpcMemHandle_t, so the code now fails with:
AttributeError: 'cuda.bindings.runtime.cudaIpcMemHandle_t' object has no attribute 'reserved'


When that happens, vLLM falls back to the slower non-fused path, and test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk fails. It shows up in the torch-nightly CI lane because that environment installs cuda-bindings 13.4.x.

### The fix

Copy the 64 handle bytes through handle.getPtr(), the handle's memory address, using ctypes. Every cuda-bindings version supports it, so no version check is needed.

_ipc_handle_to_bytes(handle) reads the 64 bytes out of a handle.
_ipc_handle_from_bytes(raw) creates a new handle and copies the 64 bytes into it.
The fix is limited to vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/lamport_workspace.py.


### Test plan
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk -k "2-"
Before: fails with the AttributeError above and logs "Falling back to the eager allreduce".
After: 6 passed, 12 skipped (the 4- and 8-GPU cases, since there are only 2 GPUs). The fallback message is gone, so the fused path runs.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Expose completion response schemas in OpenAPI
author: GuanLuo
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Expose JSON response and SSE event schemas for chat and legacy completions in `/openapi.json`, using existing Pydantic models and OpenAPI 3.2. Related to #25272; broader client-generator issues are out of scope.

## Claims

- Both endpoints expose distinct unary JSON and SSE contracts with resolvable model references.
- SSE `itemSchema` describes an event envelope whose `data` is a JSON chunk, JSON error, or `[DONE]`. Keep-alive comments are not data events.
- Inference and stream generation are unchanged. Early disconnects now return an explicit empty `Response()` from the shared cancellation wrapper instead of `None`, avoiding response-model validation errors without making successful response schemas nullable.
- Bundled Swagger UI is updated to v5.33.1 so offline docs can load OpenAPI 3.2 documents. Rendering the SSE item schema remains an upstream limitation (see Details).

## Validation

Linux CPU checks were run by Codex at the author's request. The implementation and assertions in `b04e80127b` passed the checks below; the subsequent changes before committing only clarified test docstrings. The author confirmed validation and approved publishing this revision.

Before/after JSON captured through `GET /openapi.json` using the production routers and an in-process ASGI client, without an inference engine. These excerpts select HTTP 200 response content for the two endpoints, not the entire document. On a running server, reproduce this projection with:

```bash
curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/openapi.json | jq '
  .paths
  | with_entries(select(.key == "/v1/chat/completions" or .key == "/v1/completions"))
  | map_values(.post.responses["200"].content)'
```

Before (`4cf1307e72cb`):

```json
{
  "/v1/chat/completions": {
    "application/json": {"schema": {}},
    "text/event-stream": {}
  },
  "/v1/completions": {
    "application/json": {"schema": {}},
    "text/event-stream": {}
  }
}
```

After (`b04e80127b`; the document declares `"openapi": "3.2.0"`):

```json
{
  "/v1/chat/completions": {
    "application/json": {
      "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ChatCompletionResponse"}
    },
    "text/event-stream": {
      "itemSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["data"],
        "properties": {
          "data": {
            "type": "string",
            "anyOf": [
              {"const": "[DONE]"},
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ChatCompletionStreamResponse"}
              },
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"}
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "/v1/completions": {
    "application/json": {
      "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/CompletionResponse"}
    },
    "text/event-stream": {
      "itemSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["data"],
        "properties": {
          "data": {
            "type": "string",
            "anyOf": [
              {"const": "[DONE]"},
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/CompletionStreamResponse"}
              },
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"}
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The references resolve to generated model schemas in the same document's `components.schemas`; those definitions are omitted here. Direct payload tests check the selected models and reject malformed `choices`. Separate Schemathesis tests exercise real ASGI routes with synthetic serving-handler streams: chunks, errors, `[DONE]`, and keep-alive comments pass; malformed choices and non-JSON data fail.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_openai_schema.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_sse_keep_alive.py \
  -k 'not test_openapi_stateless' -q
```

- **40 passed, 1 deselected**, with Schemathesis 4.21.6 and FastAPI 0.136.3; also **40 passed, 1 deselected** with the minimum FastAPI 0.133.0.
- Cancellation regression: restoring the old wrapper reproduces `ResponseValidationError` on disconnect; the updated wrapper passes both disconnect and normal-completion cases.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and the additional mypy 3.12 check passed before the final docstring clarification.
- Browser checks loaded `/docs`, `/openapi.json`, and Swagger assets in online/offline modes. The OpenAPI 3.2 document loads; SSE `itemSchema` is not displayed correctly (upstream issue below).
- Existing Buildkite coverage includes the test files. The model-backed `test_openapi_stateless`, inference evaluation, and benchmarks were **not run**; the focused tests do not establish a full model-backed suite pass.

## Details

Register unary/chunk models with FastAPI; `openapi_extra` restores the unary JSON ref because the additional response model otherwise replaces it. Request structure is unchanged, but FastAPI renames `FunctionCall` to `FunctionCall-Input`; name-dependent consumers may notice.

Set the production app's OpenAPI version to 3.2.0, which defines `itemSchema`. This is a document-version change; no FastAPI dependency bump is needed. The cancellation fix is in the shared decorator and therefore applies to its other callers too; it does not change mid-stream disconnect handling by `StreamingResponse`.

**Swagger UI limitation:** v5.33.1 can load the OpenAPI 3.2 document but does not yet render `itemSchema` for sequential media types properly: [swagger-api/swagger-ui#11065](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui/issues/11065). The SSE contract is present in `/openapi.json` and exercised by Schemathesis, even though Swagger's response-schema display is incomplete. title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix TP group hang on steps without scheduled tokens
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

With a host pool shared across TP ranks (#56629), a TP group can hang forever on a step with no scheduled tokens. On such steps, every TP rank now waits at a CPU barrier right after its event wait.

## Claims

- Fixes a hang between TP rank 0 and a TP rank whose host is one step behind, on steps with no scheduled tokens (`no_forward`).
- Steps with tokens are unchanged.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** The script below copies the shared-event protocol from `hisparse/worker.py` onto 2 GPUs and holds rank 1's host for 0.5 s before one wait. Run on H100s:

```
torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 hisparse_event_hang.py {zero_next|zero_now|tokens} {none|sync|barrier}
```

| Case | `main` (`none`) | rank 0 host sync (`sync`) | this PR (`barrier`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zero_next`: rank 1 late, next step has no tokens | HANG 3/3 | PASS 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| `zero_now`: rank 1 late on a step with no tokens, next step has tokens | HANG 3/3 | HANG 3/3 | PASS 3/3 |
| `tokens`: rank 1 late, every step has tokens | PASS 3/3 | | |

When it hangs, GPU 0 is at 100% (spinning in the all-reduce) and GPU 1 is at 0% (its stream is blocked on the event).

**Unit test.** `test_zero_token_step_holds_tp_ranks_after_host_write_wait` checks that start_step waits at the TP barrier after the event wait on steps with no tokens, and only when the host region is shared.

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py -k "zero_token_step or draft_layer or full_graph_step or no_forward"
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` `worker.py` | 1 failed (`shared=True, num_tokens=0`), 7 passed |
| this PR | 8 passed |

These tests ran in a vLLM 0.31.0 H100 image (`f6d5a33`) with this branch's `worker.py` and test file swapped in. The image has no pytest, so a small runner expanded the parametrization. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

**Production.** A P/D decode deployment hit this hang. It runs HiSparse and NIXL through `MultiConnector`, at TP8 x DP4 with EP32 and MTP:
- One TP rank's GPU sat at 0% while its 7 TP peers sat at 100%.
- The other DP ranks then hit DeepEP dispatch timeouts.
- Each time, the engine was in its first minutes, when first contact with new prefill engines slows the NIXL read post on the main thread (0.1 to 2.4 s).

The reproducer shows the same GPU pattern. This patch has not yet run end to end on that deployment.

## Details

The protocol uses two shared events, A and B:
- Every step, each TP rank's stream waits on the event rank 0 recorded in the previous step.
- Rank 0 then records the other event in `finish_forward`.
- A stream wait binds to the most recent record at the time of the wait call.

**Trigger.** A TP rank's host falls one step behind rank 0, and the next step has no scheduled tokens.

**Mechanism:**

| | TP rank 0 | TP rank 1 (host late) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | step 5: wait A, launch forward 5, record B | still before its step 5 wait |
| 2 | step 6, no tokens: wait B, record A right away | |
| 3 | | step 5: wait A. The wait binds to rank 0's step 6 record |
| 4 | GPU: the forward 5 all-reduce waits for rank 1 | GPU: waits for the step 6 record, which is queued behind rank 0's forward 5 |

**Effect.** The TP group hangs and nothing times out. With DP and EP, the other DP ranks then block in their MoE collectives.

**Why steps with tokens are safe.** Before recording, rank 0 host-syncs on staging (`_finish_mirror_phase`). That staging is queued behind the previous forward's TP collectives, and every rank joins those only after its wait. A step with no tokens has no forward, so nothing orders rank 0's record after the other ranks' waits.

**Fix.** On steps with no tokens, every TP rank joins `get_tp_group().barrier()` (the CPU group) right after its wait. Every rank has then issued its wait before rank 0 can record again, on this step and the next.
- `num_tokens` comes from the same scheduler output on every TP rank, so all ranks take the barrier on the same steps.
- Without a shared host region, each rank uses its own local events, so there is no barrier.

**Why not a host sync on rank 0 alone.** The `zero_now` row: a sync can only prove that the other ranks reached the last step with a forward. A step with no tokens followed by a step with tokens still hangs.

**Cost.** One CPU barrier per step with no tokens. Those steps launch no forward.

**Not a duplicate.** I checked the 30 open PRs matching `hisparse`, plus searches for `host_write_event`, `hisparse hang`, `hisparse deadlock` and `hisparse barrier`. None changes how the shared host write events are ordered. #59877 fixes a separate NIXL thread-safety bug found in the same investigation.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, the change, the test and the reproducer.

<details>
<summary>hisparse_event_hang.py</summary>

```python
"""Two-rank model of HiSparse's shared host write events (hisparse/worker.py).

Rank 0 creates two IPC events and shares them. Every step, each rank flips to the
other event and its stream waits on the previous one (`start_step`). Rank 0 alone
records the current event at the end of the step (`finish_forward`), after a host
sync on staging queued before the step on steps with tokens (`_finish_mirror_phase`).
The forward is matmuls plus an all-reduce, standing in for the TP collectives.
Rank 1's host is held DELAY s before its step 5 wait.

  PLAN  zero_next  step 6 has no tokens
        zero_now   step 5 has no tokens, step 6 has tokens
        tokens     every step has tokens
  FIX   none       as on main
        sync       rank 0 also host-syncs before recording on steps without tokens
        barrier    every rank joins a CPU barrier after its wait on steps without tokens

torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 hisparse_event_hang.py PLAN FIX [DELAY]
Prints PASS, or HANG with per-GPU utilization after 20 s.
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, threading, time

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

plan, fix = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
delay = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0.5
zero_step = {"zero_next": 6, "zero_now": 5, "tokens": None}[plan]
assert fix in ("none", "sync", "barrier")
rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
dist.init_process_group("nccl")
cpu_group = dist.new_group(backend="gloo")
stream = torch.cuda.current_stream()

handles = [None]
if rank == 0:
    events = (torch.cuda.Event(interprocess=True), torch.cuda.Event(interprocess=True))
    for e in events:
        e.record(stream)
    handles = [tuple(e.ipc_handle() for e in events)]
dist.broadcast_object_list(handles, src=0)
if rank != 0:
    device = torch.device("cuda", rank)
    events = tuple(torch.cuda.Event.from_ipc_handle(device, h) for h in handles[0])
torch.cuda.synchronize()
dist.barrier()

done = threading.Event()


def watchdog():
    if not done.wait(20):
        util = subprocess.run(
            ["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu", "--format=csv,noheader", "-i", "0,1"],
            capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        print(f"rank{rank} HANG at step {step}, GPU util: " + util.strip().replace("\n", " | "), flush=True)
        os._exit(2)


threading.Thread(target=watchdog, daemon=True).start()
a = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
cur, nxt = events[1], 0
for step in range(10):
    has_tokens = step != zero_step
    staging = torch.cuda.Event()
    staging.record(stream)
    if rank == 1 and step == 5:
        time.sleep(delay)  # e.g. a slow NIXL read post before start_step
    prev, cur = cur, events[nxt]
    nxt ^= 1
    stream.wait_event(prev)
    if not has_tokens and fix == "barrier":
        dist.barrier(group=cpu_group)
    if has_tokens:
        y = a
        for _ in range(8):
            y = y @ a
            dist.all_reduce(y)
            y = y / 4096
    if rank == 0:
        if has_tokens or fix == "sync":
            staging.synchronize()
        cur.record(stream)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
done.set()
print(f"rank{rank} PASS", flush=True)
dist.destroy_process_group()
```

</details>

title: [Bugfix] Fix Triton prefill attention OutOfResources on GPUs with 99KiB shared memory
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60847.

`google/embeddinggemma-2` crashes in engine warmup with Triton `OutOfResources` (`Required: 163840, Hardware limit: 101376`) on GPUs with 99 KiB of shared memory per block, such as RTX 30/40/50 cards and L4. The cause is that `context_attention_fwd` picks its tile size from the dtype and compute capability only. This change keeps halving the tile on CUDA until its Q, K and P tiles fit the device's opt-in shared memory per block.

Compared with #60848, this fix:

- Keeps every tile that already fits. [#60848](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60847). estimates the need as `3*B*D`, which is up to 50% above what the kernel really needs. So on A100 it halves tiles that launch fine today, for example bf16 head size 256 (128 → 64) on this model's sliding layers. On an RTX 5090, halving a tile that fits made this kernel 1.18x to 1.65x slower.
- Adds a test that also catches the fp32 head-size-512 failure (`Required: 135168`). The test in [#60848](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60847) adds only D=256, so it would also pass with a fix that leaves that path broken.

Compared with #60631, this fix:

- Also fixes the reported model in float32. With [#60631](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60631), `vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 --runner pooling --dtype float32` still dies at engine start with `OutOfResources ... Required: 135168, Hardware limit: 101376`, from the same `context_attention_fwd` launch.
- Fits the tile for every head size, not only 256. With [#60631](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60631), on 99 KiB GPUs, bf16 head sizes 192, 320, 384, 576 and 1024 still fail, and so do fp32 head sizes 320 to 512. bf16 head sizes 320 and 384 also still fail on A100 and H100.

## Claims

- `vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 --runner pooling` now starts and serves embeddings on a GPU with 99 KiB of shared memory, in bf16 (the command from the issue) and in fp32. Before the fix, engine warmup failed with `OutOfResources`.
- On such GPUs, `context_attention_fwd` now launches for every tested bf16/fp16 head size from 160 to 1024 and for fp32 head sizes 320, 384 and 512. All of these failed before.
- Tiles that already launched do not change. Output is bitwise the same for every configuration that worked before.
- `test_context_attention` gets D=256 and D=512. 8 of the new cases fail on the old code on a 99 KiB GPU and pass with the fix.

## Validation

Hardware: 1x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (compute capability 12.0, driver 615.71.09). It has 101376 bytes of opt-in shared memory per block, the same limit as the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 3060 in the issue. Software: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev173+g8cbd5d030` (commit `8cbd5d03006c`), and this change on top of it.

Reproducer. No request is needed, because the failure happens at startup:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 --runner pooling --dtype bfloat16 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"audio":0,"video":0}' --max-model-len 4096
```

Before: all 4 runs failed in engine warmup. 3 ran in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986` image (torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1). 1 ran from an editable install of the same commit.

```
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py", line 784, in _forward_encoder_attention
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py", line 270, in context_attention_fwd
triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 163840, Hardware limit: 101376. Reducing block sizes or `num_stages` may help.
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

After: all 3 runs passed warmup with the same `TRITON_ATTN` backend and reached `Application startup complete`. `POST /v1/embeddings` returned 200 OK. The logs have no `Traceback` and no `OutOfResources`. The same command with `--dtype float32` also starts and serves.

Embedding values: I compared the served embeddings with `transformers` 5.19 in fp32 on CPU (mean pooling, then normalize). Cosine similarity was 0.99996 for the 9-token and 1492-token inputs and 0.99995 for a 4092-token input. The 4092-token input goes past the 512-token sliding window.

Kernel tests:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_prefill_attention.py
```

- With the fix: 41 passed.
- Old kernel file with the new test file (`-k "test_context_attention and not sliding"`): 8 failed, 16 passed. The failures are bf16 D=256 (`Required: 163840`) and fp32 D=512 (`Required: 135168`).
- These tests ran with `--noconftest`, because the test venv did not have `tblib`.
- The new cases fail on the old code only on GPUs with less than 160 KiB per block, such as L4 or RTX cards. On H100 they pass with or without the fix.

Old and new kernel side by side: both ran on the same inputs (sequences of 37, 300 and 700 tokens, 8 query heads, 2 KV heads, non-causal), and each output was compared with fp32 SDPA:

| dtype | head size | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| fp16, bf16 | 32, 64, 80, 96, 128, 512 | OK | OK, bitwise the same |
| fp16, bf16 | 160, 192, 256, 320, 384, 576, 768, 1024 | `OutOfResources` | OK, error 0.0005 (fp16), 0.0036 to 0.0045 (bf16) |
| fp32 | 32 to 256 | OK | OK, bitwise the same |
| fp32 | 320, 384, 512 | `OutOfResources` | OK, error 0.0020 to 0.0025 |
| fp32 | 576, 768, 1024 | `OutOfResources` | `OutOfResources` |

`pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passed.

## Details

Root cause: `context_attention_fwd` sets `BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = BLOCK` from `get_block_size(dtype)`. That returns 128 for bf16/fp16 on any GPU with capability 8.0 or higher, and 32 for fp32. The only other rule is `if Lk >= 512: BLOCK = min(BLOCK, 32)`. The kernel keeps a Q tile, a K tile and a P tile in shared memory. For bf16, head size 256 and BLOCK 128, that is `2 * (128*256 + 128*256 + 128*128) = 163840` bytes. A100 (166912) and H100/B200 (232448) have room for it, but sm_86, sm_89, sm_120 and sm_121 GPUs have only 101376. EmbeddingGemma2 has head size 256 on its sliding layers and 512 on its full layers, so vLLM forces `TRITON_ATTN`. Its bidirectional layers go through `_forward_encoder_attention` → `context_attention_fwd`. The 512 layers already get BLOCK 32 and fit. The 256 layers do not fit. The same problem breaks bf16/fp16 head size 192 and fp32 head size 512 (135168 bytes).

Fix: on CUDA, after the existing choices, halve BLOCK until `element_size * BLOCK * (2 * D + BLOCK)` fits in `get_max_shared_memory_bytes()` (`cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin`). Here D is `next_power_of_2(Lk)`. BLOCK never goes below 16, the smallest tile `tl.dot` accepts. The result is cached per (block, head size, element size), so each call costs one cache lookup.

The formula comes from `_fwd_kernel.warmup().metadata.shared` on sm_120. For large head sizes it matches the real use exactly. For small head sizes it is higher than the real use. This holds for all 60 configurations measured. I do not claim it is an upper bound on every GPU: a review found that it under-counts fp16 use on sm_75, but the tiles it picks there still fit.

Effect on 99 KiB GPUs: head sizes up to 128 keep 128. bf16/fp16 head size 192 or 256 goes from 128 to 64 (73728 bytes). fp32 head size 512 goes from 32 to 16. On A100, bf16 head size 256 keeps 128 and fp32 head size 512 keeps 32.

Limitations:

- ROCm does not change (there is an `is_cuda()` gate). The formula was measured on NVIDIA's Triton backend. On MI300 (65536 bytes of LDS) it would shrink the common head-size-128 tile, and I could not check if that is needed. Head-size-256 encoder attention on 64 KiB ROCm GPUs may have the same bug. I did not test it.
- fp32 with head size above 512 still fails on 99 KiB GPUs, because 16 is the smallest tile. It also failed before this change.
- `get_max_shared_memory_bytes()` reads GPU 0 and keeps the first value it reads. On a host with mixed GPU types, the limit comes from one GPU. Other users of this helper have the same limit.
- The cache key does not include the limit, so a test that mocks a different limit in the same process can get a stale tile. The existing mocked tests `test_kv_tile_width_is_gated_by_platform` and `test_rdna_narrows_the_kv_tile_and_nothing_else` now read the real limit on CUDA. They pass on the RTX 5090. On a GPU with less than 98304 bytes, the `[not-rocm]` case would see tile 64.
