title: [Bugfix][PCP] Align MoE routing padding with gathered tokens
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Purpose

The non-all-to-all PCP path gathers hidden states and router logits across PCP ranks, but the router still reads the rank-local padding mask. With N local rows and P PCP ranks, routing processes P*N rows while the mask still has N entries. CUDA top-k checks that the mask length matches the token count and can raise an `is_padding` size mismatch.

This PR aligns the MoE padding mask with the PCP-gathered token rows and restores the original rank-local mask in a `finally` block. The dispatch/combine interfaces and PCP1/all-to-all paths remain unchanged. Regression tests cover PCP1/2/4, the all-to-all bypass, per-forward caching, and exception cleanup.

A search of open PRs covering PCP padding, PCP MoE, and the relevant padding-cache key found no equivalent fix. Nearby PRs #53639, #60049, and #56258 address different paths.

## Implementation

- Non-all-to-all PCP routing receives a padding mask with the same rank-major layout and row count as the gathered hidden states.
- The original local padding mask is restored on normal and exceptional exits.
- The gathered mask is cached per forward context and reused across MoE calls.

## Validation

### Environment

- Model: official `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603` native FP8 checkpoint.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`.
- Hardware: two nodes, each with 4x NVIDIA H20 GPUs.

### vLLM startup arguments

```bash
# Set MASTER_ADDR to the reachable IP address of the master node.
vllm serve /models/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 19180 \
  --served-model-name mistral-small4-pcp-ab \
  --config-format mistral \
  --load-format mistral \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --master-addr "${MASTER_ADDR}" \
  --master-port 29511 \
  --language-model-only \
  --enforce-eager \
  --attention-backend TRITON_MLA \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

### Result

**Without this fix** (baseline): 
With the unmodified image and model, all seven native weight shards loaded (29.34 GiB per rank). The unpatched run then failed during vLLM's standard startup memory profiling, before the API server became ready:

```text
RuntimeError: .../topk_softmax_kernels.cu:785, is_padding size mismatch, expected: 4096
```

**With this PR**:
Applying the `_sequence_parallel_context` change from this PR at startup allowed the TP2/PCP2 deployment to start and generate successfully. It passed all five chat smoke requests, including a 2,235-token input and concurrent requests of different lengths.

Using the official `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` scoring logic, we evaluated all 1,319 test examples with 5-shot prompts, temperature=0, seed=42, `max_tokens=256`, and concurrency=4. Results:

| Run  | GSM8K | Invalid answers | Runtime result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Baseline + TP4/PCP1 | 1191/1319 (90.2957%) | 0 | Full evaluation completed; 0 API errors and 0 Pod restarts |
| Baseline + TP2/PCP2 | Could not run | — | Failed during startup profiling with the padding-size mismatch above |
| This PR applied + TP2/PCP2 | 1197/1319 (90.7506%) | 0 | Full evaluation completed; 0 API errors and 0 Pod restarts |

AI assistance was used to extract the change, prepare regression tests and run the validation described above. The human submitter retains responsibility for line-by-line review and final sign-off.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Restore AXK1 config defaults dropped with the vendored config
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Default `scoring_func` to `sigmoid` and `topk_method` to `noaux_tc` in `AXK1MoE`
- Default `moe_layer_freq` to 1 in `AXK1DecoderLayer._is_layer_sparse`
- Drop the asserts that these fields exist on the config

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60623 replaced vLLM's vendored `AXK1Config` with the one from Transformers. The vendored class gave defaults for `scoring_func`, `topk_method` and `moe_layer_freq`, but the Transformers class doesn't define these fields, so any AXK1 config that leaves them out now fails with `AttributeError` while the model is being built. The official checkpoint sets them explicitly, so it still loads, but the minimal config in `test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` doesn't, and that test has been failing since the change landed: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93915/list?jid=01a12348-9645-4aec-9354-4373972e9a30. This reads the fields with `getattr` and falls back to the old defaults, the same pattern `deepseek_v2.py` uses. The defaults also match what the Transformers AXK1 model always does: sigmoid routing with a score-correction bias, and an MoE layer on every layer from `first_k_dense_replace` onward.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Bound prefix cache reuse by the first requested prompt score
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Overview

With `prompt_logprob_token_ids` and `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False`, a cache hit can skip requested scores. Cap prefix reuse at `prompt_logprob_start` so those rows are recomputed.

## Claims

Reuse the unscored prefix without dropping requested scores. Cache reads remain disabled by default for prompt scoring.

## Validation

Ten targeted cases, the Qwen3-0.6B model test and pre-commit passed. Batch-invariant scores matched exactly, including a single-host NIXL check. Default BF16 returned complete scores but differed by up to 0.29844; the cause remains unresolved.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction: environment, complete script and before/after results</summary>

On main `ab905a885d`, real Qwen3-0.6B/MMLU scoring reproduced:

```text
AssertionError: Missing scores: skip_cache=False, cached=32, first_scored_row=27
```

With candidate `6344014bb8`, 32 requests containing 184 scored rows matched exactly across eight cache-on/cache-off runs in batch-invariant mode. They also matched main with cache reads disabled. Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`; dataset: `cais/mmlu`, revision `c30699e8356da336a370243923dbaf21066bb9fe`, first eight high_school_biology/test questions and all four options. Hardware: RTX 5090; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. This checks score completeness and consistency, not MMLU accuracy.

A separate default compiled/CUDA graph run passed start offsets 0, 31, 32 and 33, with 0, 16, 32 and 32 cached tokens respectively. The cached scores matched uncached scores at the existing numerical tolerances.

A later H200 check with Qwen3-0.6B and three candidate IDs returned the complete
123-row matrix and reused 16 tokens. Default BF16 execution differed from the
uncached scores by up to 0.29844, failing `atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3`. The same test
with batch-invariant execution matched exactly. This does not establish default
execution score equivalence or fully attribute the numerical difference.

Historical regression validation of `6344014bb8` first recorded 317 passed and
69 failed. After unsetting the allocator environment configuration, rerunning
the 69 failed cases passed. This covers 386 cases across two runs, not a single
clean run. The corresponding manual pre-commit hooks also passed:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files vllm/sampling_params.py vllm/v1/request.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
```

The follow-up adds the connector-admission fallback and updates the existing
model test and documentation. Its targeted checks on one H200 were:

```bash
python -m pytest -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p pytest_mock -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_fixed_token_scores_reuse_only_unscored_prefix \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_kv_connector_honors_skip_reading_prefix_cache
python -m pytest -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p pytest_mock -q \
  tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_preserve_scores_with_prefix_cache
```

The first two tests passed all ten parameterized cases. The final model test
sets batch-invariant execution and spawn internally and passed independently.
The full historical regression suite was not rerun for this follow-up.

Supplemental validation outside the repository tests used a single H200 and
two Qwen3-0.6B instances with NIXL 1.5.0,
UCX, eager execution and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. An ordinary request
transferred 141 prompt tokens' KV to the cold decoder. With
`prompt_logprob_start=17` and candidate IDs `[10, 100, 1000]`, both instances
returned finite `123 × 3` score matrices, exactly matching the explicit
no-cache reference. The scored decoder read zero remote blocks; it only
notified the prefiller to release them. The probe exited on an overly strict
assertion that disallowed this notification hook; CPU replay of the saved
outputs and transfer logs passed the corrected checks. This validates the
dense-model fallback, not Mamba backoff, multi-host RDMA or default-mode
numerical equivalence.

Save the script below as `reproduce.py` outside the checkout. Use an installed build of the selected vLLM revision with `numpy`, `transformers`, `pyarrow` and `huggingface_hub` available. Download the pinned MMLU input beside the script:

```python
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
import shutil
revision = "c30699e8356da336a370243923dbaf21066bb9fe"
shutil.copyfile(hf_hub_download(
    "cais/mmlu", "high_school_biology/test-00000-of-00001.parquet",
    repo_type="dataset", revision=revision,
), "mmlu.parquet")
```

Run the same script from that directory against baseline `ab905a885dfbfc60a2c02286cc9c608c93884de3`, then against the candidate with this patch applied:

```bash
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 python reproduce.py result.json
```

The model resolves to the pinned public revision in the script. The validation used local cached copies of those same model and dataset revisions.

```python
import argparse
import atexit
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams, TokensPrompt


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    model = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
    revision = "c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca"
    data = pq.read_table(Path(__file__).with_name("mmlu.parquet")).slice(0, 8).to_pylist()
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, revision=revision)
    prompts, starts = [], []
    for row in data:
        context = tokenizer.encode("Question: " + row["question"] + "\nAnswer:", add_special_tokens=False)
        for option in row["choices"]:
            suffix = tokenizer.encode(" " + option, add_special_tokens=False)
            ids = (context + suffix)[-4095:]
            prompts.append(TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids))
            starts.append(len(ids) - len(suffix) - 1)
    assert len(prompts) == 32 and min(starts) >= 0
    llm = LLM(
        model=model, revision=revision, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=4096,
        max_num_seqs=128, max_num_batched_tokens=8192,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.65, enforce_eager=True, seed=233,
    )
    atexit.register(llm.llm_engine.engine_core.shutdown, timeout=30)
    arms = []
    # The first pair warms scorer kernels; retain three further pairs for timing.
    for skip in [True, False] * 4:
        assert llm.reset_prefix_cache()
        llm.generate(prompts, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1), use_tqdm=False)
        params = [
            SamplingParams(
                temperature=0, max_tokens=1, prompt_logprob_start=start,
                prompt_logprob_token_ids=[[token] for token in p["prompt_token_ids"][start + 1:]],
                skip_reading_prefix_cache=skip,
            )
            for p, start in zip(prompts, starts)
        ]
        begin = time.perf_counter()
        outputs = llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - begin
        rows = []
        for output, p, start in zip(outputs, prompts, starts):
            scores = output.prompt_token_id_logprobs
            assert scores is not None, (
                f"Missing scores: skip_cache={skip}, cached={output.num_cached_tokens}, "
                f"first_scored_row={start}"
            )
            assert scores.shape == (len(p["prompt_token_ids"]) - start - 1, 1)
            assert 0 <= (output.num_cached_tokens or 0) <= start
            rows.append({"scores": scores.tolist(), "cached_tokens": output.num_cached_tokens})
        arms.append({"skip_cache": skip, "elapsed_s": elapsed, "rows": rows})
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps({"prompts": prompts, "starts": starts, "arms": arms}))
        print("ARM", len(arms), skip, elapsed, sum(r["cached_tokens"] or 0 for r in rows), flush=True)
    for arm in arms[1:]:
        for reference, actual in zip(arms[0]["rows"], arm["rows"]):
            np.testing.assert_allclose(actual["scores"], reference["scores"], atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3)
    assert any(r["cached_tokens"] for r in arms[1]["rows"])
    print("INTERVAL_OK", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Candidate success marker (excerpt from the original log):

```text
INTERVAL_OK
```

The MMLU and historical regression results above cover `6344014bb8`, before the
connector-admission follow-up. The separate compiled boundary run covered that
earlier product code before repository tests were simplified.

</details>

## Details

Both cache lookup paths use the same limit. Ordinary `prompt_logprobs` disable reuse. Connector requests set the skip flag before admission to prevent prompt truncation; MoRIIO's existing hybrid-producer hook ignores this flag and remains unverified.

Repository tests cover cache boundaries, connector admission and batch-invariant scoring. MMLU, compiled-boundary and NIXL runs are supplemental checks.

title: [Fast Start][Bugfix] Snapshot GPU memory after external weights are ready
author: UNIDY2002
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When the IPC weight-cache daemon loads zero-copy weights concurrently with engine startup, the current initialization order counts the daemon's late allocations twice. This can leave no valid memory budget for the KV cache even though the GPU has enough free memory.

## Claims

- Take `init_snapshot` after external weight memory is ready.
- Restore automatic KV-cache sizing for static EP IPC loading.

## Validation

```text
python3 -m pytest -q -s tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k qwen3-ep --timeout=1800
```

With a real Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct MoE model used by #57320, TP=2, EP enabled, and the fixed KV-cache override temporarily removed in the validation harness: `1 passed, 15 deselected`. Baseline, cold fallback, warm zero-copy, and zero-copy restart all produced identical outputs; both zero-copy runs mapped 676 tensors per rank. Automatic sizing reported about 28 GiB of available KV-cache memory and 611,440 KV-cache tokens. The test file is unchanged in this PR.

## Details

Assume 100 GiB total memory and `gpu_memory_utilization=90%`:

```text
Memory usage
100 ┤
 90 ┤──────────────────────────────── budget limit
 80 ┤
 75 ┤                         ┌──────────────┐
 70 ┤                         │ daemon 50    │
 60 ┤                         │ engine 25    │
 50 ┤               ┌─────────┴──────────────┘
 40 ┤               │ daemon 50
 30 ┤               │
 20 ┤     ┌─────────┘
 10 ┤     │ daemon 20
  0 ┼─────┴────────────────────────────────────→ time
       t0              t1                 t2
   snapshot        daemon ready       profiling
```

At `t0`, the daemon uses 20 GiB, so `init_snapshot` records 80 GiB free. At `t1`, daemon loading completes at 50 GiB and `get_memory()` reports 50 GiB. At `t2`, the engine itself uses 25 GiB, so the actual total is 75 GiB.

The target budget is 90 GiB. The intended engine budget is `90 - 50 = 40 GiB`, but profiling measures `80 - 25 = 55 GiB` from the old snapshot. That 55 GiB includes the daemon's late 30 GiB allocation and the engine's 25 GiB allocation. The daemon's 30 GiB is therefore charged once through `get_memory()` and again through the profiling delta. The resulting requested KV-cache budget is reduced by 30 GiB too much; in the real Qwen3 EP test it became `-2.46 GiB`, so KV-cache initialization failed.

With the snapshot taken after daemon readiness, the profiling delta is `50 - 25 = 25 GiB`, which measures only engine allocations. The external-weight deduction and profiling baseline then describe the same memory state.

author: hpdkhoa
body:
## Overview The Step3 tool parser silently drops any parameter whose value contains `<`. This PR makes the parameter regex match up to the closing tag instead of the first `<`. ## Claims - Step3 tool calls keep parameter values that contain `<`, such as `a < 5` or `hi`, in streaming and non-streaming mode. - Values without `<` parse exactly as before. ## Validation New unit test `test_parameter_value_with_angle_bracket`, run in both streaming and non-streaming mode: ```bash python -m pytest -q tests/tool_parsers/test_step3_tool_parser.py ``` | | Result | |---|---| | Before (test only) | `2 failed, 9 passed, 8 xfailed`: `assert {} == {'sql': 'SELECT * FROM t WHERE a < 5', 'html': 'hi'}` | | After | `11 passed, 8 xfailed` | The 8 xfails already exist on main and are unchanged. End-to-end check with a Step3 model (`tool_choice="auto"`, a tool with a string parameter, prompt asking for a SQL query with `<`): Parser check with the real Step3 tokenizer (`stepfun-ai/step3`). A tool call whose `sql` value contains `<` goes through `run_tool_extraction`, the helper the tool parser tests use, in both modes: | Mode | `main` (`arguments`) | This PR (`arguments`) | |---|---|---| | non-streaming | `{}` | `{"sql": "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total < 100"}` | | streaming | `{}` | `{"sql": "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total < 100"}` | On `main` the call is still emitted, but its arguments come back empty, so a client runs the tool with no input. Not run end to end: Step3 has 321B parameters and I have no hardware that can serve it. The change is confined to the parameter regex, which the check above drives with the model's real tokenizer.
Reproduction script import json from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer from vllm.tool_parsers import ToolParserManager from tests.tool_parsers.utils import run_tool_extraction tok = get_tokenizer("stepfun-ai/step3") out = ("<｜tool_calls_begin｜><｜tool_call_begin｜>function<｜tool_sep｜>" '' 'SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total < 100' "<｜tool_call_end｜><｜tool_calls_end｜>") for streaming in (False, True): parser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("step3")(tok) _, calls = run_tool_extraction(parser, out, streaming=streaming) print(streaming, [json.loads(c.function.arguments or "{}") for c in calls])
## Details Root cause: `_parse_steptml_invoke` matched values with `([^<]*)`, so the regex failed on any value containing `<` and the parameter was skipped without a log line. The value group is now `(.*?)` with `re.DOTALL`. It ends at the first ``, and multi-line values still match as before. Limit: a value that contains the literal text `` still ends early. The format has no escaping, so this cannot be fixed in the parser. Not a duplicate: I searched open and closed PRs for "step3 tool parser" and issues and PRs for "steptml". #49567 (whitespace in Step3 values) only removes `.strip()` and keeps `[^<]*`. #55115 and #57809 change streaming bookkeeping, not the regex. #55175 changes test fixtures only. No issue reports this bug. Co-author: Claude ---

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Use embedding_dim for pooling output size
author: Neuro1729
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60977.

`ModelConfig.embedding_size` can report the transformer hidden size instead of the final embedding width for pooling models with an output projection.

For `google/embeddinggemma-2`, this results in a reported size of 512 instead of 768, causing `PoolingParams(dimensions=768)` to fail validation.

## Claims

This change uses `embedding_dim` as a fallback for pooling models before falling back to `hidden_size`.

The existing precedence for explicit `embedding_size` values and Sentence-Transformers Dense modules is preserved. Generation runners are unaffected.

## Validation

**Tests**

```bash
pytest -q tests/test_pooling_params.py
# 14 passed
```

Added network-free tests:

- `test_pooling_embedding_dim_preferred_over_hidden_size_without_network`
- `test_matryoshka_accepts_native_embedding_width_without_network`

These cover the `embedding_dim` fallback, override/Dense/generate precedence, and Matryoshka dims 128/256/512/768 (with 0/769 rejected).

**GPU reproduction (RTX A5000)**

| Dimensions | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default | 768 | 768 |
| 128 | Pass | Pass |
| 256 | Pass | Pass |
| 512 | Pass | Pass |
| 768 | Validation error | Pass |
| 769 | Rejected | Rejected |

The resulting embeddings were also compared against Hugging Face, with cosine similarity ≥ 0.99997 in the tested cases.

Ruff lint and formatting checks passed.

## Details

The current fallback in `ModelConfig.embedding_size` uses `get_hidden_size()` when neither an explicit override nor a Sentence-Transformers Dense module is available.

That assumption doesn't hold for models such as EmbeddingGemma 2, where a final projection changes the embedding width.

The patch checks `hf_text_config.embedding_dim` (or top-level `embedding_dim`) for pooling runners before using the hidden size.

Other pooling models exposing this configuration field may also be affected; EmbeddingGemma 2 is the reproduced case.

The unrelated Triton shared-memory issue #60847 is outside the scope of this PR.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and testing.

### E2E Test
vllm version: 0.31.0(https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6)
Model: Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B
Python: 3.12.14
PyTorch: 2.13.0
GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB
CUDA graph: full and piecewise
| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 concurrent requests, mixed ~5s / ~14s unique audios (deterministic crash case) | 8/8 HTTP 500, EngineCore dead | **8/8 OK**, 0 exceptions in logs |
| Single-request multi-clip (unequal clips) — regression check on the 3-D path | OK | **OK** |
| Single clip (batch of one, `unsqueeze` path) — regression check | OK | **OK** |

## Details


### Root Cause
1. The multimodal registry declares `input_audio_features` as `FieldLayout::Batched`, so the Rust frontend emits one item per clip — a 2-D `[n_mels, padded_seq]` tensor, padded to the request's longest clip.
2. The model contract is `MultiModalFieldConfig.flat_from_sizes(..., dim=1)`: a single flat `[n_mels, total_seq]` tensor.
3. `_reduce_data` stacks only when all shapes are equal; unequal durations (or unequal intra-request padding) → `return batch` raw list.
4. The parser's guard only matches `torch.Tensor` with `dim() == 3`; the list falls through and dies in TensorSchema validation.


## Why this is not a duplicate
Following PR (before 2026.10.10) are related but none of them solved this problem.
- #50958 — canonical model-side fix for familiar bug of Gemma series model. Not involved rust frontend.
- #57146  — It addresses Python preprocessing parity but does not add ragged-list handling or change the Rust preprocessing path.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MiniMax-M3] Reject unbuilt index-head counts in the AITER indexer
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

The MiniMax-M3 AITER indexer selector now rejects index-head counts AITER has no kernels for. At attention TP=1 (4 index heads per rank), the server now fails at load with a clear error instead of crashing on the first decode step.

## Claims

- `aiter_indexer_unsupported_reason` accepts only 1 or 2 index heads, the counts AITER builds its MSA score kernels for (`SPARSE_DECODE_TABLE`/`SPARSE_PREFILL_TABLE`, unchanged from the `v0.1.24.post1` pin through AITER main).
- A new regression test in `test_minimax_m3.py` fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950). At TP=1, `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` crashed before the fix at the first forward with `pa_sparse_block_score_decode: no build for num_idx_heads=4`. With the fix it refuses to start with a configuration error. `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` passed 10/10 runs.

At TP=2 the same AITER kernels run before and after. I ran 5 interleaved runs per column, each with a fresh server, using `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` and the fp8 index cache. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 256 out, conc 16) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 2.366 ± 0.007 | 2.365 ± 0.009 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 18.83 ± 0.73 | 18.53 ± 0.86 |

| gsm8k (5-shot, n=1319) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match | 0.8799 ± 0.0089 | 0.8708 ± 0.0089 |

The gsm8k difference is not significant (Welch p ≈ 0.14).

## Details

The selector only rejected head counts above the 16 MFMA columns, so 4 heads got through and failed inside AITER's kernel dispatch. A rejected config falls back to the platform-neutral indexer, which turns this case into a load-time error. TP ≥ 2 still gives each rank 1 or 2 heads, so it keeps the AITER path. The test asks the selector instead of naming an architecture, so it keeps working as more CDNA targets are added. No open PR fixes this. If #57909 (which moves this selector to `indexer_msa.py`) lands first, the guard belongs there.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Fuse GLM-5.3 KDA q|k|v convs into one conv1d parameter
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Overview

`Glm5NextLinearAttention` cached the merged q|k|v conv weight on the first forward, so an RL refit left the conv kernels reading stale values (#55087). This PR replaces the three `q/k/v_conv1d` modules with a single `conv1d` parameter of shape `[3 * C_local, 1, K]`, which the kernels read directly. Checkpoint `q_conv1d` / `k_conv1d` / `v_conv1d` weights load into it as shards 0/1/2 through `stacked_params_mapping`, using the `_make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader` already used by Kimi-Linear KDA and OLMo-Hybrid GDN. There is no second tensor to keep in sync, so every write path lands in the tensor the kernels read, at a fixed address.

Alternative fixes for the same issue: #56298 and #57638 (see Details; their authors are co-authors on the commit). The fused-parameter design was suggested by hao-aaron in review and replaces this PR's first approach (parameter views into a merged buffer), which broke under weight offloading and `ipc_cache` copy mode.

## Claims

- After `load_weights` / `reload_weights` (checkpoint or kernel format), GLM-5.3 KDA decode uses the refitted conv weights, in eager mode **and** with the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs.
- The conv weight keeps its address across refits, so FULL decode graphs captured before a refit stay valid.
- Works with `--cpu-offload-gb` (with and without refit) and with `--load-format ipc_cache` in both `copy` and `zero_copy` modes.
- No numerical change: the per-rank layout is `[q_r | k_r | v_r]`, the same as the old `torch.cat`. Direct-load outputs are identical to `main`. One copy of the conv weights is dropped.

## Validation

Hardware: GB300 (SM100), TP1, 4-layer pruned GLM-5.3-Flash at full width (`JaredforReal/GLM-5.3-Flash-4L`).

```
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py -v
```

- Unit tests (CPU, `conv1d` sub-module): checkpoint q/k/v shards (2D and 3D) land in q|k|v order; `load_weights`-style refit and a real `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload` cycle update the weight without moving it. 22 passed with `test_kda_recurrent.py`.
- `test_refit_reaches_cudagraph_decode[cpu_offload_gb=0|10]` (pruned model, default cudagraphs, one engine per case): direct load -> reference tokens; `reload_weights` of the checkpoint with the conv weights x2 -> output changes; checkpoint as-is -> == reference; kernel-format `reload_weights(is_checkpoint_format=False)` on `conv1d.weight` x2 / x0.5 -> changes / == reference; the conv weight address is identical after all four refits. 2 passed (~5 min each, mostly startup). On `main` the first refit step fails (#55087).
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: passed (ruff, mypy, SPDX, test tethering).

CI note: the e2e test is the first in `tests/models/glm5next` to use the pruned checkpoint (19 GB download, needs SM90/SM100, skipped elsewhere). It runs in the existing `glm5next-unit-tests` step; the two offload cases take about 10 min together on GB300, mostly engine startup. #57537 adds a dedicated step for pruned-checkpoint e2e tests that this test could move to once it lands.

Full refit flow, 3 prompts x 24 greedy tokens, compared with `main` direct load:

| tree | config | direct load | dummy -> `reload_weights()` | `load_weights` partial update / kernel-format refit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | cudagraphs | reference | wrong (#55087) | wrong |
| previous revision (buffer views) | cudagraphs | == main | == main | == main |
| previous revision (buffer views) | `cpu_offload_gb=10` | **wrong** | – | – |
| this PR | cudagraphs | == main | == main | == main |
| this PR | eager | == main | == main | == main |
| this PR | `cpu_offload_gb=10` | == main | – | – |

After the reload, every language-model parameter and buffer checksum equals a fresh load.

`--load-format ipc_cache` (a `vllm preload` daemon per GPU, default cudagraphs). After each refit the check compares the conv weight the kernel reads against the checkpoint × scale (max abs diff), then compares the output:

| tree | mode | load | kernel-format refit x2 / x1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | copy | == main | weight stale (diff 0.72), output unchanged (#55087) |
| previous revision (buffer views) | copy | == main | **weight stale (diff 0.72), output unchanged** |
| previous revision (buffer views) | zero_copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main |
| this PR | copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main, address unchanged |
| this PR | zero_copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main, address unchanged |

Checkpoint-format refits are not supported on an `ipc_cache`-loaded model on `main` either, so they're not compared here. `_apply_entries` re-registers every parameter as a plain `nn.Parameter` (399/399 lose `weight_loader`), so `load_weights` of any stacked weight raises `AttributeError` (verified on `main` with `self_attn.q_proj`), and the layerwise `reload_weights` fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor`. On `main` the three conv weights happened to fall through to `default_weight_loader`; with this PR they're stacked like the other projections. Making checkpoint-format refit work after `ipc_cache` is a separate issue.

## Details

**Root cause.** The KDA layer runs one causal conv over the concatenated q|k|v channels. The merged weight was built lazily on the first forward with `torch.cat` and cached, so later writes to `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` (RL refit through the weight-transfer engines, `reload_weights`, or kernel-format `copy_`) never reached it.

**Why not invalidate the cache (#56298, #57638).** Both PRs drop the cached tensor on refit and rebuild it on the next forward. That works with `enforce_eager=True`, but with the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs the KDA forward is captured inside the FULL decode graphs, which keep the old tensor's address, so decode replays never see the rebuilt weight.

**Why one parameter instead of views into a merged buffer.** Views only hold while nothing replaces a parameter's storage. The UVA and prefetch CPU offloaders set each parameter's `.data` right after the layer is built, and the `ipc_cache` loader in copy mode clones every entry separately; either way the three weights stop aliasing the tensor the kernels read. With a single parameter, those paths, the layerwise reload, and kernel-format `copy_` all write the tensor the kernels use. This matches how Kimi-Linear and OLMo-Hybrid already store their fused short convs.

**Trade-offs.**
- The vLLM parameter name changes from `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` to `conv1d.weight`. Checkpoint-format updates keep the HF names and go through the stacked mapping. Kernel-format writers need the fused name, and GLM-5.3 artifacts saved with vLLM parameter names (`sharded_state`, vLLM-serialized tensorizer) before this change will not load.
- Open PRs #59304 (KCP) and #57496 (CPU KDA backend) reference `q_conv1d` / `_merged_conv_weight` and will need a small rebase.

**Not covered here.** The TP2 cudagraph reload drift from the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP8 MoE `gemm1_clamp_limit` tensor and the DSA indexer's lazily cached `_wp_fp32` are separate issues, left for follow-ups.

title: [Bugfix][Weight Cache] Include RoPE parameters in IPC cache key
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Prevent IPC weight cache reuse across different text RoPE configurations, which could otherwise cause engines to use incompatible cached rotary buffers.

## Claims

- Reject incompatible RoPE configurations through the existing cache-key mismatch and disk fallback handling.
- Preserve cache reuse for matching configurations, including explicitly specified defaults.
- Preserve standalone in-place weight reloading when model construction normalizes RoPE parameters.

## Validation

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py \
  -k 'not cold_start_and_warm_restart' -q
```

18 passed, 3 deselected. Tests cover RoPE configuration differences, explicit defaults, nested multimodal text configs, and startup versus reload matching.

Separately validated with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on an H800 (TP=1, V1 runner, eager mode):

- Matching configurations load through IPC and match normal disk loading.
- Different theta values raise a configuration mismatch when fallback is disabled.
- With fallback enabled, both `zero_copy` and `copy` modes match normal loading with the requested configuration in generated token IDs and prompt logprobs.

A CPU regression check using the DeepseekV2 attention constructor and IPC protocol verified that standalone `load_weights` accepts constructor-normalized RoPE parameters and rejects mismatched theta values.

All applicable pre-commit checks passed. The three existing model E2E tests were not run. GPU validation covers startup, not in-place reloading.

## Details

The daemon exports non-persistent buffers, including rotary caches, but `WeightCacheKey` previously omitted RoPE parameters. Engines using the same checkpoint with different RoPE settings could therefore reuse incompatible buffers.

Add a fingerprint of `hf_text_config.rope_parameters` to the cache key. For standalone in-place reloading, also accept the daemon's post-construction RoPE fingerprint, since model constructors can normalize these parameters. Startup still requires the original fingerprint, and all other cache-key checks remain unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Own SHM out-of-band buffers before releasing read slots
author: hubert-marek
body:
## Overview

Fix retained NumPy arrays changing after `MessageQueue.dequeue()` releases their shared-memory ring slot. Copy out-of-band buffers before releasing the slot, following the ownership rule used for Torch tensors in #48442.

## Claims

- Received out-of-band arrays retain their values after ring reuse, including writable and read-only NumPy arrays.
- Torch reconstruction reuses the owned `bytearray`, avoiding a second copy. The wire format, inline pickle payload, and ZMQ receive paths remain unchanged.

## Validation

Added a deterministic regression in `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`: two SHM cases using `uint16`, covering writable and read-only arrays. It retains a received array while reusing a one-slot queue, then checks that its values and writability remain correct. The broader dtype/transport matrix was used as a development control, not retained in CI.

A separate real-queue reproducer sent a valid `[2048, 48, 10]` uint16 routing array in `(WorkerProc.ResponseStatus.SUCCESS, ModelRunnerOutput)`, retained it, cycled the ten-slot ring, and sent a smaller valid routing message. Sender data remained unchanged in every case:

| Receive path | Invalid retained IDs (>511) |
|---|---:|
| Baseline | 1,430 |
| Baseline + sender-copy control matching #53217 | 1,430 |
| This fix | 0 |

CPU copy-cost microbenchmark: one writer/local reader, one SHM slot, five trials of 100 measured messages after five warmups per trial. Values are median dequeue time; parentheses show the range of trial medians. This measures transport overhead, not serving throughput.

| NumPy payload | Baseline dequeue (ms) | Fixed dequeue (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 MiB | 0.0181 (0.0180–0.0184) | 0.0792 (0.0790–0.0804) |
| 2 MiB | 0.0209 (0.0204–0.0219) | 0.1754 (0.1753–0.1758) |
| 8 MiB | 0.0228 (0.0223–0.0230) | 0.6334 (0.6331–0.6335) |

### Qwen3.8 Flash Next GPU validation

[Reproduction scripts and all measurements](https://gist.github.com/aoshen02/43ed12722a1a724519c2cb5897b40562).

One node with **4 GB200 GPUs**, Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next revision `09c48120cd32ed3a6f9bb1506035015135ced7a3`, BF16, TP4 + EP, AsyncLLM/Multiproc, async scheduling, R3 and prefix caching enabled. Pinned image source `2eb491e18`; its queue file is byte-identical to this PR's base. Only the two ownership expressions differ between arms.

The diagnostic retains actual received R3 arrays and hashes them **before releasing the SHM slot**, then rechecks after subsequent messages. This compares the same execution's data, not separate inference runs:

| Actual large R3 arrays retained | Baseline | Fixed |
|---|---:|---:|
| Arrays whose bytes changed after receipt | **17 / 26** | **0 / 26** |
| Repeated array checks | 5,060 | 5,066 |

The 26 arrays cover 8 warmup text requests, 16 measured text requests and 2 image requests. Both arms passed final shape, dtype and expert-ID bounds; the retention audit catches corruption that bounds checks alone miss.

Separate **uninstrumented** throughput runs: 2,048 input / 256 output tokens, concurrency 32, 64 requests per trial. After a full 64-request warmup, run five trials per arm in fixed-then-baseline order:

| Output tokens/s | Baseline | Fixed |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median | 2,066.7 | 2,076.5 |
| Trial range | 2,049.5–2,069.7 | 2,063.9–2,078.2 |

Median difference **+0.48%**: no throughput regression observed in this workload; not a claim of significant speedup. Each arm also passed two image-request smoke tests. An earlier baseline-first pair used insufficient warmup and showed first-trial drift; all preliminary and final samples are retained in the linked results.

These are synthetic text/image serving-engine tests, **not** the reporter's exact Prime-RL training workload or a language-model task-accuracy benchmark. They establish the SHM lifetime bug and its fix, not that it was the sole cause of a historical training failure.

## Details

`pickle.loads(..., buffers=...)` reconstructs large NumPy arrays from views into the ring slot. Exiting `acquire_read` marks that slot reusable, but downstream consumers can retain the arrays. Later writes then change the already received data. Copying the out-of-band buffers inside the read context gives those consumers independently owned storage. `bytearray` preserves writability; `_rebuild_tensor` can safely reuse it.

This adds one allocation and CPU copy per SHM out-of-band buffer. Remote and overflow ZMQ frames keep their existing ownership behavior; the separate tensor arena is unchanged.

**Duplicate check:** searched open PRs for `shm_broadcast`, NumPy/shared-memory copying, and out-of-band/dequeue lifetime. #53217 fixes sender buffers being mutated during asynchronous ZMQ sends; it does not detach received arrays from reusable SHM slots. The sender-copy control above still reproduces this failure. #48442 protects Torch tensors, but ordinary NumPy arrays bypass its reducer. Nearby #50548 and #50606 concern reader-index retries and queue sizing respectively.

Developed with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) for investigation, implementation, and validation. Submitted as a draft for human review.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Pair non-divisible hybrid MLA block sizes in NixlConnector
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
NixlConnector now pairs P/D blocks of a hybrid MLA model when neither block size divides the other. That happens when P and D run different TP on ROCm. Kimi-K3 with P TP2 (2944-token blocks) and D TP1 (5760) used to fail the handshake and now runs.  Hybrid block sizes follow the TP-sharded SSM page, so P and D pick different sizes when their TP differs. On CUDA, MLA backends force 64-token kernel blocks, so the sizes always divide. ROCm AITER MLA accepts any kernel block size, so `block_size_ratio` asserts. During the handshake, `_split_remote_blocks` now views the remote blocks as gcd-sized kernel blocks (2944 → 23 × 128). The existing `block_size_ratio > 1` path then pairs them with D's 45 sub-blocks and zeroes the untransferred tail. This only applies to hybrid MLA with plainly strided remote regions. With prefix caching on, D still rejects such pairs through the existing hybrid check, as on CUDA.

- Hybrid MLA P/D with non-divisible block sizes transfers in gcd-sized units (128 tokens for Kimi-K3) instead of asserting at the handshake.
- Pairs that work today never reach the new code, so they are unaffected.

On MI355 with AITER MLA:
- `test_prefix_cache.py -k pd-tp2-dep2` (Kimi-K3): failed the handshake before; now 4/4 pass, 10/10 runs.
- Also added a new `test_hetero_non_divisible_block_sizes`: 28 fail before, 28 pass after.

The model-level runs used `moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` with NIXL P/D, 5 interleaved runs per column, each with fresh servers. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 128 out, conc 16) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| P TP2 → D TP1, equal 2048 blocks: req/s | 3.478 ± 0.077 | 3.480 ± 0.045 |
| P TP2 → D TP1, equal 2048 blocks: TPOT (ms) | 29.54 ± 0.65 | 29.36 ± 0.55 |
| P TP2 → D TP1, 1024 → 1920: req/s | handshake assert | 3.432 ± 0.027 |

| gsm8k strict-match (5-shot, n=1319) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| P TP2 → D TP1, equal 2048 blocks | 0.8748 ± 0.0034 | 0.8748 ± 0.0025 |
| P TP2 → D TP1, 1024 → 1920 | handshake assert | 0.8748 ± 0.0020 |
| P TP1 → D TP2, 1920 → 1024 | handshake assert | 0.8732 ± 0.0031 |

The existing ROCm NIXL P/D accuracy groups also pass.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Use the EAGLE replay boundary when retaining sliding-window tails
author: stu-cao
body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeStoreCoordinator.store_mask` mirrors the core's sparse sliding-window retention (`SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask`) so the store keeps the same tails the local prefix cache does. It passed the non-EAGLE replay boundary, `(num_prompt_tokens - 1,)`, while masking with `use_eagle=True`. Under EAGLE the lookup matches one block past the hit and drops back from it, so the core's `replay_boundaries` places the boundary one scheduler block lower; the store did not. For a prompt that is not block-aligned the retained tail therefore ended one block too high, the saved prefix held `need - 1` of the `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) + 1` contiguous blocks the lookup requires, and the joint hit collapsed to 0. Only block-aligned prompts hit.

Affected layout: a full-attention target group plus a sliding-window EAGLE drafter group (DFlash-style, e.g. window 2048 / block 64) with `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`. Same family as #57610 (sparse sliding-window retention keeping a tail exactly `need` blocks long), but on the store side and with a different cause; #57613 composes with this change.

The fix extracts the core rule into a module-level `replay_boundaries()` in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` (called directly from `KVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks`, behaviour unchanged) and calls it from `_reachable_masks`, so the two sides cannot drift again. The non-EAGLE path still yields `(num_prompt_tokens - 1,)`. On a block-aligned prompt the store now also keeps the core's lower "resend" tail: one extra sliding-window tail per aligned prompt, identical to what the local cache retains.

Not a duplicate: #56615 pairs Mamba and attention boundaries for partial-tail handoffs and does not touch the retention boundary; #57444 changes the core boundary alignment for fine-grained hits (same function, orthogonal change; trivial rebase whichever lands first); #46906 sidesteps by making store retention dense; #57613 fixes #57610 inside `reachable_block_mask`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py`: `test_store_mask_retention_interval_zero_eagle_keeps_lookup_tail` (the mask keeps the `need`-block tail at the lowered boundary, for an unaligned and an aligned prompt) and `test_store_mask_retention_interval_zero_eagle_round_trip` (save through `store_mask`, then the EAGLE lookup hits).
- Existing Mooncake coordinator, worker and scheduler unit tests, and `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` + `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache` for the core refactor.

## Test Result

- Direct-call cleanup validation: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q -k "mooncake or retention or eagle or replay"` — 62 passed, 147 deselected. All pre-commit hooks passed on the three changed files. This cleanup used OpenAI Codex assistance.

- On B300: 677 passed across the suites above. The two `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate` cases error identically on `main` in that environment (the test server cannot fetch its Hub model there) and are unrelated.
- On `main` the new tests fail for the unaligned prompt (mask mismatch; hit 0); with this change they pass.
- Lint: ruff check / format and mypy pass.
- Model output is unaffected: retention only decides which already-computed blocks the store keeps.

AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude (Anthropic) under human direction; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, who ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Fix FlashInfer attention and ReplaySSM warmups on MRV2
author: njhill
body:
FlashInfer attention warmup:
- The warmup ran a hard-coded 16-token mixed dummy batch without clamping to `max_num_batched_tokens`. On V1 this tripped the `num_tokens <= max_num_tokens` assert; on MRV2 `make_dummy` silently sliced input buffers shorter than `query_start_loc`, failing later in FlashInfer forward (`prefill_query.shape[0] == num_prefill_tokens`). Seen on Blackwell, where FlashInfer is the default, e.g. `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py`.
- MRV2's `_dummy_run` ignored `create_mixed_batch`, so the warmup never ran a mixed prefill+decode batch.

Add `mixed_batch_attention_warmup()`, used by the FlashInfer and MiniMax M3 MSA warmups. It clamps the token count, keeps the V1 mixed dummy batch, and on MRV2 uses `run_mixed_prefill_decode_warmup()` (skipping when that can't run). MRV2's `_dummy_run` now asserts the token budget like V1.

ReplaySSM autotune:
- MRV2 profile dummy runs drop Mamba metadata, so the FlashInfer ReplaySSM autotune never ran the ReplaySSM kernel on MRV2 and `valid_dummy_state_slots` had no effect. Keep Mamba metadata for profile runs that set `valid_dummy_state_slots`.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Keep input_ids on later PP stages for raw-token models
author: booth-algo
body:
## Overview

Model Runner V2 drops `input_ids` on every pipeline stage after the first, so models that set
`requires_raw_input_tokens` (they read token ids inside their decoder layers) cannot run with
`--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`. This keeps `input_ids` on later stages for those models, as Model Runner V1
already does. Fixes #55515.

## Claims

- MRV2 with pipeline parallelism works for models that set `requires_raw_input_tokens` (DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1
  vision variants, Qwen4Exp with N-gram PLE, Voxtral realtime): later stages receive `input_ids` in the execute
  path and in CUDA graph capture.
- Other models are unchanged: later stages still get `input_ids=None`.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 x PP2 + EP, 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), max-model-len 1M, CUDA graphs,
no speculative decoding. Same image both times; only the two files in this PR differ.

| | Startup | Smoke (25k- and 60k-token prompts) | Needle at 20/50/90% of a 22.5k-token prompt | ITL p50, bs1 / bs16 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| upstream main | fails: every PP rank 1 worker raises `ValueError: DeepSeek V4 vision MoE routing requires input_ids.` | – | – | – |
| this PR | serves (health OK after 250 s) | pass | 3/3 found | 11.1 / 17.7 ms per token |

<details><summary>Build and reproduction</summary>

Base: vLLM nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-7d0b4e57aac4c4323225b0eee9ae960ce75ffffe` with FlashInfer
0.7.1 (for the sm_120 sparse-MLA decode shapes). DeepSeek-V4.1 on sm_120 with PP also needs fixes that are not on
main yet, so the validation build is our fork branch
[`quettaflop/vllm:sm120-dsv41-main`](https://github.com/quettaflop/vllm/tree/sm120-dsv41-main) on that commit. It
includes per-stage KV tensor placement (same fix as #60569) and 64-row sparse-MLA/indexer pages on sm_120 (same
issue as #60762 / #56509), plus other DeepSeek-V4.1 changes. Between the two runs only the two files in this PR
differ.

    vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
      --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 64 --block-size 64 \
      --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41"}' \
      --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41

</details>

`pre-commit run` passes on the changed files. CI test: `test_distributed_oot_pp_raw_input_tokens` in
`tests/distributed/test_distributed_oot.py` serves a dummy OPT from the `vllm_add_dummy_model` plugin that sets
`requires_raw_input_tokens = True` and asserts `input_ids` is not None, with PP=2 on MRV2, eager and with CUDA
graphs, in the 2×L4 plugin step. Without the fix both cases fail on the PP rank 1 worker; reverting only the
`cudagraph_utils.py` change fails the CUDA-graph case during capture. It passes in
[Buildkite build 94033](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94033). A dummy model is used because DeepSeek
V4/V4.1's sparse MLA kernels need sm90+ and the step runs on L4.

## Details

Root cause: `GPUModelRunner.execute_model` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) and
`ModelCudaGraphManager.capture` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`) set `model_inputs["input_ids"] = None`
on every non-first PP rank. Every rank still prepares the same input batch, so the ids are already in the input
buffer there; MRV1 passes them to all ranks (the text-only branch of `gpu_model_runner.py`). The new condition
reuses `requires_raw_input_tokens`, the check MRV2 already applies on the first rank when it passes
`inputs_embeds`.

Relation to open PRs: #55520 (DeepSeek V4) and #56444 (Qwen4Exp) relay `input_ids` through `IntermediateTensors`
per model, and #60234 forbids PLE layers on later ranks. This change fixes the runner once, with no extra
inter-stage transfer and no per-model code; the input_ids relays in those PRs become unnecessary, while their
other fixes (KV allocation, MTP drafter) are independent.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Serve and store OffloadingConnector partial tails with EAGLE/MTP groups
author: kimseunghyun-kr
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Problem.** With an EAGLE/MTP draft model and `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, the native CPU `OffloadingConnector` never serves a partial tail. So every hit from the CPU tier stops at a scheduler-block boundary, and the tokens after it are computed again.

**Fix, in three parts:**
1. **Lookup:** look up the tail at the EAGLE proof position, as Mooncake does since #60695.
2. **Store:** fix the store gate. Before, it always skipped the one step that can store the tail.
3. **Store policy:** store an EAGLE tail only for a request that loaded from the CPU tier. Without this, parts 1 and 2 double the GPU → CPU traffic, and serving gets slower (P95 TTFT 13 % higher without it in a same-day control, see Validation).

**Result** (8 × A100, MLPerf agentic, 3 × 60 min per arm): no serving regression; SLO pass 92.42 % against 91.70 % without this PR. The CPU-tier hits now end at partial tails, as designed.

Related: #60533 (core proof), #52832 (producer partial tails), #54165 (a different bug in the same file).

## Claims

- With an EAGLE group and align Mamba, a CPU-tier hit can now end at `prefix_match_unit` granularity, as a GPU prefix-cache hit already does. Before, it ended at a whole scheduler block, minus one more block for the EAGLE pop.
- The EAGLE group's tail is keyed at `boundary + eagle_proof_margin`, the same proof that core uses since #60533. Mamba groups and non-EAGLE groups stay keyed at the boundary.
- The tail is stored on the step that computes the proof.
- With an EAGLE group, only a request that loaded from the CPU tier stores its partial tail.
- No change without an EAGLE group, or where partial tails are not supported (DCP > 1, `blocks_per_chunk > 1`, mixed block sizes, sliding-window groups). No new config option.

## Validation

### Serving A/B

**Setup.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (36 GDN + 12 full-attention layers + 1 MTP layer), TP8 + EP on 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, MTP 3, scheduler block 800 tokens, `prefix_match_unit` 16, `--kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 256`. MLPerf agentic multi-turn workload, 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min per arm, same node type.

**SLO** (Artificial Analysis percentile convention): **P95 TTFT ≤ 2.93 s** and **P95 TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms** (that is, P5 output speed ≥ 46 tokens/s). "SLO pass" below is the share of requests that meet both limits. The SLO holds when SLO pass ≥ 95 %.

| Arm | SLO pass, run 1 / 2 / 3 | Mean | Goodput | CPU → GPU load (whole run) | GPU prefix hit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Without this PR | 92.01 / 90.92 / 92.18 % | 91.70 % | 1.866 req/s | — | — |
| Parts 1 + 2 only (tail stored on every turn) | 85.2 / 87.3 / 87.2 % | 86.6 % | 1.67–1.72 req/s | 19.9 TB | 79.0 % |
| **This PR** (parts 1 + 2 + 3) | 93.49 / 91.93 / 91.84 % | **92.42 %** | **1.922 req/s** | **16.0 TB** | **85.2 %** |

The gain of this PR over "without" (+0.7 points, +3 % goodput) is within about two repeat spreads. So I claim no regression, not a speed-up. The "This PR" arm ran a backport on vLLM 81198e97 with the store policy behind an opt-in flag. On this model every partial tail is an EAGLE tail, so that flag gives the same rule as this PR's default.

**Same-day control (15 Oct, one node, 1 × 60 min per arm, same setup).** The "parts 1 + 2 only" arm above ran on another day; on the same day and node as this PR the gap is smaller:

| Store rule | GPU → CPU store per request | Requests done | Output tok/s per GPU | TTFT P50 / P95 | TPOT P50 / P95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Parts 1 + 2 only (no store gate) | 247 MB | 7,450 | 111.7 | 949 / 2,297 ms | 14.07 / 23.41 ms |
| Store gate `num_locally_computed_tokens >= boundary` (review suggestion) | 247 MB | 7,490 | 111.6 | 935 / 2,203 ms | 14.16 / 23.07 ms |
| **This PR** (store only after a load from the CPU tier) | **126 MB** | **7,721** | **113.6** | 924 / **2,025 ms** | **13.69 / 22.56 ms** |

Part 3 halves the stores and, against no gate, lowers P95 TTFT by 12 % and P95 TPOT by 4 % (one run per arm). The "−5 points" of the 3 × 60 table is not reproduced on a single day; treat it as an upper bound. The review-suggested gate rarely applies here: the stored tail is past the request's GPU prefix hit.

<details>
<summary>Why parts 1 + 2 alone are slower (earlier A/B)</summary>

| Measure | Without this PR | Parts 1 + 2 only |
|---|---|---|
| CPU-tier hit tokens mod 800 | 0 in all snapshots | not 0 (e.g. 224): partial tails are served |
| SLO pass, run 1 / 2 / 3 | 90.0 / 89.2 / 89.5 % | 75.1 / 79.3 / 79.9 % |
| Goodput | 1.83–1.89 req/s | 1.31–1.43 req/s |
| P95 / P99 TTFT | 2.22–2.35 / 3.13–3.58 s | 2.94–4.18 / 5.5–13.9 s |
| P50 / P95 TPOT | 14.1–14.3 / 23.9–24.5 ms | 15.7–16.4 / 29.0–34.0 ms |
| MTP mean acceptance length | 2.676 | 2.676 |
| GPU → CPU store bytes / time | 3.00 TB / 3,814 s | 6.93 TB / 8,196 s |
| Scheduler lookup time (sum) | 1.3 s | 8.4 s |

The tails work: they are stored, found and loaded, and the drafter is unchanged. But each turn stores one new tail block (800 tokens, about 6 MB) in every KV group. Most requests hit the GPU prefix cache on the next turn, so most of these stores are never read. Tail stores were 18,650 (about one per request) and 64.5 % of the 6.93 TB stored. Part 3 removes these stores.

How the bug was found: without this PR, `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` was an exact multiple of 800 in all 17 snapshots of two 3-hour runs (example: 402,580,800 = 503,226 × 800). With part 1 only, it was still a multiple of 800. That pointed to the store gate.

</details>

### Unit tests

All in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`:

| What | Tests |
|---|---|
| Proof key: store and lookup | `test_eagle_proof_margin_follows_core_hit_alignment`, `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_keys_attention_at_proof`, `test_eagle_partial_lookup_loads_attention_proof` |
| Store gate (part 2): round trip | `test_eagle_partial_tail_round_trip_serves_mamba_checkpoint[True]`: fails with part 1 only, passes with part 2 |
| Store only when the proof is in the prompt | `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_needs_proof_in_prompt` (5 cases) |
| Popped chunk looked up once | `test_eagle_partial_lookup_probes_popped_chunk_once` (6 lookups instead of 7; 7 instead of 9) |
| Store policy (part 3) | `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_needs_offload_load` ([False] and [True] cases) |

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| A100 (CUDA), nightly 5555a2d8 image, whole `offloading_connector/` | 589 passed, 0 failed. With #61375 also applied: 590 passed. |
| macOS (CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`), whole `offloading_connector/`, 21 Oct, head 321cd8672 | 603 passed, 2 skipped. Split branches: parts 1 + 2 601 passed; with part 3 603 passed. |
| `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.14.0) | clean |

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/
```

This PR and #61375 (a different bug in `offloading/scheduler.py`) merge without conflicts.

## Details

**Root cause 1: lookup.** `SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec` set `supports_partial_tail = False` when any group was an EAGLE group. For an EAGLE group, the complete-chunk lookup asks for one extra chunk and then drops it. So the hit ended one scheduler block before the last stored chunk, and no partial tail was tried.

**Root cause 2: store gate.**
1. With EAGLE block drop, core stops the prefill at the Mamba checkpoint T = floor(P/h)·h − h.
2. On the next step (tokens T..P), the state is copied (CoW), and the manager hands `(group, cow_block, T)` to the connector one time.
3. The scheduler builds the connector metadata before `_update_after_schedule`, so `num_computed_tokens == T` at that point.
4. So the gate `boundary + margin > num_computed_tokens` reads `T + h > T`. This is always true, so the store is always skipped, and the hand-off does not come again.

**Changes.**
- Remove the EAGLE exclusion from `supports_partial_tail`.
- Key the EAGLE non-recurrent groups at `boundary + margin` in store, lookup and load.
- Margin rule as in core: one hash unit if `cache_hit_alignment_tokens` < block and the group manager supports fine-grained lookup; else one block.
- Widen the partial search by one block, with bridge keys for the dropped chunk. That chunk is looked up once per lookup; a miss skips that block.
- Check the proof against `min(num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens[req_id], num_prompt_tokens)`. The cap keeps the proof out of speculative tokens.
- With an EAGLE group, store a partial tail only if `update_state_after_alloc` scheduled a CPU-tier load for this request (`RequestOffloadState.loaded_from_offload`). Complete chunks and aligned boundary states are stored as before.

**Why the proof-step store is safe.** Stores are only queued in `wait_for_save` and are sent at the start of the next step. The CPU transfer stream waits on the compute stream at that point, so the copy runs after this step's forward wrote the proof block.

**Difference from #60695.** Mooncake stores one key per hash unit. The native connector stores whole chunks and keeps its chunk-level EAGLE drop for complete chunks. So only the partial-tail key of EAGLE groups changes.

**Limitations.**
- If the hand-off step stops before `T + h`, the tail is not stored. I ran core's chunk-split code on 20,000 prompts (1k–200k tokens) per configuration. No hand-off was lost when block ≤ `max_num_batched_tokens` with EAGLE or single-module MTP. Losses occur only with multi-module MTP (0.2–0.45 %) or with a block larger than the token budget (≤ 1.7 %). A fix would need core to keep the CoW block across steps; not done.
- The store policy is a heuristic. A request served only from the GPU prefix cache stores no EAGLE tail. If the GPU later evicts that prefix, the next turn's CPU-tier hit ends at the last complete chunk. That turn then loads from the CPU tier and stores its tail, so the turn after it can get a partial hit. Measured on one workload only.
- When the dropped chunk is present, the search covers two blocks. This applies only with an EAGLE group.
- Existing CPU caches hold no EAGLE tails, so no migration is needed.

**Size:** `offloading/scheduler.py` +161 / −32 (no core files changed); tests +400 / −1. Part 3 alone is 7 lines (`RequestOffloadState.loaded_from_offload`, set in `update_state_after_alloc`, checked in `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs`) and 57 test lines.

**Why part 3 stays in this PR.** Without it, parts 1 + 2 make serving slower in the A/B above (SLO pass 86.6 % against 91.7 % without this PR; same-day P95 TTFT 2,297 against 2,025 ms). A split would land that regression until the second PR merges. Extra stores cost latency, not only bandwidth: on A100 the copy engine serves GPU → host copies of different streams in order. A 4 KB copy on its own stream takes 0.04 ms; with a 32 MB or 128 MB store queued on another stream (one copy or `swap_blocks_batch`), it waits 1.3 or 5.1 ms (1 × A100-SXM4-40GB, test script on request). MRV2 copies the sampled tokens to the host in this way, so each queued store byte can delay the step output. The split is ready if a reviewer prefers it: branches `offload-eagle-keying-only` (parts 1 + 2) and `offload-eagle-store-gate-split` (part 3) on my fork.

title: [Docs] Fix broken llm-d.ai links on the llm-d integration page
author: almogtavor
body:
## Overview

Every llm-d.ai documentation link on the [llm-d integration page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/deployment/integrations/llm-d/) returns 404. This repoints all nine at their current published URLs. Docs only, no link text changed.

## Claims

- Fixes 9 broken links (all returning 404) on `docs/deployment/integrations/llm-d.md`.
- No remaining `llm-d.ai` link on the page 404s.
- Link text and prose are untouched, so the rendered page reads identically.

## Validation

Before, every one of these was a 404:

```console
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides                                 404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/precise-prefix-cache-aware      404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/tiered-prefix-cache             404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/pd-disaggregation               404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/wide-expert-parallelism         404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/workload-autoscaling            404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/flow-control                    404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/optimized-baseline              404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/getting-started                        404
```

After, every `llm-d.ai` link on the page resolves:

```console
$ grep -oE 'https://llm-d\.ai[^)]*' docs/deployment/integrations/llm-d.md | sort -u \
    | while read -r u; do printf '%-80s %s\n' "$u" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -L "$u")"; done
https://llm-d.ai/                                                                200
https://llm-d.ai/docs                                                            200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/architecture                                               200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/architecture/advanced/kv-management                        200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart                                 200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths                                             200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/flow-control                    200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/optimized-baseline              200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/pd-disaggregation               200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/precise-prefix-cache-routing    200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/tiered-prefix-cache             200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/wide-expert-parallelism         200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/workload-autoscaling            200
https://llm-d.ai/slack                                                           200
```

A `grep -c 'docs/guides'` on the file now returns 0, and the only remaining `getting-started` reference is `/getting-started/quickstart`, which is valid.

## Details

Root cause: `/docs/guides/...` has never been a route on llm-d.ai. The `llm-d/llm-d` repository has a top-level `guides/` directory holding deployment recipes (Helm values, scripts), but the website is built from `docs/`, which publishes the well-lit paths under `/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/`. `git log` on `llm-d/llm-d` confirms no `docs/guides` directory has ever existed, and the llm-d.ai sitemap has no `/docs/guides` entry in any published version (0.7, 0.8, 0.9, current). So these are not links broken by a later rename; they have never resolved.

Two links needed more than the path prefix swap:

| Old | New | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/docs/guides/precise-prefix-cache-aware` | `/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/precise-prefix-cache-routing` | The page was additionally renamed from `precise-prefix-cache-aware` to `precise-prefix-cache-routing` in llm-d/llm-d#1560. |
| `/docs/guides#advanced-kv-cache-management` | `/docs/architecture/advanced/kv-management` | That anchor does not exist. The topic now has its own page, titled "KV Cache Management". |

Separately, `/docs/getting-started` 404s even though `docs/getting-started/README.mdx` exists, because that file sets `slug: /` and is therefore served at the `/docs` root. The "Introduction" link now points at `/docs`.

Since these URLs were never published, there is nothing for llm-d.ai to redirect from, so the fix belongs here rather than in the llm-d website.

title: [Bugfix] Keep legacy WNA16 MoE dispatch on Triton under batch invariance
author: yifanFengg
body:
## Purpose

`should_moe_wna16_use_cuda` selects the CUDA WNA16 MoE kernel (`moe_wna16_gemm`) when there are at most six tokens per expert and the Triton `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` otherwise. For the legacy `fused_experts` path with `use_int4_w4a16` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` this means a request's experts are computed by the CUDA kernel when it is processed alone and by the Triton kernel when it is processed in a large enough batch, which defeats batch invariance. Two more things show up at the kernel level: the CUDA kernel is not deterministic run to run (same inputs, different output), and with the fixed batch-invariant config (`BLOCK_SIZE_K=32`) it rejects group sizes above 32 (`BLOCK_SIZE_K must divisible by group_size`). The Triton kernel with the fixed config gave bitwise identical rows for every batch size tried (M = 1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 300).

This PR makes `should_moe_wna16_use_cuda` return `False` in batch-invariant mode, so the Triton kernel with the fixed config is always used. Nothing changes when the flag is unset.

Note: the modular MoE path (`TritonWNA16Experts`, used by the compressed-tensors and GPTQ/AWQ MoE methods when serving) already calls the Triton kernel directly, so this only affects direct `fused_experts` users and the `get_default_config` path; it is a hardening of the public API rather than a serving fix.

## Test Plan

- Kernel-level check on an A10 (`main` at `d09ff7763`): a random int4 MoE (128 experts, top-8, N=768, K=2048) run through the `fused_moe` test helper (`tests/kernels/moe/utils.py`, which calls `fused_experts`) with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` for M = 1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 300; row 0 compared bitwise with the M=1 result, with the CUDA kernel allowed (current behaviour) and disabled (this PR), for group sizes 32 and 128. Script attached below.

## Test Result

Each group size is run twice by the script: first with the CUDA kernel allowed, which is what `main` does, then with it disabled, which is what this PR does. The `ERROR` line below is therefore `main` failing; the line after it is this PR passing.

```text
COMMAND: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 PYTHONPATH=/data00/vllm-eval-mla python /data00/runs/wna16_moe_bi/kernel_repro.py 32
COMMIT: d09ff77637 [Bugfix] Give each data-parallel engine its own global RNG streams (#5 (main, 0 modified files)
GPU: NVIDIA A10, 580.126.20
group_size 32
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT = True | should_moe_wna16_use_cuda(8*topk...) = True
# main (CUDA kernel allowed):
cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed=True: row0 vs M=1 -> M=1 repeated:DIFF(maxabs=0.00195), M=1:DIFF(maxabs=0.00238), M=2:DIFF(maxabs=0.00171), M=8:DIFF(maxabs=0.00171), M=32:DIFF(maxabs=0.00171), M=128:DIFF(maxabs=0.00217), M=300:DIFF(maxabs=0.00217)
# this PR (CUDA kernel disabled):
cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed=False: row0 vs M=1 -> M=1 repeated:same, M=1:same, M=2:same, M=8:same, M=32:same, M=128:same, M=300:same

COMMAND: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 PYTHONPATH=/data00/vllm-eval-mla python /data00/runs/wna16_moe_bi/kernel_repro.py 128
COMMIT: d09ff77637 [Bugfix] Give each data-parallel engine its own global RNG streams (#5 (main, 0 modified files)
GPU: NVIDIA A10, 580.126.20
group_size 128
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT = True | should_moe_wna16_use_cuda(8*topk...) = True
# main (CUDA kernel allowed):
cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed=True: row0 vs M=1 -> ERROR RuntimeError: moe_wna16_gemm, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/moe_wna16.cu:314, BLOCK_SIZE_K must divisible by group_size
# this PR (CUDA kernel disabled):
cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed=False: row0 vs M=1 -> M=1 repeated:same, M=1:same, M=2:same, M=8:same, M=32:same, M=128:same, M=300:same
```

<details><summary>kernel_repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Kernel-level batch-invariance check of the W4A16 Triton/CUDA MoE path.

Builds a random int4 (group 128, symmetric) MoE, runs fused_moe on a batch of
M rows and on row 0 alone, and compares row 0 bitwise. Runs with the CUDA
small-batch kernel allowed (main behaviour) and with it disabled (the fix).
"""
import os, sys
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", "1")
import torch
import vllm.envs as envs
import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe as fm
from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from tests.kernels.moe.utils import fused_moe
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import int4_w4a16_moe_quant_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import quantize_weights
from vllm.scalar_type import scalar_types

torch.manual_seed(0)
dev = "cuda"
dtype = torch.bfloat16
e, n, k, topk = 128, 768, 2048, 8   # Qwen3-30B-A3B-like shapes
group_size = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 32
print("group_size", group_size)
print("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT =", envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT, "| should_moe_wna16_use_cuda(8*topk...) =", fm.should_moe_wna16_use_cuda(8 * topk, group_size, e, 4))

w1 = torch.randn((e, 2 * n, k), device=dev, dtype=dtype) / 10
w2 = torch.randn((e, k, n), device=dev, dtype=dtype) / 10
w1_q = torch.empty((e, 2 * n, k // 2), device=dev, dtype=torch.uint8)
w2_q = torch.empty((e, k, n // 2), device=dev, dtype=torch.uint8)
w1_s = torch.empty((e, 2 * n, k // group_size), device=dev, dtype=dtype)
w2_s = torch.empty((e, k, n // group_size), device=dev, dtype=dtype)
for i in range(e):
    for w, wq, ws in ((w1, w1_q, w1_s), (w2, w2_q, w2_s)):
        _, qweight, scales, _ = quantize_weights(w[i].T, scalar_types.uint4b8, group_size, False, False)
        qweight = qweight.T.contiguous().to(torch.uint8)
        wq[i] = qweight[:, 1::2] * 16 + qweight[:, ::2]
        ws[i] = scales.T
qc = int4_w4a16_moe_quant_config(w1_scale=w1_s, w2_scale=w2_s, w1_zp=None, w2_zp=None, block_shape=[0, group_size])

def run(a, score):
    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
        return fused_moe(a, w1_q, w2_q, score, topk, renormalize=False, global_num_experts=e, quant_config=qc)

Ms = [1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 300]
a_all = torch.randn((max(Ms), k), device=dev, dtype=dtype) / 10
s_all = torch.randn((max(Ms), e), device=dev, dtype=dtype)
for allow_cuda in (True, False):
    orig = fm.should_moe_wna16_use_cuda
    if not allow_cuda:
        fm.should_moe_wna16_use_cuda = lambda *a_, **k_: False
    res = []
    try:
        ref = run(a_all[:1].clone(), s_all[:1].clone())[0]
        again = run(a_all[:1].clone(), s_all[:1].clone())[0]
        res.append(f"M=1 repeated:{'same' if torch.equal(again, ref) else 'DIFF(maxabs=%.3g)' % (again.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()}")
        for M in Ms:
            out = run(a_all[:M].clone(), s_all[:M].clone())[0]
            res.append(f"M={M}:{'same' if torch.equal(out, ref) else 'DIFF(maxabs=%.3g)' % (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()}")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        res.append(f"ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0][:160]}")
    print(f"cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed={allow_cuda}: row0 vs M=1 ->", ", ".join(res))
    fm.should_moe_wna16_use_cuda = orig
```
</details>
