title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Match decoder-replay input_ids dtype for FlashInfer MegaMoE
author: wangshangsam
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61040. DeepSeek-V4.1 served with `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` or `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` crashes in the decoder-replay CUDA graph once it serves long prompts or batched prefills (e.g. GSM8K at concurrency 128) (`RuntimeError: Expected out tensor to have dtype int, but got long int instead`), because the replay graph's `input_ids` buffer is int64 while the model passes int32 ids for these backends. This PR sizes the buffer to match what the model passes.

## Claims

- **Bug fix:** with either FlashInfer MegaMoE backend, the replay graph's `input_ids` buffer is now int32, matching the ids `DeepseekV4Model.forward` passes. GSM8K serving no longer crashes. `deep_gemm_mega_moe` keeps its int64 buffer, and the default backend keeps int32, so neither changes.
- **Test:** `test_replay_graph_matches_eager` now sweeps the MoE backends and feeds `input_ids` in the dtype the model passes, instead of the buffer's own dtype. Without the fix both FlashInfer cases fail; run on its own, each fails at the line that crashes in serving.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (1× GB200, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:f853a683…`, built from 7d0b4e57aa, which includes #59532; the fix installed by copying this PR's `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py`, the PR's only non-test change, into the image):

```bash
cd tests && pytest -v -rs models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py \
  models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| without the fix | 16 passed, 2 failed: `test_replay_graph_matches_eager[flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl-torch.int32]` fails at `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:95` with `RuntimeError: expected scalar type Long but found Int`; `[flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm-torch.int32]` fails the same way when run on its own (after the first failure in the same process it fails during capture instead) |
| with the fix | **18 passed** |

**Serving** (4× GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42`, `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend <backend>`, default CUDA graphs; GSM8K via `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 128`, one run each):

| `--moe-backend` | Image | without the fix | with the fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` | nightly above | serves and answers short prompts, then the engine dies under GSM8K load with `RuntimeError: Expected out tensor to have dtype int, but got long int instead` at `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:95`: GSM8K **0.027** (97% invalid) | GSM8K **0.899**, no errors |
| `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | `main` c41b2639e2 + #59912 + #59900 | same crash: GSM8K 0.070 (earlier run, same image) | GSM8K **0.899**, no errors |
| `deep_gemm_mega_moe` (int64 path, unchanged) | nightly above | — | GSM8K 0.901 |
| default (`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`; int32 path, unchanged) | nightly above | — | GSM8K 0.910 |

Every run in this round logged `Decoder SWA bounded replay` and captured all 8 decoder replay CUDA graph sizes, so the replay path was active. The earlier CuTeDSL "without the fix" run's server log was not kept, but its crash was in the replay graph's own `run()`. Short prompts ("capital of France", "17 * 23", a `fib(n)` function, "why is the sky blue") were answered correctly in every run.

The `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` row needs `nvshmem4py` (#59912) and the FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 kwarg fix (#59900), both still open, so it uses an image built from `main` c41b2639e2 + #59912 + #59900, with this PR's file copied in the same way.

**pre-commit:** `pre-commit run --files tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py` passes.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager.__init__` sized its `input_ids` buffer as int64 when `kernel_config.moe_backend in MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` (`decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:59-60`). `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` is `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS | FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_BACKENDS` (`vllm/config/kernel.py`).
- `DeepseekV4Model.forward` casts `input_ids` to int64 only when `use_native_mega_moe` (`moe_backend in NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:671-673`, `:929-930`); the runner's ids are int32 (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py:25`).
- So for both FlashInfer backends `run()` copies int32 ids into the int64 buffer with `torch.index_select(..., out=buf[:num_rows])` (`decoder_replay_cudagraph.py:95`), which requires matching dtypes.
- It needs a large enough step, not concurrency as such: `run()` is reached only when a replay batch dispatches to a replay graph (a PIECEWISE step of at least `decoder_replay_trim_threshold` = 768 padded tokens, or an eager step with a prefill chunk longer than the 128-token window; `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py:456-501`), so by the code a single prompt of 768 or more tokens hits it too. Capture feeds the buffers directly and the eager fallback has no `out=`, so startup and short prompts work.
- The two checks diverged when #54049 narrowed the model's cast (and the other native-only paths) to `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` while #59532 was in flight with the wider `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` check.

**Fix.** Key the buffer dtype on `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`, with a comment pointing at the cast in `DeepseekV4Model.forward`. The FlashInfer backends don't need int64 ids: the router accepts int32 (`fused_topk_bias` only casts when a hash table exists; `dsv4_topk` widens the ids to int64 after loading them, and the CUDA fallback accepts int32 or int64 ids), the FlashInfer experts never see `input_ids`, and the non-replay layers already run with int32 ids on these backends.

**Alternatives considered.** Deriving the dtype from one shared helper on `vllm_config`, called from both `DeepseekV4Model.__init__` and `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager.__init__`, would stop the two from drifting again; this PR keeps to the minimal fix. Removing the native backend's int64 cast (a DSv4 hash-routing leftover; DSv4.1 has no hash layers) would need native MegaMoE revalidation. Both are possible follow-ups.

**CI.** The test runs in `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) Basic Models (Other)` and its `:amd: (MI355) Basic Models (Other)` mirror (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`); it needs one GPU but no weights or FlashInfer kernels.

**Duplicate check.** `gh issue list` / `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm` searches for `decoder replay`, `decoder_replay`, `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`, `NATIVE_MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`, `Expected out tensor to have dtype int` and `59532` found no issue or PR that fixes this bug. The only hit that describes it is #59912 (nvshmem4py), whose validation notes record this crash and leave the fix to a separate PR (this one); it does not change `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py`. Open #59039 (ROCm decoder replay) doesn't touch `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py`'s dtype logic, and the AMD model has no native MegaMoE.

title: [Bugfix] Create cuBLAS handles before memory profiling to avoid OOM
author: laithsakka
body:
Fix https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/199944
Purpose
On small GPUs (e.g. an H200 35GB MIG slice), engine startup can fail during the memory profiling run with:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when calling `cublasCreate(handle)`
```
This was seen in tests/v1/e2e/general/test_kv_sharing_fast_prefill.py with google/gemma-3n-E2B-it on torch 2.14.1 and the 2.15.0 RC (pytorch/pytorch#199944).

### Root cause

cuBLAS(Lt) asks CUDA for its handle memory directly. When torch's own cudaMalloc fails, torch frees its unused cache and retries, but a cuBLAS request never triggers that because torch doesn't see it. Profiling can grow torch's cache until the GPU is full, and the first cuBLAS call then fails even though torch holds idle memory it could have given back.
In this case:

- Loading weights does no matmuls, so the first cuBLAS call in the process happens inside profile_run, at the gemma3n vision projection. That call creates the handle.
- By then, torch had reserved 29.5 GiB, while live tensors peaked at 21.9 GiB. That left 0.04 GiB free on the device, and cublasCreate failed with about 19 GiB sitting unused in torch's cache.
- The scoped max_split_size_mb:20 from #58430 makes this more likely, adding about 2.9 GiB of reserved memory during profiling.

### Fix

Create the handles while memory is still free. At the start of Worker.determine_available_memory, call torch.cuda.current_blas_handle() and run one tiny linear with a bias, which also sets up cuBLASLt. Every GEMM during profiling then reuses the existing handles, so profiling needs no allocations outside torch's allocator.

The handles are created after init_snapshot, so their memory is still counted in total_consumed and comes out of the KV-cache budget as before. In the repro the KV cache was about 0.1 GiB smaller, which is the handle cost.

### Test Result

Without fix (2 runs) | FAIL ×2, CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED | 29.52 / 0.04 GiB
With fix (4 runs) | PASS ×4 | 29.43 / 0.07 GiB

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Drain compilation tasks before releasing the backend
author: DimensionSTP
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61043. Stop structured-output thread pools before destroying the backend, so an in-flight grammar compilation cannot access a released xgrammar compiler.

## Claims

- Cancel queued compilation tasks and wait for running tasks before releasing the backend.
- Close the optional mask-filling executor and make repeated cleanup safe.
- Preserve normal structured-output generation; no request handling or backend API changes.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/structured_output
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py
```

- Official structured-output suite: 237 passed, 1 existing xfail. The new tests use the real manager, thread pools and xgrammar compiler. The shutdown regression also passed in five independent runs.
- With the original `clear_backend()` restored through a local test plugin, the new regression fails with the reported `AttributeError: 'XgrammarBackend' object has no attribute 'compiler'`.
- Actual HTTP serving on H100 with `facebook/opt-125m`, BF16, TP=1, eager execution and Model Runner V2: both versions returned the expected JSON for three normal requests. With a cold compilation paused at the compiler entry point, SIGTERM caused the original method to release the backend first and reproduce the compiler error. The fix let compilation finish before backend destruction, without that error.
- All applicable project hooks pass. The existing Buildkite structured-output step includes the regression file.

The serving comparison used a local timing-control wrapper and existing native extensions, not a new clean build. It validates the shutdown ordering deterministically, not the frequency of an uncontrolled race. The in-flight HTTP request is aborted during shutdown; its response is not counted as a successful structured-output result.

## Details

`EngineCore.shutdown()` calls `clear_backend()` while grammar futures can still be running or queued. `XgrammarBackend.destroy()` deletes the compiler, leaving those tasks able to access a destroyed backend.

Drain the initialized executors with `shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=True)`, then destroy the backend and clear its reference. The initialization guards match the constructor. This keeps the repair in the manager's existing cleanup method and does not reorder engine shutdown.

Shutdown now waits for already-running compilation; Python cannot cancel a running thread. No timeout, runtime dependency or steady-state synchronization is added.

No open PR addressing #61043 was found. Related closed, unmerged #34690 also explored executor cleanup as part of a broader leak fix; this change is limited to backend teardown and its regression tests.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve running request prefixes across LRU store batches
author: ztysth
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve the reusable head of CPU-offloaded prefixes while their requests are still running, across store batches and KV groups. Related to [the unfinished-request observation in #58804](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58804#issuecomment-6098736505); this addresses that eviction pattern rather than the issue's entire throughput regression.

## Claims

- Positioned keys share a provisional request rank, with later token positions evicted first across batches.
- `insert(key, chunk, req_context)` assigns new chunks their final provisional rank directly. First observations still handle resident prefixes reused by load/store and anchor requests before allocation retries.
- Finalization commits recency and ARC frequency accounting; transfer pinning, newer shared accesses, reset and keys without positions retain their behavior.

## Validation

Latest review revision: Linux x86_64, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu, based on the bot-merged head `b27bfdfde95e835043749b82bc3d4e2c558eace0`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/base.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/lru.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/arc.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
```

76 manager/policy tests and 500 tiering/scheduler tests passed. All applicable hooks passed. The two new insertion-contract cases fail on the merged head because `insert` lacks `req_context`; with the revision, ready and pending chunks both evict tail before head without a follow-up access call. The original running-prefix regression tests previously gave 11 failed/2 passed against the unmodified base.

A native CPU replay through `LLM` used a two-layer tiny Llama, dummy weights, float32, greedy decoding, two 192-token prompts, block size 32 and eight offload slots. A remains unfinished while B adds pressure. Aborting A, clearing only model-side prefix caching and replaying A gives the same result before and after this interface revision: 64 cached tokens, 2 actual CPU KV blocks loaded and output token IDs `[11, 11, 11, 11]`. A test-only worker synchronously copies real CPU KV pages; the installed native extensions are shared by both runs. This validates usable KV reuse and observed output, not model quality or CUDA transfer behavior.

Manager-only timings, five runs per row, nine groups and batches of eight; median [min,max] milliseconds:

| Chunks/group | Merged PR head | Insertion revision |
|---|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.980 [1.805,3.454] | 1.807 [1.732,2.703] |
| 256 | 8.911 [7.935,13.120] | 7.887 [7.435,12.620] |
| 1024 | 39.069 [37.165,362.716] | 34.581 [33.813,321.299] |

These are bookkeeping measurements; GPU TTFT and serving throughput were not measured in this review revision.

## Details

Insertion previously made an unfinished request's head older than its tail until finalization. Evicting the head makes every remaining suffix unreachable by contiguous-prefix lookup.

LRU uses `(request_rank, -token_position)` and the existing lazy heap update/compaction paths. The request rank is anchored at first observation; new chunks receive it inside `insert`, while existing resident accesses preserve any newer shared recency. This avoids revisiting the full prefix after every store batch. Cache reset invalidates provisional state. Chunks remain evictable and finalization still commits recency.

Custom `CachePolicy` implementations must accept the additional `req_context` insertion argument; policies that do not use it can ignore it. The custom-policy guide and ARC implementation reflect that interface. ARC frequency promotion remains at finalization.

The fix is distinct from optional in-flight pin protection (#57813), session-aware policies (#50422), GPU-local reuse recording (#57746) and KVCR recency changes (#60469); those target different policies or access sources. This revision addresses the existing review request on #61050.

title: [Bugfix] Respect the configured offline chat template
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Overview

Use the template configured through `LLM(chat_template=...)` in `chat()` and `enqueue_chat()`. Explicit per-call templates continue to override the constructor default.

## Claims

- Both offline chat entry points use the configured template instead of silently falling back to the tokenizer template.
- Per-call template overrides retain their existing behavior.

## Validation

Real Qwen3-0.6B inference: both constructor-default cases fail on main, pass with this change, and fail again after reverting it. Both explicit override controls pass throughout. Applicable manual pre-commit hooks pass.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and original results</summary>

Baseline: `187a0eb98aa42341d703f83421d693fa7585581b`; candidate: `8535b1c179`. Hardware: one RTX 5090. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.16.1; eager execution. This checks prompt construction and short generation, not benchmark accuracy.

Model revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`.

```bash
hf download Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --revision c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca --local-dir model
```

With each code revision installed, save this as `repro.py` and run `.venv/bin/python repro.py result.json`:

```python
import json,sys,pathlib
from vllm import LLM,SamplingParams
MODEL='./model'
TEMPLATE="User: {{ messages[0]['content'] }}\nAssistant:"
OVERRIDE="Question: {{ messages[0]['content'] }}\nAnswer:"
def main():
 llm=LLM(model=MODEL,chat_template=TEMPLATE,enforce_eager=True,max_model_len=512,gpu_memory_utilization=0.25)
 tokenizer=llm.get_tokenizer();messages=[{'role':'user','content':'What is the capital of France?'}]
 results=[]
 for entry in ['chat','enqueue_chat']:
  for override in [None,OVERRIDE]:

   result['matches']=result['actual']==expected;results.append(result);print(json.dumps(result),flush=True)
 pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2))
 print('CHAT_TEMPLATE_PASSED' if all(r['matches'] for r in results) else 'CHAT_TEMPLATE_MISMATCH',flush=True)
```

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve token IDs in chat derender responses
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Overview

Preserve requested `token_ids` in chat derender responses, including plain and parsed streaming. Follow normal chat behavior when reasoning is hidden.

## Claims

- The render → generate → derender flow returns the generated token IDs when requested.
- Requests without `return_token_ids` still omit them; parsed responses with `include_reasoning=False` also omit them.

## Validation

Real Qwen3-0.6B HTTP before/fix/revert confirms batch and streaming IDs are lost on main, retained by the fix, and lost again after revert. False/absent flag controls and a real reasoning-parser privacy check pass. The existing DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B parity suite passes 10 tests with 6 native skips; the hidden-reasoning unit test passes. Applicable manual pre-commit hooks pass.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and original results</summary>

Baseline `187a0eb98aa42341d703f83421d693fa7585581b`; candidate `6ddf5f431f`. One RTX 5090; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.16.1. Eager execution. This checks response metadata and parser parity, not model accuracy.

```bash
hf download Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --revision c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca --local-dir model
vllm serve ./model --served-model-name qwen3 --enable-scale-out --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18491 --max-model-len 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --enforce-eager
```

Save as `repro.py`, then run `.venv/bin/python repro.py 18491 qwen3`:

```python
import json
import sys
import time
from typing import Any

import requests


def post_json(base_url: str, path: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    response = requests.post(f"{base_url}{path}", json=payload, timeout=120)
    try:
        data = response.json()
    except Exception:
        data = {"raw_text": response.text}
    if response.status_code != 200:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{path} returned {response.status_code}: "
            f"{json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)}"
        )
    return data


def wait_ready(base_url: str, model: str) -> None:
    deadline = time.time() + 180
    last_error = None
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/v1/models", timeout=5)
            if response.status_code == 200:
                models = response.json().get("data", [])
                if not models or any(item.get("id") == model for item in models):
                    return
        except Exception as exc:
            last_error = exc
        time.sleep(2)
    raise RuntimeError(f"server did not become ready: {last_error!r}")


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("usage: probe.py PORT MODEL", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    port = int(sys.argv[1])
    model = sys.argv[2]
    base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    wait_ready(base_url, model)

    chat_request = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say alpha beta gamma."}],
        "max_tokens": 8,
        "temperature": 0,
        "return_token_ids": True,
    }

    render = post_json(base_url, "/v1/chat/completions/render", chat_request)
    generate = post_json(base_url, "/inference/v1/generate", render)
    derender = post_json(
        base_url,
        "/v1/chat/completions/derender",
        {
            "model": model,
            "generate_response": generate,
            "prompt_tokens": len(render["token_ids"]),
            "chat_request": chat_request,
        },
    )
    for flag in (False, None):
        control_request = dict(chat_request)
        if flag is None:
            control_request.pop("return_token_ids")
        else:
            control_request["return_token_ids"] = flag
        control = post_json(base_url, "/v1/chat/completions/derender", {
            "model": model, "generate_response": generate,
            "prompt_tokens": len(render["token_ids"]), "chat_request": control_request})
        assert control["choices"][0].get("token_ids") is None, control
    stream_results = []
    state = None
    ids = generate["choices"][0]["token_ids"]
    for i, tid in enumerate(ids):
        streamed = post_json(base_url, "/v1/chat/completions/derender", {
            "stream": True, "model": model,
            "generate_chunk": {"request_id": generate["request_id"], "choices": [{
                "index": 0, "token_ids": [tid], "finish_reason": "length" if i == len(ids)-1 else None}]},
            "stream_state": state, "prompt_tokens": len(render["token_ids"]),
            "prompt_token_ids": render["token_ids"], "chat_request": chat_request})
        state = streamed["stream_state"]
        stream_results.append(streamed["chunk"]["choices"][0].get("token_ids"))
    print("STREAM_TOKEN_IDS", json.dumps(stream_results), flush=True)
    normal = post_json(base_url, "/v1/chat/completions", chat_request)

    generated_token_ids = generate["choices"][0]["token_ids"]
    derender_choice = derender["choices"][0]
    normal_choice = normal["choices"][0]
    derender_token_ids = derender_choice.get("token_ids")
    normal_token_ids = normal_choice.get("token_ids")

    result = {
        "render_request_id": render["request_id"],
        "generate_request_id": generate["request_id"],
        "generated_token_ids": generated_token_ids,
        "derender_token_ids": derender_token_ids,
        "normal_token_ids_present": isinstance(normal_token_ids, list),
        "normal_prompt_token_ids_present": isinstance(
            normal.get("prompt_token_ids"), list
        ),
        "derender_prompt_token_ids": derender.get("prompt_token_ids"),
        "derender_matches_generate": derender_token_ids == generated_token_ids,
        "usage": derender.get("usage"),
    }
    print("RESULT", json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))

    if not isinstance(normal_token_ids, list):
        print("CONTROL_FAILED_NORMAL_CHAT_DID_NOT_RETURN_TOKEN_IDS")
        return 3
    if derender_token_ids == generated_token_ids and stream_results == [[tid] for tid in ids]:
        print("NO_BUG_REPRODUCED")
        return 0

    print("BUG_REPRODUCED_DERENDER_CHAT_DROPPED_TOKEN_IDS")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```python
suite.ARGS.extend(['--enforce-eager', '--max-model-len', '2048', '--gpu-memory-utilization', '0.6'])
raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
```


The six skips are existing model-output-dependent skips, including cases where this small model does not emit the requested tool call.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hidden-reasoning HTTP control</summary>

Restart the Qwen server above with `--reasoning-parser qwen3`. Keep `repro.py` from the first block alongside this file, save as `hidden.py`, and run `.venv/bin/python hidden.py`:

```python
import sys
from repro import post_json, wait_ready

base = 'http://127.0.0.1:18491'
wait_ready(base, 'qwen3')
request = {'model': 'qwen3', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is 2 + 2?'}],
           'max_tokens': 16, 'temperature': 0, 'return_token_ids': True,
           'include_reasoning': False}
render = post_json(base, '/v1/chat/completions/render', request)
generated = post_json(base, '/inference/v1/generate', render)
common = {'model': 'qwen3', 'chat_request': request,
          'prompt_tokens': len(render['token_ids'])}
response = post_json(base, '/v1/chat/completions/derender',
                     {**common, 'generate_response': generated})
assert response['choices'][0].get('token_ids') is None, response
assert response['choices'][0]['message'].get('reasoning') is None, response
state = None
ids = generated['choices'][0]['token_ids']
assert ids
for i, tid in enumerate(ids):
    response = post_json(base, '/v1/chat/completions/derender', {
        **common, 'stream': True, 'stream_state': state,
        'prompt_token_ids': render['token_ids'],
        'generate_chunk': {'request_id': generated['request_id'], 'choices': [{
            'index': 0, 'token_ids': [tid],
            'finish_reason': 'length' if i == len(ids) - 1 else None}]}})
    state = response['stream_state']
    for choice in response['chunk']['choices']:
        assert choice.get('token_ids') is None, choice
```

## Details

The generate response already contains IDs; the chat derender response constructors omitted them. Forward that existing field at each response constructor, gated by the request and the same hidden-reasoning policy used by ordinary chat. title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Restore MTP index sharing across draft iterations
author: gcanlin
body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash's checkpoint sets `index_share_for_mtp_iteration: true`: the MTP head computes the sparse indexer top-k on draft step 0 and reuses it on the later steps. Since #57387 the flag is no longer visible on the draft config, so sharing has been silently off. This restores it.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `index_share_for_mtp_iteration`, `share_mtp_topk_indices`, `glm5_next_mtp` and GLM-5.3-Flash MTP and found nothing covering this.

## Claims

- With MTP on GLM-5.3-Flash, draft steps 1+ reuse step 0's top-k again, as before #57387.
- Accepted tokens per draft step go from 3.28 to 3.42 on GSM8K (MTP 5), and decode throughput is +2.7% at a fixed acceptance length.

## Validation

4x B200, nightly `8cbd5d03`, TP1 x DP4 with expert parallel and #60895's MegaMoE path, MTP 5, one run each.

| | sharing off (main) | sharing on |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, 1,319 questions) | 0.9704 ± 0.0047 | 0.9750 ± 0.0043 |
| draft steps for that GSM8K run | 58,471 | 56,072 |
| accepted tokens per draft step | 3.28 | 3.42 |
| random 1024 in / 1024 out, concurrency 128, output tok/s | 11,639 | 11,952 |
| mean TPOT | 10.13 ms | 9.90 ms |

The GSM8K rows use real acceptance; the throughput rows fix it with `synthetic_acceptance_length` 3.61.

The GPU runs switched the same proposer flag (`share_mtp_topk_indices`) through a local patch that read it from `text_config`. With this PR's code I ran:

- `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py`: 17 passed; the new test fails without the change. Run against nightly `8cbd5d03`, whose `speculative.py` is identical to `main`'s.
- `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override` on the real checkpoint config: `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is `True` (missing before).
- pre-commit on the changed files.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97

lm_eval run --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048 temperature=0.0
# accepted per draft step = vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens / vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts

# throughput rows: same server with
#   "rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.61
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 512 --num-warmups 64 --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 0 --seed 42
```

The remaining serve flags (CUDA graph sizes, KV offload, `--prefix-match-unit 16`) are the ones listed in #60895.
</details>

## Details

- Root cause: the MTP proposers read the flag from the draft config (`mtp/speculator.py`, `llm_base_proposer.py`). The in-tree `Glm5NextConfig` forwarded `text_config` attributes to the top level; the upstream Transformers config that #57387 switched to does not. That PR moved `num_nextn_predict_layers` to `get_text_config()` but not this flag.
- Fix: promote the flag onto the draft config in the `glm5_next` override, as the Qwen4-Exp override already does. An explicit `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` in `--speculative-config` still takes precedence.
- The GSM8K difference is within one standard error; I read it as no regression, not as an accuracy gain.
- Limitations: validated on NVIDIA SM100 only, not on ROCm. Acceptance was measured on GSM8K only.

title: Fix torchcodec lazy-import startup crash when native lib raises OSError
author: SIDDARTHAREDDY8
body:
## Overview

Widens the module-scope torchcodec import guard in `vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py` to also catch `OSError`, so `vllm serve` starts cleanly even when torchcodec's bundled native library fails to load (e.g. built against a CUDA runtime that is not installed). Fixes #60406.

## Claims

- `vllm serve` no longer dies at import time when `torch.ops.load_library` inside torchcodec raises `OSError`.
- With torchcodec unavailable, `AudioDecoder` is `None` and `load_audio(backend='auto')` falls back to soundfile/PyAV instead of crashing.
- The original `OSError` is preserved in `_torchcodec_import_exc` and chained into the deferred `ImportError`, so the real cause is not hidden.

## Validation

The full vLLM test suite is not runnable in this environment (needs CUDA + full install). I verified with a harness driving the real fixed `audio.py` with heavy deps stubbed and a fake torchcodec whose `decoders/__init__.py` raises `OSError` at import (faithful to the issue): 9/9 checks passed — fixed module imports cleanly, `AudioDecoder` is `None`, the `OSError` is preserved and chained into the deferred `ImportError`, the healthy-torchcodec control is unaffected, and the pre-fix file demonstrably crashes with `OSError` on import.

## Details

Root cause: torchcodec 0.17.0's bundled native lib (built against CUDA 13) fails inside `torch.ops.load_library`, which raises `OSError` (torch/_ops.py). The existing guard caught only `(ImportError, RuntimeError)`, so the `OSError` propagated and killed the whole `vllm serve` startup path even for text-only serving. The fix is a one-line widening of the except clause plus a comment citing the issue. No new third-party APIs are called; `requirements/cuda.txt` already pins `torchcodec >= 0.14` unbounded, matching the issue's analysis.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix EXAONE-4.5 image inputs: ViT received un-normalised pixels
author: Godmook
body:
## Overview

EXAONE-4.5 (`Exaone4_5_ForConditionalGeneration`) produces garbage for any request that contains an image on every release since #50411 (v0.29.0, v0.30.0, v0.31.0, main). Text-only requests are unaffected.

Root cause: the class inherits `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = True` from `Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration`, so `mm_device_do_normalize` defaults to on and the HF processor is told `do_rescale=False, do_normalize=False`. But `EXAONE4_5_VisionTransformer` is constructed without `input_norm`, so the inherited `Qwen2_5_VisionTransformer` uses `IdentityInputNorm` and the ViT receives raw 0–255 pixels.

Two smaller issues in the same constructor are fixed alongside, since they are the same missing wiring relative to the parent class:

- `self.model_config` and `self.video_pruning_rate` are never set, but the inherited `embed_multimodal` / encoder-CUDA-graph paths read them (`AttributeError` with `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'`).
- The MTP drafter (`Exaone4_5MultiTokenPredictor`) builds its `Exaone4DecoderLayer` without `cache_config`, so the drafter's attention ignores `--kv-cache-dtype`.

## Claims

- With the fix, image requests give coherent answers and are identical to the pre-#50411 behaviour (processor-side normalisation); text-only outputs and MTP acceptance are unchanged.
- No API change: the device-side normalisation feature stays on by default for this model, now with the correct normalisation module (`build_mm_input_norm(model_config)`), exactly as `Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration` does.
- Users on affected releases can work around it with `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`.

## Validation

`LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.5-33B-FP8`, TP=2, 2× A100-SXM4-40GB, greedy, thinking off, image = the model card's `assets/exaone45_input1.jpg` (a bowl of kimchi):

| | "Describe this image in one sentence." | gsm8k-50 (text only) |
|---|---|---|
| main (default flags) | `The\n</think>\n</think>one\n</think>…/or/or/or/or/or…` | 0.90 |
| this PR (default flags) | `A person in a light blue shirt is serving freshly made kimchi from a large black bowl into a smaller black dish, …` | 0.90 |

Second prompt ("What objects are in this image? List them.") shows the same pattern: `/or/or/or…` before, a correct itemised list (kimchi, dark ceramic bowl, …) after.

- `pre-commit` passes (ruff, mypy, typos).
- CI: the model is 33B and not in the multimodal generation test lists; the processing test (`tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py`) already covers it and still passes.

## Details

- `exaone4_5.py`: `EXAONE4_5_VisionTransformer.__init__` gains `input_norm` and forwards it to `Qwen2_5_VisionTransformer`; `Exaone4_5_ForConditionalGeneration.__init__` passes `input_norm=build_mm_input_norm(self.model_config)` and sets `self.model_config` / `self.video_pruning_rate` like the parent.
- `exaone4_5_mtp.py`: pass `cache_config=vllm_config.cache_config` to the MTP decoder layer.

Not in this PR (follow-ups): `Exaone4Model` lacks `EagleModelMixin` although the VLM advertises `SupportsEagle3` (asserts at load); `EXAONE4_5_VisionTransformer` builds and discards the full Qwen2.5 MHA block stack in `super().__init__` before replacing it with GQA blocks.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR or issue mentions EXAONE-4.5 image output, `mm_device_do_normalize` for EXAONE, or `exaone4_5` (searched `exaone4_5`, `EXAONE-4.5`, `mm_device_do_normalize input_norm`; the closed #45071 / #42281 are different bugs).

title: [Fix][Compile] Declare group_shape in the static FP8 quant fusion …
author: laithsakka
body:
Fix https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/9053
### Purpose
On recent torch (main, and the 2.15.0 RC from rc3), the fusion passes stop matching static per-tensor FP8 quant: RMSNormQuantFusionPass.matched_count == 0. CI shows it as All nodes remain for op _C::static_scaled_fp8_quant and rms_quant_fusion expected: [12], found: [0] (pytorch/test-infra#9053).

### Root cause

- QuantFP8 calls the static quant op with group_shape=[-1, -1] for per-tensor (input_quant_fp8.py). The shared pattern in MatcherQuantFP8 doesn't declare group_shape at all.
- Older torch matchers silently dropped any kwarg a pattern didn't declare, so this matched.
- pytorch/pytorch#199871 makes the matcher refuse a node that sets an undeclared kwarg to a non-default value, so a replacement can't silently lose it. pytorch/pytorch#200442 extends that check to auto_functionalized by reading the wrapped op's defaults.
- The schema default is group_shape=None, and the graph carries [-1, -1]. So even with #200442 the match is still refused.

### Fix
Declare group_shape in the static quant pattern, taken from the quant key: group_shape=[group_shape.row, group_shape.col]. That's the value QuantFP8 passes, and it's how rope_kvcache_fusion.py and qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py already write their static quant patterns. The pattern now states exactly what it matches, and it works with both old and new torch.

title: [Bugfix] Enable inductor batch-invariant mode under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
author: yifanFengg
body:
## Purpose

With torch.compile (used under batch invariance for quantized models, among others), RMSNorm and the other vLLM custom ops are lowered by inductor instead of using vLLM's batch-invariant kernels. Inductor picks the tile config of its reduction kernels in each worker process by on-device autotuning among candidates whose reduction block differs (`dynamic_scale_rblock`), and the reduction block sets the fp32 accumulation order: logging the decisions (`TORCH_LOGS=+torch._inductor.runtime.triton_heuristics`, block 3c) shows the same fused residual-add + RMSNorm kernel autotuned to `R0_BLOCK: 1024` in some workers and compiled pieces and to `R0_BLOCK: 512` in others, so two workers can norm the same row to different bits. Inductor has a batch-invariant mode for exactly this (`torch._inductor.config.batch_invariant`, "stable per-sample compiled kernel across batch sizes"; it implies inductor's deterministic mode, which skips that autotuning), but `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` did not enable it: every generated kernel carried `'deterministic': False, 'batch_invariant': False` in its `inductor_meta`.

This showed up as MoE models served with DP > 1, TP > 1 and expert parallelism not being batch invariant. The split itself is not specific to that layout: the DP=4 x TP=1 + EP layout's fused norm kernel shows it too (block 3c), and that layout passed the check in every run here. What the sequence-parallel MoE path adds is that a token's MoE input is the post-attention norm output of whichever TP rank's chunk holds the token, and that depends on the token's position in the batch, so within one replica the disagreement becomes a batch dependence. The failure is intermittent (1 to 14 of 32 prompts per run, usually a sampled token flipping at a late decode step from a small logprob change), and it disappears with `--enforce-eager`, with the custom ops kept (`custom_ops=all` or `none,+rms_norm`), with dynamo alone (`DYNAMO_TRACE_ONCE`), or with `TORCHINDUCTOR_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` / `TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC=1`; it stays with CUDA graphs off, with every fusion pass off, with the EP combine replaced by an all-to-all + fixed-order sum, with the router padding mask chunk-aligned, and with `moe_forward`'s stale `mutates_args` removed.

This PR sets inductor's `batch_invariant` config in `enable_batch_invariant_mode()`, which every worker runs before compiling. Nothing changes when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is unset. With it, the DP x TP + EP deployment passes with sequence-parallel MoE enabled.

The first revision of this PR disabled sequence-parallel MoE under batch invariance as a stopgap; following review, it now fixes the cause instead, and the evidence below replaces the earlier description.

## Test Plan

Online bitwise check (32 prompts, `temperature=0.6`, fixed seed, `max_tokens=8`, each prompt alone vs all 32 in one batched request, per-step top logprobs compared bitwise; "ragged" uses 1024-2048-word prompts), server started with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, 4x GB300 (SM103), `main` at `c19c263ac8`, torch 2.13.0:

- `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP4` (VLLM_CUTLASS NvFp4 MoE experts), DP=2 x TP=2 + EP: `main` (several server starts, the failure is intermittent), `main` + `TORCHINDUCTOR_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (the env form of what the patch sets), `main` + this PR (one run with `TORCH_COMPILE_DEBUG=1` to show the generated kernels' `inductor_meta`).
- Regressions: TP=4 (env form and this PR), DP=4 x TP=1 + EP (env form).
- `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16` (Triton WNA16 MoE experts, on a tree that also carries the pending #61038 fix for that path): `main`, env form, this PR.
- Cost: `vllm bench serve` (random 1024/128 x256 and 64/256 x128 prompts, 16 warmups, seed 0), `main` vs this PR, DP=2 x TP=2 + EP (one run each) and TP=4 (two runs each).
- Regression: the batch-invariance test suite (22 ids of `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py`), `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP4` TP=1, `main` and this PR side by side.
- A table of every other configuration tried during the bisection (one server start each).

## Test Result

`COMMIT:` lines: "clean checkout" is `main` at `c19c263ac8`; "1 file changed, 9 insertions(+)" is `main` + this PR; the W4A16 runs additionally carry the pending #61038 fix for that model's MoE path ("1 file changed, 5 insertions(+)" without this PR, "2 files changed, 14 insertions(+)" with it). The evidence was produced on `c19c263ac8`; the branch is rebased onto `a2fb482732`, where `vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py` is unchanged.

title: [Bugfix] Bump tokenspeed-mla to 2.0.2 to fix nanobind conflict with Triton 3.9
author: warrendeng
body:
## Overview

`tokenspeed-mla` depends on `tokenspeed-triton` which uses nanobind. Upstream Triton also switched to nanobind in 3.9 (triton-lang/triton#10283). Older `tokenspeed-triton` builds register the same C++ types in nanobind's shared registry, so loading both aborts with `Critical nanobind error: refusing to add duplicate key "PAD_ZERO"`. This breaks vLLM CI on the torch 2.15 RC and nightly lanes (pytorch/test-infra#9050).

[`tokenspeed-triton` 3.9.10.post20261008](https://github.com/lightseekorg/triton/tree/release/3.9.10.post20261008) uses its own nanobind domain, so the copies no longer collide, and `tokenspeed-mla` requires it from 0.2.20. This PR bumps the `tokenspeed-mla` pin from 0.2.15 to 2.0.2 to pick up that fix.

## Claims

- Fixes the `PAD_ZERO` abort with Triton 3.9.
- Passes the TokenSpeed MLA correctness and CUDA graph tests on B200.

## Validation

All tested on one B200.

**Fixes the pytorch/test-infra#9050 repro** (torch 2.15.0 + triton 3.9.0):

| Check | 0.2.15 (tokenspeed-triton 3.8.10) | 2.0.2 (tokenspeed-triton 3.9.10) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `import triton; import tokenspeed_triton`, both orders, Python 3.11/3.12 | abort | pass |
| `test_supported_backend_preserves_dcp_eligibility[TOKENSPEED_MLA]` | abort | 1 passed |
| `test_attention_selector.py` | - | 97 passed, 14 skipped |
| Both Tritons' kernels + `torch.compile` in one process | - | pass |

**Correctness** (torch 2.13, unless noted):

| Check | 2.0.2 |
| --- | --- |
| `test_mla_backends.py -k tokenspeed_mla` (torch 2.13 and 2.15) | 307 passed, 290 skipped each |
| TokenSpeed decode tests (accuracy, CUDA graphs, split-KV) | 203 passed, 77 skipped (SM107) |
| Accuracy and CUDA graphs with both Tritons loaded (torch 2.15) | 63 passed |
| Additional FP8 reference cases | 16 passed |
| GSM8K, eager x2 | 0.7771, 0.7801 |
| GSM8K, CUDA graphs x2 | 0.7718, 0.7756 |

All four GSM8K runs passed. The model was `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8`, with 1,319 questions, five-shot, seed 42 and temperature 0.

**Installs correctly:** `uv pip compile` picks `tokenspeed-triton==3.9.10.post20261008` on the default and nightly indexes. `pre-commit` passes; `requirements/test/cuda.txt` is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

B200 (sm100), driver 580.82.07, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12. torch 2.15 env: torch 2.15.0+cu130 and triton 3.9.0 from `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/test/cu130`; vLLM via `tools/use_existing_torch.py` and `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

Tests used vLLM snapshot `b48ae0e6` and matching precompiled artifacts from its main parent `624a5dda`. Model evaluations used torch 2.13; torch 2.15 covered imports, selectors and kernels. Python 3.11 coverage is limited to compiler imports.

```bash
python -c "import triton; import tokenspeed_triton"
python -c "import tokenspeed_triton; import triton"
pytest -v "tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py::test_supported_backend_preserves_dcp_eligibility[TOKENSPEED_MLA]"
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k tokenspeed_mla
pytest -s tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=<list>
# lightseekorg/tokenspeed at the release commit:
pytest -v tokenspeed-mla/tests/test_mla_decode.py
```

GSM8K server args: `--max-model-len 4096 --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --block-size 64`, plus `--enforce-eager` for the eager runs. Model revision: `efe1ced428db63e7ccbcf367334596f77e9af140`.

</details>

## Details

- DCP visibility/masking and empty-shard output/LSE handling (0.2.16, lightseekorg/tokenspeed#1853), plus decode synchronization and zero-tile guards. The added `local_visible_lens` argument defaults to `None`; vLLM does not pass it.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Read the text config under `thinker_config`
author: GoDiao
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The Rust frontend now finds the text config under `thinker_config`, so Qwen2.5-Omni, Qwen3-Omni and Qwen3-ASR checkpoints no longer fail at startup with "the model config does not define `vocab_size`". Fixes part 2 of #61057.

## Claims

- `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B` starts and serves requests without `--hf-overrides`; before this change it exits during startup.
- Same for Qwen3-ASR once a `tokenizer.json` is present (the missing `tokenizer.json` is part 1 of #61057 and is not addressed here).
- `vocab_size`, `eos_token_ids`, `model_type` and the expert count (`is_moe`) now come from the same config Python's `get_text_config()` returns for these models. Top-level values still take precedence, so `--hf-overrides` behaves as before.

## Validation

Unit tests (Linux, Rust 1.95.0):

```
cargo test -p vllm-text --lib backend::hf::config
test result: ok. 14 passed; 0 failed
```

End to end on one A40 (driver 580.159.04), with the Rust frontend built from the base commit and from this change against the same Python install:

```
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH=<vllm-rs> \
  vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
```

| Model | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B` (ships `tokenizer.json`) | Rust frontend exits: `tokenizer error: the model config does not define vocab_size` | Starts; `/v1/chat/completions` "What is the capital of France? Answer in one word." (temperature 0) returns `Paris` |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` + `tokenizer.json` saved from `AutoTokenizer` | Same error | Starts; `/v1/models` responds |

Validated on `3fe917abb` (the newest main commit with a published precompiled wheel at the time). This branch is rebased onto a later main; nothing under `rust/` changed between the two.

<details>
<summary>Startup log excerpts</summary>

Before:
```
(RustFrontend) INFO [hf.rs:227] loading tokenizer with fastokens path=.../Qwen2.5-Omni-3B/.../tokenizer.json
(RustFrontend) ERROR [cmd/src/main.rs:110] process failed with error: failed to create chat/text backends
  tokenizer error: the model config does not define `vocab_size`
RuntimeError: Frontend process failed during engine core initialization.
```

After:
```
INFO [utils.py:372] Launching Rust frontend: /root/vllm-rs-fix frontend ...
{"choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Paris"},"finish_reason":"stop"}], ...}
```
</details>

Not tested: `vllm-rs serve` with data parallelism on Qwen3-Omni (see Details).

## Details

**Root cause.** These configs nest the language model config two levels deep:

```
{ "model_type": "qwen3_asr",
  "thinker_config": { "audio_config": {...}, "text_config": { "vocab_size": 151936, ... } } }
```

`ModelConfig` in `rust/src/text/src/backend/hf/config.rs` only looks at the top level and `text_config` (alias `llm_config`). On the Python side, `Qwen3ASRConfig.get_text_config()` (and the transformers configs for Qwen2.5-Omni / Qwen3-Omni) return `thinker_config.text_config`, which is why the Python frontend works.

**Change.** Treat `thinker_config` as another alias of `text_config` (next to `llm_config`), and make `effective_text_config()` follow nested text configs to the innermost one. `vocab_size()`, `eos_token_ids()` and `model_type()` already recurse into `text_config`, so they reach `thinker_config.text_config` without further changes. Top-level values still win, so every config that worked before resolves the same way. A config with both a top-level `text_config` and a `thinker_config` would be rejected as a duplicate field; none of the Qwen2.5-Omni, Qwen3-Omni or Qwen3-ASR checkpoints has both. `talker_config` is not followed.

**Side effect worth reviewing.** For Qwen3-Omni, `num_experts` (128) also lives under the thinker, so `is_moe()` changes from false to true. In `vllm-rs serve`, that value decides whether the in-process DP coordinator is started (`rust/src/server/src/config.rs`). The new value matches what the Python engine computes, but I have only reasoned about this from the code and have not run Qwen3-Omni with DP > 1.

**Not in this PR.** Part 1 of #61057 (no `tokenizer.json` in the official Qwen3-ASR / Qwen3-Omni repos). I asked in the issue whether a clearer error or building the tokenizer from `vocab.json`/`merges.txt` is preferred.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR references #61057. #60979 touches the same model family but only the Python side (`qwen3_asr.py`, ragged audio batches).

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid reusing random draws across block verification rounds
author: DimensionSTP
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61114. Give block verification fresh acceptance and draft random draws when an uncommitted position is revisited in a later round.

## Claims

- Removes the cross-round sampling bias for deterministic and probabilistic drafts in Model Runner V2.
- Preserves seeded repeat, request-order and batch-splitting behavior in both verification modes. Standard probabilistic token sequences change, but their target distribution is retained.
- Uses a shared step-seed helper without new forwarding parameters, round-position tensors, scheduler state, host synchronization or sampling kernel launches.
- Covers ordinary draft sampling, the shared DFlash2/LiLiCorr candidate walk, DSpark and ordinary watermark fallback.

## Validation

Real V2 generation with one-layer, context-independent Llama target/draft models, TP=1, float32, two speculative tokens and 10,000 requests per configuration:

| Draft | Verification | Expected P(third token = 0) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deterministic | standard | 0.5000 | 0.5039 | 0.5039 |
| Deterministic | block | 0.5000 | 0.4171 | 0.4989 |
| Probabilistic | standard | 0.3000 | 0.3083 | 0.3055 |
| Probabilistic | block | 0.3000 | 0.3558 | 0.2898 |

All six output marginals pass in each updated configuration; both original block cases fail. Worker types and nonzero acceptance metrics confirm the real V2 draft-model path. All four updated configurations pass seeded repeat, reordered requests and split batches. Standard deterministic output retains its original hash; standard probabilistic output does not. The probabilistic block run also passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Before-fix values are the retained original model measurements; the updated four-case matrix was rerun after this review.

The official multi-round regression fails before the fix. Disabling only the acceptance step helper fails the deterministic block distribution assertion. Disabling only the cached draft step helper while retaining the acceptance repair also fails the probabilistic distribution assertion. Disabling only the candidate-walk helper fails both FP32/FP64 parity cases. These negative controls contain actual assertion failures, not setup errors or skips. The mixed watermark test covers the fused ordinary fallback and unchanged raw-logit caching.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/watermarking --ignore=tests/watermarking/test_engine_compatibility.py --ignore=tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/watermark.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash2/speculator.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/watermarking/test_gumbel.py
git diff --check
```

Results: 350 official tests pass in the CUDA run, with three existing skips; all applicable native hooks pass. Separately, 175 CPU controls pass, with 76 accelerator-dependent skips. Five supplemental CUDA controls cover signed seeds, scalar/per-token cache columns, padding, graph replay and ordinary watermark fallback. Model tests use Triton attention and a bounded KV cache because this host's driver cannot run the reused CUDA 13 FlashAttention wheel. The candidate-walk tests cover FP32/FP64 step-seed parity and retain the existing conditional proposal-cache, padding and graph-replay checks. No AMD, full-runner CUDA graph, adaptive-policy model evaluation or throughput claim is made.

## Details

Block verification reads uniforms for draft positions past the finally accepted prefix. Reusing `(request seed, position)` in the next round reuses randomness conditioned on the preceding decision. Probabilistic drafting has the same problem with its position-keyed Gumbel noise.

Following review, `spec_step_seed(seed, step)` mixes the draft step into the seed's upper 32 bits. Cached Gumbel sampling uses its existing cache column; the DFlash2/LiLiCorr walk uses its loop step. A request's `(position, step)` pair does not repeat across rounds. Block acceptance calls the same helper with `i` inside its verification loop, always starting from the original request seed. No new flag is needed, including in DSpark and the watermark adapters. The fused ordinary watermark fallback uses the same cached step seed; context-keyed watermark draws are unchanged.

Cached draft seeding now applies under standard verification too. This changes standard probabilistic seeded sequences, not their target distribution; the updated implementation remains reproducible. This is distinct from #59355/#60945's residual lookahead bounds and #60652's grammar-invalid drafts, and complements #54282's within-round draft/target stream separation.

Related PR #61153 addresses the same bug with an explicit round-position tensor and a different seed mixer. This implementation instead uses the existing draft step inside the kernels. Both implementations passed the earlier shared four-case CUDA distribution comparison on #61153 at `170dcc217`; that comparison predates this reviewer-requested simplification. This is an alternative implementation of the same repair, not a claim that #61153 is incorrect.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][LoRA] Disable KV-sharing fast prefill for LoRA batches
author: waizuichougou
body:
## Overview

MRV2 KV-sharing fast prefill reduces the batch to logits rows while LoRA mappings still describe the full batch, causing incorrect outputs or CUDA illegal memory access. Following review, this PR chooses a batch-level fallback over additional LoRA metadata and graph-capture machinery: batches containing LoRA use regular prefill, while base-only batches retain fast prefill.

## Claims

- LoRA and mixed base/LoRA batches fall back; base-only batches retain fast prefill, including after LoRA requests.
- Removes the previous compact-metadata and graph-capture changes.

## Validation

- CPU mock regression: **1 passed**, with GPU visibility disabled. Verifies LoRA fallback and subsequent base fast-prefill recovery. Worker test file: **53 passed**.
- Local real-weight E2E: CUDA illegal memory access before the fix; passes afterward. Kept outside the repository CI tests.
- Gemma4 E2B on NVIDIA GB10: compile-only, breakable PIECEWISE, and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE each completed **20/20 requests** and **20/20 full-prefill controls**, with finite logits and correct fallback routing.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Clear stale shared block-table rows
author: positive666
body:
## Overview

A larger MTP decode graph can read stale shared block-table rows after the target batch shrinks, allowing padded work to address another request's cache or state.

Move shared-row cleanup into `BlockTables`, as suggested in review.

## Claims

- Preserve active rows, returned views, and independent PCP output buffers.
- Remove the MTP caller workaround without changing model math.

| BlockTables, speculator, PCP suites with the fix | 140 passed |

title: [Bugfix][Watermarking] Skip incomplete opening contexts
author: TQCB
body:
## Overview

Skip watermarking until the response contains a complete generated-token context, across Gumbel and dual-key Gumbel standard and speculative sampling. Follow-up to the shared padded-opening issue discussed in #58426; that PR adds SynthID and leaves this behavior question separate.

## Claims

- The first `context_width` output tokens use ordinary sampling independently of context deduplication, including draft, recovery, and bonus tokens.
- Detection behavior and PRF mappings are preserved.

## Validation

- `../vllm_fork/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/watermarking -q`: 134 passed, 61 accelerator-only tests skipped on macOS.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.
- Rescored all 23 pre-change golden generations with the default detector: scores, p-values, scored-token counts, and decisions match within the existing 1e-9 tolerance.
- GPU engine validation remains pending. Retained model outputs establish detection compatibility only; they do not evaluate generation with this patch.

## Details

Response-local contexts are padded with -1 before enough output tokens exist. With a fixed key, this reuses the same opening watermark randomness across prompts and can reduce opening diversity. The patch combines an incomplete-context mask with the existing sampling masks; it adds no host read or device synchronization. Prompt tokens remain excluded from the seed under every deduplication setting; `all` still searches the prompt for repeated contexts.

Submitted detection text may be a fragment and need not start at the generation boundary, so this PR does not change detector preprocessing or add detector options. On new full responses, the unwatermarked opening positions can dilute the detector signal. Generation can diverge beyond the opening because later tokens depend on earlier choices.

Goldens reflect the new generation behavior. Engine reproducibility tests now pin request seeds because openings use ordinary randomness. The repetitive-fixture confidence guard allows a p-value ratio up to 0.6 rather than 0.5: one updated fixture has ratio 0.514 while remaining below the unchanged detection threshold.

AI assistance: implementation, tests, and this description were prepared with Codex (OpenAI).

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix Gemma 4 image/audio placeholder strings
author: Damin3927
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61195. `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.get_placeholder_str` returned Gemma 3n's `<image_soft_token>` / `<audio_soft_token>`, so with `--chat-template-content-format string` every Gemma 4 image or audio chat request failed with `Failed to apply prompt replacement`. It now returns `<|image|>` / `<|audio|>`, the tokens the prompt replacements target.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 image and audio chat requests work with `--chat-template-content-format string` instead of returning HTTP 500.
- `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration`, which registers Gemma 4's multimodal processor, gets the same image fix. `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` inherits the Gemma 4 method and is covered without a change.
- No change for the default `openai` content format: there the chat template inserts `<|image|>` itself, and `get_placeholder_str` never reaches the prompt text.

## Validation

New test `test_placeholder_str_is_replaced` in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py`. It resolves the model class the way the chat frontend does (`get_model_cls`), writes its `get_placeholder_str` into a prompt, and runs the real multimodal processor (configs and tokenizer only, no weights).

| Case | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, image | `Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]` | passed |
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, audio | `Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['audio'][0]` | passed |
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, video | passed | passed |
| `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`, image | `Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]` | passed |
| `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`, video | passed | passed |

Commands, run on macOS arm64 with CPU only. vLLM was imported from the source tree without compiled extensions, so `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` selects the CPU platform:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py \
  tests/renderers/test_gemma4_chat_template.py
# 55 passed, 19 skipped (the skips are test_gemma4_unified.py: checkpoint marked not available online)

pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py
# all hooks pass
```

Through the chat frontend: `parse_chat_messages(..., content_format="string")`, then the Gemma 4 chat template, then the processor, with `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` and one image + text user message:

- Before: content is `'<image_soft_token>\nWhat is in this image?'`, and processing fails with `AssertionError: Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]`.
- After: content is `'<|image|>\nWhat is in this image?'`, and the image placeholder lands at offset 4 with length 258, the same as with the `openai` format. The two rendered prompts differ only by the `\n` that the string path puts between content parts.

Not tested: a GPU server run of this branch, and model evals. The original failure came from `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0` serving a Gemma 4 31B instruction model, and this machine has no GPU.

## Details

Root cause (full write-up in #61195):

- `_get_prompt_updates` targets the HF processor's `image_token_id` / `audio_token_id`. In Gemma 4's `tokenizer_config.json` these are `<|image|>` (258880) and `<|audio|>` (258881), and the chat template emits the same tokens.
- `<image_soft_token>` / `<audio_soft_token>` are the Gemma 3n strings (`gemma3n_mm.py`) and are not in Gemma 4's vocabulary.
- In the `string` content format, `MultiModalItemTracker.add` returns `get_placeholder_str(...)`, and `_get_full_multimodal_text_prompt` writes it into the message text. So the replacement target never appears in the prompt.

`get_placeholder_str` is a classmethod with no processor access, so the fix keeps the hard-coded strings that `gemma3_mm.py`, `gemma3n_mm.py` and the existing Gemma 4 `"<|video|>"` branch use. The Gemma 4 offline example (`examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py`) and the Rust frontend's Gemma 4 spec in #58649 already use `<|image|>`.

Why this is not a duplicate: I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `image_soft_token`, `get_placeholder_str` + Gemma 4, `Failed to apply prompt replacement`, and Gemma 4 + content format. #41452 / #41459 fixed the same error message for images in tool messages, which has a different cause (the tool-message template). The follow-on `Expected a cached item for mm_hash` error described in #61195 is the general cache desync tracked in #46354 and is not addressed here.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the fix and test, and draft this description. The commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Stage fused KDA decode weights after loading
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

The ROCm Kimi-K3 fused KDA decode read uninitialized memory as its conv1d and gated-norm weights whenever weight loaders were skipped, as with `--load-format dummy`. This intermittently produced NaN logprobs. Those copies are now built from the final parameters after loading.

## Claims

- `process_weights_after_loading` stages `decode_conv1d_weight` and `decode_norm_weight` from `conv1d.weight` and `o_norm.weight`, and the two side-effect weight loaders are removed.
- This fixes the intermittent HTTP 400 (`Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan`) in `test_prefix_cache.py` on MI355.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. In `test_prefix_cache.py[offload-partial]`, NaN runs went from 5 of 21 to 0 of 20. The new `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` fails before (18432/18432 elements are NaN) and passes after. `models/kimi_k3` passes: 311 passed.

The perf runs used `riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy` at TP1, 5 interleaved runs per column, each with a fresh server. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 256 out, conc 16) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 7.687 ± 0.025 | 7.672 ± 0.009 |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 634.4 ± 6.5 | 633.5 ± 2.5 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 5.434 ± 0.004 | 5.454 ± 0.017 |

No real-weight Kimi-K3 checkpoint was available for an accuracy run. With real weights, the buffers receive the same values the loaders wrote before.

## Details

The fp32 copies from #50654 are non-persistent `torch.empty` buffers that were written only inside the conv1d and o_norm weight loaders. `DummyModelLoader` skips both, so the fused decode used whatever the allocator returned: usually zeros, sometimes NaN. That poisoned the recurrent state from the first decode step. The post-load hook runs for every loader, including layerwise reload (the buffer storage is reused, so CUDA graphs stay valid). It skips weights that arrive already processed. The NVIDIA `KimiK3DeltaAttention` has the same latent issue and is left for a follow-up. #59245 reads these buffers and will need a rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Keep VLLM_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES out of the compile cache key
author: DanBlanaru
body:
## Overview

Exclude `VLLM_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES` from `envs.compile_factors()`, so engines that differ only in which placement-group bundles they run on share a torch.compile cache key.

## Claims

- Fixes cache misses across engines and runs: with this variable hashed, every engine of a multi-engine Ray deployment that sets it per engine (e.g. RL frameworks placing one engine per GPU group of a shared placement group) compiles under its own key, and a later run reuses the cache only if each engine happens to get the same bundles again.
- No change for deployments that don't set the variable.

## Validation

Unit test (new `test_ray_bundle_indices_is_not_compile_factor`), CPU, `vllm/` from this branch on `PYTHONPATH` with dependencies from the vllm 0.31.0 wheel; `--noconftest` because `tests/conftest.py` needs the full test requirements:

```
PYTHONPATH=$PWD VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -q --noconftest tests/test_envs.py
```

| `vllm/envs.py` | new test | rest of `tests/test_envs.py` |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | pass | 58 pass |
| `main` (2534a96fc) | **fail** | 58 pass |

End to end: the identical one-line my RL runs on vLLM 0.25.1 (10 TP8 engines with `RayExecutorV2`, each with its own `VLLM_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES`, on a multi-node GB300 job). Before it, each run wrote ~10 torch.compile cache keys (one per engine); with it, a cold run writes one key and warm runs load it (Dynamo + Inductor ~12 s -> ~2 s per engine). Not re-run end to end on `main`: the change only edits the `ignored_factors` set, and both consumers (`compilation/backends.py`, `compilation/caching.py`) still hash `envs.compile_factors()` the same way.

## Details

Root cause: `compile_factors()` hashes every known env var not in `ignored_factors`. `VLLM_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES` only selects which bundles (GPUs) of a placement group the engine's workers use (`v1/executor/ray_executor.py`, `ray_executor_v2.py`); it has no effect on the compiled graphs. Same category as `VLLM_HOST_IP` and `VLLM_PORT`, which are already ignored.

Interaction with #42136 (envs.py to pydantic-settings): that branch keeps `ray_bundle_indices` hashed as well. If it lands first, the equivalent fix is `json_schema_extra={"compile_factor": False}` on that field; happy to rebase either way.

Not a duplicate: searched open issues/PRs for `VLLM_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES`, `compile_factors` and `ignored_factors`; none excludes this variable. #39479 (hashing refactor follow-ups) and #42136 touch the same function but not this variable.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find the root cause, write the change and test, and draft this description; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Reject beam search in completion render
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Reject `use_beam_search=true` in `/v1/completions/render`, consistent with the existing behavior of `/v1/chat/completions/render`.

## Claims

Reject unsupported beam search requests with HTTP 400 instead of silently converting them into ordinary sampling requests.

## Validation

Added a service-level regression test covering the error code, message, and rejection before prompt preprocessing. The test fails before the fix because the handler returns a list of `GenerateRequest` objects instead of an error.

After the fix:

- Render tests: **29 passed**.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, mypy, and test tethering.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py \
  -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/render/serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py
```

## Details

Completion render previously converted beam search requests into `SamplingParams` without preserving beam search semantics or `length_penalty`, potentially causing these requests to be executed as ordinary sampling.

This change rejects unsupported beam search requests after model validation and before prompt preprocessing, using the existing chat render error message.

Regular `/v1/completions` beam search support is unaffected.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Fix MultiConnector stats and proxy SSE responses
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Using direct Mooncake with Mooncake Store can fail in MultiConnector's metrics handler, and the Mooncake example proxy labels SSE responses as JSON, causing clients such as AIPerf to reject them. Fix both integration issues by respecting optional metrics exporters and returning the correct streaming Content-Type.

## Claims

- Skip children without Prometheus exporters while continuing to forward supported metrics and `engine_idx`.
- Return `text/event-stream` for streaming requests on `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`; preserve JSON responses for non-streaming requests and forward response bytes unchanged.

```diff
 P transfer stats -> MultiConnector metrics
-  require an exporter for every child with stats
+  forward stats only to registered exporters

 D SSE frames -> Mooncake proxy -> client
-  Content-Type: application/json
+  Content-Type: text/event-stream
```

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_proxy.py \
  -k 'TestMultiConnectorStats or test_mooncake_proxy' -q
```

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stats-only child, with empty or mixed exporter registry | Both regression cases fail on main `c75cb63cd2bb` | All 17 stats cases pass |
| Real ASGI routes, completion/chat × streaming/non-streaming | 2 streaming cases fail on main `258b97ff6bc1`; 2 non-streaming cases pass | All 4 cases pass |
| Combined PR branch, based on `258b97ff6bc1` | — | **21 passed, 15 deselected** |

The metrics regression also checks that the supported child's payload reaches its exporter with `engine_idx=2`. The proxy regression mocks only the remote P/D calls and checks the actual response headers and bytes. In Buildkite, the V1 KV Connectors step runs the metrics regression. The proxy regression is CPU-only, so it is marked `cpu_test` and runs in the CPU V1 Others step, which also lists the proxy as a source dependency so proxy-only changes still trigger it.

Changed-file pre-commit checks pass:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  .buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml \
  examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_proxy.py
```

Earlier ROCm end-to-end validation used integration commit `b41cf676db9cc124fffbcf305f7fa8c8d2f895b8`, containing the identical proxy file and metrics `observe()` implementation:

- [Before the proxy fix](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38169410559): AIPerf attempted JSON parsing of SSE frames; all 13 sampled warmup responses were rejected.
- [C16 serving](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38174661539): Kimi-K3 + DSpark3, 1P1D/16 MI355X, Mooncake RDMA + TCP Store completed a 3600-second performance window with 2006 successes and 4 errors. The workflow later failed while importing the separate GSM8K evaluator.
- [Natural GSM8K](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38203116096): flexible extraction 1269/1319 (96.21%).

GPU evidence belongs to that integration revision; the current main-based PR branch has local regression coverage. Store lease timeouts and empty-response failures remain separate limitations. No additional GPU experiment was dispatched for this PR.

## Details

**Metrics:** `KVConnectorBase_V1.build_prom_metrics()` may return `None`. MultiConnector's metrics factory already excludes null exporters, while stats collection independently includes stats-only children. Direct Mooncake provides stats without an exporter, so its worker stats trigger the assertion in the API output handler. A conditional exporter lookup follows the existing optional-interface contract. Stats collection is unchanged; missing exporter IDs are skipped, so this assertion no longer detects inconsistent IDs in the metrics path.

**HTTP:** `_handle_completions` already forwards the request's streaming mode to D. Use the same flag to select the response media type. KV transfer and generation logic are unchanged.

The metrics portion follows up the **same fix proposed in #43836 for #43828**, adapted to the current flat stats payload with regression coverage. That PR remains open; this is not a distinct solution. The submitting operator explicitly requested including it here to cover both direct-Mooncake integration failures. Searches found no overlapping proxy SSE-header fix.

Both changes are reversible and scoped to metrics forwarding and the example proxy. AI assistance (Codex) was used; this remains a draft submitted at the human operator's request.
