title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] V2 rejection sampler: return logprob_token_ids scores
author: SCcagg5
body:
## Overview

With the V2 model runner and speculative decoding, a request that sets `logprob_token_ids` (and no `logprobs`) gets no logprobs back whenever another request in the same batch has draft tokens. `RejectionSampler` only looked at `max_num_logprobs`, so `logprob_token_ids` was dropped on that path. The regular V2 `Sampler` already handles it through `get_logprobs_dims`.

`/v1/systemone` reads are such requests (`max_tokens=1`, `logprob_token_ids`): next to a streaming chat on an MTP model, every read failed with `HTTP 400: No logprobs available for item 0`. This passes the per-request token ids to `compute_topk_scores` in the rejection sampler. Related: #42592 / #44727 (the same kind of mixed batch, on the V1 sampler, a different file).

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-27B with MTP 3, 6 `/v1/systemone` calls (4 questions, 2k-token state) while 4 chat streams run: 6/6 fail before, 6/6 succeed after.
- Chat is not affected: time to first token 0.52 → 0.60 s and inter-chunk latency p50 191 → 192 ms with and without systemone on the engine.
- The returned probabilities are not changed by the chat load: mean absolute difference 0.007 (max 0.041) between a cold call and the same call next to chat, the same as between a cold call and the same call repeated alone on a cached state (0.007, max 0.039).
- Batches without `logprob_token_ids` are unchanged (`compute_topk_scores` takes its fast path when `max_token_ids == 0`); without speculative decoding this code path is not used.

## Validation

Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit with MTP 3 on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev273` (`2eb491e18b`), V2 model runner, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --logprobs-mode raw_logprobs`, `--max-num-seqs 8`. The same change was applied to the nightly's copy of the file for the runs. Chat: 4 closed-loop streaming requests (256 tokens).

| | systemone alone | systemone + 4 chats, main | systemone + 4 chats, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| errors | 0 / 6 | 6 / 6 (HTTP 400, no logprobs) | 0 / 6 |
| chat errors | | 0 | 0 |

After the review changes the run was repeated (mixed: 0 errors, cold vs next-to-chat mean absolute difference 0.004, max 0.033). The same server also runs `/v1/systemone` accuracy (120 synthetic tickets: 0.90 / 0.67 / 1.00, unchanged) and the question-count cases (6.4 / 8.2 / 11.9 / 28.7 s for 1 / 4 / 16 / 64 questions, unchanged) with the change applied. MTP off, on main: no errors (no drafts, so the batch does not go through the rejection sampler); not re-run with the change.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py
```

31 passed with the change. New tests in `test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py` build a real `LogprobTokenIdsState` and check the returned ids and scores against `log_softmax` / the raw logits for every row:
- `test_logprob_token_ids_without_topk_logprobs`: token ids only, raw and logits modes, and nothing is computed when none are requested;
- `test_logprob_token_ids_with_topk_logprobs`: top-k `logprobs=1` narrower than the widest `logprob_token_ids`, requests with and without ids;
- `test_logprob_token_ids_with_adaptive_verification`: one chunk over compacted logits, device `cu_num_logits` and a host-side upper bound, same result as the fixed-boundary layout;
- `test_get_logprobs_dims_with_only_token_ids`.

`test_gather_sampler_output_logprobs_and_nans` is parametrized over top-k only, token ids only and token ids wider than top-k. The CUDA tests of these files are skipped on ROCm by `current_platform.is_cuda()`; I ran them locally with that check replaced by `torch.cuda.is_available()`. The new tests fail on main. The `model_runner.py` call site of the sharded gather (TP > 1) has no test and was not run.

## Details

- `RejectionSampler.__call__` calls `Sampler.get_logprobs_dims` once and passes `logprobs_dims` to `_verify_in_chunks` and `_get_logprobs_tensors`, which also takes the chunk's `expanded_idx_mapping` (`compute_topk_scores` needs it to map each logits row to its request).
- `Sampler.get_logprobs_dims` no longer has `include_token_ids`: the sharded gather in `model_runner.py` sizes its buffers with the token-id columns for batches with draft tokens too.
- Not covered: DSpark and the other speculators were not run; they go through the same `RejectionSampler.__call__`.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Omit unset sampling params in render output
author: hickeyma
body:
## Overview

Rust render sends `null` for every unset sampling field and Python `/inference/v1/generate` rejects them. This skips serializing `None` so Rust render output can go straight into Python generate. 

## Claims

- `/v1/chat/completions/render` on the Rust frontend no longer emits `null` in `sampling_params`
- Rust render → Python generate works for requests that leave float fields like `temperature` or `top_p` unset which is nearly every request

## Validation

Before, a minimal chat render returned:

    "sampling_params": {"temperature": null, "top_p": null, "max_tokens": 64, "watermarking": true, ...}

After, the null keys are gone.

Tests added:
- `sampling_params_serialization_omits_unset_fields` (`vllm-text` unit test, includes a round trip)
- `render_chat_omits_unset_sampling_params` (`vllm-server` route test)
- `test_rust_render_sampling_params_without_nulls_validate` (Python test for a body without nulls validates, `"temperature": null` is rejected)

## Details

`vllm_text::SamplingParams` has `Option` fields but no `skip_serializing_none`. The attribute on `GenerateSamplingParams` doesn't reach the flattened inner struct, so the nulls leaked out.

- `watermarking: true` is still emitted. It isn't an `Option` and Python treats `None` and `True` the same
- Nested `structured_outputs` and `repetition_detection` don't emit nulls, so they needed no change
- No schema change. Unset fields come back as `None` through `#[serde(default)]`

No existing PR covers this (checked open PRs for "skip_serializing_none sampling" and "Rust render null sampling_params").

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Slice expert LoRA by the unpadded per-rank size under TP
author: aoshen02
body:
## Overview

Expert LoRA factors are sliced at the wrong offset under TP > 1 when the MoE backend pads the expert intermediate dimension (e.g. Marlin / FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4). Every rank except rank 0 silently applies the wrong LoRA rows.

## Claims

- `FusedMoEWithLoRA` and `FusedMoE3DWithLoRA` shard an adapter along the intermediate dim by the unpadded per-rank size, matching how the base expert weights are sharded.
- No behavior change when the backend does not pad.
- No dependency on a FlashInfer version.

## Validation

CPU-only check of the slicing (TP 2 and 4, every rank, per-expert and both 3D layouts, padded and unpadded), run locally and not added to the test suite:

| `vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py` | passed | failed |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 6 (unpadded cases) | 6 (padded cases) |
| this PR | 12 | 0 |

`ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` are clean on the changed file.

End-to-end on `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, TP 2, `moe_backend="marlin"` (per-rank intermediate size 1440 padded to 1536), random expert-only LoRA (rank 8, seeded; `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj`). Reference: the same model at TP 1 with `triton_unfused`, which does no TP slicing. 16 prompts x 200 tokens, teacher-forced `prompt_logprobs`. Nightly arm64 image at `af7f9488c` (the changed file is byte-identical to `ffec22127` there), one run per row:

| TP 2 marlin | adapter | MAE vs ref | effect projection | effect correlation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | none | 0.150 | – | – |
| `main` | small | 0.444 | 0.38 | 0.47 |
| `main` | large | 1.682 | 0.53 | 0.50 |
| this PR | none | 0.157 | – | – |
| this PR | small | 0.139 | 0.76 | 0.82 |
| this PR | large | 1.013 | 0.83 | 0.77 |

`triton_unfused` at TP 2 is affected as well (1440 padded to 1472): small adapter 0.444 on `main`, 0.144 with this PR (no-adapter floor 0.137).

The no-adapter rows are the Marlin-vs-Triton floor (Marlin differs from itself by 0.09 across two runs). With this change the small adapter is back at that floor; the projection of the adapter effect (logprob with adapter minus base) on the reference effect goes from 0.38 to 0.76. The large adapter degrades the model itself (Marlin self-difference 0.69), so only the direction is meaningful there.

The same on/off contrast on DeepSeek V4.1 (TP 4, 576 padded to 640, FlashInfer TRTLLM experts with a prototype LoRA path, change backported to an older dev build): MAE against the unpadded Triton backend 0.028 -> 0.014 for a small adapter (no-adapter floor 0.014) and 0.73 -> 0.31 for a large one.

## Details

Root cause: `_slice_w13_b` / `_slice_w2_a` use `moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition` as the per-rank stride. `RoutedExperts.__init__` overwrites that field with the result of `maybe_roundup_sizes()`, so it is the padded size (MXFP4 rounds up to 128 for Marlin / TRTLLM / DeepGEMM / CUTLASS and to 64 for Triton). The base weights are sharded by `loaded_weight.shape[shard_dim] // tp_size` in `RoutedExperts._load_w13` / `_load_w2`. With 576 padded to 640, the base weight of rank `r` holds rows `[576 r, 576 (r + 1))` while the adapter slice is `[640 r, 640 (r + 1))`. Nothing raises because the slice is copied into the head of a zero buffer. We first observed this on DeepSeek V4.1 (TP 4, padded MoE backends).

Fix: use `moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded` as the stride. Buffers keep the padded size with a zero tail. For the concatenated `(gate, up)` layout of the 3D class, the up half is placed at the allocated per-rank size, where the base `w13` has it.

Not addressed: GPT-OSS MXFP4 uses a block-aligned shard stride in its own loader (`cdiv(intermediate_size / 32, tp_size) * 32`), which differs from `intermediate_size // tp_size` at TP 4 / 8.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs and issues for `_slice_w13_b`, `intermediate_size_per_partition LoRA padded`, `fused_moe LoRA TP slice`; nothing addresses this. #61164 and #61165 touch other parts of the MoE LoRA path and do not overlap.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor request_id and X-Request-Id in chat and completions render
author: hickeyma
body:
## Overview

Python render now uses the caller's `request_id` / `X-Request-Id` for chat and completions instead of always minting a random one.

## Claims

- `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/messages/render` return `chatcmpl-{id}` where `id` is the `X-Request-Id` header, else the body `request_id`, else a random UUID
- `/v1/completions/render` returns `cmpl-{id}` for one prompt and `cmpl-{id}-{i}` for several
- Requests that send no ID behave as before

## Validation

New tests in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py`:

- body ID is honored
- header beats body
- random IDs are unique across calls
- single-prompt completions
- multi-prompt completions with the suffix

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -v
```

## Details

Rust render and the coupled chat path already honor both the header and the body field. Python render didn't, so an ID couldn't be followed across render, generate and derender. I reused `BaseServing._base_request_id`, so the precedence matches the coupled path.

For multi-prompt completions I only add the `-{i}` suffix when there is more than one prompt. That keeps a single prompt equal to Rust's `cmpl-{id}`. The coupled `OpenAIServingCompletion` always appends `-{i}`, so this differs slightly from it.

`raw_request` is optional on the render methods, so the Cohere and Anthropic callers and the coupled paths are unchanged. Responses render is untouched.

No duplicate: I searched open PRs for render request ID handling and found nothing.

title: [Bugfix] Share PCP-aware local GPU indexing for NUMA binding
author: SherifWaly
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix PCP-aware NUMA binding for colocated data-parallel GPU workers and their EngineCore processes by sharing GPU-index calculation with device selection.

Identified while evaluating [ivanium/vllm#53](https://github.com/ivanium/vllm/pull/53). This PR only fixes indexing; automatic default enablement is separate work.

## Claims

- Use one `ParallelConfig.get_local_gpu_index()` helper for GPU device selection, NUMA worker lookup, and EngineCore DP shard starts.
- Use the existing PCP-aware `ParallelConfig.world_size` for DP offsets and EngineCore shard bounds, so both account for TP × PCP × PP.
- Preserve existing local-rank behavior for Ray, external launchers, and DP replicas spanning multiple nodes; preserve manual binding overrides and memory-policy fallback.

## Validation

Local checks (macOS, using an existing adjacent virtualenv for pytest):

```bash
../vllm-upstream-kv-metrics/.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/utils_/test_numa_utils.py tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py -q
# 51 passed

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/parallel.py vllm/utils/numa_utils.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py tests/utils_/test_numa_utils.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy and CI test tethering.
```

Seven PCP regression cases failed before the fix. The passing suite covers PCP/PP DP offsets, manual CPU-list indexing, local/global DP rank precedence, launch-rank overrides, complete EngineCore shard coverage, and unchanged non-offset branches.

A helper reproducer using a real `ParallelConfig` with TP=2, PCP=2, PP=1, DP=2 and local DP rank 1 confirms `world_size=4`, first-worker GPU index 4, and NUMA node 1 for both worker and EngineCore with topology `[0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1]`.

The existing Buildkite `utils_` suites include these tests on NVIDIA and AMD jobs.

Validation limitations: no Linux/GPU serving run, model evaluation, or performance benchmark has been performed. A PCP × DP serving reproducer checking actual worker and EngineCore binding is still needed. The normal local pytest invocation is blocked by missing `tblib` in `tests/conftest.py`; the focused run above bypasses that conftest and does not establish a full-suite pass.

## Details

GPU device selection already includes PCP in the DP stride, but the NUMA helper used only TP × PP. EngineCore also used a too-small, incorrectly offset shard range. This can select another shard's NUMA node or omit nodes needed by PCP workers.

For colocated single-node MP with TP=2, PP=1, local DP rank=1, and worker local rank=0:

| PCP | Actual worker GPU | Old NUMA lookup | New NUMA lookup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| 2 | 4 | 2 | 4 |
| 4 | 8 | 2 | 8 |

GPU selection is unchanged; NUMA lookup now matches it. With PCP=2, EngineCore's NUMA lookup covers GPUs `[4, 5, 6, 7]` instead of `[2, 3]`.

DCP groups existing ranks; it does not introduce another worker-count multiplier. The worker world size remains TP × PCP × PP.

The new config helper centralizes the existing device-selection rules and uses the already computed worker world size. NUMA worker lookup calls that helper, and EngineCore uses it for the shard start plus `world_size` for the shard length. No steady-state inference operation or synchronization is added.

Duplicate-work searches on 2026-10-12 for open upstream PRs mentioning NUMA with PCP or `prefill_context_parallel_size` found no other PR addressing this GPU binding mismatch. The predecessor trial concerns automatic default enablement, not this fix.

Human review and confirmation of relevant tests are required; they are not claimed by this description.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Emit kv/ec transfer params at the top level of render output
author: hickeyma
body:
## Overview

Python render now puts `kv_transfer_params` and `ec_transfer_params` at the top level of the generate request on every route, instead of leaving them in `sampling_params.extra_args`. 

## Claims

- Chat and completions render emit the transfer params as top-level fields, the same as responses render
- `sampling_params.extra_args` no longer carries `kv_transfer_params` / `ec_transfer_params` on any render route
- Python render → Rust generate keeps the KV params. Before, P/D quietly recomputed the prompt

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -v
```

Added tests:
- Chat render: both params at the top level, `extra_args == {"foo": 1}` and the request's own `vllm_xargs` untouched
- Completions with two prompts: each generate request carries both params with no `extra_args`
- The existing responses test now also checks that `extra_args` is empty

## Details

Chat and completions only got the params through `to_sampling_params` which puts them in `extra_args`. Responses render sent them in both places. Rust generate never reads `extra_args`. It merges the top-level fields into `vllm_xargs`, so a Python render in front of a Rust generate lost the KV params with no error.

Leaving a copy in `extra_args` is also a trap. If a router clears the top-level block to turn P/D off, Python generate only copies non `None` values back, so the stale `extra_args` copy would still reach the engine.

The fix is a small helper `_hoist_transfer_params`. It copies `extra_args` before popping because `to_sampling_params ` aliases `request.vllm_xargs`. Python generate copies the top-level values back into `extra_args` for the engine, so engine behavior doesn't change.

One observable change. Anything reading `sampling_params.extra_args.kv_transfer_params` from render output won't find it there anymore. I am unaware of any such client doing this. llm-d's coordinator doesn't read it. `vllm_xargs` can't carry a dict value, so stripping these keys can't remove anything a client put there.

Not a duplicate.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stop re-parsing the whole GLM tool argument per chunk
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

Streaming a GLM tool call re-parses the whole argument on every chunk, so a long argument (for example a 100 KB file `Write`) costs quadratic CPU on the API server. This PR streams the open argument value with work proportional to each chunk.

Related: #51141 fixes the same pattern for the Inkling parser only (compared under Details).

## Claims

- Parser cost per streamed GLM argument chunk no longer grows with argument length: 6.4 ms at 100 KB and 12.7 ms at 200 KB become 7 us at every size (M4 Pro, table below).
- Streamed deltas are unchanged, including schema type coercion and the held-back trailing value for non-string keys.
- Opt-in per parser through a new `ParserEngineConfig.arg_value_extender`. Only `glm47_moe` (GLM-4.7 and later, including GLM-5.x) sets it. Every other parser keeps its current path.
- Model evaluation does not apply, since model output and streamed tool-call text are unchanged.

## Validation

Tests on `691b6c37c`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/parser/engine` | 5869 passed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py` | 39 passed |
| pre-commit on the changed files | passed |

New tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py`:
- `test_long_call_streams_non_streaming_arguments`: a 26 KB GLM call with escapes, non-ASCII and tag-like text, streamed in 7-character chunks through `parse_delta`, gives the same arguments as `extract_tool_calls`. Runs with no schema and with a schema that coerces an integer key.
- `test_conversions_do_not_grow_with_argument_length`: counts streaming calls to the arg converter. With this PR the count is 23 for both 40 and 400 lines of content. On `main` it is 547 and 5,227, so the test fails there.
- Two small tests for the GLM extender: a closing tag split across chunks, and the cases where no extender is created.

**Same output as `main`.** A local differential test streamed 15,000 random GLM tool calls through `main`'s parser and this branch. It used random chunk sizes; schemas with string, integer, object, array, boolean and nullable keys; repeated keys; truncated calls; and tag fragments inside values. Every per-chunk `DeltaMessage` was identical. Both new paths ran: per 3,000 cases, about 100K chunks extended a streamed string value and about 57K extended a held-back value. The same check passed on 6,000 more cases with the GLM regexes from #54971 applied to both sides.

**Per-chunk cost.** The script below streams a GLM `Write` call through `Glm47MoeParser.parse_delta` in 8-character chunks. Each row is the mean cost per chunk since the previous row. Apple M4 Pro, Python 3.12, 3 runs each, range across runs.

| Argument size | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 25 KB | 1.04-1.06 ms | 6.9-7.1 us |
| 50 KB | 3.11-3.17 ms | 7.0-7.1 us |
| 100 KB | 6.37-6.44 ms | 6.9-7.0 us |
| 200 KB | 12.68-12.79 ms | 6.8-7.0 us |

`_compute_arg_delta` alone, timed with a script that drives the extracted parser functions, goes from 6.7 ms to 0.9 us per chunk at 100 KB and from 13.3 ms to 0.95 us at 200 KB, with byte-identical streamed arguments.

**Replay at serving step rate.** A 115 KB Python-file `Write` call, tokenized with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer, replayed through the streaming lexer and `_compute_arg_delta` at 22.4 decode steps/s and 2.8 tokens per step (the rate measured on a GLM-5.3 decode server). Parser CPU per 30 s of stream climbs from 0.008 to 0.20 cores on `main` over the 6.3-minute stream. With this PR it stays between 0.00006 and 0.00008 cores. The streamed arguments are byte-identical.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

Run from the root of a vLLM checkout:

```python
import time
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from tests.parser.engine.conftest import make_mock_tokenizer
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.glm47_moe import Glm47MoeParser

vocab = {"<think>": 1, "</think>": 2, "<tool_call>": 3, "</tool_call>": 4}
request = MagicMock(spec=ChatCompletionRequest)
request.tools, request.tool_choice, request.include_reasoning = [], "auto", True
parser = Glm47MoeParser(make_mock_tokenizer(vocab))

head = (
    "</think><tool_call>Write<arg_key>file_path</arg_key>"
    "<arg_value>/repo/app.py</arg_value><arg_key>content</arg_key><arg_value>"
)
body = (open("vllm/sampling_params.py").read() * 10)[:200_000]
parser.parse_delta(head, [], request, finished=False)

marks, elapsed, chunks = [25_000, 50_000, 100_000, 200_000], 0.0, 0
for i in range(0, len(body), 8):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    parser.parse_delta(body[i : i + 8], [], request, finished=False)
    elapsed += time.perf_counter() - start
    chunks += 1
    if marks and i + 8 >= marks[0]:
        print(f"{marks.pop(0) // 1000} KB: {elapsed / chunks * 1e6:.1f} us per chunk")
        elapsed, chunks = 0.0, 0
```

</details>

## Details

**Trigger.** Any streamed GLM tool call with a long argument, for example a coding agent writing a file.

**Mechanism.** `_compute_arg_delta` runs once per `ARG_VALUE_CHUNK`. Each run works on the whole argument received so far:
- joins `slot.args`;
- runs `_glm47_arg_converter`: three regex passes and `json.dumps`;
- runs `_fix_arg_types`: `json.loads`;
- runs `_safe_arg_prefix`: a Python character loop over the whole JSON, 89% of the time under cProfile.

GLM sets `stream_arg_deltas=True` and no `arg_structural_chars`, so every chunk takes this path.

**Effect.** Cost per chunk grows linearly with the argument, so one tool call costs quadratic time. It runs inside `parse_delta` on the API server's event loop, so it also delays other requests on that server.

**Why the fix is in `engine/`.** The full conversion per chunk lives in `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta`. Every parser that sets `arg_converter` and streams deltas without `arg_structural_chars` runs it on every chunk: GLM-4.7, Granite, Inkling, MiniMax-M2, Nemotron-v3, Qwen3 and Step-3.5. The engine part is a generic opt-in hook, and the format knowledge stays in each parser's file. This PR wires GLM only.

**Fix.**
- After a full conversion, once the safe prefix is sent, the engine calls `arg_value_extender(slot.args)`. It returns an extender for the open trailing value, or `None`.
- For each later chunk, the extender returns the JSON text the chunk appends to that value, or `None` when the chunk may change anything else. On `None`, the engine runs the full conversion as today, which may create a new extender.
- `_safe_arg_prefix` also reports whether the open value streams. If it does, the engine sends the extender's text. If the value is held back (non-string key), it sends nothing, as today.
- `ToolCallSlot.streamed_json` keeps its parts in a list and joins them on read, like `args`, so the fast path does no work proportional to the argument.

Full conversions now happen only around argument boundaries.

**Why the GLM extender gives the same output.**
- The open value runs to the end of the raw arguments, and the converter emits it as a JSON string with `json.dumps`. JSON string escaping maps each character on its own, so a chunk appends `json.dumps(chunk)[1:-1]`.
- A chunk can only change the parse by completing `</arg_value>`. The extender keeps the last 11 raw characters, so it also sees a closing tag split across chunks.
- The extender is only created when the open key is the last key of the parsed arguments. A repeated earlier key updates an earlier position, so that case falls back to the full conversion.
- Schema coercion leaves string keys alone and coerces earlier values the same way every time, so the JSON before the open value stays the same.

**Overlapping PRs** (checked 2026-10-12).
- #51141 (Inkling) caches the wrapper offset, scans the safe prefix incrementally, and sets `arg_structural_chars`. Its scan resumes from the previous end of the JSON. That fits Inkling, whose converter returns a growing slice of the raw text. The GLM converter closes the JSON (`"}`) again on every chunk, so it needs a different approach. I think Inkling could implement `arg_value_extender` too, so both parsers share one mechanism; we can align with #51141 on the order.
- #54971 changes only the GLM key regexes. The extender reuses `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE`, and its close check depends only on `</arg_value>`, so it works with either version (differential above).
- #53739 and #58780 also edit `_compute_arg_delta` or `_safe_arg_prefix`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

**Limitations.** All measurements drive the parser code directly. There is no end-to-end run on a GPU serving deployment.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the implementation, tests and measurements.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] respect `attention_k_eq_v=True` QKK LoRA layers
author: cjackal
body:
## Overview



Fix LoRA weight loading on `attention_k_eq_v` full-attention layers (e.g. `google/gemma-4-31b-it`), where the V slice of the packed `qkv_proj` received no LoRA delta even though HF applies the `k_proj` LoRA to V.

## Claims



- On `attention_k_eq_v` full-attention layers, the `k_proj` LoRA is now packed into both the K and V slices of `qkv_proj`. This matches HF, where `value_states = key_states` (pre-`k_norm`), so a PEFT `k_proj` adapter also changes V.
- Adds an optional per-module `lora_packed_modules` override that `LoRAModelManager._register_packed_modules` checks before the class-level `packed_modules_mapping`.

## Validation



```shell
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py -k packed_loras -v
```

```log
tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_packed_loras[cuda:0] PASSED                                                                                                                                  [ 25%]
tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_packed_loras[cuda:1] PASSED                                                                                                                                  [ 50%]
tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_packed_loras_layer_override[cuda:0] PASSED                                                                                                                   [ 75%]
tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_packed_loras_layer_override[cuda:1] PASSED                                                                                                                   [100%]

============================================================================================ warnings summary ============================================================================================
...
============================================================================== 4 passed, 38 deselected, 14 warnings in 8.08s =============================================================================
```

E2E LoRA adapter eval (internal bench w/ internal adapter)

(baseline is the weight-merged checkpoint)

| run           | greedy_match | mean\|dlp\| | max\|dlp\| | top1_agree |
| ------------- | ------------ | ----------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| LoRA(this PR) | 10 / 10      | 0.0011      | 0.2483     | 100.00%    |
| LoRA(main)    | 10 / 10      | 0.0018      | 0.4157     | 100.00%    |
| base          | 9 / 10       | 0.0053      | 2.0177     | 100.00%    |

## Details



On `attention_k_eq_v` checkpoints, full-attention layers have no `v_proj`. For base weights, `_gemma4_layer_weights_mapper` loads `k_proj` into both the K and V shards of `qkv_proj`. LoRA packing has no equivalent: it used the class-level `packed_modules_mapping` (`q_proj, k_proj, v_proj`) for every layer. The adapter has no `v_proj` for these layers, so the V slice was packed as `None` and V lost the `k_proj` LoRA delta.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve independent tokenizer code_revision in snapshot resolution
author: dskwe
body:
## Overview

Preserve an independent Hugging Face tokenizer `code_revision` when resolving a Hub ID to a local data snapshot. This applies the same guard the processor path already has (introduced in #60825) to the tokenizer resolver.

## Claims

- Before this change, `resolve_tokenizer_args` rewrote `tokenizer_name` to a data-revision snapshot unconditionally. Transformers reads dynamic tokenizer code from a local directory as-is, so a `code_revision` distinct from the data revision was silently shadowed: the code from the data snapshot was loaded, and invalid/older code revisions were silently accepted instead of rejected.
- After this change, default and matching code/data revisions keep the snapshot optimization (byte-identical token IDs vs direct Transformers loading in the regression fixture), while a distinct code revision is passed to Transformers with the Hub ID intact.

## Validation

Linux x86_64 container (Ubuntu, Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0, HF Hub 2.2.0), native source build of this branch (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, editable install). Normal production imports and `get_tokenizer` were exercised; no AST extraction or tokenizer stubs.

Pinned fixture: `hf-internal-testing/test_dynamic_tokenizer` at data revision `08a35780b7a78794436d8654aafa26ee0165c149` (repo has exactly two commits; `73293ac504e43f4a895688b57c65cebe24f01a38` predates the tokenizer code and contains only `.gitattributes`).

- With the fix: `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` → **10 passed** (6 pre-existing + 4 new: 2 parametrized rejection cases, matching/default control pair, and a resolver-contract test).
- A/B discriminative check: reverting only the `code_revision` guard in `vllm/tokenizers/registry.py` and re-running → **3 failed** (`test_tokenizer_code_revision_rejects_missing_code[unknown-revision]` and `[revision-without-code]` both `DID NOT RAISE OSError`; `test_tokenizer_code_revision_distinct_from_revision` assertion on kept Hub ID), 2 passed (matching/default controls). Guard restored, 10 passed again.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py`: passed (Ruff, mypy, SPDX, test tethering included).
- `git diff --check`: passed.

### How to test

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -k code_revision -q -p no:cacheprovider
pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py
```

Manual reproduction: call `get_tokenizer` with `tokenizer_mode="hf"`, `trust_remote_code=True`, the pinned data revision above, and either `code_revision="never"` or the older code commit. Before this fix both calls load code from the data snapshot (no error); after the fix both fail with the Transformers missing-revision/missing-code error. With omitted or matching `code_revision`, encoding `"hello world"` remains equal to direct `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained`.

## Details

`resolve_tokenizer_args` previously resolved every HF tokenizer to a directory pinned to the data `revision`. Dynamic code cannot be re-selected against a local directory, so forwarding `code_revision` in kwargs cannot restore the requested code selection. The fix preserves the Hub ID when the two revisions differ, mirroring the processor path from #60825. This deliberately gives up the snapshot request reduction for independently versioned code, as the processor path already does.

The tests extend the existing tokenizer suite and use its supported `skip_global_cleanup` marker (tokenizers only, no GPU models). They remain wired into the existing tokenizer CI area.

Scope is direct `get_tokenizer(..., code_revision=...)` loading. No `vllm serve --code-revision` regression, inference accuracy improvement, or performance gain is claimed. Full tokenizer-suite, serving E2E, GPU and model evaluations were not run; the targeted validation above must not be read as those results.

Duplicate-work searches covered #60825 references, open PRs matching `code_revision` + tokenizer keywords, and `get_non_weight_snapshot_path`. author: lucamotz

## Overview

The Qwen3.5 exclusion is still needed: with the list emptied, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8 drops from 79.4% to 71.0% on the 5-shot eval (95% CI −10.5 to −6.2 pt), below its CI threshold of 0.76.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Disable shared-expert aux stream with fully-sharded LoRA
author: jyizheng
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60845.

With `--fully-sharded-loras`, the shared experts' LoRA layers all-gather / all-reduce across TP, and the routed experts' fused MoE LoRA kernel does its own collectives on the main stream. Running the shared experts on the aux stream puts two collectives in flight on the same communicator. Under CUDA graph capture they become independent graph branches, and the replay order is not guaranteed to match across ranks, so NCCL deadlocks (first LoRA decode step hangs, then `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`).

This PR runs the shared experts on the main stream when fully-sharded LoRA is enabled, same as the existing EPLB / flashinfer exclusions in `SharedExperts._disable_shared_experts_overlap`.

## Test Plan

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP=2, `--enable-lora --fully-sharded-loras --max-lora-rank 32`, default CUDA graphs, two rank-32 adapters alternating.

- v0.28.0 (reproduces the hang on the first LoRA request): with this patch, first request returns in 1s, 1000/1000 requests OK.
- v0.31.0 / main: 1000/1000 requests OK.

## Test Result

No hang, 0 failed in both runs.

title: [Bugfix] Merge supported KV cache layouts across pipeline stages instead of asserting they match
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview With pipeline parallelism, a model whose stages use different attention backends fails at startup. `resolve_kv_cache_layout` asserts that every worker reports the same list of supported KV cache layouts, but PP stages hold different layers, so their lists can differ. This PR makes the engine core merge the worker lists with the same rule `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` already uses for the backends of one worker. This addresses failure 1 ("PP2 on SM100") of #60791. Failures 2-5 in that issue are not touched here. ## Claims - `vllm serve` of a 10-layer MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 with `--pipeline-parallel-size 2` on B200 now starts, picks `LBHNC`, and answers requests. Before, it died in `_initialize_kv_caches` with `AssertionError: Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts`. - When all workers report the same list (one GPU, TP only, PP with equal stages), the result is the same as before. - If no layout is supported by every worker, the existing `ValueError` is still raised. - New unit test `test_pipeline_stages_resolve_a_layout_every_stage_supports`. It fails on the old code with the bug's assertion. ## Validation Hardware: 2 x NVIDIA B200 (SM100, x86_64). The issue was reported on GB200 (aarch64), which has the same SM. Software: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev173+g8cbd5d030` (commit `8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986`), with and without this patch. Attention backend chosen: FLASHINFER. Model: the issue's 10-layer cut of `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` is not published, so I rebuilt it from the Hub checkpoint (revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`) with the script below. Layers 0-2 are dense and layers 3-9 are sparse. I cannot show it is tensor-identical to the reporter's cut.
cut script (replace $HF_HOME with your Hugging Face cache path) ```python # Cut MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 to its first 10 decoder layers (+ vision tower), as the report describes. import json, re, glob, os, shutil, sys from safetensors import safe_open from safetensors.torch import save_file src = glob.glob("$HF_HOME/hub/models--MiniMaxAI--MiniMax-M3-MXFP8/snapshots/*")[0] dst = "/tmp/m3-10layer" os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True) N = 10 for f in os.listdir(src): if f.endswith(".safetensors") or f == "model.safetensors.index.json": continue shutil.copy(os.path.realpath(os.path.join(src, f)), os.path.join(dst, f)) def trunc(o): if isinstance(o, dict): return {k: trunc(v) for k, v in o.items()} if isinstance(o, list) and len(o) == 60 and all(isinstance(x, int) for x in o): return o[:N] return o cfg = json.load(open(os.path.join(dst, "config.json"))) cfg["text_config"] = trunc(cfg["text_config"]); cfg["text_config"]["num_hidden_layers"] = N q = cfg["quantization_config"] q["ignored_layers"] = [x for x in q["ignored_layers"] if not (m := re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.", x)) or int(m.group(1)) < N] json.dump(cfg, open(os.path.join(dst, "config.json"), "w"), indent=2) wm = {} for shard in sorted(glob.glob(src + "/*.safetensors")): out = {} with safe_open(shard, "pt") as f: for k in f.keys(): m = re.search(r"language_model\.model\.layers\.(\d+)\.", k) if m and int(m.group(1)) >= N: continue out[k] = f.get_tensor(k) name = os.path.basename(shard) save_file(out, os.path.join(dst, name), metadata={"format": "pt"}) for k in out: wm[k] = name print(name, len(out), flush=True) json.dump({"metadata": {}, "weight_map": wm}, open(os.path.join(dst, "model.safetensors.index.json"), "w")) ```
Reproducer. It fails at startup, so no request is needed to see the bug: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \ vllm serve /tmp/m3-10layer --trust-remote-code --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \ --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --enable-prefix-caching --pipeline-parallel-size 2 ``` Before: 4 of 4 runs failed like this, about 160 s after start. 3 runs used the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986` image and 1 used a source install. One more source run never got this far, because of a file permission problem in my setup, so it is not counted. ``` AssertionError: Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts: [['LBHNC', 'BLHNC'], ['LBNHC', 'LBHNC', 'BLNHC', 'BLHNC', 'BHLNC', 'LHBNC']]. ``` After: 5 of 5 runs started and answered one request with HTTP 200. 3 of the runs used the final code (the last one was run by a separate reviewer) and 2 used an earlier version of the patch. ``` Using LBHNC KV cache layout. INFO: Application startup complete. "POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` The request was `curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -d '{"model":"/tmp/m3-10layer","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":8,"temperature":0}'`. The returned text is junk, which is expected from a 10-layer cut of a much deeper model. I did not run an accuracy eval. Startup takes more than 10 minutes, mostly for FlashInfer autotuning of the MXFP8 MoE kernels. Unit tests (run with `--noconftest`, because my environment had no `tblib`, which `tests/conftest.py` imports): - `pytest --noconftest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k pipeline_stages`: passes with this patch. With the old `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` it fails with the same `Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts` assertion. - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py`: 197 passed, 76 skipped. The 8 errors are tests that need the `caplog_vllm` fixture from `tests/conftest.py`. The 2 failures are PP tests that need 4 GPUs (`World size (4) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`). They fail the same way on the old code with 1 GPU, and they pass with 4 GPUs visible. - `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks pass. ## Details Root cause: each worker reports the layouts that all of its own attention backends support (`WorkerBase.get_supported_kv_cache_layouts`). `resolve_kv_cache_layout` then asserted that all reports are equal, because "all ranks run the same backends". With PP, each stage builds only its own layers. For this model with PP2: - PP0 holds layers 0-4. Layers 0-2 use FlashInfer, which supports only `(LBHNC, BLHNC)` on SM100, so PP0 reports `['LBHNC', 'BLHNC']`. - PP1 holds layers 5-9, which are all sparse. `MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE` and `MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE_INDEXER` declare no layout set, so PP1 reports the default list of six layouts. The two lists differ, but they share `LBHNC` and `BLHNC`. With PP=1 the model works, because one worker sees all backends and intersects their sets. A debug run that printed each stage's backends confirmed this. Fix: the merge code in `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` moves into a helper, `_merge_supported_layouts`, and `resolve_kv_cache_layout` now uses the helper on the worker reports. - Identical lists keep their order, so setups where all workers agree are unchanged. - Otherwise, the candidates are the layouts that appear in every list, and the layout that the most lists put first wins. - A worker that reports the default list (no backend declares a set) does not vote, in the same way that a backend that declares nothing does not vote inside one worker. Without this rule, an all-sparse stage would vote for `LBNHC`, and PP could pick a different layout from PP=1. The second case of the new test covers this. - If no layout is in every list, the code still raises `ValueError: No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set`. Tradeoff: the removed assertion also caught TP ranks of one stage that report different lists, for example after one rank picked a different backend by mistake. Those lists are now merged like PP stages. The chosen layout is still one that every worker supports. A per-stage check could be added back, but the engine core would then need to know which worker is in which stage, and this fix does not need that. Limitations: only failure 1 of the issue is fixed. Validation used B200 with FLASHINFER and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, not GB200. ---

title: [Bugfix] Accept whole-number floats for integer tool arguments in the response parser
author: yonigozlan
body:
When tool schemas are passed to the response parser, an `integer` argument written as a whole-number float like `"3.0"` is now cast to `3` instead of being left as the raw string.

- JSON Schema (draft 6 onward, including 2020-12) defines `integer` as any number with a zero fractional part, so `3.0` is a valid `integer` value. `jsonschema` (Draft 7 and 2020-12 validators) and Pydantic v2 both accept it, and Pydantic returns `3`.
- Models do sometimes write integer arguments this way, and the tool then receives a string where its schema declares an integer.
- Values with a fractional part (`"3.5"`), `inf` and `NaN` still fail the `integer` cast, so they fall through to the next declared type or stay raw, as before.
- Adds a unit test next to the existing argument coercion tests.
- Same change as in Transformers: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49547.

title: [CPU] Fix underflow in FP8 AMX attention
author: tianmu-li
body:
## Overview

Fix underflow in CPU FP8 AMX attention with BF16 exponent lifting and delayed scale compensation, plus cache writes that avoid tiny FP32 intermediates. Follow-up to #39445.

## Claims

- AMX decoding retains FTZ with **four instead of six** vector conversion instructions per 32 values.
- E4M3/E5M2 attention latency: **5.4% lower** than the original decoder across six workloads per format.

## Validation

### Model evaluation

GSM8K results are from earlier decoder comparisons; FTZ rows precede delayed scaling (`da46b8b`).

RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8, BF16 compute, all 1,319 GSM8K questions, 5-shot, chat template, seed 42, greedy decoding, maximum 512 generated tokens, batch size 32, prefix caching disabled.

| KV format / decoder | Flexible extract | Strict match |
|---|---:|---:|
| E4M3, original underflow-prone | 77.786% | 73.995% |
| E4M3, exact-subnormal alternative | 83.245% | 81.804% |
| E4M3, FTZ before delayed scaling | 83.017% | 79.757% |
| E5M2, proper-subnormal integer alternative | 80.667% | 78.772% |
| E5M2, FTZ before delayed scaling | 81.804% | 78.999% |

All runs passed sample-count validation; prompt, target, and document hashes match within each comparison.

```bash
MODEL=RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8
KV_DTYPE=fp8_e4m3  # Repeat with fp8_e5m2.
MODEL_ARGS="pretrained=$MODEL,dtype=bfloat16,kv_cache_dtype=$KV_DTYPE,seed=42"
MODEL_ARGS+=",max_model_len=4096,max_num_seqs=32,max_num_batched_tokens=8192"
MODEL_ARGS+=",enable_prefix_caching=false,enforce_eager=true,kv_cache_memory_bytes=17179869184"

VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 lm_eval run \
  --model vllm --model_args "$MODEL_ARGS" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 \
  --apply_chat_template --seed 42 \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=512 \
  --log_samples --output_path "gsm8k_$KV_DTYPE"
```

### Kernel validation and performance

- Full CPU build and pre-commit passed.
- Eight targeted attention regressions passed, covering encoded subnormals, split reduction, and large cache scales.
- 28 attention behavior checks passed, including split/unsplit, sliding window, softcap, ALiBi, sinks, and VEC.
- All 256 byte encodings of each format were checked against the selected conversion contract with FTZ/DAZ enabled and disabled.

Production assembly confirms four vector conversion instructions per 32 values for E4M3/E5M2 at head sizes 128 and 256.

Three balanced rounds; five repetitions of 20 timed calls per workload. Workload medians pool 15 repetitions; ratios are geometric means across six workloads per format.

| Attention comparison | E4M3 | E5M2 | Combined |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| This PR / original underflow-prone decoder | 0.9525 | 0.9402 | 0.9463 |
| This PR / delayed scaling without FTZ | 1.0248 | 1.0019 | 1.0133 |

Combined ratios by round were 0.9570/0.9435/0.9415 versus original and 1.0222/1.0039/1.0043 versus delayed scaling without FTZ. BF16 controls were within 0.2% overall; the small latter gap is subject to timing variation. These are kernel timings, not end-to-end serving speedups.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv pip install -e . -v --no-build-isolation

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py \
  -k 'fp8_qk_covers_full_64_token_group or fp8_large_prefill_amx' -q

# Representative large-prefill benchmark.
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_attn.py \
  --isa amx --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2 \
  --batch-size 1 --q-len-min 512 --q-len-max 512 \
  --kv-len-min 4096 --kv-len-max 4096 \
  --head-size 128 --num-query-heads 32 --num-kv-heads 8 \
  --block-size 128 --num-blocks 32 --iters 20
```

The existing pytest selection above passed one case and skipped one. The additional reproducers and conversion checks were run locally; no new tests or benchmark files are added to CI.

## Details

The old decoder scaled BF16 values by `2^-120`/`2^-112`; AMX flushed small operands/products before the later scale correction could recover them.

Both AMX decoders lift normal values by `2^8`/`2^16`, compensated in K/V scales, and flush encoded FP8 subnormals to zero. NaN/Inf correction is omitted because the cache writer saturates inputs to finite FP8 codes.

Open-PR searches for CPU FP8 attention and AMX underflow found no overlapping fix.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, source and assembly review, and drafting.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Run the AITER AR+RMSNorm fallback test on the platform…
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
`tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py::test_rocm_aiter_gemma_rmsnorm_falls_back_after_allreduce` fails in `:amd: (MI355) Distributed Features`. The test was added yesterday by #58547, together with the fallback it covers.

[The failing job.](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94315/list?jid=01a131ef-a206-418e-b06e-7a6311a6c957&tab=output)

> NotImplementedError: Could not run 'vllm_aiter::fused_add_rms_norm' with arguments from the 'CPU' backend. This could be because the operator doesn't exist for this backend, or was omitted during the selective/custom build process. 'vllm_aiter::fused_add_rms_norm' is only available for these backends: [CUDA, Meta, BackendSelect, ...].

The test builds its tensors on the CPU, while the fallback it exercises leaves Python through `torch.ops.vllm_aiter.fused_add_rms_norm`. That op is registered for the platform's dispatch key alone, which is `CUDA` on a ROCm build, so a CPU tensor has nothing to dispatch to and the test fails before reaching any of its assertions. The two neighbouring tests in `test_quick_all_reduce.py` do pass with CPU tensors, because their path calls into AITER directly with no registered op in between.

Building the tensors on `current_platform.device_type` is enough, which is what 125 other test files already do. The AITER kernel behind the op stays faked, so the test needs neither real hardware nor an AITER install, and it still passes on a CPU only box, where that device and the dispatch key are both CPU. No `skipif` is needed and nothing outside the test changes.

Worth noting that this is not AMD specific. `vllm/kernels/__init__.py` imports the AITER ops unconditionally and the registration does not need AITER installed, so the op exists on NVIDIA builds too and the test would fail there in exactly the same way. It is only ever run in the AMD step, so nobody sees it.

## Test Result

The test passes on MI355, and the two neighbouring tests in `test_quick_all_reduce.py` still pass.

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Fix INC ARK weight loading for small TP shards
author: Yejing-Lai
body:
Issue: Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 INT4 AWQ fail on TP4 with tensor size mismatch 0 vs 2

Root cause: auto_round_kernel's QuantLinear preallocates buffers with floor-rounded shapes (e.g. qzeros width `out // 32 * bits`), which become 0 for narrow TP shards such as Qwen3.5 GDN in_proj_ba at TP=4, causing copy_() to fail with a shape mismatch.

Fixed: Assign the loaded qweight/qzeros/scales directly instead, since post_init() only relies on the actual tensor shapes.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma 4 encoder CUDA graph capture OOM at startup
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61045.

With `cudagraph_mm_encoder` on, Gemma 4 made every encoder CUDA graph capture buffer far bigger than any batch its token budget can hold. Because of this, `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4` ran out of memory at engine start on a 32 GB GPU. This PR captures one graph per budget and per row width (70, 140 or 280 soft tokens). Each graph gets only as many rows as the budget can fill, so no capture buffer is larger than `budget * 9` patches.

Compared with #61092, this fix:

- Fixes the reported startup OOM. [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) limits the number of rows but keeps every row 2520 patches wide. On the reported setup, [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) still dies in encoder CUDA graph capture (`Tried to allocate 662.00 MiB ... 8.43 GiB allocated in private pools`), both with the issue's flags and with images only.
- Makes video graph output match eager output (mean cosine 0.9994). On [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) the graph rows stay 2520 patches wide but the replay gathers at 630, so video output stays wrong.
- Adds 4 CPU test cases. They fail on the old code and also on [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092). [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) adds no test.

## Claims

- With the issue's flags, `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4` now starts on 1x RTX 5090 32 GB: 21 encoder graphs, 2.61 GiB CUDA graph pool. Before: OOM at startup (`Tried to allocate 6.69 GiB`).
- The images-only variant (`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}'`) also ran out of memory at startup before. It now starts and serves images.
- Encoder graph output now matches eager output for video and for batches of 70-token and 140-token images. On the old code these outputs were wrong.
- The change is only in `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py` (+49/-10). It uses the existing `capture_axes` support of the encoder CUDA graph manager. The manager and other models do not change.

## Validation

Setup: 1x NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB). vLLM commit `fe4df3df0eb703862c686b256e9fe44fa94c8945` (0.31.1rc1.dev296), with and without this patch.

Reproducer (the issue's command). No request is needed, because the failure happens at engine start:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --async-scheduling \
  --attention-config '{"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}' --moe-backend marlin \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 1}' \
  --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"num_frames": 32}}' \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'
```

Before: 4 runs out of 4 failed the same way. 3 ran in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-fe4df3df0eb703862c686b256e9fe44fa94c8945` image and 1 in an editable install of that commit.

```
EncoderCudaGraphManager initialized with paths={'default': [70, 140, 280, 560, 1120, 2240, 4096]}, max_batch_size=58, max_frames_per_batch=1856, use_dp=False, capture_axes=()
...
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py", line 1992, in encoder_cudagraph_forward
...
    pixel_values = 2 * (pixel_values - 0.5)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 6.69 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.45 GiB of which 4.94 GiB is free.
```

After: 3 runs out of 3 on the final code started:

```
EncoderCudaGraphManager initialized with paths={'default': [70, 140, 280, 560, 1120, 2240, 4096]}, max_batch_size=58, max_frames_per_batch=1856, use_dp=False, capture_axes=((70, 140, 280),)
Encoder CUDA graph capture complete. Captured 21 graphs across 1 paths.
CUDA graph pool memory: 2.61 GiB (actual), 2.99 GiB (estimated), difference: 0.39 GiB (14.8%).
Application startup complete.
```

The started servers answered every request. One run sent 14 concurrent 448x448 images, each showing a circle in one color, at temperature 0. Another run sent 1 image, 12 concurrent images and 4 videos of 32 frames. Each image answer named the circle's color.

Images only (same command with `{"image": 1, "video": 0}`, 1 run each):

- Old code: OOM in encoder graph capture, `Tried to allocate 644.00 MiB ... with 8.43 GiB allocated in private pools`.
- This PR: 21 graphs, 2.61 GiB graph pool, startup complete. 6 concurrent images were each answered with the right color.

Graph output against eager output. A script outside this PR called `cudagraph_manager.execute(...)` and `model.embed_multimodal(...)` on the same inputs. The table gives the mean cosine over the leading tokens that the prompt uses:

| Input | Old code | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 image, 280 tokens | 0.9994 | 0.9995 |
| Batch of 70-token or 140-token images | items after the first: near 0 | 0.9995 or better | | 1 video 480x336, 32 frames | 0.185 | 0.9994 |
| 2 videos 480x336, 16 frames each | 0.191 | 0.9994 |

The old code could not start with the issue's flags. For this comparison it ran with a smaller config: `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets=[2240]`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch=1`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch=32`. The batch-of-images row came from separate runs with images only and 4 items per batch. These comparisons ran on an earlier revision of this patch. The later changes were a rename, test edits, and removing one capture row that no batch fills.

Unit tests (CPU, `device="meta"`):

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py
34 passed

# with the old gemma4_mm.py, -k "encoder_cudagraph or encoder_chunk"
E       assert 2520 == (70 * 9)
E       assert 1856 == 14
E       assert 630 == (280 * 9)
E       assert [280, 70] == [280, 280]
4 failed, 5 passed, 25 deselected
```

`pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: every hook passed or was skipped, including mypy and `check-test-tethering`.

## Details

Root cause: the Gemma 4 encoder graph takes pixels as `(rows, patches_per_row, 768)`, with one image or video frame per row. `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs` made this buffer too large in both dimensions:

1. Rows: it used `max(max_batch_size, max_frames_per_batch)` for every budget. With video on, that is `58 * 32 = 1856`. But every row is at least 70 soft tokens, so a batch that fits 4096 tokens has at most 58 rows.
2. Width: every row had the width of the widest image, `min(budget, 280) * 9 = 2520` patches. A video frame, or a 70-token image, needs only 630.

So the 4096-token graph got a `(1856, 2520, 768)` bf16 buffer of 7,184,056,320 bytes: the 6.69 GiB in the issue. The first operation of the patch embedder needs another tensor of the same size. Limiting only the rows is not enough. The 4096 graph then still runs the vision tower on about 4 times the patches its budget can hold and takes 8.57 GiB of graph pool, and the next budget's warm-up runs out of memory. The width problem alone also breaks image-only configs, where every budget of 280 or more gets 58 rows of 2520 patches.

The fix, all in `gemma4_mm.py`:

- `get_encoder_cudagraph_config` declares one capture axis: the row width in soft tokens, `(70, 140, 280)`, up to the configured maximum.
- `select_encoder_cudagraph_items` returns the batch's row width as the axis key: 70 for video frames, and the padded width for images.
- `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs` builds rows of exactly that width, and `min(max(max_batch_size, max_frames_per_batch), max(1, budget // width))` rows. The one-row minimum is there only so that capture works when one row is wider than the budget.
- The replay pads list images of mixed widths to the widest one. So `get_encoder_cudagraph_item_specs` sets `path_output_tokens` to that widest width, and the manager never packs more rows into a batch than its graph has. `output_tokens` stays the real count and is still used to slice the output. Note: the docstring of `EncoderItemSpec.path_output_tokens` says single-path models leave it empty. Gemma 4 now sets it on its one path, for this reason.

The graph row width now equals the replay gather width. That is why video and narrow-image graph output, which were wrong before, now match eager.

Trade-offs:

- With the issue's flags, encoder graphs go from 7 to 21, one per budget and width. 3 of them can never be replayed: budget 70 with widths 140 and 280, and budget 140 with width 280. Each is one row. Skipping them would need a change to the manager's capture loop.
- In a config that already worked (images only, budgets `[280, 1120, 2240]`, 4 items per batch), the graph pool grew from 0.93 to 1.12 GiB and the KV cache shrank from 7.71 to 7.46 GiB. This was measured before the final row-count change.
- A list of images of mixed widths is packed at its widest width. It can need a bigger budget, or run eagerly when no budget fits it. The output stays correct.

Not changed here. These are older defects that are the same before and after this PR, and each needs a different change:

- Video frames with padding (for example 320x240, 63 real tokens per frame): the graph path counts the padding slots, so its output is longer than eager output (2240 against 2016 tokens) and later frames are shifted.
- Images with `max_soft_tokens` 560 or 1120 crash when `cudagraph_mm_encoder` is on, because the vision config has no `num_soft_tokens` attribute.
- `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` fails at encoder graph capture.

---

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Restore TP-sharded routed-expert capture for DP=1
author: Ronald1995
body:
## Overview

Restore complete routed-expert rows when model-level sequence parallelism shards tokens across TP ranks and DP=1 has no DP metadata. Related platform-specific work: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18502.

## Claims

- Identify TP shards using the existing `BatchDescriptor.num_tokens` (or `DPMetadata` for multi-DP), gather in rank order, and trim SP padding.
- Reuse the descriptor in eager, graph, microbatch and decoder-replay contexts; no extra `ForwardContext.num_tokens` field or count-only caller arguments.
- Preserve multi-DP layout priority and reject malformed shard grouping explicitly, including under optimized Python.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py
pre-commit run --files tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py vllm/forward_context.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts_capturer.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/ubatch_utils.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py
git diff --check
```

- **62 pytest cases passed** on GB200, using isolated test-root collection (`--confcutdir`) against a nightly-image overlay. Includes real `sp_padding_mask` mutation and compact V4.1 replay contexts. A mask-length implementation fails both new TP-rank regressions.
- Real NCCL/CUDA-graph layout checks passed for **TP2/DP1, TP4/DP1 and TP2/DP2**: 36 cases per rank, including odd/empty counts, unequal DP counts and buffer reuse.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks (including mypy and test tethering) and diff checks passed.
- Final helper cleanup: **51 capture tests passed** locally, with **30 targeted cases** rerun during review. **89,469 CPU layout cases** compared the previous and simplified production helper in both normal and optimized Python: identical rows, strides, exception types and collective calls. Collective outputs were simulated in this differential check; the GPU/model results below precede this cleanup.
- Historical CPU checks: 25 isolated capture cases (also 25 under `optimize=1`) and 96,203 multi-DP differential cases passed. Earlier model reproducer and commands: [discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61388#issuecomment-6148311175).

### Real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash A/B

Control: `fe18b045fd`; candidate: this descriptor simplification. GB200, TP2/DP1/EP, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, default padding skipping, async scheduling, prefix caching, chunked prefill, SHM/value delivery. Both eager and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` were exercised.

- Five model runs, including a control reload: **41,315 returned rows / 9,915,600 expert IDs**, with no missing or mismatched IDs. Compare raw per-rank routes to capture snapshots and HTTP outputs; prefix hits use the existing first-published immutable Store values. Multi-chunk prefill, decode, a measured cache hit and actual graph replays were verified.
- Fixed-token scoring: three sequences (33/257/1025 tokens), three uncached repeats each. Short-sequence logprobs were exactly equal. The long sequence varies even across control runs: same-GPU control/candidate mean absolute logprob difference **0.05360**, versus **0.05179** between control initializations. Mean NLL shift was **0.00174**, versus control-reload shift **0.00459**. No clear additional degradation in these bounded checks; **not** a claim of bitwise equivalence or broad benchmark accuracy. R3-disabled serving smoke checks also passed.
- **DBO is not fixed:** real V2 UBatchRunner/TP collectives/graph checks reproduce the same existing microbatch overwrite in both variants. V4.1 Engram itself rejects DBO, so these are separate checks, not a claimed V4.1+DBO model pass. Offset repair remains outside this PR (#57184).

Environment: official nightly `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:a7deff2c216def98c193352aca50fb03a2ee29231355b3033dc3789009f6d23e`, V4.1 snapshot `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`. Only the affected production Python files were overlaid per variant; **not a full checkout rebuild**. Model runs used `--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, concurrent prompt lengths 33/1024/2051/4096 and 8 output tokens, then repeated the 1024-token prefix. `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip` bypassed an existing image warmup API mismatch; normal JIT and graph capture still ran. Correctness instrumentation makes these runs unsuitable for throughput claims.

## Details

The previous DP=1 path wrote only the received TP shard, leaving later routing rows stale. Restore the local token axis before buffer assignment. Layer bounds are checked before collectives and gather inputs are contiguous.

The pre-SP count must survive model-level sharding: `is_padding` can itself become a TP shard and is not a reliable count source. The existing batch descriptor retains the original size, including in compact decoder-replay contexts. Creating that descriptor for eager execution removes duplicate state and three count-only caller edits (production diff for this refinement: net -11 lines).

This updates the existing TP fix rather than opening a duplicate. Microbatch write offsets (#57184) and decoder-replay row retention (#61643) remain separate concerns, unchanged here. The restoration helper shares one layout error, reads the declared `DPMetadata.local_sizes` field directly, and retains the existing layout priority. Tests use actual `DPMetadata` objects.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review and validation.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Treat an already-published fs block as stored
author: shreyanshj10
body:
## Overview

The `fs` secondary tier fails a whole store job with `EEXIST` when another writer has already
published the same block. Related to #61373 (the second, write-side bug in that report).

## Claims

- A store job that loses the publish race on a content-addressed block is reported successful
  instead of being counted as a `cascade_job_failure`.
- The same guard is applied in both implementations of the primitive, the Python `_store_block`
  and the `fs_io_C` one, so behaviour does not depend on whether the extension is built.
- Nothing else changes: the bytes on disk, and every other errno, behave as before.

## Validation

- New unit test `test_store_accepts_block_published_by_another_writer` in
  `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py`: it stores a block, then hides it from the
  existence check and fails the publish with `EEXIST`, which is what losing the race looks like.
  It asserts the job result is a success, that no temp file is left behind, and that the
  published bytes are untouched. Without the guard `_store_block` raises and the job is reported
  failed. The injected `EEXIST` is unavoidable here, since `rename(2)` on a local POSIX
  filesystem replaces the destination and never reports it; the test follows the patching style
  already used in that file.
- pre-commit hooks on the changed files: `ruff check`, `ruff format` and `clang-format` are
  clean.
- Not a model-affecting change: this path only decides whether an already-present KV block file
  counts as a store failure, so there are no eval numbers to report.
- Not duplicating an existing PR: I searched the open PRs for `61373 in:body`, for `fs_io`, and
  for fs-tier store keywords, and found nothing covering this.

## Details

Root cause: `_store_block` writes the block to a temp file and publishes it with `rename(2)`. It
skips the write entirely when the destination already exists, but that check and the rename are
not atomic, and with several engine instances sharing one `root_dir` the window between them is
routinely lost. POSIX `rename` would replace the destination silently, but several shared
filesystems (the report is on 3FS over FUSE) return `EEXIST` instead, and that error propagated
out of `batch_store_block` and failed the batch at the first such block.

Block file names are the content hash, so a destination that exists already holds these bytes:
there is nothing left to do and the store has succeeded. Both implementations now drop the temp
file and return success for `EEXIST` from the publish step only. Every other errno still fails
the job, and the `O_EXCL` temp-file open is deliberately left outside the guard so a genuine
temp-path collision remains an error rather than a silently skipped block.

I did not touch the promotion symptom that #61373 leads with, since I could not establish it from
the code. One thing worth noting for whoever picks that up: the two metrics quoted in the report,
`chunk_queries` and `lookup_async_delay_seconds`, are both recorded when an async lookup resolves
to a miss as well as to a hit (`_observe_resolved_lookup` in
`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/metrics.py`), so they do not on their own show that the block was
found. `chunk_hits` is the one that separates the two cases.

---

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Sync cluster before DSMEM stores in ll_bf16 split-K router GEMM
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

The `ll_bf16` split-K router GEMM (#42562, M >= 8) stores partials into peer CTAs' shared memory (`st.shared::cluster`) before any cluster barrier. If a peer CTA hasn't started yet, the GPU raises Xid 13 `CTA Not Present`, which surfaces as `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`.

Fix: all threads `cluster_arrive_relaxed()` after pipeline init. DMA warps `cluster_wait()` after committing stage 0, and MMA warps wait at the start of their branch. So every peer is resident before the epilogue's `st.shared::cluster`, and the wait stays out of the PDL prologue (split suggested by @LopezCastroRoberto).

## Reproduction

This uses @Skyseaee's single-GPU harness ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61463#issuecomment-6210051133)). It runs the router GEMM in a CUDA graph, concurrent with non-cluster copy kernels that write to mapped pinned host memory:
```bash
nvcc -O3 -shared -Xcompiler -fPIC -arch=sm_103a copy.cu -o libhostcopy.so
python -u router_probe.py --tag <tag> --mode direct --seconds 120
```

| B300, fresh process per run | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`a12e122206`) | `unspecified launch failure` in the first batch, 4/4 runs |
| this PR (`ac5c06ee4b`) | 120 s clean, 4,912,896 router calls, outputs correct |

The harness does not trigger the fault on H200. In serving, the same Xid hit GLM-5.3 HiSparse P/D decode (2x 8xH200, TP4) within minutes. The first revision of this fix (arrive+wait at kernel start) ran 6/6 passes clean there; the current revision has not been run in serving.

No regression test: the race depends on hardware CTA scheduling, so it can't be made deterministic. `test_ll_bf16_gemm.py` covers numerics only.

## Test results

All on `ac5c06ee4b`.

`pytest tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py`: 144 passed on B300 and on H200.

Latency is µs per call: the median of 30 replays of a CUDA graph holding 200 back-to-back PDL `ll_bf16_gemm` calls, N=256.

| GPU, K | M=8 / 12 / 16, `main` | M=8 / 12 / 16, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| B300, 6144 | 2.45 / 2.74 / 2.71 | 2.47 / 2.81 / 2.77 |
| B300, 7168 | 2.78 / 2.79 / 2.76 | 2.80 / 2.80 / 2.76 |
| B300, 4096 | 2.59 / 2.46 / 2.47 | 2.61 / 2.47 / 2.47 |
| H200, 6144 | 2.62 / 2.68 / 2.72 | 2.66 / 2.72 / 2.75 |
| H200, 7168 | 2.79 / 2.78 / 2.85 | 2.84 / 2.82 / 2.88 |
| H200, 4096 | 2.40 / 2.61 / 3.00 | 2.44 / 2.66 / 2.94 |
