author: PeganovAnton
body:
## Purpose

Raise the `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` floor in `requirements/cuda.txt` from
`1.19.1` to `1.31.0`, the first release containing
[NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1195](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1195),
"Keep execution plans alive for the CUDA graphs recorded from them".

Before that fix, cuDNN could unload a just-in-time compiled kernel's library
when the last cuDNN owner of it went away, while a CUDA graph still contained
a node that launched that kernel. Replaying the graph then dispatched whatever
had taken over that code address. The upstream fix makes the graph hold a
reference for as long as it can launch the kernel.

The affected `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0-ubuntu2404` stack has both conditions:

- `FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` is first in `_POSSIBLE_FP8_KERNELS` for
  CUDA and calls `bmm_fp8(..., backend="auto")`. Because
  `requirements/cuda.txt` declares `nvidia-cudnn-frontend`, the `cudnn` module
  is importable and `auto` admits the cuDNN runner.
- FlashInfer memoises those cuDNN graphs in
  `functools.lru_cache(maxsize=2048)`, keyed per shape, and the cache evicts
  cold entries. The GEMMs themselves are captured into the decode CUDA graphs.

In that stack, an eviction can release the last owner of a kernel that a live decode graph
still launches. The observable outcomes are an illegal-address fault, a CUDA
error reported at synchronisation, or — the case that matters most for a
serving stack — **silently wrong output with no error reported at all**.

FlashInfer 0.7.2, pinned by the tested base, now has a
[capture-retention helper](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py#L3761-L3774)
that keeps captured cuDNN GEMM graphs alive for the process lifetime. This
separately mitigates the GEMM eviction path on current `main`. The frontend
floor still ensures that cudnn-frontend's own CUDA-graph lifetime fix is
installed.

## What this fixes

| Issue | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| #52225 | root cause identified directly | The investigation that led here, and the attribution is not statistical. A GPU coredump and CUDA-GDB independently confirmed the faulting kernel as `cudnn_generated_fort_native_sm80_matMul_pointwise_pointwise_knob_0_256x128x128_3_0`, launched with block (384,1,1) against a cubin declaring a 256-thread launch bound and 246 registers — the instruction-issue rejection that reports as Xid 13 `Out Of Range Register`. In the retained fault run, the cuDNN LRU eviction destroying a cold captured graph's plans and runtime kernels was observed directly, 436 µs after a newly compiled graph of a different shape, with the evicted kernel's CUDA graph node still live and no host launch since its capture 66 minutes earlier. A source audit confirmed no graph retention existed in the deployed cuDNN. That is the mechanism this fix removes. |
| #55571 | likely fixed | A third-party report, so the attribution is indirect: no coredump of their fault was analysed and no run on their hardware used the fixed wheel. What makes it strong is that *either* `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` *or* `--enforce-eager` reportedly makes it go away, and those remove exactly the two conditions this defect needs — the cuDNN lane, and CUDA graph capture. |

Deliberately **not** claimed:

- **#61007** (GB10 hang inside a cuDNN FP8 GEMM) is the same lane but a
  different failure: an unbounded host-side hang while cuDNN builds a plan
  lazily per shape in the hot path. This change does not address plan
  construction cost. #57209 is the change aimed at that.
- **#61069, #60119, #59768, #49926** share the Xid 13 or illegal-access
  symptom class but implicate other kernel families, and in #60119's case the
  report itself declines to claim a common root cause. No evidence either way.

## Relationship to #57209

[#57209](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57209) pins `bmm_fp8` to
cuBLAS on sm_12x, avoiding the cuDNN lane. This PR fixes the lane instead, by
taking the upstream fix, and is not an alternative proposal to it: #57209 also
cites host-side plan-construction latency in the serving hot path, which a
frontend bump does not change. If #57209 lands, this bump still matters for
every other cuDNN consumer reached through cudnn-frontend — the
`flashinfer_cudnn` NVFP4 linear backend and the cuDNN ViT and multimodal
encoder attention paths — and for sm_100 and sm_121, which #57209 does not
cover.

## Why the frontend and not the backend

Both upstream fixes work and each is sufficient alone: cuDNN 9.27.0.42 fixes it
for every caller including torch's own, while the frontend fix covers
cudnn-frontend consumers only.

In fairness to upstream, they consider the backend the thorough fix and the
frontend a workaround, and the frontend fix retains the whole `ExecutionPlan`
where the backend retains only the kernel code — so it holds more memory per
plan captured into a live graph. That cost is not quantified here.

The frontend is still the right change *for vLLM*: vLLM already declares a
floor for it and this is one line, whereas pinning `nvidia-cudnn-cu13` would
override the cuDNN version torch resolves transitively. Upstream chose to
write the frontend fix for exactly this reason — so that frameworks could pick
it up without waiting on a backend upgrade — and it is the vehicle they
offered for this report.

The consequence is stated plainly: cuDNN callers that do not go through
cudnn-frontend are unaffected by this PR. In vLLM that means torch
convolutions (`vllm/model_executor/layers/conv.py`) and torch's
`SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION` (`phi4mm_utils.py`). Those are fixed when torch's
transitive cuDNN pin reaches 9.27.0.42, which is the right lever for them; they
are not known to be affected today. If maintainers would rather take the
thorough fix, the backend pin is the alternative and I am happy to switch —
but it should be one or the other, since applying both creates two user
objects for the same kernel.

Upstream has already commented on #52225 pointing at the frontend fix:
<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52225#issuecomment-5900569717>.

## Test plan and results

Hardware: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), driver 580.126.20.

**Frontend fix, either side of the upstream merge commit**, with the backend
wheel as a second axis — 96 cells each side across backends 9.19.0.56 through
9.26.0.51, varying graph construction, workload profile, kernel-cache size and
owner-lifetime arm:

| frontend | reproducing cells |
|---|---|
| `07c939a6cce4` (pre-fix) | 22 of 96 |
| `4d4e428bd747` (PR #1195) | **0 of 96** |

Every reproducing cell is in the arm that releases the owner. The paired
`retain` and `user-object` arms are clean on both sides, which is what makes
this a comparison rather than an absence of failure.

**Backend fix on the public wheel**, with the pre-fix frontend held fixed so
the wheel is the only variable, run control-first within each configuration:

| configuration | 9.20.0.48 | 9.27.0.42 |
|---|---|---|
| populate, cache default/off, release | `SIGSEGV` | clean |
| stream capture, cache default/off, release | CUDA error 718, invalid program counter | clean |
| profile 52225, cache default/off, release | **3,948,544 of 5,275,648 elements wrong, 2,637,824 non-finite, `sync_status=0`** | clean, 0 mismatches |
| all six of the above, retain arm | clean | clean |

The wrong-result rows report no error to the host. The 9.27.0.42 release notes
carry the matching entry: "Runtime-compiled kernel code now stays loaded for
as long as a CUDA graph can launch it."

**The fix is in the binary vLLM actually imports.** vLLM reaches cuDNN through
FlashInfer's `import cudnn`, the compiled module in the wheel, not through
headers:

| wheel | `cuda_graph_retention.h` | retention symbols in `_compiled_module*.so` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.30.0 | absent | 0 |
| 1.31.0 | present | 41 |

**Cost**, measured on the stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0-ubuntu2404` image
with only the frontend wheel swapped, three repetitions per arm, medians:

| measurement | 1.28.0 | 1.31.0 |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph replay | 45.04 µs | 45.04 µs |
| CUDA graph capture | 192.0 µs | 229.1 µs |
| plan build | 7655 µs | 7710 µs |
| max relative error vs cuBLAS | 0.000000 | 0.000000 |

Replay is unchanged, so the steady-state decode path pays nothing. Capture
costs about 37 µs more, once per captured graph at warmup, and the capture
ranges do not overlap across repetitions. The plan-build difference is within
noise at three samples. Numerics are unchanged against the cuBLAS backend.

Eager execution, measured separately because the cost might not be specific to
graphs — per-call host time with GPU work left asynchronous, two repetitions of
seven rounds — shows no regression either: 1.31.0 medians 95.80 and 94.88 µs
against 1.28.0's noisier 112.10 and 95.34 µs, with overlapping ranges.

One nuance for anyone assessing exposure: from backend 9.22 onward the pre-fix
frontend stops reproducing at the default kernel-cache size and still
reproduces with the cache disabled, because the cache was holding a second
reference. Backend version alone therefore does not tell you whether a
deployment is exposed.

Note also that `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0` resolves cudnn-frontend **1.28.0**
against the declared floor of 1.19.1, so the effective bump for that image is
1.28.0 → 1.31.0.

## Not measured

- **No end-to-end serving before-and-after with the released wheel.** The
  mechanism is directly established and the fix is verified on the
  deterministic reproducer, but the remaining step — serving the affected
  model at full exposure on the released wheel and showing the fault rate go
  to zero — is a multi-hour stochastic measurement and is not included. An
  earlier run with both fixes built from source did not reproduce the bug on
  Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4.
- **Read the lane ablation carefully if you cite it.** Disabling the
  FlashInfer FP8 class gave 7 of 12 against 0 of 12 at p≈0.0023 on the
  *family* endpoint (any `0x0d`/`0x0e`/`0x0f` fault in a cuDNN matMul); on the
  exact `0x0d` subtype alone it is 1 of 12 against 0 of 12, p=0.5 and
  uninformative. It corroborates that the lane is necessary; it is not the
  basis for the root-cause attribution, which is the coredump evidence above.
- **A Python-level reproduction was attempted and failed to fault its own
  control**, so it proves nothing in either direction and is not offered as
  evidence. The deterministic reproducer pins the engine and kernel config for
  both the target and the reoccupying donor, and FlashInfer's Python API
  exposes no way to select either.
- **The memory retained by the frontend fix is not quantified.** It keeps the
  whole execution plan alive per plan captured into a live graph, where the
  backend fix keeps only the kernel code.
- **No specific models are claimed as fixed.** There are internal reports that
  the backend upgrade resolved corruption for some FP8 Nemotron checkpoints,
  but they are soak observations without a paired control, so they are not
  offered here as evidence.
- The plan-build cost difference and cuDNN 9.28's expected opt-out are
  unresolved here.

## Duplicate check

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "cudnn-frontend in:body OR cudnn frontend in:title"` — no open PR changes this floor.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52225 in:body"` — one unrelated MoE PR.
- #57209 is the nearest open work; it avoids the lane rather than fixing it, and the difference is described above.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance. Every line of the diff and every
number above was reviewed by the submitter, the measurements were run on
first-party hardware, and the cells that were not measured are labelled as
such rather than inferred.

title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Periodic stats line: dead Preemptions field + Finished count
author: michael-gpu
body:
## Overview

The periodic serving-stats line (`Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: ...`)
could not show preemption churn: the interval counters it reports were
reset before the line was built, so the `Preemptions: N` field
introduced in #28522 never fired, and nothing reported finished-request
counts. This change fixes the ordering and adds an unconditional
`Finished: N reqs` field — `Finished: 0` while generation throughput is
high is the churn signal.

## Changes

- `LoggingStatLogger` now computes throughputs in `_calc_throughput(now)`
  and resets the interval counters *after* the log line is built, so the
  line reads the live counters (`num_preemptions`, `num_corrupted_reqs`,
  `num_finished_reqs`) directly — no snapshot fields.
- `Finished: N reqs` is unconditional: the zero is the diagnostic.
  Prometheus counters are unchanged and already correct; this PR is
  scoped to the human-readable line.
- New `tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py` covers
  `LoggingStatLogger` through `StatLoggerManager.record()`/`log()`:
  counter accumulate/log/reset, latest-snapshot scheduler values, the
  INFO → two quiet intervals → DEBUG noise policy, the
  Preemptions/Corrupted fields, and the DP-aggregated variant.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py -v` → 5 passed.
- The same suite against pre-PR `main` fails exactly the bug-guard
  tests (dead `Preemptions` field, missing `Finished` count) and passes
  the rest — the tests demonstrably guard the fix.
- `pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py tests/v1/metrics/test_metrics_reader.py
  tests/v1/metrics/test_histogram_buckets.py -q` → 45 passed.
- One interval with 100 preemptions and 0 finished requests:
  - before: no `Preemptions`, no `Finished` field
  - after: `Finished: 0 reqs, Preemptions: 100`

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stream Gemma4 string tool arguments incrementally
author: bbrowning
body:
## Overview

Stream Gemma4 `<|"|>` string tool arguments incrementally and in linear time by adopting the `arg_value_extender` hook from #61253, and fix the engine so a live extender runs before the `arg_structural_chars` gate. Follow-up to #61253; same root cause as the DeepSeek symptom in #52846 / #58780.

## Claims

- Gemma4 string argument bodies now stream token by token. Before, a value without one of `,:{}[]<` arrived as a single fragment when its closing delimiter did.
- Long string arguments no longer cost quadratic parser time. A 32 KB code value drops from 7.0 s to 0.15 s of parser CPU on this machine; the converter runs a constant 8 times instead of 5008.
- Accumulated streamed arguments are byte-identical to the previous streaming path and to non-streaming extraction, including streams cut inside a value.
- Engine: a live extender now receives every delta. Before, the `arg_structural_chars` gate dropped non-structural deltas from the open value and the stream truncated at the next conversion. GLM, the only previous extender user, sets no gate and is unaffected. `ParserEngineConfig` rejects an extender without `arg_converter` or with `stream_arg_deltas=False`, which the engine silently ignored.

## Validation

Tests (CPU-only machine, no GPU; see Details for the eval gap):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_gemma4_reasoning_parser.py -q
# 6105 passed
```

New tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_gemma4_streaming_reasoning.py::TestGemma4ArgValueExtender` compare the extender against the converter-only engine (`arg_value_extender=None`) and against non-streaming extraction at chunk sizes 1, 3, 7 and 64, with and without a schema, over values containing commas, braces, parens, whitespace runs, every proper prefix of `<|"|>`, quotes, backslashes, unicode and lexer terminals (`call:`, `:`, `{`); truncated streams cut inside the value; the closing delimiter split at every offset; the factory's refusals (closed value, open key, nested value, duplicate key, bare value, partial opener); and that converter calls do not grow with value length. With the engine gate reorder reverted, 31 of these tests fail, which is the evidence that the engine change is load-bearing.

`tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py::TestArgValueExtender` pins the engine contract: the gate-order test fails on the previous engine, and the config validation test covers both rejected configurations.

Differential fuzz (not checked in): a grammar-based generator over Gemma4's format, random nesting, duplicate and delimited keys, both brace and paren call forms, with and without schema coercion, delivered as random char chunks, token-ID batches with `<|"|>` as its own token, and truncated streams with cut points biased to whitespace, closers and partial delimiters. 33,000 cases over three seeds, zero divergences in content, reasoning, tool names or accumulated arguments. Mutation check: breaking the extender's hold-back, escaping or split-delimiter window each made the fuzz fail in 12-23% of cases.

Benchmark (`parse_delta`, 4-char chunks, mock tokenizer, parser time only):

| Content | Chars | Extender | Parser time | Converter calls | Ticks emitting arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| code | 2k | off / on | 36 ms / 10 ms | 319 / 8 | 284 / 503 |
| code | 8k | off / on | 459 ms / 38 ms | 1258 / 8 | 1129 / 2004 |
| code | 32k | off / on | 7005 ms / 152 ms | 5008 / 8 | 4504 / 8004 |
| prose | 32k | off / on | 28 ms / 87 ms | 8 / 8 | 4 / 8004 |

Pre-commit passes on all changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_compute_arg_delta` returned early for any delta without an `arg_structural_chars` character, before consulting a live extender. Gemma4 sets that gate to `,:{}[]<`, so a body delta like `Paris` never reached the extender or the converter, and the whole value was emitted when the close arrived. Every delta that did pass the gate re-parsed the full argument text, which is quadratic in value length and is why code-like values, full of structural characters, were the worst case.

**Engine change.** The gate now applies only when no extender is live; a live extender sees every delta. The factory is called after each accepted conversion and decides whether the raw text ends in an open value, because the engine cannot tell from converted JSON (converters serialise an open raw value as a closed JSON string). The `arg_value_extender` comment documents this and the lexer invariant extenders rely on: a terminal is never split across deltas, except that a held partial terminal is flushed as text at end of stream or before a token-ID terminal. The `_safe_arg_prefix` docstring is corrected to say the flag describes the returned prefix.

**Gemma4 extender.** `_parse_gemma4_fields` reports the key of an unterminated trailing string so the factory can confirm it is also the last key in the parsed dict (a duplicate key would otherwise stream into the wrong slot). The hard part is that `_gemma4_arg_converter` hides a tail of the open value until more text arrives: `.strip()` removes trailing whitespace, one trailing `}` or excess `)` is dropped as the call-body closer, and `_strip_partial_delim` removes a partial `<|"|>`. The extender keeps exactly that tail unemitted and uses it as the window that detects a split close, so its output stays a prefix of every later conversion, including the final flush of a truncated stream. `_drop_call_closer` is shared with the converter so the two cannot drift. Unlike GLM's tags, `<|"|>` is not a lexer terminal, so the window is required rather than defensive.

**Tradeoffs.** Prose values now cost about three times the parser time because every token is emitted instead of one lump; absolute numbers stay small and linear (87 ms for 32 KB). `Gemma4Parser` accepts `parser_engine_config` as an override, matching `Glm47MoeParser`, so tests can swap the converter or extender.

**Limitations.** A duplicate top-level key whose first value already streamed cannot be extended; both the old and new paths stop at the same point. That is pre-existing behaviour in the area of #53739. No model eval was run: this machine has no GPU. The change alters only when argument fragments are emitted, and the tests pin the accumulated text to the non-streaming result; a reviewer with a Gemma4 checkpoint could confirm by streaming a long file-write tool call with and without the change and diffing the concatenated arguments.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds an extender to any parser (`gh pr list --search arg_value_extender` is empty). #58780 fixes the same symptom for DeepSeek by relaxing the gate in the engine, which keeps the quadratic cost; that engine hunk is superseded by the reorder here, and the DeepSeek extender can follow as its own PR.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, the implementation, the tests and this description. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Capture DCP FULL cudagraphs with KV context
author: ayush1399
body:
## Overview

On MRV2, GQA models with DCP produce garbage under the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraph mode, including the Qwen3-235B `-tp 8 -dcp 2` example in `docs/serving/context_parallel_deployment.md`. This PR captures DCP FULL graphs with KV context, as V1 already does (`get_dcp_dummy_context_len`).

## Claims

- Fixes GQA + DCP + FULL cudagraphs on MRV2. Qwen3-235B at TP=8 DCP=2: needle retrieval 0/9 → 9/9.
- No regression for MLA + DCP (DeepSeek-V2-Lite).

## Validation

8x H100, `main` @ de8291e24f, default settings. Needle: 6-digit code at depths 0.1/0.5/0.9 of ~8k/~31k/~100k-token prompts, greedy. gsm8k: 5-shot, chat template.

| Model | Build | Needle | gsm8k flex / strict | KV tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=2 | `main` | **0/9** | garbage | 1,851,136 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=2 | this PR | **9/9** | 91.66 / 80.74 | 1,846,080 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=1 | this PR | 9/9 | 92.80 / 81.50 | 925,920 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | `main` | **0/6** | | |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | `main`, PIECEWISE | 6/6 | | |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | this PR | 6/6 | | |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MLA), TP=4 DCP=4 | `main` | 6/6 | 53.83 | 8,634,624 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MLA), TP=4 DCP=4 | this PR | 6/6 | 54.89 | 8,634,624 |

gsm8k stderr is ±0.7–1.1 (Qwen3) and ±1.4 (DeepSeek).

Zero-context batches (64 concurrent one-token prompts after a long request, FA3): first-token logprobs at DCP=2 match DCP=1 exactly (64/64).

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 -tp 8 -dcp 2 --max-model-len 131072
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py  # new test fails on main
```

## Details

**Root cause.** For DCP, the FlashAttention metadata builder skips context attention on the host when no request has context (`should_skip_dcp_context_attention`, #40996). MRV2 captures FULL graphs from a dummy batch with `seq_lens == query_lens`, so every FULL graph records the skip path and replays ignore the KV cache. Piecewise and eager rebuild metadata each step and are unaffected.

**Fix.** On FULL capture with `cp_size > 1`, give the dummy batch `cp_size * cp_interleave` tokens of context through the existing `set_dummy_context`. Applied on both FULL capture paths, normal and DBO. Capture-time only.

**Limitations.**
- The FA2 decode/prefill split (`should_split_fa2_dcp_context_attention`) is still decided at capture; unchanged by this PR.
- `set_dummy_context` clamps context to `max_model_len - max_query_len`, so a capture size within `cp_size * cp_interleave` of `max_model_len` still gets zero context.
- The DBO path is not tested end-to-end (needs DeepEP).

**Alternative.** Forcing `skip_dcp_context_attention=False` in the FlashAttention builder during capture. The runner-side fix matches V1 and is backend-agnostic.

No existing PR or issue covers this; nearest are #59951 and #54300 (different code paths).

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Don't count adaptive verification profiling cache as CUDA graph memory
author: nishantrevur
body:
## Overview

With adaptive verification on, Model Runner V2 counts the allocator cache left by adaptive verification's cost-profiling dummy runs as CUDA graph memory, and takes it from the KV cache. This PR releases that cache before `capture_model` takes its closing memory reading.

## Claims

- Fixes the over-counted CUDA graph memory under adaptive verification, in both the memory-profiling estimate pass and the real capture (0.92 → 0.07 GiB in the run below). The KV cache gets that memory back.
- When KV capacity is the bottleneck, decode throughput recovers: 40.5 → 113.2 tok/s in the run below, matching the same config without adaptive verification (110.2 tok/s).
- Startup only. Nothing changes in steady-state execution, and runs without adaptive verification are unaffected.

## Validation

**Startup log.** 1× L4, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` as `draft_model`, `num_speculative_tokens=4`, `enable_adaptive_verification=true`, `TRITON_ATTN`, `max_model_len=32768`, `max_num_seqs=3`, prefix caching on:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 3 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.36 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "enable_adaptive_verification": true}'
# compare the two "Graph capturing finished ... took X GiB" lines and "GPU KV cache size"
```

**Throughput.** Decode-bound long-context workload, greedy, `max_tokens=256`:
- 12 prompts, each a 24K-token slice of vLLM's docs followed by a question.
- Contexts are processed in groups of 3. Each group is first prefilled with one question, then timed with a different question, so the timed requests reuse the warmed prefix.
- One run per config. The memory numbers are deterministic: both runs without the fix logged 0.92 / 0.88 GiB.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | Config | "Graph capturing ... took" (estimate / real) | GPU KV cache | Prefix hit rate | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.36 | main, adaptive verification | 0.92 / 0.88 GiB | 64,688 tokens | 37.8% | 40.5 |
| 0.36 | this PR, adaptive verification | 0.07 / 0.04 GiB | 86,960 tokens | 50.0% | 113.2 |
| 0.36 | adaptive verification off (reference) | 0.07 / 0.03 GiB | 87,376 tokens | 50.0% | 110.2 |
| 0.9 | main, adaptive verification | 0.92 / 0.88 GiB | 376,432 tokens | 50.0% | 110.6 |
| 0.9 | this PR, adaptive verification | 0.07 / 0.04 GiB | 398,912 tokens | 50.0% | 110.1 |

At 0.36, 64,688 tokens can't hold three ~24.3K-token requests. Prefixes get evicted and re-prefilled (hit rate 37.8% vs 50%), and decode runs fewer requests at once. At 0.9 there's enough KV either way, so only the KV size changes.

The effect is larger with bigger models. With #60339's suffix speculator and adaptive verification on Qwen2.5-7B at 24K context (L4, utilization 0.9), the leftover cache was 1.88 GiB:
- KV cache: 44,400 tokens before, 79,584 after.
- Long-context decode: 0.28× of no speculation before, 1.39× after.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
# 48 passed
```

The new `test_capture_model_excludes_adaptive_verification_profiling_cache` covers both `profile_only=False` and `profile_only=True`, and fails on main.

## Details

**Root cause.** `capture_model` reads free memory, captures the graphs, then reads free memory again. The difference is reported as CUDA graph memory. When adaptive verification is on, the profiling for its cost curves also runs between those two readings: `batches_to_profile`, i.e. 5 replays of each capture size plus tail sizes up to `max_num_batched_tokens`, with the profiling context length. Those dummy runs free their tensors, but the caching allocator keeps the blocks. `get_memory_info` therefore sees them as used: about 0.85 GiB here, and 1.9 GiB with a 7B target (allocated delta ≈ 0, all of it reserved cache).

The same `capture_model` serves `profile_cudagraph_memory`'s estimate pass, whose result is subtracted from the KV budget. So the KV cache is sized as if graphs needed that memory.

**Fix.** Call `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` after `set_initial_cost_curves`, matching the `empty_cache()` that already runs before the first reading. The profiling timings are already collected by then, since `StepTimingCollector.collect` synchronizes on exit.

**Scope.**
- Model Runner V1 has no adaptive verification.
- #52233 (opt-in persistent profile cache) touches the same block. On a cache hit it would skip the dummy runs, but it's off by default and doesn't change the accounting.
- #54065 and #54077 change the shapes of the profiled tail, not the memory accounting.

**Not duplicating existing work.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for "empty_cache adaptive verification", "capture_model memory adaptive", "cuda graph memory adaptive verification", "adaptive verification KV cache memory" and "batches_to_profile". The only related results are the PRs listed under Scope.

title: [ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Enable fp8 KV and indexer caches on the AMD QSA path
author: mrodden
body:
## Summary On AMD GPUs, two vLLM flags that enable 8-bit (fp8) KV caching did not work for Qwen4Exp models. This PR makes both flags work. Users get ~33% more KV cache capacity at 16K context with no quality change outside the eval noise. Peak batch throughput at concurrency 16 is ~6% lower; single-request speed is unchanged. Both flags are opt-in. ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 ... \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 ``` `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` shrinks the main KV cache; `--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8` shrinks the compressed-key cache of the model's sparse indexer (QSA). The indexer's raw state cache stays bf16. AMD has two fp8 encodings — FNUZ on gfx942 (MI300) and OCP on gfx950 (MI355) — and the caches use the platform's native one. ## Claims - **Capacity:** +33% at tensor-parallel size 1 (TP1) and 16K context with both flags (2,505,113 → 3,336,874 tokens); the main KV cache halves. Measured on the pre-merge head (`87b62b06e8`). Capacity comparisons are same-max-model-len only. - **Quality:** neutral on GSM8K 5-shot (strict 0.899 vs 0.902; flexible 0.881 vs 0.895, with overlapping run ranges), within the binomial error on GPQA-Diamond (0.4747 vs 0.4596), and identical long-context retrieval (90/90 NIAH cells). - **Deterministic gates:** greedy outputs are byte-identical to the bf16 baseline (a 391-token arithmetic prompt ×3 and a France→Paris continuation at temperature 0). - **Tradeoff:** single-request decode is unchanged; concurrency-16 aggregate throughput is ~6% lower with both flags. The flags are opt-in, a capacity-vs-concurrency choice. ## Validation ### Unit tests `pytest -v tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → **55 passed** on MI355X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.13.0+rocm7.2). The same suite runs on the new MI300 CI step (gfx942/FNUZ); that leg is the regression guard for the gfx942-only scale fix and is pending a full CI run on this head. The prepare test compares the fused Triton kernel's stored fp8 codes against the C++ `reshape_and_cache_flash` reference, using separate contiguous uint8 buffers and the same 0.5/2.0 scales. Both paths write the platform's native flavor, so the C++ op is a valid unfused reference on both arches. The sparse-attention test is parametrized over bf16 and platform fp8; its reference consumes the quantized cache upcast to float, directly exercising the new fp8 read path.
Red run: the fp8 scale fix reverted (historical capture) The original red capture (`fe6ad8c6`, 2026-10-13) was on gfx950/MI355X with the fp8 destination **explicitly typed as FNUZ**. The pre-fix condition (`out_ty == tl.float8e4nv`) already matched OCP, so FNUZ typing was needed to expose the bug on OCP-native hardware. 8 cells failed (fp8 main × bf16 indexer); 16 were skipped because indexer-fp8 combinations were unsupported then. ``` FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[mrope-indexer_dtype0-True] FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[text-indexer_dtype0-True] FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[mrope-model-1d-indexer_dtype0-True] ... (8 total) ============ 8 failed, 8 passed, 16 skipped, 14 warnings in 11.37s ============ ``` The stored/expected code differences are a systematic ~8 code steps across the whole cache — exactly the `k_scale=0.5` mis-scale — far outside the tolerance (`code_diff <= 2 | abs_diff <= RTOL*|expected| + 2*ATOL`). The current test parametrizes the platform dtype. On gfx950 the fp8 cells are OCP, which the pre-fix condition already handled; the 16 `main_fp8=True` cells reproduce on the gfx942/MI300 leg. That leg is why the MI300 CI step was added.
Pre-change boot failures with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 ``` NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp QSA requires a BF16 main KV cache # impl + layer + backend gates NotImplementedError: FlashAttention does not support fp8 kv-cache on this device. # FA base check ```
Green at the current head ``` ======================= 55 passed, 14 warnings in 21.78s ======================= ``` `pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → 23 passed. `pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/ --ignore=tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → 186 passed, 86 skipped (pre-merge baseline; not re-run after the upstream merges). Whole-directory collection has a pre-existing custom-op registration clash, reproducible on the clean tree.
### Throughput Decode is unchanged; peak concurrency throughput is ~6% lower with both flags. The flags are opt-in and independent, so the indexer cache can be enabled alone at no measurable throughput cost.
Throughput numbers ``` decode, 7K context / 512 output tokens: bf16 baseline: 111.0-111.5 tok/s both fp8: 110.5-110.6 tok/s concurrency-16 aggregate: bf16 baseline: 508.4-510.1 tok/s (3 runs) indexer fp8: 509.1-512.1 tok/s (3 runs) main KV fp8: 491.7-510.3 tok/s (3 runs) both fp8: 464-485 tok/s (6 runs, two host-load levels) ```
### Capacity Table at 16K context, TP1, MI355X, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` (AMD's AITER kernels), max-num-seqs 16, no multi-token prediction (MTP), on the pre-merge head (`87b62b06e8`): | config | GPU KV cache (tokens) | greedy gates | | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 baseline | 2,505,113 | 391 ×3, France→Paris exact | | indexer fp8 | 2,541,158 (+1.5%) | identical | | main KV fp8 | 3,238,570 (+29.3%) | identical | | both | **3,336,874 (+33.2%)** | identical | At 32K context (the GPQA/NIAH eval config), the pre-merge head held 5,005,312 tokens (vs 3,336,874 at 16K, +49.9%); a post-merge boot with both flags held 5,062,656 (+1.1% vs the pre-merge 32K number). The shift comes from the upstream merge set and was not bisected. The current head includes a further upstream merge, so its 32K capacity is not re-measured. Capacity comparisons are same-max-model-len only; the +33% headline is at 16K. At tensor-parallel size 4 (TP4; cards 4–7, same protocol), the indexer-fp8 gain grows because the indexer side cache is replicated (`num_kv_heads=1`) while the main KV shards: 11,541,981 → 11,893,691 tokens (+3.05%, vs +1.5% at TP1). The FP8 checkpoint at TP4 on this tree needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` and `--disable-custom-all-reduce`; the open #60839 adds automatic fallbacks for both.
Raw boot-log lines (16K) ``` bf16: GPU KV cache size: 2,505,113 tokens indexer fp8: GPU KV cache size: 2,541,158 tokens main KV fp8: GPU KV cache size: 3,238,570 tokens both: GPU KV cache size: 3,336,874 tokens ```
### Quality All quality numbers are from pre-merge measurements (the same build within each comparison), TP1, MI355X. GSM8K 5-shot, chat template, 250-problem deterministic subset, 6 runs per config, lm-evaluation-harness against the served endpoint: | config | flexible-extract (6 runs) | mean | strict-match (6 runs) | mean | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 | 0.900 0.888 0.908 0.884 0.900 0.892 | 0.895 | 0.888 0.904 0.904 0.904 0.904 0.908 | 0.902 | | indexer fp8 | 0.900 0.892 0.876 0.892 0.884 0.896 | 0.890 | 0.908 0.896 0.884 0.916 0.884 0.912 | 0.900 | | both fp8 | 0.892 0.884 0.868 0.876 0.884 0.880 | 0.881 | 0.896 0.904 0.896 0.884 0.904 0.908 | 0.899 | Strict-match is neutral; flexible-extract is −1.4 points with fully overlapping ranges. GPQA-Diamond and needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) long-context retrieval, both arms on the pre-merge head, TP1, MI355X, max-model-len 32768, greedy temperature 0: | arm | GPQA-Diamond flexible-extract (198 q) | NIAH ({8,16,32}K × depths {0,25,50,75,100}% × 2 needles × 3 seeds) | | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 (auto) | 0.4596 ± 0.0355 | 90/90 = 100% | | fp8 main + indexer | 0.4747 ± 0.0356 | 90/90 = 100% | GPQA is within the binomial standard error (fp8 nominally +1.5 points). Strict-match is 0.00 in both arms (a chain-of-thought answer-format artifact); flexible-extract is the paired metric. NIAH retrieval is perfect in both arms at every (length, depth) cell — fp8 indexer scores and fp8 main KV preserve long-context retrieval identically up to 32K.
Raw GSM8K score lines (first two runs per config) ``` bf16: |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.900|± |0.019| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.888|± |0.0200| both fp8:|gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.892|± |0.0197| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.884|± |0.0203| ```
### Post-merge regression check After the Octave KV (#59774) and later Qwen4Exp merges, a boot with both fp8 flags is healthy: the QSA backend is selected with no Octave interference, the 32K capacity is the number above, and the greedy gates (391 ×3 and France→Paris) are byte-identical to the pre-merge head. The quality evals above were not re-run post-merge. ## Limitations / known gaps - **Unit KV scales only.** The fp8 main KV cache requires unit per-tensor scales (the default). The layer rejects a checkpoint `kv_cache_scheme`, and `forward_qsa` raises `NotImplementedError` if the runtime `_k_scale_float`/`_v_scale_float` are not 1.0. The Triton kernel casts fp8 K to the query dtype and V to fp16 without multiplying by the scale. The NVIDIA port's host-side dequant fold is the follow-up if calibrated scales matter. - **No serve-level gfx942 run.** Unit and kernel tests cover gfx942/FNUZ; the serving, capacity, and quality numbers are MI355X/OCP. A full gfx942 serve run has not been performed. - **Concurrency tradeoff.** Concurrency-16 aggregate is ~6% lower with both flags; decode is unchanged. Both flags are opt-in. ## Details
What changed (three logical changes, plus review fixups) 1. **Fix the fp8 scale divide for FNUZ destinations.** On gfx942 the fp8 cache is FNUZ (`tl.float8e4b8`); on gfx950 it is OCP (`tl.float8e4nv`). `_to_dst_dtype` divided by the KV scale only for OCP, so FNUZ destinations skipped the divide. With the unit scales this path requires today, dividing by 1.0 is a no-op; the fix matters if calibrated KV scales are supported. The test uses 0.5/2.0 scales to exercise the divide. 2. **Support `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`.** Wires `--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype` through `amd/indexer_qsa.py`, mirroring the NVIDIA reference. The compressed-key cache and the query-side cast use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()`; the raw state cache stays bf16. The fused kernel already handled fp8-typed stores and loads; the wiring and test coverage were missing. 3. **Support fp8 main KV cache.** Lifts the dtype gates and interprets the uint8 main cache in the platform's native flavor at the typed boundaries. The sparse-attention kernel gains an `IS_FP8` constexpr (K upcast to the query dtype for the QK dot; V to fp16 for the PV dot). The QSA implementation passes `"auto"` to the FlashAttention base class for its fp8-support probe and restores the real dtype afterwards, mirroring NVIDIA; the backend's combination check delegates with no fp8 dtype, so only that probe is bypassed while the other checks remain. `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` is honored per layer. The QSA cache dtype list now covers fp8 alongside the Octave formats (#59774).
Flavor design and the C++ reference AMD has two fp8 encodings: FNUZ on gfx942 (MI300) and OCP on gfx950 (MI355). The main cache is allocated as uint8 and reinterpreted with `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` in the fused prepare, the attention read, and the C++ cache-update path. The C++ `reshape_and_cache_flash` follows the platform flavor (verified on gfx950: 1.0 → 0x38 and -1.0 → 0xb8, i.e. OCP; FNUZ would encode 1.0 as 0x40). The test therefore uses the C++ op as the unfused reference, with separate contiguous uint8 buffers and the same scales.
Cross-arch and TP4 notes Validated end-to-end on gfx950/MI355X. The gfx942/FNUZ leg is unit/kernel-test validated; a serve-level gfx942 run has not been performed. At TP4, the indexer side cache is replicated while the main KV shards, so the indexer-fp8 capacity gain grows from +1.5% at TP1 to +3.05% (11,541,981 → 11,893,691 tokens); the absolute gain scales ~9×. The TP4 FP8 checkpoint needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` and `--disable-custom-all-reduce` on this tree; the open #60839 adds automatic fallbacks for both.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Preserve whitespace in HYV4 argument names
author: Vegetog
body:
## Overview

Preserve schema property names exactly in HYV4 streaming tool calls. For an integer property named `" count "`, streaming currently emits `{"count": "7"}` while non-streaming returns `{" count ": 7}`.

This addresses the argument-key whitespace case explicitly excluded from #60788.

## Claims

- Preserve whitespace in argument names in both completed-pair and partial-value streaming paths.
- Use the exact key for schema type lookup and keep `"count"` and `" count "` distinct, matching non-streaming parsing.

## Validation

Local results rerun on 2026-10-14 after updating to main `d5e62627a3ece4b2d045cbb2b22ac26c061c8313`, on macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.14 and xgrammar 0.2.8. The tested patch is `04aa841822468b4bcf66c90221cbd2e5df0e1ccc`. Tests use a tokenizer stub with the real vLLM parser, protocol objects, and xgrammar; no model weights are needed.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Whitespace regression suite | 156 failed, 4 passed | 160 passed |
| Both complete test files | 156 failed, 272 passed | 428 passed |

All 156 baseline failures in the complete files are the new whitespace cases; every other test passes on both sides (complete-file baseline rerun on 2026-10-30 at the same commits).

Targeted reproduction (run the same tests with the original and patched production file):

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/tool_parsers -k whitespace -q --tb=short
```

Full-file regression:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/tool_parsers/hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed. The existing CPU Tool Parsers CI job runs this test directory; upstream CI has not been run for this change.

### End-to-end validation with real HYV4 weights (H20, 2026-10-30)

I served the real `Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-preview-FP8` checkpoint and compared streaming against non-streaming tool calls, before and after this PR.

**Setup**
- 1× NVIDIA H20 (SM90), vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev507+g85e199e60` wheel, torch 2.14.0+cu130.
- Only `vllm/tool_parsers/hy_v4_tool_parser.py` differs between the two runs:
  - baseline = `d5e62627a3` (sha256 `d0aa7524…`, identical to the file shipped in the wheel);
  - patched = `04aa841` (sha256 `5b38e435…`).
- Serve flags:
  ```
  vllm serve Hy4-preview-FP8 --tool-call-parser hy_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 --hf-overrides '{"num_nextn_predict_layers":0}' \
    --cpu-offload-gb 690 --cpu-offload-params experts \
    --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 1 --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92
  ```
  The routed experts (MxFP8, HUMMING backend) sit in host memory, since the model does not fit on one GPU.
- Request:
  - one tool `record` whose only property is `" count "` (integer, one leading and one trailing space);
  - prompt asks the model to call it with 7;
  - `temperature=0`, `seed=0`, `reasoning_effort=no_think`.
  - The same body is sent once with `stream=false` and once with `stream=true`. The streamed arguments are rebuilt from the raw SSE deltas.
- There is no grammar or logit bias beyond what vLLM applies for each `tool_choice`.

**Results**

| tool_choice | non-stream (both) | baseline stream | patched stream |
|---|---|---|---|
| `required` | `{" count ": 7}` | `{"count": "7"}` ❌ | `{" count ": 7}` ✅ |
| named `record` | `{" count ": 7}` | `{"count": "7"}` ❌ | `{" count ": 7}` ✅ |

- In each case, the generated token ids are identical across all four requests (baseline/patched × stream/non-stream), so the difference comes from the parser alone.
- The model emits the atomic `:opensource` marker tokens (ids 120033–120043), so this exercises the token-id streaming path.
- On baseline, the stripped key no longer matches the schema, so the value also loses its integer type (`"7"`).

A tiny-random HYV4 model run on the same host showed the same pattern:
- guided (string) path: baseline stream `{"count": "-451"}`, patched `{" count ": -451}`;
- token-id path: same as above;
- non-stream `{" count ": -451}` throughout.

**Unrelated observation**
- With `tool_choice="auto"`, the real model produced a malformed call: `<arg_key:opensource> count </arg_value:opensource><arg_value:opensource>7…`, i.e. the key is closed with `</arg_value>`.
- Non-streaming then returns no tool call and puts the text in `content`, while streaming emits `record` with `{}`.
- Baseline and patched behave identically here, so it is outside this PR's scope. It is a separate stream/non-stream divergence on malformed output.

## Details

`_extract_streaming_incremental` strips keys in two places before schema lookup and argument tracking. This changes valid property names, can stringify non-string values, and can collapse two distinct properties. Remove those two normalizations; the structural-tag grammar already preserves exact schema keys.

Regression coverage includes whitespace-only names, seven value types, colliding trimmed names in both orders, whole/token/character chunks, both token suffix variants, emitted JSON prefixes, and state cleanup between tool calls. Four grammar cases check exact required/optional keys.

Upstream overlap was rechecked on 2026-10-14 at main `d5e62627a3ece4b2d045cbb2b22ac26c061c8313`: both key normalizations remain. No direct duplicate was found. #60788 excludes this case; #59620 handles truncated calls and inter-tag whitespace; #61205 limits grammar whitespace length. Those changes do not preserve whitespace inside argument keys.

AI assistance was used for implementation, test preparation, review, and this description.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][KV Connector] Fix DecodeBenchConnector crash on bounded KV cache groups
author: grYe99
body:
## Overview

`HiSparse` + `DecodeBenchConnector` **crashes** on `GLM-5.3` when `ISL > device_buffer_size(4096)`.

```
AssertionError: DecodeBenchConnector block range exceeds allocated blocks: request=chatcmpl-bd27629bd71bb94d-9ff77f54, group=22, range=[0, 87), allocated=64
```

The assertion fires in the scheduler on the first qualifying request, EngineCore goes fatal, and the whole serve instance dies. ISL ≤ 4096 passes only coincidentally (see Root Cause).

## Reproduction

Single 8xH200 node, TP8, vllm 0.32.0:

```
vllm serve /models/GLM-5.3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 256000 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{}},{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}]}}'
```

The assert above comes from this exact setup, on the first request with ~5.5k tokens.

## Root Cause

HiSparse (in-tree since v0.32.0, #60072) adds per-request hot-cache groups via `HiSparseHotSpec` — a direct `KVCacheSpec` subclass with a bounded allocation of `blocks_per_request = cdiv(device_buffer_size, block_size)` blocks. These groups opt out of external KV transfer (`enable_kv_transfer=False`, `vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`): they are ephemeral per-request replicas rebuilt from their transferable source group after a connector load. `DecodeBenchConnector.update_state_after_alloc` assumes every non-`CircularBufferSpec` group is token-paged and asserts the computed token range fits the allocation.

The numbers in the assert, decoded:

- `allocated=64`: the hot group's per-request cap — `cdiv(device_buffer_size=4096, block_size=64) = 64`, unrelated to sequence length.
- `range=[0, 87)`: the token-paged formula `cdiv(total_computed_tokens, 64)` for the request's ~5.5k tokens.
- Hence the crash is deterministic for any request with ISL > 4096, and ISL ≤ 4096 passes only because `cdiv(ISL, 64) ≤ 64` by coincidence.
- `group=22` is one of the 78 `hisparse_hot` groups of GLM-5.3.

## Fix

Skip groups that opted out of external KV transfer (i.e. groups missing from `KVCacheConfig.transfer_group_ids`): select no blocks for them at fill-scheduling time, the same way startup-fill groups are already handled. NIXL/Mooncake already key off `transfer_group_ids`; no new spec-shape heuristic is introduced.

This also aligns the fill side with the connector's load-side declaration: `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids()` defaults to `prefix_cacheable_group_ids`, which already excludes these groups. Skipping them additionally avoids selecting the 78 `hisparse_hot` layers that are absent from the connector's `kv_caches` (previously warned about on every request).

Groups with `enable_kv_transfer=True` (circular buffers, Mamba, sliding-window attention included) take exactly the same paths as on main — token-range math and the in-range assert are unchanged — so no currently working configuration changes behavior.

## Validation

- New regression test `test_decode_bench_connector_skips_non_transfer_groups`: builds a group from the real in-tree `HiSparseHotSpec` with `enable_kv_transfer=False` and asserts its entry in `reqs_to_fill` is empty; no checkpoint needed, runs in the existing kv_connector CI job. **Fails on main's `decode_bench_connector.py`, passes on this branch** (verified by checking out main's connector and re-running).
- `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py -q` → 30/30 pass.
- E2E on the Reproduction setup (single node, TP8 + MultiConnector): on v0.32.0 as released, the first request with ISL > 4096 asserts as above; with the fill-side fix in this branch, the same serving setup handles such requests normally.

AI assistance was used (analysis, fix, tests, validation); every changed line reviewed and tested by the submitter.

Co-author: @tomasruizt 
Based on https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/pull/18

## Overview

Fixes output distribution shift under spec decode + structured outputs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60451

Architecture overview at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62818.

Alternative to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60690.

## Claims

Fixes the issue with minor performance gains on the async scheduling path (~2%) and a ~2% regression on the sync path.

## Validation

Correctness:

Most direct validation is `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_distribution_shift.py`, which mirrors the issue's setup.
- Sample 4000 samples with the same prompt and regex grammar but with spec decode on vs off
- Compare the sampled distributions
- Distributions differ significantly on main but don't on this branch

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py   \

9 passed, 1 deselected, 19 warnings in 996.13s (0:16:36)

Performance:

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e550d5fb57af73372f57dc0c7c5e694b

`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark` + 15 draft tokens + adaptive verification
Run on 1 H100 80GB

```

Results report throughput in tokens/s.
- sync vs async scheduling
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c96: low vs high concurrency
- brackets report 95% confidence intervals

| Case | main | #60690 | this |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sync / broad / c1 | 536.0 [518.8, 553.2] | 526.1 [510.7, 541.6] -1.85% | 524.8 [513.4, 536.2] -2.09% |

| sync / tight / c1 | 856.9 [823.4, 890.4] | 858.6 [847.6, 869.6] +0.20% | 857.3 [837.8, 876.7] +0.04% |
| sync / tight / c96 | 17,539.1 [17,483.4, 17,594.7] | 17,089.6 [17,026.4, 17,152.9] -2.56% | 17,062.5 [17,007.0, 17,118.0] -2.72% |
| async / broad / c1 | 669.0 [667.4, 670.6] | 663.5 [662.0, 665.0] -0.83% | 666.9 [664.8, 668.9] -0.32% |
| async / broad / c96 | 10,017.3 [10,003.0, 10,031.5] | 9,969.8 [9,908.9, 10,030.7] -0.47% | 10,358.9 [10,340.3, 10,377.5] +3.41% |
| async / tight / c1 | 1,081.6 [1,077.5, 1,085.6] | 1,082.8 [1,077.4, 1,088.2] +0.12% | 1,078.3 [1,077.3, 1,079.2] -0.31% |
| async / tight / c96 | 17,066.4 [17,020.3, 17,112.5] | 16,862.1 [16,622.7, 17,101.6] -1.20% | 17,462.7 [17,411.0, 17,514.5] +2.32% |

## Details

`StructuredOutputManager` changes (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`)
- Rename `validate_tokens` to `trim_spec_tokens`; no longer trim the rejected invalid token
- Allow `grammar_bitmask` to handle unvalidated draft tokens; previously, all draft tokens were already validated by `validate_tokens`

Scheduling changes (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`):
- Remove the `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` call on the async scheduling path

`StructuredOutputGrammar` changes:
- Ensure `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` is atomic on failure: when it returns False (acceptance fails), grammar state is not updated
- Allow `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` to call `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` with unvalidated draft tokens, without an extra `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` call
- Update to XGrammar backend to rollback accepted tokens when `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` fails
- Update to Guidance backend to use `ll_matcher.try_consume_tokens` + rollback vs `ll_matcher.consume_tokens` to not advance matcher state when `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens` fails

`EngineCore` changes:

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pin AITER back to v0.1.24.post1 for DSv4.1 mono decode numerics
author: Ronald1995
body:
## Overview

Pin the ROCm base image back to AITER `v0.1.24.post1`. With AITER `v0.1.25` (#61230), the gfx950 MXFP4 fused-MoE reference selects different kernels and repeatedly fails `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py::test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[4]`. Because that step's `source_file_dependencies` do not include the ROCm base image, the regression is invisible on `main` and only surfaces as a permanently red step on every PR that touches `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`.

## Claims

- Restores the `AMD: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics` step to green.
- Makes an AITER / ROCm base-image change re-run that step, so the next bump cannot land without exercising this test.

## Validation

### Historical CI comparison

| Build | PR commit | `aiter` in the image | DSv4.1 Mono Decode Numerics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [94372](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94372) | `05f5e3fdd3` | `v0.1.24.post1` | **passed** (`exit 0`), whole build 213 finished / 0 failed |
| [94644](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94644) | `a145d106ea` | `v0.1.25` | **failed** (`exit 1`), 11/11 runs |

The two commits carry the same attention-sink change but different upstream revisions, so this is not a strict single-variable experiment. The narrower passing-to-failing window is described below. Both base images report their dependency versions explicitly:

```
# build 94372, "AMD: :docker: refresh ROCm base"
Dependency summary: base=rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete,rocm=7.2.3,python=3.12,
pytorch=733fca1,...,flash-attn=0e60e394,aiter=v0.1.24.post1,mori=v1.2.3.post1,...

# build 94644, same step
Dependency summary: ...,aiter=v0.1.25,mori=v1.2.3.post1,...
```

Repeated attempts fail at the same TP4 assertion:

```
FAILED tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py::test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[4]
AssertionError: ratio 1, 1 x 6
  File "tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py", line 471, in _check_layers
    assert _cos(o[0], same_in) > 0.9999 and _rel(o[0], same_in) < 0.015, tag
= 1 failed, 1 passed  (tp=2 passes, tp=4 fails)
```

Latest head: `259a66489693`, after merging current upstream `main`. Validation is pending in [upstream CI #94692](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94692), requested with `/ci run`. The target step is defined in `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`; the AMD-only `/amd-ci run` pipeline reads `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` and does not contain this step. A passing AMD bootstrap or other AMD jobs does not establish that the TP4 reproducer passed.

Local validation: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. With `PYTHONUTF8=1`, `uv run --no-project --python <repo-root>/.venv/Scripts/python.exe python tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py .buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` passed. YAML inspection confirmed four MI355 devices, the test-file command, the new source dependency, and the image-build dependency. No local GPU test was run; the reproducer requires CDNA4 (gfx950).

## Details

**Failure mechanism.** The mono path runs vLLM's own FlyDSL kernels; the reference uses `DeepseekV4MoE` with `moe_backend="aiter"`. In build 94372, the TP4 shape (model_dim=5120, padded inter_dim=640, token bucket=8) uses the heuristic `flydsl_moe1_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x256_w2_gui` / `flydsl_moe2_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x128_atomic_bnt2` pair. In build 94644, AITER selects `..._w2_gui_fp8` / `flydsl_moe2_layout_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x256x128_reduce_sbm32`, changing intermediate quantization and reduction. This agrees with TP2 passing and TP4 failing. It does not prove which implementation is more accurate. The failed assertion combines cosine similarity and relative L2 error without printing either value, so exceeding the 1.5% relative threshold specifically is not established. The duplicate-tuning warning also appears in the old passing log and is not evidence of a newly introduced defect.

The regression window is narrow. Between the last green run and the first red run, the only change to the branch was merging `main`; within `main` commits `c19c263ac8` (2026-10-13 20:06 UTC, proven green for this exact step by [94594](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94594)) and `4e0681ed56` (2026-10-14 00:24 UTC, the merge point), `7a9d3db896` (#61230) is the only commit touching anything this step executes. The other MoE-facing commit in that window, `ad8d39cbab`, wires padding into `fused_topk_bias`'s **non**-AITER branch, which this test does not take; `e90158d912` touches the batched Triton MoE, which `moe_backend="aiter"` does not use.

**Why the step never caught it.** The step's dependencies are `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/` and the two DSv4.1 mono test files. An AITER bump touches none of them, so the step is created but stays `blocked` on every `main` build. That is why the regression sat unnoticed and then blocked unrelated PRs (e.g. #57797) that happen to touch that directory.

**Tradeoff.** This reverts an intentional periodic bump, so AITER `v0.1.25` is not re-landed until the DSv4.1 mono numerics are understood — either the AITER kernels regressed accuracy on gfx950, or the new numerics are acceptable and the test's contract needs revisiting. ROCm/aiter has no newer tag than `v0.1.25`, so there is nothing to bump forward to. `docker/Dockerfile.rock_base` is pinned too, to keep the two base images on the same AITER.

**Not covered.** No full-model accuracy evaluation and no MI355 run outside CI. Whether `v0.1.25`'s numerics are wrong or merely different is not established by this PR.

**Duplication.** Checked: no open PR reverts the AITER pin or references #61230.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Honor EAGLE3 single-state draft configuration
author: sragrawal
body:
## Overview

Fix Model Runner V2 startup for the GPT-OSS-120B EAGLE3 [short-context](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-short-context) and [throughput](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-throughput) drafts, which set `use_aux_hidden_state=false`.

## Claims

- Single-state EAGLE3 drafts receive the target's final hidden state.
- EAGLE3's default auxiliary-state path and other speculative methods keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

CPU: 32 tests passed, including nine new configuration cases; pre-commit passed, including mypy. Tested on `2521446` plus this patch.

GPU: B200 x1 / TP1, GPT-OSS-120B MXFP4, vLLM `c19c263` plus this patch, CUDA 13, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Context 131072, GMU 0.90, max sequences 8, prefix caching off.

| Draft | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Throughput, k=1 | V2 startup fails: 2880/8640 width mismatch | Generates in eager and non-eager modes; natural acceptance in both |
| Short-context, k=3 | Not run | Generates in eager and non-eager modes; natural acceptance in both |
| Long-context, k=3 (multi-state reference) | Generates | Generates; auxiliary capture retained |

Eight fixed math/coding prompts, greedy decoding, normal EOS, 128-token cap; batches 1 and 8, one warmup and three measured repeats each.

<details>
<summary>Timings and output comparisons</summary>

Multi-state reference, identical rendered prompts and input token IDs:

| Batch | Before tok/s | After tok/s | Change | Before / after repeat ranges |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 547.840 | 537.452 | -1.90% | 544.820–549.704 / 535.911–538.325 |
| 8 | 1897.596 | 1900.161 | +0.14% | 1892.264–1906.589 / 1894.052–1906.894 |

Throughput is total output tokens divided by total wall time, including prefill and decode. Three repeats per case; before and after used separate GPU allocations. These measurements do not establish performance improvement or non-regression.

Some batch-8 outputs were not bit-identical. The unmodified baseline also varied across repeated runs, and the target-only/speculative differences started at near-tied token choices.

</details>

<details>
<summary>CPU test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/eagle3_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py
```

</details>

## Details

GPT-OSS-120B has [`hidden_size=2880`](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b/blob/b5c939de8f754692c1647ca79fbf85e8c1e70f8a/config.json): 2880 elements per token's hidden-state vector. Three-state EAGLE3 concatenates three target-layer vectors to width `3 × 2880 = 8640`, then projects them to the draft's hidden size.

These two drafts instead consume only the final target hidden state and have no auxiliary-state projection. V2 still captures three states, and [`combine_hidden_states`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c19c263ac8ea3fd6e1d2d689f0e4e725855d89cf/vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle3.py#L397) passes the 8640-wide tensor through unchanged. Copying it into the draft's 2880-wide input buffer fails.

The fix honors the flag during runner initialization, so the existing proposer uses the final hidden state instead.

Related: [#40656](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40656) proposed this fix but is closed and unmerged. [#50170](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50170) addresses fallback warnings, not this configuration bug. No equivalent open PR was found.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Mask grammar-invalid implicit reasoning ends
author: vMaroon
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With an engine-based reasoning parser, a structured-output request fails with "grammar rejected tokens" and HTTP 500 when the model samples an implicit reasoning end, such as GLM's `<tool_call>`, that the request's grammar cannot start with. Reasoning rows of the bitmask are unconstrained, so the token can be sampled, and since #59627 it is fed to the grammar. This masks those tokens while the request reasons. Implicit ends the grammar accepts stay allowed.

Related: #60722 (RFC; this is the "remaining issue" it describes, using its first option restricted to grammar-rejected tokens), #59627 (feeds the implicit end to the grammar), #59608 (`required`/named tool calls, which must keep `<tool_call>` allowed), #61456 (open; also edits `_fill_bitmasks`).

## Claims

- A request whose grammar rejects an implicit reasoning end as its first token (a JSON schema, `tool_choice="none"` with `response_format`) can no longer sample that token while reasoning, so it no longer ends in "grammar rejected tokens".
- Requests whose grammar accepts the implicit end are unchanged: `tool_choice` `required`, named, and `auto` with tools (with or without `response_format`).
- The explicit end (`</think>`) and every other token stay allowed while reasoning. Draft and bonus rows under speculative decoding are masked the same way.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, xgrammar and guidance:

```text
python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py
# main source + these tests: 181 passed, 8 failed, 1 xfailed
# this branch:               189 passed, 1 xfailed
```

The 8 that fail on main: `test_real_flow[implicit_end_rejected-*]` (pattern `RRUUU`; main gives `UUUUU`), `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[json-*]`, `test_parallel_fill_masks_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[*]`, and the two `TestReasoningEndTokenIds` cases for the new property. `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[regex_starts_with_marker-*]` passes on both: a grammar that starts with the marker keeps it allowed and consumes it.

Wider run on this branch: `tests/v1/structured_output`, `tests/parser` (without `tests/parser/cohere`, which needs `cohere_melody`), `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py`: 6636 passed, 1 xfailed. `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`: 19 passed on both. `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: the same 48 multimodal tests fail on main and on this branch, because this kernel-less install cannot inspect the Llava architecture.

**Real components, no model.** GLM-5.3 tokenizer, `--reasoning-parser glm45` (`Glm47MoeParserReasoningAdapter`), xgrammar, prompt ending in `<think>`. Bitmask rows while reasoning, then `accept_tokens([<tool_call>])` as the scheduler would call it:

| constraint | main: `<tool_call>` allowed / masked bits | this branch | `accept_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON schema, no spec | yes / 0 | no / 1 (`<tool_call>` only; `</think>` allowed) | False |
| JSON schema, 3 draft rows + bonus | yes / 0 in all 4 rows | no / 1 in all 4 rows | False |
| `required` structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |
| named structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |

**End to end, CPU server.** arm64 CPU image of main `206e45d47`, whose four changed files are identical to `a2fb48273`, with the structured-output backends from `a2fb48273` mounted in both arms and this branch's four files in the second. A 2-layer Llama with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer and vocabulary, `--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, xgrammar, greedy, 3 runs per case. `logit_bias` makes `<tool_call>` (154843) the top token.

| request | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` | 500 x3, "grammar rejected tokens [154843]" | 200 x3, no `<tool_call>` in reasoning |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"`, same bias | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` 100, `</think>` 50, answer tokens 30 | 500 x3 | 200 x3, `{"answer": "yes"}`, finish `stop` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="auto"`, same bias | 200 x3, tool call | 200 x3, same tool call |
| `tool_choice="required"` / named / `auto` without `response_format` | 200 x3 each, tool call | 200 x3 each, same tool call |
| `json_schema`, no bias | 200 x3 | 200 x3 |

Every request that returns 200 on main returns the same response on this branch. The engine log on main has one `Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843]` per 500 (12 of 12); the branch logs have none.

<details>
<summary>Raw request and responses (third row)</summary>

```json
{"model": "glm-tiny", "max_tokens": 96, "temperature": 0,
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Is the sky blue? Reply as JSON."}],
 "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "a", "schema": {
   "type": "object", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}},
   "required": ["answer"], "additionalProperties": false}}},
 "logit_bias": {"154843": 100, "154842": 50, "4913": 30, "9214": 30, "788": 30, "330": 30,
                "9689": 30, "9204": 30, "154820": 30}}
```

main, 3 of 3:

```text
HTTP 500 {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}
(EngineCore pid=131) ERROR 10-14 06:31:44 [scheduler.py:2189] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843] for request chatcmpl-8bf78d42551e682d-8a4ad66a. Terminating request.
```

this branch, 3 of 3 (fields from the response):

```text
HTTP 200  finish_reason=stop  reasoning="" (no <tool_call>)  content={"answer": "yes"}  tool_calls=[]
```
</details>

**Speculative decoding, end to end.** `logit_bias` is rejected with speculative decoding, so these runs use fixed weights instead: layer outputs are zero and the LM head prefers `<tool_call>`, then ` the`, at every position. ngram, 3 speculative tokens, `json_schema`, 96 tokens:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema` | 500 x3 | 200 x3, 96 reasoning tokens, all ` the` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"` | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| drafts accepted (`json_schema` only) | | 207 of 225 |
| `required`, `auto` + tools | tool calls | same tool calls |

Each accepted draft position used a masked row; an unmasked draft row would have sampled `<tool_call>` and failed the request.

<details>
<summary>CPU harness note</summary>

On main the CPU stand-in `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl` (`vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py`) takes its arguments in an order that no longer matches `ComputeSlotMappingKernel.kernel`, so the dispatcher passes `slot_mapping` as `block_size` and the first forward fails. These runs mount a copy of that one function, with the kernel's parameter names, in both arms. Separate from this change.
</details>

**GPU, end to end.** @simon-veitner-redhat ran main `a2fb482732` against this branch `6d144d6478` on H200 ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61574#issuecomment-6163972357)): GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, `glm47` tool and reasoning parsers, xgrammar, 8 seeds per row. "Tagged" means a tool result in the conversation quotes GLM's own tags (`<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<arg_value>`), followed by a `json_schema` request.

| request, no spec decode | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 7/8 500s, 0/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 4/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 5/8 500s, 3/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 7/8 valid JSON |
| `logit_bias` forcing `<tool_call>`, blocking `</think>` | 8/8 500s | 0 500s, empty content |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

| request, MTP 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, async scheduling | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 6/8 500s, 2/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 6/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 2/8 500s, 6/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 8/8 valid JSON |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

Main logs one `Failed to advance FSM` per 500; this branch logs none. The remaining invalid JSON on this branch is a separate frontend issue: the token stream is valid JSON, but the model quotes `<tool_call>` inside a JSON string and `content` is cut there. The CPU runs above use the V1 model runner, so both runners are covered.

**Motivation.** A GLM-5.3 deployment (MTP with 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, xgrammar, `glm45`) logged 649 "grammar rejected tokens" terminations in 8 hours; 625 of them ended on `<tool_call>` (154843). A non-streaming request terminated this way returns HTTP 500.

## Details

Path of the failure, `enable_in_reasoning=False`:

1. A request with a JSON schema is reasoning. `_get_constraint_bounds` puts `constraint_start` past every scheduled row, so `grammar_bitmask` fills each row with the full mask.
2. The model samples `<tool_call>`, which `Glm47MoeParser` treats as an implicit reasoning end: it ends reasoning and starts a tool call.
3. `accept_tokens` finds that end and, since #59627, sets `grammar_start` to its offset, so `<tool_call>` is fed to the grammar. A JSON grammar rejects it and `accept_tokens` returns False.
4. The scheduler logs "Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens" and finishes the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`.

The change, in `StructuredOutputManager`:

- `ParserEngine.implicit_reasoning_end_token_ids`: reasoning-end tokens other than the explicit end, the same split `find_reasoning_end` uses to report an implicit end. Exposed through `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter`. This only adds a read-only property, so no parser changes behavior.
- `_masked_reasoning_ends`: the implicit ends the grammar rejects as its first token (`validate_tokens([t])`, non-mutating in every backend). The grammar does not advance before reasoning ends, so the set is computed once per request and cached on `StructuredOutputRequest`.
- `_fill_bitmasks`: a row the grammar does not constrain allows every token except those ids. Only rows before `constraint_start` (including the bonus row while reasoning) get them, in both the serial and the parallel fill. Constrained rows and rows after padding are unchanged.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- This changes the reasoning distribution only by removing tokens whose sampling makes the output invalid under the request's own constraint. The model keeps reasoning or ends with the explicit end. The alternative outcome is an error, so there is no flag.
- Same scope as #59627: engine-based parsers and single-token implicit ends. Multi-token or text-only ends (`deepseek_v4`, `inkling`) are not covered.
- Cost: one `validate_tokens` call per implicit end per request, and a bit clear per masked id on reasoning rows. No device work and no host sync.
- #61456 replaces the guidance path of `_fill_bitmasks` with a batch fill. Whichever lands second has to keep the reasoning-row mask.
