title: [Bugfix] Honor code_revision in config-based tokenizer loading
author: dskwe
body:
## Overview

Honor `ModelConfig.code_revision` in both config-based tokenizer helpers when the model and tokenizer share a repository. Complements #61272, which fixed snapshot resolution for direct tokenizer loading.

## Claims

- Config-based loading no longer silently ignores an independently pinned tokenizer code revision.
- A separately configured tokenizer does not inherit an unrelated model commit.
- Explicit caller overrides, including `code_revision=None`, remain authoritative.

## Validation

### Config-code pin follow-up (`4a34bfa32d`)

`get_tokenizer` now forwards the resolved `code_revision` to `get_config`, so the remote AutoConfig module follows the same pin as tokenizer code. This is an appended commit; earlier reviewed commits are unchanged.

- New regression uses real HF dynamic config loading from `hf-internal-testing/test_dynamic_model`, with only tokenizer instantiation replaced. Default and matching revisions pass before the fix; a distinct pin fails because the loaded config class comes from the data revision. Negative control: **1 failed, 2 passed**. With the fix, the full code-revision selection is **26 passed, 5 deselected**.
- Registry, generate-stream and LoRA resolver suites: **109 passed** in the existing native Linux CPU validation container.
- All applicable pinned pre-commit hooks pass, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering.
- A separate real-backend smoke probe (no tokenizer-loader replacement) used local tokenizer assets with a remote AutoConfig reference. Baseline loaded config code from `c8ae8a2e5845fc3ad4e5237e4346e5a9ba1e87d2`; the fix loaded the requested `2efddce40dddaccd37bae208c3c7ca66dbedf68a`. Both encoded `hello world` to `[1, 2]`. This is tokenizer validation, not model inference or a new HTTP serving test.

### Review follow-up (`554c1c1842`)

Both review findings are addressed: resolved Mistral mode drops the HF-only `code_revision` key; both config helpers tolerate a missing attribute and no longer inject unset revisions. HF-backed aliases and explicit caller overrides remain supported.

Native pytest was rerun in the existing Linux CPU container (Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0, pytest 9.1.1), with this worktree's Python package and tests copied into an isolated `/validation/pr61611` directory. No AST extraction was used for these results.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py -q --tb=short` | 57 passed; original PR registry with the new tests: 20 failed, 37 passed |
| `python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -k code_revision -q --tb=short` | 23 passed, 5 deselected (includes 8 real Mistral backend cases) |
| `python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -k config_mistral_code_revision -q --tb=no` against the original PR registry | All 8 failed; real backend rejects `code_revision` |
| `python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_lora_resolvers.py -q --tb=short` | 52 passed, without changing their minimal config stubs |
| `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py` | All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering |

The Mistral tests load `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` through both helpers in explicit and auto modes, with `code_revision=None` and `"never"`. Original registry behavior was tested in the same environment with automatic restoration of the fixed file. Warnings were Torch JIT deprecations and the existing `TestTokenizer` collection warning. These are real tokenizer/backend tests, not model-weight loading, inference/GPU evaluation, or a new HTTP serving test.

### Initial validation

Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0. Validation reused a native environment based on e0317b28 with the relevant current modules and tests copied in; it was not a complete native rebuild of b9b401b2ef.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Config/code-revision regressions against baseline | 4 failed, 11 passed, 5 deselected: both helpers silently accepted unknown or missing-code revisions |
| Same tests with this fix | 15 passed, 5 deselected |
| `tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py` | 7 passed |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks on all three changed files | Passed, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

A real `ModelConfig` → `VllmConfig` → renderer integration also verified separate-repository loading and explicit `None` overrides.

A real no-weights `vllm launch render` HTTP reproducer confirmed:
- Baseline: unknown and missing-code revisions incorrectly allow startup and HTTP 200 from `/tokenize`.
- Fixed: both are rejected during tokenizer initialization with the corresponding Transformers `OSError`.
- Fixed matching revision: HTTP 200 with token IDs `[1, 0, 0, 2]`.

### How to Test

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -k code_revision -v --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py -v --tb=short
pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py
```

For manual reproduction, use `hf-internal-testing/test_dynamic_tokenizer` as both model and tokenizer, pinned to `08a35780b7a78794436d8654aafa26ee0165c149`, with `--tokenizer-mode hf --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 32`. The tokenizer-only fixture needs `--hf-config-path` pointing to a real cached OPT config (tested with `facebook/opt-125m` at `27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6`). Keep Hub access enabled. Set `--code-revision never` or `73293ac504e43f4a895688b57c65cebe24f01a38`: baseline starts, but this fix rejects the requested code. A matching code revision starts successfully and `/tokenize` returns the control token IDs above.

## Details

Both `tokenizer_args_from_config` and `cached_tokenizer_from_config` omitted the model's code revision. They now use `setdefault` and the same model/tokenizer repository equality guard already used by the processor chat-template path. This avoids applying a model commit to an independently configured tokenizer repository. The skip-tokenizer-init early return is unchanged.

- `vllm/tokenizers/registry.py`: guarded code-revision propagation in both wrappers.
- `tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py`: real remote-code loading regressions for both helpers, separate repositories and explicit overrides; real Mistral config-loading regressions; accept equivalent offline errors in the existing negative test.
- `tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py`: complete the existing config fixture and regress Mistral argument filtering, minimal configs, HF-backed aliases and explicit overrides.

Duplicate searches were refreshed October 14, 2026 for `code_revision tokenizer`, both helper names, and #61272 references. No matching open wrapper fix was found. #61210 concerns speculative MTP config; #51446 and #42616 fix other artifact boundaries; #61272 fixes the downstream resolver, not these wrappers.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, validation and review. No inference accuracy or performance improvement is claimed. Full tokenizer-suite, model-inference/GPU evaluations, repository-wide lint and a full current-HEAD native rebuild were not run; the HTTP evidence is render-only tokenization, not generation.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Keep failed activations retryable
author: YaoleWu
body:
## Overview

Commit LoRA activation metadata after all layer-loading calls return successfully. A synchronous loading exception currently leaves the adapter marked active, so a retry can skip loading and serve partially copied weights.

## Claims

- Failed activation propagates its exception without marking the adapter active or assigning its GPU slot.
- Retrying a cached adapter executes loading again. An unchanged malformed adapter keeps failing instead of falsely succeeding.
- Successful loading, capacity checks and LRU eviction retain their existing behavior.

## Validation

The CPU regression and real GPU-engine validation below were run on `de8828bf36545fdd414cfd84b1d1480e0c627b7a`. After removing the submitted test and the maintainer's subsequent merge of `main`, the production `vllm/lora/model_manager.py` remains byte-identical at `73be6d45dcc0a15e93edb882ad272d2478f5399a`. The runtime results below predate that merge.

The added regression has been removed from the PR at the maintainer's request. The recorded local regression used the existing manager fixtures and real layer buffers: an incompatible second-layer A tensor made `set_lora` raise; after restoring it, activation had to succeed and copy the restored weights. Both manager implementations were covered. The test file now matches the base exactly.

Before removal of that test, on macOS with the real CPU platform selected explicitly for this source-only installation:

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import vllm.platforms
from vllm.platforms.cpu import CpuPlatform
vllm.platforms._current_platform = CpuPlatform()
import pytest
raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
    "tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py", "-v", "--tb=short", "-k",
    "failed_lora_activation_can_be_retried or test_lora_model_manager "
    "or test_lora_lru_cache_model_manager or test_lru_lora_model_manager",
]))
PY
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/model_manager.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py
```

The local regression failed on the original source for both managers. On the patch, it and the existing selected lifecycle checks passed. After removing the submitted test, all applicable affected-file pre-commit hooks, including type checking and CI test tethering, passed again.

Real multiprocess GPU-engine validation used NVIDIA L20, TP=1, default Model Runner V2, FP16, eager mode, rank 8, two GPU/CPU adapter slots, prefix caching off, and eight prompts with eight greedy output tokens each. The checkpoint is a deterministic, locally generated OPT model with two layers, hidden size 64 and FFN size 128.

The isolated harness runs the original and patched manager sequentially:

```bash
.venv/bin/python run_engine_validation.py
```

| Engine check | Original | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One-time exception at the second LoRA layer | Failed adapter remains active; slot assigned | Failed adapter inactive; slot unassigned |
| Same-ID retry compared with a normally loaded reference | 0/8 matching token sequences; maximum selected-logprob difference 0.2615957 | 8/8 matching token sequences; logprob difference 0 |
| Actual malformed checkpoint loaded twice through worker `add_lora` | First call raises; second falsely succeeds | Both calls raise the shape error |
| Replacing the malformed adapter with valid weights | Matches normal reference | Matches normal reference |

Worker extension methods carry primitive RPC arguments and construct `LoRARequest` inside the worker; pickle-based RPC serialization stays disabled. The one-time failure is controlled fault injection, not a hardware-OOM experiment. The malformed-checkpoint check uses an actual tensor-copy shape error.

The engine validation used commit `de8828bf36545fdd414cfd84b1d1480e0c627b7a`, based on `8a8e2baa02cdd3d98ee99dbead0a8c9943a97410`; native components come from the official `be4ce2e50545c6c1bf13f224022aeb2bcf0c0070` nightly wheel. Compiled sources and the affected LoRA files are unchanged between that wheel commit and the base. GPU runtime: Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0 and Triton 3.8.0. Multi-GPU serving was not tested. These checks establish loading/retry correctness; no accuracy or throughput improvement is claimed.

## Details

Only the two metadata writes move. The submitted test was removed in `6e8d27da` following review; the effective PR diff now contains only this production file. The existing copy/reset loop and return contract are unchanged, with no additional allocation or synchronization. Physical buffers may still contain partial data after an exception, but no adapter ID is assigned to that slot; the next activation executes the existing loading/reset loop.

Open-PR searches and relevant diffs were checked. #60039 validates module-name matching, #60222 compensates failed loads in the Rust frontend, and #59819 exposes slot read/update operations. They do not defer the worker manager's activation commit after a synchronous layer-loading exception. Related overlap-loading and cache-observability PRs were also checked.

AI assistance was used: Codex prepared the implementation and validation. The submitting human confirmed reviewing every changed line and personally running the relevant validation before publication.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Make the query contiguous for TRTLLM ragged MLA prefill
author: hmellor
body:
## Overview

`TRTLLM_RAGGED` MLA prefill passes the query straight to FlashInfer's `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`, whose launcher forwards K/V strides but not Q strides, so a strided query is read as if it were packed and prefill attention is silently wrong. This makes the query contiguous at both call sites (a no-op for callers that already pass a contiguous query, such as native models).

The Transformers modeling backend hits this because it hands MLA a transposed query (`[1, heads, tokens, dim] -> [tokens, heads, dim]`), and `TRTLLM_RAGGED` is the default MLA prefill backend on Blackwell.

## Claims

- Fixes MLA prefill for strided queries with `TRTLLM_RAGGED`, which broke every MLA model on the Transformers backend on Blackwell (e.g. GLM-4.7-Flash gsm8k 0.8% -> 83.5%, native 83.6%).
- No change for contiguous queries.

## Validation

GLM-4.7-Flash, gsm8k (5-shot, 1319 questions), 1x B200:

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| Native | 83.6% | 0.1% |
| Transformers backend, `main` | 0.8% | 31.8% |
| Transformers backend, this PR | 83.5% | 0.0% |

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --max-model-len 8192 [--model-impl transformers]
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

On a small random-weight GLM-4.7-Flash-architecture checkpoint, the first generated token's logprob vs HF eager (same prompt, teacher-forced) went from 0.19 off to 0.00 with `TRTLLM_RAGGED`. Other MLA backends were already correct with the strided query: `FLASH_ATTN` prefill, and `FLASHINFER_MLA` / `CUTLASS_MLA` / `TRITON_MLA` decode.

Tests on B200:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py  # 47 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k TRTLLM_RAGGED  # 580 passed
```

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix double pinning of 3D MoE LoRA and EP dummy LoRA sizing
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #61635.

Two small fixes in `LoRAModelManager` for 3D MoE LoRA:

- After stacking, the `experts.base_layer` entry shares its gate_up tensors with the `experts` entry, so the pin loop pinned them twice. Pop the `base_layer` entry at the end of the 3D branch, same as `_convert_3d_to_2d_moe_lora` already does.
- `create_dummy_lora` sized the 3D MoE warmup dummy by local experts, but `_stack_moe_lora_weights` reshapes by `global_num_experts`. Size the dummy by `global_num_experts` so it works when `ep_size` does not divide the warmup rank.

The first fix needs a third change to be safe: `lora_device = next(iter(first_lora.lora_a))` returned a tensor, not a device, so a packed first entry made `str(lora_device) == "cpu"` False and skipped pinning entirely. Once `base_layer` is gone the first entry is the packed `experts` one, so pinning would silently turn off. Read `.device` from the first non-None tensor instead. This also makes packed LoRAs (e.g. a q/v-only adapter on `qkv_proj`) get pinned, which was previously skipped.

Note this device check was also proposed in #44149 (closed as stale).

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_lora_weights.py
```

New CPU tests (`pin_memory` is wrapped to count calls, so no CUDA needed):
- `test_pin_memory_for_packed_lora`: packed LoRA is pinned, including when the first sub-LoRA is None.
- `test_3d_moe_lora_pinned_once`: only the `experts` entry is left and each tensor is pinned once.
- `test_dummy_3d_moe_lora_is_sized_by_global_experts`: dummy rank dimension is `rank * global_num_experts` for ep_size 1, 2, 3.

## Test Result

On current main the new tests fail (6 of 7 cases; the ep_size=1 case passes either way) and pass with the change. The existing LoRA unit tests pass (42 passed). `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

GPU check on an L4 with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and a q_proj/v_proj adapter through `vllm serve`, counting `pin_memory` calls: the packed-LoRA device fix is consistent with qkv adapters now being pinned (96 pin calls per adapter load before, 528 after). I did not run a real 3D MoE model on GPU, so the double-pin and EP dummy fixes are covered by the CPU tests only.

AI assistance: this PR was prepared with Claude Code. I reviewed all changed lines and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep routing rows during DeepSeek V4.1 decoder replay
author: Ronald1995
body:
## Overview

Keep every prefill routing row when DeepSeek V4.1 decoder replay runs with returned routed experts enabled. Extracted from #61388 as a standalone fix based on `main`.

## Claims

- R3 requests use the existing prompt-logprobs keep-row mechanism so decoder replay does not omit their routing computations.
- Cover eager and PIECEWISE replay in the existing replay-batch suite.
- The diff contains the request row-retention policy and its regression coverage in two files.

## Validation

- **20 isolated CPU policy cases passed** using the actual request-admission, graph-selection, and replay row-selection methods with real CPU tensors. The same checks against unmodified `main` reproduce **6 failures / 14 passes**, including a 300-row prefill incorrectly reduced to 128 rows.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering, and `git diff --check`: passed with local UTF-8/Git Bash interpreter adaptations.
- The pre-split #61388 validation recorded real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1 TP1/DP2/EP, 300/301-token prefill: late layers previously executed only 128 rows; the keep-row fix retained all rows in all 40 layers. The request-retention change is preserved from that combined revision.

GPU/model runs were not repeated for the split. CPU checks stop at the row-selection boundary and substitute configuration/base-state/input-gather fixtures; they do not validate CUDA kernels or attention numerics. The GPU regression remains in the existing CI-tethered suite:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py
```

## Details

Decoder replay can normally skip older prefill rows when only final logits are needed. Returned routing needs every accepted token's decisions; scattering the remaining rows cannot recover computations that never ran. Mark R3 requests as requiring every row when admitted, using the existing keep-row policy.

R3-enabled replay therefore retains prefill work that could otherwise be trimmed. No throughput measurement is claimed.

Duplicate-work checks refreshed open PR searches for `61388 in:body`, routed-expert capture, and decoder replay. #52902 adds API consistency tests, #57184 handles DBO staging/offsets, and #56778 implements terminal transport; they do not implement this NVIDIA V4.1 admission policy. The same fix has been removed from #61388, so this is its single review location.

AI assistance was used to split and validate the existing fix.

title: [Bugfix] Engage indexer TP row sharding on total rows, not per-rank rows
author: zigzagcai
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

> This PR description was written by @ZJY0516.

## Overview

Follow-up to #54951, addressing https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54951#discussion_r4267244007: gate the sparse-indexer TP row sharding on **total** scheduled prefill rows instead of per-rank rows, so the 8xH100 TP8 recipe can actually engage it. The floor becomes `AttentionConfig.indexer_tp_shard_min_rows` (default 65536).

Not a duplicate: no other open PR changes how this floor scales with TP. #60601 lowers the same floor on ROCm only; whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Claims

- TP8 engages row sharding at `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`; before, it needed 131072, which OOMs on 80 GB Hopper.
- −34.1% mean TTFT on a 1.02M-token prompt at TP8 under an H100-equivalent memory budget.
- TP4 engagement point unchanged (64K total rows). TP2 moves from 32K to 64K total rows by design.
- The floor is configurable, e.g. `-ac '{"indexer_tp_shard_min_rows": 131072}'`.

## Validation

**Problem reproduced** on 8xH200 with an 80 GB-equivalent budget (`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.56`, TP8, BF16 KV, merged-commit build `3e8e1364`):

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 131072` | engine init fails: `Available KV cache memory: -6.94 GiB` |
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536` | server healthy, but a 70K-token request schedules `num_rows=65536 < threshold=131072` on every chunk → **0 engagements** |

**TTFT at the H100 budget** (8xH200, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.568` ≈ 81,662 MiB/card vs H100's 81,559 MiB), TP8, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, FP8 KV, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`, streaming completions with one request in flight; only the floor differs between arms:

| Prompt | row-sharded (default) | replicated (floor = 2,000,000) | Δ mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.02M tok (n=2) | **31.57 s** | 47.92 s | **−34.1%** |

The replicated arm was measured with an earlier revision's `VLLM_INDEXER_TP_SHARD_MIN_ROWS=2000000`; the equivalent now is `-ac '{"indexer_tp_shard_min_rows": 2000000}'`. The gain grows with context depth (0.48 s saved at 255K vs 16.35 s at 1.02M): per-row indexer cost ramps with causal depth while the per-row exchange cost stays constant.

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py`: 12 passed (TP8 parametrization, total-not-per-rank floor, TP2 32K–64K window stays replicated, floor never below `tp_size`).
- End-to-end serve + long-context completions on TP8 at the H100-equivalent budget; engagement verified via NCCL coll logging, outputs sane.

## Details

Per rank, the saved replicated indexer work (`~ (1 - 1/tp) * rows`) and the `all_gatherv` index traffic (`~ (tp - 1)/tp * rows * topk * 4B`) both scale with `(tp - 1)/tp`, so the engagement crossover in total rows is tp-independent to first order. The old per-rank floor grew the total requirement linearly with `tp`. 65536 is the TP4-calibrated total floor from #54951.

- TP2 now engages later (64K instead of 32K total rows); the exchange's fixed latency term is largest at small `tp`.
- `balanced_prefill_row_shard` takes the floor as an argument and clamps it to at least `tp_size`, so every rank always gets at least one row.
- The floor was calibrated on H200 with NVSwitch; other interconnects were not measured. Startup auto-calibration is a possible follow-up.

title: [Bugfix] Don't crash DeepGEMM MegaMoE warmup when get_bf16_mega_gate_config is missing
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
**Before:** A server started with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` on a model whose MoE layers use the bf16 mega gate crashes during kernel warmup with `AttributeError: module 'deep_gemm' has no attribute 'get_bf16_mega_gate_config'`.

**After:** Warmup completes. When DeepGEMM does not export `get_bf16_mega_gate_config`, the MegaMoE warmup buckets M values by `block_m` only.

## Overview

#60468 made `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values` call `dg.get_bf16_mega_gate_config` to pick one warmup M per gate config. #61149 moved the DeepGEMM pin to `6ce1c5ec`, which no longer exports that op. Every MegaMoE warmup that uses the mega gate now fails:

```
kernel_warmup.py:244 -> deep_gemm_warmup.py:511 -> :504 -> :366
AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'get_bf16_mega_gate_config'
```

This PR checks `hasattr(dg, "get_bf16_mega_gate_config")` and uses an empty gate config when the op is missing.

## Claims

- MegaMoE warmup no longer crashes when the installed DeepGEMM lacks `get_bf16_mega_gate_config`.
- Behavior is unchanged when the op is present.

## Validation

Existing unit tests:

```
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
# 8 passed
```

Real module, with the vendored DeepGEMM from the precompiled wheel (`vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`): `hasattr(dg, "get_bf16_mega_gate_config")` is `False`, and `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values` (EP=4, 256 experts, top-k 6, 8192 tokens, mega gate on) now returns `[106, 256, 602, 2565, 7901, 8192]` instead of raising.

End to end on 4x B300: a DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint with `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192` finishes DeepGEMM warmup (1254/1254), passes `/health`, and answers a completion request ("The capital of France is" -> " Paris.").

No open PR fixes this: searching open PRs for `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` finds none, and #61538, which edits the same function, keeps the call.

## Details

Coverage trade-off: without gate configs, warmup no longer picks one M per distinct bf16 mega gate config. Gate configs that do not line up with a `block_m` bucket are not warmed and will JIT on the first request that hits them. This costs first-request latency, not correctness.

## Follow-up

A follow-up PR will reintroduce `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` in vllm-project/DeepGEMM and bump the vLLM pin, which restores full warmup coverage for the mega gate. This guard can stay afterwards so a mismatched external `deep_gemm` install does not crash the server.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Pad staged prefill KV to avoid a trtllm-gen out-of-bounds read
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Problem

HiSparse prefill randomly crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` in `sparse_mla_attention.forward_mqa` → `_forward_mqa_kernel` on the staged prefill cache. `HiSparseRuntime.gather_prefill_cache` stages a request's KV into an exact-size buffer (often 1–3 blocks of 64 rows), and FlashInfer's trtllm-gen sparse MLA decode kernel reads ~170–250 rows from the start of its KV cache regardless of the cache's size or the top-k indices (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6484). It faults whenever the caching allocator puts the staged buffer near an unmapped page. Surfaced in #61487 (HiSparse + DBO); DBO makes it more frequent but it is not DBO-specific.

## Fix

Allocate at least 256 rows behind the staged buffer and return the exact-size view, so all downstream shapes are unchanged. Cost: ≤168 KB of transient allocation per staged layer.

## Test plan

Hardware: 2x B200 (pirate2 dell-b200-01), flashinfer 0.7.0.post1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0. vLLM `2f18d13cf` with and without this PR's diff.

**Kernel.** The flashinfer#6484 repro places an FP8 KV cache so it ends at an unmapped 2 MiB page. It faults with 1–3 pages (64–192 rows) and is clean with 4, 5, 6, 8 and 16 pages, at batch sizes 1–128. Bisecting the slack shows the kernel reads about 170–227 rows from the start of the cache, under the 256-row floor.

**Server.** GLM-5.3 NVFP4 with dummy weights and 8 layers, DP2 + EP, eager. Each server takes 3 rounds of 128 concurrent 30-word completions with `max_tokens=128`.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 8}' \
  -tp 1 -dp 2 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":24}}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'
# The DBO rows add: --enable-dbo --dbo-decode-token-threshold 2 --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 512
```

| Revision | DBO | Servers | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | on | 2 | 2/2 illegal memory access in round 1. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the trace points at `sparse_mla_attention.py:858` (`_forward_mqa_kernel` on the `stage_prefill_rows` cache) → `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` |
| main | off | 2 | 1/2 illegal memory access in round 2 |
| main + this PR | off | 2 | 768/768 requests 200 |
| main + this PR | on | 4 (+3 with launch blocking) | No illegal memory access. 2/4 servers die in round 1 from the separate #61487 crash (`dbo_register_recv_hook`, which hides microbatch 1's `CUDA error: invalid argument`); 0/3 with launch blocking |

The crash is not DBO-specific; DBO only makes it show up sooner. The remaining DBO failure is #61487 and is out of scope for this PR.

**Unit tests (B200):**

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or HiSparse or staging"   # 40 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py                              # 15 passed
```

The new `test_hisparse_staged_prefill_cache_backs_min_attention_rows` fails without the fix (`assert 192 >= 256`) and passes with it.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Allow explicit SimpleCPUOffload block counts
author: SherifWaly
body:
## Overview

Allow `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` users to set a shared `num_cpu_blocks` so uneven pipeline stages use the same offload pool size. This implements the explicit-count alternative [suggested in the review of #52921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52921#pullrequestreview-5449639086).

## Claims

- The scheduler and workers honor the configured count for CPU or disk offload.
- Startup rejects nonpositive/noninteger counts and counts exceeding the local byte-derived capacity, before allocating offload buffers.
- Omitting the option retains automatic sizing. No engine-core changes, collectives, or runtime synchronization are added.

## Validation

- **116 scheduler/worker tests passed**, including 15 added regression cases. Tested current-main Python sources on a B200 using the deployed v0.30.0 compiled extensions; this was not a full current-main native build.
- **All pre-commit hooks passed**, including mypy, formatting, and CI test tethering.
- **End-to-end A/B serving:** Kimi K3, two nodes with 8 B200 GPUs each, TP8/DCP8/PP2, fp8 KV, TOKENSPEED MLA, MRV2, RDMA, no speculative decoding, 128 MiB CPU budget per rank. The same connector change was backported to the deployed v0.30.0 image for serving validation.

| Observation | Automatic sizing | Explicit `num_cpu_blocks: 23` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Scheduler / PP0 / PP1 block counts | 25 / 25 / 23 | 23 / 23 / 23 |
| Highest CPU destination ID | 24 | 22 |
| Out-of-bounds native copy calls | 40, across all 8 PP1 ranks | 0 across 1,088 copy calls |
| Nonempty streaming responses with `[DONE]` | 34/34 | 35/35 |
| Forced CPU reload after GPU prefix-cache reset | Not requested | All 16 ranks; identical 16 output tokens |

The baseline reproduced invalid copy IDs and completed its responses without a model segfault. These results establish the sizing/copy defect; they do not attribute every historical crash to it. No throughput or broad model-accuracy improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and serving exercise</summary>

The GPU test environment put the current-main source tree at `/tmp/upstream-vllm` and used a `uv` virtualenv with the deployed wheel's compiled extensions:

```bash
/tmp/offload-test-venv/bin/python -I -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/upstream-vllm"); import pytest; sys.exit(pytest.main(["tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py", "tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py", "-v"]))'
```

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
```

Baseline transfer configuration:

```json
{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":134217728,"lazy_offload":false}}
```

Add `"num_cpu_blocks":23` for the patched run. Both runs use `--enable-prefix-caching --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA`. The tested model's stage allocations contain 12 and 13 block-strided tensors, respectively, with 442,368 bytes per tensor block. Other models/layouts need a different count.

Exercise `/v1/completions` with `stream:true`, `stream_options:{"include_usage":true}`, `return_token_ids:true`, `temperature:0`, `seed:42`, `ignore_eos:true`, and `max_tokens:16`. Send one approximately 11k-token prefix twice, then 32 different approximately 3.7k-token prefixes to cycle the CPU pool. Check positive usage and `[DONE]` for every response.

In the patched run, enable `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` and POST `/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false` after the cold prefix stores drain. Require `success:true`, repeat the prefix, and compare output text and token IDs with the cold result. Reset the GPU cache every four unique prefixes. Instrument `cuda_mem_ops.build_params`/`copy_blocks` to record tensor allocation limits, copied block-ID ranges, and actual CPU-to-GPU copies; successful API responses alone do not establish that offload was exercised.

Baseline trace excerpt:

```json
{"event":"copy_params","layers":13,"source_blocks":10844,"destination_blocks":23,"source_order":1}
{"event":"out_of_bounds_copy","source_max":27,"destination_max":24,"source_limit":10844,"destination_limit":23}
```

Patched trace excerpts (same allocation limits on both stages):

```json
{"event":"copy_enter","blocks":3,"destination_min":20,"destination_max":22,"destination_limit":23,"source_order":1}
{"event":"copy_enter","blocks":5,"source_min":1,"source_max":5,"source_limit":23,"source_order":3}
```

</details>

## Details

Automatic sizing divides the byte budget by each stage's cache geometry independently. With uneven PP stages, the scheduler can assign IDs beyond a heavier worker's allocation; the DMA implementation forms pointers from those IDs without a bounds check. An explicit shared count limits both the scheduler's pool and each worker's allocation, with worker validation based on live tensor strides. For the disk backend, the bound is `disk_capacity_bytes`.

This is materially different from the open #52921: that PR automatically aligns counts using worker collectives and engine RPC. This PR provides the reviewer's smaller configuration-based alternative and leaves engine core untouched. It requires operators to choose a count that fits every worker and configure it identically on every rank. Recalculate it when model layout, parallelism, or speculative decoding changes; unspecified automatic sizing is not repaired by this option.

title: [CI] Fix /ci run reporting a failed merge on fork PRs
author: khluu
body:
## Overview

Fix a race in the `/ci run` auto-merge from #61592: on fork PRs the bot merged `main` successfully but then reported "could not merge (API returned 404: Not Found)" and started no CI.

## Claims

- `/ci run` no longer reports a failed merge (and skips CI) when the merge into a fork branch succeeded.

## Validation

```bash
cd .github/workflows/scripts
uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python -m unittest test_run_ci_command
# Ran 60 tests ... OK
```

New regression test `test_run_waits_for_fork_merge_commit_to_reach_base_repo` (first post-merge compare returns 404, next succeeds) fails on current `main` (no build created) and passes with this change. pre-commit passes.

## Details

**Seen on #61556:** `/ci run` at 17:46:35; the bot's merge commit `8bc708e` landed on `jinzhen-lin/vllm` at 17:46:57; the bot replied ❌ "...could not merge upstream `main` into this branch (API returned 404: Not Found)" at 17:47:02. A second `/ci run` started build #94876 on the same commit.

**Root cause:** after `update-branch`, the script polls the PR until its head SHA changes and then calls `compare/main...<new head>` on `vllm-project/vllm` to confirm the branch is fresh. For fork PRs the PR's head SHA updates before the new commit is reachable from the base repository (`refs/pull/N/head` syncs a few seconds later), so that compare returns 404, and every `ApiError` was treated as a failed merge.

**Fix:** treat a 404 from the post-merge compare as "not visible yet" and keep polling within the existing ~2 minute window. Other errors still fail. Waiting until the compare succeeds also makes sure the commit is reachable from the base repo before Buildkite checks it out.

title: [CI] Fix B200 FusedMoE Layer Kernels hang on NVSHMEM IB setup
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

`(B200) FusedMoE Layer Kernels` is failing ~24% of main runs (59/247 over the last two weeks), almost all of them by hanging until the 90 minute job timeout. The hang is in `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_low_latency-2-1-True]`, where NVSHMEM's InfiniBand transport setup fails and the spawned workers never exit. This PR keeps these single-node DeepEP tests on NVLink and off the NICs, and makes any future hang fail fast.

Alternative to the stalled draft #53332, which retries the launch instead of avoiding IB; details below.

## Claims

- The CUDA DeepEP cases of `test_moe_layer` no longer use NVSHMEM's IB transports. That is where every B200 hang starts. Both GPUs in each test are on the same node, connected by NVLink, so the IB path carries no test traffic anyway.
- `parallel_launch_with_config` kills its workers and raises `TimeoutError` after 15 minutes. `test_moe_layer` already turns that into a normal test failure, so a future hang costs one test instead of the whole job.
- The B200 job timeout drops from 90 to 45 minutes. Passing runs take 15–18 minutes, and the slowest passing run in the last two weeks took 36 minutes.

## Validation

**CI history (job logs from builds 94300–94498, 56 runs: 47 passed, 8 timed out, 1 failed fast).** All 8 timeouts show the same signature and then no further output until the job is cancelled:

```
ibrc.cpp:427:  non-zero status: 22 ibv_modify_qp failed
ibrc.cpp:1526: non-zero status: 7 ep_connect failed
init.cu:1047:  non-zero status: 7 nvshmem setup connections failed
```

**Local repro (2x B300 on one node).** IB is unusable on this box for an unprivileged user (8 MB memlock), which makes it a stand-in for a broken IB setup. Command:

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k deepep
```

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_low_latency-2-1-True]` | fails in NVSHMEM init (`ibrc.cpp:314: cq creation failed`) | passes (48/48 subcases) |
| `test_moe_layer[False-deepep_high_throughput-2-1-True]` | n/a | 191/192 subcases pass |

The one high-throughput miss is a local DeepGEMM JIT failure (`nvcc fatal: Failed to preprocess host compiler properties`), unrelated to this change. DeepEP high-throughput mode with 2 ranks allocates no RDMA buffer and does not initialise NVSHMEM.

**Launcher timeout.** Tested with a worker that sleeps forever and the timeout set to 30 s: it raised `TimeoutError` after 31 s, and no child processes were left behind. A normal launch still returns.

## Details

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

- **It is the first NVSHMEM init that fails, not re-initialisation.** The test creates a new DeepEP low-latency buffer for each subtest, so a passing run initialises NVSHMEM 48 times. Each init logs 32 `cudaHostRegister` fallback warnings (1536 per passing run). All 8 hung runs stop after exactly 32, before the first subtest finishes. So the hang always happens on the first init of the job, never on a later one.
- **IBGDA is unavailable in these pods, so NVSHMEM falls back to IBRC.** The `cudaHostRegister ... error=800` / `ibgda_*` fallback warnings appear in passing runs too. The fallback IBRC queue-pair connect is what intermittently fails, and the worker group then hangs instead of exiting.
- **It looks host- or contention-related.** Timeouts hit dgxB200-09/12/14 (8 of 32 runs) and none of 01/11/16 (0 of 23). 5 of the 8 timeouts started within 2–5 minutes of another run of this job on the same host. Every B200 pod sees all of the node's NICs (the job's `nvidia-smi topo -m` lists 12), so concurrent pods share them. This is suggestive, not proven.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why these settings</summary>

- `NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` disables IBRC.
- `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST=none` hides the NICs from IBGDA. DeepEP's low-latency buffer sets `NVSHMEM_IB_ENABLE_IBGDA=1` unconditionally, and `REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` alone still tried IBGDA locally and failed.
- With no remote transport, NVSHMEM uses its P2P transport. DeepEP's low-latency kernels take the NVLink store path whenever `nvshmemi_get_p2p_ptr` returns a peer pointer, which is the case for every peer in a single-node test.
- The settings are applied through the existing `env_dict` hook, only for CUDA DeepEP backends. ROCm/MoRI paths are untouched.
- The CI pods for both jobs that run this file have their GPU pair on NVLink (`NV18` in the `nvidia-smi topo -m` of the B200 job and the H100 job). If a future runner had a GPU pair without peer access, the low-latency case would fail clearly rather than hang.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Relation to #53332</summary>

#53332 (draft, idle since Sep 14) adds an opt-in join timeout plus a single retry with NVSHMEM debug logging. It is framed around NVSHMEM re-initialisation. The B200 data above shows the failure is on the first init and in the IB transport, so this PR removes the IB dependency rather than retrying it. The timeout here applies to every `parallel_launch_with_config` caller: the longest single launch seen in a passing B200 run is ~195 s, against the 900 s limit.

The H100 SIGSEGV that #53332 also describes happened after `init failed for transport: IBGDA`. This change should avoid that too, but I have not reproduced it.

</details>

**Limitations.** This drops IB transport coverage from `test_moe_layer`. That coverage was never meaningful here: the tests are single-node, and IB setup on the CI pods only works via fallback. Multi-node DeepEP coverage belongs in a multi-node test.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] silu_and_mul_quant: run the vectorized loop
author: Monishver11
body:
## Purpose

`silu_and_mul_quant` (`act_and_mul_quant_kernel` in `csrc/quantization/activation_kernels.cu`) is the fused SiLU-and-mul + static per-tensor FP8 quant that the manual activation+quant fusion (#51415, `maybe_fused_act_quant`) routes static-FP8 models through by default.

Its 128-bit vectorized loop has never executed. The loop bound is computed as `round_to_previous_multiple_of(elems_per_128bit_load, block_end)`, with the two arguments swapped: the helper rounds its first argument down to a multiple of its second, so this rounds 8 down to a multiple of `block_end`, which is 0 for any `d > 8`. With `vec_loop_end = 0` the vectorized loop has an empty range and every element goes through the scalar cleanup loop with 2-byte loads and 1-byte stores. Present since the kernel landed in #10867. Runtime proof on `main`: with the input and output pointers misaligned by 8 bytes the op completes and matches the aligned result for d = 14336 and 10752 (no 16-byte load executed), and faults with `misaligned address` at d = 8, the one shape where the bound is non-zero.

The cost: on H100 the kernel runs at 1.9 TB/s effective against 3.1 TB/s for the Inductor-fused kernel it replaced, and Llama-3.1-8B-FP8 serves about 3.5% slower with the fusion wired than on the Inductor path (numbers below).

This PR:

- Fixes the argument order, so the bound is `block_end` rounded down to the vector width and the 128-bit loop covers the block.
- Takes the vectorized path only when `d` is a multiple of the vector width (8 for bf16/fp16) and both data pointers are 16-byte aligned, via the existing `vllm::is_16byte_aligned`. Rows of other widths are not 16-byte aligned (d = 781, hidden size 1562 in the unit test, starts odd rows 4 bytes off) and would fault on the fixed loop; they keep the scalar loop, which is what every shape runs today.
- In the scalar case the cleanup loop starts at the block's own `block_start` instead of 0. With 2 to 4 blocks per row at 32 tokens or fewer, starting at 0 made each block redo the preceding blocks' elements (same values written, wasted bandwidth).

Output is bit-identical to `main`: both loops evaluate the same per-element expression. Verified below. No change to grid, block size or arithmetic; the remaining gap to the Inductor kernel (0.9x at prefill, about 0.5x at decode) is the subject of a separate follow-up.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches this kernel. #49828 adds a separate per-token dynamic kernel in the same file with its own launch. #59514 is my earlier PR that bundled this fix with a kernel rewrite; it is being split into this fix and a follow-up so each can be reviewed on its own.

## Test Plan

- Runtime proof of the dead loop on `main` and of the alignment guard on this branch (misaligned-pointer test, script in the attached logs).
- Bitwise vs `main` (4b61f300c0): sha256 of the output bytes over bf16 and fp16, tokens 1 to 16384, d in {8192, 10752, 14336, 28672} plus {8, 24, 781, 2048, 4104, 10760, 14341}, and misaligned-pointer cases; 302 cases.
- `pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_quant_activation.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_functionalization.py`
- Microbenchmark: H100 80GB, driver 615, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, `do_bench_cudagraph`; the op on both builds and a `torch.compile` of `SiluAndMul.forward_native` + `QuantFP8(static).forward_native` as the Inductor column.
- E2e on RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 with main's own wiring, three interleaved arms: `main` kernel, this fix, and the same tree with the `llama.py` wiring line reverted (Inductor path):

```bash
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8,max_model_len=4096,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,seed=0 --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 0
vllm serve RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 --max-model-len 2048
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 1000 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 0
vllm bench latency --model RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 --max-model-len 2048 --batch-size 32 --input-len 1024 --output-len 32 --profile
```

## Test Result

- Proof: on `main`, d = 14336 and 10752 complete on 8-byte-misaligned pointers and match the aligned output, d = 8 faults with `CUDA error: misaligned address`. On this branch all three complete and match (the guard sends misaligned inputs to the scalar loop).
- Bitwise vs `main`: **302 identical, 0 mismatched**.
- Tests: **263 passed, 76 skipped** (4 files, unchanged).

**Microbenchmark**, bf16, d = 14336 (us):

| tokens | main | fix | Inductor | fix vs main | fix vs Inductor |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 9.01 | 2.30 | 1.29 | 3.91x | 0.56x |
| 32 | 9.34 | 3.45 | 1.75 | 2.71x | 0.51x |
| 256 | 11.03 | 8.53 | 4.90 | 1.29x | 0.57x |
| 1024 | 54.50 | 30.27 | 25.63 | 1.80x | 0.85x |
| 4096 | 195.15 | 106.43 | 95.54 | 1.83x | 0.90x |
| 16384 | 747.86 | 407.32 | 375.24 | 1.84x | 0.92x |

Geomean 2.18x vs main over 32 configs (tokens 1 to 16384, four d values), range 1.25x to 5.07x. Against Inductor: 0.34x to 0.66x at 256 tokens and below, 0.65x to 0.96x from 1024 tokens up (the 0.65x is 1024 tokens at d = 8192; the other prefill configs are 0.82x to 0.96x). The wider sweep in the attached logs (bf16 and fp16, 64 cases) gives 1.99x geomean, range 1.26x to 4.67x.

**E2e, Llama-3.1-8B-FP8, H100**

| GSM8K 5-shot | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---:|---:|
| main | 0.7817 ± 0.0114 | 0.7089 ± 0.0125 |
| fix | 0.7817 ± 0.0114 | 0.7089 ± 0.0125 |

Identical, as expected from bit-identical kernel output.

`vllm bench serve`, three interleaved rounds per arm:

| metric | main | fix | Inductor path | fix vs main | fix vs Inductor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 37.76 | 38.75 | 39.15 | +2.6% | -1.0% |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 4834 | 4960 | 5011 | +2.6% | -1.0% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 11708 | 11373 | 11271 | -2.9% | +0.9% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 71.80 | 69.97 | 69.22 | -2.6% | +1.1% |

Per-round req/s: main 37.82 / 37.77 / 37.70; fix 38.68 / 38.55 / 39.02; Inductor 39.01 / 39.32 / 39.12. The kernel was switched by rebuilding between rounds. Every fix round is above every main round and below every Inductor round.

Profile, one `vllm bench latency` iteration (batch 32, 1024/32), 1088 launches of the fused op per arm:

| arm | fused op | share of GPU time | decode launch (median) | prefill launch (mean) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main | 68.94 ms | 10.1% | 15.33 us | 809 us |
| fix | 36.60 ms | 5.6% | 4.03 us | 494 us |
| Inductor path | 26.96 ms | 4.1% | 2.02 us | 377 us |

Full logs attached.

I used Claude Code for this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and benchmarks above myself.

title: [Bugfix] Fix NaN output of the Mamba2 chunk scan kernel on sm90
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview Fixes #61603. On Hopper (sm90), the Mamba2 SSD kernel `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` writes NaN/Inf into whole output rows from finite inputs with some of its autotune configs (8 of 23 in the reproducer). The autotuner picks configs by speed only, so it can pick one of them. This PR drops these configs on CUDA sm90 only. It uses one rule taken from the compiled code: drop a config when `num_warps % 4 == 0`, `BLOCK_SIZE_M % 64 == 0` and `num_stages > 1`. Compared with #61664, this fix: - also drops three configs (M/N/K, warps, stages) that compile to the same racy code on Triton 3.7.1: 64/32/32 8w 2s, 128/256/64 8w 3s and 128/32/32 4w 4s. On the [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) tree the reproducer still prints `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 1 of 15` (128/32/32 4w 4s gave NaN in 81 of 100 calls), and 128/256/64 8w 3s gave NaN in 50 of 50 calls at dstate 256. - adds a test that runs the real kernel with every config in the list. It fails on the old code and on the [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) tree. The tests in [#61664](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61664) are mock-only and never run the kernel; on the old code they fail only with an `ImportError` that comes from that PR's own refactor. ## Claims - On sm90, no config left in the autotune list gives NaN on the reproducer: `0 of 12`, against `8 of 23` before. - Other platforms keep all 23 configs. The filter returns the list unchanged unless the device is CUDA with capability 9.0. - No speed cost at the shapes measured on an H20-3e: the fastest config of the old list is kept. - The new test `test_chunk_scan_fwd_every_config_matches` fails on the old code and passes with the fix. ## Validation Setup: 1 x NVIDIA H20-3e (sm90), torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, vLLM at commit `77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989`, then the same commit plus this PR. Reproducer: the issue's script, changed to force each config of `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` in turn and run it 100 times on finite inputs (seed 0, 181 tokens, 2 chunks). Run it with `python sweep.py`. I swept the whole list because the issue's `GOOD` config is not in the list at this commit.
sweep.py (the issue's unused BAD/GOOD/force_old lines left out) ```python import torch, triton from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.ssd_chunk_scan import ( _chunk_scan_fwd, _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel) print("triton", triton.__version__, "torch", torch.__version__, torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0)) seqlen, nchunks = 181, 2 dev, g = "cuda", torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0) rn = lambda *s, dt=torch.bfloat16, sc=0.5: (torch.randn(*s, generator=g, device=dev)*sc).to(dt) x, C = rn(seqlen,64,64), rn(seqlen,8,128) cb = rn(nchunks,8,128,128, dt=torch.float32, sc=1.0) dt_ = (torch.rand(64,nchunks,128, generator=g, device=dev)*0.1).float() dA = (-torch.rand(64,nchunks,128, generator=g, device=dev).cumsum(-1)*0.05).float() states = rn(nchunks,64,64,128, dt=torch.float32, sc=0.1) cu = torch.tensor([0,128,181], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) sidx = torch.zeros(nchunks, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) ALL = list(_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel.configs) print("inputs finite:", all(bool(torch.isfinite(t.float()).all()) for t in (x,C,cb,dt_,dA,states))) nbad = 0 for i, c in enumerate(ALL): _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel.configs = [c] hits = 0 try: for _ in range(100): out = torch.empty(seqlen,64,64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev) _chunk_scan_fwd(cb, x, dt_, dA, C, states, cu, out, sidx, D=rn(64,64, dt=torch.float32, sc=0.1)) hits += int((~torch.isfinite(out.float())).any().item()) except Exception as e: print(i, c.kwargs, c.num_warps, c.num_stages, "ERR", type(e).__name__); continue nbad += hits > 0 print(i, c.kwargs, "warps", c.num_warps, "stages", c.num_stages, "-> NaN in", hits, "/100 calls") print("configs producing NaN from finite inputs:", nbad, "of", len(ALL)) ```
| Tree | Runs | Last line, every run | |---|---|---| | `77154ca6116a` | 3 (1 in a source checkout, 2 in the nightly image for that commit) | `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 8 of 23` | | this PR | 3 | `configs producing NaN from finite inputs: 0 of 12` | Before the fix, the NaN configs were 64/64/64 with 4 warps and 2 stages (NaN in 22 to 31 of 100 calls) and the seven configs with 4 warps and 4 stages (53 to 100 of 100). 128/256/64 with 8 warps and 3 stages raises `OutOfResources` at this shape. After the fix, each of the 12 configs left gave NaN in 0 of 100 calls. Tests: ``` python -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py -k test_chunk_scan_fwd_every_config_matches -v ``` - With this PR: passed, 2 of 2 runs. - With the old config list: failed at 64/64/64, 4 warps, 2 stages, 2 of 2 runs. One run failed the finite check. The other failed the closeness check with `Greatest absolute difference: 1.7147041145625415e+38`, so the test compares outputs and does not only check `isfinite`. - Whole file `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` with this PR: `95 passed`. - `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed files passes. I used `--noconftest` because the test environment did not have `tblib`, which `tests/conftest.py` imports. The new test uses only `monkeypatch`. In CI, the Buildkite step `kernels-mamba-test` runs `pytest -v -s kernels/mamba` on an H200 (sm90), so the new test runs on the affected architecture. Speed: `triton.testing.do_bench` on every config of the old list, NemotronH-like prefill shape (128 heads, headdim 64, 8 groups, dstate 128, chunk 128, bf16), on the H20-3e: | seqlen | Best of old list | Best of new list | Best config | |---|---|---|---| | 1024 | 62.2 us | 62.2 us | 64/64/32, 4 warps, 1 stage | | 8192 | 425.4 us | 425.4 us | 64/64/32, 4 warps, 1 stage | At seqlen 8192 the dropped configs took 481.7 to 1818.1 us. Not run: an end-to-end NemotronH server run (the issue's empty responses and `not JSON compliant: nan`). Only the kernel reproducer and the tests above were run. ## Details Root cause. In the K loop, `acc += tl.dot(cb, x)` uses `cb` built in registers (decay `exp`, `dt`, causal mask, cast to bf16). With whole warpgroups (`num_warps % 4 == 0`) and `BLOCK_SIZE_M % 64 == 0`, Triton lowers this dot to wgmma with the A operand in registers. With `num_stages > 1`, Triton's `TritonGPUPipeline` pass splits the dot into async wgmmas and waits with `pendings = 1`. So the last wgmma of an iteration is still running when the loop jumps back. The next iteration loads the next `cb` tile into the same registers before it waits for that wgmma. The PTX ISA does not allow changes to the A registers of `wgmma.mma_async` before `wgmma.wait_group`. The running wgmma reads raw fp32 bits as bf16, which gives NaN, Inf and values near 3.4e38 in whole output rows. The race depends on timing, so the NaN rate changes by config and by run. The bug is in Triton's pipeliner, which vLLM cannot change. The vLLM part is that the autotune list offers configs that Triton compiles this way.
SASS of the K loop, 128/128/32 with 4 warps and 4 stages ``` /*58f0*/ LDS.128 R160, [R234] ; <- overwrites R160..R163 /*5b90*/ LDS.128 R156, [R234+0x1000] ; <- overwrites R156..R159 ... /*70a0*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R88, R160, gdesc[UR12].tnspB, R88 ; <- A = R160..R163 /*70b0*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R24, R156, gdesc[UR12].tnspB, R24, gsb0 ; <- A = R156..R159 /*71d0*/ WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0, 0x1 ; <- leaves the 0x70a0/0x70b0 group running ... /*7720*/ @!P5 BRA 0x5750 ; ```
The fix. `_drop_racy_wgmma_configs` wraps the existing list. On CUDA sm90 it drops 11 of the 23 configs (old indices 2, 9, 10, 12, 13 to 19). - It keeps the 1-stage wgmma configs: Triton waits on them with `pendings = 0` right after the dot. It keeps the 2-warp and `BLOCK_SIZE_M = 32` configs: they use `mma.sync`, which is synchronous. - Only sm90 has wgmma, so other GPUs keep the full list. `is_cuda()` is needed because ROCm gfx90a also reports capability (9, 0). - The filter is a rule, not a list of configs that failed once. Configs 2, 10 and 12 have the same racy code but gave little or no NaN at the reproducer's shape (12 does not fit there). At dstate 256, config 10 gave NaN in 1 of 20 calls and config 12 in 20 of 20. A TTGIR check of all 23 old configs at dstate 128 and 256 found 0 mismatches between the rule and the racy pattern. - The filter runs when the list is built, not as `early_config_prune`. Triton skips pruning when the list has one config, and `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG` walks `self.configs` without pruning, so pruned configs could still run. - A TTGIR scan of the other Mamba2 SSD kernels (`_bmm_chunk_fwd`, `_chunk_state_fwd`, `_state_passing_fwd`, `_chunk_cumsum_fwd`) found no register-A async wgmma, so only this kernel changes. Reading the diff: `ruff format` re-indents the config list because it is now a function argument. With whitespace hidden (`git diff -w`), the change in `ssd_chunk_scan.py` is about 25 lines. No config is added, removed or edited by hand. Limitations: this works around a Triton bug seen with Triton 3.6.0 (in the issue) and 3.7.1 (here). The new test does not check that non-sm90 platforms keep the full list. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Support heterogeneous TP in WRITE mode for all attention and mamba layers
author: junkang1991
body:
Fixes #60101. This PR fixes a hang in MoRIIO WRITE-mode disaggregated serving when using MLA models with a smaller tensor-parallel size on prefill than on decode.

For example, with prefill TP2 and decode TP4, the expected mapping is:

- Prefill rank 0 → decode ranks 0 and 1
- Prefill rank 1 → decode ranks 2 and 3

Previously, each prefill rank wrote the KV cache to only the first mapped decode rank. The other decode ranks did not receive their KV cache or completion notification and continued waiting indefinitely.

## Root cause

MoRIIO already calculated the first corresponding remote TP rank, but the WRITE data path treated this as a one-to-one mapping.

That behavior is sufficient for equal TP sizes and mappings that do not require replication. However, the MLA KV cache must be fanned out when the decode TP size is a multiple of and larger than the prefill TP size.

The existing heterogeneous-TP acknowledgement logic expects completion from all corresponding decode ranks, while the WRITE path previously reached only one of them.

## Changes

This PR introduces a small helper, `get_moriio_write_target_tp_ranks`, which extends the existing remote-rank mapping for MLA WRITE fan-out.

When MLA is used and decode TP is larger than prefill TP:

1. Determine the first decode rank using the existing MoRIIO TP-rank mapping.
2. Calculate the required fan-out from the prefill and decode TP sizes.
3. Establish sessions with every corresponding decode rank.
4. Write the KV cache through every target session.
5. Wait for all resulting transfer statuses before completing the request.
6. Send `write_done` to every target decode rank.
7. Send `write_failed` to every affected target if a deferred write times out.

## Scope and compatibility

The fan-out behavior is restricted to:

- MoRIIO WRITE mode
- MLA models
- Prefill TP smaller than decode TP

This change is contained within the vLLM MoRIIO connector and does not require changes to the MoRI library.

Routing is based on TP/DP ranks and the existing endpoint-resolution logic rather than physical node placement. Runtime validation was performed on a single node.

## Unit tests

Added coverage for:

- MLA TP2 → TP4 target mapping
- MLA TP4 → TP8 target mapping
- Equal and decreasing TP mappings
- Non-MLA behavior remaining unchanged
- Creating a write session for every fan-out target
- Accumulating all transfer statuses
- Sending completion notifications to every target
- Sending timeout/failure notifications to every target
- Passing fan-out routing information from the connector to the writer
- Existing DP and multi-pod notification behavior

Command:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_write_done_routing.py
```

## Runtime validation

### Environment

- Single AMD MI355X node
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite
- MoRIIO RDMA WRITE mode
- Prefill TP2
- Decode TP4

The router, prefill instance, and decode instance were started in separate terminals.

### Router

```bash
  --vllm-pd-disaggregation \
  --kv-connector moriio \
  --vllm-discovery-address 0.0.0.0:36367 \
  --port 8402
```

### Prefill instance

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --tensor_parallel_size 2 \
  --port 18400 \
  --max-model-len 65536 \

```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --tensor_parallel_size 4 \
  --port 18404 \

    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "rdma",

```

### Serving benchmark

```bash
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://localhost:8402 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
```

title: [Bugfix] Honor OPT token embedding width for prompt embeddings
author: maithilijoshi20
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61709. Use OPT's token embedding width for prompt embedding validation and runner buffers so `facebook/opt-350m` works with `--enable-prompt-embeds`.

## Claims

- Accept OPT-350m's 512-wide prompt embeddings and reject its incompatible 1024-wide hidden states.
- Allocate 512-wide input buffers for both model runners, matching `embed_input_ids()` and the decoder's `project_in` input.
- Preserve CLIP/SigLIP text embedding validation when their projection width differs from their hidden size.

## Validation

Review follow-up: CI scripts are unchanged. OPT-350m retains GPU generation coverage and is omitted from the offline CPU model matrix, whose cache lacks its weights; existing OPT-125m CPU coverage remains. The completion-renderer mock exposes the text config, and tokenizer setup uses the existing bounded retry helper. Follow-up checks: 57 renderer/width tests passed; both OPT-350m GPU cases remain selected, and neither is selected by `-m cpu_model`. Earlier CI-fix validation also passed 148 renderer/validation tests and 12 GPT-J streaming tests (4 skipped).



Tested in WSL on an RTX 3050 (8 GiB), Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, and Transformers 5.19.0. **202 pytest cases passed**, plus live HTTP and baseline reproduction checks.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original OPT-350m config and validation | 512-wide inputs rejected; incompatible 1024-wide inputs accepted; buffer width 1024 |
| Fixed OPT-350m config and validation | 512-wide inputs accepted; 1024-wide inputs rejected; buffer width 512 |
| Prompt payload, sparse tensor, and completion validation | 113 passed |
| Chat prompt embedding parsing and GPU overlay kernels | 85 passed |
| OPT-350m generation evaluation, V2 runner | 2 passed, prompt embeddings enabled/disabled |
| OPT-350m generation evaluation, legacy runner | 2 passed, prompt embeddings enabled/disabled |
| Live HTTP completions | Single/batched embeddings match token-ID generation; streaming matches; wrong width returns 400; server remains healthy |
| Pre-commit hooks and whitespace | Passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and test CI tethering |

Generation evaluations use the existing Hugging Face/vLLM greedy generation and top-5 log-probability comparison over 32 generated tokens. With prompt embeddings enabled, they also compare token-ID and embedding generation. Both runners were tested with compilation/CUDA graphs; HTTP validation additionally exercised eager mode and chunked prefill.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and local configuration</summary>

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/test_prompt_embeds_payload_validation.py \
  tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_prompt_validation.py \
  -k 'not empty_prompt and not out_of_vocab' --tb=short -q

PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_prompt_embeds.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_prompt_embeds_state.py --tb=short -q

PYTHONPATH=. VLLM_PLUGINS= .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py -k opt-350m --tb=short -xv

PYTHONPATH=. VLLM_PLUGINS= VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \
  VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py -k opt-350m --tb=short -xv

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only HEAD^ HEAD)
git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD
```

For the local 8 GiB GPU, a pytest plugin set `VllmRunner` defaults to `gpu_memory_utilization=0.65`, `attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}`, and `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`; the evaluation commands above require equivalent overrides on similarly constrained GPUs. Legacy runner testing used the supported PyTorch sampler because FlashInfer sampling warmup requires `nvcc`, which is absent from this WSL environment. Compiled libraries and the wheel-supplied FlashMLA interface were reused from the existing installation. No CUDA/C++ sources changed.

The HTTP server used `--enable-prompt-embeds --dtype float16 --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 --max-model-len 128 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 16 --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`.

</details>

## Details

OPT-350m embeds tokens at `word_embed_proj_dim=512`, then projects them to `hidden_size=1024` inside the decoder. Buffer allocation and request validation previously used 1024, causing startup/input-copy failures and accepting embeddings that `project_in` cannot consume.

Add `word_embed_proj_dim` to the input-buffer size lookup and use it for request validation when present. Validation otherwise retains `get_hidden_size()`: using the buffer accessor wholesale would change CLIP/SigLIP validation to their projection width. Both runners share the corrected buffer accessor; no runner-specific branches or inference synchronization are added.

Regression coverage extends existing suites with actual OPT-350m/OPT-125m/CLIP/SigLIP configurations and adds OPT-350m to the model registry and generation comparison matrix. Duplicate searches for `61709 in:body` and `word_embed_proj_dim` found no open PR addressing this fix.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Require exact strides for moe_forward custom ops
author: ldkhang1201
body:
## Overview

Fixes #52308: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4` outputs garbage under `torch.compile` with the FlashInfer TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE backend. `--enforce-eager` works. The fix changes the tag on `vllm.moe_forward` and `vllm.moe_forward_shared` from `needs_fixed_stride_order` to `needs_exact_strides`.

This supersedes #52383, which I closed: it moved the pad inside the op based on a wrong diagnosis (CUDA-graph replay), and that approach would break the ROCm RMSNorm+pad fusion (#34636). #49092 (`.contiguous()` in `scaled_fp4_quant`) would be a complementary kernel-side safeguard.

## Claims

- GSM8K accuracy for Nemotron-3-Nano NVFP4 on TRTLLM MoE with default compile goes from ~0.01 back to eager parity.
- A new unit test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- The change is two lines and touches no other code path.

## Validation

1x GB300, torch 2.14.0+cu132, default `vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, which selects the FLASHINFER_TRTLLM MoE backend. Evaluated with `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` on all 1319 questions. Every compiled run used fresh `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` and `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` directories (see the cache note in Details).

| Config | Completions, 5-shot, 256 tokens | Chat, thinking off, 1024 tokens, temp 0 |
|---|---|---|
| `--enforce-eager` | 0.303 | 0.882 |
| compile, main | 0.006 (46% invalid) | 0.008 (47% invalid) |
| compile, this PR | 0.299 | 0.890 |

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
    --max-tokens 1024 --temperature 0 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

Unit test: `pytest tests/quantization/test_trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_dim_padding.py -v` gives 5 passed. With the old tag, the new test fails with `[(2816, 1)] == [(2688, 1)]`.

The GPU runs used base commit 8a8e2baa02 with this exact patch. Between that commit and this branch's base, the only change under `fused_moe/` is `oracle/fp8.py`.

## Details

**Root cause.** Nemotron-3-Nano has hidden size 2688. The TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE pads it to 2816, and `MoERunner._maybe_pad_hidden_states` applies `F.pad` inside the compiled graph. Inductor fuses the preceding RMSNorm into the padded buffer. Because `needs_fixed_stride_order` only pins stride *order*, Inductor then passes `shared_experts_input` (the unpadded 2688-wide activations) to `moe_forward_shared` as a view into that buffer: `reinterpret_tensor(buf, (s, 2688), (2816, 1), 0)`. The shared expert's NVFP4 linear calls `scaled_fp4_quant`, whose kernel assumes packed rows. Row 0 is read correctly; every later row is read at the wrong offset. Eager mode never creates the alias. With this PR, the generated code passes a separate packed buffer.

**Why this tag.** `needs_fixed_stride_order` was a torch 2.6 workaround. It was already removed from the other MoE custom ops in #19346, #28974 and #33209; these two ops were missed. Since torch 2.8, `needs_exact_strides` has been the default for custom ops (pytorch/pytorch#148063, #150511), so this restores the default behavior.

**Tradeoff.** Inductor may now insert a copy when its preferred layout differs from eager, which in practice means one `(tokens, hidden)` copy per MoE layer when the hidden dim is padded. When no padding happens, inputs are already contiguous and nothing changes. The change adds no host sync. On ROCm, gpt-oss with the AITER RMSNorm+pad fusion uses `moe_forward` with the padded buffer itself, which is contiguous, so it is unaffected.

**Compile cache note.** Changing the op tag does not invalidate the Inductor FX graph cache or the vLLM AOT compile cache. `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` does not bypass the Inductor cache either. A dev install at the same vLLM version may keep loading the old aliased graph until those caches are cleared. Release upgrades are unaffected because the vLLM version is part of the cache key.

**Scope and CI.**
- `needs_fixed_stride_order` still appears in `model_executor/layers/transformers/moe.py`, `models/utils.py` and `qwen3_dflash2.py`. I did not analyze those call sites and left them unchanged.
- The new test runs in the H200 Quantization job. It mocks the MoE layer with `Mock(spec=MoERunnerInterface)` because `get_layer_from_name` asserts that type, and checks only the stride the op receives, so the result is deterministic.
- No existing GSM8K CI config covers TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE with compile: the Nemotron NVFP4 configs in `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor/` use `--enforce-eager` or CUTLASS. I can add one as a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR uses `needs_exact_strides` or addresses this stride alias. #52383 (mine, now closed) and #49092 are discussed above. Open PRs #61179 and #61367 touch the same op registration for a different bug.

**AI assistance.** I used Claude Code to investigate, write the patch and test, and run the evaluations. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evals above.
