title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fill K-padded output in silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant
author: gkswns0531
body:
## Overview

Fixes #48898. Under torch.compile, NVFP4 models whose per-rank MLP width K is 16 mod 32 (e.g. Qwen2.5-72B / Qwen2.5-VL-72B at TP=8, K = 3696) produce garbage once a batch has more than one token. The SiluMul+NVFP4 fusion replaces the K-padded `scaled_fp4_quant` of the CUTLASS NVFP4 linear (#42774) with `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant`, which writes that buffer with the unpadded row pitch. #63382 fixed the padded scale factors of this kernel; the row pitch is what remains.

## Claims

- `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` writes a K-padded output the way `scaled_fp4_quant(..., padded_n=...)` does: row pitch and scale tile from the output width, zero data in the padding.
- Compiled output matches eager again on a padded-K model (perplexity 1290959 → 29.45, eager 29.43).
- Unpadded outputs keep the same addressing, and the kernel is not slower on any of the 24 shapes timed (−13% to +0.3%).

## Validation

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.14.0+cu130. Base is main at 08e3f26, built in the same cmake tree.

| Check | Base | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel test (`test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`) | 10 failed, 20 passed | 30 passed |
| Fusion pass tests (`test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py`, `test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py`) | | 154 passed, 48 skipped |
| GEMM reproducer (K = 3696 → 3712, M = 4): relative error per row vs BF16 | 0.127, **1.533, 1.556, 1.532** | 0.127, 0.134, 0.138, 0.128 (same as unfused) |
| WikiText-2 perplexity, padded K = 4848, eager / compiled | 29.430 / **1290959** | 29.430 / 29.451 |
| Same, unpadded K = 4864, eager / compiled | 24.855 / 24.833 | 24.855 / 24.833 |

The perplexity model is `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with its MLP narrowed to 4848 channels so that `down_proj` needs K padding on one GPU (ModelOpt `NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG`, `--linear-backend cutlass`, 64 test texts).

<details>
<summary>Kernel time</summary>

`silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` in µs per launch: BF16 input, one CUDA graph of 200 launches whose inputs rotate through more than three times the 128 MB L2 (where memory allows), timed with CUDA events, mean of three alternating base/fix rounds; output buffers padded as the fusion allocates them. The base time for K = 3696 is for reference only, since that kernel writes the wrong layout.

| M | K = 3696 → 3712 | K = 4864 | K = 7392 | K = 14336 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.27 → 1.24 | 1.39 → 1.34 | 2.01 → 1.97 | 1.82 → 1.79 |
| 16 | 1.38 → 1.31 | 1.54 → 1.45 | 2.07 → 1.98 | 2.93 → 2.60 |
| 128 | 2.70 → 2.60 | 2.89 → 2.64 | 4.50 → 3.91 | 6.43 → 6.09 |
| 1000 | 11.58 → 11.00 | 14.70 → 14.04 | 23.10 → 20.66 | 39.57 → 39.19 |
| 1024 | 11.90 → 11.35 | 15.02 → 14.27 | 23.36 → 21.11 | 40.67 → 40.19 |
| 8192 | 91.09 → 91.15 | 123.8 → 123.6 | 187.6 → 187.3 | 361.1 → 362.1 |

Both builds use 40 registers per thread.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Commands and GEMM reproducer</summary>

```bash
# Both arms from one build tree (only the kernel file differs)
cmake --build cmake-build-release --target _C_stable_libtorch -j 44

pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py

# Kernel timing: for each (M, K) above, a CUDA graph of 200
#   torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant(out, out_sf, x_i, global_scale) launches over rotating inputs x_i,
#   with out, out_sf from ops.create_fp4_output_tensors(M, K, device, True, padded_n=round_up(K, 32));
#   CUDA-event time of a replay / 200, median of 7 replays

# Model check: LLM(model, quantization="modelopt_fp4", linear_backend="cutlass", enforce_eager=True/False);
#   perplexity from prompt_logprobs over 64 WikiText-2 test texts
```

```python
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_utils import (
    pad_nvfp4_weight_for_cutlass, swizzle_blockscale)

rows, k, n = 4, 3696, 512
x = torch.randn(rows, 2 * k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
weight = torch.randn(n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.02
y = torch.empty(rows, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul(y, x)
w_gs = (448.0 * 6.0 / weight.abs().amax().float()).reshape(1)
w_fp4, w_sf = ops.scaled_fp4_quant(weight, w_gs, is_sf_swizzled_layout=False)
w_sf = swizzle_blockscale(w_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn))
w_fp4, pad = pad_nvfp4_weight_for_cutlass(w_fp4)
x_gs = (448.0 * 6.0 / y.abs().amax().float()).reshape(1)
alpha = 1.0 / (x_gs * w_gs)
eager = ops.scaled_fp4_quant(y, x_gs, padded_n=k + 2 * pad)
fused = ops.create_fp4_output_tensors(rows, k, y.device, True, padded_n=k + 2 * pad)
torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant(*fused, x, x_gs)
ref = y.float() @ weight.float().T
for name, (a, a_sf) in {"eager": eager, "fused": fused}.items():
    out = ops.cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm(a, w_fp4, a_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn), w_sf, alpha, torch.bfloat16)
    print(name, [round(float((out[r].float() - ref[r]).norm() / ref[r].norm()), 3) for r in range(rows)])
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The fused kernel writes into the buffers allocated for the padded quant: `[M, (K + 16) / 2]` data and a 128x4 scale tile. It used K instead of K + 16 as the row pitch, so every row after the first is shifted against its scales. Single-token checks still pass. It also left the padded scale columns and rows unwritten (the stale-column failure analysed in #48898), which #63382 has since fixed.

**Fix.** The launcher passes the output width. The kernel takes the row pitch and the scale tile from it and writes the zeros it already computes for padded positions into the K padding. For an unpadded output the width equals K, so the addressing is the same as before. A `TORCH_CHECK` requires the output width to be a multiple of 16 that holds the input.

**Scope.** In practice only the down_proj input (K = intermediate size / TP) gets padded; the other quant fusions feed K = hidden size or heads × head_dim and are unchanged. Skipping the fusion for padded outputs would be simpler but would drop it on exactly these layers.

**Duplicate check.** #63382 fixed the padded scale factors but not the row pitch, so #48898 still reproduces on main (table above). #49092 and #49093 came out of the same investigation and fix other problems. #59467 (open) rewrites this kernel to add GELU-tanh; whichever lands second carries the padded-output handling, and I can rebase this one onto it.

**CI coverage and limitations.** The kernel test needs SM100+ and is skipped on CI's L4 runners; the `(B200) Fusion and Compile` job runs the two fusion tests. I validated on SM120 only, with a CUDA 13.4 build (16-element path; the 8-element path of CUDA < 12.9 builds has the same change but was not run). The model-level check used the narrowed 0.5B model on one GPU, not a TP=8 72B deployment.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), which traced the root cause, wrote the fix and tests, ran the validation above and drafted this description.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Leave the final stop token out of chat derender text
author: khluu
body:
## Overview

Partially fixes #57052: the chat token-stop part (EOS and `stop_token_ids`). Completion derender and stop strings remain open there.

Chat derender now leaves the stop token that finished generation out of the decoded text, the way the engine's detokenizer does. This fixes `test_parity_reasoning` and `test_stream_parity_reasoning` in `(H200 MIG 35GB) Entrypoints Integration (API Server)`, which fail on main because derender returns `...\boxed{391}\n\]<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` where the coupled server returns `...\boxed{391}\n\]`. Examples: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95020#01a13dbe-64d7-4310-bfe8-807fb58fd14b (batch) and https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94727#01a13986-c733-4d38-ad14-feb389277a93 (stream).

## Claims

- Chat derender (batch, plain stream and parser stream) no longer puts the EOS / stop-token text into `content` when `finish_reason` is `stop`. This matches the coupled `/v1/chat/completions` output.
- `include_stop_str_in_output=true` still keeps it, and `ignore_eos` turns off the EOS check, both as in the engine.
- The returned `token_ids` and the ids passed to the parser are unchanged and still include the stop token, as on the coupled path.

## Validation

All runs used the CI image for main `10d2c6083d` (the failing build 95020) on an H200:

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| new `test_parsed_derender_leaves_out_stop_token_like_engine` (EOS, `stop_token_ids`, stop string, `include_stop_str_in_output`) | **fails** on the EOS and `stop_token_ids` cases | passes |
| `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py` (non-server tests) | 94 passed, 1 failed (the new test) | 95 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py` (GPU, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) | fails intermittently on main CI | 10 passed, 6 skipped |

## Details

**Root cause.** When generation stops on a stop token, the engine's `IncrementalDetokenizer.update` drops that token before decoding unless `include_stop_str_in_output` is set (`vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py`). Derender received the same `token_ids`, including the stop token, and decoded all of them. Without a parser this was hidden, because `skip_special_tokens=True` drops the EOS anyway. With a reasoning or tool parser, derender decodes with `skip_special_tokens=False` so the parser can see its markers, and the EOS text ends up in `content`. Each test fails only on runs whose greedy, 256-token generation ends on EOS rather than at the length limit. On main that is a minority of runs, so it looks like a flake.

**Fix.** `_text_token_ids` follows the engine's `stop_terminated` using the choice's `stop_reason` (passed through since #60251): `finish_reason == "stop"` with a non-string `stop_reason` means a token stopped generation. `None` means EOS and an int means a `stop_token_ids` entry. A string `stop_reason` (stop string) never drops a token, and neither does `include_stop_str_in_output`. As a guard, because `finish_reason` defaults to `"stop"` when a client sends neither field, the last id must actually be that stop token: equal to the int `stop_reason`, or one of the model's EOS ids (tokenizer and `generation_config`) when it is `None`. This applies at the three chat decode sites only; the ids returned to the client and to the parser are untouched.

**Relation to #59510.** #59510 (@pOpO1-9, "Hide stop text on batch derender") proposes similar helpers, aimed mainly at batch derender plus stop strings. It has had no review since Oct 7 and now conflicts with main. This PR is the minimal fix for the chat paths that are failing on main today. Completion derender and stop strings are left to #59510. If a reviewer prefers to land #59510 instead, this can be closed.

Not a duplicate otherwise: I searched open PRs for derender EOS, stop-token and `test_parity_reasoning` fixes; #59510 is the only related one.

title: [Bugfix] Include KV cache quantization settings in IPC weight cache key
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix incorrect KV scales when an engine reuses IPC-cached weights prepared with a different KV cache quantization configuration.

Related to #56049

## Claims

- Detect incompatible KV cache dtype or skipped-layer settings through the existing cache mismatch and fallback handling.
- Retain the KV cache configuration used during initial loading for subsequent standalone weight reloads.

## Validation

Added one parameterized regression test covering dtype mismatches, skipped-layer mismatches, and equivalent skipped-layer lists. It checks initial loading and standalone reloading, including after the caller's configuration is mutated.

- Before: **2 failed, 1 passed**.
- After: **9 passed, 3 deselected**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/model_executor/model_loader \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py \
  -k 'not cold_start_and_warm_restart' -q
```

GPU validation used an H800 NVL, PyTorch `2.14.0+cu130`, and a synthetic FP8 checkpoint derived from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, with BF16 activations, TP=1, eager execution, and the Torch FP8 linear backend. Three prompts were tested with greedy decoding, 32 output tokens, and prompt logprobs.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Before: `auto` daemon → `fp8` engine | Incorrectly accepted cached weights; K/V scales became `1.0` instead of `0.0250244140625`, changing generated tokens for all three prompts |
| After: mismatch, fallback disabled | Raised `CacheConfigMismatchError` naming `kv_cache_dtype` |
| After: mismatch, fallback enabled | Both `zero_copy` and `copy` matched disk loading |
| After: matching `fp8` configurations | Both modes loaded 424 cached tensors and matched disk loading |

For matching configurations and fallback loading, KV scales, generated token IDs, and prompt logprobs matched disk loading exactly. Disk-loading results were unchanged by the fix. These checks validate loading consistency for the tested FP8 path, not model accuracy or all quantization backends.

## Details

The daemon caches tensors after weight processing, which depends on the KV cache configuration. The existing fingerprint includes model quantization settings but omits the KV cache dtype and skipped layers, allowing incompatible processed scales to be reused.

Include `kv_cache_dtype` and `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` in `WeightCacheKey`. Sort and deduplicate skipped layers so equivalent lists still match.

Pass `CacheConfig` when constructing daemon and engine keys. Save a copy on models returned by the IPC loader, including disk fallback, so standalone `load_weights()` calls retain the configuration used during initial loading without requiring an active configuration context. Models without a saved configuration use the current vLLM configuration.

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Allocate producer control ports at startup
author: gty111
body:
## Overview

Avoid NIXL EC producer control-port collisions when multiple instances or DP replicas share a host, while retaining explicit endpoint configuration.

## Claims

- Allocate an OS-assigned port by default and advertise the actual bound port through `ec_transfer_params.peer_port`.
- Keep `VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST` and `VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT` overrides. A nonzero port uses `base_port + data_parallel_index`; `0` remains automatic.
- Preserve `ec_transfer_config.engine_id` in the NIXL agent name and append the DP index to distinguish replicas.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Transport and configuration validation</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_{control,data,session,scheduler_nixl_ctor,scheduler_nixl_producer,scheduler_nixl_consumer}.py -q
```

112 passed, including real ZMQ request/reply and NIXL peer registration. The updated tests reproduce ignored endpoint overrides and engine IDs before the fix. GPU serving was not rerun for this revision.

</details>

## Details

Bind port `0` directly on the serving socket and read `LAST_ENDPOINT`, avoiding a separate port-reservation race. The host defaults to `get_ip()` (honoring `VLLM_HOST_IP`); set `VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=localhost` for loopback-only binding. Wildcard addresses are rejected because peers need a reachable address.

Fixed-port conflicts fail startup rather than silently choosing another port. Independent instances using fixed ports must use non-overlapping ranges; consumers use the advertised endpoint without matching port configuration.

No equivalent open fix was found in the EC control-port search.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Remap Quark layer names for the MTP draft model
author: tpopp
body:
## Overview

Previously, `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` with MTP would fail with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1280) must match the size of tensor b (2560)`.

Remap Quark's layer names (`exclude`, `layer_quant_config`) for the Qwen4Exp MTP draft (both AMD and NVIDIA copies) so that checkpoint names (`mtp.layers.0.*`) match the draft's layer names (`mtp.layers.48.*`), the same way `ignored_layers`, `exclude_modules` and ModelOpt `quantized_layers` are already remapped (#55513) in both copies.

Related checkpoint fix:https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4/commit/89d245391842bf53fb9b0700646843c1f40de341.

**Checkpoint status:** AMD has updated `config.json` on both `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` and the `-PLEFP8` sibling with literal `mtp.layers.0.*` names only -- no catch-all regex -- matching the convention other AMD checkpoints use (e.g. `amd/Qwen3.5-397B`). Per AMD's confirmation on the checkpoint discussion linked above and the model card's own Reproduction section: without MTP, the formal `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0` release runs the checkpoint as documented; with MTP enabled, that release does not remap Quark's exclude list for the draft, so this PR is required for MTP to load at all -- this is the checkpoint as shipped, not a hypothetical variant.

## Claims

- Bug fix: with a Quark checkpoint whose `exclude` list names MTP modules by checkpoint index (the form Quark exports), BF16 MTP layers are no longer built as quantized layers.
- Per-layer Quark schemes (`layer_quant_config`) for MTP modules are applied to the draft as well.
- No functional change for the target model, for no-MTP serving, or for ModelOpt checkpoints.
- Also fixes the identical bug on the NVIDIA backend: MXFP4 has real NVIDIA-native MoE backends (FlashInfer, vLLM CUTLASS, DeepGEMM, Marlin -- not just AMD's AITER path), so a Quark-quantized checkpoint with MTP hit the same dead-exclude-list bug there. Flagged by @okorzh-amd's review; same fix, ported to `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/mtp.py`.
- Scope: entries in Quark `exclude` and keys of `layer_quant_config` that **start with** `mtp.layers.<i>.` (for `i < mtp_num_hidden_layers`) are rewritten to `mtp.layers.<mtp_start_layer_idx + i>.`; this includes globs such as `mtp.layers.0.*`. Entries that start with `re:` or `*`, and non-MTP names, are left exactly as written, matching the existing `ignored_layers`/`exclude_modules`/`quantized_layers` remaps.

## Validation

**Unit test (CPU)**

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py   # 15 passed
```

`test_qwen4_exp_mtp_remaps_quark_layer_names`, parametrized over `backend` (`amd`/`nvidia`, matching the existing `test_qwen4_exp_mtp_remaps_mixed_precision_layer_indices` convention), builds the draft config from a `QuarkConfig` and checks that MTP names in `exclude` and `layer_quant_config` shift to layer 48, non-MTP and `re:` entries are unchanged, and the checkpoint's list is not mutated. It also asserts the actual `get_quant_method_target` decision for the draft's routed experts (`UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, not the quantized MoE method), using an `exclude` fixture whose only regex entry (`re:mtp\.fc_hidden`) does not match the experts path on its own -- a broader catch-all regex would mask the bug this assertion exists to catch (see Scope above). Verified locally (and re-verified by removing the `apply_vllm_mapper` call on both backends) that the exclude-list assertion is what catches the bug: it fails cleanly without the fix and passes with it, on both backends.

**End to end (MI355X, TP2)**

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8f7` with this PR. Checkpoint `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`. GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions; acceptance length (AL) over the GSM8K run, MTP k=3. Also confirmed on NVIDIA B300: this fix resolves the identical error with similar results to the MI355X run below. B300 additionally needed an out-of-scope workaround for a separate Quark/Qwen4Exp weight-conversion gap with the CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP4 MoE backend, tracked separately and not part of this PR; the NVIDIA fix itself is also covered by the parametrized unit test above, same code path as the AMD side.

| Checkpoint `exclude` | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| exact MTP module names only (as Quark exports) | fails to load: `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1280) must match the size of tensor b (2560)` | loads; GSM8K 0.923 / 0.916; AL 3.52 (0.928 / 0.845 / 0.748) |

GSM8K is flexible-extract / strict-match (±0.007); AL per draft position in parentheses. With exact names only, the server log reports `Quark excludes shared experts at mtp.layers.48.mlp.shared_expert`, i.e. the checkpoint's `mtp.layers.0.*` entries now reach the draft.

No-MTP reference on the same setup: GSM8K 0.927 / 0.921 (flexible / strict).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --served-model-name qfn \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=qfn,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The AMD Qwen4Exp draft builds its layers as `mtp.layers.<num_hidden_layers + i>`, while checkpoints name them `mtp.layers.<i>`. `_make_draft_vllm_config` shifts the checkpoint names in `ignored_layers`, `exclude_modules` and `quantized_layers`, but `QuarkConfig` keeps its layer names inside `quant_config` (`exclude`, `layer_quant_config`), which was not touched. Every literal MTP entry there was dead for the draft, so `QuarkConfig.get_quant_method` fell through to the global scheme (MXFP4) for BF16 MTP modules.

**Fix.** Rename them through Quark's existing hook for this, `QuarkConfig.apply_vllm_mapper`, with a `WeightsMapper` prefix map `mtp.layers.<i>.` -> `mtp.layers.<num_hidden_layers + i>.`. The mapper is built in the draft rather than declared as a class-level `hf_to_vllm_mapper` because the target index depends on `num_hidden_layers`.

**Why keep the layer offset.** Qwen3-Next removed the same offset in #25079 and Qwen3.5 builds its MTP layer as `mtp.layers.{idx}` (#34110), so their checkpoint names match without a remap. Qwen4Exp's offset (introduced with the model in #53896) is now relied on: #60023 documents `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48` to keep only the MTP layer's KV cache unquantized, and that option selects layers by index; the offset also keeps index-keyed PLE layer assignment (`ple_layer_ids`) off the draft. Renumbering would change both silently, so this PR keeps the offset and completes the existing remap.

**Scope.** AMD and NVIDIA Qwen4Exp MTP drafts; Quark only.

**Related.** Not duplicated by: #49900 (strips the synthetic `draft_model.` root for draft-model drafters), #59040 (`mtp.fc` in `qwen3_5_mtp.py`).

**CI.** The unit test runs on CPU in the existing Qwen4Exp test file. The end-to-end validation above was run outside CI.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

title: [Bugfix][Bench] Aggregate DP running requests for profiling
author: qianlihuang
body:
## Overview

Fix Rust bench's deferred profiling on data-parallel servers by summing `vllm:num_requests_running` across the engine series exposed by `/metrics`.

## Claims

- DP8 with 16 running requests per engine now reports 128 to `--profile-batch-threshold`, instead of 16. A threshold of 120 can therefore be reached.
- Match the exact gauge name and read its sample value before an optional timestamp. Preserve zero versus missing metrics and clarify the aggregate threshold in CLI help.

## Validation

Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04, Rust 1.95.0. From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo test --offline --locked -p vllm-bench
cargo clippy --offline --locked -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Raw test summaries (unit tests, then CLI parity tests):

```text
test result: ok. 190 passed; 0 failed; 12 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 2.60s
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.01s
```

Four synchronous parser tests cover DP sum, exact-name matching, zero versus missing metrics, and timestamps. The original parser fails the DP sum, exact-name, and timestamp cases; all four pass after the fix. Clippy and pre-commit pass.

## Details

The previous parser returned the first matching series. vLLM exports this gauge per engine, so the profiling threshold could remain unreachable despite sufficient total concurrency. Aggregate valid samples while excluding metric names that merely share the prefix. Client-side metric parsing and help text only; no new dependencies.

The total matches the aggregate scope of `--max-concurrency`, rather than requiring a minimum batch size on each engine. With uneven DP load, profiling may start while some engines still have small batches. Only engines exposed by the target `/metrics` endpoint are counted.

Duplicate check: no matching open PR found for `fetch_num_requests_running`, `profile_batch_threshold`, or Rust DP profiling.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Treat failed secondary-tier stores as back-pressure
author: YeonghyeonKO
body:
## Overview
 
Fixes #61775. Failed primary→secondary store jobs are now reported to the tier's back-pressure detector. A storage tier that rejects writes (`ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT` on a full or over-quota filesystem) is therefore put under pressure and probed at a bounded rate, instead of receiving every cascade. Follow-up to #50045. Eviction stays external to vLLM, as maintainers have asked; see **Scope** under Details.
 
## Claims
 
- With back-pressure enabled, an `fs` tier on a full filesystem receives **13 store jobs instead of 200** over the same 4 s of cascades (real `TieringOffloadingManager` + `FileSystemTierManager` on a 512 KiB tmpfs; table below).
- After space is freed, as an external evictor such as the llm-d PVC evictor would do, the tier is used again without a restart.
- No behaviour change for tiers whose stores succeed, for tiers without back-pressure configured, or for `p2p` tiers. Failure tracking is enabled by default only for the `fs` and `obj` storage tiers.
## Validation
 
**Reproducer:** a real CPU primary tier and a real `fs` tier, created through `SecondaryTierFactory` with `{"backpressure": {"backpressure_cls": "EMABackpressureDetector"}}`. `root_dir` is on a 512 KiB tmpfs (64 KiB blocks, so 7 blocks fit). The script runs 400 cascades of one block each, 20 ms apart. Halfway through, it deletes the stored `.bin` files to simulate an external evictor.
 
| | full phase (200 cascades): submitted / succeeded / failed | after freeing space (200 cascades): submitted / succeeded | back-pressure activated |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (a9fe30e9f6) | 200 / 7 / **193** | 200 / 7 | no |
| this PR | **13** / 7 / 6 | 13 / 7 | yes |
 
On `main`, every cascade after the filesystem fills is submitted and fails with `Errno 28`. With this PR, three consecutive failures put the tier under pressure, and a probe store gets through roughly every 1–1.5 s. After space is freed, the next probe succeeds and stores resume until the filesystem is full again.
 
<details>
<summary>Reproducer script</summary>
```bash
mount -t tmpfs -o size=512k tmpfs /tmp/fullfs
PYTHONPATH=. python repro_full_fs.py /tmp/fullfs/kv 400
```
 
```python
"""Reproducer: fs secondary tier on a filesystem that runs out of space.
 
Drives a real TieringOffloadingManager + CPU primary tier + FileSystemTierManager
(created through SecondaryTierFactory with back-pressure enabled) whose root_dir
is a small tmpfs. Counts how many store jobs reach the fs tier and how many fail.
 
Usage: python repro_full_fs.py <root_dir_on_small_fs> [rounds]
"""
 
import sys
import time
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
 
from tests.v1.kv_offload.tiering.test_fs_tier import (
    _make_offloading_spec,
    _page_aligned_zero_tensor,
    key,
)
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import ReqContext, ScheduleEndContext
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.factory import SecondaryTierFactory
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.manager import (
    CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager,
    TieringOffloadingManager,
)
 
root_dir = sys.argv[1]
rounds = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 300
# Simulate an external evictor freeing space halfway through the run.
free_at = rounds // 2
num_chunks = 32
block_elements = 16 * 1024  # 64 KiB per block (float32)
 
tensor = _page_aligned_zero_tensor(num_chunks, block_elements)
region = MagicMock()
region.create_kv_memoryview.return_value = memoryview(tensor.numpy())
primary = CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager(num_chunks=num_chunks, mmap_region=region)
tier = SecondaryTierFactory.create_secondary_tier(
    {
        "type": "fs",
        "root_dir": root_dir,
        "n_read_threads": 1,
        "n_write_threads": 2,
        "backpressure": {"backpressure_cls": "EMABackpressureDetector"},
    },
    region.create_kv_memoryview(),
    _make_offloading_spec(),
)
manager = TieringOffloadingManager(primary_tier=primary, secondary_tiers=[tier])
 
submitted = 0
orig_submit = tier.submit_store
 
 
def counting_submit(job):
    global submitted
    submitted += 1
    orig_submit(job)
 
 
tier.submit_store = counting_submit
 
ok = failed = 0
orig_finished = tier.get_finished_jobs
 
 
def counting_finished():
    global ok, failed
    results = list(orig_finished())
    for r in results:
        if r.success:
            ok += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
    return results
 
 
tier.get_finished_jobs = counting_finished
 
pressure_seen = False
ok_after_free = 0
start = time.monotonic()
for i in range(rounds):
    if i == free_at:
        import glob
        import os
 
        for f in glob.glob(f"{root_dir}/**/*.bin", recursive=True):
            os.remove(f)
        ok_before_free, submitted_before_free = ok, submitted
    ctx = ReqContext(req_id=f"r{i}")
    keys = [key(i)]
    manager.on_new_request(ctx)
    assert manager.prepare_store(keys, ctx) is not None
    manager.complete_store(keys, ctx, success=True)
    tier.drain_jobs()
    manager._processed_jobs_this_step = False
    manager.on_schedule_end(ScheduleEndContext(new_req_ids=[], preempted_req_ids=()))
    pressure_seen |= tier.bp_detector.is_under_pressure()
    time.sleep(0.02)
elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
 
print(
    f"rounds={rounds} elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | full phase: "
    f"submitted={submitted_before_free} succeeded={ok_before_free} "
    f"failed={submitted_before_free - ok_before_free} | after freeing space: "
    f"submitted={submitted - submitted_before_free} "
    f"succeeded={ok - ok_before_free} | back_pressure_seen={pressure_seen}"
)
tier.shutdown()
```
 
</details>

**Tests:**
 
```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_backpressure.py   # 60 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \
  --ignore=tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py      # 719 passed, 20 skipped
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                     # all applicable hooks pass
```
 
The new tests live in `test_backpressure.py`, which already runs in CI. They are:
 
- a manager-level test: a tier whose stores fail is put under pressure, leaves the healthy fast-path, and later stores are dropped without leaving primary chunks pinned;
- detector tests: failures are ignored without a threshold, a success resets the streak, failure pressure drops every store under the default policy, pressure decays even before warmup completes, and a probe after decay either re-trips pressure or recovers;
- `default_config()` sets `failure_threshold` only for `fs` and `obj`.

**E2E serving:** 
- independently validated by @Ondre119 on an RTX 4080 SUPER (Qwen3-0.6B, real `EACCES` write failures at component and serving level): store jobs during the fault window dropped from 121 → 11, pins drained, and the tier recovered after permissions were restored; all 1,220 streaming requests completed. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61780#issuecomment-6194067763
 
## Details
 
**Root cause:** `TieringOffloadingManager._process_finished_jobs()` called `_update_backpressure()` only when `completed_job.success` was true. `EMABackpressureDetector` reacts only to store latency, but a tier that rejects writes fails fast. As a result:
 
1. no samples arrive, so the EMA never crosses the high water mark;
2. `_healthy_streak` is reset only by a slow *successful* completion, so a detector in the healthy fast-path keeps returning `True` from `should_store()` while every store fails;
3. a tier that fails from its first store never completes warmup, so pressure is never signalled.

**Fix:** 
- **Manager:** reports failed store jobs through a new `BackpressureDetector.on_store_failed()`. It is a no-op by default, so out-of-tree detectors keep working unchanged.
- **`EMABackpressureDetector`:** gains `failure_threshold: int | None = None`. When it is set:
  - any failure ends the healthy fast-path;
  - `failure_threshold` consecutive failures enter pressure and raise the EMA to `4 × high_water_s`, which makes `ThrottledDropPolicy` drop every store.
- **Recovery:** reuses the existing idle decay and cooldown. A failed probe re-enters pressure immediately, because the streak only resets on success. Failure-induced pressure may decay before warmup completes.
- **Defaults:** `default_config()` sets `failure_threshold=3` for `fs` and `obj`.
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    Healthy: Healthy fast-path (policy bypassed)
    Normal: Normal (policy consulted)
    Pressure: Under pressure (stores dropped)
    Healthy --> Normal: slow completion, or any store failure (new)
    Normal --> Healthy: 10 fast completions
    Normal --> Pressure: EMA above high water, or N consecutive failures (new)
    Pressure --> Normal: idle decay below low water, probe stores resume
```
 
**Scope: eviction stays external; write admission stays in vLLM**
 
This PR follows the existing ownership split for storage tiers and does not move eviction into vLLM:
 
> "I think that for storage, especially for shared storage, but maybe even for local, eviction should be managed outside of vLLM." (@orozery, #38260)
 
> "To date we chose to do evictions externally to vllm [...] If we do decide on a clean up mechanism in vllm it should also handle evictions." (@dannyharnik, #54363)
 
Nothing here deletes, scans or sizes files. Freeing space remains the job of the external evictor, such as the llm-d PVC evictor. What this PR fixes is the other half of that contract: **whether vLLM keeps submitting writes to a tier that is rejecting them.** That decision can only be made inside vLLM:
 
- **The failures are only visible to vLLM.** Only vLLM observes its own store results. An external evictor sees disk usage, not `ENOSPC` returned to vLLM's I/O threads, and it has no way to slow vLLM down.
- **The external side is soft by design.** Its thresholds are soft, so the volume can reach 100% before space is freed (llm-d/llm-d-kv-cache#218). Without this change, vLLM spends that whole window failing every cascade against a full volume.
- **Admission is already vLLM's job.** #50045 put write admission for secondary tiers in vLLM, and #51240 / #53485 build on that. This PR only feeds the missing signal, failed stores, into that existing mechanism. Recovery is driven by the evictor freeing space: the next probe store succeeds and stores resume, with no coordination between the two sides.
**Tradeoffs and limitations:**
 
- **`p2p` is excluded.** A failed `p2p` store means a consumer never fetched the blocks (unbound or reaped batches), not that the tier is unhealthy. Dropping `p2p` stores was also a concern in the #50045 review. Users can still set `failure_threshold` explicitly for any tier.
- **Bursts after recovery.** While pressure is decaying, up to a scheduler step's worth of stores can be admitted before the next failure is observed. This is bounded by the existing cooldown. In the reproducer it amounted to a few jobs per probe window.
- **Errno is not distinguished yet.** Errno classification (#54363 item 4) would let a future change treat only `ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT` as pressure. The tier pool currently reports only a bool.
- **Admission-policy consolidation.** If #53485 / #51240 / #51576 replaces the detector with `CascadeBackpressurePolicy`, the same signal can move to its `on_completed` hook. I'm happy to port it.
**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs and issues for failed-store and back-pressure work (`kv_offload` back-pressure, `ENOSPC`, `failed store`, #50045 follow-ups). #52838 drops failed GPU↔CPU transfers but does not feed back-pressure. #53485, #51240 and #51576 cover latency-based admission only. #54363 lists tier health as out of scope.

title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Move 1-byte expert tensors as uint8 views
author: luoyuctl
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51567.

When EPLB is enabled, expert tensors whose dtype NCCL does not support make engine startup fail. MXFP4 and MXFP8 experts store block scales as `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`. ROCm AITER MXFP4 also views expert weights as `torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2`. Neither dtype exists in NCCL or RCCL.

I hit this with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash using MXFP4 experts (Humming MoE backend), TP8 + EP + EPLB, on 8x H20. The crash happens in the first rearrange during memory profiling.

With `communicator=torch_nccl`:

```text
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/eplb_utils.py", line 126, in step
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py", line 580, in step
...
File "torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py", line 4280, in all_gather
    work = group.allgather([tensor_list], [tensor], opts)
TypeError: Input tensor data type is not supported for NCCL process group: Float8_e8m0fnu
```

With `communicator=pynccl`:

```text
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py", line 756, in create_eplb_communicator
    return _create_pynccl()
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py", line 693, in _create_pynccl
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: EPLB communicator 'pynccl' requested but expert weights contain unsupported dtypes: (torch.float8_e8m0fnu).
```

## When this triggers

The bug is not tied to a specific model architecture. It depends on the dtype that the MoE backend leaves in the expert parameters after weight post-processing. Startup fails when all of these hold:

1. EPLB is enabled (`--enable-eplb`, with EP).
2. The experts use MX quantization (MXFP4/MXFP8 with E8M0 block scales).
3. After post-processing, the backend stores an expert tensor in a 1-byte dtype that NCCL/RCCL does not support. For example:
   - Marlin MXFP4 MoE: `mxfp4_marlin_process_scales()` returns scales as `float8_e8m0fnu`.
   - ROCm AITER MXFP4: expert weights are viewed as `float4_e2m1fn_x2` (`oracle/mxfp4.py`).
   - Humming MXFP4 (my repro): scales are stored as `float8_e8m0fnu`.

   Backends that keep these tensors as `uint8` are not affected.
4. The tensor is returned by `get_expert_weights()`, so it is registered for EPLB transport.

Converting at load time is not enough. DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 loaders already view checkpoint E8M0 scales as `uint8`, but the backend's kernel-format conversion writes `float8_e8m0fnu` back into the parameter. The fix therefore belongs where the tensors are registered for EPLB, not in individual loaders or backends.

## Root cause

EPLB treats expert tensors as opaque payload. It only sends, receives, and all-gathers them, and never reduces them. However, it passes their numeric dtype straight to the communicator. On the first rearrange (the dummy all-gather during `determine_available_memory`), the communicator has to map that dtype to an NCCL dtype. NCCL only supports `int8/uint8/int32/int64/fp16/fp32/fp64/bf16` and FP8 E4M3/E5M2, so the mapping fails:

- `torch_nccl` raises `TypeError` inside `all_gather`.
- `pynccl` rejects the dtype earlier, when the communicator is created.

## Fix

EPLB only copies expert bytes between ranks. It never reduces them, so the numeric dtype does not matter to the transport. In `MixtureOfExperts.set_eplb_state()`, every 1-byte expert tensor is now registered as `w.view(torch.uint8)`:

- The view keeps the shape, stride, and storage, so a rearrange writes directly into the parameter that the kernels read in the original dtype.
- Applying the view at this registration point covers `FusedMoE` layers, models with their own `get_expert_weights()` (for example DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE), and elastic EP re-registration.
- 1-byte dtypes that NCCL already supports (`int8`, `uint8`, `float8_e4m3fn`) move the same bytes as before.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k byte_dtypes -v
pre-commit run --files tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py
```

## Test Result

**Unit test:** the new test is parametrized over `float8_e8m0fnu` and `float4_e2m1fn_x2`. Both cases pass with this change and fail on `main`. pre-commit (ruff, mypy) passes.

**MXFP4 deployment with EPLB (8x H20, SM90):** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with MXFP4 experts, Humming MoE backend (`HummingIndexedExperts`), TP8 + EP + EPLB (sync, `pynccl`, 16 redundant experts, `step_interval=1500`). The image is `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` with this PR's diff applied to `interfaces.py`. On this setup, startup previously failed with the tracebacks above.

- Startup: the profile rearrange passes and the server starts.
  ```text
  Rearranging experts sync mode (profile)...
  Rearranged experts  (profile)  in 2.30 s.
  Application startup complete.
  ```
- Real rearranges: three ran during the GSM8K run below. The first took 6.64 s and the next two took 0.27 s each. Balancedness was about 0.70 before the first rearrange and 0.82 to 0.87 after.
- Accuracy across rearranges (GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot chat, concurrency 32): flex-extract 89.92% ± 0.83 (1186/1319). This matches our production deployment of the same model without EPLB (90.1%). All 8 smoke prompts were also answered correctly.
- None of the 8 ranks logged `Traceback`, `Float8_e8m0fnu`, `unsupported dtypes`, or `TypeError`.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Validate draft-token capacity in forward benchmark
author: znzryb
body:
## Overview

Validate draft-token capacity in `vllm bench forward` before preparing a case's inputs. Fixes #61766: a verify case requiring three draft tokens currently reaches CUDA execution even when the runner has zero draft capacity.

## Claims

- Reject cases whose draft count exceeds the runner's resolved `num_speculative_steps`, with a case-specific `ValueError` and a `--speculative-config` hint.
- Preserve execution for ordinary decode and verify cases with sufficient capacity.
- Cover missing and insufficient capacity in the existing benchmark test suite, and document the requirement in the microbenchmark skill.

## Validation

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selected benchmark regression tests | 2 failed, 2 passed | 4 passed, 1 deselected |
| L4: `verify=2*4@64:3`, no speculative config | CUDA illegal memory access | Expected `ValueError`, no illegal memory access |
| L4: `decode=2*1@64` | Passed | Passed |
| L4: same verify, configured draft capacity 3 | Passed | Passed |

The patched GPU controls use the same publicly exported random Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint. Both successful cases have finite, deterministic outputs and graph-versus-eager relative RMS difference 0. These are correctness smoke checks, not model-quality or performance measurements.

The existing model-dependent pytest end-to-end case was deselected; three separate benchmark CLI runs provided GPU coverage. New tests live in `tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py`, already included in the Buildkite benchmarks CLI job.

Commands executed (validation scripts are in the separate archive branch):

```bash
UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-audit-uv-cache uv run --no-project --python 3.12 \
  --with 'modal[api-proxy-support]' --with huggingface_hub \
  modal run reproductions/forward-verify-2026-10-15/validate_modal.py::check \
  --model-revision 4bae0ac45199180f8d59d05bb3b6cc1b19c58357

UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-audit-uv-cache PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/vllm-audit-precommit \
  uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with pre-commit \
  pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py .agents/skills/model-microbenchmark/SKILL.md
```

Pre-commit passed, including Ruff, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, and skill validation.

Environment: one NVIDIA L4 on Modal, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Python source at `c5f8adc0b1944b9142a31d85cfbc6a61973d0b3a` was overlaid on compiled extensions and generated wrappers from an official vLLM image reporting `0.32.0rc1.dev100+g77154ca61`. This is composite source/runtime validation, not a full build from that source commit. Source/runtime provenance is recorded separately in the archive.

- [Scripts, original logs, synthetic inputs, and validation receipts](https://github.com/znzryb/vllm/tree/contribution-rules-and-bug-audit/reproductions/forward-verify-2026-10-15)
- [Public random checkpoint, pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/znzryb/qwen3-0.6b-dummy-forward-repro/tree/4bae0ac45199180f8d59d05bb3b6cc1b19c58357)
- [Public raw data and validation logs, pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/datasets/znzryb/vllm-forward-verify-repro/tree/239159c4fdaaf568fe9c00153cbfbf57ab1bf8bc)

## Details

The benchmark builds scheduler inputs directly. Without speculative configuration, the observed runner has `num_speculative_steps=0` and a draft-token buffer of shape `[4, 0]`, yet the verify case schedules three draft tokens per request. The missing consistency check lets this invalid combination enter GPU input preparation. CUDA errors are asynchronous; no exact faulting kernel is claimed.

The guard runs at the start of `run_case`, before batch construction and input preparation, using resolved runner capacity rather than requiring a particular CLI configuration. Engine initialization still precedes the check. This is benchmark configuration validation; it does not change a CUDA kernel or repair computation under a valid configuration.

Duplicate checks: read #61766 and searched open PRs for the issue number and `bench forward`. No overlapping fix was found. #61692 adds profiling, not draft-capacity validation. The three affected files are unchanged on the latest upstream main checked before submission.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, reproduction scripts, and executing the reported checks. The human submitter reviewed the proposed change in the associated discussion and authorized submission; the test executions reported here were performed by the agent.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Apertus streaming scientific notation
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix corrupted scientific-notation arguments in Apertus streaming tool calls.

## Details

The parser could emit incomplete numbers before receiving their exponents. Since streamed arguments cannot be retracted, a value such as `-2e-3` could produce invalid arguments like `-20.002`.

Exclude `Allow.NUM` during incremental parsing to avoid emitting incomplete numeric values. Final parsing and incremental string streaming remain unchanged.

Numbers may be delayed until a terminating delimiter arrives.

## Validation

Added three regression cases covering positive and negative exponents, including numbers inside arrays.

- Before: **3 failed**.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Stop declaring the MXFP4 MoE intermediate padding to AITER
author: PerryZhang01
body:
## Purpose

The AMD CI job `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` goes red intermittently with

```
AssertionError: (0, 1, (973, 973), 'residual', nan)
```

(e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94971). The NaN comes from AITER, on
vLLM's ordinary MoE path, not from the mono kernels the test compares against.

AITER's a8w4 MoE (FP8 activations x MXFP4 weights) allocates several scratch
buffers with `torch.empty`, sized for the padded sorted length, and reads them
where the producing kernel never wrote. In FP8/E8M0 a garbage `0xFF` byte is
NaN, so a whole token row of the output comes back NaN. It only happens with a
non-zero `intermediate_pad`, at decode-sized batches, after larger calls have
run in the same process — which is why it shows up as a flaky decode failure.
Root cause, a standalone repro and a fix are filed upstream:

- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/6565
- https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6568

## This change

Stop declaring `intermediate_pad` to AITER on the MXFP4 path. It is redundant
there, and dropping it keeps the call off the buggy AITER path.

Why it is redundant — the padded region is zero at the point AITER sees it, and
stays zero through every step between allocation and the kernel call:

| step | padded region | where |
|---|---|---|
| allocation | `torch.zeros` for `w13`/`w2`, their scales and `w13_bias`/`w2_bias`, at the **padded** intermediate size | `Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` |
| checkpoint load | the destination is narrowed to the loaded shard before the copy, so the padded rows are never written — this is deliberate, the helper is named for it and its docstring calls out "padding ... on the shard (intermediate) dimension (e.g. for MXFP4 GEMM)" | `RoutedExperts._narrow_expert_data_for_padding`, used by `_load_w13` / `_load_w2` right before `expert_data.copy_()` |
| weight shuffle | pure `view` + `permute` (asserts `N % 16 == 0`, `K % 32 == 0`, no re-padding), so zeros stay zeros | `aiter.ops.shuffle.shuffle_weight` |
| scale shuffle | re-pads the scale to 256 rows / 8 cols, but fills the pad with `0x7F` (E8M0 = 1.0) before copying, so it is never garbage | `aiter.utility.fp4_utils.e8m0_shuffle` |

So for the padded columns the kernel computes

- stage 1: `x @ 0 = 0` (gate and up are both zero there, and the bias is zero,
  so the activation output is exactly `silu(0) * 0 = 0`)
- stage 2: `0 @ 0 = 0`

Exact zeros also mean the padded columns cannot disturb the stage-2 activation
quantization: `amax` over an MX group is unaffected by zeros, whether or not a
group straddles real and padded columns.

Two things are deliberately left alone:

- **`hidden_pad`** — the activation columns it covers are not guaranteed to be
  zero, so dropping it would not be equivalent.
- **SITU** (`activation == MoEActivation.SITU`, the a16w4 FlyDSL port used by
  Kimi K3) — that kernel consumes the pad. The surrounding code already skips
  the rounding for it ("SITU's A16W4 FlyDSL kernel pads per gate/up half; pass
  through unrounded"), and on that path AITER keys its own scratch
  initialization on the value: `_alloc = torch.zeros if inter_dim_pad > 0 else
  torch.empty` in `aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`. Zeroing the declaration
  there would *remove* an initialization that is currently happening, which is
  the opposite of what this PR is for.

This is a workaround and should be reverted once the AITER fix is merged and
pinned. The surrounding code already carries a similar TODO about AITER padding
behaviour.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, stock AITER 0.1.25 — i.e. **without** the
AITER-side fix — running `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` unmodified,
each run covering TP2 and TP4:

| build | runs | cells | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| exactly this patch | 4 | 8 | **all passed** |
| same logic, earlier iterations of the comment/wording | 10 | 20 | **all passed** |

14 runs, 28 cells, no NaN. Before the change the same test failed intermittently
— locally about 2 runs in 6 — so 14 clean runs is about 0.3% likely if the
change did nothing.

Overhead: none measurable. Timing the same shape with and without the
declaration (median over 6 rounds, per `fused_moe_2stages` call):

| M | declared | not declared |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.139 ms | 0.141 ms |
| 4 | 0.156 ms | 0.158 ms |
| 1439 | 0.534 ms | 0.536 ms |
| 16384 | 2.010 ms | 2.010 ms |

All within run-to-run noise (~4%).

## Scope and limits

- Validated on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 (`model_dim=5120`, per-rank
  intermediate 576 padded to 640, E=384, topk=6). Other MXFP4 models on this
  path (e.g. gpt-oss with INTERLEAVE) are covered by the same zero-fill
  argument but were not run here, so reviewers may prefer a narrower gate.
- The zero-fill chain above is established from the code, with the citations in
  the table. It is not confirmed by a run against a real MXFP4 checkpoint that
  actually has padding: the test that exercises this path uses a random-weight
  loader which also zero-fills the padding, and every MXFP4 checkpoint we have
  locally has `moe_intermediate_size = 2048`, which is already aligned per rank
  (pad = 0). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (2304) is the one that pads, and the local copy
  of it is FP8 rather than MXFP4.
- Models whose per-rank intermediate size is already 128-aligned get
  `intermediate_pad == 0` and are unaffected either way.
- The `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4` opt-in is a sub-case of
  `use_mxfp4_w4a16`, so it is covered by this change as well. The same
  zero-fill argument applies to it, but it runs different kernels and was not
  exercised here.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject Cohere REQUIRED tool choice without tools
author: KuanJia
body:
## Overview

Reject Cohere Chat v2 requests that select `tool_choice="REQUIRED"` without a nonempty tools list, as required by the [Cohere specification](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat). Both chat and render endpoints now return a Cohere-shaped HTTP 400 before downstream processing.

## Claims

- Reject omitted, null and empty `tools` when tool choice is REQUIRED.
- Preserve valid required-tool requests and existing behavior for NONE or unspecified tool choice.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_conversion.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/cohere -q

git diff --check
```

- **172 passed** on upstream base `9cede34a6`, including 7 new regression/compatibility scenarios.
- HTTP tests exercise the real routes, vLLM exception handlers and Cohere error-envelope middleware without an engine. They verify rejection before either handler is reached. Existing conversion tests cover valid REQUIRED requests with tools.
- Ruff lint and format checks passed for the three changed Python files; `git diff --check` passed. Existing Buildkite entrypoint jobs run the Cohere test directory.
- Validation runs on CPU without model weights and covers request parsing, HTTP error handling and conversion. No model-generation or accuracy evaluation was run.

## Details

The Cohere request model checks the tool-choice enum but lacks cross-field validation. Conversion constructs a shared `ChatCompletionRequest` before assigning tools and tool choice, bypassing its construction-time invariant. With no tools, rendering parameters then discard the requested tool choice. Add the check to the Cohere request model using the existing `VLLMValidationError` path.

Minimal baseline reproduction, without model weights:

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.cohere.protocol import CohereChatV2Request

CohereChatV2Request(
    model="m",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Use a tool."}],
    tool_choice="REQUIRED",
)
```

Upstream `9cede34a6` accepts this input, converts the choice to `"required"`, and then produces rendering parameters with `tool_choice=None`. This change raises `VLLMValidationError(parameter="tool_choice")` during request parsing. The same before/after behavior was verified for explicit null and empty tools.

Searches of open, closed and merged PRs on 2026-10-15 found no matching fix. Related [#52467](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52467) standardizes existing validation errors, [#60309](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60309) maps handler exceptions to client error responses, and [#60586](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60586) fixes JSON-schema forwarding; none adds this cross-field validation.

title: [BugFix][MyPy] Guard Linux-only mmap/fadvise calls with sys.platform
author: wentian-byte
body:
## Purpose

`mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE`, `os.posix_fadvise` and `os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` are
Linux-only. On macOS, mypy fails with:

```text
vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:923: error: Module has no attribute "posix_fadvise"  [attr-defined]
vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:923: error: Module has no attribute "POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED"  [attr-defined]
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py:911: error: Module has no attribute "MADV_HUGEPAGE"  [attr-defined]
```

At runtime the same lines raise `AttributeError`, which the surrounding
`except OSError` does not catch.

This PR adds a `sys.platform != "linux"` early return so that non-Linux
platforms take the existing fallbacks:

- `_allocate_huge_page_storage` returns `None`, so the caller falls back to
  pinned memory.
- `drop_checkpoint_cache` skips page-cache eviction.

mypy understands `sys.platform` checks, so the Linux-only code is no longer
type-checked on macOS. This follows the same approach as #41465.

Both call sites were introduced in #56926.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs for `posix_fadvise`, `MADV_HUGEPAGE` and `mypy sys.platform`.
None of the open PRs guards these calls or fixes the macOS mypy errors.

## Test Plan

On macOS (darwin, arm64):

```bash
pre-commit run mypy --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py
```

## Test Result

- Before: mypy reports the 3 `attr-defined` errors above.
- After: `Success: no issues found in 2 source files`. All other pre-commit
  hooks pass.

There is no behavior change on Linux, so model evaluation is not applicable.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance. A human submitter reviewed every
changed line and ran the commands above.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep the parser's tool call IDs in batch derender
author: hickeyma
body:
## Overview

Batch `/v1/chat/completions/derender` now keeps the parser's tool call IDs, the same as `/v1/chat/completions` and streaming derender. Part of #42729.

## Claims

- Batch derender uses `tc.id or make_tool_call_id()` in place of a bare `random_uuid()`. Default IDs get their `chatcmpl-tool-` prefix back and Kimi K2 style `functions.<name>:<idx>` IDs come through unchanged.
- The batch parity test compares tool call ID formats as well as names and arguments. It also gives derender the engine's `finish_reason` instead of the coupled one, so derender has to apply the `tool_calls` rewrite itself.

## Validation

New unit tests in `test_derender.py`. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change:

- `test_derender_chat_tool_call_id_matches_chat_completion`: real hermes parser, checks the ID starts with `chatcmpl-tool-`.
- `test_derender_chat_keeps_parser_tool_call_id`: a stub parser returns `functions.get_weather:1` and the test checks it's kept.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py -v
```

No model eval. The change only affects tool call IDs, not generated text.

## Details

Batch derender threw away the ID the parser had already built. Chat templates for Kimi-style models reference these IDs in multi-turn history, so a bare UUID breaks follow up turns. It also meant batch and streaming derender returned different IDs for the same tokens.

The parity test missed this because `_tool_sig` only looks at names and arguments. It also fed derender the coupled server's `finish_reason` which already had the `tool_calls` rewrite applied, so derender never had to work it out. #59324 shares `resolve_finish_reason()` between chat and derender, so the test can now pass the engine's value.

The current batch tool cases use a named `tool_choice` which never rewrites to `tool_calls`. So the `finish_reason` change mostly guards future auto tool cases.

This matters for #56851 too. The planned `parse_context` carries `history_tool_call_cnt` for Kimi IDs and that field does nothing while batch derender overwrites the IDs.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Honor a prompt-closed reasoning block in non-streaming parse and reasoning token counts
author: albertoperdomo2
body:
## Overview

With GLM-5.3 and `continue_final_message`, non-streaming Chat Completions return the continued answer as `reasoning` with `content: null`, and both streaming and non-streaming count every generated token as a reasoning token. This PR makes non-streaming parsing and `count_reasoning_tokens()` honor a prompt that already closes reasoning, as streaming `parse_delta()` already does.

## Design

Thanks to @bbrowning for catching that an earlier version leaked multi-turn reasoning into `content` for legacy parsers like `deepseek_r1`, and for suggesting moving the fix onto `ParserEngine`. This version follows his outline:

- `ParserEngine.set_prompt_token_ids()` uses the engine's turn-aware `is_reasoning_end` to start the parse in `CONTENT` when the prompt already closes reasoning. The engine's reasoning token count uses the same starting state.
- `ReasoningParser` gets a no-op `set_prompt_token_ids()`, so legacy reasoning parsers behave exactly as on `main`. `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter` and `DelegatingParser` pass the prompt through.
- The engine only uses the prompt when its config starts in `REASONING` and declares `turn_boundary_tokens`; without turn boundaries, a previous turn's `</think>` would count as closing reasoning in the new turn.

## Claims

- Non-streaming returns the continuation as `content` instead of `reasoning` when the prompt already closes reasoning.
- `reasoning_tokens` is 0 in that case, on both streaming and non-streaming. Before, it was the whole output (17 tokens in the example below).
- Normal reasoning turns are unchanged, and a previous turn's `</think>` doesn't count as closing reasoning in the new turn.

## Validation

**Dummy Reproduction** (CPU only) parser level:

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.parser_manager import ParserManager
from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer

tok = get_tokenizer("zai-org/GLM-5.3")
msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "Count from 1 to 10 separated by commas."},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "1, 2, 3, 4,"}]
prompt = tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False,
                                 continue_final_message=True)
prompt_ids = tok.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)
out = " 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10"
out_ids = tok.encode(out, add_special_tokens=False)
req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=msgs, add_generation_prompt=False,
                            continue_final_message=True)
parser_cls = ParserManager.get_parser(tool_parser_name="glm47", reasoning_parser_name="glm45",
                                      enable_auto_tools=True, tokenizer=tok)
print("prompt tail :", repr(prompt[-44:]))
print("model output:", repr(out))

# non-streaming, as chat_completion/serving.py does it
p = parser_cls(tok, None, chat_template_kwargs={}, model_config=None)
p.set_prompt_token_ids(prompt_ids)
reasoning, content, _ = p.parse(out, req, enable_auto_tools=True, model_output_token_ids=out_ids)
print(f"non-stream  reasoning={reasoning!r}  content={content!r}  "
      f"reasoning_tokens={p.count_reasoning_tokens(out_ids)}")

# streaming, one token at a time
p = parser_cls(tok, None, chat_template_kwargs={}, model_config=None)
r = c = ""
for i, t in enumerate(out_ids):
    d = p.parse_delta(tok.decode([t]), [t], req, prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids,
                      finished=i == len(out_ids) - 1)
    if d:
        r += d.reasoning or ""
        c += d.content or ""
print(f"stream      reasoning={(r or None)!r}  content={(c or None)!r}  "
      f"reasoning_tokens={p.count_reasoning_tokens(out_ids)}")
```

**Before** (`main` at `3dcfaeb4e8`, this branch's base):

```
prompt tail : 'mmas.<|assistant|><think></think>1, 2, 3, 4,'
model output: ' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'
non-stream  reasoning=' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'  content=None  reasoning_tokens=17
stream      reasoning=None  content=' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'  reasoning_tokens=17
```

**After** (this PR):

```
prompt tail : 'mmas.<|assistant|><think></think>1, 2, 3, 4,'
model output: ' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'
non-stream  reasoning=None  content=' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'  reasoning_tokens=0
stream      reasoning=None  content=' 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10'  reasoning_tokens=0
```

The "before" output matches what we saw in production on GLM-5.3: the API returned the continuation in `reasoning_content` with `content: null` and `reasoning_tokens: 17`.

Claude Code used to build up the test cases and validate the logic.

title: [Bugfix] Make Humming DeviceInfo lookups traceable under torch.compile
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Fixes vllm-project/humming#147 for vLLM: models served through Humming fail torch.compile with `RecursionError` whenever Humming's forward path quantizes or Hadamard-transforms activations (seen during warmup of MXFP4 MoE checkpoints on H200). This patches Humming from the `vllm.utils.humming` facade so the pinned `humming-kernels==0.1.17` works for v0.32.0.

## Claims

- torch.compile (`fullgraph=True`) works again on Humming forward paths that run `may_process_input` (input quantization, Hadamard): no `RecursionError`, no Dynamo `Unsupported`.
- Works with the currently pinned humming 0.1.17. The upstream fix (vllm-project/humming#148, in the upcoming 0.1.18) is **not sufficient on its own** for vLLM (see Details).
- No behavior change in eager mode, apart from no longer re-querying device properties on every forward call.

## Validation

B300 (SM103), this branch on main with `humming-kernels[cu13]==0.1.17`:

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| New `tests/quantization/test_humming_compile.py` | `RecursionError` | passed |
| E2E: Qwen3-0.6B, `--quantization humming`, int6 weights + Hadamard + int8 activations, torch.compile + CUDA graphs | `RecursionError` at engine init | correct output ("Paris, and the capital of Italy is Rome…") |
| Same E2E with only the #148 `__getattr__` fix backported (on 0.1.16) | — | `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported` on `_DeviceInfo.__new__` |
| Standalone repro from humming#147 (`copy.copy`, `torch.compile`, `fullgraph=True`) | `RecursionError` | OK |

```bash
VLLM_HUMMING_ONLINE_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int6","hadamard_block_size":-1}' \
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}' \
  python -c 'from vllm import LLM; print(LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", quantization="humming").generate("The capital of France is"))'
```

Regression tests (same setup): `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py tests/kernels/core/test_activation.py tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py tests/model_executor/test_utils.py -k humming` → 194 passed.

Not run locally on Hopper. The new test runs in the H200 Quantization CI step, and I added `vllm/utils/humming.py` to that step's trigger paths. Note the existing Humming lm-eval configs all use `--enforce-eager`, which is why CI never caught this.

## Details

**Root cause.** On every call, `LayerConfig.check_device` and the PDL heuristics (`_resolve_use_pdl` → `get_heuristics_class`) build a new `humming.device.DeviceInfo(device)`. vLLM traces these from `may_process_input` inside its fullgraph-compiled region. Two problems stack up:
1. `DeviceInfo` has `__slots__` and a catch-all `__getattr__`. When Dynamo creates the instance, it reads the unset `_value` slot, which re-enters `__getattr__` and recurses forever. humming#148 fixes this by raising `AttributeError` for private names.
2. With (1) fixed, Dynamo still can't trace the pybind `_DeviceInfo(index)` constructor, so fullgraph compile fails with `Unsupported`. Reading attributes from an extension object that already exists does trace fine; that's why the module-global `current_device` already works under compile. Humming main still has these per-call constructions, so 0.1.18 alone would still break vLLM.

**Fix.** On first use of the facade, `_patch_humming()`:
- backports the #148 `__getattr__` change (also fixes `copy.copy(DeviceInfo)`), and
- replaces the `DeviceInfo` name in the five Humming modules that call it (`config.config`, `transform`, `tune`, `tune.process_input`, `utils.smem`) with a factory that returns one cached instance per device index. `prepare_layer_config` populates the cache eagerly during weight processing, so at trace time Dynamo only sees a dict lookup on an existing object.

All vLLM Humming access goes through the lazy facade, so the patch is always applied before any layer is prepared. The swap is skipped for any module whose `DeviceInfo` is no longer Humming's class. `DeviceInfo` only exposes static device properties, so caching it is safe.

**Follow-up.** This should be removed once Humming's `DeviceInfo` can be constructed in traced code (for example, by caching inside Humming itself); there's a TODO. I'll raise this on the Humming side so 0.1.18+ can drop the patch.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Fix HTTP 500 from max_tokens_per_doc when the query…
author: hoaivoke
body:
## Overview

**TL;DR:** On BERT-style cross-encoders, `/rerank`, `/score` and `LLM.score` return HTTP 500 when `max_tokens_per_doc` is set and the query alone fills the token limit. This falls back to the usual truncation in that case.

No existing issue or PR covers this. #60877 edits the same file but not this code.

## Claims

These requests no longer fail with HTTP 500:
- `truncate_prompt_tokens` below the query length plus special tokens, with or without an empty document. They now get the usual truncation, as without `max_tokens_per_doc`.
- A query longer than `max_model_len` without truncation. It now gets the usual 400 "maximum context length" error.

Requests that work today produce the same tokens.

## Validation

`vllm serve cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` on a T4. The query is a passage (as in "find similar"), with `max_tokens_per_doc=8`:

| Request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `truncate_prompt_tokens=16` | 500 | 200 |
| same, plus an empty document | 500 | 200 |
| 600-token query, no truncation | 500 | 400 "maximum context length" |

On main all three fail with `Truncation error: Sequence to truncate too short to respect the provided max_length`. With the fix, the relevant document still ranks first.

Tests, main → this PR:
- `tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py`: 10 → 14 passed. The 4 new tests are listed below; 3 of them fail on main.
- `test_cross_encoder_online.py` 20/20, `test_cross_encoder_offline.py` 6/6, `tests/models/language/pooling/test_max_tokens_per_doc.py` 20/20, on both.

Also compared the preprocessing on main and this branch over 18,360 combinations of query and document length and both limits. Only the 2,250 that failed on main changed, and none of them goes over either limit.

## Details

**Root cause.** With `max_tokens_per_doc`, `get_score_prompt` encodes the pair with `truncation="only_second"`. That can only shorten the document, so the tokenizer raises when query + special tokens already reach `max_length`.

**Fix.** Use `only_second` only when the query leaves room for at least one document token. Otherwise the existing `truncation=True` arguments apply. The document is already cut to `max_tokens_per_doc` as text before encoding, so that limit still holds.

**Trade-off.** In the fallback the query is shortened. This can't be avoided when the query alone fills the limit, and it's what `truncate_prompt_tokens` already does without a document limit.

**New tests**, using a toy BERT-style tokenizer:
- When the query fits, only the document is cut. This passes on main too.
- When the query fills the limit, the usual truncation applies, for a normal and an empty document.
- A query that is too long without truncation gets the usual validation error.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Detokenize echoed prompts after truncation
author: cycancode
body:
## Overview

`/v1/completions` with `echo=true` and `truncate_prompt_tokens` echoes the full, untruncated prompt for token-ID prompts, although the engine only sees the truncated tokens. The renderer detokenizes the prompt before `apply_post_tokenization` truncates it; this PR detokenizes after truncation instead, restoring the behavior from before the renderer refactor.

## Claims

- For token-ID prompts, the echoed `text` is now the decode of the tokens that reach the engine, so it agrees with `usage.prompt_tokens`, `logprobs.tokens` and `logprobs.text_offset`.
- Fixed for both truncation sides, and for streaming and non-streaming responses (both read `RequestOutput.prompt`).
- No change for text prompts, chat `echo`, or `/detokenize`.

## Validation

Real server on `a9fe30e9f6` (Qwen3-0.6B, RTX 4090, `--enforce-eager`), before and after the fix. Request: token IDs of `"one two three four five six seven eight"` (8 tokens) with `echo=true, max_tokens=1, logprobs=0, truncate_prompt_tokens=4`. `usage.prompt_tokens` is 4 in every case.

| `truncation_side` | Echoed `text` before | Echoed `text` after | `text_offset` indexes `text` correctly (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| unset (tokenizer default, left) | `one two three four five six seven eight com` | ` five six seven eight com` | no (`text[0:5] == "one t"` for token `" five"`) → yes |
| `left` | `one two three four five six seven eight com` | ` five six seven eight com` | no → yes |
| `right` | `one two three four five six seven eight five` | `one two three four five` | yes, but `text` contains 4 prompt tokens the model never saw → yes |

Tests:

- New `tests/renderers/test_completions.py::TestRenderPrompt::test_detokenization_matches_truncated_tokens` covers the sync and async paths with left and right truncation. It fails on `main` (the echoed prompt contains all 10 tokens) and passes with the fix.
- `pytest tests/renderers`: 632 passed. The 3 failures in `test_hf.py` need gated Hugging Face repos (`meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-1B`, `fixie-ai/ultravox-v0_5-llama-3_2-1b`, `google/paligemma-3b-mix-224`) that my machine has no access to.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -k "echo or truncation or single_completion or prompt_logprobs or batch_completions"`: 9 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, including mypy.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8011 --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager
python repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8011
```

```python
import sys

import requests

BASE = sys.argv[1]
model = requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1/models").json()["data"][0]["id"]
ids = requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/tokenize",
    json={"model": model, "prompt": "one two three four five six seven eight",
          "add_special_tokens": False},
).json()["tokens"]

for side in (None, "left", "right"):
    body = {"model": model, "prompt": ids, "echo": True, "max_tokens": 1,
            "temperature": 0, "logprobs": 0, "truncate_prompt_tokens": 4}
    if side:
        body["truncation_side"] = side
    choice = requests.post(f"{BASE}/v1/completions", json=body).json()["choices"][0]
    lp = choice["logprobs"]
    spans = [choice["text"][o:o + len(t)] for o, t in zip(lp["text_offset"], lp["tokens"])]
    print(side, repr(choice["text"]), "offsets consistent:", spans == lp["tokens"])
```

</details>

## Details

Root cause: in `BaseRenderer._tokenize_singleton_prompt` and its async twin, `needs_detokenization` decoded `prompt_token_ids` before `TokenizeParams.apply_post_tokenization` applied `truncate_prompt_tokens`, so `prompt` described the original token list while `prompt_token_ids` was truncated. `needs_detokenization` is only set for completions/chat `echo` (without `return_token_ids`) and `/detokenize`. Before the renderer refactor, `OpenAIServing._normalize_prompt_tokens_to_input` truncated first and decoded the truncated IDs (see `v0.10.1`).

Limitation: text prompts keep echoing the original string, as they did in `v0.10.1` (the Rust frontend also echoes the request prompt). Aligning that would need the renderer to know whether tokenizer-side truncation actually dropped tokens; I left it out to keep this fix small, and can follow up if maintainers want it.

Not a duplicate: I found no issue or PR for this (searched "echo truncate", "detokenize prompt", "truncate_prompt_tokens", "truncation_side", "echo text_offset"). #61363 and #61524 change which special tokens truncation keeps, not when the echoed text is decoded.

AI assistance was used to find this bug, write the fix and the test, and run the validation shown above.
