title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Wait for pending expert buffer copies before NIXL READs
author: djramic
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the intermittent `test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy[nixl-*]` failure in `mi300_4: (MI300) EPLB Execution`:

```text
verify_redundant_experts_have_same_weights failed: rank=0, layer=0, weight_idx=0, logical_expert=1, physical_pos=4, actual_head=[2100.0, 2101.0, ...], reference_head=[1000.0, 1001.0, ...]
FAILED distributed/test_eplb_execute.py::test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy[nixl-4-2-2-5] - AssertionError
```

Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14810/list?jid=01a143f1-ca27-459c-90a8-b3ef97f5fcaf&tab=output>

The test encodes weights as `logical_expert * 1000 + layer * 100 + ...`, so layer 0 ends up with experts from layer 1. `move_from_buffer` only queues the copies out of `expert_buffer` on the stream, and `add_recv` for the next layer immediately issues NIXL READs into the same buffer from the CPU. The READs are not ordered with the stream, so when the GPU lags (e.g. waking up from idle), they overwrite the buffer before the copies of the previous layer run. Only multi-layer cases fail.

The original NIXL communicator (#36276) synchronized the stream before issuing READs. #41633 removed that sync together with the send buffer packing and made `set_stream` a no-op, while READs now land directly in `expert_buffer`. 

This PR synchronizes the current stream and the EPLB stream in `set_transfer_context`, before the first READ of each layer, and removes the no-op `set_stream` override so the stream is stored. The current stream covers the sync path. In async EPLB, the main thread copies out of the buffer on the main stream, which the worker sees only through `self._stream` waiting on `consumed_event`.

## Test Plan

MI300X (gfx942):

```bash
cd tests
pytest -v -s distributed/test_eplb_execute.py
```

To trigger the race, I ran the `nixl-4-2-2-5` and `nixl-2-2-3-4` cases of `test_rearrange_expert_weights_with_redundancy` in a loop with the same seed and expert mapping as CI, either with the GPU idle for 2 s before each rearrangement or with a `torch.cuda._sleep` delay before `move_from_buffer`.

## Test Result

| Setup | `main` | `main` + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GPU idle 2 s before each rearrangement | 5/100 failed | 0/100 failed |
| 10-20 ms GPU delay before `move_from_buffer` | 20/20 failed | 0/10 failed |
| Async EPLB flow, 10 ms GPU delay | 40/40 failed | 0/40 failed |

The async flow was emulated with a worker thread calling `transfer_layer` and the main thread calling `move_from_buffer`, as in `async_worker.py` and `eplb_state.py`. All failures had the same signature as CI, while `torch_gloo`, `pynccl` and `torch_nccl` passed under the same delay.

With this PR, `distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` passes: `35 passed, 7 skipped`.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation and validation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Ignore AMD CI webhook no-op builds in /amd-ci run and retry
author: aarushjain29
body:
Every push to a PR creates an amd-ci webhook build. bootstrap-amd.sh exits for those builds without running any tests ("AMD CI does not start automatically on PRs"), so they pass with nothing tested. The bot treated them as real runs:

1. /amd-ci run from a PR author without write access was refused with "AMD CI already ran on this commit" (for example, https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14851). Pushing again didn't help, because every push creates another no-op build.
2. /amd-ci retry picked the no-op build and replied "No failed jobs need retrying" instead of telling the author to use /amd-ci run.

The fix skips builds with source webhook for AMD CI commands in both places. This is the same condition bootstrap-amd.sh uses. Builds started from the Buildkite UI, or by comment, still count. /ci behavior is unchanged.

Test plan: new unit tests for both cases; they fail on main and pass with this change. All 62 tests in test_run_ci_command.py pass.


### Replay against real PR data

I replayed `run_ci_command.py` from upstream `main` and from this PR against the real data for #62032:
- the live PR from the GitHub API;
- every amd-ci build on the PR, from Buildkite. The only build on the head commit `f03aefad5b` is [#14851](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14851), a `webhook` build that ran no tests.

All writes (comments, reactions, branch updates, build create, retry) were stubbed and recorded, not sent. The `main` replay reproduces the bot's actual reply on #62032.

| Scenario (PR author without write access) | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/amd-ci run` (bot merges `main` into the stale branch, as in production) | ❌ "AMD CI already ran on this commit: …/builds/14851" | ✅ Merges `main`, then starts an AMD CI build on the new head |
| `/amd-ci run --allow-stale` | ❌ "AMD CI already ran on this commit: …/builds/14851" | ✅ Starts an AMD CI build on `f03aefad5b` |
| `/amd-ci retry` | Retries no-op #14851: "No failed, timed-out, or expired jobs need retrying" | "No AMD CI build exists for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` first." |
| `/amd-ci run` when a comment-triggered build already finished on the head | ❌ "already ran" | ❌ "already ran" (unchanged) |
| `/amd-ci run` when a Buildkite UI build already finished on the head | ❌ "already ran" | ❌ "already ran" (unchanged) |
| `/amd-ci retry` when a comment-triggered build failed on the head | Retries that build | Retries that build (unchanged) |

Unit tests: the two new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. All 62 tests in `test_run_ci_command.py` pass.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Account for CLIP CLS rows in LLaVA-NeXT-Video tower mappings
author: liulanze
body:
## Overview

Fixes item 7 of #61608. With `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, LLaVA-NeXT-Video's `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` counts 576 tower rows per frame, but vLLM's CLIP tower prepends a CLS token, so its LoRA layers actually see 577. The tower LoRA buffer is sized from this count, so encoder profiling overflows it and the engine fails to start:

```
$ vllm serve llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf --enable-lora --enable-tower-connector-lora
...
  File "vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py", line 291, in _lora_shrink
    assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M
AssertionError
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

When startup does pass (e.g. `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`), the runtime mapping is still one row per frame short, so the last rows of each video get the next request's adapter, or none.

The fix adds `tower_tokens_per_frame` in `__init__`, computed with `get_num_image_tokens()` as in `llava_next.py` (577 for CLIP, unchanged for SigLIP), and the hook uses it instead of `patch_grid_length ** 2`. #61799 fixes the same bug in `llava.py`; no open PR touches these counts in `llava_next_video.py`.

## Validation

1x A100 80GB, base 5bf3d9f665, `llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf`:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm serve` command above (defaults otherwise) | assert at startup | starts |
| `LLM(...)`, `max_model_len=4096`, `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048 / 8192 | assert at startup | starts |
| `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` (default `max_model_len`), 70-frame + 43-frame video in one batch | assert at runtime | completes |
| no-LoRA requests in a batch with LoRA requests vs. the same batch without LoRA | one request's logprobs change | bit-exact |
| tower LoRA vs. the same adapter merged into the weights, max \|Δlogprob\| | 0.039 | 0.012 |

The last two rows use a random rank-8 adapter on the CLIP layers, with 4 eight-frame videos in one encoder batch and greedy decoding.

All GPU runs above used the first revision (fd4daa1), which computed the same count inside the hook; the review update only moves it to `__init__`.

`pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_next_video.py`: 6 passed on e40576d.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix] Fix multi-layer MTP module selection for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next
author: spandantiwari
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen3.5-family MTP drafters (`Qwen3_5MTP`, `Qwen3_5MoeMTP`; also used by Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8 and Intern-S2 checkpoints) and Qwen3-Next (`Qwen3NextMTP`) ran **MTP module 0 for every draft step** when a checkpoint has more than one MTP module, instead of the module trained for that step. This PR makes each draft step use its own module on Model Runner V2, including in the default compiled configuration.

Not a duplicate: #35607 proposed only the `forward` part of this (closed unmerged in Mar 2026, as published Qwen3.5 checkpoints ship one MTP layer); no open PR addresses it.

## Claims

- **Bug fix (MRV2):** multi-module Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next drafting now uses module `i` for draft step `i`, in eager, default compiled (`VLLM_COMPILE` + CUDA graphs), and breakable-CUDA-graph modes. Previously every step reused module 0.
- **No behavior change for shipped checkpoints:** all published Qwen3.5 / 3.6 / 3.8 / Intern-S2 checkpoints have one MTP layer; their drafter keeps its current execution mode (compiled or CUDA graphs), and outputs and acceptance are identical to `main` (below). No published checkpoint of any MTP family changes routing.
- **Lossless:** the target verifies every draft token; this affects draft acceptance (speedup), not output.

## Validation

**Regression test through `LLM` (new):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_steps_use_their_own_module`. It adds a second MTP module with random weights to the real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base` checkpoint (the original shard is symlinked; only module 1 is written), runs MRV2 with the default compiled drafter, `num_speculative_tokens=2` and `use_local_argmax_reduction=True`, and checks that step 1 is accepted (module 0 intact) while step 2 is rejected (module 1 really used).

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_steps_use_their_own_module
# main (7128f568ac):
E       AssertionError: module 1 acceptance 0.419: module 0 was reused
# previous revision of this PR (eager-only fix, no compile gating):
E       AssertionError: module 1 acceptance 0.350: module 0 was reused
# this PR:
1 passed in 102.01s
```

Per-position acceptance on that two-module checkpoint (MI350x, greedy, 100 prompts):

| runner / mode | step 1 | step 2 |
|---|---|---|
| MRV2, default compiled | 0.807 | **0.000** |
| MRV2, `enforce_eager` | 0.805 | **0.000** |
| MRV2, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` | 0.805 | **0.000** (previous revision: `AttributeError: 'Qwen3_5Config' object has no attribute 'num_nextn_predict_layers'`) |
| MRV1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | 0.776 | 0.422 (module 0 reused; see limitations) |

**Routing unit test (real configs):** `tests/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_num_hidden_layers_selects_multi_module_mtp` builds real `Qwen3_5Config` / `Qwen3_5TextConfig` configs (multimodal and text-only) through `ModelConfig` + `SpeculativeConfig`. On `main` the two-module cases fail with `assert False is True`; with this PR all 16 tests in the file pass.

**No regression on shipped checkpoints:** `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base` (one MTP layer), MRV2 compiled, `num_speculative_tokens=3`: output tokens identical to `main`, and acceptance identical on a paired run (415 drafts, per-position `[0.7663, 0.4458, 0.2458]` on both; run-to-run noise on `main` alone is ±3 drafts). The drafter is still compiled (`[eagle_head] torch.compile took 7.7 s`).

Also passed: `pytest v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/` (5 passed, 1 CUDA-only skip), `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`, `tests/test_config.py` (2 failures need gated `meta-llama` access, unrelated).

**Qwen3-Next (local only, no small checkpoint for CI):** `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`, MRV2 compiled, `num_speculative_tokens=2`. Shipped one-module checkpoint: drafts, acceptance (`[0.9487, 0.8063]`) and outputs identical to `main`; drafter still compiled. With a second, random-weight MTP module (`num_nextn_predict_layers=2`, module-1 FP8 scales x100 so it dominates the residual): step-2 acceptance 0.000 with this PR vs 0.688 on `main`.

The Qwen3.5 MTP CI step did not run for changes to these model / config files; its `source_file_dependencies` now include them.

## Details

**Root causes (all needed for multi-module drafting to work):**
1. `Qwen3_5MTP.forward` / `Qwen3NextMTP.forward` did not pass `spec_step_idx` to the inner predictor, which selects `self.layers[spec_step_idx % num_mtp_layers]`. Their `**kwargs` silently accepted and dropped it; it is now a named parameter and `**kwargs` is removed (no caller passes anything else).
2. `use_multi_module_mtp()` only read `num_nextn_predict_layers`, but Qwen3.5 declares `mtp_num_hidden_layers` (nested in `text_config` for multimodal checkpoints), so it never routed to `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`, the only speculator that varies `spec_step_idx`. `SpeculativeConfig.num_mtp_modules()` now reads the `n_predict` that `hf_config_override` already normalizes for every MTP family, so new multi-layer models use the multi-module speculator by default. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator.capture()` uses the same count (it read `num_nextn_predict_layers` unconditionally, which Qwen3.5 configs lack).
3. **Compiled drafters reused module 0.** vLLM compiles the drafter once with all Dynamo guards dropped, so the Python-indexed module chosen on the first trace was replayed for every step. The other multi-module drafters (Inkling, Step-3.5, MiMo-V2, Qwen4Exp, MiniMax-M3) are not compiled, which is why this did not surface. The Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next drafter is now compiled only when it runs single-module (`support_torch_compile(enable_if=...)`); multi-module drafters run eager with full CUDA graphs over the draft loop, like the other multi-module drafters. Since #51012 the CUDA Qwen3.5 drafter is no longer compiled, so this gate now applies to Qwen3-Next and the ROCm Qwen3.5 drafter.
4. With multi-module routing, the local-argmax path calls `get_top_tokens(hidden_states, spec_step_idx=...)`; `Qwen3_5MTP` now accepts and ignores it, since the MTP modules share one `lm_head` (as in `compute_logits`).

**Scope:** Qwen3-Next already routed correctly via `num_nextn_predict_layers`; it needed only (1) and (3). Drafts with MTP index sharing (`index_share_for_mtp_iteration`, from the checkpoint or the override) and MiniMax-M3 stay on the single-module speculator, with TODOs: index sharing is only implemented there, and MiniMax-M3 is not yet verified with the multi-module speculator.

**Files:** since #51012, CUDA loads `Qwen3_5MTP` from `vllm/models/qwen3_5/nvidia/mtp.py`, while ROCm and Intern-S2 (`InternS2MobiusMTP`) still use `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`. Fixes (1) and (4) are applied to both files.



**Limitations:** Model Runner V1 never passes `spec_step_idx` for any MTP family (only Step-3.5's proposer does), so multi-module drafting there still uses module 0; MRV1 is deprecated and this PR targets MRV2. Multi-module Qwen drafters trade the compiled drafter for eager + full CUDA graphs; no shipped checkpoint takes that path.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve token IDs in completion derender responses

Actual child imported-module paths/hashes were checked. Independent agent reviews found no blocking patch issue and audited saved HTTP evidence; they did not independently rerun the server.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Fix speculative warmup deadlock with pipeline parallelism
author: chenjr97
body:
## Overview

Fix a pipeline-parallel startup deadlock in MRV2 speculative decoding introduced by [#59260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59260).

## Claims

- Ensure all PP stages participate in the additional greedy warmup pass.
- Add regression coverage for matching warmup rounds across PP stages, with speculative decoding enabled and disabled.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py -q
```

- **34 passed** in 9.64 seconds. These suites are covered by the existing `V1 Executor + Worker` CI job.
- **GLM-4.7-Flash smoke test passed**: MRV2, TP=2, PP=2, BF16, MTP with one speculative token, JIT warmup and CUDA graphs enabled.
- Warmup completed and generation produced exactly **1,024 tokens** using `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, and `ignore_eos=True`. Recorded 532 draft tokens and 492 accepted tokens; process exited successfully.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed.

The model run validates startup and generation; no accuracy benchmark was performed.

## Details

Only the last PP stage owns a rejection sampler. Previously, the additional greedy warmup pass was gated on its presence, so earlier stages skipped the pass while the last stage waited for their activations.

Gate this pass on `speculative_config` instead, ensuring every PP stage executes matching forwards. The change is limited to the warmup condition and regression tests.

title: [MyPy][5/N] Fix mypy errors in hard tests/ dirs and enforce follow-imports=silent
author: adarshxs
body:
## Overview

Part 5 of enabling mypy on `tests/` (#49569). Fixes the mypy errors in the PR 5 directories and moves them from `SEPARATE_GROUPS` to `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so they are now checked with `--follow-imports silent` and cannot regress: `tests/entrypoints/llm`, `tests/entrypoints/openai`, `tests/kernels` (absorbing the previously listed `tests/kernels/{attention,core,helion,mamba,quantization}` and the separate `tests/kernels/moe`), `tests/lora`, `tests/tool_parsers`, `tests/v1/attention`, `tests/v1/e2e`, `tests/v1/ec_connector`.

Builds on #49570 (PR 0/1) and #51043 (PR 2). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these directories for mypy (checked `gh pr list --search "49569 in:body"` and `"mypy tests"`; the open `[MyPy]` PRs are #55485 (PR 4), #55542 (kv-A) and #55901 (kv-B)).

Partial #26533.

## Claims

- 533 mypy errors across the eight directories → 0, with `--warn-unused-ignores` also clean. (The issue's ~650 estimate predates #59428, which disabled `arg-type` and `assignment` under `tests/`.)
- Type-only: no `vllm/` changes, no `cast()`, no bare `# type: ignore`; the 29 ignores added are scoped to an error code and carry a reason (inline when the line fits in 88 columns, on the preceding line otherwise); 12 ignores that no longer suppressed anything are removed.
- 49 mock method assignments replaced with `monkeypatch.setattr`.
- Pre-existing test defects surfaced by the stricter check are fixed where safe, and flagged in a comment where fixing would change what the test exercises (list in Details).

## Validation

Environment: the pre-commit hook env (mypy 1.20.2, no torch/transformers so they resolve to `Any`), Python 3.11 like the hook.

```bash
# 1. the directories are clean at the strictness being enforced
.venv/bin/mypy --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports silent --warn-unused-ignores \
    tests/entrypoints/llm tests/entrypoints/openai tests/kernels tests/lora \
    tests/tool_parsers tests/v1/attention tests/v1/e2e tests/v1/ec_connector
# Success: no issues found in 632 source files   (before: 533 errors in 111 files)

# 2. the hook as CI runs it, with the new grouping in effect
pre-commit run mypy --all-files --hook-stage manual
# passes; the only output is 3 darwin-only errors in vllm/ (posix_fadvise, MADV_HUGEPAGE)
# that exist on macOS before this change and do not appear on Linux CI

# 3. routing proof: each PR 5 directory now lands in the "" (silent) group
.venv/bin/python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/pre_commit'); import mypy; \
  print([k for k,v in mypy.group_files(['tests/lora/utils.py']).items() if v])"
# ['']   (same for a file in each of the other seven directories; tests/v1/core still prints ['tests/v1/core'])

# 4. all other hooks on the changed files
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only main)
# ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, ... all pass
```

Test runs (macOS CPU build of vLLM, so only CPU-runnable suites; everything else collected only):

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest --collect-only` on all 116 changed test files | 8316 tests collected; 6 collection errors, all missing optional deps on macOS (triton-cpu, tilelang, datasets), none from this change |
| `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/{chat_completion/test_chat_error,completion/test_completion_error,completion/test_completion_text_offset,responses/test_function_call_parsing,responses/test_response_input_to_harmony,responses/test_responses_utils,responses/test_serving_responses,test_render_parity,test_tool_choice_content_none}.py` | 243 passed, 1 xfailed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_*.py` (14 changed files) | 528 passed, 1 skipped, 19 xfailed |
| `pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit tests/v1/attention` (3 pre-existing non-collecting files ignored) | 984 passed, 1150 skipped, 214 failed + 16 errors; the identical set of 230 ids fails on unchanged `main` in the same environment (CUDA/ROCm-only tests, `/dev/shm`, NIXL), so none is from this change |

No model evaluation: the change does not touch `vllm/` and cannot affect output, accuracy or serving.

## Details

Most fixes follow the issue's recipe: `assert x is not None` before an `X | None` access, `assert isinstance(...)` to narrow a union or an abstract base to the concrete class the test builds, annotations on fixtures and helpers, and `monkeypatch.setattr` instead of assigning to a method. Scoped ignores remain only where a test stub intentionally does not satisfy the real interface (`misc` for `None` fallbacks of optional kernel classes and a `Final` attribute, `attr-defined` for `SimpleNamespace` stubs, `type-abstract` where a test instantiates an abstract class through a factory).

Pre-existing defects the stricter check surfaced (all in tests; none changes what a test exercises):

- `tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py`: `StructuredOutputsParams(backend=...)` has no such init field (`_backend` is `init=False`), so the call raised `TypeError`; the kwarg is removed and the helper no longer takes a backend.
- `tests/lora/utils.py`: `DummyLoRAManager.init_lora` passed `embeddings_tensor=` to `LoRALayerWeights(...)`, which no longer accepts it.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_{internlm2,longcat,phi4mini}_tool_parser.py`: `tokenizer.get_vocab = MagicMock()` permanently mutated the module-scoped tokenizer fixture and leaked into later tests; now `monkeypatch.setattr`, undone per test.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py`: assignments to a non-existent `FusedMoEParallelConfig.use_dp` removed; the no-DP state already comes from `make_no_parallel()`.
- `tests/kernels/moe/modular_kernel_tools/{mk_objects,common,cli_args}.py`: registries and `Config` fields were annotated as holding instances although they hold classes; now `type[...]` of the Modular subclasses that are actually registered.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py`: the mock prefill backends' `run_prefill_new_tokens` / `run_prefill_context_chunk` did not match the ABC (`chunk_idx` vs `chunk`, missing `out` / `output_scale`).
- `tests/v1/attention/utils.py`: `try_get_attention_backend` was annotated `type[AttentionImpl]` but `get_impl_cls()` returns `type[AttentionImplBase]`; and the `add_mock_model_methods` block is removed: its `get_num_layers` mock shadowed the real method with the wrong arity, the three `*_for_layer` hooks no longer exist on `ModelConfig`, nothing reads any of them, and no caller passed the flag.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py`: `query_len_support` is a `ClassVar` and was assigned through an instance; the assignment is removed (the inherited default is the value it set).
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`: `get_fake_sample_fn` was annotated `-> SamplerOutput` although it returns a callable.
- `tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_metadata.py`: asserted load entries as `(transfer_id, block_ids)` pairs; the metadata carries `(transfer_id, block_ids, shape)` and the worker unpacks three values, so the test is updated to the real contract.

Deliberately not changed, flagged with a comment and a scoped ignore:

- `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py`: the int8 non-block branch of `moe_quantize_weights_2d` calls `ops.scaled_int8_quant(w, w_s, use_per_token_if_dynamic=...)`, but the signature is now `(input, scale, azp, symmetric) -> (q, scale, azp)`, so it would raise if reached. No test reaches it (every int8 caller uses block quant and the modular-kernel CLI only accepts fp8); a replacement needs a GPU to validate, so it is left for a follow-up.

Typing gaps in `vllm/` that the per-test fixes keep running into, left for follow-ups:

- four identical `type-abstract` ignores: `select_common_block_size` / `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` take `type[AttentionBackend]`, but the indexer backends leave `get_impl_cls` abstract;
- repeated narrowings of `Metric.value` (only `Counter` / `Gauge` have it), `LLMEngine.engine_core` (to `InprocClient`), `EmbeddingCache.get/alloc` (`CacheEntry | None`) and `FusedMoEQuantConfig.*_scale` (`Tensor | None`).

`MockMLAAttentionLayer.forward_impl` in `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` keeps a scoped `override` ignore because the replica deliberately takes only the arguments the test passes; the prefill-registry mocks above were aligned to their ABC instead because they are registered as real backends.

The hook change is routing only: the absorbed `tests/kernels/*` entries become redundant under the `tests/kernels` parent entry and are removed, mirroring what #51043 did for `tests/plugins_tests`.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep completion derender stream logprob offsets aligned with tokens
author: dskwe
body:
## Overview

Keep streaming completion derender logprob offsets aligned with reported token strings, matching batch derender and the coupled completion fix in #60668.

## Claims

- A special token filtered from response text no longer shifts subsequent streaming `logprobs.text_offset` backwards relative to batch output.
- Missing/empty logprob metadata retains the existing emitted-text fallback; response text and token IDs are unchanged.

## Validation

Before the fix, the final regression/neighbor selection returned **2 failed, 14 passed**; with the fix, **16 passed**. The two failures are the skip-special-token cases at chunk sizes 1 and 2. With `ignore_eos=true`, `hello`, `</s>`, ` world` produced streaming offsets `[0,5,5]` versus batch `[0,5,9]`; the fix gives `[0,5,9]` in both modes.

Before publication, copied the complete tracked source at `b05ede56168b5718c425c1493914e5e79f6b8181` (including merged #62114) into an isolated Linux CPU validation directory, applied this patch, and ran both the offset selections and #62114's generated-ID regression together: **22 passed, 147 deselected in 5.94s**, exit 0.

```sh
docker exec -w /validation/completion-offset-submit-20261017 \
  -e PYTHONPATH=/validation/completion-offset-submit-20261017:/validation \
  -e VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
  vllm-tokenizer-validation-20261013 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -p completion_offset_local_assets -p completion_ids_local_assets \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  -k 'TestStreamLogprobs or TestDerenderCompletionStream or preserves_requested_token_ids' \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

Local plugins use a real cached OPT tokenizer instead of the unavailable default tiny-Llama fixture and skip the full distributed/environment/memory cleanup. They do not replace production derender methods. Those original runs did not exercise the default fixture. Standard regression selection:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  -k 'TestStreamLogprobs or TestDerenderCompletionStream' -v
```

A separate normal render-module CLI/Uvicorn HTTP A/B probe exercised supplied tokens through `/v1/completions/derender`: 12 cases per variant, covering skip-special false/true, chunk sizes 1/2, and present/missing/empty metadata. Each variant returned 66 POST 200 responses, including empty terminal and usage-only controls. Baseline had six offset/state assertion failures; fixed had none. Other inspected response fields were unchanged. Independent reviews audited the patch and saved HTTP results; they did not rerun HTTP.

Fresh pinned patch-scoped hooks, including mypy and CI test tethering, all passed:

```sh
pre-commit run --files vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
```

Environment: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.19.0. HTTP evidence is supplied-token postprocessing, not model generation, SSE, model evaluation or GPU inference. Native CPU inference is unavailable because the installed `vllm._C` raises SIGILL; no generation-quality/performance claim is made.

### CI assertion follow-up (`dae25f1497`)

Reproduced `test_completion_stream_logprobs_text_offset_absolute` with the original `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` tokenizer: the next offset is 6, while emitted `hello` has length 5 because the reported logprob token retains a leading space. Updated only the old assertion to use reported-token lengths; production logic and the direct batch/stream parity regression are unchanged.

With that tokenizer (snapshot `9408c553e5c189a7dcdc5a5dbd2feb476b061759`), the focused classes pass **16 tests**, and the broader unit-only selection passes **97 tests**. A negative control restoring emitted-text accumulation fails the updated assertion (`5 == 6`); restoring the fix passes. Patch-scoped pre-commit, including mypy, passes. These runs use CPU postprocessing and a local plugin that only skips GPU/distributed cleanup; there is no tokenizer substitution. GPU/full server integration CI remains unverified locally; an attempted wider selection had seven parser-server setup errors due to an unavailable offline model cache.

## Details

Within a chunk, logprob conversion advances offsets using the reported token strings. Across chunks, derender instead advanced the carried offset by `len(new_text)`. These differ when decoding filters special tokens, so the next chunk restarted too early. Carry the end of the last reported logprob token when available, preserving the prior fallback otherwise.

The existing ordinary-text offset test checks the next chunk offset against the lengths of reported logprob token strings, which may retain a leading space absent from response text. The parametrized regression directly compares stream and batch offsets for filtered/preserved special tokens and both chunk sizes.

Fresh open/all-state searches for `60668 in:body`, `derender offset`, `derender text_offset` and `logprob_text_offset` found no competing fix. Related #59510 handles stops and retains the old offset update; #60918 affects coupled packed logprobs, and #60542 changes generate logprob representation rather than this derender state update. #62114 is already merged and preserves token IDs; this PR is based on that merge and fixes a separate metadata field.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing and review. The submitter also confirmed personally running related tests before requesting publication; the numeric results above are from agent-executed commands.

title: [Bugfix] Fix multimodal sender-cache invalidation race with queued renders
author: YueshenZ
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62121. Apply sender-cache invalidations between generation renders on the single-worker multimodal executor so an engine cache-miss report cannot remove an entry between the processor's cache lookup and merge.

## Claims

- In-flight generation renders on the single-worker multimodal executor complete without the reported `Expected a cached item` assertion; already-queued renders consume pending invalidations before looking up cached data.
- Unrelated outputs keep flowing while multimodal processing or cache invalidation is blocked.
- Ignore uncached hashes and coalesce duplicate miss reports, avoiding unbounded notification growth on pre-rendered `features` traffic that never invokes the renderer.

## Validation

Current review cleanup (`20f04478`): both helpers return when the cache is absent; enqueue also returns for empty input or an empty filtered pending set. The output handler delegates empty-list handling to the helper while keeping its outer cache guard and enqueue-before-publish ordering.

- macOS arm64 CPU: `pytest -p pytest_skipgc tests/multimodal/test_cache.py tests/renderers/test_warmup.py tests/renderers/test_executor_replace.py -k "not sleep" -q` → **57 passed, 1 deselected**. The cleanup opt-out is described below; test assertions were unchanged.
- NVIDIA A800 80GB, Qwen2-VL-2B @ `895c3a49`: the unmodified `pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py::test_sleep_wake_preserves_mm_cache_consistency -s -vv -ra` → **1 passed, 0 skipped**. Logs confirm both generations and the intervening sleep/wake; sleep freed 38.05 GiB. Python sources were verified against `20f04478`; native artifacts were reused from official wheel `7b6310c1` with PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 / Transformers 5.19.0, and all model-file hashes matched the pinned revision.
- A real-renderer check with the invalidation lock held confirmed that empty lists, empty tuples and fully filtered hashes return without waiting or changing an existing pending invalidation. The next render resends the payload, and the following render hits the cache.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed, including ruff, format, typos, mypy, SPDX/import and configuration checks. `actionlint` was excluded because its local environment could not initialize; no workflow files changed. `git diff --check` passed.

The offline processor performance measurements compare `a0e7137c` with `d2097ba5`, not this cleanup: [initial benchmark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62164#issuecomment-6262374327), [three-repeat 1,024-prompt results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62164#issuecomment-6283546827). These synchronous measurements do not cover async miss-notification contention.

Coalescing implementation (`d2097ba5`), earlier macOS arm64 CPU validation, Python 3.13.15 / PyTorch 2.14.1:

- `pytest -p pytest_skipgc tests/multimodal/test_cache.py -k "not sleep" -q`: **29 passed, 1 deselected**. Includes LRU, SHM/IPC, the original forced-interleaving regression, coalescing/clear behavior, and a multi-hash failure with concurrent notifications.
- `pytest -p pytest_skipgc tests/renderers/test_warmup.py tests/renderers/test_executor_replace.py -q`: **28 passed**.
- The local `pytest_skipgc` plugin applies the repository's `skip_global_cleanup` marker to avoid the previously observed macOS torch teardown crash; it does not modify test assertions. SHM tests ran with local shared-memory access enabled.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, format, typos, mypy and Buildkite test tethering. `actionlint` was skipped; no workflow file changed. `git diff --check` passed.
- A method-level comparison using the real renderer/processor/LRU cache and the submitted `dc1a962` queue/drain methods reproduced the backlog: 1,000 absent hashes retained 1,000 records before and 0 after; 200 notifications for one cached hash retained 200 before and 1 after. The next render resent the payload in both cases. This was not a full baseline-tree pytest run.

The original assertion regression previously failed on pristine `a0e7137c` and passed on submitted commit `dc1a962`. That submitted implementation also has Linux CPU validation (27 passed, 1 deselected) and A800 serving evidence below. **The historical HTTP stress measurements below remain specific to `dc1a962`. The `d2097ba5` offline benchmarks and `20f04478` sleep/wake test do not replace a rerun of that HTTP stress workload.**

<details>
<summary>Historical A800 serving comparison for submitted commit dc1a962</summary>

Qwen2-VL-2B @ 895c3a49, A800 80GB PCIe, localhost HTTP using the reporter's pause/resume plus background-image load, no server-side hook. Five-minute trigger and two-minute control per arm:

| arm | rounds | target asserts | image requests | ok | other 500 | stream errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main trigger | 164 | 18 | 32,138 | 31,794 | 196 | 130 |
| dc1a962 trigger | 164 | 0 | 31,934 | 31,565 | 199 | 170 |
| main control | 56 | 0 | 24,632 | 24,632 | 0 | 0 |
| dc1a962 control | 56 | 0 | 25,070 | 25,070 | 0 | 0 |

Twelve fixed public-image responses were byte-identical for text, finish reason and completion-token count. Remaining errors were the existing P1-miss class; internal-error lines increased from 344 to 369 (1.07% to 1.16%). No overall error-rate improvement is claimed.

</details>

## Details

The output handler previously invalidated the sender cache on the asyncio thread while the renderer performed its lookup and merge on its single-worker multimodal executor.

The handler now records missed hashes before publishing the associated outputs. Only hashes currently present in the sender cache are retained. When a processor cache is present, a short lock protects a pending set; each render swaps that set before its first lookup. Both helpers return immediately when there is no cache. Enqueue also returns for empty input or when filtering leaves no live hashes, before acquiring the lock. Membership checks and cache invalidation execute outside the lock. Failed invalidation restores the current and remaining hashes without discarding newly arrived notifications. Cache clear retains its existing behavior; stale notifications become no-ops at the next render boundary.

This avoids a second executor job and queue/set mirrored state. Pending records can briefly outlive the cache entry they reference, so this does not claim that their count always equals the instantaneous live cache size. Sync LLM retains direct invalidation.

This is distinct from #34749's assertion-to-error conversion and #61656's endpoint retries. P1 drift itself, automatic HTTP retries, and #62123's SHM handle issue are out of scope. The [pre-existing pooling/embedding cross-executor race](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62164#discussion_r4311154000) is also not addressed by this fix. The issue came from a public report and was investigated with constructed reproductions; it was not encountered in the submitter's production workload. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation and validation, including this follow-up review.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Fix macOS build: read inherited listener family from its address
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fixes the macOS arm64 CPU wheel build, which fails on main (release-v2 #8588) and on `releases/v0.32.0` (release-v2 #8575):

```
error[E0599]: no method named `domain` found for struct `socket2::Socket` in the current scope
 --> src/engine-core-client/src/transport.rs:408:25
408 |     let domain = socket.domain()?;
```

#54113 uses `socket2::Socket::domain()` (`SO_DOMAIN`) in `adopt_listener` to tell inherited TCP and Unix listeners apart. socket2 only provides that method on Linux, Android, FreeBSD and Fuchsia, so `vllm-rs` doesn't compile on macOS. The macOS wheel is in the "additional wheels" group, which only runs when unblocked, so nothing caught this when it landed.

## Change

Read the family from the listener's bound address instead: `socket.local_addr()?.domain()`. `SockAddr::domain` works on every platform. The TCP/Unix branching after it is unchanged.

Also adds `inherited_unix_listener_is_adopted_without_rebinding`, a Unix-socket counterpart to the existing inherited TCP listener test. Before this, the Unix branch had no test.

## Test Plan

On macOS (arm64, rustc 1.95):
- `cargo check -p vllm-engine-core-client`: failed with the error above before the change, passes after.
- `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client inherited`: both inherited listener tests pass (TCP and Unix).
- `cargo check --manifest-path rust/src/cmd/Cargo.toml --release --features native-tls-vendored --bin vllm-rs`, the wheel build's cargo invocation: passes.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean.

Linux CI covers the Linux path.

Wanted for v0.32.0 (milestone "v0.32.0 cherry picks"), since it blocks the macOS wheel there too.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Match DeepSeek-V4.1 encoder to the 1017 reference encoding
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Match the Python DeepSeek V4.1 encoder to the updated reference [`encoding/`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/tree/main/encoding). Rust counterpart: #62200.

Affects both V4.1-Flash checkpoints (launch and 1017). DeepSeek fixed the turn handling in both repos ([launch `314113f`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/commit/314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6), 1017 release); their `encoding/` is now identical. The image-token check has been in the reference since launch.

## Claims

- Tool results alone no longer start a new user turn, so reasoning before a tool call is kept.
- Literal `<｜deepseek_image｜>` in message text or reasoning returns 400.
- All five reference golden prompts match. V4 is unchanged.

## Examples

**1. Tool call in thinking mode, with no `tools` field in the request**

```python
[{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Paris? Answer in Fahrenheit."},
 {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning": "Tool returns Celsius; convert to Fahrenheit.",
  "tool_calls": [{"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"}}]},
 {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "{\"temp_c\": 20}"}]
```

Before (reasoning dropped):
```
<｜User｜>What's the weather in Paris? Answer in Fahrenheit.<｜Assistant｜></think>

<｜DSML｜ calls>...
```
After (reasoning kept, same as the reference encoder):
```
<｜User｜>What's the weather in Paris? Answer in Fahrenheit.<｜Assistant｜><think>Tool returns Celsius; convert to Fahrenheit.</think>

<｜DSML｜ calls>...
```

**2. Literal image token in text**

```python
[{"role": "user", "content": "hi <｜deepseek_image｜>"}]
```

Before: accepted, so the prompt has an image placeholder with no image. After: 400.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py`: 84 passed. The new tests fail on main.
- E2E on 8x H100 (TP8, recipe H100 flags, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017): the prompt keeps the tool-call reasoning and matches the reference encoder; the literal image token returns 400.
- GSM8K (chat, thinking off, 1319 questions): 0.970.

## Details

Not a duplicate: #60792 (image order) and other open V4.1 tokenizer PRs don't change turn boundaries or placeholder validation. Fixtures are copied from the 1017 repo (MIT).

title: [Multimodal][Docs] State that retried media downloads count toward the request budget
author: surajm20061998
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make it visible that `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB` counts retried download attempts. As discussed above with @jperezdealgaba and @DarkLight1337, counting them is intentional: it stops a media URL that keeps disconnecting from transferring several times the limit through retries. This PR keeps that behavior and says so in the error message and in `docs/usage/security.md`.

## Claims

- The budget error now reads `Request media downloads exceed VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB=… (N bytes received, including retried attempts).`, so an operator seeing it for media under the limit knows why.
- The `security.md` row now says the budget includes "concurrent downloads and retried attempts".

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor --enable-log-outputs on /v1/completions
author: surajm20061998
body:
## Overview

`--enable-log-outputs` is silently ignored by `/v1/completions`. The handler never accepted the flag or logged generated text, while chat, Responses, Anthropic (#60982), Cohere (#61089) and `/inference/v1/generate` all do. This adds output logging to completions, mirroring chat.

## Claims

- With `--enable-log-requests --enable-log-outputs`, `/v1/completions` logs generated text: one line per output when not streaming; when streaming, one line per delta (respects `--enable-log-deltas`) plus the full text when the stream ends.
- Output lines reuse the per-prompt request id from the input log (`cmpl-<id>-<i>`), so the two can be correlated.
- Nothing changes when the flag is off (the default).

## Validation

**End-to-end,** `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-log-requests --enable-log-outputs` (CPU backend). For each request, the counts of `Received request` / `Generated response` log lines:

| Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/completions`, non-streaming | 1 / **0** | 1 / **1** |
| `/v1/completions`, streaming, 8 tokens | 1 / **0** | 1 / **9** (8 deltas + complete) |
| `/v1/chat/completions` (control) | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |

<details>
<summary>Log lines with this PR</summary>

```
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-nonstream-0: output: ' Paris. It was founded in 7', finish_reason: length
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-stream-0 (streaming delta): output: ' Paris', finish_reason: None
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-stream-0 (streaming delta): output: '.', finish_reason: None
...
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-stream-0 (streaming delta): output: '7', finish_reason: length
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-stream-0 (streaming complete): output: ' Paris. It was founded in 7', finish_reason: streaming_complete
Generated response chatcmpl-e2e-chat-nonstream: output: 'Hello! How can I assist you today', finish_reason: length
```
</details>

**Tests:** `test_completion_logs_outputs_when_enabled[stream=False|True]` drives `create_completion` with a mock engine and checks the logged text, token ids, finish reason, delta/complete lines, and that every line uses the input log's request id.

```
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py
main:    2 failed, 51 passed  (TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'enable_log_outputs')
this PR: 53 passed
```

Regression: `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/{test_completion_error,test_completion_text_offset,test_lora_resolvers}.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py tests/entrypoints/serve/utils`: `main` 279 passed, this PR 281 passed. Both have the same 19 environment-only failures (GPT-OSS/Harmony tokenizers unavailable offline). `pre-commit` ruff and mypy are clean.

Validated on macOS (Apple Silicon, CPU backend), Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0, rebased on `main` @ `e744eacf6`. No model evaluation: logging only.

## Details

The original `--enable-log-outputs` PR (#20707) implemented logging for chat and Responses only. Later endpoints that inherit from the chat handler only needed the flag forwarded (#60982, #61089). Completions has its own handler, so it needs the logging itself:

- `OpenAIServingCompletion` takes `enable_log_outputs` / `enable_log_deltas`, and `init_generate_state` passes them, as for chat.
- Non-streaming: after the response is built, log each output's generated text, token ids and finish reason.
- Streaming: log each non-empty delta, accumulate text only when logging is on, and log each choice's full text after the stream, with `finish_reason="streaming_complete"` as chat does.
- The generated text is logged, not the echoed prompt (`echo=true`); `log_inputs` already logs the prompt.

The batch chat endpoint and speech-to-text have the same gap. I'll follow up separately to keep this one small.

**Duplicate check:** searched issues/PRs for `enable-log-outputs`, `enable_log_outputs`, and log outputs + completions, and inspected every open PR touching `vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py` and `vllm/entrypoints/generate/api_router.py`. #45634 adds request arrival/completion lifecycle logs, a different feature. #40155 is about prompt log levels. None add output logging to completions.

**AI assistance:** Claude (Anthropic) helped find, reproduce and write this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and the end-to-end check above myself.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep the EAGLE-reachable SWA tail at a shared-prefix junction
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Overview

This PR fixes cross-request prefix reuse for sliding-window groups under EAGLE/MTP with sparse prefix-cache retention. The shared-prefix junction pin from #47782 kept a sliding-window tail one block too high, so requests that share only a prefix got no prefix-cache hit at all. The fix also pins the tail one block lower, which is where an EAGLE sibling's hit actually lands.

## Claims

- Under sparse retention, a sibling request that shares only a prefix now gets a prefix-cache hit when the drafter's groups are sliding-window and the full-attention groups are not EAGLE groups. On Step-5-Preview with MTP, the GSM8K 5-shot prefix goes from 0 hit tokens to a hit on every request after the first two.
- Nothing changes without EAGLE, or when every group is flagged as an EAGLE group. In those cases the junction already sits one block lower, because the full-attention group drops its block too.
- The cost is one extra cached block per sliding-window group for each request that registers a junction.

## Validation

**Unit test.** `test_swa_shared_prefix_reuse_under_zero_retention` gets a `use_eagle` case that flags only the SWA group, as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61455 does for drafters. It fails on main (0 instead of 48 hit tokens) and passes with the fix.

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py
620 passed, 2 errors
```

The 2 errors are `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate`, which needs a GPU and a model checkpoint (the run was CPU-only). On a wider set (`tests/v1/core`, Mooncake Store and offloading connector unit tests), the failure set with and without this PR is identical (GPU- or model-dependent tests), apart from the new case.

**End to end.** Step-5-Preview (MTP layers are sliding-window, the target also has full-attention DSA layers), 4x GB300, TP4 + EP, MTP k=3. Prefix caching runs with `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 1024`. The test runs on the Step5 preview branch of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61727, with this change applied.

12 GSM8K 5-shot prompts are sent one at a time. They share a 565-token prefix, and every prompt is shorter than 1024 tokens.

| | request 1 | request 2 | requests 3–12 |
|---|---|---|---|
| no MTP | 0 | 0 | 560 each |
| MTP k=3, without this PR | 0 | 0 | **0** |
| MTP k=3, this PR | 0 | 0 | 544 each |

Request 2 detects the junction, so later requests can hit. 544 is one block below the 560-token junction, which is the deepest hit an EAGLE lookup can verify.

Full GSM8K (1319 questions, concurrency 64, MTP k=3, Mooncake Store connector on):

| | without this PR | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| local prefix-cache hit tokens / queried | 0 / 839,793 | 737,520 / 839,793 (87.8%) |
| accuracy | 0.933 | 0.935 |
| Mooncake Store replay vs GPU-cache replay | 64/64 bit-identical | 64/64 bit-identical |

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. Request A runs alone.
2. Request B shares a prefix with A, but under sparse retention only A's full-attention blocks are still cached. `get_computed_blocks` reports the junction J as the full-attention hit length (B's shared prefix floored to a block), and B pins J.
3. The sliding-window mask keeps the `need`-block tail at J. Under EAGLE, that tail is shifted one block right, to include the block past J as the lookahead (#44082). This is right for a replay of the same prompt.
4. The block past J holds B's own tokens, so for request C it is not shared. C's SWA lookup must verify one block past its hit, so its best hit is J − block_size. That hit needs the window one block lower than the pinned tail, and the lowest block was never kept.
5. C gets no hit and pins the same J again, so no later request ever hits.

When every group takes the EAGLE drop (no group flagged), the full-attention hit is already one block lower, so J lands where the SWA hit can verify. The bug therefore shows only when a sliding-window group is an EAGLE group and the full-attention group that reports the junction is not. Step5 MTP already met this under the older "group holding the last registered layer" rule. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61455 makes per-group flags the general rule: drafters whose layers are sliding-window now flag only those groups.

**Fix.** Under EAGLE, `cache_blocks` registers both J and J − block_size as reachable boundaries. The masks overlap, so this keeps one extra block. Replay boundaries are unchanged, because they already account for the EAGLE drop (#54713, #61012). Mamba checkpointing reads `shared_prefix_boundary` directly and is unaffected.

**Not covered.** `OffloadingConnector` builds its own reachable boundaries from `shared_prefix_boundary` and is not changed here.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4.1] Inject Engram at pipeline stage entry
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 applies trained Engram modules at configured transformer layers. If a pipeline partition starts a non-initial stage on one of those layers, the stage-entry control-flow branch calls mHC pre directly and bypasses the normal Engram branch. Certain valid PP partitions can therefore silently skip an Engram operation for every request. The real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash configuration triggers this at layer 14 with `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26`.

This PR restores the missing NVIDIA operation by applying the local stage-entry Engram after receiving the previous stage's completed residual stream and before mHC pre.

**AMD is affected by the same issue. We currently only have access to NVIDIA hardware, so this PR fixes only the NVIDIA implementation for now.**

## Claims

- Restore Engram when its layer is the first layer of a non-initial pipeline stage.
- Preserve the incoming `pre_mix`, selected Engram hash column, mask, and existing no-hash behavior.
- Add a non-identity regression test to the NVIDIA model CI job.

## Validation

### Environment

- Hardware: two 8 x NVIDIA H20 96GB nodes.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`.

### vLLM launch

Both arms used identical arguments:

```bash
VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26 \
VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1 \
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --moe-backend humming \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

### Verify Engram execution at the pipeline boundary

This check verifies that layer 14 executes its trained Engram module before mHC pre when it is the first layer of a pipeline stage.

We compared three configurations using the real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint:

- **Without this PR, PP=1:** the reference configuration. Layer 14 runs within the same pipeline stage as the preceding layers.
- **Without this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`):** the configuration that exposes the bug. The first stage contains 14 layers, so the second stage starts at layer 14.
- **With this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`):** the same pipeline partition with the fix applied, tested independently on both H20 nodes.

Each configuration received the same fixed 256-token prompt and generated two tokens, each constrained to a single allowed token ID. This kept the token sequence fixed across configurations. Each configuration was run twice in eager mode.

#### Was layer 14's Engram actually executed?

| Configuration | Layer 14 Engram executed? | Input passed to layer 14's mHC pre |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Without this PR, PP=1 — reference | Yes | Engram output |
| Without this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`) | **No** | Tensor received from the previous stage, without applying Engram |
| With this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`) — both nodes | **Yes** | Engram output |

The unpatched PP=2 configuration had valid Engram hashes and masks available at layer 14, but never called its Engram module. The missing operation was therefore caused by the stage-entry control flow.

#### Did mHC receive the correct tensor?

We recorded SHA-256 checksums of the full tensors at the pipeline handoff, Engram input/output, and mHC pre input. These checksums track tensor contents; they are separate from the token hashes used by Engram.

For every TP rank, measured step, and repeat, the checks confirmed these paths:

- **Without this PR, PP=2:** the tensor sent by the previous stage was passed directly to mHC pre. Engram was skipped.
- **With this PR, PP=2:** the received tensor was passed to Engram, and Engram's output was passed to mHC pre.
- **PP=1 reference:** Engram's output was also passed to mHC pre.

These comparisons verify the data flow within each run; they do not require bitwise-identical outputs between PP=1 and PP=2.

#### Did Engram make a measurable change?

For runs that executed Engram, we measured the difference between its input and output at layer 14:

| Step | RMS of the Engram update | Tensor elements whose stored values changed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 0.03445–0.03557 | 67.22%–67.82% |
| Decode | 0.05899–0.06505 | 81.83%–83.14% |

The update RMS is `RMS(Engram output − Engram input)`. These nonzero differences confirm that skipping this trained Engram module changes the tensor passed to mHC pre.

**This check confirms that the affected PP partition skips a trained Engram operation and that this PR restores it before mHC pre on both tested nodes.** It does not establish an accuracy improvement: captured logits varied across repeated runs and nodes by an amount comparable to the patch effect. The GSM8K results below report the separate end-to-end accuracy evaluation.

### Full GSM8K comparison

Both configurations used PP=2 (`14,26`) with identical evaluation settings: 4-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, and a maximum of 8,192 output tokens.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://<node-ip>:18001/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-hub modelscope \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":4}}' \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-batch-size 64 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"max_tokens":8192,"reasoning_effort":"high","seed":42,"timeout":10000}' \
  --timeout 10000 \
  --no-timestamp
```

| Configuration | Correct / Total | Accuracy | API errors | Pod restarts |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Without this PR | 1283 / 1319 | 97.27% | 0 | 0 |
| With this PR | 1283 / 1319 | 97.27% | 0 | 0 |

Seven questions were correct only without the patch, and seven only with it; aggregate accuracy was unchanged.

**We have not observed an end-to-end accuracy loss in this GSM8K evaluation. However, the confirmed omission of a trained Engram operation remains a correctness bug with potential model-quality impact that this benchmark has not demonstrated.**

The focused regression test and full pre-commit suite also passed.

## Details

At the end of a pipeline stage, the previous rank completes its final mHC post and sends the full 3-D residual stream together with `pre_mix`. The next stage starts with `residual=None`, assigns that received stream to `residual`, and calls mHC pre directly. Because normal Engram injection lives in the following `elif`, an Engram on the stage's first layer is silently skipped.

This change injects the local Engram after accepting the completed stream and before mHC pre. It does not repeat the previous stage's post or alter first-layer embeddings, in-stage Engram execution, or batches without Engram hashes.

The real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash configuration has Engram layers 1 and 14. A pipeline partition beginning its second stage at layer 14 can therefore reach this path. Open PR searches for the same Engram pipeline-stage fix found no direct duplicate; related PCP work such as #62183 does not implement this injection.

AI assistance was used for implementation support and a read-only Codex CLI review. Human line-by-line review is still required before requesting maintainer review.

title: [CI][ROCm] Fix order-dependent test_rocm_aiter_sampler_defers_import (CPU tensors hit Triton)
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fix the `:amd: (MI355 DPX) V1 Sample shard 1/2` failure on main. It has failed on every main build since [95584](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95584):

```
FAILED tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py::test_rocm_aiter_sampler_defers_import_when_generators_force_native
ValueError: Pointer argument (at 0) cannot be accessed from Triton (cpu tensor?)
```

**Root cause:** `test_rocm_aiter_sampler_defers_import_when_generators_force_native` (added in #44823) builds `logits`/`k` with no device. When generators are present, the forward goes through the native path, so `apply_top_k_top_p` → `apply_top_k_top_p_triton` runs, which needs GPU tensors. The test only passed because an earlier test file in the same shard leaked a GPU default device. Runtime auto-sharding rebalanced the shards at 95584 (shard 1 went from 236 to 203 tests), so that file no longer runs first and the test now gets CPU tensors. None of the commits between 95583 (pass) and 95584 (fail) touch sampling.

**Fix:** create the test tensors on `DEVICE_TYPE` explicitly.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches this test (searched by test name).

## Test Plan

Not run locally (no ROCm host). CI for the MI355 V1 Sample step will confirm.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; reviewed by the submitter.

title: [CI][Release] Fix release wheel builds: stop excluding tracked recipes/ from Docker context
author: khluu
body:
## Purpose

Fix the release pipeline, broken since #61302 ([release-v2 #8603](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/8603)). The CUDA x86_64/aarch64 and ROCm wheel builds fail, which breaks every downstream image and publish step:

```
#58 0.576 Repo is dirty
ERROR: failed to solve: process "/bin/sh -c if [ \"$GIT_REPO_CHECK\" != \"0\" ]; then bash tools/check_repo.sh ; fi" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

**Root cause:** #61302 added `/recipes` to `.dockerignore`. Those 188 files are tracked, and `.git` is bind-mounted into the build, so git sees them as deleted. Two things then break:
- `tools/check_repo.sh` (`git diff --quiet`) fails release builds, which set `GIT_REPO_CHECK=1`.
- setuptools-scm stamps the wheel `...+g<sha>.dYYYYMMDD`, while the Rust frontend build pins `dirty=false`. This fails `test_show_version` in the H200 Rust Frontend OpenAI/Serve-Admin Coverage steps on main.

**Fix:** drop `/recipes` from `.dockerignore`. It's about 1.5 MB of YAML in the build context and isn't installed into the image. A new test, `test_dockerignore_keeps_tracked_root_paths`, fails if a root-anchored `.dockerignore` entry ever excludes tracked files again.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches `.dockerignore`. This supersedes #62214, which only masked the version symptom and would not fix `check_repo.sh`.

## Test Plan

- I extracted the new test's logic and ran it standalone (the repo conftest needs a full env): 188 tracked files excluded on `origin/main`, 0 on this branch.
- Release and Docker builds were not run locally; the release pipeline will confirm.

## Notes

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Apply text-only LoRAs to the LM of multimodal wrappers
author: BeichenHuang
body:
## Overview

Fixes #48019. A LoRA trained on the text-only `*ForCausalLM` of a multimodal model silently does nothing when served on the multimodal wrapper. This resolves such adapters on the model side, in `LoRAModelManager._get_lora_layer_weights`, so it works for every multimodal wrapper without per-model mapper rules.

This builds on #49525 by @fooSynaptic (co-author), which fixes the same bug through a `WeightsMapper` fallback and only covers wrappers whose mapper has a `model.language_model.` rule. This PR covers those wrappers too, plus the ones without such a rule.

## Claims

- Text-named adapters (`model.layers.*` / `lm_head`) now apply to the language model of multimodal wrappers, including wrappers with no `model.language_model.` mapper rule or a different LM prefix (`llm.`, `model.text_model.`), e.g. Llama4, DeepSeek-V4, MiniCPM-V, Idefics3/SmolVLM.
- Adapters that already match (trained on the full multimodal class), tower/connector LoRA, and text-only models are unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_utils.py tests/lora/test_lora_checkpoints.py
```

- New test `test_text_only_lora_binds_to_multimodal_language_model`: 3 passed (all 3 fail on main).
- The three files above: 58 passed.

E2E on 1x H20: one synthetic r=16 LoRA on the LM's q/k/v/o/gate/up/down_proj, saved twice: text-named (`base_model.model.model.layers.*`) and wrapper-named (`base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.*`, or `model.text_model.layers.*` for SmolVLM). Prompt logprobs of 4 prompts from vLLM base / text-named / wrapper-named, compared with an HF reference that has the LoRA merged into the weights.

Mean |Δ logprob| of the text-named adapter vs vLLM base (HF LoRA effect in parentheses):

| model | main | #49525 | this PR | this PR vs HF LoRA (wrapper-named vs HF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B-Base (0.056) | 0.0000 | 0.0534 | 0.0535 | 0.0146 (0.0134) |
| llava-1.5-7b-hf (0.060) | 0.0000 | 0.0575 | 0.0565 | 0.0126 (0.0111) |
| SmolVLM-256M-Instruct (0.104) | 0.0000 | **0.0000** | 0.0948 | 0.0486 (0.0507) |

vLLM-vs-HF base noise: 0.017 / 0.017 / 0.063. Llama4 and DeepSeek-V4 were not run (too large); they use the same `language_model.` prefix path as Qwen3.5.

## Details

**Root cause.** PEFT on the text-only class (what `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.5-*")` returns in transformers 5.x, i.e. the default TRL SFT path) names modules `model.layers.*` / `lm_head`. vLLM's multimodal wrappers mount the language model under `language_model.`, `llm.` or `model.text_model.`. `activate_adapter` looks weights up by the full module name, finds none, and serves the base model; load-time validation only checks the leaf name (`q_proj`), so nothing fails.

**Fix.** When a LoRA module has no exact match and lives under `get_mm_mapping().language_model`, look it up by its text-only name: the remainder after the prefix, or the remainder under `model.` when the prefix holds a bare decoder. All lookups, including packed (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`) and MoE packing, go through this function; text-named entries consumed by packing are dropped like the other sub-module entries.

- Exact names always win, so adapters trained on the full multimodal class are unaffected. No tower/connector prefix of any in-tree LoRA-capable multimodal model is nested under its LM prefix, so tower/connector lookups are unchanged.
- The lookup is driven by the model's real modules, so there is no double-mapping risk (e.g. `model.language_model. -> model.` mappers) and no effect on layers owned by other PP ranks.
- No change to base-weight loading or to any model's `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
- No new validation or error path, and no separate name-matching logic: the fallback lives inside the existing lookup, so any future "adapter matches nothing" check can reuse `_get_lora_layer_weights` and stay consistent with what is actually applied.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Align speculator hidden norm in GLM-4.5/4.6 MoE and GLM-OCR MTP with GLM5Next to recycle post-final-hidden.
author: spandantiwari
body:
### Overview

Three GLM-family MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) models — `glm4_moe_mtp.py` (GLM-4.5 / GLM-4.5-Air / GLM-4.6), `glm4_moe_lite_mtp.py` (GLM-4.7-Flash), and `glm_ocr_mtp.py` (GLM-OCR) — return the **pre-final-norm** hidden from the MTP layer, so the speculator recycles a hidden that is one RMSNorm short into the next draft step's `hnorm`. The established GLM/DeepSeek-NextN contract (already merged in vLLM by #47448 and also SGLang's `glm4_moe_nextn`/`deepseek_nextn` `vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py`) recycles the **post-final-norm** hidden. This PR extends that contract to the three models it missed, and registers them in `SpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple()` so Model Runner V1 unpacks the new tuple return. Draft-only change; verified output is unaffected.

**Relation to #62986:** #62986 (opened after this PR) fixes the same recycle for `Glm4MoeMTP` only, DeepSeek-style; its description offers to close in favour of this PR once the V1 registration is included, which it now is (`6ecfab6`). #62987 (enabling `torch.compile` for `Glm4MoeMTP`) is independent.

### Claims

- **Correctness/contract alignment:** each MTP layer now applies the final norm once (fused `shared_head.norm(hidden, residual)`) and returns the post-final-norm hidden for both tuple positions, with `compute_logits` consuming it directly — identical to #47448 and `glm5next`.
- **Both model runners:** Model Runner V2 unpacks tuple returns generically; Model Runner V1 (`SpecDecodeBaseProposer`) only unpacks registered architectures, so `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` and `GlmOcrMTPModel` are added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Without that, V1 crashes on the first draft step (below).
- **Lossless:** speculative decoding verifies every drafted token, so the target-visible output is unchanged; only the drafter's recycled state changes (affects draft steps ≥1, i.e. `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 2`).
- **No performance regression, and no performance claim.** On a real checkpoint (GLM-4.5-Air) a controlled, paired acceptance measurement shows **no statistically significant change** in draft acceptance (details below).

### Validation

**Drafter contract (unit, real objects):** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden`, parametrized over GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-OCR configs (shrunk). Each drafter is built by `get_model` with `load_format="dummy"` and runs its real forward. The feedback hidden must equal `shared_head.norm` of the MTP block output (captured with a forward hook), which is also what `compute_logits` used to feed the `lm_head`, so logits are unchanged.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k feeds_back_final_normed
# model files from the PR base (49f944be3e): 3 failed
E       AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E       Mismatched elements: 1536 / 1536 (100.0%)
# this PR: 3 passed
```

**Both model runners (e2e through `LLM`, real weights):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1|mrv2]` runs `zai-org/GLM-OCR` with `num_speculative_tokens=2` and asserts both draft positions are accepted. Per-position acceptance on MI355X: MRV2 `[0.610, 0.285]`, MRV1 `[0.592, 0.271]`.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py
# first commit of this PR (c10a4c9: tuple return, no V1 registration), [mrv1]:
TypeError: only integer tensors of a single element can be converted to an index
FAILED ...::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1] - EngineDeadError
# this PR: 2 passed
```

The registration itself is also covered by `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (CPU CI), extended with the three architectures. The new e2e directory runs in the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo (+ GLM)" step. `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` and `test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`: 13 passed; `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

**Test durations** (`pytest --durations=0`, single MI355X; checkpoints already cached):

| test | cases | time per case |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden` (new) | 3 | 1.1–4.9 s (GLM-4.5-Air 4.9 s, GLM-OCR 1.4 s, GLM-4.7-Flash 1.1 s) |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners` (new) | 2 | 52 s (MRV1), 94 s (MRV2, incl. `torch.compile` + CUDA-graph capture) |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (3 cases added, CPU) | 3 | < 0.5 s |

The e2e test adds about 2.5 min to the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo + GLM" step (first run also downloads `zai-org/GLM-OCR`, 2.7 GB).

**Acceptance measurement (end-to-end, fixed-prefix)** — GLM-4.5-Air (bf16), MI355X, `method=mtp`, k=3, 600 gsm8k prompts, each generating one spec-decode round from a **fixed starting prefix**, paired per prompt. Position 0 does not consume the recycled hidden, so it is a near-control (not bit-exact — see below):

| position | before (pre-norm) | after (post-norm) | diff | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p0 (near-control) | 0.7330 | 0.7298 | −0.0032 | 0.88 |
| p1 | 0.5438 | 0.5479 | +0.0042 | 0.86 |
| p2 | 0.2232 | 0.2277 | +0.0045 | 0.82 |

Paired per-prompt accepted tokens: +0.018 ± 0.016 (Wilcoxon p=0.25). The position-0 result is **statistically consistent with no change** (p=0.88); its tiny drift is floating-point from the eager→fused add+norm (mathematically identical). No affected position shows a significant change either. This is an end-to-end comparison from fixed prefixes; it does not isolate each later position's conditional acceptance, since draft histories can still diverge within a round. Net: acceptance (and thus speed) is effectively unaffected.

**Reference** — SGLang `glm4_moe_nextn.py` / `deepseek_nextn.py` apply the final norm and recycle the post-norm hidden; GLM-4-MoE NextN is a faithful DeepSeek-V3 NextN clone.

### Details

Root cause: the MTP layer forward ended with `hidden_states = residual + hidden_states; return hidden_states` (pre-final-norm), and `compute_logits` applied `shared_head` to it. The speculators store the model's returned hidden as the next step's `previous_hidden_states` (fed into `hnorm`), so the recycled state was missing the final `shared_head` RMSNorm that DeepSeek/`glm5next` apply; the logits path was always correctly single-normed. Fix (per file):

```python
hidden_states, _ = self.shared_head.norm(hidden_states, residual=residual)
return hidden_states, hidden_states
```

plus `compute_logits`: `shared_head.head, hidden_states` (drop the second norm), and the three architectures added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Affects the single-module AR path (`num_nextn_predict_layers=1`, k≥2 — the common GLM-4.5/4.6 case) and the multi-module path; k=1 is unaffected.

The two tuple elements are intentionally the same post-norm tensor, as in #47448 and `glm5next`, which go through the same recycle sites: the MRV2 AR step-0 setup stores `last_hidden_states[idx]`, MRV2 steps ≥1 and the multi-module path recycle the second element, and V1 unpacks the tuple once the architecture is registered.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Release vLLM's communicators on external-launcher shutdown
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
Motivation: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95633/list?jid=01a14c8b-4acc-4866-b9b8-e31d71cdc245&tab=output

`ExecutorWithExternalLauncher` (torchrun, `distributed_executor_backend="external_launcher"`) now destroys vLLM's model-parallel groups on shutdown, like `MultiprocExecutor`'s workers do. Without it, `:amd: (MI355) Distributed DP + EP` intermittently aborts at exit on the ROCm 10 image (#58761).

- Fixes the exit-time abort (`terminate called without an active exception`, SIGABRT on several ranks) of `examples/features/torchrun/torchrun_dp_example_offline.py --tp-size=2 --dp-size=4 --enable-ep` on MI355 with ROCm 10.
- Only vLLM-owned groups are destroyed; the world group and the default process group, which the launcher may own, are untouched.

Root cause: `UniProcExecutor.shutdown()` only calls `worker.shutdown()`. `MultiprocExecutor` additionally calls `destroy_model_parallel()` and `destroy_distributed_environment()`, which abort the PyNCCL communicators and destroy the NCCL subgroups. In external-launcher mode nothing does, so each rank exits with live RCCL communicators whose background threads are destroyed by static destructors; a `std::thread` destroyed while joinable calls `std::terminate`. ROCm 7.2's RCCL tolerates this; ROCm 10's does not, intermittently.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Report every transfer group as loaded in DecodeBenchConnector
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

`DecodeBenchConnector` fills a new request's own blocks in every KV cache group, like a P/D transfer, but it inherits the base `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, which reports only the prefix-cacheable groups (what a hash-addressed store holds). A bounded-replay sliding-window group (DeepSeek V4.1) is not prefix-cacheable, so `_load_restores_replay_window` is false and the scheduler replays the last window on the first step of every filled request. That step becomes a prefill of about one window (128 tokens on DeepSeek V4.1) instead of a one-token decode, and with DP every rank leaves the FULL decode graph whenever any rank admits a request, so decode-only benchmarks with this connector do not reflect P/D decode.

This returns `transfer_group_ids`, the same as `NixlConnector` and `MooncakeConnector` since #59197. The connector is synchronous, so `skip_zeroing_group_ids` (async loads only) is unaffected; the only change is that the filled window is taken as is.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR changes the loaded groups of `DecodeBenchConnector`. #61543 skips non-transfer groups on the fill side (a HiSparse crash) and is complementary: with both, the connector fills and reports the same `transfer_group_ids`. #59197 added the replay skip and the NIXL / Mooncake overrides but left this connector on the default.

## Test Plan

- New `test_decode_bench_fill_does_not_replay` in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py`: the real scheduler with `DecodeBenchConnector` on a full-attention + bounded-replay `SlidingWindowMLASpec` layout; a filled request must start with a one-token step and no replay. It fails without the fix (`replay_start` is 64, not 0).
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py`
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files

## Test Result

44 passed. `pre-commit` passed.

No model eval: this only changes which tokens a decode benchmark recomputes after a dummy fill; real serving and P/D connectors are untouched.
