title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve scheduling priority for online and offline beam search
author: dskwe
body:
## Overview

Preserve scheduling priority for beam search on `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`, and add priority support to offline `LLM.beam_search()`.

## Claims

- Forward the effective body/header priority to every beam expansion instead of silently falling back to engine priority `0`.
- Support offline scalar or per-prompt priorities through the existing priority normalization helper, retaining each prompt's priority across all beam expansions and concurrency batches.
- Preserve default priority `0`, the existing `X-vLLM-Priority` header precedence (including header `0`), and positional-call compatibility.

## Validation

CPU validation with the existing cached GPT2 tokenizer and deterministic mock engines; no GPU inference, real scheduler-dispatch benchmark, or model-quality evaluation. This change forwards scheduling metadata only; model execution, scoring and beam selection are unchanged. The HTTP reproducer checks request-to-engine propagation and frontend response parity, not real inference.

| Coverage | Baseline with regression | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Online beam-search suite | 2 failed / 28 passed | 30 passed |
| Completion/chat serving regressions | 4 failed / 2 passed | 6 passed |
| Beam search + offline helpers (offline extension) | 17 failed / 51 passed | 68 passed |
| Combined online/offline + neighboring serving tests | — | 129 passed |
| FastAPI TestClient ASGI reproducer, 16 cases per variant | 4 wrong-priority cases | 16/16 correct |

Offline extension in `55b256be2fb96e08a920132a9a86c3e1ccd0c050` (following the request to cover both modes in this PR): tests exercise real Python beam expansion, request submission and the engine loop with a deterministic fake engine. Cases cover omitted/None/scalar/list/tuple priorities, concurrency batches, an earlier prompt terminating, structured-output active-beam filtering (simulated selector), and mismatched priority lengths. This is request-propagation validation, not native inference or grammar-backend validation.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py \
  tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_offline_utils.py -q --disable-warnings
```

This command returned **17 failed / 51 passed** with the new tests on the previous production code, then **68 passed** with the offline extension. Patch-scoped pre-commit checks on the three newly changed files also passed, including mypy and CI test tethering. The submitter confirmed reviewing and running the offline extension before publication.

Both HTTP variants returned 200 throughout, and parsed response JSON matched after excluding only creation timestamps. The reproducer uses real frontend constructors, routing and tokenization but a deterministic mock engine.

Reproduction commands (Linux CPU test environment with test dependencies and cached GPT2 tokenizer):

```bash

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py -q --disable-warnings

  tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py \

  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_serving_chat_did_set_correct_cache_salt \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_serving_chat_data_parallel_rank_extraction \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

Before the offline extension, after rebasing onto `689effee6d07bfeb0afe42d44046141657238c23` (including #62072), the last command was re-run: **103 passed**, exit 0, including the upstream generation-config EOS regressions and this PR's priority regressions. Patch-scoped `pre-commit run --files` on all six changed files also passed, including mypy and Buildkite test-tethering checks (exit 0). Baseline failures above were observed before the production fix with the same regression tests.

Original RED/GREEN and HTTP validation base: `0c5dd18e7a0ace18d99438fb16b8375572ea76b5`. Rebased onto `689effee6d07bfeb0afe42d44046141657238c23` on October 19; resolved the test insertion conflict by retaining both the upstream EOS tests and this PR's priority tests. title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the Engram all-to-all buffers in one allocator
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 with host-offloaded, DP-sharded Engram tables (`cpu_offload: true`, `dp_shared_memory: false`, e.g. with `use_thp: true`) hangs in the first forward (memory profiling) when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set. This receives the Engram all-to-all into a persistent buffer allocated next to its send buffer, so both come from the same allocator.

No open PR covers this (searched open PRs/issues for Engram all-to-all, cumem, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER`). #62091 changes only the GPU-table path (`cpu_offload: false`), which has no all-to-all.

## Claims

- Fixes the hang: DSv4.1-Flash DEP2/DEP4 prefill with host DP-sharded Engram + `--enable-cumem-allocator` now starts and serves.
- No numerical change: the same bytes are exchanged, only the receive buffer's allocation changes. Peak memory is unchanged (the per-step `empty_like` of the same size becomes persistent).

## Validation

GB200 (4 GPUs/node), vLLM nightly 49cb2bbf image (CUDA 13.4, NCCL 2.32.3), env `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1`. The changed code is identical on main.

Serving: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-cumem-allocator --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"use_thp":true}' --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' ...` (same hang with DEP2).

| run | result |
|---|---|
| main | hangs in `determine_available_memory`; all ranks in `EngramBatch._stage` `all_to_all_single` (py-spy, also with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`), GPUs spin at 100%, NCCL watchdog fires after 600 s |
| main, no `--enable-cumem-allocator` | starts |
| main, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | starts |
| this PR | starts (profiling + CUDA graph capture); 48/48 completions with 8 to 30K-word prompts at concurrency 16 (both the all-to-all and the peer-exchange slots) |

Standalone reproducer, no model (4 GPUs):

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 repro.py [--same-pool]
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from vllm.device_allocator.cumem import CuMemAllocator

torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
dist.init_process_group("nccl")
shape = (32768 * dist.get_world_size(), 2, 6, 264)
with CuMemAllocator.get_instance().use_memory_pool(tag="weights"):
    sent = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    pool_recv = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
recv = pool_recv if "--same-pool" in sys.argv else torch.zeros_like(sent)
dist.all_to_all_single(recv, sent)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f"rank {dist.get_rank()} ok")
```

</details>

| send | recv | result |
|---|---|---|
| cumem pool | caching allocator | hangs (killed after 120 s) |
| cumem pool | cumem pool (`--same-pool`) | ok |
| cumem pool | caching allocator, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | ok |

`pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` passes. No test added: reproducing needs 4+ GPUs with NCCL 2.32 and the cumem allocator, which CI does not run for DSv4.1; validation above was done outside CI.

## Details

Root cause: `EngramBatch.__init__` runs during model init, inside the cumem pool when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set, so `packed_rows` (the all-to-all send buffer) is a cumem allocation. The receive buffer was `torch.empty_like(rows)` in each forward, from the caching allocator. With NCCL local user-buffer registration on (the default), NCCL 2.32 hangs an all-to-all whose buffers mix the two allocators; the reproducer shows this without the model. I did not pin down the NCCL-internal reason (the serving logs show FABRIC IPC registration failures for some buffers, the reproducer hangs without them).

Allocating the receive buffer next to `packed_rows` keeps both in one allocator in either mode, and removes a per-step allocation. `_stage` is an eager break, so the persistent buffer does not affect CUDA graphs.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and write this change; I reviewed every line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix] Disable CUTLASS FP4 MoE backend on sm_110
author: UsamaKenway
body:
## Overview

`CutlassExpertsFp4` claims device capability family 110, so NVFP4 MoE auto-selection picks
`VLLM_CUTLASS` on sm_110 (Jetson AGX Thor) and faults in `profile_run` instead of falling
back to Marlin.

110 has been in this predicate since #33417 normalised it from
`has_device_capability((10, 0))`, a `>=` check that sm_110 already passed. That PR was about
SM120 and was tested on an RTX PRO 6000. Doesn't look like 110 was ever tried on Thor.

## Claims

- NVFP4 MoE auto-selection on sm_110 reaches a backend that works instead of one that faults.
- Scoped to the MoE predicate. Dense NVFP4 (`cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_fp4`) is untouched
  and still works on sm_110.
- No behavioural change elsewhere: sm_100 and sm_120 evaluate identically.
- No regression in `tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py`.

## Validation

Jetson AGX Thor, sm_110, 20 SMs, 122.8 GiB unified.

`CutlassExpertsFp4._supports_current_device()` returns True before, False after. Checked
against 837e87e1c5.

Before, serving `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (512 experts):

```
Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 700
RuntimeError: run_fp4_blockwise_scaled_group_mm_sm100,
  csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/fp4/nvfp4_blockwise_moe_kernel.cu:410,
  Failed to initialize GEMM: status=7 workspace_size=261120
  num_experts=512 M=81920 N=1280 K=2560
```

After, the run gets through load, `profile_run` and KV alloc, then stops at an unrelated QSA
kernel on the same device (#56084). With that one fixed as well it serves: 0 errors, coherent
output at temperature 0.

Ran `test_cutlass_moe.py` on Thor before and after the patch, no failures either time. The
`[nvfp4]` padded-routes case goes from pass to skip, since the backend is no longer offered
on this device.

### Reproducing

You only need an sm_110 device to check the predicate.

The serving runs don't reproduce on stock vLLM. That checkpoint is ~126 GiB and the board has
122.8 GiB, so these runs mmap the 47.7 GiB PLE n-gram table from NVMe instead of holding it
resident. It's a lookup table, never a GEMM operand, so it can't affect which backend gets
picked. No upstream equivalent, #54129 was closed unmerged.

No sm_110 runner in CI, so no test added and everything above was run on hardware.

## Details

**Root cause.** `select_nvfp4_moe_backend` walks an ordered list and takes the first backend
that claims support. `VLLM_CUTLASS` sits above `MARLIN`. sm_90 falls through because it fails
the FP4 check; sm_110 passes and stops there. The fault lands in `profile_run`, after
selection, so there's no retry.

**Scope.** `cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_fp4(110)` is correct for dense, confirmed by calling
`cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm` on device. Only the grouped kernel is broken, so the MoE predicate is
the right place to fix it, not the global helper.

**Tradeoff.** Small shapes do work on CUTLASS here, the 4-expert unit test passes unpatched,
and those now go to Marlin, which is W4A16 and slower on prefill. Taking that: selection
happens once, before shapes are known, and it faults at real MoE sizes. The failure is
shape-dependent too, at 16k context the same call dies in the torch stable-ABI dispatcher
instead of TMA init.

**Why not `--moe-backend marlin`.** It's global, and this checkpoint leaves `mtp.*`
unquantized, so it dies earlier:

```
ValueError: moe_backend='marlin' is not supported for unquantized MoE.   (mtp.py:201)
```

Auto-selection has to be right because the flag can't express per-layer choice.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Wait for all peers before completing failed receives to avoid potential KV block write-after-free
author: zhou-yuhan
body:
## Overview

Address premature D-side KV block reclamation when one Mooncake P peer fails while another peer can still write to the request's destination blocks (write-after-free).

## Related

- [Improving MooncakeConnector #60523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523).
- [Mooncake bootstrap and KV transfer failures can leave PD requests waiting without terminal error propagation #55870](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55870)
- [Report failed remote KV loads to the scheduler #50984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50984): adds error handling at D-side but leaves this bug.
- [#61006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61006): guards stale scheduler notifications.
- [#50565](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50565): suppresses cleanup-only completions.
- [#57529](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57529): adds an unwired failure ledger.

These related PRs do not track outstanding peer results for a failed receive.


## Motivation

### Failure mechanism

A D request can receive KV slices from multiple P peers (P0, P1), if a peer (say P0) fails to transfer a request's KV:

1. P0 reports a transfer error while P1 still holds the destination addresses.
2. `_handle_failed_recv()` marks the request failed, reports its invalid blocks, and **adds it to `finished_recving_reqs` without waiting for the other peers**.
3. With `kv_load_failure_policy=fail`, the scheduler marks the request `FINISHED_ERROR` and consumes that completion to release its blocks.
4. P1 can subsequently write to those addresses, after the blocks have returned to the pool or been allocated to another request.

Failure notification therefore permits reclamation before all writers have finished. This is a KV-block write-after-free; the underlying registered GPU allocation remains valid, so the stale WRITE can succeed. [#50984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50984) fixed failure propagation and stranded requests; this reproducer exposes the remaining multi-peer destination-lifetime gap.

### Reproduction

Configs:

- Qwen3-32B BF16, P TP2 on node 0, D TP1 on node 1, Nvidia H20. Nodes are interconnected with 200 Gbps RoCE RDMA (per rail)
- Workload: replay Alibaba bailian [open-source in-production trace](https://github.com/alibaba-edu/qwen-bailian-usagetraces-anon) `qwen_coder_blksz_16.jsonl` with [trace-replayer](https://giohub.com/blitz-serving/trace-replayer). Replayed for 1800s

<details>
<summary>Launch commands</summary>

```bash
# P instance
vllm serve /home/models/Qwen3-32B \
    --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 40960 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 16 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --port 8100 --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'

# D instance
vllm serve /home/models/Qwen3-32B \
    --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 40960 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 16 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --port 8200 --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'

# vllm-router
vllm-router --vllm-pd-disaggregation --kv-connector mooncake \
    --prefill "http://$P_IP:8100" 8998 --decode "http://$D_HOST:8200" \
    --intra-node-data-parallel-size 1 --policy round_robin --disable-retries \
    --request-timeout-secs "$REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS" --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
    --prometheus-host 127.0.0.1 --prometheus-port 29000

# trace-replayer
trace-replayer --tokenizer /home/models/Qwen3-32B/tokenizer.json \
    --tokenizer-config /home/models/Qwen3-32B/tokenizer_config.json \
    --api openai --dataset bailian --hash-block-size 16 --dataset-path qwen_coder_blksz_16.jsonl \
    --stream --scale-factor 0.1 --ttft-slo "$REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS" --tpot-slo 0 \
    --threads 16 --num-producer 16 --channel-capacity 1024 \
    --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    --time-in-secs 1800
```

</details>

To trigger and observe the subtle write-after-free bug, we manually simulate P0 failed write and P1 delayed write: P0 reports `err_reqs` through its existing `MooncakeXferResponse` after a successful WRITE with 5% failure rate per request; P1 waits for a randomly sampled 0–500 ms before submitting WRITE (batch delay = maximum selected-request delay). D's failure/reclamation logic and RDMA network configuration are unchanged.

We add tracing hooks for each kv block and analyze the dumped traces offline after experimental runs, matching successful WRITE starts and target addresses to block generations, pool returns, and subsequent owners:

| Requests | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Total; all with actual writes from both P peers | 791 |
| P0 experimental failures | 33 |
| **P1 WRITE started after destination block free** | 21 |
| **Of those, P1 WRITE started after block reallocation** | 20 |

## Solution

Each peer keeps a pending request map sharing the existing `PullReqMeta` (`pull_metas.copy()` shallow copy). Success and failure both consume that peer's entry and decrement `pull_tasks_count`, including success after another peer failed. Report the first failure once; publish receives completion only when the count reaches zero. Partial replies, peer-wide errors, and receive exceptions settle only pending entries.

On `FINISH`, requests still pending for that peer are considered to be failed and are settled, covering expired requests omitted by P (otherwise, P0 expires + P1 successes -> `pull_tasks_count` remains positive and D's KV blocks would never be released -- also a mem-leak bug left in the current implementation).

Bootstrap failures with no peer tasks still complete; empty pulls produce no D completion. The fix is confined to connector bookkeeping. It covers error replies followed by the other peers' results; remote quiescence after a local
socket timeout remains outside its scope.

## Validation

### Unit Tests

All relevant unit tests pass (with two added unit tests related to this bug)

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_error_propagation.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
    vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py
```

</details>

### E2E Result

The E2E run config is the same as in the Reproduction section. With fixed:

| Requests | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total; all with actual writes from both P peers | 791 | 791 |
| P0 experimental failures| 33 | 39 |
| **P1 WRITE started after destination block free** | **21** | **0** |
| **Of those, after block reallocation** | **20** | **0** |

All 39 P0 errors reached D before P1's WRITE ended; 31 arrived before it started. Every failed receive followed **all WRITE ends -> receive completion -> scheduler consumption -> block pool return**. Thus the reproduced write-after-free did not recur.

---

title: [Bugfix][Anthropic] Map vLLM error types to Anthropic error.type vocabulary
author: zyulai
body:
## Overview

Part of #57997. `translate_error_response()` now maps vLLM's internal error types to Anthropic's documented `error.type` vocabulary (e.g. `not_found_error`, `invalid_request_error`, `api_error`) instead of copying names like `NotFoundError`.

The validation-envelope half of #57997 is already covered by open PR #58023, so this PR intentionally does not touch that path.

## Claims

- Unknown model on `/v1/messages` returns `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"not_found_error",...}}` while keeping HTTP 404.
- Other statuses map to Anthropic types: 400/422 -> `invalid_request_error`, 401 -> `authentication_error`, 403 -> `permission_error`, 404 -> `not_found_error`, 413 -> `request_too_large`, 429 -> `rate_limit_error`, 5xx -> `api_error`, 529 -> `overloaded_error`.
- HTTP status code and message are preserved.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU-only):

```text
python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_error_type_mapping.py -q
12 passed
```

End-to-end on `main` at `3f1b04e045` with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` on an RTX 2080 Ti (Triton attention backend); the branch is rebased onto `072c0886`:

Before:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"NotFoundError","message":"The model `does-not-exist` does not exist. Valid aliases: Qwen3.5-4B."}}
HTTP 404
```

After:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"not_found_error","message":"The model `does-not-exist` does not exist. Valid aliases: Qwen3.5-4B."}}
HTTP 404
```

Control: the same validation error on `/v1/messages` still uses the existing OpenAI-shaped envelope (`HTTP 400`), confirming this PR only changes `error.type` translation.

## Details

Root cause: `translate_error_response()` copied `ErrorResponse.error.type` verbatim. vLLM builds that field from internal exception class names (`NotFoundError`, `BadRequestError`, `InternalServerError`, ...), but Anthropic SDKs dispatch on the snake_case values defined by the Anthropic API.

Approach: derive the Anthropic type from the HTTP status code, which `create_error_response()` already sets consistently, and fall back to `api_error` for 5xx / `invalid_request_error` for other 4xx. This also normalizes `GracefulHTTPError`, whose type is currently an HTTP phrase (e.g. `"Bad Request"`).

Tradeoff: status-based mapping is intentionally coarse. Anthropic's public API distinguishes `request_too_large` (413) and `overloaded_error` (529), which the mapping handles explicitly. Other 4xx statuses collapse to `invalid_request_error`, matching Anthropic's client-facing behavior.

## Not duplicating existing work

- #58023 covers the validation-envelope half (`RequestValidationError` handling) and is still open; this PR does not modify it.
- #43380 adds a `VLLMValidationError -> invalid_request_error` branch at 400 for the two endpoints; this PR generalizes the mapping in `translate_error_response()` for all statuses, including 404/429/5xx.
- #59968 fixes authentication-middleware envelopes; that path does not go through `translate_error_response()`.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Codex). The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, and reproduced the fix end-to-end with a real model server.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Preserve DP replica index for standalone draft models
author: MuonChaser
body:
## Overview

Preserve the target DP replica index when constructing a standalone
`method="draft_model"` model. This prevents separate replicas from sharing
device-bound compiled draft artifacts and fixes a reproduced DP=2 warm-cache
startup failure. Follow-up to #62285 and the standalone analysis on #62062;
the root-cause analysis and suggested restoration were reported by @Siquan-Li.

#62062 currently changes DFlash/DSpark paths; this PR fixes the standalone
`draft_model` loader and does not duplicate those changes.

## Claims

- Restore the replica index after draft config construction and before loading
  the model. General `ParallelConfig` semantics and sibling speculators are
  unchanged.
- Isolate draft compilation/AOT artifacts by replica. Existing loader
  regressions cover zero and nonzero target indices.
- Fix the observed warm-cache `CUDA driver error: invalid argument`; do not
  claim an accuracy improvement or serving speedup.

## Validation

61 targeted CPU cases passed:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py -q
```

The scoped regression without the fix fails for the three nonzero-index cases;
rank-zero controls pass. It is part of the existing Buildkite
`v1-executor-worker` suite. Scoped pre-commit checks passed during
implementation; upstream pre-commit execution is currently gated by
contributor eligibility.

[Raw commands, server logs, evaluation outputs/samples and benchmark outputs/per-request JSON](https://github.com/MuonChaser/vllm/releases/tag/pr-62301-validation-20261019).

The end-to-end validation used the public Apache-2.0 model
[`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B) as both target and
draft, pinned to public revision
`c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`.
The equivalent public-model reproducer is:

```bash
export MODEL_ID=Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
export MODEL_REVISION=c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/vllm-62301/cache/vllm
export TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-62301/cache/inductor
export TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-62301/cache/triton

.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model "$MODEL_ID" \
  --revision "$MODEL_REVISION" \
  --served-model-name probe \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 18986 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-backend mp \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.15 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --seed 256 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$MODEL_ID\",\"revision\":\"$MODEL_REVISION\",\"method\":\"draft_model\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

Start once with fresh cache directories, stop after startup/serving, then run
the identical command again without deleting the caches. On the pinned main
baseline `494663940b9b44f667c4f61c8c2407ba8e725ceb`, the warm restart fails with
`CUDA driver error: invalid argument`; at PR commit
`b2303c5e49471603cd31c1904352ad7d99164dbd`, cold and warm starts both serve.
The full raw logs retain the original local snapshot path so the executed argv
is not rewritten after the fact; the updated command uses the corresponding
public model revision.

GPU experiment: 2 H100 PCIe 80GB per arm, DP=2/MP, MRV2, BF16, compilation
enabled, CUDA graphs disabled. Both arms start with a fresh shared compilation
cache, then restart without removing it. The failure/fix was reproduced over
two separate cold/warm cycles per arm, with nonzero speculative acceptance on
both replicas. The 16-request smoke outputs, finish reasons and token counts
match across successful arms.

Full GSM8K (`lm_eval` 0.4.13, 5-shot, 1,319 questions, greedy, seed 256):
default-mode accuracy was **41.39% baseline vs 40.71% PR**. Unchanged-baseline
repeats also varied (48/128 vs 46/128; prefix cache not reset). A separate
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` comparison produced identical responses for all 1,319
questions (40.33% each), with compilation still enabled. These controls do not
rule out a default-mode regression; all raw results are retained.

Three sequential `vllm bench serve` runs per arm used 128 prompts, input
256/output 128, concurrency 8, 16 warmups and fixed seed 256: **768 measured
requests and zero failures**. Shared GPU load and repeated prefix-cache effects
prevent an isolated-GPU speedup/non-regression claim.

Source is the full Python tree at main baseline
`494663940b9b44f667c4f61c8c2407ba8e725ceb` and PR
`b2303c5e49471603cd31c1904352ad7d99164dbd`, using official nightly
native/build-supplied files from parent
`3c13653738dad0acd877c23373816fefffbdd373` (PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Python
3.12.13). Native-source files do not change between the wheel parent and
baseline; CUDA kernels were not rebuilt. This is not a claim about the latest
moving main. Both arms disable the unavailable optional FlashInfer
sampler/toolchain. Same-model serving/cache validation does not establish
different-draft quality or broader model coverage.

## Details

Independent dense DP stores replica identity in `data_parallel_index` while its
distributed DP rank is reset to zero. Constructing the draft config with
`replace` reconstructs the parallel config and resets the index. Restoring the
target index before `get_model` gives distinct `rank_0_0`/`rank_0_1` draft
caches. No steady-state inference operation or synchronization is added.

AI assistance was used for implementation and to execute/document these
validations. The detailed results were collected by the agent and do not
represent independent human-run H100 validation.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: load checkpoints with quantized q/k/v and a BF16 QSA indexer
author: srkim-business
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62308. Since #59533, `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` lists `indexer.index_qk_proj`. Quant configs read that class-level mapping before the model is built, so they check q/k/v and the QSA indexer as one fused layer. Checkpoints that quantize q/k/v but keep the indexer in BF16 fail to load with `Found different quantization schemes for the shards of ...qkv_proj`.

This PR keeps the indexer out of the mapping that quant configs see, and fuses it into `qkv_proj` only when both resolve to the same quant method.

## Claims

- Checkpoints with quantized q/k/v and a BF16 indexer load again, for example `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ`. Their indexer runs as its own GEMM, as before #59533.
- No change for BF16, ModelOpt FP4, and checkpoints that treat q/k/v and the indexer the same way: the indexer stays fused.
- The `--enable-lora` mapping override is removed. It is no longer needed, and it never reached the quant config.

## Validation

End to end on 4x A100-PCIE-40GB (TP4 + EP) with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image built from `1b2a666` (2026-10-18). Its `model.py` and `qsa.py` match this PR's base `371745e`; for "after", the two files from this PR were mounted over them. A test-only hook (not part of this PR) logged the fusion decision of every QSA layer.

| Checkpoint | Code | Server start | QSA layers (12 per worker, 4 workers) | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ` (q/k/v W4A16, indexer BF16) | before | fails: `ValueError: Found different quantization schemes ... layers.3.self_attn.qkv_proj` | - | - |
| same | after | ok | 48/48 unfused: `QKVParallelLinear` (`CompressedTensorsWNA16`) + BF16 `index_qk_proj` | GSM8K 86.2% (n=500), 0 invalid |
| `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AWQ-INT4` (attention BF16) | before | ok | 48/48 fused (`Qwen4ExpQSAQKVIndexerLinear`) | - |
| same | after | ok | 48/48 fused, same layer and quant method | sample request ok |

Both GPU runs used an earlier revision of the fusion check. The final check makes the same decision for both checkpoints: different quant methods for Swift, the same for cyankiwi.

GSM8K (an API key header was added by a small wrapper):

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8002 --use-chat-completions \
  --model swift-1.5-flash-next-awq --reasoning-effort none --num-shots 0 \
  --num-questions 500 --max-tokens 512 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 32
```

The default 5-shot completions mode does not suit this model family: it emits EOS right after `Answer:` once the prompt is longer than about 400 tokens, on vLLM and on llama.cpp alike.

- Unit test (CPU): `test_qkv_proj_mapping_allows_bf16_indexer` in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py`. With the old mapping, both cases fail with the error from #62308.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passed.
- CI: the test runs in the existing CPU Qwen4 Exp step (`qwen4-exp-unit-tests-cpu`). CI has no Flash-Next checkpoint with this layout (about 165 GB), so the end-to-end load is validated only as above.

## Details

- Root cause: `configure_quant_config` passes the class-level `packed_modules_mapping` to the quant config before `__init__` runs. Even the plain `QKVParallelLinear` built before fusion is resolved as a four-shard layer. The LoRA branch rebinds the mapping on the instance, so the quant config never saw it.
- Change:
  - `packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` is `["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"]` for both model classes.
  - `Qwen4ExpQSAAttention` builds q/k/v and the indexer as before, then fuses only if both resolve to the same quant method type. Without a quant config for the fused layer (BF16, or ModelOpt FP4 via `without_modelopt_fp4`) it fuses as before.
- Limitation: if q/k/v and the indexer are both quantized with the same quant method but a different scheme or parameters (bits or group size), they are still fused, and loading fails at weight loading. I have not seen a checkpoint with this layout.
- I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, the code and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

---

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Finalize the NIXL DCP interleave size before profiling
author: NickLucche
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

NIXL P/D + DCP resolved the KV-cache interleave after profiling, allowing sparse indexers and compiled graphs to consume a stale value. Resolve global cache groups first, finalize interleave once in the engine core, and assign the resolved value on workers before profiling.

Builds on the root-cause analysis and global-group approach in #60671 by @andylolu2, and incorporates @LucasWilkinson's [suggestion](https://github.com/NickLucche/vllm/pull/13). This updates the existing alternative PR; it retains the legacy interleave field and CLI behavior that #60671 removes.

## Claims

- The engine builds global KV-cache groups before profiling and reuses them for final allocation.
- `VllmConfig.finalize_kv_cache_layout` resolves NIXL DCP interleave once in the engine core. `set_kv_cache_layout(layout_name, cp_kv_cache_interleave_size)` sends the resolved values to workers, which only assign them.
- Connector initialization no longer adjusts interleave. Sparse indexers read the shared configuration directly instead of maintaining a separate lazy cache.

## Validation

**Current revision, CPU:** 85 tests passed, including the new core-to-worker startup test with different worker block sizes and an explicit interleave override, plus empty-group handling. All pre-commit hooks passed on the combined changed files, including mypy and test-CI tethering.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/engine/test_kv_cache_group_metadata.py \
  tests/test_config.py::test_pd_dcp_interleave_size_is_adjusted_to_block_size \
  tests/test_config.py::test_kv_offloading_does_not_adjust_dcp_interleave_size \
  tests/test_config.py::test_finalizing_empty_kv_cache_layout_preserves_interleave \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py
```

**GPU serving/model evaluation has not been rerun for the global-group revision.** The results below validate the earlier worker-local revision and are retained as historical evidence. A NIXL + DCP serving rerun is still required for the updated startup flow. The new CPU tests run through the existing V1 Engine CI step; they do not replace GPU validation.

<details>
<summary>Earlier revision: GPU reproducer and model evaluation</summary>

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5next`, MRV2), real weights, 1x GB300 node, TP4 + DCP4, NIXL `kv_both`, GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions:

| Build | Configuration | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main (`e80b6c642f`) | Automatic interleave | Startup fails: compressed indexer requires interleave to be a multiple of 4; profiling still sees 1 |
| main (`e80b6c642f`) | Explicit `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4` | 0.921 |
| Earlier worker-local revision of this PR | Automatic interleave resolved to 4 before profiling | 0.920 |

```bash
VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --decode-context-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --language-model-only \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}'
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

The earlier dummy-weight `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` reproducer (`index_topk`, TP2 + DCP2, NIXL `kv_both`, compilation mode 0 and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs) observed indexer/metadata values of 1/64 during serving on main, versus 64/64 with early finalization. Its tokens/logprobs matched an explicit-interleave workaround. Dummy weights did not measure accuracy impact.

</details>

## Details

Startup order:

1. Load models and update backend block sizes.
2. Resolve the layout and global cache groups in the engine.
3. Finalize interleave once in the engine using the global groups, then send the resolved layout and interleave to workers for assignment before profiling.
4. Profile memory; allocate from the previously computed global groups.
5. Initialize the connector and capture serving graphs.

The existing layout RPC carries the resolved interleave alongside the layout name. The core owns resolution; workers assign the value to their existing `ParallelConfig`, preserving model-held references. Global groups stay in the core for final allocation. No additional RPC or configuration field is introduced.

The temporary KV cache used for CUDA-graph memory profiling still uses the model runners' existing local grouping. The core reuses its global groups for interleave resolution and final allocation; it does not redesign temporary profiling allocation or synchronize separate draft-model config copies.

Out-of-tree `set_kv_cache_layout` overrides must accept the resolved interleave argument. The legacy `dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` field and its current precedence rules are retained.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Don't count content-free chunks as streamed outputs in chat
author: dilberx
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The chat benchmark clients count the opening role-only chunk as a streamed output, so TTFT is measured to a chunk with no output in it and the first real token appends a spurious ITL sample. A check prevented this between #3768 and #12288; this restores it in a form that also handles `reasoning` and `tool_calls`. Original report: #3759.

Benchmark client only. No engine, scheduler or serving code is touched, and no measured figure here reflects a change in how fast vLLM runs.

## Claims

- TTFT for `--backend openai-chat` is measured to the opening `delta: {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}` chunk, which carries no output.
- As a result 208 of 600 requests recorded `len(itl) == output_tokens`, which cannot happen when every interval sits between two tokens; there are at most `output_tokens - 1`. `/v1/completions` on the same server recorded exactly 200 x 255 samples and zero impossible counts.
- Every request on `main` carried a first ITL sample timing the role chunk, median 4 microseconds, so the minimum and low percentiles time metadata arrival. The error runs in the flattering direction: `main` reports chat as slightly faster than it is. With the fix, the minimum and each request's first sample rise to real decode intervals, and vLLM's actual speed is unchanged.
- This does **not** materially change any printed summary metric. Mean and median TTFT, ITL and TPOT all move by less than the run-to-run spread. The fix is to the sample array, which `--save-detailed` writes to JSON.
- 43 lines across the two clients, no new abstraction, no change to `async_request_openai_completions` or `async_request_openai_audio`.

## Validation

Four behaviours added to `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, parametrized over the packaged and legacy clients. 18 tests to 26, all passing. All eight fail against current `main`:

| behaviour | fails on `main` as |
|---|---|
| opening role chunk is not a streamed output | `assert 5 == (5 - 1)` on the interval count |
| mid-stream content-free chunk adds no interval | `assert 4 == (3 - 1)` |
| stream with no streamed output is rejected | `assert not output.success`; `main` marks it successful |
| token rendering as an empty string is counted | `assert len(output.itl) == 2`, got 3, TTFT on the role chunk |

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v
```

`pre-commit run --files` clean on all three files. The test file gains 188 lines and loses 2: two small chunk builders, `_role_chunk` and `_empty_chunk`, the four tests, and the module docstring reworded to describe them. The two removed lines are the old docstring wording. No existing test function is modified and no other test file is touched.

End-to-end on one RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B`, three interleaved blocks per side against a single server, 200 requests each, 600 per side, 256 output tokens, concurrency 64:

```
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B --port 8031 --backend openai-chat \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random --num-prompts 200 \
  --output-len 256 --max-concurrency 64 --save-result --save-detailed
```

Across those 600 requests on `main`:

- all 600 had a first sample under 0.1 ms, timing the arrival of the role chunk, median 0.0040 ms. That is exactly one spurious sample per request and never more than one, and it is what drags the reported minimum ITL down to 0.0025 ms.
- 208 recorded `len(itl) == output_tokens`, more intervals than exist between that many tokens. These are the requests where no two tokens happened to share a read, so nothing offset the extra sample. The other 392 carried it too and landed under the limit.

On this branch, no request records `len(itl) == output_tokens` and none exceeds `output_tokens - 1`. Two of 600 had a first sample under 0.1 ms, both from two tokens arriving in a single read.

Total sample counts are not compared here. They differ between separate runs against a live server because the server coalesces tokens differently each time, so a gap between two runs' totals is not evidence of anything.

`/v1/completions` on the same server, same workload, recorded exactly 51,000 samples for 200 requests of 256 tokens, which is 200 x 255, and no impossible counts.

<details>
<summary>Printed summary metrics, which do not meaningfully change</summary>

Pooled over the three blocks per side, with the spread across `main`'s own three blocks for comparison:

| metric | main | this branch | delta | main's block spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mean TTFT | 463.74 ms | 251.13 ms | -212.61 | 724.23 |
| Median TTFT | 332.08 ms | 232.07 ms | -100.01 | 442.91 |
| P99 TTFT | 2465.88 ms | 423.67 ms | -2042.21 | 2293.71 |
| Mean ITL | 8.99 ms | 6.11 ms | -2.88 | 8.71 |
| Median ITL | 4.81 ms | 4.73 ms | -0.07 | 0.08 |
| P99 ITL | 114.96 ms | 53.65 ms | -61.32 | 71.91 |
| Mean TPOT | 8.94 ms | 5.98 ms | -2.96 | 8.79 |

Every delta is smaller than the spread between `main`'s own blocks, so none of it is a real difference; the pooled TTFT gap is mostly `main`'s first block being a cold start. The role chunk and the first token arrive about 4 microseconds apart, against swings of 85 ms in Mean TTFT between `main`'s two warm blocks alone.

The GPU also drives a display and was not idle during these runs. That is why the comparison is interleaved and why the spread column is included.

</details>

## Details

### Root cause

#3759 reported a chat TTFT of 0.005 s and printed the chunk it had been measured to, a role-only delta with `content: null`. @ywang96 identified the role chunk as the cause and #3768 added:

```python
delta = data["choices"][0]["delta"]
if delta.get("content", None):
```

#12288 restructured the same block to read token counts from the usage chunk. That required tolerating a trailing chunk with `choices: []`, since `data["choices"][0]` raises on it, and the gate became:

```python
if choices := data.get("choices"):
    content = choices[0]["delta"].get("content")
```

`content` is still read but no longer decides anything. The packaged client in `vllm/benchmarks/lib/` has the same shape. #3768's own note explains why nothing caught it: "This does not affect existing CI results since by default vLLM uses completions instead of chat completions for benchmarking."

### Tokens that render as empty strings

#12288 left this note on the completions side:

```python
if choices := data.get("choices"):
    # Note that text could be empty here
    # e.g. for special tokens
    text = choices[0].get("text")
```

That is correct: a token can decode to an empty string under `skip_special_tokens=True`, and dropping it would lose a real interval. #3768's truthiness gate would drop it. So the check here tests whether the chunk carries a token:

```python
if delta.get("content") or delta.get("reasoning") or delta.get("tool_calls") or delta.get("function_call"):
    return True
return delta.get("content") == "" and "role" not in delta
```

The two cases are distinguishable on the wire. An empty-rendering token serialises as `{"content": ""}`. The opening chunk serialises as `{"role": "assistant", "content": ""}`, and `role` is set only there, on the first iteration of `chat_completion_stream_generator`, and on no other `DeltaMessage` in the streaming path. A suppressed or finish chunk serialises as `{}`. A third-party server that repeats `role` on every chunk is unaffected, because a chunk with real content satisfies the first condition.

Three of the four fields, `content`, `reasoning` and `tool_calls`, are what vLLM's own streaming logger checks to decide whether a delta carried anything, in the same file. `function_call` is the fourth and vLLM never emits it; it is there because OpenAI's legacy spec puts it on streaming deltas and these clients are pointed at third-party OpenAI-compatible servers too.

### Tradeoffs and notes

The gate is a named helper with one call site per file, which §3.3 of the PR checklist would normally have inlined. It is kept because the two clients must stay in sync, per #55508, and a shared name makes a divergence between them visible; and because the second condition needs the comment explaining why an empty string counts, which reads badly inline.

Content-free chunks now reach the `elif usage:` branch, which the `if choices:` arm used to swallow. Under `continuous_usage_stats` the opening chunk carries both `choices` and `usage`, so its `completion_tokens: 0` is read and then overwritten by every later chunk. For servers that attach usage to an empty finish chunk with no trailing `choices: []` chunk, the count is now captured where it was dropped before.

`most_recent_timestamp` advances only inside the gated branch, so #55508's `latency - ttft == sum(itl)` guarantee is unchanged. #54708's rejection of tokenless streams is unchanged and now also fires on a stream whose chunks all carry content-free `choices`.

### Relation to #46652

#46652 proposed inserting zero-duration ITL samples so `len(itl)` matched the token count. `docs/benchmarking/cli.md` says ITL records only the gaps between streamed outputs and adds no zero-duration gaps for tokens in the same output, so #46652 is closed. This PR removes a sample with no output on either side of it. Both came out of #27485, which the stale bot closed; the reasoning and tool-parser case reported there is a different cause.

### Duplicate check

Nobody is fixing this. Every reference to #3759, #3768 and #12288 across issues and PRs is a coincidental numeric match; the 190 hits for 12288 are hidden and intermediate sizes. The regression was never re-reported after #12288 merged, so #3759 is still the only issue describing it.

A search by fix shape found nothing either. No PR restores a content gate, and `_choice_has_streamed_output` has no hits. #55508 touched this exact function on 2026-09-13 to make TTFT and latency accounting consistent across endpoints and left the gate ungated. #28183 attempted per-token ITL from continuous usage stats and was closed unmerged without adding a gate.

Open PRs touching either client file are #49720, #51155, #51172, #55719, #57519 and #58734. None modify the chunk gating. My own #46652 is in this area and is being closed.

#59722 is related. It reports the Rust `vllm-bench` chat backend counting token-less streams as successful and notes that Python fails them, which is true for the case tested there: a stream with no `choices` chunks at all, which `first_chunk_received` already rejects. It is not true for a stream whose chunks all carry content-free `choices`, which is the third behaviour above.

title: [Bugfix][Security] muse: fix quadratic attribute scans in tool-call extraction
author: LeizhenZhang
body:
## Overview

Bound Muse's ATEM attribute scans to a single tag and avoid reparsing tool calls on streaming deltas that cannot complete an invocation. This updates the existing fix after review; it does not add a separate parser or change the shared parser interface.

## Claims

- Attribute searches stop at the next `<` instead of scanning across repeated unterminated tags.
- Tool-call parsing runs when a delta completes `</atem:invoke>`, including split delimiters and the initial handoff. The emitted-call cursor never moves backwards between invocations.
- The rebase preserves #64518's `_parameter_types(request)` handling, including union, enum and `$ref` schemas.

## Validation

Rebased onto `81f1baa7318155cddfb45968c5ae1cf34fcb5ca0` on November 3. Fresh local validation uses the source parser and real vLLM protocol classes, Python 3.12.4 and torch 2.13.0+cu130:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest -q \
  tests/tool_use/test_muse.py tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer.py
# 139 passed in 47.13s, with repository conftests

ruff check vllm/tool_parsers/muse_tool_parser.py tests/tool_use/test_muse.py
ruff format --check vllm/tool_parsers/muse_tool_parser.py tests/tool_use/test_muse.py
git diff --check 81f1baa7318155cddfb45968c5ae1cf34fcb5ca0
# all passed (Ruff 0.14.0)
```

The pytest command ran through `uv run --no-project --python <existing-venv>/bin/python --with orjson`; the temporary dependency overlay leaves the shared environment unchanged. No protocol or tokenizer import stubs were used. Existing tests cover schema typing, parallel calls, channel routing and split streaming markers. The new streaming regression constructs a real `ChatCompletionRequest`; its counter wraps and calls the original parser implementation. A separate direct-parser run with `--noconftest` also passed all 139 tests.

Negative control: copied the two regression tests into an isolated upstream `ab9f51f1010ce94f572ba916ef84d8d90f519dea` checkout and ran:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/tool_use/test_muse.py \
  -k 'attribute_scan_stops_at_the_tag_boundary or streaming_parses_once_per_completed_invoke'
# FAILED test_attribute_scan_stops_at_the_tag_boundary:
#   repeated open tags incorrectly match the name attribute
# FAILED test_streaming_parses_once_per_completed_invoke:
#   AssertionError: pad=0 chunk=1: parsed 217x over 218 deltas
# 2 failed, 112 deselected
```

Both pass with this fix. The two additional upstream commits through `81f1baa731` only change ROCm build/CI files; the parser, test files and type-check configuration are identical to the tested upstream base.

Type-check comparison: `python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.11 vllm/tool_parsers/muse_tool_parser.py tests/tool_use/test_muse.py` with mypy 1.20.2 and the pinned hook dependencies reports one `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`/`TokenizerLike` constructor error on both upstream (line 205) and this head (line 211). No additional errors appear in the changed files; this is not a passing type-check result.

Validation limits: tests use the supported CPU target because the source-tree GPU native extension is unavailable. No Muse checkpoint/tokenizer or live serving evaluation was available, so this is not an end-to-end serving or GPU test result. Buildkite's entrypoints API-server-generate step selects `tool_use` and depends on both changed paths; fresh remote CI remains separate from local results.

## Details

The attribute classes previously allowed `<`, so a failed attribute search could restart at each open tag and rescan the remaining suffix. Restricting those classes to `[^<>]` preserves ordinary ATEM attributes while stopping that cross-tag search.

An invocation cannot be returned before its closing tag. The streaming gate checks a window extending `len(close) - 1` characters before the new delta, so delimiters split across deltas still trigger parsing. `max(previous_count, len(calls))` preserves the emission cursor on deltas that do not parse.

The merge conflict was caused by #64518 replacing `_string_parameters()` with schema-aware `_parameter_types()`. The rebased gate calls the new helper; none of that upstream schema logic is reverted.

This does **not** make total streaming work linear: `_visible_channels(current_text)` still runs on every delta, and `_INVOKE_RE` is unchanged. No engine, scheduler, model-runner or GPU synchronization code changes.

<details>
<summary>Historical performance evidence from the pre-rebase implementation</summary>

Earlier measurements used the real parser module with protocol/tokenizer import stubs, not a live server. For 26 KB of repeated opening tags closed by one `</atem:invoke>`, fed in four-character deltas:

| Path | Original | Attribute fix only | Both fixes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Non-streaming | 1849 ms | 0.99 ms | 0.98 ms |
| Streaming | >25000 ms | 19448 ms | 378 ms |

These are historical microbenchmarks, not fresh-head throughput or end-to-end latency claims. Fresh validation above replaces the previous stub-based pytest results.
</details>

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Restore LoRA state on wake-up from level-2 sleep
author: HollowMan6
body:
## Overview

Waking from level-2 sleep without `reload_weights()` / `finish_weight_update()` left LoRA GPU state with garbage contents: the TP logits reindex mapping, the adapter slots and the punica metadata. They were allocated inside the `weights` cumem pool, which level-2 sleep discards. This PR allocates them in the existing `runtime` pool instead, which sleep offloads and restores at every level, so they come back intact on wake-up.

## Claims

- **TP logits mapping (TP > 1):** after such a wake-up, every request (LoRA or not) produced corrupted output. The mapping now survives level-2 sleep.
- **Adapter slots (any TP):** active adapters stayed bound to garbage slots, so LoRA requests silently decoded as the base model. Slots, slot layout, LRU order and pins now survive level-2 sleep; nothing is reloaded from disk.
- **Scope:** `LoRAModelRunnerMixin.load_lora_model` builds the LoRA manager inside `use_memory_pool(tag="runtime")` when sleep mode is on (CUDA/ROCm), so MRV1 and MRV2 are both covered. No worker or LoRA-manager changes. SGLang avoids the same problem by initializing LoRA after, and outside, its weights memory-saver region.
- **Cost:** level-2 sleep now copies the LoRA slots (`max_loras` x layer size x rank) to host memory, as level 1 already did, instead of discarding them.
- **Affected flows:** `sleep_preserve_parameter_names`, or weights updated in place by user code (the "Update the weights" step of the RLHF flow in the sleep-mode docs). `reload_weights()` and the weight-transfer API are unchanged and still reset LoRA state.
- **Not covered:** XPU, where nested memory pools are not supported (same exception as the KV-init runtime pool in `gpu_worker.py`).
- **Tests:** `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` checks the mapping right after weights wake-up (fails on main).

## Validation

**Current approach** (LoRA state in the `runtime` pool), 4x GB200, nightly image plus a Python overlay of this branch:

| Check | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` (new post-wake mapping assertion) | fails at the new assertion | passed |
| `tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py` (incl. `test_deep_sleep_lora`, reload path) | — | 14 passed, 1 skipped |
| `tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_worker.py tests/lora/test_layers.py -k "not slow"` | — | 124 passed, 72 skipped |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py test_sleep_mode_backend.py test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py test_kv_cache_allocation_scope.py` | — | 53 passed |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct + random LoRA, `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["*"]`, TP=1/2 x MRV1/MRV2: level-1; level-2 wake all at once; level-2 wake weights before KV cache; level-2 + `reload_weights()` | level-2 without reload: LoRA output differs from before sleep (4/4) | LoRA and base output match before sleep in every case (4/4) |
| `pre-commit` (incl. mypy) | — | passed |

**Previous approaches** (non-persistent mapping buffer plus slot restore from the CPU cache, commits 3da430e and c5e4b17; then `reset_lora_state()` on wake-up, 861e916 and 1133305; both superseded). Everything below in this section was measured on the first of these:

2x H20, torch 2.14.0+cu130. Every reproducer does a level-2 sleep with `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["*"]`, then wakes up without `reload_weights()`, with greedy decoding and `enforce_eager=True`.

**Mapping** (`hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`, no LoRA request):

| Build | TP | Output after wake-up vs. before sleep |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 2 | mismatch (decodes to `''`) |
| this PR | 2 | match |
| main | 1 (no mapping; control) | match |

**Adapter slots** (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with LoRA adapters, LoRA requests):

| Build | TP / runner | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | TP=1 MRV1, TP=1 MRV2, TP=2 MRV2 | LoRA requests return base-model output |
| this PR | TP=1 MRV2, TP=2 MRV2 (waking everything at once, and weights before KV cache) | match; slot contents bit-exact vs. before sleep (SHA-256, every cycle) |
| this PR | TP=1 MRV1 | slots bit-exact; see the MRV1 note in Details |

**Tests:**

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py -k sharded_to_full_mapping` | 2 passed |
| `pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py` (incl. new `test_restore_adapter_slots_after_discard`) | passed; the new test fails without the fix |
| `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py` (incl. new `test_weights_wake_restores_lora_slots_after_level2_sleep`) | passed |
| `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py -k "test_deep_sleep_lora and not tp2"` | 1 passed |
| `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` (direct run, see below) | passed; with the mapping fix reverted it fails at the new mapping assertion |
| `pre-commit run --from-ref <base> --to-ref HEAD` | passed (including mypy) |

On this machine, the `multi_gpu_test` fork wrapper segfaults in the forked child while importing flashinfer (cutlass DSL `detect_gpu_arch`), with or without this change. So `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` was run in a fresh process by calling the undecorated test body:

```bash
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn python -c "
import pytest
from tests.basic_correctness.memory.sleep_mode import test_sleep_mode as t
with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as mp:
    t.test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2.__wrapped__(mp)
"
```

**CI note:** the Basic Correctness Sleep Mode step runs on a single GPU (H200 MIG 18GB), so `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` is skipped in CI. The new unit tests run in the existing LoRA and worker test steps.

**Model evals:** not applicable. Nothing changes outside the sleep/wake path.

**Related work / duplicate check:** no open PR touches `sharded_to_full_mapping` or restores LoRA slots on wake-up (searched open, merged and closed PRs and issues). Same approach as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53507. Relevant to the sleep/wake correctness RFC https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48310 (SW2).

## Details

**Root cause:** level-2 sleep discards the `weights` cumem pool, which also holds LoRA's logits mapping, slot tensors and punica metadata. `Worker.sleep` only saves registered buffers (plus parameters matched by `sleep_preserve_parameter_names`). LoRA state is otherwise reset only by `reset_lora_state()`, which runs from `reload_weights()` and `finish_weight_update()` (#39935).

**Why the runtime pool:** the `runtime` tag already exists for state that must survive sleep (KV-init metadata), and nested `use_memory_pool` calls restore the outer tag, so the weights pool around `load_model` is unaffected. Restoring from the pool keeps tensor addresses, so CUDA graphs and the cached LoRA kernel pointer tables stay valid, and no wake-up hook or LoRA-manager API is needed.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Fix HTTP 500 on long conversations: fuel-limit only request templates
author: ly989264
body:
## Overview

On the Rust frontend, long conversations fail with HTTP 500 even when the prompt is far below the context length (#62598). A GLM-5.3 agent session of 1,730 messages (21K tokens, about 2% of its 1M context) is rejected, while the same conversation renders in 0.12 s with transformers. Once a session reaches this point, every later request in it fails, and no setting raises the limit.

The cause is the hard-coded 500K MiniJinja instruction budget per render from #50300, which also applies to the model's own template. Since #62673, request-supplied templates are refused unless `--trust-request-chat-template` is set. This PR therefore keeps the budget for those templates only and renders the server's own template without one, as the Python frontend does. `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FUEL` overrides the request-template budget (`0` disables it), and the out-of-fuel error names it.

Fixes #62598

## Claims

- The server's own chat template renders without a fuel limit, so long conversations work by default. This matches the Python frontend, which has no instruction cap for it, only `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT`.
- Request-supplied templates, which only render with `--trust-request-chat-template`, keep the 500K budget from #50300, so the protection on that path is unchanged. `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FUEL` raises or disables it, and the out-of-fuel error says which variable to change, as the Python render-timeout error does. The variable is read once when the renderer is built, and an invalid value fails startup.

## Validation

Setup: `vllm-rs serve` + `vllm-mock-engine`, GLM-5.3 tokenizer and template, the repro from #62598 (one tool call and result per turn), `max_tokens=1`.

| build | serve flags | `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FUEL` | request | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `4e304b4d` | — | unset | server template, 1,730 msgs | 500 `engine ran out of fuel` |
| this PR | — | unset | server template, 1,730 / 3,002 msgs | 200 / 200 |
| this PR | — | unset | request template | 400, untrusted (from #62673) |
| this PR | `--trust-request-chat-template` | unset | request template, 1,728 / 1,730 msgs | 200 / 500, error names `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FUEL` |
| this PR | `--trust-request-chat-template` | `2000000` | request template, 1,730 msgs | 200 |

Tests:

- `only_request_templates_have_a_fuel_budget` renders a 20,000-message conversation with the default template, then shows that the same template runs out of fuel as a request template. It fails without the change.
- `test_long_conversation_exceeds_default_fuel` snapshots the error at the default budget.
- `test_raised_or_disabled_fuel_renders_long_conversation` covers a raised and a disabled budget.
- `test_chat_template_fuel_is_not_compile_factor` keeps the variable out of the compile cache key.

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-features --locked
pytest tests/test_envs.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py tests/test_envs.py rust/src/chat/src/renderer/hf/{error,mod,template}.rs  # also --hook-stage manual
```

All pass, except 6 tests that also fail on main on this machine: macOS grammar-replay snapshots, including `roundtrip_step5`, and a timing-sensitive audio test that passes on its own. Rendered output is unchanged, so no model eval.

## Details

- **Root cause.** Fuel counts executed instructions, and chat templates loop over messages. GLM-5.3's template spends about 290 instructions per message, so it reaches 500K at about 1,700 messages regardless of content length. #62598 measures the same limit at 1,682–21,740 messages across the templates in `examples/`.
- **No limit for the server's template.** That template is configured by the operator, through the model files or `--chat-template`. The Python frontend renders it without an instruction cap, and its cost grows with the request like tokenization does. If a cap is still wanted there, it is a one-line `with_fuel` on the default template.
- **Environment variable.** Like `VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS`, it is declared in `vllm/envs.py` and read with `std::env::var`; `vllm-rs` inherits it when started from `vllm serve`. It is excluded from `compile_factors()`, since it does not affect compiled graphs.
- **Duplicates.** No existing PR covers this. I searched `fuel`, `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE`, `50300 in:body` and `52025 in:body`; the only hit, #60199, caps `tojson` indentation. #62673 adds the flag this builds on.
- **AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line, and the commands above were run locally.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix wrong output of the QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion on ROCM_ATTN
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Purpose

On `ROCM_ATTN`, the QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion (`fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache`) stores V in an interleaved layout, and the layer's attention kernels must read it that way. Two places break that contract, so the fusion produces wrong output on `main`:

1. **Qwen3 models decode garbage** (Qwen3-8B GSM8K 0.87 → 0.005). `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` calls `set_interleaved_v_cache()` on each eligible layer, but with `layer_name` hoisted (`_USE_LAYERNAME`, torch >= 2.11) one layer's patterns cover the model, so the loop `break`s after the first eligible layer and skips the call for every other one. Those layers keep `_use_interleaved_v_cache=False`: the fused kernel then writes the NHD layout into a cache their kernels read as the paged layout. Prefill looks right because it attends over the fused kernel's `k_out`; every decode step after it reads the cache. The existing fusion tests use a single attention layer, so they never reached the second layer.
2. **With `fuse_rope_kvcache` also on, models without QK-norm get a corrupted V cache** (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K 0.766 → 0.71). The pass switches layers to the interleaved V cache before any pattern matches. On a layer the QK-norm pattern does not match, the RoPE + KV-cache fusion writes the KV cache instead, through `RocmAttentionImpl.do_rope_and_kv_cache_update`, whose Triton writer (`rocm_aiter_ops.triton_rope_and_cache`) only stores the regular V layout. A per-layer check at pattern registration cannot keep such layers out, because with `layer_name` hoisted one pattern serves every layer and graphs loaded from the compile cache skip the passes.

Fixing the first alone makes the second hit every layer instead of one (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K 0.012), so both are fixed here, one commit each:

1. `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` switches every eligible layer and only skips the duplicate pattern registration.
2. `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update` applies RoPE in place (`ops.rotary_embedding`) and takes the unfused `do_kv_cache_update`, which already writes the interleaved layout, on layers that use the interleaved V cache. Layers with the regular V cache keep the fused Triton writer.

Only `ROCM_ATTN` is affected; `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` is off by default.

## Test Plan

Single MI300-series GPU (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.11, AITER v0.1.25, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `ROCM_ATTN`, TP1. The change is on `main` @ `6af1e0ae27`; it was exercised on a source build of `main` @ `5be4266f5c` with the touched files replaced (they and the pass manager are unchanged between the two).

- `pytest tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`
- `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0` against `vllm serve <model> -cc.pass_config.fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache=true [-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=true] -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=true`
- Speed: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0.0 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency C --num-prompts max(16, 4*C)`, median TPOT, two rounds per arm in the order PR, base, PR, base.

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** 1497 and 50 passed (24 skipped). Two new cases fail on `main` and pass here:

- `test_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion_interleaves_every_layer` builds three `ROCM_ATTN` layers and checks that all of them switch.
- `test_rope_kvcache_fusion` gains an `interleaved_v` case that compares the fused and unfused caches of an interleaved-V `ROCM_ATTN` layer; its bf16 variants fail on `main`. (With an fp8 cache and `block_size=16` the two V layouts coincide, so those pass either way.)

**Root cause of the first bug, confirmed at runtime** on Qwen3-0.6B (28 layers): on `main`, `set_interleaved_v_cache()` ran for one layer; that layer's fused writes used `use_shuffle_layout=True` and the other 27 layers' used `False`. The fused writer and the unfused interleaved writer produce byte-identical caches, and the decode and prefill kernels read the interleaved layout correctly, so only the flag was missing.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions unless noted):

| Model | Fusions on | `main` | This PR | Fusions off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | QK-norm | 0.005 (200 questions) | 0.871 | 0.879 / 0.873 |
| Qwen3-8B | QK-norm + RoPE | — | 0.876 | 0.879 / 0.873 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | QK-norm + RoPE | 0.718 / 0.706 | 0.757 | 0.766 / 0.763 |

The QK-norm pass replaces all 36 patterns of Qwen3-8B in both arms. With only the first commit, the Llama row drops to 0.012.

**Speed, Qwen3-8B.** QK-norm fusion on with this PR, versus stock `main` without the fusion. On the fusion arm `splitting_ops` is limited to the attention ops and the `rotary_embedding` CustomOp is dispatched, which keeps the request from being dropped without turning on Inductor graph partition; the RoPE + KV-cache fusion is also on there but does not match Qwen3. Mean of two rounds:

| Concurrency | `main` (ms) | With fusion (ms) | TPOT | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.886 | 4.650 | **−4.8%** | +5.2% |
| 8 | 6.552 | 6.275 | **−4.2%** | +4.4% |
| 32 | 8.983 | 8.715 | −3.0% | +2.6% |
| 64 | 11.576 | 11.368 | −1.8% | +2.5% |
| 128 | 17.554 | 17.206 | −2.0% | +4.2% |

GSM8K in that setup: 0.876 / 0.876.

On interleaved-V layers the RoPE + KV-cache fusion now runs as two kernels instead of one. A fused write of the interleaved layout needs the Triton RoPE + cache kernel to support it, which is an AITER change.

---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Refresh CPU LRU for GPU-hit prefixes in eager SimpleCPUOffload
author: whx-sjtu
body:
Ready for review.

## Overview

With eager `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, a prefix that keeps hitting the GPU prefix cache is the first thing evicted from the CPU cache, because its CPU copy never leaves its first-store LRU position. When a request with a GPU prefix hit is admitted, this PR moves the CPU copy of that prefix to the MRU end.

## Claims

- Eager mode keeps hot GPU-hit prefixes on CPU; lazy mode is unchanged.
- Kimi-K3 agentic disaggregated benchmark on MI355X at `be4275d22`: +8.7% total tok/s/GPU, mean TTFT 8.6 s to 5.3 s.

## Validation

- New `test_gpu_prefix_hit_refreshes_cpu_lru` (full attention) and `test_gpu_prefix_hit_refreshes_cpu_mamba_boundary` (attention + Mamba) fail on main and pass here. The second also catches refreshing only full attention, freeing in forward order, or refreshing at lookup.
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/` and the SimpleCPUOffload connector, metrics and NIXL unit tests at `be4275d22`: 179 passed, 8 skipped (optional integration tests). pre-commit clean.
- End to end: one run per configuration, below.

<details><summary>End-to-end benchmark</summary>

Kimi-K3, agentic multi-turn trace at concurrency 48, 1 prefill + 1 decode instance on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X, TP8 + DCP8, FP8 KV cache, `MultiConnector` of MoRIIO and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (`lazy_offload: false`, 1.8 TB) on the prefill instance. vLLM ROCm nightly `81198e97`; "after" mounts this PR's `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` at `be4275d22`, ported onto the nightly; server config otherwise identical. Both ran on 2026-10-26 with prefill on the same node; decode nodes differ.

| | [before](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/40286897952/job/121452690051) | [after](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/40300366703/job/121496601447) |
|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s/GPU | 9783 | 10638 (+8.7%) |
| TTFT mean / p90 | 8.58 s / 21.71 s | 5.27 s / 11.08 s |
| TPOT p90 | 20.50 ms | 20.08 ms |
| Prefill tokens recomputed per request | 6160 | 5178 (-15.9%) |
| Prompt tokens loaded from CPU | 5.0% | 5.4% |

The first revision (`edf0671ce`, refresh at lookup) measured [9658](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38850989926) to [10616](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39054120919) tok/s/GPU in the same setup.

</details>

## Details

Root cause on the prefill instance:

1. Turn 1 computes prefix X; the eager store copies X to CPU.
2. Later turns hit X on GPU. Eager stores skip blocks already on CPU, so X's CPU copy is never touched.
3. Other requests' stores evict CPU blocks in LRU order, so X goes first although it is the hottest prefix.
4. When GPU pressure later evicts X, the next turn misses both tiers and recomputes X.

In eager mode, `get_num_new_matched_tokens` records the GPU hit length and `update_state_after_alloc` refreshes that prefix once at admission, so a request waiting for blocks does not repeat the CPU lookup each step. The refresh runs `cpu_coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` over the prefix, then touches and frees the result in reverse order like `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.free`: every full-attention block, the sliding window and the Mamba state at the boundary.

---

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return prompt token IDs from derender when requested
author: hickeyma
body:
## Overview

Derender now returns `prompt_token_ids` when the request sets `return_token_ids`, matching `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`. This follows #61065 and #62114 which did the same for the generated `token_ids`.

## Claims

- Chat derender returns `prompt_token_ids` on the response in batch and stream
- Completion derender returns it on each choice in batch and stream
- `/render` now copies `return_token_ids` onto the `GenerateRequest`, so generate actually sends the prompt IDs back
- Nothing changes when `return_token_ids` is unset or false

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -v
```

- `test_render_forwards_return_token_ids` checks that chat and completion render pass the flag on
- `test_derender_chat_returns_requested_prompt_token_ids` checks chat batch and stream over HTTP
- `test_derender_completion_preserves_requested_token_ids` (from #62114) now checks `prompt_token_ids` too

This only adds response fields when the client asks for them. Model output doesn't change, so I didn't run evals.

## Details

There were two gaps. `/render` never set `return_token_ids` on the `GenerateRequest`, so generate didn't return the prompt IDs. Derender also never put them on its responses.

Derender takes the prompt IDs from the generate response. It doesn't echo the `prompt_token_ids` the caller sent because the docs let that be just the end of the prompt (seeding only reads the last 7 IDs). Generate only sends prompt IDs on its first stream chunk, so the stream paths pass them straight through.

Not covered here:

- Responses API render which has no `return_token_ids`
- `echo`
- Streaming completions with `n > 1`. Only the first choice gets the prompt IDs while the coupled endpoint repeats them for every choice
