title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve DP rank in Responses requests
author: jianzs
body:
## Overview

Forward `X-data-parallel-rank` from the Responses API to the engine, matching Chat Completions. This prevents the frontend from silently discarding a gateway's selected DP replica.

## Claims

- Preserve the selected rank for streaming and non-streaming Responses requests, including subsequent built-in tool turns.
- Keep existing default routing when the header is absent or cannot be parsed; rank zero is preserved.

## Validation

On upstream base `fb61ac07bd1d5b8b9722c80085b99ef770efb265`, Python 3.12.13, CPU platform with accelerator visibility disabled:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  -k 'responses_data_parallel_rank or harmony_tool_followup_preserves_render_params' -v -ra --tb=short
```

Result: **11 passed, 66 deselected**, no skips. Tests exercise header parsing through the Responses serving entrypoint to `engine.generate`, and reuse the existing tool-follow-up test. They are included in the existing Buildkite Responses test area.

Serving reproduction on an Ascend-native downstream deployment with a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model, Mooncake PD, prefill TP4/DP4 and decode TP8/DP2:

| Request | Before forwarding | After forwarding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same reconstructed streaming Responses request, reasoning effort `max`, approximately 7.1k prompt tokens | No generated output within 45 seconds; decode waiting for KV fetch | Completed in approximately 3 seconds, including text and `response.completed` |

The serving comparison used a runtime implementation of the same rank-forwarding change on prefill API processes, without restarting the model. It validates the routing correction on that deployment; it is not a deployment of this exact upstream commit. The original client tool schemas were unavailable, so this was a reconstructed reproducer, not a byte-identical replay. No accuracy benchmark or general performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

The gateway can select prefill replica R and direct decode to fetch KV from R. Responses previously omitted `data_parallel_rank` from its engine call, allowing internal load balancing to choose another replica. Decode can then wait for KV at the wrong producer. The fix uses the existing header parser and passes the rank explicitly through `_generate_with_builtin_tools` to every `engine.generate` call. No connector-specific behavior or hardware branch is added.

Duplicate-work checks found no existing PR for this fix. Related #40285 changes internal DP coordinator notifications, and #49246 adds PCP/DP support; neither changes Responses rank forwarding.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change.

title: [Bugfix][Test] Stop requesting capfd in the subprocess weight cache test
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## The failure

`(MI300) Model Executor` in [AMD CI 14934](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14934), the only failure among 1238 passing tests:

```
FAILED model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep - TypeError: cannot pickle '_Local' object
```

## The cause

[#55490](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55490) added `test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep`, which combines `@create_new_process_for_each_test()` with the `capfd` fixture. The wrapper cloudpickles its arguments into the child process and `CaptureFixture` holds a thread-local, so the test raises before it runs. It is the only test in the file with that combination, and the failure is deterministic: the pickle happens before any GPU work.

## The change

The test no longer requests `capfd`. `DSV2_EP_CASE` leaves `check_flashinfer_cache` off and every use of `capfd` in `run_cold_start_and_warm_restart` sits behind that flag, so the fixture was requested but never read. It could not have worked in the child either, which inherits the parent's descriptors. The helper keeps it as an optional parameter, so the in-process cases retain their autotune-cache assertions.

A wider fix, dropping unpicklable fixtures inside the wrapper in `tests/utils.py`, would silently change behaviour for other tests, so this stays local to the one test that is wrong.

## Tests

`test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep` fails on `main` with the error above and passes with this change: 1 passed in 216.64s on MI300 (gfx942, ROCm 10.0) with 2 GPUs, through baseline, cold start, daemon, warm and restart.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: don't select float4 tail lanes past the row length
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

FIX #62466

`histogram_2048_topk` in `csrc/persistent_topk.cuh` can return indices `>= seq_len`. This happens when the row length is not a multiple of 4 and the top-k threshold lands in the fp16 `-inf` bin. This PR skips lanes past `seq_len` in the collection loop and adds a regression test.

## Claims

- `persistent_topk` no longer returns indices past the row length on the `histogram_2048_topk` path (k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows).
- The out-of-bounds reads of `logits` in the refinement pass are gone.
- Rows with length % 4 == 0 and rows whose threshold is above the `-inf` bin are unchanged. The guard only drops lanes that were never real elements.

## Validation

GPU: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130. `_C_stable_libtorch` rebuilt from this branch; main measured with the precompiled wheel for 3e96f9cf6.

New test, `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_masked_row_tail`. It covers k in {512, 1024, 2048}, length = k + {1, 2, 3, 4}, 0 or 100 finite scores, and in-row fill of `-inf` or `-1e30`:

```text
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k masked_row_tail
main:     36 failed, 12 passed   (every length % 4 != 0 case fails; % 4 == 0 passes)
this PR:  48 passed
```

Sample failure on main: `AssertionError: row 0: indices outside [0, 513): [513, 514, 515]`.

Op-level repro (1 row, k = 512, stride 516, every in-row score `-inf`, padding 0.0):

```text
            main                      this PR
len=513:    [513, 514, 515]           []
len=514:    [514, 515]                []
len=515:    [515]                     []
len=516:    []                        []
```

compute-sanitizer memcheck, one row of length 513 that is also the tensor width, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`:

```text
main:     3 x "Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes" in histogram_2048_topk<512>, kernel aborts
this PR:  ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
```

Full file with this PR: `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` gives 294 passed, 44 skipped (platform-gated cases).

No end-to-end serving repro: no shipped model reaches this path (see Details). CI runs this test file on Blackwell (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause. The last float4 load of a row (`load_float4_predicated`) fills the lanes past `seq_len` with `-inf`. They are binned like real elements. The collection loop gates candidates only on `vec_valid = i < n_vec`. When fewer than k in-row scores are above the `-inf` bin, the threshold is that bin, so the tail lanes become "equal" candidates. Refinement then reads `logits[idx]` for them and can output them.

Fix. Add `in_range = vec_valid && elem_idx < seq_len` and use it for `is_above` and `is_equal`. Tail lanes still count in the histogram, but that does not move the threshold. They only add to the `-inf` bin, the lowest non-NaN bin, so the counts above it are unchanged. And since `seq_len > k`, the in-row elements alone already reach k at the `-inf` bin.

Reachability, and why there is no end-to-end repro. The kernel path needs a decode row with k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows, and the persistent backend. The persistent backend is picked by `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend persistent`, by `auto` on SM12x and pre-SM90 GPUs, or by `auto` when the logits row stride is not divisible by 4. The bug also needs fewer than k in-row scores above the fp16 `-inf` bin. I checked every in-tree caller:

- DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5 style DSA decode (`sparse_attn_indexer`): in-row scores come from `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` and are finite. Prefill uses `top_k_per_row_prefill`, not this kernel.
- Qwen4-exp QSA: scores are sums of ReLU terms, so they are finite and >= 0.
- Step5 rejects the persistent backend.
- DeepSeek V4.1 `apply_candidate_mask` does write `-inf` inside decode rows. But the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config keeps 2048 candidate blocks of 8 tokens (16384 positions) on full-length (`compress_ratio` 1) layers. Every row on this path (<= 8192) is therefore fully covered.

So no shipped model reaches the bug with default or near-default flags. Reaching it needs a config with `candidate_topk_blocks * candidate_block_size < index_topk`, or more than `length - k` scores at or below about -65504. The layer-level script in the issue shows the V4.1 composition (`apply_candidate_mask` then `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")`) with such a candidate set. If the bug were hit, `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index` only drops `tok < 0`, so the result would be wrong KV slots with no error.

`cooperative_topk`, `histogram_256_topk` and the radix path are not affected. I checked lengths 8193 to 70001 with all-`-inf` rows on main and saw no bad indices.

Performance: one extra compare per element in the collection loop. No measurable change expected; not benchmarked.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Scale embedding LoRA deltas by the base layer's embed_scale
author: kushaldabbe
body:
## Overview

On Transformers-backend models with a scaled input embedding (VaultGemma; Gemma with `--model-impl transformers`), an `embed_tokens` LoRA adapter gets only `1 / embed_scale` of its effect. This scales the LoRA delta by the embedding's `embed_scale`, matching PEFT.

## Claims

- For an embedding that carries `embed_scale` (a Transformers `*ScaledWordEmbedding` after the backend rebases it), the `embed_tokens` LoRA output now matches PEFT 0.21.1.
- Embeddings without `embed_scale` (all native vLLM models) are unchanged.
- No per-step cost: the scale is applied once in `set_lora`, in place on the device copy.

## Validation

Tiny VaultGemma (random weights saved with `save_pretrained`) and a PEFT 0.21.1 adapter with `target_modules=["embed_tokens"]`, same token ids on both sides. PEFT reference: `PeftModel.get_input_embeddings()(ids)`. vLLM: `EngineArgs(enable_lora=True)` -> `get_model` (`TransformersForCausalLM`, embedding `VaultGemmaTextScaledWordEmbedding`) -> `load_lora_model` -> `set_active_adapters` -> `embed_input_ids`.

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| LoRA delta, vLLM / PEFT | 0.0625 (`1 / embed_scale`, `embed_scale = 16`) | 1.0000 |
| max abs diff vs PEFT embeddings | 1.11 | 2.4e-07 |
| max abs log-prob diff (HF forward on each embedding) | 1.18 | 0.000 |

```
pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py -k test_embeddings
```
48 passed. The new `embed_scale=16.0` cases (24) fail on `main` with every element mismatched.

Full `tests/lora/test_layers.py` on CPU: the same 102 tests fail on `main` and with this change (`'OffsetReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'cpu_linear'`, from this machine's build), so no new failures.

Not run: a GPU end-to-end serving run (no GPU available).

## Details

Root cause: the Transformers backend rebases a HF `*ScaledWordEmbedding` onto `VocabParallelEmbedding` and keeps its `forward`, which returns `lookup * embed_scale` (`replace_embedding_class` in `transformers/utils.py`). `VocabParallelEmbeddingWithLoRA.forward` calls that `base_layer.forward` and then adds the unscaled LoRA delta. PEFT's LoRA `Embedding.forward` multiplies the adapter output by `embed_scale` (huggingface/peft#2825, released in 0.18.0), and a merged adapter is scaled by construction.

Fix: in `set_lora`, multiply the slot's `lora_b` by `embed_scale` after copying it to the device.

Affected: VaultGemma (Transformers backend by default) and Gemma 1 to 4 with `--model-impl transformers`, which is the only way to load an `embed_tokens` LoRA for Gemma since the native classes do not declare `embedding_modules`. Native models with an embedding multiplier (Granite, MiniCPM, Falcon-H1, HyperCLOVA X) apply it after the LoRA-wrapped lookup and are unaffected.

Limitation: adapters trained with PEFT 0.17 or earlier saw an unscaled delta in the unmerged training forward. This change follows current PEFT and merged-adapter behavior.

Duplicate check: no open or closed PR or issue covers this (searched `embed_scale lora`, `ScaledWordEmbedding`, `VocabParallelEmbeddingWithLoRA`, `vaultgemma lora`, `transformers backend lora embedding`, `lora embed_tokens gemma`).

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Release every prefill rank a READ holds
author: tjtanaa
body:
## Overview

Fix three MoRIIO READ-mode bugs: prefill blocks left allocated after a fan-in read, a scrambled equal-TP read between different cache layouts, and a single-node xGMI crash in the flexible MLA mirror. Also add READ cases to the dummy-weight P/D E2E, and fix a port collision in that test. Follow-up to #61726. Split-head and Mamba READ across TP sizes is a separate PR stacked on this one.

## Claims

- **READ fan-in releases every prefill rank that holds the request.** Decode used to release only the rank it read from. With a larger prefill TP size, including the flexible MLA mirror (TP prefill + DP decode), the other prefill ranks kept the request's blocks until the `defer_timeout` reaper freed them: 60 s by default, logged as "Reaped N deferred sends".
- **Equal-TP READ between different cache layouts reads the right bytes.** Whole-block copies scrambled heads and tokens when prefill and decode lay them out differently. Such reads now move heads one by one. Matching layouts keep the same whole-block path.
- **Flexible MLA mirror on xGMI reads the fixed source.** The round-robin over prefill TP ranks spreads RDMA NIC load. On one node over xGMI it picked prefill ranks whose GPU MoRI cannot open a session to from a decode rank that sees one GPU ("MoRI could not open a session ... _tp1"). RDMA keeps the round-robin.

## Validation

- **Unit tests:** new `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_read_tp.py`, 93 tests. Each decode rank runs the real READ path on real cache tensors, and a fake transport executes the posted reads. The tests check that decode ends up byte-exact and that each prefill rank is released exactly as many times as it waits for. They cover:
  - equal TP for every fixture model × 3 cache-layout pairs
  - MLA in every TP pair, and replicated GQA at TP2 ↔ TP4
  - abort and failure releases
  - the RDMA round-robin vs the xGMI fixed source
- **The tests catch the bugs:** releasing only one holder fails 16 tests, and always copying whole blocks fails 12.
- **Full MoRIIO unit suite:** 818 passed. Ruff is clean, and mypy reports no new errors.
- **GPU, MI355X, xGMI:**

| Case (dummy-weight P/D) | Result |
|---|---|
| Equal-TP READ vs direct serve: kimi_linear, qwen3_5_moe, qwen3_dense, qwen3_dense HMA_off, deepseek_v3 HMA_off, gemma3 HMA_off | distance 0.0 on every prompt (ROCm 10; kimi_linear and qwen3_dense also on ROCm 7.2) |
| READ negative control (corrupted prefill KV): kimi_linear, qwen3_dense | detected |
| READ deepseek_v3 MLA, prefill TP1 → decode TP2 and TP2 → TP1 | pass, exact external hits. TP2 → TP1 crashed on main. |

## Details

- **Release accounting:** `get_moriio_read_holder_tp_ranks` lists the prefill ranks holding a decode rank's share. Decode releases all of them on completion, failure and abort, so prefill's existing `get_moriio_expected_ack_count` is met in both directions.
- **READ hit count in the E2E:** a READ decode always computes the last prompt token itself, so it reports `len − 1` external hits per prompt.
- **Port collisions in the E2E:** every TP rank binds the configured MoRIIO handshake and notify port plus its rank offset, and vLLM scans upward from each server's `VLLM_PORT`. The test handed out single ports, so a TP > 1 server's later ranks could land on another server's ports (`ZMQError: Address already in use`). This also affected #61726's heterogeneous WRITE cases. The test now reserves blocks of free ports.

title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Send routed-experts block hashes only for computed or scheduled blocks
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Split from #62044 (by @faresobeid): only the scheduler-side hash fix. The store eviction fix is #62392.

The scheduler sent a request's block hashes to the worker as soon as they existed. A prompt's hashes all exist before its first chunk runs, so with chunked prefill the worker pinned one store object for every prompt block, including blocks whose KV had not been computed yet. When those objects were still stored from an earlier turn, the extra pins could push the KV-sized store over capacity and make `put()` raise `BlockObjectStoreError` in the writer thread.

`AuxOutputSchedulerConnector` now sends only the hashes of blocks covered by `num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens` (or `num_computed_tokens` for hash-only updates and finished requests). It takes the hash block size from the scheduler to do that.

As a side effect, when a request finishes and its last sampled token completes a block, that block's hash is no longer sent unless a step that computes that token is already in flight: otherwise the token's KV is never computed, so the worker held a reference to a key with no stored object.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector
```

- `test_routed_experts_hashes_follow_scheduled_tokens` runs a 160-token prompt with a 64-token budget and 20 decode steps through the real scheduler, and checks the number of hashes sent after each step against fixed values: 4, 8 and 10 during prefill, then 11 once the decode tokens complete the next block.
- `test_scheduler_connector_sends_only_computed_hashes_off_schedule` (hash-only update, finish) schedules a request's first 4-token block, then lets a settled token complete a second hash block while only 7 tokens are computed. Neither a hash-only update nor the terminal event may send the second hash; the hash-only update sends it once the eighth token is computed.
- `test_worker_does_not_pin_unscheduled_prompt_blocks` drives the scheduler connector and the worker with a 4-object store. A first request stores 4 prompt blocks and finishes. A second request with the same prompt runs its first 4-token chunk next to a request that stores a new block.

## Test Result

- With this change: the new tests pass; `test_scheduler.py` and `tests/distributed/aux_output_connector` pass (288 tests).
- On `main`, with the new constructor argument removed from the tests, all new tests fail:
  - the scheduler sends all 10 prompt hashes at the first step (`[10, 10, ...] != [4, 8, ...]`);
  - after the first block is sent, the hash-only update and the terminal event both send the second hash although only 7 of its 8 tokens are computed;
  - the worker pins all 4 stored prompt blocks, so storing the new block raises `BlockObjectStoreError: auxiliary output store cannot retain the requested batch: limit=4 objects`, the writer-thread failure seen in production.
- Reverting only one of the three bounds to "send every hash" fails only the tests for that path: the scheduled-step bound fails the scheduler and worker tests, and the hash-only and terminal-event bounds each fail their case of `test_scheduler_connector_sends_only_computed_hashes_off_schedule`. The scheduler test cannot see the terminal-event bound, because its request finishes with 179 computed tokens and 11 complete hash blocks either way.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend][Kimi K3] Fix Kimi K3 XTML marker leakage in responses API
author: cjackal
body:
## Overview



Add `spaces_between_special_tokens` to `ResponsesRequest` so Kimi K3's `adjust_request` can turn it off on responses API endpoint, as it already does on chat completions API. Without it, XTML markers leak into Responses API output text.

Supersedes #51152, which has had merge conflicts since 2026-09-02 and no response from its author despite follow-ups. Original author credited via `Co-authored-by`.

## Claims



- `ResponsesRequest` accepts `spaces_between_special_tokens` (default `True`, same as `ChatCompletionRequest`) and passes it to `SamplingParams`. Requests that don't set it behave as before.

## Validation



### Minimal reproducer of the bug

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1", api_key="DUMMY")
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What time is it now in New York?"},
    {
        "type": "function_call",
        "call_id": "chatcmpl-tool-9a1b108b61cbb7cf",
        "name": "getCurrentTime",
        "arguments": "{\"location\": \"New York\"}",
    },
    {
        "type": "function_call_output",
        "call_id": "chatcmpl-tool-9a1b108b61cbb7cf",
        "output": " Current time in New York is 2026-10-14 00:05:21.",
    },
]
for e in client.responses.create(model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3", input=messages, stream=True):
    t = getattr(e, "type", "")
    if t in ("response.output_text.delta", "response.refusal.delta"):
        print(e.delta.content or "", end="")
```

| | Streamed output text |
|---|---|
| `main` | `<\|open\|> response Current time in New York is ...` |
| this PR | `Current time in New York is ...` |

### Updated unit tests

```bash
pytest tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py -v
pytest tests/tool_use/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py -v
```

```log
...
=================================================================================================== 52 passed in 0.25s ====================================================================================================

...
=================================================================================================== 27 passed in 9.04s ====================================================================================================
```

## Details



#51152 also reports trailing/leading spaces in string tool-call arguments on `/v1/responses` (e.g. `" Tokyo "`). That symptom has the same cause, so this change fixes it too.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] DeepSeek V4.1: don't leak a `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` opener into content
author: YaashuDave
body:
## Overview

The `deepseek_v41` parser now accepts `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` (V4's wrapper name, V4.1's spacing) as a tool-call opener, so it no longer leaks into `content`. Part of #62051 (the "V4 spelling" row); the other rows are not changed here.

## Claims

- For V4.1 output whose tool block opens with `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>`, the opener no longer appears in `content`, in both streaming and non-streaming. The tool calls are parsed as before.
- Like the canonical `<｜DSML｜ calls>`, this opener also ends an open reasoning block.
- No change for the canonical spelling, the unspaced V4 spelling, or truncated calls.

## Validation

The table uses the inputs from #62051, run through `DeepSeekV41EngineToolParser` on CPU (non-streaming, and streaming one character at a time followed by `finish_streaming()`):

| Model output | main @ `bde4d00113` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `\n\n<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>\n<｜DSML｜ invoke name="WebFetch">…</｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` | call `WebFetch {"url": "https://x.com"}`, but `content` = `"\n\n<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>\n"` | same call; the opener is not in `content` |
| Well-formed `<｜DSML｜ calls>` block | call parsed, `content` = `"Hi\n\n"` | unchanged |
| Unspaced V4 block (`<｜DSML｜tool_calls>…`) | returned as text, no call | unchanged |
| Truncated value / truncated name / block without an invoke | as described in #62051 | unchanged (rows 2-3 are #62259) |

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py
```

- New `test_v4_wrapper_name_opens_tool_block` (streaming at chunk sizes 1/7/10000, plus non-streaming, thinking on and off) and `test_v4_wrapper_name_ends_reasoning`. All 7 cases fail on main and pass with this change.
- All 147 tests in the three DeepSeek parser test files pass.
- `tests/parser` and `tests/tool_parsers`: 8064 passed vs. 8057 on main (the 7 new tests). Both have the same 15 errors, all in `test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py`, which needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

Validated with parser-level tests on CPU only; I did not serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The change is limited to the parser config, and these tests run in CI under the existing `parser` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

**Root cause:** `deepseek_v41_config` replaces V4's `TOOL_START` (canonical spelling plus `DSML_TOOL_START_VARIANTS`) with the single string `<｜DSML｜ calls>`. When the block opens with `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>`, the V4.1 invoke that follows still matches through the existing `(CONTENT, INVOKE_PREFIX)` transition, so the call is parsed. The opener before it, however, stays in `CONTENT` and is emitted as text.

**Fix:** add it as a `TOOL_START` variant in `deepseek_v41.py`, the same way #56141 added misspelled wrappers to the V4 config. `token_id_terminals` is unchanged: in the V4.1 tokenizer only `｜DSML｜` is an added token (non-special), so the tags reach the parser as text.

**Notes for reviewers:**

- A prose mention of `<｜DSML｜ tool_calls>` now behaves like a prose mention of `<｜DSML｜ calls>`: it opens a tool block. This matches what #56141 accepted for the V4 variants.
- **Open question (the "unspaced V4 spelling" row of #62051):** a fully V4-spelled block (`<｜DSML｜tool_calls>`, `<｜DSML｜invoke …>`) is still returned as text. That matches the Rust frontend, which keeps V4 tags as text in the V4.1 dialect on purpose (`v4_tags_remain_text_in_v41_dialect`, #56208). If V4.1 should accept V4 spellings, I can do that in both frontends in a follow-up.
- **Rust frontend:** it parses invokes only inside a recognised block, so it returns this whole block as text, and this PR doesn't change that. I can align it in a follow-up if you'd like.
- Related: #62259 (truncation rows of #62051) touches other parts of the same file. #61142 (another V4.1 opener drift) edits the same config; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: [Bugfix][RL] Fix cross-stream reuse of packed NCCL receive buffers
author: dharak-cohere
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62554. `packed_nccl_broadcast_consumer` lets the caching allocator hand a receive buffer to the next receive while a layerwise-reload replay on another slot stream still reads it. This corrupts MoE weights after packed NCCL weight updates.

## Claims

- Fixes silent weight corruption with packed NCCL weight transfer plus layerwise reload when a layer spans several packs (reproducer: 10/10 corrupted reloads on `main`, 0/10 with this PR).
- Orders every `post_unpack_func` after all earlier receives, instead of relying on NCCL's in-order completion.
- No measurable change in sync time; two-stream overlap is preserved.
- Same or lower peak memory than `main`, except layerwise reload over a slow transport, which reserves one to a few packs more because buffers with pending reads can no longer be reused early.

## Validation

All on this PR's head, 4x H100, torch 2.14.

- **New tests** (`pytest tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py -k DeferredConsumer`): 4 fail on `main` (20/20 runs), 4 pass here. The allocator test asserts the reuse directly via `data_ptr`s, so it fails on `main` regardless of GPU timing.
- **Upstream suites** (`test_packed_tensor.py`, `test_weight_transfer.py`, `test_weight_transfer_nccl_uid.py`, `test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py`, `test_reload.py`): 250 passed, 36 skipped, 2 xpassed, 0 failed.
- **Reproducer** (in the issue; real NCCL over NET, real `RoutedExperts`, real layerwise reload): 10/10 corrupted on `main`, 0/10 here.
- **Served** (`rlhf_http_nccl.py` layout, TP=2 OLMoE, NET): `/weight_checker` matched after every sync with per-expert, grouped per-expert and fused senders; greedy outputs identical to `main`.

**Latency** (`examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl.py`, median of 10–12 syncs):

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| opt-125m (example as written) | 61.9 ms | 61.7 ms |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 32 MB packs | 122.5 ms | 123.0 ms |
| OLMoE-1B-7B, 104 packs, NET | 4,886 ms | 4,929 ms |
| OLMoE-1B-7B, 13 packs (1 GB default), NET | 4,945 ms | 4,928 ms |

Overlap with 2 buffers is unchanged (NVLink 10.7 vs 10.8 ms; NET ~105 ms vs 189 ms serial, all builds within ±1.5%).

**Memory** (consumer peak reserved over baseline; `max_memory_allocated` doesn't count blocks held back by `record_stream`):

| scenario | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate load, k buffers | 2k packs | k packs |
| Served OLMoE, NET, 1 GB packs, first sync / later syncs | 4,554 / +0 MB | 4,276 / +0 MB |
| Served OLMoE, NET, per-expert, 128 MB packs | 2,270 MB | 2,404 MB |
| Reproducer (layerwise), NET, 106 MB packs, 2 / 3 buffers | 2,400 / 3,276 MB | 2,764 / 3,384 MB |

Over NVLink the layerwise numbers match `main`.

## Details

- **`record_stream`** on each receive buffer, for every slot stream and the caller's stream, fixes the corruption: the allocator won't reissue a freed block until those streams pass the free. It also covers the buffer's own pending broadcast, so the consumer no longer keeps the previous pack of each slot alive.
- **Event chain** (one event per pack): each pack's callback waits on the previous pack's receive, so callbacks are ordered after all earlier receives. Receives are never delayed, and no callback waits on another callback.
- Each half alone passes only its own test.
- Larger `num_buffers` doesn't avoid the bug: with k buffers, a layer spanning at least k + 2 packs is exposed. The allocator test covers `num_buffers=3`.
- **Alternatives considered:** copying out in the callback (an extra copy of every weight); a host sync per replay (serializes the streams).
- `test_unpack_produces_independent_copies` is replaced by `test_unpack_returns_views`; the old test passed only because the packed buffer aliased the reference tensor.

## Purpose

Kimi-K2.6 (int4 W4A16, TP8) prefill regressed between v0.29 and v0.31 on MI350/MI355: c32 TTFT went up ~150%. This PR changes that entry to BLOCK_N 128 and `num_stages=1` in the four identical `E=384,N=256,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI35*,dtype=int4_w4a16.json` files. Nothing else changes: only Kimi-K2-family int4 checkpoints at TP8 on MI350/MI355 load these files, and only batches of ~6k+ tokens use this entry.

| 256×256×32, 8 warps, **1 stage** | 7677 |
| 256×**128**×32, 8 warps, 2 stages | 7631 |
| **this PR** (256×128×32, 8 warps, 1 stage) | 6129 |

Serving (change vs. current table):

| conc | TTFT (before → after) | TPOT | E2EL | tok/s |

title: [Bugfix] Defer MRV2 Triton validation to worker startup
author: jeffreywang88
body:
## Overview

Defer MRV2's Triton availability check from `VllmConfig` construction to worker startup, allowing CPU frontends to build configs for GPU deployments.

## Claims

- CPU prompt-rendering processes can retain the deployment's speculative config without requiring a local Triton driver.
- Actual MRV2 workers still raise `Model Runner V2 requires Triton.` when Triton is unavailable. Feature compatibility checks remain in `VllmConfig`.

## Validation

- Config construction succeeds with Triton imports blocked, including Beam NVFP4 and Qwen3-4B with DFlash2. Prompt rendering and tokenization also succeed.
- MRV2 worker startup still rejects unavailable Triton.
- Both new regression tests and 73 related config/scheduler tests pass.

## Details

This fails when a CPU-only frontend constructs a full engine config for prompt rendering while inference runs on separate GPU nodes. For example, Ray Serve's `KVAwareRouter` starts an `LLMRouter` on each proxy node, including the CPU-only head. A deployment with speculative decoding needs MRV2, but the head has no active Triton driver. With MRV2 selected, config validation raises `Model Runner V2 requires Triton.`, preventing that router from starting and leaving the head's HAProxy on load-only routing.

`HAS_TRITON` reflects local runtime availability. Using it during config construction incorrectly requires the frontend to have the worker's runtime. This change removes the availability-based runner fallback and config-time rejection, and checks Triton in the shared worker constructor instead.

Related PR: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/67174.

Open-PR searches found no equivalent CPU-frontend fix. Related [#50612](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50612) addresses TPU-specific config exemptions; this change moves the runtime requirement to the worker boundary.

title: [Fast Start] Fix weight cache daemon GPU memory and warm-cache warmup hang
author: liusy58
body:
## Purpose

Fixes three issues with the weight cache daemon (`vllm preload`) that made fast start differ from a disk load, plus one logging issue.

1. **The KV cache was smaller than with a disk load.** `get_memory` reported `torch.accelerator.memory_allocated()`. That number also counts memory the engine never maps: communication buffers, warmup workspaces, and tensors outside parameters/buffers, which the engine rebuilds itself and so pays for twice. The engine subtracts the reported number from its `gpu_memory_utilization` budget. The daemon now reports the bytes of the distinct CUDA storages it exports.
2. **The daemon held its process groups for its whole lifetime.** Serving only exports CUDA IPC handles, but the NCCL / custom all-reduce / symm-mem communicators and the FlashInfer all-reduce workspace kept about 2.5 GiB per GPU pinned outside the engine's budget. The daemon now tears them down after warmup.
3. **Warmup deadlocked with a warm compile cache (TP > 1).** The daemon never set `parallel_config.rank`, so every daemon used `torch_aot_compile/<hash>/rank_0_0`. With a warm cache, all ranks loaded rank 0's artifact, whose Inductor code hard-codes `set_device(0)`. Warmup lazily creates the FlashInfer MNNVL workspace inside that graph, so on ranks 1..N it used `torch.cuda.current_device() == 0`:
   - On those ranks, `cuMulticastAddDevice` failed with `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` and they fell back to the trtllm workspace.
   - Rank 0 kept waiting in `cuMemMap` for the other ranks to add their devices.

   The daemon now sets `parallel_config.rank` the way engine workers do (`worker_base.py`).

   Caches written before this fix may still contain such an artifact under `rank_0_0`. Clear the daemon's `torch_aot_compile` cache once after upgrading.
4. **Logs were dropped in the daemon processes.** The spawned daemons never called `configure_logging`, so their vLLM logs were lost.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k "not cold_start and not rope_matching"`, including two new tests:
  - `test_daemon_reports_exported_weight_bytes`
  - `test_daemon_sets_its_rank_like_engine_workers`
- End to end on 4x B300: Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, TP4, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.6`, `--max-model-len 8192`, `--load-format ipc_cache` in zero_copy mode.
  - Ran the daemon with both a cold and a warm compile cache.
  - Compared the KV cache, the daemon's GPU memory, and a greedy completion against a disk load.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 9 passed. `test_ipc_rope_matching` fails the same way on `main`, so it is unrelated to this change.

| | disk load | daemon before | daemon after |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV cache | 152.71 GiB / 13,343,600 tokens | 152.61 GiB / 13,335,648 tokens | 152.73 GiB / 13,345,760 tokens |
| Weights charged to the engine | 4.29 GiB loaded | 4.35 GiB | 4.24 GiB |
| Daemon GPU memory | - | 8,244 MiB | 5,698 MiB |
| Warmup with a warm compile cache | - | hung 4/4 | ready 2/2 (cold and warm) |

- The greedy completion matched the disk load exactly.

title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Retain routed experts while a KV cache tier holds their blocks
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Split from #58328, after #62392 and #62489.

The routed-experts store evicts by its own LRU, so a prefix hit can reuse KV whose routed experts are gone, and the worker fails with `BlockObjectStoreError`.

- **Retention:** the scheduler tracks, from KV cache events, which blocks still have routed experts and tells the worker which to retain and release.
- **Hit capping:** a local hit past the retained blocks is dropped. An external hit is trimmed to what the connector can load (new `KVConnectorBase_V1.external_load_alignment`, full attention only), or dropped if it loads only whole hits.
- **Store sizing:** the store starts at the KV cache size and grows with a warning instead of failing.

Not handled: hits before `routed_experts_prompt_start` still need retained outputs, and hybrid Mamba hits ending mid-block are dropped.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_lmcache_connector.py \

  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
```

title: [CI][Bugfix] ColPali miss hidden_size
author: wenjinhust
body:
## Overview

Fix CI failures where ColPali model loading crashes with `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'hidden_size'` because recent Transformers versions expose `text_config` as a plain dict. Handle both the dict and config-object forms when extracting the text hidden size.

Related: [#60823](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60823) (ported ColPali configs/processors to upstream Transformers, which surfaced this issue).

## Claims

- Fixes `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'hidden_size'` in `ColPaliModel.__init__` when loading `vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf` with recent Transformers versions, restoring model initialization.
- Restores the ColPali CI coverage that regressed: model initialization tests and late-interaction pooling entrypoint tests on NVIDIA and AMD MI355.
- Preserves backward compatibility with the config-object form of `text_config` used by older Transformers versions.

## Validation

Before this fix, CI build 96076 failed with the same traceback across the following jobs:

- `nvidia-h200-mig-35gb-basic-models-extra-initialization-shard-4`
  - `tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[ColPaliForRetrieval]`
- `nvidia-h200-mig-35gb-entrypoints-integration-pooling-shard-3-slash-3`
  - `tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_late_interaction_offline_vision.py::test_query_text_vs_docs_image`
- `amd-mi355-dpx-entrypoints-integration-pooling-shard-1-slash-2` / `-shard-2-slash-2`
  - `test_query_image_vs_docs_text`, `test_query_text_vs_docs_image`, `test_query_text_vs_docs_mix`

Failure (`vllm/model_executor/models/colpali.py:123`, before fix):

```text
AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'hidden_size'
    hidden_size = config.text_config.hidden_size
```

Steps to reproduce / validate:

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k ColPaliForRetrieval
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_late_interaction_offline_vision.py
```

The affected jobs above are re-run in CI to confirm the fix.

## Details

**Root cause.** `ColPaliModel.__init__` reads the text hidden size from the top-level config and falls back to `config.text_config.hidden_size` when `hidden_size` is absent. After #60823 switched ColPali to the upstream Transformers `ColPaliConfig`, recent Transformers versions can leave `text_config` as a plain dict (e.g. when loading `vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf`), so the attribute access raises `AttributeError` and model loading aborts during `LLM` initialization.

**Fix.** In `vllm/model_executor/models/colpali.py`, read `text_config["hidden_size"]` when `text_config` is a dict, otherwise fall back to `getattr(text_config, "hidden_size", None)`. The existing `ValueError` fallback is kept for the case where neither form yields a hidden size.

**Tradeoffs / limitations.** Minimal one-place change with no behavioral impact on the config-object path. No new tests are added; the regression is covered by the existing initialization and late-interaction entrypoint tests listed above.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Materialize DeepSeek V4.1 content iterators before deepcopy
author: ltllt1
body:
## Overview

Fix DeepSeek V4.1 chat requests whose message `content` is an empty array. Before this change, both streaming and non-streaming requests can fail before generation:

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": []}],
  "stream": false
}
```

The non-streaming request returns HTTP 400; the streaming request emits an error SSE. The underlying exception is:

```text
TypeError: cannot pickle 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidatorIterator' object
```

After `ChatCompletionRequest` validation, `content=[]` can remain a Pydantic `ValidatorIterator`. DeepSeek V4.1’s message normalization deep-copies the messages, which raises this exception.

## Claims

- Materializing iterator-form `content` before the deep copy allows the affected request to render.
- Saving the resulting list in the message allows repeated rendering without consuming a one-shot iterator.
- The change is confined to the DeepSeek V4.1 tokenizer. General request validation and `tool_calls` handling are unchanged.

## Validation

- Reproduced the failure with streaming and non-streaming `content=[]` requests before the fix.
- Added regression coverage for empty content in both modes, text content parts, repeated rendering, and request JSON serialization.
- `python -m pytest --noconftest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py -q` — **48 passed**.
- Ruff check and format check passed.

## Details

The fix converts `content` to a list only when it is an iterator, immediately before `_normalize_messages()` calls `copy.deepcopy(messages)`. Existing string and list content follows the previous path. Related materialization fixes for `tool_calls` do not cover this `content=[]` case.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Build Pixtral vision position ids on device
author: JaredforReal
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes the `Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)` CI job, where `test_pixtral.py::test_chat_consolidated` fails on main in every full build (e.g. [95829](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95829), [95887](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95887)) with `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected`.

## Claims

- The Pixtral vision encoders no longer do a blocking host-to-device copy on every encoder forward: both the Mistral-format `VisionTransformer` and the HF-format `PixtralHFVisionModel` (used by Mistral3) on transformers >= 5.17.
- `test_chat_consolidated` passes again under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, and the HF-format path no longer trips the check either. Outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

On 1x GB300 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` and transformers 5.20.2 (the CI pin):

| Path | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Mistral format: `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_pixtral.py -k test_chat_consolidated` | failed, `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `pixtral.py:1033` (same trace as CI) | 1 passed, logprobs match the stored H100 reference |
| HF format: `mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512` loaded from `model.safetensors` (`Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`), one image chat request | failed, `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `pixtral.py:1596` | passes; greedy output identical to main run with the sync check disabled |

## Details

`position_meshgrid` built the per-patch `(row, col)` coordinates with `torch.arange` on the CPU, and `VisionTransformer.forward` then moved them to the GPU with `.to(self.device)`. The source tensor is pageable, so the copy blocks the host, which the sync checker in CI (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`) reports as a failure. The fix creates the coordinates directly on the device of the patch embeddings, which removes the copy.

The HF-format path (`PixtralHFVisionModel`) has the same pattern in `position_ids_in_meshgrid`. It is fixed the same way. CI does not catch it today because the HF-format Pixtral tests are skipped as large-GPU tests. Its `.to(self.device)` stays, because on transformers < 5.17 the function delegates to the transformers implementation, which still builds the ids on the CPU. When the ids are already on the device, the call does nothing.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Reject unsupported --kv-cache-dtype at CPU attention backend selection
author: patrk
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62664. The CPU platform now rejects `--kv-cache-dtype` values its attention backends can't handle, at backend selection instead of silently accepting them.

## Claims

- `turboquant_*`, `ultraquant_4bit`, `nvfp4` and `int8_per_token_head` on CPU fail at startup with a clear `ValueError`. Before this, turboquant/ultraquant ran and produced garbage (see the issue).
- `fp8*` is accepted only on hosts with AVX-512 or AMX, the same rule the kernel already enforces after weight loading.
- The MLA path on CPU accepts only unquantized dtypes.
- `auto`, `bfloat16` and `float16` are unchanged.

## Validation

macOS arm64 (Apple M4 Pro), CPU source build, on main @ e4a676cdc2.

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py -k "kv_cache_dtype_validation or rejects_quantized"` | 6 failed, 5 passed | 11 passed |
| `test_cpu_attn.py`, `tests/platforms/test_cpu.py`, `test_attention_selector.py`, `tests/config/test_kv_cache_dtype.py` | | 912 passed, 0 failed (x86-only cases skipped) |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | | passed |
| `LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", kv_cache_dtype=...)` | `auto` OK; `turboquant_k8v4` garbage; `fp8` fails after weight load | `auto` OK ("Paris"); `turboquant_k8v4`, `ultraquant_4bit`, `fp8` raise `ValueError` before weight load |

I could not run on x86. The AVX-512 path, where fp8 is accepted, is covered by the test through a monkeypatched ISA check.

Update: @adenzhou1350 independently tested this on Linux x86 with AVX-512 (no AMX): the 11 tests pass, the parent commit fails 6, and `turboquant_k8v4` is rejected before weight loading (see their comment).

## Details

- Root cause: unlike CUDA/ROCm/XPU, `CpuPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` never checked the backend's supported KV cache dtypes, so `CPUAttentionBackend.supported_kv_cache_dtypes` was never enforced. The CPU kernel treats any dtype other than fp8 as `auto`, so the unsupported formats got bf16 writes into a uint8 cache.
- I override `supports_kv_cache_dtype` instead of calling the full `validate_configuration`. The full check also validates head size and block size, which would change behaviour for models that work today.
- Custom dtypes registered through #52670 are rejected on CPU until the CPU backend declares support for them.
- Compatible with #61168: its `ultraquant_4bit` routing returns before this check, and the test doesn't parametrize `ultraquant_4bit`.
- CI: the test is in `test_cpu_attn.py` (CPU kernel tests job). That job doesn't list `vllm/platforms/cpu.py` as a dependency. I left the CI config alone.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line and ran the checks above myself.

title: [Bugfix] Retry incomplete HTTP response bodies
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Retry HTTP downloads when the response body is interrupted. These failures currently bypass the existing retry logic, even when attempts remain.

## Claims

- Retry requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError and aiohttp.ClientPayloadError.
- Preserve the existing attempt limit and backoff, while continuing to enforce download size limits.

## Validation

Added four parameterized cases covering sync and async downloads, successful recovery, and retry exhaustion. All four fail before the fix and pass afterward.

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_connections.py -q
13 passed

pre-commit run --files vllm/connections.py tests/test_connections.py
Passed

The test file is already included in the Buildkite CPU misc job.

Also validated /v1/chat/completions/render using the LLaVA 1.5 preprocessing configuration, the same explicit chat template on both revisions, and a local HTTP image server. The attempt limit was set to 2.

| Image download | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Completes normally | HTTP 200, 1 attempt | HTTP 200, 1 attempt |
| First response is interrupted | HTTP 500, 1 attempt | HTTP 200, 2 attempts |
| Every response is interrupted | HTTP 500, 1 attempt | HTTP 500, 2 attempts |

After recovery, the rendered prompt token IDs exactly match the successful control request.

This validates HTTP preprocessing; GPU inference and upstream CI were not run.

## Details

Body-read failures use different exception classes from connection failures, so _is_retryable does not currently recognize them. This change adds those classes to the existing retry classification.

These exceptions can also represent malformed responses. Such responses may be retried, but still fail once the configured attempt limit is reached.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Pad Qwen4Exp PLE n-gram inputs for piecewise CUDA graph replays
author: vllmellm
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61486

The Qwen4Exp AMD backend computes PLE n-gram ids inside PIECEWISE CUDA graph pieces, where the request search keeps the count the piece was captured with, but `Qwen4ExpModelState` only refreshed the live batch's rows of `query_start_loc` and
`ngram_context`. Replays read a stale tail, hashed the wrong n-gram and made the answer depend on what the server had served before. This pads both buffers.

## Claims

- PLE n-gram inputs no longer depend on server history: 0/300 short prompts change their answer after a 16-way burst, versus 77/300 before.
- Bit-identical replays: the max first-token logprob delta after the burst is 0.0000, versus 0.72 before.
- Eager and FULL-graph steps are unaffected: there `num_reqs_padded == num_reqs`, so the refreshed range already covers what the graph reads.


## Validation

vllm serving command:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --enable-prefix-caching --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

Using the reproducible script provided, 300 prompts served sequentially and greedily, the same prompts again as a control, a 16-way concurrent burst, then the same prompts again. Only the server state accumulated in between differs. 

---

<details>
<summary>Reproducer script (300-prompt history test)</summary>

```python
"""300-prompt history test for issue 61486.

Run against the server above. Each prompt is generated three times, and the first
16 are reused as the burst; only the server state accumulated in between differs.
Expected: the control reports 0 changed prompts, and the effect reports 0 with
the fix (about 25-30% without it).
"""
import json
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from datasets import load_dataset

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8"


def post(path, payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + path,
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600).read())


def gen(ids, max_tokens=8):
    out = post(
        "/v1/completions",
        {"model": MODEL, "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": max_tokens,
         "temperature": 0.0, "logprobs": 1},
    )
    lp = out["choices"][0]["logprobs"]
    return {"tokens": lp["tokens"], "logprob0": lp["token_logprobs"][0]}


def run_set(prompts):
    return [gen(ids) for ids in prompts]  # sequential, fixed order


questions = load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="test")["question"][:300]
prompts = [
    post("/tokenize", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": q})["tokens"] for q in questions
]

first = run_set(prompts)
again = run_set(prompts)  # control: nothing changed in between
with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:  # concurrent traffic, then repeat
    list(ex.map(lambda ids: gen(ids, 24), prompts[:16]))
after = run_set(prompts)

for name, a, b in (("control", first, again), ("effect ", first, after)):
    changed = sum(x["tokens"] != y["tokens"] for x, y in zip(a, b))
    delta = max(abs(x["logprob0"] - y["logprob0"]) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    print(f"{name}: {changed}/{len(a)} prompts changed, max |dlogprob0| = {delta:.4f}")
```

</details>

---

| suite | main | this fix |
|---|---|---|
| answers changed, first pass vs after burst (n=300) | 77/300 = 25.7% (95% CI 20.8-31.0) | **0/300** (95% CI 0-1.2) |
| max first-token logprob delta after the burst | 0.72 | **0.0000** |
| control, same prompts twice, no burst | 0/300 | 0/300 |


GSM8k: 

```
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template

```

result:

| suite | this fix |
|---|---|
| lm-eval gsm8k 25-shot (1319) | 0.9765 +- 0.0042 |

Pytest: 
```
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py  ->  15 passed
same file, fix reverted  ->  test_qwen4_exp_model_state_pads_replayed_request_range[amd] fails
```

## Details

PIECEWISE descriptors carry `num_reqs=None`, so the runner does not pad the request axis, while the captured piece uses `num_reqs = min(piece_tokens, max_num_seqs)`. `qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_ids` is not a splitting op and sizes its search from
`query_start_loc.numel() - 1`, so it keeps the capture-time count and reads rows this step never wrote. For a 24-token batch, `prepare_inputs` refreshed `query_start_loc[0:2]` while the piece reads `query_start_loc[0:25]`.

* Added a new test, covering both NVIDIA and AMD platform: buffers are non-decreasing, unused capacity cannot capture real tokens, a search over the captured request range resolves every real token to its own request (request-padded and unpadded cases), rows the batch does not own are sentinels, and the capture-time dummy inputs follow the same convention.

Each buffer is handed over as the smallest view the kernel needs: `query_start_loc` as the live prefix, because the kernel derives its request count from the view length, and `ngram_context` as the whole buffer, because it indexes rows by request, so every
reachable row must be valid. Passing the full buffers, as the NVIDIA copy does, also fixes this, but makes every eager and FULL step search `max_num_reqs + 1` boundaries instead of the live count. Therefore preferring this over the NVIDIA fixes.

Additional info: steps whose padded token count exceeds the largest captured piece (512 here) run eager and were never affected, so long and few-shot prompts show no difference; short prompts, chunked prefill and prefix-cache continuations are the exposed cases. The two model states remain separate per-backend copies; I can unify them in a follow-up PR if preferred.

title: [XPU][CI] Skip test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2 on non-CUDA platforms
author: chaojun-zhang
body:
Skips `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` on non-CUDA/ROCm platforms to fix the Intel CI failure ([intel-ci build 14791](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/14791#01a1583b-796e-48a1-b418-f77d75a8ba30)).

#62358 keeps LoRA state in the `runtime` pool so it survives level-2 sleep, but only when `is_cuda_alike()`. On XPU the state stays in the `weights` pool and is discarded, so the test fails. Supporting XPU would need a workaround for nested memory pools in the XPU allocator, so the test is skipped there for now.

Validation: `pytest ... -k deep_sleep_lora` on XPU is expected to skip (same `skipif` form as `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool`); not run locally since the test module cannot be collected on my host (`libcuda.so.1` missing).

AI assistance (GitHub Copilot) was used; I reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 for structurally-corrupted PNG images
author: reda-maizate
body:
## Overview

`ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` now catches Pillow's `SyntaxError` ("broken PNG file"), so a request containing a structurally-corrupted PNG fails with HTTP 400 instead of an unhandled HTTP 500.

Fixes #62703. Related: #60303 / #60308 cover the sibling `DecompressionBombError` case in the same except clause; this change covers the `SyntaxError` case, which that PR does not address.

## Claims

- A chat completion containing a corrupt PNG returns **HTTP 400** `BadRequestError: Failed to load image: broken PNG file (chunk ...)` instead of **HTTP 500** `InternalServerError` with the raw Pillow message.
- No behavior change for valid images, or for corrupt inputs already handled by the `OSError` / `UnidentifiedImageError` branches (they keep returning the same 400s).

## Validation

**Unit test** (real-world reproducer bytes — a 79-byte PNG whose stray bytes between the IDAT CRC and IEND shift the chunk stream):

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py -v
# => 20 passed (incl. new test_image_broken_png_rejected)
```

**End-to-end A/B on a real deployment** — `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`df3bd094a`), single H100, `google/gemma-4-26b-A4B-it`; "patched" = same container with this branch's `image.py` overlayed (byte-identical base verified before overlay):

| Request | Nightly (before) | This branch (after) |
|---|---|---|
| Corrupt PNG (reproducer above) | `500 InternalServerError: broken PNG file (chunk b'\x00\x00IE')` | `400 BadRequestError: Failed to load image: broken PNG file (chunk b'\x00\x00IE')` |
| Valid 64×64 PNG | `200` (answers "Red") | `200` (answers "Red") |
| Random non-image bytes | `400 BadRequestError: Failed to load image: cannot identify image file` | `400` (unchanged) |

CI coverage: `tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py` runs in the premerge CPU job (`pytest -m cpu_test multimodal` in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`), which is triggered by both changed paths (`vllm/multimodal/`, `tests/multimodal`).

## Details

**Root cause:** `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` wraps decode failures in a client-facing `ValueError` (`"Failed to load image: ..."`), but its except clause only catches `(OSError, Image.UnidentifiedImageError)`. Pillow raises a plain `SyntaxError` for corrupted chunk structures — it is neither of those — so it escaped unwrapped. The request-level error mapper (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/error_response.py`) promotes `ValueError` to `BadRequestError` (400) but maps unmapped exceptions to `InternalServerError` (500), which is exactly what clients observed.

**Fix:** add `SyntaxError` to the existing except tuple. The wrapping pattern — and therefore the 400 path — already existed and is proven by the A/B table above. A genuine Python `SyntaxError` cannot occur inside this try block (it only calls Pillow and plain attribute reads), so the widened catch cannot mask unrelated failures.

**Not a duplicate:** #60308 (open) adds `DecompressionBombError` to the same clause but does not handle `SyntaxError`; searches of open issues/PRs for "broken PNG" return no results. The two changes compose trivially if both merge.

**Model evaluations:** not applicable — the change only affects how invalid client input is surfaced (HTTP status/message of the error path); it cannot alter model output for accepted requests.

**AI assistance:** this change was prepared with AI assistance (GLM-5.3 via OpenCode) under the direction of, and fully reviewed line-by-line by, the human submitter, who ran all tests and end-to-end validations above.

title: [Doc] Fix Kimi-K3 GB300 disaggregated selector and guide gaps
author: Ankur-singh
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #62563 and #62528 for the Kimi-K3 GB300 disaggregated (xPyD) Dynamo + vLLM profile from [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4047](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4047). It fixes the gaps an independent review found after #62563 merged. It changes only `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml`.

## Claims

- **Selector (GB300 + Prefill/Decode + Dynamo):**
  - Restates the startup timeouts the qualified workers ran with (`VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600`, `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800`, `VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT=600000`). The `pd_cluster` Blackwell block replaces the recipe baseline, so they were dropped, and a load plus autotune takes about 25 minutes.
  - Sets `UCX_TLS=all` on GB300, overriding the Blackwell PD block's `rc,cuda_copy`. The qualified workers left UCX on its defaults.
- **Guide, Dynamo parser flags:** the GB300 worker note told users to add `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser kimi_k3` to `python3 -m dynamo.vllm`. At the pinned Dynamo (`ffbbaaa6`), `components/src/dynamo/vllm/args.py` parses leftover arguments with an `AsyncEngineArgs`-only parser (L103-126), so those API-server flags are rejected. The guide now gives the qualified flags: `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --dyn-enable-structural-tag`.
- **Guide, builder pointer:**
  - Keep the default TP pools on GB300. The DEP decode pool renders TP1 with DCP8, which vLLM rejects.
  - Leave **Spec decoding** off: the profile already carries the qualified DSpark K4 draft, and the toggle swaps in the unqualified RedHat K8 draft.
  - Untick **Tool calling**.
  - The builder decode's `--max-num-seqs 8` is the 1P2D row.
  - The guide now lists what stays guide-only: the qualified MultiConnector and Mooncake services, prefill KV events, and the router mode and session affinity.
- **Guide, environment:** adds `DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=120`, `ETCD_LEASE_TTL=600` and the three timeouts, as the qualified workers and frontend ran. It also names the `X-Dynamo-Session-Id` session header.
- **Guide, low-latency section:** TP16/DCP16 at concurrency 1 and TP8/DCP8 at concurrency 2 and 4, matching the InferenceX lane. The text previously said "1 or 2" and "2 or 4".
- Bumps `meta.date_updated`.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` passes in vllm-project/recipes.
- I rendered every variant × GB300/GB200/B300/B200/H200/H100/MI355X/MI300X × compatible strategy × feature set × router (864 renders) on main and on this branch. Only the 66 GB300 Prefill/Decode renders change, and only in env.
- Qualified evidence: InferenceX #4047 run [39140771499](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39140771499).

## Details

title: [Bugfix] Read ColPali hidden size from vlm_config
author: hmellor
body:
## Overview

Read ColPali's projection input size from `config.vlm_config.text_config`, replacing the dict/object workaround added in #62627.

## Claims

- `hidden_size` comes from the same config vLLM builds the language model from (`vllm_config.with_hf_config(config.vlm_config)`).
- Works before and after huggingface/transformers#48282. That PR stopped parsing the top-level `text_config`, which is a leftover key in checkpoints like `vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf`, so it now stays a plain `dict`. `vlm_config` is a `PaliGemmaConfig` on every supported version.

## Validation

`AutoConfig.from_pretrained("vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf")`:

| Transformers | `type(config.vlm_config)` | `config.vlm_config.text_config.hidden_size` | `type(config.text_config)` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.16.1 (minimum supported, before #48282) | `PaliGemmaConfig` | 2048 | `GemmaConfig` |
| 5.20.0 (after #48282) | `PaliGemmaConfig` | 2048 | `dict` |

```bash
uv run --isolated --no-project --with transformers==5.16.1 python -c "
from transformers import AutoConfig
c = AutoConfig.from_pretrained('vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf')
```

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Cut stop strings and stop tokens on derender
author: hickeyma
body:
## Overview

Derender was decoding every token generate sent back which meant stop strings and stop tokens came back into the text. This change cuts them the way the engine does. It fixes #57052 and supersedes #59510. 

## Claims

- Batch chat and completions derender cut the stop string and drop the stop token, the same as `vllm serve`. That includes `include_stop_str_in_output`, `min_tokens` and `ignore_eos`.
- `stop_reason` is passed through from generate. If generate doesn't send it (older servers), derender fills it in from what it matched. It stays null for the primary EOS.
- Completions streaming now drops the stop token which chat already did after #61757.
- Streaming derender returns 400 when the request has stop strings and points to `output_mode=text`, as agreed on #47161.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -v
```

- All pass. That includes the live render-server tests and `test_e2e_token_identity`, which checks `encode(derender(ids)) == ids` still holds.
- 19 of the 26 new tests fail without the fix. The other 7 check that nothing extra gets trimmed.
- `test_text_parity_stop_string` now asserts derender == `output_mode=text` == `/v1/completions`, both with a reported `stop_reason` and with the request's stop list. It needs a GPU and I haven't run it yet. It'll need `/ci run`.

## Details

- It reuses `check_stop_strings` from the engine detokenizer. The EOS ids and generation_config included are loaded once in `__init__` instead of on each call.
- The stop token is checked first, then the stop string on the text that's left. A matched string wins as `stop_reason` which is the engine's order.
- The parser still gets the full `token_ids`, like the main server.
- Streaming is a 400 rather than holding text back, so `DerenderStreamState` doesn't change.
- Known gaps:
  - A streaming request sent with no `chat_request` or `completion_request` can't be rejected.
  - With a parser configured, a stop string that overlaps a special token can cut differently from `vllm serve`.
  - Logprobs aren't trimmed.

Thanks to @pOpO1-9 for the original work on #59510.
