title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Serve gfx942 MLA verify past 4 tokens with a Triton kernel
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Route causal verify longer than 4 tokens on CDNA3 (no DCP) to a new Triton verify kernel in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`; shorter verify, decode, prefill, DCP and gfx950 keep their current paths.
- Add `decode_attention_fwd_verify` to `triton_decode_attention.py`: one program reads each KV tile once for a block of a request's (token, head) rows, with a per-row causal limit, int64 page offsets and FP8 dequant. Its variants are compiled before serving, so ngram drafts of any length never JIT mid-request.
- Undo the FP8 V-scale drop of AITER's qlen 2-4 FP8 decode kernel (ROCm/aiter#6732), found by a one-time probe, so a fixed AITER turns the correction off by itself.
- Apply the per-TP head override of `test_mla_backends.py` on ROCm as well (it was XPU only), so ROCm CI tests real per-rank head counts instead of 128 heads at every TP.
- Below page size 8 with bf16, read the block table one tile ahead instead of two: above 2 GiB of KV, Triton's global-load variant of the kernel otherwise spills VGPRs (2.1-3.1x slower at `--block-size 1`).
- Add an op test for the new kernel (bf16 and FP8, pages 1 and 16, ragged, padded and varlen rows).

On MI300X, MTP or ngram with 4 or more draft tokens fails at startup: AITER's persistent bf16 MLA decode only has kernels up to 4 query tokens, and its non-persistent kernels are not a safe fallback. They return wrong results at 32 heads, ignore the causal mask at 64/128 heads, and at 16 heads (what padded ranks such as TP2 of a 16-head model use today) read the wrong KV pages once the cache passes 4 GiB (ROCm/aiter#6733). That last case is silent: DeepSeek-V2-Lite at TP2 with k=7 drops to GSM8K 0.004 once serving fills the cache past 4 GiB, and goes back to 0.605 with this PR. Raising an error instead (as #57642 does) would leave MTP 4+ unusable on MI300 and break the gfx942 DCP verify routes that work today. This fixes item 1 of #55609 and needs no AITER change to be correct.

**Still open on the AITER side (not blocking this PR, but blocking a fully green `test_mla_backends.py` on MI300):**
- ROCm/aiter#6731: the persistent `_ps` decode kernel returns wrong output in about 1 of 1000 calls (a race). ROCm/aiter#6277 (open) brings it to 6 bad calls in 250k but not to zero. In 30 runs of the whole file on this branch it shows up as an occasional `ROCM_AITER_MLA` mismatch on unchanged decode paths.
- ROCm/aiter#6735, fixed by ROCm/aiter#6748 (rounds CK forward attention to nearest): `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[...glm...]` fails on main and on this branch because CK's FMHA forward truncates bf16; it passes 100/100 seeds with that change.
- ROCm/aiter#6732, ROCm/aiter#6733: the FP8 V-scale and the non-persistent kernel bugs worked around here.

**Results** (MI300X, AITER v0.1.25, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, ngram drafts; `vllm bench serve`, mean of 2 runs, output tok/s):

| config | workload | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP1, no spec | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 281 / 2046 | 280 / 2001 |
| TP1, no spec | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | 259 / 3202 | 258 / 3100 |
| TP1, k=3 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 306 / 2507 | 315 / 2669 |
| TP1, k=7 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | startup fails | 339 / 2700 |
| TP1, k=7 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | startup fails | 325 / 3201 |
| TP2, k=7 | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | 356 / 3042 | 370 / 3264 |
| TP2, k=7 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 | 324 / 3557 | 369 / 3766 |

The c32 differences without spec decode are within this host's run-to-run noise (the same path runs on both). GSM8K 5-shot (lm_eval, 1319) is 0.647-0.663 for every config on both branches, and the TP2 k=7 0.004 above is the >4 GiB case.

**Against the per-token row-view** (what gfx942 DCP verify uses: one row per draft token through the generic split-KV kernel). MI300X, AITER v0.1.27, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, ngram k=7, TP1, one server at a time on the same GPU, output tok/s:

| | InstructCoder c1 / c32 | random 1k/256 c1 / c32 |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 426 / 3864 | 490 / 4606 |
| row-view, launch config and splits tuned for gfx942 | 400 / 3520 | 454 / 4086 |
| row-view, as it ships | 290 / 3385 | 313 / 3511 |

Per layer, with both kernels in HIP graphs on identical inputs and a production-size KV pool, row-view is 1.8-4.6x slower as it ships and 1.44x slower on geomean when tuned (0.96-2.4x across 16-128 heads and batch 1-64). The c1 gap over tuned row-view (6-8%) is outside this host's noise; at c32 this PR is ahead in every round run, but by less than the c32 run-to-run spread. TP2 and k=5 show the same ordering, and GSM8K is 0.648-0.668 on every arm.

Tests: `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py -k verify` (48 passed; 10/10 runs with the page-size fix), `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` 30 times: every run passes all spec-decode and verify cases (634 passed). The two remaining failures are both AITER-side and listed above: `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[...auto-glm...]` fails in all 30 runs (max diff 0.031, identical on `TRITON_MLA`, the CK prefill), and 8 of 30 runs have one FP8 `large_decode` (qlen 1, unchanged decode path) `ROCM_AITER_MLA` mismatch of 0.16-0.39 from the persistent-kernel race. On main the 16 `spec_decode_medium` cases fail every run with `cannot get heuristic kernel ... qseqlen:8`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Honor add_generation_prompt and continue_final_message in the DeepSeek V4.1 tokenizer
author: JohnZhao01
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #64431. Python-frontend part of #46256 on DeepSeek V4.1 (`vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py`).

The V4.1 encoder ignores `add_generation_prompt` and `continue_final_message`. When the last message is an assistant message, the prompt always ends at `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` without an `<｜Assistant｜>` turn prefix, so the model returns empty or garbled text with HTTP 200. With `continue_final_message=true`, the final message is still closed with EOS, so the reply cannot continue it.

This PR makes the V4.1 encoder honor both controls, and declares turn boundaries for the V4.1 parser so that the prompt-aware reasoning start from #61857 also applies to V4.1. It is the Python counterpart of the Rust-frontend fix in #62189 and uses the same semantics. The encoder change is a port of #57882 by @xijiaat (closed without review; credited as co-author of the commit) onto current `main` (after #60792, image order, and #62199, the 1017 reference encoding).

**Related, not duplicates:** #62199 (merged) and #62196 (open) sync turn handling with the 1017 reference encoder (tool-result turns) and do not touch the generation controls. #62459 (open) fixes a conversation whose final message is `system`; this PR leaves that case to it and only changes conversations that end with an assistant message. #62887 (open) fixes `continue_final_message` only, by setting `wo_eos` on the final assistant message; this PR also covers `add_generation_prompt`. #64493 (draft) makes the same change for V3.2.

**Behaviour change:** a conversation that ends with an assistant message now gets a new assistant turn by default (`add_generation_prompt=true`), as with Hugging Face chat templates and #62189. To continue the final assistant message, clients send `continue_final_message=true`. Callers that pass `add_generation_prompt=false` explicitly for a conversation ending with a user message now get a prompt without the assistant turn prefix (see Details).

## Claims

- `add_generation_prompt=true` (the default): when the final message is an assistant message, the prompt now equals the DeepSeek reference encoding of the conversation followed by the reference assistant turn prefix, `<｜Assistant｜><think>` in thinking mode and `<｜Assistant｜></think>` in chat mode. The comparison is token-for-token. Earlier assistant messages keep their EOS.
- `add_generation_prompt=false`: for a conversation that ends with an assistant message, the prompt is unchanged from before and equals the DeepSeek reference encoder output. For any other final message the prompt now ends without the assistant turn prefix, as the flag asks (before, the flag was ignored).
- `continue_final_message=true`: the final assistant message is left open (no EOS). If it ends inside its reasoning, the reasoning is left open as well. A request without a final assistant message is rejected with HTTP 400 (before, the flag was ignored and the request returned 200).
- With the default `add_generation_prompt=true`, prompts that end with a user, developer or system message are token-identical to before.
- A final assistant message that is already left open with `wo_eos` (only possible when calling `encode_messages` directly; requests cannot set it) gets no new assistant turn, so it renders exactly as before.
- With `turn_boundary_tokens` declared, the V4.1 parser starts in content when the current turn's prompt already closed reasoning (for example a continued answer after `</think>`). A `</think>` in an earlier turn does not count.
- Fixes empty and garbled replies on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with the Python frontend: 210/280 empty replies before this change, 2/280 after (both remaining ones hit `max_tokens` while still reasoning).

## Validation

Setup for all server-side checks: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4×H200 with TP4, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e68efc68`, Python frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`), `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41`, speculative decoding with the model's built-in draft module (`--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'`). "Before" overlays the affected Python files from `main` @ `6e780d14` (the nightly predates #60792 and #62199); "after" overlays the same files with this PR. A fresh server for each side. These checks predate the rebase onto `main` @ `2eae56c4b`, which needed no conflict resolution, and the `wo_eos` check, which no request can reach (the E2E section below was run on the current head `3c8a7257`).

**Reference encoder.** The server's `/tokenize` output was compared, as token ids, with the updated reference `encoding/encoding.py` of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. Seven conversation shapes, each with thinking on and off:

| Shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ends with user (2 shapes) | = reference | = reference (unchanged) |
| ends with assistant (5 shapes): plain, with `reasoning_content`, after a multi-turn history, with a system message, with `tool_calls` | = reference closed history (ends at EOS, no turn prefix) | = reference + `<｜Assistant｜>` + `<think>`/`</think>` |

**Unchanged paths render identically.** The exact lm-eval requests were re-rendered with both versions (sha1 of the token ids):

| Requests | identical |
|---|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot (1,319) | 1,319 / 1,319 |
| IFEval (541) | 541 / 541 |
| HumanEval-instruct, prefill **without** `continue_final_message` (164) | 0 / 164: each differs by exactly the 2 opener tokens (see Behaviour change) |
| HumanEval-instruct, prefill with `continue_final_message` (164) | 0 / 164: each is exactly 1 token shorter (the final EOS is no longer appended) |

Of 342 saved request bodies from our other end-to-end tests (tools, streaming, `reasoning_effort`, `json_schema`, multi-turn agent loops), 335 render identically; the 5 that end with an assistant message differ as described above (3 gain the 2 opener tokens, 2 that continue the final message lose its EOS); the 2 that use the `latest_reminder` role are rejected with HTTP 400 on both sides (that role is not supported by this renderer).

**End-to-end, final assistant message.** Each cell is 40 requests: 20 greedy (`max_tokens` 1024) and 20 with T=1.0, top_p=0.95 (`max_tokens` 4096).

| Request shape | before: empty replies | after: empty replies |
|---|---|---|
| `[user]` (control) | 1 | 0 |
| `[user, assistant(code prefix)]`, no flags | 40 | 0 (40 replies with code) |
| same, `continue_final_message=true`, `add_generation_prompt=false` | 40 | 0 (40 replies continue the code) |
| `[user, assistant(complete answer)]`, thinking on | 35 | 1 (hit `max_tokens`) |
| same, thinking off | 20 | 0 |
| `[user, assistant(code prefix)]`, content as a list of text parts | 40 | 0 |
| `[user, assistant(complete answer)]`, content as a list of text parts | 34 | 1 (hit `max_tokens`) |
| **total** | **210 / 280** | **2 / 280** |

Before the change, 4 replies also leaked special-token text; after it there are no leaks and no garbled starts, and the 2 empty replies spent all 1,024 tokens in reasoning (`finish_reason=length`). The `[user]` control renders the same prompt on both sides, so its one empty reply before is run-to-run variance. A conversation that ends with a system message is unchanged by this PR (0/40 empty on both sides). Server logs have no errors.

**End-to-end on the current head: generation flags** (added for review). Run on this PR's head `3c8a7257`. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 4×H200, TP4, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-335dd77b` (= this PR's base `main` @ `2eae56c4b` plus one unrelated commit), Python frontend, the serve arguments listed above, plus `--moe-backend marlin` on both sides: this nightly's default MXFP4 MoE backend on Hopper (Humming) fails at startup for V4.1-Flash at TP4, which is #63793. "Before" is the image as is; "after" overlays this PR's 3 changed Python files. A fresh server for each side.

Prompt: server `/tokenize` (chat messages + flags) compared as token ids with the reference `encoding/encoding.py` of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. Expected = the reference encoding; a new assistant turn ends in `<｜Assistant｜>` + `</think>` (thinking off) or `<think>` (thinking on); `continue_final_message` leaves the final assistant turn open (no EOS). Every row was checked with thinking off and on, with the same result.

| Final message | `add_generation_prompt` | `continue_final_message` | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| user | True | false | = expected | = expected |
| user | False | false | assistant prefix still added (+2 tokens) | = expected |
| assistant (complete answer) | True | false | no new assistant turn (ends at EOS, −2 tokens) | = expected |
| assistant (complete answer, content as a list of text parts) | True | false | no new assistant turn (−2 tokens) | = expected |
| assistant (complete answer) | False | false | = expected | = expected |
| assistant (code prefix) | True | false | no new assistant turn (−2 tokens) | = expected |
| assistant (code prefix) | False | true | EOS still appended (+1 token) | = expected |
| assistant (code prefix) | True | true | HTTP 400 | HTTP 400 |

The last row is rejected by the chat API itself on both sides ("Cannot set both `continue_final_message` and `add_generation_prompt` to True").

Generation: 20 requests per cell, 10 greedy (`max_tokens` 1024) and 10 with T=1.0, top_p=0.95 (`max_tokens` 4096), for thinking off and thinking on. Each reply is put in the first class that matches, by how its `content` opens: **reasoning only** (`content` empty, the text is in `reasoning_content`; this is what the section above counts as an empty reply), **empty** (both empty), **user-voice line** (it opens as the user's next turn, e.g. `> Explain how it works.`; no special token is involved), **continues** (continues the code prefix, or the user's own text), **odd start** (opens with junk such as `-1`, `+++`, `@@`, `#include`, a base64 string or `<｜end▁of▁thinking｜>`), **answer** (a normal reply).

Thinking off:

| Final message, flags | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| user, `add_generation_prompt=True` | 20 answer | 20 answer |
| user, `add_generation_prompt=False` | 20 answer (the prompt still had the assistant prefix) | 17 empty, 2 continue the user's text, 1 answer |
| assistant (complete), `add_generation_prompt=True` | 14 user-voice line, 6 odd start | 20 answer |
| assistant (complete, list of text parts), `add_generation_prompt=True` | 15 user-voice line, 4 odd start, 1 answer | 20 answer |
| assistant (complete), `add_generation_prompt=False` | 11 user-voice line, 9 odd start | 11 user-voice line, 9 odd start |
| assistant (code prefix), `add_generation_prompt=True` | 17 continue the code after the EOS, 2 answer, 1 odd start | 18 answer, 2 continue the code |
| assistant (code prefix), `continue_final_message=true` | 18 continue the code, 1 answer, 1 odd start | 20 continue the code |

Thinking on:

| Final message, flags | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| user, `add_generation_prompt=True` | 20 answer | 20 answer |
| user, `add_generation_prompt=False` | 20 answer (the prompt still had the assistant prefix) | 20 continue the user's text in `reasoning_content`; 9 of them then also write a reply in `content` (see notes) |
| assistant (complete), `add_generation_prompt=True` | 16 reasoning only, 4 answer | 20 answer |
| assistant (complete, list of text parts), `add_generation_prompt=True` | 18 reasoning only, 2 answer | 20 answer |
| assistant (complete), `add_generation_prompt=False` | 19 reasoning only, 1 answer | 17 odd start, 1 user-voice line, 2 answer (see notes) |
| assistant (code prefix), `add_generation_prompt=True` | 19 reasoning only, 1 answer | 19 answer, 1 continues the code |
| assistant (code prefix), `continue_final_message=true` | 19 reasoning only, 1 answer | 20 continue the code |

Notes:

- With thinking on, "before" shows the same failure as the section above: the reply text ends up in `reasoning_content` and `content` is empty (19/20 for `continue_final_message=true`, 16/20 for a complete final answer; above: 40/40 and 35/40). With thinking off, a complete final answer gives a user-voice line or an odd start instead (14/20 and 15/20 user-voice lines); a code prefix is mostly continued even after the EOS (17/20 and 18/20), so for that shape the old prompt fails mainly with thinking on (the code-prefix rows above were run with thinking on, the server default). This run uses a newer nightly, `--moe-backend marlin`, and classifies replies by how they open, so its counts are not comparable one to one with the section above; both runs show the same direction.
- `add_generation_prompt=False` after a complete final assistant message: the prompt is identical on both sides and equals the reference (the conversation is closed at EOS), and 9 of the 10 greedy replies are the same text on both sides. What changes with thinking on is which field the text goes to. Before, the parser treats it as still inside reasoning (19/20 reasoning only); with this PR's `turn_boundary_tokens` it does not, so the same text is returned as `content`. Both are continuations after a closed conversation, not answers.
- `add_generation_prompt=False` after a user message: the prompt now has no assistant turn, as requested, so the model continues the user's own text. With thinking on, all 20 replies start by continuing the user's sentence inside `reasoning_content` (e.g. ` It should be ... handle large numbers efficiently.`); 11 stop there with empty `content`, and 9 then also write a reply in `content`. 8 of the 20 contain special-token text such as `<｜place▁holder▁no▁798｜>` (in `reasoning_content`), and 10 hit `max_tokens`. This combination is meant for `/tokenize` or scoring, not for chat generation. Elsewhere, special-token text appears in 2 "before" replies (`<｜end▁of▁thinking｜>`) and in no "after" reply.

<details>
<summary>Raw output of the generation-flags run (before / after)</summary>

The test script's stdout for each side, as printed. The last line of each log (`SUMMARY`) only repeats the `GEN` and `RENDER` lines and is left out to keep this description under GitHub's size limit.

- Shapes: `U` = final user message, `AF` = complete final assistant answer, `AFL` = the same answer as a list of text parts, `AP` = final assistant code prefix. `agp` = `add_generation_prompt`, `cont` = `continue_final_message`, `thinking` = `chat_template_kwargs.thinking`.
- `RENDER`: the `/tokenize` check for one shape and flag pair, thinking off and on. `render` is `= expected` when the server's token ids equal the reference encoding, `DIFF` when they do not, or the HTTP status; `n_tokens` = server, `n_expected` = reference; `expected_tail` = the last 60 characters of the expected prompt.
- `GEN`: one cell, 20 requests. `empty` = `content` empty (with thinking on this includes the "reasoning only" replies), `special` = special-token text in `content` or `reasoning_content`, `finish_length` = stopped at `max_tokens`; for `continue_final_message=true`, `continues_prefix` = replies that do not restart the code block (a looser check than the classifier's "continues prefix": in the "before" thinking-off cell it also counts the 1 answer and the 1 odd start, hence 20 here vs 18 in the classifier output and the table).

title: [ROCm][CI][Bug] Remove padding from AITER output for quantization/tes…
author: qli88
body:
## Overview

When using VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 as default, 2 test cases will fail:

quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py::test_online_shared_expert_loads_bf16_weights_into_mxfp4_slot;
quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py::test_online_shared_expert_reload_compatibility.
The cause is: previously VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0, so this test used Triton MoE backend, which doesn't have padding in results; now it uses AITER MoE backend, which returns results with padding. We need to remove the padding before we can compare the results.

## Claims

Now this test is able to handle possible padding in the returned results, so no matter VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 or 0, the test always finishes successfully.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Read resident prefill rows by request state slot
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

HiSparse's resident prefill conversion lazily gathers a batch-ordered copy of the residency table inside the layer-0 conversion. The gather is queued after `logical_topk_ready`, but the side-stream converter waits only on that event, so it can read the table before it's written.

This PR removes the gathered table. The sparse-MLA index remap kernel gets an optional `idx_mapping` indirection, off for other callers, and HiSparse passes its persistent residency table plus `request_state_indices` directly. Both are written before the forward, so the existing event orders them. Residency is stored group-major, so each group's view is a contiguous table.

Alternative to #62401, which keeps the gather and adds a layer-0 `wait_stream`.

## Test Result

- `test_hisparse_resident_prefill_reads_residency_by_state_row` reproduces the race: it fails on main (3/3 runs) and passes here.
- HiSparse unit and e2e tests pass.
- With JIT monitoring on, the new variant is never compiled after warmup.

**End to end:** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 8×B200 TP8, HiSparse, mean of 2 reps, change vs main. Greedy outputs are byte-identical.

| workload | c | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16k in / 1k out | 16 | −0.2% | −0.3% | +0.5% |
| 16k in / 1k out | 64 | +0.0% | +1.1% | −0.4% |
| 4k in / 64 out | 16 | +1.3% | −0.3% | −2.4% |
| 4k in / 64 out | 64 | +0.1% | −0.1% | −0.1% |

**Kernel:** speedup vs main for the HiSparse conversion. H200, top-k 2048, 256 max requests, 61 resident groups, CUDA graph timing. Other sparse-MLA callers are unchanged (0.94–1.09× across the sweep).

| query tokens | 512 pages | 2048 pages | 8192 pages |

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Count tool call deltas as generated tokens in openai-responses
author: dilberx
body:
## Overview

`vllm bench serve --backend openai-responses` marks every tool-call-only response as failed. It counts only `output_text` and `reasoning_text` deltas as tokens, and a forced tool call streams only `function_call_arguments` deltas. This counts the four tool delta events the vLLM Responses server emits, as `openai-chat` counts `tool_calls` deltas.

## Claims

- 100 tool calls the server completed with HTTP 200 went from 0 to 100 successful, with totals now identical to `openai-chat` on the same workload.
- Added events: `function_call_arguments`, `custom_tool_call_input`, `mcp_call_arguments`, `code_interpreter_call_code` (from `responses/streaming_events.py`). Tool arguments are timed but not added to `generated_text`, as on chat.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py`: a tool-call-only response (TTFT, ITL, usage, `latency - ttft == sum(itl)`), each tool delta type, and text followed by a tool call. 30 passed; the 6 new ones fail on `main` with "Never received a token delta". Timing tests (29) and pre-commit pass.

RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, 100 prompts, concurrency 16, `tool_choice: "required"` via `--extra-body`:

| | `main` | this branch | `openai-chat` |
|---|---|---|---|
| completed / failed | 0 / 100 | 100 / 0 | 100 / 0 |
| input / output tokens | 0 / 0 | 20,610 / 2,090 | 20,610 / 2,090 |

Per request, output tokens match the server's `usage` and ITL counts match the token events recorded on the wire.

## Details

#54628 added this backend with tool calls out of scope. Leaving them out fails the request, so tool-calling workloads such as the BFCL dataset (#42457) can't be measured on it. The Rust `vllm-bench` Responses backend has the same gap; I'll send that separately.

No issue or PR covers this. Open PRs touching `endpoint_request_func.py` (#51155, #55719, #57519, #58734) don't change these events.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this and write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Muse Spark: apply output multiplier and softcap in compute_logits_local
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

With `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, the ROCm Muse Spark model samples from logits that skip its output multiplier and final-logit softcap. This PR gives the model its own `compute_logits_local`, which applies the same transform as `compute_logits`. Follow-up to #62622.

## Claims

- With batch-sharded sampling, ROCm Muse Spark samples from the same fp32 logits as the default path: multiplier 32^-0.5 and softcap 20 are applied.
- With batch-sharded sampling off, which is the default, behavior is unchanged. `compute_logits` only moves its existing post-processing into a helper that both methods call.

## Validation

The new test calls `compute_logits_local` and `compute_logits` on the same hidden states and requires identical output. It fails on the base commit and passes with this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py -q      # base 2de0531d81
E   AssertionError: The values for attribute 'dtype' do not match: torch.bfloat16 != torch.float32.
FAILED tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py::test_compute_logits_local_applies_output_transform
1 failed

$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py -q      # this PR
1 passed
```

On the base commit the inherited method returns the raw bf16 lm_head output, so the comparison fails on dtype before it reaches the values. The existing Muse tests also pass with this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py tests/transformers_utils/test_muse_spark_config.py -q
21 passed
```

These runs were CPU-only, in the ROCm image with no GPU attached. Because of that, the ROCm architecture query and device detection were stubbed locally. The new test is wired into the "Basic Models (Other)" Buildkite step and its MI355 mirror. The MI355 mirror now also lists `vllm/models/muse_spark/` as a dependency.

**Not yet done:** an end-to-end GPU run with `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, and a model evaluation such as GSM8K comparing the flag on and off. Both are needed before this PR leaves draft.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- The GPU model runner enables batch-sharded sampling for any model that has a `compute_logits_local` attribute (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:447-448`).
- In the sampling step it then calls that method and runs an all-to-all instead of calling `compute_logits` (`model_runner.py:1633`).
- The ROCm `MuseSpark1xForCausalLM` inherits `LlamaForCausalLM.compute_logits_local` (`vllm/model_executor/models/llama.py:553`), which returns raw lm_head logits.
- Muse's `compute_logits` (`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py:1096`) casts to fp32 and applies the multiplier and softcap. The batch-sharded path skipped all of that.
- Greedy decoding is unaffected, because both transforms preserve order. Sampled decoding and speculative-decoding rejection sampling used the wrong distribution.

**Fix.** The transform is elementwise, so applying it to each rank's vocab shard before the all-to-all gives exactly the logits `compute_logits` produces. The runner trims vocab padding after the all-to-all. A generic guard in the model runner was considered and rejected, to keep core code untouched.

**Not a duplicate.** No other open PR changes `compute_logits_local` for Muse Spark. #63078 touches Muse RoPE, not logits.

**Test limitation.** The test builds the model with `__new__` and sets the attributes `compute_logits` reads, instead of using the real constructor. Building a real Muse Spark model needs TP state and the full checkpoint config. This conflicts with `tests/AGENTS.md`'s preference for real constructors, and is noted for reviewers.

## GSM8K: batch-sharded sampling with and without this PR

**Setup.** 8x MI355X, TP8, `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, no speculative decoding. Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-df6603f05` (aiter 0.1.26, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0), with each tree's Python overlaid; base is main 2de0531d81. Server flags are the AMD MXFP4 recipe's:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --language-model-only --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 [--enable-batch-sharded-sampling]

# 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, max 256 tokens, 64 concurrent requests
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 64 --temperature 0
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 64 --temperature 1.0 --seed 42
```

Accuracy is shown ± one binomial standard error (n = 1,319). Sampled runs also use the model's default `top_k` 64 from its generation config.

| Code | `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` | Greedy accuracy | Sampled accuracy, T=1.0 | Sampled output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main 2de0531d81 | off | 0.9507 ± 0.0060 | 0.8196 ± 0.0106 | 142,640 |
| main 2de0531d81 | on | 0.9462 ± 0.0062 | **0.9469 ± 0.0062** | 123,631 |
| this PR | on | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | **0.8067 ± 0.0109** | 143,352 |

All three servers start with the same KV cache (167.67 GiB, 8,173,209 tokens). Both flag-on servers log `Batch-sharded sampling enabled.` on all 8 ranks.

- **Greedy is unaffected.** All three greedy scores agree within one standard error, as expected: the multiplier and softcap preserve the order of the logits.
- **On main, the flag silently breaks sampling.** The temperature-1.0 run scores 0.9469 with 123,631 output tokens. That matches the greedy run (0.9462, 123,688 tokens) and is 12.7 points above main with the flag off. Without the 32^-0.5 multiplier the logits are about 5.7x too large, which acts like a temperature of about 0.18, so requested sampling becomes nearly greedy.
- **This PR restores the expected distribution.** With the flag on, the sampled score (0.8067) and output length (143,352 tokens) match main with the flag off (0.8196, 142,640 tokens). The 1.3-point gap is within 1 combined standard error.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve image normalization constants during dummy loading
author: pkuwangh
body:
## Overview

Preserve processor-derived image normalization constants when an engine starts with `load_format="dummy"`. Register `FusedMMInputNorm.weight` and `bias` as nonpersistent buffers so dummy initialization leaves them intact.

The Qwen3-VL path began using this normalization module in #51289. No existing issue reporting this exact bug or open PR addressing this fix was found in searches for dummy normalization, `FusedMMInputNorm`, and `mm_input_norm`.

## Claims

- Dummy loading preserves the image processor's rescale, mean, and standard deviation transform.
- A regression test in the existing normalization suite verifies unchanged buffer values and correct normalization across all uint8 pixel values.

## Validation

Validated on a CUDA GPU with Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regression before the fix | Failed: all three scale values were overwritten |
| Complete image normalization suite after the fix | 30 passed |
| Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct image PPL, BF16, device normalization enabled | 11.970688 vs reference 11.916607; 0.453829% difference, within the 1% tolerance |
| Applicable pre-commit checks, including mypy and test tethering | Passed |

Reproduction commands from the repository root in a configured test environment:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mm_input_norm.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest 'tests/models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py::test_ppl[True-model_info2-32-extra_kwargs2]' -v -s
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fusion/mm_input_norm.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_mm_input_norm.py
```

The regression exercises `DummyModelLoader` directly; the PPL evaluation uses a real checkpoint. Full trainer-to-engine weight synchronization was not exercised. The regression is covered by the existing Model Executor CI suite.

## Details

The normalization buffers encode `weight = rescale_factor / image_std` and `bias = -image_mean / image_std`. They come from processor configuration, but persistent registration exposes them to dummy weight initialization. Subsequent parameter-only RL weight synchronization does not restore these constants, leaving the vision encoder with incorrectly normalized inputs.

`persistent=False` excludes the buffers from checkpoint state and the dummy loader while retaining normal module device movement. The forward computation and platform kernels are unchanged.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and PR preparation.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks
author: okorzh-amd
body:
This carries #56831 by @CedricHwong forward to current main. That PR has been idle since 09-14 and no longer passes CI after the rebase. Cedric's commit is kept unchanged, with his authorship. The two commits on top address the review comments on that PR.

Adaptive verification (DSpark) picks the per-step draft budget on the host from rank-local stale confidences, then picks which slots to keep on the device from rank-local live confidences. If TP ranks disagree on either one, they run different batch layouts: different token counts, or equal totals with different request boundaries. That breaks the collectives that follow and can hang them (#54011). This PR makes TP rank 0 authoritative:

1. `get_num_tokens`: `draft_budget` is broadcast with `broadcast_object` (shm MessageQueue, host only).
2. `reallocate_drafts`: on steps that trim, the per-request `capacities` are broadcast from rank 0 before `cu_num_logits` / `query_start_loc` are built.

Both conditions around (2), `draft_budget == 0` and `draft_budget < scheduled drafts`, depend only on the broadcast budget and scheduler-provided counts. Every TP rank therefore takes the same branch, and the collective cannot be entered unevenly.

### Changes vs #56831

- **Test updates for current main.** #56888 renamed `async_copy_to_gpu` to `async_tensor_h2d`; the old monkeypatch no longer resolved, giving 12 failures, and `cpu.yaml` runs `-x`. #58466 made `reallocate_drafts` also return the admitted draft counts. #63421 replaced the compiled budget assignment with a Triton kernel; the CPU test stands in for it with its global top-k reference. #55939 made `tests/v1/spec_decode` type-checked, so the test now narrows `_batch_budget` before indexing it.
- **Real multi-rank test.** `test_tp_ranks_agree_on_verification_layout[2, 4]` spawns gloo ranks with a real TP `GroupCoordinator` and drives the real `get_num_tokens` / `reallocate_drafts`. The ranks' confidences differ by one fp32 ULP, across three cases: a draft-budget tie, an equal-total boundary split, and 64 randomized steps. Every rank must end up with the leader's budget, capacities, `cu_num_logits` and `query_start_loc`. It replaces the single-process budget emulation.
- **Transport.** The capacities sync uses plain `get_tp_group().broadcast`, i.e. c10d on the TP device group, as in #56831.
  - Routing `GroupCoordinator.broadcast` through the device communicator (PyNCCL) would be about 2x cheaper per call. On CUDA it would also avoid creating the device group's NCCL communicator on the first trimmed step. But it changes every `GroupCoordinator.broadcast` caller (PCP `sync_drafts` too) and needs XPU validation, so it will be a separate PR.

Scope: this covers TP. It also covers DCP when PCP = 1; DCP groups span PCP before TP. With PCP > 1, each PCP slice's TP group has its own leader. Since #61994, DeepSeek-V4.1 on NVIDIA rejects AV + PCP (it requires fixed-length DSpark). The generic `PCPManager` path still admits it, which predates this PR and is a follow-up.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, plus `mypy` / `ruff` via the pre-commit pins.
- Multi-rank CPU harness: real gloo groups, the real `GroupCoordinator` and the real `AdaptiveVerificationManager`. TP 2/4/8, with injected per-rank confidence drift from 1 ULP to large.
- MI355X microbenchmark of both collectives, using vLLM's real TP group (`init_distributed_environment` + `initialize_model_parallel`) at TP2/TP4.
- MI355X end to end:
  - Model: Qwen3-4B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` with `enable_adaptive_verification: true`, V2 model runner, ROCM_ATTN.
  - Workload: 600 GSM8K CoT prompts, output 512, greedy.
  - A/B: main vs this PR, conc 1/16/64, 4 interleaved rounds per arm.
  - Divergence check: an instrumented main that all-gathers every rank's locally computed budget, capacities and confidences on every step.

## Test Result

- **Unit tests** (on main `7e3e3f6ab6`): `test_adaptive_verification.py` gives 31 passed and 7 skipped (the CUDA-only kernel tests). mypy and ruff are clean, and the real-rank test passed 10 of 10 runs.
  - **Without the budget broadcast:** the real-rank test fails on the budget tie; 36/64 random steps diverge at TP2, 53/64 at TP4.
  - **Without the capacities broadcast:** the real-rank test fails on the boundary case (4/64 random steps at TP2, 10/64 at TP4: equal totals, different request boundaries). The emulated reallocation tests at TP 2/4/8 fail too.
- **Multi-rank harness:** 0 mismatches on this branch at every world size and drift level.
  - Without the fix, a single fp32 ULP is enough to change the layout. Mismatching steps per 1000 at TP 2/4/8 (capacities or boundaries):
    - 1-16 ULP: 0-2
    - 1e-4 relative: 2-9
    - 1e-2 relative: 65-382
  - Most mismatches have equal totals across ranks but different request boundaries.
- **Per-step cost, MI355X, p50 (p90), slowest rank:**

| | TP2 | TP4 |
|---|---|---|
| `broadcast_object(budget)`: every step that has drafts, host only | 6.7 us (7.5) | 7.9 us (8.2) |
| `capacities` broadcast (c10d, as in this PR): trimmed steps only. Host enqueue + in-stream GPU time; does not depend on num_reqs from 1 to 256 | ~32 + ~25 us | ~33 + ~26 us |
| Worst-case total for a trimmed step, with no overlap | ~64 us | ~68 us (p90 ~76) |

  That is 0.4-1.4% of a 5-15 ms decode step, at most. The host part overlaps GPU work under async scheduling. With PyNCCL (the planned follow-up), a trimmed step costs about 25-29 us.
- **End to end at TP2, measured with the capacities sync on PyNCCL (an earlier revision of this PR); the c10d path still needs an e2e run (GPUs were busy): no measurable regression.** Each delta is within about 1.2 standard deviations; run-to-run CV is 0.2-0.6%.

| conc | output tok/s, main | output tok/s, this PR | delta | TPOT p50, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 721.0 ± 4.1 | 727.7 ± 10 | +0.9% | 1.311 → 1.314 ms |
| 16 | 5489 ± 12 | 5493 ± 15 | +0.1% | 2.755 → 2.763 ms |
| 64 | 10590 ± 50 | 10585 ± 19 | -0.1% | 5.615 → 5.629 ms |

  Acceptance length is unchanged (±0.7%). There were 0 failed requests in 24 runs. The `capacities` broadcast fired on about 97% of c16/c64 steps and about 7% of c1 steps.
- **Natural divergence was not observed on this setup.**
  - Instrumented main ran 8434 steps at TP2 and 7886 steps at TP4: 0 budget, capacities or confidence mismatches.
  - A separate DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MI355X serving trace ran about 478k AV steps, also with 0 mismatches.
  - Here the confidence inputs are bitwise identical across ranks, because the custom all-reduce sums in a fixed rank order. Divergence needs rank-asymmetric numerics, such as rank-order-dependent reductions, non-deterministic kernels, or the TP8 H20 DeepSeek-V4 setup in #54011.
  - The fix is cheap insurance against that: per the numbers above, about 7 us host per step plus about 19 us per trimmed step.

Co-authored with @CedricHwong (original fix, #56831). Supersedes #56831.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Keep the JinaVL score token when truncating score prompts
author: cycancode
body:
## Overview

`jinaai/jina-reranker-m0` scores the hidden state of a score token (id 100) that `JinaVLForSequenceClassification.post_process_tokens` appends to the prompt. Since #28631, `CrossEncoderIOProcessor` appends it in `get_score_prompt`, before `render` calls `tok_params.apply_post_tokenization`. When `truncate_prompt_tokens` is binding, truncation runs on the prompt that already has the score token. With the default right-side truncation, that cuts the score token off, and `/score` and `/rerank` silently return the classifier output for an ordinary prompt token. This reserves room for the tokens `post_process_tokens` appends: truncation, padding and the length check run with limits reduced by that count, and the tokens are appended afterwards. The reference `compute_score` in the model repo does the same (it truncates to `max_length - 1`, then appends the score token).

## Claims

- With a binding `truncate_prompt_tokens`, jina-reranker-m0 scores match scoring the template truncated to `truncate_prompt_tokens - 1` tokens plus the score token, and the prompt stays within `truncate_prompt_tokens`.
- `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1` on prompts longer than `max_model_len` keeps working: the prompt is truncated to `max_model_len - 1` tokens plus the score token.
- No change for models whose `post_process_tokens` is a no-op (every other cross-encoder). The change stays in `CrossEncoderIOProcessor`, plus a small `reserve_tokens` helper in `vllm/entrypoints/pooling/utils.py`.

## Validation

Real server on `34ac4f96a3` (`jinaai/jina-reranker-m0 --runner pooling --max-model-len 512`, RTX 4090, `--enforce-eager`). `/rerank` with query "What is the capital of France? Please answer briefly and precisely." and two documents (Paris, Berlin). The references are `/pooling` (`task="classify"`) on the explicit template token IDs, truncated, plus the score token.

Short documents (templates of 32 and 34 tokens), `truncate_prompt_tokens=28`:

| | Paris | Berlin |
|---|---|---|
| reference: 27 tokens + score token | 0.9831 | 0.8146 |
| `main` | 0.9857 | 0.9563 |
| this PR | 0.9830 | 0.8142 |

Long documents (templates of 672 and 674 tokens), `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1`:

| | Paris | Berlin |
|---|---|---|
| reference: 511 tokens + score token | 0.9213 | 0.8930 |
| `main` | 0.9380 | 0.9980 |
| this PR | 0.9211 | 0.8914 |

On `main` the irrelevant document scores about as high as the relevant one, or higher. The remaining differences are bf16 noise between batched and single requests.

Tests:

- New `tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py::test_truncation_keeps_jinavl_score_token`, parametrized over `truncate_prompt_tokens=4` and `-1`. Both cases fail on `main` (the score token is cut off) and pass with this PR.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py`: 27 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

## Details

Before #28631, `get_score_prompt` tokenized with truncation, appended the score token, and the serving layer only validated the length. #28631 moved post-tokenization truncation into `render` after `get_score_prompt`, so it now also runs over the appended token.

`render` now shrinks `max_total_tokens`, `truncate_prompt_tokens` and `pad_prompt_tokens` by the number of appended tokens (`reserve_tokens`) (`-1` follows the reduced `max_total_tokens`), tokenizes and truncates with those limits, and then calls `post_process_tokens`. The count is derived once by running `post_process_tokens` on an empty prompt, so the model interface is unchanged. As a side effect, the "maximum context length" in the length error for jina-reranker-m0 reports `max_model_len - 1`, which is the real limit for the template.

An earlier version of this PR appended the token after truncation without reserving room, so the prompt could exceed the limits by one token (thanks to the review for catching that).

Not a duplicate: I found no issue or PR for this (searched "jina-reranker-m0 truncate", "post_process_tokens", "score token truncation rerank", "JinaVL truncate_prompt_tokens"). #55200 validates truncated prompts for the jina-reranker-v3 processor (`JinaRankingIOProcessor`), and #49963 restored `truncate_prompt_tokens` for that processor. Neither touches the JinaVL score token.

AI assistance was used to find this bug, write the fix and the test, and run the validation shown above.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Render GPT-OSS chats with Harmony in /tokenize
author: shijie-lyu
body:
## Overview

For GPT-OSS, `/tokenize` renders a chat with the model's HF chat template, while the chat route renders it with Harmony. So `/tokenize` returns ids that the chat route never prefills, which breaks the invariant `test_tokenize_matches_render_for_multimodal_input` already states for multimodal input: `/tokenize` matches `/v1/chat/completions/render`. This PR renders GPT-OSS chats in `/tokenize` through `OnlineRenderer.render_chat`, the function the chat route and the render endpoint use.

## Claims

- For GPT-OSS chats, `/tokenize` returns the ids of `/v1/chat/completions/render`. Through the shared `render_chat`, those are the ids `/v1/chat/completions` prefills; that route itself was not run. Before this change they differed for chats with a system message and no tools, and for tool-call histories.
- Other models are unchanged: their chats still go through `preprocess_chat`.

## Validation

Reproducer: `vllm launch render openai/gpt-oss-20b` (GPU-less) serves both `/tokenize` and `/v1/chat/completions/render`. The same messages were posted to both, on main b1ab16c548 and with this PR:

| Messages | main: `/tokenize` / render | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| system, user, assistant | 126 / 125 ids, first difference at 82 | 125 / 125, equal |
| system, user | 105 / 104, first difference at 82 | 104 / 104, equal |
| user | 82 / 82, equal | equal |
| system, user, `tools` | 129 / 129, equal | equal |
| system, user, an assistant tool call and its result, `tools` | 164 / 162 | 162 / 162, equal |
| system, user, `tools: []` | 83 / 83, not equal | equal |

At index 82 `/tokenize` has `"\n\n"` (279) where Harmony has `<|end|>` (200007): the GPT-OSS template ends the developer instructions with `"\n\n"` when no tools follow, and Harmony does not.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py tests/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/test_serving_tokenization.py -q
```

47 passed. The new `test_tokenize_matches_chat_render_for_gpt_oss` starts the GPU-less render server for openai/gpt-oss-20b (config and tokenizer only, about 23 s) and asserts that `/tokenize` and `/v1/chat/completions/render` return the same ids for a chat with a system message. On main it fails on the ids: `At index 71 diff: 364 != 13`.

`pre-commit` ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy and check-test-tethering: passed.

Not run on a GPU: the change affects only the ids `/tokenize` returns. Generation and the chat route are unchanged, so no model eval applies.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer script</summary>

```python
import json, sys, urllib.request

BASE = sys.argv[1]  # e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8000 for `vllm launch render openai/gpt-oss-20b`
T = "the cat sat on a warm mat and then ran to the old red barn"
CHATS = {
    "system,user,assistant": [{"role": r, "content": T} for r in ("system", "user", "assistant")],
    "system,user": [{"role": "system", "content": T}, {"role": "user", "content": T}],
    "user": [{"role": "user", "content": T}],
}

def post(path, body):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read())

for name, messages in CHATS.items():
    tokens = post("/tokenize", {"messages": messages})["tokens"]
    token_ids = post("/v1/chat/completions/render", {"messages": messages})["token_ids"]
    print(name, len(tokens), len(token_ids), tokens == token_ids)
```
</details>

## Details

Root cause: `ServingTokenization.create_tokenize` calls `OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat` for every chat, which applies the HF chat template. `OnlineRenderer.render_chat` takes its Harmony branch when `model_type` is `gpt_oss`.

The fix: for GPT-OSS, `/tokenize` builds a `ChatCompletionRequest` from the request's chat fields (`TokenizeChatRequest.to_chat_completion_request`) and calls `render_chat`, as `/v1/chat/completions/render` does. Only declared chat fields are copied, so undeclared body fields such as `stream_options` or `reasoning_effort` do not reach the chat request's validation, as in the Rust frontend's `TokenizeChatRequest::into_chat_request`. An empty `tools` list, which `/tokenize` accepts and the chat route rejects, is dropped.

Behaviour changes for GPT-OSS `/tokenize`, which now follows the chat route:
- `add_generation_prompt`, `continue_final_message`, `chat_template` and `chat_template_kwargs` no longer change the ids. The chat route ignores them for GPT-OSS today.
- A `chat_template` sent without `--trust-request-chat-template` is ignored rather than refused, since it is never rendered.

Open question: the Rust frontend's Harmony renderer honours `add_generation_prompt: false` and rejects `continue_final_message`. Doing the same in `_make_request_with_harmony` would apply to the chat route and `/tokenize` together; I left it out of this PR because it changes the chat route.

Why `/tokenize` rather than pointing callers to `/v1/chat/completions/render`: the render endpoint is off unless the server runs with `--enable-scale-out`, while `/tokenize` is always on. The Rust frontend's `/tokenize` already renders GPT-OSS chats with its Harmony renderer, through the same `prepare_text_request` as its chat route.

Related: #33693 (a draft, idle since April) moves Harmony encoding into the renderer layer, which would make this branch unnecessary. #58414 changes how Harmony is detected; this PR reads `online_renderer.use_harmony`, so `/tokenize` keeps following the chat route either way. #52513 fixes a different `/tokenize` vs chat-route mismatch (`reasoning_content`). No open issue or PR covers this one.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Take openai-audio input tokens from server usage
author: dilberx
body:
## Overview

`vllm bench serve --backend openai-audio` reports the wrong input token count for every transcription request. The audio datasets set `prompt_len` from a text prompt the request never sends, and the client ignores `usage.prompt_tokens`. This reads `prompt_tokens` from the usage chunk, as the completions and chat clients already do.

## Claims

- On Whisper the bench reported 8 input tokens per request, the tokens of the dataset prompt "Transcribe the audio.". The server reports `100 × audio seconds + 4` (304 for a 3 s clip, 2,504 for 25 s).
- Total input tokens now match the server. Output tokens were already correct.

## Validation

New test in `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, over the completions, chat and audio clients: `prompt_len` takes the server's usage value. It fails for audio on `main`. `tests/benchmarks/` passes (194) and pre-commit is clean.

RTX 3080, `openai/whisper-tiny`, 18 clips from 3 s to 25 s cut from vLLM's `mary_had_lamb` and `winning_call` test assets, `--dataset-name custom_audio`:

| | `main` | this branch | server `usage.prompt_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| total input tokens | 144 | 21,757 | 21,757 |

Total token throughput is computed from total input tokens, so it rises with this change. Request rate and output tokens are unchanged. The request on the wire carries no prompt field.

## Details

The server's `vllm:prompt_tokens_total` metric rose by 72 on the same run, 4 per request, so it counts the decoder prompt without the audio, while `usage` counts both. I left that alone; the bench follows `usage` as it does for the other backends.

The legacy `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py` reads `prompt_tokens` for no backend, so it is out of scope.

No issue or PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this and write the change and test. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Align adaptive draft prefill graph padding
author: amenomori
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62793. Align adaptive-verification draft-prefill CUDA graphs with the target's shared attention metadata, including when another data-parallel rank is prefilling.

## Claims

- Capture varlen draft-prefill graphs under AV and exclude prefill-bearing batches from decode-only graphs.
- Preserve the agreed `max_query_len` in `DPSyncState` and reuse it, including `None`, without another collective.
- Extend the existing regression with DP > 1 peer-prefill and longer-peer-decode cases.

## Validation

Rebased onto upstream main `5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9`. Local checks on macOS:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/cudagraph \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  -k 'not test_full_capture_sets_graph_pool_id_before_cuda_graph' -q
```

**29 passed, 1 deselected.** The excluded pre-existing capture test requires a current stream unavailable on this host; CI runs the complete file.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py \
  -k 'test_every_dp_rank_must_agree_to_microbatch or test_decode_threshold_only_applies_when_every_rank_is_a_uniform_decode or test_microbatching_pads_all_ranks_to_the_largest or test_microbatching_survives_a_rank_that_cannot_fill_it or test_microbatching_off_when_a_rank_does_not_allow_it' -q
```

**5 passed, 25 deselected.** Applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, mypy and CI test tethering, and `git diff --check` passed.

The existing **CPU V1 Others** (`v1-others-cpu`) Buildkite job already runs `test_cudagraph_manager.py` and depends on `vllm/v1/` and `tests/v1`. No CI configuration changes are needed. [Buildkite CI #97530](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97530) is running for `94fcf82c7f83`. Pre-commit and docs passed; `v1-others-cpu`, which includes the added DP regressions, has not completed yet.

`CPU-Spec Decode Tests` soft-failed on the existing `test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype`: `ReplicatedLinear` has no `cpu_linear`. The exact upstream base `5d35ce39` has the [same failure in main CI #97527](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97527#01a17bf7-46e5-4f1f-bc9e-95f8e3cd8d54), also with 1 failed, 111 passed and 121 skipped. The affected test/model/linear files are unchanged by this PR. The same failure was independently reproduced on both the PR head and a clean base worktree with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` and the isolated pytest node. The test omits CPU linear post-load initialization; this unrelated baseline failure is left outside this PR.

<details>
<summary>DP regression before and after the fix</summary>

Before rebasing, the extended regression was run with production files from the previous PR head `b3ae85bbec7eb348130f4a2e18a71b1bfcbca06c`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/cudagraph \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  -k draft_prefill_matches_shared_target_metadata_shape -q
```

Before: **2 failed, 5 passed, 23 deselected**. The peer-prefill case selects draft FULL versus target PIECEWISE; the longer-peer-decode case exposes the missing synchronized-bound field. With the fix: **7 passed, 23 deselected**.

These are CPU dispatch regressions with a simulated external collective, not real multi-GPU inference results. The rebased suite also passes, as reported above.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier single-GPU model validation</summary>

The equivalent candidate-source fix was validated on v0.31.0, H100 NVL, Qwen3-32B W4A16 + Eagle3, K=3, FA3, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, concurrency 4. Across two independent starts with 10s warmup and 30s measurement, mean output throughput was 352.4 tok/s unpatched versus 684.0 tok/s with the candidate; mean acceptance lengths were 1.425 and 2.906. Both candidate runs had zero request errors and matched a fixed-K greedy smoke on four prompts. The isolated FA3 reproducer in #62793 failed with mismatched padding and passed with aligned padding.

Those results are from v0.31.0, not this rebased checkout or the DP follow-up. The instance was destroyed. No current multi-GPU validation or AV trimming speedup is claimed.

</details>

## Details

Draft prefill shares the target's attention metadata and must use the same padded request layout. With DP, another rank's prefill makes the agreed query bound `None`; reusing a local decode bound can incorrectly select FULL after the target selected PIECEWISE. All state-construction paths now preserve the agreed bound, while uniform draft batches reset it to their own query length. The upstream benchmark's eager state is updated for the new field.

Duplicate checks were refreshed: #62953 handles final redispatch disagreement between rank-local graph inventories; #63523 optimizes CPU metadata math. Neither implements this target-to-draft bound reuse fix. No other open PR was found linked to #62793.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation, tests, review and validation.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Reject non-linear expert placement with EP
author: gc-fu
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62801.

Reject non-linear expert placement when wrapping fused MoE layers with LoRA and expert parallelism. Adapter loading slices a contiguous range of global experts per EP rank, which does not match round-robin ownership.

## Claims

- Check the MoE runner's resolved placement and raise a `ValueError` naming the incompatible strategy before adapter weights are allocated.
- Preserve linear placement, including requested round-robin placement that resolves to linear, and configurations without EP.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_moe_lora_ep_load.py tests/distributed/test_expert_placement.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py tests/lora/test_moe_lora_ep_load.py
```

- 12 tests passed. The added regression fails on unmodified main: 1 failed, 4 passed. It uses `ExpertMapManager` to exercise actual placement resolution, including the linear fallback.
- Changed-file pre-commit passed, including mypy.
- Real two-process XPU EP validation: a tiny randomly initialized DeepSeek-V2 fixture with two expert groups starts with round-robin on main; both workers reject it with the new error after this change.
- Tiny Qwen3-MoE FP16, TP2+EP, eager, `allgather_reducescatter`: linear and requested round-robin resolving to linear both completed base → nonzero expert adapter → base generation (two prompts, eight output tokens each). Token IDs and logprobs matched unmodified-main linear results exactly across all three phases (maximum logprob difference 0.0); both workers confirmed nonzero expert adapter weights.
- All-files pre-commit was run. It regenerated an unrelated ROCm dependency lockfile, and the entrypoint test failed under root. All 11 entrypoint cases passed as a non-root user; generated lock changes are excluded. Type checking reported no errors; the final changed-file run passed.

The existing Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13 XPU / Triton 3.7 environment was preserved; main pins PyTorch 2.14. The model fixtures validate distributed startup and generation behavior, not trained-model quality. CUDA/ROCm hardware validation was not run.

## Details

`MoERunner.expert_placement_strategy` forwards the resolved expert-map strategy. Checking the requested parallel configuration would incorrectly reject valid fallback-to-linear configurations. The check runs once during wrapper initialization.

For example, with four experts and EP2, round-robin rank 0 owns experts 0 and 2, while the contiguous LoRA checkpoint filter selects experts 0 and 1.

Duplicate-work checks found no PR implementing this placement guard. Related open work [#49058](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49058) addresses SP restrictions and padded LoRA buffers; [#48460](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48460) handles partial fused MoE adapters. Their diffs do not validate resolved expert placement.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the relevant tests.

title: [Bugfix][EPD] Check encoder readiness for prefix replay
author: gty111
body:
## Overview

Wait for encoder embeddings needed by prefix replay before admitting an EPD request.

## Claims

- Include the replayed prefix tail in EC readiness checks without changing KV-hit accounting or replay behavior when a KV load restores the window.
- Prevent missing encoder embeddings from crashing the consumer during DeepSeek-V4.1 prefix replay.

## Validation

Slurm E2E: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1E (TP1) + 1PD (TP2), Mooncake TCP, MRV2, raw-image forwarding, prefix/processor caches and CUDA Graphs enabled. After 128 disjoint random-image warmups, MUIRBench (512 questions, concurrency 64) completed with **512/512 HTTP 200**, **303/512 correct (59.18%)**, and no `Encoder cache miss`, using an 8 GiB consumer pool.

## Details

EC readiness was checked before SWA replay rewound the computed-token boundary. For example, a KV hit at 640 covers an image ending at 567, but replay starts at 512 and still needs that image. Skipping its load causes `Encoder cache miss`. Check EC readiness against the replay start while retaining the original KV-hit boundary for allocation and statistics.

Checked related open EPD/prefix-replay PRs; none addresses this missing-load path. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

title: [Bugfix] Fix GPTQ checkpoint loading for PLaMo3
author: okdshin
body:
## Overview

Fix GPTQ checkpoint loading for PLaMo3, broken since #54809, by building its `lm_head` as most models do: store `quant_config` on `Plamo3ForCausalLM`, pass it to `lm_head`, and name the head `maybe_prefix(prefix, "lm_head")`.

## Claims

- GPTQ PLaMo3 checkpoints load again. They previously failed with `ValueError: There is no module or parameter named '...g_idx'`.
- PLaMo3's head is named `lm_head`, its state-dict name, instead of `.lm_head`, so quant config entries that name it exactly (e.g. compressed-tensors `ignore` / `targets: ["lm_head"]`) now match it.
- No change for BF16 checkpoints or for GPTQ with `lm_head: false`. Nested prefixes (e.g. `draft_model.lm_head`) are unchanged.

## Validation

Reproducer: `vllm serve` any PLaMo3 checkpoint quantized by GPTQModel, which writes `.g_idx` even with `desc_act=False`. We ran a PLaMo3 31B GPTQ checkpoint (internal) on 1x A100 with the nightly image at 042ab03 (`plamo3.py` is unchanged on current main):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Before | Engine init fails with the `g_idx` `ValueError` |
| After | Serves; chat and completion requests return correct answers |

Head name matching, run on this branch:

| prefix | `should_ignore_layer(ignore=["lm_head"])` | `find_matched_target(targets=["Linear", "lm_head"])` |
|---|---|---|
| `.lm_head` (before) | `False` | `None` |
| `lm_head` (after) | `True` | `"lm_head"` |

On this branch:

- `pytest tests/model_executor/test_plamo3.py`: 1 passed (CPU-only host). This existing test does not build `Plamo3ForCausalLM` through `__init__`, so it does not cover this change.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass, including mypy.

## Details

**GPTQ loading.** Since #54809, GPTQ layers no longer register `g_idx`, and checkpoint `.g_idx` tensors are dropped by `QuantizationConfig.get_checkpoint_weight_mapper()`. `AutoWeightsLoader` takes this mapper from the first module, among the model and its direct children, that has a `quant_config` attribute. PLaMo3 set none, so the lookup stopped at `lm_head`, which `ParallelLMHead` gives `quant_config=None`, and the `.g_idx` tensors had nowhere to go. Storing `quant_config` on `Plamo3ForCausalLM` fixes the lookup. Passing it to `lm_head` too matches most models (e.g. Qwen3, Llama), and lets a head that the checkpoint quantizes get its quant method instead of always being unquantized (not tested, as we have no such PLaMo3 checkpoint).

**Head name.** `ParallelLMHead`'s `prefix` is the layer's full name in the state dict. `f"{prefix}.lm_head"` gave `.lm_head` for a top-level model, which matches no checkpoint key. Now that `lm_head` receives the quant config, quant methods look the head up by this name, so exact entries for `lm_head` would miss it. Weight loading is unaffected, since it resolves parameters by module path, and the online lm_head copies only carry the prefix over. The PLaMo3 checkpoints we know of do not quantize the head, so this does not change how they load.

No accuracy evaluation: the change only lets the loader drop `.g_idx` and renames the head, so it does not alter compute for any checkpoint that loads. No new test: CI has no GPTQ PLaMo3 checkpoint, a unit test for the loader lookup would need heavy stubbing, and checking the head name alone is trivial. No duplicate: among open PRs mentioning PLaMo3, `g_idx`, or `lm_head` quantization, only #45535 edits `plamo3.py`, and it passes `quant_config` to `embed_tokens` only, which neither the loader lookup (model and direct children) nor `lm_head` depends on. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter reviewed all changes and ran the tests.

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Avoid re-marking committed prompt-tail boundaries as cached this step
author: khyun1109
body:
## Overview

On hybrid models with `mamba_cache_mode="align"` (e.g. Qwen3.5), requests whose prompts share their last hash-aligned boundary are admitted one per engine step once that boundary is committed. This hits reads fanned out over one prompt and the children of a parallel-sampling request (`n > 1`). This PR skips re-caching that boundary in `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` when the block already carries its hash, so these requests are admitted together. Related: #29387 (the same-step guard this interacts with), #61192 (`/v1/systemone` reads over one state, which take this path).

## Claims

- Bug fix: requests that hit an already committed prompt-tail boundary are no longer deferred, so a fan-out over a shared prefix is admitted together instead of one request per step. Which blocks are cached and hit does not change.
- `vllm bench serve` on Qwen3.5-4B: 5.0x request throughput for a fan-out over shared prefixes with 1-token outputs, 3.0x with 64-token outputs, and 4.7x for parallel sampling with `n=16`. Median TTFT drops 5–15x.
- No accuracy change: on `/v1/systemone` decisions, flips against a serial reference stay at noise level (1/458 vs. 2/458, same max |Δp|), and accuracy is 0.891 with and without the fix.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** Qwen3.5-4B on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, `main` at 81c2bd702 with and without this PR, one fresh server per variant:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 --max-num-seqs 256

# Fan-out: 24 prefixes x 16 prompts, each prefix's prompts sent together.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
    --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 592 \
    --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 48 --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 24 \
    --prefix-repetition-output-len 1 --num-prompts 384 --disable-shuffle \
    --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1

# Parallel sampling: 64 prompts of 640 tokens, n=16.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 640 --random-output-len 32 \
    --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8 --extra-body '{"n": 16}' \
    --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1
```

The default `max_num_seqs` exceeds the Mamba cache blocks available at this memory share, hence `--max-num-seqs 256`. The 592-token prefix is one 576-token hybrid block plus 16 tokens, so each prompt's last hash boundary (576) lies inside the shared prefix and away from the prefix/suffix junction, where re-tokenization could shift it. Engine steps are the `/metrics` delta of the `iteration_tokens_total` count. Mean ± std over seeds 1–3:

| workload | output len | variant | req/s | median TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | engine steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fan-out, 384 prompts | 1 | main | 36.31 ± 0.72 | 3341 ± 127 | 3646 ± 21 | 342 ± 6 |
| | 1 | main + fix | **181.31 ± 7.42** | 649 ± 28 | 832 ± 22 | 42 ± 4 |
| | 64 | main | 23.71 ± 0.66 | 3729 ± 157 | 4852 ± 449 | 763 ± 15 |
| | 64 | main + fix | **70.78 ± 0.06** | 353 ± 12 | 783 ± 3 | 222 ± 1 |
| parallel sampling, n=16, 64 prompts | 32 | main | 1.52 ± 0.02 | 3871 ± 26 | 4232 ± 81 | 1952 ± 0 |
| | 32 | main + fix | **7.10 ± 0.04** | 264 ± 1 | 551 ± 8 | 293 ± 1 |

Prefix-cache hit rates are the same with and without the fix (0.844, 0.900 and 0.844 for the three rows).

**Tests** (on 81c2bd702):

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_mamba_align_siblings_hit_committed_boundary_in_one_step` fails on `main` (`sibling 0 was deferred`) and passes with the fix. A producer commits a 2-block prefix in step 1; in step 2 it finishes its prompt and three siblings hit the committed boundary.
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/`: 475 passed, including the GPU end-to-end `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` (`[base]` and `[mtp]`).
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`: all hooks pass.

The new test is marked `cpu_test`, so it runs in the existing `v1/core` CPU step in CI.

**Model evaluation.** `/v1/systemone` on `main` (0d00d8b9c): 458 questions over 30 long states (four RACE-middle passages per state, 1,200–1,600 tokens, about 15 questions per request), 8 requests in flight. The serial reference uses `--max-num-seqs 1` without prefix caching.

| | main | main + fix |
|---|---|---|
| questions/s | 36.35 | 57.10 (+57%) |
| p50 request latency | 3.22 s | 2.06 s |
| accuracy | 0.891 | 0.891 |
| decision flips vs. serial reference, max \|Δp\| | 1/458, 0.087 | 2/458, 0.087 |

<details>
<summary>Earlier end-to-end runs: main 0d00d8b9c, v0.32.0 sweep, 27B decision model</summary>

Our own harness: N prompts share a prefix that ends on a hybrid block boundary, plus a 64-token suffix each, sent as token IDs to `/v1/completions` with `max_tokens=1`, 8 groups of 16 in flight.

**main (0d00d8b9c), Qwen3.5-4B, 576-token prefix, N=16:**

| | main | main + fix |
|---|---|---|
| reads/s (prefix-cache hit rate) | 41.96 (0.84) | 235.03 (0.84), 5.6x |
| engine steps for 384 requests | 361 | 25 |
| mean running requests | 1.07 | 15.98 |
| mean queue time per request | 1.98 s | 0.18 s |

**v0.32.0, Qwen3.5-4B (528-token hybrid block), reads/s.** A dense Qwen3-4B on the same harness reaches 239.9, 195.3 and 126.8 reads/s at N=16 for the three prefix lengths.

| prefix (tokens) | fan-out | v0.32.0 | v0.32.0 + fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 528 | 16 | 37.4 | 239.3 |
| 1056 | 16 | 37.6 | 184.3 |
| 2112 | 16 | 35.0 | 128.7 |
| 528 | 4 | 35.6 | 112.8 |

**v0.32.0, 27B Qwen3.5-hybrid decision model (`openjev/openjev`, 784-token hybrid block):**

| | v0.32.0 | v0.32.0 + fix |
|---|---|---|
| fan-out reads/s | 17.4 | 36.6 |
| engine steps for 384 requests | 384 | 24 |
| `/v1/systemone` long-state questions/s | 9.44 | 13.06 |
| decision flips vs. serial reference (458 questions) | 0 | 0 |

Throughput without prefix reuse (distinct cache salts) is unchanged: 47.0 reads/s on `main` (4B) and 5.5 reads/s on v0.32.0 (27B).

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` re-caches the prompt's last hash-aligned boundary whenever a request whose prompt passes that boundary is scheduled. The request's block at that boundary may already carry exactly that hash, either because it is a prefix-cache hit or because the request committed it in an earlier step. Nothing new is written in that step, but the function still returns the hash. `cache_blocks` then adds it to `cached_blocks_this_step`, and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` defers every other request whose hit ends on that block (the guard from #29387). This repeats whenever the producer's next chunk or a sibling is scheduled, so siblings are admitted one per step. Because the deferral is reported as insufficient blocks, the scheduler also stops scanning the waiting queue for that step. We found it by logging each deferral with the step that had added the hash: every one pointed at a re-cache of a block already keyed at that boundary.

**Fix.** In the non-checkpoint branch, return early when `source_block.block_hash_num_tokens == num_tokens`. The checkpoint branch above already uses the same condition.

**Why this is safe.** The skip applies only when the block already carries the hash for exactly this boundary, so its state was written in an earlier step or arrived as a hit. A sibling scheduled in this step reads it after that write, since forwards run in order. A step that does write the state still marks the hash, either through the first `cache_partial_block` call for a mid-block boundary or through the full-block loop in `cache_blocks`, so the #29387 guard still applies where it is needed.

**Not a duplicate.** The open PRs that touch `_cache_partial_tail_block` or `cached_blocks_this_step` fix other problems:

- #52972 and #53158 add a similar check to the full-attention manager's `_cache_partial_tail_block`, for stale partial hashes after full-block promotion.
- #56525 replaces the same-step set with a commit fence. The re-mark would still re-publish the hash there and fence siblings until the step commits, so the two changes compose.
- #61282 keeps the boundary state alive until the request ends.
- #55142, #52244 and #53802 change when or where the boundary is registered (connector loads, MTP, EAGLE).

None of them skips the re-cache in `MambaManager`'s non-checkpoint path. RFC #55697 and #55873/#55875/#55876 add application-declared checkpoints with producer/consumer scheduling; this fix is for the default path, with no markers.

**Scope.** The gain depends on siblings arriving together. With many unrelated prefixes interleaved, the bug still admits about one sibling per prefix in each step before the first deferral, so the gap shrinks. In a shuffled `prefix_repetition` run (24 prefixes of 1200 tokens with 64-token suffixes, otherwise as above), main and the fix were within noise: 105.6 ± 6.5 vs. 108.4 ± 5.2 req/s with 1-token outputs, and 35.4 ± 0.2 vs. 36.4 ± 0.9 req/s with 128-token outputs. That run is also close to compute-bound, since each sibling recomputes 112 tokens.

A sibling that arrives in the same step as the producer's first write is still deferred by the #29387 guard, as intended. We also tried letting the scheduler skip a deferred request instead of stopping the scan; with this fix in place it gave no further gain, so it is not included.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the issue, write the change and the test, and run the benchmarks. The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the regression test, and reviewed the results reported here.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Accept and echo prompt-cache and safety_identifier fields in the Responses API
author: albertoperdomo2
body:
## Overview

Fixes #62855. `/v1/responses` now accepts `safety_identifier`, `prompt_cache_retention` and `prompt_cache_options` as typed fields and echoes them, together with `prompt_cache_key` (#32824), on the response object, as OpenAI does.

## Claims

- The three fields are declared on `ResponsesRequest`, so they are validated. Before this change they were untyped extras
- `ResponsesResponse` echoes all four through `from_request`, which covers non-streaming, streaming (`response.created` …) and background responses
- `prompt_cache_retention` accepts `"in-memory"` (older `openai` SDKs), `"in_memory"` (current SDKs) and `"24h"`. Any other value returns 400
- No change for requests that don't send these fields; they echo as `null`

## Validation

New tests in `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py`: each field is echoed, an omitted field is `None`, invalid retention or `ttl` is rejected, and `response.created` carries the fields. They fail on `main` and pass with this change.

## Details

- Root cause: #32824 declared `prompt_cache_key` on the request but not on the response; the other three fields were never declared
- `PromptCacheOptions` is defined locally because the minimum supported `openai` (2.25) doesn't have it
- No length limit on `safety_identifier`. vLLM doesn't use the value, and a limit would turn requests that succeed today into 400s
- vLLM still doesn't act on these fields; the field descriptions say so

Claude Code used to validate the tests.
