title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Reject multimodal inputs in chunked embeddings
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Reject multimodal embedding requests when enable_chunked_processing is enabled, instead of silently dropping their multimodal data. Return HTTP 400 with guidance to disable chunked processing.

## Claims

- Reject multimodal inputs, including short inputs, before chunk expansion or inference submission.
- Preserve text-only chunked processing and multimodal requests with chunked processing disabled.

## Validation

uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_io_processor.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_protocol.py -q

72 tests passed. Added coverage for short and long multimodal inputs in mixed batches, plus the disabled-setting case. Applicable pre-commit checks passed.

Real HTTP validation used google/siglip-base-patch16-224 on an H800, BF16, eager mode, max_model_len=64, and max_num_seqs=1:

- With chunking enabled, image requests through /v2/embed and mixed text/image batches through /v1/embeddings returned HTTP 400. Subsequent text requests succeeded.
- With chunking disabled, image and mixed-batch requests succeeded; red and blue images produced different embeddings.
- A 217-token text input was split into four chunks. Its aggregated embedding matched the independently computed weighted, normalized reference within a maximum absolute difference of 3.31e-8.

## Details

maybe_pre_process_chunked() rebuilds inputs using tokens_input(), which discards multimodal payloads, hashes, and placeholders, even when the input fits in a single chunk.

This change validates the entire batch before rewriting inputs, preventing silent multimodal data loss when chunked processing is enabled.

title: [Bugfix][DSA] Reserve the decode indexer logits in the memory profile
author: gcanlin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DSA indexer's decode logits are not counted by the memory profiler, so eager and piecewise steps can OOM at runtime. This PR reserves them in the profiling run, the way DeepInfer's profile run does.

### OOM

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4×B200 DEP4 (InferenceX recipe, `--max-num-seqs 256`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, 5 spec tokens, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97`), AgentX at concurrency 512. Rank 0 died 5 minutes into the load:

```
File "vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py", line 1086, in forward
    hidden_states, pre_mix, *late_aux = self.decoder_replay_layers(
...
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 893, in sparse_attn_indexer
    logits = as_fp32_logits(logits, seq_lens.view(-1))
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 312, in as_fp32_logits
    out = torch.empty_strided(
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.07 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 178.35 GiB of which 3.04 GiB is free.
```

### Why

- The indexer's decode path allocates the paged MQA logits on every call. DeepGEMM returns `[decode rows, max_model_len]`, in BF16 on SM100.
- Every top-k backend except `deep_select` then reads an FP32 copy made by `as_fp32_logits`. Here that copy alone is 786 rows (131 decodes × 6) × 1,049,088 columns × 4 B = 3.07 GiB.
- The profiling run reserves only `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` (512 MiB, the prefill chunk budget), so the KV cache takes this memory.
- FULL decode graphs keep the logits in their graph pool. Mixed batches, batches above the capture sizes, and eager mode allocate them from whatever the KV cache leaves.

### How DeepInfer handles it

[DeepInfer@774ce24](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer/tree/774ce244b87cc0eb8d4b94ab9f5de2ab22049f01) sizes the decode logits the same way: `max_kv_len = runtime_max_model_len // kv_compress_ratio` ([index_attn.py#L95](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer/blob/774ce244b87cc0eb8d4b94ab9f5de2ab22049f01/deepinfer/model_executor/models/v4_modules/index_attn.py#L95), [#L434-L441](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer/blob/774ce244b87cc0eb8d4b94ab9f5de2ab22049f01/deepinfer/model_executor/models/v4_modules/index_attn.py#L434-L441)). It keeps them in BF16 ([#L87](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer/blob/774ce244b87cc0eb8d4b94ab9f5de2ab22049f01/deepinfer/model_executor/models/v4_modules/index_attn.py#L87)).

On decode engines, its `profile_run` runs `max_num_seqs` sequences of `1 + nextn` query tokens ([model_runner.py#L444-L511](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer/blob/774ce244b87cc0eb8d4b94ab9f5de2ab22049f01/deepinfer/worker/model_runner.py#L444-L511)). So the `[max_num_seqs × (1 + nextn), max_kv_len]` logits are part of the measured peak before the KV cache is sized.

### Fix

vLLM's shared indexer now does the same accounting. Its profiling (dummy) path reserves the larger of the prefill budget and the decode worst case:

- **Rows:** `min(max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens) × (1 + num_speculative_tokens)`. The profiling branch reads it from the current vLLM config.
- **Width:** `max_model_len`, padded as DeepGEMM pads the rows: whole KV splits (384 columns on SM100, 256 elsewhere) at a 1024-byte stride, i.e. 1536 BF16 columns on SM100 (1,049,088 for 1M, as in the OOM above) and 256 FP32 columns elsewhere.
- **Bytes per element:** 6 on SM100 (BF16 + FP32 copy), 2 with `deep_select` and no DCP, 4 on other platforms (FP32).

The runtime upcast and the reservation use the same predicate, so they cannot drift apart.

### Memory

Same configuration, KV cache per rank at startup:

| | top-k backend | decode logits reserved | CUDA graphs | KV cache / rank |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | `auto` | none (512 MiB budget) | 18.40 GiB | 41,050,274 |
| this PR | `auto` | 9.0 GiB (1536 rows × 1M × 6 B) | 18.40 GiB | 36,636,372 (−10.8%) |
| main | `deep_select` | none (512 MiB budget) | 12.39 GiB | 48,253,887 |
| this PR | `deep_select` | 3.0 GiB (1536 rows × 1M × 2 B) | 12.39 GiB | 48,163,989 (−0.2%) |

Measured before the width was aligned to 1536 columns, which adds 4.5 MiB (`auto`) or 1.5 MiB (`deep_select`) to the reservation.

The KV cache shrinks by less than the reservation, because the reservation stacks on top of what is live inside the indexer, not on top of the run's global peak. With `deep_select` the reservation costs 0.2% of the KV cache. The decode graphs also drop the FP32 copy, so `deep_select` leaves 17.5% more KV cache than `auto` on main.

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix DP NUMA affinity regression
author: bigPYJ1151
body:
## Overview

Fix CPU data-parallel ranks all binding to the same NUMA node, a regression from #45026. Fixes #47328.

## Claims

- With `--data-parallel-size N` on a multi-NUMA CPU host, each `EngineCore_DP*` now binds the cores and memory of its own NUMA node instead of every rank binding the same cores.
- Manual pinning with `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES` without DP is unchanged.
- No change to shared engine code; the fix is CPU-only (26 lines added, 10 removed, excluding tests).

## Validation

Reproducer from the issue, on a 6-NUMA-node host:

```bash
vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --data-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 256
```

OpenMP binding chosen by each EngineCore at startup (from the `OpenMP thread binding info` log):

| | `EngineCore_DP0` | `EngineCore_DP1` |
|---|---|---|
| main | cores 192-222, reserved 223 | cores 192-222, reserved 223 (same) |
| this PR | cores 192-222 (node 0), reserved 223 | cores 224-254 (node 1), reserved 255 |

With this PR the two workers also bind memory to distinct NUMA nodes (`NUMA binding: Using MEMBIND policy ... nodes (0)` and `(1)`), and a completion request returns a correct response end to end.

Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_cpu_resource_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py   # 21 passed
```

`test_omp_manager_binds_each_dp_rank_to_its_assigned_node` builds `OMPProcessManager` on a fake 2-node topology and checks that two DP ranks get disjoint cores. It fails (both ranks pick node 0 cores) if the assigned ids are ignored.

## Details

**Root cause.** #45026 moved the per-DP-rank device list from the device-control env var into `parallel_config.assigned_physical_gpu_ids`. `CoreEngineProcManager` still computes each rank's shard and stores it there, and GPU/XPU consume it. The CPU code still read only `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`, which nothing sets per rank anymore. `OMPProcessManager`, which runs in the EngineCore process, then saw the full node list and picked `allowed_numa_nodes[local_rank]`, the same node for every DP rank.

**Fix.** `get_visible_memory_node()` takes an optional `assigned_node_ids`. Precedence is assigned ids, then `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`, then all nodes. `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA` still overrides everything. Three call sites pass the ids:

- `OMPProcessManager` reads the config. The in-process `get_assigned_physical_gpu_ids()` global is only set inside worker processes, so it is not available in the EngineCore process where this runs.
- `CPUWorker` reads `vllm_config.parallel_config.assigned_physical_gpu_ids`.
- `CpuPlatform.get_current_memory_usage` runs in the worker and uses the global.

**Limitations.** `--device-ids` also fills `assigned_physical_gpu_ids`, so on CPU it now selects NUMA nodes (composed with `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`), consistent with GPU. This path is not covered by the validation above.

title: [Bugfix] Don't enable MM embedding inputs on KV consumers in language-model-only mode
author: ChingTsai
body:
## Overview

Since #56379, `_resolve_mm_embedding_inputs()` turns on `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` and `enable_mm_embeds` on every EC/KV consumer, including ones started with `--language-model-only`. This PR leaves both flags off on a KV-only consumer that sets `language_model_only` without `--enable-mm-embeds`, so a text-only KV consumer of a multimodal checkpoint runs in text-only mode again.

## Claims

- A language-model-only KV consumer (for example the decode instance of a text-only P/D deployment of a multimodal checkpoint) reports `supports_multimodal_inputs == False` again and no longer builds a `MultiModalBudget` or an HF processor in its scheduler, frontend and workers.
- This drops the host memory those processes have carried since #56379: about 3.4 GB per decode node in the deployment measured below.
- EPD consumers, the case #56379 targets, keep working: EC consumers always enable both flags, and a KV consumer still enables them unless it sets `language_model_only`. An EPD decode instance that uses `--language-model-only` to skip the encoder can opt back in with `--enable-mm-embeds`.

## Validation

**Unit.** New test `test_consumer_resolves_mm_embedding_inputs` in `tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py` (covered by the `tests/config` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`). It covers a KV consumer, a language-model-only KV consumer with and without `--enable-mm-embeds`, and a language-model-only EC consumer. Without the change, the language-model-only KV consumer case fails because `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` is `True`. All tests in the file and `pre-commit` pass (CPU-only container).

**Reproducer.** Start any multimodal checkpoint as a KV consumer in language-model-only mode, for example `--language-model-only --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' --kv-transfer-config '{..., "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}'`.
- Before: the frontend and workers log `enable_mm_embeds is True; modalities handled as embedding-only: ('image', 'video')`, and each EngineCore loads the HF processor.
- After: they log `All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model are set to 0, running in text-only mode.`

**End to end.** Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, 1P1D on TPU (prefill PCP8, decode DP8 on one host each), served through vLLM 0.31.0 with the vllm-torchtpu platform plugin. Same image for both runs. Measured with an earlier revision that behaves identically for this decode configuration.

| decode node | without | with | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pod anonymous memory at serving start | 147.0 GB | 143.6 GB | **−3.4 GB** |
| EngineCore RSS (×8) | 1210 MiB | 802 MiB | −408 MiB each |
| API server RSS | 1743 MiB | 1325 MiB | −418 MiB |
| Worker RSS (×8, total) | 135.3 GiB | 135.5 GiB | unchanged |

The prefill node (KV producer) is unaffected. Serving with the change: 1003/1003 requests, 1503 tok/s, median TPOT 24.0 ms (4096-in / 512-out, concurrency 64, 5 min). I did not validate on GPU.

## Details

Path on the decode (KV consumer) instance of a text-only P/D deployment:

1. Decode starts with `kv_role=kv_consumer` and `--language-model-only`, so every modality limit is 0.
2. `VllmConfig._resolve_mm_embedding_inputs()` sets `allow_missing_mm_embeddings = True` (KV consumer) and then `enable_mm_embeds = True`.
3. `ModelConfig._supports_multimodal_inputs()` returns `True` despite the zero limits, because `enable_mm_embeds` is set.
4. `Scheduler.__init__` (and the frontend's `InputProcessor` and the workers) build a `MultiModalBudget`. `get_mm_max_toks_per_item()` calls e.g. `Qwen2VLProcessingInfo.get_max_image_tokens()` -> `get_image_processor()` -> `ctx.get_hf_processor()`, which instantiates the full HF processor (`Qwen3VLProcessor.from_pretrained`). That processor loads a second copy of the tokenizer and deep-copies it.

A KV role alone does not tell a text-only P/D decode instance from an EPD one, so the change uses `language_model_only` as the text-only signal.

title: [Bugfix][Test] Rotate KV into RHT domain in the INT4 unified attn test
author: dudilester
body:
## Overview

Fix the INT4 case of `test_triton_unified_attention_per_token_head_scale`. It filled the INT4 cache with unrotated K/V and compared the result against a reference that didn't match what `unified_attention_int4` computes. The test now writes the cache in the RHT domain, like `reshape_and_cache_int4`, so it actually checks the INT4 attention kernel.

Follow-up to #40835. Removes the Intel CI deselect of `[int4-16-128-num_heads0-seq_lens1]`. Downstream report: intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton#8358.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR or issue fixes this test. #62113 edits the same test but keeps the INT4 reference as is and widens the Intel deselect to two INT4 cases. See Details for how the two PRs combine.

## Claims

- The kernel output and the reference now agree (correlation 1.0000 vs ≈ 0.00 before). The test no longer passes or fails depending on the RNG stream.
- INT4 uses the same `atol=rtol=5e-2` as INT8/FP8, down from 0.5. This also removes the Hopper-only `atol=1.1`.
- The Intel CI deselect for this case is removed.
- Test-only change. No kernel or runtime code is modified.

## Validation

**Test commands run:**

```bash
pytest -q tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py
# plus a probe that reruns the INT4 attention test over 200 seeds
# (set_random_seed(seed)) and records corr(output_q, output_ref),
# max |output_q - output_ref|, and how many seeds fail atol=rtol=5e-2.
```

**Results:**

| Platform | Test | Case | corr(out_q, ref) | worst abs diff | seeds failing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intel BMG (Arc Pro B65, and a G21 board) | before | seq_lens0 | ≈ 0.00 | 0.94 | — |
| | before | seq_lens1 | ≈ 0.00 | 1.79 | fails with the default seed |
| | after, tol 5e-2 | seq_lens0 | 1.0000 | 0.006 | 0/200 |
| | after, tol 5e-2 | seq_lens1 | 1.0000 | 0.012 | 0/200 |
| NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti (sm_86) | before, tol 0.5 | seq_lens1 | +0.004 | 1.89 | 62/200 |
| | after, tol 5e-2 | seq_lens0 | 1.0000 | 0.015 | 0/200 |
| | after, tol 5e-2 | seq_lens1 | 1.0000 | 0.021 | 0/200 |

- **BMG, `main` (e9cc6244a) with this PR:** all 82 tests in the file pass. Before the fix, `seq_lens1` fails: `Mismatched elements: 2 / 1024, Greatest absolute difference: 1.086 (up to 0.5 allowed), Greatest relative difference: 1.0`.
- **RTX 3060 Ti:** all INT4/INT8 cases pass before and after with the default seed. The FP8 cases fail both before and after with `fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture` (Ampere has no e4m3). This is unrelated to this PR.
- **BMG, this PR rebased on top of #62113:** all 94 tests pass, including the new `[(4, 128), (4, 97)]` INT4 case and both `seq_threshold_3D` values, with neither of #62113's two INT4 deselects. #62113 alone fails exactly the two INT4 cases it deselects.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `typos` pass.

**CI coverage:**
- The H200 MIG "Quantization" job runs this file, so CI covers the removed Hopper special case and the `hadacore` RHT path.
- The Intel quantization job now runs the formerly deselected case.

**Not validated locally:**
- Hopper and the `hadacore` path. On the RTX 3060 Ti the RHT ran through the Triton Hadamard kernel; the H200 job above covers both.
- ROCm.

## Details

**Root cause.** `reshape_and_cache_int4` stores `K_s = H·D·k` (RHT, with `H·H = d·I`, `D·D = I`). `unified_attention_int4` relies on that layout:
- it rotates `q' = H·D·q` and uses `softmax_scale / d`, so `q'·K_s / d = q·k`;
- it applies `D·H(·) / d` to the output, which undoes the rotation of V.

The test wrote unrotated `k`, `v` into the cache. As a result the kernel attended over `D·H·k / d` and `D·H·v / d`. Those entries have std ≈ 1/√128, so `output_q ≈ 0`, which is uncorrelated with `output_ref`.

The check `|out_q − ref| ≤ 0.5 + 0.5·|ref|` then reduces to roughly `|ref| ≤ 1`:
- kv_len 128 (`ref` std ≈ 0.15) almost always passes;
- kv_len 64/32 (`ref` std ≈ 0.25–0.3) fails on 1–2 elements whenever a `|ref|` tail exceeds 1.

That explains the reported abs diff just above 1.0 and relative diff of exactly 1.0. The failure is deterministic per seed but differs across platforms because their RNG streams differ, hence the Hopper `atol=1.1` and the Intel deselect.

**Fix.** Rotate K/V with `single_rht` (rounding through bf16, like `reshape_and_cache_int4`) before quantizing. Then inverse-rotate the dequantized reference back to the original domain, as `test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head` and `test_per_token_head_round_trip_accuracy` already do. The original-domain values stay around N(0,1), so the reference attention is still meaningful.

**Tolerance.** The remaining error comes from bf16 rounding and accumulation order only. The worst case is 0.021 over 200 seeds on CUDA, 2.4× under 5e-2. CUDA's error is larger than XPU's because the Triton Hadamard path rotates in bf16. The reference divides by `head_size`, which equals `largest_power_of_2_divisor(head_size)` for the parametrized `head_size=128`, consistent with the rest of the file.

**Interaction with #62113.** The two PRs only conflict textually, on adjacent lines:
- the tolerance block, where #62113 appends an assert that should be kept;
- the Intel deselect line.

Whichever PR merges second should keep that assert and drop all `test_triton_unified_attention_per_token_head_scale[int4-*]` deselects.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Release libgomp workers before forking engine processes
author: JaredforReal
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A forked EngineCore can deadlock during startup if the process that launches it has already run a multi-threaded torch CPU op. The cause is libgomp, which has no fork handler. This PR pauses the parent's OpenMP runtime in `get_mp_context()` before vLLM forks a process, so the child starts with a fresh OpenMP thread pool.

This is what has made `(H200 MIG 35GB) Language Models (Extended Pooling) Shard 2/4` hang in the scheduled full builds since [96139](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96139) (also [96247](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96247)). It probably also explains the unexplained hang that `default_torch_num_threads=1` works around in #50130 / #50560 and in several `tests/plugins_tests` offline runners.

## Claims

- A process launched through `get_mp_context()` in `fork` mode no longer deadlocks in its first OpenMP parallel region after the parent has used OpenMP.
- `test_bge_m3.py` followed by `test_colbert.py` in a single pytest process, which is how `automatic_shard` now groups them, passes instead of hanging until the 900 s timeout.
- `spawn` mode, non-Linux platforms, and OpenMP runtimes other than libgomp behave as before.

## Validation

All runs use one GPU (GB300, aarch64) with torch 2.13.0+cu132 and its bundled `torch/lib/libgomp.so.1`. kernrec was not enabled, so it plays no part in the hang.

| Check | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest models/language/pooling/test_bge_m3.py "models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py::TestColbertSharedEngine"` | hangs: EngineCore logs `Using V2 Model Runner` and nothing after; killed by the outer `timeout` | 36 passed in 3m35s |
| new `tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py::test_forked_child_can_use_openmp_after_parent_did` | fails after its 60 s join timeout | passes; the whole file runs in about 5 s |

<details>
<summary>py-spy of the hung EngineCore (CI-equivalent repro)</summary>

```
Thread (idle): "MainThread"
    (libgomp.so.1)
    (libgomp.so.1)
    at::TensorIteratorBase::for_each (libtorch_cpu.so)
    at::native::(anonymous namespace)::fill_kernel (libtorch_cpu.so)
    at::native::zeros_symint (libtorch_cpu.so)
    __init__ (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/buffer_utils.py:33)      # UvaBuffer: torch.zeros(..., pin_memory=True)
    __init__ (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py:37)
    __init__ (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:286)
    _init_workspace_and_model_runner (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:562)
    init_device (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:549)
    ...
    _launch (multiprocessing/popen_fork.py:71)
```

The pytest process was waiting in `wait_for_engine_startup` the whole time.
</details>

Commands:

```bash
pytest -v -s models/language/pooling/test_bge_m3.py \
  "models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py::TestColbertSharedEngine" -m 'not core_model'
pytest -v tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/utils/system_utils.py tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py
```

No model evaluation: the change does not touch model execution or outputs.

## Details

**Root cause.** GNU libgomp creates its worker threads lazily and keeps them for reuse. After `fork()` the child has only the forking thread, but libgomp still believes the old team exists, so the child's first parallel region with more than one thread waits forever on a barrier. Intel and LLVM OpenMP install `pthread_atfork` handlers for this; libgomp does not. In the CI shard, `test_bge_m3.py` does CPU `torch.einsum` / `torch.allclose` in the pytest process, which starts the pool. The colbert fixture then calls `vllm_runner`, which forks EngineCore because CUDA is not initialized in the parent. The forked child hangs in MRV2's `UvaBuffer` `torch.zeros(..., pin_memory=True)`, a large CPU fill that runs in parallel. `automatic_shard` started putting these two files in the same shard in 96139, which is why the job began failing without a related code change. Users can hit the same thing by running torch CPU work before `LLM(...)` in one process.

`set_multiprocessing_worker_envs()` already notes the constraint ("a forked child whose parent had run a parallel region deadlocks"). Until now vLLM just assumed the parent had not run a parallel region. #58946 makes the forked EngineCore load weights with multiple threads on purpose, so forcing the child down to one thread would undo that.

**Fix.** When `get_mp_context()` resolves to `fork`, it calls `omp_pause_resource_all(omp_pause_hard)` (OpenMP 5.0) on every loaded libgomp. This joins the idle workers, so the child starts with no pool and builds a fresh one. The parent rebuilds its own pool on its next parallel region, which costs one round of thread creation. libgomp keeps a pool per calling thread, and the thread that calls `get_mp_context()` is the one that later calls `proc.start()`, so this releases exactly the pool the child would inherit. Pools owned by other threads are left alone. Errors are suppressed: no `/proc` (non-Linux), a libgomp without the symbol (GCC < 9), or no libgomp loaded at all make it a no-op.

A process can have more than one libgomp loaded. In my local test process, scikit-learn's bundled `libgomp-<hash>.so` sits next to torch's `libgomp.so.1`. Pausing only the first match released scikit-learn's copy and left torch's pool in place, so the child still hung. To find every copy, the scan in `find_loaded_library()` is split out into `find_loaded_libraries()`, which uses the same filename matching. `find_loaded_library()` still returns the first match, exactly as before.

`decorate_logs()` now reads the process name from `multiprocessing.current_process()` instead of `get_mp_context().current_process()`. The result is identical, but child processes no longer go through the pause during log setup. A pause there would be a no-op for vLLM-forked children. It would deadlock, though, in a child whose own parent forked it without pausing; I confirmed that in a standalone repro.

**Limitations.** If the parent runs another parallel region between `get_mp_context()` and `proc.start()`, the pool comes back and the child can still hang. No vLLM call site does that today. Once this lands, the `default_torch_num_threads=1` workarounds in tests could be removed, but that is left out of this PR.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs and issues for `libgomp`, `omp_pause_resource`, `fork OpenMP deadlock`, `fork hang EngineCore` and `test_colbert`. Nothing addresses this. #50130 / #50560 removed or kept the thread workaround for a single test without identifying the cause.

title: [Bugfix] Apply default multimodal LoRA per batch conversation
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix default multimodal LoRA selection in `/v1/chat/completions/batch`. Select the adapter independently for each conversation instead of passing the entire batch to the single-conversation selector.

## Claims

- Apply default multimodal LoRAs to the appropriate conversations in a batch.
- Preserve explicit adapter precedence and text-only behavior.

## Validation

```bash
uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py \
```

Real HTTP validation on an H800 used `ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-2b` and its bundled LoRA, with BF16, eager mode, and `max_num_seqs=1`.

- After the fix, audio-only and mixed text/audio batches matched the single-request audio output token for token.

HTTP validation preceded the rebase; the affected files are unchanged. The checks above were rerun after rebasing.

The existing Phi-4 integration test covers single and batch endpoints with default and explicit adapters. These cases are included in CI but were not run locally.

## Details

The adapter selector expects one conversation, but the batch endpoint passed a nested list of conversations. No modalities were detected, so default adapters were silently omitted.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Normalize beam search scores by generated length
author: 4arkeinlvy
body:
## Overview

Beam search divides each beam's cumulative log-prob (a sum over the *generated* tokens) by `(prompt + generated length) ** length_penalty`. It should divide by the generated length only, as Transformers does. With any non-trivial prompt, the prompt length dominates the denominator, so `length_penalty` stops having an effect and beams that hit EOS early win, often with an empty completion. This affects `LLM.beam_search` and `use_beam_search` on `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and speech-to-text, which all share `create_sort_beams_key_function`.

Fixes #2606, which was auto-closed as stale. The earlier fix in #7007 targeted the old V0 `sequence.py` and was never merged, and the bug carried over into the current frontend implementation.

## Claims

- Beams are ranked by `cum_logprob / num_generated_tokens ** length_penalty`, counting a terminating EOS token, as in Transformers' [`_update_finished_beams`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/09a71e5b32a747dbc7805599457e67c956ef212f/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L3531): `topk_log_probs / ((cur_len + 1 - decoder_prompt_len) ** length_penalty)`. Transformers fixed the same bug in huggingface/transformers#27351.
- Beam search no longer prefers empty completions. On `tests/prompts/example.txt` without trailing newlines, the top beam on `main` is EOS-only for 8 of 8 prompts (HF: 1 of 8). With this PR it is 1 of 8.
- HF parity improves. On the exact prompts `tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py` uses, the top beam matches HF on 8/8 prompts instead of 6/8.
- `length_penalty` changes the result again for long prompts. On `main`, the same beam wins for every value from 0 to 2.
- `BeamSearchParams.length_penalty` now has a docstring describing these semantics.

## Validation

All runs used upstream `1f5514ec4`, precompiled, on an RTX 3050 4 GB (torch 2.14.0+cu130) with transformers 5.20.2.

**Regression test** (CPU, existing fake-engine harness): `pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py -k test_beam_search_score_ignores_prompt_length -v`
- `main`: 2 failed. The online path returns `[]` and the offline path returns `[eos]`, i.e. the 1-token EOS beam beats `[11, 11]`.
- This PR: 2 passed.

**Existing tests with this PR:**
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py` | 65 passed |
| `pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py -k "not multimodal"` (GPU; includes the HF-parity, concurrency and structured-output tests) | 12 passed |
| `pytest tests/test_request_input_bounds.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py -k beam` | 20 passed |
| `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -k test_batch_completions` (opt-125m server, beam search) | 1 passed |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | passed |

**HF parity** (TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, fp16, `beam_width=4`, `length_penalty=1.0`). HF uses `generate(num_beams=4, num_return_sequences=4)` as in `HfRunner.generate_beam_search`; vLLM uses `LLM.beam_search` as in `VllmRunner.generate_beam_search`. `HfRunner` drops pad tokens, and TinyLlama's pad token is its EOS, so a trailing EOS is dropped from vLLM beams before comparing.

| Prompts | max_tokens | Top beam == HF (main → PR) | Beams == HF (main → PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `example.txt` as read by the test (trailing `\n`) | 64 | 6/8 → **8/8** | 24/32 → **30/32** |
| same | 128 | 6/8 → **8/8** | 21/32 → **29/32** |
| `example.txt`, stripped | 64 | 1/8 → **7/8** | 2/32 → **22/32** |
| same | 128 | 1/8 → **5/8** | 2/32 → **11/32** |

The remaining mismatches come from two algorithmic differences this PR does not touch (see Details).

**`length_penalty` sweep.** Prompt: a 590-token chat prompt (the first 2000 characters of `tests/prompts/summary.txt` plus a question with a short answer). Settings: `beam_width=4`, `max_tokens=64`. Each cell is the generated length of the best beam.

| `length_penalty` | 0.0 | 0.5 | 1.0 | 2.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 16 | 16 | 16 | 16 |
| This PR | 16 | 22 | 64 | 64 |

**Online.** `vllm serve TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0`, then `/v1/completions` with `{"prompt": "vLLM is a high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs.", "use_beam_search": true, "n": 4, "max_tokens": 64}`.
- `main`: `choices[0]` is `""` with `finish_reason: "stop"`, `stop_reason: 2`.
- This PR: `choices[0]` is the generated continuation.

`/v1/chat/completions` with beam search returns the same complete answers on both.

## Details

**Root cause.** `get_beam_search_score` divided by `len(tokens)`. `tokens` starts as the prompt (`BeamSearchInstance` and the online path's `tokens=prompt_token_ids`), but `cum_logprob` only sums generated tokens. The helper was adapted from an old Transformers `BeamHypotheses.add` that had the same bug. huggingface/transformers#27351 (v4.36) fixed it there, noting it "would cause an unexpected bias towards generating shorter sequences".

**Why `len(x.logprobs)`.** Every path that extends or completes a beam appends exactly one logprobs entry and adds that token's log-prob to `cum_logprob`. That covers offline steps, online running beams, EOS beams and aborted beams. `tokens` can't be used, because the online path drops the EOS from `tokens` unless `include_stop_str_in_output` is set. The `max(..., 1)` guard still covers a beam aborted before generating anything.

**Behavior change.** Final rankings change only when the compared beams have different generated lengths, which is the intent. Pruning of running beams is unchanged, since every running beam has the same length at each step.

**Not changed.** Two differences from Transformers remain:
- vLLM finalizes every EOS candidate among each beam's top `2 * beam_width` logprobs; Transformers only finalizes those in the global top `num_beams`.
- vLLM has no early-stopping heuristic.

**Related.**
- #59506 adds overflow handling to the same function. It is orthogonal, but it needs a rebase onto the new `(num_generated_tokens, cumulative_logprob, length_penalty)` signature.
- The Rust-frontend beam search in #47705 ports the old formula, including unit tests that encode it. The same `logprobs.len()` change applies there.
- RFC #61880 plans to reuse `get_beam_search_score` for HF-parity scoring.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `beam search length penalty`, `length_penalty`, `get_beam_search_score`, `beam search normalization` and `beam search shorter`. The only related hits are #2606, the stale V0 PR #7007, and #59506 (overflow only). I also checked every open PR touching `vllm/entrypoints/generate/beam_search/` (#59506, #60327, #60550, #52621, #36285, #60787, #49541, #47705): none changes the normalization.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). It helped locate the bug, write the change and test, and run the validation above. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

cc @DarkLight1337

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Hold promotions after a cache reset until jobs report
author: javieratomic
body:
## Overview

`reset_cache()` in the `OffloadingConnector` scheduler releases the CPU-tier chunks of in-flight transfer jobs at once, but the workers may still write those chunks until they report the jobs. With secondary tiers, a lookup in that window can promote a secondary-tier hit into one of the released chunks, and the late worker write then overwrites it, so a later load hands the GPU wrong KV. This PR adds an `OffloadingManager.on_reset_flushed()` hook, called once the workers have reported every job flushed by the reset, and `TieringOffloadingManager` holds promotions from `reset_cache()` until then.

It is a standalone bugfix on `main` and also applies to a single node.

## Claims

- With `TieringOffloadingSpec` and at least one secondary tier, no promotion into the CPU tier starts after a cache reset until the workers have reported every job the reset flushed. This covers lookups from the scheduler and from tiers that serve peers through their `ParentManager` (`p2p`, `kvcr`). A late DMA of a flushed store, or any other worker write still pending, can no longer land on a chunk a promotion has just filled.
- Lookups keep running in that window: CPU-tier hits are served as before, and a chunk found only in a secondary tier is a miss, so the request recomputes it (or the peer is told it is absent).
- Without secondary tiers (`CPUOffloadingSpec`, or `TieringOffloadingSpec` without tiers), nothing is held (see Details for why it is not needed there). The scheduler still waits for the flushed jobs' reports before calling the hook, so after a reset with jobs in flight the engine keeps stepping until they arrive, normally on the next step.
- While the scheduler waits, the engine keeps stepping even with no request left (`has_pending_push_work()`), so the flush reaches the workers and their reports come back on an idle engine too.
- The scheduler logs when it starts and stops waiting for the reports, and warns once if that lasts more than 60 s; the check runs on every step, including the empty steps of an idle engine.

## Validation

**Regression through `LLM`** (GPU): `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py::test_tiering_cache_reset_resumes_promotions_on_idle_engine`. `facebook/opt-125m`, `TieringOffloadingSpec` with an `fs` tier, `async_scheduling=False`. The engine core and its worker run in the test process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`). A prefix is stored down to the `fs` tier; then the worker's job reports are withheld behind a `threading.Event` while another prompt's stores are issued, so `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` always finds them in flight (the test asserts that the hold started). The gate is opened, the idle engine is stepped until the hold is released, and the prefix must be promoted back from the `fs` tier (`num_cached_tokens == len(prefix)`). No retries and no log parsing.

On a DGX Spark (GB10), with `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-00b6c4c565` and this branch's changed Python files on top, this test and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_worker.py` pass (18 passed). An earlier revision without the `has_pending_push_work()` change failed with `TimeoutError: timed out after 30 s waiting for promotions to resume`.

**Scheduler-level tests** (CPU), in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`, on a real `Scheduler` whose `OffloadingConnector` runs the real `TieringOffloadingSpec` manager with an `example` secondary tier. A finished request leaves real store jobs in flight, the reset goes through `Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`, `schedule()` delivers `jobs_to_flush`, and the worker reports come back through `update_from_output()`. Only the workers are played, since the CPU job has no GPU transfers.

- `test_cache_reset_holds_promotions_until_flushed_jobs_report[True|False]`: `Scheduler.has_requests()` stays true until the flushed jobs report, the next step flushes exactly the in-flight jobs, and a secondary-tier-only key is a miss until their reports arrive and promotes after; without secondary tiers nothing is held. Without the `has_pending_push_work()` change it fails on `assert scheduler.has_requests()`.
- `test_cache_reset_fence_ignores_reports_of_other_jobs`: a late report of a job completed before the reset does not count as a flushed job's report.
- `test_cache_reset_without_in_flight_jobs_holds_nothing`: a reset with nothing in flight calls `on_reset_flushed()` at once and holds nothing.
- `test_cache_reset_fence_held_too_long_warns_on_idle_steps`: with a monkeypatched `time.monotonic` in the scheduler module, the 60 s warning fires on an empty step with no request left. It fails if the check runs only on lookups, as it did before.

- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::test_held_promotions_answer_peer_lookups_with_miss`: a real `P2PSecondaryTierManager` serves a peer under a real `TieringOffloadingManager`, next to an `example` tier that holds the key; a second P2P manager is the peer, and only the control and NIXL transports are faked (the existing loopback fakes). The peer's `LookupMsg` goes through the real `serve_external_requests()` path: after `reset_cache()` it is answered MISS and nothing is submitted to the `example` tier; after `on_reset_flushed()`, the same lookup starts the promotion. It fails if the hold is ignored. (`p2p` is the lightest in-tree serving tier; `kvcr` needs the external `kvcr` package.)
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py::test_held_promotions_keep_primary_hits`: while held, a CPU-tier chunk is still a hit; `test_reset_holds_promotions_until_flushed`: `reset_cache()` holds promotions and `on_reset_flushed()` releases them.

**Suites** (CPU-only container):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
# 1289 passed, 1 failed (on 71294c2e9a)
```

The one failure, `test_worker.py::test_register_packed_kv_caches_skips_scratch_group`, needs a GPU and fails the same way on `main`. The new `LLM` test runs in the "V1 KV Connectors" GPU step (`pytest -m 'not cpu_test' v1/kv_connector/unit`).

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files, and mypy reports no new errors in them.

There is still no reproducer of the data race itself: it needs a late worker DMA to land after a promotion's copy into the same chunk, which a test cannot force on real hardware.

## Details

**Root cause.** `reset_cache()`, reached through `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` (`POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true`, or `pause_generation(clear_cache=True)`), adds every in-flight job to `jobs_to_flush`, resets the manager, which frees their CPU-tier chunks, and drops later worker reports of those jobs through `_stale_job_threshold`. The workers submit and wait for the flushed jobs in `handle_preemptions()` of the next step they run. The scheduler builds that same step first, and its lookups run before any worker has seen the flush. On a secondary-tier hit, `TieringOffloadingManager.lookup()` reserves a free CPU-tier chunk (`_initiate_promotion()` → `primary_tier.prepare_write()`), which may be one the reset has just released, and the tier copies into it from the engine core after `on_schedule_end()`. Nothing orders that copy against the worker's DMA into the same chunk. If the DMA lands last, the chunk holds stale KV (or KV from blocks the GPU already reused) under the promoted key, and the next load hands it to the GPU. `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()` already drains the secondary tiers' own transfers for exactly this reason ("preferable to silent corruption from reusing primary slots while a transfer is mid-copy"); the workers' transfers were not covered.

The scheduler is not the only caller of `lookup()`. Tiers that serve external requests (`p2p`, `kvcr`) call it through their `ParentManager` from `serve_external_requests()`, in `on_schedule_end()` and on the tier-poll thread, and such a lookup promotes from any other secondary tier the same way.

**Why only promotions.** A promotion is the only write to a CPU-tier chunk that does not come from a worker. A worker submits the flushed stores and waits for them before it submits any job of a later step, and a load, or a secondary tier's read for a cascade or a peer, only uses a chunk whose post-reset store has completed. So a late worker write either finishes before anything that depends on the chunk or is overwritten by it. That is why lookups keep serving CPU-tier hits during the hold, and why engines without secondary tiers hold nothing.

**Fix.**

- `OffloadingManager.on_reset_flushed()` is new, a no-op by default: it is called once the workers have reported every job in flight at the last `reset_cache()`, so blocks that reset freed are no longer written by them.
- `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()` holds promotions when it has secondary tiers, and `on_reset_flushed()` releases them. While held, its `lookup()` returns `MISS` for a chunk that is not in the CPU tier, without querying the secondary tiers, whoever calls it. `MISS` rather than `RETRY`: `RETRY` would stall the request (and keep a peer's lookup pending) until the hold is released, while the chunk can simply be recomputed. The hold sits in the manager rather than the scheduler because peers' lookups reach `lookup()` without going through the scheduler.
- At reset, if any job is in flight, the scheduler records, for every flushed job, the worker reports still due (`pending_count`, so reports received before the reset count). Stale reports decrement it as they arrive, and the last one calls `on_reset_flushed()`; with nothing in flight it is called right away. The reports normally arrive within a step or two of the reset, so the cost is a short window without promotions.
- `has_pending_push_work()` also returns true while the scheduler waits for those reports. The reset clears `_jobs`, so without this an engine left with no request went idle before the flush reached the workers, and promotions (including peers' lookups) stayed held until unrelated work arrived.

**Limitations.** A worker that never reports its flushed jobs keeps promotions held; the warning makes that visible.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs (`reset_cache offloading`, `offload promotion reset`, `TieringOffloadingManager reset_cache`, `hold promotions offload`). None holds promotions across a reset. The closest are complementary:

- #59099 keeps the engine stepping until a reset's flush reaches the workers and makes `reset_cache()` re-entrant. This PR keeps the engine stepping only until the flushed jobs report; #59099 also covers engines without secondary tiers. A second reset before they report adds its own flushed jobs to the wait.
- #61667 quarantines `p2p` consumer slots whose remote write is unconfirmed. It covers a secondary tier's own late write, not a worker's.

**Related.** The multi-node CPU-region mirror proposed in #54415 (#62933) adds a second late writer, a remote node's pending slot push, and relies on this hook to cover it.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][gRPC] Drain in-flight RPCs and engine work within --shutdown-timeout
author: mrn3088
body:
## Overview `vllm serve --grpc` ignores `--shutdown-timeout`. On SIGTERM it cancels in-flight RPCs after a hardcoded 5 s (`server.stop(grace=5.0)`). It then calls `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` without a timeout, so EngineCore gets the default 5 s join before SIGKILL. This PR spends the `--shutdown-timeout` budget instead: in-flight requests finish, then EngineCore drains work that outlives an RPC, such as NIXL prefill blocks that the decode side has not read yet, until the same deadline plus a 5 s teardown floor. Related: #61562 (drain order for the multi-API-server HTTP path), #41383 (NIXL KV cache lease), #55102 (previous fix to this launcher). ## Claims With `--shutdown-timeout N > 0`: - SIGTERM makes the gRPC server refuse new RPCs at once (`UNAVAILABLE`). In-flight RPCs run to completion for up to N s, and never less than the 5 s they get with the default `0`, so setting a timeout is never less graceful than not setting one. Today they are cancelled after 5 s with `UNAVAILABLE: Cancelling all calls`. - EngineCore keeps serving until no RPC that could still send it a request is in flight and AsyncLLM has no request left. RPCs are counted from the moment the server dispatches them, so a request that reached the server before SIGTERM is served even if it is still arriving, being preprocessed or queued in EngineCore. EngineCore then drains what outlives an RPC until N s plus a 5 s teardown floor. A prefill instance in a NIXL P/D deployment keeps the blocks it has handed off until the decode instance reads them. Today it is SIGKILLed about 5 s after SIGTERM, and the decode request fails under the default `kv_load_failure_policy="fail"`. - RPCs still running at the deadline (`max(N, 5 s)`) are cancelled, and their requests are aborted while EngineCore is still running. - An RPC that carries no request, such as a router's `SubscribeKvEvents` stream, does not hold shutdown: it is cancelled 5 s after EngineCore stops. - A second SIGTERM or SIGINT cancels all RPCs at once. - The process exits within `max(N, 5 s) + 5 s`, plus the time to kill what is left. - `--shutdown-timeout 0` (the default) keeps the current behavior. `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` now runs off the event loop there too. ## Validation **Setup** - Image: upstream nightly `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8e2beaa3bff595577a069d49d96bde9074294ec2` (vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev197+g8e2beaa3b`). Its `grpc_server.py` is byte-identical to this PR's base. - Extras: `smg-grpc-servicer==0.14.0` for the `grpc` extra. - Model and hardware: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, with prefill and decode on two B300 GPUs of one node. - KV transfer: `NixlConnector` (`kv_role=kv_both`). - Flags: `--enforce-eager --shutdown-timeout 60` unless a row says otherwise. - Columns: `main` is the image as is. "First revision" is this PR as first pushed (RPCs drain first, then EngineCore gets what is left of the budget). "Overlapped" is the variant suggested in review: EngineCore is signalled at SIGTERM, concurrently with the RPC drain. "This PR" is the current head. Each column mounts its `grpc_server.py` over the image's copy and starts fresh servers for each row. - The `SubscribeKvEvents` row starts both servers with `--kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events":true,"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://*:"}'`. The in-flight row starts the prefill server with `--max-num-batched-tokens 131072`. The preprocessing row runs a single `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` server (no KV transfer) with `SMG_VLLM_MM_PROCESSOR=inprocess`; the client serves the request's image from a local HTTP server that answers after 1.5 s. | Scenario | `main` | First revision | Overlapped | This PR | |---|---|---|---|---| | Control: prefill → decode handoff, no SIGTERM | 32/32 tokens, `length` | 32/32 | 32/32 | 32/32 | | NIXL handoff: SIGTERM prefill once its RPC returns, send the decode leg 8 s later | decode `finish_reason=error`, 0/32; prefill exits +6.9 s | 32/32; prefill exits +12.3 s | 32/32; +13.6 s | **32/32; prefill exits +11.9 s, after the read** | | 4000-token stream on the decode server, SIGTERM after the first tokens | cut at +5.0 s with `UNAVAILABLE: Cancelling all calls`, 419/4000; server exits +11.9 s | 4000/4000; +51.2 s | 4000/4000; +54.7 s | **4000/4000 (stream ends +48.0 s); server exits +52.0 s** | | A `SubscribeKvEvents` stream open on the SIGTERMed server, in the handoff case and in a 1000-token stream | | streams held to +60.0 s, then EngineCore SIGKILLed with 0 s left (`MPClient: start timeout=0.0s`); prefill exits +62.4 s, decode +62.3 s | subscription cancelled at +17.0 s / +21.5 s; prefill exits +18.3 s, decode +22.9 s | **subscription cancelled at +15.9 s / +20.9 s, 5 s after EngineCore stopped; prefill exits +17.1 s, decode +22.0 s** | | Prefills in flight at SIGTERM: 17 prompts of 7680 tokens fill one 131072-token step, 15 more follow 0.1 s later, SIGTERM at 0.15 s, decode legs 3 s after the prefills return | | 32/32 decoded | **15 prefills return `finish_reason=abort`, 17/32 decoded** | **32/32 decoded** | | Stream longer than the budget: `--shutdown-timeout 20`, 7000-token stream | | cancelled at +20.0 s, then EngineCore SIGKILLed with 0 s left; exits +22.2 s | cancelled at +20.0 s; EngineCore tears down; exits +24.6 s | **cancelled at +20.0 s; EngineCore gets the 5 s floor and tears down within it; exits +24.8 s** | | Second SIGTERM: on prefill 2 s after the first (decode leg at +8 s); on decode 5 s into a 7000-token stream | | | decode leg 32/32, prefill exits +12.4 s; stream cancelled at +5.0 s, exits +10.3 s | **decode leg 32/32, prefill exits +12.0 s; stream cancelled at +5.0 s, exits +8.8 s** | | `--shutdown-timeout 0` | ignored: same as the rows above | handoff `error`, prefill exits +6.9 s; stream cut at +5.0 s (426/4000), exits +8.7 s | handoff `error`, +7.2 s; stream cut at +5.0 s (396/4000), exits +10.3 s | **handoff `error`, prefill exits +7.0 s; stream cut at +5.0 s (428/4000), exits +10.2 s** | | `--shutdown-timeout 2`, below the 5 s default grace: NIXL handoff as above, 4000-token stream | | | | **decode leg 32/32, prefill exits +11.7 s; stream cut at +5.0 s (413/4000), as with `0`; exits +8.8 s** | | A request still being preprocessed at SIGTERM: its image fetch takes 1.5 s, and it was sent 50 ms before SIGTERM | | | | **32/32, done +2.1 s after SIGTERM; EngineCore is signalled once it finishes (`MPClient: start timeout=62.9s`); server exits +6.9 s** | | New RPC 0.5 s after SIGTERM | `UNAVAILABLE` | `UNAVAILABLE` | `UNAVAILABLE` | `UNAVAILABLE` | Each case ran once per column. The "This PR" column is the current head, e21408569e. With `--shutdown-timeout 2`, 8ba921b0b3 gave in-flight RPCs exactly 2 s, so the stream was cut at +2.0 s (170/4000). Its decode leg also failed: EngineCore's deadline was about 7 s, and the read came at +8 s. With a request still being preprocessed at SIGTERM, cbe28ee5e9 started EngineCore's shutdown 0.1 s after SIGTERM. `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` closes the renderer's executor first, so the request failed while its image was being processed: `INVALID_ARGUMENT: multimodal placeholder validation failed: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown`. **Why the overlapped variant aborts in-flight prefills.** When SIGTERM arrived, its prefill server logged `EngineCore: draining in-flight requests count=16`: the second wave had reached the server before SIGTERM but was still in EngineCore's input queue behind the first step. EngineCore rejects every request it reads once its shutdown has started (`_reject_add_in_shutdown`), so those 15 came back as aborts. With this PR the prefill server logged `MPClient: start timeout=64.6s`: EngineCore was signalled 0.4 s after SIGTERM, once all 32 prefills were done. **Unit test.** `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_grpc_shutdown.py` runs `_drain_and_stop` against a real `grpc.aio` server and a fake `AsyncLLM` whose `shutdown(timeout)` blocks like EngineCore's drain mode and rejects requests it reads after shutdown has started. Like `test_grpc_health.py`, it is skipped when the `grpc` extra is not installed. In the image above with `smg-grpc-servicer==0.14.0`: `8 passed`, including `test_inflight_count_follows_rpcs`, which checks that the count follows completed and cancelled RPCs and leaves subscriptions out. Against the overlapped variant, `test_requests_queued_at_sigterm_are_served` fails. Without the interceptor, `test_request_in_preprocessing_at_sigterm_is_served` fails; its fake only registers the request after a preprocessing delay. **Commands** ```bash pip install "vllm[grpc]" # smg-grpc-servicer + smg-grpc-proto CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5600 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --grpc --port 18000 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192 --shutdown-timeout 60 \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' & P=$! CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5605 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --grpc --port 18050 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192 --shutdown-timeout 60 \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' & D=$! python grpc_shutdown_repro.py pd --prefill localhost:18000 --decode localhost:18050 python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff --prefill localhost:18000 --prefill-pid $P \ --decode localhost:18050 --delay 8 python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream --addr localhost:18050 --pid $D --max-tokens 4000 ``` The other rows add, on fresh servers: ```bash # SubscribeKvEvents open (both servers also get --kv-events-config, endpoints on distinct ports) python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff ... --hold kv-events python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream ... --max-tokens 1000 --hold kv-events # prefills in flight (prefill server also gets --max-num-batched-tokens 131072) python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff ... --concurrency 32 --prompt-len 7680 \ --wave2 15 --wave-gap 0.1 --sigterm-during-prefill --sigterm-delay 0.15 --delay 3 # stream longer than the budget (both servers with --shutdown-timeout 20) python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream ... --max-tokens 7000 # second SIGTERM python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff ... --second-sigterm 2 python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream ... --max-tokens 7000 --second-sigterm 5 # request still being preprocessed: one server, no KV transfer SMG_VLLM_MM_PROCESSOR=inprocess vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct --grpc --port 18000 \ --enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192 --shutdown-timeout 60 & VL=$! python grpc_shutdown_repro.py mm --addr localhost:18000 --pid $VL \ --model-dir --media-delay 1.5 --sigterm-after 0.05 ``` On our cluster both servers were pinned to one NIC (`UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_0:1 UCX_TLS=rc_x,rc,dc_x,dc,cuda_copy`). Otherwise UCX picks the NIC nearest each GPU, and the two land on rails that do not reach each other. This is a property of the cluster, not of this change, and the control row shows the handoff path works.
grpc_shutdown_repro.py ```python """Reproducer for `vllm serve --grpc` ignoring --shutdown-timeout. Needs `pip install "vllm[grpc]"` (grpcio + smg-grpc-proto). Start the servers yourself (commands in the PR description), then: # 1) in-flight stream on SIGTERM python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream --addr localhost:50051 --pid # 2) control: plain prefill -> decode handoff, no SIGTERM (must succeed first) python grpc_shutdown_repro.py pd --prefill localhost:50051 --decode localhost:50052 # 3) NIXL handoff: SIGTERM the prefill after its RPC returns, read on decode python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff --prefill localhost:50051 \ --prefill-pid --decode localhost:50052 --delay 8 # 4) slow preprocessing at SIGTERM: a Qwen3-VL server (SMG_VLLM_MM_PROCESSOR=inprocess) # fetches the request's image from a local server that answers after # --media-delay s; SIGTERM lands --sigterm-after s after the request is sent python grpc_shutdown_repro.py mm --addr localhost:50051 --pid \ --model-dir --media-delay 1.5 --sigterm-after 0.05 Options for stream and handoff: --hold [KIND] keep an RPC open on the SIGTERMed server that only ends when the client or server ends it: a router's SubscribeKvEvents stream (kv-events, needs the server's --kv-events-config), or a reflection stream (reflection, the default, works on any server) --second-sigterm S send another SIGTERM S seconds after the first handoff only: --concurrency K --sigterm-during-prefill [--sigterm-delay S] K prefills with distinct prompts, SIGTERM S seconds (default 0.3) after sending them, while they run --wave2 W --wave-gap G send the last W of them G seconds after the others, so they reach a server that is busy with the first ones Prompt token ids are synthetic; any model with a vocabulary > 30000 works. The stream must outlive the old 5 s grace by a wide margin, so pick --max-tokens for the model's single-stream speed (e.g. 4000 with --enforce-eager). """ import argparse import json import os import random import signal import threading import time import uuid from collections import Counter from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer from io import BytesIO from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit import grpc import psutil from grpc_reflection.v1alpha import reflection_pb2, reflection_pb2_grpc from smg_grpc_proto import vllm_engine_pb2 as pb from smg_grpc_proto import vllm_engine_pb2_grpc as pb_grpc from smg_grpc_proto.generated import common_pb2 def make_request(input_ids, max_tokens, stream, kv=None): kwargs = {} if kv is not None: kwargs["kv_transfer_params_json"] = json.dumps(kv) return pb.GenerateRequest( request_id=str(uuid.uuid4()), tokenized=pb.TokenizedInput(input_ids=input_ids), sampling_params=pb.SamplingParams( max_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0.0, ignore_eos=True ), stream=stream, **kwargs, ) def prompt(args, i): if args.concurrency == 1: return list(range(1000, 1000 + args.prompt_len)) # Distinct prompts so the prefills miss every prefix cache. rng = random.Random(i) return [rng.randrange(1000, 30000) for _ in range(args.prompt_len)] class ExitWatcher: """Records when pid exits, polling from the moment SIGTERM is sent.""" def __init__(self, pid, second_after=None): self.pid = pid self.exited = None os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM) self.sigterm = time.monotonic() self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._poll, daemon=True) self.thread.start() if second_after is not None: timer = threading.Timer(second_after, self._second) timer.daemon = True timer.start() def _second(self): if self.exited is None: os.kill(self.pid, signal.SIGTERM) print(f"second SIGTERM at {self.since()}", flush=True) def _poll(self): while True: try: if psutil.Process(self.pid).status() == psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE: break except psutil.NoSuchProcess: break time.sleep(0.05) self.exited = time.monotonic() def since(self, t=None): return f"+{(time.monotonic() if t is None else t) - self.sigterm:.1f}s" def report(self, timeout): self.thread.join(timeout) if self.exited is None: return "still running" return f"{self.since(self.exited)} after SIGTERM" class Hold: """An RPC that stays open until the client or the server ends it.""" def __init__(self, addr, kind): self.release = threading.Event() self.ended = None self.result = None channel = grpc.insecure_channel(addr) if kind == "kv-events": stub = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(channel) self.responses = stub.SubscribeKvEvents(common_pb2.SubscribeKvEventsRequest()) self.responses.initial_metadata() # the stream is up else: # The client never half-closes the request stream. def requests(): yield reflection_pb2.ServerReflectionRequest(list_services="") self.release.wait() stub = reflection_pb2_grpc.ServerReflectionStub(channel) self.responses = stub.ServerReflectionInfo(requests()) next(self.responses) # the stream is up self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._drain, daemon=True) self.thread.start() def _drain(self): try: for _ in self.responses: pass self.result = "OK" except grpc.RpcError as e: self.result = f"{e.code().name}: {e.details()}" self.ended = time.monotonic() def report(self, watcher, timeout): self.thread.join(timeout) self.release.set() if self.ended is None: return "still open" return f"{self.result}, ended {watcher.since(self.ended)} after SIGTERM" def run_stream(args): hold = Hold(args.addr, args.hold) if args.hold else None stub = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.addr)) ids = prompt(args, 0) tokens, finish, error, watcher = 0, None, None, None try: for resp in stub.Generate(make_request(ids, args.max_tokens, stream=True)): if resp.HasField("chunk"): tokens += len(resp.chunk.token_ids) else: finish = resp.complete.finish_reason if watcher is None and tokens > 0: watcher = ExitWatcher(args.pid, args.second_sigterm) time.sleep(0.5) try: late = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.addr)) next(iter(late.Generate(make_request(ids, 1, stream=False)))) print("late RPC: accepted (unexpected)") except grpc.RpcError as e: print(f"late RPC: {e.code().name}") except grpc.RpcError as e: error = f"{e.code().name}: {e.details()}" t_end = time.monotonic() if watcher is None: raise SystemExit(f"stream produced no tokens: finish={finish} error={error}") print( f"stream: tokens={tokens}/{args.max_tokens} finish={finish} error={error} " f"ended={watcher.since(t_end)} after SIGTERM" ) if hold is not None: print(f"held RPC: {hold.report(watcher, args.exit_timeout)}") print(f"server exit: {watcher.report(args.exit_timeout)}") def generate(stub, req, timeout=None): """One non-streaming Generate: (complete, error).""" try: complete = None for resp in stub.Generate(req, timeout=timeout): complete = resp.complete return complete, None except grpc.RpcError as e: return None, f"{e.code().name}: {e.details()}" def prefill_then_decode(args, sigterm_pid=None): prefill = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.prefill)) decode = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.decode)) prompts = [prompt(args, i) for i in range(args.concurrency)] hold = Hold(args.prefill, args.hold) if sigterm_pid and args.hold else None pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(args.concurrency) watcher = None first = len(prompts) - getattr(args, "wave2", 0) futures = [] t_send = time.monotonic() for i, ids in enumerate(prompts): if i == first and i: time.sleep(args.wave_gap) futures.append(pool.submit( generate, prefill, make_request(ids, 1, stream=False, kv={"do_remote_decode": True}))) if sigterm_pid and args.sigterm_during_prefill: time.sleep(max(t_send + args.sigterm_delay - time.monotonic(), 0)) watcher = ExitWatcher(sigterm_pid, args.second_sigterm) prefills = [f.result() for f in futures] t_prefilled = time.monotonic() errors = [e for _, e in prefills if e] reasons = Counter(c.finish_reason for c, _ in prefills if c) handed_off = sum(1 for c, _ in prefills if c and c.kv_transfer_params_json) print(f"prefill done: {handed_off}/{len(prefills)} handed off " f"finish={dict(sorted(reasons.items()))} errors={errors[:3]}") if watcher is not None: print(f"prefill RPCs returned {watcher.since(t_prefilled)} after SIGTERM") elif sigterm_pid: watcher = ExitWatcher(sigterm_pid, args.second_sigterm) time.sleep(args.delay) jobs = [] for ids, (complete, _) in zip(prompts, prefills): if complete is not None and complete.kv_transfer_params_json: params = json.loads(complete.kv_transfer_params_json) req = make_request(ids, args.max_tokens, stream=False, kv=params) jobs.append(pool.submit(generate, decode, req, args.exit_timeout)) decodes = [j.result() for j in jobs] ok = [c for c, _ in decodes if c and c.finish_reason == "length" and len(c.output_ids) == args.max_tokens] finishes = sorted({f"{c.finish_reason}:{len(c.output_ids)}" for c, _ in decodes if c}) errors = [e for _, e in decodes if e] print(f"decode: {len(ok)}/{len(prompts)} ok (finish:tokens {finishes}, " f"max_tokens={args.max_tokens}) errors={errors[:3]}") if hold is not None: print(f"held RPC: {hold.report(watcher, args.exit_timeout)}") if watcher is not None: print(f"prefill exit: {watcher.report(args.exit_timeout)}") def run_handoff(args): prefill_then_decode(args, sigterm_pid=args.prefill_pid) class SlowMedia: """Serves one random PNG over HTTP, each answer after ?delay= seconds.""" def __init__(self, size): from PIL import Image buf = BytesIO() Image.frombytes("RGB", (size, size), os.urandom(size * size * 3)).save(buf, "PNG") png = buf.getvalue() class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): time.sleep(float(parse_qs(urlsplit(self.path).query)["delay"][0])) self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "image/png") self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(png))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(png) def log_message(self, *args): pass self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler) threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start() def url(self, delay): port = self.server.server_port return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/image.png?delay={delay}&n={uuid.uuid4().hex}" def run_mm(args): from transformers import AutoTokenizer text = ( "<|im_start|>user\n<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" "Describe this image.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n" ) ids = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_dir).encode(text, add_special_tokens=False) media = SlowMedia(args.image_size) stub = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.addr)) def request(delay): return pb.GenerateRequest( request_id=str(uuid.uuid4()), tokenized=pb.TokenizedInput(input_ids=ids, original_text=text), media_refs=pb.MediaRefs(items=[pb.MediaRef( modality=common_pb2.Modality.Value("IMAGE"), url=media.url(delay))]), sampling_params=pb.SamplingParams( max_tokens=args.max_tokens, temperature=0.0, ignore_eos=True), stream=False, ) def outcome(complete, error): if complete is None: return f"finish=None error={error}" return (f"finish={complete.finish_reason} " f"tokens={len(complete.output_ids)}/{args.max_tokens}") print(f"control (no media delay): {outcome(*generate(stub, request(0), 300))}", flush=True) t_send = time.monotonic() future = ThreadPoolExecutor(1).submit(generate, stub, request(args.media_delay), args.exit_timeout) time.sleep(max(t_send + args.sigterm_after - time.monotonic(), 0)) watcher = ExitWatcher(args.pid) result = future.result() print(f"mm request (media fetch {args.media_delay}s, SIGTERM {args.sigterm_after}s after " f"sending): {outcome(*result)}, ended {watcher.since()} after SIGTERM") print(f"server exit: {watcher.report(args.exit_timeout)}") def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="mode", required=True) stream = sub.add_parser("stream") stream.add_argument("--addr", required=True) stream.add_argument("--pid", type=int, required=True) stream.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=4000) handoff = sub.add_parser("handoff") handoff.add_argument("--prefill", required=True) handoff.add_argument("--prefill-pid", type=int, required=True) handoff.add_argument("--decode", required=True) handoff.add_argument("--delay", type=float, default=8.0) handoff.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) handoff.add_argument("--sigterm-during-prefill", action="store_true") handoff.add_argument("--sigterm-delay", type=float, default=0.3) handoff.add_argument("--wave2", type=int, default=0) handoff.add_argument("--wave-gap", type=float, default=0.0) mm = sub.add_parser("mm") mm.add_argument("--addr", required=True) mm.add_argument("--pid", type=int, required=True) mm.add_argument("--model-dir", required=True) mm.add_argument("--media-delay", type=float, default=1.5) mm.add_argument("--sigterm-after", type=float, default=0.05) mm.add_argument("--image-size", type=int, default=1024) mm.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) mm.add_argument("--exit-timeout", type=float, default=120.0) # Control: the same prefill -> decode handoff with no SIGTERM. pd = sub.add_parser("pd") pd.add_argument("--prefill", required=True) pd.add_argument("--decode", required=True) pd.add_argument("--delay", type=float, default=0.0) pd.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) for p in (handoff, pd): p.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=1) for p in (stream, handoff): p.add_argument("--hold", nargs="?", const="reflection", default=None, choices=("reflection", "kv-events")) p.add_argument("--second-sigterm", type=float, default=None) for p in (stream, handoff, pd): p.add_argument("--prompt-len", type=int, default=512) p.add_argument("--exit-timeout", type=float, default=120.0) args = parser.parse_args() if args.mode == "stream": args.concurrency = 1 run_stream(args) elif args.mode == "handoff": run_handoff(args) elif args.mode == "mm": run_mm(args) else: prefill_then_decode(args) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
`pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/launchers/grpc_server.py tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_grpc_shutdown.py` passes: ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy (3.11) and the repository's local checks. No model evaluation is needed. The change only affects process shutdown, not sampling, scheduling or outputs. ## Details **Root cause (P/D flow, NIXL pull mode)** 1. The router sends the prefill leg to P with `kv_transfer_params={"do_remote_decode": true}`. 2. P runs prefill. `request_finished` delays the block free and grants a lease (`kv_lease_duration`, 30 s by default). The Generate RPC returns the handoff params: block ids and the side-channel host and port. 3. The router sends the decode leg to D. D starts heartbeating P as soon as the request enters its scheduler, which extends the lease while the request waits. 4. SIGTERM reaches P. `server.stop(grace=5.0)` returns at once, because the prefill RPC has already finished. `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` then runs without a timeout, so `CoreEngineProcManager.shutdown(None)` calls `shutdown(procs, None)`, which sends SIGTERM, joins for 5 s, and then sends SIGKILL. EngineCore's drain mode (`_handle_shutdown`) would keep stepping while `Scheduler.has_finished_requests()` still counts requests waiting on delayed connector frees, but EngineCore is killed before D reads. 5. D schedules the request, and its NIXL handshake or read fails. With `kv_load_failure_policy="fail"` the request finishes with an error. With `"recompute"`, D recomputes the prompt. The more decode requests that are queued and heartbeating against blocks held by one prefill, the more requests a single prefill restart fails. Plain streams are also cut: any RPC still running 5 s after SIGTERM is cancelled. **Fix** With `shutdown_timeout > 0`, one deadline covers both: 1. `server.stop(grace=max(N, 5 s))` refuses new RPCs at once and resolves when no RPC is live; grpc.aio resolves `stop()` once no live RPC remains. RPCs still running at the deadline are cancelled, which aborts their requests. The 5 s minimum is the grace RPCs already get with `0`. 2. EngineCore keeps running normally while anything could still send it a request. An `_InflightRpcs` server interceptor counts the in-flight `VllmEngine` RPCs, excluding subscriptions (`SubscribeKvEvents`): an RPC counts from the moment the server dispatches it, before its request message is received, until the task that grpc.aio serves it in finishes, whether or not its handler ran. `AsyncLLM.get_num_unfinished_requests()` covers requests that outlive their RPC. Both are checked every 0.1 s, and idle has to hold on two checks in a row, which covers an RPC that gRPC accepted before SIGTERM but has not yet handed to its task. The interceptor costs about 10 µs of server CPU per RPC and nothing m

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Reserve in-flight imports' host pages at admission
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #62217. Alternative to #62230.

HiSparse admits an async KV load only if its prompt fits in free host pages, but it ignores pages that earlier admitted loads still need. Two waiting loads can each hold pages the other needs. Waiting requests are never preempted, so the scheduler stalls forever with `running == []`.

Fix: reserve host pages for admitted loads, as `reserved_blocks` does for the GPU pool. The change is confined to `HiSparseSourceManager` and `HiSparseCoordinator`; the scheduler loop is unchanged.

- At admission of a load, `HiSparseSourceManager` sizes its host pages (prompt + spec decode step) and admits it only if they fit beside the pages other loads still need.
- The coordinator keeps a running total of outstanding pages (O(1) check), reduced as each load allocates its pages and dropped when the request is freed.
- Local admissions are not gated (they can be preempted), matching the GPU pool.

Alternatives: #62230 skips past held waiting requests in the scheduler loop. It changes the core loop, can starve the head of the queue, and still deadlocks when no admitted load fits.

Trade-off: a load whose host pages don't fit beside those reserved for in-flight loads waits for them, instead of being admitted and risking the deadlock.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Repro: both cases fail on main ({'first', 'second'} == {'first'}), pass here
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running

pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py   # 1x H100
```

New/extended tests in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`:
- `test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running`: the issue's scenario, plus an MTP case where the first load to resume has no host page for its draft tokens.
- `test_hisparse_async_admission_fits_beside_inflight_import`: boundary case, a load that exactly fits is admitted.
- `test_hisparse_import_reservation_released`: released on free and on resume.
- `test_hisparse_import_reservation_does_not_gate_local_admissions`.

## Test Result

- Unit (CPU): all pass. 3 unrelated failures (`test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, `test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter[FULL|NONE]`) fail identically on `main` locally.
- E2E (1x H100, `f96ae2830d`): `test_hisparse.py` 5 passed (`standalone-fa4` skips on SM90). New path exercised: in the `offload` case (HiSparse + OffloadingConnector), a coordinator probe logged the load sized at 5 pages, a 2-page reservation, and its release to 0 on resume.

## Performance

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 P/D on 8x B200: TP4 NIXL prefiller + TP4 HiSparse decoder (`MultiConnector[HiSparse, Nixl]`, `host_pool_gib=8`), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` on both servers.

```bash
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 512 \
  --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

Fresh decoder per run, interleaved. NIXL over TCP (no IB on that node), so the run is transfer-bound with the host pool ~96% full.

| Decoder | Output tok/s (2 runs) | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR (`c02494d57c`) | 191.52, 184.44 | 68.9 s, 72.3 s | 17.00, 16.82 ms |
| `main` (`cc1a6d3135`) | 182.61, 185.10 | 73.2 s, 73.0 s | 17.26, 16.33 ms |

No regression; at most 11 of 2,949 host pages were reserved. Without MTP, a P/D load allocates all its host pages at admission and nothing is reserved, so admission matches `main` exactly (verified on an earlier revision over IB: 580–581 tok/s in both arms).

title: [Bugfix] Support online quantization of Kimi K3 NVIDIA projections
author: wzhao18
body:
## Purpose

Fix online quantization of the Kimi K3 NVIDIA projections, e.g.

```
--quantization-config '{"targets":{"*.in_proj_qkvgfab":"mxfp8","*.fused_qkv_a_g_proj":"mxfp8","*.routed_expert_down_proj":"mxfp8","*.routed_expert_up_proj":"mxfp8"}}'
```

Three places in the model broke:

- **KDA input projection padding.** `in_proj_qkvgfab` pads each TP-local row block for alignment. No checkpoint shard covers that padding, but online processing counted it toward the layer's expected load size, so the layer never reached completion and every KDA layer was deferred to `finalize_layerwise_processing`, keeping all its buffered checkpoint tensors alive until the end of loading. The projection now declares `weight_loader_numel` without the padding. Online processing also rebuilds the weight from uninitialized storage, so the padding is re-zeroed after each shard load (both `weight_loader` and `weight_loader_v2`).
- **Routed output transform.** `KimiRoutedOutputTransform` fused the residual add as `residual.addmm_(x, up_proj.weight.t())`, bypassing the quantized linear method and its scales. The fused add is now used only for an unquantized up-projection; otherwise the layer is called and the residual added in place.
- **Latent MoE tail kernels.** They multiply by the raw `up_proj.weight`, so `LatentMoERunner` now enables the fused tail path (and deferred MoE finalize) only for an unquantized up-projection.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k nvidia_kda_online_loading
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py -k deferred_finalize
```

The new KDA test (adapted from the reproducer in #61950) loads the merged projection through online processing for 96 heads (padded) and 128 heads (no padding), TP ranks 0 and 3, and both weight loaders (in forward and reverse shard order). It checks that the layer finishes loading, every source tensor is released, the loaded rows match the checkpoint, and the padding is zero (uninitialized storage is filled with NaN to catch it).

End to end: Kimi K3 MXFP4 on GB300, 2P1D (TP8 prefill x 2, DEP16 decode, 32 GPUs), DSpark K4, AgentX agentic traces at concurrency 240 for 3600 s, with and without online MXFP8 quantization of the KDA/MLA input projections, routed expert projections, and (decode only) `o_proj` and the shared experts.

## Test Result

Performance (p90; the perf runs use synthetic acceptance with AL 3.36):

| | Base | Online quant | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | 19,991 | 24,769 | +23.9 % |
| Interactivity (tok/s/user) | 40.0 | 40.5 | +1.2 % |
| E2E latency (s) | 78.2 | 59.8 | -23.4 % |
| TTFT (s) | 21.8 | 12.2 | -43.9 % |
| E2E-normalized interactivity | 6.9 | 12.5 | +79.8 % |

Accuracy (gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, real rejection sampling, 1P1D TP8 + DEP16):

| | Base | Online quant |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match | 0.9606 | 0.9674 |
