title: [Bugfix][Quantization][Spec Decode] Load ModelOpt mixed-precision DFlash and DSpark drafts
author: sragrawal
body:
## Overview

Fix loading of nested ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` checkpoints, quantization
settings for DFlash/DSpark drafts, and per-tensor FP8 normalization on FNUZ GPUs.
This incorporates the parser fix from the
earlier closed, unmerged [PR #36312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36312)
and adds draft-layer name mapping, regression tests, CI coverage and documentation.

## Claims

- Nested `MIXED_PRECISION` metadata selects the existing `modelopt_mixed` backend.
- ModelOpt draft settings match the weight aliases, runtime module prefix and
  decoder layer offset before quantized layers are constructed.
- Per-tensor FP8 weights and static input scales are normalized for FNUZ GPUs
  such as AMD MI300, using the existing conversion helper.
- Other quantization backends retain their existing quantization-config handling.
  No FP8 kernel changes are needed.

## Validation

The current source passes 24 focused CPU checks and changed-file pre-commit,
including mypy and CI selection. CPU checks used Torch 2.13.0+cpu and
Transformers 5.17.0; current main pins Torch 2.14.0.

AMD CI exposed an existing per-tensor FP8 loader omission: both checkpoint
regressions failed during engine initialization at `input.dtype == weight.dtype`
in [MI300 quantization CI](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96958#01a16a9a-8a0e-4f38-8027-3356b1307ef8).
The loader retained FN weights while the activation quantizer selected FNUZ.
The fix applies the existing FN-to-FNUZ normalization before requantization,
including both weight and static input scales. The existing regressions now
require the exact platform dtype and input scale. Fresh AMD validation is
pending CI. A CPU check confirmed the conversion preserves dequantized weights, including
negative zero, while doubling both scales.

GPU validation below used vLLM 0.32.0 with the source fixes backported. The
checkpoint-loading regressions are retained, with shared fixture setup and
the existing speculative-metric reader. GPU tests were not rerun for this
cleanup; the full current-main environment and full suites remain untested.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native/legacy mixed config, uppercase/lowercase | Four mixed-config failures; NVFP4 control passes | All five cases pass |
| Draft mapping, aliases, offsets and Quark preservation | Missing runtime-name mapping | 17 CPU cases pass against real quantization configurations |
| Small mixed Llama checkpoint through `LLM` | Config conversion fails | Loads actual FP8/BF16 layers; nested/flat metadata produce identical completions |
| Small mixed DSpark checkpoint through `LLM` | Missing `fc.weight_scale` parameter | Mixed FP8 `fc`, Markov and offset decoder projections; positive proposals and exact OFF/ON token equality |

Observed errors before the respective fixes:

```text
Value error, Unknown ModelOpt quant algo: MIXED_PRECISION

ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'fc.weight_scale' in Qwen3DSparkModel. The available parameters belonging to fc (ReplicatedLinear) are: {'fc.weight'}
```

The small GPU regressions create random checkpoints and integer token prompts
locally. Exact comparisons use batch invariance. CI dependencies and the
rendered ModelOpt documentation are updated. Changed-file pre-commit checks
pass, including mypy and CI test selection.

Additional GPT-OSS-20B mixed-FP8 DSpark smoke on B200, TP=1, fixed K=2:

- All 1,120 output tokens across 35 prompts match SpecDec OFF.
- 2,140 tokens were proposed and 16 accepted with normal verification.
- Runtime inspection confirms per-channel weight and per-token activation FP8
  for `fc`, and per-tensor FP8 for the Markov output projection.
- Export files are unchanged.

The GPT-OSS draft was trained for eight optimizer updates and quantized with
synthetic calibration inputs. These are functional smoke results, not a held-out
quality evaluation or a speedup measurement. Other hardware, tensor-parallel
sizes and quantization formats were not tested.

<details>
<summary>Regression commands</summary>

Repository test entrypoints:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k modelopt -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_modelopt_mixed_nvfp4.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'draft_quant_config or draft_weight_aliases' -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'nested_mixed_checkpoint or mixed_dspark_checkpoint' -v
```

Earlier GPU execution used the vLLM 0.32 compatibility setup described above.
The regression bodies at that point ran with the real stock test fixture:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider \
  -v -s test_gpu_regression.py
```

Each GPU regression passes after its fix and fails before it with the error
shown above. Current-main GPU execution remains pending.

</details>

## Details

There are two failures. Config conversion rejects nested `MIXED_PRECISION`
metadata before the existing backend can load it. After that is fixed, the
draft loader looks up per-layer settings using runtime names such as `model.fc`,
while the checkpoint names the layer `fc`. It builds an unquantized projection
and then fails to load `fc.weight_scale`.

The shared `map_draft_quant_config` helper in `models/utils.py` maps ModelOpt's
draft settings through the existing weight aliases, module prefix and decoder
layer offset before constructing the layers. Apply this
only to ModelOpt: other backends can use semantic configuration keys or suffix
rules that must not receive a module prefix.

Related work has different scope: [#49900](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49900)
handles `draft_model.` prefixes in another proposer path;
[#53122](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53122) configures draft
quantization aliases and context-KV projection, without this runtime-root and
teacher-layer remapping. No equivalent open PR was found.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Gather Engram hashes across DP replicas in the AMD model
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
The AMD DeepSeek V4.1 model never got the data-parallel Engram wiring that #56512 and #57651 added to the NVIDIA model. Whenever DP > 1 splits the Engram tables across replicas, ROCm returns wrong Engram rows, and the V1 model runner hangs. This PR ports that wiring.

`Engram._ready_rows` assumes the staged rows came from hashes gathered across the DP group: one slot of tokens per replica, which it then all-gathers and slices. The AMD model passed only its own hashes. As a result, rank 0 read its peer's heads for the peer's own tokens, and rank 1 read stale staging rows. On the V1 runner, an idle replica skipped the Engram lookups while the busy replica blocked in the DP all-gather, so the engine hung. The default `dp_shared_memory=true` path does not use the DP gather, so DP deployments that fit in `/dev/shm` were unaffected.

The fix mirrors the NVIDIA model line for line. With DP1, `gather_engram_hashes` returns its input unchanged and the dummy-hash branch is never taken. The THP hooks (`drop_checkpoint_cache`, `collapse_huge_pages`) only affect memory, not correctness, so they are left for a follow-up. On ROCm CI, the multi-GPU test only runs once the CUDA-only skip is lifted, which #62298 does.

- `amd/model.py`: look up the hashes gathered across the DP group (`gather_engram_hashes`), not just this replica's hashes.
- `amd/model.py`: give a replica with no attention metadata `dummy_hashes`, so it still joins the DP-sharded lookup collectives.
- `amd/model.py`: call `can_share_engram_tables` before building the layers. When `/dev/shm` is too small, ROCm now logs a warning and falls back to sharded tables, as NVIDIA does, instead of failing at startup.
- `test_engram_dp_shard.py`: on ROCm, the dummy-hash model-forward check runs the AMD model instead of the NVIDIA one.

Validated on MI300X, DP2 x TP1 on 2 GPUs, dummy weights. The proxy is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's config cut to 24 layers and 8 experts. A full-size check also used the 40-layer, 32-expert proxy with its two 23.6 GiB tables. Every Engram table row is filled with a fixed function of its global row id. A test-only hook checks each `Engram.embed` result against that function, so a wrong row shows up directly. Each replica's outputs are also compared with the DP2 `dp_shared_memory` run, which does not use the DP gather and has correct rows. Rank 1 gets one short request, so it runs idle (dummy) steps for most of rank 0's decode.

| Setup | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `dp_shared_memory=false` | 846/894 and 198/198 tokens with wrong rows | 0 wrong; tokens and logprobs bit-identical to the shared run |
| `use_thp=true` | same wrong rows | 0 wrong, bit-identical |
| `cpu_offload=false` | same wrong rows | 0 wrong, bit-identical |
| tables > `/dev/shm` (16.5 GiB vs 16 GiB) | startup `RuntimeError: Engram shared-memory creation failed ... Insufficient space in /dev/shm` | warning, falls back to sharding, 0 wrong rows |
| sharded, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` (idle rank has no attention metadata) | hang, then `RPC call to execute_dummy_batch timed out` | completes, 0 wrong rows |
| sharded, FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs | outputs differ from the shared run | bit-identical to the shared run |
| shared (default) | correct | correct, unchanged |
| 40-layer proxy, default (47 GiB of tables vs 16 GiB `/dev/shm`) | startup `RuntimeError` (24171 MiB required, 15673 MiB free) | falls back to sharding, 0 wrong rows, bit-identical to the `dp_shared_memory=false` run |

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Reset the store cursor when a request restarts from token 0
author: AdvayMonga
body:
## Overview

A request resumed from preemption kept `next_stored_chunk_idx` from before the preemption. If the CPU tier had evicted its chunks meanwhile, the chunks below the cursor were never offered again and everything stored afterwards sat behind a chunk-0 miss. Reset the cursor in `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, which only runs when a request starts from `num_computed_tokens == 0`.

## Claims

- A resumed request offers its chunks from chunk 0 again; `prepare_store` drops the ones still resident, so nothing is stored twice.
- A CPU prefix hit on resume is unchanged: `update_state_after_alloc` still raises the cursor afterwards.

## Validation

- `test_request_preemption` gains a `cpu_hit=False` case that fails on `main` and passes here, both scheduling modes.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector`: 609 passed, 2 skipped. `pre-commit` clean.
- No open PR or issue covers this (searched `next_stored_chunk_idx`, `preempt offload`); #57813, #61375, #60574, #60810 and #62929 touch nearby code and compose with it.

## Details

`_reset_cache` already resets the cursor for the same reason. The reset cannot live in `_update_req_states` under `if preempted:`, which runs after `update_state_after_alloc` in the same step and would clobber the hit-derived cursor.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; I reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Stop advertising head_dim 64 in the b12x backend
author: VidyasagarDudekula
body:
## Overview

`--attention-backend b12x` accepts head_dim 64 models at selection and then crashes after model load, at the first forward, inside the b12x paged planner (`no valid NUM_MMA_KV typed shared-memory allocation fits the device`). The b12x package cannot plan head_dim 64 decode at all, so this stops advertising 64 and lets selection fail fast. Fixes #63011.

## Claims

- head_dim 64 models with `--attention-backend b12x` are now rejected at backend selection with `Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.B12X is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['head_size not supported']`, before weights load, instead of crashing in CUDA graph capture.
- head_dim 128/192/256 are unchanged.
- One list entry removed, one unit test added. No kernel or runner changes.

## Validation

DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, aarch64), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu132, flashinfer-python 0.7.2 (provides the `b12x` module), vLLM main @ 35d01660f.

```python
from vllm import LLM
LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", attention_config={"backend": "B12X"}, block_size=128, dtype="bfloat16")
```

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| startup | model loads, torch.compile runs, then `Capturing CUDA graphs` dies: `traits.py ... select_paged_forward_traits ... ValueError: no valid NUM_MMA_KV typed shared-memory allocation fits the device` | `ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.B12X is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['head_size not supported']` at selection |

Same before/after with `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-0.5B-Instruct` (hybrid, head_dim 64). head_dim 128 (Qwen3-0.6B) still selects and runs b12x.

```
$ pytest tests/v1/attention/test_b12x.py
44 passed in 38.41s   # DGX Spark, GB10; includes the 4 new parametrized cases
```

The new test fails on main (`supports_head_size(64)` is True there) and passes with this change. `pre-commit run --files ...` is clean.

## Details

Root cause is inside the b12x package (same in `flashinfer/experimental/b12x` on FlashInfer main and in the `b12x==1.5.1` wheel pinned by the `[b12x]` extra), reported upstream as flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6977:

- `_paged_determine_cta_tile_q()` returns `cta_tile_q = 16` for every decode/verify plan, and for that family `select_paged_forward_traits()` only sweeps `num_mma_kv = 1`.
- `_paged_is_invalid()` keeps FA2's rule that `num_mma_d_vo == 4` (head_dim 64) with an odd `num_mma_kv` is invalid, so the single candidate is rejected and the sweep raises.
- The decode kernel itself (`PagedForwardKernel`, `base_use_paged_kv_tma_decode`) only accepts `num_mma_kv == 1` for the generic bf16 16-row family, so the two constraints contradict each other for head_dim 64. FlashInfer's own b12x paged tests only cover head_dim 128/192/256.

I tried the obvious package-side patches on the Spark before settling on this: forcing two KV tiles for head_dim 64 decode is rejected by the kernel constructor (`PagedForwardKernel now only supports exact-plane paged K/V TMA decode`), and relaxing the odd-tile rule for the decode family lets graph capture succeed but the head_dim 64 extend kernel warmup then compiles for 30 minutes without finishing (killed at the bound, twice). So head_dim 64 is not a working path in any released b12x, and the honest thing for vLLM to do is to not offer it. The package API has no head-dim capability query, so a static list is the only fail-fast available; 64 can be re-added, version-gated, once a b12x release supports it.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and this PR; I reviewed and tested the change on my own hardware.

title: [BugFix] Forward the configured cpu distributed timeout to `cpu_all_reduce_`
author: fangyuchu
body:
## Overview


#61767 introduced `cpu_all_reduce_` (`vllm/distributed/utils.py`), a low-latency gloo all-reduce for the DP hot path — `ParallelConfig.sync_dp_state` (engine-side DP state sync) and `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` (worker-side DP padding/cudagraph coordination). It replaced `torch.distributed.all_reduce` with raw `group.send`/`group.recv` p2p ops waited on via bare `work.wait()`.

A bare `wait()` never times out: the gloo group's default timeout is not applied to these p2p waits. So since #61767, `--cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds` silently no longer takes effect on the DP sync path — when a DP peer hangs or dies, the surviving ranks block inside the DP sync, where previously they would have raised a timeout error.

## Claims


Now `cpu_all_reduce_` will throw timeout error under defined `-cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds`.


## Validation



**Unit test** : `pytest tests/distributed/test_cpu_all_reduce.py`

`test_cpu_all_reduce_timeout` spawns 2 gloo ranks; rank 1 never joins the all-reduce, and rank 0 calls `cpu_all_reduce_` with `timeout=timedelta(seconds=1)`. It asserts a `RuntimeError("Timed out ...")` is raised and that the call returns in under 3s (measured ~1.0s), i.e. the wait honors the timeout rather than hanging until the peer process exits.

**Manual e2e**: launched a DP=2 deployment, put one DP rank to sleep, and observed the other rank raise the gloo timeout in the DP sync within the configured window instead of hanging.


## Details



Add an optional `timeout: timedelta | None = None` parameter and forward it to every p2p `work.wait(timeout)`:

- `cpu_all_reduce_` — bounds each p2p wait; `None` keeps the previous no-timeout behavior, so other callers are unaffected.
- `GroupCoordinator.cpu_all_reduce_` and `ParallelConfig.sync_dp_state` — pass-through plumbing.
- Both DP call sites now forward the configured `cpu_distributed_timeout`: `DPEngineCoreProc._has_global_unfinished_reqs` (engine DP state sync) and `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` (worker DP sync).

With this, a hung peer surfaces as a `RuntimeError("Timed out ...")` on the surviving ranks within the configured timeout, instead of an indefinite hang.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Budget prefill memory the startup profile misses
author: gcanlin
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill OOMs at `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`: three allocations that grow with the token budget are missed by the startup memory profile. This PR removes or budgets each of them. Fixes #60450.

OOM on a B200 DEP4 prefill instance (`max_model_len` 1M, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`, 17 min into an AgentX trace; the same flags at 16384 run for hours):

```
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB. GPU 2 has a total capacity of
178.35 GiB of which 2.00 GiB is free.
  deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:625 forward -> attention.py:967 _wq_b_proj
```

The startup plan left 5.31 GiB free; only 2.00 GiB was left at the OOM.

## Changes

| Gap (32768 tokens, 1M context) | Why the profile misses it | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Indexer `expanded_block_table_buffer`: 1 GiB per builder, two builders plus a replay copy | Allocated after KV sizing | Rows = `min(max_num_seqs * next_n, max_num_batched_tokens)`, the decode tokens it serves: 12 MiB |
| Engram layers 1 and 14: `previous_post` (1.25 GiB) held through attention and MoE, plus a 1.75 GiB spike in the call | Skipped in the profile run unless the table is DP-sharded | Profile runs look up dead rows (NVIDIA and AMD models); `del previous_post` after the call |
| Indexer prefill logits: SM100's BF16 output plus its FP32 copy, with the previous chunk's still alive: 2.5x the 512 MiB budget | Reserved at 1x | `del logits` per chunk; the prefill term of the #62860 reservation counts the copy (1.5x) |

No kernel, chunking or scheduling change.

## Validation

- `pre-commit`: pass.
- Unit tests: new `test_indexer_expanded_block_table_sized_by_decode_tokens` (fails on main); `test_engram_dp_shard` updated for dead-row lookups. GPU run pending.
- E2E pending: the same config at 32768 / 0.95, startup KV size and profiled peak, main vs PR.

## Notes

- Decode rows never exceed `max_num_seqs * next_n`: the indexer treats wider requests as prefills, and `build()` asserts the bound with host ints (no sync).
- The dead-row branch runs only without attention metadata (with MRV2, only the profile run), where outputs are discarded.
- Not addressed: the 4.11 GiB reserved-but-unallocated at the OOM (allocator fragmentation).

title: [Bugfix][Model] Load Granite Speech checkpoints saved by Transformers v5
author: JaredforReal
body:
## Overview

`ibm-granite/granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus` no longer loads in vLLM. Its checkpoint was re-saved with Transformers 5.19 on 2026-10-21 ([HF revision `e69efe37`](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus/commit/e69efe37f97b6283c61f5a8dadda2b3eb67765d6)), and the text model weights are now named `language_model.model.model.*` instead of `language_model.model.*`. This PR maps the extra level away in `GraniteSpeechForConditionalGeneration`, so both checkpoint layouts load.

It also fixes `test_granite_speech.py::test_models[...granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus...]`, which has failed in `Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)` on both NVIDIA and AMD since the checkpoint update (full build [96476](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96476)):

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'model' in GraniteModel.
```

## Claims

- The new `granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus` checkpoint loads, and its outputs match Transformers.
- The previous revision of the checkpoint, and the other Granite Speech checkpoints, load as before. The mapping only touches names starting with `language_model.model.model.`, which no older checkpoint has.

## Validation

GB300, transformers 5.20.2 and peft 0.21.1, matching the CI pins.

| Check | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_granite_speech.py` (3.3-2b with LoRA, 4.0-1b, 4.1-2b-plus) | 4.1-2b-plus fails with the error above | 3 passed |
| Greedy `"The capital of France is"`, 8 tokens, old revision `1454e6e1` | ` Paris.` | ` Paris.` (Transformers: ` Paris.`) |
| Same, new revision `e69efe37` | load error | ` also a city of 20 million people` (Transformers: identical) |

The new revision also switches the text config to YaRN RoPE (factor 4). The test compares against Transformers, so it covers that path too.

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_granite_speech.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/granite_speech.py
```

No separate model evaluation. The change only renames weights at load time, and the test above checks the outputs against Transformers.

## Details

**Why the extra `model.`** Transformers' `granite_speech` conversion mapping has two renamings: a top-level `^language_model.model` → `model.language_model`, and `^language_model.model` → `language_model`, scoped to `GraniteSpeechModel`. The new names are most likely `save_pretrained` reversing both of them. I have not confirmed this in the Transformers source. Transformers applies both renamings on load, so it reads the checkpoint correctly. vLLM loads checkpoint names directly, so it needs the mapping.

**Relation to #60666.** That draft PR applies Transformers' checkpoint renamings in vLLM's loader generically, and would probably make this mapping unnecessary. It is large (122 files) and not ready for review yet. This PR is a minimal fix for users and CI in the meantime. The mapping can be dropped once #60666 lands.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs and issues for `granite speech`, `granite_speech` and `granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus`. Only #60666 touches this model's weight names. Its explicit Granite Speech mapping covers `model.language_model.*`. I have not tested whether its generic renamings handle the double-nested names.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Bound late chunk sizes in the Python API
author: LinzeShi
body:
## Overview

Bound `LateChunkingParams.chunk_size` to `0 < chunk_size < 2**63`, matching the HTTP schema added in #61772.

## Claims

Reject oversized chunk sizes before engine handoff. The maximum valid value, `2**63 - 1`, still works.

## Validation

123 tests passed:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/test_pooling_params.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_methods.py
```

Pre-commit checks passed. On RunPod with an NVIDIA L4 and `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`, both model runners passed 7 tests, including the new `LLM.encode` regression, ordinary inputs and mixed chunk sizes:

```bash
for runner in 1 0; do
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=$runner .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
    tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_offline.py \
    -k 'test_late_chunking_rejects_oversized_chunk_size or test_e5_late_chunking_mixed_requests or test_str_prompts or test_token_ids_prompts'
done
```

The new regression changes `chunk_size` to `2**64` after construction, then checks that `LLM.encode` rejects it without leaving unfinished requests.

## Details

Positive integers of `2**64` or more currently pass Python parameter validation but fail MessagePack encoding after the request is registered. The shared guard rejects them during construction and request validation.

Found during [review of #61419](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61419#discussion_r4266235103). #61772 fixed the HTTP schema; this covers the remaining Python API path.

title: [CI][ROCM][Bug] Elastic DP doesn't work with AITER-on
author: qli88
body:
## Overview

The Elastic EP Scaling test (distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling) failed with AITER on. The cause is:
1. AITER requires a torch.distributed-registered group, but Elastic EP is using stateless group, which is not torch.distributed registered at all, so we need to skip AITER AR and choose next available AR;
2. During scale-up, existing workers call _release_cuda_graphs() and then re-capture into the same global graph pool. Some memory in that pool was still allocated, because FlyDSL didn't release them correctly. Graph replay never re-enters Python, so a kernel last launched during capture holds those tensors inside the graph pool indefinitely. The pool had no graphs left but still had live blocks, so PyTorch rejected capturing into it again. Now I explicitly call _switch_to_fresh_graph_pool() to switch to a new graph pool to avoid this.

## Claims

These 2 bugs are fixed. This test case works as expected no matter AITER is on or off.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Use 64-bit row offsets in the Triton W4A16 GEMM
author: subin9
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #63049. `triton_w4a16_gemm_kernel` indexes activations and outputs with int32 row offsets, which wrap once M × K or M × N passes 2^31 and fault on ROCm. Casting `pid_m` to int64 makes both products 64-bit. The weight, scale and zero-point offsets do not depend on M and stay int32.

## Test Plan

The new test runs the GEMM one block of rows past each bound, (K, N) = (256, 34816) for the output offsets and (17408, 256) for the activation offsets, and compares the last 64 rows with the float32 reference already in the file.

I also called `_triton_w4a16_gemm_impl` alone at a Qwen3.5 27B model's shapes, served `vllm-sr/d3-W4A16-AWQ` and `vllm-sr/d3-W4A16-GPTQ` at the default 262,144-token length on one MI300X, and timed the kernel before and after the change.

## Test Result

The new test passes, along with the rest of the file. Before the change the kernel faults at M = 62,000 with (K, N) = (5120, 34816) and at M = 124,000 with (17408, 5120). After it, both shapes run up to M = 262,144, and their last rows are as close to a float32 matmul as at small M. Both packages now serve at the default length, and their answers on 300 requests match those of runs at `--max-model-len 32768`, which did not reach the bound. Over three projection shapes, M from 1 to 32,768, with and without zero points, every timing is within 2.6% of the unchanged kernel, in both directions.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Respect meta initialization for Engram offload
author: gty111
body:
## Overview

Respect meta initialization when allocating DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables, preventing unnecessary host-memory allocation on encoder-only instances.

## Claims

- Skip pinned, huge-page and shared host storage during meta initialization.
- Preserve normal Engram CPU offload and suppress offload logs for meta tensors.

## Validation

Started two real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash encoder instances under Slurm using `vllm serve ... --mm-encoder-only --tensor-parallel-size 1` with Mooncake TCP. After startup, worker inspection confirmed both Engram tables remain meta with zero host-table bytes on each instance, avoiding approximately 188.8 GiB of unnecessary allocation per encoder.

## Details

Encoder-only language models are constructed under `torch.device("meta")`, but Engram explicitly allocates CPU storage. The retained language-model placeholder therefore holds two unnecessary tables, approximately 188.8 GiB per TP1 encoder instance for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

Reuse the existing device-local allocation path before any host-storage allocation. No runner, scheduler or connector changes. Open-PR searches found no existing fix for this meta-initialization bypass.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MiniMax-M3] Reject IndexCache overrides that miss text_config
author: lishuoshuo-amd
body:
## Overview

MiniMax-M3 reads its IndexCache settings (#47269) from `text_config`, so the documented top-level `--hf-overrides` form is silently ignored. This PR rejects that form on ROCm with an actionable error and fixes the docstring.

## Claims

- On ROCm, top-level `use_index_cache`, `index_topk_freq` or `index_skip_topk_offset` raise `ValueError` when `ModelConfig` is built, and the error gives the nested override. Before, the server started with IndexCache off and no log.
- The nested form is unchanged and is what the docstring now documents.
- The docstring drops the GSM8K-based "negligible accuracy impact" claim.

## Validation

MI355X, ROCm 7.2.3, `main` at `12c01a22e`:

```bash
pytest tests/models/minimax_m3/test_index_cache_overrides.py -v
# this PR:           3 passed
# main + this test:  2 failed (Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError), 1 passed
```

`vllm serve MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --load-format dummy ... --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}'`:

- `main`: starts and serves requests; nothing reports the override as ignored.
- This PR: exits after 10 s, before EngineCore starts, with `MiniMax-M3 reads IndexCache settings from text_config, so top-level use_index_cache, index_topk_freq would be ignored. Pass them as --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}}'.`
- This PR with the nested form: starts and serves requests.

## Details

`--hf-overrides` updates the outer `MiniMaxM3Config`, while the language model and `_should_skip_index_topk` read `config.text_config` (the same pitfall as #54289). The check is a `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP` entry that reads the keys from `hf_overrides`. It is ROCm only because the NVIDIA model does not implement IndexCache. Launches using the top-level form now fail at startup instead of running without IndexCache. `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py` is added to the MI355 MiniMax M3 CI steps.

GSM8K prompts fit within the 2048-token sparse top-k window, where IndexCache has no effect. A long-context proxy shows a cost: teacher-forced NLL of a ~1K-token unseen file after 12K-131K tokens of same-package Python sources (24 samples, MXFP4, TP4, one run per configuration):

| IndexCache | off | freq 2 | freq 4 | freq 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean NLL | 0.703 | 0.747 | 0.781 | 0.854 |
| samples worse than off | - | 21/24 | 21/24 | 24/24 |

<details>
<summary>nll_longctx.py and reproduction</summary>

```bash
python nll_longctx.py build <model_dir> samples.jsonl            # samples depend on the packages installed in the image
python nll_longctx.py score samples.jsonl <port> <model> nll.json  # once per server configuration
```

```python
"""Long-context teacher-forced NLL probe for sparse-attention approximations (e.g. IndexCache).

build: nll_longctx.py build <model_dir> <out.jsonl>
    Concatenates Python sources from one package directory into 32K/64K/128K-token
    contexts and appends the head of an unseen file as the scored target.
score: nll_longctx.py score <samples.jsonl> <port> <model> <out.json>
    Sends token ids to /v1/completions with prompt_logprobs and reports the mean
    NLL of the target tokens per sample.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.request

ROOTS = ["vllm", "torch", "transformers", "aiter"]
SITE = "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages"
TARGET_TOKENS = 1024


def build(model_dir, out):
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_dir, trust_remote_code=True)
    dirs = []
    for root in ROOTS:
        for d in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(SITE, root, "**/"), recursive=True)):
            files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "*.py")))
            if len(files) >= 12:
                dirs.append((d, files))
    samples = []
    for i, ctx in enumerate([32768] * 8 + [65536] * 8 + [131072] * 8):
        d, files = dirs[(i * 7919) % len(dirs)]
        ids, used = [], 0
        for f in files[:-1]:
            text = f"# file: {os.path.relpath(f, SITE)}\n" + open(f, errors="ignore").read() + "\n"
            ids += tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
            used += 1
            if len(ids) >= ctx:
                break
        ids = ids[:ctx]
        tgt_file = files[-1] if used >= len(files) - 1 else files[used]
        tgt = tok.encode(f"# file: {os.path.relpath(tgt_file, SITE)}\n" + open(tgt_file, errors="ignore").read(),
                         add_special_tokens=False)[:TARGET_TOKENS]
        samples.append({"id": i, "dir": os.path.relpath(d, SITE), "ctx": len(ids), "ids": ids + tgt, "n_target": len(tgt)})
        print(f"sample {i}: dir={samples[-1]['dir']} ctx={len(ids)} target={len(tgt)}", flush=True)
    with open(out, "w") as f:
        for s in samples:
            f.write(json.dumps(s) + "\n")


def score(path, port, model, out):
    res = []
    for line in open(path):
        s = json.loads(line)
        body = json.dumps({"model": model, "prompt": s["ids"], "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0,
                           "prompt_logprobs": 0}).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://localhost:{port}/v1/completions", data=body,
                                     headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        r = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800).read())
        plp = r["choices"][0]["prompt_logprobs"]
        n = s["n_target"]
        nll = []
        for pos in range(len(s["ids"]) - n, len(s["ids"])):
            entry = plp[pos] or {}
            lp = entry.get(str(s["ids"][pos]))
            nll.append(-lp["logprob"])
        res.append({"id": s["id"], "ctx": s["ctx"], "nll": sum(nll) / len(nll)})
        print(f"sample {s['id']} ctx={s['ctx']} nll={res[-1]['nll']:.4f}", flush=True)
    by_ctx = {}
    for r in res:
        by_ctx.setdefault(r["ctx"] // 1024, []).append(r["nll"])
    summary = {"mean_nll": sum(r["nll"] for r in res) / len(res),
               "by_ctx_k": {k: sum(v) / len(v) for k, v in sorted(by_ctx.items())}, "samples": res}
    json.dump(summary, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
    print("mean_nll", summary["mean_nll"], "by_ctx_k", summary["by_ctx_k"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1] == "build":
        build(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
    else:
        score(sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4], sys.argv[5])
```

</details>

Not a duplicate: no open or recent PR covers this (searched `use_index_cache`, `index_topk_freq` and MiniMax `hf-overrides`). AI assistance was used; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Match the DeepSeek-V4.1 FP8 config in the shared-expert FSE compatibility check
author: BaoYunkai
body:
## Overview

On CUDA and ROCm, `deepseek_v4_fp8` always resolves to the DeepSeek-V4.1 `DeepseekV4FP8Config`, which subclasses `Fp8Config`, not the V4 class. `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` runs its DeepSeek-V4 checks only for the V4 class, so on these platforms it falls through to the generic `Fp8Config` branch and reports every DeepSeek-V4 shared expert as FSE-compatible. This PR matches both classes for MXFP4 routed experts, as the online-quantization branch of the same function already does.

Founded by Hyperloom.

## Claims

- Fixes the weight-loading failure of DeepSeek-V4-Flash on ROCm with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. Quark MXFP4 checkpoints hit the same failure on the FP8 MTP shared expert.
- No change when the variable is unset: the check is not called.
- No change for FP8-expert checkpoints such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base: they keep the generic FP8 check, as on main.
- Adds `test_deepseek_v41_quant_config_rejects_fp8_mtp_shared_expert_fse` and `test_deepseek_v41_fp8_experts_keep_fp8_fse_check`.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, TP1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256`, vLLM built from main at 15a78aa88e (the touched files are unchanged on current main).

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, main fails during weight loading in 2 of 2 runs:

```
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_weight_scale_inv'
```

With this PR, all 43 layers reject FSE ("only implemented/tested with Quark MXFP4"), run the shared expert unfused, and serve.

`vllm bench serve`, random 1000 in / 200 out, 400 prompts, concurrency 50, a fresh server per run. 4 runs per arm, median of the last 3, within-arm spread in parentheses:

| Arm | Total tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, variable unset | 10061 (±3.5%) | 1026 | 24.68 |
| this PR, variable unset | 10033 (±0.8%) | 1024 | 24.76 |
| this PR, variable = 1 | 10045 (±0.2%) | 1027 | 24.77 |

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, `lm_eval --model local-completions`:

| Arm | strict-match | Same verdict as main |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9515 ± 0.0059 | - |
| main, repeated (noise floor) | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 | 98.10% |
| this PR, variable = 1 | 0.9538 ± 0.0058 | 97.95% |

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base (FP8 experts), TP2, vLLM built from main at b3b0bc3059: with the variable set, main runs the shared expert fused (257 experts, top-7 in the MoE), and GSM8K (same settings as above) stays within the noise of unfused runs: 0.9174 vs 0.9090 and 0.9234 from two runs without the variable. This PR gives the same FSE answer as main for this checkpoint.

Unit tests on MI355X against the built tree, `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py`: this PR 107 passed. Main fails `test_deepseek_v41_quant_config_rejects_fp8_mtp_shared_expert_fse`; `test_deepseek_v41_fp8_experts_keep_fp8_fse_check` passes on both.

## Details

The existing unit test missed the bug because it constructs the V4 class directly. CI does not run DeepSeek-V4 with this variable set; the new tests are CPU-only.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Validate late-interaction mode and use count in the Python API
author: he-yufeng
body:
## Overview

`LateInteractionParams` had no validation, and bad inputs fail in the worst places:

- An unknown `mode` string is silently skipped by the late-interaction runner (`_parse_late_interaction_meta` returns `None` for anything outside `cache_query`/`score_doc`), so a typo produces ordinary pooler output instead of an error.
- `cache_query` with `query_uses=None` crashes on the runner's `assert query_uses is not None`.
- `query_uses <= 0` poisons the cache lifecycle: the entry pops on the first `score_doc`, so the remaining paired documents fail with a cache miss.

`__post_init__` now rejects unknown modes and non-positive use counts, the same shape as the `LateChunkingParams.chunk_size` validation added in #63051. The HTTP scoring path builds these params programmatically with valid values (`build_late_interaction_query_params` / `build_late_interaction_doc_params`), so only hand-constructed Python-API requests change behavior.

This is not duplicating an existing PR: the only open late-interaction work is about cancelling cached queries (#56617) and request tracing (#61785), which are different seams.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/test_pooling_params.py -q
# 41 passed
```

The new rejection tests fail against unpatched main (10 failed: invalid mode and use-count values were silently accepted), while the valid-shape wire round-trip passes both before and after. CPU-only environment; no GPU run.

## AI assistance

This change was produced with AI assistance (Claude Code): the sibling gap was identified after #63051 landed, and the fix, tests, and verification above were run locally and reviewed line by line before submission.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Size AITER MLA persistent metadata for every decode query length
author: BaoYunkai
body:
## Overview

`AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` sizes its persistent decode metadata buffers with one `get_mla_metadata_info_v1` call at `reorder_batch_threshold` (#45227), but it builds metadata for every query length up to that threshold, and aiter's buffer needs are not monotonic in the query length. A bf16 DSpark draft overflows the buffers and faults. This PR sizes them for the largest need of any query length up to the threshold.

Found by Hyperloom.

## Claims

- Fixes `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` during warmup for Kimi-K3 with its DSpark draft (TP4, `num_speculative_tokens: 7`, bf16 KV cache).
- No change without speculative decoding (threshold 1, the same single call as before), or for 16-head fp8 KV caches up to threshold 8. Other configurations can get larger buffers, e.g. 32-head fp8 on gfx950, which is 64-wide at query length 3 and 128-wide at query length 4.
- Adds `test_builder_sizes_metadata_for_every_decode_qlen`.

## Validation

aiter v0.1.26 called directly on MI355X: 16 heads, 1024 requests, non-causal, bf16 Q/KV and metadata, compared with a PyTorch reference.

| Query length | Buffers sized for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 8 | memory fault |
| 7 | 7 | matches (max abs err 0.003) |
| 5, 6 | 8 | memory fault |
| 4 | 8 | matches (max abs err 0.004) |

Kimi-K3 truncated to 8 layers (`--hf-overrides`, `--load-format dummy`) with its DSpark draft (`target_layer_ids` remapped), TP4, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, CUDA graphs on, vLLM built from main at b3b0bc3059. Main faults during warmup; this PR starts and serves 24 concurrent requests.

Unit tests on MI355X against the built tree, `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py`: this PR 113 passed. Main fails 21: the new test, and the cases of `test_builder_init_sizes_decode_metadata_and_filters_dcp_maps`, which now expects one sizing call per query length.

## Details

On gfx950, aiter tiles the `num_heads x qlen` packed query rows of a bf16 block by 64 when there are fewer than 128 of them, and by 128 otherwise. With 16 heads and 1024 requests, query lengths 5-7 need `work_info_set` (2558, 8) and `reduce_final_map` (2048, 2), while query length 8 needs (1279, 8) and (1024, 2). A DSpark draft runs `k`-token blocks under a `k + 1` threshold, so `k = 7` lands on the larger case. At 1024 requests the larger sizing adds about 55 KB of int32 buffers.

CI does not run a DSpark draft on MI355X. The results above use dummy weights; a real-weight Kimi-K3 run was not done. #41016 (closed) sized the batch dimension of these buffers; this PR sizes the query-length dimension.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and reproduced the results above.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Take the AITER MLA KV cache dtype from the group's spec
author: BaoYunkai
body:
## Overview

`AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` takes the KV cache dtype from the global `cache_config.cache_dtype`, but a KV cache group can use another dtype. With a speculative draft that sets its own `kv_cache_dtype`, the target model runner still builds the draft groups' metadata with the target's config, and DSpark and DFlash draft prefill reuses it. `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` keeps some MLA layers in bf16 under a global fp8 cache. This PR takes the dtype from the group's spec.

This was reported and approved in #55591, which its author closed without merging.

Found by Hyperloom.

## Claims

- A bf16 draft under an fp8 target gets bf16 decode metadata in draft prefill. On main, the metadata it reuses from the target runner is built for fp8. The draft's own decode builders already use the draft dtype since #63251.
- A layer in `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` gets bf16 decode under an fp8 cache; on main it gets fp8.
- A bf16 target with an fp8 draft KV cache no longer fails at startup with `KeyError: torch.uint8`.
- No change when every group uses the global dtype.

## Validation

Reproducer on the stock vLLM ROCm nightly image (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-40941f2c4ba96fba0a7e282a5355e89cd74d9ac5`, main at 40941f2c4b), 4x MI355X: Kimi-K3 truncated to 8 layers with its DSpark draft, bf16 target KV cache, fp8 draft KV cache. The draft is `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` with `target_num_hidden_layers` set to 8 and `target_layer_ids` to `[1, 2, 3, 5, 6]`.

```bash

  --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"num_hidden_layers": 8, "linear_attn_config": {"full_attn_layers": [4, 8], "gate_lower_bound": -5.0, "head_dim": 128, "kda_layers": [1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7], "num_heads": 96, "short_conv_kernel_size": 4, "use_full_rank_gate": true}}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "/path/to/Kimi-K3-DSpark-trunc8", "method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "attention_backend": "ROCM_AITER_MLA", "kv_cache_dtype": "fp8"}'
```

main fails at startup:

```text
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 726, in initialize_kv_cache
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 292, in init_attn_backend
  File "vllm/v1/worker/utils.py", line 332, in create_metadata_builders
  File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py", line 1029, in __init__
    kv_dtype = {
KeyError: torch.uint8
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed
```

This branch starts and serves:

```text
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

Kimi-K3 truncated to 8 layers (`--hf-overrides`, `--load-format dummy`), TP4, CUDA graphs on, 24 concurrent requests, on the vLLM ROCm nightly image built from main at 40941f2c4b, with a debug hook (not part of this PR) that logs each AITER MLA builder's decode dtype and how often it builds metadata:

| Case | Builder | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| fp8 target, bf16 DSpark draft, 2 and 7 draft tokens | target runner, draft layers (reused by draft prefill, 100+ builds) | fp8 | bf16 |
| | speculator, draft layers | bf16 | bf16 |
| bf16 target, fp8 DSpark draft, 7 draft tokens | target runner, draft layers | fails at startup: `KeyError: torch.uint8` | fp8, serves |
| `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 3` | layer 3, bf16 cache (100+ builds) | fp8 | bf16 |

The `KeyError` also reproduces with the stock nightly vLLM. All other runs start and serve requests; since #63251, main no longer fails at startup with 2 draft tokens.

Dummy weights cannot show wrong attention, so each side's metadata plan was checked against aiter directly on the same image (aiter 0.1.27): bf16 Q and KV cache, 16 heads, 32 requests, max abs error against a PyTorch reference. Draft prefill is causal, at the target's verify length (draft tokens + 1):

| Query length | causal, fp8 plan (main) | causal, bf16 plan (this PR) | non-causal, fp8 plan (main) | non-causal, bf16 plan (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.0006 | 0.0006 | 0.0006 | 0.0006 |
| 3 | 0.0006 | 0.0006 | 0.0006 | 0.0006 |
| 4 | 0.0012 | 0.0012 | 0.0012 | 0.0012 |
| 5 | 3.66 | 0.0006 | 3.66 | 0.0005 |
| 6 | 3.71 | 0.040 | 3.71 | 0.0007 |
| 7 | 4.32 | 0.18 | 4.31 | 0.0015 |
| 8 | 0.0007 | 0.0007 | 0.0007 | 0.0007 |

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, TP1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 3 4 11 12`, measured at 15a78aa88e before #63116 (which does not change this config). A builder dump shows the skipped MLA group set up as fp8 on main and bf16 with this PR. GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, shows no measurable change:

| Arm | strict-match | Same verdict as main |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.4556 ± 0.0137 | - |
| main, repeated (noise floor) | 0.4602 ± 0.0137 | 69.67% |
| this PR | 0.4390 ± 0.0137 | 70.43% |

Unit tests on the same nightly image, `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`: this PR 75 passed; main fails `draft-bf16-kv-under-fp8-target`, `draft-fp8-kv-under-bf16-target` and `skip-layer-bf16-kv`.

## Details

The builder already reads `kv_cache_spec.cache_dtype_str` for fused DCP prefill; this PR uses the same value for the segmented DCP verify LDS check and the decode setup. The existing `bf16-group` case of `test_builder_init_sizes_decode_metadata_and_filters_dcp_maps` asserted the fp8 decode setup for a bf16 group; it is now one of the cases above and expects the group's dtype. On main, rejection sampling keeps the served output correct; the mismatch only affects the draft.

CI does not run a DSpark draft on MI355X. Kimi-Linear scores 0.88 on GSM8K with a bf16 KV cache and 0.36 with an fp8 KV cache on main; that gap is unrelated to this PR.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix cooperative_topk illegal memory access on NaN scores
author: LopezCastroRoberto
body:
## Purpose

Since #59645, `cooperative_topk` crashes with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` when a row of 64K columns or more contains more NaNs than `top_k` (e.g. 1% of a 256K row, or a fully-NaN row). NaN scores can reach decode top-k during warmup and CUDA-graph capture, where the indexer reads uninitialized KV blocks (see the note in `candidate_blocks.py`). Before #59645 such rows produced garbage indices; now they take down the process.

**Root cause.** nvcc compiles the integer expression `bits | 0x80000000u` in `convert_to_uint32_v2` as the FP operation `-|x|`:

```
ISETP.GE.AND P0, PT, R2, RZ        // bits >= 0 ?
FADD R10, -|R2|, -RZ               // "bits | 0x80000000u" emitted as -|x|
@P0 IMAD.MOV.U32 R9, RZ, RZ, R10
```

That is bit-exact for finite values and ±inf, but FADD canonicalizes NaN to `0x7FFFFFFF`, which is the ordered key of -0.0. The FP16 coarse bins put NaN above +inf (bin 1023), so the two orderings disagree. When NaNs overflow the threshold bin, the exact recovery takes the single-key path with a -0.0 pivot. Every positive score then counts as "above" it, and the unchecked append in `collect_exact_candidates` writes past `s_topk` (compute-sanitizer: invalid `__shared__` write in `unbounded_round0_single_key`).

**Fix.** Read the bits through an opaque `mov.b32`, so the key stays bit-exact and NaN orders above +inf in both the coarse and exact keys, matching `torch.topk`.

title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek-VL2 cache identity across cropping modes
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix DeepSeek-VL2 encoder-cache collisions when the same image appears in requests with different cropping modes.

## Claims

- Distinguish raw-image cache identities across cropping modes, including client-provided UUIDs.
- Preserve identities within each cropping mode and for precomputed image embeddings.

## Validation

uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_vl2.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_deepseek_vl2.py -q

6 passed. Tests cover cropping boundaries, content hashes, client-provided UUIDs, precomputed embeddings, and both single-image → three-image and reverse request sequences. Both generation cases failed before the fix.

Additional validation with real DeepSeek-VL2-tiny weights on an H800:

- Both request orders completed successfully.
- Alternating and repeated requests matched the eight-token outputs of corresponding successful requests on unpatched code. The repeated three-image request was compared against two consecutive three-image requests on unpatched code. Caching remained enabled.
- A subsequent text-only request succeeded.

## Details

DeepSeek-VL2 enables cropping for requests with at most two images and disables it for larger requests. The processor bypasses its preprocessing cache for larger requests, but still assigns the same image identity to different encoder outputs. In the reproducer, these outputs contained 1,023 and 421 embeddings.

Include the cropping mode in raw-image cache identities through _get_mm_hashes(). Precomputed image embeddings retain their existing identities.

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Gate FlashInfer all-reduce on 16-byte row widths
author: fuscof-ibm
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

FlashInfer's fused all-reduce cannot run every tensor shape and [`should_use_fi_ar`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ef5bcaa387632c9943f1e1cd0716354d75b99285/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py#L469) checks all the kernel requirements. However, this is not complete as it never validated row width, so a tensor whose row is not a whole number of 16-byte vectors passed the gate and reached a kernel that cannot run it. On the MNNVL backend this kills the worker; on the trtllm backend, which has no equivalent assert, it truncates its indexing and silently returns wrong results. This PR adds the missing check so these reductions fall back to NCCL.

Mamba2 with `mamba_n_groups=1` hits this at TP>1 (see [`mamba_mixer2.py:144`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/87b804f09d698bdcc5dc53062d2058d7faad08ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L144)). Since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52998 made `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` default to on, hybrid models using Mamba2 layers such as `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` cannot start out of the box.

To reproduce on `main`:

```
vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

fails to start on main (49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4) with the following message:

```
(EngineCore pid=2676902) ERROR 10-20 09:35:05 [core.py:1545] RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Check failed: token_dim % (sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type)) == 0 (1 vs. 0) : token_dim must be divisible by 4', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
(EngineCore pid=2676902) ERROR 10-20 09:35:09 [multiproc_executor.py:315] Worker proc VllmWorker-0 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor.
```

However, it starts correctly with the VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER disabled:

```
VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 \
  vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

CC: @njhill @tdoublep @jeejeelee 

## Claims

- Granite-4 (and any Mamba2 model with `n_groups == 1`) starts at TP>1 with the default FlashInfer all-reduce, instead of dying in `determine_available_memory`.
- Closes a silent-correctness hole on the trtllm backend, which vectorizes the same way but validates nothing.
- Pure gating change: shapes the kernel already accepted take exactly the same path as before. Only shapes that previously crashed now fall back.

## Validation

- **End-to-end.** On main, the serve command above does not start unless FlashInfer all-reduce is disabled:

```
VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 \
  vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

starts as expected. With this PR, the same command *without* the env var starts and serves.

Both the failure and the fix were exercised on the default `auto` backend, which resolves to mnnvl on this 8x H100 box. Similar results for a 2x GB200.

- **Unit test.** `tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_all_reduce.py` covers the shape/dtype combinations the gate has to separate:

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_all_reduce.py -v
```

| shape | dtype | row bytes | accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(16, 1)` | fp32 | 4 | no |
| `(16, 2)` | fp32 | 8 | no |
| `(16, 1)` | bf16 | 2 | no |
| `(16, 4)` | bf16 | 8 | no |
| `(16, 4)` | fp32 | 16 | yes |
| `(16, 8)` | bf16 | 16 | yes |
| `(16, 4096)` | bf16 | 8192 | yes |

The change only diverts shapes that previously aborted the worker onto the NCCL path, which is the default reduction when the FlashInfer all-reduce is off. Shapes the kernel already accepted are unaffected, so there is no numerical delta to measure.

## Details

### Root cause

FlashInfer's fused all-reduce kernels load each token row as a `float4`, so a row must be a whole number of 16-byte vectors. The MNNVL kernel enforces this with a throwing TVM FFI `ICHECK` ([`trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cu:59-60`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/csrc/trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cu#L59-L60)):

```cpp
TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(token_dim % (sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type)), 0)
    << "token_dim must be divisible by " << sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type);
```

The divisor is dtype-dependent — 4 for fp32, 8 for fp16/bf16 — so the observed "token_dim must be divisible by 4" is the fp32 instantiation of the general rule, not a fixed bound. The trtllm path vectorizes the same way (`reinterpret_cast<float4*>` indexed as `hidden_dim / VEC_SIZE`) but carries no equivalent assert, so an undersized dim there truncates its indexing instead of aborting.

`should_use_fi_ar` validated device, rank, contiguity, dtype and workspace capacity, but never row width. A narrow tensor therefore passed the gate and the throwing assert killed the worker instead of the communicator falling back to NCCL.

Mamba2 with `mamba_n_groups=1` hits this at TP>1. The gated RMSNorm parallelizes over the reduction dim and all-reduces an fp32 `(num_tokens, 1)` partial sum ([`mamba_mixer2.py:143-144`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L143-L144)):

```python
local_sums = x.pow(2).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
global_sums = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(local_sums)
```

A row of one fp32 is 4 bytes, so the kernel rejects it and the engine dies inside `determine_available_memory`.

### Why nobody hit this earlier

Both halves predate the user-visible breakage:

| when | what | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-02-22 | `n_groups == 1` TP all-reduce added to `Mixer2RMSNormGated` | #13660 |
| 2026-02-26 | `should_use_fi_ar` reaches current form, no row-width check | #34109 |
| 2026-08-20 | `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` flipped `0` → `1` | #52998 |

The narrow shape and the unvalidated gate coexisted for ~6 months, reachable only by users who explicitly opted in. #52998 exposed the bug rather than creating it.

### Why gate, rather than fix the caller

A caller-side flatten in `mamba_mixer2.py` would be smaller, and there is precedent for it — see #44983 below. Two reasons to prefer the gate:

- **It is not Mamba2's bug.** Any caller reducing a narrow fp32 tensor hits the same kernel constraint. The gate's job is to decide which shapes the kernel can run, and it was answering that question incompletely.
- **The trtllm path needs it regardless.** A caller-side fix for Granite leaves these shapes silently corrupting results on the backend with no assert.

A `try`/`except` fallback would be worse than either: a rank that catches the assert and falls back while its peers proceed deadlocks the collective. The fix has to be a deterministic predicate that all ranks evaluate identically.

### Relation to MiniMax, #44983

MiniMax has a structurally identical reduction — a per-token fp32 variance all-reduced across TP inside an RMSNorm — and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44983 fixed it caller-side by flattening before the reduction ([`rms_norm_tp.py:41`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4/vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/rms_norm_tp.py#L41)), relying on the `len(shape) != 2` check in `should_use_fi_ar` to keep 1-D inputs off the FlashInfer path.


## Not a duplicate

Checked per `AGENTS.md`:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "flashinfer all reduce"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "should_use_fi_ar"
```

No open PR adds a row-alignment check, so this is not a duplicate. Three open PRs are nearby, and two touch the same file:

- **#55973** — fixes FlashInfer fused all-reduce when NVLink multicast is unavailable. Same file, but entirely inside `get_fi_ar_workspace` (it caches unsupported workspace configurations and bails out during CUDA graph capture).
  It does not touch `should_use_fi_ar`. Complementary rather than overlapping: it makes workspace *creation* failures survivable, this makes a *shape* the kernel rejects survivable.
- **#53852** — honours an explicit FlashInfer size override on H200. Same file, and it rewrites the `max_workspace_size` assignment in `__init__` immediately above this change. Textually adjacent, semantically independent (it decides *how big* the workspace is, this decides *which shapes* are eligible), but expect a trivial rebase if it merges first.
- **#60011** — makes `--disable-custom-all-reduce` fall back to NCCL. A different switch, does not touch this file, and does not address shapes the kernel rejects.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Catch async lookup iterator errors
author: HaiQiao-Wang
body:
## Overview

Catch errors raised while *consuming* the `batch_lookup` iterator in tiering `AsyncLookupManager`, so a lazy backend failure resolves the request group as misses instead of losing the whole batch and stalling worker progress. Follows the issue addressed by closed, unmerged PR #59187.

## Claims

- An exception raised mid-iteration of `batch_lookup` (not just on the initial call) now resolves that request group as misses instead of dropping the batch.
- Healthy request groups in the same batch, and subsequent batches, keep making progress.
- Regression tests cover both a failure before the first result and after a partial result.

## Validation

- New regression test fails without the fix and passes with it:
  - Without fix: `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py::TestAsyncLookupManager::test_iterator_failure_returns_misses_and_preserves_progress` → `2 failed` (`fail_after=0` and `fail_after=1`).
  - With fix: full file passes.
- Full test file: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py -q` → `22 passed`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on both changed files → passed.

## Details

### Root cause

The lookup worker calls `self.batch_lookup(keys, req_context)` inside a `try`, but `batch_lookup` may return a lazy iterator (it is typed `Iterable[bool]`). Before this change, an exception raised by the backend *during iteration* escaped the `try` (which only guards the call), aborted the entire lookup-worker loop iteration, and dropped the results of all healthy request groups in the same batch. Following batches never got submitted, so worker progress stalled.

```text
Before: batch_lookup(...) returns generator -> zip() raises OSError outside try -> whole batch lost, worker loop breaks
After:  list(batch_lookup(...)) inside try -> OSError caught -> failing group resolves as misses, healthy groups proceed
```

### Implementation

A one-line change: materialize the iterator inside the `try` via `list(self.batch_lookup(keys, req_context))`, so full consumption happens where the existing exception handler applies. The `except` branch already resolves the group as misses (`hits = (False for _ in keys)`), preserving prior behavior for call-time failures. `hits` is consumed exactly once downstream (`zip`), so materializing to a list has no side effects.

### Not a duplicate

- #59187 addressed the same failure mode but was closed unmerged.
- Open PR #61988 scopes lookup verdicts per request on failed promotions (`mark_miss` isolation); it does not cover iterator-consumption errors. #61717 covers re-probing for new requests, also unrelated.

- [x] Design Fit: 1-line change in tiering code (non-default path); no new abstractions.
- [x] Testing and Validation: reproducer tests fail without the fix, pass with it.
- [x] Code Quality and Style: ruff clean.
- [x] Pull Request Contents: root cause, evidence, and duplicate check included.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Validate gfx942's int4 expert requant as int4
author: xaguilar-amd
body:
## Overview

Since #59042, Kimi-K3 with `--quantization-config '{"moe": {"weight": "int4_per_group_32"}}'` fails at startup on gfx942. This PR changes the fail-closed MoE experts check so it validates gfx942's load-time int4 requant as int4.

## Claims

- Kimi-K3 with the int4 expert requant starts and serves on gfx942 again.
- MXFP4 backend selection is unchanged for every other model and GPU.

## Validation

All runs on 8x MI325X (gfx942).

- **Before:** `upstream/main` (`87b804f09d`) fails in `Mxfp4MoEMethod._setup_kernel_k3_situ_gfx942`. I reproduced it by calling `_validate_mxfp4_experts_config(AiterMxfp4Experts, <K3 SiTU MoE config>, AITER_MXFP4_BF16)` on the device:
  ```
  ValueError: AiterMxfp4Experts does not support this MoE deployment since kernel does not support quantization scheme QuantKey(u8,scale(u8,static,GroupShape(row=1, col=32)),symmetric)xNone.
  ```
  With this change the same call passes.
- **Serving:** `vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 -tp 8 --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}'`, with DSpark (k=7) and stock decode.
  - The server starts, requantizes the experts, logs `Using AiterMxfp4Experts`, and runs AITER's `flydsl_moe*_abf16_wint4` kernels.
  - GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 1) scores 0.9575 ± 0.0056 on both strict and flexible extract.
- **Tests:** two new tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`. Both fake the arch, so any ROCm CI machine covers every arch.
  - `test_aiter_mxfp4_experts_quant_scheme_support_by_arch`: `AiterMxfp4Experts` accepts MXFP4 on gfx950 only and int4 on gfx942 only.
  - `test_mxfp4_experts_check_accepts_aiter_deployments`: the fail-closed check accepts every AITER MXFP4 backend on each arch it is deployed on, plus the gfx942 Kimi-K3 int4 requant.
  - `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k "quant_scheme_support or check_accepts_aiter"` gives 13 passed. On `upstream/main`, exactly the two gfx942 int4 cases fail (2 failed, 11 passed), one with the `ValueError` above.
  - `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_gfx942_int4.py` gives 7 passed.

## Details

- **Root cause:** #51274 requantizes K3's MXFP4 experts to packed int4 (`kInt4Static32`, bf16 activations) on gfx942. It builds the kernel with `make_mxfp4_moe_kernel(experts_cls=AiterMxfp4Experts)`.
  - #59042, a CUTLASS FP4 expert-parallel fix, added `_validate_mxfp4_experts_config` at the top of that shared function. The check validates an experts class with the first of `_MXFP4_SCHEME_CANDIDATES` the class supports. If none match, it falls back to the MXFP4 keys.
  - The AITER experts accept MXFP4 keys on gfx950 only. #60322 kept that rule when it split `AiterExperts` into per-quant classes.
  - So on gfx942 no candidate matched, and the check rejected the int4 experts.
- **Fix:** `AiterMxfp4Experts` accepts `(kInt4Static32, None)` on gfx942 only, and that pair is appended as the last candidate.
  - The oracle's backend selection passes `kMxfp4Static` explicitly, so it is unaffected.
  - Classes that support an MXFP4 key still pick that key first, so gfx950 is unchanged.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to develop this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Release the warmup memory cached on the capture streams
author: xqoasis
body:
## Overview

Empty the caching allocator once at the end of the Model Runner V2 `capture_model()`, before it reads free memory, so that warmup activations cached on the discarded capture streams are released. Fixes #63052.

## Claims

- With breakable CUDA graphs and no FULL graphs (`cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`), the largest warmup's activations stay reserved on the capture stream for the life of the process and are reported as CUDA graph memory. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill (GB200, DP4) that is 10.49 GiB per rank; this PR releases it.
- Modes with FULL graphs already end in this state, because `torch.cuda.graph()` empties the cache before each FULL capture.
- 3 lines; graph pools and allocated memory are unchanged.

## Validation

GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill, DP4, `max_model_len` 1M, breakable graphs with capture sizes up to 16384 tokens, v0.32.0-based build. Per rank, at the end of `capture_model()`, with the default-pool segments of `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` grouped by stream:

| | `PIECEWISE` (`main`) | `PIECEWISE` + `empty_cache()` at the end | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (`main`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| model capture stream: reserved (in use) | 7.93 (1.77) GiB | 2.43 (1.77) GiB | 2.43 (1.77) GiB |
| replay capture stream: reserved (in use) | 6.65 (1.65) GiB | 1.70 (1.65) GiB | 1.70 (1.65) GiB |
| graph capture memory (free-memory delta) | 26.39 GiB | 15.90 GiB | 21.00 GiB |
| `memory_allocated()` at the end | 119.12 GiB | 119.12 GiB | 119.16 GiB |

- The first two columns differ by 10.49 GiB per rank, all of it cached warmup memory. The graph pools (5.63 + 5.18 GiB), the allocated memory, and a smoke test are the same in both.
- The middle column comes from a diagnostic run that calls `empty_cache()` at the same point, after taking the snapshot above. This exact commit has not been run on a GPU.
- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` also captures 44 FULL decode graphs and 39 FULL DSpark graphs, so its total is higher; its capture streams end up in the same state as the middle column.

No test is added: the effect needs a breakable PIECEWISE capture whose warmup is large enough to matter, and CI has no runner for that configuration.

## Details

**Root cause.**

1. `capture_model()` empties the cache once before capturing, and reads free memory at the end without emptying it again.
2. Each `CudaGraphManager.capture()` enters `graph_capture()`, which creates a new stream, and runs every size eagerly once before capturing it. The caching allocator keeps the freed warmup blocks on that stream. Sizes are captured largest first, so the cache ends up holding the largest warmup's peak, and nothing allocates on that stream afterwards.
3. `capture_model()` runs under `freeze_gc_for_cudagraph_capture()`. While gc is frozen, breakable capture skips its per-descriptor `gc.collect()` + `empty_cache()` (#54646).
4. With FULL graphs, `torch.cuda.graph.__enter__` empties the cache before each FULL capture and releases these blocks as a side effect. With PIECEWISE only, nothing does.

The blocks are released only when some caching-allocator allocation fails and the allocator frees all cached blocks to retry. Allocations outside the caching allocator (NCCL, NVSHMEM, CUDA module loading) see the memory as used.

**KV budget.** `profile_cudagraph_memory()` measures `capture_model(profile_only=True)`, so the CUDA graph estimate subtracted from the KV budget also includes these blocks today; with this change it no longer does (from reading the code; the KV cache size was not measured). This complements #59368, which measures the graph pool for the estimate: with #59368 alone, the estimate would exclude this cache while the real capture still holds it.

**Tradeoff.** As noted in #50780, on a model whose profile run under-counts long-prefill activations, these cached blocks acted as reclaimable headroom. With this change that memory goes to the KV cache instead, which is the state `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` already ends in.

Related: #62965 (the decoder replay graphs' separate stream and pool).
