title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply batch tool_choice rules to streamed tool calls
author: hickeyma
body:
## Overview

Streaming chat now drops tool calls in the same cases batch does. Fixes #63346. Follow-up to #63148 which listed this as not covered.

#42752 fixed #42747 for `"none"` but only inside `DelegatingParser`. Two cases still slip through on main:

- gpt-oss with `"none"`: `HarmonyParser` isn't a `DelegatingParser` so the guard never runs.
- `null` with any parser: nothing gates it, so streaming keeps tool calls while batch drops them.

This PR moves the rule into one place that batch and streaming both call, so it no longer depends on each parser.

## Claims

- With `stream: true`, `/v1/chat/completions` now follows the same `tool_choice` rules as batch. gpt-oss (Harmony) with `"none"` and any tool parser with `null` stop returning tool calls. This PR doesn't decide what `null` should mean, it only makes streaming match batch.
- Streaming `/v1/chat/completions/derender` gets the same fix because it uses the same `ChatStreamProcessor`.
- `finish_reason` is `stop` in those cases, not `tool_calls`.
- No change for `"auto"`, `"required"` or named tools. Anthropic and Cohere turn `null` into `"auto"` when tools are set, so they're not affected.

## Validation

Reproduced before the fix at main `ccd4e4030f`, `temperature: 0` with the `auto` row as a control:

```text
--- gpt-oss-20b (openai parser), tool_choice="none"
  chat stream (auto)   tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls

--- Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (hermes), tool_choice=null
  chat stream (auto)   tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
```

After the fix:

```text
--- gpt-oss-20b (openai parser), tool_choice="none"
  chat stream (auto)   tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=[]               finish=stop

--- Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (hermes), tool_choice=null
  chat stream (auto)   tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
```

The `auto` control still streams the tool call which means nothing extra is dropped.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_stream_processor.py \
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_message_assembly.py \
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py \
tests/tool_use/mistral/test_mistral_tool_calls.py -v
```

New and changed tests:

- `test_drops_tool_calls_like_non_streaming`: `"none"` and `null`, with a mixed content and tool call delta and a tool call only delta.
- `test_e2e_harmony_tool_choice_none_drops_tool_calls`: now also runs with `stream: true` against the real gpt-oss render server.
- `test_derender_stream.py`: the `_FakeParser` fixture now has auto tools on. One test sent no tools with the default `tool_choice: "none"` and still expected tool calls, so it relied on this bug. It now sends `"auto"`.

No model eval. Generation doesn't change, only which parsed fields are returned.

No docs change. `tool_calling.md` already says `"none"` returns no tool calls.

## Details

`ChatStreamProcessor` passed `parse_delta()` output straight through and relied on the parser to check `tool_choice`. Not every parser does. `HarmonyParser` ignores `"none"` and the base `Parser` treats `null` like `"auto"`. Non-streaming doesn't have this problem because `assemble_chat_message_fields()` applies the rule itself.

The rule now lives in `keeps_tool_calls()` and both paths call it. `ChatStreamProcessor` takes `enable_auto_tools` and `parser_cls` as required keyword arguments, so a new caller can't skip them by accident.

When tool calls are dropped, the stream sends nothing for them. That matches batch which returns `content: ""`. Whether `"none"` should return tool-call-shaped text as content is #55080 and this PR doesn't change that. If a delta is empty after stripping, the processor returns `None`. Both callers already skip sending a `None` delta, the same way they handle hidden reasoning.

## Related PRs

- #42752 (merged): gates `"none"` in `DelegatingParser` only. This PR covers what that misses.
- #42868: targets the old `serving.py` streaming code which has since moved to `ChatStreamProcessor`. Obsolete and conflicting.
- #55089 / #55080: whether tool-call-shaped text should come back as content when tools are off. Out of scope here.
- #54321: makes an explicit `null` behave like an omitted field, so `"auto"` when tools are set. Complementary to this PR. If it lands, both paths follow it.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor --response-role and echo in chat derender
author: hickeyma
body:
## Overview

Chat derender always returned `role: "assistant"` and ignored `echo`, so it didn't match `/v1/chat/completions` for the same tokens. This fixes that for `/v1/chat/completions/derender` (batch and stream) and adds `--response-role` to generate `output_mode: "derender"` (batch and stream).

Fixes #63356. Related: #56851, #63103, #63148.

**Depends on #63434. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63434#issuecomment-6579638244.**

## Claims

- `/derender` returns the same role as chat: `--response-role` or the last message's role when `add_generation_prompt` is false.
- `/derender` supports `echo` for text content. In batch it's prepended to `content`. In a stream it goes at the start of the first chunk, along with the role.
- Generate `output_mode: "derender"` uses `--response-role`, in batch and on the first chunk of each choice in a stream.
- `vllm serve` and `vllm launch render` both pass `--response-role` to the derenderer.
- Chat serving, batch chat and derender share one implementation of the role and echo logic.
- `add_generation_prompt: false` with empty `messages` returns `--response-role` instead of a 500.

## Validation

New unit tests cover batch (with and without a parser), streaming on the plain and parser paths and generate derender. They fail on `main` and pass with this change.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -q

pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_message_assembly.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out -q
```

`test_derender_parity.py` now runs its server with `--response-role` bot, checks role in every batch case, and adds an echo + continue_final_message case. 

## Details

`OnlineDerenderer` had no `response_role` and hardcoded `"assistant"` in five places. The generate stream added in #63103 hardcoded it too. `echo` wasn't handled anywhere.

The role and echo logic moved into `get_chat_response_role()` and `get_echo_content()` in `message_assembly.py`, next to the shared message assembly from #63148.

Streaming doesn't send echo as its own chunk the way chat does. Each derender call returns exactly one chunk, so the echo goes in the same chunk as the role and `role_sent` already tracks it.
`DerenderStreamState` is unchanged. Clients that concatenate deltas get the same text as from chat.

Known limits:

- `/derender` builds echo from the raw `messages`, while chat uses the parsed conversation. Refusal and thinking parts and multimodal placeholders aren't echoed. This is documented in `derenderer.md`.
- Generate derender can't do echo or the last message's role because `parse_context` doesn't carry `messages`, `add_generation_prompt` or `echo`. It's documented in `token_in_token_out.md` and the wire format question is on #63356.
- Harmony `echo: true` still returns a 500. That's not new and is tracked in #XXXXX.

Small change in coupled chat: streaming echo used to pass list content straight into `DeltaMessage.content` which only takes a string. It's now joined into text like the batch path.

Docs: `derenderer.md` says the render server needs the same `--response-role` as the chat server and explains how role and echo work. `token_in_token_out.md` now lists `derender` as an `output_mode` value.

title: [Bugfix][NVFP4] Fix NaN logits and garbage output from uninitialized fused act+quant scales
author: nv-nikitaj
body:
## Overview

Make the fused `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` kernel initialize the padded entries of the swizzled NVFP4 block-scale buffer, as the unfused `scaled_fp4_quant` kernel already does. Fixes a regression from #53568, which switched the scale allocator to `torch.empty` (previously `torch.zeros`, restored in #45739).

## Claims

- Fixes NaN logits and garbage output (`other other other ...`) on NVFP4 checkpoints, e.g. `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4`.
- Fixes HTTP 400 `Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan` on `/v1/chat/completions` with `logprobs`.
- Covers both users of the kernel (the `ActivationQuantFusionPass` and the manual fusion in `fused_act_quant.py`) with no allocator memset.

## Validation

Setup: 8x RTX PRO 4500 (sm120), TP=8, `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4`, FlashInfer-Cutlass NVFP4 linear backend, `fuse_act_quant: True`, built from source with CUDA 13.2.

Repro:

```bash
# 1. Serve (TP=8)
vllm serve nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --served-model-name nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5 --port 8000

# 2. Once the server is up, send 100 chat+logprobs and 100 completions requests
NAME=nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5
echo -n "chat:  "; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /tmp/r_chat_$i.json -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"model\":\"$NAME\",\"logprobs\":true,\"top_logprobs\":1,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are a helpful assistant.\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hello!\"}],\"max_tokens\":100}"; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '; echo
echo -n "compl: "; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /tmp/r_compl_$i.json -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"model\":\"$NAME\",\"prompt\":\"What is the test plan?\",\"logprobs\":2,\"max_tokens\":50,\"temperature\":0}"; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '; echo
echo "nan-errors: $(grep -l 'Out of range float' /tmp/r_*.json | wc -l)"
```

Unit tests: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`, 20 passed (12 existing, 8 new).

## Details

The fused `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` kernel only wrote valid rows of the swizzled block-scale buffer, but the NVFP4 GEMM reads the padded entries, so since #53568 switched the allocator to `torch.empty` it consumed stale memory as scales and produced NaN logits. This PR makes the kernel zero the padded scale rows and columns itself (as `scaled_fp4_quant` does) and keeps the allocators as `torch.empty`, so there is no extra memset.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Size the extensible KV cache from exact VRAM use, not 2 MB-rounded free memory
author: GodRishUniverse
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, `hipMemGetInfo` counts every allocation as at least 2 MB, so after warmup the extensible KV cache (#56492) sizes itself from free memory that looks a few GB smaller than it is. This PR adds that memory back once, at the final sizing, using amdgpu's exact VRAM count. Only unpartitioned discrete ROCm GPUs are affected.

**Root cause.** The amdgpu driver rounds each allocation up to 2 MB in the free memory it reports, on purpose (commit 1ac354beecfd, "drm/amdgpu: Pessimistic availability based on rounded up allocations"), unless the GPU's memory is kept in system memory (`apu_prefer_gtt`). Its own allocation check uses exact sizes. The many small kernel code objects loaded during warmup therefore hide a few GB. The sysfs counter `mem_info_vram_used` counts exact sizes for the whole device.

## Claims

- On an unpartitioned discrete ROCm GPU, the extensible KV cache sizes itself from exact device memory use. On Llama 3.1 8B / R9700 the KV cache went from 51,712 to 76,288 tokens, with no OOM and no failed requests (one run per config).
- The correction is never more than what is physically free and never negative. Other processes' allocations are not added back.
- Integrated GPUs, partitioned GPUs, a missing or mismatched sysfs count, and all non-ROCm platforms keep the current behaviour (no-op platform hooks).

## Validation

Unit tests (the sysfs lookup and correction arithmetic need no GPU; the GPU tests skip off ROCm):

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_rocm_vram_lookup.py tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/v1/worker/test_rocm_device_memory.py
```

On a ROCm GPU (Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201). `--optional` adds tests that allocate all but 256 MB of the corrected free memory, both as 64 MB / 2 MB torch blocks and as one `ExtensibleTensor` chunk (the `defragment=True` case):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_rocm_device_memory.py --optional
```

Serving comparison, main vs this PR, with a fresh compile cache for each run:

```bash
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos \
  --request-rate inf --seed 0 --max-concurrency 128 --num-prompts 1280
# repeated with --max-concurrency 256 --num-prompts 2560
```

Llama 3.1 8B, TP1, Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32 GB), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97`. One run per config, so there is no variability figure:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| KV cache | 51,712 tokens | 76,288 tokens (+48%) |
| Output tok/s, concurrency 128 / 256 | 918.9 / 905.5 | 1,054.0 / 1,026.9 |
| Median TTFT, concurrency 128 / 256 | 3,934 / 25,195 ms | 1,084 / 17,110 ms |
| Most memory used / allowed | 24.6 / 31.1 GB | 27.8 / 31.1 GB |
| Failed requests / OOM | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Not yet done:
- KV cache size across several starts.
- Multi-GPU, CDNA (MI300/MI355) and spec decode. I only have access to an R9700.


**Limitations.**
- `gpu_memory_utilization` now bounds exact use on unpartitioned discrete ROCm GPUs.
- Several instances on one GPU: with the extensible cache on, `request_memory` skips the startup check. An earlier instance's rounding is already in a later instance's baseline and is never added back, so a later instance gets a smaller cache, depending on start order. This doesn't cause OOM.
- KFD's page-table reserve and RAS pages are not in the exact count (about 80 MB on R9700). The 3 GB ROCm margin floor (#65418) covers them.
- Tested on R9700 (gfx1201) only. CDNA should behave the same according to the driver code, but this is unverified. In AMD CI, `tests/v1/worker` runs on `mi355_dpx` (partitioned, so it falls back), but other jobs run on `mi300_1` / `mi355_1`. I don't know whether those pools are partitioned. If they aren't, this path runs there untested, and the correction could be limited to validated GPUs.
- The V1 runner and `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` are unchanged.

**Not a duplicate.** I found no other open PR correcting ROCm's 2 MB-rounded free memory. #65413 (merged) corrects UMA free memory and is the fallback inside the new hook. #55828 (open) changes which memory counts as this process's own and only takes effect on NVML. No runtime overlap and either merge order works.

**Related:** #56492 (extensible KV cache), #65413 (UMA free-memory correction), #65418 (ROCm 3 GiB margin floor), #55828 (process-scoped KV sizing), #60121 (asynchronous VRAM release on ROCm).

**Note:** From my understanding, `amdsmi_get_gpu_memory_usage` reads the same `mem_info_vram_used` so `amdsmi` and `sysfs` should be the same but if it can't be read then it will ask KFD and will again use 2MB rounded values that hipMemGetInfo reports.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Pass zero positions to the fused MLA decode q-prep kernel
author: seungrokj
body:
## Purpose
Fixes a large accuracy regression for Kimi-K3 on ROCm when DCP is off (dcp1). It comes from the fused decode q-prep path added in #59634.

`KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._fused_decode` gives AITER's `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` a **one-row** identity cos/sin cache (K3 is NoPE). It also passes the **real** token positions, assuming the kernel clamps them into the cache.

That assumption is false on AITER v0.1.26. DeepSeek-shaped inputs now go to the head-grouped `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla_seg_kernel<PAGE_SIZE=0>`, which only clamps on the DCP (`compute_all_q_rope`) path:
- **One head per block**, i.e. every small decode batch (`T*H/num_CU <= 32`): cos/sin reads past the cache return 0. For every token at position ≥ 1, q_pe is written as **all zeros** and a wrong k_pe goes into the KV cache. This is silent.
- **More heads per block**: the kernel reads past the allocation and can fault (see ROCm/aiter#6879).

Since the RoPE here is the identity, position 0 gives exactly the right result for every token. This PR passes a preallocated all-zeros positions buffer, sliced to the kernel's token count (taken from `slot_mapping`). That removes the dependency on any AITER clamp behaviour.
- The buffer is allocated once in `__init__` as a non-persistent buffer, so captured CUDA graphs need no extra per-layer memset.
- The now-unused `positions` argument of `_fused_decode` is dropped.
- The comment that wrongly said the kernel clamps is corrected.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Make compile_mm_encoder work for RADIO/NaViT encoders
author: HangruiCao2000
body:
FIX #63414, where the bug is:
Serving nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse with --compilation-config.compile_mm_encoder true kills
the engine on the first image request, and the server stops answering entirely
(Connection refused afterwards — it is a fatal EngineDeadError, not a per-request 500):

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'cu_seqlens'
  vllm/model_executor/models/radio.py:501 in forward   (under torch._dynamo.aot_compile)
EngineCore encountered a fatal error -> **EngineDeadError**

```
## Purpose of this PR

`--compilation-config.compile_mm_encoder true` does nothing for RADIO. Since the encoder
was rewritten to standalone modules (#58468), `RadioLayer` carries no
`@support_torch_compile`, so the flag is silently a no-op for `Nemotron-3.5-Parse`,
`Nemotron-Parse-2.0` and `nano_nemotron_vl` — the encoder is never compiled and nothing
says so.

Simply decorating the layer does not work either. Three independent static-shape
assumptions are in the way, each only visible once the previous one is fixed:

1. **Wrong dynamic dim.** RADIO packs NaViT tokens into dim 1, so marking dim 0 (the
   value inherited from InternVL before the refactor) bakes the packed length.
2. **Varlen metadata is unaddressable.** `dynamic_arg_dims` keys by argument name, and
   `cu_seqlens` was wrapped in the `MaskMetadata` dataclass, so its length could not be
   marked dynamic. It now travels as tensor arguments.
3. **Traced vs runtime mismatch.** `mask_meta` was built only when more than one image
   was present. Encoder profiling uses 2 items, so tracing saw an object while real
   single-image requests passed `None`. A no-guards graph keeps whichever form it traced
   and drops the other **silently** — measured below. When the layer is compiled, every
   call now carries metadata: one image gives `cu_seqlens [0, n]` (unmasked attention
   over a single sequence), and a uniform `[B, n, C]` batch is packed the way the conv3d
   video path already did.

Two things that review caught and this PR now does deliberately:

- **Packing only happens when the layer is compiled.** TORCH_SDPA does not synthesise
  `cu_seqlens` the way the FlashAttention and Triton wrappers do — handed a packed
  sequence it splits it and runs one attention call per item. Always packing cost a
  uniform batch B calls per layer instead of one (B=8, 2 layers: 16 `apply_sdpa` calls
  vs 2, bit-identical output), plus a `.tolist()` host sync per layer; a 128-frame video
  chunk would be 128 launches per layer. A consistent `cu_seqlens` form is only required
  for the no-guards graph, so uncompiled the batch stays unpacked and the default path is
  unchanged from main.
- **Only dim 1 is marked dynamic.** Every path reaching the compiled layer packs to
  `[1, total, C]`, and torch specializes a size-1 dim to 1 even when it is marked
  dynamic, so listing dim 0 bought nothing and implied a batch dim that cannot vary.
  Correctness rests on the batch-1 invariant, which is now asserted once in
  `RadioVisionEncoder.forward` so an unpacked caller fails on a clear precondition
  instead of a size/stride assert deep inside inductor.

Building the metadata must not copy host memory: `torch.tensor(list, device=cuda)` is a
blocking host sync on every encoder forward, which `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` rejects.
Uniform batches use a device-side `arange`; the variable-length helper stages through
pinned memory.

`RadioVisionEncoder.forward` keeps its `MaskMetadata`-facing signature and unpacks once,
so `nemotron_parse3_5` and `nano_nemotron_vl` need no changes.

## Test Plan

Dedicated 1-GPU H100 jobs, one per variant, image built from `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`
(`0.33.0rc1.dev229`, torch `2.14.0+cu130`) with the refactored RADIO files overlaid from
main, so the stock arm is exactly upstream and the only difference between images is this
PR. Each image verifies its own `radio.py` sha before running. Nemotron-3.5-Parse, 3
document images, greedy, four arms per variant covering both ViT attention backends.

## Test Result

Adding the SPDA check for this

```
stock (main)   RadioLayer decorated: False
  off      FLASH_ATTN  requests OK | alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0
  on       FLASH_ATTN  requests OK | alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0
  sdpa_off TORCH_SDPA  requests OK | alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0
  sdpa_on  TORCH_SDPA  requests OK | alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0

this PR        RadioLayer decorated: True
  off      FLASH_ATTN  requests OK | alive | compile mentions 0  | errors 0
  on       FLASH_ATTN  requests OK | alive | compile mentions 85 | errors 0
  sdpa_off TORCH_SDPA  requests OK | alive | compile mentions 0  | errors 0
  sdpa_on  TORCH_SDPA  requests OK | alive | compile mentions 85 | errors 0
             (both compiled arms run with VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error)
```

The flag is a no-op on main — 0 compile mentions with it on, on either backend. With this
PR the encoder really compiles:

```
RadioLayer] Compiling a graph for compile range (1, 2147483647) takes 2.21 s
RadioLayer] Dynamo bytecode transform time: 0.33 s
```

**No behaviour change with the flag off, on either backend** — served text is
byte-identical to main:

```
off       stock=4bb7b431 9ff45c59 ab96d7f8   PR=4bb7b431 9ff45c59 ab96d7f8   3/3
sdpa_off  stock=4bb7b431 3cac4d5d a3c3f497   PR=4bb7b431 3cac4d5d a3c3f497   3/3
```

The silently-dropped-mask failure in point 3 is measured, not inferred. On a compiled
layer (reference spread `max|masked - unmasked| = 0.5742`):

```
traced with a cu_seqlens tensor, then called with None:
  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'
traced with None, then called with a cu_seqlens tensor:
  max|out - correct| = 0.5742   max|out - traced-form| = 0.0469  -> mask silently dropped
```

Packing a uniform batch is bit-exact on the FlashAttention wrapper, which flattens the
batch and synthesises this very `cu_seqlens` when it is omitted:

```
attn backend: FLASH_ATTN
B=4 n=30: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control, one big sequence: 0.9404)
B=8 n=64: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control: 0.8105)
B=2 n=97: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control: 0.3828)
```

On TORCH_SDPA it is not free, which is why packing is gated on the layer being compiled:

```
compile_mm_encoder=False -> pack_uniform_batches=False | apply_sdpa calls = 2   (same as main)
compile_mm_encoder=True  -> pack_uniform_batches=True  | apply_sdpa calls = 16  (opt-in only)
```

On the size-1 dim, checked with `error_on_recompile` (a plain `torch.compile` recompiles
silently and hides this), torch 2.14.0: marking `[0, 1]` and marking `[1]` specialize
dim 0 identically, so dim 0 was inert.

### Performance

Dedicated pod, all arms on the same GPU, interleaved round-robin, 4 rounds, 64 distinct
DocVQA pages per experiment. 

For the page/s and TTFT at c = 16, we see some performance gain. This PR fix the issue without impacting anything and brings performance gain in some cases

| metric | stock off | this PR off | this PR on | A/A noise floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TTFT p50 @ c=1 | 286.1 ms | 285.1 (-0.4%) | 287.3 (+0.4%) | 5.10% |
| TPOT p50 @ c=1 | 1.655 ms | 1.632 (-1.3%) | 1.635 (-1.2%) | 6.42% |
| pages/s @ c=16 | 5.892 | 6.209 (+5.4%) | 6.323 (+7.3%) | 2.83% |
| TTFT p50 @ c=16 | 2338.9 ms | 2200.0 (-5.9%) | 2149.7 (-8.1%) | 8.77% |


### Coverage

Also validated on **Nemotron-Parse-2.0** and **nano_nemotron_vl**
(NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16, B=13/B=32 tiles): with the flag off this PR is
byte-identical to main on both, and an in-situ probe inside the live model shows the
encoder output is bit-exact between the packed and unpacked paths
(`max|packed-unpacked| = 0.000000e+00`).

## Behaviour note

Enabling the flag changes the output for some pages. The first difference is always a
bounding-box coordinate of ~0.001 normalised (1-2 px), but under greedy decoding that can
rewrite the rest of a long generation, so similarity ranges from 1.000 to 0.43 by page.
This is **torch.compile on the encoder, not the varlen path**: with the flag off this PR
is byte-identical to main on all three models and on both attention backends, and
`cu_seqlens [0, n]` for one image is bit-exact against unmasked attention. Flagging it
since the flag is opt-in.

title: [Bugfix][CUDA Graph] Weak-ref nested outputs of captured graphs
author: ZJY0516
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`weak_ref_tensors` only weak-refs one level. For a model output like `(hidden_states, [aux_hidden_states, ...])`, the inner list is returned as is, so every captured CUDA graph entry keeps its aux hidden states alive and the graph pool cannot reuse that memory for the next capture size. This PR makes `weak_ref_tensors` recurse into nested lists/tuples.

Related: #63406 lists this as "aux hidden states kept by every PIECEWISE size" in its memory breakdown. This PR is the standalone fix and also applies to main's capture sizes.

## Claims

- Captured graphs no longer pin the aux hidden states used by EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash and `extract_hidden_states`. Before, each captured size leaked `num_aux × num_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size` bytes (3 × 8192 × 4096 × 2 B = 192 MiB for one 8192-token size of DeepSeek-V4-Flash).
- No output change: the outputs alias the same memory as before; only the references held by the graph entries become weak.
- `weak_ref_tensors` now raises on unknown types at any nesting level, not only at the top level, and passes ints and `LayerName`s through (piecewise subgraph outputs can contain ints, and Inductor graph partition outputs can contain `LayerName`s, see below).

## Validation

**Unit test** (`tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py`, run by the "Async Engine, Inputs, Utils, Worker" CI step), on GB200:

```
# with this PR
pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py -v
39 passed

# torch_utils.py reverted to main, new tests only
pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py -v -k weak_ref
FAILED test_weak_ref_tensors_does_not_keep_nested_tensors_alive
E       AssertionError: assert 4194304 == (8388608 - 8388608)
FAILED test_weak_ref_tensors_rejects_unknown_nested_types
E       Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError
```

**What actually reaches `weak_ref_tensors`.** I wrapped the function in `vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py` and `vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`, then started each engine and recorded the structure of every input during capture (`T` = tensor; `[n:...]` = list of length n; `(n:...)` = tuple of length n):

| Model | CUDA graph path | Inputs seen |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B + EAGLE3 | torch.compile piecewise | `[1:T]` `[2:T]` `[4:T]` `[5:T]` `[6:T]` |
| Qwen3-1.7B + EAGLE3 | breakable | target `(2:T,[3:T])`, drafter `(2:T)` |
| gpt-oss-20b + EAGLE3 | torch.compile piecewise | `[1:T]` `[2:T]` `[5:T]` `[6:T]` |
| gpt-oss-20b + EAGLE3 | breakable | target `(2:T,[3:T])`, drafter `(2:T)` |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | torch.compile piecewise | `[1:T]` `[5:T]` `[6:T,int]` |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | breakable | `T` |

The nested case is the breakable target output with aux hidden states. The int case is a piecewise subgraph output of the FP8 MoE model, which is why ints are passed through. No `None`, float or 0-size tensor showed up.

The table does not cover `use_inductor_graph_partition=True`. There, on torch >= 2.11, `CUDAGraphWrapper` wraps each Inductor partition, and a partition's outputs can include `LayerName` objects that torch.compile hoists as graph inputs. This PR's first CI run caught it (`ValueError: Invalid type for tensors: <class 'vllm.utils.torch_utils.LayerName'>` in `test_full_cudagraph.py[*-partition=True]` and `test_full_graph.py::test_custom_compile_config`), so `LayerName`s pass through as well. After the fix, on GB200:

```
pytest compile/fullgraph/test_full_cudagraph.py -k "True and not MLA"
30 passed, 20 skipped (FA3, RocmAttn)

pytest compile/fullgraph/test_full_graph.py -k "compilation_config4 or compilation_config5"
2 passed
```

**End-to-end A/B**: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, TP4+EP, DSpark K=7, 4×GB200. Breakable CUDA graph is on by default for this model, and capture sizes are main's defaults. Main is this PR's parent (2c58be22b6). Memory numbers are from TP rank 0.

| | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph pool, actual | 5.86 GiB | 5.39 GiB | −0.47 GiB |
| CUDA graph pool, profiler estimate | 8.55 GiB | 7.90 GiB | −0.65 GiB |
| Available KV cache memory | 112.94 GiB | 113.59 GiB | +0.65 GiB |
| GPU KV cache size | 7,277,119 tokens | 7,319,402 tokens | +0.58% |
| GSM8K 5-shot, flexible-extract | 0.9560 | 0.9522 | −5 / 1319 questions |
| DSpark acceptance (accepted / drafted) | 57.74% | 57.84% | |
| Mean acceptance length | 5.04 | 5.05 | |

The leak on main is about 0.65 GiB here, and it grows with the number and size of PIECEWISE capture sizes (#63406 raises both).

The 5-question GSM8K gap is from a single run per arm; serving is not batch invariant, so some run-to-run variance is expected. It does not indicate corrupted aux hidden states: they only feed the drafter, so corruption would lower acceptance, and acceptance is unchanged. The target model alone decides the output tokens under greedy rejection sampling.

<details>
<summary>Serve command</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'
```

GSM8K: 5-shot, temperature 0, chat completions, thinking off. Acceptance is read from `vllm:spec_decode_*` metrics after the GSM8K run. Memory numbers come from the `CUDA graph pool memory`, `Available KV cache memory` and `GPU KV cache size` log lines.
</details>

## Details

**Affected paths.** `weak_ref_tensors` is called on capture outputs by:
- `BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper._capture`: captures the whole model forward, so EAGLE3/DSpark targets return `(hidden_states, [aux, ...])`. Breakable CUDA graph is on by default for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, MiniMax-M3, GLM-5-Next, Kimi-K3 and others, under both model runners.
- `CUDAGraphWrapper` in FULL mode on MRV1, which also wraps the whole model.

Not affected: torch.compile piecewise subgraph outputs are flat, and MRV2 FULL graphs copy outputs into persistent buffers instead of weak-refing them.

**Safety of the weak refs.** Once the aux tensors are weak, later captures may reuse their memory, the same as for `hidden_states` today. So the aux tensors must be consumed before the next graph replay. Every consumer copies them first: MRV1 `torch.cat`/`torch.stack` in `gpu_model_runner.py`, MRV2 DFlash `_store_hidden_states` (concatenates into its staging buffer), MRV2 `extract_hidden_states` (`torch.stack` + `copy_`).

**Type contract.** Previously, non-tensor values inside a list/tuple passed through `weak_ref_tensor` silently, which is how the nested list slipped through. Now containers recurse, ints and `LayerName`s pass, and any other type raises with its type name. The tradeoff: a model whose capture output contains a leaf type not in the table above (e.g. `None`) fails at capture time instead of passing silently. The raise already caught one such case before (`IntermediateTensors`, #24275), and caught `LayerName` in this PR's first CI run.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches `weak_ref_tensors` or this leak. #63406 changes capture sizes and only references the leak in its memory accounting.

The fix and analysis originate from Bo Pang (co-author). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the change, the tests and the validation scripts.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep nested-config and YaRN drafts within their rotary cache
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

The draft `max_position_embeddings` override and the V2 model runner's draft `max_model_len` limit both read the draft's top-level `hf_config`. For nested configs such as Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), `max_position_embeddings` and `rope_parameters` live in `hf_text_config`, so neither check fires: the MTP draft keeps a 262,144-row rotary cache while the target serves a longer window, and the engine dies with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`. This PR points both checks at `hf_text_config`, and bounds YaRN drafts by the real size of their rotary cache, `original_max_position_embeddings * factor`, instead of by their `max_position_embeddings`.

Follow-up to #63251 and #58094. Addresses the remaining path of #62383: its YaRN repro is already fixed on `main` by #58094, which forwards the target's YaRN to the draft, but extending the target through `max_position_embeddings` still crashes.

Not a duplicate: #58094 keeps `max_position_embeddings` target-only on purpose (#63909) and does not touch the draft checks. #62409 changes the target's M-RoPE cache size. #59789 grows the non-M-RoPE YaRN cache instead of limiting `max_model_len`, and does not handle nested configs.

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with MTP, served past 262,144 tokens through `text_config.max_position_embeddings`, no longer crashes the engine.
- On the V2 model runner, a draft that receives the target's YaRN through #58094 no longer caps `max_model_len` at its checkpoint `max_position_embeddings`. This fixes a regression from #58094 for flat drafts (DFlash on a YaRN x4 Qwen3-4B target: 40,960 back to 131,072, as before #58094), and keeps the YaRN setup of #62383 at 1,048,576 once the limit reads `hf_text_config` (262,144 otherwise).
- A nested YaRN draft whose cache is shorter than the target's `max_model_len` now limits it to the cache size. On `main` it was not limited.
- Flat drafts with cache-only RoPE types (`default`, `llama3`, ...) behave as on `main`.

## Validation

### End to end

Setup: 2 x NVIDIA B200, driver 615.71.10, torch `2.14.0+cu130`, TP=2 with EP. `main` is `b73373040d` (includes #58094). This PR is `7a5486e0b0` on `e5bec1ddd4`. Both use the same compiled extensions; only the Python sources differ.

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 524288 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"max_position_embeddings":524288}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

<details>
<summary>Clients</summary>

`long_prompt.py PORT N` sends N random token ids to `/v1/completions`, then checks `/health`:

```python
import json, random, sys, urllib.error, urllib.request

port, n = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
random.seed(0)
body = {"model": "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next", "max_tokens": 32, "temperature": 0,
        "prompt": [random.randint(1000, 100000) for _ in range(n)]}
req = urllib.request.Request(base + "/v1/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
try:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
        print("STATUS 200", json.load(r)["usage"])
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    print("STATUS", e.code, e.read().decode()[:300])
try:
    print("health", urllib.request.urlopen(base + "/health", timeout=30).status)
except Exception as e:
    print("health", e)
```

`acceptance.py PORT REPEAT` sends REPEAT filler sentences, generates 512 tokens, and reports the acceptance rate from `/metrics`:

```python
import json, sys, urllib.request

port, repeat = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
pad = "This is a filler sentence containing the number 12345 and some tokens."


def counters():
    text = urllib.request.urlopen(base + "/metrics", timeout=30).read().decode()
    sums = {"draft": 0.0, "accepted": 0.0}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total"):
            sums["draft"] += float(line.split()[-1])
        elif line.startswith("vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total"):
            sums["accepted"] += float(line.split()[-1])
    return sums


before = counters()
body = {"model": "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next", "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0,
        "ignore_eos": True, "prompt": " ".join(f"{pad} {i}" for i in range(repeat))}
req = urllib.request.Request(base + "/v1/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
    usage = json.load(r)["usage"]
after = counters()
drafted = after["draft"] - before["draft"]
accepted = after["accepted"] - before["accepted"]
print(usage["prompt_tokens"], f"acceptance={accepted / drafted:.3f}")
```

</details>

| Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| 205,890-token text, 512 tokens out | 200, acceptance 0.985 | 200, acceptance 0.995 |
| 270,000 tokens | 500, `/health` 503, `EngineDeadError` | 200, `/health` 200 |
| 300,890-token text, 512 tokens out | not run, server dead | 200, acceptance 1.000 |
| 520,000 tokens | not run, server dead | 200, `/health` 200 |

`main` died on the 270,000-token request on 2 of 2 fresh servers, both at `num_computed_tokens=[270000]`: once with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, once with a worker segfault in `cuGraphLaunch`. This PR served all four requests on one server. At startup it logs `Overriding draft model max_position_embeddings from 262144 to the target model's max_model_len (524288)`; `main` does not.

### Config level

Rows of the draft's rotary cache (`get_rope` on the draft's `hf_text_config`) and the `max_model_len` that `VllmConfig` ends up with:

| Setup | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MTP, `text_config.max_position_embeddings` 524,288 | 262,144 rows, serves 524,288: out of bounds | 524,288 rows, serves 524,288 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MTP, the YaRN x4 flags of #62383, 1,048,576 | 1,048,576 rows, serves 1,048,576 | same |
| `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` on Qwen3-4B, YaRN x4, 131,072 | 131,072 rows, serves 40,960 | 131,072 rows, serves 131,072 |

Before #58094, the DFlash row served 131,072. With only the `hf_text_config` change, the two YaRN rows served 262,144 and 40,960.

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_max_position_embeddings.py \
  tests/config/test_speculative_draft_limits_max_model_len.py \
  tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py
```

- With this PR: `50 passed`.
- With `vllm/config/speculative.py` and `speculator_config.py` from `main`: `test_mtp_draft_inherits_target_max_model_len` fails with `assert 262144 == 524288`, and `test_yarn_draft_limits_max_model_len_to_its_rotary_cache` fails for `mtp-nested-x2` (`assert 1048576 == 524288`) and `dflash-x4` (`assert 40960 == 131072`). `mtp-nested-x4` passes on `main` only because the limit reads the top-level config.
- With only the `hf_text_config` change: all three cases of `test_yarn_draft_limits_max_model_len_to_its_rotary_cache` fail (`assert 262144 == 1048576`, `assert 262144 == 524288`, `assert 40960 == 131072`).
- Other tests that build a speculative config from a mocked draft `ModelConfig` (`tests/test_config.py`, `tests/v1/worker/`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_eagle_quantization.py`, filtered to spec-decode tests): 371 passed. `test_eagle_draft_model_config` fails only because our token cannot fetch the gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`.
- The config tests run in the CI step `(CPU) Multimodal + Config` (`pytest -v -s config`).
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes.

## Details

Root cause:

- `_maybe_override_draft_max_position_embeddings` and `DraftModelSpeculatorConfig.max_model_len` read `draft_model_config.hf_config`. For Qwen4Exp that is the composite config: its top-level `max_position_embeddings` is `None` and it has no `rope_parameters`, so the override returns early and the limit treats the draft as resizable.
- Qwen4Exp builds its MTP layers from the draft `ModelConfig` (`_make_draft_vllm_config`), so the draft's cache keeps 262,144 rows while the proposer feeds positions up to the target's `max_model_len - 1`. Qwen3.5's MTP builds its layers from the target's `ModelConfig`, so it is not hit at runtime; the unit tests use `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` because its config has the same nested layout and is small.
- Since #58094, a YaRN-extended target hands YaRN to its draft, but not `max_position_embeddings`. YaRN is not in `_CACHE_ONLY_ROPE_TYPES`, so the limit returned the draft's `max_model_len`, which vLLM derives from `max_position_embeddings` without the YaRN factor. The cache itself has `original_max_position_embeddings * factor` rows (`YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding`, `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding`, and `MRotaryEmbedding` with YaRN).

Change:

- `speculator_config.py`: both checks read `hf_text_config`. For flat configs it is the same object as `hf_config`.
- `speculative.py`: `_yarn_cache_positions()` returns `original_max_position_embeddings * factor` when every RoPE entry is `yarn`, `deepseek_yarn` or `deepseek_llama_scaling`. `DraftModelSpeculatorConfig.max_model_len` returns it for drafts that share the target's positions.
- Tests: a new parametrized test for the YaRN limit. The nested-config test from the previous revision now checks `speculator_config.max_model_len`, since `draft_shares_target_positions()` is gone. Mocked draft `ModelConfig`s get an `hf_text_config`.

Limitations:

- With M-RoPE and video pruning (`positions_factor=4`), the YaRN cache is 4x larger than this bound, so the limit is conservative there.
- For YaRN drafts that share the target's positions, a user-set speculative `max_model_len` no longer lowers the target's on the V2 model runner. Drafts with cache-only RoPE types already behave this way.
- Independent `draft_model` drafts are unchanged.
- With `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1` and no RoPE scaling, the target's own cache can still be too short. Unchanged, and not this bug.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 for corrupt AVIF and BLP images
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Inspired by #62703. A chat request with a corrupt AVIF image gets HTTP 500, and one with bad BLP data gets HTTP 501, instead of 400. `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` turns only `OSError`, `UnidentifiedImageError` and `SyntaxError` into the `ValueError("Failed to load image: ...")` that becomes a 400. Pillow's AVIF decoder raises `RuntimeError`, and the BLP plugin raises `BLPFormatError`, a `NotImplementedError`, so both get past that `except`. This PR adds `RuntimeError` to it, which covers both.

#62704 fixed the case from #62703, a PNG with a broken chunk (`SyntaxError`), by adding one class to the same tuple. This PR follows the same approach for the decoder errors that it does not cover. An image over Pillow's pixel limit (`DecompressionBombError`) has the same cause, but #60308 fixes it, so this PR does not touch it.

## Claims

- A corrupt AVIF (`RuntimeError: Failed to decode image: Missing or empty image item`) now gives HTTP 400 `Failed to load image: ...`, not 500.
- A BLP file with an unknown compression (`BLPFormatError: Unknown BLP compression 0`) now gives HTTP 400, not 501.
- Any `NotImplementedError` or `RecursionError` raised while decoding (both subclass `RuntimeError`) now also gives 400 instead of 501/500. These come from the input image, so 400 is intended.
- Valid PNG, JPEG, WEBP and AVIF images load as before. vLLM's own `ValueError`s in this block (pixel limit, decoded-size budget) are not affected.
- A new parametrized test in `tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py` covers both cases and checks the wrapped cause.

## Validation

Setup: CPU only. vLLM at upstream `main` `debcf2284`, Pillow 13.0.0, Python 3.12.

Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py
```

With the patch, 22 passed. With the old `image.py`, the two new cases fail with `RuntimeError: Failed to decode image: Missing or empty image item` and `BLPFormatError: Unknown BLP compression 0`, and the 20 other tests pass.

HTTP status: I passed each input to `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` and gave the escaping exception to the real `create_error_response`:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| AVIF with no primary item | `RuntimeError` -> 500 | 400 `Failed to load image: Failed to decode image: Missing or empty image item` |
| BLP2 with compression 0 | `BLPFormatError` -> 501 | 400 `Failed to load image: Unknown BLP compression 0` |
| PNG with a broken chunk (#62703) | 400 | 400 |
| PNG with a 20000x10000 header | `DecompressionBombError` -> 500 | 500, fixed by #60308 |
| Valid PNG, JPEG, WEBP, AVIF | loads | loads |
| Garbage bytes, truncated PNG | 400 | 400 |

`pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/media/image.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py`: all hooks passed or were skipped.

No model evaluation was run. The change only affects images that fail to decode.

## Details

Pillow has no single base class for bad image data, so `load_bytes` lists the classes. The one added here covers what a fuzz run over the allowed formats found escaping that list, apart from `DecompressionBombError`:

- `RuntimeError` comes from the C AVIF decoder (`_avif.AvifDecoder`) in `Image.open()`.
- It also covers `NotImplementedError`, which Pillow plugins raise for format features they do not support (`BLPFormatError` is one), and `RecursionError` from deeply nested input.
- Every call in this block only decodes client-supplied bytes, so all of these are client errors and map to 400. A 501 in vLLM means the model does not support the API, which does not fit a bad image.

`MemoryError` is still not caught and still gives 500.

This PR and #60308 both extend the same tuple, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Pass the caller's prompt_token_ids to the chat derender parser
author: Alex-Wengg
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Non-streaming chat derender passes the parser only `generate_response.prompt_token_ids`, which generate sets only when `return_token_ids` is on. In the usual render → generate → derender flow the parser therefore never sees the prompt. Since #61857, parsers read the prompt to tell whether it already closed reasoning, so they misclassify the output here. This affects response template parsers as well as Qwen3. For example, with Qwen3 and `continue_final_message` after a closed `</think>`, the answer comes back as `reasoning`.

## Claims

- The parser gets the engine's `prompt_token_ids` when the generate response has them and falls back to the caller's `prompt_token_ids` otherwise. The engine's take precedence because the caller may send only a suffix.
- `DerenderChatRequest.prompt_token_ids` and `derenderer.md` now say that chat derender with a parser needs the full prompt IDs in both modes. The docs also note that a suffix starting after the last reasoning marker still misparses, the same as sending no IDs.

## Validation

New E2E test through the render server (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3`, no GPU):

CPU is enough here. Derender only decodes and parses token IDs that were already generated, and the render server loads just the tokenizer.

```
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py::test_e2e_parser_uses_caller_prompt_token_ids
# without the fix:  AssertionError: assert None == ' is 42.'
# with the fix:     PASSED
```

Response template parser given a suffix (`test_prompt_suffix_parses_like_full_prompt_or_no_prompt`, a two-turn prompt whose generation prompt opens reasoning, output `plan<channel|>answer<turn|>`):

| prompt IDs given to the parser | reasoning | content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none (before this PR) | `None` | `plan<channel\|>answer` |
| full prompt | `plan` | `answer` |
| suffix from the start anchor | `plan` | `answer` |
| suffix past the anchor, with the reasoning opener | `plan` | `answer` |
| suffix past the reasoning opener | `None` | `plan<channel\|>answer` |

A suffix parses like the full prompt while it still holds the opener and like no prompt after that. It is never worse than the empty prefix the parser had before.

The same holds through derender with a real checkpoint: `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`'s response template (`--reasoning-parser hf`), 15 suffix lengths (last 1–12, 16, 24 and 32 IDs) on 4 prompts (opening reasoning, mid-reasoning, closed reasoning, and the model writing its own). Every suffix parsed like either the full prompt or no prompt. For example, a prompt ending in `<|channel>thought\n` parses correctly from the last 3 IDs, the first that include `<|channel>`.

```
$ pytest tests/parser/test_response_template.py
75 passed
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
214 passed, 1 xfailed
```

## Details

- #61857 made the parsers honor a prompt-closed reasoning block in non-streaming parse and reasoning token counts, but didn't touch derender.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this call (searched "derender prompt_token_ids" and "derender reasoning"). #64041's reasoning counts build on it and #63357 touches the next line, so this should go in first.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used. I reviewed the changed lines and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash: run the aux hidden state FC in the draft dtype
author: azaidy
body:
## Overview

A DFlash / DFlash2 drafter fails to start when the target model gives it FP32 aux hidden states (Muse Spark keeps its residual stream in FP32). The drafter's bf16 `fc` gets an FP32 input. This PR casts the input of `fc` to the FC's `params_dtype` in `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM.combine_hidden_states`.

## Claims

- Bug fix: Muse Spark Open with a DFlash2 draft (`"method": "dflash"`) now loads and serves. Before this change, the profile run failed with `expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype`.
- No change for targets whose hidden states are already in the draft dtype: `Tensor.to()` returns the same tensor and adds no kernel.
- This PR makes no performance claims.

## Validation

**Unit test** (runs on CPU tensors): `test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype` in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py` builds a bf16 `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM` on CPU through its constructor (with the file's `_mock_draft_configs` helper), gives `combine_hidden_states` FP32 aux hidden states, and checks that the result is bf16 and equal to `fc` applied to the bf16 input.

Before the fix (this PR's base 5f63ea4 + the new test):

```
$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -k fp32_target -q
vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py:89: in default_unquantized_gemm
    return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, bias)
E       RuntimeError: expected m1 and m2 to have the same dtype, but got: float != c10::BFloat16
FAILED tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py::test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype
1 failed, 103 deselected
```

With the fix:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -k fp32_target -q
1 passed, 103 deselected

$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \
    tests/transformers_utils/test_muse_spark_config.py -q
34 passed, 92 skipped        # the skipped tests require CUDA
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, check-test-tethering).

**End to end** (8x MI355X, `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, `--dtype bfloat16`, TP8, speculative config `{"method": "dflash", "model": "<Muse-Spark-Open DFlash2 draft, bf16>", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, ...}`):

| Server | Result |
|---|---|
| Without the fix | Fails at startup in the profile run: `expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype` in `combine_hidden_states` |
| With the fix | Loads (`DFlash2Speculator`) and serves requests |

The GPU runs used the same change on an earlier main (6ee316e). Between 6ee316e and this base, main changed `qwen3_dflash.py` only in the draft quantization-config mapping (#63001), not in `combine_hidden_states` or `fc`, and did not change `qwen3_dflash2.py`.

## Details

**Root cause.** Muse Spark keeps its residual stream in FP32, so the aux hidden states that it captures for the drafter are FP32. `DFlashQwen3Model.fc` is a `ReplicatedLinear` with `params_dtype = model_config.dtype` (bf16). `combine_hidden_states` called `fc` on the FP32 tensor directly, and the GEMM rejects the mixed dtypes. `DFlash2Qwen3ForCausalLM` inherits this method, so DFlash2 drafters fail the same way.

**Fix.** Cast the input to `self.model.fc.params_dtype` before `fc`. We use `params_dtype` and not `fc.weight.dtype`: `params_dtype` is the activation dtype that the FC's linear method expects, also when the FC is quantized (an FP8 or packed int weight has a different dtype or no `weight`). For an unquantized FC the two are equal.

**Muse Spark DSpark.** `MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM` (subclass of `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` -> `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM`) has its own `combine_hidden_states` override that casts to `fc.weight.dtype` and then calls this method. Its draft checkpoint is bf16 and unquantized, so the second cast is a no-op. This PR does not change that file.

**Not a duplicate.** #40334 proposed the same one-line cast for an AWQ + `cpu_offload_gb` case. Its author closed it without a merge after pre-commit failures, and it did not cover the FP32-residual target case. Issue #42588 (ROCm, `float != c10::Half` at the same line) was closed after #42646, which changed the RMSNorm path and not `combine_hidden_states`. No open PR changes `combine_hidden_states` (searches: `dflash dtype`, `dflash fp32`, `dflash mat1 mat2`, `combine_hidden_states dtype`, `aux hidden states dtype draft`).

**Cost.** The cast is not a host-device sync and is safe in CUDA graphs. For a bf16 target it is a no-op. For an FP32 target it is one cast kernel on the `fc` input, which the FC needs anyway.

**CI.** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py` runs in the "V1 Spec Decode" step (`pytest -m 'not slow_test' v1/spec_decode`; `source_file_dependencies` include `vllm/model_executor/` and `tests/v1/spec_decode`). The new test runs the model on CPU tensors. We cannot add a CI regression test through `LLM` with real weights: the only FP32-residual target that we know is the 816B Muse Spark model, which needs 8 GPUs. We did the end-to-end validation above outside CI.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above.

title: [Bugfix] Release cached cuBLAS workspaces after daemon warmup
author: tryryry
body:
## Overview

Release cached cuBLAS/cuBLASLt workspaces after weight-cache daemon warmup, before accepting engine connections.

Follow-up to #62583: communication teardown leaves PyTorch-owned BLAS workspaces resident even though the daemon no longer performs inference.

## Claims

- Release cached BLAS workspaces after daemon warmup while preserving CUDA IPC weights, allowing unused allocator segments to be returned to the GPU driver.

## Validation

### Memory comparison

`nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, B300, TP=4, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`, `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `max_num_seqs=1024`.

“Before” includes #62583. Memory figures are per GPU / daemon process.

| Metric | Disk load | Daemon before | Daemon after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Available KV cache | 18.90 GiB / 1,651,280 tokens | 18.92 GiB / 1,653,488 tokens | 18.92 GiB / 1,653,488 tokens |
| Loaded / exported weights | 4,357.92 MiB loaded | 4,340.77 MiB exported | 4,340.77 MiB exported |
| PyTorch allocated memory, cold cache | — | 4,419.98 MiB | **4,387.98 MiB (−32)** |
| PyTorch allocated memory, warm cache | — | 4,419.80 MiB | **4,387.80 MiB (−32)** |
| Daemon NVML memory, cold cache | — | 5,674 MiB | 5,674 MiB |
| Daemon NVML memory, warm cache | — | 5,694 MiB | **5,566 MiB (−128)** |

Workspace allocations decreased by 32 MiB per daemon. NVML savings depend on allocator fragmentation; KV capacity and exported weights remained unchanged.

These development measurements used different B300 GPU sets and base revisions (`c569393ed2` / `404c2b510e`, with unchanged daemon code). Externally disturbed baseline runs were excluded from the KV comparison. Results are individual observations, not repeated-run averages.

### Final implementation validation

`Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, B300, TP=4, compilation enabled, utilization=0.06, maximum length=8192, batched tokens=2048, maximum sequences=32.

| Metric | Disk load | Cold daemon + IPC | Warm restarted daemon + IPC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Available KV cache | 13.82 GiB / 1,766,663 tokens | 13.85 GiB / 1,769,706 tokens | 13.85 GiB / 1,769,706 tokens |
| Daemon NVML memory | — | 1,638 MiB | 1,604 MiB |
| Daemon ranks ready | — | 4/4 | 4/4 |
| Generated tokens | Reference | Identical | Identical |

All five runs—cold/warm disk, cold IPC, warm IPC with the existing daemon, and warm IPC after daemon restart—completed successfully with identical 32-token outputs. Exported weight sizes remained unchanged. This is targeted correctness validation, not a broad accuracy evaluation; the disk/IPC KV difference is not attributed to this fix.

### Tests

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_daemon_releases_cublas_workspaces \
  'tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart[qwen3.5]' \
  -v -s
```

**2 passed.** The development reproducer failed without the fix with `daemon retained BLAS workspaces`. A separate two-stream probe released 16 MiB with GPU work pending at cleanup entry and preserved correct outputs.

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py \
  docs/features/preload.md
```

All checks passed.

## Details

PyTorch caches BLAS workspaces independently of model tensors, so garbage collection and `empty_cache()` cannot release them while those caches retain ownership.

This change clears the caches after communication teardown and before the existing `empty_cache()`. Cleanup is CUDA-only and uses `getattr` to skip gracefully when the private PyTorch API is unavailable. No additional explicit device synchronization is introduced.

Duplicate-work searches found no equivalent open fix. Related #52553 addresses workspace address stability during graph execution; this PR releases caches after daemon warmup has finished.

title: [CI] Fix the Domyn Edge (ROCm) and Qwen2 embed HF references
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- `test_common.py`: on ROCm, generate the HF reference for `domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base` with `use_cache=False`
- `test_embedding.py`: keep the `ssmits/Qwen2-7B-Instruct-embed-base` HF reference on plain text with mean pooling

`test_models[...domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base]` has failed on MI355 since the model was added in #62544 ([build 96933](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96933/list?jid=01a16a2d-3c10-49ad-af03-b262a50862bd&tab=output)). vLLM's output is correct; it is the HF reference that turns to garbage after the first token. Domyn's remote code decodes through `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn`, and on ROCm that op aligns the causal mask to the top left when `max_q < max_k`, so with a KV cache every decode step only sees the first key. Recomputing without the cache keeps `max_q == max_k`, where the ROCm kernel is correct, so vLLM's Domyn coverage on ROCm stays in place. The PyTorch fix is pytorch/pytorch#201930; this part can be dropped once it is in the ROCm image.

The embedding test for `ssmits/Qwen2-7B-Instruct-embed-base` has failed on the CPU pooling job since #62835 bumped sentence-transformers to 5.6 ([build 97015](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97015)), with cosine 0.7963. That checkpoint has no sentence-transformers config, and 5.6 now wraps plain text in the tokenizer's chat template and uses last-token pooling for causal LMs, while the test pins vLLM to mean pooling of the plain text. Removing the `"message"` modality and putting a mean `Pooling` back gives the 5.2 embeddings again, and on older versions it is a no-op.

On MI350X with torch 2.12 and the CI pin 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, `varlen_attn` with `window_size=(-1, 0)` and 1 query against 40 keys matches a top-left reference exactly, and the HF Domyn reference produces `' ItOlimpiadiOlimpiadi...'` with the KV cache and `' It is designed to run large language models (LLMs) on a wide range'` without it. For the embedding model, sentence-transformers 5.2.0 and 5.6.0 differ by exactly cosine 0.7963 on the same input; with this change, the reference from `HfRunner` under 5.6.0 matches 5.2.0 at cosine >= 0.999999 on all 8 example prompts.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: sync the CTA around radix barrier arrivals
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Sync the CTA before thread 0 arrives at the per-round inter-CTA barrier in `radix_topk`.
- Sync the CTA at the end of each radix row, before it moves on to its next row.

`radix_topk` uses thread 0 alone to signal the inter-CTA barrier. In each radix round it arrives while the other threads of its CTA may still be adding their local histogram into the group's global histogram, or (on CTA 0) zeroing the next round's buffer, so peers can read an incomplete histogram, pick a different pivot and emit duplicate or missing indices. Separately, a CTA that owns several rows moves on to the next one while slower threads are still scanning `shared_ordered` for pivot ties, and the next radix row's vectorized load, or CTA 0's short-row path, overwrites that dynamic shared memory. The cost is one CTA barrier per radix round, next to the grid-wide spin barrier that round already waits on, plus one per radix row. I found both races while porting the kernel to ROCm (stacked on #62298), and I am sending the fix on its own because the code is shared with CUDA. No CUDA GPU was available to me, so the reproduction below is on MI355X and CUDA CI has to confirm the CUDA build and the existing `persistent_topk` tests.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, tests and duplicate check</summary>

**Reproduction (MI355X, gfx950).** A standalone HIP build of `persistent_topk_kernel` from my ROCm port, launched with the same grid sizing as `topk.cu`. Its `radix_topk` matches main except for the warp-shuffle macro, and the barrier's acquire load is a device-scope HIP atomic instead of PTX. Each run executes 150 random cases (k ∈ {512, 1024, 2048}; widths 32K-256K; randn, near-constant, 4-value ties, mostly `-inf`, all-equal; ragged and negative lengths; 1-32 rows, so CTAs own several rows) and checks every row against a CPU top-k by value set.

| variant | runs | rows checked | wrong rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| neither barrier (main) | 169 | 882,700 | 146 (57 runs) |
| end-of-row barrier only | 169 | 882,700 | 152 (59 runs) |
| pre-arrival barrier only | 169 | 882,700 | 0 |
| both (this PR) | 169 | 882,700 | 0 |

The end-of-row race did not show up on its own in these runs, so I checked it by making odd waves sleep (`s_sleep`) before the tie scan:

| variant (odd waves delayed) | runs | rows checked | wrong rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-arrival barrier only | 32 | 29,820 | 712 (32 runs) |
| both (this PR) | 32 | 29,820 | 0 |

**Tests.** The kernel builds only for CUDA on main, so `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k persistent` could not run here; CUDA CI covers it.

No new test: the races depend on scheduling and do not reproduce deterministically, so a unit test would be flaky.

**Duplicate check.** Searched open PRs for `persistent_topk`, `persistent topk`, `radix_topk`, `topk race` and `persistent_topk.cuh`, and read the `persistent_topk.cuh` diffs of #62936, #55122, #41748, #41105, #58785, #55314 and #52149. None adds a sync before the per-round arrival. #55122 rewrites the tie-collection stage and ends it with a grid barrier plus `__syncthreads()`, which would also close the end-of-row race, so whichever lands second drops that hunk. #41105 adds a trailing grid barrier only for its fused page-table variant.

</details>

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Report the first failed DBO microbatch
author: algebra-MCX
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When two DBO microbatches fail, the MRV2 `UBatchRunner` reports the one with the lowest index instead of the one that failed first, which hides the root cause. Related: #61487 (the hidden microbatch-1 error), follow-up to #63372 (also a DBO microbatch fix in `UBatchRunner`).

## Claims

- `finish()` reports the first recorded microbatch failure, not the lowest microbatch index (`min(errors)` → `next(iter(errors))`).
- The behavior is unchanged when one microbatch fails or none fail.

## Validation

`test_ubatch_runner_names_the_microbatch_that_failed` is now parametrized. The new `[1]` case makes microbatch 1 fail first, then microbatch 0 registers a recv hook on the exited peer, which raises the follow-on error.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 pytest -q \
  "tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py::test_ubatch_runner_names_the_microbatch_that_failed"
```

1x H200, on base `7822663cb4`:

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Before (base + new test) | 1 failed, 1 passed: `assert 'Microbatch 1' in 'Microbatch 0 of 2 failed'` |
| After | 2 passed |

`pre-commit run` passes on the changed files. CI runs the test through the existing `v1/worker` step.

## Details

Root cause: as reproduced in #61487, microbatch 1 fails and exits, and its `UBatchContext.__exit__` clears `_CURRENT_CONTEXTS[1]`. Microbatch 0 then calls `dbo_register_recv_hook()` on that cleared slot and raises an `AttributeError`. `min(errors)` picks microbatch 0, so the original error is lost.

Each worker thread writes `errors` at most once, under its own key. `finish()` reads `errors` only after joining all threads, and dicts keep insertion order, so the first key is the first recorded failure. No locking or new state is needed.

Limitations: "first recorded" is the first failure raised in Python, which can be later than the GPU fault because CUDA errors are asynchronous. This change does not fix the hang when a peer exits mid-handoff, or the HiSparse + DBO issues in #61487.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this selection. Searched for `61487 in:body`, "ubatch failed microbatch error", "DBO microbatch exception", and "UBatchRunner error".

title: [Bugfix] [Tokenizer] Preserve Hub model identity when loading tokenizer snapshots
author: yma11
body:
## Overview

This fixes a tokenizer-routing regression introduced by #60825, "[Performance]
Load HF tokenizers and processors from a local snapshot." Loading tokenizer
files from a local snapshot can hide the original Hugging Face repository ID
from Transformers.

In `transformers.models.auto.tokenization_auto`,
`MODEL_IDS_TO_TOKENIZERS_BACKEND` routes specific Hub IDs, including
`deepseek-ai/deepseek-coder-*`, to `TokenizersBackend` by matching
`config._name_or_path`. When the config is loaded from the snapshot, that is a
local path, the pattern never matches, and the class declared on the Hub
(`LlamaTokenizerFast`) is used instead, which drops every space. That can change the
input token IDs passed to the model and affect generated output.

The fix retains local-snapshot loading while restoring the original Hub ID on
a copy of the config passed to `AutoTokenizer`. The original config remains
unchanged, and the tokenizer continues to report the Hub ID as its
`name_or_path`.

title: [Bugfix] Restore engine memory budget after IPC fallback
author: tryryry
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When `ipc_cache` falls back to disk (e.g. the daemon is reachable but its weights do not match the engine config), the worker keeps charging the daemon's weights against its memory budget even though it no longer maps them, so the KV cache is smaller than with a direct disk load by the daemon's weight size. This removes the charge of each model that falls back, so a fallback is sized exactly like a direct disk load.

Follow-up to #62583.

## Claims

- After an IPC disk fallback, the engine budget and KV cache size match a direct disk load (Qwen3-4B, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`: KV cache 10.82 → 18.34 GiB, equal to the direct load).
- Only the charge of the model (target or draft) that fell back is removed; models still mapped from the daemon keep theirs.

## Validation

Setup: NVIDIA B300, TP1, eager, `max_model_len=1024`, `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`, `max_num_seqs=1`, FlashInfer autotune off. The daemon (`vllm preload --dtype bfloat16`) and the engine (`dtype="float16"`, `load_format="ipc_cache"`, `fallback=True`) differ in dtype, so the engine logs `Weight cache unusable (WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dtype']); falling back to disk loading`. Direct-load baselines use `load_format="auto"` with the same daemon running. Outputs are greedy, 8 tokens, for "The capital of France is". The `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1` runs shared the GPU with an unrelated workload.

**Regression test** (`test_ipc_fallback_restores_memory_budget`, Qwen3-0.6B, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`):

| Model runner | upstream main (`c126ebf159`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRV2 (extensible KV cache) | failed: `assert 27539026292 == 28741612340` | passed |
| MRV1 (estimate-based sizing) | failed: `assert 27539026292 == 28741612340` | passed |

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_fallback_restores_memory_budget
# Repeat with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 for MRV1.
```

**Fallback vs. upstream main** (Qwen3-4B, extensible KV cache, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`):

| | upstream main, fallback | This PR, fallback | Direct disk load |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Engine budget | 19.27 GiB | 26.77 GiB | 26.77 GiB |
| KV cache | 10.82 GiB | 18.34 GiB | 18.34 GiB |
| Output | identical | identical | reference |

**Sizing modes with this PR:**

| Case | Fallback | Direct disk load |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B, extensible off, util 0.1 | budget 26.77 GiB, KV 25.5 GiB, same output | budget 26.77 GiB, KV 25.5 GiB |
| Qwen3-4B, extensible off, util 0.980986 (full budget exceeds startup free memory by 4 GiB) | `ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (258.59/267.68 GiB) on startup is less than desired GPU memory utilization (0.980986, 262.59 GiB)` | same `ValueError` |
| Qwen3-4B, extensible on, util unset (1.0) | budget 267.68 GiB, KV 247.49 GiB, 0.32 GiB free after the KV cache is extended, output correct | budget 267.68 GiB, KV 248.34 GiB, 0.17 GiB free |

In the last row, the fallback's KV cache is 0.85 GiB smaller because post-warmup free memory was lower (248.44 vs. 249.31 GiB); the cause was not investigated.

Unit tests and lint:

- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_external_weight_fallback_preserves_other_role`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py::test_request_memory_charges_external_weights`: **46 passed**.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passed.

CI coverage: `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py` runs in `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 18GB) V1 Executor + Worker`. The single-GPU tests in `test_weight_cache.py`, including the regression test, run only in `:amd: (MI300) Model Executor`, because the NVIDIA Model Executor step is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/model_executor.yaml`; the NVIDIA results above were run locally. Not validated: TP > 1, ROCm, and an end-to-end run where only one of the target and draft falls back (covered by the accounting unit test).

## Details

**Root cause.** `Worker.init_device` charges daemon-held weights (`get_external_weight_memory`, added in #57298) before the model is loaded. If `IpcModelLoader.load_model` then falls back to disk, the engine allocates its own copy of the weights, but `requested_memory` still excludes the daemon's copy, so KV sizing pays for weights the engine does not map.

**Fix.**

- `IpcModelLoader` records each zero-copy daemon's charge by socket and role when it is queried, and after a successful disk fallback reports that role's charge once.
- `ExternalWeightCharges.track()` binds the worker's charges during the query and the model load and accumulates `fallback_bytes`.
- `Worker._resolve_requested_memory()` recomputes the budget with `external_weight_memory - fallback_bytes`, leaving `external_weight_memory` as queried at startup. It runs after `load_model` when a fallback happened, and in `disable_extensible_kv_cache`, which re-sizes after loading. Without a fallback, both paths behave as on main.

**Tradeoff.** A fallback now behaves like a direct disk load with the daemon as another process on the GPU. The daemon's resident weights are already excluded from `init_snapshot.free_memory`, so `request_memory`'s free-memory check and the extensible KV cache's measured sizing still bound physical memory. With estimate-based sizing, a configuration that fits only because the daemon's weights were charged (budget above startup free memory) now fails at startup after a fallback, as a direct disk load would, instead of running with a smaller KV cache.

**Duplicate work.** Searched open PRs for "ipc fallback memory budget", "external_weight_memory" and "weight cache fallback": no equivalent fix. #59813 restores model state before an IPC fallback; this PR fixes memory accounting after a successful fallback.
