title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Refuse adapters with LoRA on modules vLLM does not wrap
author: subin9
body:
## Overview

Fixes #63278. A PEFT adapter can carry LoRA weights for a layer that vLLM keeps as a plain `nn.Linear`, such as `bert.pooler.dense` in BERT models trained with `target_modules="all-linear"`. vLLM loaded these adapters and ignored those weights without a warning, so outputs differed from transformers + PEFT. vLLM now refuses such an adapter at load and names the modules, as discussed in #60211.

## Claims

- An adapter with LoRA weights on a module that vLLM cannot apply LoRA to fails to load with a `ValueError` naming the modules, for example `bert.pooler.dense` on BERT and `classifier.dense` on RoBERTa. On main these adapters load and their outputs differ from transformers + PEFT.
- On a running server, `/v1/load_lora_adapter` returns the error, the adapter is not registered, and the server stays healthy.
- Adapters whose LoRA weights all land on modules vLLM wraps load as before.
- Weights the LoRA manager already skips on purpose are still skipped: layers on another pipeline stage, layers outside `--lora-target-modules`, tower and connector layers without a PunicaWrapper, the non-gated MoE `mixer.gate`, and linear layers no LoRA layer can wrap.

## Validation

RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, fp16, `llm.llm_engine.add_lora(...)` for each adapter (the call behind `/v1/load_lora_adapter`):

| Adapter | Base model | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Shankarblr/bert-emotion-lora-adapter` (LoRA on `bert.pooler.dense`) | `bert-base-uncased`, 6 labels | loads | `ValueError` for `bert.pooler.dense` |
| Same adapter with the pooler LoRA removed | same | loads | loads |
| Fresh `all-linear` SEQ_CLS adapter with saved head, as in the #63278 repro | `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` | loads | `ValueError` for `bert.pooler.dense` |
| `query`, `value`, `dense` (PEFT also matches the pooler) | same | loads | `ValueError` for `bert.pooler.dense` |
| `query`, `value`, `dense` on the encoder only | same | loads | loads |
| `query`, `value` with saved head | same | loads | loads |
| LoRA on `classifier.dense` | `FacebookAI/roberta-base`, 3 labels | loads | `ValueError` for `classifier.dense` |
| `query`, `value` only | same | loads | loads |

The adapter fails with the existing unexpected modules error, which now lists `bert.pooler.dense (not a LoRA layer)`.

What the refused adapter costs on main: on the first 500 rows of the `dair-ai/emotion` test split, the emotion adapter reaches 94.2% accuracy with transformers + PEFT and 88.2% with vLLM main. 46 predictions change and logits differ by up to 6.71.

On `vllm serve` with the same base, `/v1/load_lora_adapter` for the emotion adapter returns 200 on main. With this PR it returns 500 with the message above, `/classify` with the adapter name returns 404, and `/health` stays 200. Passing the adapter straight to `LLM.classify` raises the same `ValueError` in the engine core, which surfaces as `EngineDeadError`, like the other adapter load errors.

Adapters on other families that must keep loading, all on this PR:

- `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` with `jeeejeee/qwen35-4b-text-only-sql-lora` and the all-linear `jeeejeee/qwen35-4b-all-linear-pokemon-lora`, with `enable_tower_connector_lora` on and off. Both load on main and on this PR, and `test_qwen35_text_lora` passes locally with its CUDA skip removed.
- `openai/gpt-oss-20b` with `jeeejeee/gpt-oss-20b-lora-adapter-text2sql`, whose keys include `mlp.experts.base_layer.lora_A.weight`. It loads and answers a prompt with `SELECT count(*) FROM users`.

Tests:

```
pytest tests/lora/test_sequence_classification.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_utils.py tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py tests/lora/test_lora_checkpoints.py
94 passed, 1 skipped

pytest tests/lora/test_lora_functions.py tests/lora/test_qwen3_unembed.py tests/lora/test_lora_huggingface.py tests/lora/test_moe_lora_ep_load.py tests/lora/test_qwenvl.py
11 passed, 2 skipped

pytest tests/lora/test_worker.py
1 passed

VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 pytest tests/lora/test_transformers_model.py -k "test_ilama_lora and not tp4"
1 passed
```

The skips are the TP test, which needs 2 GPUs, and the two Qwen2.5-VL tests that skip on CUDA. This card has about 14.6 GiB free, so `test_worker.py`, `test_ilama_lora` and `test_qwen35_text_lora` ran from local copies with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85` instead of the default 0.92. The new `test_lora_on_unsupported_module_is_rejected` fails on main:

```
pytest tests/lora/test_sequence_classification.py -k unsupported_module
E       Failed: DID NOT RAISE Exception
```

## Details

Root cause: `check_unexpected_modules` in `vllm/lora/lora_model.py` compares only the last part of each module name with the expected suffixes, which come from the model's `LinearBase` layers. BERT's encoder has `LinearBase` layers named `dense`, so `bert.pooler.dense` passes, although `BertPooler.dense` is a plain `nn.Linear` that `_create_lora_modules` never wraps. `activate_adapter` only reads weights for wrapped modules, so the pooler LoRA is never used. RoBERTa's `classifier.dense` takes the same path.

Change: `_create_lora_modules` records the layers it skips because `is_supported_lora_module` rejects them although their name ends in a LoRA target suffix. `check_unexpected_modules` treats LoRA weights on those layers as unexpected, so the adapter is refused while its checkpoint is read, before the LoRA model is built. It is never cached and never evicts another adapter, including on in-place reloads.

What stays skipped, and why:

- Weights for a `PPMissingLayer` or for a path through one belong to another pipeline stage, which applies them.
- Weights outside `--lora-target-modules` are excluded by the user.
- Weights without a PunicaWrapper, such as tower and connector layers when `enable_tower_connector_lora` is off, are already logged as ignored at startup.
- The non-gated MoE `mixer.gate` is a `GateLinear` and linear layers no LoRA layer can wrap are `LinearBase` too, so `is_supported_lora_module` accepts them and they keep their current behavior.
- Names that match no module of the model at all also keep their current behavior. That case, such as a text-only adapter on a multimodal wrapper with no name mapping, is what the draft #60039 covers. It raises only when no weight matches and warns on a partial match, so the pooler case would only log a warning there. The two changes do not overlap in code and can land in either order.

Once a model wraps a head linear, as #60211 does for RoBERTa's `classifier.dense`, its LoRA weights load and this check no longer fires for it.

Limits:

- The server returns 500 for this error, as it does for other `add_lora` failures.
- Pipeline and expert parallel runs were not tested, only covered by the `PPMissingLayer` and expert name handling described above.
- The new test downloads `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` and writes a small adapter in the test, so it needs no PEFT.

title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Scope prompt reasoning-end checks to the last message
author: ehfd
body:
## Overview

With `--reasoning-parser minimax_m3`, streamed chat completions from MiniMax-M3.1-Flash put the whole `<mm:think>…</mm:think>` block (or a leading `</mm:think>`) in `delta.content` and never set `delta.reasoning`; non-streaming responses are split correctly. This fixes it in the M3 reasoning parser, on top of #63232's branch. It is the remaining failure tracked in #50549, reported for this checkpoint in [MiniMax-M3.1-Flash discussion #6](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash/discussions/6).

## Claims

- Streaming responses split reasoning from content again, in single-turn, multi-turn, tool-call, and `reasoning_effort` requests.
- For structured outputs, the grammar starts after the model's `</mm:think>` rather than at the first generated token, which matches non-streaming parsing.
- Non-streaming extraction and the handling of output-only token ids are unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit:** I added two tests to `tests/reasoning/test_minimax_m3_reasoning_parser.py`, covering a prompt shaped like the M3.1 template (thinking instructions in the system message, a prior assistant turn prefixed with `</mm:think>`). Both fail without the change and pass with it. The 22 existing tests pass either way.

```
python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_minimax_m3_reasoning_parser.py
# without the change: 2 failed, 22 passed
# with the change:    24 passed
```

**End to end:** MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash` (`sha256:86f582da…`, vLLM `0.1.dev23341+g8744dd2fb`), 8x A100, TP4 x PP2, `--reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice`. Each request was sent once streamed and once not; the table shows the streamed `content` (non-streaming was correct before and after).

| request | before: streamed content | after: streamed content / reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| single turn, default | `</mm:think>391` | `391` |
| `chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort: low` | `<mm:think>17 * 23 = 391.</mm:think>391` | `391` / 14 chars |
| top-level `reasoning_effort: high` | `</mm:think>391` | `391` / 14 chars |
| multi-turn (prior turn with `reasoning`, `reasoning_content`, inline markers, or none) | `</mm:think>Berlin.` | `Berlin.` |
| tools offered, first turn | `</mm:think>I'll check the weather…` | `I'll check the weather…` + tool call |
| after a tool result | `</mm:think>The weather in Tokyo is…` | `The weather in Tokyo is…` |
| `response_format: json_schema` | JSON from the first token, no reasoning | reasoning first, then valid JSON |

The deployment applies this change as a patch at container start. That patch's helper reverses the list and calls `list.index`, where the PR uses a plain reverse loop; the two behave the same. The unit tests ran on the PR's version.

## Details

**Root cause.** The M3.1 chat template's system message describes the thinking format with a literal `<mm:think></mm:think>` pair and tells the model to "begin your response directly after the `</mm:think>` prefix". It also prefixes assistant turns that have no reasoning with `</mm:think>`. `DelegatingParser.parse_delta()` calls `is_reasoning_end(prompt_token_ids)` once at the start of a stream. Because the parser's `rfind` finds a closer after the last opener, it returns `True`, so `reasoning_ended` is set before the first generated token and every delta bypasses `MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser`. `ChatCompletionRequest.resolve_reasoning_ended()` uses the same check, which is why structured outputs were constrained from token 0. Non-streaming never consults the prompt, which is why it worked.

The `thinking_mode: "enabled"` workaround from #45687 does not apply here. It worked on M3, whose template prefills `<mm:think>`, so the prompt's last marker was an opener. The M3.1 template does not read `thinking_mode` and never prefills one.

**Fix.** `is_reasoning_end()` and `is_reasoning_end_streaming()` now look only at the ids after the last `]~b]`, the token the template opens every message with, including the generation prompt `]~b]ai\n`. A continued final message is handled the same way. Output-only ids contain no `]~b]` and are scanned whole, as before. If a tokenizer has no `]~b]` in its vocabulary, nothing changes.

**Tradeoffs.** For prompt-prefixed ids the backward scan stops at the generation prompt. For output-only ids it walks the whole output, the same order of cost as the existing `_contains_token_sequence` scans it sits next to. #50594 addresses the same issue more broadly, with prompt-boundary hooks across the serving paths (17 files). This change stays inside the M3 parser, so it can land on the model branch without touching shared code.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Exclude rc_gda lanes from the P2P NIXL agent
author: nilig
body:
## Overview

The P2P KV offload tier creates its NIXL UCX backend with UCX's default transports, which include the `rc_gda` GPU device lanes. After a P2P peer stalls or is replaced, connecting those lanes fails, so the peer was not usable again during the observation window (90 s): registering it fails, or its WRITEs stall, and every pull from it falls back to local prefill. This creates the tier's UCX backend with `engine_config="TLS=^rc_gda"`; the tier only moves host memory.

Fixes #63499.

Related: #63207 (the control-plane freeze in the same fault cases; without it the replacement cases freeze before reaching this bug), ai-dynamo/nixl#2437 / ai-dynamo/nixl#2337 (the `NIXL_ERR_INVALID_PARAM` loop that follows the first failed registration).

## Claims

- After a pause, the peer is pulled from again: the first pull succeeded 9-12 s after SIGCONT, and every probe from 40 s after SIGCONT on was pulled. After a replacement, the first pull came 0.3-0.7 s after the switch, and every probe from 10 s after the switch was pulled. Without the change, no pull from that peer completed during the observation window (90 s).
- No change for a healthy fleet, and none when `UCX_TLS` is set: UCX env vars take precedence over `engine_config`.

## Validation

Three single-GPU engines (Qwen3-0.6B, `--enforce-eager -O0`) on 8xH200 nodes with mlx5 InfiniBand: consumer A, source B that the fault hits, healthy source C. `OffloadingConnector` + `TieringOffloadingSpec`, 8 GiB CPU tier, P2P tier over RDMA, NIXL 1.5.0. Both arms run nightly `8e2beaa3b` + #63207 (`478d86b21`); the change is the only difference. A probe seeds a fresh ~2K-token prefix on B or C every 200 ms and asks A to pull it (`kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source`); "recovered" means A's requests to B (or B2) after recovery were pulled (A logged `request_blocks ... blocks>0` for them).

| fault on B | without this change | with this change |
|---|---|---|
| none | pass 1/1 | pass 1/1 |
| SIGSTOP 60 s, then SIGCONT | no pull in 90 s, 0/3 | recovers, 2/2: first pull 9-12 s after SIGCONT; every probe pulled from SIGCONT + 40 s (p50 0.051-0.057 s) |
| pod deleted gracefully, replacement B2 | no completed pull from B2 in 90 s, 0/3 (35-36 requested per run, none completed) | recovers, 2/2: first pull 0.7 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s (p50 0.056-0.057 s) |
| pod force-deleted, replacement B2 | recovers 1/3 (no pull from B2 in 90 s in the other two) | recovers, 2/2: first pull 0.6-0.7 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s (p50 0.053-0.058 s) |
| SIGSTOP, B on another node | no pull in 90 s, 0/1 | recovers, 1/1: first pull 10.6 s after SIGCONT; 242/242 from SIGCONT + 40 s |
| graceful replacement, B2 on another node | no pull from B2 in 90 s, 0/2 | recovers, 1/1: first pull 0.3 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s |

Across nodes, the graceful replacement fails through registration (`REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, then `INVALID_PARAM`) rather than the WRITE stall seen on one node. With NIXL main + ai-dynamo/nixl#2337 (and UCX v1.23.x) the `INVALID_PARAM` loop is gone, but recovery still fails: registration retries fail with `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` in the pause and force-delete cases, and 35-39 WRITEs stall in the graceful-replacement case. With `UCX_TLS=tcp,self,cuda_copy` all three recover (5/5); with `UCX_TLS=^rc_gda` set in the environment all three recover (3/3), matching this change.

Unit tests (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p`, CPU):

```
# this change
311 passed
# updated agent-config tests against main's nixl.py
FAILED test_data_transport.py::TestNixlAgentConfigSelection::test_ucx_only_creates_backend_without_rc_gda
FAILED test_data_transport.py::TestNixlAgentConfigSelection::test_default_backends_is_ucx_only
2 failed, 1 passed
```

CI cannot reproduce the failure: it needs RDMA NICs, GPUs and a peer fault between two engines. The updated tests only pin the backend configuration.

## Details

With UCX's GPU device API (NIXL sets `UCP_FEATURE_DEVICE`), every UCX endpoint gets `rc_gda` lanes next to its `rc_mlx5` lanes, whether or not GPU memory is ever transferred. UCX debug logs on the consumer for the SIGSTOP case:

1. At t+31 s (B stopped at t+21 s) the P2P session drops B and NIXL closes the endpoint; UCX destroys it after the UD keepalive times out at t+62 s.
2. B resumes at t+81 s and the session re-registers it at t+91 s: the new endpoint connects all eight `rc_mlx5` lanes, then the next lane connect fails:
   ```
   ib_mlx5_dv.c:446  UCX  ERROR   mlx5dv_devx_obj_modify(opcode=0x503) failed, syndrome 0x5d668c: Remote I/O error
   ucp_ep.c:1621 UCX  DEBUG ep 0x...: set_ep_failed status Input/output error
   nixl_agent.cpp:1679] loadRemoteMD: error loading remote metadata for agent '<B>' with status NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
   P2PSession <B>: peer registration failed, rejecting peer: NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
   ```
3. On NIXL 1.5.0 every later registration of B then fails with `NIXL_ERR_INVALID_PARAM` (ai-dynamo/nixl#2437). With NIXL main + #2337 the retries fail with `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` instead.

In the graceful-replacement case on one node, registration succeeds, but B2's WRITEs to A do not complete during the run and report no error; the stalled transfers pin CPU-tier chunks on both sides until both report `cannot store chunks`, which also drops some pulls from the healthy C (679/847 pulled). Excluding `rc_gda` removes that form as well.

The tier registers and transfers DRAM only, so it never uses the device lanes; dropping them also removes four lanes per endpoint. The change follows the `engine_config` mechanism the NIXL connector uses for its sleep-mode agent. On UCX versions without `rc_gda`, an unknown name in a negated `TLS` list is ignored without a warning. The underlying UCX failure (an `rc_gda` connect rejected after a peer fault) is not addressed here.

title: [XPU] Fix Kimi-Linear model dispatch
author: hlin99
body:
This PR is for model enabling, and may not be the most performant way
To successfully run kimi, we also rely on a MLA fix(https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63530)

Kimi-Linear currently falls through to the NVIDIA implementation on XPU. It fails while importing the CUDA-only CUTLASS GEMM code; disabling that path still leaves calls to fused MLA ops that are not available on XPU.

Use the existing implementation in `amd.linear` for Kimi-Linear on XPU. Despite the directory name, its portable KDA/MLA path runs on XPU. This reuses existing code rather than adding a separate XPU implementation. Kimi-K3 and MTP keep their current routes. Update the existing ReplaySSM expectation to match the selected implementation.

title: [CI] Fix the Qwen2 embed memory leak and HfRunner no-cache logprobs
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- `test_embedding.py`: edit the Qwen2 embed SentenceTransformer through `hf_model.model` so `HfRunner` can free it before vLLM starts
- `conftest.py`: `HfRunner` keeps only the last position of every generation step's logprobs, not just the first step's

These are two separate failures in the Extended Pooling / Extended Generation groups, each with its own culprit.

**Qwen2 embed (all platforms).** `test_embedding.py::test_models[ssmits/Qwen2-7B-Instruct-embed-base]` first broke in #62835, whose sentence-transformers 5.6 bump changed the HF reference (cosine 0.7963, [build 97017](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97017/list?jid=01a16ca7-c942-4db4-b589-f9460ca33724&tab=output), AMD and NVIDIA). #63452 restored the reference but bound the SentenceTransformer to a local name, so `HfRunner.__exit__` could no longer free its ~13 GiB, and the same test then failed on both vendors with memory still held when vLLM starts ([build 97064](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97064): NVIDIA "Free memory on device cuda:0 (18.74/32.5 GiB) … less than desired (0.92, 29.9 GiB)", MI355 DPX "Memory of devices [0] not free"). `git bisect` from 49d634bd6a (97017) to e7473bf686 (97064), measuring GPU memory held when `vllm_runner` starts, lands on #63452 (7a64fb8fc9): 7.16 GiB held at its parent e9acf48614 vs 14.89 GiB at 7a64fb8fc9 (bisect run with sentence-transformers 5.6 fixed, good/bad threshold 8 GiB).

**Domyn Edge (ROCm only).** `test_common.py::test_models[...Domyn-Edge-Base]` has failed on MI355 since the model was added in #62544, because the HF reference decodes through `varlen_attn`, which is top-left aligned on ROCm (pytorch/pytorch#201930). #63452 switched that reference to `use_cache=False`, which exposed a latent `HfRunner` bug from #4942: `_hidden_states_to_logprobs` dropped the prompt positions only on the first step, but without a KV cache every step returns all positions, so later steps read the wrong one (the failure moved from `Test0` in 97017 to `Test3` in 97064). CUDA is unaffected: its Domyn reference keeps the KV cache, and the CUDA Extended Generation job passes.

On MI350X: the Qwen2 embed test passes 10/10 with 4.2-4.6 GiB held when vLLM starts (17.9 GiB before); `use_cache=False` now gives the same top-5 as the cached run at every step (16/16 steps on pythia-70m, 2/16 before); the Domyn tests pass 20/20 over a 10x loop (3/3 failed before); and cached models are unchanged (`test_common.py -k "tiny-mixtral or stablelm or starcoder2"`: 8 passed).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix] Keep MRV2 model state in the runtime pool under sleep mode
author: xinyuangui2
body:
## Overview Build the Model Runner V2 model state in the `runtime` cuMem pool when sleep mode is on, so its device tensors survive level-2 sleep. Same approach as the LoRA state in #62358. #60009 lists Qwen4Exp `ngram_context_offsets` as out of its scope ("held by non-module objects"); this covers it. ## Claims - **Bug fix:** after `sleep(level=2)` + `wake_up()`, Qwen4Exp's `ngram_context_offsets` (a constant `arange(-ngram_context_len, 0)` on `Qwen4ExpModelState`) comes back as garbage (zeros in practice). Every later PLE n-gram context is wrong, so outputs are corrupted even when the weights are reloaded bit-exact. With this change it survives. - **Scope:** every MRV2 model state, not only Qwen4Exp: all of `init_model_state`'s device tensors move from the `weights` pool to the `runtime` pool. Only under `enable_sleep_mode` on CUDA/ROCm (XPU excluded: no nested pools, as in #62358). - **Cost:** level-2 sleep now copies the model state to host memory, as level 1 already did, instead of discarding it. These are per-request bookkeeping buffers (`max_num_reqs`-sized), plus `inputs_embeds` (`max_num_tokens x hidden`) for models that use it. - **Test:** `test_deep_sleep_model_state` checks that every model-state device tensor is allocated in the `runtime` pool and is unchanged after level-2 sleep + weights wake-up. ## Validation 4x H100 80GB, vLLM wheel for the base commit c9dbc926 (`0.32.1rc1.dev463+gc9dbc9263`, torch 2.14.0+cu130). Each arm swaps in that commit's `model_runner.py` (Python-only change); tests run from this branch's `tests/`. | Check | main (c9dbc926) | this PR | |---|---|---| | `test_deep_sleep_model_state` | **fails**: `AssertionError: {'num_accepted_tokens_gpu': 'weights'}` | passes | | `num_accepted_tokens_gpu` (Mamba2 tiny, MRV2) after `sleep(level=2)` + `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` | all 1s → **all 0s** | all 1s → all 1s | | `tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py` | — | 15 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only) | | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 4-layer slice, TP=4: `ngram_context_offsets` on all ranks, before → after sleep | `[-2, -1]` → **`[0, 0]`** | `[-2, -1]` → `[-2, -1]` (3/3 runs) | | Same: greedy output after sleep vs before (4 prompts, 64 tokens) | diverges at token 0–1, max \|Δlogprob\| 2.29 | same divergence patterns as a no-sleep control (below) | | `pre-commit` on the changed files (incl. mypy) | — | passed | ```bash VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py -k test_deep_sleep_model_state VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py ``` The Qwen3.8 repro uses `LLM(model, tensor_parallel_size=4, enable_sleep_mode=True, max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, disable_custom_all_reduce=True)`, then generate → `sleep(level=2)` → `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` → `collective_rpc("reload_weights")` → `wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])` → generate. The slice has random weights, so greedy TP=4 decoding is not run-to-run deterministic even without sleep. A no-sleep control (generate twice on one engine, 3 runs per arm) produces the same few late divergence patterns (none, or tokens 5–63) that this PR shows after sleep. On main, every prompt diverges at token 0–1. ## Details **Root cause:** `Worker.load_model` runs `GPUModelRunner.load_model` inside the `weights` pool. `init_model_state` runs there too, so the model state's tensors land in that pool. Level-2 sleep discards the `weights` pool, and wake-up restores only `model.named_buffers()` (and parameters, through the weight update). The model state belongs to the model runner, not the model, so registering its tensors as module buffers (the #60009 approach) does not apply. **Fix:** wrap `init_model_state` in `use_memory_pool(tag="runtime")` under sleep mode. Nested `use_memory_pool` calls restore the outer tag, so the weights pool around the rest of `load_model` is unaffected. Restoring from the pool keeps tensor addresses, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid. **Unrelated, seen while testing:** exiting while the KV cache is still asleep (level-2 sleep, weights-only wake) intermittently logs `CUDA Error: invalid argument at csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp:249` on main too (also with LoRA), from freeing the asleep KV-cache allocation; on CUDA, `_python_free_callback` unmaps asleep allocations. The new test wakes the KV cache before exiting. ---

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep the AITER GDN decode fast path off for the DS conv-state layout
author: AndreasKaratzas
body: - `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`: take the AITER GDN decode fast path only when the conv state is not dim-first (`VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`) - `test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py`: check that a DS conv state routes decode to the generic path `:amd: (MI300) Hybrid SSM NixlConnector PD accuracy` fails on every weekly AITER-on build ([14875](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14875), [15350](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15350)) with `APIConnectionError`: the Qwen3.5 decode server dies on an `AssertionError` in AITER's `fused_reshape_causal_conv1d_update_single_token`, which still requires `conv_state.stride(-2) == 1`. #53623 removed the `gqa_interleaved_layout` guard, so flat-qkvz models like Qwen3.5 now take `_forward_core_decode_aiter` even when the test sets `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`, whose conv state is (blocks, dim, state_len) with the feature stride 3. Falling back to the generic path for DS, as the KDA path already does, avoids the stale AITER assertion; dropping that assertion in AITER is a separate follow-up. On MI350X with the AITER v0.1.26 pin, Qwen3.5-0.8B with AITER and the DS layout fails on main with the same assertion and passes with this change in 3/3 runs, with output byte-identical to AITER with the SD layout; the new dispatch test fails without the change and passes with it. title: [CI][ROCm] Skip the AITER MoE garbage-rows test for fp8 per-tensor until the AITER fix
author: AndreasKaratzas
body: - `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: skip `test_aiter_moe_token_padding_garbage_rows` for fp8 per-tensor configs until the AITER fix is in the pinned `AITER_BRANCH` `test_aiter_moe_token_padding_garbage_rows[single_inf-fp8_tensor_tensor]` and `[single_nan-fp8_tensor_token]` failed on MI300 in [amd-ci 15340](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15340) with `mean |mk_out| = 0`. The bug is in AITER, not vLLM: `fused_moe_2stages` allocates `a2` with `torch.empty`, stage 1 never writes the slots of `topk_ids == -1` rows, and the dynamic per-tensor a2 quant then takes its scale over that stale memory, which can push every real row to fp8 zero. Per-token and block schemes scale row by row and are unaffected, so only configs with fp8 per-tensor weights (which the test runs with no static a2 scale) are skipped. The AITER fix is ROCm/aiter#6568; this guard should be removed when `AITER_BRANCH` includes it. #62927 targets the same failure from the vLLM side but does not fix it (details in that PR). On MI350X with AITER v0.1.26, poisoning the caching allocator with 1e30 makes exactly the four skipped params fail (3/3 runs) while the other nine pass; nothing was run on MI300, where CI failed (1 failing nightly of ~10 since 2026-10-08). With the guard, the group runs 9 passed, 7 skipped. This adds a skip, which tests/AGENTS.md discourages; it is a temporary ROCm-only guard until the AITER bump, alongside the existing ROCm/aiter#6275 skip in the same test. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Pin a shared-prefix junction when a sparse group cuts the offload hit
author: KaloyanNaumov
body:
## Overview Fixes #63565. On hybrid models with sparse retention (the default), a prefix that lives only in the CPU offload tier is never reused by a request that diverges before the single stored Mamba/sliding-window state. The offload lookup now pins a shared-prefix junction there, as the local prefix cache already does, so the prefix heals after one miss. ## Claims - A revisit that shares a prefix but diverges inside the prompt's last block hits the offload tier from the second revisit on (today: never). - No change when every group hits, when no full-attention group proves a hit, under dense retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=None`), or for models without a sliding-window/Mamba group. - A junction set by the local prefix cache is never lowered. ## Validation CPU (x86, torch 2.14.0+cpu, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`): ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k junction # main: test_sparse_group_miss_registers_shared_prefix_junction FAILED assert 0 == 16; 2 passed # this PR: 3 passed pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_offload \ tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py # this PR: 86 failed / 1,740 passed / 24 skipped (the same 86 fail on main) ``` The 86 failures are the same on main and are environmental on a CPU-only host: 32 in `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py` (copies through a GPU) and 54 EC-connector cases in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` (a multimodal model config is not available there). `pre-commit run --files `: all hooks pass. GPU (4 × Intel Arc Pro B70, torch 2.14.0+xpu, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.15.4): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B BF16, TP 4, `--enforce-eager --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 16 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, 576-token blocks, GPU KV cache capped at 66K tokens (`--kv-cache-memory`) so that filler requests evict the documents from the GPU prefix cache. Serial requests. Six ~16.1K-token documents, three whose question starts inside the block that holds the stored GDN state (in-band) and three whose question starts after it (out-of-band); each is read with question A, then revisited with question B and question C, with six 16K-token fillers before each revisit. GPU prefix-cache hits were 0 on every revisit. | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | in-band, revisit B | 0/3 offload hits, TTFT 1.49 s | 0/3, TTFT 1.49 s (one more GDN state stored: 0.15 vs 0.09 GB) | | in-band, revisit C | 0/3, TTFT 1.50 s | 3/3, 15,552 of ~16,140 tokens from the offload tier, TTFT 0.30 s | | out-of-band, B and C | 3/3, 3/3 | 3/3, 3/3 | Same documents and questions in both runs (fixed seed). The greedy answers of the three healed in-band hits equal main's answers to the same prompts, which main computed without a hit. ## Details Under sparse retention each request keeps one sparse-group checkpoint, in the last block of its prompt. A later request that shares the prefix but diverges before that block finds its full-attention chunks in the offload tier but no Mamba state at or below them, so `_lookup_complete_chunks` returns 0 for the whole request. The local prefix cache handles the same geometry by returning a shared-prefix junction from `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks` (`kv_cache_manager.py:318-326`); the recompute then retains the sparse state there. The offload lookup never set one, so once the prefix had left the GPU cache every recompute stored its state inside the differing suffix again. Change (`offloading/scheduler.py`): - `_lookup_complete_chunks` also returns the boundary the full-attention groups proved before the first sliding-window/Mamba group narrowed it (not on a deferred lookup), as the second item of a tuple. - `_lookup`, when the final hit is shorter than that boundary and retention is sparse, calls `_maybe_register_shared_prefix_junction`, which raises `request.shared_prefix_boundary` to it and never lowers a junction the local prefix cache already set. No core change is needed: the scheduler sets the local junction before it calls the connector (`sched/scheduler.py:1077-1089`), and everything downstream reads the request field: the align split stops a chunk there (`sched/scheduler.py:610`), `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` retains it (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:511-518`), and the aligned-boundary hand-off stores it to the offload tier. Limits: the first revisit still misses (a first-visit hit needs a state retained below the replay boundary, which is the subject of #57613). Connectors that set `hit_diverged` and load nothing re-read the local junction (`sched/scheduler.py:1162-1172`) and can overwrite this one; the plain `OffloadingConnector` does not take that path. If #62278 (junction as a tuple of positions) merges first, this needs a small rebase to add the junction to `shared_prefix_boundaries`. Why this is not a duplicate: searched on 2026-10-24 for "shared_prefix_boundary", "junction", "offload shared_prefix_boundary", "offloading mamba junction" and "OffloadingConnector hybrid". #45238 is the GPU-cache form of this geometry (main has the GPU junction, #47782 / #37898); #57613 retains a block below sliding-window replay boundaries (first visit, different mechanism); #59146 keeps the prompt-end checkpoint; #56795 is a different offload-store bug; #52774 backfills GPU-local divergent hits only; #62400 adds junctions to the MooncakeStore connector; #63221 changes the connector load boundary under EAGLE. None sets a junction from the `OffloadingConnector` lookup. AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write the change and the tests, and draft this text. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above. ---

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Await krdy before K2's combine reads klen in index-source launches
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- In K2's `stage_combine` (`mono/attention/back.py`), an index source now waits for its token's `krdy` flag and reads `klen` past the per-XCD caches (CM_DEV), as `stage_split` already does.
- Non-index launches are unchanged: both are behind `const_expr("krdy" in c)`.

An index-source K2 rebuilds the key table (`kt`/`klen`) itself in the same launch. #61082 made the split stage wait for that, but the combine still read `klen` with a plain load and no wait, so it can see the previous launch's key count. Whether that breaks anything depends on how the stale count compares with the real one:

| Previous launch's `klen` vs this launch's | What the combine does | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Equal | Merges the right chunks by luck | Correct | Correct |
| Smaller | Merges too few chunks | Wrong attention output: 3,791 of 8,704 MXFP8 codes of the attention output wrong (`Case(ratio=2, R=17, T=1, index=True)`, TP2) | Correct |
| Larger | Waits on split chunks that are never published | Hang: the unbounded `_spin` never returns (killed at 420 s, 3/3 runs, TP2) | Correct |

That is the index-source failure caught by the slow-reference test in #63486, and the intermittent index-source hang seen while stressing it.

| Check (MI350X, AITER v0.1.26) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Index-source vs reference, TP2 | 0/3 pass | 39/40 pass (10 + 30 loop) |
| Index-source vs reference, TP4 | 0/2 pass | 3/3 pass |
| Long-then-short index sequence, TP2 | 3/3 hang | 3/3 pass |
| Same token pair, both orders, TP2 | 0/3 pass | 15/15 pass |
| Rest of the DSv4.1 mono numerics / layers / decode tests | - | 7 passed + 1 skipped / 4 passed + 1 skipped / 85 passed |

The one failing TP2 run in the 40 failed the relative-error check before per-row logging was added; the 30 logged runs after it were bit-identical (rel 0.006460). Index launches were not exercised on gfx942, which shares this code.

**Performance.** One layer step (K1 + index select + K2 + FFN) captured as a CUDA graph of 20 steps, 200 replays, 5 base and 5 fix runs interleaved. Each index case runs after its non-index twin so that the stale `klen` equals the correct one and the base result is valid. Median per step:

| Case | Base (us) | Fix (us) | Fix - base (us) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP2, index, R=17 short | 448.1-450.8 | 448.6-450.6 | -0.1 to +0.1 |
| TP2, index, R=17 long | 451.1-452.3 | 450.7-451.6 | -0.6 to +0.2 |
| TP2, index, R=4 x T=6 | 554.0-557.4 | 555.8-558.2 | -0.1 to +1.3 |
| TP4, index, R=17 short | 306.3-308.0 | 307.1-307.5 | -0.3 to +0.6 |
| TP4, index, R=17 long | 307.6-309.2 | 308.0-308.9 | -0.6 to +0.6 |
| TP4, index, R=4 x T=6 | 366.5-367.8 | 367.0-368.5 | +0.7 to +0.8 |
| Non-index control (unchanged code) | - | - | -0.3 to +0.4 |

Every delta is within the ~1 us (0.2-0.3%) run-to-run noise of the unchanged control: the `krdy` flag is normally published long before the combine reaches it, so the cost is one device-scope poll and a CTA barrier per combine unit.

This unblocks #63486, whose DSv4.1 index-source test is a plain test that depends on this fix.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Probe non-jinja renderers for inline system message support (Anthropic API)
author: robertgshaw2-redhat
body:
## Overview `/v1/messages` merges inline system messages into the leading system prompt for every renderer without a jinja template, so Claude Code's per-turn reminders invalidate the prefix cache on DeepSeek V4.1, Kimi K3 and Inkling. Probe the renderer instead of assuming. Fixes #60537. Overlaps #58772 (draft, superset: same probe plus a fold mode), #56520 and #60555 (per-tokenizer flags). This is the probe on its own as a small fix that can land first; I'm coordinating with @bbrowning on #58772. ## Claims - Non-jinja renderers keep inline system messages in place only when the renderer emits them as distinct system turns in order and a trailing one is still followed by the generation prompt; anything else merges as before. - DeepSeek V4.1, Kimi K3, Inkling: now kept in place. DeepSeek V4 (appends system text to the user turn, #46710), V3.2 (trailing system lands after the generation prompt, #53737), Mistral (moves it into the user turn): still merged. - No per-tokenizer registration. HF/jinja path unchanged. ## Validation E2E: Claude Code-style tool loop (system reminder after each tool result) via `/v1/messages`, Inkling with dummy weights (2 layers, H100). `cache_read_input_tokens` per turn: | turn | prompt | main | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 1716 | 0 | 672 | | 2 | 2756 | 640 | 1696 | | 3 | 3796 | 640 | 2752 | | 4 | 4836 | 672 | 3776 | Main logs the "merged into the leading system prompt" warning at startup; this PR doesn't. A dummy 2-layer DeepSeek V4.1 didn't report prefix hits on either side (cross-layer KV sharing breaks under the layer override), so V4.1 is covered at the render level: each turn's prompt tokens are an exact extension of the previous turn's (371/371 ... 663/663 tokens reused). New test fails on main, passes here: ``` pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k test_probes_non_jinja_renderer main: FAILED [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-False] - assert True is False here: 3 passed ``` Probe result through real renderers (`renderer_from_config`): V4-Flash merge, V4.1-Flash keep, V3.2-Exp merge, Kimi-K3 keep, Inkling keep, Pixtral (mistral) merge. `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/`: 125 + 7 passed. pre-commit clean. No model evals: prompt text for DeepSeek V4.1, Kimi K3 and Inkling changes (reminders render as system turns where the client sent them instead of in the leading system prompt). ## Details `_should_merge_inline_system` previously only probed jinja templates; non-HF renderers had no template to probe and always merged. The probe renders `[sys, user, sys, user]`, the same with the inline system as user, and `[sys, user, sys]` through `renderer.render_messages`, once at startup. "Didn't raise" is not enough: V4 and V3.2 render without error but misplace the text. ---

title: [Bugfix][Platform] Keep PIN_MEMORY eager; avoid resolving platform during import vllm
author: njhill
body:
## Overview Reworks #60766: keeps `PIN_MEMORY` a plain eagerly-computed module global (instead of a lazy module `__getattr__` plus `is_pin_memory_available()` calls in the `torch_utils` hot paths), and fixes the underlying import-order problem instead: `import vllm` resolved `current_platform` and loaded platform plugins while vLLM was half-imported. ## Claims - `import vllm` doesn't resolve the platform (same as #60766), including with `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1`, which #60766 didn't cover. - An out-of-tree platform plugin whose `register()` imports from `vllm.utils.torch_utils` is detected correctly, both for `import vllm` and `from vllm import LLM`. - `PIN_MEMORY` is a plain module global again; `async_tensor_h2d` / `np_to_pinned_tensor` read it directly. - Out-of-tree platform plugin detection failures are now logged as warnings rather than silently (debug) falling back to another platform. ## Validation Run on GB200 (CUDA), with the dummy platform plugin installed where needed: | Check | Result | |---|---| | `tests/plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py` | 4 passed | | same, `test_import_vllm_does_not_resolve_platform` with `env_override` pointed back at `torch_utils` (i.e. without the fix) | fails; new warning shows `cannot import name 'direct_register_custom_op' from partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'` | | `tests/test_force_first_config.py` | 3 passed | | `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1`: platform resolved after `import vllm` / patch installed after `import vllm.triton_utils` / installed without env var | no / yes / no | | `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` + `tests/compile/test_config.py::test_version` | 38 passed | ```bash pip install -e tests/plugins/vllm_add_dummy_platform cd tests && pytest -v plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py ``` Runs were on the commit before rebasing onto current main; none of the 17 intervening upstream commits touch the changed files. ## Details **Root cause.** `vllm/__init__.py` → `vllm.env_override` → `from vllm.utils.torch_utils import is_torch_equal, is_torch_equal_or_newer` → module-level `PIN_MEMORY = is_pin_memory_available()` → `current_platform` resolution → plugin `register()` runs against a partially initialized `torch_utils`. The `ImportError` was swallowed in `resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname`, so another platform was silently selected. **Changes.** - `is_torch_equal*` move to a new dependency-free `vllm/utils/torch_version.py` (re-exported from `torch_utils`, so existing imports keep working). `env_override` and `envs` import from it, so `import vllm` no longer imports `torch_utils` at all. - `PIN_MEMORY` is assigned at the end of `torch_utils.py`. Other paths (e.g. `from vllm import LLM` → `vllm.config.cache` → `torch_utils`) still resolve the platform while importing `torch_utils`; with the assignment last, a plugin importing anything else from `torch_utils` finds it already defined. The restored `test_platform_plugins` (runs `from vllm import LLM`) covers this. - The `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG` autotuner patch is installed on import of `vllm.triton_utils` rather than in `env_override`, since importing that package resolves the platform. All vLLM Triton kernels import through it, so the patch is still in place before any autotuning; a third-party `triton.autotune` kernel run before `vllm.triton_utils` is imported would no longer be patched. - Plugin Integration CI step now also triggers on the files involved (it didn't run for #45424, which introduced the regression). **Not addressed (also not addressed by #60766).** `import vllm.config` still resolves the platform (`vllm/config/compilation.py` imports `current_platform` at module level), and a plugin whose `register()` needs the platform itself (e.g. imports `PIN_MEMORY` or `vllm.triton_utils`) can't work under any of these schemes. ---

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Use the default template of multi-template processors
author: zw-g
body:
## Overview Processors that ship several chat templates (e.g. `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B`, `ModernVBERT/colmodernvbert-merged`) expose `chat_template` as a `{name: template}` dict. `_try_get_processor_chat_template` returned it as is, so chat rendering fails with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'`. This PR uses the `"default"` entry and carries forward #46801 (@shun-cohere). ## Claims - Chat-style requests to these models return 200 instead of 400 `unhashable type: 'dict'`. They use the `"default"` template, as `ProcessorMixin.apply_chat_template` does (content format `openai`, not `string`). - Other processors are unchanged. A dict without `"default"` raises a `TypeError` in the existing `try` (logged at debug level), so resolution falls through to the tokenizer template. ## Validation Main 9a56d4fec, CPU-only Linux VM, transformers 5.20.2. The main column uses main's `vllm/renderers/hf.py`. | Command | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | `pytest tests/renderers/test_hf.py::test_processor_multiple_chat_templates_uses_default` | failed | passed | | `pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_launch_render.py` | new test: `assert 400 == 200` | 9 passed | | `cd tests && pytest -v -s renderers` | 4 failed, 689 passed | 3 failed, 690 passed | | `vllm launch render Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B`, `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` | 400 | 200, expected `token_ids` | | `vllm serve ModernVBERT/colmodernvbert-merged`, `POST /pooling` with `messages` | 400 | 200 | The 3 shared failures are gated repos (no HF token); main's extra one is the new unit test. pre-commit passes. CI runs the tests in `entrypoints-integration-api-server` and `cpu-reasoning-renderers`. ## Details - Root cause: transformers keeps `processor.chat_template` as a dict when a repo has `additional_chat_templates/*.jinja`. Without tools, `resolve_chat_template` returns it, and the `lru_cache` of `_cached_resolve_chat_template_kwargs` raises. - On main the servers still start (the warmup only logs the `TypeError`; since #64020 the Anthropic inline-system probe no longer aborts on the dict), but chat-style requests fail. With this PR the probe checks the real template. - No model eval: only requests that failed on main change; the prompt equals `ProcessorMixin.apply_chat_template`'s output for both models. - Not a duplicate: PR searches (see logs) find no fix besides #46801 (stale-closed, no review). None of the 9 other open PRs touching `vllm/renderers/hf.py` (updated within 10 days) changes this function. - AI assistance (Claude) was used; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
Logs: main 9a56d4fec vs this PR Unit test, main: ``` $ python -m pytest -v -p no:cacheprovider tests/renderers/test_hf.py::test_processor_multiple_chat_templates_uses_default E TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict' vllm/renderers/hf.py:825: TypeError FAILED tests/renderers/test_hf.py::test_processor_multiple_chat_templates_uses_default ======================== 1 failed, 2 warnings in 12.46s ======================== ``` This PR: ``` $ python -m pytest -v -p no:cacheprovider tests/renderers/test_hf.py::test_processor_multiple_chat_templates_uses_default tests/renderers/test_hf.py::test_processor_multiple_chat_templates_uses_default PASSED [100%] ======================== 1 passed, 2 warnings in 7.64s ========================= ``` Render-server test, main: ``` $ python -m pytest -v -s -p no:cacheprovider --durations=0 tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_launch_render.py::test_chat_render_multiple_chat_templates (MainProcess pid=7986) INFO 11-04 01:52:24 [hf.py:736] Detected the chat template content format to be 'string'. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] hadacore: fix skipped wait_group on partial-chunk warp for odd row counts (#63514)
author: bandham-manikanta
body:
Fixes #63514

### Problem
When using INT4 per-token-head KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head`), `reshape_and_cache_int4` rotates Key and Value tensors via `hadacore_transform`. 

For `head_dim = 256`, `num_chunks` is 2. When the row count (`num_tokens * num_kv_heads_per_rank`) is odd, the last warp receives only 1 chunk (`real_num_chunks = 1`).

`diff_num_chunks` was calculated as:
```cpp
int64_t diff_num_chunks = real_num_chunks - num_chunks; // 1 - 2 = -1
```
Because `diff_num_chunks` was negative, `switch(k + diff_num_chunks)` evaluated to `-1`. Since the switch statement only contains `case 0..31` and had no `default:` fallback, it silently skipped `cp.async.wait_group` completely. 

The warp proceeded to read shared memory before the asynchronous DMA copy completed, causing:
1. Silent data corruption (relative errors up to 10^36).
2. Intermittent `CUDA illegal memory access` crashes during prefill.

### Fix
1. Correct the difference to `num_chunks - real_num_chunks` so `k + diff_num_chunks` maps to the intended wait barrier count (`wait_group 0` for the single tail chunk).
2. Add `default: asm volatile("cp.async.wait_group 0;\n"); break;` so an unhandled case can never silently skip synchronization.
3. Add parameterized unit test in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_hadacore.py` covering odd and large row counts (`num_rows in [1, 17, 53, 65, 165, 173, 257, 513, 1025, 4097, 8193]`).

### Validation
Verified on NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB:
- **Full range test (`N = 1` to `512`):**
  - Unpatched `main` (`2c880f1e`): 39 failing row counts (all odd), errors up to 10^36.
  - With this fix: **0 failures out of 512** (100% bit-exact match against float64 reference).
- Tested small (`N <= 128`), medium (`128 < N <= 513`), and large (`1024 <= N <= 8193`) shapes across both odd and even counts.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction Script</summary>

```python
import math
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops

D = 256
H = torch.ones(1, 1, dtype=torch.float64, device="cuda")
while H.shape[0] < D:
    H = torch.cat([torch.cat([H, H], 1), torch.cat([H, -H], 1)], 0)
H = H / math.sqrt(D)

bad = []
for n in range(1, 513):
    torch.manual_seed(n)
    x = torch.randn(n, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    y = ops.hadacore_transform(x.clone(), inplace=True)
    ref = (x.double() @ H).to(torch.bfloat16)

    rel_err = ((y.double() - ref.double()).abs().max() / ref.double().abs().max()).item()
    if rel_err > 2e-2:
        bad.append((n, f"{rel_err:.2e}"))

print(f"Tested 1..512 row counts: {len(bad)} failures")
if bad:
    print("Sample failing counts:", bad[:10])
```
</details>

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Let idle P2P-only engines park
author: albertoperdomo2
body:
## Overview Let an idle P2P-only offload engine report no pending work, using the tier-poll thread introduced in #58168 to service peers. Related context: #51476. ## Claims - P2P reports actual outstanding work instead of keeping the engine busy unconditionally. - The poll thread survives sustained failures, backs off to `max(tier_poll_interval_s, 1 s)`, and rate-limits error reports. ## Validation - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/`: **573 passed, 12 skipped**. - Instrumented engine probes verified idle queue parking and the shutdown decision; a deterministic fault probe verified bounded logging, backoff, and recovery. - Ruff 0.14.0 check/format checks, Markdown lint, and `git diff --check` passed. - **Live H100 A/B validation completed:** Qwen3-0.6B, two TP1/DP1 instances, P2P-only, real NIXL transfers over TCP. | Check | Baseline | Fixed | | --- | --- | --- | | Pause, `mode=wait&clear_cache=false` | 4/4 timed out at 10 s | 4/4 HTTP 200 in 22.7–24.7 ms | | Idle EngineCore main-thread context switches/s | 1,014–1,076 | 0 in both 5 s samples | | P2P transfers and matching outputs | 3/3 | 3/3, while source acknowledged paused | | Engine shutdown | Both forced-killed after 15 s | Both normal teardown, container exit 0 | Each arm transferred 1,008 MiB / 576 chunks with zero promotion failures. Outputs also matched across images. This validates the P2P-only path; sleep, DP, multi-tier and RDMA performance were not tested. ## Details Idle polling belongs to the poll thread. Keep the engine stepping when polling is disabled or multiple secondary tiers require scheduler-driven promotions; those configurations retain their existing pause/shutdown limitation. KVCR is unchanged. Rendered documentation describes the supported behavior. Duplicate-work searches found related #61667, #62795, and #62929, which address transfer lifetime, finalization ordering, and cache-reset fencing rather than this idle predicate. Design feedback is welcome. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, and review. ---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Roll back failed P2P NIXL registration
author: Levius-Fubuki
body:
## Overview Roll back a newly registered NIXL agent when descriptor preparation fails in the P2P KV-offload transport. Related to #63602, gap 4 only. AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for investigation, implementation, tests, and this description. The human submitter confirmed completion of manual review and authorized submission. The reviewed contribution carries their DCO sign-off. Original-submission results below are the recorded server runs; review follow-up results are the recorded local runs. No additional human test execution is asserted. ## Claims - A failure in `get_xfer_descs` or `prep_xfer_dlist` rolls back the unpublished remote registration. - A failed repeat using already-published native metadata leaves that registration owned by its existing peer. - Cleanup failure is logged without replacing the original registration exception. Native cleanup success cannot be guaranteed when NIXL itself rejects removal. ## Validation The table and native validation below describe the original submission, `18349008c`; follow-up results are recorded separately below. Base: `a7407ab44557802ca32a0ba2c2707362d7d21563`. | Check | Base | Changed | | --- | --- | --- | | Eight new constructor-based cases | 6 failed, 2 passed | 8 passed | | Complete data-transport file | Not measured | 64 passed | | Data transport, sessions, ZMQ transport | Not measured | 223 passed | | Full P2P suite, including manager | Not measured | 319 passed | | Native NIXL 1.5.0 DRAM/UCX reproducer | Metadata survives descriptor failure | Rollback succeeds; 6 real WRITE byte comparisons pass | | Applicable pre-commit hooks | Not measured | Passed, including pinned Ruff, mypy, and test tethering | ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_zmq_transport.py -q .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/data/nixl.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py ``` Tests construct the real `NixlTransport`; only the external NIXL boundary is mocked. Native validation uses the production transport with two real NIXL agents, host buffers, UCX TCP/shared memory/CUDA-copy, injected descriptor failures, native metadata queries, retries, and exact byte comparisons. Both descriptor stages and an idempotent repeat are checked. This source-level Python validation used Python 3.12.3 and the server's existing torch 2.12.1+cu130. It did not build main's torch 2.14 native extensions. The command excludes the heavyweight root `tests/conftest.py`, and uses the P2P suite's real conftest. No LLM/OpenAI serving run, output-quality evaluation, or RDMA/multi-node fault injection was performed; those are not implied by the transport results. ## Review follow-up — sync registration Commit `6ed41ccf1b` routes `add_remote_peer()` through `add_remote_peer_async(...).result()`, so synchronous and asynchronous builds share the single registration worker. Superseded synchronous registrations now raise, and the rollback check documents its serialization requirement. Validation of this follow-up used macOS/Python 3.12 with the real `NixlTransport` constructor and a mocked external NIXL boundary: | Check | Original PR `18349008c` | With follow-up | | --- | --- | --- | | Race regression plus sync/async superseded-registration cases | 2 failed, 1 passed | 3 passed within the full suite | | Complete data-transport file | 64 passed before adding the regressions | 66 passed | | Full P2P suite | Previously recorded server result: 319 passed | 321 passed | | Applicable pre-commit hooks | Previously passed | Passed, including pinned Ruff, mypy, and test tethering | The before-fix failures were `assert set() == {'peer'}` (the newer registration's agent was removed) and `Failed: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError` (superseded sync registration returned silently). ```bash # With the final tests and original nixl.py from 18349008c: .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py \ -k 'failed_registration_keeps_newer_sync_agent or registration_landing_after_remove_is_discarded' -q # 2 failed, 1 passed, 63 deselected # With the follow-up: .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p -q # 321 passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/data/nixl.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py # All applicable hooks passed ``` Both baseline and changed runs emit the same missing generated `vllm._version` warning. title: [Bugfix] Fix MOSS-Audio meta initialization
author: hlin99
body:
Root cause: Model Runner V2 constructs the audio tower on the meta device on non-first pipeline stages. MOSS-Audio reads a tensor value with `.item()` during encoder initialization, which fails on meta tensors.

Fix: Compute the downsampled mel dimension with equivalent Python integer arithmetic instead of tensor operations.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not store sliding-window chunks with null blocks
author: pepmach
body:
## Overview Fixes #63653. With offloaded chunks of several GPU blocks, `OffloadingConnector` could store a sliding-window chunk that contained a null block. A later CPU hit then loaded the never-written slot as KV, and the request's output changed with no error. ## Claims - A sliding-window chunk is stored only when every block that the store mask marks reachable is present, so a CPU hit no longer loads a slot that no store wrote. - One-block chunks and full-attention groups behave as before. A one-block chunk with a null block was already skipped, and full-attention block tables hold no null blocks. ## Validation Two new tests: - `test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`: scheduler level, sync and async scheduling. - `test_cpu_offloading_sliding_window_partial_chunk` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py`: LLM level, CUDA, `google/gemma-3-1b-it` with `blocks_per_chunk=8` and `store_threshold=2`. Request B's GPU hit ends mid-chunk, which leaves null sliding-window blocks inside chunk 0, and B stores that chunk. The test asserts that this hit length is reached, so the case is exercised, and that a request hitting the chunk on the CPU tier produces the same output as a cold run. Scheduler-level test without the fix (main `24324ef0`), failing at the store check for request B: ``` $ pytest --tb=short -q "tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored" tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py:2299: in test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/utils.py:680: in run E AssertionError FAILED ...::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored[True] FAILED ...::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored[False] 2 failed in 1.11s ``` Line 2299 is `runner.run(decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID], expected_stored=((0, 0), (0, 1)))`: on main, B also stores sliding-window block 1 without block 0. With the fix, `2 passed in 1.29s`. LLM-level test: not run on a GPU, because I don't have one. CI runs it on CUDA. I ran its helper `_sliding_window_partial_chunk_test` on CPU against a tiny random Gemma-3 (512-token window, GPU block 32, 8 blocks per chunk). The offload copy was done by an out-of-tree spec that runs `gpu_worker.py`'s transfer code with `memmove` in place of the CUDA kernel (described in the linked issue). - On main it fails at `assert out_c.outputs[0].token_ids == cold_c.outputs[0].token_ids`: C's greedy tokens change, and C loaded 114,688 bytes that no store wrote. - With the fix it passes, and C loads nothing. End to end on CPU with the same spec, comparing C's output against a run without offloading: | Run | C's CPU hit | Loaded bytes no store wrote | C's logprobs vs no offloading | |---|---|---|---| | main, 64-token window, 2 blocks per chunk | 64 tokens | 16,384 | off by 0.11 to 0.15 at every step | | main, chunk-aligned control | 64 tokens | 0 | identical | | main, 512-token window, 8 blocks per chunk | 512 tokens | 114,688 (7 blocks) | off by 0.18 to 0.39; 3 of the top-5 first tokens change | | this PR, both shapes | none (recomputed) | 0 | identical | Model evaluation: the fix changes only which chunks get stored, so an affected request recomputes a chunk instead of loading it. An accuracy benchmark wouldn't isolate the bug, because the bug needs a specific hit-then-evict pattern. The runs above construct that pattern and compare against a run without offloading. The LLM-level test does the same in CI against a cold run on `google/gemma-3-1b-it`. Suites, run with `pytest -q ` on CPU (macOS arm64, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`) at `24324ef0`: | Suite | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` | 628 passed, 2 skipped | 630 passed, 2 skipped | | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py` | 2 failed, 3 skipped | 2 failed, 4 skipped (the same 2 failures) | | `tests/v1/core` | 1059 passed, 1 failed, 4 errors | the same counts and the same failing tests | | `tests/v1/kv_offload` (without `cpu/test_gpu_worker.py`) | 718 passed, 54 failed, 10 skipped | the same counts and the same failing tests | The failures on both sides are environment limits on this Mac: - the two tiering tests download a gated model; - in `tests/v1/core`, the hybrid test model needs `causal_conv1d_weight_pack`, which the CPU build lacks, and one test's block size is unsupported; - the `kv_offload` failures are `cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py`, which needs `/dev/shm`. `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including ruff 0.14.0, typos, mypy and the Buildkite test-wiring check. The branch merges cleanly into main `237d2ffd`. On that merge, the scheduler-level test, the LLM-level helper on CPU and the `offloading_connector` suite (632 passed, 2 skipped) all pass. ## Details Root cause, with lines at `24324ef0`: - A GPU prefix-cache hit leaves sliding-window blocks before the window null (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1004-1037`). A sliding-window free also zeroes pending store positions (`offloading/scheduler.py:1503-1522`). - With the default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, a GPU hit lands on an earlier prompt's replay boundary. That boundary is block-aligned but not necessarily chunk-aligned, so the null run can end mid-chunk. - `_build_store_jobs` selected chunks by their last block only (`offloading/scheduler.py:1880-1891`, `1917`), then dropped null blocks from the store spec (`1995`). - The worker wrote part of the chunk (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py:635-654`), while `complete_store` marked all of it ready (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py:370-387`). The fix adds one check to key selection. After the existing reachability test, a chunk is skipped if any block the store mask marks reachable is null. With no mask, any null block skips it. No GPU block exists to copy for that position, so the chunk can't be completed. A later request that would have hit this chunk computes it instead: it loses a partial CPU hit and avoids loading stale KV. Null blocks that the mask marks unreachable are still allowed. A request whose window excludes them holds null blocks there too, and its load skips those slots. Test changes: - `RequestRunner` rejected `blocks_per_chunk > 1` whenever custom KV cache groups were passed. It now accepts them when every group uses the runner's block size. - `_wait_for_prefix_cache_reset` takes `reset_connector`, so the LLM-level test can clear the CPU tier before its cold run. Not a duplicate: as of 2026-10-26, no open or closed issue or PR reports this bug. I ran 20 keyword searches over issues and PRs and checked the 171 open PRs that touch the offloading connector or `kv_offload/`. The closest are these two: - #57216 guards the end-of-request partial-chunk store against null blocks. This PR covers full chunks. - Draft #61426 moves this loop into `store_triggers/on_compute.py` and keeps the last-block check. If it lands first, this check goes there. AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) found this bug with a randomized checker over the offloading connector. It also wrote the reproductions, the CPU end-to-end harness, both tests and the fix, and ran the suites above. I reviewed every changed line and reran the tests and the CPU end-to-end check. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer. ---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][OBJ] Namespace object keys by blocks_per_chunk
author: Vedant-Agarwal
body:
## Overview Fixes #63654. The OBJ tier built its `FileMapper` without `blocks_per_file`, so its namespace digest ignored `blocks_per_chunk`. This passes `blocks_per_file=offloading_spec.blocks_per_chunk`, as the fs and p2p tiers already do. ## Claims - OBJ tiers with different `blocks_per_chunk` no longer map an `OffloadKey` to the same object key, so a hit can't load a chunk written with a different size and layout. - OBJ keys now follow the same run-configuration digest as the fs tier, as `kv_offloading_usage.md` documents. - No change for the default `blocks_per_chunk=1`: the digest already hashed `blocks_per_file=1`, so existing buckets keep their keys. ## Validation New test `test_obj_tier_namespace_includes_blocks_per_chunk` builds two tiers that only differ in `blocks_per_chunk` (1 and 4) and compares the object key for the same `OffloadKey`. Without the fix (on main): ``` $ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py::test_obj_tier_namespace_includes_blocks_per_chunk E AssertionError: assert 'test/840e65f0//test_model_c32b90738e47_r0/000/00_g0/0000000000000001.bin' != 'test/840e65f0//test_model_c32b90738e47_r0/000/00_g0/0000000000000001.bin' 1 failed ``` With the fix: ``` $ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py 39 passed $ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py 646 passed, 10 skipped ``` Not run end to end against a real object store (no NIXL OBJ setup available here); the change only affects the key namespace, which the test checks directly. ## Details The test stubs in `test_obj_tier.py` are `SimpleNamespace` specs without `blocks_per_chunk`, which every real `OffloadingSpec` has (`base.py`), so they gain `blocks_per_chunk=1`, matching their config. All three `FileMapper.from_offloading_spec` callers now pass the same value. Happy to instead derive it inside `from_offloading_spec` so a future tier can't miss it, if you prefer. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Mark the session dead when its ConnectAck send fails
author: nilig
body:
## Overview `P2PSession._poll_registration` clears the pending registration before sending `ConnectAckMsg`. If that send raises, the exception escapes `poll()` and the local session remains alive. Route the ack through `_do_send` so a send exception marks the local connection dead and allows the manager to reap its pending work. Part of #63602 (gap 5). ## Claims - A raised `ConnectAckMsg` send error marks the local connection dead instead of escaping `poll()`. - The manager can reap that session and fail its pending local work without waiting for the request deadline, provided polling and cleanup can progress. - The ack still bypasses the pre-ack queue. Successful sends also refresh the session's activity timestamp. - This does not guarantee immediate remote notification or bound a blocking transport send. ## Validation New test `TestConnectHandshake::test_failed_ack_send_marks_connection_dead` (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py`): a peer's registration completes, the ack send raises, and the connection must be dead after `poll()`. The existing `test_sessions.py::TestDisconnect::test_send_failure_marks_connection_dead` covers send-error handling. The existing `test_manager.py::TestConnectionDeathMidTransfer::test_dead_connection_with_pending_work_surfaces_failures` covers failure of a dead session's pending load, and separately asserts that an unbound store stays parked for its own timeout. Neither is an end-to-end failed-ack-send test. Run on CPU in `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:cb9bc64f0f038c2c2ebf13b31248fb87aca40c356c3d20f363be087cfcff1fcd` with this tree mounted (`uv venv --system-site-packages`, then `pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p`): ``` # new test, against the base commit's session.py E ConnectionError: simulated dead connection FAILED tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py::TestConnectHandshake::test_failed_ack_send_marks_connection_dead 1 failed # new test, with this change 1 passed # the two existing dead-connection tests above, with this change 2 passed # full P2P suite (tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p), with this change FAILED tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestBidirectionalManager::test_lookup_expiry_allows_zmq_reconnect 1 failed, 311 passed ``` `test_lookup_expiry_allows_zmq_reconnect` also fails on the unmodified base. Run alone, alternating between the base and this change in one CPU container, it failed 16 of 20 times on each, always in the `poll_until(both_ready)` after the reconnect (`test_manager.py:1341`); no difference was observed in this sample. The failing full-suite run with this change contains no `send of connect_ack failed` warning, so the ack-send exception handler was not observed; successful acks still go through the changed direct-send path. Its cause is unresolved. Integration check on GPUs of this change together with a rollback patch for gap 4 (not part of this PR; gap 4 is handled in #63628), #63207 and #63498, on nightly `8e2beaa3b`: three single-GPU Qwen3-0.6B engines on one H200 node, mlx5 InfiniBand, NIXL 1.5.0, 1 run per case. A probe seeds a fresh ~2K-token prefix on a source every 200 ms and asks consumer A to pull it. A probe counts as pulled when A submitted the P2P load and the source logged `finalize ... success=True ... send_done=True` for it. Times run from SIGCONT, or from the switch to the replacement pod, to the HTTP request start and finish of the first such probe: | fault on source B | probes to B or its replacement pulled after recovery | first verified pull after recovery, request start / finish | probes to healthy source C pulled | |---|---|---|---| | none | 700/700 | - | 625/625 | | SIGSTOP 60 s, then SIGCONT | 242/242 (from SIGCONT + 40 s) | 8.7 s / 10.1 s | 616/616 | | pod force-deleted, replacement | 400/400 (from switch + 10 s) | 0.5 s / 0.8 s | 848/848 | | pod deleted gracefully, replacement | 400/400 (from switch + 10 s) | 0.3 s / 0.5 s | 839/839 | Every successful handshake in these runs sent its ack through `_do_send`. The runs do not establish that the ack-send exception handler was exercised; they check that the combined stack does not regress. No `LLM`/`RemoteOpenAIServer` fault-injection regression is included. The fault is injected at the external transport boundary in the focused tests above. We have not implemented an entry-point fixture for this failure; asking maintainers to accept this test scope. ## Details `_do_send` is the existing guarded direct-send path. It bypasses the pre-ack queue and marks the local connection dead when a send raises. Other raw-send paths are outside this change. ---

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4] Give zero and subnormal mono MXFP8 groups vLLM's scale code
author: AndreasKaratzas
body: - `stages/moe.py` (`vllm_mx_code`) and `attention/device.py` (`mx_code`) in the DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1 mono decode kernels: when `q = RN(max(amax, FLT_MIN) / 448)` is an f32 subnormal, return code 0 for `q <= 2^-127` and 1 above it, instead of the exponent-bit result, which is always 1 The four copies take the E8M0 scale code from the exponent bits of `q`. Their docstrings, and vLLM's `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`, give `clamp(ceil(log2 q) + 127, 0, 254)`. For a subnormal `q` the bit trick gives 1, so every group with `amax <= 448 * 2^-127`, including all-zero groups, gets code 1 where vLLM gives 0. The monokernel I/O tests in #63486 catch this, and it blocks that PR. In practice, zero groups (for example a zeroed norm-weight group) only get a different scale byte and still dequantize to 0. bf16-valued inputs never dequantize differently. Only the f32 attention-output quant (XO) could, for groups with amax below 2.6e-36. | amax | q | before | after | vLLM rule (Triton / torch op) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0 | FLT_MIN / 448 | 1 | 0 | 0 / 0 | | 1e-36 | subnormal | 1 | 0 | 0 / 0 | | 448 * 2^-127 | 2^-127 | 1 | 0 | 0 / 0 | | prev(448 * 2^-126) | rounds to 2^-126 | 1 | 1 | 1 / 1 | | 1.0 | normal | 119 | 119 | 119 / 119 | | check (MI355X) | before | after | |---|---|---| | every non-negative finite f32 amax (2,139,095,040), each of the 4 copies | 73,400,322 wrong codes | 0 | | `test_mono_primitives.py -k scale_codes` (#63486) | 4 failed | 5 passed | | DSv4.1 layer test, hard case with a zeroed norm group | 48 of 7680 codes wrong per quant, 16/16 runs | 0, 10/10 runs | | f32-valued tiny groups, dequantized vs vLLM | 195,270 elements differ | 0 | Decode step time, 20-step CUDA graph, median of interleaved runs (DSv4.1 TP4: 10 runs per arm; DSv4-Pro TP8: pooled runs), with #63576 applied in every DSv4.1 arm: | case | before (us) | after (us) | delta | |---|---|---|---| | DSv4.1 1x1, index source | 75.94 | 76.66 | +0.94% | | DSv4.1 1x6, index source | 102.86 | 103.03 | +0.17% | | DSv4.1 8x6, index source | 314.73 | 314.95 | +0.07% | | DSv4.1 8x6, hard case | 170.75 | 170.67 | -0.05% | | DSv4-Pro 1x1 | 90.69 | 90.79 | +0.11% | | DSv4-Pro 1x7 | 124.45 | 124.41 | -0.03% | | DSv4-Pro 64x1 | 412.24 | 412.84 | +0.15% | An unchanged-code control arm moved -0.21% to +0.11% on DSv4-Pro and +0.10 us on DSv4.1. The one case outside that is DSv4.1 at one row with an index source: +0.7 us in two 5-round sets and +0.3 us in a follow-up. The same step without the index source doesn't move, and K1's eager device time is unchanged (18.22 vs 18.05 us). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. title: [Bugfix] Initialize valid ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE dummy scales
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview Initialize ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE dummy quantization scales to valid positive values. Random initialization could produce nonpositive block/input scales and inconsistent gate/up global scales when benchmarking with `--load-format dummy`. ## Claims - Dummy NVFP4 MoE weights use positive scales and matching gate/up global scales through the existing `dummy_weight_value` loader contract. - A regression test constructs a small Qwen3 MoE through `LLM`, confirms the FlashInfer TRTLLM backend and valid scales, and generates two tokens with finite returned log probabilities. - The ModelOpt documentation explains dummy benchmarking and the FlashInfer MegaMoE backend flag. ## Validation One GB200 GPU, BF16 activations, NVFP4 dummy experts, FlashInfer TRTLLM, eager execution: | Check | Without fix | With fix | | --- | --- | --- | | `test_modelopt_nvfp4_dummy_scales` | Failed: `AssertionError: w13_weight_scale` at `assert (values > 0).all()` | 1 passed, 22 deselected; two generated tokens and finite returned log probabilities | The same test command was run with the production change removed and restored: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HF_HOME=/mnt/lustre/hf-models \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py \ -k test_modelopt_nvfp4_dummy_scales -x -v -s ``` Relevant before/after output: ```text Before: AssertionError: w13_weight_scale assert tensor(False, device='cuda:0') 1 failed, 22 deselected, 1 warning in 15.15s After: 1 passed, 22 deselected, 1 warning in 16.22s ``` The test runs in the existing B200 Quantized MoE Buildkite step, whose dependencies already cover both changed Python files. ```bash .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py \ tests/quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py \ docs/features/quantization/modelopt.md git diff --check ``` Both passed, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown lint, and test tethering. A fresh-agent local-checkout documentation search found and quoted the dummy benchmarking section. A separate real-LLM smoke run on this PR checkout also passed with two GB200 GPUs, TP2/EP2, the same tiny Qwen3 MoE configuration, and `moe_backend="flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl"`: two generated tokens with finite log probabilities. This uses the native dummy loader, without a benchmark wrapper. No real-checkpoint quality evaluation was run: this change only supplies values consumed by dummy weight initialization, and dummy outputs are unsuitable for quality evaluation. ## Details The generic dummy initializer samples floating-point values around zero. NVFP4 MoE quantization scales require positive values, and the fused gate/up projections share a global scale. The change assigns block scales `1.0`, global weight scales `1e-3`, and input scales `1e-2` using parameter metadata already supported by the loader. It adds no inference-time work; normal checkpoint loading continues to use checkpoint values. Duplicate-work searches on 2026-10-26 for `ModelOpt dummy`, `NVFP4 scales`, `MegaMoE dummy`, and `"dummy_weight_value"` found no open PR implementing this dummy initialization fix. Related #55073 reconciles differing scales in real checkpoints, #45320 rejects missing checkpoint scales, and #55997 refactors ModelOpt MoE methods; they address different behavior. There is no associated issue. AI assistance was used to implement, validate, review, and document this change. ---
