title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Bump fastokens to 0.3.5
author: BugenZhao
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The Rust frontend pins fastokens 0.2.1, whose regex split cache can give a prompt different token ids from Hugging Face depending on the previous prompt encoded on the same thread. This PR bumps fastokens to 0.3.5, which fixes the cache, and keeps the current non-truncating behavior. It covers the Rust frontend part of #63467.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong token ids for prompts that share a ≥4 KiB prefix with the previous prompt on the same thread and diverge inside a whitespace run, e.g. deeper indentation or a newline after trailing spaces. No error is raised today: the wrong ids decode to the same text.
- Ignores `tokenizer.json`'s `truncation` and `padding` in both backends, as the Python frontend does: transformers resets both on every call, and a few published checkpoints set `truncation.max_length` to 512–4096. fastokens 0.3.4+ starts applying them on encode, so the fastokens path clears them to keep main's behavior. The `tokenizers` fallback already applied them on main, silently cutting prompts for such a checkpoint when fastokens couldn't load it; it now clears them too.
- Tokenizers that 0.2.1 rejects (e.g. a `Replace` normalizer or `ByteFallback`/`Strip` decoders, as in Gemma 4) now load with fastokens instead of the `tokenizers` fallback.

## Validation

Served reproducer with `vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and `vllm-mock-engine` (aarch64). For each pair, one client sends B once, then A and B alternately 20 times to `/tokenize`, and compares each result with Hugging Face `tokenizers`:

| Pair | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ~6 KB prose + `def f():` with 4- vs 8-space indent | B wrong 20/21 | 0/21 |
| 5000 spaces + `x` vs 5000 spaces + `\n` | B wrong 20/21 | 0/21 |

A calls were right on both builds. The same pairs at crate level are wrong on 0.2.1 and right on 0.3.4 for the Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Llama 3.2, gpt-oss and GLM tokenizers. DeepSeek-V3.2 is right on both.

- New test `fastokens_encode_does_not_depend_on_previous_input` fails on main and passes here. The fixture uses a split regex with Qwen's whitespace alternatives and a `Ġ Ġ` merge, so the pieces' boundaries show up in the ids.
- `assert_ordinary_matches_added_empty` now asserts for both backends that the fixture's `truncation` is ignored. The fastokens test fails without `set_truncation(None)`, and the HF test fails without `with_truncation(None)`.
- `cargo test --workspace` (2307 passed) and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- Gemma 4, TinyLlama, ERNIE-4.5 and LFM2.5 tokenizers, which move off the `tokenizers` fallback: 0 encode and 0 decode differences from Hugging Face on 400 text slices each (37 B–40 KB).
- Encode cost with the Qwen3 tokenizer, 320 prompts of 128 KB each, 32 cores. CPU time per prompt drops from 8.1 / 7.0 / 6.0 ms to 1.25 / 1.13 / 1.10 ms at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32. Wall time per batch drops from 296 / 115 / 89 ms to 54 / 53 / 52 ms.

## Details

Root cause: fastokens' regex `Split` keeps a thread-local cache of the previous input's matches. When the next input shares at least 4096 bytes with it, matches ending inside the shared prefix are reused. Whitespace alternatives such as `\s+(?!\S)` and `\s*[\r\n]+` depend on bytes past the end of the match: in `"    x"` the run stops one space early, and with `\n` there the whole run is one piece. So a reused match near the divergence point can be wrong. crusoecloud/fastokens#78 (released in 0.3.4) reuses only matches that end before the whitespace run leading up to the unseen bytes. 0.3.5 adds a Python-binding deadlock fix and opt-in caches, and does not change the default encode path.

Changes in `hf.rs`:

- fastokens 0.3 adds `Decoder` variants. `is_byte_level_only` treats `Fuse` as a no-op, as before (0.2.1 parsed it as an empty `Sequence`). The new transforming decoders disqualify the byte-level decode fast path.
- `new_fastokens` and `new_hf` clear truncation and padding after loading.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Never block in ZmqConnection.send()
author: liranschour
body: ## Purpose Part of #63602 (gap 1). `ControlConnection.send()` is documented as non-blocking (`control/base.py`: "ControlConnection.send() must not block"), but `ZmqConnection.send()` called `dealer.send(data)` without `NOBLOCK`, at libzmq's default `SNDHWM` and with no `SNDTIMEO`. Once the queue toward a peer that stops reading fills, the send blocks. Every caller holds the tiering manager lock: the tier-poll thread holds it for a whole round, and `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._acquire_step()` waits on it with no timeout. A blocked send therefore stalls healthy-peer servicing and the engine's next scheduler step. This PR: - Sends with `zmq.NOBLOCK` at an explicit `SNDHWM` (1000, unchanged from the libzmq default but no longer implicit) and raises `ConnectionError` when the queue is full. `P2PSession._do_send` already marks the connection dead on any send error, so a stalled peer is reaped and its pending work fails over to local prefill. #63664 routes the ConnectAck send through the same path. - Bounds DEALER `LINGER` to 500 ms. While writing the test I found that, with the default (-1), closing a DEALER that still has messages queued for an unreachable peer makes `Context.destroy(linger=0)` hang forever. The context-level linger only applies to sockets that are still open. Before this change that path was rare, since a full queue blocked the sender first; now that queued-then-dead is the normal failure path, it has to be bounded. - Leaves `ZMQ_IMMEDIATE` at its default of 0. With `IMMEDIATE=1`, a `NOBLOCK` send fails before the TCP connect completes, which would break the `ConnectMsg` sent right after `connect()`. On the issue's policy question (fail now vs. retry on later polls): this fails now. Control messages are small, so a full queue means the peer went 1000 messages without reading while its TCP connection stayed up. That isn't short-lived backpressure, and a retry outbox would need its own bound plus ordering against the pre-ack queue. Not a duplicate: the only open PRs referencing #63602 are #63628 (gap 4) and #63664 (gap 5). #63207 changes the DEALER monitor teardown, not `send()`. ## Test plan New `TestZmqTransportConnectivity::test_send_raises_instead_of_blocking_when_queue_full`: a real DEALER connects to a port with no listener, with `_SNDHWM` patched to 2. `send()` must raise `ConnectionError` within 1 s, and `transport.close()` must return. ``` venv/bin/pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_zmq_transport.py::TestZmqTransportConnectivity::test_send_raises_instead_of_blocking_when_queue_full venv/bin/pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/control/zmq.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_zmq_transport.py ``` ## Test results - New test with the old blocking `send()`: hangs in `zmq/sugar/socket.py:send`, called from `ZmqConnection.send` (faulthandler dump at 20 s). - New test with this change, but without the linger bound: `send()` raises, then the test hangs in `ZmqTransport.close()` → `Context.destroy()`. - With this change: passes. - Full P2P suite (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p`): 312 passed, CPU-only (pyzmq 27.1.0, libzmq 4.3.5). - pre-commit: passed. No model evaluation: this changes only control-plane failure handling, not outputs. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? title: [Bugfix][Perf][ROCm] RDNA launch config for kernel_paged_attention_2d
author: lijipeng787
body:
## Overview On RDNA (`on_gfx1x()`), launch `kernel_paged_attention_2d` with `num_stages=1` and 4 / 8 / 16 warps by tile size, for tiles of 32+ tokens or ≥ 4096 elements. This fixes the gfx1201 Pattern A decode failures of #62697 that remain after #63268, and speeds up decode on gfx1100 and gfx1201. No open PR changes this launch config; #45916 and #58156 (open) add split-KV decode for RDNA and leave it as is. #58156 edits the same launch call, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. ## Claims - gfx1201, KV cache < 2 GiB: the new test shape and the #62697 reproducer case `p1-d128-bs528-fp16` fail on main (NaN rows, GPU memory fault) and pass with this PR. Pattern B (the cache writer) is not addressed. - Decode throughput, PR / main at batch 1 / 32, with GSM8K unchanged: | model | gfx1100 | gfx1201 | |---|---|---| | gemma-3-1b-it | 1.51× / 1.57× | 1.94× / 1.81× | | Qwen3.5-9B | 1.15× / 1.10× | 1.07–1.09× / 1.14–1.16×* | | Qwen3-4B `--block-size 32` | 1.30× / 1.50× | 1.12× / 1.05× | `LLM(..., attention_backend="ROCM_ATTN")` (the RDNA default), CUDA graphs, 1024-token random prompts, 256 output tokens; GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy. Ratio: median of 4 adjacent main/PR run pairs (2 GPUs × 2); on gfx1100 every pair is within 2% of it. \* gfx1201 runs fall into one of two throughput levels for both variants; these ratios compare runs at the same level, one per level. ## Validation W7900 (gfx1100) and R9700 (gfx1201), ROCm 10.0, Triton 3.8.0: - `test_prefix_prefill.py --optional`: no failures with this PR. On gfx1201 main, 4 nodes fail: the new shape, plus three `test_contexted_kv_attention_f32` nodes that hang. - Of 41 kernel cases from an earlier failure sweep, 35 fail on main; none fail with this PR. - `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` and pre-commit pass.

E Mismatched elements: 4096 / 21860352 (0.0%) E Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (5336, 0, 0) (up to 0.0001 allowed) Warning: Queue error - HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT FAILED tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py::test_qwen3_nonstandard_block_size[False-chunked_prefill_paged_decode-cuda:0-dtype0-32-4-128-528] ``` This PR: ``` PASSED tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py::test_qwen3_nonstandard_block_size[False-chunked_prefill_paged_decode-cuda:0-dtype0-32-4-128-528] ```
Test environment - GPUs: Radeon PRO W7900 (gfx1100) and Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), several of each; one GPU per test process, no other workload on it - Host: Ubuntu 24.04.3, kernel 6.8.0-138, amdgpu 6.16.13 - Container: `vllm/rocm10.0.0_rdna_ubuntu24.04_py3.14_pytorch_2.12.0_vllm_0.28.0.dgpu:v2.1.0`; Python 3.14.7, torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0 - vLLM: main @ a7407ab44 vs this branch, Python sources mounted over the image; `_C` / `_rocm_C` built from a7407ab44 (`PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx1100;gfx1201"`) and shared by both
## Details - Trigger: Triton uses AMD buffer ops for tensors ≤ 2 GiB. Turning them off, a KV cache > 2 GiB, or `num_stages=1` each remove the failures. Other RDNA parts were not measured. - Only `ROCM_ATTN` calls this kernel; the opt-in `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` (#59132) uses its own kernel and is unchanged. - No `LLM`-level test: the models we ran on main (Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3-1.7B / Qwen3-4B `--block-size 32`, with KV caches down to 0.52 GiB) did not hit the failing shapes, so the regression test is at kernel level. - CI has no RDNA runner, so the new test only catches regressions on gfx12. ---

title: [Bugfix][CPU] Run encoder-only attention bidirectionally in CPU_ATTN
author: GuSangmo
body:
## Overview `CPU_ATTN` runs causal attention for layers built as a plain `Attention(attn_type=ENCODER_ONLY)`, so EmbeddingGemma 2 and ColQwen3.5 silently return wrong embeddings on CPU. The CPU metadata builder now treats encoder-only groups as non-causal. ## Claims - Fixes CPU output for EmbeddingGemma 2, ColQwen3.5 with the bidirectional contract, and `openpangu` with `is_causal=False`. - EmbeddingGemma 2 now uses `EncoderOnlyAttention`, like BERT and ModernBERT. - No GPU change. The GPU backends already run `ENCODER_ONLY` attention bidirectionally. ## Validation ``` pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py -k test_encoder_only_attention_ignores_default_causal ``` - main: 2 failed. 99% of elements mismatched, max abs diff 3.05, and the output matches a causal reference within 4.8e-7. - This PR: 2 passed. `test_cpu_attn.py -k "encoder or dynamic_causal"` (74 passed), `test_embedding_gemma2.py` and pre-commit also pass. Model checks, outside CI because CPU CI does not run these model tests: | Model | Without fix | With fix | |---|---|---| | EmbeddingGemma 2, real weights, x86 CPU (v0.32.0), cosine vs sentence-transformers (text, image, video) | 0.75–0.98 | ≥ 0.99996 | | ColQwen3.5, real weights, x86 CPU (v0.32.0), max change in earlier tokens when only the last token differs | 0.0 (causal) | 0.161 (bidirectional) | | `openpangu` with `is_causal=False`, tiny dummy weights, same check | 0.0 (causal) | 1.4e-3 (bidirectional) | The ColQwen3.5 and `openpangu` rows check future-token dependence and do not compare outputs against a reference implementation. With bidirectional attention, changing the last token changes the outputs of the earlier tokens, while with causal attention it does not. ## Details Both model runners build encoder-only `CommonAttentionMetadata` with the default `causal=True`. `EncoderOnlyAttention` clears it, but a plain `Attention(ENCODER_ONLY)` does not. The GPU backends ignore the flag for encoder attention, while `CPU_ATTN` passes it to the scheduler metadata and the kernel, so the fix is in the builder where both are derived. **Why the EmbeddingGemma 2 change.** The HF reference runs every layer bidirectionally without a KV cache, which is what `EncoderOnlyAttention` encodes. BERT, ModernBERT and the `is_causal=False` paths of Llama, Qwen3 and Gemma 3 already use it, and the encoder-only runner's comment that the encoder builder forces `causal=False` assumes it. This change alone already fixes EmbeddingGemma 2 on CPU: the EmbeddingGemma 2 row above was measured with only this change applied. This is not a duplicate of the open EmbeddingGemma 2 PRs. They fix the Triton prefill kernel on GPUs, while this PR fixes how the CPU backend applies the causal flag, a path those PRs do not touch. **To reviewers.** - The EmbeddingGemma 2 commit does not change output once the builder is fixed. Keep it for consistency with the other encoder models, or drop it? - The new test covers the CPU builder and kernel directly. Would you also like an end-to-end test through `LLM`? The real checkpoints are too heavy for CPU CI, but a tiny dummy-weight `openpangu` model with `is_causal=False` reproduces the bug in a few seconds. ---

title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Reject stacked weights that received only some shards
author: Josephasafg
body: ## Overview `track_weights_loading` only diffs parameter names, so `qkv_proj.weight` counts as loaded once any one shard is written. A checkpoint missing every `v_proj` loads cleanly and serves uninitialized rows. Follow-up to #55911 agreed with @hmellor. ## Claims - A stacked parameter (`MergedColumnParallelLinear`, `QKVParallelLinear` and their subclasses) that received only some shards now fails at load, naming the parameter and the missing shard ids. - Same gate as the existing check (unquantized by default, `enable_weights_track` to force). Valid checkpoints are untouched. ## Validation `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_stacked_shard_tracking.py` → 7 passed. Qwen3-0.6B on H100, tensors deleted from the safetensors file, loaded via `LLM`: | Checkpoint | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | untouched | OK | OK | | all `v_proj` removed | loads, generates `!!!!!!!!` | `ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight.v', …}` | | `layers.3.mlp.up_proj` removed | loads, wrong text | `ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'model.layers.3.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight.1'}` | No eval needed: weights of a valid checkpoint are bitwise unchanged. ## Details New base `StackedColumnParallelLinear`: each `weight_loader`/`weight_loader_v2` records the shard it wrote on the param, and `pop_missing_shards()` reports expected shards that never arrived, then clears the record so a later load is graded on its own. Shards with zero rows on the rank are never expected. The loader runs it after the existing name check. `shard_ids` is now the single declaration per class. --- Need help on this PR? title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 token offset overflows in Qwen3.5 attention and GDN prefill kernels
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
_Requested by **Simon**_ ## Overview Fixes #63759. Several Triton kernels on the Qwen3.5 prefill path multiply an int32 token index by a row stride before adding it to a pointer. Triton passes integer arguments below 2^31 as int32, and `tl.program_id`, `tl.arange` and the int32 `query_start_loc` are int32 too, so the offset wraps once `token * stride >= 2^31`. The result is wrong outputs or an illegal memory access. This PR computes those offsets in int64, one commit per kernel, each with a regression test. | Kernel | Triggers when (Qwen3.5-9B unless noted) | Fix | |---|---|---| | `_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate_kernel` (`fused_qk_norm_rope.py`) | token index >= 209,716 (qkv row stride 10,240), i.e. a 209,717-token step; hit in the startup profile run | `tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)` | | `store_cache_checkpoints_kernel` (`mamba/checkpoint.py`) | token index >= 174,763 (qkvz stride 12,288); real prefills with prefix caching only | int64 `token_idx` before `* x_stride_0` | | `_fused_post_conv_kernel` (`fused_gdn_prefill_post_conv.py`) | token index >= 262,144 (conv row stride 8,192) | int64 per-block base offset, int32 in-block offsets | | `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` (`chunk_delta_h.py`), spotted by reviewer Roberto (`LopezCastroRoberto`) | H=64: 2+ sequences with a later one starting at token >= 131,072 | int64 before `* V * K` (as `chunk_o.py`), also h0/ht | | `solve_tril` merge kernels (`solve_tril.py`) | H=64: a sequence with rows past 524,288, or one starting at >= 524,288 | int64 base offset and row index (16/32/64 kernels) | | `layer_norm_fwd_kernel` for `RMSNormGated` (`layernorm_guard.py`) | H=64: 262,145 tokens (`num_tokens * H * 128 >= 2^31`), when the `rms_norm_gated` custom op is enabled, e.g. `--enforce-eager` | int64 first row of each block | For the last three, thresholds double at H=32. The rest of the path (`causal_conv1d`, `layernorm_gated`, `gather_initial_states`, `scatter_states`, Mamba2 `ssd_checkpoint`, FlashInfer GDN prefill) already uses int64 offsets. The KDA and Qwen4Exp PLE exporters share the fixed checkpoint kernel. Related: #43166 (closed) fixed the same overflow in the CUDA `fused_qk_norm_rope` kernel; #51406 (open) enables the first kernel on ROCm, so ROCm gets the bug and this fix. ## Claims - On main, `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --max-num-batched-tokens 209717` (or 263,168) fails in the startup profile run with an illegal memory access in `_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate_kernel`. With this PR it starts and serves correctly. - With prefix caching, one prefill step can fill the budget. At 263,168, a 258,798-token prompt and a 262,784-token two-prompt batch serve correctly; without the checkpoint and post-conv commits they crash in those kernels. - Each kernel matches its previous output below its threshold and the reference above it. - Perf: about +1% on the gate kernel (141.2 vs 139.7 us at 8,192 tokens), +2.2% on post-conv, 0.2 us on the checkpoint export, and 0 to 3% on the follow-ups (`chunk_delta_h` 0% / -3.0%, `solve_tril` +1.1%, `rmsnorm_gated` +2.4 to +3.1%). ## Validation 1x B200, torch 2.14.0+cu132, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, main `ffcabb8c7a`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` at `c202236235`. "Base" is main plus only the new tests. ```bash pytest -v tests/kernels/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate.py -k int64_row_offset pytest -v tests/kernels/mamba/test_checkpoint_exporter.py -k int64_token_offset pytest -v tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py -k int64_token_offset pytest -v tests/kernels/fla/test_chunk_int64_offsets.py pytest -v tests/kernels/fla/test_fla_layernorm_guard.py -k int64_row_offset ``` - Every new test fails on base (77.1% / 93.4% of q mismatched for the gate and post-conv kernels, illegal memory access for the other four) and passes with this PR. Existing tests in these files, `tests/kernels/fla`, `test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py` and `test_gdn_output_projection.py` pass. - Server (`--max-num-batched-tokens` 209,717 and 263,168, prefix caching on, compiled and eager): base fails in the profile run; this PR finds needles near the start and end of a 196,883 / 258,798-token prompt, answers both prompts of the 262,784-token batch, scores gsm 8/8, and matches base outputs at the default budget of 16,384. - Latency: kernels timed side by side with `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph` (follow-ups with `do_bench`), median of alternating rounds; a base-vs-base control gave 1.000 and outputs are bitwise equal to base. ## Details - Tests run each kernel just past its boundary on a realistic layout (packed qkv/qkvz buffers, contiguous conv output) and compare those rows with a reference. They need about 4 to 21 GB, skip when free device memory is short, and take a few seconds each. The gate test's CI step did not list `fused_qk_norm_rope.py` in `source_file_dependencies`, so this PR adds it there and to the AMD mirror; the other tests run in steps that already depend on their kernels. - Post-conv: an int64 per-token offset vector is a one-line change but costs 4.4% instead of 2.2%, so the PR uses an int64 base pointer. For `rmsnorm_gated` and `solve_tril` both approaches timed the same, so the simpler diff is kept. - Not fixed here: at these budgets Qwen3.5-9B needs a lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` than 0.92, with or without this PR (FlashInfer autotune and compiled-graph OOMs). The runs above used 0.88 at 209,717 and 0.84 at 263,168. ---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][OBJ] Don't lose a completed transfer when telemetry is unavailable
author: sungsooha
body:
## Problem

In `obj/manager.py`, `_poll_active_transfers` calls `get_xfer_telemetry()` after the transfer completed, and the call sits outside any `try`. Builds compiled without telemetry raise there. The exception escapes the tier, so a finished job is lost.

This is the same defect as #63787 at a different call site. In the connector an enclosing `except Exception` catches the raise and reports a false failure. Here nothing catches it.

## Change

Guard the call. On a raise, log once and leave `transfer_time` as `None`. The job still reports success and the handle is still released. Only the timing is lost. Nothing changes when telemetry works.

## Tests

`test_telemetry_failure_does_not_lose_successful_transfer`: a raising `get_xfer_telemetry` must still give `JobResult(success=True)` with `transfer_time is None`. Without the guard this test does not pass, so it pins the bug. It sits next to `test_post_transfer_cleanup_failure_does_not_lose_result` and `test_release_xfer_failure_retries_without_losing_result`, which cover the same shape for the other cleanup calls.

It passes on the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image with this branch on `main` at `4f140a2`. `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass on both files.

## Scope

I did not reproduce this one in a live deployment, because we do not run the OBJ tier. It is the same bug shape at a call site with less protection. I found it while I fixed the connector.

## Relationship to #62650

#62650 covers a failed NIXL submission in the same file. This covers a telemetry raise after the transfer completed. Different functions, no shared code.

I applied both to current `main` in both orders. There is no conflict in `obj/manager.py` or `test_obj_tier.py`. Whichever lands first, the other needs no change. I can rebase on #62650 if that is easier to review.

I also ran the tiering tests with #62650 applied on top of this branch. The result is the same as with #62650 alone, so the two changes do not interfere.

## Note

Split out of #58038 for @orozery. The NIXL connector half is #63787.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] FlashInfer sparse MLA: launch at most 65535 tokens per trtllm-gen call
author: suiyoubi
body:
## Overview The FlashInfer sparse MLA kernel silently skips attention for every token of a forward pass with more than 65535 tokens (e.g. any full prefill step at `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`), returning uninitialized memory. This PR launches it in chunks of at most 65535 tokens that write into one preallocated output. Root cause on the FlashInfer side: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3125. ## Claims - Fixes the silent skip for `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` (**DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5 / GLM-5.3 DSA layers**) and for the prefill of `FLASHATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (FA4), which delegates prefill to the same kernel. Covers prefill, decode, mixed steps and DCP. - Steps with <= 65535 tokens issue the same single launch as before (decode and CUDA graphs are unchanged). - No extra memory: chunks write into slices of one output (and LSE) buffer. - The DCP softmax-stats workspace is sized for one launch (<= 65535 tokens) instead of `max_num_batched_tokens`. ## Validation | Check | Base (main) | This PR | |---|---|---| | New `test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_attends_tokens_past_grid_limit` (69635 tokens, rope and no-rope), SM10x | 2/2 fail (NaN past token 65535) | 2/2 pass | | 40-shot GSM8K, GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4, DEP2, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, 2 greedy runs | ~3 points below the unaffected baseline; server log full of `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE ... fmhaKernels.cuh` | at the unaffected baseline (within run-to-run spread); no launch errors | | 4 TP1 prefill workers at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` + DEP4 decode, 8K/1K sa-bench, C512/C1024 | prefill OOM with an earlier chunk + `torch.cat` version of this fix | no OOM; throughput at parity with that version, median TTFT slightly lower | | RULER-64K (NeMo-Skills, 13 tasks x 100), same server shape, `--max-model-len 131072` | overall ~35 points below this PR; NIAH / variable tracking 11-82 points lower per task; ~7.7K `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE ... fmhaKernels.cuh` lines while serving | NIAH (8 tasks) and variable tracking all at or near 100%; no launch errors | Run on SM107 GPUs; end-to-end results are relative. - The 40-shot GSM8K prompts are 7-8K tokens, above the DSA top-k, so sparse MLA runs. 5-shot GSM8K does not show the bug, because short prompts take the dense MHA prefill path. - The DCP/LSE path (one launch per chunk with an `lse` slice) was also checked against a PyTorch reference at 69635 tokens. That ran outside the committed tests, because DCP needs more than one GPU. ```bash pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py \ -k "past_grid_limit or model_scale or workspace or dcp_size" ```
Before / after test output Base (main 51d2a8559): ``` E Mismatched elements: 6884 / 8192 (84.0%) E Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0, 52) (up to 0.02 allowed) E Mismatched elements: 6850 / 8192 (83.6%) E Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0, 282) (up to 0.02 allowed) FAILED tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_attends_tokens_past_grid_limit[128-64-128] FAILED tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_attends_tokens_past_grid_limit[256-0-256] FAILED tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py::test_dcp_size_is_capped_at_one_launch 3 failed, 20 passed, 1883 deselected, 18 warnings in 52.12s ``` This PR: ``` 23 passed, 1883 deselected, 18 warnings in 52.08s ```
Why not FlashInfer's cum_seq_lens_q (#3131 / #3238)? Measured at kernel level (FP8 KV, top-k 2048, 16 and 64 heads, 1 to 131072 tokens): - trtllm-gen cannot return the LSE with `cum_seq_lens_q`, and DCP needs it. - `seq_lens` becomes per request. The static-sparse (rope) path uses it as each token's active top-k length, so rows shorter than the top-k width attend the `-1` padding and give wrong outputs. - Grouping tokens by real request launches `num_reqs x max_q_len` CTAs: one long prefill plus 511 decodes ran ~9.5x slower. - Packing tokens into uniform pseudo-requests (no-rope, no LSE) is bit-exact but no faster (within 1%): the MLA generation kernels still run one CTA per token. - For comparison, chunked launches cost the same per token as one launch. Chunk + `torch.cat` is 2-11% slower, and its extra output copy (8 GiB at 65536 tokens with 64 heads) is outside vLLM's memory profile.
## Details **Root cause.** `FlashInferMLASparseImpl._forward_mqa_kernel` passes every query token to `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` as its own request (`q.unsqueeze(1)`, `topk_indices.unsqueeze(1)`), and trtllm-gen maps requests to `gridDim.z`, whose CUDA limit is 65535. A larger launch makes `cuLaunchKernelEx` return `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`, which FlashInfer only prints to stderr. Found with a profile that showed zero sparse-MLA kernels in every 65536-token step. **Fix.** Allocate `out` (and `lse`) once and call the kernel on row slices of at most 65535 tokens, passing the matching `out` / `lse` slices. FlashInfer accepts caller-owned output, so no copy is needed. The trtllm-gen softmax-stats slab is carved per launch, so the DCP workspace only needs to cover one launch. **Limitations.** Steps with more than 65535 tokens issue one extra kernel launch per additional chunk. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and write this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above. Not a duplicate: no open vLLM PR touches this backend's 65535-token limit (searched "flashinfer_mla_sparse", "65535 flashinfer", "cum_seq_lens_q"). ---

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Guard NaN scores in gfx942 mono routing
author: frida-andersson
body:
## Overview

On gfx942, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--monokernel` and adaptive DSpark verification dies with `Memory access fault` during CUDA graph capture. The profile replays a context over KV blocks no request has written. The draft FFN then sees NaN router scores. `stage_route` ranks with `fx.max`, which keeps the NaN, so the same expert is picked twice and a later gather indexes off the slot table.

A NaN score now ranks last, and the winner ballot ignores lanes past the expert count. Both edits are in this patch. The KV fill is gone.

## Claims

- Without this patch, the serve command faults during the real capture and the server does not start.
- With both router edits and no KV zero, the real capture finishes and the server starts.
- Finite scores pick the same experts. TPOT on the shapes below stays with stock.
- No config or API change.

## Validation

MI325X, 4 GPUs, gfx942. The fault is on current main. The runs below are nightly `0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56` with main's Python over it, including this `stage_route`. The binaries were not rebuilt from this tree.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --monokernel --max-model-len 266240 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"greedy","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.9,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5],"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

| | without this patch | with this patch |
|---|---|---|
| real capture | `Memory access fault` on all four ranks after the DSpark graphs | finished in 60 s, 14.30 GiB |
| startup | engine core failed | `Application startup complete` |
| one completion | n/a | `Paris. The final answer is 123` |

Accuracy is a separate serve: monokernel, no speculative decoding. lm-eval `niah_single_1` at 4096, the first 8 of the 500 repeat-haystack samples. Stock and this patch both scored 1.0, and the 8 completions were identical.

Perf is that same serve, temperature 0, seed 0, 4 warmups. Mean / median TPOT:

| ISL / OSL / concurrency | prompts | stock | this patch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 / 128 / 4 | 64 | 5.43 / 5.23 ms | 5.42 / 5.23 ms |
| 1024 / 256 / 8 | 48 | 6.95 / 6.91 ms | 6.92 / 6.87 ms |
| 512 / 512 / 16 | 32 | 9.26 / 9.32 ms | 9.20 / 9.26 ms |

`stage_route` runs once per decode token. A longer prompt adds attention on every step, so these short prompts are where that cost can show up in TPOT. The output lengths are how many decode steps were averaged.

## Details

`batches_to_profile` is the only caller that passes a nonzero `context_len` into `_dummy_run`. `set_dummy_context` fills block tables with ids nobody has written, and the draft reads them. Two requests replay 10 tokens, the gfx942 monokernel's multi-tile draft FFN, and that launch faults.

`fx.max` keeps a NaN, and the NaN then compares equal to itself, so the draft shape emits the same expert id twice. The route counts winners with a bitmap, the count comes up short, and the gather reads off the slot table. Ranking the NaN as `-inf` after the max, and masking the ballot with `cursor < ept`, removes the duplicate. Kimi-K3 and MiniMax-M3 already drop NaN scores before ranking. The ballot mask is particular to this router, which holds 2 experts per lane and picks 3.

A local ranking check matches that. Unguarded draft NaN rows pick `[[0, 64, 0], [0, 64, 0]]`, bitmap 28 against 30 slots. With both edits the bitmap is 30 and there are no duplicates. Finite draft scores, and the target 384/6 shape, match with and without the guard. That check is the ranking logic, not the GPU kernel.

`stage_route` runs on every monokernel FFN launch, including target-only decode with adaptive verification off. The TPOT rows are that path.

Warmup and `profile_run` leave `context_len` at 0. `set_dcp_capture_context` is the other fabrication, only when `cp_size > 1`, and this PR does not change it.

`test_nan_draft_route_stays_in_range` launches that draft shape with NaN logits. With this patch it finishes, and each token's ids are unique:

```text
.                                                                        [100%]
1 passed, 12 deselected, 15 warnings in 7.91s
```

The same test against main's `moe.py`:

```text
Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (Agent handle: 0x44a297b0) on address 0x7ece472b5000. Reason: Unknown.
Fatal Python error: Aborted
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/accelerator/__init__.py", line 270 in synchronize
  File "/root/vllm/tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_mono_gfx942.py", line 732 in test_nan_draft_route_stays_in_range
EXIT:134
```

title: [Bugfix][Core] Defer async KV loads on HiSparse decoders until in-flight steps finish
author: vMaroon
body:
> **Edited by @MatthewBonanni:** per @LucasWilkinson's suggestion (vMaroon/vllm#2), every async load on a HiSparse decoder is now deferred until the in-flight step is processed; the reuse detection is gone. Overview, Claims, unit tests and Details are updated. The GLM-5.3 results were measured on the earlier revision, which deferred only loads into reused pages.

## Overview

Fixes KV corruption on HiSparse P/D decoders: a NIXL load can overwrite a GPU page while the previous step is still reading it. The request that was reading it emits garbage for the rest of its output. The fix makes the scheduler start every async load on a HiSparse decoder one step later, once the in-flight step is done.

Fixes #63811.

## When it happens

All four hold at once:

1. **HiSparse is on.** It returns a running request's clean resident pages to the GPU pool early; the request keeps reading them until the pool hands them out again.
2. **Async scheduling** (`max_concurrent_batches > 1`): step N is still on the GPU while step N+1 starts.
3. **KV arrives by an async load**: a P/D decoder with `NixlConnector` as consumer. NIXL posts its reads from the CPU, so nothing orders them after step N.
4. **In step N+1, the pool hands one of those returned pages to a new request whose KV comes through that load.**

NIXL then writes the new request's KV into the page while step N still reads it as the owner's KV. The owner's tokens from step N get wrong KV, later steps attend to them, and the output never recovers.

Unaffected: pages filled by a forward or a host restore (ordered on the CUDA stream), and engines without HiSparse or without an async KV load.

## Claims

- Fixes the symptom: output cuts mid-sentence into one repeated token (`locklocklock...` on GLM-5.3) until `max_tokens`, with MTP acceptance at 0.
- With HiSparse enabled, every async load is registered with the connector once the step in flight at its allocation is processed, normally on the next step. Other requests and steps run as before.
- Cost: each async-loaded request on a HiSparse decoder starts its load about one step later. No device sync, and no check for which pages were reused.
- Active only with HiSparse and `defer_block_free` (overlapping steps and a KV consumer); otherwise nothing is deferred.

## Validation

GLM-5.3 on H100, P/D. Decoder TP8 x DP2, MTP 3, MRV2, async scheduling, `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + `HiSparseConnector`), 20,000-block GPU pool. Traffic from `benchmarks/multi_turn`: 46-77K token prompts, 2-4K token answers. Counts are answers with at least 1,024 tokens. The rig runs the production image, a vLLM fork at `110cf9dc12`; "this PR" is this change applied to that fork's scheduler, block pool and KV cache manager (it applies cleanly).

| Free-queue order | Engine | Answers | Page handed to a NIXL load while read | Collapsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default | base | 133 | 0 | 0 |
| released pages first | base | 162 | 90 | 81 |
| released pages first | this PR | 173 | 106 (load held) | 0 |

- "Released pages first" is the one-line test change in step 1 below. It makes condition 4 frequent. Any free-block order is valid for the allocator, so a correct engine keeps its output quality under it.
- Collapsed: under 1.3 tokens per step (MTP drafts stop matching) from some point to the end of the answer, for at least 512 tokens. On base, collapse starts a median 35 tokens after the overwrite.
- Holds with this PR: 151 loads, each registered in the pass where step N had been processed, none earlier.
- TTFT of later turns (prompt mostly cached on the decoder) in the stress run: p50 1.98 s base, 2.07 s this PR. First-turn TTFT is not comparable across these runs because the prefill pods' prefix cache state differed.
- Default order with long answers (12-16K tokens, KV pool up to 88% full, base engine): 0 of 5,215 reuses of returned pages went to a NIXL-filled group, so the hold would not have triggered.
- Unit tests in `tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py`: a deferred load is registered after the in-flight step, it records its prefix cache stats (with `hits_by_source`) when it starts, a load without deferral registers at once, and an abort while deferred frees the blocks after the in-flight step.

**How to reproduce**

1. In `BlockPool.unpin_blocks`, replace `self.free_block_queue.append_n(released)` with `self.free_block_queue.prepend_n(released)`.
2. Serve GLM-5.3 P/D with a decoder as above. Run `benchmarks/multi_turn/benchmark_serving_multi_turn.py --num-clients 4 --max-active-conversations 8` on a generated config: 20 conversations, 10-12 turns, 15K common plus 30-50K prefix tokens, 1-2.5K token user turns, 2-4K token answers. The tool rejects reasoning-only streams, so accept `reasoning` deltas.
3. On base, within minutes, answers end in a repeated token and the `SpecDecoding metrics` per-position acceptance falls toward 0. With this PR, no degenerate answers.

## Details

- `defer_async_loads` is set at init when `defer_block_free` is on and the KV cache config has a HiSparse host pool.
- With a step in flight, the scheduler puts an async load in `deferred_loads` with the fence `sched_step_seq` at allocation instead of calling `update_state_after_alloc`. `_drain_deferred_loads` starts it in `update_from_output`, next to `_drain_deferred_frees`, once `processed_step_seq` reaches the fence. The request stays in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` meanwhile.
- Connector prefix-cache stats for a deferred load are recorded in `_drain_deferred_loads` after `update_state_after_alloc`, so it keeps `hits_by_source` (the connector attributes tiers only after the load plan exists). The allocation-site stats code is unchanged from main apart from skipping deferred loads.
- Abort while deferred: no load was posted, so the scheduler frees the blocks itself, deferred to the same fence through `last_sched_seq`, which is set when the load is deferred. `NixlConnector.request_finished` already releases the remote blocks of a request it never registered.
- The scheduler already fences block reuse against async connector writes (`defer_block_free`), but only for freed requests' blocks; these pages still belong to a running request. Deferring the registration needs no device sync; the only HiSparse-specific line in the scheduler is the init flag.
- CI does not cover the GPU path (needs NIXL P/D on GPUs).

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Wait on per-slot events in packed NCCL consumer
author: dharak-cohere
body:
## Overview On ROCm, the packed NCCL consumer's per-slot `streams[i].synchronize()` can also wait for another slot's later `post_unpack_func` work, such as a layerwise reload replay. That stalls the host and removes the multi-buffer overlap. This PR waits on a per-slot event instead. Follow-up to #62555. ## Claims - Fixes the MI300X failure of `tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py::TestPackedBroadcastDeferredConsumer::test_freed_pack_not_reused_while_replay_pending` (all three parameterizations) when slot streams share a HIP hardware queue. The failure was seen in AMD CI. - Restores the overlap on ROCm when queues are shared. The consumer-only layerwise benchmark gets up to 7.9% faster on MI300X. - No regression on H100: every latency change is within ±0.41%, and memory is identical. ## Validation **Reproducer.** This uses the existing test. The bug only shows up when slot streams share a hardware queue. On the MI300X I tested (ROCm 7.14, torch 2.11) that doesn't happen at the default `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=4`, so the test forces one queue: ```bash GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1 pytest tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py -k replay_pending ``` | MI300X, `main` @ 533906528c | `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES` | `-k replay_pending` (3 cases) | full file (33 tests) | |---|---|---|---| | without this PR | 1 | **3/3 runs fail**: "the replay finished before every receive in the window was issued" | – | | with this PR | 1 | 3/3 runs pass | 33 passed | | without this PR | default (4) | pass | 33 passed | | with this PR | default (4) | pass | 33 passed | On H100 the full file passes with and without the change (33/33). **Performance.** Every run uses a fresh process. A and B alternate run by run, with 5 rounds of 20 timed calls each (3 rounds for end to end). Δ is the change in B's median versus A's. Noise is the larger standard deviation of the per-round medians. A result is significant if |Δ| > 2 × noise. - **Microbenchmarks:** - Consumer-only: one GPU with a fake broadcast. The payload is Llama-3-8B-shaped bf16 layers (4 or 16 GiB). `num_buffers` ∈ {2, 3}, packs of 64/256/1024 MiB. - Real RCCL/NCCL: producer on GPU 0, consumer on GPU 1. - Both run with `post_unpack_func` either copying immediately or replaying every 6 packs on the slot stream (layerwise). - **End to end:** the `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl.py` flow. Time is per weight update. OLMoE runs with real weights and `/weight_checker` checksums after every sync. | Benchmark | H100 (NVLink) | MI300X, queues = 1 | MI300X, default (4) / 16 queues | |---|---|---|---| | consumer-only, layerwise, 64 MiB packs | within ±0.41% | **−5.2% to −7.9%** (noise ≤ 1.3%) | +0.96 to +1.28% / +0.78 to +1.15% | | consumer-only, layerwise, 256 MiB packs | within ±0.41% | −1.2% to −1.5% | −0.69 to +1.38% / −0.05 to +1.06% | | consumer-only, all 24 configs | max +0.41% | – (layerwise only) | max +2.54% (noise 1.47%) / max +1.63% | | real RCCL/NCCL, all configs | within ±0.18% | within ±0.29% | within ±0.28% / ±0.37% | | E2E OLMoE-1B-7B, 128 MB packs (104 packs) | −3.2% (noise 0.6%) | – | −1.1% (noise 0.5%) | | E2E Qwen3-0.6B, 32 MB packs (36 packs) | −3.0% (noise 3.8%) | – | +1.8% (noise 2.0%) | | E2E opt-125m, 1 pack | +0.3% (noise 5.4%) | – | −0.2% (noise 0.5%) | At one queue, host time blocked in slot waits on MI300X goes from 11.5 ms to 8.9 ms per call (layerwise, 3 buffers, 64 MiB packs, 16 GiB). The final drain is unchanged. The real RCCL/NCCL path barely moves on MI300X: at about 49 GB/s the transfer dominates, so the stall is hidden. **Correctness:** every verify pass matched bit for bit: - 96 runs each on H100 and on MI300X at default queues; 24 per benchmark at one queue. - The weight checker found 0 mismatched syncs on A or B. - Generated outputs are identical with and without the change. **Memory:** peak allocated memory is identical in every config on both GPUs. Peak reserved memory is identical on H100, apart from one-pack allocator noise. On MI300X with one queue it is up to 3.1 GB higher with this PR in the layerwise configs. Receives now overlap the replay again, so PyTorch's caching allocator holds more blocks at once. Those figures stay at or below what both variants reserve at default queues.
Setup - **H100:** 4x H100 80GB (NV18), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7. Benchmarks ran on `e2b6723123` with and without this commit. End to end: TP=2 engine on GPUs 0–1, trainer on GPU 2. - **MI300X:** 2x MI300X (xGMI), ROCm 7.14, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0, RCCL 2.30.4, in `rocm/vllm:rocm7.14.0_cdna_ubuntu24.04_py3.14_pytorch_2.11.0_vllm_0.23.0`, building this branch from source. End to end: TP=1 engine on GPU 1, trainer on GPU 0. RCCL rejects a trainer sharing a GPU with a TP rank, and only 2 GPUs were available. - **Rebase:** the reproducer table was rerun on current `main` (533906528c) after rebasing. The only change to this file since `e2b6723123` is #63457 (`torch.cuda` → `torch.accelerator` renames).
## Details **Root cause.** HIP multiplexes streams onto a small pool of hardware queues per process (`GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES`, default 4). - **Before:** when two slot streams share a queue, `hipStreamSynchronize` on one also waits for work queued later on the other. The consumer's `streams[buffer_idx].synchronize()` before reusing slot `i` then waits for slot `j`'s `post_unpack_func` work, such as a layerwise replay. The host can't issue the next receive until that replay ends. The overlap the `num_buffers` window exists for is lost, and the test's assertion that the replay is still pending while the window's receives are issued fails. - **Why only ROCm:** CUDA streams don't serialize host synchronization this way. **Fix.** After `post_unpack_func`, record a `torch.Event` on the slot stream (`slot_done[buffer_idx]`). Before reusing the slot, wait on that event instead of synchronizing the stream. - **Same coverage:** the event covers the same work as before, the receive, unpack and `post_unpack_func` work on that slot's stream, but nothing queued after it. - **First use:** on a slot's first use there is nothing to wait for, so the wait is skipped. That's `num_buffers` fewer waits per call. - **Drain:** the closing `for stream in streams: stream.synchronize()` drain is unchanged. **Tradeoff.** The change adds one event record per pack. In the consumer-only microbenchmark with no queue sharing, B is about 0.4–1.6% slower on MI300X (beyond noise in some configs, with sub-millisecond packs), and within noise on H100. This doesn't show up with a real RCCL/NCCL transfer or end to end. **CI.** `tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py` already runs on AMD CI, which is where the failure appeared. No new test is added. Whether the existing test catches a regression of this fix depends on the runner's queue assignment. Forcing `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1` reproduces it every time. ---

title: [ROCm][Perf][Bugfix] wvSplitK: launch tiles of their own for gfx1151 and gfx1150; fix bigType for A_CHUNK 16
author: roberteg16
body:
## Overview Faster wave32 `wvSplitK` on gfx1151 and gfx1150/gfx1152/gfx1153: one launch tile per arch, chosen from a sweep of every non-spilling launch configuration. Related: #63015 (gfx9 rows only), #62718 (moves these kernels to a header; textual conflict), #51511 (disables the skinny GEMM on gfx1151; this PR makes it faster there instead). ## Claims - bf16/fp16 `wvSplitK` kernel time against `main`: +0.8% to +4.9% on gfx1150, +1.8% to +4.1% on gfx1151; 99.3-99.8% of the per-shape best tile (`main`: 96-98%). - Fixes `bigType` for A_CHUNK = 16 (64 B instead of 32 B: reads past the activation row, overlapping LDS writes). - GSM8K unchanged within noise. ## Validation **Performance.** Interleaved A/B against `main`, cold caches, weights padded as at load, median of 5 rounds. 43 shapes x N = 1..5, bf16 and fp16; 13 shapes not used for tuning (odd M, K = 768/1000/2880 among them); bias on 4 shapes. | | gfx1150 | gfx1151 | |---|---:|---:| | Shapes used for tuning | +1.8% to +1.9% | +2.7% to +3.0% | | Other shapes | +0.8% to +4.9% | +1.8% to +3.2% | | With bias | +1.7% | +4.1% | Cells slower by more than 2%: at most 3 of 150 per dtype, none below 0.98x. **Accuracy.** GSM8K, full set, 5-shot, greedy, a 1.5B bf16 instruct model, `max_num_seqs=5` (decode batches N = 1..5 through `wvSplitK`), gfx1151: | | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---:|---:| | `main` | 0.5807 ± 0.0136 | 0.5307 ± 0.0137 | | this PR | 0.5785 ± 0.0136 | 0.5292 ± 0.0137 | 3 and 2 of 1319 answers differ: the tile changes the summation order and `v_dot2_f32_bf16` the rounding. ``` lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct,dtype=bfloat16,max_num_seqs=5,max_model_len=4096,seed=0 \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --gen_kwargs temperature=0 --seed 0 ``` **Tests.** - `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_skinny_gemms.py -k test_rocm_wvsplitk_kernel`: 126 passed on gfx1151, including new K % 16 != 0 and N = 5 cases. The file's other failures on gfx1151 (`test_rocm_wvsplitk_fp8_kernel`, `test_rocm_llmm1_kernel`) are the same 184 on `main`. - All 43 shapes x N = 1..5, bf16/fp16, with and without bias, against `torch.nn.functional.linear`: correct on gfx1150 and gfx1151. - `pre-commit` passes. ## Details 1. **`bigType` sized by A_CHUNK.** `half4` was (A_CHUNK / 2) x bf16; it is now 4 x bf16, the operand of its only consumer. No launch used A_CHUNK = 16 before this PR. 2. **bf16 `DOT2C` on gfx11/gfx12** issues `v_dot2_f32_bf16`, as fp16 issues `v_dot2_f32_f16`, instead of widening both operands to f32. 3. **Launch rows** (`WVSPLITK_CFG_AC` takes A_CHUNK; `WVSPLITK_CFG` keeps 8): - gfx1151: (YTILE 1, UNRL 4, A_CHUNK 16); (2, 4, 8) for K < 1024. - gfx1150, gfx1152, gfx1153: (2, 1, 16); (1, 2, 16) when M <= 32 * CUs. - A_CHUNK 8 when K % 16 != 0 (wider chunks give wrong results there). - Other archs: unchanged. The sweep covered YTILE 1-4, UNRL 1/2/4/8, A_CHUNK 8/16/32 and WvPrGrp 16/32, excluding configurations that spill. AI assistance was used. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above. ---

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Apply the draft max_model_len limit before model config hooks
author: Prakash-sa
body:
## Overview

Fixes #63844. On Model Runner V2, a hybrid Mamba/attention target with prefix caching disabled and a draft whose `max_model_len` is below the target's fails config validation with `--mamba-block-size can only be set with --enable-prefix-caching`, although the flag was never set. Regression from #63251.

## Claims

- `VllmConfig` now lowers `max_model_len` to the draft's before running the model `verify_and_update_config` hooks, so values they derive from it (here the default `mamba_block_size`) use the final length.
- The reported command starts on V2; V1 and non-hybrid models are unchanged.

## Validation

New test `test_draft_limit_applies_before_hybrid_mamba_block_size` goes through `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`, the path shared by `LLM` and `vllm serve` (CPU, only config files are fetched).

Before (fix reverted):

```text
$ pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_limits_max_model_len.py -k hybrid
E       pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for VllmConfig
E         Value error, --mamba-block-size can only be set with --enable-prefix-caching
1 failed, 4 deselected
```

After:

```text
$ pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_limits_max_model_len.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_max_position_embeddings.py
20 passed
```

Wider suite `pytest tests/config tests/test_config.py` (macOS, CPU-only, `test_ray_runtime_env` deselected since Ray isn't installed): 771 passed, 29 failed. All 29 fail identically on `main` without this change (gated `meta-llama` repos, model inspection failing for multimodal architectures on this platform, CPU-specific compilation defaults, and V1-runner async-scheduling checks), so none are introduced here.

End to end, the reproducer from #63844 (`--load-format dummy`, CPU) now passes config validation; before the fix it raised the error above from `create_engine_config`:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-random --max-model-len 4096 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --load-format dummy \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","model":"ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-random","num_speculative_tokens":3,"max_model_len":1024}'
```

The test runs in the CPU "Multimodal + Config" Buildkite step (`pytest -v -s config`, depends on `vllm/config/`). `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

## Details

Root cause: #63251 added `_limit_max_model_len_to_draft()` after `try_verify_and_update_config()`. For hybrid models with prefix caching off, `MambaModelConfig.verify_and_update_config` sets `mamba_block_size = max_model_len` (4096). The limit then lowers `max_model_len` to 1024, and the after-validator `validate_mamba_block_size` reads `mamba_block_size != max_model_len` as a user-set flag.

Moving the limit ahead of the hooks is safe: it only reads the speculative config and `use_v2_model_runner`, which depends on `speculative_config`, `lora_config`, and `parallel_config` fields (executor backend, PP/DCP/PCP sizes, ubatching) that the hooks do not write. Hooks that also lower `max_model_len` (e.g. the 8192 cap for EmbeddingGemma2) still apply, now on top of the draft limit, so the result is the same minimum. Other values the hooks derive from `max_model_len`, such as `rotary_kwargs["max_position"]`, also see the final length now.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #63844 or `_limit_max_model_len_to_draft`. #52045 works around the same validator for a different trigger (CPU MLA disabling prefix caching) and does not touch this ordering.

title: [Recipes Tool] Fix TP auto-detection for heterogeneous per-layer attention models
author: louie-tsai
body:
## Overview

Fix automatic tensor-parallel (TP) selection for models with heterogeneous per-layer attention configurations, such as Gemma 4.

Previously, accessing the global `num_key_value_heads` attribute raised an exception, causing the Recipes tool to fall back to TP=1.

Follow-up to [[PR #60170](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60170)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60170).

## Claims

- Extract attention-head and KV-head constraints from individual layers.
- Support heterogeneous attention models without TP detection failures.
- Preserve existing TP compatibility checks and homogeneous model support.

## Validation

- Three targeted model tests passed.
- Gemma 4 on Xeon 6 (4 NUMA nodes): correctly selected TP=4 and initialized all four workers.
- Gemma 4 TP=4 subsequently encountered a KV-cache capacity issue; DiffusionGemma TP=2 encountered a runtime warmup stall. Both are outside the scope of this fix.

## Details

The original implementation assumed globally uniform KV-head counts. Models with heterogeneous attention configurations reject this global attribute access.

The fix extracts head constraints from each attention layer and uses the existing TP selection logic to determine a compatible TP size. No changes to inference kernels or distributed execution are required.

title: [Bugfix][Muse] Finalize dummy-loaded MegaMoE weights
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Fix Muse Spark dummy loading with `deep_gemm_mega_moe`. Run expert repacking and residual-constant materialization through the existing model post-load hook, and initialize custom NVFP4 expert scales with valid dummy values.

## Claims

- Dummy-loaded BF16 and NVFP4 Muse MegaMoE models finish initialization and generate finite outputs.
- Checkpoint and dummy loaders share the same post-load finalization hook.

## Validation

GB200 validation of the retained tests: 2 generation cases passed. All targeted pre-commit checks pass.

On one GB200, using `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py -k test_muse_megamoe_dummy_loading -x -v -s`:

| Configuration | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 Muse, 1 layer, hidden 512, 8 experts, top-2, MegaMoE | `AssertionError: finalize_weights() not called` at `mega_moe.py:313` | Pass |
| NVFP4 Muse, same shape and backend | Not run on baseline after first failure | Pass |

The regression generates two greedy tokens with finite log probabilities for both weight formats through the normal LLM dummy-loading entry point. It registers the native text class via ModelRegistry to avoid initializing unrelated multimodal towers. It does not assert private packed-weight layouts or residual-buffer structure.

Targeted pre-commit hooks passed. The existing B200 Quantized MoE CI step runs this suite, with Muse sources added to its dependency selection. No checkpoint accuracy evaluation is claimed: the reported failure and added scale metadata concern synthetic dummy weights.

## Details

DummyModelLoader initializes parameters directly and does not invoke the model's `load_weights`. Muse's expert repacking and residual coefficient setup previously lived only there. Exposing the existing operations through `process_weights_after_loading` makes them run after dummy initialization and per-layer quantization finalization. Both checkpoint and dummy loading reach the standardized model hook in BaseModelLoader; the multimodal wrapper inherits it directly.

Muse's custom MegaMoE parameter allocator also bypasses ModelOpt's generic expert scale setup. Use the existing `dummy_weight_value` parameter contract with the same constants as ModelOpt NVFP4 (block scales 1, global weight scales 0.001, input scales 0.01). This metadata does not change checkpoint values.

Open-PR searches for `"Muse" "dummy"`, `"Muse" "finalize"`, `"Muse" "post-load"`, and `"Muse" "dummy_weight_value"` found no duplicate. Merged #63698 covers generic ModelOpt parameters, which Muse's custom MegaMoE allocator does not use. Open #52487 concerns reload after sleep. No associated issue number exists.

AI assistance was used to implement and validate this change. The human submitter confirmed review of every changed line and execution of the relevant tests before submission.

title: [Bugfix][Bench] Support Muse balanced routing
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Fix Muse Spark forward benchmarks with dummy weights and the default `--routing auto`, which already selects balanced routing. No explicit routing flag is needed.

## Claims

- `BalancedRouting` discovers Muse's gate and suppresses expert selection bias while its synthetic routing fixture is installed.
- Removing the fixture restores the original bias and real model routing.

## Validation

GB200 validation of the retained tests: 2 cases passed (native CLI and router/bias behavior). All targeted pre-commit checks pass.

On GB200, using `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k test_balanced_routing_restores_expert_bias -v`:

| --- | --- | --- |

The test uses a real GateLinear and Muse router, checks exact per-rank balance despite a large expert-selection bias, and verifies bias restoration and subsequent real routing. Targeted pre-commit hooks passed. The existing Benchmarks CLI Buildkite step selects the layer regression; the B200 Quantized MoE step explicitly selects the native Muse CLI test.

The BF16 TRTLLM test passes without the separate MegaMoE initialization fix. The added `test_bench_forward_muse_balanced_routing` regression fails before the routing fix with `ValueError: No MoE gates found; use --routing real.`. title: [Bugfix][Bench] Handle packed hybrid KV and speculative recurrent state
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Fix `vllm bench forward` on hybrid attention/recurrent models: initialize packed KV caches using manager-block views and reserve/restore all speculative recurrent state slots.

## Claims

- Packed hybrid KV layouts no longer fail with `No block dim of size ...` during benchmark initialization.
- Verify requests get disjoint recurrent scratch blocks for every configured speculative token, and replay restores all those blocks.
- Changes are confined to benchmark setup and replay state; serving execution and the timed model-forward interval are unchanged.

## Validation

GB200 validation of the retained tests: 3 cases passed (native CLI, cache isolation, recurrent state). All targeted pre-commit checks pass.

Base: `b82393b77315692f390880d2e931fdc1fbd13928`. Validation used four GB200 GPUs, native MRV2, and dummy weights (this checks benchmark execution/state, not model accuracy).

| Reproducer | Base | Fixed |
|---|---|---|
| Native GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, FP8 KV, FlashInfer sparse MLA, ngram 5 target-only | All ranks fail: `ValueError: No block dim of size 3979 in (6619401, 64, 132)` | Decode, Verify, Mixed finish; all ranks finite, deterministic, graph/eager relative RMS 0 |
| Tiny Qwen3Next public CLI | `assert 5 == (1 + (7 * 2))` fails: only one state per request | Passes: all speculative slots counted, Verify/Mixed finite and deterministic |
| CPU speculative-state regression | Too few recurrent scratch slots per request | Passes capacity, non-overlap, and complete state-restoration checks |
| CPU packed-view regression | Native GLM reproducer above covers the original layout failure | Passes; adjacent interleaved layers remain unchanged |

Native cases: `decode=1*1@512`, `verify=2*6@512:5`, `mixed=128@512,2*6@512:5`; two samples of two replays. Measured medians were 4.723 / 8.443 / 20.134 ms respectively, with sample spreads 0.04% / 0.03% / 0.05%. These are execution checks, not a speedup claim.

Commands (run from this checkout with the installed vLLM environment):

```bash
/home/woosuk/workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k 'test_bench_packed_kv_blocks or test_bench_speculative_mamba_blocks or test_bench_forward_hybrid_verify' -v
```

Final CPU selection: 7 passed; public CLI: 1 passed (53.47 s), base: 1 failed (52.53 s).

The public CLI regression creates a local tiny Qwen3Next model and checks finite, deterministic Verify/Mixed replay. The benchmark instantiates the real LLM engine. No checkpoint loading behavior changes; dummy weights are appropriate to this forward-state regression.

## Details

Hybrid cache groups can pack multiple attention kernel blocks inside one manager block and interleave layers. The existing `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache_to_manager_blocks` reconstructs the correct manager view without copying. Recurrent state requires one base slot plus `MambaSpec.num_speculative_blocks`; unlike attention tails, every recurrent slot may be read or overwritten during verification.

These three fixes form one benchmark-state correctness change: without the packed-view fix the affected hybrid model cannot initialize; without either recurrent-state fix verification allocates or restores the wrong state. The CPU tests check allocation capacity and memory isolation without pinning block IDs or a complete storage layout. The snapshots use additional GPU memory proportional to the actual speculative state slots. Their copies remain outside the measured interval.

Duplicate-work checks searched open PRs for `"bench forward" "KV"`, `"bench forward" "Mamba"`, `"bench forward" "KDA"`, and `"packed" "benchmark"`. No open PR addressed these benchmark-state failures. The issue inventory came from local model experiments and has no linked GitHub issue number. Existing packed-cache connector and kernel PRs affect different paths.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement, test, and prepare this change. The human submitter confirmed review of every changed line and execution of the relevant tests before submission.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Avoid double rounding in fused MoE expand
author: chaojun-zhang
body:
## Overview

Fix FP16 residual accumulation in the fused MoE LoRA fallback on XPU, without changing tests or tolerances. CUDA and ROCm keep their previous accumulation behavior.

## Claims

- Keep the XPU expand accumulator and residual sum in FP32, converting only when storing the result.
- Preserve the existing dtype conversion and addition order for non-XPU backends.
- Addresses the precision path introduced by #59931 without changing shared behavior on CUDA/ROCm.

## Validation

- Atomic-add cast cleanup: `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -k large_rank_fallback` — 16 passed; file-level pre-commit passed. A direct `SPLIT_K=2` shrink check also matched the FP32 reference exactly for binary-scaled FP16/BF16 inputs on XPU.
- After removing the redundant cast before `tl.store`: `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` — 433 passed in 309.11s on two Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs; original tests/tolerances unchanged. CUDA was unavailable.
- `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -k test_fused_moe_lora_kernel_large_rank_fallback` — 16 passed on Intel Arc Pro B60.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py` — passed.
- The CI BMG-specific numerical discrepancy was not reproduced on local B60; Intel CI is still needed to validate that hardware-specific case.

## Details

The XPU specialization keeps the FP32 dot accumulator through residual addition so the LoRA result is not rounded to FP16 before adding the residual. It is selected only for XPU expand calls; shrink and all non-XPU calls retain the existing conversion order. No test code or tolerance was modified.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the specialized decode's FlashInfer paths on newer FlashInfer
author: yaoyaoding
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepSeek-V4.1 `latency_specialized` decode (#61868) turned on four of its FlashInfer paths only when `flashinfer-python` was exactly 0.7.2. #63466 moved `requirements/cuda.txt` to 0.7.2.post1, so on `main` all four have been off since then: the server logs a warning per path and runs the stock path, and the numerics test that covers two of them skips. This PR gates each path on what it actually needs, so they run on 0.7.2.post1 and later releases. Thanks to @mgoin for catching it ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61868#discussion_r4380766753)).

## Validation

On one GB300 tray with `main`'s FlashInfer (0.7.2.post1):

- `test_numerics.py` (4 GPUs) passes instead of skipping; it compares the publishing `wo_b` GEMM and the MXFP8 layer input with FlashInfer's own GEMM and quantize bitwise.
- `test_kernels.py::test_sparse_mla_persistent_kv_counters` and `::test_low_latency_mxfp8_mm`: 18 passed, none skipped.
- `vllm serve` with `decode_backend=latency_specialized` logs "specialized decode on" and no fallback warning, and answers a completion and a chat smoke request correctly.

## Details

- Publishing `wo_b` GEMM and MXFP8 layer input (they use FlashInfer internals): FlashInfer ≥ 0.7.2 instead of == 0.7.2. Those internals are unchanged in 0.7.2.post1, and `test_numerics.py` now runs on the pinned release, so a later change to them fails the test instead of turning the paths off.
- Pinned MXFP8 tactics: no version gate; they already fall back to tuning every tactic when FlashInfer does not list the pinned one.
- Sparse-MLA KV counters: on the decode taking `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`.

title: [Bugfix] Skip more weight formats in the tokenizer/processor snapshot
author: Prakash-sa
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #63925.

Since #60825, loading a tokenizer or processor first downloads every Hub file not matched by `_WEIGHT_FILE_PATTERNS`. That list misses several weight formats that classic repos still ship, so vLLM downloads unused weights before loading the model: about 1.57 GB extra for `openai-community/gpt2` and 534 MB for `google-bert/bert-base-uncased`. This adds those formats to the list.

## Claims

- The tokenizer/processor snapshot no longer downloads rust-bert (`*.ot`), TFLite, Core ML (`*.mlmodel`, `*.mlpackage/*`), NeMo, NumPy (`*.npy`, `*.npz`) or PaddlePaddle (`*.pdparams`) files.
- Tokenizer, processor and config files are still downloaded.

## Validation

New parametrized tests in `tests/transformers_utils/test_repo_utils.py` apply `_WEIGHT_FILE_PATTERNS` with `huggingface_hub.utils.filter_repo_objects` (the filter `snapshot_download` uses) to real file names from `openai-community/gpt2` and `google-bert/bert-base-uncased`. No network access.

Before (patterns reverted):

```text
$ pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_repo_utils.py
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[rust_model.ot]
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[64.tflite]
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[64-fp16.tflite]
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[coreml/fill-mask/float32_model.mlpackage/Data/com.apple.CoreML/model.mlmodel]
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[coreml/fill-mask/float32_model.mlpackage/Manifest.json]
5 failed, 22 passed
```

After:

```text
$ pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_repo_utils.py
27 passed
```

Against the live Hub file lists (captures the `ignore_patterns` passed to `snapshot_download` and filters `HfApi().model_info(repo).siblings`), files over 50 MB that the snapshot would fetch:

| Repo | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `openai-community/gpt2` | `rust_model.ot`, `64.tflite`, `64-fp16.tflite`, `64-8bits.tflite` (~1.57 GB) | none |
| `google-bert/bert-base-uncased` | `rust_model.ot` (534 MB) | none |

`tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py` and `tests/transformers_utils/test_processor.py` pass except `test_hub_processor_loads_from_local_snapshot` and `test_processor_reuses_tokenizer_snapshot`, which fail identically on main in my environment (macOS, no torchvision). `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

## Details

The `typos` hook flags the `ot` extension, so `ot` is added to `[tool.typos.default.extend-words]` next to the other short words already there (`fo`, `nd`, `ba`).

This keeps the deny-list approach from #60825. An allow-list of tokenizer/processor files would close the gap for future formats too, but it risks missing files that custom processors or `trust_remote_code` tokenizers need; happy to switch if preferred.

Not a duplicate: searching issues and PRs for `_WEIGHT_FILE_PATTERNS`, `get_non_weight_snapshot_path`, `rust_model.ot` and "tokenizer snapshot weights" finds only #60825 and #61272; #63482 touches the same module but not the patterns.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not offload the partially computed block of a request that finished with an error
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Overview

When a request finishes with an error before its prefill is complete, the block it was computing is stored under the hash of the full block. A later request with that prefix hits the offloaded block and loads KV for tokens that were never computed. One-expression fix in `_build_store_jobs`; sibling of #59096 and #59329.

## Claims

- A request that ends in `FINISHED_ERROR` mid-prefill stores only the blocks it fully computed, as `FINISHED_ABORTED` already does.
- Requests that finished normally are unchanged: they computed their whole prompt, so the clamp is a no-op.

## Validation

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q -k finish_mid_prefill
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

`test_finish_mid_prefill_stores_only_computed_blocks[FINISHED_ERROR|FINISHED_ABORTED]` runs a 16-token prompt through chunked prefill at 6 tokens a step (block size 4), finishes the request after the first chunk, and checks that the finish step stores nothing beyond the one full block step 1 already stored.

On main (6fe3d447ac64) the `FINISHED_ERROR` case fails:

```
AssertionError: FINISHED_ERROR: stored 1 blocks [2] but only 1 full block(s) were computed (num_computed_tokens=6, prompt=16)
```

With the fix both cases pass; the file's other tests still pass (CPU only, macOS, no GPU run). Model outputs are unaffected, so no evals.

## Details

`_build_store_jobs` (`offloading/scheduler.py:1874-1883`) clamps the storable token count to `num_computed_tokens` only for `FINISHED_ABORTED`; every other finish uses `max(num_prompt_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`, which is the whole prompt for a request that produced no output. `storable_chunks` then only bounds by allocated blocks, so the half-written block goes out under its full hash. A request can finish this way mid-prefill through `finish_requests(..., FINISHED_ERROR)` (`sched/scheduler.py:2525-2540`): an encoder-cache mismatch, or a failed KV load under the `fail` policy.

Fix: `min(req.num_computed_tokens, max(req.num_prompt_tokens, req.num_tokens - 1))`. The spec-decode clamp is kept.

Not a duplicate: #63010 (store cursor reset on a restart from token 0) and #60810 (the block table of a resumed streaming session), both merged on 10-25, and the open #62795 (flush promotions before a request's tiers are finalized) are adjacent; none touches this clamp.

AI assistance: I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to trace this path and write the test; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests myself.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Let decodes reuse divergent local hybrid prefix hits
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

`MooncakeConnector` does not opt into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` (#50344), so a hybrid-model decode (attention plus Mamba, GDN or KDA) drops its local attention hit and pulls the whole prompt from P every turn. This opts the `kv_consumer` role in, as MoRIIO READ and NIXL already do.

## Claims

- On a hybrid model, a Mooncake decode keeps its local attention prefix and pulls only the uncached suffix plus the recurrent state.
- `kv_producer` and `kv_both` keep the current lookup.

## Validation

- Kimi-K3 1P1D on MI355X, Mooncake RDMA, multi-turn agentic replay at concurrency 48: decode local prefix hit rate 0.0% to 93.9%; draft acceptance 58.78% to 58.79% (MoRIIO READ 58.79%).
- The new scheduler test fails on main and passes here. Mooncake unit tests: 164 passed. pre-commit clean.

<details><summary>Request flow, test output and serving numbers</summary>

Turn k of a session whose prompt extends turn k-1:

1. The router sends the request to P with `do_remote_decode`; P prefills and pushes KV.
2. On D, the attention blocks pulled in turn k-1 are still cached. Mamba has no state at any block boundary, since D never computes those positions.
3. Before: `get_computed_blocks` returns the hit every group shares, 0 tokens. Mooncake asks for N-1 tokens and pulls every attention block plus the state slot.
4. After: `get_computed_blocks_for_connector` returns the attention hit H. Mooncake asks for N-1-H tokens and pulls the suffix blocks plus the state slot; P pairs the last blocks of each group.
5. D decodes from the recurrent state P computed at N-1.

Unit test, on main and on this branch:

```
$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py -k keeps_local_attention_prefix
# main
E       assert 6 == 2
E        +  where 6 = len([9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14])
FAILED ...::test_hybrid_gdn_remote_prefill_keeps_local_attention_prefix[kv_consumer-2]
1 failed, 1 passed, 11 deselected
# this branch
2 passed, 11 deselected

$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
164 passed
```

Serving, Kimi-K3 1P1D, decode flags `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma"}}'`, aiperf multi-turn agentic trace replay at concurrency 48. One run per column.

| Decode metric | Mooncake before | Mooncake after | MoRIIO READ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local prefix cache hit rate (log) | 0.0% | 93.9% | 91.2% |
| Prompt tokens, `local_cache_hit` / `external_kv_transfer` | 0 / 801.7M | not recorded | 731.3M / 70.9M |
| Draft acceptance | 58.78% | 58.79% | 58.79% |
| TTFT mean / p50, same request window | 2984 / 1727 ms | 3137 / 1730 ms | 2611 / 1365 ms |

The "after" run was cancelled by the cluster after 4598 requests, so it has no end-of-run Prometheus snapshot; its hit rate is the decode's periodic log line. MoRIIO's hit rate is `local_cache_hit` over all prompt tokens.

</details>

## Details

A decode never computes the block boundaries of a pulled prompt, so it caches attention blocks but no recurrent state. With the opt-in, the scheduler keeps the attention hit, and `update_state_after_alloc` already pulls every transfer group's unhashed blocks, the state slot included. With nothing to pull, the scheduler falls back to the reconciled lookup (#50344).

Only `kv_consumer` opts in: the per-group lookup reports a shared-prefix boundary of 0, which would disable junction checkpoints on roles that prefill locally.

Limitations:
- Serving runs used vLLM 81198e97 with this property forced to True on the decode, matching this PR; not re-run on main.
- Under `MultiConnector` every child must opt in until #63041.
- TTFT did not change on this workload.

Not a duplicate: the open Mooncake PRs (#53730, #63420, #63425) do not touch this property. AI assistance (Claude in Cursor) was used to write the change, the test and this description.
