title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Match Python text-part joining for HF templates
author: luyixiao95
body:
## Overview

The Rust HF renderer currently turns `["Part one. ", "Part two."]` into `"Part one. Part two."`, while Python inserts a newline. When an HF template expects string content, this change renders each content part as one segment (a media part as its placeholder, in place), skips empty text parts, and joins the segments with `\n`.

Addresses the HF `ChatContent::Parts` case in item 1 of #63917.

## Claims

- Text-only content lists use Python's newline separator, skip empty parts, and preserve whitespace within each part.
- Lists with media keep each placeholder at its part's position and use the same separator, which matches Python's output with `--interleave-mm-strings` (pinned by `tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_image.py::test_parse_chat_messages_multiple_images_interleave`). Python's default moves placeholders to the front; Rust intentionally keeps them where the client put them.
- Renderer tests pin the joined string for text-only lists, image, video and audio placeholders, and the Step-5 VL template in string format. Existing tests cover automatic and explicit string formats and OpenAI-format content, which still passes the parts list to the template.

## Validation

On Linux aarch64, Rust 1.95:

```sh
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace
# 2436 passed, 13 skipped

cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings
# passed

cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --check
# passed
```

Changing the final `join("\n")` back to plain concatenation fails six renderer tests:

```text
renderer::hf::tests::chat_template_flattens_text_parts_for_string_templates
renderer::hf::tests::chat_template_forces_string_content_format_when_configured
renderer::hf::tests::string_content_format_replaces_image_with_placeholder_text
renderer::hf::tests::string_content_format_replaces_video_with_placeholder_text
renderer::hf::tests::string_content_format_replaces_audio_with_placeholder_text
renderer::hf::tests::step5_vl_template_places_im_patch_at_image_part_position_string_format
```

I also ran Python's `parse_chat_messages` with a local Qwen3 config and the checked-in Qwen3 template: five cases passed, covering multiple parts, empty parts, existing newlines, a single part, and empty text. The issue's input rendered as:

```text
'<|im_start|>user\nPart one. \nPart two.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
```

Validation reaches prompt rendering; real-model generation/quality evaluation was not run. The existing Rust Cargo CI job runs the affected test suites.

## Details

The separator belongs in the HF string renderer. The shared content-flattening helper is also used by model-specific renderers, so changing it would widen the behavior change. One rule now covers text-only and mixed lists, so adding media to a list does not change how its text parts are joined. This patch leaves assistant output-block aggregation and other renderers outside its scope; it does not close the whole issue.

The first revision's route test and docs paragraph were dropped: the renderer unit tests pin the joined string where it is produced, and the Rust frontend now follows Python's existing behavior, which needs no user-facing note.

Duplicate-work check: #63762 changes DeepSeek V4/V4.1 rendering; #63926 addresses items 2 and 3. Neither covers this HF path. Scope was also noted in the issue.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code) was used to prepare and validate this change.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Drain unfetched P2P stores before cache reset
author: maithilijoshi20
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix cache reset on P2P prefill nodes when store jobs are waiting for a decoder to fetch their KV blocks.

Fixes #63948.

## Claims

- Queued stores report failure and release their primary-tier pins during reset.
- Late fetches fail promptly without reading released slots or leaving stale session bindings.
- Active transfers keep their pins until completion, and fresh symmetric lookup rounds remain usable after reset.

## Validation

Tested on WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, NIXL 1.5.1/UCX, and an RTX 3050 8 GB.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py -q --tb=short
# 808 passed, 1 skipped

export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 VLLM_PLUGINS=
export CUDA_HOME=/home/maithijoshi/.venvs/vllm-py312/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nvidia/cu13
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py::test_p2p_cache_reset_with_absent_decoder \
  -q --tb=short
# 1 passed
```

The OPT-125m test waits for an active cascade with an absent decoder, calls `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`, and checks that the next request has zero cached tokens and identical greedy output. Unit tests cover queued stores, mid-drain fetches, symmetric lookup rounds, active transfer pins, and abort acknowledgements. Pre-commit checks pass for the changed files.

Without the fix, the issue's producer-reset reproducer fails at `assert not self._jobs` in `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()`; with the fix, both unbound and session-bound stores drain successfully, as confirmed in the issue author's PR feedback.

## Details

A prefill node can finish storing KV before its decoder sends a fetch. These jobs hold primary-tier slots but are not counted as active transfers, so waiting only for transfers leaves jobs behind when the parent resets its cache.

Drain fails unbound stores through the existing expiry path and withdraws queued session supply once. Fetches received during polling are rejected without binding their request IDs. In-flight writes retain their pins until the transport reports completion.

Withdrawn symmetric lookup rounds retain enough state to reject a late fetch without invalidating a fresh round under the same request ID. Aborted rounds use the existing acknowledgement path to avoid duplicate terminal messages.

This addresses producer stores waiting for decoder demand. Related #61667 covers consumer write quarantine. No duplicate fix was found when opening this PR. AI assistance was used for review, and validation.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Reserve KDA prefill workspace before profiling
author: janbernloehr
body:
## Overview

Earlier Kimi K3 NVFP4 serving OOMs exposed approximately 0.93 GiB/rank of KDA prefill workspace growth after KV cache sizing. Although the latest tested stack now completes the workload without this patch, reserve that workspace before profiling so KV sizing accounts for the memory actually needed.

## Claims

- Reserve the configured FlashKDA layout or FlashInfer output layout before attention warmup.
- Reuse the shared, grow-only workspace across layers and subsequent requests within its capacity.
- Preserve construction without an initialized workspace manager and avoid reservations for the Triton prefill backend.

## Validation

The earlier OOM no longer reproduces in the latest matched GPU comparison on GB200 NVL with Kimi K3 NVFP4, TP16, default/profile-derived KV sizing, and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`:

| Measurement | Without reservation | With reservation |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| KV cache per rank | 21.42 GiB | 20.49 GiB |
| Lowest sampled GPU-0 free memory | 0.53 GiB | 1.69 GiB |
| Both configured serving sweeps, all request counts | Passed | Passed |

Both arms completed all configured requests in both sweeps without OOM or request errors. The reservation moves 0.93 GiB/rank into the budget before KV sizing and improves runtime headroom; throughput differed by at most approximately 1.6%. This supports correcting the accounting gap, without claiming the patch was required for these runs to pass.

This campaign used an exact-content port of commit `2e3f235a2197dfb95288a9b98266900ab9767ae4` to a pinned vLLM v0.30.0 stack. The FlashInfer workspace backport, MoE workspace caller port, and separate V2 graph-accounting fix were held constant in both arms. GPU results apply to this combination; the assessment of current upstream main is based on source inspection.

The focused regression suite at commit `796d49e802fb0adacb1b94466013b2d5f912d7cb` also passed on GB200 with this installed stack: **10 passed, zero skips or errors**. It uses real layer constructors and a two-layer dummy-weight model through `LLM`, including two-token generation with both FlashKDA and FlashInfer prefill. Removing only the reservation block in the disposable installed package caused all **six reservation/engine cases to fail**: four found no reserved storage and both engine cases rejected workspace growth before memory profiling. The original source was then restored.

<details>
<summary>GPU regression commands and observed results</summary>

With the reservation:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_workspace.py -v -rA -o addopts='' --junitxml=/tmp/kda-fixed.xml
10 passed in 92.91s
```

With only the constructor reservation block removed:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_workspace.py -k 'reserved_and_shared or reservation_only_grows or engine_reserves' -v -rA -o addopts='' --junitxml=/tmp/kda-baseline.xml
6 failed, 4 deselected in 62.16s
AssertionError: Workspace is locked ... current size is 0.00 MB. Workspace growth is not allowed after locking.
```

JUnit checks confirmed the counts and zero skips or setup errors in both runs.

</details>

Confirmation on a second GB200 NVL cluster remains outstanding.

## Details

Upstream main inspected at [`eca54bd1`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/eca54bd1d937e778a939c240a2ed966fbcb12f85) still skips attention during V2 memory profiling and first requests KDA's prefill workspace during attention execution. That workspace can therefore grow during kernel warmup, after KV cache sizing. The passing control shows that the tested configuration has enough headroom despite this ordering; it does not mean the late allocation was included in the budget.

The worker initializes the workspace manager before model loading. Reserving immediately after the backend's layout is known brings the allocation into the model-loading memory measurement, reducing dependence on spare runtime headroom.

The reservation uses the same ordered specs and `get_simultaneous` call as runtime. Returned views are discarded; storage stays with the shared manager rather than each layer. FlashInfer's output scratch is reserved conservatively even when a particular request can write directly to the output. KV sizing settings and CUDA graph accounting are unchanged.

Duplicate-work check: searched open upstream PRs for `KDA workspace` and `workspace prefill in:title`; no matching KDA constructor-reservation fix was found. Related [#61250](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61250) changes prefill backend selection rather than adding this early reservation.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, and this draft. The human submitter must review every changed line and take responsibility for the validation before submission.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Parse bare FunctionGemma arguments and stream them as valid JSON
author: saifltr
body:
## Overview

Fix the `functiongemma` tool parser dropping every non-string argument, and make its streamed arguments reassemble into valid JSON. Fixes #63983.

## Claims

- Bare booleans, numbers, `null`, arrays and objects are parsed in streaming and non-streaming, nested containers included.
- Streamed deltas of a multi-argument call concatenate to one JSON object.
- A streamed call still gets closed when its end tag shares a delta with the next call's start tag.
- A streamed call with no arguments sends `{}` instead of an empty string.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py
pytest tests/entrypoints/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py
```

| Parser | parser tests (CPU) | server tests (H200) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main (`eb703fbb3d`) | 25 failed, 17 passed | 3 failed, 4 passed |
| previous head (`fa086599ec`) | 5 failed, 37 passed | 4 failed, 3 passed |
| this PR | 42 passed | 7 passed |

The server tests pin the model output with a `structured_outputs` regex, so they cover serving and parsing rather than what the model decides to call. pre-commit passes on the changed files. Existing Buildkite steps select both test files, but CI has not run on this PR yet.

### End-to-end (vllm serve, real model)

`unsloth/functiongemma-270m-it` (ungated mirror of `google/functiongemma-270m-it`, same `chat_template.jinja`) on one shared H200, through the OpenAI client with `tool_choice="auto"` and `temperature=0`. Streamed `tool_calls` deltas are concatenated per index, as a client would.

```bash
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm serve unsloth/functiongemma-270m-it \
  --tool-call-parser functiongemma --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.04 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 4
```

Raw model output for the `set_alarm` request (`/v1/completions`, `skip_special_tokens=false`):

```text
<start_function_call>call:set_alarm{days:[<escape>mon<escape>,<escape>tue<escape>],enabled:true,hour:7,label:<escape>Wake up<escape>}<end_function_call>
```

| Request | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_alarm` (int, bool, array, string), non-streaming | `{"label": "Wake up"}` | `{"days": ["mon", "tue"], "enabled": true, "hour": 7, "label": "Wake up"}` |
| `set_alarm`, streaming | `{"label": "Wake up"}` | `{"days": ["mon", "tue"], "enabled": true, "hour": 7, "label": "Wake up"}` |
| `get_weather` (two strings), non-streaming | `{"city": "San Francisco", "unit": "celsius"}` | same |
| `get_weather`, streaming | `{"city": "San Francisco"} "unit": "celsius"}` (invalid JSON) | `{"city": "San Francisco", "unit": "celsius"}` |

Review fixes, streaming, same server. The two-call rows pin the output with a regex and set `stream_interval` per request to merge deltas:

| Request | previous head (`fa086599ec`) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_current_time` (no parameters), real model output | `''` | `{}` |
| Two calls, `stream_interval=4`, delta is `<end_function_call><start_function_call>call:` | `{"city": "Paris"` (invalid JSON) | `{"city": "Paris"}` |
| Two calls, `stream_interval=8`, first call's arguments are in that delta too | `''` | `{"city": "Paris"}` |

Every `stream_interval` from 1 to 6, and 8, gives both calls with valid JSON on this PR.

Screenshots, client script and server logs from the first run (`fa086599ec`): [branch `e2e-evidence-63992`](https://github.com/saifltr/vllm/tree/e2e-evidence-63992/e2e_evidence).

<details>
<summary>client</summary>

```python
TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "set_alarm", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
    "hour": {"type": "integer"}, "enabled": {"type": "boolean"}, "label": {"type": "string"},
    "days": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}, "required": ["hour", "enabled", "label", "days"]}}}]
PROMPT = "Set an alarm for 7 o'clock labeled Wake up, enabled, on mon and tue."
WEATHER_TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
    "city": {"type": "string"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"]}}, "required": ["city", "unit"]}}}]
WEATHER_PROMPT = "What's the weather in San Francisco in celsius?"
NO_ARG_TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_current_time", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}]
NO_ARG_PROMPT = "What time is it right now?"
# client.chat.completions.create(model=..., messages=[{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}], tools=TOOLS,
#                                tool_choice="auto", temperature=0, max_tokens=128, stream=stream)
```

</details>

## Details

The template's `format_argument` macro wraps only strings in `<escape>`, e.g. `enabled:true,hour:7,days:[<escape>mon<escape>],snooze:{minutes:5}`. The old `arg_regex` only matched `key:<escape>...<escape>`, so bare values were dropped. A small recursive parser for that grammar replaces it. With `partial=True` (streaming) it stops at the first incomplete value, so each value is streamed once in its final form. A bare word that is not a JSON literal stays a string.

Streaming diffs are computed by length against `json.dumps(args)`, so the closing brace is held back until the call ends. That left two gaps, both fixed here. When an end tag and the next start tag arrive together, the start branch returned before closing the earlier call, so it never got its brace, or any arguments if they were still unsent. A call with no arguments streamed nothing because the end branch skipped empty arguments. Both paths now go through `_close_tool_call`. Deltas can merge when the client falls behind the engine or `stream_interval` is above 1.

Known limitation: from `stream_interval=10` in these runs, a call's name can share a delta with its end tag, and the name is lost. At 64 the second call is lost too. main behaves the same or worse here, so this is left for a follow-up.

Related PRs:

- #63947 fixes #63906, a separate bug. `<escape>` values keep their current decoding here, so `<escape>123<escape>` is still the integer 123.
- #48705 fixes the brace issue the same way. It is included here because the streaming tests cannot reassemble a multi-argument call without it. Happy to rebase if #48705 lands first.
- #64360 targets the same issue and was opened a day after this PR.

AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Bugfix] Forward launch grid to Triton kernel overrides
author: wangxiyuan
body:
## Overview

The kernel dispatcher's KernelOverride dropped the caller's launch grid, so platforms could not remap grids (e.g. to physical core counts). Triton kernel implementations are now swapped in directly, launching natively and staying inlinable as Triton device functions; non-Triton implementations are wrapped, receive the grid via __getitem__, and delegate compile-only warmup.

This PR fixes three gaps in the Triton kernel dispatcher: (1) the launch grid is now forwarded to overrides instead of being dropped, (2) Triton device functions called from inside other kernels can be overridden without breaking the outer kernel's compilation, and (3) JIT warmup is delegated to the override instead of failing.

title: [Bugfix] Parenthesize penalties Triton chained `or` for Ascend backends
author: drago1234
body:
## Overview

Fixes #64046

**One-line:** Ascend Triton cannot lower chained boolean `or` in V1 `_penalties_kernel` (`A or B or C` → `UnsupportedLanguageConstruct`). The first request with non-default sampling penalties can kill the TP worker group / EngineCore. This PR parenthesizes into binary `or`s. CUDA Triton semantics unchanged.

---

## What broke (feature)

This is the OpenAI-compatible **sampling penalty** path (`repetition_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` / `presence_penalty`), **not** MTP / EPLB / MDRv2 / KV pool. Those may be enabled in the same deployment but are unrelated to the compiler failure.

---

## Environment where we hit it

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Hardware | Ascend A3 NPU |
| Deploy | PD disagg **4P8–1D8**, 505B W4A8, Ascend Triton |
| Path | `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/penalties.py` → `_penalties_kernel` |
| Trigger | **First** request with non-default penalties (lazy JIT) |
| Incidents | 2026-10-24 14:35 (p0), 2026-10-26 22:34 (p1, `Worker_TP13`) |

Traffic without penalties can look healthy for a long time; sibling nodes on the same build are latent until they see a penalty request.

---

## Claims

- Removes Ascend Triton’s **chained-`or` AST** failure for `_penalties_kernel`.
- No intended behavior change on CUDA.
- Does **not** claim to fix every Ascend follow-on (BiShengIR / UB tile, missing `aclnnRightShift` in alternate torch paths). Those stay in NPU plugins / stack work.
- Not duplicating an open upstream PR for this AST issue (searched `UnsupportedLanguageConstruct` / chained boolean).

---

## Key error log (production)

```text
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/penalties.py", line 200, in apply_penalties
    _penalties_kernel[(num_tokens, num_blocks)](
...
File ".../triton/backends/ascend/__init__.py", ... in _patched_make_ir
...
triton.compiler.errors.UnsupportedLanguageConstruct: at 26:18:
    use_penalty = use_rep_penalty or use_freq_penalty or use_pres_penalty
                  ^
chained boolean operators (A or B or C) are not supported; use parentheses to split the chain.

WorkerProc hit an exception.
EngineCore encountered a fatal error.
EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

Abbreviated call chain:

```text
worker_busy_loop → sample_tokens → sampler.apply_sampling_params
  → apply_penalties → _penalties_kernel JIT → Ascend ast_to_ttir → boom
```

---

## Root cause / fix

| Layer | Status in this PR |
|-------|-------------------|
| L1 chained `or` | **Fixed** via parentheses |
| L2 BiShengIR / tile after parens | Out of scope (downstream) |
| L3 torch `>>` / RightShift gaps | Out of scope (downstream) |

```python
# before
use_penalty = use_rep_penalty or use_freq_penalty or use_pres_penalty

# after
use_penalty = (use_rep_penalty or use_freq_penalty) or use_pres_penalty
```

Ascend’s own error text recommends splitting the chain with parentheses.

---

## Validation

**Outside CI (Ascend NPU, production-like PD):**
- Repro: chat/completions with e.g. `repetition_penalty=1.1` (+ optional freq/pres).
- Before: `UnsupportedLanguageConstruct` on chained `or`, then worker/Engine death.
- After parentheses: this specific AST error is gone on stacks that only needed L1.

**CI / tests:**
- No new unit test: failure requires Ascend Triton; default CUDA CI cannot exercise it (documented resource constraint).
- Expect existing CUDA sampling / penalties paths to keep passing.

**Limitation:** some Ascend builds may still fail later (L2). NPU plugins may additionally shrink `BLOCK_SIZE` or ship a torch fallback (see omniinfer [#3147](https://gitee.com/omniai/omniinfer/pulls/3147) merged Triton adapt / [#3148](https://gitee.com/omniai/omniinfer/pulls/3148) torch exploration); that does not replace making upstream source AST-safe.

---

## Details / tradeoffs

- Tiny readability change; no CUDA perf impact expected.
- Keeps one shared kernel instead of forking Ascend-only source in core.
- **Merged NPU-plugin fix (same L1):** https://gitee.com/omniai/omniinfer/pulls/3147 — Ascend-compatible MRv2 penalty kernel writing + UT (merged). This upstream PR mirrors the L1 parentheses part into vLLM `main`.
- Alternate NPU torch rewrite (L2/L3 context, closed): https://gitee.com/omniai/omniinfer/pulls/3148

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Skip weight tying for omitted LM heads
author: jzakrzew
body:
## Overview
Fix initialization of pooling models with quantized token embeddings and `tie_word_embeddings=True`. Packed quantized embeddings have no dense `.weight`, causing initialization to crash when an omitted LM head attempts to tie its weights.


## Claims
- Prevents AttributeError when packed embeddings have no dense .weight.
- Skips weight tying for StageMissingLayer placeholders.
- Adds an end-to-end regression comparing pooled embeddings against a dequantized Transformers reference.


## Validation
```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/models/language/pooling/test_embedding.py \
    -k test_pooling_with_tied_quantized_token_embeddings -v
```

Before the fix, initialization fails with: `AttributeError: 'VocabParallelEmbedding' object has no attribute 'weight'`

  After the fix: 1 passed.



## Details
The pooling adapter replaces the unused LM head with `StageMissingLayer`. Previously, the placeholder delegated `tie_weights()` to the original head, which accessed `embed_tokens.weight`. Packed embeddings expose `weight_packed` and `scales` instead.

The placeholder now returns itself from `tie_weights()`.

This fixes omitted heads only. Sequence-classification conversions using `from_2_way_softmax` or `no_post_processing` create a real LM head and still require separate support for extracting dequantized token rows.

Related PRs #45535 and #48870 address quantized embeddings reused by active LM heads. This change specifically handles weight tying delegated through an omitted pooling head.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] fix Anthropic inline-system probe crashing startup
author: Hritik003
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61919: `vllm serve` crashes at startup for `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct`. When the Anthropic `/v1/messages` endpoint is set up, vLLM renders the model's chat template once to check how it handles system messages, and that render raised an uncaught `TypeError`. This PR  stops the server from going down if the render fails.

## Claims

- `vllm serve allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` now starts. Before this change, it stopped with `TypeError: Object of type Undefined is not JSON serializable`.
- OLMo 3 is correctly detected as accepting non-leading system messages, so inline system messages are **not** merged into the leading system prompt, and the prefix cache keeps working.
- If the startup check fails for any reason other than a template error, vLLM falls back to merging instead of stopping the server.

## Validation

- ran `vllm serve allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct --dtype bfloat16` on a local GPU. It crashed at startup before the fix and reached `Application startup complete.` with it.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k TestDetectMergeInlineSystem -q
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Without fix | 2 failed, 5 passed |
| With fix | 8 passed |

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files.

**Model output:** the change only affects the one-time startup check, not how prompts are rendered for requests, so model output is unchanged and no accuracy evaluation was needed.

## Details

**Root cause:** `AnthropicServingMessages.__init__` calls `_should_merge_inline_system`, which calls `_detect_merge_inline_system`. That function renders the chat template with a `[system, user, system, user]` conversation to find out whether the template accepts non-leading system messages. Since #58727, this check renders the model's own template.

The render did not pass `tools`, so in Jinja it was `Undefined`, not `None`. OLMo 3's template branches on `tools is none`. That is false for `Undefined`, so the template ran `tools | tojson`, and `json.dumps` raised `TypeError`. `_detect_merge_inline_system` only caught `jinja2.TemplateError`, so the error reached the top and stopped the server. Real requests to both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` pass `tools=None` and were never affected; only this startup check was.

**Fix:**

Widen `except jinja2.TemplateError` to `except Exception`, falling back to merging (`True`). This is a safety net so that a template the check can't render for some other reason causes at worst unnecessary merging, not a failed startup.

**Tradeoff:** catching `Exception` alone would also stop the crash. But for OLMo 3 it would wrongly decide that merging is needed, which moves inline system messages into the leading system prompt and breaks prefix caching. That's why (1) is included and not only (2).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for `61919` and for `merge_inline_system`. None address this crash. The related open PRs #63368 (fold inline system messages in place) and #53501 (preserve prefix cache for inline system turns) change different behavior.

---

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 when local media access is disabled
author: hemuku90
body:
## Overview

Return HTTP 400 instead of 500 when a request uses a `file://` media URL on a server started without `--allowed-local-media-path`. Fixes #61874.

## Claims

- Disabled local media access is reported as `400 BadRequestError` on the OpenAI chat and render endpoints (sync and async media loading). It was `500 InternalServerError`.
- The access restriction and the error message are unchanged; no file is read.

## Validation

Before/after on a CPU build (macOS arm64), `HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct`, server started **without** `--allowed-local-media-path`:

```bash
vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 1 --port 8811
curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' localhost:8811/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct", "max_tokens": 8,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "file:///tmp/vllm-disallowed-image.png"}}]}]}'
```

| | Response |
|---|---|
| main | `{"error":{"message":"Cannot load local files without \`--allowed-local-media-path\`.","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}` HTTP 500 |
| this PR | `{"error":{"message":"Cannot load local files without \`--allowed-local-media-path\`.","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}` HTTP 400 |

Terminal captures of the same request (top: `main` @ 9e0bc7a651, bottom: this PR @ bc9eb76e9b):

**Before (main): HTTP 500 `InternalServerError`**

![Before: HTTP 500 InternalServerError](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hemuku90/vllm/pr-assets/pr64032-before.png)

**After (this PR): HTTP 400 `BadRequestError`**

![After: HTTP 400 BadRequestError](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hemuku90/vllm/pr-assets/pr64032-after.png)

Same server with `--enable-scale-out`, `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` with this PR: HTTP 400 `BadRequestError` (the path the new regression test uses).

Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py -k "test_fetch_image_local_files and not relative and not space"
# main (with updated assertions): 4 failed — RuntimeError: Cannot load local files without `--allowed-local-media-path`.
# this PR:                        4 passed
pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py tests/multimodal/media/test_unprocessable_entity_error.py
# this PR: 94 passed
```

`tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render_multimodal.py::test_chat_completion_render_rejects_local_file_when_disabled` reuses the existing `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` `vision_server` fixture (no extra server start) and runs in the existing `entrypoints/scale_out` Buildkite step. It was not run locally (needs a GPU for that model); the same endpoint and assertion were checked by hand with SmolVLM above.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: `MediaConnector._load_file_url` raised a bare `RuntimeError` when `allowed_local_media_path` is unset. `create_error_response` maps unclassified exceptions to 500, while the adjacent out-of-directory check raises `ValueError` (400). The fix raises `VLLMValidationError`, the `VLLMClientError` subclass already used in this module, so the status comes from the typed exception path rather than the raw-`ValueError` fallback slated for removal.

Not a duplicate: #61751 handles missing files when local access is *enabled* and does not touch this branch. #63749 is the Rust frontend, which does not support `--allowed-local-media-path`. @ntu-b12505041 expressed interest in #61874 on 2026-10-15 but no PR has been opened since; happy to close this in favor of theirs if one is in progress.

No other code catches `RuntimeError` for this path (only torchcodec decode handlers in `audio.py`, unrelated). The Rust frontend does not support `--allowed-local-media-path`, so no parity change.

title: [Bugfix] Report reasoning and cached tokens in chat derender usage
author: nien-hui
body:
## Overview `/v1/chat/completions/derender` now fills `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` from the reasoning parser and `usage.prompt_tokens_details` from the generate usage, in batch and stream mode, as `/v1/chat/completions` does. Fixes #64038 ## Claims - Batch and stream chat derender report `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` when a reasoning parser is configured. Before: `null`. - Both pass `prompt_tokens_details` through from the generate usage. Before: `null`. - Stream with `n > 1` keeps `completion_tokens_details` `null` (see Details). - 3 new tests (fail on the base commit, pass here), 2 extended; both derender test files pass in full. ## Validation CPU only. Render server on main at 39e6a1aafc (before) and on this branch (after); the generate usage is hand-built with `cached_tokens: 8`. ```bash vllm launch render Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 18100 --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` ```bash python usage.py ```
usage.py ```python import json import sys import requests from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.parser import ParserManager BASE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:18100" M = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B" tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(M) def post(path, body): r = requests.post(BASE + path, json=body) r.raise_for_status() return r.json() chat = {"model": M, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], "max_tokens": 64} gen_req = post("/v1/chat/completions/render", chat) prompt_ids = gen_req["token_ids"] out_ids = tok.encode( "\nThe user wants a greeting.\n\n\nHello!", add_special_tokens=False ) + [tok.convert_tokens_to_ids("<|im_end|>")] gen_usage = { "prompt_tokens": len(prompt_ids), "completion_tokens": len(out_ids), "total_tokens": len(prompt_ids) + len(out_ids), "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 8}, } choice = {"index": 0, "token_ids": out_ids, "finish_reason": "stop"} batch = post("/v1/chat/completions/derender", { "model": M, "chat_request": chat, "prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids, "generate_response": {"request_id": "b", "usage": gen_usage, "choices": [choice]}, }) stream = post("/v1/chat/completions/derender", { "stream": True, "model": M, "chat_request": {**chat, "stream": True}, "prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids, "generate_chunk": {"request_id": "s", "usage": gen_usage, "choices": [choice]}, }) print("message:", json.dumps(batch["choices"][0]["message"], ensure_ascii=False)) print("derender batch usage:", json.dumps(batch["usage"])) print("derender stream usage:", json.dumps(stream["chunk"]["usage"])) parser = ParserManager.get_parser(reasoning_parser_name="qwen3", tokenizer=tok)(tok, None) print( "coupled /v1/chat/completions would report (computed with the parser, not run): " f"prompt_tokens={len(prompt_ids)}, " f"completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens={parser.count_reasoning_tokens(out_ids)}, " "prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens=8 (with --enable-prompt-tokens-details)" ) ```
Before: ```text derender batch usage: {"prompt_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 13, "completion_tokens": 13, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "completion_tokens_details": null} derender stream usage: {"prompt_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 23, "completion_tokens": 13, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "completion_tokens_details": null} coupled /v1/chat/completions would report (computed with the parser, not run): prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens=7, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens=8 (with --enable-prompt-tokens-details) ``` After: ```text derender batch usage: {"prompt_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 13, "completion_tokens": 13, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 8, "created_cache_tokens": null, "multimodal_tokens": null}, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 7}} derender stream usage: {"prompt_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 23, "completion_tokens": 13, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 8, "created_cache_tokens": null, "multimodal_tokens": null}, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 7}} coupled /v1/chat/completions would report (computed with the parser, not run): prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens=7, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens=8 (with --enable-prompt-tokens-details) ``` Stream with `n = 2`: the usage chunk arrives with one index's `stream_state`, so a count there covers that index only (3 or 9 here, where coupled reports the sum, 12) while `completion_tokens` from generate covers both. The details stay `null` instead of a partial number, with either index's state:
n2_stream.py and output ```python """Stream with n=2: send one chunk with for each index, then send the usage chunk with index 0's stream_state. Compares usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens with the sum of the reasoning tokens over both indices. """ import json import sys import requests from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.parser import ParserManager BASE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:18100" M = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B" tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(M) def post(path, body): r = requests.post(BASE + path, json=body) r.raise_for_status() return r.json() chat = {"model": M, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], "n": 2, "stream": True, "stream_options": {"include_usage": True}} gen_req = post("/v1/chat/completions/render", chat) prompt_ids = gen_req["token_ids"] end = tok.convert_tokens_to_ids("<|im_end|>") out0 = tok.encode("\nShort.\n\n\nHi!", add_special_tokens=False) + [end] out1 = tok.encode("\nA much longer thought about greetings here.\n\n\nHello there!", add_special_tokens=False) + [end] parser = ParserManager.get_parser(reasoning_parser_name="qwen3", tokenizer=tok)(tok, None) r0 = parser.count_reasoning_tokens(out0) r1 = parser.count_reasoning_tokens(out1) states = {} for idx, ids in ((0, out0), (1, out1)): resp = post("/v1/chat/completions/derender", { "stream": True, "model": M, "chat_request": chat, "prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids, "prompt_tokens": len(prompt_ids), "generate_chunk": {"request_id": "n2", "choices": [ {"index": idx, "token_ids": ids, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}, }) states[idx] = resp["stream_state"] gen_usage = { "prompt_tokens": len(prompt_ids), "completion_tokens": len(out0) + len(out1), "total_tokens": len(prompt_ids) + len(out0) + len(out1), } for idx in (0, 1): resp = post("/v1/chat/completions/derender", { "stream": True, "model": M, "chat_request": chat, "prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids, "prompt_tokens": len(prompt_ids), "stream_state": states[idx], "generate_chunk": {"request_id": "n2", "choices": [], "usage": gen_usage}, }) print(f"usage chunk sent with state of index {idx}:", json.dumps(resp["chunk"]["usage"])) print(f"index 0 reasoning_tokens={r0}, index 1 reasoning_tokens={r1}, coupled would report sum={r0 + r1}") print(f"completion_tokens from generate (both indexes) = {len(out0) + len(out1)}") ``` ```text usage chunk sent with state of index 0: {"prompt_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 35, "completion_tokens": 25, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "completion_tokens_details": null} usage chunk sent with state of index 1: {"prompt_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 35, "completion_tokens": 25, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "completion_tokens_details": null} index 0 reasoning_tokens=3, index 1 reasoning_tokens=9, coupled would report sum=12 completion_tokens from generate (both indexes) = 25 ```
The 3 new tests on the base commit 39e6a1aafc (test files copied over) and on this branch: ```bash pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -k test_e2e_parsed_usage_details pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -k test_stream_parsed_usage_details ``` Before: ```text > assert usage["completion_tokens_details"]["reasoning_tokens"] == reasoning_tokens E TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable FAILED tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py::test_e2e_parsed_usage_details 1 failed, 90 deselected, 14 warnings in 32.91s > assert usage["completion_tokens_details"]["reasoning_tokens"] == reasoning_tokens E TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable > assert usage["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] == 4 E TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable FAILED tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_usage_details FAILED tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_usage_details_n_gt_1_no_reasoning_tokens 2 failed, 122 deselected, 14 warnings in 32.80s ``` After: ```text 1 passed, 90 deselected, 14 warnings in 33.98s 2 passed, 122 deselected, 14 warnings in 33.23s ``` Both files in full on this branch: ```bash pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py ``` ```text 91 passed, 14 warnings in 227.08s (0:03:47) 123 passed, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 151.96s (0:02:31) ``` ## Details `/v1/chat/completions` counts `reasoning_tokens` with the reasoning parser and keeps the generate server's `cached_tokens`; both derender paths built `UsageInfo` from the token counts alone ([`derender/serving.py` L183-L192](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/39e6a1aafcaea1b90c515dacfc3a20835756758c/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/serving.py#L183-L192), [`online_derenderer.py` L888-L897](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/39e6a1aafcaea1b90c515dacfc3a20835756758c/vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py#L888-L897)). Batch now counts in `_parse_and_assemble` with the parser that parsed the choice; stream counts over every token streamed so far on the usage chunk, and `prompt_tokens_details` passes through from the generate usage. With `n > 1` the stream usage chunk carries one index's `stream_state`, so the count can't cover every choice; `completion_tokens_details` stays `null` there, documented in `derenderer.md`. Out of scope: batch `prompt_tokens` still defaults to 0 without `request.prompt_tokens`, and `output_mode="derender"` on `/inference/v1/generate` (#63103). A generate server with `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` and the GPU parity test were not run. ---

title: [Bugfix] Fix DFlash draft acceptance of 0 with FULL CUDA graphs
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #63587. With the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, the DFlash draft reads a stale kernel block table, so none of its tokens are accepted. This PR maps the draft kernel block tables before the FULL graph replay, the same way `TargetDependentARSpeculator` already does (#57169).

## Claims

- DFlash-family drafts work again under FULL draft CUDA graphs when the KV cache block is split into smaller kernel blocks. Tested with hybrid `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` and a DFlash2 draft on B200: acceptance goes from 0.0000 to about 0.185, the same as the PIECEWISE control (0.1863).
- The FULL draft path from #60692 stays on. Throughput is 20.56–21.21 requests/s, against 6.59–6.67 before the fix and 11.57 with PIECEWISE.
- Adds one row to `test_dflash_correctness`. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- The code change is 8 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py`.

## Validation

Setup: 1 x NVIDIA B200. vLLM at `00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b` (`0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56`), with and without this patch. Target `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` (rev 851bf6e8), draft `nchapman/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash2` (rev 8d8bb628), both BF16. Every server log shows `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `Using FlashAttention version 4`, `Setting attention block size to 640 tokens` and `Capturing dflash2 CUDA graphs (FULL)`.

Server:

```
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"nchapman/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":15}' \
  --max-num-seqs 24 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8000
```

Wait for `Application startup complete`, then run `python client.py`. The client uses only the standard library. It sends 200 chat requests (concurrency 16, `max_tokens` 256, temperature 0) and prints how much the `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters changed.

<details>
<summary>client.py</summary>

```python
import json, sys, time, urllib.request, concurrent.futures as cf, re
base = "http://localhost:8000"
model = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B"
N, C = 200, 16
topics = ["the water cycle","binary search","the French revolution","how a transformer works","photosynthesis","TCP congestion control","the Roman empire","quicksort","black holes","the stock market"]
def metrics():
    t = urllib.request.urlopen(base + "/metrics").read().decode()
    d = {}
    for k in ["num_drafts_total","num_draft_tokens_total","num_accepted_tokens_total"]:
        m = re.search(r"^vllm:spec_decode_%s(?:\{[^}]*\})? ([0-9.e+]+)" % k, t, re.M)
        d[k] = float(m.group(1)) if m else None
    return d
def one(i):
    body = {"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"Write a detailed explanation of {topics[i%10]} (variant {i}). Include examples."}],
            "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0}
    if i == 0: print("REQUEST BODY (example, i=0):", json.dumps(body), flush=True)
    t = time.time()
    r = urllib.request.Request(base + "/v1/chat/completions", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    resp = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(r, timeout=900))
    print(f"req {i} status 200 {time.time()-t:.2f}s tokens={resp['usage']['completion_tokens']}", flush=True)
    return resp
m0 = metrics(); t0 = time.time()
with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(C) as ex: list(ex.map(one, range(N)))
dt = time.time() - t0; m1 = metrics()
d = {k: m1[k]-m0[k] for k in m0}
print(f"requests/s {N/dt:.2f}")
print("drafts", d["num_drafts_total"], "draft_tokens", d["num_draft_tokens_total"], "accepted", d["num_accepted_tokens_total"])
print(f"acceptance {d['num_accepted_tokens_total']/max(d['num_draft_tokens_total'],1):.4f}")
```

</details>

 | Tree | `cudagraph_mode` | Runs | `acceptance` | requests/s |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | base | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (default) | 4 | 0.0000 in every run (0 of 765000 draft tokens) | 6.59–6.67 |
 | base | `PIECEWISE` (control: adds `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`) | 1 | 0.1863 (37889 of 203325) | 11.57 |
 | this PR | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (default) | 6 | 0.1850, 0.1853, 0.1845, 0.1849, 0.1856, 0.1845 | 20.56–21.21 |

```
# base
drafts 51000.0 draft_tokens 765000.0 accepted 0.0
acceptance 0.0000
# this PR (run 1 of 6)
drafts 13678.0 draft_tokens 205170.0 accepted 37948.0
acceptance 0.1850
```

Every request returned status 200 in every run. Base: 3 runs were on one server, and 1 was on a fresh server on the same GPU as the patched runs. This PR: each run started a fresh server, 3 by me and 3 in a separate check. The base result also showed in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit (0 of 765000 accepted).

Regression test (new row `qwen3.5-4b-dflash2-mrv2`, same models, 15 speculative tokens, 32 sequences, default compilation config, GSM8K):

```
cd tests && python -m pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py -k 'qwen3.5-4b-dflash2'
```

 | Tree | Runs | Result | GSM8K accuracy | acceptance_len |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | base | 2 | FAILED: `acceptance_len 1.000 is below 4.095` | 0.845 | 1.00 |
 | this PR | 2 | PASSED | 0.845 | 4.55 |

The thresholds follow the other rows: accuracy 0.8, and acceptance length `4.55 * 0.9`, from the values measured with the fix. `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passes.

## Details

**Root cause.** Qwen3.5 is a hybrid model (attention plus GDN layers). To make the attention page match the mamba page, the KV cache manager uses 640-token blocks. The draft's FlashAttention 4 backend uses 128-token kernel blocks. So the draft attention group reads its block table from the persistent `AttentionGroup.kernel_block_table` buffer (`vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`), and the captured FULL graph reads that buffer. Only `map_to_kernel_block_table` fills it, and only the eager metadata build calls that (`_with_kernel_block_table`).

Since #60692, `DFlashSpeculator.propose` skips `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` when it replays a FULL graph and every draft backend supports `update_draft_decode_metadata`. The in-graph `_update_draft_decode_metadata` only asks each builder to refresh its own data. It does not map the block table. So after capture, the buffer keeps the rows from the dummy all-zero block table: kernel pages 0..4, which belong to the null block. On every replay the draft reads the null block's K/V instead of the request's. The drafts are unrelated to the context, and the target rejects all of them. The output stays correct because the target checks every token.

A debug print before `run_fullgraph` (not part of this PR) confirmed this. Request 0 owned manager block 83, so its kernel row should be `[415, 416, 417, 418, 419]`, but the buffer held `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`. With the fix, it held `[415, 416, 417, 418, 419]`.

**Fix.** In the branch where the build is skipped, call `group.map_to_kernel_block_table(self.block_tables.input_block_tables[group.kv_cache_group_id])` for every draft attention group before the replay. This is the same step `TargetDependentARSpeculator._fused_multi_step_decode` takes before its FULL replay. `map_to_kernel_block_table` already handles the kernel block size, the packed stride and the backend, and it returns at once for groups with no split. When the build does run, it maps the table itself, so that path is unchanged. DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark, LiLiCorr and XPress all use this `propose`.

**Other FULL draft replays checked.** `TargetDependentARSpeculator` (MTP, EAGLE, Gemma4) already maps the table before its fused FULL replay. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` builds the metadata before `run_fullgraph`. `StandaloneARSpeculator` does not use FULL replay.

**Not chosen.** Mapping inside `_update_draft_decode_metadata` would also map again on every `TargetDependentAR` step, which already maps. Reporting `supports_decode_metadata_update = False` for split groups would turn #60692 off for these models.

**Limitations and notes for reviewers.**

- The issue does not name its checkpoints (a 9B FP8 target and an NVFP4 target, served through Dynamo). I validated with the 4B BF16 pair above and plain `vllm serve`. The issue saw acceptance of 0.004 and 0.0005; here it was exactly 0. The issue's `no KV cache group could be identified as the draft model's` warning did not appear here, and I did not look into it.
- The test row uses a community draft checkpoint, `nchapman/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash2`, the one used in the issue thread. If CI should use only official checkpoints, the row can point at another hybrid target/draft pair with the same block split.
- CI: the row id contains `dflash2`, so the nightly `spec-decode-dflash2-nightly-b200` step (`-k "dflash2"`) selects it. `-k dflash2` also selects it in non-B200 steps (H100, MI355), and the thresholds were measured only on B200.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix reshape & cache dropping KV heads past 512 chunks
author: giuseppegrossi
body:
## Overview

`reshape_and_cache` leaves KV heads unwritten when a token has more than 512 16-byte chunks, so `ROCM_ATTN` silently reads stale KV cache data for shapes such as 32 KV heads × head size 192/256 in bf16. This restores a thread-stride loop in the kernel and adds a regression test. It fixes Pattern B of #62697. Pattern A (decode reads at block size 528 on gfx1201) is a separate problem and isn't addressed here.

## Claims

- `reshape_and_cache` now writes every KV head for any `num_kv_heads * head_size`. Before, chunks past the 512th per token were skipped whenever `num_kv_heads * head_size * cache_element_size > 8192` bytes.
- With the reporter's script, the three failing Pattern B cases of #62697 now match `TRITON_ATTN` (max error ≤ 0.0006, previously 0.097–0.196).
- No other test outcome changes, and no performance change for shapes that fit within 512 chunks per token (see Validation).

## Testing & Validation

All runs used 1× MI355X (gfx950)
```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k test_reshape_and_cache_many_heads \
    tests/compile/passes/test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py -k ROCM_ATTN \
    tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py 
```
**Reporter's reproducer** (the gist script from #62697, unmodified), `ROCM_ATTN` max error against an fp32 reference:

| Case | Baseline | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `p2-d256-bs16-gqa1` (32/32 heads, head 256, decode) | 0.1935, mismatch | 0.0006 |
| `p2-d192-bs16-gqa1` (32/32 heads, head 192, decode) | 0.1955, mismatch | 0.0006 |
| `p2-d256-bs16-gqa1-prefill` (cached context) | 0.0967, mismatch | 0.0003 |
| `ok-d256-bs16-gqa1-fresh-prefill` | 0.0085, but cache read-back off by up to 5.31 | 0.0085, cache exact |

The other six cases (GQA-4, and the block-528 cases, which use the Triton writer) pass on both builds. A direct check of `ops.reshape_and_cache` on the baseline found exactly the unwritten heads predicted by the root cause below (heads 16–31 for 32 × 256; heads 21–31 for 32 × 192, with head 21 partly written), and none with the fix.

**Performance.** `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_reshape_and_cache.py --dtype bfloat16 --block-size 16 --mode cudagraph --iters 200`, sweeping 2 to 65,536 tokens. Each config ran 3 rounds with baseline and fix alternating; numbers are medians.

| KV heads × head size, cache | Chunks/token | Work completed by baseline | Fix/base, all sizes | Fix/base, ≥1024 tokens | Baseline spread |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 × 128, auto | 128 | 100% | 1.004× | 0.997× | 0.4–20.1% |
| 8 × 256, auto | 256 | 100% | 1.005× | 1.001× | 0.3–17.8% |
| 32 × 128, auto | 512 | 100% | 1.001× | 0.996× | 0.3–17.8% |
| 32 × 256, fp8 | 512 | 100% | 0.984× | 0.969× | 0.4–18.9% |
| 32 × 256, auto | 1024 | 50% | 1.604× | 2.260× | 0.2–17.8% |
| 64 × 256, fp8 | 1024 | 50% | 1.650× | 2.169× | 0.3–16.9% |
| 128 × 128, auto | 2048 | 25% | 2.693× | 4.487× | 0.3–15.4% |

For shapes within 512 chunks, the loop executes once and performance is unchanged (0.969–1.001× for ≥1024 tokens). For shapes over 512 chunks, raw latency is not an equivalent-work comparison: the baseline skipped half or three quarters of the writes. Normalized by bytes actually written, the fixed kernel retains 88.5%, 92.2%, and 89.1% of the broken baseline's partial-write throughput for the three over-limit configurations at ≥1024 tokens.

### GSM8K Test 

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, on one MI355X, `main` at dd4e40142a:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen1.5-14B-Chat --attention-backend <backend> --block-size 16 --max-model-len 4096 --seed 0
```

| Backend | Code | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| ROCM_ATTN | main | 0.411 |
| TRITON_ATTN | main (reference) | 0.688 |
| ROCM_ATTN | this PR | 0.691 |

Most current models use GQA with 8 KV heads, so they stay far under the limit (8 × 128 bf16 is 128 chunks). This affects models whose KV heads × head size per GPU exceeds 4096 elements in bf16, such as 13B+ multi-head models (Qwen1.5-14B, Llama-2-13B, OLMo-2-13B) at TP=1, or MHA models with head size 192/256. On MI300/MI355 it only shows up when `ROCM_ATTN` is selected explicitly. On RDNA it's the default backend.

## Details

**Root cause.** #25955 replaced the kernel's thread-stride loop over all elements with one thread per (KV head, 16-byte chunk) pair, but kept the launch cap of `dim3 block(std::min(num_heads * head_div_x, 512))`. When `num_heads * head_size / x > 512` (`x = 16 / cache element size`, so 8 for fp16/bf16 and 16 for fp8), the extra chunks get no thread. For example, with bf16 and 32 KV heads, head size 256 means 1024 chunks, so heads 16–31 are never written. Head size 192 means 768 chunks, so head 21 is partly written and heads 22–31 not at all. The unwritten slots keep whatever the cache block held before, so the outputs are silently wrong rather than crashing. `test_reshape_and_cache` only uses `NUM_HEADS = [8]` (at most 256 chunks), so CI never hit the limit.

**Fix.** The per-chunk body is wrapped in `for (h_block_idx = threadIdx.x; h_block_idx < num_heads * h_block_count; h_block_idx += blockDim.x)`, and the scale setup moves above the loop. `reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel` already strides by `blockDim.x` in the same way. The launch configuration is unchanged. Most of the diff is re-indentation, so view it with whitespace hidden (10 lines changed).

This keeps one block per token, preserving the current launch behavior and avoiding repeated token metadata and scale loads. A 2D launch with multiple blocks per token could expose more parallelism for over-limit shapes, but would add scheduling overhead and needs tuning across token counts and GPU architectures. The strided loop is the minimal correctness fix; a multi-block layout can be evaluated separately as a performance optimization.

AI assistance (Cursor) was used for the root-cause analysis, the patch, the test and the validation scripts. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix DeepSeek-OCR zero-sum patch guard in _encode…
author: nrenvo
body:
Fixes #64075.

_encode_local_features in deepseek_ocr.py and deepseek_ocr2.py used torch.sum(patches).item() == 0 to detect "no crop patches", so a tiled image whose normalized pixels cancel to zero (e.g. half-white/half-black 1536x768) wrongly returned None, dropped local features, and crashed EngineCore with a placeholder/embedding shape mismatch. Replace the guard with patches.numel() == 0; #59417 fixed the equivalent check in _parse_and_validate_image_input but left this one as "not engine-fatal", which #64075 disproves.

New test class TestDeepseekOCREncodeLocalFeaturesGuard fails on the base commit (2 failed) and passes with the fix (13 passed in tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_ocr.py); ruff check and ruff format are clean.

title: [BugFix]/minicpm ocr downsample mode
author: HwwwwwwwH
body:
## Overview

Pass `downsample_mode` through MiniCPM-OCR image resize when counting visual tokens. transformers 5.21 makes this argument required, and the previous call used the 5.20 signature.

## Claims

- `MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo._compute_visual_tokens` now passes the image processor's `downsample_mode` to both `find_best_resize` calls and to `get_refine_size`.
- The MiniCPM-OCR processing tests use the same signature, so a missing argument fails the token-count tests.

## Validation
when inferencing or starting server with vllm for [MiniCPM-OCR 1.0](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0), met this error.

```
TypeError: MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.find_best_resize() missing 1 required positional argument: 'downsample_mode'
```

## Details

Root cause: token counting still called `find_best_resize` and `get_refine_size` as in transformers 5.20. In 5.21 those methods require `downsample_mode`, so placeholder sizing raises `TypeError` before inference. 
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.21/src/transformers/models/minicpm_ocr/image_processing_minicpm_ocr.py#L165-L182

The value passed is `image_processor.downsample_mode` from the processor already pinned for the request, so a per-request override and the checkpoint default stay on the same grid as the pixels.

title: [CI] Fix stale NVFP4 decode test selector on DGX Spark
author: grYe99
body:
## Overview

Fixes #64090. The DGX Spark nightly attention step still selects `test_flashinfer_xqa_nvfp4_decode_correctness`, which #60532 renamed to `test_flashinfer_nvfp4_decode_correctness`. Pytest therefore collects 0 tests and the step fails. This updates the `-k` filter to the substring `nvfp4_decode_correctness`.

## Claims

- The `flashinfer-nvfp4-xqa-dgx-spark` step selects `test_flashinfer_nvfp4_decode_correctness` again.
- Sink-prefill coverage stays out of this fix. #63826 will later widen the same selector to `-k "nvfp4_decode_correctness or nvfp4_sink_prefill"`.

## Validation

- On current `upstream/main` (`d0c20bb840`), `.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml` still passed `-k test_flashinfer_xqa_nvfp4_decode_correctness`. The only test whose name contains `nvfp4_decode_correctness` is `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py::test_flashinfer_nvfp4_decode_correctness`.
- Pytest's `-k` expression matches `nvfp4_decode_correctness` against that name and does not match the old `test_flashinfer_xqa_nvfp4_decode_correctness` token. The new expression does not mention `nvfp4_sink_prefill`.
- No DGX Spark runner was used. The reported failure is `160 deselected / 0 selected`, which this selector change addresses.

## Details

#60532 renamed the test (XQA on SM12x and fa2 on SM8x) and left the Buildkite `-k` filter on the old name. A full-name `-k` match does not match the new function name, so the nightly step exits 1.

This PR changes only that one command in `.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml`. It does not change production code and does not include the sink tests from #63826.

This is narrower than the open PRs that also touch the selector:

- #63826 updates the stale name only as part of the fp8/NVFP4 attention-sink feature, and it adds `nvfp4_sink_prefill`.
- #63169 updates the selector together with `head_size=64` cases that #64090 notes are blocked on a newer FlashInfer.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Don't specialize MRV2 logits-stats kernels on num_logits
author: ayush1399
body:
## Overview

MRV2 spec decode JIT-compiles `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel` during serving. Triton specializes `num_logits` on divisibility by 16, and warmup only covers one of the two cases. This PR marks `num_logits` as `do_not_specialize` on that kernel and on `_compute_local_residual_mass_kernel`. The argument was added in #61451. Related: #49349.

## Claims

- No runtime JIT of either kernel when `num_logits` changes between steps.
- No output change: `num_logits` only bounds the bonus-logit mask.

## Validation

End to end on Gemma-4 31B BF16 + MTP (k=4), TP8, H100, `--jit-monitor-verbose`, with mixed sampling/JSON/tool traffic at batch sizes 1–64:

| | Runtime JIT of `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel` |
|---|---|
| `main` | 2 per rank (FP32 and BF16 logits) |
| This PR | 0 |

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py
# 98 passed
```

## Details

No new unit test. The change only drops a compile-cache specialization, and the end-to-end JIT monitor run above covers it.

Not a duplicate: #54630 and #63819 cover other warmup gaps and don't touch these kernels.

AI assistance was used. I reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

title: [Perf][DSA] Read BF16 logits directly in persistent top-k
author: Pb314314
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Merged by WoosukKwon on 2026-10-30 as [`e31cf3dec7cf`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0), following approval of final PR head `5ff957619959`. The validation revisions and their scope are recorded below.

Let the existing persistent top-k backend read BF16 indexer logits and widen loaded scores to FP32 inside its kernels. On SM100 decode without DCP, this removes the full FP32 logits allocation whenever `auto` resolves to persistent, as well as for explicit persistent.

Query chunking is separate work. This PR complements [#62172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172), which implements BF16 input for cooperative top-k. This change implements persistent, filtered and sampled paths instead. Open-PR searches found no separate persistent-BF16 implementation. The caller uses the same `takes_bf16_logits()` capability-interface design as #62172; cooperative support remains with that PR.

## Claims

- Keep the existing backend selection and top-k algorithms. Scores loaded from BF16 widen to FP32 before binning/refinement; register score arrays remain FP32.
- Remove the dense FP32 logits copy for supported persistent decode calls, including default auto. Cooperative, DCP and prefill retain their existing behavior. No DeepSelect switch or query-row chunking is introduced.
- Preserve exact selected scores and valid top-k indices in the tested cases. Equal-score index identity/order and generated-token equivalence are not claimed.

## Validation

### Performance breakdown and memory traffic

**DeepGEMM's logits computation is unchanged.** This PR saves work **after** BF16 logits have been produced: it removes the separate BF16-to-FP32 materialization and lets persistent top-k read BF16 directly. It does not reduce Q/K projection work, the score computation, or the number of logits. The measurements below exclude DeepGEMM and are not end-to-end model speedups.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["DeepGEMM: unchanged score computation"] --> B["BF16 logits in GPU memory: unchanged"]
    B -->|Before PR| C["Separate conversion kernel: read BF16, write FP32"]
    C --> F["Full FP32 logits buffer"]
    F --> O["Load FP32 scores; existing FP32 top-k algorithm"]
    B -->|With PR: supported persistent calls| N["Load BF16 scores; widen in registers; same FP32 top-k algorithm"]
    O --> I["Top-k indices"]
    N --> I
```

| Where the saving occurs | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| External conversion | Allocate a full FP32 logits buffer; read 2 bytes and write 4 bytes per valid score | Remove this allocation and GPU conversion kernel |
| Top-k input loads | 4 bytes per FP32 score; an aligned four-score load reads 16 bytes | 2 bytes per BF16 score; an aligned four-score load reads 8 bytes and expands to four FP32 registers |
| Score arithmetic inside top-k | FP32 comparison/binning/refinement | The same FP32 algorithm, with on-load widening; register score arrays are still FP32 |

Code: [producer and conversion bypass](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L939-L954), [old allocation and conversion kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L297-L329), and [FP32/BF16 load helpers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L70-L100).

**Measured breakdown: pre-PR `98fc6da9d735` versus PR `293880733f87`, GB200.** The PR source is unchanged by the subsequent main merges. The BF16 top-k timing includes its loads, register widening, and selection; it is not the cast alone.

| Q / valid K / top-k | External conversion: before → after (µs) | Native top-k: FP32 → BF16 (µs) | Native top-k latency change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | 2.848 → removed | 4.832 → 5.632 | +16.56% |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | 19.296 → removed | 31.232 → 30.240 | -3.18% |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | 35.264 → removed | 44.800 → 42.352 | -5.46% |

The **33–44% full selection-stage improvement** in the long-row cases mainly comes from eliminating the external conversion; native top-k alone improves by only about 3–5%. The short-row native kernel is slower with BF16, while the measured complete caller still improves after removing the conversion. Smaller input loads can help, but widening adds register instructions. Halving score-input bytes does not establish that total HBM traffic or latency halves; cache behavior and multiple passes matter. No hardware-counter measurement proves a bandwidth-only explanation.

**Allocation size and accessed bytes are different quantities.** At Q=128 and valid K=100000, the removed conversion logically reads 25.6 MB of BF16 data and writes 51.2 MB of FP32 data (decimal MB). A single full scan by top-k reads 51.2 MB of FP32 score payload versus 25.6 MB of BF16 payload; this is byte accounting, not measured DRAM traffic. The full FP32 allocation is larger because it retains capacity W=262144 and padded stride=262656: about **128.248 MiB**. That temporary disappears; the original BF16 logits and existing workspace remain. CUDA graph replay does not remove conversion kernels automatically; this PR removes that node and its FP32 storage from supported captured paths.

These component timings are separate cold-cache ablations, **not additive**. The complete caller measurements below remain the primary before/after result.

<details>
<summary>Breakdown measurement method and why the columns are not additive</summary>

Baseline `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus measured PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`, using the same frozen runtimes and matching fixed BF16 inputs as the full-stage table below. GB200 job 41138: A/B/B/A fresh processes, 30 cold-L2 CUPTI graph samples per stage/run (60 per arm). Conversion uses the actual `as_fp32_logits`; top-k uses the native persistent entrypoint. Input capacity W=262144, padded stride=262656, host scheduling bound=1048576.

These are separately captured cold-cache ablations, not timestamps of nodes in one production graph. Conversion warms its FP32 output for the following kernel, while standalone top-k starts cold. The full caller also clears the output-index buffer; this native-only ablation omits that common operation. Summing the component columns therefore does not reconstruct the full-stage table. Jointly captured conversion+FP32 top-k medians are retained separately in the raw results (6.816, 46.5755 and 78.0805 µs); the full caller table remains the primary before/after comparison.

For intuition only, one full score scan would give 2-byte BF16 read + 4-byte FP32 write + 4-byte FP32 read before this PR, versus a 2-byte BF16 read after it. This 10→2 byte accounting excludes unchanged producer writes, metadata/workspace accesses, multiple selection passes and cache effects; it is not a measured traffic reduction or a 5x speedup prediction.

Every ablation passes exact selected-score, valid/unique-index and input-preservation checks. Raw samples, identities and commands are retained in `main_vs_packed_breakdown_v1` (`bench.py`, `run.sbatch`, `SUMMARY.json`, `results/41138_*`). These component measurements do not establish full-model accuracy or end-to-end performance.

</details>

### Full selection-stage results

Recorded performance baseline: **unmodified pre-PR base `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus measured PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`**. The baseline has no persistent BF16 support and widens the BF16 producer output to a full FP32 logits tensor. The PR keeps BF16 for supported persistent calls. Neither arm includes cooperative BF16 support from #62172 or the FP32-producer configuration from #64580. This table measures the whole PR against its pre-PR baseline, not an intermediate PR commit.

Job 41130 on an exclusive GB200: A/B/B/A fresh processes, CUPTI cold-L2 CUDA-graph replay, 30 samples/run (60 per arm/shape). The actual indexer caller receives identical fixed injected BF16 logits. **Timing includes the required full-tensor conversion and top-k**, but excludes the real DeepGEMM producer, CPU Python dispatch and the model. Caller/provider source files match the stated revisions. Both target CUDA translation units were rebuilt; unrelated native objects/runtime are held fixed. This is a matched component comparison, not a fresh whole-main build or an end-to-end model benchmark.

| Q / valid K / top-k | Backend | Without PR / with PR median µs | Latency change | Without PR / with PR extra live MiB |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 / 4096 / 512 | cooperative (unchanged control) | 7.504 / 7.488 | -0.21% | 64.123 / 64.123 |
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | persistent | 7.616 / 6.784 | -10.92% | 66.000 / 0.000 |
| 256 / 8192 / 1024 | persistent | 15.648 / 15.456 | -1.23% | 256.498 / 0.000 |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | persistent | 47.072 / 31.392 | -33.31% | 128.248 / 0.000 |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | persistent | 78.240 / 43.488 | -44.42% | 128.248 / 0.000 |

W=262144, row stride=262656, host scheduling bound=1048576; valid K length is separate. Small-Q cooperative is an unaffected control: both arms still widen and consume FP32, and its 0.21% timing difference is not claimed as an optimization gain. Persistent cases skip the widening in the PR. The longer-context results include removing that conversion; they must not be described as a 33–44% speedup of the top-k kernel alone. No universal speedup or no-regression claim is made for unmeasured shapes/backends/hardware.

<details>
<summary>Per-process medians and memory interpretation</summary>

| Q / valid K / top-k | Baseline run medians µs | PR run medians µs |
|---|---|---|
| 64 / 4096 / 512 | 7.4880, 7.5200 | 7.4880, 7.4880 |
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | 7.6320, 7.6160 | 6.7840, 6.7680 |
| 256 / 8192 / 1024 | 15.6480, 15.6480 | 15.4080, 15.4880 |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | 46.9120, 47.2000 | 31.4555, 31.2960 |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | 78.1755, 78.2400 | 43.5200, 43.3920 |

Extra live peak excludes the already allocated BF16 inputs, outputs and workspace. Zero extra allocation does not mean zero total device/model memory. Graph-private reservations agree across repeats: Q64 66→66 MiB; Q65 66→0 MiB; Q256 258→0 MiB; both Q128 cases 130→0 MiB. Allocator reservation can exceed live tensor bytes. Profiling reservation is unchanged, so increased model KV capacity is not claimed.

All four arms at each shape have identical input hashes and selected-score bit bags, pass valid/unique-index checks, preserve input bits, and witness the expected conversion/dtype/backend behavior. Baseline FP32 widening is bit-exact against the fixed BF16 scores. Prior experiments are archived under their original baselines; their numbers are not mixed into this table.

</details>

**Expanded DeepSeek configuration coverage (GB200, job 41191).** Eighteen additional persistent-path cases use checkpoint-derived top-k and capacity, covering 16K/32K/64K raw contexts, Q=128/512/1024, uniform and mixed valid lengths, empty rows, and rows shorter than top-k. All 18 measured full-stage medians improve by **5.85%–39.66%** versus the same pre-PR baseline; no cooperative performance points were rerun. This is configuration-derived selection-stage coverage, not measured production-frequency coverage or an end-to-end model speedup.

<details>

Baseline `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus current PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`; same pinned matched top-k builds as the primary table, on an exclusive GB200 node (`gb200-rack1-04`). A/B/B/A fresh processes, 30 cold-L2 CUPTI graph replays per process (60 samples/arm). The measured boundary retains actual caller output clearing, conditional conversion and automatic persistent dispatch. It injects deterministic synthetic BF16 logits instead of running DeepGEMM; the kernels and auto policy are not retuned.

## Details

The aligned BF16 vector-load helpers use the same packed integer load and bit-expansion implementation as #62172; scalar and guarded tail loads remain available. FP32 overloads are unchanged.

### BF16 and FP32 load behavior

The helpers separate the input storage type from the existing FP32 selection arithmetic:

| Helper | BF16 input | FP32 input |
|---|---|---|
| `to_float(x)` | Widen one BF16 value with `__bfloat162float(x)` | Identity: `return x;` |
| `load_score2(ptr)` | Read 4 bytes containing two BF16 values and expand them to two FP32 values (8 bytes of value storage) | The existing `float2` load (8 input bytes) |
| `load_score4(ptr)` | Read 8 bytes containing four BF16 values and expand them to four FP32 values (16 bytes of value storage) | The existing `float4` load (16 input bytes) |
| Guarded tail load | Read only valid BF16 elements, widen individually, and fill invalid elements with negative infinity | Retain the existing FP32 predicated-load implementation |

For the aligned four-score BF16 helper, [`topk_histogram_4096.cuh:78–82`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L78-L82) contains:

```cpp
const uint2 raw = *reinterpret_cast<const uint2*>(ptr);
return make_float4(
    __uint_as_float(raw.x << 16), __uint_as_float(raw.x & 0xFFFF0000u),
    __uint_as_float(raw.y << 16), __uint_as_float(raw.y & 0xFFFF0000u));
```

`uint2` contains two 32-bit words, so the input payload is 8 bytes. Each word holds two BF16 values. The shifts and masks place each BF16 bit pattern in the upper 16 bits of its own FP32 word; `__uint_as_float` reinterprets that word as a float. `make_float4` returns four 32-bit values: **8 input bytes become 16 bytes of FP32 values, not 32 bytes**. These values feed the kernel's existing FP32 register computation; the helper does not allocate or write a full FP32 logits tensor in global memory.

The [FP32 scalar overload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L70-L73) returns its input unchanged, and the [FP32 four-score overload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L75-L77) retains `*reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(ptr)`. FP32 inputs are never downcast to BF16.


Code references: [BF16-to-FP32 register conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L71-L92), [backend capability query](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py#L236-L255), and [conditional full-tensor conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L951-L954).

BF16 input is widened losslessly on load; this avoids materializing FP32 logits in global memory. All existing raw-score rereads, including exact overflow recovery, accept the input type and immediately widen it. The FP32 comparison keys, candidate/refinement logic and backend thresholds are preserved. Candidate-block selection retains FP32 compact scores for auto/persistent so this change does not alter that selection stage's arithmetic.

The capability query reports input support; it does not change `resolve_backend()` or choose a backend by measured speed. It inspects host shape/type metadata without reading GPU tensor values. Cooperative continues to receive FP32. BF16 native persistent requires at least 128 KiB opt-in shared memory and contiguous columns. Existing addressing limits remain unchanged; large-row measurements do not cross the pre-existing filtered uint32 row-offset limit.

### Integration with #62172

The two features can coexist and share `takes_bf16_logits()` plus the same BF16 load helpers. The local reconciled version was validated as described above. **Current online heads still require rebase/conflict resolution**; helper alignment alone does not make them a clean merge.

Whichever PR merges second should:

- Combine cooperative and persistent capability predicates and their test expectations, retaining the existing explicit DeepSelect support.
- Preserve main's exact-overflow correction from #62936 when rebasing the older cooperative branch.
- Retain guarded BF16 predicated loads needed by persistent, instead of importing the cooperative-only assertion that rejects that instantiation.
- Preserve small-Q auto's FP32/cooperative fallback where only the widened stride satisfies TMA alignment, and preserve FP32 compact candidate-block scores for explicit cooperative as well. These integration-policy guards were included in the local validated reconciliation.

No cooperative implementation is copied into this standalone persistent PR. Cooperative-first followed by this PR rebasing onto the shared interface is one straightforward merge order; either order requires the same reconciliation.
