title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Build the folded q_b_proj / W_UK weight on the root model
author: seungrokj
body:
## Purpose

#60110 folds `q_b_proj` and W_UK into one GEMM for Kimi-K3's MLA decode query on ROCm. The folded weight, `_w_fold`, is built in `KimiLinearForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading`. But Kimi-K3 checkpoints load as `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration`, and the model loader calls only the root model's `process_weights_after_loading`. The root model doesn't define one, so `_w_fold` stays `None`.

The fold is on whenever AITER MLA runs with an fp8 KV cache and no DCP / PCP. Every such serve then fails during startup, at the first CUDA graph capture (see the reproduction below). DCP > 1 is unaffected because the fold is off there.

This PR makes `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration.process_weights_after_loading` call the text model's hook, which builds each MLA layer's `_w_fold`.

## Reproduction (`main` @ e96b490b12)

8× MI355X, `main`'s Python tree on image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce39`, the newest nightly. The only `csrc` changes since that image are a perf-only ROCm int4 skinny-GEMM change and a CUDA-only NVFP4 MLA binding. vLLM's own decode path (no `decode_backend` override), TP8, DCP1, fp8 KV, DSpark k = 7, concurrency 1:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm \
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --language-model-only --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":16,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[8,16]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

On `main`, every TP rank fails about 3 minutes after launch, in the CUDA graph memory profile:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 720, in determine_available_memory
    cudagraph_memory_estimate = self.model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory()
...
File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py", line 403, in forward
    attn_out = self._fused_decode(
File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py", line 210, in _fused_decode
    assert self._w_fold is not None
AssertionError
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error '', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
```

## How this PR fixes it

`process_weights_after_loading` now runs on the text model, which calls `_build_w_fold()` on every MLA wrapper. `_fused_decode` therefore gets a real `_w_fold`. The fold's math is unchanged; only the missing call is added.

```python
def process_weights_after_loading(self) -> None:
    self.language_model.process_weights_after_loading()
```

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py`, which adds `test_root_model_builds_the_fold` (CPU-only, mocks the text model).
- The reproduction above, run on `main` and on this PR, then GSM8K 5-shot (all 1319 questions, `lm_eval` `local-completions`, concurrency 1, real rejection sampling).

## Test Result

| | `main` @ e96b490b12 | this PR (`main` + this commit) |
|---|---|---|
| `test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py` | new test fails, other 12 pass | 13 passed |
| Server startup (command above) | `AssertionError: self._w_fold is not None` at CUDA graph capture | ready in about 3.5 min, no tracebacks |
| GSM8K 5-shot, strict / flexible | — | **0.9659 / 0.9659** (±0.0050) |
| DSpark mean acceptance length | — | 4.62 |

For reference, #60683 reports GSM8K 0.9598 / 0.9629 (off / on) for Kimi-K3 at c1 k7, so this is within about one standard error.

The same commit is also in #61435. Whichever PR merges first, the other drops it on rebase.

title: [Bugfix][DP] Log cross-engine step statistics ordering at debug level
author: ivanium
body:
## Overview

Log DP coordinator out-of-order step reports at DEBUG instead of WARNING. Reports from different engines can arrive in a different step order even when each engine reports in order.

## Claims

- Avoid per-report warning output for cross-engine statistics arrival skew at the default log level; retain the diagnostic at DEBUG.
- Preserve all statistics updates, step snapshots, and wave coordination.

## Validation

- Existing run evidence: a saved audit of a 32-rank DP deployment counted 1,751,591 occurrences, totaling 290,881,789 bytes. All reports had the same wave as the global latest report; 1,751,578 lagged by one step and 13 by two steps. This is evidence of logging volume, not a measured throughput improvement.
- `ruff check vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py` — passed.
- `ruff format --check vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py` — passed.
- `python -m py_compile vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py` — passed, using the existing venv.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py docs/usage/troubleshooting.md` — all applicable checks passed, including mypy and Markdown lint.
- Tests and model evaluations were not run. The sole executable change is the diagnostic level; no inference or statistics-processing behavior changes. No new test was added solely to assert log severity. Runtime validation remains pending for this draft.

## Details

The comparison is against one global `(wave, step)` position. For example, engine A's step 101 may arrive before engine B's step 100, causing a warning even if B's previous report was step 99. The warning alone does not establish same-engine message regression or a failed request.

This is a logging-only alternative to #52936, which adds per-engine position tracking and rejects regressing reports. It does not add state or discard reports, and it does not claim to repair cross-engine snapshot consistency. The original snapshot/load-balancing design from #21617 remains intact. Open-PR searches found #52936 but no separate logging-only fix.

The troubleshooting guide documents the diagnostic and how to enable it with `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`. The tradeoff is reduced default visibility of this ordering diagnostic, including any anomalous cases that reach the same branch.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the patch and PR (the exact underlying model version was not exposed); `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` assisted with source analysis and checklist review. This is a draft for human review.

title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Keep Ray metrics usable without Ray Serve
author: eicherseiji
body:
## Summary

- Import optional Ray Serve separately from Ray metrics.
- Keep `RayPrometheusStatLogger` usable when Ray is installed without the Serve extra.
- Fall back to an empty `ReplicaId` when no Serve replica context is available.

## Context

`RayPrometheusStatLogger` only uses Ray Serve to retrieve a replica ID. If `ray.serve` fails to import because `ray[serve]` dependencies are absent, the shared `try` block also discards the successful `ray.util.metrics` import. Metric construction then raises the misleading error that Ray is not installed.

This is the vLLM-side counterpart to ray-project/ray#67444. That change fixes one Serve-extra import failure in Ray. vLLM should still keep its Ray metrics independent from optional Serve dependencies.

## Duplicate check

I searched open vLLM PRs and issues for `ray_wrappers`, the `RayPrometheusMetric requires Ray to be installed` error, and Ray Serve extras. I found no existing change that separates these imports.

## Tests

- `/home/ubuntu/work/vllm-main/.venv/bin/python` smoke check with `ray.serve` unavailable and `ray.util.metrics` available: passed. Constructed a `RayCounterWrapper` and verified its tags were `{"ReplicaId": ""}`.
- `/home/ubuntu/work/vllm-main/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/metrics/ray_wrappers.py`: passed, including ruff, mypy, and repository checks.

## AI assistance

I used OpenAI Codex to help implement and test this change. I reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma 4 vision crash with online FP8 quantization
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

Fixes #63732. With `--quantization fp8`, an image request to Gemma 4 returns HTTP 500 and kills the engine core. The transformers patch embedder casts the pixel values to `input_proj.weight.dtype`. Once vLLM quantizes that layer, this dtype is `float8_e4m3fn`, so the FP8 linear gets an FP8 input. This PR runs the patch embedder steps in `gemma4_mm.py` with the pixel values cast to `self.model_dtype`. It makes the same change for the pooled states before `embedding_projection` in the encoder CUDA graph path.

Compared with #63911, this fix:

- Also fixes `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and `EmbeddingGemma2Model`. They borrow Gemma 4's `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` and build their own FP8-quantized tower. [#63911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63911) swaps the embedder only in `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.__init__`, so their image and video paths still crash with the reported error (checked with a probe that loads E4B with FP8 and builds each model's own tower, since no checkpoint of either model was at hand).
- Adds tests that fail on the old code for video and for the encoder CUDA graph path, including the `embedding_projection` cast. The compiled and encoder-graph cases in [#63911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63911) pass on the old code, so they guard neither path.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 image requests with online FP8 no longer crash the engine. `input_proj` stays FP8 and still uses the same FP8 kernel.
- The same fix covers video inputs. On the old code, `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` with video enabled crashed at engine start, because the encoder profile run sends dummy video through the same patch embedder.
- The same fix covers the encoder CUDA graph path (the patch embedder call and the `embedding_projection` cast).
- Online `fp8_per_block`, `fp8_per_channel` and `mxfp8` (eager, custom ops off) crashed at engine start on the old code. With this fix, all three answer `The sign in the image is a **STOP** sign.`
- `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and `EmbeddingGemma2Model` get the same fix through the borrowed methods.

## Validation

Hardware and software: 1 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 16 GB (SM 12.0), vLLM `00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b` (`0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56`) with and without this patch, transformers 5.20.2.

Reproducer. Server:

```bash
vllm serve --port 18000 --model google/gemma-4-E4B-it --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enforce-eager --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0}'
```

Once it logs `Application startup complete`, send a 64x64 white PNG:

```bash
BODY='{"model":"google/gemma-4-E4B-it","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAEAAAABACAIAAAAlC+aJAAAAS0lEQVR42u3PMQ0AAAwDoPo33UrYvQQckD4XAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAYHLAMpT0sIcNbcEAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"}},{"type":"text","text":"What color is this image?"}]}],"max_tokens":16}'
OUT=$(curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}' localhost:18000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$BODY")
echo "$OUT"
echo "IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=$(echo "$OUT" | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}')"
```

Before (3 of 3 runs, each on a fresh server): `IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=500`. The server log shows:

```
RuntimeError: ... "dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant_kernel_scalar_type" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
```

After (6 of 6 runs, each on a fresh server: 3 by me and 3 in a separate re-check): `IMAGE_REQUEST_HTTP_STATUS=200`, answer `"The image is **white**."`. No `not implemented`, `Traceback` or `EngineDeadError` line in any log. The server still selects `CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod`. The old code gives the same answer only when `input_proj` is left out of FP8 with `--quantization-config '{"ignore":["vision_tower.patch_embedder.input_proj"]}'`.

New tests, on the old `gemma4_mm.py` and on this patch:

 | Test | Old code | This PR |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | `pytest -v -s tests/models/quantization/test_fp8.py -k gemma4` (image, video) | 2 failed, reported `RuntimeError` | 2 passed |
 | `pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k gemma4_fp8` (image, video) | 2 failed, reported `RuntimeError` | 2 passed |

On the old code, the CUDA graph row fails earlier, in the eager video profile run. So I also checked each CUDA graph change on its own: with only the `encoder_cudagraph_forward` patch-embedder call reverted, or only the old `embedding_projection.weight.dtype` cast restored, the row fails with the same error.

Borrowing models: a script builds a vision tower with random weights from the E4B config (unquantized) and calls `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` on all three classes. Image and video outputs for all three match the old code exactly (same shapes and sums).

`pre-commit run` on the four changed files passes.

## Details

Root cause: vLLM builds the Gemma 4 vision tower with `AutoModel.from_config`. It then replaces each `nn.Linear` with a `ReplicatedLinear` that carries the tower quant config. With online FP8, `input_proj.weight` becomes `float8_e4m3fn` after loading. The transformers `Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder.forward` does:

```python
pixel_values = 2 * (pixel_values - 0.5)
if (target_dtype := self.input_proj.weight.dtype).is_floating_point:
    pixel_values = pixel_values.to(target_dtype)
hidden_states = self.input_proj(pixel_values)
```

This is right for a plain `nn.Linear`. For a quantized layer, though, the weight dtype is the storage dtype. FP8 is a floating type, so the guard lets the cast through. The bf16 pixel values are rounded to FP8 without a scale, and the FP8 linear's activation quant gets an FP8 input. `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` only accepts fp16, bf16 or fp32. A debug run confirmed the chain: the pixel values enter the patch embedder as bf16, and only `vision_tower.patch_embedder.input_proj` receives an FP8 input. `encoder_cudagraph_forward` had the same mistake in vLLM code: it cast the pooled states to `embedding_projection.weight.dtype`, which is also FP8 under the tower quant config.

The CUDA kernel runs when the `quant_fp8` custom op is on: with `--enforce-eager`, with `+quant_fp8`, and by vLLM's default for block-scaled FP8 checkpoints and ROCm AITER FP8 linear. With the op off, eager `forward_native` also fails (`"abs_cuda" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'`). Only the default compile mode passes without an error, and there the pixel values are still rounded to FP8 without a scale.

Fix: a module-level `_embed_patches(patch_embedder, pixel_values, pixel_position_ids, padding_positions, dtype)` repeats the steps of the transformers forward (`2 * (x - 0.5)`, `input_proj`, `_position_embeddings`, sum), but casts to the given dtype. The image, video and encoder CUDA graph paths call it with `self.model_dtype`. The CUDA graph path also casts the pooled states to `self.model_dtype`, as the eager paths already do before `embed_vision`. The quant config is not touched, so the layers stay FP8. For an unquantized layer nothing changes, because then the weight dtype is the model dtype. The helper is a module-level function, not a method, because the two borrowing models copy `_process_image_input` and `_process_video_input` without inheriting from Gemma 4. A method would be missing on those classes.

Alternatives not taken:

- Building `input_proj` without quantization: this changes which layers the user's quantization covers. It can also break loading of pre-quantized checkpoints that quantize this layer, and it leaves the `embedding_projection` cast as it is.
- Making the FP8 linear accept an FP8 input: this treats the crash site, and by then the input has already been rounded to FP8.

Tradeoffs and limitations:

- `_embed_patches` uses the private `_position_embeddings` of the transformers embedder. This file already splits `Gemma4VisionModel.forward` into its parts, so this goes one level deeper in the same style.
- With online FP8 in the default compile mode, which did not crash before, image outputs may change a little because the pixel values are no longer rounded to FP8 first. On `input_proj` against the bf16 weight, the relative error went from 4.50% to 3.68%. I did not run a vision eval.
- The tests use `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, which CI already uses. E2B has the same vision tower and would be cheaper, but I could not confirm the answer checks (`stop`, `book`) on E2B.
- CI: `gemma4_mm.py` is added to `source_file_dependencies` of `quantized-models-test` and its AMD mirror, so the eager test runs when this file changes. This adds an estimated 14% more runs of that step. The `gemma4_fp8` row (`core_model`) runs in the existing multimodal step.
- Not run on AMD.
- Out of scope: online `mxfp4` on SM 12.x fails at engine start in `input_proj` with `ValueError: SM12x cute-dsl requires NVFP4 with 128x4 scales`, the same before and after this patch, with a bf16 input.

title: [Doc] Fix long-text embedding example pooler config and GPU pinning
author: bantianyue
body:
## Purpose

The long-text embedding example (`examples/pooling/embed/openai_embedding_long_text/`) had two problems that break it for anyone copying it:

- The README's `--pooler-config` snippet uses `"pooling_type": "auto"`. `PoolerConfig` only accepts `CLS`, `LAST` or `MEAN`, so pasting that JSON into `vllm serve` fails validation. `auto` is only a convenience inside `service.sh`, which maps it to a real type before building the config. I changed the snippet to `MEAN` (the default for the example's e5 model) and added a short note explaining this.
- `service.sh` hard-coded `export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3,4,5`. That fails on any host with fewer than 3 GPUs and silently ignores the caller's own device selection. I removed it so the normal `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` from the environment applies. I also renamed the `VLLM_ENABLE_CHUNKED_PROCESSING` shell variable to `ENABLE_CHUNKED_PROCESSING` and stopped exporting it, since vLLM never reads it and the `VLLM_` prefix suggests it's a real env var.

## Duplicate check

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "openai_embedding_long_text"`: no results
- `gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open "VLLM_ENABLE_CHUNKED_PROCESSING"`: no results
- `gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open "pooling_type auto"`: no results

## Test plan / results

```text
$ python -c 'from vllm.config.pooler import PoolerConfig; PoolerConfig(pooling_type="auto", ...)'
auto REJECTED: Input should be 'CLS', 'LAST' or 'MEAN' [type=literal_error, input_value='auto']
$ python -c '... PoolerConfig(pooling_type="MEAN", use_activation=True, enable_chunked_processing=True, max_embed_len=3072000)'
MEAN OK
$ bash -n examples/pooling/embed/openai_embedding_long_text/service.sh
(ok)
```

This only changes the docs and example script. No library code changes, and I didn't run a GPU serve.

AI assistance was used; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Omit null `annotations` and `usage.prompt_tokens_details` in chat completions
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

On a default server, a non-streaming chat completion returns `"annotations": null` in each message and `"prompt_tokens_details": null` in `usage`. The OpenAI spec makes both fields optional but not nullable, so strict schema validators reject the reply. This PR leaves both keys out when they are `None`. It also types `annotations` as a list, as the spec and the OpenAI SDK do. Fixes vllm-project/vllm issue 61425.

Another PR, #61431, which fixes the same issue, has had no activity for two weeks.

## Claims

- Non-streaming chat completions no longer send `annotations: null` or `usage.prompt_tokens_details: null`. A field that has a value is still sent.
- `ChatMessage.annotations` is now `list[OpenAIAnnotation] | None`, the same as the OpenAI spec and SDK. Before, a real value could not be sent in the right shape.
- `/v1/completions`, and any other response that uses `UsageInfo`, also stops sending `prompt_tokens_details: null`.

## Validation

Setup: 1 x NVIDIA B200. vLLM commit `77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989` (`0.32.0rc1.dev100+g77154ca61`). Model `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`. Default server flags.

Reproducer:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 18061
```

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18061/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply READY."}],"max_tokens":16,"temperature":0}' \
| python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("CHECK", json.dumps({"annotations": d["choices"][0]["message"].get("annotations","<absent>"), "prompt_tokens_details": d["usage"].get("prompt_tokens_details","<absent>")}))'
```

Before: 3 of 3 runs on this commit showed the bug. It also showed in 3 of 3 runs with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989` image.

```
"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"<think>\nOkay, the user said \"Reply READY.\" I need to respond appropriately","refusal":null,"annotations":null,"audio":null,"function_call":null,"reasoning":null}
"usage":{"prompt_tokens":11,"total_tokens":27,"completion_tokens":16,"prompt_tokens_details":null,"completion_tokens_details":null}
CHECK {"annotations": null, "prompt_tokens_details": null}
```

After: 6 of 6 runs showed the fix, each on a fresh server. I made 3 of them, and a separate re-check made the other 3.

```
"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"<think>\nOkay, the user said \"Reply READY.\" I need to respond appropriately","refusal":null,"audio":null,"function_call":null,"reasoning":null}
"usage":{"prompt_tokens":11,"total_tokens":27,"completion_tokens":16,"completion_tokens_details":null}
CHECK {"annotations": "<absent>", "prompt_tokens_details": "<absent>"}
```

The model text did not change. Only the two keys changed. One more server start with the fix failed because a GPU test running at the same time held the GPU memory. That run sent no request.

Other checks on a live server with the fix:

- `/v1/completions`, non-streaming: `"usage":{"prompt_tokens":1,"total_tokens":5,"completion_tokens":4,"completion_tokens_details":null}`.
- Streaming chat with `include_usage`: the last chunk has `"usage":{"prompt_tokens":11,"total_tokens":15,"completion_tokens":4}`. This path already used `exclude_none=True` before the fix.
- With `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`: `CHECK {"annotations": "<absent>", "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "created_cache_tokens": 0, "multimodal_tokens": null}}`. The field is still sent when it has a value.

Tests:

```bash
python -m pytest -v tests/entrypoints/openai/test_tool_choice_content_none.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py
```

- With the fix: `10 passed`. With the two old protocol files put back: `3 failed, 7 passed`. The three failures are the three new tests.
- Existing tests with the fix: `chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k "not TestGPTOSS"` 181 passed, `completion/test_completion_error.py` 46 passed, `anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` 108 passed, `cohere/test_cohere_chat_message.py` 9 passed, `openai/test_tool_calls_serialization.py` 6 passed.
- Not run: the `TestGPTOSS*` classes, which start a real `openai/gpt-oss-20b` server. Also not run: `cohere/test_serving_conversion.py` and `cohere/test_serving_streaming.py`, because the `cohere` package is not installed in my environment.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the four changed files: all hooks pass.
- Both test files already run in Buildkite (`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause: the non-streaming chat route returns `JSONResponse(content=result.model_dump())` (`chat_completion/api_router.py`). A plain `model_dump()` writes every `None` field as `null`.

- `ChatMessage.annotations` defaults to `None`, and nothing in chat completions sets it. It was also typed as one `Annotation`, but the spec and the SDK use a list.
- `UsageInfo.prompt_tokens_details` is `None` whenever `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` is off.

`ChatMessage._serialize` drops an empty `tool_calls`, but nothing dropped these two fields. `exclude_unset=True` would not help either. `serving.py` assigns `usage.prompt_tokens_details` after it builds `UsageInfo`, so the field counts as set even when it is `None`.

Spec (openai-openapi `openapi.yaml` 2.3.0): `ChatCompletionResponseMessage.annotations` is `type: array`, and `CompletionUsage.prompt_tokens_details` is `type: object`. Both are optional and not nullable. `refusal`, `audio` and `function_call` are nullable, so they stay as they are.

Fix: `Field(default=None, exclude_if=lambda value: value is None)` on the two fields. vLLM already uses this pattern for `ResponsesResponse.metrics` (`responses/protocol.py`). It applies to both `model_dump()` and `model_dump_json()`, so every route that dumps these models gets the fix. `exclude_if` needs pydantic 2.11 or later, and vLLM requires 2.12 or later. The fields stay on the models, so code that reads `usage.prompt_tokens_details` as an attribute (the Anthropic and Cohere layers) does not change.

Options I did not choose:

- `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` in the router. It also drops `content: null` and `logprobs: null`, and the spec requires those keys. It would also fix only one router.
- `[]` and `{}` as defaults. `PromptTokenUsageInfo()` dumps `cached_tokens: null`, which the spec does not allow either. An empty details object would also claim details that `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` is meant to turn on.

Points for review:

- `usage.completion_tokens_details` is still `null`, and the spec has the same rule for it. I left it out because the issue does not ask for it. Also, `test_streaming_reasoning_usage_counts_across_deltas` in `test_serving_chat.py` asserts `model_dump()["completion_tokens_details"] == expected_details`, where `expected_details` is `None` when reasoning details are off. The same change on that field makes this test fail with `KeyError`. A maintainer should decide whether that test should change.
- Typing `annotations` as a list is a small break for outside Python code that passes one `Annotation` object to `ChatMessage`. Nothing in `vllm/` sets this field, and that input never gave a reply that the spec or the SDK accepts.
- The `UsageInfo` change also removes `prompt_tokens_details: null` from completions, pooling, scoring and transcription responses.
- Sample outputs in `docs/models/pooling_models/classify.md`, `docs/models/pooling_models/embed.md` and `examples/features/openai_batch/README.md` still show `"prompt_tokens_details": null`. They are old captured outputs, and I left them unchanged.
- The served `/openapi.json` still marks both fields as nullable, because pydantic does not put `exclude_if` into the schema.
- With `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`, the details object still has vLLM-only keys set to `null` (for example `multimodal_tokens`). That is outside this fix.

title: [Doc] Fix Case 4 math rendering in hybrid KV cache manager
author: hechengkai
body:
## Overview

Fix the two Case 4 equations in the Hybrid KV Cache Manager design document that render as literal LaTeX on the published documentation site. Resolves #64178.

## Background and fix status

Issue #64178 records that the published Case 4 equations appear as literal LaTeX. The underlying `main` Markdown lacks blank lines around display math inside numbered list items; the full MkDocs build reproduces raw `$$` in the generated HTML. This PR proposes the four-line spacing fix. It is open for review and has not been merged or deployed.

### Before and after screenshots

**Before — published documentation page:**

![Before fix: Case 4 displays literal LaTeX instead of equations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hechengkai/vllm/3b5d25d2a07dbbb04da5a071441fb0cb158d8357/issue-evidence/64178/published-case4-before.png)

**After — local MkDocs preview of this PR (not yet merged or deployed):**

![After fix: Case 4 equations render as display math](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hechengkai/vllm/9634757d652a9c6f5b0f667a5eefc70a0fd31aaa/issue-evidence/64178/local-case4-after.png)

## Claims

- Add the blank lines required for Arithmatex to parse display math inside numbered list items.
- Preserve the existing equations and the display-math style used elsewhere in this document.
- This does not duplicate #63717 or #63728: those PRs modify other equations in the same file, while this PR changes only Case 4.

## Validation

- Base: `6376fda7a95904abf8977011af526c693c4c3004` (`main`).
- `API_AUTONAV_EXCLUDE=vllm PYTHONUTF8=1 python -m mkdocs build --clean`: completed before and after the change using the repository's pinned docs dependencies.
- In the generated Case 4 HTML, Arithmatex nodes changed from 1 to 3 and literal `$$` delimiters changed from 4 to 0. The malformed `<em>` tag disappeared.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `pre-commit run markdownlint-cli2 --files docs/design/hybrid_kv_cache_manager.md`: passed.
- Browser automation could not inspect localhost due to its URL security policy. The human submitter reviewed the four-line diff and confirmed the local document change before submission.
- The full pre-commit hook could not complete in the Windows environment while initializing unrelated hook environments; the targeted Markdown lint and full docs build above completed.

## Details

Arithmatex requires block math to be separated by empty lines. In Case 4, the opening `$$` followed the numbered-list text immediately, so Markdown emitted raw delimiters and interpreted underscores in the first equation as emphasis. Adding blank lines before and after the two display-math blocks makes them parse like other block equations in the same document. No formula content or vLLM runtime code changes.

AI assistance was used to investigate the Markdown rendering, prepare the four-line change, and run the documentation builds. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and validated the rendered page before submission.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Restore --input-len/--output-len/--prefix-len in vllm bench throughput
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

`vllm bench throughput` silently ignores `--input-len`, `--output-len` and `--prefix-len` on the random dataset and benchmarks 1024 / 128 / 0 instead, while warning that the matching `--random-*` flag was also given. Regression from #29105.

## Claims

- `--input-len/--output-len/--prefix-len` take effect again; an explicit `--random-*` flag still wins, and with neither the defaults stay 1024 / 128 / 0.
- The "Both --X and --random-X are specified" warnings only fire when both are actually passed, and "--prefix-len will be ignored" only when `--prefix-len` is passed.
- The help of all six flags, and so the CLI reference, states the precedence and the effective defaults.

## Validation

```bash
vllm bench throughput --model RedHatAI/gemma-3-1b-it-FP8-dynamic --input-len 2048 --output-len 512 --prefix-len 64 --num-prompts 8
```

| | sampled lengths (log) | prompt / output tokens | warnings |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | input 1023, output 128 (the 1024 / 128 / 0 defaults) | 8192 / 1024 | 3 ("Both --input-len and --random-input-len are specified", same for output and prefix) |
| this PR | input 2047, output 512 | 16896 (8 × (2048 + 64)) / 4096 | none |

(The log reports the input length after the special token; the 64-token prefix shows in the prompt-token total.)

Every flag combination, from the real parser through `validate_args` and `get_requests` (gpt2 tokenizer, random dataset; prompt length includes the prefix):

| flags | main: prompt / output, warnings | this PR: prompt / output, warnings |
|---|---|---|
| none | 1024 / 128, "Both --prefix-len and --random-prefix-len" | 1024 / 128, none |
| `--input-len 256 --output-len 64 --prefix-len 32` | **1024 / 128**, 3 × "Both ..." | **288 / 64**, none |
| `--random-input-len 200 --random-output-len 16 --random-prefix-len 8` | 208 / 16, "Both --prefix-len ..." | 208 / 16, none |
| `--random-prefix-len 0` | 1024 / 128, "Both --prefix-len ..." | 1024 / 128, none |
| `--input-len 256 --random-input-len 100` | 100 / 128, "Both --input-len ...", "Both --prefix-len ..." | 100 / 128, "Both --input-len ..." |
| `--dataset-name hf` (no length flags) | "--prefix-len will be ignored" | no `--prefix-len` warning |

New tests build args with the real parser (the existing `test_to_serve_args_keeps_legacy_flag_fallback` uses a bare `Namespace` without the `--random-*` attributes, which is why it passes on main):

```bash
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py -k "precedence or not_warn"
# main (these tests, main's throughput.py): 5 failed, 2 passed
#   assert (1024, 128, 0) == (2048, 512, 64)
#   assert not ['Both --input-len and --random-input-len are specified. ...', ...]
#   assert not ['Both --prefix-len and --random-prefix-len are specified. ...']   (x3)
# this PR: 7 passed

pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py -k "not test_bench_throughput"
# this PR: 16 passed
```

## Details

- **Root cause.** #29105 moved the random dataset onto the shared `add_random_dataset_base_args`, whose `--random-*` lengths default to 1024 / 128 / 0. `_to_serve_args` (`getattr(args, "random_input_len", input_len)`) and `validate_args` treat `None` as "not passed", but the parser never leaves them `None`, so the legacy value is never used and the conflict warnings always fire.
- **Fix.** The throughput parser leaves the three `--random-*` lengths unset (default `None`), and `_to_serve_args` resolves explicit `--random-*` > legacy flag > `RandomDataset.DEFAULT_*`, from one `_RANDOM_LEN_FALLBACKS` table that also writes the help text. `bench mm-processor` passes its own parsed `--random-*` values (never `None`) and is unaffected.
- **No duplicate.** No open issue or PR reports or fixes this; searched open PRs and issues for `bench throughput` with `--input-len` / `--random-input-len`.
- **`--prefix-len` default.** It defaulted to 0, so it always looked passed: `--random-prefix-len` alone warned, and every non-random dataset warned that `--prefix-len` would be ignored. It now defaults to `None` like `--input-len` / `--output-len`.
- **Docs.** With the `--random-*` lengths unset in the parser, the CLI reference would no longer show their defaults, so all six flags' help now states: explicit `--random-*` > legacy flag > `RandomDataset` default (1024 / 128 / 0).
- **Impact in tree.** The documented example in `docs/cli/README.md` (`--input-len 32 --output-len 1`) has been running 1024 / 128 since #29105, and `benchmarks/benchmark_pin_memory.py` works around the bug by setting the `--random-*` lengths to `None` by hand.
- **Removed check.** `validate_args` required `--input-len` or `--random-input-len` for a random dataset; since #29105 it could not fire, and keeping it would now break runs that pass neither. Those keep today's 1024 / 128 / 0.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Count bounded-replay SWA allocations in the lazy walk target
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview

In lazy mode, SimpleCPUOffload does not offload blocks when requests free them. Each step it walks the GPU free queue from the eviction end and offloads the cached blocks it passes, so a block is already on CPU by the time the allocator reuses it. This only works if the walk length (`_target_free`, from `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) covers every block one step can take from the free queue.

`_estimate_lazy_target_blocks` only iterates over `prefix_cacheable_groups`. DeepSeek-V4.1's bounded-replay SWA groups (`SlidingWindowSpec(bounded_replay=True)`) are not prefix-cacheable: on a prefix hit their state is rebuilt by replaying the window, so they are never offloaded. They still allocate blocks for every scheduled token from the same GPU free queue, up to `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, block_size)` per group per step, just like full attention. Since they are left out of the target, the walk covers less than one step allocates. Cached prefix blocks just past the walk go to the SWA groups and are overwritten before they are offloaded, so their CPU copy never exists and later requests miss the CPU cache.

This PR counts non-cacheable `SlidingWindowSpec` groups in the target at `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, block_size)`. It complements #59383, which fixes where offloaded blocks are returned in the free queue; this PR fixes how far the walk goes.

## Claims

- In lazy mode, one walk covers the blocks every group can allocate in the next step, including bounded-replay SWA groups.
- No change for models without non-cacheable SWA groups, or for eager mode.

## Validation

- New `test_lazy_walk_covers_bounded_replay_swa_groups` fails on main (the walk stores 8 of the 12 blocks the next step can take) and passes with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/`: 165 passed, 8 skipped.
- Step simulation on the scheduler (walk, store completes, allocator takes one step's blocks from the free-queue head; 128 cached blocks; `max_num_batched_tokens=64`, block size 16). Cached blocks reallocated before being offloaded:

| | FA only | FA + 3 bounded-replay SWA groups |
|---|---|---|
| main | 120 / 128 | 120 / 128 |
| #59383 | 0 / 128 | 64 / 128 |
| #59383 + this PR | 0 / 128 | 0 / 128 |

No E2E run. The scheduler-level simulation reproduces the issue directly.

## Details

- Not a duplicate: #59383 returns lazily offloaded blocks to the eviction end of the free queue; it does not change the walk length. On main, #59383's issue dominates, so this PR shows its full effect on top of #59383. The two are independent and can merge in either order.
- Only non-cacheable `SlidingWindowSpec` groups are counted, at `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, block_size)` like full attention. Other non-cacheable specs (`CircularBufferSpec`, `HiSparseHotSpec`) hold a fixed number of blocks per request and stay excluded.
- Tradeoff: with bounded replay on, the target grows, so each walk may offload more blocks per step. That is what the allocator consumes anyway.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Retain unconfirmed source WRITEs across session teardown
author: liranschour
body:
## Overview

Part of #63602 (gap 3). When a P2P session is torn down, the source no longer releases a NIXL WRITE that may still be running. It keeps that transfer's handle, its source pins and the peer's old registration until the transport reports the transfer stopped, bounded at 120 s.

## Claims

- `ServerRole.close()` no longer releases `PROC`/`PEND` transfers or fails (unpins) the store jobs they read.
- `remove_remote_peer()` no longer frees the descriptor list and remote agent that a running transfer was prepped against.
- A reconnect under the same `peer_id` never sees the old session's retained transfers.
- Retention is bounded. Past `_RETAINED_HOLD_CAP_S` (120 s) the transfer is force-released with an error log, so a wedged handle can't permanently shrink the cache.

## Validation

The issue's CPU reproducer `test_gap3_unsafe_close.py`:

```
main:     cancel_calls=[([0], 'immediate')]; remaining_handles=[]; failed_stores_returned_for_unpin=[1]   -> FAILED
this PR:  cancel_calls=[([0], 'wait')];      remaining_handles=[0]; failed_stores_returned_for_unpin=[]  -> PASSED
```

New tests, run with this PR's test files on `main`'s code (7 of 8 fail for the reported reason):

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py -k "retain or retire or releases_stopped or without_inflight"
E   AssertionError: assert [([0], 'immediate')] == [([0], 'wait')]
E   AttributeError: 'SessionCloseResult' object has no attribute 'retained'
E   AssertionError: Expected 'release_dlist_handle' to not have been called. Called 1 times.
E   AttributeError: 'NixlTransport' object has no attribute 'poll_retired'
...
7 failed, 1 passed
```

(The one that passes, `test_remove_remote_peer_without_inflight_releases_at_once`, guards the unchanged path.)

With this PR:

```
$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.../nvidia/cu13/lib pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p
338 passed
$ pre-commit run --files <changed>      # mypy included
Passed
```

Not validated on GPU. CI runs these tests under `misc.yaml` (`pytest -v -s v1/kv_offload`), and they are CPU-only, using the fake transport and a mocked NIXL agent. An e2e run that actually wedges a WRITE (for example `rc_gda` re-enabled, as in #63499) has not been done yet.

## Details

**Root cause.** On reap, `_reap_dead_sessions` / `_reap_idle_sessions` call `session.close()` and then `ServerRole.close()`. That ran `transport.cancel(all inflight)` in the default `"immediate"` mode and returned every store job as failed. The manager then called `remove_remote_peer()`. Releasing a `PROC` handle does not stop the RDMA WRITE (`NixlTransport.cancel` docstring; #59790 saw a WRITE land after `remove_remote_agent`). So this unpinned CPU blocks the NIC may still read, and freed NIXL request and descriptor state while it was still in use. `_drain_abort` and `_timeout_pending_store_jobs` already refuse to do this, and teardown was the one path that didn't.

**Change.**
- **`ServerRole.close()`** cancels in `"wait"` mode. Transfers that are still running come back as `SessionCloseResult.retained` (`tid → store job_ids`), and their jobs are left out of `failed_stores`.
- **`NixlTransport.remove_remote_peer()`**
  - Marks the peer's in-flight entries `retired`. `poll()` skips retired entries, so a reconnected session under the same id can't receive a stale completion.
  - Defers releasing the old dlist and remote agent until no retired transfer references them.
  - `poll_retired()` releases transfers that have stopped. It uses the same terminal rule as wait-mode cancel: done, a non-PROC state, or `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`. It does not charge the peer, since a reconnected peer under that id isn't at fault.
- **`DataTransport`** gets default `poll_retired()` / `force_release_retired()`, so other transports need no change.
- **Manager**
  - Keeps `_retained` and calls `_poll_retained()` once per poll round. A store job fails (unpins) only once no retained transfer reads it.
  - Past 120 s it calls `force_release_retired()` and logs an error.
  - Shutdown keeps its existing bounded drain, now including retained transfers.

**Tradeoffs and limits.**
- The 120 s cap is a judgment call: after it, the old unsafe release happens anyway, but rarely and loudly instead of on every teardown. Whether NIXL/UCX teardown can fence a stalled WRITE, which would let the cap shrink or go away, is the open fencing question in #63602.
- This is the source side only. Consumer slot reuse after disconnect is #61667.
- This PR should land before #63715 (consumer disconnect on a missed AbortAck), because that change makes teardowns more frequent. The gap 2 source-side stall deadline is stacked on this PR and follows separately.

Complexity: about 190 non-test lines (medium), all within `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/`. No core components are touched.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Fault a peer whose source WRITE stalls
author: liranschour
body:
## Overview

Part of #63602 (gap 2, source half). Builds on #64250 (merged), which retains the stalled transfer across the teardown this fault triggers. One commit on main (`ffaa825b33`).

A source WRITE that NIXL keeps reporting as `PROC`/`PEND` past `VLLM_P2P_TRANSFER_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` (default 20 s) now faults its peer. The fault releases nothing.

## Claims

- A stalled source transfer faults its peer and ends the session. Before this change, nothing ever faulted it, and `write_blocks()` kept posting new WRITEs to the wedged peer.
- The fault releases nothing. The stalled transfer and its pins are retained across teardown (#64250) until the transport reports it stopped.
- A stall fault skips the 10 s peer-fault drain, since a stalled transfer would never drain.

## Validation

The issue's source-side property: a WRITE still pending at 300 s must have faulted its peer, while keeping the transfer and its store job held.

```
main (with #64250): consumer_failed_at_s=35.0; source_alive=True;  inflight=[0]; pinned=[1]; peer_fault=None                    -> FAILED
this PR:            consumer_failed_at_s=35.0; source_alive=False; inflight=[0]; pinned=[1]; peer_fault=transfer stalled for 20s -> PASSED
```

The issue body's `test_gap2_pending_transfer.py` still fails, for an unrelated reason. It hard-codes the consumer failing at exactly 40 s, but since #63781 the consumer fails at 35 s (30 s load + 5 s abort-ack). The check above is the same scenario without that hard-coded timing.

New tests, run with this PR's tests on #64250's code:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py -k stall
FAILED ...::test_stalled_transfer_faults_peer_without_releasing   E  assert not True
FAILED ...::test_stalled_peer_gets_no_new_writes                  E  assert None is not None
2 failed, 2 passed
```

(The two that pass guard the no-fault cases: under the deadline, and the deadline disabled with 0.)

With this PR:

```
$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.../nvidia/cu13/lib pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p
426 passed
$ pre-commit run --files <changed>      # mypy included
Passed
```

CPU-only, and CI runs it in `misc.yaml`. **The 20 s default is not yet measured on GPU.** It is far above the ~131 ms p99 tiering-lock hold we measured on H200 at c256, and above healthy transfer times seen so far. Before this leaves draft, I'd like to measure transfer duration by size under load from NIXL telemetry, and run a real stall (`rc_gda` re-enabled, as in #63499).

## Details

**Root cause.**
- `NixlTransport.poll()` treats `PROC`/`PEND` as "wait" forever.
- `_drain_abort` holds a stuck transfer and its AbortAck forever, and only logs after 10 s.
- Nothing records when a transfer was submitted, so nothing faults the peer.
- `write_blocks` is gated only on `peer_fault`, so the source keeps feeding the wedged peer.

In the GPU run in #63602, 36 WRITEs never completed, and pulls from a *healthy* peer dropped (679/847).

**Change.**
- `_InflightXfer.submitted_at` is set on submit.
- `ServerRole.collect_results()` checks for stalls when the transport reports no fault. Once the oldest in-flight transfer is past the timeout, it sets `peer_fault = "transfer stalled for Ns"` and `transfer_stalled`.
- Everything after that is the existing #60374 path: no new WRITEs, `_escalate_peer_fault` then `DisconnectMsg` (the consumer fails its loads), reap, and the data-plane reconnect backoff.
- `_escalate_peer_fault` skips its drain wait when `transfer_stalled` is set.

Detection lives in `ServerRole`, not `NixlTransport`. It sits next to the `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` logic it mirrors, it doesn't depend on which transport is used, and the session reproducers exercise it directly.

**Why it depends on #64250.** Without retention, the teardown this fault triggers would run `cancel(mode="immediate")` and unpin the stalled transfer's blocks. That is the very release the deadline must not cause.

**New env var** `VLLM_P2P_TRANSFER_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` is a float, default 20, and 0 disables it. It is documented in `vllm/envs.py` and in the P2P table in `docs/usage/security.md`, next to the other `VLLM_P2P_*` limits.

Complexity: about 40 non-test lines.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Fail a timed-out load at once, defer releasing its slots
author: liranschour
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Part of #63602 (gap 2, consumer half). A timed-out P2P load now fails at the load timeout. Its destination chunks stay held until the peer confirms its WRITEs ended (AbortAck/TransferDone), or until the session ends.

This is the P2P side of the deferred-release API from **#63779** (merged). It replaces the consumer slot quarantine proposed in #61667 and supersedes #63715, whose disconnect-on-missed-AbortAck is folded in.

Three commits on main: #63715's disconnect on a missed AbortAck (`ac5c9806e6`) with its test constant fix (`0262efcc3a`), then the deferred release (`f00e9c6710`).

## Claims

- **The request falls back 5 s sooner.** A load that times out is reported failed at once, instead of after a further `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S`: 10 s instead of 15 s for symmetric P2P, 30 s instead of 35 s for PD. The same applies to `finish()` of an in-flight load.
- **No early slot reuse.** The failed load's chunks stay out of the free pool until AbortAck, a late TransferDone, or session close. Before, the abort-ack timeout and `close()` freed them through `complete_write(False)` while the peer's WRITE might still land in them.
- **Every hold is bounded.** A missed AbortAck disconnects the peer (the folded-in #63715), and `close()` sets every held load's release.

## Validation

New and updated tests, run with this PR's test files on the code before the deferred-release commit (#63779 + main + #63715). 8 fail for the reported reason:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py \
    -k "TestClientFlows or holds_chunks_until_abort_ack or carries_its_deferred_release"
E  ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)          # no failure at the load timeout
E  AttributeError: 'LoadResult' object has no attribute 'deferred_release'
E  AssertionError: assert 7 not in {7: JobMetadata(...)}                # job still pending at the load timeout
E  TypeError: LoadResult.__new__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'deferred_release'
8 failed, 8 passed
```

`test_timed_out_load_holds_chunks_until_abort_ack` drives a real `TieringOffloadingManager` and `CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager`, with a real `P2PSession` as the P2P tier. At the load timeout the job finishes, the key misses, and the chunk is held (`num_deferred_release_chunks == 1`, the free count unchanged). After AbortAck, the chunk returns to the free pool.

With this PR:

```
$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.../nvidia/cu13/lib pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py
408 passed
$ pre-commit run --files <changed>      # mypy included
Passed
```

The #63602 consumer scenario, with a WRITE that never ends:
- the load fails at 30.001 s, with its release unset;
- the abort-ack timeout disconnects the session;
- `close()` sets the release.

All of this is CPU-only, and CI runs it in `misc.yaml`. GPU e2e is pending. The plan is to drop inbound `abort_fetch` on the source pod and check three things: fallback at about 10/30 s, `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_deferred_release_chunks` rising and then returning to 0, and the hold histogram at about 5 s.

## Details

**Root cause.** `JobResult` used to carry both the outcome and the memory release, so P2P had to pick one of two problems:
- Report late: on a load timeout, keep the job until AbortAck or `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S`.
- Free too early: an abort-ack timeout, or `close()` on peer death, reported `success=False`. The TieringManager then freed the chunks through `complete_write(False)` with the peer's WRITE possibly still landing.

#63779 splits the two. This PR uses it.

**Lifecycle of a load in `ClientRole`:**

| event | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| load timeout / `finish()` | send AbortFetch, keep job | send AbortFetch, **report failed now** with `deferred_release=Event()`, keep load |
| AbortAck | report failed | `event.set()`, no second result |
| late TransferDone | report its result | `event.set()`, no second result (request already fell back) |
| AbortAck timeout | report failed (chunks freed) | no result; record `expired_abort_ack`, which makes the session disconnect |
| `close()` | fail every in-flight load (chunks freed) | set every held load's event; in-flight loads not yet reported fail as before |

**The release point is ack or disconnect**, as agreed in #61667 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#issuecomment-6418290229)). Two cases remain:
- **A WRITE that is stalled but still alive when the session ends.** On the source side this is covered by #64250, which keeps unconfirmed WRITEs across teardown, and #64251, which faults a peer whose WRITE stalls. Whether NIXL teardown fences a stalled WRITE stays open on #63602.
- **Loads never sent** (still queued before ConnectAck) also fail through `close()`, without a deferred release. Nothing was posted for them.

**`drain_jobs()`** keeps polling while any held load remains. Each hold is bounded by the abort-ack timeout and then the disconnect, which meets #63779's rule that every event is set before `drain_jobs()` returns.

**Why not #61667 as is:** it re-reports the same `job_id` with `memory_safe=True`, which needs parallel quarantine tables. It also rejects `reset_cache()` with `UnsafeTransferError` and a retry loop. #63779's alternatives section covers this. Here each job has exactly one outcome, and the release carries none.

Complexity: about 110 non-test lines in `p2p/` (client 154+/−, manager +10), plus #63715's 44.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Fit the MLA backend bf16 atol to a bf16 SDPA reference
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- `test_mla_backends.py`: raise the bf16 (`kv_cache_dtype="auto"`) atol in `_run_backend_correctness` from 1e-2 to 2e-2.

`test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[False-trtllm-gen-auto-glm-MLAPrefillBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_FA]` started failing in MI355 V1 Attention Shard 2/4, for example in https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97849 and in main build 97866. TRITON_MLA and ROCM_AITER_MLA both failed with max diff 0.015625. No vLLM PR caused it. The runtime-shard plan is rebuilt from rolling main timings, and the new plan put 286 `test_backend_correctness` cases ahead of this test in the same process. The module seeds only once, at import, so those cases move the default CUDA generator's offset, and the GLM case gets a different random draw. The test compares against a torch SDPA reference that is also computed in bf16. At GLM dims, both the reference and the AITER prefill are up to about 0.012 off an fp32 result. Their difference goes over 0.01 + 0.01*|x| on about 6% of random draws, so 1e-2 is tighter than the reference's own error. Re-seeding per case would only pin one draw that passes, so this widens the bf16 atol to cover two bf16 kernels. A real chunk or merge bug still shows errors of 0.1 or more.

<details>
<summary>Tests (MI355X, ROCm 7.2.3, AITER v0.1.26)</summary>

All commands run from `tests/` with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.

- Before the fix:
  - A small_prefill `test_backend_correctness[deepseek-...-small_prefill]` run right before the GLM chunked case: 3/3 failed with the CI signature (`TRITON_MLA, ROCM_AITER_MLA ... Max diff: 0.015625`).
  - The GLM chunked case over fresh random draws: 6/100 failed.
  - The exact CI Shard-2 order (303 tests, rebuilt from `RUNTIME_SHARD_PLAN`) passes on this node, but only by about 0.0004; CI's ROCm 10.0 wheel is likely enough to tip it over.
- After the fix:
  - Pair: 10/10 pass.
  - Failing test alone: pass.
  - CI Shard-2 order: 10/10 pass (302 passed, 1 skipped).
  - GLM and deepseek chunked cases over 200 random draws each: 400/400 pass.
- `pytest -v v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: 8/10 clean (760 passed, 304 skipped). Neither failure touches the changed tolerance:
  - `test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[...large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]` (abs diff 11.0 on 0.1% of elements) is a separate flake; it also fails about 1/20 when run alone, without this change.
  - `test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa[fp8]` hit `EADDRINUSE` because I ran five loops in parallel on one host.

Duplicate check: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` for `test_mla_backends`, `chunked_context`, `mla tolerance` and `manual_seed attention test`. The closest is #55611, which adds an rtol override for ROCm `v_head_dim=256`. That does not cover this failure: it happens on small outputs, where atol is the limit.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Compile] Fix KV-cache corruption under whole-graph compile (revert #42129)
author: ericschreiber
body:
## Overview

Implements solution 2 as outlined in issue #62865.
In more detail: fixes #62865 by reverting #42129 and, under torch < 2.13, keeps its intended hang protection by not formatting the slow log message for vLLM ops.
Currently using compile mode 1/2, or mode 3 with `splitting_ops: []` on Transformers-backend models corrupts the KV cache because Inductor passes tensors in a different layout than the kernels assume. As discussed with maintainers and @okorzh-amd (author of #42129) in Slack, this is the revert-based alternative to #62924.

## Claims

- Fixes degenerate output for Transformers-backend models (e.g. Qwen3, Kolibri-1, likely others) under compile mode 1/2, or mode 3 with `splitting_ops: []`.
- It does so by restoring PyTorch's default handling for all `vllm::` and `vllm_aiter::` custom ops.
- Keeps the compile-hang protection from #42129 through: (1) from torch 2.13 the slow log message is only built with INFO logging; (2) below 2.13 (currently only the gfx1250 preview image) the message is never built for `vllm::` and `vllm_aiter::` ops, the same ops #42129 covered.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, torch 2.13.0+cu130, precompiled kernels. All runs with vLLM and Inductor compile caches disabled.

### Correctness
**1. Regression test** 
Added a new test `test_whole_graph_compile` which uses Qwen3-0.6B on the Transformers backend on compile mode 2 vs eager with `check_logprobs_close`:

```bash
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_whole_graph_compile -v
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | failed: `Matched tokens: []`, ref `'LLM is a large language model, ...'`, test `'>>1\n\n\n\n...'` |
| this PR | passed 2 runs|

**2. GSM8K** 
With this PR, mode 2 matches eager and the native implementation on GSM8K (Qwen3-0.6B, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`); while on main there is a clear regression.

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|
| Transformers backend, eager | 0.391 | 0.3% |
| Transformers backend, mode 2, `main` | 0.011 | 10.8% |
| Transformers backend, mode 2, this PR | 0.401 | 0.2% |
| native vLLM implementation, default mode 3 | 0.400 | 0.2% |

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl transformers --max-model-len 4096 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 2, "backend": "inductor", "cudagraph_mode": 2}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

**3. Bounded log message for vLLM ops under torch < 2.13**
Introduced a test `tests/compile/test_inductor_operator_str_patch.py` which checks that a `vllm::` op's message is only its name. Running on torch 2.12 (CPU, a small compiled graph with a `vllm::` op and a custom op from another namespace), unpatched torch builds the full message for both ops; with the patch it is never built for the `vllm::` op. 
I could not test on gfx1250 itself.

### Compile time
On CUDA, cold-cache compile time is unchanged within noise (`main` vs this PR): Kolibri-1 mode 3 28.3 vs 28.1 s, Kolibri-1 TP=2 61.1 vs 62.1 s, Qwen3-4B mode 3 19.4 vs 19.5 s.

On ROCm, @djramic reported on Slack that without the #42129 allow-list the Kimi-K2 arch (dummy weights, torch 2.13) compiles about as fast as before. I had no ROCm access to verify this myself.

## Details

**Root cause:** #42129 added every `vllm::*` and `vllm_aiter::*` op to Inductor's `FALLBACK_ALLOW_LIST`. Inductor creates fallbacks for allow-listed ops without PyTorch's default layout constraint for custom ops. Without it, Inductor passes `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` a head-major key, strides `(128, 128*S, 1)` instead of eager's `(1024, 128, 1)`. `reshape_and_cache_flash` only reads `key.stride(0)` and assumes packed heads, so every cached key is scrambled and the output is garbage. Default mode 3 is unaffected because it splits the graph at the attention and KV-cache ops.

**Why revert:** The allow-list only existed to skip an implicit-fallback INFO message that torch <= 2.12 builds eagerly, which hung compilation on deep MoE/TP graphs. pytorch/pytorch#185951 makes it lazy from torch 2.13, and CUDA, CPU, XPU and the default ROCm images are on >= 2.13. Reverting restores PyTorch's behavior for all vLLM ops. #62924's own control row (allow-list disabled) already gives token-identical output to its patched run. The allow-list cannot stay for torch < 2.13 either, because the layout bug is in that code path on every torch version; those versions only need the hang protection, which skipping the message for vLLM ops provides.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- The torch < 2.13 patch can be removed once every platform pins torch >= 2.13. Until then, Inductor messages for vLLM ops (including lowering errors) show only the op name on those versions, as with #42129.
- On torch >= 2.13 with Inductor's graph logger at INFO, the full message is still built and can be slow on very deep graphs (`IRNode.__str__` has no depth limit, as #43111 found). This is opt-in debug logging.
- Overlaps with #57310, whose allow-list change should become unnecessary.
- A follow-up PR could make the KV-cache writers (reshape_and_cache, reshape_and_cache_flash and their Triton versions) reject keys whose heads are not packed, so a future layout change raises an error instead of silently corrupting the cache.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend][ZMQ] Run ZMQ transport I/O on the dedicated runtime
author: reidliu41
body:
## Overview

Create and connect Rust frontend ZMQ sockets on the dedicated runtime so
socket readiness and background transport tasks use the same Tokio I/O
driver. Caller-runtime load or shutdown can no longer delay or terminate
engine communication.



## Claims

- Registers HandshakeOwner and Bootstrapped transport I/O with the dedicated
  ZMQ runtime instead of the runtime that calls `EngineCoreClient::connect`.
- Keeps engine communication functional after the connecting runtime is shut
  down.
- Preserves the existing transport protocol, configuration, and public API.
- Retains cancellation safety while connection setup runs on the dedicated
  runtime.



## Validation

```
cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client \
  client_transport_outlives_connecting_runtime
```


A Linux epoll probe with a mock engine confirmed the runtime ownership change:

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| ZMQ TCP descriptors on the connecting runtime | 4 | 0 |
| ZMQ TCP descriptors on the dedicated runtime | 0 | 4 |
| Output delay while the connecting runtime was blocked | ~4.70 s | 0.43–0.75 ms |




## Details

Tokio associates TCP resources with the I/O driver of the runtime active when
those resources are created. Transport setup previously ran on the caller
runtime, while `build_zmq_runtime()` was called only after the sockets had
already been bound or connected. Background transport tasks ran on the
dedicated runtime, but socket readiness was still driven by the caller
runtime.

The dedicated runtime is now created before transport setup. The complete
connection path runs on that runtime, and the same runtime is passed into
`from_connected` for background task execution and lifetime ownership.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Fail never-sent fetches locally
author: jiuyueQ
body:
## Overview

Queued P2P Fetch messages can outlive a cancelled or timed-out load and be flushed after a delayed handshake. Retire never-sent loads locally and release the producer's parked storage without closing newer work using the same request ID.

Extracts **A** from #61667 as requested in review. Refs #61532. B (#64299) and C (#64300) have merged; this PR addresses the separate unsent-fetch lifecycle.

## Claims

- Retired, cancelled or expired Fetch messages never reach transport handoff.
- Never-sent loads fail locally without abort/deferred-release work. Producer terminal release cannot close a newer live round.
- Post-disconnect AbortAck semantics and finished-request failure bookkeeping are preserved.

## Validation

Tested on main `9cd2e98b595e` with cu130 artifacts from `b2a9480dc7aa` (identical native sources), Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| P2P and tiering component suites after test trimming | 467 passed |
| Repository hooks, including mypy, docs lint and CI tethering | Passed |
| Previously recorded real-weight LLM regression, commit `e388466c` | Passed |
| Previously recorded real-weight baseline control | Failed: peer received the retired fetch |

Reproduce the retained suite from a configured checkout:

```bash
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 UCX_TLS=tcp,self .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py
```

The retained manager regression verifies that a never-sent fetch fails locally and releases parked producer blocks. Session regressions cover cancellation/expiry, both handshake orderings, finished-request propagation, subsequent ID reuse, expiry logging and dead-connection/send-failure handling.

Earlier real-entry validation used real HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M weights at `93efa2f097d58c2a74874c7e644dbc9b0cee75a2`, RTX 4060 Ti/CUDA 13.0, FP16/eager/greedy/batch-invariant inference and NIXL UCX TCP localhost. A delayed-handshake request timed out and recomputed; the peer then received a fresh fetch and never the retired one. The equivalent control observed `['retired', 'live']` and failed. That model test and its dedicated fixture were removed from CI per [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64298#issuecomment-6630803920), because the smaller manager/session suite covers the same flow. Their source remains in `e388466c`; the production code is unchanged by this test-only trimming. No task-accuracy or performance claim is made.

## Details

Track a queued Fetch by object identity until transport handoff. Timeout or cancellation retires it locally. Empty terminal Fetch messages release producer supply, subject to the existing-request guard so they cannot close newer work. The manager handles terminal-only fetches without replaying stale stores. Finished loads keep #64300's `request_finished` marker, and the liveness check applies only to data Fetch messages so #64251's abort acknowledgements remain sendable after disconnect.

Duplicate-work check: this is the requested split from the original PR. Merged #64256 handles timed-out sent loads and deferred slot release; merged B handles buffered terminals, and merged C handles finished-request failures. This PR covers the separate never-sent path.

Rendered behavior documentation is in `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`. The existing `v1-kv-offload` CI step selects the retained tests and covers the changed sources.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted implementation, tests and PR preparation.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Settle buffered terminal messages after disconnect
author: jiuyueQ
body:
## Overview

A poll can receive both a disconnect and the terminal confirmation for a completed transfer. Dropping every message once the connection is dead loses that confirmation and reports the completed load as a failure.

Extracts **B** from #61667 as [requested in review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#pullrequestreview-5651552184). Refs #61532.

## Claims

- Validated TransferDone and AbortAck messages already buffered during disconnect settle their matching load.
- Work-starting traffic is still dropped after disconnect, and malformed terminals cannot settle a load.

## Validation

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Avoid leaking failed IDs for finished requests
author: jiuyueQ
body:
## Overview

Finishing a request with a load in flight can permanently put its KV request ID back into `_failed_req_ids` after `on_request_finished()` has removed it. Repeated mid-load cancellations accumulate stale IDs for the lifetime of the process. Reusing an ID on a retry is a secondary symptom: the stale entry suppresses that request's remote lookup.

Extracts **C** from #61667 as [requested in review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#pullrequestreview-5651552184). Refs #61532.

## Claims

- Finished requests do not permanently repopulate the failed-ID set through immediate cancellation failures, already-buffered outcomes or session close.
- Late failures still complete transfer-job cleanup without restoring finished IDs to the failure set.
- Close cleanup and request-ID reuse preserve this distinction; unfinished failures continue to trigger recomputation.

## Validation

Rebased and tested on main `34091a07c7d7`, including merged #64256 and #64250. Used cu130 wheel artifacts from `fa3b9d137721` (identical C++/CUDA sources to this base), Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, an RTX 4060 Ti, and NIXL 1.4.1 over UCX TCP on localhost.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| P2P and tiering component suites | 436 passed |
| New real-weight LLM regression on the base, with only the new tests overlaid | 1 failed for the assertion below |
| Same LLM regression with this fix | 1 passed |
| Repository pre-commit hooks, including mypy and CI tethering | Passed |

A manager regression finishes a request while its load is in flight, drains `get_finished_jobs()`, and asserts that the failed-ID set stays empty. It fails on the base with `{'req-finish'} != set()` and passes with the fix.

The dedicated real LLM e2e test enqueues a remote load, cancels its internal engine request ID after the peer observes the fetch, and drains the failed load using real engine steps. AbortAck separately confirms release of its blocks. A different prompt then reuses the same KV request ID; the peer must observe its new fetch rather than an unconditional local miss.

Reproduction commands from a configured checkout/venv:

```bash
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 UCX_TLS=tcp,self .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload \

```

Base failure excerpt:
```text
E AssertionError: late failure poisoned the reused KV request id
E assert not True
E + where True = empty()
```
With the fix: `1 passed`.

Model: real `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M` weights at `93efa2f097d58c2a74874c7e644dbc9b0cee75a2`, FP16, eager, greedy sampling, and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. ## Details

Carry a default-false request_finished flag on the load state and LoadResult. Finish marks both in-flight loads and already-buffered results. Polling and close omit finished IDs from failure bookkeeping while still returning failed jobs for cleanup. This is independent of deferred slot release.
