title: [Bugfix][CPU] Name the cause when a DP rank's assigned NUMA nodes don't exist
author: amd-lalithnc
body:
## Overview

On a CPU host with fewer NUMA nodes than the ranks on it, DP=2 × TP=2 with explicit binds fails at start-up with `IndexError: list index out of range` in `CPUWorker.__init__`, and with `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA=1` it stops at a bare `AssertionError`. As discussed in review, more ranks than NUMA nodes is not a supported layout, so this PR keeps both stops and makes each error name its cause and the debugging workaround. No fallback. Fixes #64497.

## Claims

- With explicit binds and no `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA`, DP rank 1's workers raise `ValueError: None of the NUMA nodes [2, 3] assigned to this CPU worker is available; this process can use NUMA nodes [0, 1]. ...` instead of `IndexError`.
- With explicit binds and `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA=1`, start-up stops with `AssertionError: VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA requires VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=auto, got '...'` instead of a bare `AssertionError`.
- Supported setups are unchanged: `auto` + `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA=1` serves DP=2 × TP=2 on a 2-NUMA host.

## Validation

**Unit tests**, on this branch:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_cpu_resource_utils.py -v
======================== 22 passed, 2 warnings in 6.59s ========================
```

**The new tests on main** (main's `vllm/`, this branch's tests):

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_cpu_resource_utils.py \
  -k "worker_memory_nodes or sim_multi_numa_requires_auto" -v
FAILED ...::test_worker_memory_nodes_keep_available_assigned_nodes - AttributeError: module 'vllm.utils.cpu_resource_utils' has no attribute 'get_worker_memory_nodes'
FAILED ...::test_worker_memory_nodes_raise_when_assigned_nodes_are_missing - AttributeError: (same)
FAILED ...::test_worker_memory_nodes_sim_multi_numa_shares_nodes - AttributeError: (same)
FAILED ...::test_omp_manager_sim_multi_numa_requires_auto_binding - AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match.
```

**End to end on a real 2-NUMA host**, with this PR's change applied on main `9a56d4fec6`: 2× AMD EPYC 9454, node0 = CPUs 0-47,96-143, node1 = 48-95,144-191, stock `CpuPlatform`, `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=2`, `taskset -c 0-11,48-59 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct --data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 1024 --enforce-eager --seed 0`.

| Setup | main `9a56d4fec6` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| explicit binds `0-5\|6-11\|48-53\|54-59` | DP rank 1's workers: `Node 1 is not in available memory nodes []`, then `IndexError: list index out of range` | DP rank 1's workers: `ValueError: None of the NUMA nodes [2, 3] assigned to this CPU worker is available; this process can use NUMA nodes [0, 1]. Each CPU worker on a host needs its own NUMA node, ...` |
| explicit binds + `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA=1` | bare `AssertionError` | `AssertionError: VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA requires VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=auto, got '0-5\|6-11\|48-53\|54-59'.` |
| `VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=auto` + `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA=1` | serves (checked on `be09292f09`) | serves; greedy `" Paris. The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris. …"` and `" 17 * 23 = 391 …"`; DP rank 0's workers on node 0, DP rank 1's on node 1 |

**pre-commit** on the changed files: all 11 applicable hooks pass, including `ruff`, `mypy`, `typos` and `check-test-tethering`.

## Details

- **Root cause (unchanged from the first version).** Since #62867, each DP rank gets a block of `world_size` NUMA node ids (`get_physical_gpu_ids_for_local_dp_rank()`), so DP rank 1 of DP=2 × TP=2 gets `[2, 3]`. On a 2-node host those nodes don't exist, the filtered list is empty, and `allowed_memory_nodes[0]` raises.
- **Change.** `get_worker_memory_nodes()` in `cpu_resource_utils.py` wraps `get_visible_memory_node()` for the worker and raises the `ValueError` when the list is empty; `CPUWorker` calls it. The `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA` assertion in `OMPProcessManager` gets a message. `get_visible_memory_node()` itself is unchanged.
- **CI coverage.** `tests/utils_/test_cpu_resource_utils.py` runs in "Async Engine, Inputs, Utils, Worker". CPU CI sets `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA=1`, so it cannot reach the worker error end to end; the end-to-end results above were checked manually on a real 2-NUMA host.

**AI assistance was used** for the investigation, the change and tests, and the validation runs. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Prefill locally while a peer handshake is pending
author: liranschour
body:
## Overview

A symmetric-P2P consumer now prefills locally instead of waiting while a session's handshake is pending, so a request that names a stopped or deleted source returns at once rather than after up to `VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` (30 s). Closes the gap reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63602#issuecomment-6491634566.

## Claims

- `remote_kv_source` requests to a stopped (SIGSTOP), force-deleted or gracefully deleted source: p50 15.7–17.0 s / max 30.1 s → p50 22 ms / max 4.7 s. The worst case is now the 8 s lookup timeout, for a lookup already in flight when the source stops.
- No regression in the reproducer's other checks: A never freezes, A→C pulls stay at 100%, and pulls from B or its replacement B2 recover fully.
- The PD path (`remote_prefiller`) is unchanged and keeps its eager HIT.

## Validation

**E2E**, using the [reproducer from #63602](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63602#issuecomment-6491634566): three single-GPU Qwen3-0.6B engines on one 8×H200 node (mlx5 IB, NIXL), with a probe pulling a fresh ~2K-token prefix from B and C every 200 ms. The image is `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d` (it already contains #63207, #63779 and #64250) plus #64256 and #64251. **fix** adds this PR. The changed `vllm/` files were copied over the nightly at pod start. One run per case.

| case | build | requests to faulted B, p50 / max | > 15 s | B/B2 pulled after recovery | A→C pulled | PASS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c1 SIGSTOP 60 s | base | 15.7 s / 30.1 s | 157/301 | 240/240 | 614/614 | ✓ |
| | **fix** | **0.022 s / 4.7 s** | **0/304** | 239/239 | 615/615 | ✓ |
| c2 force-delete, B2 | base | 17.0 s / 30.1 s | 281/499 | 400/400 | 838/838 | ✓ |
| | **fix** | **0.022 s / 0.038 s** | **0/502** | 400/400 | 842/842 | ✓ |
| c3 graceful delete, B2 | base | 17.0 s / 30.1 s | — | 400/400 | 841/841 | ✓ |
| | **fix** | **0.023 s / 0.036 s** | 0 | 400/400 | 837/837 | ✓ |
| c0 no fault | fix | — | — | 700/700 | 625/625 | ✓ |
| c7 SIGKILL, same IP | fix | 0.023 s / 0.078 s | 0 | 400/400 | 512/512 | ✓ |
| c8 rolling replace | fix | 0.053 s / 0.084 s | 0 | 400/400 | 589/589 | ✓ |

The c1 fix run's overall max (8.1 s) comes from the two probes sent ~1 s before the SIGSTOP. Their LookupMsg was already out, so they ended on the 8 s lookup timeout.

**Unit:**
- `test_lookup_before_handshake_ack_falls_back_to_local_prefill` fails without the fix (`RETRY != MISS`) and passes with it.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/`: 618 passed, 12 skipped.

## Details

**Root cause.** For a `remote_kv_source` request, `on_new_request` opens a session to the source, and `lookup()` registers a probe and returns RETRY until the LookupResp arrives. `ClientRole.flush_pending_lookups` holds probes until the peer acks ConnectMsg, and the 8 s lookup deadline only starts when the LookupMsg goes out. While the handshake is pending, the only bound on the request is the 30 s handshake deadline.

When the source stops or goes away:
1. The first lookup timeout ends the session.
2. No reconnect backoff applies, since backoff is scheduled only after a data-plane fault.
3. The next request opens a new session at once and waits on its handshake.

Each request therefore waits for whatever remains of the current 30 s handshake, which gives the ~17 s p50 and 30 s max.

**Fix.** `lookup()` treats a session that is not `ready` like a missing session and returns MISS. It returns before `register_lookup`, so the peer never gets lookup state for the request, and `finish` owes it no terminal FetchMsg. Inbound and outbound sessions both send ConnectMsg and become `ready` on the ack, so reused inbound sessions behave the same way.

**Tradeoff.** A request that arrives before its session's handshake completes now recomputes instead of pulling. That includes the first request to a new or replacement peer. Sessions persist across requests (idle ones are reaped only near `VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS`), so this costs one window per peer of about the handshake time, 14–40 ms of registration on these pods. The c8 rolling-replace run pulled 400/400 from B2. Recomputing a prefix is cheaper than waiting up to 30 s on a peer that may be gone.

**Not changed.**
- The reconnect backoff for timeout-ended sessions (the issue's other proposal) is not added. With this change, a dead peer costs at most one cheap connect attempt per handshake window, and no request waits on it.
- A lookup already in flight when its source stops still waits up to the 8 s lookup timeout (#63781).

title: [Bugfix][Model] Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: support the native transformers config

body:
## Overview

Lets `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3` checkpoints (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL) run without `--trust-remote-code` on transformers ≥ 5.18.

Related to #63470. Alternative to #64030 (see Details).

## Claims

- `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-*` serves without `--trust-remote-code` when transformers ≥ 5.18 is installed.
- `--trust-remote-code`, older transformers versions, and the existing Nano VL / Nano Omni checkpoints behave as before.
- CI now initializes the model from transformers' built-in `nemotron_h_omni` config.
- `supported_models.md` lists the architecture and the transformers ≥ 5.18 requirement for running without the flag.

No model eval: the change only selects which config field the projector size comes from, so weights and computation are unchanged.

## Details

**Root cause.** Transformers 5.18 added a built-in `nemotron_h_omni` config. The Super VL checkpoints declare `"model_type": "nemotron_h_omni"`, so `AutoConfig` loads that class without remote code. The built-in class renames `vit_hidden_size` to `vision_hidden_size`, but `NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2.__init__` read `config.vit_hidden_size`.

**Fix.** Read `vision_hidden_size`, the name the built-in transformers config uses, and fall back to `vit_hidden_size`, which the remote-code configs use:

| Config | Field |
|---|---|
| Transformers built-in `nemotron_h_omni` (≥ 5.18) | `vision_hidden_size` |
| Checkpoint remote code (`--trust-remote-code`) | `vit_hidden_size` |
| Nano VL / Nano Omni checkpoints | `vit_hidden_size` |

**Test.** The `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3` registry entry was an offline placeholder. It now points at `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16` without `trust_remote_code`, gated on transformers ≥ 5.18.0. The built-in `NemotronHConfig` derives `hybrid_override_pattern` from `layers_block_type` and doesn't allow setting it, so the 2-layer override sets `layers_block_type` instead. The "Basic Models (Extra Initialization)" CI step selects this test.

**Why not #64030.** #64030 copies the remote-code config and image processor into vLLM, about 520 lines. Transformers ≥ 5.18 already provides the config, and serving goes through `NanoNemotronVLProcessor` either way, so vLLM only needs this one field read. This matches #60623, which removed configs vLLM had copied once Transformers shipped them.

**Limitations.**
- **Older transformers:** on transformers < 5.18, `--trust-remote-code` is still required.
- **Audio:** the built-in config also renames `sound_config` → `audio_config`, which vLLM doesn't read. The Super VL checkpoints have no audio, but a future checkpoint that loads with the built-in config and includes audio would have audio switched off with no error. Left for a follow-up.
- **Recipe:** the Super VL recipe keeps `--trust-remote-code` until a release includes this fix. Its pinned image (v0.31.0) doesn't have it.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Keep raw text for string parameters with union/enum/$ref schemas (Muse, MiniCPM5, Poolside)
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The `muse`, `minicpm5` and `poolside_v1` tool parsers keep a parameter's raw text only when its schema is exactly `{"type": "string"}`, so `Optional[str]` values such as `"1.10"` or `"1984"` come back as `1.1` or `1984`. This makes them keep the raw text whenever the schema allows a string. The Rust frontend's Muse parser gets the same fix.

FIX #64517

## Claims

- String parameters keep their raw text when the schema allows a string through `anyOf`/`oneOf`, a `type` list, `enum`/`const`, a local `$ref`, `allOf`, or `additionalProperties`. Streaming and non-streaming both get the fix.
- Values that fit another type the schema allows still decode to it: `null` -> `None` for `Optional[str]`, `"25"` -> `25` under `anyOf [integer, string]`.
- Unchanged: plain `type: string`, non-string types, untyped parameters (`{}`), Python `muse_glimmer`, and `extract_types_from_schema` / `ParserEngine` coercion.

## Validation

| Check | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/tool_use/test_muse.py tests/tool_parsers/test_{schema_types,minicpm5xml_tool_parser,poolside_v1_tool_parser}.py` | `test_muse.py` and `test_schema_types.py` do not import (no `schema_types`); MiniCPM5 4 failed, 38 passed; Poolside 2 failed, 16 passed | 199 passed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers`, `pytest tests/parser` (without cohere), `pytest tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer.py` | 1227, 6783, 25 passed | 1264, 6783, 25 passed |
| `cargo test -p vllm-parser --locked` (Rust 1.95), `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p vllm-parser --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` | | 625 passed (30 Muse, 29 on main), clean |
| B200, nightly image, served MiniCPM5-2B, Laguna-XS.2 and Muse-Glimmer-30B (`muse`): 12 string forms, 3 streaming and 3 non-streaming requests each | 6/6 wrong per form | 0/6 per form |
| Muse-Glimmer-30B on the Rust frontend (`vllm-rs`, `muse`): the same 12 forms | 6/6 wrong per form | 0/6 per form |
| 8x B200, Muse-Spark-816B (NVFP4, TP8), Python and Rust frontends: the same 12 forms ¹ | 6/6 wrong per form on both | 0/6 per form on both |
| Same servers: plain `string`, `null` on `Optional[str]`, `"25"` under `anyOf [integer, string]` | correct | correct |
| `muse_glimmer`, and `qwen3_coder` (ParserEngine) on Qwen3.5-0.8B | | identical to main |

¹ Spark ran on an earlier revision of this branch with the same rules. The final code was rerun on MiniCPM5, Laguna, Glimmer (Python and Rust) and Qwen3.5, and returned the same arguments as that revision on every request.

On Glimmer and on Spark, the Rust and Python frontends return identical arguments for every request, on main and on this PR.

The 12 forms are `anyOf [string, null]` (1984, true, a JSON body), `oneOf`, `["string", "null"]`, an untyped `enum`, `const`, a local `$ref`, `allOf [$ref, {description}]`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf [integer, string]` with 1.10, and `["number", "string"]` with true.

`tests/tool_parsers/test_schema_types.py` table-tests every schema form once against `parameter_types` and `convert_value`. Each parser has a smoke test of `Optional[str]` through `extract_tool_calls` and `extract_tool_calls_streaming` with a real request (Muse: Chat and Responses).

Each parser builds its parameter types once, on first use, because the renderer builds a throwaway parser per request for `adjust_request`. Served streaming ITL on Muse-Glimmer with 40 tools x 20 parameters is within 0.3% of main (20.21 ms vs 20.19 ms, measured on the previous revision of this branch, which caches the same way).

Size against main (Rust inline tests counted as tests):

| | Code +/- | Tests +/- |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 203 / 116 | 132 / 7 |
| Rust | 63 / 24 | 57 / 4 |
| Total | 266 / 140 | 189 / 11 |

## Details

**Root cause.** Each parser compared the schema to `"type": "string"` (Muse `_string_parameters`, MiniCPM5 `_get_argument_type`, Poolside `_is_string_type`, Rust `MuseUnifiedParser::new`) and decoded everything else.

**Change.** `parameter_types` in the new `vllm/tool_parsers/schema_types.py` computes the JSON types each top-level parameter allows (`type`, `const`, `enum`, local `$ref`, `anyOf`/`oneOf` as union, `allOf` as intersection). `convert_value` keeps the raw text unless the parser's own decoder returns another allowed type. Each parser keeps its decoder. In Rust, Muse derives the types from the existing `SchemaRoot::options` walk, which already resolves `$ref` for coercion and the output grammars, and intersects multi-branch `allOf`, where a `number` branch also admits integers.

**Scope.** `extract_types_from_schema` and `ParserEngine` coercion are not touched; consolidating them is #63385. Structured-output schema analysis (RFC #58697) checks grammar-backend features, not value types.

**Limitations.**
- Only top-level parameters are checked; nested values are decoded as a whole.
- A union with an untyped branch (`anyOf [string, {}]`) is unconstrained, so it decodes, as on main.
- `anyOf [string, object]` decodes a JSON body to an object; the schema allows both.
- Poolside V1 streams `Optional[str]` arguments in one delta at `</arg_value>`, as on main.
- The Rust frontend uses one parser for Spark and Glimmer, so Rust Glimmer gets the new rules while Python Glimmer always decodes. This split predates this PR.

**Rust differs from Python** on a few schemas that admit a string:
- `allOf` nested inside `anyOf`;
- an untyped `anyOf` beside a `type` list;
- `$ref` chains deeper than 32, which decode as on main;
- the OpenAPI `nullable` null option.

The decoders also differ. serde_json rejects `NaN`/`Infinity` and reads integers beyond 64 bits as floats, so Rust keeps the raw text in cases where Python's `json.loads` decodes.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Parse closed GLM-4.7 tool arguments once while streaming
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

A GLM tool call that repeats closed argument pairs makes `Glm47MoeParser` re-parse every pair on each streaming conversion, so the API server's cost per token grows with the call until the event loop saturates and liveness fails. This parses each closed pair once. Follow-up to #61253, which covers a single long open value.

## Claims

- Streaming a call with N closed pairs matches the argument regex N times in total. On main every conversion matches all closed pairs again: 1,345,003 matches for N = 401 in the new test.
- Streamed deltas and non-streaming results are unchanged.
- No new config, flag or API. Scope is the `glm47` tool parser; `Ling3Parser` gets the `>` gate only (see Details).

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `24e80c2614` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cost test | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py::TestStreamedToolArguments::test_closed_pairs_are_parsed_once` | `AssertionError: assert 1345003 == 401` | passed |
| GLM parser tests | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py` | 22 passed, 1 failed (the new test) | 23 passed |
| Parser suite | `pytest tests/parser --ignore=tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py --ignore=tests/parser/test_harmony.py` | 6660 passed, 3 failed | 6661 passed, 2 failed |
| Looping stream replay (below) | GLM-5.3 tokenizer, 200 tok/s, liveness 30 s / 5 s / 3 | liveness kill at 275 s | no kill in 1200 s, loop 0-7% busy at 240K tokens |

Tests ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The 2 parser-suite failures left are in `tests/parser/mistral/test_reasoning.py` and fail the same on main: the image ships mistral-common 1.11.6 and main needs 1.13.0 (#64169). The two ignored files fail collection in that image for the same reason and for a harmony download. `ruff` 0.14.0 and the repo's `mypy` hook (1.20.2, Python 3.11) are clean on both files.

Also checked on `glm47_moe.py`:
- The resumed parse equals a fresh parse on 541,418 random argument texts grown piece by piece (3 seeds), with tag fragments, repeated keys, and a second call reusing the cache.
- Streamed output with the real GLM-5.3 tokenizer through `ParserManager.get_parser("glm47", "glm45")`: 11 streams (edits, long writes, open values, typed and array arguments, repeated keys, two calls, plain content) at chunk sizes 1, 3, 4, 7 and 64, plus non-streaming. Content, reasoning, names, arguments and argument-delta counts are identical to the unpatched parser (vLLM `d6394cf758`, same `glm47_moe.py` and argument path as main) in 66 of 66 cases.

Not measured: an end-to-end server run with a GLM checkpoint.

<details>
<summary>Looping stream replay</summary>

The replay feeds one GLM-5.3 output through the streaming parser on a virtual clock. The engine emits 200 tokens/s in 4-token steps (MTP at full acceptance). Each event-loop pass hands every token emitted since the previous pass to one `parse_delta` call. Measured parser time is doubled for a slower server CPU, and kubelet liveness (30 s period, 5 s timeout, 3 failures) is replayed on those passes. The output is `</think><tool_call>Edit`, a `file_path` pair, then `old_string` / `new_string` pairs repeated.

| Stream time | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| 27 s, 5.4K tokens | loop 24% busy | 0% |
| 114 s, 22.8K tokens | 99% | 1% |
| 210-270 s | liveness fails 3 of 3 (25-58 s waits), kill at 275 s | 1% |
| 1200 s, 240K tokens, 1.46M chars | | 7% |

Once the loop saturates, each pass merges more tokens and each merged event converts again, so passes keep getting longer. The last pass on main merged 6,608 tokens, ran 7,267 conversions and took 62.9 s.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta` converts the whole raw argument text whenever the open-value extender from #61253 is inactive: between arguments, and while the open key repeats an earlier key (the extender needs the open value to be the last JSON value). GLM set no `arg_structural_chars`, so every argument chunk event converted, and `_glm47_parse_args` re-ran `_ARG_RE.finditer` over every closed pair plus `_ARG_RE.sub` over the whole text. Merging deltas under load does not bound this, because conversions scale with the events in the merged text.

We hit this serving GLM-5.3 on vLLM 0.32.0, which includes #61253. Decode API servers climbed from 0.3 to 1 core in 3-4 minutes and failed liveness, five times in 24 hours. In three of them the logs show a single request left on the pod, generating at 99-100% MTP draft acceptance (the model repeating itself) while the stats line slipped from 10 s to 15-40 s apart. Stream content was not captured in production; the replay reproduces the same failure through the parser.

**Change.**
- `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, as DeepSeek V3.2 and V4 use. A delta without `>` cannot close a key or value, so it cannot produce a streamable change: an open last value goes through the extender, and an open repeated key sits mid-JSON where the prefix check withholds it. The next conversion or the final flush converts the full text. The gate alone only delays the kill in the replay (305 s against 215 s, measured on `d6394cf758`), because each conversion still re-scans.
- `_glm47_parse_args` takes an optional `_ClosedArgs` cache, and `Glm47MoeParser` binds one per instance into its converter and extender, the same way DeepSeek V4 and MiniMax M3 replace `_arg_converter` after `super().__init__`. A text that extends the cached text resumes after its last closed pair. Any other text parses from the start, and the cache moves forward whenever a scan closes a new pair. Appending text cannot change a pair that already closed, since each match ends at the first `</arg_value>` after its key, so resuming is exact.

**Cost.** What stays linear in the text per conversion is C-level work: `startswith` against the cached text, the slice when a pair closes, and the join of text outside the pairs for the open-key search. That is the 7% at 1.46M chars above.

**Compatibility and limits.**
- A parser built with a custom `arg_converter` keeps the uncached path (identity check in `__init__`), so tests that wrap the converter still see every call.
- `Ling3Parser` calls `ParserEngine.__init__` directly, so it gets the gate from the shared config and no cache.
- A looping call still generates until `max_tokens`; this keeps the server responsive while it does.
- Unchanged here and the same on main: when a repeated key closes with a different value than before, the final JSON no longer extends what was streamed and the flush withholds it, so the client gets truncated arguments. I can file that separately.

**Not a duplicate.** #61253 (merged) covers one long open value. #58418 (open) edits `_glm47_parse_args` for an unclosed final value; the overlap is textual only. #51141 and #64196 address Inkling and DeepSeek DSML. No open PR covers re-parsing closed GLM pairs.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the root-cause analysis, the fix, the tests and this description.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix dots_ocr vision tower QKV split for TP > 1
author: majq92
body:
## Overview `DotsVisionAttention` used a QKV-split helper meant for a differently sharded layer, scrambling q/k/v at TP > 1 so `dots.ocr` repeated one sentence for every image region. Split the local shard instead. Fixes #64541. ## Claims - `DotsVisionAttention` now splits QKV correctly under TP: TP=2 with the default weight-sharded encoder matches the TP=1 reference again. Confirmed on Ascend 910B3 (12/12 layout blocks) and on CUDA (2× A800, byte-identical output). - No behaviour change at TP=1: the previous helper degenerated to the same local `chunk(3)`, which is why single-card serving was already correct. - Adds a `dots_ocr` entry to the VLM generation tests with `tensor_parallel_size=2`, marked `pytest.mark.skip` because the HF reference side cannot run under the pinned transformers version (see below). - Also covers `dots.mocr`: it ships a byte-identical `config.json` (`architectures: ["DotsOCRForCausalLM"]`, `model_type: dots_ocr`, same vision tower dims) and is served by this same file, so it carries the same TP>1 defect. ## Validation ### End-to-end reproducer (before/after, 2× Ascend 910B3, vLLM 0.30.0) Same image, prompt and sampling parameters in all runs: | # | code | TP | mm encoder | result | |---|------|----|-----------|--------| | 0 | before | 2 | weights (default) | broken: 4× identical "I am sorry ... blurry image of a person" | | 1 | before | 2 | `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` | correct: 12 layout blocks | | 2 | after | 2 | weights (default) | correct: 12 layout blocks | | 3 | before | 1 | weights | correct: 12 layout blocks (reference) | Run 1 bypasses the vision *weight* TP path (`disable_tp=True`, the encoder sees `tp_size == 1`), which isolates the failure to the TP-sharded ViT rather than to the LM or the processor. After the fix, run 2 matches run 3: - 12/12 layout blocks with identical categories and bounding boxes; - extracted text identical character-for-character except for one empty `` cell in a different column inside a table row (same length, sampling at `temperature=0.1`); - 52 s for the full page versus 8 s for the degenerate pre-fix output. A CPU-only script in the issue shows the same layout mismatch without any accelerator (it only simulates the all-gather + `chunk(3)` on a token-index tensor). ### Fix confirmed on CUDA (2× A800 80GB PCIe) Environment: vLLM 0.32.0, torch 2.13.0, transformers 5.19.0, driver 580.105.08, 2× A800 80GB PCIe (sm_80, PCIe interconnect), model `rednote-hilab/dots.ocr` (6.08 GB, 2 shards), OpenAI-compatible server with `--max-model-len 4096 --trust-remote-code`, sampling `temperature=0.1`, `seed=0`. The image was a synthetic A4 layout page (title, two-column body, 3×3 table), not the document used in the NPU run, so the post-fix result is compared against the TP=1 reference for the same image instead of block counts. | # | code | TP | mm encoder | output len | repeated-paragraph rate | matches TP=1 ref | latency | |---|------|----|-----------|-----------|------------------------|------------------|---------| | 0 | before | 2 | weights | 6095 | 93% | no | 6.6 s | | 1 | after | 2 | weights | 1117 | 0% | yes, byte-identical | 1.7 s | | 2 | before | 2 | `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` | 1117 | 0% | yes | 1.6 s | | 3 | before | 1 | weights | 1117 | 0% | reference | 3.6 s | | 4 | after | 1 | weights | 1117 | 0% | yes | 2.0 s | - Pre-fix TP=2 with the default weight-sharded encoder reproduces the reported failure: the same paragraph is emitted 6+ times regardless of image content. - Post-fix TP=2 output is byte-for-byte identical to the TP=1 reference. - The `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` control was unaffected before the fix, which isolates the defect to the TP-sharded vision weights rather than the LM or the processor. - TP=1 output is unchanged by the patch. The degenerate text differs from the NPU run ("license plate" paragraph vs. "I am sorry ... blurry image of a person"). Both are attractor states reached when the vision embeddings are noise, and the failure mode — identical text for every image region — is the same. Note: this run applied the two-state patch (PR diff on/off) to the installed 0.32.0 wheel instead of building this branch from source, because the container had no `nvcc`. `dots_ocr.py` in the 0.30/0.31/0.32 releases still contains the same pre-fix `split_qkv` call, so the two states are semantically the PR's before/after. ### Regression test A `dots_ocr` entry is added to `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py` with `tensor_parallel_size=2`, behind: ```python pytest.mark.skip(reason="Custom model code is not compatible with Transformers v5") ``` That is the same class of breakage as the existing skips in this file (`ultravox`, `kimi_vl`, …). dots.ocr's remote code declares `transformers_version: 4.51.0`, while vLLM now requires `transformers >= 5.16.1, < 5.23.0`, and it breaks in two layers on the reference side: `generate()` rejects `mm_token_type_ids` as an unused kwarg, and once that is stripped, `prepare_inputs_for_generation` does not handle a `None` `cache_position`. The entry is kept rather than dropped so the intended TP>1 coverage is recorded and can be enabled once the remote code supports transformers v5. Separately, the vision tower also trips the CI GPU-sync checker at three host copies. That is an independent property of the model — it runs under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, which the CI image sets globally — not something this diff introduces, and it is tracked in #66243 together with the plan for a dedicated, HF-free regression test. ## Details ### Root cause `DotsVisionAttention` builds its QKV with `QKVParallelLinear`, so each TP rank already owns the local `[q | k | v]` shard. It nevertheless called `Qwen2VisionAttention.split_qkv()`, a helper written for Qwen2-VL's `ColumnParallelLinear`, where each rank holds a *slice of the whole packed* `[q | k | v]` tensor. At TP > 1 that helper all-gathers and re-splits: ``` QKVParallelLinear (TP=2): [q0 k0 v0] | [q1 k1 v1] all_gather(dim=-1): [q0 k0 v0 | q1 k1 v1] chunk(3): (q0+k0), (v0+q1), (k1+v1) rank0 -> q=q0 (ok), k=v0 (wrong), v=k1 (wrong) rank1 -> q=k0 (wrong), k=q1 (wrong), v=v1 (ok) ``` The vision embeddings become noise, so the LM collapses to a fixed sentence for every region. At TP=1 the helper degenerates to a plain `chunk(3)` on the full tensor, which is why single-card serving was correct. ### Fix `DotsVisionAttention.forward` splits the local tensor directly (`x.chunk(3, dim=-1)` + reshape), exactly as `glm_ocr.py` already does for the same attention layout. ### Scope and risk - Diff is 32 added / 2 deleted lines across two files; no core component is touched. - TP=1 output is unchanged by construction. - `dots.mocr` (`dots-studio/dots.mocr`) ships a byte-identical `config.json` and the same `architectures` entry, so vLLM dispatches it to this same model class and it gets the same fix. The Ascend reproducer used `dots.mocr`; the A800 run used `dots.ocr` itself. - Only the default (weight-sharded) encoder path was broken; users on `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` were unaffected. - Verified on two independent backends (Ascend 910B3 and CUDA A800); the CUDA run also confirms TP=1 output is unchanged. ### Related work No duplicate: #63074 (`dots.ocr: support encoder CUDA graph`) is open and edits other hunks of `dots_ocr.py` (CUDA-graph wiring), not the QKV split, so the two PRs are trivially rebasable on each other. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** The change is a 2-line semantic fix in one model file and reuses the established `glm_ocr.py` pattern; no new abstraction, dependency or branch is introduced. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** End-to-end before/after is included for both Ascend 910B3 and 2× A800 CUDA, and TP=1 regression is covered. The automated test is added but skipped: dots.ocr's remote code targets transformers 4.51 and cannot run under the pinned transformers 5.x, which is why the rest of this file uses the same skip reason. Follow-up tracked in #66243. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Comments kept short; the root-cause writeup lives in this description. `pre-commit` passes locally (ruff 0.14.0, mypy 1.20.2, typos, and all local hooks). - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Summary, issue link, root cause, tradeoffs, limitations and validation are documented; AI assistance is disclosed below.
--- **AI assistance disclosure:** this change was developed with AI assistance (pair-debugging the TP layout, the CPU simulation, and the initial patch). All changed lines have been reviewed by the submitter. The Ascend before/after runs and the CUDA A800 runs were both executed by the submitter on real hardware.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Reject --dataset-path with synthetic vllm-bench datasets
author: MayaJShetty
body:
## Overview

Fixes #64538. Rust `vllm-bench` silently ignored `--dataset-path` for the synthetic datasets, so `vllm-bench --dataset-path my_workload.jsonl` without `--dataset-name` benchmarked random prompts instead of the given file. This rejects the combination with the same error as Python `vllm bench serve`.

## Claims

- `--dataset-path` with `random`, `random-mm`, `random-rerank` or `prefix_repetition` (including the default `--dataset-name random`) now fails at startup with Python's error: `Cannot use '<name>' dataset with --dataset-path. Please specify the appropriate --dataset-name (e.g., 'sharegpt', 'custom', 'hf') for your dataset file: <path>`.
- Datasets that read `--dataset-path` (`sharegpt`, `speed-bench`, `hf`, `custom`, `timed_trace`) are unchanged.
- `--dataset-path` help text and the bench README document the restriction.

## Validation

Regression tests in `config.rs`: `test_synthetic_dataset_rejects_dataset_path` and `test_default_dataset_rejects_dataset_path` fail without the fix and pass with it; `test_file_dataset_accepts_dataset_path` passes in both.

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-bench                                   # all pass
cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings    # clean
cargo fmt -p vllm-bench --check                            # clean
```

End-to-end, release build against a mock OpenAI-compatible server that logs received prompts. `my_workload.jsonl` holds 5 lines of `{"prompt": "MY_REAL_WORKLOAD_PROMPT", "output_tokens": 4}`; common args `--model mock-model --tokenizer gpt2 --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --num-prompts 5`.

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `--dataset-path my_workload.jsonl` | exit 0, "5 random prompts"; `MY_REAL_WORKLOAD_PROMPT` received 0 times | exit 1: `Cannot use 'random' dataset with --dataset-path ...` |
| `--dataset-path /no/such/file.jsonl` | exit 0 | exit 1, same error |
| `--dataset-name random-rerank --backend vllm-rerank --dataset-path my_workload.jsonl` | — | exit 1: `Cannot use 'random-rerank' dataset ...` |
| `--dataset-name custom --dataset-path my_workload.jsonl` | — | exit 0; `MY_REAL_WORKLOAD_PROMPT` received 5/5 times |
| `--dataset-name random` (no path) | — | exit 0 |
| `vllm bench serve` (Python), first row's command | exit 1, same error | unchanged |

The same error is returned with `--multi-turn`, `--sweep-max-concurrency` and `--num-runs`. `mm-processor` has no `--dataset-path` flag and already rejects it as an unexpected argument.

## Details

- **Root cause:** Python checks this combination in `vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`; the Rust port never did, and none of the four synthetic generators read `dataset_path`. Since `--dataset-name` defaults to `random`, a forgotten `--dataset-name` produced plausible-looking results for the wrong workload.
- **Placement:** the check is in `BenchConfig::from_args`, next to the other per-dataset validation. Every serve mode (single run, multi-turn, sweeps, `--num-runs`) builds its config there, so one check covers all of them.
- **Parity:** same dataset list and message as Python. The dataset name in the message comes from the CLI value (`ValueEnum::to_possible_value`), so it matches what the user typed.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open or closed PR or issue covers this; I searched for `64538`, "dataset-path", "vllm-bench dataset-path", and "Cannot use dataset with --dataset-path" before opening #64538 and this PR.

title: [CI][KV Offload][P2P] Wait for the handshake in the idle peer-hit tests
author: orozery
body:
## Overview

`TestIdleWhileServingPeers` (both tests) fails on main:

```
FAILED v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestIdleWhileServingPeers::test_pinned_peer_hit_does_not_block_idleness - assert <LookupResult.MISS: 1> is <LookupResult.RETRY: 4>
FAILED v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestIdleWhileServingPeers::test_pinned_peer_hit_without_poll_thread_is_pending - assert <LookupResult.MISS: 1> is <LookupResult.RETRY: 4>
```

It is a merge race between two PRs that each passed CI on their own:

- #64501 made a probe `lookup()` return `MISS` until the peer acks the handshake (`p2p/manager.py:440`), so the request prefills locally instead of waiting.
- #63618 added these tests on a base without #64501. Its `_peer_hit` helper probes right after `on_new_request` and asserts `RETRY`.

## Fix

Test-only. `_peer_hit` probes only once the consumer session to the peer exists and is ready, and keeps driving both managers until then. Other probe tests drain a fixed number of times before probing; polling until the deadline also covers the poll-thread case, where the producer answers asynchronously. The #64501 behavior is intended and unchanged.

## Validation

No local GPU/runtime environment, so validation is through CI:

- Before (main): the `v1-kv-offload` step fails with the two errors above, e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98388#01a188c1-0e2b-46c5-91f3-0e4141da6244 (`55b677b2d1`).
- After (this PR, `da37fb81cf`): the same step (`pytest -v -s v1/kv_offload`, `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`) passes: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98413#01a18905-afb0-4c8c-aae2-d582a5f0be49

No model evals: test-only change.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `TestIdleWhileServingPeers`, `_peer_hit`, `test_pinned_peer_hit`, and PRs referencing #63618 / #64501: none.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to diagnose the failure and write the change. I reviewed every changed line; tests are validated by CI as described above.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Count tool call deltas as generated tokens in vllm-bench openai-responses
author: dilberx
body:
## Overview

The Rust `vllm-bench` `openai-responses` backend marks every tool-call-only response as failed. It counts only `output_text` and `reasoning_text` deltas as tokens, and a forced tool call streams only `function_call_arguments` deltas. This counts the four tool delta events the vLLM Responses server emits. #62753 is the same fix for the Python `vllm bench serve` client.

## Claims

- 100 tool calls the server completed with HTTP 200 went from 0 to 100 successful.
- Added events: `function_call_arguments`, `custom_tool_call_input`, `mcp_call_arguments`, `code_interpreter_call_code` (from `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/streaming_events.py`). Tool arguments are timed but not added to `generated_text`.

## Validation

Two new tests in `openai_responses.rs`: a tool-call-only response (TTFT, ITL, latency, usage) and each tool delta type on its own. Both fail with the old match arm. `cargo test -p vllm-bench` passes (215), and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, 100 prompts, concurrency 16, `tool_choice: "required"` via `--extra-body`:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| completed / failed | 0 / 100 | 100 / 0 |
| total generated tokens | 0 | 2,090 |

The 2,090 output tokens match the Python bench on the same workload.

## Details

The backend came in with #59489. Leaving tool calls out fails the request, so tool-calling workloads such as BFCL can't be measured with it.

No issue or PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Count each key once per request toward store_threshold
author: sohom-cs
body:
## Overview

With `store_threshold >= 2`, `CPUOffloadingManager` admits a chunk to the CPU tier only after it has been offered that many times. When `prepare_store()` can't allocate, it returns `None`, and the offloading scheduler offers the same keys again on a later step. Each retry counted as another offer, so a chunk that only one request ever had could be admitted by that request's own retry. A preempted request's re-offers counted the same way: the scheduler restarts its stores from chunk 0 through the same request context. With this PR, each key counts once per request.

## Claims

- A request counts each key toward `store_threshold` once. When it offers a key again, as a retry of a failed `prepare_store()` call or after preemption, the key doesn't count again; it still moves to the most recent end of the tracker, as before. A cache reset starts the request's counting over.
- `vllm:kv_offload_stores_skipped` counts a key's skip once per request too.
- Offers from other requests count as before. Nothing changes when `store_threshold < 2`.

## Validation

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py
```

`test_store_threshold_does_not_count_retries_of_a_failed_offer` runs with `store_threshold` 2 and 3:

1. It fills the CPU tier with in-flight stores.
2. One request offers an eligible key and a cold key twice. Both calls return `None`.
3. The stores complete, and the request offers the two keys again.
4. That offer must store only the eligible key. The cold key's count must still be 1, and `STORES_SKIPPED` must be 1.

`test_store_threshold_counts_a_key_once_per_request` (also 2 and 3) is the preemption case: the request stores the eligible key, then offers both keys again through the same context, as a resumed request does. The cold key must not be stored, its count must stay 1, `STORES_SKIPPED` must be 1, and another request's offer must still count it.

With main's `manager.py` all four fail, at the store; with this PR's first commit (bb7b8b6) the two preemption cases fail the same way:

```
E       AssertionError: assert [b'1\x00\x00\...\x00\x00\x00'] == [b'1\x00\x00\x00\x00']
E         Left contains one more item: b'2\x00\x00\x00\x00'
```

`b'2...'` is the cold key: main stores it, although only this request ever offered it.

**Through the scheduler.** I ran the offloading unit tests' `RequestRunner`, which drives the real `Scheduler` and `OffloadingConnectorScheduler`, with a real `CPUOffloadingManager(num_chunks=2, store_threshold=2)` behind it:

1. Request A (one block) is offered once.
2. Both CPU chunks are filled with stores that stay in flight.
3. Request B (A's block plus one of its own) finishes in one step. Its offer fails.
4. The stores complete, and B's finish-time retry offers both blocks again.

| | B's retry stores | B's own block in the CPU tier |
|---|---|---|
| main `4440f0e263` | both blocks | yes |
| this PR | A's block only | no |

The same runner with one request preempted once (free GPU blocks set to 0, as `test_request_preemption` does) and resumed, with sync and async scheduling: the request offers its two blocks, and after the resume offers them again through the same `ReqContext`. On main `dc45a5f552` and on bb7b8b6 that re-offer stores both of its own blocks; with this PR it stores neither.

<details>
<summary>The script (copy it into tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ and run it with pytest -s)</summary>

```python
# It drives the real Scheduler and OffloadingConnectorScheduler (the offloading
# unit tests' RequestRunner) with a real CPUOffloadingManager(store_threshold=2).
# A thin proxy hands the runner's mock worker its usual MockLoadStoreSpec.
from tests.v1.kv_connector.unit.offloading_connector.utils import (
    EOS_TOKEN_ID,
    MockLoadStoreSpec,
)
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import PrepareStoreOutput, ReqContext, make_offload_key
from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.manager import CPUOffloadingManager


class _Proxy:
    def __init__(self, real: CPUOffloadingManager):
        self._real = real
        self.offers: list[tuple[str, list, list | None]] = []

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return getattr(self._real, name)

    def prepare_store(self, keys, req_context):
        keys = list(keys)
        out = self._real.prepare_store(keys, req_context)
        self.offers.append(
            (req_context.req_id, keys, None if out is None else list(out.keys_to_store))
        )
        if out is None:
            return None
        return PrepareStoreOutput(
            keys_to_store=out.keys_to_store,
            store_spec=MockLoadStoreSpec(out.keys_to_store),
            evicted_keys=out.evicted_keys,
        )

    def prepare_load(self, keys, req_context):
        self._real.prepare_load(keys, req_context)
        return MockLoadStoreSpec(keys)


def test_single_request_block_is_not_stored_by_its_own_retry(request_runner):
    runner = request_runner(block_size=4, num_gpu_blocks=20, async_scheduling=False)
    real = CPUOffloadingManager(num_chunks=2, cache_policy="lru", store_threshold=2)
    proxy = _Proxy(real)
    runner.connector_scheduler.manager = proxy

    # Request A: one block. Its offer only counts the block (count 1).
    runner.new_request(token_ids=[1] * 4)
    runner._run(decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID], complete_transfers=True)

    # Fill both CPU chunks with stores that stay in flight.
    pinned = [make_offload_key(bytes([200 + i]) * 8, 0) for i in range(2)]
    real.prepare_store(pinned, ReqContext(req_id="pin-warmup", kv_transfer_params=None))
    pin_ctx = ReqContext(req_id="pin", kv_transfer_params=None)
    out = real.prepare_store(pinned, pin_ctx)
    assert out is not None and out.keys_to_store == pinned

    freed = []

    def free_pins_once():
        if not freed:
            real.complete_store(pinned, pin_ctx)
            freed.append(True)

    # Request B: A's block plus a block only B has. Its first offer fails
    # (no free or evictable chunk); the stores then complete, and B's
    # finish-time retry offers both blocks again.
    runner.new_request(token_ids=[1] * 4 + [2] * 4)
    b_id = str(runner.req_id)
    runner._run(
        decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID], complete_transfers=True, post_step_fn=free_pins_once
    )

    b_offers = [o for o in proxy.offers if o[0] == b_id]
    print("\nB offers (keys offered -> keys admitted, None = allocation failed):")
    for _, keys, admitted in b_offers:
        print("  ", len(keys), "keys ->", None if admitted is None else len(admitted))
    shared, own = b_offers[0][1]
    print("B-only block resident in CPU tier:", real._policy.get(own) is not None)
    print("shared block resident in CPU tier:", real._policy.get(shared) is not None)
    assert real._policy.get(shared) is not None
    assert real._policy.get(own) is None, "B's own block was stored by B's retry"
```
</details>

On this branch (Linux CPU):
- `test_manager.py`: 72 passed.
- `tests/v1/kv_offload`: 893 passed, 34 failed. Main fails the same 34: 32 in `cpu/test_gpu_worker.py`, which needs a GPU, and 2 in `tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestIdleWhileServingPeers`.
- The offloading connector unit tests: 679 passed, the same as bb7b8b6.

CI: both tests are in `tests/v1/kv_offload`, which the "V1 KV Offload" step runs. I have no GPU, so I haven't run vLLM end to end. This changes which chunks are admitted, not how they are written or read, and the scheduler run above covers the path from the scheduler's retry to the manager. If you'd like an end-to-end run before merging, I'll do it when I have GPU time. Model outputs are unaffected, so no evals.

## Details

Root cause:

1. `prepare_store()` counts every offered key toward `store_threshold` (`_record_accesses`) before it allocates.
2. If no chunk is free or evictable, it returns `None`. `_build_store_jobs` counts `vllm:kv_offload_allocation_failure` and moves on without advancing the request's store position. So the same keys are offered again on a later step, and again when the request finishes (`test_scheduler_reports_allocation_failure` asserts both attempts).
3. Each retry counted again. With `store_threshold=2`, one failed allocation and its retry admit every cold chunk in the offer. That happens under CPU-tier pressure, where the filter matters most.

Why a retry isn't another offer: #52227 moved the counter from lookups to store offers. It relied on `prepare_store()` receiving "the request's whole offerable key set", so that "a block crosses store_threshold after that many repetitions of the content". A retry resends that same offer, and so does a preempted request when it resumes: no new request, no new repetition. The metric is likewise documented as skips under the "reuse threshold". The same function already counts a request's keys once across calls in two places: the policy's `on_store_miss` (through `store_miss_keys`) and the request's access record (through `seen_keys`). Before this PR, the threshold counter and its skip metric were the per-key counts that a retry or a resumed request incremented again.

Scope: the keys a request has counted are kept in `counted_keys` on its `_RequestCacheAccess`, next to `store_miss_keys` and `seen_keys`, only when `store_threshold >= 2`. The scheduler keeps a request's `ReqContext` across preemption and drops it once the request is finished, so the set lasts as long as the request; a cache reset starts it over, as it does the rest of that state.

The first commit skipped only retries of failed offers. After review, every key counts once per request, as `store_miss_keys` does, so a request's re-offers after preemption don't count either. Three existing tests offered twice through one context to stand for two requests: `test_filter_reused_manager`, `test_filter_reused_manager_oversized_offer_makes_progress` and `test_store_threshold_does_not_hide_ready_reuse`. They now use one context per request.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes `_record_accesses` or the threshold filter. I searched open PRs for `store_threshold`, `_record_accesses` and `prepare_store`. #63686 rewords the `store_threshold` docs. #57813, #63900 and #64216 change other parts of `manager.py`.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted; reviewed and tested by me.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Skip AITER tuned GEMM when M*N >= 2^31 on gfx950
author: micah-wil
body:
## Overview

Skip AITER's tuned GEMM (`tgemm.mm`) on gfx950 when M·N ≥ 2^31 (Also skip AITER tuned GEMM when A or B spans >= 4 GiB) and fall back to `F.linear` (hipBLASLt). This works around an int32 output-offset overflow in AITER's gfx950 FlyDSL A16W16 kernel (fix pending in ROCm/aiter#6853). Since AITER v0.1.26, that overflow crashes `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` at startup with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.

## Claims

- Fixes the `Memory access fault ... Write access to a read-only page` crash during the encoder-cache profile run of MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on MI355X (TP4) with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.
- No performance cost: only GEMMs with ≥ 2^31 output elements are rerouted, and hipBLASLt matches the FlyDSL kernel's throughput at those sizes. Normal LLM prefill/decode GEMMs never reach this size.

## Validation

Environment: MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`, AITER 0.1.26.

**Kernel-level repro** (`tgemm.mm` vs `F.linear`, N=6144, K=1280, bf16, with bias; this matches the tuned `minimax_m3_mxfp4_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` rows):

| M | M·N vs 2^31 | `tgemm.mm` (AITER) | `F.linear` (hipBLASLt) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 340,000 | below | 1221 TFLOP/s | 1206 TFLOP/s |
| 360,000 | above | Memory access fault | n/a |
| 768,000 | above | Memory access fault | 1229 TFLOP/s |

**End-to-end** with this patch:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 -tp 4 --trust-remote-code --block-size 128 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --moe-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 
```

Before: crashes at startup with the memory access fault. After: startup completes (178 GiB KV cache on TP0), and three chat requests with a 2016×2016 image return 200 with no faults. Confirmed there is no accuracy change.

No unit test is added: reproducing the bug needs gfx950 hardware plus AITER's model-specific tuned CSV, and a mocked test would only restate the condition.

## Details

**Root cause.** With `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, each rank runs the ViT unsharded, so the profile run issues an M=768000, N=6144, K=1280 GEMM with bias. In AITER v0.1.26, `getPaddedM` maps it to the `8192,6144,1280` FlyDSL row in `minimax_m3_mxfp4_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv`. That kernel computes `global_row * n + global_col` in int32, which wraps once M·N ≥ 2^31 and writes out of bounds. In TP mode N is sharded 4 ways, so M·N stays under the limit.

**Why route around it here.** `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` is the only vLLM call site of `tgemm.mm`. The guard is limited to gfx950 and to the exact overflow condition, so all other shapes keep AITER's tuned dispatch. Skipping FlyDSL for this call also avoids the FlyDSL 0.4.0 `from_dlpack` leak described in ROCm/aiter#6853, which pinned about 10.6 GiB after the ViT profile run.

The guard can be removed once vLLM's minimum AITER includes ROCm/aiter#6853.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Fix Mamba region stride on block-outermost layouts
author: Dao007forever
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix NIXL transfers of Mamba/SSM hybrid state on block-outermost KV cache layouts (`BLHNC`, `BLNHC`), and add a CPU test that pulls one request between two NIXL workers on real model KV layouts and checks every byte.

Related: vllm-project/vllm#63416 changes how NIXL pairs regions. This PR does not depend on it, and #63416 rebases onto it without conflicts.

## Claims

- **Fix.** With `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`, Qwen3-Next (GDN) and Nemotron-H (Mamba2) disaggregated P/D read the wrong Mamba state and wrote outside the request's blocks, with no error. They now transfer correctly. Layer-outermost layouts (the default) are unchanged. Hybrids whose attention is MLA, such as Kimi-Linear, were not affected (see Root cause).
- **Test.** The NIXL unit tests build KV cache configs and tensors by hand. The new test plans and allocates both sides with vLLM's own planner (`get_kv_cache_configs`) and allocator (`allocate_kv_cache`), from the per-layer KV specs of 12 models. D pulls one request from P through the real worker code; the recorded descriptors run as memory copies. Every page of every layer must land in D's block for the same layer and request position, and no other D byte may change.

## Validation

CPU only: `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`. No weights or model code: the KV specs are built in the test.

```
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k real_model
# 14 passed in ~10 s
```

| Case | KV plan in the test (groups → regions) | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B (same shape as GLM-4.5-Air, MiniMax-M2) | 4 full, 1 → 4 | auto (LBHNC) |
| gpt-oss-20b | SW + full, 2 → 2 shared | auto |
| Gemma 3 1B | 10 SW + 2 full, 6 → 2 shared | auto |
| MiMo-V2-Flash | 9 SW + 3 full, 4 → 3 shared | auto |
| DeepSeek-V3 (same as Kimi-K2) | 4 MLA, 1 → 4 | auto; BLNHC → BLNHC; BLNHC P → LBNHC D |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 | MLA + indexer cache, 1 → 8 | auto |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | 6 GDN + 2 full, 4 → 2 shared | auto; BLHNC |
| NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 | 11 Mamba2 + 2 full, 7 → 2 shared | auto; BLHNC |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | 6 KDA + 2 MLA, 4 → 2 shared | auto; BLNHC |

Fails before the fix: the new test with `main`'s `base_worker.py`:

```
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -k "real_model and BLHNC"
FAILED ...[Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-BLHNC-BLHNC]
  AssertionError: ['model.layers.0.linear_attn[0].0', 'model.layers.4.linear_attn[0].0', ...]
FAILED ...[NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-BLHNC-BLHNC]
  AssertionError: ['model.layers.0.mixer[0].0', 'model.layers.11.mixer[0].0', ...]
2 failed
```

Every GDN/Mamba2 page arrives wrong. With the fix, all 14 cases pass.

The test also catches descriptor bugs it was not written for: dropping the conv-state offset from the peer's SSM descriptor (`_build_mamba_remote`) fails the three layer-outermost hybrid cases.

NIXL unit suites (`test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_push_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py`), on `main` and on this branch:

| Tree | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `main` @ `4e0ad5720` | 646 | 4 |
| this branch | 660 | 4, the same ones |

- **The 4 failures on both:** `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma` needs a gated HF repo, `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray, None]` needs Ray/GPU, and `test_register_packed_dsv4_mla_cache_as_single_region[v41-aliased-groups]` fails on `main` as well.
- **Transient failures:** the branch's first suite run also had 11 consecutive failures in `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`, during a period of HF Hub rate limiting (see below). All 11 passed on rerun, and a full run of that file passed (271 tests).

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

Note on flakiness: the new test builds two `create_vllm_config` configs per case, as other NIXL unit tests do. When the HF Hub rate-limits the `facebook/opt-125m` file listing (HTTP 429), any of these tests fails in setup. That was the only failure cause seen in about 600 local runs of the new test.

## Details

**Root cause.** Under the hybrid KV cache manager, cache groups share KV cache tensors. With a block-outermost layout, block *b* of every tensor sits side by side in one row, so a layer's view advances by the row: 4,718,592 B for Qwen3-Next's two tensors in the test, not by one 2,359,296 B page. `register_kv_caches` registered Mamba regions with `block_stride = physical_page_size` and took the view's stride only for CSA-linear. So every Mamba descriptor past block 0 pointed into the other tensor's pages. Attention regions on the same rows already used the view stride.

Only some hybrids hit it. A shared region keeps the stride of the first layer registered into it (layer-name order), and a later layer replaces it only if it is MLA. Mamba sub-region descriptors use the region's stride:
- In Qwen3-Next and Nemotron-H a Mamba layer comes first, and their full-attention layers never replace its page stride.
- In Kimi-Linear the MLA layer replaces it with the row stride, so its KDA descriptors were right by accident; the Kimi-Linear BLNHC case passes with or without the fix.

The fix takes the view's stride for Mamba views on block-outermost layouts too. Elsewhere the page stride stays. A view indexed by kernel block (several per logical block) has a stride of a fraction of the page, and taking the view's stride there breaks the existing hetero-block-size tests.

Flow (pull, the failing case):
1. Startup, P and D: `register_kv_caches` registers each region as `(base, len, stride, count)`; Mamba regions get stride = one page.
2. Handshake: D builds descriptors for P's Mamba sub-regions (conv q/k/v parts, SSM state) from P's metadata, and its own from its local regions.
3. Read: a descriptor id for block *b* resolves to `base + b × stride`. With stride = page instead of row, block *b*'s address lands in another tensor's page of a lower block, on both sides.

**The test.**
- Models are those tested end to end for vllm-project/vllm#63416. MiniMax-M1 is left out; vLLM removed it in 0.23.0.
- Specs mirror what each model's layers return. Nine were dumped from a meta-device model build on CPU. DeepSeek-V3.2 (sparse MLA + indexer) and Kimi-Linear (MLA + KDA) cannot be built on CPU, so their specs come from their configs and vLLM's state-shape helpers.
- Each case uses the first layers of its model, enough for its group and region pattern (2 regions for the hybrids). The largest case allocates about 120 MB per side.
- Hybrid block sizes are the ones vLLM aligns to on CPU (1152, 1408). For Kimi-Linear it is 1920, the first 64-token multiple whose MLA page holds the KDA state.

**Not covered.**
- Push, TP mismatch, PP stages, and P and D with different settings. With the same model and settings the region pairing is the identity; those cases stay with the hand-built tests.
- GPU, and an end-to-end P/D run with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` on a hybrid model.

**Mocks.** `tests/AGENTS.md` asks for real objects. The workers are patched the same way as the existing `_make_mla_hybrid_worker` helper in this file:
- the platform reports a CUDA device, so the GPU registration path runs on a CPU host;
- attention backends and kernel block-size selection are faked, since no model layers are built;
- TP rank and size are fixed at 0 and 1;
- NIXL itself is the file's `_RecordingNixl`.

Planner, allocator, layout resolution, registration, handshake and descriptor code are all real.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#62453 fixes Mamba page padding on the CPU host-buffer path, and vllm-project/vllm#64140 fixes packed Mamba addressing in the KV offloading worker. Neither touches NIXL's Mamba region stride.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change. The submitter reviews every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Fall back from the latent-MoE tail fusion under sleep mode
author: aleksandr-inherent
body:
## Overview

On SM100 at TP 8 or 16, `LatentMoERunner` raises `ValueError: K3 latent-MoE tail fusion does not support sleep mode.` when `--enable-sleep-mode` is set, so Kimi-K3 cannot start with sleep mode, which the process checkpoint lifecycle (#62570) requires. The runner now falls back to the default latent-MoE path with a warning, as it already does for unsupported TP sizes. No open PR or issue addresses the sleep-mode raise. #64276 and #65582 change the same block; whichever merges later needs a rebase.

## Claims

- Kimi-K3 starts with `--enable-sleep-mode` on SM100 at TP 8 and 16, on the default latent-MoE path.
- Without sleep mode nothing changes, and DBO or ubatching with the tail fusion still raises.

## Validation

- The new `test_sleep_mode_falls_back_to_default_path` fails on main and passes with this change. Both tests build the runner with the file's existing stand-ins and need no GPU. A regression test through `LLM` needs Kimi-K3 on 8 B300s, which CI does not have, so the end-to-end run below is the validation outside CI.

  <details>
  <summary>Before and after</summary>

  ```text
  $ pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py -k "deferred_finalize_enabled or sleep_mode"

  # main (aa738c38c3) with the new test
  E   ValueError: K3 latent-MoE tail fusion does not support sleep mode.
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py:102: ValueError
  1 failed, 1 passed, 3 deselected

  # this branch
  2 passed, 3 deselected
  ```

  </details>

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.
- End to end on vLLM 0.31.0 with an equivalent local change (the tail fusion turned off whenever sleep mode is on), on 8x B300: `nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4` at TP 8 and DCP 8 with sleep mode, captured and restored with ai-dynamo/snapshot. Without the change the engine raised the error above at startup. With it, a restored replica returned the same text as a cold replica running the tail fusion, with per-token logprobs 0.01-0.09 apart, and served 861 requests at 48 concurrent with no errors. This exact diff has not been run end to end.

## Details

**Why fall back.** The raise came in with the runner without a stated reason. On the same GPUs the K3 specialized decode already treats sleep mode as a reason to run the stock forward (`specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py`), and the TP-size check just above falls back with a warning. Sleep mode now does the same, before the tail op is initialized.

**Tradeoff.** Under sleep mode Kimi-K3 loses the tail fusion's speedup, which we have not measured. Making the tail fusion work across sleep and wake is out of scope.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Use 64-bit row offsets in the RDNA hybrid W4A16 GEMM
author: vllmellm
body:
## Overview

`_triton_w4a16_skinny_fmt_kernel` indexed activations and outputs with int32 row offsets, which wrap once M × K or M × N passes 2^31: the store faults with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` and the process hangs, and the load returns mapped garbage, so 127 rows come back NaN. Same class as #63049, which #63054 fixed for the CDNA kernel; this is the gfx11/gfx12 sibling.

## Claims

- cast `pid_m` to int64, which widens both `offs_m * stride_am` and `offs_m * N`; `offs_m` is the only offset here that scales with M.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py -k int32_offsets   # R9700, gfx1201
```

| (K, N), M = 2^31 // max(K, N) + 128 | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| (256, 34816), M=61,808 | `Fatal Python error: Aborted` on the store, then hangs | 2 passed, 0.023 max abs dev |
| (17408, 256), M=123,489 | 127 NaN rows, first at row 123,362 | 2 passed, 0 NaN rows over all M |

Manually tested on an R9700 (gfx1201): both parametrizations fail on main and pass with the change. No CI pool covers gfx11/gfx12, so the test is gated on `on_gfx1x()` like the file's other kernel tests, because `tests/kernels/quantization` runs on MI300 and MI355 and neither ships this kernel.

## Details

Test tolerance stays at the file's `rtol=1e-2, atol=5e-2`, since a K=17,408 bf16 dot accumulates differently at 64-wide BLOCK_K.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Leave GLM-4.7 array and object tool arguments unpinned
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

The non-strict GLM-4.7 structural tag from #56403 pins array and object tool arguments to JSON. When GLM writes one of those values as text that is not valid JSON, the grammar forces tokens the model rates near zero, and the call can loop until `max_tokens`. This leaves array and object values as raw text, the way string values already are.

## Claims

- Only requests that get the non-strict GLM-4.7 tag change, and only in array and object arguments, plus type lists that contain them. These are `glm47` requests with tools (`tool_choice` auto, required or a named tool), and `ling3` requests with `required`, a named tool, or `--tool-strict-level function`. The value becomes text that ends at `</arg_value>`. Integer, number, boolean, null and enum values keep their JSON pins, and so do argument keys and the call envelope.
- A valid JSON value parses exactly as before. A value that is not JSON reaches the client as the raw string, through the parser's existing fallback (`coerce_to_schema_type`). On main the grammar rules such values out by forcing other tokens instead.
- Strict tools (`strict: true` or `--tool-strict-level parameter`) are unchanged. No other parser uses this tag.
- The change is in `_glm_4_7_value_format` only: 13 lines added and 10 removed, plus tests.

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `8084f0624d` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New tests | `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -k container` | 2 failed, 6 passed | 8 passed |
| Registry tests | `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py` | | 278 passed |
| GLM parser tests | `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py` | | 42 passed |
| Structural-tag attach | `pytest tests/parser/test_abstract_parser.py` | | 10 passed |
| GLM-5.3 served by vLLM, 10 samples per arm (below) | | intended path 4/10; 6/10 corrupted; 3/10 hit the 120-token cap | intended path 10/10, all finished |

The two failing cases on main are the two texts the model really writes: a bare backslash (`D:\SVILUPPO\docs\PLAN.md`) and an over-escaped key quote (`[{"path\": ...`). Tests ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` (xgrammar 0.2.8) with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. `ruff` 0.14.0 and the repo's `mypy` hook (1.20.2, Python 3.11) are clean.

<details>
<summary>GLM-5.3 A/B</summary>

The A/B runs on a GLM-5.3 deployment (vLLM 0.32.0, MTP with 3 speculative tokens). The prompt is a captured 5,400-token Cline request (Windows workspace, 26 tools, `tool_choice` auto), cut after the model's `</think>`. It is sent to `/v1/completions` with temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 and `max_tokens` 120, and the tag is passed in `structured_outputs.structural_tag`. The arms:

- No grammar.
- The tag main builds for the request.
- The tag this branch builds for the request. `ParserManager.get_parser("glm47", "glm45", enable_auto_tools=True)` and `adjust_request` on the branch give a tag equal to this arm's, field by field.

| Arm | Path written | Finished |
|---|---|---|
| No grammar | `D:\SVILUPPO\MantoRustPad\docs\TEAM\PROMPT_JUNIOR.md` 10/10 | 10/10 |
| main tag | correct 4/10 (written as escaped JSON); others `D:\b\bb0324-...\bb0324-...` repeating, `\test-chromium-mcp\test-chromium-mcp...`, `\bin\fake_shell_bin\...` | 7/10 |
| This PR's tag | `D:\SVILUPPO\MantoRustPad\docs\TEAM\PROMPT_JUNIOR.md` 10/10 | 10/10 |

The deployment's own tag-building code is main's. Not measured: a server running this branch end to end. The tag it builds is checked above, and the parser output for non-JSON values is covered by the existing fallback.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `_glm_4_7_value_format` returns `JSONSchemaFormat(json_schema={"type": t})` for every non-string type, arrays and objects included. Two things go wrong inside that element when the model's text is not JSON.

1. After a backslash inside a JSON string, the grammar admits only `" \ / b f n r t u`. GLM-5.3 writes Windows paths with single backslashes. On a captured request ending in `"path": "D:\`, the unconstrained next token is `SV` at p = 0.999998, and the grammar blocks all of the top 20 candidates. Sampling then picks a token the model rates below 1e-9 (`b`). The path fills with invented `\b...` and `\f...` names, and a 20-token cycle forms that top_p 0.95 cannot leave. With `max_tokens` unset, it runs to the context limit.
2. The JSON element has no excludes. When the model over-escapes a key's closing quote (`[{"newText\": ...`), the key string stays open, so `</arg_value>` and `</tool_call>` are read as string text and no stop token is allowed. In one captured turn the model wanted to stop (`<|observation|>` at p = 0.999993 unconstrained) and was forced on to 322 calls. If a later quote closes the key instead, the grammar allows only whitespace or `:`, and the output is whitespace until `max_tokens`.

We saw both in production with GLM-5.3 coding agents. In one afternoon we caught seven looping requests, and six of them were tool calls under this tag. Before #56403 these requests had no grammar. `--tool-strict-level auto` avoids the problem today by dropping the tag for non-strict auto requests, but that also drops the call-envelope constraint.

**Change.** A value keeps a JSON pin only when every type it allows is a scalar (`integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`). Anything else gets `AnyTextFormat(excludes=_GLM_4_7_VALUE_EXCLUDES)`, the format string values already use. That covers `array`, `object`, `string`, a missing type, and a type list that includes any of these. A type list with `string` was already free text in practice, because `OrFormat` with free text admits everything the JSON branch admits.

**Tradeoff.** In non-strict mode, array and object arguments lose their shape constraint. A model that writes malformed JSON there now gets it through as a string, which the client sees as an argument of the wrong type. Clients that need the shape enforced can mark the tool `strict: true`. This is the same contract string arguments have.

**Related.** #61205 (open) caps whitespace in these tags at 64 characters. That shortens the whitespace tail in case 2, but the grammar then forces `:` and the broken call continues. This PR removes the JSON element those runs happen in. The two PRs touch the same last line of `_glm_4_7_value_format`, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase. #62499 (open) changes when the tag applies alongside `response_format`, a different path. No open PR changes the GLM value formats.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the root-cause analysis, the fix, the tests and this description.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix KeyError crash when a LoRA name is reloaded with requests in flight
author: heyemlee
body:
## Overview

Fixes #64570. This change compares both `lora_name` and `lora_int_id` in `LoRARequest`, so reloading an adapter under the same name while old requests are still running no longer kills the engine.

## Claims

- Fixes the `KeyError` in `convert_mapping` → `EngineDeadError` reported in #64570.
- In-flight requests keep using the old adapter, while new requests use the reloaded one.

## Validation

- Added a regression test that crashes with `EngineDeadError` on `main` and passes with this fix.
- Reproduced the unload/reload flow against a running server. On `main`, the engine exits; with this fix, both requests complete with their respective adapters and `/health` returns 200.
- MRV2: `LoraState.get_activate_loras` returns adapter IDs `[1]` on `main` and `[1, 2]` with this fix. Local CPU testing used MRV1; the GPU CI job covers MRV2.
- Related CPU suites: 58 passed (`tests/lora/test_worker.py::test_worker_apply_lora` fails the same way on `main` because it does not support CPU). `pre-commit` passed.
- No model eval: outputs change only for batches that crashed before.

<details>
<summary>Commands and output</summary>

Regression test:

```bash
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=4 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_lora_functions.py::test_same_lora_name_with_different_ids -v -s
```

`main`:

```
  File "vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/utils.py", line 101, in convert_mapping
    lora_id_to_index[x] if x > 0 else -1 for x in mapping.prompt_mapping
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^
KeyError: np.int64(2)
...
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
============================== 1 failed in 30.67s ==============================
```

This PR:

```
tests/lora/test_lora_functions.py::test_same_lora_name_with_different_ids PASSED
============================== 1 passed in 27.57s ==============================
```

Server flow: `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-lora --max-loras 2 --max-lora-rank 8 --max-model-len 1024 --enforce-eager` with `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=True`. Load `pet` (meow adapter), start a 200-token stream on `pet`, unload `pet`, load `pet` again (woof adapter), load one more adapter so the new `pet` ID is evicted from its slot, then request `pet`.

- `main`: `KeyError: np.int64(2)` → `EngineDeadError`; both requests fail and the server exits.
- This PR: the old stream returns `Meow Meow Meow Meow Meow…`, the new request returns `Woof Woof Woof Woof Woof`, and `/health` returns 200.

</details>

## Details

`LoRARequest` currently compares only adapter names. If an adapter is unloaded and reloaded under the same name while old requests are still running, the worker can treat the old and new IDs as one adapter. The missing ID then causes `convert_mapping` to raise `KeyError`, killing the engine.

This does not change when unload takes effect or whether it waits for in-flight requests.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #64570 or changes `LoRARequest` equality. I searched open PRs by the issue number and by `convert_mapping`, `LoRARequest`, `unload_lora_adapter` and `make_lora_inputs`.
