title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Don't count content-free chunks as streamed outputs in vllm-bench chat
author: dilberx
body:
## Overview

The Rust `vllm-bench` `openai-chat` backend counts any chunk with non-empty `choices` as a streamed output. vLLM's chat stream opens with a role-only chunk, `{"role":"assistant","content":""}`, so TTFT is measured to a chunk with no token and the first real token adds a spurious ITL sample. #62341 fixed the same thing in the Python client; this ports its rule.

## Claims

- On 100 chat requests, `main` recorded one extra ITL sample on every request, a sub-0.1 ms first sample on all 100 (the role chunk arriving just before the first token), and on 22 requests more ITL samples than there are gaps between their tokens. With the fix all three are gone.
- `ChatDelta` now reads `role`, `reasoning`, `reasoning_content`, `tool_calls` and `function_call`, and a chunk counts when it carries content, reasoning or a tool call, or an empty `content` without `role` (a token that decodes to an empty string). Same rule as Python's `_choice_has_streamed_output`.

## Validation

Four new tests in `openai_chat.rs`, on the existing socket SSE server made scriptable: the role chunk, an empty mid-stream delta, an empty-string token, and reasoning plus tool call deltas. All four fail with the old gate. `cargo test -p vllm-bench` passes (217), and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, random 256 in / 128 out, 100 prompts, concurrency 16, through a proxy that recorded every streamed chunk:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| requests with one more ITL sample than token chunks on the wire | 100 | 0 |
| requests with a sub-0.1 ms ITL sample at position 0 | 100 | 0 |
| requests with `len(itl) == output_tokens` | 22 | 0 |

Forced tool calls through `openai-chat` still complete 100 of 100, with ITL counts matching the wire.

## Details

#59736 makes a token-less stream fail. With this change a stream carrying only the role chunk has no token, so the two fit together.

No issue or PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.

title: [Bugfix][SleepMode] Exact-size, reusable pinned CPU backup for level-1 sleep
author: aoshen02
body:
## Problem

Level-1 sleep backs up every cumem allocation to host memory with `torch.empty(size, pin_memory=True)`. torch's `CachingHostAllocator` rounds each pinned block up to a power of two and keeps freed blocks in its cache, so the level-1 backup costs up to ~2x the offloaded bytes in host memory, and that memory is never returned to the OS. On Mistral Large 4 at TP8 the backup is 85.19 GiB per GPU, which turned into roughly +578 GiB of host memory per node.

## Root cause

The backup size is chosen by the caching host allocator, not by the allocation. The old code already kept the memory across wake-ups: the freed pinned block stayed in the cache and was handed back on the next sleep, which is why repeated sleeps were fast. The bug is the rounding. Nothing in this path asks for the cache.

## Fix

Data model: `AllocationData.cpu_backup_tensor` is the allocation's host backup buffer, one per allocation.

- Lifetime: created exact-size on the first level-1 offload of that allocation, reused on every later offload, released only when the allocation is freed or its contents are discarded (level-2 sleep, tags not offloaded, `discard()`).
- Validity is derived, not stored: wake restores an allocation iff it is asleep and has a buffer.
- Invariant: asleep + buffer => the buffer holds this sleep's data. Every transition to asleep (`sleep` and `discard`) goes through one helper, `_put_to_sleep(ptr, data, offload)`, which either copies into the buffer or releases it before unmapping. So a buffer left over from an earlier offload can never be restored after a discard. The existing already-asleep policy checks (`cpu_backup_tensor is not None` on asleep allocations) keep their meaning unchanged.
- CUDA/ROCm (`cumem.py`): the buffer is an anonymous `mmap` wrapped with `torch.frombuffer` and pinned with the existing `libcudart.cudaHostRegister` wrapper. If registration fails, the error is drained with `cudaGetLastError`, a warning is logged once and the backup stays pageable, the same fallback as the other `cudaHostRegister` callers (`shm_tensor_arena.py`, `ec_shared_region.py`). Release unregisters only a pinned buffer, ignores the return code (draining any error) and never raises, since it also runs from the allocator's free callback; then the reference is dropped, which unmaps it.
- XPU (`xpumem.py`): same single-field reuse/release semantics with its existing pinned torch tensor. Exact-size pinning is not available there.

No config, env var, API or protocol change. None is needed: the old behavior already kept the backup memory between sleeps, and this keeps it at exactly the offloaded size.

## Results

Qwen3-8B, 1x GB200, `enable_sleep_mode=True`, 4 cycles of `sleep(level=1)`, `wake_up()` and greedy generate. Host memory is node `MemTotal - MemAvailable` relative to before the first sleep.

| | host asleep | host awake | first sleep | later sleeps | wake | outputs identical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 23.00 GiB | 22.99 GiB | 1.16 s | 0.16-0.18 s | 0.13-0.14 s | yes (4/4) |
| this PR | 16.92 GiB | 16.92 GiB | 0.84 s | 0.15 s | 0.13 s | yes (4/4) |

Host memory is flat across cycles in both cases. Sleep and wake are as fast as before.

## Test plan

No new test function; the existing tests in `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` are strengthened with deterministic checks (no RSS thresholds). Every level-1 backup must be exactly its allocation's size and page-locked, and torch's pinned host caching allocator must not be used across sleep (`torch.cuda.host_memory_stats()["allocated_bytes.allocated"]` unchanged).

- `test_release_kv_cache_memory_preserves_generation` (kv-only / sleep-1 / sleep-2) and `test_sleep_with_only_weights_asleep` (first x second level): 3 and 2 sleep/wake cycles with greedy output identical to pre-sleep every cycle. Worker-side state is read via `collective_rpc`: offloaded tags hold exact pinned backups and others hold none; the same buffers are kept after wake and reused on the next sleep; a level-1 then level-2 cycle leaves weights with no backup.
- `test_basic_cumem` (`pinned` / `register-fails`): 3 level-1 cycles with changing data, same buffers reused. A sleep that does not offload the tag releases (unregisters) its backup. Freeing an allocation releases its backup. In `register-fails`, `cudaHostRegister` returns an error: sleep/wake data is still correct, backups are pageable, a warning is logged, and release never calls `cudaHostUnregister`.
- `test_discard_tags`: `discard()` releases the kv backup, so the following wake has nothing stale to restore; weights keep and reuse theirs.
- `test_level2_discards_ordinary_tensor_with_weights_tag`: level-1 cycle, then a level-2 style sleep releases the backup; the poisoned wake proves nothing was restored.
- `test_reentered_tag`: freeing an offloaded allocation while awake releases its backup.
- `test_runtime_state_survives_sleep`: runtime backups are exact, pinned and kept at both levels without the host caching allocator.

## Test result (GB200)

- With this PR: full `test_cumem.py` 22 passed, 3 runs in a row; `test_basic_cumem[pinned]` and `test_basic_cumem[register-fails]` also pass run alone. `register-fails` fails on the previous revision of this PR, which raised on a registration failure.
- Same tests against main's `cumem.py`: 13 failed, 8 passed. Failing: `test_basic_cumem`, `test_release_kv_cache_memory_preserves_generation[sleep-1,sleep-2]`, `test_sleep_with_only_weights_asleep[all 4]`, `test_runtime_state_survives_sleep[sleep-1,sleep-2]` (torch host caching allocator used during sleep: +32 MiB to +2.5 GB), and `test_discard_tags`, `test_reentered_tag[both]`, `test_level2_discards_ordinary_tensor_with_weights_tag` (backups dropped on wake). With the host-stats check neutralized, the same 13 still fail on backup reuse.
- Engine smoke: see the table above.

XPU change is untested on hardware.

Follow-up option: an opt-in "release the backup on wake" for host-memory-constrained colocated RL is one extra `release_cpu_backup` after the restore copy in `wake_up`. The invariant still holds because it only constrains asleep allocations. Not part of this PR.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Parse closed Qwen3 tool parameters once while streaming
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

A Qwen3 XML tool call that repeats closed parameters makes `_qwen3_arg_converter` re-scan every parameter on each streaming conversion, so the API server's cost per token grows with the call until the event loop saturates and liveness fails. This parses each closed parameter once. It is the Qwen3 counterpart of #64535 (GLM) and covers every parser on the Qwen3 converter: `qwen3_coder`, Nemotron-3, Step-3.5, Step5, Seed-OSS, MiniCPM-V and Granite thinking.

## Claims

- Streaming a call with N closed parameters matches the parameter regex N times in total. On main every conversion matches all closed parameters again and the value extender scans them twice more: 2,051,331 matches for N = 401 in the new test.
- Streamed deltas and non-streaming results are unchanged.
- For a call looping on two parameters, the cost per 4-token engine step at 64K output chars drops from 6.4 ms to 92 us, and a replay at 200 tok/s no longer fails liveness (main: killed at 335 s).
- On a real server (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, one H200), that loop to 256K chars keeps the API server 100% busy on main from 148 s, and `/health` answers no probe within 10 s for the last 150 s of the stream. With this PR the API server is 7% busy and `/health` p99 is 0.9 ms.
- No new config, flag or API. `MiMoParser` keeps its own converter and is unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `8084f0624d` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cost test | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py::TestArgValueExtender::test_closed_params_are_parsed_once` | `AssertionError: assert 2051331 == 401` | passed |
| Qwen3 parser tests | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py` | 84 passed, 2 failed (the new tests) | 86 passed |
| Parser suite | `pytest tests/parser --ignore=tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py --ignore=tests/parser/test_harmony.py` | 6570 passed, 93 errors | 6574 passed, 93 errors (same set) |
| Files that need Hugging Face | `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_step3p5_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py tests/parser/test_include_reasoning.py` | 427 passed | 427 passed |
| Resumed parse against main (below) | random argument texts grown piece by piece, two calls sharing one cache | | 0 mismatches in 700,709 growth steps |
| Streaming equivalence (below) | Qwen3 tokenizer, `qwen3_coder` + `nemotron_v3`, `parse_delta` at chunk sizes 1, 3, 4, 7, 64, plus `parse` | | 114 of 114 records identical |
| Cost per step (below) | parameter loop, through `OutputProcessor` and `chat_completion_stream_generator` | 1741 us at 16K chars, 6435 us at 64K | 57 us at 16K chars, 92 us at 64K |
| Looping stream replay (below) | 200 tok/s, liveness 30 s / 5 s / 3 | liveness kill at 335 s | no kill in 1200 s, loop 10% busy at 240K tokens |
| Server run (below) | Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on one H200, forced parameter loop to 256K chars | API server 394.8 s CPU (90% busy), 16 `/health` timeouts of 10 s | 26.8 s (7%), `/health` p99 0.90 ms, no timeout |

Unit tests, equivalence and replays ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The 93 parser-suite errors are the same set on both: 70 in the three files that need Hugging Face access (the fifth row, run with access), and 23 in `tests/parser/mistral/test_reasoning.py`, which fails the same on main with the image's mistral-common. `ruff`, the repo's `mypy` hook and the CI-wiring hook pass.

CI coverage: `tests/parser` jobs are disabled since #63609, so CI will run the new tests once that job is back.

<details>
<summary>Resumed parse against main</summary>

Each case builds two calls' raw arguments from fragments: whole and split `<parameter=...>` openers, `</parameter>` and `< / parameter >` closers with prefixes of both, repeated names, newlines, `>`, `=`, non-ASCII and value text. Each call grows in random 1-9 char pieces through one shared cache. After every piece, the converter with the cache must return main's `_qwen3_arg_converter` output for `partial=True` and `partial=False`, and the extender must be `None` exactly when main's is and then stream the same text for every later piece. Seeds 1-3, 4,000 cases each.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Streaming equivalence</summary>

Each output is tokenized with the Qwen3 tokenizer and streamed as token-id chunks through `ParserManager.get_parser("qwen3_coder", "nemotron_v3")`. Every delta's content, reasoning, tool-call name and arguments are recorded, plus one non-streaming `parse`. The outputs: content, CJK content, reasoning, an open Python, HTML and CJK value, a parameter loop, a call loop, an open JSON array, a long value under a repeated name, and 9 repeated-name cases (a different, identical, extending or prefix value, a repeat that is not last, a third occurrence restoring the first value, another name after the repeat, an unclosed repeat, a second call).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cost per step and looping stream replay</summary>

The stream is `<tool_call>\n<function=Edit>\n` followed by `<parameter=old_string>\ntotal = 0\n</parameter>\n<parameter=new_string>\ntotal = 1\n</parameter>\n` repeated, with the Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer. Cost is the endpoint's time per 4-token engine step (`chat_completion_stream_generator` with `qwen3_coder` and `nemotron_v3`, prompt with reasoning closed).

| Output chars | 1K | 4K | 16K | 64K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 127 us | 642 us | 1741 us | 6435 us |
| This PR | 56 us | 51 us | 57 us | 92 us |

The replay feeds the same stream through the streaming parser on a virtual clock: 200 tokens/s in 4-token steps, one `parse_delta` per event-loop pass for every token emitted since the previous pass, measured parser time doubled for a slower server CPU, and kubelet liveness (30 s period, 5 s timeout, 3 failures) replayed on those passes.

| Stream time | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| 60 s, 12K tokens | loop 48% busy | 1% |
| 120 s, 24K tokens | 92% | 1% |
| 210-330 s | liveness fails 3 of 3 (12-70 s waits), kill at 335 s | 2-3%, no probe failure |
| 1200 s, 240K tokens, 818K chars | | 10% |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server run</summary>

`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --enable-auto-tool-choice` from the CUDA CI image of main `8084f0624d`, one H200 per server, Model Runner V2, no speculative decoding. The PR server runs the same image with `vllm/parser/qwen3.py` first on `PYTHONPATH`. A test logits processor forces the token ids of the cost-per-step stream, closed with `</function></tool_call>`, at temperature 0, so both servers generate the same output; weights, engine, detokenizer, parser and HTTP server are real. The client streams `/v1/chat/completions` with an `Edit` tool, probes `/health` every 0.5 s with a 10 s timeout and samples the API server process's CPU time.

| Run | main: API-server CPU, busy, `/health` p99, timeouts, stream time | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Forced, 64K chars (18,804 tokens) | 41.8 s, 49%, 11.4 ms, 0, 86 s | 4.0 s, 5%, 0.90 ms, 0, 86 s |
| Forced, 256K chars (75,153 tokens) | 394.8 s, 90%, 10 s, 16, 440 s | 26.8 s, 7%, 0.90 ms, 0, 389 s |
| Forced, 64K chars, 8 streams at once | 185.1 s, 96%, 10 s, 12, 193 s | 17.5 s, 13%, 1.8 ms, 0, 132 s |
| Unforced `Write` of a Python module | 0.86 s, 4%, 0.76 ms, 0, 20 s | 0.90 s, 5%, 0.72 ms, 0, 20 s |

- On main at 256K chars, the API server is 100% busy from 148 s. `/health` takes over 1 s from 216 s, and from 287 s until the stream ends at 437 s no probe answers within 10 s. A kubelet liveness probe with a 30 s period, 5 s timeout and 3 failures would restart the container by about 380 s, before the call finishes. With 8 streams at 64K chars, no probe answers from 68 s to the end at 193 s.
- The load also slows the streams on main: 440 s against 389 s at 256K chars, and 193 s against 132 s for the 8 streams.
- Streamed arguments are identical between the two servers in every run, and across the 8 streams. The unforced run's arguments parse as JSON on both.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.**
- `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta` converts the whole raw argument text whenever the open-value extender is inactive: between parameters, and while the open parameter repeats an earlier name (the extender needs the open value to be the last JSON value). Qwen3 sets no `arg_structural_chars`, so every argument delta in those states converts.
- `_qwen3_arg_converter` runs `_PARAM_RE.finditer` over every closed parameter, then `_PARAM_RE.sub` over the whole text to find the open one. After each conversion that extends the streamed JSON, `_param_value_extender` runs both again.
- A model looping on closed parameters keeps every delta in those states, so the cost per delta is linear in the call and the total is quadratic. Merging deltas under load does not bound it, because each merged pass converts the whole text again.

**Change.**
- `_qwen3_parse_params` takes an optional `_ClosedParams` cache, and `Qwen3Parser` binds one per instance into its converter and extender after `super().__init__`, as `Glm47MoeParser` does since #64535. A text that starts with the cached text resumes after the last closed parameter. Any other text parses from the start, and the cache moves forward whenever a scan closes a new parameter.
- A Qwen3 value also closes where the next `<parameter=` begins (the lookahead in `_PARAM_RE`), and holds only while that opener follows. So the cached text runs through that opener, and the scan resumes at the end of the value. Appending text cannot change a parameter closed within the cached text, so resuming is exact. `test_value_closed_by_next_parameter_needs_that_parameter` covers a text that shares the prefix but not the opener.
- The extender's repeated-name check uses the closed names from the same parse in place of a second `finditer`.
- A parser built with a custom `arg_converter` keeps the uncached path (identity check in `__init__`), as in #64535.

**Cost.** What stays linear in the text per conversion is C-level work: `startswith` against the cached text, the join of text outside the parameters for the open-parameter search, and the engine's own argument concatenation. That is the 10% busy at 818K chars in the replay.

**Not in this PR.** #64535 also set `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` for GLM, on the argument that a delta without `>` cannot close a key or value. That does not hold for Qwen3, where a value closes at `<parameter=` before any `>`, and the cache alone passes the replay. Measured with the gate added: 39 us per step at 64K chars for the parameter loop, and 385 us against 1247 us for many distinct parameters.

**Unchanged here and the same on main.**
- Many distinct parameters in one call: each conversion still serializes every parameter, so the cost per step grows with their number (1.2 ms at 64K chars, against 6.2 ms on main).
- A long value under a repeated name: `_param_value_extender` refuses any repeated name, so each delta converts the whole value (11.7 ms per step at 64K chars, against 17.6 ms on main). Letting it accept a repeated last name, as GLM's extender does, is a separate change.
- `MiMoParser` keeps its own converter with the full scan.

**Not a duplicate.** #55497 (open) narrows the parameter-name group of `_PARAM_RE` and `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE`; the cache works with either pattern and the overlap is textual. #59821 (open) edits `Qwen3Parser.__init__` for tool markup in reasoning; whichever lands second rebases. #63277 (open) changes zero-argument calls in the tool adapter. No open PR covers re-parsing closed Qwen3 parameters.

title: [Bugfix][UMBP] Copy every KV cache layout's per-head runs
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Split each layer's page into per-head runs in `data.py`, using the allocator's `compute_layout_strides`.
- Register the same runs in the `embedded.py` bulk path, falling back to per-range copies for a group whose stride doesn't match.
- Fail at startup instead of corrupting KV when a page is split and `kv_cache_layout` is unset.
- Round-trip all 6 layouts through the bulk and range paths in `test_umbp_embedded.py`.

UMBP took `cache.stride(0)` as the block stride and copied one contiguous page per layer, both on the range path in `data.py` and on the bulk path in `_register_load_layouts`, as noted in the review of #61794. Under LHBNC, the default with `ROCM_AITER_FA` and `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`, K and V are head planes spanning every block, so the engine fails at init with `KV region bytes (65536) exceed its stride (32768)`, and under BHLNC heads of different layers interleave inside a block row, so UMBP silently restores the wrong KV. `pytest -q v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_embedded.py -k every_kv_cache_layout` gives 4 failures without the fix and 12 passed with it. On MI350X with Qwen3-0.6B, 16 greedy tokens after a 192-token UMBP hit now match recompute under BHLNC (`TRITON_ATTN` with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BHLNC`) and under AITER shuffle-KV, and stay identical under the default layouts; the batch-invariant tests in `test_mori_token_e2e.py` likewise fail without the fix and pass with it under `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BHLNC` and `LHBNC`. Batch invariance rules out `ROCM_AITER_FA`, so those tests run on `TRITON_ATTN`, and AITER shuffle-KV is covered only by the greedy check above. Other layouts and MLA keep the single-span copy, and refusing LHBNC and BHLNC instead would make UMBP unusable with AITER shuffle-KV, since forcing LBHNC trips the shuffle decode path. LHBNC and BHLNC now issue one bulk range per head instead of one per layer, which I haven't benchmarked yet, and no open PR touches UMBP layout handling.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Give Mamba-1 LoRA layers every row of the batch
author: Manfredss
body:
## Overview

Fixes #61853. With LoRA enabled, `MambaMixer` (Mamba-1, used by `JambaForCausalLM` and `MambaForCausalLM`) gave `x_proj`, `dt_proj` and `out_proj` only part of the batch's rows. The LoRA kernels index rows through the whole batch's mapping, so they went out of bounds. This PR gives those layers a batch-sized input when LoRA is enabled. Root cause and GPU traces: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61853#issuecomment-6516409227

## Claims

- `ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-dev` with `enable_lora=True` starts under the default configuration (MRV2, CUDA graphs) instead of hitting an illegal memory access during CUDA graph capture.
- A LoRA request on Jamba no longer crashes, or silently changes another request's output, when its batch mixes prefill and decode rows.
- No change when LoRA is disabled: that code path is untouched.

## Validation

A40 (SM86), `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505`. `mamba_mixer.py` did not change between that commit and this branch's base. "This PR" means the nightly with this diff applied.

The first commit also added `tests/lora/test_jamba.py`, which was removed at review. It built a seeded random adapter on the Mamba projections and compared a request alone against the same request decoding next to another request's prefill chunks (`check_logprobs_close`).
```
$ python3 -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_jamba.py            # main + the test
E           vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
(EngineCore pid=13570) ERROR 10-30 05:26:53 [core.py:1634] RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
======================== 1 failed, 1 warning in 50.83s =========================

$ python3 -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_jamba.py            # this PR
======================== 1 passed, 2 warnings in 29.28s ========================

$ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 python3 -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_jamba.py   # this PR
======================== 1 passed, 2 warnings in 56.72s ========================
```

The issue's script (`LLM(model="ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-dev", enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=32, max_model_len=4096, seed=42, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85)`, then one greedy `generate`):

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| default (MRV2, CUDA graphs) | illegal memory access | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |
| `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |
| `max_lora_rank=64` | illegal memory access | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |
| `lora_target_modules=in_proj,x_proj,dt_proj,out_proj` | illegal memory access | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |
| `enable_lora=False` | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` | `' Paris, and the capital of France is'` |

Mixed prefill/decode batch: the random adapter, `max_num_batched_tokens=256`, a short request, and a ~2K-token request that prefills in chunks while the short one decodes. "short"/"long" compare each request's tokens in that run against the same request run alone:

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| eager, MRV2 | illegal memory access | short same; long differs at one token |
| eager, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | illegal memory access | short same; long differs at one token |
| CUDA graphs, MRV2 | illegal memory access (the failing test run above) | short same, long same |
| CUDA graphs, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | short same, long differs | short same, long same |
| eager, MRV2, `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` on `_lora_` kernels | `ERROR SUMMARY: 672 errors` (`Invalid __global__ read` in `_lora_expand_kernel`) | `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors` |

On main with CUDA graphs and MRV1, the long request alone gives `' Item 300 is a number. Item 2-30 is a number. ...'`. With this PR, every run gives `' Item 200 is a number. Item 200 is a number. Item 200 is a number. Item 201 is a number. ...'`. The one-token difference in eager mode is in the long request's alone run (`210` where every other run has `201`). It is the same under both runners, and the mixed run matches the CUDA graph runs, so I read it as batch-shape numerics rather than this bug.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** `forward_impl` calls `_ssm_transform` once on the decode rows and once on the prefill rows, so `x_proj` and `dt_proj` each see part of the batch, and `out_proj` sees `num_actual_tokens` rows, without CUDA graph padding. The punica kernels take `token_indices_sorted_by_lora_ids[:x.size(0)]` from `LoRAKernelMeta.meta_args`. Those are row ids of the whole batch sorted by LoRA id, so with fewer rows than the batch the expand kernel loads and stores output rows past the end. `cuda-gdb` on the capture-time core dump stops at `kernel_utils.py:231 tiled_out = tl.load(c_ptr, mask=c_mask)` in `_lora_expand_kernel`. `in_proj` already gets the full `hidden_states`. Mamba-2's `in_proj` and `out_proj` do too.

**Change.** Only when `is_lora_enabled`:
- `_ssm_transform` zero-pads its input to `hidden_states.shape[0]` rows, with the part at its batch offset (decode rows first, then prefill), runs `x_proj`/`dt_proj`, and slices the rows back.
- `out_proj` gets its input padded to `hidden_states.shape[0]` rows and keeps the first `num_actual_tokens`.

The padded copy also replaces the `.contiguous()` calls the LoRA path had. In a mixed batch, `x_proj` and `dt_proj` now run twice over the batch's rows instead of once per part. Both are small (1024→64 and 32→1024 on Jamba-tiny-dev), and only the LoRA path pays this. Slicing uses the metadata's Python ints, so there are no new host syncs.

**Tests.** No new test, per review. No test in `tests/lora` runs a Mamba-1 model, so CI does not cover this path.

**Not a duplicate.** #62553 also targets #61853. It restricts Jamba's LoRA modules to `qkv_proj, o_proj, gate_up_proj, down_proj, in_proj, embed_tokens, lm_head` and attributes the crash to MoE expert LoRA. LoRA on `experts` alone starts fine, and the crash comes from `x_proj`/`dt_proj`. That list avoids the crash by removing LoRA from those layers, and it does not cover `MambaForCausalLM`. This PR keeps LoRA on all of Jamba's modules. I searched open PRs for #61853, `mamba_mixer` + LoRA, and Jamba LoRA.

**Limitations.** Tested on Ampere (SM86) with Jamba-tiny-dev only. `MambaForCausalLM` shares the code path but I did not run a Mamba checkpoint with LoRA. Not tested with TP > 1 or on ROCm.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to trace the fault, write the change and the test, and run the GPU validation. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Clean up both roles on request finish
author: waizuichougou
body:
## Overview

Fix a small but meaningful P2P lifecycle bug in the documented `remote_kv_source` + `remote_decoder` combination. When the upstream source and downstream decoder use different peer sessions, `on_request_finished()` returns after finishing the source-side consumer session, leaving the decoder-side `_kv_to_session` entry until session teardown and potentially delaying server-round cleanup; these stale entries accumulate on long-lived peers.

## Claims

- Finish the source and destination roles independently for dual-role requests.
- Remove the destination request from `_kv_to_session` when the request finishes.
- Avoid calling `finish_request` twice when both roles use the same session and request ID.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py
```

- The added regression test fails on `upstream/main` because the decoder-side
  session is skipped by the early return, and passes with this change.
- `test_manager.py`: 118 passed
- `test_sessions.py`: 150 passed
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering`: 652 passed, 1 skipped
- Pre-commit checks: passed

</details>

## Details

`on_request_finished()` previously selected the source request ID first. With `remote_kv_source` present, it finished the source-side session and returned, so a legal dual-role request never removed its decoder-side `_kv_to_session` entry or finished the session serving that request.

The cleanup now handles both roles independently. The existing `P2PSession.finish_request()` path still performs the client and server role cleanup; the manager only routes each role to the correct session and suppresses duplicate cleanup when both roles share the same session and request ID.

No open PR covering this lifecycle bug was found.

title: [Bugfix] Stop offline beam search at the context limit
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix offline `LLM.beam_search()` raising `VLLMValidationError` when a beam reaches the model's context limit during generation. Return the completed beams instead of submitting another token step.

## Claims

- Mark beams that reach the context limit as completed with `finish_reason="length"`, preserving their tokens, logprobs and cumulative scores.
- Other prompts in the same batch continue generating.
- Candidate ranking and EOS handling remain unchanged.

## Validation

GPU validation used DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B with `max_model_len=128`, prompt lengths of 127, 124 and 16 tokens, and `max_tokens=8`.

- On base `c817cc0f8b`, the regression fails when beam search submits a subsequent request with 128 prompt tokens.
- With the fix, the three prompts return 1, 4 and 8 generated tokens per beam, respectively. Assertions cover token/logprob lengths, cumulative scores and `finish_reason="length"` for beams reaching the context limit.
- Existing beam-search tests: **74 passed, 5 deselected**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass.

Original error:

```text
vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: The decoder prompt (length 128) plus the number of requested output tokens (at least 1) is longer than the maximum model length of 128. Make sure that `max_model_len` is no smaller than the number of text tokens (prompt + requested output tokens).
```

Local validation used the branch's Python source with existing `d14f72c7fe` build artifacts, rather than a full native rebuild. TinyLlama and ROCm were not run locally.

The regression is included in the existing NVIDIA/AMD Samplers CI jobs:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py \
  -k stops_at_context_limit_per_prompt -v
```

## Details

Offline beam search repeatedly submits one-token requests. Previously, candidates remained active after reaching the context limit, so the next request failed input validation.

After the existing candidate sort and beam-width selection, move full-context beams into the completed list with `finish_reason="length"`. This keeps termination independent for each prompt and reuses the existing final ranking. Initial prompts that leave no room for generation remain subject to the existing input validation.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Fix cancellation during request submission
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix a race in the Rust frontend where cancelling a request during submission can send `Abort` before `Add`, allowing the engine to process a request that the caller has already cancelled.

## Claims

- Keep the output stream alive in the spawned Add send task until the send completes, preventing cancellation from enqueueing Abort before Add.
- Add a deterministic regression test that cancels the caller after the send task is spawned but before it runs.

## Validation

Validated on the development machine with Rust 1.95.

- The regression test fails on the base implementation and passes with this change.
- The baseline run used a test-only adaptation for the original `send_request_to_engine()` signature; no production code was changed.
- **154 passed, 0 failed** in the Rust engine-core client test suite.
- Clippy, formatting and applicable pre-commit checks passed.

Baseline regression-test failure:

```text
assertion failed: matches!(abort_rx.try_recv(), Err(mpsc::error::TryRecvError::Empty))
test client::imp::tests::cancelling_add_defers_abort_until_send_completes ... FAILED
```

Validation commands from `rust/`:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client --all-features

cargo clippy --locked -p vllm-engine-core-client --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

The regression test is covered by the existing Rust Frontend Cargo CPU CI job.

## Details

Add is sent by a spawned task that continues running when its caller is cancelled. Previously, cancellation dropped the output stream in the caller and triggered auto-abort while Add could still be pending. The scheduler ignores aborts for unknown request IDs, so an Abort received before Add does not prevent the subsequent Add from starting generation.

Move the output stream into the existing send task and return it after the send completes. If the caller has already been cancelled, the returned stream is dropped when the send task completes, triggering auto-abort. The existing send-error registration rollback remains in place.

title: [Bugfix][Mistral] Carry token ids in stream state for byte-fallback tokens
author: cjackal
body:
## Overview

Fix streaming derender for Tekken-based Mistral tokenizers, where a byte-fallback token in the decode window breaks the client-carried `stream_state`.

The `/v1/responses` corruption originally reported here was fixed by #65118; this PR only covers the derender endpoints.

## Claims

- Streaming `/v1/completions/derender` and `/v1/chat/completions/derender` keep working when the decode window contains a byte-fallback token instead of rejecting the request.
- With a parser configured, chat derender for `MistralTokenizer` now uses the request's `skip_special_tokens`, matching serving after #65118.


## Validation

### Unit test

```shell
python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -v

# 124 passed, 1 xfailed in 76.12s
```

### E2E test

#### Server:

```shell
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B \
  --config-format mistral \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --reasoning-parser mistral \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser mistral \
  --load-format mistral
```

#### Client:

**req.json**

```json
{
  "model": "mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B",
  "stream": false,
  "max_output_tokens": 100,
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "name": "get_weather",
      "description": "Get current weather for a location",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}, "unit": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["location"]
      }
    }
  ],
  "input": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "서울의 날씨가 어때?"},
    {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "udM7soqYx", "name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"location\":\"서울\",\"unit\":\"celsius\"}"},
    {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "udM7soqYx", "output": "서울의 현재 날씨: 22°C, 맑음, 습도 60%"}
  ]
}
```

**Request**

```shell
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d@/tmp/req.json | jq .output[0].content
```

#### Result:

- main: `[{"text": "사용자가 \"서울의 날씨가 어���?\"라고 물어��고, get_weather 함수를 호출해서 ...`
- PR: `[{"text": "사용자가 \"서울의 날씨가 어때?\"라고 물어봤고, get_weather 함수를 호출해서 ...`

## Details

- Root cause: `MistralTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens` returns raw `bytes` for byte-fallback tokens. This happens with `skip_special_tokens=True` too, so it already affects `main`. Streaming derender stored those pieces in `DerenderStreamState.prev_tokens: list[str]`, which goes through JSON between chunks. An incomplete UTF-8 piece can't be carried there.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Honor draft moe/attention backend overrides for MRV2 standalone draft model
author: aoshen02
body:
Proposed title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Honor draft moe/attention backend overrides for MRV2 standalone draft model

## Purpose

With model runner V2, `method: draft_model` (`StandaloneARSpeculator`) silently ignores `moe_backend` and `attention_backend` from `--speculative-config`. The draft inherits the target's `--moe-backend` / `--attention-backend` instead.

- V1 honors all three draft overrides (`moe_backend`, `attention_backend`, `kv_cache_dtype`) through `_create_draft_vllm_config` in `llm_base_proposer.py`, which `draft_model.py` inherits (#37880, #39930).
- The V2 standalone drafter (#43091) never got them. #61240 added `kv_cache_dtype` by hand. #57312 moved the V2 EAGLE/MTP overrides into `SpeculativeConfig.apply_draft_overrides` but did not touch the standalone path.

The fix builds the draft `VllmConfig` from `spec.apply_draft_overrides(self.vllm_config)`, the same way `load_eagle_model` does, and removes the hand-written `kv_cache_dtype` branch. Any new entry in `_DRAFT_VLLM_CONFIG_OVERRIDES` now reaches this drafter too.

`attn_vllm_config` is unchanged. `init_attn_backend` takes each group's backend from the constructed layer (`attn_layers[name].get_attn_backend()`), and the draft layers are built under the overridden config, so their builders already match the draft backend. No metadata builder reads `attention_config.backend` or `kernel_config.moe_backend`. The `kv_cache_dtype` condition is still needed because builders read `cache_config.cache_dtype`.

## Test Plan

- Extended `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_standalone_draft_kv_dtype_override`. It now also parametrizes the draft `moe_backend` / `attention_backend`, and asserts that the draft config gets them when set, keeps the target's when unset, and leaves the target config untouched.
- Ran this test plus `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_moe_backend_override.py` and `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_attention_backend_override.py`.
- E2E on one GB200 GPU with a recent nightly image and the patched `speculator.py` overlaid. Model runner V2 was on, with `ibm-granite/granite-3.0-1b-a400m-base` as both target and draft. Target flags: `--moe-backend triton --attention-backend FLASHINFER`. Speculative config: `{"method": "draft_model", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "moe_backend": "flashinfer_cutlass", "attention_backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}`. Three greedy prompts, 48 tokens each. I read the backends from the loaded target and draft modules.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 35 passed. Without the fix, the 6 new override cases fail with `assert 'flashinfer_cutlass' == 'triton'`.
- E2E:

| | target attn / MoE | draft attn / MoE | accepted / drafted |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | FLASHINFER / TRITON | FLASHINFER / TRITON (overrides ignored) | 108 / 108 |
| after | FLASHINFER / TRITON | TRITON_ATTN / FLASHINFER_CUTLASS | 108 / 111 |

  Greedy outputs are identical in both runs. The small acceptance drop is expected now that the draft runs different kernels than the target.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the standalone draft config path. #62193 adds a `batch_invariant` entry to `_DRAFT_VLLM_CONFIG_OVERRIDES`. This PR does not include it, but once that lands, the entry will also apply to the standalone drafter.
- Possible overlap: #60989 (AR speculator refactor / draft CUDA graph) edits `standalone_ar/speculator.py` but not `load_draft_model`, so any conflict should be trivial. #63205 (speculator config classes) adds `standalone_ar/config.py` and edits `vllm/config/speculative.py` next to `apply_draft_overrides`, but not the method itself. I don't expect a semantic conflict with either.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Pin FlashKDA and FlashMLA with NaN fixes
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64758: under load, some Kimi-K3 requests turn into streams of token 0 (`!!!!`) until `max_tokens`. This PR moves the FlashKDA and FlashMLA pins to commits with two kernel fixes: https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/16 and https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/pull/41.

Both kernel PRs are merged, and the pins point to their upstream merge commits.

## Claims

- FlashKDA prefill no longer copies a NaN from one request into other requests of the same batch. On Kimi-K3 with one injected NaN request, other decodes made bad drop from 96/240 to 0/240.
- FlashMLA's SM90 dense decode kernel now waits for the previous kernel (PDL) before it reads the query. A forced race gives NaN in 49/50 calls on stock and 0/50 with the fix.
- On the natural burst reproducer from the issue, bad requests went from 14 on stock to 0 with both fixes.
- No measurable end-to-end performance cost on Kimi-K3.

## Validation

All runs: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` @ `f831ab66`, 2 x 8 H200, TP8 x PP2 over InfiniBand, V2 model runner, stock flags from the issue, vLLM `063c0c6` (PR #61867 head). The fixes were applied by swapping only `_flashkda_C` and `_flashmla_C`.

Burst reproducer (`repro_natural_burst.py` in the issue), fresh server per arm, same seed:

| | Stock | FlashKDA fix | FlashKDA fix + FlashMLA fix (no-PDL variant) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run length | 12.5 min | 10.8 min | 25.0 min |
| First-NaN events | 2 | 1 | 0 (about 2.6 expected, P about 0.08) |
| Bad requests | 14 (groups of 2 and 13) | 1 | 0 |

The last arm used the FlashMLA variant that launches without PDL. The `griddepcontrol.wait` variant pinned here was checked with the forced kernel race (49/50 to 0/50, bit-identical outputs) and in the performance A/B below, but not on the burst reproducer.

With one NaN injected into one request by a debug hook, stock made 96 of 240 other decodes bad and the FlashKDA fix made 0. GSM8K was 0.945 on stock and 0.947 with the fix.

Performance, stock against both fixes, one server start per arm:

| Metric | Stock | Both fixes | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| TPOT, batch 1 (ms) | 15.51 | 15.50 | -0.1% |
| TPOT, batch 8 (ms) | 26.38 | 26.31 | -0.2% |
| TPOT, batch 32 (ms) | 44.20 (0.86) | 45.00 (1.3) | +1.8%, within noise |
| TPOT, batch 64 (ms) | 58.17 (3.4) | 59.38 (4.6) | +2.1%, within noise |
| TTFT, 1k-token prompt (ms) | 225.9 | 222.4 | -1.6% |
| TTFT, 8k-token prompt (ms) | 858.2 | 858.7 | +0.1% |
| TTFT, 64k-token prompt (ms) | 5046 | 5054 | +0.2% |
| GSM8K (5-shot) | 0.947 | 0.948 | +0.1% |

Each value is the median of 3 repetitions; brackets give the max-min spread where it matters. Both arms use `-O3 -DNDEBUG` builds whose SASS is identical to the wheel's; the only difference is the two patches. Three repetitions can neither show nor rule out a 1-2% cost at batch 32-64.

Decode: random 32-token prompts, 1,024 output tokens with `ignore_eos`, greedy, 4/16/64/128 prompts at concurrency 1/8/32/64. Prefill: `vllm bench serve` with random 1k/8k/64k-token prompts, 1 output token, concurrency 1, median TTFT. GSM8K: 5-shot, greedy, 1,319 questions, once per arm.

Kernel-level reproducers and tests are in the two kernel PRs.

## Details

**Spread (confirmed): FlashKDA.** Prefill works in chunks of 16 rows. For a sequence's last, partial chunk, it read `beta` and `v` from the rows after the sequence end (the next request in the batch, or the next head) and cancelled them by multiplying by zero. `0 * NaN` is NaN. vLLM runs the decode rows of a mixed step through this kernel together with the prefills, so one NaN request could hit up to 15 decodes and one prefill per step. The fix selects 0 for those rows.

**First NaN (strong suspect, not proven): FlashMLA.** K3's decode path runs `fused_kimi_k3_mla_decode_q_concat_kv_cache_insert`, which writes the query and triggers PDL completion, then FlashMLA's SM90 dense decode kernel. That kernel is launched with PDL but never called `griddepcontrol.wait`, so it could read a query buffer (`torch.empty`) that was not written yet. The fix adds the wait after the prologue. We have not shown that this race causes the natural events; one natural event appeared after the attention output, which it does not explain.

Pin contents:

- FlashKDA: `47fc9fe` (current pin, on upstream `dev`) to `9d9e928`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashKDA#16. No other upstream change comes in.
- FlashMLA: `d1a1c92` (current pin) to `847ef30` on upstream `main`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashMLA#41. It also brings vllm-project/FlashMLA#39, a one-line fix per kernel in the SM100 sparse decode head64 kernels.

Scope and limits:

- The FlashMLA change affects every model that uses the SM90 dense decode kernel, not only Kimi-K3. It adds one wait per CTA and leaves outputs bit-identical. We only measured Kimi-K3.
- CI cannot run Kimi-K3 (two 8 x H200 nodes). The validation above was done outside CI.
- vLLM code is unchanged; only the two pins in `cmake/external_projects/` move.

title: [Bugfix] Read generate usage.prompt_tokens in non-streaming derender
author: nien-hui
body:
## Overview

Non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` return `usage.prompt_tokens: 0` when the request omits `prompt_tokens`, because they never read the generate response's `usage`. They now fall back to the generate response's `usage.prompt_tokens`, as the streaming paths already do. Fixes #64778

## Claims

- Non-streaming chat derender without `prompt_tokens` returns the generate response's `usage.prompt_tokens` (10) instead of 0.
- Non-streaming completions derender without `prompt_tokens` returns the sum of the generate responses' `usage.prompt_tokens` (1 + 5 = 6) instead of 0.

Both derender test files, with this PR cherry-picked onto main `349b21487a` (2026-11-04); the xfail is the existing `triples` case:

```bash

```

`224 passed, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 469.94s (0:07:49)`

<details>
<summary>pytest summary (progress dots and warnings omitted)</summary>

```

XFAIL tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_matches_batch_reasoning[triples] - <think> leaks into reasoning when it shares a multi-token delta with reasoning text (vllm#55195)
224 passed, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 469.94s (0:07:49)
```

</details>

Not tested: encoder-decoder and multimodal prompts, where the generate count includes encoder tokens; no such model was run.
Not tested: `test_derender_parity.py`, which starts a GPU server; no GPU was free.
No model eval: the change only sets the `usage` field of the derender response; token IDs and text are untouched.
The new tests run in the `entrypoints-integration-api-server` CI step.

## Details

**Root cause.** `ServingDerender.derender_chat_response` sets `prompt_tokens` to `request.prompt_tokens`, else 0, and `OnlineDerenderer._derender_completion` expands an omitted list to `[0] * n`. Neither reads the generate response's `usage`, which `/inference/v1/generate` sets on every non-streaming response. The `prompt_tokens` docstrings on `DerenderChatRequest` and `DerenderCompletionRequest` documented the 0.

**Fix.** New `resolve_prompt_tokens(prompt_tokens, usage)` returns the request value if set (0 included), else `usage.prompt_tokens`, else 0 when `usage` is absent, the order `derender_chat_stream`, `_derender_chat_stream_parsed` and `derender_completion_stream` already used inline. All five sites call it, completions once per generate response, and the two docstrings, which `derenderer.md` includes, state this order; the stream sites' `or 0` is dropped because `UsageInfo.prompt_tokens` is a non-optional `int`.

**Related PRs.**

- #64041 — adds `reasoning_tokens` and `cached_tokens` to chat derender usage. It edits the `UsageInfo` in `derender_chat_response` next to this change and keeps the `else 0`; the two merge cleanly.
- #43606 — added the `/derender` endpoints. It introduced the `else 0`, the `[0] * n` default and the "defaults to 0 if omitted" docstrings this PR changes.
- #47301 — added streaming derender. It introduced the request-then-generate-usage order that `resolve_prompt_tokens` copies.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, write the fix and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and reran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][CUDA] Use CUDA memory accounting for integrated GPUs on WSL
author: eugr
body:
## Overview

Fix model startup on NVIDIA integrated GPUs under WSL by using CUDA-reported free memory rather than WSL guest RAM availability.

## Claims

- Apply the CUDA-on-WSL exception in the shared `device_memory_info()` helper, covering memory snapshots and extensible KV-cache sizing.
- Preserve native Linux UMA accounting, discrete GPUs, and non-CUDA platforms.
- Extend the existing helper regression test and explicitly select the native environment in the reclaimable-memory sizing test.

## Validation

Original hardware validation was performed by the human submitter using upstream vLLM containers with and without the patch on an ASUS ProArt P16 RTX Spark laptop, Ubuntu under WSL, 128 GB memory with a 64 GB GPU carveout.

This merge was checked locally with the established precompiled test environment and mocked hardware memory reports; GPU profiling and a fresh WSL model run were not performed. No accuracy or throughput changes are claimed.

## Details

The integrated-GPU correction normally replaces CUDA free memory with `psutil.virtual_memory().available` to include reclaimable native Linux system memory. Under WSL, guest RAM does not represent CUDA's allocation budget, particularly with a GPU memory carveout, so this substitution can reject a model that fits.

Upstream [#65413](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65413) extracted the correction into `device_memory_info()`. This PR retains that refactor and applies the existing cached CUDA+WSL condition in the shared helper. Native UMA behavior and the helper's callers remain intact. No options, dependencies, explicit synchronization, or transfers are added.

Duplicate-work searches before opening found no other open fix for `WSL UMA` or `WSL psutil`. title: [Bugfix][Attention] Bound SM100 decode indexer logits with query-row chunks
author: Pb314314
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On SM100, compute the sparse indexer's decode logits in chunks of query rows, each at most `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (default 2 GiB), instead of one tensor for all decode rows of a step. This applies to every model that uses this indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, V4, V4.1, GLM-5.x (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), HY-V4), with either the FP8 (default) or the MXFP4 indexer cache.

It removes most of the memory these logits take at long context, and it unblocks the CUDA graph refactor (#63406), whose wide decode graphs would otherwise hold the full logits.

### Motivation

The sparse indexer scores every cached KV position of a request for each query row and keeps the top-k (512 for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, 2048 for V3.2 and GLM-5.x). On SM100, the decode scores come from one DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` call, which writes a dense BF16 tensor of shape `[decode rows, W]`:

- `decode rows` = requests × (1 + speculative tokens);
- `W` = `max_model_len / compress_ratio`, fixed by the model length, not by the requests' actual context.

At 1M context with 8192 decode rows this tensor is 16 GiB, and main's memory profile reserves it plus an FP32 copy (48 GiB). The copy is no longer made at runtime, since persistent top-k reads BF16 (#64138). The tensor costs memory in two places:

- **Eager and PIECEWISE steps** (mixed prefill + decode steps, and decode steps wider than the largest FULL graph) allocate it at runtime. So the memory profile reserves the worst case, and that memory is taken from the KV cache.
- **FULL CUDA graphs** allocate it inside the graph memory pool, which grows with the widest captured decode graph. #63406 captures decode graphs up to the full `max_num_seqs`.

### Change

When a step's decode logits would exceed the budget, the decode rows are split into balanced, 16-row-aligned chunks. Each chunk runs the same operations as the unchunked path on its own rows, and writes its rows of the shared top-k output:

1. DeepGEMM schedule metadata for the chunk;
2. logits;
3. V4.1 candidate-block selection or masking;
4. top-k.

Rows are independent, so nothing is merged across chunks. A step that fits the budget runs the existing single call unchanged, and so do prefill rows (already chunked by `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`). The memory profile reserves one BF16 chunk instead of every decode row plus an FP32 copy.

## Results

In every table, **Baseline** means decode logits are not chunked (main, or budget `0` on the same build), and **After PR** means this PR with the default 2 GiB budget. Unless noted: one GB200 node (4 GPUs), FP8 KV cache, DSpark with 7 speculative tokens for DeepSeek-V4.1, MTP with 5 for GLM-5.3, and ShareGPT prompts with their recorded output lengths. Memory numbers come from the startup log and are deterministic.

### Memory

On main (default memory settings, extensible KV cache):

| Model and config | | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FP8 indexer cache (default), 1M, TP4+EP, `max_num_seqs` 512 | memory-profile activation peak | 26.31 GiB | 5.23 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 49.67 GiB | **86.02 GiB (+73%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, dense candidate consumers (`indexer_sparse_logits=false`), 1M, `max_num_seqs` 1024 | memory-profile activation peak | 49.49 GiB | 4.41 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 7.62 GiB | **86.51 GiB** |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (FP8 indexer cache), 256K, TP4+EP | memory-profile activation peak | 11.39 GiB | 4.37 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 38.93 GiB | **51.25 GiB (+32%)** |

With #63406 (decode graphs up to `max_num_seqs`), CUDA graph memory per GPU, KV cache fixed:

| Model and config | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FP8 indexer cache, 1M, TP4+EP, 512 seqs | 22.36 GiB | **12.36 GiB** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, 1M, TP4+EP, 512 seqs | 22.35 GiB | **12.35 GiB** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, 1M, DP4+EP, 1024 seqs per rank | 39.70 GiB | **15.71 GiB** |

For GLM-5.3 at 256K with #63406, the widest decode graph (4092 rows) already fits the budget, so graph memory is unchanged (12.35 GiB). The smaller profile reservation still raises its KV cache from 590,464 to 745,984 tokens.

### Performance

Output tok/s; each cell lists every server launch, and the change is between the means. Launches of the two versions run on the same node unless noted.

| Setting | Workload | Decode rows per step | Baseline | After PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #63406, V4.1 FP8, TP4+EP | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 13114 / 12939 | 13008 / 12834 | −0.8% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 4045 / 4055 | 4050 / 3994 | −0.7% |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4, TP4+EP ¹ | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 12828 / 12938 / 12808 | 12858 / 12759 / 12840 | −0.3% |
| | 256 concurrent | up to 2048, chunked | 11803 / 11772 | 11833 / 11848 | +0.4% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 4091 / 4106 / 4076 | 4135 / 4097 / 3958 | −0.7% |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4, DP4+EP, AV ² | random 128 in / 512 out, 2048 concurrent | up to ~4096 per rank, chunked | 57855 / 55920 | 56854 / 56687 | −0.2% |
| | same, 4096 concurrent | up to 8192 per rank, chunked | 62059 / 61396 | 61297 / 61948 | −0.2% |
| #63406, GLM-5.3, TP4+EP | 256 concurrent | up to 1536 | 7155 | 7034 | −1.7% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 192 | 2569 | 2597 | +1.1% |
| main, V4.1 FP8, TP4+EP | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 5799 / 5920 | 5890 / 6067 | +2.0% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 3509 / 3643 | 3548 / 3648 | +0.6% |
| main, V4.1 MXFP4, dense consumers, 1024 seqs | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 5666 | 5550 | −2.0% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 3324 | 3398 | +2.2% |
| main, GLM-5.3, TP4+EP | 256 concurrent | up to 1536 | 3966 | 4043 | +1.9% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 192 | 2368 | 2409 | +1.7% |

¹ Budget sweep below; KV fixed at 16 GiB. ² Adaptive verification on, KV fixed at 16 GiB.

Steps that do not chunk run the same code as Baseline, so single-launch differences of about ±2% in those rows are run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Other runs: long outputs, and a worst-case graph setup</summary>

Long outputs on main (V4.1 MXFP4, default candidate logits, 1M, TP4+EP, random 1K in / 4K out, one launch each):

| Concurrency | Chunked | Baseline | After PR | Change | TPOT p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | no | 5280 | 4873 | −7.7% | 5.39 → 5.14 ms |
| 128 | no | 9972 | 9713 | −2.6% | 10.45 → 10.60 ms |
| 256 | yes | 4596 | 4488 | −2.3% | 46.2 → 49.0 ms |

The 32 and 128 rows run identical code in both versions, so they bound the noise of these short runs.

Worst case: `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with sparse capture sizes `[8, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]` on main, V4.1 MXFP4, adaptive verification, KV fixed at 16 GiB, random 128 in. Every mixed step runs the whole model eagerly, so each extra chunk adds host launches.

| Topology | Workload | Baseline | After PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP4+EP, 1024 seqs per rank | 2048 concurrent, 512 out | 39226 / 40143 | 37518 / 36456 | −6.8% |
| | 4096 concurrent, 512 out | 34566 / 35732 | 24452 / 34633 | −16% (−1.5% without the 24452 launch) |
| TP4+EP, 1024 seqs | 1024 concurrent, 1024 out | 17054 / 15729 | 15973 / 16658 | −0.5% |

Deployments with this setup and workload should use the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, or raise `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (e.g. to 4096). Graph memory in this setup: DP4 36.46 → 12.44 GiB, TP4 32.08 → 10.12 GiB per GPU. With 2048 seqs, TP4 Baseline cannot start on main (its profile reserves 96 GiB for decode logits).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Choosing the 2 GiB default</summary>

#63406, V4.1 MXFP4, TP4+EP, 512 seqs, KV fixed at 16 GiB; one column per budget.

| | Baseline (0) | 1 GiB | **2 GiB** | 4 GiB | 6 GiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph memory | 22.35 GiB | 10.36 GiB | **12.35 GiB** | 14.35 GiB | 20.35 GiB |
| CUDA graph memory, adaptive verification | 22.51 GiB | 10.52 GiB | **12.52 GiB** | 14.51 GiB | 20.51 GiB |
| 512 concurrent | 12828 / 12938 / 12808 | – | 12858 / 12759 / 12840 (−0.3%) | 12906 / 12926 (+0.3%) | 12931 / 12757 (−0.3%) |
| 32 concurrent | 4091 / 4106 / 4076 | – | 4135 / 4097 / 3958 (−0.7%) | 4050 / 4095 (−0.6%) | 4114 / 4084 (0.0%) |
| adaptive verification, 512 concurrent | 16573 / 16815 / 16690 | – | 16149 / 17112 / 16944 (+0.3%) | 16819 / 17007 (+1.3%) | 16495 / 17060 (+0.5%) |
| adaptive verification, 512 concurrent, 9216 prompts | 18121 / 17942 / 17971 | 18059 / 18209 / 17912 (+0.3%) | 18082 / 17990 / 18041 (+0.1%) | – | – |
| adaptive verification, 128 concurrent | 10037 / 10134 / 10045 | 10245 / 10250 / 10098 (+1.2%) | 10224 / 10179 / 10150 (+1.1%) | – | – |

2 GiB is the smallest budget that leaves every step with up to 1024 decode rows at 1M (128 requests × 8 tokens) unchunked. 1 GiB saves 2 GiB more but chunks from 512 rows. 4 and 6 GiB keep 2 and 8 GiB more graph memory without a measurable gain.
</details>

### Correctness

**Chunked vs single call, on the real kernels.** A standalone check on GB200 runs DeepGEMM logits, candidate selection or masking, and the `auto` or `persistent` top-k. It compares chunking against a single call for FP8 and MXFP4 caches, 1000–8192 rows, W from 256K to 1M, and chunks down to ≤ 64 rows (which take the cooperative top-k and an FP32 upcast):

- chunked logits are bit-identical to the single call;
- candidate blocks are identical;
- the selected top-k values match an exact `torch.topk` on the same logits in every row (indices may differ only among tied scores).

The same check shows that main's single call returns a wrong top-k once one call exceeds 2^32 logits elements. At 1M context this happens above about 4094 rows: 4097 of 8192 rows were wrong, for both cache types and both top-k backends, while the logits themselves were correct. At the default budget a chunk holds at most 2^30 elements, so this PR avoids it. A separate fix for the top-k kernel's addressing will follow.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions, greedy). Same build launched repeatedly varies by up to ~1.8 points.

| Setting | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|
| #63406, V4.1 FP8 | 0.904 / 0.901 | 0.898 / 0.899 |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4 | 0.900 / 0.904 / 0.897 | 0.913 / 0.897 / 0.895 |
| #63406, GLM-5.3 | 0.907 | 0.904 |
| main, V4.1 FP8 | 0.895 / 0.903 | 0.911 / 0.894 |
| main, V4.1 MXFP4, dense consumers | 0.897 | 0.893 |
| main, GLM-5.3 | 0.916 | 0.918 |

GSM8K runs 256 concurrent requests (up to 2048 decode rows for V4.1), so these runs exercise chunked steps.

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "decode_chunk or sparse_indexer or persistent"` on GB200: 348 passed, 4 skipped. The new tests check that chunks cover every row once, respect alignment, balance and the budget, and handle zero, fitting and invalid budgets.

## Details

- **Where it applies:** SM100, top-k backend `auto` or `persistent`, top-k ∈ {512, 1024, 2048}, no decode or prefill context parallelism. Both indexer cache types, and V4.1's candidate source and masked candidate consumer layers. V4.1's compact sparse consumers (`indexer_sparse_logits`) already score only candidate blocks and are unchanged.
- **Mixed steps:** chunking depends only on the number of decode rows, so it also applies to the decode rows of a mixed prefill + decode step; prefill rows are unchanged. These steps run PIECEWISE or eager, where each extra chunk adds a few kernel launches.
- **When to raise the budget:** a step chunks once its decode rows exceed `budget / (2 bytes × W)` on the widest indexer layer (1024 rows at 1M with the default). If running requests × (1 + speculative tokens) is usually above that and the KV cache is not the bottleneck, raise `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (for example to 4096). At 1M, keep it below 8192, where one call would exceed 2^32 elements; `0` turns chunking off.
- **Disaggregated prefill/decode:** prefill rows are unchanged, and prefill instances also get the smaller reservation. The decode instance produces the first token, so time to first token includes one decode step, which pays the chunking cost above if that step is wider than the limit.
- **Interaction with #64580:** #64580 would make SM100 logits FP32 again by default. Whichever PR lands second must pass the logits dtype to the chunk's `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` call and size the budget by the logits element size.
- **Models measured:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (FP8 and MXFP4 indexer caches) and GLM-5.3-NVFP4. DeepSeek-V3.2, V4 and HY-V4 run the same indexer code but were not measured end to end; at their usual context lengths (≤ 256K) decode steps chunk only above 4096+ rows, so the main change for them is the smaller memory-profile reservation.
- **Not covered:** decode context parallelism, non-default top-k backends (e.g. `deep_select`), the V4.1 GB300 specialized decode path, and indexers with their own implementation (GLM-5-Next, MiniMax-M3) keep their current path.

## Not a duplicate

#62169 chunks the SM90 / SM120 uniform decode path by request, and excludes SM100 varlen decode. No other open PR bounds the SM100 decode logits.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Disconnect a peer whose registration fails
author: nilig
body:
## Overview

When this side's registration of a peer's NIXL agent fails, `_poll_registration` only marks the local connection dead. The peer has registered us and keeps its session waiting for our ack. Our next connection to it is routed into that session, which acks our ConnectMsg without sending its own: our session becomes `ready` without registering the peer, the peer never gets our ack and queues its `LookupRespMsg`s, and each lookup on that session waits out the 8 s lookup timeout. Send a best-effort `DisconnectMsg`, as the other teardown paths do, so the peer drops that session and the next connection gets a fresh handshake. Record the failure as a data-plane fault so the reap applies the reconnect backoff.

The routing of a reconnect into the peer's existing connection is discussed on #64060; this change does not depend on how that is resolved.

## Claims

- A failed registration sends a best-effort `DisconnectMsg`. When it is delivered, the peer drops its half-open session, and the next connection does a fresh handshake in which this side registers the peer again.
- A failed registration counts as a data-plane fault, so repeated failures use the existing reconnect backoff: no wait after the first, then 1, 2, 4 ... 60 s.
- No transport change. A reconnect that reaches the peer while its ROUTER still holds the old routing id is still dropped (#63740). If the `DisconnectMsg` is lost, for example when a handover drops the displaced pipe's messages as in #64060, the half-open state remains.

## Validation

New `TestBidirectionalManager::test_failed_registration_drops_the_peer_session`: two managers built with their constructors from `make_offloading_config()`, on real `NixlTransport` and `ZmqTransport`, with only the NIXL agent faked; A's agent fails `add_remote_agent`. It checks that B drops its session for A and that A counts the failure as a data-plane fault. It does not reconnect: whether a reconnect gets through depends on #63740, so the backoff that follows a repeated failure is covered by `data_plane_fault` here and by the existing `TestReconnectBackoff` tests. `TestConnectHandshake::test_failed_registration_rejects_peer` gains two assertions: a `DisconnectMsg` is sent, and `data_plane_fault` is set.

CPU, `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:cb9bc64f0f038c2c2ebf13b31248fb87aca40c356c3d20f363be087cfcff1fcd`:

```
# main's session.py
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py \
    -k "test_failed_registration_rejects_peer or test_failed_registration_drops_the_peer_session"
E           AssertionError: B kept its session for A
E       AssertionError: assert 'connect' == 'disconnect'
2 failed

# this change, 10 runs in fresh processes
2 passed (10 of 10)

# full P2P suite, this change, 3 runs
362 passed
```

`test_lookup_expiry_allows_zmq_reconnect` is intermittent on main (#63740): run alone in 10 fresh processes, it failed 7 of 10 on main and 7 of 10 with this change, each time with `Failed: P2P session did not reach the expected state`.

The same scenario with a diagnostic script (not part of this PR) on real ZMQ transports, the managers' `NixlTransport` replaced by fakes and A's registration of B always failing, varying the pause between the failure and A's next request:

| build | pause | A's lookup | A->B ready | B->A session | A's registration attempts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0 s | MISS | False (reconnect dropped) | not ready | 1 |
| main | 0.5 s, 2 s | RETRY | True | not ready | 1 |
| this change | 0 s | MISS | False (reconnect dropped) | absent | 1 |
| this change | 0.5 s, 2 s | MISS | absent | absent | 2 |

GPU: engines A (consumer), B (faulted source) and C (healthy source), each one Qwen3-0.6B on one H200, all on one node over mlx5 RDMA, NIXL 1.5.0. Image: nightly `3966924d` + #64256, #64251 and #64501, whose `session.py` is identical to main's; "this change" mounts this PR's `session.py` over it, and both builds share the image's other files. Every engine's P2P file hashes were checked, and every engine's restart count was checked against the restart the case injects.

With `UCX_TLS=all`, which re-enables the `rc_gda` lanes that #63498 excludes, A's registration of B's replacement B2 fails on every attempt. These timings measure requests naming a peer A cannot use, including local fallback; B2 made no successful pulls in these runs. Same node, builds alternated:

| build | fault on B, then replacement B2 | runs | requests to B2, p50 / max | A: failed registrations / lookup timeouts | B2: queued `LookupRespMsg` / `cannot store chunks` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | graceful delete | 2 | 4.373-4.377 / 8.32 s | 12 / 11 | 448-451 / 106-116 |
| this change | graceful delete | 3 | 0.025-0.028 / 0.042-0.043 s | 8 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| this change | force delete | 1 | 0.027 / 0.043 s | 8 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

With this change, each of A's 8 failed registrations is followed in the same second by B2 ending its session on `peer disconnected`, and A's attempts are spaced by the backoff: 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 s, plus the handshake.

Without `UCX_TLS=all`, this change, one run each. "Pulled" means A submitted a P2P load for the request:

| fault on B | requests to C pulled | requests to B during the fault, p50 / max | requests to B or B2 pulled after recovery | engine restarts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SIGSTOP for 60 s, then SIGCONT | 620 of 620 | 0.021 / 4.9 s | 244 of 244 | none |
| kill, restart at the same IP | 511 of 511 | 0.024 / 0.088 s | 400 of 400 | B once, from the kill |
| rolling replacement | 594 of 594 | 0.048 / 0.076 s | 400 of 400 | none |
| graceful delete, replacement B2 | 844 of 844 | 0.021 / 0.034 s | 400 of 400 | none |
| force delete, replacement B2 | 825 of 825 | 0.022 / 0.034 s | 400 of 400 | none |

Under SIGSTOP, one lookup sent as B stopped ended on the 8 s lookup timeout; the 4.9 s maximum is over requests issued during the fault. No engine logged a `UnicodeDecodeError` or an engine-core fatal error in any run; the only tracebacks were `EngineDeadError` from vLLM's shutdown when a pod was deleted, in both builds.

No `LLM`/`RemoteOpenAIServer` regression test is included: reaching this path end to end needs a NIXL registration failure, which the CPU tests inject by faking the NIXL agent and the GPU runs above force with `UCX_TLS=all`. Asking maintainers to accept that test scope.

## Details

The failure is recorded like an unacknowledged abort (`_abort_ack_fault`): `data_plane_fault` returns it, and the reap's existing backoff takes over. The `DisconnectMsg` is best-effort, like the other teardown paths: a send failure is suppressed and the connection is marked dead without waiting for the peer.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Fix bench mm-processor crash with HF datasets
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

`vllm bench mm-processor --dataset-name hf`, the HuggingFace example in `docs/benchmarking/cli.md`, crashes with `AttributeError`. This one-line fix closes the same kind of gap as #56300, which fixed random-mm sampling.

## Claims

`bench mm-processor` runs on HF datasets. `bench throughput` and `bench serve` behave as before.

## Validation

```bash
vllm bench mm-processor --model Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --dataset-name hf \
  --dataset-path lmarena-ai/VisionArena-Chat --hf-split train --num-prompts 5 --seed 0 \
  --load-format dummy --enforce-eager --disable-tqdm --output-json out.json

pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py -k hf_dataset_with_mm_processor
```

```text
# before
AttributeError: 'Namespace' object has no attribute 'hf_name'    # both commands

# after
bench: exit 0, completed 5, failed 0, 5 encoder calls
pytest: 1 passed
```

The bench ran on an L4 with real VisionArena data and dummy weights, on a pinned wheel with the same bug and the same one-line change. The new test uses the real `VisionArenaDataset` with only the HF download stubbed, and checks for text and image chat prompts.

## Details

`get_samples` reads `args.hf_name` for every HF dataset. `bench mm-processor` has no `--hf-name` flag, and `_to_serve_args` backfills its other missing flags but not this one. With `None`, datasets fall back to `--dataset-path`.

`bench mm-processor` still accepts only its listed dataset paths, so local copies stay unsupported. I found no open PR or issue for this.

title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3.1] Reserve MSA Q8KV4 prefill workspace
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60791 item 7: reserve MSA Q8KV4 prefill split partials at model load so profiling counts them before KV cache sizing.

## Claims

- Share one reservation per `(device, topk_blocks, max_tokens, num_q_heads)` key per process, avoiding 60 layers × 8.6 GiB.
- Net -70 lines, mostly deleting the SM107 builder path and metadata plumbing.

## Validation

- B300: `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py` — **53 passed**; the 3 CUDA >=13.4-gated Q8KV4 prefill tests (shared workspace reservation, Triton agreement) **passed** with toolkit **13.4.1**.
- 4x B300 serving, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, NVFP4 KV, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`: DEP4+EP startup on all ranks, KV cache **2,027,507 tokens**, `vllm bench serve` **100/100** requests; PP2 with `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` progresses past MSA.
- Pre-commit passed.

## Details

vLLM memory profiling skips attention, so Q8KV4 prefill split partials allocated after KV-pool sizing cause startup OOM (60 layers × ~8.6 GiB if reserved per layer); see [#60791 item 7](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60791) for the full repro.

Reserving at attention-impl initialization includes the workspace in the profiling snapshot, with per-layer impls sharing one reservation through a process-local `WeakValueDictionary`; the old builder ran after KV sizing, so dropping its SM107 gate alone would not help.

- **Sleep/wake:** With cumem enabled, single-locality-domain GPUs offload/restore the runtime-pool workspace; on multi-domain Rubin, the pinned [MSA library](https://github.com/vllm-project/MSA) uses raw driver allocations that stay resident during sleep—pre-existing on main, unchanged here; follow-up belongs in MSA.
- **Scope:** NVFP4 prefill only; BF16-KV prefill still allocates per call (kernel follow-up); the PP2 FlashInfer MoE autotune startup failure remains separate and unresolved ([#60791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60791)).
- **No duplicate:** [#60186](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60186) covers a different allocation site at KV init; no open PR covers #60791 item 7.

AI assistance (Kimi Code CLI) was used. The submitting human reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.
