title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Apply DeepSeek-V4 compressor and wo_a adapters
author: HollowMan6
body:
## Overview

Since #53361 ("Support LoRA for DeepSeek V4") and #55897, DeepSeek-V4 has declared `SupportsLoRA`. On the CUDA path, though, adapters on the compressor's `wkv`/`wgate` and on `wo_a` are silently dropped. Both projections run their GEMM directly on the base weight, which bypasses the LoRA wrapper.

#57245 already fixed this for DeepSeek-V4.1. It added LoRA wrappers plus V4.1-local copies of the two layers those wrappers match. This PR builds V4's projections as the same layers and moves the layers from V4.1 into V4, so the two models share one copy.

## Claims

- Adapters on `compressor.wkv`/`wgate`, `indexer.compressor.wkv`/`wgate` and `wo_a` now apply on all three V4 CUDA attention backends (FlashMLA, FlashInfer SM100, FlashInfer SM120).
- Without LoRA, every changed V4 projection runs the same kernels on the same inputs as before, so outputs are bit-identical (the tests assert this).
- FlashInfer RopeQuant (SM100) is turned off when LoRA is enabled. It writes only FP8 attention output, and the `wo_a` adapter needs the BF16 input.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 behavior is unchanged. It now imports the two layers from V4 instead of keeping copies that matched V4's apart from import paths.

## Validation

Run on an H20 (SM90) with:

```bash
pytest -v tests/lora/test_layers.py -k "dsv4 or grouped_o_projection or compressor_projection"
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py
```

| Test | With this PR | Fix reverted (`attention.py`, `nvidia/flashmla.py`, `nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` from `main`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_dsv4_compressor_projections_apply_lora_with_fp32_output` (main and indexer compressor) | passed | failed: adapter check, `Mismatched elements: 3049 / 8704` |
| `test_dsv4_grouped_o_projection_applies_each_tokens_adapter` (all three backends) | passed | failed: adapter check, ~35% of elements mismatched |
| `test_dsv4_rope_quant_is_off_with_lora` | passed | n/a |
| Existing V4.1 tests, now built from the shared V4 layers: `test_grouped_o_projection_*` (3 BF16 + 2 fully sharded), `test_compressor_projection_applies_lora_with_fp32_output` (4), `test_dsv41_gemm_rs_is_not_set_up_with_lora` | 10 passed | 10 passed |
| `test_grouped_o_projection_applies_each_tokens_adapter`, FP8 `wo_a` (3) | not runnable here* | not runnable here* |
| `test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` (stubs V4.1's `wo_a`) | 35 passed | n/a |
| `test_compressor_kv_cache.py` (V4.1 compressor) | 149 passed, 26 failed | n/a |

\* That H20 has no DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum` ("DeepGEMM backend is unavailable"). The error comes from the baseline call, before any LoRA code runs. CI's H200 `LoRA` step has DeepGEMM and runs these cases.

The 26 `test_compressor_kv_cache.py` failures are the NVFP4 cases (`cvt with .e2m1x2` is not supported on `sm_90a`). Unmodified `main` gives the same 149 passed and the same 26 failures on that GPU.

With the fix reverted, the bit-exact checks without LoRA still pass. Only the adapter checks fail, on the ~35% of tokens mapped to an adapter, which shows the adapters were being dropped.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files (ruff, mypy, typos, test tethering).

I did not do an end-to-end serving run with a V4 checkpoint and an adapter on these modules. Without LoRA, every changed V4 projection is bit-identical to `main` (asserted above), and RopeQuant only turns off when `--enable-lora` is set, so serving without LoRA is unchanged.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- The compressor kv_score closures in `DeepseekV4Attention._run_parallel_input_projections` call `torch.mm(hidden_states, fused_wkv_wgate.weight.T, out_dtype=torch.float32)`.
- Every CUDA `_o_proj` passes `self.wo_a` to `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`, which runs `fp8_einsum`/`torch.bmm` on `wo_a.weight`.
- Under LoRA, both modules are LoRA wrappers whose `weight` (and `weight_scale`) resolve to the base layer, so these GEMMs never see the adapter. Nothing raises an error.

**Compressor.**
- `DeepseekV4CompressorKVScoreLinear` is a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` whose forward is that FP32 GEMM. It moved unchanged from `deepseek_v41/compressor.py` to `deepseek_v4/compressor.py`. V4's closures now call the layer.
- `DeepseekV4CompressorKVScoreWithLoRA`, added in #57245, matches the layer by class name and adds the adapter delta.
- CPU keeps the plain layer:
  - Its packed GEMM frees the raw weight (`dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm(remove_weight=True)`).
  - CPU attention calls the layer and upcasts the result itself.
  - The CPU V4 model does not declare `SupportsLoRA`.

**`wo_a`.**
- `DeepseekV4GroupedWoA` is the `ColumnParallelLinear` `wo_a`, plus two methods:
  - `grouped_forward`, which wraps the unchanged `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`.
  - `grouped_input`, which returns the BF16 inverse-rotated groups.
- The class moved from `deepseek_v41/common/grouped_wo_a.py` to `deepseek_v4/common/grouped_wo_a.py`. Only the docstring and one import path differ, and V4.1's `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` already re-exports V4's.
- The three V4 CUDA `_o_proj`s call `wo_a.grouped_forward(...)` and then `wo_b`.
- `DeepseekV4GroupedWoAWithLoRA`, added in #57245, adds each group's delta:
  - LoRA-A is shared.
  - Group `g` uses LoRA-B rows `g*o_lora_rank:(g+1)*o_lora_rank`, each kept as its own buffer.
  - Under fully sharded LoRA, every rank keeps the full LoRA-A.
- This PR changes only the wrapper's type-only import.
- `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` keeps its signature and behavior.

**Sharing with V4.1.**
- V4.1 already imports many pieces from V4: attention helpers, ops and model classes. Its `attention.py` and `compressor.py` now also import these two layers, and `deepseek_v41/common/grouped_wo_a.py` is deleted.
- Both LoRA wrappers match by class name, so they serve both models.

**Compatibility.**
- Both layers are plain subclasses. Nothing outside `vllm/lora` checks `type(...) is ColumnParallelLinear`/`MergedColumnParallelLinear`.
- The quant methods' `is_bmm` handling and #64827's `fp8_einsum` warmup read `wo_a` attributes, which the wrapper forwards.
- ROCm keeps reading `.weight` directly (fused compressor GEMM, mono decode, FP8 `wo_a`). Neither the AMD nor the CPU V4 model declares `SupportsLoRA`.
- XPU declares `SupportsLoRA` and picks up the compressor fix through the shared closures. Its `_o_proj` still reads `wo_a.bmm_weight` directly, so its `wo_a` adapters are still dropped. That is left for a follow-up.

**Tests.**
- The new V4 tests construct the real layers, LoRA wrappers and punica wrapper. They call the real `_run_parallel_input_projections` and the three backends' `_o_proj`.
- They check only V4's call sites. With an adapter set, V4's output must match the LoRA layer's own output. Without one, it must match the raw GEMM bit for bit.
- The wrapper's own math is covered by the existing V4.1 tests on the same layers: per-group LoRA-B, FP8 `wo_a`, the pointer cache, `reset_lora` and fully sharded LoRA.
- A `SimpleNamespace` stands in for the attention module, because building a real `DeepseekV4Attention` needs a full V4 config and GPU backends.
- The tests run in the H200 `LoRA` step and are skipped on its AMD mirror. That step doesn't watch `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/`, so a later V4-only change won't rerun them.

**Not a duplicate.**
- No open PR addresses this. I searched "deepseek v4 lora", "fused_wkv_wgate", "wo_a lora", "grouped_wo_a", "RopeQuant lora" and "pointer cache lora".
- #57245 (DeepSeek-V4.1 LoRA, merged) added the LoRA wrappers and V4.1-local copies of these layers. This PR applies them to V4 and removes the copies.
- #64827 (DeepGEMM warmup for the V4 o_proj) does not touch `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` or the call sites.
- #44847 edits a different function in `o_proj.py`.

---

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Enable Matryoshka dimensions for EmbeddingGemma 2
author: YaashuDave
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #64845. EmbeddingGemma 2 is trained with Matryoshka Representation Learning, and its model card lists 128, 256, 512 and 768 as supported dimensions. None of its published configs (`config.json`, `config_sentence_transformers.json`, `sentence_bert_config.json`) declares this, so vLLM treats the model as non-Matryoshka and rejects every request that sets `dimensions`. Today users need `--hf-overrides '{"matryoshka_dimensions": [...]}'` to get the documented behavior.

This PR sets `matryoshka_dimensions = [128, 256, 512, 768]` in `EmbeddingGemma2ModelConfig.verify_and_update_model_config`, the same hook `JinaForRankingConfig` uses to set `embedding_size`.

## Claims

- Without overrides, `dimensions` of 128, 256 and 512 are accepted, and other values are rejected with the existing "only supports Matryoshka dimensions" error.
- A config that already declares `matryoshka_dimensions` or `is_matryoshka` (from the Hub or from `--hf-overrides`) is left unchanged. The hook runs after overrides are applied.
- No change for requests without `dimensions`, or for other models.
- The pooler truncates before it normalizes (`seqwise/heads.py`), which matches the model card's "re-normalize after truncating".

**768 still fails the range check until #60978 merges.** vLLM reports `embedding_size` as the text hidden size (512) instead of `embedding_dim` (768), and #60978 fixes that. The two PRs don't touch the same code and can land in either order.

## Validation

```bash
pytest -q tests/models/test_embedding_gemma2_config.py
# 5 passed
```

On CPU, I built `ModelConfig` from the model's published `config.json` and ran `PoolingParams(dimensions=d).verify()` on it:

| `dimensions` | main | this PR | this PR + #60978 |
|---|---|---|---|
| unset | OK | OK | OK |
| 128 / 256 / 512 | rejected (not Matryoshka) | OK | OK |
| 300 | rejected (not Matryoshka) | rejected (not in [128, 256, 512, 768]) | rejected |
| 768 | rejected (not Matryoshka) | rejected (range [1, 512]) | OK |

With `--hf-overrides '{"matryoshka_dimensions": [256]}'`, only 256 is accepted. With `'{"is_matryoshka": true}'`, any size is accepted, and with `'{"is_matryoshka": false}'`, `dimensions` stays disabled. All three behave as on main.

- `test_sets_matryoshka_dimensions_from_model_card` fails on main and passes with this change.
- `test_keeps_declared_matryoshka_config` checks that a declared `matryoshka_dimensions` or `is_matryoshka` is kept, including `null` and `false`.
- `test_matryoshka_parity` (added to `tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py`, gated on `EG2_MODEL_PATH` like the other tests there) compares 128/256/512-d vLLM outputs with Sentence Transformers' `truncate_dim` plus `normalize_embeddings`. I don't have a GPU, so I haven't run it. The reporter's `--hf-overrides` run in the issue exercises the same code path at 256 and 512.

Ruff lint and format pass on the changed files.

## Question

No other model in vLLM sets `matryoshka_dimensions` from its config hook; it normally comes from the checkpoint's `config.json`. Is setting it here OK, or would you rather it come from the model's config on the Hub?

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Refresh derived weight copies after in-place weight writes
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

This adds an opt-in module hook, `refresh_derived_weights()`, plus a walker in `weight_utils.py`. The walker is called from three shared paths that overwrite `state_dict()` tensors in place without the per-layer post-load hook:
- `SparseNCCLWeightTransferEngine.finish_weight_update`;
- the kernel-format branch of `reload_weights`;
- `ElasticEPScalingExecutor.prepare_new_worker`.

It does nothing unless a module defines the hook. Today only the Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA layer and MLA wrapper do, and the elastic-EP call has no model that reaches it yet. The PR also makes the Kimi-K3 ROCm `_w_fold` rebuild write in place.

Kimi-K3 on ROCm derives three tensors from its weights and keeps them outside `state_dict()`:
- `decode_conv1d_weight`, read by the AITER Gluon and HIP fused decode kernels;
- `decode_norm_weight`, read by the HIP kernel only;
- `_w_fold`, a plain attribute read by the fused decode-query GEMM.

The KDA copies (the first two) go stale on all three paths. `_w_fold` goes stale on the kernel-format reload and on elastic EP. On sparse NCCL it is rebuilt, but as a new tensor that CUDA graphs captured earlier do not read.

Related (all merged):
- #60110 added `_w_fold`.
- #61207 stages the KDA copies at load.
- #64158 builds `_w_fold` from the root model's hook.
- #64357 runs the model-level hook after every load, checkpoint-format reload and sparse NCCL update, but not after a kernel-format reload.

## Claims

The kernel-format reload claim is covered by the updated unit test. The sparse NCCL, elastic-EP and `_w_fold` claims come from reading the code (see Validation).

- **Kernel-format `reload_weights(..., is_checkpoint_format=False)`:** the Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA decode copies are re-staged from the reloaded weights, at the same addresses. On main they keep the values staged at load, while prefill reads the reloaded weights.
- **Sparse NCCL weight updates:** the same holds for an update that writes `conv1d.weight` or `o_norm.weight`.
- **Elastic-EP scale-up:** new ranks re-derive these tensors from the weights received from their peer, instead of keeping values computed from the dummy load. This is defensive for Kimi-K3. It does not set `num_moe_layers`, so EPLB never registers it and an elastic-EP scale-up cannot complete on it today (it fails at the `model.expert_weights` and `model_states` lookups).
- **`_w_fold`:** rebuilt in place. On main, layerwise reload and sparse NCCL assign a new `_w_fold`, so CUDA graphs captured before the rebuild keep the old, freed tensor's address.
- **Other models:** no change. Only modules that define `refresh_derived_weights()` are called.

## Validation

All runs used one MI355X (gfx950) with image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505`, with this branch's `vllm/` and `tests/` over the installed package. The image is 193 commits behind the base 5a233286c6; `csrc/kimi_k3` did not change in between.

`test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` builds a real `KimiK3DeltaAttention`, then reloads every parameter with new values through `reload_weights(..., is_checkpoint_format=False)`. It checks that the staged copies match the reloaded weights and that no buffer moved.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py` | 45 passed |
| `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` on the base (every changed `vllm/` file from main, new test kept) | 2 failed, 2 passed |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py` | 82 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xpassed, 2 failed. The same 2 fail on the base: the NVFP4A16 `DeepSeek-V3-debug` cases of `test_reload_weights`, whose engine fails to start on this ROCm image. |
| `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` (4 GPUs) | 114 passed, 26 skipped, 3 failed. The same 3 fail on the base: the `*_weight_transfer_between_processes` tests, whose Ray actors hit `invalid device ordinal` with two visible GPUs. |

On the base, both fp32-state cases fail after the reload, on `decode_conv1d_weight`. The bf16-state cases allocate no copies.

```
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py:446: in test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py:424: in check_staged
E   AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
E   Mismatched elements: 18432 / 18432 (100.0%)
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (ruff 0.14.0, mypy): clean.

CI: `:amd: (MI355) Kimi K3` runs `pytest -v -s models/kimi_k3 --ignore=models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py` on this PR. The B200 step skips this ROCm-only file.

Not validated:
- **End to end:** no serving or RL run of Kimi-K3 on any of the three paths.
- **Call sites without a test:** the sparse NCCL and elastic-EP call sites. Both elastic-EP scale-up tests, `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py` and `tests/v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py::test_external_lb_elastic_ep_scale_up`, use DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, which has no module with the hook.
- **The in-place `_w_fold` rebuild:** no existing Kimi-K3 test builds a real MLA wrapper with `_fold_qb_uk` enabled (AITER MLA, fp8 KV cache, unquantized `q_b_proj`, no DCP or PCP), and adding one is a larger setup than this fix.

## Details

**How it was found.** By reading the code while reviewing #63612. It was not observed in a serving or RL run.

**Root cause.**
- The KDA copies are staged only in the layer's `process_weights_after_loading`. `_w_fold` is built only from the Kimi-K3 model-level hook.
- The kernel-format branch of `reload_weights` copies parameters and runs neither hook.
- Sparse NCCL ends with `finalize_model_weights`, which reaches the MLA wrappers through the model hook but not the KDA layers.
- Elastic EP builds new ranks with `load_dummy_weights=True` (`elastic_execute.py:273`), so both hooks derive these tensors from dummy weights. `batch_transfer_weights` then receives only `model.state_dict()` from a peer (`:97`) and runs no post-load pass.

**Change.**
- **The walker:** `weight_utils.refresh_derived_weights(model)` calls `refresh_derived_weights()` on every module that defines it, under `no_grad`.
- **The hook contract** (in the docstring): idempotent; reads only non-expert `state_dict()` tensors, since elastic EP moves routed experts later; no collectives; writes in place.
- **Callers:**
  - `prepare_new_worker`, after the transfer and `torch.accelerator.synchronize()`, under the worker's vLLM config;
  - `finish_weight_update`, after `finalize_model_weights`;
  - the kernel-format branch of `reload_weights`, after the copy loop.
- **`KimiK3DeltaAttention`:** the existing copy body moves into `refresh_derived_weights()`. `process_weights_after_loading` keeps the IPC weight-cache guard and calls it.
- **`KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper`:** `process_weights_after_loading()` and `refresh_derived_weights()` both rebuild `_w_fold`, which is copied in place once it exists.
- **Precedent:** `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` (`layers/quantization/online/lm_head.py:157`) re-derives copies in place after a weight reload, for the same CUDA-graph reason.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **Re-stage the KDA copies from the Kimi-K3 model hook (`amd/linear.py:1174`).** Sparse NCCL already runs that hook, so this fixes sparse NCCL with no core change. But the kernel-format reload runs no hook, and the elastic-EP receiver runs none, so a core call is needed anyway.
- **Refresh from the weight loader, as #63612 does for its GLM layer.** This covers writes that go through `load_weights`, such as sparse NCCL. It misses the kernel-format `param.copy_` and the elastic-EP `state_dict()` copy. #61207 also moved Kimi-K3's staging out of the loaders because dummy loads skip them.
- **Register the buffers as persistent, so `state_dict()` carries them.** This covers elastic EP only. It changes the key set of every saved Kimi-K3 `sharded_state` checkpoint ("Missing keys" on load), makes that key set depend on the decode backend picked at runtime, and does not cover `_w_fold`.
- **Re-run `finalize_model_weights` or the per-layer hooks on new elastic ranks.** Model-level hooks are not idempotent on already-processed weights in general: DeepSeek-V4 AMD preshuffles in its hook.

**Trade-offs and limits.**
- On sparse NCCL, `_w_fold` is now built twice per update (model hook, then the walker). That is one extra `_w_fold` build per MLA layer: `kv_b_proj` dequant, an einsum and a concat, then an in-place copy.
- The same pattern is left for follow-ups:
  - the Kimi-K3 NVIDIA KDA buffers, which only the weight loaders fill, so they are uninitialized after a dummy load;
  - `GateLinear._bf16x3_weight` for fp32-router models on gfx950;
  - #63612's GLM-5.3-Flash decode copy, a model that does reach elastic EP. Its layer could implement this hook.

**Duplicate check.**
- I searched open and closed PRs for `refresh_derived_weights`, `decode_conv1d_weight`, `_w_fold` and elastic-EP buffer staleness, and found the PRs listed above.
- #63612 refreshes its own layer's copy from its weight loader. No PR covers kernel-format reloads or elastic EP, or adds a hook that every in-place path calls.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][XPU] greedy_argmax: treat NaN as -inf on the torch fallback
author: taneem-ibrahim
body:
## Purpose

XPU on main is broken. This PR fixes `greedy_argmax`'s torch fallback to treat NaNs as `-inf`, matching its documented contract and Triton path. This issue was introduced by #57770.

**Notes for Reviewers**

- The fix only touches the torch fallback, which runs on XPU, for fp16, and for small vocabularies. The Triton path that bf16/fp32 models use on CUDA and ROCm is unchanged, so typical deployments see no difference.
- The trade-off is one extra copy of the logits on the fallback path. That's a small cost next to the weights the draft step already reads, and it's the price of getting the same token for the same logits everywhere.
- Turning on the Triton kernel for XPU would avoid that copy, but it needs XPU performance numbers and sign-off from the XPU owners. CPU and non-contiguous inputs would still need this fallback anyway. I kept this PR to the minimal fix so XPU CI is unblocked, and we can address the Triton change in a follow up PR.
- Why not just fix the test? The docstring already promises NaN is treated as -inf, and the Triton path does exactly that. Changing the test instead would let the drafted token depend on the platform and dtype.

## Reproducer

Add `1000` to the existing test's vocab parameters, then run the same command before and after the fallback fix:

```bash
  python -m pytest -v \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py -k test_greedy_argmax_matches_torch
```

## Output on main / on branch

H100 80GB, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Main's two new fallback cases fail at the NaN row; all six Triton cases pass.

```text
Main + test parameter:
============ 2 failed, 6 passed, 22 deselected, 1 warning in 3.69s =============
Branch:
================= 8 passed, 22 deselected, 1 warning in 2.92s ==================
Full file on branch:
======================== 30 passed, 1 warning in 18.08s ========================
```

## Test Plan

The `:intel: (BMG) V1 test` in CI verifies these failures are cleared and the suite reaches later tests. 

<details>
<summary>Implementation and environment</summary>

The fallback uses `masked_fill(isnan, -inf).argmax(-1)`, preserving infinities and first-index ties without modifying inputs. It adds a mask and logits copy only on the fallback. The Triton kernels and gating are unchanged, so eligible BF16/FP32 CUDA/ROCm inputs keep the existing execution path.
</details>

## AI assistance disclosure

Codex (GPT-6) helped draft  this change.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Report reasoning tokens in batched chat completions
author: GCSimba
body:
## Overview

`/v1/chat/completions/batch` never sets `usage.completion_tokens_details`, so a server started with `--reasoning-parser` omits `reasoning_tokens` from batched responses while `/v1/chat/completions` reports them for the same conversation. This counts and sums them per conversation, the way the single-conversation path does. Follows #64757, which added the prompt-side `prompt_tokens_details` to the same endpoint.

## Claims

- With `--reasoning-parser`, `/v1/chat/completions/batch` returns `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` summed across conversations, including when `include_reasoning=false` (hidden reasoning is still generated and billed), matching `/v1/chat/completions`.
- Without a reasoning parser, `completion_tokens_details` stays `null`, as on `/v1/chat/completions`.

## Validation

New test `test_batch_reasoning_tokens_in_usage` in `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_include_reasoning.py`, through `RemoteOpenAIServer` with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3` (the module's existing server). It posts two conversations with `include_reasoning=false` and checks `0 < reasoning_tokens <= completion_tokens`.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_include_reasoning.py -k test_batch_reasoning_tokens_in_usage
```

Before the fix (main at cfa9f96):

```
>       assert details is not None
E       assert None is not None
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_include_reasoning.py:118: AssertionError
1 failed, 6 deselected
```

After the fix: `1 passed, 6 deselected`.

Usage for the same conversation on the same server (`max_tokens=64`, `temperature=0`, `include_reasoning=false`), after the fix; before it the batch `completion_tokens_details` is `null`:

| Endpoint | completion_tokens | reasoning_tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 64 | 63 |
| `/v1/chat/completions/batch`, the conversation twice | 128 | 126 |

Other checks after the fix:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test_include_reasoning.py` (whole file) | 7 passed |
| `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, the new test only | 1 skipped, no server started |
| Unit tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py` (`-k` the six non-server tests) | 6 passed |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | passed (shellcheck skipped: no shell files, and its binary download timed out locally) |

Environment: CPU only (Intel i5-11300H, AVX-512), Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2, Python 3.12, `--enforce-eager`. The Python sources are this branch; the compiled CPU extensions come from the nightly CPU wheel for 2b009fc (20 commits behind, differing only in CUDA kernels). Validated on cfa9f96, then rebased onto 564ac0d; the commits in between only change `recipes/models/*.yaml`.

Not run locally: the server tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py` (they need `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, which serves without a reasoning parser, so this path only adds a `null` field there), and GPU CI. No model evaluation: model outputs are unchanged; only response usage changes.

## Details

- Root cause: `chat_completion_full_generator_batch` builds `UsageInfo` without `completion_tokens_details`, and never counts reasoning tokens even though each conversation already runs through its parser.
- The fix mirrors `OpenAIServingChat.chat_completion_full_generator`: call `parser.count_reasoning_tokens(output.token_ids)` after `parse`, and gate the details on `_include_reasoning_tokens_details`. It reuses `_make_completion_tokens_details`.
- Three existing unit tests build `OpenAIServingChatBatch` with `__new__`, so they now set `_include_reasoning_tokens_details = False` (as #64757 did for `enable_prompt_tokens_details`), and the fake parser gains `count_reasoning_tokens`.
- The Rust frontend serves `/v1/chat/completions/batch` as `not_supported`, so the new test is skipped when `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND` is set, as the Rust frontend CI steps do (same pattern as `test_thinking_token_budget.py`). The Python-frontend steps run it.
- Docs: one sentence next to the `prompt_tokens_details` note for this endpoint in `openai_compatible_server.md`.

Not a duplicate: open and closed PRs and issues searched for "batch reasoning tokens", "completions/batch usage", "batched chat completions usage", "reasoning_tokens", `OpenAIServingChatBatch` and `batch_serving`. Related but different: #64757 (merged, prompt-side details only), #64041 (reasoning tokens on the derender endpoints), #58010 (hiding reasoning metadata in batch responses).

AI assistance (GitHub Copilot) was used to find the bug, write the change and tests, and run the validation; I reviewed every changed line and the test results.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Count reasoning_content deltas as streamed outputs in chat
author: Than0316
body:
## Overview

Some servers, like SGLang, send reasoning tokens in a field called `reasoning_content`. vLLM uses `reasoning`. Since #62341, the chat benchmark client only looks for `reasoning`, so it skips SGLang's reasoning tokens.

Two things go wrong:
- TTFT is measured to the first answer token instead of the first reasoning token, so it looks much slower than it really is.
- A response that ends before the model starts answering is counted as failed.

This PR makes the client accept `reasoning_content` too.

## Claims

- TTFT is measured to the first reasoning token again, as it was before #62341. A stub streaming SGLang's chunks went from 842 ms to 205 ms, against a true 201 ms.
- Reasoning-only responses go from 0/20 to 20/20 successful.
- No change for vLLM's own server, which streams `reasoning`.

## Validation

Two tests added to `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`: reasoning followed by an answer (TTFT and ITL), and a reasoning-only stream (success). Both are parametrized over `reasoning` / `reasoning_content` and both clients. 46 passed. The 4 `reasoning_content` cases fail on `main` (`assert 1 == (4 - 1)` and "Never received a valid chunk to calculate TTFT"). pre-commit passes.

End to end: `vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat`, 20 prompts, concurrency 4, against a local stub that streams SGLang's chunk sequence. The stub sends its first output at 200 ms, then 30 reasoning and 10 answer tokens 20 ms apart, and logs its own send times. Two runs each:

| | `main` | this branch | stub's send log |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean TTFT | 843 / 841 ms | 206 / 205 ms | first reasoning token ≈ 201 ms |
| reasoning-only, successful | 0 / 20 | 20 / 20 | 30 tokens sent per request |

<details><summary>Stub server and command</summary>

`stub_sglang_server.py` sends the same chunk sequence as SGLang's streaming chat endpoint, with fixed timings, and logs when it sent the first reasoning and answer tokens:

```python
"""Minimal stub of SGLang's streaming chat endpoint, for integration-testing a client.

It reproduces the chunk sequence SGLang streams as of sgl-project/sglang 504f9cf
(sse_utils.py StreamDelta/StreamChoice, omit_defaults=True; serving_chat.py):
  opening chunk  delta {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": null},
                 sent when the first engine output arrives
  reasoning      delta {"reasoning_content": "..."}          (no `content` key)
  answer         delta {"content": "...", "reasoning_content": null}
  finish         delta {"reasoning_content": null}, finish_reason set
  usage          "choices": [] plus "usage"
Every choice carries logprobs, finish_reason and matched_stop, as StreamChoice serializes them.
It uses fixed, known timings and logs server-side send times per request as ground truth.

Usage: python stub_sglang_server.py --port 18731 --log ground_truth.jsonl
Binds to 127.0.0.1 only.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import time

from aiohttp import web


def _chunk(delta: dict, finish_reason=None) -> bytes:
    # StreamChoice always serializes logprobs, finish_reason and matched_stop.
    choice = {
        "index": 0,
        "delta": delta,
        "logprobs": None,
        "finish_reason": finish_reason,
        "matched_stop": None,
    }
    body = {
        "id": "chatcmpl-stub",
        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
        "created": int(time.time()),
        "model": "stub",
        "choices": [choice],
    }
    return f"data: {json.dumps(body)}\n\n".encode()


def _usage_chunk(usage: dict) -> bytes:
    # SGLang's final usage chunk carries no choices (serving_chat.py ~2792-2796).
    body = {
        "id": "chatcmpl-stub",
        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
        "created": int(time.time()),
        "model": "stub",
        "choices": [],
        "usage": usage,
    }
    return f"data: {json.dumps(body)}\n\n".encode()


def make_app(args) -> web.Application:
    log = open(args.log, "a", buffering=1)

    async def chat(request: web.Request) -> web.StreamResponse:
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        await request.json()
        resp = web.StreamResponse(headers={"Content-Type": "text/event-stream"})
        await resp.prepare(request)

        sent = {}
        # SGLang sends the opening role chunk when the first engine output arrives.
        await asyncio.sleep(args.first_token_ms / 1000)
        await resp.write(_chunk({"role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": None}))
        for i in range(args.reasoning_tokens):
            if i:
                await asyncio.sleep(args.itl_ms / 1000)
            await resp.write(_chunk({"reasoning_content": f"r{i} "}))
            sent.setdefault("first_reasoning_s", time.perf_counter() - t0)
        for i in range(args.answer_tokens):
            await asyncio.sleep(args.itl_ms / 1000)
            await resp.write(_chunk({"content": f"a{i} ", "reasoning_content": None}))
            sent.setdefault("first_answer_s", time.perf_counter() - t0)
        n = args.reasoning_tokens + args.answer_tokens
        # Finish chunk: build_sse_content(finish_reason=...) gives delta {"reasoning_content": null}.
        await resp.write(
            _chunk({"reasoning_content": None}, finish_reason="stop" if args.answer_tokens else "length")
        )
        await resp.write(_usage_chunk({"prompt_tokens": 8, "completion_tokens": n, "total_tokens": 8 + n}))
        await resp.write(b"data: [DONE]\n\n")
        log.write(json.dumps({**sent, "tokens": n}) + "\n")
        return resp

    async def models(_request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        return web.json_response({"object": "list", "data": [{"id": "stub", "object": "model"}]})

    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_post("/v1/chat/completions", chat)
    app.router.add_get("/v1/models", models)
    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18731)
    p.add_argument("--log", default="ground_truth.jsonl")
    p.add_argument("--first-token-ms", type=float, default=200.0)
    p.add_argument("--reasoning-tokens", type=int, default=30)
    p.add_argument("--answer-tokens", type=int, default=10)
    p.add_argument("--itl-ms", type=float, default=20.0)
    a = p.parse_args()
    web.run_app(make_app(a), host="127.0.0.1", port=a.port, print=None)
```

Run it, then benchmark it:

```bash
python stub_sglang_server.py --port 18731 &
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18731 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model stub --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16 --random-output-len 40 \
  --num-prompts 20 --max-concurrency 4
```

For the reasoning-only case, start the stub with `--answer-tokens 0`.

</details>

## Details

SGLang streams reasoning only as `reasoning_content`; its reasoning deltas carry no `content` key (`StreamDelta` in `sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/sse_utils.py`). It fixed the same issue in its own benchmark client (sgl-project/sglang#23954). The Rust `vllm-bench` ports in #64626/#64627 have the same gap; I'll note it there.

No issue or PR covers this. #64703 edits the same file on different lines and applies independently.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this and write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and the end-to-end comparison.

cc @DarkLight1337, who reviewed #62341.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fix tool_reference results on DeepSeek V4.1 and /v1/messages
author: vMaroon
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepSeek V4.1 encoder rejects `tool_reference` content parts with a 400, and `/v1/messages` turns a `tool_result` with `tool_reference` items into two `tool` messages for one call. This renders each reference on V4.1 as the tool's name and emits one `tool` message per `tool_result`, so conversations that use Claude Code's tool search work on DeepSeek V4.1 and render one result per tool call.

## Claims

- Requests with `tool_reference` parts render on DeepSeek V4.1. On main they fail with `DeepSeek V4.1 supports text and image content only; got 'tool_reference'`. This covers `tool_result` blocks with `tool_reference` items on `/v1/messages`, and `tool_reference` parts on `/v1/chat/completions`.
- On V4.1, each reference renders as the tool's name inside its call's `<tool_result>`. Several references are joined with `\n\n`, the separator the encoder already uses between parts.
- `/v1/messages` emits one `tool` message per `tool_result`: the `tool_reference` parts first, then the text. On main, a tool search result renders an extra empty result before the references, on GLM-5.3 as well as V4.1, so after parallel tool calls the results no longer line up with the calls.
- Templates that expand references keep working: GLM-5.3 renders the referenced tool definitions as before.
- A `tool_result` without `tool_reference` items converts as before, and other unsupported part types still return 400 on V4.1.
- The change is in `_convert_user_tool_result` (`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`) and `_normalize_messages` (`vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py`): 15 lines added and 11 removed, plus three tests.

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `5d55ef1590` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New tests | `pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py::TestToolResultContent::test_tool_result_with_tool_references tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py::test_messages_render_tool_search_result_for_deepseek_v41 tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_tool_references_render_as_tool_names` | 3 failed (below) | 3 passed |
| Changed test files | `pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py` | 271 passed, 4 failed (the 3 new tests and 1 below) | 274 passed, 1 failed (below) |
| `vllm launch render` with the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config and tokenizer, 4 requests (below) | | 4 of 4 HTTP 400 | 4 of 4 HTTP 200, one `<tool_result>` per call |
| `vllm launch render` with the GLM-5.3 config, tokenizer and chat template, 3 requests (below) | | 3 of 3 HTTP 200, one extra `<tool_response>` each | 3 of 3 HTTP 200, one `<tool_response>` per call |

The conversion test sends a `tool_result` with text, two `tool_reference` items and an image, and checks for one `tool` message with the references first, followed by the image's `user` message. The render test starts `vllm launch render deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` through `RemoteLaunchRenderServer`, which downloads only the config and tokenizer, like the existing GPT-OSS render test. It sends a `/v1/messages` turn where a tool search and a file read ran in parallel, and checks the rendered user turn through `/detokenize`. On main the new tests fail like this:

```
E       AssertionError: assert ['assistant',...user', 'tool'] == ['assistant', 'tool', 'user']
E           AssertionError: {"error":{"message":"DeepSeek V4.1 supports text and image content only; got 'tool_reference'","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}
E                       ValueError: DeepSeek V4.1 supports text and image content only; got 'tool_reference'
3 failed, 3 warnings in 18.48s
```

With only the V4.1 encoder change and main's converter, the render test still fails: the parallel turn renders three `<tool_result>`s for two calls.

The one other failure in the changed files is `test_tokenize_matches_chat_render_for_gpt_oss`, which fails the same way on main here because the container cannot download the Harmony vocab file. Tests ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The repo's pre-commit hooks pass, including `ruff`, `mypy` and the test tethering check. No model evaluation is included: the change only affects prompts with `tool_reference` items.

<details>
<summary>Render server checks</summary>

**DeepSeek V4.1.** The server runs `vllm launch render deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --language-model-only`, with `config.json` and the tokenizer from revision `314113f8` and no weights. Every request declares a `ToolSearch` tool, plus `get_weather` and `get_time` with `defer_loading: true`.

1. `/v1/messages/render`, shaped like a Claude Code tool search: the last user turn is a `tool_result` whose content is `[{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "get_weather"}]`.
2. The same conversation one turn later, after `get_weather` was called and returned.
3. `/v1/chat/completions/render` with a `tool` message whose content is `[{"type": "tool_reference", "name": "get_weather"}]`.
4. `/v1/messages/render` where one assistant turn calls `ToolSearch` and `Read` in parallel, and the user turn returns the reference result and a text result.

On main all four return the 400 above. On this branch, requests 1 and 3 end with `<tool_result>get_weather</tool_result>` before the generation prompt, request 2 has one result for each of its two calls, request 4 ends with `<tool_result>get_weather</tool_result>\n\n<tool_result>NOTES-FILE-BODY</tool_result>`, and the system prompt of every request lists all tools.

**GLM-5.3.** The server runs `vllm launch render` with the GLM-5.3 `config.json` and tokenizer, the chat template from Hub revision `ba32f8c19c`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, and requests 1 and 4 above plus a third `/v1/messages` request whose `tool_result` holds a text block and a `tool_reference`.

| Request | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Tool search | `<tool_response></tool_response><tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response>` | `<tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response>` |
| Parallel `ToolSearch` + `Read` | 3 `<tool_response>`s for 2 calls, the first one empty | `<tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response><tool_response>NOTES-FILE-BODY</tool_response>` |
| Text and reference in one result | `<tool_response>Found 1 tool</tool_response><tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response>` | `<tool_response><tools>{get_weather}</tools></tool_response>` |

`{get_weather}` stands for the tool's full JSON definition, which both arms render identically.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** #40190 added `tool_reference` parts. `_convert_user_tool_result` emits a `tool` message with the result's text (empty for a plain tool search), then a second `tool` message with the `tool_reference` items, both for the same `tool_use_id`. An image in the result goes into a `user` message between the two. Templates and encoders that render one result per `tool` message render one result too many. Separately, V4.1 renders with its own encoder, and `_normalize_messages` raises `ValueError` for any part type other than text and image. The `tool_result` stays in the conversation history, so on V4.1 every later request in that conversation fails too, and an agent session that runs a tool search cannot continue.

**Why one message, references first.** Templates that expand references look for a `tool` message whose first part is a `tool_reference` (GLM-5.3's does), so the references lead and the text follows. Images stay in the `user` message after the `tool` message. Limitation: GLM-5.3's template expands such a message and skips its other parts, so text that sits beside references in one `tool_result` no longer renders there; on main it rendered as an extra result. The tool search docs show results that hold only `tool_reference` blocks.

**Why the name.** `apply_chat_template` puts every request tool into the V4.1 system prompt, deferred ones included, so the definitions a reference points at are already in context. The name tells the model which tools the search returned. The Cohere renderer renders these parts the same way (`vllm/renderers/cohere.py`). The model's Jinja template on the Hub drops unknown block types, which would render the search result empty.

**Related.** #52498 and #52610 (open, for #52489) rewrite `tool_reference` items as text in the Anthropic converter for every model. That would also stop the V4.1 400 on `/v1/messages`, but `/v1/chat/completions` requests with these parts would still fail, and the structured parts that templates expanding references rely on would be gone.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the root-cause analysis, the fix, the tests and this description.

title: [Bugfix][MM] Keep FlashInfer cu_seqlens halves aligned in Qwen3-VL encoder CUDA graph replay
author: wguo7
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `mm_encoder_attn_backend=FLASHINFER` and encoder CUDA graphs enabled, Qwen3-VL image replays copy the packed FlashInfer `cu_seqlens` into the capture buffer with `EncoderCudaGraphManager._copy_padded_buffer`. That copy misaligns the q/k/o and v halves of the packed tensor. The vision encoder output then differs between replays of the same image and from eager mode. This registers the existing Qwen2.5-VL helper `_pad_flashinfer_cu_seqlens_buffer` (from #42796) for Qwen3-VL through `EncoderCudaGraphConfig.padding_logics`. SyaOtiLan found the instability and ran the GPU validation below while testing #63809, which adds the same hook for Qwen3-Omni.

## Claims

- Qwen3-VL encoder CUDA graph replays on FLASHINFER keep each half of the packed `cu_seqlens` in its own half of the capture buffer. In the tested cases, replays are identical and match eager mode on the same padded buffers.
- Other attention backends use `_pad_cumulative_seqlens_buffer`, as Qwen2.5-VL does (changed in 3b80be3 after review). It repeats the last offset, so padded entries are zero-length sequences, while the default copy filled them with zeros. The default copy gave no wrong output in the FLASH_ATTN replays of the earlier GPU runs below, and the GPU run of 3b80be3 below shows exact replays on both backends.

## Validation

CPU unit tests (no GPU) in `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`, class `TestFlashInferCuSeqlensPadding`:

```
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -k FlashInferCuSeqlens
```

On this branch, 8 pass. The test pads replay `cu_seqlens` with the padding function Qwen3-VL registers (falling back to `_copy_padded_buffer`, as replay does) and checks that the result equals the `cu_seqlens` computed for the same inputs at the capture batch size. It runs four replay and capture batch sizes on FLASHINFER and FLASH_ATTN. With `qwen3_vl.py` from main, 7 of the 8 cases fail. The one that passes is the FlashInfer case where replay and capture fall in the same batch bucket, so no padding happens. The whole file passes (52 passed, 25 skipped on CPU).

GPU validation by SyaOtiLan ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557439065), with raw outputs and scripts): RTX 4090 (SM 8.9), FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct in BF16 through `LLM(mm_encoder_only=True)`, `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`, budgets [64, 256, 1024], at most 2 vision items and 16 frames per batch, one 224 x 224 image. The values are max abs differences of the vision encoder output embeddings. "Replay vs replay" compares later replays of the same input with the first one, and "Replay vs eager" compares the first replay with eager mode on the same padded buffers. The run used the same `qwen3_vl.py` change on top of 3687acad21, the head of #63809 at the time. `encoder_cudagraph.py`, `mm_encoder_attention.py`, `vit_attn_wrappers.py` and `qwen2_5_vl.py` are identical there and on this branch.

| Input | Replay vs replay, before | Replay vs replay, after | Replay vs eager, before | Replay vs eager, after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 x 16 grid (processor default), 64 tokens | 9.65625 | 0 | 26.984375 | 0 |
| 14 x 14 grid, 49 tokens | 10.875 | 0 | 23.234375 | 0 |

In a [second run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557974253) on the same branch, mixed-size and two-image batches, video, alternating input shapes and oversized inputs that fall back to eager were also checked: all 110 graph-covered conditions matched eager on the same padded buffers exactly, and the 1,368 calls of a shape-transition stress test were exact.

Padded and unpadded eager runs of the 49-token input still differ (max 0.28125, RMSE 0.0088). That difference does not involve graph replay, and this PR does not change it. A per-layer trace in the second run found that the first difference appears in `blocks.0.mlp.linear_fc1`, while the patch embedding, norms, QKV and attention before it match exactly, which points to shape-dependent numerics in the linear layer. End-to-end generation quality was not measured.

GPU validation of the current head 3b80be3 by SyaOtiLan ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64984#issuecomment-6570819059), with scripts, raw logs and checksums): same RTX 4090, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct in BF16, TP=1, `LLM(mm_encoder_only=True)`, budgets [64, 256, 1024], at most 2 vision items and 16 frames per batch, two fresh worker lifetimes per backend. The run reused precompiled extensions from 4135590ffe01 rather than a new wheel, and this PR changes only Python files. Each cell gives two max abs differences of the vision encoder output: a later replay against the first replay, then the first replay against eager mode on the same padded buffers.

| Input | Output tokens | FLASH_ATTN | FLASHINFER |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image 224, matched grid | 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Image 448 | 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Image 224, default processor grid | 64 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Mixed images 224 + 448 | 49 + 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Mixed images 448 + 224 | 196 + 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 2 frames | 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 8 frames | 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 16 frames | 392 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

The image replays exercise the new tail fill: on FLASH_ATTN, 3 replay offsets go into a 17-entry capture buffer and the last offset fills the 14 tail entries. FLASHINFER keeps its split-half padding (18 replay entries, 34 capture entries). Video replays have the same length as capture on both backends. All 32 case checks and 192 later shape-switch executions passed. These results cover encoder replay correctness, not generation quality or latency.

## Details

For FlashInfer, `MMEncoderAttention.maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens` returns the q/k/o offsets followed by the v offsets, each half padded to a FlashInfer batch bucket (8, 16, 32 or 64), and `flashinfer_wrapper` splits the tensor at its midpoint. The BF16 and FP8 paths both use this two-half layout, and only BF16 was run on a GPU. Qwen3-VL captures with `cu_seqlens` padded to `max_frames_per_batch` (bucket 16 for 16 frames, 34 entries) and pads image replays to `max_batch_size` (bucket 8 for 2 items, 18 entries). `_copy_padded_buffer` zeroes the capture buffer and copies the 18 entries to its start. The q/k/o half then holds the 9 q/k/o offsets followed by the first 8 v offsets, and the v half holds the last v offset followed by zeros. Offsets count elements of the packed QKV buffer, so a v offset is 3 x tokens x hidden size. For one 196-patch image with an illustrative hidden size of 1152, the first two v offsets are [0, 677376] in eager mode and [677376, 0] after the default copy, so the kernel sees a sequence of negative length. That would explain why replays of the same input differ from each other, since the kernel then reads outside the valid range, but I have not confirmed this inside the kernel.

The fix mirrors the registration Qwen2.5-VL already has for the same key (`cu_seqlens`) and layout. Changing how image replays are padded would touch the shared graph manager and every model that uses it, while the hook keeps the change inside Qwen3-VL. Video replays pad to `max_frames_per_batch`, the same bucket as capture, so they are not affected, and video replays on the base commit were stable in the second run.

This PR and #63809 touch different model files. Both add tests to `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`, and this commit cherry-picks cleanly onto #63809, so they can merge in either order.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix KV-sharing fast prefill hang from unsynchronized host offsets
author: hojuna
body:
## Overview

Fixes #64985. Under async scheduling, `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill` can hand the attention metadata builders a `query_start_loc_cpu` whose device-to-host copy has not finished yet. The trtllm-gen decode kernel then receives a garbage query length and hangs.

## Claims

- Fixes the hang: `query_start_loc_cpu` from `make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata` now always holds final values.
- No new sync on the common path. With one logit per request (no speculative decoding), the host offsets are built with `torch.arange` instead of being copied.
- Adds a regression test that fails on `main` and passes with this change.

## Validation

**Unit test** `tests/v1/attention/test_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_metadata.py`. The CUDA case keeps the stream busy and reads the host offsets without a sync, the way the builders do.

```
# base
E       assert [0, 4, 7, 8, 10] == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
E       assert [0, 0, 0, 0, 0] == [0, 2, 3, 6, 7]
2 failed, 6 passed
# this PR
8 passed
```

**End-to-end.** Setup: B200, Gemma 4 E4B fine-tune (bf16), `vllm serve --kv-sharing-fast-prefill --enable-prefix-caching -cc '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`, MRV2, async scheduling on. The workload replays `/v1/completions` requests (`max_tokens=1`, 96 concurrent).

| run | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4,649-request slice | hangs (4/4 runs) | completes, 20 s |
| full 31,649 requests | hangs | completes, 105 s |

Pre-commit (ruff check/format) passes locally.

**Review follow-up (9c5b0d7, rebased on main).** `arange` now uses `device="cpu"`. Added `[1, 1, 1, 0]` (a request with no logits) and `[2, 1, 1, 0]` (`num_logits_indices == num_reqs` with `max_logits_per_req > 1`) so each branch condition is tested on its own, plus a CUDA test under `torch.device("cuda")`. CPU run: `5 passed, 3 skipped (CUDA)`. Removing either branch condition makes exactly one of the new cases fail. The CUDA cases were not re-run in this round (no GPU available right now); the earlier CUDA results above are unchanged code paths. Only `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` were run locally, not the full official pre-commit.

## Details

`decode_query_start_loc` is computed on the GPU, and its host copy was made with `.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)`. The builders read it on the host right away:

- `split_decodes_and_prefills`
- FlashInfer `_compute_decode_query_lens`

With async scheduling the copy sits behind in-flight GPU work, so the host reads unfinished memory. Instrumentation is in the issue. The bug reproduces on MRV1 and MRV2 and with both PIECEWISE and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE.

The change:

- **One logit per request** (`max_logits_per_req == 1` and `num_logits_indices == num_reqs`): the offsets are `[0, 1, ..., num_reqs]`, built on the host directly.
- **Otherwise** (speculative decoding with fast prefill, e.g. #63553): use a blocking copy. Correctness requires the values now. A sync-free alternative would pass the host-side per-request logits counts from the model runner (MRV2 already has `cu_num_logits_np` in `FastPrefillHelper.prepare`). I kept that out of this fix to avoid touching `CommonAttentionMetadata` and the runners, and I'm happy to follow up.

Relation to #60445: it builds the same one-logit host offsets with `arange`, so that path overlaps. Its multi-logit fallback still uses `.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)`, which has the same race. This PR makes the fallback safe to read immediately and adds regression tests for both paths, so it is worth merging on its own; whichever lands second can drop the duplicate one-logit branch.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Release temporary device KV bindings after graph profiling
author: zhenwenqi2024
body:
## Overview

Release HiSparse's temporary device KV bindings after CUDA-graph memory profiling, while preserving the engine-scoped registered host pool for the real KV cache.

## Claims

- Live attention handles and runtimes no longer retain the throwaway KV slab and its per-binding tables after profiling cleanup.
- Cleanup is idempotent. Rebinding preserves host registration and clears stale hot-cache tags before the new backing is consumed.
- No throughput, accuracy, or reproduced model OOM improvement is claimed.

## Validation

### Review follow-up (2026-11-04)

- Both the runtime and attention handle now use `_reset_binding_state()` from construction and unbinding. Persistent index-group/draft membership is retained.
- Removed the `runtimes` argument from `release_pinned_state()`. Connector shutdown/error paths detach their attention handles; the Host release helper retains its existing drain, unregistration and shared-region cleanup responsibilities.
- Also fixed an adjacent partial-initialization failure path: if KV binding fails before initialization returns, already-bound context handles are detached before the Host-pool reference is dropped.
- Removed redundant handle deduplication and the extra bind-time Hot-state reset. Real model capture retains ownership of the existing connector reset; the throwaway profiling capture uses a no-op connector.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. Four source-isolated CPU lifecycle checks passed (2.52 s), covering storage detachment, repeated cleanup, shutdown and partial-binding rollback. These checks use real CPU tensors/handles with external device services substituted; they are not full-package or device tests.
- Full-package pytest collection was blocked by missing `tblib`. Fresh CUDA/model validation of this follow-up has not been run. Device/model results from the initial submission below remain historical and do not validate this revision.

### Review follow-up (2026-11-03)

- `release_pinned_state()` now calls the same `HiSparseRuntime.unbind_cache()` used by profiling cleanup. Final shutdown retains its existing synchronization, Host unregistration, and shared-region cleanup; profiling cleanup retains the registered Host pool.
- Added a HiSparse-op availability skip guard to the Host-pool reuse test. Its teardown also exercises `release_pinned_state()` on the already-unbound real runtime.
- Narrowed the device regression to binding a temporary 64 MiB backing with a real runtime/attention handle, then checking that profiling cleanup drops the views and releases the allocation. Removed the unrelated gather, rebind, and graph-replay checks from this test; Host-pool reuse remains covered separately.
- Local pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed for the follow-up. The Dockerfile graph hook was checked separately through Git Bash; actionlint had no applicable workflow files.
- The device/model results below are historical results from the initial submission, not a rerun of this follow-up. Updated GPU tests have not been rerun locally.

Functional validation completed in the current container; the human submitter reviewed the change and approved submission.

- Current H200 container, frozen main 24e80c261428cc45200b28f77fd0e2fdc36a56a8 plus existing PR63801 changes; unchanged matching native libraries.
- New storage-lifetime regression before this fix: 1 failed, at the retained-view weak-reference assertion (2.94 s).
- The same regression after this fix: 1 passed (2.80 s).
- Compute Sanitizer memcheck: 1 passed, ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors.
- Adjacent eviction, MTP multi-step, and invalidation contracts: 7 passed.
- Real GLM-5.2-FP8 TP8/MTP3 startup, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, CUDA graph memory profiling enabled: passed through profiling capture, teardown, real KV initialization, final capture, and API readiness. Available KV cache memory: 31.11 GiB. Four concurrent greedy requests succeeded (103/128/128/70 output tokens); no request errors or pre-cleanup ERROR lines. This is a short serving smoke, not accuracy or performance evaluation.
- Existing host-pool cleanup test migrated from fake runtime objects to real runtime/handle/pool objects; worker HiSparse subset: 15 passed. Original fake-object test failure is preserved.
- Final committed tests: 2 passed (3.47 s) after adopting torch.accelerator memory queries and explicit type-narrowing assertions.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed, including pinned Ruff, typos, mypy (Python 3.11), Buildkite keys, test tethering, and API checks. actionlint was skipped because no GitHub Actions workflow changed; Dockerfile graph check was run successfully via Git Bash (Windows lacks /bin/bash for its direct shebang). CI YAML parsing and git diff --check also passed.
- The standalone startup wrapper failed during intentional cleanup with pidfd EINVAL, after all requests completed. The original failed state and post-termination EngineDeadError logs are preserved. An independent audit verified no surviving task processes and all eight GPUs at 0 MiB/0% utilization; the model was not rerun to replace this evidence.
- Evidence archive (retained locally): profiling-cache-release-current-v2-evidence.tar.gz, SHA256 2dc1cbdb80d271bcf37e265bb498641db3e57a8a87c6b901fab37ecb97d9cdd2; 63 files hash-verified. Original downloaded evidence had 56 individually verified files; v2 adds final committed tests and contribution checks.

The contributed patch is isolated against main 5d55ef1590c92213e3893dc8e8712f7f2e0bc508. Latest-main native validation was cancelled in favor of validating the fix directly in the user's current container. No CUDA source or package dependency is changed by this patch. NPU and ROCm hardware were not validated.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Run from the configured vLLM checkout:

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_profiling_releases_device_storage \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py::test_profiling_cleanup_keeps_host_pool_for_real_kv_cache -v

compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --report-api-errors extended --error-exitcode 42 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_profiling_releases_device_storage -v -s

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  -k 'hisparse or profiling_cleanup' -v

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -v \
  -k 'test_hisparse_resident_rows_bypass_hot_lru or test_hisparse_swap_in_preserves_rows_across_eviction or test_hisparse_multi_step_swaps_match_independent or test_hisparse_multi_step_writes_request_major_output or test_hisparse_newest_write_and_recycled_slot_invalidation or test_hisparse_invalidation_covers_every_index_group'
```

The current device regression binds a 64 MiB temporary backing with a real attention handle and runtime, then checks dead view weak references and the fall in allocated device memory after profiling cleanup. The separate worker test checks Host-pool reuse. The earlier, broader regression also checked rebinding and graph replay; its historical validation is recorded above.

</details>

## Details

The profiling teardown clears the runner's normal caches, but model layers still own HiSparseCacheHandle objects. Their PagedCacheView and Runtime.hot keep the temporary device backing alive. release_pinned_state(..., []) removes only some runtime aliases; it does not detach those handle-owned device views.

Separate per-binding detachment from final host-pool shutdown. Keep the permanent index group, streams, and shared workspaces; drop only storage and metadata associated with the old KV binding. Group leaders reset the existing hot state when binding new storage.

Duplicate-work review: #61668 is the merged host-pool reuse change and leaves these device aliases attached. The inspected open ROCm PR #60358 addresses other cleanup/registration behavior, without this device-binding detachment. Searches for HiSparse profiling release and the exact cleanup function found no open PR addressing this fix as of 2026-11-01.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Report the line of a run-batch request rejected by request validators
author: Arsh624
body:
## Overview

`vllm run-batch` checks every input line before loading the model and reports a bad one as `Invalid request on line N: ...`. That only works for pydantic errors. A line that fails one of vLLM's own request checks, such as an empty `prompt`, `stream_options` without `stream`, or `top_logprobs` without `logprobs`, crashes the run with a bare `VLLMValidationError` traceback that doesn't say which line is bad.

## Claims

- `validate_batch` now reports `VLLMValidationError` from the chat and completion request models the same way as pydantic errors: `Invalid request on line N: <message>`, before the model loads.

## Validation

Repro (3-line batch, line 3 has `"prompt": ""`), `vllm run-batch -i bad.jsonl -o out.jsonl --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`:

- Before: `vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: Either prompt or prompt_embeds must be provided and non-empty. (parameter=prompt)` (no line number).
- After: `ValueError: Invalid request on line 3: Either prompt or prompt_embeds must be provided and non-empty. (parameter=prompt)`, exit 1 after about 10 seconds, without loading the model. Same for a chat line with `top_logprobs` but no `logprobs`.

Tests (RTX 4070 Laptop, WSL2 Ubuntu, Python 3.12):

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k validate_batch
```

- Without the fix: the new `test_validate_batch_reports_request_validation_errors` fails in both cases with `VLLMValidationError` (2 failed, 2 passed).
- With the fix: 4 passed.

<details>
<summary>Test output before and after</summary>

Fix reverted, new test kept:

```
FAILED tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py::test_validate_batch_reports_request_validation_errors[/v1/completions-body0]
FAILED tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py::test_validate_batch_reports_request_validation_errors[/v1/chat/completions-body1]
vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py:626: vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: Either prompt or prompt_embeds must be provided and non-empty. (parameter=prompt)
vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py:866: vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: Stream options can only be defined when `stream=True`. (parameter=stream_options)
2 failed, 2 passed, 61 deselected, 2 warnings in 1.32s
```

With the fix:

```
4 passed, 61 deselected, 2 warnings in 1.11s
```

</details>

- Full `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py`: 54 passed. The other 11 are the subprocess tests that start an engine at the default `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92`, which my 8 GB laptop GPU can't provide (`Free memory on device cuda:0 (6.83/8.0 GiB) ... less than desired`). The same 11 fail with the same error on main without this change. A valid batch still runs normally with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.6`.
- `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, typos, test tethering).

## Details

The request models' `mode="before"` validators raise `VLLMValidationError`, which is a `VLLMClientError`, not a `ValueError`, so pydantic doesn't wrap it in a `ValidationError` and it escapes the `except` in `validate_batch`. The fix adds it to that `except`. The runtime path (`run_one_request`) is unchanged; it only parses lines that already passed validation. The test calls `validate_batch` directly, like the existing `validate_batch` tests, because the failure happens before any engine starts.

This doesn't overlap #64102, which handles a missing or non-string `url` (a `KeyError` in `check_type_for_url`). The code changes don't conflict, but both PRs add a test right after `test_validate_batch_rejects_malformed_request`, so whichever lands second needs a small test-file merge.

I found this while using Claude Code to test `vllm run-batch` on main against deliberately invalid batch files, on a local Qwen3-0.6B. Claude Code also wrote the first version of the fix and the test. I reproduced the crash on my machine, reviewed every changed line, and ran the tests and pre-commit above myself.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Report the prompt cache split in the first streamed usage
author: subin9
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65035. The first continuous-usage chunk of a Chat Completions stream now carries `prompt_tokens_details`, so the Anthropic `message_start` reports the same split as `message_delta`.

## Claims

- With `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`, the first streamed usage chunk carries the same `cached_tokens` and `created_cache_tokens` as the final one.
- `message_start.usage.input_tokens` excludes cache reads and writes, matching `message_delta`.

## Validation

```
# unit test, base
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k test_streaming_first_chunk_reports_prompt_tokens_details
E       KeyError: 'prompt_tokens_details'
1 failed, 221 deselected
# unit tests, this branch
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k "usage or prompt_tokens_details"
124 passed, 98 deselected
```

End to end on v0.32.0 (MI300X, Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, `--enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details`), the issue's reproducer, second request:

| | `message_start` | `message_delta` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v0.32.0 | `input_tokens` 3656, no cache fields | 520 uncached, 3136 cache read, 0 written |
| v0.32.0 + this patch | 520 uncached, 3136 cache read, 0 written | 520 uncached, 3136 cache read, 0 written |

`test_anthropic_streaming_cache_usage` now expects the split in `message_start`. It needs a GPU server, so I checked that behaviour with the run above instead.

## Details

The first iteration already reads `num_cached_tokens` and `num_cache_creation_tokens`, but only the final usage chunk passed them to `_make_prompt_tokens_details`. The first chunk now does too. With the flag off it still returns `None`, so cache fields stay absent as #40912 intends.
