title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Keep P/D prompt tails on FULL graphs with adaptive verification
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview On a P/D decode instance with adaptive verification (AV), a step that admits a KV-transferred request runs eager instead of replaying the FULL decode graph, and under DP every rank runs eager with it. This PR fixes the condition that rejects the graph, in the runner and in the EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP drafter: two lines. ## Claims - **Before.** On D, a transferred request recomputes its last prompt token, so it is scheduled as 1 real token + K placeholder drafts, the shape of a decode row. It still counts as prefilling (`has_prefill=True`). The AV path (#57263) drops the query-length bound for any batch with `has_prefill`, so the AV decode graph rejects the step. The step runs eager under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (PIECEWISE under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), and the requests already decoding in the batch run eager with it. DP ranks agree on the bound, so one rank's arrival makes every rank run eager. - **After.** The bound is dropped only when the batch is not `decode_graph_eligible` (#58400). That existing classifier admits a one-token extension over existing KV and rejects real prefills, and the non-AV decode path already uses it. The drafter uses the same condition, so it keeps the target's padded layout (#62796). - **Effect.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark, vLLM P/D recipe settings at 1P1D DEP4. On main, eager steps (about 6x slower than FULL) take 60–77% of D's time, and most of them are ranks pulled eager by another rank's arrival. With this PR all of them replay FULL: output throughput is **2.0x** (OSL 256) and **1.76x** (OSL 1024), and D TPOT goes from 19.2 to 6.95 ms and from 10.6 to 5.69 ms. - **No degradation expected.** The changed value only feeds CUDA graph dispatch, and matching is monotonic: a bound where there was `None` can only add a match, since graphs without a bound match either way. Only AV captures bounded graphs, so dispatch without AV is unchanged. Real prefills (multi-token prompts, one-token prompts without prior KV, PCP batches) still run eager or PIECEWISE. GSM8K and draft acceptance stay within the baseline's run-to-run spread (DSpark and MTP, TP4 and DEP4). - **No extra resources.** No new graphs are captured, so graph count, CUDA graph memory and KV cache size are unchanged. The condition is a host-side bool already computed each step, so there is no new GPU sync or DP collective. - **Trade-offs.** An arrival step now pads its requests to the graph's capture size, the same padding every decode step pays; it is still about 6x faster than eager in the runs below. With D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, arrival steps move from PIECEWISE to FULL; D TPOT is unchanged within noise (TP4 cross-check below).
Code path on main: why an arrival step runs eager 1. **The arriving request counts as prefilling.** `prefill_len` is the number of tokens handed to the runner ([`states.py#L106`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py#L106)), usually the prompt length. `num_computed_prefill_tokens = min(num_computed_tokens, prefill_len)` ([`model_runner.py#L1332-L1336`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1332-L1336)). On D, the transferred KV covers all but the last prompt token, so the request arrives with `num_computed = prefill_len - 1` and is prefilling ([`#L1385-L1386`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1385-L1386)). After that step `num_computed >= prefill_len`, and the request decodes. 2. **`has_prefill` clears the bound.** The runner passes `max_query_len = None` for any batch with `has_prefill` ([`model_runner.py#L1848-L1851`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1848-L1851)), and so does the drafter ([`speculator.py#L273`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/target_dependent_ar/speculator.py#L273)). 3. **DP spreads `None`.** Ranks exchange the bound and keep it only if no rank sent `None` ([`dp_utils.py#L117-L119`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/dp_utils.py#L117-L119)). 4. **AV decode graphs need a bound.** With AV, decode graphs are captured as varlen graphs with `max_query_len=decode_query_len` ([`cudagraph_utils.py#L305-L319`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L305-L319)). A bounded graph matches only a batch that carries a bound within it ([`cudagraph_utils.py#L130-L133`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L130-L133)), so a `None` batch matches no decode graph. Under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` there is no PIECEWISE graph to fall back to, so the step runs eager. 5. **Without AV this does not happen.** Uniform decode graphs carry no bound and are matched by `uniform_token_count`, which already uses `decode_graph_eligible` ([`model_runner.py#L1404`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1404), [`utils.py#L1011`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L1011)). An arrival row (1 real token + K placeholder drafts) is uniform with the decode rows, so the step replays FULL. This PR uses `decode_graph_eligible` in step 2, the same classifier step 5 already uses.
## Validation All runs use upstream main `b8c04dd3b4` with that commit's precompiled wheel, 1P1D on two GB200 nodes over NIXL, with a fresh P/D pair per run. "Baseline" is that main commit without this PR. ### Performance The deployment follows the vLLM recipe preset for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (`gb300_agentx_pd`, from InferenceX #3941), scaled to one GB200 node per role: - P: DEP4, 64 seqs/rank, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, no AV. - D: DEP4, 40 seqs/rank, `max_num_batched_tokens=400`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with capture sizes 6..240, AV on, no prefix caching. - Both: DSpark K=5, MegaAttention, MegaMoE, DeepSelect top-k, Engram CPU offload. The client keeps 320 requests in flight (2x D capacity). Each request goes to P with `max_tokens=1`, then streams from D. Prompts are unique, outputs use `ignore_eos`, and 640 warmup requests run first. Baseline and this PR run in ABAB order; the table shows both rounds. TPOT and TTFT are measured on the D stream; TTFT includes queueing, since the client oversubscribes D. | Workload | Version | Output tok/s | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ISL ~290, OSL 256, 4096 req | baseline | 4,100 / 4,385 | 19.0 / 19.4 ms | 33.4 / 32.8 ms | 7.4 / 6.8 s | | | this PR | **8,559 / 8,519** | **6.93 / 6.97 ms** | 10.5 / 10.5 ms | 3.6 / 3.7 s | | ISL ~2.2K, OSL 1024, 2048 req | baseline | 8,533 / 8,666 | 10.7 / 10.6 ms | 19.3 / 19.4 ms | 13.0 / 12.8 s | | | this PR | **15,099 / 15,231** | **5.71 / 5.66 ms** | 9.9 / 10.1 ms | 7.3 / 7.2 s | **Why it is large under data parallelism.** DP ranks agree on one graph shape per step, and the agreed query-length bound is `None` if any rank sends `None`. So a single rank admitting a transferred request forces every rank's step to run eager, including ranks that only have decodes. A second traced run of the same setup splits D's steps per rank (4 ranks, warmup excluded). Step time is the gap to the next step on the same rank: | Workload | Version | Own arrival steps | Decode steps forced eager by another rank | FULL decode steps | Time in eager steps | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | OSL 256 | baseline | 11.7%, eager, 102 ms | **20.5%, 102 ms** | 67.8%, 15.0 ms | 77% | | | this PR | 10.0%, FULL, 15.2 ms | 0 | 90.0%, 15.4 ms | 0 | | OSL 1024 | baseline | 5.4%, eager, 101 ms | **13.0%, 101 ms** | 81.6%, 17.1 ms | 60% | | | this PR | 5.5%, FULL, 16.1 ms | 0 | 94.5%, 17.7 ms | 0 | Steps forced eager by another rank outnumber a rank's own arrival steps 1.75–2.4x. The chance that some rank admits a request in a given step rises with the DP size, so we expect the effect to be larger on the recipe's DEP16 decode (not measured here). The gain depends on how often a decode step admits a transferred request, so it is smaller for longer outputs. In the TP4 cross-check below, D under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with this PR reaches the same TPOT (6.7 ms) as the same D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, where arrival steps ran PIECEWISE instead of eager.
TP4 cross-check: P PIECEWISE, D TP4 FULL_DECODE_ONLY + AV, 128 seqs, 128 in flight, ISL ~290, OSL 256, 3 ABAB rounds | Model | Version | TPOT mean (3 rounds) | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark K=3 | baseline | 17.8 / 20.0 / 20.0 ms | 29.9-31.0 ms | 1.08-1.12 s | | | this PR | 6.72 / 6.70 / 6.75 ms | 9.4 ms | 0.40-0.42 s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP K=3 | baseline | 17.8 / 24.7 / 25.8 ms | 35.0-37.6 ms | 1.41-1.54 s | | | this PR | 5.42 / 5.41 / 5.38 ms | 7.1-7.2 ms | 0.37-0.39 s | Same workload with D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, where main runs arrival steps PIECEWISE and this PR runs them FULL: | Model | Version | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark K=3 | baseline | 6.72 ms | 9.38 ms | 0.44 s | | | this PR | 6.75 ms | 9.27 ms | 0.41 s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP K=3 | baseline | 5.44 / 5.68 ms | 7.41 / 7.48 ms | 0.47 / 0.39 s | | | this PR | 5.33 ms | 7.19 ms | 0.39 s |
### Correctness Setup: - P and D TP4 + EP. - D: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` + AV, 128 seqs. - The decode-side graph mode is traced per step on all ranks; the ranks agree. - "Arrival step" means a decode-eligible batch with `has_prefill`, i.e. it contains a transferred request computing its last prompt token. Workload per run: - 8 serial prompts (19..8195 tokens), 16 staggered and 32 burst requests. - Two direct-to-D negative controls: a multi-token prompt without transferred KV, and a fresh one-token prompt. - Full GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 8, temperature 0. **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=3)** | Version | Arrival steps | Real prefills | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 1128 eager | 6 eager | 1190 / 1319 | 1.962 | | this PR | **1316 FULL** | 6 eager | 1194 / 1319 | 1.961 | | baseline, repeat | | | 1187 / 1319 | 1.976 | **DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP (K=3)**, which uses `TargetDependentARSpeculator` | Version | Arrival steps: target / drafter | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | eager / eager (1010) | 1248 / 1319 | 1.879 | | runner condition only | FULL / **eager** (1168) | 1249 / 1319 | 1.877 | | this PR | **FULL / FULL** (1163) | 1253 / 1319 | 1.873 | **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=5), DEP4 recipe config from the performance section** | Version | Own arrival steps | Decode steps forced eager by another rank | Real prefills | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 5.0%, eager | 11.7%, eager | 2 eager | 1193 / 1319 | 2.067 | | this PR | 5.1%, **FULL** | **0** | 2 eager | 1184 / 1319 | 2.049 | | baseline, repeat | | | | 1196 / 1319 | 2.048 | | this PR, repeat | | | | 1200 / 1319 | 2.090 | Serving with expert parallelism is not bitwise deterministic run to run. Baseline spans 1193–1196 and 2.048–2.067; this PR spans 1184–1200 and 2.049–2.090. Between the first baseline and first PR runs, 45 questions flip correct → wrong and 36 wrong → correct. With only the runner condition, an arrival step replays the target graph padded to, for example, 32 requests, while the drafter runs eager over the 7 real ones on the same attention metadata. That is the mismatch #62796 removed. On this sparse-MLA model it costs no measurable acceptance; #62793 shows that it does on FA3. In every run, all measured requests succeeded, with no preemptions and no KV transfer failures. Pure decode steps are FULL in every run, except the startup warmup steps, which run eager. The GSM8K and acceptance differences fall within the baseline repeat spread.
Unit tests ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dp_utils.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py # 116 passed, on the branch rebased onto current main ``` - Reverting only the runner condition fails `test_prompt_tail_keeps_decode_graph_bound[True-8]`. - Reverting only the drafter condition fails `test_draft_prefill_matches_shared_target_metadata_shape[decode-eligible-prefill-tail]`. - Both files already run in CI under `tests/v1/worker` and `tests/v1/cudagraph`.
## Details **Request path.** 1. The proxy sends the prompt to P with `max_tokens=1` and `do_remote_decode`; P prefills and returns KV transfer metadata. 2. The proxy sends the same prompt with that metadata to D. D's scheduler pulls the KV over NIXL and marks the whole prompt as computed. 3. On load completion, the scheduler sets `num_computed_tokens = N - 1`, so D recomputes the last prompt position to get logits for its first sampled token. With K speculative tokens, the request is scheduled as 1 real token + K placeholder drafts (`q = K + 1`): the shape of a decode row. 4. The runner classifies the batch and dispatches a CUDA graph. This step is the one that changes. **Root cause.** In step 4, the request is still prefilling (`num_computed_prefill < prefill_len`), so `has_prefill` is True. - #57263 cleared the runner's `max_query_len` for any batch with `has_prefill`, because a varlen decode graph matched on that bound alone would admit a short real prefill. - Two days later, #58400 added `decode_graph_eligible`, which treats a one-token extension over existing context as a decode. Input preparation already handles this case through `prefill_runs_as_decode`. #58400 wired the classification into the uniform decode path only. - The varlen path that AV uses kept the `has_prefill` check. So with AV off, D replays FULL on arrival steps; with AV on, it does not. - `TargetDependentARSpeculator.propose` has the same check for its draft-prefill dispatch. **Dispatch before and after.** The red edge is main's path for a P/D arrival step; the green edge is the path this PR takes. Real prefills take the grey path in both. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["D step: transferred request = 1 real token + K placeholder drafts
(+ requests already decoding)"] --> B["gather_batch_req_state
has_prefill = True
decode_graph_eligible = True"] P["Real prefill: multi-token prompt, or one-token prompt without context"] --> Q["decode_graph_eligible = False"] Q --> N B -->|"main: if has_prefill"| N["max_query_len = None"] B -->|"this PR: if not decode_graph_eligible"| K["max_query_len = K + 1"] N --> S["DP sync: the agreed bound is None if any rank sent None"] S --> X["AV varlen FULL decode graph rejected on every DP rank
FULL_DECODE_ONLY → eager · FULL_AND_PIECEWISE → PIECEWISE"] K --> Y["AV varlen FULL decode graph replayed
(drafter draft-prefill uses the same bound and padded layout)"] linkStyle 3 stroke:#d62728,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 4 stroke:#2ca02c,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 2 stroke:#999999 ``` Without AV, the decode graph is matched by `uniform_token_count`, which already uses `decode_graph_eligible`, so arrival steps were not affected. **Change.** - Two conditions change from `has_prefill` to `not decode_graph_eligible`: one in `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`, one in `TargetDependentARSpeculator.propose`. The other edits update comments that described the old rule. - The classifier, scheduler, input preparation, capture sizes and kernels are unchanged. - Keeping the bound only removes one rejection reason. The existing graph checks (query-length bound, request/token coverage, explicit eager, DP agreement on the bound) still apply. - DFlash/DSpark drafters dispatch with a fixed uniform shape and are not affected. - Model Runner V1 does not support AV, so it needs no change. **Relation to #64915.** #64915 contains the same runner condition as part of a larger feature: varlen decode graphs for fixed-width speculation, with new backend and capacity checks. This PR is only the AV bug fix. It adds the drafter condition, which #64915 lacks, plus a regression test and P/D validation with real KV transfer, which #64915 lists as outstanding. If this PR merges first, #64915 drops the overlapping line. No other open PR changes these conditions. **Limitations.** - GPU validation covers DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DSpark) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MTP) on GB200 with the MLA backends those models use. FA3/FlashInfer targets are covered only by the unit test of the drafter/target layout contract. - The performance runs are 1P1D with D scaled down from the recipe's DEP16 to DEP4. Prompts are synthetic, with no prefix reuse. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, implementation, validation and this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the results. ---

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Skip MoE-LoRA shrink/expand when no LoRA is active
author: chaojun-zhang
body:
## Overview

Skip the MoE-LoRA shrink/expand launches when there are no active LoRAs, fixing a segmentation fault on XPU in `test_fused_moe_lora_kernel_zero_grid_no_crash[two_kernel]` ([Intel CI build 16155](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/16155#01a19356-b9b6-4244-a603-173c195758e5)). Follow-up to #64653.

## Claims

- `_fused_moe_lora_shrink` / `_fused_moe_lora_expand` no longer launch a Triton grid with a zero dimension when `num_active_loras == 0`.
- The output is left unchanged in that case, as the existing test asserts.

## Validation

- Before: `pytest tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -k zero_grid_no_crash` on XPU (Arc Pro B60, torch 2.14) -> `Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault`.
- After: `pytest tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` on XPU -> 463 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: passed.

 

---

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Only set PDL launch attr for MoE top-k gating on SM90+
author: srkim-business
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65055. Since #59737, `topkGating` is launched with the PDL attribute on every CUDA arch. Pre-SM90 GPUs cannot use PDL, but stream capture still records the attribute as a programmatic edge in the CUDA graph, and replaying those graphs is slower. This PR sets the attribute only when the device is SM90+. SM90+ keeps the #59737 behaviour; older GPUs launch without the attribute, which measured the same as the v0.32 `<<<>>>` launch. The standalone effect was measured on sm80, sm86 and sm89; end-to-end numbers are A100 only.

## Claims

- 4× A100, TP4 + EP + MTP (our deployment config, private NVFP4 checkpoint of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; setup below): per-request decode is 6.5–13.6% faster in 17 of 18 prompt × concurrency (1–16) cells, and 2.1% in the 18th. At concurrency 16: prose 74.3 → 80.1 and code 88.7 → 94.8 tok/s, close to the last commit before #59737 (3b05805d4: 81.5 and 95.3, one run).
- Standalone CUDA (no vLLM): the attribute adds one programmatic edge per launch and 0.6–1.1 µs of graph replay per edge on A100 (sm80), RTX A4000 (sm86) and RTX 4090 (sm89), in every round; without the attribute `cudaLaunchKernelEx` matches `<<<>>>`.
- 1× A100, CUDA graph replay of a router GEMM → `topk_softmax` chain: 6.9–9.0% faster for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Qwen3-30B-A3B and OLMoE shapes at 1/16/48 tokens, in every round against a no-change rebuild.
- 1× A100 end to end, `vllm bench latency`: batch 1 is 0.7% faster for OLMoE-1B-7B (every round vs a no-change rebuild, 2 of 3 rounds vs the shipped build) and 1.2% faster for Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 (every round). Batch 16 is within noise for both.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K 5-shot on Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 is 85.90% (base) vs 86.13% (fix). The kernel body is identical.
- SM90+ is unchanged by construction (the same attribute is set as before); not measured.

## Validation

Hardware: A100-PCIE-40GB, driver 590.48.01, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, vLLM v0.33.0 (4ba787ec9). `base` = the v0.33.0 `_moe_C` as shipped. `rebuilt` = the same source built with the same toolchain, no change. `fix` = `rebuilt` + this diff. Builds are `_moe_C` only, for sm80, overlaid on the v0.33.0 install. The diff applies unchanged to main (the file is identical).

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py` on A100: base 864 passed, fix 864 passed.
- GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`): Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 85.90% → 86.13%; OLMoE-1B-7B (base model, near the floor with this script) 9.93% → 10.01%. Invalid rate 0–0.8%.
- CI: the L4 (sm89) "MoE Kernels" step runs `tests/kernels/moe` on `csrc/moe/` changes and covers the launch without the attribute; the SM90+ launch is unchanged. No new test: there is no functional change, and a regression check would need graph-edge inspection or timing, which does not belong in `tests/`.

**Op chain, CUDA graph, µs per replay** (median of 6 rounds, A/B/B/A order; Δ = median paired `fix − rebuilt`)

| shape (experts, top-k, hidden, layers) | tokens | base | rebuilt | fix | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (512, 10, 2560, 48) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 843 / 893 / 917 | 846 / 894 / 916 | 782 / 831 / 850 | −7.6% / −6.9% / −7.2% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (128, 8, 2048, 48) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 592 / 672 / 688 | 596 / 674 / 691 | 542 / 620 / 636 | −9.0% / −7.9% / −8.0% |
| OLMoE-1B-7B (64, 8, 2048, 16) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 194 / 209 / 221 | 194 / 209 / 221 | 177 / 192 / 204 | −8.7% / −8.4% / −7.8% |

**End to end, `vllm bench latency`** (input 128, output 256, 3 rounds, ms per step)

| model | batch | base | rebuilt | fix | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 | 1 | 2.952 | 2.950 | 2.932 | −0.7% (3/3 rounds vs rebuilt, 2/3 vs base) |
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 | 16 | 7.789 | 7.731 | 7.802 | within noise |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 1 | 5.805 | – | 5.722 | −1.2% (3/3 rounds) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 16 | 12.188 | – | 12.136 | within noise (2/3 rounds faster) |

<details>
<summary>TP4 setup</summary>

v0.33.0, 4× A100-PCIE-40GB, `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel`, NVFP4 weights, MTP with 2 draft tokens, `--compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, bf16 KV, a custom logits processor. Client: c concurrent streaming chat requests, 384 output tokens, model-default sampling; per-request decode = (tokens − 1) / (last − first token time), averaged. Prose / code / numbers prompts × c = 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16; two server starts per arm, A/B/B/A. With MTP, c = 1 varies by about ±10% from run to run through the draft acceptance rate.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Standalone CUDA reproduction (no vLLM) and commands</summary>

48 × (plain kernel → consumer kernel); only the consumer launch changes. A100, 21 rounds:

| consumer launch | graph replay, GPU µs | eager, GPU µs |
|---|---:|---:|
| `<<<>>>` | 128.7 | 239.8 |
| `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, no attribute | 128.7 | 239.3 |
| `cudaLaunchKernelEx` + PDL attribute | 181.8 | 239.8 |
| PDL attribute on the first consumer only | 130.3 | 239.4 |

Same harness, graph replay, other pre-Hopper GPUs (21 rounds, PDL attribute slower in every round):

| GPU (arch) | `<<<>>>` µs | + PDL attribute | per edge | `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, no attribute |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A100-PCIE-40GB (sm80) | 128.7 | +53.1 (+41%) | 1.1 µs | +0.03 |
| RTX A4000 (sm86) | 83.6 | +29.9 (+36%) | 0.62 µs | +0.11 |
| RTX 4090 (sm89) | 79.0 | +30.0 (+38%) | 0.63 µs | −0.10 |

`cudaGraphGetEdges` reports one programmatic edge per PDL launch on all three. The standalone harness and the op-chain script are in https://gist.github.com/srkim-business/ec5db57f7b78a9c9f06af65c891216c2.

```bash
# end to end (OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, batch 1 and 16)
vllm bench latency --model <model> --batch-size <1|16> --input-len 128 --output-len 256 \
  --num-iters-warmup 5 --num-iters 15 --seed 0 --max-model-len 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
# GSM8K
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --seed 0
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --seed 42 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64
# kernel tests
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Root cause: on pre-SM90 the attribute does nothing for eager launches, but stream capture records it as a programmatic edge (`cudaGraphGetEdges` counts one per launch on sm80). Each edge adds about 1.1 µs of GPU time per graph replay on A100.
- #59737 first had this host check (uncached); review asked to drop it for consistency with `topk_softplus_sqrt` / `per_token_group_quant` and to avoid `cudaGetDevice` + `call_once` per eager launch. The measurements above are the reason to bring it back. It is cached in a function-local static as in `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` (`numAttrs = (sm_version >= 90) ? 1 : 0`), so eager launches pay nothing per call. This also matches the scope in #59737's own description ("Enable PDL for the consumer on SM90+"). Python launch sites already gate PDL on `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`.
- The static is initialized once per template instantiation, on the device the caller's `DeviceGuard` selects. It assumes all GPUs in a process share the major arch, which holds for vLLM workers (one GPU each); a mismatch would only affect speed, not results.
- The 1-GPU gain (about 1%) matches the GPU-side edge cost. The TP4 + EP + MTP gain does not: at concurrency 16 a decode step goes from about 29.5 to 27.3 ms, while 48 edges × 1.1 µs is about 0.05 ms per forward; we have not located the rest. The TP4 A/B swaps only `_moe_C` (shipped → this diff built from the same source); on one GPU a no-change rebuild is within 0.8% (median) of the shipped build, so we attribute the gain to this diff.
- Other C++ launchers still set the attribute on all archs, for example `topk_softplus_sqrt_kernels.cu` and `per_token_group_quant.cu` (the latter can run on sm89 for FP8). They are left out to keep this fix small enough to cherry-pick; a shared helper can follow if maintainers prefer.
- Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR changes this launch attribute (searched `topkGating PDL`, `topk_softmax PDL`, `59737`). #62912 (open) changes top-k selection in the same file and keeps `config.numAttrs = 1` as context next to this change, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; it does not touch the attribute.
- Not covered: Hopper/Blackwell (unchanged code path, not measured), sm75 and older, end to end on GPUs other than A100, and a full main build (only `_moe_C` was rebuilt and overlaid on v0.33.0).
- This is a performance regression against v0.32.0; we'd like it cherry-picked into a v0.33.x patch release if one is planned.
- I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, the code and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix KV role detection for MultiConnector with nested connectors
author: xsxszab
body:
## Overview

`KVTransferConfig.is_kv_producer` and `is_kv_consumer` only look at the top-level `kv_role`, but a `MultiConnector` never passes that role to its child connectors; each child uses its own. The documented MooncakeStore prefiller (top-level `kv_producer`, with a `kv_both` MooncakeStore child) therefore does not look like a consumer, so the scheduler does not defer freeing blocks, and a step still running for an aborted request can overwrite KV that was just loaded into the reused blocks. This PR makes both properties follow the child connectors' roles.

Credit to @nandanadileep, who found this issue and proposed the first fix in [#62438](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62438), and is a co-author of this PR. #62438 defers block freeing for every connector; this PR instead fixes how a `MultiConnector`'s role is determined, so blocks are deferred only when one of its child connectors loads KV.

## Claims

- For a `MultiConnector`, `is_kv_producer` and `is_kv_consumer` follow the roles of its child connectors. The top-level `kv_role` no longer matters.
- The documented prefiller is now a consumer, so it defers block freeing and its loaded KV is no longer overwritten after an abort. If every child is `kv_producer`, blocks are still freed immediately.

## Validation

**Regression test.** `test_multi_connector_role_follows_children` checks both properties for four combinations of top-level and child roles. On main, the three where the top-level role disagrees with the children fail; with this PR, all four pass. It is marked `cpu_test`, so the CPU CI step runs it.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children
```

<details>
<summary>Output on main and with this PR (B300, trimmed)</summary>

```text
# vllm/ at main (db7f2d7c44), with this PR's test
$ cd tests && python -m pytest -v -m cpu_test v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -k role_follows_children
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[loading-child] FAILED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[pure-producers] PASSED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[saving-child] FAILED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[no-loading-child] FAILED

[loading-child]
>       assert config.is_kv_consumer is consumer
E       AssertionError: assert False is True
[saving-child]
>       assert config.is_kv_producer is producer
E       AssertionError: assert False is True
[no-loading-child]
>       assert config.is_kv_consumer is consumer
E       AssertionError: assert True is False

3 failed, 1 passed, 32 deselected in 2.06s

# this PR (1167d0cfa7), same command
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[loading-child] PASSED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[pure-producers] PASSED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[saving-child] PASSED
...::test_multi_connector_role_follows_children[no-loading-child] PASSED

4 passed, 32 deselected in 2.37s
```

</details>

**Effect on the documented configs.** For each config, I built a real `VllmConfig` (Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct) and a `PrometheusStatLogger` on main and with this PR. Changed values are shown as main → this PR.

| Config | `is_kv_consumer` | `is_kv_producer` | KV fetch metric | Requests may omit multimodal embeddings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prefiller: top-level `kv_producer`; MooncakeConnector `kv_producer` + MooncakeStore `kv_both` | False → True | True | missing → present | no → yes |
| Decoder: everything `kv_consumer` | True | False | present | yes |
| Top-level `kv_consumer`; MooncakeConnector `kv_consumer` + MooncakeStore `kv_both` | True | False → True | present | yes |

`is_kv_consumer` also decides whether the scheduler defers freeing blocks (only with async scheduling or PP), and `is_kv_producer` decides whether `finalize_partial_tail_offloads` runs when a request finishes.

**End to end.** The prefiller config on B300, PP=4, Model Runner V2, async scheduling, MooncakeStore over RDMA with `load_async`. Four concurrent loops each abort a request, then send a request whose prefix is loaded from MooncakeStore into the blocks just freed. Every loaded block is checksummed when its load completes and again before the request's first forward pass; a mismatch means the KV was overwritten in between.

| Model / setting | Top-level `kv_producer`, no deferred freeing | With deferred freeing | How deferred freeing was enabled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-32B, 1 s sleep added to the aborted request's steps | 13/24 loads overwritten | 0/24 | This PR |
| Qwen3-32B, no added sleep | 0/298 | 0/598 | This PR |
| Qwen2.5-7B, no added sleep (`70d67f19d`) | 0/300, 3/300, 3/300, 4/300 by PP rank | 0/303 on every rank | Top-level `kv_both` |

The added sleep runs on the compute stream in steps that contain the aborted request, so its writes land after the load and the overwrite shows up often.

## Details

**Root cause.** `Scheduler.__init__` sets `defer_block_free` from `kv_transfer_config.is_kv_consumer`. Deferring keeps a finished request's blocks out of the free pool until its in-flight steps are done. With the documented prefiller config:

1. Request A is aborted while one of its steps is still queued on the GPU.
2. The top-level role is `kv_producer`, so A's blocks go back to the free pool at once.
3. Request B finds its prefix in MooncakeStore and is given those blocks. The `kv_both` child loads B's KV into them over RDMA, which is not ordered with the GPU compute stream.
4. A's queued step runs and writes A's KV into the same blocks. B then computes on that KV without any error.

**Change.** For a `MultiConnector`, `is_kv_producer` and `is_kv_consumer` read each child's `kv_role` from `kv_connector_extra_config["connectors"]`, the same way `has_connector()` and `uses_custom_mem_pool()` read the children. Behavior only changes when the top-level role disagrees with the children, as in the three test cases that fail on main: a top-level `kv_producer` with a child that loads KV (the documented prefiller) becomes a consumer; a top-level `kv_consumer` with a `kv_both` child becomes a producer; and a top-level `kv_both` with only `kv_producer` children is no longer a consumer, so it frees blocks immediately, since nothing loads into them.

AI assistance: Claude Code for implementation, tests, and experiments; Claude Code and ChatGPT for this description. I reviewed the changes and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Muse Spark: merge the two process_weights_after_loading hooks
author: Alex-Wengg
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #65081, the pre-commit failure on `main` since #63440 merged:

```
vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py:1214: error: Name "process_weights_after_loading" already defined on line 1207  [no-redef]
```

#64357 and #63440 each added `process_weights_after_loading` to `MuseSpark1xForCausalLM`, and the second definition replaced the first. Every pre-commit run on `main` since 04:46 UTC has failed, so any PR that reruns CI fails it too (e.g. #65005).

## Claims

- One hook that runs `materialize_residual_path_constants`, then `maybe_attach_mono`.

## Details

- Order matters: materializing folds the router multiplier into `router.weight` and caches the gate coefficients, and the monokernel reads both, including when it refreshes after a reload.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this file's hook.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Keep numeric-string prompts as strings in CustomDataset
author: Vegetog
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65071. `CustomDataset.load_data()` lets `pd.read_json` infer the `prompt` column's dtype, so a JSONL file whose prompts are all numeric strings (`"00123"`, `"00456"`) is loaded as integers. Leading zeros are lost and `sample()` then fails in the tokenizer.

## Claims

- JSON string prompts are kept exactly as written, regardless of what other rows contain.
- `output_tokens` and other columns are unaffected.

## Validation

New regression test `test_custom_dataset_keeps_numeric_string_prompts` (CPU-only, local `WordLevel` tokenizer, no download) builds a real `CustomDataset` and calls `sample()`.

Before the fix (source reverted to `origin/main`):

```text
$ pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py -k numeric_string
E   ValueError: text input must be of type `str` (single example), `list[str]` ...
1 failed, 2 deselected
```

With the fix:

```text
$ pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py
3 passed
```

Lint: `pre-commit` hooks pass on the commit (ruff check/format, mypy, forbidden imports, test tethering). The test is picked up by the existing "Benchmarks CLI" step (`pytest -v -s benchmarks/`).

## Details

Root cause: pandas' default `dtype=True` coerces string columns that all parse as numbers. Passing `dtype={"prompt": str}` keeps the column as-is; other columns keep their current inference, so `output_tokens` behaviour is unchanged.

The other two `pd.read_json` callers in `datasets.py` read list-valued columns (`turns` / `messages`), which pandas does not coerce, so they are left alone.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #65071. #60506 and #61776 also touch `CustomDataset` but address output lengths / audio without a tokenizer in `sample()`, not the `read_json` dtype.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix Ling3 SwiGLU clamping
author: zexplorerhj
body:
## Overview

While investigating an accuracy issue during training–inference alignment for Ling RL, we found that routed experts applied the SwiGLU gate limit before SiLU, whereas the training/reference implementation applies it after SiLU. This mismatch can affect RL accuracy through inconsistent training and rollout computations, even though its impact is not obvious in standalone inference evaluations.

Use the existing `swiglustep` activation for Ling layers with a configured limit and forward that limit through the common MoE activation paths.

## Claims

- For limited Ling routed experts, compute `clamp(SiLU(gate), max=L) * clamp(up, -L, L)` instead of `SiLU(clamp(gate, max=L)) * clamp(up, -L, L)`.
- Honor the configured limit in both standard and masked `SWIGLUSTEP` activation paths.
- Keep unlimited Ling layers on `silu` and retain the default `SWIGLUSTEP` limit of `7.0` when no limit is supplied.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Reserve kpool decode indexer logits in workspace during profiling
author: vllmellm
body:
## Overview

Fixes #64874.

Serving `GLM-5.3-Flash` on ROCm crashes in decode once `batch_size * next_n * max_pool_len * 4` outgrows both the prefill K-gather workspace and the largest captured CUDA graph batch (`AssertionError: Workspace is locked but allocation from 'rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:...:rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits' requires 276.00 MB, current size is 265.00 MB`).

## Claims

- reserve the worst-case decode logits buffer on `current_workspace_manager()` during `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool`'s profiling pass, matching `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`, and keep the `torch.empty` reservation for the `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` prefill logits cap.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v -s tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py -k decode_logits_workspace

# serve + benchmark (96 concurrent decode requests -> 576 decode rows -> 288.00 MB)
# with or without --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0}' is the same, the bug doesn't depends on mm inputs
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0}' --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --port 8025

vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8025 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2200 --random-output-len 128 \
  --random-prefix-len 2150 \
  --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 96 --ignore-eos
```

| workload | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| unit test (`16 seqs x 6 = 96` decode rows, `max_pool_len=4096`) | `AssertionError: Workspace is locked ... requires 1.50 MB, current size is 1.27 MB` | passed |
| `GLM-5.3-Flash` e2e (`max_model_len=524288`, `max_num_seqs=128`, `MTP=5`, 92 concurrent requests = 552 decode rows) | `AssertionError: Workspace is locked ... requires 276.00 MB, current size is 265.00 MB` | 92/92 requests completed (locked workspace 384.00 MB) |

## Details

On ROCm, `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool` calls `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits(..., max_model_len=max_pool_len)` on decode, which takes `out_logits` of shape `(batch_size * next_n, max_pool_len)` in `float32` (or `(heads, batch_size * next_n, max_pool_len)` on the stage-1 fallback) from `current_workspace_manager()`. Its profiling branch (`if not isinstance(attn_metadata, dict):`) was copied from the CUDA implementation, where DeepGEMM allocates decode logits through the PyTorch caching allocator (`torch.empty`), so the ROCm workspace only ever saw the prefill K-gather buffers before `lock_workspace()`.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Fix scoring token limits with MistralTokenizer
author: anhtra3889
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65075. Bi-encoder scoring with a positive `max_tokens_per_query` or `max_tokens_per_doc` failed with a `TypeError` for models served with `MistralTokenizer`, because `truncate_text_to_tokens` always requested `return_offsets_mapping=True`. For `MistralTokenizer`, the cut point now comes from the decoded token prefix instead.

## Claims

- `max_tokens_per_query` and `max_tokens_per_doc` now work with `MistralTokenizer` in `LLM.score()`, `/score` and `/rerank`. Before, any positive limit failed (HTTP 400 online), even one that truncated nothing.
- A binding limit cuts the text to a prefix of the original with at most that many tokens. On every input tested, the cut lands at the same point as the HF `offset_mapping` path for the same model. A non-binding limit leaves the text unchanged.
- HF tokenizers are unaffected: they keep the existing `offset_mapping` code.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` with the default `--tokenizer-mode auto`, which selects `MistralTokenizer`. Only tokenization matters, so dummy weights and one layer are enough:

```bash
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 --runner pooling --convert embed \
  --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 1}' \
  --enforce-eager --max-model-len 1024

curl localhost:8000/rerank -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3",
  "query": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
  "documents": ["A fox is a small omnivorous mammal."],
  "max_tokens_per_query": 3
}'
```

The same requests were also sent to `/score`, using `"queries"` instead of `"query"`. Both endpoints gave identical results:

| Limits in the request | `main` (76c6f3f2a9) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | 200, 26 prompt tokens | 200, 26 prompt tokens |
| `max_tokens_per_doc: 100` (does not bind) | 400 | 200, 26 prompt tokens |
| `max_tokens_per_query: 3` | 400 | 200, 18 prompt tokens (query cut from 11 tokens to 3) |

Each 400 was `MistralTokenizer.__call__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'return_offsets_mapping'`.

**New tests.** Both fail on `main` with that `TypeError` and pass with this PR:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_utils.py -k mistral -v               # main: 2 failed; PR: 2 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_bi_encoder_offline.py -k mistral -v  # main: 1 failed; PR: 1 passed
```

<details>
<summary>Regression suites, cut-point comparison with the HF path, and the issue's script</summary>

Regression suites, all passing with this PR:

```bash
# 34 passed: the new unit tests plus the existing scoring unit tests
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_utils.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py

# 11 passed, including the moved Mistral test
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_bi_encoder_offline.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_cross_encoder_offline.py

# 20 passed: exact prompt-token counts through /rerank with HF tokenizers on
# jina-reranker-v2, jina-reranker-v3, Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, multilingual-e5-small
# and answerai-colbert-small-v1
pytest -v tests/models/language/pooling/test_max_tokens_per_doc.py
```

`pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files passes.

To compare cut points with the HF path, each repo was loaded with both `tokenizer_mode="mistral"` and `tokenizer_mode="hf"`. `truncate_text_to_tokens` then ran at every limit from 1 to the full length on 10 strings covering English, whitespace runs, newlines, accented Latin, CJK, emoji, code and punctuation:

| Model | Tokenizer | Identical cut points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` | SentencePiece | 164 / 164 (one string skipped: the two tokenizers already split its leading spaces differently) |
| `mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407` | Tekken | 134 / 134 |

The issue's script calls `BiEncoderIOProcessor._truncate_scoring_data` with limits 0, 1 and 100. On `main`, 1 and 100 raise the `TypeError`. With this PR, 1 gives `['The']` / `['A']`, and 0 and 100 return the input unchanged.

</details>

**Model evaluation.** Not run. Outputs change only for requests that used to fail, and the HF path is untouched (see `test_max_tokens_per_doc.py` above).

## Details

**Root cause.** `truncate_text_to_tokens`, added in #38827, calls `tokenizer(text, add_special_tokens=False, return_offsets_mapping=True)` before checking the length. vLLM's `MistralTokenizer.__call__` has a fixed signature without that argument, so every positive limit raised, even for text already within it. Forwarding the argument would not help, because transformers' `MistralCommonBackend` raises a `ValueError` for `return_offsets_mapping=True`. This went unnoticed because `test_max_tokens_per_doc.py` only covers HF tokenizers.

**Who is affected.** Pooling models that end up with `MistralTokenizer`: either `--tokenizer-mode mistral`, or the default `auto` on official Mistral repos, such as `--convert embed` on `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3`. Bi-encoder, late-interaction and Jina-ranking scoring all go through `_truncate_scoring_data`, so they share the fix. Cross-encoder scoring already rejects `MistralTokenizer`. Popular Mistral-based embedding models (e5-mistral, SFR-Embedding-Mistral, Linq-Embed-Mistral) ship HF tokenizers and were never affected.

**Fix.** For `MistralTokenizer`, the helper encodes the text, decodes the first `max_tokens` ids, and cuts the original text at the length of that decoded prefix. The existing loop then re-encodes and repeats until the text fits, as on the offsets path. The result is therefore always a prefix of the original text and never exceeds the limit. `skip_special_tokens=True` is required: without it, `MistralTokenizer.decode` returns raw SentencePiece pieces (`'▁line▁one<0x0A>line'`), whose length doesn't match the original text.

**Why `is_mistral_tokenizer`.** `MistralTokenizer.is_fast` is `True`, so an `is_fast` check (what `HfRenderer._can_produce_offsets` uses) would still send it down the offsets path. The renderer's private method also isn't reachable from this helper. The cross-encoder processor uses the same `is_mistral_tokenizer` check to reject Mistral.

**Cost.** A binding limit usually takes two encodes, one to find the cut and one to confirm it, plus one decode of at most `max_tokens` ids. The worst case on the strings above was four passes. Only `MistralTokenizer` takes the new branch.

**Tests.** The unit test covers both Mistral tokenizer formats, SentencePiece and Tekken. The end-to-end test, in `test_bi_encoder_offline.py`, goes through `LLM.score()` with `PoolingParams(extra_kwargs=...)`. It checks that the prompt token ids match scoring `"What is the"` against the unchanged document. It uses dummy weights and one layer, so it downloads only config and tokenizer files (about 620 KB). It sets `gpu_memory_utilization=0.3` so it fits next to the file's module-scoped e5 engine. Both tests run in the "Entrypoints Integration (Pooling)" CI step.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR references #65075. Two open PRs touch `return_offsets_mapping`, #61363 and #62691, but both change only renderer and tokenizer code, not the scoring helper. #62691 adds `return_special_tokens_mask`, not offsets, to `MistralTokenizer.__call__`.

No docs change: this adds no options, and the docs don't say Mistral tokenizers are unsupported.

title: [Bugfix][Mistral] Keep skip_special_tokens for MistralTokenizer in Responses / legacy parser path
author: joa-stdn
body:
## Overview

Stop `MistralParser.adjust_request` from forcing `skip_special_tokens=False` when the tokenizer is a `MistralTokenizer`. This fixes corrupted non-ASCII output (`�`) from `/v1/responses` with tools for Tekken models. Alternative to #64743, which fixes the same symptom by changing the tokenizer and the derender stream state.

## Claims

- `/v1/responses` with tools no longer corrupts multi-byte characters (e.g. Korean `맑음` → `��음`) for Mistral models. This holds streaming and non-streaming, with and without reasoning.
- Responses now decodes Mistral output the same way as Chat Completions, which already runs with `skip_special_tokens=True` on the grammar path.
- Tool calls and reasoning are still parsed: `MistralTokenizer` keeps `[TOOL_CALLS]`, `[ARGS]`, `[THINK]` and `[/THINK]` when skipping special tokens.

## Validation

### Unit tests

`test_adjust_request_mistral_tokenizer_keeps_skip_special_tokens` covers Responses and non-grammar Chat Completions with a `MistralTokenizer`. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.

```shell
pytest tests/parser/mistral/ tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py
# 781 passed, 233 skipped, 0 failed (82 errors are gated meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct fixtures, unrelated)
```

### E2E

`mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603` (FP8) on 2xH200 with `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0`. The "fix" server is the same image with this patch applied to the installed `vllm/parser/mistral.py`.

```shell
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral --load-format mistral --config-format mistral \
  --tool-call-parser mistral --reasoning-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Requests were sent to `/v1/responses` with the `get_weather` tool. There are two inputs:
- **Korean answer:** the conversation from #64743 (Korean question, `function_call`, `function_call_output`).
- **Korean tool call:** `"부산이랑 서울 날씨 둘 다 알려줘."`

Each was run 5 times per configuration at temperature 0.7. The table shows the number of responses whose output text or tool-call arguments contained `U+FFFD`:

| Input | Mode | Reasoning | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Korean answer | non-stream | off | 5/5 | 0/5 |
| Korean answer | non-stream | high | 5/5 | 0/5 |
| Korean answer | stream | off | 5/5 | 0/5 |
| Korean answer | stream | high | 5/5 | 0/5 |
| Korean tool call | non-stream | off | 0/5 | 0/5 |
| Korean tool call | non-stream | high | 4/5 | 0/5 |
| Korean tool call | stream | off | 0/5 | 0/5 |
| Korean tool call | stream | high | 5/5 | 0/5 |

Example from `main`: `상태: ��음`, `22°C (상���한 온도예요!)`. With this PR: `상태: 맑음`.

Tool calls (`get_weather` for 부산 and 서울) and reasoning items are parsed identically on both servers. Over 15 requests per server with reasoning on, a request occasionally returns no tool call: on `main` 1/15 non-stream and 3/15 stream; with this PR 2/15 and 3/15. In those cases the model emits `get_weather[ARGS]{...}` without `[TOOL_CALLS]`. `main` keeps every special token, so if the marker had been emitted it would appear there; this is model behaviour, not caused by this change.

## Details

**Root cause.** `MistralParser.adjust_request` sends every `ResponsesRequest` through its legacy (non-grammar) branch. That branch calls `ParserEngine.adjust_request`, which unconditionally sets `skip_special_tokens=False`, and then sets it to `False` again when tools are present. With `False`, `MistralTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens` returns `id_to_piece` directly. That skips its Tekken byte-fallback handling, so partial UTF-8 pieces become `�` before they are joined.

**Why `False` isn't needed for `MistralTokenizer`.** With `skip_special_tokens=True`, `MistralTokenizer` already keeps exactly the tokens the parser needs (`[TOOL_CALLS]`, `[ARGS]`, `[THINK]`, `[/THINK]`) in both `convert_ids_to_tokens` and `convert_tokens_to_string`. The parser also matches `[TOOL_CALLS]` and `[ARGS]` by token id. The original tool parser guarded this explicitly with `not isinstance(self.model_tokenizer, MistralTokenizer)` and the note "we don't want skip_special_tokens=False with MistralTokenizer as it is incompatible". The guard was lost when Responses requests were routed into this branch (#38150), and the unified parser (#48947) carried that behaviour over.

**Change.** In the legacy branch, only call `ParserEngine.adjust_request` (which forces `False`) for non-Mistral tokenizers, i.e. HF chat-template tokenizers driving the Mistral parser. The behaviour for those is unchanged.

**Limitations.** A client that explicitly sends `skip_special_tokens=False` still hits the byte-fallback bug in `MistralTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens`. Fixing that changes the token pieces returned to other callers (`_vocab_dict`, `/tokenize`, derender stream state), which is what #64743 does, so it's left out of this PR to keep it small.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Abort inbound loads when draining for a cache reset
author: liranschour
body:
## Purpose

On a P2P consumer (decoder), `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()` (`/reset_prefix_cache` with `reset_connector`, sleep, weight update) blocks the engine thread in `P2PSecondaryTierManager.drain_jobs()` for the full load timeout plus the abort-ack window (~35 s for PD, ~15 s symmetric) whenever a load waits on a prefiller that never writes. `has_pending_work` counts client loads, and the drain never aborts them.

This is the consumer-side counterpart of #63948, which #63988 fixes on the producer side (stores waiting for a fetch). It came up in review there.

`drain_jobs()` now aborts every inbound load not already aborting before it polls, through the same path a load timeout takes (#64256): `AbortFetch`, fail the job at once, defer the chunk release until the `AbortAck` or the session's `close()`. The drain then waits only for the acks, bounded by `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S` (5 s, after which the session disconnects and `close()` releases), so every deferred release is set on return as the `drain_jobs()` contract in `tiering/base.py` requires. Lookup state is untouched.

## Test Plan

- `test_reset_cache_aborts_load_from_silent_peer` (test_manager.py): a real `TieringOffloadingManager` + CPU primary + `P2PSession`; a PD load whose peer only answers `AbortFetch`. `reset_cache()` returns after the ack, the job is finished, the chunk is released, and the session stays up. Fails on main ("drain_jobs waited on a load no peer will write").
- `test_abort_loads_fails_each_load_once` (test_sessions.py): `abort_loads()` aborts each load exactly once (skipping one already aborted by `finish_request`), fails it at once with a deferred release, and the acks release it.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tier_poll_thread.py`

## Test Result

463 passed.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Muse Spark DSpark: initialize _context_kv_proj so the draft loads
author: fanxingran
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Muse Spark with DSpark fails at startup on main: loading the draft raises `AttributeError: 'MuseSparkDSparkModel' object has no attribute '_context_kv_proj'`. Regressed by #64357. This PR initializes the attribute in `MuseSparkDSparkModel.__init__`.

## Claims

- Muse Spark + DSpark (`--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark",...}'`, the recipe's DSpark profiles) starts again. The failing code path is shared by CUDA and ROCm.
- DSpark acceptance is unchanged from before the regression.
- A unit test builds the real draft model and loads weights; it fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Validation

MI355X x8, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-76c6f3f2a95f6049657db1e513133b824a5c8175` (Muse and `qwen3_dflash.py` byte-identical to main `51c6dfd8c8`), target `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, draft `Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark`, the recipe's AMD MXFP4 + DSpark command (TP8, K=7):

| | Startup | DSpark acceptance length | Per-position acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| nightly | `AttributeError` in every rank while loading the draft | - | - |
| nightly + this PR | OK | 3.900 | 0.802 0.625 0.482 0.365 0.274 0.203 0.148 |
| before #64357 (main `19c0e170d2`) | OK | 3.913 | 0.806 0.634 0.491 0.373 0.280 0.206 0.147 |
| model card | | 3.94 | |

Acceptance: 256 GSM8K test questions as chat requests, T=1.0, top-p 0.95, max 2048 tokens, concurrency 16; acceptance length = 1 + accepted / drafts from `vllm:spec_decode_*` metrics. Run-to-run spread at T=1.0 is about 0.05.

<details>
<summary>Serve command and stock traceback</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN_SHORT_QUERY_3D=1 VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 --dtype bfloat16 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --language-model-only \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --tensor-parallel-size 8 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --reasoning-parser muse --tool-call-parser muse \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'
```

```text
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py", line 120, in load_dspark_model
    draft_model = get_model(
  ...
  File "vllm/models/muse_spark/common/dspark.py", line 375, in load_weights
    return AutoWeightsLoader(self).load_weights(
  File "vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py", line 407, in _load_module
    loaded_params = module_load_weights(weights)
  File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py", line 839, in load_weights
    proj = self._context_kv_proj
AttributeError: 'MuseSparkDSparkModel' object has no attribute '_context_kv_proj'
```

</details>

Tests (in the same image, without and with the fix):

```bash
pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_muse_spark_config.py
# without the fix: 1 failed (test_dspark_draft_loads_weights, the AttributeError above), 8 passed
# with the fix:    9 passed
```

`pre-commit` hooks `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, and `mypy` (3.11) pass on the changed files.

## Details

Root cause: #64357 moved the creation of the MXFP8 context K/V projection from `_build_fused_kv_buffers` (run at the end of `load_weights`) into `DFlashQwen3Model.__init__`, and `DFlashQwen3Model.load_weights` now reads `self._context_kv_proj`. `MuseSparkDSparkModel` inherits `load_weights` but calls `nn.Module.__init__` instead of the parent's `__init__`, so the attribute never exists. `AutoWeightsLoader` reaches the inherited `load_weights` through `MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM.load_weights` and fails.

Fix: set `self._context_kv_proj = None`. Muse projects its context K/V in `_project_muse_context_kv` (from the weights `_build_fused_kv_buffers` stacks) and never uses the parent's MXFP8 projection, so `None` keeps the pre-#64357 behavior. Of the other `DFlashQwen3Model` subclasses, the two that also skip the parent `__init__` never reach the inherited `load_weights`: Laguna DFlash overrides it, and Gemma4 DSpark loads parameters directly from its `ForCausalLM`.

Why CI missed it: the Muse DSpark registry entry is `is_available_online=False` and the model initialization test loads dummy weights, so no CI job runs the draft's `load_weights`. The new test does; `tests/transformers_utils` is currently not run by any Buildkite step (the step is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`), so it is covered only by local runs until that step is re-enabled.

Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR mentions `_context_kv_proj` or this failure; #64692 and #64690 touch weight loading but not this attribute. #65080, the other Muse fix today, merged the duplicate `process_weights_after_loading` from #64357 and #63440 in `amd/model.py` and does not touch the draft.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write, and validate this change; I reviewed every line and reran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix] Validate global model seed range
author: xu797
body:
## Overview
Fixes #64953. Validate the global model seed at configuration time so unsupported values fail before EngineCore startup.

## Claims
- Constrain `ModelConfig.seed` to NumPy's supported range `[0, 2**32 - 1]`, and document the range.
- Add an LLM initialization regression test for values below and above this range.

## Validation
- Before this config change, the regression test proceeds to worker startup and fails with `ValueError: Seed must be between 0 and 2**32 - 1`, and the caller receives `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`.
- After the change: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/llm/test_prompt_validation.py -k model_seed_out_of_numpy_range -v -s` — 2 passed.
- `uv tool run ruff check vllm/config/model.py tests/entrypoints/llm/test_prompt_validation.py` — passed.
- `uv tool run ruff format --check vllm/config/model.py tests/entrypoints/llm/test_prompt_validation.py` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Model evaluation is not applicable: this change only rejects invalid configuration values and does not alter model outputs for valid seeds.

## Details
`ModelConfig.seed` was previously unbounded. Invalid values would propagate into `np.random.seed()` during worker initialization and crash the engine.
The config field now validates against NumPy's supported range before worker startup.

This applies to the global engine seed. Request-level `SamplingParams.seed=-1` has separate semantics and remains unchanged.

Duplicate-work check: Coordinated with @ntu-b12505041; they are okay with me taking this fix. No existing open PR referenced #64953.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Keep same-host NIXL on NVLink with the extensible KV cache
author: gcanlin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Since the extensible KV cache (#56492) became the default, same-host NIXL P/D silently moves KV over TCP instead of NVLink. This keeps NVLink: with an IMEX channel the cache gets a FABRIC handle, and without one it stays off for NIXL by default.

## Claims

- Per KV transfer, same-host: **9.9 s → about 24 ms**.
- With an IMEX channel, NVLink and the extensible KV cache work together.
- Nothing changes without NIXL on device memory.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash 1P1D on one node, DEP4 + DEP4, 8x B200, driver 590.48.01, NIXL 1.5.2, real MTP 5, 1,319 GSM8K prompts:

| Build | KV read protocol | Avg transfer | GSM8K | GSM8K time |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | `software emulation`, `tcp/cilium_host` | 9.9 s | – | ~5 min |
| main, without `UCX_CUDA_COPY_DMABUF=no` | same | 205 s | – | >50 min |
| main, `--disable-extensible-kv-cache` | `zero-copy`, `cuda_ipc` | 23.4 ms | 0.9742 | 49 s |
| **This PR, no channel** | `zero-copy`, `cuda_ipc` | 23.6 ms | 0.9757 | 52 s |
| This PR, with a channel | `zero-copy`, `cuda_ipc` | 24.2 ms | 0.9750 | 49 s |

Both PR rows ran on `4904c38f42`. Under load, on the previous commit `ff4c74f38c` with no channel, a one-hour AgentX run at concurrency 256 made 24,041 transfers averaging 894 MB in 22.1 ms, with 0 failures.

The new tests fail with the rule and driver change reverted. To see the transport, run P and D on one node with `UCX_PROTO_INFO=y` and look for `remote memory read by ucp_get*(multi)` in D's log.

## Details

**Root cause.** No code chooses TCP. #56492 maps the KV cache with `cuMemCreate` + `cuMemMap`. UCX's `cuda_ipc` exports plain memory with `cuIpcGetMemHandle`, which cannot export driver-mapped memory, and uses a FABRIC handle only on memory created with one. So that memory has no `cuda_ipc` path and UCX picks the next transport without an error. Accuracy does not change, so #56492's NIXL accuracy check would not show it. This is inferred from UCX's protocol tables and library strings, and the comment on the `LMCacheMPConnector` gate; I did not read UCX's source.

**Fix.**
- `CudaVmmDriver` requests `CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_FABRIC` when the device supports it and an IMEX channel opens. The attribute alone is not enough: it reads 1 with no channel.
- If `cuMemCreate` still rejects the FABRIC handle with `NOT_PERMITTED` or `NOT_SUPPORTED`, the errors `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp` also falls back on, the driver allocates without it, warns, and stops requesting it for that device. Without this, such a device could not allocate the cache at all. (Nick Hill's commit.)
- `_resolve_extensible_kv_cache` keeps the feature off by default with NIXL on device memory and no channel, and logs that transfers that only cross hosts can opt back in. An explicit `--enable-extensible-kv-cache` is honored with a warning.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix Muse Spark RoPE cache leak between tests
author: djramic
body:
## Overview

Fixes the remaining 26 `tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` failures in `:amd: (MI355) Basic Models (Other)` on the [nightly build #99098](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99098/list?sid=01a19b12-86dc-48ba-811c-30a4d4e009ed). `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` leaves a CPU `RotaryEmbedding` in `get_rope`'s global cache, and the mono test's tiny GPU model picks it up when both files run in the same pytest session, as they do in that shard. The other 2 failures in the job (`test_layer_guards_follow_the_weight_finalize`, `test_weight_views_alias_the_rank_slices`) are fixed by #65080.

## Claims

- `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` runs with its own empty `_ROPE_DICT`, so its CPU RoPE no longer leaks into later tests.
- Together with #65080, `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` passes when it runs after the shared-RoPE test.
- Test-only change: no model or kernel code is touched.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), using the ROCm wheel from build #99098 (`0e5b2ba11`) with `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py` from current `main` (#65080):

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py
```

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` alone | 33 passed | 33 passed |
| `shared_rope` then `mono` | 26 failed, 8 passed | 34 passed |

Before, all 26 failures are `RuntimeError: fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert, ...: cos_sin_cache must be a contiguous 2-D CUDA tensor`, the same as in CI. The four Muse Spark files in CI order (`rocm_loading`, `logits_local`, `shared_rope`, `mono`) give 48 passed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.

## Details

- `get_rope()` caches `RotaryEmbedding` objects in the global `_ROPE_DICT` without the device in the key, so the CPU RoPE created by `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` stays in the cache after that test. The tiny GPU model in `test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` then gets that CPU RoPE, and `fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert` fails because `cos_sin_cache` is not on the GPU.
- The fix isolates the cache in the test that leaks it, the same way `tests/models/quantization/test_gptq_marlin.py` already clears `_ROPE_DICT`. Adding the device to the cache key would affect every model for a test-only problem.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Include error sources in HTTP 400 messages
author: BugenZhao
body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend's HTTP 400 responses drop the source chain of request validation errors. A request pinned with `X-data-parallel-rank` to a rank the frontend does not own returns only `"engine-core error"`, hiding which ranks are connected. Related: vllm-project/vllm#64801.

## Claims

- HTTP 400 validation errors from `text_submit_error` / `chat_submit_error` include the full error report, matching the 500 branch and the gRPC path (`text_error_to_status`).
- Hyper connection errors in the trace log include their source chain.
- No other validation error message changes: `InvalidDataParallelRank` is the only one wrapped by a non-transparent layer.

## Validation

New test `chat_completions_unconnected_data_parallel_rank_reports_connected_ranks` mirrors the existing gRPC test `unary_generate_unconnected_data_parallel_rank_returns_invalid_argument`. It connects a mock engine at global rank 3 and pins the request to rank 0.

| | `error.message` |
| --- | --- |
| Before (test fails) | `engine-core error` |
| After | `engine-core error: data parallel rank 0 is not connected to this frontend; connected ranks: [3]` |

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server`: 553 passed, including the existing `error::tests` that pin other 400 messages.
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Details

`text_submit_error` and `chat_submit_error` formatted 400 messages with `"{error}"` (`Display`), while their 500 branch uses `to_report_string()`. The data-parallel rank error reaches them as `vllm_chat::Error::Text` → `vllm_text::Error::Llm` → `vllm_llm::Error::EngineCoreClient` → `InvalidDataParallelRank`. The first two layers are transparent, but `EngineCoreClient` is `#[error("engine-core error")]`, so `Display` stops there and the rank detail lives only in `source()`.

For the trace log: hyper 1.x prints only the error kind in `Display` (e.g. "connection error") and keeps the underlying I/O error in `source()`.

Other error formatting sites in production code were audited. The remaining `Display` uses format leaf errors (serde, I/O, join, parse errors), or types whose `Display` already embeds the inner error.

title: [Bugfix][Step5] Size the KV block to the CSA tail ring
author: akii96
body:
## Overview

Step-5 with FP8 KV cache crashes at startup if `--block-size` is not passed. The default block size of 16 is too small for the CSA tail ring. #61837 worked around this by telling users to pass `--block-size 32`. This PR makes vLLM pick a large enough block size on its own.

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` works without `--block-size`.
- When 16 is already big enough, nothing changes. That covers BF16, and FP8 at TP2 and TP1.
- Other models are not affected. Only the Step-5 tail ring backend asks for a larger block.

## Validation

Before this change, this command crashed on 8x MI300X after the weights loaded:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --reasoning-parser step5 \
  --tool-call-parser step5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch
```

```text
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Step5 CSA tail ring needs 7 rows of 1024 bytes in one 6144-byte KV page; increase --block-size.'
```

With this branch, I ran the same command on 8x MI325X with `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` added. All 8 workers picked block size 32 and the server started:

```text
Setting kv cache block size to 32 for ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN/STEP5_CSA_SUMMARY/STEP5_CSA_TAIL_RING backend(s).
```

I then ran GSM8K against that server with the same setup as #61837: all 1319 questions, 5-shot. It scored 97.27% strict and 97.50% flexible.

To check more than one KV head per GPU, I started the small Step-5 test model from the test registry with dummy weights, FP8 KV and no `--block-size`:

| TP | KV heads per GPU | Block size picked |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 16 |
| 2 | 2 | 16 |
| 8 | 1 | 32 |

All three started and generated text.

The new unit test goes through the same startup code and then builds the tail ring's KV spec, which is the call that fails on main. It covers FP8 at TP8, TP2 and TP1, BF16, a larger speculative ring (moves to 64), and a padded page.

## Details

The tail ring has to fit in one KV page. It needs 7 rows of 1024 bytes, plus one more row per speculative token. Step-5 has 4 KV heads, so at TP8 each GPU holds one. With FP8, a 16-token page is then 6144 bytes, which is only 6 rows. At TP2 each GPU holds two heads, so the page is already 12 rows and nothing changes.

vLLM already lets each attention backend say which block sizes it supports, and it picks a size that works for all of them at startup. The tail ring backend now takes part in that. It asks for 32, 64 or 128, whichever is the smallest that fits. If 16 already fits, it accepts any size. The math uses the page size without padding, so padding never counts as room for the ring.

The code is in `common/csa_tail_ring.py`, which the AMD and NVIDIA Step-5 models both use. If a user passes a `--block-size` that is too small, they still get the same error as before.

AI assistance was used to write this change. I reviewed the diff, ran the unit test, and ran the serve, GSM8K and TP checks above.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Close the parent's listening sockets after launching the Rust frontend
author: theminjunchoi
body:
## Overview

Part of #65155. The parent process kept its copies of the HTTP and gRPC sockets after passing them to the Rust frontend, so both ports kept listening after Rust closed its listeners at shutdown. Clients that connected during a drain were never answered. This closes them right after `Popen`, where the ZMQ listeners are already closed.

## Claims

- During a drain, new HTTP and gRPC clients are refused instead of hanging. Requests already running still finish.
- New gRPC clients can still hang while another gRPC call is open. That's the Rust side of the issue and needs a separate fix.

## Validation

Ran `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct --grpc-port 50052 --shutdown-timeout 40` on the `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest` image (0.33.0, same `RustFrontendProcessManager` as main; "After" has this change applied). I kept a long HTTP completion running, sent SIGTERM, and connected to each port 2s later:

| | New HTTP client | New gRPC client | In-flight request |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | no reply after 5s | `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` after 5s | 200 |
| After | connection refused | `UNAVAILABLE` (connection refused) | 200 |

The new test gives the manager real listening sockets and a fake `Popen`, then checks that connecting afterwards is refused. It fails on main with `DID NOT RAISE ConnectionRefusedError`.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py  # 13 passed
```

## Details

The child already has the fds through `pass_fds` once `Popen` returns, and the parent doesn't touch the sockets after that. `test_rust_frontend_inherits_grpc_listener` now reads the fds before the manager closes them.

#64426 adds per-rank sockets to this class, so whichever PR lands second should close those too.

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-VL] Set pad_token_id explicitly in KimiVLConfig
author: kazutoiris
body:
## Overview

`KimiVLConfig` passed `pad_token_id` to `super().__init__` as a keyword argument. With the dataclass-based `PreTrainedConfig`, `pad_token_id` is not a declared field.

## Claims

- Fixes the `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pad_token_id'` raised when `KimiVLConfig` is constructed on a `PreTrainedConfig` base that does not forward unknown keyword arguments.
- `pad_token_id` is now assigned explicitly on `KimiVLConfig` before the `super().__init__` call, so the attribute exists regardless of how the base class handles unused kwargs.
- No change to the public constructor signature: existing callers passing `pad_token_id=` continue to work.
- No change to serialization behavior for the `pad_token_id` value itself; the fix only removes the reliance on an implicit `setattr` path.

## Validation

- Reproduction before the fix: construct `KimiVLConfig` on a base that rejects unknown kwargs (or monkeypatch the base `__init__` to not forward extras); observe `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pad_token_id'`.
- After the fix: the same construction succeeds, and `config.pad_token_id` returns the supplied value.

## Details

`PreTrainedConfig` is a dataclass, and `pad_token_id` is not a declared field on it; the field is only used by `KimiVLConfig` itself.

I've checked the code on [huggingface](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct/blob/main/configuration_kimi_vl.py) and #16387, it can be confirmed that MoonshotAI has modified the base `PreTrainedConfig`.
