title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Index INT8 MoE per-channel weight scales independently of act quant - #58570
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
**PR authors: @gokay-ai @ahsan-ca @fxmarty-amd - resubmitting https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58570 here with some minor fixes.** I lost ability to push to `https://github.com/gokay-ai/vllm.git` so landing here.

## Overview

Fixes #58532

`QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` can load static per-tensor activation scales with per-output-channel weight scales. The legacy Triton `fused_experts` path still used `per_act_token_quant` to pick both layouts, so static activations (`per_act_token_quant=False`) also took the tensor weight-scale branch. Routed experts' channel scales were ignored.

This keeps the legacy static-INT8 path (no oracle migration) and splits the two flags:

- The non-block W8A8 Triton kernels (`fused_moe_kernel` and the batched `moe_mmk` kernels) index A scales with `per_act_token_quant` / `per_channel_quant` and W scales with a new `per_out_ch_quant` constexpr. `TritonExperts` and the batched Triton experts forward `quant_config.per_out_ch_quant`.
- `int8_w8a8_moe_quant_config` / `make_int8_moe_quant_config` now take `per_out_ch_quant`. Quark, compressed-tensors and online INT8 set it from the actual weight scheme.
- Quark INT8 (static and dynamic branches) derives `per_act_token_quant` from the activation `QuantKey` and `per_out_ch_quant` from the weight `QuantKey`, instead of deriving activation granularity from `weight_qscheme`.

No open PR already covers this combo. #57092 is the opposite mixed case (per-token acts + per-tensor weights) and is still open.

### Note on `per_out_ch_quant` defaults

`FusedMoEQuantConfig.make` and the `fp8` / `int8` / `int4` quant-config factories keep `per_out_ch_quant=False` as the default (unchanged from `main`). All in-tree production callers now pass it explicitly. `Fp8MoEMethod` passes `per_out_ch_quant=False`, which matters for per-token activations + per-tensor weights under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`.

**Behavior change for callers of the factories:** previously, setting `per_act_token_quant=True` alone made the Triton kernels index weight scales per channel. Now the weight-scale layout follows `per_out_ch_quant`, so callers with per-channel weight scales must pass `per_out_ch_quant=True`. The in-tree tests that relied on the implicit coupling were updated (`test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py`, `test_int8_kernel.py`, `test_cpu_fused_moe.py`, `test_deepep_moe.py`, `test_deepep_v2_moe.py`). The direct Triton launchers (`invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`, `dispatch_fused_moe_kernel`, `fused_experts_impl`, `invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel`) still default `per_out_ch_quant=None` to `per_channel_quant`.

This is a stopgap: as per #61024, `FusedMoEQuantConfig` should move to `QuantKey` and drop the `per_act_token_quant` / `per_out_ch_quant` flags.

The W8A16 path does not need the flag: the W8A16 kernels always index weight scales per output channel.

## Validation

Run on MI350X (gfx950), ROCm `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly image, at commit
9cd72c182ad74b20f19ebd90cd835c5beaec4d6f (branch head, `main` merged in,
working tree clean). The checkout was installed editable
(`pip install -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation`); the compiled extensions were
built from this same source tree, and the only later change in the tree was the
`per_out_ch_quant` docstring.

New / modified tests:

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k int8
# 23 passed, 118 deselected, 14 warnings in 79.59s (0:01:19)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k launcher
# 3 passed, 1086 deselected, 17 warnings in 1.05s

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_zen_cpu_int8_moe.py
# 474 passed, 509 skipped, 14 warnings in 154.18s (0:02:34)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_int8_kernel.py
# 76 passed, 16 warnings in 20.35s

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py -k int8
# 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 0.25s  (x86 CPU int8 kernel not available on this node)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py
```

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Avoid the MNNVL FlashInfer all-reduce with HiSparse
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #64327. Unblocks #63801.

FlashInfer's MNNVL fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm has a cluster-barrier race (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782). The vLLM default single-node backend has been MNNVL since #61989. With HiSparse running host-memory gathers on its copy stream, the race fires and the engine dies with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (Xid 13 `CTA Not Present`).

With HiSparse enabled and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=auto`, backend selection now:
- single node: uses `trtllm`;
- multi-node: disables FlashInfer all-reduce, since `trtllm` doesn't support multi-node groups.

An explicit `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` setting is still respected. This is temporary: the check should be removed once vLLM picks up a FlashInfer release with #7782.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer_auto_backend or workspace_failure or standalone_workspace"
```

## Test Result

Server check that the new path runs: 4× H100 (driver 580.126.09), `main` + #63801 (Python side; kernels from the `main` precompiled wheel) + this PR, GLM-5.3 config with dummy weights cut to 5 layers, HiSparse with spec decode. Same build, same load; the only difference is the backend env var.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND={mnnvl,auto} \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 -tp 4 --enforce-eager --load-format dummy \
  --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 5, "first_k_dense_replace": 5, "indexer_types": ["full", "full", "full", "shared", "shared"]}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G \
  --max-model-len 67584 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":16}}'

# 6 waves, seeds 1..6
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 52000 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --seed $seed
```

| `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` | Fused AR workspace | Result | Output tok/s (mean of 6 waves) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mnnvl` (stock behavior) | `backend=mnnvl` | 6/6 waves, 0 failed requests | 499 |
| `auto` (this PR) | `backend=trtllm`, logs `Using flashinfer allreduce backend trtllm: ...` | 6/6 waves, 0 failed requests | 552 |

HiSparse was reading heavily from host memory (8.9 TB host-to-device, ~50% hot-buffer miss rate), but this reduced server didn't hit the race on H100 even with `mnnvl`. The crash evidence is the B200 result below and the standalone repro in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782, which faults within seconds on this same box.


10 passed. The two new HiSparse cases fail without the change.

Server-level evidence that `trtllm` avoids the crash (from #64327 / flashinfer#7782, set by hand via `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm`): GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP8 on 8× B200 with HiSparse went from a crash on wave 1 in 7/7 runs (MNNVL) to clean for 4/4 waves (TRTLLM), at about 3% lower decode throughput.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Share one RoPE cache across Muse Spark NVIDIA layers
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
_Requested by **Simon**_



## Overview

The NVIDIA Muse Spark model builds a private fp32 RoPE table in each of its 46 RoPE attention layers. The tables are identical and cost 11.5 GiB per GPU. This PR shares one table, as #62757 did for the ROCm path.

Fixes #65205

## Claims

- Model loading drops from 81.0 to 69.75 GiB per GPU on 8x B200, TP8, `Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`.
- The KV cache grows from 9,248,688 to 10,589,618 tokens (+14.5 %).
- Output does not change: greedy output is bit-identical, and GSM8K-100 is 96/100 on stock and 95/100 with this PR, which is within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

New unit test `tests/models/test_muse_spark_nvidia_shared_rope.py`, CPU only, with the heavy submodules stubbed. It mirrors `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` from #62757.

- Two target layers must hold the same fp32 `RotaryEmbedding`.
- It uses its own empty `_ROPE_DICT`, so the CPU tables it builds do not leak into later GPU tests (the failure #65138 and #65140 fixed for the ROCm twin).

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest -v tests/models/test_muse_spark_nvidia_shared_rope.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py
```

On this branch: 16 passed. Without the model change, the new test fails (two different objects). The test is added to the "Basic Models (Other)" step next to its ROCm twin.

End to end on 8x B200, TP8, `unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`, default `max_model_len` (1,048,576), with prefix caching. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-76c6f3f2a95f6049657db1e513133b824a5c8175` (digest `sha256:7a933b7c…`), the newest nightly; no nightly at this base exists yet. `nvidia/model.py` is byte-identical on 76c6f3f2a and this PR's base, so the PR arm loaded this branch's `nvidia/model.py` on that image. Each arm ran on a fresh server start, and each start logged the sha256 of the file that was loaded.

| Check | Stock | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Model loading per GPU | 81.0 GiB | 69.75 GiB |
| Available KV cache memory, TP0 | 90.01 GiB | 101.26 GiB |
| GPU KV cache size | 9,248,688 tokens | 10,589,618 tokens (+14.5 %) |
| Greedy, 8 prompts × 256 tokens, one at a time | reference | 8/8 bit-identical |
| GSM8K-100, temperature 0, 32 concurrent | 96/100 | 95/100 |

The saving is 11.25 GiB, which is 45 × 256 MiB: one table remains. The GSM8K gap is batch-order noise: the four questions only stock got right hit the 6,000-token cap in a reasoning loop on this PR's arm. Stock shows the same loops (it hit the cap twice). An earlier pair of runs on the same patch scored 97/100 on both arms.

On the same pod, an earlier version of the new test (the sharing check plus a bit-equality check against a private table) and the ROCm twin passed against this PR's `nvidia/model.py`. Against the stock file, the sharing check failed. The GPU runs used a version of `nvidia/model.py` that differs from this PR only in two code comments.

Sanity pass on fresh starts of the same setup. Without speculative decoding, 100 varied prompts (chat, code, math, 8k-token summaries, tool calls, multilingual, JSON, multi-turn) gave token-identical output on stock and this PR, greedy and 30 seeded samples at temperature 0.7. With the DSpark draft from the recipe (`Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark`, 7 speculative tokens), whose RoPE table this PR leaves private, the acceptance rate was 0.2679 on stock and 0.2680 with this PR (mean acceptance length 2.875 and 2.876). The KV cache grew from 5,043,740 to 6,359,813 tokens. Greedy output was 93/100 identical; a second stock start was 92/100 identical to the first, with differences only on the 8k-token prompts in both cases. On this base, DSpark fails to load on stock, because `MuseSparkDSparkModel` never sets `_context_kv_proj` (read in `qwen3_dflash.py` `load_weights`). Both spec arms set it to `None` for the test; that is a separate bug.

Not measured: performance. No kernel changes, and the kernels read the same table values.

## Details

Root cause, in `vllm/models/muse_spark/nvidia/model.py`:

- Each target `MuseSpark1xAttention` with RoPE constructs its own `RotaryEmbedding` with an fp32 `cos_sin_cache` of `[max_position, 64]`.
- `MuseSpark1xDecoderLayer` passes `max(config.max_position_embeddings, max_model_len)`, so the table has at least 1,048,576 rows whatever `--max-model-len` is.
- 46 of the 62 layers use RoPE, all with theta 500000. 46 × 1,048,576 × 64 × 4 B = 11.5 GiB.

Change:

- Target layers take their table from `get_rope(..., dtype=torch.float, rope_parameters={"rope_theta": theta, "rope_type": "default"})`. `get_rope` caches one instance per key, so all 46 layers share one table.
- `MuseSpark1xDecoderLayer` sizes the target table by `max_model_len`, since target positions never reach it. With a smaller `--max-model-len` the table shrinks too (64 MiB at 262,144); that case was not run end to end.
- The DSpark draft keeps its private table, dtype and size.

Numerics: each row of the table is computed the same way whatever the table length, and sharing does not change any value. On the unfused path, `_match_cos_sin_cache_dtype` now converts one shared table instead of 46 identical ones, with the same result.

Related: #63078 (open) keeps these tables fp32 at the unfused call sites. It touches different lines of `nvidia/model.py` and applies cleanly on top of this branch. #65170 (open, ROCm) moves the shared table to CUDA before the ROCm monokernel reads it; the NVIDIA path has no monokernel, and the fused kernel worked with the shared table in the runs above.

title: [Bugfix] Pad extensible KV cache segments instead of rounding the block count
author: njhill
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65204. Supersedes #65210 (carries over its connector gating, with Vegetog as co-author).

With the extensible KV cache (#56492), any KV connector made the engine round the KV block count down to a multiple of `granule / gcd(granule, block_stride)`. For awkward strides that multiple is huge, so engines with `--kv-offloading-size` could fail to start. This PR pads segment placement instead, and applies it (and the defragmenting commit) only for connectors that register the KV cache for RDMA.

## Claims

- `--kv-offloading-size` (and any connector that doesn't register the device KV cache) keeps its measured block count: no rounding, no padding, no defragmenting commit.
- NIXL / Mooncake / MoRIIO / UMBP keep one physical chunk per committed segment for RDMA registration at **any** block count, instead of losing up to one alignment unit (2048 blocks, ~11.6 GB, for the stride in #65204) or failing to start below it.
- `UMBPStoreConnector` is added to `registers_kv_cache_memory()`: it registers GPU KV storage through MORI. This also turns the extensible cache off for it on ROCm, as for MoRIIO.

## Validation

GB200, all on this branch unless noted.

**Reproducer**: `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct` (20 KiB page = 2¹²·5, so main needs a multiple of 512 blocks), `kv_offloading_size=1`, `block_size=16`, `max_model_len=1024`, `enforce_eager=True`. Baseline = `origin/main` versions of the changed files over the same build.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 0.014 | fails at startup: "No available memory for the cache blocks … decrease `max_model_len`" (102 blocks rounded to 0) | starts, 102 blocks, correct greedy output |
| 0.018 | 1024 blocks | 1331 blocks, same output |

**NIXL P/D**: `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh` with `PREFILL_BLOCK_SIZE=16 DECODE_BLOCK_SIZE=16` (Qwen3-0.6B, 1P1D): passes for the default layer-outermost layout (padded) and with `--enable-cross-layers` (block-outermost, single segment), 0 failed transfers. A separate DEBUG run with `NixlConnector` confirmed the padded path ran: capacity 19254 blocks (main would have rounded to 19232), NIXL registered the padded segments, and the final 18624 blocks committed exactly the nominal 31.83 GiB.

**Unit tests**: `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py`, `tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py`, `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py` all pass. New/changed coverage:
- `test_pad_kv_cache_segments` (CPU): uniform and mixed block strides, block-outermost no-op.
- `test_defragmenting_commit_backs_each_segment_with_one_allocation[padded]`: unpadded segments still share chunks after a defragmenting commit; padded ones get one chunk each at an unaligned count.
- `test_padded_config_allocates_and_defragments` (LBNHC, BLNHC, mixed strides): views, committed views and connector placements agree on a padded reservation.
- `test_extensible_extend_asks_connector_for_its_memory_pool`: a registering connector gets `defragment=True`.

## Details

**Root cause.** A connector that registers each committed segment for RDMA needs that segment backed by one physical chunk. Segments were placed at multiples of `capacity × block_stride`, so they only started on commit granules when the block count was a granule multiple; the engine forced that by rounding the reserved capacity and the post-warmup count for *every* connector. CPU offloading only copies blocks and needs none of it.

**Fix.**
- When `registers_kv_cache_memory()`, each worker pads its own copy of the KV cache config in `initialize_from_config` (`pad_kv_cache_segments`): each layer region of a block-compact layer-outermost layout starts on that device's commit granule. This costs address space only; commits already map whole granules per segment (`physical_bytes_for`), so a defragmenting commit of any count backs each segment with exactly one chunk. Block-outermost layouts have one segment at offset 0 and are untouched. KV connectors with the extensible cache are already restricted to block-compact layouts.
- Padding is worker-local so the engine/scheduler configs keep unpadded placements: `shrink_kv_cache_configs` scales `size` by block count and scheduler-side connectors read `size // num_blocks`.
- `ExtensibleKVCache` takes the layout to derive one segment per layer region (gaps allowed) rather than inferring segments from a single stride, which can't tell padding from LHBNC head groups for small caches.
- Removed: engine-side `align_extensible_kv_cache_capacity` / `granule_aligned_kv_cache_blocks`, the `kv_cache_commit_granule` RPC, `granule_aligned_blocks` / `granule_block_alignment`, `blocks_within(aligned=)`.
- The defragmenting commit is gated on `registers_kv_cache_memory()` (#65210).

**Tradeoff/limitation.** `registers_kv_cache_memory()` is a name-based allowlist, so out-of-tree connectors loaded via `kv_connector_module_path` that register device memory no longer get one-chunk segments by default (previously any connector did). Unpadded configs (no registering connector) behave as before.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Pad MiniMax-M3 encoder graph cu_seqlens with zero-length sequences
author: Pb314314
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The MiniMax-M3 encoder CUDA graph declares the unused rows of a captured buffer as one extra attention sequence, so every replay smaller than its budget runs full self-attention over its padding rows. This PR pads `cu_seqlens` with zero-length sequences instead, as the Qwen2.5-VL, Kimi-K2.5, LFM2 and DeepSeek-V4.1 encoder graphs already do.

The main reason is correctness with shared capture buffers (#65084). The speedup is large only when replays carry many padding rows, e.g. the default power-of-two budgets.

## Why the padding sequence existed, and why it is no longer needed

- #58673 added the padding sequence to avoid NaN. FlashAttention does not write rows that belong to no sequence. With an uninitialized output those rows hold garbage, and a real sequence's last K/V tile in the next layer reads them: the mask sets P = 0, but 0 · NaN = NaN.
- #56711, merged the same day after #58673, makes FA's output `torch.zeros` while capturing ([`vit_attn_wrappers.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/254a2a33908a9bd974e9656f05592f83de604298/vllm/v1/attention/ops/vit_attn_wrappers.py#L61-L69)). The memset is recorded in the graph, so rows outside every sequence replay as 0.
- Outside attention, the MiniMax tower is row-wise: LayerNorm, MLP, residual, and the 2x2 merge on aligned row groups. The input tail is zeroed by the encoder graph manager and the rope tail by `pad_rope_planes`. So padding rows stay finite and cannot reach real rows.
- Poisoning FA's captured output with NaN does reproduce NaN in real rows with zero-length padding, so the zeroed output is what makes this safe.
- **ROCm.** The change applies to every platform. ROCm AITER does not take `out=`, so its output is not zeroed. This PR does not add a ROCm-specific path: Qwen2.5-VL and Kimi-K2.5 already use zero-length padding there. MiniMax encoder graphs on ROCm were not tested with this change.

## Claims

- **Correct with shared capture buffers (#65084).** The old padding looks up its total by `cu_seqlens.data_ptr()`. With buffers shared across budgets, all budgets share one pointer and replays use the wrong total. On #65084 alone, MiniMax encoder outputs are wrong and every replay takes ~140 ms. With this PR on top, outputs are correct.
- **Same outputs.** Every replay is bitwise equal to before the change and to an eager forward of the same batch.
- **Less work on padding.** Padding rows no longer attend to each other. That attention costs O(padding rows²), about 1.25e-7 ms per row² (GB200, TP1).

## How much padding there is

Encoder CUDA graphs are opt-in (`cudagraph_mm_encoder`), and no MiniMax-M3 recipe enables them. A batch replays the smallest budget that fits it, so its padding is the gap to that budget:

| Budgets | Largest padding per replay | Cost of the padding sequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default when enabled (powers of two, 64…16384, 64 items) | up to ~32k rows | up to ~130 ms |
| #58673 benchmark config (`[512, 1024, 2048]`, 2 items, 336² images) | ~1.5k rows | ≤ 0.3 ms |
| A finer grid (e.g. quarter-octave steps up to ~2560 tokens) | ~2k rows | ≤ 0.5 ms |

The end-to-end gains reported in #58673 still hold: in that config the padding sequence costs well under 1 ms per replay. The large gains below come from the default budgets, where a batch just above a power of two pads almost 2x.

## Validation

Encoder-only benchmark with the real MiniMax-M3.1-Flash vision weights: GB200, BF16, FA4, TP1. Default encoder graph budgets (64…16384, 64 items). Synthetic images were processed by the model's own image processor. Each value is the median of 15 interleaved runs of the full encoder call, including input staging and output copies. Correctness is checked against an eager forward of the same batch.

The table shows the batches with the most padding, plus a few full batches. Batches that fill their budget are unchanged.

| Batch | Images | Tokens | Padding rows | Before (ms) | This PR (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 224² x 1 | 1 | 64 | 0 | 2.2 | 2.3 |
| 224² x 16 | 16 | 1024 | 0 | 8.5 | 8.4 |
| 672² x 1 | 1 | 576 | 1,792 | 9.2 | 8.7 |
| 672² x 4 | 4 | 2304 | 7,168 | 35.7 | 29.5 |
| 672² x 8 | 8 | 4608 | 14,336 | 84.2 | 58.6 |
| 1344² x 1 | 1 | 2304 | 7,168 | 45.8 | 38.8 |
| 1344² x 2 | 2 | 4608 | 14,336 | 102.6 | 77.1 |
| 1344² x 4 | 4 | 9216 | 28,672 | 251.8 | 151.8 |
| 336² x 17 | 17 | 2448 | 6,592 | 33.4 | 27.5 |
| 13 mixed sizes | 13 | 5298 | 11,576 | 86.7 | 67.5 |
| 25 mixed sizes | 25 | 9214 | 28,936 | 227.6 | 122.5 |

The full matrix has 35 batches: small, medium, large, wide, unaligned and random mixes. It was run once after a large batch had dirtied the buffers, to check that stale tail rows do not leak.

- Every single-replay batch is bitwise equal to eager, before and after.
- Batches that the default dispatch splits into two replays differ from eager by the same relative L2 (0.0013) before and after. That comes from bf16 accumulation order across replays, not from padding.
- A 336x336 single image differs from eager by relative L2 0.016 with every graph variant, the padding sequence included. At layer 0 both paths are equally close to an fp32 reference (0.00171 vs 0.00172), so it is bf16 accumulation order, unrelated to this change.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
# encoder-only benchmark harness (vitbench.py, not in the repo; available on request)
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python vitbench.py --model minimax \
  --model-path <MiniMax-M3.1-Flash snapshot> --output minimax.jsonl --repeats 15 --stale-check
```

</details>

## Details

One file, +7/−19, mostly deletions. No change outside the MiniMax-M3 encoder graph mixin.

- `pad_cu_seqlens` now repeats the last real offset into the tail slots. The `data_ptr` registry and the spare `cu_seqlens` slot are removed.
- `max_seqlen` stays at the captured row count, since one image can still fill the buffer.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes MiniMax-M3 encoder graph padding. #65084 (shared capture buffers) depends on this fix to stay correct on MiniMax; it does not touch the padding.

**Tests.**
- `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k minimax_m3`: image test passed, video skipped (image-only model). It uses dummy weights and budget 512, so it covers replay with padding but only checks that generation runs. Run locally against a MiniMax-M3.1-Flash config with `block_size=128`, because the cached `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` snapshot has no tokenizer.
- Output correctness: the real-weight encoder benchmark above (35 batches, checked against eager).
- `pre-commit` passes.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid catastrophic cancellation in the acceptance estimator
author: fuscof-ibm
body:
## Overview Follow-up to #52228, which added the estimator to do adaptive verification without a confidence head. The adaptive-verification acceptance feature loses its entire signal to catastrophic cancellation whenever the drafter is confident. Every draft row more confident than `1 - 6e-8` reports the same acceptance feature, `40.0`, whatever its true confidence is. The feature is specified as a log-odds, `logit(q(m*))`, but it recovers the complement mass by subtracting 1 from a sum that includes the max's own unit term, which in fp32 destroys the quantity being measured — no NaN, no warning, just the clamp. **Headline:** at temperature 0.5 on source code, **11.5% of draft positions** had their confidence score destroyed and replaced with a constant. The failing positions are not exotic or adversarial — the single worst case in the sample is completing `tl.int64` from `tl.int6` (see the `Details` section for the error analysis). This PR computes the complement directly instead fixing completely the numerical issue. ## Claims - The feature is accurate to fp32 relative precision across the full range it is clamped to. Previously it saturated to the `_MAX_LOG_ODDS` clamp for any row more confident than `1 - 6e-8`, collapsing a ~23-nat span of distinct confidences onto a single value. - No change to the feature's definition, the fit, the trimming policy, or any buffer layout the rest of adaptive verification reads. - One extra fp32 partial per (token, vocab block): 0.1% of the kernel's memory traffic (311 KiB against 311 MiB of logit reads at 1024 tokens and a 152k vocab). No extra kernel launch. ## Validation `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py` — **18 passed in 7.08s** on an NVIDIA H100 GPU, covering the pre-existing tests plus three new ones: - `test_feature_resolves_a_tiny_complement_mass` — δ ∈ {1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-12} against an fp64 reference computed without ever forming `1 + δ`. Fails at 1e-6 and 1e-12 on `main`. - `test_feature_combines_blocks_around_the_global_max` — parametrized over which of three vocabulary blocks holds the top token. Every pre-existing test used a 2048-token vocabulary, narrower than the kernel's 4096-wide block, so `num_blocks` was always 1 and the cross-block combine was dead code in the suite. - `test_feature_drops_exactly_one_tied_maximum` — k tied maxima must leave k-1 in the complement, giving `-log(k-1)`. Parametrized over ties within one block and across blocks, which catch different mistakes and are each blind to the other's. ## Details The estimator introduced in #52228 basically trains a logistic regression using as a feature the probability of the most likely draft token, $qmax$ , to construct a feature: ```math f={logit}(qmax) =\log\!\left(\frac{qmax}{1-qmax}\right) ``` Let the temperature-scaled logits be $x_1 \ldots x_V$, and let $m=max_i x_i$, then #### ```math qmax=q_{i^*}=\frac{e^m}{\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^V e^{x_j}}=\frac{1}{1+\sum_{j\ne i^*}e^{x_j-m}} ``` Let's define ```math S=\sum_{j\ne i^*}e^{x_j-m} ``` Then : ```math \begin{aligned} q_{\max} &= \frac{1}{1+S} \\[6pt] 1-q_{\max} &= 1-\frac{1}{1+S} = \frac{1+S}{1+S}-\frac{1}{1+S}= \frac{S}{1+S} \end{aligned} ``` We can rewrite as: ```math f=\log\left(\frac{qmax}{1-qmax}\right)=\log\left(\frac{1}{S}\right)=-\log S. ``` The computation of $S$ is what makes the current code in `main` exposed to catastrophic cancellation. The previous approach (in `main`) computes $S$ (see the logic in the `_predict_kernel`) by summing the totals (`total_sumexp` in the code, $A$ in what follows) and then subtracting `1`: ```math A = \sum_{j=1}^V e^{x_j-m} = 1 +S ``` ```math S = A - 1 = \left(\sum_{j=1}^V e^{x_j-m}\right)-1 ``` The problem is that when there is a confident prediction (i.e. $qmax$ is high) $S$ must be small as $qmax=\frac{1}{1+S}$. The result is that for a small $S$ (e.g. $S= 10^{-12}$) $A = 1.0 + S = 1.0 $. Therefore, $1.0 - 1.0 = 0.0$, and the final feature becomes $+\inf$, leading to a clamped value of $40.0$. The real value for the feature when $S= 10^{-12}$ would be instead $f = -\log(10^{-12}) \approx 27.63 \ldots$. This PR introduced a block based algorithm to compute $S$ as a sum of positive quantities: ```math S = \sum_{j\ne i^*}e^{x_j-M} ``` We introduce the function `_max_and_sumexps` which returns three quantities for each vocabulary block: its maximum logit, its full exponential sum, and its sum excluding *one* maximum position. For one block $b$, let $m_b$ denote its maximum, and $j_b$ a single index where that maximum occurs, the routines compute: ```math $$ \begin{aligned} m_b &= \max_{j\in b} x_j,\\ A_b &= \sum_{j\in b} e^{x_j-m_b},\\ E_b &= \sum_{\substack{j\in b\\j\ne j_b}} e^{x_j-m_b}. \end{aligned} $$ ``` The vocabulary is split into blocks (the new tests identify a width of \(4096\) elements). Each block has a different $m_b$, so its local $A_b$ and $E_b$ are expressed in a different exponential scale. They cannot be added without rescaling. Let's the global maximum and one selected winning block as: ```math $$ M = \max_b m_b,\qquad b^* \in {argmax}_b m_b. $$ ``` For any token in block $b$, the identity $e^{x_j-M} = e^{x_j-m_b}\,e^{m_b-M}$ shows how to convert the block's local exponential sum to the global scale. Its factor is $e^{m_b-M}$. This allows to perform the sum in blocks. What want to achieve is that the block that contains the actual max provides the sum omitting exactly one index, while the other blocks provide the full sum. This formula is simply a partition of $\sum_{j\ne i^*}e^{x_j-M}$ into blocks. ```math S=\sum_b e^{m_b-M} \begin{cases} E_b,&b=b^*,\\ A_b,&b\ne b^*. \end{cases} ``` - If $ b = b^* $, one globally maximal token must be left out, so use $E_{b^*}$. - If $b \neq b^*$, every token in block $b$ belongs in the complement and the contribution is $e^{m_b-M}A_b$. #### Error analysis setup To simplify the analysis/data collection we use CPU code in python. The Triton path on the GPU (before the fix) has the same cancellation problem. **Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`**, loaded from the local Hugging Face cache in fp32 on CPU via `transformers`: ```python tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B") model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", dtype=torch.float32).eval() ids = tok(text, return_tensors="pt").input_ids[:, :512] logits = model(ids).logits[0][:-1] # drop the last row: no next token follows it ``` Chosen for three reasons: 1. **Plausible drafter size.** 0.6B is in the range actually used for draft models 2. **Production-scale vocabulary — 151,936 tokens.** The complement sums over the *whole* tail, so a large vocabulary adds roughly `log(V)` to δ and makes saturation **harder**. Measuring on a large vocabulary is therefore the `conservative choice`; a smaller-vocabulary drafter would saturate more often, not less. 3. **It spans three vocabulary blocks.** The kernel reduces in 4096-wide blocks, so 151,936 tokens exercise the cross-block combine rather than the single-block degenerate case. We compute the `new` and `old` values as follows: ```python # old: everything, then subtract the top token's own unit term total = (sumexps * rescale).sum(dim=1) old = (total - 1.0).clamp(min=0.0) # new: the max's own block contributes its excluding sum, so nothing cancels use = sumexps.scatter(1, best_block[:, None], excl.gather(1, best_block[:, None])) new = (use * rescale).sum(dim=1) ``` **Inputs.** Two files from the vllm repo representing two different language distributions (code and prose): - code: [acceptance_estimator.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/acceptance_estimator.py) - prose:[README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/README.md) **thresholds**: Two thresholds are used: | name | condition | meaning | |---|---|---| | **degraded** | δ < 1e-5 | the subtraction is shedding digits; ≥1% error in the feature | | **saturated** | δ < 2^-24 ≈ 5.96e-8 | the value is gone; the feature pins to 40.0 | **Scripts, all CPU-only** to inspect the failure modes: | script | purpose | |---|---| | `measure_feature_distribution.py` | degraded/saturated rates by temperature | | `find_saturating_tokens.py` | decodes the failing positions | | `plot_feature_histogram.py` | the old-vs-new distribution figure | | `emulate_feature_error.py` | synthetic δ sweep, no model needed | Environment: `torch 2.11.0`, `transformers 5.13.0`, CPU, fp32. #### Acceptance feature distribution(s) The following plot highlights the acceptance feature distributions, original vs fixed. **logit(q_max)** is computed twice from identical logits in fp32 with the kernel's 4096-wide vocabulary blocking (Qwen3-0.6B, temp 0.5, 1022 code and prose positions), histogrammed on a log y-axis. _The original Σe^(z−m*) − 1 path cannot represent anything between 15.94 — one fp32 ulp of 1.0 — and the ±40 clamp, so 14% of positions with true features spanning 16–35 collapse to a single spike at 40, while the excluding-sum fix tracks the fp64 reference continuously to 34.86._ Analysis code: [plot_feature_histogram.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34314874/plot_feature_histogram.py) Command `python3 plot_feature_histogram.py ` #### Temperature dependence Analysis code: [measure_feature_distribution.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34315254/measure_feature_distribution.py) Command: `python3 PR_numerical_stability/measure_feature_distribution.py --temperatures 1.0 0.9 0.8 0.7 0.6 0.5 0.4 0.3 0.2 0.1 ` Temperature is applied *before* the feature is computed, in `_local_max_sumexp_kernel` (the `temp = tl.where(temp > 0.0, temp, 1.0)` guard and the division just below it), dividing the logit gap and multiplying the feature by `1/temp`. So lowering temperature pushes rows over the fp32 wall mechanically. Measured rates: | temp | code degraded | code **saturated** | prose degraded | prose **saturated** | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1.0 | 2.0% | **0.2%** | 2.9% | **0.0%** | | 0.9 | 3.7% | **0.6%** | 6.1% | **0.2%** | | 0.8 | 7.8% | **1.2%** | 11.0% | **1.8%** | | 0.7 | 11.5% | **2.3%** | 15.7% | **3.7%** | | 0.6 | 15.5% | **6.3%** | 22.3% | **8.2%** | | 0.5 | 22.1% | **11.5%** | 28.0% | **15.3%** | | 0.4 | 28.0% | **17.0%** | 35.6% | **24.5%** | | 0.3 | 35.2% | **25.8%** | 42.1% | **33.1%** | | 0.2 | 46.6% | **36.0%** | 49.3% | **43.1%** | | 0.1 | 67.7% | **56.2%** | 65.8% | **57.7%** | Reading this: - **At temp 1.0 the bug is nearly invisible** — 0.2% of code rows, 0% of prose. A benchmark run at temperature 1.0 will show nothing, on any metric. This is worth stating plainly because it means "we A/B tested and saw no difference" is the *expected* result at that setting, not evidence the bug is benign. - **The knee is between 0.8 and 0.5.** Saturation roughly doubles per 0.1 step of temperature through that range: 1.2% → 2.3% → 6.3% → 11.5%. - **Greedy decoding (temp = 0) is a separate case.** `temp == 0` is mapped to `1.0` rather than dividing by zero, so greedy rows land in the temp-1.0 row of this table. They also mix an unscaled feature into the same shared slope as temperature-scaled rows, which is its own modelling issue and out of scope here. - **Prose saturates slightly *more* than code below 0.6.** That surprised me; I had expected code to dominate throughout. Natural language has plenty of near-deterministic continuations too (fixed phrases, inflections, markup), and at low temperature those cross the wall just as easily. **The failure is not code-specific — code is simply where low temperatures are _*conventional*_.** The practical reading: **temp ≤ 0.7 is where this starts to matter, and temp ≤ 0.5 is where it is common. ** Both are ordinary settings for code completion and structured-output serving. #### Real examples All from this repository's own source, Qwen3-0.6B. `true` is the fp64 value;`old` is what the original fp32 path produced; `gap` is the *raw* pre-temperature top-2 logit gap. Analysis code: [find_saturating_tokens.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34315054/find_saturating_tokens.py) ##### At temp 0.5 — `acceptance_estimator.py`, 59/511 positions saturate (11.5%) Command: `python3 find_saturating_tokens.py`: ``` true 34.86 | old 40.0 | δ 7.3e-16 | gap 17.51 ...' other=0).to(\n tl.int6' -> '4' (runner-up '3') true 32.22 | old 40.0 | δ 1.0e-14 | gap 16.54 ...'.0,\n ).to(tl.float3' -> '2' (runner-up 'b') true 30.19 | old 40.0 | δ 7.8e-14 | gap 15.10 ...' num_accepted = tl.maximum(num_sample' -> 'd' (runner-up 'ded') true 28.63 | old 40.0 | δ 3.7e-13 | gap 14.60 ...'.program_id(0).to(tl.int6' -> '4' (runner-up '5') ``` `tl.int6` → `4`. The model has to complete `tl.int64`, and `tl.int63` is not a type. It is right to be certain. The feature that exists to express certainty reports the same number it would for a coin flip between two tokens 17 nats apart — because both exceed what fp32 can represent. ##### At temp 0.7 — same file, 12/511 saturate (2.3%) Command: `python3 find_saturating_tokens.py --temperature 0.7` The rate drops but the character does not; the same tokens are simply closer to the wall: ``` true 24.69 | old 40.0 | ...'tl.int6' -> '4' true 22.55 | old 40.0 | ...').to(tl.float3' -> '2' true 18.56 | old 40.0 | ...'pred_ptr + req_state' -> '_block' (runner-up '_blocks') ``` That last one is interesting: the runner-up `'_blocks'` is a *plausible* alternative, and the true feature of 18.56 says "confident, not certain." The old path reports 40.0 — maximal certainty — for a row where the model itself left room for doubt. ---

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Keep lazy SimpleCPUOffload stores at the GPU eviction end
author: Juntian777
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Lazy SimpleCPUOffload should offload the blocks the allocator will evict next, but two behaviors move it away from them. This PR fixes both: stored blocks go back to the front of the GPU free queue, and every walk starts from the head of the queue instead of a saved cursor.

Includes the two commits of #59383 by @obendidi, rebased onto main with authorship kept, plus the walk change. Builds on #64229.

## Claims

- Lazy stores return GPU blocks to the eviction end (from #59383).
- The lazy walk starts at the head of the free queue on every step, so it no longer offloads blocks far from eviction.
- With sliding-window groups that are not prefix-cacheable (DeepSeek-V4.1) and a contended CPU tier, the walk change is what lowers recomputed blocks; #59383 alone does not help there. The simulation below went from 67.5% to 59.7% recomputed blocks with 32 such blocks per cached block.
- No change to eager mode. Net -3 lines outside tests (+17/-20).

## Validation

Tests, on CPU:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py
```

Result: 152 passed. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

`test_lazy_walk_does_not_offload_past_eviction_window` fails before the walk change: the second walk offloads the blocks past `target_free`. `test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end` comes from #59383.

Simulation: the real `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` and `BlockPool` replaying one multi-turn session trace per row, with only the requests and store completions simulated. Each cell is the share of prompt blocks recomputed, averaged over 2 seeds (lower is better). The CPU tier is 2x the GPU pool and the working set is about 2.7x the CPU tier. SWA blocks are taken from the same free queue and freed on the next step. The 32 row uses twice the pool and half the per-step budget of the others, so that the SWA blocks fit, and runs long enough to reach steady state.

| Uncached SWA blocks per cached block | main | #59383 only | walk from head only | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 74.8% | 55.8% | 74.5% | 55.7% |
| 8 | 64.7% | 66.5% | 60.0% | 57.6% |
| 32 | 67.5% | 70.5% | 62.6% | 59.7% |

Per request, #59383 alone also writes 1.8x (8 SWA) to 2.1x (32 SWA) as many blocks to the CPU tier as this PR. When the CPU tier holds the whole working set (8 SWA), all four variants recompute 4.0%.

Not validated:

- No E2E serving run was done for this PR, so these are block-level hit rates and not a throughput measurement. The pool sizes and session shape are assumptions.
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_integration.py` has no passing result: its 2 non-optional tests need a GPU. They failed at engine startup on a GPU without enough free memory, and also fail without a GPU, as `test_chunked_local_partial_gpu_hit` does on main. They need a run in CI or on a free GPU.

## Details

Root cause: the cursor is only reset when its block leaves the free queue. Uncached SWA blocks are freed to the front of the queue and reused there, so the block under the cursor is often neither stored nor reallocated, and the walk resumes past it. In the simulation with SWA groups, about 99% of walks with only #59383 applied resumed from the cursor, against 72% without SWA. The walk then misses the blocks #59383 returned to the front and keeps offloading fresher blocks, which turns over the CPU tier.

Why not just #59383: it is sufficient without such groups (first row), but on DeepSeek-V4.1-style configurations it needs the walk change. The two are combined here so they can be reviewed and merged together. If #59383 merges first, this PR reduces to the walk commit.

Tradeoffs: a walk now revisits blocks already on CPU near the head, but it is still bounded by `target_free`, the same bound as before. One simulated case favors #59383 alone: without SWA groups and with an 8-step store latency, it recomputes 67.2% against 70.8% here. With 8 SWA blocks and the same latency, this PR is better (65.6% against 58.7%).

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Skip the client-side chat template on chat backends
author: dilberx
body:
The `custom`, `hf`, `spec_bench` and `speed_bench` datasets apply the tokenizer's chat template to each prompt unless `--skip-chat-template` is passed. With `--backend openai-chat`, `openai-responses` or `vllm-chat`, that already-templated prompt is sent as the content of a user message, and the server (or `LLM.chat` for `vllm bench throughput`) applies the template a second time. The model sees two nested templates, and input token counts are inflated.

`get_samples` now treats chat backends as `--skip-chat-template`. Completion backends (`openai`, `vllm`) keep the client-side template, since their endpoint takes raw text.

On Qwen2.5-1.5B with 8 custom-dataset prompts and `--backend openai-chat`, using server-reported usage:

| client | total input tokens | per request |
|---|---|---|
| main | 384 | 48 |
| this PR | 232 | 29 |

232 matches the same prompts sent through `--backend openai` with the client template, so the chat path now sends one template.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_chat_template_kwargs.py`: 7 passed. On main, the three new chat-backend cases fail and the two completion-backend cases pass.
- `pytest tests/benchmarks` (excluding the serve/throughput/latency CLI tests): the same 9 tests fail on main and on this branch (`test_bench_startup`, `test_forward_cli`, `test_mm_processor_cli`), all `FileNotFoundError: 'vllm'` from the `vllm` CLI not being on PATH in my environment.
- GPU check above on an RTX 3080.

## Duplicate check

Searched open PRs and issues for skip-chat-template / chat template applied twice in the bench client; found none.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the commands above.

title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Preserve inactive expert IDs in synthetic forward routing
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Preserve inactive `-1` expert IDs in `vllm bench forward`'s Zipf and balanced routing hook. Previously, substituting the synthetic fixture could reactivate masked expert slots.

## Claims

- Inactive slots remain `-1`; active slots receive the same synthetic IDs and routing weights remain unchanged.
- The fixture is not mutated, so subsequent replays can activate previously inactive slots.

## Validation

The focused regression failed all four parameters without the fix and passed with it (positional/keyword IDs, int32/int64). The existing Zipf selection test also passed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \
  -k 'synthetic_expert_ids_preserve_inactive_slots or zipf_expert_selection' -q
```

On GB200, the real Muse router/bias test and both tiny Muse CLI configurations passed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \
  -k 'muse_synthetic_routing or balanced_routing_restores_expert_bias' -v
```

Balanced and Zipf each produced finite, deterministic prefill/decode output with exact graph/eager equality. The CLI uses the gate-logits path without capture-bucket padding; the focused hook regression establishes sentinel preservation. This does not claim end-to-end padded EP performance validation.

File-scoped pre-commit checks passed. GPU validation used `78fc2bbed0`; the rebased routing, test and documentation files are byte-identical. The rebase only reconciled the CI selector with upstream additions. [Validation details](https://github.com/Inferact/vllm-perf-data/blob/main/patches/forward-zipf-padding.md).

## Details

The generic expert-input hook replaced the entire ID tensor without preserving its inactive sentinel. A tensor selection now retains existing `-1` entries. This adds comparison/selection work inside the timed generic hook, without host synchronization. The gate-logits hook and production serving are unchanged. Docs clarify exact-shape benchmark graphs versus serving capture-bucket padding.

Duplicate checks found no competing fix. #64167 introduced the Zipf default and is merged; #57100 concerns the separate MoE kernel benchmark, #65085 concerns forward batch budgets, and #52532 concerns Marlin token ordering.

title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Fix mixed draft-model warmup token budget
author: wxsIcey
body:
## Overview
Draft-model initialization with speculative decoding can fail during mixed prefill/decode warmup:
```
AssertionError: Shape: 2050 out of considered ranges: [(1, 2048)]
```

The warmup creates one synthetic decode request and one synthetic prefill request, but builds the scheduler inputs directly and bypasses the scheduler's correction-slot reservation. The extra query slots for these requests were missing from the warmup token budget, allowing the resulting shape to exceed max_num_tokens.

When a speculator is enabled, cap the warmup token count at max_num_tokens - num_warmup_reqs * num_extra_query_per_req. Skip the warmup if the adjusted budget is too small for a mixed step.

This fixes a regression in the mixed warmup path added by [#56492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492).

## Validation

```
vllm serve /shared/models/modelscope/models/Qwen/Qwen3-32B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8900 \
  --served-model-name qwen3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --seed 42 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 10000 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
```

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Don't split a multimodal item when a prefix cache hit ends inside it
author: Anieca
body:
## Overview

With `disable_chunked_mm_input`, the scheduler still splits a multimodal item when a prefix cache hit ends inside it and the step has no room for the rest of the item. Models with bidirectional attention over the item then prefill its first part without seeing the rest.

#52306 reported these splits and #52412 and #59721 fixed them, but this path remained.

## Claims

- When a cache hit ends inside a multimodal item, the request waits for a step that can schedule the rest of the item.
- Adds tests for a cache hit inside an image, at the scheduler and end to end.

## Validation

On base `51c6dfd8c`:

```text
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k mm_input_chunking                                   # CPU
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py -k cache_hit_inside_image      # L4
```

With the original `scheduler.py`, three of the new checks fail: the request that hit the cache is scheduled 39 tokens into the image, the guard returns 500 tokens for a chunk that starts inside the item, and end to end the 40 image tokens prefilled first differ from the request run alone (320 / 800 elements, max abs diff 8.5e-3). With the fix, all pass.

## Details

Root cause: the guard assumes a chunk never starts inside an item, which does not hold in these cases:

- The same image is followed by a different question. The last block of the image also holds the start of the question, so that block misses and the hit stops inside the image.
- The KV cache runs short. Blocks are reused tail first, so the hit can stop early in the image, leaving most of it.

With the flag on, startup checks that one item fits in a step (`max_num_batched_tokens`), so the request is not starved. A `long_prefill_token_threshold` smaller than the item stalls it, as it already does on main (#62031, #62030).

#62782 changes the same lines; the two combine in either merge order.

No open issue or PR covers this case (checked 2026-11-02).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Step3 tool parser: coerce nullable and object/array parameters by schema
author: 0xDexe
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65273. `Step3ToolParser._cast_arguments` only coerced a parameter when its schema had a single string `type`, so nullable parameters (`Optional[int]`, `Optional[bool]`, …) and `object`/`array` parameters reached clients as raw strings. It now resolves types with the shared `extract_types_from_schema` + `coerce_to_schema_type` helpers.

Related: #64517 / #64546, fixed for the Muse, MiniCPM5, and Poolside V1 parsers in #64539.

## Claims

- Nullable parameters are coerced to their declared type, whether written as `"type": ["integer", "null"]` or `anyOf`/`oneOf` with `{"type": "null"}` (the form pydantic emits for `Optional[...]`): `"5"` → `5`, `"true"` → `True`, `"null"` → `None`.
- `object` and `array` parameters are parsed as JSON instead of being returned as strings.
- Plain `string`/`integer`/`number`/`boolean`/`null` parameters, untyped parameters, and values that cannot be coerced (e.g. `"many"` for an integer) behave as before.

## Validation

Reproduction script from #65273 (CPU only, no model download):

```
# main
{'count': 5, 'opt_count': '5', 'opt_count_list': '5', 'opt_flag': 'true', 'filters': '{"a": 1}', 'tags': '["x", "y"]'}

# this PR
{'count': 5, 'opt_count': 5, 'opt_count_list': 5, 'opt_flag': True, 'filters': {'a': 1}, 'tags': ['x', 'y']}
```

Tests: added 13 parametrized cases to `tests/tool_parsers/test_step3_tool_parser.py` covering nullable integer/number/boolean/string via `type` lists, `anyOf` and `oneOf`, plus object, array, untyped, and uncoercible values. They construct the parser with a mock tokenizer, so they need no download.

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_step3_tool_parser.py
24 passed, 8 xfailed
```

The 8 xfails are pre-existing markers on this file and are unchanged. `pre-commit` passes on both changed files. Run on CPU (WSL2, Python 3.14).

## Details

**Root cause:** `_cast_arguments` read `prop.get("type")` and dispatched on it with an `if typ == "string" / "integer" / "number" / "boolean" / "null"` chain. A list `type`, an `anyOf`/`oneOf` schema, or `object`/`array` matched no branch, so the value was left as the raw string.

**Fix:** replace the chain with `coerce_to_schema_type(value.strip(), extract_types_from_schema(prop))`, the same helpers `k2_horizon_tool_parser.py` uses. They already handle type lists, `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`, enum inference, type aliases, and non-finite numbers. The now-unused `contextlib` import is removed.

**Behavior changes inherited from the shared helper** (noting for reviewers):
- Whole `number` values come back as `5` rather than `5.0`. Both are valid JSON numbers.
- `"1"` and `"0"` are accepted for `boolean` parameters, in addition to `true`/`false`.

**Not changed:** the separate issue behind this file's existing xfail markers. Non-streaming extraction only parses calls in the `<｜tool_call_begin｜>function<｜tool_sep｜>…` form. That is out of scope here.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Use promised max_query_len for encoder-only FULL CUDA graphs
author: pst2154
body:
## Overview

With the V2 model runner, models whose attention is encoder-only (non-causal, no KV cache) produce wrong outputs when they
are served with `cudagraph_mode=FULL`.

A FULL CUDA graph for mixed batches is captured on a dummy batch that spreads its tokens over many requests (down to one
token each), but it may later replay a batch with one long prompt. `DefaultModelState` already builds the captured
attention metadata from the batch's promised `max_query_len` for this reason. `EncoderOnlyModelState` instead used the
dummy batch's actual largest query length, so the encoder attention kernels in the graph kept a very short
`max_seqlen_q` / `max_seqlen_k`. Prompts that replay such a graph are then computed incorrectly. There is no error.

The fix applies the same rule as `DefaultModelState`: use `input_batch.max_query_len` when the batch sets it, and fall
back to the largest scheduled query length otherwise.

```python
max_query_len = input_batch.max_query_len
if max_query_len is None:
    max_query_len = int(input_batch.num_scheduled_tokens.max())
```

One file changed (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/encoder_only.py`), plus a regression test.

## Claims

- Encoder-only models served with `cudagraph_mode=FULL` give the same outputs as eager execution.
- No change for `PIECEWISE` or `NONE`, for decoder models, or for batches without FULL graphs.
- With the fix, FULL graphs are a correct option for these models: slightly faster single-request reads than PIECEWISE,
  about equal under load (table below).

## Validation

| test | hardware | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_only_full_cudagraph.py`: `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` with `is_causal=False`, FP32, prompts of 23 / 150 / 600 / 1000 tokens one at a time; FULL (capture to 1024) vs eager, last-position logprobs, atol = rtol = 1e-4 | L40S | **fails** (max abs difference 0.034) | passes |
| 8B non-causal decoder fine-tune, FP8, accuracy eval of 13,904 requests, FULL graphs (capture to 8192) vs PIECEWISE | GB200 | 1.5-2 points lower than PIECEWISE (wrong reads) | **identical to PIECEWISE**, two full repeats on each of three configurations (capture to 8192, capture to 2048, 0.6 memory utilization) |
| same eval | L40S | pending | pending |
| ruff check / format | — | | clean |

## Benchmark

NVIDIA GB200 (one GPU), 8B non-causal decoder fine-tune, FP8, `max_cudagraph_capture_size=8192`, one exclusive node,
each configuration measured alone.

| | FULL, this PR | PIECEWISE |
|---|---|---|
| 512-token read, concurrency 1, p50 / p95 | 13.4 / 14.8 ms | 14.0 / 16.5 ms |
| mixed prompts (~1.7k tokens), concurrency 1, requests/s | 35.3 | 32.7 |
| same, concurrency 16, requests/s | 41.8 | 42.8 |
| same, concurrency 64, requests/s | 41.1 | 42.3 |

The main point of the PR is correctness: on main, FULL looks faster (12.6 ms for the same 512-token read) only because
it computes the wrong attention.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve SWA null-page offsets after store retry
author: waizuichougou
body:
## Overview

When a CPU offload store is retried after capacity exhaustion, SWA can release a GPU block and reallocate it for another logical position. The offloading scheduler marks the old position as `NULL_BLOCK_ID` but removes it from the source spec, so later pages shift into the wrong positions in the destination CPU chunk and can be loaded back as incorrect KV data.

## Claims

- Preserve the logical page layout of every full SWA chunk in the GPU-to-CPU store spec, including null blocks as placeholders for unreachable pages.
- Prevent store retries from corrupting the mapping between GPU source pages and CPU chunk offsets.
- Add a scheduler regression test with a mocked store failure and SWA block reuse.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Test command</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k test_swa_retry_keeps_internal_null_block_in_store_spec -q
```

With the fix:

```text
1 passed, 484 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.94s
```

With the regression test applied to the parent revision:

```text
At index 6 diff: 8 != 0
Right contains one more item: 9
1 failed, 484 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.90s
```

</details>

Without the fix, the generated store spec contains only 8 source pages and skips the internal null page. With the fix, it contains all 9 logical pages with `group_sizes=[9]` and `block_indices=[0]`.

A separate validation with the real `CPUOffloadingManager`, scheduler, offloading handler, and CUDA transfers reproduced the data error before the fix: loading logical pages 7 and 8 returned `[9, -99]` instead of `[8, 9]`. After the fix, the stored chunk was `[0, 8, 9]` and loading logical pages 7 and 8 returned `[8, 9]`.

No model-level evaluation was performed. The V1 KV Connectors GPU CI job is currently disabled, so the regression test was run manually.

## Details

`prepare_store()` can return `None` when all CPU chunks are held by in-flight loads and no chunk is free or evictable. During the retry window, SWA may release a GPU block and reallocate it for another position. The offloading scheduler then marks the old logical position as `NULL_BLOCK_ID`. `_build_store_jobs()` previously dropped that null block when building `GPULoadStoreSpec.block_ids`. The remaining pages were then packed without their original logical offset, although the destination CPU chunk still reserved a slot for every page in the full chunk.

The fix keeps null blocks as placeholders for unreachable pages in the source spec so source and destination chunk offsets remain aligned. Null blocks are excluded from the fence set because block 0 is the permanently reserved GPU null block and is not a live allocation.

Unlike #62932, which bounds secondary-tier loads by CPU capacity, this fixes GPU-to-CPU store page alignment after a retry.

The change is limited to source-spec construction in `OffloadingConnectorScheduler` and one focused regression test. It does not change admission, eviction, retry, or partial-tail behavior.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Mooncake store: register the committed blocks of an extensible KV cache
author: gcanlin
body:
## Overview

With the extensible KV cache (on by default since #56492), `MooncakeStoreConnector` fails at startup. Its worker splits each layer's view by `cache_config.num_gpu_blocks`, but `extend_kv_cache` creates the connector against the committed views before it updates that value, so `group_kernel_blocks` asserts. The worker now takes the block count from its own `kv_cache_config`, as the rest of the worker already does.

```
mooncake/store/worker.py, in register_kv_caches
    group_kernel_blocks(view, self.num_blocks)
kv_cache_interface.py, in group_kernel_blocks
    assert cache.shape[0] % num_blocks == 0
AssertionError
```

No open PR covers this (searched for Mooncake + extensible KV cache). Related: #56492, #65225, #65137.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash, colocated DEP8 on 8x B200, `MooncakeStoreConnector` with a standalone store (1.3 TB DRAM plus a 6 TiB SSD tier), real MTP 5. Image nightly `e0d00e4b8e` with this change applied:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Startup | `AssertionError` in `group_kernel_blocks` | Serves; KV cache extended to 1920 blocks (105.38 GiB, 15,728,640 tokens per rank) |
| GSM8K, 5-shot | – | 0.9727 (0.975 with `--disable-extensible-kv-cache`) |
| Needle read-back | – | 16/16 on a cold store; 32/32 after 15 minutes of AgentX at concurrency 384, by which time 2.61 TB had spilled to SSD |

Needle read-back: 16 contexts of about 20K tokens with 800 locker codes each. Each context is asked one code on a cold store, then the same code and a new one after the load.

The new unit test fails without the fix and passes with it. The rest of `test_mooncake_store_worker.py`, `test_mooncake_store_connector.py` and `test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py` give the same results with and without it.

```bash

```

title: [Multimodal][Bugfix] Fix Step3-VL encoder output aliasing and guard shared CUDA graph capture buffers
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #65084, which shares encoder CUDA graph capture buffers across token budgets. Sharing introduced two issues, and this PR fixes both:

1. Step3-VL returns views of the graph output, which a later replay overwrites.
2. The model protocol was tightened without saying so: buffers written only at capture time can be overwritten by other budgets.

## Claims

- **Step3-VL embeddings no longer get overwritten.** A no-patch image's embedding was a view of the `global` graph output, even with `clone=True`. A later replay in the same `execute()` overwrote it. Before #65084 this needed two batches on the *same* budget; with sharing, any budget on the path does it. Fix: honor `clone`.
- **Capture-time-only buffers are guarded.**
  - Before: 0-dim buffers were shared wholesale, so after capture every budget's graph saw the smallest budget's value. A shared buffer that replay did not refill silently kept another budget's contents.
  - After: 0-dim buffers stay per budget. These scalars cost no memory, so nothing is lost. Replay raises if it omits a buffer that smaller budgets view.
  - The constraints are documented: replay must refill shared buffers, `padding_logics` must write the whole destination, and `postprocess_encoder_output(clone=True)` must not alias its outputs.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (`tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py`): 118 passed.

| Test | Covers | Fails without the fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_step3_vl_postprocess_clones_global_only_item` (new) | Step3-VL honors `clone=True` | ✔ |
| `test_replay_without_shared_buffer_raises` (new) | Replay guard | ✔ |
| `test_scalar_buffers_keep_own_value` (was `test_scalar_buffers_are_shared`) | Each budget's graph keeps its own scalar | ✔ |

**End-to-end on MI355X** (Model Runner V2, default budgets). A 3-image prompt with `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch=2` splits one `execute()` into several batches. Each returned embedding is compared with the same image encoded alone (relative L2; bf16 noise is ≤ 0.05).

| Model | Corrupted embeddings, before → after | Capture buffers, before → after |
|---|---|---|
| Step3-VL-10B | **5/11 → 0/11** (max rel. error 0.62 → 0.04) | 430.1 → 430.1 MiB |
| Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct | 0/11 → 0/11 | 488.0 → 488.0 MiB |
| Gemma4-E2B-it | 0/11 → 0/11 | 344.1 → 344.1 MiB |
| MiniMax-M3 (TP2, `mm_encoder_tp_mode=data`) | — → 0/11; guard not triggered | — → 554.0 MiB |

## Details

- **Why main is safe today.** The only capture-time-only key in-tree is the CPU `max_seqlen`. ViT attention reads it with `.item()` at capture, so later overwrites never reach a graph. The guard and the docs keep future or out-of-tree models from silently depending on this.
- **Why the fix is in Step3-VL, not the manager.** Every other `postprocess_encoder_output` already returns fresh tensors. Cloning in the manager would add a full copy for all of them.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Handle media cache eviction during reads
author: Woolgathererer
body:
## Overview

A media cache entry evicted between its metadata check and read can be recreated as an empty file, causing image decoding to fail. Treat this race as a cache miss so the media is downloaded again.

## Claims

- Refresh cache entry timestamps without recreating files removed by concurrent LRU eviction.
- Add synchronous and asynchronous regression coverage for cache eviction during reads.

## Validation

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py -q --tb=short`: 84 passed.
- The synchronous and asynchronous regression tests fail on the original implementation with an image-decoding error and pass with the fix.
- On a DGX Spark, a Qwen3.8-27B `LLM.chat` request reproduced the failure with the original cache method and succeeded with the patched method. Normal requests had identical prompt and generated token IDs. This test used installed vLLM 0.31.0 with the patched `_get_cached_bytes` method from this checkout injected into the runtime.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md`: passed.

## Details

`Path.touch()` recreates a cache file if eviction occurs after `stat()`. The resulting empty file is returned as a cache hit, so image decoding fails instead of fetching the media again. `os.utime()` updates the timestamp only when the file exists; if eviction wins the race, the existing `OSError` handler returns a cache miss.

This change addresses the read/eviction race. It does not repair already-corrupt cache files or measure production incidence. It is separate from [#56062](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56062), which bounds cache entries and handles failed downloads, and [#55616](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55616), which changes cache lookup identity.

title: [Bugfix] Keep default max_tokens in rendered sampling_params
author: nien-hui
body:
## Overview

In scale-out serving, `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/completions/render` with `max_tokens` 16 return `sampling_params` without `max_tokens`, so `/inference/v1/generate` produces 700 (chat) and 40943 (completions) tokens instead of 16; a `/v1/completions/render` request without `max_tokens` defaults to 16 and takes the same path. `SamplingParams` omits fields equal to their defaults, and generate reads the absent key as not sent. `GenerateRequest` now writes `max_tokens` back into the dumped `sampling_params` when the request set it.

Fixes #65388

## Claims

- Render → generate with `max_tokens` 16 stops at 16 tokens with `length` on chat and completions, instead of 700 and 40943 tokens.
- `/v1/completions/render` with `max_tokens` omitted or `null` returns `max_tokens` 16, and generate stops at 16 tokens as coupled `/v1/completions` does, instead of 40943.
- `/v1/chat/completions/render` with `max_completion_tokens` 16, `/v1/messages/render` with `max_tokens` 16 and `/v1/responses/render` with `max_output_tokens` 16 return `max_tokens` 16 instead of leaving it out.

Not tested: the Rust frontend's `/inference/v1/generate` (the local `vllm-rs` binary predates main's launcher and exits with `unexpected argument '--input-listener-fd'`), gRPC render, `/cohere/v2/chat/render` with `max_tokens` 16 (404 on the test render server), the `RequestLogger` body log of a `GenerateRequest` (no test logs one), and streaming generate and `n` > 1 with a rendered 16 on this base (run only on the earlier base `e8570ef757`).
No model eval: the change adds the `max_tokens` key to the serialized request body; sampling under a given limit is unchanged.
The new tests run in the `Entrypoints Integration (API Server)` CI step.

## Details

**Root cause.** `SamplingParams` is a `msgspec.Struct` with `omit_defaults=True` and `max_tokens` default 16, so `GenerateRequest.model_dump()`, which render returns, leaves out `max_tokens` when it is 16. Generate's `is_sampling_param_provided("max_tokens")` checks the keys of the raw `sampling_params` dict, so `serve_tokens` treats the absent key as not sent and replaces it with the `get_max_tokens` server default. `CompletionRequest.max_tokens` defaults to 16 and `normalize_null_max_tokens` maps `null` to it, so completions requests without `max_tokens` take the same path.

**Fix.** A wrap `model_serializer` on `GenerateRequest` writes `sampling_params.max_tokens` back after the normal dump when `is_sampling_param_provided("max_tokens")` is True and the key is missing. In-process requests (render) count every field as provided; a body parsed without `max_tokens` dumps unchanged.

**Related PRs.**
- #42329 — added `is_sampling_param_provided` and the server-side `max_tokens` default in `serve_tokens`. It introduced the fallback that the absent key triggers.
- #35684 — added `_serialize_msgspec`, which dumps `SamplingParams` with `msgspec.to_builtins`. It introduced the dump that leaves out default fields.


Only `max_tokens` is written back: `serve_tokens` is the only caller of `is_sampling_param_provided`, and other omitted defaults (`top_k` 0, `min_tokens` 0) parse back to the same value.
Generate cannot fix this on its side: once the key is absent, a resolved 16 and an unsent limit look the same.
The fix is on the serializing side, so a render server on main talking to a generate server with this PR still drops 16.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, write the fix and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and reran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Respect disabled chunked prefill for multimodal requests
author: jzakrzew
body:
## Overview
Fix partial prefill of multimodal pooling requests when chunked prefill is disabled. Bidirectional MEAN-pooling models can crash under async encoder-cache pressure or an explicit long-prefill threshold.


## Claims
- Defer the whole request when encoder limits would force partial prefill, releasing acquired cache references and restoring the compute budget.
- Ignore `long_prefill_token_threshold` when chunked prefill is disabled.
- Add scheduler and real-model regression coverage for both triggers.


## Validation
Reproduced with real weights for `nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2`, using Model Runner V2. Both cases queue two distinct images with chunked prefill disabled:

- **Encoder-cache pressure:** async scheduling, a 384-token budget/cache, and 256 tokens per image. The second request fits the next step's token budget while the first image still occupies the encoder cache.
- **Prefill threshold:** synchronous scheduling with `long_prefill_token_threshold=128`, which incorrectly splits the queued prompts.

With the unchanged upstream scheduler (`c7a7607519`), both cases raise `RuntimeError: partial prefill is not supported with MEAN pooling`. With this fix, both complete and every batched embedding matches its individually processed reference with cosine similarity ≥0.999.

Focused regressions, **2 passed each**:
```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k encoder_cache_pressure_respects_disabled_chunked_prefill -v

python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_llama_nemotron_vl.py \
  -k test_image_embeddings_without_chunked_prefill -v
```

## Details
The scheduler checks the token budget before scheduling encoder inputs. Encoder-cache exhaustion can subsequently shorten the request to the text before an image, violating disabled chunked prefill. Async scheduling exposes this when an earlier batch still holds encoder-cache references. An explicit long-prefill threshold provides a separate path to partial prefill under synchronous scheduling.

The encoder check lives in `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs`. The threshold is applied only when chunked prefill is enabled.

Open-PR searches found no equivalent fix. Related work: [#63033](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63033) adds a PaliGemma-specific whole-prompt guard; [#61733](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61733) rejects permanently oversized prompts at admission. Neither covers these two triggers.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Count the expert down-projection bias once under TP
author: yannicks1
body:
## Overview `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` copied the full `w2_bias` to every TP rank, so the row-parallel down projection added it `tp_size` times before the all-reduce. Only TP rank 0 now keeps it, as gpt-oss's own loader already does. Fixes #65405. ## Claims - Biased experts loaded through the generic loader are correct at TP>1. TP=1, EP (where `tp_rank` is 0 on every rank) and gpt-oss's native loader are unchanged. ## Validation New test `test_moe_layer_tp_expert_bias` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py`: a TP=1/2 forward of a biased `FusedMoEFactory` loaded through `weight_loader`, compared against the unsharded `torch_moe` reference with both biases. ```bash pytest -v "tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py::test_moe_layer_tp_expert_bias" ``` | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | TP=1 | passed | passed | | TP=2 | failed: 1882/2048 outputs out of tolerance, max abs error 1.85 | passed | End to end, the reproducer below builds a tiny synthetic Mixtral-style checkpoint with biased `ModuleList` experts and serves it with `LLM(model_impl="transformers")`. The correct next token is 3; if the down bias is counted per rank, token 4 wins. ```bash VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python repro_moe_w2_bias_tp.py --tp 2 ``` | | TP=1 | TP=2 | TP=4 | |---|---|---|---| | main | token 3 | token 4 (fails) | token 4 (fails) | | this PR | token 3 | token 3 | token 3 |
repro_moe_w2_bias_tp.py ```python """CPU reproducer: expert down bias is counted once per TP rank. python repro_moe_w2_bias_tp.py --tp 1 # passes python repro_moe_w2_bias_tp.py --tp 2 # fails without the fix The synthetic checkpoint has residual [1, 0, ...] and expert bias [0, 1, ...]. After the final norm, logits 3 and 4 are proportional to 1.5 and 1. With the bug, logit 4 is proportional to tp_size instead, so the wrong token wins. """ import argparse import tempfile from pathlib import Path import torch from torch import nn from transformers import MixtralConfig, MixtralForCausalLM, MixtralModel from transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama import LlamaMLP class TinyMoEModel(MixtralModel): def __init__(self, config): super().__init__(config) # vLLM replaces this container with its generic RoutedExperts layer. self.layers[0].mlp.experts = nn.ModuleList( LlamaMLP(config) for _ in range(config.num_local_experts) ) def main(): from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) parser.add_argument("--tp", type=int, default=2) tp = parser.parse_args().tp with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp: path = Path(tmp) (path / "modeling_repro.py").write_text(Path(__file__).read_text()) config = MixtralConfig( hidden_size=64, intermediate_size=128, num_hidden_layers=1, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=4, head_dim=32, vocab_size=8, max_position_embeddings=32, mlp_bias=True, num_local_experts=2, num_experts_per_tok=2, tie_word_embeddings=False, ) config.auto_map = {"AutoModel": "modeling_repro.TinyMoEModel"} model = MixtralForCausalLM(config) model.model = TinyMoEModel(config) with torch.no_grad(): for name, param in model.named_parameters(): param.fill_(1 if "norm" in name else 0) model.model.embed_tokens.weight[:, 0] = 1 for expert in model.model.layers[0].mlp.experts: expert.down_proj.bias[1] = 1 model.lm_head.weight[3, 0] = 1.5 model.lm_head.weight[4, 1] = 1 model.save_pretrained(path, save_original_format=False) llm = LLM( model=str(path), model_impl="transformers", trust_remote_code=True, skip_tokenizer_init=True, dtype="float32", tensor_parallel_size=tp, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=32, kv_cache_memory_bytes=16 << 20, ) output = llm.generate( [{"prompt_token_ids": [1]}], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1, detokenize=False), use_tqdm=False, )[0].outputs[0] print(f"tp={tp}: expected=[3], actual={output.token_ids}") assert output.token_ids == [3], "Expert down bias was counted more than once" if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
Both were run on CPU (fp32, vLLM 0.32.0 CPU wheel). The new test has not run on GPU yet; the 2-GPU FusedMoE Layer Kernels CI step selects it. I found no public pretrained checkpoint that loads a nonzero expert down bias through this path, so there is no pretrained-model accuracy eval. ## Details The check reads `moe_config.tp_rank`, the rank inside the group the down-projection all-reduce spans. With DP/PCP folded into TP that is the flattened rank. With EP, and with sequence-parallel MoE (which requires EP), `tp_rank` is 0 on every rank, so each rank keeps the bias of the experts it owns. No open PR covers this branch (searched `w2_bias` and `moe bias tp_rank`). The open reload PRs #61287, #50523 and #65353 don't touch `routed_experts.py`. ---
