title: [Bugfix] Granite4Vision: strip padding tiles for list pixel_values
author: artem-spector
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix a `split_with_sizes` crash in Granite 4.1 Vision (`Granite4VisionForConditionalGeneration`) when one encoder batch contains images with different anyres tile counts from more than one request. Padding tiles were stripped only when `pixel_values` arrived as a 5-D tensor, not when it arrived as a list of per-image tensors. Also removes a GPU<->CPU sync in `embed_input_ids` that CI's sync check rejects for every Granite 4.1 Vision image request.

## Claims

- Fixes `RuntimeError: split_with_sizes expects split_sizes to sum exactly to N ... but got split_sizes=[...]`, which kills EngineCore and fails every in-flight request (`EngineDeadError`).
- Per-image embeddings on the fixed list path are bit-identical to encoding each image alone.
- Removes the GPU<->CPU sync from zeroing image positions in `embed_input_ids` (`text_embeds[is_multimodal] = 0.0` with a CPU mask), which fails under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Output is unchanged.
- Adds a regression test that fails on `main` and passes with the fix, checking batched outputs against running each request alone.

## Validation

New test `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_granite4_vision.py`, run on an H100:

```bash
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_granite4_vision.py -v
```

| Code | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `test_mixed_tile_counts_across_requests[5-16] FAILED` — `RuntimeError: split_with_sizes expects split_sizes to sum exactly to 27 (input tensor's size at dimension 0), but got split_sizes=[5, 10, 7]` (`granite4_vision.py:706`, `_get_all_layer_features`) |
| padding fix only | `FAILED` — `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()` (`granite4_vision.py:824`, `embed_input_ids`); the same failure as the first CI run of this PR |
| this PR | `test_mixed_tile_counts_across_requests[5-16] PASSED` |

On a standalone check with `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")` and the same shapes and devices (pinned CPU bool mask, GPU embeddings), `emb[cpu_mask] = 0.0` synchronizes and `emb.masked_fill(mask_on_gpu.unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)` does not; the two results are `torch.equal`.

Embedding equivalence: in the same two-request scenario, I wrapped `embed_multimodal` to also encode each image alone (a one-item 5-D batch, the path `main` already handles) and compared the outputs. Max abs diff for all three images: **0**, with shapes `(594, 20480)`, `(1032, 20480)`, `(936, 20480)`.

Also passing with this PR: `tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Granite4Vision`, `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k granite-vision-4.1` (3 cases), `tests/models/test_registry.py -k Granite4Vision`, and pre-commit.

## Details

**Root cause.** The HF processor pads every image in one call to that call's largest tile count. A request with images of 5 and 10 tiles therefore produces two 10-tile tensors, the first with 5 trailing zero tiles. `MultiModalFieldConfig.batched` stacks the items of an encoder batch only when their shapes match. Add a second request with a 7-tile image to the same batch, and `embed_multimodal` receives a list of tensors with 10, 10 and 7 tiles.

`_get_all_layer_features` removed padding with `pv[:num_patches]` only for 5-D input. `embed_multimodal` concatenated the list as-is (27 tiles), while the per-image split used the real counts from `image_size_to_num_patches` (5 + 10 + 7 = 22):

```
EMBED call: list tiles/item=[(10,), (10,), (7,)] image_sizes=[[480, 640], [876, 1300], [768, 1024]]
RuntimeError: split_with_sizes expects split_sizes to sum exactly to 27 ... but got split_sizes=[5, 10, 7]
```

**Fix.** Apply the same per-image slice for list input, and move the concatenation into `_get_all_layer_features` so both layouts go through one path. The change is model-local: no core or runner changes. Both model runners call `embed_multimodal` with the same batched kwargs.

**GPU<->CPU sync.** `embed_input_ids` zeroed image-token positions with `text_embeds[is_multimodal] = 0.0`. The model runner passes `is_multimodal` as a pinned CPU tensor, so boolean indexing a GPU tensor with it synchronizes on every request with images. It wasn't visible before because the only existing Granite 4.1 Vision generation test (`test_common.py`) is skipped; once the padding fix lets the new test reach this line, CI's `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` rejects it. Replaced with `masked_fill_` using the mask copied to the device non-blocking (a no-op when it is already there). The deepstack buffer fill a few lines below (`target[is_multimodal] = ...`) does not sync and is unchanged.

**When it triggers.** It needs images with different tile counts, from more than one request, none served from the encoder cache, in the same encoder batch. That depends on load, so in production it is intermittent: we first hit it after 17 hours of GRPO rollouts.

**Test design.** The test runs the engine in-process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) so both requests are queued before the first engine step and their images are encoded together. With a separate engine process, the same test passes on `main`: the two requests can reach the scheduler in different steps. I checked that the processor cache isn't the reason: with a separate engine process, `main` doesn't crash with the cache on, off, or set to `shm`. The two requests are first run in one call (one encoder batch, list `pixel_values`), then each alone on a fresh engine (5-D `pixel_values`, no cache reuse), and the outputs are compared with `check_logprobs_close`, since batching can flip greedy tokens. Images are synthetic solid colors, so the test needs no assets.

**Not in this PR.** The existing `granite4_vision` entry in `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py` is always skipped, because the registry marks the model `is_available_online=False`. This PR leaves that entry as it is.

title: [Bugfix] Size the extensible KV cache from UMA-corrected free memory
author: aijanai
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65378. On integrated (UMA) GPUs the extensible KV cache (#56492) sized itself from raw `cudaMemGetInfo`, which does not count reclaimable page cache as free, so it undersized the KV cache by up to 84% on a DGX Spark (GB10) and to zero blocks in disaggregated serving. This reads free memory through one helper with the same `psutil` correction the classic sizing path already applies (#35920).

## Claims

- On GB10 the extensible KV cache now gets the KV cache the classic path finds: 1302 blocks / 67.6 GiB instead of 216 blocks / 11.2 GiB for Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.8`, and no longer fails with "No available memory for the cache blocks" in P/D.
- Discrete GPUs are unchanged: the helper returns `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info` as is when `is_integrated_gpu()` is false.
- No new configuration; `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` is no longer needed as a workaround on UMA parts.

## Validation

All runs on one GB10 (DGX Spark, 119.7 GiB unified memory, CC 12.1) or one RTX PRO 6000 (discrete, 96 GB), image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` at 40941f2c4b (the extensible code it ships is identical to this branch's base), with this PR's `mem_utils.py` and `extensible_kv_cache.py` copied over the installed package for the "with fix" rows.

**End to end**, `vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --max-num-seqs 32 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, V2 model runner, extensible KV cache at its default:

| Device | Load strategy | Fix | Extensible KV cache after warmup | Classic path (`Available KV cache memory`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX PRO 6000 (discrete) | prefetch | no | 560 blocks, 29.1 GiB, starts | 52.95 GiB |
| GB10 | prefetch | no | 216 blocks, 11.2 GiB (42,130 tokens) | 71.04 GiB |
| GB10 | default | no | 302 blocks, 15.7 GiB | 71.55 GiB |
| GB10 | prefetch | **yes** | **1302 blocks, 67.6 GiB (253,952 tokens)** | 70.80 GiB |

Before the server started on GB10, `cudaMemGetInfo` reported 59-81 GiB free while `psutil.virtual_memory().available` reported 114-116 GiB: the difference is page cache, from this load and earlier runs on the node. In disaggregated P/D (NIXL, same model, MTP k=3) the larger transient peak (7.28 GiB vs 1.71 GiB) took the same deficit below zero: both workers failed with `0 KV cache blocks (0.0 GiB) fit within the requested 95.71 GiB` / `ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks`.

**Device allocations reclaim the page cache.** After filling the page cache by reading the checkpoint, committing through the extensible cache's own `_VirtualBuffer` (`cuMemCreate` + `cuMemMap`) in 1 GiB steps reached 106 GiB, 1.8x the 59.2 GiB `cudaMemGetInfo` reported free, with no error; `psutil` "cached" fell from 56.4 to 4.1 GiB in step with the commits. So the `psutil` figure is the one an allocation can actually obtain.

**New test fails before the fix, passes after** (GB10):

```text
$ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_measured_sizing_counts_reclaimable_memory_on_integrated_gpu
# nightly 40941f2c4b as shipped
>       assert num_blocks == 80
E       assert 0 == 80
tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py:285: AssertionError
1 failed in 3.87s
# with this PR
1 passed in 3.89s
```

`tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py` and `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py` with the fix on GB10: 26 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `test_memory_profiling` (asserts 256 MiB of non-torch memory, measures ~269-273 MB), also fails on the unmodified nightly with the upstream test file, 2 out of 2 runs, so it is a pre-existing UMA flake unrelated to this change. Both files are already run by CI (`pytest -v -s v1/worker`, `pytest -v -s utils_` in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`).

## Details

**Root cause.** `MemorySnapshot.measure()` (`vllm/utils/mem_utils.py`) replaces `cudaMemGetInfo`'s free memory with `psutil.virtual_memory().available` on integrated GPUs, and the extensible cache receives that as `init_free_memory`. But `committable_blocks()` and `measure_kv_cache_blocks()` in `vllm/v1/worker/extensible_kv_cache.py` re-read raw `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info`. The sizing in `measure_kv_cache_bytes()` is `min(requested - non_kv_used, free + committed - margin) - transient_peak` with `non_kv_used = init_free - free - committed`: with the raw figure, page cache counts as engine memory in the first term and is missing from the headroom in the second. In the P/D failure the headroom term alone was already negative: 10.46 + 0.73 - 5.46 - 7.28 = -1.55 GiB. Warmup was capped by the same raw read (only 0.73 GiB committed).

**Fix.** Move the existing correction into `device_memory_info(device)` in `mem_utils` and use it from `MemorySnapshot.measure()` and the three extensible call sites (`committable_blocks`, `measure_kv_cache_blocks`, and the free-memory read when releasing for a weight update). The one remaining `get_memory_info` call in the extensible cache reads only the total. Main-code change is ~30 lines; the rest is tests.

**Alternative considered.** Turning the extensible cache off on integrated GPUs in `_resolve_extensible_kv_cache` would also avoid the failure, but would hide the inconsistency and drop the feature on UMA parts. The reclaim measurement above shows the corrected figure is safe to size from, so this PR fixes the measurement instead.

**Tests.** The new tests patch `current_platform.is_integrated_gpu`, `psutil` and `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info`: CI has no integrated GPU, and these stand in for the hardware/OS readings rather than for vLLM objects. One covers the helper (integrated vs discrete), one covers the extensible sizing end to end through `measure_kv_cache_blocks` with the readings from this report.

**Related.** #55828 (open) sizes the KV cache from the process's own memory via NVML with a fallback to the device-wide delta; on GB10 that fallback would hit the same raw reading, so the two changes should agree on `device_memory_info`. #65204 / #65225 (granule rounding with offload connectors) is a different cause with the same error message.

title: [XPU] fix case test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py and test_mm_prefix_lm.py
author: yma11
body:
## Overview
Fix two independent root causes behind three failed jobs in [Intel CI build 16461](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/16461):

Align the producer and consumer block sizes in the P2P lifecycle regression test.
Pad Triton prefill attention’s head-dimension tile to at least 16.

## Root Cause
P2P lifecycle test: incompatible default block sizes
The producer uses native LLM, while the consumer uses VllmRunner. With batch invariance enabled, both select Triton Attention, but their effective defaults differ on XPU:

`test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py` :
Producer: 16 tokens per block.
Consumer: 64 tokens per block.
Consequently, their offloaded blocks have different byte sizes (368640 versus 1474560). The P2P handshake correctly rejects this incompatible layout. The test then fails at assert buffered.is_set() because no transfer completion arrives—not because buffered completion handling is broken.

Set block_size=16 in the shared engine parameters so both peers use the same layout. Also assert that the disconnect was injected, ensuring the test exercises its intended failure ordering rather than passing without reaching it.

`test_mm_prefix_lm.py` :
Multimodal tests: insufficient Triton dot tile width
Both multimodal jobs fail in test_mm_prefix_lm_cache_hit_inside_image. Its tiny Gemma3 model has a vision attention head dimension of 8.

The prefill kernel previously used next_power_of_2(head_dim), producing a tile width of 8. For tl.dot(p, v, acc), this is the output dimension, but the XPU Triton compiler requires it to be at least 16:


Use max(16, next_power_of_2(head_dim)). Existing masks zero-fill padded loads and restrict output stores to the actual head dimension. Tile widths for head dimensions of 16 or greater remain unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Raise the extensible KV cache margin floor to 3 GiB
author: djramic
body:
## Overview

Raises the ROCm margin floor of the extensible KV cache (#56492) from 2 GiB to 3 GiB, so torch has enough room for memory fragmentation on MI355.

## Claims
 Fixes the OOMs in `(MI355) Spec Decode Eagle Nightly` ([ci#99485](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99485#01a1a039-403f-474a-9c3c-6c1ae7bc7fe5)) and `(MI355 DPX) Spec Decode Speculators + MTP` ([amd-ci#15764](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15764#01a1a0db-a987-452c-8c10-7a097faded05)).


## Validation

Tested on MI355X with the CI images. Without this PR, the Eagle and MiMo tests run out of memory when less memory is left for torch. With it, they pass, and the smallest headroom under the cap goes from 0.10 GiB to 0.67 GiB. The Eagle spec decode tests and the extensible KV cache unit tests give the same results with and without this PR.

To reproduce, run `test_eagle_correctness_medium[ROCM_AITER_FA-llama3_eagle3]` in the ci image with 100-200 MiB added to `KV_CACHE_NON_TORCH_RESERVE_BYTES`.

## Details

After warmup, vLLM limits how much memory torch can reserve. On ROCm, only about 1 GiB of that limit is left for fragmentation. The first large prefill of a 7-8B model leaves 1.3-1.7 GiB reserved but unused, so the next large allocation goes over the limit, even though the tensors in use would fit:

| Build | Limit | In use | Reserved, unused | Request |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ci#99485](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99485#01a1a039-403f-474a-9c3c-6c1ae7bc7fe5) | 18.84 GiB | 16.73 GiB | 1.27 GiB | 896 MiB |
| [amd-ci#15764](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15764#01a1a0db-a987-452c-8c10-7a097faded05) (DPX) | 18.93 GiB | 16.81 GiB | 1.70 GiB | 688 MiB |

The limit was added in #56492, and the spare room was small from the start: about 0.05-0.08 GiB, while fragmentation changes by 0.2-0.3 GiB from run to run.

title: [Bugfix][CI] Keep the chat template on NixlConnector PD + SD acceptance prompts
author: mirza-halilcevic
body:
## Overview

Fixes `(MI355) NixlConnector PD + Spec Decode acceptance`, which has failed since [#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245) landed ([amd-ci #15764](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15764#01a1a0db-a963-418a-a1cd-a003f97c4f00)). The test's MT-Bench prompts lost their chat template; dropping `backend="openai-chat"` from the `get_samples()` args restores it.

## Claims

- Test-only, one-line fix. The prompts are byte-identical to those before [#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245).
- EAGLE3 acceptance length: 1.928 (FAIL, expected 2.600 ± 5%) → 2.583 (pass).
- No open PR addresses this failure: none touches this test or references [#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245).

## Validation

CI job command, run on 2x MI355 in the failing build's image (`rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1a0d9-f1de-4511-92ce-35681c627064`), before and after the change:

```bash
cd /vllm-workspace/tests
KV_CACHE_MEMORY_BYTES=8G ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN \
  bash v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/config_sweep_spec_decode_test.sh
```

| Config | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EAGLE3 Llama-3.1-8B, `kv_buffer_device=cuda` | 1.928 (FAIL) | 2.583 |
| EAGLE3 Llama-3.1-8B, `kv_buffer_device=cpu` | not reached | 2.583 |
| MTP Qwen3.5-0.8B, `kv_buffer_device=cuda` | not reached | 1.785 (expected 1.798) |

<details>
<summary>Output</summary>

Before:
```
llama3-8b-eagle3: acceptance_length=1.928 (expected=2.600)
  Drafts: 10651, Accepted: 9884
E       AssertionError: Acceptance length regression for llama3-8b-eagle3! Expected: 2.600, Got: 1.928, Relative error: 25.85% (tolerance: 5%)
```

After:
```
llama3-8b-eagle3: acceptance_length=2.583 (expected=2.600)
  Drafts: 6663, Accepted: 10548
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 83.60s (0:01:23) ===================
llama3-8b-eagle3: acceptance_length=2.583 (expected=2.600)
  Drafts: 6663, Accepted: 10548
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 85.64s (0:01:25) ===================
qwen35-0.8b-mtp: acceptance_length=1.785 (expected=1.798)
  Drafts: 9428, Accepted: 7399
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 155.43s (0:02:35) ==================
✅ All spec decode acceptance tests passed!
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** [#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245) made `get_samples()` skip the client-side chat template for chat backends, since those endpoints apply it server-side. This test declares `backend="openai-chat"` but sends the prompts to `/v1/completions` with `add_special_tokens=False`. The prompts therefore reached the server with no chat template and no BOS, and acceptance dropped at every draft position. Without `backend`, the test builds its prompts the same way the standalone baseline in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_length.py` does.

**Bisect.** Earlier nightlies consistently scored 2.603. The ROCm, PyTorch and Triton versions are identical between the passing and failing images. Overlaying each candidate commit's Python sources onto the last passing image (`5cdeea9`) gave `8b30f56` ([#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245)) as the first bad commit.

**Limitation.** With identical prompts, EAGLE3 scores 2.583 rather than 2.603. That shift is deterministic and comes from other engine changes that landed the same day. It is within tolerance, so the baseline is left unchanged.

AI assistance was used for the bisect, root-cause analysis, and this description. The submitter reviewed the change and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Initialize Mistral EAGLE weight-loader state
author: sragrawal
body:
## Overview

Fix draft weight loading for Mistral EAGLE models, including [Mistral Small 4 EAGLE](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-eagle).

## Claims

- Initialize the shared-expert state used by the inherited weight loader.
- Initialize `hidden_size`, which the inherited forward path reads during sequence-parallel gathering.

## Validation

CPU: five tests passed on `b14e2f279` plus this patch. Pre-commit passed, including mypy. The new regression constructs a real draft model and checks the loaded weight tensor.

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft weight loading | `AttributeError: 'EagleMistralLarge3Model' object has no attribute 'fused_shared_expert_layers'` | Loads the norm weight with exact tensor equality |

GPU: B200 x1 / TP1, Mistral Small 4 NVFP4 with its public EAGLE draft, vLLM `b14e2f279` plus this patch, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130. Context 8192, GMU 0.85, max sequences 8, prefix caching off. Both patched runs used Model Runner V2.

| Configuration | Startup and generation | GSM8K smoke | Mean acceptance length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unpatched EAGLE, k=3 | Startup fails with the missing attribute above | — | — |
| Target only | Generates | 28/32 | — |
| Patched EAGLE, k=3, eager | Generates; nonzero draft acceptance | 28/32 | 3.25 |
| Patched EAGLE, k=3, non-eager | Generates; nonzero draft acceptance | 30/32 | 3.18 |

Acceptance length includes one target-generated token; its maximum is `k + 1`. The corresponding draft acceptance rates were 75.0% and 72.8%.

The smoke uses the first 32 GSM8K test questions, five-shot prompts, greedy decoding and a 512-token cap. No GSM8K response reached the cap. Generation was also checked on eight math/coding prompts at batches 1 and 8 with a 128-token cap. Greedy outputs differ between target-only and speculative decoding.

Public checkpoints: [NVFP4 target](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4/tree/45331841b631f4e281df8e959ea3cc9beb84298a), [EAGLE draft](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-eagle/tree/9a8ea22dca0161ff7af7879f4a0000f65314797d).

<details>

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/test_mistral_large_3_eagle.py -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_mistral_large_3_eagle.py
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>GPU reproducer</summary>

From a vLLM checkout with GPU dependencies installed:

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import evaluate_gsm8k_offline

llm = LLM(
    model="mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4",
    revision="45331841b631f4e281df8e959ea3cc9beb84298a",
    config_format="mistral", load_format="mistral", tokenizer_mode="mistral",
    tensor_parallel_size=1, max_model_len=8192,
    max_num_seqs=8, max_num_batched_tokens=8192,

    enforce_eager=True,
    attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_MLA"},
    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0},
    speculative_config={
        "model": "mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-eagle",
        "revision": "9a8ea22dca0161ff7af7879f4a0000f65314797d",
        "method": "eagle", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
        "max_model_len": 8192,
    },
)
print(llm.chat(
    [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 multiplied by 23? Show the calculation."}],
    SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128, seed=42),
))
print(evaluate_gsm8k_offline(llm, num_questions=32, num_shots=5, max_tokens=512))
print([metric for metric in llm.get_metrics() if "spec_decode" in metric.name])
```

Repeat with `enforce_eager=False` for non-eager execution. Omit `speculative_config` for the target-only reference. The checked-in loader regression runs in Model Executor CI; the real-weight 119B checks were run separately on B200.

</details>

## Details

`EagleMistralLarge3Model` inherits `load_weights` and `forward` from `DeepseekV2Model` but skips its constructor. The draft constructor does not initialize the shared-expert state that the weight loader reads, so loading fails even for a dense draft.

Use the same helper as the parent to derive fused shared-expert layers from the constructed model. This also preserves the parent's policy checks if a draft contains MoE layers.

Based on Ruben Debien's open [#61369](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61369), adapted to the per-layer shared-expert API introduced by [#61457](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61457). The earlier patch initializes the old boolean flag using a helper that no longer exists on main.

AI-assisted implementation and testing using Codex.

title: [Bugfix] Keep the extensible tensor's PyCapsule_New prototype private
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

The extensible tensor's DLPack helper configures the process-wide `ctypes.pythonapi.PyCapsule_New`. FlashInfer's MNNVL helpers (`flashinfer.comm.dlpack_utils`) reset that same object's `restype` to `c_void_p`. This PR binds a private `PYFUNCTYPE` prototype instead, so other libraries can't change it. Follow-up to #56492.

## Claims

- Fixes `RuntimeError: from_dlpack received an invalid capsule` in `ExtensibleTensor` views (e.g. `allocate_kv_cache` → `full_view`) when a FlashInfer MNNVL / symmetric-memory buffer was created earlier in the process.
- No behavior change otherwise: the same C function is called with the same signature.

## Validation

- New test `test_views_survive_shared_pycapsule_new_restype_change` in `tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py` sets `ctypes.pythonapi.PyCapsule_New.restype = c_void_p` (what FlashInfer does), then takes a view. It runs in its own spawned process like the rest of the file, so the global change doesn't leak into other tests.
  - Without the fix: fails with `RuntimeError: from_dlpack received an invalid capsule ...`.
  - With the fix: passes.
- `pytest tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py` on GB200: 11 passed.
- End to end: a TP4 model that allocates a FlashInfer MNNVL buffer during weight loading failed in `initialize_kv_cache` on all ranks with the error above. With this change it loads and runs.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass.

## Details

Root cause: `ctypes.pythonapi.PyCapsule_New` is one shared `_FuncPtr`, so its `restype` / `argtypes` are global mutable state and the last writer wins. FlashInfer's `create_dlpack_capsule` sets `restype = c_void_p`, after which our call returns an int address instead of a capsule and `torch.from_dlpack` rejects it. `ctypes.PYFUNCTYPE(...)(("PyCapsule_New", ctypes.pythonapi))` creates a separate function object bound to the same symbol, so it is unaffected.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `extensible_tensor.py` or this error.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Support min_tokens in the Anthropic Messages API
author: nliu365
body:
## Overview

The Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) silently ignores `min_tokens`, while Chat Completions supports it. This adds `min_tokens` as a vLLM extra parameter on `AnthropicMessagesRequest` and forwards it to the engine.

Fixes #65095. The Responses API counterpart is #64009 / #64015; this PR does not touch that path.

## Claims

- `/v1/messages` accepts `min_tokens` (default `0`), and it now reaches `SamplingParams`, so EOS and stop sequences cannot end the response before that many tokens.
- Out-of-range values are rejected by the existing `SamplingParams` checks (`0 <= min_tokens <= max_tokens`), the same as for Chat Completions.
- Documented under "Anthropic APIs" in the online serving docs.

## Validation

New regression test `test_min_tokens_delays_stop_sequence` in `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py` (`RemoteOpenAIServer`, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, greedy). It first checks that a `"\n"` stop sequence ends the response early without `min_tokens`, then sends `min_tokens=16`.

Without the fix (`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/` from `origin/main`, new test kept):

```
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py -k min_tokens
E       AssertionError: assert 2 >= 16
E        +  where 2 = Usage(... input_tokens=15, output_tokens=2, ...).output_tokens
1 failed, 8 deselected
```

With the fix:

```
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py -k min_tokens
1 passed, 8 deselected

$ pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic
163 passed
```

Run on CPU (macOS arm64). `pre-commit` passes on the changed files. The `entrypoints/anthropic` Buildkite step already runs the whole directory, so the new test runs in CI.

## Details

- Root cause: `AnthropicMessagesRequest` had no `min_tokens` field, and `AnthropicServingMessages._build_base_request` did not set it on the `ChatCompletionRequest` it builds, so `to_sampling_params` always used `0`.
- No request-level range check was added. Keeping it in `SamplingParams` matches Chat Completions and avoids a second copy of the rule.
- P/D: the reference proxies (`tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py`, `disagg_proxy_multiturn.py`) already strip `min_tokens` from the prefill leg (`max_tokens=1`) and restore it on the decode leg, so the prefill leg does not trip `min_tokens <= max_tokens`.
- `min_tokens` is not part of Anthropic's spec. It sits with the other vLLM extra fields (`cache_salt`, `watermarking`, `kv_transfer_params`, ...). Anthropic SDK users pass it via `extra_body`.

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Re-fit `--max-model-len auto` after the extensible KV cache shrinks
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview

With the extensible KV cache (default on CUDA/ROCm with model runner V2, #56492), `--max-model-len auto` is fitted at planning time, against a budget that leaves out CUDA graphs and warmup on purpose: the KV cache is committed later, from the memory measured after warmup. When that measurement can no longer hold the fitted length, `finalize_extensible_kv_cache` only checks it and startup fails, even though the user never asked for that length. This PR fits the length again to the measured capacity, for `auto` only.

## Claims

- `--max-model-len auto` no longer fails at startup when CUDA graphs and warmup leave less KV cache than the planning-time fit assumed. It starts at the longest length that fits the measured capacity and logs the reduction.
- No change for any configuration that starts today:
  - An explicit `--max-model-len` that does not fit still fails, as before.
  - For `auto`, the re-fit searches only lengths at or below the current one, so when the measured capacity holds the current length, it is kept and nothing else happens.
- +24 lines: `kv_cache_planning.py` +19, `engine/core.py` +5. Plus one unit test.

## Validation

**Unit test:** `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_finalize_extensible_kv_cache_refits_auto_max_model_len`. It fails without the fix (startup `ValueError`) and passes with it. The whole file passes: 66 passed. Pre-commit passes.

**Reproducer on GB200 (4x GPU, TP4), on main alone.** The model is MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4-DFlash with the command from `docs/features/speculative_decoding/adaptive_verification.md`, adaptive verification off. Both trees are main `254a2a3390`; the PR tree adds this fix. CUDA graphs take 3.93 GiB in every run, and the full 1,048,576-token context needs 15.06 GiB of KV cache.

| `--gpu-memory-utilization` | KV budget at planning (`auto` keeps 1,048,576) | KV measured after warmup | main | this PR: `max_model_len` from `/v1/models` | GSM8K, 1319 questions, C256 (main → this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 (default) | 42.26 GiB | 23.09 GiB | starts at 1,048,576 | 1,048,576, unchanged | 94.77% → 94.62% |
| 0.93 | | 17.76 GiB | starts at 1,048,576 | 1,048,576, unchanged | 94.39% → 94.62% |
| 0.90 | 24.33 GiB | 12.24 GiB | **fails**: `ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (1048576), (15.06 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (12.24 GiB). Based on the available memory, the estimated maximum model length is 812064.` | **starts at 812,064**, the length main's own error suggests | fails → 95.07% |

The same failure happens at the default utilization whenever graphs or warmup take more memory. With the wider CUDA graphs of #63406, about 12.7 GiB of KV cache is left, and main fails the same way. With this fix on top, the server starts at 846,480 tokens and scores 94.24% on GSM8K at C256 and at C1024.

## Details

Root cause: under the extensible KV cache, `profile_cudagraph_memory` returns 0, because the capture footprint is measured after warmup rather than estimated. That is right for sizing the KV cache, but `auto` still picks its length from the pre-capture budget. `finalize_extensible_kv_cache` then commits the measured block count, and `shrink_kv_cache_configs` raises if one request of `max_model_len` no longer fits.

The fix calls the planning-time `_auto_fit_max_model_len` again, with the measured block count and the same bytes-per-block and null-block accounting that `shrink_kv_cache_configs` checks. If the length changes, the engine core syncs it to the workers with the existing `update_max_model_len`, as the planning-time auto-fit already does.

Shrinking after capture is safe: buffers sized from the planning-time length, such as block tables, still cover a shorter one. Moving the whole `auto` decision after warmup is not an option, because block tables, warmup steps and drafters need a length before capture.

The extensible KV cache is only enabled with model runner V2, so model runner V1 is unaffected.

title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Don't emit MXFP8 from the input norm under sequence parallelism
author: xsxszab
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MiniMax-M3 on NVIDIA fails at startup when MegaMoE, TP > 1 and EP are combined and `qkv_proj` takes MXFP8 input (e.g. `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`). With sequence parallelism (SP, #64659), the input norm output is all-gathered before attention; since #64852 that output is a `QuantizedActivation`, which the all-gather cannot take. This PR keeps the norm output in BF16 under SP and lets `qkv_proj` quantize after the gather.

## Claims

- Fixes `AttributeError: 'QuantizedActivation' object has no attribute 'contiguous'` in the profile run for TP > 1 + EP + `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` (SP is enabled automatically in that setup).
- No change when SP is off.
- With the fix, GSM8K is 0.958 (0.964 with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1`), in line with the 95.5–96.1% that #64659 reports for TP4 with and without SP.

## Validation

`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` on 4× B300, main at `39dbf51839`. GSM8K is the full 1319 questions, 5-shot, chat mode with thinking off.

| Setup | Code | Result | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---:|
| TP4 + EP + MegaMoE (SP on) | main | crashes in the profile run | – |
| TP4 + EP + MegaMoE (SP on) | this PR | starts | 0.958 |
| TP4 + EP + MegaMoE (SP on), `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1` | this PR | starts | 0.964 |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

The serve command is the one from #64659's validation, without the NVFP4 KV and indexer caches: their Q8KV4 prefill kernel needs CUDA 13.4+, and this cluster has 13.1. The crash path does not depend on the KV cache dtype.

```bash
VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high \
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
  -tp 4 -ep --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER_TS","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port <port> --max-concurrency 64 \
  --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 1024 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

</details>

No unit test is added: the failure needs SP end to end (4 SM100 GPUs in one NVLink domain and the M3.1 checkpoint), which CI does not have, as noted in #64659. `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual` passes on the changed file.

## Details

**Root cause.** `forward_input_norm` asks the norm for MXFP8 output whenever `qkv_proj` can consume it, assuming the activation goes straight from the norm to `qkv_proj`. Under SP, `forward_after_input_norm` all-gathers it first, and `sp_all_gather` only handles tensors. `QuantizedActivation` is a dataclass holding the E4M3 data and UE8M0 scales, so the custom all-gather fails on `.contiguous()`.

**Scope.** Only the plain norm branch is reachable under SP: MegaMoE never defers its finalize (no `MoEOutput` input), and SP layers never defer the FFN all-reduce, so `fuse_input_allreduce` stays off. With SP off, the condition evaluates exactly as before. The dense MLP already handles SP this way: it all-gathers BF16 and quantizes after the gather.

**Tradeoff.** Under SP the fused norm+quant is not used. The data flow is the same as when #64659 measured SP (before #64852), with the BF16 norm now on #64852's Triton kernel. Gathering the MXFP8 data and scales instead would halve the all-gather bytes, but the 128x4 swizzled scales cannot be concatenated by rows: it needs unswizzled scales from the norm kernel and a swizzle after the gather. That is left as a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** Searched open and closed PRs and issues for the error message, `QuantizedActivation` + all-gather, and MiniMax SP + MXFP8; no existing fix.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find the root cause, write the change and run the validation; I reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoE] Fix tkw1 rejecting count-free expert metadata, rename AITER QuantMethod
author: divakar-amd
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #63204 (part of #54966 item 5), addressing its post-merge review comments.

## Claims

- **Fix:** `AiterFp8ChannelExperts` again accepts expert-token metadata without token counts on the tkw1 route (e.g. DeepEP v2 under CUDA graphs). #63204 made the check reject *any* metadata; it now rejects only metadata that carries counts, as before. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447566182))
- **Rename:** `QuantMethod` → `AiterQuantType` (plus `_AITER_QUANT_TYPE`, `quant_type=`, `derive_aiter_quant_type()`), since "quant method" means the weight-loading quantization classes in vLLM. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447852851))
- **Removal:** `ActivationMethod`. It only named SILU/GELU; every activation now resolves via `rocm_aiter_ops.get_aiter_activation_type()`, as SWIGLU/SITU already did. ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63204#discussion_r4447841385))
- **Guard:** assert `a1q_scale is None` on the tkw1 branch. tkw1 quantizes the activation itself, so a dispatch-side scale would be silently dropped where the generic route forwards it.
- No numerical change intended.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` | 88 passed |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k aiter` | 67 passed, 14 skipped |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py` | 53 passed |

The new regression test was mutation-checked against both ways the fix can regress:

| Mutation | Failure |
|---|---|
| revert the fix (reject any metadata) | `AssertionError: AITER tkw1 kernel does not support num_local_tokens` |
| let count-free metadata fall through to the generic route | `count-free metadata did not reach the tkw1 kernel` |

The second is why the test spies on `rocm_aiter_ops.asm_moe_tkw1` rather than only comparing outputs: `asm_moe_tkw1` is `fused_moe(quant_type=per_Token, doweight_stage1=True)`, so the generic route is numerically equivalent and an output-only check passes through a fall-through.

## Details

- Output comparison uses `rtol=atol=1e-2`: tkw1 differs by ~1 bf16 ulp run to run. The test is gated on gfx942/gfx950, like the other asm/FP8 tests in the file.
- The enum-value test now checks `AiterQuantType` against `aiter.QuantType` rather than literals, so drift from AITER is caught.
- The mirror enum is kept because subclasses declare `_AITER_QUANT_TYPE` at class definition, in a module imported where AITER isn't installed.
- Raw custom-op tests now pass AITER's own `ActivationType`/`QuantType`.
- `rocm_aiter_ops` custom-op argument names (`quant_method: int`, `activation_method: int`) are unchanged: they are `torch.ops.vllm.*` schema names, so renaming them is a schema change rather than a Python rename. Out-of-tree callers of `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` must rename `quant_method=` to `quant_type=`.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these names or the tkw1 check.

title: [Bugfix] Keep the HiSparse FlashInfer all-reduce backend on lazy workspace creation

## Overview

#65201 forces the `trtllm` FlashInfer all-reduce backend under HiSparse to avoid the MNNVL fused AR+RMSNorm race (#64327). The override was skipped when the shared workspace was created lazily outside the vLLM config context. HiSparse servers then still came up on `mnnvl` and crashed with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`. Related: #56699.

## Claims

- HiSparse servers on main now get the `trtllm` all-reduce workspace without needing `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND`.

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Fix PP rank derivation when prefill context parallelism is enabled
author: xsxszab
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix PP rank calculation when pipeline parallelism (PP) and prefill context parallelism (PCP) are enabled together. The current calculation ignores the PCP dimension, causing incorrect MooncakeStoreConnector keys, model layer metadata, and Ray actor names.

Workers follow a PP × PCP × TP layout, so each PP stage contains `tp_size * pcp_size` workers. This PR replaces `rank // tp_size % pp_size` with `rank // (tp_size * pcp_size) % pp_size` in all three affected locations.

This PR also includes a small PP fix that I don't think warrants a separate PR: rejecting negative layer counts in VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION, such as "-1,5", instead of allowing invalid layer ranges.

## Claims

- MooncakeStoreConnector uses the correct PP stage in store keys, restoring external prefix cache hits in the tested PP2 × PCP2 configuration.
- `ModelConfig.get_layers_start_end_indices` returns the correct stage's layer range, including the layer count used by KV connectors and EAGLE drafters for uneven partitions.
- Ray actor names report the correct PP and PCP indices.
- Negative custom layer counts fail validation at startup. PP rank calculation is unchanged when PCP = 1.

## Validation

### End-to-end

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (MLA, 27 layers, split 14/13).
- Hardware and parallelism: 4 × B300, PP2 × PCP2 × TP1.
- Connector: `MooncakeStoreConnector`, `kv_both`, standalone store, asynchronous loading.
- Workload: GSM8K 5-shot, run twice against the same server so the second pass can reuse stored prompt KV. Local prefix caching is disabled.

| Metric | main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| External prefix cache hit rate, pass 2 | 0.0% | 97.7% |
| GSM8K accuracy, pass 1 / pass 2 | 0.644 / 0.643 | 0.654 / 0.636 |

Accuracy remains within the observed evaluation noise (SE ≈ 0.013). Reference runs on main without the connector score 0.635 at PP2 × PCP2, 0.644 at PP1 × PCP2, and 0.635 at PP2 × PCP1.

Start the server with a standalone Mooncake store available:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 8192 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"load_async":true}}'
```

Run the evaluation twice:

```bash
for pass in 1 2; do
  python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
done
```

Both main and this PR use `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`: MooncakeStoreConnector did not support extensible KV cache at the base revision used for these runs.

### Regression tests and CI

All four regression tests fail on main and pass with this PR; the remaining 272 tests in their files also pass.

```bash
pytest tests/test_config.py::test_layer_range_with_prefill_context_parallel \
  tests/distributed/test_pipeline_partition.py::test_custom_layer_partition \
  tests/utils_/test_ray_utils.py::test_build_actor_name_follows_pp_pcp_tp_layout \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py::test_pp_stages_write_distinct_keys_with_pcp
```

This PR adds `test_pipeline_partition.py` to the **Distributed Comm Ops** CI step and marks the Mooncake regression test `cpu_test` so it runs in the KV connector unit-test job. The end-to-end validation above was run outside CI; no existing job combines an MLA model with PCP, four GPUs, and a Mooncake store.

## Details

At PP2 × PCP2 × TP1, ranks 0–3 belong to PP stages `[0, 0, 1, 1]`, but the old formula returns `[0, 1, 0, 1]`. In MooncakeStoreConnector, this makes the computed PP rank equal the PCP rank: only `(PP, PCP)` key combinations `(0, 0)` and `(1, 1)` are written. Each stage's lookup requires all PCP shards, but `(0, 1)` and `(1, 0)` are missing, preventing cache hits.

Model layer construction already uses the PP process group through `make_layers`. The model-config fix aligns the reported layer ranges and counts with that existing assignment.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, and tests, with AI assistance also used to edit this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Accept an empty tools array like OpenAI
author: sfeng33
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Accept `tools: []` on `/v1/chat/completions` like an omitted `tools` field, matching what the OpenAI API does today. Supersedes #49346 (stale, conflicting) and reverses the check from #39780. The Rust frontend keeps its matching check from #63060; that is a follow-up.

## Claims

- `tools: []` with `tool_choice` omitted, `"none"`, `"auto"` or `"required"` now returns a normal chat completion (HTTP 200) instead of 400 `` `tools` must not be an empty array ``, as OpenAI does. Before, every empty array was rejected.
- `tools: []` with a named function still returns 400, and the message now names the function that is not in `tools` (also for non-empty lists), as OpenAI's does.
- Requests without a `tools` field, and with a non-empty `tools` list, are unchanged. `/tokenize` keeps accepting an empty list without its own workaround.

## Validation

**OpenAI today** (gpt-4o-mini, 2026-11-04): `tools: []` returns 200 with text for `tool_choice` omitted, `none`, `auto` and even `required`; a named function returns 400 `no function named 'f' was specified`. So the `empty_array` 400 that #39780 matched no longer exists upstream.

**Live before/after on one H200**, `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --no-enable-prefix-caching`, before = d8a13402fe (merge-base), after = this branch:

| request | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tools: []`, no `tool_choice` | 400 `tools` must not be an empty array | 200, text, `finish_reason=length` |
| `tools: []`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 400 | 200, text |
| `tools: []`, `tool_choice: "auto"` (stream and non-stream) | 400 | 200, text, usage present |
| `tools: []`, `tool_choice: "required"` | 400 (param `tools`) | 200, text |
| `tools: []`, named function `f` | 400 (param `tools`) | 400 `` The tool `f` specified in `tool_choice` does not match any of the specified `tools` `` (param `tool_choice`) |
| no `tools`, `tool_choice: "auto"` | 400 | 400, unchanged |
| one tool, `tool_choice: "auto"` | 200, tool call | 200, identical output |
| `/tokenize` chat with `tools: []` | 200 | 200, identical |

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in three words."}],"max_tokens":30,"tools":[]}'
```

title: [Bugfix] Fix startup illegal memory access from unaligned extensible KV cache segments
author: xsxszab
body:
## Overview Fix a startup illegal memory access in FlashMLA sparse prefill with the extensible KV cache (#56492), reproduced with DeepSeek-V3.2 on B300. FlashInfer autotuning runs FlashMLA before warmup expands the cache. When a sparse gather includes an invalid (padding) index, FlashMLA reads past the selected rows. With only the null block committed, those reads can reach unmapped memory inside the layer's reserved KV view. This PR extends the segment alignment introduced in #65225 to caches without an RDMA connector, and commits a second block at allocation for block-outermost layouts (follow-up commit by Nick Hill). ## Claims - Prevents the reproduced startup crash by keeping memory mapped beyond each layer's initial KV rows. - Covers block-compact, layer-outermost layouts and block-outermost layouts. - Preserves logical KV capacity and block strides. ## Validation ### End-to-end The segment-alignment fix was validated with DeepSeek-V3.2 (FP8) on 8×B300, using EP + TP2 + DP2 + PP2, eager execution, and prefix caching disabled. Settings: `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=64`, and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`. Each startup test used an empty `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` to exercise autotuning. | Check | main | With segment alignment | Extensible KV cache disabled | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Startup | Illegal memory access in 3/3 runs | Pass | Pass | | GSM8K accuracy, 250 questions | — | 0.884 | 0.880 | | 32 requests with 4096-token prompts | — | 32/32 succeed | 32/32 succeed | ### Regression coverage - Engine initialization without a KV connector verifies that per-layer segments are granule-aligned. - Block-outermost allocation tests verify mapped memory beyond the last layer's view start. - A FlashMLA kernel regression test exercises the newly allocated cache with both `LBNHC` and `BLNHC` layouts, using offsets that would otherwise expose unmapped memory. ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py \ "tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py::test_sparse_flashmla_prefill_on_the_kv_cache_at_allocation" ``` All 70 tests pass on B300; with only the test changes applied on main, 6 fail. The FlashMLA test needs SM100 and is skipped on the H100 CI runner; it was run on B300 and, by Nick Hill, on GB300.
Kernel reproduction On one GPU, place a bf16 KV view near a granule boundary and commit only block 0 (73,728 bytes). The minimum mapped size depends on the indices: | Inputs | Faults when mapped bytes from the view's start are below | |---|---| | Valid indices inside block 0, padded with `-1`, as in the failing startup | Up to about 130 KiB, depending on the query row | | All indices `-1`, `topk_length=0` | Approximately 100 KiB | | All indices valid | No over-read detected | Views fully contained in committed memory do not fault in these tests. The rows above combine our B300 measurements with Nick Hill's on GB300. The following reproduces the all-invalid-indices case: ```python import torch from vllm.third_party.flashmla.flash_mla_interface import flash_mla_sparse_fwd from vllm.utils.extensible_tensor import ExtensibleTensor BLOCK, D, HQ, TOPK, SQ, G = 64, 576, 64, 2048, 128, 2 << 20 room = 81408 # Mapped bytes from the KV view's start to the granule boundary. dev = torch.device("cuda") q = torch.randn(SQ, HQ, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev) indices = torch.full((SQ, 1, TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) topk_length = torch.zeros(SQ, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) offset, view_bytes = 4 * G - room, 1024 * BLOCK * D * 2 buf = ExtensibleTensor( offset + view_bytes, device=dev, segment_capacities=[offset, view_bytes], ) buf.resize_segments_([0, BLOCK * D * 2], zero_new=True) kv = buf.full_view()[offset:].view(torch.bfloat16).view(-1, 1, D) flash_mla_sparse_fwd(q, kv, indices, D**-0.5, topk_length=topk_length) torch.cuda.synchronize() # Illegal memory access: only 81,408 bytes are mapped. ```
## Details The allocator previously committed only block 0 while exposing each layer's full reserved KV view. FlashMLA's SM100 sparse prefill kernel reads past the rows selected by the sparse indices when a TMA gather includes an invalid index: about 100 KiB from the view start when every index is invalid, and up to about 130 KiB when only some are. In the failing startup, `model.layers.17` had a 72 KiB null block and only 80,128 mapped bytes from its view start, less than the roughly 128 KiB the kernel read there. The fix handles the two layouts differently: - **Block-compact, layer-outermost:** align each layer's segment to a memory granule, so committing the null block maps the full first granule. This reuses the existing RDMA padding path. Padding increases reserved address space without adding physical memory, since each segment's commits already map whole granules. - **Block-outermost:** layers share one segment, and their views start at different offsets within block 0. Committing two blocks keeps at least half a granule (1 MiB on the tested device) mapped beyond each layer's view start, well above the roughly 130 KiB FlashMLA reads. This can increase the initial physical mapping; logical KV capacity is unchanged. Layouts that are neither, such as `LHBNC`, keep the current allocation; forcing `LHBNC` with sparse MLA can still fault. This keeps the allocation policy independent of a hard-coded FlashMLA access size. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the crash, write the change and tests, and draft this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations listed above. ---

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix tensor conversion in audio parsing and hashing
author: Woolgathererer
body:
## Overview

Fix tensor-to-NumPy conversion in audio input parsing and shared multimodal hashing.

Following @DarkLight1337's suggestion, I checked the other explicit conversion paths and confirmed the same gradient-related failure in multimodal hashing.

## Claims

- Handle CUDA and gradient-tracking audio tensors by detaching and moving them to CPU before NumPy conversion.
- Detach tensors before hashing, covering image/video tensors and precomputed audio embeddings.
- Add regression coverage and document direct audio Tensor inputs.

## Validation

Before the fixes, the audio model test and the three CPU hashing cases failed with:

```text
RuntimeError: Can't call numpy() on Tensor that requires grad.
```

After the fixes:

| Environment | Validation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS, CPU | Full parser and hasher suites | 57 passed, 4 skipped |
| DGX Spark, CPU/CUDA | New hashing regression for image, video, and audio embeddings | 6 passed |
| DGX Spark | Full parser suite | 34 passed |
| DGX Spark | Whisper Tiny `LLM.generate()` regression | 1 passed |

The hashing tests verify exact hash equality with detached reference tensors.

The Whisper test uses real weights and the `mary_had_lamb` audio sample. It compares gradient-tracking CPU tensors, CUDA tensors, and gradient-tracking CUDA tensors with a NumPy reference using `check_logprobs_close`.

Image/video and embedding coverage exercises parsing and hashing; the real-model test covers raw audio.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

Local parser and hasher suites:

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
  ../vllm-dev/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/multimodal/test_parse.py \
  tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py -q --tb=short
```

The new hashing regression was run before and after changing the hasher:

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
  ../vllm-dev/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/multimodal/test_parse.py::test_hash_parsed_tensor_with_grad \
  -q --tb=short
```

Before: `3 failed, 3 skipped`. After: `3 passed, 3 skipped`.

DGX CUDA coverage:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/audio-tensor-fix/worktree:/tmp/audio-tensor-fix/testdeps \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=ERROR \
/home/matrix/vllm-venv/bin/python -m pytest \
tests/multimodal/test_parse.py::test_hash_parsed_tensor_with_grad \
-v -s --tb=short
```

DGX model regression:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/audio-tensor-fix/worktree:/tmp/audio-tensor-fix/testdeps \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=ERROR \
/home/matrix/vllm-venv/bin/python -m pytest \
tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py::test_audio_tensor_inputs \
-m core_model -q -s --tb=short
```

</details>

All applicable pre-commit hooks, test tethering, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Details

Audio parsing previously called `.numpy()` directly, which fails for CUDA tensors and tensors requiring gradients.

The shared multimodal hasher already moved tensors to CPU, but did not detach them before calling `.numpy()`. Adding `detach()` fixes gradient-tracking inputs while preserving the hashes produced for their detached equivalents.

The DGX validation used this branch's Python source with installed vLLM 0.31.0 native extensions. Startup reported missing Triton kernels and unavailable FlashInfer sampling, but Whisper inference completed. These tests validate input compatibility, not model accuracy.

The earlier search of open PRs found no matching audio conversion fix.

author: subhashpolisetti
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Since #50981, `vllm bench throughput` builds its requests with `bench serve`'s `get_samples`, through `_to_serve_args`. For the BlazeEdit datasets (`vdaita/edit_5k_char`, `vdaita/edit_10k_char`), `get_samples` reads `args.blazedit_min_distance` and `args.blazedit_max_distance`. `bench throughput` defines neither flag and `_to_serve_args` does not fill them in, so the run fails with `AttributeError` before the dataset is loaded. `docs/benchmarking/cli.md` lists BlazeEdit as supported offline.

## Claims

- `bench throughput` runs on both BlazeEdit datasets, over the full distance range (`bench serve`'s defaults, 0.0 and 1.0).
- Other datasets and `bench serve` are unaffected.

## Validation

New regression test `test_get_requests_hf_blazedit` (CPU, HF download stubbed) runs the real `get_requests` and `BlazeditDataset` and checks that every prompt carries the change request.

Before the fix:

```text
$ pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py -k hf_blazedit
E   AttributeError: 'Namespace' object has no attribute 'blazedit_min_distance'
1 failed, 18 deselected
```

With the fix:

```text
$ pytest tests/benchmarks/test_throughput_cli.py -k hf_blazedit
1 passed, 18 deselected
```

End to end on an A10G, in one container: the main nightly wheel, with current main's `datasets.py` and the compared `throughput.py` (main's, then this PR's) copied over the installed package.

```text
$ vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --dataset-name hf \
    --dataset-path vdaita/edit_5k_char --num-prompts 5 --max-model-len 8192

# main: exit 1
AttributeError: 'Namespace' object has no attribute 'blazedit_min_distance'

# this PR: exit 0
Throughput: 0.31 requests/s, 1758.09 total tokens/s, 1258.70 output tokens/s
Total num prompt tokens:  7935
Total num output tokens:  20000
```

`pytest tests/benchmarks` on CPU: 188 passed with this PR and 187 on main; the new test is the only difference. The remaining 27 failures and 5 errors also occur on main and come from my environment: the `vllm` executable is not on PATH, `pandas` and `soundfile` are not installed, and `test_bench_serve*` needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`. `pre-commit` passes.

## Details

Root cause: `_to_serve_args` backfills the `bench serve` attributes that `bench throughput` never exposes, but not the BlazeEdit ones. The fix adds them with `bench serve`'s defaults, next to the other backfilled attributes.

`get_samples` reads six more attributes that `bench throughput` lacks, but it cannot reach them: BFCL rejects backends other than `openai-chat` before reading `bfcl_categories`, and SpecBench and SpeedBench are `--dataset-name` values that `bench throughput` does not offer.

`docs/benchmarking/cli.md` now notes, below the BlazeEdit example, that `bench throughput` has no `--blazedit-*` flags and uses the full range.

Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue covers this. #64537 fixes duplicate request IDs after BlazeEdit filtering in `bench serve`, and the open PRs that touch `throughput.py` (#59881, #56354, #59301, #53082) do not change `_to_serve_args`. This changes a different line of `_to_serve_args` than #64831, and the two merge cleanly in either order.

title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Make control-plane ZMQ heartbeats take effect
author: CJJ1008
body:
## Overview

The EC CPU connector's consumer sets ZMTP heartbeats on its DEALER only after `make_zmq_socket` has connected it, so libzmq never runs them. A producer that freezes or becomes unreachable is therefore never reported to `_on_peer_down`. This PR sets the options before the socket connects.

## Claims

- A producer that stops responding without closing TCP (frozen, host down, network partition) is reported within `HEARTBEAT_IVL + HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` = 6 s. On main it is never reported.
- A killed producer was already reported, because TCP closes. A busy producer is not reported.
- No new option, and `make_zmq_socket` is unchanged.

## Validation

**New test** `test_control.py::test_zmq_client_transport_reports_frozen_peer`: a subprocess runs a ZMQ ROUTER that takes one request and never replies. The test connects through `ZmqClientTransport`, sends a request, `SIGSTOP`s the subprocess, and waits 5 s for `poll_dead()`. Heartbeats are patched to 100 ms / 500 ms.

```
pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_control.py -k frozen
main:     FAILED  AssertionError: frozen producer never reported
this PR:  1 passed in 0.8 s (5/5 runs)
```

**Real constants** (2 s / 4 s), same setup:

| Producer | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `SIGSTOP` | no event in 11 s | reported after 6.00 s |
| Pure-Python loop holding the GIL for 12 s | no event | no event |

**EC unit tests** in a Linux CPU container: `pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit` gives 406 passed on main and 407 passed with this PR, with 36 skipped on both. The extra pass is the new test. Two `test_ec_transfer_params.py` cases time out on both because the container cannot reach the Hugging Face Hub. With Hub access they pass on both. `pre-commit` passes.

The new test is marked `cpu_test`, so the CPU "V1 Others" step runs it. The rest of `test_control.py` runs only in the V1 KV Connectors step, which is disabled.

## Details

**Root cause:** `ZmqClientTransport.connect()` calls `make_zmq_socket(..., bind=False)`, which connects, and only then sets `HEARTBEAT_IVL`, `HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` and `HEARTBEAT_TTL`. libzmq copies socket options into a connection when it is created, and most options affect only later `bind()`/`connect()` calls (see `zmq_setsockopt`). The connection therefore runs without heartbeats, and the `EVENT_DISCONNECTED` monitor fires only when TCP closes.

**Fix:** set the three options as defaults on the transport's own `zmq.Context`. pyzmq applies context defaults when `make_zmq_socket` creates the socket, before it connects. This keeps `make_zmq_socket`'s other DEALER settings and leaves its signature alone. #65575 fixes the same pitfall for the Mooncake KV connector by adding heartbeat arguments to `make_zmq_socket`.

No open PR touches `ec_connector/cpu/control/zmq.py`. I searched open PRs for EC connector, heartbeat, and `ec_connector/cpu`.

**AI assistance:** written with Claude Code. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep FlashInfer TRTLLM prefill query offsets in a persistent buffer
author: Pb314314
body:
## Purpose

Fix an illegal memory access / segfault during CUDA graph replay of the standalone draft-model prefill on Blackwell (SM100), reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60989#issuecomment-6620438731.

Since #60989, the standalone draft model (`method: "draft_model"`) captures FULL CUDA graphs for its prefill. That prefill is a uniform batch of `num_speculative_tokens + 2` tokens per request, because it adds a correction token. That is one token more than FlashInfer's `reorder_batch_threshold` (`1 + num_speculative_tokens`). The builder therefore classifies every request as a prefill and, on SM100, takes the TRTLLM prefill path.

On that path, `build()` allocated `cum_seq_lens_q` as a new tensor (`qo_indptr[prefill_start:] - qo_indptr[prefill_start]`). Attention metadata is built outside the graph, so a FULL graph keeps the address that tensor had at capture time. The tensor is freed after capture and its memory is reused. At replay, the attention kernel reads query offsets from that reused memory. The result is wrong drafts or, for large batches, `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` or a segfault in `cuGraphLaunch`.

This PR writes the offsets into a persistent buffer owned by the builder, the same way `paged_kv_indptr` already works, so every build updates the memory the graph reads. The other tensors on this path (`seq_lens`, `block_tables`, `cum_seq_lens_kv`) are already views of persistent buffers.

Not covered here: with an FP8 KV cache and a non-FP8 query, the same path also makes a contiguous copy of `block_tables` on each build, which would have the same problem under a FULL graph. That configuration was not tested, so this PR leaves it alone.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_prefill_cudagraph.py`. It builds TRTLLM prefill metadata twice, for uniform batches wider than the reorder threshold, and checks that `cum_seq_lens_q` holds the right offsets and stays at the same address.
- End to end on 1x GB200 with model runner V2:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 \
  --max-concurrency 256 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0 --seed 0
# and again with --max-concurrency 32
```

## Test Result

- Unit test: passes with this PR. On main it fails with `cum_seq_lens_q moved between builds`.
- GSM8K end to end (1319 questions, greedy decoding; target Qwen/Qwen3-8B, draft Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, K=3):

| Setup | C256 | C32 | Mean accepted tokens per draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform decode graphs up to 256 requests (as in #63406), without this fix | crash (illegal memory access) | n/a | n/a |
| Same, with this fix | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |
| `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, attention runs eagerly (reference) | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |
| main, with this fix | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |

On main without this fix, the crash is intermittent: graphs there stop at about 200 requests, so a crash depends on what the freed memory holds. With the fix, accuracy and acceptance match the PIECEWISE reference, which shows the replayed draft prefill now reads the correct query offsets.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep FA sliding window active under batch invariance
author: anhtra3889
body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, keep FlashAttention's sliding window active in every step, so Gemma-2 outputs on H100 (FA3) no longer depend on which requests share the batch.

Fixes #65587

## Claims

- Fixes #65587: under batch invariance, a sliding-window request on FA3 gives the same tokens and bitwise-equal logprobs alone as when it decodes next to other requests' prefill chunks.
- A 9-line change in `FlashAttentionImpl.forward`. It only runs with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on layers that have a sliding window; every other configuration is unchanged.
- Adds `test_sliding_window_logprobs_bitwise_alone_vs_mixed_batch` to `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py`, which the existing H100 and B200 batch invariance CI jobs already run.

## Validation

[@imthomp ran the fix on an H100](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65627#issuecomment-6634783966) (vLLM nightly 0.33.0rc1.dev454 plus this diff): the issue reproducer went from 5/20 differing prompts to 0/20. The first version of the new test passed there without the fix too. Its targets were 8–14 tokens, so each decode step read fewer than 64 KV tokens. That is a single KV tile for both FA3 kernels, and with one tile they produce identical bits. The second commit lengthens the targets to 233–393 tokens and the fillers to 1.2k–1.7k tokens. Every prompt stays below the 4096-token window: a sequence longer than the window makes the mixed steps it is part of keep the window too, which hides the bug in those steps. **H100 results for the updated test are still to be filled in.**

FA3 needs SM90 and only A100s were available to me. FA2 runs there and uses the same KV tile either way, so the bug does not reproduce on A100. To check the updated test's workload without an H100, I recorded the `max_seqlen_k` and window that the sliding-window layers actually pass to the FA kernel, and applied FA3's host-side kernel selection to them (trace below).

| Check (A100-SXM4-80GB unless noted) | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| Issue reproducer on H100 (`google/gemma-2-9b-it`), prompts that differ (@imthomp) | 5/20 | 0/20 |
| Existing batch invariance tests on `google/gemma-2-2b-it`, FLASH_ATTN, on H100 (@imthomp) | not run | 8 passed |
| First version of the new test on H100 (@imthomp) | passed | passed |
| Updated new test on H100 (FA3) | TODO, expected to fail | TODO, expected to pass |
| Updated new test on A100 (FA2) | passed | passed |
| Target decode steps whose FA3 kernel differs alone vs batched, from the trace of the updated test's workload | all 60 (15 per target) | 0 |
| Issue reproducer on A100 with H100 scheduler defaults, prompts that differ | 0/20 | 0/20 |
| Existing batch invariance tests on `google/gemma-2-2b-it`, FLASH_ATTN (`max_model_len` 2048 to 8192) | not run | 8 passed |
| `test_sliding_window_backend_correctness` (batch invariance off) | not run | 18 passed |

Commands (from `tests/`, with `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`):

```bash
# New regression test
pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_sliding_window_logprobs_bitwise_alone_vs_mixed_batch

# Existing batch invariance tests on a sliding-window model
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=google/gemma-2-2b-it pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "FLASH_ATTN and not test_sliding_window"

# Sliding-window attention backend correctness
pytest -q v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k test_sliding_window_backend_correctness

# Reproducer script from #65587 (on A100, add max_num_batched_tokens=16384 and
# max_num_seqs=1024 to the LLM kwargs to match H100's offline defaults)
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 python repro_gemma2.py
```

No accuracy evaluation was run: when the new floor applies, every sequence in the batch fits inside the window, so the attention result is mathematically the same and only the kernel's accumulation order changes.

<details>
<summary>FA3 kernel trace of the updated test's workload (target 0, 233 prompt tokens; the other 3 targets match)</summary>

FULL decode graphs are captured with `max_seqlen_k=8192` and window `(4095, 0)`, so FA3 keeps the window there: local kernel, kBlockN=64.

```text
Without fix
  alone  : prefill eager/k=233/causal/N=80  decode FULL/k=8192/local/N=64, ...
  batched: prefill eager/k=233/causal/N=80  decode eager/k=278/causal/N=80, eager/k=360/causal/N=80, eager/k=393/causal/N=80, ...
  decode steps whose FA3 kernel differs alone vs batched: all 15

With fix
  alone  : prefill eager/k=4097/local/N=64  decode FULL/k=8192/local/N=64, ...
  batched: prefill eager/k=4097/local/N=64  decode eager/k=4097/local/N=64, ...
  decode steps whose FA3 kernel differs alone vs batched: none
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** FA3 picks its kernel on the host from `max_seqlen_k`:

- It drops a left window that covers the longest sequence ([`hopper/flash_api.cpp#L865`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/b273a02621d3c94bc747df67204f591b67f38fae/hopper/flash_api.cpp#L865): `if (window_size_left >= seqlen_k - 1) window_size_left = -1;`), which turns local attention off.
- For head dim 256 the KV tile is `is_local ? 64 : 80` ([`hopper/tile_size.h#L51`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/b273a02621d3c94bc747df67204f591b67f38fae/hopper/tile_size.h#L51)). Once the KV spans more than one tile, a different tile changes the online-softmax accumulation order, and with it the output bits.

vLLM passes the batch's real maximum as `max_seqlen_k` in eager steps, but `max_model_len` when capturing FULL CUDA graphs (`for_cudagraph_capture` in MRV1 `gpu_model_runner.py` and MRV2 `model_states/default.py`). With `max_model_len` above the window (8192 vs 4096 in the issue), uniform-decode steps replay graphs that keep the window. Mixed prefill/decode steps run attention eagerly and drop it, unless some sequence in the batch is longer than the window. Without CUDA graphs the same flip happens whenever a batch contains a sequence longer than the window. This matches the issue's results, which were invariant in four cases: with `max_model_len=4096`, with CUDA graphs off and only short prompts, with TRITON_ATTN, and with the sliding window disabled.

**Fix.** Under batch invariance, raise `max_seqlen_k` to at least `window_left + 2` for windowed layers. FA then keeps the window and uses the local kernel in every step, matching the captured graphs. FA2's drop rule (`window_size_left >= max_seqlen_k`) is covered by the same floor.

**Why it is safe.** FA uses `max_seqlen_k` only for host-side decisions (window drop, tile and scheduling heuristics, declared page-table extent). Per-request lengths come from `seqused_k`, which is how captured graphs already run with `max_model_len`. Two existing tests run below the window (`max_model_len` 2048 and 4096, so the floor exceeds `max_model_len`), and both pass on FA2. The added code only compares Python ints, so it adds no GPU sync.

**Not a duplicate.**

- No open PR references #65587.
- #48694 (open, for #47069) routes all regular Hopper attention to FA2 under batch invariance. That would also hide this bug, but it gives up FA3 for every model. This change keeps FA3 and fixes the window-specific cause, and the two are independent.
- flash-attention#169 (open) adds an FA3 `batch_invariant` mode that pins the MMA warpgroup, paged-KV TMA, split-KV and decode causal choices. It leaves the window drop alone, so it would not fix this on its own.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- Under batch invariance, head-dim-256 windowed layers on FA3 now always use the 64-wide local tile. That includes `max_model_len` at or below the window, where they previously always used the 80-wide one. Not benchmarked; batch-invariant mode only.
- Head-dim-128 windowed models (e.g. Gemma-2-27B, Granite SWA) get a 128-wide tile from both kernels on vLLM's paged-KV path, which is why they were not affected.
- `_forward_encoder_attention` (encoder-only sliding-window models) drops the window the same way. I left it out because there is no report for it and nothing to test it on here.
- In CI, only the H100 batch invariance job runs this on FA3. B200 and A100 run FA2 under batch invariance, so they pass with or without the fix, and ROCm skips the test.

AI assistance (Claude in Cursor) was used for the investigation, the fix, the test and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Keep whole-chunk max_load_tokens caps with sliding window groups
author: albertoperdomo2
body:
## Overview

With sliding window groups, the OffloadingConnector applied its prompt-end `-1` after the `max_load_tokens` / `max_num_new_tokens` caps, so a whole-chunk cap lost a chunk (a one-chunk cap loaded nothing). Follow-up to #55885.

## Claims

- With sliding window groups (and no partial-tail support, e.g. gpt-oss, Gemma 2/3), `max_load_tokens = k * tokens_per_chunk` now loads `k` chunks instead of `k - 1`.
- The same lost chunk is fixed for `max_num_new_tokens` (the bound from groups the connector does not offload).
- No change when there is no cap: the hit still stops before the last prompt token.

## Validation

New test `test_max_load_tokens_preserves_aligned_sliding_window_chunk` (16-token chunks, 65-token prompt, mixed full/sliding-window groups):

| Cap | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 16 tokens | 0 | 16 |
| 32 tokens | 16 | 32 |
| none | 64 | 64 |

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "max_load_tokens or sliding"   # 132 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
```

## Details

`_lookup_complete_chunks` computed `min(num_tokens, computed + cap) - 1`. The `-1` exists so a sliding-window hit stops before the last prompt token, which must be recomputed. When a cap ends earlier, it is already a supported boundary, but the `-1` moved it one token below, and the per-group `round_down` then dropped a whole chunk. The fix applies the `-1` to the prompt-end ceiling only: `min(num_tokens - 1, computed + cap)`. This matches the partial-tail path, which already uses `num_prompt_tokens - 1` with uncapped limits. Mamba alignment is unchanged.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `max_load_tokens`, `max_hit_size_tokens`, sliding window + offloading). Draft #62932 edits nearby lines for a different purpose (capacity-bounded loads); expect a trivial rebase for whichever lands second.

Test creation and validation assisted by Claude Code.
