title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Refresh streaming request keys after preemption
author: waizuichougou
body:
## Overview

With lookahead block hashing, a streaming input continuation can replace a token included in a cached block's hash. If the request is preempted, the scheduler recomputes its block hashes from the current tokens, but `OffloadingConnector` retains its previously recorded keys. It can then look up stale entries or skip storing the recomputed KV, causing later requests to miss the CPU cache and recompute the prefix.

Before looking up a resumed request, clear each group's offload keys and rebuild them from the current block hashes.

This is a follow-up to lookahead hash support in #61589 and #64096.

## Claims

- Offload lookups use the recomputed hashes after a streaming request resumes.
- All group keys are rebuilt from the current block hashes.

## Validation

On `main` at `0db3734d51`, the new unit test fails before the fix because the connector retains the old key, and passes with the fix.

<details>
<summary>Unit test</summary>

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

</details>

**End-to-end:** Qwen3.5-0.8B, MTP with one speculative token, `OffloadingConnector`, and NVIDIA GB10. A two-part streaming request was resumed with `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True, reset_connector=False)`. After it completed, the GPU prefix cache was reset and a second request reused the resulting prefix.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Second request's CPU cache hit | 0 tokens | 576 tokens |
| Second request's output tokens | `[198, 196, 196]` | `[198, 196, 196]` |

Before the fix, three KV groups had the new key but the MTP group did not, so the prefix could not be loaded. With the fix, all four groups hit and the 576-token prefix was loaded from CPU. This is a single functional run, not a latency benchmark.

## Details

While a streaming request's KV remains resident, its existing hash still describes that KV. When the request restarts from zero computed tokens, the core scheduler recomputes hashes for the current token sequence. The connector previously only appended keys, leaving already-recorded positions unchanged.

For resumable requests with lookahead hashing, the connector clears each group's recorded keys and uses the existing update logic to rebuild them from the current hashes.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2]  Read routed experts from unkeyed full blocks
author: chenjr97
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix routed-expert output reconstruction after a prefix-cache hit when EAGLE/MTP lookahead hashing leaves a complete block without a key. Read request-local pending blocks alongside the incomplete tail.

Related: [[#61589 — Lookahead block hashes for EAGLE prefix caching](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61589)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61589).

## Claims

- Handle output ranges spanning published blocks, pending full blocks, and an incomplete tail.
- Return an independent array that remains valid after buffer reuse.
- Add buffer, worker, and `LLM` regression coverage, with auxiliary-output changes triggering the existing speculative-decoding CI jobs.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py -q
```
**81 passed, 14 warnings in 13.82s.**

## Details

Lookahead hashing requires the token after a block before its hash can be generated. Routing rows can therefore form a complete block while still waiting in `pending_blocks`.

For a 48-token prompt with block size 16:

1. A cold request computes `[0,48)` and returns its current rows directly.
2. A subsequent request reuses `[0,32)` and recomputes `[32,48)`.
3. The recomputed block is complete, but its hash depends on the new request's first generated token at position 48.
4. Output reconstruction reads `[0,32)` from the store, then needs the pending `[32,48)` block. The old `read()` only checked the incomplete tail, which does not exist here, and asserted.

The fix passes pending blocks to `RoutedExpertsBuffer.read()` and combines them with the tail to cover the requested interval. It retains the coverage assertion and copies the output. Reading leaves pending blocks available for publication when their hashes arrive.

title: [Bugfix] Require fastokens >= 0.3.5 for VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS
author: waynehacking8
body:
## Overview

Raises the minimum `fastokens` version for `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` from 0.2.0 to 0.3.5, in `vllm/tokenizers/fastokens.py`, the `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS` comment in `vllm/envs.py`, the docs and the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning recipe. This is the Python-frontend part of #63467; #63707 already moved the Rust frontend to 0.3.5.

## Claims

- With `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1`, vLLM now refuses a fastokens release older than 0.3.5 when it loads the tokenizer, with an `ImportError` that names 0.3.5.
- This is a hard error at startup for anyone who installed fastokens 0.2.0 to 0.3.4 themselves and sets `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1`: the wheels and the Docker image don't bundle fastokens, so the fix for them is `pip install -U "fastokens>=0.3.5"`. A warning would let the wrong ids through without a sign, since they decode to the same text.
- The releases it now refuses have two bugs:
  - Before 0.3.4, a text that shares a prefix of 4 KB or more with the text the same thread encoded just before it can get different token ids than Hugging Face, which decode to the same text (#63467; fixed in 0.3.4 by crusoecloud/fastokens#78).
  - 0.3.3 and 0.3.4 can deadlock in `encode_batch` while another thread changes the tokenizer's padding or truncation (crusoecloud/fastokens#84, fixed in 0.3.5 by crusoecloud/fastokens#85).

## Validation

- vLLM's `get_tokenizer("Qwen/Qwen3-8B")` with `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` and the new floor: with fastokens 0.3.4 it raises `ImportError: fastokens >= 0.3.5 is required when VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1 (found 0.3.4).`, and with 0.3.5 it loads.
- The spaces pair from #63467 through vLLM's tokenizer loader (5,000 spaces then `x`, then 5,000 spaces then a newline, counted on the second text):

  | Tokenizer | Ids for the second text |
  | --- | --- |
  | fastokens 0.2.0, the current minimum | 41 |
  | fastokens 0.3.4 | 40 |
  | fastokens 0.3.5 | 40 |
  | Hugging Face (`transformers` 5.19.0, `tokenizers` 0.23.3) | 40 |

- fastokens' own `python/tests/test_batch_thread_safety.py` from the 0.3.5 sdist: all 8 concurrent encode-while-changing-settings cases hang on 0.3.4 (the test's 15 s watchdog fires in each) and pass on 0.3.5.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files passes.

The two tokenizer-loader checks ran on vLLM `153a17166e`, whose `vllm/tokenizers/fastokens.py` matches this branch apart from the floor. I compared ids only with Qwen3-8B's tokenizer, on the pair above. 0.3.4 and later also apply a `tokenizer.json`'s truncation and padding blocks on encode and load some tokenizers 0.2.x rejected (#63707 has the Rust-side details); I haven't compared those cases through the Python frontend.

## Details

- 0.3.5 is on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/fastokens/0.3.5/). The fastokens repository has no tag or release for it, so PyPI is the reference for that version.
- #84 shows the deadlock is reachable through transformers: `PreTrainedTokenizerFast` changes padding before each batch encode, so one thread encoding plain text while another tokenizes with `padding=True` is enough. It was reported from SGLang; I haven't reproduced it through vLLM.
- Open #47863 adds `fastokens>=0.2.0` to `docker/Dockerfile` and the `setup.py` extras. Those entries are not on main, so this PR cannot change them; #47863 would need `>=0.3.5` there as well.
- I checked the open PRs that mention fastokens; none changes the Python floor.

This change was prepared with AI assistance.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Don't validate model-built dummy inputs against mm limits
author: cjackal
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes engine startup for Pixtral (+ other models with the same problem) when a modality is embedding-only (`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"<modality>": 0}'` with `--enable-mm-embeds`). This is the root cause of the failure observed in #65648.

## Claims

- Every model registered as of now obeys the contract that #32493 introduced.

## Validation

```shell
vllm serve mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409 --tokenizer-mode mistral \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0}' --enable-mm-embeds
```

## Details

#32493 added embedding input for disabled modality. It introduced the following split:

- User inputs are checked against `--limit-mm-per-prompt` and `--enable-mm-embeds` once, in the renderer (`BaseRenderer` calling `info.parse_mm_data`).
- Data the processor builds or re-parses is parsed with `validate=False`. #32493 switched both call sites:
  - the dummy inputs used for profiling (`get_dummy_inputs`)
  - the cache-miss items in `_get_cache_missing_items`

The split is needed because `MultiModalBudget` profiles each embedding-only modality with `mm_counts={modality: 1}` while its limit is 0. A dummy input that gets validated can never pass that check.

4 models including Pixtral override `get_dummy_inputs` and call `self.info.parse_mm_data(dummy_mm_data)` with the default `validate=True`. This PR fixes the processor-side contract violation. Without it, any deployment of these models that relies on embedding-only modalities still crashes at startup, including KV/EC consumers that should receive embeddings.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Count prompts over max_model_len in Anthropic count_tokens
author: GCSimba
body:
## Overview

`/v1/messages/count_tokens` returns HTTP 400 ("This model's maximum context length is ...") for any conversation longer than `max_model_len`, so a client cannot learn how long such a conversation is, which is exactly when it needs the number to trim it. `/tokenize` counts the same messages. This makes `count_tokens` tokenize without the context-length check, as `/tokenize` does; generation requests keep the check.

## Claims

- `/v1/messages/count_tokens` returns `input_tokens` for a prompt longer than `max_model_len`, equal to the `/tokenize` count for the same messages, instead of a 400.
- Prompts within the limit are counted as before, equal to `usage.input_tokens` of the same `/v1/messages` request (also with a system prompt, tools or disabled thinking), and `/v1/messages` and `/v1/chat/completions` still reject over-length prompts.

## Validation

New test `test_count_tokens_over_max_model_len` in `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py`, on the module's existing `RemoteOpenAIServer` (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--max-model-len 2048`). It counts a ~3,000-token conversation with the Anthropic SDK, compares the result with `/tokenize`, and checks that `messages.create` still rejects the same conversation.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py -k test_count_tokens_over_max_model_len
```

Before the fix (main at 7663a8c):

```
>       count = await client.messages.count_tokens(
E           anthropic.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'message': "This model's maximum context length is 2048 tokens. However, your prompt contains at least 2049 input tokens, which exceeds this limit even without any output tokens. ..."}}
1 failed
```

After the fix: `1 passed`. The test runs in the existing `entrypoints/anthropic` CI step.

Probe server: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3`. One user message of N repeated words, before (7663a8c) and after this change:

| Words | `/tokenize` count | `count_tokens` before | `count_tokens` after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 300 | 309 | 309 | 309 |
| 1900 | 1909 | 1909 | 1909 |
| 2100 | 2109 | 400 | 2109 |
| 4000 | 4009 | 400 | 4009 |
| 2100, plus one tool | — | 400 | 2248 |

Prompts that fit, compared with `usage.input_tokens` of a `/v1/messages` request with the same body (`max_tokens: 1`); identical before and after:

| Request | `count_tokens` | `/v1/messages` `input_tokens` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one short user message | 15 | 15 |
| + `system` | 24 | 24 |
| + one tool | 154 | 154 |
| + `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | 19 | 19 |

With the 2100-word message, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/chat/completions` return 400 ("maximum context length is 2048 tokens") both before and after.

Other checks after the fix:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py` (whole file) | 10 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/`: `test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`, `test_error_type_mapping.py`, `test_protocol_exports.py` | 151 passed; 3 failed: the `TestDetectMergeInlineSystem::test_probes_non_jinja_renderer[deepseek-ai/...]` cases need DeepSeek configs from the Hugging Face Hub, which this machine cannot reach, and fail the same way on main |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | passed (shellcheck skipped: no shell files) |

Environment: CPU only (Intel i5-11300H), Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2, Python 3.12, `--enforce-eager`. The Python sources are this branch; the compiled CPU extensions come from the nightly CPU wheel for dd4e401 (31 commits behind, with no CPU kernel or custom-op changes in between). No model evaluation: generation is unchanged.

## Details

- Root cause: `count_tokens` converts the request with `to_chat_completion_request` and renders it through `render_chat_request`, which tokenizes with `ChatCompletionRequest.build_tok_params` (`max_total_tokens=max_model_len`). Tokenization then stops at `max_model_len + 1` tokens and `_token_len_check` raises. `/tokenize` renders with `max_total_tokens=None`.
- Fix: `_build_base_request` already builds count requests separately (without sampling fields); it now builds them as `_CountTokensChatRequest`, a `ChatCompletionRequest` whose `build_tok_params` matches `TokenizeChatRequest.build_tok_params` (`max_total_tokens=None`, `max_output_tokens=0`). That turns off both the length check and the early truncation, for counting only. `count_tokens` still renders through `render_chat_request`, so templating, tools, thinking and the tool/reasoning parsers are the same as for `/v1/messages`; no shared signatures change.
- Harmony (gpt-oss) chat rendering does not apply tokenization params, so `count_tokens` already counted over-length prompts there; unchanged.
- Counting an over-length prompt now tokenizes all of it, the same work `/tokenize` already does for such a prompt; generation paths are unchanged.
- Why count rather than reject: Anthropic presents token counting as the way to check that a prompt fits the context window before sending it ("Use token counts to ... fit prompts to a target length", [token counting](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting)), and an error that says "at least 2049" does not tell the client how much to trim. #64050 (open) adds an OpenAI Responses `input_tokens` endpoint that mirrors the generation request's validation; this PR does not touch it.

Not a duplicate: searched open and closed issues and PRs for `count_tokens` (by title: #63573/#61063 tool-parser requirement, #59180 thinking and `output_config`, #52896/#47753 Rust frontend, #44725 load counter, #35588 the original endpoint), "count_tokens max_model_len", "count_tokens maximum context length" and "count tokens context length". #59616/#59617 (open) change `/v1/messages` context-overflow errors and stop reasons, not counting.

AI assistance (GitHub Copilot) was used to find the bug, write the change and test, and run the validation; I reviewed every changed line and the test results.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3] Build the MTP eh_proj low-latency GEMM plan
author: csahithi
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On CUDA, `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictorLayer` (the MTP draft layer for `glm_moe_dsa` checkpoints such as GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3) never builds its `eh_proj` low-latency GEMM plan: it checks the draft config's `model_type`, which `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override` rewrites from `glm_moe_dsa` to `deepseek_mtp`. Gate on the target model type instead, as `DeepseekV32MTP` already does. This enables the `eh_proj` rows added in #49791 (SM103), #62843 (SM107) and #64481 (SM100).

## Claims

- Fixes: on SM100, SM103 and SM107 with a BF16 model dtype, the draft's 6144x12288 `eh_proj` now gets the GLM low-latency plan: CuTe skinny GEMM at M 1-4 on SM100/SM107 and M 1-3 on SM103; other M stay on cuBLAS. Before, the plan was never built, so `eh_proj` always ran through `nn.Linear` (cuBLAS).
- Adds a unit test (CPU tensors, mocked configs and submodules) that builds the layer with draft `model_type` `deepseek_mtp` and target `glm_moe_dsa`, and checks that `build_glm52_plan` is called with `eh_proj`'s weight and its plan is kept.

## Validation

Unit tests on main `173d063` (its Python tree over a `2d8e9a9bb7` build's compiled extensions), run on a VR200 (SM107) node:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k "eh_proj or glm"
# with the fix: 5 passed (the new test and 4 existing GLM MTP tests that do not build DeepseekV32MTP)
# test change only, on unpatched main: 1 failed, 4 passed. The new test fails with:
#   AssertionError: Expected 'build_glm52_plan' to be called once. Called 0 times.
```

**Isolated serving A/B: stock vs stock plus only this PR's `mtp.py` change.**
- **Build:** a vLLM `2d8e9a9bb7` build whose `mtp.py` and SM107 table are identical to main `173d063`'s.
- **Config:** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4 on 4x VR200 (SM107), lossless MTP K=7 (greedy draft, standard rejection), FP8 KV, `--numa-bind`.
- **Eval:** GSM8K with all 1,319 questions, 8-shot, greedy, at concurrency 4, so the draft's `eh_proj` runs at M <= 4, where the rows apply.

| | stock | + this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `Compiling CuTeDSL kernels: N/N` at startup | 33 | 36 |
| GSM8K accuracy | 90.83% | 91.51% |
| draft acceptance (accepted / draft tokens) | 49.6% | 49.3% |
| mean acceptance length | 4.48 | 4.45 |

- **Acceptance:** within 0.5%.
- **Why +3 compiles, not +4:** the SM107 `eh_proj` row has 4 configs, and its M=2 config equals the TP4 `o_proj` and shared-expert `down_proj` M=2 configs.
- **Reproduce:** serve a `glm_moe_dsa` checkpoint with `--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 7}'` and read the startup line.

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** as of 2026-11-04, no open PR changes this check. I diffed every open PR updated since 2026-09-15 and ran keyword searches.
- **AI assistance:** This PR is developed with AI assistance, which also ran the tests and measurements above on VR200 nodes. I reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Handle EOS in speculative Guidance batches
author: sragrawal
body:
## Overview

Fix Guidance rejecting committed speculative token batches that contain EOS followed by more tokens when `ignore_eos=True`.

## Claims

- Validate the grammar only through the first primary EOS, preserving the caller's generated token list.
- Keep invalid-prefix rejection atomic and preserve normal EOS stopping and speculative rollback.

## Validation

CPU, PR head `055ccc9fb` plus the test correction: **81 passed, 2 existing xfails** across the Guidance, grammar-backend and structured-output-manager suites. The two new regression cases fail on the unmodified base. Changed-file pre-commit passes, including mypy and CI selection.

H200 ×1, OPT-125M, using the CI image built from `055ccc9fb`: the revised regression test fails with the unpatched backend—grammar rejection stops generation after 5 of 8 tokens—and passes with the fix, producing all eight tokens with a length finish reason and nonzero speculative acceptance. The test forces the `a → EOS` prefix through grammar masking and allowed token IDs, without the unsupported `logit_bias` setting.

GPU, vLLM 0.32.0 with the equivalent fix backported: H200 ×8 / TP8, Mistral Medium 3.5 FP8 with its [EAGLE draft](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-EAGLE), k=3, context 262144, concurrency 8, `ignore_eos=True`. Actual request payloads were identical between runs.

| Streaming check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completed requests | 10/16 | 16/16 |
| Grammar-related SSE500 errors | 6 | 0 |
| Exact requested output lengths | 10/10 successful requests | 16/16; 41,660 output tokens |

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q

# H200, from the repository root:
pytest -v -s \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py::test_guidance_ignore_eos_with_speculative_decoding

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py
```

</details>

## Details

Guidance already accepts further tokens after grammar termination. However, it rejects a batch containing EOS and a suffix before checking that state. The same tokens can therefore succeed one at a time and fail when committed together. The older bulk-consumption implementation can also leave the matcher in an invalid state after consuming past EOS.

Pass only the prefix through EOS to the matcher. The existing atomic acceptance and rollback from [#61557](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61557) remain intact. Normal EOS stopping trims the generated batch before grammar acceptance; temporary draft-mask advancement uses singleton tokens.

Related open [#65608](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65608) handles additional request/model stop tokens. This change concerns the tokenizer's primary EOS and does not add stop-token mapping. When combining the changes, primary-EOS prefix handling should precede additional-stop mapping.

AI-assisted implementation and testing using Codex.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Stop AITER FA from skipping 1-token prompts in prefill/extend
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

The ROCm AITER FA backend passes `min_seqlen_q=1` to aiter's `flash_attn_varlen_func`. On aiter's CK path that is a skip threshold, not a hint: every sequence with `seqlen_q <= 1` gets no output. This passes 0 instead. Upstream root cause: [ROCm/aiter#2229](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2229), fixed in [ROCm/aiter#7473](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7473).

## Claims

- Fixes garbage output for a 1-token prompt batched behind a longer prefill on the V1 model runner, whenever the prefill/extend call runs on CK (fp16, head size 64, sinks or sliding window).
- `test_aiter_mha_decode_single_token[float16]` passes without its xfail.
- No accuracy or throughput change on Qwen3-0.6B fp16 or gpt-oss-20b.

## Validation

MI350X, aiter 0.1.27, built from `main` 2a777ce26e.

- Reproducer: fp16 Qwen3-0.6B with `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA` and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`. One `generate([201-token prompt, 1-token prompt])` call, compared with the 1-token prompt alone, greedy decoding:
  - before: `'[](ệnệtệtệt…'` vs the normal answer
  - after: identical
  - V2 runner: identical both before and after
- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_fa.py`: 95 passed in each of 10 runs. With only the backend change reverted, `test_aiter_fa_shared_kv_matches_reference[prefill-{auto,fp8}-False-16]` fail.
- gsm8k, 5-shot, `lm_eval --model vllm ... attention_backend=ROCM_AITER_FA`:

| Model | Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B fp16 | flexible / strict | 0.4170 / 0.4193 | 0.4170 / 0.4185 |
| gpt-oss-20b (2 runs each) | flexible | 0.3571, 0.3434 | 0.3389, 0.3389 |
| gpt-oss-20b (2 runs each) | strict | 0.2062, 0.2032 | 0.1933, 0.2146 |

  For gpt-oss, both sides vary as much between their own runs as between each other. Its attention output from aiter is bitwise identical either way, except on batches whose longest query is ≤32 tokens: there aiter now picks a smaller CK tile and results differ by one bf16 ulp.
- `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 400 prompts, concurrency 64, 2 runs per side, requests/s:

| Model | in/out | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B fp16 | 1024/128 | 100.6, 100.2 | 101.5, 101.9 |
| Qwen3-0.6B fp16 | 2048/1 | 262.6, 250.2 | 258.0, 266.1 |
| gpt-oss-20b | 1024/128 | 58.1, 59.0 | 58.7, 58.7 |
| gpt-oss-20b | 2048/1 | 124.0, 124.2 | 123.9, 124.4 |

`tests/kernels/attention` runs in the AMD kernels attention job in `test-amd.yaml`.

## Details

#28670 hard-coded `min_seqlen_q=1` after #25763 lost accuracy by passing the batch's true minimum query length. Both values are wrong for the same reason. The CK kernel returns early for `seqlen_q <= min_seqlen_q`, a behaviour added for an older design where paged attention computed the decode rows. The asm v3 kernel ignores the argument, which is why bf16 head size 128 without sinks looked fine.

MRV2 is not affected in practice: `sort_batch_req_ids` puts every request with decode-length queries first, so a 1-token prompt is treated as a decode. MRV1's reorder keeps all first-chunk prompts together at the end, so a 1-token prompt behind a longer one lands in the prefill call. MRV1 is still the ROCm default for DeepSeek-V3.2/V4 and GLM-MoE-DSA, and the fallback when MRV2 lacks a feature.

The shared-KV test's prefill batch now ends with a 1-token prompt. Its sliding-window case runs on CK, so it fails if the skip comes back. No open PR changes `min_seqlen_q` in this backend.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Normalize Chat Completions tools and tool_choice validation
author: yzong-rh
body:
## Overview

Refactor vLLM `v1/chat/completions` `tool_choice` x `tools` validation.

## Claims

Align tools and tool_choice validation with OpenAI where sensible, while allowing intentional vLLM permissiveness.

Ensure `tools=omitted`, `tools=[]`, and `tools=None` are treated identically (follow up to #65547).

Ensure `tool_choice=None` and `tool_choice=omitted` are treated identically, normalizing both to either `"none"` or `"auto"` (subsumes #54321).

Simplify code.

This change updates the Python frontend only. The Rust frontend is still rejects `tools=[]`.

## Validation

[openai_chat_completion_tool_choice_matrix.py](https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/8d9f0d72aed6c09935db3dc3f5b13089) probes each endpoint with crosses of `tool_choice` and `tools` and asks the model to make a tool call if and only if a tool is provided. It records
- whether a request is rejected
- whether a request led to a tool call

Query official endpoint:
```
OPENAI_API_KEY=... .venv/bin/python openai_chat_completion_tool_choice_matrix.py \
  --output openai-results.txt
```

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B   \

```

Results:
- R: rejected
- T: tool call
- T*: tool call but tool is hallucinated
- N: no tool call
- Effective vLLM `tools` / `tool_choice` after validation in brackets
   - `0` means no tool, `1` means one tool

OpenAI (2026/11/04)

```
  --api-key EMPTY   \
  --smoke-model moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5   \
  --think-mode opensource   -ra -v
```

On main:
```
FAILED tests/k3_features/test_tool_choice.py::test_tool_choice_without_tools_field_accepted[nostream-auto] - openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'When using `tool_choice`, `tools` must be set. (para...

```

```

```

```
34 passed, 5 warnings
```

## Details

Comparing to vLLM main:
- main handled `tools=omitted`, `tools=None` and `tools=[]` differently for `tool_choice=auto` and `tool_choice=required`, they are now treated the same.
    - `tools = omitted / None / []` + `tool_choice=auto` is now consistently accepted and will lead to no tool call.
    - `tools = omitted / None / []` + `tool_choice=required` is now consistently rejected, matching the semantics of `required`.
- main did not normalize `tool_choice=None`, treating `tools=[get_weather]` + `tool_choice=None` as no tool call
    - `tools=[get_weather]` + `tool_choice=None` is now treated as `tool_choice=auto` matching openai behavior.
    - otherwise, when `tools=omitted / None / []`, `tool_choice=None` is normalized as `none`.

Comparing to OpenAI:
- OpenAI rejects any explicit `tool_choice` other than `None` when `tools` is omitted or `None`; vLLM is more permissive, allowing `none` and `auto` in those cases.
- OpenAI allows `tools=[]` + `tool_choice=required` but this leads to a hallucinated tool call. vLLM rejects it outright.

The existing tool-calling documentation remains accurate, so no documentation update is included.

title: [Bugfix][Step5] Fix FP32 residual truncation at pipeline boundaries
author: xsxszab
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix silent FP32-to-BF16 rounding at Step5 pipeline boundaries by allocating the NVIDIA implementation's intermediate buffer in FP32 when `fp32_residual_connection` is enabled. Add a one-time MRV2 check of the tensors each non-first PP stage receives against its persistent receive buffers.

## Claims

- In the tested Step5 PP2 configuration, prompt logprobs match PP1 exactly at all 418 scored positions, and greedy outputs match on all 53 prompts, up from 10 before the fix.
- MRV2 no longer copies mismatched PP tensors silently. A missing tensor or a different per-token shape fails on the first step; a received tensor without a buffer, or a buffer with lower precision or range, is logged with the tensor's name.
- PP communication volume is unchanged. The FP32 buffer adds 128 MiB per non-first-stage worker at 16,384 batched tokens and hidden size 4,096.

## Validation

**Setup:** `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview`, B300, TP4 + EP + MegaMoE with sequence parallelism, MRV2. Compared PP2 before and after the fix against PP1.

**Prompt logprobs:** six fixed prompts via `/v1/completions` with `prompt_logprobs: 0`, covering 418 scored positions.

| Configuration | Mean absolute logprob difference from PP1 | Maximum absolute difference |
|---|---:|---:|
| PP1, repeat run | 0 | 0 |
| PP2, main | 0.036 | 1.59 |
| PP2, this PR | 0 | 0 |

**Greedy outputs:** 53 sequential requests comprising 48 GSM8K questions and five long prompts of 2K–25K tokens, generating up to 256 tokens each.

| Configuration | Outputs identical to PP1 |
|---|---:|
| PP1, repeat run | 53/53 |
| PP2, main | 10/53 |
| PP2, this PR | 53/53 |

All 43 divergences on main began at a near-tie. GSM8K accuracy on all 1,319 questions with 5-shot prompting was 0.933 for PP2 with this PR and 0.934 for PP1.

**Receive check and unit tests:** with the check but without the Step5 buffer change, each of the four receiving workers logs once for FP32 `hidden_states` copied into BF16, with logprobs unchanged from main. With both changes, nothing is logged. `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py`: 16 passed, including six dtype cases and cases for a missing, reshaped and unbuffered tensor.

The Step5 end-to-end validation ran outside CI because the tested configuration requires eight GPUs and the full checkpoint. The check's unit tests run in the existing V1 Executor + Worker CI step.

<details>
<summary>Additional compatibility and synchronization checks</summary>

- The dtype check emitted no warnings in PP serving for PowerLM-3b, Llama-3.2-1B, e5-mistral-7b, bge-multilingual-gemma2, InternVL3-1B, Phi-3.5-vision, and `test_pp_mixed_precision_kv_cache`.
- The key and shape checks raised and logged nothing in PP=2 generation for Qwen3.5-0.8B (with and without MTP), OPT-350m and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (8 layers, dummy weights).
- With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn`, no synchronization was attributed to the new code, and prompt logprobs still matched PP1 exactly.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Validation commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview \
  --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 2

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64

pytest -v -s tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py
pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py
```

Use `--pipeline-parallel-size 1` for the PP1 reference. Prompt-logprob comparisons use `/v1/completions` with `temperature: 0`, `max_tokens: 1`, and `prompt_logprobs: 0`.

</details>

## Details

Step5 produces FP32 stage outputs when `fp32_residual_connection` is enabled, and PP transport preserves that dtype. The NVIDIA implementation previously declared its persistent intermediate buffer in the model dtype, BF16, so MRV2's receive-side `copy_` rounded the residual stream at each boundary. Allocating the buffer in FP32 fixes this loss and follows the existing AMD implementation. When the option is disabled, the buffer retains the runner-provided dtype.

On the first real step of each non-first PP worker, MRV2 compares the received tensors with the persistent buffers it copies them into. The copy reads only the buffers' keys, broadcasts trailing dimensions and converts dtypes, so most mismatches otherwise go unnoticed. A different per-token shape raises, since the copy would broadcast values; a missing tensor raises with its name instead of a bare `KeyError`; a received tensor without a buffer is dropped and is logged. Lower precision or range is detected with `torch.finfo.eps` and `max`, including conversions involving FP8, and is logged. The check uses CPU metadata, adds no GPU synchronization, and leaves the copy unchanged.

No other open PR was found addressing Step5's PP buffer dtype or this MRV2 receive-side check.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, implement, and validate the change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Encoder CUDA graph: cap each graph's frame slots at its token budget
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview

When encoder CUDA graphs are on and the model accepts video, every captured graph is sized for `max_batch_size x max_frames_per_video` frames, including the graphs for small token budgets. For GLM-4.1V that is 64 x 600 = 38,400 frames, so even the smallest graph computes at least 38,400 tokens, and every image or video request replays a graph far larger than its input.

This PR caps each graph's frame slots at its token budget.

## Claims

- **GLM-4.1V** (encoder graph on, video allowed, which is the default):
  - Median image request: 470–481 ms → 31–32 ms.
  - Median video request: 475–484 ms → 35–36 ms.
  - Eager takes 57 ms (image) and 61 ms (video). Before this PR the graph path was ~8x slower than eager; after it, it is faster.
- **Qwen2.5-VL-7B at 128k context:**
  - Median image request: 30–33 ms → 27 ms.
  - Median video request: 32–33 ms → 30–31 ms.
- **Video outputs are unchanged:**
  - GLM-4.1V: graph outputs match eager bit for bit.
  - Qwen2.5-VL: graph outputs match main's graph outputs token for token.
  - Both hold for single videos and for 4-video batches replayed as one graph.
- **No effect** when video is disabled, or when `max_frames_per_batch` is at most the budget.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GB200, bf16, default ViT attention backend.
- Baseline is main at 2a777ce26e; this PR is the same commit plus the change.

**Latency.**
- One engine per run with `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 1}`, so image and video requests share the same graphs.
- Each run sends 24 image requests and 24 video requests one at a time, with `max_tokens=1`.
- Images and videos are fresh random inputs, so there are no encoder-cache hits:
  - images cycle through 6 sizes from 224x224 to 896x672;
  - videos have 4–16 frames at 224–448 px.
- Each graph-on request replays exactly one graph, counted via `EncoderCudaGraphManager.execute` calls.
- Runs were in the order baseline, this PR, this PR, baseline. The two values per cell are pass 1 / pass 2, each the median request latency.

| Model (`max_model_len`) | Requests | Baseline, graph on | This PR, graph on | Eager |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V-9B (8192) | image | 469.8 / 480.6 ms | 31.9 / 31.2 ms | 56.8 ms |
| GLM-4.1V-9B (8192) | video | 475.4 / 484.2 ms | 35.9 / 35.2 ms | 60.7 ms |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (128000) | image | 32.6 / 30.3 ms | 27.2 / 27.1 ms | 56.9 ms |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (128000) | video | 32.1 / 31.9 ms | 30.8 / 29.7 ms | 55.7 ms |

**Video correctness.** Greedy decoding with `logprobs=2`; each comparison is graph vs eager on the same tree, and every video is fresh.

| Model | Inputs | Graph replays | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V (`max_model_len=8192`, 38,400 → budget frame slots on every graph) | 4 single videos (48 tokens each) + 2 batches of 4 videos (32 tokens each) | each 4-video batch is one replay | tokens identical, logprob diff 0 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (`max_model_len=128000`, 896 → budget frame slots on graphs ≤ 512) | 4 single videos + 2 batches of 4 videos (32 tokens each) | 4 single replays, and each 4-video batch is one replay | identical to main's graph: 12/12 token sequences |

On Qwen2.5-VL, both main and this PR match eager on 10 of 12 sequences. The 2 that diverge are the same on both. Each divergence happens at a step where eager's top-2 logprobs are exactly tied, after bf16 differences of up to 0.24 in logprob. That drift between graph and eager already exists on main and is unrelated to this change.

On GLM-4.1V, the encoder outputs for videos were also compared directly:
- Graph vs eager has a relative L2 error of ≤ 0.2%, the same as eager vs eager in a different batch.
- Replaying after other inputs have dirtied the capture buffers gives identical outputs.

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: 79 passed. The new test captures with `max_frames_per_batch=1000` and checks two things: each graph keeps `min(1000, budget)` frame slots, and a video batch still replays. `pre-commit` passes.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
# Image latency (square images only); run with cudagraph_mm_encoder True and False.
import time, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
llm = LLM("zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking", max_model_len=8192, max_num_seqs=8,
          enable_prefix_caching=False, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 1},
          compilation_config={"cudagraph_mm_encoder": True})
P = ("[gMASK]<sop><|user|>\n<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>"
     "Describe the image.<|assistant|>assistant\n")
rng, sp, ts = np.random.default_rng(0), SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1), []
for _ in range(6):
    for s in (224, 336, 448, 672):
        im = Image.fromarray(rng.integers(0, 255, (s, s, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
        t = time.time(); llm.generate([{"prompt": P, "multi_modal_data": {"image": im}}], sp)
        ts.append(time.time() - t)
print(f"median {1e3 * sorted(ts)[len(ts) // 2]:.1f} ms")
```

The video runs use the same setup with synthetic videos (4–16 frames, 224–448 px). For correctness they use `temperature=0` and `logprobs=2`, run once with `cudagraph_mm_encoder` on and once off, and compare tokens and logprobs. For batches, 4 fresh videos are submitted in one `generate` call.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `EncoderCudaGraphManager` passes one `max_frames_per_batch` to every budget's capture. That value is `max_batch_size * max_frames_per_video`, which became the default in #40445.

Qwen2/2.5/3-VL and GLM-4.1V build their capture layout from it: each item gets `frames_per_item = max_frames_per_batch // max_batch_size` frames, and each frame has at least one token. The captured size is therefore at least `max_frames_per_batch` tokens, whatever the budget.

How badly a model is affected depends on where its frame limit comes from:
- **GLM-4.1V:** the limit is a constant 600 frames per video, so every budget captures at least 38,400 tokens.
- **Qwen:** the limit is derived from `max_model_len` and the video limit, so the graphs grow only with long contexts. For example, Qwen2.5-VL at 128k context gets 896 frame slots, which inflates the 64–512 budgets.

**Fix.** Every frame yields at least one output token, so a batch that fits budget `B` has at most `B` frames. Concretely:
- Each graph is captured with `min(max_frames_per_batch, B)` frame slots.
- That value is stored in `BudgetGraphMetadata`.
- Replay pads `cu_seqlens` to the same per-graph value.

The model capture layouts are unchanged; they shrink because they derive from the value passed in.

Every auto or validated configuration keeps `B >= max_batch_size`, so a graph never gets fewer frame slots than `max_batch_size`, and image replays are unaffected.

`EncoderCudaGraphManager` is shared by Model Runner V1 and V2 (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py`), so both get the fix. The change adds no host sync.

**Related: GLM-4.1V image outputs (not changed by this PR).**
- On main, with video enabled, GLM-4.1V image replays are numerically wrong. GLM registers no `cu_seqlens` padding, so the replay buffer's tail is filled with zeros.
- Measured at the encoder output on main, graph vs eager has a relative L2 error of up to 169% for a 576-token image. Eager vs eager in a different batch varies by only 0.2–2.7%.
- This PR does not fix that: 576-token images are still wrong with it. #65453 registers the padding and fixes it; with both applied, the error is back within the eager variation.

**Not a duplicate:**
- #60112 (open) falls back to eager when a replay exceeds a capture buffer.
- #43403 (closed draft) proposed an eager fallback for `T > frames_per_item`.
- #65453 (open) registers `cu_seqlens` padding for GLM-4.1V and Kimi-K2.5.

None of these changes the capture size. #65453 touches the same padding path but no lines in common; with this PR, capture and replay still use the same per-graph frame count.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix FlashInfer ViT attention for GLM-4.1V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview

With `--mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASHINFER`, the GLM-4.1V/4.5V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash vision encoders fail on main, in eager mode and with encoder CUDA graphs alike.

This PR fixes their attention so FlashInfer runs and matches the other ViT backends. The default backend's output does not change.

## Claims

- **FlashInfer now works on all three models.** On main, every forward asserts `sequence_lengths is not None`. With this PR, FlashInfer's output differs from FlashAttention's by the same amount as `TORCH_SDPA`'s does.
- **Batching is now correct.** With only the assert fixed, every sequence after the first in a batch read the wrong `v`:
  - outputs were off by 166% relative L2, or NaN;
  - capturing a 1024-token encoder graph hit an illegal memory access.
  
  With this PR, an image's output in a batch matches its output alone within 0.2%, in either batch order.
- **Default backend unchanged.** FlashAttention outputs are bitwise identical to main. Encoder latency is 1.5% lower, since `v` is no longer copied.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GB200, bf16, TP1.
- Baseline is main at 2a777ce26e; this PR is the same commit plus the change.

**Method.**
- Each image is a fresh random image of 224x224 to 896x672.
- Every value is the relative L2 error `‖a − b‖ / ‖b‖` of the vision encoder output.

**Backend agreement (eager).** In the cross-backend columns below, FlashInfer is this PR; FlashAttention and SDPA are main. "Batched" is the largest error of an image's output in a 5-image batch against its output alone, over both batch orders.

| Model | Weights | FlashInfer, main | FlashInfer vs FlashAttention | SDPA vs FlashAttention | FlashInfer, batched vs alone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking | real | AssertionError | 2.55–2.82% | 2.42–2.88% | ≤ 0.21% |
| GLM-OCR | real | AssertionError | 4.20–5.72% | 3.93–6.72% | ≤ 0.26% |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (vision tower only) | random, seeded | AssertionError | 2.81–2.94% | 2.81–2.91% | ≤ 0.34% |

GLM-5.3-Flash uses the real `config.json` and processor with seeded random vision weights, because the full checkpoint was not available.

**Encoder CUDA graphs with FlashInfer (GLM-4.1V, `max_model_len=8192`, video enabled).**
- Graph vs eager is ≤ 0.20% for 6 single images (64–576 tokens) and 4 videos (256–768 tokens).
- Replaying after a larger batch has dirtied the capture buffers gives identical output.
- This holds with and without #65453.
- On main, capture fails.

**Default backend.**
- GLM-4.1V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash FlashAttention outputs are bitwise identical to main: single images, batches in both orders, and GLM-4.1V graph replays.
- GLM-4.1V encoder latency was measured over 34 batches of 1–200 images (64–13,800 tokens). Each value is the median of 15 runs. Runs went baseline, this PR, this PR, baseline, and each batch keeps the faster pass.

| | This PR / baseline (geomean) | Slowest batch | Batches > 2% slower | Baseline pass-to-pass spread (median) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph replay | 0.985 | 0.996 | 0 / 34 | 0.13% |
| Eager | 0.984 | 1.001 | 0 / 34 | 0.35% |

**FlashInfer vs FlashAttention latency (GLM-4.1V, with this PR).**
- This PR is a correctness fix; it does not make FlashInfer faster. FlashAttention (FA4) stays the default backend.
- Measured over the same 34 batches as above, alternating FlashAttention, FlashInfer, FlashInfer, FlashAttention, keeping the faster pass per batch.
- Every FlashInfer batch matched eager within the graph-vs-eager tolerance.

| | FlashInfer / FlashAttention (geomean) | Range | Batches > 2% slower |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph replay | 1.003 | 0.989–1.032 | 2 / 34 |
| Eager | 1.041 | 0.999–1.159 | 10 / 34 |

- **With graphs:** the two backends are within 1.1% for batches above 1,300 tokens. Smaller batches are up to 3.2% slower with FlashInfer.
- **In eager mode:** most batches up to 1,100 tokens are 12–16% slower with FlashInfer, where per-call host overhead dominates. Above 1,300 tokens they are within 2%.

**Tests.**
- This PR adds GLM-4.1V to `test_eonly_vit_cudagraph_outputs`, which runs FlashInfer with encoder CUDA graphs on image and video batches. It fails on main (`assert sequence_lengths is not None`) and passes with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: 78 passed.
- `pre-commit` passes.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
# Fails on main with AssertionError; runs with this PR.
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

llm = LLM("zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking", max_model_len=8192,
          mm_encoder_attn_backend="FLASHINFER", limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 2})
P = ("[gMASK]<sop><|user|>\n<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>"
     "Describe the image.<|assistant|>assistant\n")
im = Image.fromarray(np.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 255, (448, 448, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
print(llm.generate([{"prompt": P, "multi_modal_data": {"image": im}}],
                   SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8))[0].outputs[0].text)
```

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_eonly_vit_cudagraph_outputs -k glm4_1v
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The FlashInfer ViT path, `flashinfer_wrapper` (cuDNN batch prefill), needs two things these models did not provide.

1. **`sequence_lengths`.**
   - GLM-4.1V's `prepare_encoder_metadata` already computes it, but the vision transformer never passes it to its blocks.
   - GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash do not compute it in eager mode either. They also build plain `cu_seqlens` there, rather than FlashInfer's offset layout from `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`.
2. **The `v` layout.**
   - `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens` gives q/k token offsets of `hidden_size` and v offsets of `3 * hidden_size`. It expects `v` to be a view into the fused qkv output, as in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL.
   - The GLM attention made `v` contiguous, so its token stride was `hidden_size`. Every sequence after the first then read `v` at three times its real offset.

**Fix.**
- Thread `sequence_lengths` through the GLM vision attention and blocks.
- Keep `v` as a view: `.contiguous()` now applies only to `q` and `k`, which RoPE copies anyway.
- On the eager paths, build FlashInfer's metadata when FlashInfer is selected:
  - GLM-5.3-Flash reuses its existing `prepare_encoder_metadata`;
  - GLM-OCR calls the same `MMEncoderAttention` helpers inline, because its inherited `prepare_encoder_metadata` needs position embeddings that GLM-OCR removes.
- Other backends keep their existing code paths.

**Not covered.** GLM-5.3-Flash with encoder CUDA graphs was not run end to end: the full checkpoint was not available. Its graph path uses the same metadata keys as GLM-4.1V, which was tested.

**Related.** #65453 aligns FlashInfer's `cu_seqlens` between capture and replay for GLM and Kimi-K2.5. It touches different lines and composes with this PR; the graph results above hold with and without it.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds FlashInfer ViT support for the GLM vision encoders. #65453 assumes FlashInfer already runs on these models.

title: [BugFix][DP] Hash the parallel config before engine init for DP validation
author: vMaroon
body:
## Overview

With `data_parallel_size > 1`, a `NixlConnector` and `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`, every engine fails the DP configuration check at READY since #62330. The READY message now carries the hash of the parallel config the engine was started with, which is the config the front-end compares it against (#26218).

## Claims

- Fixes the startup failure `Configuration mismatch detected for engine N ... Worker hash: ..., Expected hash: ...` for DP > 1 deployments that rely on the automatic `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` resolve (NIXL + DCP). The set of compared fields is unchanged, only the moment of hashing moves.
- One file, +12/-4, no new configuration and no user-visible behaviour change.

## Validation

- Root cause reproduced on a live deployment at `44965a1097` (2026-11-03): an MLA MoE model (GLM-5.3 shape), one engine per node, `--data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 1 --data-parallel-rank N --prefill-context-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --block-size 64 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector", ...}'`. Every rank exits at READY with the mismatch, right after logging `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size is automatically adjusted from 1 to block_size 64`. Recomputing the front-end's `ParallelConfig.compute_hash()` factors inside the running API server reproduces the "Expected hash"; changing the single factor `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` from 1 to 64 reproduces the "Worker hash" exactly.
- Workaround confirmed on the same deployment: `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 64` (which turns the auto-resolve off) brings all four ranks to READY.
- The patch passes `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` with the repository configuration. The hash is computed from the same `ParallelConfig` fields as before, after `startup_handshake` has applied the coordinator's updates, so a real mismatch (for example a different `--enable-expert-parallel` on one rank) is still detected.

## Details

Root cause. #26218 added `parallel_config_hash` to the READY message, computed in `EngineCoreProc._perform_handshake` after the generator resumes, that is after `EngineCore.__init__` has run. #62330 moved `VllmConfig.adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` into `_initialize_kv_caches`, before profiling, so with NIXL + DCP and no explicit size the engine's `parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` becomes the block size before the hash is taken. `wait_for_engine_startup` compares that hash with the front-end's `ParallelConfig`, which still holds the default, and `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` is not in `compute_hash`'s `ignored_factors`.

Change. `_perform_handshake` computes `parallel_config.compute_hash()` right after `startup_handshake` returns and before the `yield`, and sends the stored value in the READY message. Handshake-time updates (`data_parallel_size`, the master address and port) are still included; the front-end applies the same updates to its own config, as before.

Alternative considered. Adding `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to `ParallelConfig.compute_hash`'s `ignored_factors`. That hash also feeds `VllmConfig.compute_hash`, the compile cache key, where the interleave size matters, and the same mismatch would come back with the next setting the engine resolves after startup. Hashing before initialization covers both.

Related. #60671 (open) moves the NIXL + DCP interleave resolve into `VllmConfig` so that both processes hold the resolved value. This change is the minimal fix for the check itself and stands on its own; the two compose.

title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Initialize the shard record in the indexer QKV layer
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Purpose

Since #63752, MiniMax-M3 checkpoints fail to load:

```
AttributeError: 'MinimaxM3QKVParallelLinearWithIndexer' object has no attribute 'loaded_shard_ids'
```

#63752 added the per-shard loading record (`loaded_shard_ids`) in
`StackedColumnParallelLinear.__init__`. `MinimaxM3QKVParallelLinearWithIndexer` skips
`QKVParallelLinear.__init__` (it builds its own 5-group layout) by calling
`ColumnParallelLinear.__init__` directly, so it skipped the stacked init too.

Call `StackedColumnParallelLinear.__init__` instead. It sets up the record and forwards to
`ColumnParallelLinear.__init__` unchanged. The layer is also added to the shard-tracking tests.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_stacked_shard_tracking.py`
- E2E: `vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash -pp 2` on 2x B300, then a few chat requests.

## Test Result

- Shard-tracking tests: 9 passed. The new test fails on main with the `AttributeError` above.
- E2E: the server starts (it fails on main during weight loading) and answers correctly, e.g. "What is the capital of France? Answer in one word." → "Paris"; "Translate to German: The weather is nice today." → "Das Wetter ist heute schön."

title: [Bugfix] Fix DP ViT all-gather dtype mismatch when the first parameter is fp32
author: micah-wil
body:
## Summary

With `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, ranks that get no images all-gather placeholder embeddings whose dtype comes from `next(vision_model.parameters())`. Since #64111, MiniMax-M3 keeps its patch embedding in fp32 while the tower outputs bf16. Ranks with images then gather bf16 and ranks without gather fp32, so the all-gather mismatches and startup hangs.

This uses the vision model's `dtype` attribute when it has one, and falls back to the first parameter's dtype otherwise. Other models are unchanged: their `dtype` either matches the first parameter or isn't defined.

## Test plan

- `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` with `-tp 4 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data` now starts and serves image requests. Before the fix, it hung after the encoder profile run.
- Ongoing coverage comes from the nightly MiniMax-M3 evals, which run with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.

title: [Bugfix] Honor checkpoint FP8 KV scales in Qwen4Exp QSA
author: lHrHenry233
body:
## Overview

Load checkpoint K/V scales into the host floats used by Qwen4Exp QSA with an FP8 KV cache. This splits the fix out of #59209. The CUDA reproducer runs with HiSparse disabled. [Original review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59209#discussion_r4471891384)

## Claims

- On CUDA, the fused cache writer and sparse attention reader use the checkpoint scales.
- On ROCm, the sparse attention reader requires both scales to be `1.0`. Its existing check now sees the loaded values and rejects a non-unit K or V scale.

## Validation

Both checks used safetensors with `k_proj.output_scale=0.5` and `v_proj.output_scale=2.0`.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA engine startup (SM100, `fp8_e4m3`) | Device K/V = 0.5/2.0, host K/V = 1.0/1.0. Scale assertion failed. | Device and host K/V = 0.5/2.0. Scale assertion passed. |
| ROCm QSA implementation exercised on CPU (PyTorch 2.13.0) | Host K/V = 1.0/1.0. The reader passed the unit-scale check. | Host K/V = 0.5/2.0. The reader raised its existing `NotImplementedError` before GPU dispatch. |

The CPU probe used the AMD QSA layer, the vLLM safetensors loader and the standard post-load pass. It also checked that `fp8` with K/V = 1.0/2.0 is rejected, and that unit-scale FP8 and BF16 reach the GPU dispatch boundary. I haven't run the ROCm backend on AMD hardware. Repository pre-commit checks passed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the CUDA result or check on ROCm hardware</summary>

The original CUDA run used upstream `fd75a7a920`, an SM100 GPU, PyTorch `2.14.0+cu130`, and native extensions from the `0cb25c3574` wheel for both runs. Both generated identical checkpoint weights. To repeat the check in a disposable checkout with the PR commits available, restore the original test and run it:

```bash
git diff 58bfefd8^ 58bfefd8 -- tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py | git apply
pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py::test_qsa_fp8_uses_checkpoint_kv_scales
```

For ROCm, save the [same one-layer checkpoint](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/58bfefd8a077d223f555878a763285e58ab11409/tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py#L253-L281) and run one request with the code below. With K/V = 0.5/2.0 the expected error includes `requires unit scales on the AMD path`. With K/V = 1.0/1.0 the request should produce one token.

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

if __name__ == "__main__":
    llm = LLM(
        model="./checkpoint", dtype="bfloat16", kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3",
        skip_tokenizer_init=True, enable_prefix_caching=False, enforce_eager=True,
        max_model_len=128, max_num_seqs=2,
    )
    result = llm.generate(
        {"prompt_token_ids": [1, 2]},
        SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0, detokenize=False),
    )
    assert len(result[0].outputs[0].token_ids) == 1
```

</details>

## Details

The loader populates `_k_scale` and `_v_scale`, which the unfused writer reads directly. Both platform implementations also keep Python floats initialized to `1.0`. The post-load hook copies the tensor values into those floats once per FP8 layer.

title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek-V4] Share the target embedding with the MTP drafter under PP
author: xsxszab
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix low draft acceptance with DeepSeek-V4 MTP under pipeline parallelism by sharing the target's input embedding with the drafter. This uses the existing embedding-sharing mechanism, as in [#58648](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58648).

## Claims

- Restores PP2 draft acceptance from 0.030 to 0.820, matching the PP1 baseline.
- Maintains comparable GSM8K accuracy: 0.949 with the fix versus 0.948 on main.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on B300, TP2 + EP, MegaMoE, MRV2, and MTP with 2 speculative tokens.

| Configuration | GSM8K accuracy | Draft acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| PP1, main | 0.947 | 0.820 |
| PP2, main | 0.948 | 0.030 |
| PP2, this PR | 0.949 | 0.820 |

GSM8K: 1,319 questions, 5-shot. Draft acceptance is total accepted tokens divided by total drafted tokens over the evaluation.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative_config.method=mtp \
  --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens=2

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
```

Use `--pipeline-parallel-size 1` for the PP1 baseline.

`pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k may_use_target_embed`: **2 passed**. Without the fix, the DeepSeek-V4 case fails because `may_use_target_embed` is `False`; the OPT control passes in both versions.

## Details

The checkpoint contains no separate MTP embedding. Under PP, the NVIDIA `DeepSeekV4MTP` does not declare `has_own_embed_tokens`, so the target's last stage omits its embedding and `maybe_share_target_embed` returns early. The drafter uses an unloaded embedding, causing almost every draft token to be rejected.

Setting `has_own_embed_tokens = False` enables both parts of the existing mechanism: the registry marks the drafter as `may_use_target_embed`, causing the target's last PP stage to load the embedding, and the drafter then shares that module. The retained embedding is TP-sharded (0.49 GiB per GPU at TP2 in this setup).

The change and registry regression test cover the NVIDIA implementation. Related PRs address other models: [#63141](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63141) adds an error for DeepSeek-V3/V3.2 MTP, and [#62903](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62903) fixes Inkling MTP.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Granite 4.1 Vision deepstack handoff between pipeline stages
author: xsxszab
body:
## Overview

Granite 4.1 Vision (#40282) does not work with `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`. Every non-first stage fails at startup with `KeyError: 'ds_<layer>'`, and once that is fixed, later stages receive the forwarded deepstack features as zeros, which silently drops them from image requests. This PR fixes both: each stage declares only the deepstack buffers it receives, and the first stage forwards copies of the features instead of views of buffers it zeroes before the PP send.

## Claims

- Granite 4.1 Vision starts and serves with PP > 1; on main it fails at startup for any split.
- With eager execution, PP2 output is identical to PP1 on image and text prompts: same greedy tokens and logprobs.
- Adds a CI test that compares an image request between PP2 and no PP; it fails without the second fix and passes with this PR.

## Validation

`ibm-granite/granite-vision-4.1-4b`, bf16, 1–2× B300, `--max-model-len 8192`. Six requests sent one at a time: three image chats and three text completions, 32 greedy tokens each with top-5 logprobs.

| Check | main | Declaration fix only | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| PP2 startup | `KeyError: 'ds_9'` on stage 1 during warmup | Starts | Starts |
| Eager PP2 vs PP1, text prompts | — | 3/3 identical | 3/3 identical |
| Eager PP2 vs PP1, image prompts | — | 2/3 identical tokens, logprobs differ by up to 0.27 | 3/3 identical, logprob difference 0 |

Two eager PP1 runs are identical (6/6, difference 0). With CUDA graphs, PP2 starts and serves; its outputs differ from PP1 at near-ties by the same amount as PP1 with CUDA graphs differs from PP1 in eager mode, because the two configurations capture different graph sizes.

```bash
vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-vision-4.1-4b --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --enforce-eager
```

**Test.** `test_pp_granite4_vision_deepstack` serves a 4-layer dummy-weight variant with and without PP2 and compares a text and an image request (`generate_with_image`). With four layers, deepstack layers 0 and 3 land on different stages. It fails with only the declaration fix and passes with this PR:

```bash
pytest -v -s "tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py::test_pp_granite4_vision_deepstack"
```

```text
declaration fix only:  AssertionError: Results for model='ibm-granite/granite-vision-4.1-4b' are not the same.
                       (the text_image comparison; pure_text matches)
this PR:               1 passed
```

On main the same test cannot start the PP2 server (the `KeyError` above). It runs in the "(L4) Distributed" CI step, which runs the whole file. It uses dummy weights because the registry still marks this checkpoint as not available online; the real-weight runs above were done outside CI.

## Details

**Startup failure.** The deepstack and spatial features target layers 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. On a non-last stage, `Granite4VisionLLMModel.forward` forwards only `ds_<l>` with `l >= end_layer`, the features later stages inject. `Granite4VisionLLMForCausalLM.make_empty_intermediate_tensors` declared `ds_<l>` for every layer regardless of the stage, and Model Runner V2 copies every declared key from the received tensors (#42187), so the keys of earlier layers were missing. The fix declares `ds_<l>` only for `l >= start_layer`, which is exactly what the previous stage sends. The runner's strict copy is left as is: a declared key that never arrives should keep failing loudly rather than reuse a stale buffer.

**Zeroed features.** On the first stage, the forwarded `ds_<l>` are views of `_ds_buffers`. `Granite4VisionForConditionalGeneration.forward` zeroes those buffers right after the language model returns, so that stale features do not leak into the next request, and the worker sends the intermediate tensors only after the forward returns. Later stages therefore received zeros: with a 20/20 split, layer 21 lost its features, and with PP4, layers 12–21 lost theirs. Text requests are unaffected because their buffers are zero anyway. The fix forwards copies, at the cost of one `(num_tokens, hidden_size)` copy per forwarded layer.

No open PR changes this code path; #65412, the other open Granite 4.1 Vision PR, touches only the image preprocessing.

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Align GPT-OSS MXFP4 LoRA TP shards with base weights
author: linitra24
body:
## Overview

Fix GPT-OSS MXFP4 expert LoRA sharding under tensor parallelism by aligning the shard stride to 32 elements, matching the base weight loader.

## Claims

Fixes mismatched intermediate-channel slices at TP=4/8 for both 2D and 3D expert LoRA.

## Validation

Tested locally on 4× NVIDIA H20 using `openai/gpt-oss-20b` and the existing `gptoss20b_lora_files` SQL adapter.

Added a local `test_gpt_oss_lora_tp4` in `tests/lora/test_gptoss_tp.py`, configured with:
- `tensor_parallel_size=4`
- `fully_sharded_loras=True`
- `enable_expert_parallel=False`
- `moe_backend="marlin"` and `linear_backend="marlin"`

The test reuses the existing `generate_and_test` helper, prompts, and expected outputs, and exercises LoRA IDs 1 and 2.

On main, the first response is:
`SELECT AVG(Working_Horses) FROM farm WHERE Total_Horses > 5000;`

The expected response starts with:
`SELECT avg(Working_Horses) FROM farm WHERE Total_Horses > 5000`

With the fix, all responses satisfy the existing assertions. The baseline failure is a casing difference in semantically equivalent SQL.

This test was run locally and is not included in the PR.

## Details

The GPT-OSS MXFP4 loader partitions the intermediate dimension in whole 32-element quantization blocks:

`ceil((intermediate_size / 32) / tp_size) * 32`

However, LoRA previously used the unpadded per-rank size, `intermediate_size // tp_size`, as its shard stride. These values differ when the number of MXFP4 blocks is not divisible by the TP size.

For GPT-OSS-20B, `intermediate_size=2880`:

| TP size | Base weight stride | Previous LoRA stride |
|---------|--------------------|----------------------|
| 2       | 1440               | 1440                 |
| 4       | 736                | 720                  |
| 8       | 384                | 360                  |

For example, at TP=4, rank 1 loads base intermediate channels `[736:1472]`, but its LoRA factors select `[720:1440]`. Local tensor positions therefore refer to different global channels. Padding the LoRA buffers does not correct this offset, so the mismatch can produce incorrect results without a shape error.

This change rounds the LoRA shard stride up to the MXFP4 block size for `gpt_oss_mxfp4`, matching the base loader while keeping backend-specific buffer padding separate.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Only divide shared expert output in FP16 for models that compensate
author: nliu365
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65533. Since #35949, the MoE runner divides the shared expert output by `routed_scaling_factor` in FP16 (instead of scaling the routed output) whenever a model sets `apply_routed_scale_to_output=True`. That is only correct for models whose decoder layers compensate (DeepseekV2-style). GLM-4 MoE does not, so FP16 GLM-4.7 produces degenerate output on v0.20.0+. This makes the divide-shared path opt-in.

## Claims

- FP16 GLM-4.7-AWQ (`routed_scaling_factor=2.5`, one shared expert) generates correct output again; it loops on v0.20.0–v0.31.0 without this fix.
- Models that set `apply_routed_scale_to_output=True` without FP16 compensation (glm4_moe, bailing_moe_linear, laguna, nemotron_h) now get `routed * scale + shared` in FP16, matching BF16.
- No behavior change for models that compensate: `DeepseekV2MoE` (deepseek_v2, deepseek_v32, unlimited_ocr), AXK1 and OpenPangu opt in.
- No change for BF16/FP32, for layers without shared experts, or for the fused-shared-expert path (`shared_output` is `None` there).

## Validation

**Unit test** (new, `tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_scale_shared_experts.py`): real `FusedMoEFactory` layers with shared experts and `routed_scaling_factor=2.5`, compared against a routed-only layer with the same weights; FP16/BF16 × opt-in on/off. Run on CPU (macOS); CI runs it in `:nvidia: (L4) MoE Kernels`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_scale_shared_experts.py -v
```

| Source | FP16, no opt-in | BF16, no opt-in | FP16, opt-in | BF16, opt-in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (`1ab4476ac9`) | **FAILED** | passed | n/a (kwarg does not exist) | n/a |
| this PR | passed | passed | passed | passed |

<details>
<summary>Failure on main</summary>

The opt-in cases were deselected (`-k False`) and the new kwarg omitted, since it does not exist on `main`.

```
E       Mismatched elements: 2048 / 2048 (100.0%)
E       Greatest absolute difference: 4.8359375 at index (3, 95) (up to 0.001 allowed)
E       Greatest relative difference: 0.6005859375 at index (0, 40) (up to 0.001 allowed)
FAILED ...test_routed_scale_applied_to_output_with_shared_experts[False-dtype0]
1 failed, 1 passed, 2 deselected
```

A relative difference of 0.6 = 1 − 1/2.5 is the expected signature of the MoE output being scaled down by `routed_scaling_factor`.
</details>

**End-to-end** on 4× H100 80GB (TP=4): `QuantTrio/GLM-4.7-AWQ` (`torch_dtype=float16`), with the reporter's flags (`--enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192`, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`), `temperature=0`. The patched run mounts the equivalent runner change, applied to v0.31.0, over the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` image; the rest of the image is unchanged.

| Run | dtype | `1+1等于几？` | "What is 1+1? Answer in one short sentence." |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.19.0 | fp16 | `1+1等于2。` | 1+1 equals 2. |
| v0.31.0 | fp16 | `1+1等于几。\n1+1=几\n1+1=1\n1+1=1…` (until `max_tokens`) | Two. |
| v0.31.0 | bf16 | `1+1等于2。` | 1+1 equals 2. |
| **v0.31.0 + this fix** | **fp16** | **`1+1等于2。`** | One plus one equals two. |

All runs used the Marlin MoE path (no WNA16 fallback) with no errors. A release bisect (v0.20.0–v0.25.0, v0.25.1) showed every release from v0.20.0 on loops; v0.19.0 is clean.

```bash
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # all hooks passed
```

## Details

**Root cause.** Before #35949, `glm4_moe.py` passed `routed_scaling_factor=1.0` to the MoE layer and computed `routed * scale + shared` itself. #35949 moved the scaling into `MoERunner._maybe_apply_routed_scale_to_output`, which, for FP16 with shared experts, avoids overflow by computing `routed + shared / scale` and relies on the decoder layer to divide the residual and attention output by the same factor. `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer` does that; the GLM-4 decoder layer does not, so every MoE layer's contribution was `scale`× too small.

**Fix.** A new `divide_shared_output_in_fp16` argument on `FusedMoEFactory`/`MoERunner` (default `False`) gates the divide-shared path. Without it, the runner always does `fused_output *= routed_scaling_factor`, which is what GLM-4 computed before #35949 (and ran fine in FP16 on v0.19.0). Models with FP16 compensation opt in, so their numerics are unchanged. I chose this over adding DeepSeek-style compensation to GLM-4, because it fixes the unsafe default for every model rather than one, and it keeps GLM-4 on its pre-regression numerics.

**Notes for reviewers.**
- The Transformers backend already works around this edge case (`divides_shared_output` in `transformers/moe.py` refuses to fuse in FP16). It never opts in, so it is correct either way. Its guard is now overly conservative; I left it unchanged to keep this fix focused.
- I did not audit bailing_moe_linear, laguna and nemotron_h individually beyond confirming they set `apply_routed_scale_to_output=True` without FP16 compensation. They now take the same path as BF16.
- No `vllm_runner`-level test: there is no small GLM-4 MoE checkpoint under `vllm-project`. The layer test reproduces the exact arithmetic bug deterministically, and the GPU results above cover the end-to-end behavior. Happy to add a model-level test if you'd prefer one.
- The end-to-end runs used a v0.31.0 version of the runner change, not this branch, because there was no GPU build of `main`. The unit test, which CI runs on L4, has not yet run on CUDA.
- Thanks to the reporter (chenshufei6688) for the detailed analysis in #65533, which pointed at the Marlin MoE path and ruled out several Python-side causes.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR references #65533, and a keyword search (`routed_scaling_factor float16 shared`) found no related PR. The issue has no linked PR, and its only comments are mine (repro and root cause).

title: [Bugfix] Move model inspection RPC out of LLM.__repr__
author: vcdlk
body:
## Overview

Keep `LLM.__repr__` local so debugger variable inspection does not implicitly issue blocking worker RPCs. Move the existing model hierarchy inspection and cache into an explicit `LLM.get_model_inspection()` method.

## Claims

- `repr(llm)` and `print(llm)` return a local summary such as `LLM(model='Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B')` without querying workers.
- The full model hierarchy remains available through `llm.get_model_inspection()`, with the existing first-call caching behavior.
- Add an `LLM` regression test and document the explicit inspection API in the offline inference guide.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_collective_rpc.py::test_model_inspection_requires_explicit_call
```

Result from the submitter's latest local run: **1 passed, 15 warnings in 26.72s** (Python 3.12.13), using `vllm-project/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`.

The test constructs a real `LLM` with a tiny Llama checkpoint, checks the local representation, and verifies that explicit inspection returns the model hierarchy. It covers the public API behavior; the VS Code thread-blocking scenario is not automated by this test. A before-fix run of the regression test remains to be recorded.

Additional validation: the following pre-commit run passed all applicable hooks, including Ruff, Markdown lint, mypy, and test-to-CI wiring checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/llm.py \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_collective_rpc.py \
  docs/serving/offline_inference.md
```

Model evaluations are not applicable: this change affects object display and explicit inspection, without changing model execution, generation, or serving behavior.

## Details

VS Code/debugpy can call `repr()` automatically when displaying variables. Previously, the first such call on an `LLM` invoked `self.llm_engine.collective_rpc("get_model_inspection")`. If completing that RPC depends on threads or workers that are paused or blocked during debugging, variable inspection can stall waiting for the response. Caching only helps after the first successful call.

[Python's data model documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.12/reference/datamodel.html#object.__repr__) describes `__repr__` as commonly used for debugging. [debugpy maintainers explain](https://github.com/microsoft/debugpy/issues/952) that the debugger invokes `repr()` for unfamiliar types, and that a representation blocked in native I/O cannot reliably be interrupted with a Python exception. These are the reasons for keeping `LLM.__repr__` local; 

Users who need the hierarchy previously shown by `print(llm)` can now request it explicitly:

```python
print(llm.get_model_inspection())
```

The first explicit call still performs synchronous worker RPC and may block. Subsequent calls return the cached result. The existing selection of the first worker's result and local-summary fallback for an empty result are preserved.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs for `get_model_inspection`, `repr in:title`, `repr debugger`, `repr blocking`, and `61366 in:body`. Related PRs [#61414](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61414) and [#61613](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61613) address non-PyTorch model inspection errors and retain the RPC in `__repr__`. This PR addresses implicit blocking during debugger variable inspection; no open PR implementing that fix was found in those searches.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and its PR description.

This is my first contribution to vLLM. Feedback on the approach and tests is welcome, and I’m happy to address any review comments.

title: [Bugfix][CI] Fix duplicate max_num_seqs in Llama Nemotron VL pooling test
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Overview

`tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_llama_nemotron_vl.py::test_image_embeddings_without_chunked_prefill` fails on ROCm in both of its parametrisations:

```
TypeError: tests.conftest.VllmRunner() got multiple values for keyword argument 'max_num_seqs'
```

Seen in the `(MI355 DPX) Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling) Shard 1/2` step of [build 100175](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100175/list?jid=01a1aa9f-d8ba-44ee-aa29-e22baeae7304&tab=output).

The test was added in 947bd30e0b (#65399). It passes `max_num_seqs=2` directly and also unpacks `**ROCM_ENGINE_KWARGS`. That constant is empty on CUDA, so the duplicate never shows up there, but on ROCm it carries `max_num_seqs`, and Python rejects the call while binding the arguments, before the model is loaded.

## Fix

I merge the two so the explicit value wins, which keeps `enable_prefix_caching=False` from the ROCm set and leaves CUDA unchanged. The test needs `max_num_seqs=2` rather than the ROCm value of 1, since both requests have to be resident at once for the encoder cache to come under pressure, which is what the test is checking.

## Validation

On MI355X, 2 passed in 52.08 s.
