title: [ROCm][CI] Fix flaky layer 0 bound in test_dsv4_mono_layers
author: bogdan-petkovic
body:
## Overview

Raise the layer 0 bound of `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model` in `tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` from 5% to 7%. The 5% bound sits inside the run to run noise of the vLLM reference path itself, so the test fails now and then on MI355 in `(MI355) DeepSeek-V4-Pro Mono Decode Numerics`. This is a stopgap until #63486 replaces this test.

## Claims

- Fixes the flaky layer 0 check in `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model`. Every CI failure since Oct 27 is this check on the same token (prompt 5541, position 5544) at 5.04% to 5.37%, and the retry passed each time.
- Only the layer 0 bound changes. Layers 1 to 4 stay at 10% and the residual and mix checks are unchanged.

## Validation

CI failures of the layer 0 check, all passed on retry

- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97458#01a17ac4-7686-4f72-8ead-e40dd48b31e1 (5.37%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97976#01a182e3-a60b-4e26-968f-8e0402ebd6a7 (5.37%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98662#01a18c10-7a32-4ea0-aa42-c711c120ecc7 (5.22%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99438#01a19f8b-f4e6-4cda-a62c-068654353a6b (5.05%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100146#01a1aa23-6b81-4e6b-b58e-1502def2668d (5.04%)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100181#01a1aa94-8dec-4de8-99e1-5fe95c43b00c (5.05%)

Layer 0 relative error for the same decode tokens across separate runs with identical inputs and identical generated tokens (MI350X, 8 GPUs, CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1a5a4-ac64-4181-8fd7-fb84016eddd6`)

| Comparison | Median | Max |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM path against itself | 0.96% | 4.23% |
| mono path against itself | 2.75% | 4.27% |
| mono against vLLM (what the test checks) | 3.07% | 5.04% |

Before the fix, 1 of 10 local runs on MI350X failed the layer 0 check at 5.04%.

After the fix, 20 of 20 runs passed on MI355X with the same image.

```bash
pytest -q tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model
```

## Details

Layer 0 sees the same inputs on both paths, but the vLLM path is not deterministic run to run with these random weights (the comment in `_fill` already notes that the order of atomics moves vLLM's own logits). Its output moves by up to 4.3% between runs on its own, so a 5% bound between mono and vLLM leaves almost no room for the MXFP8 against FP8 difference the test is meant to allow. 7% covers the worst case seen in CI (5.37%) with some margin and still fails at once on a layer the kernels no longer follow, since layer 0 is hash routed and has no near tie exemption.

The test author confirmed the flakiness was already seen when the test was written, and the bound was set to 5% for a stable local pass.

#63486 rewrites this test with both paths on the same inputs and derived bounds, which removes this check. This PR does not overlap with it and only keeps CI stable until it lands.

The other test in the same job, `test_dsv4_mono_numerics.py::test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm`, also failed a few times recently (a replay mismatch and a NaN). That is a different problem and is not touched here.

AI assistance (Cursor) was used for the investigation and the change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [ROCm][CI] Fix flaky streaming checks in test_translation_validation
author: bogdan-petkovic
body:
## Overview

Fix the two flaky streaming checks in `tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/test_translation_validation.py` that fail now and then in `(MI355 DPX) Entrypoints Integration (Speech to Text)`. The streaming requests get an explicit 30 s timeout, and `test_streaming_response` aligns the words before counting matches instead of comparing them by position.

## Claims

- Fixes `httpx.ReadTimeout` in `test_streaming_response` and `test_stream_options`. Both used httpx's default 5 s timeout. The transcription streaming tests already use 30 s since #20913.
- Fixes `test_streaming_response` failing when one word is dropped or inserted. The 87% threshold is unchanged.
- The check also gets stricter. The old check only looked at as many words as the stream had, so an empty or truncated stream passed. It now fails.

## Validation

CI failures on MI355 DPX. All passed on retry except build 99892, where the first attempt hit the timeout and the retry hit the word check.

- ReadTimeout https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98508#01a18a4b-632f-4951-a936-46dc1ae1302f (`test_stream_options[google/gemma-3n-E2B-it]`)
- ReadTimeout https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100175#01a1aa87-b089-4f16-b28b-1425881adfbe (`test_stream_options[google/gemma-3n-E2B-it]`)
- ReadTimeout https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99892#01a1a5c7-a1cc-4cbc-9538-e19da2d0948f (`test_streaming_response[openai/whisper-small]`)
- Word check https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99609#01a1a25c-88e1-47ef-8688-a788a7fd32ab (`assert 58 >= (76 * 0.87)`)
- Word check https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99743#01a1a3d9-8dcd-491d-8688-577d1e3b1eb4 (`assert 58 >= (76 * 0.87)`)
- Word check https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99892#01a1a5de-506c-4002-a548-f77d48ab9978 (`assert 57 >= (78 * 0.87)`)

The H200 version of the job had no retries over the same period.

**Timeout.** On MI350X the largest gap between two stream chunks of `test_streaming_response[openai/whisper-small]` was 0.065 s. With the client timeout set below that gap, the test fails with the same `httpcore.ReadTimeout` and `httpx.ReadTimeout` chain as in CI. In CI the server had already answered and the stream stalled for more than 5 s in the middle. 30 s keeps a stuck server failing the test.

**Word check.** Both checks run on the real 77 word whisper translation of `foscolo`, with the same cases as in CI and a few broken streams.

| Stream | Old check (`zip`) | New check (`SequenceMatcher` ratio) |
|---|---|---|
| Same text | PASS | 1.000 PASS |
| One word dropped (the CI case) | FAIL | 0.993 PASS |
| One word inserted | FAIL | 0.994 PASS |
| Empty stream | PASS | 0.000 FAIL |
| First half only | PASS | 0.661 FAIL |
| Unrelated text | FAIL | 0.089 FAIL |

**After the fix.** 20 of 20 runs passed on MI350X (CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1a5c0-f715-44fa-97bf-62c86bea67ab`).

```bash
pytest -v entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/test_translation_validation.py -k whisper
```

`google/gemma-3n-E2B-it` is gated and I could not run it locally, so it is covered by the CI jobs of this PR.

## Details

The comment in `test_streaming_response` already says a few tokens may differ between the streaming and the non streaming request. On MI355 DPX that sometimes means one word fewer or one word more around the same spot. Comparing by position then shifts every later word, so a single word difference drops the score from about 99% to 76%. Aligning the two word lists first counts only the words that really differ. `SequenceMatcher.ratio()` is symmetric, which fits two outputs of the same model better than WER against a reference, and it keeps the 87% meaning of the existing threshold. On failure the assert now prints both texts.

Not covered here are two other rare failures in the same job, a `test_wer_correctness` outlier for `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` and GPU memory not released in time between servers.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Bound store prefix lookups with a circuit breaker
author: hj-mistral
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Bound MooncakeStoreConnector prefix lookups with a configurable deadline and a circuit breaker, so a slow or unavailable store returns cache misses instead of holding up the scheduler indefinitely.

## Claims

- `kv_connector_extra_config.lookup_timeout_s` bounds blocking, async and prefetched lookups, including executor queue time; the default is 1 second.
- Three consecutive RPC failures open the breaker for 30 seconds. After cooldown, one probe is admitted; queue expiry does not count as a store failure.
- Late replies are ignored, cached outcomes update the breaker once, and the reset RPC has a 60-second deadline.

## Validation

- 30 CPU regressions passed with `python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_lookup.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py -k 'lookup or prefetch or circuit_breaker or cached_hit' -q` in a uv-managed Python 3.12 environment. These include real local ZMQ sockets and the existing lookup/prefetch integration tests.
- Repository hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, markdownlint and test tethering.
- Real Mooncake-master and GPU validation remains pending. This stays a draft; no accuracy or performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

Incorporates Nicolò Lucchesi's adjustments from https://github.com/hj-mistral/vllm/pull/5. Configuration now uses one connector key rather than three environment variables; breaker threshold/cooldown remain constants. The breaker lives in the existing KV connector utilities, and the CPU-marked tests run in the existing V1 Others step without an extra CI job.

Queue expiry returns a cache miss without penalizing a healthy but busy master. A half-open probe prevents a recovery burst, and an abandoned probe releases its slot after one timeout window. Only new lookups are gated, allowing pending requests to read their results.

The reset request reuses the bounded socket helper and allows longer for the server to drain saves. Its existing caller contract still requires in-flight work to be drained before reset. This change bounds client waits; it does not cancel an RPC already executing on the master or change KV load/save behavior.

Two existing integration tests were aligned with the multipart reset helper and the new default: the TTL test explicitly keeps its RPC deadline beyond its simulated TTL expiry.

title: [Bugfix] Map compressed-tensors KV-cache scale names for GPT-J
author: HollowMan6
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #65945.

LLM Compressor stores GPT-J's FP8 KV-cache scales on the HF attention module, as `transformer.h.<i>.attn.{k,v}_scale`. In vLLM that module's `Attention` layer is its child, also named `attn`. The default cache-scale rule skips names that already end in `.attn.k_scale`, so these scales are never placed. They are then dropped with only a DEBUG message, and attention runs with 1.0.

This PR adds a GPT-J-specific rule to `GPTJForCausalLM.hf_to_vllm_mapper`. It maps `.attn.{q,k,v}_scale` and the `*_zero_point` variants to `.attn.attn.<suffix>`. The rule leaves alone names already in vLLM form, and the deprecated `.attn.kv_scale`, which the generic rule already handles. Only GPT-J changes.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -k "KvCacheScaleMapper"
```
plus the self-contained repro script from #65945.

## Test Result

- **New test:** 4 of its 7 cases fail before the change; all 7 pass after.
- **Nearby suites:** 79 passed, and `ruff` reports no problems.
- **Repro:** the attention layers now apply the checkpoint scales (layer 0: 0.5 / 0.25; layer 1: 0.75 / 0.375) instead of 1.0 / 1.0.
- **ModelOpt-named checkpoints:** they still fail loudly, as described in the issue; this is unchanged.

**Why this is not a duplicate.** No open PR references #65945, and `gh pr list --state open --search` for "gptj kv scale" and "gpt_j k_scale" finds no PR that changes GPT-J's KV-cache scale names.

Parts of this change were drafted with AI assistance and reviewed and tested by the author.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Accept Anthropic thinking.type=between_tools on the Messages API
author: albertoperdomo2
body:
## Overview

The Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) rejects `thinking: {"type": "between_tools"}`
with HTTP 400 `union_tag_invalid`, because `AnthropicThinkingConfig` admits only
`enabled`, `disabled` and `adaptive`. This change accepts `between_tools` and maps it
to disabled thinking, matching the Anthropic SDK semantics. It also fixes the same
rejection on `/v1/messages/count_tokens`, which shares the union.

## Claims

- `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` accept `thinking: {"type": "between_tools"}`
  instead of returning `union_tag_invalid`.
- `between_tools` maps to disabled upfront thinking: `reasoning_effort` is set to the
  resolved disabled-thinking effort (`"none"`, or the configured low-effort fallback for
  models that cannot turn thinking off).
- `enabled`, `disabled` and `adaptive` behavior, budget validation, thinking history and
  tool-use/result continuations are unchanged.
- The mapping and its limits are documented on the rendered reasoning page.

## Validation

Changed-file checks, all clean:

```
git diff --check
ruff check <changed files>
ruff format --check <changed files>
```

Focused tests through the native Messages entry point (FastAPI `TestClient` +
`attach_router`), with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`:

```
pytest -q tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py
```

Result: `141 passed, 3 failed`. The three failures are
`TestDetectMergeInlineSystem::test_probes_non_jinja_renderer[*]`, which fetch model
configuration from the Hugging Face hub; they fail identically on the base revision and
are unrelated to this change (the validation host has no network).

Regression discrimination: the eight `between_tools` tests (conversion, fallback,
`count_tokens` parity, tool round trip, streaming parity, native entry point, resolver)
all fail on the base revision with `union_tag_invalid` and pass on this change.

## Details

### Root cause

`AnthropicThinkingConfig` (`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py`) is a Pydantic
discriminated union over `type` admitting `enabled`, `disabled` and `adaptive`. A
`between_tools` request fails validation before reaching the handler, so the endpoint
returns 400.

### Design

The SDK definition (`anthropic` `ThinkingTypes.between_tools`) is "thinking turned off,
and any short progress updates the model writes between tool calls come back as thinking
blocks". That is disabled thinking up front, so `between_tools` maps to the existing
`disabled` path rather than to `adaptive`:

- `AnthropicThinkingConfigBetweenTools` is added to the union.
- `_handle_thinking` treats `between_tools` like `disabled`, setting `req.reasoning_effort`
  to the resolved disabled-thinking effort.
- `DisabledThinkingEffortResolver.resolve_for` resolves the effort for `between_tools` as
  well, so the model/template compatibility probe (the `--anthropic-disabled-thinking-effort`
  fallback) applies. Its CLI help now names both types.
- `adaptive` is untouched: it pins nothing and leaves the `output_config.effort` ceiling to
  the model.

### Limits

vLLM has no request-level control over *when* a model reasons, only whether thinking is on
and its budget, so the type cannot force a model to emit progress notes strictly between
tool calls; whether reasoning appears there depends on the model and chat template. Because
the resolved effort applies to every round including tool continuations, a template that
honors `"none"` suppresses thinking in those rounds too. Any reasoning the model does emit
is still returned as thinking blocks. Models that reason between tool calls are described in
`docs/features/interleaved_thinking.md`.

### Tests

Added to `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`: `between_tools`
acceptance through the native entry point, converted settings matching disabled, the
disabled-effort fallback, `count_tokens` parity, a full tool round trip that preserves echoed
thinking and `tool_result` blocks, streaming settings parity, and resolver fallback.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject Anthropic max_tokens=0 prewarm with an actionable error
author: albertoperdomo2
body:
## Overview

The Anthropic Messages route rejects `max_tokens=0` with a bare `max_tokens must be positive`. This makes the failure actionable: it names the prompt-cache pre-warming contract the client asked for and the supported workaround.

## Claims

- `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/render` reject `max_tokens=0` with a 400 whose message says `max_tokens=0 (prompt-cache pre-warming) is not supported` and points at `max_tokens=1`.
- Negative limits keep their existing `max_tokens must be positive` message; positive limits are unchanged and still reach the handler.
- The rejection is documented in the Anthropic serving docs and the Claude Code integration page.

## Validation

Focused route tests added in `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` (`TestZeroTokenPrewarm`) and run against the pushed revision: `test_zero_token_request_is_rejected_by_messages_route[False]` (non-streaming), `test_zero_token_request_is_rejected_by_messages_route[True]` (streaming), `test_negative_max_tokens_are_rejected_by_messages_route`, `test_positive_max_tokens_still_reaches_messages_handler`. All four pass, and the `TestCacheSalt` tests still pass.

Run with: `PYTHONPATH=$PWD uv run --no-project --with-requirements requirements/common.txt --with pytest --with tblib --with pytest-asyncio --with ray python -m pytest -q tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k "ZeroTokenPrewarm or CacheSalt"`.

Each test passes and the interpreter then segfaults in the shared `tests/conftest.py` teardown (`cleanup_dist_env_and_memory` -> `torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache`), which also happens on this machine without the change; it is an environment issue, not the test body.

No model evaluation is included: the change does not alter generated output for any request that previously succeeded.

## Details

True pre-warming is not supported here. Anthropic's API accepts `max_tokens: 0` to populate the prompt cache without generating a response; vLLM requires at least one sampled token per request, enforced in `vllm/sampling_params.py` (`max_tokens must be at least 1`). Generating a token and discarding it to synthesize the Anthropic contract would still bill and account one output token, which is the accounting the caller relies on when it asks for zero, so the change documents explicit rejection instead of pretending to pre-warm.

The workaround that is documented, `max_tokens=1`, does generate one output token and bill it as output. It warms the prefix cache through normal automatic prefix caching. It is not usable when thinking is enabled: `max_tokens=1` with `thinking.budget_tokens=1024` is rejected because `thinking.budget_tokens` must be less than `max_tokens`.

Changed surface: `AnthropicMessagesRequest.validate_max_tokens` distinguishes `0` from negative values; `docs/serving/online_serving/README.md` and `docs/serving/integrations/claude_code.md` note the rejection. Sampling, engine caching and the other API surfaces are untouched.

Read-only upstream searches for `max_tokens=0`, Anthropic pre-warming and cache prewarm found no existing issue or pull request covering this, so the change does not duplicate open work.

## Limitations

Zero-token pre-warming still returns 400; this change only makes the error actionable and documents the workaround. There is no test that exercises a real prefix-cache warm, which needs GPU hardware.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Build the tied embedding on the last PP rank for ERNIE 4.5 MoE and Falcon-H1
author: xsxszab
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix pipeline-parallel startup failures for ERNIE 4.5 MoE and Falcon-H1 checkpoints with tied word embeddings.

#66291 (RFC #66290) registers the ERNIE 4.5 MoE failure as a strict xfail; whichever of the two PRs merges second removes that entry.

## Claims

- Create the embedding on the last pipeline stage so `lm_head` can share its weight.
- Restrict ERNIE weight tying to the last pipeline stage.
- Add PP=2 regression coverage for Falcon-H1 and ERNIE 4.5 MoE.

## Validation

Run the regression test on two GPUs:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py::test_pp_tied_word_embeddings
```

Both cases run PP=1 and PP=2 with eight prompts, greedy decoding, eight output tokens, and top-5 logprobs:

| Case | Configuration | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `falcon_h1` | `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct`, real weights | Startup and generation comparison using `check_logprobs_close` |
| `ernie45_moe` | `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT`, two layers and four experts, dummy weights | Startup and generation smoke test |

On 2× B300, both cases failed before the fix and passed with the fix (`2 passed`, 313.62s).

Serving validation with real checkpoints on 2× B300 compared PP=2 prompt logprobs against PP=1:

| Model | Before fix, PP=2 | With fix, PP=2 versus PP=1 |
|---|---|---|
| `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` | Startup failed | 461 positions; mean absolute logprob difference 0.0166, maximum 0.246; prompt NLL 1.0465 versus 1.0472; same greedy text |
| `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct` | Startup failed | Identical logprobs across 493 positions |

The existing Pipeline + Context Parallelism CI step runs this test file: nightly on NVIDIA L4 and on PRs through its AMD MI250 mirror.

## Details

These models created `embed_tokens` only on the first pipeline stage. With `tie_word_embeddings=True`, the last stage tried to tie `lm_head` to a `PPMissingLayer` and raised an `AttributeError` for `weight`. ERNIE 4.5 MoE also called `tie_weights` on non-final stages, where `lm_head` was a `PPMissingLayer`.

Following the existing Llama and Qwen2 pattern, tied models now create `embed_tokens` on both the first and last stages. The last stage loads `model.embed_tokens.weight` from the checkpoint and shares it with `lm_head`. ERNIE's `tie_weights` call moves inside the last-stage branch; Falcon-H1 already performs tying there.

ERNIE 4.5 VL MoE (`baidu/ERNIE-4.5-VL-28B-A3B-PT`) fails at startup the same way but is left unchanged. With the embedding fixed, its later stages would still route image and video tokens to the text experts, because the visual-token mask is set only while the first stage embeds the inputs. It keeps failing at startup until that is fixed separately.

title: [Bugfix] Make fused MoE expert weights contiguous before GPU copy in Llama-4
author: yuvalluria
body:
Fixes #31624.

## Summary

In `load_moe_expert_weights`, a sliced/transposed fused MoE expert weight view is passed to `weight_loader()` and copied to GPU while still non-contiguous. A non-contiguous CPU tensor's DMA transfer to GPU is dramatically slower than a contiguous one. Adds `.contiguous()` right before the `weight_loader()` call, on the already-sliced piece — not upfront on the whole weight, since a prior attempt at this fix (#32081, auto-closed by staleness, not rejected) found that naive blanket `.contiguous()` can regress smaller tensors.

## Scope note

A synthetic benchmark on H100 NVL (the real Llama-4 checkpoints, 109B-400B, don't fit on one GPU) tested three locations that could have the same issue. Only the fused MoE expert weight path (this PR) showed an unambiguous, large improvement — FP8 block-scale and Q/K rotary permute tensors were *slower* with `.contiguous()` added at their (smaller) sizes in isolation. Since MoE expert weights dominate total checkpoint bytes, this is the change with validated, measured benefit; the other two locations are deliberately excluded pending more precise real-world sizing data.

## Validation

```
torch 2.6.0a0+df5bbc09d1.nv24.11 | GPU: NVIDIA H100 NVL
=== fused MoE expert weight, basic-indexed view after transpose(-1,-2), shape [64,4096,1024] ===
non-contiguous transfer: mean=574.401ms min=536.849ms max=585.899ms
contiguous() transfer:   mean=28.911ms min=24.788ms max=103.387ms
speedup: 19.87x
```
(A first run on the same shape measured 22.35x; 19.87x on a clean isolated re-run — consistent within normal GPU/CPU scheduling noise.)

title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Read per-layer embeddings on later pipeline stages
author: xsxszab
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix corrupted output from Gemma 4 models with per-layer embeddings (PLE) under pipeline parallelism by loading the PLE tensor received from the preceding stage.

## Claims

- Restore PLE consumption on every pipeline stage in the shared Gemma 4 text and multimodal model implementation.
- Add a PP=2 versus PP=1 generation regression test for `google/gemma-4-E2B`.

## Validation

Run the regression test on two GPUs:

  tests/models/language/generation/test_gemma.py::test_gemma4_per_layer_embeddings_pipeline_parallel

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Support AITER's preload() in FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce init
author: amd-sriram
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Since #65937 (merged 2026-11-06) vLLM main pins AITER v0.1.28.post1, and with it every ROCm worker dies at start-up when INT4 QuickReduce is on, because ROCm/aiter#5461 renamed `QuickAllReduceInt4.compile()` to `preload()`; this calls `preload()` when `compile()` is gone. #65628 carries the same check inside a larger feature PR; this is the standalone fix, co-authored with @eppaneamd.

## Claims

- ROCm serving with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` and TP > 1 starts again on AITER with #5461.
- No change on AITER without #5461 (v0.1.27 and older): the `compile()` branch runs as before.

## Validation

**Reproduction** (vLLM main + AITER main `20455aa6`, which has #5461; MI355X, TP4). Any TP > 1 server with these two variables hits the same init path; the exact command run is below.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 ...
```

```
File ".../device_communicators/quick_all_reduce.py", line 280, in _init_flydsl_int4
    flydsl_int4.compile(warmup, torch.empty_like(warmup))
AttributeError: 'QuickAllReduceInt4' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

With this PR, the same server starts and serves (`POST /v1/completions 200`), and every worker logs the FlyDSL path:

```
INFO [quick_all_reduce.py:289] Using AITER FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce for BF16 payloads; other payloads use the HIP QuickReduce kernels.
```

**Unit test**: `pytest tests/distributed/test_rocm_quick_reduce.py -k "flydsl_int4 or two_gpu_correctness"`, 2x MI355X (gfx950), vLLM nightly `a2bcb565`:

| AITER | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| main `20455aa6` (has `preload()`) | 1 failed, 4 passed (`AttributeError` above) | 5 passed |
| `269675de` (has `compile()`, before #5461) | 5 passed | 5 passed |

The new case `test_quick_allreduce_two_gpu_flydsl_int4` asserts the FlyDSL INT4 object was built (the path under test ran, not the HIP fallback) and checks a BF16 all-reduce result.

<details>
<summary>Full server command</summary>

```bash
SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MOE_DISPATCH_POLICY=0 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=0 \
AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 AITER_DISABLE_FLYDSL_TOPK_DECODE=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla": true}, "use_inductor_graph_partition": true}' \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4, "index_share_for_mtp_iteration": false}'
```

</details>

## Details

- `compile(inp, out)` built the kernels and ran one all-reduce on every rank, to keep the JIT out of the first prefill and out of CUDA graph capture. `preload()` only builds and loads the kernels (local to the rank), so one warm-up `allreduce()` follows it. Every rank runs this init, so the collective stays matched.
- `hasattr` keeps both AITER versions working; the `compile()` branch can be dropped once the pin is past #5461.
- Arch: only CDNA3/CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950) reach this code (`is_flydsl_quick_reduce_available`); RDNA, gfx1250, CUDA and AITER-off paths are unchanged.
- Test: one new case in the existing `test_rocm_quick_reduce.py` (the existing two-GPU cases run with AITER off and never reach this init). That file runs in the existing distributed AMD CI step.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Build multimodal prefix-LM attention ranges on every PP stage
author: xsxszab
body:
## Overview

With Model Runner V2 and pipeline parallelism, multimodal prefix-LM models (Gemma3, PaliGemma, and others with `is_mm_prefix_lm`) lose bidirectional attention over image tokens on every PP stage after the first. `DefaultModelState.prepare_attn` reads the image ranges from the encoder cache, but the model runner creates the encoder cache only on the first PP rank. Later stages build causal-only attention metadata, and the output is silently wrong.

## Claims

- Gemma3 with PP=2 now matches PP=1. Before the fix, prompt logprobs differed by about 10 on average.
- PP=1 output is unchanged: bit-identical with and without the fix.
- Each request's ranges are computed once when the request is added, instead of on every step.

## Validation

Run on 2x B300 with MRV2, at an upstream main commit from 2026-11-04 (`da0b6ac221`). The changed file is identical there and on current main. The cluster has no HF token, so I ran with `unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it`, an ungated mirror with the same weights. The test uses `google/gemma-3-4b-it`.

New test: `test_mm_prefix_lm_pipeline_parallel`. It sends one image request with PP=1 and with PP=2 and compares the prompt logprobs.

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py::test_mm_prefix_lm_pipeline_parallel
```

Before the fix:
```
E   AssertionError: PP=2 prompt logprobs differ from PP=1: mean_diff=9.687689781188965
1 failed, 4 warnings in 215.73s
```

After the fix:
```
1 passed, 4 warnings in 108.74s
```

Gemma3-4b-it, the test prompt with two images (stop sign, cherry blossom), greedy, 32 tokens. Prompt logprobs over 280 positions, compared with PP=1:

| Run | mean abs diff | max abs diff | greedy tokens equal to PP=1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| PP=2, main | 9.69 / 7.79 | 50.1 / 42.7 | 3/32, 2/32 |
| PP=2, this PR, one request at a time | 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.000 / 0.000 | 32/32, 32/32 |
| PP=1, this PR vs main | 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.000 / 0.000 | 32/32, 32/32 |

When both requests are sent in one batch, PP=1 and PP=2 schedule them differently. The second request then differs by 0.24 mean, both with and without the fix. PP=1 shows the same 0.24 difference between batched and one-at-a-time runs, so this is normal batch variance and not related to PP. The test sends one request so the batch is the same for both PP sizes.

Earlier end-to-end check through the OpenAI server (chat request with one image, PP=2 vs PP=1, prompt logprobs at image positions): main mean 8.16, max 30.29, greedy reply 19/48 tokens equal. With a first version of this fix: mean 0.113, max 0.620, 48/48 equal. Text-only prompts were unchanged.

CI: the L4 "Distributed Models" step runs `pytest models/multimodal -m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)'`, which selects the new test. I added `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/default.py` to that step's `source_file_dependencies`. I did not run the test on L4.

## Details

`DefaultModelState` now keeps a `req_id -> ranges` dict, filled in `add_request` and cleared in `remove_request`. Both hooks run on every PP rank, and resumed requests come back through `add_request` in MRV2. `prepare_attn` only maps the ranges to batch indices. The arguments to `compute_mm_prefix_ranges` are unchanged.

The dict holds the ranges, not the `mm_features`. The features carry the image data, and keeping them would hold image tensors on later stages for the whole request. M-RoPE models (Qwen-VL family) are not affected by this bug, because their positions are already built from `new_req_data.mm_features` on every rank.

#56813 caches the same ranges per request inside `EncoderCache` for speed. That keeps them on the first rank only, so it does not fix PP, and it edits the same lines. #63033 adds a similar per-request dict to `DefaultModelState` for PaliGemma prompt lengths.

`test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py` and `test_mrope_prompt_embeds.py` build the model state without `__init__`, and the fixture in `test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py` uses a `MagicMock` config, so these tests now set `mm_prefix_ranges` or `supports_multimodal_inputs` explicitly.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and run the validation. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

title: [Bugfix][Step5][Spec Decode] Skip VllmConfig re-validation for the MTP draft config
author: xsxszab
body:
## Overview

Fix NVIDIA Step5 MTP startup with pipeline parallelism and preserve the target's resolved CUDA graph settings when constructing the draft config view. Reuse the derived-view handling introduced in #58212.

## Claims

- Step5 MTP starts with PP > 1 without validating the `Step5MTP` architecture against the target's pipeline size.
- Constructing the draft view preserves the target's `cudagraph_mode` and `use_breakable_cudagraph` settings.
- The view retains the draft's HF config and the target's shared runtime configs without modifying the original `draft_model_config`.

## Validation

Serving and evaluation used `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview` (FP8) on NVIDIA B300, Model Runner V2, expert parallelism, three speculative tokens, and prefix caching disabled.

| Configuration | Startup | GSM8K accuracy | MTP acceptance rate | Mean acceptance length |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PP2 × TP2, before fix | `NotImplementedError` | — | — | — |
| PP2 × TP2, this PR | OK | 0.931 | 0.765 | 3.294 |
| PP1 × TP4, before fix | OK | 0.929 | 0.766 | 3.297 |
| PP1 × TP4, this PR | OK | 0.929 | 0.764 | 3.292 |

**CUDA graph capture, PP1 × TP4 with MTP:**

| | Before fix | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CUDA graph mode | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` |
| Graph memory | 0.69 GiB | 4.74 GiB |
| KV cache capacity | 983,723 tokens | 925,755 tokens |

The fixed run retains the same graph mode as the deployment without MTP. Restoring piecewise prefill graphs increases graph memory and reduces the space available for KV cache.

**Prompt logprobs, PP1 × TP4:** six fixed prompts, 418 positions, `prompt_logprobs=0`. Each row compares MTP enabled against MTP disabled under the listed graph setting.

| Code / graph setting | Mean absolute logprob difference | Maximum absolute logprob difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| This PR / default | 0 | 0 |
| This PR / `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | 0 | 0 |
| Before fix / default | 0.048 | 4.04 |
| Before fix / `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | 0 | 0 |

**Serving throughput, PP1 × TP4:** random 2,048-token inputs and 256-token outputs, one run per configuration.

| Concurrency | Prompts | Output tok/s, before → after | TTFT, before → after | TPOT, before → after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 256 | 1008.5 → 1064.3 | 1183 → 1146 ms | 57.6 → 54.6 ms |
| 8 | 64 | 239.0 → 251.7 | 327 → 241 ms | 31.4 → 30.1 ms |

**Regression tests:** `test_mtp_config_view` builds real Step5 engine configs at PP1 and PP2 using config downloads and `load_format="dummy"`, then constructs the MTP view. It checks draft HF-config identity, shared parallel-config identity, preservation of the original draft config's flag, and unchanged target graph settings.

| Test | Before fix | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_mtp_config_view[1]` | Graph-mode assertion fails | Passed |
| `test_mtp_config_view[2]` | PP validation raises `NotImplementedError` | Passed |
| Entire `tests/models/step5` suite | — | 15 passed, 17 ROCm-only tests skipped |

The existing `:nvidia: (H200) Step5` CI step selects the new test through `pytest -v -s models/step5`. Full-checkpoint serving, GSM8K, logprob, and throughput measurements above ran on B300 outside CI.

<details>
<summary>Regression output</summary>

```text
# Before fix
FAILED models/step5/test_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_config_view[1] - AssertionError: assert <CUDAGraphMode.FULL_DECODE_ONLY: (2, 0)> == <CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE: (2, 1)>
FAILED models/step5/test_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_config_view[2] - NotImplementedError: Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model. ...

# This PR
models/step5/test_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_config_view[1] PASSED
models/step5/test_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_config_view[2] PASSED
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Run from the repository root with the vLLM environment activated:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2
```

For PP1 × TP4, use `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 1`. For the no-MTP comparison, omit `--speculative-config`. Repeat the logprob comparisons with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` set on both server runs.

```bash
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 \
  --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 \
  --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8 --ignore-eos

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/models/step5/test_mtp_config.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/models/step5
```

The logprob comparison uses `/v1/completions` with identical prompts, `max_tokens=1`, `temperature=0`, and `prompt_logprobs=0`.

</details>

## Details

`_get_mtp_vllm_config()` replaces the target's `model_config` with the draft's config while retaining the target's parallel, cache, and compilation config objects. Since `replace()` reconstructs the dataclass, it re-enters `VllmConfig.__post_init__` with the draft architecture and the target's deployment settings.

This causes two failures:

1. At PP > 1, `verify_with_parallel_config()` rejects `Step5MTP`, even though the MTP head runs entirely on the last stage.
2. With default CUDA graph settings, `Step5MTP` is absent from the breakable-graph default list. Initialization disables breakable graphs and downgrades the shared graph mode from `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, changing the target's configuration after its model has been constructed.

The helper now shallow-copies the initialized draft `ModelConfig`, marks the copy with `is_submodel_config=True`, and creates the view through the existing early-return path. The draft retains its HF config objects, and the runtime configs retain their resolved values. The docstring and early-return comment now describe both submodule and draft views.

#58212 introduced this mechanism for `with_hf_config()` views. #56936 addresses the same reinitialization pattern in the Gemma4 speculator. Open-PR searches found no other change fixing the NVIDIA Step5 MTP config view.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and validation (Claude), and for code review and description editing (Codex).

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix GraniteMoeHybrid pipeline-parallel startup
author: xsxszab
body:
## Overview

Fix GraniteMoeHybrid startup under pipeline parallelism by loading and executing only the decoder layers assigned to each stage. This resolves the weight-loading failure in #50961 and the forward-pass failure that follows it.

Fixes #50961. Incorporates the loader guard from #50962 by @nikJ13, credited as co-author.

## Claims

- GraniteMoeHybrid loads and generates with PP=2.
- PP=2 passes the existing `check_logprobs_close` comparison against PP=1 on `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-tiny-preview`.
- PP=1 retains the same parameter loading and decoder execution order.
- The PP=4 equivalence tests pass for GraniteMoeHybrid and ERNIE 4.5 MoE with their strict xfail entries removed.

## Validation

### Regression tests

The new `test_pipeline_parallel_correctness` compares PP=1 and PP=2 using `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-tiny-preview`, the same prompts, greedy decoding, up to 64 output tokens, top-5 logprobs, and chunked prefill enabled. The MoE checkpoint exercises router-to-gate weight loading and both Mamba and attention layers.

The test uses `check_logprobs_close`: at the first generated-token mismatch, each selected token must appear in the other run's top-k logprobs.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py::test_pipeline_parallel_correctness
```

Results on 2 × B300 with Model Runner V2, against baseline `da0b6ac221`:

| Code | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline + new test | Weight loading fails with `KeyError` for `layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight` on PP rank 1 and `layers.20.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight` on PP rank 0 |
| Baseline + this PR | 1 passed in 293 s |

The model and generation-test files are identical between the baseline and upstream `86fdabec0c`. The existing 2-GPU **Distributed Models** CI step selects the new test and covers both files in its source dependencies.

The GraniteMoeHybrid and ERNIE 4.5 MoE PP=4 equivalence tests also pass on 4 × B300 with their xfail entries removed. Both run in the nightly 4-GPU step.

```bash
VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  "tests/models/test_pp_equivalence.py::test_pp_equivalence_middle_stages[Ernie4_5_MoeForCausalLM]" \
  "tests/models/test_pp_equivalence.py::test_pp_equivalence_middle_stages[GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM]"
```

### Serving validation

`ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny`, TP=1, with default compilation and CUDA graph settings:

| Code | PP=2 behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | Weight loading fails with `KeyError` |
| Loader guard only | Loading succeeds; forward fails with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` |
| Both fixes | Starts and generates |

With both fixes, compared with PP=1:

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Mean absolute prompt-logprob difference | 0.0258 |
| Maximum absolute prompt-logprob difference | 0.444 |
| Mean NLL, PP=2 / PP=1 | 1.1858 / 1.1827 |
| Identical greedy completions | 6 of 7 |

## Details

`make_layers()` constructs decoder layers in `[start_layer, end_layer)` and fills the remaining positions with `PPMissingLayer` placeholders. Each rank processes the full checkpoint.

- **Loading:** `load_weights()` skips other stages' layers with one `is_pp_missing_parameter()` check per checkpoint entry; every rename keeps the `layers.N.` prefix.
- **Execution:** the forward loop previously called every entry in `self.layers`. A `PPMissingLayer` returns the first keyword argument, `positions`, instead of a `(hidden_states, residual)` pair. Using `islice(self.layers, self.start_layer, self.end_layer)` restricts execution to local layers. The unused attention counter is removed.

The PR also removes two strict xfail entries introduced by #66291 (RFC #66290): GraniteMoeHybrid, fixed here, and ERNIE 4.5 MoE, already fixed by the merged #65983.

AI assistance was used for implementation and test development (Claude), and for code review and description editing (Codex).

title: [Sleep Mode] Level 2 discards only parameters
author: aoshen02
body:
## Overview

Level 2 frees GPU memory by not keeping what can be rebuilt, and the only thing rebuilt on wake is what the weight update writes: parameters. Today it discards everything allocated while the model was built, because the weights pool wraps model construction. The rest then has to be rescued one site at a time: buffers by name, and everything held some other way is lost. With this change `sleep(level=2)` states what the caller rewrites and keeps the rest, at the same address. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477, F11).

This replaces this PR's earlier site-by-site fixes (MXFP4 permute cache, DeepSeek-V4.1 `permute_on_load`, GEMM-RS/AR), which are reverted here because the rule covers them.

## Failures this addresses

All come from non-parameter state in the weights pool. Measured on GB200 without any fix:

| State | How it is held | Failure after a level-2 wake |
|---|---|---|
| GEMM-RS/AR peer pointer table from `symm_mem.rendezvous` | Inside the torch handle | Table reads all zeros, then `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` on the first forward. Kimi-K3 placeholder weights, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with GEMM-RS |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `permute_on_load` indices | Weight loader closure | GSM8K 0.90 → 0.0, and later reloads don't repair it |
| MXFP4 TRT-LLM permute cache | Quant method attribute | gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.375 → 0.0 |

The same pattern is in code but not measured: Inkling and Beam peer tables, DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram handles (#64922), plain attributes (#60009), attention impl state (#62634).

## Change

- `CuMemAllocator.sleep` and `XpuMemAllocator.sleep` take `discardable`: a weights allocation is discarded only if every live block in it starts at an address in `discardable`. An address that doesn't match keeps the allocation, so a wrong match costs host memory, not state.
- `Worker.sleep(level=2)` passes the storage addresses of the parameters the update rewrites, through `SleepModeBackend.suspend(discardable)`. That replaces `level`, which said the same thing: nothing discardable is level 1. It changes a plugin interface, so an out-of-tree backend must follow.

Kept tensors stay in `weights` and return on `wake_up(["weights"])`, so tags keep their meaning. Level 1 is unchanged.

## Removed

These existed to survive level 2, which now keeps them:

- Model state in the runtime pool (#63548), LoRA state in the runtime pool (#62358), and the MiniMax-M3 MSA prefill workspace in the runtime pool (#64856). All three are built during `load_model`; none is a parameter.
- The CPU copies of `named_buffers()`, on every platform.
- The separate CPU save and restore of `sleep_preserve_parameter_names`. Preserved parameters are now just not discardable, so their backup goes through the allocator: pinned where `PIN_MEMORY` is on, instead of pageable, and kept across wake for reuse.

Left in place: buffers registered for this reason (they are still correct as buffers), and the KV-init and CUDA graph runtime pools, which are outside `load_model`.

## Not covered

- Parameters the update doesn't write, such as those absent from the checkpoint: still discarded, as today. `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` is for those.
- `discard(tags)`: unchanged. Its only caller passes `kv_cache`.
- Weight-derived tensors that post-load processing doesn't refresh now keep old values instead of garbage. That is a separate bug class.


## Validation

Every run is the RL cycle: `sleep(level=2)` → `wake_up(["weights"])` → update → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`. Nightly `a2bcb5657a` with Python files overlaid. GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions unless noted. Code at 33056538ad and e82bcb85c4; later commits change only docs and comments and merge main.

**Weights over NCCL, through the state-transition verifier.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GB300, TP4, 2 updates, every tensor sent except the Engram embedding tables. The fixed-token oracle compares logprobs before and after.

| Code | GSM8K before → after | Oracle | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9007 → **0.0** | Differs | 28331 |
| Earlier site-by-site fixes | 0.9045 → 0.9037 | Same | 28323 |
| | 0.9030 → 0.9067 | Same | 28329 |
| This PR | 0.9067 → 0.8923 | Same | 28322 |
| | 0.9022 → 0.9098 | Same | 28327 |
| | 0.9007 → 0.8984 | Same | 28328 |

Across the three runs of this PR GSM8K moves -1.44, +0.76 and -0.23 points. The noise between identical runs here is about 1.5 points.

**Reload from disk**, GB200, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 3 cycles. "Differing" compares tensors per rank with a real cold start.

| Model | Code | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 | Differing | Job |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | This PR, real start | 0.9052 → 0.9060 → 0.9037 | 0 / 160 experts | 46269 |
| | This PR, dummy start | — → 0.9030 → 0.9014 | 0 / 160 experts | 46269 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark | main | 0.9022 → **0.0** → **0.0** | 160 / 160 experts | 46346 |

title: [Bugfix] Do not retry safetensors metadata lookup in offline mode
author: Hrushikesh-ramilla
body:
## Overview
Fixes #66006.

When `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, calling `hf_api().get_safetensors_metadata(...)` raises `huggingface_hub.errors.OfflineModeIsEnabled`. In `try_get_safetensors_metadata`, `with_retry` was not including `OfflineModeIsEnabled` in `fatal_errors`, treating it as a transient failure and attempting retries with a 2-second sleep delay and logging two spurious `ERROR` messages before falling back to reading the cached snapshot headers.

This PR adds `OfflineModeIsEnabled` to `fatal_errors`, allowing offline mode to raise immediately and proceed straight to the local cache fallback without retry delays or error logs.

## Claims
- Eliminates spurious `ERROR ... offline mode is enabled` logs during offline speculative draft model initialization.
- Eliminates the 2-second retry sleep during startup in offline mode.
- Immediately proceeds to reading metadata from the pre-populated local cache snapshot.

## Validation
- Added `test_safetensors_metadata_offline_mode_does_not_retry` to `tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py` asserting that `get_safetensors_metadata` is called exactly once when `OfflineModeIsEnabled` is raised.
- Ran tests in `tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py`.
- Formatted and linted with `ruff check` and `ruff format`.

## Details
In `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`, `try_get_safetensors_metadata` wraps the Hub metadata call with `with_retry(..., fatal_errors=(huggingface_hub.errors.NotASafetensorsRepoError,))`. In offline mode, the error is definitive rather than transient. Adding `huggingface_hub.errors.OfflineModeIsEnabled` to `fatal_errors` ensures immediate failure without logging or delay, which is then cleanly handled by `except Exception: return None` so `get_safetensors_params_metadata` proceeds directly to `snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)`.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Stop DeepGEMM's MLOPart helper once MegaMoE caches its SM map
author: galletas1712
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepGEMM MegaMoE leaves an MPS helper process tree alive in every worker for the whole serving lifetime. This makes MegaMoE workers impossible to checkpoint with CUDA checkpoint (as used by [NVIDIA Snapshot](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/snapshot)). This PR stops the helper as soon as DeepGEMM has cached what MegaMoE needs from it. Context: ai-dynamo/snapshot#859.

## Claims

- After startup, a `deep_gemm_mega_moe` worker no longer keeps the DeepGEMM MLOPart helper, MPS control daemon and MPS server alive (8 + 8 + 8 processes on DEP8 → 0).
- MegaMoE kernels read the same cached SM locality-domain map as before, so serving behavior is unchanged: GSM8K and throughput are within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (rev `2cba9e42`), 8×B200, driver 615.71.09, `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0`, DEP8 with `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'` (the B200 `single_node_dep` recipe flags). "Patched" is the same image with this one-file change mounted over `deep_gemm_mega_moe.py`. `get_symm_buffer()` is identical on v0.33.0 and main apart from this change. The two variants were run alternately on the same node.

| Run (in order) | MPS helper trees after startup | GSM8K 5-shot (1319) | Output tok/s, 3 runs | Mean TPOT ms, 3 runs |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| stock | 8 | 90.30% | 5727 / 5944 / 5974 | 9.90 / 9.82 / 9.84 |
| patched | 0 | 90.22% | 5824 / 6057 / 6110 | 9.71 / 9.66 / 9.65 |
| stock | 8 | 90.22% | 5874 / 6443 / 6491 | 9.44 / 9.09 / 9.07 |
| patched | 0 | 90.90% | 6206 / 6469 / 6362 | 9.14 / 9.10 / 9.11 |

Throughput drifts upward across the sequence for both variants. Stock and patched alternate in the lead, so there is no regression.

The same A/B on Vera Rubin: 4x VR200 (compute capability 10.7, driver 620.47), DEP4, `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly` at main `a2bcb565`, whose `deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` is identical to this PR's base. The patched runs mount this PR's file. Same flags minus the attention and Engram overrides. (`v0.33.0-aarch64` cannot run DSv4.1 on Rubin: its CUDA 13.0 `ptxas` does not know `sm_107a`.)

| Run (in order) | MPS helper trees after startup | GSM8K 5-shot (1319) | Output tok/s, 3 runs | Mean TPOT ms, 3 runs |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| stock | 4 | 90.14% | 7371 / 7579 / 7671 | 7.99 / 7.97 / 7.91 |
| patched | 0 | 91.58% | 7659 / 7561 / 7690 | 7.93 / 8.00 / 7.90 |
| stock | 4 | 90.52% | 7557 / 7616 / 7648 | 8.00 / 7.98 / 7.93 |
| patched | 0 | 90.07% | 7672 / 7656 / 7619 | 7.95 / 7.93 / 7.96 |

MLOPart is available on VR200 too, so the helper tree is present there and this change removes it. Throughput and TPOT are within run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --revision 2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --engram-config '{"embedding_across_dp":true}'

ps -eo pid,ppid,args --forest | grep -c deep_gemm/utils/mlopart.py   # helper trees
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 128
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 512 \
  --num-prompts 640 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed {1,2,3}
```
</details>

With this change, together with the cuInterpose fix in ai-dynamo/snapshot#860, a pod running DeepGEMM's locality-domain probe on B200 can be captured by Snapshot. Without it, capture fails with `cuCheckpointProcessLock: CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

CI coverage: none. The path needs an SM100 GPU on which DeepGEMM can start an MLOPart MPS server, which CI does not provide, so validation was done manually as above.

## Details

**Root cause.** On first use, MegaMoE calls DeepGEMM's `get_balanced_sm_locality_domains()`. DeepGEMM then starts `python -I deep_gemm/utils/mlopart.py`, which runs `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with an `-mlopart` MPS server. The helper allocates memory on each die, sends it to the worker as a POSIX FD, and the worker uses it to measure SM-to-die latency. DeepGEMM caches the resulting map and keeps the helper tree until `deep_gemm.destroy_localizer()`. vLLM never calls it. The helper is an MPS client, and the CUDA driver refuses to checkpoint-lock MPS clients, so CUDA checkpoint of any MegaMoE worker fails.

**Fix.** Call `destroy_localizer()` right after `get_symm_buffer()` creates a symmetric buffer, as the [DeepGEMM README](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/82ca617e5879d0efb0aba5b91b1c81852588af6f/README.md) shows. `destroy_localizer()` first computes and caches the balanced map (`get_balanced_sm_locality_domains()`), then stops the helper, so every later kernel launch reads the identical cached tensor.
- **No steady-state change.** The map and the kernel arguments are identical, and the call runs once per new buffer key, never in the forward hot path.
- **Hardware independent.** On a GPU where MLOPart is unavailable, DeepGEMM already uses its even map, and the call changes nothing.
- **No per-die memory affected.** vLLM does not place any MegaMoE memory per die (`deep_gemm.localize`), so nothing still needs the helper.
- **Guard for older DeepGEMM.** The `hasattr` guard keeps externally installed DeepGEMM versions working: `destroy_localizer` first appeared in the 26/09/30 release, while MegaMoE exists since 26/04, and older releases have no helper to stop.
- **Small memory change.** The 8 MPS servers each held 60 MiB of GPU memory, which is now freed. That memory is allocated and released after the worker's initial memory snapshot, so the startup free-memory check is unaffected.

**Not duplicating existing work.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `destroy_localizer`, `MLOPart` and MegaMoE locality domains. #64835 (closed) placed MegaMoE weights per die and did not address the helper's lifetime. `vllm/distributed/localization.py` is the separate opt-in FlashInfer CuTeDSL path using the native CUDA 13.4 API, and is not affected.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, write and validate this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Build][Bugfix] Never fall back from an x.yf CUDA arch to a lower minor
author: mispa-ms
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes the CUDA arch selection so an `x.yf` (family) source arch never falls back to a lower minor of the same major. Before this change, `cuda_archs_loose_intersection` mapped `10.7f` onto a plain `10.0` target. With CUDA >= 13.4 and an arch list without 10.7, such as the cu134 release list, this compiled the LUT-B MoE kernel from #62759 for `sm_100`, and ptxas rejected it.

The first version of this PR filtered only the LUT-B arch list. This version fixes the shared function instead and removes that filter.

## Claims

- The family fallback for `x.yf` now only takes a target with the same major and a version >= `x.y`. It tries the highest `x.y` first. `12.0f` still matches `12.1a`. `10.7f` no longer matches `10.0`, `10.0a` or `10.0f`.
- The fallback now runs after all exact and cross-suffix matches. So it cannot take a target that another source entry matches by name, whatever the source order.
- In real builds, the only output that changes is `LUT_B_MOE_ARCHS` on CUDA 13.4 without a 10.7 target. It goes from `10.0` to empty, so the kernel is skipped and LUT-B MoE uses its existing emulation path. Every other kernel's arch list and `CUDA_ARCHS` are unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit tests.** `tests/test_cmake_utils.py` adds two tests. Its CI step is currently disabled ("pending locked cmake installation"), so I ran it locally with cmake 4.4.4:

```
# this PR
$ pytest -q tests/test_cmake_utils.py -k "not hipify"
10 passed, 1 deselected

# the same tests with cmake/utils.cmake from main (86fdabec0)
FAILED ...test_family_arch_fallback_never_picks_lower_minor[cu134-release-list]        Expected '', got '10.0'
FAILED ...test_family_arch_fallback_never_picks_lower_minor[lower-minor-arch-specific]  Expected '', got '10.0a'
FAILED ...test_family_arch_fallback_never_picks_lower_minor[lower-minor-plain]          Expected '', got '12.0'
FAILED ...test_family_arch_fallback_never_picks_lower_minor[skips-lower-minor]          Expected '10.7a', got '10.0a'
4 failed, 6 passed, 1 deselected
```

The hipify test is deselected because it needs torch. `test_family_arch_fallback_runs_after_name_matches` passes on main too. It guards the ordering: with only the version check and no separate fallback pass, `10.0f;10.7f` with targets `10.7a;10.3a` gives `10.7a` instead of `10.7a;10.3a`.

**Every call site.** I ran the old and new function with `cmake -P` on every `cuda_archs_loose_intersection` call. That covers 51 calls in `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/utils.cmake` and `cmake/external_projects/*.cmake`, with each CUDA-version branch. It also covers CUDA 11.8, 12.0, 12.3, 12.8, 12.9, 13.0 and 13.4, and every arch list the repo builds with: the release x86 and aarch64 lists, `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker-bake.hcl`, the CI image build scripts, and `.github/workflows/scripts/build.sh`. I applied the `CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS` intersection first, as the build does. The only changed outputs were `LUT_B_MOE_ARCHS` on CUDA 13.4 (`10.0`, `10.0a` or `10.0f` → empty) and the existing test-only call in `tests/test_cmake_utils.py`.

**cu134 build image.** This ran in `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.4`, the cu134 release `BUILD_BASE_IMAGE`, with torch `2.16.0.dev20261009+cu134`. With the release list, main configures `Building LUT-B MoE for archs: 10.0`, and that object fails with 103 ptxas errors such as `Instruction 'tcgen05.alloc' not supported on .target 'sm_100'`. I compared this version with the first version of this PR, the LUT-B-only filter. I configured both, then diffed every `... for archs` line and every command from `ninja -t commands`:

| `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` | `Building LUT-B MoE for archs:` | arch lines and compile commands vs first version | build |
|---|---|---|---|
| `7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0` (cu134 x86 release) | not printed | identical (577 commands) | `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` builds |
| `8.0 8.7 8.9 9.0 10.0 11.0 12.0` (aarch64 release list, configured in the x86 image) | not printed | identical (567 commands) | not run |
| `10.0 10.7` | `10.7f` | identical (544 commands) | LUT-B object builds with `arch=compute_107f,code=sm_107f` |

## Known limitations (unchanged by this PR)

I found these while reviewing the function. I left them out to keep this change small:

1. If the fallback target is plain, the plain value is emitted, so family features are off. For example, `10.0f` with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.7` on CUDA 13.4 gives plain `10.7`. Kernels whose list is only `10.0f` then compile for `compute_107` without family features, the same kind of failure as this bug. No release or CI list hits this. Emitting an `f` arch in that case would fix it.
2. Each source entry takes at most one target. For example, `10.0f` with targets `10.0a;10.7a` gives only `10.0a`.
3. "Same major, minor >= y" approximates the CUDA family table. With CUDA 12.x, 10.1 is not in the 10.0f family but still matches.
4. `+PTX` on an `f` source is dropped when it matches by cross-suffix or fallback.
5. The header comment of `cuda_archs_loose_intersection` still describes only the old `x.0a` special case.

## Details

**Why not a duplicate.** #66014 adds the same LUT-B-only filter as the first version of this PR. This PR instead fixes the shared arch selection, as maintainers suggested. The LUT-B result is the same, and the same mistake is prevented for other `f` sources.

**AI assistance.** I used Claude Code for the analysis, the change, the call-site comparison and the validation scripts. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen3-Omni] Size the video encoder budget from the processor's video limits
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen3-Omni sizes its video encoder budget from the image limits (3584x3584 frames), but the HF processor caps video frames at `768 * 32 * 32` pixels. The budget therefore stops short of `max_model_len`, and valid video requests are rejected with HTTP 400, for example a 60 s 896x504 clip at 2 fps with `--max-model-len 32768`. The same mismatch makes startup profiling run the vision encoder on a dummy video of ~1.5k tokens instead of a long one. This sizes both from the processor's video limits. Clef-Omni shares the code and caps frames lower (`MAX_FRAME_PIXELS`), so it gets its own canvas.

## Claims

- Fixes the erroneous encoder-budget rejection of valid video requests within the context limit. The 60 s clip above returns 200 instead of `video item with 26880 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 25088`, and a 145 s clip at `--max-model-len 65536` (64,960 video tokens, budget 62,720 on main) also returns 200. Clef-Omni at 32k has the same gap: a 120 s 896x504 clip is 30,240 video tokens against a 25,088 budget on main, and fits the 32,768 budget with this PR (checked on the processor, not served).
- On main there is no setting that raises the budget short of `--max-num-batched-tokens`: `--limit-mm-per-prompt` video options only shrink the profiling dummy (`_get_dummy_videos` ignores larger values), and the budget stays 25,088 with them.
- Startup profiling runs the vision encoder on a video that fills the budget: 32,256 / 65,280 video tokens at `max_model_len` 32768 / 65536 for Qwen3-Omni (1,458 / 3,645 on main), and 32,768 at 32k for Clef-Omni (512 on main).
- It also closes an engine crash on main. On an H100 80GB at the default `max_model_len` (65,536), main starts, but a 120 s clip it admits (55,339 tokens) runs the vision encoder out of memory (`torch.OutOfMemoryError` in the vision MLP), and every request after that returns 500. With this PR, startup reports that the KV cache only fits 20,816 tokens and asks for a lower `--max-model-len`, instead of failing under load.
- Images are unchanged (budget 12,544, same dummy).
- Trade-off: profiling a full-length video reserves more memory, so the KV cache is smaller: -3.0 GiB at 32k and -7.6 GiB at 65k on an H200 (below). On an 80 GB H100 this means the default 65k context no longer starts (see the crash above for what main does there). This is the reservation Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL already make: at 32k their processed profiling video is 100% of the video budget (32,768 and 12,288 tokens), while Qwen3-Omni's was 6% (1,458 of 25,088).

## Validation

New tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py` use the real processors: the budget reaches `max_model_len`, a 30 s 896x504 clip (13,440 video tokens) fits it at 16k, the profiling dummy fills the budget within one temporal step for Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni, the video canvas matches what processing produces (no override, flat `max_pixels`, scoped `videos_kwargs.size`, and Clef-Omni's cap), and the image budget is unchanged.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py   # 16 passed (12 new)
pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_audio_in_video.py   # 40 passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "Qwen3-Omni or clef"   # 10 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # passes
```

With both model files from main, 11 of the 12 new tests fail (the image test passes on both). With only `clef_omni.py` from main, the 3 Clef-Omni cases fail:

```
E   assert 25088 == 32768
E   assert 12544 == 16384
E   assert (12544 - 768) < 729
E   assert (12544 - 768) < 256
E   AttributeError: 'Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerProcessingInfo' object has no attribute 'get_video_size_with_most_features'
11 failed, 5 passed
```

End to end on an H200 with `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct`, the same wheel with only the model file swapped, `vllm serve` with the default `--max-num-batched-tokens` and `--media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"num_frames": -1, "fps": 2}}'`:

| `--max-model-len` | request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32768 | 60 s 896x504 clip, `use_audio_in_video` (27,680 tokens) | 400 | 200 |
| 65536 | same 60 s clip | 200 | 200, same greedy text |
| 65536 | 145 s 896x504 clip, video only (64,977 tokens) | 400 | 200 |
| 65536 | 4 concurrent 120 s clips with audio (55,339 tokens each) | 200 | 200 |

| `--max-model-len` | encoder budget main → PR | KV cache memory main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| 32768 | 25,088 → 32,768 | 64.13 → 61.11 GiB |
| 65536 | 62,720 → 65,536 | 64.11 → 56.47 GiB |

The 60 s request returned identical greedy text on main and with this PR. The four concurrent requests had equal prompt-token counts on both; 2 of the 4 outputs match and the other 2 diverge after about ten words, for a reason I haven't confirmed (vLLM is not batch invariant by default). The maximum sampled GPU memory across the 65k request phase was 141,461 MiB on main and 136,251 MiB with this PR (of 143,771 MiB). These serving runs used the revision before the switch to `_merge_kwargs`, which resolves the same video size (checked with no override, a scoped override and unrelated kwargs). `test_model_tensor_schema` passes for Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni on main and with this PR on the same GPU.

The same check on an H100 80GB, default `--max-model-len` (65,536), with the same requests in order:

| | startup | 60 s clip | 120 s clip with audio (55,339 tokens) | 60 s clip again |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | starts, 9.53 GiB KV cache | 200 | 500, `CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.72 GiB` in the vision encoder; engine dead | 500 |
| this PR | `ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (65536), (6.0 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (1.91 GiB). Based on the available memory, the estimated maximum model length is 20816.` | | | |

## Details

- Root cause: `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerProcessingInfo` inherits the Qwen2-VL video estimate, which uses the largest image (3584x3584, 12,544 tokens per two frames with patch size 16) and adds frames until `seq_len`. That stops at 25,088 for 32k. Processing then shrinks real frames to the processor's video default (`Qwen3OmniMoeProcessorKwargs` videos `size`, `longest_edge = 768 * 32 * 32`), which is also why the dummy video only reaches ~1.5k tokens.
- The video size now comes from where processing takes it: flat `size` / `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` over `video_processor.size` (as in #49015), otherwise the processor's merged `videos_kwargs`, resolved with `processor._merge_kwargs` as Gemma 3 does for its image size. Frames are added at that size until `seq_len`, without the 14-frame dummy cap, because this processor caps pixels per frame rather than per video, so a single video can fill the prompt. The per-item budget is therefore `seq_len`, the same pattern as #59565 sizing GLM-5.3 images from the exact token ceiling.
- `Qwen3OmniMoeProcessorKwargs` and its video defaults are the same in transformers 5.16.1 and 5.22.1, the range vLLM supports.
- #65534 (configurable `--encoder-cache-size`) is complementary: it changes cache capacity, while this fixes the per-item size that the cache is floored to.
- #63809 (Qwen3-Omni ViT CUDA graphs) reads `get_num_frames_with_most_features` for its `max_frames_per_video`, which sizes the `cu_seqlens` buffer. With this change it returns 84 frames at 32k instead of 4. That is the frame count of the profiling input at the largest frame size, not a bound on every valid video: smaller frames allow more.
- Qwen2.5-Omni has the same under-profiling (its processed profiling video is 1,458 of a 32,768 budget at 32k) but not the 400 at 32k, so I left it for a separate change.
- The shared Qwen2-VL estimate has the same gap whenever `max_model_len` is not a multiple of its two-frame step. With Qwen2.5-VL (step 16,384) at `--max-model-len 40000` the budget is 32,768, while a 68 s 896x504 clip is 39,168 tokens. I kept this PR to Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni, where the gap shows up at the common 32k setting, and can follow up on the shared estimate.

title: [Doc][Bugfix] Fix strict docs build broken by unresolved autorefs
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Overview

The strict MkDocs build (Read the Docs, `fail_on_warning: true`) has been failing on `main` since 2026-11-05 with `Aborted with 12 warnings in strict mode!`. Every PR's docs check fails with the same warnings, e.g. builds [35688234](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35688234/) (`main` at `e336407a3d`) and [35688313](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35688313/). This PR fixes the docstrings behind those warnings. No code behavior changes.

## Claims

- The strict docs build passes again. All 12 `mkdocs_autorefs: Could not find cross-reference target` warnings are gone.
- The only changes are docstrings. No code changes.

## Validation

Ran the same command as Read the Docs, with `requirements/docs.txt` installed in a clean venv:

```bash
uv venv -p 3.12 /tmp/docs-venv
VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/docs-venv uv pip install -r requirements/docs.txt
/tmp/docs-venv/bin/python -m mkdocs build --clean --site-dir /tmp/docs-site --config-file mkdocs.yaml --strict
```

| Tree | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`e336407a3d`) | Exit 1, `Aborted with 12 warnings in strict mode!`, the same 12 warnings as Read the Docs build 35688234 |
| This PR | Exit 0, `Documentation built in 178.18 seconds`, no warnings |

## Details

There are two root causes.

**1. MiniMax-M3.1 drafter docstrings (11 warnings), from #65386.**
- Some docstrings write array shapes as consecutive brackets, such as `red[8 t + wave][row][token]`, `x [16][K]`, `x_in [rows][6144]`, `x8[t][16 tid ..]`, `xs8[t][tid / 2]` and `o [112][128]`.
- Markdown parses `[a][b]` as a reference-style link, so autorefs tries to resolve `b` (`row`, `K`, `6144`, `16 tid ..`, `tid / 2`, `128`) and fails.
- Fix: wrap these shapes in code spans in `drafter/device.py` (`red_store`, `xq_chunk`, `row_x`, `quant_store`) and `drafter/attention.py` (`store_partial`). Single brackets such as `[1, rank, site]` are not affected, so they are left as is.

**2. `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` lost its docstring (1 warning), from #54109.**
- #54109 renamed the documented class to `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModularBase`, then added new `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` and `TrtLlmMxfp4Mxfp8ExpertsModular` subclasses without docstrings.
- mkdocstrings skips objects without a docstring by default, so the API page has no anchor for `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular`. The link in `docs/design/moe_kernel_features.md` then cannot resolve.
- Fix: give both subclasses a one-line docstring that names their activation quantization, so both get API anchors. The docs link stays as it is, because it names the concrete experts class.

title: [BugFix] Fix/spec decode insert resampled race
author: shustovTE
body:
## Overview

Run `_insert_resampled_kernel` with `num_warps=1` to avoid a race when reading and updating `num_sampled` in place. The race can cause an out-of-range lookup during speculative decoding and a fatal CUDA exception.

## Claims

- Removes the cross-warp read/write race in `_insert_resampled_kernel` by restricting its execution to one warp.
- Changes only this kernel's launch configuration.
- Makes no performance or model-quality claims.

## Validation

Two CUDA core dumps from separate crashes on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell show the same failure mechanism:

| Incident | Threads reading `num_sampled = 4` | Threads reading `num_sampled = 5` |
|---|---|---|
| First | 0, 32 | 64, 96 |
| Second | 0, 32, 64 | 96 |

The listed threads represent different warps within the same block. Disassembly maps these values to the load of `num_sampled`; the corresponding resampling indices are 4 and 5, with an exclusive end index of 5.

Both dumps report `Warp Out of range Address` at `_insert_resampled_kernel+384`, corresponding to:

    temp = tl.load(temp_ptr + req_state_idx).to(tl.float32)

The failing environment used vLLM 0.32.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, and Gemma 4 MTP with four speculative tokens. The same read/update pattern remains in the main-branch code patched here.

Local validation:
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, typos, and repository Python checks.
- Python syntax validation and `git diff --check` passed.

The dumps establish the original failure mechanism.

## Details

The kernel loads `num_sampled`, uses it to compute a resampling index, and increments the same counter in global memory. In the captured machine code, there is no inter-warp barrier between the load and the store.

A delayed warp can therefore read the incremented value after another warp has performed the update. In both incidents, this changes the resampling index from 4 to 5, outside the request's logits range. The subsequent mapping lookup supplies an invalid request-state index, causing the temperature load to fault.

Using one warp removes this inter-warp dependency without changing the sampling algorithm or introducing another kernel launch.

This failure occurs before the NaN/argmax handling addressed by #50183.

title: [Doc][Bugfix] Fix strict docs build broken by subclassing mocked torch classes
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

The strict docs build on main has failed since #65235 with `Failed to import vllm.entrypoints.cli.preload.PreloadSubcommand` and `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'PydanticMagicMock'` ([main build at #65235](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35689810/)). Every main build since then fails the same way. PRs that change docs fail too, while PRs without docs changes skip the build.

## Claims

- Fixes the strict docs build. The argparse docs generator imports every CLI subcommand again, including `vllm preload`.
- Generated CLI and engine-args pages are unchanged.

## Validation

`mkdocs build --strict` in a docs-only environment, as on Read the Docs (`requirements/docs.txt`, Python 3.12, no torch):

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .docs-venv
uv pip install --python .docs-venv/bin/python -r requirements/docs.txt
.docs-venv/bin/python -m mkdocs build --clean --strict --config-file mkdocs.yaml --site-dir /tmp/site
```

| `generate_argparse.py` | Result |
|---|---|
| main | exit 1, `Failed to import vllm.entrypoints.cli.preload.PreloadSubcommand`, same `TypeError` as the Read the Docs log |
| this PR | exit 0, all CLI pages built, including `cli/preload` |

## Details

- Root cause: `TraceTensor` subclasses `torch.Tensor`, which is mocked in the docs build. Subclassing a mock produced a mock instance rather than a class, and `@dataclass` then failed on the `Copy.src: TraceTensor` annotation in `reload/bake.py`.
- Fix: `PydanticMagicMock.__mro_entries__` gives any class inheriting from a mock a real `MockBase` base, so it is a real type. `MockBase` supports pydantic schemas and subscripting (for `cachetools.LRUCache[_K, _V]`). `torch.nn` now uses `PydanticMagicMock`, so `nn.*` subclasses are covered too.
- Validated with `mkdocs build --strict` on current main without torch: exit 0, no warnings. Compared with the previous fix, the page set is identical. `cli/bench/serve` differs only in its random `--result-filename` default and the order of a `set` of choices.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `generate_argparse.py` or this failure. #66044 fixed unrelated cross-reference warnings.
