title: [Bugfix][DeepGEMM] Match relax warmup M values to the vendored SM100 heuristic
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Overview

Fix a dense FP8 runtime-JIT gap in the default `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=relax` mode on SM100. Serving-time token counts can select configurations that startup warmup never probed, triggering nvcc compilation of `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d` kernels on the serving critical path. GPU reproduction measured 1.7 seconds per new cubin for weight shapes used by public Qwen3 and MiniMax models.

Related to [#64824](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64824), which tracks remaining DeepGEMM runtime-JIT gaps but does not list this dense-path cause. The duplicate-work check on 2026-11-06 found no open PR touching `_generate_optimal_warmup_m_values`.

Authored with AI assistance.

## Claims

- Expands relax warmup's candidate `block_m` values to match the vendored SM100 dense heuristic; CPU checks cover all 16 candidate multiples, including `block_m=224`.
- GPU validation confirms that the expanded probes eliminate runtime compilation at the previously failing serving M values for both reproduced weight shapes, including a non-swap `block_n` gap.
- The gap is shape-dependent: a host-side scan found uncovered configurations for 39 of 512 eligible N values on a 152-SM part (40 of 512 at 148 SMs). Warmup wall time increased from ~36 s to ~37 s for the measured weight shape.

## Validation

Called the real `_generate_optimal_warmup_m_values` on a CPU-only host with `num_sms=148` and `n=7168`:

| Check | main | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Missing candidate `block_m` multiples | 9 | 0 |
| Probe count at `max_tokens=8192` | 288 | 1060 |

The missing values on main are `[80, 96, 112, 144, 160, 176, 208, 224, 240]`.

An exact host-side port of the vendored SM100 `get_layout_candidates` + `compare` heuristic and vLLM's warmup generator scanned serving M in [1, 8192] across all 512 eligible weight N values (multiples of 128). Real DeepGEMM config selection via `DG_PRINT_CONFIGS=1` matched every sampled point. The scan found these model-level gaps in existing relax warmup:

| Public model(s) | `o_proj` weight (N, K) | Uncovered serving M | Selected configuration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8; Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 | (2048, 4096) | 257–288 | Swap-AB; `block_m=32`, `block_n=128`, cluster (1,2) |
| MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2 | (3072, 6144) | 385–400 on SM100 with 152 SMs | Non-swap; `block_m=128`, `block_n=96`, cluster (2,1) |
| MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2 | (3072, 6144) | 1729–1760 on SM100 with 148 SMs | Non-swap; `block_n=160` |

The Qwen M range overlaps default CUDA-graph capture sizes (multiples of 8 up to 512), so ordinary decode batches can hit it. Negative controls—DeepSeek-V3.x/R1, Kimi-K2, Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, and Qwen3-32B-FP8—had no uncovered serving M in the scan.

GPU reproduction on a GB300 node used dummy FP8 block-quantized weights, with no model download: ran the real `_deepgemm_fp8_gemm_nt_warmup` in relax mode with `max_tokens=8192`, then called `fp8_gemm_nt` at serving M values.

| Weight (N, K) | Existing relax warmup: serving results |
|---|---|
| (2048, 4096) | M=256 cached; M=264 compiled a new cubin (1.7 s); M=272/288 reused it |
| (3072, 6144) | M=384 cached; M=385 compiled a new cubin (1.7 s); M=392/400/401 cached |

Repeating both experiments with `block_ms = list(range(16, 257, 16))` served all previously failing M values from the warmup cache. Measured warmup wall time went from ~36 s to ~37 s for the tested weight shape. These runs validate the reproduced gaps; they do not establish exhaustive GPU coverage of every shape.

Repository pre-commit hooks pass, including ruff and mypy. No unit test was added: a CPU test of the candidate list would mirror the constant without detecting drift in the vendored heuristic. The GPU cache check exercises the actual failure mode and aligns with #64824's `jit_monitor` sub-item.

## Details

`_generate_optimal_warmup_m_values` in `vllm/model_executor/warmup/deep_gemm_warmup.py` hardcodes `block_ms = [64, 128, 256]`, reflecting a 2025-era [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM) heuristic.

The vendored [vllm-project/DeepGEMM](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM) heuristic in `csrc/jit_kernels/heuristics/sm100.hpp` now enumerates `block_m` in steps of 16 through 256 on the swap-AB path. The non-swap candidates `{32, 64, 128}` are a subset. Missing warmup M probes can leave configurations uncovered even when their `block_m` is already in the old list: the MiniMax reproduction is a `block_n` effect.

The fix changes one functional line to `block_ms = list(range(16, 257, 16))` and adds a docstring noting the requirement to stay synchronized with the vendored heuristic. This increases startup probes, with the measured timing above. `full` mode remains the exhaustive, much slower option.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix non-deferred structured-output draft retrieval
author: yzong-rh
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix a bug affecting spec decode + structured outputs under async scheduling, where the EngineCore does not retrieve the real draft token ids from the worker before computing the grammar bitmask, leading to a failed request and `500: Internal Server error`.

## Claims

Suppose PP=1 + async scheduling + spec decode, suppose request `p` requiring structured outputs is scheduled in batch A, skipped for batch B but remains RUNNING, and scheduled again in batch C. In step C, it will take the non-deferred sampling path and will not retrieve draft tokens from batch A. Grammar bitmask are then computed from `-1` placeholders instead of the real draft tokens, leading to grammar-invalid generation and `"Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens %s for request %s"`.

The non-deferred path can be most easily reached when model generation nears `max_model_len` (see repro below). I think it can also occur under KV pressure in P/D and KV offloading deployments. `Scheduler.defer_block_free` and `KVConnectorBase_V1.has_pending_block_frees()` can shortcut preemption, leaving requests RUNNING but unscheduled.

See "Details" for more background and code trace.

## Validation

Ran on H100.

Repro:
```
.venv/bin/vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B  \
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}'   \
--max-model-len 20

curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/completions   -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -d '{
    "prompt": "Return only the JSON object required by the output constraint.",
    "temperature": 0,
    "structured_outputs": {"regex": "\\{\"v\":\"x\"\\}"}
  }'
```

On main, the request fails with:
```
(EngineCore pid=3266911) ERROR 11-06 04:16:14 [scheduler.py:2475] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [788, 330, 16] for request cmpl-802fafd32fa38c7c-0-8cca2192. Terminating request.
(APIServer pid=3265988) ERROR 11-06 04:16:14 [serving.py:203] Request cmpl-802fafd32fa38c7c failed with an internal error during generation
INFO:     127.0.0.1:40586 - "POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

With the fix, the request succeeds, returning the correctly constrained output:
```
{"id":"cmpl-b0eb899cdb680c05","object":"text_completion","created":1793956679,"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-4B","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"{\"v\":\"x\"}","logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","stop_reason":null,"token_ids":null,"prompt_logprobs":null,"prompt_token_ids":null,"routed_experts":null,"weight_versions":null}],"service_tier":null,"system_fingerprint":"vllm-0.33.0rc1.dev752+g1b16698eb0e5719412ecc3b2c7a05afad4d02354-2af0d37d","usage":{"prompt_tokens":11,"total_tokens":18,"completion_tokens":7,"completion_tokens_details":null},"kv_transfer_params":null,"ec_transfer_params":null,"metrics":null}
```

`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_async_spec_decode_structured_output` is essentially the same test to be run in CI. On main, it fails with `AssertionError: assert 'error' == 'stop'`.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -vs -m 'cpu_test' tests/v1/core

908 passed, 343 deselected

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -vs -m 'not cpu_test' tests/v1/core tests/v1/worker tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py

1469 passed, 145 skipped, 941 deselected

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s -m 'not cpu_test' \
  tests/v1/engine \
  --ignore=tests/v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py \
  --deselect=tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_engine_core_tp

315 passed, 1 skipped, 62 deselected
```

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e15dc602fbfd11e2b64c2d41527a1a72
Qwen/Qwen3-4B + RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark + 8 draft tokens + async scheduling + structured outputs.
Ran on 1 x B200.
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c64: low vs high concurrency

```
.venv/bin/python run.py --output ... --pipeline-parallel-size ... --num-repeats 10
```

Workload | Baseline | Fix | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad, c=1 | 1082.0 | 1076.6 | −0.50%
broad, c=64 | 16601.2 | 16632.3 | +0.19%
tight, c=1 | 1627.7 | 1620.3 | −0.45%
tight, c=64 | 32677.9 | 32642.1 | −0.11%

Results not stat-sig

## Details

Suppose PP=1, async scheduling, and spec decode are used, batch queue size will be 2 (two batches can be inflight concurrently). Suppose some request `p` uses structured outputs.

### Deferred sampling path (not buggy)
The following normally occurs inside `EngineCore.step_with_batch_queue`:
- Step A: `p` is RUNNING and scheduled in a batch
- Step B: `p` is RUNNING and scheduled again, but since `p` needs the draft tokens from step A for `grammar_bitmask` constraints, it will defer sampling.
  - It will instead wait for Step A to finish and retire the request. It will retreive the draft tokens via `model_executor.take_draft_token_ids` to generate the bitmasks before dispatching step B sampling.
  - This is the deferred sampling path taken when there are `pending_structured_output_tokens`.

### Non-deferred sampling path (buggy)
However, there's no guarantee that Step B will schedule request `p`:
- Step A: `p` is RUNNING and scheduled in a batch
- Step B: `p` remains RUNNING but not scheduled
- Step C: Batch A is awaited on and retired due to batch queue size limit. Only after is `p` scheduled again.
  - Because Batch A has been retired, there batch C no longer has `pending_structured_output_tokens`. The deferred path is not taken.
  - The non-deferred path however never calls `model_executor.take_draft_token_ids` to retrieve `p`'s real draft tokens. Gramamr bitmask is generated from `-1` placeholders and could be incorrect.
  - When batch C eventually retires, grammar-invalid generation will cause "Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens %s for request %s", failing the request.

Cases where step A schedules `p` but step B skips it are rare, but can occur when:
- `p`'s generation is near the `max_model_len`. So step B does not have the budget to reschedule `p` until step A rejected some draft tokens and been retired, freeing up budget for `p` in step C.
- Preemption is shortcutted (no more RUNNING requests can be scheduled or pre-empted for that step) leaving RUNNING requests unscheduled. This notably occur with KVConnectors:
  - For P/D deployments, `Scheduler.defer_block_free` fences blocks belonging to inflight steps and preventing preemption.
  - For KV offlaoding deployments, `KVConnectorBase_V1.has_pending_block_frees()` can also stop preemption from choosing a victim when connector frees are still pending.

### Fix

The fix is to introduce a `SchedulerOutput.has_structured_output_spec_decode` flag orthogonal to the existing `SchedulerOutput.pending_structured_output_tokens`.
- `pending_structured_output_tokens` indicates whether sampling should be deferred for a structured outputs request `p`, which is needed whenever an earlier batch with `p` is stil inflight. It doesn't care about whether spec decode is used, `p` should be deferred regardless.
- `has_structured_output_spec_decode` indicates whether there's a structured output request `p` expecting draft tokens. It doesn't care whether `p` is deferred or not. Draft tokens should be retrieve regardless.

Note this introduces a sychronization between scheduler-side and worker-side on the non-deferred sampling path but this is required for correctness. Pipeline bubbles due to `take_draft_token_ids` is a known issue and being worked on in #64531. I hope to land this correctness fix first before finalizing #64531.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject translation on models that cannot translate
author: hmellor
body:
## Overview

`/v1/audio/translations` returns a transcript with a 200 on models that cannot translate. These now return a 400, as Ming V3 ASR and Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe already do. Found while checking translation for #65735 and #62398.

## Claims

- Voxtral, Voxtral Realtime, GLM-ASR, Kimi Audio, Cohere ASR, FunASR, FireRedASR2 and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize raise `ValueError` on `translate`, which the server returns as a 400.
- This is a breaking change for anyone calling `/v1/audio/translations` on these models and using the transcript. `/v1/audio/transcriptions` still works. Kimi Audio and MOSS callers who put an instruction in `prompt` can send it there instead.
- Unrelated small change: the audio upload size error now names `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB`, as the decode limit errors already name theirs.

## Validation

B200, Transformers 5.23.0.dev0, `temperature=0`, `/v1/audio/translations` with `language=en`.

| Model | Before, `to_language=de` | After |
|---|---|---|
| `zai-org/GLM-ASR-Nano-2512` | 200, English | 400 |
| `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507` | 200, English | 400 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B` | 200, mostly German | Unchanged |
| `ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-2b` | 200, English then German | Unchanged |

GLM-ASR and Voxtral also returned Italian for Italian audio with `to_language=en`, where `openai/whisper-small` translated. Transcription still returns 200 on all four.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/test_translation_validation.py -k transcription_only
```

1 passed through `RemoteOpenAIServer`. The test itself was not run without the fix, but the same request returned 200 before it. Those runs used this patch on `9b34fec`. Pre-commit passes.

## Details

- GLM-ASR had a translate prompt, but the model ignores it. The others never read the task, so their prompt is the same as for transcription.
- Only GLM-ASR and Voxtral were run. Kimi Audio, Cohere ASR, FunASR, FireRedASR2 and Voxtral Realtime were not run: I called each `get_generation_prompt` directly and confirmed it raises. MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize was checked the same way, because it failed at startup on this environment with `KeyError: 'padding_mask'`, before reaching this code.
- Gemma 3n was not run (`timm` missing), and the existing translation tests cover it. Canary and Qwen3-Omni were not run and are unchanged.

No open PR or issue covers this: searched open PRs and issues for translation on these endpoints.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve embedding size overrides
author: bzsuni
body:
## Overview

Fix rejection of valid dimensions=2048 requests for voyageai/voyage-4-nano by honoring its configured embedding size.

## Changes

- Honor hf_config.embedding_size before falling back to embedding_dim, Dense module output size, or hidden size.
- Preserve existing EmbeddingGemma 2 dimension support.

## Validation

43 tests passed, including the Voyage GPU regression on H800, pooling parameter tests, and EmbeddingGemma 2 configuration tests.

Before the fix, the Voyage regression failed because the dimension limit was incorrectly set to 1024. After the fix, dimensions=2048 returns 2048-dimensional embeddings with cosine similarity ≥ 0.999999 compared with default inference.

VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/pooling/test_embedding.py \
  -k test_voyage_native_embedding_dimensions -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_pooling_params.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py \
  -k 'not test_embedding_gemma2 or test_embeddinggemma2_embedding_size_matches_native_dim' \
  -q

All applicable pre-commit checks passed.

## Details

Voyage's embedding head maps 1024-dimensional hidden states to 2048-dimensional embeddings. Its model adapter sets hf_config.embedding_size from num_labels, but dimension validation ignored that field and fell back to the hidden size.

The fix honors the configured embedding size and adds a regression test through LLM.embed using official model weights. The existing Extended Pooling CI task covers the test. Documentation now distinguishes output embedding size from hidden size.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen2.5-Omni] Size the video encoder budget from the processor's video limits
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen2.5-Omni has the same video budget gap that #66017 fixed for Qwen3-Omni. It sizes the video encoder budget and the profiling dummy from the image limits (3584x3584 frames), while its HF processor caps video frames at `768 * 28 * 28` pixels (`Qwen2_5OmniProcessorKwargs`). So the budget stops short of `max_model_len` when `max_model_len` isn't a multiple of the two-frame step, and startup profiling runs the vision encoder on a ~1.5k-token dummy video. This moves the video sizing from #66017 into Qwen2.5-Omni and lets Qwen3-Omni inherit it.

## Claims

The two failures have different causes:

- At `--max-model-len 24000` the admission limit is wrong. A synthetic 30 s 896x504 video at 2 fps (17,280 video tokens) is rejected with `exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 16384`; with this PR the budget reaches 24,000 and it is served.
- At the default 32768 the admission limit is already right, but startup profiling runs the vision encoder on a 1,458-token dummy. On an NVIDIA A10 (23 GB), a synthetic 56 s 896x504 video (32,256 video tokens, admitted) then runs the vision encoder out of memory. With this PR the dummy fills the budget (within one two-frame step), profiling reserves that memory, and the video is served.
- Trade-off: the reserved encoder memory comes out of the KV cache, -19% at 24k and -28% at 32k on the A10 (below). The default context still starts there. Deployments with shorter videos can lower the reservation with the `limit_mm_per_prompt` video size hints in the [memory docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/configuration/conserving_memory/#configurable-options); at 32k, `{"count": 1, "num_frames": 32, "width": 640, "height": 360}` brings the profiled video from 32,256 to 4,784 tokens.
- With a `limit_mm_per_prompt` video size hint, for the configurations checked, the dummy produces the same number of video tokens as a real video of that size. Checked on CPU for Qwen2.5-Omni, Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni with 11 hint sizes (portrait, landscape, narrow, oversized, tiny) under no processor kwargs, flat `max_pixels`, scoped `videos_kwargs.size`, scoped `images_kwargs.size` and both scoped settings, plus `do_resize=False` (flat, scoped to videos, scoped to images) for Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni: 205 of 205 cases match, against 150 mismatches on main. Some Clef-Omni inputs fail with `do_resize=False`, on main as well, because frame capping can produce dimensions incompatible with patchification. This also fixes Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni on main, where a 540x960 hint on Qwen3-Omni was profiled at 408 tokens per frame pair vs 510 for a real video.
- Images are unchanged (budget 16,384). Without size hints, Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni profiling is unchanged.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni.py` use the real Qwen2.5-Omni-3B processor: the budget reaches `max_model_len` at 20000 and 24000, a 30 s video fits at 24000, the profiling dummy fills the budget at 4096 / 16384 / 24000, the video canvas matches what processing produces (no override, flat `max_pixels`, scoped `videos_kwargs.size`), a size-hinted dummy matches a real video of that size, and the image budget is unchanged. `test_qwen3_omni.py` gets the size-hint test for Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni. With main's model files, 17 of the 22 new tests fail; the image test and four size-hint cases that main already handles pass on both.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py   # 38 passed (22 new)
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni_embed.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_audio_in_video.py   # 58 passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "Qwen2.5-Omni or Qwen3-Omni or clef"   # 17 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # passes
```

End to end on an NVIDIA A10 (23 GB) with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B`, synthetic random-pixel videos, `limit_mm_per_prompt` image 0 / video 1 / audio 0, default `max_num_batched_tokens` (8192) and `gpu_memory_utilization`, the same wheel with only `qwen2_5_omni_thinker.py` swapped. This ran on the first commit; the second commit only changes profiling when a size hint is set, and the dummy without hints is identical (same `video_grid_thw` at 4096 / 16384 / 24000 / 32768 for all three models).

| `max_model_len` | request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24000 | 30 s 896x504 video (17,280 video tokens) | `VLLMValidationError: ... 17280 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 16384` | served (17,294 prompt tokens) |
| 32768 | 10 s 896x504 video | served | served, same greedy text |
| 32768 | 56 s 896x504 video (32,256 video tokens) | `CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 630.00 MiB` in the vision encoder (`_process_video_input`) | served (32,270 prompt tokens) |

| `max_model_len` | encoder budget main → PR | KV cache memory main → PR | KV cache tokens main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24000 | 16,384 → 24,000 | 13.45 → 10.83 GiB | 335,872 → 221,183 |
| 32768 | 32,768 → 32,768 | 13.44 → 9.71 GiB | 335,872 → 163,840 |

## Details

- Root cause: `Qwen2_5OmniThinkerProcessingInfo` inherits the Qwen2-VL video estimate, which sizes frames at the largest image and adds two-frame steps of 16,384 tokens until `seq_len`, so at 24000 it stops at 16,384. Processing then shrinks real frames to the processor's video default, which is also why the dummy video only reaches 729 tokens per step.
- Default sizing: the video methods #66017 added to `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerProcessingInfo` move to `Qwen2_5OmniThinkerProcessingInfo`, keyed by `processor_kwargs_cls`, and Qwen3-Omni inherits them; its dummy builder goes back to the alias it was before #66017.
- Size hints: a hinted frame is resolved with the video processor's settings (`get_video_frame_size`: `smart_resize` within the video limits, the hinted size when the video `do_resize` is off, and Clef-Omni's own frame cap) instead of being clamped per dimension against the landscape video canvas. With resizing enabled, Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni resolve hinted dimensions within the video processor's pixel limits, so an oversized hint doesn't allocate a full-size dummy; with `do_resize=False` the hinted dimensions are kept, as processing keeps them.
- #63374 (Qwen2.5-Omni ViT CUDA graphs) reads `get_num_frames_with_most_features` through the Qwen2.5-VL encoder graph code. With this change it returns 84 frames at 32k with one video per prompt (4 on main), and 2 with the default video limit (1 on main).
- The shared Qwen2-VL estimate has the same budget gap for Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL at `max_model_len` values that aren't a multiple of the step. I kept this PR to the Omni models and can follow up on that one.

title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo-V2 omni: label video grids with the sampled frames' media time
author: Pb314314
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #65523. MiMo-V2 omni writes a timestamp before each 2-frame video grid in the prompt, but stamped the sampled frames 1 s apart. vLLM's video loader samples 32 frames across the whole clip by default, so every clip was labelled `00:00`–`00:30` whatever its length. This PR takes the frame times from the loader metadata (`frames_indices / fps`). Source change: +36/−5 in `mimo_v2_omni.py`.

Example: a 120 s video at 24 fps. The default loader picks 32 frames evenly across it, one every ~3.9 s. MiMo groups them in pairs into 16 grids and writes a `mm:ss` label before each grid in the prompt (`<label><|vision_start|><grid tokens><|vision_end|>`). The label should be the time of the grid's first frame in the video:

| Grid | Its first frame is at | Label on Baseline | Label After PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0 s | `00:00` | `00:00` |
| 2 | 7.8 s | `00:02` | `00:07` |
| 3 | 15.5 s | `00:04` | `00:15` |
| … | … | … | … |
| 16 | 116.1 s | `00:30` | `01:56` |

On Baseline the model is told the whole 2-minute video lasts 30 s.

## Claims

- Prompt timestamps match the sampled frames' media time: at most 1 s off (labels are whole seconds) for every loader setting and input layout tested, versus up to 434 s off before.
- MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL answers timing questions correctly: "when does the screen turn red" 5/20 → 19/20, "how long is the video" 4/20 → 20/20 (Baseline answers `00:31` for every clip, 30 s to 8 min).
- Unchanged where there is no frame timing: text and image outputs are identical, inputs without metadata keep 1 s spacing, and prompt length and KV cache size are the same.
- No performance change: the processor's host time per video request is unchanged (16 ms), and serving throughput is within 2.5% at concurrency 1 and within the launch-to-launch variation at higher concurrency.

## Validation

Baseline is main `f8b116409c`; After PR is this PR on it.

**Affected models.** Every MiMo-V2 checkpoint with a `vision_config`, since those load as `MiMoV2OmniForCausalLM`: MiMo-V2.5, -V2.5-Base, -V2.6-Flash-RL, -V2.6-Flash-MOPD, -V2.6-Pro-RL, -V2.6-Pro-MOPD. Text-only MiMo-V2 checkpoints (V2-Flash, V2.5-Pro) and MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B (Qwen3.5 architecture) are not affected. The fix is in the processor and does not depend on weights. All six share the same video settings (1 fps, temporal patch 2; V2.5-Base has `max_frames` 1024 instead of 3600). With each checkpoint's own config and tokenizer, a 120 s clip ends at `00:30` on Baseline and at `01:56` After PR (true 116.1 s).

**Label accuracy across input layouts.** A video reaches the processor in several forms: as a URL decoded by vLLM's loader (with different frame-sampling settings and decoders), or offline as frames the user passes in (with or without the loader's metadata). For each form, we feed a real MP4 through the same loader (`MediaConnector`) and processor used in serving, read the 16 or so labels out of the resulting prompt, and compare each label with the actual time of the frame it labels. The table gives the largest difference over all labels of a video (0 is perfect; labels are whole seconds, so up to 1 s is rounding):

| How the video arrives | Largest label error, Baseline | Largest label error, After PR |
|---|---|---|
| default loader (32 frames), 0.5 s–480 s clips at 24 / 29.97 / 60 fps | 9.6–434.5 s | ≤ 0.92 s |
| `num_frames` 8 / 31 (odd, padded) / 64 / all | 32.6–405.4 s | ≤ 0.92 s |
| `fps: 2` | 58.6–118.1 s | ≤ 0.95 s |
| `fps: 1` | 0.92 s | 0.92 s (unchanged) |
| TorchCodec decode (CPU and CUDA), offline `(array or tensor, metadata)` | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| offline raw array or PIL frames (no timing) | 1 s spacing | 1 s spacing (unchanged) |
| prebuilt `(frames_TCHW, timestamps)` | given timestamps ignored | given timestamps used |

<details>
<summary>All 22 cases</summary>

| Input | Clip | Frames | Baseline max error | After PR max error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | 120 s, 24 fps | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| default | 480 s, 24 fps | 32 | 434.5 s | 0.54 s |
| default | 120 s, 29.97 fps | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| default | 60 s, 60 fps | 32 | 28.0 s | 0.87 s |
| default | 1.5 s, 24 fps | 32 | 28.6 s | 0.92 s |
| default | 0.5 s, 24 fps | 12 | 9.6 s | 0.42 s |
| default | 75 min, 4 fps | 32 | 4,324.5 s | 4.5 s (see Details) |
| `num_frames: 64` | 120 s | 64 | 56.0 s | 0.88 s |
| `num_frames: 8` | 480 s | 8 | 405.4 s | 0.38 s |
| `num_frames: 31` | 120 s | 31 | 90.0 s | 0.04 s |
| `num_frames: -1` | 1.5 s | 36 | 32.6 s | 0.92 s |
| `fps: 2` | 60 s, 24 fps | 120 | 58.6 s | 0.42 s |
| `fps: 2` | 120 s, 29.97 fps | 239 | 118.1 s | 0.95 s |
| `fps: 1` | 120 s | 120 | 0.92 s | 0.92 s |
| TorchCodec, CPU | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| TorchCodec, CUDA | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| offline `(ndarray, metadata)` | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| offline `(tensor, metadata)` | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| offline raw ndarray | 120 s | 32 | 1 s spacing | 1 s spacing |
| offline list of PIL frames | 120 s | 32 | 1 s spacing | 1 s spacing |
| prebuilt `(frames_TCHW, timestamps)` | 120 s | 32 | 1 s spacing | given timestamps |
| same request twice | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |

</details>

**Does the model answer timing questions correctly?** We generated 20 test videos with a known answer. Each is gray with a moving white square, and for a stretch the whole screen turns one solid color, e.g. a 2-minute video that turns red from 78 s to 93 s. Lengths are 30 s, 1, 2, 4 and 8 min; the color starts 15%, 40%, 65% or 85% of the way in. For each video we ask MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL two questions and check the answer against the truth:

- "At what time in the video does the whole screen turn red? Reply with only the timestamp in mm:ss format." (with the video's own color: red, blue, green or yellow) Counted correct if within one grid of the truth (video length / 16, e.g. 7.5 s for a 2-minute video).
- "How long is this video? Reply with only the duration in mm:ss format." Counted correct if within 1/8 of the length.

Example answers, Baseline → After PR: the 2-minute video turning red at 78 s, `00:21` → `01:17`; the 8-minute video's length, `00:31` → `07:59`.

Setup: FP8 checkpoint, TP4 on one GB200 node, requests via `video_url`, greedy, thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`), `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`. Number of correct answers out of 20 videos:

| Frame sampling (`media_io_kwargs` video settings) | Question | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (32 frames) | when does the color change | 5/20, median error 35 s | 19/20, median error 2 s |
| default (32 frames) | how long is the video | 4/20 | 20/20 |
| `num_frames: 64` | when does the color change | 2/20, median error 37 s | 12/20, median error 7 s |
| `num_frames: 64` | how long is the video | 4/20 | 20/20 |
| `num_frames: 8` | when does the color change | 2/20, median error 45 s | 3/20, median error 36 s |
| `num_frames: 8` | how long is the video | 0/20 | 11/20 |
| `fps: 2` | when does the color change | 0/20, median error 72 s | 6/20, median error 12 s |
| `fps: 2` | how long is the video | 0/20 | 20/20 |

The default-loader scores are the same in all three launches of each build. Loader settings are set per request (`media_io_kwargs`, server started with `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`). After PR is better for every setting; the remaining misses on "when" are the model's limit, not the labels: With 8 frames one grid spans a quarter of the clip, so the event cannot be placed closely. With `fps: 2`, the long clips become 120–960 frames.

Baseline sees the color change at the right fraction of the video but reports the label it was given, so only the ~30 s videos come out right. With the default sampling, the one After PR miss is the 8-minute video turning red at 72 s, answered `01:33` (one grid is 30 s there).

Text-only (6 prompts) and image (3 prompts) outputs are identical between Baseline and After PR in two of the three launch pairs that ran them. In the third, the After PR launch differs from all other launches, including another launch of the same build (4/9 identical), so the difference is launch-to-launch, not the change. The KV cache is the same size (3,614,670 tokens), so memory profiling with dummy videos is unchanged.

**Performance.** The fix adds a few host-side operations per video and leaves the prompt length unchanged (labels stay `mm:ss`), so no change is expected. Two measurements:

- Processor host time per video request (parse, HF processing, prompt update; 120 s clip, 4 pinned cores, 300 calls, builds alternated three times): 15.95–16.25 ms After PR, 16.02–17.13 ms Baseline. The new `_video_timestamps` takes 1.9 µs per video; Baseline's `arange(T) / 1 fps` took 4.6 µs.
- Serving, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL as above, streamed video requests (~1.4k prompt tokens, 64 output tokens, `ignore_eos`), each pair on one node:

| Pair | Concurrency 1, req/s (Baseline → After PR) | Concurrency 8, req/s (Baseline → After PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.42 → 2.40 | 14.41 → 14.63 |
| 2 (After PR launched first) | 2.50 → 2.53 | 15.04 → 13.47 |
| 3 | 2.36 → 2.39 (two nodes) | 14.79 → 14.32 (two nodes) |
| 4 | 2.11 → 2.16 | 14.28 → 14.94 |

At concurrency 1 the builds are within 2.5%. At concurrency 8 and 32 this workload varies a lot between launches of the same build: two Baseline launches on one node gave 14.28 and 11.18 req/s at concurrency 8 (−22%) and 12.12 and 10.40 at 32 (−14%), so the After PR differences there (−10% to +23%) are within launch-to-launch variation.

**Tests.** `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mimo_v2_omni.py` (CPU, public `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` config and tokenizer, no weights): 11 passed After PR. On Baseline, `test_labels_use_frame_media_time` fails for both the plain and the `MediaWithBytes` (serving) input (`second_per_grid_ts` 2.0, expected 16.0).

## Details

- **Root cause.** The data parser dropped the loader metadata (`video_needs_metadata` was off), so `_get_hf_mm_inputs` saw only frames and stamped them `arange(T) / 1 fps`. The HF processor derives the grid spacing (`second_per_grid_ts`) from those stamps, and `get_video_replacement` writes labels as `start + j * second_per_grid_ts`. Labels were right only when the loader happened to sample at exactly 1 fps.
- **Fix.** Enable `video_needs_metadata` in the MiMo data parser and stamp frames from `frames_indices / fps`, evenly spaced from the first to the last sampled frame. The loaders sample (nearly) uniformly, and the labels are arithmetic steps from the first two stamps, so even spacing keeps them consistent. Inputs without timing (raw arrays, PIL frames, metadata without `frames_indices` or `fps`) keep 1 s spacing instead of being rejected, and so does a clip whose first and last sampled frame are the same (for example a one-frame clip that a loader pads to two frames), which would otherwise give equal timestamps and a division by zero in the processor. Dummy profiling videos are raw arrays, so profiling is unchanged.
- **Not changed.** The `video_audio` conversion loop: the data parser has no `video_audio` modality, so serving never reaches it.
- **Remaining error on very long clips.** `second_per_grid_ts` is cast to bf16, so a 75 min clip's 290.3 s grid step becomes 290 s and the last label is 4.5 s early. #64477 fixes the same cast for Qwen2.5-VL.
- **Related work.** #65581 also targets #65523 but reads `frames_indices` / `fps` as attributes of the frame array, which never has them (the parser has dropped the metadata by then), so it always falls back to 1 fps. ziywang50 claimed the issue first and handed it over in the thread; the approach follows the diagnosis ngutten posted there.

title: [CI] Fix B200 nightly gsm8k evals: ReplaySSM and DeepEP LL
author: csahithi
body:
## Overview

Fixes two NVIDIA B200 nightly gsm8k eval failures on `main` with config-only changes (6 YAML files, no library code).One is a regression from #63231's new default block size. The other is an intermittent NVSHMEM startup hang in the DeepEP low-latency (LL) evals.

## Claims

- **`(B200) [Nightly] LM Eval ReplaySSM`**: since #63231, startup fails with `Invalid prefix_match_unit=327`. Fixed by pinning `--block-size 16`.
- **`(B200) [Nightly] MoE Refactor DP Integration TEMPORARY`** (the 4 `*deepep-ll` configs): startup intermittently hangs until the timeout after NVSHMEM's IB transport fails (`ibv_modify_qp failed`). Fixed by keeping NVSHMEM off the NICs on one node. This is the same env `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py` already uses (#61695). **See the caveat under Details.**
- No pass criteria change: thresholds, tolerance, question counts, acceptance-length minimums, prefix-cache-hit checks and timeouts are untouched. Nothing is skipped or retried.

## Validation

Before/after runs on B200:

| Config | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Nemotron-3-Super-120B ReplaySSM-align (2×B200) | `ValueError: Invalid prefix_match_unit=327; ... Got group block sizes=[5248, ...]` | accuracy 0.9295 (threshold 0.93, tol 0.08), 861,972 prefix-cache hit tokens, acceptance 4.261 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NvFp4-CT-fi-cutedsl-deepep-ll (2×B200) | not reproduced locally (see notes) | passed; NVSHMEM falls back from IBGDA to NVLink |

```bash
cd tests
pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/models-replayssm.txt
pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor-dp-ep/config-b200.txt -k deepep-ll
```

Notes on these runs:
- **Separate patch applied.** The runs also had an unrelated worker patch applied: it releases warmup KV blocks before CUDA graph capture and is going up as a separate PR.
  - ReplaySSM and the DeepEP evals use `--enforce-eager`, so that patch is inactive for them.
- **ReplaySSM teardown.** In the "after" run every eval assertion passed. Pytest reported a failure only in the teardown GPU-memory check, because another eval was running on the node's other GPUs at the same time.
- **DeepEP.** Our two GPUs shared a CPU socket, so the hang didn't reproduce locally; the evidence is the CI logs below. Only one of the four configs was run; the env is identical in all four.

CI history across the 23 scheduled `main` builds from Oct 28 to Nov 6:
- **ReplaySSM:** passed in its first run ([100175](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100175#01a1aa87-b0dd-4ef6-ae65-300c2ae603a7)). It has failed in every build since #63231 merged: 100339, 100488, 100546 and [100655](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100655#01a1b23f-8c17-43cc-8493-9ac255a449ef).
- **DeepEP LL:** `ibv_modify_qp failed`, then "nvshmem setup connections failed", then the startup timeout. This happened in 9 shards across 8 of 19 regular builds (e.g. [100339](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100339#01a1ad1b-67f9-4e75-ad00-df2f4b92175c)), on 5 different hosts, before and after both PRs above.

## Details

**ReplaySSM.** `--prefix-match-unit 327` was chosen to divide the hybrid attention/Mamba page of 16×327 = 5232 tokens, as the config's own comment says. With #63231's 64-token default block size, the page becomes 64×82 = 5248 tokens. 327 doesn't divide that, so startup validation rejects the config. Pinning `--block-size 16` restores the page the test was designed around, including the shared 654-token few-shot boundary; changing the match unit instead would move that boundary. Tradeoff: this config no longer runs with the 64-token default.

**DeepEP LL.** On a single node, the DP peer is reachable over NVLink, but NVSHMEM still sets up its IB transport. On some host/GPU pairings `ibv_modify_qp` fails and the workers never exit.
- `NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` removes the IB transport.
- `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST=none` hides the NICs from IBGDA, which DeepEP forces on.

The DeepEP LL path and kernels are unchanged; only NVSHMEM's transport moves to NVLink.

> [!WARNING]
> **Caveat: this depends on the NVSHMEM host library version.** With the NICs hidden, IBGDA fails to initialize. What happens next depends on the version:
> - NVSHMEM 3.4.5 (via torch 2.14.0, the regular CI image) leaves the IBGDA device state at its "invalid" sentinel, so DeepEP's `num_rc_per_pe >= num_local_experts` check (`csrc/kernels/legacy/internode_ll.cu:284`) passes trivially.
> - NVSHMEM 3.6 and later leaves the state zeroed, so the check fails and DeepEP aborts.
>
> In practice:
> - **Regular image:** this fixes the hang. `test_moe_layer.py` passes there with the same env.
> - **Torch-nightly image (NVSHMEM 3.7.2):** these four configs would fail on every host instead of on some hosts. `test_moe_layer[...-deepep_low_latency-2-1-True]` already fails this way in every torch-nightly build checked (98680, 99535, 99905, 100546).
> - **After the torch 2.15 upgrade** (#60324, which brings NVSHMEM 3.7.2): the regular lane will hit the same assertion, here and in `test_moe_layer.py`. That needs its own fix: in DeepEP (skip the check when all peers are reachable over NVLink), in NVSHMEM, or in the image's NVSHMEM pin.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR changes these configs or fixes these failures. I searched open PRs and issues for ReplaySSM / `prefix_match_unit`, Kimi-K3 DSpark, `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens`, `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST`, and deepep_low_latency with NVSHMEM. No upstream commit has touched `tests/evals/gsm8k/` since `10c8574264`. Related issue: #66192.

**CI coverage.** All three are B200 nightly steps, so please trigger the nightly B200 LM Eval and MoE Refactor DP steps on this PR.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance. I have reviewed every changed line.

title: [Bugfix] Do not initialize CUDA when importing vendored FLA
author: aijanai
body:
## Purpose

Importing the vendored FLA (`vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/utils.py`) initializes CUDA: platform detection calls `triton.runtime.driver.active.get_current_target()`, which goes through `torch.cuda.current_device()`, and the Hopper check calls `torch.cuda.get_device_name` / `get_device_capability`. For models whose layers import FLA at module level (GDN: Qwen3-Next/3.5, Olmo, Kimi GDN; Bailing linear attention; KDA), this happens in the API-server process while the engine config is built. vLLM then logs `We must use the spawn multiprocessing start method ... Reasons: CUDA is initialized` and spawns the engine core, which re-imports torch and vLLM.

This PR uses `current_platform` (NVML-based, no CUDA context) for the vendor and Hopper checks, so the engine core can be forked as by default.

## Test Plan

- Build the engine config for a Qwen3.5-style GDN model (`EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`) and check `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` afterwards.
- `vllm serve` startup on DGX Spark (GB10), same node, 3 starts after a discarded warm-up, page cache evicted, warm compile caches; check the spawn warning and greedy output.

## Test Result

- `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` after `create_engine_config()`: `True` before, `False` after.
- The forced-spawn warning disappears and torch is imported once instead of twice.
- Qwen3.8 27B NVFP4 + MTP, time to `/health` ready: 41.3 ± 1.8 s with spawn, 37.6 ± 3.3 s with fork. Greedy output identical.

Models without FLA at module level (e.g. Nemotron-H) are unaffected: they were already forked.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen3.5] Replace FlashInfer GemmaRMSNorm JIT with Triton for arch<sm80
author: yassienashrafwasfy
body:
## Overview

Qwen3.5's RMSNorm no longer JIT-compiles FlashInfer kernels on sm75 (T4). Fixes #66288.

## Claims

- Qwen3.5 starts on sm75 without building the FlashInfer `norm` module (previously a ~1 min slower cold start, or `Ninja build failed` / `cannot find -lcuda` where nvcc cannot link).
- SM80+ behaviour is unchanged.
- T4 decode is within ~3% of the warm FlashInfer kernel; GSM8K is unchanged.

## Validation

2xT4, Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, TP=2, `--dtype half`, `--max-model-len 4096`, FlashInfer cache cleared before each server.

`pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/test_rms_norm.py`
- without the fix: 1 failed in 50 s (`Building JIT module norm` -> `cannot find -lcuda` -> `Ninja build failed`)
- with the fix: 2 passed, 2 skipped (bf16 unsupported on T4)

| | FlashInfer norm | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| startup | 139 s (needs a libcuda stub) | 81 s |
| GSM8K (200 q, chat, thinking off) | 0.535 | 0.540 |
| output tok/s (3 runs, 512 in / 128 out, concurrency 8) | 428 / 426 / 420 | 419 / 415 / 412 |
| mean TPOT | 15.0-15.3 ms | 15.4-15.7 ms |

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
  --max-tokens 512 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --num-questions 200 --seed 42
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 48 --max-concurrency 8
```

`tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py` + `test_qsa_prepare.py` on T4: 44 failed before, 43 after, none newly failing (the remaining failures also occur without this change). The padded-QK test, which hit the same JIT error before, now passes.

Startup times are single cold runs.

## Details

- `Qwen3_5RMSNorm` now subclasses `GemmaRMSNorm`. It uses FlashInfer when `has_device_capability(80) and has_flashinfer()`, otherwise `ir.ops.rms_norm` / `fused_add_rms_norm`.
- The `ir` path passes the Gemma weight `(1 + w)` computed in fp32 and cast to the activation dtype, so the fused vllm_c kernels are selected. The rounding is of the same order as the fp16 output rounding and is within the `ir` test tolerance. With an fp32 weight decode was ~366-372 tok/s.
- The FlashInfer path updates `x` and `residual` in place; the `ir` path returns new tensors. All callers use the returned values.
- `has_flashinfer()` does not detect a missing `flashinfer-jit-cache` on CUDA < 12.9.
- `qsa_indexer.py` (qwen4_exp) now calls its existing `GemmaRMSNorm` modules instead of `flashinfer.norm.gemma_rmsnorm`; the fake norm in `test_qsa_reference.py` is a real `GemmaRMSNorm`.
- CI runs on SM100, so it covers the FlashInfer path; there is no sm75 runner.

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Validate CLI stochastic rounding against the platform
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- `arg_utils.py`: re-run `MambaConfig.__post_init__()` after the CLI Mamba overrides, instead of only `validate_ssu_algorithm()`.
- `test_arg_utils.py`: regression test that `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding` on a non-CUDA platform fails at config time with the platform error.

`MambaConfig.__post_init__` rejects Mamba cache stochastic rounding on non-CUDA platforms and, for the Triton backend, on anything other than SM100, because the Triton kernels use the PTX `cvt.rs.f16x2.f32` instruction. `EngineArgs.create_engine_config` copies the default `MambaConfig` (where the flag is off) and only then sets `enable_stochastic_rounding` from the CLI, so those checks never ran for the CLI flag and only `validate_ssu_algorithm()` was called again. On MI355 a Nemotron-3-Super ReplaySSM server with `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding` got through config and died in warmup with `RuntimeError: LLD failed to link hsaco ... ld.lld: error: target emulation unknown`. With this change the same command fails at config time with the intended "only supported on NVIDIA CUDA platforms" error. `__post_init__` only does validation, so running it again is safe and also keeps future checks there in sync with the CLI path.

No open PR fixes this (searched open PRs for "stochastic rounding mamba", "enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding", "MambaConfig validate", "mamba_config __post_init__"). #61191 changes the backend override a few lines above and also adds a test after `test_attention_config`, so whichever lands second gets a trivial test-file conflict. #59814 adds a separate SR + speculation check in `VllmConfig` and does not overlap.

### Validation

On MI350X (gfx950), from `tests/`:

| Command | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest engine/test_arg_utils.py -k test_mamba_stochastic_rounding_cli_platform_check` | fails: no platform error, a later float16-cache check fires instead | 10/10 passed in a row |
| `pytest -v -s engine/test_arg_utils.py` | - | 118 passed |
| `pytest -v -s test_config.py -k mamba` | - | 5 passed |
| Engine Core CI command (`pytest -v -s engine test_sequence.py test_config.py test_logger.py test_vllm_port.py jit_monitor/test_hooks.py jit_monitor/test_hooks_gpu.py`) | - | 691 passed, 5 skipped (none in the changed test file) |
| `vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8 ... --mamba-backend triton --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --use-replayssm` | crashes in warmup (LLD link error) | `ValueError` at config time |

pre-commit is clean on both files. This is a config validation change only, so no model eval or perf numbers apply.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Let the FP8 MoE oracle fall back when the global AITER flag can't serve the layer
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

With only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, the FP8 MoE oracle now prefers AITER and falls back when AITER can't serve the layer, instead of raising. Unblocks the MI355 Nemotron-3-Super FP8 ReplaySSM mirror in #66318.

## Claims

- `oracle/fp8.py`: only an explicit `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` (set and enabled) forces the AITER FP8 MoE backend. The global flag leaves AITER first in the priority list and the normal auto selection decides.
- `test_moe_kernel_oracle.py`: `test_fp8_aiter_env_selection` covers the env combinations (global flag falls back, global flag still picks AITER when supported, explicit MoE flag still raises, either flag at 0 removes AITER).

## Validation

All runs on gfx950.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py`, without the `fp8.py` change | `global-falls-back` fails, the other 4 new cases pass |
| Same file with the change, 10 runs in a loop | 10/10, 69 passed each |
| Same file after rebasing on current main | 69 passed |
| `test_unquantized_backend_selection.py`, `test_mxfp8_aiter_backend_selection.py`, `test_fp8_tp_loading.py` | 73 passed, 9 skipped |
| `tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k "moe or fp8"` | 56 passed, 3 skipped |
| `tests/quantization/test_online.py -k moe` | 69 passed, 1 failed (`test_online_lut_b_moe`: `lut_b_moe` is not supported on ROCm, unrelated) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B `--quantization fp8`, only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` | `Using AITER Fp8 MoE backend`, so AITER is still picked where it works |
| #66318 mirror: Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8, TP2 + EP, ReplaySSM + MTP, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` | Without the change: `ValueError: Fp8 MoE backend 'AITER' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support no act_and_mul MLP layer.` With it: `TRITON` is picked, GSM8K 3/3 pass (0.9348, 0.9310, 0.9287; acceptance length 4.24) |

Mirror command, from `tests/`: `pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=<the #66318 Nemotron-3-Super config>`.

## Details

`select_fp8_moe_backend` treated the global `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` the same as an explicit AITER MoE request and returned `return_or_raise(AITER)`. Layers AITER can't serve, like the non-gated (no `act_and_mul`) MoE in Nemotron-3-Super FP8, then failed at startup and auto selection never got to Triton. Now the explicit path is only taken when `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` is set, so `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1` and `--moe-backend aiter` still raise as before, and setting either flag to 0 still removes AITER. The unquantized oracle already falls back in this case (#56590), and the other MoE oracles have no such forced path.

Overlap: draft #60839 (open since 2026-10-09, last commit the same day, `needs-rebase`) has the same `oracle/fp8.py` hunk, together with an AITER custom all-reduce fallback and a Qwen-specific test in `test_fp8_tp_loading.py`. This PR is only the MoE oracle part, rebased on current main, with an env-selection test that fails without the fix. Happy to close either one in favour of the other.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Re-prepare model state after extensible KV cache extension (Kimi-K3 AMD specialized decode)
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

With the extensible KV cache (#56492, on by default with MRV2 on CUDA and ROCm), the first eager decode step after startup kills a Kimi-K3 engine on AMD with `decode_backend=latency_specialized`. This adds a `ModelState.rebind_kv_cache` hook that `extend_kv_cache` calls once it has re-bound the KV views, and Kimi-K3's AMD model state re-runs `prepare_kv()` there.

Found while validating #63486, which disables the extensible KV cache in its Kimi-K3 engine tests until this lands.

## Claims

- Kimi-K3 AMD specialized decode (eager steps) now works with the extensible KV cache. Before this change every TP rank raised `RuntimeError: Kimi-K3 specialized decode: the KV cache was re-bound without prepare_kv`.
- Model states can see the final KV views through a hook that does nothing by default. The safety guard in `SpecializedDecode.plan()` is unchanged.

## Validation

**New test, failing before the fix** (`tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_engine_rebinds_model_state_to_extended_views`, a real Qwen3-0.6B engine, in process). On `main` (5629b26146), with only `raising=False` added, since `main` has no hook to patch:
```
E       AssertionError: assert [] == [(163456, {'model.layers.0.self_attn.attn': (139321971572736, 5356126208), ...})]
```
With the fix it passes: the hook runs exactly once, with the final `num_gpu_blocks` and exactly the views in `runner.kv_caches_by_layer`.

**End to end, 8x MI355X, Kimi-K3 8-layer dummy, TP8/DCP8, DSpark k=3.** These use #63486's `tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_e2e_parity.py` with the extensible KV cache on.

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_layer_kernels_match_vllm_layers` (eager) | 1 failed: every rank raises `re-bound without prepare_kv` right after `Extended KV cache to 2460 blocks (14.19 GiB)` | 1 passed (with #63486's NaN-aware `conv_bits`*) |
| `test_verify_steps_replay_the_kernels` (FULL graphs captured before extension) | not reached | 2 passed |

\* Blocks committed during warmup keep their warmup contents. One slot's three unread conv-state entries held NaN in both the kernel's state and the reference, and `torch.equal` treats NaN as unequal. #63486 compares those entries NaN-aware.

Other runs:
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_runtime.py`: 141 passed. This includes `test_plan_refuses_a_kv_cache_bound_behind_its_back`.
- `test_engine_pads_segments_without_a_connector` failed once because another container was holding GPUs 0-3 on the shared host. It passed on an idle GPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`: 51 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on all changed files.

CI: the new test runs in `V1 Executor + Worker` (`pytest -v -s v1/worker`, and its AMD mirror). The Kimi-K3 e2e checks need 8x MI355X and run in #63486's Kimi-K3 monokernel steps.

## Details

**Root cause.** With the extensible KV cache, `initialize_kv_cache` binds views that span the whole reservation, and `ModelState.initialize_kv_cache` sees those. After warmup and capture, `extend_kv_cache` commits the measured size. It then rebuilds every view over the same addresses with the final block count (`committed_views`) and re-binds them with `bind_kv_caches`, but it never notifies the model state. `SpecializedDecode.prepare_kv()` records `(data_ptr, numel)` of a KDA state, and `plan()` refuses to run on caches it has not checked. The numel changes, so the first eager step fails. FULL graphs replay without calling `plan()`, which is why only eager steps (and graph-padding fallbacks) hit it.

**Design.** `ModelState.rebind_kv_cache(kv_cache_config)` does nothing by default. `extend_kv_cache` calls it at the end of the `committed is not None` branch, which runs only when views were rebuilt, after binding and the replayssm re-init. `KimiK3ModelState` overrides it to re-run `prepare_kv()`. That call is a TP CPU-group collective. It is safe here because every worker reaches `extend_kv_cache` through the same `collective_rpc`, and whether views get rebuilt depends only on the layout.

Alternatives I rejected:
- Calling `initialize_kv_cache` again. It does one-time setup; for example, DSv4.1's state releases metadata graphs that already-captured FULL graphs use.
- Keying on `data_ptr` alone. That would silently accept a re-bind whose geometry changed, which is exactly what the guard exists to catch.
- Re-preparing lazily in `plan()`. That puts a collective inside the forward pass, including during graph capture.

**Other model states, audited and unchanged.** Kimi-K3 NVIDIA and Muse Spark NVIDIA call `plan()` only at capture, and the addresses do not change. MiniMax-M3 AMD binds capacity views and checks staleness by `data_ptr`. The DSv4/DSv4.1 and Muse Spark AMD mono runtimes read pointers and strides on every launch. hisparse and replayssm are already re-bound in `extend_kv_cache`.

**Supersedes #66357.** #66357 makes the same runtime change (the no-op `ModelState.rebind_kv_cache` hook, the call from `extend_kv_cache`, and the Kimi-K3 AMD override). This PR also factors out `_prepare_kv()`, updates the related docstrings and the `plan()` error text, and tests through a real engine, so #66357 is closed in favour of this one.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Don't reopen reasoning after the prompt closed it
author: 2arian3
body:
## Overview

On the Rust frontend, structured outputs are not enforced when the chat template closes reasoning in the prompt, for example Qwen3 with `enable_thinking: false`. The output grammar still offers a new reasoning block, the model opens one, and `content` comes back as `<think>...` text instead of the requested JSON. This PR makes the grammar start at the visible output in that case, as the Python frontend does.

## Claims

- For reasoning parsers built on `DelimitedReasoningParser`, a prompt whose last reasoning boundary is the end marker now gets only its unconsumed separator followed by the visible-output grammar, without the optional reasoning block.
- With thinking disabled, Rust frontend responses now satisfy `response_format` / `structured_outputs` and are identical to the Python frontend's on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-8B.
- Prompts that open reasoning or have no reasoning boundary (thinking enabled) are unchanged: output is byte-identical to before.

## Validation

H100 MIG 1g.24gb, driver 580.105.08, torch 2.14.0+cu132. "Before" and "after" are local release builds of `vllm-rs` without and with this change; their `rust/` is identical to this PR's base `7a90549f7e`. Rust unit tests ran on macOS.

**Repro** (served with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3`, plus `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.8` for the MIG slice):

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Describe a cat."}],
  "max_tokens": 200, "temperature": 0,
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
  "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "animal", "schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}, "legs": {"type": "integer"}},
    "required": ["name", "legs"]}}}
}'
```

| | finish_reason | content |
|---|---|---|
| Python frontend | `stop` | `{ "name": "A Cat", "legs": 4 }` |
| Rust, before | `length` | `<think>\nOkay, I need to describe a cat. Let me start by thinking about what makes a cat unique...` |
| Rust, after | `stop` | `{ "name": "A Cat", "legs": 4 }` |

**Constraint validity with thinking disabled** (greedy, streaming and non-streaming; 5 prompts on 0.6B, 10 on 8B; servers also had `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --seed 0`; valid = content parses and matches the constraint):

| Model | Constraint | Python | Rust before | Rust after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B | `json_schema` | 10/10 | 4/10 | 10/10 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | `json_object` | 10/10 | 4/10 | 10/10 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | `choice` | 10/10 | 6/10 | 10/10 |
| Qwen3-8B | `json_schema` | 20/20 | 10/20 | 20/20 |
| Qwen3-8B | `json_object` | 14/20 | 8/20 | 14/20 |
| Qwen3-8B | `choice` | 20/20 | 6/20 | 20/20 |

The Python `json_object` misses on 8B are long answers cut off at `max_tokens=200`. A `regex` constraint gave the same counts on all three (6/10 and 4/20; the model repeats digits until `max_tokens`).

- Thinking disabled: Rust-after content equals Python's in 40/40 requests on 0.6B and 80/80 on 8B (four constraint types).
- Thinking enabled: Rust-after output (content and reasoning) equals Rust-before in 40/40 requests on 0.6B and 10/10 on 8B.
- A 121-request differential suite (completions, chat, tools, logprobs, errors) differs between before and after only in the `json_schema` case, plus random request ids in two error messages.

**Tests**

```
# new e2e test, test_completion_with_function_calling.py (runs in the Rust Frontend Tool Use step)
pytest ... -k test_response_format_with_thinking_disabled
  Python frontend      -> 2 passed
  Rust, before         -> 2 failed (JSONDecodeError; content '<think>\nOkay, I need to describe a cat...')
  Rust, after          -> 2 passed
pytest test_completion_with_function_calling.py -k "not test_no_args_tool_call"   (Rust, after) -> 30 passed

# rust/
cargo test -p vllm-parser                -> 627 passed (both prompt_closed_reasoning_* tests fail on main)
cargo fmt --all -- --check               -> clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings -> clean
```

<details>
<summary>Local environment notes</summary>

`cargo test -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server` passes except for tests that fail here regardless of this change: `roundtrip_{qwen3,mimo_v26,kimi_k25,step5}` fail identically on main (local HF files: the Step-5 config has no `vocab_size`, and the Qwen3 fixture differs only in `all_stop_token_ids`); `audio_pipeline_attributes_stage_timings_to_request` and `chat_completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_seeded_sample` failed once in the full parallel run and pass when run alone.

</details>

No model eval: logits and sampling are untouched. Only the grammar sent for structured-output requests whose prompt closed reasoning changes, which the results above cover.

## Details

**Root cause.** `DelimitedReasoningParser::wrap_visible_format` (added in #57340) treats two different prompt states the same way: no reasoning boundary in the prompt, and a prompt that already closed reasoning. Both get `optional(<think> ... </think>)` in front of the visible grammar. With thinking disabled, Qwen3's template renders `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`, and the model takes the optional block. It spells `<think>` with ordinary tokens (27, 26865, 397), so the output parser, which matches markers by token identity, keeps the block in `content`. The Python frontend checks the prompt in `resolve_reasoning_ended` and applies the plain grammar from the first token.

**Change.**
- `delimited.rs`: record whether the prompt's last boundary is the end marker, and in that case return the unconsumed separator plus the visible grammar. The removed `pending_after` branch was only reachable in that case.
- `prompt_closed_reasoning_keeps_only_unconsumed_separator` and HY3's `grammar_root_follows_prompt_reasoning_state` pinned the optional block for a closed prompt and now expect the visible grammar. A new test covers Qwen3, DeepSeek V3, GLM-4.5 and Nemotron V3 with their thinking-disabled prompt endings.

This affects `qwen3`, `deepseek_r1`, `deepseek_v3`, `glm45`, `hy`, `step3p5` and the parsers aliased to them (MiniMax M2, Step3, DeepSeek V4/V4.1, GLM-4.7/5, Kimi K2, MiMo, Nemotron V3).

**Relation to other PRs.** I found no issue or PR for this. #65397 and #60815 (both drafts) edit the same files but do not change the closed-prompt case.

**Limitations.** Real-checkpoint runs used Qwen3 only; the other families are covered by the unit tests. Not run on ROCm.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Avoid host synchronization in dots.ocr vision encoder
author: nulllt2
body:
## Overview

Running `dots.ocr` image inference with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` currently crashes before returning an OCR result. The vision encoder builds position indices on the CPU and computes sequence metadata on the GPU, triggering host-device transfers and host reads that trip the synchronization check (Fixes [#66243](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/66243)).

## Claims

This PR resolves the synchronization overhead in the shared `dots.ocr` / `dots.mocr` vision encoder by:

1. Allocating position indices directly on the model device (`self.device`) so rotary embedding lookups don't trigger cross-device copies.
2. Computing cumulative sequence boundaries (`cu_seqlens`) and `max_seqlen` directly on the CPU from the existing Python `grid_thw` list via `itertools.accumulate`, avoiding blocking H2D copies, `repeat_interleave` host-read sizing, and `.item()` calls.
3. Transferring cumulative lengths asynchronously via `async_tensor_h2d` (keeping `int32` for normal inference and preserving the `int64` branch for TorchScript tracing).
4. Dropping the unused `grid_thw` tensor argument from the patch-embedding call.

## Validation

### Test Plan

#### 1. Unit & Distributed Tests (`tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py`)

Tested on 2x RTX 4090 GPUs (Python 3.12.11, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.22.2) against baseline `cf5cea2da37d3dfed27d2e0aa3041c3e553c2d57` using `rednote-hilab/dots.ocr` (`c0111ce6bc07803dbc267932ffef0ae3a51dc951`, bf16, eager mode).

- `vision_without_host_sync`: Warms up a small vision model and runs the forward pass under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`.
- `tensor_parallel_without_host_sync`: Runs `vllm_runner` with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (prefix and multimodal processor caches disabled), verifying OCR outputs at TP=1 and TP=2 and comparing logprobs via `check_logprobs_close`.

### Test Result

#### 1. Synchronization Check (Before vs. After)

```bash
# Baseline (cf5cea2da): fails with synchronization errors
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py \
  -k vision_without_host_sync -v -s
# FAILED: 1 failed, 1 deselected
# rotary_pos_emb = rotary_pos_emb_full[pos_ids].flatten(1)
# RuntimeError: called a synchronizing CUDA operation

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py \
  -k tensor_parallel_without_host_sync -v -s
# FAILED during image inference:
# RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()

# This PR: passes both checks
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3,1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py -v -s
# 2 passed, 2 warnings in 212.28s

```

#### 2. Numerical Equivalence Across Backends

Compared output embeddings (`rtol=0, atol=0`) using a seeded 2-layer vision model across two grid shapes (`[[1, 4, 6]]` and `[[2, 4, 6], [1, 6, 8]]`):

| Vision Backend | Baseline vs. Patch (Both Grids) | `set_sync_debug_mode("error")` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashAttention 2 | Bit-identical | Passed |
| Triton | Bit-identical | Passed |
| Torch SDPA | Bit-identical | Fails in `torch_sdpa_wrapper` (`.tolist()`) |

*Note: `torch_sdpa_wrapper` still reads device sequence lengths via `.tolist()`, which is outside the scope of this model-level fix.*

#### 3. End-to-End OCR Regression Check

Evaluated 3 synthetic PIL-rendered images via `LLM.generate` (TP=1, greedy decoding, seed 0, `max_tokens=32`, top-5 logprobs, `max_model_len=1024`, `max_num_seqs=2`, 256 MiB KV cache, caches disabled). Baseline ran with sync checks disabled; this patch ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:

| Image Text | Resolution | Baseline Output | Patch Output | Token IDs & Top-5 Logprobs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HELLO 1234` | 448 × 224 | `HELLO 1234` | `HELLO 1234` | Exact match |
| `TOTAL 56` | 224 × 336 | `TOTAL 56` | `TOTAL 56` | Exact match |
| `DATE 2026` | 448 × 336 | `DATE 2026` | `DATE 2026` | Exact match |

#### 4. Linting

```bash
uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/dots_ocr.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py \
  docs/models/supported_models.md \
  docs/usage/troubleshooting.md

```

All hooks (Ruff, markdownlint, mypy, test tethering) passed. The added `core_model` and `distributed(num_gpus=2)` tests map directly to the existing multimodal and distributed CI lanes.

## Details

**Related work:**

- [#64543](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64543) (merged) fixed QKV splitting at TP > 1, which is a separate issue.
- [#63074](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63074) (open) adds encoder CUDA graph support and overlaps with the CPU sequence-metadata change, but leaves CPU-allocated position indices in place. This PR focuses strictly on fixing the remaining synchronization bugs and adding regression coverage without introducing graph changes.
