title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Build DSv4.1 replay builders at warmup and the DSv4/DSv4.1 mono runner at load
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR stops two DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 builds from running inside the first real step, where `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` raises on them. The DSv4.1 decoder-replay attention builders are now built on the first warmup batch. The DSv4/DSv4.1 mono decode runner (peer memory included) is now built at load. Neither site is wrapped in `gpu_sync_allowed()`.

This is part of a 5-PR series that replaces the allow-wrap approach of #64176. In that PR, the review asked for the syncs to be fixed, not allowed. The CI failures by site (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97758, https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532):
- **Replay builders** (`indexer.py` `dcp_rank_tensor`): (MI355) DeepSeek V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics and (MI300) DeepSeek V4.1 gfx942 Mono Decode Layers.
- **Mono runner** (`peer_memory.py:93`): only (MI355) DeepSeek V4 Pro Mono Decode Numerics, in `test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` at TP8. The DSv4.1 mono-runner sync never showed in CI, because the replay-builder failure came first; it was reproduced locally (see Validation).

The follow-up PR that wraps the test-only probe hooks and turns `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` back on in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` depends on this PR.

## Claims

- **DSv4.1 replay builders.** `DeepseekV41ModelState` built its copies of the decoder-replay attention groups lazily, in the first eager prefill step that trims a request to the SWA window. That runs every metadata builder's `__init__`, and the indexer builder's `dcp_rank_tensor = torch.tensor(..., device=...)` is a blocking H2D copy inside `execute_model`. The copies are now built on the first `prepare_attn` call, a warmup batch, for every config (before, only PCP>1 did this).
- **Mono runner at load.** The runner was built in the first decode step that took the mono path: IPC heap allocation, gloo handle exchange, `tp_agree`, and the blocking H2D copy of the peer addresses at `peer_memory.py:93`. It is now built in `process_weights_after_loading`, where every TP rank processes the same layers in the same order. For DSv4-Pro the layer's weights are also taken there, which moves the `torch.equal` check in `_scale_bytes` out of the step too.
- **No intended numeric change.** The same builders, runner and weights are built, only earlier. Eager greedy tokens match base token for token (see Validation).
- **CUDA is affected too.** `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py` is shared by CUDA and ROCm, and CUDA eager mode took the same in-step builder construction.

## Validation

All runs used MI355X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13 and amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1.

| Check | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| New unit test `test_replay_builders_built_before_first_trimmed_step` | fails at `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py:165`: `assert (None is None and 0 == 2)` | passes |
| E2E DSv4.1 replay repro, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, eager, TP1, mxfp4 indexer | `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `indexer.py` `dcp_rank_tensor` (same traceback as CI) | passes; also with the FP8 indexer (block 64, the gfx942 config) and with CUDA graphs plus decoder-replay graph capture |
| Eager greedy tokens, 4 prompts of 300-1203 tokens x 8 tokens | reference (base, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn`) | identical, token for token (mxfp4 and fp8 indexers) |
| E2E DSv4.1-Flash, 5 layers, dummy weights, TP2, `--monokernel`, eager, `enable_extensible_kv_cache=False`, `max_num_seqs=64` (so no warmup batch fits DSv4.1's 48-row mono limit), `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | base = `main` with the replay-builder site temporarily wrapped in `gpu_sync_allowed()` to get past it: exit 1, sync at `peer_memory.py:93` via `mono_decode.py` `_mono_runner` | exit 0, mono layer active inside the checked steps, no sync detected |
| `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[2-8]`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, TP2. Ran on the stacked series (all five PRs' fixes plus the probe-hook wrap; this PR's code there is identical apart from comment wording) | n/a | 1 passed (127 s); it would raise on any sync, and the log has no `sync detected` line |

**Partial, to be completed before leaving draft: DSv4-Pro at TP8.** `tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` (the only CI job that hit `peer_memory.py:93`) uses random weights and only the cached DeepSeek-V4-Pro config, but needs TP8 (the kernels require `TP_SIZE=8`). One attempt on this branch plus the probe-hook commit from #64176, under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: the first (mono-on) engine logged `DSv4 mono decode layer active (decode steps of <= 64 rows)` and generated all 8 prompts with no sync detected; the second (mono-off reference) engine then failed in KV-cache sizing (`No available memory for the cache blocks`) because other jobs on the shared host took GPU memory mid-run, so the mono-vs-reference comparison did not complete. To finish (tree: this branch plus the probe-hook commit; base: `main` plus only that commit):

```bash
cd tests && VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
  python -m pytest -v -s models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py
```

On current `main` the base is expected to pass too, because #62560's sampler warmup (`max_num_seqs=8`) builds the runner before the sync check (see Details), so this run checks that the PR does not regress the DSv4-Pro path rather than reproducing the CI failure.

The replay-builder fix alone is what lets the TP2 test get past its first prefill. Whether it also exercises the DSv4.1 mono at-load path depends on warmup (its `max_num_seqs` is within DSv4.1's 48-row limit, so on current `main` the sampler warmup builds the runner anyway); the `max_num_seqs=64` E2E row is the direct evidence for the DSv4.1 mono runner.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
# Unit tests on this branch: 147 passed, 2 skipped (test_deepseek_v41_pcp needs 8 GPUs)
cd tests && HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 python -m pytest -q \
  models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py \
  models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py \
  models/test_deepseek_v41_amd_replay_forward.py models/test_dsv4_mono_decode.py \
  models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py
```

Earlier, without the sync check, `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py`, `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py`, `test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` and `test_dsv4_mono_numerics.py` were run on 2 GPUs: 3 passed, 9 skipped (the skipped cases need 4 or 8 GPUs, or gfx942).

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.
</details>

**Model evaluation.** None was run. The change only moves when the same objects are constructed and does not touch any kernel or math path. Eager greedy outputs are token-identical to base, and the per-layer mono-vs-reference test `test_dsv41_mono_layers[2-8]` passes; the DSv4-Pro one is pending (above).

**Not covered locally:**
- **gfx942 / MI300** and the **DSv4.1 TP4** mono tests were not run. The gfx942 config was only covered by the TP1 FP8-indexer replay repro above.
- **DSpark draft runner:** it is now built at the draft model's load, but no DSpark speculative run was done.

## Details

**Root cause: replay builders.** Warmup dummy batches never trim, so `_prepare_replay_batch` skipped the lazy copy during warmup, and the first real trimmed eager prefill built every replay builder inside `execute_model`. With CUDA graphs, the replay-graph capture happened to build the copies at warmup, which hid the problem; the mono CI tests run with `enforce_eager=True`. The fix:
- `prepare_attn` builds the copies on its first call, for every config. In eager MRV2 without JIT warmup or the extensible KV cache, that first call is the sampler warmup's dummy run (#62560), before `enable_gpu_sync_check`.
- `capture_inner_cudagraphs` rebuilds the copies from the real groups instead of dropping them, because `profile_only` captures run on the pre-KV-cache groups.
- `_prepare_replay_batch` asserts that the copies exist instead of building them.

**Root cause: mono runner.** The runner depends only on the TP group, the rank, the device and static config; whether a warmup step built it first depended on the tree and the configuration. The failing CI job ran a tree (`a85566cc9`, 2026-10-28) from before #62560, which added the MRV2 sampler warmup dummy run. In that tree, an eager MRV2 run with `enable_jit_warmup=False` and no extensible KV cache (the CI config: `max_num_seqs=8`) ran no warmup forward with attention metadata (the profile run skips attention), so the first real decode step built the runner. Since #62560 (2026-11-02), the sampler warmup's dummy batch of `max_num_seqs` one-token requests is decode-only and builds the runner when `max_num_seqs` is within the mono kernels' row limit (48 for DSv4.1, 64 for DSv4-Pro), so by code reading (not yet run) the CI config no longer reproduces on current `main`; with more rows than that (the local DSv4.1 repro uses 64), or on a non-last PP rank, the first real decode step still builds it. The runner is now built at load:
- **DSv4.1:** a new `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.process_weights_after_loading` builds the target runner, or the draft runner for DSpark draft layers. `finalize_model_weights` runs it children-first in a fixed order, so the gloo handshake stays aligned across TP ranks. DSv4.1 `weights()` only takes views and has no sync, so it stays lazy.
- **DSv4-Pro:** the runner and the layer's weights are built at the end of `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading`, after the attn/gate_up preshuffle, because the weights need the preshuffled scales.
- The lazy build in `_mono_runner` stays as a fallback for direct callers such as the unit tests.

**Tradeoffs and limitations:**
- The mono IPC heap and runner buffers are now allocated at load, so the KV-cache sizing counts them. Before, they appeared after KV sizing.
- Eager non-PCP configs now always build the replay builder copies, and their device buffers, at warmup. CUDA-graph mode and PCP>1 already did. The cost is small and fixed.
- In graph mode the copies are built at the first capture `prepare_attn` and rebuilt in `capture_inner_cudagraphs`: a transient double construction, at warmup only.
- **Non-last PP ranks:** the MRV2 sampler warmup runs only on the last PP rank. On other ranks in eager mode without JIT warmup or the extensible KV cache, the first `prepare_attn` (and so the replay builders, like the existing lazy `_replay` upload there) is still a real step. The mono runner is unaffected, as it is built at load.
- **Weight reload:** DSv4-Pro `MonoLayerWeights` is still cached and not refreshed on reload, as before. One narrow new case: a weight update before the first decode step (for example a dummy load followed by an RL weight sync) now keeps the scales computed at load; before, they were captured lazily after the update.
- **Sleep mode (not verified):** with `--enable-sleep-mode`, the runner's torch-allocated buffers (for example `PeerBuffer.addresses`) are now allocated during load and may land in the CuMem `weights` pool. Level 2 sleep discards that pool, and the cached runner is not rebuilt on wake-up, so its buffers could hold stale data. Before, they were allocated at step time, outside the tagged pool. `--monokernel` with sleep level 2 should be treated as unsupported until checked.
- **Runner device:** it is taken from `attn_norm.weight.device`; before, from the activation's device. These are the same unless decoder-layer weights are CPU/UVA-offloaded.
- **Other models:** MiniMax-M3 and Kimi-K3 use a similar `PeerBuffer` build-in-step pattern. They did not fail in CI and are out of scope here.

**Duplicate-work check.** I searched open PRs for `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`, `gpu_sync_allowed`, sync rocm, and each site's keywords (`dcp_rank_tensor`, `_replay_attn_groups`, mono runner, `PeerBuffer`). No other open PR addresses these sites. #64176 is the submitter's own predecessor, which wrapped them in `gpu_sync_allowed()`; this series replaces that approach. #66003 removes a different allowed sync in the `ROCM_AITER_FA` builder and does not overlap.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement, validate and write this description.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Stash DiffusionGemma logprobs on device without host syncs
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes the per-step GPU->CPU syncs in `DiffusionSampler.__call__`'s logprobs stash (DiffusionGemma), which crash the engine under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` in the AMD "Entrypoints Integration (API Server Generate)" group (`tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_joint_e2e.py`). The logprobs of converging slots now go into a fixed-size device stash, written where the converged mask (known only on device) says so.

Part of the series that replaces the `gpu_sync_allowed()` wrapping in #64176 with real fixes (following `njhill`'s review there). The final PR in the series re-enables `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` and depends on this one.

Failing CI: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532 (`mi355-dpx-entrypoints-integration-api-server-generate`):

```
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py", line 1598, in __call__
    if just_converged.any():
RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
FAILED entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_joint_e2e.py::test_joint_one_canvas - ... 500
```

CUDA CI also runs `entrypoints/generate` (`docker/Dockerfile` sets `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`), but on an H200 MIG 35GB slice, where `test_joint_e2e.py` (`large_gpu_mark(min_gb=80)`) is skipped. So this path never ran under the sync check there.

## Claims

- With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, DiffusionGemma decode steps with logprobs requests (top-k, `logprob_token_ids`, read-only slots, constrained allowed-set reads) no longer sync with the host. The one exception is a top-k wider than 128, which needs a raised `--max-logprobs`: that path syncs explicitly under `gpu_sync_allowed()`, only in steps that contain such a request.
- The CI-failing path (structured decisions: read-only reads with `logprob_token_ids`, no `diffusion_constrained`) goes through the new Triton kernels with per-request token ids. The PyTorch fallback (`_tile_logprobs` + `_masked_stash_write`) serves only `diffusion_constrained` steps and non-CUDA platforms.
- On ROCm, logprob values, argmax, and ranks match `compute_topk_scores` bit for bit for non-read-only slots. Top-k ids differ from main only in the order of ids with tied values: the kernels order ties by lower id, `torch.topk` arbitrarily.
- Read-only slots: logprobs are still reported at temperature 1, and the argmax (column 0) is now taken from the same temperature-1 rows. Main took it from the schedule-tempered rows. On GPU the emitted token is `sample_row_stats`'s argmax of the raw rows, so column 0 now equals the emitted token (except on the wide top-k > 128 path, which keeps main's tempered argmax); main's could differ when the division by the temperature rounds two distinct top logits to the same value.
- The sampler step with logprobs is faster than main in every measured logprobs scenario (e.g. model defaults, all top-20: 4.72 -> 4.01 ms). Steps with no logprobs request are 10-20 us slower than main (e.g. 3.306 -> 3.326 ms at the defaults).
- The stash is `[max_num_reqs, canvas_length, 129]`, allocated in `DiffusionSampler.__init__` (during `load_model`, before memory profiling) and never resized: 3.2 MB at the model defaults.
- Two more syncs on the constrained-read path are fixed: `allowed_tensor` now uses `async_tensor_h2d`, and `_mask_rows_to_allowed` uses `index_fill_` instead of `keep[allowed] = True` (an `index_put_` of the Python scalar `True`).

## Validation

All runs: MI355X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13, single GPU per server, this branch unless noted. "main" is the merge base `fd0c471b3a`.

**The CI failure, end to end.** `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`:

```
$ cd tests && VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -v -s entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_joint_e2e.py
this PR: 6 passed (10/10 in a loop)
main:    6 failed, 1 error (teardown, after the server died)
  diffusion_gemma.py:1646 in __call__  (if just_converged.any():)
  RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
```

With a temporary print in `_stash_tile_logprobs`, all 22 stash calls in that run took the kernel branch (0 fallback), most of them with per-request token ids (`ids=3..52, k=0`).

**Fail before / pass after (unit).** With main's `diffusion_gemma.py` and `diffusion_gemma_sampler.py` swapped in, the three new sampler tests fail with the CI error:

```
$ cd tests && pytest -q v1/worker/test_gpu_diffusion_sampler.py -k "host_sync or full_vocab"   # main's model files
diffusion_gemma.py:1646: in __call__   (if just_converged.any():)
E   RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
diffusion_gemma.py:813: in allowed_tensor   (constrained-read test)
E   RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
3 failed
```

Reverting only the `allowed_tensor` fix, or only the `index_fill_` fix, fails `test_constrained_reads_report_their_allowed_ids_without_a_host_sync`, while `test_joint_e2e.py` still passes 6/6 under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. That unit case is the only coverage for those two fixes.

**Unit tests:**

```
$ cd tests && pytest -q v1/worker/test_gpu_diffusion_sampler.py v1/sample/test_diffusion_gemma_reads.py v1/sample/test_diffusion_sampler_stats.py
61 passed
$ VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -q <same files>
61 passed
$ for i in $(seq 10); do pytest -q v1/sample/test_diffusion_sampler_stats.py; done
33 passed, 10/10
```

`test_stashed_logprobs_match_compute_topk_scores` runs fp32 and bf16 logits. It checks the values, that every reported id holds its value, the first-index argmax and the rank exactly. The top-k id set is compared only where the cutoff is not tied. Ties are built explicitly: a 201-way tie that straddles every cutoff, and a row with 129 distinct maxima. With `torch.topk` patched to break ties toward the highest index (another valid choice), the previous version of this test fails 6/12 and this one passes 24/24.

**OpenAI server, PR vs main.** `/v1/completions`, 6 prompts x `logprobs` 5, 20 and 0, `max_tokens=128`, sent one at a time to a fresh server. Diffusion requests reject `temperature` and `seed`, so these use the model's own schedule with the default engine seed. A restarted main server reproduces main bit for bit, and so does main on the other GPU, so any difference below comes from the code.

| | PR vs main (both GPU assignments) |
|---|---|
| sampled tokens | 1510/1510 identical |
| sampled-token logprobs | bitwise identical (max abs diff 0.0) |
| top-k id sets | identical in 1510/1510 rows |
| top-k values | identical (max abs diff 0.0) |
| top-k order | 543 rows differ, all only between entries with equal values |

The first PR server ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, served every request, and logged no sync. `/v1/systemone` joint answers are identical to main. The non-joint answers differ between two main runs too, so they are not compared.

**Serving latency.** `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 0 --num-warmups 8` (plus `--logprobs 5`), server defaults (canvas 256). Each build ran each config twice on each of the two GPUs. The runs were interleaved main/PR, and the GPUs were swapped between rounds. A canvas comes out in one piece, so TTFT equals E2E and TPOT is 0.

| logprobs | metric | main (n=4, range) | PR (n=4, range) | PR vs main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | E2E mean (ms) | 2527 (2455-2591) | 2515 (2449-2584) | -0.5% |
| none | E2E p99 (ms) | 2596 (2494-2693) | 2556 (2504-2617) | -1.5% |
| none | output tok/s | 810 (790-834) | 814 (792-836) | +0.5% |
| 5 | E2E mean (ms) | 2644 (2585-2701) | 2519 (2472-2567) | -4.7% |
| 5 | E2E p99 (ms) | 2704 (2642-2774) | 2556 (2507-2596) | -5.4% |
| 5 | output tok/s | 771 (753-787) | 812 (797-827) | +5.3% |

Paired on the same GPU, the E2E mean changes by -0.2% / -0.8% without logprobs and -5.0% / -4.5% with `logprobs=5`. The 10-20 us/step no-logprobs cost from the sampler benchmark stays inside the run-to-run noise (about ±3%). With logprobs the PR is about as fast as no logprobs, while main pays about 4.5%.

<details>
<summary>All runs</summary>

| logprobs | build | run (GPU) | E2E mean | E2E p50 | E2E p99 | out tok/s | req/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | main | r1.1 (1) | 2522.82 | 2511.43 | 2693.26 | 811.25 | 3.17 |

</details>

**Sampler-level performance** (unchanged from before; sampler alone, V=262144, fp32 logits, mean GPU ms per step):

<details>
<summary>Table</summary>

| scenario | main, no logprobs | main | first take | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| canvas 16, step caps 2..8, 512 rows, all top-20 | 1.18 | 4.52 | 3.41 | 1.57 |
| same, 1 of 32 requests top-20 | 1.18 | 4.51 | 3.39 | 1.32 |
| canvas 16, 2048 rows, `logprob_token_ids` only | 3.28 | 14.47 | 5.84 | 3.95 |
| canvas 16, step where nothing converges, all top-20 (median) | 1.17 | 1.53 | 3.35 | 1.32 |
| model defaults (canvas 256, 8 seqs, 48 steps, caps 16..48), all top-20 | 3.31 | 4.72 | 9.80 | 4.01 |

| every slot converges every 2nd step, top-128 | 3.31 | 7.71 | 9.00 | 3.80 |

</details>

**CI steps, run locally.** I ran the "V1 Sample" and "V1 Executor + Worker" commands on this branch and on main, side by side on the same machine:

```
$ cd tests && pytest -v -s v1/sample
this PR: 1 failed, 317 passed, 43 skipped
main:    1 failed, 293 passed, 43 skipped
$ pytest -v -s v1/executor
this PR: 126 passed      main: 126 passed
$ pytest -v -s v1/worker
this PR: 1023 passed, 231 skipped      main: 1020 passed, 231 skipped
```

The one `v1/sample` failure, `test_logprobs.py::test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_with_chunking_and_preemption`, fails the same way on main (1/136 elements off by 0.2498 vs `atol=0.2`) and does not touch DiffusionGemma. The extra passes are this PR's new tests: 24 cases in `v1/sample` and 3 in `v1/worker`. Buildkite has not run on this PR yet.

**Not validated:** NVIDIA GPUs (the temperature division uses `tl.div_rn`, which is IEEE like torch's, but the bitwise match was only checked on ROCm), and gfx942/MI300.

## Details

**Root cause.** Which slots converged is only known on the device, after the compiled sample step. The stash read it back on every step that mattered: `just_converged.any()`, `.nonzero()`, two `.item()` calls per converged slot, and `num_sampled.cpu()` to pick the emitting slots.

**Fix.**
- Requests without logprobs are dropped on the host, where their sampling params are mirrored.
- `stash_converged_logprobs` (new, `diffusion_gemma_sampler.py`) runs chunked max/argmax, block-sum/rank, top-k, top-k merge, and write kernels over a (request, position, 16x1024-chunk) grid. Rows of slots that did not converge, and canvas padding, exit at once. The logsumexp is summed in the same 1024-wide blocks and order as `_topk_log_softmax_kernel`; top-k keys pack order-preserving fp32 bits with the inverted index, and the K-th largest block max bounds which elements are considered. The temperature is applied in the kernels, so no scaled `[rows, vocab]` copy is made.
- The output carries a canvas of rows for every logprobs request, with `cu_num_generated_tokens` known on the host. The scheduler slices each request by the tokens it emitted, so the host never needs to know which slots emitted, and stale rows are never read.
- Constrained (shared allowed-set) steps and non-CUDA platforms keep a PyTorch pass over the logprobs requests' rows (`_tile_logprobs`, the existing per-slot code moved into a helper, plus `_masked_stash_write`).

**Why this is so large** (+809/-99 in `vllm/`; the new code in `diffusion_gemma_sampler.py` is about 340 lines of Triton kernels and 150 of launcher). Simpler designs were measured and rejected:
- Wrapping the reads in `gpu_sync_allowed()` (#64176) leaves the syncs in place, which is the feedback this series answers.
- `compute_topk_scores` over every row on every step ("first take") is sync-free but about 2x slower than main at the model defaults (9.80 vs 4.72 ms).
- Kernels for argmax/logsumexp/rank with `torch.topk` still over every row: 8.51 ms at the defaults, still slower than main, because almost no slot converges on a given step at canvas 256 / 48 steps.

Splitting into a minimal sync-free fix plus a follow-up kernel PR was considered; the minimal fix alone would regress logprobs steps about 2x, so they are kept together.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- **Wide top-k (> 128).** Only with a raised `--max-logprobs`. A per-slot stash for it would be `[canvas, vocab]` per slot. Such requests keep a per-slot dict filled only for converged slots and read convergence and emission back under `gpu_sync_allowed()`, only in steps that contain one (about 100 lines: `_pend_wide_logprobs`, `_emitted_logprobs`). Rejecting top-k > 128 for DiffusionGemma would remove them and the last allowed sync; open for reviewer preference.
- **Per-step D2H.** Every step with a logprobs request copies a canvas of stash rows per logprobs request to the host, emitting or not: `n_lp * canvas * lp_width * 12 B` (+8 B rank per row). Bounded by `max_num_reqs * canvas * 129 * 12 B`: 3.2 MB at the defaults (8 seqs, canvas 256), about 25 MB at 64 seqs with top-128. At the defaults with all top-20 this is 2048 rows/step (516 KB) vs 72 rows/step on main.
- **Steps where nothing converges** still cost about 0.15-0.25 ms over no logprobs (early-exit launches plus that D2H).
- **Tie order.** Tied top-k ids, including the `-inf` ties of `top_k`/`top_p`-masked rows, now come in lower-id order. Values and id sets are unchanged.
- **Adversarial top-k input.** On synthetic logits that ascend within blocks with many near-top block maxima, K=128 over 2048 converged rows at V=262144 took 25.7 ms vs 7.0 ms for `torch.topk`. Gaussian, bf16-quantized, low-temperature, and `top_k`-masked rows are 2-4x faster than torch.
- **First use of a top-k bucket** pays a Triton JIT compile.
- **Coupling.** The ROCm bitwise match depends on `_topk_log_softmax_kernel` keeping BLOCK=1024 and 4 warps.

**Duplicate-work check.** Searched open PRs for `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`, `gpu_sync_allowed`, `sync rocm`, and DiffusionGemma/logprobs keywords: no open PR addresses this site. #64176 is the submitter's own predecessor, which wrapped this site in `gpu_sync_allowed()`; this PR replaces that approach here.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Remove step-path GPU syncs in EPLB skip-rearrange, AITER GDN prefill metadata, Moondream3 BOS and INT4 RHT signs
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes the GPU<->CPU syncs that `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` flags on ROCm at four step-path sites: the EPLB ROCm skip-rearrange heuristic, the AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill metadata build, the Moondream3 BOS embedding, and the lazy INT4 KV-cache RHT sign upload. No fix uses `gpu_sync_allowed()`. This is part of the series that replaces the allow-wrap approach of #64176 (as `njhill` suggested in review) so the ROCm test image can turn the check back on (#61939 dropped it).

## Claims

- **EPLB (sync mode, ROCm):** the skip-rearrange heuristic from #47206 now runs on the CPU copies of the load window and current map that the host policy already fetched. On `main` it runs on device tensors: `bool((map >= 0).all())` once, then `rank_load_imbalance()` twice, each doing `mean_load == 0` and `.item()`, and the second call also copies the CPU policy map to the GPU (`mapping.to(device=...)`, pageable). That is up to five D2H syncs and one pageable H2D copy per rearrange step. Skip decisions are unchanged.
- **AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill (Qwen3.5 on ROCm):** the per-step metadata is built on the host and uploaded with one pinned non-blocking copy, instead of AITER's blocking pageable `torch.tensor(..., device=cuda)`. The metadata is bit-identical and gsm8k does not change.
- **Moondream3:** the BOS id is a non-persistent buffer registered at init, instead of a blocking `torch.tensor(..., device=...)` on every multimodal step.
- **INT4 per-token-head KV cache:** the RHT signs are built in `TritonAttentionImpl.__init__` instead of on a cache miss in the first forward that writes the INT4 cache. On current `main` this is latent (see Details); it applies to CUDA as well.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13, amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1. Each before/after pair is an end-to-end `LLM` repro with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, run against the base file and the fixed file. The per-site repros ran on this PR's merge base, `main` at 5629b26146.

| Site | Before (base) | After (this PR) | Output equivalence |
|---|---|---|---|
| EPLB: DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, TP2+EP, sync EPLB (window 5, interval 20), eager | rc=1, `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `bool((physical_to_logical_map >= 0).all())` (same stack as CI `qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8-block-sync-eplb-accuracy-tp2`) | rc=0, 0 sync errors. Both heuristic outcomes ran under the checker: after the profile pass, 7 rearrange steps, 6 skipped and 1 that moved weights. The split depends on scheduling (the series integration run gave 5 skipped, 2 moved) | Old (GPU) vs new (CPU) heuristic on 150 random load/map cases (EP2/4/8, with and without redundant experts): `max_rel_diff=1.192e-07 skip_decision_mismatches=0` |
| GDN: Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B, MRV2, CUDA graphs, FlyDSL prefill | rc=1, sync at `aiter/ops/prefill_batch_metadata.py` `packed = torch.tensor(` (same stack as CI `lm-eval-qwen3-5-models-shard-1-2`) | rc=0, 0 sync errors; also with chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=256`) and prefix caching | Pickled metadata before vs after: equal. 10 greedy generations identical |
| Moondream3: moondream/moondream3-preview, bf16, eager, single and batched image requests | rc=1, sync at `moondream3.py` `embed_multimodal` | rc=0, 0 sync errors | Greedy outputs identical to base |
| INT4: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, `int4_per_token_head`, TRITON_ATTN, eager, sign cache reset to its post-`load_model` contents when the check is enabled | rc=1, sync at `_get_rht_signs` -> `signs.to(device)` (same stack as the CI `test_per_token_head_kv_cache_accuracy` failure) | rc=0, `RHT cache at check enable: [(64, 0, 'cuda:0')]` | Token ids identical to an unmodified base run |

The per-site repros ran before the final INT4 fixup that draws the signs explicitly as float32; the INT4 rows below were re-run on this branch.

<details>
<summary>Tests run on this branch</summary>

From `tests/` with `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>`, one MI355X unless noted.

```
# EPLB
pytest -q distributed/test_eplb_algo.py distributed/test_eplb_utils.py \
  distributed/test_eplb_events.py distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py
  => 53 passed, 2 skipped
# GDN
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -q v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py
  => 79 passed
pytest -q v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py \
  kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py
  => 106 passed, 6 skipped
# Moondream3
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3.py \
  models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3_moe.py
  => 11 passed, 1 skipped (test_tensor_parallel needs 2 GPUs)
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py -k moondream3
  => 1 passed (vLLM vs HF)
# INT4
pytest -q quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py => 85 passed
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -q models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k "int4 and TRITON_ATTN"
  => 1 passed (int4_per_token_head), 0 `sync detected` lines (GPU 7, HEAD 1c7acbc722)
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -q kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py -k int4 => 6 passed
```

Series integration pass (all fixes of the series applied together, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, before the INT4 float32 fixup), 0 `sync detected` lines each: the EPLB e2e repro (5 skipped, 2 moved), the Qwen3.5 GDN e2e repro, `models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3.py` (6 passed, 1 skipped), and `models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k int4` (1 passed; a first attempt failed on the shared-GPU "Memory of devices not free" wait, not on a sync).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Model eval: gsm8k on Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN metadata path)</summary>

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, 1x MI355X; both logs show "Dispatching AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill (prepare=flydsl, chunk=flydsl)". The baseline is this branch with only `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` taken from `main` (the only file of this PR on that model's path).

```

  --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B,max_model_len=4096,gpu_memory_utilization=0.6,seed=0 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 250 --batch_size auto
```

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`_aiter_ops.py` from `main`) | 0.360 ± 0.0304 | 0.356 ± 0.0303 |
| this PR | 0.360 ± 0.0304 | 0.356 ± 0.0303 |

</details>

## Details

**Not duplicating existing work.** I searched open PRs for `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`, `gpu_sync_allowed`, "sync rocm" and each site's keywords:
- #62946 (`aarushjain29`) reported the INT4 RHT-sign sync first and wraps it in `gpu_sync_allowed()`; credit to it for the report. Here the signs are built at attention-impl init, so no allowance is needed and no forward takes the miss.
- #66003 removes a different allowed sync (ROCM_AITER_FA builder); no overlap.
- #64176 is my earlier allow-wrap PR; this series replaces it.

CI with the check re-enabled on ROCm: [vllm/ci #97758](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97758), [vllm/amd-ci #15532](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532).

### EPLB ROCm skip-rearrange
In sync EPLB mode, `EplbState.rearrange()` runs inside the checked `sample_tokens` step. The generic path already copies the global load window and the current `physical_to_logical_map` to CPU under `gpu_sync_allowed()` because the default policy runs in numpy; the ROCm heuristic then ignored those copies and re-read the device tensors. The copies are now kept as locals and the heuristic uses them, and `policy.rebalance_experts` moves out of the allowance since it only touches CPU tensors. `DefaultEplbPolicy`, the only registered policy, does not mutate its inputs, so reusing the CPU map is safe. The float32 reduction order on CPU can differ by about 1e-7 relative; every rank computes on the same all-reduced data, so all ranks still agree. CUDA is unaffected (the heuristic is `is_rocm()`-guarded).

### AITER GDN prefill metadata
`GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` calls `rocm_aiter_ops.build_gdn_flydsl_prefill_metadata()` on every prefill step. AITER computes the schedule as Python lists and materializes it on `cu_seqlens.device` with a blocking pageable H2D copy, the only sync on this path. The wrapper keeps its signature: it passes AITER a host `cu_seqlens` built from `seq_lens_cpu`, uploads the five int32 tensors with one `async_tensor_h2d`, and uses `dataclasses.replace` on AITER's frozen dataclasses to point at the device tensors and the caller's device `cu_seqlens` (so AITER's `layout.cu_seqlens is cu_seqlens` check holds). This mirrors the FLA path's `_build_chunk_metadata`.

Tradeoffs and limitations:
- The wrapper depends on AITER's dataclass field names. A rename fails loudly in `replace`; a new tensor field would silently stay on the CPU.
- AITER's async device assert that `cu_seqlens` matches `seq_lens` now compares the host cumsum with itself. Both callers derive the two from the same `query_start_loc`, so it could not fail in practice.
- AITER's "building during stream capture" error no longer triggers because the build runs on a CPU tensor. The metadata builders run outside capture today.
- The long-term fix is a pinned, non-blocking build path in AITER, after which this wrapper can go back to a plain call.

### Moondream3 BOS
`embed_multimodal` called `torch.tensor([bos_token_id], device=device)` on every multimodal step. The value is a model constant, so it is registered once as a non-persistent buffer, the same pattern the file uses for `_expert_map`. It is not in the state dict, so weight loading is unaffected. With the base code, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` reported only this line on the path.

### INT4 RHT signs
`_get_rht_signs()` draws the signs on CPU and calls `.to(device)` on a cache miss, and nothing filled the cache before the first forward that writes the INT4 KV cache. In the failing CI run no warmup forward reached that write before the check was enabled, so `test_per_token_head_kv_cache_accuracy` failed. On current `main` that test passes, only because the MRV2 post-capture `_dummy_run` from #62560 happens to fill the cache first; nothing guarantees this, on ROCm or CUDA. The INT4 e2e "before" above therefore resets the cache to its post-`load_model` contents to reproduce the CI ordering, and the existing CI test is not a regression signal for this site.

`TritonAttentionImpl.__init__` (the only backend supporting `int4_per_token_head`) now builds the signs for the head size's power-of-two block on the current device. The signs are drawn explicitly as float32: init runs under the model loader's default dtype, so otherwise they would be cached as bf16 rather than the float32 the lazy path produced (values are ±1 either way; callers pass float32 activations). Eager init is used instead of a pinned lazy upload so a first miss during CUDA-graph capture cannot leave a capture-only tensor in the cache.

### Coverage gaps
- **Not run locally:** gfx942/MI300; CUDA (all four paths are shared with CUDA except the ROCm-only EPLB heuristic); the CI models Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (EPLB, DP2) and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (DEP2/TP2/MXFP4), whose code paths were exercised with DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3.5-0.8B; Moondream3 TP=2; EPLB `test_eplb_execute.py` and `test_eplb_fused_moe_layer.py` (hit a 1500 s local timeout; neither exercises `EplbState.rearrange`).
- **No new tests.** Once the ROCm test image sets `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` again (#64176), the EPLB accuracy jobs, Qwen3.5 lm-eval and the Moondream3 generation tests fail without these fixes. INT4 has no CI regression signal on current `main` (see above). CUDA CI already runs with the check on.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Drop sparse MLA metadata host sync; use persistent AITER for gfx950 long BF16 prefills
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR removes the host `synchronize()` that `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` runs after each `get_mla_metadata_v1` rebuild. That sync fails `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` inside `execute_model`. The PR also stops gfx950 from sending long pure BF16 prefills to AITER's nonpersistent ASM decode kernels, which give wrong results that change from run to run at 32, 64 and 128 heads. That kernel is what made `large_q_pure_prefill-auto-ROCMAiterMLA` flaky, on main and once the sync was gone.

The persistent-metadata block keeps its pre-existing `gpu_sync_allowed()` `seq_lens[:num_reqs].cpu()` read. Because of the routing change, gfx950 long pure BF16 prefill steps now enter that block and so now hit that allowed read; before this PR they skipped it. Removing that read is follow-up work, not part of this PR.

This is part of the work to re-enable `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on AMD CI, which #61939 dropped from `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`. It replaces the `gpu_sync_allowed()` wrap that #64176 used for this site, following `njhill`'s review there (fix the syncs instead of allowing them). Related PRs: #66397, #66398, #66399; #64176 turns the check back on and depends on all of them.

## Claims

- **Post-metadata `synchronize()` removed, with no allow-wrap in its place.** The pre-existing allowed `seq_lens` read in the same block remains (see Overview). Before this PR, the removed sync (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:726` on main) failed these AMD jobs with the check on: in [build 97758](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97758), `mi300 v1-attention shard 1/3`, `mi355 dpx v1-attention shard 2/4`, `mi355 lm-eval deepseek-v3-2-tp` and `-dp`; in [amd-ci 15532](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532), `mi300 v1-attention shard 1` and `shard 2`, `mi355 dpx v1-attention shard 1` and `shard 2`, `mi355 lm-eval deepseek-v3-2-tp` and `-dp`.
- **Flaky test fixed.** `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[deepseek-1.0-1.0-64-1-auto-large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]` now gives the same result on every run on gfx950. Pristine main: 3/60 in-process failures. This PR: 0/60.
- **Correct at every head count on gfx950.** For long pure BF16 prefills, AITER's persistent kernel was deterministic and within 0.006 of an fp32 reference at 16-128 heads. The nonpersistent kernels main uses are nondeterministic with errors up to 0.036 (32 heads), 0.092 (64) and 0.173 (128), and at 48/80/96/112 heads AITER has no nonpersistent kernel at all (table in Details).
- **Faster only at 128 heads.** At 128 heads the persistent kernel is about 1.2-1.5x faster per layer (kernel table below). At fewer heads it is slower: at TP4 DeepSeek-V3.2 (32 heads per rank) TTFT on an 8192-token prompt rises by 17.0 ms (+2.6%) (see Model eval). Each such step also pays one `get_mla_metadata_v1` launch (1.3 ms at 8192 tokens) and the allowed `seq_lens` read.
- **No metadata that AITER would ignore.** The builder skips persistent metadata and its `seq_lens` read when AITER would not use the persistent kernel for the batch (gfx950, BF16, 16 heads, at least 32 tokens). With AITER 0.1.28.post1 on MI350X (gfx950), 16 heads and BF16, output with and without metadata was bit-identical at 32, 64, 512 and 4096 tokens over 3 reruns each. At 31 tokens, below the threshold, the two outputs differ (max 2.4e-4) because a different kernel runs; that is the positive control. At TP8 DeepSeek-V3.2 the kernel trace now matches main exactly. This covers batches of 32 or more tokens; a 16-head long-context prefill with fewer than 32 new tokens (prefix hit or short chunked tail) still builds metadata and runs the persistent kernel, which was deterministic in the study.
- **gfx942 unchanged.** Long BF16 prefills there still skip persistent metadata and take the Triton fallback.

## Validation

All local runs: MI350X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13, amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. Commands 1 and 2 were re-run on 2deae9c3dd and gave the same results: 155 passed / 108 skipped, and 30/30. The other runs used 36442e9f. Both earlier commits differ from 14f9dc450e only in docstrings. The command 1, unit-test and 25-run fresh-process counts were rerun at the head with the metadata-skip change and the head-count test parametrization.

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Sparse MLA CI set with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (command 1) | 2 failed (`test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa[auto]`, `[fp8]`: `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at the removed line), 141 passed, 108 skipped | 181 passed, 108 skipped, 0 failed (the extra passes come from the gfx942 and head-count parametrizations and the 2 metadata-skip tests) |
| `kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py` (this PR's test file; main column runs it against main's source) | 2 failed (`test_sparse_persistent_metadata_recomputes_without_host_sync`, `test_sparse_metadata_workload_length_dtype_matrix[prefill-long-auto-False]`), 40 passed | 68 passed |
| `large_q_pure_prefill-auto-ROCMAiterMLA`, repeated in one process | 3/60 failed (mismatched elements: 11464, 11640, 217); separately 5/30 | 0/60; also 0/30 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (command 2) |
| Same test, one fresh process per run | 3/12 failed | 0/40, and 0/20 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`; 0/25 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` after the metadata-skip change |
| Integration stack (`sync-fix/rocm-enable-gpu-sync-check`: this fix at 36442e9f plus #66397/#66398/#66399 and the Dockerfile change), `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, command 1 | - | 155 passed, 108 skipped, no syncs |

The unit matrix is the deterministic guard for the routing change. The e2e `large_q_pure_prefill` test only catches the bad kernel about 5-25% of the time on main (3/60, 5/30, 3/12), so it is a weak regression signal on its own.

<details>
<summary>Extra stress runs and commands</summary>

Independent reviewer stress of the target test: 0/50 fresh-process failures and 100/100 in-process passes (one reviewer), and another 100/100 in-process (a second reviewer). A full run of the `ROCMAiterMLA` cases of `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness`, repeated 10 times, gave 108 passed / 108 skipped every time.

```bash
# 1. CI set (from tests/)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -q \
  v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py \
  -k "rocm or sparse_persistent or sink"

# 2. Target test, repeated in one process (REPEAT_N from a small local repeat plugin)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error REPEAT_N=30 pytest -q -p repeat_plugin \
  "v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[deepseek-1.0-1.0-64-1-auto-large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]"
```
</details>

**Kernel timings** (MI350X, BF16, CUDA events, mean over 20 iterations, us). The AITER-only repro and timing script uses random inputs, a fresh zeroed output and a device sync around every call. "Differing reruns" counts reruns whose output differed from the first run.

| shape (reqs x tokens, topk, heads) | nonpersistent (old gfx950 path) | persistent (this PR) | Triton | differing reruns: nonpersistent / persistent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2x256, 128, 128 | 83.5 | 71.1 | 385 | 20-49/49 (two runs) / 0/49 |
| 1x4096, 2048, 128 | 2958 | 2005 | 36272 | 5/19 / 0/19 |
| 4x2048, 2048, 128 | 4236 | 3017 | 49728 | 7/19 / 0/19 |
| 1x4096, 2048, 64 | 1214 | 1163 | 18264 | 0/19 / 0/19 |

The extra `get_mla_metadata_v1` launch runs once per step and all layers share it: 113 us at 512 tokens, 1.3 ms at 8192, 2.6 ms at 16384.

**Model eval and end-to-end latency.** DeepSeek-V3.2 on 8x MI350X (gfx950), amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1, main (fd0c471b3a) vs this PR with the same arguments. The changed path is reached only by pure-prefill steps whose longest prefill exceeds topk=2048, with BF16 KV. So the runs use `num_concurrent=1`, 25-shot GSM8K (all 1319 prompts are 3151-5087 tokens) and `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, so each prompt prefills in one step. MTP is off and CUDA graphs are on (FULL_DECODE_ONLY). Dispatch was checked with rocprofv3 on an 8192-token request.

- TP4 (32 heads per rank): the PR runs the persistent `mla_a16w16_qh64_qseqlen1_gqaratio64_v3_ps` plus `kn_mla_reduce_v1_ps` instead of main's nonpersistent `mla_a16w16_qh16_m16x4_n32x1`. That is 155.0 vs 144.0 ms over 61 layers, plus 2.7 ms of reduce and a 1.44 ms metadata launch.
- TP8 (16 heads per rank): AITER falls back to nonpersistent split-KV (`mla_dec_stage1_bf16_a16w16_subQ16_mqa16`) on both sides. With the metadata skip, kernel names and counts match main on all 8 ranks. Without it, the only extra work was one ignored metadata launch (1.44 ms) and one `seq_lens` copy.

TP4 (32 heads per rank):

| TP4 | GSM8K flexible | GSM8K strict | TTFT med (ms) | TPOT med (ms) | E2E med (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9545 | 0.9553 | 667.2 | 13.45 | 2372.8 |
| this PR | 0.9560 | 0.9568 | 684.2 | 13.46 | 2393.8 |

TP8 (16 heads per rank):

| TP8 | GSM8K flexible | GSM8K strict | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | E2E (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9545 | 0.9545 | 493.4 ± 1.8 | 12.87 | 2127.7 ± 2.0 |
| this PR without the metadata skip | - | - | 493.8 ± 2.1 | 12.87 | 2127.6 ± 1.5 |
| this PR | 0.9522 | 0.9530 | 493.0 ± 2.8 | 12.86 | 2126.4 ± 0.9 |

- Latency is from `vllm bench serve` with random 8192 in / 128 out, concurrency 1, 50 prompts plus 5 warmups, `--ignore-eos`.
  - TP4: 3 repeats per side on each of two GPU sets, alternating, then swapped (300 requests per side). The result is +17.0 ms TTFT (+2.6%) and +21.1 ms E2E (+0.9%), and it holds with the GPU sets swapped.
  - TP8: 4 fresh-server rounds in rotated order, 3 repeats each. Values are the mean ± sd of the per-round medians. The 1.44 ms metadata launch is below restart-to-restart noise.
- Accuracy: GSM8K standard error is about ±0.006. Paired McNemar tests give p = 0.79 (TP4) and p = 0.61 / 0.79 (TP8, flexible/strict). At TP8 main and this PR run identical kernels and still share only 579/1319 identical generations, so differences of this size come from run-to-run nondeterminism.
- The CI-parity eval (`configs/models-mi355-deepseek-v32-tp.txt`, TP4 + MTP + eager, 5-shot) has not been rerun; its 0.6k-1.6k token prompts and high concurrency probably never reach the changed path.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 --tensor-parallel-size {4,8} --enable-expert-parallel \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --moe-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 128 --max-concurrency 1 \
  --num-prompts 50 --num-warmups 5 --ignore-eos
```

**Not validated locally:**
- gfx942/MI300. gfx942 routing is unchanged, but its FP8-KV persistent path also loses the sync. CI's mi300 v1-attention shards cover that path, but not MTP + CUDA graphs at 200k context (#47404's setup, see below).
- MTP with DeepSeek-V3.2 at model level. TP4/TP8 runs above use CUDA graphs (FULL_DECODE_ONLY) without MTP. Kernel-level graph replay after an unsynced metadata rebuild was checked (see "Why the sync can go").

## Details

**Why the sync can go.** With `fast_mode=True`, `get_mla_metadata_v1` dispatches to AITER's `get_mla_metadata_v1_2_device`. That function launches one device kernel on `aiter::getCurrentHIPStream()`, and AITER's `compile_ops` sets that stream to torch's current stream before each call. Nothing is staged through host memory, there is no `hipMemcpy`, and the function owns no buffers. The decode kernel, whether eager or captured in a graph and replayed, runs later on the same stream and reads the metadata on the device, so stream order already puts the write before the read. The block also already starts with a blocking `seq_lens.cpu()`, so the removed sync only waited for the single metadata kernel launched after it. The dense `rocm_aiter_mla` builder already rebuilds the same metadata every step without a sync. Two investigation experiments back this up:
- Outputs stayed bit-identical with no sync even with a 5M-cycle `torch.cuda._sleep` queued before the metadata kernel, which lets the host run far ahead of the GPU.
- Direct graph-replay race test (AITER persistent FP8 MLA decode, 128 heads, 256 tokens, same metadata arguments as vLLM): capture a CUDA graph, then per iteration rewrite `kv_indptr` to a different config, queue a 20M-cycle sleep, rebuild metadata with no host sync and replay. Same stream: 0/50 mismatches against per-config eager references. Positive control replaying on an unordered side stream: 49/50 mismatches.

**Concern about #47404.** The sync came from #47404, which reported that it removed a fault on 8x MI300X (gfx942), TP8, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` + MTP + CUDA graphs, FP8 KV, `max_model_len=200000`. That PR gave no root cause beyond "graph replay could observe stale metadata". The kernel-level graph-replay test above shows that same-stream ordering covers that case, but it ran on gfx950 with one GPU and no model. #47404's exact configuration has not been rerun with this PR; all local hardware is gfx950. Plan before leaving draft: rerun that configuration (100+ requests) on MI300X with this PR, through AMD CI or a reviewer with MI300X access, or get confirmation from the #47404 author; if none is possible, the regression risk stays open and is called out to reviewers.

**Why the flaky test failed.** `large_q_pure_prefill` (2x256 tokens, topk 128, BF16 KV) never reached the sync. On main, `_is_long_bf16_prefill()` skipped persistent metadata for long pure BF16 prefills on every architecture, but only gfx942 sent those batches to Triton. On gfx950 they fell through to AITER's nonpersistent `mla_dec_stage1_bf16_a16w16_subQ128_mqa128`. With bit-identical inputs and device syncs around every call, that kernel returns different rows from run to run. Against an fp32 reference its max error is 0.12-0.21, compared with 0.0053 for the persistent kernel. So the kernel computes wrong values; this is not an ordering race. Syncs placed before or after stage 1, `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` and `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` all still reproduce the failure. It reproduces with AITER alone and the newest AITER nightly ships the same binary; reported as ROCm/aiter#7631. The 32- and 64-head nonpersistent kernels are also nondeterministic, mostly on multi-request shapes (the single-request 1x4096 64-head row above showed 0/19). The sink/LSE path still calls the nonpersistent kernel. This PR leaves it alone, and #66454 handles it separately (see Tradeoffs).

Determinism by head count (AITER only, sparse layout: one entry per query token, ragged top-k indices, page_size 1; same inputs every run, NaN-poisoned output, with and without an L2 flush; 50-400 runs per config at 2x256 to 1x8192 tokens; error is the max against an fp32 reference):

| padded heads | nonpersistent kernel | nondeterministic configs | max err | persistent nondeterministic configs | max err |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | `subQ16_mqa16` | 0/18 | 0.0059 | 0/12 (AITER runs the nonpersistent kernel) | 0.0051 |
| 32 | `qh16_m16x4_n32x1` | 4/22 | 0.036 | 0/22 | 0.0052 |
| 64 | `qh64_qseqlen1_gqaratio64_v3` | 5/18 | 0.092 | 0/18 | 0.0057 |
| 128 | `subQ128_mqa128` | 12/18 | 0.173 | 0/18 | 0.0060 |
| 48/80/96/112 | none (`cannot get heuristic kernel`) | - | - | 0/4 each | ≤0.0059 |

**The fix.** `_is_long_bf16_prefill` is renamed to `_use_triton_long_bf16_prefill` and now checks `on_gfx942()` first. The builder and `_forward_mla` share this helper, so they cannot disagree about which path a batch takes. The import of `on_gfx942` stays lazy so that the tests' monkeypatch still applies. The gfx942-only Triton routing for these prefills was in place before this PR. The all-architecture skip of persistent metadata came from #49263 (cc `tjtanaa`), which gave no reason for it. Routing gfx950 to Triton instead would be deterministic, but 5-18x slower (table above).

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- On gfx950, long pure BF16 prefill steps now enter the persistent block. So they now also pay the existing `gpu_sync_allowed()` `seq_lens.cpu()` read and one metadata launch per step. At TP4 DeepSeek-V3.2 (32 heads per rank) the persistent kernel is also slower than the nonpersistent one, so 8192-token TTFT rises by 17 ms (+2.6%). That is the cost of not running the 32-head nonpersistent kernel, which gives wrong values (see the determinism table).
- The one exception is 16-head BF16 batches of at least `AITER_MLA_DECODE_PERSISTENT_MAX_BATCH` tokens (32 by default). There, AITER's `mla_decode_fwd` ignores `work_meta_data` and runs the nonpersistent split-KV kernel. The builder asks AITER's own `_use_persistent_mla_decode` and skips both the metadata and the read in that case, so these steps do what main did. The check also covers decode and mixed batches, where main built metadata that AITER then dropped. If the installed AITER lacks that function, the builder keeps the old behavior.
- Layers with sinks or `use_aiter_sparse_mla` set `_use_persistent_metadata=False`. This PR does not change sink layers. On gfx950, BF16 sink layers still run AITER's nonpersistent `mla_decode_fwd_lse`, which ROCm/aiter#7631 also covers (`return_lse=True`). #66454 routes those layers to Triton until #7631 is fixed. The two PRs are independent, and either can land first.
- `metadata_key` does not include `max_split_per_batch`. That was already true before this PR; it is only flagged for follow-up.

**Tests.**
- `test_sparse_persistent_metadata_syncs_only_after_recompute` is renamed to `test_sparse_persistent_metadata_recomputes_without_host_sync` and now asserts that no sync happens.
- `test_sparse_metadata_workload_length_dtype_matrix` is parametrized over `(on_gfx942, num_heads)` in `(True, 128), (False, 32), (False, 64), (False, 128)`: only gfx942 may skip persistent metadata for long BF16 prefills. Against main's source `[prefill-long-auto-False]` failed (before the head parametrization), and a 128-only rule fails the 32- and 64-head cases, so this is the deterministic guard for the routing change.
- `test_build_skips_metadata_aiter_ignores[-1|0]` uses AITER's real predicate with gfx950 and its default threshold patched in. At the threshold, it checks that the builder launches no `get_mla_metadata_v1`, enters no `gpu_sync_allowed()` read and returns `work_meta_data=None`. One token below the threshold, it checks that metadata is still built. Without the source change, `[0]` fails.
- The previously flaky `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[...large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]` runs in the AMD v1-attention CI shards, but it is a low-rate catcher (see Validation).

**Duplicate check.** Searched open PRs for `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`, `gpu_sync_allowed`, "sync rocm" and sparse MLA metadata keywords. #64176 is the submitter's own predecessor, and this PR replaces its approach for this site. #66003 removes a different allowed sync, in the `ROCM_AITER_FA` builder, so the two do not overlap. #62946 targets the INT4 RHT-signs site, which is handled in #66399. No open PR touches this site.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change. The human submitter is responsible for the change.

- [x] DeepSeek-V3.2 long-prefill eval and latency (TP4 and TP8, BF16 KV, concurrency 1) on main and this PR, results added above
- [ ] DeepSeek-V3.2 CI-parity eval (TP4 + MTP + eager, 5-shot)
- [ ] #47404 configuration rerun on MI300X, or confirmation from its author / AMD
- [x] ROCm/aiter issue filed and linked (ROCm/aiter#7631)

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Render messages for return_prompt_text with reused prompt token ids
author: roytman
body:
## Overview

Ignore `kv_transfer_params.prompt_token_ids` on chat requests that set `return_prompt_text`, so `prompt_text` is the rendered prompt instead of `null`. Fixes #66402.

## Claims

- A `/v1/chat/completions` request with `return_prompt_text: true` and forwarded `prompt_token_ids` returns the rendered prompt in `prompt_text`, in both the streaming and the non-streaming path. Before this change it returned `null` with HTTP 200.
- Requests without `return_prompt_text` still reuse the forwarded ids as before.

## Validation

Unit test: extended `test_chat_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_ignored_with_echo` to also cover `return_prompt_text`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k ignored_with_echo
```

| | `echo` cases | `return_prompt_text` cases |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (c6b2d6ecbb) | 2 passed | 2 failed |
| this PR | 2 passed | 2 passed |

The full `test_serving_chat.py` gives 214 passed and 10 errors on this PR. All 10 are `TestGPTOSS*` setup errors (`FileNotFoundError: 'vllm'`, the `vllm` binary is not on PATH on my machine); the same error occurs on `main` without this change.

Server test: added `test_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_return_prompt_text` to `test_chat_completion.py` next to the existing `kv_transfer_params` round-trip tests. It checks through `RemoteOpenAIServer` that a decode request with forwarded ids returns the same `prompt_text` as the plain request. CI runs it in the `entrypoints-integration-api-server-openai-chat_completion` step.

Run on one H100 80GB with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-cf5cea2da3` image (10 commits behind this PR's base, none touching `vllm/renderers/` or `chat_completion/`), `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`:

```bash
pytest entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_completion.py -k return_prompt_text -v
```

Without the fix:

```text
test_chat_completion.py::test_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_return_prompt_text FAILED
E       AssertionError: assert None == '<|im_start|>system\nYou are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nHello, how are you today?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
================== 1 failed, 8 deselected in 81.63s (0:01:21) ==================
```

With the fix:

```text
test_chat_completion.py::test_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_return_prompt_text PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 8 deselected in 43.78s =======================
```

With `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the server logs `return_prompt_text is set, so messages are rendered instead`, which confirms the server ran the new check.

`pre-commit run ruff-check` and `ruff-format` pass on the changed files.

This change does not affect model output, so no model evaluation was run.

## Details

Root cause: decode-side id reuse (#48145) builds the engine input with `tokens_input(reuse_ids, ...)` and skips the chat template, so the input has no `prompt` text. `AsyncLLM.add_request` takes the request's prompt text from that input's `prompt` key, and `chat_completion/serving.py` returns it as `prompt_text`, so it is `None`. #55771 fixed the same conflict for `echo` and media by ignoring the ids and rendering `messages`; this PR adds `return_prompt_text` to that check in `_reused_prompt_token_ids`.

Flow on a P/D decode request:
1. The decode request arrives with `messages`, `return_prompt_text: true` and `kv_transfer_params.prompt_token_ids`.
2. `preprocess_chat` calls `_reused_prompt_token_ids`, which now returns `None`, so `messages` is rendered as on a request without forwarded ids.
3. The ids are still popped from `kv_transfer_params`, so they stay out of the engine's sampling metadata, and the KV transfer proceeds unchanged.

Tradeoff: these requests pay for chat templating and tokenization again on decode. That is the cost `return_prompt_text` needs, since the field returns that rendered text.

Both callers of `_reused_prompt_token_ids` (`preprocess_chat` and the Harmony chat path) read the flag from the request, so both are covered. `docs/features/disagg_prefill.md` lists `return_prompt_text` with `echo` and non-text content as the cases where the ids are ignored.

Not a duplicate: open PRs #64721 and #62333 change `_reused_prompt_token_ids`, but neither handles `return_prompt_text`.

AI assistance was used to trace the code path and draft the change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Keep CLIP and SigLIP special tokens for chat text embeddings
author: Alex-Wengg
body:
## Overview

On CLIP and SigLIP, text sent to `/v1/embeddings` as `messages` loses the special tokens its tokenizer adds, so it returns a different embedding than the same text sent as `input`. Chat requests default to `add_special_tokens=False`, and both models fall back to `template_basic.jinja`, which only joins the message text: CLIP loses BOS and EOS, SigLIP loses EOS.

This adds `template_clip.jinja` (BOS + text + EOS) and `template_siglip.jinja` (text + EOS; SigLIP defines no BOS), and drops the now-wrong `--chat-template template_basic.jinja` from the SigLIP example. Image-only requests are unchanged.

## Validation

New test `test_dual_encoder_chat_text_matches_input` (through `RemoteOpenAIServer`), on an RTX A6000:

- Before: prompt tokens 5 vs 7 (CLIP), 7 vs 8 (SigLIP), 2 failed
- After: 2 passed; `messages` and `input` give identical tokens and embeddings (max difference 0.0)

`test_clip.py`, `test_siglip.py` and `pre-commit` pass.

## Notes

- Clients that pass `add_special_tokens=true` on CLIP as a workaround now get doubled BOS/EOS and should drop the flag.
- SigLIP2 is not fixed: its tokenizer ships a Gemma chat template that outranks the fallback. That needs a chat template resolution change, left for a follow-up.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the code, tests and this description; the validation runs above were executed locally.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fill the Qwen2-VL video budget up to the context length
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

The Qwen2-VL video budget grows only in whole full-size frame steps (16,384 tokens for Qwen2.5-VL), so a video that fits `max_model_len` but not the last whole step is rejected with "exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size". This fills the budget up to the context. It covers Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, EXAONE 4.5 and OpenPangu-VL. #66017 and #66190 fixed the same gap for Qwen3-Omni and Qwen2.5-Omni.

## Claims

- When the context holds more than one full-size step, the video budget fills `max_model_len` up to the 14-frame cap, and the profiling dummy has exactly that many tokens. Qwen2.5-VL-3B at 40000: 32,768 → 39,999.
- The budget is never below main's: the spread shape is used only when it has more tokens than main's full-size shape and still fits the context. Contexts of one step or less and contexts the 14-frame cap limits are unchanged.
- Videos that fit the context are served instead of rejected, including a 1760x990 clip at the server's default 32 frames.
- Profiling runs a video as large as the new budget, so startup reserves more activation memory at contexts that were cut before (KV cache −26% at 40000 on A10).
- With video pruning or `limit_mm_per_prompt` video size hints, the budget and dummy are unchanged from main. A `num_frames`-only hint caps the frames of the spread shape, which is used only when it beats main's budget; then the budget equals the dummy, so the gap between the admitted budget and the profiled dummy is never wider than on main.
- Qwen3-VL and encoder CUDA graph frame sizing are unchanged.

## Validation

**Regression test through `LLM`** (A10, wheel of main 7a90549f7e with this PR's `qwen2_vl.py` overlaid; budgets and dummy shapes for every configuration below are identical in the final revision, checked on CPU):

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_5_vl.py::test_qwen2_5_vl_video_fits_max_model_len
# main:    1 failed: VLLMValidationError: The decoder prompt contains a(n) video item with 17280 embedding tokens,
#          which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 16384.
# this PR: 1 passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_5_vl.py -m core_model   # this PR: 13 passed
```

**Processor test** (CPU):

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_vl.py   # 47 passed
# main: the 6 test_max_video_tokens_fills_context cases fail with assert 16384 == 20000
# test_dummy_video_follows_size_hint, test_max_video_tokens_matches_dummy_video and test_max_video_tokens_with_pruning_keeps_full_size_frames
# pass on main and guard the shape selection with hints, min_pixels and pruning
```

**Budget vs. `max_model_len`** (CPU, real processors; budget equals the processed dummy in every row):

| `max_model_len` | Qwen2.5-VL-3B main | this PR | EXAONE-4.5 main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 16,384 | 16,384 | 4,096 | 4,096 |
| 20000 | 16,384 | 20,000 | 16,384 | 20,000 |
| 40000 | 32,768 | 39,999 | 28,672 | 28,672 |
| 100000 | 98,304 | 99,981 | 28,672 | 28,672 |
| 128000 | 114,688 | 114,688 | 28,672 | 28,672 |

Grid over Qwen2-VL-2B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B and EXAONE-4.5, 23 contexts from 1024 to 128000, default settings plus flat `max_pixels`, `min_pixels` (including `min_pixels = max_pixels` and `min_pixels > max_pixels`), `videos_kwargs.size`, `videos_kwargs.min_pixels`, `images_kwargs.size` and `videos_kwargs.do_resize=False` (549 settings): the budget is never below main's (423 equal, 126 higher), never above both `max_model_len` and main's value, and equals the processed dummy wherever it was built. With video hints (portrait, landscape, width-only, height-only, 540x9000, 3584x3584 with and without `num_frames`, and `num_frames` 3/4/6/20; 132 settings), size-hinted budgets and dummies equal main's, and with `num_frames`-only hints the budget is never below main's, the budget-to-dummy gap is never wider than main's, and wherever the budget rises the dummy equals it.

**Serving** (A10, `max_model_len=40000`, greedy, synthetic random-pixel videos, fresh process per run):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1760x990, 32 frames (35,280 tokens) | rejected: exceeds encoder cache size 32768 | served |
| 896x504, 132 frames (38,016 tokens) | rejected | served |
| Peak activation at profiling | 4.19 GiB | 5.13 GiB |
| KV cache | 182,272 tokens | 135,168 tokens |

At the default `max_model_len` (128000), both main and this PR run out of memory in vision encoder profiling on this 24 GB card; the budget there is unchanged.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py tests/multimodal/test_processing.py tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py   # 300 passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py \
  -k "Qwen2-VL or Qwen2.5-VL or EXAONE-4.5 or jina-reranker-m0 or OpenCUA or dots"   # 18 passed, 3 skipped (not available online)
```

## Details

- **Root cause:** `get_max_video_tokens` and the dummy builder used frames at the largest image size and only varied the frame count, so the budget is the largest multiple of one temporal step that fits the context.
- **When it shows:** the encoder cache is `max(max_num_batched_tokens, budget)`, so the rejection needs chunked prefill (the default) with `max_num_batched_tokens` below the video. Without chunked prefill, `max_num_batched_tokens` is `max_model_len` and covers it.
- **Fix:** `get_video_size_and_frames_with_most_features` takes as many steps as needed to cover the context, bounded by the 14-frame cap and by how many steps fit at the processor's minimum frame size, and shrinks each step to an equal share with `get_image_size_with_most_features(max_pixels=...)`. It keeps that shape only when its processed token count is above the full-size shape's and within the context; otherwise it returns main's full-size shape. The budget is the dummy's own token count; rounding leaves it at most 19 tokens under `max_model_len` in the sweep above.
- **Hints:** size hints are clipped per dimension against the dummy canvas, so a wide spread canvas would cut portrait hints (1400x2800 at 40000 would profile 3,350 tokens instead of 5,000), and keeping main's hinted dummy under a larger budget would admit videos that fit the hint but exceed the profile (3584x3584 at 40000: budget 39,999, dummy 32,768). With size hints the helper therefore returns main's shape for both. A `num_frames` hint caps the spread shape, and the spread shape is used only when it beats main's budget.
- **Why one step or less, and video pruning, keep main's shape:** with video pruning, placeholders count retained tokens while the vision encoder runs on the whole video, so an admitted video can be larger than `max_model_len` before pruning. With pruning 0.75 at `max_model_len=4000`, a 48-frame 896x504 clip is 3,458 prompt tokens but 13,824 encoder tokens. Shrinking the dummy below main's 16,384 would profile less encoder memory than such a video needs. For the same reason a larger budget with pruning would grow the unpruned video it admits faster than the profile (four times faster at pruning 0.75), so pruning keeps main's budget and dummy at every context (21 settings checked, identical to main).
- **Why not budget = `seq_len` as in #66190:** Qwen2.5-Omni video steps are 768 tokens, so its whole-step dummy lands within one small step of the budget. Here a step is 16,384 tokens, so the same shape would admit videos up to 16,383 tokens larger than the profiled one (32,768 profiled vs. 40,000 at `max_model_len=40000`). Measured on A10 with that shape (main's dummy, budget = `seq_len`): one 38,016-token video runs out of memory in the vision encoder at request time ("Tried to allocate 992.00 MiB ... 732.81 MiB is free"), while this PR serves it and four such videos submitted together.
- **KV tradeoff:** startup profiling sizes the KV cache from the peak activation of the largest item the budget admits; a dummy smaller than the budget would leave the difference unreserved at runtime. Covering it costs 0.94 GiB of peak activation at `max_model_len=40000` (4.19 → 5.13 GiB for 7,231 more profiled tokens), and the post-warmup fit keeps 1.62 GiB more for torch, so KV cache memory drops from 6.26 to 4.64 GiB (182,272 → 135,168 tokens, 3.38x concurrency). The cost applies only where the budget grows. `limit_mm_per_prompt` video size hints still shrink the profile for users who prefer KV cache.
- **Unchanged on purpose:** `get_num_frames_with_most_features` and `_get_max_video_frames`, which Qwen3-VL (through `super()`) and `get_max_frames_per_video` for encoder CUDA graphs still read.
- **Workaround on main:** a `--max-num-batched-tokens` at least as large as the video also admits it, but profiling still uses the smaller dummy. The error message suggests `--limit-mm-per-prompt`, which can only shrink the estimate.
- **Not covered:** the 14-frame cap still limits the budget at long contexts (114,688 for Qwen2.5-VL, 28,672 for EXAONE 4.5). Size-hinted configurations keep main's budget; fitting the spread shape inside the hint box is left for a follow-up. OpenPangu-VL needs transformers <= 4.57 and was not run; it uses the Qwen2.5-VL info and dummy builder without overrides.
- The new `LLM` test is skipped on CPU because a 17k-token video prefill is too slow there.
- Docs: `conserving_memory.md` notes that for Qwen2-VL-family models a larger `max_model_len` can increase the profiled video size and reduce KV cache memory, within the processor's pixel limits and the frame cap, and that `video` hints lower it.

title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Exclude the HC padding shard from the loaded-shard check
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Overview

Since #63752, every Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`) checkpoint fails to load. The merged HC down/block-inject linear has a padding shard that no checkpoint carries, and the new loaded-shard check reports it as missing. This PR lists only the two real shards.

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoints load again. On main, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` fails with `ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'...attn_hyper_connection.input_mix_weight_down_block_inject.weight.2', ...}`.
- No numerical change: the padding rows' output was already discarded.

## Validation

**Reproducer** (4x GB200 node, `main` at 3213796cd3; the HC and loader code is unchanged up to this PR's base, 199c2e4bff):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel
```

- `main`: every worker fails during weight loading with the error above, for each `attn_hyper_connection` and `mlp_hyper_connection` of all 48 layers.
- This PR: the weights load (`Loading weights took 146.63 seconds`, MTP drafter 2.56 s) and the server starts.

**Unit test.** `test_hc_padding_shard_is_not_expected_from_checkpoints` loads the two checkpoint shards into a `GatedResidual` with the default config (16 + 4 rows, padded to 32) and checks that no shard is reported missing:

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops.py
# with this PR: 17 passed
# with the fix reverted: test_hc_padding_shard_is_not_expected_from_checkpoints fails
#   AssertionError: assert ['weight.2'] == []
```

The test is in `test_hc_ops.py`, which the existing `qwen4-exp-unit-tests` Buildkite step already runs.

## Details

**Root cause.** `GatedResidual` builds `input_mix_weight_down_block_inject` as a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` with output sizes `[hc_lowrank, hc_count, pad_size]`. The padding (to a multiple of 16 rows) only keeps the skinny GEMM aligned: `_down_and_inject` splits it off and discards it. Checkpoints store `input_mix_weight_down` and `block_inject_weight` separately, which the weights mapper stacks into shards 0 and 1. Shard 2 is never loaded. #63752 made `track_weights_loading` fail on any shard listed in `shard_ids` that a load did not fill, and `MergedColumnParallelLinear.shard_ids` defaults to every output size, the padding included.

**Fix.** Set `shard_ids = (0, 1)` on that linear. This narrows only what the loader expects: shards 0 and 1 load as before, and the padding rows are handled exactly as before #63752.
