title: [Core][Bugfix] Run the warmup dummy forward on every PP rank before the GPU sync check
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

Run the post-capture warmup dummy forward on every PP rank before `enable_gpu_sync_check()`; keep the sampler warmup on the last rank. Follow-up requested in the review of #66397; needed before #64176 turns `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` back on for AMD CI.

## Claims

- `gpu_worker.py`: `_compile_or_warm_up_model` runs the attention-bearing `_dummy_run(max_num_reqs)` on every non-pooling PP rank; only the last rank then runs `_dummy_sampler_run`.
- `test_gpu_worker.py`: a non-last and a last PP rank both run a forward before the sync check, and only the last rank runs the sampler. The non-last case fails on `main`.

## Validation

MI350X (gfx950), PP=2, TP=1, eager, `enable_extensible_kv_cache=False`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B with a probe worker extension whose first attention-metadata build does a blocking H2D copy (the pattern of the DSv4.1 indexer's `dcp_rank_tensor`) | PP rank 0 had 0 metadata builds before the check, then raised `GPU<->CPU sync detected` in its first `execute_model` | both ranks built before the check; 10/10 runs, no sync |
| New unit test | non-last case fails | passes |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py` + `tests/utils_/test_gpu_sync_debug.py` | | 73 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py`, `test_pipeline_parallel.py -k "mp and not Phi-3.5-MoE or mixed_precision"` (2 GPUs) | | 10 passed, 6 skipped |

## Details

On `main`, the dummy forward right before `enable_gpu_sync_check()` runs only on the last PP rank, because it came in with the sampler warmup (#62560). With eager mode, JIT warmup off and the extensible KV cache off, nothing else gives the other ranks an attention-bearing forward before the check (the profile run skips attention), so anything built lazily on the first forward is built inside the first checked step and raises there.

No in-tree model is known to hit this today: Qwen3-0.6B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Nemotron-3-Nano and mamba-130m pass on plain `main` in this configuration, and DSv4.1 is covered already (decoder replay only runs on the last stage, and the DSv4 sparse-MLA warmup runs a forward on every rank). The reproduction above uses a probe to show the ordering gap; this change closes it before the check is enabled rather than fixing an observed model failure. Cost: one extra `max_num_reqs` forward on non-last ranks at startup (PP rank 0's CUDA-graph build count goes from 22 to 23); startup time stayed within noise.

It does not depend on #66397 and can land independently. Not a duplicate: the only open PR touching PP warmup, #54630, changes the seeded sampler pass in `gpu/warmup.py`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject empty messages in ChatCompletionRequest
author: Yunt1
body:
## Overview

An empty `messages` list passed chat-completions protocol validation and only failed after the engine had produced a full generation: `OpenAIServingChat.get_chat_request_role` does `request.messages[-1]["role"]`, raising `IndexError` that maps to HTTP 500. Reject it before any generation is scheduled.

## Claims

- `OpenAIServingChat.create_chat_completion` now returns a 400 `invalid_request_error` with `param: "messages"` when `messages` is empty, before the request is rendered or scheduled.
- The check lives at the serving entry rather than on `ChatCompletionRequest`, because internal callers (renderers, response/cohere adapters, and tests) construct the request model with an empty `messages` list and must keep working.
- No change for non-empty messages. `BatchChatCompletionRequest` already enforced `min_length=1` on its `messages` field.

## Validation

No unit tests are added, per review. Manually verified:

- `ChatCompletionRequest(messages=[], model=...)` still constructs successfully (internal compatibility preserved).
- `create_error_response(VLLMValidationError("messages must be a non-empty list.", parameter="messages"))` → HTTP 400, `type=BadRequestError`, `param="messages"`.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

## Details

Root cause: `messages` had no emptiness constraint, and `get_chat_request_role` indexes `request.messages[-1]` after generation. Enforcing the constraint on the pydantic model (a `mode="before"` validator) is too broad — the same model is built by internal adapters and tests with an empty list. The fix guards `create_chat_completion` instead, so only the chat-completions endpoint rejects empty input, and it does so before any work is scheduled.

Docs: equivalent validation rejections (e.g. an empty completion prompt) are not separately documented; this restores expected OpenAI-compatible behavior, so no docs change.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open and closed PRs and issues for empty-messages / falsy `messages` validation in chat completions. No open or merged PR rejects an empty `messages` list. Adjacent but distinct work: #65357 / #65366 (empty *developer-message content* → 400) and #57394 (empty `logprob_token_ids`) target different fields, not the `messages` list; #59108 is about turns a chat template silently drops.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR (development and drafting by an AI agent). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and defends the change end to end.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Use a free port for the Mooncake client in the weight-cache tests
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

`MooncakeCluster` in `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py` starts `mooncake_client` without `-port`, so it uses the default 50052 and the abstract IPC socket `@mooncake_client_50052.sock`. When another client in the same network namespace already holds that name, the client exits during setup and the test fails with "mooncake store is not ready". The fixture already takes the master and metrics ports from `get_open_port()`; this does the same for the client. Follow-up to #65168.

## Claims

- The client no longer shares the hard-coded default IPC socket name with other default-port clients.
- Nothing else changes: the in-process `MooncakeArtifactStore` reaches the segment through the master and never addresses the client's port.

## Validation

CI failure in `(B200) Distributed Preload with Mooncake Store` ([build 100998](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100998#01a1befc-0bb3-4298-a610-eacdbabf93bd)), from `test_mooncake_warmup_cache_store_e2e`:

```text
real_client.cpp:6572] Failed to bind UDS socket '@mooncake_client_50052.sock': Address already in use
real_client.cpp:1101] Failed to start IPC server at @mooncake_client_50052.sock
real_client_main.cpp:134] Failed to setup client: INTERNAL_ERROR
```

Reproduced with `mooncake-transfer-engine==0.3.13.post1` on one T4 (the same Mooncake version as CI, which installs the CUDA 13 variant), with a master and one default-port client running. This checks client startup and segment mounting, not the full weight-cache fixture:

| Second client | Result |
|---|---|
| default port (main) | exits with the same three lines |
| `-port <free port>` (this PR) | starts and mounts its segment: `Starting real client service on 0.0.0.0:56778` |

`pre-commit` passes on the changed file. Both `MooncakeCluster` tests need CUDA and Mooncake; the B200 step runs `test_mooncake_warmup_cache_store_e2e` on this PR.

## Details

- Mooncake's `real_client_main.cpp` defaults `-port` to 50052 and names the IPC socket `@mooncake_client_<port>.sock`. Selecting a port avoids sharing the hard-coded default IPC socket name. `get_open_port()` releases its socket before the client starts, so uniqueness is not guaranteed, the same as for the master and metrics ports.
- The CI log does not show which process held the name. The failure is intermittent; the same job passes on other builds.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve confirmed junction after lookup retry
author: Alex-ai-future
body:
## Overview

Preserve a confirmed full-attention junction when offload lookup convergence excludes an in-flight chunk. Related to #63565 and its fix #63566.

## Claims

- A deferred full-attention lookup can become confirmed after a sparse group shortens the lookup range, even when the pending chunk itself remains pending. Record the confirmed boundary if a later sparse group shortens the hit again.
- Never record a junction from a full-attention group that has not been confirmed, even if another group has reset the convergence loop's deferred flag.
- This changes junction retention, not the converged hit length or the manager's lookup semantics.

## Validation

- Real `CPUOffloadingManager`, real requests and scheduler: both new regression tests fail on the base revision and pass with the fix. The first returns a 16-token hit and changes the junction from 0 to 32; the second prevents an unconfirmed 16-token junction.
- Full `test_scheduler.py`: **507 passed**, 15 warnings. The worktree lacked compiled extensions, so the run used the configured venv and a temporary Python bootstrap that loaded the existing extensions from another checkout. The actual command was `$VENV/bin/python /tmp/vllm-junction-investigation/pytest_boot.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q --disable-warnings --maxfail=2`.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`: passed.
- End-to-end, Qwen3.5-0.8B-text-only BF16 on one H100 MIG 10 GiB with native CPU offload: real producer requests populated CPU caches; lookup responses were selectively demoted to reproduce the interleaving while using real cached data. The original and fixed scheduler each loaded 576 tokens and generated the same next token (264); the original recorded junction 0 and the fix recorded 1152. This is a controlled single-prompt correctness check, not an accuracy benchmark or a performance measurement.
- Four rounds of natural shared-prefix and eviction traffic on that model produced 195 hits and 41 misses, but did not encounter a pending full-attention lookup. Natural occurrence and workload frequency remain unverified; no speedup is claimed.

## Details

The old code writes 0 when full-attention lookup is deferred, then only captures the boundary while the field is `None`. A sparse group can narrow the candidate and trigger a full recheck that no longer includes the pending key; a second sparse constraint can then narrow the final hit. The original 0 masks the confirmed boundary. Also, the shared defer flag can be reset by another full-attention group before the first sparse lookup; track the per-iteration full-attention confirmation separately to avoid registering an unconfirmed boundary.

Duplicate check: #63566 covers stable lookup, while open #62278 and #62400 address junction representation / MooncakeStore and do not update this deferred-convergence logic. Searches for offload junction / pending / lookup found no open PR addressing this path. The boundary representation will need a rebase if #62278 lands first.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to investigate, implement and test this change and draft this description. The human submitter confirmed reviewing the changes and running the relevant tests.

title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Use the SigLIP chat template over the Gemma one for SigLIP2
author: Alex-Wengg
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #66417. SigLIP2 text sent to `/v1/embeddings` as `messages` still gets a different embedding than the same text sent as `input`. The SigLIP2 checkpoints report `model_type: "siglip"` but reuse the Gemma tokenizer, which ships Gemma's chat template. A tokenizer template outranks vLLM's predefined fallbacks, so the text is wrapped in `<start_of_turn>user ... <end_of_turn>` and loses EOS (11 tokens instead of 6 for "a photo of a cat").

This lets selected model types use their predefined template ahead of templates shipped on the Hub, and enables it only for `siglip`, whose `template_siglip.jinja` from #66417 gives the same tokens as the tokenizer. An explicit `--chat-template` still wins.

The NaFlex checkpoints (`model_type: "siglip2"`) ship no chat template, but their fallback was still `template_basic.jinja`, which drops the EOS their tokenizer adds (5 tokens instead of 6). They now use `template_siglip.jinja` too.

Hub-side fix for the template itself: https://huggingface.co/google/siglip2-base-patch16-224/discussions/23

## Validation

- Chat vs. `input` tokens for CLIP, SigLIP, SigLIP2 and both NaFlex checkpoints: all identical with the fix; SigLIP2 and NaFlex differ without it
- `test_dual_encoder_chat_text_matches_input` now includes `google/siglip2-base-patch16-224`

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Avoid runtime JIT of two prefill sparse-attention kernels
author: Juntian777
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix runtime JIT of `_block_scores_kernel` and `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel` in DeepSeek-V4.1 serving. Triton specialized both on values that change from step to step, so serving compiled new variants after warmup.

## Claims

- `_block_scores_kernel`: `stride_scores` joins `do_not_specialize`.
- `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel`: `query_start_loc_ptr`, `seq_lens_ptr` and `gather_lens_ptr` move to `do_not_specialize_on_alignment`, and the warmup compiles two pointer variants per layer type (`topk_indices` aligned or not) instead of three.
- No change to outputs or to the work the kernels do.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 with `--jit-monitor-mode warn`: on main, both kernels compile during inference in DEP4 serving (5 of 5 runs); TP4 serving shows neither. With `--jit-monitor-verbose`, every other pointer and specialized stride in the runtime `_block_scores_kernel` key is 16-divisible or constant, which leaves `stride_scores` as the only specialized argument that follows the step's shape.

Runtime JIT before/after on GB200: compile the kernels' registered warmup keys plus one launch of each (startup), call `jit_monitor.activate(mode="warn")`, then launch with new logits widths (33-1537 blocks) and prefill chunk offsets (serving):

```text
# main
Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _block_scores_kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config.
Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config.

# this PR
(no runtime JIT)
```

Kernel-level check on GB200 (two runs each): `select_candidate_blocks` over full-width rows of 32-1537 blocks with 256-aligned logits, and `combine_topk_swa_indices` with `query_start_loc`/`seq_lens` and `gather_lens` sliced at independent offsets, as prefill chunks pass them.

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_block_scores_kernel` variants compiled | 2 | 1 |
| `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel` variants compiled | 4 | 1 |
| candidate blocks (rows sorted), combined indices and lens | identical | identical |

Candidate rows are compared sorted because `torch.topk` orders tied block scores differently from run to run, on main as well.

## Details

- `_block_scores_kernel` writes `scores[row * stride_scores + block]`. The scores row stride is `nblocks` on the full-width path and `nblocks` rounded up to DeepSelect's alignment otherwise, so it follows each step's logits width; a width in a divisibility class startup did not see compiles a new variant. The hint only aligned the small scores store; the kernel is bound by its logits reads, and the non-divisible variant is what these shapes already run.
- A prefill chunk passes `query_start_loc` and `seq_lens` at `num_decodes + chunk_start` and `gather_lens` at `chunk_start`, so each int32 pointer is 16 B aligned or not independently. The warmup registered 3 of the combinations; mixed DEP steps reach the others. Each program reads one value per request from these pointers, so alignment buys nothing.
- #64001 makes the same `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel` change for ROCm; this PR also covers `_block_scores_kernel`.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Let DomynEdge mix sliding and full attention layers
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Overview

`test_can_initialize_large_subset[DomynEdgeForCausalLM]` fails on every CI run that collects it since `domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base` updated its config on the Hub (2026-11-10 12:06 UTC). The new config sets `layer_types` with both sliding and full attention layers, which `Qwen2Model` rejects. DomynEdge already applies each layer's window itself, so this lets it skip that check.

## Claims

- `test_can_initialize_large_subset[DomynEdgeForCausalLM]` no longer fails on `Sliding window for some but all layers is not supported`.
- No behavior change for any other `Qwen2Model` subclass (Qwen2, Qwen3, MiMo, DeepSeek-V4, ...): the check still runs for them.
- No change to how DomynEdge computes attention: its layers already take their windows from `config.window_sizes`.

## Validation

Seen on both platforms in https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101457, unchanged after a retry:

```
AssertionError: Sliding window for some but all layers is not supported. This model uses sliding window but `max_window_layers` = 36 is less than `num_hidden_layers` = 1.
FAILED models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[DomynEdgeForCausalLM]
```

This PR has not been run on a GPU locally; the reproducer is `pytest models/test_initialization.py -k DomynEdgeForCausalLM`, which runs in the Basic Models (Extra Initialization) jobs. `tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py` (`domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base`, vLLM vs HF logprobs) covers the full model with the new config.

Checked statically:
- In the new config, `window_sizes` (derived from `layer_types` by the remote `DomynEdgeConfig`) marks exactly the `sliding_attention` layers, all with `(1024, 0)`, and `sliding_window = 1025`. `DomynEdgeAttention` passes `window_size + 1 = 1025` as `per_layer_sliding_window` on those layers and `None` on full attention layers.
- Full attention layers do not pick up the model-level window: `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()` only sets `CacheConfig.sliding_window` when every entry of `layer_types` is `sliding_attention`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `check-docstring-style`: clean.

## Details

**Root cause.** `Qwen2Model.__init__` asserts `max_window_layers == num_hidden_layers` whenever `layer_types` has more than one value, because `Qwen2DecoderLayer` cannot apply a per-layer window. The remote `DomynEdgeConfig` defaults `max_window_layers` to `num_hidden_layers` only to get past this check (its comment: "remove once vLLM's native DomynEdge no longer requires it ... in Domyn Edge `layer_types` alone decides which layers slide"). A full model therefore loads, but `test_can_initialize` overrides `num_hidden_layers` to 1 after the config is built, leaving `max_window_layers = 36`.

**Fix.** A `supports_per_layer_sliding_window` class attribute on `Qwen2Model`, `False` by default, guards the check. `DomynEdgeModel` sets it to `True`.

**Why not pin the checkpoint revision** in `tests/models/registry.py`: the Hub repo history was rewritten and now has a single commit, so no earlier revision exists.

title: [Transformers backend] Fix M-RoPE models under CUDA graphs
author: hmellor
body:
## Overview

Fix Transformers modeling backend models that use M-RoPE (Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, ...) under CUDA graphs: they generate garbage with the default graph mode and hit an illegal memory access with `PIECEWISE`. Unblocks moving the Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL text models to the backend in #66821.

## Claims

- M-RoPE models on the backend give the same output with CUDA graphs as without.
- The `[3, seq_len] -> [3, 1, seq_len]` M-RoPE position reshape moves from the multimodal mixin to `Base.forward`, so text-only backend models with M-RoPE (the language model of a native VLM) get it too.

## Validation

B200, `--model-impl transformers`, greedy, one image prompt (a red square) and one text prompt:

| Model | Graph mode | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct | none | "The image is a solid red color." / "Mercury, Venus, and Mars." | same |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | "\n\nThe image you're referring to is a solid red color." / "\n\n\n\n..." | "The image is a solid red color." / "Mercury, Venus, and Mars." |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct | `PIECEWISE` | illegal memory access | "The image is a solid red color." / "Mercury, Venus, and Mars." |
| Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | garbage | "The image is of a red color." / "Mercury, Venus, Earth" (same as no graphs) |

```python
LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct", model_impl="transformers", compilation_config={"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"})
```

## Details

vLLM's M-RoPE positions are a `[3, max_tokens + 1]` buffer sliced to `[3, num_tokens]`, and Transformers' M-RoPE text models want `[3, batch, seq_len]`. The backend made that with `positions[:, None].contiguous()` outside the compiled region, so every step passed the graph a freshly allocated tensor while the captured graph kept reading the address from capture time. Dropping the copy doesn't work either: the strided view's buffer length shows up in Dynamo's shapes and fails the compile-range check.

The positions are now copied into a persistent flat buffer of `3 * max_num_batched_tokens` and viewed as a contiguous `[3, 1, num_tokens]` prefix, so the address is fixed and the layout stays contiguous. The buffer is only allocated for M-RoPE models.

No open PR duplicates this (searched for M-RoPE, the Transformers backend and CUDA graphs).

title: [Bugfix][Tokenizers] Raise ValueError on unknown message role in deepseek_v41_encoding
author: rudy-07
body:
## Overview

Raise `ValueError` instead of `NotImplementedError` when an unknown role is passed to `deepseek_v41_encoding.render_message()`. This aligns `deepseek_v41_encoding` with `deepseek_v32_encoding` and `deepseek_v4_encoding`, allowing the OpenAI serving layer to correctly catch invalid roles and return HTTP 400 Bad Request instead of an unhandled HTTP 501 / 500 error.

## Claims

- Fixes exception type in `deepseek_v41_encoding.render_message` from `NotImplementedError` to `ValueError` when encountering an unrecognized message role.
- Prevents server errors (HTTP 501 / 500) on invalid client input, ensuring proper HTTP 400 mapping in the OpenAI chat serving endpoint.
- Extends test coverage across `tests/test_request_input_bounds.py` and `tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py`.

## Validation

- Verified existing and new unit tests:
  - `pytest tests/test_request_input_bounds.py -k test_encode_messages_unknown_role_raises_value_error` (passes for v32, v4, and v41)
  - `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py -k test_deepseek_v41_unknown_role_raises_value_error` (passes)
- Verified code formatting and linting:
  - `ruff check vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py`
  - `ruff format --check vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py`

## Details

In `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v41_encoding.py`, line 505 previously raised `NotImplementedError(f"Unknown role: {role}")`. Both `deepseek_v32_encoding.py` (line 261) and `deepseek_v4_encoding.py` (line 392) raise `ValueError(f"Invalid role: {role}")`. Because invalid roles are client errors rather than unimplemented server features, raising `ValueError` is required so `serving_chat.py` maps the failure to HTTP 400.

Checked open and closed pull requests on GitHub; no active or prior PR addresses this mismatch.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Key the FSE MXFP8 scale-layout test check on the selected backend
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

Fix `test_fse_online_quantization_routed_shared` so it checks the MXFP8 scale layout of the backend that was actually selected. The three `routed_mxfp8` cases fail on gfx942 (MI300) because the test assumes every MXFP8 backend stores flattened scales. This is a test-only change. It lets the three MI300 `--deselect` flags in #66672 be removed.

Fixes: <!-- issue link to be filled -->

## Claims

- Fixes the 3 `routed_mxfp8` failures (`assert 4 == (4 * 512)`) on any ROCm GPU where `supports_mx()` is False (gfx942), or where AITER fused MoE or flydsl is unavailable.
- Keeps the flattened-layout check on the AITER_MXFP8 (FlyDSL) path, where that layout is produced.
- Does not change vLLM runtime behaviour.

## Validation

All runs were on MI355X (gfx950), from `tests/`, with `W=<worktree>` and torchao placed off the default path as in #66672 (`/tmp/qdeps`). gfx942 was **simulated** with a pytest plugin that patches the platform at `pytest_configure`. No real MI300 run was done.

| Configuration | Command | Before (`b76e2401f8`) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fuller gfx942 simulation (`rocm._ON_GFX950=False`, `_ON_GFX942=True`, `supports_mx()=False`; MXFP4 and MXFP8 both select EMULATION) | `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=$W:/tmp/qdeps:<plugin dir> python -m pytest -p <plugin> quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py -q` | 3 failed, 43 passed, 3 skipped | 46 passed, 3 skipped |
| `supports_mx()=False` only | same, with the `force_no_mx` plugin | 3 failed, 44 passed, 2 skipped | 47 passed, 2 skipped |
| Native gfx950 (AITER_MXFP8, no forcing) | `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=$W:/tmp/qdeps python -m pytest quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py -q` | 47 passed, 2 skipped | 47 passed, 2 skipped |
| gfx950 with `moe_backend="triton"` forced (TRITON_MXFP8) | `-k routed_mxfp8` | 3 failed | 3 passed |

In each "before" row the failures are exactly `[nvfp4_routed_mxfp8_shared-routed_mxfp8]`, `[quark_nvfp4_routed_bf16_shared-routed_mxfp8]` and `[quark_nvfp4_routed_nvfp4_shared-routed_mxfp8]`, each failing with `assert 4 == (4 * 512)`. These are the same three ids that #66672 deselects on MI300.

Scale shapes logged during the runs:
- Native gfx950: MXFP8 uses AITER_MXFP8 with flattened scales `(2048, 8)` / `(1024, 8)`, so the flattened check still runs there. MXFP4 and Quark OCP_MX use AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4 with 3-D scales `(N, 512, 8)`.
- Simulated gfx942: every case uses EMULATION with 3-D scales `(N, 512, 8)` / `(N, 256, 8)`.

Lint: `pre-commit run --files tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` passes.

**Not covered locally:** I did not run this on real gfx942/MI300 hardware. I validated it with the simulation above, and the MI300 Quantization job in #66672 will exercise it. NVIDIA does not apply: the module has `pytestmark = skipif(not current_platform.is_rocm())`. No csrc is involved.

## Details

**Root cause.** For every `Mxfp8OnlineMoEMethod`, the test asserted the flattened layout `w13_weight_scale.shape[0] == num_slots * w13_weight.shape[1]`. Only AITER_MXFP8 produces that layout. In `oracle/fp8.py`, `convert_to_fp8_moe_kernel_format` calls `rocm_aiter_ops.shuffle_mxfp8_moe_weights` only for that backend, and that function reshapes the scales to `(-1, K // 32)`. `select_mxfp8_moe_backend` (`oracle/mxfp8.py`) picks the first supported backend. AITER_MXFP8 and TRITON_MXFP8 both need `current_platform.supports_mx()`, which is False on gfx942, so EMULATION is selected there. EMULATION keeps 3-D `[num_slots, rows, K // 32]` scales, so `shape[0] == num_slots` and the assertion fails. Forcing only `supports_mx()=False` on gfx950 reproduces the failure exactly, which shows that fnuz FP8 and the gfx942 arch flags play no part.

**Culprit.** #64378 (`2abde627d9`, "[ROCm][Quantization] NVFP4 MoE re-quantization and fused shared experts through online quantization") added the `routed_mxfp8` case and the class-keyed flattened assertion. Pickaxe on `routed_method_cls is Mxfp8OnlineMoEMethod` finds only that commit. It merged on 2026-10-29, after the ROCm Quantization job was disabled on 2026-10-25 by #63608 (`9d48c8ab95`), so the test never ran on MI300. A bisect is not meaningful because the failing assertion was introduced together with the test.

**Fix.** The flattened layout is checked only when `quant_method.fp8_backend == Fp8MoeBackend.AITER_MXFP8`. Every other case (EMULATION, TRITON_MXFP8, and the MXFP4 and Quark OCP_MX methods, which have no `fp8_backend`) asserts `w13/w2_weight_scale.shape[0] == num_slots`. The MXFP4 and Quark OCP_MX routed cases had no scale-shape check before, so this PR also makes them stricter. The check holds for AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4 and EMULATION. If a future MXFP4 backend flattens its scales, this branch will need updating. Diff: +6/-2, test only.

**Related PRs.**
- #66672: with this PR merged, the three `--deselect='...routed_mxfp8]'` flags can be removed from the MI300 Quantization step in `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` and from its mirror in `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml`.
- #66803 edits a different line of the same file (around L1433, `NvFp4MoeBackend.EMULATION` to `NONE`). At most a trivial rebase is expected and no conflict.

**Duplicate-work check.** I searched open PRs for `test_online_shared_expert_fusion` (no results), `routed_mxfp8` (only #66672, which deselects these tests rather than fixing them), `mxfp8 scale layout`, `mxfp8 scale shape shared expert fusion` and `w13_weight_scale num_slots`. None of the other hits (for example #65479, #65421, #57977, #63203, #66771) touch this test.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Allow lut_b_moe online quantization on ROCm
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
## Overview

Add `lut_b_moe` to `RocmPlatform.supported_quantization` so `quantization="lut_b_moe"` passes validation on ROCm and uses the LUT-B emulation experts, as the docs say it should for non-Rubin GPUs. This fixes `tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_lut_b_moe` on ROCm. That test fails on ROCm and is one of the failures the ROCm Quantization re-enable in vllm#66672 currently works around.

Fixes #<issue-to-be-filed>. Culprit: vllm#62759.

## Claims

- `quantization="lut_b_moe"` no longer fails with `ValidationError: lut_b_moe quantization is currently not supported in rocm.` on ROCm. It loads, falls back to `LutBEmulationTritonExperts`, and generates coherent output.
- `test_online_lut_b_moe` passes on gfx950 with this change. It has never passed on ROCm since it was added.
- No behavior change on NVIDIA or XPU. `CudaPlatform` has no allow-list here, and the XPU list is not touched.

## Validation

All runs were on MI355X (gfx950), from `tests/`, with torchao off the default path in `/tmp/qdeps` (installed from vllm#66672's `requirements/test/quantization_deps_rocm.txt`).

| Check | Command | Before (`origin/main` b76e2401f8) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reproducer | `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=<worktree>:/tmp/qdeps .venv/bin/python -m pytest quantization/test_online.py::test_online_lut_b_moe` | 1 failed (pydantic `ValidationError` from `ModelConfig`: `lut_b_moe quantization is currently not supported in rocm.`) | 1 passed (42s). The log shows `LUT-B MoE falls back to emulation: kernel does not support current device rocm`, and greedy output is `'Hello my name is' -> ' Mary. I'` |
| Neighbouring online methods | `pytest quantization/test_online.py -k 'lut_b or nvfp4_per_token_moe or mxfp4_hadamard'` | - | 1 passed, 1 skipped (`nvfp4_per_token_moe` is CUDA-only), 200 deselected |
| LUT-B kernels / config args | `pytest kernels/moe/test_lut_b_moe.py quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py` | - | 52 passed, 7 skipped (all 7 are SM107/Rubin native-kernel tests) |
| Lint | `pre-commit run --files vllm/platforms/rocm.py` | - | clean |

The compiled extensions came from a slightly older main (5629b26146). That does not matter here because no csrc code is involved; this is a Python allow-list change only.

**Not covered locally:**
- gfx942 (MI300) was not run. I expect it to behave the same, because the allow-list check is not arch-gated and ROCm always takes the emulation experts. However, the emulation's activation QDQ goes through the ROCm Triton MXFP8 quantizer (`_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_triton`), which is only tested in-tree on gfx95x. The already allow-listed `mxfp8` online method has the same dependency. The MI300 Quantization job that vllm#66672 re-enables should confirm this.
- NVIDIA was not run. It is unaffected because the ROCm list is the only thing that changes.

CI: the existing `test_online_lut_b_moe` (gated on `is_cuda_alike()`) is the regression guard. It runs in the ROCm Quantization jobs once vllm#66672 re-enables them. No new test is needed.

## Details

**Root cause.** `Platform.verify_quantization` (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`) rejects any method that is missing from a platform's non-empty `supported_quantization` list. vllm#62759 (df05643664, "[Quant] LUT-B MoE with MXFP8 activations: native Rubin kernel + emulation") added the `lut_b_moe` shorthand to `QuantizationMethods` and `_ONLINE_SHORTHANDS`, along with the emulation experts and `test_online_lut_b_moe`. It did not add the shorthand to `RocmPlatform.supported_quantization`, where the other online shorthands (`mxfp8`, `fp8_per_*`, `mxfp4_hadamard32`) are listed. ROCm does not actually lack the feature. `LutBEmulationTritonExperts._supports_current_device` returns `is_cuda_alike()`, the native `LutBSm107Experts` requires `is_cuda()`, and `docs/features/quantization/online.md` says "Other GPUs emulate the same numerics". The method was simply rejected before it could be built. I found the culprit with `git log -S lut_b_moe`, which returns only that commit, so no bisect was needed. The test was added while the ROCm Quantization job was disabled (since 2026-10-25), so the failure went unnoticed.

**Fix.** One line: add `"lut_b_moe"` next to `mxfp4_hadamard32`. With this change, the only behavior difference is that ROCm accepts `quantization="lut_b_moe"` instead of rejecting it.

**Interaction with open PRs:**
- vllm#66672 (`Thangnguyenvn98`) and vllm#66803 (`fxmarty-amd`) both change the `test_online_lut_b_moe` gate from `is_cuda_alike()` to `is_cuda()` with "ROCm does not support lut_b_moe". That would skip the test on ROCm rather than fix it. With this PR, those hunks should be dropped and the `is_cuda_alike()` gate kept. Otherwise this fix loses its regression guard on ROCm. This PR unblocks that case in vllm#66672's re-enabled MI300/MI355 Quantization jobs.
- vllm#66607 (`mgoin`, LUT-B for linear layers) adds a `lut_b` shorthand and `test_online_lut_b`, also gated on `is_cuda_alike()`, without a ROCm allow-list entry. It will hit the same `ValidationError` on ROCm, so `lut_b` should be added to the ROCm list either in that PR or in a follow-up after it merges.

**Duplicate-work check.** I searched open PRs for `lut_b_moe`, `LUT-B`, `lut_b rocm` and `supported_quantization rocm`. The hits were vllm#66607, #66803, #66672, #66874 (compressed-tensors LUT-B MoE checkpoints; does not touch platforms), #66194, #65802, #60321, #62770 and #65165. None of them adds `lut_b_moe` to the ROCm allow-list.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change. The submitter reviewed the diff and ran the commands above.

title: [Bugfix][Muse Spark] Avoid the FlashInfer Cake PDL race in gated_residual_rmsnorm
author: jeejeelee
body:
## Overview

Run Muse Spark's `gated_residual_rmsnorm` on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL backend instead of the default Cake backend. The Cake programs for 128 rows or fewer read `branch` before `griddepcontrol.wait` (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9343). This corrupts the hidden states that DSpark reads, so DSpark output is garbage at DP + EP with TP=1. No open PR addresses this.

## Claims

- Fixes DSpark at DEP8: AIME25 0% → 98.9%, GSM8K 23.1% → 94.8%, sdAL back to 3.7–3.9.
- No end-to-end perf change at TEP4.

## Validation

B300, Muse Spark NVFP4 + DSpark (7 draft tokens), FP8 KV.

**DEP8 accuracy**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| AIME25 (3 epochs, temperature 0.6) | 0% (garbage output) | 98.9% (pass@3 100%) |
| sdAL, AIME25 | 8.00 | 3.66 |
| GSM8K 5-shot strict / flexible (greedy) | 23.1% / 27.2% | 94.8% / 94.8% |
| sdAL, GSM8K | 1.01 | 3.91 |
| sdAL, greedy probe (1 request / C48) | 1.01 / 1.01 | 3.44 / 3.73 |

Target-only DEP8 scores 100% on AIME25; TEP4 GSM8K is 95.0% with sdAL 3.90.

**TEP4 TPOT (140k in / 512 out, 95% prefix hit, median of 3 runs)**

| concurrency | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.61 ms | 3.61 ms |
| 8 | 8.27 ms | 8.73 ms |
| 48 | 19.16 ms | 18.84 ms |

The c=8 gap is acceptance noise: sdAL was 2.26 vs 2.33. Time per step (TPOT × sdAL) is 19.66 vs 19.41 ms. TTFT matches within 1% at every concurrency.

The kernel runs 5 times per decode step, once per captured aux layer. Per-call latency, B300, CUDA graph of 64 chained calls:

| rows | Cake + PDL (main) | CuTe + PDL (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1.50 µs | 1.58 µs |
| 48 | 2.06 µs | 2.14 µs |
| 384 | 6.38 µs | 6.20 µs |
| 4096 | 52.9 µs | 55.1 µs |

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/muse_spark/common/ops/fused_rmsnorm.py
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
mqa-run --task aime25 --epoch-num 3 --temperature 0.6 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 98304 --think true
```

## Details

- **Root cause:** DSpark reads 5 auxiliary target hidden states through `norm_then_gated_residual`, which calls `flashinfer.norm.gated_residual_rmsnorm` with `backend="auto"` and `enable_pdl=True`. For 1–128 rows, the Cake PDL programs prefetch `branch` before `griddepcontrol.wait`. When the preceding kernel triggers its dependents early, the norm reads a stale `branch` and emits NaN. The NaN flows through the draft's context K/V into its logits:
  - Most drafts are rejected (sdAL ≈ 1 under greedy GSM8K), but the NaN drafts that do get accepted still derail outputs (GSM8K 23%).
  - With sampling, NaN draft probabilities pass the acceptance test, so every draft is accepted and the output is garbage (AIME25 0%, sdAL 8.00).
- **Why only TP=1:** the same kernel runs at TP>1 without failing there. The trigger depends on which kernel runs just before it. The target's own boundary uses `gated_residual_next_rmsnorm`, whose Cake programs have no PDL, so target-only serving is unaffected.
- **Why CuTe instead of `enable_pdl=False`:** both fix DEP8 and tie end to end. CuTe keeps PDL and is about 0.5 µs faster per decode-size call. Disabling PDL keeps Cake's numerics and is 7–13% faster per call on prefill chunks of 2048 rows or more, which is under 0.05% of a 140k prefill.
- **Support check:** `supports_gated_residual_rmsnorm` is now asked about the CuTe backend too, so shapes that CuTe can't run fall back to the existing Triton path instead of raising.
- **Revert plan:** go back to the default backend once FlashInfer re-renders the Cake programs with the fix.
- **No unit test:** the race needs a producer that triggers its dependents early. The issue has a standalone repro; the end-to-end DEP8 eval above covers the fix.
